For this “Adam” is to enter the created world as appointed by God to be its ruler and master. This world is prepared for the entrance of its lord. In this sense the plural נעשה might be understood. The use of the “Pluralis Majestatis” with which human sovereigns proclaim their will to their subjects probably has its origin in the idea that the ruler is not issuing orders from the standpoint of his own individual will, in his own personal interests, but that he only looks upon himself as being at one with his people, and the orders and decisions are only made from the point of view of the general interest, and for the general well-being and happiness. It is only as representative of the people that the King rules over them. In the same way the Creator announces to the world the appointment of its master equally in its own interest, out of consideration of the purpose for which it exists. In similar way at the scattering of the people of the world we find הבה נרדה נבלה שם, out of consideration of, for the benefit of, the future of mankind itself. The “Pluralis Majestatis” occurs in the speeches of God in those cases where that, which on the surface appears to be a restricting, disturbing, interference, is meant to be understood as being in reality something which is happiness-bringing, rescuing and necessary. אדם, see Jeshurun VII p. 524 et seq. There we tried to make it clear that both grammatical and logical analogy speak against the usual assumption that the word אדם is derived from אדמה, which would make “earth-born” the characteristic of Man, whereas clearly אדמה is derived from the word אדם. The characteristic of being “earth-born” is one which is common to all animals, and the special characteristic of Man would be just that he is not entirely originated from the earth, but that the breath of God, breathed into his earth-made body made him into a Man. The manner in which a preliminary announcement is made here already tells us that in אדם the creation of a being of a higher nature and a higher calling is about to be made. In sentences like ואתנה צאני צאן מרעיתי אדם אתם the word אדם can not possibly have reference to origin from a block of earth. In the article referred to above we traced the etymology of the word אדם to come from the meaning אדום red, as the leastbroken ray of the spectrum, of the pure ray of light, i.e. the nearest revelation of the divine on earth; from the phonetic relation to הדם, foot-stool, as הדום רגלי שכינה on earth, as transmitter and bearer of the glory of God on earth (in contrast to במה ,במה is the means of raising something or somebody while הדום spares a superior from placing his feet on the earth. Without setting Man to be הדום = אדם, God Himself would have to consummate all the truth, the equity, the benevolence and the love that He wishes to be demanded on earth. The pure activity of Man achieving the Will of God spares the Supreme Being from having directly Himself to fulfil His Will on earth, (במת-האדם = בהמה ,הדום שכינה = אדם); — with חתם, seal (which relation is also indicated by the root אטם to close), as God’s seal on the creation which brings home to the world its unseen Lord and Master; — finally, with (דמ(ה with the individualising א prefixed, a being whose whole mission consists in his being “a likeness of God”, but who is to effect this likeness through his own free-willed, independent energy, thereby the representative, the deputy, the alter ego of the Supreme Being — all these ideas at rock bottom come to the same thing, just as the derivations of the word א-דם ,חתם ,הדום ,אדום :אדם have substantially the same conception, they could all be summed up in the idea of representative, and designate אדם as representative, deputy. בצלמו. There, on p. 526, we have in the same way pointed out that צלם, related to סמל (שמלה), שלם (שלמה), only means the outer covering, the bodily form. בצלמנו: “in our sheath”, i.e. if all the compassion and love, the truth and equity and holiness of the Divine Rule wished to appear cased in an exterior visible form, it would appear in the figure which the Creator gave Man. The bodily form of Man already proclaims him as the representative of God, as the divine on earth, it is כדמותנו, it is such as complies with, is adequate to, a being having the calling of being “godlike”. דמה: to be similar to. As דמה at the same time means to be silent, so that the idea of similarity here is construed that the similarity of the object must be “silent” towards that to which it is similar, i.e. may in no way contradict it, the likeness to God expected of Man is expressed to be primarily negative, that in his whole being he does not foster anything which would contradict the divine truth, love, justice and holiness. Like God no man can be, but similar to Him he should be, should not tolerate anything in himself or with himself, which is contradictory to God. התקדש, to work himself up towards the holiness of God is his mission. וירדו: Here at once אדם is taken as the collective conception of human beings, hence the plural form. רדו: fundamental meaning, to bring something down from its free height into the hand, i.e. into your power, וירדהו אל כפיך ,רדה דבש מגוית האריה at Samson, and רודה פת in Talmudic Hebrew, for bringing the loaves sticking fast to the walls of the oven down into your hands. From that: bringing something out of its free independence into your power, making it subservient to you. Used with the accusative it means, to make the whole condition subservient, used thus only twice: לעיניך לא ירדנו בפרך and רודה באף גוים (Is. 14,6) where, in both cases it refers to exercising force beyond the authority which normally pertains to a master or a king. In all other cases we find it used with a preposition רדא ב-, ruling over certain conditions of an object, bringing something into subjugation in certain respects. This is the position Man is to have towards all other living creatures on earth. He has not been given the mission to make them all, and indeed not entirely, subservient to him. The earth and its creatures may have other relationships, of which we are ignorant, in which they serve their own purpose. But Man has been given the position לרדות בם, not אותם, to exercise his mastery over living creatures, and on the earth itself, to bring some of them out of their free independence under his hand for the fulfilment of his human calling. If Man approaches the world as בצלם ובדמות א׳ ,אדם, and demands its service only in the service of God, then the earth gladly renders it, gladly recognises Man as its ruler, his mastery is no enslavement or degradation, but rather a raising and elevation of all earthly material elements into the sphere of free-willed moral God-serving purposes. The whole world bows willingly to pure God-serving Man. But if Man misuses his position, if he does not approach the world as אדם, as the representative of God, but in his own power of mastery, then animals too, do not willingly bow their neck to him. ויֵרֵדו, זכו ויׅרדו, לא זכוׅ ויֵרֵדו את שהוא בצלמנו כדמותנו ויׅרדו, את שאינו בצלמנו כדמותנו, so our sages teach. For רדה is not רדה ,כבש is only the relation of a ruler to the people, which indeed is only a conditional one. כבש is a different relation, which in v. 28 specialises the relationship of Man to the lifeless earth. We meet the word כבש in כבש the ramp of the altar, on which our sages say דרך כבושה, “downtrodden”, and in כבשן the furnace, in which the things that are thrown into it, are completely demolished and changed. So that כבש means forcibly trodden down so that it can not arise, to completely force or change and reform something in its innermost nature. This calling, to impress his stamp on a thing, to change it completely to his “thing”, Man is given only over lifeless Nature, things that belong to that, are to be material and means for him to carry out his ideas. כבשן is at the root of human art, the great calcinating furnace which reduces and produces the raw materials of the earth in quite changed forms. That is why it differentiates so clearly in v. 28: ובעוף השמים וׅגו׳ מלאו את הארץ וכבשוה ,ורדו בדגת הים. For originally, (during the first 1526 years I.L.) Man was not allowed to kill living creatures! So that God spake: Let Us make an Adam in a form worthy of Us, as is commensurate with being in Our likeness, and they shall rule over the fish of the sea, and the birds of the heaven and over the whole earth, and all the creeping things that move on the earth. As ובכל הארץ is interposed in the list of the living creatures, and ובכל הרמש only follows after it, it seems that Man’s dominion over the small creeping animals is to be taken only as being in consequence of his dominating the whole world. And as a matter of fact Man only exercises dominion over the lower animals by destroying them, or driving them away from every spot on the earth that he demands for his dominion.

V. 27. ויברא א׳ את האדם בצלמו. This sentence repeated again and again, that the mortal frame of Man is one which is worthy of God and commensurate with the godly calling of Man, shows what definite value the Torah lays on recognition of the godlike dignity of the human body. And actually the whole Torah rests primarily on making the body holy. The whole mortality of human beings rests on the fact that the human body, with all its urges, forces and organs, was formed commensurately with the godly calling of Man, and is to be kept holy and dedicated exclusively to that godly calling. Nothing digs the grave of the moral calling of Man more effectively than the erroneous conception which cleaves asunder the nature of Man; only recognising godlike dignity in the spirit, directs the spirit to elevate itself to the heights, and in mind and thought to soar upwards to a higher sphere, but leaves the body to unbridled licence, animal-like, nay lower than animal, to indulge in all the smut of sensuality. More, reckons the higher and highest genius and briliance of the mind as the greater permit for the moral degeneration of the body. Not so is Man’s calling as designated by God. There, keeping the body holy is the foundation of all ennoblement of the spirit, and the preparatory condition for all spiritual greatness; and the higher spiritual and mental greatness is reached, the more serious are the demands made for the control and dedication of the body. The bond of God with Israel to rebuild a purer mankind begins with Mila, dedicating the body to God. A whole list of God’s commands have the definitely expressed purpose of begetting, feeding, and keeping the body pure and fit for the spiritual, mental and moral likeness of God in Man, that he remains a צלם א׳ and does not become שקץ ,טמא and תועבה.

זכר ונקבה ברא אתם. Although all living creatures were created in both sexes, this is only stressed at human beings to lay down the fact that both sexes were created equally directly by God, and in equal likeness to Him. An equality which is also quite specially pregnantly expressed by the transition from the singular to the plural אותו to אותם. The one Adam-creature in the likeness of God is presented in two sexes, which only both together form the complete conception “Adam”. — זכר, from זכר to remember, related to סגר ,סכר, — the spiritual “keeper” of godliness, and of human traditions. The male sex forms the perpetuators, the links of the chain of traditions. נקבה — from נקב to determine, decide, fix — the “fixed” one (construction similar to גנבה ,גזלה from גנב ,גזל); it is only in conjunction with the man and in joining his efforts that woman finds the decision for the particular direction and the particular sphere in which she is to carry out her share in the common joint mission of mankind. The man chooses his own profession, the woman receives it in joining a husband.

V. 28. God blessed both of them, and to both of them He gave the command to fulfil the mission of mankind on earth. Whereas above, in v. 22 it says: ויברך אתם א׳ לאמר, here it says: ויברך אתם א׳, ויאמר א׳. There, in the unfree living creatures, as already remarked thereon, with the giving of the blessing, i.e. with granting the power and ability for reproduction and care of the young, the fulfilment of this blessing is already automatically also given. Reproduction and care for the young, in that case are purely physical acts. By the urge which the all-powerful blessing gave, they are carried out with just the same necessity as all other physical developments of living organisms. Here, in human beings, the blessing, i.e. the granting of the power and ability, is separated from the fulfilment i.e. from using this power and ability for the purposes for which God intended them. The fulfilment is directed to the human-beings who are to carry it out of their own free-will as duty. That which in animals is a purely physical act becomes in Man a free-willed moral act. But with the fourfold mission, ורבו מלאו את הארץ וכבשה פרו, the whole free-willed moral development of the human race is given. פרו is marriage, רבו is the family, מלאו is society, כבשוה is property.

פרו: marriage, the union of the sexes for production of human-fruit, children. Just as in the plant-fruit, the most precious strength and saps of the tree ripen to an independent germ, which becomes “free” (see v. 11 above), so do the noblest traits of godliness and humaneness which are innate in father and mother unite to produce a human germ which will become independent.

רבו: the family. רבה to multiply, duplicate, triplicate yourself. Already the mere physical increase of the human race presupposes something more than just begetting children. If even in the case of many species of animals the increase of the breed is dependent on the care of the young, this is much more the case in the human race. Even looked at purely from a physical point of view it is a much greater necessity. A human child would have no chance of survival at all were it not cared for by its parents right from birth and its bodily preservation and development furthered by this parental care. Not the birth, the aftercare is the real factor of increase of the human race. But רבה is something more and higher. The parents are to multiply themselves by their children, they are to repeat themselves in their children. The children are to be replicas not only of the physical bodily traits of their parents, but also of their spiritual, intellectual and moral selves. Accordingly the parents have to plant the spiritual and moral best of themselves in their children, and carefully nurture and mature its development. In short, they have to form, educate and cultivate them. Only so have they reproduced themselves in their children and discharged the duty of רבו. The meaning of forming, educating which is innate in the root רבה is found in רבה קשת shooting instructor, תרבות brood, also discipline, disciple, and not unlikely even the name רב and רבי for teacher come from the same conception. For the true business of a teacher is in fact nothing but to make the pupil a replica of his own spiritual and intellectual self. So that רבו demands the founding of the home, the family, the only nursery for human education. Only by taking over רבו does פרו attain its high, moral importance for the building of mankind. And even from this point of view, extra-matrimonial births are the grave of mankind, for although children there do indeed get born from parents, they lack their bodily moral and spiritual education, the parental love, the parental home in which, and by which alone, the child blossoms to a Man, to an Adam.

מלאו is society. As each individual pair is given the task to see to it that the earth becomes full of human beings, and with such plentitude of people their own real purport is achieved, obviously the demand goes beyond establishing their own home and requires that each one shall make it his business to see that next to his own home many other homes shall be established and thrive. But this makes “society” a duty encumbent on every individual.

כבשה is property (see on v. 26): the mastering, appropriating and transforming the earth and its products for human purposes. This acquirement of property is a preliminary necessity for the preceding tasks of home and society which require it as the means for accomplishing them. This makes the acquisition of property itself into a moral duty. But as this preliminary duty is mentioned last, it gives it its limitation, as having a moral meaning and importance only if it is devoted to the preceding purposes; only if fortune is sought and acquired to found family and further the needs of social work. But not if the order is reversed and one looks on marriage and society as merely the means to acquire property and riches.

This mission פרו ורבו is given at the same time to both sexes; for the united cooperation of both sexes for this human mission is equally essential. But nevertheless, as carrying-out this mission is essentially dependent on the possession of means, and acquiring such means, forcing the earth to yield them, is primarily the duty of the male sex, — which is also why the plural in וכבשה is not written in full — the duty of marriage and establishing the home is given directly and unconditionally to the man. For woman it is only conditional and only applies with the beginning of her union with a man. (Yebamoth 65b).

By these sentences the seal of God is stamped on the whole of family and civic life. The Word of God knows no division of life into two compartments, the so-called religious, directed to God, and the other, the profane, which has nothing to do with divine matters. God takes the whole of life for His service, demands it for the calling of “Adam”, and in the very first place, the family and civil life.

ומלאו את הארץ further expresses the intention of God, that the human race should spread all over the earth. Thereby the carrying out of Man’s mission on earth is not attached to any particular zone or climate, and can not be affected by any special conditions brought about by the influence of any land or climate. The whole world is meant to be אדמה, the human Kingdom, “Adam’s earth”. Everywhere, under every climatic and topographic influence, and with every variety of life brought about thereby, the great human mission of life can be carried out, and Man’s likeness to God not lost.

ורדו בדגת וגו׳. Above, in giving the command, the whole higher animal world is expressed by בהמה, the word חיה is missing, so that there חיה בכלל בהמה. Here it only says חיה, so that בהמה is understood as being included in חיה. There, in the command, the whole animal world to be mastered and ruled by Man is presented as בהמה, as pedestal for the higher dignity of Man. Here, where they first are actually to be brought to Man, they are described as חיה, they are still חיה, in the sphere of their own closed independent life.

V. 29—30. It does not say הגה נתתי לכם לאבלה, but simply לכם הנה נתתי. Also by the interpunctuation ֑ on זָרַע the לכם יהיה לאכלה is separated from the preceding as a completely independent sentence. Also if here it simply wanted to give the permission to eat vegetarian food, that surely would have already been included in the וכבשה of the preceding verse. Moreover one cannot overlook the fact that at the fruit-trees זורע זרע is expressly stressed, although the seeds of fruit are not meant for human consumption. From all this, the sense of the verse seems to be: See, I have given you all herbage that strews seed, which is on the surface of the whole world, and every tree on which there is fruit which strews its seed, i.e. the first of that which grows from seed, and the first fruit-trees I have created, henceforth they are לכם, I have given them over to you, their further preservation and continuation for food depends on your attention and care. “They are to be your food”. So that your heedful and wise care and attention given to them is in your own interest. — כל(ה) ,אכל with prefixed א׳ is destruction for assimilation with one’s own personality, (see Jeshurun VIII p. 278). Eating, accordingly, is no כליון, no destructive ending, but a transposition of material to another individual. The word gives the moral purpose and the moral limitation of eating. Only that is to be eaten which is suitable for, compatible with, the personality of the person whom it is to nourish. All the dietary laws are only the decision: “This is suitable to be assimilated with your personality”. But only God can make this decision. Only He knows the real nature of any given material, only He knows the real nature of us. For men, as we see here, only vegetarian food — the seeds of agricultural plants (grain, pulse etc.) as well as fruit — was appointed, for animals, the ירק עשב, the green of plants: leaves and herbage. So that originally complete peace reigned between man and beast. If, at the same time as the command was given ומלאו את הארץ, Man was restricted exclusively to vegetarian food — grain and fruit — the earth must everywhere have offered the possibility of such food, and so must have had a different climatic nature to what it has now. A fact for which proof is offered by the discovery of fossiled remains in the extreme North, of plants which now only grow in tropical regions. It was only after the flood that men were allowed to kill animals and to eat animal food. But with the flood there was also a change, a general disturbing change, in the nature of the conditions of the earth itself, הנני משחיתם את הארץ, and that may account for the permission to eat animal food being given. With the permission to eat animal food the first dietary law, אבר מן החי was introduced, as the dietary laws altogether only refer to animal food, and the conception of vegetarian food may not unlikely be a guide to the understanding of the choice of animals which the Torah has made for food.
ויהי כן. Thus did the present condition — the earth being inhabited by animals and men, and the relation of Man towards the earth and animals — come into existence.

V. 31. וירא א׳. We already know this saying: וירא א׳ כי טוב which we have encountered at every phase of the creation. We have already recognised how the fact that this saying always occurs after the completion of a creation, is to bring home to us the completely free power of the Creator over His creation, and the work continuing in existence being dependent on His approval. Here, too, we should not find anything striking, if here, at the final phase of the Creation it only said: וירא א׳ כי טוב. But it says והנה וגו׳ and הנה always introduces us to something we have not yet seen: “see there!” “lo”, so that here, apart from what this saying has hitherto conveyed to us, there must be in addition some new thought to be brought to us. In any case this would have occured to us at the first glance at the added word מאוד. All the phonetic relations of the root speak for this way of taking the meaning of the word הנה (compare the meanings of ענה ,חנה ,הנה ,אנה).

If then הנה always leads the trend of our thoughts to a new idea, and if מאוד is added to this new conception of טוב, that we have hitherto been taught to consider only as טוב good, we are now to consider as טוב מאוד “very good”, then there must be something indicated which must be the motive for this new nuance of our judgment, and this new conception is obviously the word כל. Every single creation is good, but only now, when the series of creations is closed, and each single one can be considered in relation to the whole, everything, כל is not only טוב but כל .טוב מאוד is not only the conception of plurality “all”, that therein everyone is included and none left out, but כל is a conception of the union of the plurality, is many looked on as a single unit, not so much “all” as “the whole”. כל, root is כליל .כלל in the mouth of the חכמים means, ring, hoop, wreath, crown, the idea of round, circle. (cf. גלל to turn about an axis). But a circle is naught but the most complete line, that space that is ruled with the same measure of force from one point in every conceivable direction. A circle is therefore a pregnant expression for the whole sphere that a being can control from his own standpoint. Hence all the expressions for the conception of completion and perfection are related in Hebrew to the word “circle”. That is why כל, too, is not so much the sum of many as the designation of the totality of a conception. So here too: God saw the whole of what He had created, saw how everything fitted together harmoniously, how they all turned round one point (it does not say את הכל אשר עשה but כל אשר עשה) the harmony, the union of all that He had created, He considered each in its connection with the whole, והנה טוב מאוד. Good, there too where we should not have expected it, where, looked at separately, by one who does not see the whole, it would appear imperfect. Thus everything created, everything in existence, looked at in connection with everything else, is very good. Everything relatively רע only appears רע when looked at alone, by itself, in a fraction of time and space. But this disappears, yea itself becomes טוב — even יסורים ,מות ,יצר הרע temptation, suffering, death — and then because we did not expect it, even טוב מאוד — as soon as we broaden our minds and look at the whole. If we would look at single things in connection with the whole, look on ourselves, our lives in connection with the whole of our true lives, not merely as תחתונים but also as עליונים, not only in our earthly life of our senses, but also in our spiritual godly relationship, not only in relation to עולם הזה but also to עולם הבא, consider every internal and external fight in the light of the spiritual freedom which victory brings, every contemporary moment in relation to the eternity that awaits us, then we too, with ר׳ מאיר would write in the margin of our תורה on the words והנה טוב מאוד the gloss והנה טוב מות, or with the other sages: .(’והנה טוב זו מדת טוב, מאוד זו יםורים; והנה טוב זה יצר הטוב, מאוד זה יצר הרע (ב״ר ט Just in the real “goodness” of these apparently “bad” things in life not only the טוב, but the טוב מאוד of all that God created, shows itself. I can suffer in the present, if through that I become wiser and nobler for the future, may even suffer for, yea, may have to spend the whole of my seventy years in trials, after all they are only a drop in the ocean of eternity that awaits me. Could we but see at one glance the whole picture of God’s management of events interworking with and on each other in all time and in all spheres, even as He sees it, we should indeed agree with His verdict: ! והנה טוב מאוד

מאוד. As a noun, it denotes the whole extent of means and strength, hence fortune. As an adverb it describes the conception to which it refers, in the whole measure of its possible extent, as far as it can possibly reach, accordingly, to the highest degree.

ויהי ערב ויהי בקר יום הששי, so it became evening, so it became morning, the sixth day. (ב״ר ט׳) זו שעה יתירה שמוספין מחול על הקדש אתם מקיימין ואם לאו אני מחזיר אתכם לתהו ובהו (שבת פח״א). יום הששי, אמר ר׳ יודו למה לי, מלמד שהתנה הקב״ה עם מעשה בראשית ואמר להם אם ישראל מקבלים התורה אמר ריש לקיש מאי דכתיב ויהי ערב ויהי בקר יום הששי ,ה׳ יתירה. We can find the explanation of these sentences if we realise the meaning of the ה. In general, a noun given the distinguishing adjective ה, by itself, without any following qualifying sentence, is designated as an object for which our minds have been prepared by what preceded it. “This is a man” brings the idea “man” to our minds quite by itself as something fresh; but “This is the man” or also “this is the man” presents him as something about which we already know. Were it to have said here יום ששי, this was a sixth day, it would have had no further relationship to the preceding days beyond its being number six in the series. But when we are told יום הששי that this was the sixth day, we are clearly meant to regard this day as one for which the others were preparatory, one to which they led up to, in which the list of creations found a goal and came to an end. It is, of course, stressed, as none of the other days had the distinguishing ה. If now this sixth day was just the one which was to bring to the created world its “Adam”, its God-representing lord and master, the ה of the יום הששי literally tells us that עם מעשה בראשית תנאי התנה הקב״ה, that the continuance and the purpose of the preceding creations were dependent on the creature created on the sixth day, dependent that this creature Man, undertakes and faithfully fulfils his mission. But if this creature Man, in the course of time misjudged and misused his position and left his mission unfulfilled, and only the entry of Israel into the history of the world was the first step taken for the ultimate return of mankind to a pure true recognition of its real position and mission, then this תנאי can in truth be expressed לאו אני מחזיר אתכם לתוהו ובהו אם ישראל מקבלים התורה אתם מתקיימין ואם and only with יום מתן תורה did יום הששי return to its rights.

But thereby the sixth day itself received the deep meaning of the conclusion of the Creation, and so is raised within the sphere of the Sabbath of Creation. For the seventh day, the Sabbath of Creation — as we shall see — was meant to be essentially an ever-recurring reminder to Man, who was set in the world on the sixth day to be the representative of God on earth, always to be conscious of this high calling, but of his still being dependent on God, and of the duties it imposes. The seventh day, accordingly is simply the result of the sixth, it presupposes its existence, and is to be the guarantee of the ultimate realisation of the high calling of Man in the Creation. That is why the Sabbath-consecration reaches over into the sixth day and it is a deep truth that ר׳ יודן expresses when he says: שעה יתירה שמוסיפין מחול על הקדש יום הששי זו. — The sixth day is what was essential to bring the concrete world to its conclusion, the seventh brings what is essential for the persistance of the spiritual metaphysical world in the consciousness of the highest concrete creation of the sixth. Not without reason do we begin our יום הששי וגו׳ :קידוש.

V. 1. ויכלו. The root כלה combines two apparently opposing meanings, כלה means to be destroyed, completely cease to exist: כליתם ואתם בני יעקב לא (Malachi 3,6) “Ye sons of Jacob have not ceased to exist”; and at the same time כלה means to reach the highest degree of perfection, לכל דבריו כלה הבית (Kings I. 6,38) “the house was complete in every way”. We find the same peculiarity in the root תמם. A double significant truth may be at the root of this peculiarity. Firstly, that every perfection on one side presupposes the complete cessation in the opposite side. Anything and anybody can only be perfect in one thing if the person or thing gives itself up completely to that end. He who wishes to be perfect in various things at the same time will only be half-perfect in each of them. Further there is no such thing as absolute destruction. All ceasing to be is only relative, is only the complete transition to another condition and form. (Matter is indestructible (I.L.).

— The fundamental conception of כלה is: to strive for a certain end, hence תכלית: the end: the purpose, תכלה, striving towards achieving a goal. לכל תכלה ראיתי קץ, “for every striving towards any end there is a limit”, there is no end to which one may devote everything else, מאוד רחבה מצרתך, “only to fulfill God’s Commandment is an end which is all-embracing and all-demanding” (Ps. 119,96). Hence also כלה: to long for an end and כלי: anything which serves a definite purpose, tool, vessel, clothes etc. בַּלֵה, to lead to an end, ויכלו: they were brought to their destined end.

Just as the first word of the history of creation called us to look at heaven and earth, and let us hear the great fact that quite at the beginning God had created this heaven and this earth, so now at the conclusion of the history of the creation we are again brought to consider the heaven and earth and told the equally great Word ויכלו, they had been brought to this end! They had not always been there, they became! and before they “became”, their existence and their being in existence was there as an end in the thoughts of their Originator. Of heaven and earth, of the whole universe, at one time there was nothing in existence except as a thought in the Mind of their Originator. The cause of heaven and earth’s existence does not lie in themselves, they themselves are not the cause of their having come into existence — the most contradictory, unthinkable, completely unimaginable thought! — the cause of their existence lies external to them. They are not the result of some force working blindly, but the work of One thinking Being, creating them with intention and purpose; ויכלו!

Our sages teach us to take this conception even more poignantly. See, they teach, המעשים היו מותהין והולכיז, matter and forces which had been called into existence were in a state of continuously progressive evolution and development, ויכלו, then God set a goal and limit to their development, then He was שדי, He, שאמר לעולמו די, Who called “it is sufficient” to His world. שאלמלא אמר לשמים וארץ די עד עכשיו היו מותחין והולכיז, had He not called His “enough” to heaven and earth, they would still be to-day in a state of continuous progressive development. (כלה) .(ב״ר י׳ ומ״ו also has the meaning, like כלא, to restrain, hold back, fence in, אל יכלה ממך Gen. XXIII. 6, ואת בניהם כלו בבית Sam. I. 6,10. These are all nuances of the same conception, to set a goal).

The ending of creation, that no new formations emerge, in a word, the Sabbath of creation, is a yet louder, more pronounced revelation of the Creator than the positive existence of heaven and earth. If, as the materialistic outlook on the world has taught in all ages, the origin of the world was due to physical causes, that there was no free-willed, thinking almighty Will active thereat, if the world has only to thank the existing forces of nature for its evolution, why then has there been a Sabbath in creation for thousands of years? Why are these forces not still working, producing almighty new things? If the causes are still to hand why is the effect missing? What has brought their creative power to an end? Just the fact that as far back as human memory goes, or records exist, no new creations have appeared, just the fact that Sabbath reigns in Creation, proves that this Sabbath was preceded by a thinking, limit-setting, all-powerful Creator, that this world is not the result of the forces of nature working with blind automatic necessity, but the work of a free-willed, free-working with full consciousness and intent, Almighty Thinking Being.

More, our sages take us round the separate spheres of the creation and show us how this די!, revealing the limit-setting almight of the Creator and Master, is stamped not only on the creation as a whole, but how the definitely fixed and sharply differentiated forms and developments of the individual kinds within the same species, reveal the Hand of a Master setting measure and limit. “Look”, they say there, “at the heaven”. The one star completes its course in twelve months, the other in twelve years, this one in thirty days, that one in thirty years, another only in 480 years. Look on the earth: how varied and yet how regular the ripening of the different plants, this fruit ripens every year, that one takes three years — everything in heaven and earth says clearly כֻלינו! A free-willed Mind and a free almighty Will rules over us, ties us down to a fixed purpose and measure, and just in this limitation and by this limitation lets us come into existence and to be what we are! ויכלו, everything is limited according to size and purpose, everything has its material and its powers and time of development and its nature measured out to it. Without a Creator, thinking directing, keeping all things in order with His almighty power, simply by a blind bound force of nature, no world, no blade of grass could have emerged. Thus ויכלו is the great Jewish protest against that materialistic point of view that denies — and has denied in all ages — a free-willed Creator for the world. Thus ויכלו is the great Jewish attestation for the creation of the world by a free, wise, almighty God.

וכל צבאם. The fact that the Jewish nation, in its most peaceful aspect, encamped round about the Sanctuary, was counted according to יוצאי צבא, that the Levites serving the Sanctuary, are designated as לעבוד עבודה באהל מועד כל הבא לצבא צבא (Numb. 4,23), finally, that the women, gathered together to bring their gifts for the Sanctuary, are called אהל מועד הצבאת אשר צבאו פתח, all do away with the idea that the word צבא necessarily implies anything military. It clearly has the basic meaning of “host”. Not every gathering of a multitude is a host in the sense of a צבא. Only such a multitude that submits itself to the will of a leader who has to command the spiritual and bodily forces of those that have joined the “host”, is called a צבא. The intelligence, the mind and will of the leader makes the multitude into a host, so that a host is a large mass commanded by the mind and will of a leader. צַוֵה means to place somebody in the sphere of your will, to direct him to his post, to make him liable, to command him.

Everything created in heaven and on earth forms one great צבא, one great host whose centre point is its Creator and Master, its Lord and Leader. Everything is placed on its post by Him. Everything has to do its part on its place with the powers given to it to accomplish its allotted task. The plan of the whole rests in the mind of the Leader. Everyone has completely fulfilled his task as long as he has faithfully carried out the Creation of the whole which has been entrusted to him. Great and small, none stand where they do stand by their own authority, and none stand for themselves alone. We all belong to the one great host of God. His is the power, and the greatness, and the insight, and the command, ours the obedience, the punctuality, the faithfulness, the keenness and the work. No one has the right to be proud or conceited. The greatest that any single one can accomplish is but a fraction of the whole; but even the smallest is not lost or overlooked so long as he has only faithfully done what the One Great Leader of the host expects from him. The smallest does not escape His Eye, and for His plan nothing is superfluous or insignificant. — הלא צבא לאנוש על ארץ “everyone on earth is in “military service”, כל ימי צבאי איחל עד בוא חליפתי “all the days of my service I must stand fast until the arrival of my relief” when God will call me away and lead me to another post. (Job 8,1, XIV, 14).

V. 2. There is another conception, closely connected with that of צבא, which we meet in this verse. Everything which God created is called מלאכה .מלאכתו is not work looked on as labour or toil, but מלאכה is work looked on as something done, accomplished. Working is a term which only looks on the labour, on the greater or lesser effort of an activity, without consideration of the result, the product; מלאכה only considers the result, the product of the activity. But מלאכה is simply the feminine of מלאך. What מלאך is personally, מלאכה is factually. Just as מלאך, a messenger, is the bearer and executor of the thought and intention of another, so מלאכה is a thing which has become the bearer and executor of the thought and intention of a mind. Every material to which a directing mind has given a form conforming to a definite purpose, by being given that form, becomes the מלאכה of that mind, its actual messenger, it serves as the bearer of the thought and intention of that mind. For example:— willow-twigs lie there, as such they can be used for all sorts of purposes. I weave them into a basket. Now the twigs serve exclusively the purpose I gave them by the form into which I made them. So that the twigs which I wove into a basket have become thereby my factual מלאך, my מלאכה. In a wider sense all the things which serve the purpose of an intelligent being are its מלאכה. So we find of Jacob’s property לרגל המלאכה אשר לפני (Gen. 33,14). It is clear that only an intelligent being — God — and deep beneath Him, Man, can make a מלאכה. When an animal achieves a מלאכה, its activity only becomes a מלאכה through the intelligence of a human-being who uses its strength and powers as his instrument. All that exists is here called מלאכת א׳. It is not only in itself, by its existence, the realisation of a thought of God, הגה = היה, but it goes on continuously being the bearer and realiser of the thought of God that had been implanted in it, and of which it is to be the realisation. The amount of material and forces given to each, and the form into which it is stamped, makes everything into a מלאכת ה׳. “Being” and “doing” in the whole universe is naught but a thought of God and a message from God. All human knowledge and science is, in effect, only the effort to get at the nature and meaning of life from peering into the working of this “thought of God”, and Man only thinks he does know something, when he half succeeds in getting some indication of the Divine Thought. The naturalist who denies God discloses a trace of the very God he denies, with every law, with every force, with every purpose he works out of any form or shape he investigates. Yea he denies his denial with the very step which he takes in his searching in the realm of nature. The end he seeks presupposes the thinking God Whom he denies, Who must have established the laws and brought about the results, to discover the nature of which is his desire, and some inkling of which leads him, and the discovery of which fills him with supreme joy.

“Thus the heaven and the earth and their whole host was brought by God to their destined end”. Not only the universe as a whole, but every individual part of it which was placed in space by God, was placed there for that place and endowed with forces and forms by God. “Then God completed, with the seventh day, His work that He had made, and with the seventh day He ceased from all the work that He had made”. At this record of the installation of the Sabbath in the Creation we must again remind ourselves that the people to whom it was handed were completely conversant with the whole of the Torah. Accordingly the meaning of the seventh day as memorial of the creation of the world and of keeping the position of Man in the world, and to the world, subordinate to God, was perfectly clear to them. Without such presupposed meaning of the seventh day for Man’s cognizance of God and himself, that which is said here of the seventh day, of the Creation being completed by it, its blessing and its sanctification, would be completely ununderstandable. The visible concrete world was completed on the sixth day, but it was only on the seventh day, by instituting the seventh day for the education of mankind to truth and morality, that God, in truth, completed His work. Only with it, with its establishment, and through it, the ensuring of Man’s education for his great calling, did God cease from all His work. With the establishment of Sabbath, all the work of the creation — not only Man — received its final completion. The Sabbath was the last touch which the Finger of God, its Creator, laid on every one of His creations that He had formed in the visible world. For the continuance and the calling of every one of His Works is associated with the realisation of the Sabbath in the lap of mankind. There is no gulf between physical nature and the spiritual world and the calling of Man. God set Sabbath in the visible physical world as its purpose and its completion. “Adama”, to be the base and realm for Man, Man, ruling the world morally in the likeness of God, according to His Will, is the function of the earth. It is entrusted to him, to the “Adam”, as a wife to her husband; the whole physical world rejoices and blooms with the moral happy blossoming of the race of men, it mourns and withers when the race of men withers morally and degenerates. That is a fact that runs right through the Word of God down to the last prophet, it has its root in our record here of the installation of the Sabbath. God completed the Creation with Sabbath for Man; the appointment of Sabbath for Man was the last act that the Finger of God impressed on every one of His created works.

וישבת. The conception “rest” does not contain the whole meaning of the root שבת .שבת is no complete inactivity, שבת is the cessation of, leaving off, an activity that has been going on until then. The phonetic relationship to שבט ,שפד ,שפט ,שפת ,שות nevertheless gives this root a positive meaning also. All these roots have the common underlying idea of bringing and keeping something in the place where it belongs; hence, placing, arranging in order, directing, a skewer, a rod or staff. Hence שבת would mean such a “halt” in an activity, through which persons and things are kept in the position, the setting, in which they should be, which is due and proper for them. The kind of activity which is to find its end indicated by the root שבת is therefore always either a disturbing fermenting one as תשביתו חמץ ,משבית מלחמות ,והשבתי היה רעה והשבתי גאון זדים, etc., or one which is still unfinished, has still to be completed as מלאכתו וישבת ביום השביעי מכל .שביתה ממלאכה, with the seventh day God ceased from all the work He had done, for with the seventh day everything had reached the place in the Creation where it was always to be; God ceased, because no further alteration was necessary. And שבת was to teach Man too, to consider himself and the world in their true position. Provided that the week’s work had been of the nature that Sabbath-laws proclaim that it should have been, — עבודה — ועשית כל מלאכתך ששת ימים תעבוד, done in the service of God — then a man can consider himself at every Sabbath as having reached his goal — מלאכתך ועשית כל — he ceases work because according to the Will of God he has done what he has to do, and with the entry of the Sabbath can lay down the completed six days’ work in homage at the feet of God — his Sabbath is a true שבת.

V. 3. ברך, blessed, as above, at the creation of animals and Man. God endowed the seventh day with the power of enduring, blossoming increasing, of an ever richer abundance of results, with the power of attaining its lofty pupose on mankind. ויקדש אותו: and He set it high and holy, unimpeachable, imperishable and eternal. קדש expresses complete firmness, unaffected by opposition, absolute. Hence קדוש: the unresisting acquiesence to everything good and noble, which nothing can disturb, that moral condition in which there is no longer any fight against the pull of the senses; and קדש the opposite, complete acquiescence in sensuality, where the opposition of one’s better self is completely extinguished, (cf. כבוד the impression of the spiritual content of capacity and כבד, that of the material; שלום, the inner spiritual harmony and שלם material totality). Hence קדוש is also that which is protected against the conception of death. The absolute pure is also the absolute eternal לו כל כתוב לחיים בירושלים מה קדוש לעולם קיים אף הם לעולם קיימים והיה הנשאר בציון והנותר בירושלם קדוש יאמר (Is. 4,3) (Sanhedrin 92a). (The opposite: חלל ,חול, that which has been killed, that which is perishable).

Thus God blessed the seventh day and made it holy, gave it the power to accomplish the spiritual and moral education of the race of men, and established this education as something that would be absolutely victorious, inviolably ensured against all confusion and death. Why? “Because בו, with this means of educating mankind, He ceased from all His work”, because it is the last, for its purpose is the goal of the whole created world, and God had called this world into existence to lead it ultimately to this goal. Had Man been created without free-will like all other creations, God’s work would have been completed with the sixth day. But because Man had been created with free-will, and this freedom — raising him even superior to angels — necessarily gives the possibility of error and going astray, he will have to be educated up to the recognition of the Truth from his own free-will and to practise goodness of his own free-will. So that although God’s work in the history of Nature was completed, His work in the history of mankind and the further continuous management of natural conditions to be His educational means for mankind had only begun with the seventh day: ב״ר י״א) ממלאכת עולמו שגת ממלאכת צדיקים ורשעים לא שבת). This education of the human race to the spiritual and moral height of being “Adam” was entrusted to the Sabbath. The whole following history of God’s managements and revelations have no other purport than to lead the Sabbath to victory, to make it ever more and more — as our sages so pithily put it — בני זוג, to create for itself ever more and more intimately related consorts. That is why He blessed it and made it holy; and the guarantee for the irrefutable achievement of this spiritual and moral purpose of the Sabbath lies in the words אשר ברא א׳ לעשות, that God had not only shaped this world for this purpose, but that He had actually created it, its material and forces, for this purpose. This repetition of ברא אשר at the conclusion of the charter of the Sabbath and of the history of the Creation is the granitic rock on which the whole rests. The same God Who has set Man to reach his goal of his own spiritually-and-morally-free-will, has of His Own Free Will — יש מאין — called the whole material and spiritual world into being. So that there can be nothing in this whole world that stands hinderingly in the way of this free-willed spiritual and moral goal of mankind; yea, which does not exactly correspond to and further the attainment of this goal. This gradual winning mankind to what is good and true was God’s purpose from the beginning. That is why the ultimate attainment of this goal is the one victory which is absolutely sure and certain.

V. 4. אלה תולדות השמים והארץ בהבראם וגו׳. This can not mean: such was, or this is, the genealogy or origin of the heaven and earth. Firstly because אלה at the beginning of a sentence as a rule refers to what follows, but nothing is said further about the origin of the heaven and earth. Then תולדות does not refer back to parents but to children. תרח, תולדות ישמעאל תולדות אדם, תולדות נח, תולדות etc. do not refer to the origin of Adam, Noah, Terah etc., but to the offspring that they had begotten, produced. Finally תולדות is just the expression for the most natural organic begetting, whereas, as we have seen, בריאה the specific growth purely out of the Will of God, creating something out of nothing, the very opposite of תולדה is stressed with such extreme emphasis on the origin of heaven and earth. There would be no more unsuitable expression for that origin than תולדה. Hence we have taken it to refer solely to the products of heaven and earth, and this embraces everything which now, after the creation is produced by the combined work of the heavens and the earth. This is accordingly the heading for the whole series of the development of the natural phenomena of the world which appear before our eyes after the creation. They are certainly the natural productions of the heavens and the earth, but it is significantly added for us: בהבראם. This whole series of the developments from the heavens and the earth which follow was contained in the Creation. The heavens and the earth do not stand in the active relation to these, their products, but in passive; not as creating godheads, but as themselves being creations. Their products seem natural to us, because they are produced according to the laws of their nature which we constantly see in action, but this nature of theirs is something that was created. The laws, according to which they work, produce and develop, are those that were implanted in them by the Creator at their creation, and all תולדות השמים והארץ were given בהבראם and have their origin in their creation. This passivity of the earth at their products — which here is expressed by the ה of the Niphal — is only realised by the thinking man. To the superficial glance throughout the ages this passivity disappears. To its eye, the ה, which to the thinker stamps passivity and feminine dependence on the heavens and the earth, is זעירא, small and disappearing, hence, according to the Massora this has also to be written small. Through the constant mighty working of His creations, the Almighty Creator Himself escapes their notice. The הבראם escapes them through the תולדות. Where they should recognise נבראים they pray to בוראים. It was only the clear-sighted mind of an Abraham that saw this ה, the dependent nature of the heavens and the earth. The recognition of this ה, which escaped the eye of the ordinary glance was his זכות, his merit, and made him the leader of the monotheistic conception of there being but One Creator and Lord of Heaven and Earth — thoughts which may lie beneath the saying of the sages (in הבראם) — (ב)הבראם, בזכות אברהם :(ב״ר י״ב is an anagram on the name אברהם I.L.).

But this thought, that the laws of Nature are something created by God, is not sufficient by itself for us to understand the further products of the heavens and the earth, or to teach us the right estimation of them. We are given another factor for our appreciation, without which we should not properly understand matters and events. This forms the contents of the second half of the verse: —

ביום עשות ה׳ א׳ ארץ ושמים. Here it says עשות not בריאה: we meet here a new name of God, ה׳; and here the earth is placed before the heavens, whereas otherwise it has always been שמים וארץ or rather השמים והארץ. Let us first try to understand what is meant by the name ה׳. Even if the deep essential nature of God which is contained in this Name must always remain unfathomable to us, we still have to figure out to ourselves what of the meaning of this Name is meant to be accessible to us. Our sages already tell us to take it as the מדת הרחמים, as the management of God exercised in love, as God being the God of Love for Humanity. This already shows us how far off the idea “Eternal” is from its real meaning, and how this conception, which this Name is usually taken to imply, is not in the least adequate, and certainly does not express anything like the whole meaning. “Eternal” is a metaphysical, transcendental conception which has scarcely any practical application to anything else, certainly not to our own lives and existence. An Eternal Being would present to us the nature of the Being in itself. To ascribe to it the quality of eternity would tell us no more than that, but would not give the slightest indication of the nature of His working and rule. The thought “Eternal” leaves our hearts cold, contains nothing for our lives, and hence has no relationship whatsoever with מדת הרחמים. The four-lettered name of God, with whatever punctuation one thinks of it — the traditional points are those under the שם אדנות with which we pronounce it — does not present itself as the present tense of an intransitive form of the Kal, but as the transitive form of the Piel or Hiphil of the root היה; not the existing one, but the one who gives, dispenses existence, causes existence, also not Who did cause existence, but Who is always ready to give new existence, and that is, in its full depth, the מדת הרחמים. God is not some eternal “Ancient One of Days” (Dan. 7,9. I.L.) Who, after He had created the world, now reposes in the depth of His eternal existence, He is עולם אלקים חיים ומלך, the living ever ruling God, from Whom not only the whole past originated, but Who grants every coming moment in accordance with the educational requirements of mankind, Who is ready to grant every moment—however much the past may have forfeited it — new fresh life out of the abundance of His Almighty Love and Compassion. אלקים is דין, is the Creator and director of the world Who gives law and order and measure and limits which must be kept. Had there been no Man created in this world, no creature gifted with freedom of will and so having the possibility to deviate from his right path, there would be no necessity for the מדת הרחמים for the development of the world. All the creations, except Man, move irrefutably along the track indicated for them in the Creation, and all the developments, all the תולדות השמים והארץ would simply be the product of the בהבראם, of the laws of growth and development which the law-giving Creator had instilled in them. With Man, endowed with freedom of will, and hence the ability to go astray, and who had first to be educated to his true high calling, the מדת הרחמים entered. The rule of God in compassionate love, which allows mankind to continue in spite of its errors, which leads it over its deviations, to the Truth, over its aberrations back to faithful attention to duty, is always ready to grant fresh life and a new future, and forms the והארץ תולדות השמים according to the contemporary requirements of the education of mankind. This method of God’s ruling, arranging the further development of the world in accordance with the deserts and requirements of mankind, is already expressed in the preceding verse by the word לעשות, and that is what is represented by the Name ה׳. As אלקים, God had created heaven and earth and fixed its development on law and order; as ה׳ He interferes with this development, and alters and regulates it every second in accordance with its purpose, the education of mankind. There, in the physical arrangement of the world, earth is dependent on the heavens; here, in the spiritual moral considerations for ruling the world, for which the physical was created, the heaven is swayed by the contemporary behaviour of mankind on earth, hence the heaven is dependent on the earth. There, it always says והארץ השמים, here, יום עשות ה׳ א׳ ארץ ושמים .ארץ ושמים is just the seventh day, on which God introduced Sabbath into the Creation, placed His whole work of heaven and earth in the service of educating Man to be “Adam”, and made the continuance and purpose of the world dependent on the realisation of such education. For with Man the Name ה׳ was added to אלקים and there are two factors which rule the further development of the world: a) the ordinary laws of nature which God had already set in the original Creation and b) the guidance and modification which the same God gives every moment to this development with reference to, and in consideration of, the behaviour of mankind. “All the natural products of the working of the heavens and the earth result firstly in accordance with their original creation, and secondly they are caused by the day that God made the earth and the heaven dependent on the free-willed deeds of Man”, and it is the Name ‘“אלקים ה״ which guides us through history.

אלה תולדות השמים והארץ בהבראם ביום עשות ה׳ אלקים ארץ ושמים “These are the given products of the heaven and the earth which were already in their creation, with the day that God, as ה׳ א׳ formed earth and heaven”. This introductory sentence to the history of the world is at the same time a protestation against any deification of nature, and against the mistake of thinking that the physical development of the world has nothing to do with the moral behaviour of mankind. The name “ה׳ אלקים״ gives us a glance at the physical and moral order of the world, and of God’s rule and His methods with nature and history. Abraham had understood the one name אלקים and undeterred by תולדות השמים והארץ, by what was going on in the world, he had come to understand this Name by hearkening to, and considering God in nature. Therefore God picked him out to teach the Name ה׳ also, His Name as the Ruler in history, the One Who creates and orders the moral world. But this name became apparent, נודע, really known, only when Abraham’s descendants had grown into a people to whom all the conditions necessary for becoming a nation, were — from the point of view of the ordinary physical order of the world — entirely lacking. They were to receive their physical existence as a nation from the Hand of God only by means of their moral behaviour which they attained by their giving themselves up to, and having faith in, God. The whole of the history of Israel is a revelation of the Name. Our response to the idea ה׳ is our moral subordination to the Will of God, the placing of the whole of our existence in His service. It is accordingly completely understandable that we call ה׳ by the name: אדנ׳ (The name ה׳ is untranslateable, we therefore propose to use the name God in italics to designate ה׳ and God in ordinary print for אלקים, which is more of an attribute than a name of God. But we must refrain from attempting to indicate in the translation, that most significant combination of both names ה׳ א׳).

V. 5. The previous verse was the introduction to the history of mankind, and showed us the further development of the world after its creation to be dependent on the existence and behaviour of Man. Then this verse takes the story back again to the moment when creation is at a standstill awaiting its further development which is dependent on Man. At the same time it shows us that the fact which is expressed in general terms in the previous verse is functioning at once with the very entry of Man into the world. It also shows us at the same time special phases in the training of Man, which give us an understanding of his nature in relation to his high position and calling in the world, which has already been mentioned in the description of his creation in the series of the other creations.

The words שדה and אדמה which occur here for the first time, show at once that we are now in the realm of mankind. Until now it has always used the general term ארץ. But שדה is that piece of ground that a man lays claim to for the purpose of obtaining food: a field. שדה could well be related to שדה the root of שד, the maternal breast, in which in a similar way, out of the general sap and juices of the body, a special part is separated out to flow for the nourishment of another being. אדמה is, in any case, the earth looked on not as a cosmic body but as being associated with man, given over as the realm of his activity. — שיח is the general name for growth. (Hence used also for the spiritual growth of Man. Our sages take it then to refer specially to prayer. Praying, looked at from this point of view, is simply drinking from the source of all spiritual life, accordingly, watering all the fibres and filaments of our inner being to produce new blossoms). שיח elsewhere generally means growth itself, vegetation, but here it can not have that meaning, for vegetation was already in existence before the sixth day when Man was created. Here it must mean the activity of growth. Plants were in existence on the third day, but they made no progress, did not grow. Rain was lacking, which God did not grant to the physical world, but to mankind, not as אלקים but as ה׳ אלקים, and Man was not yet there, Man whose moral government on earth was demanded by God, its Master, for the further development of the earth.

It is deeply significant that the activity of Man mastering the earth is called עבודה, service. עבד (related to אבד) is being completely engulfed in the purposes of someone else. At Man’s mastery over the earth he himself is directly in the service of God, but indirectly in the service of the earth although God has made him master of its uses. When Man lays claim to the forces of the earth to use them for the purposes God indicated to him, and changes it about for such uses, the earth does not lose the dignity of its original status and calling, but rather attains it thereby. By his work on it Man raises its purely physical nature into playing a part in the sphere of the moral purposes of the world. The mastery of a true “Adam” over the earth is really in truth עבודת האדמה, “serving it”, furthering its true purpose. And for this “service” of man to earth, God, ה׳ אלקים, gives rain. The actual formation of the rain itself belongs to the physical laws of nature created by אלקים. But that the rain does come, when, and where, and how it falls, that it comes לברכה and not לקללה, that, God kept back for His government of the moral world, for that which is expressed by the name ”שאלו מה׳ מטר בעת מלקוש״ ה׳. cries the Prophet Zachariah (X,1) to his contemporaries “entreat God for rain in the time of early rains”, ומטר גשם יתן להם לאיש עשב בשדה וגו׳ ה׳ עושה חזיזים “God makes the clouds and gives them showers of rain for one single man, for one single grass in the field”, (ibid.). “והיה אם שמוע תשמעו״ “if ye will hearken diligently unto my commandments says God in his Torah (Deut. 11,13) ונתתי מטר ארצכם בעתו, I will give the rain of your land in its right time; but if your hearts be deceived, and ye turn aside from God ועצר את השמים, then God will close up the heavens and there will be no rain”. This relationship between rain and morality, spoken of the Jewish people and the Jewish land, the land of the Torah, the land of the Divine laws of morality, is accordingly no exceptional case, nothing unnatural. It is rather what was originally appointed for the human world and for its earth, and the condition to which both will return ultimately when the human race will submit itself to the Divine laws of morality. So that here, in our verse, the fact is given, which our sages express in their dictum, that rain is one of the things the responsibility for which God did not hand over to a שליח, to a messenger. All the forces which work in nature, acting as God’s messengers לא יסבו בלכתן, go unalterably on their straight unswerving appointed path. Thus for instance, the sun, that great factor in the development and blossoming of life on earth. Its path rests on mathematically precise laws, לא יסבו בלכתן, there, there is no turning aside, no change brought about by the changing requirements of the education of men. Nature goes her way. But not everything is handed over to the ways of nature. The gift of rain, the whole formation of the atmospherical downfall and the whole formation of the atmosphere which is caused by it, which modifies to such a large extent the effect of the sun’s rays on the earth, and makes it seem alterable, the מפתח של גשמים, the “key of the rain”, God retained for the moral ruling of His governing the world for mankind. “ירעם אל בקולו נפלאות״, God thundereth with His Voice in wonders, great things doeth He, where we notice it not; for He saith to snow: Be thou on the earth, and rain is of His sending, yea, rains are the manifold sendings of His Might. Thereby He lays His seal in the hand of every man, that all men may observe His work (Job. 37,5) — So, as Man was not yet there, there was also no rain, and vegetation still awaited its first development.

ואד יעלה “and vapour rose continuously from the earth and watered the whole surface of the soil”. This watering of the earth can not have taken the place of rain, for just before we have been told that because of the rain, the plants had not begun to grow. So that watering of the earth can only be taken as being probably only the preliminary preparation for the following cultivation by Man. From the day the earth with its plant-world stood ready for the reception of Man, it awaited his arrival and was constantly kept in a state of preparation for his work on it.

V. 7. וייצר ה״א וגו׳. In this sentence the whole secret of the nature of Man is laid down, and the whole higher dignity and the whole calling of Man rest on the facts revealed here. It has struck many commentators as remarkable that the dignity of man seems here to be concentrated in the fact that he became נפש חיה, a character which is borne by the whole of the rest of the living world down to the tiniest insect. But the salient point of this verse does not lie in נפש חיה, but in ויהי האדם לנפש חיה: so Man became a נפש חיה. Not that Man became a living individual being, but the manner in which he did so, is what raised him so high and made him different from all the other living creatures.

יצר .יצר is to the material what יסד is to the spirit and feelings. Both mean to confine spiritual or material matter in a fixed direction for a fixed purpose. The one is the business of spiritual and moral education and culture, the other the formation and shaping material matter. Both again are related to ישר which means the shortest and most direct direction to an end: the straight line.

So here we read: — ד׳ א׳ the Creator and Director of the world — Who is about to introduce with Man a further higher development of the world He has created — formed Man “dust from the soil, and He breathed in his countenance the breath of life, then the Man became a living creature.” At the creation of the other living creatures it says: תוצא הארץ נפש חיה, let the earth bring forth living creatures. At the creation of plant and animal life the earth was active and from it came forth not only the body of the animal, but the whole life. The earth brought forth the actual living individual creature. Not so with Man. At the creation of Man, even at the creation of his body, the earth was passive. Its activity for the formation of Man was before Man was created. Since it had come into existence it had to water itself every day to prepare the material for the noblest of the creations. With this preparation it had reached the zenith of its work. The material for the human body was its culminating and noblest product. From that point onwards the earth was not active at the creation of the body of Man. It is ה׳ א׳ who forms the human body. Here again is stressed the special dignity of even the body of a human being, as it was above in Ch. I. 26,27. But even after the formation of the body had been made, Man was still עפר. It does not say God formed Man מן עפר, out of dust of the earth, but את האדם עפר מן האדמה וייצר ה׳, He formed him, dust of the earth. That which God formed of earth into Man, was only that which was עפר, earthly on him, comes from the earth, is earthly, and like dust, falls back again into earth. Human life, that which lives in Man, God did not take from the earth. Lifeless עפר, lay the body formed for the future Man, then ה׳ א׳ breathed the breath of life into his countenance and thus Man became a living creature. What is tre difference between Man and Beast? At animals the living individuality of the creature adheres to the earthly material, like the body so the soul too came forth from the earth. At Man only the dead material came from the earth, and it was only the Breath of God which made it into a living individual. That is where the freedom, the immortality, the whole greatness of Man comes from. All that makes an animal into an individual life comes from the earth and returns to earth. Not so that which makes a man alive. Not only the soul, also the force of life is something different, something higher in Man to that in animal. It too is attached, not to the body, but to the spirit He only received life with the spirit, and his soul adheres to the spirit. When the spirit leaves the body, life is not included in the coffin, for life adheres to the spirit. That is why his earthly material existence, his health is also not dependent solely on the body. That which kills an animal does not necessarily, on that account, kill a man; the life of a man, and whether he will survive or not can not be estimated with the same certainty as that of an animal can be. אדם יש לו מזל, there is something in Man that goes beyond ordinary reckoning, and even when everything else seems gone, a Man can go on living by his spirit, by sheer force of will alone. Thus Man has in himself the combination of two completely different beings. The one belongs to the earth. But just as Man does not belong to the earth, but the earth is אדמה, is given over to him for his use, for his rule, so the little bit of עפר מן אדמה of which his body is formed, is to be subservient to the true Man. His real spiritual living self does not cling to the earth, and even during the time it is combined with it, Man can and should master and rule over that which is earthly in him. That which is עפר, earthly in him can not as such avoid belonging to the realm of the unfree, and, as such, is subject to the effects of physical factors. But that which makes him into a Man, the נשמת חיים which ה׳ א׳ gave with His breath, makes it partake of the nature of its origin, raises it above all the forces of physical necessity, makes him free, and able to raise the body with it into the realm of freedom.

Further, it is very significant that it says here that God breathed the soul of life into his countenance. It does not say בפניו but באפיו. The root of אף and אפים would not be אנף but אפף, which means to pant, greedily to want to absorb something. Hence אף, also, if something preceding is so strong that it draws something which follows into its sphere (cf. גם from גמא). Related to אפף is אבב, the stalks greedily drawing in sap from the ground, hence אב and אביב. Hence אפים means the opening of the body through which men greedily take in the stream of life necessary for the maintenance of life, i.e. the nose, and also used in a broad sense, in general, the striving, wishing, longing, face, hence ארך אפים patience, קצר אפים impatience, and אף unsatisfied desire, anger. But פנים in general, is the face turned in any direction. Hence also preferably השתחוה אפים ארצה to submit to somebody with all one’s desires and efforts. And בזעת אפיך תאכל לחם, not אפים .פניך, the effort to absorb the world in oneself, to gain a little piece of the universe to oneself, is the object of all work. In the original position of Man in גן עדן the world responded readily and cheerfully to such efforts. Since the gates of Paradise closed behind him Man can only gain, even the necessities of life, by the sweat of effort and exertion. — So that here lay the body of Man, inert and lifeless, his countenance open to take in, like an animal, the requirement of individual life. Into this countenance God breathed for him the breath of life. Inasmuch as here the requirement of life was blown into him through his head into his countenance, Man was raised, in his outward appearance too, above all creatures in the world. By that he is a complete contrast to plants. Plants have the condition for living from below, out of the earth; animals have the condition for living in the centre, the heart; man in the head. Man looks upward, all his forces are above, when he hopes, when he wishes, when he thinks. The life breathed into his countenance bears the man, keeps him upright; with the disappearance of his spirit he falls.

Our sages also draw our attention to the spelling of וייצר with the י doubled it is the only case in which the radical י appears prominently. They are inexhaustible in giving meaning to this double י in which they see the ב׳ יצירות, the dual nature of Man indicated. For he combines mortal and immortal, earthly and heavenly, has יצר טוב and יצר הרע combined within him, he is created for עה״ז and וייצר .עולם הבא: the one י is sounded, the other quiescent, one יצירה is audible, the other quiescent. Man’s appearance is always a double one. One form is always predominant, but it does not remove the other, the other is always there. The loftiest man still belongs to the earth, in the lowest one can see glimmerings of humanity shining through. Even the loftiest deed of the יצר טוב will not deny the fight it had to conquer the יצר רע and vice versa. Thanks are due to them for bringing the fact to our notice that Man was formed right from the beginning for these two impulses. For the יצר הרע sensuality (the temptation to follow the attraction of the senses. I.L.) in itself is not רע. Every inclination, as long as the מיוסר is from the יוצר is pure and holy. וייצר, the same One Who created the one inclination, created the other. Man, אדם, the “red one”, is not the white ray, he is the “broken up” pure white godly light, combined with the earthly; he is not מלאך but אדם; has to carry out his godly moral task, primarily not בע׳ הבא but in this material world of the senses with his sensuous nature. This world of the senses and this sensuous nature of Man does not belong to Satan and does not originate from Satan. That idea is a contorted conception which has been invented to the curse of Mankind. Jewish teaching shows Man with both inclinations coming from God’s Hands, for Man is just to be a creature where the divine, the heavenly, is joined to the earthly, the spiritual to the material, the immortal to the mortal.

V. 8. Not אלקים, but ה׳ א׳ — God’s providence for the education of Man — planted the garden. גן (from גנן, to protect, guard), a fenced-in place, enclosed for human purposes. (In German, English and other languages too, the word, Garten, garden, jardin is derived from gard, to protect, guard). עדן designates the highest satisfaction, usually of material demands of people. Here it positively refers to a place down here on earth, indeed the exact topographical position is given later on. — וישם שם is not merely placing there, but indicating the position he was to occupy. What is here in this verse told in general terms, כלל, is explained in detail in the following verses. The garden itself is described, and we are told that its occupation is not granted unconditionally. But we learn already here, and it is repeated in V. 15, that Man was created outside Paradise, and that he was destined, already in this life here below, to live in a Paradise. This earthly Paradise is, already here below, the destiny for Man and the earth. We are shown what we should be, how we should live, how this world of ours would form a paradise for us, if we would be that which we should be. A similar lesson was to be repeated on a reduced scale for a small sample, chosen as an example for the whole human race, in ארץ ישראל which was also to be a גן עדן for the People of God’s Law. It was meant to show the world a second time, by its prosperity and progress, what an abundance of blessing and happiness would be attained here on earth when the Will of God is taken as the sole measure for arranging all phases of human life.

V. 9. It should not be overlooked that here, in the description of the laying-out of the garden for human requirements, נחמד למראה, satisfying the sense of beauty precedes טוב למאכל that of the sense of taste and the requirements for food. It gives justification for, and dedication to, the aesthetic, the sense of appreciating beauty, and this too, may confirm the higher stage designed for Man. The abundance of beauty of every kind which we are given in this, our world, and the fact that — as far as we know — Man is the only creature that has been provided with the ability to enjoy beauty for itself, proves what value the Creator lays on this aesthetic sense for the spiritual-moral calling of Man. Indeed this beauty of nature showered in every form all over the world, and the sense of enjoyment which Man derives from it, is one of the first means to protect Man from complete brutalisation. Joy in the beauties of Nature and the beauties of form, which God has lavished especially on plant-world, forms a bridge towards what is spiritually and morally beautiful.
