In surroundings where no consideration is given to harmony and beauty, Man too easily grows up wild and unruly. The feeling which gives one joy in harmony and order is related to the feeling for order and harmony in the sphere of morality, so much so that evil and bad appear to us as רע (from רעע to break into pieces. I.L.) as something broken, the harmony disturbed, where one single thought no longer rules the whole.

עץ החיים. As we read at the end of the catastrophe, that Man, in his degeneracy is not to achieve living for ever by eating the fruit of this tree, we can deduce from that, that this fruit must have had the ability constantly to restore and completely regenerate ever afresh the forces of Man. ועץ, and yet another tree stood in the midst of the garden, the properties of its fruit are not told us, but its detailed description is given as: הדעת טוב ורע. It can scarcely be the right assumption to make, that only by eating its fruit, Man would receive the knowledge of good and evil, but before that he did not have the ability to distinguish between good and bad, or that — as some of our philosophical writers teach — until then he stood only at the stage of the theoretical differentiation of truth and falsehood, but the conception “good and bad” which belongs to the faculty of practical judgement was entirely lacking in him. As sure as freedom of will formed the specific fundamental character of the human in Man, so certain is it that he could not be Man without the conception of good and its opposite. Had the whole conception of moral good and bad been lacking to Man, God could not have given him any prohibition and could not have called him to account and punished him for transgressing it. Both must assume that the one, to whom the prohibition is issued, has the knowledge of duty, of what is in accordance with right and what is wrong; and that is nothing else but the knowledge of good and evil, a knowledge which does indeed belong to the faculty of practical and not theoretical decision. But rather the tree הדעת טוב ורע, was so designated — as so often סופו על שם, already beforehand according to the final result — as the tree by which the decision of the knowledge of good and evil was made, through which the man would decide how he wished to recognise what was good or bad. There is only one condition for the earth to be able to form a paradise for us, and the condition is this, that we only call that good, which God stamps as being good, and bad, which He declares as such. But not that we leave the decision between good and bad to our senses. If we place ourselves under the dictate of our senses, the gates of Paradise are closed to us and only by a long way round can Man regain admittance thereto. Yea the tree could have been called the “Tree of Knowledge of good and evil” inasmuch as it was to represent to Man what good and evil was to be to him, what he was to recognise as good or bad. The tree, as we shall see later, was endowed with every attraction for taste, for the imagination, sight, and reasoning judgment, all one’s senses declared it “good”, that it should be eaten, and yet God had forbidden it to be eaten, was accordingly designated “bad” for Man. The tree, accordingly, was constantly to remind him of the teaching on which the realisation of the whole purity and height of his calling depends. The teaching that, according to the judgement of his bodily senses, his mind and understanding, a thing may appear absolutely good, yea the very best, and still to take it may be contrary to the high calling of Man, may still be judged by God as a capital crime. The teaching that Man is to recognize what is good and bad, not by the judgement of his senses or his own mind, but by accepting the will of God when it has been revealed to him, and that he must take such judgement of God as the one guide he is to follow, if he wishes to fulfil his mission on earth and remain worthy for the world to be a Paradise for him.

V. 10.—14. These four streams have been repeatedly sought for, and some of them have been recognised, as especially חדקל and פרת which are considered to be definitely the Tigris and Euphrates. (By the way, the Tigris flows to the west of Assyria). The geographical description in our verse has been criticised because it has been taken to refer to a river which divides into four streams, and no such river has been found. But perhaps the fact has been overlooked that ראשים does not mean branches, but four separate heads. The river described starts as a single stream. But outside Eden, after it has watered the garden, it evidently disappears into the ground, and breaks out again in four different places as four separate rivers. Moreover the description refers to rivers and places which, at the time the Torah was handed over, were well-known. Four districts seem to be named which, each in its way, yielded the richest of products. All the riches and all the abundance which lay separately in these lands were found together in Paradise.

V. 15. ויניחהו is not simply placing, it always has the underlying idea of letting go, conceding, setting free. God had formed him, and after that he was still in God’s Hand’s; God let him go, be free, trusted him to himself for the first time, and gave him the ג״ע to work and to guard. Even when the earth is made into a Paradise for Man, he is only to thank his own faithful, dutiful activity for it, the difference in Paradise is only that this activity is met with the richest, untroubled blessing and success. It must be noticed that, with one single exception, גן is always masculine, so that the feminine suffixes in this verse are striking. One can find an analogy for this in Song of Songs IV. 16 הפיחי גני. But perhaps the suffixes here refer to עדן which, as an abstract noun, can well be feminine gender. “God transposed him to a garden of delight, of happiness, to serve and to guard this happiness”, by faithfully fulfilling his task, he is to keep this happy condition (לשמרה I.L.) and to raise it ever higher and higher (לעבדה I.L.). In any case the terms עבודה and שמירה include not only the direct work and care of the ground, but also the whole moral behaviour of Man in acting and refraining from acting in accordance with his duty. Indeed, as already indicated earlier, Nature itself finds its appointed purpose promoted, as well as the necessary condition for its continuance, in Man’s conscientious dutiful use of the bounties of nature, as expressed by עבודה ושמירה. Our sages too refer this conception here, to תורה ומצות, accordingly to the general mission of mankind.

V. 16 & 17. With this prohibition the education of Man for his moral, high godly calling begins. It is the beginning of the history of mankind, and shows all following generations the path they are to tread. It is a prohibition, and it is not a so-called “reasonable prohibition”, no מצוה שכלית, but rather one which all the human means of judgment would speak against; taste, sight, appeal to imagination and mind, are all in favour of eating the fruit. Of oneself one would never have come to forbid it, and even after the prohibition no other reason for it could possibly have been found than the absolute Will of God, accordingly a חוק in optima forma. Furthermore it is a dietary law, and it reached the one to whom it applied only by way of tradition, oral communication. It was given to Adam, and Eve was to obey it. Accordingly, it was: — תורה שבעל פה ,מאכלות אסורות ,חוק ,מצות לא תעשה, had all the points at which — in the words of our sages — יצר רע and אומות העולם, the understanding and judgment of our senses, and the non-Jewish world, take umbrage and have always resented. All these points were combined in the prohibition which God made at the beginning of the development of the human race לדעת טוב ורע, so that by it would be known what Man would call “good”, and what he would avoid as “bad”. This was to establish the condition for all morality as being subordinating the dictates of our senses to the expressed will of God, a condition which is inseparable from, and forms a part of, the morally high station and calling of Man. Moral freedom, freedom of will, that fundamental palladium of the greatness of Man, itself is unthinkable without the ability to sin, and the ability to sin presupposes irrefutably that evil does have an attraction to our senses, and that goodness finds opposition in them. Otherwise the choice of “good” and the avoidance of “bad” would be instinctive in Man as it is in animals, and human beings would not be “men”. In this mastering sensual urges, in this subordinating his sensual nature to the Will of God, human beings rise to be “men”, and exercising self-control is the first problem of human education, which received its first principle from the Education of Man just in this first command. At every demand of God’s laws of morality, still today, every one of us stands, like the first human pair, before the tree of this knowledge and has to decide whether he will follow the voice of his bodily sensuality, his own judgment and sense, and the wisdom of instictive animal life, or, conscious of his higher calling, the voice of his God. And still today this voice of God is not revealed directly to us, but only through tradition, even as God entrusted His first command to Man to verbal tradition. According to the teaching of our sages, the codex of the laws of morality for mankind in general, the seven Noachian Laws, also rest on the Divine revelation which ר׳ יוחנן (Sanhedrin 56b.) finds indicated already in this first pattern of a prohibition: —, עץ הגן ולא גזל ,אכל תאכל ולא אבר מן החי ה׳ זו ברכת ה׳, אלקים זו עבודה זרה, על האדם זו שפיכת דמים, לאמר זו גלוי עריות, מכל ויצו אלו הדינין. A closer consideration of this first declaration of a Law of God may perhaps make this comment of ר׳ יוחנן seem not so far-fetched.

דינין = ויצו. We have already recognized צוה having the meaning of “appointing someone to his post”, (from its relation to צבא and צוה). Thus our sages see everywhere in צווי not merely a simple command but, as they put it, זירוז מיד ולדורות, a spur for zeal that what is commanded shall be carried out in the present and in all future time. (ספרי נשא). So that in צווי there lies not only the duty to oneself to carry out what is commanded but the mission to see to it that it is generally carried out. The first receiver of the Law was accordingly automatically appointed as guardian of the Law, and this applies to every man to whom a צווי is addressed. But this is nothing but the first Noachian duty: דינין, administration of justice, the care for the general laws of morality being observed by mankind. (In parenthesis it may be noted that hereby the state receives a much higher moral meaning than by any idea of their making civil laws out of necessity or expediency).

ברכת ה׳ = ה׳. The Law was given to Man in the name of ה׳, in that Name which designates a special relation to Man, the Love of God educating Man to his ultimate moral spiritual happiness. But the whole consciousness of duty being encumbent on Man rests on the consciousness of this special relation of Man to God, and on his keeping that consciousness in undisturbed holiness. So that together with the declaration of Man’s duty by virtue of this Name, the duty of keeping this Name holy is automatically given, which of course implies the prohibition of blasphemy: ברכת ה׳.

ע״ז = אלקים. But as ה׳ is at once given as אלקים, the Lawgiver to Man as the One Who gave and fixed law and order to all His other creations in nature, so that all the other creations — however great and powerful they appear — obey Him, being only His creations and servitors, thereby the deification of any other being is automatically denied and forbidden: ע״ז.

צזה .שפיכת דמים = על האדם is not usually construed with על. When על is used, it generally refers not to the person to whom the command is given, but to the person or thing that is to be affected by the command. Thus ועל פעל ידי תצוני ,ויצו עליו פרעה אנשים. Where it does refer to the person to whom the command is given, as כי מרדכי צוה עליה, and indeed here too, then — as has been remarked long ago — as a rule it is a prohibition. But nevertheless exceptions to this rule can also be found, as אצוה על חגב לאכול והן (Chron. II. 7,13). This peculiarity seems to be due to the idea that when על refers to the person to whom the command is given, that person is the object concerning which he is given a duty. He is given the duty to watch על over himself, to see that he does not do that which the command forbids him to do. It is the same idea as השמד, keeping guard over oneself, which always introduces a prohibition. So that here too, as Man is at the same time designated as the object which is to be affected by the command (על I.L.) as well as the person to whom the command is given, and at the same time the command is a limitation of the exercise of his free will in eating, i.e. a limitation in the use of his own bodily power and even to the material he is to feed it with, this automatically brings him to the conclusion: — if even my own body is not my own, but is the property of God, and I am responsible to Him for even the smallest material with which I build it up, certainly then, the whole body of another person and the whole of my own must be God’s holy property, regarding which I must restrain any capricious destruction: שפיכת דמים.

לאמר .גלוי עריות = לאמר in the Torah is always the task of handing on the most precise contents of what one has received. See Sifra I. Thus God gave Man His command to hand it on from generation to generation. But this is only possible if young human beings find fathers and mothers who do hand the Law to them and bring them up to observe it. That is why our sages, when asked for the reason why God chose Israel to be the bearers of His Torah, always replied in the first instance that it was because their family-life had blossomed in sexual moral purity, and referred to the oft-repeated census of the people למשפחותם לבית אבותם. The continued conservation of the Torah accordingly reckons on sexually pure families, and לאמר prohibits: גלוי עריות.
ולא מן הגזל = מכל עץ הגן. Man is only to eat from the garden which is fenced-in for him, but not מן הגזל.

אכל) ,אכל תאכל ,ולא אבר מן החי = אכל תאכל as already remarked above, כלה with the prefixed א) what we eat is to be אכילה, it is to be material suitable to be consumed, suitable to be absorbed into our person, to become part of the wrapper in which the godly spirit in encased. Hence, at once בשר בהמה .ולא אבר מן החי can indeed be raised to בשר אדם, but נפש בהמה can never be assimilated to נפש אדם. The נפש בהמה must first be separated from the בשר בהמה before the animal body may be absorbed into the human body, hence: אכל תאכל but not אבר מן החי (See תוספות Sanhedrin 56b. אכל תאכל ד״ה).

V. 17. “On the day that thou eatest thereof thou must die”. Probably only: you are liable to death, for actually they did not die immediately, but rather as a result of their non-observance of the divine prohibition, death was to be their ultimate fate. The exact nature of death is recognized, even to-day, as a problem of physiology which is still not solved. One day, when mankind will ultimately have worked its way completely back to God, we are told that death will disappear from the world (Is. 25,8) According to the teaching of the חכמים this period would have started for Israel with מתן תורה, if Israel would only have fulfilled God’s Laws with absolute devotion (ע״ז, 5, a). But it is possible that the decree מות תמות was actually carried out immediately. For we do find elsewhere too that banishment from home takes the place of, and is imposed in lieu of the death penalty, as for instance in the case of Cain, and with the unpremeditated manslaughter. Banishment from home is death on a reduced scale. Death itself is not a termination of existence, but only a termination of existence here. And so banishment from Paradise may have been death in a milder form. For we can form no conception of what life in ג״ע is really like. Between that and the ordinary life out in the world there may be such a break, such a gulf, that the transition from one to the other may have been not dissimilar to our departure from this world to the next world.

V. 18. In the same way as Creation tarried and waited its completion before Man was created, and God had announced to it this crown of His creation, so was the case here before the creation of Woman. Man was there, and all about him all the beauties of paradise blossomed, and still God did not pronounce His “טוב״! It does not say: לבדו לא טוב לאדם היותו, that it was not good for man to be alone, but לא טוב היות האדם לבדו “this is not good, Man being alone” as long as Man stands alone it is altogether not yet good, the goal of perfection, which the world is to attain through him will never be reached as long as he stands alone. The completion of the “good” was not Man but Woman, and it was only brought to mankind and the world by Woman. And this fact has been so deeply appreciated by those “orientals”, the “rabbis”, that they teach in the Talmud: only through his wife does a man become a “Man”, only husband and wife together are “Adam”. A task which is too great for one person must be divided, and just for the accomplishment of the whole of Man’s mission, God created Woman for Man. And this Woman is to be עזר כנגדו. Even looked at quite superficially this designation expresses the whole dignity of Woman. It contains not the slightest reference to any sexual relationship, she is placed purely in the realm of Man’s work, it was there that she was missing, she is to be עזר כנגדו. And עזר כנגדו certainly expresses no idea of subordination, but rather complete equality, and on a footing of equal independence. Woman stands to Man כנגדו, parallel, on one line, at his side.

עזר, to help, assist. Considered in the light of its corelated roots, peculiarly contradictory ideas appear which all have the underlying conception of restricting, confining, limiting; עצר ,אצר ,אסר ,אזר, and yet עזר, to help. So that עזר designates that kind of help which relieves the other from a part of his obligations (division of labour I.L.), allowing him thereby to concentrate his efforts to a smaller sphere of activity, and so to accomplish what is left to him in a more complete and perfect manner. It is a help by limiting and thus concentrating. Whereas עצר implies forcible (עזר ,(צ is the welcome restriction so as to be able to use one’s activities more powerfully in the restricted sphere so afforded. Thus the auxiliary hall was called the עזרה. Instead of the קרבנות having to be offered in the היכל, as otherwise would be the case, the עזרה allowed the היכל to be reserved for the highest כפרה, and all the ways that lead up to כפרה to be demonstrated in the “auxiliary” hall. In a similar way, the wife too is to take over a part of the obligations which comprise the great task of mankind, and thus make it possible for her husband to accomplish more perfectly the part that is left to him. But this is only possible if the being who is to be an עזר to him is כנגדו not עמו, does not work at what he is doing, but works opposite him. Were the other being a man, he himself would have all the obligations upon his own shoulders, and he would again need “help”. That is is why it is אשה, a “feminine man”, who stands, not with him, but next to him, נגדו, who works at another point in the same line, so that each one of them fills a separate position, and they mutually complement each other.

V. 19. ויצר, according to the sages in ב״ר, not to be taken as “formed”, for the creation and formation of animals took place before that of mankind, but in the meaning of כבוש, mastering, forcing, as in עיר תצור אל. Although the underlying conception of תצור from צרר is to limit, constrain, press, cramp, so indeed is that of יצר. All forming is a compression of the material into the encompassment of the desired form. יצר itself occurs with the meaning of stress, strait, מן המיצר ,ויצר לו etc. This way of taking ויצר as “forcing” seems confirmed by the fact that בהמה is missing here and only חית השדה (the wild animals) and עוף (birds) are mentioned, while in V.20, בהמה is specifically mentioned. בהמה would not have to be forced to be brought to Man, by their nature they submit themselves to Man, and of their own free will live in human surroundings. The position in the verse of the term נפש חיה shows that it is to be taken as being in apposition to האדם: Man gives things names, not as God, Who sees things objectively as they truly are, but as נפש חיה, subjectively, from his own point of view as a נפש an individual, חיה, who receives the acceptable or rejectable impression of the things about him. It is according to the impression they make on him, that he gives things names. In these names he expresses the impression which his imagination forms of things, and thereby he indicates their שָׁם (hence the word שֵׁם) place in his world, ranks them in the appropriate kind, species etc. of things. All our knowledge of things is such a name-giving. But this knowledge is only subjective, is only אשר יקרא לו האדם נפש חיה, how a man calls things for himself, לו, what they are to him. What things really are, the true nature of things in themselves, no human eye sees. But although the נפש חיה does refer back to the whole limited extent of human knowledge, nevertheless scepticism is opposed by the assurance which the addition of הוא שמו gives, that, even if that which we know from the impression things make on us is not the whole truth of the real nature of things, still it does contain the truth. God, Who created Man and things, and led His created creatures to Man for him to give them names according to the impression they made on him, also guarantees men that the amount of knowledge of the nature of things which is granted to him, is no deception. That this fraction of the truth is also true, and is as much of the truth of the real true nature of things that he requires in his association with things for the accomplishment of his mission on earth, and that he may safely have confidence in it. Thus belief in God Who created men and things forms an essential foundation also to our theoretical knowledge. Without this belief, theoretical scientific knowledge can not escape hopeless scepticism, has no guarantee that they are not deducing a dream from a dream, and proving a dream by a dream.

That this name-giving did rest on a recognition — even if only a subjective one — of the nature of things is evident from the fact that here God led all the living creatures to Man, so that he could recognize that among all these living creatures there was not one that was suitable to step to his side as the missing helpmate, as is proved by the concluding words of the next verse: לאדם לא מצא עזר כנגדו. Testing the creatures for this purpose is called: לראות מה יקרא לו האדם. So may we translate these words: to see how he would call it for himself, or how he would name it, or what he would appoint it to be for himself.

קרא means: to call, i.e. to summon something to come towards us (from which לקראת also comes, literally to give the direction which is to be taken up by the one who is called) hence also “to name”. By naming anything I call it up to my mind, bring it mentally before me. Possibly ירא is also related to it, which might account for the fact that although it designates an intransitive condition it is construed with the objective את. It would then mean: to hold something always present in one’s mind. This is actually the fact with fear and the one true יראת ה׳ is שויתי הי לנגדי תמיד.

V. 20. Thus Man tested all living creatures in their characteristics and listed them in his mind according to what they impressed him as being, and so gave them names, placed them in his mind. He did this to the animals that were nearest to him (בהמה) and to those that were farther off from him (חיה) as well as to those that are least submissive to him (עוף), but for an “Adam”, (it does not say ולָאדם, the man), a vice-regent of God on earth, he found none that would be parallel to himself, none that could share his obligations with him.

V. 21. רדם .תרדמה, related to רתם which occurs as a verb המרכבה רתם (Micah I. 13) where it means “bind firmly”. So that it is possible that רדם has the underlying meaning of binding fast, and הרדם designates that completely bound condition in which people lose every possibility of moving, all independence, something like anaesthesia. This degree of loss of power is not present in ישן, the term denoting ordinary sleep. ישן, basic meaning: old, also black, dark, hence אישן לילה and אישון בת עין, the darkness of night, and the eyeball. Accordingly, to be dark, without sparkle, without light, and to age; accordingly, to lose sparkle, strength, freshness; and ישן, as sleep, is the condition of being asleep, languid, whereas תרדמה indicates the condition of being completely fettered. Perhaps the tree under which Elijah fell asleep (Kings I. XIX) was one which had some narcotic effects and on that account was called צלע — .רתם does not occur elsewhere in תנ״ל as a “rib”, but always as a “side”, which is also why צלוע means to be inclined towards one side, to limp. — סגר, related to סכר ,שכר, to close, stop up, to close where there was a hole, from which, too, we get שכר, compensation, wages. — בשר, related to בַשֵׂר to announce, proclaim, expresses the deep importance of the pure human body, to be the herald of the spirit to the world, and of the world to the spirit. בשר, flesh, includes everything which is not blood and not bone, accordingly, skin, muscle and nerve, the means by which the interposition the mediation between the spirit, the mind, and the world takes place. Without בשר there is no consciousness of the world, and no effect can be made on the world. Hence the opposite to אבן :בשר (Ezekiel 36,26). — בנה ,ויבן occurs elsewhere too with the meaning of “forming”, from which we get the word תבנית. — So that with Woman, the material for her body was not taken from the earth as it was with man. God formed one side of Man into Woman; Man, as it were, was divided, and the one part formed into Woman, not עשה ,יצר ,ברא but בנה, only built out, arranged as Woman. So that what was previously one creature was now two, and thereby the complete equality of women for ever attested. Our sages also ascribe all the special characteristics of the female voice, the female character and temperament, as well as the earlier spiritual and mental maturity of women, as being connected with this formation of Woman out of the already feeling, sensitive living body of Man, in contrast to Man, whose body was created out of earth.

V. 23. הפעם itself means: this time, now, finally, at last, as הפעם יזבלני אישי ,הפעם אמותה. So that here it means either: “at last this is it!” and the cantillation speaks for this, or: “this at last is bone of my bone etc.”. This הפעם expresses finally reaching that which one has hitherto striven for in vain. “Amongst all the creatures have I sought, but found none who could take over part of my work from me, and do it on a line with me; now I have found it”. כי מאיש לקחה זאת, the name אשה, accordingly, does not designate the dependence of Woman on Man, but rather the equality, the two belonging together, the division of the one human calling between the two sexes.

V. 24. על כן. Therefore, because as long as the man was alone it was not yet “good”, and because once the division had been made, it was no longer at all possible for the man to fulfil his calling by himself, because his wife was to be עזר כנגדו, without her he was only half a man, and only together with her did he feel himself a whole man, therefore a man leaves his father and his mother and attaches himself to a wife, and they become one single body. Just as before the division, originally, the man’s body subordinated itself under one spirit and under one Divine Will, so after the reunion Man and Woman become one single body. But that can only take place if at the same time they become one mind, one heart, one soul, and this again is only possible if they subordinate all their strength and efforts, all their thoughts and desires to the service of a Higher Will. But herein lies the great difference between the sexual life of all other living creatures and that of human marriage. All the rest of the living world is also divided into sexes. But in their case both sexes sprang at the same time independently from the earth. They do not require each other for the fulfilment of their lives’ calling, and only for the purpose of breeding, and for the time necessary for perpetuating the species, do they seek and find each other. But the human female is a part of the human male, is עזר כנגדו. The man is helpless and lacking independence without his wife. Only the two together form a complete human being. Life in its entirety, in every phase, demands their union. Only of men does it say ודבק באשתו.

Our sages in the Gemora (Sanhedrin 56 et. seq.) find already in this verse indication of the laws of עריות of the בני נח. In the admonition “therefore shall a man forsake his father and his mother and cleave to his wife”, they see the law indicated that a man, in the choice of a wife, is to go away from the parental home, accordingly not to look for a wife amongst too near relations. If we take this in connection with the whole context of what is introduced by על כן we can perhaps get a glimmer of light on the dark, apparently inexplicable domain of the צריות-laws. Because the wife is to be the עזר of her husband, she must be כנגדו; because she is to complement him she must have different characteristics to his. If they are nearly related they would perhaps have the same virtues, but also perhaps the same faults; the same pefections, but also the same deficiencies; their union would only strengthen and intensify the characteristics in both directions, good and bad, but they would not complement each other. Only in more distant grades would the salubrious wholesome differences be most likely to be present, which when united, would tend to produce the perfect being suitable to become perfectly בשר אחד, and to achieve more purely and completely the one great human task. This motive might perhaps suffice for the עריות בני נח. For Israel, where, for example, forbidden grades start already with קידושין, there must be some higher motive.

V. 25 The etymology of the word ערום, naked, presents considerable difficulty. We find the root ערם elsewhere having the two meanings: cunning, subtle, as in the verse immediately following, and as ערמה a heap of grain. The connection between these two is easily found. Analogous would be תחבולה rope, from חבל twine, with which things are tied together, and rope by which things are dragged along. A rope itself consists of single strands, themselves weak, joined together. Every subtle plan is a joining up of single arrangements to achieve an ultimate purpose. In any case the conception of thinking is expressed in Hebrew by the conception of joining together, thus חשב to think, and חשב האפוד, aparon or girdle of the ephod. In a similar way the conception of guile, cunning comes from the conception of heaping up. עָרמה is an עֲרֵמה, a heaping up of grains of thought which finally mount to a point. The subtle one does various things which are unnoticed, the single little grains have no importance, but together they make the heap. (חרם, the net for catching, made out of single meshes joined together, is also related o ערם, cunning.) But it still remains difficult to find the relation of ערם naked, if it comes from the root ערם. Perhaps, therefore the root of ערם naked is עור which also means naked, עורה פשוטה stripped naked, (Is. 32,11), הביט אל מעוריהם (Hab. 2,15) et. alia. The נח occurs quite clearly in עירמים in v. 7 of next chapter. We can find analogies for the change of the ָ to : in the suffix although the נח of the root rests in it, e.g. זָדון from זוד which in stat. constr. is זְדון, although in the plural the נח appears markedly as זֵדונים. Equally so, יְמֵי ,יָמים ,יום. The root, accordingly could be עור, and we would have עור naked, awake, and skin, with the underlying conception of being sensitive to external impression. The deeper the sleep, the less do external impressions reach us. When we awake we begin to take notice. Now the most general recipient of sensation is the skin, the organ of the sense of touch. The man who is consigned really to his sense of touch, who can get impressions of visible things only through his sense of touch is called עִוֵר, “a skin man”, blind.

בוש to be ashamed; in the Piel בושש to stay away, to be expected and not to come. So that בושש, an active form of the word, means to disappoint expectations, and בוש in the Kal, intransitive, to feel one self disappointed in one’s expectations. But really, at bottom, that is: shame. It is the feeling of one who has fallen short, has not come up to his expectations of himself. When someone has not attained that which he should be, finds that he is not what he ought to be, then he feels ashamed of himself. This feeling that God has implanted in Man, which at once comes over him when he becomes conscious of his shortcoming, is the greatest gift which the Grace of God has given mankind of whom He probably knew quite well that he would often not come up to what he was meant to be. Through it, Man becomes his own monitor and guardian. The related feeling of shyness and modesty, too — in Hebrew also designated by כשהוא בישן סימן טוב באדם ,בוש — are nothing but the consciousness that one is still far off that picture of one’s ideal self which one carries in one’s own breast. Thus God has entrusted every man to himself, has implanted in every man the ideal by which to judge himself. The consciousness of this ideal is what we call conscience, and the condemning verdict of one’s conscience is בוש: shame.

The original condition of the first human pair is described to us in the curt sentence: they were both, the man and his wife, naked and were not ashamed; perhaps, as it does not say ולא התבוששו, but ולא יתבוששו, they were not to be ashamed. For as long as man and woman were both אדם, together בשר אחד, one body, having the same spirit, serving the One God, as long as with body and soul they come up to the ideal of Man being in the likeness of God, for so long was their body pure and holy like their soul, spiritual and sensual, body and soul, both given by God for the fulfilment of their human mission. No matter whether Man is engaged in his spiritual or physical efforts, as long as he keeps both within the limits which God has ordained, and uses both for the purposes for which God has given them, he has nothing to be ashamed of in one or the other. The pure human body, the moral life of the senses, are no whit less holy than the soul, the spiritual life. The moral and spiritual greatness of human beings demanded by the Divine Law and God’s Torah is based in the very first place on his keeping the body holy, that in satisfying all the urges of our senses, we keep within the bounds sanctified by God, and then we should not have to be ashamed of our animal body, our nakedness. But as soon as Man hands over the reins to his sensuousness, does not exercise moral energy to raise his sensual life up into the realm of godliness, but on the contrary, by his sensuality his godliness itself gets dragged down into the unfree state of the senses, then at once he has to be ashamed of his nakedness. And this feeling of shame is the warning guardian of morality, is the Voice of God to Man who has forsaken his pure moral height, warning him to be the master of this sensual body of his, and by such subjugating mastery to work himself up with his moral freedom of will to the height of his godly calling with both, body and soul. As long as the power of their senses had not lured them down from this pure height they could both be naked and had not to be ashamed of their nakedness.

The stressed repetition האדם ואשתו is highly significant, both, the man and wife were naked and were not to be ashamed. This lays down the far-reaching deep truth that not only in spiritual matters, but also in bodily relations, Man and Woman are to be equally pure, equally moral, equally holy. The human race will never be sound as long as the first fundamental virtue of life is not considered with the same seriousness by both sexes; as long as youth and men believe that it is part of youth and manliness that youths and men should allow themselves things that are not to be permitted to girls and women. Not for nothing do Jewish men have on their bodies the sign of the admonition: התהלך לפני והיה תמים, the warning that God expects from them the same innocence, the same moral chastity as is expected from women.

V. 1. The contrast to animals is the touchstone and the rock, by which, and on which, the morality of men proves itself or splits asunder. It was animal wisdom which lured the first human beings from their duty, to-day it is the same animal wisdom which serves as midwife to every sin. The history of the first lapse is the history of all straying from the right path. Animals are really כאלקים יודעי טוב ורע. They have innate instinct, and this instinct is the Voice of God, the Will of God for them. Accordingly what they do in accordance with this Divine Providence which rules within them — and they do nothing else, can do nothing else — is good, and everything which this instinct keeps them back from doing, is bad. Animals do no wrong, they have only their one nature that they are to follow. Not so Man. He is to decide for the good and eschew evil from his own free choice, and from the consciousness of his duty; he is also to give his sensuous nature its due, not out of the allure of his senses, but from a feeling of duty. Sensual enjoyment for him is to be a moral free-willed act, he is never, and in to ways whatsoever, to be an animal. For that purpose he has both, sensuality and godliness, within him, that which is good and right must often oppose his sensuality, bad and evil must often appear attractive and tempting to him, so that for the sake of his high godly calling he practices the good and eschews the evil with the free-willed energy of his godly nature, in spite of his sensuality, and never yields to passion. That is why the Voice of God does not speak in him, but to him, to say what is good and what is bad, and this Voice of God speaking to him finds opposition in his excited sensuality when this latter is allowed to speak on its own, untouched and uncontrolled by his godly nature. The Voice of God breathed into him — his conscience, whose messenger we have recognised shame to be — only warns Man in general to be good and avoid evil, but what is good and what is evil he has to hear from the Mouth of God. Animals have only to develop their sensual nature, and their intelligence is completely in the service of this nature. Man was not set in the paradise on the earth to satisfy his sensual nature on the delights and food which it proffered; לעבדה ולשמרה, it was to the service of God and His world that he was called there. This service was his mission, and for this service the delights of the paradisical fruits were permitted to him. Accordingly, animals may test everything simply by their own individual natures, they are there only for themselves. But Man is there for God and the world, and is joyfully to sacrifice his personal nature to this higher calling. So that it is not out of his personal nature, but out of its relation to this higher calling of his that Man has to find out what is good and what is bad for him. For that purpose the tree stood for him in all its glory, appealing to all his senses, his whole personal nature must say to him “this is good”, and God’s Word had forbidden the eating of it as “bad”. That was to be to him the model, the pattern and the rule for all good and bad for mankind, that was for him the tree of the knowledge of good and bad; as indeed our sages recognised in God’s declaration concerning it (Ch. 2,16) the revelation of all the universal duties of mankind. Then the wisdom of the animal world approached him in its cleverest representative, the serpent. To an animal, even to the wisest, it is incomprehensible how anybody could pass over the most beautiful, most alluring, the best and most enjoyable food and remain indifferent to it. — אף כי אמר אלקים, “and even if God has said so”, this beginning of the speech shows us mankind already in conversation with the animal. The human being had already presented God’s prohibition as the reason for not eating. “Well, and even if God has said so?!” Is that a reason for your having to obey? Is not the urge within you the Voice of God? If eating it is bad for you, why did He give the food the appeal to you, and you the urge to eat it, did He not tell you thereby quite clearly that this food and you are there for each other? Is not this Voice His earlier clearer Voice? Would God first create the food and give you the longing for it, and then — would He forbid you everything?

Thus spoke the serpent, and thus speaks animal wisdom to us still to-day, either straight out or cloaked in philosophical covering, when a direct prohibition of God holds us at a distance from alluring enjoyment of our senses, and it exaggerates to-day as it did then, in the little that is prohibited, it overlooks all that is morally permitted, and presents God’s Law of morality as the enemy of all sensual enjoyment.

V. 2.—3. The answer to a certain extent is perfectly correct. “By no means is everything forbidden to us, but rather the same Voice which has allowed the rich profusion of food in the garden has forbidden us this single one”. But nevertheless there is one element contained in this answer that we may not overlook, and to which our sages have already directed our attention. We have already seen how this first law of God and its history contains all the essential factors which characterise just those laws of the further Lawgiving to which the non-Jewish world and the un-Jewish mind have, and always have had, taken umbrage and resented. It was a חוק, belonged to מאכלות אסורות, and to the first transgressor it was תשב״ם, only known to her by “traditional” word of mouth. In this answer there is still a fourth factor which completes the sum of the elements which have irritated those who look at our laws in a superficial manner. Here we have at once the beginning of a סייג, a “protective fence”, a מצות דרבנן. God had only forbidden eating the fruit of the tree. Eve declares that even touching it is prohibited. This was a “fence-law”, which Adam’s conscientiousness had added to God’s prohibition, to protect himself from transgressing it. We can see therefrom how these סייגים and גזרות are formed quite naturally from the conscientiousness that the observance of the Laws of God expect from us. But at the same time our sages admonish us תמותון כיון שראה שכזבה דחפה עליו א״ל כמה דלא דמכת במקרובתיה אף לא במיכליה הנטיעות כך הקב״ה אמר ביום אכלו ממנו ועמדה והעידה עדות שקר לא תגעו בו פן שלא תעשה את הגדר יותר על העיקר שלא יפול ויקצץ את. They warn us not to exaggerate and to set the fence too high, lest it fall in and destroy the plants it was placed to protect. God had said: “as soon as you eat of it you will die”, but she said, quite untruthfully, that God had said “touch it not or you will die”. The serpent caught at this falsehood. It pushed Eve against the tree, and then said: “see, you have not died by touching it, so you will also not die through eating it”. (ב״ר י״ט and דר׳ נתן אבות). They warn us never to lose sight of the origin and the importance of these “fence-laws” ordered by Jewish conscientiousness, always to keep in mind that they are man-made and not God-made, not דאוריתא, only as long as we remember this do they serve us as warning and protection. If we forget that this is their character, then transgressing them will just lead more easily to trangressing the real God’s law too. This danger the sages always bear in mind themselves, and always take great care to make it evident that their סייגים and גזרות are only such, and to differentiate them from the מצות which are דאוריתא. Adam erred therein that he transmitted the touching of the tree with the eating hereof as being equally forbidden by God.

V.4.—5. After the serpent had tried in vain to excite some doubts as to the necessity of absolute literal obedience, it aroused a doubt as to the gravity of the command: “You will not die!” “One does not die so quickly!” It is only to keep you in childish dependence on Himself that He has forbidden you to eat. Eat, and your eyes will be opened, you will obtain understanding, be able to know for yourselves what is good and what is bad, and with this understanding you will become godlike and independent of God, it is an understanding that even the smallest animal around you possesses.” — פקח related to פקע ,בקע, to split, to spring open.

עין, eye, and spring, or well. A spring is that by which that which was hidden comes to light. Thus חקר means to investigate, study, go deep into, and also to dig up from the depths. Similarly באר a well, and באר, clear, to explain, make clear. And so we get עין: spring and eye. But not in the sense of the soul, the mind showing itself through the eye, but rather the contrary, the eye is the source through which the external world flows in to the human mind. The universe is brought to a focus through the narrow eye on the path of the mind. (אַיִן is the expression for the unsatisfied eye).

V. 6. תאוה from the root אוה, related to עוה, crooked, departing from the straight direction. Referring to the human mind, ישר, (cf. גשר ,קשר ,כשר) is that which physically or normally is attainable by me, lies within my straight path. But if I strive for something which lies out of that path, I am מתאוה, trying to draw a circular line about myself, seeking to enlarge the boundaries of my province, to make myself the centre point of a larger circle.

נחמד, from the root חמד, related to אמד to value, appraise. Whereas תאוה values an object only as regards oneself, and wishes to have it because it appeals to one’s own liking, חמד regards it more objectively in itself.

השכל, from root שכל related to סגולה ,סגל, that which is appropriated exclusively to someone. שכל is the power which a person has of comprehending the picture of things which flow in through his eyes, and adopting them accordingly to himself. סכל is the person whose perception is too subjective, who obstinately sticks to the opinion he has formed of things without testing it with actual reality outside his mind. השכל means to direct your mind to something, to be and act understandingly, also to direct somebody else’s mind to something, to instruct. But it never has the meaning of being happy.

V. 7. The serpent was perfectly right. Their eyes were opened, they became enlightened people — but their first recognition was — that they were naked! But the consciousness of being naked is the consciousness that something is visible that should not be so. This is the feeling of shame, which, as already indicated above, has its roots in the consciousness of a person of the real calling of Man. As long as Man stands completely in the service of his God, he has not to be ashamed of any part of his body. Even the bodily lures and attractions are pure and godly as long as they submit themselves as means for God’s holy purposes. But when this condition is not entirely there we certainly should be ashamed of displaying them. This shame awakes the voice within us, which is intimately connected with the conscience, and reminds us that we are not meant to be animals.

V. 8. On this verse our sages remark: “עיקר שכינה בתחתונים, that originally and essentially the principle proximity of God was to rest down here on earth”. We are apt to look on the cases of intimate intercourse between Man and God as being something extraordinary, and to consider them as being outside the ordinary conditions of life, which is why their authenticity is doubted by many people and considered impossible. In opposition to that comes the great proclamation: — Not the later mission of the Prophets, not God’s speaking to the Patriarchs, to Moses, and to Israel, not these are extraordinary conditions, but rather the six thousand years of the distance between men and God is the unnatural condition; the original relationship is that of עיקר שכינה בתחתונים. Not on the other side of life, but down here — that is what this history shows us — is a condition for mankind possible in which — peace within his own breast, peace with nature all around him, peace with his God — everything is completely in harmony with it, everything is harmoniously bound up with it. Nature — a blossoming garden, the animal world at his feet, even those amphibians which now keep at a distance from him, friendly and amicably associating with him, and amongst all this, Man standing upright, in the likeness of God, raising himself up to his God, and God near to him, speaking to him, directing and guiding him, all this, only dependent on Man, with all this glory and delight, submitting himself to God, asking God “what is good, what is evil?” But “Man does not remain in his glory even for one night, as soon as he takes animals to be his model and allows the difference between Man and animal to disappear”. To open the gates of Paradise once again, to re-establish peace and harmony on earth, peace from the wild beasts up to Man, and to bring the Glory of God back to earth, that is what is proclaimed on every page of the Word of God as the result and aim of the Torah. It is not unimportant to establish this fact out of this beginning of the history of mankind, so that when later on we come across single instances, such as the mission given to the prophets, or even that one occasion when the whole of Israel (at very least over a million people I.L.) became elevated into prophets, we do not consider such instances as supernatural or rather unnatural events, but we take them for what they were viz. momentary return, brought about by the strength of the תורה to the original natural condition.

מתהלך, while הלו as a rule, means a movement towards a goal, התהלך expresses a movement with the intention of keeping within a limited sphere. Hence: התהלך לפני ה׳, keeping within the limits prescribed by God in the paths of life. The התפעל indicates the conscious and energetic keeping oneself back from other spheres, equally with the positive keeping oneself to the right track. Our sages, accordingly, see in this מתהלך the סילוק שכינה, the withdrawing, the retiring to Itself of the proximity of the Glory of God on earth, (thus, later, כי ה׳ אלקיך מתהלך בקרב מחנך, whereas all over the world the proximity of God is missed, it is present in Israel’s camp, thither it withdraws itself). For God and His Voice only reach Man as long as he stands upright in his purity above animals. And so too, later on it is conditional on מחניך קדש! The word מחניך shows that the proximity of God is not to be sought in ecstasy, fanatic visions and transports, but that God will be near to us, God will come to us in the midst of our ordinary varied life with our feet squarely on the earth in all the phases of our earthly life, if only this earthly life of ours, this earthly circle of ours, our מחניך, is קדש, a holy one. — They heard the Voice of God withdrawing itself in the garden.

לרוח היום, either to the side from which the day comes, the East, or where the sun was at that time, the West. According to the latter view, which seems the more likely, and which אונקלס too adopts, that the first סילוק שכינה was towards sunset in the West, another plan of disposition and tradition may have a deep significance. The קדש הקדשים, the Holy of Holies, was in the West. In the opinion of our sages the שכינה is in the West. The ever-burning light on the מנורה, that representation of the עץ החיים, was the מערבי נר turned towards the West. If it is true that the fast farewell greeting of the שכינה was in the West, it is understandable that it is to the West we turn and stand and look after it and wait and hope. Since, coincidentally with the first setting of the earthly sun for mankind, its spiritual Divine Sun also set, we stand and gaze there and await its return, and the whole service, the whole עבודה in the מקדש is naught but the means to prepare the way for the return of that time.

ויתחבא. The man and woman crept away. They no longer stood upright before God, לפני ה׳, but מפני, they feared His proximity. Now they felt all sorts of contrasts and differences themselves. They had already felt the first discord, their body being at variance with their spirit and had made aprons for themselves. At once now they feel themselves — no longer mastering their senses, no longer pure in body and spirit — at variance with God. They felt they had lost their worthy status of human beings and slunk away and hid themselves amongst the other creatures.

V. 9. ויקרא, called to him from a distance to call him back. אי) איכה an enclosed isolated place, an island, and also א״י, because of its special and isolating mission, איה, the question concerning the place) Where art thou? What position hast thou adopted?

V. 10. I feel that I can not come before You because something has become apparent to me which has made me afraid even to show myself to myself, and certainly to You. This being afraid, not ashamed, proves that the consciousness of being naked has to be taken in the sense of its moral reason, as explained above on V. 7. Not because of his body being naked, but because he no longer dared to let his naked body be seen, was what made him afraid for himself.

V. 11. הגיד (from the root נגד) to make present, to represent, to bring home. How did the consciousness come to you that you are to be ashamed of your naked body? אשר צויתיך לבלתי וגו׳. In Hebrew there is no special word for forbidding. All laws are מצות, God’s directions which each of us has to fulfil on his post; מצות עשה and מצות לא תעשה, directions what we are to do and what to abstain from doing. The prohibitions too are also מצות. All God’s Laws are at rock bottom positive. The prohibitions also do not leave us just inactive, but on the contrary demand our most energetic efforts, our most positive activity, to bridle and keep ourselves in check, to overcome inclinations, urges and passions. They often involve a much greater expenditure of energy and demand more strength of character than the accomplishment of a good deed, an עשה. Therefore we should feel ourselves spurred to as much joyful activity when God forbids us anything, as we do when He commands us to do something. This point of view is probably what Rab. Akiba meant when he says that, at the revelation on Sinai, Israel not only responded על הן הן, but also on על לאו הן, not only the positive commands did they receive with a “yes, we will”, but with the same “yes”, the prohibitions.

V. 12. אשר נתחה, whom Thou hast set by my side; who according to Thy Will, was to be equal in rank to me, that we together are to form not only one לב and נפש but to be one בשר, one body to carry out the efforts and dictates of mind and will; she gave me, and her will was accordingly decisive for me. The fact that Adam did not excuse himself with the luscious temptation of the fruit, nor that his wife had led him astray, but simply stated that naturally her decision went for him too, shows clearly the original completely harmonious equality of the status of man and woman.

V. 13. נשא (related to נשה) to have an undischarged claim, to have to demand the fulfilment of a promise from somebody. השיא to make promises which remain permanently unfulfilled. Thus אל ישא לכם חזקיהו. Here “the serpent made me deceptive representations”.

V. 14.—15. It was הי א׳ Who spoke to the serpent. Not only as אלקים, creator and judge, but as the power directing the education of mankind to its real calling. So that we have to take this pronouncement against the serpent not so much as punishment for the serpent as from the point of view of the education of mankind. — ארד (related to ערר, lonely, desolate, not in company of others, without any future: childless) without joy, without blossom, the opposite of ברכה, the conception of expansion, smiles of fortune. The meaning of ארור מכל הבהמה ומכל חית השדה seems doubtful. It is generally taken as the comparative, more cursed than all the other animals. But that implies that all the other animals are cursed, for which there is no apparent reason. Possibly it is to be taken in the same sense as ארור אתה מן האדמה in Ch. 4,11 i.e. “thou wilt be cursed by all cattle and all animals”. Similarly too מנשים באוהל תברך ,תברך מנשים יעל, (Judges 5,24) “all women bless Jael”. But nevertheless it is probably comparative and would be in connection with a remark which we have to make on V. 16 & 17. Neither of these run: אל האדם ,ויאמר אל האשה, but אל האשה אמר ,ולאדם אמד and this shows that the speech to the serpent had been preceded by the speech to the woman, and that this had been preceded by that to the man. Accordingly ארורה האדמה בעבורך, the earth had already been cursed for the sake of mankind. The whole world, including its animal life, had already been doomed to suffer by Man’s sin, for his sake i.e. as a means for his betterment, but the serpent most of all. בהמה, the animals that submit to mankind, although they participate in the hardships which are now allotted to mankind and have to suffer in and through Man’s struggle for existence, nevertheless — considered from the human point of view — they do become raised and ennobled and, to a certain extent, gain in intelligence from their association with mankind. חיות, the free animals of the wild enjoy their freedom and vigour in unhampered joy. The serpent is denied both. In contrast to the animals of the wild it has to slink on its belly and to eat earth. The meaning of eating dust is obscure. Actually snakes do not eat earth but live solely on living creatures. It seems only to be a figurative picture of creeping about on one’s belly, similar to ואויביו עפר ילחכו (Ps. 72,9) “and his enemies shall lick the dust”, ילחכו עפר כנחש “shall lick dust like a serpent” (Micha 7,17). Or possibly snakes, whose tongues seem hardly adapted for tasting, lack the sense of taste altogether, so that their eating is only to satisfy their hunger and gives them no taste of enjoyment, and that the explanation of our sages in Yoma 75a that “the most tasty food tastes to it only like dust” may be an actual physiological fact. — Enmity is established between the serpent and mankind, and cattle or such animals that are connected with mankind. As a matter of fact, amongst the four higher classes it is only the amphibians, of which snakes are representative, which are completely strange and hostile, and by the innate aversion and repugnance to mankind are completely apart from them.

From the point of view of the educational care for mankind, the איבה, the strong antipathy implanted in mankind towards snakes may be meant to bring home to his mind that it was “animal wisdom” that led him astray, and to remind him of the gulf that separates Man from animal; and at the same time, by a concrete example, to keep the fact constantly before his eyes that there must be a different criterion for good and evil than the dictates of blind instinctive inclinations. The snake bites as a result of its natural impulse and still a snake-bite is evil for mankind. Thus the moral evil of passion may give satisfaction to man and still be injurious for higher matters and in other directions. So that the mere dictates of his senses may not tell Man what is good or evil. If we dare take it that the sight of a snake is henceforth to remind mankind to fight his lusts, then ישופך ראש ואתה תשופנו עקב הוא would say very significantly: Man is given greater strength over his lusts, than these have over him. Man can stamp his lusts on the head, they can at the most catch him on his heel. Further שוף (in rabbinic Hebrew, to move from its place — seems to mean the quick spring, the sudden dart of the snake, hence the words שפן and שפיפון) is to catch unforeseen, when the other is careless. Only when Man is off his guard does the snake, and lust, catch him on his heel. By constant watchfulness and being always on one’s guard, both can be avoided. And equally so, only when Man does not allow lusts to awake, to become passions, as long as snakes and lusts are still slumbering can he stamp both of them on the head, but not if he awakes and excites them.

V. 16. עצבון: only a mental pain and hurt feeling or worry. If it does once occur with physical bodily pain it refers to the result of pain on one’s mind and feelings. The root עצב, a modification of עזב forsaken, by the צ, leaving something against one’s will, through force, harshness or violence. So that עצב is the feeling that we have to give something up that we would have liked to keep, or to have attained: renouncing, foregoing. ולא עצבו אביו מימיו (Kings I. 1,6) “David had never asked his son to give anything up”. ויתעצב אל לבו (Gen. 6,6). God felt — to speak in terms of human beings — that He would have to renounce, abandon, mankind. — God had just said to Adam: בעצבון תאכלנה, exactly the same term as He used here to Eve. With the word עצבון, Man entered an entirely new situation for a long space of time. Until then Man knew no wrong, and no renunciation. But now for Man nature is no longer at one with his wishes as it was previously, he must wrest everything from her, and only by renunciation, by giving up one thing, one enjoyment, can he attain another. In a remarkable manner gods too are designated by a word derived from this root, viz. עצבים. Mankind, who really had only themselves to thank for the hard struggle for existence which now prevails, forgot that the cause for it lay in themselves, and imagined themselves surrounded by inimical powers and forces who maliciously made life hard and took pleasure in the toil and worry of men. They accordingly called these powers עצבים, gods who cause renunciation, אלילים, “refusers, who always say No!” — “But to the woman He had said: thy renunciation and thy conception will I let be still greater”. The fact that the speech to the woman did not start with כי עשית זאת already shows that it is only a continuation of what had already been said to Adam. Of the עצבון of the man, the wife is, to the greatest part, free. Not by the sweat of her brow has she to gain her bread. But her renunciation is a still greater one. The whole life of a woman, from earliest girlhood, is a life full of sacrifice, giving herself up for others, and then הרונך comes, where the woman gives up her whole existence to make her own flesh and blood a contribution for a new human growth. בעצב תלדי בנים, there is no higher happiness for a woman than to have children, and this highest happiness can only be bought with the greatest sacrifices.

שוק .ואל אישך תשוקתך, market, שוק thigh, שוקק, a strong mass-movement of locusts or horses, the basic conception accordingly, to move oneself powerfully towards one direction, hence תשוקה, the direction of feelings and the other efforts towards one goal, striving towards, longing. It is in the nature of woman to feel that she can only really live a full life in union with a husband, and yet it is only adding a fresh renunciation: והוא ימשל בך! The altered condition of the earth towards Man, that henceforth it will only yield him his bread by his hard labour, already makes Woman more dependent on Man, the actual breadwinner, and so endangers the original equality. Thus it develops in general, where the תורה does not bring the recovery and peace in all this, and establishes Man and Woman again in an equal God-serving calling of being priests to God, and again makes the wife “the crown of her husband”, and to the “invaluable pearl” of his life (Prov. 12,4, XXXI, 10).

V. 17. Adam, to whom the care of the Law, which he had received himself, had been entrusted, should have opposed his wife. אדמה ,בעבורך ארורה האדמה, Man’s earth, the earth inasmuch as it is the stage for Man. What it is in itself as a cosmic body is quite beyond the point here. But because the top surface at any rate was made for mankind, they are in a state of intimate relationship and interaction to each other. — בעבור, literally: in “going over”, for a purpose, similar to בגלל “in bringing about”. In most places בעבור gives the purpose and בגלל the cause. לי בעבורך וחיתה נפשי בגללך למען ייטב “for your sake”, literally “to get at you”, to get your favour, they will deal well with me, and because of you I will remain alive. So here: not because you sinned, but for your betterment, for your sake, ארורה וגו׳, is the ground to be restrained in its development. I will not let it develop freely any longer, it will no longer smile at you, will no longer of its own will offer you its products, only with renunciation of a great deal will you be able to enjoy any of it, בעצבון תאכלנה. The purpose of this blight on the blessing of the soil is to habituate Man to this בכל עצב יהיה מותר״ .עצבון״ “Every sacrifice brings a profit” (Prov. 14,23) is still to-day a principle of education. Giving things up makes a man free, brings out his better, nobler self, makes him independent of external things, of that which the world offers or denies, and allows him to find his own true worth in faithfulness to God, and at the same time his undisturbable happiness. Into this school of renunciation Man was now to be led. As every enjoyment, everything “good”, worth having, has to be bought by work, toil, and renunciation, the life of his senses already drives the fact home to him that what is bitter is not always bad, and what is sweet is not always good; and this preparatory school of renunciation finally raises him to that mastery of life which happily renounces what is sweet to the senses for what is good for the morals. Our sages teach that all מתנות טובות, the most glorious gifts that God gives us, are only to be gained by way of the יסורין.

V. 18. קוץ ודרדר. Just as סנה thorn, (from שנא, to hate, to be inimical, to fend off), “touch me not”, is what it says, so קוץ, the prickle, comes from קוץ nausea, repugnance, aversion. קיץ, summer, really summer-fruit, comes from the same root. The fruit is ripe (גמל) when it is “weaned” from further sucking the nourishing juices of the tree: ויגמל שקדים. Perhaps קיץ — קוץ, when fruit becomes over ripe so that the juices of the tree are not only no longer necessary for it but actually harmful for it, so that it gets an aversion to the tree and falls off. So קוץ is the thorn, the prickle which fends off, hinders touch. — דרדר from the root דרר which only occurs as דרור which does not designate so much “freedom” as “homecoming”, coming back. Hence צפור דרור, the swallow, the bird that always returns to its old home. So that דרדר seems to mean holding back, holding fast (perhaps the terms in Rabbinic Hebrew דרדא טומאה ,דררא דממונא, “there is some question of money sticking to this” etc. also comes from this) according to which דרדד would be the burr, or wild bugloss, which holds us fast, and then דרדר would be the contrast to קוץ. The earth will offer you only thorns and burrs, will repulse you where you wish to approach, and cling to you where you wish to go away. — תצמיח לך, nothing else will it offer you, while to all other creatures it still offers to-day all that they require. Man alone, if he does not want to work hard, only finds קוץ ודרדר; “wouldst thou go on living as if still in paradise, thou wouldst have to eat grass”.

V. 19. זעה .בזעת אפיך תאכל לחם from the root זוע movement. Sweat is, accordingly only an expression of movement, exertion: “in hefty exertion of your presence”. (Sweat is also called יזע, related to יצא to come out, i.e. an exhalation, and גזע, the prominent shoot or stem coming out of the earth). And it says אפיך not פניך. As already remarked above (Ch. 2,7 אפים has a much more characteristic, higher meaning than פגים .פגים is used of all creatures and things to designate the side to which they are turned. Not so אפים, from אפף, striving to absorb something in oneself, the higher energy to overcome something. With אפים a man strives to master the things about him, he scans his domain. Accordingly, not by the sweat of your body, your hands, or even פניך, but בזעת אפיך will you eat bread. Your godlike countenance, the seat of the mind, of insight, of all divine light, which should express all your mastery of the world, will you have to direct to obtaining your daily bread. The whole lamentable condition of gaining a scanty subsistence in עצבון is expressed in that little word לחם. Sustenence is called טרף, inasmuch as it has to be “snatched” in the struggle with nature, לחם (root of מלחמה) as, at the same time, it has to go through the struggle for existence against fellow men, the struggle of all against all. Did we not have to direct our minds so much to obtaining our daily bread, strife between man and man would not be so pre-eminent, and the idea of property would not weigh so heavily in the scales. But after part of man’s very existence depends on every little piece of bread which he must gain with עצבון, with sacrificing something for it, after he has struggled to wrest it from nature, he at once starts the struggle with his fellowman to keep that which he has won, or even earlier, to get ahead of him at the source in Nature.

In the לקחת lies the idea of being forced. Left to himself Man belongs to the earth: כי עפר אתה ואל עפר חשוב. But God’s Almight had taken the man away from the earth out of which He had created him, and had set him in Paradise. In the Hands of God, even the part taken from the dust is eternal, knows no death, as long as Man remained in God’s Hands. But since Man withdrew himself out of God’s Hands and gave himself up to his own guidance, he falls back, and goes the way of mortality. “The bread that you wrest from Nature and your fellow-man does not restore you completely, it is not from the עץ החיים, it only keeps you going for a time, שובך אל האדמה עד, until you return to the earth, כי ממנה לקחת, for only by God were you taken away from it.

In this ארורה אדמה בעבורך, in this curse which the earth receives for the sake of mankind, for their betterment, we meet the first example of the flourishing, the blessings of the earth, running parallel, not only with the sunshine, rain and normal causes, but with the degree of the obedience and faithfulness of Man to the laws of God. With the תורה, a beginning was to have been made for the world to return to its original harmonious condition. ארץ ישראל was to have been a revival of Paradise on a small scale, which is why the Torah makes definite promises to be fulfilled here in this world. The way which leads back to Paradise is the way of life laid down and prescribed in the Torah. That is why this blossoming, or the reverse, of the earth running parallel to that of mankind is most prominent in ישראל ארץ and in its fate as revealed in בחקתי.

One considreation does however seem to us of the utmost importance In the whole of this verdict of God, the curse is pronounced only against the ground and an animal, but in no wise over Man. Mankind is in no manner whatsoever placed under a ban for his first disobedience. In all that was said, not a single syllable altered by a hairbreadth Man’s high calling or his ability to reach and fulfil it. Only the stage on which, and the external circumstances under which, he has to accomplish his mission are altered for his benefit. The mission itself, his God-like calling and his God-like competence for it, remains undisturbed. Still to-day, every human child comes from the Hand of God as pure as Adam did, still to-day every child is born to mankind pure as an angel. This is one of the cardinal points of Jewish life and of the essential Jewish nature. What a disconsolate lie, undermining the whole moral future of mankind, has been forged out of this history. The dogma of original sin has been founded on it, a dogma, upon which a whole structure has been built, against which, if against anything, the whole being of a Jew has to raise the most emphatic protest. Certainly, through this sin, all the descendants of Adam have inherited the task of having to live in a world which no longer smiles benevolently in harmony with them, but that is just because the same sin is constantly being repeated. But the reason for this opposition of the world to man is, that through the struggle for existence and the resulting “school of renunciation”, mankind is to be educated up to that state of moral perfection which will pave the way back to Paradise on earth. But that, because of this, Man has become “sinful”, has forfeited the ability to be good, must sin, and for individuals and mankind in general to be saved for a return to God and to be led back to Paradise on earth, something else is required other than the possibility which everyone possesses to elevate himself up to faithful fulfilment of his duty, against that belief Judaism raises the most vehement protest. For that, no dead and no resurrected intermediary is necessary. This is taught by the whole of Jewish history. This shows how pure men were able to get as near to God as the first man was before his fall. An Abraham, a Moses, an Isaiah, a Jeremiah etc. etc. attained their nearness to God by nothing else than a pure effort to be faithful to duty. Next to the ne plus ultra, the highest conceivable height, the One Free-willed God, Jewish conception places, as second, the pure free-willed Man. The teaching of original sin and thereby the curse of sinfulness of mankind which can only be removed by the belief in a certain fact is the most regrettable error. Just as our history recounts no curse being pronounced over Man, so still to-day every Jew approaches his God with the avowal: הנשמה שנתת בי טהורה היא “the soul that Thou hast given me is pure”, and it is up to me to keep it pure, and to restore it to You pure. Our sages teach (אין דור שאין בו כאברהם כיעקב כמשה כשמואל (ב״ר נ״ו), “there is no age in which men like Abraham, Jacob, Moses, Samuel do not live”; in every age, in every generation the spiritual and moral highest is attainable.

It may not be superfluous to remark how the flourishing and development of the earth was impaired for the sake of mankind, and the Word of God teaches us that this deterioration kept pace with the progressive moral degeneration of the generations of mankind, and increased accordingly. So that the condition of the earth, as we now find it, is no longer the same as it originally was, and as it will again be in the future. Accordingly, every conclusion that we draw from its present condition and constitution as to what it was originally when it first emerged from the Creator’s Hands is, to say the least, risky, and is based on a false premise. But equally unjustified is the conclusion concerning men in their former harmonious condition and those living in circumstances nearly approaching these original ones, drawn from mankind in its present condition where it has to struggle אפו בזעת to wrest an existence from an unfriendly Nature. When in Israel’s Land under the influnece of God’s Torah men could live in surroundings somewhat similar to a modified paradise, we saw men like Elijah and Isaiah and a whole line of illustrious men arise, who lifted up their eyes to God, and to whom God allowed His Word to come, and they were men of flesh and blood as we are, mortal men born of mortal parents. Forming an idea of God, and elevating earthly life up to God and Godliness by the moral power given to every human being, that is the sum total of the Book of God and of the Divine Rule.

V. 20. חוה. The piel form of חיה, giving life. It had just been made clear to Adam that he would not live for ever, that he would die. It had been further said to him that his wife would bear him children. Thereupon he named his wife “the life-giver”. Individuals die, mankind lives, and it is through Woman that Man lives on in children. Adam could well have railed at his wife for the loss of Paradise and he calls her by the loveliest calling of Woman! Man had been allotted renunciation, Woman had been allotted renunciation, but the purpose for which Woman had been given renunciation was the higher; she had become the saviour from death, the dispenser of life, in her the immortality of mankind took refuge. And, significantly, she is not called חיה but חוה .חוה is always referring to giving spiritual life, to animating the mind, אֲתַוֶךּ ,יחוה דעת. It is accordingly looking at Woman as אם, as the conditio sine qua non, in every respect, not only for the physical bodily continuance of the race, but also for the spiritual and intellectual perpetuation of the higher calling of mankind. היתה can only be meant to refer to the mission in life which has just been given her.

V. 21. Here we see clothing mentioned for the second time, as the final farewell to Paradise; and here in a fuller manner. Before it was merely חגורה, covering for the lower part of the body. In between, an announcement had been made which increased the requirement for clothing, for ארורה האדמה, Nature had become raw, and here clothes receive their double importance, as requirements for protection against the consciousness of shame, and against inclemencies of Nature. But as Man received clothing from ה׳ א׳ from the Hand of God, it gets a holy spiritual meaning, and in reference to both its meanings it is in service of the education of mankind, for winning it back to its original condition. As covering for the animal nakedness it reminds one of Man’s calling being something higher than of an animal, a reminder that had become the more necessary as the mind itself had now to be occupied with the requirements of the body בזעת אפך תאכל לחם since the struggle for existence had commenced. As protection against the effects of inclement Nature it serves equally as a reminder that Man is no longer, and not yet, that which he originally was supposed to be. Created without covering, Nature about him was meant to smile benignantly and mildly to him in a paradise-like temperate atmosphere, and as long as he required clothing, it was an admonition to him that we no longer live in Paradise, and the curse does not recede from the earth as long as we have to be ashamed of the animal within us. From this point of view it can be understandable that (ב״ר כ׳) ר׳ מאיר could call this garment כתנות אור “A garment of light”, and by others be called “a priestly garment”. לו הקב׳׳ה בגדי כהונה שעשה, just because of the enlightening and sanctifying purpose of clothes. It is further understandable how the conception of garment can be used in the תנ״ך so symbolically and meaningly, similarly to the pregnant symbolism of the בגדי כהונה, thus we find בגדי צדקה, בגדי ישע and others. Further, that just מצות ציצית, — that מצוה which is to remind us not to follow that serpent-whisper of the argument of our sensuous speculation: Has not God given you, in yourself, in your own nature, a light and a guide, your eye and your heart — that just מצות ציצית is attached to garments.
