Compare ותרא האשה כי טוב העץ למאכל וכי תאוה הוא לעינים and ולא תתורו אתרי לבבכם ואחרי עיניכם וגו׳ “If your clothing tells you that you are a Man, and that the animal within you is not to be the ruler, if it tells you that the world about you, in spite of all inventions, has not become a paradise again, then let ציץ, that “blossom” on your garment, represent the holy Jewish life that brings out the godly-human element within you and bring the world again nearer to Paradise”. Thus could the ציצית-garment express itself in its obvious connection with the origin of clothes as here depicted. Our sages remind us on this verse, how here the first trace of גמילות חסד occurs, how God Himself practised גמילות חסד, the active form of deeds of love amongst mankind. They say the Torah begins and ends with examples of גמילות חסד shown us by God. It shows us at the beginning, how God clothed the first naked human beings, and at the end how He buried the noblest human being קבורת מתים-מלביש ערומים. If up till now we have considered — and not without justification — the altered condition of Nature to mankind as a lowered condition, still this condition has another aspect to it. For, on the other hand, just this lowering has given him the opportunity of showing himself in his nearest likeness to God. Everything which, when done selfishly for ourselves, is lowering, becomes divinely great when done for others. Slaving away בזעת אפו straining ones strength to provide bread and happiness for others is, according to Jewish ideas, the greatest “likeness to God” that Man exercises. “Even as God showed you that He clothed the naked, healed the sick, comforted the troubled, buried the dead, so shall you, likewise, clothe the naked, heal the sick, comfort the afflicted, bury the dead etc.”, that is the conception and principle of Jewish love of fellow-man, of Jewish גמילות חסדים. It is this thought which has constituted the Jewish people into the oldest Benevolent Society, the oldest meetings for humanitarian purposes, with members all over the world. Thus the hardship of life, the need for assistance, has become the basis on which everybody, who so wills, can elevate himself to God-like heights. The fact that the practice of this disinterested, unselfish, personal sacrifice of one’s own powers for the benefit of others, has found, and still finds, so many souls willing and eager to render such service, is the most speaking refutation of that gloomy lie that, by Man’s first sin, humanity had been cursed, and had been doomed to lose the pure godliness of his being for all future generations. So that it is a piece of profound wisdom on the part of our sages when they associate the teaching, the lofty conception of גמילות חסדים, just here with the departure from Paradise, for without the need for assistance which thereby began for mankind, we would hardly know where there would be any opportunity for the practice of ג״ה.

V. 22. The way to take כאחד ממנו is obscure. It is generally understood to be: “as one of us”, which is linguistically justified, similarly to ומת אחד מתם, אל אחד מבניו etc. The plural would then refer to the angels, and then, as we believed the eating of the tree had in no way given the first human any higher knowledge which they had not previously possessed, we would have to take the sense to be: — Man has behaved like one of us to know for himself what is good and what is bad. This way of taking it is old. Already in ב״ר כ״א Rab. Papis explained the כאחד ממנו as ממלאכי השרת כאהד. But Rab. Akiba, with the words דייך פפיס, at once reproved him for the impropriety of placing God Himself in one line with the angels regarding insight into good and evil. When, then he was demanded to give his opinion as to the meaning of הן האדם היה כאחד ממנו, Rab. Akiba replied שנתן לו המקום שני דרכים דרך החיים ודרך המות ובירר לו דרך המות (this is the version in the ילקוט). “God had placed two paths before him to choose from, the path of life and the path of death, and he chose the latter”. This explanation, which, according to its sense, seems so much more to be recommended, may also be more literally found in the words than seems at first apparent. אַחַד always designates: one out of two or more. ממנו means equally “of it”, and can very well be used in the senses of the Rabbinic term כל כמיניה, and mean according to his choice, his decision. אחד ממנו would accordingly mean, the one of the two choices which had been given for his decision, and היה כאחד ממנו, “he has become like one of the alternatives which were left to his choice”. God had left it for him to decide, of his own free-will, whether he would defer to the Will of God in determining what was good, what bad, and thereby tread the path of life, or decide himself what was good or evil and thereby have to be fated to death. Now he had decided that he would know himself what was good and evil. But with this decision he had also decided his ultimate fate. Created outside Paradise, his being placed in Paradise was only a test to set before him these two ways of life. Inside Paradise, in a Paradisal life, Paradise is not to be regained, only in עצבון, in the school of self sacrifices lies the way to the regaining of the pure greatness of Man. ארורה, with hostility is Nature now to stand towards him, his life is to be one of struggle and exertion. In these new conditions, death is a welcome friendly relief from the continuous toil and moil of life, to live for ever, would be no blessing, God’s Love does not leave him in the vicinity of the eternally regenerating fruit of the tree of life. Simply forbidding him to eat it would be no protection, he would, in spite of it, stretch forth his hand to the forbidden fruit. שלח יד is usually unlawfully laying one’s hand on an object.

V. 23. God, as ה׳א׳ sent him out. The same Divine Love which had set him in the Garden of Eden, that same Love sent him out of it. He, ה׳ א׳ had, from the beginning, created him for both possibilities, either for faithful obedience in Paradise, or for the education for it in the world outside. Hence, also, אשד לקח משם, the world outside was no new stage for him. It was the place on which, and for which, he had been created. In Paradise he had only learnt to know the goal, the state of bliss on earth, for which he was to mature in the school of renunciation and self-sacrifice. This state of complete happiness of life on earth, this life in Paradise, is something of which all the peoples of the world have retained some intuitive presentiment.

V. 24. ויגרש is probably not the actual removal out of Paradise but the greater separation from God. Man, obeying own senses and passions is set on his own feet, to let him find out, in the school of renunciation, the necessity for the guidance of God, and to feel again the longing for the nearness of God.

לשמור את דרך עץ החיים can mean, to protect the way to the tree of life so that Man shall not find it, but it can also mean, to protect and preserve the way so that it shall not be lost for mankind, so that he will be able to find it again, and ultimately go back again on it. The indications of our חכמים point to this latter meaning. כרובים always appear as the bearers of the Glory of God revealing itself to mankind, intervening in human affairs. כרובים protected the “Tree of Life” in the rejuvenated temporary Paradise, the מקדש, as here they kept the way to the tree of life, that it should not be lost for mankind. כרובים were behind the קרשי המשכן, behind the walls of the Tabernacle. In accordance with the words כתלנו הנה הוא עומד אחר there too they are the bearers of the Divine Glory “the angels whom He sends to help us on all our ways”. And if our sages let us see in them the form of human children, כרביא, and on the other hand דמות יעקב the ideal of Jacob appearing supporting the Throne of the Glory of God, the conception lies to hand to take כרובים to represent the idea of humanity being the bearers of the Glory of God. It, the Divine Glory, is also depicted as יושב תהלות ישראל being enthroned on the homage of Israel. Here too, it says הכרובים, the Cherubim, as being already known to Israel from the Temple when they took over the responsibility for the Word of God, the Torah. — ואת להט החרב המתהפכת, compare Judges 7,13 מתהפך במחנה מדין צלל לחם שעורים, “a cake of barley bread (referring to the sword of Gideon, see V. 14 I.L.) is rolling to and fro in the camp of Midian”. Now, as here it does not speak of the flame of a sword rolling to and fro, but of the sword, it would refer to the ever recurring trouble and sorrow, and especially social (חרב) trouble, against which mankind, left to itself, fights in vain. And so, by the Cherubim and the sword rolling to and fro, the two factors could be given, by which God keeps the way to the tree of Life open for mankind, and finally makes them set themselves right on that path. החרב המתהפכת, trouble, worry, pain, derangement, disturbance in general, that recurs again and again. Immediately, as soon as we foresook the realm of Paradise we meet the blood-stained realm of human history. Its first incident is fratricide. Trouble, not personal individual trouble, but in general, the unrest, feeling of insecurity of mankind in general, paves the way for the recognition that it is only by casting one’s eyes above, and univeral submission to the Law of the One Highest One, that eternal life can be found here below in this world. If general happiness, eternal life and peace were associated with the passions and the self-conceit of mankind depending on their own imagined self-sufficiency, if הבל, “futility” could not be expressed on all the great events of history, the way to the tree of eternal life would be lost to mankind. דדך חיים תוכחות מוסר, “the way to Life leads over trouble”. Accordingly להט החרב המתהפכת, would be the negative result of world-history. The second, the Cherubim, would be the traces of the revelation of God, which are sent from time to time to mankind, those signs of the Finger of God by which chastened mankind gets an inkling of, and sees, the Hand of God in the course of history. This would be the positive means of instruction of God’s arrangements for the education of mankind. The two together, the sword and the Cherubim protect and guard the way to the tree of life. Taking the whole verse together it would mean: — God severed His direct contact with Man, but He took steps — established the Cherubim and the Sword — to keep the way open back to the Tree of life. In תנא דבי אליהו and ויקרא רבה ט׳ the sages designate the road that leads to the tree of life still more definitely, as דרך ארץ, as the way of culture, the way of that social refinement which results from people living together in the world, as being the first tutor and educator to morals, manners and order. כ״ו דורות so runs the signficant saying of דרך זו דרך ארץ ואח״ב עץ החיים זו תורה ר׳ ישמעאל בר רב נחמן, קדמה דרך ארץ את התורה הה״ד לשמור את דרך עץ החיים,. “Twenty six generations did דרך ארץ precede the תורה, for it says, cherubim and sword were established to keep the way to the tree of life; but the way is culture, and only then can one reach to the tree of life, to the Torah”. Culture starts the work of educating the generations of mankind and the Torah completes it; for the Torah is the most finished education of Man. The fig-leaf and apron, those first gifts which Man possessed on his way to education, were the first appurtenances of culture, and culture in the service of morality is the first stage of Man’s return to God. For us Jews, דרך ארץ and תורה are one. The most perfect gentleman and the most perfect Jew, to the Jewish teaching, are identical. But in the general development of mankind culture comes earlier. The “Sword and the Cherubim”, the exigencies of life and the intuition of Something Higher in life lead the generation of mankind to the path of culture which ultimately opens onto the tree of life. That is why the Jew rejoices whenever and wherever culture elevates people to a perception of true values and to nurture goodness. But of course where culture and civilastion are used in the service of sensuality the degeneration only gets all the greater. But still such misuse of culture does not do away with the intrinsic value and blessing of דרך ארץ, for אם אין דרך ארץ אין תורה. Therefore Jews, too, are to attach themselves to, and love all good and true culture and by the ways and manner of their behaviour and demeanour appear as educated people, and show that being a Jew is only a higher stage of being a man. And of course, on the other side too, אם אין תורה אין דרך ארץ, if culture and education instead of leading to תורה, take the place of it, then it is not the way that leads to the Tree of Life, but is the way that leads to degeneration.

V. 1.—2. קניתי איש את ה׳. The original conception of ownership rests on production. Man’s primary capital is his strength. Hence קנה in its first meaning is not acquisition by money but by strength, power, energy. Thus God is קונה שמים וארץ. He is the Owner of heaven and earth because He created them. So, too, קנה is the stalk or stipe which produce the blossom and seed-box. So, too, here: With God, i.e. with God’s assistance and co-operation I have acquired a male human being by the expenditure of my strength. So the first enthusiasm of the first mother was a raised feeling of self importance, and the question can arise in our minds whether this feeling does not already show some clouding of the pure conception of motherhood. A mother, standing on the pure height of consciousness of duty, would have thought more of God and of the new duties and tasks which come with this gift of God, rather than proudly of her own merit. A clouding of the point of view, and a disclosure of egotism and vanity which very easily may have affected the tendency of the character of the son, on whose very name she imprinted the stamp of this self-esteem. For קין is derived from קון, property. — As the verb ידע is in the past tense, Cain would have been born before the dismissal from Paradise, and in the ecstasy of her joy the mother called him קין, what she herself had achieved, acquired by herself. When the second son was born, the world already stared at the parents full of worries, in which a child can be an additional burden. Eve’s heart was heavy when she called her second son הבל, “transitoriness”. Cf. Sanhedrin 38b תוספות. (According to another opinion Cain and Abel were twins, and both born while still in Paradise, see ב״ר, Ch. 22). — הבל, related to עפל ,אפל ,אבל the basic conception of which is checking, restraining, that which checks all entry of light is אפל, dark, — the high wall which checks access is העפיל ;עפל to restrain yourself, to put yourself in opposition. אבל, but, the particle of opposition. אבל, grief, the feeling of a broken state of life. Hence also חבל, the chain. הבל, existence checked in its continuity, transitoriness.

רעה .ויהי הבל רעה צאן is, at the same time, the root of leading to pasture, grazing, thinking, and neighbour. Grazing, i.e. going about seeking food i.e. that which is suitable to restore us, to be assimilated by us. Hence also רעיון רֵעַ: mental grazing, seeking mental nourishment, i.e. seeking that which, as being true, we can absorb into our minds, pondering, considering. Further רעה: to go about with somebody, to seek what is necessary and sufficing for our social requirements. רעה רוח, to find what satisfies your social requirements in “wind”, in empty things. רֵעַ designates our neighbour, our fellowman, inasmuch as he finds in us, and we in him, what is necessary for us, that which should be mutually complementary. It is also worth noting that רעה occurs referring both to the animals, and to the shepherd, and also to the pasturage. ירעם גרן ויקב לא Hosea 9,2, “the granary and the winepress afford them no pasturage, shall not feed them”.

It may seem remarkable that here it speaks first of Abel, although Cain was the first-born, and in the following verse he is mentioned first. But the most natural occupation which we should have expected to be followed would be agriculture. It was to this that Man was specially directed לעבוד את האדמה as the means of obtaining his food. Cain took up this natural occupation. But Abel turned to another occupation, which could be the reason for its nature to be prominently brought to our notice. Cain’s occupation was the more natural one, more self-understood. But as we are told hardly anything more of this first pair of brothers — whom we shall immediately find in such sharp contrast to each other — than this contrast of occupation, it may wish to indicate that just in that may lie a contrast of character, way of thinking and tendencies which, later on, in the development of peoples has shown itself sharply with striking clarity. We mean the contrast of agricultural and pastoral peoples, which, sure enough can be seen in its beginning in this first pair of brothers, who separated from each other just in this difference of their occupations. Agriculture calls primarily for the expenditure of all one’s bodily strength and energies. The verdict “in the sweat of thy contenance, etc.” is quite specially and literally carried out in the agricultural labourer. He becomes totally absorbed in his “profession” of gaining a scanty subsistence for his bodily requirements, and what we found of pride of possession, and pride of one’s own accomplishment, in the conception of קנה ,קין, is most predominently to the fore in the occupation of agriculture. The soil, fertilised with his own sweat is something which is precious to him, it contains part of his very self, it chains him, he becomes stationary, earthbound. On the one hand, however, all the great advances in the development of culture have been stimulated by agriculture, and a great part of the inventions and arts have been evoked by it. By personal contact society, the state, administration of justice all come into being. By the verdict given to Man after his dismissal from Paradise, “לעבוד את האדמה״, the most important die was cast for the future development of mankind. But on the other hand, working on the land always has the tendency to lower the agricultural worker more and down to the level of the clod which he serves. In bending his neck under the yoke of the effort to attain real property his soul too becomes bowed. He gets caught by this effort. It begets subjugation, one man enslaved by the other. At the same time the worker on the land comes to worship the forces of Nature on whose influence the success of the fields he serves is visibly dependent. The agricultural peoples were the first to lose the pure consciousness of God and humanity, there slavery and polytheism were first begotten. — In contrast, pastoral life has its advantages Already the fact that it deals only with living creatures whose care and attention call for, and keep alive, all the humane feelings of tenderness and consideration, is no small advantage. The instability of the property as such, as well as the fact that it does not owe its existence, but only its care, to human beings is a protection against placing too much value on property and its owners. The occupation does not make such a demand on the expenditure of actual strength, is not such a strain on the mind in service of the work, and gives the mind opportunity for elevating thoughts of godliness and goodness. Thus we find our patriarchs as shepherds, and a Moses and a David with the flocks. Towards it we find the hatred of Egypt directed to shepherds and pastoral people. All the results of agricultural work indicated above existed in Egypt developed to the highest degree. There a culture founded and built up on agriculture had been formed, polytheism and a slavish system of caste and subjugating man under man were its characteristics. A man was tightly bound to his occupation. A man in himself, his worth as a human being, his free right to arrange his life, to decide his career for himself, was lost. He was born a slave to his inherited occupation. The conception of God and freedom, and of Man’s likeness to God, was only retained by a race of shepherds — our forefathers. The Egyptian politicians knew quite well what they were about when they instilled an unconquerable aversion to pastoral peoples in the minds of their people. So it worked out later on. Can we perhaps deduce backwards from this that it was perhaps his nature and his character that induced Abel to become a shepherd? But, on the whole, of course, Man was directed to husbandry rather than to the life of a shepherd. Israel, too, in the תורה and through the תורה. But there, in the Torah, all the adverse habits, the tendency to become a clod-hopper, and also to worship the possession of property, is worked against and prevented. There, the Sabbath days and the Sabbath years are external evidence that the soil, and the power to work it, belong, not to Man but to God. The agricutural laws, such as כלאים and ערלה, and, on the other hand, לקט שכחה ופאה, are a constant reminder of Him, and an admonition to humaneness and brotherly love. By these and other laws the Torah solves the problem of an agricultural state serving God, of a nation united in freedom and fraternal equality. But, outside the realm of the תורה, the pure consciousness of God and the freedom and equality of Man was endangered.
So Abel became a shepherd, but Cain “the man of property” was an agriculturist.

V. 3—6. מנחה. Amongst the offerings, Mincha is specially an offering of flour and oil. But, although seldom, offerings in general, animal offerings too, are called מנחה; thus in Malachi 1,10, 13, II,13 and generally in Malachi. Outside the sphere of the Temple, מנחה means a gift given as a sign of the recognition, the allegiance of a subordinate to a superior. The derivation is rather difficult.

This is the first time we hear of an offering. Let us note two things. No idolatry existed as yet, so that the opinion that offerings are only to be explained as a concession to polytheism is at once shown to be untrue. Offerings are older than polytheism. They are as old as mankind, and so must be the natural expression of pure human feelings and thoughts. Further, here, at once, at the first offering, we find a rejected offering next to one received with satisfaction (in exactly the same way, at the first offerings at the consecration of the Tabernacle, the rejected offering of the priestly youths came in the midst of those that were well-pleasing to God). So that, from the very beginning, no absolute value in itself was laid on offerings as such. So that the opinion that it was only the prophets who deserved the merit of giving the teaching that offerings have only a relative value, is a misrepresentation, the untruth of which is shown by facts. Of course it is true that pagans offered sacrifices, but so did they pray, and a great deal would have to be given up, if everything was to be abandoned which was misused and debased in the hands of spiritually and morally degenerated circles. It all depends on the spirit, the idea in which offerings and prayers are offered. Two people can bring exactly identical offerings, pray exactly the same prayers, and still present themselves to God in infinite dissimilarity. That is clear just here at the very first offering. It does not say here: God turned to Abel’s offering, and did not turn to Cain’s offering, but He turned to Abel and his offering but to Cain and his offering He did not turn. The essential difference lay in the person of the offerer not in the offering itself. Cain’s attitude was unpleasing and therefore his offering was unpleasing too.

Perhaps some nuances in what is told us reveal a difference in the attitude of the two brothers. It was מקץ ימים, after some time had passed, accordingly, after a time in which Cain’s fields and Abel’s flocks had flourished under God’s blessing. So there was occasion for an offering of acknowledgment. Cain brings to God מפרי האדמה, some of the produce of the earth, any, without choice. After all he must offer God too, “something”. This shows that objectionable attitude which Malachi later on censures so severely. The attitude which looks on our relationship to God and the godly, “religion”, as it is called, as something which also belongs to our affairs, something which is not to be entirely left out, and so we can devote just the “spare moments of life” to it, and give “the lame and the sick, and whatever else is useless” to it. וניבו נבזה אכלו is how Malachi describes it, “All that the Altar gets, is food which otherwise is despised”. It is that allegiance which is only brought by fear, which supports temple and church in the same spirit as it builds hospitals and prisons. — But Abel took מבכורות צאנו ומחלביהן, took some of the firstlings of his flock, and of those the very best. He who brings the first and the best, places his relationship to God and the godly in the foreground, for him this relationship is the first and most important, to which all the rest of his life is only accessory; more, offering the “first” is always taken in the Torah as representative dedication of all the rest. Thus we find it explicitly said in Ex. 34,19. וכל מקנך תזכר פטר שור ושה, “the whole of your herd shall be dedicated (cf. אזכרה and מזכיר לבונה) by the firstborn of ox and sheep”. — Moreover, it says: והבל הביא גם הוא. This גם הוא “also he”, shows quite clearly that we should not have expected Abel on his part, to have also brought an offering. If we are justified in drawing conclusions from the later meaning of the בכור, the firstborn did not bring offerings for himself alone but on behalf of the whole family, and here too, Abel could and should have been represented in Cain’s offering. In a remarkeable manner we find everywhere, as here too, the בכור, who was appointed to be the bearer of the material and spiritual representation of the family home, rejected. So with עשו ,קין ,ראובן and all the בכורים in Israel in the wilderness. And still, originally it was meant to be otherwise! We can accordingly well say that only when כל סיר בירושלים וביהודה קדש “when every pot in Jerusalem and Judah shall be holy”, (Zachariah 14,21), only when the whole of life is lived dedicated to holiness unto God, then indeed we may expect that just those who will be the representatives of the home life (the pots and pans I.L.) of homes which will have no other owners than God, they, eo ipso, will be the most priestly, the most absorbed in and devoted to God. But as long as life is not completely penetrated with spirituality and thoughts of God it is to be feared — and has actually occurred — that just the bearer of the material side of life, those who are called on to found the welfare of the family, who have the responsibility for the material welfare do not become at the same time the most fitting bearers of the priestly calling. Only when that one comes who will come as a “growth” (צמח I.L.) of the ages, who will bear on his head simultaneously the dual crown of priest and King, who will be “a priest upon his throne”, only then will the two callings fall harmoniously into one. Until that time arrives “the two crowns will only hang as a reminder in the Temple of the Lord”, (Zach. 6,12-14). So, here too, we should have expected that Abel would have been included and represented in Cain’s offering and that there would have been no occasion for him to bring a separate one. But if in spite of that it is stressed that Abel גם הוא, he also brought an offering, then either Abel did not feel himself represented in Cain’s offering, or Cain, caught up in his egoism, did not want to include him also. From what follows the first supposition seems more likely.

חֵלֶב fat, has the same root as חָלָב milk. חֵלֶב is the overflow of nourishment which the animal organism does not use up at the moment, and separates out for future use, it is the reserve capital of the animal. חָלָב is the complete nourishing material which the organism separates out for a new animal. חָלָב is the חֵלֶב for the young, חֵלֶב is the חָלָב for the aged. It is very significant that חלב is only fat which is set aside, separated out of the tissues by itself, תותב קרום ונקלף. The fat that grows in together with the rest of the organism, forms an integral part of, and belongs to the living organism, and is not חלב.

שעה does not occur again in a similar connection. But we do find פנה אל מנחה. Thus with Korach, תפן אל מנחתם, where again the בכור and the כהן appointed by God stand in contrast before God. But פנה is much stronger, the whole turning, the direction of the whole of one’s attention, while שעה is only a momentary turning towards.

ויחר, literally: “this burnt Cain very much”. חרה is the feeling of irritation, anger, which an occurrence which we consider wrong provokes in us. נפל פנים does not occur elsewhere. It is most likely the opposite of נשא פנים and probably express not so much a feeling of suffering from a wrong, as downcast, dejection, depression. They are accordingly two different feelings and appear as such in God’s questioning: “Why art thou angered at the past, and why so depressed and hopeless for the future?”.

V. 7. According to the cantillation, with the word רובץ one sentence is concluded and with ואליך a second sentence begins, which, however, can be connected with the first one. Further, again according to the cantillation, the לפתח חטאת רובץ is in no closer relation to ואם לא תיטיב than it is to אם תיטיב; and the accent on תיטיב shows שאת to be more the object of תיטיב than a consequent clause of a conditional sentence. Now as נשא is a very frequent expression for bringing an offering, נשא מנחה, it could very well mean: whether you bring a good offering or not a good one, sin lieth before the door. But as we shall see, לפתח חטאת רובץ does not express the danger of sin crouching at the door threatening to spring, but rather the reverse, another way of taking it recommends itself, which, moreover, throws a clearer light over the incident, and is in close connection with what went before.

We find the word שאת having the meaning of a specially privileged position, an honour, יתר שאת, in Jacob’s last speech about Reuben, and indeed there too it is referring to the privilege of the firstborn, and just at the moment in which Reuben, the בכור is declared unworthy of that honoured position. Exactly the same here. Cain, as the firstborn, had brought the “Offering of the Year” (מקץ ימים). In that Abel was included as being represented too. But Abel הביא גם הוא, Abel did not see in Cain’s offering the expression of his sentiments, so he also brought an offering, an offering chosen in a different manner which expressed a different feeling, a different point of view. This offering was a silent protest against Cain’s worthiness for the honoured privileges of the firstborn. And God, in turning to Abel and not turning to Cain, thereby confirmed Abel’s worthiness and Cain’s unworthiness. This annoyed Cain and depressed him. But God said to him: Why does this annoy you, and why does it depress you with such hopelessness? (It is only momentarily, only לפי שעה that I turned to Abel and not to you also. As already remarked, it says וישע not ויפן). It still lies in your own hands. It only depends whether you will use the specially privileged position which is due to you by birth and position (for, after all, as remarked above, agricultural work is the more pre-eminent calling, more fully corresponding to the calling of mankind) in a good way or in a way that is not good. (ואם לא תיטיב I.L.).

לפתח חטאת רובץ. But whichever way one decides to take וגו׳ הלא אם תיטיב, in any case לפתח חטאת רובץ ואליך תשוקתו וגו׳ seems to have found a most deplorable misconception, against which one cannot protest too strongly. How, in certain circles, has this sentence been twisted to be used as a support, “from the bible itself”, of the theory that there is an element of evil lurking in the world, like a wild beast, is lying in wait for men, full of avidity to spring upon them, eager to overpower them and “bring about their fall” ! And yet on mature thorough reflection and study, the sentence expresses the very opposite.

Compare all the places where רבץ referring to animals occurs. Not one single instance can one find where it has the meaning of a lurking, lying-in-wait attitude. Without exception it refers just to the most peaceful, undisturbed resting, with no incitement to attack or molest. Equally so, תשוקה is not only never the expression for a hostile eagerness, but for the longing for a most valued possession, the most devoted longing for love! אני לדודי ועלי תשוקתו “I belong to my beloved and his desire is for me” sings the Songs of Songs. And luckily enough, just a few verses previously, exactly a similar sentence with the very same words is used for the relation to exist of the wife to her husband ואל אישך תשוקתך והוא ימשל בך where certainly it does not wish to say that there is to be an eternal condition of war between them, that the wife is just longing to overcome her husband, but that he, as the stronger, will come off the victor, but surely it rather pictures the longing of a loving wife who finds the completion of her most intimate self just in subordinatingly devoting her life to the work and efforts and the direction of her husband. And ten verses after are the same words to have exactly the opposite meaning? Surely not.

Aptly is חטאת, sin, the appeal of the senses, here given the masculine gender, רובץ. Its power is not to be underestimated. It has the power to master you, but it remains quietly behind your door. It does not come in to you by itself, uninvited. If it is at home with you, yea, finally to become the master of your house, you must in the first instance have invited it in, set a chair for it at your table. By itself it remains quietly before your door. More, all its desire is, that you should master it and direct it. God has given sensuality an appeal to your senses, not that it should master and direct you, but that you should master and direct it, not that you should suppress or kill it, but תמשל, regulate it, rule over it and direct it. That is its whole purpose and calling. By you mastering it and guiding it, it achieves its purpose, and that is why it longs to achieve it. For there is not a single natural tendency in Man which is, in itself, either good or bad. And truly, the attraction which satisfying the urge of his senses has for Man is by no means one of the least salubrious, nay, necessary, elements for his high calling. If all good were sweet, and all evil bitter, our whole virtue would be no more than the natural unfree following of that which attracted our senses, and the whole nobility of being a human being would be lost. And it is just on the correct control and use of our natural tendencies that the loftiest purposes of our life down here are found. So that in truth the relationship between Man and his passions should be essentially not unlike that between husband and wife. A man should be freely affianced to his sensuality, so as, under his guidance, together with it, to achieve the highest purposes of his life. Not for nothing does the Holy Script use the same terms in reference to these two relationships. Yea, after all this, it seems possible that the whole sentence would mean: “See, whether you will take up your privilege for good or for bad, for that, sensuality waits before your door, its desire is directed towards you, longing for you to master it.” For actually נשא is also used with the meaning of “taking up to oneself”, as in לא חמור אחד מתם נשאתי, more, it also quite specially designates taking a wife home in marriage, as: וישאו להם נשים מואביות (Ruth 1,4) and elsewhere.

This desire of the power of sin and sensuality to achieve the purpose for which it was designed, by being mastered by mankind, is beautifully pictured by our sages and pithily expressed by: יורד ומסית עולה ומשטין, “Satan comes from God and tempts human beings, and when they have yielded to his temptations, he goes up and accuses them and complains to God”; for he had not enticed them for them to succumb to him, but that they should conquer him and take him under their mastery. Quite this same point of view is expressed by ר׳ סימון in ב״ר on our verse כבר הכתבתי בתורה ואליך תשוקתו וגו׳ כאילו בראת את ב׳ עולמות תצור שלום אין כתיב כאן אלא שלום שלום א״ת שאינו ברשותך להשתיקך שמחהו בדברי תורה שנאמר יצר םמוך תצור שלום ואם עשית כן מעלה אני עליך אם בא יצרך. “if Satan comes to entice you to sin, make him glad with the words of the Torah: for its says (Is. 26,3) ‘with thy controlled sensuality thou keepeth peace’; and then it will be reckoned unto you as if you were the creator of both worlds, for it does not simply say you have created שלום but dual peace שלום שלום. And if you think this is beyond your powers, has not God already pronounced in His Torah: “his longing is, to be mastered by you”.

משל: basic meaning: to declare what something is and should be, to give its character and designation. Hence: to command, to rule. The מושל directs everybody what he is to be and do. So that it is by no means synonymous with כבש, to force, to subjugate, it is rather to guide and rule. Hence also משלי שלמה: saying which tell us what men and things are and should be. So in general. But hence משל also means quite specially such a saying or sentence whose meaning refers not to the things actually described in it, but they are used metaphorically to refer to some general fact or teaching, to describe the character or designation of something else, i.e. a parable.

V. 8. We are not told what Cain told Abel. Most probably the preceding, that which God had said to him, the more so, as Abel was implicated in it, and God had declared that Abel’s preference and Cain’s rejection were something which could possibly be temporary and in no way decided as permanent.

ויהי בהיותם בשדה. It is not said at all that there was any quarrel or fight between them. The ויקם אל rather implies the contrary. It occurs once again at the incident of Saul in the cave, ולא נתנם לקום אל שאול, and there also it refers to an unexpected sudden attack. Indeed קום אל, not על, literally means, to get up, to set out, to go towards the other, and so implies that they were not at close quarters, next to one another. According to that, then, the בהיותם בשדה would simply wish to say that they were quietly engaged in their ordinary occupations, the one on his fields, the other at his flock, when suddenly the terrible idea came to Cain, he went to Abel and killed him.

V. 9. אִ אֵי. An enclosed, divided-off place. Hence אֵי the question after the place of an absentee. The whole depth of the criminal depravity and the most definite warning against family discord is expressed in God’s question‘ “Where is Abel thy brother?” and Cain’s answer. It is everbody’s duty to know where the other is. The question was quite justified even if nothing had happened. And then the answer! “I know not, am I my brother’s keeper? Cain finds it a most complete excuse that it is not his business to look after his brother, he has enough to do to look after himself! This answer, showing the most cold-blooded egoism, contains the most serious warning that the loveless principle, “Every man for himself” is not far away from that malevolent hatred which is ready to do away with his neighbour if the latter stands in the way of his own progress.

V. 10. The accent, the notation (נגינה) on קול is a separating one, disjunction. It is as much as saying: Hark! (הרכסים לבקעה, from ז״ל ר׳ ליב פ״פ) — דם .דמי אחיך from דמה to be similar, to assimilate, is that which contains the materials to be assimilated by the body, it is human body in liquid which circulates and deposits the suitable material in its appropriate place. He who murders a man spills and scatters this material containing all the components of the whole organism, hence דמים, the plural.

In verses 10, 11 and 12 the distinction between the meanings of אדמה and ארץ is sharply drawn. אדמה is the earth, regarded as the terrain entrusted to mankind to live a life on it dedicated to God. But אדמה only belongs to a man for as long as he respects the rights of every other man made in the image of God, אדמה no longer belongs to a murderer. But the earth itself as אדמה, demands from God that He should execute justice on one who destroys a man.

V. 11. And now, ארור אתה, there is no need for Me to pass sentence on you, you are already condemned inasmuch as the whole world rises up against you. In this cry of the אדמה lies your judgment. Note that it is only here that a curse is proclaimed against a human being, against the criminal. Above it was the earth that was affected by a curse for the benefit of the education of mankind. — ארר related to ערר from which we get ערער, lonely, isolated. Whereas everything flows harmoniously to the one who is ברוך, to further his happiness and prosperity, the one who is ארור is isolated, out of touch with all that which brings prosperity and the blossoming of life. מן האדמה, by the cantillation and notation, this is separated from ארור אתה, either, away from the earth etc., or, as we have translated it, by the earth etc. You are already cursed, and indeed by the earth which etc. — פצה, related to פצח ,פצע, is always a forced opening, either with repugnance, or by force of circumstances. Thus, by vows which were made in an emergency, at a crisis, as by Jephtha, ואנכי פציתי פי, so also ופוצה פה ומצפצף, even in fear and anguish, none dare open their mouth (Is. 10,15). So here too, “which had to open its mouth”, you forced it to take up the blood of your brother from your hand. מידך, Man does, in any case, come back to the earth, but from the hand of his brother, the earth does not expect the brother.

V. 12. When God placed the Earth under Man’s sway, it was to be elevated in the service of moral human purposes by the use of its powers. But crime severs the bond between earth and Man. To the criminal God says: the earth will no longer give its powers unto you. Only when Man is הדום שכינה :אדם, then the אדמה is also הדום אדם. But when Man tears the bond between himself and God asunder, then God tears asunder the bond between Man and the earth. Then Man indeed goes on living on the globe, but it is no longer הדום to him, no longer נע — .אדמה the opposite of נח, to have no place of rest, referring to the earth, to be cut off from it, to have no spot on it to call “his own”. נד, referring to mankind, to be cut off from all fellow-men. The general underlying meaning of נוד is the separation of that which is related from that to which it is related, of things which by nature belong together. To Cain, the husbandman, whose pride it was to cultivate the soil, and to extract its produce by his strength, the earth will no longer yield its powers, yea, he will have no spot on earth that he can call his own as a home. And whereas, otherwise, even the landless stranger, the גר, receives the means of existence in the brotherly love of other people, Cain is denied even this, the murderer becomes נע and נד, homeless and shunned, forsaken by earth and man.

V. 13.—14. גדול עוני מנשוא. This cannot mean: my sin is too great for it to be forgiven, as Cain gives the reason for it הן גדשת וגו׳ which in no wise speaks of the crime but solely of the punishment. Accordingly, עון has been taken to mean punishment. But it is by no means sure that this is its meaning. In any case עון as a rule means sin and not punishment. Let us take it here too as meaning sin, and the verse would then run: “My sin is greater than I can bear, see, today you have driven me etc.”. This would then give us a deep insight into the dark feelings and mind of the criminal, and, at the same time, into the justice of God. “My sin is greater than I can bear”, You have shown me how great it is, “You have driven me away today, have severed the bond that gave the earth to me as the ground for human beings, and from Your Presence too. I am not to be protected and watched over, and so, forsaken by the earth, God and man, I must fear that every creature that meets me might kill me”. Imagine Cain, just Cain, begotten in the feeling of קניתי, stamped with the character קין, brought to crime through קנאה, irritated egoism, this Cain realising that he had lost all this, had forfeited all this by his crime. He comes to the realisation of his guilt, not by the thought of what he had done to his brother, but by what he had done to himself. He is still the same Cain, would still now have said השומר אחי אנכי! “My sin is too great” says Cain, had I only murdered my brother it would be bearable, but I did not know that I had thereby murdered myself, had made myself ארור, to נע ונד, and had foreited every claim to the world or to brother-man.

The תורה imposes quite a similar result for careless manslaughter. He becomes נע in גלות if not also נד. Also כל מוצאי יהרגני is present in his constant fear of the גואל הדם should he venture forth from his exile. In the law of עגלה ערופה too, somewhat similar thoughts may be present. If murder has been committed by an unknown hand, and the muderer as it were, in mockery of the court of justice, has thrown the body, unburied, in the open, then the court has to clear itself by declaring that it had incurred no responsibility for the crime by any Sodom-like treatment of strangers. But before that declaration, by killing an עגלת אשר לא עבד בה ולא משכה בעול on hard stony ground, they had to proclaim that: in Jewish circles, the unbridled raw strength and force which will not bow itself under the yoke of the Law, is not tolerated, and the earth beneath such a one becomes hard and stony: לא תוסיף תת כחה לך!

So Cain did not recognise the sin he had committed as being so much against his brother as being against himself. That is why he called it עון, wrong, crooked. That which leads most directly to its goal and to happiness is the ישר, straight, right. Every עון is not only turning aside from our duty but also from our happiness. Thus God has ordered it.

V. 15. ויאמד לו ה׳, not אליו, unto him, but לו, concerning him, did not answer him, but proclaimed: נקם — .לכן כל הרג קין! שבעתים יוקם! — connected with קום — is the raising up of Right, Justice, which is downtrodden lying on the ground, also used referring to persons. Not the stricken one who cannot be brought back to life, but the stricken principle of Right is to be avenged, to be re-erected. He who undertakes to do that is נוקם. The Word of God, the תורה, says לא תקום, you are not to take revenge for any wrong done to you, but not that you are to refrain from taking up the avenging of wrong done to others. Hence, לכן, therefore, because the condition in which Cain has placed himself is so unbearable “listen all ye that would kill Cain to avenge the blood of Abel!” Cain is punished sevenfold heavier by being left alive, the crime is atoned-for seven times more strongly, Abel revenged seven times more strongly, than by a death which is over in a minute. The subject to יוקם is Abel, or as he is not mentioned, the murder, thereby it is thus atoned-for sevenfold! Once we do find עד יקום גוי אויביו (Jos. 10,13) where the object of נקם is not, as usual, the victim but the criminal. And so here, too, Cain could be the subject of יוקם.

וישם ה׳ לקין אות. The opinion of our sages differ as to the nature of this sign according to whether they take Cain to be a remorseful penitent or the reverse. But another way of taking it is given in the Midrash, רב explains it as עשאו אות לרצהנים, or ר׳ יוחנן as עשאו אות לבעלי תשובה, God made Cain himself into a sign or warning for murderers or penitents. We do find שום construed with ל- in this way once in Sam. I. 22,7 ישים שרי אלפים לכלכם “make you all to captains of thousands”. According to that, here too, it could mean וישם קין לאות. But even without this anomaly it could be taken to have such a meaning: “Therefore” — because Cain’s condition is such a depressing one — “let everyone who would kill him hear: thus is revenge taken on him sevenfold.” Thereby God decreed a striking condition over Cain so that nobody who met him would kill him, for everybody recognised in his distressed condition a greater deterrent sign than his death would be.

V. 16. מלפני ה׳, according to the way our sages take it, this does not mean just away from the place of the Presence of God, but altogether turned right away from Him; turned his back to God, and, banned by the earth and mankind, wished to try to found an independent life on his own. Although banished from Paradise, Man still stood לפני הי. But Cain, by his crime and his subsequent behaviour left this relationship.

We saw the Glory of God departing from Man in the west. Here we see a removal to the east, קדמת עדן, accordingly, a still greater withdrawal away from God, and thereby introducing the attempt to found an independent life based on Man’s own human powers, without God.

V. 17. It does not say ויבן עיר, he built a city, but, he became a builder of a city. With him a new enterprise started — the city. Cain had been cut off from the earth, the soil would no longer respond to his efforts; cut off from God and his fellow-men, what remained unto him? He himself was what remained for him, the stock of mental powers and abilities which was part of his personality, and from that, quite naturally the “city-builder” emerged. The city, as contrasted to the land, is quite free from the fields, from agriculture. It is a complex of human beings who make their living purely out of human powers. In cities the products of the land are transformed for human purposes, and are stamped by art and industry with the mark of human intelligence. The fields which the town-dweller has to cultivate are his powers, his mind, and his abilities. Hence these are developed as we are immediately informed in the succeeding verses. On the land the fields are “cultivated”, in the city it is the man. In the city all the slumbering capabilities of men are awakened, and men become wide awake. Perhaps that is why the city is called עיר, to be awake, and it is a literal fact that ויציצו מעיר כעשב הארץ, that “the human blossom develops in the city as the blossom of the plants on the land” (Ps. 72,16). This contrast between city and country life also appears later in the laws of the Torah. The tribe of Levi who were to have no share of the land received cities; the manslaughter, who was to be banished from the holy soil, as Cain was from the whole of the soil, was relegated to cities. Equally so the חומה בתי ערי, houses in the walled cities, were considered as not being part of the land, and like mobile possessions could be transferred permanently from hand to hand. It is accordingly, extremely characteristic that city life first began with Cain, the one who was cut off from the land and thrown back on himself. His first son made it encumbent on him to think of providing for the future, and for him there was no other way but to make a beginning of founding city life.

V. 18.—22. Here we find a whole list of generations mentioned. While the first ones laid the foundations for building up city life, in the later ones here depicted we see this life developed in its principle tendencies. In Jubal-Cain and Thubal-Cain art and industry are clearly shown. בן לוי ר׳ יהושע asserts in ב״ר that all these names designate an ever-increasing revolt of the generations against God. Taking this as a precedent, we would essay a speculation, which after all, is perhaps an empty dream. But the fact that almost the same names, only slightly modified, occur in the list of the generations of the Seth family which is given later on, does make it seem not far-fetched to think that these names are significant and have meanings. After all, the names Eve, Cain as well as later on Seth and Noah are expressly mentioned as having meanings. This speculation, that the names are meant to designate something, is perhaps all the more not to be rejected, as we are told nothing at all more about these generations than their names.

חנוך. Cain had been relegated to the stock of powers and abilities which God had made innate in every human being. This was all there, but it had to be developed. He called his son חנוך, initiation, practice, training.

עירד. The training, education to culture finds resistance from the freedom-loving younger generation. An עירד-generation follows תנוך; a generation that is like ערוד the wild ass (Job 39,5 I.L.), that shows itself obstreperous towards cuture. Possibly the exceptional term ויולד (in the the passive, not the usual ילד) “Irad was born unto him”, used here, indicates that, the generation deteriorating, it became עירד against Enoch’s will.

מחיאל=מחויאל. Irad begat Mechujael, מחוי אל in which godliness was extinguished, מהי אל who extinguished godliness. When the generation that freed itself from culture was young, it was מחויאל, passive, godliness was extinguished in it, but later when it was older it was מחייאל, active, tried to do away with godliness in general. It was followed by a generation of מתו) מתושאל the root of מתים), seeking masses of people.
למך. When masses of people were formed למך followed, the etymology of which is completely obscure. But he had three sons:

יובל ,יבל, and תובל קין whose names, all three of them, are formed from the root יבל. What the two latter sons accomplished for furthering the development of town life is quite clear. At the base of all industry lies Tubal Cain’s invention of metal cutting instruments. The father of all Art which elevates human nature, was Jubal. More doubtful is that which told us of Jabal, that he was יושב אהל ומקנה. This is usually taken, as רש״י does, to refer to the life of nomads. But we find יושב אהל used referring to Jacob as being just the opposite of the open-air life of an איש שדה. Now מקנה is also used in its original meaning of buying and selling, earning, acquiring. So that it is possible, taking מקנה as trade, that Jabal was the first merchant. But even without that, איש מקנה could very well designate the industrial side of cattle breeding, the substantial dealer in the market, consonnant with city culture, in contrast to ריצה צאן, the more nomad shepherd. Thus Joseph says, the Egyptians despise all רועה צאן, and still Pharaoh had flocks, and all the Egyptians had מקנה הצאן and מקנה הבקר which they brought to Joseph in the years of famine in exchange for corn. So it was not having or breeding cattle as such to which the Egyptians objected but to the pastoral life of the nomads. It was quite in keeping with Egyptian policy to inculcate their people with hatred towards all wandering landless people. Very significant too, is how Joseph decribes his brothers to Pharaoh in Ch. 46,32 רעי צאן כי אנשי מקנה היו וצאנם ובקרם וכל אשר להם הביאו והאנשים: “True now they are homeless nomadic shepherds, but up till now they were established possessors of flocks and herds”. Similarly Joseph impressed on his brothers that they were to tell Pharaoh, that they, and their forefathers before them had been אנשי מקנה. Now of course, their property was mobile, now they are רעי צאן, but only because they have emigrated with their herds and flocks. In any case is is worthy of note that livestock is called מקנה so that in Jabal we can greet the first man of property, the first business man. All three names are formed from the root יבל .יבל means to bring, to bring home, to bring in, hence יבול: produce.
a. יבל is the personal active form; the one who brings something in, who creates things of value, produces.
b. יובל passive, the opposite of יבל, who is dependent for יבול, he produces nothing, things are brought to him.
c. תובל, nouns formed with ת as a rule indicate not the person who acts, but the abstract conception of an activity or of a condition, hence here: producing in itself.
So that here by these names all the various activities of men may be indicated.

a. יבל, the productive, wealth-bringing status of producers and merchants, the earning classes. But as soon as culture rises above the creating for the absolute necessities of life, an activity develops that brings nothing in, does nothing to increase the wealth, the מקנה of mankind. This activity here, as

b. יובל is introduced by the harp and flute as music, accordingly Art. To the Cainite world, cut off from God, it is just as necessary as handicraft. By external stimulation it endeavours to bring back the same internal harmony which had departed from Man with his departure from God. Especially music, which expresses neither forms nor ideas, but only moods and feelings, and just thereby works ennoblingly on the mind, as it brings and awakes finer feelings to it, and acts, like all art and beauty, as a preliminary stage in educating mankind back to goodness and truth. Already the fact that it produces no actual wealth, so that יובל has to be supported for the means of his existence by the אנשי מקנה. Art, in the Cainite world, represents the Truth that Man has still higher requirements than material possessions.
But the condition for all this, for a. and b., for industry and art is:

c. תובל. He creates nothing that one can directly enjoy or use, he creates the means for all progress and art, he creates creating, he creates the tools and instruments for industry and art. He is the real Tubal-Cain, the real production of Cain, the pride of the Cainite generation. God had taken the earth away from Cain. It will no longer yield its יבול to him. But now he no longer requires it. His own mind is now his field. And by his production of mechanical art, that mighty lever for industry, landless Cain regains his field, and the country brings the riches of its fields into the town to exchange them for participation in the advantage of its products.

But Tubal-Cain’s sister was נעים .נעמה is primarily physical beauty, beauty which appeals to the senses. The first purpose of industry is usefulness. But it shows progress when the purpose of beauty is joined to that of usefulness, when taste is applied to industry; this combination is itself a step towards the education of mankind back to higher things. Did Naamah stand helpingly at her brother’s side for the purpose of adding charm and grace to his work as her name implies? Perhaps.

V. 23. The different ways in which this verse is taken are well known. They all leave difficulties more or less unsolved. We have already referred to the parallel of the list of the generations of the Cainites to that of the generations of the Sethites. There too, at the end, we find a “Lamech” who makes a significant pronouncement on the future of the generations: “זה ינחמנו וגו׳״. Here the style of the language of the speech already shows us that here we have before us a שיר, a pronouncement dictated by a higher Spirit. If we consider this form of the speech, if we take the actual words in their most simple unforced meanings, if we remind ourselves that a Midrash — referring it, it is true, to an actual occurrence — takes the killed man to be the ancestor and the killed child, to be his own child, and we take the whole in connection with what precedes it, then the whole verse may well be taken to be the last testament of a Cainite seer. Lamech had three sons, and with them he founded the whole of the culture of mankind. What proud feelings of self-satisfaction should have filled the breast of this man! How he should have jubilated! But the events of his life’s experience had filled his soul with the bitterest opposite feelings. He says: Hark unto me, Ada and Zillah, even if ye were not my own wives; for that which I have to say concerns all men. But ye, as Lamechs wives, as the mother of these sons, list doubly unto me, take in my speech. Ye imagine that with what we have accomplished we have re-established Cain in the world, have worked up a happy present for ourselves and a still happier future for our children? “I have not wrought atonement for my ancestor, I have killed my forebear, murdered the youth, and with all inflicted the deepest wound to myself” All efforts towards culture, if they stand in the service of God, are holy and bring happiness. They build on, continuing the inherited godly treasures of the forefathers, hand them on enriched to their children, and themselves live a happy life in the present. But from “Mehujael and Mehijael” out of a generation in which godliness is extinguished, and all efforts are directed only to extinguish it even more in the coming generation, nothing results but תובל קין, the whole product are men who work with all their forces to fight against God. Such a generation kills the ancestors who preceded them, kills the generation that comes after them, and only creates deep wounds and pain for themselves. It sacrifices the past and the future and gains no present.

V. 25. Eve, who at the birth of her first son, let her thoughts dwell primarily on herself, on her part in the production, had by now had profound impressions. She no longer says קניתי but שת לי אלקים, and looks at the child, not as an איש but as זרע, seed, the means of a new future; for by Cain killing Abel, he had destroyed not only Abel, but his own future and that of his generation, as his great-grandson had prophetically expressed in the previous verse. In שת, foundation, support (כי השתות יהרסון Ps. 11,3), the hopes of mankind received a fresh foundation.

V. 26. But development does not progress only in an upward direction, it also goes downwards. Seth also begot a son, he called him Enos, אנוש .אנוש designates a troubled stage of mankind in contrast to the pure state of man אדם. It is related to אנס rabbinic Hebrew and עגש, the former designates force exercised against another, the latter used later for punishment generally, originally refers primarily to money fines. As a verb אנש occurs only in the passive, and then means the hopeless stage of an illness or suffering, the condition of complete debility or enervation. But as it occurs referring specifically not to the nature of the ill person but to the illness, the suffering, the wound, אנוש חצי (Job. XXXIV), כאב אנוש (Job. XVII), אנושה מכתיה (Micha I), it seems, in the passive, to describe not the effect of the illness, but the cause of it. The illness, the pain, the wound is then no local offering but the effect of the disease of the whole organism, אנש in the Kal would accordingly mean, to exert force, to cause illness, to weaken, and ענש probably means primarily a money fine, because by money not so much real, present property is taken away as the means of obtaining it for the future. Now אנש, like סגר ,שאל ,שאר, is not passive but an active form, and designates men who no longer look on themselves as אדם, as a governor, standing in the service of God, and as such leads the world towards a healthy development to happiness, but misuses the position which God has given him only to domineering, selfish capricious tyranny, making the world sick and ill. אדם is the health and welfare bringer of the world, אנש the reverse. But where this debasement in the generations of Seth came from is told us in the next sentence:

אז הוחל לקרא בשם ה׳. The possibility that הוחל can just as well mean “it was profaned, desecrated” as “it was begun” has brought about the most varied and different ways of taking this sentence. It can mean either, “then one began to invoke the Name of God, or to proclaim the Name of God”, or “then the invoking or proclaiming the Name of God was profaned or desecrated”. The first way of taking it has been abandoned because in it one could only see praise, and in no way a degeneration of the age. But against the second way, firstly would be the construction-ל, and then also it would imply too deep a degree of degeneration having been already reached. Rashi’s explanation is that then one began to call men and other objects idolatrously with the Name of God, but against that is the fact that the four-lettered Name ה׳ can never be associated with idolatry. At no time in all history was the Name ה׳ given to idols. There is no other way left but to take the simple and unforced meaning to be “then one began to proclaim the Name of God”. But the explanation which I once heard from my unforgettable teacher, the late Bernays of blessed memory, is surely the right one. קרא בשם ’ה, which in Abraham’s time was a merit, and meant the beginning again of a return to a better time after the Name of God had been completely forgotten, was in Enos’s time the sign of the beginning of defection. In this time the necessity first started of having to proclaim the Name of God. Until then it was superfluous, as it will ultimately be once again in the future. — את ד׳ כי כלם ידעו אותי מקטנם ועד גדולם ולא ילמדו עוד איש את רעהו ואיש את אחיו לאמר דעו (Jer. 31,34) “And they shall no longer teach one the other saying: Know God, for they shall all know Me, from the least of them unto the greatest of them”.

“Then one started to proclaim the Name ה׳.” Mankind had become אנוש, had become the cause of the illness of the world because the Name ה׳ began to be forgotten, and thereby the special relation of God to Man and Man to God (see above) not to be considered. The descendants of Cain went to ruin because there — מחויאל מחייאל — godliness became more and more altogether extinguished, those of Seth degenerated because the consciousness of the godly calling of mankind which the Name ה׳ keeps awake in the human mind became lost, through which they sank from אדם to אנוש. The Name אלקים, the consciousness of there being a God, some Almighty high power to which the world owes its origin and order, has never entirely disappeared from the mind of mankind, even if only the conception דאלהא אלהא, as the God of the gods. But this consciousness does not yet make mankind into Man, nor Jews into Jews. We can have the full conviction that everything about us is made and regulated by a Creator, and believe that the fate of mankind too is dependent on these same regulations, we have only to search and penetrate into the nature of these regulations to ensure our happiness. But, not to exploit the world in our own interests, but to make its forces subservient to us for the purpose of fulfilling God’s Will on earth, to use them, not for the world, but for the submission of our own hearts, our own will, and all human society under the dictates of God, and to keep Man in close contact with Him, that is what the four-lettered Name ה׳ teaches and preaches to Jews and Mankind. Hence it is not just fortuitous but is based on deep inner reasoning that we express the Name ה׳ as אדנ׳. The recognition of God as our Lord and Master, the submission as עבד ה׳, that most ennobling calling, is the most direct reciprocation to the Name ה׳. We recognise God as ה׳ in our calling Him “our Master”. ה׳ is not to be found in Nature but in the development of human history. It, the Name, gives Man the feeling of his worth, the consciousness of his greatness and of his smallness, the consciousness of his greatness dwindling to nothing before God, and yet appointed by Him to be רגליו הדום at the head of His creation; it protects Man from boasting and presumption and at the same time from becoming brutalized, degenerated and stunted. According to the teaching of our sages, when Man sank from being Adam to Enos by forgetting or not considering this Name, the physical world sank with him. The earth lost more and more of its fertility, human physique became stunted and the human face became brutish in appearance, and Man fell under the influences of harmful physical powers. The Name of God makes people feel free and full of life and protectingly raises them above everything. As it disappeared from mankind their physical nature became more and more subjected to the physical laws of the physical world. — So it was in the age of Enos that the Name ה׳ came to be forgotten and not considered, and the necessity first arose לקרא בשם ה׳.

קרא בשם ה׳, literally: to call in the Name of God, i.e. to summon people in the Name of God, to challenge them in the Name of God. It is more than mere preaching or proclaiming, its object is not the mere teaching or knowledge of God, it is recognition i.e. the devotion and submission to the Divine Will, the call, to come to God and to pay Him homage. It involves coming to a clear understanding of the relation of Man to God and the demands which this relation makes. It is in this sense that the term is used here and with Abraham.

It is with this requirement for לקרא בשם ה׳ that the history of the Jewish nation is introduced. For with it, the necessity arises for an arrangement to have men in the midst of mankind who are to preserve and awaken the consciousness and knowledge of the true calling of Man, and of his true relation to God. Hence the nation of Israel was born whose mission is none other than לקרא בשם ה׳.

V. 1—2. זה ספר תולדת אדם. This sentence, with which a new period in the history of the education of mankind is introduced, bears a marked similarity to the sentence above, Ch. 2,4 בהבראם וגו׳ אלה תולדות השמים והארץ with which the history of the development of the world was introduced. Just as there it was said, that all the succeeding phenomena in nature were nothing other than the natural development of heaven and earth, and they all had their origin בהבראם in the laws which the Creator had already made for heaven and earth at their origin, in the same way, here, at the beginning of the development of mankind, a similar pronouncement is made; that all the manifold marked differences in human beings are naught but the natural development of the fact that God made Man in His own likeness. ספר from ספר, to count, i.e. summing together different things under one fundamental idea. And a ספר, a book, is a collection of common ideas, teachings etc., which in a wide sense are systematically connected with each other, thus the ספר תורה; here, all further developments and events. The whole history of mankind, with its lowest depths and loftiest heights, which shows human beings in the most varied happenings, forms one whole, One thought, one idea lives and is realised in them; in spite of their striking contrast they are all nothing but the developments of Adam having been created in the likeness of God, (having been granted complete power of self-determination, I.L.) Man could not have been “Adam” if all this could not have developed out of him. If he — by his freedom of will — is to be higher than an angel, then he must also be able to be — to use a common expression — worse than the devil. The possibility of the deepest degeneration was already foreseen in Adam. In no wise had God miscalculated, had anything miscarried in His world, in His mankind. All that occurred was only the one great development of the conception: “Adam”. This being so, we can understand the sayings: — R. Akiba taught that ואהבת לרעך כמוך “love thy neighbour as thyself” is כלל גדול בתורה is a great all-embracing comprehensive sentence of the Teaching. At the bottom there is, after all, only one עברה, selfishness, egoism. In the moment in which a person places himself completely in the position of somebody else, strips himself completely of all egoism, he has raised himself to the height of that standpoint from which all the duties of life, all the מצות, wish to be performed. But Ben Azai is of the opinion that our sentence זה ספר תולדת ארם is a still greater, still more comprehensive one. Here a much greater, much higher union of all men is given. This verse looks on the greatest criminal, the greatest degeneration, the greatest bestiality, all as תולדת אדם, all as developing out of the one Adam, the one creation in the likeness of God, all together entered in God’s great Book of the World in which he enters mankind. תולדת, written חסר, even the deficient, imperfect produces of humanity are still תולדת אדם!
So ALL men are human beings, the צלם אלקים is never completely lost, that is the first Truth which stands at the head of the history of Man.

The second Truth runs: ביום ברא אלקים אדם בדמות אלקים עשה אתו “on the day that God created Man, He formed him in the likeness of God”. The real original condition of Man was not the mentally and morally restricted condition of the savage almost bordering on the animal, which people think as the “natural condition” of Man, nor is the likeness to God something super-natural, for the sake of which Man would have to give up his natural earthly character, neither is it something unnatural and artificial that would have first to be acquired by Culture. On the contrary just that mentally and morally restricted so-called “natural condition” is the unnatural, degenerated condition into which Man sank the more he forgot the Name ה׳. His true natural state is the likeness to God, in his true natural condition he is mentally awake and morally pure, godlike, the world blossoms around him as a paradise and he hears the Voice of God wandering in the garden; for “on the day that God created Man, he was godlike and pure and strove upwards to God”.

Hence not for naught is here, even after the so-called “fall of Man”, yea, after the age that bore the character of אנוש, once again repeated all those conceptions and signs by which Man is to be recognised as צלם אלקים It is highly significant that it says ביום ברא אלקים and not ברא ה׳, just to indicate that the likeness of Man to God was given as his nature, to teach that just as the Creator, the God of Nature, created the worm to be a worm so did He create mankind to be “Men”.

V. 2. זכר ונקבה בראם. It is equally untrue that dividing the mission of life in the world between men and women is something arbitrary. Right from the beginning God reached “mankind” male and female, both equally godly, of equal worth, neither more in the likeness of God than the other, both given the same blessing by God, both together given the name “Adam”. ברכה and אדם “blessing and resembling God, human beings near unto God”, such is the natural state of Man — עיקר שכינה בתחתונים — and the return to this blessing and to this nearness to God, back to this “natural condition” out of the degeneration, is the object and goal of all the history of the world.

V. 3. בדמותו כצלמו. Above it says בצלמנו כדמותנו, “We would make a bearer of our שכינה on earth in a bodily case which is befitting thereto, who is to be spiritually, mentally similar to Us.” Here the order is reversed, בדמותו כצלמו, in his spiritual likeness just as his bodily form. Here, clearly the spiritual likeness, דמות, appears greater than the bodily, צלם. Perhaps all human beings are spiritually the same, the דמות, the immortal eternal spirit is equal in all, and the difference only lies in the degree of perfection of its means of accomplishment in the world, the body. Adam bequeathed his spiritual likeness completely; physically, however, the succeeding generation weakened, his first son already was only כצלמו. Hence, then, the great value the Torah lays on טהרה, the purity of the body. Hence, then, הקים, as the fundamental condition for all hopes of the future. The purer the body, the clearer will the צלם אלקים in it come to be realised, as long as it — the body — submits itself to the spirit. הקים, as a rule, are mentioned before משפטים, for only to a nation begotten and fed in accordance with these dictates can the fulfilment of the משפטים be ascribed. So Seth was כצלמו, “born in an already weakened degree of his physical likeness”, ויקרא, he called him Seth; Adam, too, considered him in the same way as Eve had done before.

V. 4—28. Now follows a whole list of generations until למך similarly to the generations of the Cain line. Here, too, we venture to assume that the names have meaning. We need in no way to take it that this meaning of the names presumes some gift of prophesy in the fathers, nor that the actual bearers of the names need necessarily themselves have the character which is expressed by the name. For instance, Enos need by no means himself have been אנוש. The father could very well have given the name to the baby according to the character which that particular generation were adopting. The similarity — though modified — of the names in the two lists of generations springs at once to one’s eye: .קין :קינן ;למך :למך ;מתושאל :מתושלח ;מחייאל :מהללאל ;חנוך :חנוך ;עירד :ירד But it is also striking that, whereas there, in the one line, the generations go steadily downwards, חנוך ,עירד ,מחייאל ,מתושאל ,קין until למך, who finally declares the hopeless worthlessness of the generations, here a swing from bad to better and from better to worse shows itself until again a למך proclaims the final salvation of the generation by his son. To אנוש followed a קינן, related to קין, in any case a disturbed generation falling away from God, to that מחלל-אל, a rising up towards God, then ירד, again a sinking, חנוך, a rising up again, מתושלח an abandoning of the masses, and then למך. Let us now consider the way of this development more closely.
To שת followed an

אנוש, and in that time mankind began to forget the name ה׳, not the consciousness of there being a God, but of the high value and godliness of Man, to forget and lose the special relation of God to Man which the name ה׳ expresses. But where this consciousness disappeares, whether it is in large or small human circles, and people no longer find their satisfaction in life in God and in fulfilling His Will, then they become אנוש (see Ch. 4,26) and an אנוש is always followed by a: -

קינן, a generation which idolizes possessions, to whom, not the use of them for God serving purposes but the possession of possessions hovers before them as the ideal: the materialism of wealth. Individuals go to their ruin in this endeavour, but on the whole something higher, something more spiritual always works its way to the fore. Pure materialism, after all, never satisfies everybody and everywhere loftier ideas towards the godly are sought. קינן is always followed by a

מהלל-אל. Praise, an upward swing of the pendulum toward God. Materialism is followed by a generation of piety. But mere praising God, mere psalm-singing and looking up towards God never effects a regeneration of any generation. Where honouring God consists in hymns and prayers, and not — as in Judaism — in subordinating one’s life under the laws of God’s Will, the name God certainly does return but not the Name ה׳, and then a מהללאל is always followed by a
ירד, then, in spite of the “lip-service”, the generation sinks. But just out of spiritual and moral debasement an age gathers itself together to

חנוך, to educate itself to nurturing and cultivating the seeds of something nobler. But in times of general debasement such efforts remain the work of only individual nobler natures and these feel themselves in such contrast to the masses that they

מתושלח give up the masses. They believe they have achieved their goal if they have saved themselves and elevated themselves only. To them the masses were מתים whom they שלח, give up, abandon. The root of מתים is מתה only otherwise found in מתי, the question about a future moment, when? The question מתי misses something in the present, and asks about the point in time when that which really should already be there will arrive. Similarly in מתה the present is left out of consideration and is only thought of as a bridge to the future.
