Intellectual, haughty arrogance, according to established usage, has labelled people, who are just as good צלם אלקים as the very highest, with the horrible name “proletariat” (= good for nothing else than for producing children for the future). It is possible that a similar pride is expressed by מתים, and according to that in מתושלח. In any case in מתושלח the idea of abandoning the masses is present. Now it says peculiarily of ויתהלך חנוך את האלקים ואיננו וגו׳ :חנוך. Even our sages are uncertain in their opinion of his character, although exactly the same words referring to Noah express the very highest degree of virtue. (ב״ר כ״ט). But here — taken in conjunction with the idea מתושלח — this “walking” with God” designates that חנוך, to equip himself for walking with God, avoided the masses, either out of fear or out of disdain, contempt. But התבודדות, monk-like retirement from he world of men is un-Jewish. Our צדיקים and חסידים lived in the masses, with the masses, and for the masses. They considered it their mission to draw the masses up to them. To abandon the masses — מתושלח — is a diseased condition in times in which the conception God had become merely a theoretical speculation, and where the thought of God makes men into fanatics, drives them to eschew life because they fear its temptations or — in blind arrogance — disdain its problems. This retirement into oneself, this asceticism, which is exactly what the Torah opposes, is based on the erroneous idea that godliness is somethiing pertaining to the next world, something that lies outside the sphere of ordinary life. With Noah the התהלך את האלקים was not the total, the summit, but the base, the foundation of a whole active life. Noah was איש צדיק תמים בדרתיו and the source from which he drew the spiritual and moral forces for such a life was that את האלקים התהלך נח, that he kept the course of his life with God. But with Enoch where this “being with God” is all that is said, seems to be the whole sum of his life, not leading him to life in general but away from it, there it is a misdirected effort which at best does nothing to better the world, is quite useless for the world. This too, is the opinion of our sages ז״ל. It is the more important to stress this fact, as another opinion, not originating from Jewish sources, has made Enoch into a demigod, and finds in him the apotheosis of an ascetic life. The מינים wanted to justify the claim that, it says כי לקח אתו אלקים, Enoch did not die, from analogy with what it says of Elijah ה׳ לוקח את אדניך. But R. Abahu refuted this with Ezekiel 24,16 הנני לוקח ממך את מחמד עיניך, where by the term לקיחה the death of the Prophet’s wife by the plague was pronounced, and this refutation was specifically approved by the sages יפה השיבן ר׳ אבהו. The sages find the whole reproach summarised in the word ואיננו, that he was איננו, that even in life he was dead, was of no use to the world, he “was not there” for the world, and they see in the לקח אתו אלקים an early death. אמר ר׳ אבהו חנוך חנף היה פעמים צדיק פעמים רשע אמר הקב״ה עד שהוא בצדקו אסלקנו. He adds, most significantly, בר״ה בשעה שהוא דן כל באי עולם “God judged him on ר״ה together with all the other inhabitants of the world”. He thereby opposes the opinion that considers such a retired, meditative devotional life something specially holy, something to receive special consideration from God; he stresses that Enoch received no special consideration from God, but was judged only in common with all other people.
Methuselah was followed by

V. 28—29. למך. Just like the Cainite למך, so does the Sethite למך (for which we know of no etymological meaning) speak most significant words over the future, but in the completely opposite sense. There the generation ends in utter despair (as far as we understood his prophetic words). But in the Sethite generation another picture of the development presents itself. Here we see the upward trend to the better constantly germinating and attempting to fight the evil. That is why the declaration for the future of mankind finds words of hope and consolation: “This one, or this, will console us for all what we have done and for all that our hands had to give up”.

V. 30—31. נח. It has been remarked long ago ולא המדרש הוא השם לא השם הוא המדרש that that name נח does not correspond to the meaning ינחמנו. Attention has also been drawn to the fact that here, when compared to the preceding list of names, it says exceptionally: ויולד בן, and this is explained as indicating כי ממנו נבנה העולם in him the Jewish conception of a son, בן, appears in its fullest significance as the one through whom the building of the world is continued. All the previous cases when they had the joy of having a child in their arms were not satisfied merely to have a child, they always saw in it some special trend, something special. In his child Lamech saw only the son, the בן; and in his name wished to say ינחמנו זה, this, our children, our בן, is, amongst all that we do, and give up so much (עצבון, I.L.) to accomplish, the one thing that can give us comfort. It does not say — ינחמנו על — but מ-, not consolation for all our work, but from all our work. The whole earth, all the means for Man’s work, were — for the training and education of mankind — oppressed and impeded, Man alone did not come under the curse; only the ground was impeded in its development. Now while the whole of Lamech’s surroundings tried to bring success forth from the entire world of human development, and foundered on the lack of blessing that lay on the earth, Lamech spoke these significant words: ממעשנו וגו׳, out of all that we produce, out of all that we have to give up by our activities, out of the whole world on which we perceive the curse of God, there is only one thing that can console us, only one thing in which we find the goal of all our efforts and that we can, without obstruction, bring to the complete height of its designation, and that is זה, our child our בן, the “brick”, the building-stone for all the future of the world. For just because no curse lay on mankind, with every human being, in every age, the very loftiest stage in life can be reached, so that children are always, to use the words of David, “arrows in the hand of a mighty man” which we can aim, give the direction to become בוני עולם. This is something that is completely independent of אשר ארדה ה׳ ממעשנו ומעצבון ידינו מן האדמה.

Therefore he called his son נוח .נח is movement come to rest. It is phonetically related to נוא .נוע ,נה ,נוא is interrupted motion, hence נא half-cooked, הניא to hinder somebody in his intentions. נה I beg of you, is used to interrupt and change what we take to be an objectionable frame of mind in somebody, נוע is actual movement towards a goal. “Not that we have to be busy”, is what Lamech expresses with these words, “but that we tire ourselves out to no purpose, without attaining our goal, is what makes us wretched. If we direct our attention to our children, there we can find in them a purpose and a goal that in all conditions can be attained and that can be a consolation to us for all that we have to leave unattained or unfinished”. Our children are the בוני עולם they build on what we have started, they complete where our hands failed. He did not call him נחמן ,מנחם and did not say זה יניחנו, but called him נח and said זה ינחמנו, for he wished to express two things, a) that consolation was to be found in children, and b) where the fault lay for which consolation had to be sought. b) would not have been expressed by נחמן, and a) not by יניחנו. But what he did say was: we are unconsolable because we can see no goal to our work, we have תנועה but no מנוחה. In our children we visualise a goal, and in that itself is consolation.

נחם. This root has a peculiar meaning. In the piel: to comfort, in Niphal: to be comforted, but also to alter your mind or your decision regarding some intended action, finally also contrition, remorse at something which had occurred as אין איש נחם על רעתו, or אחרי שובי נחמתי. The basic underlying meaning is: to change one’s mind, hence repentance and altering one’s decision. Consolation is also a complete reversal of the previous feeling regarding an occurrence. In a remarkable manner the roots נחם ,נעם ,נהם ,נאם are in similar relation to each other as נוח ,נוע ,נה ,נוא are (see above). Just as these latter designate four stages of an actual movement, so do they refer to the same, but to an internal mental one. — נאם occurs in נְאֻם a specific term for the prophetic world of God. The sayings of God are no mere expressed thoughts, but are already motion, the beginning of a deed, but still נא, still restrained, held back.

— נהם (similar to נה), the expression of a feeling of checked movement, as the roaring of a lion, or the pain of suppressed will, complaining, moaning, wailing, — נעם (similar to נע) is that which sets us in motion, attracts us, to which we move freely and gladly, that which is pleasant — נחם (similar to נוח) is a movement which is reversed, like נח. Hence נחם, also where it means repentance, seems to be connected with the complete giving up of a direction hitherto held. But that is also consolation. A painful loss sets us in motion internally, consolation brings us to rest, closes the gap, and stays the motion.

V. 32. In contrast to all his predecessors Noah married very late in life and that is why it does not simply say ויחי as at all the others, but ויהי בן, a contrast, the meaning of which appears still clearer in the following verses. — Shem, Ham and Jepheth are further introduced to us in their characteristic differences.

V. 1—2. Here we are shown the reason for the state of mankind growing worse as being due to the mixing of two classes, the בני אלקים and the בנות האדם. We have just previously learned to know of two lines of generations. The one Cainite development of mankind which, without God, strove to found a human existence on the basis of inventions and industry. This in itself would be fully justified, but here, with God left out, only ended in despair without any consolation. The other, the Sethite generations, at the head of which, the divine stamp, the power and blessing of Man’s pure calling which God had originally conferred, צלם ,ברכה ,דמות אדם, is repeated. Also — on account of what follows — the doubly important stress on the equality of birth and importance of the female sex, זכר ונקבה בראם. etc. From the former, the Cainite line, in which “the godly was entirely eradicated”, מחויאל, came the בנות האדם. The latter, the Sethite line, on whom the Divine Stamp devolved, were the בני אלקים. In it, as we have seen, the godly, even if not strong enough to effect the complete salvation of the generation, did always recur. But the fact that the progress towards godliness was not as constant and sure as the downward path towards corruption was in the other line, came about because they did not keep themselves pure, but intermarried with the Cainite generations. It says it came about “when mankind began to increase”, before, there was no great choice in the selection of brides, but now the Sethites could have kept their line pure. “Then the sons of the godly race saw the daughters of the other race that they were good — probably טבת מראה, beautiful —”. They did not look from whom they were descended, did not consider what children they could expect from mothers brought up in such environments, they simply looked at the girls, and they appealed to them. The corruption did not lie in the women themselves but in their descent: מכל אשר בחרו in this “מ״ in the wherefrom; they did not keep themselves to the race of אלקים.

It is true that the wrongfulness of this proceeding has always been sought, but one found it in the ויקחו, in which one thought one found an expression of rape and altogether found it an immoral procedure. But אשה לקח always designates an honorable relationship and is the actual technical term for marriage. The sin which, on account of the following verse, must of necessity be indicated in this verse, would accordingly, only have to be sought in the מכל אשר בחרו. They married girls without considering from where they were taking them. Therein lay the sin.

The results could have been propitious had it been possible for the godly spirit which the Sethite race had in them to be strong enough to overpower the seed of evil which the wife brought into the home. But the risk is always too great. It is always a question which tendency will prevail in the children, and whether the longer the intermixture continues the more the depravity will grow. The following verse gives the disclosure how the problem settled itself here.

V. 3. When this intermixture became quite prevalent God said לא ידון רוחי באדם לעולם בשגם הוא בשר. This cannot mean: My Spirit shall not strive eternally against mankind. Apart from the fact that דון is never construed with ידין בגוים) ב- means amongst the nations), that the verb דון elsewhere hardly ever means to strive but only to judge, here according to the accent and cantillation רוחי belongs to באדם and forms one conception with it. דוחי באדם is the subject of the sentence. My Spirit in Man i.e. the Spirit of God which I breathed into Man was to be the דַיָן the Voice of God in Man by which he is to judge himself. “The spirit of Man is the lamp of God with which God searcheth the most secret inwards of Man”, (Prov. 20,27) not only sees but also judges. It was due to this self-judging spirit of God in Man that, in spite of the intermixture, a Mahalallel succeeded a Cainain etc., that after a bad generation a good one can follow again. But this judge is accessible to bribery and corruption, it allows itself to be lulled into slumber, it is possible that its voice becomes more and more deadened, that sensuality becomes more and more awakened in the course of generations and the self-judging spirit in men finally lays down its office. Not for nothing does the divine Torah place the laws of chastity and those of marriage so much in the foreground. Here we are shown how much the keeping of the spirit of God in Man is dependent on them. When God saw how the sons of the godly race were going about their marriages quite indiscriminately He said: “Now My Spirit in Man will not continue exercising it office of judge for ever”. The conditions which had prevailed hitherto, in which the development, even if not a continuous upward one was not a continuous downward one but rather formed an up and down wave, will not endure in that fashion much longer בשגם הוא בשר, seeing that Man is not altogether spiritual but also physical. He consists of בשר flesh as well as רוח spirit, body in opposition to soul. This contrast, which in pure human beings is settled by the subordination of the בשר under the רוח ה׳ באדם, can, by continued mixture with elements that pay no attention to the godly in life, end in the contrary manner, by the death of the spiritual through the physical. “If the present conditions go on for ever, the end will surely be in this way”. Therefore God set this tendency a limit of one hundred and twenty years. For that period the result of this struggle shall be tested.

V. 4. That which was said in general in the previous verse, is in this verse made still clearer by a single example which could have been even more understandable to our fathers in whose time some members of the “Nephilim” race were still to be found. — נפילים. How the conception of giants came to be designated by the term נפילים is not easily decided. נפל: to fall; as a rule the idea of weakness is certainly associated with the conception of falling. But nevertheless it is used for the overwhelming of a weaker one by a more powerful force. Thus נפל פחדם עליהם. Also for the overpowering effect of receiving inspiration from God: ותפל עלי יד ה׳. Further, for the occurrence of some contingency: איך יפול הדבר. Also once of Ishmael על פני כל אחיו נפל. Perhaps נפל here in our case indicates somebody or something surprising beyond all reckoning falling in one’s path as if dropped from heaven. Ishmael was a פדא אדם, something extraordinary, his power ranged beyond the ordinary order of things. Possibly נפילים were so called on account of their quite extraordinary strength and size threatening to overpower everything. Perhaps in וארץ רפאים תפיל (Is. XXVI. 19.) the meaning of making נפילים underlies the word תפיל and the sense of the whole verse כי טל אורות טליך וארץ רפאים תפיל would be: “The giants that Thy Dew awakes are spiritual illuminating great ones; the gigantic productions of the world are only giants in body”. If the conception נפילים indicates something extraordinary it is evident that the name can only be used in a time when the rest of the human race was already smaller. In antediluvian times נפילים were nothing extraordinary, הנפילים היו בארץ בימים ההם “those that are now wondered at as נפילים were quite common in the world in those days”. In the Cainite line where the purely spiritual was entirely submerged, the physical development grew to gigantic proportions. Had the intermixture of the two lines produced the desired results, the spiritual element brought by the paternal parent to the mother would have overcome the purely physical one and used it in its service. Intellectual spiritual giants would have developed. The mind lives on physical strength, and uses a great deal in its work. But, it says, וגם אחרי כן etc. also later on, בנות אדם had already born children to them—the fathers of the godly line,—the spiritual was overgrown by the physical, sensual. So that this union of the two lines bore the germ of the defection and profanation of the generations of the המה הגבורים .בני אלקים, from these unions came “the heroes of the ancient times”, who, it is true, occasionally towered above their contemporaries in intellect and spirit too, but in whom, for the most part, the mind stood in the service of their mighty physical strength.

V. 5. In the word רע lies the conception of “broken”, in contrast to שלם and תמים. It is probably not without reason that it says בארץ, in the world, and not באדמה, on the earth, the stage for “Adam’s” activities. God had created the world and set Man to be His representative, His agent, on it. But, through what was happening, a “large break” had been made in the harmony of the world. It is questionable whether רעת אדם designates the evil of men, or the unhappiness, the evil, that befalls men, that men have brought into the world. We believe the latter. When God looked down, mankind had already brought the greatest state of harm and evil into the world, the present was bad beyond all measure, and as for the future: כל יצר מחשבות לבו רק רע כל היום.

יצר. It is unfortunate that this word is so often translated by “instinct, inclination, impulse”, as if there was a force in man that drives him to evil. From that there was then formed that hopeless view of life on which a great “religious” society rests, that dogma of the power of evil in which Man supposed to be born, and out if which he can only be saved by a certain belief. Out of this little word יצר accordingly a strong cord has been woven by which mankind is bound and gagged, and yet nothing is further from this idea than this very word.

Already in the root יצר there is absolutely nothing of forcing, but rather of forming. But the form of the word יצר is not active at all, but passive, it does not mean “the former” the one who forms, but that which is formed. יצר is clearly in relation to יוצר as the creation is to the creator: ויצר אמר ליוצרו (Is. XXIX. 16). יצר is accordingly like the material, ביד היוצר כחמר, subordinated to the יוצר, and יצר מחשבות is the creation, the formation of our thoughts.

Our soul is a חושב a weaver, the material is given to it. As the raw material, all possibilities, good and bad, lie in its hand. The soul has to weave them together to form them into shapes, צורות, i.e. our thoughts our ideas, and these צורות are יצר, the formations of our weaving soul. Out of the material given us we can make whatever we like. But at the same time God has given us the “pattern” according to which we are to weave. If we do this then it is altogether good. The חושב is not to leave out, cannot spare, any thread, any colour. In its appointed place, and used in the prescribed way, everything is good. יצר, the idea, the picture of what we can achieve, certainly does urge, “tempt” us to achieve it, but we ourselves have formed it. If this idea (יצר literally in Greek ’Ιδἑα that which is formed, a picture) is a good one, then we strive for the good, and also the reverse is true. Thus Job calls the ideas which form in his mind, in a stressed passive form יצורים (Job. XVII.8). Thus David calls the joy in devotion to God, the שמחה להתנדב which the people showed in their gifts for the building of the Temple יצר מחשבות לבב העם, and prays שמרה זאת i.e. the שמחה להתנדב, “this joy of giving things up for holy purposes, preserve Thou for ever to be the formation of the thoughts of Thy People.” (Chron. I. 29,18).

Accordingly, what it says here is: Already, at the moment, the evil brought about by human beings in the world was great, and regarding the future that could be expected from them, “all the formation of the thought of their hearts was only bad all the day, or every day”. The term כל יצר itself already proves that it cannot be talking of the so-called “evil inclination”, of it, it could not say “all” nor would רק be applicable. But of ideas and notions it can well say that every ideal they set themselves out to accomplish had not a single good point, and this tendency to evil was continuous, the same in all phases of their life.

V. 6. וינחם. For the meaning of נחם refer to V. 29 above. Questions have been raised on what is said here that God altered His Mind, especially in face of the sentence, לא איש אל ויכזב ובן אדם ויתנחם (Num. XXIII. 19). But there seems to be a difference between הׅנָחֵם and הׅתְנַחֵם The former is an altering of the mind brought about by external causes, by an alteration of circumstance, thus of Saul: נחמתי. Of course God had appointed Saul to be King but when Saul rendered himself unworthy to continue reigning, Saul’s alteration in behaviour caused God to alter His decision. Similarly we find the reverse case of וינחם ה׳ על הרעה. But Man alters his decisions by himself without any external cause, hence the reflexive התנחם, and so it says of God לא איש וגו׳ ויתנחם. Only once does it say, at the end of האזינו (Deut. 32,36) ועל עבדיו יתנחם (and also correspondingly in Ps. CXXXV. 14) and there the meaning is very significant: even if God is given no cause to alter His decision by תשובה, from His Own Self will He decide to change it from the fate hitherto decided on, and bring the גאולה. This would refer to the גאולה בעתה if לא זכו.

ויתעצב אל לבו here the Hispael not the Nifal. עצב see above III. 16. התעצב, to have painful feeling of renunciation. Thus, of the sons of Jacob when the purity of the family was destroyed by the shameful crime committed against their sister. There the first feeling was not of anger at the wrong that had been done, but ויתעצבו, they were pained that the priceless pearl they had hitherto possessed, the purity and innocence of a Jewish daughter was now lost; the feeling of anger came afterwards. As this pain arose from the way in which this event affected them, so that its source was within themselves it is expressed by the Hispael and not the Nifal. Equally so, here. Regarding the אל- (not ב- as we should expect) we have an analogy in reference to Jonathan: נעצב אל דוד (Sam. I. XX., 34), it indicates the object concerning which the pain is felt. So that literally it would say here: “He had a feeling of painful renunciation concerning His heart”. But לב ה׳ is the most intimate expression that can be used of God’s relation to Man. והיו עיני ולבי שם כל הימים (Kings I. 9,3), His love and His feelings will linger there perpetually, not merely His providence. Here, accordingly, לבו, — speaking in human terms — the joy that God wished to have at the mutual thriving of mankind and the earth — ישמח ה׳ במעשיו — He now must renounce. The continued existence of the world for men would be a misfortune for mankind, hence וינחם וגו׳ He altered His decision; but God’s “Heart” remained unaltered, “He was grieved that He had to renounce His heart-felt wish for the happy prosperous continued existence of mankind”.

Regarding this and similar anthropomorphic expressions of God, we would like to make a general remark. For so long people have philosophied all round these expressions to remove the danger of the slightest thought of any materiality or corporality of God that at the end one runs very nearly into the danger of losing all idea of the personality of God. Had that been the purpose of the Torah, those kind of expressions could easily have been avoided. But this last danger is greater than the first. The two anthropomorphic expressions here save the two essential conceptions: the freedom, the free-will of God, and that of Man. Not for nothing does it say, “when God saw etc.”. The wickedness of Man was not a matter of necessity. God had to see it before He knew it. This expression gives us the guarantee of human free-will. And the fate that overtook mankind was not the result of physical causes which followed set laws, it was preceded by an examination by God and His decision; the decision itself pained the Decider. All this presupposes the personality and free-will of God and keeps this clear in our minds. The ראב״ד already, one of the most Jewish of our thinkers, is of the opinion that such consciousness of the personality of God is of much greater importance than speculating about it, as to whether this or that can be asserted of God.

V. 7. ה׳, the same mercy, the same God of Love, that had placed Man on earth, now proclaims the decision for his destruction. The degeneracy was so great, that the extermination itself was an act of mercy. Even in the moment of his destruction, the greatness of Man shows itself in the fact that his destruction dragged the destruction of the whole living world with it. Not the world itself, but פני האדמה, the surface which belongs to mankind as the ground for its mission. It is not just merely a physical bond that joins men to things. It consists also of a moral relationship. When mankind sinks, the world mourns and withers. This fact runs through all the books of the תנ״ד (the Bible I.L.). Further, it does not say אמחה את האדם, absolutely, but with the addition מעל פני האדמה. It does not exclude the possibility that even this destruction was only a relative one, removal from the earth, Whether even then, the godly element in Man is not preserved for other spheres, other conditions, that, we can only dare interrogatively to hint at. The actual words of the text, anyway, imply only relative destruction.

Our sages in the Midrash give the word מחה an explanation which may be of no small significance. According to them מחה means a complete dissolving. Not simply death and decay of the soft tissues, but also of the bones, is decreed. Even that part of the skeleton which, our sages say, never perishes, here was completely dissolved. Through this complete dissolution it is less remarkable that none, or according to modern supposition, so few, relics of antediluvian mankind are met with. Apart from this, in the opinion of our sages, in Sabbath 152b, passion and sensuality have influence on the quicker dissolution of the remains of the human body, and the corruption which was so common in that generation could have raised this to a still higher degree.
Whereas a whole generation of mankind went thus to their ruin, it says: —

V. 8. ונח מצא חן בעיני ה׳. Not, Noah found grace in the sense of being spared or excused. — מצא חן בעיני never means finding grace with somebody that he should excuse you from punishment etc. But rather it is always used in cases where the granting of a wish or a favour is to be expected by somebody from somebody. Thus when Abraham wishes the angels to enter his tent, when the Egyptians are to make gifts to the people, etc. Between God and Man it is really the very highest state that Man can reach towards God. Thus Moses says למען אמצא חן בעיניך, “so that I may know what I have to do to continue to be worthy of your favour”. חן is not yet the favour being granted, but is being found worthy for it. Now it does not say לפני, but בעיני, in the judgement of, according to the insight of. If somebody is so that God can be חונן to him, then he has מצא—.חן בעיניו is, in most cases, not a casual finding but the accomplishment of an end for which one has been striving. Hence the use of מצא for attaining those spiritual possessions חכמה ,דעת etc. which are never to be obtained by chance, but only after earnest effort. So also used for the dispensations of God, which He sends to men because they deserve them. בדרך את כל התלאה אשר מצאתם (Ex. 18,8). Thus מצא חן בעיני ה׳ is also not just by chance. It only occurs with those people whom God furnishes with quite special strength and means for quite special purposes. So referring to Moses, and to Israel (מצא חן במדבר) and so here referring to Noah. While everything was so degenerate that it had to be destroyed, “Noah, in God’s judgement, was found worthy to have the whole work of saving the future transferred to him.”

The thought fills one with horror, that, as the product of 1600 years of the history of mankind, one single man and his family stand there alone, and with this single man God carried on His plan for mankind. Not without reason, did David, centuries later look back on just this phase of God’s rule, when he sang in Ps. XXIX of the Presence of God being in everything on earth that is awesome and sublime, that is beautiful and grand, in all that is thrilling and glorious, and concluded with the idea that, diverse and manifold though the differences in Nature and mankind appear, nevertheless in all this God’s rule and His plans remain unshaken. “He ‘sat’ at the flood” and even when the whole of mankind went to ruin, He remained מלך and His מלכות, His plans for the education of mankind remained unshaken. And as firm and unshaken as God stands in face of all change, so firm and unshaken will God let all those be that devotedly attach themselves to Him as His people, and this firmness does not lead to strife, does not disturb peace, it is the one condition for peace: .לעולם, ה׳ עוז לעמו יתן ה׳ יברך את עמו בשלום ה׳ למבול ישב וישב ה׳ מלך

V. 9. אלה תולדת נח. Just as above אלה תולדת השמים והארץ introduces a new series of developments, so here a new series of developments of mankind is introduced. The rest of mankind perishes. Noah is a second Adam and stands at the head of a new generation of mankind.

But as, not his children, but he himself is named as being his first תולדה, this gives our sages the opportunity of remarking that the first product of a man, the first result of his work, is his own character. This would be especially the case, in a time, like that of Noah’s in which it would certainly require the highest amount of energetic working on oneself to save oneself out of the general depravity, up to purity and goodness. There, surely, the first and noblest product of the upright is himself. איש צדיק תמים, these are the points of his character by which Noah מצא חן בעיני ה׳ and which God chose as the grains of seed for the future generations of man in this new ancestor.

איש. According to the remarks of our sages the name איש is not lightly used in the ונ״ך. When the Word of God calls somebody a man, he is a MAN, a proven charcter, a צדיק מומחה. And who had to stand the test of firm manliness more than Noah, in the 600 years he had spent his life hitherto in the midst of the changing generations! — השחתת דרך and חמם moral depravity and improbity, moral and social corruption are shown us immediately as the character of his time, in contrast to which Noah was צדיק and צדיק .תמים against חמם, and תמים against צדיק .השחתת דרך means: to render to the person and circumstances about us that which is due to them. .(In this respect it is both phonetically and in meaning related to the Chaldean שדך to satisfy, to give what is due). The צדיק looks at everything objectively, at nothing from the standpoint of his own interests, but everything from the point of view of what is right. It is primarily social justice and hence is preferably construed with expressions of deeds. עשה ,צדקה פעולת צדיק etc. — תמים, on the other hand, is preferably connected with הלך and דרך .דרך is primarily the development through which a person goes to the consummation of his own personality, in which he proceeds from step to step (related to מדרגה ,דרג). Whereas in deeds, consideration of his own personality is relegated to the background, in דרך, the satisfaction and perfection of his own personality is the aim, which, accordingly, embraces the whole sensuous development. תמים דרך is the one who remains pure even on the way to this sensuous development. The relationship to דמם to keep from any speech, any movement, and with the Chaldean טמם to be closed, restrained, would give תמם the underlying conception of self control, that from within oneself keeps all efforts under the mastery of a strong moral will, and does not allow oneself to be torn away in the slightest by any external allurement, accordingly, does not allow oneself to be made morally lacking in any way.

בדרתיו, the double way of taking it: in his time (i.e. for such times I.L.) he was a righteous man, or, even in his time he remained a righteous man, is probably true in both ways. Surely such a struggle as Noah had to endure does not remain without some weakening influence on ones’ character. But surely, on the other side, even a somewhat lesser degree of morality and honesty, attained and kept in such times, weighs incomparably heavier in God’s scales than a greater amount in any better times. It is significant that the בדרתיו is stressed at תמים and not at צדיק. It is incomparably more difficult to remain moral in immoral times than to remain honest in dishonest times.

That Noah was an איש צדיק had its roots in his moral purity, and this moral purity had its roots in the התהלך, in allowing himself to be led by God’s Hand. Whereas of the great men in later times it says that they went through life before God, as His messengers, of Noah it says with God. That he paid no attention to the jeers and gibes of his contemporaries, but held fast to God, and just thereby became “נח״, the one in whom mankind which was without any prospect of a future, attained a future.

V. 10. Noah was already 500 years old when he begat children. All his predecessors and contemporaries were fathers of families much earlier It seems, very probable that Noah was afraid to get children earlier, he did not trust himself to found a family in such an age, to be able to bring up good and morally pure children. Only 20 years after the end had been announced, and after he had accustomed himself to live isolated and alone with God for 500 years, without wife and family, to save himself from the universal corruption, did he dare to become the father of children. The repetition of the name Noah may be to tell us that he took this step too in the consciousness of his destination to be “Noah”.

שלשה בנים, three sons. The ancestors of the new world of human beings, are introduced in tripartition. If a closer consideration of these names discloses a marked difference in the characteristics of these ancestors of all mankind, that fact can be a source of the greatest hope and comfort to us. Completely different though the various races of man appear, such difference existed even before the flood, and as all three were saved by God, it must lie in the plan of God to bring about the ultimate goal of mankind in spite of all these differences, or perhaps just by all such different nationalities working together and inter-influencing each other just by their different characteristics — a שם, a חם and a יפת were all saved in the ark.
Let us consider these names which present to us three different tendencies already in the sons of the איש צדיק תמים.

שם, name, conception of objects. The whole wisdom of men consisted originally, and in truth still consists today, in the ability to give things names; to be able to express a conception, and thereby to indicate its “mental compass”, its שָׁם. In any case שֵׁם points to a mental activity, a discernment expressing a conception, giving a name.
חם means heat, the excited action of our senses; from the root חמם glowing, related to המם, fermenting.

יפת from יפה, related to פתה, the underlying meaning of which is to stand open, as פתח. From that we get פתי to be open to all external impressions, to let oneself be overwhelmed by them. מופת, an appearance which overwhelms somebody, obtains conviction in his mind of something. It is also related to יפה the beautiful, the attractive. In any case whereas שם is the conception of the spiritual, mental, חם, the glowing, excited, of the highest degree of sensuality, יפת expresses the feeling, the imagination which is sensitive to beauty. It is quite possible that יפת simply comes directly from יפה as צפת from צפה and דלת from דלה.

So we have here the three factors which comprise the whole of the life of our mind. In a healthy life all three phases place themselves under one higher principle, and, as in Noah, in התהלך את האלקים achieve the highest potentiality of the mind, in תמים the highest power over the senses, and in צדיק the purest power over the will and efforts. Separated, שם, would be the thinking one, חם, the sensuous one, and יפה, the one who seeks after beauty. שם is to come to חם ,להתהלך את ה׳ to להיות תמים, and יפת instead of being guided by the ideal of beauty, to come to the ideal of goodness and become צדיק. For where the tendency יפת is predominantly the directive, although, it is true, sensuality does become protected from coarseness by the application of the standard of decency and refinement, this standard applied to the general activities of life is still only a relative one. Later on (in Ch. IX.22 et seq. I.L.) we shall be brought back in a more direct manner to this characteristic fundamental difference in the new ancestry of the nations. We have only touched on it here to emphasize that these pronounced national differences are not to be regarded as degenerations, but that they had already been brought into the ark. So that if history shows us, in contrast to intellectual gifted nations or those of noble sentiments, others where hot sensuality seems to be their predominant feature, this is not to disturb our conviction that all the different races of men are created for the one lofty ideal of mankind, and will, in due course, mature to that goal, the goal that ומלאה הארץ דעה את ה׳ וגו׳.

V. 11. שחת is the conception of corruption, not destruction. It is the overthrow of a good condition, and the impeding of progress, and the changing into the opposite of anything which was meant to thrive and prosper. The basic meaning of שחת is a pit, and not with any idea of its being useful for preserving things, but as a means of interrupting the path of somebody striding to his goal, and bringing him to destruction. It is related to שחד: bribery, which is a pit dug in the path of a judge on his way to delivering a true and just verdict, and also to שחט which interrupts the progress of the life of an animal. From this basic meaning of שחת we can understand why it is preferably connected with השחת .דרך in general means: to be interrupted on the way to prosperity. השחית דרך presupposes that the whole path of life, also that directed to the sensual, in itself leads only to moral welfare; immorality is the pit which diverts this direction, in itself so good, into corruption. חמס is a wrong that is too petty to be caught by human justice, אינו יוצא בדינים, but if committed continuously can gradually ruin your fellow-man. Now here it says very significantly: The world was corrupt before God, and then the world was full of wrong-doing. First of all there was corruption of morals, sins that one imagined did not affect general civic life. The debauchery of youth, the foulness of marriages, one thought, need not prevent business in general, trade and traffic prospering and being honestly carried on. But when the world is corrupt before God, all the human institutions and laws of society cannot prevent society in general from going to ruin. By גזל, open robbery, it will never fall, it knows how to protect itself against that by prisons and penalties But by חמם, underhand dealing by cunning, astute dishonesty, craftily keeping within the letter of the law, it does go to ruin, by wrong which human justice cannot reach, but which can only be prevented by self-judging conscientiousness before God. Immorality kills this trait of the human mind, and with its loss the grave of civic well-being is also dug. החמס קם למטה רשע, it says in Ez. VII.11. “the lack of conscientiousness begotten by immorality becomes finally its own rod, לא מהם, the misfortune does not come from the natural state of men, does not come מהמונם, from overcrowding, not מהמהם, not from natural social relationship (the double ולא נה בהם ,(מהם, the misery altogether does not lie in men as such, but it is the חמם on which they go to ruin, through which the whole of society becomes חמץ, ends in fermenting foulness.”

V. 12. Then God looked at the world, and, lo! the earth as such,—not regarded as a cosmic body, with which the Torah is not concerned, but in as far as its upper surface is the stage for man’s activities—was checked in its progress towards pure development, by the forces and materials it gives to mankind being used in the service of corrupt morals.

V. 13. קץ from קצץ (related to גזז): to cut off, hence the end, where somehing leaves off. “The end of all flesh has come before Me” can mean: “the condition of all flesh has reached such a stage that it demands that I shall make an end of it”. Or, more probably, “if I do not intervene, it will all go completely to ruin by itself, “its end is already before Me”. As was already said above by למינהו, the thriving of the species is connected with the purity of the mating to such a degree that when God says the earth shall prosper it implicitly means that sexual purity is an essential condition. Accordingly when השחית כל בשר את דרכו צל הארץ, the קץ is already there automatically, and if God had not intervened, even the spark of purity which could be saved with Noah would have been irrevocably lost. This would also explain the מפניהם. For מפני always means a drawing oneself back from something out of a feeling of inferiority, fear, consideration etc. חמס occurs also referring to inanimate objects, ויחמם כגפן בסרו (Job. XV.33) et alia. Perhaps here similarly: “The end of all flesh has come before Me”. If this goes on there is no longer any future for mankind, for מפניהם “out of fear of them” the earth is already full of חמם, it is already withdrawing its forces out of fear of the immorality, robbery and murder, to support which they would be used. והיה מקול זנותה ותחנף הארץ (Jer. III.9), הדם יחניף את הארץ (Numb. XXXV.33), והארץ חנפה תחת יושביה (Is. XXIV.5). — הנה .והנני משחיתם the term for presenting, granting. With הנה one fulfills the demands which arise from the circumstances. Accordingly: against these circumsances I interpose destruction. But this destruction is no annihilation, it is the salvation which is demanded by these circumstances.

V. 14. תבה, a receptacle that only occurs in this narrative and in that of the saving of Moses, where it also serves as means of saving a person from the water. Its derivation is obscure. In any case its shape is that of a box and not of a boat. Its shape is broad at the bottom and tapering at the top, the reverse of the shape of a boat. For it is not designed at all to cleave through the waters, but to be borne by them. — קנים, from קנן a stronger form of גנן to protect, to fence in, from which we get גן, garden, קן, a smaller enclosure to shelter live creatures, a nest, here in general, cages for animals. It does not say לתבה, but את התבה, the whole structure is to be קנים, not primarily a dwelling for Noah and his family, and in it also accommodation for animals, possibly for their use, but the whole structure is to be a house of salvation for living creatures.

כפר (related to קבר ,גבר), basic meaning: a protecting or restricting covering. Protective, so that nothing from outside affects it, as here, and so also כפרת, cover; restrictive, that what is covered is kept in and does not affect what is outside, as כפר פנים, keeping rage back, כפר ברית (Is. XXVIII. 18) restricting the working of a covenant. In reference to sin it occurs with both meanings כפר על הנפש וגו׳ ,מן החטא, to protect the person, the nation, the Sanctuary, from the effects of sins committed, and also פשע וכו׳ כפר על עון ,כפר, to keep back, to prevent the sin from having its effects. כפר: village, where the houses have no other meaning than protection for the field-workers, in contrast to עיר where the houses have meaning in themselves as centres for the whole civic culture; the house of the land-worker is not his עיר (see above IV. 17). כפיר, a young male lion who already begins to be a leader and protector of a pride of lions. The name of the word גפר is in close phonetic relationship to כפר, and perhaps in the wood itself there may by some special water-resisting quality.

V. 16. צהר. The צ-form of זהר seems almost to indicate artificial lighting. (Is oil perhaps primarily called יצהר, as its most important use was as a means of lighting, otherwise, as a means for nourishment שמן?). Surely it is not without reason that the arangements for the ark are so specially told us, and later on again stressed that Noah did everything כן, exactly as prescribed. God could have saved Noah in a thousand different ways. Whether the size of the ark was sufficient normally to hold its contents etc. etc. are considerations which we really can leave aside. God chose one man, he is to save himself, his family, and the animal world for the future, he can save them and himself if, and only if, he does everything as, and only as, he is commanded. גדול המצווה ועושה ממי שאין מצווה ועושה, doing a good deed which you are commanded to do being greater than doing it spontaneously, is one of the first Jewish principles. Contrary to the opinion usually held, only that has really true value which is done in fulfilment of the Will of God. What one does according to one’s own prompting etc. has only doubtful, secondary importance. What a lot more could Noah have done in the 120 years; built a hundred arks etc. etc. So that what it may want to tell us here is that Noah restricted himself to do, but to do exactly and completely, that which God had ordered, and left the rest to God.

V. 17. “This thou hast to do, and I, — behold I, etc.”; in the הנני lies the expression that the terrible and serious act which God had the intention to do, was demanded by the circumstances themselves. — מבול, clearly from the root נבל which means the decay, the wasting away of the forces of life, in the organic, animal, or spiritual world. Hence נבל the withering of leaves, נבל the dwindling of strength, becoming fatigued, נָבָל ,נְבָלָה, becoming foolish, spiritual weakness, and finally נְבֵלָה, the body completely without spirit, the corpse. It is only a weaker form of נפל, accordingly the gradual withering, dying off, whether of animal, vegetable, or mental and moral forces. מבול, accordingly, the deprivation of life, and as the doom which is about to be inflicted is expressed by this term, the catastrophe is stamped as being of the mildest charcter, (If I dared, I would translate מבול by euthanasia I.L.). Everything which is earthly, in any case, is destinated finally to “נבול״; all those who were affected by the destruction would not have lived for ever; they only met an earlier death. Altogether it says, with great discriminating care, what is to be killed: אשר בו רוח חיים לשחת כל בשר, only the “cases” which contain the spirit of life, which, in any case, at some time become נבלות, but not the life itself, also not the spirit of life (רוח is the invisible force that causes movement), and least of all, the נפש, the immortal personality. “Cessation of life comes, to interrupt the path of the life of the sheaths in which the spirit of life is enclosed”.

יגוע, root גוע. Our sages already remark that this is an expression which preferably is used in connection with the death of righteous men, at Abraham, Isaac, Jacob: ויגוע וימת ויאסף אל עמיו, and here it is used to describe the fall of this generation! Nothing is more significant than the choice of just this expression. For here it is not a human being who is picturing with all its horrors the nightmare of an extermination of a whole generation, as we find it depicted in the various pictures in words and brush. It is the merciful compassionate Creator and Lord of the world Who is giving us particulars of His actions. Just like the term מבול, so is this גרע in this respect highly significant. גוע, relation to גוה, the root of גֵוָה, materiality, גו the body, the back, גויה the dead body, גוי, the national body as a whole in its external relations, as opposed to עם, its internal, social ones. Further to גֵבֶא, an assemblage of liquid, a well, to גבה, an assemblage of solid materials, hence high, then גבעה ,גבע a hillock, גבה a humpback. From all this we get the underlying basic meaning, a mass of material, and גוע would describe the moment in which the body, which till then had been conscious, feeling, responsive, becomes simply ‘a mass of material”, i.e. unconscious, non-responsive. It would be a condition which, if it precedes death, makes death painless to the dying. Thus in ב״ר the word יגוע is explained simply as יצמוק, to become torpid. How could the compassionate God — to speak in terms of human beings — behave in a more merciful manner, how could He announce the coming event to the man who had to live through it, and who could hardly have lived through the picture in his mind of the struggling, panting despair of so many millions of creatures drowning, how could He have announced it in a more mild and reassuring manner than: all בשר, everything conscious, everything responsive will, in one moment, become torpid, become a mass of material, יגוע! Material feels nothing, and then, what happens further to it is naught but reduction back to its elements. Unconsciousness, death, dissolution — וימה ,מתו ,ויגוע — these three stages are also, later on at the historical account of the event in Ch. VII. 21, 22, 23, clearly kept apart.

V. 18. ברית, root ברת, related to פרט ,פרד ,ברד, all of which express a separation (from which ברת, a piece, ברת ארץ a stretch, probably comes). ברית is an arrangement which is to be carried out, quite independently of all external circumstances, even in opposition to them. It literally corresponds to the conception of the “absolute”, something separated, cut off from all connection between cause and effect, something absolutely unconditional. Hence also the establishing of a ברית is called כרת, separate, disconnect, and keeping it called קום .הקים is not the same as עמד, which is the opposite of movement, not as התיצב, the opposite of letting oneself go. קום is the opposite of falling. Now ברית is just something which has no support whatever in connection with matters in general, if left to itself would fall down, and now is only held up by the כורת הברית. The conception “covenant” is by no means adequate for ברית. Even if only because a covenant is always a two-party, a mutual agreement, whereas ברית can be completely unilateral. Thus God’s ברית with Noah, and that with the whole world that it would not be destroyed again. So also His הנני נותן לו את בריתי שלום to Phineas. Perhaps nothing has ever required the nature of a ברית more than the preservation of Noah. The few boards themselves surely were not the actual means of salvation, otherwise others could also have saved themselves. But probably in the sense of אין סומכין על הנם, according to which we always have to do everything possible ourselves, Noah had to build his ark, but the real salvation itself surely required the quite special protection of the Divine Providence; hence אתך — .ברית, the rest was all for the sake of Noah, and his merit. The family and the world of living creatures that were to be saved was all due to him.

V. 19. מכל החי, according to our sages: of all those that have the vigour and energies of life, whose vitality had not become effete by the degeneracy which had also been brought into the animal world. Equally so, זכר ונקבה יהיו, not זכר ונקבה תביא, but their characters are to be still the pure, undisturbed uncorrupted male and female. This is probably also what is meant to be stressed by the repeated למינהו in V.20. They are to be such specimens in whom the characteristics of their species had still remained unmixed and unadulterated. This undisturbed purity of breed of the pairs of animals to be saved is further designated below in Ch. VII.2 by ואשתו איש. The breeds that were to be saved were thorough-bred to such a degree that they were to be considered, in this elevated moment — elevated by God Himself — almost in human relation of marriage to each other. For the fundamental source of the whole degeneration was השחתת דרך (sexual immorality I.L.) just as the root of Noah’s beeing saved was just in his תמים character.

V. 1. Until this point everything has been related in the name of אלקים, related, how God, as Creator, Lawgiver, and Judge of the world, separated out of the degenerated world the one man and those animals who had not participated in the general corruption who were to be saved. They had deserved to be kept alive and were kept alive. The immediate primary purpose was להחיות (V. 19 I.L.) to save their lives. The following is introduced with the name ’ה. That Name which designates God as the One to Whom — lovingly educating mankind to its ultimate goal — every coming moment is considered with its reference to its attainment of this end, and arranged accordingly. By the use of this Name, the act of preservation is designated as being the foundation-stone of a new future for mankind. This further purpose of the salvation is, accordingly, in V. 3, not described as להחיות but לחיות זרע, to give life to the seed of a future on earth.

צדיק. That which above is differentiated in צדיק and תמים is here summarised in צדיק. For taken in general the whole total of our faithfulness to duty is to be just. Not only the duty to our fellow-men, but also morality. No tiny spark of intellect or spirit and life, no shred of power or strength, is our own. All are goods entrusted to us by God, with which we must deal justly and honestly. He who is immoral, who squanders and wastes forces which belong to God, who uses them outside the limits set by God, is a scoundrel before God as is a thief before men. — לפני, before Me; some things can appear right in the eyes of men but not in God’s, and the reverse. Also the ideals which men attach to words are not always true and right, least of all in times of such general degeneracy. The words virtue, just etc. remain, in every age, in current use. But the meaning applied to those words often varies with the ideas and customs of the time. Even the name “God” can pass from mouth to mouth and have lost its true meaning. Therefore לפני is by no means superfluous: צדיק לפני, righteous before Me, in the sense that I call righteous. — בדור הזה. We have already remarked how the roots תפר, דבר, תור, טור, דור have the underlying conception of a row of several objects on one thread, whether the thread be Time or something else. No person can entirely escape all the influences of his age. The strands of contemporaneity cut deep. In an age where duty is forgotten it is truly difficult for a man to be faithful to duty before God. But inasmuch as God as ’ה says this to Noah it says at the same time that He had found him suitable for His plan for the future of mankind, by his having remained faithful to duty in such times, he had within him the right nucleus for the future which God intended.

V. 2. Speaking of the animals in general above it says: they will come to you. Here of the pure animals it says: you are to take them to you. This is the first mention of בהמה טהורה. Although at that time animal flesh was not an object of human consumption and the difference between “pure” and “impure” animals was only made later on by the laws given on Sinai, nevertheless already here God designates animals to Noah by the characteristic of being “pure”. So that there must, already then, have been some occasion for making this distinction, and this occasion was offerings, for Noachides also were not allowed — and are not allowed — to bring other than pure animals as sacrifices. (Zebachim 115a). So that it is only that which is fit for all men to offer, that Jews are allowed to eat. The Jewish table and the Noachian altar stand at the same level. The choice of animals for both must, accordingly, have the same motive. What does טהור mean? טהר related to צהרים) צהר in Chaldean is טיהרא), the transparent, the particles of which are homogeneous, and allow rays of light to pass through them. So that טהור is receptive, that which allows God’s rays to pass through, offers no resistance to them. He is a “pure” man, who is receptive for the spiritual, the divine; whose mind, feelings, and body are penetrated with the godly. Its opposite is טמא; closed up, non-receptive to the godly. The prohibition of the use of certain animals for food, given in the Sinaitic laws rests in no ways on considerations of physical health, and equally just as little on climatic conditions. The same Lord even orders it to be given to the גר׳ תושב, the alien living in Israel, the benevolent support of whose well-being is made a duty of love for Jews (Levit. 25,35, Deut. 14,21). But the motive for the prohibition is given explicitly in the Torah as being for the avoidance of the results of טומאה and שקוץ, and the object to be achieved by its observance, as קדושה, holiness. The forbidden foods are partly מטמא, negative, tend to render the eater not susceptible to higher thoughts, feelings etc., partly משקץ, positive, lead to the ungodly, bad. So that if the purity of man towards God consists in his being receptive to the godly, and this receptivity is dependent on his בשר, his body, being truly מבשר, “the herald, the messenger”, in service of the spirit, then only such animal foods would be “pure” which, when they are absorbed for renewing the tissues of the body, do not tend to dull impressions, or awake impulses through which people become insusceptible to the spiritual, and more inclined to the appeal of the senses, the material, (elsewhere Hirsch puts it that, in this world, the spirit can only express itself through the medium of the body, we can only think thoughts, however sublime and lofty, through our brains, and only have feelings, however tender, through our nerves, and brain and nerves are concrete material, the tissues of which are constantly wearing away and being renewed, in the wonderful metabolism of the body, by the food which we eat. I.L.). This food, then, would come from such animals which, on their part, are more inclined to be receptive to human influences, whose nature is such that, without requiring taming, they easily submit to man, and serve his purposes; such animals in which altogether the qualities of beast and passion do not overwhelmingly predominate. Now, on the other hand, which animals would be most suitable for sacrifices? We do not see the prototype of mankind in savages, the first human being, and the nobler natures amongst the Noachides, stood near to God. An Adam, Abel, Seth, Noah, an Abraham, Isaac, Jacob did not stand before an idol when they brought offerings, as people nowdays like to ascribe not only our idea in praying for the restoration of the sacrifices, but all the great minds of the past who did bring them, a David, an Isaiah etc. who in bringing sacrifices saw Israel’s nearness to God, and in them celebrated the glorification of God. To all of these — even as to us — God is not thought of as a cruel, bloody idol who finds delight in the quivering of the muscles of a dying animal, or who would be so stupid as to accept the death of an ox as an atonement for a man’s own death, who would be content to transfer all the agony and pain and fear of death which really a man should suffer, to the death-rattle in the throat of an animal. But to us, as in the past, sacrifices were and are זבח תודה, an expression of unresisting acquiescence and devotion. The sprinkled blood, the demand and the vow to devote one’s own blood (blood, symbolic of life I.L.) to the holy Will of God; the head and limbs, breast and body, fat and kidneys placed on the Altar to God, devoted our limbs, our eyes, our breast our whole self with everything even the lowest stimulus (of which the kidneys are symbolic, see the precise symbolism in Leviticus Ch. I. I.L.) to be אשה ה׳ לחם, “food to keep godliness alive on earth” (see ibid I.L.). The one who brought an offering — even Noachides — was taught and vowed to offer himself to God. And so, again, only such animals are suitable for offerings, which come nearest to human nature and submit most readily to higher dictation, and so would appear best to represent human beings. Accordingly the same animals as, later on, were allowed by the Torah to be used for food for Jews were those that were chosen as the most suitable for offerings, and the same motive would seem to apply to both. Now whether the order here, to take to him “seven pair” of the pure animals, was given to Noah with an eye to his future offering (which he made immediately on his release from the ark, see Ch. 8,20 I.L.) or for the future requirements for food in accordance with the laws of God, or out of consideration of both factors, in any case we can understand why this command is introduced with the name ’ה. Simply for the purpose of the preservation of the animal world in general there would be no reason for taking more than three times more of the pure animals. The “purity” of animals only exists in connection with the purposes of the education of mankind which the name ’ה represents.

V. 4. אנכי ממטיר. He who reads the תנ״ך carefully will find that the pronoun אנכי used of God in differentiation to אני is highly characteristic. אנכי is always used in cases where the “I” does not place itself harshly against a person or being, where it designates a ruling of God in which His Love and Grace is revealed. (See פסיקתא on the verse אנכי אנכי הוא מנחמכם Is. L), whereas אני (from אנה to send, to decree) designates the Person from whom a motion or agitation starts, who is מאנה, who sends something to somebody but Himself remains afar. — אנכי, from אנך related to חנק ,ענק ,ענג ,חנך. Once אנך occurs as an independent noun: Amos 7,7, 8. הנני שם אנך בקרב עמי ישראל There it probably means the onyx, according to the Aruch, the gem שוהם, which, as we know is used for engraving, i.e. is the bearer of inscriptions. Thus in Avoda Zara 7b, the great superiority of the magnificence of the Torah over gems is demonstrated by the onyx, inasmuch as אינך נעשה בסיס לס״ת that one would use the onyx underneath the Torah as a base for it, and therefrom again the value of Israel (and the people) is shown which has the Torah hidden within it. According to that, the meaning of the verses in Amos would be:— “See, I make My people Israel, into a setting for a gem (bearing My Torah), My People are to be in no wise independent, but are to be simply a “setting for My Onyx”. (the vision shown to Amos: חומת אנך, a wall enclosing an onyx), therefore will I bring an end to this Kingdom of theirs which has become completely estranged from devotion to this idea”. — חנך is the setting, the practising, getting habituated in one’s vocation; ענג, being pleasantly surrounded by external accommodating circumstances; ענק, a collar, necklace; אנק tightening at the neck and חנק, complete strangling. All these meanings give us the underlying meaning of the root as being embracing, enclosing, bearing, taking care of, etc., and אנכי corresponds to an activity which the second person is borne, kept, and cared for by the “I”, where the “I” is in close connection with the “thou”. (The פסיקתא says that our fathers heard אנכי twice on Sinai, viz. אנכי וגו׳ אשר הוצאתיך and אנכי וגו׳ אל קנא, the same אנכי Who enclosed you, and raised you out of Egypt, is the same Who is at the same time, אל קנא Who will not tolerate that you should consider yourself borne by another).

If all this is right, then the אנכי here is infinitely significant. Although you see Me now bringing death and destruction over the whole human and animal world, nevertheless I remain in My Love and Benevolence, am, even at that moment, still the same “אנכי״ Who embraces everything, bears, keeps, and cares for everything, and even this harshest treatment has only the happiness and well-being of the whole as its purpose. This is the same idea which is expressed by speaking the Name ’ה in the books of the Prophets as אלקים. It is God’s Love which shows itself as Judge, it is the most pithy expression of the Oneness of God, the most expressive negation of any idea of Dualism.

Forty days. Our sages remind us that this is the same period as that required for the formation of the human foetus, so that this duration of the catastrophe could in itself be taken as showing the destruction to be, in its deeper meaning, the formation of a new future.

מחה ,ומחיתי, blot out, obliterate; to wipe away presupposes the previous dissolution. Its opposite is יקום, which only occurs once, and also in connection with a destruction, at the rebellion of Korach, and it means the independent, standing oneself up as being independent, and thus opposing and resisting the fall. The אשר עשיתי is significant, it was I, Myself Who made them, life and independence of My creatures is My Joy, My Purpose, and it is only their misuse that I am opposing. — ’כאשד צוהו ה, again ’ה, for the essential element of these orders belonged to the formation of the future לחיות זרע, to sow new life on the new world again; and even the taking “clean animals” sevenfold was, as already remarked, perhaps with an eye to that People of God’s Torah which had the mission to be the most important instrument in the Hands of God to educate mankind to their ultimate happiness without the necessity of a fresh מבול.

V. 6. בן שש מאות שנה. A man is the continuous product of the years of his life. Every year works physically and psychically at changing him. Accordingly our language calls him a son of his years. Similarly it calls him also a son of his character, בן בליעל, also a son of the punishment to be given him, בן הכות.

V. 9. They came in pairs as God had commanded Noah. God had given Noah the command to take in the pairs of animals, but carrying it out, especially respecting חיות, and the selection of pairs that had kept pure in their breeding, lay quite beyond his powers. But here appears in concrete actuality that important fact, shown in the sacred scriptures, that the same God Who gives laws to mankind is also the lawgiver and director of Nature, in other words that ’ה is also אלקים. He Who gave Noah the command which he was to obey of his own free will, also led the animals to him in such a manner that he was able to fulfil the command. This fact, that the God of mankind is identical with the God of Nature, that the Word of God which administers Nature is the same which gave His Law to Man to be observed by his own free will is a principle of Jewish consciousness which, amongst others, David sang in Ps. CXLVII השלח אמרתו ארץ וגו׳ הנתן שלג כצמר וגו׳ משליך קרחו כפתים וגו׳ ישלח דברו וימסם זגו׳ מגיד דבריו ליעקב חקיו ומשפטיו לישראל וגו׳. Cf. 5,5 above. ’ויעש נח ככל אשר צוהו ה and here, שנים שנים באו וגו׳ כאשר צוה אלקים את נח.

V. 10. We are now given an exact account, with dates, of the actual occurrence, how everything happened precisely as it had been previously announced. This raises the whole catastrophe out of the realm of the blind workings of the forces of nature, and stamps it as the free-willed administration of the Divine Providence. In the same way we find later on the miracles in Egypt being always announced before they happened. Here the worlds of Nature and of mankind are shown to be under the government of One Single Lord and Master. In opposition to the non-Jewish view, which sees in the flood only the result of blind natural forces, here we have the record of Noah showing us two powers in faithful obedience to the Will of God, on the one hand Noah and on the other unreasoning Nature. The birds in the air, the crawling worm, all knew the way to Noah “at God’s command”, and — in no way in a natural manner — two by two, male and female, and in the same way, the invading flood burst open only on the day fixed by God.

V. 11. פקח ,פקע) בקע) to tear asunder. — עין ,מעין: source and eye. The eye, as already remarked, is the source through which the visible world flows into the mind. So also באר is a well, and also to clarify, make clear; חפר to dig and to examine, investigate. — תהום (from המם the billowing wave) the great mighty flood. To the water already in existence, wide openings were torn asunder. — ארבה .ארבות is a preventative by which something is kept ready to break forth suddenly. A river lock.

V. 14. עוף .כל צפור כל כנף designates the bird after its movement. עוף to strive towards something, to fly there. כנף related to גנב, designates the wing after its movement, it withdraws the bird from the earth. The derivation of צפור is obscure. It is to be found in צפרן, nail, and in צפיר, synonymous with שעיר the hairy one, the goat. So that צפור could be the bird called after its covering with feathers, the feathered one. The root צפר would then be common for nails, hair and feathers which are all three really derivatives fundamentally from the same tissue, (the epidermis I.L.). It is also not clear what is said here by the threefold description “כל העוף למינהו בל צפור כל כנף״. Perhaps by עוף is meant everything that flies, in general, and here, differentiating from צפור, would refer to flying insects, butterflies etc., while צפור would then be “feathered fliers”, birds. But our sages always take צפור to refer to pure birds only. Perhaps the reason why everything that flies seems to be so specially stressed, is that the inhabitants of the air are those that keep farthest away from the habitations of men, but, here, at God’s command they all came in to Noah.
V. 15. Here Man appears in his highest dignity. The whole animal world comes to him as its saviour and preserver.

V. 16. They were only allowed to enter because they came “male and female”, two by two. ויסגר ה׳ בעדו. Although Noah had done everything, the rescue was not assured thereby, he had done all that he had been commanded to do, but it was ’ה, God’s intention of preservation of life for the future, that protected him. What this protection consisted of, what God did for Noah, is told us in the following verses.

V. 17—20. The story as it is related here seems to be interrupted in the middle. Verses 17 and 18 are told with ו׳ ההיפוך, in successive order. But verse 19 starts with the past tense, והמים גברו, not ויגברו המים and accordingly refers to a previous time (not the waters rose, but the waters had risen I.L.). The ark had been built, be it ever so strong, the danger would be immediately very imminent that, at a flood which demolished everything, it would be dashed to pieces at the first cliff or mountain it encountered. So, immediately, the protective foresight of God was necessary. As the waters first swelled and covered the surface of the earth, and certainly gushed in torrents, the ark was only raised,

but it stood still only when, V,18, the water had risen to an immense height, only then did it begin to move, for then, V,19, the waters had swollen to such a height that all mountains were covered to a height of 15 cubits above their summits, and the danger of crashing was past.
V. 21 See above, VI,17.

V. 22. If it is true that the diluvial strata of the geologists are attributable to our flood, the fact that the remnants found therein are especially those of land animals, and not of marine animals, would be explained by מכל אשר בחרבה מתו, as, according to this only land animals were affected by the flood.

V. 1. זכר .ויזכור: (related to סכר, to lock up): to keep and hold fast in the memory. — אלקים. According to the sages this rescue and retoration was judged by God, as being justly deserved, apart from the associated consideration for the new future of mankind. Hence this Name of God is used.

וישכו (root שכך). The use of this expression indicates that the action of the waters of the flood was not merely mechanically destructive but also chemically dissolving. According to one remark in Sanhedrin 108b, they were רותחין, seething. שכך is the reverse of boiling and bubbling up of a torrent. חמת המלך שככה (Esther 7,10). שכך in this sense is related to שגג the opposite of זוד ,מזיד to boil. שגג is not to be confused with שגג .שגה is error brought about by carelessness. The wrong consists in being quiet and indifferent when one should be neither. Regarding our fate, our fortune, placidity, indifference is something very good, but considering as to how we behave, it is something very bad. Of the latter it says אשרי איש מפחד תמיד and of the former שגה .פחדו בציון חטאים, on the other hand is error brought about by too intensive concentration of the mind. It designates such a blind attachment of the mind to one particular direction or to one object that by that it is drawn away from everything else, and has no consideration of anything else. Hence we find the expression שוגה בײן ,באהבתה תשגה תמיד. Hence also in פ׳ קרבנות (Levit. I.) שגגה is used for actual practical errors of the people and שגיה for the theoretical errors of the Sanhedrin.
V. 2. סכר ,ויסכרו related to סגר to close. שכר too, is nothing else but closing a void, making good, restoring, hence wage.
V. 3. וישובו. They returned to the depths out of which they had come.

V. 7. יבשת המים. The last stage was יבשה הארץ (V.14), the beginning was יבשת המים, that already here and there something dry was visible in the water. The stages of becoming dry are described by the expressions: ויחסרו המים, the waters abated until the tops of the mountains first became visible; קלו מעל פני האדמה, they then became just a light layer on the surface of the earth; חרבו פני האדמה, the surface of the earth became dry, no more water was visible; יבשה הארץ, the earth was dry became again יבשה, regained its original firmness.

Noah first of all sent the עורב out, a bird that normally does not seek the vicinity of men, ערבה, the wilderness is its home. If it comes back, it must be quite homeless outside. That is also probably the reason that with the raven it does not say מאתו, as it does with the dove which is used to being with human beings, and of which it says in V.9, at its return: ויקחה ויבא אותה אליו. If the dove does not come back it must have already become quite comfortable outside.

V. 10. ויחל. If ויחל were to be taken as “and he waited”, as some contracted form of וײחל, or in the sense of ויחילו עד בוש (Judges 3,25) (which latter really rather means an expectation), then the עוד שבעת ימים אחרים “yet another seven days” would be inexplicable, as we have not been told that he had already waited once seven days. Perhaps ויחל is the Hiphil of either חלל to begin, or of חול to enter, and it would say: “Noah first let yet another seven days start”. For the destruction had come in just such periods, first seven days and then forty. Between the age that was to be destroyed and the beginning of the destruction, seven days passed (V.10, I.L.) in which nothing was changed. It was just a period for letting the age run out. Noah was conscious that God had not forgotten him, the ark had come to rest and the tops of the mountains were visible. But Noah still did not open the ark, he thought that the flood would subside in the same way that it had come. He waited accordingly forty days. But then he found out that the conditions outside were not yet habitable, so he supposed that, similarly to the onset of the flood, seven days would again have to elapse between the complete end of the destruction and the entry of the new age. Accordingly “he allowed a similar seven days to pass again”. We find such periods of seven days to mark the complete passing away of one condition before the entry of a new one, later on in the Torah in connection with טומאה וטהרה etc.

V. 11. Towards evening: so it had remained outside the whole day so that a considerable change had already occurred. — טָרָף, is not a verb, but a noun like טֶרֶף, food seized by oneself, and the word is chosen here with the utmost significance. What an animal in a free condition takes independently for food is called טרף. Thus טרף נתן ליראיו, that which others only get by “snatching” the יראים get from the Hand of God. For a whole year the dove had been fed but had not enjoyed טרף, food gained independently by its own efforts. That it had remained out the whole day was already a sign that קלו המים; it already found מנוח for its foot. But it could have been driven back again by hunger. Then it arrives with an olive leaf in its mouth as food — something that it normally does not use for food! Our sages take this bitter olive leaf in the mouth of the dove to preach the great fact: Bitter, unusual, normally intolerable food, eaten in freedom and independence, is sweeter than the sweetest in a dependent condition. So for us the olive leaf is not a symbol of peace but of the value of independence and freedom and of content and moderation.

V. 12. וײחל, the Niphal of יחל to await, to stay for something, really the anticipated beginning of something, differentiated from קוה, to hope, in which no opinion is expressed about the beginning of the desired thing, but of which in יחל one is convinced. Here it is used in the Niphal whereas generally יחל only occurs in the Piel and Hiphil. But the Niphal, when it is used gives it almost the opposite meaning e.g. Ez. 19,5 ותרא כי נוחלה אבדה תקותה, “she saw herself dissappointed in her expectations”. We can find an analogy for this effect of the Niphal in revoking the conception of the Kal or Piel in: נהײתי נחלתי (Dan. 8,27). “I was faint and fell ill” (my state of life was checked, interrupted). תאוה נהיה (Prov. 13,19) “desire conquered or overcome”. Similarly here: Noah had believed that he would be able to go out after the expiration of the first seven days, but he found himself disappointed in his expectation, and in this state of deferred expectation, allowed seven days more to pass.

V. 17. היצא, whereas הוצא means lead them out, היצא means, give them the permission to go out. In the form הוצא the activity of those that go out, is quite secondary to the one that takes them out, they are quite passive. In היצא the activity of those that go out is kept in its independance. Only give them the permission and they go out by themselves.
