The whole relief, the breathing freely again of those going out of the unnatural restriction of their stay in the ark, out into the free air again, is expressed in the היצא.

V. 19. למשפחתיהם. Once again, at their going out, the great law of למיניהם for the living organic world is given as their accompanying escort. משפחה, root שפח, related to צבא ,סבא ,שפה ,ספה ,ספח ,שבע ,שבע ,שפע etc. all of which have the meaning of plentitude, of the accumulation, the gathering of many to a mass. (By way of parenthesis note how the שפחה, that person who, in the non-Jewish point of view, stands at the very lowest social grade, in the Jewish point of view, as is expressed in the name they give her, is raised to a member of the family).

V. 20. If there is anything by which the deep significance of offerings is disclosed, and which proves the falsity of all the disparaging representation of their idea, it is here, where we are first introduced to מזבח and עולות.

For a whole year Noah had had to spend all his energies and give all his time to feeding and looking after the animals and keeping them alive and now, at the first moment after having saved them — he sacrificed them! And this sacrifice is of such infinite, far-reaching importance for the whole of the history of the world, that in the following verses 21 and 22, expressly as a result of this offering, almost as if it were an answer to it, — ’וירח ה׳ וגו׳, ויאמר ה׳ אל לבו וגו — the whole future development of the world and mankind is fixed! Now what really was expressed by Noah’s building an altar and bringing עולות, that could result in such provision by God for preserving the world and founding development? It is evident from many places in the scriptures that מזבח is an elevation of the earth towards God built by the hands of Man, so that in Ezekiel the מזבח is simply called הראל, the Mount of God. More, it is extremely likely that the מזבח in the מקדש is nothing else but a representation of Mt. Sinai, and the אש המערכה on its summit corresponded to the אש אוכלה בראש ההר. Thus we find in Ps. LXVIII, אדני בם סיני בקדש “then God steeped out of the lofty heights of Heaven into the narrow sphere of Man, and His Mount into the Sanctuary”; and the term in עולת תמיד העשויה בהר סיני :פ׳ התמיד almost certainly means the same. In this respect it is characteristic that one of the things in which the Jewish Sanctuary of the Torah differs from the Noachian conceptions is, that there the altar on which we are allowed to bring offerings had to be a מזבח built up of stones, but not a מצבה, not made of one single stone or rock presented for it by Nature. We have to build the altar ourselves. It must not be על גבי כיפין ועמודים, standing on arch or pillars, must be מחובר באדמה, must be מזבח אדמה, in direct contact with the ground, must represent a continuation of the earth. Only thus does the altar express the elevation of the earth towards God by human activity. To take a single slab of stone and sacrifice thereon would mean recognizing God from the standpoint of Nature; whereas the built מזבח expresses the conception of first working oneself up above the bound character of Nature to the godlike free-willed standpoint of Man, and, from that point of view, strive upward to God. So that inasmuch as Noah built an altar to God on the fresh gift of the earth, he, as the Ancestor, dedicated this newly-gifted earth to ba a place on which the future activity of mankind is to add stone to stone until ultimately the whole becomes a holy mount of God.

When other nations tried, and try, to get near their God, they get away from human surroundings and believe they can find God nearer to them out in nature. Certainly one can find God there too, but He is much nearer in all His Glory in the sphere of a human life. There, in Nature, His Omnipotence, His infinite Power is revealed, here His infinite Love. That is why the מזבח is the more dedicated altar in comparison with the stone set up from nature as a מצבה. This thought is such an essential one for the Jewish Sanctuary of the Torah, that in all the surroundings of the altar, or in the building that encloses it, no tree or any board that reminds one of a tree, was allowed to be visible.

מזבח, root זבח, that killing which had no purpose of destroying, but of nourishing. זבח really means a meal, it is phonetically related to שבע סבא, etc. all of which have the meaning of fulness, satiation. Altogether offerings are considered as a “meal”, they are ’לחם אשה ה food to nourish the fire of godliness on earth. The one who brings an offering devotes himself to keep the flame of the Divine Light illuminating the world.

Moreover, in connection with offerings God is always referred to as ’ה (the God of Love, I.L.) never as אלקים (the God of Nature and Justice, I.L.) to avoid the slightest idea of confusion with the non-Jewish sacrifices which were brought to the powers of nature. But the name, ’ה, at the same time, violently opposes that blasphemous view of people who see in offerings nothing but slaughter and death, see therein the “bloody” satisfaction of an angry vengeful god, and in their narrow-minded dullness rejoice that, thank God, today we bring no sacrifices, and thank God we are sufficiently enlightened to know that God is not served by the blood of offerings. Against them the Name ’ה at offerings comes with confounding defence. It was to this conception of God, too, (’ה the God of Love. I.L.) that here Noah built the altar, and that also which the forehead of the Jewish High Priest bore to counter any impure disturbance of the true pure thoughts of Jewish offerings. It is accordingly, just to ’ה, to that conception of God which desires life, not death, to which our offerings are directed, from Whom all life and all future flows, Who is ready, every moment, to grant fresh life, fresh strength and a fresh future; one sacrifices one’s life to God, to get life from Him, to have one’s life elevated into the sphere of a happy godly life on earth. At Jewish offerings there is no thought of a bloody sacrifice to a god of revenge burning with anger. There, every beat of the pulse, every impulse of the nerves, every force of the muscles is dedicated to God and to the fulfilment of His Holy Will. To sacrifice, means: to absorb oneself into a godly eternal life. It is not the animal, it is oneself, represented by the animal, that one offers. When we bring it near, support ourselves with our hands upon it, let its blood be taken up and sprinkled onto the altar, its head, its feet, its breast and its body etc. be given over to the fire, it is our blood, our head, all the strength of our muscles that we are completely giving up to godliness, giving ourselves completely over to the overwhelming power of the Divine Will which He has laid down for us in the Torah.

Noah brought עולות. The offerings of Cain and Abel were מנחות, gifts of allegiance, offerings of recognition, but עולות have the idea of the dedication of our actions. עלה, to rise, to develop oneself. עולה is מכפר על עשה, is to wake up one’s power of action, which has become sluggish, to energetic activity in dutiful actions, is to spur it on לעלות to make progress, to strive upwards to the heights which beckon to us as our goal and destination. Whereas חטאת teaches us to hold fast to that height of morality which we had reached, but from which we had lapsed through carelessness or indifference (שגגה, I.L.), and to which, accordingly the finger of the priest directs the blood on the top of the altar בנתינה על קרנות המזבח, at עולה the priest stands with the blood (representing the life I.L.) at a distance, and from there throws it onto the lower half of the altar, and thereby says to the one who brings the offering who has sinned by inactivity, (has not actually done anything wrong but has not done enough right, I.L.) out of laziness or conceit: you stand far away, not even בתחתית ההר and certainly not on the height of the mission of your life, so you have to gather all the strength of your life together to direct them with all your energy (the act of throwing I.L.) towards, and up to, the heights of what you are meant to be.

All these points require more detailed reasoning and further working out, but will be left to our consideration and investigations on the פ׳ הקרבנות (Levit. I). Here we only had to touch on them to get the point of view for a correct estimation of Noah’s offering.

When Noah built an altar to God on the earth once again presented to mankind, and brought עולות thereon, he thereby dedicated the earth to be a place on which mankind striving upwards to God would add stone to stone until they formed the whole world into a mount of God, on which, devoting all their energy and strength, they would strive in constant progress, to the height of their God-serving vocation in life.

For this offering he took some of all the pure animals and birds. We have already remarked above that the Noachides also used only pure animals for offerings, and we thought that their reason for this choice might lie in the fact that these seem by their natures to be more suitable to represent human personalities. And actually, later on, in the laws given for offerings, we do find the different animals ordered to be used vary, both as to kind and sex, in accordance with the different personalities they are to represent: the כה״ג and סנהדרין by a פר; the נשיא by a הדיוט ;שעיר by a שעירה or a כבש נקבה etc. If, then, this offering on behalf of the future of mankind consisted of all the kinds of pure animals, the thought behind it could have had the additional nuance: into however different personalities human beings may form themselves in the course of the development of the ages, all are to become עולות on this מזבח, on this earth raising itself to an altar to God.

V. 21. ניחוח ,ריח הניחוח is the noun from נוח, like ניצוץ from נוץ, and only occurs in connection with offerings. נוח is motion come to rest, and hence הניח is really bringing to rest, granting rest, also used for granting a wish, giving satisfaction; thus יסר בנך ויניחך (Prov. XXIX), פני ילכו והנחתי לך (Ex. XXXIII). But the root נוח with this meaning never occurs for giving satisfaction or pleasure to the senses, as it would be if ריח ניחוח were to mean “a pleasant odour, a sweet savour”. In one single instance we do find ונחת שלחנך שלא דשן (Job. 36,16). But there too, and just there, it would also be only an expression for spiritual satisfaction. There it says: “Even if God had removed thee from every strait, thy well-being would still lack a sound foundation, even if the satisfaction which thy table grants thee would be the fulness of super-abundance, as long as thou accomplisheth the guilt of the guilty, guilt and foredoom will hold thee”. Accordingly there is not the slightest doubt that the gerundial form of the Piel: ניחוח means the satisfaction granted to the wishes or efforts of another. ריח ניחוח would then be, the smell or odour of giving satisfaction, of fulfilling the wishes, not that the smell itself is pleasant. — ריח, root רוח: wind. If we consider that רחים means a mill, we see that ריח does not primarily mean the action of the sense of smelling but really refers to the quality of the substance diffusing its exhalation. For a mill is an instrument for reducing a substance to its finest particles. הריח means to smell because in smelling the finest particles of a substance are received. Only those things give off a smell, from which finest particles emanate. The sense of smell is that sense in which fine particles of a substance at a distance have to come into direct contact with the nerve-ending. Whereas in the senses of taste and touch the substance itself has to come into contact with the nerve-endings, hearing and sight only receive impressions from things at a distance, the sense of smell is between the other four. The objects can be at some distance, as in sight and sound, but tiny particles must come into direct contact, as in taste and touch. Hence ריח is used as an idiom for receiving the slightest impression of anything (“getting a hint” I.L.): מריח מים יפריח (Job 14,19) “from the ‘smell’ of water, the withered plant blooms up again”; מרחוק יריח מלחמה “the war-horse ‘smells’ war from afar”. (cf. our English: this “smells” fishy to me, etc, I.L.). If then ריח in general mans: the finest, most delicate realisation of something, an offering as ריח ניחוח would be a slight, just indicating expression of compliance with the Will of God. A slight expression, only indicating that we would fulfil the Will of God. The offering itself is not yet compliance, ניחוח, but ריח ניחוח, a hint, an indication of the satisfying of His Will that God is to find in our lives, an indication of readiness to yield to His Will. That the conceptions of ריח and ניחוח are separate ones is apparent from the six demands that are made for each offering (Zebachim 46b): לשם ששה דברים הזבח נזבח לשם זבח וכו׳, לשם ריח and quite separately לשם ניחוח i.e. הנחת רוח.

But here, at this important occasion it says for the only time in the whole of ריח הניחוח :תנ״ך. All other offerings are only symbolic expressions of a fulfilling of God’s Will, for no single individual and no single age can accomplish the whole of it, hence ריח ניחוח. But Noah had the whole of future mankind before him, his offering referred to all that which, in the course of time, was to be accomplished by the whole of mankind to the final complete satisfaction of God with Man, hence his offering was ריח הניחוח, an indication of the complete compliance with God’s Will to which the whole of mankind is to mature on the freshly regained earth, now dedicated to be an altar to God.

ויאמר ה׳ אל לבו. We have already drawn attention to the importance of the use of this and similar anthropomorphic expressions referring to God. The danger of getting some corporeal conception of God is by far not so great as that of volatalising Him to a vague, obscure, metaphysical idea. It is much more important to be convinced of the personality of God, and of His intimate relations to every man on earth, than to speculate on the transcendental conceptions of infinity, incorporeality, etc. which have almost as little to do with the morality of our lives as algebraic ciphers. Everything which, in human beings, attaches them to the creatures around them, and especially to those near to them, is here, in God, epitomised in the expression לב. As truly as we can say of God that He is חנון ,רחום, loving, merciful, gracious, etc., so can all these qualities, His מדות, be expressed together in לב here. It is completely parallel to the previous ויתעצב אל לבו (VI,6) where “He grieved at His heart” i.e. where He sorrowfully renounced all the happiness which His Benevolence and Love had wished mankind to attain. So here too, the whole complex of the Divine Benevolence and Love spoke for the future preservation of the human world. Our sages point out to us that it says here אל לבו not בלבו as an example for morally free-willed human beings who are not to be ברשות לבם, the slaves of their sentiments and feelings (their hearts are not to run away with their heads I.L.). They remind us how everywhere, when referring to men who are to be examples for us, it says אל לבו, thus חנה היא מדברת על לבה, ויאמר דניאל אל לבו, ויאמר דוד אל לבו and in contrast ויאמר ירבעם בלבו, ויאמר עשו בלבו, אמר נבל בלבו, ויאמר המן בלבו. Accordingly, ויאמר ה׳ אל לבו all the מדות הרחמים stood before God and pleaded for the future preservation of mankind, and however far away the earth might be from the goal it was to reach, having regard to this goal indicated by Noah in his offering, God said: ’לא אוסיף עוד וגו.

קלל .לקלל, the root of קל light, the opposite of כבד, heavy, and so the opposite of ברכה, blessing. Blessing is the continuously progressive development of a creature by which it receives ever increasing expansion, always assimilates more material matter, its being bears the impression of, and impresses by, an ever greater material diversity. Thus the blessing of fertility to man, animal, tree, etc. The opposite: — if anything is losing its material matter, is checked in its material development, is קללה. Up to then God had slowed down the development of the אדמה for the benefit of man. בעבור האדם, for the purpose of his moral and spiritual salvation, thus, with Adam, Cain, etc.. God will not curtail the fertile powers of the earth any further for the purpose of educating mankind. Now, as far as we can see, the following ’כי יצר לב האדם וגו has been completely erroneously taken to be the cause of this new determination of destiny: “For the inclination of the heart of Man is evil from his youth”. We can not understand what the reasoning is supposed to be. Possibly “because, after all it would be of no use!” That would be an extremely unworthy statement for us to ascribe God making about Himself and His Work. For one may not over-look the fact that the same words are used above for the cause of the punishment, and now here they are to be the cause for the reverse! God brought the מבול because כל יצר מחשבות לבו רק רע כל היום (VI,5) and here out of consideration of this same יצר הרע forbearance, indulgence is to be granted! The construction of the verse also speaks against this way of taking it. According to it, the ’כי יצר לב וגו should come last: לא אוסיף עוד לקלל וגו׳, ולא אוסיף להכות וגו׳, כי יצר וגו׳, because then the stress should have to fall on it. As the verse stands, the stress lies on the two ’לא אוסיף וגו and the ’כי יצר וגו is in parenthesis — “If the יצר לב האדם should be רע again, and even מנעוריו, so that the only way of saving it would be the destruction of that generation, nevertheless I will not again, as I did, לא ’אוסיף עוד וגו. We have already pointed out (Ch. 2,19) that יצר does not designate the active impelling force, but the passive result of it, that which the human mind forms, makes the ideal for which it strives; now what is the meaning of נעורים ,מנעוריו youth? Why is youth so called? The original meaning of נער is to shake off, thus of Samson (Judges 16,20) אנער or נוער כפיו מתמול בשוחד (Is. 43,15) etc. Also נעורת, tow, oakum, the waste of flax. Youth is called נעורים because it is the time in which young human beings really want to grow out of themselves. Neither good nor bad impressions cling very fast to them, human nature is still in its natural state with them, not yet cloaked with hypocrisy, easily shakes off both good and bad impressions. “Boys will be boys, we can not put old heads on young shoulders” (Jugend hat keine Tugend:), true, but also no vice. Woe unto them that take the average of child and adolescent nature to be evil! Who has really observed children, says: No, it is not true that youth is bad, it is not מנעוריו that יצר לב האדם רע that man makes evil his ideal. In normal times one finds a much greater number of adults than of adolescents whose hearts and minds are directed to evil. Quite a lot does get done by youth that is bad because they are not yet used to bow to the command of duty, to place their necks under the עול מצות, because they still regard self-control and obedience to duty as an irksome yoke which their natures, striving up to independence, “shake off”. But it is just in this independence of Will, which is not so easily overcome, and which in their immaturity certainly does appear as obstinacy, that the whole morality of the future man has its roots. Just as God chose Israel, not because it was the most amenable of nations but because it was the most stiff-necked, because once this obstinacy and independence of spirit had been overcome and directed into use in the right direction for good (as occurred) then this obstinacy and independence would be used to preserve and stick obstinately to the good and right. In the same way, for the sake of the future firmness in goodness and virtue God has implanted the principle of independence in the heart of every man. It is true that in youth, this does appear as נעורים, shaking the restraining reins off, unwilling to submit to guidance. But when the mind matures, and insight ripens to realise that what hitherto has been regarded as restraint and restriction, in reality leads to freedom and ensures the true freedom of will of Man, then it is just youth that becomes enthusiastic for the ideals of pure morality and nobility, and makes resolutions for the deepest devotion to, and sacrifices for, all that is high and noble and sublime. It is not youth, but age, where selfishness and voluptuousness and greed, and the false “cleverness” which passes for wisdom, mocks at goodness and nobility and loftiness as the dreams of youth, teaches, indeed to be proper and becoming and have good manners, but itself, no longer “נער״ indulges in its passions and greed. In ordinary times it is then in the older people that רע gathers its real harvest. But an age of which one could say even of the youth that they consciously aim at evil for its own sake as יצר לבם, as the ideal they have formed in their minds, that indeed would be an age that would demand a second מבול. But such a condition would not be a normal but an abnormal one. Hence it says here: “even if the images formed by the hearts of mankind should be bad right from youth”, when even the youth (in contrast to natural conditions) should have set רע as their ideal, and then really nothing more could be expected from such a generation — for all hope for the future lies in the youth, not in the old — so that there would again be reason, בעבור האדם, for the salvation of mankind, for God again to destroy the earth — nevertheless God would not do this, but:

V. 22. עוד כל ימי הארץ. This is usually taken to mean that during the time of the flood the ordinary course of time, day and night and seasons were disturbed, and here the resolution is declared, that just as altogether there will not be another general destruction, so also the regular course of time will not again be disturbed. This assumes that in the antediluvian period this change of seasons, as we know it now, was already in existence. The traditions which have been handed down to us, however, speak against this supposition (as do also the opinions of modern geologists and students of palaeogean research. Wells quotes authorities who have arrived at conclusions which agree remarkably, almost word for word, with ר׳ יצחק I.L.). According to ר׳ יצחק in ב״ר before the Flood, the fields had only to be cultivated every forty years, as eternal spring-time reigned, the seasons never changed היה להם אויר יפה כמן הפסח עד העצרת the temperature was constant and moderate, and the continents were not split asunder so that there was easy communication throughout the world, היו מהלכין מסוף העולם ועד סופו לשעה קלה. The seasons of the year mentioned in our verse here are there definitely declared to have been fresh postdiluvian innovations: ’מכאן ואילך זרע וקציר וגו so that when ר׳ שמואל בר נחמן suffered from headaches in thundery weather, he jokingly said: חזי מה עבד לן דרא דמבולא, “see what we have to thank the age of the Flood for!” The climatic stability which obtained before the Flood is quoted as being a foremost cause of the general slackness and degeneration: מי גרם להם שימרודו בי לא ע׳׳י שהיו זורעין ולא קוצרין יולדין ולא קוברין and, by the addition of יולדין ולא קוברין at the same time recognizes in these climatic conditions the cause of the longevity which prevailed before the flood, as well as in the ’מכאן ואילך זרע וקציר וגו in the altered conditions afterwards, the cause of the shorter duration of life which ensued. With this assumption of different climatic conditions, the results of geological and physical-geographical research are completely in agreement. The places where so-called antediluvian remains have been found indicate that in earlier times there was a quite different assignment of seasons and temperatures and that the splitting asunder and the conformations of the earth by oceans, rivers, mountains, volcanic eruptions, etc. as we know it now are of a later period. A saying of our sages (Berachoth 59a) seems to declare that even the position of the constellations were altered and a consequent disturbance of the telluric equilibrium was brought about by the Creator through the Flood. בשעה שבקש הקב״ה להביא מבול לעולם נטל שני כוכבים מכימה והביא מבול לעולם. But, apart from this, it is certain that our sages did not believe that there was any change of seasons in the period before the Flood.

If we consider our verse more closely we note that at הארץ the cantillation is אתנח which, as a rule, closes the sentence, so that עוד כל ימי הארץ is a complete sentence expressing a complete thought in itself. עוד, basic meaning: to last, continue, usually the particle: still, yet, which also designates continuance. But it also occurs in itself with the meaning of continuance, always etc. as עוד יהללוך סלה, “they praise Thee continually”. In this sense, here, too, עוד כל ימי הארץ could mean: All days of the earth shall henceforth be always there.

The earth until then had also experienced changes, but these changes came one after the other. To educate the existing generation God had repeatedly brought catastrophies of lack of blessing on the earth, adversity which came suddenly. But still at the end, in the centuries before the Flood, everything was still in perpetual blossom, the people were rich and grew old, they were luxurious, חמס grew, they were all old רשעים, until in face of the culminated השחתת דרך and חמס, the merciful compassionate God could do nothing but bring sudden universal destruction. This is not to occur again. All the different changes in the nature of the earth which hitherto God had suddenly effected, the changes of blossoming and withering, of growing and dying-off, the paradise-like wafting of the balmy air of Spring and the icy chill of the piercing congealing cold, all these henceforth shall be always in existence; sowing and reaping, cold and heat, summer and winter, day and night henceforth shall always be on earth at the same time, shall never cease to work, לא ישבתו. The earth is to have such a position and conformation in the universe that all times of the day and year, all temperatures and climates shall unceasingly be effective at the same time on earth, when here it is day, there it will be night, here Spring there Autumn, here Summer there Winter, here cold, there hot etc. as these differences in countries and differences in times, since then present themselves to our eyes in the manifold diversity of the word according to zones, countries, climates, etc.

If we dared to try and glimpse at the surface, out of the depth of the working of God’s government of the world, we would say: By the whole of these new arrangements for the world, a new means of the education of mankind was introduced. Since then Man is constantly dependent. It no longer suffices “to sow once to suffice for forty years”, and his means of living and his efforts are constantly faced with the possibility of failure.
Thereby, too, a greater difference in the individuals is called forth, different of course, in goodness, but also in the degree of badness.

This greater and quicker change in the conditions of life also shortened the duration of life, which very soon after the Flood sunk to its present level where it has since remained. One has only to think of the words of Caleb who Boasted to Joshua as being exceptional at eightyfive years old to be as hefty and strong as a man of forty (Jos. 14,11), and of the “seventy and at most eighty” of the Mosaic psalm. With this curtailment of the length of life a great barrier is imposed to the possibility of human evil gaining the upper hand permanently. Even the mightiest tyrant can not wield the sceptre much more than seventy years.

Finally, it is thereby even today still a fact that מפי עוללים ויונקים יסדת עוז, that God can establish His Kingdom on the mouths of children and babes. Not on the “cleverness” of the old, but on the undisturbed purity of mind and innocence of childhood and youth has He founded His Kingdom. With the birth of every child an angel enters the world. But as long as the bad ones reached their seven to eight hundred years, a better youth did not get a chance. In this new shortness of life God can make a generation die out quickly and a better one grow up in its place. Since then, mankind can ever look forward, and hope, and the future belong to youth. Only when Man returns to his God, and with this return the old conditions of peace on earth can also return, only then will this shortness of life also disappear, and with the true devotion and allegiance to God the original paradise-existence which Man was meant to enjoy can once again begin (Is. 115,17, 20 etc. seq.).

If we add to this diversity of individuals, the still greater diversity of nations, which the new arrangements for the earth effected, and also the natural hindrance to communication brought about by the division of the earth into continents and countries which will only be (is being I.L.) slowly overcome after thousands of years; if we think how, thereby, for thousands of years no degeneration spread universally all over the world, and how, just as in the quicker change of the generations in the individuals, so thereby the wider development of the history of nations was started in which new nations with fresh unvitiated powers always take the place of degenerated enervated ones: then, with this verse, everything is said by which God started a completely new phase in the development and education of mankind. “If” says God, “the endeavours of mankind are bad, and even from youth are directed to evil, I will not, — as I have done before — for Man’s own sake disturb the earth and bring about universal destruction, but will rather arrange that all the contrasts of the times of days and years henceforth shall all be present and working simultaneously on the earth”.

Here six seasons are mentioned, three winter and three summer seasons, זרע, the beginning of the winter, from 15th Tishri till 15th Kislev: קציר, the beginning of the summer, from 15th Nissan till 15th Sivan. קור, the end of winter, from 15th Shevat till 15th Nissan, חום, the end of summer, from 15th Ab till 15the Tishri. קיץ the midsummer from 15th Sivan till 15th Ab; חורף the midwinter, from 15th Kislev till 15th Shevat (Baba Mezia 106b).

Die Etymologie von זרע haben wir schon oben versucht (Kap.1, 11). — קצר ,קציר ist das verstärkte גזר, abschneiden. – קיץ von קוץ Überdruss haben, die Zeit, in welcher die Früchte der Säfte der Erde nicht nur nicht mehr bedürfen, sondern sie sogar verschmähen, indem sie abfallen. — חורף von חרף: im Piel: preisgeben, חרף נפשו, daher im Kal: der Zustand der vollständigen Unselbständigkeit der Erde, in welcher ,למות sie allen Einwirkungen der Elemente preisgegeben ist, und sich nichts selbständig entwickelt, die passive Zeit; somit Gegensatz zum קיץ, worin die Erzeugnisse ihre vollste Selbständigkeit erlangen.

V. 1—2. And now, on this earth, introduced with all these fresh conditions, ויברך, mankind receives God’s blessing a second time. The ויברך and the ויאמר are here, too, two separate sentences. In ברך it is endowed with the necessary powers for it, and then פרו and רבו given the mission of begetting children and bringing them up (see above Ch. 1,28). It is important that all this is repeated again here, for this blessing of mankind was after all given after the so-called fall of Man. But where God’s blessing is given, there no curse can lie. We miss two things here: רדו and כבשוה. Originally God placed Man over the world as its lord and master as was expressed by רדיה and כבוש. But רדיה and כבוש only establish the subordination of subordinates, are terms used even for the subjection of conquered provinces under their governors. Such a connection certainly does imply a subordination but gives no right to kill, the subordinates are left free to develop, although only in accordance with the will of the governor. All that is demanded is obedience. In the same way this was to have been the relation of Man to the world, he was to be superior to it, but attached to it and to take protective care of it, לעבדה ולשמרה. But this is to be no longer so. Man is now placed in the world to keep himself alive, and instead of the previous intimate relation between Man and the animal world it now says: All the animals of the world are to stand in fear and dread of you, etc.

מוראכם, from ירא .ירא is a mental process in which one pictures in one’s mind the greatness and the power even of the absent; hence also to keep back out of fear of this power, to keep out of its way. Thus כי יראו מפני הכשדים (Kings II. 25,26).

חתת ,חתכם is terror which breaks and cripples one’s strength and powers: חתתה קשתותם (Jer. 51,56). Whereas מורא makes the fearful one keep out of the way of the feared one, חתת keeps him back from attacking him. Consequently what it says here is: All other living creatures are timidly to keep out of Man’s way, always retreat before him and give him ever more room to spread, and shall lurk in their hiding-places out of fear of attacking him. The attachment between Man and animal is broken, animals fear Man, he is no longer their guiding master, Man has unlearnt to understand animals and they keep fearfully away from him. The ב in בכל אשר וגו׳ בכל דגי הים בידכם נתנו is difficult. One could take it to mean: in everything that treads the earth, yea even in the fish in the water, is the consciousness that it is given into your hand. But then one would have to insert ‘is the consciousness”. But ב also occurs in the sense of a part of something, thus לכו לחמו בלחמי ושתו בײן מסכתי (Prov. 9,5) “Come, eat of my bread, and drink of the wine I have mixed”. Here, too, it could have that meaning All living creatures are to have the fear and dread of man, thereby he gets space to live and security from attack, but that does not mean that all animals are given into his power, but rather “of all (ב I.L.) that tread the earth, and of all the fish of the sea (there are some) which are given into your hand”.

In any case, with this a difinite alteration in the position of mankind in relation to the world begins. If, in the previous verses, by the changed position and conditions of the earth, we are informed of the plan for paving the way for education, namely, that evil should not again increase as before, but that men should separate into greater diversity, and thereby the spread of evil both in individuals and nations would be paralysed, and by the shortened duration of life a quicker change-about in the character of the generations could be effected, and the Kingdom of God be founded on the entry of ever-fresh youth, and bring progress in the life of men and nations towards the ever-beckoning ultimate goal; if all this is no mere dream then we may tell ourselves that in the way that was started here until the very far distant future Man’s mission is no longer to master and perfect the physical and animal world in which he was set, but now he is only given the mission to ennoble, to perfect himself, to work himself up again to his true position and relation to God. This restitution of mankind to the standpoint which he should occupy, with the return of peace on earth, of longevity, of “the new heaven and the new earth” which the words of the Prophet pictures, will, according to the profound words of our sages — “אין בן דוד בא עד שיכלו כל הנשמות שבגוף״ not arrive until “materialism has been absorbed by everything spiritual, and become ennobled”. From our verse here until the last word of the last prophet, the whole contents of Scripture is nothing but a description of the return of mankind towards this future condition, and God’s contrivance to this goal. In the meantime, however, and until then, this standpoint is lost, the bond between mankind and the animal-world is torn, and mankind is primarily directed to work on itself and for itself.

V. 3. With the altered conditions of life, mankind also received fresh kind of food. It is not unlikely that the shortened duration of life, where everything that the earlier generations had lived through in seven to eight hundred years had to be concentrated into seventy to eighty years, the quicker development and the rapid changes, all stipulated for animal food. The differences in temperature, the changes of seasons and climates could equally have been not without influence in the permission now given for animal food. Thereby mankind becomes less dependent on the food that the earth grants it. Before the Flood, as has already been remarked, according to the teachings of our sages, and in accordance with geological assumptions, the temperature was much more constant and vegetation more luxurious, so that vegetarian food was always available in sufficient quantity and there was no necessity for a meat diet. The תורה demands no vegetarianism, it has no aversion to the eating of meat, it even makes it a duty on י״ט. If our physical condition were still the original one, probably the eating of meat would not be permitted to us, but now it is probably necessary. But as soon as we were allowed to eat animal food, dietary laws, מאכלות אסורות started. For even the later prohibitions of food in the Jewish laws are concerned solely with animal food, which, originally not allowed, was only permitted with restrictions. In the vegetable world no plant, as such, is forbidden to be eaten. The prohibition of ערלה ,חדש and כלאי כרם are rooted in quite other considerations. The first dietary law which applies far beyond Jewish circles and is binding on the whole of Noachian humanity, viz. אבר מן החי, is declared in the following verse.

V. 4. אך בשר בנפשו דמו לא תאכלו; the usual translation, taking דמו to be in apposition to בנפשו and accordingly running thus:— “nevertheless flesh in which its soul, namely its blood, still is, shall ye not eat”, is against the Halacha, as well as the wording and the cantillation. According to that, Noachides would be prohibited to eat meat with the blood in it, and this is by no means the case. Blood is altogether not forbidden to a בן נח not even דם מן החי, only אבר מן החי, and the blood in meat — which would be “flesh in which its blood still is” — דם איברים שלא פירש is not forbidden even for us. Also it does not say בשר אשר בו נפשו דמו but בנפשו דמו. Further, the cantillation on בשר is a completely separating one, and according to the wording and cantillation it can not read otherwise than “nevertheless, flesh, while its blood is in its soul, shalt thou not eat”, and clearly here by בנפשו דמו the living state of the animal is described. Accordingly the prohibition is given not to eat “flesh from the living animal”, i.e. אבר מן החי.

Still, we should have expected נפשו בדמו, not, as long as the blood is in the soul, but, as long as the soul is in the blood. But when the Word of God is speaking of blood and life it is extraordinary precise in its expressions. Even of animals, — and especially there where the animal material is absorbed into the human, and a human being is to supplement his body by the body of an animal — the Torah wants to avoid that materialistic point of view which looks on strength, mind, spirit, soul, life as nothing more than attributes of the material, modifications of it, as if really הדם הוא הנפש, the blood was really the soul and with the blood the soul was also destroyed, and not that the blood was merely the instrument and agent of the soul. The Word of God says something different. As long as the animal is alive the נפשו is not בדמו, the soul is not in the blood, but דמו בנפשו the blood is in the soul, the blood is encompassed and ruled by the soul, the soul is no attribute of the blood but vice versa.

We have already (I,20, II,19) recognised in נפש, related to נפץ, the summit, the highest degree of individualisation in the order of succession of the creation. נפש is the most independent amongst the created beings. Equally so we have recognised in דם (from דמה to be like something else, to be assimilated) the prototype of the whole body. The blood is the whole body in liquid state. It contains all the material matters of the body, and circulating throughout it, deposits in every part the appropriate material which that particular part requires to restore the used-up matter. So that the whole organism is involved in the blood, and it is true that every part of the body is formed by, and dependent on, the blood. But that to which the blood of the whole body is subservient is the נפש. As long as the blood is subservient to the נפש, the body is בשר, the messenger, the herald of the soul. For as long as the בשר is subservient to the soul through the medium of the blood, and it, the soul with this “red cord” connects everything and holds it together to itself, for so long, and for so long only, does the organism remain an individual with its own individuality. As soon as this bond of the soul is torn asunder the organism reverts to its elements. So that the דם is only the material agent of the soul. Through the דם the soul rules the body. It is to this relationship that the Word of God refers with the words בנפשו דמו “as long as its blood is held by its soul”. The individuality, whose herald, בשר, the nerves and muscles are, is the נפש; the agent between the two is the דם. Therefore it does not say: בשר ,דמו בנפשו but בשר בנפשו דמו for בשר and נפש belong together, and דם is only a means. The animal body is only allowed to be used for food when the blood is no longer under the control of the soul; the tissues of the animal body can become tissues of the human body for it is something entirely passive, inert, but the animal soul can never become, is never to become, the human soul. According to this, what the Torah says here is: no limb may be eaten if it comes from the animal while it was still under the sway of the animal soul. Not on account of the blood, for blood taken away from the animal is already dead, no longer represents the soul. But in אבר מן החי, in a limb taken off from the living animal, which, at the moment of its being separated, still stood completely in the service of the soul and ready to obey its dictates, there the idea of the invisible working of the animal mind or soul still remains, and that may not be taken over with it into a human being. Blood is only forbidden to people, to the nation, who are called to the higher priestly degree, who are to become a ממלכת כהנים. It is just the law which allows the בן נח the דם מן החי and forbids him אבר מן החי which would be taken as the significant warning to the Noachian world tto differentiate between the soul, — the mind of an animal — and the blood — the physical means of animal life. The one is allowed, the other forbidden.

In אחרי מזת (Levit. 17,11 et seq.) where blood is forbidden to Jews, the expressions of the prohibition vary four times, כי נפש כל בשר, הדם הוא בנפש יכפר, כי נפש הבשר בדם היא, כי נפש כל בשר דמו היא, דמו בנפשו הוא. When we consider these sentences we are first struck by the change of gender in them, דם is masculine, נפש feminine. So that in the sentence נפש כל בשר דמו היא, the subject is not דם and נפש the object, but the reverse, not the blood is the soul, but the soul is the blood, i.e. all that the blood does is really the soul doing. The former is the materialistic erroneous way of looking at life, the latter what the תורה teaches. The whole sentence says כי נפש כל בשר דמו בנפשו הוא ואמר לבני ישראל דם כל בשר לא תאכלו כי נפש כל בשר דמו היא כל אכליו יכרת i.e. because the blood, ruled by the soul (דמו נפשו I.L.) is the soul of all flesh (נפש כל בשר I.L.), therefore I say unto the Children of Israel ye shall not eat the blood of any flesh, for the soul of all flesh is its blood. The repeated term דמו בנפשו is a definite proof for the way we have taken the בנפשו דמו in our verse. Only the first verse כי נפש הבשר בדם היא seems to be against it. But there it is not wanting to tell us the reason why blood is forbidden for food, but why it is suitable to be used on the altar as representing the soul, and how the same reason underlies the prohibition to eat it. So that the -ב of the נפש בדם would be meant to be taken in the same sense as רוח החיה באופנים, the אופנים were moved by the spirit of the חיה, so here too, “for the soul is there, in the blood”, in every activity of the blood, there is really the activity of the soul, כי הדם הוא, for the blood is הדם, the prototype of the body (the word דם itself indeed really means the symbol, the metaphor, the representative), it is the blood by means of which all the working of the soul on the body is carried out, therefore הדם הוא בנפש יכפר, it effects כפרה, not on itself, but through the soul which it represents. Only in משנה תורה (Deut. 12,23 et seq.) where with repeated warnings the prohibition against eating blood is given, and it is pointed out how our own well-being and that of our children is connected with it, there it says — apparently materialistically — but in connection with the context of all the preceding verses surely metaphorically, actually כי הדם הוא הנפש, so that we and our children should realise with most definite certainty how eating blood would incorporate animal desires and tendencies into us.

V. 5. In human beings the relation of the soul to the blood is even more differentiated. At animals the blood was בנפש although something separate, still in an intimate organic connection with it, but the blood of Man is only לנפשו, something which belongs to it, is ordered by, subordinate to it, just as at the creation of animal and human souls we were told that, in the former case the soul arose from the earth together with the body, but in the latter came into the body from a source completely different from that of the earthly body, as a “breath of God”.

— אך from the root נכה, literally: I strike off, exclude. Whereas, in the previous verses, animals, together with their lives were given over into the hands of mankind, and the higher rank of Man already dictated the restriction of אבר מן חהי, inasmuch as בשר אדם and בשר בהמה may well be related and the one incorporated in the other, but נפש בהמה may never, in any way whatsoever, be transposed into נפש אדם, here, in this verse, this higher rank appears in a much more acute contrast. The animal’s body, and blood, and soul (life I.L.) are yours, are at your disposal, but your blood which belongs to your soul is Mine, is not yours. That, אדרש that I demand as My property, that is there at My disposal, and I demand an account for every drop of it. דרש is a term specially used for demanding the return of, and the accounting for something entrusted to other hands or which happens to be in somebody else’s possession. Thus עד דרוש אחיד אתו (Deut. 22,2), ודרשתי את צאני מידם (Ez. 34,10). When God declares אדרש concerning blood consigned to human souls, He claims the right to human blood as His possession and denies the right of dispoal of our own blood. It primarily forbids suicide.
מיד כל חיה. How God exercises His jurisdiction over the animal world lies beyond our ken. In the Jewish laws one aspect of this law occurs in שור הנסקל.

’ומיד האדם וגו. From animals, God demands a reckoning for דם האדם but from men, for נפש האדם. Men, as אדם, as being appointed by God as His representative, to protect and rule over the whole world, down to its lowest creature in accordance with the Divine Will, and as איש אחיו, to recognise in every human being his brother, equally coming from God, he, as אדם, should certainly beware of abusing that holiest and highest of all earthly creatures, a נפש אדם, and, as אחיו, from the consciousness of his own nature, should recognise and respect the spirit of God breathed into earthly form of his brother-men. The whole value of our being human rests on our associating, not bodies with bodies, but spirits with kindred spirits and recognising such spirit in every human being. The life, the נפש, of every human being is entrusted to the care of every other human being. And if, through the guilt of a human being, a human soul departs from this world earlier than God, who had placed it here, had willed it, then God misses it here and is דורש מידו; Every tiny minute of the earthly existence of even the most miserable human being is sacred to God, and whosoever shortens his own or anybody else’s life by one second is responsible to God.

V. 6. Behind the judicial punishments ordained by the Torah, there is neither the idea of deterrence nor of retaliation, the so-called jus. talionis, much as one thought one could deduce the former from וכל ישראל ישמעו ויראו (Deut. 13,11 et seq.) and the latter from עין תחת עין (Ex. 21,24). The fact that, in the laws of Jewish judicial punishments, no circumstantial evidence whatsoever, and no self-confession is accepted, that in cases of capital or corporal punishment, only such evidence may be admitted בעדים והתראה, of witnesses who not only saw the crime committed but who had warned the accused at the moment of the occurrence of the letter of the law and of the penalty it would incur, a state of affairs which in any premeditated crime could easily be avoided; the further fact that in most crimes against property, even for robbery, no punishment at all, not even a fine (קנס), but only restitution (תשלומין) was incurred, already these striking peculiarities of Jewish jurisprudence definitely refute any idea that legal punishments are based on the principle of deterrence. And just the וכל ישראל ישמעו ויראו to which the supposed principle is referred proves the very contrary. There are only four cases in which the Torah makes this remark in reference to the punishment, viz. עדים זוממין, בן סורר ומורה, זקן ממרה, מסית ומדיח “let all the people hear it and fear and do no more any such wickedness as this”. But just these four crimes and the punishment incurred appear as something quite abnormal. The nature of the deeds in themselves and the consideration of their immediate effect, does not seem to be so very terrible. The one, מסית, has only made the suggestion — unsucessfully — of seduction; the other עד זומם has only tried, but again has not succeeded, to bring about the death of the accused; the זקן ממרה may really actually be in the right, although he must submit to the decisions of the ב״ד הגדול, the Sanhedrin, made in accordance with the opinions of the majority of its members; the בן סורר ומורה quite clearly only gets the capital punishment על שם סופו. Actually all four receive the death penalty על שם סופן out of consideration of the extremely pernicious results which could ensure from such apparently disproportionately small sins. Regarding them the Torah accordingly finds it important that the whole nation should get to know that on account of one of these sins somebody has paid the death penalty. Deterrence is not the reason for the punishment itself but for its being carried out in public or for making it publicly known (which is just the difference between the opinions of ר׳ עקיבא and ר׳ יהודה (Sanhedrin 89a). The fact that the publicity or the publication of the carrying out of the death sentence is demanded only for these four cases proves that otherwise, in general, deterrence is not the motive for punishments. (Sanhedrin 89a). — Just as little is the jus talionis (retaliation I.L.) to be deduced from the “eye for an eye” etc. of the Jewish Law. Tradition teaches that thereby only a calculated amount of money is imposed, and at the same time points out how the taking of this legal canon literally in the sense of “an eye for an eye” would be morally impossible for any idea of equity (e.g. if a one-eyed man were to put out the eye of an ordinary two-eyed man, etc. I.L.). But even from the text itself it is evident that by an eye for an eye only the exact reckoning in money of the amount of indemnification to be paid is meant. Just before it says in v. 24 of Ch. XXI in Exodus, “an eye for an eye etc.”, in v. 19 it has already said that שבתו יתן ורפא ירפא, that compensation in money is to be paid for inflicting wounds. In “an eye for an eye” what is expressed is rather the great principle which underlies the whole of Jewish penal laws viz. A man can only expect and demand such rights as he is ready to grant to others. He loses the right to demand his rights as soon as he does not respect the rights of others. He regains it, when, restitution or by payments — directly or by acknowledgment, he restores the principle he had offended. To the intelligent, all punishments are כפרה, atonement, “not atonement of the offended principle” but atonement, rehabilitation of himself. The future life of even the criminal who suffers capital punishment is taken to extend beyond the short span of his earthly existence. If he has paid for the damage he has done to the principle of Law by the loss of his existence here, he goes to meet a new existence with regained purity. — כי בצלם אלקים צשה את האדם, in this sentence of the higher God-like nature of human beings the motive for the whole group of these laws may well be given, for the handing over of the animal world for food for men, for the prohibition of assimilating the animal soul in the human body, — אבר מן החי — as well as human mortal life belonging to God and His intervention against any attack on it.

V. 7. שרצו בארץ ורבו בה — a highly significant addition to the mission of development given here to the Noachian world with which this whole new constitution of humanity concludes. Its meaning is given by רשב״ל in ב״ר by the explanation ברית נחלק לאוירות, that God gave a special covenant, a special dispensation, to the different climates and countries. שרץ, as already shown, is the name given to the lowest stage of life, according to the essential sign of its existence, movement, ישרצו המים. Inasmuch as here the procreation and propagation of the human race have this designation added, the term would represent a swarm of the most manifold different kinds of men. It would accordingly be a description of a diversity and infinite variety of human races, and moreover בארץ, on the earth, and by the earth, under the influences of the differences of the various lands. And not only שרצו בארץ but also רבו — the whole physical, moral and intellectual education — equally בה, under the same influences. That, which above, in the sentence ’עוד כל ימי הארץ וגו, could only be presumed, is here definitely stated. Noachian mankind is given the mission to spread over the whole world, and under the most diverse conditions and influences of climate and physical nature of the countries, to become Men and develop the one common real character of Man; a diversity and a multiplicity which appeared to us in the above connection as God’s new plan for the education of mankind, to avoid the necessity for any fresh total catastrophe. The diversity is to balance the deficiency and so pave the way to progress to the goal. Hence ברית נחלק לאוירות, say our sages on this sentence ברוך שנתן חן המקום בעיני יושביו. “God has provided the most differing zones and climates with a special dispensation”, (or perhaps more literally: The general covenant of God with mankind is spread over the most diverse districts) — “Blessed be God, Who has given every country an attraction to its inhabitants”, and they point out how every race feels at ease in its homeland even under the most inhospitable circumstances, and the most unfriendly districts affect their sons with homesickness when they are away from them, and in strange lands disturbs their spiritual development. Man, who thinks he is master of the land is, in many ways, in his innermost self, in his mind, feelings, understanding and speech, mastered by his native land, and this variety of countries has a purpose. Everywhere a man can conduct himself as a human being, everywhere be happy, everywhere pure human qualities can be developed in people. Only no man may judge others by his own standards. That is why, at the end of this new conditioning of the world and mankind it says: “diversify yourselves on the earth and multiply yourselves on it, by it, in it, with it etc.”

V. 8. What God had said above as His decision אל לבו, here He assures mankind as a ברית to Man and his world, as an unalterable absolute provision, and is revealed as the motive for the natural order of things which from now onwards is to prevail.

V. 12. Just as here God did not satisfy Himself with merely proclaiming His Word, but dedicated a memorial to His proclamation, so, in the whole course of the history of the Divine government for the well-being of mankind and Israel, He appointed אותות, signs, reminders for the great Truths and principles He gave them, which were to serve to keep these teachings ever fresh and present in the minds of men; thus תפלין ,שבת ,מילה etc. — לדרת עולם doubly חסר, for times which appear intensively and extensively deficient, which, if left to themselves would go to ruin. If, in such times, one is overcome by despair for the future, or doubts the justice of God in allowing such a state to continue, the rainbow in the clouds is to remind us that over and beyond even such times God has given mankind His covenant, and even through such times His management will lead mankind to its ultimate goal.

V. 13. את קשתי נתתי בענן. It is by no means necessary to assume that hitherto there had been no rainbow and to place it in connection with the atmospheric changes which occurred after the Flood. Just as God showed Abraham the starry heavens and said: כה יהיה זרעך, as He showed Moses and Aaron the new moon, and with the words החדש הזה לכם consecrated this monthly phenomenon — which, of course, had been in existence since the beginning of the world — to be a sign of physical and moral rejuvenation for Israel; as existing seasons and dates became memorials for historical and instructive remembrance for Israel, so the rainbow can also have been a well-known phenomenon in the sky, and now became designated by God to be a sign of His covenant with Man and the world. The נתתי can therefore quite literally be: My bow, I have long ago placed it in the clouds, henceforth it shall serve as a sign of the covenant between Me and you.

V. 15. The sign and its meaning is told us, about that there can be no doubt. It only remains to consider the connection between the sign and its signification. This has been attempted in various ways. The sign is a reversed weapon, a bow with the string towards the earth, so that it would shoot away from the earth, accordingly a sign of peace, no more arrows from heaven. — Its appearance is that of an arc joining the earth to heaven, accordingly a bond between heaven and earth. The phenomenon itself is woven from light and water. In the midst of overcast threatening clouds it announces the presence of light, is accordingly a reminder that in the midst of God’s threatened wrath His preserving grace is still there. — But perhaps the sight of the colours of the rainbow is in closer relation than all these ideas. By it our attention would repeatedly be directed to the fact that, in spite of all differences in the degree of human development, God would never again decree the downfall of the whole human race, but that its future education to its godly purpose was to be founded just on these differences and varieties of humanity. For is the rainbow anything else but the one pure complete ray of light, broken up into seven degrees of seven colours, from the red rays nearest to the light to the violet, most distant from the light, losing itself into the darkness; and from the one to the other are they not all rays of light, and combined all together, do they not form the one complete pure white ray? Could not this perhaps be meant to say: the whole manifold variety of all living creatures from the “most alive” Adam, the אדם “red one”, “Man”, nearest to the godly, down to the lowest, humblest form of life in the humblest worm, all נפש חיה בכל בשר, and above all, the whole variety of shades in which henceforth the purely “human” would show itself in the races of mankind, from the bright highly intellectual people down to those in whom, to the human eye, the spiritual element hardly glimmers, God unites them all together in one common bond of peace, all fragments of one life, all refracted rays of the one spirit of God, even the lowest, darkest, most distant one, still a son of the light? Thus, later on, our sages describe the different spiritual and moral degrees of the צדיקים in the metaphor of nuances of light, from the bright, illuminating rays of the sun to the gleam of the lamp in the Temple, all is light, only according to the difference of the material it appears different, שבע כתות של צדיקים וכו׳ ופניהם דומות לחמה, ללבנה, לרקיע, לברקים, לכוכבים, לשושנים ולמנורות בית המקדש.

V. 18. We have already referred above to the significance of the fact that Shem, Ham and Japhet belonged to those who were saved in the ark, we saw how important it was that, already before the Flood they had their different characters, and in spite of this difference were all three considered to be worthy of being saved with Noah. So that still today, in the different types of humanity that we find, some races even bordering on absolute degeneration, this difference can be no hindrance to their being “human”, or to their becoming pure human beings. All were יוצאי התבה, all are צלם אלקים, none can say to the other: “you are less of a human being than I am, you really do not belong to the conception of a “man”. It is because of its importance that this thought is again repeated at the beginning of this chapter.

וחם הוא אבי כנען. Just, as regarding that part of the Torah which deals with laws and commandments we have constantly to bear in mind that the fact that the תשב״פ preceded the תשב״כ; that the whole Torah with the full explanation had been verbally taught to the people before they were entrusted with the written Torah as notes with which to refresh their memories, so that everywhere at these written notes the oral teaching is taken as being known and is taken into consideration; in the same way, we must remind ourselves, at the historical part, that, for instance, what is recorded here was not written down at the time of Noah, but at a time when the Canaanite people were quite well-known to Israel. The Canaanites had already sunk to the highest degree of moral degeneration, the “land would no longer tolerate its inhabitants” and Israel was to inherit the land in their place. For, even if the covenant established above did exclude the universal destruction of mankind, it by no means granted a licence for the moral degeneration of any nation. Rather, nation after nation disappeared from the stage of history when “their measure was full”, and other fresher ones took their place. But at the head of such degeneration stood Canaan, and they were well known to Israel to whom this history was given. Now here it is told, וחם, that one of the roots which had been saved for planting the future world was the father of this degenerate nation. This degenerate nation, which the earth would no longer tolerate had its ancestor in Ham. It was highly instructive for Israel, and is so for us, to learn from God’s Mouth, in what small, slight transgressions on the part of the ancestor the germ of the later degeneration of the nation is to be found.

V. 19. Once again repeated: All three: sons of one father, and indeed of a father who was ’צדיק תמים וגו, and still all three so very different! “Out of these three individualised types the whole world spread”, (נפץ, from which מפץ the hammer is derived, that which breaks into little pieces). All the later differences which developed are to be traced back to these fundamental types.

(20-21) כרם, vielleicht verwandt mit גרם, Stufe, גרם המעלות, von den Reihen der Reben sich terrassenförmig erheben. — יין rad. יין möglich (wie קין mit :übervorteilt werden, im Hiphil: übervorteilen, auch :ינה verwandt ינה mit (קנה mit Worten wehe tun. Zunächst also: sich im Verkehr mehr als ihm zukommt geben lassen, jemandem das Seinige ablisten, abpressen. Wir rauben nicht, sondern: setzen den Andern in die Lage, daß er uns von dem Seinigen das hergebe, was er eigentlich behalten sollte. Es ist nun sehr möglich, daß der Wein deshalb יין heißt, weil er das der Beere abgepresste Eigentum ist. Vergleiche הירוש, das doch unbestritten von ירש: Jemanden aus seinem Besitze drängen, stammt. Zuerst ist der Saft תירוש, einfach aus der Beere gepresst. Wird dies gewaltsam Genommene nun noch allerhand Misshandlungen, Kränkungen und Trübungen ausgesetzt, damit es uns seine innerste Kraft zum Genuss herauskehre, so ist dies: שכר — יין verwandt mit שיר .שגר ,שקר ,שיר ist der begeisterte Ausdruck des geistig Geschauten, des Wahren, aber nicht, oder noch nicht in konkreter Wirklichkeit Vorhandenen. das שיר ;singt das unsichtbare Göttliche in den Ereignissen der Gegenwart שירה in der Gegenwart noch nicht sichtbare Künftige. Beides spricht das für das sinnliche Auge nicht Vorhandene aus, obgleich es wahr ist, wahrer und wirklicher vielleicht als das, was das sinnliche Auge für wahr und wirklich erkennt. — שכר: der Rausch, der Zustand, in welchem die Phantasie sich eine Wirklichkeit bildet, der in Wahrheit nichts entspricht. שקר: die vollendete Lüge, die keinen Rausch hat, sondern mit Bewusstsein das Falsche für das Wahre ausgibt. — Was alle drei geistig sind, ein Produzieren von Innen heraus, das ist שגר leiblich: die tierische Geburt.

V. 21. גלה .ויתגל to uncover, and at the same time, to emigrate, and indeed to go unwillingly into exile. This strange relationship could confirm what we said above about עיר and כפר .כפר: village, because it protects and covers; עיר, city because it grants people in a still closer relationship like עור skin, the organic surrounding for their spiritual development. Whereas the village merely gives protection, but the real life is lived outside it, the city embraces the whole life, contains its inhabitants like their skin. He who has to emigrate and become homeless, he is stripped, loses protection and shelter, loses the place where he has rights and can demand all conditions that further his progress; he goes naked “without his skin” into foreign lands. In this word — גלה — lies the whole fervour and the feeling of pain which homeland is to the Jew. Not for naught is sympathy so often and so warmly recommended towards the גר — the alien. Related to גלה is גלח, forcibly to bare, to shave, to remove the protection of the skin, the hair, גלע equally means to uncover, to reveal. — אהל, tent, from הלל with the prefixed א (cf. אבד ,אבל etc.) הלל to radiate, to let forces flow out from one point in all directions. When these benefit primarily, only the centre point, then an אהל is formed, a sphere within which an individual collects all his forces about him, really the domain of his forces, his belongings. Here, we could be remainded the more of this meaning as it says בתוך אהלה not באהלה .באהלה in the tent generally, בתוך אהלה in the middle of, in the innermost part of the tent.

There is an אתנח on האדמה; moreover it does not say איש אדמה which perhaps could have meant a husbandman, (like איש שדה, a sportsman), though the term does not occur elsewhere, but איש האדמה. So that it can not mean: Noah, the husbandman planted the first vine-yard. But rather we have two sentences here: ויחל נח איש האדמה and ויטע כרם. If we picture to ourselves how Noah had lived through the downfall of the earth and of the whole of human beings, and the world now lay before him deserted and desolate, we can understand that it says: he was the man and master of the earth, it was all entrusted to him; hence: after destruction had raged for so long “Noah began to be איש האדמה״ and to occupy himself as such, and he even succeeded in planting earth’s noblest growth once again in the old way. Then he saw that the old blessing of fertility of the earth had not been taken away. The proof was given to him by the regained first grape, the regained first cup of wine! Can we be surprised that the first wine gained from the hard-tried earth filled him with ecstasy, and can we not believe that in such a state of ecstasy, where one is already half drunk with the thoughts of joy in one’s mind, that it does not take much to become intoxicated with actual drink? — There is also an אתנח on וישכר. He had not drunk the wine בתוך אהל in the innermost part of his tent: ויתגל בתוך אהלה, when he felt that the wine was going to his head, he took refuge in the innermost part of the tent, where he could hope nobody would see him. More, our sages remark that it says אהלה, apparently the womens’ tent, where he certainly could hope to be kept away from being seen by his sons, who were not to see him in the condition he was in.

V. 22. His other sons remained respectfully, בחוץ, outside. But Ham went inside. The going in, itself, to look for his father there where he could expect not to be seen “to see his father also once drunk” already stamps Ham as a Canaanite. And then, to make matters worse, וירא, — חם אבי כנען, who, after all, himself was already a father, and so by the thought of the relation of his son towards him ought to have been doubly filled with the right feelings of a son towards his own father — ערות אביו, and then ויגד! Not merely ויאמר but related in detail, painted the scene in words, made a whole story of it, enjoyed the event he had witnessed, and believed he had something delectable to relate to his brothers!

We have alerady indicated how the אבי כנען had reference for Israel to the degenerate nation of their time. Thus Israel, placed between two nations descended from Ham (מצרים was also one of Ham’s sons Ch. 6. I.L.), having social degeneration in Egypt and moral degeneration in Canaan before their eyes, was to realise at the grave of both these nations the slight beginning which started the degeneration — and this beginning was the behaviour of Ham towards his father!

The whole world of humanity is built on the relation of children to their parents. Of course parents are there for their children; the mother אם, the condition for their existence, the father אב (from אבה), the one whose life should be given up to the well-being of his children. But both are conditioned on כבוד ומורא אב ואם, on honouring and reverencing father and mother. Not for naught does this Mitzva stand as the key-stone of the first tablet of the Law. As long as children see in their parents the depository of God’s mission, do not regard the bodily material, but the spiritual being in them, out of whose hands they receive their spiritual being, for so long mankind flourishes like a tree. But, if, on the other hand, this factor is quite absent from the minds of the children, if there is a possibility that a child can find pleasure in that part of its parents’ nature that is sexual, if reverence of the child for its parents is absent, then the stem is cut through which, out of the past should make the future spring forth ever nobler. Then, the younger generation considers itself only as the יורש of the older, and, as the more vigorous, supplants the older decrepit generation and steps into its shoes. ירש to dispossess someone, related to גרש and even to כרש the great world-conqueror). In Israel the relation is to be of one generation following the other, נחלה, “a stream”, a flow; there, the older generation hands over its strength and powers, its spiritual and material treasures, to the younger. Elsewhere each fresh generation wants to start afresh, does not want to learn anything from the past, each generation is a new and different aspect of life on earth, and what the future will be remains to be seen. There the source of strength and power comes from above, the stream flows, the spiritual mission is handed over from the older, through the middle, to the younger generation (see Yebamoth 62a, נחלח only applies to ירושה ;ישראל to בן נח). So that כבוד אב ואם is the foundation for all development of mankind. So that when Israel had been led to the border of the land whose inhabitants were to be cleared out for Israel to build up a pure mode of life, degeneration and its result were shown to them, and they were told: — “See, this degeneration had its beginning in the first disrespect with which the ancestor of this nation behaved towards his father!”

Moreover וירא את ערות אביו need not be meant in a literal sense. Apart from the fact that ערוה occurs as an expression for a general weakness, a weak failing, a shameful condition, and ראה is also used in such a connection, e.g. לראות את ערות הארץ (Gen. 42,9) “the nakedness”, to spy out the weaknesses of the land are ye come, we find the word “nakedness” used quite specially as a description of the degrading condition to which drunkenness lowers men; הוי it says in Hab. 2,15 משקה רעהו מספח חמתך ואף שכר למען הביט על מעוריהם “Woe unto him that giveth his neighbour drink, poureth thy venon thereto, and maketh him drunken that thou mayest look on their nakedness”. To that can be added that גלה (here ויתגל) also occurs not meaning literally baring but as an expression of lowering oneself, of letting oneself go. Thus Michal says to David (Sam.II. 6,20) מה נכבד היום מלך ישראל אשר נגלה היום לעיני אמהות עבדיו כהגלות נגלות אחד הריקים “How glorious hath the King of Israel honoured himself today, who ‘uncovered himself’ today in the eyes of handmaids of his servants as one of the good-for-nothings uncovereth himself”. So that Noah could merely have been lying in his tent in a low condition of drunkenness, without necessarily any bodily nakedness exposed.

V. 23. Shem acted first, Japheth joined him, Ham did not understand, even when he saw what his brothers were doing. In these three stages the brothers showed their characters. — שכם, shoulder, also the root of השכם, to raise oneself from sleep, to get up. When a person who is lying down decides to get up, he raises his shoulders first of all.

אחרנית. Eigentümlich heißt אחר sowohl ein Anderer, als auch אחר: hinten und אחרית: das Ende. Vielleicht ist אחר ebenso wie אכל usw. von חר mit vorgesetztem א׳ gebildet. ארר ,ערר ,חרר sprechen alle die Verneinung einer vorhandenen Kraft usw. aus: חרר, Säfte ausdorren, ערר, vereinsamen, ארר: vollste Negierung der Möglichkeit, sich weiter zu entwickeln. Auch חרה: glühen und חרה ל־ einem Andern gegenüberstehen, Verdruss machen, eigentlich: die betreffende Sache stellt das dar, was der Andere nicht haben will, verwirklicht das ihm zuwider Seiende. Liegt so in חר die Verneinung, so ist אחר: das, was eben durch diese Verneinung charakterisiert wird. אחר: jeder Gegenstand, der das ist, was der andere nicht ist. Es ist immer ein, wenn auch relativer, Gegensatz, selbst wenn der andere demselben Begriff angehört, nur ein anderes Exemplar derselben Gattung ist. Daher auch räumlicher und zeitlicher Gegensatz: אָחר, räumlich, die dem פנים entgegengesetzte Seite. אחר, zeitlich, derjenige Moment, der dann eintritt, wenn ein anderer zu Ende ist. Während פנים, räumlich, die Vorderseite und אחר die Rückseite ist, heißt (der Vermutung entgegengesetzt) לפנים die Vergangenheit; denn אחרית, die Zukunft, ist dasjenige, was אחר הפנים was eintritt, wenn das Vorhergehende gewesen ist. אחרית Ende, Ziel, Gegensatz von ראשית, ist dasjenige, was im ראשית noch nicht vorhanden war, das immer erst zuletzt kommt, während קץ ,קצה nur einfach Grenze und daher ebenso Anfang als Ende bedeutet. אחרית ist sehr oft der gerade Gegensatz von Anfang: והיה ראשיתך מצער ואחריתך ישגה מאור (Job 8, 7). Daher: אחרית לאיש שלום (Psalm 37, 37). Dem איש שלום ist anfangs viel versagt, aber er findet ein אחרית, er hat eine Zukunft; der רשע hingegen hat nur ein קץ.

V. 24. קוץ and יקץ to wake up, just as קוץ in קיץ denotes the time of the year when the fruit has sucked up “enough”, similarly to קוץ of people with reference to sleep. In sleep we lie on the breast of sleep which nourishes us, we wake up when we have suckled to satiety.

בנו הקטן, we are not justified in seeing in this term anything other than “his youngest son” and have to take Ham as being the youngest of the sons, although in the list of the sons he appears to be the second one. Japheth too is called the eldest, יפת הגדול in Ch. 10,21, although he is named last. So that according to age the order would be Japheth, Shem, Ham. Naming them Shem, Ham and Japheth is understandable when we consider that all these historical disclosures are primarily given for Israel. But for Israel, Shem, as their own ancestor, is the most important. Next to him would be Ham, whose descendants, Egypt and Canaan, formed the nations most in contrast to them, in overcoming whom Israel continuously found their historical development. With the nations descended from Japheth, Israel only came into contact much later. Apart from this Shem and Ham are contrasts in the history of nations and Japheth the bridge between them. But that, in what follows, Noah speaks of Canaan and not of Ham need not seem strange to us. Ham in as little cursed as Shem is blessed. Curses and blessings are given, not to Ham and Shem personally but to what they become to mankind through their descendants, not ברוך שם but ברוך אלקי שם. But it is deeply affecting that Noah pronounces the curse for Ham in his child, and this expresses the momentous warning: He who does not wish to be punished in his children must honour his own parents. If Ham does not want to be punished in the future of Canaan, let him not sin against Noah. — The sin which children commit against parents punishes itself by the way their children will treat them. And just as in private families, this law applies to the development of whole generations of mankind. Only where the younger generation stands with respect on the grave of the by-gone one, draws a cloak over its lapses but takes to itself all that it had of nobility, truth and greatness as a valuable inheritance on which to build further its own life, is the development of the generations a tree that progressively develops in new blossoms. But as soon as the younger generation gloats over the “nakedness” of the fathers, and because of their human frailties mocks at their great spiritual traditions; as soon as the future jeeringly tears asunder the bond with the past, their own future is also a dream, and just as they jeer at the memories of their forefathers so will their grandchildren jeer at them — Ham is always the father of Canaan.

V. 25.—26.—27. That which is said in these verses contains perhaps the deepest and farthest reaching prophesy which ever a human eye has been allowed to see of the future, and which God has allowed to be spoken by human lips. The whole history of mankind, the beginning the end and the middle lies in these three verses.

Above we have already thought we could recognize in the names of the sons of Noah the essential nuances which characterise the nations which descend from them, according to whether spirit, sensuality or feelings predominate in their national character. Here they stand in their double significance, as individuals and as the founders of the nations of the future.

V. 25. When Noah woke up and got to know of Ham’s behaviour, his first thought was:— the principle that showed itself here in Ham can, and may, and will — (for it is no means necessary that ארור always expresses a wish in the ordinary sense of a “curse”, but rather, and especially here, a declaration) — never be the ruling one.
