Raw “hot” sensuality, which has no control over itself, which has lost all reserve and all respect for anything spiritually high is unfit for ruling, yea, for freedom, it in itself is unfruitful, is ארור without progress or blessing, it bears its ruin in itself. — עבד עבדים not the lowest slave, but, just as אלקי האלקים does not mean the highest God, but the God of the gods, so also עבד עבדים, the others too are עבדים, but Canaan will be עבד עבדים. Inasmuch as it is repeated again in the next verse that Canaan will have the fate of being an עבד, there must undoubtedly be some connection between the Canaan-character and the עבד fate. And, as a matter of fact, as ארור lies in Canaan, so that the future belongs only to the pure and ennobled, but not to the coarse, unrefined, so also in social life, in the social and national life, in the relation of man to man and nation to nation, freedom is only achieved and retained by those who can master and control themselves. Sensuality, uncontrolled licentiousness, is the bait by which one is led by strings into slavery. He who at all times is master of himself, who can easily control giving satisfaction to the urges of his senses, he cannot be bribed or enticed, for him gold can not become golden chains; he can go under, die — but he can not become enslaved. Thus for men, thus for nations.

V. 26. ויאמר. This is a second, a fresh, further pronouncement, hence ויאמר repeated. — אלקי שם is meant here in the same sense as we everywhere in the Torah find the expression אלקי אברהם. This never means the supposedly particular God of Abraham — as people like to think the Jewish conception of God is of One Who is peculiar to them — but this designation is common because, (a) God is specially revealed in the history and guidance of Abraham, Isaac, Jacob, and Israel and (b) because they recognised Him and proclaimed Him. This designation is extremely necessary because by the name “God”, so many and such different conceptions are understood, from the raw and pantheisitic fetishism to the speculative idea which relegates the existence of God to an empty abstraction. So that there is no other means of a description of the true and actual God differentiating from the empty masks of erroneous delusion and imaginative speculation than to call it the “God of Abraham Isaac and Jacob”, i.e. the God as they recognised and taught Him. And it is in this sense that here He is called אלקי שם. Abraham’s knowledge of God, even Jacob’s was matured in the school of Shem, and long before Abraham had been chosen as the instrument for the proclamation of God to the world, Shem had known Him. אלקי שם means the God Whom Shem recognised, honoured and Whose priest Shem is. Hence it says:— in contrast to the ארור of Canaan is the ’ברוך וגו, the recognition of the God Whom Shem teaches will gain an ever greater circle, will spread, progress until finally it will become that principle to which all the world will subscribe. While Ham represents the most ignoble, unvarnished audacious sensuality, Shem teaches of a God Who not only once upon a time served as the Original Force Which called heaven and earth into being but Who still is קונה the heaven and earth, still rules everything, so that every fibre of our being and every impulse of our will belongs to Him; accordingly, the very opposite principle to that of Ham. To the ויהי כנען עבד למו we will come later. Here we will only remark that the plural למו (the poetic expression for להם I.L.) proves that here Shem and correspondingly Canaan also are not looked on personally as individuals but as the future nations descended from them.

V. 27. ’יפת וגו, usually taken to mean: God will extend, spread abroad, Japheth, in the meaning of the Chaldean פתה. But we believe, as a general principle of explanation of the meaning of words, that one is only justified in taking the meaning of a word from another language, even though the two languages are closely related, when there is no other explanation for it to be found in its use in its own language. But the root פתה is quite well-known in the Hebrew language, and there is no question at all as to its meaning. פתה designates feelings being open to all external impressions and influences. Hence פתי, one who is easily talked over and easily deceived. Also פתאום, that to which our mind is quite open i.e. unprepared, unexpected. Equally so, פתה .פתע is related to פדע ,פדה ,פתח all meaning open. יַפתּ is a Hiphil form and hence means: to open minds. “God will open the mind, the feelings of Japheth”. Will make him responsive to feelings.

Thus we have placed before us the representatives of the three main tendencies which characterise people and nations. שם, having the names and conception of things and conditions, represents the mind, the spirit; contrasted to him המם ,חמם) חם) the highest power of glowing hot sensuality. Whereas in שם the mind predominates, which looks at things as much as possible objectively, which requires tranquility, which may know nothing of המם and certainly not of חמם, in חם the body predominates, and mind and spirit are reduced to a minimum. יפת represents that which lies in the middle, that centre point in which mind and sensuality meet, this is feelings, sentiment. Spirit, sensuality and sentiment constitute the inner man, and these three powers predominate characteristically in nations. Not that there are completely one-sided nations who have either only mind, only sentiment, etc. But just as in individuals all three are present, but nevertheless everybody has one of them which marks his personality, so is it with nations. For us who do not stand, as Noah did, at the very beginning of history, but can look back on four thousand years of history, it is easy to see the working of these different forces in nations in the development of world-history.

The greatest ado in the world has been made by חם, that sensuality, worldliness, which harnesses all that belongs to spirit and mind to their chariots of fame, and only allows intellect to be used or valued as far as it serves as a means of furthering the material side of life, nations that conquer, plunder and enjoy. Nations pass across the stage who represent hardly anything but raw force, sensuality and bestiality.

But nations also appear which use their forces in the service of beauty who characterise themselves in nurturing art, aesthetic beauty. They are conscious of some higher ideal up to which mankind is to work itself out of its crudeness. This tendency teaches people to cloak raw sensuality in the garb of respectability and graciousness. Through grace and beauty they foster a taste for more spiritual activities, music, poetry, art. All those nations who cherish that which appeals to feelings represent the יפת-character.

But the education of raw unrefined humanity to the sense of beauty is not the highest. Wavering, unsettled is the culture which only gives Man the satisfying of his own higher standards as the criterion of the activities of his life, but gives him no ideal external to himself, glowing in its own lights, as a beacon, a goal and a criterion. Only that which can elevate the mind to a knowledge of, and the feelings to a recognition of what is good and true in itself, leads a man to the height of what he is meant to be. Nations who have made their contribution by cultivating the spiritual amongst mankind to a recognition of the Truth have worked in the שם-character for the happiness and well-being of humanity.

When we look around in historical facts we can say: the stem of Japheth reached its fullest blossoming in יון, the Greeks: that of Shem in עבר the Hebrews, Israel, who bore and bear the ’שם ה as their God through the world of nations. Right to the present day it is only these two races, the descendants of Japheth and Shem, the Greeks and the Jews who have become the real educators and teachers of humanity. For all the spiritual treasures which the world has acquired these two have to be thanked, and everything, which, even today, works at the culture and education of mankind connects up with that which Japheth and Shem brought to the world. The spiritual gifts of the Romans too was only a gift of the Hellenes. Japheth has ennobled the world aesthetically. Shem has enlightened it spiritually and morally, Hellenism and Judaism have become the great active forces in the educational work on mankind, and the rest of the world has been merely the passive material on which they worked. — In this sense Noah’s enlightened eye sees three things:

He sees ארור כנען! sees that coarseness and ruthless glowing sensuality does not bear the seed of the future blossoming of mankind within it; sees that the nations who give themselves up to sensuality and in whose character, the lower nature of man remains the prevailing trait, instead of becoming free, independent and mighty sink down to עבדים, to slaves. More, he sees centuries in which the conception of human beings having the right to freedom is quite lost. Canaan is עבד עבדים but the others are also עבדים. Only nations who are themselves enslaved have enslaved others. He who sets out to be a world-conqueror, to force other nations to obey his will, must first have abased his own people to act slavishly as the blind instruments of his lust for power and mastery. From Ham’s descendants, tyrants, mighty despots and “hunters of men” went forth. Not freedom, slavery is begotten by passion. Freedom, חרות, only lives in Law, only blossoms there, where untouchably above all, a law of morals rules. He remains free who learns to obey the law of morals. Sensuous nations are the breeding places of slavery, חם begets עבדים and where sensuality is at its height, as in כנען, they sink to עבד עבדים.

But his vision rises, he sees, in contrast, ברוך ה׳ אלקי שם sees the salvation of mankind proceeding from another stem. Ham, too, has gods, but they are gods of raw force, powers that show their “godliness” only in crushing violence, gods before whom man can only tremble, and to whom the mighty ones on earth build altars so that the people can honour the reflection of these gods in these powerful ones themselves, and sink to the dust as slaves before them as before their gods. Then Shem steps into the sphere of mankind with ’שם ה with the Name ’ה, a conception of a God before whom the enslaving gods disappear, a God Who makes men free, Who raises them up to Himself in equal value above the dreaded gods of Nature, Who with the living breath of God within him gives every man the consciousness of his own unloseable value and worth as a human being, Who, in his benevolence and educating Love is near to every man, Who calls every one to His service, makes him free in His service, ennobles him and makes him happy in His service. — And he sees the teaching of this God as ברוך, sees it blessed, sees it entering the ranks of the nations, not armed with the sword or violence nor with the enticing attractions of licence; sees it gaining ever more ground, ever more blossoming, ever more power, and finally gaining the ultimate victory of mastery of the whole world. He wishes — it does not say והיה nor יהיה, but ויהי, the usual expression for a wish or prayer — that Canaan should be the עבד of Shem. He sees in that a salvation for Ham, that the principle which is so opposed to him may prevail over him, and wishes, as in any case Canaan will be an עבד, that he might be Shem’s עבד, and so, even כנען, the highest degree of the most degenerate licentiousness, through the influence of Shem would lay himself at God’s Feet and in this submission be won over to a godly life.

But he sees that this goal will not be achieved at once. Between Ham and Shem there is Japheth. A Ham is not immediately responsive to the teaching of the God of Shem. Out of the raw uncultured man, a cultured person has first to be made. The demand which the God of Shem makes is no small one, it demands the complete devotion and submission of the whole person to God. A person must first acquire “the taste” of something higher than he is in his raw nature, even if this something higher is at first also something that appeals to his senses. The savage who paints himself, makes a change in his outward appearance, is thereby making the first beginning of improving himself, the threshold of culture, which ends in people subordinating themselves in their external appearance, their surroundings their behaviour, to the dictates of decorum, decency, good manners and beauty. This culture of beauty and grace, the καλοκᾀγαθόν of “Japheth” schooling is a precursor of the Semitic mission, a preparatory school for teaching people to reach the loftier concept of life, the still greater beauty which lies in a harmonious joining all the aspects of life under the single idea of devotion to God.

Accordingly he sees יפת אלקים ליפת, how God “opens” people’s feelings to the “beauty” of Japhet, and Japhet first accomplishes his mission in the education of nations so that then the mission entrusted to Shem of the ultimate goal of mankind on earth will be accomplished. וישכון באהלי שם, that mankind learn from Shem “to build their homes on earth in such a manner that God dwells with them”, to live the whole of human life on earth in such a way that the Glory of God once again takes up Its abode down here amongst mankind, ויהי כנען עבד למו, and then even Canaan by devoting himself to Shem will find his salvation for the godly-human life.

We allow ourself to make a further remark on two expressions which we meet here in the mouth of the oldest ancestor of the new human race, and in which the whole Jewish knowledge is concentrated. We refer to the expressions ברוך and ישכון.

ברוך. The understanding of this term has been confused because people have objected to take this word “to bless” referring from man to God, in the same meaning as it has when used from God to man. It has been taken to be adjectival like חנון ,רחום, so that, like these, it designates the active source, the holder of blessing as of pity and grace. But that does not get us much further, we are constantly called upon ’לברך את ה, and the feeling of the greatest enthusiasm and inspiration declares that it is מברך את ’ה. If the man is active in blessing God, then God must be blessed in a passive sense, He must be receiving blessing from man, one can not get away from it. And why should one have to try and get away from it? At the moment that God made the fulfilment of His Will on earth dependent on the free decision of Man He said to them ברכני, bless Me, further My purposes fulfil My wishes, realize my Will, bless My work, the achievement of which on earth I have laid in your hands. And in the same way as מלאכיו, as כל צבאיו משרתיו עושי רצונו as כל מעשיו בכל מקומות ממשלתו, as His angels, as all the hosts of His creations in the world who serve Him fulfilling His Will, as all His creatures in every place of His Kingdom ’מברכים את ה — not praise God, not thank Him — but bless God, work for His one great purpose of this world, so does every Jewish mind say to its soul: ברכי נפשי ’את ה “bless thou, too, O my soul, (my life I.L.), God. And when Jews say ’ברוך אתה ה, they express the vow to God to dedicate all their forces to the fulfilment of the Divine Will. Looked at in this way, ברכה is the fundamental thought which the whole of every Jewish life is to convert into a reality. The whole Torah teaches us nothing else than how we can ’מברך את ה and that we are to do so. To take it to mean praise or thank God, by which one has lost the true conception of ברך את הי, is only then ברכה when it primarily effects its real work on ourselves; if it directs our minds into the right channels and lifts our hearts and so furthers the work which God expects us to accomplish on ourselves. ברכה is the expression in words of that which עבודה expresses in deeds, ברכה is the expression in words of that which the קרבנות express in action, and in our שמונה-עשרה it is not the prayers but the ברכות with which each one concludes, the ברוך אתה הי in which each of us expresses the vow to dedicate all the great and little powers and possessions which God has granted, or will grant to us to be ’לחם אשה ה “food, fuel and care for keeping the fire of godliness alive on earth” — it is only they, the ברכות, which make our תפלה במקום קרבן. But it is highly significant that we meet this conception already in the theurgic speech of the oldest ancestor of the new world. When we say ברוך we are only carrying on the work which here is said to be expected at the beginning and end of humanity We use the oldest word which is known to have been spoken to express the relation of Man to God.

ישכון. A conception that is no less characteristic of Judaism is this second one, שכינה, that we also find already in the mouth of this oldest ancestor of the new world. Other religions teach what one has to do so that one can come to God in the next world. Judaism teaches what we have to do so that God comes to us already in this world. Judaism teaches עיקר שכינה בתחתונים, that God wishes primarily to dwell on earth with mankind, speaks of men ועשו לי מקדש ושכנתי בתוכם, may they make their lives on earth to a Sanctuary, then will I dwell in their midst. So to prepare for the time when the Kingdom of God begins again, not only in heaven but down here on earth, is the mission of Israel, the blossom from the stem of Shem, and that is the goal of its Divine Torah. That is why all the promises of this Torah of God are earthly, refer to our present life. To bank on the next world, to promise heaven or hell in the next world lies in the power of any impostor. But to pledge His word for what will happen down here before our very eyes, that only ה׳ אלקים אמת ומלך עולם can do. This idea, שכינה, that everywhere where the weakest, most unostentatious man sanctifies his small humble home, makes his “camp holy”, that there God מתהלך בקרב מחניך, will make him “blessed”, happy, blessed with completion of celestial enjoyment, make him find, here and today מעין עה״ב, that is what the תורה wishes to see made into a reality in the realm of the Jewish race of men.. So that then it can become the common property of all mankind again and “they find their way back again to the Tree of Life”. But although the conception שכינה does thus teach the most intimate connection of Man to God in this world, in the word itself there lies the greatest protection against all fanaticism and extravagance of fancy from which just on this account no religion has remained as free as Judaism. For, peculiarily enough, שכן means to dwell and also to be a neighbour. Therein lies the highest social idea. In Jewish thought, to dwell, means to be a neighbour. When a Jew takes a place on earth to be his dwelling-place he must at the same time concede space and domain to his fellow-men for a similar dwelling-place. Without a neighbour, his own existence can afford no true settling down. One Jewish man says to another צר לי המקום גשה לי ואשבה “the place, in truth, is narrow for me — there is hardly room for myself — but come thou next to me, for I would settle down”. (Is. 49,20). And now, this same conception שכינה is applied to the Glory of God settling in human circles here on earth. This teaches the intimate approach of the Divine to the human without the least encroachment on the sphere of human life, but always with the assumption of, and bearing in mind, the complete free-will with which Man must achieve his development. It is in this conception of the שכינה that we believed we could see the parrying, the warding off, of all fanaticism in Israel. The Divine is the שכן of Man, and Man of the Divine, but neither become completely absorbed by the other. The same Jewish wisdom which teaches עיקר שכינה בתחתונים, also teaches מעולם לא ירדה שכינה למטה מעשרה. The true Jewish mind forms no visionary fanatics, who extravagantly and wildly go beyond all bonds of reality, and, entranced in their intuitive visions of the Truth — go mad. While Judaism does teach us the most intimate nearness of God to Man, it wants to keep us to the clearest, most comprehensible, we would say sober, way of contemplating it. Not by a fanatic gushing over into the divine, not by a so-called absorption into God, not by finally coming to lose all freedom of self decision, and feeling that all we do, is really God doing in us, and through us, do we become the servants of God. Only in using the mind and the freedom of will which God has given us, in the earthly sphere to which He has appointed us, in the most complete faithfulness to God with deliberation and the clearest human insight, do we ourselves attain the height of human perfection, and our earthly management of life gains the holiness that makes it worthy of the proximity of God. Only where the ten טפחים of human activity end does the management of the happiness-bringing proximity of God begin.

V. 1. They themselves had lived before the Flood, but their children were already born under the influence of the new conditions. Now follows a list of the branches of these new families. We need not bother to indicate to which well known races and nations and their branches these names may refer. We may mention how they occur in absolute historical accuracy more and more in the archaeological researches into these nations whose history, apart from here, the Torah does not go into. We only allow ourself a few more general remarks.

V. 2. The sons of Japheth are mentioned first, and of these, only the further branches of Gomer and Yavan are named. So that these must be the most typical bearers of the Japheth characteristics, and it is just these that one takes the greatest part of the present-day inhabitants of Europe and West Asia to be.

V. 5. נפרדו. Of the real dispersion and differentation of languages we are only told later. Nevertheless we see already here a spreading out of nations according to language and countries. That which occured later on as a result of a quite special intervention of the Divine management of the education of mankind is something different from what is here related. What is said here is nothing more than the perfectly natural development which was bound to occur in accordance with the newly formed fresh conditions. By the differences of climate, temperature, soil etc., the development of a diversity of peoples in their natural spreading out over the earth had been given as their purpose. For פרד which is again repeated (V.32) referring to this separation of nations must not be confused with פוץ and הפיץ which characterised the later event and which means a forcible scattering. הפרד on the other hand, means a quite natural or free-willed scattering or separating. Thus it is used referring to the streams (Ch. II.10) and to Abraham and Lot. (Ch. XIII.11 and 14).

אי, root איה. Just as איה and אי are the questions as to the unknown place in which some object is to be found, so אי altogether the isolated place in which a multitutde is to be found, hence an island and a shut-in land, then used for the inhabitants who are thus cut off from other people.

איש ללשנו not בלשנו. Their different dialect was not the cause but the result of their separation. As a result of their multiplying they spread abroad into different districts, and under the influence of the land etc., their speech became modified. There would be a definite difference between the שפה of the later event and the לשון of what is related here. שפה would designate the language, French, German, etc., but לשון the way of pronouncing, the dialect. (see Ch. 11,1). לשון, probably from לוש (anal. to זדון from לצון ,זוד from לוץ) to knead, i.e. (a) to bring a mass of separate parts into one uniform mass, and at the same time (b) to shape and form it. In the same way the tongue acts. It forms the mouthful to a shape for swallowing, and regulates the breath to form sounds. Through it the column of air exhaled from the lungs, which by the fine vibrations of the vocal chords produce the infinite variety of the sounds of human speech, becomes formed and modified. Then just as לוש is the formation of the voice to sounds and words, so is לוץ the ingenious use of words לצון לץ ;מליצה מליץ, a master of speech, dialectics. Accordingly we are told, as the descendants of Noah grew in numbers, they naturally spread out, became אײם, cut off from one another, the one land, ארץ became divided into different ארצות, the one גוי separated into different groups of peoples, and then, as personalities are ruled and changed by external conditions, the one speech became differentiated into different dialects. So each one separated ללשונו. But whereas such difference in dialect was a cause of separation from others externally and formed various גוים it acted internally as a means of holding together the משפחות בגויהם. There is no union without separation. We note further that the same separating and uniting factors are mentioned in connection with Ham’s and Shem’s descendants למשפחתם ללשנתם בארצתם בגויהם but אײ הגוים, the still greater separation is recorded only of the races of Japheth, so that these must have separated out into a still greater diversity of people with their own characteristics. This is known to us of the בני יון, the Greeks. And if — as seems very probable — there is truth in the popular tradition that אשכנז are the Germanic races, then we should have in אשכנז the second striking example of national splitting up, a decentralisation which must have furthered very considerably the Japhetic mission in the world. Culture has always been accorded the greatest care in small states.

V. 8. Up till now the sons were founders, ancestors, of nations. Now follows a son, who founded no nation, but with whom, nevertheless, a new and powerful factor in the development of nations was introduced. He started being a גבור on earth. There had been גבורים before him, we have only to remember the Nefilim (Ch. VI.4). But he started להיות גבור בארץ, to find his whole character, his profession, his whole position in life in גבור-ism, something which started with him in the life of nations, and since then has continued. We have already remarked on the עבד עבדים which had been declared as the future fate of the Hamitic race, how through the lack of moral freedom of will which yielding to sensuality brings about, social freedom also becomes ruined, and now it is highly significant to see how, already in Ham’s grandson, the creator of the גבור profession appears. גבור always assumes that something else has been overcome by the exercise of considerable force, primarily physical bodily force. גור .קבר ,כפר ,גבר ,גור a young lion, who then becomes כפיר, a leader. כפר to cover up, קבר to bury completely. גבר is in the middle, is is not covering up, not burying, but such overpowering with one’s strength that the other personality can not recover. Now גבורה is also one of the מתנות, the gifts of God reckoned by Jeremiah (IX,22) together with חכמה and עושר. All these gifts granted to men by God are means of the greatest happiness and well-being if they are used for the purposes mentioned there in the verse, if חכמה serves חסד, if גבורה is used for משפט and עושר for צדקה, that חכמה does not become calculating, self-serving cunning, but is used in self-sacrificing love for others, in preaching and advising; strength in the service of enforcing justice; and riches in doing good. גבור בארץ courage and strength on earth, is nothing bad in itself, but it does become so in V.9 where this גבור is more precisely described as גבר-ציד.

V. 9. It is this ציד modification which makes the appearance of a גבור profession ominous. Although ציד is usually used for hunting animals, the conception צוד occurs frequently referring to hunting and catching human beings, as חמד רשע מצוד רעים (Prov. 12,12) and elsewhere. מצודה, a fortress or strong castle served quite entirely for the enclosure and locking up of human beings. Related roots are זוד .צוד ,סוד ,זוד is the hidden intention for a deed, not the deed itself, but the resolution to do it, which remains hidden until it is carried out. If altogether the intention only is taken which is to be kept as such for some time, or if its motives are never to be revealed, then it becomes סוד, secret. סוד, secrecy is something which is never really appropriate in human circles. Only the סוד of God is good. If amongst men something has to be kept בסוד then either the person himself, or that which is to be kept secret, or the surroundings must be bad. Especially public life, the rule of the ruler — and here, we are at the cradle of Kingship — is never honoured by סוד. Secret politics, according to the Jewish idea, are bad politics. כבוד מלכים it says in Prov. 25,2, the honour of Kings is חקור דבר when all their doings are so clear and transparent that everybody can fathom them. Publicity, openness, is the touch-stone for the doings of rulers. Only of God does it say, כבוד אלקים הסתר דבר, the inscrutability of His Rule is for men the seal of His greatness. Now צוד is a זוד, something resolved בזדון, kept בסוד, and at the right moment bursts forth with sudden violence (צ). That is also what מצודה, fortified castles were originally, nests of robbers, and traps, isolated places in which tyrants locked themselves up in safety and at opportune times burst forth to plunder.

Nimrod started being a גבור ציד, a champion at “man catching”, a powerful man who mixed his violence with cunning to catch men for his plans. Nothing should be so much in contrast to each other than גבורה and סוד. Might, Power in service of right and justice disdains secrecy and craft, does not require it. To that must be added that ציד itself must involve the conception of self-interest, for צידה means victuals. Whereas לחם means that which has been won for immediate use, צידה is the food which has been cleverly obtained beforehand, that one seizes now to have to hand at the appointed time. So that צוד and ציד is not catching something to destroy it (which is also why צד נחש on שבת is פטור), but for use. So that it is also the carrying-out of a plan in one’s own interest. Herein lies the danger of power combined with ציד, or rather of power used in the service of ציד which constitutes the גבוד ציד. For, that גבורים “the superior ones” go to the lead and the others yield to them, is the natural order for well-being. Provided, of course, that the powerful ones use their power in the interest of others, are the protectors and defenders of the rights of the weaker ones. But the diametrical opposite of this is גבורת ציד, the power of the mighty misused to trap men for their own egoistic purposes. And it was just Nimrod who was the first, in the feeling of his own material, perhaps also intellectual, overpowering superiority over his contemporaries, to subjugate the lesser strong and clear sighted, and to keep them under his yoke until the time he would need them for his own purposes. Here, accordingly, is shown the evil of tyranny which continued so perniciously through the history of nations, and moreover it is shown here that it had its origin in force and cunning from above and not in the voluntary submission from below. But, that ציד here is speaking of trapping human beings not as is usually taken, of hunting animals, “a mighty hunter”, is proved by the immediately following ותהי ראשית ממלכתו from which it is evident that the גבור ציד must have had a ממלכה, or that גבור ציד here is altogether identical with מלך. Nimrod was the first King.

Now two most significant words follow: ’גבור ציד לפני ה. In תנ״ך the word ’לפני ה never designates that anything is being done against God’s will, but rather just that which is done in accordance with it. Thus we find it used repeatedly in פרשת בני ראובן ובני גד (Numb. 32,20 etc. seq.) to designate the readiness to take part in the war in the service of God, אם תחלצו לפני ה׳ למלחמה etc. So that here, too, the ’לפני ה could mean simply, “in the name of God”, in a quite “pious God-pleasing” manner and this would be the culmination of the wickedness. The Name ’ה had not yet become lost, the Name which, rightly understood, makes all men equal and free, and makes benevolence and love regulate all and apply to all. Now Nimrod began to suppress his fellow-men “in the Name of God” ’לפני ה. He was the first to misuse the Name of God, to cloak his domination under the show of its being pleasing to God, or rather to demand the recognition of his power in the name of God. This went so far later on, that in ancient times kings not only considered themselves there by divine-right and “Nimrods” adorned themselves with the reflection of divine majesty but they themselves became gods, and just in Ham’s descendants we see Pharaohs kneeling in worship before images of themselves. Thereby Nimrod was the first, the prototype of all those dynasties who craftily crowned themselves with the halo of seeming holiness, whose might, politics and semblance of holiness, one characterised as ’כנמרד גבור ציד לפני ה.

מלך .ממלכתו. hat weiter keine Verwandtschaft im Hebräischen als mit מלק das mit dem verstärkten p-Laut: gewaltsam den Kopf abdrücken heißt. Vielleicht heißt מלך demnach: an die Stelle des Kopfes für andere treten, Kopf für andere sein, daher auch Chaldäisch נמלך, sich des Kopfes des andern bedienen, sich Rat bei jemandem holen. Dürften wir die Behauptung wagen, daß in den hebräischen Sprachwurzeln jeder Buchstabe ein Merkmal des auszudrückenden Begriffes bezeichnet, eine Annahme, die um so weniger unwahrscheinlich sein dürfte, da die Hälfte der hebräischen Buchstaben in der Tat ganz offenkundig ihre besondere begriffliche Bedeutung hat, so böte dafür das Wort מלך einen eklatanten Beleg. Der Begriff מלך in reinster Auffassung ist erschöpft durch die Merkmale מ .מ ,ל ,ך: derjenige, von dem alles ausgehen soll, ל: zu dem alles zurückkehren und כ: der das Vorbild, das Ideal für alle sein soll. Darin unterscheidet er sich von משל, wo nicht das geistige Vorbild in כ ausgedrückt ist. מלך, der Edelste, Weiseste, Voranleuchtendste, das ist׳s, was den jüdischen König zum Könige machen soll; denn im jüdischen Schrifttum ist das Königtum durchaus nicht aus dem auf Erden zu gründenden Gottesreiche verwiesen. Auch unsere und der Menschheit Zukunft erfüllt sich durch einen מלך המשיח. Dieses persönlich voranleuchtende Sittliche fehlt im Begriffe משל, in welchem mehr das Herrschende, Gebietende ausgedrückt ist, wovon die Bestimmung ausgeht, was etwas sei oder sein soll (ש). Daher ja auch מָשָל, ein Spruch, der ausspricht, was Menschen oder Dinge sind oder sollen — und ebenso ein Symbol, welches beides veranschaulicht.

V. 11. אשור we find as the descendants of Shem. It seems that Nimrod could only succeed in being גבור ציד in his own circles. This is, after all, primarily only possible where the moral lack of freedom, self control, makes people fit and suitable to become עבד עבדים. Nimrod’s efforts accordingly, seem primarily only to have met with success in the descendants of Ham. But אשור went out of his way, moved away, and while Nimrod found his greatness in political tyrannical rule, אשור found his in building cities and in building roads to them (רחובות עיר). Nimrod was a conqueror, Asshur a builder. But all this is, after all, only surmise.
V. 18. ואחר נפוצו. So far they had branched off naturally. Afterwards they scattered farther afield, forced by external conditions.

V. 21. ולשם ילד גם הוא. To Shem also, upon whom, according to the prophetic speech of his father, the final goal of mankind rested, descendants were born. He is brought into prominence here on two counts. Firstly, as the father of all the children of עבר. Although עבר was the great-grandchild of Shem, and it was just his children who first began to make the pronouncement of Noah, וישכון באהלי שם, into a reality, nevertheless Shem was their spiritual father. Even יעקב still learnt from Shem. That an Abraham could be born in Terach’s house and that his sons could carry on that which God had entrusted to him as a treasure for mankind we have to thank Shem for. Often nobody knows what he has to thank the זכות of his father and grandfather for, whose point of view he perhaps derides and laughts at, and does not ask himself how much of such spiritual and moral זכות he will then leave to his sons and grandchildren. And secondly, he was at the same time יפת .אחי יפת הגדול was his elder brother and preceded him with the mission to act as his herald to make Men’s hearts receptive to higher things and so ultimately for the reception of Shem’s teachings. Quite naturally for a long long time Shem would not be recognized as the גדול on earth. For Japhetic art and science people are easily receptive. The quiet tranquil Light, as the representative of which Shem is to go through the world, the great Truths which he is to bring, the conception of life which one must either carry out or reject — there is no middle way — for that to be generally accepted one must have patience for a long time.

V. 1. We have already seen above that from quite natural causes the people spread out in different groups, and in consequence acquired different לשונות. But these לשונות were not different languages. Just as the relation is between לשון the tongue and שפה the lip, so is that of their product, speech. They had one lip but various tongues i.e. they had one language, only it was spoken in different dialects. שפה really means the border, not the end where something has to leave off, but where its natural end is, where it has reached the limit it is to reach, and so comes to its end. Now the lip is called שפה as being the border line the end of the interior of the body. Then just as שפה thus really represents the whole oral cavity and לשון the single organ which regulates the breath etc., לשון can designate the various dialects, but שפה only speech in general. Apart from various dialects there was still only one language. We may not forget that there was nearly 400 years between the Flood and the הפלגה, during which the natural spreading abroad and the resulting modification of speech which results had plenty of time to develop into various dialects which nevertheless remained שפה אחת, one language.

ודברים אחדים is not the same as שפה אחת .שפה אחת is the phonetic sameness of speech (the sound of the language I.L.) which is fundamentally based on organic causes. דברים אחדים is the sameness of the formation of words and sentences which is brought about by spiritual mental agreement in the way that things and their relations are looked at. We have already considered the relationship of דבר to תור ,טור ,דור ,תפר all of which designate the joining of several similar things. Every spoken word is a joining together of several sounds, both, as expressing a thought which is combining several characteristics to form one conception (a conception itself designates the combination of several characteristics), and, as the contents of sentences and speeches, the combination of several thoughts to the expression of one complete idea. All this is designed by דבר. So that the whole human race was still harmoniously in unison, for good and for bad, both organically and mentally.

V. 2. נסע, related to נשא .נסח ,נסה ,נשא: to lift something from the place where it is. נסה: to place somebody on a higher standpoint than that which he occupies so as to test him whether he can stand there; for that is what every test is. נסע: a voluntary moving away from the place one occupies. It is probably never a compulsory going away but always to a more attractive place. נסח is a forced tearing away (יסחך Ps. 55,7). — קדם: that which comes first, in space or time, the east or the past. It is remarkable that there where the earthly sun rises the spiritual origin of the human race lies. The older generation remained there, the younger generation no longer felt at ease there, they felt themselves able to fly on their own wings, went forth, as our sages put it, מקדמונו של עולם. The old leaders of education, like שם and perhaps Noah remained in the East, there, where the original beginning and foundation of the development of mankind had been. Now it does not say ויסעו וימצאו, in which case ויסעו would simply be an introduction to וימצאו, but בנסעם, they were on their journey away from their homeland, getting away was their object. They sought something better, more attractive. Then they found a plain in the land of Shinar. This was the territory where the first ’גבור ציד לפני ה began his reign (Ch. 10,10). In this land they found a plain, without mountains, without forests (בקעה really a gap, a cleft) there it was free, there they settled.

V. 3. רעו ,רעהו of cattle, to graze, to seek that which is congenial of the pasturage, to yield that which is congenial. This is the relation in which every man should stand towards every other man. Each should offer himself as “pasturage” to the other, each should find his congenial “grazing ground” in the other, they are mutually to complement, nourish and care for each other. הבה, come give! commanding imperative of יהב, and indeed primarily, “give yourself here, lend your strength”; and when it is one רע speaking to another it implies “I will do the same”, hence at once the plural נלבנה, implying “let us see what we can do together”. נשרפה לשרפה, not נשרפה שרפה, not “let us make a fire” but let us burn whatever it is, to make a fire. והחמר היה להם לחומר this is usually translated, the clay served them for mortar. But חמר never means clay, nor חומר mortar, but the reverse: ותחמרה בחמר ,כחומר ביד היוצר, so that here it must mean: the mortar served them for clay.

If we look at what we are told here in toto, and it is the more necessary to pay attention to every detail, for, as our sages have already remarked, while at the המבול the sin is clearly told us, here at the דור הפלגה it is not definitely said what they did, or on what God’s displeasure fell.

They found a plain where all building material was lacking. There they wanted to remain, wanted to see if they could not make something by themselves, “let us make artificial, man-made stones” (this lies in the הבה). And just as there was no material for building so was there no material for burning to bake such a huge quantity of bricks, hence נשרפה לשרפה. Where, as here, the object is not mentioned, it means the most comprehensive generality: “let us burn whatever it is, whatever we can find”. And so bricks served them for stones and what otherwise is only used as a binding material, as mortar, they used as a building material. Elsewhere one built with stone and cemented with clay. The stone was the חומר the building material, clay the mortar, both provided by Nature. But here both were artificially man-made products, and what previously was חֵמָר they used for חוֹמָר.

V. 4. If it goes on to say that God descended to see, לראות, the city and the tower which men had built for themselves, that is to say, to look into the matter before giving judgement, that tells us that building a city or a tower is nothing wrong in itself. Accordingly the wrong and the danger to the whole moral future must lie in the purpose for which it was built and the feelings which actuated the builders. The stress of the whole project clearly lies in the expressed purpose: נעשה לנו שם! If we consider what that implies we note: — We are standing at the threshold of world history. Who says this נעשה לנו? The whole of that generation. But if the general public say: we would make ourselves a name, it can only be directed against two powers, against God Who is above them, or against the individual who is beneath them, for a whole generation as a community has nobody beside them. Of future fame there can be no question, for the פן נפוץ shows they were thinking of the immediate present, and in any case the undertaking was one, to which we shall come back to further on, which was to be continued building by all succeeding generations.

Accordingly the whole community came together in a plain, they come to the idea, there, where there are no forests, no rocks, no stone, nothing provided by nature for building, they will manufacture everything by human hands, they see thereby, what a community can do if they all join forces and work together, how they can overcome and master nature. They decide to make something that shall serve as a perpetual reminder of the power of the community over the individual. Now it is just on the community that God reckons ואגדתו על ארץ יסדה. Not for nothing has God made men so different from one another, one is to complement the other, to feel the need of the other, individuals die, the power of individuals is limited. Only אין צבור מת ואין צבור עני only the community does not die, and only the community is never poor. Everything permanently great and noble is only made by the union of forces. But the community only stands there as the flower of perfection if it takes the same stand towards God as the individual should, if like the individual, it does not consider itself above the Law of God, if it uses the power with which the united forces of the community invest it, only in the service of God, and looks on its mission as nothing other than to fulfil the service of God with the combined forces of the community more completely and more perfectly than lies in the power of the individual. But here lies the danger. Whereas the individual is finally brought by itself to realise the limitation of its power this is not the case with the community. For it really is strong, it really has power. It easily comes to regard itself as the purpose of its existence, and the establishment of itself as its mission, as if the individual has importance only for the community, the community is not there for supplementing the individual, but the individual is merely a pawn for the use of the community.

When the community says: We will make the powers which lie in a community recognised, will unite our powers to establish ourself; if they as the herald of God, do not call on the individuals בשם השם to the service of God, but to their own service, — נעשה לנו שם — if they place themselves there, instead of a means, as an end, then the whole moral future of mankind goes to ruin, then what is almost prophetically said here occurs: mankind perceives its own powers, and, the more originality used the more arrogantly comes to believe that the community as such can dispense with God and His laws of morality. “The old people had to have stone, but we build even where there is no stone”. Then the idol of an empty purpose is created, an idol which brings no happiness and to which the individual has to give up the whole of his existence and the community its allegiance to the laws of morality. Individuals, of course, must weep when one of them falls, but at the building of the fame of the community the toll of human lives is not counted. The community says נשרפה לשרפה: whatever it is, as long as it furthers the building of our fame it is to be used. The individual believes he has lived enough if he gives up his life, though it be for an idle cause, if that cause is one on which the community has set its idea of obtaining fame and glory. That glory which is content to march triumphantly on over millions of dead bodies. And in the same way in spiritual and moral matters the חֵמָר becomes the חמֶר the means the end.

Our sages teach us that this undertaking only succeeded under Nimrod’s leadership, and indeed it is only a ’גבור ציד לפני ה like Nimrod who could move men to such sacrifice. He, too, could not have succeeded if he had not understood how to make men enthusiastic for his own ends, if he had not known how to make his own fame identical with that of the masses who sacrificed themselves for him. Not with gold or possessions, but with a little bit of ribbon in the lapel or on the breast does a Napoleon or an Alexander understand how to lure the masses for his purpose.

But it is the most pernicious error to imagine that the state or the community has the right to purpose any other purposes than such that would find value and meaning if weighed in the scales of the laws of morality. The very opposite is the truth. For the individual there may be, even if no justification, at least some excuse if some cogent pressing situation necessitates some deviation from the strict moral law, but for the community no such situation can arise.

In this the פן נפוץ, becomes understandable. They feared to cease to form a whole community. What would that matter if the community was only a union to look after the individuals, and what was there to fear if all that the community wanted was to enable the laws of morality to be fulfilled in a higher and more perfect degree. If the community is what it should be, even if it consists of millions, it requires no artificial means of holding it together, the bond lies in the consciousness of every individual, and its point of union is God. But if it is not there for the sake of the individual but for the reverse, if it says נעשה לנו שם, then naturally the individual is only forced, or artificially lured, to sacrifice himself and be submissive to it.

With this נעשה לנו שם, with the introduction of this false, so-called patriotism, with the unchaining of the lust for fame which in the individual is considered as a vice, but nationally as a virtue, the whole moral mission of states and individuals is undermined. All passions have their limit of satiation, the lust for fame has no limits. This lust for fame has not only built its tower here, not only here has it unconcernedly burnt up everything to obtain bricks for the building of its triumph, but the whole of world-history has, for the greatest part, to relate only of such building of towers of imaginary glory for which Nimrods have understood how to lure and force the nations. But of the simple life of mankind, of that which goes on in the homes, the pen of history has little to relate; that, in the beautiful metaphor of our sages, only God Himself records, and Elijah and the Messiah, those messengers and bringers of the ultimate salvation of mankind, sign it as witnesses.

A pithy saying in פרקי דר״א characterises these erroneous ideas as follows: — אם נפל אדם ומת לא היו שמים את לבם עליו, ואם נפלה לבינה היו יושבים ובוכים אוי לנו אימתי תעלה אחרת תחתיה: “If a man had a fatal accident at the building they did not take it to heart, but if a brick fell to the ground they sat and wept and wailed: when shall we get another one up into its place!”

We mentioned above that the undertaking to build a tower reaching right into heaven was to be a work which all future generations were to be called on to continue. Later on we also find such buildings which were built on and on interminably. In the land of that state which became the heir of Nimrod-like plans, Egypt, there still stand pyramids one of which every King started to build at the beginning of his reign and which were built on and on during the whole duration of his reign. There the whole nation was yoked uninterruptedly to go on building the sepulchred monument to the King’s fame, a similar work in miniature to the project here. Our sages, accordingly ascribe the words נעשה לנו שם to Nimrod and take the plural to be the plural of majesty. And actually such memorials erected to national fame are only apparently a glorification of the nation or community, in reality they are the glorification of the one powerful man who understood how to get the laurel wreath placed on his brow which the powers of the community had won. The whole history of mankind up to the present seems to be a realisation of the sentence: הקנאה והתאוה והכבוד מוציאין את האדם מן העולם. The antediluvial world went to its ruin through נחש ;תאוה וקנאה and השחתת דרך ,קין and חמס. With the בכוד ,דור הפלגה enters the pernicious reign.

V. 5. Whereas at the דור המבול the name אלקים always appeared, here, as רמב״ן already has remarked, only the שם הויה is used. Sexual and social degeneration as at the age of the Flood, is not only a danger to human society, it is a threat to the laws of nature ordained by the Creator. But the sin of the דור הפלגה was no physical one, on the surface it was apparently not even a social one, peace and union were still present, but the future of mankind which is dependent on the recognition of the priceless value and moral importance of the individual, was, to the highest degree, endangered by the purpose which the leaders had in mind. Therefore the intervention is described as the work of ’ה, the Divine Rule for bringing about the ultimate happiness and true well-being of mankind.

וירד occurs here for the first time. When we consider that עיקר שכינה בתחתונים, then וירד always designates such a crisis in the development of world affairs that God intervenes to prevent the gap between heaven and earth becoming larger. It brings the world a step nearer to the goal where the שכינה can again stay בתחתונים. But here וירד stands out in bold relief much more pointedly. The state, the community will not allow the individual any other supreme lord than itstelf. But just as this is an attack on the priceless worth of every individual, which is not just transfered to him through the total worth of the community, and whose value can never be reckoned in a brick, even if that brick is part of the building of the national glory; so is it an attack on God, Who calls every man directly to His service, and thereby makes every man, prince or slave, equal and free. The Name ’ה tolerates no slave! Now, in the moment where the community of mankind instead of summoning every individual ’בשם ה places its own name in the place of God’s then ’וירד ה, God interferes, does not let the world go on, comes down to “see” the communal building of mankind, i.e. with the intention of testing the purpose of it. (About anthropomorphism see on Ch. 6,6).

V. 6. ’ויאמר ה׳ וגו. There they stood in complete agreement, found themselves for the first time all of one mind after they had journeyed out all together — and the first thought which the consciousness of the meaning and importance of being a united community was not: we could glorify God, use our united strength for His glorification, but: נעשה לנו שם. That was immediately the first beginning for which they wanted to use their united strength and powers: — בצר occurs with two meanings, wine harvest and fortifying, making secure. The basic conception seems to be, surrounding something with a firm protection, rendering it secure. So that בצר does not mean fixing securely in the ground, but strengthening the walls so that they can not easily be breached, and also surrounding the city with wall and bulwarks. Now if בצר also means to harvest grapes it does not mean to empty the vine of the grapes, but refers to the grapes which are to be made secure, to be brought home to security. So that בצר means to make something unconquerable, secure from attack, and the ועתה לא יבצר מהם here, would mean nothing will be secure, unattainable by them.

יזם .יזמו does not occur elsewhere. One takes it to mean the same as זמם, analogous to טוב and יטב and the relation of ע״ע to זמם .ע״ו is a difficult word. It occurs with quite opposite meanings. Thus in Zacharia 8,14,15 we find immediately next to each other: כאשר זממתי להרע לכם וגו׳ כן שבתי וממתי וגו׳ להיטיב, and although זמה occurs almost excusively in a bad sense מזמה is used in Prov. with equal frequency in a good sense. If we compare זמם with the related roots סמם and צמם we find צמם is a compressing together, צמתך, holding together wavy hair, and סמם in סם to describe such materials (poisons, drugs, etc.) of which the smallest quantities have great powers concentrated in them, where the effect is far beyond the visible size of the cause. According to this זמם would mean the devising of such means whereby out of small causes unproportionately great things are to occur. Thus, speaking of the אשת חיל it says זממה שדה, by saving up pennies, by small unostentatious beginnings she achieves the great purchase of a field. Thus at עדים זוממים with a word and apparently in perfect innocence — they are apparently only doing their duty in giving their evidence, ’אם לא יגיד וגו — they want to accomplish their plan of murder. זמה is the term applied to those sins, which, bad and corrupt, in themselves, are nevertheless in their pernicious consequences immeasurably further reaching. On the other hand the same thing applies in the opposite direction for there are also good purposes and results which only grow out of small, simple beginnings which have to be constantly watched and kept in mind. These are called מזמות. Thus, above all, in the business of educating and teaching, the pupil has to be constantly practised in small tests and trials and little acts of unselfishness, small beginnings out of which all greatness in the future is to ensue. Thus the child learns natural מזמות. Now here it does not say ײזמו, what they have in mind with this beginning is something which goes much farther, they call it, the fame of the community but it really means the fame of an individual, it is called the fame of the community but it really means the enslavement of the community! So what it says here is “and that at once was their beginning and this is what they started to do, and now nothing will remain unattainable by them, all which they already plan to accomplish with starting this building”.

But it is possible, and more probable that יזם is related to גזם .גזם is a kind of locust, an ארבה, a swarm, an immense mass. In rabbinic Hebrew גזם and גוזמא is an extravagant exaggeration, a hyperbole, also related to קסם magic which similarly wants to accomplish something beyond the necessary connection between cause and effect. Taken from this כל אשר יזמו לעשות would mean “all which they have planned to accomplish beyond all measure”.

V. 7. ’ונבלה וגו. Usually translated, confuse, from בלל. But there is no active, form of בלל, which would correspond to this form of the word. It would have to be ונבֹלָה in Kal or ונבֵלָה in Hiphil. The word clearly comes from נבל, to cause to wither, dry up, fade away, and it says: “we would go down, and their speech will at once become withered, or will have become withered”. No further special action is required. The נבלה of their speech is the immediate result of ירידה. At the end it certainly does say ’כי שם בלל ה׳ וגו, so that the procedure is clearly described with the word בלל and from this description the procedure is called a “confusion of language”. But this idea does not correspond to that which one usually takes this event to have been. It was to have been a division of languages, not a mixing of them. A mixing would imply that there were already different languages in existence which now were all mixed up. Besides, בלל never means simply intermixing existing ingredients, but the introduction of a fresh material to another and then stirring them so thoroughly together that in every particle of the old there is some of the new. סולת בלולה בשמן יש בילה, or אין בילה. So here there is not the slightest idea of confusion.

בלל is related to בלל .פלל is the concrete mixing of one substance into another, it is more than simple ערב where the particles of the mixture are not incorporated into one unit. And now, just as out of ערב, transposed to human society, we get the guarantor, the third party who comes between two separated people, and standing in the middle becomes the uniting factor which joins them together, in the same way of פלל — the stronger form of בלל — we get the judge. The judge brings a factor which stands outside the contending parties which can look impartially at the matter, and lets this objective consideration penetrate into every aspect of the case and thereby settles the dispute and brings together those that were standing apart and opposed to one another. The ordinary way of looking at the matter is that the parties have got themselves entangled with each other, the judge decides and separates them, justice is something dividing. According to the Jewish concept injustice divides, justice unites. In the same way we find ויעמוד פנחס ויפלל. So also התפלל to get oneself completely penetrated with all that is godly which should be the ruling and forming factor for mankind in every direction. In prayer the Jew becomes his own judge.

If this is the meaning of בלל then here, too, something must have come into the formation of their speech which hitherto had had no influence on it, and this new element must by itself have brought about that people no longer understood each other. The effect of the entry of this strange element into the way they formed their speech is primarily called נבל. Just as בלל is the beginning of פלל so is נבל the beginning of נפל. That which later effects the fall begins in the first stage with withering, drying up. A flower becomes withered as soon as it begins to be separated from the source of its thriving. As soon as the canals which join the source of life to the canals which form the flower become contracted, the flower begins to wither, and when the connection entirely ceases, the flower falls off. So here, as soon as God came down, the language became separated from the source which hitherto had formed it.

What are the elements that form words and language. There are, or, at least, there can be, two, an objective one and a subjective one. We can think of a language, the naming of things and their connections, being formed from what things are in themselves and what their connections are in the world in general, i.e. objectively. Or subjectively from the special point of view which a nation may have of things and their relationships. In the languages now prevalent, it is only seldom that we find words in the different languages which were formed from the same point of view of looking at the thing. For instance take the word judge which we have just been considering. In German “Richter”, the one who gives things the direction, “richtung” in which they are to turn, he decides, “ent-scheidet”, separates this here, that there. In Hebrew the judge is called שופט the “uniter” justice is משפט, the creation of harmonious order (שפת ,שפד ,שפט), which places everybody where he ought to be in conjunction with the other party. In German, bad, “schlecht” seems to come from “schlichte”, simple, unpretending, so that everybody who does not want to be bad must not be “schlicht” simple, and cunning would be the quality to strive for, whereas in Hebrew it is ישר the straight. Or take, for example, the words virtue, religion. In German “Tugend”, virtue — the highest moral aim — comes from “taugen” to be useful, something that is of use, in Latin languages it comes from “vir”, manliness, virility. In Hebrew we have no word at all for it, our highest is מצוה and we have only the separate virtues, חסד, משפם, מצוה etc. The same with religion. Every European language speaks of religion. We, the People of Religion par excellence have no expression for it. As soon as anything is used to designate some special relationship in our life as religious, it specialises just this, and implies that there are phases in life which have no relation to it. It makes it a separate realm. But where everything from birth to death belongs to religion this conception can not exist inasmuch as every phase of life is penetrated with it and nothing at all left out. The word religion, if it comes from the Latin “religare”, to bind, is even contrary to the Jewish point of view. Our relation to God makes us free, חרות על הלוחות. Or in social life. One language has the conception of people, nations as “volk”, can only think of the idea of a nation as people who have to “folgen” follow, a depressing thought of lack of independence; others, the Latin languages, see in a nation, in people, only the all-devouring masses “populus”; a third the Hebrew, see them only as עם, an association, a union of equals and looked at from outside as גוי a closed corporate unit. The one sees in a lord “Herrn” only the domineering, mastering “herrschend” the other just the אדן) אדון), the base which bears and supports everything. (אלופינו מסובלים our leaders are the heaviest laden) etc. etc. If these nations spoke the same language, with the same word they would express the opposite idea. With all these examples, of which we could continue almost endlessly, we only wish to make it clear that there could be one language, phonetically and organically the same, שפה אחת and still, through looking at the words from different points of view, people need not understand each other any more. So that, even without any external influences making any organic changes, from within, by a change in the mind which conceives the words, differences of speech could arise. In a word, that there could be שפה אחת and still not necessarily ודברים אחדים.

Until then, we are told, there was שפה אחת and ודברים אחדים, not only a physical and climatic sameness, one common organic language, but also the same universal turn of mind; the same way of looking at life and things granted also דברים אחדים. Such spiritual unity could only last as long as words which were spoken were not formed by each individual himself, but had been handed down traditionally. So long as one was in agreement over things in general and this agreement had been given by a higher sanction, in short, as long as the language was objective and not subjective, for so long the language would be based on the actual permanent nature and purpose of things and not on the way each individual looked at them. Such a given objective language would rather create and keep the agreement in the way of looking at the world and life, in it all wisdom would have been laid down. All there is in the teachings of right and morality, of physics and metaphysics is nothing more than the conception of what things are and what they should be, and all this would be laid down in the language. Disturbing such a language would cause no small revolution. For example, think for a minute that the word to “have” was missing from our vocabulary. In Hebrew it does not exist. “To have” has the conception of corporal holding fast, “habere”, “avere” to desire something, and when one has seized it, then one “has it”. Let us imagine this whole conception was not there, a man could only consider that to be his which really appertains to him, is “לו״ as in the Hebrew. Think, how then, in that language the idea of “mine and thine” would not exist in the separated cut-off centralization in which we use the words. All things would only be thought of in their befitting connection with persons. Then the first person who introduced the idea of “have” (I have it, whether, it really pertains to me or not I.L.) would indeed have brought about the greatest revolution; he would have changed the idea of right to the idea of “grab”. Or take the narrower circle of family life, on which our sages lay such important stress, and when Adam called his wife Isha, remark thereon מכאן שנברא העולם בלשון הקודש. In the word איש and אשה ( man and a female man I.L.) lay the guarantee for the equality in rank and mutually complementing calling of Man and Woman. As long as man and woman were איש and אשה there was no need for man to be emancipated from woman nor woman from man, neither could make the other into a slave nor yet into a god or goddess. The first who altered this designation — as indeed our sages remark, in no other language are man and woman designated by words coming from the same root and so regarded from the same trend of thought — brought it about that one man would yoke his woman to the plough while the other would throw himself at her feet. Equally so, as long as father and mother are called אב and אם and are before the children’s eyes as such, and brother and sister אח and אחות are ranked on one thread and bound closely to each other, one really only has to know names and with them one gets all the social wisdom and philosophy, while e.g. “Father” and “Mother” convey nothing at all.

If this שפה אחת was the language in which God taught the first man to look at things and the words were the names with which God called things for man, so that they contained the right way which God wants man to look at things, not subjectively or capriciously but in accordance with His Will, then it is quite possible that perhaps ’קרא בשם ה means nothing else but to teach the world what things are and should be according to God’s Will for Man. For it is only when we call things by their right names that Truth remains clear and not clouded for us.

The element which then could enter this universal language and suddenly cut it off from its old source could be nothing other than the awakening of the consciousness of the individual of himself which made subjective caprice oppose the objective viewpoint which hitherto had been given him. The attempt of the community by this building to do away with the individuality of the individual was broken by the awakening consciousness of the independent value of the individual, apart from his value as a unit of the community. The feeling dawned in them that every human being, Nimrod and slave alike, is called on to have the same freedom of exercising his own will. Obstinacy, his own opinion, egoism awoke in the individual, he would no longer accept or submit to any point of view other that his own, not even if it came traditionally from God Himself — exaggerated excuses which however in God’s Hands became the means for saving humanity.

When the united power of the community is misused and, instead of using it on the treasure which is entrusted to it, the individuals, for what it is there for, viz. ’לקרא בשם ה, it wants to use it only in the service of its own name נעשה לנו שם, then the individuals arise and say: “I acknowledge no community, I acknowledge myself, and myself only”. True he is rejecting the good together with the bad, cutting himself off from the root which should hand down to him all the human wisdom from its divine source, and is throwing himself into the arms of a vague pathless subjective life, but such decentralisation is then the only means of saving humaneness in man. The subjectiveness, this feeling of oneself which names things, not according to the will of a forcing community, but just as they appear to oneself, would be the new element ’אשר בלל ה which God allowed to awake so disintegratingly in the minds and hence in the speech of mankind. The one would say: “Let us keep the old regime, the old law, that only that belongs to a man which really properly appertains to him”, the other would answer: “I know no law, what I grab, what I have is mine” etc. etc. This awakening of self-determination would be the effect of the ירידה and thereby the נבלה already accomplished. As it had already earlier said ’וירד ה and now again נרדה, and נרדה indeed as a wish (not נרד, I.L.) it seems thereby to indicate a still deeper entry into the consciousness of the people that, after all there is a power in existence above Nimrod. נרדה “I would, after all go down”. Therein lies that עיקר שכינה בתחתונים, that God’s intention and purpose is not to allow Himself to be dismissed from the minds of man, but ultimately again to let His Presence dwell in their midst, and even the slightest activity in this direction effected the נבלה of the language. Spite, obstinacy, moods etc., yea sensuality, gave things other names than the old universal way that God had named them. Thus it came about that the one no longer understood the other. The one would call something by quite a different name just out of spite, for independence shows itself in obstinacy of thought, of one’s own way of looking at things which is synonymous with obstinacy in the way one calls things. Later on, in the course of history, every centralisation begins with robbing the language of its own special peculiarities.

So that the disunion did not arise out of a number of languages but the other way round. It was the discord which first begot the disruption of the language, so that, at the beginning, the שפה אחת could still have remained, and still ונבלה שם, without climatic change, even before the scattering which ensued, in the שפה אחת there was no longer דברים אחדים. This variance in opinions afterwards drove people completely away from one another, where then the climatic differences of the regions had the influence of making them and their languages completely and organically different.

V. 8. חדל, related to חתל: to apply a bandage, חתול: the splint to prevent movement (Ezekiel 30,21). So that the underlying meaning is to check movement, to restrain, thus חדל also primarily, to discontinue an activity. Accordingly, they left off building the city. But the propensity towards it, that they took everywhere with them. Of course no more a city and a tower for the enslavement of the whole of mankind, but single cities and towers here and there, from which little Nimrods thought they could reach the skies.

With this individualising scattering of the peoples, on which indeed we believed the Noachism covenant of God with Man reckoned (see on Ch. 9,15; X,5), the introduction to the Torah, with which the Jewish thinker is to be orientated in the history of the development of mankind, comes to its conclusion. From now on, the history of one single nation, the Jewish people, is introduced, whose special mission is founded just on this description of the development of the history of the nations and their ultimate goal.

The universal history of the world is left to take its course until the time of the Prophets whose eyes were again opened to the time in which the ever-repeated downfall of all that great and small “buildings to the fame of men” will finally bring mankind to the conviction that there is only one “Name” to whose glorification mankind as a whole — individual and state — must devote the whole of their individual and joint strength in every phase of private and public life if happiness and peace is to come permanently on earth. A time which the prophet Zephania (III,9) characterises with the words: כי אז אהפוך אל עמים שפה ברורה לקרא כלם בשם ה׳ לעבדו שכם אחד: “For then will I restore to the nations a purified language (cf. ויהפד לו אלקים לב אחר, Sam. 9,9) to call them all in the Name of God to serve Him with one shoulder i.e. with united strength!” Unless we are greatly mistaken there lies herein no small confirmation of the way we have taken this whole incident. ברר, the very opposite of בלל is the separating out of a foreign element which has entered and become mixed up with what we want. Thus history begins with an infiltration into the original pure language, and will end with a refinement of it. Only so is understandable that this purification of language is put in connection with the ’לקרא כלם בשם ה, that then men will cease looking at things, and so calling them in accordance with what לעשות להם שם ,בשמם, they want them to be for their own ideas and purposes, but will look at everything objectively as it really is in accordance with God’s Will. With this submission to God, the spiritual and social unity of mankind will again be attained, the peace on earth which went astray at the first building of a tower to the glorification of Man.

Now the Torah takes us into a small narrow sphere, so that we can learn how God arranges matters. Out of the smallest, most unlikely beginning, a preceding herald and instrument for the positive development of mankind to this ultimate goal is first to be forged. The chapter concludes with a register of the generations of Shem until it comes to one simple man, Abram. He, a contemporary of an age that had carried on the נעשה לנו שם as the guiding principle of life, had made, in direct contrast, the aim of his own life, — and was to hand down to his descendants as the aim of the life of a whole nation — that ’קרא בשם ה in which mankind will ultimately find the solution to all the problems of the long long centuries of their wandering on earth. He and his descendants, by example and admonition were to keep this beacon shining on the way, so that the consciousness of the ultimate solution should never entirely disappear from the midst of the nations.

V. 10 et seq. In this register of generations we pick out primarily פלג, whose name has already been explained to us (Ch. 10,25) in connection with the event of the separation of the nations, כי בימיו נפלגה הארץ. We would remark that expressions like פלג לשונם in Ps. 55,10, בפלגות ראובן in Jud. 2,15 lead us to see, in the root פלג rather a social discord than an actual separation, so that, according to this name here too, the fundamental cause for the national upset could be found in inner spiritual differences. Also, in this register of generations lies an indication of the history of the trend of their development, similar to those of Cain and Seth above, the names: שרוג ,רעו ,פלג ,עבר ,שלח seem to suggest it. שלח again would designate letting things go, giving up the masses, the better ones retiring to themselves without hope of bringing the masses to better living. עבר would then be — in accordance with ר׳ יהודה explanation כל :(ב״ר מ״א) אברם העברי העולם כלו מעבר אחד והוא מעבר אחר — the strongest protest against the whole of the rest of the contemporary world. If it is no dream that, as we believe, the formation and alteration of the language arose from the individuals rebelling against the enforced mastery that was being introduced, it would not be impossible that the rebellion started from the descendants of Shem in whom some idea of godliness, and of the pure concept of a human being, still remained. Then, after separation had taken place in רעו ,פלג would designate those of a similar turn of mind joining together and שרוג the further branching out of these. This is, at any rate, possible.

V. 30. עקר, related to אגר: to gather in, חגר: to gird and in Chaldean, lame has the fundamental meaning of holding in, restraining forces, hence also a check in free movement (lame I.L.). Hence עֵקֶר means that point in which the forces of a movement are concentrated עקר and in Chaldean עיקר: the root, as well as checking the movement at the point from which it proceeds, עקור הנטוע, to pull out the root, and עקר: to make an animal lame. Then עקר and עקרה, one who is checked at the root of propagation, organic infertility.

V. 31. כַלָה from כלה, the one who completes, because she is the last member that completes the family of her father-in-law. Also the root כלל from which, according to Jer. 2,2, כלה seems to be derived, has the meaning to complete, to make perfect. Thus כללו יפיך in Ezekiel 27,4. The daughter-in-law enters the circle of her father-in-law, whose relation to her is חמיה, from חמה, her wall. He encompasses her protectingly within his circle. Whereas in other languages the relation of the son-in-law and the daughter-in-law to their father-in-law is expressed in the same terms, the Hebrew language looks deeper. Father-in-law and son-in-law are to one another חותן and חתן — the relationship is a mutual one “connected with each other”. But the relationship of a daughter-in-law to her father-in-law is a much more intimate one, “going into” and “accepted into”. He accepts her and “encompasses” her as the coming “completer” of his family circle.

As רמב״ן thoroughly proves, the birthplace of Terach, Nachor and Abraham was not Ur-Kasdim but Aram in which Charan also lies. Only Haran was born in Ur-Kasdim which was ארץ מולדתו.
