הרה related to אריתי מרי ודבשי ,ארה to pluck fruit, and to absorb fruit. הרה to absorb the seed of fruit in oneself. In Hiphil הורה (like הוליך from הלך) to plant a spiritual seed in someone, to teach, from which we get the word תורה the teaching.

V. 6. ענה ,תענה: to be, or to say something caused by somebody else, to answer, or to be dependent; עַנֵה, to make somebody feel their dependence. Sarah’s whole intention depended on Hagar, even as Abraham’s wife and mother of his child, remaining her slave, so that the child to be born by her could be completely treated as Sarah’s child, and Hagar’s influence on it completely countered and excluded. ותענה, so she intentionally constantly brought this dependent condition home to Hagar’s mind. But she had forgotten that what she had wished was an impossible thing viz. that a woman who had become a wife to Abraham and a mother to his child could not, on the other hand, be a slave. Abraham’s proximity and Abraham’s spirit would break the feelings of slavery, would awaken the feeling of the equality of all human beings, would arouse the urge of freedom and break all chains. Hagar would no longer tolerate to be considered as a slave.

V. 7. וימצאה, used perhaps in contrast to her flight. She had fled into the desert where she hoped that nobody would find her, above all nobody who knew her. But an angel found her. על עין she fled there because it was a well in the desert. It was העין, the well, which by reason of remembrance of this event became renowned. It was the well-known well which was all the more suitable to keep the event in the remembrance of the descendants because it was on the way to the desert of Shur, that awful, driest, most dreary wilderness, and on that account was well-known as the welcome resting place for all the caravans going into and coming out of the desert.

V. 8. — אי מזה: where is the place from which —; לאן = אנה to where, אן from root אנה the direction towards a place from which we get אניה the ship. מפני גברתי (because she is my mistress I.L.) I can, or I will, no longer be a slave.
V. 9, 10, 11. Three separate speeches. The first is the condition, the second the promise, the third the task and its result.

V. 9. “Go back of your own free will, and of your own free will submit yourself to Sarah”. The son is to mature and be born under the influence of free-willed recognition of Sarah’s authority, and grow up under the influence of Sarah’s guidance. Hagar does not move.
V. 10. “At this price you will become the ancestress of countless descendants”. Hagar does not move.
V. 11.—12. “Your descendant will become the freest man in the world”. That was sufficient. For that price she is ready to submit.

But the fundamental thought that she is to implant in her son and which is to make him so free, is: ישמעאל, the consciousness of God, of a watching Providence, that not only sees the sufferings and activities of men, but also hears, and so weighs and judges their words and feelings. ’כי שמע ה אל עניך; nowhere else do we find שמיעה used in conection with עני but always עני ;ראיה is usually something seen, not heard. But Hagar had not been illtreated. Sarah — (to fulfil her purpose in her plan I.L.) — had tried to keep her in mind of her subservient position by words, had made her feel her dependent position. Hagar’s suffering was something mental, in her feelings, that could only be heard and realised.

He will not be just אדם פרא, a free man, he will be פרא אדם, the פרא amongst mankind. פרה ,פרא ,פרע ,פרה, and so also ברח ,ברה ,ברא, all only different nuances of the basic idea of being or becoming free, unbound. פרא specially designates being free from human yoke and from the constraint of cities, hence of wild animals פרא למוד מדבר that can not bear the constraint of cities. Such a race of men who do not bow their necks to the yoke of other men or to the constraint of life, in towns, will your seed become amongst mankind. The whole fundamental character of the social life of the Ishmaelites is described by one word על פני כל אחיו — .פרא, the expression על פני has often the meaning of being contrary to, standing in the way of, limiting or hindering the point of view and tendency of others. That which one does not like to see is על פניו. Thus, מכעיסים אותי על פני (Is. LXVI.2), אלהים אחרים על פני (Ex. XX.3) שלח מעל פני (Jer. XV.1) etc. So here too, he will quietly take up and maintain his position in spite of all his brothers. Nobody will be his friend and still nobody will dare to oppose him.

V. 13. רֳאִי a noun, like חֳלִי, seeing, sight, “thou art a God of seeing, sight belongs to Thee, Thou seeth!” — ’רואי :אחרי רואי ,כי אמרה וגו can not mean anything other than “one who sees me” the present tense with the suffix, like רועי, one who shepherds me. הלום never means “here” but “up to here”, אל תקרב הלום (Ex. III.5), מי הביאך הלום (Judges XVIII.3) etc. so here literally: “Have I then also here too looked after one who still might see me?” Hagar had run away, on the whole flight she had looked back to see if anybody was following her. Then she fled into the desert, there she felt safe, there she need no longer expect that anybody would see her and there — it was brought home to her that one could flee from Man but not from God. “Right here I no longer looked around after anybody who might see me, but Thou art a God of Seeing, Thy Eye is everywhere, from Thee, one can not escape”. The angel had given her אל שומע, more, ישמעאל “the Hearing God”, “the God Who, in all the future would always be hearing, as the heritage of her son; that consciousness that lays open to God not only external happenings but also feelings and stirrings which are only revealed to the mind. This consciousness of being able to leave everything that happens and even one’s innermost self always to God’s providence was to make her son and her descendants into free beings. But Hagar had only just become consciously free. The impression had just strongly affected her that one could become free from Man but not from God, that God was One Who could see everywhere and everything. So she did not call Him אל שמע, but א׳ רֳאִי, the God of absolute sight.

V. 14. Abraham took note of the experience which Hagar had had at the spot and named the well accordingly but completed her idea by adding the word חי (from the root חײ, life). So we see this well, situated at the entry to the most terribly desolate desert, so very suitable to be the most prominent meeting-place of a Beduin people, made, by this experience of the ancestors, into a memorial for the Arab people to which everything could be attached which that race became for mankind. Here the ancestress had learnt to recognize the complete independence of God towards space — no place was beyond the Eye of God. To this the ancestor of the race added the conception of His independence towards time — no life in any age is beyond His Eye, and at the same time changed the term רֳאִי sight in general, expressing the general השגחה, to רואי “who seeth me”, the special individual providence, the השגחה פרטית. Only he who understands God as being still exactly the same God to the last grandson of the succeeding generations, Who tomorrow is as today, Who never changes, never alters His mind, Who is as near, with the same faithfulness, to the last descendant as He was to the old ancestress — only he who feels himself under the same Eye that looked on the ancestress even in the desert, only such a man understands God as חי רואי. But it is just these two thoughts: חי רואי, God as the absolute Master of space and time, and His guiding and watching Providence, these gifts of the matriarch, it is just those thoughts which all Arabian thinkers and philosophers developed in the works they gave to mankind, and which constitute the great treasury of philosophy of the Arabian people. Altogether one can see in this story of the Islamic people all the seeds which produced the salient points of their marked characteristics throughout the centuries. Hamitic sensuality, Hagar’s urge for a free life, and Abraham’s spirit (monotheism, Allah il Allah; complete trust in Providence, Kismet I.L.) are the threads out of which the Arab character is woven. The nation descended from Abraham and Hagar is one-half Jewish. God has given us. the Jewish nation, a mission which has a dual aspect, 1. אמונה, theoretical truths which we have to accept and which our minds are to develop and 2. the Law, the commandments, which in harmonious agreement with these truths form our whole life in accordance with the dictates of the Divine Will. On the one aspect, the theoretical one, the Arabic nation holds high place in the ranks of mankind. It has developed the Abrahamic thoughts of God with such fine acuteness that the thoughts of the Unity of God in the works of Jewish theological philosophers, as far as they are developed philosophically,rest predominently on the works of Arabian writers. These have the אמונה but not the מצות. It is not sufficient to have spiritual thoughts of the Unity of God,to שמע must be added ואהבת, the practical submission of all forces and efforts בכל לב נפש ומאד. And for that it is not sufficient only to be begotten and brought up by an Abraham, for that one must be born from a Sarah. The specific People of Abraham is not given the mission to be the theological philosophical herald of the Unity of God, but ’לשמור דרך ה לעשות צדקה ומשפט. and that requires the submission of all one’s forces, and above all, all one’s sensuous forces, urges and impulses, that demands the dedication of the body. One only begins to be a Jew with the dedication of all the senses of the body. Ishmael has the dedication of the mind from Abraham, but he lacks the dedication of the life of his senses from Sarah. Where a Jewish mother bears, feeds, and brings up the children, there the senses are dedicated in their very roots. Not for naught is the story of Sarah and Hagar interposed between the ברית בין הבתרים and the מילה.

V. 1. Abraham was already ninety-nine years old, a whole life lay already completed behind him, he could really have thought it was completed when he found out he was only now standing at the beginning.

This fact is important from two aspects. Some people say: “as long as one has satisfied the moral and humane demands of life, one has satisfied God’s demands too, Judaism also demands no more”. Others think: “To be a Jew is something different from being an ordinary man, it is a substitute for it”. If it did not tell us here that Abraham was already ninety-nine years old when the “founding-covenant” of Judaism, the covenant of Mila (circumcision) was concluded with him, one could have believed that all the great virtues of Abraham, of which we have learnt up till now, were somehow the result of this covenant concluded with him in earliest infancy, that the whole blossoming of this covenant consisted in these virtues. But we see that they all preceded the Mila. The demand now made on him היה תמים (“become perfect” I.L.) evidently presupposes the full accomplishment of the purely humane virtues. The covenant of Abraham is a higher perfection of the humane virtues; “You must first be a complete ordinary man if you want to be a Jew”. To be a Jew, presupposes that nothing of the purely human qualities is lacking in you. You are a long way off from being a Jew if you have only the qualities which Abraham had developed up till now. To be as kind, benevolent, humane, forgiving, unselfish, ungrasping as Abraham has shown himself hitherto is no more than the ideal of what every man, every Noachides should be. God had first led Abraham through all the educating events of his ninety-nine years of life, had first let him accomplish all that He demands from every pure human being, and only then did God appear a second time to Abraham and say to him ’אני א׳ ש etc.

From Ex. VI.13 we know that the special quality of God which was revealed to the patriarchs was expressed by this Name. Opinions differ as to the etymology of the word. It is thought to come from שדד or from די with the prefix of the relative pronoun ש. The latter is favoured by most of our sages, and the form of the word seems to point undoubtedly to that derivation. For were it to come from שדד the י would be inexplicable, whereas for the form of the relative pronoun ש with a dagesh in the following letter we have examples in בשגם ,שקמתי. Accordingly it would mean אשר די, I am the “Sufficing One” and I am “All-Sufficient”. In both these aspects our sages ז״ל discover the deepest intuitive contemplation of God. אני הוא שאמרתי לעולמי די שאלמלא שאמרתי לשמים וארץ די עד עכשיו היו מותחיו והולכין — אני הוא שאין העולם ומלואו כדי לאלוקותי — דײך שאני פטרונך ולא לך (ב״ר מ״ו) לבדך אלא דיו לעולם שאני אלקיו שאני פטרונו. “I am He Who called to My world”, sufficient! had I not called “sufficient” to heaven and earth they would be going on evolving now. I am He for Whose Divinity the whole world and all that fills it is not sufficient — for you it is sufficient that I am your Protector, and not only to you alone, but it is sufficient for the world that I am its God, that I am its Protector”.

Look about in My world! Everywhere you see stamped on the whole and on every part of it a “it is sufficient”, and this “sufficient” reveals “Me”. If heaven and earth are the product of a blind force of nature — as the old hoary wisdom of human error says they are — why do these creative forces not go on creating, what has set the end of their creation during the thousands of years of their existence, what “it is sufficient” keeps their almighty power of creation back, that they do not go on continually producing new creations! It is just this “sufficient”, that stamp of Sabbath in the Creation, which is the seal of God on heaven and earth, which makes the wisdom of men into an absurdity, which announces heaven and earth as being not the product of blind unfree physical forces, but as the work of a free-willed Master, an ’א׳ ש׳ ד One Who fixes the purpose and end of His Own Creations.

And not only the universe as a whole, every tiniest being, the smallest particle of matter given a shape and endowed with force (e.g. an atom I.L.) has He stamped with His “די״. This “די״ is the one source of its existence and of the manner of its existence. Every force is set a limit to its activity within which it is a form of the liveliest energy, and beyond which it is just nothing. Every shape sets its own boundaries (צור), is a delimitation of matter within which the forces innate in matter are confined: is perhaps just the product of the די called to that force which has found its boundaries in its lineaments. It is the Creator’s די that decides the weight and size of everything, which reveals itself in every measure, every size, every law and every purpose (cf. above on ויכולו in Ch. II.1).

And this God is not absorbed by His world. He is די for the world, but the whole world with all that it contains is not די for His Divinity. He is not only present as the Soul, the Spirit of the world, as the inherent creative force of the works of creation, as the philosophising and speculating heathen concept of the world has worked out — He has not spent Himself in accomplishing His work and become absorbed by it — as the hoary wisdom solved the riddle of the universe, but אין העולם ומלואו כדי לאלקותו external to, and above His work, and beyond His work stands the God, Who did not find His purpose at an end in the Creation of the world, but, as sufficient for His own free-willed Thoughts, sets the די on His own works.

A later opinion takes this name of God to be derived from שדד and explains it as משדד מערכות which, as already remarked though not completely justified grammatically, is a very similar conception to the one above. מערכה is the natural order of things, the laws of nature. משדד is the one who rules by his own free will over these laws which He Himself has made. This way of taking it makes the conception of God’s complete freedom of will more prominent in this Name. It prevents our conception of God from falling into that error which would identify the Creator of the world with that sorcerer’s apprentice who forgot the spell to banish the spirit he himself had called up. It shows God the Master of, and not mastered by, His own laws of nature. It is again the same truth of God not being absorbed by the world, His work, but being above it and ruling over it in Almighty free-willed power.

Accordingly: “I am the Free Almighty God, He Who has set a limit for all things, boundaries within which they have free play; conduct thou thyself before My Presence, and become perfect”. There is a difference between הלך and הלך .התהלך is not only used for the movement of men, but is any movement towards an aim. It can also be involuntary, mechanical or unconscious. Thus of rivers: והלך על כל גדותיו (Is. VIII.7). But התהלך means going your way in spite of opposition, not making it dependent on external circumstances, but being led from within yourself, i.e. a movement proceeding from your own free-willed decision. Hence only used referring to human beings or to God. Only once we find it referring to lightning, looked at as the arrows of God, אף חצציך יתהלכו (Ps. 77,18). But just by this term it is raised out of a purely physical blind movement up into a messenger of God moving in a special mission it had accepted from Him. התהלך לפני not התהלך אתי which would only mean to let himself be led by God in his lot in life, but לפני, to keep the Presence of God always in mind, here accordingly: at every step look to Him Who has set limits and boundaries for everything, who has only granted freedom within the Law.

The character which following such a path demands and forms, can be nothing other than the same which ’א׳ ש has stamped on all beings, which all the other creations have unconsciously and irrevocably but which Abraham is to make his own of his own free-will. This character of the work of the Creator is naught but הצור תמים פעלו .תמים, our sages take to mean: הצײר, the One Who forms and shapes and by that form sets size and purpose and limits to everything, thereby has stamped the character of תמים on His Work as a whole and on every part of it.

תמים, root תמם, mostly, ceasing to exist, then also ceasing to do, to be brought to the end, to have nothing more to do, to be finished. Then also applied to conditions: having nothing lacking, having been brought to the edge of perfection, having not too much and not too little, thus the תמים demanded for offerings. We have already remarked above (on ויכולו II.1) how, in the Jewish language, being completed and ceasing to exist are expressed by the same term; how everything really complete can only be one-sided, must have ceased to be anything else. If one takes תמים to be only relative as a quality of Man in relation to God, as ’תמים תהיה עם ה etc., it would designate a character that does not wish for anything else, has consideration for nothing else than: to serve God. People can easily deceive such a man, just because he has no mind for anything else and is entirely absorbed by this one effort, but nevertheless הולך בתום ילך בטח (Prov. X.9) Still, in this sense תמים would only be relatively good, there could also be a תמים לעזאזל whereas it is quite evident from here that תמים is to be taken as the superlative of good. In the basic conception of תמים the negative meaning is certainly to the fore: “so far and no farther” דמם to be silent, to keep oneself modestly in the background and wait, is related to טמם, also טמם to be inaccessibly closed. So that תמים seems to be he who, in every way goes to the border line of what is permitted and what is prohibited, but there he stops, so that he practices self control both positively and negatively. One who is תמים takes full advantage, to the full extent in every direction, of the limits which God has indicated, but never oversteps them. It corresponds to: “no more and no less”, the לא תוסיף and ‘לא תגרע (Deut. XIII.1).

So that תמים in the human character is the exact correlation of what שדי means of the Divine character. All the creations excepting Man can go no farther, the די which God has fixed for them is impassable. To the Jew it is said: Be your own “די setter” you say די where God has told you it is די. That is the whole of Judaism. The whole תורה is nothing else but God’s די for every phase of human life. Hence the Jewish term for sin, עברה, as stepping over these borders. Within the elbow-room which God has given us, everything, the life of our senses too, is holy and good. In itself, nothing in Man is absolutely good and nothing bad. No prohibition demands the complete killing of any tendency of our lives but only directs it to be kept within the given permitted limits. Only by going beyond these limits and mostly by not reaching these limits does it become sinful. Such is the Jewish fundamental nature of lawfulness. “Within the limits set by God thou shalt conduct thyself freely”. This is also the difference between the Jew Abraham and Abraham as he was hitherto. For the Abrahamitic being without this “covenant”, virtue is satisfied by simple good will. In the non-Jewish world every deed is covered by the good intention. Judaism is not satisfied by mere good intention by the כונה being good. The deed to which the good intention is directed must be a truly good one, and the criterion for the goodness of the deed is the “די״ of God, the Will of God, the Law of God. This is a truth which Reb. Jehuda Halevi has laid as the foundation for his Kuzari. Up till now Abraham was respected and valued and loved for his good heart and personality. Now something higher is demanded from him, and that is, doing all these good deeds as a duty, as a law to be obeyed, obeyed from his free-willed submission to the Law of God, so that he becomes, of his own free will that which all other creations are forced to be by their very nature. Thus our sages say: בתחלה המליכו על רמ״ג איברים ולבסוף המליכו על רמ״ח איברים אלו הן שתי עינים ושתי אזנים וראש הגויה (Nedarim 32b). Until then Abraham had complete mastery over all the parts of his body except those senses over which ordinary human beings seldom attain complete control. From now on a different condition begins. Feelings and urges which other people follow more blindly, are, in the new covenant, to be kept under the free-willed mastery of the human power of self-control. Even the most powerful urges are to be mastered. One is to say to all of them, in the name of God: די! Not merely where it is a question of being humane, but always, and in every direction Jewish men are to be godly, and only just thereby do they become complete, true human beings. On the decision to submit all one acts, of one’s own free will, under God’s direction, has God built up the whole edifice of the Jewish nation.

V. 2. ’ואתנה בריתי וגו. Make this decision to place yourself under My Law, for I would establish something between you and Me which is to be a ברית, something “absolute” on My side and on your side. Jewish destiny is not the result of the natural course of events. In the ordinary course of nature the first Jew would never have come into existence, and the last Jew would long ago have ceased to exist. יצחק, an absurd impossibility by ordinary reckoning, is the type of all Jewish history. On both sides, ביני וביניך, the historical existence which I grant you, as well as the devotion you give Me, are to be of the nature of a ברית, completely independent of, completely detached from, all external circumstances and causes.

ואתנה בריתי. The combination of ברית and נתן hardly occurs again. (once in the case of Phineas: הנני נותן לו את בריתי שלום). Otherwise establishing a covenant is always called כרת ברית or הקים ברית but never נתן ברית. It accordingly seems possible that ואתנה בריתי does not mean establishing an actual covenant but transfering an existing one to Abraham. Long before already, when God gave the world a second time to mankind, He made a covenant with mankind in general and established it as a ברית, that in spite of all future aberrations, mankind as a whole would not be destroyed, but that education would be given such a course that the חמס and השחתת דרך would become ever less and mankind ever worthier to find Paradise on earth. For this ברית for this goal which was absolutely ultimately to be reached, God had hitherto been seeking an instrument, a working-tool, and hoped now to have found one in Abraham. He says accordingly: I would like that ברית which I established with mankind to be brought to realisation through you, וארבה אותך במאד מאד to begin with you, and appoint you to be the original germ from which the whole of the return of mankind to Me will grow. You would then be the first man to be regained for that happy future, and I will guide mankind in such a way that finally all men will live in your spirit, and you will be reproduced in every living man (see on Ch. I.28). At Phineas, too, the הנני נותן לו את בריתי may have a similar explanation. Phineas, too, showed a devotion which really should have been expected from the whole community. The ברית which God had established with the whole community of Israel, He accordingly transfers quite especially to Phineas; perhaps gives that covenant to him to have it realised.

V. 3. To “throw yourself down” expresses giving up one’s independence. Throwing oneself at the same time “on one’s face”, one ceases to see, becomes purely listening, gives up one’s material and spiritual independence entirely to the one before whom one so prostrates oneself. In the same way as we are told in the visions of the angels about the Throne of God that they have their faces covered with their wings, their feet covered with their wings, and are only prepared to use their powers of flight to carry out the commands of God. By this throwing himself on his face Abraham showed the acceptance on his side of the demands of the covenant.

Whereas up till now it has been ’וירא אליו ה and ואתנה בריתי now it says וידבר אתו אלקים. Before the agreed obligation, the decision was left to Abraham’s free-willed agreement, it was only God’s wish. Had Abraham not resolved to agree he could have remained a בן נח. But once he had accepted the obligation the conditions had grown to a duty. Hence now it is as אלקים, as the God of justice and order, Who does not allow Himself and His commands to be played about with, that He says the following, and hence also לאמר, for Abraham to transmit further.

Verses 4—8 give the one side of the covenant, what is to be expected from God; verses 9—14, on the other hand, what Abraham and his descendants have to do. ’אני הנה וגו. I, on My part, from this minute give you My absolute promise that you will become a “father of the thronged masses of the nations”. This can hardly refer to the physical descendants of Abraham, they are referred to in verse 6. The name Abraham by which this promise was to be perpetuated also proves that here it is not to be taken in the physical sense, otherwise it would say אבהם and the ר would be without meaning and in the way. But אב המון גוים is equivalent to אבר המון גוים. But אבר is the wing, metaphorically the power of soaring, from which we get אביר, thus God is called אביר יעקב, He Who ישאהו על אברתו. In that sense too Abraham is אביר הגוים, he is the lever who raises them to spiritual and moral heights. Without Abraham’s spirit the masses of the nations are a המון, a mixed-up swaying throng, nobody knows from where they come, nobody knows where they are going, their movement lacks all direction and purpose. They are no צבא, no mass of people formed into a united group around a common central directing force for a common purpose, but a המון, a disorderly muddled mass. Abraham brings a centralising spirit to them, becomes thereby their spiritual father. It is possible too that that is why the ordinary אבי המון גוים is not used, but אב המון גוים.

V. 6. But for this purpose of raising mankind in general to their spiritual and moral height, and apart from this universal importance, My ברית ensures you something special: you yourself will become the ancestor of a great nation. This nation which is to walk in the van of the general mass of nations as the model nation, is itself to figure as גוים as a plurality, as several nations. It will consist of tribes, each one of which is to show its own special natural character (soldiers, sailors, teachers, students, husbandmen, merchants, priests, confectioners, etc. etc. I.L.) and thus demonstrate factually that the covenant of God, the godly calling of mankind, is not attached to any special profession and not hindered by any. Not lion-hearted courage, not business acumen, not the urge to study etc. etc. form the condition for, and neither are they any hindrance to, the mission of Abraham to mankind. A military nation like Judah, a nation of mercantile marine like Zebulun, a nation of scholarship like Issachar, of agriculture like Asher etc. etc. all are called upon to make the common calling which Judaism teaches, a reality in the activities of their different lives. No church, but a nation was what God wished to found with Abraham, a nation for the whole multitude of nations, that was why this nation itself was to consist of tribes with every kind of different national characteristics of גוים. Thus the Jewish Nation promised to Jacob — to whom indeed no other nation can be thought of — is expressly called גוי וקהל גוים (Gen. XXXV.11) גוי וקהל גוים יהיו ממך, on the one hand it is a גוי, a closed unit and on the other consists of קהל גוים.

V. 7. והקימתי את בריתי, the realisation of this destiny which I have fixed for your descendants will be no easy task. It will meet with many obstacles and endure many struggles, but I will “keep it established”, will form, guide, purify, educate, your children after you until they become My children.

V. 8. Then only, it says, after I have won your descendants to be My People, will I give them the land in which you have tarried as a stranger and there will prove Myself to them as a guiding, protecting, providing God.

V. 9. ואתה is in reciprocal relation to the preceding אני of V.4. תשמר: I, God had said, will keep My covenant established in all circumstances, even if conditions should arise which could bring it to ruin, but אתה את בריתי תשמר you have to take care of My ברית, it is up to you and your descendants to see that it does not come into such danger. This duty is encumbent on all Abraham’s descendants. These descendants have to thank this duty undertaken by Abraham not only for their spiritual and moral calling but even for their physical and material very existence. Their whole existence proceeded from this duty undertaken. Without it no Isaac would have been born. They only came into existence under this condition, and only breathe as the children of this covenant. Their very existence itself makes them in duty bound to keep this covenant.

V. 10. In a striking manner the Mila itself is first called ברית, so that the performance of it itself seems to be fulfilling the covenant, and then, in the following verse it is declared to be אות ברית, the sign of the covenant, as a symbol to represent the ברית, so that the fulfilment of the covenant itself must be something transcending the mere act of the circumcision. These expressions used at the first specific Jewish law — and a symbolic Law at that — could be of the highest importance for the correct appreciation of all similar laws that follow. And indeed in two ways.

At symbolic commands, not only is the perpetuation of the idea of which the act is symbolic important and necessary, but in the first instance the actual performance of the prescribed procedure is an inviolable law of God, which can never be dispensed with or its place taken by keeping the idea. Not performing the act is equivalent to denying the idea. He who neglects the sign of the covenant has broken the covenant (V.14) and making the sign itself is already called caring for, guarding the covenant (V.10) שמירת הברית.

On the other hand, performing the act, only then achieves its full purpose when it does become an אות a symbol, if it is taken to heart as such and the idea it expresses becomes a reality for us. But doing the act itself still remains the first carrying out of the command of God. What the act is to accomplish is, that through it the idea is constantly expressed by us as a declaration of God, and as such is to be firmly held, kept and constantly repeated and revived for ourselves and others.

First of all the command is given in three sentences: המול לכם כל זכר (V.10), ונמלתם את ערלתכם (V.11), ובן שמנת ימים ימול (V.12). First the command to the nation המול לכם כל זכר, the nation is to be responsible that לכם, everybody who belongs to you becomes circumcised. This then has the result ונמלתם, that every one of us has the Mila performed on himself, ’והיה לאות וגו, so that it can be a sign of the covenant with God for him; and moreover בן שמנת ימים, this is to be done at the age of eight days, and not only on those who are descended from Abraham but also on all those who become members of his household. Only in verse 13 is the command given to the father, and the duty placed on him to perform the Mila on his children, and indeed, highly significantly, not as a father on his son, but as the representative of an Abrahamitic house on those born to his household. Every child of such a household is born to, and acquired by, the Abrahamitic community, and every representative of an Abrahamitic house has to see to it that the Mila is performed on every male member of his house for that community. Finally V.14 makes every descendant of Abraham himself responsible for having the Mila performed on himself, and declares the neglect of it as being on his part a breaking of the covenant and losing the justification of existence amongst the Abrahamites.

מקור נפעל ,המול לכם from מול, equally so ימול definitely from מול, and also וימל את בשר ערלתם of V.23. Probably the other forms of the verb, — נמול in V.26 and נמלו — which occur have come from the same root.

But מול by no means generally means to cut, to circumcise, it only occurs in this sense referring to Mila. מול means “opposite”. והוא יושב ממולי (Numb. XXV.15); אמילם (Ps. CXVIII.10) “it is in the Name of God that I oppose them”. So that מול as a verb means oppose, restrict, limit, and if when used in connection with ערלה it means cut — for which we also have a confirmation in Ex. IX.25 ותכרת את ערלת בנה — the actual cutting is only the means, the purpose and intention is to oppose, to limit the ערלה, more correctly the בשר ערלה, by cutting it off. Removing the ערלה to oppose it, to restrict it to due limits. The ערלה is cut off, the בשר which otherwise would be בשר ערלה is thereby מול, restricted, it is opposed.

If we compare the expressions: ערלת אזנם ,ערל שפתים (Jer. VI.10), שתה גם אתה והערל (Habak. II.16), ערל לב, finally the designation of fruit for the first three years as ערלה, it is evident that ערל designates the condition in which people are denied mastery over something to which they are really meant to have mastery. ערל לב, he who has not mastery over the inclinations and urges of his heart. הערל, the condition of complete deadening of conscience, in which all self-control has been given up. In our relation to the fruits of the first three years we are ערלים, they are in a condition of ערלה, withdrawn from our use. The opposite of ערלה seems to be הכנעה, bending, bowing down, submission, או אז יכנע לבבם הערל (Levit. XXVI.41); and here מילה, literally, opposing, relegating to its limits.

ערל בשר is he who has no control over his body. This body of ours is not meant to be master but rather מבשר ,בשר, servitor and herald of the soul. But if it does not submit itself to the morally free spirit, then it is in a condition of ערלה, is בשר ערלה, and the act which is to express opposition to it, the free-willed human energy opposing the unruly body, is called מילת בשר ערלה. It does not say ימול את ערלת בשרו ,ומלתם את ערלת בשרֹכם but the other way round, בשר ערלתו ,בשר ערלתכם. The uncircumcised body does not bear the sign of submission. With cutting away the foreskin the whole body receives the stamp of submission to the spirit carrying out the Divine Law of morality. It is on the body in the first instance, not on the mind, that God founded His Covenant first of all. The Jewish covenant of God knows no splitting apart of the human being, that the spirit, the soul, the mind should soar upward to lofty thoughts and noble conceptions while the body may wallow in the mire of sensuality. It rather demands as the very first condition, the moral submission of all the bodily urges and only allows a true godly life to blossom out of a truly pure life of the senses.

מילה accordingly, is in truth nothing but the symbolic expression of the duty להתהלך לפני א׳ שדי ולהיות תמים, to tread the path, with free-willed moral energy before the Presence of the God Who has fixed His די for everything, and positively and negatively to fulfil His Law in keeping within the limits it sets. מילה is the די of שדי for our body.

המול לכם כל זכר, this perpetuation of the fundamental condition of the Abrahamitic covenant of God is to be performed on the body of that sex which, as זכר (see above Ch. I.21) is appointed to be the bearer of the spiritual traditions of mankind, and, accordingly of the special Abrahamitic tradition. Not like in common Romanic and Teutonic language where “male” is characterised as the “strong one’, in our language it is characterised as the “remembering one”, so that the duty of ת״ת, studying the Law, devolves primarily on him, whereas the female sex is given the great task of forming and directing the earthly home as a place in which the godly spiritual, joined to all the earthly material, lives a life of blossoming and development.

V. 11. Here a difference is made between what the act itself actually is, and what it means when it has been performed on our body. In the moment when the community of Israel, or as its nearest representatives to the child, the father, with the sharp knife stamps the די on the child, he marks his child as being destined to obey א׳ שדי, that is שמירת הברית carrying on the tradition of the duties of the covenant. But thereby, ’ונמלתם וגו we shall all have the Mila on us, והיה לאות ברית and it is to be a sign for us, a constant reminder of our connection with God and our duty to Him, never to become ערל בשר, never unbridled, dissolute, but to tread even with the most powerful urges, with the whole of our bodily senses, the path which the God Who sets the limits and purpose of everything, fixes for us. Not כריתה, annulment, abolishment but “limitation” is the fundamental idea of the covenant of God. To the Jewish covenant of God, celibacy and castration are as grievous excesses as debauchery and licentiousness. To be a Jew means making the most sensuous life, kept within the precribed moral limits, holy to God.

V. 12.—13. We have tried to give a copious detailed explanation of the institution of Mila and the meaning of the various procedures and laws concerning it, in vols. 4 and 5 of the Jeshurun and would refer to that, especially with regards to the law of its having to be performed on the eighth day (in special cases, immediately on the first day). (Also transcribed in the article “Grundlinien einer judischen Symbolik” on p. 269 et seq. in vol. III of Gesammelte Schriften. I.L.)

V.14. He Who, by neglecting the Mila, cuts himself off from his past, just thereby also cuts himself off from his future. He who acknowledges that his existence only sprang from the covenant of Abraham — as it actually did — and feels himself in duty bound to carry on in that covenant, and by Mila gives the sanctioning expression of this acknowledgment to devote the life of his senses to the terms of that covenant, to such a one a future in this life and the next beckons. A future in which to live his life out here below, to continue living on in children after him, and when his life here has been completed, להאסף אל עמיו, to be gathered, in the true eternal home, to those of his people who have preceded him there. But he who, by scorning the Mila, forswears the root of his past and denies the calling of his present, such a one destroys his own future, ונכרתה הנפש ההיא מעמיה he has — as far as lies in his power — את בריתי הפר, not destroyed, that is beyond the power of all the efforts of human beings, and הפר indeed does not mean that, but made the covenant ineffective for himself.

V. 15. Up till now the covenant was, as it were, made solely with Abraham, and only the male descendants are thought of as factors of this particular covenant. But here Sarah is called upon in completely equal worthiness and importance as the second, no less essential factor of this whole covenant-promise, and just as Abraham’s significance in this covenant was to be perpetuated by a change of his name to Abraham, so here, henceforth is the equal essential importance of Sarai to be perpetuated by changing her name to Sarah.

שרה — שרי. The usual explanation of this change is taken to be that Sarai designates “my princess” as applying only to Abraham, her husband, and Sarah “princess”, having general universal meaning. But this overlooks the fact that if the suffix י- was pronominal it would not mean my princess but my princes, or, at most, as pluralis majestatis my prince and so could not possibly apply to the feminine gender, which would have to be שרתי or שרותי. But rather the suffix י— in שרי seems to be not pronominal but a noun-ending from the root שרה, like דוי from יעלוז שדי ,דוה from שדה, and שרי and שרה differ only in that שרי is derived from שרה, and שרה is the feminine of שר from the root שור.

We have three roots for the conception of ruling, being a prince: שור from which we get שר the usual expression for “prince”; שרה from which we get שרית ,המשרה; and שרר from which we get השתרר עלינו. All three have the idea of “prince”, but look at it from a different aspect. שרר related to זרר and צרר, both of which mean to press together, to compress, the first in a milder, the second in a more forcible degree. Between them both comes שרר, which accordingly looks on the power of ruler as suppression and force and so only occurs in reproach (Numb. XVI.13) and in להיות כל איש שרר בביתו (Esther I.22) where it always means unlimited power.

שרה, related to סרח to be longer, סרח העודף, and to השתרע ,שרע to extend oneself, to stretch out, also to זרע, to strew, disseminate, to be effective from a distance and זרע the outstretched arm of power. So that שרר and שרה are conceptions both of which refer more to the greatness the power, including the force of a superior and שרי Sarai from שרה would be the one who has the upper hand, the superior.

שור on the other hand, from which we get the ordinary שר only occurs elsewhere as the root of משורה, measure. And not measure of length but of circumference, periphery, it is the inclusion of all that belongs together and the exclusion of all that does not belong to it. שר formed from this root would look at the prince as the one who keeps the bounds, sets the bounds, keeps everything back to its due measure. For שר is never the highest but always a high personage under the highest who has to superintend a certain sphere of conditions, to keep and develop these in a given prescribed order. So we find שר הטבחים ,שר המשקה ,שר האופה etc.

Looked at more closely we find from the words of our sages that משורה primarily designates a smallest measure 1/36 of a לוג — the smallest, most accurate measure for very valuable things, for only for such valuable things would one use such a tiny measure. In this sense it is also used for the finest testing of the smallest and finest nick in the blade of a knife which requires the keenest sense of touch הרגשה by the term סר סכינא which also comes from this root שור. So that — applying this conception in a social sense — the real שרים the true nobility in a people, would be those that set the measure, the tone, for all that is becoming, noble and moral, who have the most important moral influence in the nation, who do not seek to be מדה, the measure, the pattern of the material but משורה, the finest delicate measure for the spiritual moral, for which the grosser minds have no measure. The true שר does not become a שר through birth, wealth etc., but by the spiritual and moral degree of perfection of himself, by the moral “delicacy” of feelings and character combined with power.

Applied to the change of name of our ancestress this would tell us: she is no longer to be called Sarai — superior, overtowering — for she is Sarah, one who sets the tone, the measure, she is that which the wife of an Abraham should be, what Jewish women, if they are worthy daughters of Sarah, always are. Above, to Abraham it was said: “thou shalt no longer be called Abram for Abraham יהיה שמיך, shall thy name be, for from now on I have destined thee to be “Abraham”; this is a destiny which thou hast not yet attained but which thou shalt attain”. But here it says: thou shalt no longer call thy wife Sarai, כי שרה שמה for Sarah is her name, she is Sarah, the tone-setter, the regulator, who has in her heart the most delicate הרגשה, the most delicate feelings for the right measure of what is right and good and beautiful, what is praiseworthy and holy, practices it herself and with the greatest delicacy applies it to others. And this she has not to become, she is all this already.

The pure feminine sex, if it descends from Sarah, does not require the external sign of the covenant with שדי, the God Who “sets the measure”. It itself bears this warning of די within itself, in the pure feeling of the limits set by its צניעות with which the true Jewish women are filled. She has the tendency by itself to submit herself to all the laws of purity and godliness, and demands such submission from all that come into contact with her. Where a pure “Sarah” reigns as wife and mother, nothing low and common dare show itself, she is the spirit of godliness, purity and good breeding. And this is so important, as all what follows quite specially shows, how it is not sufficient only to have an Abraham for a father if one does not also have a Sarah for a mother. The spiritual may come from the father, but the fine feeling of the measure of what is due and befitting and the feeling for what is morally correct and nice is what comes from the pure true woman. An אשת חיל like Sarah, say our sages, is the crown of her husband הוא נתעטר בה he becomes distinguished through her, but she does require him to receive the wreath of fame.

V. 16. Just as I blessed you that you shall repeat yourself in your descendants and live on in them, so also do I bless Sarah. To plant a people for Himself, God did not only take a man who was to repeat himself in the sons, but also a woman who was to be repeated in the daughters. To plant a people of God the right fathers and mothers must be won, Abrahams must find Sarahs and not unite themselves to Hagars. Accordingly the same covenant is repeated here with Sarah as had already above been promised to Abraham. וגם, is added, I have already assigned a son to you from her. In the covenant I concluded with you I had already reckoned on Sarah. The descendants promised to you could only be promised to you from Sarah. Without her I could not have made My covenant even with you. Regarding the daughters Sarah gets blessed separately, regarding the sons she was already included in the blessing to Abraham. “She shall become nations”, her character shall live on in the tribes of the promised nation. מלכי עמים. With great nicety it does not say here מלכי גוים but מלכי עמים shall come from her, not the leaders of nations towards the outer world, but the leaders of nations towards their internal, social life. She would become גוים and the עמים-leaders would come from her. Sarah’s influence in the appearance of the tribes to the world as גוים would also be apparent. That the sons of the nation are healthy, brave, and strong is to no small degree inherited from the mother. And even if our women do not actually become queens, do not appear directly in public life, still their spiritual and moral influence does make a definite impression on public life in general, נודע בשערים בעלה, by the mildness, carefulness, and consideration with which public affairs are conducted. That there were שרים and נשיאים in Israel who were self-controlled and set an example of moderation not only in external affairs as the representatives and deliverers of the nation, but, by their example, led the way in the internal life of the nation, is an inheritance not only from Abraham but no less from Sarah.

So that if the beginning of the chapter shows us the זכרים as the זוכרים and מזכירים, as responsible for handing on and handing down the spiritual heritage, here, the feminine sex, who certainly are not called on to make the decisions in the “great” national matters, are given the great mission to impress the seal of humaneness on all those “small matters” which nevertheless have such deep penetrating effect on the life of the nation.

V. 17. It has been thought that the only way to take ויצחק here is as an expression of joy, but the meaning of צחק throughout the תנ״ך by no means concedes this supposition. Even שחק is not really an expression of joy but of laughter, and, indeed, predominantly of jeering, depreciative laughter, or a joke or a game, but not actually joy. But צחק is used without exception for ironic laughter, laughter that has in it a certain denying, condemnation, of the matter which excited the laughter. In the next verse it says in exactly the same manner, referring to Sarah, ותצחק שרה, and this was certainly no expression of joy, otherwise she would not have denied it, nor have been reproached for it.

שאג ,צעק ,שחק ,צחק are clearly phonetically related roots, and still they have apparently opposite meanings, those with ע and א as the middle letter meaning to cry out, and those with ח, to laugh. In what does the common underlying conception of these apparently completely different conceptions lie? Both are caused by noticing or feeling contrasts, i.e. the pairing of unbecoming or incompatible objects. Looked at objectively they produce laughter, subjectively, pain, crying out. Noticing such a contrast on something which is dissociated from ourself, or which at any rate has no relation to us at the moment, makes us laugh; but a ridiculous contrast affecting ourself, or someone with whom we identify ourself, pains us and makes us cry out. A small child in a full-bottomed wig, a grey-haired old man dressed as a baby, etc., causes laughter. Equally so, the complete disproportion, the complete incongruity of the expectation of an undertaking or of a performance to the means available for it, or of the performance to the expectation. To want to empty out the sea with a nutshell, or a grown-up person toddling like an infant — providing we do not participate in the shame by feeling ourselves identified with him, in which case we should “cry out”, — etc. etc., all cause laughter. (Even שחק, joyful laughter, which occurs is only produced by the perception of some opposition which has been overcome, something which has happened beyond one’s expectation etc. etc. Even שַׂחֵק which occurs in reference to races, gymnastic exercises, and music seems to have its root in the joy of having overcome opposing difficulties, and so would have a striking similarity to that other term for musical virtuosity: נצח).

In any case צחק is produced only by noticing something which strikes as ridiculous. But where, in the whole world, is there any greater absurd contradiction than the expectation that a hundred year-old man and his ninety year-old wife, who have never had a child in the course of their long married life, now, practically at the end of their lives, should get a son! And then, to expect a great, world-conquering nation to arise, to place the hopes of the whole future of mankind on this late-born only child — whose very existence was not to be expected, and in any case would be early orphaned! That surely is — only taking the ordinary natural course of events into consideration — an absolute absurdity, placing the very greatest expectations on the very smallest, almost non-existent beginning.

This contrast was so great that even an Abraham, with all his full confidence in God — as was shown by his falling on his face — could not help laughing at the absurdity of the idea of himself and Sarah still getting a baby. And this laughter was — and is — so important that it is again brought into prominence with Sarah and was to be perpetuated for all future generations in the name of the promised child.

According to all the natural conditions of cause and effect, the whole beginning of the Jewish people, its history, its expectations, its hopes, its whole life based on these hopes must appear as the most unwarranted laughable pretention. It only makes sense, yea it can then be reckoned on with certainty, when it reckons on the deeply infringing, completely free almighty will, and free-willed almighty power of a free-willed Almighty God, as the basis of its opinion.

That was to be brought home to the minds of our ancestors already beforehand, and that fact was to remain in the minds of all their descendants. That was why God waited for the first seed of this nation to be laid until the “absurd” age of its ancestors, that was why He waited to fulfil His promise until all human hopes of its realisation had ended. For it was a question of creating a nation, which from the beginning to the end of its existence was to be, even by its very existence, in opposition to all the ordinary laws of world-history, an intimation of God in the midst of mankind, and therefore up to the present day, to the narrow-minded deniers of God, appears as the most absurd absurdity. The loud laugh that has followed the path of the Jews throughout the course of their history is a true proof of the Divine nature of this path, it does not disturb them as they were prepared for this laughter beforehand.

V. 18. The first feeling was a joyful one but the second thought was a painful one. How unsuitable must the child be that was already there, that, to found the promised future, which was only to be formed by one child, such overpowering and changing the ordinary conditions of nature was necessary. Hence the utterance לו ישמעאל יחיה לפניך. O that Ishmael might live before Thy Presence! Might not he be able to carry on the promise, satisfy Thy demand להתהלך לפניך, at least partly to live up to it, to have part of the promise, even if he did not walk always before Thee, at least could he not live before Thy Presence!

V. 19. אבל .אבל to mourn, אפל darkness, אול from which אולי perhaps, to doubt, is derived, all three express an unclear condition, אפל, physically, אבל, disturbed, unclear, in one’s feelings, אול in one’s mind, אבל always opposes the trend of thought expressed, limiting it: but, nevertheless. So here, too, “not so”, the way that Abraham wished that the future of Ishmael might develop would not be realised.

V.20. ברכתי אותו ,שמעתיך. The guarantee for this lies already in his name. And this I will continue to do. But that ברית, that absolute promise, which I have made the turning-point for the development of the whole of mankind, that I will only fulfil with the “Isaac” born from Sarah, and his descendants.

נשיאים, the Jewish conception of a nation does not find its summit in שרים but in נשיאים. They נשיאים, like clouds, are only raised on high and suck sap and power from the nation, only to shower it back to fructify and strengthen the nation above which and by which they have been raised. They are borne bearers.

V. 23. בעצם, on that very day, there was no question with him of any deliberation, and as he did, so did all his household join him בעצם היום הזה. Our sages take it that wherever it says בעצם היום הזה it means in broad daylight. It would then be stressed here that Abraham performed this act, by which he placed himself in the sharpest contrast to the whole of the rest of mankind, not secretly but openly and publicly. Apart from that, Mila may not be done at night, but pertains to the wakeful human life in clear daylight. It is no secret mysterious rite, no “blood-ritual” dedicated to the dark powers of Nature ruling the night side of life. It is to the א׳ שדי, to Him Who has free control and rule over these dark powers which He has created, that Mila is to dedicate men, is to call them up to Him even with their darkest urges into the bright height of conscious, free-willed, unforced, moral life. It is not a completion or supplement of the actual physical birth, but is the octave of it, the second, higher, day of birth, the entry of man into the life of completely free, unforced moral activity. Physical birth pertains to the night — מלאך הממונה על הריון לילה שמו — mila, birth as a Jew — to the day.

V. 1. וירא אליו. Gods Presence is everywhere, but it is not apparent to everybody. Only after an act of devotion such as Abraham had just performed, and as he was constantly performing, does it become really apparent to human beings. כחם היום, the heat of the day would drive people indoors into the shaded rooms. But Abraham — and אליו joins it directly to the preceding and makes the following directly connected with it — so that the pain and weakness from the Mila just recently performed must be added, Abraham did not seek the shade, did not allow himself this relief, but looked out for travellers, with the burning sun beating down on their heads, to invite them to the hospitality of the shade of his tent. Nothing was immediately told to Abraham at this visitation. What God really was to tell him we learn later on: ’וה׳ אמר המכסה וגו the revelation of the decision to destroy Sodom.

This is the first time in which we see Abraham standing before God really as an actual נביא to whom He is מגלה סודו אל עבדיו הנביאים. This degree Abraham had only reached as a result of the Mila. Let us consider the circumstances in which God made this revelation to Abraham and ascertain its connection with them.

God wished to reveal to him the downfall and ruin of the richest, most luxurious cities of the land which was to be the future country of the nation which was promised to him. God definitely says:- because Abraham was to be the ancestor of such a nation. Personally, for his own sake, Abraham would not have required this revelation of the cause for the impending deplorable downfall of the prosperous smiling province of towns. He, himself was already in the sharpest contrast to the Sodomite character and the Sodomite views on life. The scene itself in which the revelation found him proves how little the revelation was required for him himself. The man who was sitting in the burning sun in front of his door to look out for weary wanderers, to whom he then asks, as if begging for a favour, to be allowed to show them hospitality, that man does not need to be warned by the terrible fate of Sodom and Gemorrah against the frame of mind of the inhabitants of Sodom and Gemorrah. But, so that in the future none of his descendants in that same luxurious land should grow luxuriantly to the same frame of mind, but that the Abrahamitic frame of mind should remain the unlosable inheritance of the Abrahamitic children and childrens’ children, that, in the future, luxury and plenty do not bury and destroy the God-serving universal benevolence of the spirit of Abraham, in short, that the People of Abraham remain for ever in such contrast to the Sodomite principles of life as their ancestor showed so gloriously, for that, the downfall of Sodom, and Abraham sitting before his tent, are placed in one picture in the minds of his descendants.

How this inheritance of Judaism and its bearers, the Jews, have been falsely and maliciously charged with its very opposite! How these “circumcised ones” are supposed to imagine themselves the favoured “only ones” of their God. How just this segregating sign is supposed to strip them of all cosmopolitan feelings and thoughts for mankind in general, and to constrict the God of all human souls to the exclusive God of their corner of the world, and to the national God of their race!

And now there sits the first circumcised Jew! and where? “in the groves of Mamre”. Still among Aner, Eshcol and Mamre (who were not אנשי בריתו (members of his alliance I.L.) but בעלי ברית אברהם the lords who had accepted him in their alliance, and “although circumcised” he remained in his behaviour to the non-Abrahamitic world entirely unaltered. Abraham’s one worry was, — so those old rabbis, those true sons of Abraham, teach — and this drove him out into the burning sun, that now, after his circumcision, people might draw away from him. They teach this, to impress on his sons by Abraham’s example, the dictum גדולה הכנסת אורחים יותר מקבלת פני שכינה “to receive wanderers hospitably is greater than to stand before the Presence of God”. And what kind of wanderers! uncircumcised idolaters — for no others could Abraham expect — Abraham hurries away from before God to practice on them the duty of brotherly love! And how does he practice it! Nobody could rush more eagerly to obtain a prospective prize than here Abraham does to seize the opportunity, as the first circumcised Jew, to show himself a man to his brother man. Wife and child, the whole household he hustles into activity, has everything prepared afresh — as if otherwise there was nothing in his tent wherewith to offer refreshment to three wanderers — to wait on the first guests who present themselves to him as the first נמול! All this shows his joy at the removal of his worry that he might now be isolated which our sages ז״ל — the true heirs of his spirit and feelings — read so deeply and truly out of his heart.

The picture comes immediately following the Mila. The Abrahamites flourishing in the circumcision-isolation are to be the most humane mortals. They form the most definite contrast to the world in general but nevertheless they are always to be found ready for all general humane purposes. For fostering such humaneness they are set apart, and as the herald of this spirit Abraham, above all, proved himself as אב and אבר of המון גוים as the “spiritual father and the inspirer of soaring to the heights” (אבר = wing I.L.) of the masses of humanity.

And not for nothing did Abraham hasten into the glowing sunshine in front of his tent. If his sons, the defamed Jews, have inherited anything from him, this spirit of general benevolence and universal charity they certainly have had as their heritage from him. That, at least, has never been denied of them. Where open hearts, open houses, open hands are sought for, where readiness for sacrifice of time, energy and money for general humane purposes is required — and thank God, a spark of the teachings of Abrahm has not fallen in vain in the lap of mankind, and these are also to be found in non-Abrahamitic circles — even today, even the disparagers of Judaism turn in the first place to Jews.

The sequence of the story requires one further assumption. We see that the visit to Abraham had the primary purpose of announcing a son to be born to Sarah. Although Abraham had already been informed of it, it seems that he did not feel he had the right to tell Sarah (at the giving of the covenant God had said לאמר but not at the communication regarding Sarah). It seems that the intention was that Sarah should hear the news that she was to become a mother just accidently so that the surprising abnormality should strike her the more suddenly, and to her too — as actually happened — should at first appear ridiculous. We have already remarked on the significance of this “laughter” — we do not seem able to get away from this laughter at Isaac’s birth, Abraham laughed, Sarah laughed, כל השומע יצחק, the whole world laughed — and so it seems that the mother, as well as the father, were to be deeply impressed by, and at all future care and bringing up of the child, always to keep in mind, how they themselves, when they first heard of the expected event found the very thought of it “laughable”.

V. 2.—3. If the word אדני in the third verse were חול and so would mean “my master” then the וירא in the first verse would be simply introductory, and would say: God appeared to him as he was just sitting before his tent in the glowing sun to look out for travellers, whom he then saw and offered hospitality. Then the appearance of God actually would only have occurred after their departure, (V.20). But if the word is קדש, the Name of God, which both the punctuation and also that the address is made in the singular, indicates and which is also accepted as הלכה (all the special precautions which have to be taken when a Name of God is written in the scrolls of the Torah I.L.) then the great sentence proclaiming the superior greatness of active deeds of brotherly love of mankind even over the intuitive vision of God, is sanctioned as a Jewish maxim. Then the first verse, וירא etc. is not just an introduction to the story but is the beginning of it. God appears to him to make a revelation to him. But he is just engaged with seeking an opportunity to exercise hospitality. Simultaneously with the appearance of the vision he sees men whom he can serve with brotherly love, he hurries away to meet them, and while he prays in his heart to his God — Whose commands he is just hurrying to fulfil in active deeds — not to depart from him before he has fulfilled this duty, he says to the travellers יקח נא etc. Cf. in V.22 ’ואברהם עודנו עומד לפני ה.

Whether one prefers the one or the other interpretation, in any case, the fact remains that God revealed Himself to Abraham while he was engaged in active work of hospitality, or that Abraham proceeded to such activity at the moment when God revealed Himself to him. This fact is of extraordinary import regarding the true nature of Jewish prophesy. How greatly one is inclined to relegate prophesy, our prophesy, to the category of exaggerated enthusiasm, auguries, extasies, clairvoyance etc. etc.! Finally extasy becomes just a preliminary to prophesy, and prophesy merely a higher stage of extasy. Even Jewish philosophic writings are not free from the idea that so-called התבודדות, abstraction in space and mind, isolation of man and thought, leads to prophesy, to the revelation of God. And yet, what a gulf yawns between all that and real true prophesy. It is not abstract contemplation, but fresh pulsating faithful-to-God active life that attains proximity to God. Our prophesy is not the product of a sick imagination, of an excited abnormal condition, it pertains to the healthy, active, cheerful, wide awake life, as indeed our sages expressed it:- “not slackness torpidity and depression, also not hilarity and levity or foolishness are the conditions in which the spirit of God comes upon a man, but it is in the joy of mitzvas, in the joy that comes from true, God-serving deeds אין השכינה שורה לא מתוך עצלות ולא מתוך עצבות ולא מתוך שחוק ולא מתוך קלות ראש ולא מתוך שיחה ולא מתוך דברים בטלים אלא מתוך שמחה של מצוה (Sabbath 30b). And if the Word of God describes one degree of prophesy as פה אל פה אדבר בו ומראה ולא בחידות and another as במראה אליו אתודע בחלום אדבר בו (Numb. XII.6, 8), in this latter too dreams are only a medium used for God’s communications to Man and far removed from the condition of visionary entranced men, for God choses for His instrument only a strong rich, wise and modest man אין הקב״ה משרה שכינתו אלא על גבור ועשיר וחכם ועניו (Nedarim 38a). Here we see that the practical most complete clarity of mind furthest removed from all idea of visionary was the condition in which Abraham here becomes a נביא.

V. 5. כי על כן, a form of conjunction difficult to explain. It seems that it is to be taken as elliptical: — for therefore (do I do this or do I wish this etc.) because…etc. When it is used it always seems to introduce a reason for the request or the activity which is different from what would have been supposed. Thus כי על כן ידעת חנותנו במדבר (Numb. X.31), “not (as you would think I.L.) for your advantage, but therefore (am I asking you to remain with us) because you are acquainted with every spot in the wilderness where God might order us to encamp”. כי על כן לא נתתיה לשלה בני (Gen. XXXVIII.26). She is more righteous than I am, she was only led by pure motives “for therefore (did she do this) because I had not given her to my son”. כי על כן ראיתי פניך כראות פני אלקים (Gen. XXXIII.10). For (not because you might really require it) but therefore, because I would like to express my acknowledgment to you. Thus here too: “Not because you are really in need, but therefore, because you passed my tent, and my tent wants to prove itself hospitable to every one that passes by.”

V. 6. קמח סלת .שלש סאים קמח סלת a combination that is not found elsewhere. קמח is the inferior kind of flour, סלת the better. Coarser and finer presents a wrong picture, for according to the process described in Menachoth 76b סלת would be the inner best kernel, freed, by repeated sieving, from the inferior קמח which passes through the sieve as fine dust, which also explains the saying (in the ethics of the fathers V. 18) “A sieve which lets out the coarse flour and retains the fine flour”. But we know from Menachoth that, for the shewbread, out of the one סאה (⅓ Epha) one tenth of an epha of the finest flour was obtained. But one tenth of an epha corresponds to the Omer which was the normal measure of the standard daily meal of each person (also significantly the מהרי שלש .(שיעור חלה סאים קמח סלת seems therefore to mean: quickly sieve the very best out of three סאה mixed flour, this would then yield one עשרון for each guest, a quantity which would be entirely in accordance with Abraham’s sense of due proportion.

V. 8. חלב, related to חלף change. Milk is blood changed to feeding material which in its turn is changed to blood, a cycle of blood to blood via milk. What חלב is for the young, the food set aside for its nourishment, חֵלֶב is for the old: feeding material set aside for future requirement, reserve capital stored-up.

V. 9 אֹליֹוֹ. The dots on איו, according to Baba Metzia 87a, are to remind us, that, while it is correct etiquette for male guests to enquire after the lady of the house, to whom indeed they probably owe the greatest thanks for their entertainment, this should be done through the husband, but they should not directly ask to see their hostess personally. This is probably why the “ל״ remains undotted, as it is correct to ask לשרה ,ל but not אֵלֶיחָ take out איו.

V. 10. כעת חיה. There are two words for time, זמן and זמן .עת is probably time in general in its duration and effect; עת designates a point in time, a moment either as befitting for some purpose or altogether as a fraction of time (it may by analogous to and derived like the Chaldean word from ענה or from the root עתת related to אתת from which we get אתים cutting tools, and עטט from which we get עט the pointed stylus). לכל זמן ועת לכל חפץ “Everything requires its time, and there is a fixed, proper moment for every effort”.

חיה from the root חײ. This root is closely related to the roots חקק, חכך ,חגג, which relation gives it also a conception of forming a cycle or circle which conception is common to חגג and חײ. Thus, ויאספו, פלשתים לַחַיָה וֵחַיַת פלשׁתים חנה (Sam. II. XXIII.11 & 13). Cf. ויבא המעגלה (Sam. I. XVII.20). A circle formed round a centre point. Every moment in time, too, is nothing but the momentary, terrestial and cosmic relation of the world so that עת חיה would indicate the recurring moment in the “living” course of the cycle of time. כעת חיה would accordingly mean — “as the present moment recurs in the living cycle of time so will I return”.

ושרה שמעת, not only she just chanced to hear this but altogether “she was listening”, although she did not sit at table with them, she still wanted to have something of the table-talk. It was probably well worth while taking the trouble to listen when an Abraham conversed with guests. It mentions that the entrance was behind the speaker, had it been facing him, Sarah would not have found it correct to participate.

V. 12. The past tense היתה in the verse is extremely difficult. Perhaps it means: it seemed laughable to her to think that in future people should say that in her old worn-out age she obtained the satisfaction of her deepest innermost earthly desires.
V. 15. כי יראה. She was afraid that she had offended the guest by laughing. לא כי צחקת. You need not deny it, but rather you are not to forget that you did laugh.

V. 16. From there, from the hospitable meal at Abraham, they stood up and looked towards Sodom. We already know this Sodom district whose luxurious abundance we believed was already expressed in the names of its cities: סדום, region of orchards; עמורה, richness of grain; אדמה, richness of minerals; צבוים, richness of game. But we also know their moral depravity, how, in their abundance, and through their abundance, they sank to רעים וחטאים, destitute of love towards their fellowmen and sunken to bestial depravity in immorality. So that Sodom offered the most complete contrast to the simple pure atmosphere from which these men were just emerging.

They had just seen the foundation of a nation laid on two factors, (a) on sanctifying the body with all its urges and lures in pure moral submission to God in Mila and (b) on practising universal brotherly love, as the גמילות חסד which they themselves had just enjoyed in Abraham’s home. The hospitable meal at which they had just had to announce the first foundation-stone of the future People of God offered such a contrast to Sodom, formed such a loftiness to the Sodomite debasement to which they now had to wend their way, that they “looked down to the plains of Sodom with criticising gauging consideration”. For that is the meaning of שקף .וישקפו seems to be related to שכב, to rest, to lie down, and שגב, to tower above, and to combine the meanings of both and to express “to rest in the height over something below”. Hence משקף, the lintel, נשקף, projecting from a height, being looked at as prominent, high above. השקיף, finally, to look down on the depths from a height. Hence השקפה always: a serious, testing look. Also so used in the וידוי מעשר (Deut. XXVI.15). We are to have satisfied the holy demands on our wealth and property to such a degree, can say בערתי הקדש מן הבית with such sincerity that we can say to God, השקיפה “Let Thy testing glance down on what we have done and abstained from doing and as Thou findest no fault therein, ’וברך וגו send Thy Blessing etc.

V. 17.—19. וה׳ אמר, probably to the מלאכים when He sent them off. The decision which I have just told you, should I keep that back from Abraham! For is he not just as much as you are, My messenger on earth, and the knowledge of this decision belongs essentially to the carrying-out of his mission. היו יהיה, for in victorious fighting his way through all opposition he too is to become a great, prosperous and mighty nation, and this nation, in contrast to Sodom, is to use its greatness and strength, not to be a curse to the world but to blossom into a blessing for mankind. כי ידעתיו, for, not for his own sake, not just to make him into a rich and powerful prince have I chosen him but just to be the founder and educator of such a nation, and not for himself, but for this nation, to be an enduring support for his mission of training this nation, is the knowledge of this decision and the insight into My Ways which it imparts, of such significant importance. For he is to achieve the unique great pedagogic success of implanting the principles of this future nation so deeply in the breast of his only late-born son, that long after he, the ancestor, had departed this world his children and his home after him and the whole future nation would stand on these principles, live in them, and make them into a reality. He will live on so immortally in his children that every particle of blessing that comes to his very last descendant can be ascribed back to the great ancestor. As a help to this unique marvellous pedagogic task he is given this insight into the Ways of God to hand on to his descendants, quite in the same way as later on his greatest son, Moses, begged God to grant him such insight to help him in leading His People.

ידע .כי ידעתיו to bring something into one’s mind in its specific characteristics, to perceive, to know. Of the relationship of man to woman it designates the most intimate procedure of married life. Of God to man it designates the special consideration of His Providence. People not turned towards God are under His general protection. Those who place themselves completely under the guidance of God, who are not, and do not wish to be, anything else than God’s messengers on earth, to them God directs His special guidance and protection. Measure for measure. He whose attitude towards God is just casual, who treads the paths of God just if and when it happens to suit him, בקרי, as the Torah calls it later on, who leaves living in God’s ways just to hazard, who does not make agreement with God’s Will his first consideration but allows other considerations to come first and leaves it to chance whether it does agree with God’s Will, to him God also turns and leaves him to the haphazard chances of life. But those who offer themselves to be His instruments on earth, who strive with their whole existence and activities to fulfil His Will, and leave everything else to Him, they form a complete contrast, and God takes them under His special guidance and care. This is what is called ידע.

’דרך ה occurs in two meanings. The Way of God that He takes, and that which He wishes us to tread. Both really come to the same thing. The way of goodness which He wishes to see us treading forms a tiny replica of His Great Ways of love. It fulfils His purpose which He wishes to be accomplished by us at His bidding. That is why the way of the good runs harmoniously parallel to the way in which God is leading the world and is guarded and helped by Him. That is why the way of the wicked clashes against it and becomes destroyed by it. כי ישרים דרכי ה׳ צדיקים ילכו בם ופושעים יכשלו בם (Hosea XIV.10).

The task for which Abraham is to bring up his descendants is called ’לשמר דרך ה, to keep to the path indicated by God, and לעשות צדקה ומשפט, practising acts of duty and justice. The former carries out the התהלך לפני ה׳ והיות תמים the holy pure moral life before God, to which Mila lays the foundation, and the latter, living humanely and benevolently with one’s fellow men as was shown in the example set by Abraham. Together they constitute the most complete contrast to Sodom, the former to the immorality of the חטאים, the latter to the hardness of heart of the רעים.

Now Abraham’s צואה does not run ושמרו דרך ה׳ ועשו צדקה ומשפט but ושמרו דרך ה׳ ל ע ש ו ת צדקה ומשפט.
