V. 32. “I would tell him just that you belong to the class of shepherds, although that profession is not considered in Egypt as the most honourable one. For they were breeders of sheep”. Not that they themselves actually shepherded the flocks, that they left to their herdsmen, but they lived from breeding the animals.

V. 33. In a state like Egypt, where caste prevailed and men were completely absorbed into their trade, and men were born as artisans, workers on the land, soldiers, etc. the first question was naturally about their profession. To Pharaoh’s question they were unashamedly to acknowledge this unpleasant fact, for the disgust which the Egyptians had for their calling, which they could not disguise, — just as altogether, the dislike of the Jews by the nations — was the first means for the preservation of that race that was destined for an isolated path through the ages. Until the spiritual moral morn dawns for the nations of the world, the barriers that the false conception which they have, have raised against the Jews, have served to protect them from being infected by the barbarism and demoralisation of the people in whose midst they were to have to wander for centuries. That is why, here too, Joseph at once brought to the fore that aspect of his brethren which was unpleasant to the Egyptians with the expressed purpose of obtaining thereby for them, a separated province in which to settle.

V. 1. Joseph introduces his brothers to Pharaoh before his father. He probably knew quite well that Jacob, feeling his moral superiority would not bow his knees before a Pharaoh. So he prefers first to bring before him some members of the family who would not fail to show him suitable signs of their subservience. Hence also ויציגם לפני he placed them at Pharaoh’s disposition, like אציגה נא וגו׳ (Ch. XXXIII.15).

V. 3. רעה צאן, in the singular. We, your servants belong to the caste of shepherds. Joseph had put it to them to say אנשי מקנה, breeders of heds. But they were not shy of their profession and said straight out: shepherds.

V. 4. Although probably there was just as little grazing possibilites in Goshen as in Canaan in the years of famine, Joseph would have stored fodder for the animals also in Goshen as elsewhere in the purlieus of the city.
V. 5. They came to you, the care for them is on your shoulders, and I give you herewith the means to do so.

V. 6. הושב, not as גרים (aliens I.L.) but as permanent authorised inhabitants, ואם ידעת ויש בם — .תושבים. With great delicacy Pharaoh says this as two possibilities. There may be יש בם אנשי חיל but אם ידעת, you may not know it, or may not wish to know it, you may not wish to make them state officials, he himself puts the excuse in Joseph’s hand should he not wish it.

ויבא, not לקח as with brothers, equally so, not ויציגהו but ויעמדהו. Jacob also does not wait for the king to address him first. He feels himself also a prince on earth and meets him on equal footing with a greeting of blessing.

V. 8. Still today, royalty, whose time naturally is extremely precious at audiences, as a rule just throw out a few short words or enquiries, the replies to which they are in reality entirely indifferent. But it must be rare indeed for a king to have understood to secure more delicacy in a few interrogative words than Pharaoh did here. And even more seldom has the person addressed expressed more wisdom in a short reply, than Jacob did here. When one counts by years, one does not reckon any more the days. It is only with a few select people that each day is full of importance and is considered by them as having a special meaning. A really true human being does not live years but days. Similarly in the great psalm of Moses (Ps. XC. I.L.) in which the whole history of the world passes by as in a dream, it says at the end: if even a thousand years of world-history mean no more than one minute, then a day means nothing. Only there where the תורה has entered and people’s activities are decided by, and dedicated to, the service of God, do people live daily, each day they are strong, each day they accomplish something, make progress, undisturbed by what tomorrow may bring, each such day is reckoned up by God, and no day is lost. למנות ימינו כן הודע. “Teach us thus to count our days”! Thus Pharaoh too, says here: How many days hast thou lived in the years of thy life? And in putting the question “how old are you?” in these words, he reveals the deep impression which the whole appearance and dignified behaviour of Jacob had made on him.

V. 9. In his reply Jacob differentiates between living and existing. You ask after the days of the years of my life. I have not lived much. I have sojourned on earth during one hundred and thirty years. The days of the years that I can really call my life (on which I really fully carried out all that I should) were in reality only few, and they were רעים, were just the bitterest and those most full of worry. I had the mission of doing the duties of unhappiness in unhappiness. The contents of my life can in no way be compared to the contents of the lives of my fathers. They lived more, every day of existence here below was living, and they had to carry out the mission of their lives under cheerful conditions. This was no complaint against the shortness of his life, but modesty in looking back at the moral worth of the life he had lived through.

V. 11. They had only come in the expressed intention of staying temporarily in the land. At Pharaoh’s definite wish, and by his command, they were induced to official settlement and landed possession was allotted to them. — אחוזה. According to the Jewish way of looking at it, man does not so much take possession of land as being himself taken over, gripped, by his land, allowing himself to be chained to it; not אוחז by האחז is the term used for taking possession of land. Only moveable goods are really absorbed by the personality of their owner and really “belong”, go over to their possessor. But a man rather belongs to his land, and only immobile possessions are considered as bearers of the person and can represent him in the legal sense. A relationship which has far-reaching effects in Jewish civil law.

V. 12. לחם לפי הטף. One can not let little children go short, even in times of inflated prices and scarcity, they do not let themselves be cut down as the adults have to, especially not טף in the tender age which this word expresses. It seems, accordingly, that Joseph provided his father and family only with wise economy.

V. 13. ותלה, the land wasted, grew weak, root להה related to לאה to lose strength. לאה is probably the root of לא, logical negation, the denial of an existence differentiated from אל, moral negation, the denial of a will or obligation. לאה is the transition of being into not being, the draining away of strength.
V. 17. בסוסים, the most valuable of all possessions of herds, Egypt was renowned for its horses.

V. 21. לערים, not in, or to, cities, but “citywise”, the inhabitants of one whole city all together to another city. The whole land had become state property, and to make this newly acquired right completely actual, every owner had to leave property that hitherto had been his own and move to another district, so that a general evacuation took place. But Joseph’s wisdom tempered the edict by arranging that the residents who had always lived together remained together and found themselves still together with their friends but only in a fresh environment. So that the old social and communal conditions remained the same, and there was no complete upheaval by the change. Our sages point out the beneficial result that this transposition of all the inhabitants must have had for the new arrivals, the family of Jacob, to whom henceforth no Egyptian could look down with disdain as newcomers. For no Egyptian either was an “old inhabitant” on his native hearth. The whole measure, moreover, was no invention of Joseph’s. The people themselves had proposed it, v.19, and indeed, at the same time actual bondage. Joseph rejected the proposed thraldom and only adopted the state purchase of the landed property out of which finally merely a land-tax resulted.

V. 22. “Only the land of the priest did he not buy etc.” Here we see a complete contrast, which opposes that theory which has become rooted in so many people’s views, that Moses had learnt and adopted his legal and religious wisdom from the Egyptians. The supposed teachers of Moses, the Egyptian priests, possessed land, more, after the alteration in Joseph’s time, were the sole actual owners of land, and besides had a fixed assured state income. Our כהנים possessed no land at all, and had no income from state funds, but were dependent for their existence on the good-will and the respect of private individuals. Had משה רבנו ע״ה been a “Moses” he would have made other arrangements for his own tribe.

חק. As a rule חקים are taken to be limitations which have once been fixed without any reason given and no reason for them ascertainable. But, both according to the derivation, חקק, related to חכך ,חגג, as well as to their application and practice, the very opposite is the case. חק is that which is demanded by the conditions, stipulations, requirements and set-purposes of any being, thing, or condition, is accordingly something that flows deep out of the very nature of the thing, and is the condition for its existence and its purpose. Thus, הטריפני לחם חקי (Prov. XXX.8) the food which is necessary for my existence, and which is indicated to me by Thee. They are fixed laws which emanate deep from the nature of our beings and of what we are meant to be. Keeping them is as essential for the existence and vocation of our moral and spiritual nature as our daily bread is for the existence and fulfilment of the purpose of our material bodily nature.

V. 26. לפרעה לחמש. The ground belonged to Paraoh for the fifth, i.e. was his property as surety for payment of a fifth of the produce. If anybody failed to pay the fifth the crown was entitled to take the whole. Actually all Egyptians, as far as land went were only אריסים, tenant-farmers to whom only ½, ⅓, or ¼ of the produce was due. But that in fact was not to be the case, they are to keep four-fifths for themselves and only have to pay one fifth to the ground-landlord. But the principle was to remain in force that not חמש לפרעה, not that one fifth belonged to Pharaoh, but לפרעה לחמש the whole was to belong to Pharaoh to guarantee the fifth. The whole relationship excluded the imposition of serfdom.
V. 27. ויאחזו בה, they let themselves be gripped by the land. Herein lies an indication of the beginning of that sin, the facts of which Ezekiel (Ch. XX.) has preserved to us.

V. 28. ויחי continues the preceding directly, without the usual פרשה division. When one considers that the seventeen years which are introduced hereby are really the only ones in which Jacob lived a quiet undisturbed life, so that, in comparison with the previous years of his life, they can be considered as the real flowering of his life, we should have expected all the more to find the relation of them to be brought into prominence by starting with a fresh chapter. But the fact that this is not the case teaches us that through these seventeen years certainly are to be reckoned with the rest of his life, nationally they form the lesser important part of it. But it was rather the troubled years of his life, in which the test had to be gone through, in the midst of the bitterest fate of a Jacob to be worthy of acquiring the name of Israel, that were those in which Jacob won his everlasting national importance, to which the seventeen years that follow here form just the happy rewarding conclusion.

Hence also the peculiar ויהי ימי. The picture of the whole of Jacob’s life was a uniform one. שני חייך, the term seems to refer back Jacob’s own modest declaration of the contents of his life, to wish to have the same rectifying faithfulness to actual truth. They were not merely מגוריו which could only count a little חיים, but rather all the days of his wandering here below were years of real and true living. — Perhaps the reason that we express small numbers in the plural, large ones in the singular may be that in a small number the single ones present themselves to our eyes and our thoughts more in their individualities, whereas in a larger number they present themselves more as a common mass which all bear the common character of the object counted. We say חמשה אנשים and עשרים איש, “five men” and “twenty man”.

V. 29. אם נא מצאתי חן בעיניך. No father speaks thus to his son, not even a son to his father, least of all did Jacob have to speak in such terms to Joseph. The little word נא may solve our difficulty. Joseph, with all his devotion to his father, certainly wanted to give his father all the privileges which his exalted position would have allowed him to, but Jacob was never willing to accept them. He did not want to be father of the Prime Minister. But here, at least, was an opportunity in which Jacob did wish to use Joseph’s great influence: “if, after all I have found grace etc., if you do wish to show me special favour, then grant me this request”. — שים נא ידך תחת ירכי. (See above on XXIV.2). ירך related to ירק, to throw away from oneself, spit. ירך, the back or under part of the body which in sitting down or lying, first comes into contact with the ground. The opposite of שכם in השכם. “Lay your hand beneath me” let me rest on you, depend on you, promise me that you will use the influence of your power, so that I can confidently lay myself down to die. The form עמדי for עמי is striking, as already remarked, it occurs with no other suffix.

חסד, related to אשד to pour oneself out, hence to devote Oneself entirely (חַסֵד to give oneself up entirely to someone else: to abandon oneself to degradation). The addition of ואמת (and truth I.L.) to the conception of guarding true חסד is characteristic. Thus all the Ways of God are חסד ואמת. Man often does רעות just out of love (he allows his heart to run away with his head I.L.). חסד ואמת is a love that does not forget what is essential, when practising devotion. Abraham had the most ardent desire to see his son married. But if he would have allowed himself to be so dominated by this wish for his beloved son that, if he could find no wife, spiritually and morally suitable for the זרע אברהם, he would have allowed another one to be chosen, it would have been חסד an act of loving kindness but not a אמת .חסד של אמת is always a stipulating reservation when added to חסד.

Jacob knew quite certainly that Joseph would bury his father with all possible splendour. But he says: “With all the חסד do not forget the אמת״. I would rather not be buried at all than be buried in Egypt. The whole stress is on the request not to be buried in Egypt. We would have thought that carrying out this request did not entail such difficulties that it should have required a ceremonious oath for it. But, as can be deduced from everything, Pharaoh and the Egyptians would by no means have been pleased if Jacob and his family had moved again back out of Egypt, so that the bringing of the body up to Canaan would by no means make a good impression. It would clearly show that Joseph’s family still did not consider themselves naturalised and that their hearts were still in their old homeland.

But the real motive could lie much deeper. Jacob had still lived seventeen years with his family in Egypt, could have noticed what a powerful influence the האחז בה (being gripped by the land I.L.) was beginning to have on his descendants, how they already began to see the Jordan in the Nile, and to find their stay in Egypt no Galut. Sufficient motive this for him to press with such ceremonious solemnity that they should not bury him in Egypt, but that they should carry him to the land of their old true homeland. Motive enough for him to say to them: You hope and wish to live in Egypt, I do not wish even to be buried there. That is also why he did not express this wish as Jacob, from his individual personal standpoint, but as “Israel”, as bearer of the national mission, as a warning of the national future of his children.

V. 30. ושכבתי. To lie with one’s fathers is not to be buried in their proximity but is the physical act of death, as האסף designates the spiritual side of that act. האסף, the return home of the soul to the homeland of souls; שכב, the laying down of the body into the earth, into the common bosom, wherever one may be buried, in which, wherever they too may be buried, one’s preceding parents rest.

V. 31. וישתחו ישראל על ראש המטה. Just as Eliezer threw himself down before God, when before God, when he had accomplished his mission, so does Jacob here. He had now reached the last thing that he had to see about on earth. The head of the bed was behind him. Naturally he sat in bed facing the foot, and Joseph was in front of him. To bow towards the head of the bed, was accordingly, a movement backwards. It was a devotional thanking to Him Who had led him through all his past life to this goal. God had led him hither to his well-beloved son.

V. 1. אחרי always introduces a turning-point, a crisis. ח- .חלה always expresses a check of an action, similarly to נוע and עלה .נוח is the independent raising, development, rising (dead material sinks, the force of life raises living material upwards). If this going forwards, really the movement of raising oneself, is checked, hindered, then it is חלה, checked development. רפא (healing) רפה (loosening) is the loosening of the knots that were hindering the upward movement i.e. healing, hence, recovery. תעלה, the development upwards starting again.

Above, where Jacob wants something from Joseph, he has him called. Here, where he wishes to give something to Joseph, and indeed the highest, most precious gift, the בכורה, he simply has him told: your father is ill. He is not to be called, he is to come as a child, in the feelings of a child when he hears that his aged father is ill, and at this opportunity Jacob gives him that which he has to apportion to him. A Jacob, even where it is the highest gift that he is presenting does not make much parade of it.
V. 2. Joseph does not know how his father is and does not wish to excite him, so he has him told just casually that he is coming to visit him: ויגד, and only then has him told that he is there.

V. 3 et seq. By the ועתה (and now) in V.5, it is clear the conferring of the בכורה on Joseph by installing his two sons as separate tribes had to have a preparatory explanation. And this must be found in the two preceding verses. Now, it seems to us hardly thinkable that this could lie in the fact that Jacob, on his way home, was given the promise הנני מפרך וגו׳ ונתתיך לקהל עמים or, as the actual promise was worded פרה ורבה גוי וקהל גוים יהיה ממך (XXXV.11) and that this was to mean that the increase in the family was only to occur through Benjamin, Ephraim and Menasseh, and that the גוים would then refer solely to the two latter, so that they would have been designated already beforehand as two sparate tribes. For in a family circle that already consists of eleven sons such an increase could hardly be reckoned as appearing so important that it could be announced by God with the words הנני מפרך והרביתיך. Rather, as we already indicated above on the verse, the קהל גוים, here denoted קהל עמים, gives this nation in general the characteristic mission that, in spite of their being united into one completely similar body of men by their all having the one common spiritual and moral mission and outlook on life, they are nevertheless to consist of a diversity of tribes (a קהל עמים I.L.). The nation is to represent agriculture as well as commerce, militarism as well as culture and learning etc. Thereby, as a model nation, factually to establish the Truth that the one great personal and national calling which God has revealed in His Torah is not dependent on any particular kind of calling or trait, but that the whole of mankind in all its shades of diversity, can equally find its calling in the one common spiritual and moral mission and outlook in life. The division of the nation into separate tribes, and the resulting division of the Promised Land into different provinces for the different tribes, the diversity of whom is thus to be retained, is what is referred to here. Only in its having such a result does it altogether make any difference that Ephraim and Menasseh are to grow into two separate tribes. Without it every speciality, all particular tendencies, would be absorbed in the general national masses, just as the land would come to be divided to the nation as a whole, and not according to different tribes. אחזת עולם. Although for thousands of years we did not possess it, it was still our נאחז בה ;אחזה we were gripped and held by it, it holds us even when we do not have it.

V. 7. מתה עלי, it was a fatal disaster that befell me. כברת: see Ch. XXXV.16. This speech of Jacob, referring back to Rachel’s death and burial is usually taken as having been said as exoneration for his placing such weight on his being buried in Machpela although Joseph’s mother was not buried there. But if that was its meaning, we should have expected it to have been said above in the previous conversation, where Jacob asked for the promise for his burial. In the connection in which we find it here it can only have reference to the matter of the discourse here, the decision about the sons of Joseph. In this conversation until the moment when he gives his blessing and imparts to his grandsons their position in the future of the nation, V.8, Jacob is designated solely as Jacob, and not as Israel. In V.2 when Joseph came to him ויתחזק ישראל, Jacob pulled himself together so as to regard Joseph not only as his son, but in his importance for the national future which is associated with the name ישראל; and from this standpoint too, he expresses, V.8 his blessing on Joseph’s sons. But favouring him by making him a double tribe, sprung from Jacob’s personal relationship to Joseph, hence ויאמר יעקב V.3, and only at V.8 again וירא ישראל. For it seems that this favouritism to the sons of Joseph came, not from national considerations, but from the individual personal feelings which Jacob, as Jacob, the man, personally felt. In the last days of his life thoughts of the wife whom he loved the most deeply, who was the actual wife of his choice, and who had been taken away from him the earliest, were specially prominent in his mind; her whole fate made it likely that her memory would be more in the background in the future memorials of the nation. When the children of Israel in later times visited the graves of their ancestors, they would find Abraham and Sarah, Isaac and Rebecca, Jacob and Leah, but Rachel, Joseph’s mother, was not granted, even in death, to receive her place in the common resting-place of the ancestors of the nation. And only two tribes call her their mother. So it would be just the wife of his heart, whom he had thought of as the real mother of his future people, who might vanish from the hearts of the nation. That was why it was the deep desire of his heart to raise Joseph Rachel’s firstborn, to be the firstborn of his national tribes, by making his sons into two tribes, to grant him the right of the firstborn to a “double portion”.

V. 9. קחם נא אלי. When that which we bring to somebody makes us ourselves receive some fresh consecration, this thought is expressed by לקח אל-, as in ויקחו לי תרומה. By bringing them to me you get them doubly for yourself. Therein lies the whole depth of feeling which a son feels when he is fortunate enough to bring his children to his old father to be blessed by him. With verse 8 the name of Israel is reintroduced. It is the ancestor of the future nation, who, elevated by the spirit of God, blesses his grandsons for their position in the national future of his people.

V. 11. פלל ,פללתי, related to בלל to bring some extraneous matter into a material, and so integrate it therein that the whole becomes one single mass (differentiated from ערב to mix, when the whole mass remains still a mixture I.L.). That which בלל is concretely פלל is mentally, to bring a spiritual element, a thought, a fact, a principle etc. in a sphere of heterogeneous thoughts or conditions, and by being penetrated by this element to make it unified and homogeneous. Hence פלל the business of a judge. He has to bring the principle of right and justice and make it penetrate all conditions laid before him and thereby form the conflicting conditions into one harmonious unity. Hence judges are also called אלהים, from אלה, these, a conception which always presupposes the subsuming a plurality under the idea of unity. התפלל, to penetrate oneself with godly thoughts. Jewish praying is not from within outwards, but from without inwards. Were there only one form of praying, from within outwards, i.e. pouring out thoughts or prayers which are already present within oneself, then fixed “prescribed” prayers, and added thereto, at a fixed time to be prayed by an unlimited number of persons, would be pure folly. For it would assume that, at the word of command, at some fixed moment, any number of people would have the same thoughts and feelings and have the urge to put them into words. Not so. התפלל means to penetrate oneself, ever afresh again, with eternal, essential lasting Truths and facts, because otherwise they become weaker and weaker, fade away from one’s consciousness, yea, may even already have disappeared. Here ראה פניך לא פללתי means, “the thought of seeing you once again seemed to me so far from any possibility of its being realised, that I could not give it any entry into my mind”.
V.12. The feelings which filled the father at these thoughts, overpowered the son to an even higher degree.

V. 15. He blessed Joseph in blessing his sons. For the highest blessing a father can receive, is indeed the blessing which his children receive. — התהלך is a term only used of God and Man and designates a leading of oneself, accordingly, a going of one’s own free-willed moral energy, or figuratively of elements going about as messengers in the service of God, thus, of lightning. He modestly only speaks of such free-willed conduct of life before God referring to his father. But he says that he, too, had learnt to know God, He had been the Shepherd Who had led and guided, fed and maintained him from the beginning of his existence to that very day.

V. 16. It is very difficult in this connection to say of an angel that it should dispense blessing especially as, immediately before, God Himself is mentioned, in Whose Hands alone blessing lies. In ב״ר Ch. 97 according to the version of the Yalkut, ר׳ אליעזר expresses himself as follows: — הקיש גאולה לפרנסה ופרנסה לגאולה, מה גאולה פלאים אף פרנסה פלאים, מה פרנסה בכל יום אף גאולה בכל יום “here maintenance (הרועה) and deliverance are placed interchangeably equal to each other, just as deliverance occurs through miracles so does our maintenance, and just as our maintenance occurs daily, so does deliverance occur daily”. So that here we have not to think of deliverance from some special danger, but of that salvation which we require, like our food, day by day. Both of them Parnasa and Geula, are no result of the general laws of nature which God fixed once for always, but are the outcome of God’s special providence. That the fair, conscientious man, seeking his livelihood only in honest moral ways, does find his bread by that way is פלאים, is a miracle, a gift of God each time, as it says: טרף נתן ליראיו יזכור לעולם בריתו, “that which others obtain by using force (טרף I.L.) He gives to those that honour Him, He everlastingly keeps His covenant in mind”. And that such an honest upright man remains unmolested in the midst of a world threatening with physical and social evils, for that he requires constantly Divine deliverance, constant גאולה.

גאל, related to גחל, a piece of still glowing coal withdrawn from fire. It has been in the fire but has been withdrawn before it has been completely overcome by the fire. But גאלה is complete salvation which, unlike גחל bearing the traces of burning still on it, is completely free and unscathed, like Abraham from the Chaldean fire, and Daniel’s comrades from the red-hot furnace. “Had we but eyes to see”, remarks a saying of our sages, “we would realise how everywhere we are constantly surrounded by מזיקים, by dangerous elements of the physical world” (did they have an inkling of bacteria? I wonder I.L.), and if it is thus in physical life, truly it is indeed so in social life. Woe unto us if we were not blind to it. Happy can we be, that we do not see the dangers to life from which we escape every minute in the physical world, nor do we realise the ruin and misfortune which is wished to us by envy and wickedness which, in social life, daily and hourly may pass over us without our even being conscious of it. That is the רע out of which הקב״ה saves us every minute, and saves us indeed so that we are not even conscious of the danger we have been in. “Now”, ר׳ שמואל בר נחמן remarks, ”פרנסה גדולה מן הגאולה שהגאולה ע״י מלאך פרנסה ע״י הקב״ה״ one’s livelihood is greater than one’s deliverance, as the latter occurs through an angel (המלאך הגואל), while the other is through הקב״ה Himself”. If we understand this sentence correctly, it is based on the underlying fact that the constant unfailing geula from the threatening evil of destruction, the geula from the threatening evil of destruction, the geula on which the actual existence of life is dependent, must precede parnassa. It is a factor that must be given beforehand at the very incipience of the existence of an individual or state, coincidentally with the place in the world, which is created by Divine direction. This is the “fate” of people, at which the Jew always thinks of the “One” Who sent it, regards his fate as a מלאך, as a messenger carrying out the Divine providence. It is the Divine destiny which, at the entry of a human child or a nation into physical, social, or historic existence says “it shall live” and God commands His מלאכים the “carriers-out” of the destiny He has fixed for it — “to guard it in all its paths, to bear it upon their hands that no stone injures its foot, that it shall walk along over jackal and otter, trample on young lion and serpent” (Ps. XCI). (Possibly the word מלאך is indeed derived from מלך, a powerful acting force, but which does not act out of its own powerful force but bears invisibly within itself an א, the sign of another personality which guides and sends it: literally שמי בקרבו, as it says of the מלאן). So Jacob’s wishes that God may bless his grandsons through the same מלאך through which He had delivered him from all harm, i.e. that his grandsons may carry on the same “destiny” within which, and through which, God had let him find existence and prosperity; that they might live as little as he had done, unlike Esau, depending on their own strength and their own sword, but, like Jacob, seek and find their protection and support solely in God, only so ויקרא וגו׳, would he and his fathers live on in them, וידגו לרב בקרב הארץ.

וידגו. The word דגה does not occur again anywhere except as the root of דג, fish. But just as that, fish, does it express the whole depth of the intenseness of Jacob’s blessing, and the meaning of what it entails to participate in the fate of Jacob; what it means to walk before the same God, as their fathers did, to be guided by the same God, and allow yourself to be saved by the same providence of God. In a different element, quietly, at a depth unreachable by the eyes of men, do fish live their lives. Thoughtlessly do people stand on shore and have no idea what a happy, fresh, joyful, undisturbed life goes on down below in rich abundance from generation to generation. In a similar way בקרב הארץ, in the midst of the world are the generations of Jacob to live and achieve their own quiet happy lives in their own separated element whither the world around them do not follow them, have no conception of what such a life means, “like fish”, “like fish in water, in the midst of human beings on earth” בגו בני אנשא על ארעא כנוני ימא יסגון (Tar. Onkelos).

V. 19. גוים ,לעם. cf. above גוי וקהל גוים (XXXV.11) and והיית לקהל עמים (XXVIII.3) (where the tribes of Israel are called nations — I.L.) תרעו יהיה מלא גוים, literally this would say: his seed shall become that which fills the nations, the nations are to become filled with his descendants, as מלא כל הארץ כבודו (the whole world is full of the Glory of God I.L.). This would then mean, that Ephraim’s descendants would be scattered amongst all the nations. But this would then be קללה, and no blessing. Hence Rashi takes it to mean: the nations will be full of the renown of his children. But this is not what it says in the text. But we find the word מלא having the meaning of arming, equipping e.g. ויהוא מלא ידו בקשת (II Kings IX.24) ואיש יגע בו ימלא ברזל וחנית (II Sam. XXIII.7). But arming is only artificially supplementing the lack of strength and ability, complementing, מלא. By that Ephraim would be characteristically described. Ephraim’s descendants will become the armour of the tribes of Israel towards the rest of the world. Hence גוים (as Israel is called towards the rest of the world I.L.) and not עמים (Israel looked at interiorly, socially, I.L.). As Joseph himself was first separated from the family of Jacob, and so importantly became a member of a non-Jewish state, but, of course, even as such, remained faithful to the Jewish conception of God — “ה״ — עדות ביהוסף שמו בצאתו על ארץ מצרים — so later on Ephraim also was the first to adopt the character of a non-Jewish state, of course in a sad estrangement from Judaism. But an estrangement that, as little as with his ancestor, need necessarily have occurred with that separation. It is therefore very possible that what it says is this: — His descendants, as a power respected externally, shall fill a gap in the appearance of the tribes of Israel towards the rest of the world, shall become the powerful armour of the other tribes externally. In any case, after Judah, Ephraim was the bravest of the tribes. Perhaps זרעו also refers primarily to Joshua who could quite specially be called the armour of the tribes.

Characteristically here we see again the firstborn placed behind the younger brother. Right down from Cain and Abel we find this disregard of the בכורים. God was pleased with Abel, Cain was rejected. Of the sons of Noah, Shem was probably not the eldest. Of Abraham’s sons, Ishmael gives place to Isaac, of Isaac’s, Esau to Jacob, of Jacob’s Reuben to Joseph, of Joseph’s Menasseh to Ephraim, and the real ruling leadership came to Judah. Moses, too, was the younger, David the youngest of the family. Yea, the בכורות as a whole lost their status in the nation. Out of all this, one thing is clear. Whereas, on the one hand, the firstborn remains the most favoured, is the recognised representative of the family, and has the responsibility of such, and accordingly receives פי שנים, a double portion of the inheritance, and thereby is indicated that really, spirituality and power should go hand in hand, the history of the world, nevertheless shows nothing else but the fight of material power against godly spirituality. The goal is, as was announced to Rebecca, רב יעבד צעיר, the strong to be in service to the weak. But, as an obstacle to this goal, spiritual power and national might are separated from each other הקול קול יעקב הידים ידי עשו (the voice is the voice of Jacob, but the hands are the hands of Esau). כאשר תריד, was said to Esau, only then will you stand at his side as his equal, when, of your own free will, you voluntarily place yourself under him. Until then the material imagines itself to be the superior, but is always mastered. These, (the spiritual and the material I.L.) are the two crowns which, according to Zachariah VI.11—15, ultimately will be united in משיה (the Messiah) who will be the כהן על כסאו, the “priest on his throne”, and will accomplish the peaceful union of the two: ועצת שלום תהיה בין שניהם. Until that time, the two crowns remain לזכרון בהיכל ה׳, their union is only an ideal kept in God’s Sanctuary. It is to be taught continuously throughout Jewish history that material power should go hand in hand with the spiritual, but reality does not yet correspond to the ideal. The spiritual aspect of the firstborn is discarded, advantage is taken of the other, the material preference, and this temporary contradiction between what should be and what is seems to be represented even in the Torah by פדיון בכור.

V. 20. ביום ההוא. On that day the ברכה was pronounced for the first time, the blessing which since then has lived on the lips of all Jewish parents when they bless their children. בך יברך וגו׳, your children shall be so blessed, that, when fathers in Israel wish to bless their children, they can know of no higher blessing than to wish: May God let thee become even as Ephraim and Menasseh.

V. 22. שׁכם אַחַד על אחיך, The אחד attached to שכם makes it impossible for it to be the name of a city. And even if שכם meant, as it is usually taken to mean, a portion, an allotment, the אַחַד would still remain completely unexplained. For אַחַד never means one, but always one of two, or more, one out of many. So that it can not mean, “I have given you one portion more than your brother”. Also there is really no example of שכם meaning part or portion. But שכם occurs as shoulder bearing a burden and also as bearing dignity, honour, preferment, e.g. ותהי המשרה על שכמו “dominion will rest on his shoulder” (Is. IX.5); הסירתי מסבל שכמו “I removed his shoulder from the burden” (Ps. LXXXI.7). So that literally it would say. “I have given thee the shoulder of the one above thy brethren”, i.e. I have appointed you to bear the burden and the honour to be the one amongst your brothers, the one who, after my death, is to represent me, to be the head of the family and guide them. — אשר לקחתי וגו׳, your brothers, my children whom I have wrenched away from the Amorite with “my sword and my bow”, with that which — in contrast to Esau’s sword — is my weapon, my spiritual force, and my spiritual work. Jacob says: See, I die, I have no great heritage to leave, we are in a foreign country. God must first lead you back to our own land, there you will have נחלות, here we have only ברכות and wishes. But what I have to bequeath, that I have given to you. That is the burden and the honour to be my successor in the leadership and responsibility of the family, to be the first over your brothers, over my children who are the only conquests I have made in my life, and whom I dispose of in dying. That, in the midst of the Amorite they became no Amorites, that I can now gather them all around me as my sons, as carriers-on of the name and calling of Israel, those are my trophies, my conquests and victory out of the hand of the Amorites.

V. 1.—2. האספו and הקבצו have by no means the same meaning. This is evident already from the fact that האסף can be said even of a single, individual, e.g. עד האסף מרים (Numb. XII.15). אסף means, to bring something from the place or sphere where it does not really belong, to where it does belong. There is always some idea of its relationship to עזב, a breaking away from everything else that is improper. Hence here האספו, break away from everything to which you really do not belong, and find yourselves all united in the one common purpose. Be all taken up with that which is common to you all! Place yourselves all on one common footing! So that האספו demands the spiritual gathering together on the single point, for one single purpose — as our sages, accordingly, pithily explain it הטהרו! Literally it would read: Let yourselves be gathered up (i.e. by your common mission).

קבץ, on the other hand (related to קפץ to close, כוץ to shrink together, כבש to press together, even to יבש dry, solid in contrast to liquid, גביש a precious stone, (probably the diamond on account of its hardness) always refers to the external gathering together of people, not uniting in mind but in space.

So we have here two pronouncements: All of you together give yourselves up to your one purpose in life for I would picture to you what will happen to you at the end of time. Really, what will “call to you” at the end of time (see Ch. XLII.4) אחרית must be differentiated from קץ. קץ is the end, where something ceases, אחרית is that which comes afterwards, after the other has ended. Here, accordingly, after the present development of time has run out, the legacy of days, the goal of world-history.

We know from what follows that Jacob was not having in mind the uniformity of his sons, but was thinking of them in their characteristic diversity. Hence: “different though you all are, if you will all give yourselves up entirely to the one spirit, I will reveal to you what the end of time will be for you”. First one spirit must pervade all the sons of the Family of Jacob before the אחרית הימים will come. It will not come before the האספו has become a reality Yea — perhaps — it will not even be conceived, understood, until then, and that is why only just short hinting references to the אחרית הימים follow.

הקבצו ושמעו! these two words from the mouth of the dying father contain the whole Jewish history until the אחרית הימים. Materially you are בני יעקב, a powerless minority. But because you are a powerless minority הקבצו, keep together, grow together, do not split up into parties, in קבוץ, in unity lies your strength. And שמעו בני יעקב, only by one thing can the weakest material minority obtain the victory over the strongest majority, and that is spirit, mind, it is שמעו, it is by giving yourselves up to spirituality, hence שמעו בני יעקב, have an ear, get understanding for the spiritual, thirst for it, as the word itself means (שמע is the spiritual צמא) drink deeply, absorb it! Such is the testament of our Father Jacob. “Unity, concord, and spirit”, therein he recognised the strength and life of his children, and “when the thirst for spiritual matters awakes in you, have thirst for nothing but the traditions of your father Israel”, ושמעו אל ישראל אביכם. Drinking out of the Jewish well of spirituality, and harmoniously keeping together, that is the oldest legacy of our dying father, and the same call comes to us from our last prophet: והאמת והשלום אהבו (Zach. VIII.19).

V. 3. הקבצו ,האספו, were the first thoughts which filled the mind of Jacob when he saw his sons around his death-bed. Keeping together and keen wakeful interest for all spiritual matters was the first thought which filled his mind as the primary advice he could leave behind him for them. But if such a gathering consisting of so many different elements is to form one united unit internally and externally it must have a leader, and Jacob now looks around his mustered sons for such a guiding head for this future nation. The most natural person for this position would be the eldest, the firstborn. He therefore first turns to Reuben.

כח .כחי, force, strength is related to כה: thus, which itself is related to כהה: to become dark. כח is that mysterious force, the dark source of beings coming into existence, which in ourselves and everywhere we recognise in its results but which in itself always remains dark to us. We call it force, strength. כה: thus, is the designation of the picture, the outline after which something is to form itself.

און related to הון, the ability to acquire and possess something (See above XXXV.18) Jacob says: you are כחי, either: you are the one in whose formation and spiritual bringing-up and care, my strength was shown; or: my strength, my power rests on you, through you my spirit works quietly further. With the success or failure of the education of the eldest son and eldest daughter of a family, however numerous it may be, almost the whole work of bringing it up is won or lost.
ראשית אוני: you are my first possession; cf. above אשר לקחתי מיד האמרי וגו׳. Jacob’s first acquisition was Reuben.

יתר: that which reaches farther than another; in time: to remain over; in space: a sinew or string stretched beyond its natural extent. Hence יֶתֶר either a noun: pre-eminence in worthiness, and pre-eminence in power, in which case one would have to supplement “you are fit for”; or more probably it is an adjective, and stat. cons, of יָתֵר (like יֶרֶךְ from יָלֵךְ and כֶּתֶף from כָּתֵף): pre-eminent, surpassing in worthiness etc. שאת, probably here meaning height, eminence, as הלא שאתו תבעת אתכם “shall not his excellency make you afraid?” (Job. XII.11) or אך משאתו יעצו להדיח “they only take counsel to cast him down from his excellency” (Ps. LXII.5), the more so, as the Jewish excellency is called נשיא (see on XXV.16); “you are the בכור, and as such have the pre-eminence in worth and therefore also pre-eminence in power”. As the firstborn you have the calling to be the נשיא of your brothers, the head and leader of the family, and therefore, too, to receive a greater portion of material power so that the material foundation for the spiritual leadership may not be wanting. Possibly also that is why it is just called נשיא, bearing, you are to be the bearer, to have the most to bear (in contrast to Esau’s אלופים ours אלופינו מסובלים are the laden ones) and therefore have also to have a greater share of power.

V. 4. It is to be regretted that the root פחז does not occur more frequently. But from אנשים רקים ופוחזים (Judges IX.4) we can see that it means some shortcoming in character. But we still do not know which. Unfortunately here it is compared to water. There is hardly anything else that lends itself to such a variety of qualities as water. Water has no internal stability hence it could mean “unstable as water”. Water always flows downwards to the lowest level, strives after lowness (except when it evaporates to rise to the clouds for the formation of rain). Water is liquid, flows rapidly forwards, etc. In Talmudical language איפחז צלוחיתו means the overflowing of a glass. The most general innate characteristic of liquids as such would be the lack of cohesion, instability. — תותר is a Hiphil form, and so does not mean “you may not have pre-eminence”, but is the predicate of the subject פחז, “the unstableness of your character does not allow you the pre-eminence, because you etc.” “then you disgraced him who etc. i.e. yourself, a gentle circumlocation. But as nevertheless he says here: “you are the most precious gem in my treasury, are כחי וראשית אוני, but for the leadership of the family you are not qualified, for that one must be עז, may not be moved by soft flattering winds nor by stormy hurricanes, must have strong inner firmness not be unstable like water”, from all this it is evident that the incident referred to could not have had that importance which the harsh blunt words וישכב וגו׳ would seem to imply. To a son who was the כח וראשית אונו of his father and who should be יתר שאת ויתר עז any offence which otherwise would be considered quite lightly, is taken most seriously. Had he really committed a real sin, surely a Jacob would not have designated a Reuben by such a mild and gentle epithet as merely פחז כמים.

V. 5. In Simeon and Levi’s characters a trait was prominent which really would quite specially have qualified them to be placed at the head of the future nation. They were אחים had the feeling of communal brotherhood developed to a high degree, which, completely free from egoism, made them feel affected by any wrong done to the least important member of the family circle, as if it had been done to them themselves. But כלי מכרותיהם .חמס מכרותיהם: either derived from כור and then מכרה would be “means” in general, or more probably from כרה to dig, which, in contrast to חפר which means to dig right down, means to start digging, and then came to be used for preparation in general, as e.g. a meal, finally also for acquiring as אשר כריתי לי (Gen. L.5) or ואכרה לי (Hosea III.2) or מים תכרו מאתם בכסף ושתיתם (Deut. II.6). From the quotation from Hosea מכרה would quite specially refer to the means for obtaining a person. Simeon and Levi used what appeared to be quite peaceful and friendly means of agreement, made conditions for Schechem to fulfil under the guise of מהר ומתן and then used them as the means for the act of dreadful violence.

V. 6. סוד: joint conference, council. קהל: coming together to carry out. Accordingly: Simeon and Levi would have indeed the right dispositions and feelings for leadership but the means and ways they adopt are objectionable, therefore my will (the will of my nation) may not enter their council i.e. their decisions may never decide the nation’s actions, their counsel may never represent the will of the nation. “With their gatherings my honour may never be identified” (תחד from יחד), the national teachings may never rest on their actions. When they advise, my will may never be staked, nor my honour when they act; for באפם הרגו איש, their אף, their rage was perfectly justified, but in their rage they committed “murder”, in their rage they killed innocent men — had they confined their attack to the young squire Jacob would hardly have blamed them so severely.

וברצונם עקרו שור. What this means is more than doubtful. שור definitely means ox, and עַקֵר definitely to lame, to hamstring. But רצון, in any case, is predominantly only friendly good-will, and as it does not say כרצונם (as in Nehemiah IX.24.37 and Esther IX.5) but ברצונם it can hardly mean here capriciously, just as they pleased, but must just mean friendliness. So that it could therefore be, similarly to מכרתיהם, a description of their cunning, in which they pretended friendship, but שור, as in בכור שורו הדר לו mean that strength, which, peaceful in itself, proves itself when it comes to a fight, and then the sense would be: — “For in their rage they murdered men whose strength — ordinarily peaceful but if attacked able bravely to be used in defence — they had lamed by their friendliness”, by their friendly persuasion to מילה they had first weakened their power of resistance, then in their weak state had attacked them, so that it was not even an heroic act! Therefore

V. 7. ארור אפם וגו׳, therefore no blessing can rest on the אף and their עברה, their ruthless impetuosity must be kept in check by being cursed. אף from the root אנף, the inner feeling which comes out externally, is expressed on the face, attitude, etc. (חמה, wrath, which boils inside). עברה fury which takes you quite beyond yourself, with which all reason is lost. Accordingly: when they want to do anything in their anger, it is עז, not to be overcome, and their עברה, their fury is קשה, obstinate, not to be tempered by any consideration, therefore both must be struck by ארור, must be made ערירים, unfruitful, unsuccessful, without result. Their אף and their עברה may never make propaganda, and their position in the future must be arranged accordingly. They are unfit for leadership, more, as leaders of the nation they would constitute a danger. Whereas Reuben had too little self-confidence, in them the consciousness of their own power and strength was too hot, and, where it was a matter of the general welfare, was ruthless, knew no bounds.

It is of the most profound importance that here, at once, at laying the foundation of the Jewish nation, a curse is laid on any and every transgression of the laws of morality and justice even if done in the interests of the public and the state. All other states and nations justify themselves by the principle that public and state interests sanctify everything. Cunning, trickery and force, which in private life would be punished with prison and gallows are rewarded with civic honours and medals, the laws of morality only exist for private life, but in politics and diplomacy the only code recognised is the interests of the party or state. The original testament for the Jewish nation here lays a curse on all trickery and violence even if practiced for the most justified cause in the public interest, and perpetuates the teaching that even in public life and in the public interests, not only the end but the means too must be pure. In no case does the end justify the means.
But nevertheless it is only their אף and their עברה which is cursed. The curse is not directed at them nor on their effort in itself.

חלק .אחלקם ביעקב ואפיצם בישראל, to divide up, not with the intention of breaking up a hitherto whole, but rather to portion out something valuable so that as many people as possible can have a part of it.
הפיץ ,פוץ on the other hand, to scatter, to divide up into the smallest possible pieces so that the whole no longer remains intact as such.
יעקב, the Galut aspect of the Jewish people, oppressed, persecuted.

ישראל, the “God won” victorious aspect of the Jewish people. Accordingly: the danger to the general weal by Simeon and Levi’s excessive impetuosity and choleric disposition is only present at a time when the nation is flourishing, when it forms a powerful body of people who could easily be influenced by two compact tribes filled with glowing feelings of strength and power and of the unity and brotherhood of the whole nation. Therefore in אפיצם :ישראל in a flourishing state of Israel they are to be scattered. As actually happened. Levi received no province at all when the land was divided up, and his existence was, through מעשר, made entirely dependent on the good-will of each individual. For the Jewish tithe, in contrast to the later and present-day tithe of the Church and landlord, was absolutely ממון שאין לו תובעים, a tax which it was certainly the duty of the occupier of the land to pay, but to which no particular Levite had any direct claim. The one who had to pay it could give the tithe to any one of the tribe of Levi that he pleased and none had the right to demand it from him. Simeon’s province was in an enclave, entirely shut in by Judah and made it completely dependent on that powerful tribe. So that at the time when Israel was in a flourishing state, Simeon and Levi’s political influence was completely paralysed.

But in Galut, where the pressure of our fate bows everything down and the nation itself torn asunder, there the danger lies, that all feelings of one’s own importance becomes lost, and the sense of oppression kills all spiritual force and energy. That even the wandering Jew, peddling through Europe, still looked down on the street boys of the various countries with proud feeling of his own value, and he, downtrodden and driven all over the world still keeps the feelings of the importance of his own person and the sense of belonging to his people, for that אחלקם ביעקב, it was of the greatest benefit that the tribes of Simeon and Levi were scattered amongst the other tribes, which (the majority of teachers came from the tribe of Simeon — see below — so that most probably they too were to be found in all parts of the land I.L.) had the natural result, that, when the state collapsed and the nation scattered in all directions, in this dispersion, Simeonites and Levites would be found everywhere, who, with their fiery and proud dispositions would keep alive the energy and the courage, the fire and the noble Jewish pride of the Jewish spirit, outliving the loss of the state. An old tradition comments that at all times the tribes of Simeon and Levi constituted the most important contingent of the Jewish teachers and scholars and scribes: — משמעון סופרים ומשנים בבתי כנסיות ומשבט לוי בתי מדרשות שהיו עוסקין בתורה “Scribes and teachers in the synagogue came from Simeon, and from Levi schools where the study of the Torah was pursued” (ב״ר צ״ח).

V. 8. As Jacob mustered his sons to find one who was qualified to be the leader, and had found Reuben, Simeon and Levi unfit for that leadership, he comes to Judah and proclaims: “Thou art the one, thou art the one who is called on for the post, thou combinest all the qualities demanded, which Reuben on the one hand, Simeon and Levi on the other, lack”. ידך בערף אויביך, not even your sword, your own natural power keeps your enemies down, you commit no murder, you require no כלי חמס against your enemies. The development of your power will bring about such respect, that your enemies will turn their backs to you and not dare attack you, will be pleased if you leave them alone. And internally, you will stand in such noble superiority that your brethren will voluntarily submit themselves to you.
V. 9. You combine the courage of youth with the prudence of age, have no lust for fighting and plunder for its own sake, are no wildcat and no wolf, are a lion and above low robbery with murder.

כרע רבץ וגו׳, not in fighting and in the thick of the fray does Judah’s greatness lie. Not flaring-up courage, which in the hour of danger wins respect, and then becomes languid, is what distinguished him, even when he is quietly resting he remains a lion. The greatness which commands respect which he develops in political repose ensures security from without, and internally grants the peace which, under his guidance, allows development to proceed along well-planned lines. It is regrettable that the actual meaning of לביא is unknown. It is certainly as characteristic as גור and אריה. Possibly its meaning lies in the root לבה which in Rabbinic Hebrew means inflamed, enkindled, the same meaning as להב, and לביא would be excited, inflamed lion. וכלביא מי יקימנו who would stir him up that he rises like an inflamed lion!

V. 10. This trend in Judah’s character to have influence in the nation both internally and externally befitted him for “sceptre and law-giving style”, to be the Lord protector of both material and spiritual forces. שבט, related to שפט ,שפת, is the symbolic expression for force used to bring matters into due order and to keep them there. The baton, the power to direct order will not depart from him nor מחקק מבין רגליו. There is no need to seek analogy with שליתה בין רגליה. From Numb. XXI. 18.באר חפרוה וגו׳ כרוה וגו׳ במחוקק במשענתם where מחוקק is placed together with the princely baton, and both are used, if not to dig right down to the well (חפר), at least for starting the digging, turning over the first piece of soil (כרה), it is evident that מחוקק designates a style for writing or engraving, an instrument of much larger dimensions and much stronger than our pens. Perhaps an instrument for making inscriptions in stone, a chisel. More, the construction במחוקק במשענותם itself almost leads one to suppose that מחוקק is a point on the end of their staff serving for inscriptions. Anyway it is evident that the ruler sat with a baton, the emblem of his power, and a staff with a style on its end, “beween his feet”, and that is what the לא יסור מבין רגליו could refer to here. Sceptre and law-inscribing style will always rest between Judah’s feet. The authority that looks after the keeping and consciousness of the Divine Law, the Torah, (ריש גלותא) שבט and the (נשיא) מחוקק will always be of the tribe of Judah.

שילה. עד כי יבא שילה can be derived from שול, the lower hem of a garment, and denote the extreme end. Jacob is lying here on his death bed, at the very first beginning of the nation of which the foundation stone has hardly been laid, and looks down the centuries at the last “sprout from the stem” of Judah. The suffix ו is written with ה to indicate weakness (feminine I.L.) and by calling the last generation שילה, Jacob says: — the time will come when the מלכות בית דוד will appear at its lowest deepest end, and Judah no longer as אדי, strong as a lion, but femininely weak, and one will think that it has reached its final stage where Judah’s strength and virility will almost have disappeared, and then — just then — when the undertakers of world-history will already have ordered the coffin for Judah’s body apparently coming to its end, לו יקהת עמים, it will manfully arise and to it the יקהת עמים will come.

יקהת, root יקה, identical with קהה (like יאל and יעל ,אלא and .עלה יסף and יפה ,ספה and יפת ,פחה and פתה) to become stunted, dull. Thus, of the eye that mocks at the ליקהת אם the dullness of the old mother (Prov. XXX.17). Here also, the dullness, the senile weakness of humanity. Accordingly: the time will come when the spirit of Judaism seems to have come to its end, and the world at large, have become worn out and dull, have lived through everything, tried and tested everything, feels that some new regenerating spirit must come, and this, that last sprout from the stem of Judah will bring.

V. 11. So Jacob visualises משיח (the Messiah I.L.), and how does he see him? He sees the saviour of mankind, the conqueror of nations, not on a steed, but on a young ass’s foal. The “ass” is always used to represent peaceful well-being, peaceful national greatness, whereas “steed” is used to represent military might. Similarly the ass is chosen from all the “unclean”, animals, to express by פטר חמור, the dedication of all one’s movable possessions. It is the animal that carries people at a leisurely pace and bears his packs and baggage for him. Thus the Jewish conception of the power of kings is not to be represented by horses. The Jewish Kings were prohibited by the Torah להרבות סוס. A Jewish King was also not to be chosen until after ירושה וישיבה, after the complete conquest and settlement in the land, expressly not primarily for military purposes, and it was just in that that the sin of the people lay in Samuel’s time, that they demanded a king to lead them in the wars defending the land, as Samuel reproached them Ch. XII. 12. ותראו כי נחש מלך בני עמון בא עליכם ותאמרו לי לא כי מלך ימלוך עלינו וה׳ אלקיכם מלככם. That is why here the one real true king, saving Israel and mankind appears on בני אתונו ,עירו. Two points are stressed with this picture painted here of the future time. The king of mankind does not ride on a charger, but on an ass, so he comes as the King of Peace, and he ties up his animal to a vine. If one can tie an animal, and especially an עיר, the lively mettlesome young donkey, to a vine, it is a sign of an infinitely increased development in nature (the vine stem growing like that of a tree), and in general of immense prosperity and abundance. Abundance in an infinitely increased blessing in the world ot nature, and peace in the world of mankind are the two signs that always characterise this final age in the mouth of our prophets. As long as the animal of peace is not placed in its true worth, the leaders of men always represented on horseback, on chargers, and as long as one does not tie up one’s animals to vines, for so long are we still a long way off from the promised regeneration of the world of nature and the world of Man.

A confirmation for the way we have taken the meaning of this verse here to be, could be provided by Zechariah IX.9 גילי מאד בת ציון הריצי בת ירושלים הנה מלכך יבוא לך צדיק ונושע הוא עני ורכב על חמור ועל עיר בן אתונות “Rejoice greatly, O daughter of Zion, shout with joy O daughter of Jerusalem, for see, thy King cometh unto thee, he is a צדיק and נושע״, he is no משיח ;מֹושוע does not come to help us, but to teach us by his example how we would be helped. He is a צדיק, a righteous man, and therefore נושע that is why he has been helped. He is no God, Who helps, but a man, whose greatness lies in his being so eminently “righteous”, that because of his righteousness, God has helped him. Further he is עני, without riches, appears as king without a civil list, and finally, not as a military hero, mounted on his charger, but רוכב על חמור, as the bringer of peace and prosperity, that is what חמור symbolises, and specially repeated “on a foal, son of asses”. This is very peculiar. It seems to mean, he is riding on an ass, but not out of poverty, the ass is עיר בן אתונות. Whereas other kings keep the royal stables full of horses, he has אתונות, a breed of animals for peaceful purposes. The animal on which he rides is one bred from his peaceful treasures. Thus, here too, בני אתונו ,עירה. At this final age of the weakness of the world (שילה) he suddenly shows himself virile and strong (ולו), and in face of that the nations admit themselves bankrupt. But in spite of his having become so manly and strong, in himself he remains modestly feminine and gentle (עירה and סותה) even after he has conquered the world and his whole virility consists in his collecting peaceful riches (בני אתונו). In a painting that draws a picture of the most imposing dimensions with such few strokes of the brush, one is justified in paying attention to the slightest nuances.

כבם וגו׳. He sees this last sprout from Judah’s stem — his clothes are stained red, but not with blood of man, with the “blood” of grapes. סותו, from סוה (from which we get מסוה, a mask) a sheath envelope, wrap.

V. 12. Thus he sees his final generation, sees the return of paradise on earth, the whole of nature rejuvenated as it was at the beginning, the subjugators and slayers of men no longer regarded as heroes, no drop of blood on the garments of its great men, and he sees this generation, with eyes more sparkling than wine (חכלילי only used for eyes: sparkling shine), teeth whiter than milk, the joy of life shines from their eyes, their white teeth prove their health.
This was something of the אחרית הימים, of which Jacob probably would have like to reveal more to his sons, had he been permitted to do so.

V. 13. With Judah, Jacob had found that which he had been seeking, a leader and a bearer of the whole future mission of the Jewish people until the farthest future. Then he passes through the rest of his sons, and just shortly indicates to each his speciality for the future nation, until he comes to a pause again at Joseph. With Judah the means for the defence of the nation had been found, he then passes on to Zebulun on whom the responsibility for maritime imports and exports was to rest. חוף from חפף, the harbour bay, where the sea is protected and enclosed by the land on as many sides as possible, perhaps also because in such a bay the currents of the sea are checked, and the waves break on the projecting land on each side, from חפף in rabbinic Hebrew, to rub against. Zebulun, accordingly, will live at a haven, a bay on the sea shore, whereby his province itself becomes a haven for ships, he will be visited by merchant ships, who will come for the products of the land, but he will not engage in world traffic, his extreme limit will be Zidon, that most important commercial port of ancient times. He will be a commercial tribe, but will not lose himself in commerce, will be satisfied with coastal traffic and with the visits of ships dealing with world traffic, and be commercially dependent on Zidon.

V. 14. גרם, bone but not the same as עצם .עצם designates the hard, strong, material, related to אסם, a heaping up of matter. גרם occurs in II Kings IX.13, as גרם המעלות, a step of the staircase, hence leading forward and upward (from which we also get כרם the vineyard laid out in steps, terraces), so also in rabbinic Hebrew גרם, by means of, causing, to lead up to. According to that גרם would not be bone as bearing weight, but as limb and joint, as the moving, working force of a lever. That חמור is used figuratively to designate a trait of character which is quite on a level with all other noble qualities, is clear from Is. XXXII.20. There it says אשריכם זורעי על כל מים משלחי רגל השוד והחמור “Ye are they that make progress (progress is yours) to whom all waters are equal by which to sow the seeds of godliness, who give themselves up to allow themselves to be harnessed to the yoke to work like oxen and to bear burdens like asses”, (literally: who vigorously stretch forth the foot of oxen and asses i.e. who vigorously go in the steps of oxen and asses, like שלח אצבע ,שלח יד. Similarly in Job. XXX.11 רגלי שלחו “they wanted to stretch forth my foot” i.e. to tell me how I should go, should behave) שור: the strength to work, חמור: the strength to bear. Accordingly חמור גרם, a flexible, supple power, which takes heavy burdens: Such strength will Issachar develop, a strength which works and bears, which combines שור and חמור in itself. משפתים, the place where two rows of household vessels are placed in order. Just as we designate homeliness by the term hearth, so, in Hebrew it is termed “rows of vessels arranged in order”. Thus we find the thought expressed in Ps. LXVIII.14 by אם תשכבון בין שפתים! O, if only you would satisfy yourself with your נות בית make your simple household duties the calling of your life instead of worrying yourselves with the “kings of the armies”. Accordingly, “Isaachar is a strong and hefty worker, who enjoys the quiet of his homely hearth”. Figuratively: Isaachar is a beast of burden by whose limbs one can see that he can work hard, and has indeed done so, and now, in the comfort of the homely circle he himself has made by force of his work, now takes his rest.

V. 15. In Isaachar that disposition is described which works gladly but only in such a way, and with such an idea, as has worth in the true Jewish nation. While in Judah the ruling tribe and in Zebulun the commercial tribe is presented, in Isaachar the real back-bone of the Jewish nation appears: — the Jewish land-worker. He does not work to go on and on and earn more and more wealth, the Jewish man of the people, he does not wear himself out in the pressure of his work, he works to earn leisure for himself. He is content to allow Zebulun to earn millions with his products, prefers to stay quietly at home, and sees that leisure, so won, won by one’s own independent work, is the highest prize that man can strive for by his work. For it is in his leisure that a man really comes to himself. For that he bends his shoulder to take on burdens, leaves the ruler’s sceptre to Judah, the prize of commerce to Zebulun; he is not tempted by military glory nor by the wealth to be made in trade, He knows other conquests and other treasures that can only be won and only nurtured in leisure. It was just this tribe that became thereby cultivators of the spiritual treasures of the nation. When, after the fall of Saul, all the tribes gathered about David, thousands and hundreds of thousands came from them all. Isaachar sent only two hundred, and they were ראשים, the heads of the tribe, — the others stayed at home and did not leave their work. But these two hundred were all philosophers and scientists יודעי בינה לעתים, they brought בינה with them, בינה is really discrimination, recognition of the true relation of men and matters to each other and the result of their constant reaction on each other. This insight Isaachar had won in its leisure for which it had worked and indeed יודע בינה, practical knowledge, not mere sophistic cleverness, but that practical understanding of the real relationship of men and matters which the true חכמת התורה gives, and indeed לעתים, applied it to a just estimation of the special meaning and implications of any moment. That was why וכל אחיהם על פיהם “on their pronouncements all their brethren lived”. Such knowledge of the תורה and its use in practical application to concrete conditions of life is not obtained by incessant application to the physical demands of life, is not obtained by incessant application to the demands of one’s business or occupation, but is only won in the quiet hours of leisure which one has earned for oneself by one’s work. It is therefore only obtained by people who realise that, for this purpose, וירא מנוחה כי טוב, who consider leisure as the real pure object for which one works, who, in the words of our sages, לעשות תורתם קבע ומלאכתם עראי who value the knowledge and study of the Torah as the essential goal, and their work as only the conditional means. And the purest, surest and the means most suitable and corresponding to this object seemed to Isaachar to be הארץ, agriculture. So he accordingly enthusiastically took on his shoulders the hard work of farming: ויהי למס עובד.

The use of the term עם הארץ to designate “an ignorant fellow” dates from a much later period, in which the quiet, leisure-gaining occupation of land by Jews had long been forgotten, in which knowledge and spiritual culture had become concentrated in cities, Jews lived on the land sporadically, and, far away from the centres of learning and education, under the stress of their labour on the land became intellectually stunted, and only too often, morally also. In תנ״ך the term עם הארץ is always used in its noblest sense as the “local council”.

V. 16. With Isaachar, the six sons of Leah were accounted for. The whole nucleus of the nation decended from her. Dan was the first son of the שפחות, whom one of the ex-handmaids bore to Jacob. The words with which Jacob refers to him are quite understandable. For that marriage had proceeded from the noble wish of his wife to have as many sons as possible with whom to build up the People of God. Dan was the first son of the handmaid of Rachel, who could not overcome her grief in remaining as seemed to be the case, completely unparticipating in the building up of the promised nation. Jacob accordingly says: Dan will represent his people as much as any other of the tribes of Israel. He is, in no way secondary, is as much essentially one of the whole, as the others (although the union of Jacob with Bilha and Zilpah was not originally intended by Jacob and these mothers were originally in a subordinate position). He is to be entirely equal to all the others, and on his part, has equally to contribute his special contribution to the national whole. Now follow the four sons of the שפחות. Whereas Judah, Zebulun, and Isaachar form the main features of the nation which are essential and permanent, the sons of the handmaids bring features which are not just essential and continuous fundamental needs of the community but are nevertheless useful and helpful.

V. 17. דן. It does not say דן נחש וגו׳ like יששכר חמור, נפתלי אילה וגו׳ etc. Don is a serpent but יהי דן נחש, Dan will be a serpent on the highway. דרך: the open highway, the military road on which one openly advances towards one another, in contrast to ארח, which also designates a private road leading from one man to another. שפיפון from שפף, synonymous with שוף, to glide from a place (שף מדוכתיה) Dan will not develop any fear-inspiring power, but the strength of the weak, brains, cleverness, and indeed עלי דרך and עלי אורח. When Israel is attacked by military strength, he will defend it, but not by Judah-like lion’s strength but by strategy. When Israel can not save itself in human social intercourse from fanatic malevolence, then Dan is the gliding rattlesnake on the path which bites the steed in its hoof so that the rider falls backward. It does not say, as remarked above, דן נחש עלי דרך — God forbid that this should ever be a permanent character-trait of one of the Jewish tribes — but יהי דן “Dan will be”, etc. will not be able to help himself by other means than by snake-like cleverness, and that is also probably why then:

V. 18. לישועתך קויתי ה׳. As Jacob sees here Dan being forced to take refuge in that kind of cleverness, he could very well have thought of the time when he himself found himself in a similar necessity towards Laban, and so prays to God that, even as it was granted to him to remain an איש תם, an honest man, in spite of that test of wits, so may it be granted to his descendants when, under oppressions and struggle, they are forced to use their wits in self-preservation, shyness and trickery may never be allowed to become a principle of their characters, a hope, that has been gloriously realised in the Galut-history of his descendants.

V. 19. Dan formed the defence on the frontier against the Philistines in the West, and our sages see in Samson the perfect type of the war pictured in the preceding verse of an individual using clever strategy against an immensely overwhelming enemy, גדד: to cut into, to suddenly drive into. גדוד, a detached body of troops which raids into a province like a wedge. Gad rests quietly at his frontiers, does not disturb neighbours, but if attacked, hits back lustily and pursues his raiders over the boundary, עקב. He proves thereby his fresh bold courage which, when attacked, shows that he knows what to do. The very opposite of Dan.

V. 20. Gad and Dan’s importance shows itself in defending their rights externally. Asher and Naphtali have their specialities internally in the land. From Asher, i.e. Asher brings it about that the nation has fat, healthy, choice food, inasmuch as he provides delicatessen “fit for a King”. It seems that Asher’s land was more suitable for growing luxuries than for the more ordinary necessities of life.

V. 21. If one could use deer as messengers, one would be sure of obtaining the most speedy delivery. Accordingly: what one entrusts Naphtali to do, will be speedily carried out. Naphtali does not act on his own initiative, is not self-productive, but what others have decided for the benefit of the community he quickly adopts and quickly carries out. At the same time he is נותן וגו׳. This נותן can not be governed by אילה (but the subject must be נפתלי I.L.) for אילה is feminine. שפר: beautiful. שופר, a hollow animal horn and שפרור, a rounded pavillion (ונטה את שפרורו Jer. XLIII.10) come from the same root. So שפר does not designate so much external beauty but rather the harmonious graceful conformation of the separate parts of an object, whereas יפה, (related to יפה ,יפע, radiant exhaling) designates beauty according to how it strikes the beholder. שפר is accordingly, arched, curved, the harmonious formation where the whole is built about a guiding centre point. Also the related ספר to count is bringing several objects under a single conception. But unity in diversity is the conception of harmony. Referred to speech שפר is the elegant beautiful articulation, moulding speech into beautiful form. Neither for deed nor for thought is Naphtali original. But he knows how to adopt the thoughts of others happily both for deed and speech, knows how to carry them out speedily and present them beautifully. Unless our way of taking it is erroneous, Gad and Dan would be supplementary to Judah, Asher to Zebulun, and Naphtali to Isaachar.

V. 22. בן פרת can not mean a fruitful bough. פרת altogether can not here come from פרה as then the ת would be the feminine suffix and בן is definitely masculine. צעדה can not be the predicate of בנות, for the one is singular and the other plural. The wording of the text would justify the following way of taking it. We find the root פרת used in Rabbinic Hebrew having the meaning of separating, being apart, e.g. אוכלא דאפרת and is related to ברת ,ברד ,פרט ,פרד, all of which have the meaning of separating, dividing. In addition we have the word אפרתי which in no way means of the tribe of Ephraim, thus דוד איש אפרתי (I Sam. XVI.12) but rather means מוכתר בנימוס ,פלטיאני, fit to be received at court, ennobled by his manners, so, in general, meaning distinguished, aristocratic, as ריב״ל and ר׳ יהודה בן נחמני explain it (Yalkut I. Sam. I. 77). It is quite in accordance with the fundamental meaning “separated, apart”, distinguished by character or position, apart from the ordinary.
