But the alien “has no real right to be here at all”, and so finds none amongst those who “rightfully belong here” to champion his cause. “No infringement can be made on the rights of the alien, because he has no real right to be here at all, and he should be thankful that he is allowed to be here and that nothing worse happens to him.” Such is the hard lot of the alien, the homeless, stateless one, without claim to rights anywhere. Out of this condition, that they were גרים in Egypt, all the succeeding miseries grew quite naturally. Because they were גרים they were made into עבדים and into עניים מעונים. That is why in the historical prediction of this misery, גרות comes first, גר יהיה זרעך, and then ועבדום וענו אותם. But here, when the deliverance from the existing misery is announced, the order is reversed, first ענוי then עבדות and then גרות. First is promised the deliverance from the existing concrete conditions which they felt so acutely, and then is announced the removal of the causative conditions right back to the root of the whole trouble.

והוצאתי אתכם מתחת וגו׳. Not, I shall do away with your burdens so that you can raise yourselves up by yourselves. The burden remains a burden, but I take you up and lead you up and out from beneath it. You remain perfectly passive at the deliverance.

נצל ,והצלתי וגו׳ a stronger form of נשל, of ונשל הברזל (Deut. 19,5) the flying off of the iron head of a tool from its shaft, hence הציל to cause, to bring about, that something, having no will of its own, which is being held fast by somebody as a tool, becomes freed from, or flies away from, this condition. Egypt has put your necks into stocks from which you can not get out. You are not meant to be able to get out of them; for what is to be shown is, that, from oppressions and burdens out of which you can not save yourselves, I have the power to lead you out.

וגאלתי. In Egypt you have no relatives, no soul that feels itself injured by the mishandling that you suffer. I stand up as your relation. I am injured, I am hurt, when any one of My Children is hurt. In Me you find again your rights and your feeling of self-assertion. Whereas הציל is deliverance from a threatening danger, גאל is deliverance from a destruction which has already occurred. In Jewish Law the גואל steps up when his relation has sold his heritage or his own person from dire necessity i.e., when he is already legally given over to loss of freedom or loss of landed property. That is God’s relation to us. The Egyptians had not the slightest right to the סבלות and the עבדות they imposed. But it is not only in ancient times, in Egypt, that states have thought they had the right to treat us as גרים, and as aliens, deny us the right to live in a country, and from that point of view to heap upon us special taxes and oppressive conditions, and Jew-laws for tolerating our existence in their state. So they did in Egypt. Then God, with His arm stretched far afield over all men and all things, entered the arena for the homeless ones, who, on that account had been declared to be without rights. He asserted His prerogative over all men and over the whole universe, and from this, the right to appeal to Him, He restored the feeling of having rights and home to those who had been bereft of both; and with שפטים גדזלים, with His great judgments (שפטים, bringing the world in order) forced recognition of the Rights of Mankind He demands. בני בכורי ישראל. In this גואל conception lies the whole depth of the הנה אנכי הורג את בנך בכורך — בני בכורי ישראל. You refuse Me My ill-treated child: I will make you realise what it means to lose one’s child.

V. 7. ולקחתי, then when you will have become upstanding free, and once again conscious of your rights, will I take you to be My people. As soon as you become free you become My People. My people, without a country, without a patch of land, a people, a Nation, by belonging to Me and by nothing else.

לי לעם in these two short words, by which here, for the first time, the whole future destiny of Israel is expressed, lies the specific difference, the speciality of Judaism, in which it is so absolutely unique. People thoughtlessly choose to include what they so unfittingly call “the Jewish Religion” in the category of religions generally, as being also a kind of religion, and then afterwards they are surprised to find so much within the purlieus of this “religion” which lies quite outside the sphere of ordinary “religions”. לי — לעם, to God — to be a People! This itself already tells us that Judaism, Judaism founded by God, is, in no wise, a religion. In Judaism we do find also what is generally understood by religion, but the idea of Judaism is something infinitely broader and different. In “religions”, God has only temples, churches, priesthoods, congregations etc., nations, peoples, have only relationship to kings, presidents, leaders, and become constituted and built up, on the idea of a State and not on religion and God. But here God founds not a Church, but a Nation, a whole national life is to form itself on Him. As a nation, not merely as a religion, is Israel His. (עם is the term used in Hebrew to designate a nation looked on not as a corporate body of men גוי, but as a completely self-contained number of people living in social relationship to one another). So when God says ולקחתי אתכם לי לעם, it means nothing else but:- the conditions of your ordinary social life are to be guided by My judgment and discernment; — the conditions of your ordinary social life are to be a revelation of My spirit. So that when a later generation (Read Jer. Ch. VII) was apt to relegate its whole relationship to God to sacrifices and life in the Temple, and to entrench themselves against reproaches of social sins and social degeneration behind the cry !היכל ה׳! היכל ה׳ (the Temple of God, the Temple of God!) the Prophet could thunder against them היכל ה׳ המה, “they themselves should be the temple of God”, and further on adding explanatorily, “for on the day that I brought your fathers out of the land of Egypt I spake not unto them of עולה וזבח, not for that did I take them into service. But this it is, concerning which I took- them into service: obey My voice then I will be your God ואתם תהיו לי לעם etc.” (Jer. 7,4, 22). It is true that God did also speak to us of offerings, yea, on the day of our deliverance from Egypt, it was an offering and only an offering by which He constituted us into a nation, but He did not constitute us into a Temple congregation “to bring offerings”, He wished to constitute us into a people, an עם, by that offering. It was just that first institution of an offering that founded the “State” on its most essential basic plan, as we hope to show when we come to it. While other nations have their national bond in their country, the Jewish nation have theirs in their common God.

ולקחתי אתכם לי לעם by the exodus, והייתי לכם לאלהים ;יציאת מצרים by וידעתם כי אני ה׳ אלהיכם המוציא וגו׳ ;מתן תורה by the forty years’ wandering in the wilderness, where their experiences were so thoroughly to impress them with the certain knowledge that ה׳ not only had brought them out of Egypt, but that He remained their God, Who in the present and for all future, would protect them from Egypt-like hardships and lead them out “from under such burdens.” “עבדים״ we have never again become; “גרים״ we should never again have become, but סבלות we shall always have to bear, as long as we are human, and, that we may be absolutely certain of God’s continuance of abiding and even miraculous support and assistance as long as we remain true to Him, that was first of all to be made convincingly clear to us for all time by the wandering in the wilderness; and only then,

V. 8. והבאתי אתכם וגו׳, will I bring you etc. So that Israel is to be fully constituted into a nation before they receive a land of their own. So that the possession of a country is not the condition for its existence as a nation, but rather the faithful fulfilment of their task as a nation is the condition for their possession of a country. מורשה it had been given in spirit to their forefathers, they get it only as heirs of these fathers.

V. 9. קוצר רוח seems synonymous with קצר אפים the opposite of ארך אפים i.e., impatience. The inhumanity of their present state lay so heavily upon them, and to satisfy its demands and get even a momentary respite for themselves, so completely took up all their energy, that they had no mind left even to give a thought to the future of which Moses would speak to them. They were so pressed by the demands made upon them, the work burdened them down so completely, that they had no patience to listen to him quietly.
V. 10. So, once again, Moses felt his complete insufficiency. And just as he was smarting under this experience, God summons him again to go with His message to Pharaoh.

V. 12. לפני ה׳, not אל ה׳. This expression does not occur elsewhere in the Torah except in V,30, where this fact is repeated. Moses says this, not to God but to himself, so that, speaking in a human way, God heard it. It was the perfectly natural feeling and the perfectly natural doubt that involuntarily escaped him. ערל שפתים is more than the כבד פה ולשון of above, (Ch. IV, V,10). That refers merely to a clumsiness of speech, but, ערל is one who has no power, no control over that which organically or by nature should be under his command. “Even if I conquer the clumsiness of my vocal organs, I still lack the actual power of speech, the right words fail me; with the very best will in the world to announce the most glorious news to the people, and to inspire them with enthusiasm and raise them out of their depression, the power to do so fails me, I have not the ability, and I fail, as I have just experienced”.

V. 13. Now God makes an end of all these dilly-dallyings. Up till now God had imparted his missions by אמרים the milder form of speech, used for speeches which are intended to win over the hearer to the contents of the speech. Now, already at V,10, וידבר, peremptorily, and ויצום, giving orders. “You have no longer to consider whether you are fit or not, you have only to obey”. Herewith the real history of the deliverance begins.

V. 14. But in a most striking manner, we see the story immediately interrupted, a genealogical table is interposed which concludes with the words: הוא משה ואהרן ,הם המדברים וגו׳ ,הוא אהרן ומשה וגו׳ etc., as if they were up till now entirely strange men whom we get to know here for the first time and only in verse 29, our last two verses are repeated and the story continued!

Why is this? But, let us consider what we are told in this genealogical register. It does not merely contain the direct family tree of Moses and Aaron, but gives a short outline of the two preceding tribes, and in their own tribe, not only the direct line of Moses and Aaron, but also all the side branches showing their uncles and cousins, great uncles and second cousins; so that we are shown the relationship of their tribe with the preceding ones, of their family and house in connection with the families and houses that went before them, and that were contemporary with them; further we are told the great age which their father and their grandfather reached, so that these could not have been very long dead when Moses and Aaron took their stand, and then pointing to these two in the midst of this whole circle of cousins and relations, repeatedly says: “these, these, were Moses and Aaron on the day that God appointed them”. If we then further consider what the exact moment was that this proof of their descent and relationship is placed in our hands, we can quite see the importance and the object of this whole communication.

Up till now Moses’ and Aaron’s efforts had been completely frustrated, and if nothing further was to occur, it would probably have been considered unnecessary to provide us with such exact proof of their parentage and relations. But, from this point onwards begins their triumphal mission, a mission which has never been accomplished before or after them, so that then it became a real necessity to first of all establish their parentage and relationships so that for all time their absolutely human origin, and the absolutely ordinary human nature of their beings should be firmly established.

Right from the earliest times it has occurred that men who have shown themselves quite strikingly to be benefactors to their people on account of their “godlike” deeds, have been invested after their passing away from this world, with a “godly” origin. We know well enough how, in later times, a Jew whose genealogical table was not available, and because it was not available, and because he brought the world a few sparks of light borrowed from the man Moses, became to be considered by nations as begotten of God, and to doubt his divinity became a capital crime. Our Moses was a man, remained a man and is to remain a man. When his countenance had already become radiant from what he was allowed to see of God, when he had already brought the Torah from heaven, and had miraculously and victoriously brought the people through the wilderness, God made him lay down here his genealogical table, and thereby establish the fact how ביום דבר ה׳ אל משה בארץ מצרים how, on the day when God first spoke to him in Egypt, people knew his parents and grandparents, his uncles and aunts and all his cousins, knew his origin and relations, had known him for eighty years in his perfectly ordinary human nature, subject to all failings and weaknesses, to all the limits and requirements of human beings, just like all other men amongst whom he had been born and grown up, הם המדברים אל פרעה; הוא משה ואהרן, they were men, like all other men, whom God selected for His great work, men like all other men who carried out His great work.

But if this “citation of origin” is once and for all to counter and oppose all erroneous deification, every illusion of an incarnation of Deity in a human form, if it wants to give us documentary evidence of the fact: Moses, the greatest man of all time, was just a man, nothing but an ordinary human being, and the position he attained towards God did not transcend the sphere of mortal beings, it also serves to oppose a no less pernicious delusion. That is why the register of names is not confined to the direct line of descent of Moses and Aaron — Jacob, Levi, Kehath, Amram, Moses — but contains the names of the tribes coming before Levi with all their descendants, as well as the other branches of the Levi tribe. For even if this proof of their descent in the first place establishes the purely human nature of Moses and Aaron, it might at the same time further the belief that, without exception, any and everybody is suitable to become a prophet. A man could be known as a complete idiot today, and tomorrow proclaim the word of God. The spirit of God could suddenly descend upon an ignorant uneducated person and lo! he can speak in seventy languages, which phenomenon is not without alleged instance in imaginary or pretended prophets in other circles; and then, the more ignorant, the more uneducated the prophet of today was yesterday, the greater the proof of the divinity of the Call that worked this change. Our register here counters this dangerous error. Certainly Moses and Aaron were men and nothing but men, but they were picked, chosen men. Had God wished simply to pick the first comer, other tribes than Levi stood at His disposal, and in Levi other branches than Kehath, and amongst the families of Kehath other households than Amram, and among Amram’s children there was the older Aaron. But God chooses the noblest and most suitable to be His tools and messengers. Before he receives his call, the human being must develop and mature his human qualities. It was not Abraham nor Isaac but Jacob who became the real founder of the House of Israel. Not Reuben or Simeon but Levi is to be the chosen tribe. Not Aaron nor Miriam, but Moses became the “Messenger of God”. Everything has to ripen up to the degree of fitness which qualifies it for selection. We have already referred on Ch. 2,11, 12, to the teaching of our sages that the spirit of God does not choose for its bearers weaklings or simpletons or dependants, rather, the messengers of God stood forth as גבור חכם ועשיר already before their being selected, bodily, mentally and socially “healthy”. Bodily, so that deluded impostors (i.e., those whose state of ill-health affect their mental outlook) should not send out morbid hallucinations which are given out and looked upon as visions of God. Mentally, because only a mind which has developed to its full human capacity can have the understanding to grasp the meaning of the Word of God, and hand it on. Socially, because only an independent person, who requires nothing for himself and seeks nothing for himself, can look on and understand men and things in that complete objectivity, without any, even subconscious, reference to himself, which is so necessary for a messenger of God.

In Genesis at the very inception of our tribes, we were able to catch the feelings and thoughts with which Leah, that glorious mother of our people, bore under her heart those who were to be the future heads of the families of Israel, how it was only with Levi that she attained that happy state of bliss which characterises true Jewish married life. If, as is quite probable, the thoughts and feelings with which a mother bears her child under her heart, are not without influence on the mental nature of the future man, then, from the very names in which she expressed her innermost feelings, we can get an idea why not ראו-בן and not שמ-עון, why it was just לוי who was suitable for selection. And when we realise the thoughts and feelings, the strong courage and inspiration to duty, that sent “a man from the house of Levi” back to a “daughter of Levi” even in such a time of terror; and if we realise all the feelings of anxious hope and hopeful anxiety, and the complete resignation and surrender of self to the Will of God, with which Jochebed must have become the mother of Moses, then we can well dare to form an idea what an influence these pre-natal feelings may have had on the future man, in whose character the most valuable trait, the pearl that most made him suitable for his high mission, was ענוה.

V. 1. אלהים לפרעה, perhaps not without reference to the thoughts which develop as being the underlying reason for the preceding register of pedigree. To a Pharaoh, Moses must finally have appeared as an incarnation of a god. To the heathen idea the first attribute of deity is the fearsome power of God, inimical to the greatness of men, and we should not have been surpised if, after all the wonders Moses performed, Pharaoh laid himself at his feet and worshipped him as a god.

ואהרן אחיך יהיה נביאך As a prophet is to Me, so shall Aaron be unto thee. This description is of paramount importance for the whole fact of true Jewish prophecy. As sure as Moses and Aaron here are two separate personalities, Moses who arranges and gives commands, Aaron who carries them out and hands them on, so sure is it, that that Idea of prophecy is false, which declares that God does not speak to the prophet but in him. This denial of actual revelations of God to the prophet negates the true idea that God reveals Himself to the prophet, and then the prophet brings what God has revealed to him to the people, but reduces the prophet to an inspired poet or lawgiver out of whom, while he is in a state of ecstasy, or elevation of spirit, God speaks. Actually the prophet stands before God, as here Aaron before Moses. נביא is accordingly a passive idea; הִנָבֵא (related to נבע to bubble forth, to gush out, a gushing stream. Prov. 18,4) used in relation to God, “a source”, a fountainhead to cause His word to be made known through the prophet. The prophet is not the originator of the words he speaks.

V. 3. אקשה, in reference to Pharaoh’s heart we find three expressions: אחזק ,אכבד ,אקשה. (a) קשה to be hard altogether, not to receive impressions, to let everything pass over one without making any impression. (b) כבד heavy, one can receive impressions, but there can be a big gap between the impression and the moment one lets oneself be guided by this impression, heavy, difficult to move, to set in motion. But, even if it takes a lot of effort this moment can be reached, but (c) חזק firm, consciously opposes any pliancy, any submission. Even the impression is completely lost as far as any consequences of it go. Pharaoh’s coldness, his apathetic insensibility becomes a means for the performance of a whole series of אותות and מופתים from which all subsequent ages could derive a knowledge and conviction of the Almightiness, the Presence and the Direction of God, in human history. After that there should be no necessity for נסים.

V. 4. By these אותות and מופתים which were to occur for the ultimate benefit of the whole of humanity — in the first instance, Israel is to become צבאות ה׳ and עם ה׳ before “I lead them out” to freedom and independence. The knowledge of God which they are to gain thereby will gather them as a צבא about ה׳ and unite them together as עם ה׳ (For note re. צבא see Gen. 2,1). They gather themselves around Me as their Leader, place themselves under My command, receive My מצות (צוה — צבא) for the positions to which I post them. It is this common life around Me, which gives them the common factor which unites them to one another as a national community. But Israel is not called צבא ה׳ but צבאות ה׳, quite in the same sense that it was not called only a גוי but קהל גוים, because it is to be composed of elements of all the most diverse characteristics which mark any national body. This is to establish the fact that the Torah, the common national profession of all Israel, is not confined to students, to professional classes or to any particular class, or any national peculiarity at all. The Torah invites and appeals to every degree and shade of position and class and occupation, it calls the whole of humanity to submission to God and His Law. (See also notes on Gen. 35,11).

V. 9. תנו לכם. Proudly, he does not require or wish for any miracles, has no desire to be convinced, “but if you want to stand forth, well and good, you must of course justify yourself by some sign, legitimise the position you take, by performing some magic”. — מטך There is absolutely no necessity to believe that this was Moses’ staff and not Aaron’s. (Some of the commentators put themselves to considerable effort to try and prove it must have been Moses’ staff). It is much more reasonable to take it, as the verse clearly says, as Aaron’s staff. There was no special godliness in the stick. It was simply a means that God used, and any stick could have served. — תנין not actually a serpent but a huge amphibian living in the water. (See Gen. 1,21). Pharaoh himself is described (in Ez. 29,3), as התנים הגדול הרובץ בוך יאוריו as the great crocodile who enjoys repose by the grace of the water gods. This sign says to Pharaoh. “You and your gods are no more than a stick in my hand.” We imagine that תנין here means crocodile.

V. 11. גם. Pharaoh saw Moses and Aaron as magicians, so he also called for his. — כשף .מכשפים — magic (etymologically related to ישב ,כזב ,קשב, fundamental meaning, ישב — body at rest; ישב ל- to rest with reference to somebody, i.e., to await somebody, to stand ready for somebody, that which ישב ל- is bodily, קשב ל- is mentally, to let the mind be completely at rest from everything else and to direct it to somebody, the most intensive concentration on the words of another person. מְיַשֵׁב ל־, or מְקַשֵׁב ל־ would mean to bring something to concentrate on somebody, or to rest on him, or to direct its attention to him. Now the business of a מכשף is nothing else but to supposedly לישב or לקשב the existing ways and forces of nature, either, supposedly to put them in abeyance, or to force their obedience for some given object. But the whole thing is nevertheless כזב, deception, it is nothing but getting the better of the insight and intelligence of the other party. כשוף according to the Torah, is a capital crime although it is כזב. All sins which are ע״ז, idol-worship, or connected with it, are not crimes because they are untrue and false in themselves, but because of the moral ruin of those that practise them. For good moral purposes no one has ever sought the aid of magicians. Where one has felt that the object one is pursuing has the approval of God, and is in accordance with His Laws of Nature, one has never seen occasion to grasp at such means of help. Only when the evil of what one wishes to accomplish prevents one reckoning on the support of the Lord of Nature, does one attempt, by the supposed art of כשוף, to accomplish the evil, in spite of God’s Laws of Nature, through the sidedoor of Magic. That is why our sages say מכחישים פמליא של מעלה ;מכשפים, supposedly put to shame the higher laws of Nature. In תנ״ך we find everywhere that the rulers of old had מכשפים in their service, just as today we find scientists in the service of the state, and if the scientists of today were to occupy themselves in trying to solve problems such as, for example, how to be able to indulge in every excess and debauchery without having to fear the consequences to one’s health, that would be attempting a כשוף-like misuse of one’s power over Nature.

חרטומי from חרט the instrument of writing (stylus) hence readers or decipherers of writing. Not necessarily hieroglyphics. There is no implication of picture in חרט and there was also cursive writing existant in Egypt. But it has erroneously been assumed that חרט implies a kind of chisel for engraving on stone similar to חרת. It is hardly thinkable that the slow engraving on stone was used for ordinary writing. The usual medium used was rolls of papyrus. In Isaiah 8,1, חרט is used for writing on a scroll, and there it is quite impossible to think of an engraving, חרט is very likely related to חרד which does not mean only a hefty movement of your inner feelings, but also a strong mental and physical activity for the carrying out of some desired object. חרדת אלינו את כל החרדה הזאת (Kings II. 4,13) חרד על דברי ,חרדים אל דברו (Isaiah 2,5). So perhaps a pen or stylus is looked on as the active, quickly-moving servant of human thoughts. (So in Rabbinic Hebrew חרטה is synonymous with חרדה as in internal mental activity of our feelings).

בלהטיהם. Later בלטיהם i.e., from roots להט and לוט. It could be that להט and לוט are completely identical, as רהב and כהן ;רוב and בהן ;כוו and בון and we need only think of the meaning לוט, concealing, covering up, to take both להטים and לטים to mean secret arts. But this is by no means necessary. It can well be that these two names are used for the same thing to show us the nature of the art. להט means flame i.e., light and לוט, secret, concealed, the hidden. The great art of illusion consists in showing the onlooker something bright and dazzling and thereby diverting his attention from what is really happening. This is the method of our modern conjurors. They draw the eyes and attention of the audience away from what is actually happening at the critical moment. Perhaps להט is the name of flame in the sense that being the brightest, most dazzling, it puts everything else in the shade, a “dazzling light” fixes our optical nerves so that we do not see anything else. The art of the magician was accordingly a hidden one לטים because it was a dazzling one. להטים were להטים because of their effect on the onlookers, לטים because of what they were.

V. 15. הנה. That is the usual time that he daily goes to the Nile. This river is really the origin of the whole existence of the land of Egypt. It was only due to it, that this most fruitful land could develop in the midst of the desert, so that the existence and continuance of the country hung on the benevolence of the river-gods. No wonder then that the King paid his respects to the Nile each morning. “Place yourself to meet him so that he sees you are waiting for him, and meets you before he meets his river.”

We are now at the beginning of the עשר מכות. Let us make a survey of them. R. Jehuda has already grouped them: ד׳צ׳ך׳; ע׳ד׳ש׳; ב׳א׳ח׳ב׳. This grouping is immediately self-evident from the story itself. Two plagues occur after due warning having been given and the third viz., שחין ,כנים and חשך comes without any warning. The third accordingly seems to be a punishment for not having paid attention to the preceding two.

On closer inspection we find these groups are in intimate relation to the three phases which formed the pith of the Egyptian Galut. עבדות ,גרות and ענוי was the progressive nature of the fate which Egypt’s crime against Israel inflicted. עבדות ,גרות, and ענוי were the conditions which the plagues brought on the Egyptians to impress them with the falsity of their assumed superiority, and to bring home to them the actual bitterness of the misery they dealt to their unhappy victims.

ברד ,ערוב ,דם (the first of each group) showed the Egyptians how they themselves were no better than גרים in their own land, and so how little justification they could find for treating the Jews as גרים and depriving them of all civil rights. ארבה ,דבר ,צפרדע showed them the emptiness of the pride and masterfulness which the possession of עבדים, of slaves, produces. חשך ,שחין ,כנים, finally were ענויים which made them feel for themselves what it meant to have to submit to a systematic ענוי destiny. מכת בכורות finally brought the whole to a climax and accomplished the redemption.
According to this the plagues grouped themselves: —

ד׳צ׳ך׳ was to remedy Egypt from the erroneous ideas of עבדות ,גרות and ענוי by the revelation of God’s Power and Almightiness on water and land; ע׳ד׳ש׳ by revelation of God’s Power and Almightiness on the living inhabitants of the land, and ב׳א׳ח׳ on the air which encompasses land and people.

ברד ,ערוב ,דם, come under the heading of גרות. A גר is he whose stay in a country is dependent on the goodwill and tolerance of others. The self-consciousness of the Egyptians had its base in their river, through the Nile and its annual overflowing they felt themselves more secure and prouder than any other nation, independent even of heaven, said לי יאורי ואני עשיתיני. By מכת דם, God said to them לי יאורך, if I will, your river will not only fail, but in place of bringing you blessing, and giving endurance to your land, will bring foulness and disease and drive you out of the land. You, yourselves are only גרים in the land, can only stay there as long as is My will. Showed them by ערוב, how it is only by God’s ban that the animals of the wild (ערבה — ערוב) give men the room to live on the land. He has only to give the word, and the barrier falls, and in his own house Man is no longer secure, and the only land which the animals still respect is just that of the people whom you consider and treat as strangers without any rights to the land. Showed them finally by ברד, to their stark horror, how it only requires a nod from above, and the whole climatic conditions of the land are completely changed. Egypt, which has altogether very little moisture from the atmosphere but gets it from the Nile, where it had never hailed before, suddenly sees its whole atmospheric nature change, and sees, in this first storm of hail the threatened possibility of becoming changed into an entirely different country. (That explains why the hail was announced with the words: בפעם הזאת אני שולח את כל מגפותי אל לבך).

ארבה דבר ,צפרדע come under the heading of עבדות. Two false ideas fill the breast of the slave-owner with the conceit that his superiority over a slave is justified, (a) the idea that he belongs to an altogether higher order of beings and (b) the idea of haughty superiority due to power and riches. צפרדע, the frog, one of the most timorous and remote of animals, which normally slips away before Man to the marshes and bulrushes, now leaves its secluded retreat, and boldly enters the precincts of the humans, pertly hops up even on the sacred person of His Majesty himself, and so teaches them how even the lowest and smallest animal has lost all respect for them, to heal them from their overbearing arrogance. And דבר comes, and kills their horses, the pride and renown of Egypt; and their asses and camels, the beasts of burden that bear their possessions, and their cattle and flocks, their real riches. And ארבה comes, and gleans all the riches of fruit and produce of Egypt — all that had not already been destroyed by the hail.

חשך ,שחין ,כנים come under the heading of ענוי. And what is means to lead a harrassed, painful and starving life was taught by the corporal plagues which the כנים and the שחין, and the three days’ imprisonment and hunger which the חשך brought (for it was nothing less than this which the חשך meant to the Egyptians). God requires no chains or cages to imprison men. God imprisoned them by Night so that they dared not move from the spot where they happened to be, and there they sat, chained to the spot, and went hungry until God gave them light again.

לך אל פרעה בבקר. As we observed above, the first two plagues of each group were rather more to teach a lesson, and only the third was really a punishment, and that was why the two first ones only came after having been announced beforehand. At the first one of each group, with which a new lesson was to begin i.e., at ערב ,דם and ברד, Moses had to meet the King at the Nile early in the morning, thereby saying to him: “Your future does not depend on the goodwill of the River but on the will of Him Who has sent me.”

V. 17. בזאת תדע כי אני ה׳, that the present moment and each following one is not the irrevocable result and product of the preceding thousand years, but that each coming moment is the direct product of My Will inasmuch as I am ה׳ i.e., hold the whole future completely in My hands.

V. 18. ונלאו, they will be brought to see the “negation”, to see the impossibility. It will be brought home to them by this, that, if things remain as they are, they will have to leave the land. No rain from above, no more water from the Nile, Egypt will become a desert. לאה the root of לא the negation of being, of existing (in contrast to אל the negation of willing). It is characteristic that the prohibitions in the תורה are in most instances not expressed with אל, as we should expect, but with לא. It appears that לא תגנוב etc., is a much deeper negation of the evil than אל תגנוב etc., would be. אל would presuppose a will, a desire which becomes supressed by the prohibition, but לא negates the practice of the evil altogether. If you are a Torah Jew, it will not be your will to do anything which the Torah must then oppose. As a Torah Jew not only shall you not do it, but as a Jew you will not do it. In this idea R. Akiba says that our fathers on Sinai greeted the negative commands of the Torah with the same joyous “Yes” as they did the positive commands על הן הן, ועל לאו הן (i.e. Will you keep? Yes. Will you not desecrate? Yes!! They put the same lively happy energy in carrying out a prohibition as in fulfilling a Mitzva).

V. 19. מטך, your staff, not the staff of Moses, the implement does not matter, there was no magic in the staff, it was God’s action. Before Aaron touched the water of the Nile before the eyes of Pharaoh, he is to wave the staff in the direction of all its different and derivative waters, to announce beforehand that the change which was to occur in them was also his intention and working. Otherwise, when the transformation occurred also in waters not touched by Aaron, Pharaoh could have taken the whole thing to be some natural phenomenon. That is also probably why only the water of the Nile flowing through the land in canals, aqueducts etc. was affected. Anyway, both in the proclamation and in the actual plague, the Torah speaks repeatedly and definitely only of the water of the Nile, המים אשר ביאר. Water of wells remained good. It was only the Nile, as such, as the basic proviso of the land of Egypt with reference to גרות that was to be affected
V. 26. בא אל וגו׳, not לר, visit him in his palace.

V. 27. נגף, related to נקב, to hit very sharply and pointedly. גבול seems originally to mean, not so much the border but rather the domain, related to יבול, that which has come into our domain, in the sphere of our possessions. צפרדע can not mean crocodiles, otherwise there would have been no Egyptians left in the land. It is clear that they were only annoying creatures, not dangerous ones. Tradition has it that they were frogs. The word is made up of צפר, day and דע, knowing (we have the Chaldean עור דעניא, knowing the time of awakening). An animal that is noisy at night, but at the first rays and sounds of day becomes shy and silent.

V. 28. ועלו ובאו וגו׳. These animals, normally so shy of light and noise, will come up out of their obscurity and disturb the whole country, from the King in his palace, even in his private bedchamber and on his bed, to the members of the court, and to all the people. They will make their bread loathsome in oven and kneading-trough, yea, hop up on the very person of prince, subject, and servitor, and so teach the Egyptians, who so proudly exalt themselves as gods over their slaves, how, even the smallest, most timid creatures were absolutely without respect or fear for them.

If we take the places together which are mentioned as being disturbed so disrespectfully by the frogs, we find reference to all the instances in which the Egyptian masters embittered the lives of their Jewish slaves. As עבדים our fathers had no homes, no private family rooms, no sleep, no proper bread (our לחם עוני also reminds us of this), in all these places these timid creatures promenaded and showed the Egyptians what it meant if one could not quietly enjoy even one’s house, one’s bed, one’s bread, without having to fear at every moment that one would be disturbed by annoying entries. It is characteristic that, when reckoning the houses (V. 28) the order is, the Palace of the King, the houses of the royal retainers and then of the people, while (V. 29) in reckoning the persons, the people are mentioned before the retainers. In outward appearance the houses of the court officials were, of course, superior to that of the ordinary populace. But when it comes to respect the actual personalities, under a regime such as Pharaoh’s, the court officials are the lowest. In a Pharaoh’s kingdom only the two extremes are free men, the king, and comparatively also, the ordinary citizen who at least in his inner private condition is unmolested, while the gaudily uniformed court officials are really the most despicable slaves, and tremble before the slightest change in the royal mood. “A fly in the goblet”, “a hair in the loaf”, and a kick deposits the gold-braided “great one” in the dungeon, to await a “suitable occasion” to be led to the gallows.

V. 3. If this is to be taken that the magicians also wanted to bring up frogs, and did so, then this verse seems quite inexplicable. Aaron had already brought the frogs up, over the land of Egypt, what remained for the magicians to do? One might think that when Aaron waved his hand they quickly did some hocus pocus so that it should appear that they had brought the frogs up. But if that was the case why could they not do this also at the plague of כנים? It also can not be that they made their experiment on some small pool water for it says “they brought the frogs over the land of Egypt”. When one considers the position of the magicians more closely in the whole story, they appear altogether very peculiar. If they were really such masters of their art, surely they should have used their powers to free the land from the plagues, not to increase them. Were there then perhaps too few frogs! And really it seems, in opposition to the way it is usually taken, that their efforts in each case, was to do away with the plague. So in V.14, ויעשו וגו׳ להוציא את הכנים ולא יכלו it means quite clearly “they did etc. to make the lice go away, but they were not able to”. It seems that the ויעשו כן in each case is generally taken to refer to the effect which Moses and Aaron accomplished, whereas to us it appears clearly to refer only to the apparent means they used, to the preceding waving of hand and staff. These movements the חרטומים copied, presumably to work immediately against the entering plague. That this כן does refer to the introductory waving is quite clear just from V. 14. In V. 13 it says also of Moses and Aaron ויעשו כן and this is immediately explained ויט אהרן וגו׳. So according to this it would read here: — Aaron waved his hand over the waters of Egypt. The magicians made similar wavings to annul and oppose Aaron’s doings, but the result was just the opposite, ויעלו את הצפרדעים וגו׳, on their actions the frogs came up more and more over the land of Egypt. A confirmation of this may lie in the fact that first in V. 2 the singular is used and here the plural. The relationship of הצפרדע to צפרדעים is the same as הדגה to דגים. The singular describes the creature as the whole species, according to its characteristics. The plural describes the creature in its masses, a mass of such individuals. When, here at the plagues, it wants to say that, at God’s behest, the species behaves in a way contrary to its usual nature, the singular is used. So הדגה, who normally are in their element in the water, died in the river. הצפרדע, the timid species of frogs, who normally eschew man, come up over the land. Had the magicians really brought up frogs it would only have strengthened Pharaoh in his refusal, and there would be no motive for ויקרא פרעה וגו׳ in the following V. 4. But, as we take it, when he realised the ridiculous impotency of his magicians, who, with their magic only provoked the very opposite of what they were trying to achieve, he had Moses and Aaron called.

V. 4. עתר .העתירו related to חתר to force one’s way in somewhere, also to row a boat forcibly against the current, hence עתר to entreat someone ardently. Accordingly in Hiphil, make my urgent entreaty reach God; or, just as one required an intercessor with Pharaoh, so, he imagined, Moses and Aaron did not come directly to God but had powerful mediators with Him, whom they could now use on his behalf.

V. 5. The motive for Moses making the exit of the plague itself into an אות, and not simply undertaking Pharaoh’s request, lay in the request itself. Had Pharaoh been already convinced, he would simply have let the people go. But as it was, it was apparent that all he wanted was to be freed from the plague. That was why the departure of the frogs was itself to be a further instructive אות; perhaps this would produce the desired result. Accordingly, the frogs are not simply to go back from where they came, that could be taken as merely the cessation of God’s activity and a return to normal conditions. They are to die, but as emphasised repeatedly ביאר תשארנה, not all of them, that could again be taken as some phenomenon of Nature, (cf. V.9).

V. 6. Our God is not just another god, not even the highest of the gods. For even the highest of the heathen gods is not free, is bound by the all-powerful forces of Nature, can be forced by necessity to act against his will, is thought to have indeed power to direct the fate of human beings within the laws of Nature, but has no power over these forces. It must be made clear to you that אין כה׳ אלהינו; that God can not be compared to any other.

V. 7. מלרע ,וסרו, against the rule of עו׳, which has only very few exceptions. מלרע the root would be סרה and not סור. In Chaldean סרה means to decay, become foul. In Hebrew, not סרה but סרח means to become foul. It is possible that here it does not mean, “they will depart”, but they will rot away.

V. 8. ויצעק, v.5 was the first independent act of Moses, the first word he had spoken on his own account. He had dared to risk it. A man who gives himself up entirely to God’s ideas, easily feels what is right, and hits on the right thing, in the sense that God Himself would wish, hence עצת מלאכיו ישלים, God carries out the counsel of His messengers. But just because this was the first time that Moses had risked to promise something without having been told to do so, he “cried” up to God that He should fulfil his (Moses’) word.

V. 9. מן הבתים מן החצרות ומן השדות the order is the reverse of that in which they came. חצרות are the courts and yards in front of the houses. Not only in the houses, but also in the courtyards and even in the fields, where they normally lived and could easily have returned to the safety of the river, did they die.

V. 10. צבר .ויצברו related to ספר ,צור etc. צבר, gathering together single scattered objects, so that they do not become lost by themselves. The intention is less to make a big heap than to prevent the single object remaining scattered. Hence also it is quite pertinently the term used for the miser’s collecting, where again his mind is not so much directed on the total, as the single coins. (ספר, joining the units to a whole, to count). צִבור would accordingly give the idea of a congregation, in the first place, more of a negative meaning, that the individuals do not become lost, that the whole should not be dispersed in particles. — חֹמֶר, a heap, חָמוֹר to ferment, חֹמֶר, clay, חֵמָר, mortar, חֲמוֹר an ass. The fundamental meaning: formation of masses, of heaps, joining together for the purpose of making a heap, of having a mass. Hence heaps, loads, beasts to carry loads, earth which naturally sticks together, does not fall apart i.e., clay, means for holding together i.e., mortar. Fermentation too, is after all, nothing but the condition of a fluid when the various similar constituents join together to separate masses. This combination of affinities is the positive cause of the falling to pieces in which fermentation terminates. Every fermentation forms חמרים ,חמרים. Hence עמר a sheaf, is related to it, and אמר, thoughts and words combined to make speech, sheaves of thoughts and words. — Now here it does not say ויצברו צבורים, nor ויחמרו המרים but ויצברו חמרים. Their purpose was, clearing the land from the dead frogs. But from that, unintentionally, heaps were formed and the heaped up masses only furthered the decay and foulness.

V. 12. The first two of the first group, corresponding to גרות and עבדות had occurred without effect, thereupon the third starts without previous warning, as a punishment. — עפר, in English we have only one word for the two totally different ideas אבק and אבק — עפר is the quite worthless dust, what we generally call “dust”, while עפר is the most valuable, (אפר ,עור ,עֵבר ,עפר) the loose particles of earth which form the superficial layer of the surface of the world, the fertile soil, the humus. Not the אבק, but the עפר הארץ, the soil, is to be struck and become alive. Up till now they have been made to feel their גרות and עבדות through water. Now their land rises up against them. Their fertile Egyptian soil is to change to vermin.

כנים from כנן to establish firmly, כַן a base, related to גנן and קנן .קנן is to “nest in” to make oneself at home. גנן to fence in a piece of land in which to live. גן a big nest, a garden. It is not impossible that כנים are so called because they are parasites, live on other living organisms, they are “nesting-in” creatures who live on others and feed on their sweat and blood.

V. 13. Parasites כנים, do not usually crawl on to animals, they breed on them. Not so here. The humus of the earth turned to כנים and they crawled on to persons and animals. This, too, was against the ordinary order of Nature.

In this punishing plague גרות and עבדות are concentrated in a personally painful manner. The Egyptians would have to leave Egypt if their soil — the pride of their existence — were to remain permanently changed to כנים, and if these irritating creatures were to continue without hindrance to crawl up and over the bodies of the proud and haughty “master race”.

V. 14. להוציא see Note on v.4; after thrice experiencing their lack of power, the magicians humbly acknowledge אצבע אלהים היא and do not appear again in the story. אצבע אלהים, just as a plague sent directly from God is called a נגע, literally “a touch”, so does the expression אצבע אלהים היא express the same idea, the finger being the organ of touch. Both look at it from the point of view, that God lets ordinary illnesses occur by means of the ordinary laws of physical nature. In these, God does not appear in direct contact with Man. But נגעים are direct touches of God’s Finger. The former, where it is only Nature that is directly governing, Egyptian art imagined or claimed to be able to master, but before the direct power of God, they felt they could bow their heads without shame.

V. 16. With this verse the second group starts, ע׳ד׳ש׳. It begins again with a גרות-plague, which is to bring home to them again, but in a more powerful form, how their very remaining in the land is dependent on the Will of the Almighty God. Above, Moses was told to go out and await Pharaoh at the Nile, for there, it was a matter of showing Pharaoh in the first place, that this powerful god, the Nile itself was entirely dependent on the One God. Here, Moses is to forestall Pharaoh going out, is to seek him in his home, so that he can realise that the river and the soil — the father and mother of Egypt — can remain unaffected, and if so be God’s Will there is neverthless no staying in the land for the Egyptians.

V. 17. שלח .הנני משליח in the Kal means to send something or somebody, somewhere, without the person or thing which is sent having special impulse of its own to get there. In the Piel שַׁלַחַ it has rather the meaning, of allowing to go, to let something or somebody go in the direction it is striving to go. The impulse lies more in what is sent than in the sender. It is remarkable that the Hiphil — which is used here — is only found in connection with plagues, and seems to be a combination of both ideas. It is the intention of the sender, and it coincides with the efforts and will of what is sent. So, specially here with the ערוב .ערוב is not a mixture of beasts. The very הֶערוב ,ה־ shows that. There is no recognised mixture of beasts. ערוב seems rather to come from the idea ערבה, the wilderness, and to refer to the animals of the wild. But the wilderness, in contrast to the humanly inhabited world, is called “ערבה״, either because, looked at from the human point of view, everything grows there in unordered mixture, or, because there is no separated property there, everything belongs to everybody. The animals of the wild by themselves have the courage, and would attack human beings, it is only God’s Will that has implanted i[[illegible]] them a certain timidity towards Man, and it is only this timidity and restraint from invading the precincts of Man that allows an ever-increasing space to be won for human development. Now, God has only to remove this restraint to show the Egyptians that the Nile and the fertility of the soil can remain quite unchanged, and yet the inhabitants of Egypt, who imagine themselves so irrevocably fixed to their land, must depart the land. The whole of Egypt is, after all, only an oasis wrung from the surrounding desert. God has only to nod and the Wild invades the land.

וגם האדמה can only be said (i.e. the וגם) from the point of view of the humans, for the wild animals are obviously more at home in the fields than in the houses. But it wants to say that the animals will drive you out of your houses and you will not be able to take refuge in the fields. If you want to escape them, you will have no alternative but to change over with them and flee to the “wild”.
V. 18. So you will have to go into exile, and just those whom you have treated as גרים, as having no right to be in the land, will remain undisturbed.

פלח ,פלה ,פלא to separate, clearly and decisively, something from everything else, hence (a) to divide, to cleave assunder, and (b) of occurrences, a wonder, something that happens apart from, without any connection with, an original cause. — בקרב הארץ: You are to realise that it is not only above the earth, in some unreachable height, from which I have the general direction of matters on the earth, but that I also guide detailed events directly down on the earth according to My Will.

V. 19. פדה ,פדות means, when anything has fallen into the power of someone else, to bring it out of that power. The fact that they — who, unarmed and unable to defend themselves, should have been the first victims — were untouched by the universal calamity, will be the mark of differentiation between עמי and עמך, between men who place their dependence only on human powers, and those who give themselves up entirely to God, and His commands. למחר, at this and the following plagues; as Pharaoh himself had asked for (V.6), so that it could not be taken as a natural occurrence. אות, it is an instructive sign, no מופת, no ענוי.

V. 21. Characteristically ויקרא אל- ול-. To have somebody called, is usually expressed by קרא ל-, to call for someone, to order a third person to bring somebody before you. קרא אל occurs only seldom, and is always significant. It places the one who is to be called in a much more independent position. Pharaoh had Moses told that he desired to speak to him, which left him entirely free to comply or not. At the same time he had him told that if he came, he was to bring Aaron with him. It is thus perfectly clear that Pharaoh understood and estimated quite correctly, the relative position of Moses and Aaron to each other.

V. 22. תועבת מצרים. An expression in the mouth of Moses towards Pharaoh which it is very difficult to explain; either, that which to us is disgusting that Egypt should consider a god; or, that which is disgusting to Egypt, that we should use as a sacrifice. In any case it is characteristic of Judaism’s attitude towards ancient and modern paganism. That to which other nations sacrifice themselves, is what Jews sacrifice to their God. The gods of other nations are the mighty forces of Nature to which Man must submit, as well as the powerful forces of Nature within himself to which he is subject. They worship the forces about them and within themselves. But the Jew in his sacrifice, kills the representatives of these forces, and thereby makes himself conscious of his power of mastering the forces of Nature within himself. In obtaining free control of these, and submitting them to the Will of the Almighty One, he frees himself also from the dominion of all the blind external forces of Nature. He sacrifices the gods in his own inner self, and thereby breaks the chains of the dominion of the external forces of Nature.

V. 25. התל from תלל related to דלל ,טלל, basic meaning “to tumble down from a height”. דל is not one who has always been poor, but one who has come down to poverty. טל vapour, which was about to rise, but precipitates, dew. תֵל something which was originally high but now lies in ruins. הָתֵל first to build up something big, and then to make it fall down again. Analagous to רַמֵה (from רמה to hurl), to suddenly cast someone away who placed himself trustfully in your hand, to misuse his trust, to his downfall. So here הָתֵל to bait, to deceive somebody with great promises. “You have raised our hopes high, do not cast your promises down into ruins”.

V. 1. The second עבדות plague. Pharaoh had considered Israel as his property, thought that as they were גרים they were legally in his power. Accordingly here: אלהי העברים and שלח את עמי, the Hebrews, even if they are aliens are My property, and they have Me to defend them, in Me they have a country, and as My people they can not lose their human rights. That is why the calamity was to affect primarily Pharaoh’s property, he is to be shown that even what is really his rightful property has only its existence by the grace of God, and that the property just of his slaves remains ensured by Him.

V. 3. All kinds of property are mentioned. Horses, representing the power of the State and cavalry. Asses, the vehicle of peaceful inland traffic; camels (גמל — weaned) can do without drink for a long time, hence the means of foreign trade; cattle and sheep, the means of labour and providing food and clothing. הויה the present tense of היה hardly ever occurs again, expresses suddenness, something that has no past and no future. The hidden and invisible Hand of God, suddenly appears in visible happenings. דבר the “Word” of God, that fulfils itself suddenly in the death of that which is affected.

V. 8. שחין. The second ענוי plague, corresponding to the כנים of the first group, a painful punishment for lack of obedience. קחו לכם both of them are to take both their hands full (חפן means a complete handful) — a complete negligible quantity if — as was here the case — it is to spread over the whole land of Egypt. This may have been to teach, that, however insufficient it may seem to be to accomplish the desired result, men must always do, fully and completely, the utmost that is within human capability. [פיח from פוח, to blow, to breathe, the deposit from smoke: soot. — כבשן, an oven, in which substances, such as limestone are completely mastered (כבוש), calcined and reduced]. .

That anything at all was to be taken and strewn over the land was probably to show that the plague was brought about by Moses and Aaron, at God’s bidding. But why just soot? Perhaps if we consider the meaning of the word שחין we can get at the reason. שחין occurs again in the Torah amongst the נגעי צרעת and we know from the Gemora that in relation to מכוה it is a wound similar to a burn, but not caused by fire, but by a knock, blow or pressure etc., i.e., inflammation. שחן in Chaldean means generally “to be hot”, שנה שחונה a hot year. שחין is accordingly an inflammatory condition which can develop and form boils, where pus forms which wants to force its way out, — אבעבועות from בעה, wanting to get out. If שחין is such an inflammation which ends up in pus, necroses and ultimate grangrene (the מוכה שחין ultimately loses limbs and members through gangrene) it is clear why soot was taken to induce it. There is nothing which, by its nature, works so much against inflammation, gangrene and foulness, as charcoal, tar, creosote and their derivatives, all materials related to, and even derived from soot. It is quite probable that soot was the recognised remedy for שחין. Here, just that, was to induce it

V. 11. The “readers of scrolls” were probably also the doctors. This plague, calling for medical treatment, accordingly attacked them first — and it seems, as they are never mentioned otherwise as coming together with Moses — immediately the soot was strewn.
V. 13. A גרות plague starts again, which brings the conviction that the existence of the land of Egypt and the continuance of the Egyptians living in it, is entirely dependent on God.

V. 14. את כל מגפתי. This time you will get some idea of what you can expect to get from Me, if you continue to oppose Me. כי אין כמני that you can make no comparison between Me and your gods, that I am Something entirely and basically different. בכל הארץ in the power of My might over everything earthly.

V. 15. כחד related to יחד, to unite, to annex. In Hebrew, where the words express ideas, every existence is a separation — and every real existence begins with a separation. The commencement of a new existence is being a separate entity, thereby the negation of everything else. Whereas all idea of non-existence, of ceasing, are designate by the roots of not being different, e.g., שוא, vain, empty, and שוה to be the same, to be absorbed in everything else, not to be for itself. דמה, to be silent, to be similar and also to fade away, to have nothing any longer to compare or oppose anything else, to offer oneself as dumb material to everything. So also כחד, a stronger form of יחד, in the Piel: to keep something joined, to oneself, not to share or communicate with others, to conceal; In the Niphal: to be connected again with all others, to lose all being for oneself, all independence. There is no such thing as absolute destruction, only irresistable absorption into other independent existences e.g., a dead body into its constituent elements.
V. 17. הסתולל :מסתולל means literally “to imagine oneself immensely higher than others.” You imagine yourself to be so wonderfully high above My people, I come out of the heights, above you.

V. 18. רפה ,הוסדה, its early weak foundation. Hail in Egypt, where any downpour at all from the air was hardly known, shows — as remarked above at commencement — a complete revolution in the telluric and cosmic conditions of Egypt, shows that it only requires a nod from above and Egypt is Egypt no longer, hence את כל מגפתי in V. 14.
V. 19. העז from עוז (related to חוז, from which we get מחוז, the refuge for one sheltering from a storm) always means a gathering together of masses before threatening danger.

V. 23. God had only announced hail, but thunder and lightning and hail came. This may confirm the assumption that hail, as atmospheric condensation generally, is accompanied by electrical discharge either as cause or result. (Cf. ברקים למטר עשה). God did not simply let hail come, not just that hailstones fell, that would not have indicated necessarily a change in the atmospheric conditions of the land. But God made the hail develop over Egypt in the same way that it forms and falls in other countries, and indeed, in tremendous quantities, in a land that had hitherto never seen a hailstone. This threatened a complete change in the whole climatic character of the country. שלמים ,ותִהֲלַךְ-form for the more frequent ,ותֵלךְ expresses the slow and continuous falling of the fire. The lightning was so continuous that no interruption could be noticed. וימטר God made hail ‘rain’ over Egypt, the wonder lay in the naturalness of the formation and downpour.
V. 24. מתלקחת “gripping itself”, the fire only affected itself in the midst of the hail, otherwise the hail would have melted, turned to rain.
V. 26. In accordance with its being a גרות plague, here also, as by the ערוב, the land of the Israelites, the גרים, was protected and spared.

V. 27. That which I have now learnt makes me see that God is right and we are wrong. I have now seen that it is God and not we who are the masters and lords of the land, i.e., that we have no right to behave to aliens as if we were the masters of the country. Pharaoh’s comprehension was only amenable to the effects of might and power, and under the tremendous impression that this plague made, some idea dawned in his mind of the unlimited power of the God of the Hebrews.

.צדיק ורשע צדיק related to שדך to satisfy: one who responds to the real objective requirements without considering himself. רשע, related to רשה to behave just as one likes to: one who acts entirely according to his own sweet will. “What God has made to happen is entirely in accordance with our guilt, we gave no consideration to His Power and to what was objectively required, but acted entirely in accordance with what we felt like doing.”

V. 28. ורב can hardly mean “it is too much” since he has just declared ה׳ הצדיק. It seems, rather, to be a noun as in Prov. 26,10. רב מחולל כל or (Isaiah 12,20) ורב מושיע. He alone is the One who can master this thunder and hail. He is Master.

V. 29. כף the closed hand, the hand holding something. The spread open hand is always the expression of helplessness, that has nothing to hold and nothing to hold on to. כצאתי The town was full of idols, that is probably why Moses always went out of it to pray to God on Pharaoh’s behalf, so that it could not be taken that he was appealing to one of the Egyptian gods. The הנה אנכי יוצא מעמך in Ch. VIII. v.25, also probably means outside the city. But there, where the plague was only to cease on the next day, it was not necessary to mention it expressly. But here where Pharaoh wanted the cessation to take place immediately, Moses had to tell him that he would first leave the city, so that Pharaoh could estimate the necessary time for it, and realise that the storm stopped immediately at Moses’ request. Note that not only the oncoming of the plague and not so much the oncoming of the plague, but its cessation at God’s will was the most striking אות of the Almighty Power of God. The most powerful revelation of His productive, creative force may even now not yet bring to the world the realisation of the true idea of our Jewish conception of God; at the most it would reveal Him as the highest power of all powers, as the greatest might of all might. The Jewish conception of God is that which considers God as the completely free Master over His work, Whose creations do not outgrow His control. It was in the cessation of a plague at God’s command, in its negation, and in the differentation between Egypt and Goshen that, above all, God showed Himself. No other Power can regain control once the elements have been unchained. So the Jew celebrates the last day of creation, the Sabbath, the non-Jewish world, in thoughtless contrast, Sunday the first. The view that considers that the world came into existence from natural forces can perhaps explain the Sunday of creation, but never the actual fact of the Sabbath of creation. Why does creation not go on producing new creatures? The same creative forces of nature are still there. That is why God made Sabbath, the שבת with which Creation ceased, and not the day of creation, to be the memorial of creation.

V. 31—32. These two verses seem to be the continuation and end of Moses’ speech to Pharaoh. They contain the reason why (V. 30) Pharaoh and his subordinates were “yet far from fearing God”. “You know quite well, says Moses, that even if the flax and barely are destroyed (certainly important products of Egyptian agriculture, the one, the material for byssus and the other for the renowned Egyptian beer the זתום המצרי) nevertheless the most important of all the products of Egyptian fertility, wheat and maize had not suffered. You imagine our God has made a mistake, should have waited a few weeks later to send the hail. And because of that, because the most important of your produce has been left to you, you are yet far from really and truly fearing the Power of God.”

אבב ,אביב seems to be related to אפף, to strive eagerly for something (from which we get אף also, and אַפַיִם the yearning countenance; cf. גם also, and גמה to drink eagerly) from which we get אַב the stalk which sucks up nourishment from the soil and transmits it to the fruit. אָבִיב: the time and the condition of completed stalk formation.

— גבעול; the formation of words like ברזל from ברז to bore, ערפל from ערף to trickle or pour down, קרסול from קרס to bow down, kneel, allow us to presume the root גבע as being the root of גבע .גבעול related to קבע ,קוה ,גוע ,גוה ,גבה ,גבא of which the underlying meaning is, a collection, gathering, a concentration of matter, so, also, כפה pressing together, forcing. From that גבעול seems to mean firm hard stalk. — אפילות late ripening, probably from אפל dark, plants which are not so readily influenced by the light, remain longer in darkness.

V. 33. ומטר לא נתך. Until then there was no mention made of rain. We should have supposed that when the downpour of hailstones suddenly ceased, the mass of water-vapour still left in the air would have come down as rain. But that did not happen. Everything suddenly stopped. For that the expression נתך is most apt. For נתך is primarily used for the melting of metals (hence the name מתכת) i.e., the liquidation of solids — כהתוך כסף בתוך כור Ez. 22,22 —, and here can refer to the melting of the mass of hail which would be expected to occur, and rain descend in the place of hail. But against this theory are the words in the following verse חדל המטר which implies that rain had actually been falling.

V. 1. As by all the עבדות plagues, the previous צפרדע and דבר, so here, at the third and last plague we find בא אל פרעה, go in to Pharaoh, seek him in his Palace, in the midst of all his splendour. For these plagues were to make Pharaoh conscious of the fact that even if the river and the soil, the land with all its luxurious riches of nature remained unchanged, yet the use and enjoyment of all this richness depended on the consent of God. If he, proud of the possession of all this, considered aliens as being without rights, and thought he was justified in making them pay for the small amount of use of it that was granted them, by giving up their freedom and independence and enslaving them, then God would know how to destroy all this richness, and to send quite other ‘aliens’ in his kingdom, strangers who would know how to devour all his riches before his very eyes, right down to the very last shred.

אני הכבדתי, thereby, that I did not destroy everything of his at once, but always left him — as is particularly emphasised with the hail — the most valuable of his possessions untouched. I left him something to which he could cling, and by sparing him to the last that which would touch him most deeply, namely the complete destruction of the real riches of Egyptian agriculture, he could always still have doubts of the real extent of My power. He could thus always take refuge in the thought that the real basic foundation of Egyptian power and Egyptian wealth was under the protection of some power that was beyond My reach. And I did this, so as to impress the stamp of My greatness and My rule successively on each one of those things on which men believe they can establish human might and power; so as to set up אותותי, the signs of the fact of My existence בקרבו in the proud powerful Egyptian State.

V. 2. באזני, not simply לספר to tell, but to tell “right into him”, to impress it so deeply that through the ears it penetrates the heart. עולל ,עלל, a child, considered as progressing and developing constantly, hence עלילה not an isolated deed, and עולל not an isolated action, but a developing series of deeds and actions, and עולל, to accomplish something by such a continuous series of actions. התעלל to reveal oneself in a progressive series of actions; ב- on somebody, i.e., to treat somebody simply as material by which one reveals one’s power by a progressive series of actions or deeds. Hence, usually, when used in reference to men: — treating people entirely according to your whim, having no respect for the human worth of the other party: hence, used in reference to God: — “How I revealed Myself i.e., My Power, My Greatness in Egypt in a progressive series of deeds.” — וידעתם, even if Egypt learnt nothing from it, they were done primarily for your benefit, to lay the foundation of your knowledge of God.

V. 3. Usually, for brevity’s sake, we are told of the mission that Moses was given to Pharaoh, and then at once, of the beginning of the plague, without bothering to tell us that Moses had first gone to Pharaoh and spoken to him in the name of God, as this was self-understood. Here it is the reverse. We only get to know what the mission was, when we are told of its being carried out. The reason for this is, that in this case, there is something special to tell us about the happenings when the locusts came. עד מתי מאנת וגו׳ “For how long then, have you made up your mind to refuse to recognise your poverty (לענות) before Me.”

V. 4. בגבולך: You give a sigh of relief, you have still got your old domain, and because the real basic riches of Egypt still remain untouched, you feel secure and rich, and accordingly believe that you are in a position to keep My people in slavery. If you will not let them go I shall send My army into your domain.

V. 5. צין הארץ. The human eye is called עין a spring, or source, not because the soul of man flows out of it, but because it is through the eye that the world flows into a man. The eye of a man is therefore literally עין הארץ, the source of the world. The locusts will bring about that nothing of the world will penetrate through, into the eye of man. The eye will no longer be able to see the earth. — הצמח לכם ,יתר הפליטה הנשארת לכם, in accordance with its being an עבדות plague it stresses just those riches which were the cause of Egypt’s pride, and as these had been spared to them, filled them with the hope that they could yet flout the God of Moses.
V. 6. It is not impossible that never before had locusts swarmed in Egypt. The real home of such swarms is Asia, from whither we are told the East wind brought them.

V. 7. למוקש. Moses had all the time been perfectly open and frank, how then could they call him a מוקש? But this confirms the correctness of the way we have interpreted the happenings. Had God sent one plague and let it endure until they let the people go, Israel would have been free long ago. But that each plague was only a partial one, that at Pharaoh’s request it always ceased — but only then to recur in a new plague, that made God’s power felt in ever increasing greatness and terror, this התעלל בם, that, through the pauses, Pharaoh’s heart was always encouraged to fresh resistance, this הכבד את לבו, from their standpoint, this could only be described as a “trap!”.
V. 8. ויושב. Pharaoh did not give the order explicitly, but his subordinates could see that he would approve.

V. 9. בנערינו וגו׳. We have no intermediary, no priests, no representative before our God. If we are to go, we must all go; the tiniest baby in the cradle, the last sheep of our possessions. Each and all are integral parts of our community. None and nothing may remain, for we are all to form a חג ה׳, “a circle about God”. God calls us together around Him, and when God calls us, He wants to see us with every member of our family and with all our possessions, about Him.
V. 10. רעה נגד פניכם, as לא אשית נגד עיני דבר בליעל (Ps. 101,3). Your intentions are evil (literally your faces are directed towards evil). You have something evil in your minds.
V. 12. בארבה, wider die Heuschrecke. Sie ist jetzt in ihrer Ruhe und ihrem Behagen im fernen Osten und du sollst sie aufstöbern.
V. 13. בארץ durch die Erde hin, um von überall her die vorhandenen Heuschrecken herbeizuführen.

V. 14. כן — כמהו. It is doubtful to what this double comparison refers. כמהו seems to refer to the manner of their coming, the numbers, the names etc., כן to the breed or kind. Possibly it was a collection of every kind of locusts. In Ps. 78,46, 47, חנמל ,ארבה ,חסיל, are mentioned

V. 17. המות הזה. In the complete destruction of every vestige of the Egyptian agriculture riches, Pharaoh finally realises the complete downfall of Egypt. If the locusts remain in Egypt and deposit their larvae in the land, all future harvests are doomed.

V. 19. ויהפך רוח ים. Usually the active verb הפך has for its object the thing to be changed, as, ויהפך ים ליבשה. But here it is the thing that is brought about by the change which is the object of the verb. It does not say ויהפך רוח קדים לרוח ים as we would expect but ויהפך רוח ים. We find exactly the same construction in Sam. I. 10,9, in Zephania 3,9 and in Job 34,25.
V. 20. ויחזק ה׳ וגו׳, “Thus, or thereby did God make Pharaoh’s heart strong again.”

V. 21. חשך, the last ענוי-plague. Just as the גרות and עבדות were all-embracing, hail and locusts threatening to destroy the whole land and the whole of Egypt’s riches, so this third and last ענוי-plague was the most all-embracing and affected the whole of each person. Every man was completely cut off from his fellow man, and from access to his possessions. He was prevented from using hand or foot to obtain the necessities of life. It was the most complete, the most comprehensive literal ענוי. It meant each man being held, chained and fasting, to the spot in which he happened to be.

וימש חשך (cause them to feel, to touch) the hiphil of מוש. Samson, in his blindness, begged his guides המישני את העמדים (Judges 16,26) “make me touch the pillars.” And ימש חשך would accordingly mean “darkness would cause the Egyptians to use their sense of touch”; they would in no wise be able to use their eyes for differentation of objects, they would literally be thrown back on their sense of touch. This certainly implies that they were also unable to help themselves with artificial illumination.
V. 22. אפלה is the higher degree of darkness in which everything becomes אול doubtful.
V. 24. After three days, when the darkness began to wane and the Egyptians again could move about. — יוצג are to be deposited here under control as pledge for their return.

V. 25. זבחים עלת. According to the opinion of the Gemora (Zebachim 116a) that the offerings of the בני נח consisted solely of עולות, that honouring God by שלמים, by the idea that the cheerful enjoyment of a happy life comes from God, and can be dedicated to God, is something specifically Jewish, the term זבחים here must be taken to refer to festive meals rather than to sacrifices which were eaten as meals.

V. 26. פרסה. As פרסה occurs also referring to the single-hoofed horse פרסות סוסיו it can not be derived from פרס to break, and mean a cloven hoof. It seems rather, from the meaning of פרס to spread over, to cover, to mean the horny covering which forms the hoof in which the claws of hoofed animals are set, and then פרסה would mean “hoof”. — מה נעבד את ה׳. This construction only occurs in one other instance, Is. 19,21, ועבדו זבח ומנחה, and remarkably enough, also speaking of Egypt. Perhaps נעבד את means to make something or somebody serviceable, as an עבד, which perhaps would be supported by ועבדום in Gen. 16,13, which Onkelos translates ויפלחון בהון, and then מה נעבד את ה׳ could mean: what we are to make serviceable to God, i.e., what we are to subjugate to the service of God in offerings. Then the expression, used just to Egyptians would be most apt. That which Egyptians honour as gods and to which they subjugate themselves in service, in Jewish offerings is subjugated to God in service. [See above VIII,22.]
V. 27. ויחזק, by the ever-dwindling darkness.

V. 29. As Moses could give this answer, the information about the final plague which was to bring about the end, must have already been given to him. This fact is also confirmed when we investigate the contents of the two following chapters, in which the chronological sequence of the events recorded require elucidation.

It is evident that Vv. 4—9 of the following chapter are the continuation of our verse here, of Moses’ reply to Pharaoh. As, however, he announces in this reply, the death of the firstborn at midnight it is clear that this speech could not have been made earlier than after midnight of 13th—14th Nissan, as the following night to which he refers was that of 14th—15th Nissan. This would date the three days of darkness, 11th, 12th and 13th of Nissan. But chapter XII tells us that already on Nissan 1st, Moses and Aaron — and through them the people — were told that the death of the firstborn and the resulting exodus would occur on the night of 14th—15th and that they were to take and dedicate the Pascal lamb on the 10th i.e., before the beginning of the darkness, in the sight of the Egyptians. If then, what is told in Chapter XII must have preceded this last summons of Moses to Pharaoh (our verses here), the contents of Ch. XI, Vv. 1—3 can also equally well have preceded it, and is only interpolated here to give the motives for Moses’ reply to Pharaoh. In any case the words עוד נגע אחד וגו׳ could not possibly have been spoken before the end of the plague of darkness.
