Hence נוה a place that offers herds or flocks all that they require, where they can remain permanently without having to seek pasturage elsewhere. (לקחתיך מן הנוה Sam. II. 7,8). Thus ואנוהו “I will be a place unto Him”, or “by my whole life I will prepare a place for Him, of which He will gladly say: אלהי אבי וארוממנהו — .”ושכנתי בתוכם. He had already proved Himself as God to my Father. As such was He recognised by my ancestors and handed down to me. But through me the knowledge of His greatness and His sovereign authority and control shall be raised ever higher and higher. Hereby the mission of every succeeding generation in Israel is indicated — to carry on the spreading of the knowledge of God, and allegiance and homage to God, to an ever-ascending height.

V. 3. Here begins the expression of the new knowledge which the event had given them. ה׳, the One who sees to it that a new, better future shall come for mankind, is on that very account an איש מלחמה a man of war. He fights down every social force in humanity that stands in the way of His plan for this better future. ה׳ שמו this fact lies even in His Name, The Name ה׳ The God of Love, by which name He has announced Himself to us. The path that leads to the ultimate happy solution to the problem of life, can only lead via destruction of the bad and evil.

V. 4. ירה ;ירה בים not simply cast, but to cast towards some particular place, to aim at a target, hence the usual expression for shooting arrows. Is seems related to קרע ,קרא ,קרה to bring something out of its natural direction, or what hitherto has been its direction, into another opposite direction. Hence the horizontal shot, opposing gravity. (Also we find המצבה אשר יריתי in Gen. 31,51, and ירה אבן פנתה casting at a very definite place. In Josh. 18,6 instead of the usual הפיל גורל it says: ויריתי לכם גורל. There must be a difference in the manner in which the lot is taken. The sentence in Prov. 16,33, בחיק יוטל את הגורל as well as the procedure which is described in Baba Bathra 122a, of how the Land was apportioned by Goral, and quite similarly in Yoma 39a regarding the Goral for the two שעירים on י״כ in no wise speak of a “casting” of lots, but describe the lots lying in a container קלפי חיק, out of which they are drawn, יוטל, quickly, without choosing: טרף בקלפי. The word הפיל used for lots, accordingly does not seem to refer to the procedure, but to be the effect of the lots. By lots something is apportioned to somebody, not by choice or by previous consideration, so the effect is, that something just falls to the receiver. In Numb. 34,2, speaking of the Land to be divided, it expressly says אשר תפל לכם בנחלה. The same in Josh. 13,6, הפילה לישראל בנחלה and also in Ezek. 45,1, XLVII,22, XLVIII,29. More, in one of these verses XLVII,22, נפל is used to refer to the land as well as the people to whom the land is to be apportioned, תפילו אותה בנחלה לכם ולהגרים אתכם יפלו בנחלה וגו׳. As possession of land is expressed in Hebrew by הֵאָחֵז to be gripped by the land, the last expression is quite fitting; and possibly the על פני כל אחיו נפל of Ishmael Gen. 25,18, may best be explained in this way. According to this where הפיל is connected with גורל it would not refer to the ticket or other token for drawing lots, but to the object for which the lot is drawn, as in Numb. 36,3, ומגרל נחלתנו יגרע, in Judges I. 32 עלה יהודה לגרל and elsewhere. Now in Joshua 18,6, it says, instead of the usual ויריתי לכם גרל ,והפלתי וגו׳, but ירה means, as we have said, to cast at a previously decided spot, and so would be apparently the most inappropriate term to use for casting lots. But according to Baba Bathra, at this dividing up of the land, the lottery was connected with the אורים ותומים to such a degree, that Joshua always declared beforehand what the result of the draw would be. So the procedure could not have been more aptly described than by ויריתי לכם גורל. If thereupon in V. 8 & 10 the procedure is called השליך גרל, its absolute impartiality, and the assurance that Joshua exercised no influence in directing the division, was thereby given. So ירה בים means literally “he shot into the sea”). God’s way of conducting war is the very opposite of the human. War-faring man shoots the shot at the enemy. God shoots the enemy at the shot! So also in V.1, רמה בים.

טבע always means “to embed” something in a material that holds the object fast. טבעתי ביון וגו׳ ,טבעו בארץ שעריה, etc. Hence, also טבעת ring. So this refers to their sinking in the soft mud of the bed of the sea. Of the leaders, the captains, שלישיו, it does not say טָבעוּ, intransive, as וצללו ,ירדו but uses the passive טֻבעו and also not, as elsewhere, בים but בים סוף. Both highly characteristic. They, the leaders who should have been the active directive of the whole operation, lost all power of activity, were gripped by a higher power, and tied up and held fast by the mud. And this did not occur in some strange unknown sea, in “a” sea, this occurred in ים סוף, in territory which must have been through and through, thoroughly well known to the officers of the general staff, especially to the מבחר, the picked chosen officers. (It almost seems as if these expressions are chosen to protest against all those fairy tales of ebb and flood, by which one tries to explain this passage through the Red Sea, as an everyday occurrence of Nature. If this were so, it would surely have been well known to the מבחר שלישים of the great Egyptian Army!).

V. 5. תהומות not depth but from המם — הום wavy swirling floods. — מצולות (shady depths) from צול, similar meaning to צלל from which we get צל shade, in general, anything withdrawn from the influence of light or sound. Hence צל shade, צל to sink into darkness, מצולה, the dark shady depth, and תצלנה אונים to become deaf, and צלצל a deafening ear-splitting instrument (clashing cymbals).

V. 6. נאדרי. From many places in the תנ״ך (Ps. 76,5, XCIII,4, CXXXVI,18, Sam. I. 4,8, and many others), it is evident that אדיר expresses not the character of grace, magnificence or beauty, but that of extraordinary power. Further, from its relation to עדר and חדר which mean a final heaping up to a mass, or, into a confined space, it would mean a mighty one, who by the extent to which his might reaches, is marked out as being powerful and mighty beyond all others. It would be the mighty one without equal and הֵאָדֵר would be, to become seen as unparalleled mighty. It does not say בְכֹחַ in strength, but בַכֹּחַ; it also does not say האויב but אויב. Hence: “Your Right Hand, O, God, which in this (ב) exhibition of might has shown itself unique in power, will henceforth terrify every enemy.” כח is the possibility of doing something. You have shown here what You can do, shown that You have a power of which even the mightiest of human powers must stand in dread, if it is an enemy to that happiness of mankind which You desire. Hence, also ימין, the Right Hand of God, which grants help to those threatened. The idea that the helping, salvation-bringing power of God lies in His Right Hand, and the punishing destroying power in His יד the Left, has its source deep in the Jewish conception of God. God shows His real power and greatness, in help and creation, in granting life and blessing, not in punishment and destruction. Punishment and destruction coming from Him, is itself only a means towards happiness and blessing. His Left Hand is merely an adjunct in service of His Right Hand.

V. 7. גאון is used towards קמים “Thou towerest high above those that set themselves up in supposedly great height against Thee.” גאה is not to be in high place, but “yourself to tower above”. Your helping Right Hand which has shown itself in such extraordinary power, frightens every enemy power from attacking Your protectees, and You destroy the built-up greatness of any, that, in spite thereof, do dare to take up combat with You. הרס is a very apt expression here, it means the knocking down of some artificially made greatness, a wall, a tower etc. תשלח חרונך, (you have only to let your anger go, not to hold it back I.L.). They have only a momentary duration because You held Your anger back. “Wouldst Thou let it go, it would destroy them like straw”.

V. 8. Verses 3—7 sing of the Power of God, which the event revealed, against all human might; V. 8—12 against all the might of the laws of Nature, and both, in service of His completely free, unfettered control of all matters, both helping and saving and judging and punishing.

אף .רוח אפיך meaning anger never occurs in the plural with pronoun ending, always אַפְּךָ ,אַפִּי etc. More, we are inclined to believe that even in the one connection in which אפים seems to mean anger i.e., ארך אפים, it does not mean anger. Prolonged anger would indeed be exactly the opposite of what is to be expressed by ארך אפים. We think that אפים does not come from אנף to become angry, but from אפף to pant for, to long for something. אפים is the longing, expectant, striving, contenance (see note on בזעת אפיך) and ארך אפים one who hopes for a long time, who does not lose patience if he has to wait a long time for the realisation of his hopes and desires. Hence רוח אפיך is “the wind sent by Thy desire, the wind carrying out Thy wish.” — ערם the stacking, heaping up of smallest materials, corn, dust, etc., here, the single drops of water. — נֵד is only used as a wall in this description, and in that of the similar passage through the Jordan. — קפא .קפאו, to become stiff, used for the curdling of milk וכגבינה תקפיאני (Job 10,10). — בלב ים on either side of the walls of water the sea flowed in its ordinary way, only there, where the People of God were to find the path of salvation, was the nature of the water changed.

V. 9. The song turns back. The deepest impression had, of course, been made by the last happening and that found its expression first of all in סוס ורוכבו רמה בים, and in this act God is conceived as איש מלחמה, as making war against all that is at enmity with humanity. Pharaoh’s might and power, because it was אויב, at enmity with all principles of humaneness, had been buried by God, in the depths of the floods. And (V.3) these very floods at God’s behest had towered back to grant Israel passage. And (V.9) the enemy had imagined he could use this very path to bring his nefarious intentions to a successful conclusion! The enemy saw in this path suddenly appearing in the midst of the sea a phenomenon of nature that would serve the pursuer equally with the pursued. Here again it says אויב and not האויב in order to generalise this idea of Pharaoh that refuses to believe that the forces of Nature are in the control of God, in carrying out His acts of justice. This idea is pictured in ארדף ,אשיג etc.

In a somewhat remarkable manner אחלק שלל, the division of the spoil which surely is the last act, after conclusion of the victory, is here placed in the middle, immediately after overtaking. We should have expected it to come at the end after תורישמו ידי. It seems, therefore, that Pharaoh wanted to encourage his army by the prospect and promise of loot and rape, or at least to spur them on to greater daring thereby. Probably after their late experiences in Egypt this was necessary. It would then not be Pharaoh’s thoughts, but Pharaoh’s actual words to his people: “I shall pursue, overtake them — you will all take part in the spoil — I will satiate my desire on them, and then, with drawn sword bring them back into our possession.”

מַלֵא נפשׁ .תמלאמו נפשי is to satisfy a longing. ונפש רעבה מלא טוב (Ps. 107,9) or וגם הנפש לא תמלא (Eccl. 6,7); למלא נפשו כי ירעב (Prov. 6,30), and elsewhere. “My cravings will be satiated on them.” I will take full revenge on them — ירש ,תורישמו ידי related to גרש means to force out either the owner from the property, or the property from the owner, both וירשתם את הארץ (Deut. 11,8) and וירשתם גוים (Ibid. 5,23) (hence also תירוש the juice of the grape pressed out of the skin). Similarly the Hiphil is used for the person (the heir) and the object (the heritage). But here, as Pharaoh’s intention was not to drive the people out, תורישמו can only be taken in the sense of והורשתם את הארץ (Numb. 34,53) “the land will be given over into your possession”; והורשתם את עיר (Josh. 8,7), “you will inherit the city as your property.” את אשר יורישך כמוש (Judges 11,24) “That which he lets you take into your possession.” So also here תורישמו ידי. My hand will let us take them again into our possession.

V. 10. An East wind had split the sea and towered it up. By a West wind God made the waters return. במים אדירים, Even the turmoil of the mighty swirling of the waves rushing together from opposite sides did not keep them up, but motionless like lead, they sank to the shady depths (צללו).

V. 11. Just as in V. 6 & 7 ימינך וגו׳ summarises the effect that their experience of the power of God over human might had on them, so מי כמכה וגו׳ summarises the effect on them of having seen God’s power completely unlimited and unfettered, over the laws of Nature, there are, of course, אלים, laws and powers of nature which are effective and influential, but, although they are idolised and worshipped, Thou art above them, and they are held and bound by Thy wishes and orders. Thou alone art free, art not bound by Thine own works, by the laws of Nature. Thou reignest free over the forces and powers that Thou Thyself created, but which men have deified and worship.

בקדש. The idea of קדושה is the absolute freedom of existence, of will and of power — completely independent, not conditioned on anything, not dependent on anything. not hindered by anything, not able to be hindered by anything. In its real sense it can only be said of God Himself. קדוש לה׳ relative, is that which is proclaimed free from everything else, standing ready for God, with absolutely all its being, all its willing and all its possibilities.

Human קדושה is the highest possible degree of moral freedom in which the will to morality has no longer any resistance to overcome, but is absolutely ready to carry out the Will of God. (Hence also the opposite, קִדֵש the highest degree of moral depravity, where evil no longer finds any resistance to overcome, but is absolutely ready to carry out evil. We have a similar contrast in כָּבוֹד and כָּבֵד where one expresses the idea of the amount of appreciation of spiritual qualities, the other of mass or material qualities). The word in the form קדושה does not occur at all in the whole of the תנ״ך. Instead we find קדֶש which is used both for the abstract idea of קדושה as well as for an object, sphere or place which bears the character of קדושה. That, at a sign from God, the sea meekly retired, offering salvation to the innocent pursued ones, and equally at His sign, crashed destructively down on the guilty pursuers, had demonstrated God for all time in His absolute power of free willing and ordering, had made Him recognized as נאדר בקדש as uniquely powerful in the “holiness” of being, willing, and means. This קדש, this absolute freedom of being, willing and means, makes Him the Unique One, and completely differentiates Him from all other powers and forces that are deified by men, makes the אלים to לא-אל.

הלל .תהלות (see Hirsch Jeshurun Vol. 8 p. 170). תהלה is the word in which the rays of the acts of God are reflected, hence, words celebrating in song the deeds of God. נורא תהלות would then express the idea: — Whereas we gather the rays that emanate from the act of God through which we have just lived, as in a focus within us, in inspired words, the first effect on us is יראה. We learn to fear Him, to be always conscious that associated with His Almighty Power and His All-pervading Presence is His Justice, so that we live true obedient lives in a way that will be pleasing to Him. Such God-fearing obedience is the first indispensable result which is expected from the knowledge of God, and from expressing such knowledge in “praise”. This is also what just above was announced as the immediate result of their great experience: וייראו העם את ה׳! All songs of praise to God are blasphemous if they do not bring about the fear of God, or which are even meant to be a substitute for the fear of God. These words נורא תהלות remain the most exacting criterion for all “psalm-singing” or “praising of God” which, consciously or unconsciously affected by it, has arisen in the world since this “song at the sea”. תהלות are the objective realisation of God, יראה is the subjective permanent result on us.

פֶלֶא is that deed which occurs purely and absolutely by the free and untrammelled will of the doer, independent of, and mostly in contrast to, the existing laws of Nature. We call it by the not very adequate name “wonder”. “Wonder” only expresses an occurrence according to its relation to our limited stock of knowledge. We wonder at it. Looked at from this point of view, are not the most ordinary happenings, the physical laws of Nature which seem to us so eternal, are not these the greatest wonder of all. But פֶלֶא designates the occurrence, not according to its effect on us, but according to its real nature, as being independent of, and usually in contrast to, the laws of Nature, and so are a revelation of the One Who is above, and directs the laws of Nature. The first and intentional פלא was the creation of the laws of Nature, and every further interference with these laws by God is a פלא, and remains a פלא even if we cease to “wonder” at it because we are constantly and daily conscious of this indirect acting and guiding of God. In accordance with this explanation of the root פלא, a vow, an act of pure freewill on the part of a human being, independent of the actual moral law, is also called פלא and it is a very precise and exact expression איש כי יפליא לנדור נדר (Numb. 6,2). Hence: “Who is like unto Thee amongst the gods, O God, who is at all like Thee uniquely mighty in absolute Holiness! We learn to fear Thee in all our praises of Thee, as Accomplisher of Wonders”.

V. 12. נטה. “You stretched forth Your Right Hand to help us (see V.6) and the earth swallowed them up.” Here the whole God-revealing event is again poignantly summarised. Our salvation and their destruction was one single act. As above ה׳ איש מלחמה ה׳ שמו (in all, the God of Love I.L.). ארץ, of course, is here, not in contrast to water, but to the Heavens. “Thou stretched forth Thy Right Hand from above, the earth below obeyed Thee and swallowed them up.”

V. 13. V. 3—7 & 8—12, sing of the event as revealing God in His awesome greatness and power over all human political might, and over all the physical powers of Nature. Now V. 13—17, sing of how the event reveals His Almighty Love in the guidance and upbuilding of a nation. The first two sets of four verses were dedicated to יראה, these four to אמונה. As in V.14 the Philistines are mentioned as being the first to be struck by their fate, and in V.15 — introduced by אז — Edom and Moab are named, it seems that verses 13 & 14 refer to the first effects of the exodus from Egypt, and V.15 et seq., to the effects of their journey after the passage through the Red Sea. When God had just led His people out of Egypt to bring them into the promised possession of Palestine, the inhabitants of Philistinia were the first to take fright. In the natural order of things they would be the first people threatened, as above דרך ארץ פלשתים כי קרוב הוא. But now, that God made the people take the way through the wilderness, across and along the Red Sea, so that they would approach the Land from the south-east, is was Edom and Moab that saw themselves threatened.

נחית, Up till now the subject had been God’s acts to Egypt. Now it begins to be God’s acts for Israel. נחה means to lead to the desired goal (see XIII,17). נהל is always used with reference to leading weak ones with consideration for their weakness. So עלות ינהל (Is. 11,11), על מי מנוחות ינהלני (Ps. 23,2), אתנהלה לאטי (Gen. 33,14) and elsewhere. Hence: In Thy love, hast Thou not only saved this People, but hast further undertaken to guide them to their goal. In Thy irresistable Might Thou couldst have taken them direct to their goal. i.e., to the place (or home) of Thy Holiness, but out of consideration of their immaturity and weakness, Thou leadest them along a path that is within their powers to tread, (see above ולא נחם אלהים וגו׳). The salvation from the slavery and mishandling in Egypt was primarily an act of justice. The further care and guidance, an act of pure love. חסד (giving oneself up to the well being of others). The goal to which they were aiming was not possession of a fruitful country, but a land that was to be נוה קדשך “the home of the absolute reign of God” (see note on זה אלי ואנוהו).

V. 14. חיל from חול, the feeling of dread of passive birth, where something new produces itself at the expense of what is already there. Hence it is mostly used for the dread of the pangs of childbirth. The inhabitants of Philistinia had already been seized with pangs of anxiety as they thought that the children of Israel would step into a new free existence over their destruction.

V. 15. אז, thereupon, then, as אז אמרה (IV,26). Edom was a military state (Esau, Rome etc. By thy sword shalt thou live etc.) its princes were אלופים, generals (cf. Gen. 36,15). Of them it is said נבהלו (related to בעל) confused, bewildered, overcome by dread of a higher power against which their swords and military strategy would be powerless. Moab’s princes are called אילים, powerful ones, aristocrats. Moab’s “rams”. Moab was a state untroubled by wars, proud of the power which the riches of its land gave it (cf. Isaiah 5,16 & Jeremiah 48,7). Its upper class and leaders began to tremble, יאחזמו רעד, for their riches and their security. The inhabitants of Canaan who were really threatened with destruction may be already considered completely liquidated. מיי ,מקק ,מכך ,מגג, all expressions of various grades of melting, deliquescense.

V. 16. אימה is always the dread of a superior force or power which is present. So (Job 9,34) ואימתו אל תבעתני or (Ps. 60,5) ואימות מות נפלו עלי etc. etc. פחד on the other hand, is the dread of a threatened danger. So fright over the imminent, fear for the coming danger. Or fright at the might and greatness of God, which had suddenly become apparent to them, and fear of all that they would expect from such power. — בגדול is probably a verbal form, inasmuch as Your arm shows itself so great i.e., which the greatness of Your power was developing more and more before their very eyes, they became rigid like stones. All this filled them with petrifying wonder. — קנית, Therein lies the whole of Israel’s destiny. By all that Thou hast done for this people, it belongs with every fibre of its being to Thee, with every ounce of its strength has no other mission than the most faithful carrying out of Thy Will, than that of becoming Thy “servant”.

V. 17. תבאמו, for this destiny dost Thou bring them there, literally bring them home. So לבוא is in contrast to לצאת, and תבואה that which is brought home, the harvest, the ultimate aim of seed, etc, etc. — נטע used of human beings and especially of a nation, means to give a permanent place for thriving development. So (in Jer. 12,2), נטעתם גם שרשו or ונטעתיו ושכן תחתיו (Sam. II. 7,10) etc., etc. The People whom You have redeemed, are to find, in the land to which You lead them, their native home and the soil for their development. There, all their forces and powers shall develop richly for the goal that You have set for them. — בהר נחלתך, it is not their property but Yours to which they are coming, hence it is only for You that they have to expand there. Palestine, a predominantly hilly country, and even its plains lie considerably above the sea level, is generally referred to as הר, so ההר הטוב הזה והלבנון (Deut. 3,25) הר זה קנתה ימינו (Ps. 78,54). It is considered as the gradually sloping down extension of the mountains of Lebanon, and so Mount Zion, the southern-most extremity is called ירכתי צפון, “the outermost spur of the North”. (Ps. 48,3 & Is. 14,13). Also ירכתי לבנון (Kings II. 19,23). ירכתים is the end of a place, opposite to the entrance ירכתי בור ,ירכתי הבית. Reckoning from the beginning of the Lebanon in the North, Mount Zion is the ירכתים. More, the whole land, the whole length of Palestine ranging from south to north, is all comprised under the name of Lebanon. Hence the limits of the promised land from south to north, and then from east to west are described (Deut. 11,24) מן המדבר והלבנון מן הנהר נהר פרת ועד הים האחרון, “From the wilderness (in S.E.) and up the Lebanon and from the Euphrates to the Mediterranean”.

נחל .נחלתך (the strong form of נהל) primarily designates the strong downward flow of water, hence a stream. Used in relation to social life, property which continuously goes over from one generation to the succeeding one, is looked on as a national flow downwards, and נחלה is an inheritance. But just as נחל means not only the stream, but also the downward-sloping bed of the stream, the valley, whose slope it is that makes the stream flow downwards, so נחלה is used, not only for the “downward flowing property”, but נחול means also the receiving, the taking into possession of such property, to take possession of an heritage, to inherit, and thereby wants to designate the heir as merely an intermediary. The heir receives his heritage to hand it down in his turn. Every heritage is only “the bed of the stream” which leads the recipient further downwards. Now, that which ultimately will come to God out of all the worship of other gods and other influences to which mankind has given itself up, is called by the name of נחלה. God is the Heir. So we find כי אתה תנחל בכל הגוים “for all the people of, and all that pertains to all the nations will ultimately come to you” (Ps. 82,8). וסלחת לעוננו ולחטאתנו ונחלתנו (Ex. 34,9). “Thou wilt always forgive our “crookedness” and our carelessness again and again, until we belong entirely unto Thee, until we have been freed from all other influences and have become entirely Thine.” So we find Israel called נחלתו. Out of all mankind, it is the first to fall again into God’s Hands as His “portion”. And here the land destined for Israel is called נחלת ה׳. It is the first portion of the world to return to His sole ruling.

מכון לשבתך. “The prepared place for Thy dwelling”. The real destiny of the land to which Israel is journeying is not to be a Home for the Jewish People but a Home for the Presence of God on Earth. — פעל ,פעלת is not so much actual producing or making, as doing something with an object in mind, to work on for an ultimate object. Hence פעולת שכיר (Levit. 30,13) is not the work that has been accomplished by a day-labourer, but the wages for which he has been working. Here also it does not wish to state that God had made the land, the home. As far as its concrete existence, the land and home of the Jew is no more the work of God than the rest of the world. But by designing the land for a people that was to serve Him with every fibre of its being, and above all, by His preparation and education of this people for such a calling, God had produced for Himself a Home for the re-entry of His Glory into this world.

מקדש וגו׳. “A place of holiness, O God, my Master, that Thy Hands have founded”. “The management of Thy Right Hand and Thy Left Hand, Thy helping, blessing-dispensing Right together with the might of Thy punishing, destroying Left, has founded this place for sanctifying Thee on earth.” Perhaps it is not going too far to suggest that the Dagesh in the ק gives the preceding מ the meaning of מן, and would indicate to us that this sanctuary which was now to be started and which the exodus had already founded, was only מן קדש a “part”, a beginning, a start in miniature of that real sanctuary which will ultimately be the sanctifying centre, not only of Israel, but of the whole of mankind. It is, for the present, only מקצת הקדש. And that would be why the name אדני is used. This name always appears in the mouth of one who would regard himself as an instrument, a tool of God’s handiwork. Moses and Israel regard themselves as servants and tools for that great future of the happiness of mankind, which God has now founded with the revelation to the world of the unique power of His Rule of Love and Justice. That is why the Song closes with words referring to the ultimate far-distant future: ה׳ ימלוך לעולם ועד. This can not only mean “God will reign on in all future time”, i.e., just as here, by the sea, we have recognised His Ruling in all His Almighty Power, so will He rule on for ever and ever; but can equally well mean “Some time in a distant, but none the less certain, future, God will be King of the whole of mankind”. For it is by no means improbable that ועד comes from יעד to fix, to appoint (as the Chaldean בית ועד ,וַעַד) and the combination עולם ועד would indicate the future which is hidden from us (עלם) but none the less certain, positive and fixed (יעד).

V. 19. Terminates the Song with a reminder of the event that had inspired it. Everything, God’s might over human, political powers, over the physical powers of nature, His saving, guiding and planting Love, Israel’s mission to serve and glorify God, His direct intervention into History as the beginning of His reign over the whole world, all is evident from the fact כי בא וגו׳ that Pharaoh’s chargers etc.

V. 20. Aaron’s sister: Amongst the women she occupied the position that Aaron held amongst the men. As Aaron spread amongst the men the Word that was revealed to Moses, so did Miriam amongst the women. תוף from תפף, as דבב the faltering word, תפף tripping gait, so does תפף indicate short successive beats of sound and תוף a kettledrum, or cymbal. Hence also תפף על לב (Nachum 2,8) to beat the breast in grief.

V. 21. ותעז. As the following להם is masculine, this להם can refer to Moses and Israel and ענה have its ordinary meaning of replying, rejoining. Moses and Israel sang, Miriam and the women responded. But we do find ענה also at the beginning of speeches where it can not mean reply or respond, as nothing has been said before, as e.g., וענית ואמרת (Deut. 26,5), כלם יענו ויאמרו (Is. 14,10), ויען איוב (Job 3,2). In such instances ענה nevertheless retain its original conception of response. As ענה ordinarily implies an answer provoked by something said, so in these cases it is what is said, provoked by, or in response to, what has happened. If it is to be taken in this sense here, then the להם would refer to the women, and we then have to find out why the masculine form is employed. Perhaps it would tell us that although the women followed the men in their inspired song, they were fully their equals in expressing the whole deep meaning of the Song, and in realising the high mission of the nation which is expressed therein.

V. 22. ויסע משה. This expression does not occur in any of the further moves of the people. It tells us that more than ordinary insistance had to be used to induce the people to break camp from the shores of the Red Sea. And indeed that which they had experienced on these shores was of quite sufficient weight to chain their minds and feelings to the spot permanently. And then, to journey away from this place of the most direct protection of God straight into a desert which seems to have been the most arid and desolate of all parts of the desert! Hence, also the term ויצאו, they “went out”, as if from a protecting enclosing place into the opposite.

V. 24. לון .וילונו to seek shelter from hardship, hence to stay somewhere overnight, and מלון an inn. From which we get הלזן על- to seek redress from a hardship which one has to endure, to put yourself above somebody, to speak and spread abroad complaints about somebody, to grumble about somebody.

V. 25. The salvation from Egypt and the passage through the sea had taught for all time that God was extraordinarily near at moments of extraordinary danger and crisis. But that He could be depended on for the ordinary requirements of everyday life in all circumstances, that the so-called little daily necessities of man are not too small and petty for the Divine Eye to see, and the Divine Hand to provide, that one who is faithful to God with every breath he draws, can confidently rely on the constant presence of His help, that is what the journey through the wilderness was to teach them. This journey was now only really beginning. From beforehand already, it had been declared to be one great object of the salvation from Egypt בהוציאך את העם ממצרים תעבדון את האלהים על ההר הזה (Ex. 3,12), there, with the acceptance of the Torah, they were to enter the service of God. This Torah that wants every second of our daily life to be spent in the service of God, requires as an essential trait, confidence in God. It requires complete confidence in the constant presence of God ever ready to help, and in the knowledge that carrying out His will, as expressed in the Torah, has the power to guide us safely and happily through the most desolate deserts of Life, and to sweeten for us the bitterest draughts that Life can offer us. To induce such confidence was the preparatory work which was to be accomplished in the wilderness for the acceptance of the Divine Torah. The first experience was to be gained at Mara. For three days they had found no water and the water which they did finally find was bitter. Thereupon God taught Moses of a tree, he threw it into the water and the water became sweet and drinkable. שָׁם there, in face of this experience, of seeing how the bitterest becomes sweet by that which God teaches us to combine with it, there God gave them the fundaments of law and justice, and made them look upon His Law and His Justice as the remedy for all physical and social ills, inasmuch as He proclaimed Himself thereby as their “Doctor”, כי אני ה׳ רופאך.

It is quite evident that the “foundation of Law and Justice” was in connection with this sweetening of the bitter waters by the addition of the ingredient that God had taught them to use, and that this experience was to make them realise the value and the meaning of God’s Laws for our daily earthly lives. That is vouched for by the שם, there did He gives them the fundaments of Law and Justice, and also by the proclamation which God immediately made on the value of His Law which He declares as the prophylactic medicine against all earthly evils. Hence, also the dictum of ר׳ שמעון בן יוחאי: דבר מן התורה הראהו, שנאמר ויורהו ה׳ עץ. ויראהו אינו אומר אלא ויורהו, כענין שנאמר ויורני ויאמר לי וגו׳, expresses nothing but the clear actual meaning of the procedure.

חק, primarily, ordinances referring to that which is appropriate to, or inappropriate to the spiritual-material nature of Man, limitations to the caprice of the individual, such as עריות and משפט .מאכלות אסורות, laws referring to social order. If, as Rashi takes it, it means here the establishment of פרה ,שבת, and דינין we can see in פרה the fundamental element of all the הקים, for which moral freedom of will is essential, as פרה itself is the symbolic proclamation of the basic Jewish principle of free will, of טהרה. The Gemora in Sanhedrin 56b puts כבוד אב ואם in place of פרה — the education to free obedience by placing oneself under the will of parents, which equally lays the foundation of moral freedom.

דינים are quite simply the basic principle of social rights, משפט, and we have only to seek some indication for שבת in the text. Perhaps this lies in the word שׂם, and refers to the actual establishing of the foundation. The basis for the whole moral and social giving of the Torah is the recognition of מלכות שמים, the Kingship of God, i.e., that the whole world, including Man with the powers he has been given over matter belongs to God; in general, the subordination of Man to God, and it is to this basis of human beings recognising Law that the institution of שבת is dedicated. (The full meanings of both פרה and שבת must, of course, be deferred until we actually come to them in the Torah I.L.).

נסה .נסהו means either to test, prove, examine somebody or something, or to habituate, to practise. All practising, all habituating is nothing but the “trying out” of a force to accomplish something which up to the present has not, or has not efficiently been accomplished. So כי לא נסיתי באלה (Sam. I. 17,39). The expression here and throughout the whole course of the wandering in the wilderness (as in V.4 of next chapter etc.), can be taken in this latter meaning. By bringing Israel into such dire trials, God wanted to get the people practised in the necessary traits for the fulfilment of His Torah. But as it is used here after שם שם לו וגו׳ it can be taken in the ordinary meaning, to test, prove, and the people are the subject, and the Law the object of נסהו viz. “There God gave it (the Nation) the fundaments of His Law, and there it (the Nation) proved or tested it, learnt to know the power of faithful carrying out of the Will of God, by the sweetening of the bitter waters.”

V. 26. אם שמוע וגו׳ until תעשה seems to belong together as one sentence. The doubling of שמע תשמע implies the exclusive attention to the Voice of God, in order to understand what in His Eyes is “straight-forward, honest” ישר, i.e., in any given case, is the correct right thing to do. Thereby משפט the social order ordained by God is achieved. Simply to “listen”, i.e., to tell yourselves, or let yourself, be told what is the right thing to do at any occurrence is naturally what you are called upon to do by the occurrence itself, but here the demand is made that you go for your decision to the Word of God. It is different with the מצות. These are the commands which God has given you on the “post” (צוה) to which He has appointed you, regarding the positive promoting of your own and your fellow-man’s welfare, self-ennoblement, love of one’s neighbour etc. In most cases, with regard to these laws, you would not feel yourself called upon to make a mental decision as to how to act. Hence it says here והאזנת, you are to “set your mental ear in motion” למצותיו for His commands, to learn what He demands of you. שימור :ושמרת כל חקיו applied to the Laws of God is always twofold. The word places the Laws of God in our hands as valuables entrusted to us, for whose charge we are responsible. This charge or care is twofold. Firstly the care to obtain the theoretical knowledge, what we call “learning”, for a law can obviously not be kept correctly, and will soon become lost, if knowledge and understanding of it is not obtained. Then the care that it shall be kept and carried out practically, the self-imposed controlling conscientiousness, out of which the law-“protecting” גזירות and תקנות result. This “care” is here primarily required for חוקים. These laws which restrict and limit our sensuality and our free choice run the greatest risk of being neglected theoretically, and disregarded practically. In most cases where the Torah enumerates the separate headings of the Law, חקים are mentioned before משפטים. For it is just the education and sanctifying of our senses within the limits drawn by the הקים which produce men who are able to satisfy, completely and to the highest degree, the demands of justice and brotherly love as these are envisaged and expressed by God. So we find just above שם לו חק ומשפט. But here משפטים and מצות are in the foreground, because here the contrast is to be drawn to the degeneration which they had seen and experienced in Egypt. There it had been just a social degeneration which had been primarily evident, and which Israel had been made specially to feel, although, of course, this in its origin only grew and flourished out of the moral degeneration of the individuals.

מחלה is used not only of bodily illness, but also of any hindrance to well being, of the mind (worry) as ואין חולה מכם עלי (Sam. I. 22,8), of general existence ובל יאמר שכן חליתי (Is. 33,24), of the land, ואת תחלואיה אשר חלה ה׳ בה (Deut. 29,21), also especially to those which were sent for the purpose of correction, punishment, הכית אותם ולא חלו (Jer. 5,3), הכוני בל חליתי (Prov. 23,35). God says “The keeping of My Laws protects you from such sufferings which otherwise I should have to use to educate you, as I had to inflict on the Egyptians”. God does not allow people or states to endure without consideration for מצות ,משפטים and חקים, without them they go to ruin, and degenerate physically and socially, and so, keeping the divine Law is the most preventative medicine against all physical and social evil.

V. 1. In this record, between V. 1—10 the expressions vary: עדת בני ישראל, כל בני ישראל, בני ישראל surely not without reason. כל עדת בני ישראל looks on the Jewish community in its highest meaning as a community united by its common mission. It is the community which is meant to be the “congregation” of God. By the use of this nomination right at the beginning of the story, we are prepared for the fact that here events will be recorded that affect to the highest degree the interest of the general mission of the whole Jewish community. For this reason, too, we are given the precise locality and date. It was just one month after their attaining freedom, the 15th of the second month after their exodus from Egypt which they had left on the 15th of the first month. It was again a 15th, but a 15th of a very different kind, indeed a “Pessach Koton”, after the Pessach Hagodol. (Later on, too, the evening of Iyar 15th was given as subsidiary to the evening of Nissan 15th) (Numbers 9,11). It was now not a question of breaking external chains, of building up and saving homes out of slavery and death. Now, it was a matter of freeing the souls and the minds from the binding chains of the worry for providing the daily sustenance, which was to be achieved by placing the existence of individual and family under the aegis of the ruling and guidance of God by the institution of the Sabbath. For it is nothing less than the institution of the Sabbath, that great institution which is at the base of all Jewry and all Judaism, which is here announced. It was introduced by a daily miracle which occurred unin-terruptedly for forty years, and thereby made the people who experienced it perfectly familiar with the underlying idea. If it was the Pessach that built the Jewish homes up for God (see above), it was the Sabbath that kept them for Him.

V. 2. First of all we learn of the tremendous necessity for such an institution. כל עדת בני ישראל, it was the whole community (which, after all, must have had within it the noble germs of their ultimate destiny) that began to murmur against Moses and Aaron as soon as they found themselves again in the wilderness after leaving fruitful Elim. Nothing helped, the miracles of the salvation from Egypt and on the Red Sea, as well as the preparatory experience in Mara, all dwindled to nothing in face of the threatening spectre of hunger and famine for wife and child. In this direction too, the saying may apply קשין מזונותיו של אדם יותר מקריעת ים סוף, “The provision of daily bread is more difficult than the splitting asunder of the Red Sea.” Real or supposed danger of hunger makes all principles shaky, silences all better resolutions, and as long as a man is not relieved, not from the worry, but from the crushing burden of the worry about his daily bread, there is no place left for a thoroughly complete realisation of the Divine Torah. Freedom from the mountainous pressure of this spectre is only possible by deep implantations of the consciousness that this first of all human worries, the worry about one’s actual material existence, does not have to rest on one’s own shoulders alone, and not primarily on one’s shoulders. One has to be convinced that for this object too, a man can only do, and is only to do his part, i.e., all that God expects him to do for this object, and is to depend on God for the result being a sufficiency. He must be convinced that every single human soul, and every home with every tiny hungry soul within it, is a direct object of God’s constant, everwatching, almighty, providing Love. He must be convinced that human activity for its existence, is not to be considered as a right, but as a duty.

Without this conviction, so long as a man feels himself, himself alone, with all his limited powers, fettered to the yoke of the effort of ensuring the necessities of life for himself and his dependents, there is no limit to this worry. It is not just in a wilderness, but in the midst of a social world most abounding in all goods — and most abounding in competition too — this worry can turn any Man’s world into wilderness. This worry can make a man believe that he must secure and protect not only the morrow, but the whole of his future, the future of his children, of his grandchildren and then of his great-grandchildren. It makes it seem to him a necessity to acquire with complete ruthlessness, for himself and his dependents, an ever increasing portion of the wealth of the world; and apart from this, hardly any space or time is left for any other object in life.

Accordingly God led the future people of His Torah out into the actual desert, most completely bare of any of the necessities of life; let them there first feel the whole anxiety of a place where the necessities of life were completely unobtainable, and the future seemed completely hopeless, let them first experience for themselves and for all their descendants, to what loss of all considerations, the force of such a position, even if it is only momentary, can drag one. Of course, as can be deduced from the following verse, the whole of that generation had been unaccustomed to the worry of providing the bare necessities of life. As slaves, it was to the interest of their masters to provide the means of existence for their property, and to keep up their strength, just as one does for one’s cattle and beasts. “In the desert, the whole congregation of Israel began to murmur against Moses and Aaron.”

V. 3. בני ישראל, individuals, the boldest, most pert of the community, expressed the general feeling of dissatisfaction in open words of reproach and accusation against Moses and Aaron. ביד ה׳, there in Egypt we should have died natural deaths at God’s Hands. Here we die through your fault. It is quite impossible that it is at God’s behest that you have led us here into the desert, where it is certain that we shall all die of starvation.

V. 4. הנני. Not just as a result of this dissatisfaction — God’s reply to the people referring to that is only given in V.11 & 12 — simultaneously with the dissatisfaction becoming audible and without Moses having appealed to God, as above in XV,25, did God say unto him הנני, “I am already prepared”. When I led the people into the desert I had decided to provide them with food in this way. לכם, it is possible that this refers to Moses and Aaron. My decision to provide the people with manna just fits in with saving you and justifying you. הילך בתורתי, for bearers of My Torah it is essential that I find men for whom it suffices to be provided for wife and family for each day by itself. Men who can cheerfully and happily enjoy today, carry out their duties for today and leave the worry for tomorrow to Him Who has provided for today and Who can be trusted for tomorrow. Only such unreserved confidence in God ensures the fulfilment of His Laws against infringement out of supposed or actual concern about material necessities. He who has not learnt to trust God for the next day, will ultimately be led away from God and His Law, by his provident care for next year. Hence the great saying of Reb. Eleaser Hamodai: ,דבר יום ביומו מי שברא היום ברא פרנסתו, מכאן היה ר׳ אליעזר אומר: כל מי שיש לו מה שיאכל היום ואומר מה אוכל למחר הרי זה מקטני אמנה; “He who created the day, created also its requisite sustenance, and who has enough to eat for today and says: What shall I have to eat tomorrow? such a one belongs to those who are poor in trust in God.”

V. 5. והכינו את אשר יביאו. They will not notice any increased quantity in the amount they bring home and prepare it as usual for the day’s requirements, but then it will become apparent that the quantity is doubled. In these two verses God tells Moses what would have occurred even without the people having “complained”. They were to be given daily only and exactly the requirements for that day to accustom them to look up to God, with confidence for the so-called petty necessities of daily life, and to impress them with the certainty that each individual man and each man’s individual little home is a special object to which God gives His attention; and by the double portion on the sixth day, that God also provides for the special requirements which the demands of His Law involves.

V. 6. אל כל בני ישראל, both to those who had confined their murmurings against Moses and Aaron to their own immediate circle, and to those who had publicly stood up and denounced Moses and Aaron. ערב, this very evening ye shall be shown your error in ascribing the exodus from Egypt to us and not to God. The evening bounty of quails was given them only in response to their complaints, to show them that God pays attention to every word. As usual, the announcement of the quails is not mentioned in the report of God’s Word to Moses in V. 4 & 5, because it is immediately known from the speech of Moses to the People.

V. 7. ובקר וראיתם את כבוד ה׳. Just as כבד weight, gives us the idea of the material, mass or content of an object, so כבוד designates the spiritual weight, the impression that the mental and moral worth of a person makes on us, and by which we estimate his mental and moral worth. Applied to God, כבוד is the impression, the trail which His intervention in earthly affairs leaves behind it, from which one gets an intimation of His Presence and His Greatness. So, Moses prays: “הראני נא את כבודך״ and “טובו״ is revealed to him, the whole of God’s Goodness in the direction of human affairs, the track of the ways of God — דרכך — in history which gives an intimation of the Presence of God and the Greatness of God in the affairs of humanity. So the appearance of the cloud is called כבוד ה׳, because, as the impression of the Presence of God amongst the People, it gave an intimation of this Presence. But nowhere is the impression of this Presence greater and its effect more overwhelming than where a condition of hopeless desolation, a bleak desert, is changed to paradise-like conditions, into a fruitful pasture, where the sudden contrast makes the impression so deep. So here: This evening you will merely get proof that God is your leader and that He hears every word you utter. But the morn will bring you a sight that will give you an intimation of the whole greatness of your God. The desert which to your utter despair, now stares you in the face with its hopeless desolation, that desert will you see all at once transformed by the Hand of God miraculously into a gloriously laden table laid for you, your wives and children. — בשמעו את תלונתיכם וגו׳ and that, in spite of the fact that He shows you this evening that He has noted your murmurings and you could very well think that you had forfeited the care that His providing Love gives. ונחנו מה, but we, at all this, how our part in directing your fate vanishes into complete unimportance, and how little are we worth that you should murmur against us, or at any rate stir up dissatisfaction about us, even if you do not openly come out with it, (for open charges were only made by a few amongst the people. See V.3). — תַלִינוּ an unusual form of the הפעיל the נ״ע for תָלִינוּ. Perhaps because תלינו could also appear to be the קל, and as here the “causitive” was definitely to be stressed, the form תַלִינוּ is used so that all the other marks of the הפעיל remain. In V.2, the קרי is וילונו and the וילינו :כתיב. Here it is the reverse. There we were told that grumbling was universal, although a great part only indirectly caused the open revolt. Moses’ meekness only reproached them all with indirectly causing the revolt, although in fact, it had come to open outbreak.

V. 8. Nothing is more characteristic of the “man Moses”, this ענו מאד מכל אדם, who claimed nothing for himself, who wanted nothing for himself, who gave himself up so entirely to be “the servant of God”, than this speech! What would anybody else not have made for himself out of such a situation, where, to use the words of Isaiah (LXIII,12) — מוליך לימין משה זרוע תפארתו — God’s wonder-working Arm is shown to be ready at his elbow with all Its grandeur. How could he not, at least, have let some little reflection of the blinding brilliance of such a miracle fall upon himself. What are all the provision of loaves and other miracles which are recorded of all the other miracle-workers in the world, compared to this forty-year long regular daily feeding of this million and a half human souls on their path through the desert. One really would only have to be a hair’s-breadth less “Moses” than Moses was, not to resist the temptation to acquire such an unparalleled nimbus. And behold “the man Moses” trembles lest he should acquire just such a nimbus! He is not satisfied just to mention in conjunction with his brother (V.7) that their complaints were really directed against God and not against them, as they were merely the instruments of God. He takes up these last words of their speech and emphatically demands that out of the experience they are about to get, viz., that God will feed them night and morning, they are to realise that God had heard their complaints by Himself, without his appealing to Him about them. Moses demands that this experience must teach them not only כבוד ה׳ (V.7) the Greatness of God, but at the same time the fact that they stand directly under the leadership of God; that he, Moses, is not even necessary as an intermediary and that the idea of his own importance, and the importance of his brother must vanish from their minds. And, indeed, Moses’ whole mission depends on its being recognised as being through and through purely the work of God, without the slightest trace of human addition to it. Such a passage through the desert, such a Sabbath as the “Mosaic” Sabbath, or even the later sabbath-years of the “Mosaic” Law and many other institutions of this Law, would not only be folly, but actually crimes if they were ordained by Man and not by God. No man has the right to lead his wife and children into the hopeless desert, no man has the right to abstain from his duty of providing his daily bread for one day, much less occasionally for a whole year. Leaving God out as the One Who has ordered it, such ordinances would be, in the words of Ezekiel (XX,25) חוקים לא טובים ומשפטים לא יחיו בהם and our sages have pronounced the justified saying: גוי ששבת חייב מיתה, a non-Jew who would make it his duty to keep a Jewish Sabbath would be committing a serious crime. But commanded by God, demanded by God as a sign and habit of unreserved recognition and trust, that which otherwise would be folly becomes the deepest wisdom, what otherwise is a crime becomes highest virtue, and not carrying it out would be denying God and dishonouring oneself. But the institution which was to be founded with this forty-year experience of the Manna, this institution of שבת quite specially requires the unassailable conviction that Man, with all his little but indispensable requirements of daily family life does stand directly under God, that he can whisper all his little wishes and worries directly to Him, and that no intermediary or intercessor is necessary for God to take note of all his requirements, be they great or small. Sabbath, as well as the whole Torah was indeed to outlive Moses. Hence this anxious care of this “man Moses” — whose supreme greatness lay in just the fact that he was only a man and did not wish to be anything else — that in the minds of his People, as between themselves and God, he should entirely disappear.
V. 9. כי שמע וגו׳. He has already heard, He does not require my intervention.

V. 10. ויפנו אל המדבר. They had turned away from the desert, whose aspect terrified them. But the cloud that led them had already entered the desert, and, as the Glory of God became visible in the cloud, it was apparent to them that it was God, Who was leading them by means of that cloud.

V. 11. All that Moses and Aaron had spoken to the People up to now was only the preparation for this speech of God, so that they should understand it in the right way and learn the lesson it was intended to preach.

V. 13. In Yoma 75b, the Gemora reckons up four kinds of שלו, amongst them פסניני probably pheasants. שלו is described as the commonest kind and as an extremely fat bird. It is taken to be a kind of quail. The quails were thrown to them in the camp itself, they did not have to trouble about them as they did for the Manna which they had to go out and gather up from the surrounds of the camp. It is highly significant that the quails, which were sent to them, not as a blessing, but only to teach them that God had noted their complaints, were, so to speak, thrown right at their feet, whereas that which the loving foresight and care of God granted could only be obtained by their own co-operation. They had to do their part. שכבת הטל, the fall of the dew. In deserts generally, especially in the Asiatic and African deserts where there is no evaporation, dew is unusual. If the Manna, as is apparent from Numbers 11,9, was always preceded by a fall of dew, and, as here declared, followed by one, so that the Manna lay between two layers of dew, both must have been sent specially for the Manna and must have had importance for it. We imagine that the preceding layer of dew moistened the surface layer of the sand of the desert and made it firm, so that the grains of Manna did not fall into sand and become sandy. The second fall then washed the grains completely from any dust or dirt that might have settled on them in their descent.

V. 14. והנה indicates that the Manna was not visible before the evaporation of the dew. It must accordingly have been entirely transparent or, as some things do, become transparent when wet, and so not to be distinguished from the droplets of dew. That also seems indicated by the description in Numbers 11,7, ועינו כעין הבדלח, which Rashi says means crystal. מחספס from חסף same meaning as חשׂף, stripped, shelled i.e., freed from all husk or shell. By the double fall of dew it was quite fresh and freed from any extraneous adhesions. As חשף has also the meaning of drawing anything out of a liquid, לחשוף מים מגבא (Is. 30,14), it is possible that it has that meaning here too. After the evaporation of the dew, the Manna lay there as something fine “scooped off from the liquid”. Possibly the Manna was lighter in weight than the dew and so swam in it. The grains of Manna would then be raised off the surface of the ground by the double fall of dew and protected form contact with the ground itself.
כפר hoarfrost, from כפר protectingly to cover, from which we get כפרת the cover.
V. 15. מן from מנה, to fix a certain number of anything tor a certain purpose. Hence מְנָת מָנָה and here מָן a gift allotted to somebody.

V. 16—18. They were to gather it, having in mind the requirements of their household to bring home one Omer for each person. Then, if at the time when the Manna melted away (V.21) one had gathered up more than the exact correct amount, another, less, when they came to measure it, it was found that each one had the exact correct proportionate amount. But the intention to gather the right quantity seems to have been an essential, indispensable condition, otherwise, after the first experience, nobody need to have bothered to gather more than a minimum quantity since the result would be a sufficiency, and in no case more. In this lay the whole teaching of the importance of conscientious industrious work to be able to rely on the blessing of Providence in seeking a livelihood for oneself and one’s family.

V. 19. יותר. There seems to be a difference between הותיר and השאיר. The basic meaning of יתר is “to stretch”, so that יתר is a bowstring and מיתר a fully hauled sail i.e., something stretched tight-beyond its normal extension. Hence an unjustified leaving over, a stingy stretching and making something reach beyond what it is meant to last, is, primarily designated by השאיר .הותיר, on the other hand, expresses rather a justified leaving over, a prevention of waste. This prohibition makes the use and enjoyment of that which God grants to your honest industry an actual duty and stamps as a sin the denying or stinting oneself in the use and enjoyment of that which is given, whether out of pusillanimity or stinginess, just as in the preceding verse, laziness and avarice are shown to be reprehensible and bad.

V. 20. וירם וגו׳ from root רמם in Kal and Niphal וירם כבוד וגו׳ (Ezk. 10,4), הרמו מתוך העדה (Numbers 17,6), to raise oneself from where one is. The transition of a lifeless mass lying inert on the ground, into a live moving being, as appears to occur in putrefaction can not be more pertinently expressed than by רמם. The tiny point which hitherto has been chained to the ground by gravity begins to raise itself from the ground, it lives! Hence the worm which breeds in putrefaction is called רמה and the dead mass raising itself to life רמם. From this expression, of course, nothing can be deduced on the question of Generatis equivoca (spontaneous generation) as even if the generation comes from spores or eggs, the expression denoting the coming to life of a dead mass simply describes the occurrence as it appears to the eye. But תולעת ,תולע is the name for worms which come from outside and eat up the substance. The worms that bred in the Manna were not of the kind that usually come from putrefaction, but rather the reverse, they were not the result but the cause of the putrefaction, they preceded it, not ויבאש וירם תולעים, but וירם תולעים ויבאש. So that it by no means seems to be a מקרא מסורס. The deduction from V.24 seems also to show this. If the worms were the result of the putrefaction, then it need only say ולא הבאיש, that then there were no worms would be self-understood; or anyway the order should then have been reversed: not only were there no worms but there was no putrefaction. But the way it puts it must mean: not only had it not become foul but there was not even a worm to be found in it. The lesson this whole procedure taught for gaining one’s livelihood was:- that which Man hoards up against God’s will in a miserly, property-worshipping, God-denying spirit, God gives over to the worms and it becomes foul.

The experiences which were made at the six-days gathering of the Manna were to form the Jewish system of getting one’s livelihood, and gave the most important teachings and principles for it for all time. Laziness, avarice, greed and embittering despondency and pessimism is severely criticised, while being industrious, satisfied with sufficiency, happily enjoying life, and confidence and trust in God, is lauded.

V. 22. Moses was not to inform the people of what he had been told would be the experience of the sixth day. Quite unprepared, they were to get the startling actual fact of the Sabbath and of God’s care and provision for the specifically Jewish requirements as a complete surprise, so that these facts should impress them the more poignantly.

V. 23. שבתון. As has already been worked out on Gen. 2,2, שבת is not resting from, or after exertions, but a leaving-off, a cessation of what has been up to then a continuous activity. It is related to ,שפד ,שפת ,שות שפט ,שבט, all of which have the meaning of putting a thing in the place where it belongs. The שובת witholds his hand from things over which hitherto he had administered change of form or condition. For him, they have already attained their due shape and condition. However incomplete they may be in themselves, at the time of שביתה he has already done what he has to do to them. Looked at subjectively, i.e., in relation to what is demanded of him to do, the work is always a completed one as soon as he has worked on anything in honest service of God with all his energy and power. If God calls him away in the midst of uncompleted work, as far as he is concerned, the work is completed. That is the one phase of the idea of שבתון, cessation of work, which here is demanded from the Jewish People for the seventh day.

The seventh day as a memorial of the creation of the world and of God’s sovereignty of the world had already been known since the first seventh day of the world. Possibly it had even already since then borne the name Sabbath as the Sabbath of God, as the day כי בו שבת מכל מלאכתו on which God withdrew His creative Hand from His work on the world, and let it remain from then on, in the degree of completion He had given it. We have already in connection with the first Sabbath (Gen. 2,1) developed the thought, how it is just the negation, the fact that since there has been Sabbath in the creation i.e., that no new creations come into being before our eyes, this fact reveals a Free Creator of the World. And the day and the name may also have kept the consciousness of God alive and awake in the circles of the descendants of Abraham. But the Sabbath of God had not yet developed into a symbolic expression of Man’s acknowledging that his activities owed allegiance to God, nor had the logical conclusion as to the general position of Man in the world and his relation to God therein been drawn from this consciousness of God. Both were accomplished by the introduction here of the Sabbath in the sphere of the Jewish People and the beginning of the institution of the sanctification of Sabbath by Man. Sabbath itself had been in existence long ago, but שבתון its celebration by Man was what was new.

שבת קדש לה׳ מחר, is the object of שבתון. If it was meant to be a command it would say: תשבתו שבת קדש וגו׳, “celebrate God’s holy Sabbath by שבתון שבת קדש וגו׳ .”שביתה accordingly means: “To-morrow is a cessation of work, celebrating the holy Sabbath of God”. Sabbath, which, in the Lawgiving on Sinai, demands as its expression the whole creative activity of Man being sacrificed to it, is here introduced in Man’s activity in seeking his livelihood and preparing his food. In inhibiting his activity — שבתון — the Jew is first of all to show his submission to God in his activity in seeking his livelihood — that first and mightiest incitement to conquer the world, and just as the Sabbath of God impresses the seal of God’s creation on the world, so does the Sabbath of Man impress the seal of the authority of God on Man’s efforts at creation. With Sabbath, Man places himself and his work in the service of God. But just as the various teachings for Man’s efforts in gaining a livelihood — the warning against laziness and avarice as well as the encouragement to industriousness, the warning against depressing worry etc., — were brought to the minds of the people step by step, so we see the various teachings of the Sabbath being brought to the people by actual experience one by one. Here, first of all, the meaning of Sabbath for the preceding workdays. Although in general the care and worry for to-morrow is not to be the spur that urges you on to activity, here the care and worry for providing for Sabbath is introduced as being a factor to be included in our obligations in seeking our livelihood. Not only the requirements of our actual existence but also the requirements of our Judaism are to be the object of our care and worry, and what we gather in excess of our actual requirements for the purpose of מצות does not become given over the worms, but is under the protection of the Divine protective blessing.

V. 25. אכלהו היום כי שבת היום לה׳. Whereas, in general, only that which today’s industry has gained may be eaten, on Sabbath you are to eat without any preceding labour. For this inactivity is no wrong, self-chosen laziness, it is ordered by God and dedicated to God, and therefore has as high, as positive a value as any activity ordered by God. Also this makes eating on Sabbath itself a מצוה, an act ordered by God, directed to God, an ennobling and happiness-bringing deed. The fact that Man is to submit his efforts to gain his living to the direction of God, is not to lessen or do away with enjoyment of his earthly existence, on the contrary, it is to enhance the enjoyment of his material existence, and to raise the enjoyment of even sensual pleasures into the sphere of free, moral, God-serving acts, so that even by the enjoyment of his senses, his eating, his drinking etc., he feels himself near to his God. This elevation of the enjoyment of one’s senses into a God-serving act, dedicated to God, constitutes one of the most characteristic marks of the difference between Jewish teachings and others. Generally, the thought of the might of the gods is rather an oppressive one, and happy laughter has to fear the anger of the gods. Jewish thought of the Might of God, is a cheering comforting one. Man, with all his “littleness” struggles upward to this Might. Entering the service of this Might, Man, with all his weakness, takes part in this Might. The Might gives meaning and protection to his small existence and it fills him with the consciousness that his great and mighty God has pleasure in the happiness and enjoyment of His small creatures, His creations. Hence also the meaning and importance of the third meal of Sabbath is referred to this verse. Not to curtail our enjoyment of Life has God forbidden us to gain or prepare our means of living, but to give meaning to, and to raise the whole conception of human worth by submitting our means of living to God. And getting and having this idea is indeed calculated to raise Man, untouched, above all those troubles which otherwise God’s educative direction brings on the Jewish People for the purpose of preparing the way for this idea, and on the individual and the social-political world in general, to cleanse and purify them, אמר ר׳ שמעון בן פזי אמר ר׳ יהושע בן לוי משום בר קפרא כל המקיים שלש סעודות בשבת ניצול משלש פורעניות: מחבלו של משיח ומדינה של גיהנם וממלחמת גוג ומגוג. מחבלו של משיח כתיב הכא יום וכתיב התם הנה אנכי שולח לכם את אליהו הנביא לפני בא יום וגו׳ (Sabbath 118a).

היום לא תמצאהו וגו׳. On the field you are not to find it today, but in your homes. Not because you are not to eat today, but because you are not to gather it up from the field is why God does not let it fall today. As מצא does not only mean a chance finding but also an intentional one, seeking, as מצא את החצים (Sam. I. 20,36); (בראשית) נח מצא חן etc. etc., here it can very well mean: Today you are not to seek for it on the field, and then the prohibition of “gathering” would be expressly given, as appears from V.28, otherwise we must take it as being included in the general command of שבתון of V.23, or inferred from the following ששת ימים תלקטהו.

V. 26. שבת לא יהיה בו. According to the cantillation these four words belong together, probably to express the idea that the לא יהיה בו is simply the natural consequence of the nature of the day, “on the seventh day is Sabbath, on which accordingly it does not come into existence”. The Manna was a fresh creation each day, the idea of Sabbath would be contradicted if anything new came into existence on it. Just as the Sabbath of creation signalised the world as the free creation of God, so the non-appearance of the Manna on Sabbath proved its appearance on the other six days as a free gift of God. By the non-appearance of the Manna on the seventh day the Jewish Sabbath is proved beyond all doubt, right at the beginning of its institution, as being really instituted by God.

V. 28. He who seeks his livelihood on Sabbath against God’s Will denies that his food is sent from God at all. He reveals his belief that he can get his livelihood without any reference to God’s Will, even against God’s Will, and that it is not the Divine goodwill but his own actual efforts and that which can be obtained by the ordinary means governed entirely by physical laws, which keeps him and feeds him. He has only to seek, to find; to find; to have; to have, to be happy, neither the one nor the other is dependent on God. The Jew who seeks his livelihood on Sabbath, completely turns his back to God, and to following His Will, places himself on his own, and tears up the bond with all His teachings. Hence the words: עד אנה מאנתם לשמר מצותי ותורתי, for with חלול שבת is expressed the denial to pay any attention at all to the commands and teachings of God. Sabbath is especially both a מצוה and a תורה as are all symbolic commands. It demands a concrete doing something or refraining from doing something (a מצות) to demonstrate a truth and to impress it on the mind and feelings (a תורה).

If Moses seems included in the reproach מאנתם it was probably meant to give him the hint that perhaps he could have warned the people more carefully against transgressing, and so have prevented the transgression. Such precautionary care belongs quite properly to the שמירת המצות.

V. 29. ראו. Each word in this sentence it to be emphasised. ראו, By your own actual experience of the alteration in the dispensation of the Manna, as well as by the inner feelings of the blessing that Sabbath gives, you can make sure כי ה׳, that the Sabbath is an institution sent by God, and נתן, that it is not a burden, a restriction or a loss, but that it is a valuable gift that God has given לכם, to you, not for His sake but for yours, for your happiness-bringing welfare. And in fact, there is hardly any spiritual or moral idea — knowledge of God, knowledge of the world, knowledge of oneself, feeling dutybound, consolation, energy, joy of existence, joy of accomplishment — which is not to be gained and always freshly regained by the Divine ordinance of subjecting one’s food-seeking activities and one’s work to the laws of the Sabbath! על כן הוא וגו׳, God does not wish to deprive you of anything by the Sabbath, He will see to it by blessing your weekday work that you are in a position to keep the Sabbath.

אל יצא איש וגו׳. If, as is the opinion of the ירושלמי (see עירובין ,רי״ף 1 at the end), and the רמב״ם as Halacha, that תחומי י״ב מיל דאורייתא then this prohibition here refers to people going on Sabbath beyond the place of their habitation at the entry of Sabbath. In that case the Torah prohibitions of the Sabbath include not only the productive activity of Man on matter, but also the disposition of his own person with regard to the sphere of his existence and work. Then the Sabbath idea extends to the subordination of his own person to God, as well as it does to his giving up for the day his power of dominion over the material matter of the world. Nevertheless the former would only be בלאו and not במיתה. But if תחומין is altogether only דרבנן then the prohibition here refers only to going out to gather the Manna, i.e., to carrying out the empty vessels and bringing home the full ones, הוצאה and הכנסה.

It may not be superfluous to remark here what kind of work was prohibited at the very first introduction of Sabbath to the life of the Jewish People. All those who try to rob our Jewish People of the true idea of Sabbath and try to talk us over to understand the לא תעשה כל מלאכה of the Ten Commandments as referring only to hard work comprising bodily exertion, are here shown how right at the first foundation of the Sabbath, it is expressly search for food, cooking, and baking and generally preparing the daily meals, bringing things out of the free common domain into private domain and the reverse, and possibly also leaving the environs of the place of one’s residence which were forbidden. All are activities which these Sabbath-reform gentlemen would declare as “not contradictory to the sanctity of the Sabbath”. Moreover, one must remember, that here it was a question simply of gathering up the finished ready food that was lying there, and most probably the whole matter of gathering the Manna was completed, had to be completed within at most a couple of hours, so that the whole of the rest of the day remained for so-called Divine Service with accompanying choir and sermon, and still the simple gathering of the Manna is “desecration of the Sabbath”. From V.21 we know that the limit of time for the gathering of the Manna was fixed by וחם השמש ונמס, but הם השמש, (in contrast to חום היום when it is hot everywhere) the time when it is hot in the sun and cool in the shade is the 4th hour of the day (Berachoth 27a). But they could only start their gathering of the Manna, according to V.14, after the dew had risen again. So, anyway, some time after sunrise. Accordingly, the gathering was limited to this short interval. But altogether, it may not be overlooked how the idea שבתון, which here is placed at the head of all the ordinances for the institution of Sabbath, at once ordains a limitation of activities which extends far beyond the conception of איסור מלאכה. Whereas the prohibition of מלאכה only forbids actual human creation, producing an artificial change in material, and this then is the highest חלול שבת entailing the death penalty, שבתון is the substantive idea of the command תשבות. According to its etymological meaning, and in general without any specific object, it orders cessation from weekday activity in general, even if such activity is not directly productive. The idea שביתה accordingly includes all activities of trade and gain, everything which the Prophet (Is. 58,13) describes as desecration of the Sabbath, in the sentence אם תשיב משבת רגלך וגו׳, “If thou keepest back thy foot from the Sabbath, from carrying out thine own will on My holy day, and call the Sabbath a delight, the holy of God, honourable, and shalt honour it, by not doing thine own ways, nor seeking thine own will, not even speaking a word about it.” Everything further is comprised in the general duty of שמירת התורה and especially of שמירת השבת as the principle of “guarding” the Torah, and has only been more precisely defined by the גזירות and שבותים of our הז״ל. So the idea of שבתון is understood in the מכילתא and in the ספרא. See רמב״ן on Levit. 23,24. All שבותים, as indeed all תקנות and גזרות of our חכמים are, accordingly, in principle, דאורייתא, and if they are taken in certain cases as e.g., in cases of doubt, less strictly than אסורי דאורייתא, this itself is what the sages themselves ordered when they made these institutions, especially when the object is only protection against infringement of the Law (גזרות).

Just as the Prophet (Amos 9,11) prophesying the re-erection of the “falling tabernacle of David” sees the enclosure first re-established and then the structure itself built up again, because it is only within a protected space that the building can be ensured of a permanent existence, in the same way we see here for the weekly renewed great upbuilding of the Sabbath, first demands made on the whole sphere of human activity, within which then, the great building of איסור מלאכה can safely be carried out. This איסור מלאכה makes human power to use, improve and transform the matter of the world, into bricks for the building of an ברית ,אות and קדש, of a Sanctuary which proclaims God and joins Man and God with each other, and it is only within this consecration of the whole sphere of Man’s activity to the Sabbath, that the permanence of such a Sanctuary can be assured for all time.
