Thus a national life is to be produced having its roots in purity, growing upwards in purity, taking its stand on purity, combining never-ending progress and development with absolute firmness and immutability towards exterior influences, in all its divers characteristics ever keeping one central uniting bond of union; a national life which as the “gold-clad cedar stems (the boards. I.L.) on silver feet”, forms the human group which eternally offers the “wood and gold” out of which it forms its “Table and Lamp and Ark” for the reception of the “Law”, the Torah, which rests there as the heart of this cycle which pulsates from earth to heaven and from heaven to earth.

But these cherubim who are to represent the presence of God in the human world are to be שש משזר תכלת וארגמן ותולעת שני, they present the same materials and the same colours which are used for the presentation of the ideal of human perfection in the attire of the High Priest (see notes on Ch. XXVIII). For it is just in the granting, protecting and blessing of these elements which are the foundations of perfection in human life that the special presence and proximity of God (the שכינה. I.L.) proclaims and manifests itself, as is expressed in Levit. 26,3—13 and Deut. 7,12—16. That is why the presentation of these cherubim is to be woven out of the linen threads of the pure vegetable element, the crimson woollen threads of the animal element, the purple woollen threads of the human element, and the sky-blue woollen threads of the godly element of the human being. It is only the element that specially characterises the high-priestly garments that represents the noblest moral force, the threads of gold, that is lacking in the representation of the cherubim. For that is the one factor which is not presented by the cherubim, it is the one factor that Man and Man alone has to bring to this structure of godliness on earth — הכל בידי שמים חוץ מיראת שמים.

But the threads out of which the cherubim are woven are to be “twisted six-ply” שש משזר (V.1). The number seven we have repeatedly shown, represents the invisible “Creator” in connection with the “created”, the One in combination with the six. So that “six” is the sign of the “created”, and this sign is also impressed on each element of the cherubim. For they are to proclaim themselves not as independent divinities, but as created messengers and instruments, as proclaiming the presence of God’s “creation”.

If we dared, we would remark the following:— When we picture the description of the weaving of the cherubim, the red colour, ארגמן ושני, is predominantly evident. But red is the symbolic colour of “life”, and thereby the cherubim are characterised as חיות (Ezek. 10,20). The picture of the cherubim is woven from four constituents, “of four forms is the appearance of the חיות״. When we remember that שור is characterised as predominantly of the “vegetative” nature among living creatures (see notes on Levit. 11,3) the parallel at once suggests itself: — Vegetative שור=שש, animal אריה=שני, human אדם=ארגמן, godly נשר=תכלת.

The human group protectingly surrounded by the cherubim of God in the מקדש, is represented by the gold-clad shittim-boards resting in and on silver feet. They stand there as קרשים, primarily “warding off” (גרש) from outside everything unholy, everything that would alienate the souls of those who form the holy group about the עדות; and also as “accepting” ירש, מורשה) from inside the Divine Torah, and on the foundation of the basis of moral purification and purity (אדני כסף) which this Torah gives, unfolding a “tree-like”, constantly growing, life of eternally youthful fresh development (see V.15) within the “pure gold” limits drawn from the highest ideal of morality.

Unless we are quite mistaken, these cedar stems which surround the Sanctuary are the tribes (the geneological trees. I.L.) of the Jewish people who accept the Torah and its ideals of a spiritual and material national life to be realised in their midst. This is what Ezekiel refers to (XXXVII,15) as the עץ יוסף and the עץ יהודה, they are the “trees” which שתולים בבית הי, בחצרות אלהינו יפריחו (Ps. 92,14) which “planted in the House of God, blossom in the ‘courts’, the general life, surrounding God’s House”; they are the tribes of Israel of whom their first leader sang “Thou bringest them home, Thou plantest them on the mount of Thy inheritance, on the home that Thou, O God, hast prepared for Thy sojourn on earth, the Sanctuary, O God, that Thy Hands have established” (Ex. 15,17); they are “the tents of Jacob, the dwelling-places of Israel”, which the alien seer saw “as gardens by the riverside, as ‘aloe-trees which God has planted’ and as cedar trees besides the waters, the water trickles out of God’s buckets, and his seed shall be in many waters” (Numbers 24,5—7); this is the “vine that God has brought out of Egypt, driven out the heathen, and planted it, whose shadows covered mountains and whose boughs were like the cedar of God” (Ps. 80,9 & 11); they are “the trees of God’s planting”, of which the pages of the prophet’s word speak, and which ultimately “will perfect themselves to the glory of God” — מטע ה׳ להתפאר — Is. 61,3.

We originally thought that the number and construction of these “cedar-stems” — which even as wall-boards had still to remain דרך גדלתן standing cedar trunks עצי שטים עומדים (V.15) — could also be explained in this same way, but we found that the reckoning we had made was based on an error. So that the meaning of the number of the קרשים is still to be found out. But their meaning as the tribes of Israel united around the Sanctuary is nevertheless to be maintained. The boards were joined together in two ways. Externally, visibly, on each side they were held together by four bolts. Internally, invisibly, one bolt closed them all together to form one united whole. (V.26—29). The tribes of Israel came from four mothers and one father. Each mother formed a joining bolt of common ancestry. The tribes, accordingly, were externally, according to physical maternal descent, divided into four groups. But, just as they all came from one father, so the common Jacob-Israel mission that they inherited from this father, and the Jacob-Israel spirit that they inherited with this mission, formed the בריח התיכון בתוך הקרשים the inner bolt which held all the tribes, with all their different characteristics, together as ’שבטי ה; internally united to a miraculous unity. One spirit and one power, one goal and one strength lives and works in all of them, and holds them for ever united in one brotherhood, about the Sanctuary of God.

Visible up above, coming down, invisible behind the walls, the cherubim protected and surrounded that group of humanity that embraces the Torah and its Sanctuary. The cherubim of whom the Song of Songs sings (Ch. 2,9) “הנה זה עומד אחר כתלנו משגיח מן החלונות מציץ מן החרכים״, “see, he tarries behind our walls, looks in through the windows, peeps in through the lattice”. But they also descended, protecting and separating, between the Ark of Evidence and the Table and Lamp.

The cherubim-surround consisting of tapestries to the number of ten — the number designating a complete whole — representing the whole direction which God exercises, nevertheless was divided into two parts of five each. These parts were joined by “strong clasps”, but could be separated from each other. The point of separation and joining was exactly along the border line between the “Holy-of-Holies” (the room containing the Ark of Evidence with its cherubim-lid) and the “Holy” (the room containing the Table and Lamp). It was just at this separating and joining border line that the cherubim descended as the protecting and separating פרוכת. So that, if the necessity were to arise, if the cherubim-envelope of the Table and Light were to separate itself from the Ark of Evidence, the room of the latter would remain by itself surrounded and enclosed on all sides by cherubim.
This separation and joining expresses this most important idea:-

Certain though it is, that Israel’s Table and Light, Israel’s national material well-being and Israel’s intellectual spiritual development, stand under the special protection of the Divine direction no less than God’s Torah and its mission on earth — does not one cherubim-camp surround all three — no less certain is it, that God’s Torah and its mission on earth comes first as the object of His care and concern in His direction of this world. It is only inasmuch, and when, Israel derives and bases its intellectual development (Lamp. I.L.) and its material welfare (Table) from and on the Torah, and uses both only in furthering the ideal taught by the Torah, then, and only then, does Israel’s spiritual and material welfare also partake of the special protection of God’s provision. That is why this ideal itself has to be protected and separated from Israel’s “Lamp and Table”, against the possibility, at any time, of Israel’s spiritual and material prosperity, for which they have to thank the Torah, turning against the Torah; of their coming to consider this prosperity as being of primary importance, and “crossing the border line”, alter, modify and reform the Torah, according to the imagined “advance” of their intellect, and the imagined requirements of their material prosperity. The Torah, as being “evidenced” by God, (the Tablets of Stone. I.L.), the highest possible idea for all time, must remain “given” (i.e., received by Israel, not emanating from them, the ארון-idea. I.L.); from it alone is Israel’s Tree of spiritual development to derive its root and nourishment, the material and power and formula for growth and progress, and in it alone is Israel’s Table of prosperity to find its foundation and lasting power and happiness-bringing abundance. If ever Israel’s Table and Lamp should be in opposition to the “Ark” then the cherubim protection comes away from above the heads of Table and Lamp — Table and Lamp are given up — and the Ark of Evidence can remain safely hidden and protected in its cherubim-tent, until a new generation arises which kindles its light only from the Light of the Torah and builds up its Table only on the basis of the Torah. It is not the existence of the Torah, but the existence of the national spiritual and material prosperity which is endangered when the nation goes against the Torah with the one or the other of them.
Such is the deep and important significance and meaning of the cherubim-parocheth descending between the Ark and the Table and Lamp.

The whole “Dwelling of the Evidence”, is set under a covering of goats’-hair canvas, יריעות עזים לאהל על המשכן; this gives the Sanctuary the nature of “a living organism protected against outside dangers”. And while the hem of the goats’-hair covering hanging down behind and trailing on the earth give the Sanctuary the appearance of “striding along” כאשה המהלכת בשוק (see note on V.11—13) i.e., of making its way through the spaces and ages of the world, the red-coloured rams’ skin and tachash-skin formed its head and guaranteed to this living organism of the Divine Sanctuary striding through the history of the world the fullness of life-force (red, I.L.) of a ram striding forward leading the flock, and at the same time with the unceasing action of the animal of speed (V.14).
We shall consider the implications of the “curtain at the door of the tent” (V.36 & 37) in connection with the curtain at the door of the courtyard in Ch. 27,16 & 17.

V. 1. ועשית את המזבח not מזבח: This ה either refers to the image which had been shown on the Mount (V.8) or it shows the Altar as something that was automatically suggested as a necessary corollary by all that has already been said. ’רבוע יהיה וגו for the Altar to be allowed to be used it had to be square, but its dimensions, length breadth and height could vary מדת ארכו ומדת רחבו ומדת קומתו אין מעכבין (Zebachim 62a). Nevertheless the height actually never did and never will change, the Altars erected by Moses, by Solomon, and in the second Temple, were all of equal height although the length and breadth rose from the five cubits of Moses’ Altar to thirty two cubits in the second Temple. The Altar in the Temple of the future, as envisioned and described by Ezekiel, will have the same height (Maim. הל׳ בית הבחירה II,5). According to that the וההראל ארבע אמות (Ez. 43,15) would be measured with its קרנות not as Rashi takes it there. Perhaps this is the reason why it says here חמש אמות ארך וחמש אמות רחב (not ארכו and רחבו) while it says שלש אמות קמתו. The height is its height which remains constant, not so the length and breadth.

ושלש אמות קמתו. These three cubits were according to ר׳ יוסי (Zebachim 59b) the height of the Altar itself, which Ezekiel calls הראל (XLIII,15). This is the top part resting on a step or ledge סובב, here in our text called כרכב (V.5) which measured three cubits from this סובב to the קרנות (V.2) and together with them, four cubits (Ezek. ibid.). From this כרכב (the סובב) to the ground was six cubits, so the total height of the Altar from the ground to the top of its horns was ten cubits.

V. 2. קרנות were cubes rising on the four corners of the top surface, each measuring one cubic cubit. ממנו תהײן, they were not to be joined on to it but to be of one piece with the Altar itself, or at least with the top surface plate of the Altar (according to how one takes the נבוב לחות of V.8), so that it is the Altar itself that strives upwards with these corner horns.

V. 3. סיר, a pot or saucepan (here an ashpan) is perhaps related to סגר close in; יעים vessels for clearing away, shovels as: ויעה ברד מחסה כזב (Is. 28,17); מזלג root זלג, from its relation on the one hand to the Chaldean זלג and שלך from which we get השליך to throw and שלג snow, and on the other hand with סלק (Chaldean) to be taken away, seems to indicate מזלג as a utensil by means of which something is taken away from one place to lay it down on another place, hence a fork.

V. 4. כבר .מכבר related to גבר, underlying meaning “to overpower”, hence the idea of power: כבר .מַכבִּיר ;כַּבִּיר is related to כור, the smelting-pot. Just as the conception כבשן, furnace is formed from כבש, overpowering, so is כור, where metals are melted, differentiated and refined, formed from a similar idea. The same idea underlies the meaning of a sieve for כברה, and is even more evident when we consider that, as we are told in Menachoth 76b, to obtain סלת, the finest flour, the peeled grains of corn were placed in a sieve and repeatedly shaken till the coarser sheaths of the flour, קמח were shaken off and fell through the meshes of the sieve as dust, so that the סלת remained as the fine inner grains as קרטין in the sieve. From which the simile comes in Aboth 5,18 נפה שמוציאה את הקמח וקולטת את הסולת, and also in Amos 9,9, והנעותי בכל הגוים את בית ישראל כאשר ינוע בכברה ולא יפול צרור ארץ; “I shake the House of Israel through all the nations as something which is shaken in a sieve and yet nothing solid, compact falls to the ground”, i.e. Israel being sifted amongst the nations, in exile, only effects their refining, purification. That which falls away from them in the process is only ignoble dust. All that is solidly true remains and does not get absorbed by the nations. This sieving בכברה is accordingly a real mastering of the material that is to be cleaned through it. (It is remarkable that Rabba’s explanation in Menachoth 63b, ’קסבר ר׳ ישמעאל עשרון מובחר בלא טרחא וכו, is in contradiction to this procedure which is founded on Rashi’s description in Menachoth 76b and also on the expression of the Tosefta there קולטת סולת. He takes it that it was the סלת which falls through the sieve as fine dust רשת — .(וצ״ע, a net, probably comes from ירש, to take in possession, to acquire, accordingly, the means for catching and holding. This copper band of network went right round the four walls of the Altar, and was, as we shall find when we come to consider the meaning of the Altar, of the highest importance.

V. 5. This copper network was to reach down from the כרכב to half the height of the Altar. We have translated כרכב as step or projection. (It seems that כרכב is derived from רכב, in a similar way as קרקע from רכב .רקע is to be mounted on some base or support, this base or support is called מרכב .רֶכֶּב and מרכבה e.g., a carriage). As we shall see more exactly when we come to consider the Altar as a whole, it consisted of two, really three essential parts. There were three squares, one on top of the other, and each lower square was longer and broader than the one on top of it. In the second Temple the base was one cubit high and thirty two cubits square, and on it stood the next section, five cubits high and thirty cubits square, and on it again, the top section, three cubits high and twenty eight cubits square. This top section, on the upper surface of which the four קרנות rose a further cubit, and which was the real actual Altar, the הראל, rested accordingly on a foundation which projected one cubit outwards on all sides, and on which one could walk right round, and which was therefore called the סובב. Here in our text it is called כרכב because the uppermost part, the real actual Altar rested on it. (According to רבי, on Moses’ Altar, this סובב was not an actual ledge but was only indicated by an ornamentation (Zebachim 62a) (but there is no question that it played an important part on the permanent Altar I.L.).
עד חצי המזבח, reaching down to five cubits from the ground. The copper network was accordingly one cubit wide.

V. 8. נבוב ;נבוב לוחות only occurs once elsewhere ואיש נבוב ילבב (Job 11,12) “And the hollow man (without a heart) gets a heart”. So here too “make it hollow, of slabs”, i.e., not of a solid block. This portable Altar was, as already mentioned above, Ch. 20,21, set up over a mound of earth thrown up for the purpose. It was the מזבח אדמה which was to accompany us on our wanderings until the Sanctuary had obtained a fixed permanent home, when a מזבח אבנים was to be erected. The temporary Altars in Shilo, Nob and Gibeon were, according to Reb. Nathan (Zebachim 61b) filled with stones instead of earth.
THE מזבח

We have already indicated above on Ch. 20,21 how the contrasting position in the verse, of לא תעשון אתי וגו׳ and מזבח אדמה תעשה לי confirms our taking the מזבח as the representation of the “elevation of the earth upwards to God” by human efforts, and we are keeping to this idea as the guiding thought in understanding its construction. In the form of three terraces, on a base of thirty two cubits square and two other sections each diminishing by two cubits square, the Altar in the Temple rose nine cubits from the ground to a top flat surface of twenty eight cubits square. From this surface at each of the four corners, the “rays” or “horns” of the Altar, the קרנות reached upwards as solid cubes of one cubit. Ezekiel 43,15 calls the top eminence of the Altar (d e) “the Mount of God” to which the two lower elevations, on whose backs the “Mount of God” rises, stand in the relation of עזרות, antechambers, preliminary stages. The lower, smaller elevation (a) the base יסוד is called in V.14 the עזרה קטנה, the larger (b c) עזרה גדולה. The top surface, the plateau (f) of the “Mount of God” is called the אריאל (ibid.) the “lion of God”, on it the “fire of God” (representing godliness on earth. I.L.) that, with “lion’s power” as אש אוכלה, awaited the offerings of self-sacrifice in which Israel gave up its אימורים and its איברים — the kidneys representing their lower desires, the fat, their wealth, all the separated parts of the body representing their understanding, their knowledge and their actions — to this fire of godliness on earth, to let themselves be altered, through and through, to become “food”, fuel to keep the fire of godliness burning on earth, and to attain the approval of God with every phase of their earthly existence and efforts.

The הראל with the אריאל the Mount of God with the fire of God on its summit evidently expresses a miniature הר אלהים and אש אוכלת בראש ההר, a miniature Sinai. Ps. LXVIII, referring to Israel and the relationship to God into which they entered with the Revelation on Sinai sings: רכב אלהים רבתים אלפי שנאן “the bearers of the Glory of God, are myriads of thousands of heavenly beings”, but אדני בם סיני בקדש “but God entered into their (Israel’s. I.L.) midst, and Sinai is henceforth in the Sanctuary”. This might also be a possible explanation of the otherwise difficult verse, in the chapter of the Tamid-offering (Numbers 28,6) עלת תמיד העשויה בהר סיני, that here the Altar is just called הר סיני.

A careful perusal of Ex. Ch. XXIV will show that it is especially the summit of the Mount which is called הר אלהים and also preferentially הר, just as here it is the upper portion of the Altar which is primarily called הראל; and just as there, the greater or lesser distance from the summit indicated the greater or lesser degree of worthiness to nearness of God, of Moses, Joshua, the elders, and the people, so here, the graduations up the “Mount of God in the Sanctuary” are designated as עזרות as antechambers which lead up to Harel and Ariel.

This division of the Altar into the real eminence and the way up to the eminence, is further clearly marked by a special provision. Just as the lower half rests on a base of one cubit in height, the יסוד (a), so does the upper half, the real eminence, begin one cubit below the end of the second unit at (c). From there the רשות קרנות begins, the realm of the upward-soaring horns (Zebachim 53a). On the stone Altar of the Temple this cubit was marked by being painted red and was accordingly called חוט הסיקרא, the “red band”, or, as it encircled the whole of the Altar, “the red girdle”. On the Altar in the Mishkon, it was filled by the מכבר מעשה רשת, by the copper net-work (V.4), the place of which, the “red girdle” took on the stone Altar, which, accordingly, must have the same meaning, and this meaning, we can presume, is to represent the peculiar combination of מכבר and רשת. (Zebachim 53a).

חוט הסיקרא divides the Altar for דמים עליונים and דמים תחתונים. For sacrifices are divided essentially into ניתנין למטה and ניתנין למעלה, into those whose blood is placed below the חוט הסיקרא on the lower half of the Altar, and those whose blood is placed above it, on the upper half which conveys the meaning of the קרנות. To the former, the lower, belong שלמים ,עולה and אשם, to the latter, the upper, exclusively חטאת. Just as they differ in place, so also do they differ in the manner of the procedure of placing the blood. For the upper, the חטאת, the כהן mounted the סובב, the ledge of the base of the upper half, the הראל, and placed ונתן, with his finger some of the blood on the corner horns, the קרנות of the Altar. For the others, the lower ones, שלמים עולות and אשם, the כהן stood on the ground at a distance from the Altar and threw, זרק, the blood, which was in a sacred offering bowl, on to the lower half, the עזרה, the way up to הראל. And this difference in the placing of the blood is characteristically in accordance with the different lessons which the different offerings are meant to teach. חטאת is called for, by thoughtless transgression of the Torah, by careless commission of such sins, which, had they been done consciously and intentionally, would entail כרת מעמיה, eradication from the Jewish community. The individual or the nation had not kept itself fully conscious of the height of its Jewish calling; it had slipped, through thoughtlessness; so the priestly finger has to show it that in future it must keep its own self, which is so holy to God, firmly at the height of its Jewish calling and by earnestly keeping itself conscious of it, guard itself from stumbling, ולקח הכהן באצבעו ונתן על קרנת מזבח העלה. But עולה is ת״כ) ,מכפר על עשה on I,4 and in many places in Zebachim) is called for, not for actually having done wrong, but for not having done what should have been done, has to atone for sinning out of laziness. The individual, or the nation, fondly imagined itself already on the height of moral perfection, and so had become indifferent to the necessity for progress, and so became slack in observance. The כהן, accordingly, as the instrument of the מקדש, has to show him, how, far from being already on the קרנות ההראל, he is still far away from being even on the way up to the heights of godliness, and has first, with all his energy, to strive towards the path that leads upwards towards the moral heights of godliness, וזרקו חטאת .הדם על המזבח סביב teaches to remain steady, עולה to progress; חטאת, to cling fast to the heights of the Altar, עולה to strive towards the way up to the heights. And if, according to רשב״י (in עולה (ויקרא רבה at the same time atones על הרהורי הלב for irregular thoughts, the deep psychological truth would thereby be expressed, that sinful thoughts are not to be taken so much as positive mental sins, but rather as negative, failing to direct the mind to correct channels of truth. הרהורי הלב form themselves immediately, and by themselves, as soon as the mind relinquishes the energy for acquiring the knowledge of, and recognising, truth. So that just as עשה-sins arise from a lack of practical energy, so הרהורי הלב come from a lack of mental energy, and they have to be shown just like the חײבי עשה, that they must exercise the utmost energy in pulling themselves together to climb upwards to the spiritual heights of perfection. No less necessary is it to show the שלום-consciousness, the feeling of undisturbed happiness granted by God, which prompts a שלמים, that when one reaches the summit of earthly happiness, one is only then standing at the beginning of one’s spiritual calling, that what one is called upon to do now, is to strive upwards with all the blessings which have been granted by God, upwards to the height of the Jewish calling, it is only such resolve that can make one worthy to enjoy the blessings which one has. In quite a similar way the same sermon has to be preached in regard to the causes which make the bringing of the various אשמות necessary as בע״ה we shall have to show when we come to study each individual אשם.

Summing all this up, the lesson which the ritual of the blood above or below the חוט הסיקרא has to teach is a twofold one. It is the demand to hold fast to every degree of purity that one has attained, and equally so, untiringly and unceasingly to strive to attain that perfection that is still lacking. The קרנות preach: Keep zealously every degree of perfection that you have; the עזרות: Always become more and more complete, purer and purer. The former reach a “net” (רשת I.L.) down to us, to keep fast that which we have already spiritually and morally achieved. The latter hand us a “sieve” (מכבר I.L.) to work everlastingly at purifying, refining and perfecting oureslves. Thus the מכבר מעשה רשת, or the חוט הסיקרא which took its place on the stone Altar, represented, in the most suggestive manner, exactly that which the division of the Altar by it for the most important and essential ritual of sacrifices, the מתנות הדם, meant.

רבוע יהיה המזבח, the square form of the Altar is, as already remarked on V.1, one of the essentials, it is מעכב. In our dissertation on Tephillin in the Jeshurun Volume V, page 468, we have pointed out the fact that, in all forms made by organic forces unconsciously or at least unreasoningly, the curved or circular form predominates, or perhaps is even exclusive. It is only the free, self-directed force, of free, reasoning Man, that makes its buildings and creations in straight lines and angles. The circle, the curve, appertains to subjection, to lack of free-will, to טומאה. The rectangle is the sign of the freedom of the human will, and of its mastery over the material world, of טהרה. From this general point of view can already be understood that the construction of the Mishkon as well as its appurtenances, the Ark of Evidence, the Table, the Altar are all constructed on rectangular lines, and that this is quite specially emphasised as being essential for the Altar. The whole building is to be in direct opposition to every form of nature cults, it is to be dedicated to the building up of a morally completely free-willed human life, and the Altar is quite specially to represent this.

But the different sides of the rectangle of the Sanctuary, and especially those of the Altar appear in very definitely prescribed different uses: The Table had to be on the north side, the Lamp on the south, certain procedures of the ritual of the offerings had to be performed on the north side of the Altar, others only on the north east and south east, others again only on the south western corner etc., so that we have thereby cause to claim for the various sides of the Sanctuary in general, and those of the Altar in particular, special and different meanings.

Now it would seem that the simplest and most apparent explanation would be simply to take the meaning of the sides from their position in space, N.S.W.E. and apply the meaning of midnight midday, morning and evening to human life and its development. The Sanctuary itself had to be placed in a very definite position in space. The Holy-of-Holies had always to be in the west, the entrance always in the east. The Tamid offering was offered in the north-west in the morning and in the north-east in the evening, always corresponding to where the daylight fell.

But quite definite laws regarding the Altar, prevent us from remaining at this simple general explanation, and force us to seek the meaning of the sides of the Altar in narrower and more intimate spheres. רבוע, the squareness of the Altar, is one of the characteristics which are essential for the validity of the Altar and which differentiate a מזבח from a ת״ר .במה, it says in Zebachim 62a, קרן וכבש ויסוד וריבוע מעכבין, the corner-horns, the ascent (see below), the base and the squareness are essentials for the Altar to be valid. And in Zebachim 120a, it says: דברים שבין במה גדולה לבמה קטנה קרן וכבש ויסוד וריבוע לבמה גדולה ואין קרן וכבש ויסוד וריבוע לבמה קטנה וגו׳. How does a “great Bama” (this, of course refers to the מזבח) differ from a small Bama? A great Bama has corner horns, ascent and base and must be square, whereas a small Bama has none of these requirements.

במה is a knoll or eminence erected anywhere at will for the purpose of sacrifices, מזבח is the Altar erected in the forecourt of the Sanctuary of the Torah, and it is just in the presence or absence of the Torah and its Sanctuary that the specific difference between the two, and the doubtful admissibility of the Bama seems to lie. God is present everywhere and one can raise oneself up to Him anywhere. But the Bama-offering lacks every visible sign that it is dedicated to the One Only One and not to some supposed deity. Above all, it in no way represents that the surrender to God is only to be understood as a surrender to His Torah, and as an undertaking faithfully to fulfil it and carry out its behests. Both are provided for by erecting the Altar at the national abode of the Torah, before the entrance to its Sanctuary. One who makes an offering on a Bama can be led entirely by his own views about God and His relations to Man, so that a Bama gives room for the most subjective caprice. By bringing his offering to the national home of the Torah, at the entrance to the Sanctuary of the Torah, a man thereby places himself on the basis of the national creed, his offering is dedicated to the One and Only God Who teaches the Torah which is guarded and kept at this national abode, and his offering is nothing else but surrender to this Torah. The Altar in the מקדש is the הראל, is the Mount of God, on the summit of which the fire of the Torah awaits, as אריאל, with lion-like power, the complete surrender of the nation and the individual. This characteristic relation of the Altar to the Sanctuary of the Torah before the entrance of which it was erected, is expressed by the law, that offerings ששחטן קודם שיפתחו דלתות ההיכל פסולין, which were slaughtered before the gates of the Sanctuary were opened, were rendered invalid (Zebachim 55b, and see תוספות י״ט on Tamid 3,7). And this contrast of the Bama to the Altar, the absence of any relation in the Bama-offering to the Torah, is clearly brought out by the law, that only כל הנידר ונידב, only “free will” offerings, never obligatory ones, and especially no kind of חטאת ואשם were allowed to be offered on a Bama, even in the time of היתר במה (Zebachim 117a). To this, the other sentence is closely connected, that סמיכה ושחיטת צפון ומתן סביב ותנופה והגשה וכיהון ובגדי שרד וכלי שרת וריח ניחוח ומחיצה לדמים וריחוץ ידים ורגלים are all not applicable to Bama-offerings, but on the other hand זמן נותר טמא have to be observed at the Bama just as at the Altar-offerings. All the first named conditions are, as we shall have to show when dealing with them separately, in essential connection with the expression in the offering of renewed resolve to fulfil the dictates of God’s Torah. But נותר ,זמן or טמא give the offering a heathen character, as we have already remarked in connection with נותר (on Ch. 12,10 & XXII,18), so these naturally have to be observed at Bama-offerings too. We shall have to treat the idea of the Bama more fully when we come to Levit. XVII, where the matter is dealt with. For the understanding of the characteristic construction of the מזבח, what has been said above suffices. To sum up: The Bama offerer looks on God, to Whom he brings his offering, more as the Director of Fate for good or bad, rather than as the Giver of Laws which are to fix his active life. His offering is, accordingly, more an expression of thanks or of request, than of surrendering himself to the fulfilment of His will. But the Altar-offering is, in the first place, a renewal of the vow of obedience to fulfil the will of God, as revealed in His Torah, and even offerings of thanks and requests which are brought there, are only brought on the basis of such obedience. The “Altar-thanks” and the “Altar-requests”, only know of one means of showing themselves worthy of what has been granted, or what is to be granted, and that is:- With what has been given, or with what is to be given, to dedicate oneself to fulfil in an even higher degree than heretofore, the will of God.

So we can understand that קרן יסוד וכבש are essential ideas for the character of the מזבח and have to seek the meaning of ריבוע which is put together with these as one of the essential ideas for the character of the Altar, מזבח, in the same line of thought as the others.

It is only the מזבח, as הראל — as the way to the moral heights of the Torah, or the eminence which directs persisting at these heights, — that has קרנות, has high corners which aspire to reach even above the surface of the Altar. For it is just these קרנות that express “soaring upwards from the earth”, and it is they that give the Altar the meaning of “calling upwards”. When we come to consider the מזבח הזהב (Ch. XXX) we shall find these קרנות of the מזבח עולה in an even closer relation to the ennoblement and working up to the pure heights of the Torah which the Altar teaches.

So that in the very first place the Altar must have יסוד. On a firm basis its immovable position is indicated on the ground of the Sanctuary of the Torah, in front of its opened entrance. The Altar stands on the ground of the Torah and it is from this position that it derives its meaning. By it, it becomes הראל, the Mount of God leading to the loftiness of the Torah whose fire burns on its summit.

קרן and יסוד, these two belong together. קרן is the most characteristic part of the upper half, the real actual יסוד ;הראל that of the lower half, the עזרות, of the antechamber and the way up to the Mount of God. Both of them, as well as כבש, the actual material way up, by means of which the different parts of the Altar, the סובב and מערכה were reached, are characteristic only for the מזבח, and are lacking for the Bama, and equally so, and for the same reason is the מחיצה לדמים, that most characteristic division of the Altar for the ritual of the blood into upper and lower parts by the “netsieve” or the חוט הסיקרא (see above), also missing in the Bama. It is only the מזבח which invites Man to climb up to the heights of morality or to persist in every height he has attained; which is a contrivance which invites Man to realise the ideals which are represented by the שלחן ,ארון and מנורה. Therefore it alone has כבש ,יסוד ,קרן and חוט הסיקרא.
And that is why ריבוע squareness, is essential only for it, and why, equally with מתן סביב, placing the blood on the four sides, it is lacking on a Bama.

The דביר the “place of the Word”, the All Holiest, the real קדש הקדשים, from which all the קדשים derive their holiness, in which the “Evidence of the Torah” rests, has always to be in the west; in the היכל, the “place of executive power” for material and spiritual development, the north has always to be reserved for the “pure Table of material well-being”, and the south for the “Lamp which gets its light from the Teaching and gives its light to Teaching and to God”; but the east is to remain open for the nation created by the Word of God for these heights, and who are to be refined and strengthened by obtaining their material and their spiritual development from this Word of God. By this arrangement which had to be constant, each side of the Sanctuary and from that, each side of the Altar — the Altar which was to direct the way to the ideal life which the Sanctuary represents — took on the meaning of the particular object which was allocated to that side. The west side would belong to the תורה, the east to the nation, the people who are to be won for the Torah and strengthened in the Torah, the north to its material, the south to its spiritual, intellectual, affairs. So that if, for example, the identification of the bringer with his offering (סמיכה), the killing (שחיטה), and the taking up of the blood by the Sanctuary (קיבול דמים בכלי שרת) of עולה וחטאת and all קדשי קדשים had to be done in the north side (בצפון) this wants to express the idea that the whole “fresh new life”, which is the purpose of the offering, must start in the first instance, with the killing and restarting on a higher level of the material worldly sensual affairs of the old life. Exactly as the dedication to become a member of the National Covenant starts with the Milah. Or, to take an opposite example, the כבש, the actual way up to the heights of the Altar, up which the priest has to go to take the blood which has been accepted for its surrender to these heights, or to surrender the parts of the offerings to the Fire, if this כבש had to be on the south side it wants to express thereby, that the second condition for achieving the heights of moral perfection, is treading the path of obtaining clear illuminating mental clarity in the Torah and from the Torah (בדרום). Quite specially does the meaning of the sides appear in combination at the corners, and always turning to the right from the ascent, as south-east, east-north, north-west and west-south. In such combination, S.E. would designate: The Jewish nation awakened to the Torah by their intellect, by their understanding of it (the E coming from the S. I.L.); E.N. a material, worldly physical life brought about by such a nation (the N. coming from such an E. I.L.); N.W. the carrying out of the whole of the Divine Torah, the attempts to achieve the whole Torah, on the basis of such a moral material life (the W. from the N. I.L.); and W.S. the enlightenment of the human mind, having its source in the Torah. (the S. coming from the W. I.L.). The priestly finger making the ד׳ מתנות למעלה of the חטאת for one who has fallen through carelessness, would accordingly, preach to him that henceforth he must keep his נפש (that which the blood represents. I.L.) up to the heights of these four energies. He had stumbled because his mind had not clearly realised that being a Jew, a member of the Jewish people, must come from the source of the Torah (S. E.); or he had not sufficiently realised the demands that this Jewish life makes to control and elevate the ordinary material life of business and senses (E.N.) or, he had not understood that all material possessions and enjoyments must be regarded only as means to help towards achieving the Torah (N.W.); or, he had not kept the Torah in such a way that the higher development and enlightenment of his mind should grow out of it, (W.S.), and that it is only by holding fast to all these factors that one can remain protected from sinning through thoughtlessness. נסכים, expression of the deepest joy to be found before God, and only to be warranted by God, were poured down from the horn, the height of the W.S. corner, from the summit of mental enthusiasm which can be won from the Torah. All מנחות, all the means of bodily nourishment, health and content, were brought to this S.W. corner, to clear spiritual intellectual understanding coming from the Torah and directed to the Torah, מגישה בקרן דרומית מערבית כנגד חודה של קרן (Menachoth 29b), ביכורים, the first fruits of the material riches of the land were also deposited in this S.W. corner of the spirit, the mind directed towards the Torah and emphasised that they are to be regarded from a spiritual basis. בקרן דרומית מערבית בדרומה של קרן (Jerusalmi Bikurim 3,3) etc. etc.

If, then, the meaning of the sides of the Temple and the Altar all take their meaning from the “Evidence of the Torah” which rests in the west, which, with its right hand reaches us the Light, and with its left the Table, and which we, the people, go to meet on the opposite side, the east, and surrender our Table to it with our right hand and our Light with our left, we can dare to ask why should it be just in the west that the holiest of the Sanctuary, the Evidence of the Torah, should rest beneath the wings of the cherubim, and the east from which we approach it in homage? In a similar connection the Gemora in Baba Bathra (25a) says וצבא השמים לך משתחוים (Nehemiah 9,6), we see that “thus does the whole host of the heavens prostrate itself unto God”. Just as the whole heaven with all its constellations, the whole visible universe, appears to us daily to complete its course from east to west, and then sink down in the west, and this invariable phenomenon reverently proclaims “Him Who creates the heaven and its hosts” Whose almighty, world-regulating Law is proclaimed by every single star in its course; so has He taught us to set His Law for our little world and for our course through that little world in the west, so that we emulate the stars and keep immutably on the course He has set for us by His Law, and by in homage prostrating ourselves to His Law, proclaim His Name over the world.

That the שולחן, the representation of the material life of the senses, should be in the north, the side of darkness, the night; and the מנורה the representation of the spiritual life of mental illumination and clear thinking on the side of the midday, of intensity of light, is self-explanatory.

But if the sides of the הראל, the actual Altar, reproduce the sides of the היכל, the whole Altar itself in its upward-rising vertical plane may be taken to present the same structure that the Sanctuary does in the horizontal plane. The Torah resting in the Holy-of-Holies corresponds to the Fire on the Ariel summit; the הראל, reproducing the four sides of the היכל, leads up to it, and the lower portion is called the עזרה, just as the spaces in front of and around the Sanctuary in its horizontal projection are called עזרות.

The whole מזבח עולה is an arrangement to teach the ways by which the ignoble, and, as yet, unsanctified, human nature has to be discarded in order to become suitable for the ideals which are represented in the היכל and דביר. That is why it is covered with נחשת, copper, the metal representing the stage of not yet being ennobled. This metal relegates it as belonging to the introductory stage, the ante-chamber, the חצר, whose central point it forms, just as היכל and דביר obtain their character and meaning by the “golden” the מנורה ,שלחן ,ארון representing the “ideal” of the Jewish mission. It is accordingly called, simply, “the מזבח נחשת״.

V. 9. ועשית את חצר המשכן. As in the roots עצר ,עזר ,אצר ,אסר ,אזר, the idea of enclosure is expressed in its two-fold reference: beneficial to, and limiting, so a similar double meaning is in the roots חצר ,חשד ,חסר. חצר is a “spacious enclosure”, the fencing around a main building, so that the objects of the building are given the space to be developed. “Yard” in its real meaning, as a surrounding, encompassing adjunct. Hence the halls and rooms built around the later Temples, which also served the various purposes of the Temple, were called instead of חצר, “helping-rooms” עזרות. Nevertheless, we use the usual translation “forecourt”, although the חצר extended not only in front of the Sanctuary, but all around it, because by “yard” one usually understands a space behind the house, and because the essential part of the משכן-yard was actually the forecourt in front of the structure, the dimensions of which are mentioned in V.18 as an independent part, as being 50 cubits square.

לפאת נגב. Whereas צלע designates the solid fixed side of any space or room, פאה (related to פאה the root of פֶּה mouth, and פֹה, here) seems to refer more to the border line one fixes in one’s mind for an open space. So in Numbers 34,3, only the southern border of Palestine which was open to the desert is called פאה; and in Numbers 35,5 the border line of the extent to which the jurisdiction of the Levite cities extended (which also was, of course, quite open to the surrounding country I.L.) is called פאה on all sides. Here too, פאה is not the limits fixed by the קלעים but the border line of the חצר which is to be provided with curtains.

קלעים, Umhänge. Die Ableitung ist zweifelhaft. קלע heißt schleudern. Vielleicht heißen davon leichte, gleichsam nur umgeworfene Umhänge, im Gegensatz zu festen, dicken Teppichen: קלעים. Rabbinisch ist איקלע, passiv: treffen, zufällig irgendwo hingeraten, eigentlich: nach einem Orte hingeworfen werden, d. h. absichtslos dort hingeraten. Von dieser Bedeutung scheint die andere Bedeutung קליעה, flechten hergenommen zu sein: gegeneinandergeworfene, d. i, sich kreuzende Fäden. Daher auch möglich קלעים: geflochtene, oder flechtartig, hohle, dünne Vorhänge oder dergleichen Umhänge.

V. 10. חשקיהם. As the pillars are called מחשקים (V.17), חשוקים can not mean appurtenances of the pillars, but can only refer to the nature of the pillars themselves. השק is known as an expression for a strong desire for something. The root is related to עשׁק ,עשׂק .עזק ,אזק ,חזק ,חשׂך ,חשׁך, all of which have at root the idea of a strong taking hold of, either in a concrete sense or in a spiritual, intellectual one. חשק as a strong desire implies also enveloping the object in one’s mind, and is used here in a concrete sense for a silver encirclement surrounding each pillar.

V. 14. כתף .לכתף, the side pieces, taken from כתף the shoulder blade, were the side pieces on each side of the door at the front. The court was fifty cubits in width, fifteen cubits on each side were covered by curtains, so that a space of twenty cubits was left in the centre for an entrance.

V. 18. The whole area of the courtyard was five thousand square cubits (from which we take the standard size for enclosures for living purposes שבעים אמה ושירים על שבעים אמה ושירים ,סאתים ,קרפף (70 + x 70+ = 5,000. I.L.) Erubin 23b) 100 cubits long by 50 cubits broad. The משכן itself, thirty cubits in length and ten cubits in width stood on the border line of the front fifty cubits, so that it had a space behind it and on each side, of twenty cubits, but in front of it an open square of fifty cubits in each direction. So that if one stood at the eastern extremity of the forecourt one could see on either side the whole length of one hundred cubits of the חצר but in front of the Sanctuary only a square of fifty cubits. We have translated the ורובה of this verse as the “free width” which really is the underlying literal meaning of the root, implying “free, spacious”.
חצר

Let us picture the courtyard to ourselves. It was formed by white curtains made of linen which itself was made of sixply twisted thread. The curtains were hung from pillars, which stood on copper sockets or feet, and which were encircled by silver, and held the curtains by silver hooks. The whole of the arrangement stood in close connection with the meaning of the forecourt and the Altar from which it really derives its meaning and importance. Like the Altar, the whole environment announces to us: we are standing in the forecourt of purification. The main impression we receive is of whiteness, and moreover of white linen. This conveys to us the idea of purity, of טהרה, and moreover of טהרה in the first place in the sphere of the vegetable side of human nature, the sphere of eating and drinking and sexual life. This is the very first stage to be aimed at, its nature is purely negative, the keeping away from everything unholy, from everything which defiles human nature for its holy and high calling. It is the preliminary stipulation for all positive progress. And this representation of the purity that is demanded from us, both in the number of the threads and in the name which the material bears, has the symbol שש, “six”, the symbol of “the created”, of this material world. The great mission of self-control to which the חצר calls us is nothing super-human, is nothing that calls for some sublime elevation that is beyond the normal power of human nature. It is the Creator of that human nature Who calls us to it, and He demands nothing that He has not granted us the gifts and ability to accomplish. It is just for this purity that He has created us, it is only by it that we are complete human beings, and justify the godly nature of our being that He has infused into the making of us. The whole concept of Man is a being with complete freedom of moral will, and the first expression of that is purity.

The pillars of the חצר stand on copper feet, but have silver encirclements, and at the top silver hooks; the walls of the sanctuary stand on silver feet, but otherwise are overlaid with gold. From copper to silver, to gold. that is the progress out of ignoble character, through purification, to immutable pure gold. That, up to which the forecourt struggles, forms the basis on which the Sanctuary stands, and which offers the noblest perfection. By this allocation of the metals, the step-by-step progressive nature of the teaching of the whole edifice is indicated.

We have still to consider the מסך פתח האהל (Ch. 26,36 & 37) the curtain at the entrance of the Sanctuary, and the מסך שער החצר Ch 27,16) the curtain at the entrance of the forecourt. Both consisted of the same materials as the tapestry (the curtains around the walls of the Mishkon. I.L.) viz., תכלת וארגמן ותולעת שני ושש. But they did not consist of woven cherubim, from our text we must assume that they were quite without any figures, and if, nevertheless, they are described as מעשה רוקם as embroidery fancywork, one material, presumably the linen, was woven for the background and the other woollen threads of blue, purple and scarlet worked on it as needlework (see above on XXVI,1). The curtain at the entrance to the courtyard was hung on pillars similar to those of the surround of the court. But the curtain at the entrance to the Mishkon was hung or pillars which although in all other respects were similar to the other pillars round the walls of the Mishkon and were of shittim wood overlaid with gold, were, like those of the forecourt, on feet of copper.

We have already remarked above, that the materials of the cherubim-tapestry were the same which in the garments of the High Priest represent the elements of perfection in the human character. If these materials appear here in these door and gate curtains without the pattern of cherubim woven into them, they can not be meant to bring to our notice cherubim announcing the presence of God, as the tapestries are, but only the fundamental elements of the human character which are to be brought to perfection. If what we have taken to be the meaning of the מעשה רוקם is correct, then the two reds and the blue woollen threads stitched on the white linen background would represent the godly (blue) in conjunction with the animal and human (the two degrees of red) activities of actual life, lived on the foundation of vegetative (eating and drinking and sexual) purity. When we come to consider the prescribed priestly garments we shall find that the ordinary priests wore the colour of the forecourt, the High Priest colours of the Mishkon, thereby relegating the former to representing the preliminary negative stage of purity, the latter to the positive achievement of raising every phase of human life — vegetative, animal, human, divine — into the realm of spirituality. Now, just as even the white-clad כהן הדיוט bore in his girdle the positive colours of the Mishkon, and thereby appeared as “girded” for the positive holy perfection of Man, showing thereby this positive holiness as the goal to be aimed at; in the same way, the “white” forecourt displayed at its entrance the positive colours of the Sanctuary. It thereby held up to the eyes of all who entered there, from the very start, as the real object and goal, the positive holy perfection of life by carrying out the purposes of God, with the Table and Lamp, with all material and spiritual possessions and powers, as the Sanctuary teaches. The “white” forecourt of purity must at once be recognised as forming only the indispensable preliminary stage, but the intention and resolve to attain the ultimate height of the Sanctuary must be made at the beginning on entry to the forecourt.

That is probably also why exactly the same curtain hung at the entrance to the Sanctuary itself, and why the pillars from which it was hung stood, not like the other shittim walls of the Sanctuary on silver feet, but exactly like the pillars of the curtain of the forecourt, on copper feet, to tell us:- Here (in the Sanctuary) is nothing new on some different standpoint to be taught, but only the realisation of that which already at the entrance to the forecourt had to be visualised as the goal to be worked for.

V. 20. We have already remarked above on Ch. 25,6, that there “oil for lighting”, is reckoned amongst the articles which were to be donated for the establishing of the Mishkon. The fact that the oil and the קטרת (which is also mentioned there) both of which really belong to the עבודה of the Mishkon rather than to the Mishkon itself, are mentioned in that list, expresses the idea that these two — the one representing illumination and clarity of the mind, and the other complete sublimation of all actions to make them something that is pleasing to God — together express the whole aim of that ennoblement of Man for which the מקדש is to work, and so they do belong essentially to that which the מקדש itself represents. (In the עבודה too, we find נרות and קטרת intimately connected with each other, see Ch. 30,7 & 8). Here it can not speak of קטרת, as the making of the קטרת has not yet been ordered. By bringing “the Service of the Lights” here, immediately following the orders for building the Sanctuary, and even preceding the instructions for the priestly garments, two things are indicated. On the one hand the עבודת הנרות, “the Care of the Lights” is the duty which in point of time is to take precedence over all other duties, as the clearness of mental vision which is to be derived from the Torah, is the “mother” of keeping the dictates of the Torah, גדול תלמוד שמביא לידי מעשה; and on the other hand, that the essential mission of the כהן is nurturing the enlightenment that is to be derived from the Torah. שפתי כהן ישמרו דעת ותורה יבקשו מפיהו (Mal. 2,7). These points are necessary for the understanding of the meaning of the priestly garments, the instructions for the making of which immediately follow in the succeeding verses.

ואתה תצוה את בני ישראל. “Thou” as the transmitter of the Torah, the study of which, as a very first duty for all time, is to be represented by this care of the Lights, תצוה “command”, put it before them as a special duty. The Sages in the Gemora remark that תצוה is used where special emphasis is to be laid on the seriousness and importance of a duty which is incumbent immediately and also for all time מיד ולדורות, and above all, וביותר שיש בו חסרון כיס, where it is a question of sacrificing material wealth for spiritual ends, the profit of which does not seem to be immediately apparent. את בני ישראל, and repeated also in V.21, מאת בני ישראל, the care for looking after the spiritual education is to be the responsibility of the general community, not the special prerogative of the priestly caste. The “oil” of the nation is to be offered for the light of the תורה; the מנורה represents the tree of the national spirit, not that of the priests. It is highly characteristic that it is only הטבת נרות — the daily provision of the means for obtaining light, and the conditioning of the lamps and wicks to produce a clear bright light — that is the real עבודת כהונה. The actual lighting might, if the necessity arose, be performed by a “non-priest” a “layman” (Yoma 25b; Maim. הל׳ ביאת המקדש IX,7) as הדלקה לאו עבודה היא.

ויקחו אליך. Even when you use it, it is to remain theirs. You are only the גזבר for it, and its use is made in their name. (See on Ch. 25,2). מזיתו :שמן זית ;שמן זית זך כתית ripened on the tree, become oil on the tree. כתית, pressed, extracted from the fruit by pressure alone, but not by טחינה crushing or grinding in a mill (Menachoth Mishna, 86a). — למאור, the very best, finest, purest oil which was obtained in this way was only required למאור for lighting, for מנחות all these refinements were not necessary (ibid.).

להעלות נר, this expression for kindling lights occurs only with reference to the service of the מנורה. It is the precise description of the demand to keep the kindling flame against the wick until the latter “burns by itself” שתהא שלהבת עולה מאליה. The work of a תורה-teacher is to make himself superfluous! Not to keep the “laity” in lasting dependence on the teachers or priests. At the same time it is an admonition to enduring patience for teacher and pupil.
נר תמיד, according to ת״כ on Levit. 24,2, the נר מערבי. See above end of Ch. XXV and תוספות Menachoth 86b.

V. 21. באהל מועד. The most usual name for the Sanctuary, from יעד, related to יחד, to fix a meeting. See on Ch. 25,21, מועד, the time, or, as here, the place, for such a meeting. It is called אהל מועד, either since it is by the Sanctuary that the special presence of God in Israel, brought about by their acceptance of the Torah with complete self-surrender, is manifested; or, inasmuch as God has appointed it as the place for His revelation to Moses (see ibid.), as well as the place where Israel is constantly to give afresh practical proof of their connection with God, where they have ever afresh “to come to a meeting with God”. Next in importance to the existence of the “Place of the Evidence of the Torah” — the דביר, the “Place of the Word”, the source of the Light — the constant service of the “Lights” on the “Tree of National Development” (the Menorah. I.L.) is necessary for the meaning of the “Tent” as אהל מועד, as the Tent of “finding oneself together with God”.

מחוץ לפרכת אשר על העדות. Repeated similarly in Levit. 24,3. מחוץ לפרכת העדות. The human mind, turning towards the Torah and receiving enlightenment from the Torah, has constantly to be kept conscious that it stands מחוץ, outside the תורה. The Torah is something that has been given to it, not produced by it. It has to draw and increase its knowledge and enlightenment out of the Torah, but never to take its own light into the realm of the Torah to alter or reform it. It has always to keep itself conscious of the פרכת, of the cherubim who come down to divide off and protect the Torah, and, should the need arise, to preserve it against any tendency of the human mind, which misjudging its true position, could turn against the inviolability of the Torah, and, instead of sitting as a disciple at the feet of the Torah, dare to assume an arrogant mastery over it.

יערוך אותו אהרן ובניו. Not יעלה. By עריכה is probably to be understood what is known as the הטבה, keeping the lamps in order, cleaning, putting in oil and wick etc. The הדלקה is not restricted exclusively to the כהן although it was usually done by them. (See on V.20).

מערב עד בקר. All the seven lamps were given just sufficient oil to burn from nightfall till morning. For the people in general, the day was there primarily for work, for activity, and only the relaxation of the night was to be available for study, for the work of the intellect. Hence only מערב עד בקר. Nevertheless the נר מערבי went on burning from one evening till the next in spite of not receiving more oil than the other six. This happened continuously right down to the time of שמעון הצדיק (over 1,100 years. I.L.). If, after that time it was found to have gone out by the morning, it was kindled again from the fire on the Altar (see above, end of Ch. XXV and on Levit. 6,6 & XXIV,3).

V. 1. ואתה הקרב as ואתה תצוה. Thou, as the transmitter and representative of the Torah. Later on, too, the High Priests could only be appointed by the highest Court, the Sanhedrin, who succeeded to the post that Moses occupied. (Maim. הל׳ כלי המקדש IV,15). It is the nation which gives the High Priest the honour of being their representative for the Sanctuary of the Torah which had been entrusted to it.

הקרב אליך. He attains the honour of being taken from the midst of the nation to be placed near to “you”, for your work for the nation, inasmuch as he is set to work for the accomplishment of the object of your mission.

כַהֵן ,לכהנו לי, in the Piel, never means to set someone up as a priest, but to function as a priest. So ויכהן אלעזר (Numbers 3,4). — לכהנו לי and equally in V.4. בגדי קדש לאהרן אחיך ולבניו לכהנו לי. The service of the priesthood and also that which is to be expressed symbolically by the garments, refers primarily to Aaron, to the High Priest. Nadab, Abihu etc., the כהני הדיוט are to be to him as sons to a father, helping him and performing part of the service in his stead. He, the High Priest, can at any time, bring any of the sacrifices, and do any עבודה himself without any consideration for the rota which was established for the other כהנים. He belonged to no special משמר or בית אב, and had not to take part in any פײס (casting lots for the right to perform any special service. I.L.) (Yoma 14a). In the מקדש all the other priests were only his representative helpers. But regarding the gifts which had to be given to the priests outside the מקדש, the קדשי גבול, he had absolutely no preferential rights. (Maim. כלי המקדש V.12).

V. 2. בגדי קדש, holy garments, really “garments of the Sanctuary”, garments which show the wearers as standing in the service of the Sanctuary. — כבוד ;לכבוד is the spiritual כָּבֵד, the weight, the mass, that by which the spiritual and moral content, the character, of a person impresses itself on others. So that the meaning of the כהונה is to express itself in the garments. כבוד is the real actual character of the garments. At the same time they are to be made in such a manner that they also serve as תפארת to the פאר .כהן related to בחר ,בהר ,באר which all have the idea at root of shining forth, being conspicuous, or distinguished. לתפארת adds the demand that besides the given necessary conditions expressed by לכבוד, the garments also satisfy the requirements of the sense of beauty; that they distinguish the כהן in an aesthetic manner.

V. 3. ואתה תדבר. As the כהן is to be the elect of the nation, the garments too, in which alone he may function as כהן, are to be made by the nation, to be national property. It is the garb of the nation in which the כהן approaches to עבודה (Yoma 35b). If here, at the making of the garments the requisite חכמה is at once specially stressed, whereas for the making of all the rest of the work this quality is only mentioned in Ch. XXXI when Bezalal and Ahaliab are named, the reason can well be, that regarding the Sanctuary itself and its appurtenances, everything in every detail had to follow meticulously the model shown to Moses, whereas, in the case of the garments, more room was left for the taste of the maker. ועשו וגו׳ לקדשו: The garments had to be made with the definite idea in the mind of the worker of the purpose for which they were to be used. Then, and then only, did they give the כהן the requisite קדושה (see also רמב״ן).

V. 4. חשן. This word only occurs referring to this article of clothing of the High Priest. According to V.16 its size was a square span and according to V.22—29 it was worn on the breast, hence it is usually translated a “breast plate”. It is phonetically related to חסן which means the safe keeping of valuable possessions, and to חצן the arm bent to hold something fast. According חשן which was double (V.16) and which was for the purpose of keeping the Urim and Tumim between its two layers, would really designate a kind of breast pocket or pouch.

אפד. From V. 5—7 we know what the ephod consisted of: — a back piece from which two shoulder strips went over the shoulders to the front, and were joined to the back piece on either side under the arms. It was also buttoned or buckled up in front below the breast by a חשב, a kind of bib. We know further from V.31. מעיל האפד and from Levit. 8,7 ויתן עליו את הכתנת ויחגר אתו באבנט וילבש אתו את המעיל ויתן עליו את האפד ויחגר אתו בחשב האפד ויאפד לו בו, that the essential purpose of the ephod was to keep the מעיל, the mantle, the outer-garment, fitted closely to the figure. So that the אפד served the מעיל as the אבנט the girdle served the כתנת. More, we know from the last quotation as well as from ואפדת לו בחשב האפד (XXIX,5) that the root אפד itself must mean a girding, fitting and holding a garment close to and about the body, so that, as our ephod gets its name from that root, its essential symbolic meaning must be taken as “girding”. According to Rashi and also to Maim. הל׳ כלי המקדש IX,9, a piece of the material hung down at the back to the feet. But there is no indication of this at all in the text or in the Gemora. It seems to us that ויתן עליו את האפד ויחגר אתו בחשב האפד (Ex. 8,7) from which Rashi is driven to the conclusion that the ephod must have had some constituent part other than that which served to gird, does not necessarily prove this. In any case the ephod was more than just an ordinary girdle. A girdle just goes round the waist. But the ephod embraced the back, shoulders, breast and loins. But it only did this when it was buckled up in front by the חשב. By this חשב the back piece and the shoulder pieces too, were firmly tightened. By the closing of the חשב it really became אפד, hence ויאפד לו בו.

When we try to find the literal meaning of the root אפד, we get the phonetic relation to עבת then עבד ,אות ,אוד .אות ,אוד ,עבד refer respectively to the mechanical, mental and social means of attaining one’s object. עבת (cord or rope. I.L.), is most frequently used to designate, not a means for tying up, for restricting or checking, but as a means of binding and holding together to make something serviceable for one’s purpose. So קצץ עבות רשעים (Ps. 129,4), עבות העגלה (Is. 5,18), תלם עבותו (Job 39,10), עבתות אהבה (Hosea 11,4). And so אפד too, seems to express and mean gathering together one’s forces in the service of a Higher One, just as being girded denotes being ready for action. So that אפד is intimately related to עבד and wearing an אפד is the most significant expression for an עבד לעבוד עבודה, for one girded for עבודה. Hence ’שאת אפד לפני ה is synonymous with being a priest before God (Sam. I. 2,28). Hence to place oneself as a servant to God, was expressed by wearing an ephod (Sam. I. 2,18; Sam. II. 6,14). Hence, while the linen-woollen-golden Ephod prescribed here belonged to the garments which the High Priest had to wear when officiating, the priests generally outside the “service”, just as in the last quotations, Samuel and David, wore a linen ephod. (Sam. I. 22,18).

מעיל. From V. 31—33 we learn that the מעיל was a garment which had a circular opening at the neck, so that it was drawn on over the head like a shirt, and, enclosing the whole body, hung down from the shoulders to the feet. From all the places where מעיל occurs elsewhere it was evidently used for the top or outer garment which embraced the whole body, on account of which the term עטה is repeatedly used regarding it, and was only worn by those of superior rank (like the Roman toga. I.L.). The מעיל was made entirely of sky-blue wool. (V.31).

כתנת .כתנת תשבץ is a garment which, as we learn from Levit. 8,7, is worn directly next to the skin. It was made of fine linen (V.39). It receives its special nature by the addition of the word תשבץ. This can not mean merely some kind of ornamentation on it, as the way in which it is to be made is described in V.19 as ושבצת הכתנת שש. So that תשבץ must be some speciality of the material itself. In V.11 and V.20 שבץ occurs as the settings of precious stones. In Sam. II. 1,9 the Amalekite makes the dying Saul say “אחזני השבץ״ and this seems to refer to cramp, the death struggle, a meaning which is very closely related to the tight gripping of the settings of precious stones. According to Rashi and also Maim. הל׳ כלי המקדש VIII,16 the linen for the כתנת was woven into a pattern of small hollows, like hollows into which stones were to be set. Maimonides adds as an explanatory note כמו בית הכוסות, like the second stomach of ruminants, the inner surface of which consists of a kind of rough network of lozenge-shaped little pits. We accordingly translate תשבץ: Inset pattern or box pattern.

מצנפת. From Isaiah 22,18 it is evident that צנף means a circular movement about a central point. There it refers to the rolling of a ball. That would be in accordance with the explanation which Maim. gives in הל׳ כלי המקדש VIII,19 that the מצנפת consisted of sixteen cubits (about 10 yards. I.L.) of cloth wound round the head (like a turban. I.L.). V.39 tells us that it was made of fine linen.

אבנט. Acording to Maim. (ibid.) it was a girdle, three finger-breadths in width and thirty-two cubits in length, which, as we can see from Levit. 8,7 girded the כתנת. It was not allowed to be worn higher than the hip, in a line with the elbow joint. (Maim. ibid. X,1 & 2). It was according to V.39. מעשה רקם i.e., similar to the curtain at the door and gate (Ch. 26,36 & XXVII,16) with the three coloured wools on a white linen background. (See notes on Ch. 26,36).
’ועשו בגדי קדש וגו, in this repetition the sons are also mentioned. Here too, as remarked on V.1, they appear as subordinate and auxiliary to Aaron.

V. 6. Moses was only to name and appoint the workers, but they were to receive the materials for making the garments directly from the hands of the people. If we remember that these garments were to be associated for all time with the consecration and the dignity and honour of the priesthood, and in these garments the priests attain the high distinction of being the chosen representatives of the nation in the Sanctuary, but on the other hand, were only to carry out their service in the Sanctuary as servants of the nation, we can well understand, from both points of view, that it is expressly stressed that the makers of these garments should receive the materials for them directly from the hands of the people. Thereby the people themselves declare their agreement with the granting of this distinction, and it is the people who invest the priest with his garments.
V. 7. וחבר. The two parts which come over the shoulders are again to be joined to the back part below the shoulders on either side, and so make the ephod one single piece.

V. 8. חשב, basic meaning is “joining together”, but in such a way that even when joined the parts can still be seen to be separate. In that it differs from חבר which expresses a complete junction, and that makes חשב also the expression used for a combination of thoughts and for reckoning. חשב a connecting bib that joins the two sides of a garment together about the body, temporarily, while the garment is being worn.

V. 9. שהם. Although שהם-stones also occur amongst the אבני מִל֭אִים, the precious stones set in the חשן, they are nevertheless mentioned separately in Ch. 25,7, in the summons to provide the gifts, it says there were אבני שהם ואבני מלאים. It seems that the word שהם was originally not the actual name of the special stone, as אדם ,פטדה etc. are, but a general name for a class of stones, like מלאים is, which designates the use to which these stones are put. The root שהם points, as כהן and בהן ,כון and רהב ,בון and רוב, to שום which is the root of שם, and so would designate a stone which is principally used for engraving a seal. That would concur with what the Gemora says in ע״ז 8b:- אנך וספר תורה איזה מהן יעשה בסיס לחברו ,אנך לס״ת, that ס״ת is more valuable than onyx, as onyx is used as a base for writing the words. According to the Aruch, שהם is onyx. The two onyx or shoham stones of the ephod would then differ from the stones of the choshen in that these two have no meaning in themselves, but merely serve as a base for the names of the tribes to be engraved on them, whereas the stones in the choshen would by their special characteristics, themselves represent, each one a different tribe. This would also allow us to understand more correctly the words of V.21:— והאבנים תהײן על שמת בני ישראל שתים עשרה על שמתם, פתוחי חותם איש על שמו תהײן לשנים עשר שבט, that the first half of the verse says, that, even without the engraving, the stones themselves are in close relationship to the names which are to be engraved on them. It would also conform to a dictum in Sota 49b. There the Gemora explains the יהיו במלואתם of V.20 to mean “they shall be in their completeness”, that the names were not to be cut into the surface by a tool or graver, but cast up upon it by a שמיר working within the stone, so that not a grain of the material of the stone is discarded, but the stones remain במלואתם “in their full completeness”. Disagreeing with Rashi (ibid.), Ramban on Ex. 25,7 takes this to apply only to the stones of the choshen. The shoham stones here on the ephod were definitely engraved with a graver, it says quite clearly in V.11 מעשה חרש אבן. This would all be perfectly in accordance with our explanation. The two shoham stones had no meaning in themselves, were merely to serve as a base for the inscription of the names of the tribes. It was only by the engraving on them that they had a meaning, so the engraving could do away with some of their material. But the choshen stones, even without the engraving had the symbolic meaning of the tribes they were to represent, and so nothing of their material was to be missing, but the particles of the material could be separated and thrown up in ridges to form the names of the tribes.

V. 10. כתולדתם. According to Sota 36b this does not mean in order of their birth, but is a qualification of שמות, the names are not to be patronymic or tribal, not שמעוני ,ראובני etc., the tribe of Reuben, Simeon etc., but the actual name of the ancestor, “as were given to them at their birth” i.e., ראובן ,שמעון etc. The Gemora there gives the order in which they were engraved on the stones as being:— בני לאה כסדרן ,בני רחל אחד מכאן ואחד מכאן, ובני שפחות באמצע which Rashi takes to mean the six sons of Leah, Reuben, Simeon, Levi, Judah, Issachar and Zebulun on the one stone, and on the other the two sons of Rachel, Joseph and Benjamin, and between them the sons of the maidservants i.e., Benjamin, Dan, Naphtali, Gad, Asher, Joseph, the order in which they are ennumerated in Ex. 1,2—4. Maim. הל׳ כלי המקדש puts them in a different order (See כ״מ thereon).

V. 13. משבצות. Where these “settings” were placed on the ephod is not at all clear. From V.14 and 25 it is clear that they were placed on the shoulderpieces of the ephod and that the chains from which the choshen hung were fastened on to them. We are very much inclined to think that these משבצות (perhaps mentioned here separately again, to say that they must be made for the double purpose of mounting the stones and of supporting the choshen, possibly by means of an extra claw. I.L.) are none other than the settings of the shoham-stones mentioned in V.11.

V. 14. שרשרות, chains. As these same chains are called שרשות in V.22, the root seems to be שרש (and not שרר). In Gen. 39,1, we have shown the connection between שרש and זרז and סרס and taken the underlying meaning to be:- Transmitted or indirect use. It is possible that therefrom it became the expression for chains, inasmuch as a chain is a combination of links by means of which the strength is transmitted from one to the other and from the last one to the desired object.

מגבלות is obscure (we have translated it “end-chains” I.L.). It, as well as שרשות גבלת in V.22, seems to describe the nature of the chains, the special way in which they were to be made, and definitely not the place to which they had to extend. Disagreeing with Rashi, Maim. הל׳ כלי המקדש IX,8, 9, and 10, says that the חשן and the כתפות האפוד were joined together not by two but by four gold chains. On either side one chain went down from the משבצות of the shoulderpieces of the ephod, and was fastened to a ring on the top of the חשן, and another chain went up from the חשן and was fastened to a ring on the ephod, i.e., on each side two chains. This agrees better with the actual wording of the text. The two chains of V.14 would be the ephod-chains and the chains of V.22, the two choshen-chains. V.24 would describe the fixing of the two ephod-chains to the chosen-rings, and V.25 the fixing of the two choshen-chains to the rings of the ephod-mountings. The only thing that then would be missing in the text would be the order, that in addition to the outgoing chains, two rings were to be placed on the mountings to receive the choshen-chains. (If, as is the opinion of the רמב״ן, the משבצות were not box-mountings, but bent claw mounts, which just held the stones in place, then the חשן chains could also fix on such משבצות-claws and would not require any special rings). Apart from this, this way of taking it is far more in accordance with the text. It avoids the difficulty which otherwise arises as to the repetition in V.22 and 23 of what has already been said in V.14. And then we may also find the meaning of the מגבלות and גבלות. The text differentiates between chains which are attached to a ring in an object, and those which come out directly as a continuation or extension of an object. These latter are called מגבלות and their nature is called גבלות, they are “end-chains”, extensions which really form the extreme ends (גבל I.L.) of the object itself. The difference in the meaning of the two means of attachment is obvious. If A ends in a גבלות chain and this chain is hung on a ring in B, then A is chained to B, not B to A. But if at the same time an end-chain goes from B and hooks in to a ring in A, then the attachment of A and B is completely mutual. A attaches itself to B in exactly the same way as B does to A.
