Each one holds the other and is held by it. This most intimate form of junction is to exist between the אפד and the חשן. From each of them “end-chains” go to join the other.

מעשה עבות (like ropes or cords. I.L.). Each of the chains is not to consist of a single strand of pure gold, but to be made up of several strands twisted together like a cord. That is what the expression שרשרת עבתת must mean. So it seems to us. If, as Rashi seems to explain, they did not consist of links at all, but were קליעת חוטין threads braided together then the addition of עבות would do away with the idea of שרשרת altogether, they would not be chains but cords.
V. 16. רבוע יהיה כפול; it was two spans long, and one span wide, so that when folded over it formed a square of one span.
V. 17. טור, phonetically related to דבר ,תפר ,דור ,תור all of which express ranging in a row.

V. 21. ’והאבנים תהײן וגו see above on V.9. — ’פתוחי חותם וגו. According to Yoma 73b, apart from the names of the twelve tribes, אברהם יצחק ויעקב and שבטי ישורון were also on the stones. The מ״ר at the end of תצוה says that on אדם was engraved אברהם יצחק ויעקב ראובן, on פטדה the name of שמעון, and then one each on all the stones till ישפה, on which was engraved בנימן ,שבטי ישורון. Thus every letter of the א״ב could be found for the purpose of asking the Urim and Tumim, otherwise ח ,ט ,צ ,ק would be lacking, as they do not occur in the names of the tribes.
V. 22—25. See above on V.14.

V. 26—28. By the chains just described the חשן was joined to the shoulderpieces of the ephod, but the lower edge of it still hung loose on the breast. So that it should be fixed below also, two rings were fixed on its lower end, ביתה on the inner side, the surface towards the ephod אל עבר האפד. Similarly two rings were fixed on the lower end of the shoulderpieces of the ephod where they joined the back-piece לעמת מחברתו above the חשב. Then by means of a sky-blue tape, the lower end of the choshen was firmly laced through these four rings to the ephod. ולא יזח החשן מעל האפד is not merely the purpose, but is a direct prohibition similar to that which we had above (Ch. 25,15) with regards to the לא יסורו ממנו בדי הארון. The choshen may never be allowed to be separated from the ephod (Yoma 72a).

V. 32. ’והיה פי ראשו וגו. The opening at the top is to be doubled inwards and so form a strong stiff hem. The hem is to go סביב right round, the neck of the garment is to be a complete circle and מעשה ארג, woven from the beginning with the garment, not made afterwards by stitching the edge inwards. כפי תחרא, Onkelos translates תחרא by שרײן, a coat of mail. The word does not occur anywhere else in the Scriptures and its derivation is obscure. — לא יקרע is a prohibition, that, according to Yoma 72a, applies likewise to all the priestly garments. But according to one opinion this prohibition as regards the other garments is only, if done with destructive intent דרך השחתה. But the close hem of the מעיל may not be rent for any purpose whatsoever (e.g., to make it fit the neck more easily. I.L.) (See מל״מ on הל׳ כלי המקדש IX,3).

V. 33. ’רמני תכלת וגו. These pomegranates were the only instances where the three coloured wool materials occur in the garments without the linen (white. I.L.). In the tapestries and curtains of the Sanctuary and courtyard too, it does not occur. According to Zebachim 88b, they were made in the form of unopened pomegranates so that the seeds were not shown, but would be concealed within the fruit. The bells were placed alternately with the pomegranates. There were seventy two bells and the same number of pomegranates. Ramban is of the opinion that the bells were inside the pomegranates. The explanation in the Gemora that דמונים שלא פתחו פיהן, they were of the shape of unopened pomegranates would favour the previous opinion which both Rashi and Maimonides adopt (הלי כלי המקדש IX,4).

V. 35. לשרת. If we compare the places in which שרת occurs in connections other than that of the service which the priests had to render in the Sanctuary, we find that its meaning relatively to the synonymous עבד is, that עבד is generally placing one’s services at the disposal of another whether for his person, his property or his purposes and to act under his orders, but שרת is quite specially not so much for “serving” as for “waiting on” (not so much “dienen” as “bedienen”), seeing that the personal requirements of another are efficiently satisfied. If then, the activities of the כהן in the Sanctuary are regarded under the idea of שרת, this designates the presence of God in Israel which is to be the whole object expressed by the Sanctuary — שכינתו בתוכם — as being God’s wish and desire, but at the same time as being conditional on Israel’s fulfilling something, which is just what the “service” of the כהן in the מקדש is to express. This is a feeling of a personal relationship to God, an attendance on Him, seeing to it that His requirements are satisfied. This is why the service of the כהן which is to picture a similar personal relationship to God, is designated by the term שרת. It is never directly alluded to in the תורה as עבודה, only in Numbers 18,7, to differentiate it from the service of the Levites, which actually is עבודה (and which, only with reference to their personal relationship to the כהנים as their assistants is called שרת); it is called עבודת מתנה, “service of devotion”. This characterises their service as one whose special mission is performing such rites which express the “devotion” of the individual and the nation to God. עבודת מתנה is nothing but a paraphrase of שרת, and accordingly is the legal idea of those עבודות, regarding which it is there said that והזר הקרב יומת, and which are defined in Yoma 24a as עבודת מתנה ולא עבודת סילוק “services of positive devotion” (such as זריקה הקטרה וניסוך המים וײן) but not “negative service of clearing away” (such as תרומת הדשן). Apart from this, another condition is necessary, viz., that it is also עבודה תמה, i.e., that the sacrificial procedure must be complete and nothing lacking. Here and also in Ch. 39,26 the purpose לשרת is specially stressed at the מעיל, and this idea is not unimportant for our understanding of the significance and meaning of the garments (see below).

V. 36. ציץ, (phonetically related to זיז and שיש, outer and inner movement becoming perceptible), ציץ means “springing into view” and hence “breaking into bloom”, the blossom; ציצת ראש, the projecting forelock which first strikes one. מציץ בין החרכים (Song of Songs 2,9) peering forth between the lattices. Hence here ציץ, something which presents itself strikingly to the eye of the onlooker. According to Sabbath 63b, it was a narrow oblong of gold extending across the forehead from ear to ear. It bore the inscription ’קדש לה in two lines with the ’ה, the full name of God at the end of the top line first, Maimonides says it was רבי .קדש לה׳ אליעזר ברבי יוסי reported (ibid.) that he had seen it in Rome among the trophies, with the inscription written in one line, from which Maimonides deduces that the writing in two separate lines was not prescribed as obligatory.

V. 38. ונשא אהרן את עון הקדשים. The concluding sentence ’והיה וגו׳ לרצון וגו proves that the expression נשא עון is not to be taken here in the sense of taking on oneself, and bearing, guilt, but as נושא עון, doing away with such guilt, repenting for and obtaining forgiveness for such guilt. עוה ;עון הקדשים from which עון comes, means primarily, crooked. So that, used with regard to morals, it is the opposite of ישר, straight, and indicates any deviation from the straight path, i.e., from what is really moral. Transferred from persons to things, here to sacred things, קדשים, it designates literally, removing them from the path which is set for them by their being dedicated to God’s Sanctuary, bringing them to a condition which would impress upon them a removal from that which is their purpose. This condition must be of a purely objective nature, עון הקדשים the עון of the sacred objects themselves, not עון מקדישים, not the עון of those who make, or consider them sacred. Their condition is one that contradicts the idea of their consecration, one that would make them invalid, פסול, for the idea of that consecration. By the forehead of the High Priest, who represents the whole service of the Sanctuary, bearing the inscription ’קדש לה i.e., positively declaring God, — as He is represented in the whole completeness of His free personal nature by the name ’ה, — as the One Being to Whom the Sanctuary is consecrated, and to Whom, accordingly, all the sacred objects of the Sanctuary are directed, by this declaration, any possible disturbance or clouding of the pure idea of the true relationship to God which these sacred objects of the Sanctuary might have suffered, is eliminated. The positive proclamation ’קדש לה which radiates from the forehead of the High Priest over the whole of the Sanctuary gives every object in the Sanctuary the positive function of being ’קדש לה. It can remove a misconception by which, in certain conditions, sacred objects could be affected. It is effective when these conditions concern the actual nature of the objects themselves, and if these objects are within the most limited sphere of the Sanctuary. Tradition teaches (Pesachim 80b, 77a and b; Menachoth 25a; Zebachim 23a and b) that the power of ’קדש לה on the ציץ to remove any disturbance of the efficiency of sacred objects only applies to טומאה, and with certainty, only to עולין i.e., to those parts of the offerings that as דם ,קומץ ,אימורים, are placed on the Altar as expressing direct surrender to ’ה. With less certainty the ציץ is effective also for אכילות as e.g., בשר, where the relationship to God is not so direct, and the priests or owners who eat it are in the foreground. Opinions differ on this point, and equally so, on טומאת הגוף of the officiating priest in a case of טומאת התהום i.e., such טומאה the existence of which was impossible to have been known at the time by any human being, or in the case of קרבנות צבור שקבוע להם זמן of communal offerings which have to be brought for a special occasion, where the importance of the occasion and the community are in the foreground. Hence we find written in Pesachim 81a הציץ מרצה על טומאת הדם ואין הציץ מרצה על טומאת הגוף נטמא טומאת התהום הציץ מרצה: נטמא הקומץ והקריבו הציץ מרצה, יצא והקריבו אין הציץ מרצה, שהציץ מרצה על הטמא ואינו מרצה על היוצא (Menachot 25a): טומאה דחויה היא בצבור ובעיא ציץ לרצות (Pesachim 77a). אין ציץ מרצה על אכילות (ibid.), Now in fact there is no פסול מוקדשים which stands in such direct contradiction to the pure conception of God that the word ’ה conveys to the Jewish mind, and which is so necessary for the whole consecration and purpose of the Sanctuary, and which the positive protesting declaration, the ’קדש לה of the ציץ is qualified to remove, than the פסול טומאה. All the other פסולים as חוץ למקומו, חוץ לזמנו, יוצא leave the thought of God itself untouched, and only bring disturbing ideas in the sphere of our relation to Him, which would not be dispelled by the fact proclaimed by ’קדש לה. But טימאה attacks the idea of God itself, and as it is a denial of ’קדש לה it is countered by ’קדש לה. For טומאה is a condition which, like its basic source טומאת מת, brings home to a person’s mind, a physical force to which everything living — including Man who is called upon to exercise moral freedom of will — has to submit, a blind mastering force of Nature. This force has formed at rock bottom the highest god of paganism of all times, paganism which denies the idea of a free god equally with that of a free man, and makes everything merge in the physical compulsion of blind governing necessity. But this conception is diametrically opposed to a Sanctuary whose object is to cultivate the idea of spiritually morally free man on just that idea of a completely free God. Blood, fat, kidneys or a handful of flour and oil which had been touched by the finger of טומאה and then brought on the Altar could bring with it the misleading idea, that life-endeavours and food and health are to be offered in homage to that blind physical force which is imagined to be all powerful, and to whose destructive power everything is supposed to be liable. Against this עון קדשים in its literal sense, this misdirecting sacred objects from their pure straight true meaning, comes the bright happy ’קדש לה on Aaron’s forehead, and eradicates every hint of such a dark false opinion, by claiming every sacred object of the Altar for the One free true living God ’ה, Whose creations and servants are all the physical forces and laws of Nature to whom the pagans pray in trembling fear. He, Who, just as He Himself in His almighty free power reigns above all compulsion of Nature, has breathed into Man a breath of His divine freedom, and ordained for him a life to be lived in morally free energy, serving God, and God only.

’והיה על מצחו תמיד וגו. In Yoma 7b the views of ר׳ שמעון and ’ר יהודה differ in deciding the question whether the efficacy of the ציץ in doing away with טומאה is dependent on its simply being there in existence for the forehead of the High Priest, or whether it is limited to the time when the High Priest is actually wearing it. According to ר׳ יהודה the latter is the case: עודהו על מצחו מרצה אין עודהו על מצחו אינו מרצה. This is also the view that Maimonides adopts ה׳ ביאת המקדש IV,8. ’לרצון להם לפני ה. According to the way the Gemora in Zebachim, 47a takes לרצונכם תזבחהו (Levit. 19,5) to mean לדעתכם זבוחו “as an expression of your intentions” so that רצון would not refer to obtaining the goodwill of God, but to the good intention of the bringer of the offering, and ת״כ takes ’לרצנו לפני ה (Levit. 1,3) in the same way, and also לרצונכם תמים (ibid. XXII,19), the ’והיה על מצחו תמיד לרצון להם לפני ה here, may similarly be taken to mean “the showband” shall always be on Aaron’s forehead as an expression of goodwill on their part before God” i.e., the ’קדש לה on Aaron’s forehead shall constantly express Israel’s opinion and intentions regarding the Sanctuary, that the Sanctuary is dedicated solely and only to God, and by this positive declaration do away with any possible misinterpretation.

V. 40. The gowns and girdles of the sons were exactly the same as those of Aaron. The gowns were of linen of the same “lozenge” or box pattern, and the girdles embroidered with the three colours of woollen threads on a white linen ground. (Yoma 12b). גבע ;מגבעות is related to גבה etc., from which we get also גבעה the hill; the headgear of the כה״ג was מצנפת a circular turban. Those of the כהני הדיוט were wound up to a high point. (See Maimonides הל׳ כלי המקדש VIII,2, and כ״מ thereon).
V. 41. ומלאת את ידם corresponding to the German “bevollmächtigen” “invest with full powers”.

V. 42—43. The shorts, reaching to the knee, covering the nakedness, but themselves covered by the gown, are not mentioned under the garments לכבוד ולתפארת, but are mentioned separately. They wore them not merely as priests, but as ordinary human beings, and as they fulfilled the requirements of common decency, the other garments could retain their special priestly meaning. Nevertheless they also were בגדי קדש, were supplied by the nation for service in the Sanctuary, and were, equally with the other garments, absolutely essential and indispensable for the assumption of the priestly character. More, it specially mentions here, already with the order for their being made, והיו על אהרן וגו׳, ולא ישאו עון ומתו that any עבודה performed without the priest being clothed in them would incur the death penalty (מיתה בידי שמים), whereas regarding the other garments, this is only deduced from what it says later on in Ch. 29,9, at the order to invest the priests with their garments: — ולקחת את הבגדים וגו׳, והיתה להם כהנה which the Gemora Sanhedrin 83b explains as:- בזמן שבגדיהם עליהם כהונתם עליהם, אין בגדיהם עליהם אין כהונתם עליהם i.e., unless fully clothed with the priestly garments the כהן has only the character of a זר, a non-priest. So that the עבודה of a מחוסר בגדים is חײב מיתה just as a זר is. The priestly garments of an ordinary כהן consisted accordingly of four garments viz., מגבעת, אבנט, כתנת, מכנסים. The כה״ג had eight, the four of the ordinary priest, except that he wore a מצנפת in place of מגבעת and in addition מעיל ציץ, חושן, אפוד. If any single one of these were lacking, he is called מחוסר בגדים, and any single עבודה performed by a priest in such a state is invalid, פסולה. If the עבודה is an עבודת מתנה ועבודה תמה (see above on V.35) for which a זר would be חײב מיתה then the penalty for a כהן מחוסר בגדים who is regarded as מחלל העבודה (Zebach. 18a) is likewise חיוב מיתה —. The לשרת בקדש refers to the whole of the verse, including בבאם אל אהל. For if a priest simply goes into the היכל, a ביאה ריקנית, not on behalf of an עבודה, not clad in all his priestly garments, he is not חײב מיתה (see תוספות Sanhedrin 83a and ’תוס Yoma ה׳ ב׳ ד״ה להביא Ramban also says אביאה ריקנית לא מיחײב).
THE בגדי כהונה

What significance must the priestly garments have, if, as we have just seen, they form such an essential presentation of the priestly character on which the validity of the offering depends, that, without them the priest is regarded as a זר towards the Sanctuary and, as such would fall under the dictum כל הזר הקרב יומת!

Now the very fact noted on V.2 and 3 that the priestly garments must be משל צבור, supplied and owned by the nation, gives us the clue to understand that only a כהן clad in such garments can be considered a כהן at all. Only so, does he appear as a servant of the nation for the Sanctuary of the Torah. Only so, does the ritual he performs appear as that which is due to be rendered by the nation to the Sanctuary of the Torah. Only so, do the thoughts and lessons which are to be taught by the ritual he perfoms, receive the character of being commanded in the Torah which God gave to the nation. Altogether, only so, does it become עבודת מתנה, an act of devoted obedience to the will of God, as revealed in His Torah, become שרת, satisfying the demands necessary for getting near to God, and ’קרבן לה, a getting near, and a bringing near to God. Without them the priest stands there merely as an individual. What he does, appears to be purely his own idea of what should be done, is accordingly the very reverse of that teaching which is the basic idea which the Sanctuary of the Torah is meant to foster. — Let us at once add, that without them, the individuality of the particular functioning priest stands forth in all its nakedness, and with all the weaknesses and faults to which even the best of humans are liable, and would form an ideal which is only too likely to be far far below that model which the offerings are meant to show us as being that which God’s Torah demands us to try to achieve; even as Hosea (IV,8) lashes the unworthiness of the priests in his time with the stinging words: חטאת עמי יאכלו ואל עונם ישאו נפשו “they eat the atonement offerings of My people and hold up their own sins to the soul of My people.” i.e., “they, thus (by eating the חטאת I.L.) hold up their own sinful lives as a model for My people.” In the priestly garments the priest does not appear in the character which he actually has, but in that which he should have in accordance with the demands of the Torah, it is just in clothing himself for the service of the Sanctuary in these priestly garments that he expresses to himself and to others his own real imperfection.

That clothes can express the priestly character, lies, both etymologically and actually, in the Jewish conception of “clothes”. We have already elsewhere had occasion to remark on the phonetic relation of בגד to פקד. Just as פקד denotes the mental or spiritual investment of something with its appropriate attributes, so בגד too, does not express merely a covering, but clothing which gives Man his appropriate appearance. As פקד also means investing in office, so can בגד too have a very similar meaning. Actually, too, clothing has a very significant origin in the history of Man’s moral upbringing, and because of this origin, moral importance. It was given, as an eternal reminder of his moral calling as Man, by the Father of Mankind, when He dismissed His children from Paradise out into the educational school of work and self-sacrifice with its attendant danger of animal erring. Clothing is itself a reminder of Man’s calling, and is the first and most striking appearance which characterises a being as human.

Hence we find עטה, לבש, בגד used for adopting any characteristic which serves a personality as a spiritual cloak which can be recognised by the mental eye of the observer. So even of God: “He hath clothed Himself with majesty, He hath clothed Himself with strength wherewith He hath girded Himself”, (Ps. 93,1). “Thou hast clothed Thyself in הוד and הדר (Ps. 104,1). Who covereth Thyself with Light as with a garment” (ibid. 2). “For He clothes Himself with righteousness as armour, and the helmet of salvation upon His Head, and He puts on the garments of retribution as clothing, and wrapped Himself in zeal as in a cloak” (Is. 59,17) and many other places. But so also especially of men. “For He hath clothed me with the garments of salvation and hath covered me with the robe of righteousness (Is. 61,10). “Job put on righteousness and it clothed him, his judgment was a mantle and a turban for him” (Job 29,14). “Zion shall clothe itself in its strength” (Is. 52,1). “The valiant woman is clothed in strength and worthiness” (Prov. 31,25). “The girdle of the lions of the future sprout from the stem of Jesse shall be righteousness and faithfulness (Is. 11,5). Or, “all our righteousnesses are but as filthy rags” (Is.LXIV,5). The High Priest Joshua was still clothed in unclean garments, but he was to be given clothing that would not hinder his progress (Zac. 3,3 and 4). “The enemies (of God) are to clothe themselves in shame and dishonour” (Ps. 35,26). “Who clotheth himself with cursing as if it were a close fitting garment, the curse will remain to him as a garment which encloseth him, and as a girdle wherewith he is girded continually” (Ps. 109,18 and 19). — And also particularly of priests: “The priest of God clotheth himself with righteousness”. (Ps. 132,9) “with successful help” (Chron. II. 6,41). “God clotheth the priests of Zion with salvation” (Ps. 132,16) etc. etc. etc.

After all these quotations we think we are justified in assuming that the garments which are essential for the priests to appear as priests, also have to express the character which the priest is to represent as such. That they are not to be simply external adornment, that they must mean something which is not only to affect the mind of the onlooker, but to have a meaning for the wearer himself is shown by the law שלא יהא דבר חוצץ בינם לבשרו (Zebachim 19a) that absolutely nothing may intervene between them and the body of the priest. They must be in direct contact with, and completely cover, the particular part of the body they are meant to cover, the priest must be entirely at one with his garments. The symbolic nature of the garments and of the materials out of which they are made is also shown by the injunction that the coloured wool (purple-blue תכלת) which is to be used, has to be dyed expressly and exclusively for that purpose, has to be צביעה לשמה, that טעימה פסולה and טעמה פסלה, that e.g., a thread which had been dyed to test the colour may not be used, and a thread dipped into the dye pot to test the colour makes all the dye in that pot unfit to be used (Menachoth 42b). (It is remarkable that Maimonides mentions this in הל׳ ציצית but not in הל׳ כלי המקדש).

Inasmuch as it is with these garments that the priest enters into the service of the Sanctuary, and it is the nation that hands him the garments, the clothing of the priest expresses that character, the attainment of which, the nation understands to be the task demanded by the Sanctuary of God’s Torah. It expresses the קדושה which the מקדש is to bring to the Jewish personality, which it expects from the Jewish personality. And inasmuch as the בגדי כהונה are divided into בגדי כה״ג and בגדי כהן הדיוט, but the כה״ג is the real representative of the מקדש to whom the כהן הדיוט only stand as subordinate helpers (see V.1), further, that the בגדי כה״ג also include the four of the כהן הדיוט, to which the additional four special ones which complete the high-priestly garments are only added, we must regard the בגדי כה״ג as representing the ideal Jewish qualities, the idea of ישראל as the perfect Jew, to which the בגדי כהן הדיוט represent the qualities which form the preparatory stages.

מכנסים clothe בשר ערוה from מתנים עד ירכים in white linen made of six-ply threads. They accordingly clothe in purity the whole vegetable nature of Man (nourishment and reproduction) in accordance with the idea for which it was created. Quite characteristically, it is only here, in connection with these particular garments which express moral purity in its most suggestive significance — although כתנת and מגבעות too were made from the same material — that linen is called by its botanical name of בד (in Ch. 39,28, it is actually called ואת מכנסי הבד שש). — (We have repeatedly observed that the Sanctuary is regarded quite specially from the point of view of purity when referring to food and sexual life). In Yoma 71b this name is explained as a description of the special way in which the flax grows, as it rises from the ground, דבר העולה מן הקרקע בד בד, it grows up in straight, separate, unbranched stems. The form of the plant already represents a straight undeviating effort upwards in the prescribed line to the goal aimed at. A form which is understandably intimately related to purity, the necessary fundamental conditions for which must be decisiveness, individuality and keeping away from everything impure. All the preliminary stages of טהרה which the Gemora enumerates in ע״ז 20b viz., זהירות זריזות, נקיות, פרישות, are represented by the word and the real meaning of בד. Hence also we find the linen garments of the כה״ג on י״כ depicted solely by this name (Levit. 16,4).

כתונת תשבץ clothed the upper part of the body, back, breast, arms and also the legs, over which the מכנסים did not reach. It reached from shoulder to heel, i.e., it clothed the parts representing the animal nature of Man (feeling and will and activity and movement) — (it being understood that the vegetable nature of Man, his lusts and allurements are already clothed with purity) — with the character of purity for which they were originally created. But this purity was given a special additional meaning, by the linen being תשבץ. The whole material of the gown, as already mentioned in V.4, was woven in the pattern of small box settings (in modern knitting known, I understand, as basket pattern I.L.) in small, sunken squares as if for insetting stones. Whereas purity is primarily a negative idea, keeping oneself away from all impurity and evil, and is essential everywhere as the סור מדע idea, as the first necessary stage towards moral perfection and active goodness, תשבץ implies the readiness for an entry into the higher stage of something positive. The limbs — and the powers and activities they represent — being clad in תשבץ receive thereby the mission to offer themselves as being ready to receive the call for something higher. The human powers, raised by purity above what is low and evil — and the lower inclinations and urges of Man’s “vegetable” system too, raised likewise by purity from mere animal forces into the realm of controlled moral forces — are to make themselves receptive for active service in all that is good and noble, receptive to the teaching that all these powers are to be put to positive use for good. So that the כתונת תשבץ would accordingly designate its wearer as a pupil or disciple of the Torah which the Sanctuary guards.

אבנט. It is to be regretted that the special meaning of the word, the particular kind of girdle which the word indicates, is unknown. It only occurs referring to the priestly girdle, and once again with reference to the uniform of the palace official Shebna (Is. 22,21). So we can only keep to the general meaning of a girdle. But girdle and girding are everywhere used to designate being equipped, or equipping oneself, ready for action. The usual expression אזר designates a concentration of one’s forces for some desired purpose. Inasmuch as the girdle of the כהן הדיוט also consisted of the four materials of the high-priestly garments — the two reds and the sky-blue wools stitched on a white linen ground — it thereby sets this high-priestly stage of attained perfection as the goal to be achieved by concentrating all one’s forces for it. The כהן הדיוט has not yet reached this stage, but he is girded for it. If white is the colour of purity, red the colour of life (and indeed in double nuance, of the higher and lower, the human and animal life, see Ch. 25,8) and sky-blue that of the godly element in Man, and in the combination here, the red is predominant in the proportion of 2 to 1, then these four colours, the two reds and the blue wools embroidered on the white linen of the priests’ girdles express a full human life lived fully in every direction on a pure moral base, as being the goal of all priestly endeavours. And as all the materials are made from six-ply thread, this priestly ideal is shown to be nothing superhuman, abstract or supernatural, but merely the simple natural realisation of what Man was created for and meant to be.

Then the מעיל envelopes the body, which is already arranged in the colour of purity, equipped as a disciple of purity, ready for performance of duty, envelopes it entirely in the colour of the godly element of Man. With the מעיל, the whole being of the man, after it has been cleansed from everything impure, has accepted the Word of the Teaching and prepared itself for active service, enters entirely and exclusively in the service of duty. This idea raises every phase of human life on to the same level, imparts the character of godliness to every aspect of human life, to the vegetable no less than to the animal-human, “clothes them all in the colour of heaven”. That is why the מעיל encloses the throat i.e., the combination of the animal and vegetable organs (ושט and קנה oesophagus and trachea) with a strong, inwoven, continuous closed seam and from there flows over the body down to the heel.

At the lower hem, turned towards the ground were “pomegranates” made out of תכלת ארגמן ותולעת שני. This was the only place where these three materials occur without the fourth, שש. According to the well-known saying מלאין מצות כרמון (Eruvin 19a) on account of the numerous seed pips which entirely fill their interiors, they are the symbol of fruitful seed. Taking into account that here, the more negative white colour is lacking, and that they consist only of the positive animal two red and one blue colours and materials we can take the pomegranates to represent: — Rich fruitful seed of a life allied to God. Their being placed at the hem of the מעיל facing downwards gives this the further nuance: It is not heaven, it is here below, the earth which is to receive the benefit of the fruits of having consecrated one’s life to God. The service of God, to which the whole of one’s life is to be given up, accepting all the teaching which the Sanctuary preaches, is to strew an abundance of rich fruitful seeds for one’s earthly life here below.

In addition to the pomegranates there were bells on the hem of the מעיל, and of them it says ונשמע קולו בבאו אל הקדש לפני ה׳ ובצאתו ולא ימות which definitely gives the purpose of these פעמנים, he shall be “heard” when he goes into the Sanctuary and when he goes out, ולא ימות. The simple context as well as the addition ובצאתו speaks for adopting the opinion of the רמב״ן, that this ולא ימות refers to the ונשמע קולו and not to והיה על אהרן לשרת (as Rashi takes it I.L.) as being מחוסר בגדים, the מיתה for which is mentioned elsewhere. See on XLII,43. But it is difficult to take this ונשמע קולו as an announcement of his coming which would be a “breach of good manners” if “unannounced”, we prefer to refer this “being heard” to his colleagues and to the community, as whose representative, and in whose name, he approaches before God, and we think this also explains the addition of ולא ימות to ונשמע קולו. Not as an individual and not for himself, but as representative of the community and on their behalf, and so that his coming before God should be noted and taken to heart by the community, must he step before God. Without the expression of this idea and this intention, his entering would be, just like מחוסר בגדים, a זר-like presumption and arrogance. Hence the ובצאתו is also understandable. The going-out from the Sanctuary is not only as important as the entry, it is even more important. If, and how, you stood before God is to be seen, not on how you went in, but on how you come out of the Sanctuary. Perhaps that is also why Ezekiel (XLIII,11) when he is to hold up the picture of the Sanctuary to the people as the ideal before which they are to be ashamed of themselves, puts מוצאיו their goings-out before מובאיו their goings-in.

Of the מעיל it quite specially says והיה על אהרן לשרת that Aaron is to wear it as an expression of “service”. For the מעיל clothes everything earthly in the colour of the heavenly i.e., the arranging of all earthly-human matters in a way that is approved by God, so that God likes to come into the proximity of human beings in accordance with the terms of the “Bris”, and this is the essential idea of שרת. See on V.35.

אפוד and חשן, white, the two reds, blue and gold. The High Priest, — the whole of his self already dedicated to the service of devoted duty — is now further girded for the highest degree of human perfection by the אפוד and חשן (see on V.4). The higher side of the human being — the אפוד only enclosed the upper part of the body — feelings (the back), will (the breast), action (shoulder joint), and power (loins) are energetically joined together for devotion to the Jewish ideal of humanity, so that by combining the four materials woven together with gold, it comes to express that which אורים and תומים mean.

The אבנט, the girdle of the preliminary stage was מעשה רקם. One material, we assume it to be the linen, formed the foundation, and on it the other positive coloured materials were embroidered. The girdle of the אפוד, the stage of perfection, was מעשה חשב the threads were all incorporated into one whole pattern, all of equal importance, except, perhaps that the idea of life was brought into the foreground by the relative preponderance of the colour red. Further, each of the four materials did not consist of six-ply threads — six, being the number symbolic of the material, the created — but to each of the materials was added a thread of gold — the material symbolic of solid unaltering nobility — thus raising the now seven-ply material into the symbolic meaning of the number seven, the number of completion, perfection, the joining of the visible created six, to the One invisible Creator. So that here all the four phases of human nature, by means of the highest moral nobility, join together in equal value to the most perfect complete life, the heart of which is formed by the אורים and תומים.

Exactly what the אורים and תומים were is an unapproachable secret, but the words themselves indicate an “enlightenment” and “moral perfection” And אור in the form of אור in which it includes the warming, or even the overpowering consuming force of fire. תומים is the plural form of תום perfection, completeness. The plural form of אורים ותומים indicates a plurality of objects which possess the innate quality of, or the efficacy for, the clarifying animating enlightenment of the mind, and moral perfection. What is actually known to us, is only the Word of God, the תורות and מצות which, as they originate from the fountain-head of the highest absolute knowledge, and the highest and most absolute perfection, have the ability to exercise the highest intellectual and spiritual and moral influence on us. The תורה preserved in the ארון הברית becomes אורים and תומים in the breast of Jews and of the Jewish nation. Their representative, the כה״ג carries them as a treasure to be guarded (בחשן see on V.4) “on his heart” and the knowledge and instruction obtained from the Word of God, forms the משפט .משפט בני ישראל in the stat. constr. as משפט אלקי הארץ ,משפט הכהנים משפט הנער, משפט המלך or used with pron. poss. as משפטי ודיני etc., always means “that which belongs by right to somebody, that which is in accordance with his rights and calling.” משפט בני ישראל would accordingly be:- What is befitting and right for Israel, what is in accordance with its calling, what it is to expect, and what it is to endeavour to accomplish in accordance with its calling. Inasmuch as this משפט בני ישראל is to be ascertained only by the אורים ותומים this implies that the aims and desires of Israel are only to be formed under the influence of the אורים ותומים, that Israel is not to desire or strive for anything that is not in accordance with that, which, as ascertained from the Word of God, is really “true” (אור I.L.) and “good” (תום I.L.). So that the words ונשא אהרן את משפט בני ישראל על לבו לפני ה׳ תמיד really mean that Aaron is to bear Israel’s concerns, Israel’s desires and endeavours, continually on his heart before God, corresponding to ויהיו דברי אלה אשר התחננתי לפני ה׳ קרובים אל ה׳ אלהינו יומם ולילה לעשות משפט עבדו ומשפט עמו ישראל דבר יום ביומו (Kings I. 8,59).

But on his shoulder and breast the High Priest bears the names of the tribes of Israel לוכרון לפני ה׳. Thereby the כה״ג appears as the personification of the nation of Israel. It is the power of activity, the understanding and knowledge and the will of the nation which is to be represented in the כה״ג symbolically as having attained its ideal state. And the ,אפוד וחשן ,חשו ואפוד the active forces of the nation and the understanding and will of the nation awakened and governed by the אורים ותומים are never to be separated from each other. אורים ותומים are to be translated into active deeds, and the deeds and actions are to be directed solely by the אורים ותומים. The will of the nation is to be identical with the will of God. משפט בני ישראל and the משפט אורים ותומים are to be one. And it is the golden chains of the noblest spiritual force, that bind the active power of the nation for ever to the חשן משפט; and it is a פתיל תכלת the strong thread of godlike faithful duty to the Bris, that binds the collected energy (חשב) of the whole moral spiritual nature of the human being for ever to the אורים ותומים of the חשן משפט.

If we picture to ourselves the progressive stages of moral perfection which the בגדי כהונה represent, there seem to be three: מכנסים וכתונת, purity regarding moral and social wrong, corresponding to the idea צדק, right, justice, which in reality, at the root, is but a negative idea; (b) מעיל, the whole of the human being giving itself up to the dictates of doing right, corresponding to the positive idea, צדקה; and (c) אפוד the devoting of all one’s powers and all one’s forces to achieve the godly ideal of חסד (love I.L.). These would correspond to the three verses: כהניך ילבשו צדק (Psalms 132,9), מעיל צדקה יעטני, (Is. 61,10), תומיך ואוריך לאיש חסידך (Deut. 33,8).

מצנפת ,מגבעות. Expressions such as צניף מלוכה בכף אלהיד (Is. 62,3), הסיר המצנפת והרים העטרה (Ezek. 21,31) show us that מצנפת is to be regarded as a specific mark of “distinction, worthiness” similar to a crown. A band or coil etc., wound round the head, marks the wearer out from all others. For the priest it was made of white linen, reminding him that keeping pure from everything base and impure must be his very fundamental sine qua non! The turban of the כה״ג was flat and round, in it the dignity of the priest reached its conclusion. The headgear of the כהני הדיוט were מגבעות, rising upwards to a point. Their dignity was indicated as the preliminary stage, which has still to strive upwards.

The מצנפת of the כה״ג by a cord of תכלת, by the thread of godlike devotion to the Bris — bore, on a gold base — on the purest, noblest, most unalterable foundation — as a constant reminder to his own mind and to the minds of all others (Yoma 8a) the words קדש לה׳, which proclaimed the whole of the Sanctuary and its contents as dedicated to God, in the complete exclusiveness which these two words imply (see note on V.36 and 38).

If we contrast in our minds the picture of a כהן הדיוט in his בגדי לבן and a כה״ג in his בגדי זהב, the כהן הדיוט appears in the preliminary stage of the חצר which also bears the ground colour of purity, whereas the כה״ג is clothed in the materials and colours of the קדש and the קדש הקדשים.

Further, the בגדי כהונה stand in close relationship to the קרבנות. The giving up of the אימורים, the חלב, כליות and יותרת הכבד to the אש דת of the Altar, is exactly the same as the clothing of the בשר ערוה from מתנים עד ירכים with מכנסים, and the positive act of covering these parts with the כתונת and מעיל is nothing but the purification and consecration of the sensuous vegetable side of human nature by investing it with the character of purity and devotion to the Bris, exactly as the offering of the איברים in quite a similar sense corresponds to clothing them with כתונת and מעיל. Every כהן clothed in the Sanctuary-garments given to him by the nation, is a call to the nation and to every member of the nation to make every sacrifice to invest himself with that character which just the priestly garments make it apparent that the national Sanctuary of the Torah demands of the nation itself (i.e., that the Sanctuary demands this character for the nation rather than exclusively for the priests).

We find such a close relationship between the בגדי כהונה and the קרבנות indicated already in the Gemora in Zebachim 88b and Erachin 16a: — למה נסמכה פרשת קרבנות לפרשת בגדי בהונה לומר לך מה קרבנות מכפרין אף בגדי כהונה מכפרין, כתונת מכפרת על שפיכות דם שנ׳ וגר׳, מכנסים מכפרים על גלוי עריות שנ׳ וגר׳, מצנפת מכפרת על גסי הרוח מניין וגר׳, אבנט מכפר על הרהור הלב היכא דאיתיה, השן מכפר על הדינין שנ׳ וגר׳, אפוד מכפר על ע״א שנ׳ וגר׳, מעיל מכפר על לשון הרע מניין וגר׳ וציץ מכפר על עזות פנים, בציץ כתיב וגר׳.

These sentences indeed afford in general a complete confirmation of the way we take priestly garments to have a symbolic meaning. They show that our sages too, understood them to be in very essential and intimate relationship to moral human character and to the moral mission of human life. A closer consideration shows that the special relation of atonement associated with each individual garment to special definite transgressions and sins which are enumerated here, are in quite harmonious agreement with the meaning we have taken these garments to have. This agreement seems to us in the large majority of the sentences to be quite obvious. Only we must first realise a special aspect of the idea כפרה in the תורה. This is especially necessary here, as one could here so easily fall into the misunderstanding of thinking that כפרה can be obtained without the slightest cooperating or even consciousness on the part of the penitent. The Torah recognises two cases where כפרה is necessary. One where somebody has been guilty of a transgression of the Torah. The other refers to the Torah-Sanctuary and its constituents. For, every sin that remains unpunished produces a danger that the ideal of a perfect life which the Torah-Sanctuary holds out to us, becomes tarnished and lowered. The concrete actual life of the people, with all their faults, in whose midst the Torah-Sanctuary stands, is considered as being approved of by this Torah-Sanctuary, and as sufficiently satisfying its demands as long as the sin committed has been brought home to the consciousness of the perpetrator by punishment, or so long as actual disapproval or disagreement with the ideals of the Torah-Sanctuary has not been expressed in any way. So, the עבדת י״כ drove home the contrast between the ideal of the Torah-Sanctuary and the concrete actuality of the life of the people. That served to protect the ideals of the Torah-Sanctuary from becoming gradually and consistently lowered by the sins of the people. This is what is meant by: וכפר על הקדש מטמאת בני ישראל ומפשעיהם לכל חטאותם. It also served at the same time thereby to avoid the necessity for a retributive punishment having to be inflicted on the nation itself as is expressed in the sentence which combines both the aspects of כפרה viz: וכפר את מקדש הקדש ואת אהל מועד ואת המזבח יכפר ועל הכהנים ועל כל עם הקהל יכפר (Levit. 16,33).

Similarly here. By the fact that the moral demands which the nation acknowledges as being the dictates of the Sanctuary being positively expressed by the garments which the priests wear in the name of the nation, sins against these moral demands can lose the danger of their becoming a threat to the integrity of the national ideals, and, to a certain extent, these sins can remain free, both from being recognised by the law-courts and from the punishing Hand of God. By the positive expression by the national Sanctuary of the demands of the laws of morality which the בגדי כהנה give, any semblance of the nation or the Sanctuary countenancing moral sins is done away with, and, in this way, the בגדי כהונה like the offerings, achieve מכנסים .כפרה put moral purity as the first postulate for the whole of our “vegetable” our sexual and feeding life, and so express the national disapproval of any and every sexual transgression. Hence they are מכפר על ג״ע as far as these escape the attentions of the law-courts. Similarly כתונת, investing the upper part of the body and the arms and feet, i.e., our activities, with the character of guiltless purity obeying the Law, express likewise the national disapproval of any and every social transgression, i.e., שפיכת דמים in its widest sense. אבנט demands the gathering together of all one’s forces for a full active life of doing good, a condition which leaves no room for sinful thoughts (see above XXVII,8) and so is מכפר על הרהורי הלב. The מצנפת warns even the highest and most honoured in the nation of the necessity for constant watch and attention to keep himself free from everything impure or ignoble, and so makes the banishing of all conceit and over-estimation of oneself the basic stipulation for the honour he enjoys, and so is מכפר על גסי הרוח. The השן subjugates all משפט :ני ישראל to the אורים and תומים “full-of-light-and-perfection-utterances” of God’s will, and so does away with any semblance of any judicial departure from the Law of the Torah occurring under the intentional sanction of the nation, and so is מכפר על הדינין.
More difficult to understand, are the sentences referring to the מעיל אפוד and ציץ.

It says “אפוד מכפר על ע״ז״. Perhaps the following consideration may come somewhere near the truth. In the story of the פסל מיכה (Judges XVII and XVIII) an אפוד is mentioned in quite definite and prominent connection with תרפים פסל ומסכה i.e., with ע״ז. Equally so, in Judges 8,27, it seems to stand in a similar connection, or, at least, after the death of Gideon to have been placed in such a connection (see Jerushalmi Avoda Zara 3,6). The shape of an אפוד, as well as the word itself, represents, as we have seen (see above) a being, pulling himself together to place his receptivity, his will and his actions in the service of, to carry out the purposes of, some other being. Such an אפוד by itself, without any visible body to wear it could express the intention or the illusion of making some invisible being, some invisible force, of service to our purposes. We presume that this was the idea and the intention when an אפוד was used in idol worship. Idol worship always had the idea that by its cults it could sway powers that by their nature were inimical to human welfare, over to their favour; more, by the art of magic and oracle it could cast a spell on such powers and force them to do their will. Then an אפוד would have been a means to persuade or force the gods to action, in the same way as תרפים were to persuade or force the gods to speech. Then we could understand the combination, the placing together of אפוד ותרפים. Judaism teaches the very opposite of all this, the Jew does not try to make his God serve his purposes, but to make himself serve God’s purposes, and inasmuch as the Jewish High Priest instead of preparing an אפוד for the cult of the gods, puts it on himself, he thereby expresses the most definite protest against heathenism, and we can understand the sentence אפוד מכפר על ע״ז.

More obscure is the sentence מעיל מכפר על לשון הרע. National disapproval is to keep scandal-mongering away, to restrain that disposition which is so common, diligently to show up the moral nakedness of one’s neighbours. So that the meaning of the מעיל must in some way postulate the opposite disposition, that ascribes some good to even those who are most deficient in morals, and accordingly considers even them as being not entirely without some moral value in the sum total of the nation, and also has hopes for their possible betterment and ultimate ennoblement. Actually the מעיל does present such an aspect by its characteristic רמונים and פעמונים. Multifold as life itself are the lessons and tasks of the Torah, and accordingly it requires all sorts and conditions of men for its realisation. Hence the most different kinds of men according to their natures find different spheres of activity to justify their moral calling, weaknesses and virtues compensate each other in the individual and supplement each other in the mass — one thinks of the saying of our sages that אפי׳ ריקנים שבך מלאין מצות כרמון — so that they can all be considered as an integral part of the Holy Nation, and the call of the פעמונים can invite them all to take part in the sanctification when the High Priest clad in the “mantle of duty” enters the Sanctuary. According to these thoughts, it may not seem so far fetched to say that מעיל מכפר על לשון הרע.

Finally, ציץ מכפר על עזי פנים. This sentence seems to us the most obscure of all and the connection remains vague. Nevertheless we would remark: - All the special traits of character which are to find כפרה through the בגדי כהונה which have hitherto been mentioned are quite definitely moral faults. But עזות (obstinacy, inflexibility. I.L.) is, in itself, by no means so, in itself it is quite neutral. Inflexibility, stubbornness is an essential characteristic for the highest degree of moral perfection, and it can lead equally easily to moral debasement. We find an עזות לה׳ and an עזות לעזאזל as is represented by the שני שעירי יום הכפורים. Armed with the noblest, most resistant of metals, the forehead of the High Priest has to bear the truth קדש לה׳ as a protest against every misconception or lie that would disturb the purity of the Sanctuary. This gives to stubbornness, obstinacy, inflexibility — the firmness of character which keeps itself in opposition to lies, delusions, and false opinions — the consecration of the noblest purpose. Could not this be taken as meaning the repulse of the ignoble abuse of עזות — as a כפרה for the very existence of עזות?

V. 1. וזה הדבר. As, in accordance with its basic meaning, — connecting single parts to form a whole, — דבר means idea, word, speech, so it also means, as here, a single procedure which consists of several separate individual procedures all belonging together.

לקדש .לכהן — לקדש: to prepare them for a profession; this always contains the idea of a separation from what has gone before and from things which are foreign to the profession. It always has the negative idea in the foreground. לכהן expresses in full the whole positive idea of the new profession. — פר אחד בן בקר. From ת״כ on Levit. 4,3, we learn that the addition בן בקד designates the youth of the animal. It is already to have reached the stage of being a פר but to be still youthful; though mature, still with the remembrance of its youth fresh in its mind. In the first and second years of its life it is called an עגל, with the entry of the third year it becomes a פר and throughout this third year it is called a פר בן בקר (see on Levit. 4,3, and IX,2, and Rosh Hashana 10a). איל is a sheep after thirty days in its second year. On the thirtieth day it is called a פלגם the half-way point, where it has lost the character of a כבש and not yet attained that of an איל. The two rams have different designations, the one is designed to become an עולה, the other a שלמים. So that Aaron and his sons are not treated separately but are represented together by the one single animal, together as a פר and together as an איל. From this we can deduce that each of these sacrificial animals represent Aaron and his sons, not as individuals but as a class, not the priests themselves, but the priesthood, not a כהן but the כהונה. The priesthood is here shown in its twofold aspect: (a) in its activity in the service of God, in its office, it is represented by a פד, it is a co-worker in working the “field of God” God’s acre. God’s acre is not (as in old English and German. I.L.) the graveyard, the place of death, but the field of life. So the prophet can say לא נביא אנכי איש עבד אדמה אנכי כי אדם הקנני מנעורי (Zacc. 13,5) “Not a prophet am I, a worker of the human world am I, for He has given me to humanity from my youth”; (b) as leading, directing the community in its privileged position, in its post of honour, it is represented by an איל, it, (the priesthood I.L.) in its power, strength and influence is the bell-wether that leads God’s flock. (See note on Gen. 15,9). For his future office the כהן, as a פר בן בקר has first of all in a חטאת to promise that he will assiduously at all times keep himself firmly at the height of his calling and guard himself against lapses through carelessness (see note on Ch. 27,8). The dignity, the honour of the post, as represented by an איל has to be brought home to him in two aspects: — (1) In its influence on the people, as a leader. In this respect he has to vow in an עולה, setting the example as an איל, always to strive upwards to ever greater perfection, and as a model, to show the way for the realisation of everything that is godly on earth (see ibid.). (2) In the privileges and advantages which are granted for this influence. He is to enjoy these privileges. As an איל in שלמים he is to come to the enjoyment of his own self, but only under the conditions which all שלמים teach, and which are specifically prominent at this שלמים, being the איל מלואים and which we shall go into detail below. For the present we only remark that:- the פר החטאת has the office in mind, the איל העולה, the honour, with reference to its influence, and the איל מלואים the honour, with reference to its privileges and advantages.

V. 2. From the Mishna (Menachoth 78a) we learn that המילואים היו באין כמצה שבתודה חלות רקיקין ורבוכה, that the different kinds of bread mentioned here are the same as the three kinds of unleavened bread prescribed for the thank-offering in Levit. 7,12. These are: חלות, רבוכה and .רקיקין רבוכה here called לחם מצות, further on in V.23, and in Levit 8,26, called חלת לחם שמן was a kind of fancy bread. After it had been kneaded with oil, it was treated to all the three kinds of cooking, first boiled (חליטה) then baked (אפיה) in the oven, and finally toasted (טיגון). It also received double the quantity of oil that either of the other two kinds had: רביעית לוג לרבוכה ,שמינית לחלות שמינית לרקיקין. So that its preparation made it richer and was more complicated. It was the same as the daily חביתי כהן גדול (Levit. 6,13 and 14) The בלולת בשמן of our verse accordingly refers also to the חלות מצות בלולת בשמן .ולחם מצות, called ככר לחם in V.23, were simpler both in preparation and in the oil content. They were kneaded with half the quantity of oil and simply baked in the oven. More simple still were the רקיקין. They were ordinary thin Mattzoth which after baking were besmeared with oil. All three were מצה, unleavened, they all bore the stamp of dependence, they were the bread of service, dependent on God, and granted by Him in His service (see on Ch. 12,18). But just as in the case of תודה, brought to express thanks to God for some special deliverance and happiness, to the קרבן representing the personality who has been saved and made happy, oil-mattzoth too have to be added, representing the material welfare, the food and comfort as the factor in which the deliverance and happiness is mostly manifested, or at least which is essentially necessary for the continuance of the happiness-bringing condition: so here, to the איל מלואים expressing the privileges and advantages connected with the honour of the priesthood, the factor of material food and comfort has also to be added, in which these advantages find their most concrete realisation. After all, with regard to his existence the priest is thrown entirely on the income connected with his office. Does not God say to Aaron: “Thou shalt have no inheritance in the land of the nation, neither shalt thou have any portion in their midst. I am thy portion and thine inheritance amongst the Children of Israel?” (Numbers 18,20). But their claim to this income was by no means a direct one. Apart from the parts of the offerings which had to be given to the officiating priest, no priest had any fixed income. The bounties which the people and the Levites had to render to the priests could be given to any priest they liked, these bounties were, in part, as תרומה and חלה of a purely symbolic nature, and מדאורייתא could be discharged with a minimum (one single ear of corn as a token was all that was actually required from the whole stack. I.L.). So that the existence, to say nothing of the comfort or well-being of the priest, was completely dependent on the goodwill of the people, and depended on the degree of impressive teaching which the Word of God obtained through the personality of the priest, and altogether on the extent to which this teaching was recognised and treasured by the people. We can understand, therefore, how the participation in earthly goods which was connected with the honour of priesthood could be expressed in various degrees of wealth, רקיקין, חלות, לחם שמן. We think that just these three different kinds of mattzoth — from the rich fancy mattzoth to the simple plain mattzo just daubed with oil — were to bring home to the tribe of Aaron, when being initiated into the office and honour of priesthood, the solemn warning not to abuse the rights associated with the honours of their office as means for any form of voluptuousness. But they were to feel themselves being made quite as happy in being an איל, with the רקיק מעה משוח בשמן as with the rich לחם שמן; and with this latter equally as מצה, as being in the service of God, and subordinote to His will, as with the simple plain bread which just sustains one’s life and strength; altogether in his whole civil life, in whatever state he lives it, never to lose the מצה idea and the מצה spirit.

V. 3. על סל. This expression makes us presume that it was not a basket with any depth, in which, but a flat surface, on which, the bread was laid. The idea of סל from the root סלל to lift upwards, does not necessarily imply any depth as being essential, and can equally well designate a tray on which anything is carried.

V. 4. רחץ במים .ורחצת אותם במים without mention of any special part of the body as a rule means, to bathe. It is the complete immersion of the whole body in water, i.e., טבילה in the full measure of water which corresponds to the normal measure of the human body אמה על אמה ברום ג׳ אמות i.e., 24 cu. ft. This water must not be contained in a vessel, but must still be in its primitive state, for instance, gathered in a natural hollow in the ground. Being under water was the original condition of the world. Also, water, in contrast to the dry land, is that part of the world on which human domain did not establish its realm. So, finally, the world of water is that sphere where no טומאה reaches. No dead sea-animal is a source of טומאה and no vessel made out of its material is מקבל טומאה (Kelim 17,13). Only as אוכלין are fish מ״ט. So that immersion in the element of water, טבילה, expresses a complete departure from the realm of humanity subject to טומאה, and a return to original conditions, completely breaks off connection with the past and introduces a quite fresh pure future. ורחצת, Moses, the highest representative of the nation, by this טבילה, raises those to be consecrated as priests, out of their previous associations, and then the further clothing with the garments etc. was performed by Moses in a similar sense. For it is the nation that consecrates and dedicates the Jewish priests (see Ch. 1 et seq.).

V. 5. מכנסים are not mentioned. See Ch. 26,42. Also not in Levit. 8,7, where the actual carrying out of this consecrating induction is described. Moses also probably rendered no assistance in putting them on. The אבנט is not mentioned here specially with reference to Aaron. But it is left for V.9, where it is mentioned for Aaron together with his sons. See note on that verse.

V. 6. The ציץ is repeatedly called נזר .נזר הקדש crown (from נזר to separate, from which we get the stronger form נצר to guard against everything that is alien and harmful) expresses the singling-out and separating-off that which is encompassed by the circlet. The ציץ itself is only a half-circlet, which is held round the head by the thread of תכלת. But the inscription which this half-circlet bears makes it into a veritable נזר, inasmuch as it rejects with firm unalterable (pure gold) decision everything that would dim the sanctity of the Sanctuary (See 28,36).

V. 7. משה .המשחה to draw out of the water; משח, to besmear with oil, the material that will not mix with water, to anoint, the general symbol of separating from, rejecting anything low or vulgar. The person or thing that is anointed is henceforth not to mix with that which is low or vulgar. We learn from Kerithoth 5b that the anointing of the High Priest was in the form of כי יונית, of the Greek “chi”. The sentence in Kelim 20,7 מחצלת שעשה לה קנים לארכה טהורה, וחכמים אומרים עד שיעשה כמין כי implies that the figure that Rashi gives in Kerithoth is not the right one, but that in fact it was two intersecting lines, quite in the familiar form of the Greek letter X. It seems accordingly to have been meant to indicate that the effect of the anointing was to be extended in every direction. The daubing of the mattzoth with oil in V.2 was also done in this form.

V. 9. According to Levit. 8,7 and 13 Aaron had the girdle put on at the same time as he was clothed in the other garments, so that he was first completely clothed with all the garments and only then was the clothing of the sons proceeded with. If, nevertheless here the girding of Aaron is mentioned together with that of his sons, it is to substantiate the significant fact — recorded in Yoma 6a, and accepted as Halacha — אבנט של כה״ג זהו אבנטו של כהן הדיוט, that regarding girdles, the כה״ג and the כהן הדיוט stood on the same ground. The כהן הדיוט too, was girdled with the high-priestly positive material and colours (his girdle was not like the rest of his garments made out of simple white linen), and — let us add — the girdle of the High Priest was only מעשה רוקם and not מעשה אורג. Such girdles preach to High Priest and ordinary priest alike that the highest goal in life is to devote all one’s energies to strive for spiritual perfection on a foundation of moral purity, and moreover, to both alike, that this goal is still a goal, something for which they still have to work with the utmost exertion of all their strength. See note above on אבנט. There already we noted the parallel case of the same kind of curtains to the door of the משכן and the gate of the תצר, and also thought of the relationship of the כהן הדיוט to the חצר and the כה״ג to the משכן. It is also significant that here the girdle is put together with the מגבעות of the כהני הדיוט. See note above on והיתה להם כהנה — .מגבעות. This joins the character of being a כהן to being clad in the garments. (See note on Ch. 28,42 and 43) — להקת עולם. We have already worked out (on Gen. 47,22) how the root חקק has the basic idea of that which is due to, in accordance with the nature of, or the rights of, a person or thing. We found that even the idea חק as a law or statute is far away from the idea of an arbitrary dogma without a reason. On the contrary, that which is called a חק is in accordance with the deep true nature and the real calling of that to which it applies. Here and in many similar cases חקה means the rights granted to a position or personality on account of its nature and its purpose. By means of this first investment of Aaron and his sons in the garments in the name of the nation, they and their descendants are granted the right to be invested with the office and the dignity and honour of the כהונה by being clad in similar garments.

ומלאת יד, and by this investiture the representative of the nation grants them the “full power” (power of attorney, authorising somebody to act in his stead. I.L.) to perform all the tasks that have to be done by means of a כהן.

V. 10. סמיכה .וסמך is no simple laying-on of hands, but is an act of supporting with all one’s strength. By this act, the identification of the person with the offering is expressed. Aaron and his sons are to realise that they stand before the Sanctuary as a פר. Those who have just been invested with the priesthood have now to learn the conditions and the demands which this office and this honour impose upon them. First, the office: they are to regard themselves as פר, as serving co-workers with God in His great Work, and moreover, not as פרים but as פר, not as so many individuals, but as one unit of which each member must work together with the others to accomplish the one common mission. They are still standing before the Sanctuary (לפני אהל מועד I.L.). To go into the Sanctuary, certain conditions have first to be fulfilled:-

V. 11. ושחטת. The first is שחיטה. He who would be a פר, must give up living for himself. “To give oneself up before God, in front of the opened doors of the Sanctuary” is the first demand of every קרבן. The demand is doubly powerful for one who is called upon to be a פר.

V. 12. But this giving up of one’s life is no passive abrogation. To a new life, “a life belonging to the Sanctuary” (the blood representing the life, the whole personality, has to be received in a vessel which is an integral part of the Mikdosh. I.L.) the “sacrificed being” arises, and receives the direction from “the finger of the Sanctuary” to keep itself at all times on “the heights of earthly life striving upwards to God” (the קרנת המזבח I.L.) and for such an ideal to let his whole life his whole self (ואת כל דם I.L.) “have its roots in” the base of the Sanctuary of the Torah (יסד I.L.), on which base alone, the elevation of the earth to God is possible.

V. 13. The most direct result of this “surrender of the blood” is to be, the giving of all the “riches” (חלב) which the vegetable, sensual nature of Man endeavours to obtain, of the “liver” (יותרת על הכבד) which sets Man’s activities in life in motion for these endeavours, and of the sensual longing themselves (שתי הכליות) which are at the root of all this, to be fuel to keep alive on earth the fire of God’s Torah. It is the changing of the lower animal side of Man’s nature into free moral, godly deeds. המזבחה: We think that this form (to, not on, almost always used when referring to הקטרה) refers to the law מד דם בזריקה אף בשר בזריקה (Zebachim 62b) that the parts of the sacrifices which were to be burnt on the Altar were not laid down on the Altar, but like the blood of the עולה, had to be thrown there (to express the necessity of using all one’s energy. I.L.). It was for this purpose too, that a small space was left between the כבש and the מזבח (a לול קטן the Gemora calls it). We presume that, in this respect, the אימורים were the same as the איברים.

V. 14. חטאת הוא. We believe that חטאת is formed from the Piel meaning of the root חטא, and so, need not necessarily, as a “sin-offering”, presume a sin committed, but as “freeing from sin” is to bring about the resolution to keep free from sin in the future. It is, after all, primarily, this resolution too, which obtains absolution from sins actually committed. Here it says חטאת הוא to give the reason for burning the פר outside the camp. If it had the character of a שלמים as the איל מלואים had, then, after the whole of the life and the sensual nature of the bringer had received its lesson of dedication for higher purposes, in דם and אימורים, the meat etc. came back to the personality represented in the offering, the בעלים, to be eaten and enjoyed by his own self. But in the חטאת, the eating of the meat of the sacrificial animal is itself part of the symbolic עבודה to achieve כפרה. The personality represented in the offering has still to be taught that it is not only the נפש and כליות, but also the whole of the corporeality which is at the service of the נפש and כליות which must be used for the benefit of the ideals of the Sanctuary of the Torah which are represented by the כהן. Even where a כהן brings his own חטאת he has to eat it not as the בעלים but as the כהן. It has to be eaten within the confines of the Sanctuary, in the עזרה (according to מל״מ מעשה הקרבנות X,3, it even has to be just opposite the entrance to the מקדש like שחיטת קדשים, but the סמי מכאן אכילה in Zebachim 56a seems to be against this opinion), has to be eaten in the priestly garments (Yoma 68a), and perhaps may even only be eaten standing (מל״מ ibid.). But here, there was no כהן yet in existence, they had still to become כהנים and hence the whole פר — in the same way as, for similar reasons, the פרים ושעירים הנשרפין — was to be burnt outside the camp, to show that there was nobody within the nation, or in this case nobody yet, who was fit for the symbolic teaching which the eating of the חטאת by the כהן preached.

V. 15. Then they were to realise their future position regarding its privileges and honours, and represent themselves in the character of the איל. In the first place, regarding the influence which, as such, was expected from them, being placed “at the head of God’s flock” to enlighten and direct the people on to the path they are to tread.

V. 16. Here, too, self-sacrifice, stripping oneself of every thought of living for oneself, is again the first condition, but after that, in this case of the leading and guiding איל, the doubly necessary consciousness of being still far away from the height — yea even from the bottom of the ascent — to which Jewish Perfection beckons. That which represented the personality of the one who is destined to be leading איל, — having been accepted and adopted by the Sanctuary (קבלה I.L.) — is first given its standing far away from the Altar, and from there is first “thrown” with full energy towards the “lower” part of the “Mount of God”, ב׳ מתנות שהן :סביב ארבע בקרן מזרחית צפונית ומערבית דרומית onto these lower preparatory stages of the whole mission of Israel. These two corners together represent the combination of the two energies demanded. The E.N. corner: to sanctify all the material sensual factors of life by directing them to the purposes indicated to them by the life lived in accordance with God’s Torah. The W.S. corner: to achieve mental clarity and spiritual illumination from the realisation of God’s Torah (see notes on the מזבח Ch. XXVII) i.e., they are to exercise the influence which their leading position gives them, being a pattern and example of untiring efforts towards practical and theoretical perfection.

V. 17. But these efforts are not to remain simply internal or one-sided. With the whole of his “thinking” and “active” life (ראש and נתחים), even with his activities in eating and procuring his food (קרבו וכרעיו), has the כהן to be an “איל״, to lead the way. His whole personality is laid before him in every member of his organism (לנתחיו in the natural division of the body. Chulin 11a).

V. 18. And it is the “whole” איל-personality which is to be given over with full energy to the “fire of the Torah which, with lion’s power, demands its ‘food’ on the summit of the Mount of God” (see Ch. XXVII, ibid.), עולה הוא לה׳ the whole איל becomes an offering “rising upwards to God”, and making the whole of one’s material self sublimated to the godly, — both meanings lie in עלה. See note on Gen. 22,2 — ריח ניחוח see on Gen. 8,21. אשה לה׳ הוא. The whole איל is a surrender to the “fire of the Torah” (אש דת I.L.) and thereby a surrender to God. The only way of actual surrender to God is surrender to His Torah. God recognises no other surrender than devotion to His revealed will.
V. 19. Once again, those who are to become כהנים are to regard themselves in their איל-dignity, but now from the point of view of the enjoyment they are to derive from their high position.

V. 20. Again it is giving oneself up, giving up living just for oneself which is the first condition (שחיטה I.L.). But before this striving up to the heights of the Altar is expressed by the “throwing of the blood” as with the עולה (V.16), some of the blood, which has been accepted by the Sanctuary (קבלה I.L.) is to be placed on the car, hand and foot of the priests, who are to be made conscious of the dignity and honour to be bestowed on them. The ear through which they hear and understand, the hand by which they achieve, the foot by which they go where they wish i.e., their understanding, their actions and steps, by which, above all, a personality invested with the honour of being an איל, leading the community, has to prove itself, must all be identified with the דם שחוט ומקובל. Like the blood given up as profane, and accepted as holy, died as profane and revived as holy, they too must be given up and accepted, must die and revive. The איל offering must not remain a mere external solemnization, the symbolic סמיכה-identification must become concrete and real in the actual rebirth of the actual ear, the actual hand and the actual foot. The נפש (represented by the blood. I.L.), the personality, of the priest-to-be must actually begin its devotion and surrender by this giving-itself-up to the Altar if this personality really has within itself the true dignity of its position, and if it is consciously to enjoy the privileges connected with this dignity. — כהן (see Gen. 14,18). — תנוך seems phonetically related to דנג, wax, and designates the soft, mobile, cartilaginous rim of the ear.

V. 21. It is only after the giving-up of his own self, combined with the ordination given by God and the nation that the priest, and also the garb of the priest, receives its holiness. This act of sanctifying the whole personality of the priest clad in all his dignity and honour was the final act of the whole of the induction ceremony, as recorded in Levit. 8,30. It is mentioned here immediately after the placing of the blood on the ear, hand and foot, because it brings to its conclusion the idea of the sanctification of the whole personality of the priest which is started by this placing.

V. 22—25. At every שלמים, the offering that expresses the happy enjoyment of one’s own self, realising that this happiness comes from God, תנופה ,(שלום ,שָׁלֵם) and תרומה take place beforehand with the אימורים of sensual allurements and purposes, and with the חזה .חזה ושוק, the breast, enclosing all the feelings and will and aspirations of Man (the heart, lungs etc. I.L.). שוק, the thigh and leg, representing standing and going, man’s power and man’s efforts (cf. the juxtaposition of גבורת הסוס and שוקי האיש in Ps. 147,10). תנופה is a horizontal movement away from oneself and towards oneself in all four directions, מוליך ומביא (in front, to the right, behind and to the left. I.L.). תרומה is an up and down movement, rising and sinking, מעלה ומוריד. Both mean literally a gift directed towards the world in general, all one’s fellowmen and to God, and hence these movements are symbolic expressions of the same idea. The horizontal movement to all sides, תנופה, “waves” the object towards the community and promises that your own use of the object will only be enjoyed bearing the community in mind; the raising and sinking movement dedicates the object to heaven and dedicates the earth for heaven. At the offering which sanctifies the enjoyment of one’s own happiness (שלמים I.L.), before eating and enjoying it, the אימורים, together with breast and shank have first to be “waved and raised”, expressing thereby that only he is worthy of the enjoyment of his own happy state, who, divesting himself of all selfishness, sees to it that his feelings and senses, his aspirations and his willpower, his strength and his efforts are all used for the benefit of his fellow-man and of God. A man may only enjoy his own happiness if God and the community also enjoy it. Although both movements are performed equally with both the חזה and the שוק it is peculiar that we find constantly that תנופה is primarily referred to חזה, and תרומה to שוק. It always speaks of חזה התנופה and שוק התרומה. It seems, that one is more inclined to devote one’s feelings towards God than to the community, and one’s strength and powers turn more naturally to help the purposes of the community and one’s fellow-men than for godly purposes. Hence the warning is specially emphasised in the opposite direction. (In Levit. Hirsch gives another, additional reason. I.L.). In the case of שלמים both the חזה and the שוק are given to the כהן as the representative of the Sanctuary-of-the-Torah for the purpose of which all the feelings and will and the independent strength and power of the people who feel happy in their lot should be used.

Here, in our case, when in the איל מלאים a whole life is dedicated to God and to the community, and personal rights and privileges are only to be granted because of, and for, this dedication, this תנופה and תרומה, but especially the תנופה is quite specially important. The thought of the priest’s relation to God is already impressed by the whole preceding procedure of the induction ceremony, as well as by the mere idea of the honour which is to be conferred on him. But the fact that the priest is a priest only in the name of the people, for the people and by the people, that the “איל״ leading, in front of the community is only upheld by the זכות of the community, that all his privileged honour is only there for the community, all this has certainly to be quite specially brought home to the mind of the priest-to-be. Hence here (V.24 and 26) תנופה alone is thought of, although, as is evident from V.27, the act of תרומה was also done. Further, in the same way, we see here, that when the אימורים (representing the sensual and material efforts and aims) are laid on the hands of the priest and the act of תנופה performed before God, before they were placed on the Altar on to the עולה, the שוק was added to them (note how significantly there the words are added “for it is a ram of the ceremony of investing with full power” כי איל מלואים הוא), the שוק and one of each of the three kinds of Matzoth representing the greater or lesser degree of comfort in life granted by the priestly revenues.
