For in that too, in how the priest uses the material powers and wealth associated with his honourable post only for the well-being of, and in the interest of, the community in general, is he to be an illuminating example. More, with reference to the עולה (V.18) it says: ריח ניחוח אשה לה׳ הוא, the whole איל is an expression of doing the will of God, and hence is fuel, nourishment of the fire of His Torah. Here it says אשה הוא לה׳, only these parts of the איל are אשה לה׳, the rest comes to the priests-who-are-to-be-consecrated, as בעלים, for their own consumption. Further it says here — an expression which never occurs again — לריח ניחוח לפני ה׳, elsewhere always לה׳. Here the שוק is also given up to the fire on the Altar, the שוק with which, otherwise only תנופה לפני ה׳ takes place, and this is to express that also that part of the priest’s life which is not lived directly לה׳ to God, but לפני ה׳ should also be ניחוח לה׳.

V. 26. In the case of the איל המלאים by which the priests-to-be were to be specially impressed with the correct estimation of the rights and privileges attached to their honoured position, the שוק הימין, symbol of the position of progressive power, was laid on the אימורים to be offered up on the Altar. The חזה, the breast of the priest, his spiritual aspirations and planning was kept back for the ordinary תנופה-שלמים and was, as otherwise to the כהן, here, given to Moses, thanks to whom the priests-to-be had received their spiritual aspirations and wishes, and to whose teaching they were to keep them dedicated.

V. 27—28. This חזה ושוק “waving and raising” of the priests at the induction to their position, gave the חזה ושוק of all future שלמים-bringers the significant designation, the meaning of which we have explained above on V.22—25. The masc. sing. והיה, הוא seems to refer to חזה and to שוק looking at each one separately. תרומתם לה׳, in giving them to the כהן they express their relation to God, Whose Word and Teaching the כהן represents to them.

V. 29. ובגדי הקדש וגו׳ i.e., just as Aaron was invested with the office of High Priest by being clothed in the eight garments of the Sanctuary, so are his descendants to be invested in the honour and office of High Priest by clothing and anointing.

V. 30. תחתיו מבניו, a son who is qualified for it, ממלא מקומו (i.e., תחתיו I.L.) takes precedence over others for the succession. Perhaps this explains the unusual form יִלבּשָׁם instead of יִלבּשֵׁם. It is a form of the future with the suffix of the past tense, and perhaps wants to say that the past investure of his father includes him to the extent that he gets the preference thereby to be clothed in the garments in succession to the father.

שבעת ימים. Just as the consecration and induction of the first כה״ג was repeated on each of seven days, so was every future High Priest to be inducted to his office for seven days. Nothing speaks as much for the symbolic nature and the deep significance of the high-priestly garments, as well as of the whole מלאים-procedure, of which we certainly have only been able to form a faint idea, as these seven daily repetitions. For a period of seven days and with sevenfold repetitions are they to saturate themselves with the whole depth and richness of thought of these procedures.
אשר יבא אל אהל מועד לשרת בקדש, this addition designates the כה״ג. This refers to the עבודת י״כ, the sole normal קרבנות צבור which belong exclusively to the כה״ג.
However, in default of the anointing-oil, the consecration of the כה״ג can be perfectly validly carried out by the clothing with the eight garments alone, such a כה״ג is called מרובה בגדים.

V. 31—33. After all the conditions have been fulfilled by the עבודת הדם, תנופת ותרומת אימרים ושוק, הקטרת אימרים ושוק, תנופת ותרומת החזה ונתינתה למשה which are the necessary stipulations for the pure happy enjoyment of the honour, then the איל המלאים, as well as the מצות in their three degrees of richness, come to the priests who have now started their honourable career, for their own enjoyment.

ואכלו אותם אשר כפר בהם וגו׳. As כפר-ב never refers to the person or object for whom, or for which, כפרה is achieved, but always to the means by which it is accomplished, the בהם here can only refer to the איל המלואים and the מצות. Now although the איל and the מצות have predominantly the character of שלמים, and as such the idea of כפרה in its real sense, can not be applied to them, still the specific conditions, וזר לא יאכל כי קדש הם, ואכל וגו׳ פתח אהל מועד ובשלת וגו׳, במקום קדש that cooking and eating may only be done in the חצר) עזרה) and no non-priest may partake of it, makes them belong to the קדשי קדשים class. Hence they can be considered as raised above the ordinary שלמים, and at any rate the procedures of the אימורים ,דם and שוק which had taken place for the מלואים purpose can certainly be considered in the wider sense of כפרה, as the end of a less sanctified and less elevated past, and the opening of a holier higher future. This would be literally כפר בהם למלא את ידם לקדש אותם. But as the eating is here put in connection with the כפרה to be attained, the eating itself must be regarded as the continuation and conclusion of the כפרה. The eating of the בשר מלואים and the לחם that went with it receives, in addition to its being a concrete enjoyment of their priestly position, at the same time the symbolic character of the אכילת בשר חטאת, they eat it both as בעלים (it being a שלמים I.L.) and as כהנים. The general dictum for the priestly eating אכילת חטאת ואשם that כהנים אוכלין ובעלים מתכפרין (Pesachim 59b) becomes applicable here. See above on V.14.

V. 34. For the meaning of the burning of נותר see notes on Ch. 11,10. This too, in our case of an איל מלואים applies with even greater force than in the usual cases. The eating of it without its being connected with the שחיטה would imply the possibility of enjoying the honours and privileges of the priesthood without the necessity of giving up living for oneself (שחיטה I.L.) and dedicating oneself to one’s mission. Hence with the איל מלואים the connection to the day of the שחיטה is drawn still closer than with an ordinary שלמים which may be eaten during שני ימים ולילה אחד whereas the eating of the איל מלואים is restricted to יום ולילה. The reason for this greater restriction seems also to be given in the כי קדש הם. They are קדשי קדשים and in this matter too, they stand in the חטאת rank. Note that it does not say here ולא יותירו מהם עד בקר, as presumably Aaron and his four sons would not be able to eat a whole איל and twenty seven matzo-loaves in the one day.

V. 35. ככה “thus”, with prominently stressed emphasis, makes every detail of the procedure prescribed here, even for instance, תנופה, סמיכה which otherwise, if omitted do not invalidate the purpose of the offering, absolutely indispensable for the consecration ceremonies: מלואים כל הכתוב בהן מעכב בהן מאי טעמא; אמר קרא ככה וגו׳, ככה עיכובא היא (Yoma 5a). אתכָה you, in your characteristic quality as the highest representative of the nation. שבעת ימים see above on V.30.

V. 36. The פר prescribed above in V.1 and 10 et seq., which, equally with the אילים and the loaves, had to be repeated on each of the seven days, is here specially brought into prominence to give it a special extra relation to the Altar, which in having the כפרה for the priests-to-be achieved on it, itself partakes of this כפרה obtained by means of the .אילים עולה, as we know, is מכפר על עשה, and to what degree כפרה too can be ascribed to the איל מלואים which has really the character of a שלמים, we have remarked on V.33. But the real כפרה is innate in the הטאת, which, inasmuch as it promises future earnest adherence to the whole height of one’s calling, atones for all carelessness and slips of the past. Above, in considering the כפרה which is innate in the בגדי כהונה we have already tried to explain the point of view which recognises a כפרה not only for an erring person but also for the Sanctuary of the Torah. The Sanctuary’s high ideal can be blurred and lowered by the actual concrete life of the people who erect it and amongst whom it stands, and to that degree it requires כפרה i.e., protection from the results of the sins of the nation. This idea appears here immediately at the dedication of the inauguration of the altar, in which the Sanctuary’s idea of morality concentrates itself. It had been erected by men who at any rate had not reached perfection, by the whole nation, which includes every degree of moral imperfection. It can appear that the highest ideal to which the Altar was erected, instead of being the ideal which God sets and which reposed in the Holy of Holies, was the actual standard attained by the nation with all its imperfections. More it was quite possible — as the necessity for this “freeing from sin” (וחטאת I.L.) of the Altar is explained in the ברייתא דמלואים which is preserved in ת״כ — that men of moral weaknesses and sinners worked with the others in the erection of the Sanctuary and the Altar; it was quite possible that in the gifts out of which the whole erection was made, one or the other may not have given them in quite the right spirit of joyful sacrifice, it could even be that ill-gotten and illegally held property had been subscribed amongst the תרומה. All this made it necessary that an act should be performed by which, right from the first, the danger of any transference of the imperfection on the part of the builders to the idea that the building they erect is to represent, would be prevented. This act — as is stated here (וחטאת וגו׳ I.L.) — was the כפרה itself which was to be achieved on the Altar for the consecration of the priests and the High Priest. If even the elite of the nation may only step up to the Altar in the guise of requiring כפרה at the moment of their being chosen; if the first offering to be brought on the Altar is a חטאת, a “cleansing of error” of the High Priest and his sons; if this cleansing-of-error offering has to be brought seven times, daily for seven days; if the first High Priest and the first priest have first to recognise themselves and make it known by סמיכה on the פר החטאת, seven times daily for seven days, that they require כפרה before they themselves may function at the Altar, then surely the fact is fully expressed and proclaimed as publicly as possible that it is not the standard which the nation or its priests may have attained, but the ideal of the Sanctuary which is to be the goal for their future lives, that that ideal, and nothing less, is the purpose for which the Sanctuary and the Altar stand erected in their midst. That is the meaning of וחטאת על המזבח בכפרד עליו and only in the assumption of this “cleansing-of-error” of the Altar is it, by anointing, to be sanctified for its purpose.

V. 37. והיה המזבח קדש קדשים כל הנוגע וגו׳. We doubt whether this expression is to be taken simply as a superlative, “the very holiest”. עבד עבדים is not the veriest slave but a slave to slaves, מלך מלכים is a king over kings (cf. שמי השמים ,(הלא שרי יחדיו מלכים a higher heaven to which the heaven that we can see dwindles to a similar proportion that our earth holds to our heaven, etc. etc. So in all probability קדש קדשים means a holy place from which all other holy places receive their holiness.

If we compare the relationship of the place of the Ark of the Covenant, the לביר, which is called קדש הקדשים to the היכל, the place of the מנורה and the שלחן, which is called קדש, with the relationship of those offerings which like עולה, חטאת, אשם stand as קדשי קדשים to בכור, מעשר, פסח and שלמים which are called קדשים קלים then we find that אשם, חטאת, עולה, דביר have this in common that they relate to Man’s activities to the Torah, and Man’s relation to it, whereas the היכל with the שולחן and מנורה, and פסח, מעשר, בכור, שלמים have as their direct object, Man’s possessions, the fate, the fortune he receives from God’s Hand. We could then say: that the sanctification of his acts i.e., Man’s placing himself ready to actually carry out the precepts of the Divine Torah, is the calling which is the very first, the most essential fundamental condition which forms the basis of the Sanctuary on which the sanctification of all other relations rests, out of which the sanctification of all his other relations emanate. It is the קדש הקדשים, the base and source of the sanctification of all other holy things in his life. The sanctification of the passive side of Man, that which he receives from God, is only of value if beforehand, before he has received it, he has placed himself with every phase of his life, ready to carry out the will of God. Accordingly we find that all offerings have to be sandwiched between the two עולה ;עולות תמיד, the dedication of all one’s acts towards ever progressive and ever higher perfection has to form the basis and the goal of all offerings, according to the profound dictum וערד עליה העולה והקטיר עליה חלבי השלמים, on which the Gemora comments עליה השלם כל הקרבנות כולן (Yoma 33a).

Now nothing stands more in the service of sanctifying the actions of Man than the Altar. It stands directly in front of the entrance to the Sanctuary, opposite the Ark of the Torah in the Holy-of-Holies. It is the real centre of the space in front of, and round about the Sanctuary, and represents, by the אש דת flaming on its summit, giving oneself up to God’s Torah as the condition for entry into the Sanctuary. That is why it is called מזבח העולה, is entirely on the basis of the sanctifying of actions, it is קדש קדשים.

כל הנגע במזבח יקדש would be the direct result of והיה המזבח קדש קדשים. The concrete working of the קדש קדשים character of the Altar is, that כל הנגע במזבח יקדש. Exactly in the same way it says of the כלי שרת in Ch. 30,29. וקדשת אתם והיו קדש קדשים כל הנגע בהם יקדש. This corresponds entirely with the explanation given above of the expression קדש קדשים, it is that by which other things become raised to קדש i.e., into the sphere of חורה-consecration. (Twice more in a similar manner in connection with the קדש קדשים character of the חטאת and the מנחה, it says כל אשר יגע בבשרה יקדש ,כל אשר בהם יקדש. Levit. 6,11 and 20. But there it concerns an actual concrete communication of קדושה i.e., בליעה, see note there). All Jewish ideas of a Sanctuary are ideas of sanctifying, it is not made holy so that holiness should be concentrated in it, and all other is left to non-holiness. Everything becomes Holy so that it makes things Holy.

This action of the top of the Altar as אריאל to grip and hold fast everything that touches it with “lion’s strength” is modified by the verse that follows וזה אשר תעשה על המזבח, as well as by a similar limitation in Levit. 6,2. זאת תורת העולה היא העולה על מוקדה (see notes there) that it is only הראוי לו, only that which is already assigned, which is appropriate to it, שהוברר לחלקו, that is gripped and held by the Altar: המזבח מקדש הראוי לו, even if in the meantime it has become unfit for an offering. Moreover, according to ר׳ יהושע the idea is specifically directed to the Fire and not to the Altar, not כל הראוי למזבח which would include דם ונסכים but only כל הראוי לאשים אם עלה לא ירד (Zebachim, 83a). But even this idea that what is unfit, if once brought on the Altar, remains gripped and held for the fire, אם עלה לא ירד is limited in its application. It says אלו אם עלו לא ירדו, הלן והיוצא והטמא ושנשחט חוץ לזמנו וחוץ למקומו ושקבלו פסולין וזרקו את דמו: but on the other hand, הרובע, והנרבע, והמוקצה, והנעבד, והאתנן, והמחיר, והכלאים, והטרפה, והיוצא דופן, אם עלו ירדו. The formula applies: כל שפסולו בקודש הקודש מקבלו לא היה פסולו בקודש אין הקודש מקבלו. But the meaning of this formula is not quite sure. According to Rashi it means שבאה בעזרה בהכשרה ונפסלה i.e., לא ירד only applies when the פםול occurred after entry into the עזרה. But רובע and נרבע and טרפה could possibly also occur in the עזרה on account of which תוספות takes פסולו בקודש to mean שאירע פסול משנשחטה ונתקדשה קדושת כלי that the פסול occurred only after שחיטה; or after it had already received קדושה by being received in a כלי שרת (as e.g., קומץ). In favour of this explanation is both the idea הראוי לו meaning שהוברר לחלקו, and the expression used for the contrary i.e., לא היה פסולו בקודש which seems to say that the פסול occurred when it was not yet affected by the קדושת מזבח. This expression is less easily explained according to the other way of taking it, which תוספות also quotes, Zebachim 68b, כל שפסולו כשר בעלמא בקודש i.e., where the פסול does not make it positively unfit, but only relatively and in certain cases it would not hinder the offering being made, for instance טמא בצבור, so that the פסול can not be said to be absolutely in contrast to the קודש. Or according to the way that תוספות takes it in Nidda 41a: that שאין פסולו יכול להיות עד אחר שהוקדש whose פסול is only a result of its קדושה where the פסול can only occur after it has become קודש. See תוספות there and the קרבן אהרן on ת״כ Levit. 6,2. Finally, according to ר׳ יהודה the idea of פסולו קודש gives the further limitation, that שנשחטה בלילה ונשפך דמה ויצא דמה, nevertheless אם עלתה תרד (Zebachim 84a).

To take anything that is ראוי למזבח or, more specifically ראוי לאשים away from the Altar-fire would express the pernicious error that the particular function of a human being which is represented by the organ concerned, is something that is not to be given over to be dedicated by the Altar-fire to the Torah; so that there would be some phase of human life which does not pertain to the purification and sanctification by the אש דת, the fire of the Torah. And it is the whole of the human being in every phase of its life which is called upon to become לחם אשה ריח ניחוח לה׳. On the other hand the things which cause a פסול making the offering unfit to be brought, all represent, to a major or minor degree, phases of life which are in opposition to those ideas which the Mikdosh wants to represent, and so, if brought, would effect a disturbance in the clarity of those ideas. In an object that, on the one hand, has once become הוברר לחלקו, ראוי למזבח and so, raised out of the sphere of concrete objects into the realm of symbolic objects of the Mikdosh, and, on the other hand, through some circumstance has become פסול, two opposing elements are present regarding which the formula פסולו בקודש gives the decision. We can understand that where the קדושה, the בירור לחלק מזבח by the שחיטה or קדושת כלי has preceded the פסול, or the פסול is of a nature that does not absolutely ban it from the precincts of the Sanctuary, or where it does actually represent the קדושה insamuch as it was presupposed in the first instance, that in all these cases, the קודש element in the object is in the foreground, the consideration that nothing that represents any function of human life and, as such, has been brought up and given over to the Altar fire symbolically representing one aspect of human life, should then not be taken away from the Altar, אם עלה לא ירד. But we can also fully understand that פסולים like רובע ונרבע מוקצה ונעבד וגו׳ have, in contrast the פסול-character well in the foreground and אם עלו ירדו.

V. 38. With the preceding verse the prescriptions concerning the erection of the Sanctuary, its consecration, and that of the priests, are concluded. But it is not the establishment and consecration of Sanctuary and priests that by itself brings about the promised goal of God’s presence in the nation as expressed in the verse ועשו לי מקדש ושכנתי בתוכם (see note on XXV,8). This goal is only achieved by the priests expressing ever afresh on behalf of the nation the daily devotion of the lives of the people to the ideals of Judaism as represented by the Sanctuary. This, and only this, makes the מקדש the place of the שכינה and this is what is expressed in V. 38—46 as the realisation of the object of the whole building of the Sanctuary. The establishment of the Temple does not achieve this object once for always, but only provides the possibility for it. It is only achieved when the Sanctuary becomes alive and active through the acts of devotion of the people which is to be equivalent to the heart-beat, the central driving force of the national life. This constant devotion of the people to the ideals of the Divine Torah to which the Sanctuary was built which is the necessary condition for the purpose of the Sanctuary, is the meaning of the Tamid-offering. That is why its place is here in direct connection with the מלואים offerings.

כבשים בני שנה, in the hour of its national birth, Israel placed itself before God, as “sheep of His flock”, more, it only attained its national existence by giving itself up for ever to God as its Shepherd. But that which it vowed in the great solemn hour of its birth, it is to fulfil throughout the whole period of its existence. It shall never imagine that it has grown out of having to be led by the guidance of its Shepherd, it shall remain eternally young, shall eternally stand towards God as in the first year of its existence, eternally go to Him as the “one-year old lamb of His flock” (see note on XII,5). But whereas in the hour of its historical birth, it had to occupy itself primarily with the idea of surrendering itself to God’s guidance with reference to the fate it was to receive from Him, and hence its Pessach-offering was more in the nature of a שלמים, in the course of its further life under God’s guidance, it has to consider this surrender to this Guide, not so much in passive acceptance of the fate that God grants it, as in active attempts to strive upwards to accomplish the mission God has set it, and its Tamid offering, accordingly is not שלמים but עולה.

שנים ליום. It does not simply say כבש אחד תעשה בבקר וכבש אחד תעשה בין הערבים nor does it say שני כבשים בני שנה ליום but, before, in the following verse, the bringing of the two animals is separated, they are first of all considered together; and, moreover, the שנים, the number, is placed in close connection with the day, as being corresponding to, and resulting from, the meaning of the day. All this is explained by the explanatory Halacha in Yoma 62b: תניא, שנים ליום כנגד היום, אתה אומר כנגד היום או אינו אלא חובת היום. כשהוא אומר את הכבש האחד וגו׳ הרי חובת היום אמור ומה אני מקיים שנים ליום כנגד היום כיצד תמיד של שחר היה נשחט על קרן צפונית מערבית וגו׳ ע״ש.

Day, יום, (related to קום) the time of upright independence, is bound on both sides by night, it rises from night to the zenith of midday and sinks from midday to night. In this rising and sinking tendency, the whole physical world of Man moves, and is the basis of his own physical existence and everything which he requires for his work and accomplishments on earth. But both the rising and falling of day, the rising and falling of fortune, the rising and falling of earthly life, are equally an arrangement of God, the One, Only One; both are under the protection of the One Shepherd and Guide of life, and therefore the rays of the sinking day, of falling fortune, of sinking life, call us to the same mission, to the one and same happiness of life as do the rising ones. Jewish life, the Torah-life, stands under the One God, at one level, high above the change of time. As the same “sheep of God’s flock”, with the same symbols of “food, comfort and happiness”, Israel presents itself to the rising as to the sinking rays. It acknowledges the Oneness of its God, by the “oneness” of its mission in life and its happiness in life. (See V.41). That is why its morning Tamid was offered at the N.W. side of the Altar, so that the morning rays from the east fall upon it, and the evening one in the N.E., opposite the evening rays from the west, so that Israel shows itself in the same unchangeable character in the declining as in the rising rays. This, the constant devotion of the people to the idea of the Divine Torah which is the necessary condition for the attainment of the object for which the Sanctuary was built, is the meaning of the Tamid offering. In Tamid IV we read לא היו כופתין את הטלה אלא מעקידין אתו מי שזכו באברין אוחזין בו which רמב״ם explains (הל׳ תמידין ומוספין א׳ ד׳) that the lamb of the Tamid was not bound, but was only held by priests by the fore and hind legs. An opinion in the Gemora (31b) gives the remarkable reason for this dictum of the Mishna: משום דמהלך בחוק העמים, because by tying it up he would be “acting in the manner of the other nations”. ראב״ד and also רמב״ם there on the Gemora seem to have had the version אפיקורסין instead of עמים (nevertheless in his commentary on the Mishna רמב״ם has it also שלא יחקו לאומות). Which pagan or un-Jewish idea is to be countered by this proceeding is not mentioned. We have already remarked above on Ch. 12,5, what a contrast the “lamb” in Jewish symbolism is to the idea of the “lamb” in another non-Jewish idea. Ours is the happy, joyful, virile, unblemished lamb in eternal freshness of youth, that finds its constant happiness and fullness of life just in giving itself up to the guidance of its Shepherd, in contrast to that idea which sees in the “lamb” the symbol of passive suffering and endurance without resistance, and finds in this endurance to the death (like a lamb to the slaughter. I.L.) the ideal of life’s mission. We are very much inclined to find in this un-Jewish way of looking at the symbolism of the lamb that point of view which is to be opposed by the particular item of the ritual in question. Not the lamb tied hand and foot but as the free living creature (restrained only by the hands of the priests of God’s Torah. I.L.) is how Israel represents itself, giving itself up freely to the lead and guidance of its Shepherd, and only in such devotion finding true freedom and true life.

V. 40. עשרון. One tenth of an איפה represents the עומר לגלגלת, the measure of the Manna which was given as the daily requirement of nourishment for a human being (Ch. 16,36, see notes thereon), and hence was used generally to express Man’s food granted by God. סלת בלול בשמן: see above on V.2. The מנחת נסכים which accompanied the עולה and שלמים always consisted only of סלת, of unbaked flour, so that it bore still more the character of God’s gift still unaltered by Man’s hand. בשמן כתית: see on Ch. 27,21. In Menachoth 86a it is explained that this purest kind of oil was only indispensable for use in the Menora and that it is to be taken here, as being permissible to be used for מנחות too. — רבע ההין. The masculine form רבע for a quarter does not occur anywhere else in the תורה and altogether in תנ״ך only once elsewhere, in the mouth of the servant of Saul. (Sam. I. 9,8) הנה נמצא בידי רבע שקל כסף. Otherwise, and indeed immediately following here, רביעת ההין. The Mishna in Menachoth 90a teaches מדות הלח בירוציהן קדש that in liquid measures any overflow that touches the outside of the vessel is also קדש. Further in the Gemora 87b and 88a, a difference of opinion between ר״י and ר״מ is explained to be, that, according to בירוצי המדות נתקדשו :ר״י and according to לא נתקדשו :ר״מ, and in לתוספות׳s way of taking this difference, as explained by מל״מ on ה׳ מעשה קרבנות II,9, this difference is independent of that general statement of the Mishna on 90a and must be taken so that according to ר״י׳s view the בירוצי רביעית מגזרת הכתוב are included in the רביעית which the Torah fixes, and are an essential part of the מנחה. We think that this could find its explanation in the unusual form רבע. Here, where the liquid quarter measure is mentioned for the first time in connection with offerings the strong masculine form is used instead of the weak feminine one, just to tell us (or rather to remind us. I.L.) that included in this measure must be the additional בירוצים. Ps. 104,15, ,ויין ישמח לבב אנוש ,להצהיל פנים משמן ,ולחם לבב אנוש יסעד gives us the meaning of the three נסכים-materials, flour: food; oil: comfort; wine: joy. When Israel, in the עולה gives itself up to striving with the whole of its being upwards to the heights of the calling given to it by its “Shepherd”, it brings at the same time to this same God, Who gives it its mission, symbols of the conditions necessary for its existence, its comfort and its happiness in life, as a מנחה, an offering of acknowledgment. It thus renews ever afresh, the consciousness that the Lawgiver of its life is at the same time One Who gives it life, keeps and sustains its life, and is the happiness-bringer to its life.

V. 41. See note on 38. סלת and שמן form the real מנחה, and by it, one’s existence and the continuation of one’s existence is laid in the Hand of God, and on that the promise of obedience is founded. נסך is the acknowledgment of the happiness which one finds just in the feeling of this dependence and subordination. This consciousness and this happiness are the same at the sinking rays as at the rising ones. Hence it does not say here נסכו but סנכה referring to the מנחה. The מנחת ערב is accompanied by the same נסך as the מנחת הבקר. The לה is difficult, as כבש is the final object of the sentence. It seems to be added to the train of thought of the מנחת ערב: just as you carry out the ritual (תעשה I.L.) at the acknowledging- offering of the morning and by its “pouring-out-offering”, so shall you do at the acknowledgment-offering of the evening.

V. 42. See note on V.38. פתח אהל מועד לפני ה׳. Only by standing ready for His Torah do we stand before God. שמה, thither, where the “Testimony of His Torah” has its home, has God fixed the place for us to meet Him. There, He expects and awaits us, thither we have to go with our elevating-offering as a sign of our constant devotion to Him and His Torah, if we want to expect that He shall come to us אועד לכם שמה לדבר אליך שם: it is not the individuality of Moses, but the devotion of the nation which brings about the proximity of God, and it is the nation to whom God comes when He speaks to Moses.

V. 43—44. All the preceding consecrations and sanctifications are only symbolic proceedings, the Sanctuary only really becomes holy by the presence of the Glory of God, by which God impresses the seal of His satisfaction and pleasure on the work of Man and the actions of Man.

V. 45. And this presence of the Glory of God in the Temple is itself only the proof of His presence in the nation of which He desires to be God, i.e., the Decider of their destiny and the Leader of their actions.

V. 46. And this special presence of God in the nation will remain no mere abstract idea, but they will experience this special proximity of God. The whole tenor of their internal and external lives will prove to them this nearness of God, as God Himself has said, that wherever He wishes that His Name to be remembered, i.e., wherever He wishes that one should recognise and acknowledge that ה׳ שמה, that God is there, there will He come to us and bless us. It is in the blessing of our material existence that we are to be conscious of the presence of God, בכל המקום אשר אזכיר את שמי אבוא אליך וברכתיך. (XX,21, see note there).

V. 1. It was only after the complete conclusion of the instructions for the erection and consecration of the whole institution of the Sanctuary, and immediately after the assurance of the accomplishment of the highest object of the whole Sanctuary, that the making of the Incense Altar and thereby the completion of the Heichal was ordered. Both of these facts are deeply characteristic for the meaning of this Altar. Its position, within the Heichal and not in the forecourt, already ranks it amongst those things which are meant to serve as representing the actual ideals of the Jewish calling, and not, like the constituent parts of the forecourt, only to show the way to these ideals. Accordingly it belongs to the “contents”, to the כלים of the Sanctuary, and is not to be regarded like the “Offering-Altar” as merely raised רצפה and part of the actual building itself (Zebachim 27b). It was placed in front, between the Table and the Lamp, opposite the “Evidence of the Torah”.

This position makes one regard it as representing the realisation of the ideal taught by the תורה in the combination of the material and spiritual blessings granted by the תורה. The ארון gives שלחן and מנורה so that both together can then be joined to be used again in the מזבח הזהב for the objects of the ארון.

The meaning of the forecourt reaches its zenith in the constantly recurring expression אשה ריח ניחוח לה׳. The summit of the עזרה is the מערכה, the אריאל, the place on which the fire-of-the-Torah shines forth with the demand that everything earthly and material is to be so purified and dedicated to upward efforts that it becomes fuel for keeping godliness alive on earth, and gives satisfaction to God above. The עזרה works on the material which is at the stage of being still completely unennobled (נחשת) and teaches by זריקה ,קבלה ,שחיטה and הקטרה the way to ריח ניחוח לה׳. But the Jewish ideal is that solid pure golden stage, without dross (זהב), which does not still require the purifying sacrifice and surrender, which already has the whole earthly and material existence so permeated with the godly, that, without any residue whatsoever from it, it is through and through ריח ניחוח לה׳. It is this ideal that קטרת על מזבח הזהב serves to express. So that in truth the מזבח הזהב is a קרן of the מזבח הנחשת, it is the extension, the height up to which the מזבח נחשת is aspiring. In Ezekiel 43,13 — according to the explanation given in Menachoth 97b and Erubin 4a — the מזבח הזהב is actually called גב המזבח, the top of the מזבח הנחשת. So, quite clearly in Yoma 59a כוליה מזבח פנימי במקום חרא קרן דחיצון קאי. (The whole of the golden Altar stands as a horn of the outer Altar. I.L.).

That is why its erection only comes after the ultimate goal, the regaining of the שכינה on earth, which is what the working of the Sanctuary aims at, had been expressed; it is in intimate connection with this goal. Both together form the complete pinnacle of the Jewish ideal. The whole earthly existence, every phase completely permeated with spirituality, without leaving any residue לריח ניחוח לה׳, completely קטרת without שחיטה etc., the intimate penetration of the מנורה into the שלחן. And abreast of that, and directly dependent on that, and brought about by that: the presence of the Glory of God in the midst of our material earthly life, which is felt and recognised by the blossoming of all our material life into the complete flower of unalloyed happiness; ושכנתי בתוך בני ישראל וגוי וידעו כי אני ה׳ וגו׳.

V. 2. אמה ארכה וגו׳. The whole מזבח is naught but an upward-aspiring קרן. The קרנות of the Offering-Altar also measured one cubit square. But they were just complete cubes whereas the golden Altar rose upwards to twice the height. ממנו קרנתיו, the whole mass was a קרן.

V. 3. זר זהב. By this circlet it attained the character of the symbolic items like the ארון and the שלחן, and by it, the idea which it is to represent is established as an unassailable goal for the minds of the nation.

V. 4. תעשה לו וגו׳ על שתי צלעתיו תעשה על שני צדיו. This repetition and the relation of צלעתיו to צדיו is obscure. In the same way when the work was carried out in Ch. 37,27, it says על שתי צלעתיו על שני צדיו. Rashi explains צלעתיו here, (following Onkelos) as meaning corners, although there is no other example of its having this meaning. Apart from this, it is difficult to understand even with this meaning. If the rings were fixed at the corners, it would clearly require four rings, so that each pole should go through two rings, and we could then not understand why it does not say here, similarly to what it does in the case of the Offering-Altar, that four rings are to be made (Ch. 27,4). It seems rather that the addition of על שני צריו comes to oppose this way of taking it. One could have taken the שתי טבעות על שתי צלעתיו to mean that on each of two sides there were to be two rings, four rings in all, and hence it adds explanatorily תעשה על שני צדיו the two rings are to be on two sides, i.e., on each side one ring. So that the rings were not like those on the other Altar, על ארבע קצותיו, but על צלעות המובח על שני צדיו on both sides only one ring in the middle of the wall of the Altar. So that the poles only went through one ring, which, considering the very much smaller size of this Altar, was quite sufficient and perhaps was to demonstrate its character as a כלי in contrast to the other Altar. (There are points of difference in Halacha, e.g., the size of the אמה for the כלים was only five tevachim, while for the building itself, of which the Offering-Altar was part, it was six tevachim, etc. I.L.).

V. 6. לפני הפרכת אשר על ארן העדות. Like the שלחן and the מנורה it was to be placed in the היכל, outside the Holy-of-Holies, in front of the curtain which divided off and protected the “Evidence”. It belonged to the sphere of the national life which was to be attained through the Torah which rested in the Ark, indeed, it expressed the highest perfection of such a life. But, just as in relation to the material and intellectual development of the nation, the attested Torah of God’s will rested under separate cherubim-protection, so that if ever the intellectual and material life of the nation should turn away from subordinating itself to the carrying out of the Torah, and set itself up in opposition to it, the cherubim-protection would cease caring for the material and intellectual life of the nation, and save up the Torah for a purer, more faithful future: (see explanation of the פרכת I.L.): in exactly the same manner if the spiritual soul-life of the nation — which is begotten by the union of the material and intellectual life, and which finds its expression in קטרת — instead of letting itself be shown the idea of ניחוח לה׳ by the Torah, forms ideals from its own dreams and ideas in the place of God’s Truth, then it too, together with the Torah-estranged material and intellectual life, loses the special protection of the cherubim and the intimate nearness of God. The Torah is to be protected against errors of self-formed ideology, equally with errors regarding material and intellectual matters. (See notes on Chapter 26,36 at the end of notes).

לפני הכפרת וגו׳. That is why the מזבח הזהב has its place in a straight line opposite the כפרת. Israel has to draw its ideals only and solely from the תורד, only the carrying-out of the Israel-ideal as represented by the cherubim is ניחוח לה׳, ascends completely to God as קטרת, and only such an uplift to God, drawn from the תורה, obtains that nearness of God which makes the Sanctuary into an אהל מועד of which God has said: אשר אועד לך שמה. But it does not say regarding the מזבח קטרת as it does of the שלחן and the מחוץ לפרכת ,מנורה (XXVI,35) but לפני הפרכת, it is equally לפני הפרכת as לפני הכפרת, or as it actually puts it in Ch. 40,5 לפני ארון העדות. In the carrying out to the highest degree, the ideal taught by the תורה, the פרכת as well as the כפרת finds its enduring integral meaning in this idea of the מזבח הקטרת, the פרכת as well as the כפרת gets its true realisation, both, שמירה and עשיה go hand in hand, more, the higher the rank the more essential does the שמירה become, the easier is it to fall, the greater is the necessity to keep in mind always the immutability of the תורה, to guard it against oneself, even as the cherubim were simultaneously פרשי כנפים למעלה סככים בכנפיהם על הכפרת — (See note thereon).

V. 7—8. It is highly characteristic, and we have already remarked on this, above on Ch. 27,20, that the “service of the Lights” and the “offering of the incense”, the national care for intellectual work for understanding theory, and the highest ideal of perfection in action, go hand in hand. More, דישון מזבח הפנימי, the preparation of the golden Altar for the offering of the highest ideal of ניחוח precedes the הטבת הנרות, the preparation of the Menora for the lighting ceremony. According to the view of the חכמים (Yoma 14b) it took place in the morning ceremony in the middle of the preparation of the Menora מפסיק בקטרת בין הטבת חמש נרות להטבת ב׳ נרות, and in the evening service too, the קטרת precedes the lighting of the lamps (ibid. 15a). The idea of the highest moral perfection of practical behaviour must be held up beforehand as the purpose of Jewish development of the mind. In the Jewish conception of life, genius is no license for non-observation of the laws of morality, but on the contrary, the highest degree of morality is made the test for the highest degree of true intelligence, and only in it and by it does the nobility of the mind show itself and prove its genuineness. Significantly the “orders” תצוה of this chapter for the consecration of the Jewish priesthood start with the service of the Lights and finish with the highest ideal ניחוח-offering. Both together, in intimate combination make the priest into a priest.

V. 9. קטרת זרה. Any bringing of incense other than as prescribed here is to be considered as זרה (Menachoth 50a & b). Thus every arbitrary forming of the highest ideal of life is excluded. Hence there is not a highest ideal of life. There is only the highest ideal of life. Only completely sublimating oneself in the expressed will of God, putting aside one’s own ideal, only sublimating oneself in the will of God as attested in the ארון העדות is ניחוח לה׳. And, equally so, all other offerings עולה מנחה נסכים are excluded from this Altar. All other offerings express only part of the meaning, or their meaning is only preparatory, compared to the completeness and perfection of achievement, to the expression of which the מזבח הקטרת is dedicated.

V. 10. We have already above (in the article on the priestly garments. I.L.) indicated the meaning of the כפרת “atoning for the Mikdosh”. If anything requires protection against its ideal becoming dimmed by the distance between it and the actuality, surely it is this ideal of the highest moral perfection, which we are to keep unceasingly before our eyes as our ultimate goal, as it finds its expression in the קטרת on the מזבח הפנימי. The priests and the people have to remind themselves once a year of this distance between the ideal and the reality by the פר and שעיר of י״ב and by the נתינת הדם on the horns of the מזבח הזהב to bring to their minds the height on which the reality should stand.

קדש קדשים הוא לה׳. In Zebachim 27a, we are taught concerning the מזבח פנימי מקדש פסולין בין ראוי לו בין אין ראוי לו —:מזבח פנימי, it has the power of symbolically conferring קדושה in a greater degree than the מזבח החצון which can only מקדש פסולין הראוין לו (see note on Ch. 29,37). We think we can say, that, just because it is dedicated to the most complete spiritualisation through and through, and permeating with morality through and through, of every phase of life, that nothing may appear as being not ראוי לו, as not appertaining to it, everything is ראוי לו. To it must be applied with even more power than to the מזבח החיצון the dictum אם עלו לא ירדו. Nevertheless, although the limiting condition ראוי לו does not apply, we still think that the idea of פסולו בקדש would be applicable here too, and הרובע ונרבע וגו׳ would here also אם עלו ירדו. But we have not been able to find a positive declaration on this point.

V. 11. וידבר ה׳ וגו׳. From Ch. 25,1 to this verse was one continuous speech of God. It ordained the establishing of the Sanctuary and the priesthood and the consecrating of them. With the succeeding speech of God, the relation of the nation to this Sanctuary is then indicated. Just as from beforehand it was taught that the life in the Temple and the life of the nation were not to be considered as two separate spheres, just as the Sanhedrin had their place next to the Altar, and the Altar was to bring justice and peace and morality to the national life (which was the reason why the fundamental ideas for the kind of life to be developed in the nation, (משפטים. I.L.) were given before the instructions for building the Temple); so here after the completion of the building of the Temple, the fact that the “Temple-life” and the national life belonged intimately together is brought permanently home to the people by the Law of the Shekel, and the great Jewish truth proclaimed: That the Sanctuary is not an institution which has to be erected and then stands there once for all and thereafter its work can be carried on by priests, but that its purpose can not be achieved without the constant ever fresh and lively participation of the nation. And, equally so, that the importance of each individual, and of the nation as a whole, only consists in the contribution which is made individually and collectively, towards making the Sanctuary of the Torah achieve its practical realisation.

V. 12. נשא ראש .כי תשא את ראש: the usual expression for counting a mass of persons. One could question in which sense the ראש is to be taken in this figure of speech, whether as “head” and then it would be collective, “to take up the heads”, or as “sum-total”. As נשא meaning to count, never occurs by itself without mentioning the objects to be counted but always נשא ראש or נשא מספר (Deut. 3,40), and apart from that, ראש in phrases like ושלם אותו בראשו (Levit. 5,24) has the meaning of the amount, the sum, it seems also in נשא ראש to have the meaning of sum total. Physiologically the head can be taken as the part of the body where all the active and passive threads of life are gathered. From the head, all impulses are sent to all parts of the body, and all sensations registered. The head may well be considered the summary of all the threads of life, and so have become an idiom expressing generally the idea of the summary or sum-total.

לפקדיהם. We have already, from its phonetic relation to בגד, taken פקד to mean, clothing or investing an object with its attributes, hence, also, the placing of an object in some sphere, or in the special sphere of which it is characteristic, from which we get the idea of its meaning appointing to an office and counting etc. All counting ranges the objects counted under one idea, and makes each one of the objects counted of value, as an integral bearer of this idea. פקודי בני ישראל are all those who are thought of as בני ישראל, in whom the idea בני ישראל has a concrete bearer. At the moment in which anybody is counted לפקודי בני ישראל, he learns to value himself as a בן ישראל, the self-appreciative consciousness is aroused to see the idea of his nation incorporated in himself. Then, at that point, the important teaching is addressed to him: - Not by mere existence, by living for himself, has his נפש, his personality, value and meaning, not by his just being there is he an integral part of the nation, his mere existence does not even give him the right to be there; only by giving, doing something, is he to be counted, only by giving, doing, does he gain the right for the continuance of his existence, only by contributing his share in accordance with his duty does he obtain a justifiable position as a creature who has been crowned by God with Life, a justifiable position in the community of his nation. Only by contributing something may he be reckoned in the number of the Children of Israel. The moment he allows himself to be counted without having contributed anything to the community, and so wishes to claim the right to live without doing anything for the common welfare, at that moment he forfeits the right to exist. But where is the man who can feel that what he does for the world is so completely in accordance with what he ought to do, that he can depend on it to give him the full right to demand a full life for even one minute? Does there live a man whose imperfections do not make him feel the necessity for atonement in the moment when he is to be “counted in”? Where is the man who dares, without atonement, to let himself be counted? Therefore

V. 13. זה יתנו, not with the amount of what he actually does for the common good, but with the symbolic expression of what he knows is his duty, has he to approach God in the moment when he is to עובר על הפקודים, when he is to “pass over”, out of the ranks of the uncounted into the circle of those counted. There is no higher nobility, nor is there any deeper feeling of happiness than to belong to the פקודי ה׳, to those who are counted for God and by God, in the most unpretentious modest circumstances, in the fleeting moment of a most transitory existence, to be given a place in God’s register, to be counted in amongst God’s host. Only with the consciousness of resolving to do the whole of one’s duty does one pass over, out of the meaningless crowd of the selfish masses, into the ennobled sphere of those counted by God, into the happy consciousness of being counted by God.

But the symbolic expression of the duty to work for the common weal is מחצית השקל, half a shekel per person. Objectively, actually, even the most complete and most perfect work of any single individual is never the whole of the work, can never accomplish everything, the work of any single person will always remain but a fragment, it requires an equally devoted sacrifice on the part of his brother to establish a whole. No individual is asked to do the whole, as it says in Aboth 2,21 לא עליך המלאכה לגמור. But it must be a contribution to the whole, weighed on the scales of the Sanctuary. The Shekel must be one of twenty geras, and that which the individual gives must be ten, in itself, subjectively, a rounded whole. As far as the giver is concerned, it must be a whole, his whole, conscientiously weighed out. However small a fragment what he does may be, in relation to all that has to be done, he may leave nothing out, no power, no ability, no possessions, that could further the happiness of the whole may he keep back, although לא עליך המלאכה לגמור nevertheless ולא אתה בן חורין להבטל ממנה (Aboth ibid.). His half-shekel must weigh ten (a complete unit. I.L.) geras on the scales of the Sanctuary.

V. 14. In Shekalim 1,1, we are told that the תרומת ה׳ mentioned in this verse does not refer to the half-shekel gift ordered in the preceding verse. It is to be taken as a separate duty to contribute, without any amount being fixed, towards the requirements of the Sanctuary. The whole repetition too, would otherwise be unnecessary (— it need not repeat the whole verse simply to tell us מבן עשרים וגו׳, this could easily have been introduced into one of the preceding verses —). Also in the next verse, the fixed תרומה is called את תרומת ה׳, the Teruma, whereas here it says יתן תרומת ה׳, he shall give a Teruma, i.e., any Teruma, an unfixed amount. מבן עשרים שנה ומעלה In Jewish life the Sanctuary is not to be given over to childhood and youth, and after reaching the age of manhood, all one’s care is to be given to the selfish career of getting one’s livelihood, and so the egotism of manhood suppresses and supplants the inspirations of childhood. It is not the Jewish Sanctuary which says “let the little children come to me”. It is the grown-ups, the seriousness and the power of virile life and endeavours that it awaits. At the age in which a man, in common parlance, gets the call to think for himself and to work for himself, the Jewish Sanctuary calls him into service. A Jewish boy attains manhood for the Sanctuary of God’s Torah, and his thinking for himself and of his own future and his work and endeavours for himself are also to be for the benefit of the Sanctuary of God’s Torah, are to be thoughts of this Sanctuary and endeavours for this Sanctuary.

V. 15. Inasmuch as in this verse the object of a fixed gift of half a shekel is given as being לכפר על נפשתיכם, as a contribution towards the כפרה of the community and not as כֹּפֶר נפשו as in V. 12, as individual ransom of the giver, and, as altogether the gift itself is not described as כֹפֶר but as a contribution towards obtaining כפרה, this תרומה too, is not taken to refer to the כפר-gift described in V.12 as to be given at the time of a census, but as the permanent regular duty for each person to contribute a half-shekel yearly for the purpose of defraying the expenses of providing the public offerings.

העשיר לא ירבה והדל לא ימעיט. Just in this equality, the symbolic nature of the fixed gift of half a shekel is expressed. As long as the rich man and the poor man give, each all that he can, does the whole of what he can do, then, as far as God and His Sanctuary are concerned, the pounds of the rich weigh no more than the pennies and shillings of the poor, and the pennies and shillings of the poor are quite equal to the pounds of the rich. The rich man can do no more, and the poor man shall do no less, than the half of a whole shekel. God and the Sanctuary weigh, not the actual, but the relative size of the contribution, they value what is given and what is done in relation to the fortune and the abilities of the givers. Every one who uses the full powers of the fortune and the abilities with which he has been graced, in the service of God, in furthering the aims of the Sanctuary, lays thereby his מחצית השקל as his “symbolum” on the Altar of God.

V. 16. כסף הכפרים is the כסף כפר נפש of V.12 (cf. אם כפר יושת עליו Ch. 21,30) and this verse, accordingly, refers to the half-shekels which were given at the time of the census; here the כסף achieves the כפורים at the moment it is given, it itself is כפר נפשו לה׳ and all that was still required was to be told the use to which it was to be put. This, we are told here was: ונתת אתו על עבדת אהל מועד. “For the service of the Mikdosh.” עבודת אהל מועד is never the Service in the Temple in the sense with which we usually use that expression, never the performance of the procedures of the offerings etc. Once only is the service of the priests called עבודה (Numbers 18,7) and there it is specialised by the addition עבודת מתנה, and one offering only is especially called עבודה. This is the קרבן פסח, as we have already remarked (Ch. 12,25). עבודת אהל מועד is throughout not the service in the Temple but service for the Temple, for the actual erection and upkeep of the Temple and refers either to the service of the Levites (carrying the parts during the wandering, cleaning, sweeping etc. I.L.) or as in Ch. 35,21; XXXVI,1 & 3 & 39; XXXII,40 the erection and making of the building and its contents. As it is speaking here of the use of money it can only be understood in the latter sense. As a matter of fact the nation was counted by the half-shekels given, before the Sanctuary was established, and the silver was used for making the silver sockets for the walls and pillars, as well as for the silver hooks and encirclements of the pillars (Ch. 38,27 & 28).

והיה לבני ישראל לזכרון לפני ה׳. It remains as an eternal memory that the base, above all, on which the Sanctuary stood was the completely equal sacrifice of every man in Israel; so that the purpose too, the כפרה which was to be obtained by means of the Sanctuary, affected every personality in the nation: לכפר על נפשתיכם.

ג׳ תרומות נאמרין בפרשה. So that there are three contributions mentioned in this paragraph. Two fixed amounts of half a shekel and one not specified, the amount being left to the free will of each individual. The one fixed contribution (V. 12 & 16) was a temporary measure, only to be given when a census was necessary, what it brought in, was, in this case, used for the feet of the walls and pillars of the Sanctuary. The other fixed gift of a half shekel (V.15) was a regular yearly tax for the provision of the public offerings קרבנות צבור, in which rich and poor are to share equally. These have always to be paid for out of the current year’s contributions. This was the מחצית השקל gift or tax which was yearly collected in Adar, so that just as the first erection of the Temple was on 1st Nissan, so each year, with the 1st Nissan the offerings should proceed from the eternally fresh participation of the whole nation. This tax was called תרומת הלשכה. The third Teruma mentioned here (V.14) was also a permanent one. But it was of no fixed amount, but left entirely to the free will of each donor, as was the first Teruma for the building of the Sanctuary 25,2 et seq.) and it had a similar purpose viz., the upkeep of the structure of the Temple, its purpose was called: קדשי בדק הבית. So there were two separate funds for the Temple: the תרומת הלשכה and the קדשי בדק הבית. The תרומת הלשכה fund, formed out of the yearly מחצית השקל offerings, had to be completely used up each year, it was not allowed to accumulate, but had to be formed afresh each year. In the בדק הבית fund a Temple treasury could accumulate. The use to which these two funds were put is highly characteristic. Out of the בדק הבית fund only the expenses of the provision and upkeep of the lifeless stones and bricks, the actual structure of the Temple and its accessory buildings, מזבח העולה, הלשכות והעזרות were defrayed. These could be provided for, and their upkeep ensured, by the generosity of individuals, by the devotion of an earlier generation for all time. But the provision and upkeep of everything living, the life that is to be awakened by the Temple, the public sacrifices, as well as what was necessary for ensuring that everything was carried out strictly in accordance with the teaching of the Torah, הקטרת וכל קרבנות צבור, מבקרי מומין, תלמידי חכמים המלמדין הל׳ שחיטה והל׳ קמיצה לכהנים, מגיהי ספרים, דייני גזלות, שומרי ספיחים בשביעית וגוי, all had to be provided for out of the תרומת הלשכה. All this was to come from the ever fresh, live participation of the contemporary members of the nation at any given time. According to the views of the ראב״ד, not even a subsidiary contribution would be allowed to be taken from the בדק הבית fund for these purposes (הל׳ שקלים IV, 10. See Comm. קרבן העדה on Jerushalmi Shekalim V at the end). But in the תרומת הלשכה fund, the money could not accumulate from one year to the other, as any surplus was used for קיץ המזבח i.e., for עולות נדבה של צבור.

Owing to the enormous number of half-shekel coins required each year in Adar, these were greatly in demand, and the money-changers made a small fixed charge of an agio for changing whole into half shekels. This was called a קלבון, and it was made a rule that if two half-shekel payers joined together and paid in a whole shekel, this agio had to be added. (— the word קלבון is a remarkable example of the travels which words often undergo. It is clear that the word comes from the Hebrew or from the closely related Phonecian חלף “to change”, and was originally pronounced חלפון. The Greeks to whom this semitic word came, probably through Phonecian traders (as did several other commercial expressions as e.g., arrabone, ערבון) changed it to Kollùbos, and in this Greek guise it returned to its original Hebrew home as קלבון).

The shekel of the תורה weighed 320 barley corns. In the time of the second Temple its weight was increased by 1/5 i.e., to 384. This is what the Talmud refers to as a סלע. A סלע had 4 דינרין, a דינר had 6 מעין. A מעה in the time of Moses was called a גרה. One פונדיונין 2 = מעה, one פונדיון = 2 איסרין, one פרוטות 8 = איסר, one פרוטה weighed barleycorn of silver. (See Maim. הל׳ שקלים I,2,3).

כיור
V. 17. Whereas in the preceding laws of shekalim, the Sanctuary has been looked on as a national institution, with the whole nation individually called upon to participate in it, here, by the ordering of the כיור the ministering priests themselves are continuously reminded that they do not enter the Sanctuary on behalf of the nation on the grounds that their “doings and goings” (יד ורגל I.L.) in their ordinary life are already sufficiently sanctified to justify their position. It is only in their symbolic character, as representation of the holiness of life that this Sanctuary-of-the-Torah demands, that they have any meaning as priests.

V. 18—19. This symbolic nature of the priesthood is bestowed on the whole of the rest of their bodies by being clothed in the priestly garments (see Ch. XXVIII). Only their hands and feet — the principal means of their doings and endeavours — remain unclothed. For these, comes the washing out of the basin, literally: “overthrowing the hands and feet” with water out of the רחץ) .כיור, related to רעץ, as has already been remarked, really means “to overthrow”). That this washing was not to be taken in the concrete meaning of cleanliness, is clear from all the conditions which are associated with this command. So, for instance, it was only effective if the washing was done בכלי שרת and בפנים but if קדש בכלי שרת בחוץ או בכלי חול בפנים, או שטבל במי מערה ועבד, עבודתו פסולה (Zebachim 20b) (it had to be done with a vessel that belonged to the Sanctuary and was national property, and had to be done within the precincts of the Sanctuary, but if he used a “holy vessel” and washed outside the gates of the Sanctuary, or if he washed inside, but used an ordinary vessel, or if he dipped completely in a Mikva, and then performed his priestly function, the function so performed was invalid and had to be repeated. I.L.). Or this condition, לינה והיסח הדעת פוםלין בקידוש: — The dawn of a fresh day, or even in the middle of the same day if one’s attention had been withdrawn from the service in the Sanctuary, necessitated a repetition of the washing (ibid.) etc. etc. But it is equally clear from these conditions that this symbolic washing is also not to be taken as having the same meaning as symbolic טבילה, the complete immersion in natural water, which symbolises the merely negative idea of getting back to a state of mind which one can not be in when one is in a state of טומאה. In complete contrast to טבילה, here it is essential that the water must be in a כלי, and that the כלי must be a כלי שרת, so that, like everything which is accepted in a כלי שרת, the water becomes קדוש, and again like everything that is accepted by a כלי שרת becomes פסול בלינה (is unfit to be used if it is not freshly put into the כלי on the day that it is used. I.L.). The כיור itself is not essential, any other כלי שרת would do, the water is to be made into an element of the Sanctuary, and not בו, in it, but ממנו, from it, the element of the Sanctuary is to be made to flow over the hands and feet, and clothe them — as the garments of the Sanctuary do to the rest of the body — with the element of the Sanctuary. שלא רחוץ ידים ורגלים (functioning without washing the hands and feet) is, accordingly, exactly the same as functioning מחוסר בגדים (without all the priestly garments). (Zebachim 19b. See notes on XXVIII,42 and 43).

The position of the בין אהל מועד ובין המזבח :כיור, or as it says of the later בין האולם והמזבח :מקדש is striking. As is apparent from V.20, קידוש ידים ורגלים is required also בגשתם אל המזבח לשרת וגו׳ we should have expected the place of the כיור to be in front of the Altar and not behind it. Now תוספות (Yoma 5b and Sanhedrin 83a and b) leaves it undecided whether שלא רחוץ ידים ורגלים in the היכל is חייב מיתה also on אביאה ריקנית i.e., whether simply entering the היכל without the purpose of performing an עבודה there, would be punishable by death or whether in this respect the היכל and the מזבח החיצון are quite equal, and in this latter it distinctly only forbids approach without the washing if it is for the purpose of service, as it says לשרת להקטיר וגו׳ (V.20). It is true that Tosephoth seems to incline towards this latter alternative and so does Rashi on V.20 here. But nevertheless it is not decided, the question is left open, and the way V.19, 20 and 21 run certainly seems to indicate much more strongly the first alternative, viz., that, in the היכל even simple entry, ביאה ריקנית, but in the עזרה only גשת לשרת would entail חיוב מיתה. Then, perhaps, we can understand the position of the כיור. We have already indicated above in Ch. 27,8, how the מזבח הנחשת in its vertical elevation (striving upwards) could be considered as a sign-post showing the way to the actual accomplishment of the ideals of the Torah as represented by the היכל and its contents. So that simple ביאה בהיכל and גשת אל המזבח לשרת להקטיר אשה לה׳ would have identical meanings, and the כיור by being placed between the Altar and the entrance to the היכל would express the meaning of both. Actually, purposeless entry into the היכל without any צורך עבודה is forbidden to every כהן (Menachoth 27b) and here we are only told that doing it שלא רחוץ ידים ורגלים raises the sin to חיוב מיתה. It then would only require explanation why entry מחוסר בגדים is not raised to the same degree.

V. 21. וזק עולם לו וגו׳, really: a “tax” to be paid by the priests to the Sanctuary for all time. By קידוש ידים ורגלים the priests pay the Sanctuary the tribute of recognising the supreme dominion of its ideals, that they are only worthy of appearing as the ministers of this Sanctuary by virtue of their symbolically representing the demands of the Sanctuary, and not on account of their own real personalities. The והיתה refers probably to the fem. word רחצה (V.18). “This washing shall be unto them, etc.”

שמן המשחה
V. 23. ואתה קח לך. This form of command occurs only at the שמן המשחה by which the production of the object was quite specially directed to Moses. For by means of שמן המשחה the Sanctuary and all its parts, were, in the name of God, given their sanctifying purpose and consecration. It was therefore only to be produced by Moses, the instrument of God’s will. The oil which Moses prepared remained the only anointing-oil ever made, and was used for anointing Saul and all the Kings of the dynasty of David and all the High Priests of all time.

בשמים ראש similarly (in Song of Songs 4,14) ראשי בשמים, spices of first-class quality. — מור דרור וגו׳, myrrh, cinnamon etc. We can not be certain of exactly what the spices named here actually are, but one accepts the usual translation. דרור, this word only occurs in the meaning of freedom or homecoming as וקראתם דרור (Levit. 25,10, and elsewhere) and in the name of a bird, דרור which is usually taken to be the swallow, which according to Beza 24a דרה בבית כבשדה “is as free in human habitations as in the wild” (or perhaps דרה she lives in houses as in the fields, swallows “live” i.e., “make their nest” in the eaves of houses, (or perhaps דרור in the sense of Levit. 15,10, homecoming, as swallows emigrate and are the first birds to “return home” in the spring each year. I.L.). — Also the difference between בֶשֶׂם and בֹשֶׂם in this verse should be sought. בֶשֶׂם as singular of בשמים seems to indicate spices according to their aromatic qualities (קנמן-בשם would then be translated spicy i.e., sweet-smelling cinnamon) while the form בֹשֶׂם like קדֶשׁ etc., would mean the application, the use of spices. (קנה-בשם, translate rods or sticks of spices possibly either vanilla pods or perhaps even cinnamon sticks. I.L.) — מחציתו חמשים וגו׳ can not mean that of cinnamon only half the quantity that was used of myrrh was to be taken; for then the word מחציתו would be entirely superfluous. But the suffix מחציתו -ו refers to קנמן בשם itself, according to the Gemora in Kerith. 5a, cinnamon is to be taken in halves; not 500 shekels all in one but in two halves of 250 each.

V. 25. רקח. It is not quite sure which part of the process of perfume manufacture is to be understood by רקח. Phonetically it is closely related to רקח and ריח. But in ריח itself, as already remarked on Gen. 8,21 lies the original idea of dividing into the finest particles, from which we get also the word ריחים, a mill, so it is doubtful whether רקח is the mechanical grating of the dried roots of the spices or the penetration of other materials, here the oil, with their aroma. Expressions such as שמן רוקח (Koheleth 10,1) יין הרֶקַח (Song of Songs 8,2) indicate the latter meaning. So too, does Job 41,23, ים ישים כמרקחה where clearly the reference would apply rather to a boiling seething distilling-apparatus than to a pulverising bowl or a mortar.

שמן משחת קדש. The idea קדושה, as has already repeatedly been remarked, contains two essential factors: (a) the negative, the idea of separating from everything else פרישה and (b) the positive, the idea of absolute devotion, as we put it, the holding oneself ready for the one high purpose. The medium by means of which this homage is expressed contains accordingly also both these ingredients: the negative, oil (משה משח) the ingredient that separates from everything else, and the positive, spices, perfume, expressing pleasure, satisfaction to the higher, more refined sense. It, and that which it anoints, is only separated and picked out from everything else to completely subordinate itself exclusively to the Highest. This absolute devotion to the Highest necessitates the separation away from everything lower.

V. 27—28. In the case of the שולחן and the מזבח העולה it says ואת כל כליו, while of the מנורה the כל is missing. In the case of the מנורה, representing spiritual intellectual development, it seems that all the preparatory means and activities, כלים, to be included in the sanctifying consecration, are to be presumed as self-understood, more than in the case of the שולחן representing material welfare, or of the מזבח העולה which represents the showing of the path out of the material stage up to the heights of the spiritual moral life.
V. 29. כל הנגע בהם יקדש, hence the dictum: כשם שהמזבח והכבש מקדשין את הראוי להן כך הכלים מקדשין (Zebachim 86a) See Ch. 29,37.

V. 31—33. שמן המשחה is God’s seal for the sanctification and consecration of persons and things. One can understand how copying this “seal”, or the misuse of it for anything other than the sanctifying use ordained by God, would be a denial of the fact that God does sanctify, or an act which profanes the idea of God’s sanctifying, and can understand that such an act would entail כרת “being uprooted from the Jewish present and future”. יִיסָךְ an unusual form, similar to וַיִישֶם (Gen. 50,27. see note thereon). Perhaps here, too, it is a form meaning hovering between an active and a passive meaning. The Gemora in Kerithot 6b, takes it in that way: — כל שישנו בסך ישנו בבל ייסך וכל שאינו בסך אינו בבל ייסך, that the prohibition is only transgressed by anointing such persons or objects to whom or to which the prohibition is directed but הסך בשמן המשחה לבהמה ולכלים לכותים ולמתים פטור by using the anointing oil on animals, domestic vessels, non-Jews, or dead bodies, the death penalty is not incurred. — ובמתכנתו see note on Ch. V.8. It is worth noting that the prohibition only applies if the anointing oil is copied in the same proportion (במתכנתו) of the ingredients, and in the same quantity (כמהו) as prescribed, whereas copying the קטרת incurs the penalty if mixed in the same proportions even if not in the same quantity, קטרת שפטמה לחציין חייב, שמן שפטמו לחציין פטור (Kerithot 5a).

קטרת
V. 34. סמים. From the phonetic relation to the roots צמם, זמם, סמם we have already on Gen. 11,6 derived the basic implication of סמים as designation of such materials, the smallest quantity of which contain a large measure of effective activity (poisons, medicaments etc. I.L.). Here it refers to materials filled with volatile aroma. The form in which the sentence is couched is that of כלל ופרט וכלל with an additional פרט added afterwards a פרט [[illegible]]הרון. (a כלל, is a generic all embracing term, and a פרט is a specific example. I.L.). “God spake to Moses: Take fragrant spices, balsam, sea-lavender and galban; these spices and pure incense; each is to be taken separately by itself”. סמים is a כלל, would include every and any kind of spice; נטף שחלת חלבנה is a פרט, specifies these three fragrant spices out of the whole range of סמים, and if nothing further were said, the form of the sentence would be כלל ופרט and out of the whole range of סמים, the ingredients for the קטרת would be limited to these three, and to these three only, according to the rule אין בכלל אלא מה שבפרט. But as the פרט is followed by a repetition of סמים as a כלל again (כללא בתרא) the materials mentioned in the פרט are raised to being of the nature of a כלל, are to be considered as examples of their kind, and the limitation which they impose, is extended to all such סמים which are similar to all three of them in their common essential qualities: אי אתה דן אלא כעין הפרט. This would exclude לבונה which lacks one of these qualities, and so, as an exception, the instruction to use it has to be expressly added afterwards. The three as פרט viz., נטף שחלת וחלבנה have the two essential qualities in common, that, when ignited, they produce a dense vapour which rises straight upwards, and they disseminate perfume שקיטר ועולה וריחו נודף. The mentioning of all three is necessary, נבף is vegetable matter מן אילן while שחלת is mineral גדילי קרקע, so both have to be mentioned so as not to restrict the materials to one or the other species. חלבנה has to be mentioned because the perfume which it spreads is unpleasant and so would normally not have been taken as an ingredient for קטרת had it not been expressly prescribed. לבונה lacks one of the essential qualities, as its vapour does not rise straight upwards, it is not מקטר ועולה (Kerithoth 6b). The Halacha teaches that eleven ingredients were used to prepare the קטרת. These were חלבנה (שחלת) צפורן (נטף) צרי קנמון, קלופה, קושט, כרכום, שבולת, נרד (קדה) קציעה, מר, לבונה, these were not taken in equal parts but in various fixed quantities, apart from these, also מעלה עשן and to improve the mixing and preparation בורית כרשיגה and יין קפרסין, and also מלח סדומית about which there is a doubt as to whether it came under the instruction ממלח (V.35) or whether it was an actual part of the preparation itself. It is certain that each ingredient of the קטרת and the שמן המשחה had its own special meaning. Unfortunately no information on this point has come down to us, and in the translation we simply follow the usually accepted terms.
בד בבד יהיה. It is not sure what is to be understood by this. According to Kerithoth 5a, it demands either the exact, or the separate, weighing-out of each ingredient.

V. 35. ממלח. We have already remarked that some authorities take this to refer to the addition of מלח סדומיה. More generally it is taken to refer to the way in which it is to be prepared, “integrated”, and the context and the form מְמֻלָת seem to indicate this too. Were it to mean salted, it would demand a strength for which the small quantity of Kab in the whole total mass of the other ingredients would hardly justify the term. Taking the specific gravity of sodomic salt in comparison with water to be 3:1, Kab equalling one Log, and taking the reckonings given in Maimonides הל׳ עירובין I,12, and כלי מקדש II,3, the proportion of salt to the whole mass would work out at 210 in 36800. One רביעית water weighs  דינר, one לוג sodomic salt, according to the reckoning quoted above would be  דינר, the eleven ingredients of the קטרת, weighed together 368 Mena and a Mena 100 דינר i.e., 36800. One could hardly call by the addition of 1/175 salt, any mass מְמֻלָת But we have already elsewhere taken the basic meaning of מלח (from the phonetic relation of מלח and מלא) to be the most intimate permeation, as such a thorough permeation by which one material becomes “full” of another material in all its particles, from which then the word “salt” would derive from the idea of thoroughly penetrating. According to this, here too מַלֵח could mean the most intimate penetration of each ingredient into the other, the most thorough mixing. Each material is first to be separately grated as fine as possible and then ממֻלח, most thoroughly and intimately mixed together. Onkelos also takes it this way: מערב.

V. 36—37. By its two constituents, oil and incense, the שמן המשחה expresses the idea that persons and objects receive the calling of being פרוש לריח ניחוח, of being separated, singled out, to be “hints of”, symbols of, a “desire to be pleasing to God.” This ריח ניחוח, as the highest aim of the purest most ideal accomplishment of the whole Sanctuary is, as already remarked on Ch. 30,1, what קטרת expresses. We can understand how the national ideal as expressed by the קטרת was, like the Seal of God, as expressed by the שמץ המשחה, to be carefully protected from profanation by being copied. Any preparation of it, in the same proportion of ingredients, for profane use would be a parody of its symbolism and a mockery of the idea which it expresses. The copying of the building of the Sanctuary or of its contents is likewise forbidden, and is included in the prohibition, לא תעשון אתי (Ch. 20,20).

V. 1. With the preceding verse, the instructions for the establishment of the Sanctuary are completed. All that was now needed was the appointment of the craftsmen to carry them out, and the presentation of an object, the “Evidence of the Torah”, the Tablets of the Law, which was to be given by God Himself, and not to be made by the hand of Man. It was to make a home for this object that the whole Sanctuary was to be erected by human hands. Both, the appointment and the presentation now follow in this chapter.

V. 2. ראה קראתי בשם, and, in the same way, from Moses to Israel (Ch. 35,30) קרא בשם .ראו קרא ה׳ בשם, to call by name, means to call somebody specially and expressly for something. Inasmuch as it says: “I have called”, and Moses and Israel are asked to ראו ,ראה, are called upon to use their own judgment and experience on the fact of this appointment, it is evident that the quite special and well known gifts of Bezalel had already shown themselves, so that even in the judgment of his contemporaries, he stood out as the only one suited for the appointment. But these gifts and abilities are shown by God’s Word קראתי בשם to be the working of quite special provision on God’s part. רמב״ן already points out, on this verse, how unlikely Israel’s past, under the pressure of their slave-labour, would be to awake and develop a sense of art or artistic ability, and that the existence of a Bezalel and his fellow-artists amongst the people could only be the result of quite special Divine provision. — On to this point, that God called on Moses ראה, and Moses on the people ראו, for their concurring judgment on the appointment of Bezalel, our sages hang their pertinent observation: that אין מעמידין פרנס על הצבור אלא אם כן נמלכים בצבור (Berachoth 55a), one may not impose an official on the community, one may not appoint an official, without first asking the community for its agreement.

V. 3. For the meaning of דעת, בינה, חכמה, and their relation to each other, see notes on Gen. 41,33. The fact that these highest mental and intellectual attributes have to be ascribed to Bezalel makes it evident that here it is no question of producing a merely external work of art, but that it concerns a work that is to be symbolic in every part of it, and that the ideas which are to be expressed in it, and through it, are to be kept present in the minds of the makers as their guiding thoughts and intentions.

V. 6. בלב כל חכם לב נתתי חכמה. On this phrase our sages found their belief that אין הקב״ה נותן חכמה אלא למי שיש בו חכמה, God only grants wisdom to those in whom wisdom is already innate, as, indeed it says also in Daniel 2,21. יהב חכמתא לחכימין ומנדעא לידעי בינה (Berachoth 55a), God only uses as an instrument for His Divine Wisdom one who already has, and has developed from himself, the ordinary human gift of wisdom. Jewish Truth knows nothing of that miracle of God which suddenly makes the simpleton of yesterday into the wise and inspired genius, the man of God of today.

V. 7—8. ואת כל כלי האהל.
