Let us compare places like Ps. 139,16 גלמי ראו עיניך ועל ספרד כלם יכתבו ימים יצרו ולא (ק׳ ולו) אחד בהם “Thine Eye saw my yet unformed being, and in Thy book is written all the days fixed for (their) formation, even if not one of them has yet actual existence”, or if we take the קרי when the לו would refer back to גלמי: — “Thine Eye saw my yet unformed being, and when they were all inscribed in Thy book for the days fixed for formation, it, too, had one of them ascribed to it,” and Ps. 69,29 ימחו מספר חיים ועם צדיקים אל יכתבו “May they be blotted out of the Book of the Living and not be written down with the righteous ones.” Or the related verse in Ps. 56,9, נדי ספרתה אתה, שימה דמעתי בנאדך הלא בספרתך, “My waverings hast Thou booked, grant my tears also a place in Thy flask, are they not too in Thy booking”, or Malachi 3,16, אז נדברו יראי ה׳ איש אל רעהו ויקשב ה׳ וישמע ויכתב ספר זכרון לפניו ליראי ה׳ ולחשבי שמו וגו׳ “Then they that feared God, consulted one with another, and God hearkened down and heard and a book of remembrance was written before Him for them that feared God, and that thought upon His name; and they remain Mine, saith God, etc.” From these quotations we think we are justified in saying: If everything that exists, gets its existence from the “word” of God, and everything that occurs, does so at the “word” of God, then all these creations and all these occurrences are considered as the contents of a “book” of God. The whole world-plan which God carries out as the world-history can be described as the “book” that God had written beforehand, the contents of which He brings to maturity by His direction of the world in the course of time. In this “book” then, all those men would be inscribed, whom God uses as the tools for carrying out His plan. But in this book too, a place is found for every person, who, in the limited sphere of his individual life and with the limited powers at his disposal, lives his life in faithful service of his God. In this book no honest tear, no honest deed, yea, as Malachi teaches, no true thought is unrecorded. In this book the existence and deeds of a Moses have surely not the last place. “Blot me out of the book that Thou hast written”, accordingly means nothing else but: cancel me out of the number of those whose existence is of importance to Thee, take away the future that Thou hadst ascribed to me in Thy world-plan.

V. 34. ועתה. This ועתה in opposition to the ועתה of Moses. You think that there is only one future possible for you, if the sin of the people is not “lifted up”, removed as if it had not occurred. You have to enter a future on the base of the sin being not yet atoned for — a future which has to raise the people to a higher standard by passing the most testing experiences of trying events, and so attain atonement. A complete forgiveness, a lifting-off of the sin, making it as if it had not occurred (נשא) would imply that the people were already back to the stage of moral elevation at which they were when they received the Torah, when it was promised that the observance of the Torah would bring about the direct evidence of the direct presence of God as Leader in their midst, that, ועשו לי מקדש ושכנתי בתוכם was accomplished, that ושכנתי בתוך בני ישראל והייתי להם לאלהים וידעו כי אני ה׳ אלהיהם אשר הוצאתי אתם מארץ מצרים לשכני בתוכם (XXIX,45, 46) was realised. This direct proximity to God presupposes a purer degree of national life and national feelings, and this the people had forfeited for the present. For the present, what was granted, was the further existence of the nation, and the acquisition of national independence on their own promised land. “Lead them thither,” הנה מלאכי ילך לפניך. Just what kind of Divine guidance was assured by this, we can learn from Abraham’s words to Eliezer, Gen. 24,7, ה׳ אלקי השמים וגו׳ הוא ישלח מלאכו לפניך וגו׳. It is the invisible direct guidance of God, which makes things happen so that circumstances become favourable for human purposes to be accomplished. These helpful circumstances themselves are the “angels”, the “messengers” of God. This was the degree of God’s guidance which the Patriarchs enjoyed. In their experience the particular dispensations which are expressed by the name ה׳ did not manifest themselves (see VI,3) ושמי ה׳ לא נודעתי להם. But this was not the manner of the Divine dispensation which was to commence with the entry of Israel into the world as the nation of God, which was to be a revelation of God, and of the elevation of human existence through Him. וביום פקדי: the opposite, (to מלאך I.L.) the immediate direct guidance of God is here expressed by פקד which was the key-word used for the government of God which was to begin with the redemption from Egypt: פקד יפקד אלהים אתכם and which occurs once only in the lives of the Patriarchs at the ability to bear and become a mother which was sent to the ninety-year-old barren Sarah, וה׳ פקד את שרה. Here it says: If at this stage, I were to intervene and again direct their future by My direct government, I could only help them to כפרה by decreeing the fate that their sin demands. At the moment, the direct proximity of My love could only show itself in punishment, as immediately in the following verse.

V. 35. נגף, a fatal thrust, related to נקב puncture. It is the verb of מגפה, sudden death. It is a higher degree of נגע which literally means “a touch” and which is the expression for plagues sent by God; the victim is “touched by the Finger of God”. — אשר עשו וגו׳ see note on V.1. According to Yoma 66b it was those who had publicly taken part in the worship of the calf, but who, either through lack of having had express warning, or through the modified degree of their sin, i.e., עדים בלא התראה (in the presence of witnesses but the witnesses did not actually warn them. I.L.) or גפף ונישק (embracing, kissing, etc. of the calf but not actually bringing sacrifices to it. I.L.) were not legally liable to the extreme penalty of human justice as carried out by the Levites. As their participation was notorious and done in public, their sudden death showing itself as the Finger of God, proclaimed itself as revealing the proximity of the love of God, healing the national body by His judgment.

V. 1. That which was indicated in V.34 above in the reply to Moses’ petition is now given here with further particulars, as a separate command. — העם אשר העלית, still in the sense of the nation’s sin, and emphasized here, as henceforth the guidance through His “messengers” is to take the place of God’s direct leadership.
V. 2. The ושלחתי is the further working out of the idea הנה מלאכי ילך לפניו. Perhaps it means to say: I shall so pre-arrange events that you will find the land left empty for you.

V. 3. Verse 2 is in parenthesis, and this verse (3) continues the idea started in V.1. But אל ארץ זבת וגו׳ is the beginning of a fresh verse and כי לא אעלה וגו׳ is the reason for this, and not for ושלחתי מלאך. The meaning according to Siporno is: — You must go into a land that produces food in a natural way, for here in the wilderness you can only be fed by the special miraculous power of God, and for this direct leadership you have proved yourself to be still immature, and you would not be able to stand His proximity. The wandering in the wilderness necessitates the complete surrender of one’s self to God, necessitates having the full conviction that all one has to worry about is carrying out one’s duty, and that one can leave all the rest to God, necessitates having the conviction that just doing one’s duty, keeping the Torah, is the one and only bond that joins Man to God, and raises him, on the eagle wings of God’s direct care and guidance, high above the ordinary conditions of human life. To feel that one lacked nothing, that one can be quietly confident that God is there if we keep His Torah in our lives, that was the test with which Israel was tried on Horeb, and at which they failed. That was why they had to be brought down again from the loftiness of being borne on the eagle wings of God’s direct care, down to the ordinary earth level of ordinary human physical existence, פן אכלך וגו׳, see on V.5.

V. 4. That the people took these tidings of an easy entry into the Land without trouble or fighting as “bad news”, as a דבר הרע because it told them at the same time that it entailed the loss of the spiritual proximity of God, and of His Self-revealing mastery of this world, showed after all what deep feelings, what consciousness of their calling was, in spite of their grave lapse, innate in Israel. The deep grief into which they were plunged by this news showed in truth what little consolation they found in the prospect of material riches and plenty, and was the first important step towards their re-elevation to spiritual heights.

ולא שתו איש עדיו עליו. “And no man put on his ornament”. It is not said what kind of an ornament this was. That it was a real concrete ornament which could be put on and taken off is quite clear from the context. If one takes מהר חרב in V.6, to mean that they had received this decoration at Horeb, it must refer to some special decoration and not to decorations and jewellery in general. We venture a suggestion. There is only one object that is decribed to us as a national decoration. It is called טוטפות “forehead ornament” (Ex. 13,16), and quite simply פאר “ornament” (Ezekiel 24,17) and moreover, it is taken off as a sign of mourning. Should we not take it, that it is this one Jewish national ornament which is referred to? They received תפלין immediately at the exodus from Egypt. קדש and והיה כי יביאך informed every Jewish man of his calling to be dedicated and consecrated to God. It consecrated every Jewish arm and every Jewish brain to this calling, decorated the arm and head of every Jew with the emblem and diadem of this calling — a calling which only at Horeb was to receive the details of its nature — and just at Horeb did they realise how they had failed to live up to this calling which had been given them with their exit from Egypt. Is anything more natural than that the feeling of grief when they realised their spiritual and moral immaturity prevented them from putting on this emblem? The מֵהר חרב would then mean “from”, in the sense of “from the time of” or causative, “because of Mt. Horeb”, as in Hosea 12,10 אנכי ה׳ אלהיך מארץ מצרים. Mt. Horeb, which was to have given their calling its right and full conception, Mt. Horeb robbed them of this calling. This meaning of עדיו would also explain what otherwise seems surprising viz., that God says in V.5, הורד וגו׳ after they had already left the “decoration” off, as well as the repetition in V.6, ויתנצלו, that they did not put it on. For if this decoration was something which they had been commanded to put on: תפלין, then we can understand that it still required the agreement, the approval from God, that they had His permission to continue leaving them off, and then it is not superfluous to tell us that they had already, of their own free will, feeling their unworthiness, left them off. For it was just this stripping themselves on their own initiative which gave it its value, as showing their own realisation of what they had done.

V. 5. ויאמר in contrast to וידבר of V.1, explanatorily, soothingly. אתם וגו׳ ,וכליתיך: That I make My relation to you and your fate return to the manner in which I guided the fate and history of your ancestors, the בני נח (see Ch. 31,34) is entirely because it is now a necessity for your continued existence. The special relation of God to Israel, and of Israel to God, has a double purpose: to reveal to humanity the guidance and government of God in human history and the affairs of man, and God’s Laws for the behaviour and actions of man. Both belong essentially together. If Israel’s fate, Israel’s history is to reveal the guidance of God, then their life must be a mirror of what the Laws of God for man are. Special guidance and care of God for a sinful people would proclaim sin as the will of God, and would bring about the exact opposite of that which was the object of choosing Israel. The people who are to stand before the world as “the people of God”, must be the pattern of obedience to the Law of God. By reason of the name they bear, every lapse from the Laws of God, would be a capital crime of חלול השם, a sanctifying of evil, of wrong, in the Name of God. The salvation of the Divine Laws of morality for mankind would demand punitive correction of every fault on the part of the people of God. This is the practical application of the principle which is expressed by בקרבי אקדש (Levit. 10,3) regarding the responsibility and danger which are borne by all people who bear the stamp of being specially near to God. It offers a key to the history of Israel, and is given as such by the word of the prophet (Amos 3,2) רק אתכם ידעתי מכל משפחות האדמה .על כן אפקד עליכם את כל עונתיכם
ועתה הורד וגו׳. See on Verse 4.
V. 6. ויתנצלו. See on Verse 4.

V. 7. ומשה יקח, can hardly be taken as the “narrative” future (as יקימו in V.8, and ירד in V.9, etc. etc.). Such “futurum historicum” is only used for events which are constantly recurring. But the removal of the Tent only occurred once. We, therefore, think that we are to take the יקה here as being imperative. It still belongs to the contents of the speech of God to Moses of V.1—3 and 5. Not by his own decision, but by God’s command, did Moses transfer the Tent to a distance outside the camp. Thereby the כי לא אעלה בקרבך was brought concretely home to the people. But inasmuch as God, nevertheless, remained near to Moses for anybody who sought God, i.e., who wished to learn His will, the continuance of a connection between the people and God was indicated; and thereby the hope indicated of the granting of future restoration of the old conditions which had been hinted at by the words ואדעה מה אעשה לך (V.5) (for I would know what I have to do unto you. I.L.).

V. 9—11. Neither God, nor anything Godly, lived in the Tent. Moses lived there and so his attendant too remained always there. He was there as נער, as one who had yet to become a man. The presence of God did not attend on him there. Only when Moses entered the Tent did the cloud which announced the presence of God, descend on it. From Deut. Ch. IX and X we learn that Moses spent three periods of forty days before God, twice to receive the Tablets of the Law (IX,9 and X,10) and once in the interim between the two, to achieve pardon for the sin of the golden calf (IX, 18). Regarding these middle forty days it does not state that he spent them on the Mount but ואתנפל לפני ה׳, he spent forty days fasting and praying before God. We accordingly think that these middle forty days were spent in the Tent outside the camp. Then the narrative remains in quite chronological order. On 17th Tamuz the Tablets were broken. On the 18th the destruction of the calf and the execution of the guilty took place. From the 19th Tamuz till Ellul 1st all that is related from Ch. 32,10 till XXXIII,23 occurred. These were the forty days which were taken up with Moses’s efforts to regain the complete grace of God for the people. And פסל לך Ch. 34,1 was said on 1st Ellul, on which day Moses ascended the Mount again, to come down again on 10th Tishri, to bring to the people, with the second gift of the “Evidence of the Torah”, the pledge of the regained Grace of God. We only have to allow that the words ואתנפל לפני ה׳ כראשנה ארבעים יום וגו׳ (Deut. 9,18) need not exclude the possibility (also an extremely likely probability. I.L.) that during these forty days Moses went back into the camp from time to time to keep an eye on the people, and instruct and advise them, to which then the coming and going reported in V.8—10 would refer.

V. 12. At no part of the Torah does translation and explanation have to tread with greater care and diffidence than at the contents of V. 12—23. For here we are led to the extreme limit of Man’s knowledge of God, and even that which lies beyond this limit is intimated to us, for the purpose of letting us know just this boundary-line, beyond which the degree of our actual knowledge of God can not extend during the period of our life here below. How fearful must we be that our attempts at understanding and our efforts at putting this understanding into words, will miss the exact point of the truth, and fail to convey exactly what it is meant to do. We shall accordingly attempt to reproduce only that which the actual words of the text and the context seem to offer.

ראה אתה אמר אלי. By the mission which had been given and explained to Moses in V.1 et seq., he and the people — at least, it seems to us that it can not be taken otherwise — were relegated back to that manner of the guidance of God which He employs invisibly and indirectly from afar, similarly to that given to the Patriarchs down to the time of the Redemption in Egypt. God had promised that He would arrange matters beforehand so that they would be able to take possession of the land — ושלחתי לפניך מלאך — but had made the whole actual leading of the people up to this end, up to it, over it and beyond it, Moses’ task, thereby throwing him entirely on his own resources, on his own innate powers of knowledge and action. This complete relegation of Moses to himself is what is expressed, we think, by ואתה לא הודעתני את אשר תשלח עמי “Thou hast indeed told me what Thou wilt send in front of me, to overcome the forces that oppose Israel from without, but Thou hast not told me what Thou wilt send with me, to support me further in leading and guiding the people.” Thereby hast thou left me entirely to myself and my own initiative.

ואתה אמרת וגו׳, and Thou hast said thereby that Thou hast “known me by name”, i.e., by entrusting me with such a mission Thou hast indicated that Thou hast raised me personally up from amongst the rest of mankind for Thy special purposes, וגם מצאת חן וגו׳ at the same time, that, by my behaviour up to now I have shown myself not altogether unworthy of Thy satisfaction with the gifts and abilities with which Thou hast provided me (see notes on Gen. 6,8). For in giving me such a commission, to be carried out purely by my own personality, Thou hast justified me in assuming that Thou hast found me worthy of being equipped with all those great spiritual gifts that I shall certainly require to accomplish such a mission.

V. 13. ועתה וגו׳. And now, to be able to lead this people in the immediate future according to my own acumen, I require, first of all, a cognizance which I still lack. I require a knowledge of דרכך וגו׳. It does not say דַרכֶּךָ nor דְַרָכֶיךָ but [[illegible]]דְַרָכֶךָ the diversity of the ways of God in their uniformity. I lack the understanding of how, in the manifold diversity of all Thy ways, Thou still followest the one same goal. In this special instance: how, in the now apparently altered leadership of the people, Thou hast not given up Thine original intention towards them, but surely wish to see this one goal pursued and reached also on this different path. But I require this insight into the “uniformity of the multiformity” of the ways of God, ואדעך, so that I remain clear as to Thine intentions, למען אמצא וגו׳, so that I can go on showing myself worthy of Thine approval, so that I can justify the trust which Thou hast placed in me, and can accomplish the mission that Thou hast given me, which can be no other than to lead this people in accordance with Thine intentions. וראה וגו׳, just as above ראה אתה וגו׳: And this request, which the consideration of the mission entrusted to me has emboldened me to make, I am also basing on the consideration of the calling of this people, הגוי הזה. This nation, even as it stands now, in the presence of its sin, is, after all, and remains after all עמך, is, after all, and remains, after all, the community that Thou hast made into a nation, and whose calling to be Thy people Thou hast proclaimed when they were made into a nation, ולקחתי אתכם לי לעם (see Ch. 32,11). Thou knewest their failings when Thou chosest them. In spite of their imperfections which have now become apparent, surely the purpose for which Thou hadst designed them is not lost. Even in their present altered relationship to Thee, they are surely to proceed towards the accomplishment of this purpose.
I, who am to lead them towards this end, feel that I require an insight into the way to this end, so that I can lead them to this end in a manner which will be in accordance with Thy Way.

V. 14. פני ילכו, as ופניך הלכים בקרבי (Sam. II. 17,11). My Presence Itself will again go with you, i.e., not much longer will you have to carry out the task of leading the people alone on the strength of your own judgment. The deep feelings of grief, which the proclamation לא אעלה בקרבך produced, have already achieved half the object of the proclamation, has already raised the people one step up from their degradation, the degradation which would have made the proclaimed alteration in God’s leading the people really necessary. That פני ילכו is equivalent to אעלה בקרבך or at least to what is perhaps a middle stage expressed by אלך עמכם, is proved by the request V.15 אם אין פניך הולכים וגו׳, which accordingly gives rise to V.16 ובמה יודע וגו׳ הלא בלכתך עמנו וגו׳ where לכתך עמנו ונפלינו וגו׳ is a comment on פניך הולכים. Accordingly, פני ילכו, and nevertheless והנחתי לך (I accede to you, i.e., I comply with your request I.L.). Although the supposition on which you base your request is not a condition which will last for any length of time, as I myself will again take up the leadership in direct guidance, nevertheless I will grant your request, and give you the requested insight into My Ways.

V. 15—16. Moses gives as the reason for his request that there should be no interruption in God’s direct leadership, the consideration that only by such a direct leadership showing complete superiority to the ordinary physical laws of Nature (which is just what ונפלינו expresses) would the world acknowledge, יִוָדַע, that Moses and Israel were sent by God, led by God. This shows that the spreading of the recognition of the Divine origin of the mission of Moses and Israel by mankind in general, outside Judaism, must be an essential aim of the choice and appointment of Moses and Israel. But if it was an essential intention of God to show Moses and Israel in the midst of mankind as being sent by Him and being His people, then mankind in general must have been meant to receive something from the hands of Moses and Israel, the Divine origin of which was to be guaranteed by just this evidence of God’s special care for those that brought it. And this “something” can be nothing else but the Law, the תורה, the Divine origin of which was to be proved and guaranteed by the direct evidence of God in the whole history of Moses and Israel. Here Moses declares the world-wide meaning and importance of himself and his people. A messenger of God, and people of God, are necessary to transmit the Word of God to the world. The history of Israel revealing God is the necessary vehicle for planting the Law revealed by God in the lap of mankind.
V. 17. כי מצאת וגו׳, ואדעך בשם: since I chose you, you have shown yourself worthy of having been chosen, and having been endowed with ever growing talents.

V. 18. We have already repeatedly remarked that כבוד expresses in a spiritual and moral sense, that which כבֶד, weight, mass, is in a material sense. It accordingly describes that which announces the whole spiritual and moral contents of a being, and therefore, used of God, every trace which announces the reality of God. Repeatedly we find in the תורה that וַיֵרָא כבוד הי. If then Moses here begs to be given a sight which up to now has not been granted to him, and which even now, as the following verses show, was not granted to him to the extent, or in the way, that he asked for, then the וַיֵרָא כבוד ה׳ which was granted to the whole nation must be something very different from what Moses was asking for here, and which was not completely granted even to him. The difference can perhaps lie in the degree of seeing. The ordinary term used is always וירא … אל. Now, הֵרָאֵה אל really means: to become visible to somebody, to come out of invisibility for someone. Even the slightest semblance merely indicating the presence of a being, could come under this idea, whereas ראה את expresses a full complete seeing, and that was what Moses asked for — הראני גא את כבודך. And even if we do find this term too, applied to the people, בקר וראיתם את כבוד ה׳ (XXVI,7), הרואים את כבודי (Numbers 14,22), in these places it is perfectly clear from the context that there it does not mean an appearance which proclaims the presence of God, but which proclaims His Almighty power and the special providence of His Divine government, and ראה in both these places is not so much seeing as experiencing (this meaning of ראה occurs repeatedly in Isaiah, e.g., XXXV,2 and LXVI,18, and also in Psalms e.g. XCVII,6). Anyway V.20 and 23 tell us that this request of Moses was for a direct seeing of the personal Being, or at least for something approaching that, similar to the way one recognises a person by seeing his face. Because of the fresh mission which had been given to him, Moses in V.12—14, had begged to be shown God’s Ways in the “uniformity of their multiformity” so that by his understanding the Ways of God, he could teach the understanding of God, and so become qualified to carry on the leadership of the people in a way that would be in accordance with God’s intentions for them, הודיעני נא את דרכך ואדעך למען אמצא חן בעיניך. In V.14, God had promised that He would grant this request independently of the reason on the base of which Moses had thought he was justified in daring to make it. But, by this, God had promised Moses an enrichment of his spiritual knowledge, not because of his special necessity for it, but for his own sake, and out of this Moses could derive the hope that God would not refuse to grant him the very highest degree of the knowledge of God that it is possible for a human being to attain. He accordingly renews his request, but now makes it for a higher degree. His original request was for an understanding of the ways of God, so that he could get an understanding of God, הודיעני נא את דרכך ואדעך, now his second prayer raises his wish for the direct understanding and knowledge of God, out of which then, the understanding of His ways would follow by itself and moreover, for the knowledge itself on the higher stage of direct perception, הראני not הודיעני, which compares to that degree of knowledge as ראיה does to ידיעה.

V. 19—20. The answer to this request is given to him in two sentences. V.19 tells him what will be granted, V.20 what must be denied to him. The higher stage of understanding and knowledge, intuition, is granted: על פניך וקראתי וגו׳, אני אעביר וגו׳ he will get not words only, but a view too. He will actually see, and while he is being shown, the word of God will explain the meaning of what he sees. But what he is to see is nothing other than to which his first request referred, the ways of God, in the uniformity of their diversity. This uniformity which is fulfilled and occurs uniformly in every part of all the manifold diversity is called ,”טובי״ טוב ה׳, God’s “Kindness, Goodness” as חטאות נעורי וגו׳ למען טובך ה׳ (Ps. 25,7). טוב, good, is essentially a relative idea, in itself it is that of which well-being and happiness consists, but this well-being, this happiness itself is dependent on the characteristics of the particular individual whose happiness is to be achieved. Inasmuch as God will make כל טובו pass before Moses, Moses is to see the whole manifold diversity of the ways in which the one constant uniform goodness of God is given to His creatures, especially to His human creatures. For it is just the diversity of the natures of human beings, brought about by their having been granted freedom of will, that makes such a diversity of ways necessary in God’s methods for achieving their true well-being. To the ordinary eye these methods seem to be of a contradictory and contrasting diversity. The eye of Moses is to see the underlying uniformity in all this diversity, this highest harmony of all harmonies, not merely to get an idea of it, to grasp it, to understand it, but actually to see it, אעביר כל טובי על פניר and simultaneously with his seeing it, God will explain in words that which he is being shown, וקראתי בשם ה׳ לפניך. This could be taken in the same sense that we took the phrase קרא בשם ה׳, in the case of Abraham etc., viz., God will teach him how to put into words that which he is to see, so as to proclaim God to men. And actually in the Gemora (Rosh Hashana 17b) the carrying out of this promise is described as follows:— אמר רבי יוחנן אלמלא מקרא כתוב אי אפשר לאמרו, מלמד שנתעטף הקב״ה כשליח צבור והראה למשה סדר תפלה, God taught Moses how human beings are to make Him known to themselves. But, in all other places (referring to Abraham, and elsewhere I.L.) where it means proclaiming to men the Name of God (i.e., the meaning, the nature of our Jewish conception of God I.L.) בשם and ה׳ are joined together by the accents. Here, however, and in Ch. 34,5, בשם is joined to קרא forming one verbal phrase, of which verb ה׳ is the object. According to that, here it would mean: “I will proclaim God before you by name, or, what would have the same meaning, will name the name of God before you, the whole sentence reading: I will make the whole diversity of My uniform goodness pass before you and bring to your understanding every nuance of this diversity by a special Name of God, which is appropriate to it. וחנתי וגו׳, before your very eyes will I exercise My חנינה and רחמים. I will let you see how differently, in different cases, My חנינה and רחמים work according to the special characteristics of the one to whom I am granting them. I will not only show you how My one uniform goodness manifests itself diversely as רחמים, חנינה etc. etc., but how even the same manifestation has again divers shades of difference according to the different individuality of the receivers. You are to learn how specified and individual My guiding care is. It is just this specialised individual application of God’s Goodness, that God’s חן works differently according to את אשר יחון, His רחמים according to את אשר ירחם which escapes the insight of mortals who can only realise the general trend of conditions, but to which the true nature of any individual remains a closed secret. That is why we err so easily in judging the “ways of God”, and forget that where to our judgment it seems צדיק ורע לו or רשע וטוב לו we not only can be mistaken in our estimation of צדיק ורשע, but certainly lack the ability to be certain in any given case to state with any certainty what is רע לו or טוב לו. Only the deepest insight into the true nature of any individual can be sure what in real truth is רע or טוב. Looking at it this way both the views given on this matter in the Gemora (Berachoth 7a) can be correct. Rabbi Jose thinks that the solution to this problem (צדיק ורע לו וגו׳ I.L.) was given to Moses, whereas Rab. Meir says that even to Moses it remained unsolved. For even if God showed him the answer by letting him see the specialised individuality meted out in His conduct of affairs, as lies in the words וחנותי את אשר אחון וגו׳, nevertheless the limited human insight even of a Moses is not able to judge the conduct of God in every specified case.

Of all the thirteen nuances in which the one “goodness” of God manifests itself (Hirsch elsewhere compares it to the one white light breaking up into the seven coloured rays of the spectrum, each is different, yet all are still rays of light. I.L.) here only חנינה and רחמים are mentioned. They are the commonest and most comprehensive. חנן (related to הנן, ענן) literally to bestow, to endow with powers, abilities, and means, is the first in time, the earliest of the relations of God to a creature. To it, it owes its existence; fundamentally חנן is “to allow to be”, to grant a future to a creature; and רחמים is the second, — henceforth never to be lost — that accompanies the creature which has come into existence through God’s חנינה, throughout all the phases of its existence, that never gives it up, just because it was the source of its existence, because it had been the רחם, the “womb” of its existence, and therefore remains the “protecting and maintaining womb” for its whole existence. That is why everywhere חנון precedes רחום, and in places where רחום comes first, as in Ch. 34,6; Ps. 86,15, and CIII,8, it only designates a regranting of חנינה.

That what was promised here and carried out in Ch. 34,6 was only a response to Moses’ first request הודיעני נא את דרכך is evident from Ps. 103,7 and 8, where the revelation granted to Moses in Ch. 34,6 is referred to in the words: יודיע דרכיו למשה וגו׳.
V. 20. V.20 gives the reason for not granting the request, because its nature lies beyond the border-line which is drawn as the highest possible attainment of the human mind here on earth.

V. 21. ויאמר ה׳ וגו׳. We can almost say that the answer contained in the two preceding verses was given with didactic composition, first the positive which was to be granted, and then the negative which had to be denied, and the reason for the denial. Each in a separate ויאמר, pronunciation of God, offering an understandable reason. — ויאמר ה׳, and then God adds explanatorily: הנה מקום אתי, and — if we understand these words rightly — indicates with these words, in the most pregnant manner, the loftiest height, but at the same time, the limit, to which the human mind can soar, “not to see God, but to see the earth and earthly conditions, man and human conditions from God’s point of view”, that is the loftiest height that can be reached by human minds here below, and that, accordingly, is the one goal up to which all men should strive. הנה מקום אתי: One and one only point-of-view exists as the highest goal to be attained by the highest human mind, even for a Moses, only one point-of-view, and that is not to try and get a sight of God, but, elevated by God, and godliness, to look at men and human conditions from a height, next to God, near to God, from God’s point of view, to understand and appreciate all men and all conditions of human life. — “Not at Me, nor up to Me, next to Me is the stand-point you are to take to look at things, place yourself high up on the rock, look down on the earth from the height to get a glimpse of the earth, a glimpse of understanding the mighty guidance of God in human conditions”.
V. 23. אחרי. Thou canst not see Me working, but the traces of My work thou canst and thou shouldst see.

V. 1. The condition for the return to the original direct and intimate relationship between God and Israel is that Israel should again take up God’s Law in their midst as the one mediator for this relationship. As Israel had broken this Law, it is up to them to hand God the blank tablets, and beg that the old Law may be written afresh on the new tablets by the Finger of God. Our transgressions in no wise alter the contents of the Divine Law. God does not modify or reform the Torah to accommodate our weaknesses. Unaltered, the insulted Torah awaits our conversion and return, to give it undiminished and unsullied respect and homage. לחת אבנים, above in Ch. 31,18 it says לחת אבן, they were מעשה אלהים and אבן describes the material. But the material for these second Tablets was to be taken from the physical world. They were to be hewn from existing stones, hence לחת אבנים.

אשר שברת. As it was just in this gracious moment of God’s re-entry into the midst of the people, and in the most supreme moment of grace in his life that Moses was reminded of his act of breaking the Tablets, and, as, moreover these words were not added at the beginning of the verse where Moses was told to replace the Tablets (it does not say פסל לד וגו׳ כראשנים אשר שברת which might be taken as a mild reproach. I.L.) but at the end in conjunction with God’s promise to rewrite them, our חכמים (Sabbath 87a) see in these words an expression of approbation of the act which Moses had done on his own initiative, in his מקנא character, יישר כחך אשר שברת, as much as to say “that thou didst so rightly break.”

V. 2. והיה נכון, ready with the tablets. לבקר ,בבקר, it is repeatedly mentioned that this, the highest revelation that was given to Moses, occurred in the daytime, the time of a clear, wakeful fully conscious state of mind, accordingly, free from that condition of dream-like visions of the night to which certain circles like to relegate all revelation and prophecy. — ונצבת לי similarly ימים רבים תשבי לי (Hosea 3,3).

V. 3. ואיש לא יעלה וגו׳. Even more than at the giving of the first Tablets, now after the proved defection of the people, the Law is to come to the people completely from without. It is Moses who receives the Law afresh so as to come to the people with it, and it is he who has to struggle to obtain a home for it, the Torah in the midst of the people (see note on Ch. 34,10, 10). That is why the Mount of God is to appear here in even greater, in complete, isolation. Only God and Moses are to be present.
V. 5. ויקרא בשם ה׳ see Ch. 33,19. It describes the abstract general notion of the procedure, the details of which are given in the following verses.

V. 6—7. ויעבר על פניו ויקרא וגו׳ is the fulfilment of the promise made in Ch. 33,19 viz., אני אעביר כל טובי על פניך וקראתי בשם ה׳ לפניך, see note thereon. Moses’ first request was הודיעני נא את דרכך, “teach me, I beg Thee, Thy ways in the uniformity of their diversity”, and they are to be taught him in the higher stage asked for in his second request הראני, as well as in the simpler stage asked for in the first הודיעני. Both are granted to him. ויעבר is the ויקרא :הראני the response to הודיעני. Moses had been led to seek the uniformity in the diversity of God’s ways quite specially by the serious event of the golden calf. In this one event God had let Moses see Him governing in a manifold diversity of ways to which Moses sought the key. He felt that there must be an underlying factor of uniformity. The people whom God had picked out בכה גדול וביד חזקה to be His people, to fulfil with them His sworn promise to the Patriarchs, were successively: first Ch. 32,10. ואכלם, to be completely destroyed; then in V.14 וינחם, to be left with just negative existence, after human justice had meted out punishment (death) to the most guilty (V.33, 35) they were to receive indirect care for their further existence viz., מלאכי ילך לפניך, but direct teaching for their betterment, by suffering, ופקדתי עליהם חטאתם and thereby the possibility expressed, in the event of their persisting in sin, of their being completely cut out of God’s plan for the education of mankind, אמחנו מספרי; and then after the beginning of a deepfelt, self-judging change of mind showing itself in the people, a corresponding improvement in the relation of God to the people was visualised, ואדעה מה אעשה לך which was then assured in V.17. In all these variations of God’s relation to Man, He shows Himself in the whole height of His Personal nature i.e., in absolute mastery and freedom, in striking contrast to the physically bound nature of all other powers which human delusion has raised to the status of world- gods, as well as to all the philosophical abstractions into which the no less erroneous illusions of speculation have volatilised the Being of God. Moses sought the uniformity in all this multiform diversity. He had presumed to desire to lay hold of this uniformity, this unity, at its very source, by a direct sight of the Personal Godly Being Himself, so that from this direct sight he could gain an insight into the harmonious uniformity of the apparently divers ways of God’s rule, and government. This a priori knowledge was denied him, but the Divine uniformity in all the diversity of His rule, and the diversity arising from this uniformity, he was to see, and be taught to understand. This is now here shown him and explained to him. What he actually saw remains unknown to us, but the words, the “Names”, by which that which he saw was explained to him, are told us. Those we can try stammeringly to follow and attempt some understanding of them.

ה׳ ה׳. That is the unity, the oneness, the uniformity of all the manifold variety of the manifestations of God in His ruling. The Name by which He announced Himself to us after He had completed the creation of the physical world as the “continuing Creator” in the moral world of the history of mankind which He then introduced. In it, this Name, this conception of God, we find uniformity in the manifold and various forms which the manifestations of God’s ruling the world and mankind takes. The manifold variety is brought about by God having given Man freedom of will, hence his ability to err, and the possibility of his losing his way and of his defection in every possible degree in any given phase of the development of the individual and mankind in general. ה׳ remains ה׳! “Ruling the world for the education of men and mankind up to the ultimate solution of the problem of happiness in the future”. This Name gives us a conception, a thought, in the light of which בל טובו, the universal goodness of His ruling for men and of His work for mankind can be presented to us. It is always the same “goodness” always working for the goal of the happiness and salvation of men and mankind, whether it manifests itself as: —
אל, the original fount of all energy, the basic lever of all movement, giving energy and using energy (אֶל ,אֵל) [[illegible]] or

as רחום, Who never forsakes any creature which has been equipped by Him with energy and movement, surrounds it with loving maintaining care, because it is His work the child of His creative love (רחם, the mother’s womb); or

as חנון, never becoming tired of granting anew the energy and powers which had been used-up or trifled away, and of increasing and enriching by fresh gifts those powers which had already been granted and which had been truly used (ענן :חנן the fructifying dispensing cloud); or

as ארך אפים, Who has patience, is forbearing and gives time for the powers which He has granted, and grants again and again, to bear the intended fruit of moral development of life — Who gives patient consideration to the moral weakness — which are just what give the possibility of moral greatness — of those of his creatures who are called upon to give free-willed obedience. Who has pleasure in waiting and waiting until the godly freedom in Man has gained the upper hand in the fight against the temptations of the senses, and in this expectation keeps up even those who are still ignoble and incomplete with His strength-giving, never ending, maintaining love (ארך אפים, see Gen. 2,7; Ex. 15,8); or, where the gifts granted expand faithfully in accordance with the object for which they were given,

as רב חסד, Who appears so infinitely rich in furthering the efforts, in fulfilling the desires of those who are striving and desiring in the right direction; Who shows Himself so רב, so great, so rich just in devoting His love to giving satisfaction and happiness to any of His creatures: Who shows Himself so inexhaustible in variety, giving to each one his own particular kind of satisfaction and happiness (חסד love, the complete devotion to another, hence also, in Piel, חַסֵד complete surrender, prostitution); or, at the same time

as רב אמת Who nevertheless, in an equally great measure, in the overflowing fullness of His great love still tempers חסד with אמת. Who does not — as humans do in their weakness, let His love run away with the truth — Who knows when to deny the granting of the wish which would endanger the way to the true goal of life, to true happiness, and the denial would further the way to it. Who knows how to mix the most abundant granting of wishes with as much denial as will prevent the receiver of the desired blessing from his apparent good fortune having a deteriorating effect; and in this faithfulness to the educative requirements (אמן ,אמת) of individuals He shows Himself as having such a richness, such a variety of treatment, each separate individual offering his own peculiar problem of education; or

as נוצר חסד לאלפים, Who does not restrict the love He gives to His beloved ones to themselves, does not pour out His blessings on them alone, but grants them the highest of all blessings, that all blessings become a seed of happiness working on a thousandfold in time and eternity. Above all, that goodness itself becomes a tree of happiness and salvation for the farthest thousandth generation; so that the effect of any man’s fate, or that of any nation, is not merely for his own individual self and for the duration of his own lifetime, but is felt by all his contemporaries as well as by the whole future. Only he can begin to estimate the love which is showered on good people, who includes the whole extent of the blessing which God’s Providence allows to blossom out of the lives and endeavours of good people to all their contemporaries, and above all, to their children and children’s children down to the thousandth generation. What is the mere self-enjoyment of an abundance of all worldly blessings, reckoned against the recompensing bliss of such a “root and bud” existence for the future blessing of a line of descendants reaching down to all time. We venture to think that the view of just this particular “way” of God’s dealing, connecting the fleeting moment of a man’s life and work with this endlessness of its effect, was quite specially shown to Moses because it is just the one which above all is designed to teach us diffidence in the narrow view with which we are inclined to judge the ways of God according to just what we see happening at any given time. This may be the reason that this particular “way” of God’s ruling is recommended to our special attention by means of a big נצר) .נ from which נצר, the bud, which closes up the blossom and the fruit seed within itself, to protect and mature it). חסד is both the highest degree of doing good which human beings can accomplish, and the highest expression for the love that God shows to human beings. So that נצר חסד can equally well mean: (a) He allows the good that a man does, to become “buds” of blessings for all his descendants, rewards the highest good deeds of a man not to the doer himself but to his children and children’s children, and just thereby gives the selfless חסיד what to him is the very highest blessing; or (b) He allows His greatest love which a good man has won, to become a “bud” of blessing for all his descendants; God exercises His greatest love in allowing a good man to become a source, a root and “bud” of salvation and happiness to his children and children’s children down the ages. Actually both come to the same thing, and this can be the explanation of a peculiarity which we find in the explanations of our חכמים. They very frequently take the term: חסדי הי to refer to the acts of חסד which men are to do, e.g., in Jerushalmi Kiddushin 6,1, ג׳ מתנות טובות נתן הקב״ה לישראל רחמנין וביישנין וגומלי חסדים וכר׳, גומלי חסדים מנייו, ושמר ה׳ אלהיך את הברית ואת החסד אשר נשבע לאבתיד (Deut. 7,12). Similarly, Jerushalmi Sanhedrin 10,1, referring to וחסדי מאתך לא ימוש (Is. 54,10). So also Midrash Tehillim on חסד אל כל היום (LII,3); Sukka 49b on חסד ה׳ מלאה הארץ (Ps. 33,5), on מה יקר חסדך א׳ (Ps. 36,8), on חסד ה׳ מעולם ועד עולם על יראיו (Ps. 103,17) and others. This way of looking at חסדי ה׳ could have its root in the point of view that only the ungrudging unselfishness of a חסיר is fit for the חסדי ה׳, only such a one would find his richest, most blissful reward in ג׳ חסדים, just in the חסדי ה׳ which transcends far beyond his own enjoyment, his own life. Only a Chanina ben Dossa will be filled with the highest bliss when it can be said of him: כל העולם כולו ניזון בשביל חנינא בני וחנינא בני דיו בקב חרובין מע״ש לע״ש. “The whole world is fed, thanks to the merit of my son Chanina, and my son Chanina, has enough with one measure of carob-beans from one Friday to the next!” (Tanith 24b). Hence only עם חסיד תתחסד (Ps. 18,26), God can only exercise His חסד towards a חסיד, and חסדי ה׳ automatically presupposes חסד on earth; or

as נשא עון ופשע וחטאה Who, for those that are repentant, seeking atonement, and wanting to return, takes away and takes over transgression (עון crooked, not straight. I.L.), rebellion (פשע) and carelessness (חטאה). Who accomplishes for them that wonder of wonders, raising (נשא. I.L.) a sinful act — whether a departure from the straight path through weakly yielding to temptation (עון I.L.), or done in wilful opposition to the Torah (פשע I.L.), or through having become careless in keeping one’s mind alert to the spirit of the Torah (חטאה I.L.) — raising the act above the ordinary laws of cause and effect. (Every wrong done, every sin committed automatically has its effect on one’s mind and person, it makes it easier to do the next, one’s resistance to sin is lowered, and it has its effect on one’s strength and self-confident happiness etc. etc. I.L.). If truly repentant, God promises not only סליחה forgiveness, but כפרה. (The sin will actually become as if it had not been committed, and the natural effects of sin will not take place, the consequences will be “lifted out” of the ordinary law of cause and effect (I.L.); but Who also, on the other hand

ונקה לא ינקה. Who does not free any man from even the smallest of his sins without his doing his part towards it. Who, without honest sincere repentance and determination henceforth to do better, leaves sinners over to the consequences of their deeds, and even the smallest departure from the right path brings unhappiness and misfortune in its wake; or finally,

Who as פקד עון אבות thinks — judges — punishes -— remembers (see on Ch. 20,5) the defection of the parents on the children until the fourth generation, and just as goodness and good men under God’s sway become a tree bearing the fruits of happiness and salvation for descendants right unto eternity, so does unatoned wrong-doing make life harder, and trials more difficult to overcome, for children, but only until the fourth generation; or: who allows the goodness of children to atone for the defections of parents; (see ibid.); — in whichever form of the diversity of this summary of the ways of the government of God He may show Himself, ה׳ is always ה׳, always the God of love, always the one same pure Goodness of God, which in all these various ways of manifestation is always working for the one goal, the education of humanity up to their salvation and happiness.

V. 8—9. That, of which Moses previously had had only a presentiment of its being God’s intention in choosing the “most stiff-necked nation” (Ch. 32,11) had now been made absolutely clear to him. Just as it was their political weakness and abandoned helplessness which made Israel the most suitable nation for the revelation of God’s power to govern human history, so was it the natural innate obstinacy of the race, which made it the most suitable for the revelation of the Divinity of His Torah, by means of which God showed the mightiness of His power of education. Just because it is a stiff-necked people should God wander in their midst, to show on them, on this “hardest” nation, the wonderful educational power of His Torah and of His sway, and forgive them again and again, and go on forgiving them — every pardon presupposes a step towards betterment — until the miracle of the education of Israel shall have become accomplished, and this hardest of all peoples shall have in reality become God’s Own for ever.

We have already suggested on Ch. 20,5 that the mode of God’s rule indicated by פקד עון אבות וגו׳ was one of clemency which treated a degenerate generation with consideration on account of the bad influence of the father’s sins, and waited for this influence to die out, and a return to betterment until the third and fourth generation. The וימהר משה of our verse would confirm this suggestion. The prayer ילך גא ה׳ בקרבנו וגו׳ would then have been called forth by the immediately preceding פקד עון אבות וגו׳. In a similar way Moses appeals to this particular phase of God’s rule, in Numbers 14,18, to attach to it the prayer סלח נא לעון העם וגו׳.
ויקד וישתחו. See Gen. 24,26.

V. 10. הנה אנכי כרת בריח, literally: I establish as absolute, and independent of all external conditions: (See Gen. 6,18). As Moses is addressed in עַמךָ, the אתה and עמָךְ must also obviously refer to him, and כל העם אשר אתה בקרבו to Israel. So that God is here assuring Moses that his activity amongst the people will be assisted by Him to success, by events which will be נפלאות (see Ch. 3,20). That these will be direct creations of God will be evident by their having no connection whatsoever with ordinary physical causes, and indeed אשר לא נבראו בכל הארץ ובכל הגוים the like of which is not to be found in the whole realm of Nature, or in the history of Man. The “mission of Moses” will thereby stand unique and the unparalleled nature, the Godly origin, the unalterable nature — (נורא —) of the Torah which he brought will be vouched for, for all time. A guarantee which primarily is to be used for Israel. For, inasmuch, with this reply, the request of Moses in V.9, is to be granted, in which the present condition of the people has to be considered in connection with the whole future of the nation, and throughout a whole generation, the continuous education of the people up to the height of a complete knowledge of the Divine Torah is contemplated, this Torah must first of all be firmly established in its absolute Divine origin. It must clearly and firmly be understood by the people for all time that the “mission of Moses” was a “בריאה״, a creation of God, in the midst of human history. A creation in its whole nature completely different from all others, and in no ways comparable to what has elsewhere been developed, or will be developed, on earth, as religion, law etc. This “mission of Moses” now comes primarily to Israel and has to prove the Divine certainty of its conquering powers in mastering this “hardest and most obstinate” nation.

V.11—14. The first indispensable condition is, that this “work of Moses on the people” should have no directly contrary influence at work in the nation itself. If we have understood the קמיהם of Ch. 32,25 correctly, the recent defection itself, if not actually evoked, was nevertheless essentially furthered by just such an influence. To this end the nation must be filled with the consciousness of its complete isolation with this Divine Torah. With this Divine Torah in its hand it stands completely alone on earth. It is not that it has one God, and the nations also have a God, it an altar, and the nations also altars, memorials and sanctuary as the nations have theirs too, so that both can exist side by side, both be true, but equally both be untrue. Its God, its altar, its memorials and sanctuaries exclude all others, its God is קנא, and the name of its God, that is to say, the way it acknowledges its God, is קנא, tolerates no other God beside it. More, ,תכרתון תשברון ,תתוצון “destruction of heathenism” in its worship (מזבחתם), its traditions (מצבתם) and its superstitions (אשריו) “is really your mission”. Not only are you not to tolerate the previous inhabitants of the land with their heathen ideas and ways of life, but you are to wipe out all traces of their having been in your land.

אשרה and אשר which in the plural only occurs in the masculine form seems to have been a tree which one imagined to be under the special protection of a god whose presence and influence one believed could be obtained by tending and looking after the אשרה.

If, in contrast to מזבחתם and מצבתם the possessive pronoun in אשריו is in the singular, and so refers back to the collective idea of יושב הארץ of the previous verse, it seems that heathen altars and memorials could be erected by private individuals too, but אשרות could only be sanctified by national delusion. If, moreover as רמב״ן proves on Deut. 20,10, the previous inhabitants of the land were also allowed to continue living in the land, provided they gave up idolatry and accepted the seven מצות בני נח, then פן תכרת ברית ליושב הארץ would only warn against an absolute, unconditional permission to remain.

כי לא תשתחוה לאל אחר. The big ר emphasises just here at the most significant place the contrast to אחד. You are indeed to bow down, more, completely prostrate yourself, but only before אל אחד. But just by that, by completely prostrating yourself before the One Only One, you are to keep perfectly upright before all other powers and forces, there is no other power before which you have to bow.

V. 15—16. The fact that idol worship of the other nations is also expressed by the term זנה shows that the relation in which God wishes to stand to all the rest of mankind, and in which they should stand to Him, is considered in the same picture of intimacy as that in which Israel is described — the state of marriage. They should also be married to God in eternal faithfulness, and their idolatry is also an act of infidelity against God. זנה (a higher degree of זנח שנא), literally, a separation from the one with whom one should be joined in the most intimate union.

V. 17. This Law as well as the laws which follow here, have already been given above as the conclusion of the basic principles of the laws of social life, משפטים. There, as bringing the recital of these laws to a close, they were given prominence as being of such a nature that their observance would tend continuously to keep alive and further attachment to the Torah in general, and particularly stress the idea of the equality of every inhabitant in the eyes of the Torah. Here, at the representation of the almost forfeited Torah, they are repeated, having regard to their special contrast to the ideas of heathenism, and to the particular erroneous heathen idea which had just almost caused the people the loss of themselves and the Torah. “עשה לנו אלהים״, therein it showed itself, as if Man could — and then it would be his duty to — make for himself a god, or something godly, let it be only as an intermediary, as an agent for the protection and guidance of God, as if Man did not stand in direct relationship to God, as if he could, or must, ensure God’s protection and guidance by anything other than by faithful adherence to His Law. It is this idea which this and the following verses oppose. They set Man up in direct proximity to God, and show that Man is not raised up into nearness to God by Nature, or anything pertaining to the earth, but on the contrary, by Nature and the whole world being raised up into the covenant of God by Man. Hence, first V.17, אלהי מסכה וגו׳ You have not to make an image of a God for yourself, not to delude yourself into thinking you have to conjure that which is Godly down to you by means of an image, but rather to raise yourself up to your God, by arranging all your human affairs according to His will. Then V.18 et seq. את חג המצות תשמר וגו׳ when Spring beckons, when Summer ripens the fruit, when Autumn brings the harvest, you have not to celebrate Nature with her gifts, but in Spring you are to celebrate your Spring, in Summer your maturity, and in Autumn your consummation. The manifestations of the life-year of Nature are not to call you to the Temple of Nature, but at each great step of Nature through the year, you are to leave her realm, and hasten up to and into the Temple of the One Only One, Who is her master as well as yours, and Who is more to you and nearer to you than He is to her. Who, through His Torah, to the Temple of which you hasten, is ה׳ אלהי ישראל i.e., did not establish you once for all as He did Nature, but Who is actively near to every coming moment of your life, guiding, leading, protecting, arranging and blessing, and Whose protection for yourself and your land against all enemy powers you gain just by showing your allegiance to His Torah in its Temple. This contrasting connection between the Festivals and heathenism is also expressed in the Gemora, (Pesachim 118a) in the dictum כל המבזה את המועדות כאלו עובד ע״ז שנא׳ אלהי מסכה לא תעשה לד וכתיב בתריה את חג המצות תשמור.

V. 18. את חג המצות, “With the bread of slavery and social degradation in thy hands art thou to celebrate the Festival of thine elevation to freedom and independence.” Just as it was by no exterior material means that you achieved your historical national existence, poor and stripped of everything, you only had yourselves and your children when you were to become free, and only had to give yourselves and your children up to God, for ever, to become saved by Him and Him alone, so is your Festival of Redemption to remain for ever, a renewal of your direct personal relation to God, without any mediator whatsoever. Now, and for ever, you require nothing more than yourself, just your bare self, to find and reach your God, and to be sure of His protection and guidance. אשר צויתך, not even as it says above in Ch. 23,15. כאשר צויתך, here you are not to use your own judgment at all as to what I want, you have to do and carry out that which I have commanded you. The little piece of Mattzo which you eat in accordance with God’s command, brings you in a nearer, deeper, and more intimate relation to God, than all the forms and images and buildings of man’s invention to honour God put together.

V. 19—20. Above, Ch. 23,15, at the conclusion of the first law-giving, the consecration of the first-born is not specially stressed, the ולא יראו פני ריקם which here comes in V.20, concludes immediately the verse on the Mattzo Festival. But here, where, as has already been indicated it is a question of stressing above all that aspect of the institutions which work against the erroneous ideas of idolatry, and especially the lesson which they teach of the direct relation of God to Man without any intermediary, the institution of the Festival of יציאת מצרים is supplemented further by the institution of the consecration of the firsborn. כל פטר רחם לי, “Mine is every physical birth in Israel” so does this institution express itself in this connection. Me, your direct relation to Me, not the grace of the powers of Nature, is what you have to thank for all that lives for you. Coming from Me, and for Me, does your nourishment (בהמה טדורה) flourish, as well as your possessions (חמור) and your family (בכור אדם). Nature does not stand between you and Me, but you stand between Nature and Me. It is according to your behaviour towards Me that everything that flourishes and breathes for you in your sphere, lives or dies, flourishes or withers, dies off, or endures. In בכור it is not just the first that becomes holy, by the consecration of the firstborn, the mother’s womb becomes sanctified to God, together with everything that it bears henceforth. כל מקנך, all your possessions, תזכר, by the consecration of the first male “are brought into remembrance” towards God. — (תזכר is doubly anomalous; it is the predicate of מקנה this is masculine and תזכר is feminine. Further, it is written תזכָר instead of תזכֵר. It seems to us that here we must take the meaning of זכר to be in the sense in which it appears in אזכָּרָה where it indicates that part of the מנחות which was given over to fire on the Altar, and by which, that which the whole מנחה represents, is, literally “brought to remembrance”, i.e., recommended for Divine protection and care. What the קומץ is to the מנחה, the בכור is in relation to the kind of property to which it belongs, and which, by its dedication as being belonging to God, is “brought to the remembrance of God” i.e., is placed under His care. Now, by changing תזכֵר into [[illegible]]תזכָר in the most concise pregnant manner, the object, namely the [[illegible]]זָכָר the male, is indicated, by whose dedication, this אזכרה of the whole of the rest of the property is achieved. But in this connection the rest of the property, the מקנה is considered feminine, just to indicate it as being of a dependent (fem. I.L.) nature, dependent on God, and His blessing of it. In this sense we translate the sentence, (trying to get into the translation all the finer nuances implied in the one word so strangely written תזכר I.L.) “And all your property, being of a dependent nature, shall receive ‘remembrance’ through your dedicating the male that starts the birth of cattle and sheep.”). The word, in the way it is written really expresses: Your מקנה, however great it may be, is weak “feminine” as long as it is not made זָכָר by the אזכרה of the בכור, which is brought home to our minds by the ואם לא תפדה וערפתו of the וכל פטר חמור תפדה בשה .פטר חמור. And all your lifeless property, (חמור, the beast of burden, represents your lifeless property, valuables I.L.) your possessions, only have any value, and can only endure, if they are changed into the life of a “God-following personality” (represented by שה I.L.). Your children, too, (כל בכר בניך תפדה) only belong to you, if they belong to God. (ואם לא תפדה וערפתו, if you do not redeem your פטר חמור, you must kill it, have no use of it at all, to impress upon yourself the same idea, your possessions are not your own, and can only last if they are blessed and protected by God I.L.). ולא יראו פני ריקם, For there can be no division in your life, that you, yourself, your inner self, your life of thought and feelings all belong to God, but your business life, your wealth, your worldly possessions, depend on yourself and other factors and powers, and must be treated accordingly. “When you appear before Me” you must bring with you that which represents all that you have. God does not wish to see you before His presence without at the same time everything that goes to make up your own personality (see on all this, notes on Ch. 13,2, and 11 et seq., and Ch. 23,15).

V. 21. Above, Ch. 30,10, where at the conclusion of the fundamental Torah-laws of social life, institutions were mentioned with reference to their bearing on the principles of equality and brotherhood on which the whole Torah is based, the institutions of the “year-sabbath” and the “week-sabbath” שביעית and שבת, stood at the head. They are the loudest and most continuous proclamation of God being the One Owner of the land and the whole world, out of which the equality of the inhabitants of the land, and the brotherhood of all men, immediately springs. But here, where these institutions and their laws are repeated, but where they are mentioned to stress their bearing on the opposition to heathen ideas, יציאת מצרים is the starting point, as being the great fact proving the truth of the immediate direct relationship of God to Man, and the institution of Sabbath also attaches itself to this idea. ששת ימים תעבוד. “serving, you master the world”, only by subordinating yourself with all your forces directly to God, do you become master of your world, the earth only submits to your working of it if your work is God-serving, and your not working on Sabbath is the acknowledgement that your work is of such a nature. And this God-acknowledging Sabbath — laying yourself and your work at the feet of God — are you to keep even בחריש ובקציר, even when the question of your very livelihood is dependent on your labour. Moed Katan 4a attaches the Halacha that קציר עומר של מצוה דוחה שבת to this verse. Whereas above, in connection with משפטים the institutions of civil rights, שביעית naturally had a first place, here it is not mentioned at all, as here it is not so much the relationship of the Jewish State to God, as that of the Jew himself, which is to be stressed.

V. 22. “And equally so, hast thou to make the חג בכורי קציר חטים into a חג שבועות for thyself”. Thou art not to take the first ripening of the fruit of human bread as a Festival of Nature, but the first ripening of the fruit of human bread art thou to celebrate as a Festival of thine own first ripening, as indeed is the sense and meaning of our counting the seven weeks from the first swing of the sickle over the land which yields us our material independence until the day of remembrance of the receiving of the Torah (see Levit. 23,15). As the חג הקציר בכורי מעשיך (Ch. 23,16) is here, only after the עגל, first called חג שבועות, the meaning of this counting becomes clear in significant sharpness. For it had just been shown in the most depressing manner how much easier it was to accept freedom and land from God’s Hands, than to accept and actively keep His Law from His Hands, and that the freed people on the way to their independence still required seven times sevenfold refining, to work themselves up to be receivers and keepers of the Divine Torah. So that in connection with the context of the chapter this would say: For the blessing of your work in the field you have to thank your work on yourselves, on your own ripening and maturity, your fruit will ripen and mature for you, and only then חג האסיף תקופת השנה. The Harvest Festival is not the beginning, but the end of your cycle of festivals. You must first in Pessach have received your freedom and independence from God’s Hands, first on Shevuoth have received from His Hands the Law of your life, to be able to celebrate at the turn of the year, the harvest for your earthly existence.

V. 23. את פני האדון expresses the nearness and directness of God, more strongly than the אל פני האדון of Ch. 23,17 above, and the addition here of אלהי ישראל also indicates the special, the quite special, relationship in which God stands to Israel.

V. 24. כי אוריש וגו׳. Three times yearly will the fact repeat itself; the fact which is to prove in the clearest and most striking manner the direct relation of God to Israel, and the powerful success of Israel simply giving themselves up to the Torah of God. כל זכורך, as it says in the previous verse, every able-bodied man, every soldier in Israel, will be gathered at the centre-point in Jerusalem, round about the Sanctuary of the Torah, and no covetous enemy will dare to cross the border into the rich unprotected land lying open before him. Israel’s land will not be protected by an army at its frontiers, but from its central point by its devotion to, and acknowledgment of, God. ולא יחמד, see Ch. 20,14.

V. 25. Above in Ch. 23,18, it puts it לא תזבח על חמץ דם זבחי as from the very beginning already, the offering of the פסח had been regarded as זבח, as a family meal, hence the introduction to it, the killing of the lamb, is called זבוח. But here, the killing itself is regarded in its own independent meaning, as שחיטה .שחיטה is symbolically giving up one’s personality to God, and it is placed as contrasting to, and being the opposite of חמץ which, referred to property, is symbolic of the denial of possesions being dependent on God. In connection with its context here, this is what it would express: But you will only then receive this direct special protection of God, if you do not separate the submission of yourself, your person to God from submitting your property, your possessions to Him; that you do not offer up your נפש in the Temple, and for your home and business retain your own imagined control and law. For חמץ in your רשות does not permit שחיטת דם זבחך in the Temple. And, on the other hand ולא ילין לבקר זבח חג הפסח: feeding the fire of God on the Altar with your כליות וחלב, with your activities to amass wealth and earthly enjoyments, itself, as well as the feeding and building up of your family life on the basis of your offering in the Temple (as symbolised by the eating of the פסח lamb in your family circle. I.L.) belong essentially to your offering in the Temple. Your offering is not to be separated from the “feeding” of the Altar and the feeding of your family, nor is your “feeding” of the Altar and of your family to be separated from your offering. The former would make your offering, your killing of the lamb, into a mere destructive act, the latter would imply the possibility of your keeping alive God’s fire on earth, the “feeding” of the Altar, as well as the building up of your family life, without previously giving up your self to the will of God. Above in accordance with the context it says: חלב חגי and, in accordance with the idea of the Jewish State’s moral laws of civil justice which there, is in the foreground, refers to הקטרת אימורי חגיגה (see notes thereon); here, where it is rather the proximity of God to the individual and the family also in their activities in life to amass wealth and earthly enjoyments, it accordingly says זבח חג הפסח and refers to the הקטרת אימורים ואכילת בשר of the פסח. (See תוספות, Pesachim 59b ד״ה ולא עולת חול. But also see מל״מ ה׳ קרבן פסח א׳ ז׳).

V. 26. The whole ענין concludes again with those two all-comprehensive sentences: Every ear of corn in the field, every fruit on the tree, ripens in your land for the Sanctuary of the Torah of your God; and also in eating, the godly-human in you is not to lower itself to the physical-animal in you, but all your physical-animal aspect is to be elevated by you, so that you become humane, a true human being with all the worthiness that that implies. Nature is not the intermediary between you and God, but you are the intermediary between Nature and God! (See note on Ch. 23,19).

V. 27. If, על פי הדברים האלה were to mean, “according to what these words say”, then they must refer to the mode of the setting up of the covenant. And this is not the case. What they refer to are rather the subjects about which — i.e., regarding their becoming established and kept — the covenant had been made. So the על can mean nothing else but “about”, concerning”. But in that case it should say על הדברים האלה as it does above, Ch. 24,8. The addition here of פי, the פי הדברים defines further and more exactly the objects about which the covenant had been concluded, clearly extends them beyond the ideas which are given by דברים. It is not merely הדברים, the fixed written words as they stand before our eyes, on which our ברית with God is to be established, but the full living meaning and spirit of the words as had been explained to Moses before the “letter” had been fixed; and which even after the “letter” had been fixed, was to remain a living thing in the minds and mouths of Israel. This, the full comprehensive understanding of the meaning and spirit of the Torah is what the covenant was built on. The פי הדברים. That which is to be written down are merely notes to refer to, as an aid to memory. (The על כל הדברים האלה above, refers to all that Moses had verbally told the people, and what the people had said to him thereupon, see notes.) So we can understand the חכמים remarking on our verse (Gittin 60b) לא כרת הקב״ה ברית עם ישראל אלא בשביל דברים שבעל פה. Here in our verse both the fixed written word, and the spirit and meaning which was left to verbal tradition, are referred to. Also their further saying דברים שבכתב אי אתה רשאי לאומרן על פה דברים שבעל פה אי אתה רשאי לאומרן בכתב. That the carefully contracted and condensed words and sentences — often just hints — by which the written Word is to act as reference notes for an aid to memory are lost and often lack meaning if used verbally, but just as little can the whole meaning and the whole spirit be conveyed by being fixed in writing. Just let anybody read a written report of the whole eloquent testimony which he so convincingly gave the court. How seldom will he find what he had said completely reproduced in the spirit in which he had said it. The Gemora says even of the official secretaries of the Sanhedrin: אף על גב דשני סופרי הדיינין עומדין לפניהם וכותבין דברי המזכין ודברי המחייבין נהי דבפומא כתבין ליבא דאינשא אינשא (Sanhedrin 35a) “Although two official secretaries have always to be present and make records of the words of the members of the Sanhedrin who speak in favour of the accused, and of those who find him guilty, they can indeed record the actual words of the speakers, but it is the inner heart of the man (which can not be put on paper) which is the true man.” The very phonetic expression of the word כתב, close to קטף, to bend, קטב to kill, גדף to disfigure, but also with כתף shoulders, expresses the idea that although it is a welcome bearer (shoulder I.L.) of thoughts and ideas it is nevertheless, by itself, a danger to the completeness, the life and the truth of the thoughts. Hence, not על הדברים האלה not only on the naked sound of words fixed in writing alone, but על פי הדברים האלה, on what was left for the verbal transmission of the Word, on those which were not fixed in writing, did God establish His covenant with Israel.
V. 28. Forty days from the 1st of Ellul to the 10th of Tishri.

V. 31—32. From the two verses together it is deduced that Moses first transmitted the commandments which had been given him, to Aaron and the elders of the community, and then, in their presence, told them again directly to the people, so that we get the tradition in the Gemora Erubin 54b: that Aaron received each Law four times from Moses, his sons three times, the elders twice, and each individual of the people, once.

V. 33. סוה ,מסוה erscheint in Lautverwandtschaft mit צפה, das sowohl Schauen als, im Piel, einen Überzug über etwas machen bedeutet. Auch סוה kommt rabbinisch als Schauen vor: סוי לבה פרח רוחה (Ketubot 62b nach Raschi) und heißt hier in der Form מסוה eine Decke. Beidem liegt der Begriff zu Grunde: eine künstliche Oberfläche zum Anschauen machen.
V. 34—35. Moses’ modesty would not allow him, except when he went before God, or when he had to speak in the name of God, to show himself with the skin of his face radiant.

V. 1. With the return of the “Tablets of Testimony”, that pledge of the special “presence” of God in Israel, the erection of a home for this testimony again became pertinent. The serious events which they had just lived through as narrated in the previous chapter which had made it very questionable whether this mission would have to be carried out at all, have the most far-reaching significance for this mision itself, for the Sanctuary and its purpose. The Sanctuary would now have to be built on quite a different basis, in view of the actual experience. The people and the priests had learnt to know themselves in their state of complete immature weakness, to realise the necessity for incessant work on themselves, and how great was their necessity for elevation and atonement. They had also learnt to know God in the whole weight of His justice and the infinite depth of His grace. From the stage of feeling completely rejected by God, up to the extreme height of regained grace, they had tasted every shade of our relation to God. If then, the Sanctuary which was to be erected was to be the place from where the ideal of what the nation and every individual of it should be was eternally to radiate; and from where at every stage of weakness and error they were to find ever the strength to work up to the height of their calling, and ever the strength to keep up to this height when attained, and for both the assistance and blessing of God — the history of the events which had occurred between the time of their receiving the mission to build the very first Temple and of their carrying it out, made it an historically proven fact for all time, that at any and every degree of falling from it, God’s grace can always be regained.
