But, above all, it is of important significance to consider, that this experience which preceded the building of the first Temple, occurred, that the very greatest national crime was committed, and the highest grace of God was regained, without Temple and without offering. If the truth that Temple and Offering do not in themselves bring about the grace of God, but are only to be, only wish to be, means of showing the way to gain the grace of God, if this truth requires any proof, the proof lies to hand in the most striking manner in the whole history which is deeply interwoven in this experience which preceded the first building of the Temple.

אלה הדברים וגו׳: As in V.4 the orders for the building of the Sanctuary are introduced again by זה הדבר אשר צוה ה׳, the אלה הדברים וגו׳ of this first verse can only refer to the building solely with reference to the immediately following repetition of the law of Sabbath. It would want to teach that even to further this building — directed and commanded by God Himself though it be — the Sabbath may not be broken (see Ch. 31,13). From this, of course, we can derive that all the activities necessary to further the construction of this building constitute that which is included in the idea of a prohibited מלאכה on Sabbath. If now we compare this introductory sentence of the warning against breaking the Sabbath laws for the building of the Mishkon, with that introducing the orders for the building itself, we note that there in V.4 it says’ זה הדבר אשר צוה ה׳ but here in our verse 1: אלה הדברים אשר צוה ה׳ לעשות אותם, there singular, here plural, and the plural quite specially stressed by repetition: אותם, not אלה הדברים אשר צוה הי לעשות but לעשות אותם. There, the building is regarded as a whole complete work to which all the required objects and activities are subsidiary as parts to the whole. But here, at the introduction of the Sabbath laws, attention is drawn to the plurality of objects and activities required for the building. We are required to note the separate things אלה הדברים and the activities required for each one of them לעשות אותם, thereupon to tell us ששת ימים תעשה מלאכה וגו׳, that any one of these activities may only be undertaken during the six days of the week, but not on the Sabbath. Thereby each single one of the activities required for the erection of the Mishkon is constituted a desecration of the Sabbath. The Gemora, expressing the Halacha, refers to our verse: לפי שנאמר ויקהל משה וגו׳ ,אלה הדברים וגו׳ ,ששת ימים תעשה אלו שלשים (=36. I.L.) אלה (=1. I.L.) הַדברים (=2. I.L.) מלאכה וגו׳ ,דברים ותשע מלאכות שנאמרו למשה מסיני (Sabbath 70a and 97b) and reckons up thirty-nine productive activities at the building of the Sanctuary, the doing of any of which would be a forbidden מלאכה on Sabbath. The building of the Mishkon, if not from the point of view of Art, still surely from the point of view of the idea and the purpose to be realised by the idea ועשו לי מקדש ושכנתי בתוכם is the very highest conceivable plan for human artistic activity. The mastery of Man over matter, in getting, producing, changing, manufacturing the raw materials of the world, attained its highest meaning in the Temple. The world submits to Man, for him to submit himself and his world to God, and for him to change this earthly world into a home for the Kingdom of God, to a Temple in which the Glory of God tarries on earth. The building of the Temple is a sanctification of human labour, and in the context here, it is represented as being a combination of all those creative activities of Man, by the cessation of which, — by שביתה from all מלאכה — the Sabbath is made into an acknowledgment of man’s allegiance to God. Each kind of activity which came to be used for the building of the Temple is made thereby into an אב מלאכה, a heading for a category of that kind of מלאכה, which includes many creative activities of the same basic idea, as תולדות, as derivatives of that idea. For instance זורע ונוטע form an אב, a category of productive activities, under which are listed activities such as זומר, pruning trees, watering plants and all acts of furthering growth, as תולדות (Sab. 73b). As our text limits the penalty of כל העשה בו מלאכה יומת to הדברים אשר צוה ה׳, and then stresses לעשות אותם, the intention must be not only לעשות, to do the act (which would exclude דבר שאין מתכוין I.L.) but לעשות אותם, the intention must be to produce the actual result of the action (excluding שאינה צריכה לגופה I.L.). Only productive, not destructive activities constitute the idea of מקלקלין פטורין — מלאכה — and only, provided it is neither דבר שאין מתכוין nor מלאכה שאינה צריכה לגופה is it considered the full desecration of Sabbath regarding which it says כל העושה בו מלאכה יומת. In all cases reference to מלאכת המשכן is considered (see Tosephoth Sab. 94a ד״ה ר׳ שמעון פוטר). The thirty-nine categories of productive work (אבות מלאכה) according to Sab. 73a, are: — sowing, ploughing, cutting, gathering (making into sheaves or heaps in fields, orchards or woods I.L.), threshing, winnowing, picking out (chaff from wheat I.L. etc.), grinding, sieving, kneading, baking (boiling or cooking I.L.) — shearing, washing or bleaching, combing (wool or flax I.L.) dyeing or colouring, spinning, chainmaking, loop-making, weaving, splitting threads, knotting (making permanent knots I.L.), undoing such knots, sewing, tearing in order to sew (See on Ch. 20,10) — (the latter, from “shearing”, primarily for cloth-making I.L.) — hunting (i.e., catching wild animals, birds or fish. I.L.) killing, flaying, tanning and salting (pickling I.L.), drawing lines (see Sab. 75b) smoothing (sand-papering or polishing I.L.), cutting (into shape I.L.), writing, rubbing out for the purpose of writing (see on Ch. 20,10) — building, demolishing (for the purpose of building see Sab. 31b) — kindling fire, extinguishing fire, (to relight, see ibid.) — “giving the last tap of the hammer” (expression for putting the last, final, finishing touch to complete any work) — carrying from one domain to another. If we look into all these categories they all have the common quality of being actual constructive or productive activities i.e., such by which the object becomes changed, and by the intentional work accomplished, Man’s power and mastery over matter is demonstrated. Hence refraining from exercising this power on Sabbath is a befitting manner of showing Man’s allegiance to the One Only True Master and Creator, to Whom Man in his mastery over matter and apparently creative powers is only a leaseholder, a servant. Even the gathering together and heaping up of the products of the soil, and the catching of a wild animal or fish, although the fruit or the animal is not changed in itself, brings about such an essential change in bringing it out of the free state of Nature into the control and power of human possession, that these acts too, fall under the same basic idea as the others. It is only the last of the thirty-nine, the הוצאה, the transfer of an object from one domain to another, from רשות היחיד out into רשות הרבים or the reverse, as well as מעביר די אמות ברה״ד, transferring an object a minimum distance of four cubits in the public domain, which seems (as the Gemora calls it a מלאכה גרועה) hardly to come under our conception of a productive or constructive activity. It would not appear as a מלאכה amongst the activities which occurred at the building of the Mishkon, if attention had not specially been drawn to it, and not, indeed only to the actual carrying but also to its subsidiary תולדות (see תוספות Sabbath 2a ד״ה פשט). And, nevertheless, just this, in its concrete self, such a “small, weak” (גרועה I.L.) example of a מלאכה, must on the other hand, be of such extreme importance that when Jeremiah (Ch. 17,19 et seq.) in the last days of the Jewish State, had to proclaim that the State would endure, more, would flourish to the greatest extent, if only Sabbath would be kept holy, apart from the general keeping of Sabbath, what he had to demand quite specially was refraining from “carrying on Sabbath”, refraining from הוצאה. “Thus hath God spoken unto me”, so it runs, “Go and place yourself in the gate of the sons of the people, the gate through which the Kings of Judah go in and out, and in all the other gates of Jerusalem, and say unto them: Hear the word of God, ye Kings of Judah, and everybody in Judah, and all the inhabitants of Jerusalem who pass through these gates, thus hath God spoken: For your soul’s sake take care not to carry anything on the day of Sabbath, and bring nothing in, into the gates of Jerusalem, and bring nothing out of your houses on the Sabbath day, and keep the Sabbath holy even as I commanded your fathers. But they did not obey Me, did not incline their ears, and obstinately would not listen and would not accept teaching. Now, if you will earnestly obey Me, not to carry anything through the gates of this city on the Sabbath day, and keep the Sabbath holy, to do no manner of work on it, then it will come to pass, says God, that kings and princes sitting on the throne of David, will pass through the gates of this city, riding in chariots and on horseback, they, their princes, the inhabitants of Judah and the citizens of Jerusalem, and this city will endure for ever. Out of the cities of Judah, from the surroundings of Jerusalem, out of the land of Benjamin, from the plains, from the mountains and from the South will they come, bringing elevating-offerings and peace-offerings, allegiance-offerings, incense and thank-offerings into the House of God. But if you will not hearken unto Me to keep the day of Sabbath holy, and not to pass through the gates of Jerusalem carrying things on the Sabbath day, then will I kindle fire at your gates which will destroy the palaces of Jerusalem and be not extinguished.”

We have quoted this whole passage at length to show what great weight the word of the prophet lays on איסור הוצאה, carrying on שבת, but especially to point out how it does not seem to be regarded as an integral part of the איסור מלאכה in general, but to be an idea which runs parallel to it. According to Jeremiah, keeping Sabbath comprises איסור הוצאה as well as איסור מלאכה, V.22 says לא תוציאו משא מבתיכם וכל מלאכה לא תעשו. If we look for the common idea which underlies all other מלאכות they all show the position of Man as master of matter, of all things of the physical world. But הוצאה is an affair purely of the social world. The whole idea of social life, of living not isolated, but in a community, in a state, can not be represented more fully than by the relation of the individual to the community, and the community to the individual, what the individual has to give to the community and what the community gives and does for the individual, what the individual takes out of his own private possessions and pays to the State, and what he gets back for himself, and finally the furthering of public purposes and needs in the public domain. This is most clearly expressed by הוצאה, by הכנסה מרשות הרבים לרשות היחיד, הוצאה מרשות היחיד לרשות הרבים, העברה ד׳ אמות ברשות הרבים. If accordingly, the איסור of all the other מלאכות expresses the idea that Man subordinates the use of his powers over matter to the will of God, the איסור of הוצאה, may well express the idea of Man’s placing his social life too, under the dictates of the Laws of God. The former is the acknowledgment of God in nature, the latter in history and human affairs. The one places Man’s work in nature, and on matter, under the rule of God, the other, his work in the State under the same rule. And as certain as it is, that the conception of our world comprises both Nature and State, so certain is it that God’s mastery of the world includes both Nature and history; and that the establishment of the Kingdom of God on earth to be built up by recognition of the Sabbath, will only then be complete and real when Man acknowledges and keeps the Laws of God in making the rules for his own working life in connection with Nature and matter, and also his national life of the State. Now, all the better do we understand the two motives the Torah gives for the Sabbath, how בריאת שמים וארץ and יציאת מצרים essentially complement each other. בריאת שמים וארץ is the fact on which God’s mastery of the world rests — as is expressed on Sabbath by all the other מלאכות — the Geula from Egypt, the fact on which God’s mastery of State-life rests — as is expressed on Sabbath by איסור הוצאה. So that איסור הוצאה places the Jewish State, the activities of the individual Jew for the State, as well as the activities of the Government in all affairs of state, obediently under the Rule and Law of God, and we understand how, in the Word of the prophet we have quoted, it was the recognition of Sabbath by איסור הוצאה above all, on which the continuance of the State was made dependent, and its fall proclaimed by desecrating Sabbath just by איסור הוצאה .הוצאה impresses the seal of God on the life of the State; “carrying” on Sabbath wrenches the banner of God from the State and from the social life within the State.

V. 3. לא תבערו אש וגו׳. On the one hand, kindling fire in itself is not a productive, creative, but primarily, rather a destructive activity. But on the other hand, the ability to produce fire artificially is just that which first gave Man his true mastery over the materials of the world. Only by means of fire can he create his tools, can he analytically and synthetically probe into the inner nature of things. We can acordingly understand the two different opinions given in the Gemora (Sabbath 70a): (a) That הבערה ללאו יוצאת, that the special mention of הבערה in this verse out of all the other מלאכות is to tell us that it is only a לאו, that kindling fire on שבת is forbidden by the Torah, but it does not incur the penalty of death with which the other מלאכות are threatened in the previous verse. (b) The other opinion which is the one accepted by the Halacha, is that לחלק יוצאת, that it is mentioned separately by itself as the classic example for all the other מלאכות — in accordance with the basic postulate דבר שהיה בכלל ויצא מן הכלל ללמד לא ללמד על עצמו יצא אלא ללמד על הכלל כלו יצא that what the Torah tells us of any special case taken out of a collective idea in which it was included, is meant to apply to all the other examples of that collective idea. It teaches us that for the whole of the איסור מלאכה on Sabbath that is included in the אלה הדברים וגו׳ of verse 1 the sanctification of שבת repeats itself independently in each one of the forbidden מלאכות, so that if one has desecrated Sabbath by doing various מלאכות — not, of course, intentionally, for one can not suffer death more than once — בשגגה, each מלאכה is considered a separate desecration of Sabbath, has to be atoned for separately, and the gravity of the offence driven home to one’s mind by a separate חטאת. For instance if someone had ploughed, sown, and cut corn on Sabbath, he has to bring a חטאת for each מלאכה-category, i.e., three חטאות. This is called חלוק מלאכות לשבת, and in this, the איסור מלאכה on Sabbath differs characteristically from that on יום-טוב. The Gemora (Mackoth 21b) says יש חלוק מלאכות בשבת ואין חלוק מלאכות בי״ט. On Yomtov the cessation of work is solely the result of the Moed-idea, the עבודת ה׳ to which we are called, excludes and precludes מלאכת עבודה) .מלאכת עבודה is prohibited on יום טוב in contrast to כל מלאכה on שבת I.L.). This single total idea of Yomtov is broken by doing any kind of מלאכה on it. But on Sabbath the cessation of work is the belief and acknowledgment that the ability to “master matter”, the creative productive power that Man has, is lent to him by God, and is only to be used in His service. This belief and acknowledgment repeats itself independently in each single category of the kinds of this ability. If we consider that it is not the number of different kinds of articles produced, but the number of the different kinds of productive activities used, that constitutes the number of the desecrations of Sabbath — if, for instance, corn, grapes and apples have been plucked, only one חטאת has to be brought, whereas if corn had been sown, plucked and gathered together, three would be required — the idea of שבת is to be understood, not so much as laying our world at the Feet of God, but as laying our relation to our world at His Feet.

V. 5. נדיב לבו. We have already remarked on the relationship of נדב to נטף according to which נדב would indicate a “flowing out from within”. נָדִיב is one whose actions arise solely from the dictates of his own inner self, free, independent. Whereas, then, נדיב in itself would designate the free-willed nature of the action, this voluntary nature of the action is quite specially stressed by the addition of the word נדיב לב ,לב and to a still higher degree by נדיב לבו, moved by his own heart. Any and every compelling influence, or even any exterior directing influence is definitely excluded. From this verse the Gemora (Shebuoth 26b) teaches, that for תרומת המשכן as well as for קדשים in general (in reference to which the expression נדיב לב also occurs, Chron. II. 29,31), גמד בלבו אינו צריד להוציא בשפתיו having had the intention, even without expressly promising in words, is binding, whereas for all other vows or promises only the actual spoken word is binding, גמר בלבו צריך להוציא בשפתיו. We can not apply this binding force of the unspoken word, the unspoken promise, from here, from תרומת המשכן and קדשים to all other promises, for if this rule was meant to be an example for all promises it would only mention נדיב לב in one of the two cases, the fact that it is mentioned both with תרומת המשכן and קדשים proves that it is restricted to these two cases only — שני כתובים הבאים כאחד אין מלמדין. It is true that there is one opinion that a rule must be quoted in three separate examples before it can be excluded from general application ג׳ כתובים וכו׳ אין מלמדין. But even then we would not be able to apply it here generally on account of the other rule that חולין מקדשין לא גמרינן, we would not apply what is said concerning vows made to give holy things, to ordinary matters. (נדרי צדקה, vows to give charity, or generally to do benevolent acts, according to Yoreh Deah 258,13 have in this respect the character of נדרי הקדש). The Gemora in Chagiga 10a finds in the sentence כל נדיב לבו יביאה also a proof for the traditional halachic principle of היתר נדרים, dispensation from vows, which, as it puts it, would otherwise be פורחין באויר, be “floating in the air” i.e., would appear to be entirely without any reference in the Torah. But, it says there יש להם על מה שיסמכו. This would also explain the otherwise apparently superfluous suffix in יביאה. Even at the moment of actually bringing it, the bringer is to be נדיב לבו, is still to be completely master over his decision, so that he is not absolutely and irrevocably bound by his vow. If he regrets his vow, even at the moment of bringing it, he can get dispensation from it.
V. 15. Here too, the שמן המשחה appears in close connection with the קטרת (see on Ch. 25,6).

V. 17. את אדניה: everywhere else the feet are referred to as belonging to the pillars, here they are described as being the base of the court, and the חצר, otherwise masculine, here is made feminine. The courtyard forms the point of transition out of the ordinary life of the people into that of the Sanctuary and its character expresses itself essentially in the material on which it stands, the still completely unrefined metal, copper (see on Ch. 22,8). This symbolic meaning is here stressed for the people. All, even those who are still the most unrefined are invited to enter into the Sanctuary, and the חצר is not itself an independent goal, it is a “feminine” place, necessary for the real goal of the Sanctuary and leading to it. So also at the completed Sanctuary in Ch. 39,400 the feet are again referred to as being of the courtyard itself and the חצר again put in the feminine gender, and only in reference to the completely subsidiary ropes is it referred to as masculine.
V. 19. את בגד השרד. See Ch. 31,10.
V. 20. משה. They had been gathered לפני משה, and now went away from the meeting which had been held by Moses.

V. 21. ויבאו וגו׳. Both by the accent as well as in accordance with the ו copul. of the following וכל, this ויבאו וגו׳ is to be taken as an independent sentence. Also נשאו לבו is by no means identical with נדבה רוחו אתו. Whereas נדבה וגו׳ usually indicates the inner urge to give something, נשאו לבו indicates the inner uplift which urges one to do something oneself above the run of one’s ordinary actions. ויבאו וגו׳ seems accordingly to describe the general impression and result which the demand first produced. The purpose of the Mishkon and its whole high meaning was grasped. Everyone who thought he was able to help in any way, by gifts or work, felt himself personally elevated by taking part in a work for such an object. In this spirit יבאו they came and placed themselves, each, according to his powers and abilities, ready to do his part for the work.

נדבה רוחו is also something different and something more than נדבה לב .לבו is used primarily as the organ of thought and will in Man. But רוח is the whole inner Man, the whole inner source of action. The gifts flowed from the whole being of the people, everybody put the whole of himself into helping. ולכל עברתו, the expression עבדה occurs repeatedly in this chapter in a similar connection. It is used in the actual sense of “service” which really is: - to be helpful in carrying out the purposes of someone else, it is literally the German word “zweckdienlich”, but in the sense of the sharp degree of service, so that it expresses an act being not merely of service, but demanded, being required and necessary. See V.24.

V. 22. The ויבאו of the previous verse is here given in fuller detail. Not only the men came but also the women and indeed here the women were in the forefront. For the עגל the women had refused their jewellery. Here they were the first, and the men only appeared in the second rank. They came על הנשים led by the women, as in ועליו מטה מנשה (Numbers 2,20). — כל נדיב לב וגו׳ the preceding verses had described the participation of the people in general, now follows that of the individuals. — חח we find חוח as thorn, כשושנה בין החוחים (Song of Songs 2,2), as a sharp point, ובחוח תקוב לחיו (Job 40,26) and as a means of holding things together וילכדו את מנשה בחחים (Chron. II. 33,11). So that חח as an ornament would seem to be a brooch which serves as a safety-pin to hold a garment together. כומז, the phonetic relation to קמש which, like חוח means a thorn, קמוש וחוח (Is. 34,13) shows the understandable relation of כומז with חח. The further relation to כמס to hide in safety, קמץ to grip together, points to a piece of jewellery which holds things together or keeps them safe — probably a buckle.

תנופת זהב would be a gift of gold metal in contrast to זהב worked gold. Here it says תנופת זהב, V.24 תרומת כסף ונחשת, Ch. 38,24 זהב התנופה, V.29 נחשת התנופה and everywhere else the ordinary term for gifts for consecrated purposes: תרומה. The reason for this change of terms seems worth investigation. Similarly in the sacrifices the term תנופה is constantly applied to the הזה and תרומה to the שוק, always חזה התנופה and שוק התרומה although both movements of dedication, the horizontal (תנופה) and the perpendicular (תרומה) were made equally with both of them. In the horizontal movement of dedication תנופה, the object to be dedicated appears to be in the same plane as the object to which it is to be dedicated. It is already in the direction of its goal, and is given over to the end for which it is destined. The lifting movement of dedication, תרומה, makes the goal of the object to be dedicated, appear high above its present standpoint. The object to be dedicated is elevated by being dedicated. Gold, (see on Ch. 25,8) as the noblest metal, symbolically representing the purest and most refined, finds in the Sanctuary its most appropriate use, hence ,זהב התנופה תנופת הזהב. But copper and silver, (see ibid.) representing the ignoble and the capability of attaining the noble state by refinement, find in the Sanctuary the high goal up to which they are to strive, hence תרומת כסף ונחשת. In the same way חזה התנופה and חזה .שוק התרומה enclosing the whole spiritual wealth of Man finds in the devotion to God and His Sanctuary its most natural calling, hence חזה התנופה. But שוק representing the bodily wealth, the strength of Man, becomes elevated by dedicating it to God and His Sanctuary hence שוק התרומה. If all this is true, it is significant that while joined with silver, copper is called תרומת הכסף ונחשת, but by itself Ch. 28,29 it is called נחשת התנופה. That would then express the profound truth which underlies the whole idea of the Sanctuary, namely, that in its true depth the realm of the Jewish Sanctuary is nothing supernormal, towering above, and denying ordinary life and its conditions. But just as the Altar had to be erected actually on the earth itself, without any space intervening, the Altar of the Torah not on the verdant Gerisim but on the stark bare Ebal, so altogether the Sanctuary of the Torah presupposes the concrete actuality of human earthly life. It is to this that it belongs, it is in this that it is to be realised. Its highest goal and its highest consecration, is at rock bottom, just that which is most natural to the most earthly of earthly conditions. The refining dedication of the ignoble, the תרומה of the נחשת itself is in truth its תנופה.

V. 24. לכל מלאכת העבדה. The whole work of the Sanctuary is called עבודה. It was a task which had been ordered by the Highest Authority, to the accomplishment of which the nation was to give all its energies. The מקדש was what was ordered, and was the purpose which commanded and directed the energies of the people, which accordingly, they had to give as עבדים so that the carrying out can well be termed עבודה, as above in Ch. 30,16, ונתת אתו על עבודת אהל מועד and in Ch. 31,6, לעשות את כל מלאכת עבודת הקדש.

V. 25. בידיה טוו. While the men brought wool as raw material, or spun by others, they eagerly took on themselves to spin, and were happy to be able to do something with their own hands for the work of the Sanctuary.

V. 26. אשר נשא לבן וגו׳. As here the בחכמה is added as qualification of נשא לבן וגו׳ it can not refer to their skill, but characterises the decision to which their hearts directed them. While the other skilled women rushed to work the beautiful materials required for the curtains and hangings, these, their wiser sisters, chose to make the more modest material for the goats-hair covering. This, after all, was the essential part which held the whole together, was the real actual אהל and the making of an אהל is where the quintessence of womanhood is concentrated, so that in this they displayed both careful thought and their sense of true womanhood, their חכמה. Hence also the precise emphasis אתנה. The גמרא in Sabbath 99a and 74b also describes the method by which these women spun the goats’ hair as an unusual and exceptionally skilful one. The hair was שטוף בעזים וטווי מן העזים translating literally “flooded away from the skin of the goats and spun directly from the bodies of the goats”. The שטוף וגו׳ describes a painless separation of the hair from the body by a kind of powerful spraying.

V. 27. והנשאם. In מ׳ רבות נשא (and similarly in the ספרי on Ch. 7,2) it speaks disparagingly of the princes feeling themselves somewhat slighted in their office by the call for gifts being made direct to the people, and accordingly holding back from the נדבה in the expectation that the people’s contributions would not be sufficient for all the work, and they would then, in all honour, step in and make up the deficit. But they had not reckoned on the enthusiasm of the people, so that, in the end, nothing remained for them to contribute except the precious stones for the garments of the High Priest, and the oil and fragrant spices for the incense and the anointing-oil. That such a way of thinking was blameworthy, that, in this highest national task it was most reprehensible for them to feel that their office placed them preferably above the people, and representing the people, rather than as being in the midst of the people, where, as the noblest sons and brothers of the people, their task would be to lead the way in enthusiasm in giving and be the first instead of the last of the givers, is indicated by the defective spelling of הנשאם instead of הנשיאים. In this instance they did not show themselves as the נשיאים of the people.

V. 29. The lack of true national feeling on the part of the princes, on this occasion, indicated in V.27, may explain the otherwise striking construction of the verse: בני ישראל. כל איש ואשה וגו׳, הביאו בני ישראל seems to be in apposition to איש ואשה and stresses the contrast of the spirit in which the whole of the people brought their gifts, to that of the נשיאים. Towards God, and the task He had set them, they all felt themselves as בני ישראל as the completely equal children of the nation, and as such they brought Him their gifts. ועוד יש לומר שמסרום לצבור כראוי.

V. 33. מלאכת מחשבת literally “work of (or resulting from) thoughts” or “the work of a thought”. It is the specific expression which contains the essential nature of all the skilled work of the erection of the Mishkon. Hence it is also the prescriptive standard for the idea of prohibited work on the Sabbath (for which, indeed, the work of the building of the Mishkon is fixed as the decisive norm. See Ch. 34,1). Thereby human מלאכה in its highest power is described as the conscious creative realisation of a thought, by human skill. From this we get the law that for a מלאכה to come within the conception of a prohibited work on Sabbath it must not be done as מתעסק (not actually directed by the mind I.L.) nor דבר שאין מתכוין (unintentionally I.L.) not מלאכה שאינה צריכה לגופה (where the actual product of the act was not what was wanted) not כלאחר יד (not done in the correct skilled manner) and not מקלקל (destructive). (See חורב Ch. XXI).

V. 3. מלפני משה. Moses represented the national community. Each individual brought his gift to him. Thereby מסרה לצבור he gave it over to the nation. Henceforth it was no longer private property, but belonged to the nation, and only and solely out of the national property was the Mikdosh allowed to be built (See Ch. 25,2).
בבקר בבקר. They made it their first business of the day to come with their gifts to Moses.
V. 5. מדי העבדה למלאכה, literally: more than what was demanded for carrying out the task which God had commanded.

V. 6. איש ואשה אל יעשו עוד מלאכה וגו׳ ויכלא העם מהביא. Here the bringing out of the private domain into the public domain is called מלאכה, and herein is taught in Sabbath 96b the proof that הוצאה falls under the conception of prohibited מלאכה on Sabbath (See תוספות thereon).

V. 7. והמלאכה. The “work” which the people did i.e., the bringing of the materials (see previous verse) was sufficient for those that completed the Mikdosh to do so (והותר .(לעשות אתה is in connection with לעשות אותה, as much as ולהותר, it was sufficient to carry out all the work, and to have some left over.

V. 8 et seq. If we realise that the whole Sanctuary was to have symbolic meaning in all its separate parts, but that no object can stand as a symbol if it is not intended and made to be that symbol; if we realise that even the written word, which we should certainly imagine to be so clearly of symbolic nature that it can have no other meaning and automatically carries its meaning in itself, that in its most holy application, the intention of the writer is so essential that a ספר תורה only then has the קדושת ספר תורה if it is written with the intention לשם קדושת ס״ת. More, with regard to the Names of God אזכרות, the intention to write the letters as expressing the Name of God, לשם קדושת השם has to be expressly repeated, or at least be present in the mind of the writer, at the writing of every אזכרה, and the spirit in which the writer inscribes the letters is so necessary to their meaning that a ס״ת שכתבו מין ישרף has even to be burnt — see Yoreh Deah 274,1, 276,2 and 284,1. — If, further, we remember that the realisation of the symbolic meaning of everyday objects — and the Sanctuary consisted of such — which are normally in ordinary use, having their concrete meaning as cupboard, table, lamp, curtains, clothes, etc., requires quite special stress on their being symbolic, then all these considerations make it quite understandable to us, why here from Ch. 36,8, to Ch. 39,32, the making of the Mishkon is described again in all its details, although we know all these details already from the previous chapters, when the commands ordering them, were given. Also that in Ch. 39,33—43 all the single articles are again mentioned when they were delivered, and in Ch. XL the erection is again described of each individual part, and the Torah does not find it sufficient simply to say: - The artists and artisans carried everything out in accordance with the instructions, brought it all to Moses, and Moses erected the Sanctuary as he had been commanded. If we are not mistaken, all this prolixity is meant to tell us that both at the making, as well as at the delivering, and finally at the assembling and erecting, the holy and symbolic meaning and purpose of each and every part which made up the whole edifice was present and vivid in the minds of the workers and Moses, so that each part and the whole was made, delivered and set up in the spirit of its purpose, and so the symbolic character and meaning of the whole edifice and every part of it was vindicated.

עשה אתם. The singular (he made I.L.), here, and in the following verses refers to Bezalel to whom the supreme direction of the whole work was entrusted. We have already remarked on Ch. 32,35 that עשה is used to express not only actual doing but also the directing, ordering and guiding production of a work.

V. 17. החברת השנית as it does not say בחברת השנית we think it must be taken not as a noun but as an adjective qualifying היריעה, (i.e., the other curtain which adjoins it. I.L.). It is also possible, however, that שפת refers to both, and the translation would then be: “on the edge of the curtain of the second group” (of coupled curtains. I.L.).

V. 1. ויעש בצלאל (and not simply, as all along ויעש I.L.). Whereas with all the other objects, Bezalel may have limited himself to more or less simply directing and guiding the other workers, the ארון, the principal object, for which really the whole holy edifice was erected, the ארון was what he himself made, his own actual work.

V. 8. קצוותו, a similar spelling to that used in Ch. 39,4, referring to the shoulders of the ephod which were designed to carry the two shoham-stones. It stresses the plural by the additional ו, for one ו could be taken to come from the third letter of the root, ה (קצה I.L.) but on the other hand allows the plural sign י to be missing from the suffix, and it is just this latter fact which seems to have made the extra plural ו necessary, to avoid the whole word being taken as singular. It seems that in both these cases, the cherubim and the shoulder-pieces of the ephod, the Torah wanted to have the idea of the singular kept, in spite of there being two of them. Even if the Torah guarded in the ארון actually, concretely, appears in a dual, two-sided form, consists of two tablets, nevertheless the two are essentially one, form one unit, and neither is to be given greater importance than the other (as we tried to evolve on Ch. 25,17—20) as is represented by the position of the cherubim and the manner in which their gaze is to be directed (see ibid. I.L.). And in quite a similar manner although the nation appears divided into right and left on the two shoham-stones, before God the nation is nevertheless one indivisible unit, no part of which is to be granted superior importance, as is even more expressly stressed referring to the shoulder-pieces which bear the stones by the addition of חֻבָּל.

V. 16. אשר על השלחן. The קערות which are immediately mentioned were the golden forms in which the loaves were kept from the time they were baked until they were arranged on the Table. They themselves were never actually on the Table, so the על must be taken in the wider sense (as we so often find it used. I.L.) of pertaining to, belonging to, the Table.
V. 22. וקנותם. See notes on Ch. 25,36.
V. 27. על שני צדיו (see on Ch. 30,4 I.L.).

V. 8. במראת הצבאת. To carry out an idea, in material which is appropriate to that idea, is expressed by עשה ב-. So, in Ch. 31,4, לחשב מחשבת לעשות בזהב וגו׳. So that when here it says ויעש את הכיור וגו׳ במראת וגו׳, the shape and the nature of the materials out of which the כיור was made are designated as being as important as the actual raw material itself for the idea which the כיור was to symbolise. It is deeply significant that the vessel of the Sanctuary which was to represent “the moral ‘keeping holy’ of one’s acts and efforts” קידוש ידים ורגלים was made out of the women’s mirrors. Mirrors are articles which lay stress on the physical bodily appearance of people being an object of special consideration. So that it was shown that the physical sensual side of human beings is not merely not excluded from the sphere which is to be sanctified by the Mikdosh, but that it is the first and most essential object of this sanctification. After all, at rock bottom, as Man has complete free will in moral matters, it is just this side of human nature which is necessary to come under the influence of the Mikdosh, if the sanctification of life which is aimed at, is to be achieved. This designation of the כיור emerges with great significance in the laws of סוטה in Numbers Ch. 5,17 (see notes thereon). The wording מראות הצובאות can even be meant to say that the copper mirrors were not melted down but that the כיור was made up of the mirrors fitted together almost without any alteration at all, so that it was recognisable that the basin consisted actually of mirrors. Although, in general, כלי הדיוט should not be used for מלאכת גבוה in an unchanged form, here, on account of the profound moral idea which would be expressed, an exception would have been made. See the remarks of אלי׳ רבה on א״ח 147,1.

V. 17. ווי העמודים וגו׳ והם מחשקים כסף כל עמדי החצר. This repeated insistence on the silver which was on the pillars of the forecourt, seems to wish to stress the contrast to the copper feet, and thereby to stress the symbolic meaning of the forecourt as the place for self-betterment, self-refining. The feet of the pillars were of copper, but the hooks at the top and the garlands as well as the overings of the capitals were of silver, so that not only was there silver at the tops of the pillars but הם, the whole of the pillars themselves, were wreathed around from the bottom upwards, with silver, so that the whole appearance of the pillars represented the upward struggle from the standpoint of copper to that of silver.

V. 21. אלה פקודי. There are difficulties in the several ways of taking the meaning of these words. The most general way of taking it, understanding פקודי to mean, the computation of the gifts received, and the citation of the uses to which they were put. There are difficulties in this way of taking it, but they are surmountable. For both the reckoning up and the information regarding the uses are extremely incomplete. Only the total of the gold and the copper given are recorded. Of silver only the total of that received from the half-shekels of the census is given, but not of that which, according to XXXV,24, came in as free-willed gifts. Of the amounts of the other materials no mention at all is made, and of gold only the amount that came in is given, but no account of the uses to which it was allotted. In addition to all this, there is no other occaasion when we can find the meaning of פקד to be a final reckoning up. Elsewhere we only find it used in reference to numbers of people, and in such connection it has the fundamental idea of פקד: to think. פקודי העדה are all those who are to be thought of under the conception of עדה, whom the idea of עדה comprises, i.e., all those who belong to the community, who, as members, make up the community. According to that פקודי המשכן would be everything that is thought of in the idea of משכן, that which belongs to the משכן, and which essentially constitutes the משכן. This would be all the completed parts and contents of the Mishkon. As they are all summarised under the one designation פקודי המשכן, their essential meaning and importance for the משכן is established, not one of them can be regarded as being unconcerned with the total purpose of the משכן as משכן העדות. It is in this sense that Siporno too, takes the meanings of these words, and he thinks that the total sum of the precious metals spent on this משכן is mentioned, to show how small this total is in comparison to the treasure spent on the later Temple, and yet no other Temple achieved the importance in heaven that this simple modest Temple-Tent reached. In it alone was the presence of the שכינה visibly shown by the Cloud of the Glory of God. It alone never fell into the hands of an enemy. The buildings of the second Temple even lacked that which was the real visible inhabitant of the Temple, the Ark of the Testimony and also the Urim and Tumim. So little does splendour mean to the real nature of the Temple. Let us add too, that the משכן was the only Temple which was established completely out of the voluntary sacrifices and devotion of the nation. At this way of taking the meaning of פקודי it would only be the meaning of אלה which would remain to be considered, which, at the beginning of a chapter, as a rule refers to what follows and not to what has preceded. But this difficulty could be explained by the consideration that in fact really what follows here is basically a continuation of the contents of the preceding chapters. Also in what follows, from Ch. 39,1 et seq., does not deal only with what was made for the Sanctuary, but really forms a continuation of the preceding chapters. So that the אלה stands in the middle of the description of the building of the Sanctuary, and consequently the things to which it refers can be considered also as those which follow. The verse would accordingly be translated: “These are the things which are to be reckoned up for the Mishkon, the Mishkon of the Testimony, which were designed for it at the command of Moses. The care of them became the service of the Levites under the supervision of Ithamar the son of Aaron, the priest”. This last sentence meant that the whole inventory of the Sanctuary was given over to the Levites under the direction of Ithamar. The care of the whole was their responsibility. They became the גזברים, the treasurers. This general appointment of the Levites as a whole, was later on (Numbers 3,5 et seq) given its specific detailed regulations. By this way of taking our verse, the following two verses also fall appropriately into place. At the mention of the total impression of all the various completed works, the two masters are named as whose work the whole may well be considered.

24. כל הזהב העשוי למלאכה בכל מלאכת הקדש, this appears to be a cut-off part of a sentence, as the following ויהי וגו׳ starts a fresh complete sentence. According to the usual way of taking V.21, according to which it is a computation of the gifts received, and a citation of the uses to which they were put that is given here, it could perhaps be explained as follows: Above in Ch. 36,6, the obtaining and bringing of the gifts is described by the terms עשית מלאכה. Accordingly כל הזהב העשוי למלאכה could mean all the gold which was obtained and brought (עשוי I.L.) was בכל מלאכת הקדש, was in the whole work of the Sanctuary, i.e., was used up in that work, there was none left over.

But, nevertheless, it seems that here in הקדש, the אהל מועד is specially meant, in contrast to the חצר, similarly to אדני הקדש in V.27, where quite definitely הקדש must refer to the אהל מועד in contrast to the feet of the forecourt which were of copper. Then, and especially if we accept the second way of taking V.21, the idea of the progressive order in the arrangement of the buildings of the Sanctuary, as symbolically shown by the metals used, would be referred to here. After it has been shown by the idea expressed by פקודי המשכן that every and each part of the “Abode of the Sanctuary” was equally essential for it, they are now shown nevertheless to be graded, and these grades to be characterised symbolically. All the gold was used solely for the קדש; the feet of the קדש, the capitals, the holders and the garlands of the columns of the forecourt were of silver; the feet and appurtenances of the forecourt were of copper. This denotes the horizontal projection of the whole of the Sanctuary in three stages (See Ch. 27,18). This also explains why, in the case of the silver and copper, the uses to which they were put are specified, whereas for the gold such specification is lacking. In the case of the gold it is sufficient to say: במלאכת הקדש; apart from the קדש, gold was not used. But silver was not restricted to one place, it formed the transitional middle stage between קדש and חצר, it represented the highest goal of the חצר and the lowest rung, the basis of the קדש. And the use of the copper, too, could not simply be described as החצר, as the יתדות המשכן (see Ch. 26,37) as well as the אדני פתח אהל מועד were of copper, and besides the כיור belonging to the חצר was not made out of the “copper of the gifts” but was specially made from the mirrors of the women.

The total sum of the “voluntarily-gifted” silver is not mentioned at all, because its use was not restricted to the building and to the essential parts of the Sanctuary. Presumably many of the כלי שרת such as the מזרקות for the Altar (the one in the חצר for the offerings. I.L.) which only need be of copper, but were allowed to be of silver (רמב״ם הל׳ בית הבחירה אי י״ט) were made from this silver.

An ordinary commercial ככר has 60 מנה, a סלעים 25 מנה which are equivalent to שקלים (as a סלע=4 דינרין, a מנה in the Talmud=100 דינרין). But the ככר of the Mikdosh was of double value and had 120 מנה or 120x25 i.e., 3,000 שקל (Bechoroth 5a). 603,550 half-shekels=301,775 shekels, and 300,000 shekel=100 @ 3,000 שקל, so that 1,775 שקל were left over for צפוי ראשי העמדיםֿ וויהם וחשוקיהם.

V. 1. בגדי השרד (see Ch. 31,10). The fact that פקודי המשכן comes after the completion of the Sanctuary, but not after the completion of all the sacred objects which were made from the gifts — to which, of course, the priestly garments belonged — also speaks for the conception that here it is not dealing with a settlement of the account of the amounts given and the uses to which they had been put. כאשר צוה ה׳ וגו׳, it says this when recounting the finishing of making the garments, but not at the finishing of the various components of the משכן. This is only said later when the parts were assembled and the Mishkon erected in Ch. 40,19 and 21 et seq. Each separate garment was considered finished as soon as it was made. But the curtains forming the Tent, the furniture of the Abode etc., could only be considered completed when assembled and the Mishkon erected.

V. 3. פחי הזהב. The meaning of פחים here and in Numbers 17,3 as thin beaten-out sheets of metal is clear, and can not be doubted. But the derivation and the relationship to פח, a trap, a noose, is very obscure. וירקעו וגו׳ ,וקצץ and similarly ויעשו את בגדי and ויעש את האפד and again in the following verses the change to the third person singular is, either, in all cases where it refers to something where the abstract idea is more important, or where the technical difficulties are greater, and so the work is ascribed personally to Bezalel.

V. 43. וירא משה וגו׳ והנה עשו אתה ,כאשר צוה ה׳ כן עשו. Moses looked over the whole completed work, and lo! on the work two things were imprinted:- עשו אותה “they had made it”; in every part, in the smallest, in the greatest, the whole personality, the devotion, the voluntary enthusiasm, the power of accomplishment of the nation was expressed; and secondly כאשר צוה ה׳ “as God had commanded, exactly so had they made it” this whole energetic zeal and enthusiasm had nevertheless, in part and in whole restricted itself meticulously to the Divine commands. Nowhere could be detected an effort, by adding or leaving out, to carry out any idea of improvement, to leave some impression of the artist’s own personality on the work. Each and every workman accepted as his highest aim the careful and precise carrying out, not of his own ideas, but the ideas and thoughts which were embodied in the commands of God. This free joyful obedience, this freedom in obedience and obedience in freedom, which fills one with the happy consciousness of one’s own powers just by sinking one’s own personality in complete subordination to God’s will is what forms the most essential sign that characterises a human being as עבד ה׳ — the highest moral perfection that can be attained. That this might remain for ever the character of Jewish life and actions is the final sentence of the great Prayer of Moses (Ps. 90,17) as his deepest wish for the future of his people. Our sages, accordingly, take this to be the blessing here where it says ויברך אתם משה. That Tefilla concludes with the words “May Thy working be made manifest unto Thy servants and Thy majesty remain unto their children! May the happiness-spreading of God, our Lord, remain our lot. Let the work of our hands be established on ourselves, and the work of our hands establish Thou it”. מעשה ידינו כוננה עלינו this is our freedom, ומעשה ידינו כוננהו, that is our obedience. Only the identical, intimate combination of the two yield נועם happiness, the “pleasantness” which God prepares for us when we dedicate ourselves to Him as our “Lord”, our “Master” (אלהינו I.L.). Our verse יירא משה את כל המלאכה והנה עשו אתה כאשר צוה ה׳ כן עשו ויברך אותם משה is the source out of which those Tefilla thoughts flowed. Hence the words of our sages: — ויברך אותם משה אמר להם יהי רצון שתשרה שכינה במעשה ידיכם ויהי נועם ה׳ אלהנו עלינו וגו׳.

V. 2. ביום החדש הראשון באחד לחדש literally: “On the day of the first new-moon, on the first of the month”. This apparent tautology is explained, if we remember that — as we have already explained on Ch. 12,2, — that the significance of our “new-moons” lies in that we do not celebrate them with reference to the astronomical cosmic occurrence, but that, in that phenomenon of Nature we have the model and the exhortation and incentive for the foundation and celebration of human-social “new-moons”, renewals and revivals in our own lives.

The erection of the אהל מועד, the “Tent of Reunion” with which the entry of the Glory of God into the midst of the Jewish sphere here on earth was to begin, and thereby to begin Israel’s “Moed”, the conjunction of Israel with its “Sun”, its illumination by the light of its God, the erection was to begin on the day of the first new-moon i.e., was to take place on the day of that new-moon with which Israel’s years begin. For this was the new-moon, which first (in Egypt החדש הזה I.L.) brought to Israel the glorious message that they too could always find rejuvenation and revival, and through Israel the message was to be conveyed to mankind in general. The new-moon of the arising of the nation, of the national-birth is to be also the new-moon of the entry of the Schechina, the fulfilment of the ושכנתי בתוכם, in which the national redemption first finds its completion Hence ביום החדש הראשון, that alone suffices to indicate the first of Nissan. But באחד לחדש is still added to ensure the meaning of the celebration of this most-to-be-celebrated of all firsts of Nissan against any tinge of a pagan festival of Nature. Not because there is an astronomical new-moon on this day, but because as a result of this new-moon, Israel reckons its first day of the month, was it chosen for the erection of the Sanctuary. If החדש הראשון here meant the first month, the sentence would run in the usual way: ביום החדש הראשון ;בחדש הראשון באחד לחדש can mean nothing else but: - on the day of the first new-moon, and could also indicate the law which the Gemora (Shebuoth 15b) learns from the sentence in Numbers 9,15 וביום הקים את המשכן that אין בנין בית המקדש בלילה, that the erecting of the Mishkon has to be done in the daytime. This law itself (as is fully worked out in the Jeshurun IV, p.621 et seq.) raises all procedures to which it applies out of the dark realm of the blind forces of Nature, into the clear sphere of conscious freedom of will, the realm of which begins with Man’s work by daylight.

V. 17. הוקם המשכן. The Mishkon was erected. In the same way as, according to Ch. 29,30 and 37, the inauguration of the priests was celebrated during seven days, on each of which the ceremonial acts of inauguration, and the sacrifices of inauguration were repeated by Moses, so the ספרי on Numbers 7,1, teaches that for seven days, here, too, Moses erected the משבן, anointed it, and had it taken down again, before it was erected on this first day, the first of Nissan, as permanently consecrated. Hence הוקם המשכן, the erection on the first of Nissan was the final definite permanent consecration. Was this also perhaps a significant hint that it was destined to be erected seven times and seven times either taken down to change its home or be destroyed, before it would finally become the permanent everlasting home of the Glory of God on earth, the central height for all humanity, up to which all nations will pilgrim and change their allegiance to the sword to allegiance to the Law of God which goes forth from Zion? We only dare to put this forward as a question, and point out that ,במדבר גלגל, שילה, נוב, גבעון, בית ראשון, בית שני, do actually present us with the historical fact of seven such incidents happening to the “House”. Seven erections followed by הורבן, until the advent of באחרית הימים for which we are all waiting, when the eighth building will be erected, of which it is promised: — נכון יהיה הר בית ה׳ בראש ההרים ונשא מגבעות ונהרו אליו כל הגוים והלכו עמים רבים וגד׳ כי מציון תצא תורה ודבר ה׳ מירושלים ושפט וגד׳, וכתתו וגו׳ לא ישא גוי אל גוי חרב ולא ילמדו עוד מלחמה (Is. 2,1—4), “And it shall come to pass in the latter days that the mount of God’s house shall be firmly established at the top of mountains and shall be exalted above all hills; and all the nations will stream towards it. And many peoples shall go and say: Come, and let us go up to the Mount of God, to the house of the God of Jacob; and He will teach us of His ways and we will walk in His paths, for out of Zion shall the Law go forth, and the Word of God from Jerusalem. And He will judge between the nations, and rebuke many peoples and they will beat their swords into plowshares and their spears into pruning hooks; nation will not lift up sword against nation neither shall they learn war any more”.

V. 18. et seq. ויקם משה, Finally, on the eighth day, the first of Nissan, Moses erected the “Abode” etc., and V.33, when ויכל משה, when Moses had completed the work, then V.34, ויכס הענן then “the cloud covered the Tent and the Glory of God filled the Mishkon” and announced thereby that the work had been accomplished in accordance with God’s will, and that the object, the purpose of the whole: ועשו לי מקדש ושכנתי בתוכם had actually been achieved. In the same way as we were told above in Ch. 24,16 referring to Sinai that וישכן כבוד ה׳ על הר סיני ויכסהו הענן וגו׳, so now, when the תורה had found a home in human circles, this was henceforth to be the place for the revelation of the Glory of God on earth. It was, as the “revelation-psalm” LXVIII sings, ה׳ בם סיני בקדש, “God has come into their midst and Sinai is henceforth in the Sanctuary.” And just as there it says ויכסהו הענן ששת ימים ויקרא אל משה ביום השביעי מתוך הענן so here, too, it says first in V.35 ולא יכל משה לבא וגו׳ and only then in the first verse of Levit. ויקרא אל משה וידבר ה׳ אליו מאהל מועד. As soon as Moses had completed the work of erecting the Mishkon, he immediately retired in his relation towards it, to the status of one of the rest of the nation. It was not his work, not his relationship to the Divine Laws — the testimony for which rested therein and was what made the Mishkon into a “home for the Glory of God, “and into a “Tent of Meeting” of God with His people — which had found its visible expression there; it was the nation, who by this Sanctuary had prepared a home for the Torah, and an Altar for their devotion to it, and it was the nation for whom God allowed His Glory to enter into the home of the Torah on earth and there to reside. In that supreme moment of God’s relation to Israel, even Moses at first stepped back into the ranks of the people. Only then did he receive a fresh call (ויקרא I.L.), now to learn for the nation, מאהל מועד, from this Tent of Meeting, the demands which the presence of God in their midst made for sanctification of the individual and the national community; and how these demands were to be brought home to the people by the symbolic rites of the sacrifices, and translated into deeds in every action of their lives. At this point the history of the building of the Sanctuary is brought to a close with the report of its success as evidenced by the visible presence of the Glory of God. The detailed description of the initiation ceremonies is passed over here, and retrospectively taken up again in Levit. VIII, after the various symbolic sacrificial procedures of the Sanctuary had been taught in the first seven chapters.

With this acceptance of the Divine Torah in Israel’s midst as the highest supreme aim of the Jewish mission for all time, and with the visible entry of the Glory of God into the home which Israel had prepared for this Torah, the book of the Redemption from Egypt comes to an end. It was the goal which God Himself had declared as the object of His work of redemption, Ch. 6,6 and 7 והוצאתי אתכם וגו׳, והצלתי אתכם וגו׳, וגאלתי אתכם וגו׳, ולקחתי אתכם לי לעם וגו׳, the founding of this Sanctuary of His Torah, the acceptance of this home for the Torah in their midst, and the devotion to this Torah as symbolised by the Altar, made the nation into the People of God. And the presence of the cloud above the Sanctuary-of-the-Torah by day, and the fire by night, “before the eyes of the whole House of Israel on all their journeyings” declared to the “whole House of Israel”, to young and old, that, if, as Table, Lamp, Altar and the cherubim-tapestries proclaimed, God’s Torah is taken up with “ever-progressing freshness and pure gold firmness and tenacity”, and “material and spiritual happiness” is accepted only out of the hands of this Torah, and dedicated to the realisation of the Torah, then visibly and invisibly, the cherubim of God’s administration will descend bringing protection and blessing. This is not to be a “belief” mercifully invented as a consolation for this earthly life, but a “knowledge”, a conviction based on the certainty of actual experience. וידעתם, as God says, “you will learn by experience” כי אני ה׳ אלהיכם המוציא אתכם מתחת סבלות מצרים that “when I took you to Me to be My people” it was not just then and for once that I led you out from the weight of the Egyptian burden, but that I shall remain your God, in similar guiding, protecting and blessing nearness for ever.
Leviticus: V. 1. ויקרא אל משה וגו׳. Had it said ויקרא ה׳ אל משה וידבר אליו we should take it in the ordinary way, the calling as an independent act, separated from the speech, simply God called him to speak to him. But as it puts it, with ה׳ only after וידבר, the ויקרא is attached to, part of, וידבר and tells us exactly the manner of the speaking. A call came, and then God spoke to Moses. This is probably meant to establish the speeches of God to Moses as the Word of God coming to Moses, and to prevent that misused misrepresentation which tries to change the Divine revelation to Moses into some kind of revelation in Moses, and either to put it on par with all those imaginary visions of a so-called ecstasy, or simply as an inspiration coming from within a human being. This, of course, relegates Judaism, “the Jewish Religion,” to the nature of all other religious phases which have occured in human history, to a “contemporary phase in the history of the development of the human mind.” But this is not so. כאשר ידבר איש אל רעהו Ex. 33,11. “As the word of one man comes to another,” as speech from one man to another emanates purely and completely from the mind of the speaker, and in no wise whatsoever comes from the mind of the hearer, and nothing from within the hearer brings it about, so was God’s Word to Moses purely and solely the speech of God. Not from within Moses, from without, it came to him, called him out of whatever train of thought he might be in at the moment, to listen to what God wished to say to him. This ויקרא, this call preceding God’s speech, does away with that idea of the words of God which he transmitted arising from within Moses himself. It characterises God alone as the Speaker, and Moses purely as the listener. The Word of God to Moses was in no way provoked by him, he had not even any idea beforehand that it was coming. Perhaps that is what our חכמים mean when they say in ספרי on Deut. 34,10, that — amongst others — one of the most characteristic differences between the prophesy of Moses and that of Balaam was, that משה לא היה יודע מתי מדבר עמו עד שנדבר עמו ובלעם היה יודע אימתי מדבר עמו “Moses did not know when God would speak to him until the moment when He did speak to him, but Balaam knew when God would speak to him.” It is not impossible that they meant to say that Balaam’s prophesy was always preceded by his working himself up into an ecstasy, of which there was no trace in that of Moses. Perhaps, too, this is why Balaam’s prophesy is expressed by וַיִקָר ה׳ אל בלעם. God’s Word to Balaam had something of the passive in it, was provoked by Balaam himself, perhaps could only occur by his working himself up into some elevated state of mind; it says “Balaam went to seek the Word of God.” But the Word of God came to Moses completely extraneously, without any previous preparation on his part, without his having any idea that It was coming. Perhaps also this is the reason for the small א זעירא) א) in ויקרא, just to give a suggestion of the prophesy of Moses being completely “unprepared.” Of the Word of God to Moses one could leave out the א and say קל) וַיִקָר), it was something that “happened” to him, came to him completely unforseen. This characteristic call to attention preceding God’s speech to Moses, is taken in ספרא as occurring before every occasion when God spoke to Moses. It is specially mentioned here, at God’s first Word from the אהל מועד, at the thorn-bush (Ex. 3,4) and at the first Word on Sinai (Ex. 19,3) only to tell us that, no matter what the occasion was, no matter what the place was, whether from the lowly lonesome thorn-bush, from the flame and thunder blazing and roaring on Sinai, or from the still quietude of the Tent of Meeting, the Word of God came to Moses in exactly the same manner.

מאהל מועד לאמר. The אהל מועד represents the Divine Torah being accepted and taken up as the central soul of the Nation; the Nation regarding its material and spiritual welfare being granted by its keeping the Torah, and dedicating itself to a realisation of the Torah in every phase of its national life; and as a result of such a national Torah-life — the Glory of God in the midst of the people. All this was expressed by the אהל מועד as the attainable ideal of the people. The way to realise and attain this ideal is what this book of תורת כהנים deals with, and is the object of all the laws given in it. The אהל מועד is not only the place from where they originate, but they are quite understandably nothing but the result of its influence and teaching.

V. 2. דבר ,דבר אל בני ישראל ואמרת אלהם, say it in curt precise sentences: תשב״כ the written Law, ואמרת אלהם and explain the meaning of it to them תשב״פ, the oral Law (see note on Gen. 1,22). אלהם חסר take steps to ensure that this oral tradition comes to them “uniformly,” as if to one person. And actually, in fact, in spite of the fall of the State and the troubles of the times, the tradition came down undisputed from generation to generation through responsible individuals right down to the early years of the second Temple. Then, for the first time, a difference of opinion (which was never decided) arose amongst the חכמים regarding one single law. It was about the immediately following (v.4.) Law of סמיכה (whether it is to be done on Yomtof or not — I.L.), which, as we shall see further on, is in close connection with the בני ישראל of our verse (see Chagiga 16 b).

דבר אל בני ישראל וגו׳ אדם כי יקריב מכם וגו׳ מן הבהמה מן הבקר ומן הצאן תקריבו את קרבנכם. If all it wanted to tell us here was the general rule that if the Children of Israel want to bring an offering, it must be brought from either בקר or צאן, it would have sufficed to say simply: כי תקריבו קרבן לה׳ בקר וצאן תקריבוהו (cf. Deut. 16,2, where it says וזבחת פסח לה׳ אלקיך צאן ובקר). But in our verse, the subject, already given as בני ישראל, is, on the one hand extended by the comprehensive term אדם and on the other hand limited by מכם (some of you — I.L.). Similarly to the object בקר וצאן is extended by the comprehensive term בהמה and again limited by the selective preposition מן. Finally, the singular used at the beginning כי יקריב is changed at the end to the plural תקריבו את קרבנכם. All these are delicate modifications which are fully explained by the Halachoth which the oral tradition finds indicated by them:

Firstly, the subject בני ישראל is extended by אדם and thereby, at the very portal of the laws given for the Jewish Temple, an inscription is made which opens this Temple to all men — not exclusively to Jews. Every human being can bring his offering here. As is expressed by the hypothetic כי יקריב, here it is dealing primarily with free-will offerings, נדרים ונדבות, and tradition teaches expressly (Chulin 13 b) נכרים נודרים נדרים ונדבות כישראל. Rashi, too, takes the word אדם here in its most general sense including non-Jews (Chulin 5 a). Accordingly it is not just “the progress of Solomon’s advanced illuminating theories” which first extended “the narrow Mosaic ideas of God and the Temple” to that cosmopolitan outlook. The very first word of the “Mosaic” laws of the Temple gives the Temple the most universal mission, and with this one word expressed that which came to be a prophetic proclamation through the mouth of Isaiah: והביאותים אל הר קדשי ושמחתים בבית תפילתי עולותיהם וזבחיהם לרצון על מזבחי כי ביתי בית תפלה יקרא לכל העמים “I shall bring them (the children of the other nations) to the Mount of My Sanctuary, I shall make them happy in My House of Prayer, their elevating-offerings and their meal-offerings will find favour on My Altar, for My House will be called a House of Prayer for all the nations.” (Isaiah 56,7).

But while by אדם as subject, those from whom offerings are to be accepted are extended to the most universal conception, with regards to ישראל to whom this law is directly given, מכם is added as a limitation, מכם ולא כולכם להוציא את המומר. By מכם a מומר, one “who has become changed,” has become “un-Jewish,” one who has gone over to that which is a contradiction to Judaism, is excluded. To the non-Jew, the Jewish Temple is open without exception, everyone who has the calling to be “אדם״ may bring his offering to the Altar. But for a Jew it is not sufficient for his calling, merely to be a human being. He must not have completely departed from that high pure conception of a human being which the Jewish Torah teaches, בכם חלקתי ולא באומות. Not that this limitation excludes any Jew who may not be perfect. It says immediately להביא בני אדם שדומין לבהמה :מן הבהמה. It is just for, and with, the not yet ennobled side of human nature that offerings are to be brought, that by sacrificing and devoting just this “animal” side of his nature a man may be taught to purify and ennoble and consecrate to a higher purpose just this sensuous nature of his. מכאן אמרו מקבלין קרבנות מפושעי ישראל כדי שיחזרו בהן בתשובה hence the traditional teaching runs: “offerings from sinners against the Torah (except sin-offerings, of course. I.L.) are to be accepted, so that they may influence them to betterment,” חוץ ממומר, but they must not have reached the stage of מומר, the basic principles of his being must still be Jewish, nor may his fall have shown itself in acts of idol-worship עבודה זרה or of what is equal to it, חלול שבת בפרהסיא (see Chulin 5 a). The reason for this exclusion of this Jew who has fallen to heathenism, and admission of the born heathen to offerings in the Jewish Temple may perhaps be that the Altar erected by Jewish hands to God would forfeit the purity of its meaning by an offering on it of a heathen Jew, the Jewish ideology which gives the Altar its meaning would be drawn over to the heathen idea. But through a heathen the Jewish Altar can forfeit nothing of its pure relation to God. On the contrary, it is erected by Jews for the purpose of ultimately gathering all heathens to God.

קרבן. It is most regrettable that we have no word which really reproduces the idea which lies in the expression קרבן. The unfortunate use of the term “sacrifice” implies the idea of giving something up that is of value to oneself for the benefit of another, or of having to do without something of value, ideas which are not only entirely absent from the nature and idea of a קרבן but are diametrically opposed to it. Also the underlying idea of “offering” makes it by no means an adequate expression for קרבן. The idea of an offering presupposes a wish, a desire, a requirement for what is brought, on the part of the one to whom it is brought, which is satisfied by the “offering.” One can not get away from the idea of gift, a present. But the idea of a קרבן is far away from all this. It is never used for a present or gift, it is used exclusively with reference to Man’s relation to God, and can only be understood from the meaning which lies in its root קרב .קרב means to approach, to come near, and so to get into close relationship with somebody. This at once most positively gives the idea of the object and purpose of הקרבה as the attainment of a higher sphere of life. It thus rejects both the idea of a sacrifice, of giving something up, of losing something, as well as of its being a requirement of the One to Whom one gets near, and shows the מקריב as the one who has to find what he requires in the קרבן. The מקריב desires that something of himself should come into closer relationship to God, that is what his קרבן is, and the procedure by which this greater nearness to God is to be achieved is called “הקרבה״. It is קרבת אלקים, nearness to God which is striven for by a קרבת אלקים יחפצון .קרבן (Isaiah 58,2), just קרבת אלקים which for a Jew is the highest, yea the only conception of what is “good” (Ps. 73,28), without which he feels himself “בהמות״ like an animal, stripped of all that raises him into a human being (ibid v.22); קרבת אל׳ the value of which as the sole measure for one’s own outlook on life, and for estimating true happiness in life, is just what is made clear to us in the halls of the Sanctuary of God (ibid v. 17). In the מקדשי אל in the holy halls of God, in the דביר and the היכל, where the highest degree of human spiritual and material well-being and happiness which develops in keeping near to God under the rule of His Torah, is shown to be the ideal calling of human beings, and in the חצר where devotion to the illuminating purifying life-giving fire of the Torah is shown as the one sole way of attaining this nearness to God. There, in those halls, the problems of life solve themselves; there, life’s happiness rises and falls in accordance with the proximity or distance of God; there, “body and soul” learn to long for God (שארי ולבבי ibid) and the consciousness of God, which alone give happiness; there every retirement of, or from, God spells ruin. (רחקיך יאבדו); there, happiness is found only in the nearness of God, that alone is the one thing that is considered “good” קרבת אלקים לי טוב, and so all prosperity has lost its attraction if it entails estrangement from God; and even suffering itself becomes exalted happiness in the nearness of God to those who have refined their minds in the halls of the Sanctuary to get an understanding of, and their souls to be receptive for, the true real happiness of life: אך טוב לישראל אלקים לברי לבב (ibid 1.).

כל מקום :קרבן לה׳ “everywhere”, remarks ר׳ יוסי in ת״כ on this verse, כל מקום שנאמר קרבן אמור ביו״ד ה״א, שלא ליתן פתחון פה לאפיקורסים לרדות “everywhere where it talks of offerings, the four-lettered name of God is used, to give no opportunity for those who hold the Torah in contempt to degrade Jewish truths to heathen errors.” Not אלהים does God call Himself in connection with offerings, not in the vengeful, retributive nature of His unforgiving Justice does He wish there to be thought of, that would demand an offering as a reparation, and, in accordance with the blaspheming heathen illusion of a bloodthirsty vengeful deity, would accept the quivering death struggle of an animal’s life as a substitute for the forfeited life of a human being. As ה׳, the God of Love, in the whole plentitude of the power of His Almighty Love, ever ready to grant fresh life and a fresh future, does He wish to be thought of at offerings. Not killing — fresh restoration to life, repairing the old life, spiritual and moral resurrection, entering and re-entering again and again an ever higher, purer life, and gaining afresh the strength for such a new life from the never-failing well of eternal Love — that is the idea, that is the thought of Jewish offering. What does die there is nought but that which is dead in real human life, what does die there is only that which is transitory and perishable when kept at a distance from God, but which, if brought into the proximity of godliness, comes into the real purpose of its existence and partakes of eternal life in being pleasing to God and giving Him satisfaction (ניחח — I.L.). The name “ה׳״ which appears exclusively in connection with Jewish offerings, puts to shame all that, still today, אפיקורסים blasphemingly drivel about “the bloody cult of sacrifices”, לרדות thereby to drag down what they call “the Judaism of Moses” out of its eternal ideal height into the muddy puddle of a heathen standpoint which we have long ago left behind us.

מן הבהמה מן הבקר ומן הצאן . Inasmuch as בהמה is first mentioned, which in its broader sense includes the whole order of mammals חיה בכלל בהמה (as in Deut. 14,4&5), and then, out of this collective idea, בקר וצאן are specified, that, in accordance with the hermenutic rule כלל ופרט אין בכלל אלא מה שבפרט, limits the general idea of בהמה to בקר וצאן, so that it is to be taken in the narrower sense in which it only includes those animals which by their nature submit more readily to Man, and excludes חיה the free animals of the wild (Zebachim 34 a). This limitation to בקר וצאן and exclusion of חיה from offerings is raised to a definite prohibition of חיה for offerings by the repetition in v.3 and v.10 בקר וצאן אמרתי לך ולא חיה (ibid). So that — to represent human personalities in offerings only those animals are prescribed which on account of their characteristics are the ones which mostly come into the human community. מן הבהמה להוציא את הרובע ונרבע, מן הבקר להוציא את הנעבד, מן הצאן להוציא את המוקצה, ומן הצאן להוציא את הנוגח (Temura 28 a). The selection indicated by the preposition מן is here explained that by מן הבהמה, an animal that has been used for bestial sexual immorality, by מן הבקר, an animal that has been worshipped as an idol, by מן הצאן, an animal that has been dedicated to a heathen idol or god and by the superfluous conjunction ו, an animal that has killed a human being, are all precluded from being brought as offerings. רובע ונרבע מוקצה ונעבד and נוגח represent the very extremes of all classes of human crimes, the crimes, of ע״ז (idol worship) ג״ע (sexual immorality) and ש״ד (murder) and it is quite understandable that an object which is to serve as the symbolic expression of a person’s striving up to godliness, to moral and social truths and sanctity, should not, by its actual concrete reality represent the scorn and derision of the importance and gravity of just these three major crimes. The קרבן אהרן gives an explanatory answer to the question which the Gemora there raises under the term איפך אנא why we take רובע ונרבע to be excluded by the first מן, and ע״ז from the second, while one would have thought the ע״ז should be the very first to be excluded. He says the reason is that we find בהמה mentioned in connection with the crime רובע ונרבע: viz, ואיש כי יתן שכבתו בבהמה but ע״ז occurs under the term בקר viz. וימירו את כבודם בתבנית שור אוכל עשב (Ps. 106,20). If we consider our attempted etymological explanation of the words צאן, בקר, בהמה which we gave on Gen. 1,24-25; and Ex. 21,37, we get a simple understandable reason for the application of the particular exclusion to the particular word. We took בהמה (from בום = בהם the root of במה etc.) to be: the animal that naturally submits itself to Man. This association must not have led to criminal procedures בקר .להוציא את הרובע ונרבע :מן הבהמה (related to פקר ,בכר), we took to be: the independent animal, the animal given in charge of itself. This realisation of its independence must not have led to idolatry: צאן.להוציא הנעבד :מן הבקר (from שאן with the צ of exertion) we took to be, the animal artificially protected and penned. This care and protection may not lead to placing them under the protection of the gods by supposing them to be sacred to gods, להוציא את המוקצה :מן הצאן, and equally so, the animal may not have forefeited the natural mildness of its character and made itself unworthy of further protection by human care: להוציא את הנוגח :ומן הצאן.

תקריבו את קרבנכם. As here the singular of the subject with which the verse is begun, אדם כי יקריב is altered to the plural, the ת״כ teaches therefrom that the law is laid down that עולת בהמה may be brought, not only as the free-will offering of one individual, but also as נדבת שנים, as the conjoint offering of several people, as well as נדבת צבור the free-will offering on behalf of the nation. It differs in this from עולת עוף which also can be brought by several individuals together but never on behalf of the whole community, and from a מנחה which, as a free-will offering, can only be brought by separate individuals. The fact that עוף can never be brought by the צבור and מנחת נדבה only by separate individuals must be taken as an essential characteristic of these things and serve to help us when we come to consider the meaning of these offerings.

V. 3. In the previous verse we were given the classes of animals and the limitations within those classes to which the choice of animals for free-will offerings are restricted.
