The fact that this verse starts with the hypothetical אם עולה קרבנו gives us the definite implication that the previous verse with all its limitations must apply to at least one other class of offerings, אם עולה קרבנו לרבות את השלמים :שלמים; “if the קרבן mentioned in the previous verse is an עולה״ quite obviously implies it could have been something else and the only other class of free-will offerings is שלמים.

עולה. The usual translation “burnt-offering” (R.V.) (meaning completely consumed by fire—I.L.) has only a very weak foundation in the actual meaning of the root, תבוא בכלח אלי קבר כעלות גדיש בעתו (Job 5,26), very evidently means “Thou shalt come to thy grave in full mature age (כלה = כלח), (Gesinius also gives this derivation of כלח I.L.) even as the ripe corn in its time rises to its perfection.” There can certainly be no thought of being burnt or consumed here. The whole context would be against it. Even in אל תעלני בחצי ימי (Ps. 102,25), the idea is more of being taken up from this world rather than the destructive idea of death. Perhaps in this instance there may be some idea of “taking away from” of being lost to his world. But anyway if we compare the names given to all the other offerings: תודה ,שלמים ,אשם ,חטאת, we find that they all have reference to the inducement for the offering and the object of it, none of them are taken from any special procedure of that particular offering. And so we believe that עולה is the name given to an offering which is brought on account of the necessity for, and the aspiration to, “striving to rise higher.” We have already remarked elsewhere that arising from the fact that all dead matter is subject by the laws of gravity to be attracted down-ward to the earth, the Hebrew language expresses all development towards perfection, towards life and goodness and spirituality, not as a progressive step forwards, but as a progressive step upwards. עולה arises out of the consciousness that greater progress towards goodness and godliness is necessary and is able to be made. It is מכפר על עשה ועל לא תעשה הניתק לעשה (Yoma 36 a) or as ת״כ in v. 4 puts it, שיש בו קום עשה. An עולה is brought in the consciousness of not having done what one ought to have done, and is meant to guard against such neglect in the future. But every duty carried out is a positive step forwards, it is a raising of one’s own moral state, and a step upwards towards the moral height that brings God nearer. So that inducement and purpose, the character of offering, and its meaning and importance, are completely expressed by the idea of עולה: progress-offering, elevating-offering. אם עולה קרבנו מן הבקר would mean: If it is greater progress that he seeks to get nearer to God and he wants to express this through an animal of the herd …

In our article “Outlines of Jewish Symbolism,” (reprinted in Ges. Schriften vol.3. — I.L.) (see also notes on Gen. 15,9) we have already pointed out how frequently in the Scriptures animals occur as representing the character of human beings, that עגל & פר) בקר) is used to represent a personality active and working in the service of a higher personality whereas כבש & איל ,עז & שעיר) צאן) is used for a personality who is cared-for, looked after by a higher one, i.e. one who is “shepherded.” So that by צאן & בקר the two phases are expressed which together form the whole earthly existence of Man, — his work and his lot. Here and in v. 10 the choice is given to bring an עולה either from בקר of צאן. The consciousness of slackness in doing our duty and the resolution to give greater devotion to actively carrying out our obligations can arise out of the recognition of the position in the world to which God has allotted us. In such a case the choice for an עולה would fall on בקר. The approach to God would be as a פר — or as an עגל, one who is to become a פר — as a worker in that field of activity which God has allotted to him to cultivate. Or the consciousness of slackness, and the resolve to give greater devotion in future to the commands of God, may arise out of our feeling of the debt we owe to the Shepherd of our lives, we feel how every fibre of our body has been obtained and is being kept under His care and protection, and we feel urged to use every drop of our blood which He has given us and every ounce of strength which He has given us, in His service, and to live in accordance with His Will. Such a feeling would make us choose our עולה from the צאן. We should approach the “Shepherd of Israel” as a כבש, a simple sheep of His flock, or, in the enthusiasm of our debt of gratitude, as an איל, as one, who under God’s richer blessing, had grown into an influential member of His flock; or to express our resolve stubbornly to resist anything and everything that might tempt us away from His Divine Guidance, as an עז or שעיר.

First of all זכר תמים יקריבנו :אם עולה קרבנו מן הבקר. An עולה can only be brought מן הזכרים. With regards to the activities we have to perform in life (מצות עשה I.L.) God expects from all His children — men and women alike — virile independance. The מצות themselves, for which we have to stand up, make us, quite irrespective of sex or position, into men: אם עולה קרבנו זכר יקריבנו. Everything that we have in us of manly strength and manly independence we must dedicate to the service of God. It is not the effeminate in us, not womanly endurance or tolerance, it is virile firm action that seeks nearness to God in the עולה.

And תמים יקריבנו, complete must the animal be, by which one brings oneself, one’s acts, one’s efforts into the proximity of God. From Levit. 22,17—25 and Deut. 15,21, we learn exactly what is demanded by the term תמים. From the examples given there, the Gemora (Bechoroth 38 a), derives the rule that the animal may not have any מומין שבגלוי ואינן חוזרין any visible defect which will not right itself again. Such a failing is called a מום. Such a מום must not be confused with טריפה, vital faults in, or injuries to, the organs, nor with חולה illness, זקן senile debility, or מזוהם evil smelling, all of which deter an animal from being brought as an offering. All these are excluded by the repeated מן הבקר (v. 3.) להוציא את הטריפה (Menachoth 5 b), although הבקר, an animal left in the fields to fend for itself, it may not thereby have come to vital injuries. מן הצאן מן הכבשים מן העזים (v. 10) להוציא חולה זקן ומזוהם (Themura 28 b) although צאן, although requiring care and protection, this requirement must not be necessitated by conditions of weakness brought about by illness. A בעל מום can otherwise be completely healthy and vigorous but it has some visible permanent mutilation, however small it is, a permanent wound in the cartilage of the ear, נפגמה אזנו מן החסחוס, in the eyelid ריס של עיץ etc., etc., or any abnormality of the body, a high hip — שרוע — a club-foot קלוט etc.

Malachi in Ch. I, scourges those that offer up the blind, the lame or the sick, as being a degradation of the Name of God and the Altar of God. The priests are reproached as having provoked such degradation by their teaching. ואתם מחללים אותו “But ye have profaned it” באמרכם שלחן ה׳ מגאל הוא וניבו נבזה אכלו “in your speeches the Table of God is represented as being one which is rejected with disdain by others, and that which it garners is such the eating of which is contemptible.” It is quite clear that here the priests are reproached that, instead of representing God and His Sanctuary as the very highest, that demands the best, the freshest, the most vigorous and strongest of all that Man can give, they had degraded the Sanctuary into a hospital and old-age home erected for the wrecks of humanity, a place where only those come who are of no use in the world, and can find no home anywhere else, and who must be satisfied with what is left over from the tables of the rest of humanity. הקריבהו נא לפחתך “Just try bringing that to your Pasha” cries the Prophet in indignation “and see if he will be pleased with you and receive you!” It is exactly the same reproach which Hosea in Ch. 10,6 makes against the “parsons” of Israel: כי אבל עליו עמו וכמריו עליו יגילו “When the people mourn over it, their parsons rejoice thereat.” They and their sanctuaries speculate on the pain and grief of the “believers.” It is not the vivacious and happy ones who go to their halls. It is the blind, the lame, the sick and the weak who wend their way to their altars. Not as the ruler of fresh pulsating active life, and of the joy of life, but the consoler for what they have to endure and suffer and do without, is what religion is to them. Not so is God and His Temple which Israel is to bear through history as the God of the whole of humanity. The Sanctuary of His Torah demands the full complete life with nothing left out, nothing missing, and promises in exchange a rich full life in which, even death and pain lose their sting. So just as the priests serving at Israel’s Altar of the Law have to be without wound or mutilation, so, must the animals be without wounds or mutilation and vigorous undamaged if they are to serve as the means by which human beings celebrate their entry into, and progress in, the “covenant of nearness of God” on the Altar of His Torah.

But amongst all the פסולי מוקדשים, none have the unfitness to be used as offerings so stressed as that, the absence of which is here demanded, by the words תמים יקריבנו and again in Ch. 22,21, תמים יהי׳ לרצון. Not only is the presence of this bar to use בעל מום made into a definite prohibition (לא תעשה I.L.) in every stage of the הקרבה by the repeated prohibitions (Ch. 22,22 & 25); ואשה לא תתנו מהם ,לא תקריבו ,לא תקריבו ,לא תקריבו so that הזורק or השוחט or המקטיר or even המבדיל the very first stage, simply dedicating an animal that is a בעל מום incurs the penalty of מלקות (Temura 6 b); but the positive command of תמים demanding “absolute completeness” of the animal goes even farther than the negative prohibition. Whereas the idea of בעל מום comprises only visible external defectiveness of the body structure, the idea תמים demands internal completeness as well, and an animal whose internal organs are found to be defective or missing — אבר מבפנים מחוסר — is פסול for an offering (Bechoroth 39 a).

So that for each and every aspect of our relation to God which is to be expressed by an offering, “completion”, i.e. the demand for the application of the whole of oneself to that aspect, is the first and most indispensable condition. It is the בכל לבבך ובכל נפשך ובכל מאודך. It is the most direct consequence of the very first demand made to us: והייתם לי סגלה (Ex. 19,5) (see notes thereon), whereby it is just this relation to God excluding every and any other consideration which is made the foundation-stone of our whole mission. Anything missing of the living creature which is to express our relation to God would give the idea of excluding this missing organ, and thereby the sphere of our life which this organ serves to represent, from our relation to God, and from our giving ourselves up to Him in that particular sphere. We should not be giving ourselves up completely to the bond with our God as we should, with every particle of our being and in every sphere of our life. We are making some reserve, keeping something back. But as certain as it is that the most immediate result of our conception of the אחדות of God is the completeness with which we give ourselves up to Him, the result of שמע etc. is ואהבת etc., so certain is it that the very smallest, the slightest keeping back of any part of ourselves and our lives as being excluded from our relation to God is a denial of His Oneness. As we have already remarked on Gen. 17,1, the root תמם from which תמים is derived, has the innate meaning equally strong of the negation of every other state of existence as the positiveness of a really complete existence.

ת״כ on this verse has the following: כשם שאם אינו תמים ,תמים אינו לרצון כך אם אינו כענין הזה אינו לרצון a sentence, the meaning of which is difficult to fix with any certainty (see ק״א there). It is perhaps not far fetched to take it to mean; just as the offering itself must be תמים, so must the הקרבה be completely and entirely כענין הזה, according to the procedure prescribed here. Then תמים would not be an adjective qualifying “it” (in יקריבנו I.L.) but an adverb modifying יקריבנו. But ק״א quotes the sentence out of the פסיקתא זוטרתי as follows: כשם שהקרבן אם אינו תמים אינו לרצון ,תמים כך האיש אם אינו תמים אינו לרצון, the אינו in the second sentence of the ת״כ would then refer not to the offering, but to the person who brings it. This way of taking it sees in the offering the expression of the personality who brings it, so that the conditions mentioned as necessary to qualify the offering to be brought imply the necessity for these qualities in the character of the bringer, to make it acceptable to God. זכר תמים יקריבנו “virile, complete shall he offer it” would then characterise the subject as well as the object.

יקריבנו, this is the first act, the “bringing near to God”, the הקדשה, the consecration, the decision that this particular animal shall be used as a קרבן. The actual bringing the animal near is what the second half of the sentence says (ק״א).

אל פתח אהל מועד יקריב אותו. Getting near to God can only be done by getting near to His Torah; the progress which is sought for in the עולה is only to be obtained by a progress in carrying out the Torah. The offering dedicated to God is to be brought to the entrance to the “Tent of fixing the meeting.” The only road to God is by way of His Torah, the testimony for which rests on the ארון of which God had said: ונועדתי לך שם “that is the place which I have appointed for Myself to meet you”; where the testimony of My Law rests, there wilt thou find Me.”

יקריב אותו לרצונו :יקריב אותו imperative, expresses a duty, while לרצונו expresses an act of one’s own inner will. So that the Torah recognises it as a duty, to make it one’s will to act in a certain way. As a matter of fact, once one has dedicated the animal for an עולה, one has no further choice in the matter, the bringing of it has attained the force of a vow, which, if the necessity arises, one can be made to keep, hence כופין :יקריב אותו אותו. But the offering has to be brought לרצונו, as an expression of his own will, and only if he brings it as such, has he fulfilled his vow. So that where the necessity for compulsion arises, this must be directed not merely to make the negligent one bring his offering, but to make him realise and state that at heart he really does want to bring it. (The assumption being that at heart every Jew really does want to do his duty, but that greed, stinginess etc. get the better of him, and have to be removed — I.L.). כופין אותו עד שיאמר רוצה אני. In every case where the act concerned is one to fulfil an obligation laid down by the Torah, or any other obligation where no actual loss is involved, it is presumed when such a declaration רוצה אני is made, that the act will be performed really in accordance with his desire, although the declaration had to be brought about by compulsion. Hence the Mishna Arachin 21 a: חייבי עולות ושלמים ממשכנין אותן אף על פי שאין מתכפר לו עד שיתרצה שנאמר לרצונו כופין אותו עד שיאמר רוצה אני, וכן אתה אומר בגיטי נשים (where according to the דין he must divorce) כופין אותו עד שיאמר רוצה אני, and in Kiddushin 50a and Baba Basra 48a the motive is given משום אנן סהדין דניחא ליה בכפרה and משום דמצוה לשמוע דברי חכמים. The actual measures which were taken to bring about the declaration are disregarded and it is taken that they only conduced to a return to a sense of duty and that the declaration is genuine. In a similar way in the דינים of commerce, תלוה תבין זבינה זביני, if by means of pressure, someone is induced to declare his willingness to sell an object and then the sale has peacefully taken place at a fair price, the Gemora, Baba Basra 48 a declares that we can assume that אגב אונסיה גמר ומקני, by means of the pressure put on him he has been brought to agree that he is willing to sell, and the sale is valid and legal. But where pressure is brought to bear to make a person agree to do something which he is not obliged to do by the Law, גט מעושה שלא כדין or to part with something without receiving due payment for it, תליוה ויהיב, there the willing agreement which is demanded to make such acts valid is not presumed in spite of any רוצה אני “I agree” which he may have declared, and any procedure brought about in such a way is invalid (see תוספות B. Bathra 48 a).

V. 4. וסמך ידו על is not merely, “laying hands on”. The predominant meaning of סמך is “to support” and in the few places where it does not exactly mean support as סמך מלך בבל (Ezek. 24,2), עלי סמכה חמתך (Ps. 87,8) it still expresses an intensified touching, either, as in the first quotation, in place: very near, or in the second, in time: very long, lasting. The Halacha, too, is סמיכה בכל כחו בעינן (Chagiga 16 b) that what is demanded here is supporting with all one’s strength, and with both hands (Menachoth 93 a).

Apart from at offerings we find סמיכת יד על- in the Torah: at the initiation of the Levites וסמכו בני ישראל את ידיהם על הלוים (Numb. 8,10), at the initiation of Joshua וסמכת ידך עליו (Numb. 27,18) ויסמך את ידיו עליו ויצוהו (ibid 23), ויהושע בן נון מלא רוח חכמה כי סמך משה את ידיו עליו (Deut. 34,9) and finally at the execution of the blasphemer, וסמכו כל השמעים את ידיהם על ראשו (Levit. 24,14). Let us try and find the common idea which is expressed in these three cases by ‘supporting with hands’. The idea common to the first two cases is understandable and clear. In both cases by the “supporting with hands” a person is invested with full powers, such powers being in close connection with those possesed by the one who performs the investment. The Levites receive the sovereignty of the service of the Sanctuary, but they receive it as the representatives of the nation, of the Children of Israel, who invest them with it. Joshua becomes the Leader of the Nation as the successor of Moses. The effect of this “supporting with hands” is accordingly a simultaneous granting and gaining. By granting powers to representatives the giver gains an increase of his powers either in extent or time. By the service of the Levites, the obligations of the people are fulfilled and they are saved from having to carry them out themselves. In Joshua, Moses goes on living and his work is continued. So that by “supporting his hands”, the “hand” the obligation and the right and power to do some act is transferred to another, and at the same time it itself gains support, assistance. How does the third case, “the supporting with hands” of the witnesses and judge on the head of the condemned blasphemer, fit in with this? The ת״כ אמור explains the meaning as follows: אומרים לו דמך בראשך שאתה גרמת לכך “they say to him thereby: your blood is on your own head, you, yourself have caused it to come to this pitch” (i.e. that it has to come to your execution). They place the responsibility for his death on himself. Their “hands”, that which they are causing to be done to him, is really his hand, supports itself on him, they are only carrying out that which they are in duty bound to do, and authorised to do, by him, through his actions. True, it is the reversed order here, the idea of “being supported is in the foreground, the ‘supporter’ looks on himself as being induced to act through the other. But it is a simultaneous “giving and gaining”. The criminal is made the bearer of the procedure to be carried out on him, and the judge and witnesses thereby free themselves from responsibility.

What then would סמיכת יד on the head of an offering be? Without further ado we would simply say: the “hand” that had become morally weak by omission or commission (in the case of an עולה or חטאת respectively — I.L.) “supports” itself on the resolution of future betterment that is expressed by the offering. The idea of receiving “support from” would then be in the foreground and the idea of “handing over” would only be present inasmuch as the “laying on of the hand” gives the offering its specific relationship to the one who does the act. In favour of this explanation would be the fact that סמיכה only takes place at such offerings which are brought in connection with the bringer’s actions, as עולה ,חטאת ,אשם and שלמים, but not at בכור מעשר ופסח which are brought more in relation to one’s property and lot in life (Menachoth 92 b). This close relationship of סמיכה to the meaning of the offering atoning for actions and behaviour would also explain the further fact that סמיכה must be performed by the person who is seeking atonement himself and not by a deputy: וסמך ידו ולא יד שלוחו, the “hand” itself that is to be atoned for must perform the סמיכה (ibid 93 b). Even if more than one person bring an offering conjointly, each one of them has to do לרבות כל בעלי קרבן לסמיכה :קרבנו .סמיכה every one whose behaviour is to be brought nearer to God by means of the offering must “support his hand” on it (ibid 94 a). Perhaps this may also be the reason why at קרבנות צבור, where it would be impossible for all the בעלים to perform סמיכה, no סמיסה at all takes place, and so just this absence of סמיכה and thereby the absence of definite בעלים marks the offering as a קרבן ,צבור. Only the פר העלם דבר של צבור (in Mishna, Menachoth 92 a improperly called פר הבא על כל המצות which everywhere else refers to פר כהן המשיח) and שעיר המשתלח have סמיכה although they are קרבנות צבור, the former by three members of the ב״ד, the latter by the כה״ג. But the פר העלם דבר של צבור really primarily concerns the ב״ד, whose special relationship to this קרבן is expressed just by this סמיכה of three of its members; and the סמיכה of the כה״ג on the head of the שעיר המשתלח would publicly express the fact that for this כפרה — according to the view accepted as Halacha — the priests are not excluded, but are considered as standing in the midst of the people, and equally requiring atonement before God. But if סמיכה is really entirely symbolic of the personal relationship of the one who is seeking “nearness to God” to his offering, we should expect it to be required from any and every person who brings one, and also that סמיכה would be an essential part of the offering. But the Halacha teaches (Menachoth 93 a), הכל סומכין חוץ מחרש שוטה וקטן וסומא ונכרי והעבד והשליח והאשה and then adds immediately וסמיכה שירי מצוה i.e. סמיכה is only necessary as a completion of the Mitzva, as this is explained there (93 b). שאם עשאה לסמיכה שירי מצוה מעלה עליו הכתוב כאלו לא כיפר וכיפר that if he had omitted סמיסה the text speaks of him (וסמד ידו וגו׳ ונרצה לו לכפר עליו) as if he had not achieved atonement although in all essentials he had done so.

So there must be some additional idea innate in סמיכה which would give a reason for these laws. If we look at the list of persons just quoted, who are excluded from סמיכה, we find that in every case — apart from the שליח — their disqualification for performing סמיכה would lie, not in their personal individual character, but in their being regarded from a national point of view. All of them do not stand — or at least not in front line — as the national representatives and bearers of the responsibility of the national mission. Even סומא, a blind man, is excluded, just as he is from the Mitzva of ראיה, the duty for the whole nation to appear three times a year in the Sanctuary, and also from the ability to become a judge, he can not belong to the זקני העדה — the elders representing the nation (ibid 93 a). As already pointed out on v.2, the בני ישראל (apparently specialising the Jewish nation for the sacrificial laws given here) which preceded the all-inclusive term אדם (bringing all human beings within the scope of these laws) is referred entirely to סמיסה, as being that procedure at the offerings as which the personality of the bringer comes quite specially into consideration. So that at the סמיכה at an offering the סומך must be acting not simply as a private individual, but as one of בני ישראל, as a national member of the Jewish nation, and thereby just as at the סמיכת לוים and the סמיכת יהושע, not only the meaning of “support” but also that of “granting” must prevail.

We believe: by the act of סמיכה the סומך as one of the national representatives of the Law, of the Torah, rises up against himself. He expresses thereby, that the demands which are expressed by the various coming acts of the procedure of the offering are made in his name. It is he himself who asserts the demands which the Sanctuary makes from him. Without סמיכה it is the Sanctuary which brings home to him the demands for “progress” or “persistance” in goodness. By סמיכה he himself rises up for the Sanctuary of the Torah, against himself, and, as a בן ישראל, as one of the bearers of the Torah, in the name of the Torah, and for its realisation, he assigns the vocation of the various procedure which are to follow, viz. שחיטה etc. (which is also the reason why תיכף לסמיכה שחיטה, the שחיטה has to follow immediately after the סמיכה (Zebachim 33 a). By this his sin of slackness in doing right, or of carelessness in doing wrong, becomes atoned for in a higher degree, inasmuch as he is made conscious of his position as a בן ישראל, who is even responsible for seeing that the Torah is kept by others in the national community, and so all the more must be careful in his own life not to become slack or careless. According to this one can understand that סמיכה is not מעכב כפרה, but nevertheless if omitted it leaves the כפרה with something lacking. In Zebachim 6 a & b, this is expressed in the following terms, כיפר גברא ,לא כיפר קמי שמיא, as גברא, as an individual, the atonement is achieved, as indeed it is in the cases of all those people whose offerings are always without סמיכה. But קמי שמיא, in the position which he has before God as a בן ישראל, the כפרה has remained incomplete. We can then also understand the דין סמיכה, that סמיכה is only performed לפני ה׳, only in the משכן and מקדש, where the relation of the offering to God stands out as the relation to His Torah, but not when the offering is brought on a במה where there is nothing to express this relationship (Zebachim 119 b).

על ראש העולה. It is only on the head of the animal that the whole animal is affected by the סמיכה. On any other part it would appear as if the סמיכה referred only to a part of that which the whole animal represents.
העולה: by the specialising ה the סמיכה is restricted to עולת בהמה. There is no סמיכה at an עולת עוף (see note on v.14).

לכפר עליו, not that כפרה is already achieved by the סמיכה, it comes with the זריקת הדם, with devoting the נפש, the whole of one’s self to the mission demanded by the Torah. But by סמיכת ידים על ראש העולה the whole strength of a member of the Jewish People is assigned for carrying out the devotion of the whole personality which is about to be expressed by the זריקה, and thereby complete preparation made for the כפרה.

V. 5. ושחט וגו׳ ,והקריבו בני אהרן וגו׳, as the priests only come into it with the הקרבה it is at once evident that שחיטה כשרה בזד, that the act of שחיטה can be done by anybody, and only מקבלה ואילך מצות כהונה, only with the receiving the blood in a holy vessel of the Sanctuary, that third הקרבה, that third “bringing the קרבן near” (the first was the dedicating the particular animal to be an offering, the הפרשה v. 2, the second the bringing of the animal into the precincts of the Sanctuary, the עזרה, v. 3) did the functions of the priests begin (Zebachim 32 a). שחיטה is the preliminary condition for the transition and entry into the sphere of the Sanctuary of the Torah. It is the giving up of the life that has hitherto been lived, the purely physical selfish existence. All slackness and all carelessness has its origin in the fact that the דם, the נפש, the personality of the human being is, in some phase of its nature, still encompassed by the selfishness of purely physical existence, has not yet completely given up living for itself, has not yet completely given itself up to belonging to the Torah. When the person who is seeking to get nearer to God has dedicated an animal to express his own personality, when, in the consciousness of the way to God being only found by way of His Torah, he has brought the animal to the Sanctuary of the Torah, and there, by סמיכה has demanded, in his own name as a Jew, that the conditions necessary for getting nearer to God as laid down in this Torah, which are to be brought to his mind by his offering, be carried out by himself, and has pledged his future life to carry out those conditions, then he, or someone acting for him in his name, has, by שחיטה, to make him realise what the first condition is, viz, completely giving up his own life being lived for himself; (the animal life, “the world is too much with us”, the root of all lapses — I.L.). This is a condition which, it is true, can only be made לפני ה׳ and having regard for His Torah, and hence must be made in the Sanctuary, but it is something which must be accomplished not by the Sanctuary on the person, but by the person on himself, if he is to be able to live the positive active life which the Sanctuary has to teach him. These considerations may give us the reason for the דינים, that, as already remarked שחיטה כשרה בזרים ובנשים ובעבדים ובטמאים ואפילו בקדשי קדשים וכו׳ (Zebachim 31b); further, that, although the act of שחיטה itself must be performed לפני ה׳, within the ולא השוחט לפני ה׳ ,עזרה, the one who does the act may stand outside it (Zebachim 26 b); that altogether שחיטה לאו עבודה היא, the act of שחיטה in itself is not reckoned as one of the עבודות (ibid 14 b). This is highly characteristic of the Jewish conception of offerings. The very thing that, in the general notion of sacrifices, forms the essential part of the sacrifice, does not belong to the real “cult”; even in its symbolic meaning it only forms an indispensable preparatory condition. Not by slaughter, and not by self-destruction “is God served”; only as a preparation for קבלה etc. for the entry into a higher, holier stage of life and activity, has it any meaning; it is only when this higher holier existence and life has been attained that “the service of God” begins!

So that it is significant that at the שחיטה it speaks of בן הבקר whereas already at the סמיכה it calls the animal עולה, and later in the next verse, too, it is also called עולה. At the שחיטה it is still in the condition of being a בן בקר of not yet being encompassed by the Torah, only after שחיטה does it become fit to become an עולה.

Nevertheless, or rather just because of this, the שחיטה must be carried out under the full consciousness that the animal is placed there before God to be used as a sacrifice; מניין למתעסק בקדשים שהוא פסול שנאמר ושחט את בן הבקר לפני ה׳ עד שתהא שחיטה לשם בקר, more, if the שחיטה had been made unthinkingly, מתעסק בדבר אחר, with one’s thoughts not on the sacrifice e.g., if one thought one was slaughtering an ordinary animal, שחט משום חולין the whole sacrifice is invalid. This insistence on the absolute necessity of having the right כונה at שחיטת קדשים (although it is not part of the עבודה — I.L.) is expressed by the repeated demand לרצונכם תזבחהו (Levit. 19,5) i.e., לדעתכם תזבחהו; Any rule concerning offerings which is repeated, by such repetition becomes an indispensable condition, שנה עליו הכתוב לעכב (Zeb. 47 a).

בן הבקר. In Rosh Hachona 100 a, it says: כל מקום שנאמר עגל בתורה סתם בן שגה, בן בקר בן שתים, פר בן שלש and Rashi and Thosafoth explain that as the word סתם already shows, בן בקר refers to עגל בן בקר .עגל is a two year old animal, and פר בן בקר designates a three year old (see Ch. 4,3). From this can be deduced that בן בקר only expresses the age when added to עגל or פר but used by itself it would only designate the species and can refer to either an עגל or a פר. This is quite in keeping with its use here, as עולת נדבה can be either an עגל or a פר, and there would be no reason why here it should speak only of a young ox. (but still see מל״מ on פרה אדומה, at end of I,1).

והקריבו. This act of “bringing near” includes קבלה and הולכה the receiving the blood in a “service vessel” a כלי שרת (an integral part of the Mikdosh — I.L.) and carrying it to the place from which the blood is to be thrown on to the Altar. As already explained on Ex. 30,29, everything taken up in a כלי שרת becomes holy, it then belongs to the sphere of the Sanctuary. The דם הנפש of the שחיטה which hitherto had been kept back by belonging to its own selfish ends, by the קבלה, by being received in the כלי שרת, receives the higher calling of belonging to the Sanctuary of the Torah of God; הולכה, the actual bringing of the blood into the proximity of the Altar is only the carrying out of the ideal “bringing near”, the ideal הקרבה which is brought about by the קבלה in the הולכה .כלי שרת is therefore also an עבודה שאפשר לבטלה a procedure of the offering which can be omitted if the קבלה took place so near to the Altar that the זריקה can be done without any further הולכה (Zebachim 4 a, but still see משנה למלך on הל׳ פסולי המוקדשים I,23).  שתהא בכהן כשר ובכלי שרת :בני אהרן הכהנים designates the personal qualifications, unblemished descent and bodily lack of imperfections i.e., not חללים and not הכהנים ,בעלי מומין, having their complete priestly appearance, i.e., clothed in the prescribed priestly vestments (see notes on Ex. 28,43). It is worth noting that here the Gemora calls the בגדי כהונה in exactly the same way as the vessels for the sacrificial-service כלי שרת. Just as the holy vessels receive and accept whatever is placed in them, as belonging to, as being part of the Mikdosh, so, with the putting on of the vestments does the priest become a representative servant of the Mikdosh. Only when clothed in the priestly garments does the priest stand as a minister of the Sanctuary. Only when clothed in the garments of the Mikdosh, does he stand in the symbolic meaning of his office. Further, everywhere where, at a דבר המעכב כפרה, at an act which is essential for the כפרה — as here קבלה is, the operator is called by the name מהן, the act must always be done with the right hand, and if done with the left would be invalid, כל מקום שנאמר כהונה אינה אלא ימין (Menachoth 10 a). The procedure, teaching how to get near God, must be carried out with all the earnestness of the fullest possible strength and force.

זורקו וגו׳ סביב. This “service” of the blood is explained in Zebachim 53 b, as follows: יכול יזרקנו זריקה אחת תלמוד לומר סביב, יכול יקיפנו כחוט ת׳׳ל וזרקו, פי׳ רש״י ואין זריקה אלא מרחוק וכחוט אי אפשר להקיף אלא באצבע ובנגיעה, הא כיצד כמין גמא ודמה טעון שתי מתנות שהם ארבע, i.e., the action to be performed with the blood is prescribed by the two expressions, זריקה, throwing from a distance, and סביב the blood having to be on all four sides of the Altar. The blood had to be thrown on two diagonally opposite corners of the Altar and each of these זריקות had to be a זריקה סביב. The blood had to be thrown so that it spread round both sides of the corner. When this is repeated on the diagonally opposite corner, the blood will have been deposited on all four sides of the Altar in two “throwings”: שתי מתנות שהן ארבע. This was done on the east-north and the west-south corners (one always had to go round via the S.E., E.N., N.W. and W.S. route — I.L.) the מזרחית צפונית and מערבית דרומית. It had to be these two corners and not the S.E. and N.W. as is explained in Yoma 15 b, because an עולה טעונה יסוד וקרן דרומית מזרחית לא הוה ליה יסוד an עולה in common with all other offerings the blood of which has to come on the lower half of the Altar (viz. שלמים and אשם) has to have the blood placed above the base, the יסוד of the Altar, and the South-East corner had no base.

When we considered the construction of the Altar (Ex. XXVII on v. 8 et seq.) we went into the ideas that were expressed thereby, and particularly into those special characteristics that differentiated the national Mikdosh Altar from a Bama. We found the fundamental thought in the idea expressed in the name הראל, the raising of the earth upwards to God i.e., the elevation of everything material, earthly, upwards to the realm of the spiritual, the Godly. We found that this thought was more definitely and precisely expressed by the יסוד, the base which was an essential part of the Altar of the Mikdosh. It expressed the idea, that this elevation of everything earthly up to God was only to be accomplished by carrying out His expressed Will (the Torah — I.L.) in all earthly matters only on the very earth, the base of the National Sanctuary of the Torah on which our Altar rose up just by means of its יסוד. He who brings his offering to our Altar, for his נפש, his personality to be taught by the דם the way to be elevated to the proximity of God thereby places himself on the basis of the Divine Torah on which alone is the path upwards to God to be found. And the non-Jew too, who brings his offering to God to this Altar, by the very fact, acknowledges that conception of God which was revealed to Israel and through Israel to the world, and also his duty of fulfilling those general demands which God makes to all mankind, as revealed through Israel’s Law. He places himself on the basis of the “Laws of the Sons of Noah” as chartered to the world through Israel. We can understand why this reference to the “base” occurs as important above all at דמים התחתונים, at the עולה etc., as they teach the very first striving upwards to the first preliminary stage of the way up to the summit of the Altar (remember that the lower half of the Altar is called the עזרה — ibid above).

Further, we have already considered the implication of the characteristic square shape of the Mikdosh-Altar, as well as of the fact that the Altar lost the whole of its meaning if the door of the Sanctuary, פתח אהל מועד, was closed, both of which facts are here again specially indicated by the sentence המזבח סביב אשר פתח אהל מועד (see ת״כ on our verse and Zebachim 62b). By this, the Altar itself (even its summit I.L.) is regarded merely as a way up to the real heights which the Sanctuary teaches is to be reached by carrying out its precepts. It itself only gets its meaning from being part of the Sanctuary as we have already remarked there (ibid), it represents for the meaning of the courtyard in upward vertical projection that which the different enclosures or halls of the Sanctuary represented in horizontal progression. Accordingly, as soon as the doors of the Sanctuary were opened, the sides of the Altar took on the meaning of the sides of the Sanctuary. By the ארון, the west side of the Altar represented the Torah; the south, by the מנורה, the intellect, the spiritual; the north, by the שולחן, the material; the east, by the door, the awaiting of the entrances and exits of the People, represented the nation, Israel living a life as the product of שולחן תורה and מנורה, as the culmination of their ideal life was represented inside by the מזבח הקטרת. The junction of the sides in the W.S. corner would represent the intellectual life produced by, and coming out of the Torah, the S.E. the life of the Nation produced by this intellectual life and so directed to the Torah; E.N. the material life, the worldly life developed from such a national life; N.W. the material riches obtained by the National life being lived in accordance with the Torah, being directed to the realisation of the Torah. So summarising, W.S. = the life of the intellect coming from the Torah; S.E. = the Torah life of the Nation emanating from this intellectual life; E.N. = the material prosperity emanating from the nation; N.W. = the carrying out of the Torah emanating from the material prosperity. Progress towards ever greater perfection as preached by the עולה, as well as holding fast to — and not slipping down from — the height already achieved (as taught by the חטאת — I.L.), is only to be achieved by the individual as well as by the nation, by a combination of every one of these sides. The Torah must be the source of the intelligence; and intelligence must give life to the Jewish National consciousness that its mission is to keep the Torah; only in the spirit of such consciousness is material wealth to be worked for; and all material wealth and worldly life must be directed towards the carrying out of the Torah. These are exactly the same four aspects of life, which are urged upon us by our תפלין, each one separately for the theory in תפלין של ראש and all combined for the practice, the actual carrying out, in קדש .תפלין של יד is the consecration of the nation to the Torah, the East. והיה כי יביאך is the material prosperity granted to the nation, the North. שמע is the spiritual life, the life of the intellect aroused through the Torah, the South. והיה אם שמוע is the realisation, the carrying out of the Torah which is expected from the national prosperity, the West. Or better, קדש, the S.E. והיה כי יביאך the E.N., שמע the W.S., והיה אם שמוע the N.W.

Now it is of the deepest significance and describes the whole idea of Jewish History ( — as Hirsch has fully worked out in his article on the שמנה עשרה in the Jeshurun Vol. XII, and reproduced in the Gesammelte Schriften — I.L.) that the קרן דרומית מזרחית, the S.E. corner of the Altar, had no יסוד at all. Only the N. & W. sides had the base completely built up. On the E. & S. sides there was only the beginning of a base extending just one cubit at the N.E. & S.W. corners respectively. So that the Altar, which at its base measured 32 × 32 cubits had no יסוד along 31 cubits on the S. side, and the same on the E. All that we were to receive from the hands of God, the תורה (represented by the W.) and our national material prosperity through keeping the תורה (represented by the N.) was on a firm and completely established basis, but for that which was to evolve from these gifts of God by our own activities and devotion, for our intellectual and spiritual life (the S.) developing from the תורה, and for our whole actual national life based on the Torah and lived solely for it (the E.) only a beginning was made. It is accordingly, perhaps, not too bold to say that the lack of the south eastern basis is the sad cause of the whole Jewish history up to the present day, and that in the building out of the south eastern corner lies the whole goal and hope of the Jewish future. This way of looking at it from a historical point of view gains weight and meaning from the fact that the Gemora in Zebachim 53 b gives as the reason for this lack of base on the S.E. corner לפי שלא היתה בחלקו של טורף that the ground on which this unbuilt south eastern base must have rested was not situated in the province of Benjamin. For, according to the view (Yoma 12 a and Megilla 29 a) that the territory of Jerusalem was also apportioned to the tribes like the rest of the land and was not kept as common national domain, the dividing line of the borders of the provinces of Judah and Benjamin passed just across the Mount of the Temple. The whole of the approach on the east side as well as the side-halls, to which לשכת הגזית, (the seat of the supreme court, the Sanhedrin — I.L.) also belonged, and the three ante-chambers; the עזרת נשים, the עזרת ישראל and the עזרת מהנים up to the Altar were all in the province of Judah. But the site of the Altar itself and all the Temple to the west of it, the whole of the Sanctuary, including the holy of holies, lay in the province of Benjamin. The מהרש״א in ח״א in Zebachim points out that from Judges 1,8 & 21, it is also apparent that both Judah and Benjamin must have had part in Jerusalem, this also appears in the description of the apportioning of the Land in Joshua, XV,8 & XVIII,28. In the “Blessing of Moses”, (וזאת הברכה) too, Benjamin follows immediately after Judah, with Levi between the two as partaking of the character on either side. To Judah is allocated the power of the State (Deut. 33,7), to Benjamin (ibid v. 12) the protective proximity of God — the Schechina. Levi (v. 10) takes part in both. By יורו משפטיך ליעקב וגו׳, in the Sanhedrin belonging to the province of Judah, and by ישימו קטרת וגו׳ in the position of the Altar in that of Benjamin. According to this tradition it was not in the province of the lion-hearted ruling tribe, but in that of the smallest weakest one that the National Sanctuary stood, and as far as the base stretched over into the province of the royal Judah, it was left unfinished. Hereby was expressed the deeply significant fact, confirmed by the whole of Jewish History, and disclosing its final goal: in Israel, the highest power of the State should of course be permeated with the spirit of the Torah and consider that it is based solely and solidly on the Torah, and that its sole function is to direct the nation to keeping the divine Torah. On this power of the State, the south and east base of the Altar should rest firmly. But this combination of Power and Spirituality is a thing of the future. It is only the future “sprout from the stem of Jesse” of the tribe of Judah, who will combine the highest degree of power with the highest degree of intellect and spirituality, more it is just his very spirituality which will give him his power (Is. 11,1 et seq.). He will be the one who at last will be “a priest on the Kingly throne” (Zacch. 6,13). Throughout the course of the whole Jewish History it has been but seldom that the royal power looked on itself as priestly, and behaved accordingly. Only seldom did the spirit of the Torah, and the Nation as the Nation of the Torah, find its foundation on the base of royalty, — the foundation of the southern and eastern base of the Altar which stretched over into Judah’s domain remained unfinished, incomplete.

Accordingly, as there was no יסוד on the south eastern corner of the Altar, the depositing of the blood of the עולה which had to be done on two diagonally opposite corners could only be done on the east-north and west-south corners. The reason that the order had to be E.N. and then W.S. is as follows: —

In v. 11, the command for the procedure in the case of an עולה is given as: ושחט אותו על ירך המזבח צפנה לפני ה׳ וזרקו וגו׳. From this we learn two things, Firstly that שחיטת עולה (and equally so, all קדשי קדשים) had to be done בצפון in the north, and secondly that the north side was ירך המזבח, the back of the Altar. The front was accordingly to the south, and on this front side (in the middle — I.L.) was the כבש the ascent which according to Ex. 20,23, had to be not by means of steps, but was a flat inclined plane (see Zebachim 62 b). This כבש had to be ascended for offerings like the חטאת where the blood had to be placed on the four horns of the Altar, which was ten cubits (roughly 20ft.) high: The שחיטה and קבלת הדם was done on the north side, then the blood caught in a כלי שדת was brought to the south side to be taken up the incline, and the “sticking” of the blood on the S.E., E.N., N.W. and W.S. horns duly performed. This order had to be followed in accordance with the general rule: כל פנות שאתה פונה לא יהו אלא דרך ימין “all turnings that have to be made in the Sanctuary must always be to the right.” Turning to the right from the ascent in the south, the first corner one comes to would be the south-eastern one. But with the עולה too, although its blood did not have to be taken to the top of the Altar but thrown from a distance on to the lower half, and so the ascent was not mounted at all, the blood was taken in the same way from the north side, the back of the Altar, where the killling and receiving of the blood had taken place, round to the foot of the ascent in the front and from there carried round the Altar to the corners desired — always turning to the right. As the first corner arrived at, the S.E. one, was not suitable for the “throwing of the blood” owing to its lacking the יסוד, the first suitable corner which the ministering priest arrived at, starting from and going round the Altar to the right, would be the north-east. (See Yoma 15 b, and Rashi thereon.)

But, if, as Rashi says (ibid), the reason for the front of the Altar being the south side and for the ramp being on that side was because the south was the side which was nearest to the entrance, and when one entered the Temple it was the south side of the Altar which one would first meet, this could fit in with the opinion that כוליה מזבח בצפון קאי (Zebachim 53 a & 58 a) that the whole of the Altar was within the northern half of the עזרה. Then, certainly, the door being in the centre, on entry one would first meet the ramp in the South. But the generally accepted view, given in the Mishna, Middoth V. 2, and also taught by Maimonides הל׳ בית הבחירה V. 13-15 is that the whole of the Altar, or at least by far the greatest part of it (27 or 25 of its 32 cubites, see תוספות יום טוב on Middoth V. 2) was within the southern half of the עזרה. Then it would be the north side, the back of the Altar which would be nearest to the entry, and the ramp on the south would be farthest from the entrance. So that there must be some very definite inner reason for the front of, and the ascent to, the Altar being on the south side.

If the way we have explained the symbolic meaning of the various sides be not erroneous, and the South side, as being the side of the מנורה, the side of Light and Spirit and understanding, then this reason lies very close to hand. By setting the Altar, and especially its front and its ramp in the south (even according to the view that כוליה מזבח בצפון the כבש was still בדרום) we are told that the lesson which the Altar has to teach us viz. “the way to get closer up to God”, but particularly the approach and the start up to this height, lies in the sphere of the spirit and clear thinking and understanding.

Judaism knows nothing of that nebulous hazy beatitude of feeling which subordinates clear thinking of the mind to the vague realm of feelings, and sees the nature of religion in just such subordination. Judaism makes no appeal to feelings as a means of influencing the mind. Judaism appeals to the mind, to intelligent understanding and clear thinking as a means of guiding, clarifying one’s feelings and making one really enthusiastic for them. It is only on the side of the Light where the ascent to its Altar stands, only from there does all “progress and all holding firm” begin, progress to, and holding firm to, all goodnes and nobility, and to getting near to God with both.

If, then, the front of the Altar is in the South, its back must be to the North, the side of the שולחן, the material. All קדשי קדשים, such as עולה חטאת ואִשם, offerings that have this in common, that they presuppose some fault in one’s active life שחיטתן בצפון וקבול דמן בכלי שרת בצפון have to be placed on the north side, the side of the ‘material-sensuous’, there the animal life, the life of living for oneself, has to be ended by שחיטה; there the entry into the higher existence of the Sanctuary begins by the קבלה. It is in material life of the senses that the root of deficiencies in progress of morality or firmness in morality lies.

Mila, the subordination and consecration of the material-sensuousness is the preliminary condition for the moral existence of the Nation, and the preliminary condition for the moral existence of each individual Jew. שחיטה בצפון וקבול דם בצפון, the cessation of the uncontrolled selfish life of the senses, and its being accepted under the guidance of the Sanctuary of the Torah, is the preliminary condition for being raised out of every moral deficiency. The “slaughtered one” awaiting resurrection to a higher moral life, is first brought בדרום, under the rays of the enlightening of the mind. From the south it is taken to the east to bring to its consciousness that every individual belongs to the ‘Nation of the Torah’. Then as its first activity, by being placed on the corner which strives upwards above the east-north base, the true estimation of the value of all the physical-material things of life and the use to which they are to be put, is demanded to be made from the point of view of one’s belonging to the national community, This gives the physical-material its first consecration. Everything material and pertaining to the senses is first elevated out of the jurisdiction of physical compulsion into the realm of free-willed morality as soon as the breath of selfishness is stripped from it, and it enters the service of one’s brother-man, and is used for the purposes of the general community. A penny, worked for, earned and spent entirely for oneself is no higher than the food which an animal takes to eat. But used to help a fellow-creature to live, or even earned and used to keep oneself alive for others, it belongs to the realm, to the moral free-willed realm, of duty, love and holiness. For it is not just the idea of belonging to a community in general, it is the consciousness of the “National Jewish calling of belonging to the Torah” that is awakened by the East side of the Temple; this Torah teaches everywhere not the doing away with the material and sensual, but demands, in the very first place, the utilisation of every phase of our material and sensual life for the realisation of holy purposes. It demands the coupling of all that is material, sensual and earthly with the moral, free, godly, eternal, “the planting of the heavenly, and the elevation of the earthly up to heavenly imperishableness”, as the Prophet puts it (Is. 51,16). This is the sum-total of the Jewish National calling, and so the life of the senses which had first been killed in “the pure North”, celebrates, by means of the enlightment it had gained in “the South,” its godly-human resurrection in the upward-striving corner of the east-north base.

Proceeding always to the right from the North to the West, this “creature of the spiritualised senses” is now taught to apply all the powers he possesses, all that has been granted to him on the “table” of his material existence, to the realisation of the Divine Torah which rests in the West beneath the wings of the Cherubim. For this purpose, it is brought home to him, on the corner striving upwards over the west-south base, that his second activity must be, devoting his whole life to his mental development, to his clear understanding of the meaning and spirit of the Torah, that והגית בו יומם ולילה is the indispensable condition for all future progress towards the moral heights. Unselfishness in one’s material life, and devoting one’s mental life to clear understanding of the Torah are the two energies to which one must devote one’s activities. It — the lack of these in the past and their fulfilment in the future — is what is preached by the שתי מתנות שהן ארבע בקרן מזרחית-צפונית ומערבית-דרומית and by this is achieved atonement for the previous slackness, and help to the one who is trying and seeking to get nearer to God in his earthly life.

In every case, the “service of the blood” finished up with שפיכת שירים ליסוד, with pouring the remainder of the blood which had not been used, out of the כלי שרת on to the base of the Altar. שפיכה differs from זריקה inasmuch as זריקה was a throwing from a distance, while for שפיכה the priest stood next to the base and poured the blood on to it. This שפיכת שירים ליסוד is mentioned expressly only in connection with חטאות פנימיות and חיצוניות(Ch. 4,7,18,28,30 & 34) ואת כל דם הפר ישפך אל יסור מזבח העולה but it is applied to all other offerings in the sentence ודם זבחיך ישפך (Deut. 12,27) or we find it indicated as being extended to all the Altar blood by the redundancy of words in the expression (Deut. 6,9) והנשאר בדם ימצה אל יסוד המזבח (Zebachim 37a). In the case of חטאות פנימיות where the מתנות הדם in the היכל took place on the מזבח הזהב the שפיכת שירים was made on the יסוד מערבי, in all other cases on the יסוד דרומי, in every case בסמוך לו on the place which at the conclusion of the מתנות, was nearest to the ministering priest. Coming out of the היכל this would be the west, coming down from the ramp it would be the South (Zebachim 53 a). The legal status of this שפיכת שירים is exactly the same as סמיכה it is מצוה but not מעכב (ibid 52 a). If we want to try and find the meaning or significance of this final act of the service of the blood we must first realise the difference between שפיכה and נתינה or זריקה. While זריקה and נתינה express the idea of devoting oneself to one of the aims which the Altar represents, שפיכה does not preach any particular way of living or direct ones energy in any particular direction, but expresses an innate existing condition of the נפש of the personality who is represented in the offering. זריקה and נתינה expresses activities which are expected from the שפיכה ,נפש shows the ground and fundamental soil in which the whole nature of the personality has its roots. It has its roots לפני ה׳, in the basis of the תורה — the West — or in the animation and enlightening of the mind and spirit which radiates from the תורה — the South — שפיכת שירים בדרום. It is, accordingly, the fruit, the result of the מתנות. Whatever the past may have been, the resolution that in future all ones energies will be directed to making progress, and to cling fast to all that is good — ensures that כל הדם, the whole being, the whole נפש of the person represented by the offering will have — what in its true inner depth it had never really lost — its roots embedded in the soil of the Torah, לפני ה׳, before God. Would it be too bold to suggest that שפיכת כל הדם אל היסוד is the opposite of הכרת הנפש מישראל ,הכרת הנפש מעמיה ,הכרת הנפש מלפני, as it says in Levit. 22,3. This is literally, being cut off, hewn down from the standpoint with which נפש has its roots in its People, in Israel, before God. After all, it is primarily such sins that could result in כרת that have to seek their atonement in the מתנות הדם on the Altar of the Torah. Does its previous slackness and carelessness threaten להכרת הנפש מיסודה בקרב עמיה לפני ה׳, the resolution for future faithfulness to duty, as expressed by נתינת הנפש על המזבח, gives the firm continuance ביסוד ישראל לפני ה׳ back again to the נפש.

והקריבו את הדם חרקו את הדם. The unnecessary repetition of הדם is, according to Zebachim 81 b, a note to remind us of the Halacha that the זריקה takes place even if the relation of the דם to its special offering has lost its definiteness by becoming mixed with some blood of some other offering, or even with some ordinary blood.

V. 6. הפשט וניתוח כשרה בזר (Yoma 22 a), that is why it says והפשיט etc. quite generally, as ושחט above, and in the following verse the בני אהרן are again specifically mentioned. By the definite article ה- and the specialising אותה the הפשט and ניתוח are limited to עולות כשרות. In the case of פסולין even if עלו and so לא ירדו (see on Ex. 29,37) they were neither flayed nor disjointed (Zebachim 85 a). It does not say ונתח אותה לנתחים but לנתחיה, the animal is not to be cut into any pieces but into its pieces i.e., into its natural parts, also לנתחיה and not נתחיה לנתחים, not the parts which form the organs of a whole animal cut up into smaller parts.

V. 7. This bringing fire to the Altar and arranging the wood נתינת האש and עריכת העצים are not part of the “service of the offerings” like הפשט ונתוח ,שחיטה etc. The fire was always burning on the Altar, must never be allowed to go out, as commanded in Ch. 6,2-6. In accordance with this command, every morning several מערכות for various purposes were laid and lit. But there was one special one, a מערכה גדולה, a large pile of wood was stacked up and kindled, as the Altar fire, that was always ready and awaiting its offerings. This Altar fire, that had to be kept burning uninterruptedly, was accordingly, always to hand when an offering was to be given over to the fire on the Altar so there was no necessity for a special kindling to be done. If, nevertheless, the preparation and making of the fire is mentioned here, between ניתוח and הקטרת איברים this can only be for the purpose of reminding one, at this stage, when about to place the limbs etc. on the fire, of the duty of keeping up this fire in general, and the application of what this fire and this duty means to this particular offering (see Rashi, Yoma 27 b). Yoma 21 b and 45 a tells us that this sentence ונתנו בני אהרן הכהן אש על המזבח teaches the duty אף על פי שאש יורדת מן השמים מצוה להביא מן ההדיוט, that, in addition to the fire which came down from Heaven ( — and which, as the ת״כ remarks remained burning from Moses’ time till the Temple was consecrated in Solomon’s time, and then, the fire which came down again continued burning until the days of Menasseh) it was a duty to bring ordinary fire on the Altar. It is also taken to refer as well to הצתת אליתא lighting thin dry sticks by means of which the big pile, the מערכה גדולה, was ignited. All had to be done בראשו של מזבח and בכהן כשר ובכלי שרת, by a priest eligible for service and clothed in the priestly garments of service (see תוספות Yoma 45 a). וערכו עצים על האש refers, according to Yoma 26 b, to the service, that every evening before the daily evening תמיד, the תמיד של בין הערבים, two logs were laid on by two כהנים, while referring to the morning offering וערד הכהן עצים בבקר בבקר (in the singular) ובער עליה (Levit. 6,5) before the morning תמיד was offered, two logs were kindled by one priest.

If, as we believe we have correctly understood it, the fire on the Altar represents the Torah as אשדת, as that element which, like fire, illuminating and warming, refining and reviving, penetrating our whole being, and as אריאל and אש אוכלה, is to “eat up”, to absorb every aspect of our whole being, so that every phase of our life becomes its “food” i.e. becomes nourishment for keeping godliness alive on earth. If all this is true, then it is no small significance that אש הדיוט was added to the אש מן השמים on the Altar. So that the fire on the Altar flamed in the name of God and the Nation; God and the Nation proclaimed the Torah as אש. The אש מן השמים demanded in the name of God the “power and force of fire” for His Torah, the אש הדיוט brought to it the כהנים as the sanctuary-representatives of the Nation, expressed the national recognition of this demand. The continuous tending of this fire, the שני גזרי עצים בבקר and שני גזרי עצים בין הערבים bring to mind that this representation of the Torah as the all mastering power of fire, is not to be acknowledged just once in principle, but is to be kept maintained unceasingly afresh in the minds of the Jewish people. The שני גזרי עצים by one כהן in the morning and the שני גזרי עצים by two כהנים in the evening would represent: the recognition of and the keeping alive of, this way of regarding the Torah is the responsibility of both, the whole community as such (one priest with two logs) as well as that of the separate individuals (two Cohanim each with one log). Alternatively it can be taken: the individual with the sum of all his powers (one Cohan with two logs) as well as the Community with its combined forces (two Cohanim each with one log). But above all, he who would keep up the fire of God’s Torah and see that its demands are fulfilled, must himself stand בראש המזבח, must himself be on the height of the Altar. Woe unto him who, in the words of the Gemora — Yoma 45 a — קאי אארעא ועביד במפוחא, imagines that he can kindle and blow up the fire for others and himself remain standing below on the ground!

All this meaning of the Altar-fire is brought home to the one who is bringing his “elevating-offering” and by it seeking to get nearer to God, just at this point where he is occupied in the איברים) נתחי קרבנו) with the idea of having that which represents every part of his being — his being which has already been dedicated to strive upwards to the utmost heights of God’s Torah, and which is now standing ready, prepared to carry out this vow — given over to this very Altar-fire by the servitor of the Sanctuary of the Torah. The fire which is maintained generally is also prepared for him, the demands made by God’s Torah in general are directed to him also, are awaiting quite specially his devotion; for the Jewish National mission is fulfilled, not by public national devotion, but by the devotion of all its individuals; and only in making his contribution to the general mission does the individual really achieve his vocation.

So that verses 6 & 7 taken together say: Just like שחיטה, the giving up of the unsanctified living for oneself has to be done, not by the Sanctuary but by the person himself who is seeking by the offering to get nearer to God, or by his representative, in the same way, he and not the servitor of the Sanctuary as such, has himself to place his offering, divided into its single organic parts, ready for being given over to the Torah-fire on the Altar. But the Altar-fire itself, the expression of the demand the Torah makes on us, and to which all the will and energy of the one seeking to get nearer to God is henceforth to be given up to, that is to be established and maintained only by the servitors of the Torah-Sanctuary in their official capacity as such. The Altar-fire itself is to be there objectively and it is only in the homage brought to it and in the complete submission to it, that the subjective self-discipline of the sacrificer appears.

V. 8. את הנתחים. From Tamid III and IV and Yoma 25 a and b we learn, that, if it consists of a sheep, as i.e., the תמיד, an עולה was cut up into ten parts and the entrails. These ten parts were divided into five paired groups, each of which was brought to the Altar and laid out on the lower half of the ramp by one כהן before being given over to the fire, הולכת איברים לכבש. These parts were I (a) הראש עם הפדר the head with the cut surface covered with the omentum (the separate layer of fat that covers the entrails. I.L.); (b) רגל הימנית וב׳ ביצים עמה, the right hind leg with the testicles. 2. שתי ידים the two forelegs. 3 (a) העוקץ עם שתי צלעות מכאן ומכאן והאליה ואצבע הכבד וב׳ כליות עמו; the lower part of the backbone with the attached ribs on either side together with the rump, the extension of the liver and the two kidneys; (b) הרגל השמאל, the left hind-leg. 4 (a) החזה, the breast, (b) והגרה, the throat, עם שתי צלעות מכאן ומכאן ובה הקנה הלב והריאה, with the two upper ribs on either side with the air (and food (?)) tubes on them, the heart and the lungs. 5. דפנות, the two flanks: (a) דופן הימנית עם צלעות דקות למעלה ולמטה והכבד תלויה בה; (b) ודופן השמאלית עם ב׳ צלעות למעלה ולמטה והשדרה עמו והטחול תלוי בה; the two flanks with the backbone and the ribs above and below, the liver with the right flank and the spleen with the left. 6. הקרב וכרעים על גביהן, stomach and entrails together with the feet. So that bringing the parts of the offering over to the Altar in the case of a כבש was performed by six Cohanim. In the case of a פר it was done by eighteen Cohanim, as is apparent from Yoma 26 b. (actually it took twenty four, as six carried סלת and יין). This does not mean, as ראב״ד and קרבן אהרן in ת״כ take it to mean, that in the case of a פר the parts — in striking contradiction to the rule: ולא נתחיה לנתחים — were cut up into a greater number of parts, but as תוספות י״ט remarks referring to Maimonides הל׳ מעשה קרבנות VI,19, on account of the size and weight of the limbs of an ox, the carrying of the parts had to be given over to a large number of priests. While, for example, the head and the leg of a sheep were carried by one priest, in the case of a פר, the head alone was carried by one priest and the leg by two, etc. etc. The grouping of the parts of a פר was — as is evident from the Mishna (ibid) exactly the same as in case of a כבש, namely שתי ,הראש והרגל ,העוקץ והרגל החזה והגרה ,הקרביים ,שתי ידים ,דפנות, the same six groups. For the reason that the order is given differently here, see תוספות ibid.

As then the normal grouping of a כבש is the foundation for the grouping of the parts even of a פר, we can all the easier understand why ר׳ עקיבא in ת״כ and Yoma 27 a, where it refers principally to a פר, finds the standard rule indicated for a כבש. The principle of the grouping itself is laid down in the change from וערכו בני אהרן הכהנים וגו׳ in our verse to וערך הכהן אותם in verse 12, inasmuch as by וערכו a number of priests are indicated as being necessary for the הולכת איברים while וערך הכהן אותם implies more than one part be given to a single priest. (The significance of the grouping and pairing etc. has been worked out by Hirsch in his article on the sequence etc. of the ברכות of our daily Schemona Essre which, ofcourse, was instituted as a parallel to the קרבן תמיד; he refers his readers to this article originally issued in Jeshurun XI & XII. It is reproduced in the Gesammelte Schriften. — I.L.).

את הנתחים את הראש ואת הפדר. As the head is mentioned here in addition to the נתחים and not taken as included in them, it is clear that it must have been separated from the body already without the נתוח prescribed for the body in the previous verse. This is taken in Chulin 27 a, as a reference to the traditional law that שחיטה מן הצואר that שחיטה has to be done by a cut straight across the throat. פדר as explained by רמב״ן, is the fatty layer which covers the entrails like a cloth, elsewhere it is designated as חלב המכסה את הקרב. It is not the active fat in use in the tissues but it is a cohesive independent layer separated from the organs, so that it forms a part by itself and does not belong to the נתחים which have to be cut asunder. The ראש ופדר form the two extremes of the animal organism The head is the individuality of the animal concentrated to its highest mental capacity. In it, therefore, lies the regulating power of the whole animal creature. The פדר fat is that which is, for the time being, separated from the organism and laid aside as capital to be eventually drawn upon and used as and when required.

על העצים אשר על האש אשר על המזבח: by this phrasing the עצים get their significance and meaning from the אש, and the אש from the מזבח. Hence the sentence in Thamid 29 b: עצים אשר על האש, עצים הנתוכים להיות אש “wood which easily is transformed to fire,” (lit, “dissolves” into fire). Further: על המזבח, שלא יהו עצים יוצאין מן המזבח כלום (Zebachim 62b) the wood may not project over the edges of the Altar. The offering is, not to be given over to fire but to the Altar-fire. Finally מה מזבח משל :על העצים וגו׳ צבור אף עצים ואש משל צבור, מה מזבח שלא נשתמש בו הדיוט אף עצים ואש שלא נשתמש בהן הדיוט (Menachoth 22 a). Like the Altar, the wood and the fire are not to be brought by the individual offerers, but by the Community, and like the Altar, may not have been used for any other purpose. The fire on the Altar is simply meant to be the Altar become alive, to be the summons and demand that, on the soil of the Jewish Nation, before the Sanctuary of God’s Torah, the earth — and earthly matters— are to be worked upwards to God. The Fire and that which is to become fire, the wood, stand therefore, completely in the character of the Altar itself.

We note further: In verse 7, at the order for bringing fire on to the Altar it says, בני אהרן הכהן. This is the sole occasion on which this expression occurs in the תורה, everywhere else as indeed here in our very verse referring to the הולכת איברים לכבש, it says בני אהרן הכהנים. We have already remarked in Ex.XXVIII,1, that the priestly service refers primarily to Aaron, to the High Priest, the כה״ג to whom the כהני הדיוט stand as sons to a father, as helpers, to carry out part of the service on his behalf. The כה״ג, clad in the שמנה בגדים — and only so is he the כה״ג of the Sanctuary — represents the ideal which is to be reached by the Jewish individual, and by the Jewish National life, following the dictates of the Torah which rests in the Sanctuary. Now it is this very ideal, not merely the preparatory stages as represented by the כהני הדיוט, which is prescribed as the ultimate goal by the transformation of the whole individual and national existence which the Altar-fire demands. So not as בני אהרן הכהנים but as בני אהרן הכהן, as being in the service of the ministrant of the highest Jewish ideals do the priests have to kindle the Fire on the Altar. As the מזבח החיצון forms only the preliminary stages to the מזבח הפנימי the הקטרה על מזבח החיצון only the preliminary stage to the קטרת על מזבח הפנימי, so is this relationship, so essential for the whole idea of the מקדש and especially so for the עזרה and for what is to be performed in it, to be brought home to our minds by the appellation בני אהרן הכהן just here at the first teaching of the kindling of the fire on the Altar by which the whole demand of the עזרה-stage is expressed. Hence it is on this verse also that the Gemora says (Zebachim 18 a) ונתנו בני אהרן הכהן, נכהונו לימד על כה״ג שלבש בגדי כהן הדיוט ועבד עבודתו פסולה, וערכו בני אהרן הכהנים וגו׳, הכהנים מכאן לכהן הדיוט שלבש בגדי כהן גדול ועבד עבודתו פסולה that both the כה״ג and the כהן הדיוט must appear when they officiate in the garments which characterise the relative nature of their service. Every עבודה performed either by the כה״ג in the garments of a כהן הדיוט or by a כהן הדיוט in the garments of a כה״ג is פסולה.

But it still remains to be established exactly which procedure is to be understood by וערכו וגו׳, הנתחים וגו׳, על העצים וגו׳ in this verse. From the wording one would take it to be the הקטרת האברים על גבי המזבח, as well as הולכת האברים מן הכבש למזבח. But in the following verse the washing of the entrails and the feet is prescribed as having still to be done, and only after that does it say: והקטיר הכהן וגו׳. To which must be added that as already remarked above, in the succeeding expressions וערך הכהן וגו׳, וערכו וגו׳ has been found the principle of the grouping and ordering of the “parts”, that the bringing of the parts of a כבש has to be done by six כהנים and the corresponding parts of a פר by a greater number, but in any case in six groups. But this grouping and bringing over the ‘parts’ by six or more כהנים is definitely to be understood as referring only to the הולכת אברים לכבש, only to the bringing over to, and laying out on, the lower half of the ramp. Taking them over from there to the fire, the actual הקטרה, was done, according to the generally accepted version, by one single כהן (see תוספות and רש״י Yoma 26 b ד״ה והא תניא שבעה עשר also רמב״ם הל׳ תמידין ומוספין ד״ח). Also רמב״ן and בעל המאור ibid. Only תוספות ישנים ibid are of the opinion that the הולכה מן כבש למזבח was done by as many כהנים as by the bringing of them to the כבש, and so would seem to have been the opinion of ר׳ אליעזר בן יעקב according to whom המעלה אברים לכבש הוא המעלה אותן למזבח which view however, is not accepted as Halacha. According to all this, we must take the וערכו וגו׳ הנתחים וגו׳ על העצים וגו׳ to refer only to הולכת אברים לכבש and then the על העצים would have the meaning “with direction towards” as it has in וזבחת עליו וגו׳ in Ex. 20,21 and in ונתת על המערכת וגו׳ Levit. 24,7. Even if וערכו וגו׳ is taken to refer to סידור איברים על גבי המזבח, the Gemora in Menachoth 27 a, is still undecided whether the על is to be understood as על ממש or whether על בסמוך, placing them next to the wood would suffice.

V. 9. כרעים .וכרעיו seem to be the lower joints of the foot which the animal bends over when it kneels. Both parts, the entrails and the feet require washing to clean them from any extraneous matter that does not belong to the offering (and which would have no symbolic meaning as each and every part of the animal has — I.L.).

והקטיר וגו׳ המזבחה. See note on Ex. 29,13. This giving the parts of the offering over to the Altar-fire constitutes the second great act of the procedure which is essentially accomplished by זריקת דם והקטרת איברים in the case of an עולה. In Deut. 12,27, we read ועשית עלתיך הבשר והדם על מזבח ה׳ אלהיך “Your elevation-offering is accomplished by the flesh and blood on the Altar of your God”. From this Zebachim 104 a, derives the intimate connection between these two procedures of the offering, the זריקת הדם and the הקטרת איברים, both with regards to the outer form, as well as their complementary nature which makes each one essential for the other. With regard to the form of the procedure מה דם בזריקה אף בשר בזריקה in both cases it consisted of a throwing, just as the blood was thrown towards the Altar from a distance, similarly were the parts of the offering thrown on to the fire. There was an empty space left between the top of the ramp and the Altar אויר בין כבש למזבח expressly to mark the essential nature of this act of throwing on to the Altar-fire (see לחם משנה on הל׳ מעשה הקרבנות VI,4). In a similar way to זריקת הדם the זריקת הבשר teaches the necessity for resolving to resolute progress in the future, both call for the same energetic directing one’s will to moral purposes. But both belong together and each is essential for the other. If דם represents the נפש, the inner individual presonality, then בשר represents the איברים the complex of all those activities by means of which the will achieves its purpose; בשר is the announcing and fulfilling messenger of the נפש. The זריקת הדם makes the demand on the נפש that it shall form the will to devote all its powers to the desire to work on oneself to reach the moral heights of what a man is meant to be; the זריקת האברים makes the demand that this theoretical decision shall be translated into practical action, that all the activities which stand at the command of the נפש shall be given up with all one’s energy to the one purpose: to be food (fuel) for keeping godliness alive in the world by carrying out the Will of God. Now we are taught that both are mutually complementary, each is necessary for the other, אם אין דם אין בשר, אם אין בשר אין דם (ibid), if the blood can not be thrown on to the Altar, none of the “parts” may be given over to the fire, and if there are no “parts” to be given over to the Altar-fire, the blood can not be thrown on to the Altar. זריקת איברים without זריקת דם would be doing the right thing externally without inner inspiration and consecration. זריקת דם without זריקת איברים would be having the inner consecration and inspiration, but being satisfied to leave it at this inner feeling without translating it in one’s outer life to the exercising of one’s will in active deed. The nearness to God that is sought by bringing an offering is only to be found in the harmonious working together of the whole of the inner and outer life of thought and deed, theory and practice. Neither external correctness without devotion of the mind, nor any amount of learning and working on one’s inner self without submitting one’s external life to the dictates of God’s Torah is the way which leads up to God. The Sanctuary of the Torah teaches that it is only in allegiance to the Torah which emanates from within, and in an inner allegiance to the Torah which leads to an outward conforming life, that the path that leads upward is to be found. “Only in בשר and דם is our elevating-offering achieved on the Altar of our God.” These two procedures belong so much together that, according to רשב״א the הקטרת איברים has even to be done by the same כהן who did the זריקת דם (see מל״ל on הלי תמידים ומוספין IV,6).
