But as here it says: והקטיר הכהן את הכל וגו׳ that the whole animal with all its parts is to be given over to the Fire, and on the other hand in the verse quoted above it says: ועשית עולתיך הבשר והדם that what is to be given over to the fire is only the בשר, the flesh and nerve tissue, the Gemora teaches that bones, tendons, horns, claws etc., are only to be brought on to the Altar when attached to flesh, but if they have become separated are not to be brought (העצמות והגידים והקרנים והטלפים בזמן שהם מחוברים יעלו פירשו לא יעלו Zebachim 55 b). For it is just בשר, muscles and nerves, representing action, the life of activity which can serve to keep alive the fires of God and so can be used as fuel on the Altar to keep up the Altar-fire. עצמות etc. the passive instruments for carrying out activities only belong to the Altar when in conjunction with the בשר.

עלה אשה ריח ניחוח לה׳ is in apposition to הכל, everything has to be given over to the fire as עלה וגו׳. I am inserting here the gist of the explanation which Hirsch gives in נחוח — :בראשית is the noun form of נוח and does not occur except in this connection. נוח is movement come to rest and הניח really means to bring to rest, to grant rest and is also used for the granting of a wish, to give satisfaction, as in יסר בנך ויניחך (Pro. XXIX) פגי ילכו והנחתי לך (Ex. XXXIII). But the root נוח never occurs with this meaning for giving satisfaction to physical senses as it would have to if ריח ניחוח were to mean “a sweet savour”, a pleasant smell. There is one single occasion where it does seem to have that meaning, viz. Job,XXXVI,16, but Hirsch shows how just there, particularly there, it must express giving spiritual satisfaction. So that ריח ניחוח means: “the smell” of Satisfaction, of fulfilment of wishes, not that the smell itself gives pleasure. דיח comes from the root רוח, the wind. The fact that רחים means a pulverizer shows that ריח does not primarily indicate expressing the sense of smell but refers more to the nature of the substance diffusing odour. A substance only has a smell if finest particles of it are volatilized. Smell is that sense by which the finest particles of a substance which may be at a distance come into direct contract. Whereas the senses of taste and touch require the substance itself to come into direct contract with the organs of these senses, and sight and hearing receive sensations from a distance, the sense of smell stands in the middle. The objects may remain at a distance as in sound and sight, but particles of them must touch the organ, as in taste and touch. Hence ריח, smell, is used as a metaphor for receiving the finest realisation of something Thus in Job 14,19 מריח מים יפריח from ‘the smell’ of water the withered plant blossoms again, and XXXIX,25 מרחוק יריח מלחמה, the charger “smells” the war from afar. So that if ריח in general means: perception of the faintest expression, an offering as ניחוח would be a slight, just an indication of the gratification of God’s wishes, an expression which is only a hint of our desire to fulfil the wishes of God. The offering itself is not ניחוח, compliance, but ריח ניחוח, an indication of compliance. I have accordingly translated it “a hint of the desire to please God”—I.L.]. On this Zebachim 46 b teaches: לשם ששה דברים הזבח נזבח, לשם זבח, לשם זובח, לשם השם, לשם אשים, לשם ריח, לשם ניחוח “In a sixfold sense is the offering to be made, (a) in the thought of the particular kind of offering for which it is brought, (b) in the sense of its being the offering of the particular person whose offering it is, (c) in the sense of its being directed to God, (d) with the sense of its producing ריח, (e) with the idea of its being fuel for the fire, (f) and with the idea of complying with the Will of God. These ideas — with the exception of (b) לשם זובח which finds its explanation on 4 a ibid, and can find no mention in our verse as our verse speaks primarily of הקטרה and the reference to the person is only absolutely essential at the four עבודות דם (which represents the נפש the personality), see תוספות Zebachim 2 a and מל״מ מעשה הקרבנות IV,11 — are explained as being referred to in our verse as follows: עולה לשם עולה לאפוקי לשם שלמים דלא, אשה לשם אשה לאפוקי כבבה דלא, ריח לשם ריח לאפוקי אברים שצלאן והעלן דלא, ניחוח לשם הנחת רוח לה׳ מי שאמר והיה העולם The עולה must be brought as עולה and similarly every other offering in the thought of its special character and not in that of another offering e.g. an עולה thinking it is a שלמים etc.: as לשם אשים ,אשה to be completely consumed in the Fire, to be actually fuel for the Fire and not with some such idea as the flesh to be roasted; as ריח, with the idea that the smell of the actual burning is spread and not in such a way that the smell arises by allowing the flesh to roast even before it comes on to the Altar-fire: ניחוח as הנחת רוח to give spiritual satisfaction; לה׳ as directed to a God Who is thought of as ה׳ the God of Love. (On אשה see Ch. 3,11).

As this law does not run: אשה לאפוקי כבבה דלא, ריח לאפוקי איברים שצלאן וכו׳, but אשה לשם אשה, ריח לשם ריח לאפוקי וכוי, etc., it is clear that not only the acutal bringing of it as כבבא as איברים שצלאן is repudiated, but that not even a thought of such an intention may be in the mind at the precedure (and according to one view in Zebachim 2 a, in תוספות at any of the procedures of the offering e.g., at the שחיטה there may be no intention להקטיר כבבא etc., see מל״מ I c. Hence all these ideas must be intimately in connection with the very nature of the whole idea of an offering, as their absence is able to cancel the whole idea of the offering. That this should be so seems perfectly clear, and self evident in עולה לשם עולה לאפוקי לשם שלמים, דלא. That it is necessary for the specific nature of any particular offering to be clearly understood (or even to be expressly mentioned) see תוספות ibid and Baba Mazia 43 b) needs no explanation — אשה לשם אשה לאפוקי כבבא דלא, the roasting of the parts of the offering at the Altar-fire (as might conceivably be done at e.g. the קרבן פסח which is to be eaten by the בעלים) would be in direct contradiction to the idea of the offering being אכילת מזבח, or as it is more generally termed לחם אשה ה׳ “food for the Fire of God”. As כבבא it would look as if the offering itself were the purpose and the Fire merely a means of its preparation, whereas the very contrary is what is intended. The אשדת is to be kept up on the Altar, on the הראל as אריאל, the Fire of God’s Torah is to be kept alive on this world-which-wants-to raise-itself upwards-to-God, (the מזבח — I.L.) in its all-mastering and all-absorbing power, it is to find its “food” in the devotion of the whole active life of those that seek to get nearer to God by the aid of offerings. The idea of אשה accordingly is diametrically opposite to and entirely excludes that of ריח .ריח לשם ריח לאפוקי איברים שצלאן והעלן דלא — .כבבא carries the news of what is happening into the far distance. We have already on Gen. 8,21, shown how ריח in general describes the receiving and recognising of the slightest and most distant impressions, and also that ניחוח or rather the root נוח in its active form, is never used for satisfaction of the senses. If then, it is demanded that the offering is to be brought with the intention that the burning is to proclaim itself afar by ריח, just this intention ensures the symbolic character of the whole procedure. What is happening up there on the Altar is to be noticed, to be given attention to. So that it is not the burning in itself as such which must be intended, but the idea of which the burning is but a slight indication must be present. להעלות איברים שצלאן which, as Zebachim 46 b explains, would do away with ריח, would allow the whole object of the burning to be summed-up in the concrete procedure of burning. — ניחוח לשם הנחת רוח does away with the erroneous conception that offerings could be brought with the idea of the offering itself giving some concrete satisfaction to the concrete senses of the Godhead, it is His satisfaction with us, our readiness to fulfil His will that we are to express when we try to get nearer to God by an offering. לשם מי שאמר והיה העולם ,לה׳ or as it puts it in לשם מי שעשה את העולם :ספרא, we see here too, — as we have already worked out in Gen. 2,4 — how far the conception which our חכמים have of the meaning of this Name is from that erroneous way of taking it as an expression of the transcendental idea of eternity, ה׳ is an active form of the verb “to be” and does not designate “the one Who exists for all time” but “the One Who creates all that exists”.

It is not required that the one who performs the various procedures of the offering should have to actually say “ לשם וגו׳ ” these six essential points, as long as they are in his mind, and he expresses nothing to the contrary it can be assumed that סתמא לשמן (Zebachim 46 b and 2 b). Indeed the positive pronouncing is discouraged to prevent the possibility of a slip of the tongue (such as saying לשם שלמים when you mean to say לשם עולה I.L.) אתנו בית דין דלא לימא לשמו דלמא אתי למימר שלא לשמו (ibid).

The effect of a wrong pronouncement (שלא לשמן) on the validity of the offering varies in different cases. עולה לשם שלמים) שנוי קדש) and עולת לוי לשם שמעון) שנוי בעלים) leave the קרבן objective as an offering כשר, but the person who had to bring it has not thereby fulfilled his obligation, and would have to bring another offering, כל הזבחים שנזבחו שלא לשמן כשרים אלא שלא עלו לבעלים לשם חובה (Zebachim 2 a). Only in the cases of פסח and חטאת is the קרבן altogether פסול (ibid). שנוי in the other four points does not affect the validity of the offering at all (תוספות ibid).

Characteristic and decisive for the whole way of looking at offerings is the fact that it is not what is in the mind of the one who brings the offering, the בעלים, but in the mind of the ministrant on the Altar that counts. אין המחשבה הולכת אלא אחר העובד (Zebachim 46 b). This sentence proves that the whole procedure of offerings is not an expression of thoughts, feelings and resolutions which may exist in the mind of the person who is trying to get nearer to God by means of an offering, but is meant to express quite definitely the demands that the Sanctuary-of-the-Torah makes as being the only means of getting near to God. It is these thoughts, these feelings, these resolutions which those who bring offerings have to accept, and to express their willingness to do so by handing over the offering to the Sanctuary. Not primarily as שלוחי דידן, as our representatives, but in the first place as שלוחי דרחמנא do those that perform the procedure of the offerings stand there; by order of the Sanctuary do they carry out the procedure (see Nedarim 35 b, Yoma 19 b תוספות).

V. 10-13. If, as we have already remarked on v. 3 an offering brought from צאן represents a personality looked at from the angle of his lot depending on the guidance of God, as being a member of God’s flock, while those brought from בקר are looked on from the point of view of their mission to work in the world, as workers in God’s fields, so that each of these kinds of offerings belongs respectively to one of the two aspects which together comprise the whole idea of human life; then it can easily be understood why עולת בקר and עולת צאן, although completely alike in all details of the rites to be performed, are nevertheless taught in two separate paragraphs, which, however, are complementary to each other, and whose belonging together is shown by the copulative-conjunction ו at the beginning of the צאן paragraph — ויו מוסיף על ענין ראשון וילמד עליון מתחתון (Zebachim 48 a). (The “vav” connects and adds the second paragraph to the first, so that what is said in either paragraph can be taken to apply equally to the other — I.L.). For it is the one and same lesson of unceasing progress in life, עולה which is taught both from the standpoint of one’s duty (בקר) and from that of the dependence of one’s fate in life on God (צאן) and, as, for inner reasons, the Law of עולה was to be taught in two sections, some of the essential laws, e.g. צפון and פסול חולה זקן ומזוהם are reserved for the second פרשה as complementary to the first. By keeping in mind the inner difference of these two פרשיות (i.e. the different symbolic reference which צאן and בקר make — I.L.), the actual factual differences in the second פרשה as well as certain deviations in the language, can perhaps be explained.

מן הצאן מן הכבשים מן העזים. The choice of animals which is given in V. 2, is here still further restricted by the limitation implied by the repeated “מן״. According to Bechoroth 41 a, this excludes זקן חולה ומזוהם, the old and infirm (see איסורי מזבח מל״מ II,b), the sick, and the evil-smelling. The exclusion of רובע ונרבע מוקצה נעבד ונוגח, all cases where the unfitness for offerings is brought about by sin, is given in the paragraph of עולת בקר where the working of oneself upwards to higher standards is taught from the standpoint of the duties of one’s working life (בקר I.L.). The unfitness of זקן חולה ומזוהם which all represent a condition of ill-fortune, the mishaps of fate, are taught here in the paragraph of עולת צאן, which is to teach the working of oneself upwards to higher standards from the standpoint of our fate, our fortune resting in, and dependent on, the guidance of God. This limitation is meant to stress the point that not just in condition of suffering or misfortune, but that conditions of full strength and vigour and health, unweakened and serene, are the state in which we are to seek to get nearer and nearer to God by our progressive activity in carrying out the dictates of the Will of God as revealed to us in His Torah. Not only in old age, in illness and in loneliness, but in “the freshness of youth, in glowing health, and from the midst of social life” are we meant to strive up the path to God in spiritual and moral perfection, and indeed זכר תמים, with all the virile vigour which is granted to us, and with the whole of ourselves, no part of ourselves to be missing.

סמיכה is not repeated in the paragraph on עולת צאן. If at עולת בקר, where from the standpoint of בקר we bring an עולה, already conscious of our duty to be workers for God we still have to bring to our minds that each one of us is a representative of the People of Israel, and, as such, in the name of the National Mission have to demand of ourselves that we carry out the requirements of the Torah, then in the case of an עולת צאן it is surely required, where the feeling that we are not active enough arises only from the standpoint of our dependance on God.

ושחט וגו׳ צפונה וגו׳. On the other hand צפון is to be found mentioned at שחיטה וקבלה בצפון .עולת צאן giving up the material selfish life of the senses, and bringing just this life into the realm of higher things, as the very first preliminary condition for working upwards to God, is taught just at עולת צאן, although the dependance of the whole material existence on God is just there already present in the mind of the bringer. For this simple feeling of dependance is just insipid and meaningless if it leads merely to hopes and not to obedience; if it does realise that all the good things of life do come from God but is not willing to use them as the holy property of God, to be used solely fulfilling His Will also with the material side of life. The reason for placing the teaching of סמיכה for all עולות in the paragraph on עולת בקר and that of צפון in that of עולת צאן seems to us to be strikingly clear. סמיכה and בקר both lie in the sphere of thought of action, deeds, while צפון and צאן are in the sphere of thought of fate, fortune.

ונתח אותו לנתחיו, above it says ונתח אותה לנתחיה, above the object is עולה hence the feminine suffix, here it is either קרבן or צאן hence the masculine. Above, the עולה-idea of consecrating one’s acts and deeds is already present in the choice of the animal itself בקר, hence its predominance. Here at צאן, it is the personality “shepherded” by God that represents itself in the animal, and it is just only by being actually given over to the Altar that it receives, and all its parts become absorbed into the עולה idea. Hence in the preliminary laying out the parts in order, before placing it on the Altar, our verse takes it rather as the sheep of God’s flock than as the עולה it is to become. Also, when he brings a בן בקר, representing himself as a “worker”, the bringer looks on himself (or herself) as being virile, strong, (masculine), and the offering has rather to remind him of his dependence on, and devotion (feminine) to the Will of God with regards to his deeds. In the case of צאן, representing himself as a sheep of God’s flock, the ruling feeling is the consciousness of dependance, and the offering then has to awake in the bringer the consciousness of virile masculine strength for deed in the service of God.

וערך וגו׳. The difficulty occured to us already above to decide precisely what procedure is to be understood by עריכת הנתחים על העצים וגו׳. The difficulty is even greater in this פרשה, as not only, as above, the washing of the entrails comes after, but because the carrying of the parts to, and laying them down in order on the ramp איברים לכבש is only first expressed in V. 13 in והקריב הכהן את הכל as explained in Yoma 27 a. So that according to that, וערך וגו׳ can not even be taken to refer to that procedure. Perhaps וערך etc. refers altogether to the first “ordering” of the parts of the offering, i.e. the actual dividing the offering in the first instance into groups of parts that belong together with symbolic meaning, as we have proved in our article on the “Schemone Essre”, showing how closely the ברכות are arranged parallel to the grouping of the parts of the עולה. Then the על העצים would mean “for the wood” i.e. for the purpose of the parts being finally given over on to the wood, and the principle would then be indicated, for which they are to be grouped and ordered. They are to be arranged in accordance with the idea of their being offered on the Fire of the Altar, which has to be maintained by the Nation (עצים), and from that can be deduced the double principle of the arrangement: (a) the pairing of the parts in accordance with the underlying idea of their belonging together viz. the head and the hind foot, the two forefeet, etc., etc., and (b) the order in which they were to be brought to the Altar.

והקריב הכהן וגו׳ is, as we have just remarked, definitely the הולכת איברים לכבש. If — as we took it to be in the article on the Schemone Essre — the laying down of the ‘parts’ on the ramp of the Altar, before giving them over to the Fire, was meant to impress on us the idea that it is only God Whom we have to thank for the gifts and abilities which these limbs or parts represent, so that we are merely giving back to Him what we have received from Him, if this is so, we can understand why this procedure is specially and primarily mentioned in the פרשת עולת צאן where just the idea of “God’s care for us”, is predominant.

עולה הוא. In ת״כ on these words it says: — עולה, אע״פ שלא הפשיט, אע״פ שלא נתח או אע״פ שלא שחט בצפון ת״ל הוא מה ראית וכו׳ מפני מה אני מכשיר בהפשט וניתוח שהן לאחר הרציה, פוסל בצפון שהוא לפני הרציה according to which the אשה ריח וגוי is to be taken as a consequence of and not as the foundation of the עולה character. Not, it is an עולה because it comes as a “gift to the fire” (אשה — I.L.) on the Altar, but it is an עולה, and therefore it comes on the Altar as a “gift to the fire”. The offering has the עולה-character before it is changed to smoke on the Altar, even without it. The nature of the offering in definitely fixed by, and in, the זריקה, this is what the ת״כ calls “רציה״. All the rites which have to be performed after the זריקה are only מצזה but are not מעכב. As mentioned above, at the time of the זריקה the possibility of the הקטרה must be there. But if after the זריקה has been done, the איברים and אימורים even get lost or become unfit, so that no הקטרה at all can be done, the character of the offering remains unaltered. This fact also goes to prove that the real idea of the עולה is not to be sought in the fact of its being entirely burnt on the Altar, but in the idea of working oneself ever upwards towards the loftiest heights as is expressed by זריקה למטה (the ת״ב on V. 17 על פסוק עולה הוא גבי עולת העוף ועי׳ שם בק״א requires going into).

V. 14. ואם מן העוף עולה קרבנו. The only case where birds can be brought as a קרבן נדבה — and this whole chapter speaks exclusively of such offerings — is as an עולה. There is no such thing as a שלמים of עוף. That is why it does not say, as in V. 10, ואם מן העוף קרבנו but ואם מן העוף עולה קרבנו, i.e. a קרבן מן העוף can only be an עולה. “If he wants to bring this one קרבן from העוף namely עולה then etc.”

מן העוף again implies a limitation, but the limitation to the choice are not as great as in the case of תמות תכרות בבהמה ואין תמות :עולת בהמה וזכרות בעופות, יכול יבשה גפה, נקטעה רגלה, או נחטטה עינה ת״ל מן השף ולא כל העוף (Kiddushin 24 b). Neither חמים nor זכר is demanded in the case of birds, no attention need be paid to the sex, nor is complete bodily perfection demanded, but they may not be מחוסר איבד, may not have the loss or atrophy of a whole limb, such as an atrophied wing, a broken leg, an eye poked out etc.

קרבנו וגו׳ :והקריב: in contrast to the תקריבו את קרבנכם of the קרבן מהמה (V. 2); a קרבן עוף can only be brought by single individuals, representing a private personality. There is no קרבן צבור which consists of birds (Themura 14 a).

מן התרים או מן בני היונה of תרים it is only the older ones, of יונה only the young that may be brought, hence it never says בני התור and never יונים. The age of the birds can be determined by the colour of the wings. The intermediate stage when the colour has begun to form, but is not yet completed may not be brought either in a תור or in a יונה (Chulin 22 a ואם מן העוף וגו׳, והקריב מן התורים וגו׳ (תחלת הציהוב שבזה ובזה only תורים and בני יונה may be used for bird-offerings (ת״כ).

V. 15. והקריבו: even one single bird can be brought. — והקריבו הכהן ומלק. While at a קרבן בהמה the שחיטה may be done by a non-Kohen, at a קרבן עוף everything, even the מליקה which corresponds to the שחיטה has to be done by a כהן and even by בעצמו של כהן, literally by the כהן himself, by means of his finger nails and not with a knife. והקריבו אל המזבח ומלק והקטיר, the bringing to the Altar comes before the מליקה and no הקרבה is necessary between the מליקה and the הקטרה, hence, מה הקטרה בראש המזבח אף מליקה בראש המזבח the מליקה and also the following מצוי הדם, the squeezing out of the blood, had to be done at the top of the Altar, למעלה מחוט הסקרה. It took place בקרן דרומית מזרחית at the south-west top corner of the Altar. — ומלק והקטיר by the מליקה the הקטרה is prepared and made possible. As the הקטרה of the head was done separately from the הקטרה of the rest of the body, — as is evident from V.15 & V.17 — the head was completely separated from the body by the מליקה. The מליקה of an עולת עוף (in contrast to חטאת עוף at which it says: ולא יבדיל) had to cut through both the סימנים with the finger-nail. The מליקה was done, as it expressly mentions at חטאת העוף, from the back of the neck below the nape: ממול עורף, in contrast to שחיטה (Zebachim 64 b et seq.).

דם כלו :ונמצה דמו, the blood of the whole bird, of the head as well as of the body, the latter being מעכב (ibid 66 a). It is possible that this pressing out of the blood on קיר המזבח is expressed passively and not actively, to include the blood which flows out by itself by the מליקה, similarly to the explanation given (ibid 64 b) of the ימצה of the חטאת עוף.

V. 16. והסיר את מראתו בנצתה. In the Mishna (Zebachim 64 b) it says: והסיר את המוראה ואת הנוצה ואת בני מעיין היוצאין עמם. In consideration of this, and taking it that this Mishna is identical with the explanation of אבא יוסי בן חנן which runs (ibid 65 a) נוטלה ונוטל קורקבנה עמה, Rambam on the תורה takes מראה to mean not only the crop, but also the gullet and stomach, so that including the entrails, the בני מעיין mentioned in the Mishna, it would refer to the whole of the digestive apparatus. According to רמב״ן מראה, would be derived from ראי excrement, dung. But it seems to us remarkable that the whole nutritive and digestive apparatus should derive its name from just that which is discarded as being unfit and useless for nourishment. In זפק, the crop, there is not yet any ראי at all. It seems more likely that מראה (like טמאה from טמא) would come from the root מרא from which we get מריא “a fattened animal” and the rabinical term המראה to cram food down the throat to fatten an animal (Ezek. 39,18, also Sam. II. 6,13; Kings I. 1,9; XIX,25! Isaiah 11,6; 1,2; Amos 5,22 — (Gesenius also gives it as coming from a root מרא, well-fed, etc. — I.L.).
והשליך: According to תוספות Yoma 59 b this השלכה was not actually considered as part of the עבודה, and could be done without בגלי כהונה.
V. 17. ושסע, like שוסעת שסע and כשסע הגדי (Judges 14,6) to split, to tear into two parts related to הוא ישסה אוצר ,שסה (Hosea 13,15), to spoil. ושסע אותו בכנפיו he shall tear it apart by its wings.

אם הבדיל כשר :לא יבדיל (Zebachim 64 b). The ת״כ gives as the reason, because it is done after הרצייה i.e. after the מצוי הדם, which, parallel to the זריקה of an עולת בהמה, is what gives the offering its character. In the same way the Gemora (Zebachim ibid) says of other improprieties: כל ששינה מאחר שמיצה את הדם כשרה.

If we picture to ourselves all the procedures prescribed for an עולת עוף we find that not only are they completely different to those for an עולת בהמה, but mostly they are absolutely in contrast to them, and even against the דינים given for all other offerings. תמות וזכרות are absent from the requirements of bird-offerings. Only עולה and חטאת but no שלמים and no קרבן צבור at all may be brought of birds. Instead of שחיטה there is מליקה and מליקה is the very opposite of שחיטה. Everything which renders שחיטה invalid, and makes the animal into נבלה is prescribed for מליקה .מליקה takes the place of שחיטה at bird-offering, but still it may only be done by a כהן whereas שחיטת עולת בהמה .שחיטה כשרה בזר is בצפון and על ירך המזבח while מליקת עולת עוף is בדרום and בראש המזבח. Instead of זריקה there is מצוי הדם, in the place of laying the organs out in order נתח לנתחיה we find שסוע, a tearing apart, prescribed. The stomach and entrails of an עולת בהמה are offered up like the other parts, at an עולת עוף the corresponding parts are torn out and thrown away. But the most striking peculiarity is, that, just in the most essential procedure of the offering, the עבודת הדם the character of an עולה and a חטאת are completely reversed in bird-offerings, the דם עולת בהמה is בזריקה and למטה מחוט הסקרה, the דם חטאת בהמה is בנתינה and למעלה על הקרנות, and at עולת and חטאת העוף it is exactly the opposite: עולה is למעלה and במצוי which corresponds to the נתינה of חטאת בהמה, while חטאת is למטה and בהזיה, which corresponds to the זריקה of עולת בהמה.

All these peculiarities can not have their reason in the idea of עולה itself, as this is common to both, birds and animals. So the reason for these peculiarities can only be sought in עוף, in the meaning of birds in offerings. Just as in עולת בקר, the עולה represented from the standpoint of בקר, the standpoint of a life of work in the service of God, and in עולת צאן from the standpoint of צאן, from the standpoint of the fate of life being dependent on God, so עולת עוף must be taken from the standpoint of עוף, and this standpoint must be of such a nature that it explains all these contrasts.

In תנ״ך we find birds used metaphorically mainly to picture a fugitive existence, threatened by danger, threatened by dire necessity, and defenceless. כצפור לנוד ,כצפור נודדת מקנה ,כעוף נודד, in Isaiah 16,2, and Prov. 27,8 & XXVI,2, עוף is the picture of an unsettled state of nomadic homelessness. כצפור מיד יקוש ;כצפרים האחוזות בפח ;צוד צדוני כצפור, Lament 3,52, Eccl. 9,12 and Prov. 6,5 express an existence which is unceasingly threatened, or already in the toils of distress. Nets are spread and lying in wait for the דם and נפש of כל בעל כנף of all feathered creatures. Prov. 1,17 & 18, כצפור בודד על גג “lonely as a bird on the roof” in Ps. 7,8, the picture of an unhappy life, and in Is. 38,14, Jer. 48,27, Nachum 2,6 and Is. 59,11 אהגה כיונה etc., the dove is especially made the picture of lamenting, moaning, suffering. Hence we do not think we are wrong if we take birds in offerings to represent a precarious, suffering unhappy condition, or rather a person in precarious suffering unhappy circumstances. That, in קרבן עולה ויורד, birds constitute the offering of the poor, and that otherwise we only find birds directly prescribed for offering in cases of conditions of bodily suffering or illness מצורע זב וזבה ויולדת can only confirm this theory. We can then also understand why birds may not be used for שלמים. For the שלמים idea, the idea of a complete undisturbed happy condition is the very opposite of that which is expressed by a bird-offering. For a קרבן צבור too, they are unfit. The national community as such, especially the Nation as it is represented in the Jewish Sanctuary of the Torah, knows, as our חכמים put it, no death, no poverty אין צבור מת ואין צבור עני. In Galuth, of course, it has no מקדש. Quite in accord with the character of suffering, neither the demand for זכרות virility, nor for תמות complete bodily perfection, is made for bird-offerings. Similarly we can understand that there is no סמיכה which altogether has only to take place at offerings which primarily belong to the idea of consecrating actions and deeds, and so is not done at בכור מעשר ופסח, and would be still less in place at offerings which represent persons in conditions of suffering weakness.

Now one has to ask whether the procedures of the עולת עוף described here are equally easily explained by this idea of its being an offering brought in suffering, and whether that justifies us in looking on עולת עוף as an עולה from the standpoint of a condition of suffering ordained by God, in the same way that we looked on עולת בקר as an עולה from the standpoint of a life of work in the service of God, and עולת צאן as an עולה from the standpoint of a life “shepherded” by the guidance of God. The whole of the procedure of offering an עולת עוף viz. שסוע ,הסרת מוראה ,מצוי ,מליקה compared with the corresponding acts in an עולת בהמה viz., ניתוח ,זריקה ,שחיטה רחיצת קרבים, gives one immediately the impression of acting forcibly with violence. Whereas שחיטה does not mean killing, destruction, but raising the animal into the sphere of the Jewish human mission, and the use of the word שחט to designate killing in general is only a transferred one, and שחיטה accordingly is done by skilled humane means, מליקה בצפורן is altogether an act which bears the stamp not of skilled humane treatment, but of violent raw destruction, and its analogy can only be found in עריפת פטר חמור and עריפת עגלה (actually, in spite if its apparent coarseness it was a highly skilled and extremely difficult act — I.L.). In a quite similar characteristic contrast is the squeezing out of the blood on to the walls of the Altar to קבלה and זריקה. And equally positive is the contrast of the tearing out and throwing away of the crop and tearing the body apart by the wings, to the treatment of the entrails and the cutting up of the organic parts of an עולת בהמה. All these acts prescribed for עולת עוף show a definite connection with the idea of the defenceless suffering condition which, from the general metaphorical meaning of birds in the תנ״ך, we have concluded to be underlying thought at the base of this offering. Accordingly we can understand, even at this introductory stage of our deliberations, why מליקה, unlike שחיטה, may not be done by a non-כהן. For מליקה does not express, as שחיטה does, an action which the בעלים have to perform on themselves as the moral preliminary condition for their admittance into the sphere of the Sanctuary, but, like מצוי and the following procedure, belongs to the whole idea which the Sanctuary wishes to express in this case. Hence it has to be done by a ministrant of the Mikdosh, the כהן, and also בראש המזבח, on the top of the Altar like the הקטרה.

Now, after these preliminary considerations let us try to understand the procedure of an עולת עוף. It is one who feels he is “suffering” who by this offering of עולת עוף is seeking the way to make progress that will bring him nearer to God. He hands himself over as a “dove” to the כהן. Not in the “midnightly” side of material life, into the right south, the side of clear understanding and thinking and up to the very height of the Altar does this כהן lead the symbol of the bringer’s personality, the dove. There, by מליקה בראש המזבח the lesson is taught that endurance of, and submitting to, the most oppressive violence and harshest of circumstances, also belong to the tasks which the spiritual heights of the Altar-of-the-Torah expects us to solve. And by מצוי בקיר המזבח העליונה דרומית, that the spiritual demand in suffering is: with all one’s energy to cling to the heights of the ideals of the תורה, right up to the very end, even to מצוי דם הנפש, even to the loss of all strength, all the powers of life. Every drop of life-blood lost in submitting to such a test falls on the heights of the conception of what a Jew should be, and — הסרת המראה עם נוצתה — even if every external means of livelihood were forcibly to be torn away, and our “bloodless” starved, resistless” body — שסוע בכנפיו — “violently torn asunder”, in the resigned endurance of even such extreme tests, too, is Godliness on earth sustained, just as it is in vigorous energetic God-serving deeds. Both phases of life, submissive endurance, as well as cheerful working belong to the tasks of life as preached from the heights of Jewish conceptions. Even the bloodless head, even the bloodless torn body, robbed of all means of nourishment והקטיר אותו הכהן המזבחה על העצים אשר על האש עולה הוא אשה ריח ניחוח לה׳ it, too, can contribute to the means of keeping the Fires of God alive on earthly elevations, striving upwards to God (the מזבח I.L.), can become fuel for the fire which expresses our desire to be a “satisfaction to God”. (אשה וגו׳ I.L.) — יקר בעיני ה׳ המותה לחסידיו such death, such martyrdom is full of meaning in God’s Eye from those who offer themselves up to Him in love.

Finally, this way of taking it gives a natural and impressive explanation to the striking reversal of the roles of עולה and חטאת in the case of birds, that in bird-offerings the עולה is למעלה and the חטאת is למטה. For not only, in the case of birds have the עולה and חטאת, has the מתנות הדם changed places, so that דם עולה which usually has to come למטה מחוט הסקרא here is done למעלה on the upper half, and דם חטאת which otherwise comes on to the upper half here is directed to the lower. But in addition the whole manner of application is reversed. In acordance with the whole underlying idea of the עולה and the חטאת, the first of which is to atone for a lack of activity, a lack of progress, the latter a lack of firmness, the service of the blood at an עולה teaches by זריקה the most energetic spurring of one’s personality upwards towards moral perfection, and נתינת דם with the finger at a חטאת, the remaining at, the sticking fast to, the height of moral achievements already attained, as the task henceforth to be acomplished. At an עולת וחטאת עוף all this is reversed. The ritual of the blood at an עולה is מצוי, a pressing of the blood firmly on the wall of the top of the Altar, clearly just a more emphatic נתינה of the חטאת, and is the expression of remaining firmly unchanged; whereas the ritual at a חטאת is הזיה sprinkling, obviously a weakened form af זריקה, and the expression of activity towards something higher. But if we look at the meaning of עולה and חטאת from the standpoint of “suffering”, all surprise at these contradictions disappears. Looked at from the standpoint of an ordinary life, as expressed by בקר and צאן, an עולה is to combat lassitude — insufficient energy in doing right — and חטאת to work against overhaste and heedlessness on one’s active life, hence עולה teaches energetic action towards the way upwards to the heights, and חטאת, repose in remaining firmly unchanged up on the heights. But in the case of a life of suffering which finds its representation in תור ובני יונה, the positive task which is to be represented by עולה is just resoluteness, stoicism; the energy which, in normal life shows itself in action, in doing what is right and good, in a condition of suffering has to turn itself inwards and be expended in keeping oneself up on a high spiritual and moral level in spite of all the suffering. עולת עוף has to oppose a lack of resoluteness, of stoicism, hence what it expresses is: firm repose, remaining firmly unchanged up on the heights. On the other hand, sinning, looked on from the standpoint of suffering comes from a state of despair where one looks on the future as hopeless, and so does not care what one does, where one has no belief of the possibility of ever rising up again, and so succumbs to the state of passively believing one has lost all the power to do any good in the world. חטאת העוף has to work against this condition by preaching — action upwards to the path that leads to the heights.

The difference which characterises תור from יונה is obscure. In Jeremiah 8,7 תור is reckoned amongst the birds of passage, vagrant birds. In any case it seems to be a bird that lives a freer life, does not settle and attach itself to the precincts of human beings, like the יונה. Possibly it could then have a nuance of being for birds a similar idea of what עז is in the family of צאן. This could then possibly be connected with the law that of תורים only the old ones are fit for offerings, while of יונה it is just the young ones which have to be used.

V. 1. ונפש כי תקריב קרבן מנחה לה׳. In an overwhelming majority of cases where the term מנחה is used — not in connection with offerings — it has the meaning of a gift by which the giver recognises the receiver as the arbiter of his fate, and by the gift acknowledges and expresses his dependence on, and bondage and subjection to, the receiver of the gift. We are therefore justified in ascribing this meaning to offerings which are called by this name, and from this aspect to find an explanation for the various laws prescribed for this offering. As we have already remarked on Gen. 4,3, the derivation of the word is doubtful. If it comes from נחה it would be a recognition of the “Leadership” of the receiver. The form in the plural so often used מנחות would refer to a root מנח, as שמלות ,שפחות. From the analogy of צלח and נוח ,צלע and נוע etc., מנח would then be the opposite of מנע i.e. to keep nothing back from anybody, to give him a right to all that we have, to lay everything at his feet; a meaning which would be well expressed by “homage, allegiance.” One who is מקריב מנחה expresses by his gift that that part of his possessions which is represented by what he brings really belongs to the Receiver of the gift, is only granted by Him, is only in the possession of the bringer as a fief at the receiver’s disposal, so that with regard to these goods and his use of them, the bringer feels that he is subject to the will of the receiver.

From this point of view, we can readily understand the distinctive character of the introductory words of the מנחה-chapter: נפש כי תקריב וגו׳. In the preceding offerings it is the דם, the נפש itself, which is given up to the Altar-height of our moral task, as a means of getting nearer to God. The נפש itself is the קרבן. But in מנחה, the נפש is not the קרבן but the מקריב. It does not bring itself but its possessions before the Altar of God. “A soul that would give expression to its efforts to get into the proximity of God by bringing a “homage-gift”, let flour be his offering, oil shall he pour on it, and place frankincense on it.” Flour, oil and frankincense are the ingredients of all Menachoth, which here are described in five different forms viz: מאפה תנור ,מנחת סולת, two different kinds, namely חלות and מחבת ,רקיקין and מרחשת. Here, immediately in the first verse we can see that flour is the main part to which oil and incense are added as adjuncts, so that it is in flour that we have to look for the fundamental idea of the Mincha and take oil and incense to form modifications of this idea. That flour is generally used as the basic idea of food, of nourishment, as a symbol of the necessities of life, can be accepted without further proof, and to bring flour as a Mincha as a sign of homage, would express the idea that the condition for our very existence lies in the hands of Him to Whom the sign of homage is brought. If oil is added and it thereby becomes שמנה לחמו (Gen. 49,20), or as Habakuk more generally terms it שמן חלקו (I,16), to the general conception of simply “nourishment” is added the idea of “comfort”, “fat nourishment”. But לבונה, as קטרת-material, fragrant odour, would bring to both of these the further idea of “satisfaction” which by no means is an automatic result of food and comfort, but is to be considered as a special benefit. With the richest food and every comfort one can still feel wretched and dissatisfied. The לבונה, as we are immediately taught, is brought by itself as an independent part of the offering, together with the flour and oil mixed together.

Now it is most significant that by the expression ונפש כי תקריב וגו׳, right from the beginning מנחת נדבה is restricted to single individuals. הכל באין בשותפות לא סילק הכתוב אלא מנחה שנאמר נפש (Menachoth 104 b). Every offering, even a single dove, can be brought by two or more conjointly, Mincha alone is the exception inasmuch as the Torah excludes it from being brought in partnership by the word נפש. In all animal-offerings the personality of a human being is in the foreground as having a task to fulfil, the animal representing the נפש with its faculties. But this task is something that is common to all, more, in it each person is really complementary to the other כל ישראל ערבין זה לזה and really the whole nation should be moved by one spirit, form one soul, one body. We can therefore, very well understand how a completely unlimited number of people can find their mutual representation in one single animal. But in מנחה it is not the personality which is in the foreground, but that which is granted by God to the personality, as a means of existence, of comfort, of a life of satisfaction, and with the conditions of life to be provided by God each person stands individually before God. Here it aims at establishing the authenticity of the most complete אין שנים מתנדבין עשרון אחד .השגחה פרטית (ibid) because each one gets his own special “עשרון״ from God. For the Mincha had to be kept with meticulous exactitude on the basic measure — which lies at the base of all Menachoth (Menachoth 27a) — of the עשירית האיפה ,עשרון. It thus goes back to the fundamental idea of the manna whose עומד לגלגלת was just an עשרון, proving the special individual case of God’s providing for each separate soul in Israel. (It is even not so very far fetched to see in the name מנחה merely an extension of the name מנח whose root מנה is phonetically closely related to מנח, and then מנחה would have the meaning “allotted by God”; and by handing ones flour etc. to God as a מנחה one would express the idea that still today we look on the bread that we live by, as manna).

Just as the word נפש excludes a plurality of persons from bringing a Mincha, so does it also exclude צבור from bringing מנחת נדבה of which our chapter here speaks. For the צבור there is only מנחת חובה as ,מנחת נסכים לחם הפנים ,שתי הלחם ,עומר. In this law too, a significant fact seems laid down. Whereas, in other nations, material independence and material prosperity form the primary, almost the sole concern of their national unity, in the Jewish national unity, just this anxiety is very significantly placed in the background. The national welfare of the Jewish Nation as a unit, as apart from the special care of each individual, does, of course, form a special object of God’s Providence, and this aspect of the national relationship to God has its constant expression in the שלחן and לחם הפנים as well as in the yearly recurring עומר and שתי הלחם. Immediately following the time when the elite of the nation having been sent out to gather information about the Land, by their cowardice and despondency revealed their failure to recognise that the material welfare of the nation was absolutely and exclusively dependent on God alone, and so had fixed in their minds the impossibility of obtaining the Land which God had promised Israel, immediately following this, came the Word of God that henceforth no עולה or זבח was to be brought without an accompanying מנחה and נסכים. This was to induce us to feel that our material welfare was just as completely dependent on the same God as He Whom we recognised as the One that our persons and the fate of our lives, belonged to. It was to ensure that we remained protected from that false idea which says to God: “Thou certainly art my Lord, but טובתי בל עליך, my material welfare (my business affairs I.L.) do not reach up unto Thee,” as David (Ps. 16,2) confessed, that once in a weak moment, he had allowed such erroneous thoughts to occupy his mind. This rule to bring מנחת נסכים with every עולה was then also imposed on עולת צבור. But in this too, the relation of the צבור to מנחה remained limited. Only as חובה when God orders it, has the Nation as such, to remember its material welfare being also before God. Of their own free will, as נדבה, it has only to bring a Mincha with עולות with the idea of consecrating the national activities to God, at which then מנחת נסכים only expresses the material welfare of the nation as a secondary consideration, and as being conditional to the idea of the עולה. But a מנחת נדבה as such, the צבור has never to bring. In והיה אם שמוע, the national part of קריאת שמע, too, we note that ובכל מאודכם which occurs in the individual personal chapter ואהבת is missing. The Jewish Nation, as such has, in its real meaning, no national might and no national fortune.

It says כי תקריב קרבן מנחה not just כי תקריב מנחה which, according to Zebachim 91b, is to teach, that while a complete קרבן מנחה certainly consists of all three constituents, a Mincha can be brought of שמן by itself, and similarly from לבונה by itself (see ת״כ on this verse). סלת see Gen. 23,6.

ויצק עליה שמן ונתן עליה לבונה. The word עליה has to be repeated because it is not the same for יציקת שמן and נתינת לבונה. The oil was spread over the whole mass, while the incense was placed all together in one place. So that the second עליה is a limitation, in accordance with the rule: אין רבוי ת״כ) אחר רבוי אלא למעט).
V. 2. והביאה אל בני אהרן הכהנים the preceding activities, יציקה and בלילה could also be done by a non-Kohen, only מקמיצה ואילך מצות כהונה (Menachoth 18b).

קמץ :וקמץ only occurs, apart from in connection with this procedure, in Gen. 41,47 ותעש הארץ וגוי לקמצים. The word seems to be related to חופר גומץ ,גמץ (Koheleth 10,8), a pit, and on the other hand to כמס and כמז both of which mean hiding, burying, locking up. If now the Halacha teaches that the procedure of קמיצה consists in the priest sinking his hand in the dough and lifting out as much, and only exactly as much, as can be enclosed in the hollow space formed by closing up the three middle fingers on to the palm, חופה גי אצבעותיו עד שמגיע על פס ידו וקומץ (Menachoth 11,a), we see that the procedure of קמיצה combines the idea of both גמץ and גמץ .כמס is digging a hollow space out of a mass, כמס is shutting in, hiding, and קמץ is both digging out and holding fast, and indeed, lifting out only just as much as one is able to hold fast, i.e. “gripping out”. But to grip something and hold it fast in a perfectly natural way, only the three middle fingers are efficient. Without exercising special intentional force the little finger does not reach the palm when one closes the hand. Hence by the term קומץ, only that which is gripped by the closing of the three middle fingers is to be understood. The whole hand has to be sunk in the mass and then with the little finger on the one side and the thumb on the other, everything which projects beyond the קומץ has to be wiped away. In this way he achieves exactly מלא קומצו, not more nor less. קמיצה belongs to the עבודות הקשות שבמקדש, to the very difficult procedures at offerings, together with מליקה and חפינה, (see רמב״ם הלכי מעשה קרבנות י״ג ,כ״מ). It is from this ritual that the finger next to the little finger gets its name קמיצה, the gripping finger. The little finger itself is called זרת, the spanning finger, a span is measured by the space between the extended little finger and the thumb. The middle finger is called אמה, the cubit finger, the length of an arm, the cubit is measured from its tip. The index finger is called אצבע and wherever אצבע is mentioned in offering-ritual it refers to this finger. Finally the thumb called בהן in the text, in rabbinic Hebrew is called גודל (Menachoth 11,a).

וקמץ משם, from there, i.e., ממקום שרגלי הזר עומדות from there, where the non-כהן bringer of the Mincha (Menachoth 8b) stood, regardless of which side of the Mishkon it happened to be. Although קמיצה is the parallel of שחיטה, and מנחה belongs to the קדשי הקדשים group equally to עולה, nevertheless, קמיצה does not require the North side. An animal brought as an offering represents all and every aspect of a human personality and when any particular procedure wants to stress the material aspect, this has to be expressed by placing the animal on the side of the “Table of our material life” — the north. But Mincha itself represents just this very one aspect, so that it does not require the special stressing of קמיצה .צפון is the first real essential ritual of this offering, and hence, overlooking the ritual of הגשה which is intermediate between הבאה and קמיצה (see verse 8), is here brought directly in connection with the הבאה. The object of הבאה is קמיצה.

מסלתה ומשמנה: from its flour and its oil, from the correct prescribed proportion of flour and oil, מיעוטו מעכב את רובו, the slightest deviation from the full amount makes the whole of the rest invalid (Menachoth 27a) and any חסרון of the Mincha is compared to בעל מום in a בהמה (ibid 9b) החסרון כבעל מום דמי. The basic measure for all Menachoth is one עשרון flour and one לוג oil. One can bring several עשרונות as מנחת נדבה but must bring an equal number of “logs” of oil (ibid 88a). But in all cases the basic measure is one עשרון and it was always measured out in a one-עשרון measure. We have already noted the significance of this measure as corresponding to the עומר לגלגלת of the Manna, to that the precision which is demanded here respecting this measure is understandable. What relation the לוג of oil as a basic measure bears to this is unknown to us. It very likely is simply the correct proportion of oil to flour required for a perfect mixing, so that it would be a result of the עשרון itself. It is further taught by the similar placing together מסלתה ומשמנה (Sota 14b) that the קומץ is to be taken ממקום שנתרבה שמנה (Sota 14b), from where the flour is very thoroughly saturated with the oil, so that both the ingredients are equally represented in the קומץ. However big the Mincha might be (it was allowed to be up to sixty עשרונים in one vessel) only one single קומץ of incense was used for the whole.

According to Sota 14b, the ritual of the bringing of a Mincha is as follows: סדר מנחות כיצד, אדם מביא מנחה מתוך ביתו בקלתות של כסף ושל זהב ונותנה לתוך כלי שרת לקדשה בכלי שרת ונותן עליה שמנה ולבונתה ומוליכה אצל כהן וכהן מוליכה אצל מזבח ומגישה בקרן דרומית מערבית נגד חודה של קרן ודיו ומסלק את הלבונה לצד אחד וקומץ ממקום שנתרבה שמנה ונותנו לתוך כלי שרת לקדשו בכלי שרת ומלקט את לבונתה ונותנה על גביו ומעלהו בכלי שרת להקטירו ומולחו ונותנו על גבי האישים.

From this we learn that, between קמיצה and הקטרה there was another ceremony: קידוש הקומץ i.e., נתינת הקומץ לתוך כלי שרת לקדשו, that there was a special sanctification of the קומץ, although it had already been sanctified as part of the whole Mincha. We have already mentioned on Ex. 30,29, that the קדושה of the כלי שדת consisted in their accepting, on behalf of the Mikdosh such objects as are placed in them, making them a part of the Mikdosh; giving them קדושת הגוף which can have no פדיון, can not be redeemed. The mere appointing the material to be a Mincha, and the bringing of it into the precincts of the Temple, only gives it קדושת דמים, it is only their value which has been given over to the purposes of Mincha. If, for instance, they have become unfit for this purpose by טומאה, they can be redeemed by the payment of their value, and they return then to their ordinary non-holy character. But if they have been given over to a כלי שרת i.e., placed in a vessel which belongs to the Mikdosh, they receive the character of unredeemable קדושת הגוף, become קודש which shows itself amongst other characteristics, in their becoming פסול בטבול יום, ובלינה (see on Ch. 22,7 and VI,2). The whole Mincha was accordingly קודש already before the Kemitza, but nevertheless after the קמיצה, the קומץ had to be sanctified by itself, as such, in a כלי שרת. In exactly the same way as when the whole of a sacrificial animal has become קודש by contact with a knife of the Mikdosh in Schechita, the blood has nevertheless to be specially accepted and sanctified by itself for the purpose of זריקה, by means of a vessel which is itself considered as an internal part of the Mikdosh. So the קומץ has to be specially accepted and sanctified by itself for the purpose of הקטרה—which corresponds to זריקה—by נתינה בכלי שדת (Sota 17b & Rashi there). קידוש מנחה as a whole could be done in a vessel standing on the floor of the Mikdosh and so could the קמיצה be taken up from it, but for the קידוש הקומץ the Priest had to take a holy vessel in his hand and thereby receive and accept the קומץ for the הקטרה, just as by קבלת הדם בכלי שרת the Priest had to receive and accept the blood for the מקדשין מנחה בכלי .זריקה שעל גבי קרקע, קומץ מכלי שעל גבי קרקע, ואין מקדשין קומץ בכלי שעל גבי קרקע, דילפינן מדם (Menachoth 7b). So that at the Mincha offering we have four עבודות which run parallel to, and share the character of, the four :עבודות הדם זריקה = הקטרה ,הולכה = הולכה ,קבלח = קידוש קומץ ,שחיטה = קמיצה.
על כל לבונתה he adds the whole of the incense to the קומץ in the בלי שרת.

והקטיר הכהן את אזכרתה. On this, the ת״כ says: אזכרתה נזכרים בה נזכרים בקמיצתה ונזכרים בלבונתה. Our text does not run והקטיר אותם הכהן אזכרתה, if it did, the idea אזכרה would only apply to the parts which were given over to the Fire, and would express the purpose of their being offered; they are to be offered as אזכרה, or to obtain אזכרה. But as these parts are called the אזכרה of the Mincha, through them the whole of the Mincha becomes invested with the idea of אזכרה. By the offering of the קומץ and the לבונה, the שיריים the נותרת מן המנחה of the following verse, become also מוזכרים before God. This is the meaning of our quotation from נזכרים בה .ת״כ: through the Mincha in general, the personality of the bringer comes לזכרון before God, and indeed נזכרים בקמיצה וגו׳, this being “remembered” is brought about by the קמיצה and by the לבונה (see ק״א on this verse). But just this indicates the intimate relation of the קומץ and לבונה to the שיריים and the fact that they are essential, or rather that their הקטרה is essential for the שיריים to be eaten. הקטרת אימורים is rather a ritual of the offering of secondary importance only. Although the בשר הקרבן is not to be eaten before the אימודים are given over to the fire on the altar, nevertheless, if it is not possible to offer up the אימורים e.g., if נטמאו האימורים the בשר still מותר באכילה. For it is not the אימודים but the דם which is the מתיר and the cardinal point of the offering lies in the מתנות הדם (such as זריקה etc.). But הקטרת קומץ ולבונה is a ritual of the very first importance, it is that which is the מתיר for the eating of the שיריים, it is essential like זריקה and it forms the cardinal point of the Mincha. (See תוספות Zebachim 43a). So that the הקטרת קומץ ולבונה stands in the same relation to the שיריים as the דם does to the בשר at an עולה (see on Ch. 1,9). Only here the connection is an even more intimate one, for, while זריקת דם can be done as long as even a כזית בשר, or a כזית חלב is still existing to be מותר for the מזבח or for human consumption through the זריקה, in the case of a מנחה if even the smallest amount of the שירים is missing before the הקטרה (if שירים חסרו בין קמיצה להקטרה), according to רבי יוחנן, although the קומץ may be brought the שירים are פסול, while according to ריש לקיש even the הקטרת הקומץ may not be done (Menachoth 9a and b).

But if the cardinal point of the Mincha lies in a ritual which has the idea of אזכרה, then this idea must surely be an essential complementary one to the whole basic idea of Mincha, and together with this basic idea must constitute the meaning of the Mincha offering. But אזכרתה quite clearly expresses the purpose of this particular ritual of the Mincha to be: — the bringing of whatever special relationship or condition the Mincha represents לזכרון לפני ה׳, to effect that God will “remember them”, i.e., that God will let them be the object of his special care and attention, cf. Numbers 10,9, ונזכרתם לפני ה׳ אלהיכם. So that the Mincha offering is not solely an expression of allegiance or homage, but at the same time a prayer, that God, in Whose Hands our daily bread our comfort and our satisfaction with life rests, may remember these things on which all the happiness of our external life depends, and bless them for us. Or perhaps better, that our allegiance and homage really lies in the fact that we acknowledge that we await all the good things of our life solely from the special care of God. This idea of זכירה is so essentially a part of the Mincha, that we find the whole purpose of the Mincha, as well as the granting of it expressed by the term יזכור כל מנחתיך :זכה (Ps. 20,4) מזכיר לבונה (Is. 66,3).

V. 3. קרב הקומץ, שיריה נאכלין :והנותרת מן המנחה (Yoma 61a). The eating of the Mincha by the priests is dependent on the offering up of the קומץ, that is why this latter is called the מן המנחה .מתיר, only if the Mincha is still there in its entirety at the moment of the הקטרה may the remainder be enjoyed by the Cohanim, as already remarked on V. 2. But we have already, on Ex. 29,33, worked out, how the eating, the actual enjoyment of the offering itself by the Cohanim, is an integral part of, and belongs to, the ritual which makes up the idea of the offerings, הכהנים אוכלין ובעלים מתכפרין. The אכילת כהנים teaches the consequence, the result of the זריקה [[illegible]]ימה and הקטרה. All three represent no denial of life, but are directed to a positive building up of life, כהנים משלחן גבוה קזכו, as it says at the end of our verse מאשי ה׳, the אכילת כהנים is a continuance of the אכילת מזבח. Feeding, keeping alive godliness on earth, consists in the last instance, in using all human powers and possessions for the upkeeping and furthering human life sanctified by the rule of God’s Torah, as is represented by the Priest clothed in the garments of the Mikdosh. אכילת כהנים teaches the one who comes with an offering to seek nearness to God, how to retain this nearness to God, by living his material life in a priest-like manner of sanctity and endeavour. To an even higher degree does this positive effect appear to be the object of the offering in the case of a Mincha. For this particular קרבן is brought to seek nearness to God, just in that relation of human existence to God which the heathen trend of thought takes to be contrary to nearness of God, only to be obtained by its negation (i.e., the idea that saintly men must abstain from riches, comfort etc. I.L.). In a Mincha it is not the man who brings his own self to God, but one who seeks to get nearer to God with his possessions, with the goods of his life. Food, comfort and joy of life in satisfying abundance, according to the heathen view are only grudgingly granted to humans by the gods, who are jealous of human happiness. The gods only find satisfaction in a self-limiting sacrifice on the part of human beings, but not in their happy enjoyment of the good things of life. To oppose this view is the reason we might say, why, even more than at an animal-offering, at the moment of “feeding” the Altar-Fire, the rest of the Mincha must be absolutely complete, and חסרון at a Mincha is equivalent to מום at a זבח (Menachoth 9b). Only a קומץ, not less but also not more (not מבורץ) was given over to the Altar-fire, and this is not to be regarded as destroying it, but is אזכרתה, is only the symbolic expression of the doctrine that the good things and joys of life need only to be enjoyed in a “priest-like” manner for one to be able to reckon on the full blessing of God!

לאהרן ולבניו. We have repeatedly touched on the relation of the כה״ג to the rest of the priests. The כה״ג is the real representative of the People in the service of the Sanctuary-of-the-Torah, the כהני הדיוט appear only as his assistants. He is, accordingly, in a separate class by himself, and when it says here לאהרן ולבניו it is as much as saying מחצה לאהרן ומחצה לבניו, hence the sentence: כהן גדול מקריב חלק בראש ונוטל חלק בראש, in the first place it is really he who should offer up every offering, and he also has priority in those parts of the offerings which are to be divided amongst the priests (Yoma 14a). But in קדשי גבול i.e., the gifts that have to be given to the Cohanim outside the Temple, such as תרומה etc., the כה״ג stands on a completely equal footing with all the other priests.
קדש קדשים, see on Ex. 29,37.
מאשי ה׳, the realisation of אכילת מזבח is taught in the אכילת כהנים.

V. 4 — 7. In the מנחת סלת described in vv. 1 — 3 the materials of nutriment and comfort, flour and oil, are brought as such, without any further preparation of them except simply mixing them together, בלילה. Now four kinds of cooked מנחות follow, viz., two kinds of מאפה תנור, baked in the oven: (a) חלות and (b) רקיקין; (c) מנחה על מחבת, baked on a flat pan, and (d) מנחת מרחשת, loosely prepared in a deep pot. The etymology of the word חלות itself is obscure, and it is difficult to find an English word which really translates it. The word “cake” always refers to a special preparation which is to appeal more to the taste rather than to satisfy hunger, while חלה in Numbers 15,20 definitely refers to ordinary bread-dough, and also in Ex. 29,2 and 23, alternates ככר which is an expression for the shape or weight. חלה accordingly, seems to designate any part of a dough which is formed into a separate loaf, and here being contrasted to רקיקין, to have some thickness, while רקיקין are thin wafer-like forms of bread.

Three different expressions occur here at מנחות for the method of applying the oil. V. 2 and 6 ויצקת עליה שמן to pour oil on it or over it: יציקה; V. 4 and 5 בלולות בשמן, thoroughly mixed: בלילה; V. 7 סלת בשמן, flour in oil, first oil in the vessel and then flour onto it: מתן שמן בכלי. This is a threefold placing of the oil which is done for all מנחות except מאפה תנור. Oil is first placed in the vessel, — מתן שמן בכלי — then the flour, and then oil a second time with which the whole is thoroughly stirred and mixed — בלילה — and after it lies in a כלי שרת — quite ready for the קמיצה — with מנחת סלת after בלילה and נתינה בכלי שרת (it is not quite sure whether the בלילה took place in the כלי שרת), with מחבת and מרחשת after the פתיתה, the whole of the remainder of the oil (which altogether was 1 Log), was poured over it: יציקה. With מאפה תנור no יציקה took place, according to רמב״ם no מתן שמן בכלי either, and with חלות מאפה תנור there was only בלילה and with רקיקין there was no oil at all in the dough, and only משיחה was done, after they were baked. (See מל״מ at length, on הל׳ מעשה קרבנות XIII,5). According to the Mishna, Menachoth 14b this משיחה was done in the form of a Greek X, והשאר נאכל לכהנים (about this משיחה look up note on Ex. 29,7). (According to a different view in Menachoth 15a, at מנחת רקיקין the whole of the oil was used up by repeated painting over the מושחן וחוזר ומושחן עד שיכלה כל השמן שבלוג ,רקיקין Rambam accepts this view as הלכה, although the general rule is that an undivided opinion expressed in the Mishna is taken as הלכה. See כ״מ and ל״מ on 9,ibid.

According to Menachoth 63a מחבת would be a flat pan (according to Rambam only a flat metal plate without any rim). מרחשת a deep vessel (according to ר׳ יוסי הגלילי even with a cover). Hence, Levit. 7,9: וכל נעשה במרחשת ועל מחבת, everything that is prepared in a מרחשת and on a מחבת. In any case the מנחה על מחבת was baked hard by frying in the oil, and במרחשת loosely cooked, and rich in oil.

If our assumption is correct that מנחה expresses our acknowledgment to God in respect to our food, comfort and satisfaction, altogether referring to our happiness in life, then we can very well understand that that which מנחת סלת in its general basic elements represents finds further expression of various degrees and various proportions of the necessities, the comforts and the joys of life. For the conditions of joys and happiness in life are indeed multifarious, although it is true that, as shown here, the fundamental conditions out of which they are formed, remain essentially the same, and with all the qualitative and quantitative differences of conditions and appearances, the ultimate “handful of real satisfaction”, the מלא כף נחת to be won from all of them, remains about the same, as the one constant קומץ לבונה occurs in all מנחות.

If we compare the products of מחבת ,מאפה תנור, and מרחשת, they seem to have the relation to each other of bread, cake, and specially prepared dishes. Bread, מאפה תנור, would be ordinary food for happy daily life — cake, מחבת, the extra enjoyment, the unusual condition of luxury, — but מרחשת, a dish specially prepared for a special occasion, the temporary, passing moment of special joy. So that taken all together, they may express our consciousness of the fact that not only the actual necessities for a happy daily life, but also the extras that we could really do without, as well as every passing moment of special joy, are all to be looked upon as the direct gift of God’s care and arrangement for us, and so come within the sphere of those things for which we give Him acknowledgment and homage.

Further, those מנחות, in which, like מחבת ,מנחת סלת and מרחשת, the preparation begins with מתן שמן בכלי and finishes with יציקה i.e., in which סלת בשמן the flour is put into oil, flour is added to oil, and finally again עליה שמן, oil is poured over it, the idea of comfort, being in good circumstances, seems well in the foreground, to which, food, and food which proves prosperity, בלולות בשמן, only belongs as a considerable component.

At מאפה תנור which we take to express the necessities of daily life, יציקה, and probably (see above) מתן שמן בכלי too, is missing. Only בלילה is done with חלות, and with רקיקין none of the מתנות שמן of the other מנחות takes place, they are only daubed over with oil externally after being baked. משיחה לאחר אפיה. Here on the other hand, accordingly, the idea of food is in the foreground, the sign of prosperity is added in חלות בלולות בשמן where the bread shows evidence of prosperity, or the bread itself is completely free of this sign as in רקיקין, just ordinary Mazzo, where as a side issue, “prosperity” does also find its expression in oil, but the bread itself only reveals an external trace of it. As the actual quantity of the oil and flour is the same for both these מנחות, the משיחה כמין כי וכו׳ which is prescribed in the Mishna would represent חלות in comparison to רקיקין as satisfying themselves with a limited amount of “external show” in their food and using their means for other purposes.

V. 8. והבאת וגו׳, והקריבה וגו׳, והגישה וגו׳, והרים וגו׳. Here, the intermediate ritual, הגשה to which we referred on V. 2 is prescribed. After the Mincha has been handed over, in a כלי שרת to the כהן, he has to take it to the south-west corner of the Altar in the כלי שרת before taking the קמיצה. This הגשה is more precisely described in Ch. 6,7: הקרב אתה בני אהרן לפני ה׳ אל פני המזבח והרים וגו׳, it is accordingly, bringing the whole Mincha next to the Altar before the קמיצה and it is to be לפני ה׳ i.e., on the west side, and אל פני המזבח i.e., the south, combined accordingly, to the south-west corner, בקרן דרומית מערבית (Menachoth 12b). This הגשה had to be performed at all independent Menachoth הבאות בגלל עצמן, which were either entirely given up to the Altar, or of which a קומץ was burnt on the Altar. Accordingly, not at מנחת נסכים which were not independent offerings, and not at the שתי לחם and the לחם הפנים, of which nothing at all came onto the Altar (Menachoth 60a and b). This הגשה, although it was not one of the essential rituals on which the validity of the offering depended, was nevertheless a ritual which could only be done by a כהן in his full בגדים. It must therefore have some important meaning for the idea of the Mincha.

In I. Kings 5,1 it says ושלמה היה מושל בכל הממלכות וגו׳ מגישים מנחה ועובדים את שלמה וגוי. So that הגשה would be that act by means of which the gift is given the character of homage, it is presenting, a laying at the feet, a placing at the disposal of, and הגשה of the קרבן מנחה would have precisely this meaning. Before the Priest lifts out the קומץ and the לבונה from the Mincha, representing the resources of our material life, to place them on the sacrificial Fire, he first lays the whole at the Feet of God, at the place representing the spirit which flows from the Torah (the S.W.). He thereby expresses acknowledgment that it is God Whom we have to thank for all the material resources of our life, food and comfort, and the satisfaction of life which we aim at getting from both. And as they come from Him we will dispose of them in accordance with His Wish, for the enlightening spirit of His Torah. That expresses the foundation on which all the succeeding procedures rest. It indicates the frame of mind, the intention in which we are expected to regard the הקטרה ,נתינה בכלי ,קמיצה, and אכילת כהנים. If, by קמיצה and נתינה בכלי we allow the demands of the Sanctuary-of-the-Torah to encroach on the resources of our lives and take them away to serve its purpose; if, in הקטרת קומץ וכל הלבונה we dedicate a part of our worldly goods, and all our joy in life to keeping godliness alive on earth; if thereby we have decided to give over to the divine sacrificial fire, not only our spiritual life but those resources that belong to our material bodily existence and comfort, more, if we allow our joy of life to consist in God’s having joy of our lives, and all our happiness to be that He is happy with us; if, then, אכילת כהנים teaches us that this giving up all our material resources to God, is no renunciation at all of worldly goods and pleasures, but only demands that they be enjoyed in a priest-like manner within the limits of, and in the spirit of, the divine Torah, and that then even the material enjoyment of the senses become raised to a Mitzva, to a morally free-willed God-serving act; then הגשה has taught us beforehand not to look on all this devotion and sacrifice and dedication as some extraordinarily good act on our part, but that it is all purely that which we owe to God with every particle of our being. That which we dedicate to the Altar of God, in קמיצה and הקטרה we have already acknowledged in הגשה having been received from Him and Him alone. With the greatest sacrifice we only pay the debt of our simple duty. ממך הכל ומידך נתנו לך “Everything comes from Thee, and that which we give unto Thee is only what has come from Thy Hand” (I. Chron. 29,14). In this connection we can also understand why הגשה was only done at such Menachoth where an offering on the Altar was made.

We further note the peculiarity that whereas in all preceding and succeeding laws the Torah speaks of the offering-bringer in the third person, here at the Mincha vv. 6-8, perhaps already in V. 5, the speech goes over to the second person. Perhaps this may be the reason for this peculiarity:- At all other offerings it is the person himself דם = נפש who is first trying to get near to God, in his קרבן. God is considered still at a distance, and He is accordingly spoken of in the third person. But in the מנחה offering, a person who feels he is already near to God is trying to bring material goods of his material life (his animal life of food etc. I.L.) also into the sphere of proximity to God. He feels himself standing before God, and lays the good things of his life at His feet, and the address is accordingly in the second person. The transition to the third person in V. 8 from והבאת to והקריבה can be explained by the preceding יעשה the subject of which can not be the preceding מנחה as it is feminine, but must be taken to be the impersonal “one”, which would then continue והקריבה in the third person. This might also wish to say, that although the מצות כהונה only begins with הגשה, the preceding activities need not necessarily be done by the בעלים themselves, but can be carried out by anybody on their behalf.
V. 9 and 10. את אזכרתה i.e., קומץ and לבונה. Here the קמיצה, the הקטרה and the אכילת כהנים are placed in connection with the הגשה.

V. 11 and 12. In vv. 4 and 5, the order has already been given concerning מנחת תנור and מחבת that they have to consist of Matzo, unleavened bread (see Ex. 12,8). Now, here, in our verse follows the prohibition for all Mincha offerings, that no part of any of them may be allowed to leaven. Moreover, as this prohibition is again repeated in Chapter VI.10 regarding one special form of preparation (baking I.L.) לא תאפה חמץ in accordance with the basic principle that דבר שהיה בכלל ויצא מן הכלל ללמד לא ללמד על עצמו יצא אלא ללמד על הכלל כולו יצא “that where anything is included in a general proposition in the Torah, and is then made the subject of a special statement, that which is specially stated is not to be understood to be limited to itself alone, but is to be applied to the whole of the general proposition”, in accordance with this principle, the prohibition of allowing it to leaven would apply to every part of the preparation of the Mincha, so that חייב על לישתה ועל עריכתה ועל אפייתה (Menachoth 55a). Further, inasmuch as there the prohibition clearly refers primarily to the שירים which the כהן gets, for והנותרת ממנה וגו׳ precedes it and חלקם נתתי אותה וגו׳ immediately follows it, so that נותרת is the subject of לא תאפה חמץ, the prohibition extends not only to the part which is to be given over onto the Altar of God, but quite definitely and expressly to the שירים also, in the possession of the priests (ibid). The prevention of the Menachoth becoming Chometz demands quite special care and attention, such as was and could be expected only from זריזין, from people whose activities are spurred by extreme conscientiousness, as normally prevailed in the workroom of the Temple, as כל המנחות נילשות בפושרין, all Mincha offerings were kneaded with warm water (ibid).

כי כל שאור וגו׳. The reason for the prohibition of Chometz in the preparation of the Mincha is given as being the general prohibition of Chometz in offerings. With regard to הקטרה the prohibition is extended to the tiniest quantity, כל שהן, by the word כל, and as the motive for the prohibition in the preparation is referred to the prohibition of offering Chometz by כי כל, so that it is to be looked at with special seriousness, it is extended even to עירובו to any admixture with חמץ (ibid 58a).

וכל דבש. Regarding the הקטרה here דבש is prohibited equally with שאור. From the contrast קרבן ראשית וגו׳ it is evident that by דבש only such a substance can be understood that is brought as בכורים. So that it can not mean bees’ honey, but refers to all fruit of trees. Date-honey is specially called דבש תמרים — honey. The term is used here to represent all מתיקת פרי all “sweetness of fruit” as Rashi expresses it. See איסורי מזבח ,מל״מ 5,1, for examples and quotations out of the Talmud. Probably the general characterisation of the Land as זבת חלב ודבש refers also to this meaning of sweet fruit juices; שאור and דבש are only אסור for the Altar if brought as offerings but not if, for instance, they were used as addition to the wood as fuel, or for any other purpose, לריח ניחוח אי אתה מעלה אבל אתה מעלה לשם עצים (Zebachim 76b). But דבש is only אסור for הקטרה but the שירים may be eaten mixed with דבש, so the איסור of שאור goes farther than the איסור דבש.

קרבן ראשית, the שתי לחם and שתי לחם .בכורים — which were brought on שבועות from the new wheat, and on the bringing of which depended the permission to bring מנחות from new products of the year within the מקדש, just as the bringing of the עומר allowed them to be eaten outside the מקדש, on account of which they were called מנחה חדשה and בכורים — were חמץ תאפינה) חמץ Levit. 23,16 & 17) — ביכורים (Deut. 26,1) were brought from the seven kinds of fruit which represented the agricultural riches of Palestine, the שבח ארץ ישראל viz. חטה שעורה גפן תאנה רימון זית שמן ודבש (Deut. 8,8). So that amongst these דבש תמרים and fruit, which here come under the name דבש, are forbidden as offerings on the Altar. Both שתי לחם and בכורים are here comprised under the general term קרבן ראשית and here it says that although שאור and דבש have to be brought to the Altar in שתי לחם and ביכורים as קרבן ראשית they still may not be given over to the Altar-fire לריח ניחוח. And actually as a matter of fact both of them were only “waved” תנופה on the east side of the עזרה and then given to the priests (Menachoth 61a).

So that, whereas, the juxtaposition of שאור and דבש in the prohibition for הקטרה, and combining them in the idea of קרבן ראשית sets us the task of finding out what the inner similarity and connection between the two really is, the Halacha gives us a third law, concurrent with the prohibition regarding שאור and דבש of לא תקטירו ממנו אשה לה׳ and which is apparently not even distantly connected with the idea behind these two. For in Menachoth 57b we read: תנו רבנן מניין למעלה מבשר חטאת ומבשר אשם ומבשר קדשי קדשים ומקדשים קלים וממותר העומר וממותר שתי הלחם ומלחם הפנים ומשירי המנחות שהוא בלא תעשה ת״ל כי כל שאור ובל דבש לא תקטירו ממנו אשת לה׳ כל שהוא ממנו לאשים הרי הוא בבל תקטירו, i.e., just as שאור and דבש are prohibited בהקטרה so is the הקטרה forbidden of all parts of offerings of which, or for which, offerings have already been made in the Altar-fire (such as בשר חטאת ואשם etc., of which the אימורים have been offered, or שירי המנחות of which the קומץ has been offered, or the שתי לחם on behalf of which the חלקי כבשי עצרת, or the לחם הפנים for which the בזיכי לבונה have been offered) by means of which offerings these parts are allowed and meant to be eaten by human beings.
