On 58a (ibid) the law is even applied not only to where parts have actually been given over to the Altar-fire, but altogether to anything which can come under the conception of קרבן, to everything which is allowed and meant to be eaten as a result of some part of it having partaken in a ritual on the Altar, including then בשר חטאת העוף of which only the blood came onto the Altar; more, even מותר לוג שמן של מצורע of which the prescribed sprinklings towards the Holy of Holies and on the lobe of the ear of the מצורע etc., had been duly performed after which the rest of the לוג was given to the priest. Levit. 19,15. (Zebachim 91a and 44a). So that we have the whole collective idea of שירים under which conception everything that has been mentioned comes, and so the prohibition כל שממנו לאשים הרי הוא בבל תקטירו is to be taken that everything which falls under the conception of שירים as well as שאור and דבש is forbidden to be offered on the Altar.
Hence we have here three איסורי המזבח viz. שאור ,דבש and שירים which must have some deep inner connection. Let us try and find the idea which is meant to be expressed by these laws.

שאור. The meaning of חמץ and מצה is an historical one, as we worked out on Ex. 12,8. מצה is the symbol of political lack of independence, that condition in which we have lost the free disposal of our time, which amounts to the disposal of our powers. It is the sign of עבדות, and in contrast, שאור and חמץ are the signs of independence and being one’s own master. The original bread of Israel was מצה. Left to themselves, the “bread of slavery” would never have disappeared from their hands. If, at every recurrence of the Festival of Remembrance of the Delivery from Egypt, מצה drives שאור and חמץ out of our homes, and always brings up afresh in our minds that we have freedom and independence not through our own means, but solely as the continuous gracious gifts of God, in the same way, with regards to the Altar of His Torah, the remembrance of this fact is at no time absent from His Mikdosh. The bread which we bring on God’s Altar as a sign of allegiance must always be מצה. The bread of freedom was given to us out of His Hands only under the condition that we go out of עבדות פרעה to enter for ever עבודת ה׳. Matzo in our hands is the very base and foundation on which our relationship to God and to His Torah rests. Of course, freedom from every other kind of עבדות, the most complete political freedom in the whole world, is the promised reward for this עבודת ה׳, for this unique complete subordination to the dictates of His Will. And on the Day of Remembrance of the giving of His Law, on ביום הביכורים ,שבועות, on which the “Laying down of the first-fruits before God” begins, as an acknowledgment that כי באתי אל הארץ, that God had kept His word regarding the Promised Land, Israel appeared before God also with the שתי לחם חמץ with the bread of Freedom and Independence, and acknowledged thereby, that, at the price of subordination under His Torah it finds itself enjoying freedom and independence. But it is just this once in the year, just on the completion of the yearly recurrence of the day of the giving of the Jewish Law, and as a result of the keeping of it, as an acknowledgment of something that has matured on the Tree of the Torah, that Israel has to bring the bread of its political independence before God, but אל המזבח לא יעלה לריח ניחוח it may not be brought up unto the Altar, as אשה to become fuel for the Fire of God, expressing compliance with the Will of God. For that which does come on to the Altar as אשה ריח ניחוח לה׳ is just that which we consider as being our own possession, not obtained as a result of giving anything up, and which we do now give up, give up to God, to further His Will on earth. But חמץ ,שאור, political independence is a possession regarding which we should always remain conscious that we do not have even a trace of it through our own selves, that we can only partake of it by completely devoting ourselves to God’s Torah. It is what we are to obtain through אשה ריח ניחוח לה׳, but it can never be brought by us to obtain proximity to God, just because it is a possession which we do not have without our being in the proximity of God.

דבש. But from this we at once can get an understanding of the meaning of the prohibition of מתיקת פרי ,דבש .דבש, “the sweetness of fruit” is that product of the land which quite specially clearly expresses the value of possessing land. It is that which Nature furnishes finished and ready for Man’s immediate consumption and enjoyment, so that fruit is well fitted to represent the possession of land. But possession of land is just the second possession which Israel owes just as little to its own prowess and powers, as freedom and political independence. The possession of the Land for Israel can only be gained and retained by the keeping of God’s Torah. That is why it is with the Festival of the Giving of the Torah that the time begins during which the first-fruits of the products of the Land — and amongst them primarily fruit — has to be carried up to God, into the Sanctuary of His Torah, and given over to the priests to be laid down in front of the Altar, with the declaration: הגדתי היום לה׳ אלהיך כי באתי אל הארץ אשר נשבע ה׳ לאבותינו לתת לנו. But again אל המזבח לא יעלו לריח ניחוח, “they could not be brought up onto the Altar as an expression of the desire to carry out the Will of God.” Possession of the Land is again something that is not our own, which we can dispose of to express our devotion to the Torah of God. It too, is a possession that we can only obtain by our devotion to the Torah of God.

Taking the two together we can say: שאר and דבש, political independence and possession of the Land, in the Jewish National Sanctuary are to be regarded as a result, never as a means. So that they appear in the Mikdosh always only in the idea of שירים i.e., of such things that can only be eaten or enjoyed by הקטרה or by some other act of relinquishment, which acts as the מתיר, the condition which has to be fulfilled to permit the eating or enjoyment of them. The idea can aptly be expressed thus: שאור and דבש are the שירים of the תורה, the תורה is the מתיר for שאור and דבש. הקטרת שאור ודבש would deny their שירים-character and would raise them to having the meaning of a מתיר, hence כל שאור ודבש לא תקטירו ממנו אשה לה׳.

But thereby the איסור שאור ודבש, according to its underlying idea, becomes classified under the heading of that comprehensive law which is laid down in the term לא תקטירו ממנו אשה לה׳ and which, according to the Halacha forbids the הקטרה of all those sacrificial objects which are given over to human consumption as שירים, but only obtain such permission as a result of the preceding הקרבה of a כל שממנו לאשים הרי הוא בבל תקטירו :מתיר. We have already repeatedly considered the meaning of אכילת שירים the eating of those parts of the offerings which are to be eaten, כהנים אוכלים ובעלים מתכפרין; and also in such cases, as in שלמים, where they come back to the בעלים themselves to be eaten, the meaning is, as we shall see, of no less importance. It is, in all cases, the final flower and the result of the preceding אכילת המזבח. But in every case it is a fundamental condition that the idea be kept in mind that this eating is only permitted as the result of a preceding submission of a מתיר on the Altar, more, that it is then become a holy act of duty, in short, that this eating is only allowable and only becomes holy as שירים. But הקטרת שירים would remove this fundamental idea and would express the very contrary idea, inasmuch as it would change the שירים-character, requiring a מתיר, into an offering in itself, a מתיר. It would make the part to be eaten appear originally and in itself as the purpose of the offering, exactly in the same way as the הקטרת שאור ודבש would do, to the possessions which שאור and דבש represent.

The איסור שאור however, goes farther than the איסור דבש as is indicated in the construction of the sentence כל מנחה וגו׳ לא תעשה חמץ כי כל דבש .שאור וכל דבש לא תקטירו וגו׳ is only אסור בהקטרה, but the priest would be allowed to mix דבש with the שירים and eat them. But the idea of שאור, as expression of one’s own independence is in such direct opposition to the allegiance-idea of the Mincha, that שאור is banned entirely and in every stage of the מנחה. (Regarding the חלת לחם חמץ of the תודה see Ch. 7,13.)

V. 13. כל קרבן מנחתך is all that part of the Mincha which was offered on the Altar, viz, קומץ and במלח תמלח .לבונה, before being placed on the Fire on the Altar they have to be sprinkled with salt on all sides, just as meat has to be salted before cooking to draw out the blood. (Menachoth 21a). ולא תשבית וגו׳ imposes a “prohibitive law” on to the preceding positive one. על כל קרבנך תקריב מלח extends the commands given here for the מנחה to everything which, like the קומץ of the Mincha is given over to the Altar-fire as an offering. This excludes דם and יין נסכים neither of which comes on to the fire itself, and עצים which form the fire but which are not really considered as offered to the fire. (There is doubt regarding קטרת as it was not brought on (the מזבח החיצון (see Menachoth 20a — 21a, and כ״מ and ל״מ on Rambam הל׳ איסורי המזבח 5,11). The salt which was used for offerings — like the עצים, the wood for the Altar-fire — was provided by public funds משל צבור even for private offerings. According to Menachoth 21b the reason for this lies in the ברית-character of the salt. Just as in Levit. 24,8, the shewbread is designated as ברית and had to be provided by the public, מאת בני ישראל as it says מאת בני ישראל ברית עולם, so also was the salt which equally bears the ברית-character: מלח ברית אלקיך, and which in Numbers 17,19 is even used generally as an expression of the ברית-character ברית מלח עולם הוא.

On the meaning of salt at offerings there can, in general be little doubt. It says clearly מלח ברית אלקיך and by the accent under מלח the word ברית is not genitive, but in apposition to מלח, not salt of the Bris, but salt, the Bris of your God. Apart from the concrete use of salt as an indispensable taste-giver to all food: היא כל תפל מבלי מלח (Job 6,6), salt occurs both in concrete and allegorical sense as the means of suppression of all vegetable growth. A field is renderd sterile if it is “sown” with salt. (Judges 9,45). An unfruitful land is called מלחה (Ps. 107,34 et seq.). If we put this together with the other quality of salt, its conservative power of preventing decay, and remember that decay is nothing but the working of the beginning of a new structure, we can take salt generally to represent unchangeableness. It closes an object in to itself, and renders it not susceptible to exterior changing influences. To that extent it completely expresses the idea ברית, the basic underlying meaning of which we have already (Gen. 6,18) shown to be, separated and apart, quite independent and unaffected by outer influences. Whereas ברית already in itself has the meaning of something that is to be kept under every possible condition and remain in all circumstances, the addition of ברית מלח ,מלח, adds to it the quality of unalterableness. That which is designated as ברית does not only remain permanently for ever, but it also remains unchanged for ever, suffers, no change both with regards to its permanence and its nature, it is absolute. So, that salt is a sign of the “covenant”, and inasmuch as it is “salt from the national treasury” it is a sign of that “covenant” which rests in charge of the nation. The Nation as a whole is responsible for its endurance and its immutability. Its meaning and its authority is not subject to the choice and opinion of individuals, but is something for which the Nation stands as guarantor and trustee. But as this ברית, the symbol of which is to be מלח at all offerings, is referred to as ברית אלקיך it can be no other than that which is guarded in the ארון, which indeed is called ארון ברית ה׳. It is accordingly nothing else but the symbol of God’s Torah in its permanence and immutability. “To salt something on all sides with the salt of God’s Torah — the salt being received from the hands of the Nation”, would mean: to make it affected by being completely permeated by the spirit of the eternal unalterable Torah of God, guarded and kept by the Nation and handed down by the Nation. It is only through the medium of this eternal, unalterable spirit of the Torah that anything of our goods and property (קומץ, לבונה), of our efforts and endeavours (אימורים) or of our accomplishments and deeds (איברים) can become the means of keeping the Fire of Godliness alive and present amongst mortal beings. Not דם, not the נפש that which in itself is unalterable, but איברים, אימודים, לבונה, שמן, סלת do indeed require this salt-impression of the eternity and unalterableness of the Divine Covenant, of the Torah. The external conditions and circumstances under which the wealth which governs our external life is found, and which has such an influence on our efforts and accomplishments, do change with time and place and bring about the false idea of thinking that our duties and the mission of our life change with them. The changes which occur in the conditions of just those possessions which are represented in the Mincha, in the standard of life which governs our food, our comfort, our happiness, are particularly liable to give rise to this error. That is why the Torah says: “When you try and get nearer to God by acknowledging your allegiance to Him with regards to your material posessions, you are to salt your allegiance offerings with the salt of immutability which the Nation possesses; let salt, the symbol of the covenant of God, in all its eternal unchangeableness be never missing, above all in your allegiance offerings and also from all the offerings by which you seek to get nearer to your God” — We think it is now understandable why this command for salt is given primarily for מנחות and then taught to be carried over to everything that is analogous to the מנחה. The רמב״ם even says that it is only at a מנחה that the omission of salt would render the whole offering פסול, at other offerings, salt is only a מצוה but not מעכב. This, however, is an opinion which it is extremely difficult to bring in concordance with the various processes referring to the matter in the Gemora in Menachoth. Moreover, the reason which כ״מ gives for Rambam’s opinion viz., that ברית is mentioned only in connection with מנחה seems rather weak as רמב״ם himself refers the לא תשבית מלח ברית אלקיך וגו׳ :ל״ת as applying to all offerings וצ״ע.

But if, as remarked above, perhaps קסרת is excluded from the command of salting, and salting is limited to only that which is given over to the Fire on the מזבח החיצון, this would be quite in accordance with the meaning we have sought to give to קטרת and to the מזבח הפנימי. Only when still on the paths leading upwards to the heights of the Jewish Ideals, as taught by the מזבח החיצון is there any necessity for a special warning of the permanence and unalterableness of God’s Torah. But, for that which represents this ideal itself, for this embodied ריח ניחוח as it appears in קטרת, entirely sublimated without any substratum, on the מזבח הזהב, which, facing the ארון הברית, is dedicated to expressing the combination of the שולחן and מנורה for the most ideal realisation of the Torah which rests in the ארון, here there is surely no necessity for reminder of the eternity and unalterableness of this Torah. The whole idea of the מזבח הקטרת itself presupposes all this.

V. 14. מנחת בכורים is the עומד called ראשית קצירכם in Ch. 23,10. It was brought from the first ripe barley, to which the name אביב refers, which in Ex. 9,31 is used to designate the ripening of the barley. In any case the עומר could only be brought from barley not wheat, as otherwise the בכורים brought on שבועות could not be called בכורים (Menachoth 86b)

— קלוי באש, the barley which was cut for the עומר was not to be left to dry on the field, but was brought fresh on the stalks into the עזרה, there was beaten out of the ears by thin sticks, then roasted over a fire in perforated tubes and spread out in the עזרה where the wind would blow over it (ibid 66a) — גרש, phonetically related to גרס ,גרז which mean separating out by cutting or breaking. Here גרש would seem to mean the peeled barley, the grains, and from the expression in V. 16. מגרשה ומשמנה one could conclude that the מנחת עומר was brought from barley grains. But this was not the case. In the same way as מנחת סלת was from wheat flour, it was prepared from barley flour, worked with oil into a dough, and גרש is the grain ground in a barley mill, ריחים של גרוסות which was then shuffled through several sieves — the עומר was put through thirteen sieves, the שתי לחם twelve, and the לחם פנים eleven — to clear it from all husks and fibres, and the coarser flour the קמח, until only the finest barley flour remained (similarly to סלת in wheat) which when finally ground yielded the purest and best flour (see Gen. 18,6). So that גרש and סלת are identical terms and גרש for מנחת בכורים means exactly the same as סלת does for the other Menachoth (Menachoth 27a and Rashi thereupon).

כרמל. The meaning of this word we only know from Menachoth 84a, according to which it means the very earliest stage of the ripening of corn, where the grains are still soft and easily plucked out of the ears. In 66 ibid it is explained as רך ומל tender and easy to be shelled, and referred to the בכורים-present brought to Elisha (Kings II. 4,42) which consisted of לחם בכורים ועשרים לחם שעורים וכרמל. According to תנא דבי ר׳ ישמעאל the word כר מלא = כרמל “well filled out” (lit. upholstered) and then it would mean fully ripe, when the grains have grown to their full extent. Apart from the name of the mountain, כרמל elsewhere in תנ״ך always designates flourishing green fields in contrast to forests and wildernesses. Taking the analogy of ברזל from גבעל ,ברד from ערפל ,גבל from קרסל ,ערף from קרס ,כרמל could come from כרם and would then refer to a flourishing region rising in terraces like a vineyard or olive plantation (גרם = כרם a step, a degree). But still its use to describe a certain stage of the ripeness of corn is obscure. Perhaps כרמל describes the terrace-like formation of the ears themselves?

V. 15. מנחה היא. The עומר is a complete Mincha in contrast to the לחם which, although they are also called Mincha, have neither oil nor frankincense, and no part of them comes on to the Altar. For the meaning and mutual relationship of the two first-fruit Menachoth, see Ch. 23,9 et. seq. and 16 et. seq., and notes thereon. Here, we will only add that although מנחת עומר is quoted here in the list of מנחות נדבה and is also introduced with the hypothetical ואם (v. 14) it is nevertheless מנחות חובה and, as ר״י explains in ת״כ the hypothetical ואם refers to the circumstance that עתידה מנחת בכורים לפסוק ולחזור that on account of the loss of the Land, מנחת עומר would suffer a temporary interruption. But ר״ש sees in this hypothetic introduction a positive command for the offering and in the placing of it amongst the מנחות נדבה the teaching that אם אתם מביאים אותה לרצון מעלה אני עליכם כאילו נדבה הבאתם אותה, ואם אין אתם מביאים אותה לרצון מעלה אני עליכם כאילו לא הבאתם אותה אלא לצורך עצמכם that duty offerings are to be brought in the same spirit as a נדבה offering, and if this spirit is lacking, then the offering is regarded as having been brought for ulterior motives e.g., that the עומר is only brought for the permission to eat the new produce. See ק״א.

V. 1. ואם זבח שלמים. Apart from its use referring to an offering the word זבח is used for a meal, and generally for a meal to be eaten in company with others; it might be phonetically related to שבע satiety. Referring to offerings it is used above all in connection with שלמים, and is also used by itself to designate this offering which the bringers themselves eat outside the Temple in their home circle, and so offers a complete contrast to עולות which are completely consumed on the Altar by the Fire. Hence the common contrasting phrases עולותיכם וזבחיכם ,עולה או זבח etc. זבח specially designates the procedure of שחיטה, the killing according to the prescribed manner for the purpose of eating as in Deut. 12,21 וזבחת מבקרו וגו׳ כאשד צויתיך. Hence Zebachim 4a takes it, that as in Ch. 7,14 and 33 the offering is mentioned without the addition of זבח, viz. הזורק ,המקריב את דם השלמים את דם השלמים while here it says זבח השלמים, it is to teach incidentally, the close connection which must exist between the idea of שלמים and the act of שחיטה, namely that the idea of שלמים must be present in the mind when the שחיטה is done, that בעינן זביחה לשמה; just as in the passages quoted, in הזורק וגו׳ המקריב וגו־ lies the demand that the הקרבה, i.e., הולכה and קבלה, and the זריקה must be done לשמה. This is there applied both to שנוי קדש i.e., giving it the idea of some other offering e.g., שלמים לשם עולה and to שנוי בעלים, having in mind the wrong bringers. By the summing-up sentence זאת התורה לעולה ולמנחה ולחטאת ולאשם ולמילואים ולזבח השלמים (ibid 37) it is extended to apply to all offerings. Nevertheless, with the exception of חטאת and פסח, this demand is only למצוה but not מעכב inasmuch as the offering is כשר, but the obligation (whether imposed by duty or undertaking) is not considered as fulfilled: כל הזבחים שנזבחו שלא לשמן כשרים אלא לא עלו לבעלים לשם חובה (Zebachim 2a). See above.

שלם .שלמים really designates the completeness, the lack of any deficiency, of an object. אבן שלמה etc. Referring to human beings it expresses the condition in which a man feels that he has nothing lacking in any respect, that he has everything that he wants, ויבא יעקב שלם (Gen. 33,18). So that שלם is a relative idea, it describes, primarily, an object in relation to all its parts, a man in relation to his circumstances and surroundings. But it also describes, although seldom, the condition of these circumstances and surroundings which make a man feel שלם, as in Gen. 34,21, האנשים האלה שלמים הם אתנו, “their relation to us is such that in no way we have to miss anything through them.”

שלום is that condition of all circumstances where no one has to miss anything on account of the other, but rather finds his complement in and through the other. We have already shown (Jeshurun VIII. P. 526) from the phonetic relation of שלם and צלם how the true conception of שלום is not merely the external mutual relationship of not interfering with one another, but the internal harmonious agreeing with one another. שלמים are offerings which are brought from the feeling of being in a שלם-condition. While קרבן עולה seeks getting nearer to God on account of the necessity to raise the standard of the holiness of one’s activities, and קרבן מנחה on account of feeling the necessity of reminding oneself that all one’s means of livelihood and one’s joys and satisfaction in life, are owing to God, קרבן שלמים seeks to get nearer to God, on account of feeling completely satisfied with life, feeling that there is nothing lacking in one’s circumstances, the only thing that is still necessary is the crowning feeling that one is near to God, which is the whole object of his offering. שלמים is the very summit of the Jewish “lebensanschauung.” Not trouble, joy, is to be the eternal bridge up to God, and to enjoy this life on earth in the Presence of God is the highest service of God. To seek God, just when, and just because, one wants nothing special from Him, has not even to thank Him for some special joy or fortune, that is the idea of a שלמים offering.

שלמים is the specific Jewish offering. According to a view expressed in Zebachim 116a, a non-Jew who obeserves the seven Noachian Laws, could bring עולות but not שלמים. It there expresses this view in conformity with the verse in the Song of Songs, seeing in the first half of the verse עורי צפון a call to the “Noachidic” world, תתנער אומה שמעשיה בצפון, and in the second half ובואי תימן the call to the Jewish world, ותבוא אומה שמעשיה בצפון ובדרום. The non-Jewish-world may indeed have had some idea of seeking God, based on the “midnightly dark side of life”, (עולה בצפון), but to seek God also in the bright midday rays of the bright side of life was reserved for Judaism. The שחיטה of שלמים could be done on any side. The actual accepted Halacha, too seems to agree with this view, as שלמי נכרי עולות only עולות were brought in the Jewish Temple from non-Jews (Menachoth 73b).

From this idea of the feeling of an undamaged complete condition of life out of which שלמים offerings result, we can understand the Halacha that אונן אינו משלח קרבנותיו, on the day that one has lost a near relative (husband or wife, parents, brother or sister) by death, and in the resulting feelings of grief and pain, is called an אונן, no offerings may be brought by such a person in the Temple, a Law that is said primarily regarding שלמים כשהוא שלם מביא ואינו מביא כשהוא אונן :שלמים, but which is extended to all offerings, even to the קרבן פסח. The שלום-feeling which in the case of שלמים is entirely and completely present, and out of which indeed the offering comes and represents, may not be entirely lacking at any offering to God. The overcoming of the feelings of grief and pain, consolation for the troubles of life, wherein other religions find the highest triumph of their mission, is but a preliminary condition for the help which the Jewish Temple gives. Not consolation for grief, but the power and determination for happy God-serving activity in life is what it wishes to grant, cheerful courage to face life is the spirit which permeates its halls. The Temple of God is the Temple of His Torah (see notes on Ch. 10,19).

אם מן הבקר וגו׳. See note on Ch. 1.v.3. According to how the person who feels himself שלם looks on himself—whether as בקר, to serve and work for God is the mission of his life, or as צאן, his life spent in following God as His Leader, and in that case, either as כבש purely in trustful devotion to his Shepherd, or as עז, in the feeling of the power given him to resist all that might entice him away from this Guidance — has the choice to be made between בקר or, v.6 and 12, the appropriate kind of צאן. The offering can also be either זכר or נקבה according to the greater or lesser degree of independence or dependence in which the bringer regards his or her position in life. For even in a dependent position a person can feel himself שלם. The Torah even recognises an דבע-condition in which טוב לו עמך, where the slave would not change his condition for that of free independence! But in all cases the offering must be תמים; his whole united self, no part kept back, with which he tries to get nearer to the One Unique Guide of his acts and Disposer of his fate.

But it says הוא מקריב and in ת״כ stress is laid on this הוא, and from it learns the significant law: הוא, היחיד מביא שלמים נדבה אין צבור מביא שלמים נדבה, the nation as such can never bring שלמי נדבה. Altogether there is only one שלמי צבור, the שני כבשי עצרת which were brought together with the שתי לחם on שבועות. Even in that case, the nation was not represented as one unit, as כבש אחד, but as שני כבשים, as a plurality consisting of individual members. Even with this modification, the כבשי עצרת as קדשי קדשים have the character of half עולה וחטאת and their general שלם character expresses rather a goal to be striven for, something that has been missing than an achievement already achieved. After all they are חובה and ק״ק and שחיטתן בצפון (see Zebachim 55a). They express the goal of the Torah, the אפס כי לא יהיה בך אביון! (see note on Ch. 23,19). The שלם-feeling out of which שלמים are brought is essentially and exclusively a definite individual one. True, two or more individuals, can, as individuals, together bring one שלמים. Their belonging together can indeed by the very reason for their שלם condition, human happiness essentially requires association with others, and it is difficult to picture a true human being feeling שלם in complete isolation. But Jewish institutions to not admit the fiction that a nation can be thought to be in a national happy condition without every single member of that nation being happy, that a nation as an ideal unit dare feel itself שלם, if in concrete reality its concrete masses suffer want. The Jewish Nation is only to understand its שלום in the general and universal שלום of its actual people. A שלמים offering brought by the Nation as an ideal unit is unknown on the Altar of God.

V. 2. וסמך ידו (see on Ch. 1,4). If, as we worked out there, by סמיכה, the סומך reminds himself of his position as a Jew and his responsibilities to the demands of the Jewish mission as expressed in the procedures of the offering which follow, then this procedure of סמיכה can be of no greater significance at any other offering than at שלמים. For no other, does the duty to stand up for and act for God and His Will appear greater than for one who, by the Grace of God, feels himself שלם, in the possession of a happy and undisturbed life. He for whom God has done everything, has now to do everything for God, and he who is on the way to seek God, in his feelings of being שלם is met first of all by סמיכה with the admonition: “In your happiness and content be a Jew and stand up for the Will of God”.

ושחטו (see on Ch. 1,5) פתה אהל מועד. For עולה the North, צפון (Ch. 1,11, ירך המזבח צפונה) is the prescribed side of the Altar where the שחיטה has to be performed, and the same applies to all קדשי קדשים. They are all brought in the consciousness of some previous failing, and the most prominent factor in causing such failing is always to be found in an overgrowth of the material, sensual side of our nature. (“The world is too much with us.” I.L.). Hence the first step towards atonement is שחיטה, the giving up of the uncontrolled living for oneself, and this must be done בצפון, in the side of the “Table”, representing our material life of the senses. But שלמים are not brought from any such feeling. They come from a completely undisturbed mind, that “seeks God’s Presence” with its happy position in life. It too, and it above all, has to leran from שחיטה to strip its happy and contented self from all feeling that it may selfishly live and work for itself alone. And to appear with his happiness לפני ה׳, and to enter His sanctuary so that he can then really and truly enjoy his happiness in the higher stage where alone true happiness exists, he must, by the symbolic act of שחיטה, entirely give up all selfish life that he may hitherto have been living, and, by קבלת דמו בכלי שרת, allow his whole nature to be elevated by the Sanctuary to a new fresh sanctified life. But this שחיטה and קבלה must take place at פתח אהל מועד, before the opened gate at the entrance to the “Tent fixed for leading to our meeting with God”. By the sentences ושחט אותו לפני אהל מועד in V. 8 and 13 the idea and meaning of פתח אהל מועד is extended to include the whole of the antechamber to the Sanctuary, the whole of the עזרה, so that שחיטתו בכל מקום בעזרה and even to the צדדים which are not directly opposite the entrance of the היכל but are spaces and alcoves on the north and south sides of the עזרה. According to רמב״ם even the space of the עזרה behind the היכל, the אחורי ההיכל can be used for the שחיטה of שלמים; for the whole of the עזרה has the meaning of לפני אהל מועד, as the antechamber, the preparatory place for the Sanctuary. Only the צדי צדדים, the לשכות, the halls at the sides of the עזרה, partitioned-off for special purposes, are excluded. The precept לפני אהל מועד only imposes the condition that נפתחו דלתות ההיכל that the doors of the Sanctuary must be open שלמים ששחטו קודם שיפתחו דלתות ההיכל פסולין; a rule that is applied from שלמים to all other קרבנות (Yoma 29a תוספות) as we have already referred to (on Ex. 29,42).

וזרקו וגו׳ סביב. See on Ch. 1,5. The שלם, the one who feels “he is lacking nothing”, is taught that it is easier to be שלם בגופו וממונו than to be שלם בתורתו. The blood representing his being, accepted and received in a bowl of the Mikdosh, is taken to the south, to the rays of light and understanding which are kindled in his mind from the תורה, still far off from the very foot of the “Altar-heights” which struggle up, up to God. From there, turning to the right (similar to the procedure at an עולה) i.e., from the south stepping round to the east, the נפש of the “happy one” is taught by the east of the Altar, to consider himself as a member of the nation that was appointed to live for the Torah; and by the throwing onto the upward-reaching corner at the east-north angle, the estimation and valuation of his wealth and material position which give him his condition of שלם, from the point of view of his being a member of the Nation, is demanded as the first expenditure of his energy. After that, always proceeding to the right, from the north, the side of the Table, to the west, the side of the Torah, the “happy one” learns to consider his mission in life to be the dedication of all the powers which the “Table” gives him to the fulfilment of the Torah, and for that, by the throwing of the blood to the upward-reaching west-south corner, to consider the constant enlightenment of his mind from the source of the Torah, as the second expenditure of his energy which is demanded of him. Finally by the שפיכת השירים ליסוד בדרום (similarly to the עולה) he is taught to find the roots of his whole being in the spirit which is awakened and animated by the תורה.

V. 3 — 5. חלב (see Gen. 4,4 )is the fat which is separated from the organism of the animal, which is set aside for future use for the necessary nourishment, for the upkeep of the animal itself, as חָלָב milk, is for the necessary upkeep of the species. By חלב only such fat is understood which has not grown intermingled with the flesh but which lies over the flesh or on it, covered b ya skin or membrance which is easily peeled off תותב קרום ונקלף. The parts mentioned here, are, first: חלב המכסה את הקרב the covering of fat, which, like a cloth is spread over the intestines in the whole abdomen. Then כל החלב אשר על הקרב, the fat which lies over the paunch, farding-bag and rennet-bag (the compartments of the stomach of ruminants. I.L.) בית הכוסות המסס וקיבה and over a part of the bowels, חלב שעל גבי דקין. Then the fat over the kidneys חלב שעל הכליות and חלב על הכסלים. It is difficult to know exactly what is described by כסלים. It does not seem to be exactly the loins. Loins are מתנים as is apparent from Rashi in Chulin 93a. But there it is evident that כסלים are different from מתנים, and that מתנים start directly below the false ribs, whereas כסלים must be muscles which lie more towards the hips separated from the muscles of the loins, but covered by the loin muscle, תרבי דתותי מתני. Also the תרבא קליבוסתא mentioned there as belonging to the חלב שעל הכסלים lies, according to both Rashi and Rambam (who explains it is חלב שבעיקרי הירכים) towards the hip. Rabbi Menachem Asaria שו״ת 113, explains מתנים as the צדדי השדרה למטה מהצלעות and כסלים as being הם הבשר החופים על המתנים, according to which כסלים would really be the hips, וצ״ע. Anyway according to the wording of the text חלב על הכליות seem to be in connection with the חלב על הכסלים as it does not say ואשר על הכסלים, but יותרת .אשר על הכסלים is the diaphragm stretched between the respiratory organs and the digestive organs: חצר הכבד, it directly separates the lungs from the liver. It lines the whole cavity of the breast and it functions principally in the movements of respiration. Its back surface turned towards the liver has also some importance for the process of digestion.

ואת היותרת על הכבד על הכליות יסירנה. In Ch. 9,10, it says: ואת היותרת מן הכבד, so the liver was not offered with it, but here it says על הכבד, this is explained in ת״כ that שיטול מן הכבד על היותרת that a part of the liver is taken with the whole of the diaphragm; the יסירנה clearly refers to the יותרת (see ק״א). It is obscure what the על הכליות יסירנה wishes to convey. These parts of the שלמים (also those of the חטאת and אשם) which have to be burnt on the Altar are called אימורים to differentiate them from parts of the עולה (the whole of which is offered up on the Altar) and which are called איברים. The derivation of the word אימורים is obscure (see מל״מ on מעשה הקרבנות 1,18).

והקטירו אתו (V. 5),והקטירו (V. 11), והקטירם (V. 16): והקטירו אותו כשר ת״כ) והקטירם כלם כאחת ;והקטירו שלא יערב חלבים בחלבים ;ולא הפסול). We learn from the changed suffixes: אותו, that only such אימורים may be brought on to the Altar where due attention has been paid to all the preceding laws affecting the שלמים; from והקטירו, that the אימורים of each offering must be brought on to the Altar separately; from והקטירם that the parts mentioned are to be brought on to the Altar all together, and not like the אברים of the עולה, separately. These various parts must accordingly all together express one idea.

We have the כליות, the חלב, the יותרת and a part of the liver, which have to be given to the Altar-fire after the זריקת דם השלמים. Together they form, as just remarked, one idea. They all belong to the “vegetative” system of the organs of digestion and reproduction. The diaphragm alone, which forms the boundary between the “vegetative” and “animal” systems, can also represent the “animal” functions. But here, in the offerings it seems to stress its relation to the “vegetative” realm by describing it as חלב .על הכבד על הכליות is the end-product of the alimentary activity, the unused superabundance of the nourishing fluids which is not changed into blood. It provides both protection for the digestive organs and a store against any possible future want. It is the saved-up riches of the animal. Hence we find חלב used also as a metaphor for the richest and best: כליות — .חלב הארץ, חלב חטים, חלב תירוש, חלב יצהר, the actual physiological importance of the kidneys for the animal organism — apart from the formation of urine, — is not known. In תנ״ך we find it used in combination with לב as צרפה כליותי ולבי ,בוחן כליות ולב ,בוחן לבות וכליות, so that כליות seem to take the same place in the realm of “vegetative” desires and urges, as לב does in the realm of the higher desires and urges. The derivation of the word from כלה, the expression used for a deep longing and urge, points to the same idea. The כליות accordingly, represent the innermost source of sensuous desires. — יותרת, the diaphragm, as already mentioned, is the most important factor for the movement of respiration. Both expanding the thorax for inspiration and contracting it for expiration is principally brought about by the muscles of the diaphragm. If here the diaphragm appears in connection with the kidneys and liver, it can be taken to express the “animal” functions of life used in service of the “vegetative” urges. For if, as our חכמים teach, כבד כועס, the provocative stimulus of anger is traced back to the liver, — anger being nothing but the feeling roused by disgust — then כבד would form the opposite of כליות .כליות represent the hefty desire towards that which appeals to one, כבד the hefty rejection of that which is disagreeable or repulsive to one. Both together would comprise the complex of the purely physical activities of life which consist simply in taking up that which agrees with one, and rejecting that which disagrees. יותרת על הכבד על הכליות would then be using the higher functions of life in the service of the “vegetative” urges of the senses, the ultimate object and goal of which is represented by חלב.

He, whose קרבן is a זבח שלמים, who seeks the “nearness of God, at the meal of his happiness”, who wants to enjoy his good fortune in the Presence of his God, is first taught by שחיטה and זריקה to change his personality from all and any selfish ideas of living for himself, to devotion and attachment to God, and to the sacred national mission of carrying out the Torah, and of establishing a knowledge and understanding of it. This is the first fundamental condition. Then by הקטרת אימורים he is shown that the result of such attachment and devotion is that he attains a stage where even חלב and כליות and כבד and יותרת על הכבד על הכליות even the demands and efforts of his senses can be raised out of the realm of mere physical necessity into that of the moral free and holy demands which further godliness on earth. Can be raised, and must be raised, if the enjoyment of the wordly possessions and the position of the שלם-one is to be the pure joy which, after all, is the desire and aim of the שלמים-bringer. So, that even חלב המכסה את הקרב ואת כל החלב אשר על הקרב ושתי הכליות והחלב אשר עליהם אשר על הכסלים והיותרת על הכבד על הכליות must be able to become אשה ריח ניחוח לה׳ if his זבח שלמים is to be a קרבן לה׳!

Before the הקטרת האימורים are brought on to the fire, the procedure of תנופה (see Ch. 7,30 et. seq.) has to be undertaken together with the חזה ושוק which are laid on top of them. The חזה ושוק become the property of the כהנים after the הקטרת האימורים. The whole of the rest of the animal is to be eaten by the בעלים in the company of any Jewish friends they may invite. It is to be eaten outside the Temple (but see מל״מ on הל׳ שחיטה II,3), but within the environment of it, i.e., in the Wilderness, not outside the מחנה ישראל, in Shilo, not outside the area in which the town can be seen, and in Jerusalem, not outside the walls of the city (see Zebachim 11a). It must be eaten within the prescribed time limit of שני ימים זלילה אחד.

והקטירו אותו וגו׳ על העולה וגו׳. From the verses (Ch. 6,5) וערך עליה העולה והקטיר עליה חלבי השלמים and (Numbers 28,23). מלבד עולת הבקר אשר לעולת התמיד תעשו את אלה referring to the מוספין, the law is derived (Pesachim 58a and Zebachim 89a) that all other offerings have to be brought after the תמיד של שחר, the daily עולה, which is העולה par excellence, the עליה ;עולה השלם כל הקרבנות. The daily national עולה, brought morning and evening, at the rising and sinking rays of daylight, is the constant breathing of the Jewish National devotion, between these two all the other offerings are sandwiched, all the others are merely consequences, results of the great national fundamental offering. Here, too, it says, and here for the first time והקטירו אותו וגו׳ על העולה וגו׳. If here, too, (as Rashi indeed takes it) all that it wanted to say by these words was the same negative Law, that the שלמים may not be brought until after “the עולה״, the תמיד, then—as Wessely remarks in his commentary — we should have expected it to be quoted for that Law in the Talmud in Pesachim and Zebachim. We therefore prefer to take that here we have the positive declaration of that which so significantly characterises the “peace-meal offering” viz., that it, too, in spite of its apparent intrinsic contrast to it, finds its place upon, and belongs to, the great national עולה. It has to be laid on it, and like all the other offerings, is to be encompassed by it. The תמיד is a national offering and is burnt in its entirety on the Altar. The שלמים, as already remarked, is essentially and exclusively an individual offering, and only its אימורים come on to the Altar-fire, while the real animal comes back to be eaten by the bringers, the בעלים themselves. Now, inasmuch as the אימורים of the “peace-meal” of the private individual have to attach themselves to the national עולה, have to find their place on it and in it, exactly like every other offering, this could be to express the great Truth, that it is just in the pure happiness of the families and individuals that the national devotion to the Torah finds its fruits, and that making the striving even after material wealth and enjoyment into a moral and holy act, which makes the happy enjoyment of them worthy of the Presence of God (as is expressed in the הקטרת הכליות והחלב) forms one of the most important consequences of the National Devotion. אתו, the בני אהרן, the national ministers of the Sanctuary of the Torah, have to bring the אשה the parts of the שלמים of the individual which are to bring God nearer, upon the national עולה which bears up to God the expression of the constant devotion of the nation, on the Altar-fire which is kept uninterruptedly burning by the nation, thus showing the status of the שלמים to the Tomid, it too, is equally אשה ריח ניחוח לה׳.

V. 6. (See note on V. 1). Already there we had designated שלמים as the specifically Jewish offering. This is so very much the case, that the very first offering, by which the Children of Israel were constituted by God into a nation, and entered into a national bond with God, and which was to be repeated afresh each year on the anniversary of the Constitution Day, the קרבן פסח, is fundamentally a form of זבח שלמים. Even מותר פסח i.e., an animal that had been appointed for a קרבן פסח but when the time arrived could not be found, and so could not be used for the פסח, if it turned up later קרב שלמים, was brought as an ordinary שלמים. In Menachoth 83b, it points out that, as in V. 7 it says אם כבש and in V. 12 אם עז, the introductory words of our verse ואם מן הצאן וגו׳ are superfluous, but they come to teach us that an animal that was not really originally meant to be a שלמים but is the result of a פסח having been missing, as מותר פסח, has to have all the procedures of an ordinary שלמים such as סמיכה ונסכים ותנופת חזה ושוק which ordinarily do not apply to the פסח.

V. 8. (See note on V. 2). ושחט אותו, and above V. 2 ושחטו and in V. 13 ושחט אותו. By this precisely stressing the object to be slaughtered in the עזרה the Gemora in Kidushin 57b learns the following laws: — the fundamental law שלא ישחטו חולין בעזרה (see note on Deut. 12,21), that though שלמים, this “meal-offering” which borders most nearly on חולין and is indeed eaten at home, must be slaughtered within the עזרה, ordinary חולין animals, to be used solely for profane purposes, may not be slaughtered there. This prohibition is extended to include animals which could not possibly be used for offerings, such as בעלי מומין and חיות and עופות. More, not only שחיטת חולין but even the bringing of חולין objects of any kind into the עזרה is forbidden. (According to רשב״א this only applies to such חולין objects which at least are of the same kind as those which are used in connection with some procedure of offerings, e.g., bread, fruit, etc. See מל״מ on הלי שחיטה II,3). Only and solely symbolic procedures and symbolic objects are to appear in the hall of the Sanctuary. Bringing in ordinary profane objects, and especially doing such acts in their concrete meaning which are there performed in the symbolic meaning of the Sanctuary — such as שחיטת חולין — is a debasement, yea, a desecration of the place and the procedure to such a degree that חולין שנשחטו בעזרה are even שחיטת חולין בעזרה .אסורין בהנאה would dull the symbolic meaning of שחיטה in which alone שחיטת קדשים must be performed.

V. 9. חלבו. It is difficult to understand the sense of this word here. According to ר״ע in תיכ it designates a certain fat part in the region of the חלב שבין הפקוקלות :אליה. But this is the same fat that ר״ע above on V. 4 designates as חלב שעל הכסלים, and this is mentioned here separately in V. 10. According to ר״י by this word חלבו, the אליה which follows is given for מוקדשין as least the character of חלב, so that anyone who האוכל אליה של מוקדשין also transgresses the prohibition of eating חלב although אליה של חולין is allowed to be eaten and does not come under the heading of prohibited חלב (see Ch. 27,23 et. seq.). We have translated the verse in this sense, taking חלבו to be the collective word introducing all the parts that follow as the חלב which has to be offered on the Altar-fire in the case of a כבש. The word חלבו heads the list, to let us know that in a כבש the idea of חלב includes the אליה which in no other animal is reckoned amongst the אימורים. It is, however, not necessarily the case that from the opinion of ר׳ יהודה one must assume that האוכל אליה מן מוקדשים חייב משום חלב as the word חלב in its broad sense includes all the אימורים (as והקטיר עליה חלבי השלמים, Ch. 6,5), without, of course, כבד ,יותרת ,כליות being reckoned as חלב in its narrower meaning (see מ׳ א׳ רמב״ם 7,5).

אליה only occurs in this connection, and it is only by tradition that we know that it means the extreme end-piece of the trunk, the tail-piece. עצה is, according to Chulin 11a, the backbone in the region of the kidneys: עצה .מקום שהכליות יועצות could then come from עוץ (Is. 8,10 עוצו עצה) with a ה hung on, as צֹנֶה ואלפים (Ps. 8,8). Bringing the אליה amongst the אימורים is what is most characteristic at a כבש. Probably this extension of the חלב idea with the אימורי כבש is in connection with the meaning of כבש as the pure expression of the most complete trust in leaving our fate in the direction of the Shepherd of our lives. In the same way in general the חלב on the כלוית and on and over the קרב and on the כסלים may have not only the idea of חלב in general, but this idea of being the aim of striving for plenty and riches, may also have the idea of the characteristics of the particular part where it is found. So, for example חלב הכלוית of the lower urges, חלב הקרב of nutrition. Unfortunately we lack the physiological knowledge of the meaning of כסלים and of the אליה to be able to follow up this suggestion with regards to these parts.

V. 11. לחם אשה לה׳ and in V. 16 at the שלמים of an לחם אשה :עז לריח ניחוח, while above at בקר V. 5, it says אשה ריח ניחוח לה׳. There is one word common to all three verses, אשה, and ת״כ learns from it that the other different and varying expressions viz., ריח ניחוח לה׳, and לחם apply to all three kinds of שלמים and that these verses are complementary. So that the complete sentence in each case would be לחם אשה (ל) ריח ניחוח לה׳. The first point to be settled is, what the idea לחם adds to the idea אשה. If we could take אשה to mean simply fire, or even the fire to be kept burning on the Altar, then לחם would be “the food of this fire”, that which is given to keep this fire alive. The Torah is the אש דת whose existence on earth is dependent on the devotion of the חלב and the כליות, on all phases of our endeavours being given up to it. But a comparison of all the places up to here, and later on, in which the word אשה occurs leaves no room for doubt that אשה does not mean the fire but that which is given over to the fire i.e., just that which לחם אש would express. So that it remains to find out what the combined לחם אשה expresses. לחם and אשה must of necessity mean two separate nuances of the idea. Chapter 21 offers us various verses which may help us in this investigation. There, in verses 6, 8, 18 and 21 the expressions occur repeatedly and in various applications. The reason given for the priests keeping away from טומאת מת, even when away from the Temple, as well as for specially impressing on them the prohibitions of שריטה ,פאת זקן ,קרחה, is given as: קדושים יהיו לאלקיהם ולא יחללו שם אלקיהם כי את אשי ה׳ לחם אלקיהם הם מקריבים והיו קדש. The command to the Nation not to tolerate in the priests, even in their private lives outside the Temple, any infringment of the special sanctifying priestly marriage laws, but on the other hand, to honour the priests in general, runs:—וקדשתו כי את לחם אלקיך הוא מקריב וגו׳. The prohibition excluding any priest with a bodily defect from service at the Altar reads:—איש וגו׳ אשר יהיה בו מום לא יקרב להקריב לחם אלהיו, כל איש וגו׳ לא יגש להקריב את אשי ה׳ מום בו את לחם אלקיו לא יגש להקריב. Clearly here לחם and אשה are two different aspects of the offering, here לחם is not used referring to אשה but, like אשה is used referring directly to God; it constantly speaks of אשי הי and לחם אלקיך or לחם אלקיו and the idea לחם is specially predominant in the motive for the sanctification of, and for sanctifying, the priests, in V.v. 8 & 18.

A closer examination shows the result which is desired to be effected by giving the offering over to the Altar-fire to be a double one: (a) the effect of the Fire on the parts given over to it, and (b) the effect of the parts on the Fire. The first is the complete penetration of, and being mastered by, the Fire of the Torah on those human phases of life which are represented by the particular parts of the offering, and the second, at the same time to give the Fire its fuel i.e., to keep godlliness alive and active and present on earth. The first may be expressed by אשה, the second by לחם. The words אש and אשה themselves may come from different roots. אש from אשש related to עשש, to consume (from which עש, the moth, is derived) looks on fire from the angle of its consuming power which finds its nourishment in, and consumes all that is given to it. אִשֶׁה from אשה related to עשה to form, to make, looks on fire from the angle of its shaping, forming power. So that אש would be the nourishing of the Fire by the material: לחם; and אשה the forming and shaping of the material by the fire.

לחם referring directly to God, as in לחם אלקיו ,לחם אלקיך, and so also לחמי in Numbers 28,2 can mean nothing else than the table that you lay for Me, i.e., that in which I am to find My content, My satisfaction, and which you have to prepare for Me on earth if I am to “take up M abode with you, if I am to “live” amongst you. אשי ה׳ would, on the other hand, be that which you give over to the Fire of His Torah, according to His Will to be purified and formed. In purpose they both really meet. What is to be להם אלקיך must become אשי הי and what becomes אשי ה׳ just thereby becomes להם אלקיך. By allowing our earthly part to be penetrated and mastered by the Fire of God’s Torah, it becomes a bearer and agent of godliness on earth, and if we want our earthly existence and efforts to achieve the Presence of God on earth, then we must give it over to be penetrated and mastered by the Fire of His Divine Torah. In exactly the same way as the wings of the cherubim are at the same time סוככים בכנפיהם על הכפרת and פורשים כנפים למעלה, forming themselves to be bearers of the Divine Presence from above by protecting the Torah on earth.

If this way of taking it is correct, we can very well understand why it is just in those laws which bring and keep the lives of the priests outside the Temple, and also their personal appearance, into ideal harmony with their profession of service in the Sanctuary of God’s Torah that this profession is described as הקרבת להם אלקיהם as הקרבת לחם אלקיך. It tells us thereby that his service in the Sanctuary is symbolically to teach how the whole of our earthly life, our efforts and deeds are to be לחם אלקינו, to be so ordered that it satisfies the demands which are conditional to having the Presence of God in our midst, to the promise of ושכנתי בתוכם. The life of the priest outside the Temple may not be in contradiction to this idea of his Temple-service, otherwise his real life kills the ideal which his symbolic procedures within the Temple are meant to express קדושים יהיו לאלקיהם ולא יחללו שם אלקיהם כי את אשי ה׳ לחם אלקיהם הם מקריבים והיו קדש, “outside the Temple too, are they to keep the holiness to God which they are to teach within the Temple and not to desecrate the name of their God which they teach there; for in the Temple they bring those earthly things that are to be given over to be mastered and formed by the Fire of the Divine Torah near to God, so that they become the means of giving such satisfaction to God that they bring about His Presence on earth. Therefore, outside the Temple, they themselves are to be a Sanctuary” (see notes on Ch. XXI).

Further, we think that we can now see why this idea of לחם which we know from Ch. XXI, applies to all offerings that are brought on to the Altar, is primarily expressed in our chapter in connection with שלמים .שלמים is just that offering which by the procedure of the offering itself,—of which the enjoyment of it at home, with the table raised to the status of an altar, and the home to a temple, and the company to priests and priestesses, is all part and parcel,—it is just this offering which represents the Presence of God in our whole happy earthly life. It is this that the idea לחם is essential as a preliminary condition, namely, that this earthly life that wants to have the joy of God’s Presence must make itself worthy of that Presence by its endeavours, and by the goals it sets itself to attain by its endeavours.

V. 12. (et seq.). A שלמים of an עז only differs from that of a כבש in the fact that the אליה of an עז is not brought onto the Altar, and the procedures are repeated in full just to tell us that otherwise there is no difference (ת״כ).

V. 16. כל חלב לה׳. All that is to be offered as חלב, everything that comes under the heading אימורים (see on V. 9) belongs to God, i.e., is “holy”, and any other use of it would fall under the idea of מעילה (see on Ch. 5,14 et seq.). But this is here specially emphasized at שלמים because as קדשים קלים ממון בעלים, the animal itself is the property of the bringers who are to eat it, and even בחייהם, while alive, no מעילה applies to it. But as soon as זריקת דם takes place, the אימורים here thought of as חלב, become holy and belong to God, come under the idea of קדשי ה׳ (Ch. 5,15) and their profane use is מעילה (Chulin 117a).

V. 17. הקת עולם וגו׳. The detailed and full laws of חלב follow in Ch. 7,23 et seq. Here the warning of the איסור חלב ודם is added to the foregoing כל חלב לה׳ only to indicate the connection of the prohibition to eat these materials with their use in offerings. Then at the same time to add the law, that, although the use of these materials in offerings is limited in time and space, the prohibition of the eating of חלב ודם remains in full force לדרתיכם בכל מושבותיכם both בפני הבית and שלא בפני הבית, whether the Temple is in existence or not, and both בארץ and בחוצה לארץ, in the Holy Land where the Temple is meant to be, and outside it, where the service of offerings in the Temple is forbidden. (Kiddushin 37b and וצ״ע ,בכריתות ד׳ ב׳). The ת״כ on this verse runs: — בכל ,לינהג הדבר לדורות :לדרתיכם ,לבית עולמים :חקת עולם .בארץ ובחוצה לארץ :מושבותיכם. There it tells us, first, that by חקת עולם, the preceding כל חלב לה׳ is continued, as an everlasting law of the Temple, not only in the משכן, but also in the place that should remain for all times as the one place for offerings as the Sanctuary of God on earth, in the בית המקדש which is therefore called בית עולמים. The Law remains: all what is חלב of an offering is for God. And then to that law is attached לדרתיכם בכל מושבותיכם כל חלב לה׳ that לדרתיכם and בכל מושבותיכם all חלב and all דם may not be eaten. For just because the בית המקדש is called the עולמים — as indeed the law of offering is given as a חקת עולם — the duty of offerings is altogether an everlasting one and the laws of the offerings and the consequences of them apply at all times. It is only the temporary destruction of the Temple and our exile from the Land, which for the time-being prevent our carrying out these laws. It is only for the time-being that the conditions are not there under which such carrying out of the laws is expected from us and permitted to us. But that does not mean that the Laws themselves and the consequences of them are abrogated. As little as the law כבד את אביך has ceased for one whose father is absent, or the law ולמדתם את בניכם for one who has not yet got any children. So that, by our having to keep the חלב-ודם-laws as it says מושבותיכם לדורותיכם, the duties of the Temple and offerings are effective for us even today. Every time we refrain from eating any blood or חלב we prove the lasting reality of the sacrificial laws, show that we expect them ultimately to be reinstated, and make the most practical protest against every attempt at making a starting point in so-called efforts at reform in finding that a supposed abrogation and obsoleteness of the sacrificial laws has taken place. The connection between the prohibition of eating חלב and the sacrificial laws is also specially apparent in the fact that, according to Ch. 7,25, that the prohibition is limited to those animals of which offering could be brought, to שור כשב ועז excluding חיה and עוף. But, on the other hand, the prohibition of eating blood, which here is placed equally with חלב in connection with bringing offerings, goes beyond this restriction, it is not limited to the kinds of animal which are fit for offerings, it extends to חיה and עוף, to all warm-blooded animals. So that the prohibition of eating blood must have an additional reason apart from its relation to offerings. (See on Ch. 17,10 et seq.).

Inasmuch as here the prohibition of חלב and דם is in connection with the bringing of offerings the underlying thought can be as follows:- Blood and חלב-fat are the two poles of the whole animal organism. In the blood, the whole ego, the whole being of the animal is concentrated, הדם הוא הנפש and חלב-fat is the final product, the ultimate aim of the whole organic life of the animal. (חֵלֶב is only דם changed to purely selfish purposes, while חָלָב is דם changed to purposes of love, and both are forms of חלף). Symbolically, i.e., in an animal-offering animal, blood can be used to represent the human being, the human ego, and animal-חלב can express human aims. But concretely, the animal ego may never become the human ego, and animal aims are never to become human aims. And just because they are used in the offering-symbolism for human beings, they are never to be allowed to concretely become part of the human body, to that the identification of human nature and animal nature find no place in the way we regard ourselves. Cf. regarding blood Ch. 17,11.

V. 2. נפש .נפש כי תחטא וגו׳ ועשה וגו׳, the soul, is the real essence of a human personality. It manifests itself as mind and will. The body with its organs and powers is entrusted to it for mastery and guidance. To use this mastery and guidance in accordance with the Will of God, the נפש itself has to submit itself to the “fire” of the Torah and to allow itself uninterruptedly to be ruled by its light and warmth. The body subservient to the soul, the soul to God, then the spiritual-physical active life of Man is spent in the service of God, and when the man exercises his own free will by means of the use of his body, he is exercising the Will of God. But if the נפש withdraws itself from the enlightenment and life-giving warmth of the Fire of the Torah — this is what the literal basic meaning of חטא is, as we concluded from the phonetic relation of חטא to חתה see note on Gen. 39,9 — then it runs the danger of allowing the organs and powers of its body, which it should only allow to act within the limits imposed by the Will of God, to act in opposition to the Will of God. The offering, with which a soul that has fallen out of the focus of the Will of God which should form the centre which directs all its actions, seeks to regain the nearness of God, is called a קרבן חטאת. This seeking again for the nearness of God (קרבן) atones for the withdrawal away from the אש דת into which the soul had fallen.

But one can only attempt to compensate for a sin by means of an offering if the sin had occured בשגגה, not only through carelessness, inadvertence, but in it. The act must be תחלתו וסופו שגגה, begun and completed in inadvertence. But if either at the beginning or at the completion of the act there was consciousness of its sinful nature (זדון), even if this consciousness came at a moment when it was impossible to prevent the sin being completed e.g., הזורק אבן לרה״ר בשבת ונזכר לאחר שיצתה מידו (Sabbath 102a) and of course where תחלתו וסופו זדון, where the whole act is done consciously knowing it was sinful, here the sin lies beyond the sphere where an offering can atone.

We have already remarked (on Gen. 8,1) on the difference between שגג and שגג .שגה is an error done through carelessness. In the moment of the שגגה the perpetrator is not conscious of, does not worry about the legality or otherwise of his act, he is not, at that moment: חרד על דבר הי as Isaiah expresses it. It is just this lack of attention, this carelessness as to whether his actions are in accordance with the demands of the law, wherein lies the sinfulness of his mistake, it is this which is the פשע which lies in every חטא, (Ch. 16,16) פשעיהם לכל חטאתם. The inattention which caused the mistake can be in regards to the Law itself e.g., it slipped his memory that חלב was אסור, or that it was serious enough to be punishable by שגג ;כרת בלאו או שגג בפרת; or it can be that he was quite conscious of the Law with all its implications, but the nature of the object escaped him, e.g., he knew the איסור חלב in all its gravity but he thought that the piece of fat was שומן (fat which is allowed to be eaten), or similar cases. Whether a שגגה has to be atoned for by a חטאת only in cases where a knowledge of the law had been present beforehand הכיר ולבסוף שכח, or even in the case of a תינוק שנשבה בין הנכרים, a child that had grown up with non-Jews, so that it had never had a knowledge of Judaism, is a matter of controversy which is dealt with in Sab. 69b. Rambam decides as Halacha according to the latter opinion. Even שוגג בלא מתכוין, an action done, only in temporary unconsciousness of its sinful nature, but even if done without any intention of doing it at all מתעסק (e.g., he had a piece of חלב in his mouth and quite unintentionally swallowed it without having any intention of eating anything, as וקסבר רוק הוא ובלעו) comes under the idea of a שגגה which necessitates a מתעסק בחלבים :חטאת ובעריות חייב שכן נהנה; for at any rate he has derived enjoyment from it. It is only regarding שבת, where the sin consists in carrying out an intention (showing Man’s power over matter. I.L.)—מלאכת מחשבת—that מתעסק is not חייב a חטאת; e.g., נתכוין להגביה, if he only intended to lift a knife from the ground, or even נתכוין לחתוך את התלוש וחתך את המחובר if he intended cutting an apple which had been picked yesterday but cut one off which was still growing on the tree, his action חתיכת המחובר is not the carrying out of human intention, and so is not an action which really profanes שבת and does not necessitate a חטאת (Kerithoth 19b).

מכל מצות ד׳ וגו׳. The expression מצות אשר לא תעשינה for prohibitions is an awkward one. According to the grammatical construction מצות would be the subject of אשר לא תעשינה, and it would then mean: “commands which are not to be fulfilled”. The only way we can explain it is to take the אשר to refer not to מצות but to the objects of the מצות, “God’s commands regarding such things which are not to be done”. Equally difficult is the construction of the sentence נפש כי תחטא מכל מצות ד׳ וגו׳. Usually חטא does not have the sin following it in the accusative. Also to take the מ in מכל as expressing even not having kept at a distance from the sin would be against any analogous construction to be found anywhere in connection with חטא. There is, however, no alternative but to accept here a construction of חטא with the accusative, and to take the מ in מכל to be—as is quite common in these laws of the offerings—a “partitive”, some of all the prohibitions. And, as a matter of fact, the Halacha teaches that not all sins done out of inadvertence necessitate a חטאת. A חטאת has only to be brought for such a sin done in שוגג which, were it done intentionally, would entail the punishment of כרת: a לא תעשה שיש בו מעשה שחייבין על זדונו כרת. So that all prohibitions are excluded where the intentional transgression would not incur the penalty of כרת even if they do incur capital punishment as וגונב נפש מישראל ,מכה אב ואם. Also פסח ומילה, although omitting them is punishable by כרת, because they are positive commands and not prohibitions. Finally, also מגדף, blasphemy, which although it is definitely a “כרת״-prohibition, is not done by any action, but merely by words (Kerithoth 2a). The example which is taken as setting the standard is ע״ז, the one special sin, the only one whose שגגה is actually mentioned in the Torah as necessitating a חטאת (Numbers 15,21 et seq. see notes thereon). There it says תורה אחת, in V. 29 תורה אחת יהיה לכם לעושה בשגגה והנפש אשר תעשה ביד רמה וגו׳ ונכרתה הנפש וגו׳, and thereby concerning the חטאת duty for שוגג, all cases must be similar to ע״ז (ibid 3a) הוקשה כל התורה כולה לע״ז.

This limitation of the חטאת-duty to ל״ת שיש בו כרת may, on the one hand be, because of the natural weaknesses of humanity no man can be expected to be so perfect that he never unintentionally makes a slip. (of Man is not said שגיאות מי יבין). Hence it is only such שגגות that need special atonement, the sins of which are of such special gravity that they are punishable by כרת, and consequently people can be expected not to fall into carelessness or indifference with regard to them. It could also be that the limiting of a חטאת to שגגה of a כרת-prohibition is meant to impress us to take special care to keep ourselves keen and conscious of just this particular group of God’s laws. As we shall have to go into and prove at another place, the חייבי כריתות comprise by preference sins which are specifically Jewish, and even those that, apart from כרת are at the same time חייבי מיתות ב״ד, the כרת still has its roots in their special Jewish relationship. As examples we mention נדה ,דם ,חלב ,פסח ,מילה and all עריות which are only בכרת, and in accordance with our supposition do not all fall upon a ,בן נח כל ערוה שב״ד של ישראל ממיתין עליה ב״ג מוזהר עליה וגו׳ (Sanhedrin 57b). According to הל׳ מלכים ,רמב״ם 9,5, אחותו מן האם would be an exception, but see כ״מ on it. Little as it becomes us to try to appear to know, or even to imagine anything precise about something like the כרת-fate which is entirely in the Hands of God alone, the words הכרת מעמיה does express primarily a complete uprooting from the present and the future of our People. The sins penalised by כרת would accordingly render the person committing them unworthy of permanent root which our People have in the soil of the future. These sins then, do have a deep connection with the specific nature of Judaism. This relationship would also be in accordance with what the ת״כ says on our verse, viz. that, while נפש includes everybody who belongs to the bond of Judaism and so גרים and עבדים are included, בני ישראל excludes all non-Jews. So that although non-Jews bring עולות on the Jewish Altar, no חטאת may be accepted from them.

ועשה מאחת .ועשה מאחת מהנה can mean nothing else but even if he only does part of some forbidden act. For instance, regarding the prohibition of working on Sabbath, as soon as he has completed an integral part of the whole forbidden act בשוגג, has written the name שם from the name שמעון דן, from דניאל or נח from נחור, has woven a sufficient amount of the whole, mesh to hold together permanently, he would be חייב חטאת (Sabbath 103b). Just as here the מ in מאחת can only be understood in a partitive sense, so the מ in מהנה must also be taken to be partitive, something which belongs, as a part to a collective idea. For instance, from the basic idea (אב) of the prohibition to plant on Sabbath (נוטע), the pruning of a tree (זומר) is considered as a part of the same collective idea of furthering growth (תולדה) (Sabbath 103b & 13b). Hence the dictum: הנה אבות, מהנה תולדות (ibid). At the same time, the combination מאחת מהנה leads to the consideration of the number of errors committed, they can be considered as אחת מהנה or as מאחת מהנה. Several forbidden acts may have been committed, but as they all come from one and the same error are considered as one, (אחת מהנה); e.g., someone forgot that today is Sabbath, and in this one error performed several מלאכות of several אבות (see notes on Ex. 35,1), שגגת שבת וזדון מלאכות, they are all considered as one error and only one חטאת is to be brought. Or, he knew today was Sabbath, but it slipped his mind, that certain activities were forbidden, and so performed several אבות מלאכות. In this case the breaking of the one prohibition to work on שבת is regarded as several separate errors, as מאחת מהנה) זדון שבת ושגגת מלאכות), and a separate חטאת has to be brought for each separate מלאכה.

Altogether the חיוב חטאת is reckoned by the number of errors and not by the number of acts. A work done through thoughtlessness on יום הכפורים which falls on a שבת necessitates two חטאות. Repeatedly eating חלב over a lengthy period, having forgotten that חלב is forbidden food (בהעלם א׳), and not remembering it in between, necessitates only one חטאת.

V. 3. הכהן המשיח. According to Horioth 11b & 12a, this refers only to a High Priest who has actually been annointed to serve in the Mikdosh, but not to one who is a מרובה בבגדים, one who, in the absence of the שמן המשחה, as in the time of the second Temple, has only been inducted into his office by investure with the high-priestly garments. Further, it does not apply to a משוח מלחמה, who has only been annointed for the purpose of making the prescribed proclamations before the army went to war (Deut. 20,2). So that it is only the most complete and highest priestly representative of the Nation who is designated here as הכהן המשיח. On the other hand משיח שעבר, one who had been annointed to serve in the place of a כה״ג who was temporarily unfit to serve, and who resigns his office when the first one is fit again to resume his fuctions, and a High Priest who has retired on account of his advanced age, are not excluded (Horioth ibid and 9b).

לאשמת העם. On Gen. 40,21 we have already found from its etymology, that the basic idea of the word אשם is “to bear a seed of desolation within oneself”. If, then, here the erring of the כהן המשיח is described as a factor that could become אשמת העם, or even be considered as an אשמת העם, we must realise how the כה״ג as such, represents the Nation having achieved and living the ideal Jewish life (see on Ex. XXVIII). Hence we can understand how the חטאת הכהן המשיח comes to be atoned for in the Mikdosh as לאשמת העם as something that endangers the future of the Nation. This symbolic incorporation of the National Idea in the person of the High-Priest appears even more stikingly when we compare this first paragraph of our chapter verses 3—12, with the next paragraph, verses 13—21. For exactly the same offering, and exactly the same procedure, is prescribed there as here. Both are פרים, both are חטאות פנימיות, i.e., their blood is not placed on the קרנות מזבח החיצון but is taken into the היכל and there a two-fold procedure performed הזיה על הפרוכת and מתנות על קרנות מזבח הקטרת. Both are פרים הנשרפים i.e., with the exception of the אימורים which come onto the Altar Fire, have to be burnt entirely outside the ג׳ מחנות. Apart from שחיטה neither of them have anything in common with ordinary חטאות חצוניות (dealt with in the succeeding paragraphs verses 22—26 & 27—35) except שפיכת שירים ליסוד and הקטרת אימורים. And now think; the personality to be atoned for in the second paragraph verses 13—21 is none other than the Nation in its real actuality and considered jointedly in the two elements that constitute it, viz., עיני הקהל the guiding intelligence of the Nation, the ב״ד הגדול, the סנהדרין, and the Nation itself whose acts are to be guided by it. This חטאת has only to be brought if the Sanhedrin had made an erroneous decision regarding a matter that חייבין על זדונו כרת, i.e., שגגו בהוראה, and following this wrong decision the people had actually committed the sin. Both elements, the National guiding intelligence and the national behaviour, which are concretely present in the ב״ד הגדול together with the צבור are joined in the כה״ג, the symbolic highest representative of the Nation as a whole. He, the כה״ג has to bring exactly the same חטאת if he הורה לעצמו שוגג ועשה שוגג if he committed a grave sin by reason of a mistaken decision of his own as to what the דין really is, בדבר שחייבין על זדונו ״שהוראת כהן משיח לעצמו כהוראת ב״ד לצבור״ ,כרת, the decision which the כהן משיח makes for his own practice is exactly parallel to that of the ב״ד הגדול for the practice of the Nation. (Horioth 6b). A parity which finds its expression in the לאשמת העם of our verse (ibid). But there (7a) too, it says that the הוראת כהן המשיח לעצמו only has this result if he is מופלא, i.e., if he excels sufficiently in knowledge of the Law that, being qualified to make such decisions, he is entitled to do so. But if he is not מופלא, then הוראה דידיה לאו כלום הוא, his decision for himself is completely null and invalid, is nothing but meaningless pretension, and his sin falls into the category of an ordinary שגגה, which in the case of a כה״ג has no atonement in an offering. In the same way teachings and decisions of a ב״ד that is not מופלא, that is not competent to make national decisions by excelling in knowledge of the Law, and therefore has no right to make them, are similarly without meaning and הוראה דלהון ולא כלום, invalid. A Jewish community which has acted against the Divine Law by reason of a wrong decision given by an insufficiently learned and hence incompetent ב״ד, has only committed an ordinary שגגה which is not to be treated as a communal sin and atoned for by a פו העלם דבר של צבור,—called a פר חטאת in the following paragraph—but each individual must atone separately by a חטאת יחיד. It is not office and dignity, but knowledge, which grants competence in Jewish circles.

והקריב על חטאתו אשר חטא. Whereas by לאשמת העם the error of the כהן משיח which is to be atoned for by the חטאת—quite similarly to an error committed by the Nation—is fixed as being an actual practical sin brought about by an intellectual error, העלם דבר עם שגגת מעשה, the addition of the words על חטאתו אשר חטא makes it clear that the הוראה of the כהן משיח only grows into an אשמת עם by חטאתו אשר חטא, only by a sin wihch he has committed as a result of his own false interpretation of the Law, but not when הורה ועשו אחריו בהוראתו, but not when he has made an erroneous decision and others, even a whole Jewish community have sinned on the ground of his error (ibid. Horioth).

This stipulation sharply differentiates the respective functions of the office of a כה״ג and those of the ב״ד הגדול. The Jewish priest, even the High Priest, as such, has no authority whatsoever. Interpretation of the Law, of the Torah, is not his high-priestly attribute. Only symbolically in the Temple does he represent in himself the united combination of ב״ד and צבור, the ideal of the nation living the perfect Torah-life. His word has no power “to bind or to loosen”. But his הוראה is only valid for himself, and in the Temple הוראת כהן משיח לעצמו כהוראת ב״ד לצבור, has the same atonement before God. In actual life, outside the Temple in the midst of his people, the Jewish High Priest stands with relation to the Law of God on exactly the same plane as the lowest hewer of wood. The only difference is that an ordinary error of the High Priest, a simple שגגת מעשה has no atonement by means of an offering.

But this evaporates into thin air all the thoughtless fables of a Jewish hierarchy which try to make the Jewish hierarchy the father and mother of all hierarchic presumption. A presumption which has passed from mouth to mouth as an axiom, and which is destroyed equally by the theory of the Jewish Torah, as by the facts of Jewish History. Nowhere in the course of the thousands of years of Jewish history do we find that the authority of the priests as such had any important influence on the shaping of the community.
