In the overwhelming majority of cases, the men who influenced Jewish national life as teachers and leaders were non-priests, and those amongst them who were priests, owed the influence they exerted, not to their priestly position, but to their personal qualities, which would have swayed the nation in any case, even if they did not belong to the tribe of Aaron. So that if in Deut. 17,9, the call to the highest authority in the Law is worded: ובאת אל הכהנים הלוים ואל השופט וגו׳, this is explained in Sifri—quite in agreement with what we say here—to mean that if amongst the priests and Levites there can be found persons qualified to sit in the supreme tribunal of the Law it is a מצוה to have priests and Levites also amongst the members of the Sanhedrin, but not that the presence of such is a necessity for the validity of the Sanhedrin, and certainly not that it must consist exclusively of priests, מצות ב״ד שיהו בו כהנים ולוים, אעפ״י שאין בו כהנים ולוים כשר. In Sanhedrin 42b it is further explained that this placing together the highest court with priests comes to tell us that the competence of the supreme court in its full powers is bound up with the existence of the priestly service in the Temple, as indeed the exercise of its highest authority is connected with the Sanhedrin sitting in a hall of the Temple, מלמד שהמקום גורם. By this, Jewish Justice is shown to stand not merely as a separate branch of the necessities of political-national requirements, but as an issue of the same Will of God which ordered the Altar to be built for His Torah, and Who commanded that the carrying-out of His Will was to be represented in His Mikdosh by offerings brought to the fire of His Torah. That which the Priest taught symbolically in the Temple was to be carried out in actuality in the concrete lives of the People by the direction of the Sanhedrin. Both were עבודת ה׳.

Certainly the Torah expects that the priests, altogether the whole tribe of Levi, by the service in the Sanctuary of the Torah to which they are allocated, and by the position in the Nation to which they are appointed and by which they lacked the security of landed property, should preeminently see, as it says, their inheritance in God”, and develop into men with deep knowledge of the Torah and of the spirit of the Torah, so that those who ישימו קטורה באפך וכליל על מזבחך are at the same time יורו משפטיך ליעקב ותורתך לישראל, or as the last of the Prophets, Malachi, still exhorted the degenerate priests of his time:— שפתי כהן ישמרו דעת ותורה יבקשו מפיהו (Ch. 2,7). Only it is activity in teaching, in exhortation, directing and leading people back to God and to their fellowmen, which the Jewish priest is expected to show by word and example. תורת אמת היתה בפיהו ועולה לא נמצא בשפתיו בשלום ובמישור הלך אתי ורבים השיב מעון (ibid). But there was no compelling force for the Word of the Law in the office of the Priest, as the Gemora (Sanhedrin 6b) commenting on this verse in Malachi differentiates very sharply the contrast between the offices of Sanhedrin and Priest: — משה היה אומר יקוב הדין את ההר אבל אהרן אוהב שלום ורודף שלום ומשים שלום בין אדם לחברו, “The principle of Moses is: Justice must bore through a mountain, but that of Aaron is: To love peace, pursue peace and to bring peace between man and man”. More, by the saying: מלך במשפט יעמיד ארץ ואיש תרומות יהרסנה (Prov. XXIX4) the dependent position in life of the priest as איש תרומות makes him considered as unsuitable for wielding the power of the office of judge. (Kethuboth 105b). In no case whatsoever can one find even the slightest trace of finding in the Jewish High Priest a prototype for the authority of a “pope”. The Urim and Tummim were the pronouncements of God for very restricted cases of national undertakings, and solely regarding their expediency or inexpediency, but not with reference to their being in accordance with, or not in accordance with, the demand of the Law of God.

When we consider that the פר כהן המשיח had to be brought only על חטאתו אשר חטא, for his own sin caused by his erroneous interpretation of the Law, but not like פר העלם דבר של צבור for הוראה לאחרים ושגגת אחרים, the mission of the Jewish High Priest is clearly seen to be, to show by his life the example of the true understanding and the true carrying out of the Torah. To that which the ב״ד הגדול has to bring the Nation to fulfil, by their teaching, he has to bring them by the exemplary model of his life. He is to be מופלא בהוראה, but is to use the powers of decision his learning gives him, primarily in ordering his own life in an exemplary manner. That is also why our High Priest must be a complete man, as husband and father must live the full life of a Man and a citizen in the midst of the people. Our High Priest was not allowed to live a celibate life.

פר בן בקר, his offering is:- פר, “the serving animal of work”, for he does not bring his offering as a private individual, but as one appointed to work in Gods acre—the Jewish “God’s acre” is not the churchyard, the home of death, but the field of life—. As the כהן המשיח he has to appreciate his sin and to bring to his mind the resolution to be faithful and mindful of his position in the future. As פר, as the worker in God’s fields, by living a life which is commensurate with his service in the Sanctuary of God’s Law is he to open up the minds and feelings of God’s People to receive the seeds of Light and Life out of the Torah. As such a פר is he to stand at the entrance of the Sanctuary of the Torah, and moreover as a פר בן בקר. According to ת״כ, the animal is called a פר when it is mature, בן בקר when it is still young. The combination פר בן בקר would accordingly designate “a young mature ox”, that would be an ox in the first year of its maturity, namely a בן שלש, in the third year of its life, (see also Rosh Hashona 10a). Just as the Nation has always to remain בן שנה, to keep itself always in its youth towards God, just as the Torah fears hardly anything as much as ונושנתם בארץ (Deut. 6,25), as the community “becoming old” in their relationship to God, but wishes each fresh day to waken us to lay hold of our mission with new freshness and new enthusiasm, so is the bearer and minister of this People of God to remain eternally “young” in spite of his maturity, he is always to enter afresh into his great calling, never become “old” in his office, never feel “old” in his office. For it is just this “becoming old in his office” that is primarily the cause of such errors which here he is coming to atone for. Long years of study of the Law, and long years of practicing it, easily lead to a life of habit and to arrogance and self-conceit, both of which easily lead us to imagine that we are above the necessity of going afresh to the source of the Law of God with fresh devotion before each step in our practical life, to make certain that it is in accordance with the demand of this Law. The כהן המשיח who טעה בהוראה לעצמו and thereby שגג במעשה has to place himself before God in his offering as פר בן בקר, to undertake that in future he will free himself from the arrogance of having become old in the knowledge and practice of the Torah.

V. 4. ושחט את הפר לפני ה׳: on the North side בצפון as it says above Ch. 1,11 regarding the ושחט וגו׳ צפונה לפני ה׳ :עולה and below in V. 29 regarding the חטאת יחיד the general order for חטאת is given: — ושחט את החטאת במקום העולה and זה בנה אב לכל חטאות שיהו טעונות צפון (Zebachim 48b). Not only purely practical active errors arise from some preponderance of the material-sensuous side of our nature, but also theoretical-practical errors have their root in the same fault. So, for the פר כהן משיח the preliminary condition is also שחיטה וקבלה בצפון (see note on Ch. 1,11).

V. 5. ולקח הכהן המשיח. In the following verses 6 & 7 it simply says הכהן from which the ת״כ learns that although it is a מצוה for the High Priest to do all the procedures of his חטאת himself, they can be done for him by any other כהן.

מדם הנפש ולא מדם העור ולא מדם התמצית :ולקח מדם הפר (Zebachim 25a) i.e., only דם הפר, the blood in which the individuality of the פר, its נפש is concentrated, with which its נפש flows out דם שהנפש יוצאת בו is qualified to be used for the ritual of the blood. This is the blood that spurts out in a stream מקלח; but not the דם העוד or, as it is called in ת״כ the דם הבשד, the blood that oozes out of the skin and flesh when the throat is cut, before the large vessels are cut through, also not דם התמצית, the blood that trickles out—שותת— after the stream, the דם הקילוח, has finished. (וצ״ע דמשמע דאיכא נמי דם התמצית קודם דם הקילוח ואם כן כיון שהשוחט צריך שיתן וורידין לתוך הבלי אי אפשר שלא יהא בו מדם התמצית הראשון, וצ״ל או דלא ממעט אלא דם התמצית האחרון או דלא ממעט אלא כשיש דם התמצית לבד אבל עם דם הנפש לא פסל ואפשר דלא קאמר אלא דלא צריך לקבל גם דם העור ודם התמצית ולא דצריך לכוון שלא לקבלן, וצ״ע, עי׳ זבחים ע״ט ב׳ דאם לא רבה דם התמצית על דם הנפש לא פסל ופליגי אי שכיח לרבות דם התמצית ע״ש). Further מדם הפר, this מ can not be a partitive one, that one only need take some of the blood מקצת הדם, in the כלי, as in V. 7, even after the הזיות ומתנות it still speaks of כל דם הפר and, as a fact, השוחט צריך לקבל את כל דמו של הפר. This מ is a localising one, and teaches that the דם הפר must go directly מהפר from the animal into the כלי, So that נשפך הדם על הרצפה ואספו פסול if the blood had been spilt on the ground and gathered up from there into the כלי, it would be פסול (Zebachim 25a). This explanation of the מדם הפר as meaning דם מהפר is there termed גורעין ומוסיפין ודודשין i.e., you take the מ from the word דם and apply it to the word הפר and take it as if it was written so. But this hermeneutic form is only to be taken for didactic explicitness, in reality the מדם פר expresses the deep real nature of the קבלה:- by קבלה in a כלי שרת the blood is to pass from the actual condition of being דם הפו into the symbolic condition of דם הקדש. By שחיטה is ceases to be דם הפר and by קבלה it becomes דם הקדש. In the same intimate relation in which up to now it stood to the פר it now stands to the קדש. Henceforth it now serves קדש purposes as hitherto it served the purposes of the פר. This removes every remote idea of destructive killing from the שחיטה, and its meaning as a preparation—a necessary preliminary—for a transition to a higher existence, under the direction of, and “contained” by, the idea קדש, is vindicated. Up till now פר was the vessel containing the blood, now the Mikdosh becomes its living organism, from which it receives its direction and aim, (Cf. רשב״ם Baba Bathra 3b the first explanation).
והביא אתו, see notes on V. 6 & 7.

V. 6 & 7. וטבל. Only once in the תנ״ך (Kings II. 5,14) is the word טבל used in the ordinary rabbinic meaning of bathing. This, otherwise, is always expressed by רחץ; but טבל is always a dipping of something in a liquid with the object of some of the liquid adhering to it e.g., ויטבלו את הכחנת בדם (Gen. 37,36), וטבלת פתך בחמץ (Ruth 2,14) etc.

על כל הזייה טבילה :וטבל והזה, the dipping must be repeated at each .הזייה (ת״כ) המיומנת שבימין :אצבעו the most efficient one, or the first one to the right on the right hand, i.e., the index finger on the right hand .(ק״א) הזה trans. is to sprinkle, aiming at an object. הזיה is accordingly a minor זריקה.

נזה ,והזה intrans.: spritzen, und zwar durchweg: anspritzen ( – somit: das Gelangen kleiner Teilchen einer größeren Masse durch Bewegung dieser letzteren an einen anderen Gegenstand. Daher verwandt mit נשֶה .“נשה“ ist derjenige, der freiwillig – ש – etwas von dem Seinigen an einen andern abgegeben hat, das aber damit nicht aufgehört hat, zu dem Seinigen zu gehören – ) ”הזה“, trans. sprengen, ansprengen. הזיה ist somit eine verjüngte זריקה.

וטבל ולא מספיג, בדם שיהא בדם שיעור טבילה מעיקרו, :וטבל בדם והזה מן הדם מן הדם, מן הדם שבענין (Menachoth 7b) i.e., the prescribed ritual is טבילה, to wet by dipping into the blood, not by taking some of the blood up from the sides of the vessel; at the first dipping, the whole quantity of the blood required must already be in the vessel (and this quantity must be received in the vessel at one go, see מה״ק מל״מ 5,9); and finally each הזיה must be made with blood taken afresh from the vessel (דם שבענין as in V. 5) and not with blood left on the finger from the previous sprinkling i.e., על כל הזיה טבילה as above.

‘את פני פרכת הקדש towards where the פרכת covers and separates the קדש i.e., the מלמד שהוא מכוין כנגד בין הבדים .ארון, he has to sprinkle the blood towards the space between the two carrying-poles of the ארון. He has only to aim as this space on the פרכת, it is not necessary for the blood actually to reach the כשהוא מזה לא היו נוגעין בפרכת ואם נגעו נגעו ;פרכת (Yoma 57a). מן הדם שבענין :ונתן מן הדם i.e., for these מתנות on the קרנות מזבח הזהב too, he must always dip afresh each time into the blood —. מזבח קטרת הסמים. The Altar must have been used at least once for the daily קטרת with the full consciousness of its meaning so that the Altar is really and fully a מזבח קטרת (Zebachim 40b) —. מזבח לפני ד׳ ואין הכהן לפני ד׳, הא כיצד עומד :לפני ד׳ חוץ למזבח ומזה, i.e., for the הזיות, towards the פרכת also, the כהן stands in front of the מזבח קטרת so that the Altar is between him and the פרכת, whereas on י״כ he stands between the Altar and the פרכת and has the Altar behind him, in accordance with what it says there that ויצא אל המזבח to perform the מתנות (Yoma 58b).
אשר באהל מועד. The מתנות have to be done with consideration of the whole position of the Altar in the היכל i.e., on the horns of all the four corners of the Altar (Zebachim 40a).

When we consider the ritual of the עבודות הדם which is prescribed here, we find that it differs from that of all other offerings not only in the place of the procedure, which here is in the היכל in the אהל מועד itself, (which is why these offerings are called חטאות פנימיות in contrast to the other חטאות which are only brought in the עזרה on the מזבח החיצון) but also in the actual ritual itself. Whereas for other חטאות only one kind of procedure is prescribed, viz., מתנות דם על קרנות המזבח :נתינה, here there are two: הזיה and וצ״ע, לרמב״ם מתנות דם על קרנות המזבח הקטרת היו ג״כ בהזיה עי׳ הל׳ מ״ק) זריקה ה׳ י״ב והל׳ י״כ ה״ג. ולא ידעתי מקור לדבר זה. הלא הכתוב מחלק בפי׳ וקרא לנתינות על בין הבדים ועל הפרוכת ועל טהרו של מזבח הזהב הזיה, ולמתנה על קרנות מזבח הזהב קרא נתינה וצלע״ג מרש״י יומא נ׳׳ד א׳. נראה לענ״ד בבירור שס״ל ג״כ שמתנות על הקרן היו בנתינה ולא בהזיה ע״ש וצ״ע במשנה פ׳ איזהו מקומן איתא ודמן טעון הזיה על בין הבדים ועל הפרכת ועל מזבח הזהב, זה משמע לכאורה כרמב״ם ונראה שאין ראיה משם דהא לא באה המשנה רק להורות מקום השחיטה והמתנות לא איכות המתנות למתלקותם וכן המשנה ג׳ לא מחלקת ביןׅ מתנות חטאת שהם בנתינה באצבע ובין מתנות עולה שהם בהזיה בכלי וע״ש).

Just as by זריקה, the blood by הזיה is set in active motion towards a given direction, in contrast to נתינה באצבע by which the blood is directed to “stay put” on the height of a given stand-point. The latter נתינה, we have explained above (Ch. 1,5 and 15) as being the characteristic ritual for חטאות which come to atone for an active transgression of the Law. It is meant to impress the atonement-seeking bringer with the necessity in future remaining firm and fast on the moral heights of duty. זריקה the characteristic ritual for an עולה is meant to impress on one who seeks atonement, not for actively having done wrong, but for lack of energy, for neglecting to do that which he ought to do, to impress on such a one the necessity in the future to be energetic in keeping himself active towards the prescribed goal, viz., doing all his duty. If then, here in פר כהן המשיח (as well as in the case of פר העלם דבר של צבור which follows) both rituals, הזיה and נתינה are prescribed to be performed, the sin for which atonement is sought must consist of both these factors. It must have consisted of a passive neglect to which the הזיה applies, as well as an active transgression which is atoned for by נתינה. And as a matter of fact, such is actually the case here. Both at פר כהן המשיח and at פר העלם דבר של צבור the שגגה to be atoned for does consist of two factors viz., העלם דבר) שגגת הוראה) and שגגת מעשה. The one, the שגגת הוראה, the error in theory, is a sin of neglect, of slackness in devotion to “learning” the Law. The other, the שגגת מעשה is, like the שגגה of every other חטאת, a sin of actual transgression. שגגת הוראה finds its atonement in הזיה פני פרכת הקדש and שגגת מעשה in נתינת דם על קרנת המזבח.

שבע פעמים הזיה את פני פרכת הקדש, and according to the כנגד :הלכה בין הבדים. “Protecting and separating” is the combined meaning of the פרכת, the cherubim-curtain hanging over the ארון and between the קדש הקדשים, the דביר, the place of “the Word”, and the קדש, the היכל the place of “the Power of the carrying out of the Word”. (See notes on Ex. 26,33.) Separating: granting complete and absolute protection of God to the דביר the “Torah of God” itself, but only conditional protection to the היכל, to the Table and Lamp of Jewish National prosperity and intellectual development. Protecting, making the Torah itself secure against material and intellectual errors. Both ideas come under the heading of שמירה. As before the “Tree of Life”, so do God’s Cherubim keep guard at the portals of the Torah לשמור את דרך עץ החיים.

If then the כהן משיח (and in quite a similar way the ב״ד הגדול in the פר העלם דבר) brings his blood as a פר before ה׳, and taking it before the פרכת הקדש, sprinkles it seven times towards it. this is to bring home to him:- that, as a פר, as a “worker in the service of sowing God’s seeds”, in the very first place he must take part in the שמירה which God gives to His Law. He must therefore direct all the highest powers of his נפש again and again unceasingly towards this שמידת התורה “seven times” until he achieves perfection—the utmost possible juncture of God’s clear perception of His Own Truths with what can be reached by the human earthly mind (6+1. I.L.). But the שמירת התורה which human beings can accomplish is done in the first instance by למוד התורה, by “learning”, as indeed the שמירה which precedes the עשיה, as is prescribed often in the words ושמרתם ועשיתם is always explained by תלמוד “learning”.

The כהן משיח, who through insufficient knowledge of the Law, has made an erroneous decision for himself הורה לעצמו שוגג, and so has come to do an actual sin עשה שוגג, and a sin of such cardinal importance that it involves כרת במזיד is taught by his דם הפר in front of the פרכת that the בדי הארון stretching out towards the Nation as a whole, expect to find in him, above all, a bearer, and that henceforth he must satisfy this demand in the unceasing study which is the necessary preliminary to the keeping of the Torah — שבע הזיות את פני הפרכת כנגד הבדים. He must at all times endeavour to reach the goal of getting the real meaning and the principles and truths of God which are in the Divine Torah, even although he knows that this goal is but seldom reached. The הזיות were not made על הפרכת but כנגד הפרכת, and ואם נגעו נגעו. He has done what he has to do as long as he has done his utmost.

But he has only then done what he has to do, if he has fulfilled the three conditions which are necessary for the attainment of this goal of using all one’s energies to seek knowledge, (a) וטבל ולא מספיג, that he shall employ this energetic devotion to attaining knowledge at the very source from which human knowledge is drawn, and not from that which has already been used and set aside. (b) ועל כל הזיה טבילה, not only the first, but every subsequent step forward, even the final one just before the goal, must be taken with equally fresh force. (c) ויהא בדם שיעור טבילה מעיקרו, even in cases where the intelligence is already fully developed, the work can only reach its goal by progressive steps forward. The whole quantity is there at the beginning and still the הזיה has to be performed in seven הזיות. Acquiring a knowledge and understanding of the real Truth is always such a lofty goal that even the מופלא, the fully efficient—and here it is dealing only with such—can never reach it by a sudden quick intellectual effort, but must always go back and refer again, and be sure of, his first premises. Perhaps it was just as a מופלא that he came to err, he trusted to his הפלאה (and did not think it necessay for him to look up the דין. I.L.).

And further: עומד חוץ למזבח ומזה, at these הזיות, at these intellectual efforts to attain a knowledge of the Torah, he is to have the מזבח, the representation of the ideal practical fulfilment of the Torah, not behind him but in front of him. The purpose of knowledge of the Torah is not to be merely purely speculative theory. In front of the fulfilment, the מעשה, we are to be placed, and it is for this practical carrying-out that the theoretical knowledge is to be striven for. The מזבח קטרת הסמים לפני ה׳ stands in front of the כהן המשיח. His ideal is to be the fulfilment of the Jewish mission to the highest and most complete degree, to complete ריח ניחוח לה׳. This mission is to be ever present in his mind when he is spending his energy in striving for knowledge and understanding. His הזיות את פני פרכת הקדש have to be made over the מזבח הקטרת as indeed it goes for all of us that גדול תלמוד שמביא לידי מעשה and שכל טוב לכל עושיהם true knowledge only gets revealed to those whose object in striving for true knowledge is true living.

But the error wos not only theoretical שגגת הוראה, it resulted in שגגת מעשה, in actual transgression, in reference to which the finger of the Mikdosh directs the כהן משיח to the “heights” of the Incense Altar which stands before God. This, as we have worked out in Ch. XXX of Exodus represent the Ideal of Judaism, the complete penetration of the תורה into the מנורה and שלחן to render them ריח ניחוח לה׳, the complete penetration of the spiritual and material life of the individual and the nation with the spirit of the Torah to the satisfaction of God in its purest completest conception; an ideal which is threatened at all times with a lowering of its standard by the distance between the perfection of the ideal and the imperfection of the reality. For this reason, even in normal circumstances, once a year at least, this ideal is brought to the minds of the people in its complete purity (Ex. 30,10). But the pure height of this ideal never runs a greater danger of being lowered than when a כהן משיח who is also מופלא בתורה has committed a major sin, an איסור כרת by an erroneous conception of the demands of the Law; or when, as depicted in the next paragraph, the highest authority entrusted with the interpretation of the Law, the ב״ד הגדול has led the nation into committing an איסור כרת sin by their erroneous conception of the demands of the Law. In both these cases acts which the Torah so earnestly forbids have received the stamp of legality by the spiritual heads of the Nation. That is why the finger of the Mikdosh points to all the heights of the ideal (the horns on all the four sides of the Altar. I.L.). Only by taking them all together can the life be formed which can please God and give Him satisfaction, and which makes the אהל into an אהל מועד. These ideals are what the כהן משיח and the ב״ד הגדול in their פר character — as “God’s workers on earth”, must keep constantly in mind, to that by complete and ever-fresh devotion to gaining a knowledge of God’s Will and of the Torah (the preceding הזיות כנגד פרכת הקדש), the ideal itself, in whose service they stand, should not be tumbled down from its height, in the one case by his own sinning and in the other by causing sinning to be committed. By the correct knowledge of the Torah Truth, the ideal must be kept alive in all its height in every direction ונתן הכהן מן הדם על קרנות מזבח קטרת הסמים לפני ה׳ אשר באהל מועד.

But the מזבח לפני ה׳ must stand there already as מזבח קטרת הסמים, it must have received its full meaning as מזבח קטרת by having been used at least once for קטרת הסמים when the מתנות דם are performed on it. For מתנות דם is not its real purpose. The נפש which in שחיטה, in being ready to give up the life it has led hitherto, has taken the first step towards getting near to God, is shown the way to the ideal heights on the מזבח החיצון. The מזבח הפנימי represents this ideal as having been already reached, as is expressed just by קטרת הסמים and it is only to warn the נפש of the כהן המשיח never again to disturb the idea of this ideal, that his blood is brought on the heights of this Altar. So that the Altar must stand there in its ideal meaning as מזבח קטרת הסמים if this דם פר בהן המשיח is to touch its heights.

ואת כל דם הפר ישפך אל יסוד מזבח העולה אשר פתח אהל מועד. The הזיות and המתנות הפנימיות only admonish the כהן המשיח regarding the ideal spiritual and practical heights which should ever be in his mind as the spiritual head of the Nation to protect him from theoretical and practical errors. But the actual standpoint for his practical life, he receives, exactly in the same way as the lowest of the people, not in the אהל מועד but at the פתח אהל מועד, in the antechamber of the Mikdosh, where the מזבח העולה shows the path to be taken which leads upwards to the ideal heights of perfection. It is יסוד מזבח העולה where all the blood of the כל דם הפר ,פר really belongs. When he had performed the הזיות ומתנות הפנימיות he had thereby only won back and ensured the place which he should occupy in common with the whole national community of נפשות בית ישראל which forms the base on which a life which strives upwards to God is built. It was out of this life that he had been in danger of being “uprooted” (see above Ch. 1,5). The שפיכת שירים of these חטאות פנימיות only differs from that of ordinary חיצוניות in that it is poured on the western base, the יסוד מערבי, which faced directly the היכל and was the nearest to the entrance of the היכל, as it says אשר פחח אהל מועד (Zebachim 51a) whereas the שירים of the חיצוניות were poured on יסוד דרומי (see V. 25).

V. 8—10. ואת כל חלב פר וגו׳. With the ritual of the blood, the עבודת הדם, the כפרה is completed. The נפש of the seeker for atonement is re-established on the basis of Judaism in the Sanctuary of God, as a consequence of this regained position before God, he is taught in the הקטרת אימורים how, henceforth, also הלב and כליות and יותרת על הכבד, how, henceforth, his efforts to satisfy the demands of his senses can also be, and should be, raised out of the sphere of purely physical matters, and can be, and should be, devoted to becoming “fuel” for the fire of God’s Torah; that the fault he has committed in no wise stands in the way of a happy pure future, but that just as the אימורי שלמים do, so do the אימורי חטאת belong to the happy cheerful surrender to the power of God’s direction.

V. 11 & 12. ואת עור הפר וגו׳. As a further consequence, the whole of the body of the animal should now, as in the case of all other חטאות, be given to the כהנים to be eaten within the precincts of the Mikdosh in their priestly garments. This is designed to bring the further teaching of the Mikdosh into ordinary life, to preach that, where the דם and the אימורים, the spiritual nature and the inner desires have found their right place before God, then every self-seeking action (such as enjoying a good meal, I.L.), the whole human being, is to be raised to such a priestly degree that every self-seeking act is impressed with the seal of a priestly antechamber of the Mikdosh. But, in our case here, where the נפש that is seeking atonement is not that of one who represents the level of the ordinary man trying to live up to the חורה-Ideal—which is the stage that the antechamber of the Mikdosh represents—but that of one who represents the Perfect Jew who has attained that Ideal, then there is no priestly personality to be found in the whole nation, whose eating these חטאות פנימיות would, even symbolically, preach any lesson to one who is a High Priest, or to the Sanhedrin as a body. Hence that, which, in ordinary cases of חטאות חיצוניות is handed over to be eaten by the כתנים, in cases of חטאות פנימיות has to be taken right out of the National environment of the Temple, חוץ לשלש מחנות and there burnt במקום טהור.

ואת עור הפר ואת כל בשרו וגו׳. After the אימורים have been removed, the whole of the rest of the animal, without flaying or cutting up, was taken out חוץ לשלש מחנות. The Mikdosh as a whole formed one מחנה, the מחנה שכינה, the הר הבית ,the second one, the מחנה לויה; and the whole town of Jerusalem up to the walls, the third, the מתנה ישראל. Thither was it taken, right out of Jerusalem to the בית דשן ,שפך הדשן, where the ashes from the Fire of the Altar were thrown, and moreover, the place must already have been used for this purpose, שיהא לשם דשן, there must actually be ashes there (Yoma 68b), but nevertheless the place must be טהור and ואם טמא יטהרנו if there is anything טמא there it must first be removed (ת״כ). There, the ox is burnt after having been cut up into pieces like the עולה to which the words of our verse על ראשו ועל כרעיו וגו׳ refer, but without הפשטה, unflayed (Yoma 68b). Finally על עצים באש, not as in the case of the על העצים אשר על האש ,עולה, on wood which has been selected specially for the purpose, but on any wood, or straw etc., as long as it is burnt by an actual fire and not by סיד רותח quicklime or גיפסית רותח, other chemical means (Pesachim 75a & ת״כ ibid). But this burning בבית דשן outside the city is only to be done if the פר is still כשר i.e., if nothing has happened which would render it unfit as an offering; ושרף אותו taken to mean כשר (ת״כ) ולא פסול. If, however, it had become פסול, it was burnt exactly in the same way as any other פסולי המוקדשים, within the precincts of the Mikdosh. Hence the sentence: פרים הנשרפים ושעירים הנשרפים בזמן שהן נשרפין כמצותן נשרפין בבית הדשן (ומטמאים בגדים) ואם אינן נשרפין כמצותן נשרפין בבית הבירה (ואין מטמאין בגדים).

In the latter case, if the פסול occured before the זריקה (according to לוי before the יציאה) they were burnt like other פסולי קדשי קדשים ואימורי קדשים קלים in the עזרה, if after the זריקה (or according to לוי after the יציאה) on the הר הבית (Zebachim 104a & b).

Now we are told in Ch. 16,28 of the פר ושעיר של יום הכפורים which were also חטאות פנימיות, and which together with our פר כהן המשיח and פר העלם דבר של ציבור form the whole class which are burnt outside the פרים הנשרפים ושעירים הנשרפים—:שלש מחנות, the שעירים are the שעיר של י״כ and the והשרף אתם יכבס בגדיו ורחץ את בשרו (שעירי ע״ז במים וגו׳, and furthermore that everybody else too, who occupies himself with bringing out and burning the פרים הנשרפים ושעירים הנשרפים becomes טמא and even to the extent of לטמא בגדים וכלים במגע so that the טומאה goes over to clothes and כלים which they touch while engaged with such animals, quite similarly to משא נבלה. They receive this טומאה as soon as they have passed out of the first מחנה, the עזרה. This טומאה, too, is restricted solely to פרים ושעירים הנשרפים כמצותן but פסולים are not מטמא. If we consider all these laws we find that they can all be connected with the motive that lies at the root of this bringing these animals outside the whole national environment of the Mikdosh. On the one hand they make this motive clear to our understanding, and on the other they work against any erroneous deductions which could be made out of the procedure. The חטאות פנימיות like the חיצוניות should really be given to the כהנים so that the אכילת כהנים acting as the symbolic בעלים, completes the אכילת המזבח. But the personality does not exist who would be worthy to serve even only as the symbolic expression of the lofty Ideal of having reached the stage of Perfection of a חטאת פנימית. There can not be anybody, as the reason for every חטאת פנימית is the unreliability, the imperfection of even the very highest heads of the national community. This is so, also in the case of פר ושעיר של יה״כ, as we shall work out when we come to them later. In the whole nation, living around its central point, the Sanctuary of the Torah, there is no personality to be found who would be commensurate with this ideal stage of life, not in the מחנה שכינה, not in the מחנה לויה nor in the מחנה ישראל. So that the bringing it out, anl burning it חוץ לשלש מחנות brings home to the Nation the imperfection of the whole nation, inasmuch as no single person can be found who is actually fit to eat this חטאת, This at once makes it clear why all these laws only apply when נשרפין כמצותן. Should any of these פרים הנשרפים ושעירים הנשרפים have become פסול by any means e.g., by טומאה—(In Zebachim 104b), it remains an undecided question whether even לינה מועיל בפרים הנשרפים although they are not to be eaten,—(are not there לאכילה and the opinion that לינה is פוסלת would materially strengthen our exposition), then even if there was a כהן worthy enough, he would still not be allowed to eat them. So that if נשרפין שלא כמצותן the whole idea falls away, and there is no more point in their שרפה than in the burning of any other פסולי מוקדשין. They are burnt בבית הדשן, it repeatedly says that they are to be taken out to אל שפך הדשן and burnt על שפך הדשן, it stresses that it is to be there where the ashes “which are not able to be burnt further by the altar-fire” are thrown. Their character is also דשן but for an entirely different reason, their אוכלים are lacking. There they are cut up and laid out in their parts just like an עולה so that, the burning, their offering-character is still maintained, and the imperfection of each phase of our life as represented by the various limbs and parts is separately driven home. Only the cutting up is to be done without skinning the body, and the cleansing of the קרב וכרעים is not to be done, and also with regards to the עצים the עולה-requirements are not to be fulfilled, to prevent any idea that this burning represents, or takes the place of, an original idea of a real offering. It must be made clear that these are parts of an offering which have to be burnt because their real purpose can not be carried out.

Finally: פרים הנשרפים ושעירים הנשרפים בזמן שהן נשרפין כמצותן מטמאין בגדים or as רבי expresses the sentence in כל שדמו נכנס לפנים :ת״כ אחרי מות השרפו מטמא בגדים. Later on, in explaining פרשת הטומאה in שמיני we shall work out how the conception of טומאה is identical with that of lack of freedom of will, and that the laws of טומאה are instituted to work against this idea wherever it is likely to be awakened in us by any object or circumstance.

For instance, if we come into contact with the dead body of a human being, or of one of the animals, which are similar in construction to that of a human being. Such a body demonstrates a human being, or an organism similar to a human being, lying powerless under the force of the powers of nature outside him. It, accordingly, awakes the idea that Man has altogether no free will, it brings the idea of death into life, and that Man is a mere puppet in the hands of the physical powers of Nature. The body lying in the utter helplessness of death makes it seem that Life and Death appear as merely different products of one and the same power of Nature. Such a conception would undermine the basic foundation of the whole Torah—the Truth, the fact, of Man’s free will. It is countered by the Laws of טומאה and especially by טבילה במקוה separating the sphere of Life from that of Death, which is imposed before re-entry into the Sanctuary of the Torah which is dedicated to morally human life raising itself above physical compulsion.

But such a conception of the lack of human free will in matters of morality could receive encouragement from nothing more than from פרים הנשרפין כמצותן. For the whole שריפה rests on the plain fact that the Torah presupposes that in the whole nation there is not a single man who could really be said to live up to the ideal of the complete demands of the Torah. How near does this fact, that no absolute and complete victory of the spirit over the body is expected, how near does this border on the fallacious theory that Man is born to sin, and with all the exertion of the best will in the world, can not avoid sinning! How often is the fact that אדם אין צדיק בארץ אשר יעשה טוב ולא יחטא (Eccl. 7,9) used as the commencement of the argument for original sin and that Man is not to be blamed for sinning since it is his nature and he can not avoid it. This dangerous error which lurks in חטאות פנימיות and which would cut the ground away from the very foundation of the Torah, is countered by the law that everybody who comes into contact with the carrying out and burning of these ח׳ פ׳ must get rid of such depressing theories before he may go back into the .מחנה שכינה השורף אותם יכבס בגדיו ורחץ בשרו במים ואחרי כן יבוא אל המחנה (Levit. 35,28). The פרים ושעירים הנשרפין themselves are not מיטמא in themselves—indeed it is stressed that the place of burning must be טהור—but only the מתעסקין in ביציאתן ובשריפתן have to consider themselves טמאים. Are we not told that the goal of the whole development of Mankind is the stage beyond the present state where constant fight has to be waged against one’s lower self. The stage in which the Ideal of Humanity will be realised to such an extent that not only Death will have disappeared from the world בלע המות לנצח, but the holiness that emanates from the Sanctuary of God’s Torah will have so penetrated Life in general that the difference between חול and קדש will have disappeared, that the מחנה שכינה will reach everywhere, far beyond the walls of the Temple into wherever men live and work and then: ביום ההוא יהיה על מצלות הסוס קדש לה׳ והיה הסירות בבית ה׳ כמזרקים לפני המזבח והיה כל סיר בירושלים וביהודה קדש לה׳ צבאות ובאו כל הזבחים ולקחו מהם ובשלו בהם “on the bells of the horses, the high-priestly קדש לה׳ shines, the pots of the Temple like the bowls of the Altar, and every cooking vessel in Judah and Jerusalem is so holy to God, that those that bring offerings can use them for their offerings (Zach. 14,20 & 21).

V. 13. כל עדת ישראל. As a rule the community of Israel is called עדת בני ישראל, the community that is formed by all the Children of Israel. Only in Ex. Ch. XII, at the first constitution of the Nation, they are repeatedly called עדת ישראל i.e., the Community that is formed by the common mission which lies in the name ישראל. And on two other occasions are they called by this name עדת ישראל. Once, when in opposition to the presumption of Korach, the higher mission to which the Levites had already been assigned over the original complete equality of the tribes of the Nation, is to be brought to the fore. (Numbers 16,9). And again, when in respect of the demand for preferential treatment by the tribes of Reuben and Gad, the complete equality of rights of the whole Nation to the conquered territories is to be established from the very beginning (Numbers 32,4). Elsewhere the whole national community is always referred to as עדת בני ישראל. Here by the term עדת ישראל is to be understood, the body which is entrusted with seeing that the national duties of Israel are faithfully carried out, the supreme court of Justice, the ב״ל הגדול, the סנהדרין, just as in Numbers 35,24 & 25, the high criminal court with powers of life and death is simply called: העדה. But that here it is only the very highest senate at the supreme head of the whole nation which is referred to, is indicated by the addition of עדת ישראל ,ישראל, i.e., the full senate consisting of seventy one members. Thus ת״כ (Numbers 35,25) יכול ככל העדה הכתוב מדבר ת״ל כאן עדה ולהלן נאמר עדה מה עדה אמורה להלן ב״ד אף כאן ב״ד או מה עדה אמורה להלן בעשרים ושלשה אף כאן בב״ג ת״ל עדת ישראל המיוחדת שבישראל ואיזו זו סנהדרי גדזלה היושבת בלשכת הגזית.

By כל עדת וגו׳ the Law is given, which in any case already lies in the idea עדת ישראל, that the sin which is to be atoned for must originate in the whole of the full—qualitative as well as quantitative—gathering of the Sanhedrin. If one of the members of this highest senate was legally unfit to have been elected, or if the מופלא של ב״ד, the President, who occupies that position by reason of his predominant knowledge of the Law, should be absent, and his place taken by a substitute, or if the mistake was not shared by all, so that if it was only one single member who declared the others to be in error, or even if he only answered the vote with איני יודע so that the decision was not unanimous, the error is not to be treated as an “error of the Sanhedrin”. (ת״כ ibid & Horioth 4b). The case of איני יודע is not mentioned there. But האי דקאמר איני יודע כמאן דליתא דמי ולא היה צריד להזכירו במתניתין עי׳ סנהדרין י״ז א׳ ורמב״ם הל׳ סנהדרין פ״ח ב׳ מ״מ שם, והגאון באד שבע ס״ל דלא איתותב ר׳ יונתן אלא בהא דקאמר מאה שישבו להורות, אבל ע״א שהוא מנין המיוחד לסנהדרין גדולה בעינן לכ״ע שיהו כולם כהוראה שאף המיעוט שידעו שטעו הסכימו לפחות בהרכנת הראש כהוראה ולא כדמשמע מכל הפוסקים דסגי שישתקו ע״ש בפירושו להודיות ג׳ ב׳, וד׳ א׳ במתניתין הורו ב״ד וידע אחד מהן שטעו ע״ש מלתא .בטוב טעם ודעת ע״ש

ישגו ונעלם וגו׳. We have already (Gen. VIII.1) pointed out and remarked on the difference between שגג and שגה. How שגה denotes a theoretical error, the mind being caught by some definite trend of thought which excludes the consideration of all else. Hence, the stronger form שגע (from which we get “Meshugga” משוגע. I.L.), a fixed wrong idea. This theoretical error is then immediately explained further ונעלם דבר מעיני הקהל וגו׳. The ב״ד גדול is: עיני הקהל, the eyes of the Nation. In their hands the National Intelligence reposes. Out of the Law it has to draw the knowledge for fixing the practice of the Nation. Now “something”, דבר, has slipped from the knowledge of this National Intelligence. They were caught (ישגו) in a false way of understanding the Law, and thereby something escaped them (ונעלם מהם דבר) in their application of the Law. It is true Horioth 7b, seems to take ישגו to denote actual sin, שגגת מעשה. But as ישגו without any doubt refers to עדת ישראל, the Sanhedrin, and in this case it is quite immaterial whether they themselves committed the מעשה or not, it seems that all the Gemora means to say there, is:- were it to say simply ישגו ועשו then one could think that it referred to a sin which the Sanhedrin had committed through an error of judgment, but inasmuch as it says ישגו ונעלם it shows clearly that the Sanhedrin had only made a שגגת הוראה, a העלם דבר which had led to a שגגת מעשה on the part of the קהל. In Horioth 36 & 4a this is given more in detail:— הורו ב״ד לעקור את בל הגוף. אמרו אין נידה בתורה אין שבת בתורה אין ע״ז בתורה הרי אלו פטורין הורו לבטל מקצת ולקיים מקצת הרי אלו חייבין, “If their error denied the complete “body” of a Law, would annul that whole Law itself, then the atonement described here does not apply, it only applies if their error referred to some special part of a Law”, e.g., if they taught that you may not carry on Sabbath מרשות לרשות, but that throwing is allowed. For it says ונעלם דבר ולא שתתעלם מצוה כולה (ibid). It goes on there to say: אין ב״ד חייבין עד שיורו בדבר שאין הצדוקין מודין בו, the erroneous decision of the Sanhedrin has to be atoned for, as such, only yhen it deals with a matter which is not expressly written in the Torah (otherwise even the Sadducees would acknowledge it). Any decision which would contradict something clearly mentioned in the Torah, every schoolboy would know to be a mistake זיל קרי בי רב הוא. Every Jewish child knows it and so is not a matter for the teaching, the הוראה, of the Sanhedrin at all.

ונעלם דבר מעיני הקהל ועשו וגו׳, the theoretical error of the ב״ד הגדול to be atoned for, as such, only when it has resulted in actual practice of the sin. And, moreover, only when their error has caused the קהל to commit the sin: מעשה תלוי בקהל והוראה תלוי׳ בב״ד (Horioth 3a). It is quite immaterial whether the ב״ד have acted in accordance with their הוראה or not. But the practical sinning of the community is only ascribed to the theoretical error of the ב״ד if they had expressly declared it to be the normal rule for actual practice. It would not suffice for the ב״ד to have published their decision as מותרין אתם, but they have expressly to declare מותרין אתם לעשות (Horioth 2a). If somebody had acted on their decision knowing that it was a wrong one שטעו, but having some idea that it was a מצוה לשמוע דברי חכמים, or, if in general he did not recognise the authority of the ב״ד, he was a מבעט בהוראה (Horioth 2b), then the individual himself is considered responsible and not the ב״ד (ibid).

By קהל is understood, according to רשב״א which רמב״ם accepts as הלכה, (Horioth 3a), the majority of the Nation. This majority can be either the majority of the Jews living in Israel at the time (Horioth 5a) even if this consists of a minority of the tribes, or the majority of the tribes, even if this consists of a minority of the whole Jewish population of Israel. ואשמו, by this national sin, brought about by the error of the national intelligence, guilt rests on the whole nation. Like all other חטאות, this חטאת הקהל is only to be brought על דבר שחייבין על זדונו כרת.

V.14. והקריבו הקהל פר וגו׳. The nation, not the ב״ד הגדול, has to provide the offering for the atonement of the ב״ד (according to the teaching of the ר״י (Horioth 4b) which is accepted as Halacha). Here the Nation appears in truth as one organised body. The ב״ד הגדול is the intelligent soul of the national body, the עיני הקהל, hence the Nation provides the פר for its ב״ד, and admonishes itself and them, that it is to hold itself in the service of God as a פר. And most significantly the Nation has to appear here in its “twelve-membered” unity. We hawe already repeatedly had occasion to remark how Israel, to achieve the ideal of its national development is not to consider itself merely as one unit, but as קהל עמים (Gen. 28,3 & XLVIII,4), as קהל גוים (XXXV,2). It is in accordance with this idea that this national offering, brought to atone for a national sin caused by the error of the national intelligence, has to consist not of one פר but of twelve פרים. Each tribe, even the minority who had not sinned, has to provide one פר for the ב״ד הגדול (and as in Jacob’s blessing, and on the אפוד and חשן of the High Priest, the tribes of Ephraim and Menasheh join as one tribe, the שבט יוסף, so that there were just twelve oxen. Horioth 5b). Each tribe, in its own special characteristic calling has to express its expectation that the ב״ד הגדול fulfils its function as פר. And furthermore these פרים are not brought out of the general Temple fund, the תרומת הלשכה like the other קרבנות צבור, but the cost is collected from each individual member of the Tribe (ibid 3b). So that the error of the ב״ד הגדול was brought directly home to every individual Jewish citizen.

V. 15. זקני העדה, not the whole of the Sanhedrin, but three (according to ר׳ יהודה, five, see ל״מ on ה׳ מ׳ ק׳ 3,10) of its most prominent members as representative of the whole. Above on Chap. 1,4 we remarked that this פר העלם דבר של צבור, was one of the two exceptions to the general rule that סמיכה is not done on any קרבן צבור. It seems to be specially required here, to mark the ב״ד as really being the בעלים who are seeking atonement, although the פרים are provided by the participating Nation. But the fact that the סמיכה is done by a representative of the Sanhedrin, and not by each of the seventy one members, as is always done in other קרבנות שותפין goes to show that it is to be clearly understood that it is not an offering for seventy one individuals, but an offering to atone for the Institution of the Sanhedrin as such.

V. 16—21. The ritual prescribed here is exactly the same as that for the פר כהן המשיח, and in our notes on that, we have already drawn attention to the relationship between it and our פר העלם דבר של צבור. Both the כהן המשיח and the ב״ד הגדול are the highest spiritual heads of the Nation, the one to use his knowledge of the Torah to act as a model Jew in front of the Nation, and also symbolically as the embodiment of the National Ideal; the other, as the highest intelligence of the Nation, is entrusted with the teaching of the Law to the Nation. Just as the כהן המשיח has, for his own life, so has the ב״ד הגדול for guiding the life of the Nation, always to keep before it in its mind, the Ideal of the Torah in all its ramifications: — the guarding of the Torah (פרכת), the ideal of a perfect life of the senses and of the spirit (מזבח הזהב), and the practical endeavours to reach these ideals (מזבח העולה). And in the case of פר העלם דבר, similarly to that of the כהן המשיח, there is no personality to be found, who, by eating the פר could represent the actuality of having achieved these ideals in his life. פר העלם דבר, like פר כהן המשיח, belongs to the class of פרים which have to be burnt חוץ לשלש מחנות, as is stressed, as the motive and object of this שריפה, by the concluding words, בנין אב לכל חטאות הקהל :חטאת הקהל הוא (ת״כ) שישרפו; all חטאות by which the imperfection of the actual life of the Nation, in contrast to the National Ideal Life, is brought home, which would include the שעירי ע״ז (Numbers 15,24), and altogether all חטאות פנימיות have to be burnt outside the national area of the Temple.

V. 22. The two preceding cases, the פר כהן המשיח and the העלם דבר של צבור are cases for the atonement of national sins—the חטא כהן משיח is also לאשמת העם—; they are both characterised by being, not merely practical committed sins, but sins committed as the result of theoretical mistakes made by the two highest intelligences competent in the knowledge of the Law, כהן משיח מופלא and ב״ד הגדול.

Now two other cases follow, חטאת נשיא and חטאת יחיד both of which are purely and simply practical sins, שגגת מעשה without שגגת הוראה, both purely to atone for private individual sins, and in contrast to the preceding חטאות belong to the category of חטאות חיצוניות.

The נשיא about whom it speaks here, designates—as Horioth 11a derives from the addition of the words מי שאין על גביו אלא ד׳ :מצות ד׳ אלקיו אלקיו—the one “who has nobody above him but God”, i.e., not נשיא שבט, the Prince of a Tribe, but the Prince who stands at the head of the whole combined Nation, the King: (of whom it uses a similar phrase in Deut. 17,19: למען ילמד ליראה את ה׳ אלקיו וגו׳). At the time when the Nation was divided, both the King of Judah and Israel came under this denomination (ibid. b). Calling ה׳ the אלקים of some special individual, as here ה׳ אלקיו, is generally used to indicate some special relationship in which that individual stands towards God, as His messenger, His tool, His announcer or herald etc., etc. So we find it used of the High Priest in Levit. 21,12; of the priests in general, ibid XXI,17 & 22; and Deut. 18,7. Of Kings in Deut. 17,19; Sam. I. XXX.6; Kings I. V.3 et alia. Of Prophets, Kings II. 5,11 et alia. Here, too, it indicates the King as the special tool of God, in His service. The King, into whose hand is placed the powers of disposition over the Nation for the purpose of furthering matters pertaining to God in the Nation; who, for certain purposes, is placed, under God, over the whole Nation, שתהא אימתו עליך :שום תשים עליך מלך (Zebachim 20b, see notes on Deut. 17,14 et seq.). The office of King is also called נשיא in Kings I. 11,34; Ezekiel 34,24 & XXXVII,25, as well as repeatedly in Ch. XLV & XLVI.

The grouping of these פרשיות החטאות points to the King occupying the first place in the carrying out of the Torah, as the כהן המשיח does in the knowledge of it. The first one in the Nation to obey the Law is to be the King. But as no שגגת הוראה appears in his חטאת, no interpretation of the Law is connected with his position as King. With regards to decisions as to what is right according to the Law, he is directed, like every other יחיד, to the ב״ד. He is the First יחיד amongst the יחידים. In contrast to the sin of the High Priest and that of the Nation caused by the supreme Court which are designated אשמת העם (V. 3) and ואשמו (V. 13) and חטאת הקהל (V. 21), of his sin it says אשר נשיא יחטא וגו׳ ואשם, that the sin which a King commits is a guilt which is a threat to his own future only. High above the Nation though he is raised by the position of power allotted to him, with regard to his sins he stands alone as an individual before God, even as the lowest of his subjects. Well can we understand the words which ר׳ יוחנן בן זכאי applies to אשר נשיא יחטא viz.: אשרי הדור שהנשיא שלו מביא קרבן על שגגתו. אם נשיא שלו מביא קרבן צריך אתה לומר מהו הדיוט, ואם על שגגתו מביא קרבן צריך אתה לומר מהו זדונו. “Happy the generation whose King seeks atonement by an offering for a sin done unintentionally. How must the conscience of the ordinary people be stirred by the conscientiousness of their King, and if an unintentional sin affects him like this, what would he feel for an intentional wrong!”.

V. 23. או הודע אליו וגו׳. The או is in contrast to the ואשם in the preceding verse. It reads like this: — If the King sins by doing a major sin unconsciously then ואשם, the guilt and its consequence remains resting on him and his future, או, or if he becomes conscious of his sin, he can atone for it by means of a הודע אליו .חטאת: The sin must come, or be brought, to his mind, so that he now knows he has committed it. But if even two witnesses assure him that, for instance, he had eaten חלב and he denies it, and asserts לא אכלתי, he is not חייב קרבן. For, as a sin committed consciously, במזיד, can not be atoned for by a חטאת and only a man himself can judge whether he was conscious or not of the sinfulness of any of his actions at the moment of doing it, the obligation of a man to bring a חטאת can never be established by witnesses. They can testify אכלת חלב but they can not assert חייב אתה קרבן. So that regarding the obligation to bring an offering, even the testimony of two witnesses is of no avail against his contradiction: מה אם ירצה לומד מזיד הייתי (Kerithoth 11b & Yebamoth 88a).

Now the fact that here the Torah makes the reservation in the case of a King (exactly as in that of an ordinary הדיוט v. 28) that the testimony of witnesses does not suffice in this case to make offering obligatory, proves that in ordinary cases, the King would be under the jurisdiction of the courts like any other citizen: דנין אותו ומעידין אותו. What it says in Sanhedrin 18a המלך לא דן ולא דנין אותו לא מעיד ולא מעידין אותו, “that a King can neither be a judge, nor can he be brought before a court of Justice, has neither to testify as a witness, nor can witnesses testify against him”, is explained on the next page, viz., 19a as follows: לא שנו אלא מלכי בית ישראל אבל מלכי בית דוד דן ודנין אותן דכתיב בית דוד כה אמר ה׳ דינו לבקר משפם ואי לא דיינין ליה אינהו היכי דייני והכתיב התקוששו וקושו ואמר ריש (Jer. 21,12). לקיש קשוט עצמך ואחר כך קשוט אחרים, this active and passive exemption of Kings from the Courts of Justice and from the duty of giving evidence, was only a later introduction, a regulation necessitated by the intractibility of King Jannai and the Kings of Israel. But that it did not apply to the Kings of Judah, and was by no means in accordance with the original idea of the Law, is apparent from the injunction of Jeremiah to the Kings of the House of David to exercise the office of Judge with justice, and the Scripture says that only one who himself submits to law and justice may judge others. (See הל׳ מלכים :לחם משנה 3,7.)

אשר חטא בה. It is not sufficient to merely become conscious of having unconsciously committed a sin punishable by כרת, but the actual sin itself אשר חטא בה must have become known to the one who did it; not for instance, that you have eaten either חלב or נותר, that pieces of חלב ונותר were there in front of you, ואכל אחד מהן ואינו יודע איזה מהן אכל, you must specifically know that you have eaten חלב or that you have eaten נותר (Kerithoth 19a). On V. 24 we shall have the opportunity of showing how, in general, in what very limited circumstances the Torah orders or allows a חטאת to be brought. This specialised knowledge of the sin which is demanded here is quite in keeping with, and confirms, what we say there, viz., that very definitely it is not sinfulness in general, but a quite definite occurrence which calls for a חטאת יחיד, with the idea of begetting more conscientious care in future towards quite definite actions.

והביא את קרבנו שעיר עזים זכר תמים, “then he has to try and get near to God again, by placing himself in the Sanctuary of the Torah, as a שעיר עזים זכר תמים. We have already noted on Ch. 1,10 that the species צאן, in contrast to בקר, represents the personality, not so much with reference to its useful work, as to its receiving its fate and its guidance in life from the “Shepherd of Israel”; also that in this species the family of עזים, on account of their character of obstinacy and resistance, represent the additional nuance of resistence to all others, and docile obedience to their owner. This character of obstinate resistance to strangers reaches its climax in the male of the species, the שעיר. Here the requirement for a male animal for the חטאת נשיא is not only למצוה but is מעכב as it expressly adds the word זכר (which is already implied by the word שעיר. I.L.) (see ק״א on ת״כ on our verse). Accordingly if the קרבן נשיא consists, not like that of the כהן משיח and the ב״ד הגדול of a פר, but of a שעיר, it is here indicated that the function of the King, and its attendant duty of constantly watching his step, is derived not so much from the kingly office to which he has been charged by the Nation as from the position in the Nation to which he has been appointed by God. He has been raised to the highest position of power to be שעיר “defending, warding off”, “vindicating the rights of” the Nation, “protecting the Nation, and God’s matters in the Nation”. And, as a matter of fact, according to Deut. 17,14, the function of the King was not to lead the Nation in conquering the Land or extending its territory. ירושה and ישיבה were to precede the appointment of a King, and the concentration of the national power in his hand as far as external relations go, can, at most, be for defence, for standing up for the rights of the Land. He is to be a שעיר. But equally for internal relations his function of power is to be in the first place “שעיר״. He is to use his power to protect and defend matters pertaining to God and His Torah, which, after all, form the sum of the National Mission, protect and defend them against infringement, or becoming stunted and spoilt, stand up against any alteration or attack on them. The National Power is through him to be a שעיר. This is also how רש״י (in Sanhedrin 20b) understands the “לשפטנו״ to be a justified demand of the זקנים שבדור at the election of a King (Sam. 1,8) who כהוגן לשפטם ולרדות הסרבנים שבהם — :שאלו. But he who has to stand up to protect matters pertaining to God against others, must in the very first place stand up against himself, and has to beware of slipping down from the קרנות מזבח העולה, from the “moral heights” which form the goal of Jewish upward progress, to beware of moral “carelessness”—which is the literal meaning of שגגה (cf. our remarks in our commentary on Ps. LVIII & LXXII).

ת״כ .שעיר עזים on V. 28 teaches that all שעירי חטאות, including that of the נשיא, must be בני שנה, may only be animals that have not passed beyond their first year. The King, too, must never have grown “old” in his position of power. He is always to keep the “freshness’ and enthusiasm which he had in the first year of becoming King. But there is evidence to show that this law is not expressed by the term שעיר עזים, but is established by other references, so that, accordingly there is no difference regarding the age between שעיר and שעיר עזים (in מל״מ on מ״ק 1,14, this is questioned and left in doubt).

V. 24. ושחט אותו. To the limiting precision of אותו, as well as the similar ושחט אותה of v. 33, the ת״כ attaches the traditional Halacha (Temura 15a & 21 b) that only this animal,—dedicated by the sinner for atonement of his חטא—may be brought as a חטאת, but that ולד חטאת ותמורת חטאת וחטאת שמתו בעליה ושכפרו בעליה, a kid or a lamb born from a חטאת (the חטאת יחיד is a nanny-goat or a female sheep), the exchange-animal of a חטאת whose owner has died, or one whose owner had brought another one during the time that this one had been lost, all these may not be brought either directly or indirectly as an offering, but מתות, must be left to die. In Temura 15a in the Mishna and similarly in ת״כ a fifth category of חטאות המתות is named viz., שעברה שנתה, which accounts for the generally used expression חמש חטאות מתות. But according to Temura 22a, this class is combined with אבודה (as would naturally be the case. How otherwise would it “pass its first birthday”? I.L.) אבודה שעברה שנתה and equally so אבודה שנמצאת בעלת מום. According to Rashi on the Mishna there, this does actually form a fifth category, as even if it had been found again קודם שכפרו בעלים באחרת, it has to be left to die, and so is one of the חטאות המתות. But תוספות there, simply reckons this category under the heading of חטאת שכפרו בעליה and then it is difficult to find the fifth class of חמש חטאות מתות.—This Halacha is definitely characteristic of חטאת. Other offerings תודה ,שלמים ,עולה, completely transmit their own character to animals that derive from them by birth or exchange וולדותיהן ותמורותיהן כיוצא בהן. They are offered up as שלמים ,עולה or תודה in exactly the same way as the animal from which they are derived (Temura 17b & 18b). In the same way עולה ושלמים שמתו בעליהן, after the death of their owners have to be brought by the heirs (Zebachim 5a & Menachoth 92a). Even in the case of an אשם, which, after all is similar to a חטאת regarding the cause on account of which it is brought, although it is not actually offered up itself, does come indirectly to be offered. It has to be allowed to graze until it gets a מום and so is unfit, then it has to be redeemed, and the redemption money goes to the Temple fund (the שופרות), out of which עולות נדבת צבור are brought: כל שבחטאת מתה באשם ירעה עד שיסתאב וימכר ויפלו דמיו לנדבה (Temura 20b). More, according to the opinion of ר״ת (Zebachim 5b & Menachoth 4a) the contrast of אשם to חטאת is even sharper. He says that the whole idea of רעייה is only a תקנת חכמים, and an אשם שכפרו בעליו וגו׳ could מדאורייתא itself be brought as עולת נדבה של צבור and that the wording of the Halacha originally ran:— כל שבחטאת מחה באשם קרב עולה.

This Halacha, which is so significant for חטאת may well be connected with that other equally characteristic law of the חטאת (which the Gemora in Zebachim 7b & 8a explain on the phrases: ולקח הכהן מדם החטאת, ושחט אותה לחטאת V. 33 & 34 et alia) namely that כל הזבחים שנזבחו שלא לשמן כשרים אלא שלא עלו לבעלים לשם חובה, whereas all other offerings that have received some change in their denomination at the עבודת הדם, i.e., at the הולכה ,קבלה ,שחיטה or זריקה, whether it be an alteration in the nature of the offering, שנוי קדש, e.g. עולה לשם שלמים, or in the name of the owners, שנוי בעלים e.g., עולת ראובן לשם עולת שמעון such offerings are כשר in themselves, but the owners are not absolved from bringing the offering to which they were committed; but חטאת שלא לשמה e.g., חטאת לשם עולה or חטאת ראובן לשם חטאת שמעון (perhaps even חטאת חלב לשם חטאת דם Zebachim 7a & 9b, see כ״מ on הלי פ״מ 15,6) is completely פסול. In this respect פסח alone is similar to חטאת and פסח שלא לשמו is also פסול (Zebachim 2a & תוספות there). And again in this respect אשם stands in line with עולה and the other קרבנות, and not with חטאת.

Now, finally, the motive for all these special regulations for the חטאת may be found in that peculiarity which, it seems to us, marks the whole basic nature of this offering. We refer to the fact that amongst all the offerings חטאת is the single one which may only be brought as an obligation from some definite and specific cause (in the case of the חטאת המוספים, the cause lies in the special implication of the particular day). It can only be brought as an obligation, as a חובה and never, even indirectly or remotely as a נדבה (see above אשר חטא בה v. 23). All the other forms of offerings: מנחה ,תודה ,שלמים ,עולה, can be brought as a free-will offering, for a feeling of general urge for such an offering. Even אשם, in the case of תלוי can, at any rate, be brought from a doubtful indefinite cause. More, in Chulin 41b, according to the opinion of ר׳ אלעזר, which is accepted by the Mishna, and which the Tur Orach-Chaim, Ch. 1 & Youre-Dea 5, follows, (in opposition to the מתנדב אדם ,(2,18 הל׳ שחיטה & 14,8 מ״ק רמב״ם אשם תלוי בכל יום so that the אשם form of offering would belong to דבר הנידר והנידב.

According to this, the assumption seems very probable that it is because חטאת can not occur as a נדבה that the “intermediate” condition, that it is כשר and still not עולה לחובה can not exist. As far as we know this intermediate condition is only referred to in connection with חטאת in the one single case (Zebachim 46b) of חטאת ששחטה לשם חולין and the explanation for this must be sought (see notes on Ch. 22,15). But רמב״ם (פ״מ 15,8 & 9) also reckons it for the case of שחטה על מי שמחוייב עולה and also for שחטה על מת, but nevertheless for these two cases the Gemora (Zebachim 7a) simply says כשרה, and according to the whole trend of the discussion there, it is difficult to take it as כשר ואינו מרצה. For the question made there (on 5a) regarding this intermediate stage: — אם אין מרצין למה באין is quite definitely answered by reference to מוצא שפתיך תשמר (Deut. 23,24), that an offering which does not suffice לחובה should be considered as נדבה, and on the other hand, עולות לאחר מיתה come also to be brought, so that they are כשרין ואין מרצין. But both these cases do not occur with a חטאת which can neither be brought בנדבה nor אחר מיתת בעליה to which the צאן קדשים already refers on Zebachim 5 a.

Quite in the same way the חמש חטאות המתות can be in deep intimate connection with this basic peculiarity of the חטאת, and may be understood as the consequence of the fact that a חטאת can only be brought in connection with, and as a result of, some definite cause. For all these five cases can all be regarded in the light of the idea, namely that an animal which bears the חטאת-character without being related as such to a quite definite existing cause, not only itself, but even indirectly through a deputy, may not be allowed to become an offering. תמורת חטאת and ולד חטאת have received their חטאת-character by reason of birth or exchange, but for them at no time was there any special motive for obtaining atonement by their being brought as an offering. In the cases of חטאת שמתו בעליה and שכפרו בעליה באחרת, the moment when there was such a motive has already passed away and become lost by the death of the person requiring atonement, or by atonement having been already attained by means of another animal. They are all חטאות for which no special חטא is there to be atoned for.

But the lesson to be brought home by this fundamental speciality of the חטאת must be such an important one that even when the חטאת-character of the animal is in itself quite undiminished, but only by external conditions the relationship has become lost, or it has never had such relationship, it may not, even then, be brought to the Altar, not even by indirect means. All other offerings in such cases—and חטאת too, if it had become unfit to be offered through receiving a מום, or if it had never definitely been a חטאת, in the case where the owner had taken the precaution of setting aside two animals for his one חטאת in case the one should escape or become unfit, מותרות חטאת—are left to graze until they get a מום, are then sold, and with the redemption money another animal is bought which offered as עולת קיץ המזבח) נדבת צבור), so that they do reach the Altar by indirect means. But a complete and fit חטאת which has lost the relationship to the sinner has to be left to die, and may not reach the Altar even through such an indirect change to an עולה; not even when פסול מום has been added to אבודה (see תוספות Temura 21b). But the easier transformation of all other offerings into עולות may also be contributed to by the fact that regarding that procedure which is based on the very nature of the offering viz., the עבודת הדם, they all belong to the same category as the עולה, they are all בזריקה למטה, and חטאת alone by נתינה למעלה stands in characteristic isolation.

If now we consider that עולה is that form of offering into which all other offerings, with the exception of the sharply differentiated חטאת, can be transformed, also that it is that form of offering which, amongst all the others is most accessible to נדבה, as it is the only one that can be brought by the צבור as נדבה, then the normal basic form of all offerings appears to be the עולה, and in contrast to it, as the purely exceptional form, the יחיד .חטאת and צבור can bring עולות every minute of the day; all offerings which otherwise can not be brought, are indirectly changed into עולות; the offering-altar is also generally called מזבח העולה; the continuous offering, daily, morning and evening, the תמיֹד, is an עולה; the underlying thought, the idea which the עולה expresses must accordingly be one that can fill, that should fill, the breast of the individual as well as the Community with every breath that it takes. This thought must express the purest, most natural result of our relation to God, on which the whole practical application of this relationship rests. On the other hand, the underlying thought, the idea which the חטאת expresses would be one that should only, that may only, fill our breasts, in exceptional moments, and one which must find its justification in special causes.

If we consider, as has already been remarked on Ch. 1,2 et seq., that עולה מכפר על עשה ועל הרהודי הלב that עולה is the expression of the idea of positive progress towards greater moral perfection, as well as the filling of the mind with pure good moral thoughts, by which alone—as the mind is never at rest—no room is left for useless evil thoughts to arise, then here we have given, as the fundamental thought which directly results from our relation to God: - the duty of unceasing efforts for mental and active progress towards spiritual and moral perfection. The consciousness of our imperfection regarding the never completely achieved spiritual-moral ideal of Life, the consciousness of the eternal necessity for progress, and of the ability to make progress, and of the constant energy which must be used for progress, as is expressed in the עולה-offering can, may, and must fill our minds unceasingly; in the spiritual-moral realm, making progress, alone can be called living.

But חטאת is brought from the consciousness of having fallen, and the lesson it preaches is, accordingly, to stand fast and firm, not to slip down again from the moral height already attained, Neither of these form the atmosphere in which Jewish life flourishes. Indeed the latter, remaining still on the moral height already attained, as the נתינה על קרנות המזבח drives home as a counter-measure for one who has fallen through carelessness, would mean, without such reference to a lapse which had occured, just the death of all spiritual life. For, if in the moral-sphere, progress is life, then standing still there, is death. When it refers to some special sin or to a special fall, the directing finger of the priest onto the heights of the Altar has only the meaning of a relatively high stage in comparison with what had happened. But in general, without such reference, the heights of the Altar represent the absolute height of the moral Ideal. Not to have to sink from that, would imply that that Ideal had already been reached. But even the slightest hint of the thought of already standing at the absolute height of the moral Ideal would be the grave of all moral perfection.

We understand why it is עולה and not חטאת that forms the key-note of the thoughts that underline our offerings; why the תמיד is not a חטאת but an עולה; why it is the עולה and not the חטאת to which all other offerings join in the form of their most essential procedure, the עבודות הדם, so that they can really all be considered as modified עולות, inasmuch as אכילת כהנים ואכילת בעלים only complement אכילת מזבח and carry the same idea further, and כהנים משלחן גבוה קזכו, and finally, why it is only עולות that can come without any conditions בין ביחיד בין בצבור as נדבה on the Altar of the Jewish Sanctuary of God. It is not a permanent consciousness of חטאת, not a permanent feeling of being a sinner, not a state of permanent penitent contrition that is the mood in which Jewish hearts are to beat, Jewish breasts to breathe up to God, and Jewish minds to find their enthusiastic soaring upwards to God, in God-serving, world-building deeds. ,עולה ,עולה עולה: Upwards, upwards, upwards! Up to the radiant proximity of God, and ever higher and higher! That is the call that unceasingly comes to His sons and daughters out of the Sanctuary of God. This call of the Living God of the Jewish Sanctuary is the loudest and most definite protest against all the heathen theories of mortification and contrition, and teachings of pious self-deprecation as sinners, into which the Temple of offerings of the Living God of eternal life is converted and buried in thoughtless blasphemy. Not for nought—as we have already remarked on V. 10 and which we shall repeatedly meet in verses 26, 31 & 35—is the הקטרת אימורים at the חטאת always expressly referred to the similar procedure at the זבח שלמים. The חטאת idea is only a passing abnormal pathological condition. Once the עבודת הדם has been completed, the חלב וכליות belong in a cheerful שלמים mood to the endeavour towards ריח ניחוח לה׳ without any disturbing element.

Further, we think we can understand the care which the Divine Torah takes to keep every חטאת away from its altar, and if there is no relation, or no longer any relation, to an existing cause, will not allow them to be brought even indirectly by round-about changes. As we have already remarked, a חטאת without such a cause would allow, either the חטה-condition, “our sinfulness”, to be considered as the normal condition of a human being, or, which would be equally pernicious, it would express the idea of the stage of ideal perfection having been reached. Such “spiritual arrogance” would be equally the grave of all moral perfection as that permanent pious complacency brought about by the “I am a sinful sinner” feeling. Both lead to moral death. The one because it believes no further progress is required, the other because it believes it has no ability for progress. For חטאת שמתו בעליה, ושכפרו בעליה באחרת, altogether for a חטאת without a חטא the Jewish Altar has no use, it assigns it to מיתה.

One peculiarity, which we think we can understand, still remains, namely that the Law of the חטאות מתות does not apply to חטאות צבור. In any case ולד חטאת and חטאת שמתו בעליה and תמורת חטאת do not come into question, as חטאת צבור always has to be a חמורה .זכר is not effective for a צבור, and a community as such never dies אין צבור מת. But חטאת שכפרו בעליה באחרת e.g., פר ושעיר של יום הכפורים שאבדו והפרישו אחרים תחתיהן should really themselves be brought as עולה for קיץ המזבח but, because of גזרה לאחר כפרה אטו לפני כפרה, the Rabbonim introduced רעיה (Temura 15, 16 & Shebuoth 12a). Can we perhaps take it that erroneous conception of the human relation to its moral calling which it is feared might result from חטאת without חטא would only be encouraged by cases where the חטאת refers to a definite person, but that this fear falls away in the case of the צבור? Both extremes, spiritual arrogance, and the giving oneself up to the feeling of being a confirmed sinner are essentially individual, personal feelings. The Community, as such, is made up of persons of every shade and degree of goodness and a חטא can always be presupposed for every חטאת of a צבור. A חטאת צבור can never be considered to such an extent without reference to some sin or some sinner that it has to be consigned to מיתה, and that the Altar can not accept it at least as an עולה.
במקום אשר ישחט את העולה i.e.,בצפון. See notes on Ch. 1,5 and 11.

חטאת הוא: The הוא is taken: פרט ששחטו שלא לשמו and שיהיו :חטאת כל מעשיו לשם חטאת. This is the verse where the fundamental principle is laid down — which has already been expounded — that a חטאת שנזבח שלא לשמו פסול.

V. 25. ולקח הכהן מדם החטאת וגו׳. In conformity with what has already been developed on the preceding verse, the whole of the blood of the חטאת does not come on the קרנות of the Altar as the blood of the עולה does, (it says מדם here I.L.). It is only a partial and only a relatively high moral stage on which the חטאת is to direct one to stand fast. Standing firm and fast on a moral stage already reached is also something which is to be done, but in itself has but negative importance. It is really only a result of the positive progress made by the active energy of the moral nature of the human being, which is to find its outlet in exerting every fibre of its being in constant progress, striving forward and upward. But all such progress become illusory if the general outlook of life is not sufficiently serious to avoid all carelessness in moral matters, and to realise the value of the stage reached, and the consequent necessity for keeping up to it. The חטאת itself rests on the basis of the עולה. Hence ולקח הכהן מדם החטאת באצבעו ונתן על קרנת מזבח העולה ואת דמו ישפך אל יסוד מזבח העולה.

On Ch. 1,5, we have explained the procedure of the “Ritual of the Blood” of the חטאת and of the שפיכת שירים in connection with the זריקת הדם of the עולה, and to that we would refer. Here, we would only remark that whereas the עולה summarises the four sides of the Altar into the two diagonal opposite corners — שתים שהם ארבע, — the מתנות of the חטאת have to be done separately on each of the four corners: ארבע מתנות על ארבע קרנות (Zebachim 52b). The finger of the priest directs the one who has fallen through carelessness, through שגגה, to each of the four sides which together build up Jewish Life; the spirit of the Torah penetrating into the life of the People (S.E.); the material life of the people to be developed from such a national life (E.N.); the Law, the Torah, to be carried out by means of such a material life (N.W.) and the minds and intellectual spiritual life to be fed and enlightened by the Torah and in the spirit of the Torah (W.S.). It points to each separately as a moral height, which, if properly valued, must save it from careless treatment. If our way of taking the meaning of the four sides of the Altar is not erroneous, they appear in a surprisingly striking manner as identical with the fundamental idea of the four פרשיות, which, in the תפלין too, are given as the basis of the Jewish Life of thought (של ראש I.L.) and activity (של יד I.L.). There too, they are presented for us to take to heart, in two ways, taken together in the של יד and although on one base, separately in the קדש .של ראש — the People of the Law, the Nation corresponding to the E.; והיה כי יביאך — the material well-being, corresponding to the N.; שמע — the Torah, the W.; והיה אם שמוע — “learning”, studying, understanding the Torah, ת״ת corresponding to the S. Moreover, from the start on the ramp on the south, going round the Altar to the right in the prescribed way to the S.E. corner, the E.N.W.S. sides give the arrangement of the פרשיות in the Tephillin of the universally used תפלין של רש״י.
The שתי מתנות of the עולה and the ארבע מתנות of the חטאת, however, are only למצוה, the כפרה is completed with one כל הניתנין על :מתנה מזבח החיצון שנתן במתנה אחת כיפר. (Zebachim 36b, see on V. 18).
V. 26. ואת כל חלבו וגו׳ (see on V. 9)

וכפר עליו הכהן וגו׳, literally, the priest covers over his sin for him, and it is forgiven unto him.
