That is to say: without the duty of taking more care in future to keep himself up on the high level of the Torah being brought home to him by the מתנות על קרנות המזבח, the fault which he has committed will have the effect of bringing his inner life into ever increasing carelessness, and then, to bring him back to the seriousness of his duty would necessiate punishment by the educating Fatherly Hand of God. By the כפרה which the priest accomplishes both are avoided. His future is not endangered by his past, and so he is forgiven — סלח, related to שלח and צלח, an unhindered progress in life is granted to him.

V. 27—35. These verses deal with the חטאת יחיד the חטאת offering of the ordinary people of the Nation, נפש אחת מעם הארץ. This, in every point, is exactly similar to that of the חטאת נשיא. It is characteristic to the highest degree, that, herewith, regarding the responsibility for carrying out the moral laws of the Torah, the King stands on exactly the same footing before God, as the humblest of his subjects. The only difference between them consists in the animal which is to represent the personality of the person who is attempting to get nearer to God by means of an offering. The King has to appear, as we have seen, as a שעיר, the male of the goat species, and from this we have deduced the nature of the position he is to occupy in the Nation. The personality of the ordinary people has to be represented by a female animal either from the goats or from the sheep. The femininity of the animal expresses the subordinate nature of their civic position in relation to the masculine dominant representation of the King. But the choice is left free between a שעירה and a כבשה according to whether the bringer feels that he wishes to express the independence of his position in social life, or whether he feels he wishes to express himself simply and purely as כבשה, as a creature in God’s flock who requires guidance. In any case the three פרשיות of the חטאת יחיד teach that the different status of social life makes no difference to the moral demands which the Torah makes on us, nor to the moral value in which human beings are estimated, nor to the proximity to God which is to be gained and granted. The שעיר of the King, the שעירה of the highest leading citizens and the כבשה of the lowest peasant all have to submit themselves in שחיטה to the same sharp knife of the moral dictates of the Law. The King, like the beggar, the beggar like the King, has, in סמיכה, to acknowledge his responsibility for the Torah being kept in Israel as a nation. The דם השעיר of the King, the דם השעירה of the proud leading citizens, or the דם הכבשה of the homely man in the street, have alike to receive the same direction from the finger of the priest to seriously keep in mind the duty of keeping oneself up on the heights of the moral laws. Hie blood of all of them is to find its roots in the one and same basis of building up its Jewish life out of the elevating spirit of the Torah (יסוד דרומי); after they have achieved atonement, the חלב וכליות of all of them, all their goals and efforts are brought into the happy sphere of those whose existence and desires nourish and keep alive God’s satisfaction with this world; and it is significant that the חטאת כבשה concludes with the addition of the words על אשי ה׳: the desires and efforts of the lowest man in the nation — if they are kept morally — find their equally valued place on the Altar of God along with all the other achievements of the nation which have been accomplished towards godliness on earth.

In the construction of V. 27 more of the laws which complete the Law of the חטאת are indicated. By the repeated stress which is laid on a single individual being the bearer of the sin which comes to be atoned for by a בעשתה ,אחת ,נפש :חטאת, the Law is given (Sabbath 93b) that the sin which necessitates the bringing of a חטאת must have been committed completely by one single person. For instance, the מלאכת הוצאה on שבת consists of two factors; עקירה, the taking of an object out of one רשות, and הנחה the depositing of it in another. Now, if one person did the עקירה and another the הנחה, i.e., זה עוקר וזה מניח, neither of them has to bring a חטאת. In the same way if two people together did an act which each one of them could have done alone זה יכול וזה יכול e.g., they held a pen together and wrote in that way, they would not have to bring the offering. But if they did something together which neither could have accomplished alone, זה אינו יכול וזה אינו יכול e.g., they carried out a heavy beam between them into the רשות הרבים which neither could have managed alone, then both have to bring a חטאת. If one of them could have done it alone, but not the other, זה יכול וזה אינו יכול, then the strong one has to bring a חטאת and the unnecessary assistance which the other rendered is not considered as anything, under the rule that מסייע אין בו ממש. But this general rule of מסייע אין בו ממש which has other possible applications, requires more exact definition and limitation (see ט״ז on א״ח 328,1; 198,21; the י״ד 198,21 and נקה״כ there).

Further, as above, Ch. I. v. 2, the limiting expression מכם excluded a מומר, a Jew who had become estranged from the Torah, from bringing an עולה, so here, by the term מעם הארץ the same exclusion is made: פרט למומר (Chulin 9b). Even in the case of חטאת, which, after all, one is commanded to bring, it is a חובה, no one may approach God, who, in general, or at any rate regarding the act he had committed, does not stand on the basis of the Jewish Law. He must have been, as a somewhat subtle wording of this principle runs, שב מידיעתו, or as it puts it in יושב מידיעתו ,ת״כ i.e., his condition must be such, that, had he been conscious of the illegality of his action when he committed it, he would not have done it. It is not sufficient that he did it בשגגה, it must also have been done only because of שגגה. In general the Law differentiates between מומר לכל התורה כולה to which class מומר לע״ז and מומר לחלל שבת בפרהסיה also belong; between מומר לדבר מומר לאותו דבר ;אחד; further between מומר לתיאבון and מומר להכעיס, as well as the in-between case of שלא לתיאבון ושלא להכעיס. The case of a מומר להכעיס לדבר אחד, one who, on principle, holds even one single Law of the Torah in contempt, is considered equal to one who has fallen from the whole of the Torah (Chulin 5b; Y.D.24,7). Regarding the permission for bringing an offering it is the condition at the moment when the action was committed, which is decisive. He who was a מומר לכל התורה or a מומר לאותו דבר at the moment of the שגגה, even if afterwards he was חוזר בתשובה is not allowed to bring a חטאת for that particular action. Although it was done בשגגה it was not done simply because of שגגה (see תוספות Chulin 5b אינו שב and מל״מ on הל׳ שגגות 3,7.). That the bringer may not still be a מומר when he brings the offering, that, especially with regards to the action he has done, he must be filled with true repentance, and with the resolve to avoid any repetition of his act, is, of course, already understood from the general fundamental verse זבח רשעים תועבה. Here the further law is added that, in the moment when the sin was committed, too, no general מומר-feeling, or even if only specially directed to that particular action, no מומר-feeling may have been present if a חטאת referring to it is to be allowed to approach the Altar of God. (ibid).

V. 31. ואת כל חלבה יסיר וגו׳ and again in V. 35. In the case of the פר כהן המשיח (v. 8) and in that of the פר העלם דבר it uses the term ירים. Perhaps, because in the case of the פרים הנשרפין it is only the חלבים which reach their true destination in אכילת מזבח, but all the rest is נשרף חוץ למחנה so that in comparison to the rest of the offering, the taking out of the חלבים which do reach their true destination can be considered a הרמה.

V. 1. The חטאות dealt with in the previous chapter were all such that, had the act been done consciously and intentionally, במזיד, the punishment incurred would be כרת, in accordance with the general rule, that only כל שחייבין על זדונו כרת חייבין על שגגתו חטאת. All these חטאות were “fixed”, חטאת קבועה, without any adjustment to meet the pecuniary circumstances of the person who was under the obligation to bring a חטאת. If his circumstances were such that he could not afford to bring a שעירה or a כבשה, the obligation to fulfil this duty had to stand over until his circumstances improved.

Now in this chapter V. 1—13, three laws are picked out from all the others, — two of which do not belong to the class that incur כרת, — and for them a special category is established: קרבן עולה ויורד, “a rising and falling offering”, i.e., one that varies according to the means of the person who has to bring the offering. The three transgressions referring to which this special category is formed are:- שבועת עדות also called שמיעת קול (v. 1); טומאת מקדש וקדשיו (v. 2 and 3); שבועת בטוי also called בטוי שפתים (v. 4). For all three בעשירות, where means permitted a שעירה או כבשה לחטאת is brought; בדלות, in straightened circumstances שתי תורים או בני יונה, אחד לחטאת ואחד לעולה, and בדלי דלות in extreme proverty עשירית איפה סלת חטאת. Of these three the שבועת העדות has the distinctive feature that מביא על הזדון כשגגה, that the offering has to be brought even if the transgression had been done as a complete מזיד, whereas all other חטאות can only be brought for transgressions done בשגגה.
Let us first make ourselves conversant with the wording of the text and the most essential laws, and then try to get an insight into the motives which underlie these laws.

ושמעה אלה .ושמעה קול אלה would mean: he hears an oath; ושמעה קול אלה he hears the demand for an oath; satisfying such a demand would read ושמעה לקול אלה. The construction שמע קול meaning hearing the demand or request is quite common e.g., שמע ה׳ קול יהודה (Deut. 33,7), וישמע ה׳ את קול דבריכם (ibid I,34), שמע ה׳ קול בכיי (Ps. 6,9) etc. etc. In the קול אלה here, the circumstances are depicted that a demand or request that he should take an oath is directed to him (on אלה as an oath, see note on Ex. 20,7).

עד .והוא עד from עוד, basic meaning: lasting, hence we get עוד, still, yet, עודד giving duration, permanence, העד to give permanence to, to establish, something which otherwise would die away from the consciousness and conviction of people. This is what the עד, the witness, effects. An עד, a witness, is one who observes an occurence which disappears in the passing moment, puts it in his mind, keeps it there (gives it עוד), so that, long after it has ceased actually to exist, he can reproduce it in words by הגדה and so, by מעיד, establish it and give it durableness.

או ראה או ידע is in parenthesis, and gives the ways and means by which somebody can become a witness. He has either seen the transaction with his own eyes ראה e.g., he saw A giving B a sum of money without knowing anything of the nature of the transaction, whether it was given as a loan, or as payment, or for safe-keeping etc. This would be a ראיה without ידיעה, which testimony can be relevant if, for instance B denies altogether that he had received any money from A. Or, he heard with his own ears an admission from B that he owed A a sum of money, so that he can give authentic testimony that a legal claim had existed, although he had not been present at the transaction. This would be ידיעה without ראיה. In Shevuoth 33b and 34a it is pointed out that this proves that this Law can only be applied to witnesses in cases in civil law, דיני ממונות, as in criminal cases דיני נפשות, no circumstantial evidence, which ידיעה בלא ראיה is, is allowed to be admitted. More, even ראיה without ידיעה would not suffice, as, in criminal cases the witnesses have to be in a position where they are able to substantiate the circumstances which render the deed punishable.

אם לא יגיד ונשא עונו, this sentence does not follow on שמעה קול אלה, that only not responding to the demand to give evidence is a sin, but it is a further explanatory sentence qualifying והוא עד, he must be such a witness that the witholding of his evidence would load him with a sin, his behaviour would be an עון, an injustice. From that can be learnt, firstly, that also without שמיעת קול אלה, without receiving a demand for it, to give any evidence you know, is a positive duty. Even where there are not the two witnesses necessary to establish the case — and it is only of such cases which require two witnesses that the Torah speaks of here, (Baba Kama 56a) — but only the one, so that the utmost he could achieve by his testimony would be to force the parties to take an oath, it still says of him (ibid 55b) היודע עדות לחברו ואינו מעיד לו פטור מדיני אדם וחייב בדיני שמים, he who knows of some evidence that he could give, and does not give it, can, of course, not be punished for witholding it, in human courts, but is subject to the punishment of God: (see תוספות ibid 56a). Similarly in Pesachim 113b: שלשה הקב״ה שונאן, המדבר אחד בפה ואחד בלב, והיודע עדות לחבירו ואינו מעיד לו, והרואה דבר ערוה בחברו ומעיד בו יחידי. There are three who are hated by God, he who says one thing with his lips but another in his heart, he who knows of some evidence which he could give and witholds it, and he who gives evidence as a single witness in a case in the criminal courts, as, as is explained there, in the last case, the evidence is completely without any effect whatsoever and comes under the idea of מוציא שם רע. Further we can learn that the duty to come forward and give evidence is only then incurred, and witholding it only then is considered a sin, when, both with regards to his personality, and to the manner in which he obtained his evidence, his testimony is a valid one אם לא יגיד ונשא עונו, בראויין להגדה הכתוב מדבר, the text speaks only of such witnesses whose testimony can legally have some effect, but not קרוב או פסול, not of such who, on account of relationship or for other personal reasons, are invalid as witnesses, also not if their evidence rests, not on their own observation, but only on what they have heard from others, i.e., עד מפי עד (Shebuoth 35a).

In the case which is dealt with here, to this ordinary duty of having to give evidence, is added the special case where the demand to bear witness is made in the form of an oath: משביע אני עליכם אם לא תבאו ותעידוני וכו׳. Even if such a demand by oath was not answered by אמן (saying אמן to an oath taken by somebody else is equivalent to taking it yourself I.L.) and even if it was made outside the courts, מושבע מפי אחרים, and then when brought into court, the witness declares he has no evidence to give אין אנו יודעים לך עדות he still comes under our case here of coming under the heading of שמיעת קול. (But according to רמב״ם הל׳ שבועות 9,1, only if the demand on oath had been made in court, otherwise only if he answered אמן to the oath. See כ״מ and ל״מ there). Needless to say, then, that it would be the case if the one from whom it is demanded to give witness himself swears on oath that he knows nothing about it שבועה שאין אנו יודעים לך עדות, or if he answers אמן to the demand משביע אני עליכם as כל העונה אמן אחר שבועה כמוציא שבועה בפיו דמי (Shebuoth 29b).

But the duty which entails the bringing of an offering laid down here only arises when the demand is made personally by the interested party himself, which is the reason given in Shebuoth 35a for the spelling of לא in the phrase אם לוא יגיד as לוא, to imply אם לו לא יגיד. Further, an offering has only to be brought in such cases where — similarly to the law regarding שבועת פקדון (V. 21 and 22) — the witholding of the evidence for the one who was justified in demanding it entails a direct loss of money, i.e., when, if the evidence had been given, the party against whom it would have been directed would have had to make a payment (ibid 34a). Hence also, as already mentioned, a single witness who witholds his evidence after the requisite demand, would not have to bring the offering, although, by his evidence, the defendant would be obliged to swear on oath in court, and thereby perhaps would have been brought to admit liability, so that, indirectly, the “one-man” evidence has had, or would have had, the effect of causing money to be paid, nevertheless the general rule is adhered to that דבר הגורם לממון לאו כממון דמי i.e., something that only indirectly causes money to be paid, here the oath of the defendant brought about by the evidence demanded by the plaintiff, is in such and similar cases not to be considered as itself directly causing money or loss of money to be brought about (Shebuoth 32a). The obligation to bring this offering only falls in cases which refer to such objects which in general are the subject of oaths imposed by the court, but not to עבדים שטרות וקרקעות so that משביע עדי קרקע פטור (ibid 37b, see notes on Ex. 22,8).

V. 2. בנבלת חיה טמאה וגו׳. From the בנבלת שרץ טמא which follows, it is evident that the טמאה of the חיה and בהמה here does not refer to their relation to the dietary laws, as there is no שרץ which is טהור as food. But here the idea of טומאה is to be understood to refer to טומאת מגע, to the ability to make things טמא by touch. It would then only refer to the eight שרצים mentioned in Ch. 11,29, החלד והעכבר etc., which in this respect are טמאים. And then in any case the addition of the word טמאה to נבלת חיה ובהמה would be superfluous as the נבלה of every חיה and בהמה is טמא to the touch. But this addition, as well as the phrase בהמה טמאה which would have been included in חיה as בהמה בכלל חיה, is specially stressed to teach us, with an eye to Ch. 7,21, that it is dealing here with טמאה in relation to מקדש וקדשיו, to entering the Sanctuary or eating its sacred food, (excluding קדשי גבול such as תרומה). See Shebuoth 7a לרבנן דפליגי אדרבי יוסי הגלילי and Rashi thereon.

ונעלם ממנו. In Shebuoth 14b this particular specification has special attention drawn to it as a characteristic peculiarity, that here the obligation to bring a חטאת only occurs if the error was preceded by a consciousness ידיעה בתחלה. He must have known that he had become טמא and that this was the מקדש or this food ונעלם ממנו ;קדשים, but when he entered the מקדש or ate the קדשים, his טומאה condition or the קדושה of the place or object slipped his memory. This, the Gemora terms ידיעות קמייתא דליתנהי בכל התורה כולה. At all other שגגות which make a חטאת obligatory (Ch. IV), e.g., חטאת חלב, it is only necessary that he gets to know of that which caused his error after he has committed it, ידיעה בסוף, even if he had never, known that this was a piece of חלב, and similarly, with all other שגגות. Shebuoth 5a finds this preceding יתיעה which is necessary to make a קרבן עולה ויורד obligatory for טומאת מקדש וקדשיו expressed in the word :ונעלם ונעלם מכלל שידע. But the demand that he must have known of the actual law of טומאה itself, is there taken to be satisfied by ידיעת בית רבו, by the assumption that every Jewish boy has been taught the laws of the Torah whilst still at school, and the necessity יתיעה בתחלה, as far as that goes, is regarded as fulfilled, so that even if this knowledge of his youth had already entirely disappeared it would make no difference.

(In parenthesis we venture to remark that this knowledge obtained by having been taught in youth is taken in the Gemora as being able to be assumed also in the female sex. The laws of this offering apply equally to men and women, and there in the Gemora, the one and only case which could be found in reply to the question מי איכא דלית ביה ידיעת בית רבו “is there then any person in Israel who has not been taught Torah in his youth?” is the exetremely rare case of תינוק שנשבה לבין הנכרים, a child who has been captured and brought up amongst heathens, and so has grown up knowing nothing of Judaism). תוספות, however, in opposition to Rashi, takes this ידיעת בית רבו as if, it, by itself, constitutes the only previous knowledge necessary to satisfy the demand for a ידיעה בתחלה, and that it is not necessary even to have known that you have come into contact with something that has made you טומאה. But if one takes it this way, then the most characteristic difference between our case and all other שגגות falls away (the difference mentioned above, where the Gemora says that the “ידיעה קמייתא״ does not exist in any other case. I.L.) as, with שגגת חלב or any other שגגה there is ידיעת בית רבו. The difference would then only exist in the exceptional case of תינוק שנשבה, and even that would fall away, if, as according to one view in Sabbath 68b it does, תינוק שנשבה comes under the category of אונס. Hence we adopted above the way in which Rashi takes it. (See Shebuoth 5a and 15b ד״ה או דלמא and תוספות there and on 19b. Compare תוספות י״ט on Mishna 2,1 and ל״מ on שגגות Ch. 11,1.)
והוא טמא ואשם, he is טמא, and as such has transgressed, inasmuch as he had either entered the מקדש or had eaten קדשים, both of which are punishable by כרת.

V. 3. טמאת אדם, the טומאה which exists through the dead body of a human being, either the מת itself, or טמא מת one who has touched such a body, who has the character of אב הטומאה, from which the body itself is called לכל טומאתו וגו׳ .אבי אבות הטומאה, such טומאות which exist through certain conditions of living human beings, as .זבים זבות נדות ויולדות בה is לרבות נבלת עוף טהור, which does not make טמא by being touched but only בבית הבליעה, by being swallowed (ת״כ and Shebuoth 7b). On Ch. XI we shall have to point out that the טומאה of מאכלות אסורות is as a rule expressed by טמא ב- while טומאת מגע is expressed by טמא ל-. This would be quite in accordance with טמא בה being used here to indicate a טומאה which is only incurred by אכילה.

But אשר יטמא בה is necessary for explaining which kind of טומאה the verse is speaking about. אדם וכלים are only טמאים through an אב הטומאה. Hence both sentences, 2 as well as 3, speak only of cases where someone has come into contact with such a טומאה by which he becomes טמא, as it expressly says יטמא בה. So that only in cases, where he has touched an אב הטומאה and so had become טמא and then, forgetting the מקדש-character of the place, or the קדש nature of the food, has entered the Mikdosh or eaten the קדשים. These cases are called, in the Mishna, Shebuoth 2a and 14a ידיעות הטומאה שתים שהם ארבע. They are called ידיעות because the ידיעות בתחלה are their most characteristic feature. Two ידיעות of which the text there speaks: ידיעת הטומאה which has slipped the memory in connection with מקדש, or relating to קדשים. The view of ר׳ ישמעאל — which is the one which is accepted as Halacha — puts two other cases besides these, where it is not the טומאה-condition which has slipped the memory, but the מקדש character of the place or the קדשים nature of the food העלם טומאה וזכור את המקדש או את הקדש and העלם מקדש או קדש וזכור את הטומאה.
והוא ידע, (according to Shebuoth 4b) is the ידיעה בסוף, the remembering, the becoming conscious, of the error that has been committed.

V. 4. בטא .לבטא only occurs here and Numbers 30,8 and 9 referring to vows and oaths, and elsewhere in Prov. 12,18 בוטה כמדקרות חרב and Ps. 106,33 ויבטא בשפתיו. If we consider that in both these latter cases, it very definitely speaks of utterances that would have been far better not made, and that vows too, belong to the class of utterances that, as a rule, are not approved of, then we can take it that this particular word is employed here to indicate that here too we are dealing with utterances which, in themselves, are not to be approved of. This is confirmed by the more detailed provisions of this law, which, as already remarked, deals with promissory vows which, as a rule, are not approved of, or of assertive oaths which are actually untrue. The addition of the word בשפתים teaches (Shebuoth 26b) that for promissory vows of which the text speaks, that גמד בלבו צריך שיוציא בשפתיו, that, making a vow in your mind is not binding until and unless you actually utter it with your lips. Only תרומה and קדשים of which the text says כל נדיב לבו (Ex. 35,5) and כל נדיב לב עולות (Chron. 29,31), form exceptions to this rule (and also צדקה, deciding in your mind, to give certain charities I.L.).

להרע ולהטיב is not to be taken as referring to Laws. An oath swearing to do, or abstain from doing, anything which is against the Law is, in itself, invalid, and comes under the heading of שבועת שדא (see on Ex. 20,7). Vows to do something physically impossible or morally impossible are equally of no meaning. להרע ולהטיב has only personal, individual meaning, personally to do something or to abstain from doing it. The construction of the sentence או נפש כי תשבע לבטא בשפתים להרע או להטיב לכל אשר יבטא האדם בשבועה is explained in Shebuoth 25 and 26a, according to the hermeneutical rule of ריבה מיעט וריבה. The first part of the sentence או נפש וגוי being comprehensive, would include any and every kind of oath, assertive or promissory, and similarly the last phrase of the sentence לכל אשר יבטא וגו׳ is most comprehensive again. This brings the middle phrase להרע ולהטיב out of what would otherwise be its completely limiting and specialising the sphere of the oath, and gives it a merely limiting effect as an example. By the generalising implication of the preceding and final phrases of the sentence the obligation to bring a קרבן remains applicable for שבועת בטוי to an assertive oath (לשעבר e.g., לא נתתי and in fact נתתי לא אכלתי and אכלתי) as well as to promissory ones (להבא e.g., לא אתן and לא אוכל ;אתן and אוכל), and moreover not only to oaths which have some actual positive or negative material effect, שיש בו הרעה והטבה but also to cases which make absolutely no material difference at all, such as לא אזרוק אזרוק צרור לים ,צרור לים or זרקתי ,לא זרקתי. But taking the middle phrase להרע ולהטיב as an example does exclude דבר מצוה, everything that one is commanded by the Torah to do, or forbidden to do, and similarly also anything which is physically impossible, altogether everything that comes under the heading of שבועת שוא (This is all according to the teaching of רב, according to שמואל, the scope of the matters dealt with here is still more limited and Hirsch goes more deeply into the underlying principles which cause their difference of opinion I.L.).

לכל אשר יבטא האדם בשבועה ונעלם ממנו, Shebuoth 26a, on this verse says: תנו רבנן :האדם בשבועה פרט לאנוס, ונעלם פרט למזיד, ממנו, שנתעלמה ממנו שבועה, יכול שנתעלמה ממנו חפץ תלמוד לומר בשבועה ונעלם, על העלם שבועה הוא חייב ואינו חייב על העלם חפץ. As the subject of the sentence, the one who takes the oath, is specially mentioned and is called האדם, it is taken that, at the moment of taking the oath he is a full אדם, in complete intelligent control of his actions. At promissory oaths or vows he must be conscious of the forbidden nature of broken vows, and at assertive ones he must also have been fully aware of the falsity of his statement, if the consequences as depicted here, of not fulfilling his word, or of having made the false statement, are to be imposed on him. That an assertive oath, at which the one who makes it honestly believes his statement to be true, even if afterwards it is proved to be false, is far removed from any idea of a sinful false oath, and is considered a pure אונס, is, of course, perfectly clear. The one who makes a statement on oath, has only to express, can only express, what remains in his mind as having occured. Even if this is based on an error, he could not swear to anything else, his mind lay under the force of the error which as an אונם raises him above all responsibility. But that the consciousness of the forbidden nature of the act belongs so much to the nature of the sin of false swearing, that if this is forgotten at the moment of taking the oath, it is not considered as a שגגה — which would nevertheless require atonement — but as an אונס — which does not even require atonement — is a peculiarity which characterises the sin of false swearing, and differentiates it from all other שגגות. (Sabbath 69b and Rashi ד״ה הא מני מונבז). If, for example, someone had eaten חלב or done a מלאכה on Sabbath, entirely forgetting the forbidden and punishable nature of his act שגג בלאו וכרת שבו, the act is still considered a sin which requires atonement. It is a שגגה which requires the חטאת קבועה of which Ch. IV speaks. But a false oath taken in a similar condition of forgetfulness is considered an אונס and does not necessitate a קרבן. This peculiarity which characterises the Law of Oaths can be well understood as the result of the whole underlying meaning of an oath, as we have believed we could understand it.

For if the way we have taken the meaning of an oath be not erroneous, that השבע is nothing but the placing of oneself under the whole weight of God’s Justice and punishment, if what we swear is false, or if we fail to carry out that which we have sworn to do (see Ex. 20,7), then it follows automatically that the act of the שבועה must in the very first place presuppose the consciousness that a false oath is a sin against God’s will. Without this consciousness the השבע means absolutely nothing, inasmuch as the whole idea of an oath is lacking. Now, if nevertheless the addition of ונעלם ממנו excludes a complete מזיד, is פרט למזיד, tells us that the קרבן עולה ויורד is not to be brought where the sin is done completely במזיד, the case for this העלמה in promissory oaths, שבועת בטוי להבא is quite simple. He took the vow with full consciousness of all that it implied, he was an אדם בשבועה, but then he forgot that he had made the vow נעלם ממנו שבועה and in consequence of this forgetfulness he broke his vow. And here again it is characteristic that על העלם שבועה חייב ואינו חייב על העלם חפץ. The קרבן עולה ויורד has only to be brought when the vow was broken through forgetfulness of having made it, but not through mistaking the object of the vow. Not, for instance, if a man had sworn not to eat wheaten-bread, and then ate some under the impression that it was made of oats. In all other שגגות there is no difference between making a mistake in the object, or forgetting the prohibition. If one had eaten חלב thinking it was שומן, one is just as much bound to bring a חטאת as when one had eaten it forgetting the prohibition to eat חלב. But at קרבן עולה ויורד a complete forgetfulness of the oath, נעלמה ממנו שבועה must be the cause of the dereliction. In the case of assertive oaths, שבועת בטוי לשעבר however, the case for this העלמה is more difficult to find. The העלמה there must be at the moment of taking the oath, when, on the other hand האדם בשבועה, complete consciousness regarding both the subject of the matter and the sinful nature of false oaths are demanded. Shebuoth 26b can accordingly only find the case where, at the time of swearing, the person taking the oath was quite aware of the sinfulness of false oaths, but did not realise the obligation to bring a קרבן which results from it. באומר יודע אני ששבועה זו אסורה, אבל אינו יודע אם חייבין עליה קרבן או לאו. For the obligation to bring a חטאת for שבועת בטוי is altogether something special and exceptional, for in every other case a חטאת has only to be brought for a “חייב כרת״ sin. (In all this we have followed Rashi’s way of explanation. רמב״ם takes it differently in some instances, but these are not without difficulties).

V. 5. והתודה. It is most significant that confession of guilt, “confessions of sin” is expressed almost exclusively in the reflexive form התודה. To no man — in the first instance, not even to God, Who, in any case, does not have to wait for our confession to obtain knowledge of our sins —, but to himself has the sinner to confess the sin he has committed. To himself must be admit he has sinned. Such admission to himself is, of course, the very first indispensable step towards betterment; the earnest resolve and promise for betterment is, of course, altogether the condition for bringing an offering. The offering presupposes this earnest resolve to תשובה, it is only the outward expression of it, and without it, has absolutely no meaning whatsoever (see Ch. 1,2 and IV,3). But the first step towards this תשובה-resolve is, making clear to oneself without any self-deception, exactly where, and in what, one has sinned. As long as one allows one’s mind to be bemused with apologetic self-deception, there is no thought of really pure conscientiousness for the future. It is not sufficient התודה אשר חטא, to admit to oneself in general that one has sinned, but אשר חטא עליה, but one must consider the exact special circumstances which led to the sin being committed; only then can it be avoided in future. This וידוי was made at all חטאות אשמות ועולות and had to be said at the סמיכה (Yoma 33). This וידוי is so far away from the ordinary conception of “confession” that Jewish teaching consideres confessing one’s sins to other human beings as an act rather to be blamed than praised. It sees in such revealing of sins שבין אדם למקום, which only concern our relations to God, and only need be known by Him, as a somewhat ill-bred exposure of matters which the truly repentant hide in shame deep within their hearts (Berachoth 34 and Yoma 56).

V. 6. והביא את אשמו לה׳ וגו׳ לחטאת and the same in V. 7. Here אשמו cannot mean to describe the nature of the offering as an אשם, for, as a matter of fact, it is not an אשם but has, in every respect all the qualities of a חטאת. It can accordingly only be meant to describe the condition of the bringer of the offering, as being still “guilt laden”. His atonement is to be expressed in the אשם .חטאת regards this condition more from the point of view of the external results of the sin, endangering his future existence, while חטאת looks at it more from the point of view of inner degradation. But that the חטאת is described here from the stand-point of an אשם may perhaps be explained by the fact that all the three sins for which this קרבן עולה ויורד is prescribed touch very closely to מזיד. Both שמיעת קול and שבועת בטוי exclude an ordinary simple שגגה (a גדידה). By the requisition that האדם בשבועה, and טומאת מקדש וקדשיו has to have at least a ידיעה בתחלה the העלמה is an altogether greater sin than an ordinary שגגה. And in any case, as we shall still have to go into, the fact that in these cases, atonement is made possible for all persons down to the very lowest state of poverty, showing a more than usual necessity for attaining atonement, shows that these sins are regarded with a greater seriousness, so that by this אשמו anyone who has fallen into committing such a sin is reminded of the whole serious consequences with which his own future existence is threatened thereby. When he brings his offering he is to clearly realise that by disregarding the fundamental principles which are laid down in these laws he is rendering the existence of his own personality desolate: “אשם״. See notes on V. 15 et. seq.—(But with regards to שמיעת קול and שבועת בטוי, altogether with regards to sins connected with oaths, the כפרה achieved by a קרבן, or even that obtained by judical מלקות does not entirely remove that which was proclaimed on Sinai הלול השם .כי לא ינקה ה׳ committed במזיד is only completely atoned for by the punishment meted out by God’s justice. See Rambam הל׳ שבועות XXI, 1. כ״מ and ל״מ thereon).

V. 8 & 9. והקריב את אשר לחטאת ראשונה Pessachim 59a: זה בנה אב לכל חטאות שיהיו קודמות לכל עולות הבאות עמהן. Herewith the general canon is given, that whenever חטאת and עולה are offered together, the חטאת is to be offered first. If חטאת comes to counter transgressions and עולה to counter inactivity, then this law may draw our attention to the principle, that in the first place we are to סור מרע and only then strive to ומלק את — .עשה טוב ראשו וגו׳. See notes on עולת העוף Ch. 1,15. חטאת העוף differs from עולת העוף in that, while at an עולה, both the סימנים, the trachea and the oesophagus, have to be cut through, more, the whole head has to be cut off, here it expressly says ולא יבדיל and only one סימן has to be cut through by מליקה (according to רמב״ם the difference only lies in not cutting the head right off). Further, whereas at an עולה the מליקה is already done בראש המזבח and מצוי הדם likewise has to be done למעלה, at a חטאת the מליקה is done below in the south-west corner, (but could be done below at any side of the Altar) and instead of מצוי, the real עבודת הדם viz., הזיה sprinkling (weaker form of זריקה), is done and that is done למטה מחוט הסקרא. This is expressed in והנשאר וגו׳ יִמָצֵה וגו׳ (not יַמְצֶה) by which the blood reaching the יסוד is designated as an automatic result of the הזיה, so that the הזיה should take place at such a spot where some of the blood of the הזיה would reach the יסוד. This would only be the case למטה מן החוט, as if done למעלה מן החוט, above the סובב, any blood flowing down would fall on the סובב and not on the קיר שהשירין :יסוד שלו מתמצים ליסוד. Still this מצוי is one of the procedures which come after the הזיה regarding which it is not quite decided whether it is מעכב or like all other שירים, only מצוה. Probably the latter (Zebachim 63,64). But the הזיה must take place, as prescribed, in the South-west corner בקרן דרומית מערבית (ibid) as must also the מנחה which takes its place in the case of בדלי דלות. Of the חטאת העוף only the blood comes on the Altar. The rest of the body is eaten by the כהנים similarly to the בשר חטאת בהמה.

V. 10. כמשפט would primarily refer to the laws which have already been given for עולת העוף (Ch. 1,14 et seq.). But Chulin 21,a, nevertheless, takes it to refer to the preceding general laws of the חטאת — it does take the place of a חטאת בהמה — and ק״א on this verse in ת״כ thinks, that, if it referred to the laws of an ordinary עולת העוף it would have said כמשפטו.

V. 11. את קרבנו אשר חטא. If we compare places like ואת אשר חטא מן הקדש (Ch.V,16), חוטא נפשו (Prov. 20,2), וחוטא נפשך (Habakuk 2,10), we find that the verb חטא can have as its object, not only sin itself, the חטא but also the thing against which one has sinned, which one has violated by one’s sin. So that קרבנו אשר חטא means: the expression of the nearness of God, which he has thrown lightly away by his sin.
V. 12. והביאה אל הכהן. See above Ch. II. מנחת חוטא, too, like all מנחות where קמיצה takes place, requires הגשה to the south-west corner before taking the קמיצה (Menachoth 60a and b).

V. 13. והיתה לכהן כמנחה. The שירים are given to the כהן to be eaten, like those of a מנחת נדבה (Ch. 2,3). But if a כהן himself is the one who had to bring the מנחה, he can be קמריב it himself, as in the case of a מנחת נדבה of a כהן, it is כליל, and has to be burnt in its entirety on the Altar, without taking off a קמיצה (Menachoth 73b; see Ch. 6,16).

שבועת בטוי ,טומאת מקדש וקדשיו ,שמיעת קול, apparently belonging to entirely diverse categories of laws, must nevertheless show some very essential close inner connection with each other, and, at the same time present a closed circle of some special idea of the Law, if the Torah picks them out from the whole large sphere of its laws to form a special group having its own characteristic and prescriptions, which differ from all others for transgressions done out of carelessness.

Let us first look for what is common to these three cases which necessitate the bringing of a קרבן עולה ויודד. It at once strikes us that all three are concerned with ידיעה “knowledge”. Knowledge which one has of something, is denied or overlooked. שמיעת הקול denies having the knowledge of somebody else’s affairs which one has gained by ראיה or ידיעה; in טומאת מקדש וקדשיו, one allows the ידיעת טומאה or the ידיעת מקדש וקדשיו which one had, to escape one’s mind; שבועת בטוי לשעבד tells a lie against the truth of one’s own knowledge. To this one side of Man’s inner self, his knowledge, his consciousness, שבועת בטוי להבא adds the other side, Man’s power to exercise his will in predetermination; so that we have here the sum of Man’s principle inner activities, his knowledge and his Will. The חטאת-Chapter begins (v.4) with שגגת הוראה, errors in making decisions as to what is right or wrong, made by highest spiritual authorities in the land, the כהן המשיח and the ב״ד הגדול. The people themselves only have to get atonement by an offering for actual sins committed. The קרבן עולה ויורד, with which the חטאת laws conclude, takes us into the mental spiritual realm of that consciousness which should be the constant common possession of every Jew, and as such, should be kept guarded against any and every defilement or demoralisation.

If now we consider the spheres in which these קרבן עולה ויורד-sins occur:- in שמיעת הקול it is society, and the principle involved is: Justice; in טומאת מקדש וקדשיו it is the Sanctuary of the Torah, and the principle involved is: Freedom of the Will, moral freedom; in שבועת בטוי it is the Mind, and the principle involved is: Truth in thought and Will. All three can be classed under the conception. “Truth”. Truth in Justice, truth in Morality, truth to one’s own mind. And these truths not to be taken as being merely postulates for personal or social puposes, but as being postulated by God, as being fixed by God, for every נפש in Israel for their behaviour and relation to the Sanctuary, to Society, to themsleves and to God. These are ידיעות which make the נפש into a Jewish personality, and, for any discordance of their purity, God demands a reckoning.

שמיעת הקול places every Jew in Society; shows him God, as the guarantor of society and its matters of justice and right; every member of society, placed by God, in the service of the well-being of his fellow-members, readily giving his knowledge and his word those spiritual bonds which hold all social life together. It picks the duty of giving true evidence out of all other social duties, as being the one in which the meaning of right and justice of man towards his fellowman reaches its highest degree of importance and consequence. In the name of God, every man can demand from every other man — even without a court of justice — to fulfil the duty which lies upon him of giving legal evidence in his favour. And if, thereupon, in court, he denies his knowledge of such evidence, then without having taken an oath himself, or having answered “amen” to the demand made by oath, he has committed the sin af perjury not only against his fellow-man, but against God, the Defender of the Rights of Man, and against the truth of his own consciousness. Truth in matters of Justice and Right amongst men is a concern of God.

טומאת מקדש וקדשיו, places every Jew in the presence of the Sanctuary of the Law and its appurtenances which rest solely on the truth of moral freedom of the will, and in the presence of the טומאה which is preached by death, the lack of freedom of the will which death preaches, and says to him: “Be not depressed, let not the fact of the death of physical life rob you of, or make you have doubts of, the consciousness of the freedom of your moral spiritual life, the freedom of your god-like spiritual self which does not come under the force and power of death. The Mikdosh which God has established for you, and its קדשים which He gives you, guarantee in His name the truth of your moral spiritual consciousness which invites you, — surrounded though you are with all the most compelling forces of your physical nature, — to serve your God, with the complete freedom of will of your spiritual self. Both spheres, that of טומאה, your physical lack of free-will, your having willy-nilly to submit to physical forces, and that of טהרה, your complete free-will in moral and spiritual matters, both are truths, both come from God, the One Creator of physical Nature and spiritual life. They only become lies when you mix them. You belong to both realms, but beware of setting foot in the one with the breath of the other upon you. Physically you are unfree, but morally you are free, and while you are alive, God has wedded your unfree physical forces to the free mastery of your god-like free moral energy for the service of His Sanctuary of the Torah. Physical truths are only valid for physical existence. But your human existence reaches beyond, over the realm of purely physical being. It is ennobled by God, Who is free, with the breath of god-like freedom of will, and in that realm the true laws of physical matter and forces become untrue. Let not the ידיעת בית רבך, the teaching of the טהרה with which alone the מקדש is to be entered, or its קדשים to be eaten, the teaching of טומאה and טהרה between which Man has to choose, and of which טומאה closes up the way to the מקדש and to eating of its קדשים, let not this teaching with which every young Jewish soul has the consciousness of our being born for God’s Sanctuary and for the enjoyment of its blessings impressed on it, let not this teaching of your youth become a childrens’ fairytale. Let this ידיעת בית רבן be your guide through the seriousness of life, and do not deny the Mikdosh-truth of moral and spiritual freedom of will, by entering the Sanctuary of God, or eating His קדשים, with thoughts of טומאה awakened by contact with Death. Maintain the consciousness of the difference of the ways of קדושה and of טומאה. The Truth of moral and spiritual freedom in the consciousness of Men is a concern of God.

שבועת בטוי places the inner self of every Jew before God, and says: — “see, your whole spiritual inner self, with all its thoughts, and will and intensions, belongs to God. The very slightest creation of your mind, the slightest impulse of your will is known to Him. He pays attention to every thought that you express, to every resolution that you declare. He does not wish you to play with the spoken thought, with declared intentions. Even in matters which otherwise are not of the slightest importance, דבר רשות, you can call Him to be the guarantor of your word, of your intention. And if you have called upon Him as guarantor of your word, or of your intention, in quite immaterial matters, even where it does not affect the interest of anybody else at all, and your word is not true, or you fail to carry out your intention, see, Heaven and Earth are the carriers of His judgment on you for even the most unimportant word that you have untruthfully uttered with His Name, for the most trivial intention that you have sworn to carry out and have failed to make your vow true. The Truth of Thought and Will in the mind of Man is a concern of God.

Right, Justice, the basis of society, moral freedom of will, the basis of the Mikdosh, Truth, the basis of the human mind and will, all documented and championed by God Himself, these are the convictions on the ground of which Jewish life flourishes. Not one of them can be dispensed with, not אחת מאלה, without becoming unfaithful to the whole future of the mission of every Jew. And if he has slipped and sinned against one of these fundamental principles, even with a certain amount of העלם, with a certain amount of unconsciousness and unintention, then the Torah sees to it that everyone, down to the poorest member of the Jewish Nation, is brought to realise how אשם לאחת מאלה, how, having sinned against being always conscious of one of these, he has trodden the threshold of “desolation and solitude”. How God expects everyone, down to the very poorest, to be a guarantor of Justice in Society, of Morality in the Sanctuary, and of Truth in the human mind; and that He will only spare entry into “desolation and loneliness” if he התרדה to himself אשר חטא עליה, if he takes to heart in all its absolute objectivity, the whole initial impulse which brought about the sin; and then with a suitable offering expressing his determination in future to keep his mind more fully conscious of his duty, finds his way back to his lost nearness to God on the heights of the Altar of the Sanctuary of the Torah.

This offering, in normal circumstances is a כשבה or a שעירה as a חטאת (see notes on Ch. 4,27 et seq.). In straitened circumstance, a חטאת עוף and an עולת עוף take the place of the חטאת בהמה, and in still greater poverty, a מנחת חוטא.

We have already worked out, on עולת עוף נדבה (Ch. 1,14 et seq) the meaning of birds in offerings, and of the procedures of an עולת עוף, and also, in general, the special peculiarities of a חטאת עוף, and we would refer back to that. Here we still have to consider the more detailed specialities of a חטאת עוף, and also the fact that in the case of עוף both a חטאת and an עולה have to be brought in the place of a חטאת בהמה.

That תור and יונה represent the personality of a suffering person, one who lacks the feeling of being under the special care and guidance of God as is expressed by כבשה and שעירה, has already been shown there; and here, the fact that birds are the offering of a poor man is quite in accordance with that interpretation. We also gave an explanation there of the peculiar reversal of the mode of the proceedings of the עבודת הדם in offerings of birds; namely that, contrary to the corresponding norm for עולת בהמה and חטאת בהמה an עולת עוף is במצד׳ למעלה and a חטאת עוף is בהזיה למטה. We ascribed this also to our idea that birds were the offering of suffering people. We took it that the sins of people in a suffering condition arise, in the main, out of despondent hopelessness begetting indifference. To counter this, הדיה למטה comes to express the newly awakened striving upwards to the heights. We also thought that the energy which suffering people have to expend, is mainly in tenaciously holding on to the heights of their spiritual calling. This is accordingly expressed in an עולת עוף by מצוי למעלה. From these considerations we can at once see that active sinning against the Torah on the part of poverty-striken and suffering people would, as a rule, arise out of both these factors. Because they presume that they have been forsaken by God’s care, abandoned by God, they abandon themselves, give themselves up to despair, and lose the energy to keep themselves up on the heights of the moral stage they had reached; because they despair of themselves they lose their self-respect and indifferently allow themselves to sink into positive sin, they fall because they have given up all thoughts of betterment. Or, to speak in the language of offering-procedure: — because he denied the life-stream of his personality, דם נפשו, any attempt to strive up again to the heights, הזיה למטה of the עולה, therefore he sank, and that, too, was why he had not the energy to keep himself up on the spiritual height of the Torah, he gave up the מצוי-energy למעלה of the חטאת. So it is easy to understand why, in the place of the one חטאת בהמה, the poor man brings both חטאת ועולת העוף.

The ritual of the offering of the עולת העוף expresses, as already mentioned above, the great teaching, that patiently enduring the hardest blows of fate without sinking down from the spiritual height of our calling, is valued on the Altar of God, as a great God-serving act, לריח ניחוח לה׳. Hence מליקה בראש המזבח, and indeed מליקה with complete שיסוע ,מצדי ,הבדלה etc. But חטאת העוף, which teaches, not passive endurance, but cheerful progressive activity forwards and upwards, in spite of suffering poverty, has accordingly not to have the violent mishandling procedures of the .עולה מליקה is kept in the background and is only done בסימן א׳, it says ולא יבדיל; only הזיה is done, and that is done on the “happy, God’s-corner”, the -מערבית דרומית corner selected for the הגשת מנחה, to the פני המזבח and לפגי ה׳, where under the rays of the מנורה-light of the Spirit kindled by the Torah, one’s intelligence and carrying out of the Torah directs itself towards God; מצוי שירים אל יסוד המזבח, the throbbing life-pulse of the poor man who thus lives his life for God and His Torah, is also ranked in the great basis of the whole united national life; and finally by אכילת הבשר לכהנים, the poor man is taught how one whose pulse beats for God and His Torah, can, and should, even in the most humble and insignificant station of life, consider his life a priestly one, which can and should be enjoyed in purity and cheerfulness before God (see notes on Ch. 2,10). The חטאת of a כבשה or שעירה of the rich man, as well as the חטאת and עולה of תורים or בני יונה of the poor man are called אשם. They express the resolution which, if they are carried out, will prevent the desolation with which the future life of the sinner is threatened, from taking effect. The עשירית האפה of the extreme poor, which, as we explained in the מנחות (Ch. II) does not represent bringing the person himself near to God, but the bringing of the possessions which have been granted for his existence, is accordingly not designated as אשם but as קרבנו, as his getting near to God, אשר חטא, which, by his sin, he had denied and trifled with. He, the poorest man, in his dire poverty — the state which this קרבן assumes — considered himself the farthest away from the blessing-giving nearness to God, and so could easily fall into the delusion that he was not reckoned on by God amongst the guarantors of Right and Justice in society, amongst the upholders of the morality and freedom of His Sanctuary, or amongst those that foster Truth of Mind and Will.

And if, in the state of indifference and carelessness which such self-contempt breeds, he had sinned against one of these institutions of God, and then had realised his guilt, the Torah bids him come to the Sanctuary, and with עשירית האיפה סולת, the manna-measure of the means of existence for one single day, drive home to his mind, that even the smallest measure of earthly possessions, that even the simplest, most precarious means of one day’s existence, is no smaller pledge of the nearness of God, than is the richest and most luxurious means of life. Even the most unpretentious living of the poorest is in quite the same nearness of God, the product of His care and attention, and calls the poorest, too, to the same cheerful service to his fellow men, to the Sanctuary and to his own spiritual mentality. God awaits the oil-less and incense-less עשירית האיפה of flour of the poorest, too, accepted and sanctified in the vessel of His Sanctuary (קידוש בכלי). It, too, is brought by the hand of a minister of His Sanctuary under the rays of Light of His Torah, and laid dedicatingly at His feet (הגשה בקרן לרומית מערבית), and thus the life of even the poorest is shown to be valued and dedicated to getting an understanding of the Torah and carrying out its dictates. The poorest, too, has to give all he can (his handful קומץ) towards the claims of the Sanctuary of God’s Torah, and with this “handful” to ensure that he and his life will be “remembered” with quite the equal care and provision, and take equal rank with the richest sacrifices for the up-keeping of godliness on earth (אזכרתה — על אשי ה׳, cf, Ch. 4,35), Then, finally, he is to be made conscious, by such value being placed on his life and on his sacrifice, of how even his simple life can attain, and can participate in, holy priest-like enjoyment of life (והיתה לכהן כמנחה).

The fact that the offering brought from this extreme state of poverty should consist simply of סלת, the means of bare existence, without שמן, the symbol of wealth, well-being, and without לבנה, expressing satisfaction-giving comfort, seems quite natural. The offering is to be brought just to express the nearness of God even in the condition of the most bare existence. But it is expressly forbidden to put oil or incense on it: לא ישים עליה שמן ולא יתן עליה לבנה, each is to be taken as a separate prohibition חייב על השמן בפני עצמו ועל לבנה בפני עצמו (Menachoth 59b). And the reason given for these prohibitions is, not that they are on account of the direst poverty, but because they are brought on account of a condition of sin, because it is a sin-offering: כי חטאה היא! (Similar to the מנחת סוטה, Numbers 5,16). This may well be to tell us that if only poverty keeps itself free from sin, then the poorest of the poor can feel himself rich, and in greatest poverty still be happy. It is not poverty but sin which precludes the oil and the incense. In a condition of sin even riches would prevent the real feeling of happiness לא ישים עליה שמן ולא יתן עליה לבנה כי חטאת היא.

Looking at it from this point of view, one can also understand the traditional Halacha given in Menachoth 59b, according to which נתן משהו שמן על גבי כזית מנחה פסול, נתן כזית לבנה על גבי משהו מנחה פסול. In the case of שמן the prohibition uses the term שימה “putting anything at all on” לא ישים עליה שמן, so that even the smallest quantity of oil, פשהו, would render חייב. But regarding the incense, the prohibition is couched under the term ולא יתן and “giving” implies the minimum quantity of a “gift” viz., כזית. But with regards to the מנחה itself the matter is reversed. The word עליה demands at least such a quantity by which the whole מנחה can be represented, i.e., a כזית. But עליה is repeated for לבנה, which tells us that it is not for the demand for the quantity that has already been made for the oil, but that the עליה for the לבנה is to have a comprehensive meaning “as long as it is put on it” i.e., even on a משהו מנחה, (in accordance with the general canon אין רבוי אחר רבוי אלא למעט). So that the two prohibitions would accordingly run:—“not even a drop of oil may be placed on a piece of Mincha which can be considered as “nourishing” or satisfying (a כזית), and no satisfying quantity of incense is to be placed on even a grain of the Mincha, for it is a sin-offering. The idea would be; it is not poverty, the lack of plenty, that makes the poor man have no feelings of happiness and well-being. Without sin, even the poorest of the poor would have some feeling of riches with every bit of food that nourishes him, and every mite gives him satisfaction, it is only here, under the regime of sin, that the nourishing little bit of food lacks “all oil”, and every tiny grain is robbed of giving him the feeling of “satisfaction”. (According to another tradition quoted ibid 60a, the application of the prohibition of oil to even a single drop, is considered doubtful).

V. 14. וידבר. The preceding verse concluded God’s commands regarding the various חטאות which were commenced in Ch. 4. With this chapter we now get His commands for another category of offerings, the אשם. Three אשמות follow here: אשם תלוי ,אשם מעילה and אשם גזלה, the last being introduced specially by itself. Although the causes which occasion the necessity to bring these offerings seem to be very different, the offering and procedure is exactly the same for all three. So that there must certainly be some inner connection and similarity between them; but we can only try to find out in what this consists, after we have considered the principle details which the Torah lays down for each of them.

V. 15. (ת״ב) לרבות כהן משיח למעילה :נפש .נפש כי תמעל וגו׳ :אשם מעילה, the all-comprehensive נפש makes everybody — even the High Priest — equal in this sin against the Mikdosh. מעל :כי תמעל מעל, the word, in its relationship to מעיל, the mantle of the High Priest — similar to בגד, to be faithless, disloyal, and בגד garment — is an excellent example of the harmonious trend of thought which is formed by the roots of the words of the Hebrew language. בגד means the garment of a human being, and בגוד to be faithless, to break faith in general human matters. מעיל the garment of a High Priest, and מעול, to break faith in holy, priestly matters. Obviously בגוד is to behave as a mere garment, and מעול to behave as merely the cloak of a Priest. To see someone clothed in human garments makes one conclude that here is a real human being. If someone puts trust in me as being a true human being, and I betray that trust, then I have shown myself to be merely the cloak of a human being. I wear the outer appearance of a human being but it was only the mask of a human being. In the same way מעול, one was justified in expecting priestly sentiments and behaviour from me, and I have proved myself to be merely the mask of a priest. In Meila 18a we read: אין מעל אלא שנוי וכן הוא אומר איש איש כי תשטה אשתו ומעלה בו מעל, ואומר וימעלו באלקי אבותיהם ויזנו אחרי הבעלים; there, in consideration of the fact that the same expression is used in connection with a woman being unfaithful to her husband as with Israel being unfaithful to God, the idea of מעילה is explained as שנוי, ie.e., as behaving differently from the way one was justified in expecting from you. Here, referring to קדשי ה׳, as behaving towards the holy things of God differently to what is expected of us, considering what they were meant to be. קדשי ה׳ are the objects which belong exclusively to God’s relation to us. These are: (a) קדשי מזבח, “holy things for the Altar”, things which one has dedicated to be used as offerings, animals or מנחות, i.e., things which are themselves to be used for holy purposes, which have קדושת הגוף; and (b) קדשי בדק הבית, things which have been dedicated to the upkeep of the Temple, things which are not themselves actually used in the Temple, but are given to the coffers of the Temple to be sold for the Temple treasury, which have קדושת דמים. The Mikdosh of God and its holy appurtenances are entrusted to the care of the whole nation to be kept holy. It is expected that everybody in the nation will honour this trust by comporting himself towards them in a high-priestly manner, i.e., that they are kept exclusively for the purpose for which they were destined, and not used for anything else. If we betray this trust, we have behaved in an “unpriestly” manner, have committed מעילה.

From the comparison of מעילה to ע״ז and to סוטה, and from its being made similar to (חטא חטא מתרומה) תרומה, it is deduced that the sin of מעילה is committed by שנוי רשות without direct הנאה, removing the article out of the possession of the Mikdosh, without actually making direct use of it, e.g., giving it as a present to someone, selling it or lending it (similar to the transference out of רשות הקב״ה into רשות ע״ז); by נהנה ולא פגם, using the article without involving any wear, e.g., wearing a piece of jewellery belonging to the Mikdosh (similar to סוטה); or by נהנה ופגם, using it when it does wear it out (similar to אכילת תרומה, Levit. 22,14). From its being made similar to תרומה the law also follows that פגם ולא נהנה, if damage is done without any personal use or enjoyment, it does not come under the heading of מעילה, just as the norm goes for ואיש כי יאכל קדש פרט למזיק :תרומה (see Meila 18 & 19 and תוספות there). We have already remarked on Ex. 21,34 the significant law that the whole responsibility for damages, נזיקין, in the case of הקדש does not fall within the jurisdiction of any human court of justice. Objects which are of no importance to the Mikdosh for their actual value so there is no loss at all to the Mikdosh by their being used e.g., animals for offerings, or such objects which only lose in intrinsic value after a great deal of use over a long period, a golden cup, a piece of gold jewellery, are subjects to מעילה as soon as they are used for profane purposes. But objects, the use of which normally entails loss or damages, are only subject to מעילה when such loss or damage is actually incurred: כל דבר שיש בו פגם לא מעל עד שיפגם, ושאין בו פגם כיון שנהנה מעל (Meila 18a). From this same comparison to תרומה it is also deduced that just as the dedication to תרומה can be made by a שליח, so can the desecration through מעילה be made by a duly authorised שליח and the responsibility for it falls on the משלח and not on the actual perpetrator. In this, מעילה is one of the few exceptional cases where יש שליח לדבר עברה, a law which we have already considered on Ex. 21,37. Further, מעילה like תרומה is restricted to objects which are תלוש מז הקרקע, and which are moveable. But, on the other hand, in many respects מעילה goes further than תרומה particularly in that, while the קרן וחומש which is imposed for inadvertent sinning against תרומה is restricted to אכילה only, מעילה includes any and every kind of usage.

It is characteristic that — as indeed it mentions expressly in the text וחטא בשגגה — the whole idea of מעילה, with the consequent imposition of קרבן ותשלומי קרן וחומש is only applied to sinning מזיר במעילה .בשגגה does not entails these consequences, it only results in לוקה or משלם (see רמב״ם הל׳ מעילה, 1, 3).

This limitation to שוגג appears also in the following: — All objects which have only קדושת דמים (i.e., are not intrinsically קודש in themselves), such as קדשי בדק הבית lose their קדושה by מעילה and become חולין (— according to רמב״ם however, only in the one case of מעילה, viz., הוצאה מרשות הקדש e.g., selling, giving away, or lending, but not by usage, by נהנה ונפגם or where פגם is not applicable, by נהנה alone. See מל״מ on הל׳ מעילה 6,4). Hence the dictum: אין מועל אחר מועל במוקדשין אלא בהמה וכלי שרת בלבד (Meila 19b). For these, as having קדושה in themselves, having קדושת הגוף, do not lose their character of holiness by מעילה and then sin of מעילה can be repeated on them again and again, whereas those which are only holy for their value, become profane by one מעילה and are then considered as חולין. Now this limitation to שוגג, as mentioned above, results in the canon that הקדש בשוגג מתחלל, במזיד אין מתחלל (Kidushin 55a). A conscious, intentional desecration of an holy object does not rob it of its nature of holiness, only an inadvertent profane use of it does so!

The conception קדשי ה׳ which underlies מעילה, excludes all objects of the Mikdosh at the time when they do not yet belong exclusively לגבוה, or when they have already been handed over to the כהנים or the בעלים for their own use. קדשים קלים are considered as ממון בעלים, and only come into the status of being liable to מעילה when זריקה takes place by which act the אימורים become dedicated to the מזבח. In these cases מעילה is restricted to the אימורים after זריקה, as the בשר is then at once handed over to the בעלים and קדשי קדשים .כהנים belong entirely לגבוד from the moment they have been dedicated as offerings, משהוקדשו, and מעילה accordingly applies to them even before זריקה, but after זריקה in the case of חטאת and מעילה ,אשם would only apply to the אימורים but not to the בשר, as this, by the זריקה already belongs to the יש היתר לכהנים :כהנים (Meila 7b).

Further, אין לך דבר שנעשה מצותו ומועלין בו, once the prescribed procedure for which the object was destined has been done, the liability to מעילה ceases, with the exception of תרומת הדשן and of the once-used בגדי כהונה of the High Priest on י״כ and of the עגלה ערופה (Meila 11b).

Of all the objects pertaining to the Mikdosh, there is one exception to which מעילה does not apply, viz., דם, the blood which is destined for the מתנות on the זריקה ,נתינה ,הזיה — מזבח (for the blood is nothing that is dedicated itself, but represents the personality of the person who is dedicating his various activities. Meila 2a & Zebachim 46a). In ת״כ on this verse, it takes the limiting מ in מקדשי ה׳ to refer to this. וכן אמעיט מנוחר ומטומאה לאכל בטומאת הגוף (Zebachim 45b).

איל is the male of the sheep, which has reached the thirty-first day of its second year. During the first thirty days of the second year it is called פלגס, and is not to be brought either as a כבש or as an איל.

בערכו. We believe that the ך in the form ערכך is simply the suffix of the second person: thy valuation, i.e., the valuation of the nation, the worth of the object according to national valuation, the amount fixed by the representatives of the nation, the priests, estimated for national purposes as for instance, here and in Ch. 27,12; or, in most other cases, the valuation acording to the fixed national market price, as repeatedly expressed in Ch. XXVII. — כסף שקלים, the ram for the אשם must be worth at least two שקלים.

לאשם. As explained in Ch. VII, the אשם resembles the עולה in שחיטה and זריקה and the חטאת in הקטרת אימורים and אכילת בשר לכהנים. The three אשמות prescribed here, as well as the אשם שפחה חרופה differ from both only in the fact that they must consist of an איל and must have the fixed value of two שקלים (an אשם נזיד or an אשם מצורע consists of a כבש).

V. 16. תשלומין .ואת אשר חטא מן הקדש has to be paid even for פחות משוה פרוטה, but אשם and חומש only if it is at least a ואת חמישיתו .פרוטה its fifth, i.e., its lacking fifth. The amount of the valuation is considered as four-fifths of a whole and the lacking fifth has to be added; שיהא הוא וחומשו חמשה. This is called חומש מלבר, not the fifth of the sum before one, מלגיו, but that which lies “outside” it, the fifth which is lacking to make a whole. This, according to our usual reckoning is one quarter. באיל אשם וגו׳. It is the איל and the קרן, but not the חומש, which are essential to accomplish the כפרה (according to Numbers 5,7 & 8 as well as Baba Kama 3a). To summarise the laws of אשם מעילה: — If anybody, forgetting its holy character, disposes of any article of the Mikdosh (whether it be intrinsically holy, or only dedicated for its value) by selling, giving or lending; or if he uses it — according to the nature of the object — with or without reducing its value —, he has to bring an offering of a ram worth two shekels as an אשם, and has to pay the הקדש, the value of that which he has disposed of, or make good the reduction in value he has used, and on that he has to add one fifth. Holy objects which have been dedicated only for their value lose their character of holiness by inadvertent misuse. Conscious intentional misuse does not affect their character of holiness, and also does not entail the bringing of an offering or the payment of an extra fifth, is not חייב קרבן וחומש, but is only באזהרה (see מל״מ on הל׳ מעילה 1,3).

V. 17. Verses 17—19 deal with אשם תלוי, the offering one has to bring when one is in doubt whether one has committed inadvertently a sin, which if done intentionally, would be punishable by פרת. As long as he is not sure that he has committed it, he has to bring an אשם, which just because of his being “suspended” in doubt, is called אשם תלוי. This doubt is expressed in the text by ולא ידע, in contrast to the הודע אליו, when he has to bring a חטאת (Ch. 4,28). Although he is still in doubt whether he has actually sinned or not, this doubting state of mind is shown to be one by which אשם, he is threatened with “desolation”, and as a sin with which he is burdened. Even more, the paragraph concludes with the repetition, אשם הוא, אשם אשם לה׳, and thereby drives home to us, how just this wavering doubt over the lawfulness or otherwise of our acts is to be considered as a serious wrong in our behaviour towards God, a wrong which threatens our future life with desolation. The way and manner in which a doubtful case is expressed in Numbers 5,14, may offer an explanatory parallel to our case here. There, the two alternatives of the doubt are both expressed in two positive sentences. Here also the possibility about which there is the doubt, is expressed in the positive alternative only. It suffices to say that if he has sinned against the Law and does not know whether he has done so, even by this condition of a “not knowing” he commits a sin against God which requires atonement. In Kerithoth 25a Reb. Eliezer has actually the opinion — which is not accepted — that מתנדב אדם אשם תלוי בכל יום ובכל עת שירצה that at any time, one can bring an אשם תלוי as a free will offering, as there can always be a doubt in one’s mind whether one has not unconsciously sinned. But the Halacha is that no sin-offering of any kind may be brought without a specific cause and then always only as חובה, as an obligatory offering (cf. what we wrote above on the ה׳ חטאות מתות). So far away indeed is the Jewish Torah teaching from that self-tormented doctrine of being always conscious of “what a sinner I am!”. Even אשם תלוי may only be brought on account of some definite act which causes the doubt, which then makes the bringing of an אשם a חובה, an obligation duty. For instance, he had eaten a piece of fat, and then is in doubt whether it was a piece of שומן which is allowed to be eaten, or חלב which is forbidden (and the eating of which is a כרת-sin); or he performed a מלאכה during בין השמשות, the time which it is doubtful whether it is still day or already night, and so does not know whether the moment was שבת or חול etc etc. In Kerithoth 17b the explantion is given — which רמב״ם accepts as Halacha in הל׳ שגגות — that חתיכה משתי חתיכות שנינו, that the doubt for which an אשם תלוי has to be brought must arise from a case in which it is certain that the איסור as well as the היתר lay before him, איקבע איסודא, and then afterwards he is in doubt whether he ate the one or the other, or whether he did the prohibited or allowed action etc. In such a case it is not necessary that — as another opinion there demands — it is possible to decide the doubt by examining the remaining uneaten piece, אפשר לברר איסורא, but the obligation to bring an אשם תלוי arises even in a case where, for instance, a non-Jew had eaten one of the pieces and he the other, so that although איקבע איסורא it is certain that one piece was חלב it is not possible לברר איסודא. This would make the literal way of taking the wording of our text even more precise. It does not say that he has done something, and does not know whether perhaps he has thereby sinned, but that he has done something sinful, unlawful, and does not know (i. e., whether after all it was not a lawful act). The “unlawful” was there before him איקבע איסורא (or as it is often expressed אתחזק איסורא), and it is only by the fact of the presence of the “lawful” also’, that the unlawfulness of his act is not sure. We think we may translate the ולא ידע by “he is uncertain”, which, after all is also nothing else but a negative knowing.

V. 18. בערכן: also כסף שקלים similar to the אשם מעילה mentioned above in V. 15 (Kerithoth 22b). — וכפר וגו׳ אשר שגג והוא לא ידע וגו׳. The אשם תלוי only atones for what is not known, the doubt. If afterwards he gets to know for certain that he did commit the sin, so that now he knows for certain that he has done an action that if done במזיד is punishable with כרת, then he has to bring the prescribed חטאת. If this certainty becomes known to him before he has brought his אשם תלוי, he does not have to bring it. But if the uncertainty was still present at the moment of זריקה, the offering is to be considered as brought בחובה and proceeded with, and completed as such. (Kerithoth 23b).

V. 20—26. These verses treat of אשם גזלה, the offering to be brought by a man who has denied on oath a justified claim for reparation, and later admits that his oath was false. In such a case he has to return the object itself, or if that is not possible, or the whole case deals only with a claim for money, the value of the claim plus an “external” fifth, i.e., one quarter of the same (see V. 16) and then has to bring an אשם.

כי תחטא ומעלה מעל בה׳. Any dishonesty in affairs between man and man is considered as a breach of faith towards God. God, is the שליש, as the ת״כ puts it, is the invisible third party Who is present everywhere where one man has dealings with his fellowman, even if there are no other witnesses present. God is the guarantee for honesty in intercourse and business. And in a case like ours here, where a fact has been denied, and this Guarantee has been called upon, it is no longer a simple case of ordinary בגידה, but the defence has pledged his relation to God for the honesty of his case, and then this calling on God has turned out to be nought but a hollow mask, then the most appropriate appellation that could be applied is: — מעילה (see note on V. 14).

כחש .וכחש verwandt mit כעס. Wie כעס die wirkliche und begründete Entrüstung über uns gegenüber gezeigte oder geäußerte Ungebühr bedeutet, so dürfte כחש die erkünstelte Entrüstung bedeuten, durch welche wir eine uns gestellte berechtigte Zumutung als Ungebühr zurückweisen. Daher כחש ב־: eine berechtigte Forderung ableugnen. Daher denn überhaupt: einer berechtigten Erwartung nicht entsprechen, בשרי כחש משמן (Ps. 109, 24) כחש מעשה זית (Habakuk 13, 16) בני נכר יכחשו לי (Ps. 18, 48) hieße dann: sie weisen den Vorwurf der Feindseligkeit mit erkünstelter Entrüstung zurück. Nur in den beiden Stellen: למען כחש (Secharja 13, 4) und כחש לו (Kön. I. 13, 18) scheint כחש einfache Täuschung zu bedeuten.

תשומת יד .בפקדון או בתשומת יד וגו׳ is “that which has been placed in the hand”, i.e., something which has been given to somebody to “use”, given as a loan, הלואה. Examples are given of the different ways in which other peoples’ property comes to be in one’s possession. פקדון and תשומת יד are examples of property which came into possession of the defendant with the full knowledge and will of the plaintiff; גזל, that which came with the full knowledge, but against his will; עשק, an unpaid claim on the property of the defendant of which he has knowledge, e.g., wages which have not been paid; אבדה, property which has found its way by itself into the possession of the defendant, which the plaintiff possibly even only surmises to be there. They are all only examples, and include all demands which if the defendant freely admits them would entail payment on his part, i.e., ממון, actual value, but not קנס, not penalties imposed, as מודה בקנס פטור (see on Ex. 22,3), but only of such objects concerning which a judical oath can be taken, i.e., excluding קרקעות ועבדים and שטרות, and also הקדש, which anyway is excluded by עמיתו (see Ex. 29,1).

This oath, called שבועת הפקדון can have been made either in court or outside it, either privately as a free-willed gesture of denial by the defendant, or as a result of the demand of the plaintiff in court. More, even if the claimant presses his claim by an oath, the denial by the defendant is in this case considered as perjury. The אשם וחומש mentioned here are imposed both in cases of complete conscious and intentional מזיד and of partial שוגג but not in cases of complete שוגג of שוגג גרידה, not when the one who takes the oath is unaware of the actual falsity of what he is swearing to, or is ignorant of the unlawfulness of a false oath, in accordance with the general fundamental principle האדם בשבועה (see above on V. 4).

V. 23. והיה כי יחטא ואשם. In Numb. 5,5, to complete this law, the case is given when the justified claimant has died and, being a גר, has no heirs to whom the guilty party could pay the debt, גזל הגר. There, in V. 7 it says והתודו את חטאתם, and that establishes the law that this duty of bringing an אשם and adding the חומש only occurs as a result of free confession of guilt. If he is convicted of the perjury by witnesses, he has not to seek atonement by אשם and חומש. He has only to pay the simple קרן, the actual value of the claim he had denied — in the case of פקדון he has to pay כפל as טוען טענת גנב (see Ex. 22,6 & 7 and Shebuoth 48a) — and with regards to his sin of false swearing he comes under the full weight of the threatened punishment on Sinai לא ינקה ה׳. It is in this sense that we have translated the ואשם and אשמתו of V. 23 & 24. (“And it shall be, if he is guilty of sin and knows himself burdened with guilt then he must return” etc., and in V. 24, ביום אשמתו, “on the day he confesses his guilt” I.L.).

והשיב את הגזלה אשר גזל: If the article is still there in the same condition, he has to return it “in natura”, but if it has already been essentially and permanently altered שנוי שאינו חוזר לבריותו, then he has to pay the value in money והשיב את הגזלה, מה ת״ל אשר גזל, אם כעין שגזל יחזיר ואם לאו דמים בעלמא בעי שלומי (B. K. 67a). Also the אשר גזל limits the payment of the חומש to his own robbery, but if an heir has to restore property his late father had robbed — על גזל אביו — he does not have to pay the חומש (ibid).
