V. 24. וחמשתיו in the plural, it can happen that he has to pay several fifths. If, for instance, he has repeatedly refuted by oath a claim which proves to be a justified one (B. K. 65b); or if he takes an oath that he does not owe a “fifth” which he already does owe (ibid 103).

הגוזל את חבירו שוה פרוטה ונשבע לו יוליכנו אחריו למדי :לאשר הוא לו יתננו “he who has robbed his neighbour, even if only to the value of a peruta, and has sworn falsely regarding the claim, must travel as far as to Media to restore it to him” (B. K. 103a). He can not seek atonement by bringing an offering of an אשם and חומש until he has seen to it that the robbed article, about which he has sworn falsely, has been returned into hands of its rightful owner personally.
V. 25. בערכך. Two shekels as in the preceding ונסלח לו .אשם. See remarks on V. 6.

Just as טומאת מקדש וקדשיו ,שמיעת הקול and שבועת בטוי with which this chapter began, formed a special group, picked out from all other laws to bring a special offering, קרבן עולה ויורד, so does the chapter close with three other laws, שבועת הפקדון ,ספק ,מעילה, again picked out from all other sins to have to bring a special offering, the אשם. As they find their atonement through this same אשם these sins must stand, in their inner essential nature, in close relation to each other.

If we consider these three sins and look for a factor which is common to them all we find that all three of them fall under the category of a careless attitude of mind towards the legality of our actions and possessions. מעילה, the unintentional profane disposal or use of a holy object dedicated to God, can only occur if we do not keep profane and holy objects which may be in our possession sufficiently apart from each other, and fail to make some clearly recognizable sign to which their holy and dedicated nature entitles them. מעילה is a thoughtless enrichment of oneself at the expense of the Mikdosh (— giving away or lending a holy object is also such an enrichment, we dispose of the property of the Mikdosh as if it were our own property —). The case of ספק, doubt, whether we have sinned or not, for which the אשם תלוי has to be brought, likewise arises from a similar careless attitude of mind, towards the Torah in its most serious demand — demands to which the punishment of כרת is attached. The carelessness is shown to an even greater degree when the אשם has to be brought on account of ,איקבע איסודא חתיכה אחת בין שתי חתיכות. Such unsolved doubt can only arise if the conscientiousness which we should exercise towards the Torah has not led us to keep that which is permitted and that which is prohibited strictly apart from each other. We allow permitted and forbidden to be so close to each other that they can quite easily be interchanged, or we allow ourselves to do work just at the border line where permission and prohibition touch, whereas respect for the Torah should so rule the whole of our life that no action of our should border on the prohibited. The ספק of אשם תלוי is a thoughtless enrichment of oneself at the expense of the Torah. The case of שבועת פקדון for which one has to bring an אשם גזלה is a point-blank God-derisive enrichment of oneself at the expense of one’s fellow-man. This way of looking at them makes it understandable that אשם מעילה and אשם תלוי are bracketed together in one paragraph, while אשם גזלה is introduced as a separate speech of God. Both of the former arise from a culpable carelessness in not keeping the holy apart from the profane, the permitted from the prohibited. But the sin for which an אשם גזלה has to be brought is a conscious and intentional enrichment of oneself by prohibited means. This idea of “enrichment” is also quite in accordance with the law that אשם גזלה has to be brought for the rejection on oath of only such demands which, in the event of the defendant admitting the claim, would have resulted in his having to pay, but not for a claim for קנס where a free admission of liability would absolve from payment. So that שבועת הפקדון is not to be taken simply as the sin of swearing falsely — for which it would come under the heading of שִבועת בטוי — but as the sin of enriching oneself by means of a false oath. In the same way פגם ולא נהנה is not מעילה.

If we compare the preceding עולה ויורד group with this אשם group, we find that it is the same three factors, which there in the sphere of ידיעה, the mind which forms the Jewish personality, and here in the רשות, in the sphere of the use of the powers of such personality, which are to be maintained and kept clear from being imperiled. The parallel מעילה בקדשי ה׳ and טומאת מקדש וקדשיו, and between שבועת הפקדון and שמיעת הקול is at once apparent, but also that the ספק of אשם תלוי is parallel to שבועת בטוי seems in its deeper implication to be also clear. טומאת מקדש וקדשיו is to guard the basic principle of the Sanctuary and all that appertains to it, as a Truth guaranteed by God, for the minds of the Jewish People to guard it against being overcast and oppressed by that false conception that טומאה gives. In a similar way אשם מעילה is to protect the whole idea of the existence and meaning of the holy objects of God, as such, against being thoughtlessly encroached upon by our own powers of profane use. שמיעת הקול places — without any personal interest in the matter — the mind of every Jew in the service of the rights of his fellowman; שבועת הפקדון places the whole sphere of the use of power and of self-interest under the restrictions demanded by the rights of others. שבועת בטוי demand Truth in the inner source of human thinking and acting even בדבר רשות, in matters which in themselves are of no consequence and do not affect the interests of anybody; אשם תלוי demands clarity, in the sphere of external place and time of human actions and goods. So that it may be said that what the עולה ויורד group represents as being guaranteed by God, as unimpeachable for the personal aspect of the Jewish People, viz. Justice and Human Rights, Freedom of Will and Truth, are the same which the אשם group wishes to ensure in the sphere of the exercise of powers and interests.

And the respective offerings are quite in accordance with this. In חטאת the personality of the offender which has sunk in careless forgetfulness regains its position on the height of its spiritual moral calling. אשם, as the word literally implies, makes the Jew realise that in his sphere of exercising power and interests, he is threatened with desolation by his sinful ill-use of his powers. It shows him under which conditions alone, the Jew, who is called on to be an example in this sphere, can hope for a happy flourishing future.

If in this sphere of exercising his powers and his interests, a man has only thought of his own interests, and, in consequence, has carelessly placed the demands of the Mikdosh or of the Torah so much in the background, has allowed holy and profane, permitted and prohibited things to be at hand in such undistinguishable proximity, that he has come to have enriched himself at the expense of the Mikdosh; or has, with complete indifference, allowed his eating or his actions to have had the possibility of having transgressed the Torah or he has enriched himself with illegal ill-gotten possessions, and when justified claims for them have been made on his possessions, he has rejected them by mockingly swearing: “May God destroy all my possessions if this claim is a true one” ………………………

והיה כי יחטא ואשם. And if now he feels that, having “extinguished the Fire of the Divine Torah”, (the literal meaning of חטא I.L.) he has incurred the penalty of “desolation” (אשם) by having taken to himself a Peruta that belonged to the Mikdosh, taken or withheld a Peruta that rightly belonged to his neighbour and mocked at God thereby, or by carelessly and indifferently leaving his actions to chance, and thereby running the risk of having transgressed the Torah, he feels that he has removed the root and basis for the continuance of his own life of riches and possessions, then he has to approach God with an אשם, the expression of his being conscious of all this, and of his resolve to be more seriously attentive to these matters in future.

In this offering he represents himself by an איל. As has already been remarked on Ex. 29,1, the איל, the ram, which by reason of its strength and age, leads the rest of the flock, represents the well-to-do personality endowed with possessions and power. The relation of these three אשמות to the sphere of the posessions of the personality who is to be represented in them, is even more clearly brought to the fore by the requirement “בערכך״, that — as is the case in no other offering — the אשם must have a definite value, and must be worth at least שתי כסף.

אשם, like חטאת and עולה belongs to the category of קדשי קדשים and its שחיטה has likewise to be done בצפון. The procedure of the sacrifice of an אשם is partly like that of an עולה and partly like that of a חטאת. It has the עבודת הדם of an עולה i.e., זריקת שתי מתנות שהם ארבע למטה, but הקטרת אימורים ואכילת בשד לכהנים, like a חטאת. Although it comes to atone for transgressions, one can understand that אשם has not got the “sticking-fast-מתנות״ of the חטאת on the heights of the Altar, but the progress-making upward-striving זריקה of the עולה. For the whole essence of one’s duty in the sphere of material possessions, and the whole object of our being given material posessions, is to use them for assiduous efforts to make progress in life, as indeed its symbol in the Mikdosh, the שלחן consisting essentially of עץ, bears the character of continuous progressive thriving. The איל which has gone astray, the use of possessions and interests in the wrong direction, has to be atoned for, not by remaining static and inactive in the future, but by occupying itself in vigorous active progress, progress which is at the same time progressive striving upwards to the heights of Man’s spiritual calling. Hence the איל אשם has the זריקה of the עולה. But this is just the reason why it has הקטרת אימורים and אכילת בשר לכהנים of the חטאת. For this is exactly just what is to be driven home to him, that, if his material progress is to be nothing else but a moral spiritual striving upwards towards the heights of the Altar of the Divine Torah, then his חלב and כליות, his material aims and his material efforts themselves become לחם אשה ריח ניחוח לה׳, themselves become contributions for the increase of godliness on earth, and of giving God satisfaction with earthly matters. Even his own enjoyment of the results of the wealth he works for and acquires becomes priestly God-serving and holy, as the אכילת בשר איל אשם לכהנים teaches and preaches. By מעילה or by the possibility that, in the sphere of his possessions and activities, there can be a doubt as to the legality of his deeds, and certainly in the case where, accompanied by derision of God, he has retained or taken that to which he has no right, by any of these he has shown that he has not kept this sphere of his material interests within those bounds which God has set for our general behaviour with our possessions. He has not kept the use of his own possessions distinctly apart from the symbolically ideal possessions of God, he has not taken due care to avoid the possibility of committing major transgressions of the Law, he has not respected the social rights of his neighbour arising out of the conception of the equality of all (עמיתו, see Ch. 19,15 & 17). Instead of increasing or intensifying his material interests, such neglect and lack of consideration of the ideal demands of the Torah, such keeping the spiritual and material apart from each other in his life, only brings “desolation” to his material interests, the prospering of which is really dependent on his using them for the ideals of the Torah. So that when he approaches God in His Sanctuary as an איל שוה שתי כסף gives himself up בצפון, on the side of Material (שחיטה) and lets himself be taken up (קבלה) into the sphere of the Mikdosh, and from the Mikdosh receives the direction which his progress as an איל שתי כסף is to take in the future, and sees his חלב וכליות on the Altar, and his בשר being eaten in priestly enjoyment in the Mikdosh, from all this he learns: — That also as an איל שוה שתי כסף, as a man of possessions and in pursuit of possessions, he also is to stand within the Sanctuary of God; he is to give up even his material progress to the moral and spiritual working upwards to the Altar-heights of the Divine Ideal; that his material goal and efforts themselves are to be given up to the demands of God’s Will; and that if desolation is to be kept afar from the sphere of his material interests, the enjoyment of the results of his material activities itself must become priestly holy service of God, so that the blessing of God may give it stability and endurance.

In the case of אשם מעילה and of אשם גזלה, before an אשם may be brought, full restitution of the value of the loss, קרן, must be made to the Sanctuary, or to the person whose possessions have been violated, or to his heirs. But for כפרה an additional fifth of the value has to be added. We find the addition of such a fifth, here and also at זר שאכל תרומה (Levit 22,14) and when מעשר שני or הקדש is bought back by the בעלים (Levit. 27,13, 27 & 31). All these five cases have this in common, that they show the necessity of impressing upon ourselves, in its true light, the danger of thinking that we ourselves have some claim to something which is really holy property. (The possessions of our neighbour also became holy property at the moment when we received our mission from God). We have enriched the sphere of our own possessions at the expense of the Mikdosh; we have paid the value of it back; we are reminded by the חומש that, instead of endangering or taking to ourselves any of the interests of Mikdosh or of our fellowmen, it is really up to us to enlarge and enrich them out of our own possessions. The taking back for our own use (redeeming) something which we had dedicated to the Mikdosh has also the semblance of such endangering. Our taking back an object which we had decided to dedicate for holy use, allows it to appear, as if it was too good or too precious for this purpose. As we are allowed to take it back and give its value in cash to the Mikdosh, the addition of the חומש to its value counters any such derogatory conception of the dignity of the Mikdosh. Perhaps we can look on the חומש as a double tenth and that might then also explain the חומש מלבר which, as explained above, is actually a quarter. That our possessions belong to the carrying out of the ideas which the Mikdosh represents is expressed in the ordinary way, by giving up one tenth. This dedication of the tenth expresses the idea that we do not take unto ourselves any “ten”, i.e., any completed whole amount of what we gain, for our own exclusive use, without first having to think of the demands of the purposes of the Mikdosh. So מעשר בהמה ,מעשר עני ,מעשר שני ,מעשר ראשון. We do not call nine our own without having given one to the Mikdosh for them. When, as here, an encroachment on another’s rights has to be atoned for, this expression has to be doubled, then we do not call eight our own without having given two to the Mikdosh; but that is just חומש מלבר. This tells us, that, far from daring to harm the Mikdosh or our neighbours by taking their property for our own use, on the contrary we may never consider such a sum as we have deprived them of as being our own justified property without having given some of our own honestly gained possessions in addition to returning what belongs to them.

Out of the laws described above, there are two characteristic ones to which we would give further consideration. They seem to be related to each other, and to have an important bearing on our appreciation of what our attitude to the Divine Torah should be. We refer to the legal fact that an unintentional misuse of a holy object profanes it, whereas the intentional misuse does not do so but allows it to retain its character of holiness — הקדש בשוגג מתחלל, במזיד אינו מתחלל and further to the fact that — as remarked already in ת״כ — the necessity for atonement for a transgression, about which there is a doubt whether it has been committed at all or not, appears greater and more serious than that for a sin which has definitely been committed; for a ספק the offering must have a definitely high value, for a ודאי a minimum value suffices! (Zebachim 48a).

It is not direct opposition, not intentional sin, but indifference which the Jewish Sanctuary has to fear from its sons. That seems to be the thought that is expressed by the fact that הקדש בשוגג מתהלל, במזיד אינו מתחלל. Towards direct opposition the Mikdosh stands high and untouchable in holiness, the very fact that it is being consciously opposed, fought against, is itself a warrant of its holiness. But שגגה, indifference, careless forgetting the holiness of the Sanctuary and its justification to direct our actions, therein lies the grave of the holiness of the Sanctuary. For its throne, from which it is meant to direct and master and penetrate our lives, consists solely in those that acknowledge it, keeping it ever in mind.

And in the same way the keeping of the Torah is endangered to a far greater degree, where unsolved doubt can reign over transgressions which may have been done, than there, where, if transgression has been committed, it can be at once clearly ascertained. In what criminal careless lack of restraint must the whole sphere of man’s acts, possessions, person and times be allowed to waver indiscriminately, without the slightest consideration for the Will of God’s Torah, where the possibility of the case of doubt of the אשם תלוי (Kerithoth 17a & b) can find a place.

In the opinion of an overwhelming majority of our teachers, the Laws of Prohibition of the Torah directly include the prohibition of doubtful cases: ספק דאוריתא מדאוריתא לחומרא, so that not only ספק חתיכה משתי חתיכות where איקבע איסורא and an אשם תלוי is required, but also e.g., חתיכה אחת ספק חלב ספק שומן, would be prohibited by the Torah itself. According to רמב״ם however, a ספק which is not איתחזק איסורא and would not require an אשם תלוי would not be included in the actual prohibition, but be prohibited מדרבנן לחומרא. But even then the duty of keeping afar from every possibility of transgressing the Torah and of not slipping into doubt, lies within the orbit of that general duty with which the Torah places the responsibility for the carrying out of its Laws upon our own conscientiousness, and expects us to make our own precautionary measures to guard them (see note on Ex. 23,13). And indeed, if a doubt of our having transgressed the Torah through lack of care does — as the אשם תלוי chapter teaches — “burden us with sin” and threaten the whole sphere of our activities with “desolation”, then the consideration of the seriousness of the Torah and of one’s own future happiness, will see to it that the conscientiousness which should regulate all our actions extends not only to the avoidance of actual sin, but also to everything that might lead to it. Such conscientiousness may be expressed in the words of Eliphaz (Job. 5,24). “Woulds’t thou know that Peace characterises thy home, then regulate thy habitation so that thou sinnest not” וידעת כי שלום אהלך ופקדת נוך ולא תחטא.

V. 1. The preceding Chapters I—V present the various categories of offerings, the voluntary ones קרבנות נדבה viz., עולה ,מנחה ,שלמים and those ordered for people seeking atonement for sins committed, the קרבנות חובה viz., חטאת and אשם. They describe the various kinds of offerings and procedures from the point of view of those that bring them seeking to get nearer to God. Now, in this, and the succeeding chapter, further important complementary laws are given, which for the greater part primarily concern the ministering priests, which is why they are specially addressed to אהרן ובניו. This consideration also fixes a different order in the sequence, which here is based not on the motive for bringing them, נדבה or חובה, but on the degree of their sanctity, קדשי קדשים and קדשים קלים, hence, first ,עולה חטאת ,מנחה ,ואשם, and then שלמים.

V. 2. זאת תורת העולה. This complementary teaching of the handling by the Priests of the offerings given over to them, begins with the laws governing that time in the Mikdosh when it is given over exclusively to the Priests and closed to the rest of the Nation — the time of Night. The whole of the regulations for the offerings concludes in Ch. 7,37 & 38 with the words:— זאת התורה לעולה למנחה וגר׳ אשר צוה ה׳ את משה בהר סיני ביום צותו את בני ישראל להקריב את קרבניהם לה׳ במדבר סיני While it is the place במדבר סיני, where the Children of Israel had to bring their first offerings to God, which this concluding verse evidently stresses, the Halacha quite specially stresses the time as well; the time in which the Mitzva of getting near to God by bringing offerings was given to the Children of Israel. It was ביום צותו, it was “day” when they received this command. Just as the Word of God itself differentiates sharply between the prophecy of Moses, the transmitter of His Torah, from that of all other prophets: פה אל פה אדבר בו ומראה ולא בחידות, that the Word did not come to him by means of a condition of twilight-like dream, not בחלום אדבר בו but to the lucid intelligence of a clear fully-awake man. (Numbers 12,6 & 7); so, in the same way it is to the intelligence of a clear fully awake man, that Moses was to bring the Word of God, and so, in the same way, the Halacha teaches, it is lucid, clear, fully awake Man with his wakeful, clear thinking and free-willed mind, who is to come near God with the expression of dedicating himself to carrying out His Laws. אשד צוה ה׳ ת״ב) .את משה בהר סיני ביום צותו למדנו לכל הקרבנות שאין כשרים אלא ביום on Ch. 7,38; Megilla 20b). All הקרבנות, all approach to God with an offering may only be done by day. (See Rashi Megilla ibid).

Night — לילה, the time when things are “confusedly mixed up” — the time when Man, too, sinks back into the realm of things bound by physical forces, Night is the time that brings the heathen mind nearer to his gods. The heathen then feels the might of the gods which bind him, as it does all other creatures, and Day — יום, the time of “upright existence” (קום) — in which man feels himself, and enters the fight to conquer the physical world, is to the heathen mind nothing else but the time of Man’s fight with the gods. Along directly opposite lines is the Jewish mind to run according to the Word of God. Not just when he has to succumb to his night existence is he first to feel the might of his God; with a clear mind and with the productive world-forcing power of his upstanding day-life is he, above all, to stand near to his God. The light of his clear mind, the energy of his free will, and the accomplishments of his productive work, the whole of his free personality establishing itself to the highest degree of power in his daily life, is to him a gift from his one unique God. He is to recognise that, out of the infinite fulness of His spirit which fills the world with His Thoughts, out of His holy completely free-willed creative Power, God has breathed a tiny spark into him, and thereby has raised him high above the state of being bound by the merely physical world, and has made him stand upright, in His likeness, as a personality freely mastering the world, in His service for His purposes. And it is just in using this free personal achievements of daily work that a man carries out the Will of his God, that he accomplishes the service of God for His world. The Day in the heathen’s mind is a battle of mortals against the power of the gods. The day, to the Jew, is the time for accomplishment, in the service of, and to give satisfaction to, his God. Hence in the Jewish Sanctuary of God, it is not the night which drags the day too into the grave of morality, but it is the day which elevates the night too, with it, into the eternity of its life in the proximity of God. Not היום הולך אתר הלילה, but הלילה הולך אחר היום. It is not physical nature, which is the mediator between the Jew and his God, but raised above physical nature, he stands directly before his God. במדבר, in the wilderness, where a man has nothing else but himself, God accordingly came near to Israel, there established the bond of His Torah with him, and there, במדבר, where a man has nothing to offer God but himself, all that he bears in his own living personality, there God first told him to bring the offering of his submission. It is the free-willed personality, of its own free will submitting its thinking, its desiring, its accomplishments, to God, which is bound by God’s Torah; it is the free-willed personality, of its own free will submitting its thinking, its desires, its accomplishments to God, from whom God’s offerings are expected: זאת התורה לעולה למנחה ולחטאת ולאשם ולמלואים ולזבח השלמים אשר צוה ה׳ את משה בהר סיני ביום צותו את בני ישראל להקריב את קרבניהם לה׳ במדבר סיני.

“ביום צותו״ — “The offering, at the time it was commanded”, so runs the short norm by which the Halacha limits all הקרבנות on every occasion to the daytime. It is a norm, the spirit of which we meet in other laws concerning offerings and which is in close and deep relationship to the antithesis of all טומאה, the מקדש. Here, this norm only comes into consideration by the limitation which is imposed by היא העולה על מוקדה כל הלילה. For ,תנופה ,שחיטה ,סמיכה הקטרת קומץ ,קמיצה ,הגשה — (קמיצה is parallel in meaning to שחיטה, and הקטרת קומץ to זריקה, see above II,2) — זריקה והזיה ,קבלה ,מליקה, the procedure is limited to the daytime, for which we find special indication in the text referring to them. All procedures, accordingly, which are to bring the offering, and thereby the personality represented by it, (or some special part of it representing some special quality of the bringer) afresh into renewed relationship to God and His Torah, all that is comprised by הקרבה in its wider sense, have to be performed exclusively by day. It follows from the sentence in our text היא העולה על מוקדה כל הלילה, that all that for which כפרה has already been achieved by the הקרבות and which only have to represent on the Altar the further consequences of such הקרבות can be given over to the Altar-fire כל הלילה עד הבקר, the whole night until daybreak. This would also teach that if פקעו, if they have slipped off the Fire, they have to be replaced. (All this applies to such procedures as הקטרת חלבים ואיברים, the burning of the parts of the עולה, and the kidneys and fat of the חטאת, the אשם and the שלמים, which are all to be understood under the idea of that which is brought up on the “burning top” of the Altar עולה על מוקדה). For night, and the night-phase of human life, is not to be considered as a realm away from God, and that it is only day and day-life which is in connection with God. “Night as well as Day is His”. Just as He is יוצר אור, “the Former of Light”, so is He בורא חשך, “the Creator of Darkness”. It is only the contrary idea that is to be negatived, the idea that it is just the dark night-side of life that turns to God, and that it is just for the dark night side of life that one seeks God. The idea is only to be stressed that יום, the time when Man is “upstanding” and alert, when his mind is awake and he is active and working and independent, that time is to be in the foreground; and in that time and with that phase of his life, the nearness to God is to be sought, and the nearness to God to be approached.

But, when a human personality in all its upstanding independence has found God again, and in day ביום, in קבלה וזריקה ,שחיטה, has given up its whole being to God and to the Sanctuary of His Torah, then the “day-dedication” of his human being comprehends the night phases with it in the bond of consecration to God, then הלילה הולך אחר היום, then the earthly sun never sets for it, then it remains in the proximity of God throughout the nights; and the חלבים and the איברים, “the aims and efforts” and the “achievements” of the נפש which has struggled upwards to the nearness of God with its “day”, remains also in the “night”, nutriment for the Divine Satisfaction, on God’s Altar.

Hence even those things which have to be given over to the Altar-fire which are not to be taken as the result of nearness to God having been already achieved, but must be considered as themselves achieving it, and so must be done by day, such as הקומץ והלבונה והקטרת ומנחת כתנים ומנחת כהן משיח ומנחת נסכים שדרכן ליקרב ביום, may be done quite near sunset, though they would only be completely consumed by the Fire during the night, מעלוי ומקטירין עם בא השמש ומתעכלין והולכין כל הלילה, as is expressed in the generalising introductory words זאת תורת העולה, which extends the staying on the hearth of the Altar during the night to everything which has come on the hearth of the Altar (Menachoth 26b). This attaching the night to the preceding day and its accomplished getting near to God, is such an essential conception for all procedures in the Mikdosh, that everything which should have been given over to the Altar-fire during the night and this had not been done during the whole of the night, becomes disqualified for the Altar at the break of a new Mikdosh day, and may no longer be placed on the Altar-fire: שלן מחוץ למזבח is פסול לינה.

Can we perhaps take it that מוקדה which here refers to the “hearth on the Altar at night” is written with a small מ expressing the smallness of the place, just to indicate this dependent state of the night on the preceding day? That which takes place on the top of the מוקדה is only a pendant of and complementary to, that which has taken place at its base or on its sides, — ?.

From the implication of the sentence היא העולה על מוקדה על המזבח כל הלילה, the rule is also derived that everything which has once been placed on the Altar has to remain there. While the היא referring back to the normal עולה of the preceding chapter would restrict this rule to normal offerings which have been brought in accordance with the prescribed laws, the generalisation term זאת תודת העולה, extends it to everything which can be comprised under the idea of עולה. Hence the canon results: המזבח מקדש הראוי לו, i.e., בל הראוי לאשים אם עלה לא ירד, that anything that had once been destined for the Altar-fire הראוי לאשים even if afterwards became פסול and so was unfit to have been brought, if it had nevertheless been placed on the Altar, it has to remain there. The only condition for this canon to apply is that it must be פסולו בקדש. But such פסולים whose פסולן was not בקדש such as רובע ונרבע מוקצה ונעבד etc. אין הקדש מקבלו, i.e., אפילו עלו ירדו (Zebachim 83, 84). These rules, ensuring the sanctifying effect of the Mikdosh being all-embracing (with the mentioned exceptions which the Mikdosh rejects altogether) have been gone into and explained on Ex. 29,37.

The Service of the Altar was accordingly closed for the acceptance of fresh offerings at sunset. But the Altar fire on the top of the Altar was active throughout the night כל הלילה, to complete the offerings of the day as fuel to keep godliness on earth alive, עד הבקר, until day dawned, ואש המזבח תוקד בו, and then the Altar-fire was to be kindled afresh for the beginning of the service of the new day. In Ch. 1,7 reference was already made to this kindling and keeping of the Fire on the Altar, there we have already tried to establish its more detailed laws and the thoughts which were expressed by them. (Refer back to those notes. I.L.). There were three separate fires, מערכות, laid: מערכה גדולה, the one here called מוקדה, the real Altar-fire for the acceptance of offerings as fuel for the אש דת, “the Fire of the Law” to be ריח ניחוח לה׳. And, apart from this, the אש המזבח, a second fire: מערכה שניה של קטרת, was laid in the southwest corner, from which glowing coals were taken for bringing the קטרת on the inner Altar in the היכל (see on V. 6); and finally מערכה של קיום האש, a third fire simply to express the idea of the Fire on the Altar to be kept incessantly burning, and never allowed to be extinguished, in accordance with the verse והאש על המזבח תוקד בו לא תכבה.

V. 3. But before the Fire of the new day was laid and lit, the ritual of תרומת הדשן — the “lifting up” ordered in this verse — had to be performed. This act of תרומת הדשן does not belong to the preparation of the Altar for the service of the new day just beginning, this is done by the הוצאת הדשן prescribed in the next verse. תרומת הדשן is rather to be considered as the final conclusion of the service of the preceding day. It is an עבודה in itself, and may only be done by a כהן כשד in complete priestly vestments. Just as in V. 8, speaking of the מנחה, it says: והרים ממנו מקומצו, so here the והרים את הדשן is the lifting out of a קומץ of the ashes of the offering-fire. After the priest had clothed himself in the vestments of the Mikdosh, he lifted a whole handful of the ashes out of the offering-fire of the day which was then ending, ושמו אצל המזבח, and laid it down “deliberately, to be left completely there and not scattered” — ,ושמו בנחת ושמו כולו, ושמו שלא יפזר, — on the east side, next to the ramp of the Altar, (Yoma 23b & 24a; Tamid 63a; Temura 34a). Just as the קומץ of the מנחה serves as אזכרה for the whole, that it may be remembered before God, so may this קומץ of the תרומת הדשן have been laid down as a remembrance of the devotion represented by the sacrifices of the past day to God and to His holy Torah, and indeed, במזרח, primarily for the permanent consciousness of the Nation.. It would give the idea, as the introduction to the service of the day, that:—To-day brings no new mission, it has only to carry out, ever afresh, the mission that yesterday too was to accomplish. The very last Jewish grandchild stands there, before God, with the same mission of life that his first ancestors bore, and every day adds to all its predecessors in the whole passing of the centuries, his contribution to the solution of the task given to all generations of the House of Israel. The Jewish “To-day” has to take its mission from the hand of its “Yesterday”. If, then, תרומת הדשן is related to and has a similar meaning to the קומץ המנחה, that might be the explanation of the wish expressed in Ps. 20,4: יזכר כל מנחתיך ועולתו ירשנה סלה, “May He take the אזכרה of all your מנחות and the תרומת הדשן (actually literally דשן) of your עולה״, i.e., May the remembrance of all your acts of allegiance to Him, and your efforts to elevate yourselves up to Him, be constantly in God’s mind. If this way of taking the meaning of the depositing of the תרומת הדשן as the reminder of the permanence of that which was dedicated to God on the previous day is not erroneous, then we can also understand the apparent exception of תרומת הדשן to the general rule that כל שנעשה מצותו אין בו משום מעילה, that once an object has fulfilled its purpose, all the prohibition of using it for profane purposes ceases. For תרומת הדשן remains קדש even after the prescribed מצוה of depositing it has been carried out, and making any use of these ashes is מעילה (Pesachim 26a, see above Ch. 5,15 et seq.) But in its deeper meaning the purpose of this lifting out of the ashes is not completed with just depositing it. If its meaning is the remembrance of the past for all the future, it has a never ending קדושה.

מדו בד. Yoma 23b takes מדו to refer primarily to the כתנת, the robe that covered the whole body down to the feet, and by מדו, the law to be indicated that it must be כמדתו, “made to measure”, not too short but also not too long. Its purpose is to cover the body, not to add dignity by its appearance. Therefore it may not be too short but not also too long. A trailing train for instance, would give it quite another meaning. בד, see note on Ex. 28,43. שלא יהא דבר חוצץ בינו לבשרו :ילבש על בשרו, directly on the body, so that nothing of any other nature intervenes between the garment and the body it is to clothe (Zebachim 19a). The meaning of the priestly garb is not primarily outwards for the eye of the beholder but inwards for the mind of the priest himself. By it his body is to receive and be given up to, the character of purity that is demanded by the Mikdosh (see ibid). Only מכנסים and כתונת are mentioned, but the complete vestments of the priests, i.e., אבנט and מגבעת too, are necessary (Yoma 23b).

Regarding the time for תרומת הדשן, the continuity of verses 2 & 3 teach that הקטרה as well as הרמה is allowable during the whole of the night. Only the new מערכה has to wait for the morning. Nevertheless the first half of the night, before midnight, is the time preferably for הקטרה, after midnight preferably for הרמה. Hence the Halacha runs: “pieces which are still quite untouched by the fire”, איברים שיש בהן ממש, and have fallen out of the fire must be put back on to the fire even after midnight, those which are quite black and burnt need not be replaced even before midnight, but שרידין, pieces which are half burnt, חצות עושה עיכול, depend on midnight, before midnight they have to be put back, but after that, it is considered that they have done their mitzva, they need not be replaced and hence אין מועלין בהן as כל דבר שנעשה מצותו וגוי, (Zebachim 86 & Yoma 20a).

Usually, תרומת הדשן was performed round about קריאת הגבר either a little before or just after. קריאת הגבר is also used elsewhere as a term for cock-crow, but here, it is the cry of the herald: — עמדו כהנים לעבודתכם ולוים לדוכנכם וישראל למעמדכם. On י״כ it was done after midnight, on the רגלים already after the first watch of the night, and then at the time of קריאת הגבר, the whole עזרה was already full of the crowd who came with their offerings (Yoma 20a).

V. 4. בגדים אחרים, also בגדי כהונה but פחותים, of smaller value than those worn for the הרמה which themselves could be, perhaps should be, שחקים, older, more worn out, than ordinary daily garments of the priests were allowed to be (Yoma 23b & 12b and מל״מ on הל׳ תמידין ומוספין ב׳ י׳). The הוצתא הדשן prescribed here, the clearing of the hearth from all the remains of the preceding day to make it ready for the service of the new day (the parts of offerings which had not been consumed by the Fire were laid at the side of the great pile) is most probably also an עבודה, a procedure of the Service of the Offerings (see מל״מ ibid). (The fact that it has to be done in priestly garments seems to confirm this too. I.L.). If תרומת הדשן is to introduce the service of the young new day with reference back to that which had been accomplished on the previous day, הוצאה would, on the other hand, contrastingly express the thought, that nevertheless every fresh day brings the whole Jewish mission to be accomplished afresh. Fresh, as if nothing had yet been accomplished, does the beginning of every new day, call us to go to our mission with full new devotion and sacrifice, and nothing that has already been done may lessen the energy with which we go to do our duty. The thought of what has already been accomplished can be the death of that which is still to be accomplished. Woe unto him who, with smug self-complacency thinks he can rest on his laurels, on what he has already achieved, and who does not meet the task of every fresh day with full fresh devotion as if it were the first day of his life’s work! והוציא את הדשן, every trace of yesterday’s sacrifice is to be removed from the hearth on the Altar, so that the service of the new day can be started on completely fresh ground. Under these considerations, the law, that occupation with the achievements of the previous day, הוצאה, and indeed הרמה too, should be done in worn-out, less valuable garments, gets its understandable meaning. The past is to be there and not forgotten, but it is to be retired to the background, and is not to invest us with pride before the fresh task to which each new day calls us.

It is doubtful whether the ashes have to be carried outside the city every day. Every day they were removed from the hearth to the centre of the Altar to a ball, the so-called תפוח, “apple”, and from there they were taken outside the City; according to some opinions only when the תפוח had grown too large (see מל״מ ibid 13). In Tamid 28b it is recorded that the תפוח once reached the dimensions of כשלש מאות כור (some 2520 cu. feet) of ashes (but this is supposed to be a גוזמה, an exaggeration. I.L.). On the רגלים they liked to leave the תפוח as a נוי למזבח.

According to רמב״ם (ibid 51) the ashes of the offerings which were taken outside the city had to be carefully deposited on a place where they were protected from being scattered, and they too are included in the persisting קרש-character of the תרומת הדשן to which מעילה applies. (In the Jeshurun Vol. I. p. 549, an account is given of the analysis of the recently discovered layer of ashes in the soil just outside Jerusalem. These ashes were definitely of animal and not mineral origin. Most probably these are ashes from the שפך הדשן ordered in our verse here, and so after thousands of years bring us remembrances of the offerings of our ancestors!).
אל מתוץ למחנה אל מקום טהור. See note on Ch. 4,12.
V. 5. והאש על המזבח תוקד בו. See note on V. 2. ובער עליה הכהן, see note on Ch. 1,7. בבקר בבקר is according to Yoma 33a, an intensification of the idea, in the morning: in the very early morning.

וערד עליה העולה וגו׳. As explained in Ch. 1,7, the Fire burning on the top of the Altar expressed the demand that all phases of individual and national life be given up as “fuel for the אש דת״, i.e., for the realisation of the Torah. The understanding of this demand and its being taken to heart, is expressed by the Tamid offering. This, as the first and continuous daily offering which the nation was commanded to bring, (see Ex. 29,38) in which the whole object of the building and sanctity of the Mikdosh is summarised, is accordingly the one with which the daily Service of offerings has to begin. This Tamid offering is “the עולה״, par excellence. Hence Pesachim 58b: מנין שלא יהא דבר קודם לתמיד של שחר, תלמוד לומר וערד עליה העולה מאי תלמודא אמר רבא העולה עולה ראשונה. We believe, that it is having regard to this quotation, the regulation that it must be the first offering of the day, that the Tamid offering is called ראשונה. (Perhaps Rashi too, whose words there, as they stand, are difficult, is to be understood in this way?).

Now it does not say והקטיר עליה העולה, as it does immediately afterwards והקטיר עליה חלבי השלמים, but וערך עליה העולה והקטיר וגוי. From this is inferred that in the same way as the burning pile of logs formed a base for the Tamid, וערכו עצים על האש) מערכה, Ch. 1,7), so did the עולה form a base for all the succeeding offerings. ומנין שאין דבר קרב אחר תמיד של בין הערבים ת״ל והקטיר עליה חלבי השלמים: no other offering may be brought after the evening Tamid which closes the daily service of offerings for we learn עליה שלמים but ולא על חברתה שלמים, or as רבא expresses the Halacha, punning on the word עליה השלם כל הקרבנות ,השלמים. But, inasmuch as the Tamid-offering begins and ends the Service of Offerings on the Altar, and all other offerings, including private individual ones, like שלמים are sandwiched between them, the whole of the Service on the Altar takes on the appearance of the idea of a continuous national offering. It, the עולת תמיד של צבור, the uninterrupted continuous dedication of the activities of the nation, is the impetus with which everything begins, and in which everything ends. All other phases of the national life and of the individual lives find their foundation, their raison-d’etre on it, and it finds its realisation in them. עולת תמיד של צבור: unceasingly to struggle upwards with all the forces and abilities inherent in the Nation, upwards to the height of the ideal taught by the Torah, and thereby to prepare a place on earth on which the satisfaction of God can rest — such is the meaning of every Jewish day. In happy dedication to the achievement of this goal, the very last loneliest hut in Israel finds its national importance. Dedication of the activities of the nation, העולה ראשונה, that is the foundation and the goal of the whole; והקטיר עליה חלבי השלמים: and on it and in it “the efforts and aim for happiness in life” are to be spent. The dedication, the consecration of the Nation with everything that lives and strives within the bosom of each individual, that is the meaning of Israel before God, as is represented by the morning and evening Tamid-offering with all the other offerings in between. — There is only one offering which has to come after the closing offering of the day, the Pessach (Pessachim 59a). That offering with which year by year the Nation steps back again into those anxious moments when it was awaiting the hour of the birth of its national existence; and, with the united Pessach-devotedness and readiness for sacrifice of every one of its members, has to go to meet the night in which the alternative of death and slavery or life and freedom was decided for them and — tarrying for the fresh renewal of such devotedness and readiness for sacrifice — is to be decided for them.

V. 6. אש תמיד תוקד וגו׳. With the preceding verses the fitting up and arrangements for the Fire on the Altar for the requirements of the Service on it are completed, and even the regulation for the offerings to be brought on it prescribed. From this, the Halacha is derived (Yoma 45b) that, with this verse which goes beyond the requirements of the offering-altar, the law is given that, all and every fire, the fire for the incense-altar (already referred to in V. 2) as well as that for the נר תמיד of the מנורה, and even the glowing coals that were taken on יום הכפורים into the Holy of Holies with the קטרת, all had to be taken from the offering-altar in the עזרה. Looking at the cantilation according to which the לא תכבה is an addition to the word המזבח, the translation should run: “Fire shall continuously be kindled on the Altar, where it is never extinguished”. So there is only one place where the Divine Torah allows its Fire to shine, from where and whereon all other fire in the Mikdosh, even the Fire of the קטרה-ideal, even the Light of the מנורה-spirit; more, even the Fire of the highest devotion on יום הכפורים receives its origin and existence. The highest inspiration, the deepest enthusiasm of life in the Jewish idea, has its roots in the dedication of one’s activities to the Torah, and makes this the inexorable preliminary. Without אש של עולה על מזבח החיצון there is no life on the מזבח הזהב, on the מנורה or בין הבדים in front of the Cherubim-sanctuary. Without sacrifice on the altar of duty there is no elevation of mind, no illumination of spirit, no soaring to the ideal of the Torah which rests under the Cherubim.

V. 7. וזאת תודת המנחה. These too are laws, partly generalising, partly repetition, to make all the details an absolute necessity, partly supplementary to the laws already given regarding the מנחה offering. Generalising, as e.g., in V. 9, the assigning of the שירי מנחה to the priests in all cases of Menachoth of which only a קומץ is burnt on the Altar, i.e., also for מנחת חוטא which is not expressly stated in Ch. 5,12 (Menachoth 72,b); by repetition, the כשדות is made dependent on the whole process being done in all its parts שנה הכתוב לעכב, that it is not only for מצוה but if anything is missing it renders the whole Mincha פסול e.g., the addition of the incense prescribed in Ch. 2,2 and repeated here in V. 8, so that the Halacha is: הקומץ והלבונה מעכבין זה את זה (Menachoth 27a); supplementary: e.g., the קביעת מקום fixing the place for the הגשה in verse 7: לפני ה׳ אל פני המזבח which is missing in Ch. 2,8 above; also extending the prohibition of חמץ to the שירי מנחה in vv. 9 & 10, and the direction for the place where the שירי מנחה have to be eaten in V. 9, all of which is not mentioned above in Ch. 2,3 etc. etc. The underlying meaning of all these laws has been considered above in Ch. II, the chapter on Minchas and here we shall only go into such as were not touched on there.

הקרב וגו׳ לפני ה׳ אל פני המזבח, this is the הגשה בקרן דרומית מערבית, placing the Mincha in the south-west corner of the Altar, representing:—laying our means of nourishment, our well-to-do position and the feeling of comfort arising from both, acknowledgingly at the feet of God, from Whom we receive them, to be used for Him, and for the spirit engendered by His Torah. (See Ch. II).

V. 8. במחובר :והרים ממנו .והרים ממנו בקמצו וגו׳ ואת כל הלבנה וגו׳. The מנחה by which the bringer’s “remembrance” is to be brought before God by the קומץ must be all contained in one vessel, so that the קומץ taken out of it comes from the whole Mincha. It is our material situation altogether, and not any single part of it, that we place before God (Menachoth 24a). — בקומצו, with the actual hand and not with some vessel or spoon that measures just his handful (ibid 19b). It is not only the dedication of our objective material possessions but at the same time the dedication of our activities that we want to represent in a Mincha. Not simply the wealth, the possessions themselves, but the man who handles and disposes of them too. It is just this that raises the Mincha into the category of offerings which dedicate our activities קדשי קדשים (see notes on Ex. 29,37). This is also the reason for the further law, בקומצו: not מבודץ (the same as מפורץ), just the handful, not more than that (not overflowing, ibid 11a, see תוספות 19b); it is to be only your possessions, in as far as you handle them. לבונה לא יפחת מן הקומץ ,מקיש לבונה להרמה : והרים וגו׳ בקומצו וגו׳ ואת כל הלבנה וגו׳, the incense is not to be less in quantity than the קומץ; the measure of our feeling of comfort in having our food and in our well-to-do- position in life will always be the same as the measure of our devoting them to the service of God.

V. 9—11. אכילת שידי מנחה is a מצוה, as is the eating of all parts of offerings which are handed over to the cohanim, it is the final symbolic procedure, to be regarded as the result, the consequence, of the whole ritual of the offering. It shows how, as a result of the kind of life which was symbolically represented by the preceding ritual, the nearness to God which is sought for in every קרבן is to be obtained to such a degree that even the personal enjoyment of a good meal becomes a holy priestly service to God, by which one in no wise departs from the holy precincts of the Sanctuary of God’s Torah. The שירי מנחות, like all בשר קדשי קדשים were always only to be eaten by the זכרי כהונה in the עזרה. From the manifold description of the place, במקום קדוש בחער אהל מועד, Zebachim 56a learns that the place which is here ordered for the eating is extended התורה רבתה חצרות הרבה אצל אכילה אחת and includes in the idea of the עזרה for אכילת קדשים all לשכות הבנויות בחול ופתוחות לקדש, halls built onto the sides of the Mikdosh, not on the actual sacred ground of the Mikdosh, but opening only into the Mikdosh. This eating by the priests is meant to picture just the fact that even on private חולין-soil one is to remain close to the Sanctuary, and not allow it to become mentally “out of sight”.

לא תאפה חמץ חלקם וגו׳, see notes on Ch. 2,11. By the subject of לא תאפה referring back to אותה it is evident that the prohibition of preparing it with חמץ refers not only to the Mincha before קמיצה והקטרה but also to the שירי מנחה handed over to the cohen, אפילו חלקם לא תאפה חמץ (Menachoth 55a). If מצה, — as remarked on Ch. 2,11 — is the idea of one’s existence being dependent on God which the מנחה wishes to express, and חמץ is, accordingly, completely excluded from the מנחה, we can understand the necessity for mentioning the prohibition specifically for the שירים. They, after all, are not brought onto the מזבח but the מתיד for them has already been brought on the Altar (see the remarks ibid, on כל שממנו לאשים). The reason for this prohibition is at once given by the juxtaposition of לא תאפה חמץ and אכילת כהנים .חלקם נתתי אותה מאשי itself is but a symbolic continuation of אכילת מזבח and, inasmuch as the priests are, at the same time, given their concrete living in this gift from the table of God, משלחן גבוה, it is impressed upon them that their existence, even more than that of the rest of the nation, is markedly dependent on the Sanctuary of God.

קדש קדשים היא כחטאת וכאשם, like חטאת and אשם the מנחה too comes under the idea of dedicating our actions and like the eating of the בשר חטאת ואשם so also is the אכילת שירי מנחה restricted to the עזרה and to the זכרי כהונה.

V. 11. כל אשר יגע בהם יקדש, in accordance with the grammatical construction the plural בהם can only refer either to the immediately preceding אשי הי or to the more distant קדשים. As a matter of fact this law, too, does not belong exclusively to the מנחה, but applies to all קדשים, the Gemora finds this taught by the concluding sentence: זאת התורה לעולה למנחה וגו׳ ולזבח השלמים (Zebachim 97a). This lays down the law that all eatables which, by coming into contact with a מנחה or one of the other קדשים, have absorbed some of it, so that the קדשים-material has penetrated into them, receive the full character of קדשים, and have to be treated in exactly the same manner as the קדש which has penetrated into them. So that, for example, if a piece of חולין-food the size of half a זית has absorbed half a זית of קדש-food, the whole has to be treated as a כזית קדש, so that if a זר ate it, or if the piece of קדש was פסול, e.g., נותר if anybody at all ate it, he would be חייב. This is the principle that היתר מצטרף לאיסור which has no application outside קדשים. This law is repeated for חטאת (V. 20): כל אשר יגע בבשרה יקדש and Zebachim 97b and Pesachim 45a et seq. explains this verse:— ת״ר כל אשר יגע יכול אפילו שלא בלע ת״ל בבשרה עד שיבלע בבשרה יקדש להיות כמוה הא כיצד אם פסולה היא תפסל אם כשרה היא תאכל כחמור שבה. The בשר in the text is the בשר חטאת and accordingly, it speaks primarily of the case where, by coming into contact the היתר has penetrated into the איסור. But for the conception היתר מצטרף לאיסור it should be quite the same in the case of איסור שנבלע בהיתר as היתר שנבלע באיסור. But that would require the consideration that here יגע ב- is to be taken only as penetration and not as mere external contact. It is difficult to assume that this is expressed by the term יגע בבשרה, as everywhere else, and indeed in quite parallel places as כל הנגע במזבח יקדש (Ex. 29,37), כל הנגע בהם יקדש (ibid XXX,29), in the same manner and with similar effect נגע ב- designates simply external contact. We therefore presume that the Talmuda of the Boraitha, ,בבשרה עד שיבלע בבשרה, only wants to fix the Halacha, which is traditional, to the words of the text as a mnemonic device; but we also think that in the parallel places which we have quoted, we can find an agreement with the meaning of our text which the Halacha teaches. For the נגיעה to the מזבח or the כלי שרת to impart קדושה, of which these parallel cases speak, is also no completely external unconditional touching. Only ראשו של מזבח, only the top flat surface of the Altar, and the כבש, the ramp leading up to it (the former having the purpose of being the place for the reception of consecrated objects, and, on the latter too, the איברי עולה were laid out before being given over to the Fire on the top), and similarly only תוכן, the inside of the כלי שרת which was designed to receive the consecrated objects, could impart קדושה by contact. And not every object received קדושה by such contact. Only such as were appropriate for them; only הראוי לאשים for the מזבח, and only לח liquids for the כלי שרת and only יבש, flour etc. for the מידות היבש (see Zebachim 83 & 88a). So that, there too, נגיעה requires and implies some inner mutual relationship between the two objects in contact, similar to the idea of an abstract penetration. That which there is effected by an abstract penetration is here effected by an actual material penetration. — As explained on Ex. 29,37, impartation of קדושה there comes from the קדש קדשים character, it is just that which makes it of that nature. But here, in the case of actual penetration, it is effective in all cases, also in קדשים קלים.

V. 13. The offering described in this and the following verses, according to the elucidation given of the Halacha, are:— חביתי כהן גדול, a daily morning and evening מנחה to be brought by every contemporary כהן גדול, and the מנחת חינוך לכהן הדיוט, a מנחה which every priest had to bring on his induction to the priestly service. Without this exposition the verse would offer insolvable difficulties. In V.13 the offering is described as אהרן ובניו, and everywhere by the term אהרן ובניו, the High Priest and the other priests, Aaron and his attendant sons, is understood, but never only Aaron and his successors in the office of High Priest — these are mentioned expressly in V. 15 — and nevertheless in this very V. 15, the offering is to be brought only by a כהן המשיח, by the High Priest. Further, ביום המשח אותו prescribes this offering only for the day of his induction and then immediately it calls it מנחת תמיד, a continuous, i.e., daily offering similar to the עולת תמיד (Numbers 28,3). But actually, in accordance with the Halacha, it is dealing with an offering that was brought daily by the High Priest, but only once in his lifetime by every other priest, on the day of his induction to office, before he was allowed to bring any other offering. We, therefore, think that אשר (V. 13) does not refer to קרבן but to אהרן ובניו, and עשירת האפה וגו׳ may be taken as the object of יקריבו. That, which is to be brought daily as a מנחת תמיד, and, as ordered in V. 15 by the כה״ג, that, everyone, אהרן ובניו, the High Priest and the other priests, is to bring on the day of his induction to office. The High Priest, acordingly, on the day of his entry into the office of a High Priest had to bring the offering twice, and if it happened that he was appointed before he had officiated at an offering as an ordinary priest, he would have had to bring it three times. (Menachoth 78a).

מנחת תמיד: This expression places this offering on par with the national daily offering which is דוחה שבת וטומאה, which has to be brought even on Sabbath and even when the circumstances are such that it would only be brought in a condition of טומאת מת (Menachoth 50b).

מחציתה בבקר ומחציתה בערב. This refers only to the חביתין which the כה״ג had to bring as a מנחת תמיד. The Mincha of induction, מנחת חינוך, was brought שלימה, the whole of it at once. — :עשירת האפה וגו׳ מחציתה בבקר וגוי חביתי כהן גדול לא היו באין חצאין אלא מביא עשרון שלם וחוציהו מקריב מחצה בבקר ומחצה בין הערבים: the חביתי כה״ג had, in all cases, to be brought as one half of a whole. He did not have to bring one twentieth of an Epha in the morning and one twentieth in the evening, but one tenth of an Epha in the morning, half of which was offered in the morning and the other half in the evening, so that if a כה״ג died after bringing his חביתין in the morning, and his successor took office the same day, the latter had to prepare a whole tenth for his even Mincha although only half of it would be offered (ibid 50b).

V. 14. על מחבת בשמן. Three kinds of preparation are named here: על מחבת בשמן, i.e., טיגון, baked in oil on a pan, and, as על מחבת by itself already designates frying in oil (Ch. 2,5), the addition of the word בשמן expresses an extra quantity of oil, and indeed, similar to the מנחת נסכים of the תמיד, 3 Logs, triple the quantity of an ordinary מנחת נדבה. Further, and this really preceded the מדבכת ,טיגון, which ת״כ explains was נּעשית ברותהין כל צורכה, boiled up thoroughly in boiling water, חליטה, similar to the מרחשת of the מנחת נדבה (Ch. 2,7), only that was boiled in oil. Finally תופיני which Menachoth 50b takes to be derived from the root אפה with a prefix ת, i.e., אפיה, baked in the oven. So that the חביתי כה״ג is the same fancy-bread that we already found described in Ex. 29,2 & 23 at the מילואים as חלת לחם שמן which similarly was prepared by these three kinds of cooking טיגון ,חליטה and אפיה. Of these חליטה was done first, and it seems that this is indicated by the word תביאנה in הבאה .מרבכת תכיאנה is the first bringing it to its destination, and then follows עשיה and אפיה. In Menachoth 50b it is left doubtful whether טיגון preceded אפיה or the reverse.

תפיני מנחת פתים, these words offer difficulties which, however, can be overcome. (See מזרחי ק״א thereon, מל״מ ,ל״מ on הל׳ מעשה קרבנות 13,4). We know from Menachoth 75b that the חביתי כה״ג were not broken into pieces at all nor were any other מנחות of the פוזות אותה פתים .כהנים (Ch. 2,5), “break it up into pieces” only applied to all those מנחות where קמיצה took place, quite obviously because only a קומץ of them was to be burnt on the Altar. Hence the dictum: מנחת ישראל כופל אחד לשנים ושנים לארבעה ומבדיל, ordinary Minchas were doubled over twice and then broken, so that each cake or loaf was broken up into four pieces. But, מנחת כהנים כופל אחד לשנים ושנים לארבעה ואינו מבדיל, the Mincha of the cohanim was similarly doubled over twice but not broken through; more, מנחת כהן משיח לא היה מקפלה, the Mincha of the High Priest was not doubled over at all, or, as the ברייתא puts it, only doubled in half, but in any case it was not broken through, and yet it is called in our text מנחת פתים! Hence, we venture to believe that מנחת פתים does not mean a Mincha which is actually broken into pieces, but is a general name for all מנחות “which are able to be broken into pieces”, i.e., for all baked מנחות ישראל of which only a קומץ was brought onto the Altar, and which were broken up for this purpose. It would accordingly be a general name for all the three kinds of מנחת נדבה mentioned in Ch. 2,4—7:— תופיני .מאפה תנור ,מחבת ,מרחשת is, in any case, a plural noun in stat. constr. and denotes the manner of baking. תופיני מנחת פתים would accordingly mean, baked in the manner of breakable Minchas, i.e., in the way that מנחת מאפה תנור, מחבת and מרחשת were baked. All the three ways in which a free-will Mincha could be prepared were united in the preparation of the מנחת כהן המשיח, the חביתי כה״ג prescribed here. It was baked in an oven like the מאפה תנור, fried in a pan like מחבת, and boiled soft like מרחשת, so that the חביתי כה״ג represented every kind of Mincha. So that it, itself, is not מנחת פתים but is prepared in the manner of those Minchas which are understood by this term. The one מנחת כה״ג combines in itself all the מנחת ישראל.

It should not be overlooked that the instructions for the preparation of this מנחה are given in the second person, whereas the preceding and succeeding verses 13 & 15 are in the third person. They are accordingly directed to Moses or to the Nation in general, תעשה ,תביאנה; we shall return to this fact when we work out the meaning of these laws of this offering.

V. 15, המשיח תחתיו מבניו, given the requisite qualification of character and intellectual gifts, the office of High Priest is hereditary. But the office is not automatically assumed. The representatives of the Nation, after assuring themselves of his qualifications, have to induct the High Priest elect into his office by anointment, or, after the loss of the שמן המשחה, by investment with the special garments, רבוי בגדים (see notes on Ex. 29,30). חק עולם: The term חק occurs preferably not with the meaning of a law or statute, but as that which has to be rendered as payment, as in Gen. 47,22; Ex. 10,13 & 14; Prov. 30,8. We, accordingly, believe that it must be taken here in that sense. The שירי מנחות ישראל like all the other מתנות כהונה are handed over to the cohanim as חק. In the מנחת כהן המשיח they go back to God again, as an expression of homage and acknowledgment.

חק עולם. In Ch. 24,9, לחם הפנים is also called חק עולם, and to this similarity of terms, the Gemora, in Menachoth 76a, attaches the Halacha that, like the לחם הפנים, the חביתי כה״ג have also to be laid in twelve loaves on the Table in the Mikdosh, which represents the placing of the National well-being before the Presence of God. By this number of twelve, the חביתים loaves are given a national meaning, similar to that of the .לחם הפנים כליל תקטר, it was given over to the Fire on the Altar in its complete state, i.e., unbroken and without a קומץ being taken from it.

The מנחת חינוך to be brought at the induction into office differs from the חביתין in that the whole עשרון was brought as once, and not in two halves one in the morning, and the other in the evening. It is not quite sure whether it had to be treated in the same way with regards to the quantity of oil, טיגון ,חליטה and אפיה. According to ת״כ it was not similar to the חביתין in all these matters, and consisted of only one עשרון with one לוג of oil. But according to Menachoth 78a, the מנחת חינוך appears to have been quite similar to the חביתין as far as the method of preparation is concerned. But even in that, already in Rashi there are different ways of looking at it (see מה״ק ,רמב״ם 13, 4; כלי המקדש 5, 17 & מל״מ thereon). Both חביתין as well as חיניד are accompanied by לבונה as are all מנחות יחיד (Menachoth 59a), and, with the חביתין the one קומץ לבונה is, just like the עשרון, brought half in the morning and the other half in the evening (ibid 25a).

We have already seen in the פרשת מילואים (Ex. 29,2) how, in the induction of Aaron and his sons into the priesthood, the priestly office is expressed by a פר with regards to the meaning of the office itself, and by אילים with regard to its dignity and honour. And we saw how this latter was represented in its dual capacity, with reference to its influence by the איל עולה and to its advantages by the איל מילואים which is really of the nature of a שלמים and as such is connected with the סל המצות which represents the means of material existence which is promised to the priests. Among the three kinds of the מילואים-loaves we find, as already remarked, in לחם שמן exactly the same kind of מנחה as that of which the חביתי כה״ג consisted. Now we see this לחם שמן picked out from all the sacrificial ritual which constituted the act of the foundation-consecration of the priestly tribe, not only to repeat afresh the original מילואים act at the entry of every priest into office (taking it — not as it appears from the ת״כ, but according to the Gemora and רמב״ם — that the מנחת חינוך is prepared in the same way as חביחין) but also to continue for all time daily in חביתי כה״ג the original act of the מילואים with one of the most essential things that result from it.

It is certainly characteristic that it is just the material advantages which are connected with the office, which the Priest, before he actually enters into the Service of the Sacrifices, and the High Priest daily, as the representative of the whole priestly tribe, offers up to the Altar-Fire as the expression of complying with God’s Will. According to one reading of the ת״כ the whole offering is even פסול if it is brought by a כהן who has not yet brought his מנחת חינוך! (See מל״מ ;5,16 הל׳ כלי מקדש thereon). Surely all this is meant to continually bring home to the priest that he is not to hold his office for the sake of the material benefits it brings with it, but to consider these material benefits merely as an unavoidable necessity for his existence which are to be part and parcel of the sacred purposes of his offce. For, after all, his service was the sole foundation of the existence of the Jewish Priest, but he is not to allow his service to be absorbed by his existence, but his existence is to be “given up” to his service, entirely absorbed by the idea of it כל מנחת כהן כליל תהיה לא תאכל! Every individual of the People has to lay the whole of his material possessions “at the feet of God”, and to devote the full “handful” of it, according to God’s command, to keep godliness alive on earth. It is just this participation of his possessions for the Sanctuary of God, which makes a man into a Jew and places his material existence under the “remembrance” and care of God, and makes his joy and happiness in life dependent on God’s satisfaction with his life. But the whole existence of the priest with the whole material side of his existence too, is to be given up to the service of the godly on earth; by the pattern of his life in its entirety, outside the Sanctuary too, — as quite clearly can be seen from the special laws for his conduct in general life (Ch. XXI) — he is “to prepare a home, a base for holiness on earth, as his very name ‘cohen’ expresses”; there is to be nothing on him that is not priestly, not holy. Hence when he brings his own Mincha unto the Sanctuary, the expression of his own “nourishment”, his own “well-being” his own “satisfaction” with life, it is not just a “part for remembrance” which is brought from it on to God’s Altar, it is absorbed in its entirety by the Fire of Godliness on Earth.

But the daily Mincha which the High Priest has to bring is the “richest” (ג׳ לוגין) amongst all the kinds of Mincha and comprises a combination of the expressions of every degree of material fortune:— the needy (מאפה תנור), the extraordinary (מחבת) and the momentary exuberant מרחשת=מרבכת (see notes on Ch. 2,4—7), not because he, as an individual considers his position on earth as such a rich state of happy fortune, but because, as High Priest, he is the symbolic representation of the Nation. That which the לחם הפנים means for the Nation in its concrete actuality is what the חביתין represents for the idea of the ideal unity of the Nation as is represented by the person of the כה״ג. That is why these latter, like the former, consist of twelve חלות. But whereas the לחם הפנים, in accordance with the idea of brotherly social life, were baked in pairs, the חביתין in accordance with the idea of unity were most probably (see רמב״ם מה״ק 13 & מל״מ thereon) נאפות אחד אחד. And it is also out of this national point of view that we think we can explain why, in the laws for its preparation the address is made to Moses or to the Nation — תקריב ,תביאנה, V. 14 — and not to the priests. It is the nation which commissions its High Priest to bring his חביתין in such a rich form of preparation, as indeed the Nation is recommended to do in an actual concrete form: גדלהו משל אחיו (Ch. 21,10), to see to it that their High Priest is in a position to appear in his external life and appearance also, in a manner befitting the dignity of the Nation.

The pages of all history teach us that every deterioration, every corruption, from earliest times was brought about by the degeneration of the upper classes. If then, as the whole position of the Jewish priests and high priests — who had to be married and have a “home” — show, priests and high priests were to exercise a moralising and ennobling influence on the nation by the exemplary pattern of their home life, and for that reason were to live a social life in the midst of the people, we can well understand that it could be the intention of the Torah that the high priests, by living a well-to-do existence, were to belong to the wealthier class, with their homes, the education and culture of their children, and with the whole tenor of their civil lives. Thus they would exercise the silent, but nevertheless powerful, influence of a model example just where the keynote of the national moral life tended to lie. The richness of the חביתין-Mincha which they had to bring each morning and evening might well have been a reminder to them to carry out this intention of the Torah.

We have already remarked on Ex. 29,38 how the Tamid offering was designed to impress on our minds how the rules of the universe, and the relations of human beings to them, were the same in all the various and contrasting conditions of life, as are typified in the contrasts of day and night. It is the same personality with exactly the same symbols of nourishment, of well being, and of the joy of life, which presents itself at the darkening rays of eve as at the brightening rays of morn, as a member of the flock of the One Unique Shepherd of Life. To a still higher degree would the necessity be present of showing the “oneness”, the uniformity of the relationship of our attitude to the world in all diverse conditions of life, where — as in מנחת חביתין — it is just these physical conditions of life which are being brought independently by themselves as symbolic daily offerings to God. There the morning and evening Mincha form one single whole. It is brought as one single עשרון and שלמה, undivided and complete. So much are the morning and evening Mincha to appear only as half of one and the same whole, that even in the case where a High Priest has suddenly died and his successor has to bring the evening Mincha, he has to consecrate a whole fresh עשרון and bring the half of it for his evening Mincha.

We have indicated the national meaning and importance of the חביתי כה״ג, and it is not impossible that this may be the explanation of the designation of morning and evening time by עלות המנתה (Kings I. 18,36; II. 3,20) and the recurring expression מנחת הערב. This could refer to the bringing of the חביתין, as the מנחת נסכים at the Tamid offerings appears as quite of a secondary nature (see also our commentary on Ps. 141,2).

V. 18. זאת תודח החטאת, these words generalise the laws given in V. 20 on the washing out of blood which has splashed on to a garment — which is the only one of the laws enumerated in vv. 18—20, which applies exclusively to the חטאת — to apply to all חטאות בהמה, both פנימיות and חיצוניות, and only excludes חטאת עוף of which our verse is not speaking at all, as it deals only with חטאות הנשחטות (Zebachim 92a). במקום אשך שחיטת חטאת :תשחט וגו׳, like that of the עולה had to be done on the north side, בצפון. If, as we thought we could explain at the עולה, (see Chap. 1,11) — שחיטה וקבלה בצפון means that the giving up of the life of living for oneself (שחיטה. I.L.) and going over to the life of the Mikdosh (קבלה. I.L.) makes demands primarily on the material side (צפון. I.L.) of human life, then this putting the חטאת in the same place as the עולה would express the following thought:— Just as slackness lack of energy in moral-ideal matters, out of which the need for עולה results, so does the lack of serious firmness in moral-active matters out of which the need for חטאת results, have its primary cause in allowing material-matters to have a preponderant influence on our lives. (“The world is too much with us; late and soon, getting and spending we lay waste our powers”. I.L.). For firmness, just as for progress in morality and goodness, moral power can only be gained by self-sacrifice in the material side of life, the side pertaining to the senses.

V. 19. הכהן המחטא אותה וגו׳. This can not mean that the authorisation for eating the בשר חטאת is limited to the priest who performed the ritual of the offering, for immediately in v. 22, this authorisation is given to all male members of the priestly tribe, even to בעלי מום (Ch. 21,22) who are precluded from taking active part in the offering ritual. But here, it speaks of the legal claim to the parts of the offerings which are to be divided amongst the priests. In Deut. 18,8, the general rule for such claim is given: חלק כחלק יאכלו לבד ממכריו על האבות, all are to have an equal right except to that to which the family sections resign their rights. This lays down first the principle of the original right for each priest to claim an equal share in the distribution of the meat of the offerings. But it then suggests that, in time, when the priestly population will have grown, it will be expedient, by mutual reciprocal renunciation, for only one family section at a time to be on duty and to take part in the distribution. In accordance with this, in the time between Moses and David, the priesthood was divided into eight משמרות who took weekly turns to be on duty in the Temple. Each משמר was then subdivided into family groups, בתי-אב, of which a different בית אב served each day. (Taanith 27a; הל׳ כלי המקדש 4, 11). Only during the general national assembly on the רגלים the original basic norm חלק כחלק יאכלו remained in practice regarding the קרבנות צבור (Succa 56a). So the כהן המחטא of our verse would be the משמר of that particular week, or rather the בית אב who were on service (מה״ק 10, 14 & 15, ל״מ thereon) on whom the duty of carrying out the ritual of the offerings fell. The condition is made that the parts of the offering which are to be eaten, are to be divided amongst all the members of the משמר on duty who were ראוי לחיטוי ולאכילה at the time that the offering was made, i.e., who were not excluded from service or from being allowed to eat the sacrificial-meat by reason of being in a state of טומאה, or in the אונן condition. So that an אונן and a טבול יום, although they may eat of the offering after nightfall, have no right of participation in the division, because at the moment the offering was brought they lacked the ability for service or eating. Regarding a בעל מום see v. 22 (Zebachim 99a). — במקום קדש תאכל וגו׳. See notes on v. 9. By this, אכילת חטאת is here placed in the closest connection with the עבודת החטאת and in equal importance to it. The right to eat of it is made dependent on the fitness for service and for such eating, which was present at the time, at the moment of the offering being made (a כה״ג who was an אונן was excluded from the חלוקה although he was allowed to perform the whole ritual, because, while in that condition he was not allowed to eat the offering) and this shows the great importance and significance of the אכילת כהנים in the clearest manner as being an עבודה in itself. Taken together with verse 18 the thought is expressed: — The indispensable basis for חטאת as for עולה is the giving up of uncontrolled life of the senses. But in חטאת the ultimate desired result is shown not as ascetic restraint from all satisfaction of the senses, but as the rendering priest-like and holy even of the satisfaction of the senses.

V. 20. כל אשר יגע בבשרה יקדש: See verse 11. יזה :ואשר יזה וגו׳, the קל of נזה, the intransitive form of הזה to splash, see on Ch. 4,6. Here it is ordained that if some of the -חטאתblood splashes on to a garment, the blood-stained spot must be washed out again in the עזרה. The הלכה restricts this law to the חטאת and it does not apply to other דם קדשים and only to חטאת בהמה and not to חטאת העוף, and only to דם חטאת כשר שנתקבל בכלי וראוי להזיה, to blood of a חטאת which is כשרה and has already been received in a כלי שרת to perform the עבודת הדם with it, but not before the קבלה or after the מתנה. Further, only if the blood has come on דבר ראוי לקבל טומאה and לכבוס, on an object which is able to be affected by טומאה and is washable. Moreover, the whole of the object need not be washed, only the place which is stained. (This washing-out had to be done progressively with seven solvents, מעבירין עליו שבעה סממנים, after the spot had first been washed in water, רוק תפל ,מי רגלים ,נתר ,בורית ,אהל ,קמוניא ,אשלג, a process which no blood can withstand, and which therefore also serves as a test for blood (Nidda 61b; Zebachim 92a, 93a & b, & 95a). A כלי which is not ראוי לכבוס requires גרידה, scraping and paring the surface of the blood-stained spot, (Zebachim 94a). If we take all these laws together and try to find the underlying thought, we must look for it in what we have taken to be the nature and meaning of חטאת inasmuch as these laws only apply to the מתנות דמים of a חטאת בהמה.
