The idea which is represented by blood destined for מתנה on the Altar coming on to a כלי הראוי לקבל טומאה (i.e., a כלי bearing the stamp of pertaining to human use) must be so very contrary to its real idea, that its removal by כיבוס has to be done as a positive Mikdosh procedure within the precincts of the Mikdosh במקום קדוש. Now דם חטאת בהמה המקובל בכלי שרת differs — if our understanding of it be not erroneous — from both דם חטאת העוף and from the דם of other קדשים in that the blood of all other offerings, being ניתנין למטה are meant to represent the נפש as being still in a lower stage, requiring energetic efforts to strive upwards to higher things. To the conception of such a stage in life, nothing which bears the stamp of human life, such as a garment or a vessel, can be considered as being incompatibly incongruous. In reality everything which pertains to human life, even that which is farthest away and lowest, should be brought in to the sphere of this דם המקובל במזרק, in to the sphere of our efforts and progress upwards towards holiness. Hence the דם of all other offerings דם שנתז על הבגד can not be considered as having violated thereby the idea which is innate in it. But the דם of חטאת בהמה which is ניתנין למעלה על קרנות המזבח, destined to be placed on the very top of the Altar, or even, if it is a פנימית to be ניתניז על קרנות מזבח הזהב, or even higher still to have הזיה על הפרכת כנגד בין הבדים represents the person, the נפש at a stage when he has already achieved moral heights and only requires serious attention to keep there and not slip down; or even, in the case of פנימיות, at the stage of that ideal moral perfection that always shines as an illuminating beacon before us, but which no concrete actuality ever completely attains. So that דם חטאת בהמה which stands ready for מתנות על קרנות המזבח (and even more in the other שניתז על הבגד ,(חטאות, by the contrast between the moral heights which it represents, and the stage of existence which the garment or vessel brings to one’s mind, and on to which it has come instead of on to the קרנות המזבח suffers such a fall that the keeping of the underlying idea of what this represents has to be re-established by כיבוס במקום קדוש. Against the theory of this explanation would be the fact that דם שניתז on even בגדי כה״ג e.g., on מעיל, which itself represents an ideal stage of moral perfection has to be treated with the כיבוס process. But perhaps this objection disappears when we consider that בגדי כהונה ניתנו ליהנות and were allowed to be worn also שלא בשעת עבודה (Yoma 68b) so that they are not to be considered entirely on their own and apart from the actual real person of the priest (וצ״ע מאבנט לסברת הרמב״ם שאסר שלא בשעת עבודה עי׳ כלאים י׳ ל״ב וע״ש בראב״ד ובכ״מ). But the אבנט in any case, the priestly girdle, does not represent a stage of ideal perfection being already reached (as the other garments do. I.L.) but only the energetic intention and preparation for the effort to reach it, and so does fall into the stage of the עולה and would be a disturbing contrast to the חטאת idea (see end of Ex. XXVIII).

The regulation which has to be observed here, that the דם only requires כיבוס if splashed before נתינה ,הזיה or זריקה, but not after the עבודה has been done with it as well as the general rule with which it seems connected, that אין לד דבר שנעשה מצותו ומועלין בו (see above VI,3) by which an object only retains its קדושה for as long as it is a means for the performance of a מעוה, but loses this holiness once the מצוה has been completed — may well be meant to counter, in Jewish circles, any and every idea of heathen mysticism or superstitious magic which might be associated with the holy appurtenances. What is holy is only the idea for which these things serve as a means of expression. Only for as long as they have to serve for such expression do they partake of the holiness of the idea. But actually in themselves or permanently they have no holiness. It is only not to go to the other extreme, and not to give the idea of serving for a Mitzva the appearance of being under-estimated that we are taught that תשמישי קדושה נגנזין, and that תשמישי מצרה also, in so far אינן נזרקיו, they may not be thrown into the dustbin or disposed of in any disrespectful manner, but do not require גניזה like תשמישי קדשים (Megilla 26b and רמ״א א״ח 21, 1).

Daß כבוס nur כלי הראוי לקבל טומאה erfordert, bewegt sich einerseits in derselben eben erwähnten Richtung (siehe zu Kap. 11, 32), andererseits ist es eben ein also qualifiziertes כלי, das den vollendeten Stempel der Menschenbeziehung trägt und somit durch seine Bestimmung eine Beziehung vergegenwärtigt, deren Stufe sich noch im Gegensatz zu der durch דם חטאת repräsentierten Idee befindet.

V. 21. וכלי חרש אשד תבשל בו: According to Zebachim 95b this is as much as saying into which some of it has “cooked”, i.e., penetrated; for the result is the same if עירה לתוכה רותחין, if it was poured in to the vessel when it was boiling hot. This has raised the question, as to what extent in general, in connection with other איסורין such an “עירוי״, pouring boiling liquid into a vessel, can be considered as having the same penetrating effect as actually cooking in it, whether it is to be considered as כלי ראשון or as כלי שני. (see תוספות there and the ש״ד on ישבר — .(2 ,105 י״ד: that which has penetrated into an earthenware vessel, can not be removed by boiling it out (Kashering. I.L.) by מרק :ומרק ושטף .התורה העידה על כלי חרס שאינו יוצא מידי דופיו לעולם :הגעלה (related to מרג, a threshing-tool, by means of which the grains are freed out of their husks) means “to free a material from foreign ingredients which have penetrated into it”, hence also “to polish”, נחשת מרוק (Chron. II. 4,16) and of smoothing skin treatment, תמרוקי הנשים (Esther 2,12). Hence also, the liquid mixed with what comes out from boiled-out meat — Meat gravy מרק (Judges 6,19). Here it means Kashering הגעלה with boiling water. שטף, rinsing with cold water (Zebachim 97a). — מריקה ושטיפה is prescribed for all קדשי מזבח but not for תרומה (ibid 95a). The מריקה ושטיפה and the שבירת כלי הרס have also to be done במקום קדוש, in the עזרה, (ibid 93b). The “Kashering” of vessels from קדשים prescribed here differs from that prescribed for all other איסורים (Numbers 31,23) in that the הגעלה in the other cases does not need to be followed by שטיפה, and further that מריקת קדשים can only be done with water, while הגעלה can be done legally, in any case in תרומה cases, with other liquids, and also that בשל במקצת כלי טעון מריקה ושטיפה כל הכלי (Zebachim 96b, תוספות). What has to be done in general cases of או״ה depends on how they have to be treated, whether שאר איסורים have to be treated like תרומה or like קדשים (see ב״י on טור א״ח 452). There are difficulties, which are not insolvable, which stand in the way of finding the motive for this מריקה ושטיפה prescribed for קדשים. For there are undecided questions regarding the laws governing the things for which the reason has to be sought. Amongst these, and above all, is the question as to when the מריקה ושטיפה has to be done, whether immediately after the occurrence, or only after the קדשים absorbed have become נותר (see Zebachim 97a; תוספות there, and ל״מ ;14 ,8 מ׳ק רמב״ם thereon); and especially the question raised on 95b and left undecided, whether, in the case of תלאו באויר התנור where בישול would take place without מריקה ושטיפה ,בלוע would have to be done or not, וצ״ע.

V. 22. כל זכר בכהנים וגו׳, see v. 19. Here, also, the right to take part in the חלוקה is expressed by יאכל אותה. The permission to eat is extended to all priests, even a בעל מום in Ch. 21,22. Here, the exception is laid down that a בעל מום although he is not ראוי לחטוי, nevertheless participates in the חלוקה (Zebachim 102a). See on Ch. 21,17 et seq. In connection with the preceding verses, this restricts מריקה ושטיפה to קדשים כשרים which are fit to be eaten (Zebachim 96b). By the double restricting words קדש קדשים היא and אותה which are מיעוט אחר מיעוט, always taken as a limitation of the limitation and hence an extension, it is extended to include all קדשים and only תרומה is excluded (Zebachim 96b; תוספות ibid).
The Law that only זכרי כהונה are allowed to eat applies to all קדשי קדשים also to שלמי צבור (Zebachim 55a).

V. 23. In Ch. 4,12 & 21, the Law has already been given for חטאות פנימיות that, unlike other חטאות, their flesh is not to be eaten, but has to be burnt. Now it says here that every חטאת, which includes חיצונית also, the blood of which is destined for the מזבח העולה, if brought במזיד, with full consciousness, into the Heichal and the blood sprinkled or placed on the פרכת or the מזבח הזהב, may not be eaten but has to be burnt. More, the Halacha teaches that as soon as any part of the blood of a חטאת intended for the מזבח החיצון has been used in the Heichal, the whole offering becomes פסול, and even if there is still enough blood left in the עזרה, e.g., שקבל דמה בשני כוסות, the offering may not be proceeded with. Zebachim 82a). The same would apply to חטאות פנימיות, e.g., פר העלם דבר (Ch. 4,16), if any of its blood destined for the Heichal, would have been taken in to the קדש הקדשים. But if the text would only have referred to the פסול of חטאות חיצוניות it would be difficult to explain why the פסול should be expressed only by לא תאכל, only referring to the איסור אכילה as the פסול prevents the whole of the further ritual of the offering — the הקטרת אימורים, the נתינת דם על הקרנות — just as much as it does the אכילה. Accordingly it seems that the way ר׳ יוסי הגלילי explains (Zebachim 82a) that כל הענין כולו אינו מדבר אלא בפרים הנשרפים ובשעירים הנשרפים לשרוף פסוליהן אבית הבירה ולעמוד בלא תעשה על אכילתן is agreed to also by those who take it that the פסול of the חטאות החיצוניות —which ר׳ יוסי הגלילי takes to be given in Ch. 10,18 — is expressed in it, and according to them, both would be contained in our text viz.: — Every חטאת whose blood — whether rightly as with פנימיות or wrongly as with חיצוניות — has been brought into the Heichal to effect atonement, may not be eaten, but in place of אכילת הקדש (v. 19) must be burnt בקדש. See Pesachim 82b, בקדש באש תשרף וגו׳ and Rashi there ד״ה פסולי שאר קדשים (cf. מה״ק ל״מ 11, 3). So that we have here two sentences:— (a) כל חטאת, both פנימיות and חיצוניות whose blood has come בהיכל לכפר may not be eaten, לא תאכל, this implies that such a חטאת חיצונית is altogether פסול. Further (b) that every חטאת פסולה and so, also חטאות פנימיות which had become פסול (and which if they had been נעשו כמצותן would have been burnt outside the מחנות, see Ch. 4,12), altogether every קדשי קדשים שנפסלו (see Pesachim 82b) must be burnt בקדש, i.e., in the עזרה.

Concerning שריפת חטאות פנימיות שנעשו כמצותן, see above on Ch. 4,12, here the prohibition of אכילה is expressly added. Its meaning is perfectly clear from the explanation given there. The fact that the burning of all קדשי קדשים שנפסלו, just as the אכילה when they are כשר, has to be done במקום קדוש, in the עזרה, proves that, (as we have already gone into on Ex. 12,10) the שריפת פסולי מוקדשים is meant to be a refutation of the anti-קדש idea which lies in that which the פסול represents. So that the burning itself continues the positive ritual of the offering. It is even insisted on, that the שריפה of the most important of the פסולים viz., נותר ופיגול, must take place, like the actual procedure of the offering, only by day! (Zebachim 56b). But the fact that all חטאות, if some of their blood שנכנס מדמן לפנים, and even פנימיות שנכנס מדמן לק״ק are פסולים, whereas all other קרבנות whose blood has been taken on to the מזבח הזהב instead of onto the מזבח החיצון are in so far כשרים that נתכפרו בעלים although the בשר is פסול (Zebachim 26b) may have its reason in the same characteristic speciality in which we believe we found the motive for כיבוס דם חטאת (v. 20). The דם of all other קרבנות represents the נפש at the stage of still requiring to make progress. So that just as the innate idea in the דם suffers no lowering by הזיה על כלי because every phase of human life, without any exception, is invited to make progress in the realm of the Sanctuary; in the same way the representation of a higher, even the highest purpose is neither presumption for any נפש whatsoever, nor a lowering of this higher, or highest goal; for the נפש in this דם is represented just as still requiring improvement and progress. But it is another matter with חטאת. There the דם represents a נפש as having already reached a stage of spiritual and moral advancement, where the necessity lies for firmness in keeping there and holding it, there the danger of presumptuous arrogance, and also of the lowering of the idea of this spiritual height is involved, and has assiduously to be removed. But the עזרה stands to the היכל and the היכל to the ק״ק in the relation of a preliminary stage to the stage of higher and highest perfection.

V. 1—7. In these verses the sacrificial procedures of the אשם which was not specially detailed in Ch. 5,14—26, are completed. Its שחיטה and זריקה are similar to the עולה while the הקטרת אימורים and אכילת בשד לכהנים are like the חטאה and, as an אשם can only be brought from צאן, v. 3 & 4 prescribe the הקטרה of a חטאת כבש as in Ch. 4,35. Above on Ch. V.14—26 we have already considered these rituals of the אשם all together, and would refer to that, here. We have also explained, on Ch. 4,24, on explaining the rule כל שבחטאת מתה באשם ירעה, the mid-course which the אשם takes between the חטאת and the other offerings, in the case where an animal bears the character of an אשם, without being directly related to a special offence or direct indebtedness, e.g., חמורת אשם or שמתו בעליו or שכפרו באחר. In such cases it is not itself offered up on the Altar, as חמודת עולה or שכפרו באחר or שמתו בעליה would be, but is only brought indirectly and then as an עולה. It is left to graze, ניתק לרעיה, until it gets a מום which renders it unfit to be brought itself, is then sold and with the money an עולה has to be bought. Now we are taught in Zebachim 5b that if, after it has been put out to graze one did not wait for it to receive a מום but offered it up, שחטו סתם, it would be כשד and tacitly taken to be an עולה which indeed was its ultimate destination. But before it had been put out to graze it would still have the character of an אשם, and, as such, having no direct relation to a person or sin, would be פסול. This retaining its אשם-character as long as it is not ניתק לרעיה is indicated by אשם הוא in v. 5, בהוייתו יהא. Above, in Ch. 4,24 we tried to explain this ability of all offerings, except חטאת, to ultimately change into an עולה and there we already remarked how, according to ר״ת, even the whole of the procedure of רעיה for an אשם was only דרבנן, and that originally אשם שמתו בעליה etc., was simply allowed to be brought itself as an עולה (see ל״מ on פה״מ 4, 15).

V. 8. עולת איש. According to Zebachim 103a & b, this unusual designation instead of the usual עולה, excludes two cases, viz., פרט לעולה שלא עלתה לאיש and פרט לעולת הקדש. The skin of the עולה as altogether, of all קדשי קדשים, only then is given to the priest: (a) when the offering does benefit the בעלים, i.e., when the זריקה has been duly and properly carried out, and any פסול which may have occurred, only happened after the זריקה; and (b) when the עולה was not מתפיס עולה לבדק הבית, for in these cases the skin goes to the בדק הבית fund. Here again the term המקריב, just like the term המחטא of v. 19, designates הראוי להקרבה all those priests who, being fit, are called to service, But this law has specially to be expressed regarding the עור עולה as in other offerings the skin goes with the meat, in קדשי קדשים to the כהנים and in קדשים קלים to the בעלים.

V. 9 & 10. In v. 9 the same law is given for מנחות, that only all those who were ראויים להקרבה, i.e., excluding אונן and טבול-יום, come to participate in the division, although these latter are allowed to eat of the מנחה after night. But v. 10 adds the provision that כל מנחה, every single מנחה, is to be divided between those who have the right to participate, איש כאחיו. Each member of the בית אב of that day receive a portion of each מנחה, and it is not permitted to hand out even quite similar מנחות such as מנחת מרחשת כנגד מנחת מרחשת, in a way that one would receive this whole מנחה, and another that whole one, but each מנחה must be divided amongst all the members of the בית אב even if it means reducing it to quite tiny pieces. This applies to all מנחות and all offerings. But the law is taught at מנחה בלולה וחרבה to insist on its being applied even in extreme cases, as in these the portion can often consist of a minimum of unbaked dough or even of only flour! (Menachoth 73a, רמב״ם מה״ק 10, 15 & 16). This law could very well have been designed to make it perfectly clear that this participation in the offerings by the priests eating thereof, is meant to have symbolic meaning, as we have repeatedly taken אכילת כהנים itself to be an integral part of the ritual of the offerings. Were it to be regarded simply as payment for service, then, on the contrary, one would be allowed to see to it, nay, one would have to see to it, that each portion should retain at least some value, and not, by dividing them up, frequently become valueless; one would certainly be allowed to hand out Mincha against another Mincha, one offering to be an offset against another. But as it is, it is quite clearly a מצוה and an עבודה which repeats itself in each individual offering, to fulfil which, accordingly, each one of those called on to serve, should take part. There was only one part of the offering which did not belong to the symbolism of the עבודה and which does appear purely as payment for service rendered, and that is the עורות קדשים spoken of in v. 8. Regarding the apportionment of these, each one of those entitled to participation was at liberty to make any suitable arrangement. (Pesachim 57; B.K. 110a).

V. 11. וזאת תורת זבח השלמים וגו׳. In Zebachim 120b, this generalising teaching is taken to indicate that the laws concerning פגול and נותר contained in the following verses, apply to every שלמים and תודה, even when, at the time of היתר במות, they were brought on a במה (see on Deut. 12,5 et seq., and Ex. 27,8).

V. 12—14. אם על תודה יקריבנו. Above, in Ch. III, the meaning of the שלמים-offering has already been taught. We believe we could take it to be the expression of a person who feels himself שלם, in a condition of completeness, lacking nothing and in this condition, and with it, he wishes to get nearer to his God. Now, here, a special kind of שלמים offering is primarily presented, namely one which arises from the שלם condition having been endangered and regained. Thus the ארבעה צריכין להודות the four who are duty bound to give thanks publicly of whom Ps. CVII sings:— they that have been saved from the dangers of the desert, of imprisonment, of illness, or of the sea, יודו לה׳ חסדו וגו׳, they are to acknowledge the Love and the miracles which God shows to Man, ויזבחו זבחי תורה and are to offer thanksgiving offerings and exultingly proclaim what God has done for them. The hypothetical phrase אם על תודה יקריבנו referring back to תורת זבח השלמים clearly characterises תודה as belonging to the category of שלמים. Here, accordingly, only that which is charcteristic for תודה is fixed, but everything else that has been prescribed for שלמים applies also to תודה, namely סמיכה והקריב על זבח התודה חלות וגו׳ — .(ת״ב) ונסכים ותנופה וחזה ושוק: the זבח התודה the animal for the שלמים forms the centre-point, to which the loaves which are prescribed here are added, and by which it is that the שלמים receives its character as a תודה. Three kinds of מצה-loaves are mentioned first in v. 12, two of them occur above in Ch. 2,4 as מנחת מאפה תנור, and the third מרבכת we know as the חביתי כה״ג in Ch. 6,14, and all three are identical with the three kinds of Mazzos described at the מילואים in Ex. 29,2 (Menachoth 78a). Leaven-bread — Chometz — has also to be brought at the same time. The prescription in v. 13: על חלת לחם חמץ יקריב קרבנו, teaches that the three kinds of Mazzos form one group, קרבנו, parallel to which, and at the same time as which, Chometz loaves are to be brought at their side as a second group belonging to it, and all these four kinds of bread together, are an accompaniment to the זבח תודת שלמיו, the animal to be sacrificed. According to Menachoth 76b, the three kinds of Mazzoth have to be made together from the same quantity of flour as the one kind of Chometz is made, על חלות לחם חמץ, נגד חמץ הבא מצה. Now there is only one other offering where Chometz appears. This is the שתי לחם on Shevuoth which similarly are in close connection with the שלמים, the שני כבשי עצרת which have to be brought at the same time. These שלמי צבור with לחם חמץ appear to have the same meaning for the nation which our שלמי תודה with their לחם חמץ have for the individual. On one single occasion in the year, on the Azereth of the מתן תורה-Festival, the Nation brings its לחם חמץ before God, as does the individual during the year when he feels he has cause to bring a תודה. Each of the שתי לחם had to be made out of one עשרון of flour, as prescribed in Ch. 23,17; שתים שני עשרונים, and according to Menachoth 77b each of the Chometz-loaves of the תודה had to consist of one עשרון. Verse 14 tells us that one out of each of the four kinds of bread of the תודה — including the Chometz loaves — is to be given to the priest as תרומה לה׳. There, in Menachoth, this “תרומה״ is compared to תרומת מעשר of which, in quite similar terms the order runs: ותרמותם ממנו תרומת ה׳ (Numbers 18,26), and we are taught that this תרומת תודה also is to be one out of ten, so that each of the four kinds of bread, from which one had to be taken as “תרומה״, had to consist of ten loaves. Hence there were forty loaves, ten Chometz and thirty Mazzos. As, as already remarked, each Chometz loaf had to be made from one עשדון and the total quantity of the flour used for all the Mazzos had to be equal to the quantity used for the Chometz loaves, the forty תודה loaves were made from twenty עשדונים, ten עשרונים for the ten Chometz loaves and ten עשרונים for the thirty Mazzos (Menachoth 77a & b). A comparatively small quantity of oil was used for the ten עשרונים of the תודה-Mazzo. Whereas otherwise one Log of oil went to each עשרון of a Mincha, here the ten עשדונים together, only received ½ Log, of which half went to the חלות and the רקיקין — ⅛ Log to each kind — and the other half (i.e., ¼ Log) to the רביכין (Menachoth 89a). The four kinds of bread of the תודה were conceived as forming one whole, and each one of them is necessary for the validity of the whole, מעכבין זה את זה (Mmenachoth 27a). We find them accordingly, referred to in v. 14 in the singular והקריב ממנו, and referring to this we are taught in Menachoth 76b that all the forty loaves must lie together at the time the תרומה is lifted out: והקריב ממנו מן המחובר. — The loaves are to be considerd purely as only accessories to the זבח. Before the שחיטה of the latter, they must have been baked to at least the stage of having formed a crust, קרמו פניה, and they only receive their קדושה by the שחיטת הזבח. This is expressed in v. 13 in the יקריב קרבנו על זבח on which the Gemora says אין הלחם קדוש אלא בשחיטת הזבח (Menachoth 78b).

In Ex. XXIX, the chapter on Milluim, we have already considered in general, the Mazzos of the תודה-offering which are identical with those of the Milluim. We took it that they represented the two factors, food and well being, which are the most essential factors necessary to produce the שלמים-condition, in various degrees, from the simple plain רקיק just painted over with oil, to the complicated skilfully prepared רביד, rich in oil. The bringer, in whichever position of life he may be, seeking to get nearer to God, and confining his offering entirely to Mazzo, expresses his conviction that any and every degree of external well being he enjoys is due to his serving God, and is only to be used in such service, But the תודה offering has not only Mazzo but has two groups of bread, one Chometz and one Mazza, both made out of exactly the same quantity of flour, and the two together forming the תודה-unit. So that in תודה the same external (material) existence, this same external material existence which has been endangered and which has again been granted afresh, appears both as Chometz and Mazza. It appears in Chometz as representing the worldly position of the restored person, and this same worldly position appears in its relation towards God as Mazza and it is only as Mazza that it receives the greater or lesser participation in real well-being. For Chometz, as opposed to Mazza, designates the condition of independence and of being in possession of free untrammelled power of disposal. Whatever the nature of the suffering or misfortune from which the bringer of the תודה had been delivered, it had in every case been a צרה, a danger which entailed the feeling of restriction (הצר. I.L.) and curtailment of one’s powers. And when the sufferer comes forth from this danger and feels himself again in untrammelled secure independence, this “complete security of his external condition for happiness” (the שלם-feeling. I.L.) has no means of expression more pregnant with meaning than with “ten Chometz loaves”. “Ten”, the rounded closed number is exactly the quantitative expression of the qualitative שלם, the “undiminished, uncurtailed state of being complete”. It is just that which is expressed by the ten Chometz loaves — the regained feeling of security — that occasioned the bringing of a תודה. But it would not have brought him to bring a תודה, if that which he feels towards the world as חמץ did not appear to him as מצה towards God; if he were not filled with the feeling that it was only God Whom he had to thank for his regained חמץ-security, and that every little grain of his regained secure position in the world — of which he is now so happily conscious — only tightens afresh his dependence on God, and only makes him feel afresh his obligation to use every atom of the strength and powers his security gives him in the service of God. With exactly the same amount of Mazzo as that of Chometz does the תודה appear before God, and it is just this מצה נגד חמץ alone, which makes the תודה into a תודה With the Mazzo exactly equalising the Chometz, the person seeking nearness to God by a תודה asserts his acknowledgment that regarding his regained שלם-condition he gives up all claim to its being due to his own efforts, and his regained independence only makes him feel the more duty bound to the service of God. But this consciousness of dependence on God and duty bound towards Him, entails no lessening of his happiness and no diminution of his regained richness of life. On the contrary, it is just in it that his worldly position receives its true value; it is just in the fact that we do thank God for all our deliverances and recoveries and our happiness, and that we have to devote our regained existence in His service that our happiness and joy in living becomes real and true, and our life full and rich; it is only in the Mazzo that our daily bread receives the “oil”.

But out of each of the ten loaves of the four kinds representing our contented material position in life, one has to be separated as תרומה and given to the כהן, i.e., to the section of the priests who are on duty on that day. Just as with תרומה ,ביכורים and חלה referring to the blessing granted to fields, granaries and homes, so here with this תרומת ה׳ given to the כהן from the תודה-loaves, the acknowledgment is made that not only the actual deliverance itself but the consciousness of its entailing active duty — the whole relationship of our life towards God, as is shown by the חמץ and מצה of the תודה — is entirely thanks to the תורה, as whose teacher and priest the כהן stands. It is solely in fulfilling its laws that we can pay our debt of gratitude to God. — In Menachoth 77b the question remains undecided whether this תרומה of the לחמי תודה has the full nature of תרומה so that its profane use could entail the penalty of מיתה and חומש.

V. 15. In verses 15—18 the laws are laid down regarding the limits of time within which the parts of the offerings which are to be eaten, may be eaten, נאכלין לשני ימים ולילה אחד ,נאכלין ליום אחד, as well as the laws of the associated נותר and חוץ למקומו :פגול being פסול and חוץ לזמנו being פגול. They are given here in connection with תודה and שלמים, these being the offerings at which the eating of the meat is specially characteristic, and the offerings are called by the name זבח, a meal, a “meal” offering.

ביום קרבנו יאכל, these words place the אכילה of the offering into the closest connection with its קריבה לה׳ and their essential belonging together is expressed by the command that both must be done on the same day. On the same day that the offering is brought “near to God”, its flesh must be eaten by man. And, moreover, as this “bringing it near to God” is not expressed as a verb, such as הקריבו as in v. 16, but as a noun describing the general name of all offerings, ביום קרבנו, “on the day that it becomes a קרבן״, this belonging together of the אכילה and the קריבה of everything that bears the name קרבן, and parts of which are to be eaten by human beings is declared. For all, the time of eating is limited to יום קרבנו. So that this norm applies not only to תודה, but also to, on the one hand לחמי תודה, and on the other, to אשם ,חטאת and מנחות. It would also include שלמים had not the Torah immediately in v. 16 given an extended period for that offering. The קריבה of קרבנות in animal-offerings is the זריקה and the preceding עבודות הדם, i.e., הולכה ,קבלה ,שחיטה and זריקה; in מנחות it is the parallel-running קמיצה procedures up to the הקטרת הקומץ which corresponds to the זריקת הדם. This “day of the offering”, as can be seen from the immediately following לא יניח ממנו עד בקר comprises the day and the following night up to the next morning. So that here in the Mikdosh, the day is reckoned from morning to morning, הלילה הולך אחר היום, in contrast to the ordinary day which is reckoned from night to night where היום הולך אחר הלילה (see note on Ex. 12,2).

V. 16. נדר .ואם נדר או נדבה (see note on Gen. 28,20); נדבה (see note on Ex. 27,2). Both are completely voluntary freewill offerings. נדר is an obligation laid on oneself in the formula: הרי עלי, “I take on myself to bring” (an offering); נדבה is dedicating an object in the formula הרי זו, “this is to be” (an offering). So that נדר is a personal obligation which rests on the person until it is fulfilled, for which the responsibility, אחריות, remains on the person until the vow undertaken is accomplished. Accordingly, if someone had taken on himself to bring an offering: הרי עלי שלמים וכו׳, and the animal which he then sets apart for this purpose dies or becomes פסול, he has to bring another one in its place. But נדבה is an obligation made solely for one special object. He dedicates a particular animal to be an offering, הרי זו שלמים וכו׳. If the animal then dies or becomes otherwise unable to be offered, the obligation ceases, as it did not extend beyond this animal. Both נדד and נדבה are placed here in contrast to תודה .תודה is a שלמים, the cause for which was brought about by external circumstances. What had occurred made it encumbent on the one who had been saved to express his feelings of gratitude by means of an offering. But the שלמים bearing the נדר or נדבה character is brought through no such occurrence having happened, it is not the expression of the feeling of having been saved from some danger, but is brought from the feeling of just nothing disturbing or extraordinary having happened to break the happy “harmony” of a contented condition of life.

ביום הקריבו את זבחו יאכל. The procedure by which the offering specially bears the name זבח is essentially the שחיטה indeed identical with זביחה which primarily means “killing for human consumption”. הקרבה is, as already remarked, applied specially to the זריקה by which the נפש is shown the way to the קרבת אלקים which it is seeking. In this joining up all these three factors, as it does not say, ביום הקריבו יאכל זבחו, but ביום הקריבו את זבחו יאכל, Zebachim 56b teaches that the אכילה is not only placed in connection with the זריקה but also with the שחיטה, so that the זריקה must also be done only on the same day as the ביום שאתה זובח אתה מקריבו :זביחה ביום שאי אתה זובח אי אתה מקריבו, so that דם נפסל בשקיעת החמה, with the setting of the sun, any blood which has not yet been brought onto the Altar may no longer be used. (No שחיטה or זריקה at all may be done after nightfall, see note on Ch. 6,2. See also תוספות ibid. ר״ת, differentiates between the expressions שקיעת החמה and משתשקע החמה, the former being the beginning and the latter the complete end of the setting of the sun with which the night begins. Between the two there is time to walk four מיל, i.e., four times 18 minutes). This is, accordingly, the law that the זריקה and אכילה must be done on the day of the שחיטה. But nevertheless the time during which the אכילה of שלמי נדר ונדבה may be done, is extended by וממחרת to the following day, but only to the extent that הנותר ממנו what was left over and not eaten on the first day may still be eaten on the following day. But the מצות is even for שלמים to eat meat primarily on the day of the ת״כ) זביחה). Even so the ו copul. in והנותר remains difficult. If one could take the יאכל already in v. 15, and again the ביום הקריבו את זבחו יאכל in v. 16 to mean — as can be seen in the case in the following v. 18 — not simply the actual eating, but the intention of eating at the time the offering was brought, מחשבת אכילה, then the ו in והנותר becomes completely understandable. It would read: “The meat of his “thanks”-שלמים must be intended to be eaten on the day on which it is offered etc. etc. But if it is a נדר or a נדבה then the intention must be to eat it on the day it is brought, and also on the following day, and what really does remain over (to that next day) is to be eaten”.

V. 17. ביום השלישי באש ישרף. The meat of שלמים may only be eaten till the night of the second day, i.e., during two days and the intervening night, שני ימים ולילה אחד, but it may only be burnt after daybreak of the third day, just as all פגול and נותר (according to ת״כ all פסולים) may only be burnt by day. (See note on Ex. 22,10).

V. 18. ואם האכל יאכל. In Zebachim 28, 29 the tradition is recorded that here it is not dealing with the case where the meat of the offering has actually been eaten on the third day, but only where the intention was present at the time when the offering was brought. The intention, at the time of the הקרבה of extending the time of eating beyond the prescribed limit, מחשבת חוץ לזמן, renders the קרבן unfit פסול to such a degree that even if this intention is not carried out, and everything is done in order, anybody eating of it, even within the prescribed time, incurs the penalty of כרת, a punishment which is here expressed by נשיאת עון, by the term ונשא עונו. This way of taking the text is quite in accordance with the canon, which, in any case, applies to all offerings, that the כפרה of the offering, its essential validity, is accomplished by the זריקה and which can not be upset retrospectively by anything that occurs after that ritual has been duly carried out. So that the actual eating of the meat after the second day could not render the offering פסול. The text itself also expressly refers the האכל יאכל ביום השלישי and its resulting פסול to the moment of the הקרבה by the words המקריב אתו לא יחשב לו, hence, בשעת הקרבה הוא נפסל ואינו נפסל בשלישי. Further, by the amplification האכל יאכל, the idea of the אכילה is extended to its fullest possible meaning: אחד אכילת אדם ואחד אכילת מזבח, and by it is to be understood the “consumption” by the Altar as well as the “consumption” by man. This אכילת מזבח includes every procedure by which anything of the offering is given to the Altar, so that it includes זריקה, שפיכת שירים והקטר חלבים. Further, in Zebachim 13a the expression האכל יאכל is taken to extend the moment when this פסול מחשבה applies, to every procedure that מביאין לידי אכילה, which brings about the אכילה of the offering which, apart from זריקה would be שחיטה, קבלה והולכה. The זריקה specially implied in the המקריב אותו is taken to be merely an example, יצאת להקיש אליה, it is picked out as an example to limit the application of פסול מחשבה to such עבודות on which, like זריקה the כפרה depends, עבודה מעכבת כפרה, with the exception of שפיכת דמים which is only מצוה but not מעכב (see above I,5). This פסול caused by מחשבת חוץ לזמנו is expressed here threefold: .פגול יהיה ,לא יחשב לו ,לא ירצה

— לא ירצה : in the ordinary case the זריקה of the blood assumes the personality represented by it as being in accordance with the Will of God, it places itself hereby ready to carry out the Will of God; but if one of the preceding rituals, or the זריקה itself, is connected with the intention of an unlawful אכילה, this relation of the personality to the רצון ה׳ is abrogated, and the purpose of the זריקה is defeated and made void. This implies that the actual פסול פגול only applies if and when the הרצאה would otherwise have been perfect, i.e., that the זריקה had been properly carried out. מחשבת הזמן only causes פגול if the הרצאה would otherwise be assured, it says לא ירצה which implies that the הרצאה is negatived by the כהרצאת כשר כן הרצאת פסול .מחשבת הזמן מה הרצאת כשר עד שיקריבו כל מתירין אף הרצאת פסול עד שיקריבו כל מתירין (Zebachim 28b — מתיר is that procedure which is the preliminary condition for permitting אכילת מזבח and אכילת אדם. At קרבנות בהמה this is the זריקת הדם, at מנחות it is the הקטרת קומץ). If, for instance, the שחיטה, the קבלה or הולכה had been done in the פגול intention, but the זריקה was not performed, the offering does not bear the character of לא יחשב לו — .פגול: Further, in ordinary cases the זריקה places the קרבן in relationship to the personality of the person who is bringing the offering; it is his נפש which is to be represented by the דם. But if the עבודות הדם is connected with a מחשבת הזמן this relationship is removed, לא יחשב לו: “the idea of the offering is not placed in relationship to him”. Here, too, is implied that, apart from this מחשבת פגול every other idea of the ideal relationship between the offering and the bringer, is present, there must be no other disturbing thought: לא יערב בו מחשבות אחרות. If, at the עבודת הדם there was another anomalous thought present, for instance, מחשבת חוץ למקומו (of which later), or in the case of a פסח offering or a חטאת it was שלא לשמה, so that the offering would in any case be פסול, then the offering does not receive the character of פגול. Both these laws עד שיקריבו כל מתירין and שלא יערב בו מחשבות אחרות which are necessary for the פגול-character are expressed by the formula: פגול יהיה — .ובלבד שיקריב המתיר כמצותו. The actual meaning of the root פגול is quite obscure. It only occurs here and in a similar connection in Ch. 19,7 and otherwise in מרק פגולים (Isaiah 65,4) and לא בא בפי בשד פגול (Ezek. 4,14) in both of which cases it also clearly refers to the condition forbidden by the Torah here. The phonetic relationship too, offers no analogy. Whether פגל could perhaps be identical with פלג and mean dividing, separating, estrangement and indeed carried to its utmost extreme, we only dare to suggest as a possibility. — עונה תשא, similarly in Ch. 19,8 referring to the related נותר it says ואכליו עונו ישא, which is immediately explained as אכילת פגול ונותר .ונכרתה הנפש ההיא מעמיה is, accordingly forbidden on pain of כרת (Zeb. 28b).

Zebachim (ibid) gives us the traditional law that not only מחשבת חוץ לזמנו but also חוץ למקומו (e.g. ,לזרוק דמו או להקטיר חלבו חוץ לעזרה לאכול בשר קדשים קלים חוץ לירושלים, לאכול בשר קדשי קדשים חוץ לעזרה) makes the offering פסול. But while חוץ לזמנו entails the penalty of כרת for anyone who eats of it, חוץ למקומו only makes the offering פסול but there is no כרת attached to it. In the Talmud חוץ לזמנו is always referred to as פגול and חוץ למקומו simply as פסול. The Halacha in itself is accepted quite unanimously. But regarding the indication of פסול חוץ למקומו in the text itself, which according to the wording, both here (called קרא אריכה) and in the shorter text in פרשת קדושים (Ch. 19,7) deals only with פסול חוץ לזמנו, the opinions differ. The final opinion, that of רבא which is identical with what he explains to be that of his teacher רבא, is that both are indicated in our text, the קרא אריכא; he says פגול זה חוץ ,שלישי זה חוץ לזמנו למקומו, and of the repetition in פ׳ קדושים he says שלישי דפרשת קדושים teaches that חוץ למקומו only makes the offering פסול when למקום שיהא משולש בדם בבשר ובאימודים. These sentences seem very difficult to understand. Firstly, his explanation that פגול means חוץ למקומו when the whole context of our verse seems to refer entirely to חוץ לזמנו and moreover in the Talmud is used exclusively for חוץ לזמנו. But, nevertheless, if our conjecture that the basic meaning of פגול is “separation” is not erroneous — and, as a matter of fact, both חוץ לזמנו and חוץ למקומו can be regarded simply as a “separation” of the אכילת מזבח or the אכילת אדם from the שחיטה — then פגול in the very first instance could mean a separation in place (— for it is really only in חוץ למקומו where the אכילה takes place in an unlawful place, that the wrongful separation of it from the זביחה in the עזרה is concretely apparent to everybody, whereas, in the case of חוץ לזמנו the unlawful separation from the זביחה is not at all directly apparent and can only be known to somebody who knew the day the offering was made— ) so that according to רבא our text would say: — “If, at the time when the offering was brought there was the intention to make a separation in time between the שחיטה and the אכילה then פגול יהיה, this separation in time, although the intention is to have the אכילה entirely within the precincts of the Mikdosh, shall be reckoned as if the intention had been to make a separation in place, and to eat it outside the Mikdosh, and indeed shall be forbidden even more strictly, so that if the intention is carried out and it is eaten beyond the set time, the penalty of כרת is incurred”. From this it would then be deduced that חוץ למקומו, “the separation in place” between the שחיטה and the אכילה, the intention to eat it outside the Mikdosh makes the offering פסול but that there is no כרת attached to such eating. About the condition that מקום שיהא משולש וכו׳ with which רבא limits the application of מחשבת חוץ למקומו various explanations are given in רש״י and תוספות. The chief difficulty to be considered is that יום השלישי undoubtedly speaks of חוץ לזמנו and here it is referred to חוץ למקומו. But if our explanation of רבא׳s exposition is right, then he is taking it that the text itself contains both חוץ לזמנו ,פסולים being mentioned only as a potenial מקומו, and then the modification of חוץ לזמנו given by יום השלישי by the repetition, could very well be transferred and made to apply to תוספות :חוץ למקומו could also be explained along similar lines viz., just as יום השלישי fixes a יום משולש for לזמנו, i.e., a time which is unlawful for all three parts of the offering, דם בשד ואימודים, so by its repetition it fixes similarly for חוץ למקומו, i.e., such a place where none of the three parts may lawfully be considered. In a word: מחשבת חוץ לזמנו as well as חוץ למקומו must refer to a time or to a place which is מופגל (according to our conjecture, as much as to say מופלג) which lies completely outside the sphere of offering, where neither דם nor בשר nor אימורים have any lawful right to be.

All the above is summed up in the two sentences of Mishna in Zebachim 27b & 29b: השוחט את הזבח לזרוק דמו בחוץ או מקצת דמו בחוץ להקטיר אימוריו בחוץ או מקצת אימוריו בחוץ לאכול בשרו בחוץ או כזית מבשרו בחוץ פסול ואין בו כרת לזרוק דמו למחר או מקצת דמו למחר להקטיר אימוריו למחר או מקצת אימוריו למחר לאכול בשרו למחר או כזית מבשרו למחר פגול וחייבין עליו כרת זה הכלל כל השוחט והמקבל והזורק לאכול דבר שדרכו לאכול ולהקטיר דבר שדרכו להקטיר כזית חוץ למקומו פסול ואין בו כרת חוץ לזמנו פגול וחייבין עליו כרת ובלבד שיקריב המתיר כמצותו.

We have already remarked that the הקטרת ,הולכה ,נתינה בכלי ,קמיצה הקומץ in מנחות have the same signification as the four עבודות הדם have at a קרבן בהמה and מחשבת חוץ לזמנו ומקומו such as הקומץ לאכול שיריה בחוץ etc., at a מנחה would have exactly the same results as at a קרבן בהמה. See Menachoth 11b et seq. Whether the מחשבה must actually be expressed in words to make the קרבן posul or whether simply having the intention in one’s mind is sufficient is not quite decided. See מל״מ on פה״מ 12, 1.

If we try to find out the underlying thoughts which are expressed in the laws contained in vv. 15—18, we find that they all deal with the relationship which the ritual of the אכילה of an offering bears to that of the שחיטה, or respectively to the קמיצה. First we get the law that תודה and similarly all other offerings, except בכור מעשר ושלמים may only be eaten on the day of the שחיטה or מנחות on the day of the קמיצה and on the following night, i.e., יום ולילה, but שלמים and likewise בכור ומעשר, one day longer, i.e., שני ימים ולילה אחד. That which is not consumed within these times must be burnt by day. From this follows the law that זריקה too, as part of the idea of אכילת מזבח must also be done on the same day as the שחיטה before sunset. We have already heard in Ch. VI that the second act of אכילת מזבח, the הקטר חלבים ואיברים, may be done during the whole of the succeeding night which belongs to the day of the offering. So that, taken together, we have it that אכילת אדם as well as אכילת מזבח must be done on the same “sacrificial day” (i.e., day and following night. I.L.) as that on which the שחיטה was done, and only in the case of שלמים the time is extended for אכילת אדם. But the idea expressed by this hanging together of שחיטה and אכילת אדם ומזבח must be of such essential importance and meaning that if, at any of the four עבודות הדם which determine the character of the offering any idea of disturbing this connection is only entertained, such intention destroys the whole validity of the offering, and the intention to eat it beyond the set time would forbid any eating of it at all under pain of כרת.

זביחה ,שחיטה, representing the giving up of uncontrolled selfish life forms the negative side of the ritual of offerings, it is the negation of the life hitherto led. הקטרה ,זריקה and אכילת בשר, the אכילת מזבח ואדם, forms the positive side. In it the living for oneself which had been denied by the שחיטה receives the purpose of living in a higher sphere for holy things; in אכילת אדם, in receiving back that which had been offered, the act of eating itself is given an elevated, more holy meaning. Both these aspects belong essentially together and are mutually necessary to each other. The Torah only demands the giving up of a purely material physical life, for the purpose of allowing it to rise up again to a higher and fuller life, lived for God, and for the fulfilment of His Will on earth; and this higher life, living an earthly existence near to God, makes it an indispensable condition that a purely physical life ruled by selfish urges alone, must be given up. זביחה only for the purpose of אכילה, and no אכילה without זביחה. Separated from each other, זביחה without אכילה would represent self-destruction without any moral purpose, and אכילה without זביחה an apotheosis of the flesh, raising uncontrolled emancipation of the senses to the ideal godly vocation of Man. Brought as a קרבן as a means of getting near to God, and directed towards God, the former, זביחה without אכילה, would represent the metaphysical lie of the heathen idea that self-destruction is an act which gratifies and appeases the gods who are jealous and wrathful beings; while the latter, אכילה without זביחה, would represent the ethical lie of the heathen idea, that divine forces are honoured by our satisfying our senses, and so unbridled yielding to them is raised to a sacred ritual. זביחה without אכילה lowers the conception of God to a blood-thirsty deity, אכילה without זביחה, the Temple to the consecration of orgies of unbridled licence. We can understand the demand: ביום הקריבו את זבחו יאבל ,ביום קרבנו יאכל; by the insistence on the close connection being kept between the זריקה and the אכילה to the זביחה, the purity of the moral idea of both is safeguarded. We can also understand why the Torah picks out just תודה and שלמים as examples for the teaching of this canon which ensures the truth and morality of the whole idea of offering. It is just these particular offerings which are brought out of our feelings of the dependance of our fate being on God, and their whole purpose being the consecration of our joy and happiness in the condition of our life. And it is just in this consciousness and in these efforts to keep our happiness that these heathen lies, these false conceptions of the gods, which destroy Truth and Morality, find their most responsive soil. It is, accordingly, on the ideas of these offerings that the perniciousness of the erroneous opinions which this law of אכילה and זביחה is to counter, shows itself in the most obvious likelihood. We can also understand the law that נותר ביום באש ישרף and אוכליו עונו ישא כי את קדש ה׳ חלל ונכרתה הנפש ההיא מעמיה (Ch. 19,8). נותר, a piece of זביחה separated from the בשר קדשים represents אכילה not on the basis of זביחה, represents material enjoyment, satisfaction of the senses in freedom, uncontrolled by the laws of morality of God. Eaten as something holy as part of קדשים, it would be the absolute reversal, the complete desecration of the Sanctuary of God, which is nothing else but the Sanctuary of His Torah; its very existence is already treachery towards the holiness of this Sanctuary, and its destruction by fire is restitution of this holiness, which therefore, like every other holy ritual of the Mikdosh, may only be done by day.

We have now still to consider why the limit of the time for אכילת אדם should be extended for שלמים. The extension is not granted for the addition of a whole extra day; it is not שני ימים ושני לילות but only שני ימים ולילה אחד, two days and the intervening night. At nightfall of the second day it already becomes נותר, but must wait till the following day before it is burnt because all שריפת קדשים must be done ביום. So that it is only the day following the first night which is drawn in, to be included in the time permitted for the eating of the meat of the offering. Now we know that in the Mikdosh the night belongs to the preceding day while outside the Mikdosh the day belongs to the preceding night. But the fundamental character of the שלמים consists in the fact that its בשר may be eaten outside the Mikdosh, נאכלין בכל העיר, giving the clear idea that nearness to God is not to be found only in the Mikdosh but also in ordinary home family life, and it is to consecrate the family circle to a Temple of God. Now, just as the domain of the Mikdosh is extended in space, to draw the homely family circle into its sphere, so is this extension in time, too, the apt expression for this drawing the ordinary family life into the consecration of the Temple of God. For שני ימים ולילה אחד is nothing but a drawing of the civil day into the “sanctuary” day; one day being a combination of the two days. It begins in the Mikdosh and ends outside in civil life. The Mikdosh day includes the following night, but outside the Mikdosh that night has the following day attached to it. (Elsewhere Hirsch has given, the beautiful symbolism of the ideal day of the Mikdosh, starting with dawn, and although it passes through a period of darkness and night, it ends again with a new dawn, while outside, until the golden age returns, the day starts in darkness, and although it passes through a period of bright mid-day light, it ends again in night and death. I.L.). But תודה is brought about by having experienced the salvation of God. The Hand of God, directing our fate, has manifested itself in our life. Here, above all, the necessity is present to have the אכילה — the whole future enjoyment of the restored well-being which God has granted us — in the clearest and most definite manner, only on the grounds of the זביחה. That we have been saved from a danger makes us vow, with even deeper fervour than ordinarily, that we will use and enjoy the pleasures of life only on the basis of giving everything in our lives completely up to the Will of God. This consideration may well be the reason for giving the אכילה of the תודה the narrow limits of קדשי קדשים in its connection with זביחה.

If, then, at the עבודות הדם — at that ritual of the offerings which, by expressing the new relation to God, for which the נפש is henceforth to strive, decides the whole character of the offering — there is such a thought present, an intention of separating the זביחה from the אכילה, the אכילה from the זביחה, even if concerns only the smallest portion of the offering worth mentioning, כזית הראוי לאכילה או להקטרה, then the whole truth and purity of the idea of the offering is thereby changed into its very opposite; לא ירצה ולא יחשב לו, neither God’s satisfaction, the fulfilment of His Will, nor the idea of showing Man what he is meant to be and to do, can be represented by such a זביחה or by such אכילת מזבח ואדם. Such self-destruction on the one hand, and such lack of control of living and desiring on the other hand, is the very opposite of the Divine Will and of Man’s mission in life, פגול יהיה. Although the separation is only in time and even only in the mind, in intention, and all is to be kept within the precincts of the Mikdosh, nevertheless the offering is to be considered as “torn to bits” in its essential factors, and as if it had been actually separated in place. More, just because the killing of the pure idea of the offering takes place within the Mikdosh itself and so might appear to be sanctioned and in accordance with the teaching of the Mikdosh, the thought of the separation of the two factors of the offering by “time” מחשבת חוץ לזמנו is a still more complete killing of the idea of the Mikdosh than חוץ למקומו than the separation by “place”. מחשבת חוץ למקומו, the intention to do the הקטרה ,זריקה or אכילת בשר קדש outside the precincts of the מקדש is turning your back to the Sanctuary of God, and makes it appear that such separation of these factors is not permissable only on the ground of the Sanctuary of the Torah. But מחשבת חוץ לזמנו has the intention of tearing apart these factors of the קדשים within the Mikdosh itself, and so gives the impression that it is sanctioned by the Mikdosh. חוץ למקומו only makes the offering פסול and not חייב כרת, while חוץ לזמנו is פגול and חייב כרת. In the same way, giving up Judaism, turning one’s back entirely to the Sanctuary of the Torah is not the most dangerous attack for the Jewish Sanctuary. The Sanctuary is only then threatened with destruction when the defection is carried into the Sanctuary itself imagining one can remain on the standpoint of the Mikdosh in spite of introducing one’s own ideas which are the reverse of its ideas. That is פגול and that is also why it is only then פגול when קרב המתיר במצותו, when everything else has remained normal, when no other abnormality has already made the offering invalid. פסול. For only then would this tearing asunder of the most intimately connected moments of the קדשים appear as being sanctioned as a perfectly normal proceeding.

Vv. 19—21.—These verses add two other conditions besides נותר and פגול in which the meat of the offering may not be eaten. In verse 19 בשר קדשים שנטמא, and in vv. 20 & 21, בשר קדשים טהור בטומאת הגוף. The former טומאת עצמו is בלאו, the latter בטומאת הגוף is והבשר .בכרת, and also the בשר, at the end of the verse, quite clearly refers to בשד קדשים of which the preceding verses were speaking, and also v. 20 shows it expressly. But the fact that the טומאה-and-טהרה teaching when referring here to אכילת בשר קדשים calls the meat simply בשד (and not בשר קדשים. I.L.) may be to teach us that this insistence on טומאה being such an opposite idea to that of קדשים as well as indeed to the whole idea of טהרה which is so prominent with קדשים is, in its real depth, no far fetched high-flown idea, but nothing more than what is founded on the ordinary inner nature, and the real vocation of human beings. It is only that it is made so prominent in קדשים because the whole of all קדשים are meant to be symbolically teaching and preaching at every stage. But the Truth that is taught symbolically in קדשים is to be actually realised in the whole of our lives. After all, we know of men who took the realisation of this moral and mental “purity” of life so much to heart that they were led to apply the symbolic teaching of טהרה which the Torah only prescribes for קדשים to the whole of their ordinary lives and to לאכול חוליהן בטהרה, a tendency which we find in full swing already in the time of Saul and David (see Sam. I. 21,6).

We have already repeatedly had occasion to define the idea which is meant to be realised by טומאה and טהרה. It is quite clear that טומאה is the “lack of freedom”. Everything which shows “organic life having to submit to physical pressure” is an encouragement to apply this idea to human beings, who are called to moral and mental freedom. The most striking example of such forced submission is, of course, a dead body. Etymologically the idea of טמא can be found from its relation to דמע ,טמע and also טמה of the rabbinic idiom (cf. יורד לטמיון), all of which have the basic meaning of giving up, a sinking of independence into that of something else. So that concretely טמא would be, that which has given up the freedom of a living independent existence, and symbolically, that which would be liable to destroy moral and mental freedom in the minds of those that come into contract with it, to drag them down into the depressed state of feeling that they are not independently master of themselves, that, willy-nilly they have to do things. טהר (Hirsch proves etymologically too. I.L.) on the other hand, would be, concretely, an existence developing itself free from all estranging forces, in complete freedom under the mastery of its own pure principles; and symbolically, all that which is liable to represent to the mind a condition of moral free will, mastery of oneself, without having to submit to the force of anything exterior to oneself.

In Yebamoth 74b, תלתא קראי, three verses are explained in which the condition of טומאה seems to run in three different stages: Ch. 22,6. לא יאכל מן הקדשים כי אם רחץ בשרו במים, where the eating of קדשים is made dependent only on the טבילה; ibid 7: ובא השמש וטהר ואחר יאכל מן הקדשים, where the setting of the sun is demanded before eating; and finally, Ch. 13,8: וכפר עליה הכהן וטהרה, where the return of טהרה is attached to the bringing of an offering, as is prescribed for זב וזבה יולדת ומצורע. The meaning of these three successive stages is there explained that a טבול יום — as one who is טמא is called after the טבילה but before הערב שמש, before sunset — may eat מעשר שני but not yet תרומה or קדשים; with הערב שמש comes the permission to eat תרומה too; but with טומאות which entail the bringing of a קרבן, contact with קדשים is only permitted after it has been brought, hence one who is מחוסר כפרה, while he may eat תרומה may not eat קדשים. Parallel to these three stages in which the condition of טומאה of a person passes away, there are three degrees of טומאה for the objects which cause it. The origin of a טומאה e.g., a נבלה is called אב הטומאה, what it touches becomes ראשון, what the ראשון touches becomes שני and so on to שלישי and רביעי, and the response of an object to טומאה depends on, and rises with its degree of holiness. Ordinary objects חולין are not responsive to any טומאה beyond a טמא ראשון the rule being אין שני עושה שלישי בחולין, but תרומה is responsive to a שני, and קדשים even to a שלישי. So that a טבול יום stands at the degree of a שני and a מחוסר כפרה of a שלישי. A stage within which an object becomes טמא but can not transmit it further is called פסול and not טמא. Accordingly שני is פסול for שלישי ,חולין for רביעי ,תרומה for א׳ י״ח ,פסחים קדשים & Chagiga 24a). According to Rashi, מחוסר כפרה and שלישי for קדש are only מעלות דרבנן, but תוספות disagrees, and so does רמב״ם in הל׳ אבות הטומאות 11, 4. Now it says here: והבשר אשר יגע בכל טמא וגו׳. But in Ch. 11,33, the טמא which is in a כלי חרש, which has become טמא through a שרץ, is called: כל אשר בתוכו יטמא, and the the dead שרץ is אב, the כלי חרש is ראשון, and the contents would be שני. So that under the term בכל טמא of our text we must in any case include שני and accordingly שני must עושה שלישי בקדש. But that nevertheless שלישי is not to be included too, and that שלישי עושה רביעי בקדש is derived by deduction, ק״ו from מחוסר כפרה (Pesachim and Chagiga ibid).

In Sota 29a it is pointed out that in our verse, in the case of טומאת בשר, the איסור אכילה is made dependent on the existing טומאה being positively there, while for טומאת הגוף it puts it that the היתר אכילה is dependent on the existing טהרה being positively there. From this is deduced that where the object is טומאה the איסור only comes with the certainty of the טומאה, while where the person is טומאה the איסור comes already if the טהרה is only doubtful: והבשר אשר יגע בכל טמא לא יאכל ודאי טמא הוא דלא יאכל הא ספק טמא וספק טהור יאכל אימא סיפא והבשר כל טהור יאכל בשר ודאי טהור הוא דיאכל בשר הא ספק טמא וספק טהור לא יאכל, and on that רב גידל אמר בר explains that canon, so significant for הלכות טומאה, viz. דבר שיש בו דעת לישאל ספיקו טמא דבר שאין בו דעת לישאל ספיקו טהור and this הלכה is complemented by ר׳ יוחנן in Pesachim 19b, by ספק טומאה הבאה בידי אדם נשאלין עליה אפילו בכלי המונח על גבי קרקע כדבר שיש בו דעת לישאל. Accordingly the canon would run thus:— A doubt which arises over the טומאה or טהרה condition of an object which is devoid of reason, unable to be called upon to give an account, is to be taken as טהור, e.g., a piece of meat next to which is a שרץ טמא and it is doubtful whether they have been in contact. But if the doubt is about the condition or activity of a person, who is gifted with reason and is able to be called upon to give an account of his actions and condition, e.g., a grown-up human being, then the doubt must be treated as טמא. In the corresponding case of סוטה where similarly there is ספק טומאה, and indeed where it concerns not a question of symbolic טומאה, but of a real moral טומאה, and this ספק it treated as אסור and where the text runs ונסתרה והיא נטמאה, the canon receives the further modification that the doubt, in a case of דבר שיש בו דעת לישאל, is only then to be treated as טמא when it is במקום סתירה, in a רשות היחיד, where the personality concerned is alone, but not ברשות הרבים, where it is not alone, but together with the public, which is represented by at least three persons, so that the doubt would not have to be taken as טמא if it arose when there were even only two other people present. The whole rule then runs: — דבר שיש בו דעת ברשות היחיד ספיקו טמא ברשות הרבים ספיקו טהור ושאין בו דעת לישאל בין ברשות היחיד בין ברשות הרבים ספיקו טהור (סוטה כ״ח ב׳).

If, as it seems to be, according to תוספות in Nidda 2a and רמב״ם (הל׳ אבות הטומאה 16, 3 et seq.) in the case of doubtful טומאה, where it concerns an inanimate object, even in ספק השקול, where there is no presumption of טהרה to tip the balance, it is to be treated as טהור, and where a living person is concerned, דבר שיש בו דעת לישאל, even if there is a presumption of חזקת טהרה ,טהור, it must be treated as טמא, then in the case of the inanimate object we should have a much more lenient treatment than we find at all other איסורים, and especially having regard to the view accepted by the far greater majority of authorities that the rule is מדאורייתא that ספק דאורייתא לחומרא (see above on אשם תלוי). We believe we can see in this as in many other laws of טומאה which we shall have to consider in Ch. 11,29 et seq. — an indication of the Torah’s intent to oppose any idea in the whole realm of טומאה a complex of the whole working of some invisible concrete magic influence. For were this to be the case, did some magic concrete evil influence cling to the object which comes into contact with the טומאה, then surely any such doubtful cases would not be treated more leniently than any other איסור it would come into the sphere of סכנה to which the rule applies: חמירא סכנתא מאיסודא. But herein we see one of the many proofs that the whole realm of הלכות טומאה belong to the category of symbolic laws, i.e., to those laws by which the most important moral truths are brought home to us and kept in our minds. This is shown clearly too, to mention the most general, first of all, by the fact that the Torah does not forbid anyone who is not a כהן to become טמא, to מטמא himself deliberately, and even the כהן is only forbidden טומאת מת, but otherwise both for him and everybody else, the prohibition only comes into effect at the time when one is about to come into contact with מקדש וקדשים.

On the other hand, for דבר שיש בו דעת לישאל, where the doubt concerns the condition or the activity of an intelligence which can be asked to give an account of itself, we have a stricter teaching, to treat even the doubtful cases as טמא. Here we think we come across the same idea which rated ידיעת הטומאה as being worthy to be picked out from all the other laws to be ranked along with שמיעת הקול and שבועת בטוי, to form the class of קרבן עולה ויורד. The consciousness of a personal God, able to exercise completely His free Will, and of human beings similarly able to exercise their own free will, which the הלכות טומאה are meant to keep clear and lucid in our minds, is so much the fundamental basis of all the convictions of Judaism, to the exercise of which מקדש וקדשיו direct us, that we can well understand that just as any forgetfulness of these laws had to be brought to our minds by a special measure of atonement, so here, the conscious Jewish intelligence is allowed to eat קדשים only if there is not the slightest doubt of its condition being entirely טומאה-free, and also that all objects touched by it can only be declared as טומאה-free, if it is a position to represent their טהרה with absolute certainty.

The law which restricts this חומרא of דבר שיש בו דעת לישאל only to רשות היחיד and declares ספק טומאה ברשות הרבים, as טהור is placed by the Jerushalmi (see תוספות Sota 28b), and also by רמב״ם (הל׳ טומאה 16, 1), in connection with that other important Halacha according to which טומאה דחויה בצבור, that טומאה subsides when faced by the totality of the public, and that צבור עושין פסח בטומאה בזמן שרובו של צבור טמאין, the Nation, if the majority of it is in a state of being טמא, brings the Pessach offering בטומאה (see on Numbers IX). In this Halacha the moral height of a human community is shown clearly. אין צבור מת, a community does not die, the Nation knows no death, and the individual too, in as far as he dedicates the efficacy of his earthly life to the community, rescues the fruit of his life here below over and beyond death, already here below he partakes of immortality. Naturally such a point of view does not look on the idea of a Community as being a union of so and so many persons of so and so much material power. Then the community, the Nation and its efforts would lie, even as the individual does, under the power of death and transitoriness. It looks on the Nation as being the eternal bearer of the eternal moral spiritual Truths of Mankind, as representing the never-dying moral spiritual immortality of Mankind. It regards these truths as being the inner heart that holds the Nation together, so that the Nation itself is a representation of moral freedom being the nature of human beings, to such an extent that before it, in its presence, the possible danger of transferring the existing physical טומאה-subjection into the realm of moral freedom, retires into the shade and טומאה דחויה בצבור. And this, this idea of the Community and its innate representation of טהרה, of freedom, of self-control and self-determination in all moral spiritual matters, is also of such positive influence that if a טומאה-doubt arises under its aegis ברשות בפגי שלשה ,הרבים, it tips the scale for טהרה, and, as the Jerushalmi puts it, ספק טומאה דחויה בצבור, i.e., ספק טומאה ברה״ר ספיקו טהור.

That אכילת בשר בטומאת הגוף, when the person is טמא is punishable by כרת, while אכילת בשר שנטמא, when the meat is טמא, is only בלאו, is a simple prohibition, may be due to the consideration that in the latter case, in טומאת בשר, the קדש, idea has already been actually spoilt by טומאה, whereas in the case of טומאת הגוף it is the person himself who brings the disturbing element of טומאה to the high moral idea of the קדש in the very moment and at the very procedure in which, and at which, that idea is to be brought home in its highest degree of completion, to the whole being of the person concerned by אכילת קדשים. The moment a person becomes טמא, it is his duty to keep himself away from the Mikdosh and from eating קדשים, a duty which, even if transgressed in error, has to be atoned for by a קרבן עולה ויורד. By implication, by the idea of כולל (see note on v. 24) this duty is extended even to קדשים which have already become טמא and הטמא שאכל בין קדש טמא בין קדש טהור חייב (Zebachim 106a & 108a).

Just as the duty of burning is prescribed here for בשר שנטמא and (in v. 17) for נותר so the Halacha gives the traditional law, that this duty applies to all פסולי קדש, both קדשים קלים and קדשי קדשים. In all cases the virtue of the קדש-idea, which has been injured by the פסול, must be restored by means of שריפה (Pesachim 82b). If the פסול is on the בשר itself, as in יוצא (נותר) לן or טמא and also פגול then it is to be burnt immediately כל שפסולו בגופו ישרף מיד. But if the פסול lies external to the object to be burnt, e.g., the meat itself is quite alright, but the זריקה had not been done because the blood had been split, or בשר פסח which may only be eaten למנויו has now no אוכלים as all the בעלים have become טמא, then one has to wait for the burning till the next day, so that the meat becomes נותר as well, as the פסול does then rest objectively on it. This leaving it over night for this purpose is called עבור צורה, one leaves it “to become stale”, to loose its freshness, so that the פסול is recognisable on it. כל שפסולו בגופו ישרף מיד, בדם ובבעלים תעובר צורתן ויוצאין לבית השריפה (Pesachim 34b). Exactly the same procedure has to be followed if the פסול is only doubtful. By עבור צורה the פסול is allowed to become a certainty before the burning takes place (ibid 34a).

From the sentence: כל טהור יאכל בשד, the ת״כ learns further that anybody who is טהור may join the sacrificial family meal of שלמים. It need not be restricted, as the similar Pessach meal has to be, to a closed company which has been decided on beforehand.

That verse 20 speaks solely of טומאת הגוף and not of טומאת בשר. Zebachim 43b teaches that we can see it indicated inter alia also from the expression וטומאתו עליו, “while his טומאה is still upon him”, which clearly infers that the טומאה-condition is not a permanent one, טומאה פורחת ממנו. But this is only the case is טומאת הגוף, where טהרה can be regained by מקוה. But בשר שנטמא can not become טהור again by immersion in a מקוה.

V. 21. In v. 20, by וטומאתו עליו, primarily טומאה שיצא עליו מגופו, a טומאה which arises from bodily conditions such as וזב ,מצורע etc., is indicated. Now, v. 21 expressed the same liability of כרת for טומאה which is transmitted by נגיעה, and mentions both קלות and קלות .חמורות as שרץ and חמורות as מצורע ,זב ,מת etc. (טומאת אדם), and between the two (בהמה טמאה) טומאת נבלה, to teach us, as ת״כ explains, both that כרת is imposed also on קלות in case of טומאת הגוף and that also in חמורות only a לאו but no כרת is imposed in cases of טומאת בשר.

V. 22. Up till now, all the ordinances in Ch. VI & VII, completing the laws of the offerings, were expressly directed to the priests, for the duty of carrying them out lay primarily on them. Now two paragraphs follow beginning with v. 21 & v. 28 which are addressed directly to the people. Now if the second one, v. 28 et seq. quite definitely deals with supplementary instructions which the people have to carry out with a שלמים offering, and so, continues and is closely connected with the laws of the שלמים of vv. 11—21, it is evident that the intervening paragraph, dealing with the prohibition of eating חלב and דם must be connected with the immediately preceding laws of the שלמים, and the whole of these laws given in vv. 22—27 (which are supplementary to the prohibition of eating חלב and דם already given above in Ch. 3,17) must be taken as being in the closest connection with the offerings and regarded as a result of these offering-laws for the people.

And actually the כל חלב וכל דם לא תאכלו of Ch. 3,17 above is also only the concluding sentence of the ordinances for the שלמים-offering, and is a result of the preceding כל חלב לה׳; and there we have already considered the prohibition of חלב and דם from that point of view, and recognised in it a sequence of the offering-laws, unlimited by time or place — חקת עולם בכל מושבותיכם — to remain of ever-lasting significance in our daily life.

V. 23. Here, first of all, the prohibition of חלב is restricted to שור כבש ועז, altogether only to animals which are used for the offerings — עוף and חיה have no forbidden חלב, and כוי, a cross between a חיה and a בהמה, is in a class by itself, whose חלב as ספק אסור — and further only to those חלב-parts which are common to all these three kinds of animals. אליה which is reckoned amongst the חלבים which are to be brought on to the Altar, only in the case of כבש is accordingly excluded from the prohibition.

On the other hand, the prohibition is extended by the term חלב. For, whereas the עונש, the punishment of כרת, runs כי כל אוכל חלב (v. 25) and not כי כל אוכל כל חלב, and in accordnace with the traditional Halacha, which applies to all אכילה-prohibitions, remains restricted to at least a כזית, the אזהרה, the prohibition, here runs: כל חלב לא תאכלו, so that, as for all איסורים in the Torah: חצי שיעור אסור מן התורה, the smallest quantity of any forbidden object is forbidden, although punishment is only incurred if כזית is eaten (Yoma 74a).

V. 24. The combined case of חלב נבלה וגו׳ teaches several things. We learn from it that חלב as well as נבלה and טרפה are only forbidden to be eaten, but may be used for any other purpose, מותר בהנאה. For, according to the opinion of ר׳ אבהו which is accepted as Halacha (Pesachim 21b), wherever אכילה is forbidden it is to be taken that אסור הנאה is meant as well, unless the Torah expressely allows it, as here. Moreover, for all the three איסורים mentioned in our verse, the permission of הנאה is clear from other places. For נבלה we have the express permission in Deut. 14,21, and according to ר׳ עקיבא (Pesachim 23b) the היתר הנאה for חלב is implied, together with the permission for נבלה as he says: כשהוחרה נבלה חלבה וגידה נמי הותרו, in the היתר הנאה of נבלה, all parts of the animal, which would include חלב, are included. For טרפה the היתר הנאה is already contained in the verse (Ex. 22,30): לכלב תשליכון אותו, where the feeding of your animals is allowed with טריפה. So that, according to ר״ע, our verse here would teach primarily that חלב נבלה is not included in טומאת נבלה, and is not טמא hence can be used לכל מלאכה even for מלאכת הקדש, as: לאיסור והיתר לא צריך קרא כי איצטריך קרא לטומאה ולטהרה. But as the Torah expresses this freeing of the חלב from טומאת נבלה in connection with חלב טרפה and with the prohibition of eating either of them, ואכל לא תאכלוהו, the טהרה of חלב from טומאת נבלה is expressed only for such animals where the טרפה abnormality makes a difference but not for a בהמה טמאה and also only for such animals whose חלב is forbidden to be eaten, but not for a חיה. Hence, חלב בהמה טמאה וחלב חיה are not exempt from טומאת נבלה and only חלב בהמה טהורה is טהור מטומאת נבלה (Zebachim 70a & b).

ואכל לא תאכלוהו. Although the חלב does not come under the idea of נבלה with regards to טומאה, still regarding אכילה the איסור נבלה does apply to the חלב and who eats חלב נבלה transgresses both the איסור נבלה and the איסור חלב and is punishable for both. And the same applies to אמרה התורה יבוא איסור נבלה ויחול על איסור חלב יבוא איסור טריפה :חלב טריפה ויחול על איסור חלב (Chulin 37a). Here we have the far reaching canon for the whole of the איסור-והיתר-laws: that איסור חל על איסור, that an object forbidden on two counts can be punishable for both of them by one transgression. But this is only the case in איסור כולל ,איסור מוסיף or איסור בבת אחת, but not in איסור כולל .איסור גרידא means cases when the second איסור affects more objects than were already affected by the first איסור. In such cases that which was already prohibited by the first איסור is further affected by the second one. In our problem, the איסור of נבלה and of טרפה is a כולל one compared to חלב. By the איסור חלב only certain parts of the animal are forbidden. If the animal dies or is fatally wounded, by the איסור נבלה or the איסור טריפה, the whole of the animal, which up to then was not forbidden, becomes implicated, including the part that was already forbidden as איסור מוסיף ,חלב means cases when the second איסור does not affect more objects than were prohibited by the first, but the same object becomes forbidden in other respects to those in which it was already forbidden. (While איסור כולל is an added איסור, in extensiveness איסור מוסיף is one in intensiveness. I.L.). For instance, איסור קדשים would be an איסור מוסיף to the איסור of חלב. As חלב of an ordinary animal it is only אסור באכילה, if the animal becomes שלמים and its חלב belongs to the מזבח, it becomes also אסור בהנאה. But inasmuch as the איסור קדשים affects the הנאה of the חלב, which up to then had not been forbidden, the איסור קדשים is applied to its whole extent, i.e., also regarding the איסור אכילה and איסור קדשים חל על איסור חלב, and חלב of קדשים is אסור באכילה on both counts. Hence Kerithoth 13b gives us the poser: יש אוכל אכילה אחת וחייב עליה ארבע חטאות ואשם אחד : טמא שאכל חלב והיה נותר מן המקודשין ביום הכפורים. For קדשים, by which the חלב becomes also אסור בהנאה, and נותר, by which it becomes also אסור for לגבוה (מזבח) are איסור מוסיף, and טומאת הגוף, which extends its prohibition to all objects which are קדש, and יום הכפורים, which applies to all eatables, are איסור כולל (see Rashi ibid and Shevuoth 24b, and Yebamoth 32b & 33a). But if the second איסור is neither extensively nor intensively more comprehensive than the first, e.g., אבר מן החי and טרפה which are both only אסור באכילה and both affect the whole of the animal, then one can only be liable for both of them if both prohibitions occur simultaneously, בבת אחת, if, for instance, a part was removed from the living animal, by which, at the same time, it becomes טרפה. Provided, of course, that the assumption is valid, that אבר מן החי only starts with the severance of the member, and is not considered as existing always on every living animal, that we say בהמה בחייה לאו לאברים עומדת. If the other view is accepted, viz., that the איסור of אבר מן החי exists from the moment of birth of an animal, these two איסורים could only occur simultaneously, if the טרפה-making would have occurred at the moment of birth (Chulin 103a).

V. 25. כי כל אכל חלב וגו׳. It is impossible that the אשר יקריב is meant to restrict the prohibition of חלב to animals that are actually brought as offerings.
