Against this idea, the fact already speaks that it is unrestricted by time or place, by חקת עולם לדורתיכם בכל משבתיכם, above in Ch. 3,17. It expressly states clearly that it is forbidden in times and places where the bringing of offering is altogether forbidden. And further the immediately preceding verse also speaks against it, for there the prohibition of חלב is applied to נבלה and טריפה, which are unfit to be brought as offerings. And finally the wording of our text itself speaks against it. The חלב of a sacrificial animal is itself אשה לה׳, so that it need only to have said: כי כל אוכל חלב אשר יקריב לה׳. But חלב מן הבהמה אשר יקריב ממנה אשה לה׳ clearly designates only the kind of animal whose חלב comes under the prohibition of חלב, and as a logical consequence too, the kind of חלב. Only the fat of such animals of the classes that could be brought as offerings, and only those fat parts of such animals which were brought on the Altar as אשה are forbidden as חלב and the eating of such חלב only, is punishable by כרת. More, as כי כל אוכל וגו׳ is clearly given as the reason for the preceding חלב נבלה וחלב טרפה גו׳, the prohibition must include such animals too, which, as for instance בעלי מומין similarly to נבלה וטריפה are fit to be used for offerings as far as their species go, but which have forfeited this fitness by some external cause. (See Pesachim 43b & Rambam). At the same time, it only includes in the prohibition of חלב such parts of fat of the animal which above in Ch. 3,3 & 4, are designated to be placed on the Altar fire These fats differ from other fat parts of the animal in being תותב קרום ונקלף, that they form a separate solid layer of fat, encrusted by a skin or membrane which is easily peeled off. Certain membranes and threads of fat which are attached to this חלב (קרומין וחוטין etc.) are אסור and have to be porged out, but are not under the ban of כרת. It is characteristic, that, whereas blood is אסור from the very earliest stage of embryonic formation, חלב is only considered technically as such, when the embryonic formation is completed חדשים גרמי (it is dependent on the number of months); according to תוספות (Chulin 75a & 103a) only at complete maturity and birth.

V. 26. Although, above in Ch. 3,17, the prohibition of blood is given in conjunction with that of חלב in reference to the laws of the offerings, nevertheless it goes much farther than the range of animals affected by the איסור of חלב. That, equally with חלב, the prohibition is not merely to קדשים is clear from בכל מושבתיכם. But by לעוף ולבהמה it is applied to all the higher mammals, בהמה וחיה, and to all birds. The blood of the lower animals has only the same meaning as their flesh. Hence the blood of “pure” fish and locust (of the species that may be eaten, of course. I.L.). is permitted to be eaten, only by itself it should not be drunk on account of מראית עין, unless its source of origin is clearly discernable, for instance, if it is fish blood and fish scales are floating all over it. The Torah returns to the law of the prohibition of blood in full detail in Ch. 17,10 et seq., and Deut. 12,23 et seq. One is only חייב כרת for דם הנפש, i.e., דם שהנשמה יוצאת בה (Kerithoth 20b, תוספות there, and ל״מ on הל׳ מאכלות אסורות 6, 3). But nevertheless the prohibition applies to all the blood of an animal. — Regarding טומאת נבלה, the דם is exactly the same as the חלב, i.e., דם גבלה is not טמא (Edioth 8, 1). The רנלב״ם and the ראב״ד agree on this, ויש שיטה אחרת (see תוספות י״ט שם). We have already above in Ch. 3,17, tried to find out the underlying thoughts which exclude חלב and דם from our food. We thought we could say that in דם and חלב we have the whole nature and aim of an animal’s life before us. One can say that in animal life, the blood, as bearer of the נפש (the will. I.L) rules all the other organs of the animal to achieve חלב (look up notes on Ch. 3,17. I.L.). Now, all the other organs and materials of the animal can well be assimilated by Man, there, in the human organism, to be dominated by the will the נפש הארם, to be used for godly purposes. But it is only symbolically in offerings that דם בהמה can serve to represent נפש האדם and חלב בהמה to symbolise the giving up of all that we achieve to the אש דת, to keep the Fire of God alive on earth; but actually, concretely, the נפש בהמה may never become נפש אדם and חלב בהמה, the selfish animal purpose in life, must never concretely enter and become part of the human organism, but כל חלב לה׳, all the purposes and aims of Man belong to God.

Now the same underlying thought that excludes חלב and דם from the nourishment of Jewish people could also be the reason for what seems to be such an anomalous precept that neither are effected by טומאת נבלה. It is clear that the prototype of טומאה is a dead human body. Nothing points more strikingly to human beings having willy-nilly to submit to the forces of Nature’s demands. The bodies of dead animals only have a similar effect if their structure resembles human bodies. Hence it is only the higher mammals, the formation of whose bodies are somewhat similar to human bodies, that are מטמא. Of the smaller mammals only eight, שמנה שרצים: mice, weasels etc, are מטמא, but none of the other species of animals, fish, amphibians, insects or worms have this טומאה, and birds too have it only in the extremely restricted case of נבלת עוף טהור בבית הבליעה. For all other organs and materials of the animal body, the Torah admits a similarity to those of the human body, and so ordains טומאה for them. But for animal blood it denies such similarity. Animal blood, characteristically is considered as being too low beneath human blood for it to be able to represent human blood. To ordain טומאה for דם נבלה would play into the hands of just that error which the whole law of טומאה and טהרה is meant to fight against. But for חלב there is altogether nothing which is analogous in the human body. It is only in שור כבש ועז too, that it occurs in the specific character of stored-up deposit of a layer of fat, and just as little as in דם is Man to see in חלב any similarity to his own nature. The Torah wants us to consider the דם and the חלב of animals as being completely heterogeneous to ourselves. Taken in this sense, the reason כי כל אוכל וגו׳ of v. 25, for the preceding v. 24 seems even more completely pertinent. For both of them, for יעשה לכל מלאכה as for אכול לא תאכלוהו, the reason lies in כי כל אוכל וגו׳. The very same reason that forbids דם to be eaten, frees it from טומאה.

But whereas the prohibition to eat חלב lies only in the symbolic meaning of חלב, it seems that, in the case of דם, apart from its significance in offerings, there are also actual concrete physical reasons against eating it, which are inherent in its actual material, and so make the prohibition apply to all the higher species of animals, also to those which are not used for offerings. We shall have to consider these reasons on Ch. 17,10 & Deut. 12,13. In accordance with the purely symbolic nature of the prohibition of חלב, this only applies when the animal has attained a completely independent formation, and all its organs have attained their own real organic meaning, and hence חלב שליל מותר (the חלב of an embryo may be eaten. I.L.) whereas the actual material aspect of the prohibition of blood makes it אסור even in the very earliest stages of the formation of the animal.

V.28. Just as above in Ch. 3,16 & 17, the prohibition of חלב is introduced only as the consequence of כל חלב לה׳, and thereby a reminder of the ideals of the offerings is, for all time, interwoven into our ordinary every-day meals, so here too, to the negative command of חלב is added the positive offering-Law of חלב, and that brings the whole of the laws of the offerings to a close. For now follows the completing of the teaching of the offering of אשי ה׳, namely, the bringing and burning of the אימורים — which, as remarked already on Ch. 4,19, 26, 31 & 35, are included in the general idea of חלב in offerings by the injunction to perform the procedure of תנופה with them in שלמים together with the חזה ושוק before burning them on the Altar, the הקרבה.

We have already explained the meaning of the gift of the חזה ושוק and of the תנופה which had to be done with them, on Ex. 29,26 et seq., and here only remark on their close connection with the prohibition of חלב. While the prohibition of חלב excludes selfishness and self interests from being the final aims of our life’s work, the תנופת חזה ושוק ואימורים teach us to dedicate to God, and to our fellow-man, all the urges and aims of our senses (the אימורים), all the thoughts and desires which are stimulated by them (חזה) and all our efforts and accomplishments (שוק); to direct them to the whole of the world around us (תנופה horizontally) and to our God above us (תרומה vertically). The fact that this procedure and these gifts to the כהן only occur at שלמים, expresses to us the teaching that only that man may feel his happy condition in life complete and undisturbed before God, who places himself, with the whole structure of his happiness on earth, at the service of God and of the general purposes of the world, as indicated by Him. It is just this placing of תנופה in connection with the prohibition of חלב which reveals to us the motive for prescribing this procedure only at שלמים offerings.

V. 29. המקריב וגו׳. In this teaching of תנופה and חזה ושוק, the meaning of זבח as a “meal” is specially pronounced. It says: He who would bring the meal of his condition of peace near unto God, must bring part of the meal of his “condition of peace” unto God, i.e., he must make God a partaker of his meal, his enjoyment of his peace must not only be negatively free from selfishness but the purpose of God must be positively furthered in his enjoyment of his happiness.

V. 30. ידיו תביאנה. As in סמיכה, the בעלים themselves have to undertake the procedure of תנופה at the Altar, but with this difference, that in the case of women (the parts being heavy. I.L.) they appoint a representative, and in the case of a joint offering, one member acts on behalf of all the participants (Menachoth 61b & 94a). But neveretheless the procedure is made with the guiding co-operation of the הא כיצד כהן מניח :כהן ידיו תחת ידי הבעלים ומניף. כיצד עושה, מניח אימורין על פיסת היד וחזה ושוק עליהן, the priest places his hands under the hands of the owner who has placed the אימורים across the palms of his hands with the חזה ושוק on top of them, and so makes the prescribed movements of the תנופה (ibid 61b & 62a). The תנופה itself consisted of two movements, a horizontal one to all sides and vertical one up and down, מוליך ומביא מעלה ומוריד (ibid 61a). So that it is the priest who guides the בעלים in the dedicatory movements.

במזרח :לפני ה׳ (ibid 61a) at the place of “the life of the people directed towards God”. At the הגשה of the מנחות the words לפני ה׳ indicate מערב (Ch. 6,7) because הנשת מנחה is in closer relationship to the Altar, and had to be at the same time לפני ה׳ and אל פני המזבח, in the south, so that it had to be done in the south-west corner, which however, lacked the יסוד which was essential for the מנחה and for the חטאת (see above on Ch. 1,5). So that there, לפני ה׳, designated the side of the altar nearest to the היכל. But here לפני ה׳ is the side of “the ordinary life of the People turned towards God”, the east.
V. 31. והקטיר וגו׳. The הקטרת אימודים, as long as any are still there, must precede the giving of the חזה ושוק to the priest (Pesachim 59b).

V. 32. ואת שוק הימין וגו׳. As, in the procedure of the תנופה, both the חזה and the שוק appear together, at the same time and in completely the same way, with both תנופה and הרמה have to be done (as is taught at the first instruction concerning them אשר הונף ואשר הורם, Ex. 29,27, see notes thereon), also in v. 34 they are mentioned together in complete equality, it certainly requires consideration as to why, nevertheless, here, in the instructions in v. 31, 32 & 33, they are so separated. Clearly the idea must be a different one, in which the “breast” is given to the priest, to that in which the “shank” is to be given. He gets the חזה as the direct consequence of the הקטרת אימורין, it says והקטיר וגו׳ והיה וגו׳. But the gift of the שוק is called תרומה מזבחי שלמים similarly to the תרומה from grain. In v. 35 we shall see that this gift of חזה ושוק comes to the priest in quite another sense to that in which he gets the parts of the חטאת and אשם offerings. Whereas in these latter, the אכילת כהנים itself belongs to the symbolic procedures of the offerings, and apears as the final fructification of the כהנים אוכלים ובעלים מתכפרים — אכילת מזכח, — the priests get the חזה ושוק as an expression of recognition of their office to which they have been chosen, they are משחת אהרן ומשחת בניו, as it were, a continuous fresh consecration of the priests, and so must be in close relation to their office, as indeed they appeared immediately on the day when the priests were inducted to their office. Of the איל מלואים the שוק was offered on the Altar and the חזה was given to Moses, who officiated as priest. Of all subsequent שלמים both were given to the priests (Ex. 29,27 & 28). Now חזה, the breast, represents all “thinking and desiring”, on the one hand the spiritual moral source of all human accomplishments done in moral freedom of will, and, on the other hand, is just that sphere of the human being which forms the real field of the priest’s work. All our thoughts and all our desires and will should blossom under the rays of the teaching of the Divine Torah which the priests represent. If we give up all the aims of our life and all the urges which are directed to attain them, with all the energy of our free will to become “fuel for keeping Godliness alive on earth’” as הקטרת אימורים preaches, then this itself is fruit of the “thinking and willing” for whose maturity we have to thank the teachings of God which are administered by the priests. The הקטרת אימורים of the שלמים-offerings of our happiness begets by itself the gift of the חזה to the priest. It is an acknowledgment that, if the general view of life and the directing of our living which appears in הקטרת אימורים, forms the real nucleus of our happiness, it is the tending of the Teachings of God, which is entrusted to the priests, that we have to thank for such views and such directing. But שוק, as the expression of the posture of forward progress and power — we have already referred to the parallel of שוקי האיש to גבורת סוס in the Psalm — represents the whole sphere of external power and strength of Man which appears to owe as little to the influence of priests as the riches of the produce of his fields, from which, nevertheless, at each stage of their coming into the possession of Man, as בכורים ,תרומה and חלה, a symbol — חטה אחת, a single grain satisfies the demand of the Torah — has to be given to the priest. This symbol is to recognise and acknowledge that, in reality, the blessing of external material well-being is also thanks to the Teachings of God which the priests represent; and to act as a reminder that, in the very first place, the external material means of well-being should be used for the benefit of the knowledge of the Teachings of God which the priests represent. This symbol of acknowledgment and reminder is called by preference תרומה. It is a “raising” of the corporeal, the material, to holy, spiritual-moral purposes. So that when the happy contented person gives the שוק הימין מזבחי שלמים as תרומה to the priest, he gives it likewise in this two-fold sense; as a symbol that he acknowledges that his external position of well-being and happiness also rests on the ground of the Teachings of God, as represented by the priests, and as a symbol of his undertaking to allow “the strength of his thigh”, the power his position gives him, to support and accomplish these Teachings of God which the priests represent. Hence we can see the different ideas in which the חזה and the שוק are given to the priest. The חזה quite naturally should belong to him, but he gets the שוק only as תרומה, as a “raising”. Hence also, as we have already remarked on Ex. 35,22 & 24, the constant expression חזה התנופה and שוק התרומה although both, תנופה and תרומה, have to be done equally with both of them.

V. 33. המקריב. Here, too, as in Ch. 6,19, by המקריב is to be understood, הראוי להקרבה (see note, there) and here, according to אבא שאול, whose opinion רמב״ם מע״ק 10, 4 accepts, the addition is made that the priest must not only be ראוי at the time of זריקה but also בשעת הקטרה to have the right of participation in the division.

מבני אהרן, not every one of them, mere birth alone does not, by itself, entitle to claim participation in these priestly rights, כל כהן שאינו מודה בעבודה אין לו חלק בכהונה (Menachoth 18b), he must belong to the service in the Sanctuary to which he was born with his intelligence and feelings and understanding, he must see in such service something ordained by God Himself, and understand how he is fulfilling God’s purposes by his service (Rashi on Chulin 132b).

V. 34. (ת״כ) מרצון בני ישראל ,מאת בני ישראל :ואתן אתם וגו׳ מאת בני ישראל. Although the מתנות כהונה are given to the priests by Divine Right, they are not to demand them as a right to be forcibly taken as their due, but are to be received as a free gift from the people, אין הכהנים רשאין ליטול אותם בזרוע אלא כמו מתנה הם משלמי ישראל שהם נותנין מתנה לכהן (ראב״ד ibid).

V. 35. זאת משחת אהרן וגו׳, this gift of the חזה ושוק from the שלמים offerings of the people is a constant renewal of the original consecration of the priests. It tells the priest that it is in the “breast” of the people in the thoughts and desires of the nation that he is to find the field for his work; and in the “thigh-strength”, in the power for forward progress of the nation, to find the support for, and the carrying out of, his teachings; and in the שלמים mood, in happy joy of life, in the happy living one’s life before God, not in contrition and sorrow, is to be the atmosphere in which the seeds of the teachings of His sanctuary are to thrive. And it tells the people, that even if the priest is not a contributor to the actual direct increase of the economic welfare of the state, nevertheless the welfare of every individual of the nation finds its basis and its purpose in those spiritual treasures of God, which are entrusted to the care of the priests; that happiness and content and well-being has only a firm foundation when the “breast” has listened to the Teachings of God, and only has any real value and meaning if the “thigh”, the power and strength which such a שלמים-condition confers, is used to further the realisation and carrying-out of the Torah, whose Sanctuary the priest ministers.

ביום הקריב אתם וגו׳: as an expression of the consecration of the priesthood constantly to be renewed, the מתנת חזה ושוק was instituted immediately on the day of the מלואים. The priests to be consecrated had to dedicate their חזה and their שוק from the איל המלואים to God, and give them to Moses as the symbol of their acknowledgment and their undertaking. Every שלמים-offering is an act of a priestly consecration of a Jewish family circle, it makes their home into a Temple, and the members of it into priests, and the חזה and שוק of it is to be given to the priests in the same way as at the actual consecration of the actual priests they were given to the Altar and to Moses.

Vv.37 & 38. זאת התורה וגו׳. With these sentences the second large group of the laws given on Sinai come to an end. משפטים, the “ordering”, the laws regulating the whole social and individual life of the Jew came first. They form the purpose, the goal, to serve which this second group of the laws of the offerings stands, and from them alone can the meaning and understanding of the second group be derived. Looking back, all the offerings are mentioned: עולה and חטאת ,מנחה and אשם, the offerings of dedication of one’s actions, and that of acknowledgment of one’s livelihood, of errors of one’s actions and of offences committed — a division which is comparable to that of חזה and עולה ;שוק and חזה = חטאת and מנחה and שוק = אשם — and finally, combining both, מלואים and שלמים, the offering of dedicating one’s actions in the happy exalted feeling that one’s livelihood and well-being is borne by God. It is significant that here in this complemental final chapter, שלמים is taken out of the order in which it ranked in the chapter instituting the offerings (Ch. III) for the purpose of finishing up with it. It is also named last in this retrospective summary in order to put it together with the very first offerings, the מלואים, the offerings of the consecration of the priests, as the root and flower of all offerings, as indeed, in their meaning they to belong intimately together (see note on v. 35) and also, at the same time, to be an introduction to the following chapter, in which the interrupted account of the consecration of the Temple and Priests, of Ex. Ch. XXX, is taken up again and proceeded with.

This grouping together of all the various classes of offerings has the further effect of making important laws, such as שנוי בעלים ושנוי קדש, the results of בלוע in פגל ,קדשים, and many others, which are specified only at certain offerings, apply to all offerings, הוקשו כולם זה לזה (Zebachim 4b, 7b, 8a, 97 & 98, and Menachoth 83).

אשר צוה ה׳ את משה וגו׳: these institutions of the offerings made here had already been given to Moses on Sinai with all the other laws of the Torah, of which they form an important essential integral part. They are neither a transitory concession to a generation that was still steeped in heathen ideas, nor do they form a chapter of cabalistic, magic mysteries. They are מצוה, laws like the rest of the Torah. Their meaning and purpose is teaching the way to keep the ideals of the Torah, and a means of help to keep the Torah. They were accordingly given already on Sinai like all the rest of the Torah, and were only repeated מאהל מועד, after the erection of the Sanctuary of the Torah, as being the special institutions for that Sanctuary; according to ר׳ ישמעאל giving more fully the details and explanations, or according to ר׳ עקיבא simply repeating them: ר׳ ישמעאל אומר כללות נאמרו בסיני ופרטות באהל מועד. ר׳ עקיבא אומר כללות ופרטות נאמרו בסיני ונשנו באהל מועד (Zebachim 115b). With regards to this too, all the categories of offerings and the laws concerning them are placed together with the מלואים which had already been prescribed on Sinai (Ex. XXIX): מה מלואים נאמרו כללותיהם ודקדוקיהם בסיני אף כולם נאמרו כללותיהם ודקדוקיהם בסיני (ת״כ).
ביום צותו וגו׳ במדבר סיני (see note on Ch. 6,2).

V. 1. et seq. As already remarked on Ex. 40,17, there, in accordance with the contents of the second Book, the description of the erection of the Sanctuary together with the subsequent procedure of its dedication was brought to an end. Then, in the first seven chapters of the Third Book the procedures of the offerings were taught, these being the real purpose of the Sanctuary. Now, after the completion of these instructions, this eighth chapter, coming back to Ex. 40,16, where the information, regarding the initiation of the Sanctuary was only given in general terms: ויעש משה ככל אשר צוה ה׳ אותו כן עשה, takes this up again to give the full details of it. Moreover, according to רמב״ז, the thread of the description is taken up again immediately at the very commencement of Book III, inasmuch as the אהל מועד of v. 1 does not refer to the definite finally erected and established Sanctuary, but refers to it on the first day of the seven days of initiation. For just as the initiation ceremony of the Priests, according to Ex. 29,30 & 35 and Levit. 8,33, and the initiation ceremony of the Altar, Ex. 29,37, was repeated daily for seven days, and priests and altar only stood permanently dedicated on the eighth day, in the same way, as already remarked on Ex. 50,1, the tradition is that the אהל מועד was also taken down and re-erected on each of the seven initiation days, and only on the eighth day received its permanent erection and definite consecration. Now, according to רמב״ן, it was on the first day of the מלואים, immediately after the first erection of the אהל מועד, that the Word of God concerning the offerings came to Moses from it. These laws concerning the offerings must have been given before the מלואים offerings were made, as in these latter the majority of the classes of offerings: ,שלמים ,חטאת ,עולה מנחה, had to be made.

וידבר וגו׳ קח וגו׳. As remarked already on Ex. 40,17, the Mikdosh was finally definitely erected on Nissan 1st, after the conclusion of the seven days of initiation. So that the beginning of the Initiation with which we are dealing here was on the 23rd. of Adar.

The whole manner of this initiation of the Priests, and the thoughts and ideas which the various procedures of the מלואים-offerings were to evoke and represent, have already been fully gone into and explained in the chapter in which they were prescribed, Ex. XXIX, so that we can refer to that here.

V. 31. כאשד צויתי וגו׳. As in the words of the command, Aaron is spoken of in the third person, the צויתי must be taken in the sense of transmitting the command, and the reason for its being phrased in this way would be, that, during the מלואים-days Moses functioned, not in his usual capacity of “transmitter”, but as the ministering priest, but just in this eating of the בשר איל מלואים and the לחם out of the סל המלואים, Aaron and his sons were to become conscious of the pleasures which are also part of the dignity of the priesthood (see note on Ex. 29,31—33). In this matter Moses was to appear to them in the role of “transmitter of the Law” as altogether in the future the priests in Jewry as such were subordinate to the teachings of the Torah and the teachers of the Torah. The essential office of the Jewish priest is the carrying out of the Law rather than the study of it. The office of student of the Torah is attached to no particular ancestry or tribe. The saying: ממזר ת״ח קודם לכה״ג עם הארץ (Horioth 13a), that “a learned bastard takes precedence to an unlearned High Priest” characterises sharply the position of the Jewish priesthood towards the student of the Torah. It relegates all that which — by a thoughtless transference of ideas from other circles — is said of a hierarchy of the Jewish priesthood to the realm of absolute fables (see note on Ch. 4,3).

V. 33. ומפתח וגו׳. In a remarkable manner, רמב״ן transfers to our verse here that which the ת״כ explains on a similar saying in Ch. 10,7. He takes it accordingly that here, too, it would only be leaving the Sanctuary בשעת עבודה, that is prohibited. But it says clearly: ופתח אהל מועד תשבו יומם ולילה שבעת ימים, expressly demanding continuous staying in the Sanctuary, besides which, during these seven days Aaron and his sons were not yet authorised to perform any עבודה themselves, but all had to be done by Moses. It was only on the eighth day that they entered into their priestly duties, and it is only referring to such duties that the order in Ch. 10,5, not to leave the Sanctuary, can be taken as only בשעת עבודה. And indeed the command to remain in constant attendance was not made at all for the eighth day.

V. 34. כאשר עשה וגו׳. As Moses himself is speaking here, the subject of עשה can only be God, and have the meaning that what was being done by His command, and in His Name, shall be regarded as being done by God Himself. We find a quite similar idea expressed in Gen. 39,22: כל אשר עשים שם הוא היה עשה, he (Joseph) was the instigator, it was really his doing. The reason for Moses’ special reference back to God, as this instigator of these proceedings, may be, that as it was referring to the instituting of an office of priest, it was specially necessary to indicate that such an office has only any meaning and its consecration only any worth, if it is done by God. In the preceding ימלא את ידכם, it is obviously quite clear that God is the subject. צוה ה׳ לעשות וגו׳, in the above mentioned seven days too.

V. 35. ופתח אהל מועד תשבו וגו׳, places like בחרתי ,אשרי יושבי וגו׳ הסתופף בבית אלקי וגו׳ (Ps. 84,5 & 11), שבתי בבית ה׳ כל ימי חיי לחזות וגו׳ (Ps. 27,4), quite clearly the “dwelling, tarrying in the House of God”, implies that thereby one is brought to give oneself up to the idea which the House of God represents, and becomes penetrated by the thoughts and decisions taught by it, for only so can “staying in the House of God” be a blissful purpose in human desires. Considering this, we do not think that we can be wrong if, in this prescribed seven days living at the entrance to the אהל מועד, we seek the task of, for seven days long, giving oneself up entirely to grasping, accepting, and adapting oneself to the whole abundance of thoughts and ideas and ideals which are presented by and in the אהל מועד, the nursing and tending of which forms the whole meaning and purpose of the service of the priests. ושמרתם את משמרת ה׳: so is the expression used for the toll of obedience imposed by listening to God’s decisions as to when to tarry and when to proceed during the long wandering in the Wilderness in general (Numbres 9,23), but quite specially for enduring patiently long waits until the signal was given to break camp: ובהאריך הענן וגו׳ ושמרו בני ישראל את משמרת ד׳ ולא יסעו (ibid, v. 19).

V. 1. ויהי ביום השמיני. In the Jeshurun vol. V, p. 14, we have already, in the article on מילה, explained the meaning of an eighth day succeeding a past seven days. There we say, that by such a counting of seven days, the condition of a previous period is entirely closed, and with the eighth day a new beginning is made, similar to the octave in music, on a higher level. Here, too, with the seven days spent before the entrance to the Sanctuary, the condition of mere private, individual meaning of life is closed for those destined for priesthood. With the eighth day they step into the new elevated character of a life dedicated to belong to God and to the Nation.

V. 2. עגל בן בקר. According to Rosh Hashonnah 10a, a two-year old, i.e., an animal in its second year. It is more developed than that which is generally understood by the simple term עגל, (עגל סתם is taken to be during the first year), but has not yet reached the maturity of a פר בן בקר, which only starts in the third year. If, as according to Bechoroth 19b is the case, cattle only mature for breeding in their third year, then perhaps the term בן בקר may designate an age in which the animal appears still primarily as בן ובת and not yet as אב ואם. It is possible too, that the name of פר and פרה, which they get at this age, is derived from this ability to breed, from the root פרה, to be fruitful, and then פר בן בקר would designate the age in which the animal appears in both characters, in which the transition is made from בן to פר, and that would be, according to above, the third year. (According to רמב״ם מ״ק 6, 14, it becomes a פר already in the 2nd year. See כ״מ thereon, and מל״מ on פרה אדומה 1, 1 a,b).

This is the only case in which an עגל is prescribed for an offering, and, as we see, an עגל which is nearly a פר. For it is one who is just becoming a server of the Sanctuary who is placing himself as such before God, whereas later as כהן המשיח he represents himself by a פר. Also in the מלואים days of his office, to that office, to the “field” of his activity to which he is to be the “ploughing animal”, he represented himself as a פר.

In standing before God with an עגל לחטאת and an איל לעולה, Aaron undertakes and promises: - that, in the work of his office, although there is room and necessity for constant improvement and progress, he will always keep himself on the heights of his calling, never letting its gravity slip his memory (the חטאת. I.L.) and in the dignity and honour which the office confers on him, to always step in the van of the community, setting the example, and leading it upwards, ever upwards towards the height of Jewish perfection (the איל לעולה. I.L.).

Deeply significant, our חכמים in ת״כ see in this offering at the same time a supplementary expression of atonement for the sin of the עגל, which, of course, had actually already been forgiven. We have already stressed on Ex. 8,22, the deep contrast of Judaism to all ancient and modern heathenism, which shows itself in the fact that, that which the heathen idolises, and to which he sacrifices himself and his possessions, that is what the Jew masters and sacrifices to his God. So here, too, Aaron had made the עגל as a symbol of a subordinate power serving the One and Only God. The heathen idea of idolising the forces of Nature which was still in the minds of the people, had transferred this עגל into a god of power, co-ordinate with God. When Aaron brought an עגל as an offering to God, representing himself to God as this עגל and, in שחיטה mastering this, his עגל, and in זריקה etc., devoting it to the service of the One Only God, he thereby expressed the thought: — that it is this very same physical nature to which the erroneous idea of the rest of the world bows the knee, and submits to its demands as to that of a God, and which truly is a power within Man too, but which can find its master in godly men approaching God, it is this power which, with his free moral energy he is forcing and dedicating to the service of the One Only God. But this thought immediately rectifies the heathen erroneous idea of making the forces of Nature into a god, and lays these gods of Nature not only at the feet of God, but also at the feet of Man, who by virtue of his moral freedom is near unto a God.

In Exodus, when we went into the episode of the עגל, we remarked on the deep connection which it had with the erection of the Sanctuary, in the interim between the ordering and the carrying out of which, it occurred; how, just through it, the necessity for the atonement and education of both people and priests which the Sanctuary, as the כפרה-place was to serve, was proved. Referring back to this aberration of Aaron, his חטאת-עגל and his עולה-איל would say:— in a moment of weakness he had not kept himself on the clear height of his calling, instead of striding in front of the people and leading them, he had weakly been overpowered and led by them, and allowed himself to be led astray into sinful negligence. He undertakes henceforth always to remain, with watchful seriousness, firm and fast on the altar-summit of his Jewish calling (his חטאת. I.L.), and always to be a true leader of the people, with virile energy striding before them on the one and only path that leads upwards, ever upwards to God (his איל לעולה. I.L.).

Vv. 3 & 4. ואל בני ישראל תדבר ,גו׳. And while the Priest with his offering brings home to himself, and impresses upon his mind, the whole seriousness and importance of the mission which the office which has just been conferred on him brings to him, both towards God and towards the nation, the Nation too, with their offering, are to impress upon themselves, and make themselves conscious of their mission towards God, and the position which this is to give them as a Nation in the midst of the other nations. כי היום וגו׳. For it is not to the Priest, but to the Nation, — to the Nation who have consciously entered into their world-historical calling — that God will “make Himself apparent” and allow His Glory to find a home on earth, there, where His Torah had found a Temple and a People.

The offering of the Nation consisted of two groups: — (a) the שעיר לחטאת ועגל וכבש לעולה, and (b) שור ואיל לשלמים ומנחה בלולה בשמן, (a) the expression of their position towards God, and (b) their position as a Nation in the midst of the Nations. Towards God, the Nation undertakes, with the שעיר עזים לחטאת, to stand firmly and obstinately against all enticements of strangers, and obediently and faithfully to stand fast to the standpoint to which the One and Only Shepherd of their life directs them; and with the עגל וכבש בני שנה לעולה, to give themselves up in the eternal freshness and tractability of youth (בני שנה. I.L.), both in their active life (עגל. I.L.) and in the direction of their fate and history (כבש. I.L.), with all virile energy (the זריקה. I.L.) to the guidance of the One Guide to their actions, and Director of their fate and history, upwards, ever upwards to the heights revealed in His Torah (עולה. I.L.). But with the שור ואיל לשלמים לזבח לפני ה׳, they joyfully and happily express the important position in the midst of the nations that they are to obtain with that faithful stead-fastness and energetic devotion that they have vowed to keep by the first group. The eternally youthful עגל of their relation to God, turns into the masculine שור in the work of their activity towards the other nations, and the כבש obediently following its Shepherd, into the איל, in its full power showing the way and leading the rest of the herd of nations. This joyful aspect of the Jewish mission in world history is brought home to their consciousness by the national “happy meal of peace before God” (שלמים לזבח לפני ה׳. I.L.). And with מנחה בלולה בשמן, “flour soaked in oil”—the symbol of an existence blessed with wealth and well-being — they lay on the Altar of His Torah the tribute of allegiance to God. But although the מנחה here is placed together with שלמים, in v. 17 we find it in connection with the עולה, and it was brought between the עולה and the שלמים. So that the מנחה seems to be the complement of the עולה and the basis of the שלמים. The “giving oneself up” of the עולה finds its necessary complement in recognising at the same time that all the material possessions on which existence and well-being depend really belong to God, and must also be “given up” to His service; and the happy consciousness that one is enjoying one’s life of content and well-being before God, as is expressed by שלמים is essentially rooted in the consciousness that every grain of our food, and every ounce of our well-being, is a gift from God, (see note on v. 17). It is significant that here, in the only communal offering of happiness and content of service — altogether שלמים are never brought as צבור-offerings, with the one exception of כבשי עצרת and these, as כבשים, are not in the idea of service — the animal is given, as שור, the general designation of the whole species, instead of the specific פר, indicating that the duty of active service for God lies on every age, young and old, and on every degree of strength and power, as is represented by a whole community.

If this communal offering is also in close reference to the עגל sin, then the nation with its שעיר עזים in the חטאת undertakes henceforth never again to allow itself to be led astray from God and His Torah by an ערב רב, and in the עגל of the עולה and in the שור of the שלמים, achieves — as already indicated in Aaron’s offering in v. 2 — the direct atonement for the sin of the עגל, which, as ת״כ remarks, had not remained with the people only an עגל as Aaron had intended, but had become elevated into an independent שור; and in the כבש of the עולה and the איל of the שלמים undertakes to place the direction of its future way in life wholeheartedly under the direction of its One and Only “Shepherd”, and in such complete subjection to God, to stride manfully in joyful strength in front of the rest of the herd of humanity as a leader to God, and to recognnise and thank God and no other for its ‘flour and its oil”, for its existence and its well-being, and not recognise any intermediary for them.

V. 6. זה הדבר אשד צוה ה׳ תעשו וגו׳. This address to the people — as ק״א explains in ת״כ — can not refer to the actual carrying out of their offering. What the nation had to do for that purpose had already been done. Hence ת״כ gives the following explanation to the words: ויאמר משה זה הדבר אשר צוה ד׳ תעשו. אמר להם משה לישראל אותו יצר הרע העבירו מלבכם ותהיו כולכם ביראה ובעצה אחת לשרת לפני המקום כשם שהוא יחידי בעולם כך תהא עבודתכם מיוחדת לפניו שנאמר ומלתם את ערלת לבבכם. מפני מה, כי אני ה׳ .אלהיכם, הוא אלהי האלהים ואדוני האדונים, עשיתם כן וירא אליכם כבוד ד׳ Unless we are mistaken this explanation of the ת״כ takes הדבר to consider all the procedures of the verious offerings prescribed here as one single act, and as a דבר, as one Word of God to be expressed by them, which we are demanded to carry out. And indeed the sum of all the demands expressed in the idea of all the offerings would be:— להעבירו מלבבנו, to allow אותו יצר הרע, that uncontrolled animal sensuality — which is just what is represented by the animal we bring before God for sacrifice — to have no place in our being, but — as is represented by נתינה ,שחיטה or זריקה and הקטרה — to master it, and, by the energy of our moral free will, guide and dedicate it, so that יראה will protect us from fault (חטאת), and the only עצה we accept, is to carry out the duty of our service to God (עולה). And, as here, in what is regarded as one offering, the Community represents itself before the One and Only God, so in general, the thought of the One to Whom every one of us, each single member of the Community stands in exactly the same and equal relation, is to beget in us, both the real inner unity of the dual natures of our individual selves, and the equality and unity of the community, as is expressed regarding the unity of our animal and spiritual selves, in the words ומלתם את ערלת לבבכם וערפכם לא תקשו עוד כי ה׳ אלהיכם הוא אלהי האלהים ואדני האדנים וגו׳. (Deut. 10,16 & 17). “Cut out the urges of your hearts (firmly master the urges of your senses: חטאת ,יראה) and be no longer stiff-necked (happily and willingly do good: עולה, עצה לשרת לפני המקום) for your God is the God of gods (He alone has your whole being in His Hands), and Master of all masters (everything, consciously or unconsciously, willingly or by force, is in His service). This sentence shows clearly the unity of one’s life-service in avoiding everything which is forbidden by God, and in carrying out all that He orders, as the direct result of His Unique “Oneness”. עשיתם כן, the ת״כ concludes, “if you will really carry out the ideas which the offerings represent, by individually and nationally devoting yourselves to God’s Will, then וירא אליכם כבוד ה׳, then this united joint devotion to God will bring about, that, on its part, the Glory of God will come to meet it, and by a visible demonstration will show its entry into your midst and the accomplishment of the purpose of the building of the Sanctuary, viz. ועשו לי מקדש ושכנתי בתוכם.
It is in these lines of the ת״כ that we believe that we find the fundamental idea of all the offerings, and the symbolic meaning of the procedures of the offerings, expressed.

In Yoma 5b, referring to our verse here, we are told that מקרא פרשה מעכב, that having פרשת המלואים read aloud during the procedure of the offering, was an essential part of the ritual, the omission of which would render the whole procedure invalid. For by such reading from the Torah, the fact was driven home, that it was no subjective human idea that was being carried out, which could be altered or abrogated according to the feelings or wishes of the bringers, but was solely the directions and commands given by God Himself. In the same way, on י״כ, the High Priest, after he had completed the special עבודת היום, before he proceeded to the עבודת חוץ, read aloud the פרשת אחרי מות, in which it is made evident that the service he had done in the Holy of Holies, as well as what he was about to perform outside it, was prescribed and ordered by God (Yoma 68b, רש״י).

V. 7. וכפר בעדך ובעד העם. That Aaron’s offering accorded atonement for the people too, seems very strongly to confirm the special reference this offering is thought to have to the sin of the עגל. For in Aaron’s sin with the עגל it was the people who participated and played the most important part: עשו את העגל אשר עשה אהרן (Ex. 32,35). So that although a separate offering was brought for the atonement of the sin of the people, they participate in Aaron’s atonement-offering, inasmuch as his sin was brought about by their overwhelming power.

V. 9. ויקרבו. In V. 12, speaking of the עולה, it says: וימצאו, they reached the blood to him, he had to take the vessel with the blood from them to throw the blood against the sides of the Altar. Here, of the חטאת, it only says: ויקרבו, they brought the blood close to him so that he could dip his finger into it.

V. 11. ואת הבשר ואת העור וגו׳. Although it was only a חטאת חיצונית the meat, like that of the פר כהן המשיח was not to be eaten, but, like it, had to be burnt חוץ למחנה. There was no כהן yet who could eat it, he was only to become a כהן by this very חטאת. For the same reason, the same happened to the חטאות during the מלואים-days. Ch. 5,17; Ex. 29,14.
V. 16. כמשפט: as is prescribed above in Ch. I, for עולת נדבה.

V. 17. וימלא כפו ממנו. From Menachoth 9b & 19b, it is evident that this means קמיצה. We have already remarked on v. 4, how the מנחה-thought, which otherwise comes only as a complement to עולה and שלמים as מנחת נסכים here is expressed as an independent מנחה. Hence whereas מנחת נסכים were entirely burnt on the altar, here קמיצה was taken, as at a מנחת נדבה and the שירים were eaten. Actually this, and the מנחת עומד which has quite a similar meaning, are the only מנחת צבור of which only the קומץ is given to the Altar-fire; just as the שלמי צבור here are the only communal שלמים apart from the analagous כבשי עצרת. According to ת״כ, all the עולות, (according to ראב״ד, the שלמים too), were accompanied by the usual מנחת נסכים as well, which, for the עולות would be indicated by the כמשפט of v. 16. — מלבד עולת הבקר: these עולות ונסכים, and this independent מנחה were brought in addition to the morning-תמיד-offering and its attendant נסכים. As on Sabbath and the Festivals, the special thoughts of dedication and devotion which the underlying idea of the day induces are expressed by מוספים, but this expression does not exclude the necessity to express the thoughts of devotion which the simple gift of a new day should awake in us every morning which the תמיד expresses; and the מוספים — as it says in Numbers 28,23 — מלבד עולת הבקר אשר לעולת התמיד, only come as additional supplements to the constant daily expression of devotion attached to the daily morning offering; in the same way the offerings prescribed here for the “eighth מלואים-day” are the מוספים for that day which were to be brought מלבד עולת הבקר.

V. 19. והמכסה, according to רמב״ן, not merely short for חלב המכסה את הקרב, but a name for all חלב which was offered on the altar, the distinguishing characteristic of which was, just that it was only a covering for, only lay upon, the organs, but was not grown into and intermingled with the tissues of the organ. See note on Ch. 3,3 & 4.

Vv.21 & 22. As the תנופת חזה ושוק of the שלמים was done at the same time as that of the אימורים, hence before their הקטרה, but here the report finishes with the תנופה, after it had told us that the הקטרה was done, there can be only one reason for it. The Torah must have wanted to connect this ritual with the immediately following ברכה. As this ברכה, as the ת״כ tells us, was none other than the statutory ברכת כהנים prescribed for all time, the connection between the חזה ושוק and his ברכה is obvious. On Ch. VII et seq., we have already recognised, in the gift to the priests of the חזה ושוק of the שלמים, as well as in the תנופה which had to be performed with them, the expression of the thought that, recognising his happy condition of life (שלמים) he dedicates all his inner thoughts and wishes (חזה) and all his material powers and position, (שוק) to God and to all the communal purposes indicated by Him (תרומה ותנופה); and by giving these to the כהן, recognises and acknowledges that the spiritual and material possessions which are responsible for conditions of שלם, are derived from, and thanks to, the Torah of God, of which the כהן is the representative. Now, inasmuch as ברכת כהנים follows directly on this, it expresses just the thoughts that it is only such acknowledgment and such resolutions as are expressed by the ritual of תנופה that can make one worthy for the continuance of being blessed by material security (יברכך וישמרך), by spiritual gifts (יאר ויחנך), and by what blossoms from the combination of the two, the condition of ישא, וישם לך שלום) שלם). From this juxta-position, too, Sota 38b (in contrast to ת״כ, where it is explained to be a מקרא מסורס) looks on ברכת כהנים as being an integral concluding act of the עבודה, which is only then completed, as it says: וישא אהרן וגו׳, וירד מעשות וגו׳ (see Rashi thereon). Hence the sentence ברכת כהנים .כל כהן שאינו עולה בעבודה שוב אינו עולה is no independent absolute act, standing on its own. Only as a result of the preceding עבודה are the blessings expressed in it to be achieved, and only in close association with the עבודה may ברכת כהנים be said.

בנשיאת כפים :וישא אהרן את ידו, with upraised hands (Sota ibid). There is no power of blessing innate in the hands of our priests (hence probably why ידו is written חסר). The hands of the priest can only direct upwards towards the One who has promised blessing. For further details of ברכת כהנים see notes on Numbers 6,22 et seq.

V. 23. ויבא משה וגוי. We are not told the purpose of this entry into the אהל מועד. Keeping solely to that which lies in the text before us, this [[illegible]] and יציאה seem to be a preparation for ויברכו and this, in its turn, a preparation for וירא כבוד ה׳ וגו׳ so that the following may possibly be not too far from the truth. The Sanctuary had been consecrated, priests and people had duly brought the offerings, as a result of which, it had been promised that a visible sign would be given as a sealing of the bond that if the People made a home for the Torah of God He would dwell in their midst. But not immediately on the completion of the offerings did the Glory of God appear. Had it done so, it might have strengthened the pagan idea that there was some secret power in the offerings themselves that had the magic power to work on the god, and by sheer physical means to force or bring about a theophany (a manifestation or appearance of God, or of a god to man. I.L.). And it was the One Unique free personal God, Who, in complete control of His Own Will, had promised to give the sign of His special Presence, not to the offering, but to the People who expressed in the offering their free and happy giving themselves up to Him. So that when the offering had been made and Aaron had proclaimed, as the fruit of the offering, the blossoming out of all material and spiritual possessions into a state of happy content under the blessing, protection, grace and special care of God — all of which is the effect of what the promised ושכנתי בתוכם means, — the Presence of God did not yet manifest itself; but Moses and Aaron first entered what had now truly become an אהל מועד, the perfected place where God wished to have a “meeting-place with His People”, and where all that was symbolised by the ,מנורה ,שלחן ארון, and by the מזבח הקטרת in the משכן כרובים was represented as God had ordained, so that if the lessons it taught were accepted and practiced by the nation, He could promise to let His כרובים come down, and the blessing and protection of the Glory of God be manifest. Penetrated with, and thoroughly imbued with the ideas of this אהל מועד-thought, they come out again to the people, and, in the sense of this thought, blessed them, i.e., looking up to God, they expressed the wish that, through them and to them, this אהל מועד may be realised; and it was realised: וירא כבוד ה׳ אל כל העם וגו׳ !

In the same way as the ברכה spoken by Aaron was specified as ברכת כהנים by the preceding חזה ושוק so does this ברכה spoken by Moses and Aaron, by the preceding ביאה אל אהל מועד show itself to be the ברכת אהל מועד which was then realised by the appearance of the כבוד ה׳ and the אהל מועד completed into a real אהל מועד. In ת״כ we find the following: ויבא משה ואהרן אל אהל מועד. למה נכנס משה ואהרן ביחד, ללמד אהרן על מעשה קטרת, או לא נכנם אלא לדבר אחר, הריני דן וכו׳ וכו׳, ירידה טעונה ברכה וביאה טעונה ברכה, מה ירידה מעין עבודה אף ביאה מעין עבודה, הא למה נכנס משה עם אהרן ללמדו על מעשה הקטרת. Here, the ברכת משה ואהרן (of v. 23) is taken to be in connection with their ביאה אל אהל מועד, quite similarly to the ברכת אהרן (of v. 22) being in connection with the ירידה מעשת החטאת וגו׳; and from that, is further concluded, that just as the ירידה (which according to ת״כ, as remarked above preceded the ברכה) was connected with the עבודה, so this ביאה, out of which the ברכה of Moses and Aaron resulted, must have had some connection with עבודה, and the ת״כ finds this connection in teaching concerning the bringing of קטרת. Now, if we realise that in מעשה הקטרת on the מזבח הזהב the whole idea of the היכל reaches its loftiest conception, and further, that ללמדו על מעשה הקטרת, must refer to teaching the ideal, the meaning of that ritual, and not the actual way of performing it, as that was no time for which actual bringing of קטרת was prescribed, then these sentences of the ת״כ come to much the same idea as the way in which we tried to explain it.

V. 1. Elsewhere (Gen. 4,3) we have already pointed out, how, at the very first appearance of offerings, and so at every fresh introduction of them, reference is made, by deed or word, to a rejected offering next to an accepted one. This, from the very start, cuts the ground from under the feet of that blasphemous erroneous opinion with which the reform aspirations of our times love to pride themselves; that the insight into the merely relative worth of offerings only belonged to the progressive time of the Prophets who had advanced beyond the lower standpoint of the Pentateuch. Cain’s rejected offering next to Abel’s accepted one, the repeated warnings to Solomon at the building of, and after the completion of, his magnificent temple in Kings I. 6,12 & 13, as well as in IX,3—9, loudly proclaim that the value of the Sanctuary and offerings is entirely dependent on faithful obedience to duty. So the dead bodies of the priestly youths, who, on account of their offering, were killed by the Fire of God — just at the same moment that this very same fire had come down to express God’s satisfaction with the offering of the People, more, to proclaim the Presence of God dwelling amongst the People, — are the loudest protest against that wrong way of looking at the value of offerings, but, at the same time an even more earnest protest against every subjective choosing according to one’s own ideas in the sphere of our public worship of God.

נדב ואביהו שלא נטלו ,בני אהרן שלא חלקו כבוד לאהרן :ויקחו בני אהרן וגו׳ איש מעצמו יצאו ולא נטלו עצה זה מזה :איש מחתתו ;עצה זה מזה. With this explanation the ת״כ points out how the whole setting of the text indicates the most conceited vanity with which the youths behaved. It does not say ויקחו נדב ואביהוא מחתות ויתנו בהן אש וגו׳, but first of all gives their filial relationship בני אהרן, and then איש and מחתתו, all little points showing the self-importance which had taken hold of their minds, which makes us take the words נדב ואביהוא as having a similar implication. They were only the sons of Aaron, but did not consult their father about their ideas; or perahps just bacause they were the sons of Aaron they thought they were above all advice. But still they were only Nadab and Abihu, only individual members of the Nation and did not seek advice from the leader of the Nation; or it was just the vlaue they put on their own individual personalities that made them think they were all-sufficient for themselves. More, איש וגו׳, each one went exclusively in his own way, in the way that he thought best, they did not even consult each other. As sure as it is that their intention was a praiseworthy one — even after their sin God calls them “קרבי״, — an intention which ת״כ describes אף הם בשמחתם כיון שראו אש הדשה, עמדו להוסיף אהבה על אהבה, the mere fact that in that most glorious moment for the Nation when God’s proximity to them was so wonderfully demonstrated, they could feel the urge for a separate offering of their own, showed that they were not filled with the true spirit of a Jewish priest. A Jewish priest is entirely at one with, and part and parcel of, the Nation, is in no way separated from it, and only within the Nation has his office any meaning before God. So that the very approach itself suffered from an unclear conception, and moreover the actual offering itself was in every detail illegal. The double illegality of their action is pointed out in ת״כ on Ch. 16,1, referring to the different expressions in Levit. XVII: בקרבתם לפני ה׳ וימתו, and in Numbers 3,4, where it says: וימת נדב ואביהוא וגו׳ בהקריבם אש זרה וגו׳, that both the קריבה, the subjective approach, and הקרבה, the actual objective bringing of the offering could have been sinful. Actually, the הקרבה, the offering itself, appears in every way illegal. The מחתות as well as the אש and the קטרת were all against the Law. All the כלי שרת had to be של צבור and קדש (see הל׳ כלי המקדש ,רמב״ם 8, 7 הל׳ בית הבחירה 1, 20). By giving his offering over into a national vessel of the Sanctuary, the bringer, together with his offering, enters within the frame-work of the national sanctuary of the Torah, and thereby gives himself up to all its demands, to the exclusion of any decisions made according to his own ideas. But the מחתות of Nadab and Abihu were מחתתו, each his own; they approach God, not with the vessels of the Sanctuary, but with their own, without self-renunciation.

ויתנו בהן אש, more precisely אש זרה, מן הכיריים, from their own hearths, as ר׳ עקיבא explains in ת״כ. Not fire from the Altar as was prescribed for the daily קטרת, and on י״כ, so that it was not from the “Fire of the Torah” waiting for the devotion of the community, of the highest and lowest of the Nation, it was fire from their own hearths on which they “placed the incense”. And finally, the קטרת itself. קטרת was the one sacrificial substance, which neither from the community nor from the individual was allowed to be brought as נדבה. The bringing of קטרת was to remain restricted exclusively to that which was prescribed for the community daily and for the כה״ג on י״כ (Menachoth 50a & b). For, we believe we are justified in seeing in קטרת the expression of the complete sublimation to giving satisfaction to God, the complete and perfect giving oneself up to ריח ניחוח לה׳ (see Ex. XXX & XXXIV), a thought that represents the goal presented by God, as the absolute ideal of His demand. But presented by oneself of one’s own free-willed choice, as a נדבה, to represent one’s feeling of having attained this ideal would be presumptuous conceit. More than anything else the Word of God stresses אשר לא צוה אותם, that God had not commanded them. Even if the various phases of the offering had not themselves been wrong, as we have seen that they were, the fact that it was not a “bidden” one, would have sufficed to make it a “forbidden” one. No place is allowed in the whole service of the offerings of the Sanctuary of the Torah for subjectively doing just what you think right. Even the קרבנות נדבה, the free-will offerings, have to be kept meticulously within the limits of the forms and kinds prescribed for them. For קרבת אלקים, the proximity of and getting near to God, which is the purpose of every offering, is only to be found by the way of obedience, by compliance with God’s Will and subordination to it. This is one of the points in which Judaism and Paganism go in diametrically opposite directions. The Pagan brings his offering in an attempt to make the god subservient to his wishes. The Jew, with his offering, wishes to place himself in the service of God; by his offering he wishes to make himself subservient to the wishes of his God. So that all offerings are formulae of the demands of God, which the bringer, by his offering, undertakes to make the normal routine for his future life. So that self-devised offerings would be a killing of just those very truths which our offerings are meant to impress and dominate the bringers, would be placing a pedestal on which to glorify one’s own ideas, where a throne was meant to be built for obedience, and obedience only. We can understand that the death of the priestly youths, and their death in the first moment of the consecration of the Sanctuary of God, is the most solemn warning for all future priests of this Sanctuary; it excludes from the precincts of the Sanctuary of God — which was to be nothing else but the Sanctuary of His Torah — every expression of caprice, and every subjective idea of what is right and becoming! Not by fresh inventions even of God-serving novices, but by carrying out that which is ordained by God has the Jewish priest to establish the authenticity of his activities.

V. 3. בקרבי אקדש, if we compare Ezekiel 20,41; XXVII,22 & 25; XXXVI,23; XXXVIII,16; XXXIX,28, and also Numbers 20,13, we can see that הקדש ב-, used by God, expresses the idea, that, by declaring as קדש that which He allows to happen to somebody or something, absolutely everything else, even the highest and the most powerful, must give way to it. The demand in Levit. 22,32: ונקדשתי בתוך בני ישראל, also demands that for the fulfilment of His Will, if needs be, everything else must be sacrificed. So that בקרבי אקדש וגו׳ in the sense of the last quotation could mean: By those that are near to Me I would be shown as קדוש, i.e., as One for Whose Will the greatest difficulties have to be overcome and the greatest sacrifice made. This קדוש השם would primarily be the duty of “קרבי״, those near to God, i.e., those who had to act as leaders, teachers and examples for the People in their relation to God. Then the idea of God would be brought home to the consciousness of the People in all His כבוד, i.e., in the whole “weight” of His Greatness, in the whole “weighty” seriousness of His demands. But it is difficult to see how their refraining from bringing their offering could have been taken as effecting such a קדוש השם as — as far as we can see — it would not have entailed a great output of self-control. And even if we concede a tremendous urge to express and satisfy their enthusiasm, their refraining from doing so would have been a matter of which God alone would have known, and of which the People would have known nothing at all, so that it could not have brought about כבוד ה׳ על פני כל העם. So we have to take the בקרבי אקדש as the euphemistic positive expression of the negative: בקרבי לא יהולל שמי. For the less their refraining from bringing their offering would have been a קדוש השם the more their act was a חלול השם, especially by קרובי ה׳, by those from whom in the first instance should be learnt the obedience to be paid to God. So that it seems more probable that the phrase should be taken in the sense of the quotation mentioned above from Ezekiel: — by that which God allows to happen to those who are near Him: אקדש, i.e., inasmuch as, the more anybody stands in front of the people as a leader and teacher in their relation to Me, the less do I overlook his mistakes, and even — as in this case — show, by his death, that My Will is absolute, and towards it, even the nearest and highest — and those less than anybody else — may not allow themselves the slightest deviation, — ועל פני כל העם וגו׳, and so the whole weight of the obedience which is due to Me is impressed on the whole nation.

Taking it this way we can see also that enough consolation lies in these words, that to them it can say: וידם אהרן. Had his sons not been קרובי ה׳, pardon might perhaps have been granted to them, and the tragic fate which God so immediately dealt them would not have been such a weighty warning to the people. In sharpest contrast to the modern point of view which regards spiritual and intellectual greatness as a free pass for moral laxness, and grants men of intellect a greater consideration in lapses against God’s laws of morality, the Jewish point of view raises the strictness of the demands for morality with each higher degree of intellectuality. The Gemora (Yebamoth 121b) teaches on the verse in Ps. 50,3: וסביביו נשערה מאוד, “His environment is greatly affected by storms”, מלמד שהקב״ה מדקדק עם סביביו כחוט השערה, that this tells us that God is exacting even to a hairbreadth with those who are round about Him. A similar idea is expressed in Ps. 89,8: אל נערץ בסוד קדושים רבה ונורא על כל סביביו. Ps. XCIX is also dedicated to this “holiness” of God, and there in vv. 6—8 it is pointed out, how Moses and Aaron amongst His priests, and Samuel amongst those who proclaim Him, stand out prominently, how they were so near to God that they could always reckon on His answering their appeals, how He spoke to them from a pillar of cloud and appointed them to be watchers of His evidence and transmitters of His Law, that He would listen to their pleas for others and would prove Himself a forgiving God to such prayers, but ונוקם על עלילותם, nevertheless, for their own misdeeds He would grant no remission.

הוא אשר דבר ה׳. This seems a little difficult. As we find no such words having been spoken by God up till now, the רמב״ן takes it as being simply the explanation of the fate which had just befell Nadab and Abihu, and it would mean: “This is what God expresses by it”. But, sentences elsewhere in the Torah as הוא אשר דברתי (Gen. 48,28, and הוא הדבר אשר לא דברו ה׳ (Deut. 18,22) show that such expressions do refer back to words actually spoken already. To mean what the רמב״ן says it should have been זה אשד וגו׳. So that probably we have again a proof that not all of God’s speeches to Moses are recorded in the Written Word. Had not the occasion arisen for the practical application of these words of God, and in consequence, mention of them made in the written account of this event, they, like so many other Words of God, would have remained in the תשב״פ (the tradition handed down verbally from Moses. I.L.).

V. 4. מאת פני הקדש. From the account given of the event, it is not evident where the sons of Aaron brought offering of incense; there were only two places for such offerings: — on the מזבח הזהב in the היכל where the daily קטרת was brought, and in the קדש הקדשים where it was brought by the כה״ג on י״כ. As this latter offering had not yet been prescribed, it seems more probable that they had only offered it on the מזבח הזהב in the היכל. Nevertheless in ת״כ it says: נטלו אש זרה ונכנסו לבית קדשי הקדשים. Nothing can be concluded from Ch. 16,1 & 2 as there it actually forbids כניסה להיכל שלא בשעת עבודה. In any case at least they went into the היכל. Now the place where the bodies lay is designated here as פני הקדש, the word קדש is used for the היכל and פני הקדש for the space eastwards, in front of the היכל (see Menachoth 27b). So that they must have died in the חצר in front of the אהל מועד. This would be in accordance with what ר׳ אליעזר says in ת״כ viz., that נגפן מלאך ודחפן לחוץ והוציאם, that וימתו לפני ה׳ of v. 2 is to be taken that they were affected by the Finger of God, which forced them outside where they died.
V. 5. בכתנתם, their clothes were untouched by the fire, according to one opinion in ת״כ their bodies too were untouched, the fire only killed them as by a stroke of lightning שרפת נשמה וגוף קיים.

V. 6. ראשיכם אל תפרעו. Just as Ch. 21,10 permanently forbids the כה״ג, even at the death of his nearest relations, את ראשו לא יפרע ובגדיו לא יפרם, so here he and his sons are forbidden to display grief by פריעה and פרימה at this case of death. On this יום השמיני the sons too, otherwise regarded as כהנים הדיוטים are regarded as being in the stage of כה״ג. ראש פריעת is explained in Numbers 6,5 as גדל פרע שער ראשו, as allowing the hair to grow wild, i.e., not to cut it. פרם only occurs in this connection with an אבל and in Chapt. 13,48 with a מצורע. From Sota 7 where it says אם נקרעו נקרעו ואם נפרמו נפרמו, it is evident that פרימה is not the same as קריעה. Rashi explains there that פרימה is a tearing into tatters, into several pieces But according to the Aruch on the other hand, it is merely a rent in the seam. From the prescribed method of קריעה for an אבל, we would take פרם to be more of a tearing in the garment than a tearing of the garment. If with a מצורע (see notes there) פריעה was to express the personal depreciation, and פרימה, the social depreciation of the person affected, these same procedures at the death of nearest relations would express the consciousness of the loss which a person has suffered by this passing away. The deceased was their שאר, he was an essential part of a “complement” to their persons and their social affairs; both in themselves and in their social matters those that are left have lost in value. In their appearance they are to show their feelings of this loss by not cutting their hair or beards (both belong to ראש) and by rents in their clothes. This שאר feeling is not only a justified one but is a duty ordered by Jewish Law. The Jewish Laws of mourning (although מן התורה they are, at most, prescribed only for the first day and then, indeed only when מיתה וקבורה ביום אחד, but nevertheless, like all מצות דרבנן have been adopted by the nation as an inviolable sacred duty and apply for שבעה and שלשים) tell what, in Jewish family life, husband and wife are to be to each other, what parents are to be to their children, children to their parents and brothers and sisters to each other. But for the כה״ג, — and on this first day of their completed consecration Aaron’s sons were also כה״ג — who represents before God the ideal Jew, the ideal of the Immortal Nation, for him, the idea of God, and the idea of the Nation, is to drive into the background the feelings of his own wounded self. For before God, there is no such thing as Death, and the one who has been called away has only changed the scene of his existence; the Nation too knows no Death, אין צבור מת, in it, all past generations live on, and out of it all the coming ones blossom; in it, at all times past and future are present. This immortality in this world and the next, on this side and the other side of the grave, is what the High Priest, whose forehead proclaims קדש לה׳, has to preach by non-פריעה and non-פרימה, to him it is always said, and on יום שמיני it was said to his sons too: ראשיכם !אל תפרעו ובגדיכם לא תפרמו

ועל כל העדה יקצף. Cf. Ch. 4,3, אם הכהן המשיח יחטא לאשמת העם. when the spiritual elite of the nation, especially when they are called upon to represent the whole national community in their ideal unity before God, commit a mortal sin, and are torn away from their national efficient utility by death, their loss is a national loss and their death a national calamity. “Your death” it says “would be a קצף על כל העדה״. In this reference to their national importance and meaning before God, lies, as we have tried to indicate, the motive which forbade their פריעה ופרימה.
V. 7. See note on Ch. 8,33.

Vv. 9—11. יין ושכר. In Kerithoth 13b we find various ways of defining the objects and the extent of this prohibition. According to the accepted Halacha of רמב״ם הל׳ ביאת המקדש I 1, 2, by שכר, not only wine, but any intoxicating drink. חיוב מיתה and חילול עבודה, however, are only incurred in the case of drinking in an “intoxicating quantity”. By an intoxicating quantity is understood even a רביעית of unmixed wine, (i.e., undiluted) or any quantity more than a רביעית of diluted wine. So that here there is no question of being really drunk, but only a fear of some slight disturbance in the clarity and tranquility of the mind. After drinking even such a small quantity no עבודה in the מקדש may be undertaken (v. 9) no decision made with reference to the מקדש (v. 10) nor any practical application of the laws of the Torah taught (v. 11). Not the unclear realm of excited feelings and phantasy, but the tranquil clarity and sharpness of sober intelligence is what the Word of God demands for all its fulfilment. Not to phantasy, to the clear and understanding mind does the symbolism of the Sanctuary speak. Only the clear and comprehending mind, keeping everything in its right proportion and its right place, is able to guide our steps and decide for us what is the right way to carry out the dictates of God’s Torah. The corpses of the first youthful priests, fallen through the lofty inspirations of their stirred feelings, preach the solemn warning to all future priests and leaders of the Jewish Teaching to look on themselves only as servants, guardians, teachers and realisers of God’s Sanctuary and God’s Torah; and to guard themselves against the serious danger of teaching the intuitive ideas of their own ecstatic selves in the place of God’s Truth and God’s Will, and in the place of being a faithful agent and a reliable leader for the realisation of the Torah, of following the dictates of an erroneous imagination. The Jewish teacher of the Torah must, all his life, remain the foremost obedient pupil of the Torah, שפתי כהן ישמרו דעת ותורה יבקשו מפיהו כי מלאך ה׳ צבאות הוא.

V. 12. הנותרים. Elsewhere we have already drawn attention to the difference between נותר and נשאר. We believe that נותר designates that which is left over and not destroyed although it was intended to be consumed, similarly to what we find כהנים משלחן גבוה :המנחה הנותרת מאשי ה׳ קזכו. Hence ת״כ finds in the expression בניו הנותרים, an indication that they had the temptation to act similarly to their brothers but were saved from yielding to it by admonition.

את המנחה. This is the מנחת צבור prescribed in Ch. 9,4, which, as remarked there, is the only מנחת צבור הנקמצת (excepting the עומד). Apart from that there was also the מנחה of נחשון (Numbers 7,13). which had to be brought on that day.

Vv. 13 & 14. כי כן צויתי: that באנינות יאכלוהו (Zebachim 101a). For two reasons it required the special command to eat these שירי מנחה and similarly the חזה ושוק in vv. 4 & 15. As already remarked on Ch. 9,4, these מנחת צבור and שלמי צבור, were quite unique, so that their treatment could not be deduced from what was prescribed for מנחת יחיד and שלמי יחיד in Ch. 6,7 et seq., and VII,28 et seq. Added to this, they were אוננים and even the כה״ג, who was allowed to perform עבודה as an אונן, was nevertheless not allowed to eat קדשים when in that state. כה״ג מקריב אונן ולא אוכל (Horioth 12b). Only in the moment of actual עבודה is the demand made of him that his personal feelings of grief and pain must completely retire before the national objective consciousness of God which is to be achieved by the עבודה. But in the אכילה, it is just the subjective personal enjoyment of the food which is to be raised to a symbolic עבודה-procedure. And the unavoidable feelings of pain prevent that feeling of cheerful happiness which is such an essential part of what אכילת קדשים is meant to show as a pattern for life in general. For the full meaning of these אכילות see notes on Ch. 6,7 et seq., and VII,28 et seq.

כי חקך וחק בניך היא מאשי ה׳ and כי הקד וחק בניך נתנו מזבחי שלמי בני ישראל: it was with both of them that they actually first entered into the right relationship of themselves to the אשי ה׳ and to the זבחי שלמי ישראל, they were the first שירים and the first חזה ושוק of the offerings of the people in which they participated. Their being eaten belonged essentially to the characteristic procedure of the יום השמיני. Here repeatedly, and quite specially, and at length is חזה ושוק specially stressed, for the giving and receiving of them is an ever-recurring recognition and admonition for the whole office of the priesthood, and its meaning and importance in the Nation. Both these אכילות belonged so essentially to the meaning of the day that, for them, the אנינות-prohibition was to be in abeyance. For the שירי מנחה it says במקום קדוש, for the במקום טהור :חזה ושוק, the former was not to be eaten outside the עזרה, here the חצר, the precincts of the place of offering, the latter not outside Jerusalem, here the מחנה ישראל, the טהרה of which is shown by the expulsion of the מצורע. The former, being קדשי קדשים was only allowed to be eaten by the זכרי כהונה, the latter, being קדשים קלים by בנותיך also. The claim to take part in the disribution, however, was restricted to the males, ת״כ) חק בניך ולא חק בנותיך).

V. 16. ואת שעיר החטאת וגו׳ והנה שרף. Zebachim 101a tells us that there must have been three שעירי חטאת there on that day, whose meat would normally have been given to the כהנים to eat: (a) the שעירי חטאת of the Nation, just prescribed in Ch. 9,3; (b) שעיר עזים לחטאת brought by נחשון, the Prince of the tribe of Judah brought on the first of the חנכת המזבח days which was this יום השמיני (Numbers 7,16); and finally as the day was ראש חדש ניסן, the שעיר חטאת של ר״ח. The first two were קדשי שעה, i.e., brought about by the special importance of the day, the consecration of the Mikdosh, and were part and parcel of that consecration. The last one belonged to קדשי דורות, i.e., to the normal and permanent communal offerings commanded to be brought for the ever-present character of the day (ר״ח. I.L.), חובות היום. From the reason given for its having been brought ואותה נתן לכם לשאת את עון העדה לכפר עליהם לפני ה׳, the Gemora proves there (101b) that it was only the שעיר של ר״ח that had been burnt. It is only this one that presupposes actual עון העדה, sins actually requiring atonement, whereas the others, שעירי קדשי שעה, were to be taken more as vows for the future (promises to stick fast to heights already attained and not to slip down. I.L.) than atonement for sins already actually committed.

V. 17. במקום הקדש, i.e., as it had not been brought outside the precincts of the Mikdosh, outside the עזרה) חצר) in which case it would anyway be פסול as יוצא, it being קדשי קדשים and would rightly have been burnt. — לשאת את עון העדה. Inasmuch as the כהן eats the בשר חטאת, and thereby, as we tried to explain on Ch. 4,11 & 12, expresses the final consequence of offering the דם and חלב, the achieving priest-like holiness of every phase of the whole of human life, his eating ranks with, and is part of, the procedure of atonement by which כפרה is accomplished for a sin committed. But here, at the שעיר של ר״ח, there is an additional idea associated with it, the meaning of which, it seems to us, has its roots deep down in the nature of this חטאת. For if we consider how this שעיר חטאת לה׳, according to Shebuoth 9a, comes to atone for such sins against the Mikdosh which are only known to God, חטא שאין מכיר בו אלא ה׳, errors שאין בו ידיעה לא בתחילה ולא בסוף, which were done unconsciously and which were also afterwards not known to have been done, then the saying: ואותה נתן לכם לשאת את עון העדה, said of no other offering, could be given a twofold meaning. Either in the sense, as in Numbers 18,1: את עון ,תשאו את עון כהנתכם המקדש, “Ye bear the sin of the Mikdosh, the sin of your priesthood”, i.e., you bear the responsibility for the sins against the Sanctuary, that is to say here: — God gave you the eating of this offering to bear the responsibility for the errors of the Community. The eating of this offering is to warn you to see to it, that, by careless unconsciousness, the People do not slip more and more into ever-increasing contrast to the purity of life which the Mikdosh stands for. Or in the sense of Numbers 18,1: ונשא אהרן את עון הקדשים, God has given you the eating of this offering to “lift up” (i.e., to remove, to get forgiveness for. I.L.) the sin of the community.
