Just as by the positive proclamation קדש לה׳ which the ציץ on the forehead of the High Priest made, all misunderstandings were countered, erroneous ideas which could have arisen from עון קדשים from the association of טומאה with offerings which is so contrary to the Law, and all such misunderstandings were removed by it הציץ מרצה (see notes thereon): in the same way, by the thoughts of raising even the enjoyment of one’s senses to a priestly function, as is represented by the priests eating the meat of the sin-removing offering (the חטאת) within the precincts of the Mikdosh itself, the thought-lessness is countered which quite unconsciously could draw one’s life in ever-increasing estrangement to the Mikdosh, and all such estrangement removed by it. In Aaron’s reply (v. 19) we shall find reason to think that this second way of taking the meaning of these words to be the correct one. In any case, by stressing this special purpose of atonement of the שעיר של ר״ח, Moses uses the special importance of it as a weighty reason for the reproof he thought he ought to make Aaron and his sons for their omission of having eaten it.

V. 18. הן לא הובא וגו׳, for had that been the case, the offering would have incurred the פסול expressed in Ch. 6,23 (look up) and would rightly have been burnt. — כאשר צויתי, as I had specially been commanded with regards to the אכילת שירי כלנחה (v. 12), that they were to be eaten in spite of the אנינות, and which I had immediately, בשעת מעשה, after the tragic event (see Zebachim 101a) told you as a general rule, that מפתח אהל מועד לא תצאו, that your condition of אנינות is not to make any break with your relation to the Sanctuary.

V. 19. הן היום הקריבו את חטאתם וגו׳: the חטאת and עולה of Aaron prescribed in Ch. 9,2 above, in which offerings the personalities of his sons as priests — as son-priests — were included. If we understand this answer correctly, it was just in the special characeristic meaning of the שעיר של ר״ח, which Moses had stressed to strengthen his reproach, that Aaron finds the justification for what he had done. He and his sons had this very day brought their offering of entry into the priesthood with חטאת and עולה. With these offerings they understand to keep themselves on the heights of their callings, and to be exemplary leaders of the people in ever-upward progress, and then immediately — ותקראנה אותי כאלה, an event happened which showed the actual state of mind of the priests who had just been consecrated to be in such contrast to the vows of consecration which their offerings had just expressed, that the capital error these newly conscerated priests made would not allow them to outlive the first moments of their consecration, ואכלתי היום, and then should we, in face of our own guilt, could we feel ourselves worthy by eating חטאת to atone for and counter thoughtless errors of the People? Even if everything that had been prescribed for the השמיני and which was to be done as a result of the consecration of the Sanctuary and Priesthood — and to which the שידי מנחה and חזה ושוק also belonged, as well as the שעיר חטאת העם and the שעיר נחשון — if all these קדשי שעה ordered for the special occasion of the day, were to make the depressing feelings of אנינות repressed even at the time of the אכילה, and even after such an event the אכילת חטאת of these קדשי שעה could be allowed, nay, could be a duty, nevertheless no deduction could be made from them for permission for the שעיר של ר״ח, which belonged to the normal קדשי דורות. The meaning of the former, the קדשי שעה, was not to atone for any actual lapses of the past or present, they referred entirely and completely to the yet unformed future, which just by them was to obtain a pure foundation by suitable resolves.

That which was given to Aaron and his sons of these קדשי שעה was not to be eaten in the capacity of what they already were, but just of what they were to become by this very eating. The eating itself was an admonition as to what their calling and mission was. So that the אנינות feeling, even intensified by the thoughts of unworthiness roused by what has happened, was not in opposition to their eating. The whole eating was nothing but an admonition of what the future expected of them. But the eating of the meat of the שעיר של ר״ח, belonging to קדשי דורות, is to achieve atonement for actual concrete errors which have been committed; there, the personality of the priest has to appear in symbolic exemplary perfection; and well could Aaron ask, whether in this case, in view of an event which proclaimed with such dire consequences the gulf that yawned between the actual state of the priests and the moral ideal which was to be expressed by the offering, whether here too his eating of the חטאת could be in accordance with the Divine Will? And that it could not be so, must have seemed to him the more probable, as even his own חטאת, though a קדשי שעה was not to be eaten, but, like the פר כהן המשיח had to be burnt outside the sphere of the life of the Nation (Ch. 9,11). In this sense the Gemora, Zebachim 101a, too, puts Aaron’s response:— שמא לא שמעת אלא בקדשי שעה דאי בקדשי דורות ק״ו ממעשר הקל ומה מעשר הקל אמרה תורה לא אכלתי באוני ממנו בקדשי דורות לא כל שכן, and there, the permission to eat קדשי קדשים in the condition of אנינות is altogether denied, a denial which, it seems to us, could only be considerably strengthened by the special character of the death in the case here. That in normal cases, in the eating of the offerings, the priest is to appear as a model to the bringer of the offerings is expressed in the words of Hosea Ch. 4,8: חטאת עמי יאכלו ואל עונם ישאו נפשו, והיה העם ככהן וגו׳, “the sin-offering of My People they eat, and thereby raises his soul (i.e., the priest gives up his whole mind. I.L.) to their sins, and the People become like the Priest” etc.

There are, however, there in the Gemora, two ways of taking this reply of Aaron. The one is that מפני אנינות נשרפה, that this שעיר של ר״ח was burnt just because of the condition of אנינות; for, according to that opinion, the condition of אנינות מן התורה lasts through the night even מן התורה, the אנינות לילה is דאורייתא. So that the בשר חטאת which may only be eaten יום ולילה, could not be eaten at all, and so had to be burnt. Then the היום, in ואכלתי חטאת היום, could not refer to the ocurence, but would characterise the חטאת as קדשי דורות as an offering belonging to a day, to ראש חדש, which has a permanent general character, it would be in the sense of חטאת יום. But according to the other opinion, אנינות לילה is only דרבנן, then the eating of the offering was only disallowed during the day, and would have been allowed to be eaten after nightfall, but מפני טומאה נשרפה: while they were keeping it till the night because of אנינות, it became טמא through no action of theirs, by itself, טומאה באונס באתה, and that was why it was burnt.

הייטב בעיני ה׳. The first י has a dagesh so that the ה is not to be taken as a question but as ה׳ הידיעה, and as is always the case when used in conjunction with a verb, has the relative meaning of אשר, e.g., הבאה מצרימה (Gen. 46,27) or הנמצאו פה (Chron. I. 29,17) and elsewhere. So that here too, it might mean “that which would be in accordance with God’s Will”. Then, just in those words would be indicated, that, to which, according to the explanation given in Zebachim, Aaron’s response referred. It accepts the fact that for certain offerings, קדשי שעה, the eating of the meat could be taken as being the Will of God, but an offering such as this, which belongs to קדשי דורות, would not be understood to be included in the Saying of God, באנינות יאכלוהו.

V. 20. לא בוש משה לומר לא שמעתי אלא שמעתי ושכחתי :וייטב בעיניו (Zebachim 101b). “Moses made no attempt to hide his error by saying: ‘I have no instructions from God for such a case’ ”, but he admitted that, as Aaron rightly had taken it, he had only been told that the law of אנינות was to be abrogated only for קדשי שעה, and that, as a matter of fact, he had forgotten this limitation.

V. 1. The whole of the previous chapter has a close connection with the dietary laws which form the subject of this chapter. It had shown how even men who were worthy to be consecrated as priests could fall into grave capital errors by the force of mistaken and misleading trends of sentiments, thereon it had given the warning to priests of the Sanctuary and teachers of the Law, that when they were called to service in the Sanctuary or to give a decision on the Law, they were to deny themselves such pleasures — though perfectly permissible at all other times — which might lessen the necessary clarity of mind or the necessary lack of excitement of feelings; then finally had taught, how the Sanctuary of God’s Torah considered the elevation into holiness of even the pleasures of our senses, as the zenith of the sanctification of our lives, which was its object, and demanded “the meal of the priests in the precincts of the Sanctuary” as the completion of atonement by offerings. All this brings us very close to the thought of how little we may consider the food we eat to have no bearing on our minds and feelings for the fulfilment of our calling, and of the mission which is given us, to be ממלכת כהנים וגוי קדוש.

Agreeing with this trend of thought which the contents of the previous chapter led up to, the introductory words of v. 1 here, at once express the great weight which the Lawgiver lays on the dietary laws which are given in this chapter. Already the fact that not only Moses, but at the same time Aaron too, is called up for their reception proves their special importance, וידבר ה׳ אל משה ואל אהרן. In the whole giving of the Law we only find this at the very first fundamental laws of the New Moon and the Pessach Offering (Ex. 12,1 & 43) and with the laws of טומאת נגעים זיבה ונדה (Levit. 13,1; XIV,33; XV,1). But, quite uniquely do we find the formula as here: וידבר ה׳ אל משה ואל אהרן לאמר אלהם, whereby the contents of these laws are given first to Moses and Aaron to be explained and understood and quite specially taken to heart, having regard to their position to the Torah within the Nation. Moses as transmitter and teacher of the Law, Aaron as educator for the carrying out of the Law, are both quite specially concerned in these laws, for the success of their work in the Nation. The knowledge and understanding of the Torah by the People to which Moses is directed, the feelings and will and determination of the People, which was Aaron’s mission to them, are, in the very first instance, dependent on the faithfulness with which the People keep these laws which are here given over to Moses and Aaron to implant in the lives of the Nation. With them a second, and higher foundation of the Nation was laid. By חדש and פסח the body of the Nation was created. By משפטים its social life was arranged. From תרומה till this eleventh chapter in שמיני the Sanctuary was made and erected, in which and by which, the ideal of the Torah, as the highest aim of life, was presented, which meant nothing less than the priestly and near-to-God holiness of the Nation in every individual member of it. For this ideal to become not a mere symbolic ideal of the Mikdosh, that it should become a reality in every phase of the life of every individual son and every individual daughter of this nation, so that it could so become, it was necessary that this Sanctuary of the Torah should find around it a community, to every son and daughter of which, the proclamation could be made:— קדושים תהיו כי קדוש אני ה׳ אלקיכם. For this it required people who had been begotten and fed quite specially for this aim. The regime for this, for the begetting and feeding of such people for the holy ideal of His Torah, God has laid down in שמיני, תזריע, מצורע, אחרי מזת, the chapters, leading up to קדושים תהיו.

V. 2. זאת החיה אשר תאכלו מכל בהמה וגו׳. We have already remarked on Gen. 1,24 & 25 how in general, חיה & בהמה designate characteristically different classes of mammals in the animal world. By the term בהמה is understood those animals which normally subjugate themselves to the srevice of man, which form the במה for Man’s superiority. The idea חיה, on the other hand, comprises all the others, which normally escape his sovereignity and demonstrate an “independent life”. So, in Gen. 7,14, כל החיה למינה וכל הבהמה למינה and Gen. 8,1: ואת כל החיה ואת כל הבהמה. Nevertheless, the term חיה occurs also as the general idea of living creatures as in Gen. 8,17 & 19: כל החיה אשר אתך וגו׳ כל החיה כל הרמש וגו׳. In the same way our chapter here too finishes with: להבדיל וגו׳ ובין החיה הנאכלת ובין החיה אשר לא תאכל, and with this term includes all the animals mentioned in this chapter. But the term בהמה also occurs in a wider sense to include the whole animal world as subjugated to Man, as in Gen. 6,7: מאדם ועד בהמה, and so also Gen. 7,23 & Ex. 9,25 et alia. But in a most characteristic manner both terms occur next to each other in our verse: זאת החיה וגו׳ מכל בהמה וגו׳, a choice of expression which makes us suppose that a careful application of it was intended. The Gemora in Chulin 70b & 71a refers to this and to the corresponding verse in Deut. 14,4 & 5, and points out that here, after היה is mentioned as the object of the sentence and it then goes on by complementing the sentence with מכל בהמה וגו׳ and in the following sentence continues with בהמה so that בהמה בכלל חיה, here, clearly, בהמה must be understood to come under the classification חיה, and, contrariwise, there, in Deut. 14,4: זאת הבהמה אשר תאכלו וגו׳ איל וצבי וגו׳, clearly, חיה בכלל בהמה, the חיה comes under the classification בהמה.

These mutually complementing mode of expressions which are used just in the case of the dietary laws, making the terms חיה and בהמה interchangeable and so removing their narrower meanings and teaching a חיה to be regarded as a בהמה and equally a בהמה as a חיה, may wish to teach us to take the wider meaning of both terms as an indication for our understanding the fundamental idea which underlies the peculiarity of the choice of animals which we are given permission to use as food. These mammals which we are to be allowed to use as our food must come under the idea of both חיה and בהמה in their wider meanings. The animal must have the body of a חיה in its wider sense and the nature of a בהמה. As a בהמה it must be a חיה, and as a חיה it must still have the בהמה character in its wider sense. The חיים in it, the life, must be unaffected; it may not be טריפה. The Gemora says: טריפה אינה חיה, חיה אכול, שאינה חיה לא תיכול (Chulin 42a); and in its nature, that characteristic nature must be predominant which in בהמה does not drive the animal to be antagonistic to Man, but to yield to him without attacking him.

V. 3. כל מפרסת פרסה וגו׳. We have already pointed out on Ex. 10,26, that the fact, that the hoof of the horse is also called פרסה, proves that the word designates “hoof” in general and not “divided hoof”, and that it would be derived from פרש = פרס, cover over, a hoof is a horny cover. That the verbal form of the word מפריס ,הפריס likewise does not mean divide or split is shown by the expression מקרין מפריס (Ps. 69,32) where מפריס quite clearly means “hoofed” as מקרין “horned”. Wesseley too, in his commentary on this verse gives it this meaning. Against this, the sentences in the following verses: ופרסה לא הפריסה ,ופרסה לא יפריס ,ופרסה איננו מפריס, seem to mean that the divided hoof is not present. But, apart from the fact that hares and rabbits, to which one takes ארנבת & שפן to refer, have no hoofs at all, in the camel too, the hoof formation is by no means complete, after v. 3 explains by ושסעת שסע פרסות, that the hoof formation required here is one which divides in into two, the expression: מפריס פרסה (in v. 4) would refer back to the preceding explanation as being only that formation of hoof about which it is talking; in exactly the same way as one is forced to make such an assumption in הוא גרה לא יגר of v. 7, where also, the actually deciding word מעלה is left out. So, too in Deut. 14,2, speaking of the חזיר, it says quite shortly: כי מפריס פרסה הוא ולא גרה.
ושסעת שסע: as above, in Ch. 1,17, ושסעת שסע .ושסע אותו בכנפיו פרסות, the one hoof divided into two hooves. So in Deut. 14,6: ושסעת שסע שתי פרסות.

גרה .מעלת גרה probably derived from גרר, — as זמה ,גזה from ,גזז גרר .זמם is found in מגרה, the saw, גגר would then have the meaning “to saw up”. — But that would, immediately, in this single word give us the most characteristic trait of a בהמה טהורה. A “true” ruminant, i.e., those that also have completely divided hooves, and so form the class of animals which we are permitted to eat, lack completely any incisors in the upper jaw. In place of them they have a hard rough plate in the upper jaw, on which by grinding circular movements the incisors of the lower jaw cut up the grass and herbage which form their food. This is aptly expressed by the term “sawing up” in גרה. This complete lack of incisors in the upper jaw is already, by itself alone, a sufficiently reliable test of “true” ruminants that the canon is laid down in Chulin 59a: כל בהמה שאין לה שנים למעלה בידוע שהיא מעלה גרה ומפרסת פרסה וטהורה. The “false” ruminants שפן and ארנבת, mentioned in the following verse have a complete set of upper incisors, and the camel too, only lacks the centrals and laterals but has the two canines standing, called ניבי (in Chulin). Only in young camels, in the first dentition or milk teeth, are all incisors missing, so that as long as one can recognise a young camel, the rule holds good ובלבד שיכיר בן גמל (ibid). In any case, according to that, the והוא גרה לא יגר of v. 7, which we mentioned above, and the still shorter, ולא גרה, in Deut. 14,8, would simply explain itself. Inasmuch as the pig has complete upper incisors in his dentition, his chewing is no sawing.

Animals that chew the cud have four stomachs. The food which is incompletely masticated by mere “sawing” comes in an almost raw state into the paunch (כרס), there it is softened and then passed into the second stomach (בית הכוסות) and gets formed into balls which are pressed up into the mouth again to be now properly chewed, and then passed into the tripe stomach (המסס) and finally into the renet bag (קיבה) there to be digested by the rennet or the juices of the stomach. This pressing up again into the mouth of what had merely been sawn, from the second stomach to the mouth is called: העלה גרה.

V. 4. ופרסה איננו מפריס. The camel has no complete hooves. They are only on top and do not surround the toes like a shoe. Also the toes which are divided above grow completely together again on the soles.

טמא הוא לכם. As it already says at the beginning of the verse: אך את זה לא תאכלו, the טמא הוא לכם at the end of the verse can only wish to indicate the reason for this prohibition. Now as this reason is given as “טמא״, it at once tells us that dietary health consideration is not what lies at the reason of this prohibition, but rather that the reasons are to be sought in that sphere in which the idea טומאה has its meaning. But this sphere is no other than קדושה, the sphere of moral holiness, the symbolic bearer of which we have already learnt to be מקדש וקדשיו, the Sanctuary and its belongings; and we have already learnt that symbolic טומאה, i.e., טומאת מגע, must be strictly kept away from it. If we are forbidden food as being טמא , the prohibition takes us to be in the state we are meant to be, i.e., קדושים and tells us that the forbidden food is in opposition to the קדושה which is our mission to strive for. טומאת מאכלות is in the same concrete contrast to the concrete moral holiness which we should make into a reality, as טומאת מגע, forms the symbolic contrast to the Sanctuary, the whole symbolism of which teaches the ideal of moral holiness which we are to make a reality in our lives. The ת״כ on v. 31 explains אלה הטמאים לכם בכל השרץ as follows: — מה ת׳׳ל לפי שנא׳ לא תטמאו בהם ונטמאתם בם, שומע אני טומאת הגויות וטומאת הקדושות ת״ל החולד והעכבר והצב למינהו. We believe that here these two kinds of טומאה: (a) טומאת מאכלות, which makes the body actually and concretely טומאה, and (b) טומאת מגע, which only symbolically is in opposition to the מקדש וקדשיו, are aptly called by the two names: טומאת הגויות וטומאת הקדושות. For, as the term טמא can be applied to both of them, the final sentence of the prohibition: ולא תטמאו בהם וגוי (v. 43), can be taken to refer to both kinds of טומאה, so that all שרצים would cause not only טומאת הגויות, but also טומאת הקדושות; that is why the sentence אלה הטמאים וגוי (v. 31), limits the latter to the eight שרצים named. The very first Jewish dietary law in Ex. 22,30, already indicated this connection between the dietary laws and the spiritual holiness which we are called upon to attain, and thereby assures the dietary laws their place amongst the foundations which were laid down for the social life of the Jewish Nation, the משפטים. There, the sentence ואנשי קדש תהיון לי ובשר בשדה טרפה לא תאכלו לכלב תשליכון אותו, tells us that as people of a moral-holy calling “we are not to eat our food at the same table that the animal world does” (i.e., we are not to regard our food in the same way that animals do), that our eating should not be a purely physical procedure, that it is to be on a moral spiritual level, that not merely physical considerations but moral considerations, considerations of our calling as אנשי קדש are to decide our choice of food. The fundamental principle laid down there, finds, here, in our chapter, the detailed laws for carrying it into practice. The positive criterion for the fitness of our food given there by the words אנשי קדש is here negatively given to be excluded from our food as that which is טמא. But it does not say טמא הוא, absolutely, but טמא הוא לכם. Not as אבר מן החי, for the calling of Mankind in general, but for אנשי קדש, for the People of this Torah, is this food declared here as טמא, as being not conductive to, not assimilateable with, that קדושה, which they are to strive to attain. (Compare the ן in תשליכון ,תהיון in Ex. 22,30, see notes thereon).

Further, as the sentence טמא הוא לכם indicates the actual nature of the animal as being the causative reason for the prohibition, that reduces the presence or absence of the two things mentioned the chewing of the cud, and the division of the hoof, to mere symptoms. In themselves they cause neither permission nor prohibition for eating. They are only a sign of the presence or absence of that character which is necessary for the one or the other. If, therefore, the presence or absence of such character is ascertainable with certainty by other conditions, the existence or non existence of these סימנין, of these purely symptomatic signs, becomes of no importance whatsoever. This way of looking at it, we think, must be the reason for the rule given in Bechorth 6b: — טמא הוא, הוא טמא, ואין טמא הנולד מן הטהור טמא, by which the following canon is taught:— ,היוצא מן הטמא טמא והיוצא מן הטהור טהור, that everything that comes from an “unclean” animal is “unclean” and from a “clean” one is “clean”, so that בהמה טהורה שילדה כמין בהמה טמאה מותר באכילה וטמאה שילדה כמין בהמה טהורה אסור באכילה, if a “clean” animal casts a young which lacks the signs of permitted animals, the young is nevertheless allowed to be eaten, and equally as animal with all the signs of a permitted animal which is born from a prohibited animal may not be eaten. In both cases the nature, the character of the animal is firmly established by that of the mother animal, and the presence or absence of the signs is of no consequence. This canon that כל היוצא מן הטמא טמא, is also applied in another way to all things that have their organic origin in a forbidden animal, e.g., milk and eggs. Bee’s honey is nevertheless allowed to be eaten, because it is not a substance which is produced organically in the body of the bee, but is a material which the bee collects in a sac from outside sources מפני שמכניסות אותו לגופן ואין ממצות אותו מגופז (Bechoroth 7b).

V. 5 & 6. Whereas of the camel, which though it has no complete hoof still has the beginning of a hoof, it says: ופרסה איננו מפרים, of the שפן it says: ופרסה לא יפריס, and of the ופרסה לא הפריסה :ארנבת, both of these are not hoofed-animals at all and this change of expression is certainly in corresponding relation to the formation of their toes.

Further, both these animals are מעלה גרה. One usually takes שפן to be the rabbit, and ארנבת to be the hare. But this translation can only be right if it were sure that both these animals chew the cud, which hardly seems to be the case.

V. 8. ובנבלתם לא תגעו. As even regarding טומאת מת, that worst kind of טומאה, which has to be considered as the fundamental class of all טומאות it is only the כהנים who are forbidden to come into contact with it (Ch. XXI et seq.), this prohibition here forbidding anybody to touch נבלה can only be understood to refer to such times when they have to come into contact with מקדש וקדשים, e.g., on רגל, hence the sentence in Rosh Hashona 16b, חייב אדם לטהר עצמו ברגל. Nevertheless, see below (at the end of this chapter) about the class of men amongst the people who lived on a high spiritual level and made it the rule of their lives to keep those precautions of the טומאה & טהרה laws which are prescribed only for the sphere of the Mikdosh, also to apply to their ordinary daily life, אכילת חולין בטהרה.

The sentence: מבשרם לא תאכלו ובנבלתם לא תגעו, primarily tells us that the בשר, the meat of “unclean” animals is always נבלה, as שחיטה has no effect on such animals. בהמה טהורה is only נבלה if it has died by other means than the correct prescribed שחיטה. — מבשרם וגו׳, the prohibition only extends to the eatable parts of the animal, but not to the uneatable, such as עצמות, גידין וטלפים, the bones sinews or claws (ת״כ).

טמאים הם לכם. Inasmuch as the various בהמות טמאות are here again summarised under the common term טמאים, we are told:— firstly, that שמצטרפין זה עם זה, that the flesh of different animals is considered together to make the minimum forbidden quantity כזית. Further as they are repeatedly designated as טומאה-causing material at which their special individual characteristics, as camel, rabbit, etc., are not mentioned, it tells us that in whatever form the material occurs, that juices, gravy, sediment, which are mixed with them, all come under this same prohibition, לאסור צירן ורוטבן וקיפה שלהם. But by the הם this extension of the prohibition is limited again by the provision that in a mixture the taste of the forbidden material must be present and not entirely lost, הם, פרט לשאין בהם בנותן טעם. As a rule it is taken that in a mixture of one in sixty, the taste disappears, and the material may be considered as non-existant בטל בששים. And finally מותרים הם בהנאה :לכם, although forbidden to be eaten, for any other purpose they are לכם, permitted to be used (ת״כ).

V. 9. סנפיר, fin, the derivation is obscure. קשקשת, scales, so also in שריון קשקשים, Sam. I. 17,5, to which the Gemora also refers in Chulin 56b, in explanation of our text. The root קשש is also to be found in גזז and seems to refer to a substance which can be removed by mechanical means, and therein the rule, which is adopted by all the ראשונים and also by the י״ר 83, 1, of the רמב״ו on our verse (but queried by נ״ב מ״ת י״ד כ״ח), that by קשקשת only removeable coverings of the skin are to be understood, (a view which it seems to us could be founded on the actual facts of the case) would find support. For in Chulin 66b, the canon is laid down that כל כל שיש לו קשקשת יש לו סנפיר, and thereby the existence of scales is declared to be a sufficient sign of Kashruth by itself, as it can be taken as sufficient proof of the existence of fins. Now in the aquatic animals referred to here, the ת״כ says definitely that amphibians are to be included, הגדלים בים והגדלים ביבשה. If then, by קשקשת fixed, unremovable scales were also to be understood, the large class of scaled amphibians (crocodiles etc.) would stand in opposition to the canon in Chulin.

את זה וגו׳ במים כל וגו׳ במים בימים ובנחלים וגו׳. After the element, the inhabitants of which are being talked about here, is first mentioned in its general meaning מים, the prohibition of eating is then expressed, as only applicable to special kinds of this element, ימים ונחלים. According to the hermeneutic rule, כלל ופרט אין בכלל אלא מה שבפרט, that where a general proposition is followed by the enumeration of particulars which are already comprehended in the general proposition, the scope of the proposition is limited to the things specified, the prohibition given here of eating all acquatic animals which have not got fins and scales would apply only to ימים ונחלים, to seas and rivers. But the general proposition מים is repeated twice before mentioning the particular cases, and thereby the text shows us its intention that the idea of the particular cases is to be extended, and the form of the sentence is to have the power of כלל ופרט וכלל, by which the second כלל gives the פרט, the particular cases, the meaning of being examples and the proposition then applies to all things which are similar to the particular cases: כל מקום שאתה מוצא שני כללים הסמוכין זה לזה הטל פרט ביניהם ודונם בכלל ופרט וכלל. Thereby the prohibition is extended to everything כעין הפרט, i.e., to everything that bears the characteristics of the given conception ימים ונחלים. To what extent an exemplary כלל ופרט וכלל given in this way, is to be taken, is a matter about which opinions differ according to whether one takes כללא קמא דוקא or כללא בתרא דוקא, i.e., according to which way one takes such a כלל ופרט וכלל. The opinion that כללא קמא דוקא sees in it only a כלל ופרט sentence extended by the added second כלל, while the opinion that כללא בתרא דוקא considers that the first preceding כלל makes it into a restricted פרט וכלל sentence. In the first opinion, that it is a כלל ופרט, by the rule that אין בכלל אלא מה שבפרט, the law was restricted solely to that which was named in the פרט, and then by the addition of the second כלל extended to all objects which agreed with this in all essential qualities. In our case, the essential qualities of the (ימים ונחלים) פרט are: — גדלים על גבי קרקע and מים נובעים formed on the earth’s surface and springing from a natural source, so that חריצין ונעיצין artificially dug canals and lakes (into which natural water is diverted or collected) would be included as they participate in both the essential qualities. But בורות שיחין ומערות, cisterns, ditches and pits, which although גדלים על גבי קרקע are not נובעים, would be excluded, and certainly the law would not apply to כלים, to fish that are bred in water which is contained in vessels. In the second opinion that it is a פרט וכלל, by the rule that נעשה הכלל מוסיף על הפרט, the כלל is given its widest application and then by the first כלל, which transfers the כלל ופרט into a כלל ופרט וכלל, this wide application is restricted and thereby everything is excluded which is not similar to the פרט in any of its essential qualities, but is extended to everything which has at least one essential quality in common with the פרט. In our case, according to this opinion, even בודות שיחין ומערות would be included, which, even if not נובעים, are still גדלים על גבי קרקע and only כלים would be excluded. But even this way of taking our sentence finds in the preceding explanatory phrase את זה תאכלו, the intention of restricting the prohibition, and arrives at the same result, i.e., that the demand for fins and scales only applies to fish that are produced in waters that spring from a natural source, only to ימים ונחלים and to חריצין ונעיצין, which are fed by natural wells or springs. But according to the teaching of תנא דבי רבי ישמעאל, a form of sentence such as ours here, where במים, בימים ,שני כללים סמוכין זה לזה, is not to be considered at all as כלל ופרט, but as רבוי ומיעוט, and according to that way of taking it the law would be applicable to all flowing waters even if not coming from springs, so that the law would apply to חריצין ונעיצין שאינם נובעין, and only כלים as well as בורות שיחין ומערות שהן עצורים ככלים, i.e., only such fish are exempt from the Law which are bred in closed-in waters, in vessels, cr in closed-in pits similar to vessels etc. (Chulin 67a, תוספות thereon and י״ד 84,2). On the difference between the two ways of taking כללא קמא or בתרא as being דוקא, and the relation of these to רבוי מיעוט ורבוי, see תוספות thereon, 65b, דייה וכי תימא.
V. 10 u. 11 שקץ הם לכם. Vergl. oben V. 8 zu טמאים הם לכם. Nur ist ציר דגים, nicht durch Kochen extrahierter Saft von דגים טמאים nur שאני ציר דזיעה :דרבנן אסור בעלמא הוא (Chulin 99b 'תוספו daselbst).

In Deut. 14,10, forbidden fish are classed under the general idea expressed by טמא. But here they are more specifically described as שקץ. Whereas קיץ occurs also referring to physical loathing, sickness, as in Numb. 20,15, נפשנו קצה בלחם הקלוקל, elsewhere שקץ is used exclusively only for spiritual, mental disgust. In exactly the same way as here, eating these animals is forbidden with the words ואת נבלתם תשקצו, so in Deut. 7,26, it uses term שקץ תשקצנו referring to all forms of idol-worship, to describe the extreme extent with which we should reject, and the extreme opposite to our spiritual and moral beings which we are to regard, everything pertaining to idolatry. Accordingly in the books of the Prophets the terms שקוצים and שקוץ are used just by themselves to describe idols and idolatry, and one can indeed say that שקץ only occurs referring to these forbidden animals and to idolatry. Only once do we find: כי לא בזה ולא שקץ ענות עני (Ps. 22,25), and there too it could well have the same meaning viz., “He does not despise and does not consider giving a favourable hearing to the poor, as being in contrast or opposition to (שקץ) His Greatness and Holiness etc”. If then, the nature of a food, regarding the prohibition of eating it, is described as שקץ, eating of it must be in the sharpest contrary opposition to that condition of spiritual mentality which should form the fundamental character of our being. Whereas טמא only makes us unfit for שקץ ,קדושה leads to the very opposite of that condition.

V. 10 & 11. שקץ הם לכם ושקץ יהיו לכם, by their nature they are שקץ towards you, and therefore you are to treat them as שקץ. The prohibition to eat them rests on the actual concrete contrast of their nature to yours. To the sentence ושקץ יהיו לכם: the Gemora, Pesachim 23a, attaches the law that they are to be treated as שקץ also regarding our possession of them, that we may not have them, or anything else that is prohibited to be eaten מדאורייתא, as the wares in which we deal. Only במזדמן, if by chance one happens to come into our possession may we sell it. But this prohibition only applies to objects which are primarily used for food, but not to animals such as horses, asses etc., which are principally used for work. The only exception in things which are prohibited מדאורייתא to be eaten, is הלב, which is allowed to be used as סחורה (see Ch. 7,24). — מבשרם לא תאכלו, here, too, the prohibition only applies to the eatable parts but not to the bones etc. — ואת נבלתם תשקצו. As there is no שחיטה for fish, and touching their dead bodies does not cause טומאה, the word נבלה can not be taken in the sense in which it is used in v. 8, referring to ת״כ ,בהמה טמאה on this verse says that it refers to eating any acquatic animal without scales which is “taken out of the element in which it lives” and comes להביא מן היבחושין שסיננן. For, according to vv. 9 & 10, only such animals which are in natural waters, or at least, in flowing waters are forbidden. But those bred in standing waters in closed-in containers or in vessels, would not be included in this prohibition. But the permission to eat them is here restricted by the condition that they must still be found in their “life-element”, in the fluid in which they were produced. As soon as they leave that, for instance, if one passes the fluid through a strainer in which they are left behind, סיננן, then, immediately, תשקצו, they must be treated as שקץ, they then, according to Chulin 67a, come under the classification of כל השרץ השורץ על הארץ. Quite in agreement with this way of taking נבלתם is the law in Sabbath 107a, that taking a fish out of water is considered equivalent to the act of killing it and, according to the teaching of ב״ש in Chulin 75a, a fish taken out of the water has even immediately to be treated as dead.
V. 12. במים. It only depends on their having scales while in the water and does not matter if they lose them on being taken out of the water (as certain species of flat fish are reputed to do I.L.).

V. 13—19. We have left the names of these forbidden birds untranslated because, according to the Halacha given in Chulin 61a et seq., all other kinds of birds, those not named here, are allowed to be eaten, so that a wrong translation of the name of even one of these birds could lead to a transgression of the Torah. For the translation of most of these names rests merely on assumption. Tosephoth, in Chulin 63a, ד״ה נץ and 62b ד״ה מאי ספיקיהו, finds it necessary to cast doubts as to whether the translation of even נשר as eagle and עורב as raven is correct. From an anatomical and physiological comparison of the traits of the permitted יונה and the forbidden נשר, the Gemora there, in Chulin, gives three positive and one negative sign of טהרה, viz.: אצבע יתרה ,זפק ,קרקבנו נקלף and אינו דורס, the possession of all of which, or in certain cases even some of them, would show the permission to eat the bird. But, for us, even of these signs only two are clear and without doubt, זפק, the possession of a crop and קרקבנו נקלף, having the inner skin of the stomach easily peeled off. On the exact meaning of the sign of the claws, אצבע יתרה and of the way it holds or catches its food, אינו דורס, the opinions of the commentators of the Torah differ. And, already from the time of the Amoraim we have had the canon: עוף טהור נאכל במסורת, that birds may only be eaten on reliable tradition that they have been used for food in orthodox communities.

V. 20. כל שרץ העוף ההלד על ארבע. Winged insects have at least six feet. We therefore presume that the number four mentioned here may wish to say, only that they have more than two feet, and this multiplicity of feet is just the characteristic difference between עוף and רמב״ן .שרץ העוף, too, seems to take it this way. Nevertheless see v.23.

V. 21 & 22. V. 21 only demands “spring-feet” as the characteristic sign of permitted שרץ העוף, But v. 22 gives the names of several special kinds which, on the one hand limits the wide general application of v. 21 to those named, and on the other extends the permission, by the addition of למינו and למינהו. Hence in Chulin 65, the sentences are taken as כלל ופרט כלל and the names in v. 22 would then be examples (כעין הפרט. I.L.). By this the common characteristics of the species named are added to the כרעים of v. 12 (called קרצולין in the Mishna) as the necessary signs for permission to eat שרץ העוף, and we get the four signs: ארבע רגלים ארבע כגפים, קרצולים, וכנפיו חופין את רובו, to which a fifth condition is added ושמו חגב, that they are all known to be a species of חגב. The לו in verse 21 is written as לא, to tell us that these grasshoppers (locusts etc.) are allowed to be eaten even in the stage when the “springs” on their feet are not yet developed, אין לו עכשיו ועתיד לגדל לאחר זמן (Chulin 65a), (i.e., it looks like לא, but in reality it is לו. I.L.).

V. 23. וכל שרץ וגו׳. We have already remarked on v. 20 on the difficulty of the fact that, as far as we know, no winged insect has less than six feet. The difficulty is the greater inasmuch as רבי in ת״כ, in explaining this verse says: אם יש לו חמש הרי זה טהור. An explanation in accordance with the actual facts is very much to be desired.

V. 24. ולאלה תטמאו. Up till now it has been speaking of טומאת גויות, i.e., of the prohibition to eat animals whose flesh would concretely, physically מטמא our bodies. In this connection it enumerates the mammals, fish and birds which come under this category, and to the latter it appends the winged insects. Then follows the wingless crawling creatures, the laws, concerning which are only given in v. 41 and 42. Verse 41, וכל שרץ השרץ על הארץ, according to the sense, continues directly our verse 20, כל שרץ העוף. But the Torah interrupts to tell us the relation of the animals already dealt with, to טומאת קדושות, to the טומאה, which is not concrete but only mental and only has reference to symbolic things, to the מקדש and to קדשים. With regard to this, we are now told here, that although all those mentioned up till now cause real actual טמא, only those that follow לאלה תטמאו. it is only towards those that “one has to consider oneself טמא״. This is then immediately explained more precisely: כל הנוגע בנבלתם יטמא עד הערב, that everything that touches their dead bodies has to observe the טומאה-law. What this טומאה-law is, namely that everything so affected has to keep away from all קדשים, is explained in detail in Ch. XXII. This symbolic טומאה is, as the הרכסים לבקעה aptly remarks, as a rule expressed by ולאלה תטמאו :טמא ל- here, so also לאביו ולאמו לא יטמא ,לה יטמא (Ch. 21,3 & 11), כל טמא לנפש (Numbers 5,2) whereas the actual concrete טומאה of מאכלות אסורות and עריות is always construed טמא ב-, e.g., ולא תטמאו בהם (v. 43), ולא תטמאו את נפשתיכם בכל שרץ (v. 44), אל תטמאו בכל אלה (Ch. 18,20), לטמאה בה (ibid 24) etc., etc. In these latter cases the object construed with ב- is the concrete actual cause of the טומאה, the טומאה is the concrete physical working of it, one becomes טמא by it. In the former cases it is the ל- of the object, the relation, the aspect with which one approaches it, the frame of mind one gets לו, the feeling that one, too, belongs to that class of things, that begets the טומאה; the cause is only an idea, a train of thought induced by a procedure outside the person, and so the effect too belongs only to the realm of thoughts. The effect can be removed as soon as this train of thought is negatived by other procedures, as soon as one is removed in place and time away from connection with the object that caused it. The procedures which, in place and time, remove relation to the cause of the טומאה are טבילה and הערב שמש. See below. ולאלה תטמאו accordingly means. If you come into contact with these, you are to consider yourselves as טמא.

V. 24 & 25. וכל הנשא מנבלתם וגו׳ כל הנגע בנבלתם וגו׳: Here, the effects of מגע and משא are differentiated. מגע is direct contact, but contact only. The body of a living human being approaches the dead body of one of these creatures and touches it without moving it. This idea of touching only, applies to the outer surface of one’s body. Contact with inner parts of one’s body or the cavities of the body or folds of the body, מגע בית הסתרים, is not called נגיעה in this connection (Nidda 42b & 43a, see תוספות there משא .(ד״ה למימרא, according to Rashi, Chulin 20b, ,ד״ה מלק ר״ש Zabim 5,3 and Keilim 1,2, is not a passive bearing of an object, merely being laden with it, but an active carrying, i.e., an action moving it from its place, which would include היסט, moving it without carrying it (pushing it with a stick, kicking it etc. I.L.). According to רמב״ם on Kelim 1,2, simple passive bearing without moving the object would also come under the heading of משא. But in הל׳ טומאת מת 1,6, his opinion on this is not at all clear. According to ר״ש, a mere passive bearing comes under the heading of אבן מסמא, which comes into question at טומאת זב (Ch. 15,4). Neither משא nor היסט require direct contact, moving a נבלה from a distance, however far away from it, makes the one who moves it טמא. The consequences of משא, as both these verses show, are more far reaching than those of מגע. Of מגע it says: כל הנגע בנבלתם יטמא that only that which actually touches them: כלים ,אדם or אוכלים becomes טמא. But with משא, the טומאה extends at once to all כלים or אוכלים, which are in contact with the person at the time of the משא. They become ראשון לטומאה exactly as the person himself does. This direct transference of the טומאה to all objects which are in contract with the person who is moving the נבלה, is called טומאה בחבורין, the טומאה which is transferred by “connection”. It is expressed in our text by the term וכבס בגדיו. The word בגדיו is used in such connection in the widest sense of the conception “בגד״. This includes all objects which belongs to the presentation of a Man in his active life, with which he appears to be “equipped”, of which בגדיו, his clothes, are quoted merely as the most striking example. These כלים (and אוכלים?) are the completion of בגד, the human vesture in its narrower conception. Only אדם and כלי חרס are excluded. Anything touched by the person after he is no longer in contact with the נבלה, becomes only שני לטומאה, and this can only apply to אוכלים as אדם וכלים only become טמא from contact with an :(ת״כ) אב-הטומאה צ״ע אי הנושא נבלה מטמא אוכלין בחיבוריו להיות תחלה מדאורייתא, דהא אפילו כלי חרס ממעט ליה בת״כ, מפני שאינו דומה לבגד שיש לו טהרה במקוה אע״פ שהוא דומה לו בהיותו כלי, כ׳׳ש אוכלין ומשקין שאינו דומה לבגד כלל. והא דקאמר פ״ה דזבים מ״א. כל המטמא בגדים בשעת מגעו, מטמא אוכלין ומשקין להיות תחלה, אפשר דרק מדרבנן קאמר, תדע דהא מיירי שם ג״כ מידים שהוא ודאי רק דרבנן וצ״ע דמפרשי המשנה .והברייתא בת״כ פרשת זבים משמע דס״ל שהוא דאורייתא

יכבס בגדיו. The reinstatement of טהרה, which only takes place by טבילה, by complete immersion in a מעין or מי מקוה, (see notes on v. 32 & 36), is here and elsewhere often expressed for כלים by כביסה, an expression which otherwise designates the ordinary washing of objects. We presume that this expression is intentionally chosen to prevent the mistake of thinking that אוכלין also could regain טהרה by טבילה. This error could arise from the fact that בגדיו, as already remarked, with regard to the transmission of טומאה, in a broad sense, includes כלים and אוכלים. But the reinstatement of טהרה is limited to כלים and therefore a term is used which normally refers only to כלים.

וטמא עד הערב. The טבילה of all טמאים (except נדה ויולדות 90b) has to take place in the day time (i.e., those who are טמא for one day only, can טובל themselves immediately, or if for seven days on the seventh day, any time after sunrise, Megilla 20a). Immediately after the טבילה, the returning טהרה starts, but the complete return of the state of טהרה only comes with the entry of a new day which begins at nightfall. Untill then the טמא is called טבול-יום, and has the character of a שני לטומאה, may eat מעשר שני but not תרומה or קדשים. With the entry of night, these two are permitted to him. The four זב וזבה, מצורע ויולדת :טמאים, whose complete טהרה is dependent on their bringing the prescribed offerings, and who are accordingly called מחוסרי כפרה, after הערב שמש — nightfall — may eat תרומה, but are precluded from eating קדשים until they have brought their offerings. These laws are summarized in Yebamoth 74b, in the sentence: טבל ועלה אוכל במעשר, העריב שמשו אוכל בתרומה, הביא כפרה אוכל בקדשים, and this regaining טהרה in stages is referred back to the three entences: ולא יאכל בקדשים כי אם רחץ בשרו במים (Levit. 22,6), where the eating of קדשים is dependent on ובא השמש וטהר ואחר יאכל מן הקדשים ;טבילה (ibid 7), where it is only allowed with הערב שמש; and finally וכפר עליה הכהן וטהרה (ibid XII,8) where the טהרה is dependent on the bringing of the offering. The first sentence refers to מעשר, the second to תדומה and the third to קדשים. A יולדת, of which the last sentence speaks, during the whole time between the טבילה and the bringing of her offering, is called: טבולת יום ארוך.

In ת״כ, the טומאת נבלה spoken of in these verses is referred to טומאת אבר מן החי, which actually is quite analogous to טומאת נבלה, and only differs from it inasmuch as אבר מן החי is only טמא in its complete state, as an אבר, but not a piece of flesh separated from it, בשר הפורש מן אבר מן החי, whereas בשר הפורש מן הנבלה is טמא. According to that, the נבלה here does not refer to a whole animal that has died, but to an organic part of one, which has “died off of it”. But the Gemora in Chulin 128b, does not take טומאת אבר מן החי from here but from וכי ימות מן הבהמה in v. 39, which expression can also include a part of the animal which had died. So that our verses here remain for the laws of טומאת נבלה, which admittedly have already been given in general terms in v. 8, but which are here explained more fully in their various degrees of application.

V. 26. לכל הבהמה. The ל- in לכל has a similar meaning to the ל- in ולאלה תטמאו (v. 24) to which indeed this verse refers. טומאת נבלה is taught in v. 26—40 in four groups, and the animals forbidden to be eaten in three groups arranged according to their descending remoteness from Man. V. 26 speaks of the ungulata, the hoofed animal, but those whose hooves are not divided and who are not ruminants. Being hoofed they stand nearest to Man amongst the “unclean” animals. Then in v. 27, the unhoofed quadrupeds and finally in v. 28, the small creeping animals, still farther off from Man. Then in v. 39 follow the fourth group, טמאים הם לכם .נבלת בהמה טהורה: By comparison with v. 31, אלה הטמאים לכם וגו׳, it is evident that these words here, as well as the similar ones in verse 27 & 28 refer only to טומאת מגע and not to איסור אכילה, but the reason for these repetitions has still to be found.
V. 28. All נבלות בהמה טמאה are מטמא במגע ובמשא. Moreover, all animals are only מטמא in death. No live animal is a source of טומאה or able to become טמא. Only Man is able to be both while alive.

V. 29—31. שרץ השרץ על הארץ are the lower creeping animals. Although all of them are אסור באכילה, only the eight kinds named here are טמאי מגע. The correct translation of their name is not quite sure. חלד, weasel, עכבר, mouse, is known. צב, according to Rashi in Kethuboth 15a, and also, according to ר״ש Taharoth 5,1, is a toad, or anyway an animal like a frog. אנקה: according to Rashi is a hedgehog. כח is unknown. הלטאה, according to Rashi, is a lizard. המט, according to Rashi Chagiga 11a, would be a snail. But from Chulin 128b, it is evident that the animals classed here as שרץ are all vertebrated animals, their characteristics, are בשר גידים ועצמות, they consist of “flesh, tendons and bones”. But snails are definitely invertebrates, so חמט can hardly be snails. תנשמת also occurs amongst the birds and, according to Rashi, would there refer to the bat, and here among the שרצים to the mole. Both these animals belong to the same order, according to Oken (the zoologist I.L.), which may be the explanation of the common name.

The שמנה שרצים are only מטמא במגע, but not במשא, and, like all other animals, only במותם, but not while alive. But אבר מן החי of a שרץ is none the less מטמא, it is a מיתה of a part (Chulin 128b). They are also different from בהמה in that their blood is also טמא like their flesh אין דמם חלוק מבשרם, whereas דם נבלה in the ordinary way is not טמא. This speciality of the ח׳ שרצים is expressed by the words: וזה לכם הטמא (Meila 17a), which are taken to mean that the idea of טמא is to be applied to the שרץ in all its components (see notes on v. 36). כל הנוגע בהם וגו׳ יטמא: The בהם in this verse would imply that it is necessary to come into contact with a complete dead שרץ to become טמא, while the מהם in the next verse, 32, וכל אשר יפל עליו מהם וגו׳, brings the טומאה even from a piece of a שרץ. This is explained in Chagiga 11a, that the טומאה depends on the size of the piece being sufficiently big for its being able to be recognised for what it is and so represents the whole insect, מקצתו שהוא ככולו. For שרצים this minimum is fixed at the size of a lentil, כעדשה, as being the beginning of “size” of the smallest of the שרצים viz., the חמט. The minimum size for נבלת בהמה is a כזית. The further condition for מקצתו given in Nidda 56a, is that the body of the שרץ, or rather the piece of it must still be לח, fresh, if dried up, יבש, or שרוף, it is only מטמא if it is complete, כולו, and the form, the shape of the body uninjured: שלדו קיים.

By the repeated addition of על הארץ to שרץ the idea of the שרצים named here is confined to land animals and does not apply to e.g., עכבר הים etc. (Chulin 126b et seq.). From the combination בשרץ השורץ על הארץ (after if has said in v. 43, also, where it is talking of איסור אכילה, simply בכל השרץ השורץ), the Gemora there and in Nazir 64a learns the Halacha that for טומאת מגע both ideas: השורץ and על הארץ are decisive. It says: כתיב בכל השרץ השורץ, which implies בכל מקום שהוא שורץ that the טומאה is quite independent on the place where the שרץ happens to be, על הארץ, by which the טומאה depends on the שרץ being on the earth, ,הא כיצד ודאי מגעו טמא ספק מגעו טהור, i.e., if there is no doubt of the contact with the טומאה-bringing object then it does not matter where it was. But if there is doubt whether contact actually took place then the rule ספק טומאה ברשות היחיד שיש בו דעת לישאל טמא (see notes on Numb. 5,13) is only then to be applied if the object is על הארץ, is lying on the ground, but not if it is צפה or נזרק, if it is floating on water or if it was thrown and there is a doubt if it touched while in the air. Hence the sentence: כל הניטלין והנגררין ספקן טמא מפני שהן כמונחין והנזרקין ספקן טהור. ספק טומאה צפה בין בכלים בין בקרקע טהור. Similarly in Taharoth 4,3: השרץ בפי החולדה והנבלה בפי הכלב ועברו בין הטהורין או שעברו טהורין ביניהן ספקן טהור ,,מפני שאין לטומאה מקום״. (See ר׳׳ש thereon and Mishna 7).

These characteristic laws apply to all טומאת מגע and even to מגע של מת, but not to מאהיל על המת nor to עליונו ותחתונו של זב (see ר״ש there. Rambam in שאר אבות הטומאה 15,3, seems to limit ספק צפה only to וצ״ע .שרץ).

V. 32. וכל אשר יפל עליו מהם במותם. Going further into the details of the laws of טומאת נבלת שרץ, the Torah gives a case which, at the same time, is instructive for the conception of אבר מן החי which, regarding טומאה, is identical with נבלה. Instead of saying וכל אשר יגעו בו במותם it says וכל אשר יפל עליו מהם במותם, a part of the שרץ falls off from it, this is אבר מן החי. As this is made equal to מיתה, this partial מיתה is limited to the same idea as מיתה itself. It must be something that can not be reproduced by the animal, like a whole dead animal, כעין מיתה שאינו עושה חליפין, that is to say a whole organ, an אבר but not בשר הפורש מן החי, not a piece of flesh that has fallen off from the living animal, which the animal would reproduce. More, according to ר׳ עקיבא and רבי, the conception of אבר is even narrower, it must be a miniature representation of the whole organism, i.e.,it must be an organ which contains all the component parts of the whole organism, according to ר׳ עקיבא, at least sinews and bones, according to רבי flesh, sinews and bones: מה שרץ גידים ועצמות וגו׳, or מה שרץ בשר גידים ועצמות וגו׳ (Chulin 128b).

מכל כלי עץ או בגד או עור או שק כל כלי וגו׳: by כלי עץ, all vessels made of wood are understood; by בגד, all textiles made out of vegetable or animal threads כל שהוא טווי וארוג, any material which is spun and woven. If it is made up into a garment, the size is immaterial, if it is simply cloth, then linen or woollen material is considered a בגד if it is at least שלש על שלש (אצבעות), three finger-breadths square. Other material, if it is at least (טפחים) שלשה שלשה על, three hand-breadths square (Sabbath 63b, 26b & 27a). כלי עור are objects made of skin or leather. שק is an object made out of woven goats’ hair. In Numb. 31,20, it is expressed by the term וכל מעשה עזים. But it includes generally all articles made out of parts of animals, out of hair, bones, horns, claws etc. But it is limited to materials which come from land animals, similar to עזים. Objects made out of the bones of birds or feathers, or fish are not מקבל טומאה (Chulin 25b, Kelim 17,13).

Of these four categories, כלי-עץ, בגד, עור, שק, it is the last one, שק, which, apart from the material, also designates the form of the articles and the idea which is represented by this form and is applied to all other categories. The idea of the nature of a sack is, that יש לו בית קיבול and מיטלטל מלא וריקם, it is a receptacle into which one can put something, and it can be moved from place to place whether empty or full. But articles made out of the materials mentioned here which are simply פשוטים, flat without being hollowed out anywhere to form a receptacle into which an object can be placed, עור) ,פשוטי כלי עץ כלי עור ,כלי עצם only if it is so rigid that one can not wrap anything up in it, תוספות Sabbath 63b), or, if they are so heavy when filled that they can not be moved from their place, are not מקבל טומאה. To come under this latter heading, כלי עץ העשוי לנחת, it is assumed that if its cubical content is three cubic cubits, מחזיקין ארבעים סאה בלח, it will be too heavy to move when filled (Chulin 25a; Sabbath 83b; Chagiga 25b; Kelim 15,1).

Articles which are ראוים ומיוחדים למדרס, i.e., which are fit for, and used for, people to lie, sit, ride or stand on, and are accordingly, liable to the טומאת משכב ומושב ומרכב of a זב וזבה ונדה ויולדת (see Ch. XV), are subject to all other טומאת מגע even when פשוטים, without having a בית קיבול, and, according to תוספות, Menachoth 31a, also in any size, even if not מיטלטלין מלא וריקן (Sabbath 84b; Bechoroth 38a). See Menachoth 31a, תוספות that by מיוחדים למדרס is to be understood only such articles (as sheets, blankets, carpets, chairs, saddles, stands etc.), which serve for the body to rest on, but not such things as e.g. stilts or a pair of steps etc., which serve for movement.

With reference to פשוטי כלי עץ, a further difference is made, whether they are purely משמשי אדם, used exclusively for man, as e.g. a ladder, or if they are משמשי את האדם ואת משמשי אדם, used at the same time for Man and for his appurtenances as e.g. a table, שלחן, and in the latter case they are also מקבל טומאה. But, according to תוספות in Erubin 31a, this טומאה is only מדרבנו, and so it seems also from רמב״ם (הל׳ כלים 6,1) ר׳ יוסי in Kelim 16,7 makes a further difference in the case of משמשי משמשיו של אדם, i.e. articles which serve as appendages to vessels, and says that if they are always with the vessel בשעת מלאכה ושלא בשעת מלאכה, both when the vessel is in use and out of use, they are to be considered as belonging to the vessel and מקבל טומאה. This canon also, refers to פשוטי כלי עץ, e.g., a flat wooden cover to a vessel or a flat wooden plate or stand under it. It seems that this טומאה too is only דרבנן.

כל כלי אשר יעשה מלאכה בה: it must be able to be considered as an actual כלי, and חפויי כלים, coverings which only serve to protect the vessels, are excluded (ת״כ). As it is speaking here of containers which are able to be carried about even when full (see above. I.L.), probably by מלאכה it is that it is just this transportation which is to be understood, a conception which, regarding, שבת, also comes under the heading of מלאכה.

Amongst the materials mentioned here, out of which vessels are made, מתכות, metal, is omitted. Nevertheless, we find such vessels mentioned in Numb. 31,22: אך את הזהב דאת הכסף את הנתשת וגו׳ (Sabbath 16b) — In Aboda Zara 75b the וטהר and במי נדה יתחטא, which is said there is taken to refer to the prescribed טבילה of כלי סעודה של מתכות, which had to be done to the כלי מדין which came into Jewish possession. This “dipping” of metal vessels coming from non-Jewish sources before being used for food has nothing to do with טומאה; and from the Gemora in Sabbath 16b, the opinion seems to be formed that such “טבילת כלי מדין״ is only מדרבנן, and the references in עבודה זרה just quoted are to be taken only as אסמכתא. See כ״מ on הל׳ מאכלות אסורות 17,5. But the אך with which the paragraph is introduced, places it in connection with the preceding verses to such a degree that what it says is: - for כל בגד וכל כלי עור וגו׳, for everything that is not כלי סעודה של מתכות, the only consideration is טומאה but for these apart from טומאה, the laws of הכשר and טבילת כלי מדין apply. This connection is made even more obvious by the omission of the word כלי, which is to be supplied solely by reference back to the preceding verse — כלי מתכות, accordingly are not included in the comparison to שק, and, for them to be מקבל טומאה neither the quality of having a בית קיבול nor that of טלטול מלא וריקן is necessary. Hence, even פשוטיהן are טמאין and even if they are עשוין לנחת (Chulin 25a & Chagiga 25b). There is still another difference between כלי מתכות and כלי עץ. All כלים are only מקבלי טומאה when נגמרה מלאכתן only as soon as they bear the כלים-character, i.e. when their manufacture is completed. But the necessary stage of completion for מקבלי טומאה differs for כלי מתכות and כלי עץ. A כלי עץ is מקבל טומאה as soon as it can be used for the purpose for which it was made, even if it is not yet stained or painted and polished, and it, accordingly still is called גולם, “in the raw unfinished state”; but a כלי מתכות only when it is quite finished and does not require sand-papering and polishing. Hence the sentence: גולמי כלי עץ טמאין פשוטיהן טהורין, גולמי כלי מתכות טהורין פשוטיהן טמאין, נמצא טהור בכלי עץ טמא בכלי מתכות, טהור בכלי מתבות טמא בכלי עץ (Chulin 25a). There (on page b.) the reason for the greater degree of finish demanded for כלי מתכות is given as being either because לכבוד עשויין, apart from their utility, the idea of beauty, ornamentation, is predominant in their manufacture or because דמיהן יקרים, they are a more expensive, better class of vessels than common wooden ones.

במים יובא וטמא עד הערב וטהר. In ת״כ on this verse we find this noteworthy sentence: (Ch. 22,7), במים יובא כולו כאחת יכול מקצתו ת״ל ובא השמש וטהר מה טהרה האמורה למטן ביאת שמש כולו כאחת, אף כאן ביאת כלי כולו כאחת; the sinking of the כלי and the sinking of the sun, both of which bring the state of טהרה, are placed parallel to each other, and for both complete “sinking” is demanded, a parallel or comparison which gives us a welcome explanation of the two factors, טבילה and הערב שמש, which are necessary for טהרה (see below). Moreover, here in our verse, it does not say ובא השמש וטהר as in Ch. 22,7, or וטהר בערב as in Numb. 19,19, but וטמא עד הערב וטהר so that the טהרה-condition refers itself back also to the עד ערב time, to express the fact that after the טבילה “until the ערב״ a mixed condition of טומאה and טהרה enters, טהור למעשר and טמא לתרומה, as we have already remarked in the case of a human being, the condition of טבול יום on v. 27 & 28 (Yebamoth 75a).

V. 33. וכל כלי חרש: by כלי חרש all vessels made of baked clay are understood. Unbaked they come under the heading of כלי אדמה which, like כלי אבנים, are not liable to טומאה. כלי חרש :אשר יפל מהם אל תוכו only receive טומאה from inside, from their internal space, אויר כלי חרס, the טומאה-bringing object need not even touch the inside walls of the vessel. They do not get טמא from גביהם, their outer surface, but as soon as the object enters the inner space of the vessel, the whole vessel becomes טמא. In the same way regarding the vessel making things טמא, it says: כל אשר בתוכו יטמא, that everything inside it becomes טמא, even if it was filled with, e.g., mustard seeds of which the top and middle ones do not come into contact at all with the vessel, nevertheless, literally by being inside the vessel, all become התורה העידה על כלי חרש אפילו מלא חרדל — טמא: the manner in which it receives טומאה is derived from the manner by which the Torah says it imparts it: ילפינן תוכו ליטמא מתוכו לטמא (Chulin 24b). An earthenware vessel which has a tightly fitting lid on it, אשר צמיד פתיל עליו as its contents are protected from becoming טמא, so does it protect them from the טומאה which everything else incurs in an אהל מת, is מציל באהל המת (Numb. 19,15). So כלי חרש forms a complete contrast to all other טהור בכלי חרס :כלים טמא בכל הכלים, טהור בכל הכלים טמא בכלי חרס, אויר כלי חרס טמא וגבו טהור, אויר כל הכלים טהור וגבן טמא (Chulin ibid). But this is only as far as their capacity for becoming טמא, once a כלי חרס has become טמא by תוכו, its גבו is also טמא and what touches the vessel from outside becomes :טמא כלי חרס נטמא תוכו נטמא גבו (Bechoroth 38a). מרובה מידה דלטמא מליטמא, שכלי .(עי׳ מל״מ ה׳ כלים א׳ י״ג ,ת״כ) ,חרס מטמא אחרים מאחוריו ואינו מיטמא מאחוריו פשוטי כלי חרס, which have no תוך, can accordingly not become טמא by contact, and as אין מדרס לכלי חרס, they have no טומאה at all (Bechoroth 38a). כלי חרס, accordingly, can never become אב הטומאה. Other כלים can become אב הטומאה either as משכב ומושב של זב or by touching a dead body. But כלי חרס is not ראוי למדרס, and only such כלים, which have טהרה במקוה, become אב הטומאה by contact with a מת, but a כלי חרס which has become טמא has no means of regaining טהרה, of them it says here ואתו תשברו (Erubin 104b). There too is the characteristic law for כלי חרס that המכניס כלי חרס טמא למקדש פטור, either because לית ליה טהרה במקוה or because אינו נעשה אב הטומאה. Tosefoth in Nidda 28b takes, as a result of discussing the first motive, the consequence to be that מכניס שרץ למקדש would also be פטור. But, nevertheless, this would be according to the version of R. Chananel which Tosefoth in Erubin ibid ד״ה לא דכ״ע חייב, and Tosefoth himself there gives preference to Rashi’s version, according to the result of which the latter second motive would be the right one, and then מכניס שרץ חייב, with which Rambam too agrees (הל׳ ביאת מקדש 13,16). כל אשר בתוכו יטמא. The vessel itself becomes ראשון לטומאה and its contents שני. That is why contents are immediately more precisely described in the next verse only as אוכלין and משקין for only these can become טמא through a ולד הטומאה, as the כלי חרס here is. But כלים, like אדם, only through אב הטומאה (Pesachim 20a & b and Sabbath 138b).

V. 34. מכל האכל אשר יאכל, the addition אשר יאכל is taken in Yoma 80a, quantitatively to designate a size which represents one full mouthful, i.e., the size of a hen’s egg, כביצה, although otherwise in connection with איסור, the minimum quantity is the size of an olive: כל השיעורין כולן בכזית חוץ מטומאת אוכלין ששינה הכתוב במשמען ושינו חכמים בשיעור. According to ר״ת in Tosefoth ibid and Pesachim 33b, this שיעור כביצה applies equally to לקבל טומאה (of which it primarily speaks here) and to לטמא אחרים. But Rashi mentions another opinion according to which this size is demanded only for transferring the טומאה, but for אוכלין to become טמא the very smallest quantity, כל שהוא, suffices. Rambam, too, adopts this last opinion, in 4,1 טומאת אוכלין. But according to that, the wording of our text would be very difficult to explain. According to the explanation of תוספות) ה״ר יוסף Pesachim 33b) that, even according to this view, for הכשר (see below) the size כביצה is demanded, the difficulty might disappear as just here, in our text, the teaching of הכשר לקבל טומאה is given, by the phrase אשר .יבוא עליו מים

ת״כ on our verse explains the phrasing as giving also a qualitative meaning: האוכל — (a specified אוכל. I.L.), אוכל המיוחד — human food, מאכל אדם. Animal fodder, מאכל בהמה, is not מקבל טומאה. Then, אשר יאכל, it must still be eatable, פרט לאוכל סרוח, if the food has become rotten it is not מקבל טומאה; more, even if it had already been טמא, even the טומאה of a נבלה, the טומאה disappears as soon as decay sets in לכי מסרחא פרחה טומאתה and a difference is only made between the greater or lesser degree of decay, whether it is only not ראוי לגר or even not לכלב, and also whether סרוחא מעיקרא, whether the decay had already been there before the טומאה or had only come afterwards (Menachoth 23a & Bechoroth 23b). Nevertheless, the food need not just be fit for Jewish consumption to be מקבל מאכלות אסורות .טומאת אוכלין, which only non-Jews may eat, are also מקבל טומאה. Even אמורי הנאה, which a Jew may not give anybody else to eat, and which accordingly have to remain completely out of any use at all by a Jew are likewise מקבל טומאה (see Menachoth 101b).
אוכלין .אשר יבוא עליו מים are only מקבל טומאה after they have once been wetted, intentionally or at least with the owners’ approval. This wetting is called הכשר (see more particulars on v. 38).

וכל משקה אשר ישתה וגו׳. In Pesachim 16a et seq., there are three opinions as to the receptivity of liquids for טומאה: (a) מדאורייתא, they are both מקבל טומאה and מטמא אחרים; (b) that מדאורייתא, they are מקבל טומאה, but they can not pass it on to others, are not מטמא אחרים; (c) that מדאורייתא they are not מקבל טומאה at all, אין טומאה למשקין כל עיקר. According to this last opinion, our verse כל משקה וגו׳, would then not be speaking of טומאת משקין but of הכשר and would come to extend and limit the conception of מים of the preceding verse. It would tell us that not only מים but also כל משקה אשד ישתה, and not any מים but only such מים which has the limitation prescribed for כל משקה viz. בכל כלי, that it is תלושין, removed from the earth, no longer as מחוברין, part of the globe, only such water has the effect of rendering אוכלין liable to טומאה. And, in effect, certain other liquids do come under the heading of משקה which are מכשירין. Altogether there are seven such liquids, they are:— dew, water, wine, oil, blood (regarding blood, it must be remembered that, as mentioned above, מאכלות אסורות, too, are receptive to טומאת אוכלין), milk and honey (bees’ honey), (Machshirin 6, 4). By blood only דם חולין, but not דם קדשים is to be understood (it says אשר ישתה. I.L.), and also from חולין, only דם שהנפש יוצאה בה (Pesachim 16a & b, see note on Ch. 7,26).

רמב״ם, (הל׳ שאר אבות הטומאה 7, 1; טומאת אוכלין 1, 41), takes as Halacha the opinion that משקין מקבלין טומאה ואינם מטמאין אחרים מדאורייתא. According to that, our verse does speak of טומאת משקין and comes to tell us that, just like אוכלין as we are told here, are liable to טומאה, so are also כל משקה אשר ישתה as soon as they are בכל כלי, i.e., תלושין. But again it is only the seven liquids mentioned above, that are to be understood by משקה שבעה משקין טמאים ושאר כל המשקין טהורין :אשר ישתה (Terumoth 11, 2). Although then this idea of משקה אשר ישתה would here refer primarily to טומאת משקין, but not to הכשר, nevertheless the idea of מים for הכשר זרעים is (ת״כ on v. 38) extended to these ז׳ משקין and restricted to them, so that both הכשר and טומאה only applies to these seven liquids (רמב״ם ibid).

Moreover, just as the conception משקה with regard to טומאה does not include every drinkable liquid, so the conception אוכל in this respect is a limited one e.g., materials which only serve to flavour the food (pepper, vanilla etc.); מילי דעבידי לטעמא are not טומאת אוכלין (Nidda 51b).

Further, just as, in the case of משקין, there is מן התורה no transmission of טומאה at all, so with אוכלין too, transmission is limited. אינו עושה כיוצא בו, they do not transmit טומאה to objects in the same category as themselves, אין אוכל מטמא אוכל and only משקין can become טמא by contact with an אוכל טמא (Pesachim 14a & 18a & b). More, according to the opinion that מדאורייתא there is no טומאת משקין at all, אוכלין, too מן התורה would only be receptive for טומאה, but would not transmit it.

V. 35. תנור וכירים. The ovens referred to here, were moveable earthern vessels, like big pots without bottoms. They were fixed, temporarily to the ground with clay, and the walls were covered with a coat of clay which was called טפילה. They are specially mentioned here, to tell us that their being temporarily fixed to the ground does not do away with their character of being mobile vessels, they retain the idea of being כלי הרס and as such, are סד״א כיון דחבריה בארעא גופא דארעא דמי קמ״ל :מקבלי טומאה (Sabbath 125a, Rashi ד״ה נתנו על פי הבור and also ד״ה ההוא לאידך גיסא).

נתץ .יתץ is always used in connection with the breaking up of immobile objects, such as a house, ונתץ את הבית (Ch. 14,45). The choice here of just that word instead of the usual term applied to כלים viz. שבירה (v. 33), is to show that the ovens or hearths required smashing up, מחסרי נתיצה, that is to say, were מחוברין (Sabbath ibid). יותץ, is, equally with אותו תשברו, no direct command that every כלי or תנור of חרס is to be broken if it becomes טמא, but the Torah immediately adds וטמאים יהיו לכם (which seems redundant. I.L.). As טמאים, they are לכם, for your lay use. They may be used in a טמא state for חולין uses as long as you keep them apart and not in contact with מקדש וקדשיו. It is only the restoration of טהרה which necessitates שבירה, or in the case of a כלי חרס .נתיצה ,תנור have no טהרה במקוה as other vessels have which are accordingly called כלי שטף (after וכל כלי עץ ישטף במים Ch. 15,12, in contrast to וכלי חרס וגו׳ ישבר). (See Rashi Chulin 25a in contrast to Rashi Bechoroth 38a, according to which the term כלי שטף is only applied to כלי עץ; see תוספות there). Incidentally, all kinds of vessels, equally with כלי חרס, regain their טהרה by שבירה and while in the state of שבורים can not become טמאים. By שבירה it is not necessary for the vessel to be completely broken, but it is sufficient if it is sufficiently damaged to be rendered unfit for the use for which it was intended and so ceases to be that כלי. So, to take as example כלי חרס, it would depend on the use for which that particular vessel was intended. If it was meant to contain solid food, a hole כמוציא זית, big enough for an olive to fall through, would suffice, if it was to contain liquids, נקב ככונס משקה, the size would be a hole through which the liquid would enter or the still smaller, כמוציא משקה, through which the liquid would leak out. If it was intended for larger fruit; it only loses its טומאה by a hole, כמוציא רימון, which would allow a pomegranate (the size of melon or small child’s head) to fall through (Sabbath 95b).

So that the ability to receive טומאה and the continuation of the state of טומאה is dependent on the “designation”, the purpose for which the vessel was designed, and in the same way, the degree of “completion”, the גמר מלאכה, which as mentioned in v. 32, is necessary before a vessel can become טמא, is likewise dependent on the purpose for which it is intended to be used. For instance, a skin or hide, which is to be used as rug or carpet is considered “finished” and מקבל טומאה as soon as it is fit for that purpose, but if it is intended to be cut up for straps or shoes it would not be considered “finished” and would not be מקבל טומאה. Similarly, a ring intended for human wear can become טמא, but an exactly similar one destined for animal wear can not become טמא. It is to this “destination” of vessels that the canon given in Kelim 25, 9, refers when it declares:— כל הכלים יורדין לידי טומאתן במחשבה, ואינן עולין מידי טומאתן אלא בשינוי מעשה, שהמעשה מבטל מיד המעשה ומיד המחשבה, ומחשבה אינה מבטלה לא מיד מעשה ולא מיד מחשבה, “simply making up one’s mind to use it for any certain purpose is sufficient to bring a vessel into the condition of being able to become טמא, but once it has been brought to that condition, merely changing one’s mind to use it for a different purpose is not sufficient to remove its ability to become טמא, some change must be made in the vessel itself, (מעשה), to express the change of intention. (See Sabbath 52b).

In Chulin 118a, the expression used here, טמאים יהיו לכם, regarding כלי חרס, as well as the repeated phrase טמא הוא לכם in v. 33, referring to זרעים, is taken to mean that להכניס ולהוציא טומאה, regarding the reception and transmission of טומאה, the vessel, or the food, is not to be considered literally by itself, a כלי or an אוכל, but לכם, i.e., לכל שבצרכיכם, with everything on it that serves your requirements, i.e., with stalks, handles, hafts, etc., ידות. So that these ידות stalks etc., belong to the fruit or vessel, both להכניס and להוציא טומאה, that by means of touching the יד, a כלי or an אוכל can become טמא (i.e. להכניס) or if the כלים or אוכלין are already טמא, the טומאה would be transmitted by contact with their ידות (i.e. להוציא). Of course, with a כלי חרס, the יד can only be להוציא as contact even with the vessel itself would not make the vessel טמא, it is only מקבל טומאה מאוירו (תוספות, Chulin 24b, ד״ה וגבו טהור. See מל״מ on הל׳ כלים XVII,1).

V. 36. אן מעין וגו׳. This אד places מעין ובור מקוה מים in contrast to the מים ומשקה בכל כלי of v. 34, indeed they are the very opposite of both the laws regarding טומאה which are given there in respect to מים ומשקה בכלי, liquids contained in vessels, שאובין. For there liquids “drawn” in vessels are given the ability: (a) to become טמא, and (b) to מכשיר אוכלין, i.e. by wetting them, to make אוכלין able to become טמא. In contrast to these, it says here that מעין ובור מקוה מים, that springs, and all waters not in a כלי, but similar to spring-water, i.e. without תפיסת ידי אדם, without “being touched by Man’s hand”, waters collected on the earth, טהורים, shall neither have the ability to become טמא, nor, as הכשר, to render anything else liable to טומאה, but in both directions יהיה טהור. (See תוספות Pesachim 16a ר״ש & ד״ה בשלמא Machshirin IV,b; the ת״כ excludes מים שבבורות שיחין ומערות already in v. 34, from the ability to הכשר, because they are not בכל כלי, not taken up from the earth, not תלושין מן הקרקע).

Our verse, accordingly, tells us primarily: — that whereas if any part of a (dead) שרץ falls into a vessel containing food or drink (Vv. 33—36) the vessel and its contents become טמא, in a similar case, if the שרץ falls into a מעין ובור מקוה מים, neither the pit or whatever the water is contained in (provided of course it can be considered as part of the earth. I.L.) nor the water is contains becomes טמא. Nevertheless, ונוגע בנבלתם יטמא, the dead שרץ in the מעין or מקוה still makes anything that touches it there טמא.

But water in springs or gathered in similar hollows in the earth, i.e. without תפיסת ידי אדם, is not only contrasted to מים שאובין בכלי, but has the very opposite character to it. Not only is it not responsive to טומאה as that is, not only does it not make other things responsive to טומאה as that does, is not מקבל ומכשיר הטומאה, not only remains pure itself and allows other things to remain pure, but it also actually makes things pure, restores טהרה, is a means of טהרה, is טהור in its widest sense, just as טמא does not only mean the condition of טומאה but also the ability to transmit it.

So here we have the medium described, which is understood everywhere by the term מים, which in sentences as וטהר, ורחץ במים וטהר, במים יובא וגו׳ is given as the means of regaining טהרה for men and things. We learn from our verse the essential characteristics of such a מקוה מים in which men and objects which have become טמא can regain טהרה by complete immersion (see note on v. 32). The water may not be in כלים, not, for instance, in a bath tub, but must be similar to a מעין ובור, in a hollow which is part of the earth. Like these, it must be collected naturally in such hollow without being touched by the hand of Man, בלי תפיסת ידי אדם without having become שאובין. The Haalcha insists that the term יהיה טהור is meant literally that הוייתן על ידי טהרה בעינן, that the water in the מקוה may not have been brought there by means of anything that is able to become טמא (Zebachim 25b). This idea is by no means identical with מים שאובין. Water drawn in a stone vessel becomes פסולם שאוב for a מקרה although the vessel being a כלי אבן is not מקבל טומאה (see notes on v. 32 and 33), and a solid metal rail, not hollowed out at all, is unfit for leading the water into the mikvah, because, as פשוטי כלי מתכת (see ibid) it is מקבל טומאה although the water, provided that the rail has no בית קיבול which could hold the water, is not מים שאובין. Further, water alone and no other liquid is qualified for a Mikvah (Chulin 84a).
