Three cubic cubits of מים כשרים למקוה, the average quantity for containing completely the human body, אמה על אמה ברום ג׳ אמות must first be brought in the specified manner, into the hollow, for the idea of a “Mikvah” to be established, then as much מים שאובין as desired may be added (רמב״ם Mikvaoth IV,b).

The water qualified to form such a טהרה-bringing bath, need not be spring-water. Only for זב is מים חיים prescribed. Our text mentions בור מקוה מים next to מעין so that any other collection of water, for example, rain water in pits, holes, ditches or other cavities in the earth is designated as qualified for טהרה as long as it has not lost its elementary character in the ways indicated. Between spring and other waters the only difference is, that the latter, the “non-spring” water only effects טהרה when it is similar to בור i.e. is quiescent, not flowing, באשבורן, standing in a closed-in space, but not בזוחלין if it is running or flowing, but spring-water may be either flowing or standing. From this the consideration arises that at certain times and in certain conditions, rivers should not be chosen to be used a “mikvahs”, namely when it is to be feared, at times when the river has risen, that there might be more rain water than spring water רבו נוטפין על הזוחלין in the river, and so it would only be qualified to be used באשבורן (Sabbath 65b). But according to another opinion brought there נהרא מכיפיה מבריך, when the river is swollen by rain, the flow from its source is also increased by the rain, so that one may assume that זוחלין are always מרובין (see תוספות there).

V. 37. וכי יפול מנבלתם על כל זרע זרוע אשר יזרע. From Sabbath 95b, where speaking of זרעים, it explains that that which is sown in a flowerpot with a whole in its bottom, עציץ נקוב, is considered as מחובר, and as such is not liable to הכשר טומאה and explains our verse: שאני לענין טומאה דהתורה רבתה טהרה אצל זרעים שנאמר על כל זרע זרוע אשר יזרע, one would deduce that זרע זרוע אשר יזרע is to be taken to refer to זרעים מחוברין, to grains which are sown and that the repetition of the idea of זריעה is to indicate that in whatever manner they have been sown, even if in an עציץ נקוב, the seed is to be considered as part of the earth, and not responsive to הכשר. The following verse, וכי יתן מים על זרע, would then refer to זרע אשר לא יזרע, to fruit which is not planted, to זרעים תלושין, which are responsive to הכשר. According to ת״כ, too, the אשר יזרע of v. 37 could be taken to refer to planted fruit, מחוברין, and perhaps זרוע to indicate the idea of מאכל האדם similar to ויתנו לנו מן הזרעים in Daniel 1,12. For there, (in ת״כ. I.L.), the הכשר described in v. 38 is limited to מאכל אדם ותלושין, and v. 37 would contain the contrast מאכל בהמה) ,מאכל אדם מחוברין would then be taken to be excluded automatically, as well as the condition that the מים must be בידי אדם and not בידי שמים, from the phrase וכי יֻתַּן).

But the Gemora, Chulin 117b, 118 & 119, quite obviously takes the זרע זרוע אשר יזרע to refer to זרעים תלושין, which only lack the הכשר mentioned in the following verse to be able to קבלת טומאה; and from the addition זרוע אשר יזרע learns that the fruit is מקבל טומאה not only after it is shelled and the stalks removed so that it is ready for human consumption, but even in the stage at which it is sown, with its shell (שומר) and the remains of blossom still on it, (פיטמא), and the שומר as essentially belonging to the fruit is not only as יד (see note on v. 35), מכניס ומוציא טומאה, but is considered a part of the fruit itself and is מצטרף לטמא טומאת אוכלין, is reckoned with the fruit to make up the necessary quantity, the שיעור כביצה, to enable it to transmit טומאה (see on v. 34): על כל זרע זרוע (אשר יזרע) כדרך שבני אדם מוציאין לזריעה חטה בקליפתה ועדשים בקליפת, and equally so מצטרפת הפיטמה של רימון (ibid). In agreement with this, Rashi, accordingly, explains the quoted verse, in Sabbath 95b, התודה רבתה וכו׳ אשד כדרך שאדם מוציא לזריעה למעוטי מחובר כל דהו :יזרע which obviously can only be taken to mean: — הזרע אשר יזרע, grain which still has to be sown, which still has the sowing before it, is only טהור, because it lacks הכשר מים, but as soon as it is sown, in any way whatsoever, even if only in an עציץ נקוב it is מחובר and as such is affected neither by הכשר nor by טומאה.

Nevertheless, it is possible that the זרע זרוע אשר יזרע does actually mean seeds already planted, and the teaching of שומר לצירוף in Chulin 117b et seq. is not derived from the additional words אשר יזרע, but from זרע זרוע. Grain only remains אשר יזרע :טהור, when it is really sown. But before that, even in the ordinary condition of seed for sowing, חטה בקליפתה וכו׳, it is, as זרע זרוע able to become טמא. This seems to us the most probable meaning of this difficult verse and we have given it this meaning in our translation because in ת״כ the far reaching Halacha is expressly attached to the phrase: אשר יזרע טהור הוא, that זרעים טמאים שזרען טהרו, that not only plants in the earth, as soon as שהשרישו they have taken root are not able to become טמא, but even seeds or plants that have become טמא, as soon as they are planted and have taken root become טהור again.

In any case, in these two verses, 36 & 37, we have the important rule, that everything that is מחובר, i.e. which, like water in a well and plants rooted in the soil, is so much attached to the earth that it may be considered to be an actual part of the earth itself, all such things are removed from the whole sphere of טומאה. More, we see here that טבילה במים and השרשה בארץ actually restore טהרה, as the ת״כ puts it: הארץ מעלה את הטמאים מטומאתן והמקוה מעלה את הטמאים מטומאתן. Hence also, כלים שנעשו לקרקע ותשמישן עם הקרקע, all things that are made to be permanently fixed to the ground and are only to be used while joined to the ground, e.g., a metal drainpipe or gutter, צנור, are not מקבל טומאה (Kelim 2, 2; ר״ש thereon). To what extent תלוש ובסוף חברו, a moveable object loses its mobile character by later being fixed into the ground and כחבר דמו, differs with regards to the application of different laws (see Chulin 16a). To decide whether a vessel fixed to the ground is to be considered a כלי or not, depends on the question whether קבעו ולבסוף חקקו or חקקו ולבסוף קבעו, if the material out of which the vessel is made, e.g. a piece of wood, was first fixed into the ground and then hollowed out to form a receptacle, or if it had first been given the shape necessary for it to be a כלי (in the narrower sense of the word) and then fixed into the ground (Baba Bathra 66a). From the conception זריעה we also get the law of השקה. Although in the ordinary way אוכלין ומשקין have no טהרה במקוה, if water which has become טמא is sunk into a מקוה in such a manner that its surface becomes perfectly level with, and indistinguishable from the surface of the mikvah-water, it regains its טהרה. By thus being joined to the מי מקוה it becomes “sown” again in the earth like the mikvah-water and regains its pure elementary character (Pesachim 34b; Beitza 17b, Rashi). And according to the רא״ש (Baba Kama 67a) it is also this idea of זריעה by which the מים שאובים which, as mentioned above, are allowed to be added to a מקוה of ארבעים סאה, lose their שאובים character.

V. 38. וכי יתן גו׳. As it does not say here in a similar way to v. 34, וכי יבוא מים על זרע, which would imply that the water could come even completely automatically, but it says יתן, and נתינה always implies an intentional act, but, on the other hand, it uses the hopthal form, יֻתַּן, which always stresses the act having been done, and allows the person by whose will and intention the act was done, to remain in the background. A “twixt and between” condition is, therefore, indicated in which both factors, the intention of the mind and the unpremeditated form of the action come into consideration, it must be כי יותן דומיא דכי יתן, מה יתן דניחא ליה אף יותן דניחא ליה, i.e. an action which was not caused by Man, but which he nevertheless wishes to take place. An example would be rain which wets fruit, which the owner likes to have washed: (Kiddushin 59b). This, ניחא ליה, this being in accordance with the owner’s wishes need not necessarily refer to the actual wetting of the fruit itself, it is sufficient if the existence of the water in a תלוש-condition is in accordance with a person’s will, ניחא ליה, even if its touching the fruit was quite outside his intention, for instance, if he had placed a vessel out in the rain so that it should be washed (so that the water descending is what he wants so that although it is יֻתַּן it is as if יִתֵּן. I.L.), and the water splashes off the vessel on to some fruit, it does מכשיר the fruit. הכופה קערה על הכותל בשביל שתודח הרי זה בכי יותז, (Chulin 16a). Hence the canon: כל משקה שתחלתו לרצון, אע״פ שאין סופו לרצון, או שסופו לרצון אע״פ שאין תחלתו לרצון, הרי זה בכי יותן, And indeed it is not far-fetched to find indications of this canon in the various expressions used in verses 34 & 38. אוכל אשר יבוא עליו מים is fruit on which water comes without your intention, it comes anyhow, even וכי יתן מים .סופו שלא ברצון על זרע is תחלתו ברצון, the water must be intentional. But this תחלתו ברצון is only effective if the water was intended to be used for the benefit of a דבר תלוש, as in the given example: לצורך הקערה. This תלוש, in this respect, is given the widest interpretation so that even תלוש ולבסוף חברו, (see above), is considered תלוש, e.g. כותל בנין, a wall built up of stones (Chulin 16a). הכשר of אוכלין only requires to be done once, once they have been wetted by משקין המכשירין, (see notes on v. 34), even if they completely dry up afterwards, they remain for ever מקבל טומאה (Baba Metzia 22a). טמא הוא לכם, see note on v. 35.

V. 39 & 40. These verses treat of טומאת & טומאת נבלת בהמה טהורה אבר מן החי. For it does not say וכי תמות בהמה וגו׳ הנוגע וגו׳, but: וכי ימות מן הבהמה. Chulin 128b explains this expression to mean, both, the טומאה of a partial מיתה, namely when only a limb of the living dies, i.e. אבר מן החי, and also to restrict the application of בהמה אשר היא לכם לאכלה, from being applied to all such animals (as it says מן. I.L.): מקצת בהמה מטמאה ומקצת בהמה אינה מטמאה ואיזו זו טרפה ששחטה. For, whereas the conception נבלה in v. 24 et seq. referring to בהמה טמאה is given without any qualification, and so applies to any kind of death, even if it occurred through שחיטה, here, for בהמה אשר היא לכם לאכלה the condition of נבלה is attached to the words: כי ימות, i.e. on a מיתה by which the animal becomes not לכם לאכלה, is not looked on by us as food for our consumption. Taken to its logical conclusion then, שחיטה שאינה ראויה, a שחיטה after which we are still not allowed to eat the meat, (if, for instance the animal proves to have had some organic trouble which renders it טרפה) should also not prevent the condition of נבלה. But as the whole conception of restricting נבלה is contained in the word מן (some of, a part of. I.L.), the idea of מיתה causing נבלה is applied to the mode of death which has no power at all of causing היתר אכילה, but שחיטה, which is the means of changing the animal into food prevents its being considered נבלה, even when, for other reasons the actual היתר אכילה is hindered; as long, of course, as the animal belongs to the species אשר היא לכם לאכלה. Hence שחיטה מטהרת טרפה מטומאתה (Zebachim 69b). But, if the act of שחיטה has not been done perfectly and completely, or if the throat of the animal had been so wounded that the air and food tubes could not be cut, so that the animal dies, not by שחיטה, then in all cases טומאת נבלה occurs. There are even cases where the animal has been so crushed and wounded that, even while still living, it has to be considered as dead and is נבלה מחיים for instance if נשברה מפרקת ורוב בשר עמה (Chulin 21a, 32b ש״ך on י״ד 33, 3). (If you apply Hirsch’s basic explanation of the whole meaning of טומאה, especially of the טומאה-causing effect of the carcasses of dead animals, all these דינים become perfectly logical. I.L.).

נבלה is only applied to the muscles and nerves of the body, but not to the bones, horns, claws etc. (Chulin 117b). It seems not improbable that the term נבלה (from the root נבל, to be used up withered, dead) can only be accurately applied to the active parts of the organism, to those parts in which the power of sensitiveness and movement is innate. Bones etc., form the passive equipment of the body which is set into motion and activity by the powers of the muscles and nerves. So that it is only in the muscles and nerves that the departure of life really shows itself. The law that חלב נבלה and דם נבלה are not טמא has already been considered above on Ch. 7,24—26.

נבלה .והאוכל וגו׳ והנשא וגו׳ is מטמא במגע ובמשא, as has already been said in vv. 24—28 (look them up) with regards to נבלת בהמה טמאה. If then we are told here regarding נבלת בהמה טהורה that it is מטמא בגדים even by משא, by simply moving, (even without direct contact. I.L.), it would be superfluous to repeat this again for אכילת נבלה were it not that we are taught two things thereby. Firstly that טומאה בלועה is not מטמא, that טומאה is only incurred, by external contact with, or by the moving of, the טמא object, but not by its being in contact with the inside of the body. For it says האוכל מנבלתה — and that could be סמוך לשקיעת החמה, late in the afternoon just before sunset — has only to go into a mikvah, wait till nightfall and attain טהרה, although the נבלה is still there in his inside. In any case, even in the morning, immediately after the טבילה, he becomes a טבול-יום, but if טומאה בלועה were still to be מטמא, he would again at once become ראשון — (Chulin 71a). And, secondly, we learn from this, והאוכל, that for מגע ומשא the minimum size is the שיעור אכילת, viz. ליתן שיעור לנוגע ולנושא כאוכל, מה אוכל כזית ;כזית אף נוגע ונושא כזית, (Nidda 42b).

V. 41. וכל השרץ וגו׳. This verse is the continuation of v. 21, as already remarked there, and goes on with the laws concerning prohibited animals (see note on v. 22). By שרץ השורץ על הארץ is understood all insects without wings, and worms which are generated on land, or if generated in water as soon as they leave that element (see above v. 11). This includes all worms generated in fruit or vegetable while the tree or stalk is still attached to the ground — במחובר. Worms which are generated in things, which are not attached to the ground, בתלוש, (e.g. mites in cheese. I.L.), only come under the heading when they have moved away from the substance in which they were produced, פירשו (Chulin 67b). Although, as a rule, כל היוצא מן הטמא טמא, and hence, ביצי עופות טמאים אסורים (see note above on v. 4), nevertheless, the איסור of שרץ only begins with the actual formation of the שרץ-form (ריקום); if התליע בתלוש, when it crawls away, and ביצי שרץ are not included at all in the איסור (see תוספות 64a, ד״ה שאם רקמה ואכלה).

V. 42. לא תאכלום. In this repeated prohibition, the Gemora Yebamoth 114a finds the warning given at the same time, להזהיר גדולים על הקטנים, not to give forbidden food to children. ת״כ learns this prohibition from the expression לא יֵאָכל in v. 41 and לא יֵאָכלו in v. 13, where the מאכיל is made responsible for forbidden food which he has caused to be eaten. לחייב המאכיל כאוכל (see ק״א thereon).

V. 43. אל תשקצו את נפשתיכם וגו׳, just as here this warning concludes the teaching of forbidden שרצים, so do we find a similar warning sentence concluding the teaching of forbidden mammals and birds in Ch. 20,25: ולא תשקצו את נפשתיכם בבהמה ובעוף וגו׳. Already above on v. 10, we have worked out how the term שקץ expresses the idea of complete moral opposition. That which is שקץ must be opposed in the highest degree to the moral nature of a being. If then it is said, do not make your person to שקץ, it must take it for granted that our persons, our souls, should be homogeneous, that is to say, should have the ability to be in agreement with, to assimilate with, and be in intimate conjunction with, a higher moral being, so that we are warned not to change the nature of our person or soul into such a contrast to this higher being, that instead of finding in us something that is adapted to being related to and in intimate connection with itself, it repulses us in disgust. This Being, to whom we should keep ourselves homogeneous so that It should find us worthy of Its “choice”, Its “love”, Its “longing”, Its “satisfaction”, to Whom we are not to make ourselves שקץ, so that It will “decide to dwell amongst us, and that Its Being does not repulse us in disgust”, (Ch. 26,11), this Being is none other than God Himself, Who also immediately in verses 44 & 45 refers repeatedly and quite definitely to the — so as to speak — similar nature of our being, to His Own as the reason for our moral calling and as the cause for our ability to attain it.

We are warned in our verse against two effects of eating prohibited animal food: שקץ in אל תשקצו את נפשתיכם, and טומאה in ולא תטמאו בהם. But the objects affected by them are not quite identical. Mentioned next to ולא תטמאו, which refers to the whole personality in general, נפשתיכם would stress specially that side of our being which is quite specially designated by נפש. This is our will which in aspiring and rejecting accomplishes the most important effects of our lives. (See Gen. 1,20). שקוץ נפש would be a passionate direction of our will towards anything that is directly opposed to God’s Will, (which for us is expressed in the Laws of Morality in the Torah), and which would, accordingly, be towards purposes which are abominated by Him. The eating of מאכלות אסורות, accordingly, increases the desire for satisfaction which is prohibited by the Will of God. But at the same time it brings טומאה to the whole of the rest of the person. We have already repeatedly explained the idea of טומאה as being the lack of moral freedom (see notes on Ch. 5,12). It is the death of that certainty of being master of oneseslf, of that free moral energy which is meant to control the power of desire, and keep it within the limits of God’s Laws of Morals; that sure freedom of will which is the fundamental condition for קדושה, the joyful readiness for the prompt acceptance of the whole of God’s Will which forms the height of moral perfection. The free moral energy which should oppose the immoral paths into which the demands of our desires have been driven, is weakened by eating מאכלות אסורות. And so such eating has a baneful influence on both phases of our spiritual lives, and the combination of the two threatens to effect the final grave of our morality. It effects שקוץ נפש, it arouses and increases immoral desires, and it effects טומאה, a laming of that sense of God-like mastery of ourselves and certainty of being free of will and not bound slaves to our passions. It does not even seem far-fetched to think that this טומאה comes afterwards as a result of such שקוץ. But where two influences, positive and negative, work in one corrupting direction, the danger threatens that finally: —

ונטמתם בם. Above (ibid) we have already referred to the phonetic relationship of the root טמא to דמע and טמע, which in Rabbinic Hebrew have the meaning of mixture and the final indistinguishable absorption of a different substance into the mass. We have also there already referred to the root טמה, which with a similar meaning appears in the word טמיון, in Rabbinic Hebrew meaning complete ruin, — going under. The form of our word here ונטמתם refers back primarily to this root טמה and not to טמא, and we believe that we may see in טמא the beginning, and in טמה the completion, of the death of moral freedom of will; it designates that stage when the idea of our complete freedom of will in moral matters, has become entirely submerged in the idea of physical compulsion. (“We must sin, it is part of our physical nature, like measles, to which we must yield, a young man must sow his wild oats”. I.L.). The first stage of טומאה catches a man while still in possession of his faculties of exercising his own free will, hence תטמאו in reflexive form. The last stages come by themselves as the result of the first without any decisive effort on his part, hence ונטמתם, in the passive form.
בכל שרץ השורץ, without the addition על הארץ includes שרצים of every element: שרץ המים ,שרץ העוף and שרץ הארץ.

V. 44. כי אני ה׳ אלקיכם, is the motive for the preceding warning: אל תשקצו and ולא תטמאו, I, ה׳, am your אלקים, that is to say: I, Who am ה׳, Who educates and leads Mankind to its ultimate moral destination of future completion, and Who has approached you now already in the present for his future goal of the whole of Mankind; I am to Whom your whole being belongs with its existence; its doings and its refraining from doing, and to Whom you are therefore responsible for keeping yourselves in a fit condition for this mission which has been entrusted to you. והקדשתם, “work at making yourselves holy”, exert all your energy on yourself, fighting down everything which stands in the way of your being receptive and readily responsive to the demands of My Laws of Morality, והייתם קדושים, “thus you will become holy”, thus the fight will become less and less, the opposition within you will diminish more and more, so that finally, without any fight, with all keen energy, you stand happily ready for all the goodness and purity which My Laws of Morality have traced out for you; and all that is low and common, ignoble and impure will have lost all attraction for you. כי קדוש אני: for this holiness in its absolute ideal state, completely free, deciding for itself everything solely for good, is the most striking character of My Being, and is both the reason for your mission to be holy and the cause of your ability to achieve it. Because קדוש אני, therefore והתקדשתם, and therefore והייתם קדושים. It is the reason for והתקדשתם; because I am קדוש, therefore those that would be near to Me, and those to whom I am to be near, must strive, in harmory with My Nature, to become קדושים likewise; And that, too, is the cause and reason of והייתם קדושים; because I am קדוש, you can be קדושים, can become so. With the breath of Me which lives in you, I have raised you above all physical compulsion, i.e. I have made you participate in My Nature, have given you the power of moral free self-determination, so that you reign in the little world of forces which I have made part of your material sensuous nature for you to master, as a small god, accomplishing My Will of your own free will and determination, even as I, as the absolute Free-willed God, reign over all the great forces in the great cosmos. The completely free personal God, is the warranty of free personal Man. “Because I am holy, you are to be holy, and can become holy!”

ולא תטמאו את נפשתיכם וגו׳. For the first stage, the והתקדשתם where the clash between the powers of sensuous desires and the consciousness of moral duty is still extant, we had the warning אל תשקצו for the former, and ולא תטמאו for the latter. By avoiding the forbidden foods the powers of sensuous desires are to be protected from being aroused, and one’s free-willed moral energy from being weakened-and blunted. For the stage of והייתם קדושים, the warning is significantly repeated. Let no man imagine that the prohibition of מאכלות אסורות is only given for the lower stages of the struggle towards moral perfection, where the internal fight between the two halves of one’s self is still going on, but at the height of moral nobility where the split no longer exists, and even one’s sensuous nature, the powers of sensuous nature, the powers of sensuous desires, the נפש only desires that which is holy, there, the warning of מאכלות אסורות has lost its importance. That is why, after והייתם קדושים, when the נפש itself has already become קדוש, the warning is repeated and now runs ולא תטמאו את נפשתיכם וגו׳. Beware lest, when you become קדושים that you allow your נפש to become טמא again through מאכלות אסורות, to become blunt and irresponsive for holiness; that it does not lose its joy in holiness. It is only the same regime by which holiness was achieved in our earthly material existence, that can keep and hold such holiness.

בכל השרץ הרמש על הארץ. Der Wechsel des Ausdrucks שורץ in רומש soll nach ת׳׳כ z. St. nach der Auffassung des רמב׳׳ם auch die in generatio aegulvoea שאין פרה ורבה, entstehenden Würmer etc. mit einschließen. Dem Ausdruck שורץ wohnt nämlich in Hinblick auf Stellen wie ושרצו בארץ ופרו ורבו על הארץ. (Bereschit 8, 17, ebenso Bereschit 9, 7; Schmot 1, 7) der Nebenbegriff der Vermehrung durch geschlechtliche Fortpflanzung inne, während רמש den weiten Begriff des Fortschreitens durch Bewegungsglieder ausdrückt und שרץ gegenüber von der Art der Entstehung abstrahieren läßt.

V. 45. המעלה אתכם וגו׳. The redemption from Egypt is to be an “elevation”, a leading you upwards out of the moral depths into which Egypt had sunk, to which reference is also made at the beginning of Ch. XVIII, in the introduction to the פרשת עדיות. The goal of this upward path which began with the Exodus from Egypt is: להיות לכם לאלקים, and the demands which the attainment of this object make are summarised in the mission: והייתם קדושים כי קדוש אני, (see v. 44). So that moral free-will is the object of being given national freedom and this latter stands or falls with it.

Vv. 46 & 47. זאת תורת וגו׳. The laws which are here retrospectively summarised were given in a different order viz. mammals, aquatic animals and birds, whereas here עוף follows בהמה. Above, where it was a matter of the formal teaching of the laws, those animals were listed together where סימנים were given, rules by which they could be recognised as permitted or otherwise, hence mammals and fish, and then birds, the individual names of which were enumerated. — But here, they are placed in the natural order — from higher to lower class of animal, mammals, birds, fish, in the same order as they diversify by graduation in the intensity of life. This greater or lesser degree of intensity of life is, according to Chulin 27b, also expressed by the greater and lesser degree of the requirements of שחיטה for each of them. The שחיטה of a mammal requires the cutting through both סימנים, the oesophagus and the trachea, for the שחיטה of an עוף, one suffices, and דגים require no שחיטה at all.
By the collective expression זאת תורת וגו׳, (היקש), the preceding warning, (in v. 44), which was given primarily for אכילת שרצים, applies to all the forbidden animals.

בין הטמא ובין הטהור: between בהמה and the שמנה שרצים where the נבלה is מטמא and דגים ,עופות and שאר שרצים where נבלה is not מטמא and also between טרפה שנשחטה and נבלה (v. 39). And also, as the ת״כ says on this verse, keeping the border line — which is often very fine, which divides טמא from טהור and כשר, as בין שנשחט רובו של קנה לנשחט חציו וכמה הוא בין רובו לחציו מלא שערה (the difference between having cut through the greater part of the tube or only exactly half, is but a hairbreadth. I.L.).

After all that the Torah itself says in this chapter about forbidden food, the expression שקץ ,טמא by which it teaches us to regard them, the results, שקוץ נפש ,טומאה ,טמיון, which it gives as the result of disregarding them, the idea התקדש with which it wants us to look on our conscientiously keeping them, and finally the point of view: והייתם קדושים כי קדוש אני אני ד׳ אלקיכם, that takes it as being nothing less than the whole purpose of the redemption from Egypt; המעלה אתכם וגו׳: after all this it is absolutely undoubtably clear that it is solely the moral integrity of our being, and in no wise our bodily health which is the motive of these laws. All that people like to talk about the “dietetic” prescriptions of the Law of Moses, so as to be able to give a greater semblance of truth to their assertion that these laws had only importance at a certain time and in certain climates, is swept away by the clear Word of the Torah itself. Not our bodily health, but the spiritual and moral health of our souls is to be ensured by the observation of these laws which protect our sensuousness from animal-like unrestrained passion, and our spiritual and moral powers of Will from becoming dull and irresponsive to higher and nobler conceptions. These laws want to impress on us that a fundamental condition for our becoming what we are meant to be is the necessity for keeping our material body in that state of receptive purity which makes it the ready instrument by which we can carry out the dictates of the higher and nobler part of our being. Already in the חורב, (Chapt. 68), we have referred to this meaning of the dietary laws, and at the same time too, to the fact that practical experience also speaks for the principle of this choosing our food and the influence it has on our general feelings of self-control and morality. All the true facts out of which modern materialism draws its false conclusions, would — if God’s Torah required it — show the truth of this principle in the clearest light. If the material part of our bodies (and remember that we can only feel and think by means of nerves and brain-matter which are absolutely concrete material substances. I.L.), is able to exercise so great an influence on our minds and will that the modern lies of materialism can have the narrow-minded presumption to relegate even spirit and will to mere attributes of the material, and to make all their activities purely the product of material forces, how understandable then does the care which God’s Truth — which does not attribute this force to the material at all, but does recognize the material as the “instrument” as being essential for every manifestation here on earth of the Spirit and Will — how understandable does the care become which only allows this “instrument” of the Spirit, which is constantly being renewed, to be rebuilt each time only with such materials which will keep it in a condition of readiness and responsiveness for the service of the Spirit, and which make it easier for the spirit to master and use the instrument for the higher purposes of its mission (cf. our remarks on Gen. 27,29 et seq.; Ch. 9,3 & 4 and Ch. XVII, on the dignity of the human body, and on the prominence which is given in the whole institution of Judaism to the sanctification of the body).

In a most significant manner we see here in this Ch. 11,24—40, as well as in the concluding sentence v. 47, the teaching of טומאת מגע interwoven with the teaching of טומאת מאכלות אסורות (or to use the terms we took from ת״כ, the teaching of טומאת קדושות with that of טהמאת גויות). Both serve the one purpose. That which the טומאת מגע-Law teaches symbolically is to be helped concretely to be realised by טומאת מאכלות אסורות-Law: and that for which the concrete ability is to be preserved and guaranteed by the טומאת מאכלות אסורות-Law is to be brought to one’s mind as the constant task of life by the טומאת מגע-Law. For, in any case, one has not achieved holiness simply by observing the dietary laws, but one can then achieve it more easily, and he commits an offence against his own God-owned body and denies the whole moral purpose of the Redemption from Egypt, who treats the dietary laws with carelessness. המורים שרצים, שכל המודה במצות ,שרצים מודה ביציאת מצרים, וכל הכופר במצות שרצים כופר ביציאת מצרים (ת״כ according to the ילקוט cf. ואנשי קדש וגו׳, Ex. 22,30). To achieve holiness, for which the keeping of the dietary laws merely prepares the ability, the consciousness of such ability and the nature of the task to be accomplished must be kept ever present. The nature of the task is laid down in the Torah and its ideal accomplishment is symbolically shown in the whole group of מקדש וקדשיו. The laws of טומאת מגע are an incessant warning of the ability to accomplish the task and we shall now attempt to give a general comprehensive survey of them, as far as they are contained in this chapter, and to show their understandable meaning.

That in the objects and conditions which are affected by the Law of טומאת מגע, we have not to deal with some mystic miasma which although invisible, is real and material, and by proximity or contact with a corpse or carcase or bodily ailment some noxious effuvia passes over and takes hold of persons and things; but that in all cases we are dealing with ideas, notions and impressions which are brought about by the object concerned and its connections and which are to be corrected by the methods prescribed, all seems to be clear in, we might say, every single detail of these laws. When we consider, for instance, that not every כלי made out of every material, and that not every material in every shape or form, is מקבל טומאה, that כלי ארמה ,כלי אבנים etc., are טהורים; that פשוטי כלי מתכות are טמאים while פשוטי כלי עץ are טהורים, that a כלי is only מקבל טומאה when it is completely finished for the purpose it is designed to serve, but that this purpose depends entirely on the מחשבה, the intention of its owner; that every כלי becomes טהור by the slightest crack or damage that renders it unusable for the purposes it has served hitherto etc., etc.; that מגע, direct contact causes less טומאה than — where it applies — משא, moving the טומאה-bringing object even when distant from it, etc., etc., from all these considerations, it seems to us, it must be very definitely apparent that טומאה is nothing concrete which infects or clings to things, but must be a thought, an idea, an impression in connection with the condition of men and things, and so can not occur as long as this condition is not yet there, or can disappear when this condition no longer exists.

Let us try then to identify the thoughts which could be expressed by the laws of טומאה as far as they are contained in this chapter. These are the various categories of טומאת מגע excluding those of טומאה היוצאה מגופו, the states of טומאה brought about by bodily conditions of living people, these being the contents of the next chapter.

Here, in our chapter, we have טומאת נבלה and שרץ, the טומאה arising from the dead bodies of all the large mammals and of eight small ones. The fundamental type of all טומאה and especially of טומאת נבלה ושרץ is clearly טומאת מת, the corpse of a human being. All the laws given here regarding טומאת נבלה ושרץ are also applicable to טומאת מת, only in the latter case they exceed by הזית שלישי ושביעי ,טומאת שבעה, by טומאת אהל and by the principle that חרב הרי הוא כחלל, as is explained in Numb. Ch. XIX.

We have repeatedly had occasion to remark how a dead human body tends to bring home to one’s mind a fact which is able to give support to that pernicious misconception which is called טומאה. For, in fact, there lies before us actual evidence that Man must — willy-nilly — submit to the power of physical forces. That in this corpse that lies before us, it is not the real human being, that the real human being, the actual Man, which the powers of physical force can not touch, had departed from here before the body — merely its earthly envelope — could fall under the withering law of earthly Nature; more, that as long as the real Man, with his free-willed, self-determining Godly nature was present in this body, the body itself was freed from forced obedience to the purely physical demands, and was elevated into the sphere of moral freedom in all its powers of action and also of enjoyment, when the free-willed ruling of the higher part of Man decided to achieve the moral mission of his life; in short, that death only begins with death, but that in life, thinking striving and accomplishing Man can master, rule, and use even his sensuous body with all its innate forces, urges and powers, with God-like free self-decision, within the limits of, and for the accomplishment of, the duties set by the laws of morality; all these are Truths which, in face of human frailty and the powers of the forces of Nature which the appearance of Death preaches, are to be brought again and again to the minds of living people, so that they remain conscious of their unique position of freedom in the midst of the physical world, and remain for ever armed in proud consciousness of their freedom, armed against the doctrine of materialism.

But in the same way as מת, a human corpse, brings about the idea of subjection, the lack of freedom, the purely physical nature of human beings, so is this idea awakened by contact with any body which resembles the human form when it is lying under the power of Death. Hence it is only animals whose body-formation is similar to that of Man, primarily the larger mammals, whose dead bodies, as נבלה, are טמאים, Amongst the smaller animals there are only eight שמנה שרצים, of which those whose , names we know, viz. weasel, mouse, mole, also belong to the class of mammals, and — as we have already remarked on the text, — all the eight seem to be vertebrates, so that the formation of their bodies is not too dissimilar to that of the human body. We imagine that the שמנה שרצים are those of the smaller animals that live in the vicinity of human beings so that we are used to seeing them running about full of life, so that their dead bodies do depress us to a certain extent with the feeling of the “death of living activity”. But the טומאה of שדצים is less than that of נבלה, they are only מטמא במגע and not במשא. Animals that do not live in the same element as man, the land, and hence both in the formation of their bodies and in the manner of their living are quite different to Man, do not remind us when dead, of a dead human body. Hence fish and all aquatic animals are excluded from טומאת נבלה, and the dead bodies of birds, the inhabitants of the air, are also not מטמא — with the single exception of נבלת עוף טהור בבית הבליעה, (see Ch. 17,15).

Moreover, whereas, of a human dead body, the passive part, the bones, are also מטמא, in the case of animals, the טומאה is restricted to those parts, the muscles and nerves, in which the present dead state of what was full of life and activity is essentially presented. We have already remarked (on verses 39 & 40), how this idea is already conveyed by the term “נבלה״. We have also drawn attention to the characteristic fact that דם and חלב are excluded from טומאת נבלה, and have shown the deep connection just these exclusion have with the whole meaning and teaching of טהרה & טומאה, (see notes on Ch. 7,26). In lower animals, שרצים, included amongst which are also cold-blooded amphibians as the צב and לטאה, the blood is only reckoned as being of the same degree as the flesh, אין דמם חלוק מבשרם.

The objects to which the laws of טומאה apply, if they touch a נבלה, are:— אוכלין ומשקין ,כלים ,אדם, Man and those things which characterise his personality in appearance, in his endeavours and achievements. The law which excludes him, his clothes and his appurtenances as well as his food and drink, as soon as he or they have become טמא by an object which demonstrates the body succumbing under the physical power of death, while under this impression, from the מקדש and its קדשים which represent the moral mission of his life, this law holds up to his eyes with each such exclusion the Teaching that the mission of his life demands that he remains above, and free from, all the physical “musts” of nature. He, himself, and all that is related to his personality, he with his כלים and אוכלין ומשקין must be elevated to the height of free moral self-decision. מקדש וקדשיו take it for granted that in what he is, what he does or makes, and in what he eats Man is a morally free agent.

טומאה :מגע is incurred by direct contact, and in Man only by external contact with his body, but מגע בית הסתרים is not מטמא. The whole parallelism which is drawn here between Man and the body of an animal — and also between the living Man and the dead one — is only an external one. It is only an apparent similarity, gaining semblance of reality by the fact of their common external existence on the common earthly ground of earthly life. This idea of belonging to the earth, to which man and animal alike are directed for the conditions of their existence is indeed so essential for the idea of טומאה, that the full effect of טומאה really only begins if it is actually on the earth itself, and ספק טומאה צפה טהור, (see note on v. 29).

משא. If the contact had not been made by touching, or not only by touching, but by direct or indirect moving of the נבלה, so that the person has come into contact with the נבלה not merely passively but by exercising his active powers on it, then not only his person but at the same time every כלי, clothes or object with which he is in contact at the time he is moving the נבלה becomes טמא. For here it is the “active” man who has come into relationship with the נבלה. It is, accordingly, Man in the use of his powers, Man with his full personality in clothes which show him to be a human being and with instruments of his powers of accomplishment, who here is affected by the טומאה idea which נבלה awakens. The clothes which he is wearing as well as any clothes or things which are in contact with him whilst he is moving the נבלה, become immediately טמא, and like himself ראשון לטומאה. Only אדם, another man, and כלי הרס are exempt from this טומאה בחיבורין and also, as we mentioned above on v. 25, most probably מדאורייתא also אוכלין ומשקין. A man naturally does not form part of the personality of another man so that he could be considered as belonging to בגדיו. And כלי חרס, as we shall have to go into more fully below, we take to form, together with אוכלין ומשקין, the sphere of Man’s food where the active work of the human being which is brought to the fore by משא remains in the background.

כלים. To understand the thoughts which are expressed by the susceptibility or non-susceptibility to טומאה of different objects and materials it is not unessential to bear in mind a fact which is just the contrary of what a superficial thought would imagine. טומאה is such depressing conception, טהרה is such a refreshing elevating thought that one would easily be inclined to look for objects which have the property of being liable to become טמא in the sphere of lower things, and דברים טהורים, things which are protected against טומאה in the sphere of higher objects. And the very opposite is the case. For the liability to טומאה only begins when an object belongs to the realm of morally free human development. It must be something which represents the sphere, or some phase of the sphere which just by the morally free self-determination of Man should be raised above the unfree world of mere physical existence. This is the sphere which has to receive the Law for its morally free development for the מקדש and its קדשים, and to which, accordingly, טומאה, the type of unfreedom, is in opposition, an opposition which withholds any object touched by it from the realm of מקדש וקדשיו. But that which still belongs to the world of purely physical existence, or which has not yet been brought into the sphere of human activity, or not sufficiently so, to be regarded as representative of human morally free existence efforts and accomplishments, or if it is not suitable to be representative of that sphere, that remains belonging to the world of physical things which by their nature and purpose are subject to the laws of unfree physical necessity. Accordingly, everything that is rooted to the earth, everything that has not yet been taken away from the earth, even everything that is artificially joined to the earth so that it can be considered as part of it, e.g. plants rooted in the soil, water gathered in wells or cisterns, walls, houses and all similar things understood as coming under the idea of מחובר, are free from טומאה. Equally so living animals, the ornaments of animals and the food of animals. So also, everything that is not considered as finished for human use, שלא נגמרה מלאכתו, is not yet susceptible to טומאה. All these objects can not be considered as representing the sphere of the morally free activity of human life.

The reason why, amongst the articles which are actually used by Man, the susceptibility to טומאה is limited to certain kinds of such objects, seems to lie in the same trend of thought. For טומאה is no concrete condition which attaches itself to the concrete qualities of material and things, but is an idea, a thought, which should be kept absent in all phases of human life; and objects do refer to such phases, a box refers to the sphere of one’s possessions, a tool to one’s work, a pot to one’s preparation of food etc., etc. Because כלים are, accordingly, symbols of certain human relationships, therefore the idea of טומאה does not apply to כלים in general, but just to such as are picked out as representing most poignantly the human relationship which the laws of טומאה have in view. Just this choice, this sharp limitation ensures to the whole, the idea of a clearly defined symbolic meaning; for if something is limited to specially selected examples, and does not apply to the whole class of anything, that thing can not be real, but must be symbolic. Thus, when we are to be reminded by ציצית, of the moral sanctifying meaning of man’s clothing, garments of wool or linen are chosen for preference, because these are the materials preferably used for clothing (see Numb. 15,37 et seq.). Thus, when a house is to be consecrated by a מזוזה as being the real place where the Word of God is to find its truest realisation, the מזוזה is not to be placed on any and every room, but only on such rooms whose size and extent do precisely represent the conception of a “home”, (see Deut. 6,9). Thus, to represent the Truths which are to be expressed by איסור מלאכה on שבת, only such human activities are chosen which show in the most decisive manner Man’s constructive power over matter, but כלאחר יד ,שאין מתכוין ,מקלקלין etc., are פטורין. Thus, to express the Truth which the איסור בשר בחלב is meant to represent, only בשר וחלב of בהמה טהורה is chosen out of the whole animal world, as forming the principal food of Man, and חיה ועוף are not included, etc., etc. It is just such choice, such picking ut of special examples, and making the law apply to them only, which ensures these and similar laws a symbolic character expressing thoughts and ideas rather than actual concrete facts. So, here, too, in the laws of טומאה, we find a choice out of the articles of human use; and susceptibility to טומאה restricted to such articles which are most precisely fit to represent the idea of the various accomplished activities of human persons. Moreover, in each category of such activities, the טומאה is attached only to the characteristic traits of the activity represented.

First, regarding materials. Not all כלים, but only כלי עץ, בגד, עור, מתכות ,(שק) ,מעשה עזים and חרש, vessels made from wood, from threads of animal or vegetable origin, from the hair, skins, bones, horns, etc., of animals, metals and baked clay, are selected as being principal materials which men use in manufacture. Materials derived from fish or from any aquatic origin, as well as from birds, also vessels made from unbaked clay or stone are exempt from טומאה.

But the כלים, which are susceptible to טומאה, are only so, when they are fashioned in the way that is most characteristic of their kind and of their purpose. כלי עץ, עור, עזים, בגד, only as בני קבול when they are able to contain something, or made into garments, but פשוטיהם, just flat pieces of these materials are טהורים unless they are ראויים למדרס, meant for sitting on, lying on, standing on, or supports for the body. But כלי מתכות, metal vessels, are able to become טמא even as פשוטים, quite flat. Finally, כלי חרש, earthenware vessels, are only מקבל טומאה מאוירן, do not become טמא by external contact, but only by the טומאה-bringing object coming inside them.

We have, accordingly, three categories: (a) כלי עץ וכו׳. Vessels made from wood, etc., from materials derived from animal or vegetable sources. Their characteristic use is for clothing and as portable containers. They must accordingly be such, that things can be put into them, have בית קבול and with their contents must be portable, מיטלטל מלא וריקן. This last condition expresses the idea, than Man’s possessions do not belong to the moral sphere of humanity by being just stored-up treasures. As dead-weight possessions they are dead, and do not rise above the sphere of things bound by physical laws. It is only when it is decided to use them, to make them “portable”, that they come to life and become part and parcel of morally free human personalities, to which the physical lack of freedom which is represented by טומאה is in opposition. Hence ידות הכלים, the handles of a vessel, are considered an integral part of them. Further, each כלי must be a כלי אשר יעשה מלאכה בהם, must have an independent use of its own, must represent some work being done with it. Parts of vessels, such as covers, by themsvlees are not מקבל טומאה. This category represents Man in his social life and his activities, in handling and using his possessions (those that are ראויים למדרס, which are able to become טמא also as פשוטים, will be discussed in Ch. XV).

(b) כלי מתכות, metal vessels. Their main character is that of tools, hence flat slabs, rods etc., of metal, פשוטיהם, (non-receptacles. I.L.), are susceptible to טומאה. Their most important purpose is not to be containers, hence the condition of mobile portability, ליטלטל מלא וריקן, does not apply to them. They represent Man in his manufacturing or creative activities.

(c) כלי חרש, earthenware vessels. The peculiarity that they are only מקבל טומאה מאוירן, indicates that their meaning is applied solely to the importance of the space they enclose. Their purpose must be accomplished by the presence in such space of whatever is to be put into them. For they impart their טומאה to any object which is, or comes, into such space without it having to actually touch the כלי. They have the further peculiarity that אין להם טהרה במקוה, ואינן נעשין אב הטומאה, that their טהרה can not be restored by immersion in a מקוה, and that they can never become אב הטומאה (see below). In both these things they differ sharply from all other כלים, which do regain their טהרה in a מקוה, and by touching a dead body, or by serving as משכב ומושב של זב receive the character of אב הטומאה. In this respect, כלי חרש are quite similar to אוכלין ומשקין, which also just in these two ways differ, characteristically, from כלים (see below). Hence, we think we are not wrong if we see in כלי חרש, vessels meant for the preparation of, and the storing of food. They represent Man in his activities for purposes of food and nourishment and enjoyment.

To sum up the ideas expressed by טומאת כלים:— they warn us to tear the social phases of our life, our dealing with possessions, our activities in work and manufacture and in the preparation of food and enjoyment, away from the sphere of purely physical material accomplishments, and use our energy to keep them in the morally free, self-determining purposes of life which מקדש וקדשיו hold out before us.

אוכלין ומשקין are self-explanatory. They are the means of nourishment and enjoyment of Man. Here, again, we find the conception אוכלין also restricted to such materials which represent the idea “food” in the most suggestive manner. Things like pepper, vanilla, saffron etc., which are only לטעמא עבידא, only added to food to give it taste or appearance, are excluded, (Nidda 51b). And amongst משקין, liquids, only seven are selected: water, milk, wine ,etc., which are considered to represent this idea, and only these are מקבל טומאה. There is even an opinion expressed in the Gemora, according to which the conception of food for הלכות טומאה is only represented by אוכלין, as being the real means of nourishment, and משקין, liquids, are מדאורייתא not מקבל טומאה at all. Further, just as כלים are only brought out of the condition of belonging to the physical sphere of matter, into that of human moral purposes by מחשבה, by human thought, and must have reached a finished condition commensurate with that condition, in a similar manner edible material does not become מקבל טומאה automatically just by itself, but its ability to become טמא is dependent on a certain act having taken place, by which it is considered to have entered the sphere of food destined for human consumption. This act is הכשר, with the co-operation of human intelligence, it must have become wet by one of the seven liquids referred to just above. The idea of this הכשר-act is not easy to explain. It is understandable that edible material only achieves its purpose as food through being moistened. The presence of dissolving liquids forms the fundamental condition for the material to be absorbed as nourishment. Every solid must be reduced to liquid form before it can be carried by the blood stream to nourish and replace the tissues which become worn out in the constant cycle of change in the human body. This would make the meaning of הכשר not difficult to understand provided the wetting of the אוכלין had to be done intentionally or at least with agreement. And, actually, the רמב״ם (Ch. XII, הל׳ טומאת אוכלין), takes this to be the case. He declares there in all cases, 1—3, הניח בהן פירות ,נגיעת אוכלין ברצון etc., and the remark which the כ״מ makes on 2 anent the ראב״ד seems, as far as our text of the רמב״ם goes, competely unjustified. But, without exception, all the ראשונים declare that תחלתו ברצון אעפ״י שאין סופו ברצון, means that, סופו, the actual wetting of the אוכלין, need not be ברצון as long as תחלתו, the water becoming תלוש, had been intentional, or at least, in accordance with desire. Nevertheless, perhaps the peculiarity of this law may be explained by taking it that, in itself any material can only already be considered as an אוכל — as far as susceptibility to טומאה is concerned — if מחשבה, designing it for human uses, has preceded the הכשר, or if, on account of the very definite nature of the material it can be taken for granted that this is so (עוקצין, 3). Once the purpose of the material for human food is established, perhaps a moment of even unintentional wetting may suffice to give it the complete character of food for human consumption. וצע״ע.

אוכלין ומשקין have no טהרה במקוה; if they have become טמא, they do not regain their טהרה by being immersed in a מקוה, and אינן נעשין אב הטומאה, and they can not, like אדם and כלים, by touching a טומאה, become אב הטומאה. If אדם וכלים touch a dead body, כלים also, if they serve as משכב ומושב של זב, they acquire the character of אב הטומאה. Both these traits are closely connected with each other, so that the canon runs:— וכל שאין לו טהרה במקוה אינו נעשה אב הטומאה, (see Chulin 121a, רש״י ד״ה זרעים). Both these peculiarities also characterise כלי חרש, as mentioned above.

The idea of an אב הטומאה is, that the object itself is one which brings טומאה thoughts to mind, e.g. שרץ ,נבלה etc., so that by touching it “Man and his appurtenances”, אדם וכלים, become טמא. By a ולד הטומאה, i.e. an object which does not awaken טומאה-thoughts by itself, but only by its being associated with טומאה-bringing objects, אוכלין ומשקין can well become טמא, but never אדם וכלים. Now, that which is to be considered as אב הטומאה, as “begetter”, “awakener”, of טומאה-thoughts, i.e. of morally free Man being under the compulsion of physical force, must be, either like מת or a dead שרץ or נבלה, something which does actually represent a dead human body, or else something which itself belonging to the sphere of morally free human beings, by having been in contact with a dead body of a human being, is apt to bring טומאה-thoughts to the mind. But as representatives of this sphere of morally free Man first of all comes Man himself and then those objects which being the product and means of his intellectually free existence and doing do represent him. These objects are clearly כלים, clothes, vessels and tools. Clothes, vessels and tools are so exclusively associated with human beings, that wherever we come across clothes, vessels or tools, they automatically proclaim the existence of a human being. By their contact with a dead human body, with the actual fact of death — a human being lying — apparently — completely under the power of physical forces — the idea of freedom in the sphere of Man’s activities is shattered to such a degree that they themselves reproduce the idea of death. Like נבלה and שרץ, which are not themselves dead human bodies, but by their similiarity to them to arouse thoughts of them and so are אב הטומאה, in the same way אדם וכלים שנגעו במת, are not themselves מת, but by having been in contact with a dead body, do awaken the idea of Man’s death and so become אבות הטומאה. More, כלים are so very intimately connected with the idea of human personality that, according to the principle חרב הרי הוא כחלל, as soon as they come into contact with a מת or a טמא מת, they identify themselves completely with its טומאה-character and take the אבי-אבות-character from a מת or the אב-character from the טמא מת. For more details see notes on Numb. 19,16 et seq. (Here we have adopted the view of הר׳ יצחק מסימפונט, which is also accepted by רמב״ם in טומאת מת, v. 3, according to which the principle חרב הרי הוא כחלל applies to all כלים. But, according to ר״ת and רש״י, it only applies to כלי מתכות. See אהלות רש״י I,2, רש״י Chulin 3a. If the way we have taken כלי מתכות as representing “tools” — working creative Man — is correct, the specializing חרב הרי הוא כחלל to כלי מתכות is quite understandable, for still more than clothes or vessels, tools represent Man as thinking, creating, i.e. raised above blind, physical instinctive force, as being spiritually free).

To all these, אוכלין ומשקין form the exact contrary. As “the means of nourishment and enjoyment” they represent much more that phase of human life which it shares in common with all other living organism. In requiring nourishment and ability to satisfy his senses, Man belongs to physical Nature אוכלין ומשקין, accordingly, in themselves, do not represent the morally and intellectually free side of the human being, but rather the physically unfree phase of his nature. They, accordingly, do not stand in such contrast to מת as the phase represented by כלים does, that by contact with a dead body a new אב הטומאה should be formed. On the other hand, the sensuality of Man represented by אוכלין ומשקין is just that phase of his life in which he most easily runs the risk of forfeiting his moral freedom. Hence, it is here, that in the very first instance that מקדש וקדשיו makes the demand that in giving it satisfaction it is to be raised out of the sphere of physical unfreedom into that of morally free self control and to change the satisfying of the demands of one’s senses into a morally free God-serving act. The gratification of the senses, as represented by אוכלין ומשקין, just because it lies farthest away from the morally free, specifically human traits, is the sphere which is most responsive to spiritual טומאה and is where spiritual טומאה is most rampant. Hence the same reason that makes אוכלין ומשקין not able to become אב הטומאה, as אדם and כלים can, makes them responsive to טומאה, to a much higher degree, and whereas אדם וכלים only become טמא through an אוכלין ,אב הטומאה and משקין become טמא even through ראשון ושני, but on the other hand their ability to transfer טומאה is limited. (See on v. 34).

Exactly the same difference, and arising from the same reason, arises between אדם וכלים and אוכלין ומשקין in the matter of טהרה במקוה. Only that has טהרה במקוה which in its basic essential nature, belongs to the sphere of spiritually free human beings, rising above טומאה-unfreedom. It steps out of the טבילה במקוה back into its primeval character of spiritual freedom. So, in the case of אדם and כלים. But that which like אוכלין ומשקין products in themselves of Nature, purely of physical origin, and in their purpose, representing the physical side of human being, and only by the spiritually free mastery of Man to be raised into the sphere of human freedom, if it has been reduced back to its original character by contact with טומאה, that, naturally, can not be affected by טבילה במקוה. Not by symbolic acts but only by זריעה, actual complete removal from the sphere of the human world, back to that of the terraqueous cosmos can מים and זרעים be brought back to a completely new existence, accessible to טהרה, (see on v. 37). If, now כלי חרש, as remarked above, represent the same phase of human life as אוכלין ומשקין, it is understandable why they, too, have the two characteristic peculiarities, that אין להם טהרה במקוה and אינן נעשין אב הטומאה. They only have the character of כלים, being, equally with other כלים the product of human intelligence, in that they only become טמא through an אב הטומאה and not by a ולד.

It is significant that even מאכלות אסורות, even materials which are there only for the nourishment and enjoyment of non-Jews, are susceptible to טומאה. According to this law the principle of the food and enjoyment of non-Jews must also come within the scope of the laws of self-control which the Jewish Sanctuary of the Torah, מקדש וקדשיו, teaches. This Torah and its Sanctuary must regard every human being in the loftiness of its morally free calling; and in טומאת מאכלין in the degrading of the life of its senses and enjoyments to purely physical necessity must see therein opposition to the conceptions of the Torah, whose final goal is the moral holiness of the lives of all men.

מפץ, a sleeping-mat is in a special class of its own. Provided it is ראוי and also מיוחד למשכב, fit and set aside specially for lying on, it is מקבל טומאת מדרס and consequently is susceptible to other טומאות, according to the canon: כל המיטמא מדרס מיטמא טמא מת, and so as משכב ומושב can become אב הטומאה, but nevertheless has no טהרה במקוה (Sabbath 84b; רמב״ם Hilchoth Mikvaoth 1, 4; see Ch. XV at the end).

טבילה. Above, on v. 32, we have already pointed out the significant placing together in ת״כ of the two factors which restore ביאה —:טהרה במים and ביאת שמש. The inner connection between these two factors may be the following:— By both of them טמא steps out of being connected with the realm of טומאה. By טבילה in place, as by הערב שמש in time. Water, with the modification mentioned on v. 36, (not in a כלי, without תפיסת ידי אדם, not שאובים, not על ידי דבר מקבל טומאה), in its elementary character, gathered in a hollow in the ground, is — as is evident from v. 32 — a realm which טומאה can not reach. So much so, indeed, that, as it says in Kelim 17, 13: כל שבים טהור, even vessels made from materials derived from aquatic sources can not become אדמה ;טמא as being the stage for Mankind is the real realm of טומאה (see on Vv. 29—31). When a man immerses the whole of himself in water of that nature, and completely, and in direct contact — בלי חציצה — enters this element, he completely steps out of all connection with the realm of טומאה. He leaves the stage of Mankind and for the moment returns to the sphere of the world of elements, to begin a new life of טהרה. It is symbolic of a new birth. If, then, in addition, the sun sets, and with it the day that saw him טמא passes, then — as the expression runs in Berachoth 2b, טהור יומא, the day, too, has become טהור for him, he passes into a fresh pure day, and in time, too, out of connection with the state of טמא into which he had fallen — his טהרה is completed.

If we understand the laws of טומאה and טהרה, as they actually affect our lives; if we consider that although they only concern מקדש וקדשיו, so that a non-Cohen in his ordinary life is in no wise forbidden to touch any טומאה, nor is it forbidden to him לגרום טומאה לחולין שבא״י, to make ordinary foodstaff טמא, nevertheless, as מעשר שני ,חלה ,תרומה ,ביכורים, have to come from the lay public, there are plenty of occasions constantly arising in everyday life which demand attention to these laws. And, above all, there are the pilgrim festivals, three times each year, when the necessity arises for each individual in the nation לטהר עצמו ברגל, to free himself, his family and all possessions from every טומאה and to keep them in that state, in accordance with the demands of “the Sanctuary and קדשים״ to which he is invited. So that even by the considerations of these national institutions, the טומאה and טהרה laws were spread throughout all classes of the Nation, and the necessity of keeping a watch on all things in case they came to be used in the great National Weeks in Jerusalem had to be ever in mind. If we picture to ourselves the whole daily working life of the people, both in public and home life, being under the rule of these טומאה and טהרה-laws, in all their doings and handlings, we can form some idea of the spiritual and ennobling influence they could wield on the Nation as a whole and on each individual member of it. The conception, and the consecration of the morally free nature of human beings was spread over everything which the hand touches or does. All work and craftmanship then stands in service of this calling of Man to be morally free and near to God. The chisel and the needle, the weaving-stool and the kitchen utensils all work with an eye to the laws of morality which from the Heights of Moriah send the spirit of holiness into the ordinary life of the people. The lowest workman or workwoman feel themselves spiritually elevated by the consciousness which is brought into their work, that, with their work, they are accomplishing a moral need for a moral purpose; and thereby are making their contribution to carry out the morally free mission of Man in service of the Torah of God, which is enthroned on Moriah. Under the rule of these טומאה and טהרה laws all commonness and brutality, self-depreciation and degeneration vanish, and everything stands erect to create a People of God of morally free people for the Torah of God.

So we find quite early in our history, the spiritual elite of the Nation submitting their whole lives under the regime of the טהרה & טומאה laws, which were given only in reference to the מקדש, and, as the expression is אוכלים חוליהן בטהרה, “ate their quite ordinary and daily food in the purity of טהרה״. They accordingly lived their whole life, even the life of their senses, as if in the environment of, and in the presence of the Sanctuary, and so appointed all their doings, the whole of their intercourse with men and things, to be a constant reminder of the moral sanctifying calling of Man. Already, in the time of Saul and David, (Sam. I. 20,26 & XXI,6), we see these טהרה prescriptions kept in quite ordinary daily life, even by the ordinary common soldiers (to use a modern description of them). More, the last quotation shows that they kept these prescriptions in their חולין-life in the very highest degree and not only ate their חולין at the degree of טהרת תרומה, but even על טהרת הקדש so that ויהיו כלי הנערים קדש, they kept all their accoutrements and kit etc., not only from the standpoint of תרומה, but from that of קדש, (for it speaks there of לחם קדש). Those who made the conscientious observation of the טהרה & טומאה laws the constant rule of their lives were called in later times by the name חברים. They formed a free open “society”, whose membership was open to anybody who, in the presence of three witnesses, undertook to keep the דברי חברות, the duties of a חבר, (Bechoroth 30b). To be a member of the society entailed also great conscientiousness regarding the מעשר-laws (see notes on Numb. 18,21 et seq.). But being conscientious with טהרה and מעשר are only the most characteristic signs of being a member of this society. From all that is recounted in the Mishna and Talmud it is quite evident that the most conscientious attention to all the laws of morality formed the character of a “Chaver”. They formed this free open-to-all society whose members took, as the mission of their lives, the keeping of the “Torah” with intelligence and knowledge. We have seen how this חברות life interwove itself amongst the people even in the earliest times of Jewish history. Unless we are very much mistaken it was just it which at all times formed the quiet deep moral core of the life of the Nation, of which, of course, the history of the dynasties is silent and only here and there allows something to show through. It is out of its bosom alone that appearance of people such as Elkana and Channa, Samuel and David and the brilliant host of prophets could have sprung from, and its existence alone can give an answer to the riddle of such appearances.

Because of their keeping away, (פרישות) from all טומאה, the חברים are also called פרושים (Chagiga 18b), “Pharisees”. But nobody was so full of contempt and scorn, and, with biting irony has so severely censored those who changed true Pharisaism into vain hypocrisy, and in place of being a Pharisee, aped the appearance of one, and instead of thinking and feeling like a Pharisee, had sham pious words ever on their lips, none were such sworn enemies of all hypocritical show of piety in general, as our פרושים, our “Pharisees” themselves, a name which, after all, comprises everything that, in Judaism, begets greatness in character and spirit. Our “Pharisees” have left us a whole “natural history” of false Pharisees, and in Sota 22b have drastically described seven species of these humbugs and their characteristics. They say that these, together with the חסיד שוטה, the Chasid without discernment, the בתולה ציילנית ואלמנה שובבית, the young lady always at her devotions, and the widow who makes a parade of her “frumish-keit”, and the קטן שלא כלו לו חדשיו, the self-appointed but immature exponent of the Torah, are all מבלי עולם, destroyers, corrupters of the world. They conclude this chapter with the great saying: דמטמרא מטמרא, “That which is hidden from human beings is hidden”; ודמגליא מגליא, and only that which is revealed to them is revealed”; בי דינא רבה ליתפרע מהני דחפו גונדי, “the great justice of God will visit those who put the Pharisaic-tallis over their heads for show”. אמר לה ינאי מלכא לדביתיה, King Alexander Janus said to his wife: אל תתיראי מן הפרושין ולא ממי שאינן פרושין, אלא מן הצבועין שדומין לפרושין, שמעשיהן כמעשי זמרי ומבקשין שכר כפנחס, “have no fear of the Pharisees, nor of the non-Pharisees, but you need only fear the ‘coloured’ ones, those who appear as Pharisees, they live like Zimrei and demand the reward of Phinehas”.

From these אכילת חולין בטהרה, these חברים who made it the rule of their lives to eat their ordinary meals in the state of טהרה, which is really only requisite for קדשים, the very first stage has remained as a regular habit of life for the whole of the Jewish People, and is still the mark of the observant Jew. This is נטילת ידים, the washing of the hands before ordinary meals. In Bechoroth 30b, the duty of נטילת ידים is designated as the necessary preliminary stage to all other טהרות-duties, and this first qualification for admittance into the טהרות-Society called קבלה לכנפים. That by this term the duty of נטילת ידים is understood, is agreed by Rashi (ibid), the Aruch under כנף and Rambam הל׳ מטמאי משכב ומושב 10, 1 & 2. It is obscure why this first preliminary stage of טהרות should be called כנפים, “Wings”. We think it not improbable that thereby נטילת ידים is meant to be designated as being the first custom of life which is to be the condition necessary for all further progress up to the heights of טהרות. By נטילת ידים the entrant to טהרות receives “wings” which are to raise him up to the whole height of the practice of טהרות. The very name נטילת ידים itself points to an “Elevation”, a “raising upwards”. For נטל is the Chaldean equivalent to נשא, and נטילת ידים is literally “a raising of the hands upwards”, just as the specific name of the vessel specially used for this washing is נטלא, “raising”. (The Targum on ותשאני רוח being ונטלתני רוחא. I.L.). The נטילת ידים לסעודה is to be a reminder to us, also to elevate our meal out of the realm of merely enjoying giving a satisfaction to our purely physical senses into the character of a moral spiritual act. For it is just this spiritual consecration of even all our sensual acts that forms the very first preliminary condition for the spiritual holiness of the whole Jewish life.

V. 1. Two kinds of טומאה formed the contents of the previous chapter:— טומאת גויות, the actual demoralising of the body by building up its tissues with food which has a bad effect on the tendencies of the person, and טומאת קדושות, the disturbing of that consciousness of being complete free master over oneself in all moral matters, as is demanded by and furthered by the Sanctuary-of-the-Torah, by coming into contact with dead bodies which awaken the idea of human lack of freedom — טומאת מאכלות אסורות and טומאת מגע נבלה ושרץ. This chapter and the following one continue the teaching of טומאת קדושות and treat of conditions which are capable of endangering the consciousness of moral freedom to an even higher degree, as they present living Man succumbing to physical necessity, טומאות היוצאות עליו מגופו. They present a death of self-determination by one’s own free will, reaching right into life itself, and consequently require a special demonstration of the Truth which contradicts this idea. They are:— ,נדה וזבה בעל קרי, זב, מצורע, יולדת, which accordingly, with the exception of בעל קרי, require a longer time for the טומאה-condition to pass, and demand not just יום אחד like טומאת נבלה ושרץ. They also, with the additional exception of נדה, require in addition, the teaching of the free moral self-determination to be positively expressed by an offering. Hence זב ,מצורע ,יולדת and זבה are called the ארבעה מחוסרי כפרה.
וידבר ה׳ אל משה לאמר. See on Ch. 13,1.

V. 2. דבר אל בני ישראל אשה וגו׳. By בני ישראל, the following טומאה laws apply only to Jewish people, but by the word אשה, they apply to every woman who belongs to the Jewish community and so include שפחה and גיורת (Yebamoth 74b & Kerithoth 7b).

זרע .כי תזריע, basically, the seed of plants עשב מזריע זרע, and hence הזריע, the seed-forming activity of plants for the continuation of their species, when applied to human beings is the usual term for the offspring by which Man continues his generation. By the use of the expression תזריע here, which only occurs elsewhere in Gen. 1,11 & 12, referring to the activity of plants for the continuation of their species, the mother’s role in producing progeny is looked at in the purely material physical character of its physiological process, and with that one word the whole idea of the טומאה spoken of here, is shown. The highest and noblest occupation, on which the whole future of the human race is built, in which the whole constitution of womanhood finds its purpose and goal, the whole process in the body of a Mother for the production of a new human being — is of purely physical nature. Man originates, grows and exists like a plant and the noblest and most glorious name that the human tongue can utter, the name “Mother”, reminds one at same time of the purely physical unfree process of human origin. [Mother from Lat. mater (from matrix) the womb. I.L.]. If anywhere, it is surely here, that the fact must be established, that, in spite of this, once he is born, Man is a morally free agent. Above all, the Mother herself, under the fresh impression of her physically completely passively and painfully having to submit to the forces of the physical laws of Nature at the most sublime procedure of her earthly calling, has to re-establish again the consciousness of her own spiritual height. And only after this impression of lack of freedom of will has completely passed away has she, by an offering, to undertake to allow herself of her own free will to give herself up to the whole spiritual height of her calling of Woman and Mother which is now restarting with all its momentous and often painful moments; and to allow herself to re-enter the Sanctuary of holy happy faithfulness to duty.

תזריע וילדה זכר. Inasmuch as the לידה, the birth, on the one hand by the word תזריע being placed before וילדה, is designated not only at the stage of its being accomplished, but is referred back to the stage of the beginning of the ovum being impregnated, and on the other hand, by the word זכר refers to the completed formation of the child; and further by ביום השמיני וגו׳, the ability of the new-born baby to live is assumed, the law which follows is taken to apply also in the case of a נפל, a miscarriage. The condition, however, is imposed that it only applies when a period of at least forty days has elapsed from the first formation of the foetus, and only if the foetus has מצורת אדם, already the most salient features of human beings (forehead, eyebrows, eyes, cheeks and chin: Nidda 23b), so that the possibility of its having had the ability to attain life is not excluded. (ת״כ and Nidda 30a & 21b et seq.).

כימי נדת דותה תטמא. Statements like this, may well be also an intimation to us showing that the whole Torah had already been given in detail to the people and committed to their memory before it was given to them in the written form; (actually, only after their having been taught it by Moses and the elders for 40 years. I.L.). Here, reference is made to the law of Nidda which is only given in Ch. 15,19. נדה from נדד .נדד always designates a withdrawing away from a place or a person to which, or to whom, one really belongs. נדה is the appropriate designation for the condition which causes a temporary unapproachableness in marriage life. דותה from דוה. Whereas חלה designate the condition of illness according to its actual physiological character, (see Gen. 48,1), דוה seems rather to express the personal feeling of being ill, hence also its frequent combination with על זה היה דוה לבנו :לב (Lamet 5,17), לבב דוי (Isaiah 1,5) etc. דוה designates the periodically recurring condition of depression of normal “well-feeling”, of which נדה designates the legal result. — כימי נדת דותה תטמא, all the laws given in Ch. 15,19—24 apply to her. Just as here, in the Torah, לידה is referred to נדה so do the most modern physiological views place both these occurrences in the closest similarity and relationship.

V. 3. וביום השמיני ימול בשר ערלתו. We have very fully worked out the meaning of מילה as being the free willed moral subordination of our physical bodily sensuality under the laws of God, in Jeshurun IV & V, (see Gesammelte Schriften where the article in question has been reproduced. I.L.). This mastery over, and moral consecration of, the sensual body had already been given, in Gen. XVII, as the fundamental institution of the Abrahamitic People. It is only mentioned again here, on the one hand, to teach its intimate connection with the preceding טומאת לידה, which had only been introduced at the Lawgiving, and, on the other hand, to give instructions for the procedure when it clashes with the laws of שבת and also with the laws of צרעת which immediately follow. For, in connection with the preceding Laws of טומאת לידה, we have the canon: כל שאמו טמאה לידה נימול לשמונה וכל שאין אמו טמאה לידה אין נימול לשמונה, (Sabbath 135a), a canon which we have also already discussed and explained in the above mentioned article. There we took the period of seven days at טומאה to be the completion required for the passing away of a condition of depression which has to be overcome; and, more in detail, as the passing out of the passively created unfree existence (the symbolism of the number six), into the human free-willed existence to be won in a bond with God, (the number seven).
