Then the eighth day after birth as being the godly free nature of all human beings at birth building itself up for the higher and fuller calling of the specifically Jewish mission, as being a repetition of the first day on a higher scale, and considered as the Jewish octave of the first day of physical birth. Hence it is the same reason that brings the Mother the seven days of טומאת לידה viz., the over-powering might of the forces of Nature which was revealed to the mother and child in the process of birth, that requires, in ordinary cases, the passing of a seven days’ cycle of time before the Mila is performed. But if the mother בשעת לידה had not yet become a Jewess, and so had not become טמאת לידה, and the child, accordingly, had not become at all connected with Judaism by birth, and it is only the act of Mila that brings him into connection with Jewry and Judaism, then this Mila, by itself, forms such a new existence for the child, having no connection at all with what went before, that by it, even the connection with the process of physical birth is already sufficiently retired into the background and there is no waiting for the passing of a seven days cycle of time required. Similarly the reason is quite clear why even if the dictum of ר׳ אסי were הלכה, a יוצא דופן would also not be נימול לשמנה. (See Jeshurun ibid, P. 28 & 29).

From this sentence, וביום השמיני וגו׳, is further taught, firstly the significant law ביום ולא בלילה, that (as we have explained at length in Jeshurun 6th year p. 621 et seq., in connection with all the other institutions of the Torah which may only be done in the day-time), this law stamps the act of Mila referring purely and definitely to the free-willed moral calling of Man, and excludes all erroneous lowering it to the sphere of medical prophylaxis, or even to that of the cult of heathen rites. (See same article).

And then: וביום השמיני ואפילו בשבת, i.e. מילה בזמנה דוחה שבת. Before a Mila on the eighth day even the sanctity of Sabbath retires. We have, elsewhere, (Jeshurun 5th year, p. 22 et seq.), pointed out the deeper connection between the eighth day and the Sabbath. We showed how “Israel” not only was added to the seven works of the world’s creation, as the eighth, but quite actually stands as the visible bearer of the reminder of the Creator of the World that the Sabbath of Creation was meant to be. Israel, accordingly, exists as the “eighth” for the “seventh”. Just as the meaning of Israel, the 8th, lies entirely in the keeping of the Sabbath, the 7th, so has Sabbath the 7th its sole bearer amongst humanity in Israel the 8th. Accordingly, by the performance of the Mila on the 8th day, the whole Abrahamitic bond with God is demonstrated in its mission for the “Sabbath”. For it is the “Sabbath” — the principle of God being Master of Man and the World which Sabbath teaches — which is demonstrated by such a Mila, as receiving a new recruit to the House of Abraham to be its bearer, keeper and fighter. So it is perfectly understandable that, when the 8th day falls on a Sabbath, the Mila is nevertheless to be done on that day. Although שבת is not only a לא תעשה but לא תעשה ועשה, and the general rule is that an עשה is not דוחה לא תעשה ועשה, nevertheless, here, because of the deep significance of the מילה (just for שבת itself. I.L.), שנכרתו עליה י״ג בריתות, the עשה and the לא תעשה of שבת retire before the עשה of the Mila.

Finally, אעפ״י שיש שם בהרת יקוץ :ימול בשר ערלתו, even if there should be a נגע צרעת on the ערלה, the removal of which is prohibited by both a positive and negative command, by an עשה and a לא תעשה, in Deut. 24,8: השמר בנגע צרעת לשמר מאד ולעשות וגו׳, the Mila is still to be done, ימול בשר ערלתו. As long as the Mila has not been performed the בשר is only to be considered in relation to the existing ערלה, and this is to be removed even if the נגע is removed with it, (Sabbath 132b). — In general, to decide whether an עשה is דוחה לא תעשה, one has always to consider whether it is בעידנא, whether the positive command gets fulfilled at the same moment that the negative one is transgressed, as, for instance, it does here in our case of מילה בצרעת, or in the case of כלאים בציצית, or whether the fulfilment of the positive command only follows the transgression of the negative one (ibid); and further: whether it is quite impossible for the command to be carried out without transgressing the prohibition דלא אפשר לקיומיה לעשה, (Ketuboth 50a).

Vv. 4 & 5. ושלשים יום וגו׳ ,ואם נקבה תלד וגו׳. That, in cases of טומאה היוצאה עליו מגופו, such as יולדת ,נדה ,זב and מצורע, where the idea of the lack of human free will is awakened, not merely by contact with the body of a dead animal, which reminds one of a human body, but is forcibly brought home to oneself by actually having to submit to evidence of it, that in these cases a longer lapse of time is required to overcome the impression, than, for instance, at מגע שרץ ונבלה, where one day suffices, is easily to be understood. Even in the case of a מת, where, although it is not a טומאה היוצאה עליו מגופו, the demonstration of the lack of human free will lies clearly before one, a period of seven days טומאה is required. But at these cases of טומאות היוצאות עליו מגופו, we can presume that the duration of the טומאה is also influenced by the longer or shorter duration of the condition which brought about the bodily feeling of physical unfreedom. So that, just as in the case of מגע מת, the passing of a cycle of days after the event before the re-entry of a condition of טהרה, so here, after the cessation of the bodily condition, a period of days can well be imposed. And so we do find this to be the case, at מצורע in Ch. 14,8, at זב Ch. 15,13, at זבה ibid. 28. We can, accordingly, presume that the duration of the טהרה & טומאה periods for a יולדת is also influenced by the longer or shorter duration of the bodily after-effects of the great act of parturition, and that there is a physiological difference in this respect between the birth of a male or female child. The first period of seven or fourteen days respectively may lie completely under the depressing after-effects of child birth, while the eighth or fifteenth day respectively may be the bracing beginning of the body’s return to normal activity and hence have the character of טָהֳרָה not purity, but purification — and only with the 42nd or the 82nd (In the original it says 84th day, but I think this must be a printer’s error. I.L.) day respectively does the body feel really back to normal. During the first seven or fourteen days respectively, the laws of נדה prevail. (See Ch. 15,19 et seq.). After these have passed and טבילה has been done — ביומי וטבילה תלה רחמנא, (Nidda 36b) — she is יושבת על דם טוהר, she is טהורה לבעלה ולמעשר שני. The Mother is טהור but, like a טבול יום (see Ch. 11,24 & 25), is still טמאה לתרומה ולקדש until the evening of the fortieth, or eightieth day respectively (Nidda 71b). During this period she is called טבולת יום ארוך. At nightfall of the forty-first, or eighty-first day, respectively, she becomes טהורה לתרומה, but being מחוסר כפרה she is still טמאה לקדש until she has brought her קרבן (Jebamoth 74b). So that בכל קדש לא תגע, while she is יושבת על דם טוהר would include תרומה, and if she were to touch it, she would make it טמא, and if she were to eat it she would incur מיתה בידי שמים, and if she were to enter the מקדש would incur מעשר שני .כרת is the sanctification of one’s ordinary material food, תרומה, sanctification of the spirit of the Torah and the representatives thereof, קדש as symbolic expression for a realisation of the ideal of the Torah. The sequence of these קדשים is clear and we find its most characteristic means of recognition in the greater or lesser degree in which they have to be kept away from טומאה.

We would like to allow ourselves one further consideration. It seems to us that the manner and way in which in v. 3, the law of Mila is interposed in the middle of the prescription regarding טומאה in verses 2 & 4 indicates clearly that there must be some deep inner connection between these two institutions. Consider, it says “seven days the Mother is טמא, and on the eighth day the Mila is performed on the child, then for thirty three days she remains … etc.”. The seven days’ טומאה of the Mother, appears to us, introductory to the eighth day, the day of the Mila; the eighth day of the Mila, as bringing the first טומאה-stage of the Mother to a close, and introducing the period of טהרה; this seems clearly indicated. And, as a matter of fact, the free-willed moral subordination of the body to the will of the Torah which is demanded by the institution of Mila as the fundamental condition for the Jewish bond with God, is nothing else but the practical application of the ability to do so which the טהרה-law is meant to keep clearly and definitely in our minds. And likewise the בשר ערלה representing the sensual body remaining withdrawn from the control and mastery of Man, is naught but the realisation of the illusion of Man’s lack of moral freedom which is fostered by the טומאה-idea. Hence, in the laws, too, in many ways, ערל and טמא are similar. An ערל, just like a טמא, is prohibited from eating תרומה and קדשים. An ערל, like a טמא, is excluded from the obligation for ראיה on רגל (Yebamoth 70a & Chagiga 4b); like טמא he is פסול לעבודה (Zebachim 22b); is probably, equally with אסור ,טמא בביאת מקדש, (see לחם משנה הל׳ חגיגה 1, 1). More, ר׳ עקיבא identifies ערלה so much with מרבי ליה לערל כטמא :טומאה, that רבא (Yebamoth 72b) could find it surprising that no tradition was in existence to the effect that ר׳ עקיבא had declared that an ערל would be מטמא by touch just like a טמא, and that the fact that there was no such tradition showed that Rabbi Akiva’s identification of ערל with טמא was not meant to be taken as absolute. But from all the above, it is surely not far-fetched to say that the Mila-day brings the doctrine of “the moral freedom of the human Will” so positively to mind, that not only with it, the stage of the beginning of returning טהרה is reached, but that the טהרה & טומאה cycle of the יולדת is altogether shortened by half.

In the case of a יולדת נקבה the periods of טומאה and ימי טוהר are doubled. The שבועים כנדתה may wish to indicate that this cycle of period is to be considered a dual one. One for the Mother, as in the case of a male baby, and one for the child, for whom the second seven, and thirty-three take the place of the Mila of a boy, as we pointed out in the Mila Chapter (Gen. 17,15 et seq.), the striking characteristic of a Jewish Woman as a true “daughter of Sarah”, is the gift of free-willed subjection to the “measure” of morality and modesty — to which the Jewish Man has a constant reminder in the Mila on his body, — then these טומאה and טהרה laws for women may form, in no lesser degree, a strong preliminary reminder for the necessary preparatory training for such purity of character. For, while the Mila-day, being the first duty which a father has to perform on his son, is to fill him with all the resolutions to bring up his son to a “true strong adherence to a Torah Life before God”, and to a realisation of his responsibility to be an example of such a life, the birth of a daughter is indeed well befitted to impress the Mother, in a double degree of טהרה, with the whole importance and the whole height of her mission to be a guiding and teaching example for a future “Jewish Woman”. After all, the maternal influence on the height of the future moral standard of her daughter is double as great as on that of her son. There the gravamen of the education lies in a greater measure on the father in whom the son is more inclined to see a picture of his own future adult state. But with daughters, the mother is at the same time pattern as well as former of character, and at the birth of each fresh daughter has doubly to arm herself, for the child and for herself, to tread the lofty path of purity and morality up to the heights preached by the Sanctuary of God.

V. 6. בן שנתו :כבש בן שנתו, in it’s first year, without consideration of מנין עולם, of the year of its birth, (5673 or whatever it might be. I.L.), but מעת לעת, from the day, even, here by קדשים reckoning from the hour of its birth until the recurrence of the same day and hour has the year to be counted. Within this period it is שעות פוסלות בקדשים .כשר לקרבן and so also בבתי ערי חומה, Ch. 25,29. Otherwise, in the cases of שתי שנים שבשדה אחוזה, שש שנים שבעבד עברי, וכן שבבן ושבבת, the years are also to be counted מיום ליום, but not משעה לשעה (Nidda 47b). So too, the recording of the years for religious majority, twelve years for girls and thirteen for boys, are counted מיום ליום, but not משעה לשעה, and immediately on the twelfth or respectively the thirteenth anniversary of the birthday, although not yet of the birth hour, the girl or boy attain their religious majority (see משנה למלך on אישות 2, 21 & the מ״א on א״ח 53, 10). There are also institutions of the Torah regarding which the year is reckoned, not individually, but according to the general date of the year; e.g. with ערלה ,מעשר בהמה and נטע רבעי, the second year begins with the beginning of Tishri, even if the animal was born on the last day of Ellul, or the tree was only planted by the fifteenth of Ab, (Rosh Hashana 2a).

כבש בן שנתו לעולה. With this, with “a lamb in its first year”, and as “elevating offering”, after these long trying periods does she, at last, approach “the Shepherd of her life”, with the vow, under His guidance, always to keep the “eternal freshness of youth”, and then, after having got over all depressing bodily influences, with fresh energy, (זריקה. I.L.), “with giving up all her life-forces to strive upwards towards the very summit” of the mission of womanhood and motherhood as directed to her by God; and to allow the “whole of her being” to be given up in keeping alive the fire of God’s Torah to the complete satisfaction” of God, (the whole עולה. I.L.).

ובן יונה או תור לחטאת, but this vow expressed by the עולה offering is preceded by a חטאת העוף, for, everywhere when both an עולה and a חטאת have to be brought, the חטאת has to be brought first. The vow of dedication of one’s actions which is represented by an עולה must, in all these cases, be first preceded by the negative vow to keep free from carelessness and moral weaknesses. God awaits godly acts and deeds only from clean hands; first סור מרע and then עשה טוב. But עשה טוב is the real purpose, and that is why the עולה is mentioned here first, as the Gemora puts it, (Zebachim 90a): למקראה הקדימה הכתוב. And here, indeed there is quite special reason to mention it, (according to ר׳ חיים in תוספות, there it was even to be dedicated first, להקדישה), because it is just the conscious and active striving forwards and upwards towards the whole heights of her real calling in life which forms the most positive contrast to having been forced to lie passively under the forces of Nature.

But her חטאת is a חטאת העוף. For it is just the experience of having been given up to a completely helpless suffering condition, which is exactly what is represented by an עוף, (see notes on Ch. 1,14 et seq.), which threatened her with the danger of losing all her טהרה, with the danger of losing the conscious self-assurance that, in spite of this experience, she is never expected to lose her power of self-determination in all moral matters. That is why she first vows in her חטאת העוף, that she will not allow her power to determine her own actions in all moral matters to be broken by the painful days which are inseparable from her high calling in life; but rather, by undertaking and enduring such days of suffering in the spirit of duty, for the sake of fulfilling her high mission in life, she exercises her power of free will even in this, and so transforms the passiveness of pain itself into active moral energy (see ibid).

V. 7. והקריבו וגו׳ וכפר וגו׳ וטהרה. The כפרה and the resultant complete טהרה is connected primarily only with the bringing of the חטאת, hence והקריבו, with the object in the singular. With the bringing of the חטאת, the טהרה is regained and on that achieved basis the עולה then introduces the happy, fresh striving for progress forward and upward in a new future full of energy.

V. 8. ואם לא תמצא וגו׳. A Mother who is poor represents herself to God and His Sanctuary in the עולה, i.e. in her resolve to have got over her condition of bodily weakness, also as an עוף, having regards to her condition of being without means or power, and vows that, in spite of her manifold troubles of fortune — as is symbolised in the procedures of an עולת העוף, — not to allow herself to be deprived of her self-respect and self-esteem, and even in her impoverished condition to “keep herself” on the “whole height” of the moral godly calling of a Jewish Woman and a Jewish Mother, (see ibid and on XXV,7 et seq.).

V. 1. אל משה ואל אהרן. The special mention of Aaron can hardly be taken to be on account of the fact that in the following laws the co-operation of the כהנים is specially necessary. For we find this form of address to Moses and Aaron together, also in the introduction to the פרשת מאכלות אסורות (Ch. 11,1), and to פרשת זב ונדה (Ch. 15,1), where the כהנים are in no wise given any particular importance. And, on the other hand, just in the introduction to פרשיות, the contents of which do quite specially affect the function of the priests, such as the whole סדר הקרבנות Ch. I et seq., and equally so at the קרבן יולדת (Ch. 12,1), at the קרבן מצורע (Ch. 14,1). Aaron is not mentioned. So it seems, as we have already remarked on Ch. 11,1, that naming Aaron next to Moses at the introduction to certain laws of the Torah as טומאת צרעת, מאכלות אסורות וטומאת מגע and טומאת זב ונדה וזבה, is to indicate the quite special importance of these laws, not only for the theoretical understanding of these laws and the establishment of them for practical use in life, which was to be represented by Moses, but also for the training and education of all the individual people for such understanding and practice. The general idea of these laws is טומאת גויות וטומאת קדושות, (see Ch. XI), through the keeping of which Jews become nutured and educated for the Torah.

V. 2. אדם :אדם כי יהיה וגו׳, not only איש ואשה, grown-ups, but even תינוק בן יום א׳, a child of one day only, is already מטמא בנגעים, (Nidda 44a). כי יהיה: if henceforth a נגע develops, מן הדיבור ואילך (Horioth 10a). The law was not no be applied retrospectively. Any מצורעים who were present at the Lawgiving did not come under the following טומאה-laws. Also no נכרי ונתגייר or קטן ונולד, if the נגע had been present before the entry into Judaism, or before birth, (ת״כ).

שאת או ספהת או בהרת. In Shebuoth 6b, the נגעים mentioned here are explained as being white spots or patches in four shades, which are described in descending degrees as, snow-white, fleece-white, marble-white and skin-of-egg-white: בהרת .כקרום ביצה ,כסיד ההיכל ,כצמר לבן ,עזה כשלג is עזה כשלג שאת is בהרת .כצמר לבן is absolute white, the white of fresh fallen snow. שאת is explained in detail, there in the Gemora, as being, compared to בהרת, a lesser degree of white, the white of the fleece of a lamb which has been kept protected from any dust or dirt by covering the back of the lamb from the day of its birth, as was done for the supply of the finest Millet wool, ספחת .צמר נקי בן יומו שמכבנין למילת, with reference to Sam. 1,11 et seq.: ספחני נא, is there given the meaning of being טפילה, something subsidiary, auxiliary to something else, hence a subsidiary shade of white, as a תולדה of both שאת and בהרת. These two, snow white and fleece white, are the אבות, the two main shades, of white; כסיד, chalk-white is the תולדה, the subsidiary of snow-white of בהרת; and כקרום ביצה, the inner white skin of an egg is the תולדה of שאת. Hence, the sentence in the Mishna in Shebuoth 2a: מראות נגעים שנים שהן ארבעה. So that ספחת is the description of shades of white just above and just below שאת.

והיה :והיה בעור בשרו לנגע צרעת, not מלמד שמצטרפין זה עם זה :והיו (ת״כ), this form of the singular combines all the four shades together as if they were one (“and it develops into the leprous plague”, not “and they develop” etc. I.L.), from which we learn that the נגע, which must have the size of at least a גריס (= > = bean = 9 lentils), need not consist of only one מראה, but that spots of various white shades can be reckoned together to form the necessary minimum size. According to רמב״ם, any of the four shades, according to other opinions, only the two אבות, or an אב with its own נגע — .(ראב״ד) ,תולדה. In by far the majority of cases in which the word נגע occurs, it very definitely refers, not to a condition of ordinary disease but to one which comes as specially sent by God. The person affected is נגוע, literally “touched” by the Finger of God. It is a weaker form of נגף, from which we get מגפה, the sudden stroke of death. The word disease, by which it is usually translated, and which we have used here in default of knowing a really fitting one, by no means expresses the idea of נגע. “Plague”, also, is scarcely any better, it only refers to the person affected and makes no reference, as נגע does, to the idea of its origin. So, the Gemora in Horioth 10a refers to the explicit: ונתתי נגע צרעת בבית וגו׳ (Ch. 14,34), and concludes from it that for נגעי אדם too, all such נגעים are excluded from טומאה, which can be referred back to other pathological causes, and need not be taken as being directly sent by God (פרט לנגעי ,נגעי כשפים וגו׳ צרע :צרעת — .רוחות, (related to זרה ,זרע, to throw out, and to סרח, to rot), points to a foulness which breaks out from within, whereas נגע indicates its origin from without, and indeed, as already remarked, as the direct touch of God. Accordingly, when the Torah combines the two words in the expression נגע צרעת, it may want to teach us that not every צרעת is מטמא, but only such which proclaims itself as a נגע, as sent directly from God; and again, only such a נגע which shows itself as צרעת, as an inner foulness breaking out from within on to the skin. According to ת״כ, in the idea נגע there is also the conceptian of something objectionable and painful, מלמד שמצטער ממנו, and moreover, here, to such a degree that אחרים מצטערים ממנו, that its proximity disturbs other people too, as the ראב״ד thereon, says מריחה that its odour is objectionable. Possible this may be indicated too in the following והובא, “he is brought”, others find reason to bring him to the כהן.

לנגע צרעת. We have already mentioned that the נגע is מטמא only if the affected place has the size of a גריס, half a broken bean, a גריס הקלקי, probably a Chilician bean (Negaim 6, 1). All שיעורין, the fixed measures and sizes for the various laws of the Torah are הלכה למשה מסיני, (Sukka 5b).

והובא אל אהרן הכהן או אל אחד מבניו הכהנים. Tradition teaches that it is only the verdict טמא or טהור, which is dependent on the proclamation of a כהן. He only becomes טמא or טהור when a כהן — and even if this latter is a בעל מום as long as he is not a חלל — who has forfeited the character of a כהן, — proclaims the word טמא or טהור over him. But the examination and recognition of the נגע, if the כהן is not experienced in such diagnosis, can be made by anybody who is sufficiently expert, and then the כהן has to make the appropriate declaration טמא or טהור in accordance with such diagnosis. Perhaps we can see some indication of this law in the text of our verse. והובא indicated the intervention of others, non-Cohanim, who recognize the נגע as requiring the intervention of a כהן, and אהרן may designate the כהן בקי and אחד מבניו הכהנים in contrast to אהרן הכהן, the כהן שאינו בקי, the one for whom the only qualification demanded is, that he is a pure descendant of Aaron and only excludes חללים. From the verse Deut. 21,5: ועל פיהם יהיה כל ריב וכל נגע, where civil processes at court and נגעים are classed together, the Gemora in Nidda 50a learns that just as in ריבים, relations are barred from acting in any capacity in court so, in נגעים, no priest may function for any relation. On the other hand, נגעים do not require the verdict to be given by a body of three, one “judge” is sufficient, for our verse says: או אל אחד מבניו.

V. 3. שיהו עיניו בו בשעה שהוא רואה אותו :וראה הכהן את הנגע וגו׳ (ת׳׳כ). The כהן has to concentrate his gaze on the נגע and compare it with עוד הבשר, with the colour of the rest of the skin, and according to the הלכה of the חכמים to compare it with the tint of normal skin, בעור הבשר הבינוני, (ibid).

ושער בנגע הפך לבן, the hair which usually is found on all skin has become bleached by the נגע — there must be at least two hairs, מיעוט שיער שתי שערות, hairiness is represented by a minimum of two hairs. The colour of the hair is only of consequence when it has been caused as a result of the נגע. But if it preceded the נגע, if the שער לבן שקדם לבהרת, it does not effect טומאה, not even if it did originally come from a נגע which had healed and disappeared and only this שער לבן remained and then a fresh נגע had formed about this white hair. Such left-over hair is called שער פקודה and is טהור. Every נגע which is to become טמא by the bleaching of the hair must have effected this bleaching itself, (Negaim 5, 3).

מראה הנגע עמוק אין ממשו עמוק :ומראה הנגע עמוק מעור בשרו, “the colour of the נגע is ‘deeper’ than the skin, but the place itself is not a depression on the skin” (ת״כ). It is dealing here with the highest degree of whiteness, the snow-white, בהרת, the white of which is accordingly the “deepest”. This depth or intensity of whiteness does not effect the טומאה, but it is the שער לבן which develops in it which does. Wessely in his commentary, presumes that שער לבן usually only develops in בהרת cases, and that this is the reason why the text speaks of it in connection with it. But actually שער לבן is just as much a סימן טומאה if it occurs in any of the other three shades. ת״כ .וראהו הכהן וטמא אותו remarks וראהו implies כלו כאחת, that the נגע must be able to be seen on one flat surface in its requisite minimum size of a גריס. Hence finger tips and similar points on the body where there is no such space are not מטמא בנגעים. In Negaim 6, 7 twenty four such places are reckoned.

V. 4. ואם בהרת לבנה הוא וגו׳. The explanation of this verse which seems most fitting is that of Wessely, that here it is speaking of the subsidiary shade of בהרת, the ספחת, the chalk-white נגע, which is slightly darker than the pure snow-white of the בהרת, and of which it accordingly can be said ועמוק אין מדאה, that its white appearance is not as deep and intensive as that of the main בהרת of the preceding verse. So does the כ״מ too (on הל׳ טומאת צרעת, 1, 6), seem to have understood the meaning of these words of which Rashi remarks לא ידעתי פירושו. It only remains difficult that the Gemora in Shebuoth 6b takes the case of our verse to be that of the high shade of white of בהרת and says היא לבנה ואין אחרת לבנה :ואם בהרת לבנה היא, and this could well be that which kept Rashi away from explaining it as a weaker shade of בהרת. But after all it does not say there אין אחרת לבנה הימנה, but אין אחרת לבנה, and this could perhaps refer to the class of בהרת, and be understood to refer to בהרת and the תולדה belonging to it. Both the snow-white and the chalk-white really belong to the class of pure white and then it follows naturally that בהרת as the אב of that class, is עזה, the strongest white, snow-white. The other class, שאת ותולדתה, wool-white and egg-skin-white, is no longer absolutely pure white, it could shade slightly into blueish yellowish. Accordingly it is the תולדה of בהרת, the סיד ההיכל which would be described here in our verse; it is still בהרת-white but no longer so much “deeper” than the colour of the skin. — ושערה לא הפך לבן והסגיר וגו׳: this law, too, applies to all the four מראות. According to Wessely it is only mentioned here, at the תולדה של בהרת, because (as mentioned above. I.L.), it is with בהרת that הפיכת שער לבן usually occurs, and then it is immediately טמא without הסגר.

והסגיר הכהן את הנגע וגו׳. There are two stages of טומאה for the מצורע who has been examined viz. הסגר and החלט intermediate isolation, pending decision, and decision. There are three symptoms, סימני טומאה, which as soon as they show at the נגע render the person מוחלט, these are:— שער לבן (v. 3), פשיון (vv. 7 & 8) and מחיה (vv. 10 & 11). But if the נגע has the requisite colour, i.e. one of the four מראות, but there is not yet any שער לבן or מחיה, the person is kept isolated for seven days, is a מצורע מוסגר, and on the seventh day is examined afresh. If then one of the three סימני טומאה has appeared, he is declared מוחלט. If the נגע has remained unchanged, a second period of seven day’s הסגר is entered, but the seventh day on which the examination took place is reckoned in, so that altogether the period is thirteen days. If after these two periods of הסגר, one of the סימני טומאה shows itself, he is declared מוחלט, if not, he is פטור, declared free. In the cases of שחין (v. 18 et seq.) and מכוה (v. 24 et seq.), only one period of הסגר is imposed, and the symptoms of מחיה is not taken as a sign of טומאה. Of the three שער לבן ,סימני טומאה and מחיה can be visible at the first examination and make the מצורע into a מוחלט at once, but פשיון only applies after (not during. I.L.), the הסגר. All three do apply, however, if they appear לאחר פטור, after he has been declared free on the thirteenth day (v. 7). Hence the paragraph in Negaim 3, 3 & 4:— עור הבשר מיטמא בשני שבועות ובשלשה סימנין, בשער לבן ובמחיה בתחלה, ובסוף שבוע ראשון ובסוף שבוע שני לאחר הפטור ובפסיון בסוף שבוע ראשון ובסוף שבוע שני לאחר הפטור, ומטמא בשני שבועות שהן שלשה עשר יום. — השחין והמכוה מיטמאין בשבוע אחד ובשני סימנין, בשער לבן ובפסיון, בשער לבן בתחלה בסוף שבוע לאחר הפטור, ובפסיון בסוף שבוע לאחר הפטור, ומיטמאין בשבוע אחד שהוא שבעת ימים.

There is no difference between מצורע מוסגר and מצורע מוחלט with regards to the prescribed isolation of v. 46 — לענין שלוח — nor to טומאה, the laws of טומאה in v. 6 & 46. Only פריעה and פרימה (v. 45) are not imposed during ימי הסגר and one who becomes טהור after הסגר does not have to undergo the תגלחת or to bring the צפרים which are prescribed on attaining טהרה after being מוחלט (Megilah 8b). הסגר does not seem to be identical with שלוח מחנה. Apart from שלוח מחנה, being expelled from מחנה ישראל, the מצורע has to be isolated even there (see Rashi ibid). The Gemora there, in Megilah, does not deduce שלוח for a מצורע מוסגר from והסגירו. It is altogether not decided whether הסגר means an actual locking up or a declaration that he is to be isolated (istracised, “sent to Coventry”. I.L.). See Ch. 14,38.

V. 5. וראהו הכהן ביום השביעי. Every examination of a נגע must be made by day, not towards twilight nor in the confusing full midday light, but in the middle hours of the forenoon and afternoon, בארבע בתמש בשמנה בתשע, (Negaim 2, 2). והנה, he has to judge it only by its present appearance, any spreading or change which may have occurred during the period of הסגר does not come into consideration at all (ראב״ד on בעיניו) עמד בעיניו .(ת״כ in the plural. I.L.), even if it is not בעיניו exactly in the same shade as before, as long as it is still בעיניו, within the four מראות and has not recovered above the קרום ביצה shade, in which case it would be בהק and טהור (v. 39). והסגיר הכהן את הנגע שבעת ימים שנית, just as at the first הסגר, the day on which the הסגר was proclaimed over him was reckoned in with the seven days, so here the seventh day of the first הסגר is the first day of the second making thirteen days altogether (ת״כ).

V. 6. והנה כהה הנגע, even if it had grown darker, the טהרה depends on the absence of פשיון as long as it has not sunk past the lowest stage of white, the קרום ביצה stage. But פשיון is מטמא even if the colour has remained quite unchanged (רמב״ן). It is also possible that כהה does not mean becoming dark but becoming weak (as in ולא כהה בהם, Sam. I. 3,31, Wessely) and then would form one idea with ולא פשה. The נגע had remained as it was and had not spread.

מספחת היא, like ספחת in v. 2. It is no real נגע only nearly one. The designation מספחת supports the supposition of Wessely that here it is speaking of an appearance which usually does not occur with a בהרת but with a ספחת of a בהרת (see note on v. 4).

וכבס בגדיו וטהר, so, up till then, he was טמא and מטמא, and actually to the same degree as a מצורע מוחלט. He was מטמא ,מטמא במגע ובמשא משכב ומושב and בביאה (see v. 46). On טומאת משכב ומושב see notes on Ch. 15,4 et seq. According to רמב״ם (הל׳ טומאת צרעת 10, 11), the משכב ומושב of a מצורע is equally אב הטומאה as that of a זב וזבה. But, according to תוספות to ר״ש and ראב״ד who agree with Rashi, the משכב ומושב of a מצורע is only ולד הטומאה and would only be מטמא אוכלין ומשקין (see Pesachim 67b and מל״מ on רמב״ם thereon).

V. 7. ונראה שנית אל הכהן, as a rule it should be to the same one who had examined it in the earlier stages (ת״כ). For פסיון can altogether only be judged by one who had seen the נגע before and can compare its present size to that of the previous occasion.

V. 9. נגע צרעת וגו׳ introduces a different appearance of a נגע viz. שאת, the second major shade of white, the wool-white colour, together with the third סימן טומאה, that of מחיה. This, apparently, is most frequently found in this particular appearance of the נגע and is accordingly mentioned in connection with it, but actually, like שער לבן and פסיון, it applies equally to all the four מראות.

V. 10. שער לבן :והיא הפכה שער לבן is only a סימן טומאה for the נגע which produced it. But if the original נגע in which the bleached hair arose had been cured, and a fresh נגע forms about the bleached hair which had remained (שער פקודה), the שעד לבן is not a סימן טומאה for this new ומחית בשר וגו׳. (ת״כ) ,נגע: After שער לבן has already in v. 3 been declared to form by itself a סימן טומאה, and equally so in verses 15 & 16 that מחיה by itself does the same, the copulative ו in ומחית can not mean that both סימנים together are necessary for the proclamation טמא but must be translated “and equally so if a healthy spot of healthy flesh is in the שאת״. It indicates the equality of the two signs, and primarily with regards to size. מחיה is only מטמא if it is at least the size of a square which the removal of two hairs in each direction would make שתי שערות על שתי שערות. As שער לבן and מחיה are mentioned together in one נגע it must presuppose that there is room in the נגע for them both to exist next to each other. So there must be place in the נגע for two hairs next to the מחיה. As further, by the description: ומחית בשר חי בשאת, the Halacha is given that the spot of מחיה must be surrounded on all sides (מבוצר) by שאת, so that there must be room on all sides of it for שתי שערות. This gives us the size of the whole נגע as six hairbreadths square, i.e. thirty six square hairbreadths, and that is the size of a (ת״כ) ,גריס הקלקי. In this מחיה differs from שער לבן. As we said above, מחיה must be מבוצר, while שער לבן, although it, too, must be within the נגע, need not be surrounded by the נגע, it is טמא and מטמא even if it is right at the edge of the spot (Negaim 4,3). They differ also in this point, while שער לבן is only מטמא הפוכה, i.e. it turns white in the נגע but not if it is known to have been there before the occurrence of the מחיה ,נגע is הפוכה ושלא הפוכה, i.e. even if it was there before (ibid).

V. 11. נושנת היא וגו׳: The healthy flesh in the midst of the white spot shows that the נגע is already an old one; either the healthy tissue had resisted the attack of the נגע for some time and the נגע could only creep all round it, or it had conquered the נגע in the middle and taken its place, hence מחיה is מטמא הפוכה ושלא הפוכה (Wessely) whether it develops in the spot or whether it is found there at the first examination.

V. 12. ואם פרוח תפרח, even if it does so only very gradually, את כל עור הנגע, all those parts of the skin to which נגע applies, excluding, for instance places effected by שחין המורדת ומכוה המורדת (see v. 18 & 24). מראשו ועד רגליו: excluding the תוך ראשו ותוך רגליו, the hairy part of his head and the soles of his feet, ת״כ. (see מל״מ on הל׳ צרעת 6, 1). לכל מראה (ת״כ) ,פרט לבית הסתרים :עיני הכהן, everything which the כהן can see with the person affected standing in a natural position, excluding places which are hidden in folds of skin or by the curves of the body when bending. The legs are examined in the position of עודר, digging, and the arms in that of מוסק זיתים, plucking olives from the tree (Negaim 2, 4).

V. 13. הפורח מן הטמא טהור, מן הטהור טמא :כלו הפך לבן טהור הוא, (Negaim 8, 1), i.e. the נגע spreading over the whole body is טהור if it does so from a טמא-condition, whether הסגר or החלט. But if it occurs after a טהור-condition, either right at the beginning, at the first appearance of the נגע, or after it has already been declared cured, then פריחה בכולו is טמא. Hence, הבא כולו לבן יסגיר וכו׳, if the very first time he comes to the priest, his skin has turned white all over the body, he must be isolated, הסגר is demanded. Altogether such a condition, בהרת גדולה בתחלה, has to be treated exactly as an ordinary small בהרת. And equally so, if, after the second הסגר (v. 6), he had been declared טהור and then כולו הפך לבן, he becomes מוחלט just as in the case of a small פסיון (v. 7).

V. 14. וביום הראות בו. It does not say ובהראות בו but וביום הראות בו, from which Moed Katan 7b teaches the significant Halacha: יש יום שאתה רואה בו, ויש יום שאי אתה רואה בו, that there are days on which the examination of a נגע is not done: חתן שנולד בו נגע נותנין לו שבעה ימי משתה לו ולביתו ולכסותו, וכן ברגל נותנין לו שבעת ימי הרגל, “If a נגע shows itself on a bridegroom, he is allowed to pass his seven days of rejoicing without being examined and similarly no examinations are made on the seven days of a Yomtov, neither on the person, his house or his clothes should a נגע appear on these”. More, we find in Ch. 14,36: וצוה הכהן ופנו את הבית וגו׳, that it is expressly commanded to postpone the examination of a נגע in a house until all moveables had been taken out of the house, and the rooms cleared, ולא יטמא כל אשר בבית, so that everything in the house should not become טמא. So we find that even לדבר הרשות, for purely reasons of ordinary interests, the examination of a נגע gets postponed. On שבת, too, ראית נגעים is not done, and if the seventh day of הסגר falls on a שבת, the examination is postponed until the following day (Negaim 1, 4).
V. 15 & 16. Here it is only בשר חי which brings the טומאה back again, but not שער לבן. Neither does בהק, i.e. if it is not really healthy skin, but darker than the four מראות (see v. 39, ת״כ).
V. 17. הוא טהור ואין :טהור הוא — .(ת״כ) ,אפי׳ למראה בהק :ונהפך ללבן ,הבא בכולו לבן בתחלה טהור אלא טמא (ת״כ, see notes on v. 13).

V. 18. שחין, [we have already given its etymology on Ex. 9,9, and here, in addition, would draw attention to its relation to צחן (Joel 2,20): צחנתו), which means the smell of foulness], is applied to every inflammation of the skin, either to that which comes out from within or results from a blow or external injury, with the exception of burns. This latter is referred to in v. 24 by the term ת״כ) מכוה, Chulin 8a). — ונרפא. That it does not speak here of being completely healed is evident from v. 20, where it says: בשחין פרחה, so that the inflammation must still be there The condition, accordingly, is one where healing has begun but is not completed. נרפא ולא נרפא, as it is described in ת״כ. The skin had been broken by the inflammation and it had already formed a new thin skin, כקליפת השום, (like the fine blueish skin of garlic). As long as this stage of recovery has not begun, the inflammation is called שחין מורד ,מורדת and as such, no נגע טמא can form on it. Once the healing is complete and cicatricial tissue formed, this new skin comes under the general heading of עור בשר, and is liable to all the ordinary laws of נגע already discussed above, is טמא בשלשה סימנים ובשני שבועות. But if the healing has commenced but is not completed, נרפא ולא נרפא, then the laws which follow here apply: נגע appearing on the newly formed skin, has only to have one week of הסגר and becomes מוחלט only through two מחיה .שער לבן ופשיון :סימנים does not apply. In all respects מכוה is the same (v. 24 et seq. Negaim 3, 4 & 9, 2).
V. 19. לבנה אדמדמת (see on v. 49) this shade of white tinged with red occurs in all four מראות and also in נגעי עור בשר. In Halacha it is termed פתוך, mixed, (Shebuoth 6a).
V. 20. אבל לא בעור הבשר :בשחין פרחה. The נגע has to be judged quite isolated on the שחין. Any appearance on the adjoining skin makes no difference (ת״כ) .

V. 21. ושפלה איננה מן העור והיא כהה: V. 19 only mentions the two אבות, viz. שאת and בהרת, here the two תולדות are added:— ושפלה איננה מן העור, even if it not so “deep”, i.e. not to intensely white, as והיא כהה ,בהרת, and even if it is darker than שאת (see on v. 4).
V. 22. ואם פשה תפשה, even if this פשיון only shows itself after the seventh day of ת״כ) ,הסגר).

V. 23. ואם תחתיה וגו׳ לא פשתה. The estimation of the פשיון, too, is restricted solely to the area of the שחין. Any spreading over into the עור בשר or into the עוד מכוה would not be צרבת שחין — .(ת״כ) ,מטמא, according to ת״כ in v. 18, in contrast to צלקת, the complete cicatrization, is the beginning of the healing, which is shown by the formation of new skin. עשו קרום כקליפת השום זו היא צרבת השחין האמורה בתורה, חזרו וחיו אעפ״י שמקומן צלקת נדונין כעור הבשר (Negaim 9, 2). (When it forms a thin skin like the skin of garlic, that is what the Torah calls: צרבת השחין. I.L.).
V. 24. מחית המכוה is identical with צרבת המכוה of v. 28 (“the beginning of the formation of cicatricial tissue”, i.e. the healing. I.L.).

V. 28. והיא כהה, translate “and equally so if it is less intensely white”, i.e. darker than בהרת, namely, שאת, as it at once says: שאת המכוה היא, it is only טהור if it has not spread. Any change of colour, more intensely white or less intensely so, as long as it remains within the four shades of the מראות and has not become darker than the ordinary colour of skin, makes no difference towards טומאה and טהרה.

מכוה and שחין have exactly the same treatment. They are only mentioned separately in the Torah because they can not be combined to form the minimum size necessary to be regarded as a נגע. Half a גריס of the one and half a גריס of the other are not considered to form a נגע (Negaim 9, 2).

V. 29. ואיש או אשה וגו׳. Verses 29—37, as well, as 40—43, treat of נגעי ראש וזקן, of נגעים which appear on the head, under the hair or beard. Verses 29—37 deal with נתק, verses 40—43 with קרחת and גבחת. The symptoms which differentiate נתק from קרחת and גבחת are not quite definite. According to ראב״ד on ת״כ and רמב״ן thereon, a נתק is an isolated bald spot surrounded by hair (according to ראב״ד apparently only if it is situated on the top of the head between the front and back part of the head, centrally) whereas קרחת and גבחת is baldness starting up from the neck or forehead. But according to ר״ש (Negaim 10, 10), the difference between נתק and קרחת and גבחת is not one of position and size but of character. נתק is only a temporary loss of hair while קרחת and גבחת would be permanent incurable baldness. המב״ן remarks that the term נתק and מריטה do seem to support the latter way of taking it. נתק, to tear, separate, remove, would refer to the hair and need not indicate any permanent change in the skin, while מרט, which is also the term for polishing metals, would refer to the polished surface of the altered skin.

נתק, the isolated, or temporary bald spot, as long as it has the size of a גריס, is by itself a נגע, which, according to most authorities, even without any alteration in the colour of the skin, demands two periods of הסגר and becomes מוחלט by שער צהוב or פשיון, while the four shades of white, the מראות, have no effect on a נתק spot. On the other hand, קרחת and גבחת in themselves are no נגע, the bald scalp has the character of the ordinary skin of the body, is עור בשר and like it, is affected by the ארבע מראות נגעים has two periods of הסגר and receives the character of מוחלט by פשיון and מחיה. Only שער לבן does not apply to it.
זקן .בראש או בזקן is the hair from the temple to the Adam’s apple.

V. 30. והנה מראהו עמק מן העור. It is repeatedly evident from v. 31 and from v. 32 and also from v. 35 taken in conjunction with v. 4, that even if the נתק spot is not “deeper” white, i.e. not lighter than the colour of ordinary skin it nevertheless requires הסגר and can become מוחלט by פשיון or נתק .שער צהוב is, accordingly, טמא by itself even if the colour is darker than קרום ביצה. This law gives us a quite natural and unforced explanation to what otherwise would be difficult to explain, viz., the meaning of the interpolation of verses 38 & 39. But there it simply comes to state that בהק, the appearance of shiny white spots of any shade of white darker than קרום ביצה anywhere else on the body, on עור בשר is טהור in contrast to our case of נתק about which it has been speaking. If, nevertheless, here in our verse it says והנה מראהו עמוק מן העור, it can only want to tell us thereby, that even in the case of מראה שאת or בהרת the טומאה does not depend on שער לבן but on שער צהוב דק. In this connection the ת״ב learns further, from this putting מראה עמוק together with נקת that, just as the מראה is only בידי שמים, so נתק too, is only a נגע, if it is בידי שמים, but not if the hair had been pulled out שער :שער צהוב דק — .בידי אדם, at least שתי שערות, as in the cases of שער לבן (see v. 3). צהוב: goldish. דק, referring to hair means short, (ר׳ עקיבא in Negaim 10, 1).
ובו שער צהוב דק: here it does not say הפך, so that even if the שער צהוב שקדם לנתק, it would be טמא; Negaim 10, 2 says: מטמא הפיך ושלא הפוך (see v. 3).

V. 31. ושער שחור אין בו: again, there must be, at least, two hairs. If two dark hairs have remained within the נתק, then neither by פשיון nor שער צהוב does it become שחור .טמא, here is only used in contrast to צהוב (which is why I translated it “dark”. I.L.). Any other colour of hair as opposed to צהוב, is equally מציל.

V. 33. בכל אדם :והתגלח, by anybody, whereas the גלוח prescribed in Ch. XIV, must be done by the ואת הנתק לא יגלח .כהן: he has to leave the hair growing for two hairbreadths all round the נתק to be able to judge a possible subsequent פשיון (Negaim 10, 5). From this, the מל״מ on הל׳ ט״צ 8, 1, deduces the view, which is held by most authorities, that a נתק does not imply any change in the colour of the skin, otherwise there would be no necessity to mark off the size of the נגע by a circumference of hair to judge whether there has been any פשיון, just as there is no necessity to do so in ordinary נגעי עור בשר.
V. 34. וכבס בגדיו, see note on v. 6.
V. 36. פשיון :וראהו הכהן is מטמא without שער צהוב and equally so שער צהוב without פשיון.

V. 37. ואם בעיניו עמד הנתק וגו׳. Above, in v. 5, it says: והנה הנגע עמד בעיניו, after the first הסגר, so that the remaining as it was, refers to the appearance which the נגע had at the beginning of the הסגר, and this was solely the white colouring of one of the four מראות of the skin. But here the ואם בעיניו עמד הנתק comes after the case where פשיון or שער צהוב had occurred following the declaration of (אחרי טהרתו) פטור. We are therefore inclined to think that this בעיניו here refers to these signs of טומאה, and it would say:— even if the נתק, has remained in this condition and these signs of טומאה are still present but two dark hairs have grown in it, נרפא הנתק טהור הוא, the נתק is considered cured and in spite of the פשיון and the שער צהוב is טהור. And actually the Halacha is so: הצומח מציל מיד השער צהוב ומיד הפשיון, (Negaim 10, 3), but it makes a difference between שער שחור הצומח and המשואר, between dark hairs which have grown after the נתק had appeared and those which were there already and had remained within the נתק-patch. These latter only act as annulling the טומאה if they are מבוצר, if they are enclosed by the נתק, if they are separated from the rest of the growth of hair by at least two hairbreadths on every side (this is why in v. 31, it says: ושער שחור אין בו, as the ק״א so pertinently remarks thereon, dark hair may well be there, but אין בו, its position is not the requisite one, it is not completely within the נתק). But צומח is effective even שלא מבוצר, as long as it has grown afresh anywhere on the bald patch,ושער שחור צמח בו. But in ת״כ the בעיניו here is taken as referring to the כהן, “if in his eyes, in his judgement etc.”.

אעפ״י שהלך לו שער שחור טהור :נרפא הנתק טהור הוא. even if the dark hairs fell out again and the שער צהוב or the פשיון remained, the נתק is טהור until fresh צהוב grows or fresh פשיון occurs, (Negaim 10, 8, according to the הל׳ ט״צ ,רמב״ם 8, 8).

טהור הוא וטהרו הכהן; he only becomes טהור when the כהן declares him so, and the declaration of the כהן is only effective when the actual condition (טהור הוא) is in accordance with the requirements of the laws of the Torah. A mistaken or intentionally false declaration of a כהן is completely invalid and has no consequence (ת״כ). In exactly the same sense the Torah speaks of the טומכה-declaration in v. 44: טמא הוא, טמא יטמאנו הכהן, he only becomes טמא by the declaration of the כהן, and such declaration has only any effect if his condition really legally demands it (Negaim תוספתא Ch. 1 at end). So that this institution of נגעים gives no power at all in the hands of the priests. His declaration can be controlled by any one who is thoroughly acquainted with these laws.

V. 39. בקה הוא: all white spots, the colour of which is כהות less intensively white, darker than the lowest of the four מראות, i.e. darker than קרום ביצה, are termed בוהק and are טהור. (In Aramaic בהק means shining, glistening, illuminating. Hence probably the expression רבו המובהק, for someone’s special teacher from whom he has gained most of his knowledge שרוב חכמתו ממנו). For this connection of בהק with the laws of נתק, see note on v. 30 above.

V. 40. et seq. See note above on v. 29, טהור הוא, that is to say, his baldness as קרח, (bald at the back of the head), has not got the דין of נתק (a bald patch) to become טמא by שער צהוב, but as it goes on to say in vv. 42 & 43, the bald scalp has the character of the ordinary skin of the body and is susceptible to the ארבע מראות and their consequences. In Negaim 10, 9, the Halacha is given that even a נתק which has become מוחלט by שער צהוב or by פשיון would become טהור if the head becomes completely bald, ניתק כל הראש, or if the נתק was in the beard, by ניתק כל הזקן and ת״כ attaches this Halacha to our verse here.

This פריחה בכולו at נתק is treated exactly similarly to הפך כולו לבן at נגעי עור בשר except that it is also טהור if it comes הבא בתחילה .לאחר פטור ניתק כל הראש, or כל הזקן has to be treated as נתק, just as הפך כולו לבן בתחלה is treated as בהרת גדולה.
V. 41. גבחת .גבח, frontal baldness seems to be related to גבע ,גבה and by גבחת to indicate the height or extent of the forehead being made to reach up to the crown.

V. 43. קרחת וגבחת :כמראה צרעת עור בשר are not only מטמא בפתוך (see on v. 19. I.L.) which is expressly mentioned in v. 42 & 43, but also generally by the four מראות, as ordinary עור בשר, and, as such, necessitate twice הסגר. But they only become מוחלט by two of the סימנים viz. מחיה ופשיון, but not by שער לבן (Negaim 10, 10).

V. 44. איש צרוע, and in v. 45 it says והצדוע. Whereas the first excludes women, the second generalises the idea of צרוע to extend to women too. The Halacha, (Sota 33a), teaches that all the regulations given here for the צרוע, including the פריעה ופרימה (tearing one’s garments, letting the hair grow wild and having the head and face covered down to the upper lip. I.L.), apply to men, but a woman who is צרועה is the same as a man in all respects of טומאה etc., but is free from the obligations of טמא הוא וגו׳ .פריעה ופרימה: see note on v. 37. This repeated הוא limits the dependence of the condition of טומאה on the declaration of a כהן solely to טומאת צרעת, all other טמאים are טמאים as soon as the cause occurs: זה טומאתו (ת״כ) ,בכהן ואין שאר טמאים טומאתן בכהן.

V. 45. מי שצרעתו תלויה בגופו :אשר בו הנגע. Only he is subjected to the פריעה and פרימה prescribed in this verse, whose condition of טומאה lasts until the awaited alteration in his bodily condition occurs, i.e. a מוחלט, who remains טמא until the נגע is healed, but not a מוסגר whose טומאה is not תלויה בגופו אלא בימים, and ceases at the end of the ימי הסגר if the נגע has remained unchanged (Megilla 8b).

פרומים, (tattered, torn. I.L.), see Ch. 10,6. — פרוע, (grown wild, unshorn. I.L.), according to ר׳ עקיבא also without the ordinary headcovering (Moed Katan 15a, תוספות), although by the immediately following ועל שפם יעטה, the מצורע is commanded to keep his head covered, עטיפת הראש. Similarly in Kethuboth 72b, a married woman going without the usual head covering, although the hair may be otherwise covered, is called and considered as being וצ״ע דשם קלתה לא הוי אלא ד״י ובאן משמע .פריעת ראש דפרוע ראש מדאורייתא מקרי. ואפשר דבכתובות הוי דלא כר״ע ומשום זה ג״כ לא ועל שפם יעטה — .מייתי רמב״ם בחיבורו גבי מצורע דבעי ג״כ גלוי ראש וצ״ע, is, according to Moed Katan 24a, a drawing down of the head covering right over the lips, עד גובי דדיקנא, (Rashi thereon). But, according to R. Hai, it needs only extend to the side whiskers (Tur., Y.D. 386).

V. 46. כל ימי אשר הנגע בו, even if the נגע has been cut away, although it is prohibited to do so. מן התורה, if the נגע has gone, the טומאה has gone, (Bechoroth 34b) — כל ימי וגו׳, including the ימי הסגר, although during that period there is no פריעה ופרימה. For regarding טומאה and בדד ישב, i.e. שלוח מחנה, there is no difference between מוסגר and מוחלט (Megilla 8b). — שלא ישב טמא אחר עמו :בדד ישב, (Zebachim 118a); the מצורע is the furthest removed of all טמאים whereas טמא מת is only excluded from the מחנה שכינה and זב וזבה only from מחנה לויה, the מצורע is kept out of even מחנה ישראל (see notes on Numb. 5,2). But only enclosed cities, עיירות המוקפות חומה, are considered as a מחנה ישראל and of those only such as were originally surrounded by walls when the land was first taken into possession, המוקפות חומה מימות יהושע בן נון, (see note on Ch. 25,29; Kelim 1, 7; ר״ש thereon). According to this, a מצורע could remain in any other city.

(ת״כ) מושבו טמא :מושבו; hence הטמא עומד תחת האילן והטהור עובר טמא, טהור עומד תחת האילן וטמא עובר טהור, ואם עמד טמא, i.e. if a מצורע stands under a tree and somebody passes under the tree, that person becomes טמא; but if somebody stands under a tree and the מצורע passes under that tree, the person does not become טמא unless the מצורע stands still, (Negaim 13, 7). Any place where a מצורע is at rest is considered as מושבו, his “resting place”, and if that place is roofed or under cover, everything that is with him under that roof or cover even temporarily becomes טמא unless it is partitioned off. But even a small screen of at least ten טפחים in height and four cubits in width, suffices to protect the טהור from becoming טמא, (Negaim ibid 12). But the condition that the מצורע must be “at rest” only applies to a space which is not enclosed, such as the branches of a tree (mentioned above. I.L.). But in a house, even the passing through of a מצורע makes everything which is under the same roof at the time טמא, (Yebamoth 103b, תוספות thereon). Such טומאה of a מצורע is called ,ביאה מצורע מטמא בביאה (Kelim 1, 4). It is similar to the טומאת אהל of a מת, a similarity which ספרי finds indicated in Numb. 12,12: אל נא תהי כמת, on which it says: מה המת מטמא באהל אף מצורע מטמא בביאה. Similarly in Yebamoth 103b it says: מוחלט איתקש למת. But they differ principally in that a מת makes everything טמא which is under any אוהל with it even if it is עובר, only being carried through, and also in that a מחיצה of י׳ טפחים is not מציל in אהל המת. See ר״ש Kelim ibid.

V. 47. והבגד וגו׳. Negaim 11, 1, teaches us that כל הבגדים מיטמאין בנגעים חוץ משל נכרים, הלוקח בגדים מן הנכרים יראו בתחלה, and that gives us a characteristic difference between נגעי בגדים and נגעי הגוף. While the נגעי הגוף which a גר brings over from his נכרי state have no effect whatsoever (see v. 12), a בגד which is affected by a נגע while being the property of a נכרי as soon as it comes into the possession of a Jew must be shown to a כהן and the appropriate treatment prescribed. יראו בתחילה. According to the way the ר״ש takes Negaim 3, 1 there would be the further difference in that בגדי גר תושב, would also be liable to טומאת נגעים. With regards to טומאה, a בגד המנוגע has the same character as אדם both as מוסגר and as מוחלט. It is אב הטומאה and מטמא במגע ובמשא ובביאה. According to רמב״ם also משכב ומושב like אדם. But see ראב״ד and מל״מ thereon. With regards to שלוח מחנה, however, בגדים המנוגעים are even חמורים מאדם, as they have to be sent outside all cities whether surrounded by a wall or not. (see note on v. 46).
והבגד. Under this heading, not only clothes, but things like curtains, sails etc., made out of cloth or leather or skins, are to be included, (Negaim 11, 11; see ר״ש thereon).

V. 48. שחי :או בשתי או בערב is the warp, the threads running the long way of the fabric, the ערב is the woof, the threads that cross the warp in woven fabric. Here it is the yet unwoven spun threads for either.

או בעור. According to the Halacha, (Negaim 11, 1), only skins of land-animals. Hence we see again the principle: כל אשר בים טהור, (see note above on Ch. 11,32). Wool and flax (linen) threads or material are only מקבל טומאה through a נגע in their natural colour, i.e. whitish, but skins in any natural colour; whether skins צבועים בידי אדם are also מקבל this טומאה is not quite certain — see כ״מ on הל׳ ט״צ 13, 1.

או בעור, must be similar to או בכל מלאכת העור, skins dressed ready for use, such as מלאכת העור .(ת״כ) ,עורות אהלים, are articles made from skins. In this עור differs from בגד inasmuch as there the simple spun thread, שתי or ערב is already מקבל טומאה — which explains the expression in our verse: לפשתים ולצמר, with צמר and פשתים, the simple threads are already responsive to a נגע, whereas עור must be finished ready for use.

V. 49. ירקרק או אדמדם, according to Negaim 11, 4: ירקרק שבירוקים ואדמדם שבאדומים, the greenest of greens (according to ר׳ אליעזר in the תוספתא (including?) wax and saffron yellow) and the reddest of reds. According to that, the לבן אדמדם ,לבנה אדמדמת, of v. 19, 24 & 42, would mean white shot with deep red (Rambam commentary thereon). — בבגד או בעור וגו׳, the constant repetition of these materials at each progressive step in these laws, here and in vv. 51, 52, 53, 57 & 58 is certainly not without reasons and should and does require explanation.

V. 51. בבגד :כי פשה הנגע בבגד וגו׳, anywhere in the garment, even if the פשיון is not בסמיך, but shows itself at a distance from the first spot. ממארת, according to תן בו מאירה ולא תהנה בו :ת״כ, the word ממארת, “treat it as accursed”, would mean that בגד המוחלט may not be used in any way whatsoever. Ezekiel 28,24 uses ממאיר as an epithet for a thorn or spike: סלון ממאיר. The derivation of the word is obscure. A בגד המוסגר is אסור בהנאה too, but becomes טהור and מותר if it is cut up into pieces smaller than ג׳ על ג׳ אצבעות, (Negaim 11, 12).
V. 52. להוציא את האמריות :ושרף את הבגד וגו׳, only the white parts of the garment have to be burnt, but not the coloured trimmings on the edges or hem.
V. 53 & 54. אם יראה וגו׳ לא פשה וגו׳, so that if עומד בראשון יסגיר, if it remained unaltered during the first period of isolation, it has to be shut up for a second period.

V. 55. לא הפך וגו׳, it has not changed its colour from ירקרק ואדמדם, if it had changed from ירקרק to אדמדם or vice versa, according to the חכמים it is not considered as הפך, (ת״כ and Negaim 11, 4). In this, that if עמד בשני ישדף, they, בגדים, differ from אדם (v. 6). — פחתת היא, from פחת, a pit, a hollow, deepening. According to ק״א on our verse in ת״כ:— “the colour is unchanged and the size also, but the place has become sunken, the נגע has eaten into the material”. — בקרחתו או בגבחתו: According to אלו השחקים :בקרחתו ,ת״כ, i.e. the worn-out places which have become threadbare; אלו החדשים :בגבחתו, the new places, i.e. those where the material is still “high” and fluffy. According to ראב״ד on קרחת ,ת״כ is simply the smooth (bald) reverse side of a garment, and גבחת, the top woolly side, so that any smooth worn part can be termed קרחת and the part which is still new גבחת.
V. 56. כהה, still ירוק or אדום, but no longer ירקרק or .(ק״א) ,אדמדם וקרע, the place affected by the נגע is to be tom out and a patch of another piece of the material inserted (ת״כ).
V. 57. ואם תראה עוד וגו׳, on the patch or elsewhere on the בגד, the garment has to be burnt, but in the latter case the patch itself need not be burnt, (Negaim 11, 6).

V. 58. אשד תכבס וגו׳ וכבס שנית וטהר, the first כבוס is washing for the possible removal of the נגע, which has to be done with שבעה סמנין in the prescribed order, as in the case of דם חטאת in Ch. 6,20, (Zebachim 95a); the second כבוס is טבילה in a Mikvah for the purpose of (ת״כ) ,טהרה.

So that בגדים become טמא through ירקרק or אדמדם, if these coloured spots remain for two weeks, or if they have spread at all after one week’s מיטמאין בשני שבועות ובשלשה סימנין, בירקרק ובאדמדם ובפשיון :הסגר, (Negaim 3, 7). We learn from Zebachim 49b that פריחה בכולו, if it spreads completely over the whole of the garment or cloth it is, similarly to נתקים, (see note on v. 40). טהור: See מל״מ on הל׳ ט״צ 12, 8.

V. 59. לטהרו או לטמאו. In Nazir 65b, the Halacha is given that כל ספק נגעים בתחלה טהור עד שלא נזקק לטומאה, משנזקק לטומאה ספקו טמא, where it concerns the transition from the state of טהרה to that of טומאה, then בתחלה עד שלא נזקק לטומאה, it can only be pronounced as טמא if the symptoms are quite definite and certain and there is no doubt whatsoever, but if there is any doubt, if the symptoms are not perfectly clear it is to be declared טהור. Moreover, it says further there, that in agreement with the teaching of ר׳ יהושע that, in such a case, it is still to be declared טהור even if the חזקת הגוף — the presumption that a condition remains in the status quo until proved to be the contrary — has been lost, as where the doubt is whether בהרת קדמה לשער לבן או שער לבן קדם לבהרת, where the presumption is for the former (see תוספות there and Nidda 19b). This Halacha is there referred back to our verse here where לטהרו is put before לטמאו indicating that in decisions on נגעים the tendency is to be towards טהרה And even if it is not absolutely certain that the Halacha completely adopts this teaching of ר׳ יהושע (see ר״ש on Negaim 4, 11 and רמב״ם הל׳ ט״צ 2, 9), the canon is established in all cases except two that כל ספק נגעים טהור (Negaim 5, 1). More, in Negaim 4, 4, the case is given where a man has two separate נגע spots at the same time, one only the size of a גריס, the other as large as a סלע. After the prescribed period of הסגר both are found to be the size of סלע, so that it is sure that one of them has spread, פשיון has taken place and the case should be declared מוחלט. But there is a doubt which one of the two places had grown and which had remained in its original size, and, as there is a doubt, the case is to be declared טהור! It is not sufficient that פשיון has occured one must be able to define the place precisely where it has spread. The ת״כ, too, on אותו in וטמא הכהן אותו, v. 29, says: את הודאי הוא מטמא ואינו מטמא את הספק. This general rule for the treatment of נגעים is one of the characteristic facts which guide us to a rational understanding of the whole idea of these laws concerning נגעים.
נגעים

No part of God’s Torah can serve, as much as this chapter on נגעים, to show the absolute folly of the erroneous idea of “the tendency of the Laws of Moses to be rules and regulations to be enforced for health and sanitary purposes”. On the surface, there are certainly sufficient facts in this chapter to give rise to such an illusion. Clearly it deals with diseases, with a disease which had always, (until quite recent times at least. I.L.), been considered contagious; those affected have to be isolated; for what purpose if not to prevent contagion; this sufficed to fix the character of these laws of Negaim as being sanitary health regulations and so stamp the functioning priests who administered them as doctors. And if, out of the whole register of human pathological diseases just this illness, “leprosy”, alone was picked out for these “police” regulations evidently it must have been just this disease, the most horrible one, from which the Jews mostly suffered, and the fairy tale of Tacitus that it was because of their leprosy that the Jews were driven out of Egypt, can not be so entirely without foundation!
But let us just look at these laws in their most prominent details and see if it is even possible to give them any sanitary character.

Already the fact that real leprosy, שחין, in itself is not מטמא at all, the “evil” leprosy, the “incurable Egyptian leprosy”, שחין רע ,שחין מצרים אשר לא תוכל להרפא, does not bring any state of טומאה, as it says in v. 18 of our chapter that the נגע טמא can only arise in שחין ונרפא, when the leprosy has already begun to heal and healthy skin has already formed over it; and the fact that the outbreak of the “leprosy” over the whole of the body, מראשו ועד רגליו, brings טהרה (v. 12 & 13) — which the “health theorists” take to be a sign that a violent acute attack which covers the whole body indicates a prompt immediate healing, and yet שחין מצרים, the very worst type of case, אשר לא תוכל להרפא, which has no cure is described as being מכף רגלך ועד קדקדך — even these simple facts must have made these theorists pause. Let us consider further: In verses 10, 15, 16 & 17, it repeatedly tells us that the appearance of מחיה, healthy flesh forming on the diseased spot, is a sign of טומאה, while its disappearance and the נגע breaking out in its place renders טהרה again; verse 12 tells us that no careful examination is required in the folds of the body, but only לכל מראה עיני הכהן, only in those parts of the body which are directly visible to the eye of the כהן; in Ch. 14,36, the priest is expressly ordered to remove everything out of the house before he makes his examination, as should he have to declare the house טמא, everything in it becomes likewise טמא, and if the purpose of the isolation is to prevent the spread of infection, it would be a very peculiar procedure to take out the suspectedly infected clothes, bedding, utensils, etc., out of consideration for the loss to the owner! Altogether the Halacha learns from this that these “sanitary officers” in priestly garb are to adopt a very considerate attitude in every way and always to give the benefit of any doubt, which in dealing with such a “dangerous”, “horrible” disease as “leprosy” would be perfectly senseless if their טמא declaration and the isolation which it entails were to be for the purpose of prevention of the spread of infection. When would such “police” activity and protective isolation be most demanded but where and when large masses of people gather and the unhindered mixing of the “leper” amongst the crowds would be a real danger of infection to whole families, even to the whole nation! And yet, just on such occasions, the inspection-functions of the priests were completely in abeyance. During the week of wedding gatherings, during the whole of the pilgrim festivals when the whole nation streamed into Jerusalem, altogether on any Sabbath or Festival, no נגע was examined, (see note on v. 14). Just in Jerusalem, leprosy in houses was not considered of any consequence at all (see note on Ch. 14,34). We have already drawn attention (on v. 59) to the rule that כל ספק נגעים בתחלה טהור, which prescribes a more lenient ruling than is generally applied to איסורים of the Torah, whereas, if it were dealing with diseases and precautions against contracting them, according to the principle that חמירא סכנתא מאיסורא, (Chulin 10a), the rule would be just for נגעים to impose a stricter, more rigorous practice. We have seen above that even in a case where there is absolute certainty of the existence of a symptom showing the נגע to have character of טומאה, if there is any doubt to which of two נגע spots on the same person the symptom applies, the טומאה declaration is not to be made! Further, as quoted on v. 46, it is only out of such cities which were surrounded by a wall at the time the Land was taken into possession, even if they had lost these walls later on, that a מצורע had to be expelled! Throughout the whole open country and in open towns, or even in towns which had been enclosed by walls later on, the מצורע was allowed to move freely among the people, and no quarantine was imposed to protect the people from this alleged infection of leprosy; only leprosy in clothes, had to be expelled from all towns or inhabited places everywhere! consider also that all these laws only apply to the Jewish inhabitants of Israel; No non-Jew became טמא by any נגע, his נגע was not examined, no expulsion or isolation was imposed on him, and even if he became a Jew, no נגע which he had contracted before his conversion was of any consequence (see on v. 2). Equally so, none of these laws apply to the appearance of any leprosy on the clothes or house of a non-Jew while these were in his possession (see on v. 47).

These, and similar considerations make it quite impossible to think that this chapter deals with sanitary or prophylactic measures against disease, or that we have to regard our כהנים — regarding whom, in any case, no trace of any reference to remedial measures can be found in the whole chapter — as functioning in the health or medical care of the people.

And, as a matter of fact, the symptoms described in our chapter, have nothing at all in common with the diseases which are described in books of medical science on skin diseases under the heading of “Lepra”, leprosy. Whereas these, all start with an inflammatory swelling which makes the skin darker in colour, our נגעים consist solely of white patches, of greater or lesser bleaching of the skin, at which ת״כ expressly says there is no swelling or raising of the skin. Sforno — who was a doctor, — in his commentary on the Torah remarks on the complete difference between these נגעים and the dreadful diseases which he found described under the name of leprosy in scientific medical writings. We had, accordingly, long been completely convinced that the sequestration and expulsion which the Torah prescribes for a מצורע is in no way meant to be a protection against any possible infection, when we read in the journal “Ausland” No. 14, 1868, that a commission had been appointed by the British Government to investigate the terrible increase in the number of cases of the quite common occurrence of leprosy in the colonies, and their report was reproduced in that Journal. The “Report on Leprosy by the Royal College of Physicians” stated that the investigation resulted in the finding that leprosy even in its most terrible form is not at all infectious. “The all-important question for the Government” the report continues, “is whether this disease is contagious or not. There can be no doubt that the Jews considered it to be so, and that the strictest quarantine was imposed upon those who contracted it. Nevertheless, it seems probable from several indications that the Jews of old classed all skin diseases as leprous, and accordingly people who were affected by the contagious diseases of modern Europe, such as measles, scarlet fever or smallpox, were included in the laws of quarantine for leprosy. It is a remarkable fact, moreover, that present-day Jews seem to be less liable to the attacks of contagious illnesses than their European neighbours, which may be due to a trace which still remains from those ceremonious practices which exercised such great influence on the physical forces and energies of the ancient Jews. Be that as it may, the practically unanimous conviction of our investigating reporters from all parts of the world is: the disease is not infectious”.
We have seen that the widespread view that the biblical injunctions regarding sequestration are regulations to prevent infection rests entirely on a mistaken premise.

If then the understanding of the Negaim-laws as being sanitary-police regulations must definitely be relegated to the realm of fairy-tales, let us turn to the Torah itself, which in any case, leaves us in no possible doubt whatever as to in which light it wishes these laws to be regarded. In Deut. 24,8, in the midst of a list of laws referring entirely to social matters and all dealing with the respect due to human worth and benevolent consideration for the happiness and well-being of others, we come across the warning: השמר בנגע צרעת וגו׳, “Take heed in the plague of leprosy that thou observe diligently and do according to all that the priests, the Levites, shall teach you, as I have commanded them so shall ye observe to do. Remember what God, your God, did unto Miriam on the way when ye went out of Egypt”. By this, the meticulous observation of the laws given in our chapter here is made the conscientious duty of every single individual. From the term השטר is specially derived the prohibition of removal of the נגע by surgical or other means, although, or rather because, מן התורה thereby all טומאה and isolation ceases, (see v. 46, a fact which incidentally again excludes any precautionary health motives for the sequestration. For, if this were the case, the removal of the נגע would be most desirable as we are told that the necessity for sequestration ceases thereby) as well as the demand for the exact carrying out of all the positive commands given here. Both, the negative command, the prohibition, and the positive demand, are then supported by a reference to a certain incident in the life of Miriam, the Prophetess, which incident is to remain for ever in national remembrance. This remembrance clearly refers to the incident recorded in Numb. XII. Miriam had spoken slander about Moses, and following this לשון הרע had become “leprous” and had been expelled from the camp for seven days, and there this leprosy and this expulsion had been explained as being a sign of, and for her to take to heart, God’s displeasure at her behaviour. “If her father”, so runs God’s reply to Moses’s prayer that his sister should be cured, “if her father had so spat out before her, would she not remain ashamed for seven days? Let her be secluded outside the camp for seven days, thereafter let her be received again”. ואביה ירק ירק בפניה, a sign of disgust, as a sign of a father’s displeasure mounting to contempt, God says, the צרעת He sends is to be taken. Now, this punishing stroke was sent as a result of a social sin, a sin, which, as is there shown, consisted of both slander and over-rating oneself, presumption, conceit. If then every נגע צרעת in the future that shows itself on any member of the Jewish Nation is to recall this experience of Miriam, every such נגע צרעת is to be taken as a punitive admonition for social misbehaviour; and the expulsions מחוץ למחנה, out of the national circle which has the Sanctuary of the Torah as its centre, has, — as it says with Miriam — no other purpose or reason than הכלם, than to let oneself be permeated with the consciousness of one’s complete unworthiness — (Whereas בוש means finding oneself deceived regarding something one had expected in the future, one’s expectations, החפיר regarding a misunderstood past, הכלם is the feeling brought about by becoming conscious of present loss of worthiness). The expulsion tells the מנוגע, the one who is affected by צרעת, literally the one who is touched (נגוע. I.L.), by the Finger of God, that he has forfeited the merit of remaining in the social circle of God’s Sanctuary.

And actually we find that the teaching of our חכמים always takes “Negaim” as being a punishment sent by God, primarily for sins of the tongue, לשון הרע, but then generally for the cardinal sins of social life, of which they ennumerate seven. It says in Berachoth 5b: כל מי שיש בו אחד מארבעה מראות נגעים הללו אינן אלא מזבח כפרה, “Being affected by one of these four appearances is nothing other than an altar for atonement”. And, in Arachin 16b: מה נשתנה מצורע שאמרה תורה בדד ישב מחוץ למחנה מושבו הוא הבדיל בין איש לאשתו בין איש לרעהו לפיכך אמרה תורה בדד ישב וגו׳, “Why just for the מצורע is it ordained, ‘he shall dwell apart, outside the camp is his dwelling to be’? He caused separation beween man and wife, between friend and friend, therefore is he, too, to be separated from everybody, let him remain alone, outside the camp”; מה נשתנה מצורע שאמרה תורה יביא שתי צפרים לטהרתו, אמר הקב״ה, הוא עשה מעשה פטיט, לפיכך יביא קרבן פטיט, “Why just for the מצורע is it ordained that in his offering to regain טהרה he is to represent his personality by two birds? He sinned by chattering, therefore, is he to bring a twittering offering”. Similarly in :ויקרא רבה א״ר יהושע בן לוי, חמש תורות כתובות במצורע: זאת תורת נגע צרעת וגו׳, זאת תהיה תורת ,,המצורע״, תורת ,,המוציא רע״, ללמדך שכל האומר לשון הרע עובר על חמשה חומשי תורה, where play is made on the word מצורע as, phonetically, being able to be split up into מוציא רע, to give its meaning as slanderer. So also in Arachin 15b: זאת תהיה תורת המצורע, זאת תהיה תורתו של מוציא שם רע.

Elsewhere, in Arachin 16a, seven social sins and bad habits are reckoned as a consequence of which Negaim are sent: ,על שבעה דברים נגעים באין על לשון הרע ועל שפיכות דמים ועל שבועת שוא ועל גלוי עריות ועל גסות הרוח ועל הגול ועל צרות העין, as a result of the sins of slander, of spilling of blood, of perjury, of sexual immorality, of pride, of robbery and of unkind selfishness. In ויקרא רבה on פ׳ מצורע, the following are reckoned:— עינים רמות לשון שקר, וידים שופכות דם נקי, לב חורש מחשבות און, רגלים ממהרות לרוץ לרעה, יפיח כזבים ,עד שקר and משלח מדנים בין אחים; a lying tongue, proud eyes, hands spilling innocent blood, a heart pondering on thoughts of violence, feet always ready to run for evil purposes, spreading lies about, and bringing about quarrels between brothers and giving false witness. These are the six and seven things which are described in Prov. 6,16 as being hated by God, and abominated by His Holy Nature: שש הנה שנא ה׳ ושבע תועבות נפשו. And the division into six and seven is explained ,שביעית קשה כנגד כולן ואי זה, זה משלח מדנים, that the seventh, bringing and causing discord, (i.e. לשון הרע), is designated as the one which is worse than all the others put together. And, as a matter of fact, spreading slander, which does bring about the spiritual death of respect and love even between brothers and sisters, does combine in its consequences all the other imperfections and sins. And inasmuch as these imperfections and sins are not mentioned in the abstract but referred to the various organs of the body which are misused in practising them, it does not say רום עינים etc., but עינים רמות etc., it is the eye, the mouth, the hand, the heart, the foot; in short, the whole person who, instead of using organs which are given to him for obtaining and practising modesty, truth, doing good, justice, spreading kindness, truth and peace, has made himself the bearer and spreader of the very opposite of all these and has shown himself as the object of hate and abomination of God, Who, accordingly, sends him the mark of His deep displeasure and thereby dismisses him from the social purlieus of the Sanctuary of His Torah until הכלם, until he comes to a sense of true self-judgment.
