When we are told of Miriam, that: ויחר אף ה׳ בם וילך והענן סר מעל האהל והנה מרים מצורעת כשלג, everybody is told, everybody on whose self, on whose clothing or house, a נגע appears, that this נגע is a sign that his social behaviour has invoked God’s deepest displeasure and that God’s protecting and blessing-giving Presence no longer allows him to find a place in His circle.

Now, looking at the laws contained in this chapter from the point of view which the Torah itself indisputably shows us, we should like to try and explain them from that angle. It starts off by addressing us by the name אדם. The introductory words: אדם כי יהיה וגו׳ (v. 2), are only to be found in two other cases: אדם כי יקריב וגו׳ (Ch. 1,2), אדם כי ימות באהל וגו׳ (Ch. 19,14). In both these cases, the instructions for the offerings, and the laws of טומאת אהל, the idea of the name אדם recalls to our mind the conception of Man in the full value of what he was created to be, so that we can grasp the meaning of those laws from that conception. Here, too, the words אדם כי יהיה בעור בשרו may make us consider the object hit by the נגע, namely עור בשרו, in its relation to what the appellation אדם means. (Elsewhere Hirsch has explained that עור, the skin, is derived from the root עור, to be awake, or awaken, as it is that organ of the body which is sensitive to, and responds to external impressions, by means of which Man first gets his impression of the nature of the materials of the world about him; he there also pithily shows the relation of the term עור for a blind man, literally a “skin-man” who is dependent on his sense of touch through his skin for all his knowledge. I.L.). The object affected by the נגע is “עור בשר אדם״, is עור, the organ which takes up impressions of the world, עור belonging to the בשר, to the body which was given to “אדם״, to “the representative of God”, as a “herald” as a means of accomplishing his high mission on earth. It is an אדם who is to see in the “Nega”, the עור of בשרו touched by the Finger of God. It is an אדם, a creature created only to carry out the Will of God, with every action of his being, to nurture Truth and Right on earth, as the representative of God (see Hirsch on אדם in Gen. 1,26. I.L.), who is admonished by the Finger of God, on that organ of his body which connects him with the world, into what a contrast to what it was meant to be, his life has fallen. “White” spots, all of them עמוקות מעור בשר אדם בינוני, all of them paler than ordinary human skin, God has declared (v. 3 et seq.), as announcing His displeasure and has given exact details to differentiate them from other appearances of ordinary skin diseases. The skin turning white can indicate the partial “death” of a person from whom the animating nearness to God has departed מצורע חשוב כמת, (see notes on Numb. 12,12), or in a similar way could mean an הלבנת פנים, the deepest “shameing”, “putting to shame”. It has only this meaning when it is בגלוי, as it puts it לכל מראה העין, where on a free surface it strikes the eye, and it must be of the required size and on a flat surface, not in a fold of skin. (Vv. 2, 3 & 12). For they are sent to strike the eye. And not in themselves, not by simply being there — as all other forms of bodily conditions of טומאה as זב וזבה do — do they make the person טמא. It is only the declaration of a כהן — a servant and representative of the Sanctuary of the Torah by birth — that makes the person טמא, shuts him out, by his declaration, from the Sanctuary and its קדשים, and — as is the case by no other טמא at all — from the civil society which, on the basis of its Torah, forms a compact Jewish community, with the Sanctuary as its centre. A נגע is nothing but an injuction to the כהן to declare in the name of the Sanctuary of the Torah that the person affected is unworthy of the Sanctuary and of its national circle (v. 2 & 3). Only מצורע has to be משתלח חוץ משלש מחנות, expelled from the closed-in national circle of Jewish society. For it is just social faults and sins that God’s sign on his body show him. The motive for this expulsion which we have seen not to be precaution against infection of a disease, is just as little precaution against spreading טומאה. For all other טמאים — who could spread טומאה just as easily — are allowed to stay quite unhindered in מחנה ישראל and even the מצורע has to be expelled only from עיירות מוקפות חומה מימות יהושע בן נון, (v. 46), from such cities which at the time the land was taken into possession were closed-in cities, and as such, characterised towns as מחנה ישראל, (see Ch. 25,29), proof enough that this expulsion is purely the consequence of the social perverseness which his נגע shows him, and that this is the character in which it is clearly and definitely to be interpreted. That, too, is why the declaration of the כהן has the character of the verdict of a judge — מקיש נגעים לריבים — and why, in a similar manner, for נגעים too, כהן קרוב is barred, is פסול, (see v. 2). From this point of view we can also perfectly understand the postponement of ראית נגעים during a רגל, during the seven days of the celebration of a wedding etc. (v. 14), if we regard the priestly examination and its consequences as a moral punishment and a measure for procuring betterment. The very existence of a נגע which requires an examination must already awaken in the mind of the person affected, thoughts of the possibility of his unworthiness and of the dread consequences of it. And if he has to seek the cause of his unworthiness primarily in his social behaviour, then, such days of such intensified social intercourse, as national festivals, holidays etc., offer the most suitable oppurtunities for him to rest and improve his attitude, his feelings, his conversation and his actions in his contact with his fellow-men; and by so bettering himself bring about such an alteration of his נגע that he will be able to face the coming examination of the כהן without fear of an unfavourable verdict.

But there are two stages: הסגר, a testing period, and החלט, the positive definite stage. טומאה and expulsion are, as noted on v. 4, exactly the same for both stages, only the outward disfigurements, פריעה and פרימה are only imposed for the מוחלט, and only when returning cured from the החלט-stage do the תגלחת וצפרים regulations, described in the next chapter, apply. And indeed, the enforced loneliness of the isolating הסגר weeks may well be suited for exercising a most beneficial influence and bring the culprit to a serious contemplation and examination of how he has hitherto behaved in word, feelings and acts in his social contact with his fellow men from whom he is now separated, and so induce him towards a serious change in his attitude and feelings towards them, and to seriously make up his mind to improve, and so to emerge from this preliminary testing period already in a “pure” state. Hence also any possible changes in the נגע which may occur during this testing period do not come into consideration at all, the כהן has to decide only on the condition at the end of the הסגר.

The priest has to decide for הסגר at once at the first examination provided the נגע has the requisite size and is of the requisite shade of colour. The symptoms which necessitate a declaration for החלט are: מחיה ,שער לבן or פשיון. The first two symptoms, שער לבן or מחיה, can be present at the first examination בתחלה and necessitate immediate פשיון .החלט, the spreading of the נגע can, of course, only be recognised after the first or second week of הסגר, i.e., בסוף, (v. 4). That פשיון, the spreading of the נגע, indicates an intensification of the נגע-character is easily understandable, but it is more difficult to see why שער לבן or מחיה should indicate such intensification.

Perhaps the following may contain something akin to the truth, The skin is the general sensorium of the body, it is the means of the reception of impressions out of the surrounding world. A blemish that the Finger of God, sends on this sensorium as a “נגע צרעת״, as an external sign of inner foulness, (see v. 2), is a sign that the person affected is morally unhealthy in his comprehension of the surrounding world. He has failed to absorb the impressions of truth, justice and goodness of his world, and the way he looks on this world is, accordingly, neither true nor just non-good. Hair may be considered physiologically, actually, to be the opposite of skin. It is the protective covering of the skin, protecting against and keeping off injurous contacts. Now, transporting this idea of hair from the physiological to the psychic sphere, the spreading of the נגע into the hair would express the idea that not only good and true impressions are lacking, (the skin losing its natural colour. I.L.), but that positively bad ones which should be kept away are finding entrance, (the hair losing its natural colour. I.L.). Be that as it may, just as פשיון being an extension, spreading further in the skin, shows an intensification of the character of the נגע, so is הפיכת שער לבן also a פשיון, but in another direction, it is an extension of the bleaching reaching even into the hair. Hence also שער לבן שקדם לבהרת and שער פקודה, (see v. 3), are טהור. The first, of course, has no significance at all, and the latter, too, can not be taken as showing any increase or intensification of the נגע, which is now under consideration. More difficult is the understanding of מחיה as a sign of מחיה .החלט is a place in the centre of the נגע which has either remained healthy, or which has become healthy again and just this is a sign that necessitates החלט! In v. 11, it says referring to שער לבן ,מחיה by itself had already been given as a סימן החלט. In v. 3, (without this extra reason), צרעת נושנת היא וגו׳ לא יסגרנו כי טמא הוא. This may give us the clue that מחיה it to be taken as a sign that the working of the tendency to betterment, which otherwise is tried to be obtained by הסגר, has here already failed to succeed, and החלט has, accordingly, to be pronounced. And, as a matter of fact, מחיה מבוצר בתיך הנגע, (the מחיה in the centre, surrrounded on all sides by the נגע, v. 11, I.L.), does very well express this idea. At the very start of the moral disintegration (נגע), his better feelings (מחיה), had fought against it in vain, or, after the נגע had already broken out, his better feelings (מחיה) themselves awakened but were not strong enough to overcome the evil. The good, the healthy, the pure stands imprisoned in the midst of the evil. The reason that מחיה has no effect on cases of שחין ומכוה, could be that in those cases מחיה does not seem to be a reaction against the נגע, but is in relation to the שחין or מכוה, which is taken to be in the process of healing (v. 24).

A law which strikes one as particularly peculiar it that the spreading of the נגע completely over the whole of the body annuls the כלו :טומאה הפך לבן טהור. But if such total spreading occurs during a normal condition, when the person is in an ordinary condition of טהרה, it has to be declared as טמא requiring either הסגר or הפורח מן הטמא טהור מן הטהור טמא :החלט (v. 13). Looked at from the point of view of the moral purpose of נגעים, this law could express, in a most significant manner the following idea:— isolation, החלט ,הסגר, altogether the exclusion of טומאה from association with the Sanctuary or from the society that bases itself on it, can be hoped to bring about effective contemplation and betterment only for as long as the consciousness of the truer and better state of affairs is still fresh in the mind and so can be expected to put a fight against the wrong and bad tendency. So that if פרח בכלו — even a complete swing to the bad — occurs suddenly in the midst of ordinary “pure” association with the Sanctuary and Society, בתחלה, if it is quite a new attack, הסגר is to be pronounced; if לאחר פטור it is a recurrence of an old previous attack from which he has been cured and returned to the community החלט must be declared. The thoughts of מקדש וקדשיו and of the מחנה ישראל, from which he has suddenly been torn, accompany him in his enforced isolation and may work on him to his betterment. But if this פריחה בכלו occurs when he is already isolated during הסגר or החלט, then it expresses the fact that he has entirely lost his better feelings so that there is no hope of betterment through his isolation. The טומאה-declaration is accordingly suspended, he is again allowed free contact and intercourse with מקדש וקדשיו and מחנה ישראל until a return of בשר החי announces the beginning of regained better feelings. He is then returned to the מוחלט-condition to work out on himself the completion of his education, back to morality, in isolation (vv. 12 & 17).

The special modifications in the laws for נגעי ראש וזקן are probably to be attributed to the nature and special importance of these parts of the body, (the cerebrum, cerebellum, face, etc. I.L.), and could be explained as expressing similar ideas to the laws of נגעי בשר.

The laws for נגעי בגדים are characteristic. They are much stricter than נגעי אדם. Whereas נגעי אדם only apply to ישראל, and, e.g. a נגע which a גר has brought over from his נכרי-condition is of no consideration at all, a garment or cloth taken into Jewish possession from that of a נכרי which has symptoms of a נגע requires examination by a priest, יראה בתחלה, possibly even בגדי גר תושב come under the laws of נגעים. A בגד המנוגע which, as regards החלט ,הסגר and טומאה, has exactly the same character as אדם, regarding שלוח מחנה is even more חמור inasmuch as it has to be sent out of all cities, even those which are not מוקפות חומה (v. 47). Further, whereas a man whose נגע remains unaltered after the second week of הסגר, becomes טהור with the נגע mark still on him, the possibility for a בגד to be טהור retaining the נגע mark on it does not exist. If it has remained unaltered after the second הסגר, it must at once be burnt, (v. 55). Also the idea בגד is extended to the mere thread, שתי וערב, and remains, in the case of material woven from the specific typical garment materials, צמר ופשתים, even if it is made up into sails or anything else.

The point of view which the Torah itself has given us with regard to the laws of Negaim in general, can bring these laws, too, nearer to our comprehension. It is above all social misbehaviour and sins which a נגע sent by God, on himself, his clothes or his house, is meant to bring home to a person in all its weight its judgment by God. Now, clothes are quite particularly the expression of the social character of Man. Above all, in the Jewish way of thinking, as we have already repeatedly had occasion to remark, “clothes” and “clothing oneself” indicate character and the character one adopts. A blemish sent by God on a person’s clothes indicates more than anything else a social corruption lying under God’s deepest censure. We think we can very well understand that it is just when a נגע is on a garment that the Torah bans it with the utmost severity from the social circles of its people, perhaps draws even the גר תושב, regarding נגעי בגדים, within the scope of its laws but at any rate subjects any garment that comes over into Jewish possession, to the נגעים-laws. For, the גר תושב, in social matters, does form an integral part of the Nation, and social justice does form an essential part of the Noachian Laws which are binding also on a נכרי. And because just in נגעי בגדים the meaning of the נגע appears in the clearest, most expressive clarity, and the warning which נגעים give to the social irreproachableness expected is most loudly preached. The Torah does not limit this warning only to an actual garment, but makes this idea appear already in the mere thread to be made into cloth and retains it even if the “garment” material is made up into something else. That is probably also why in every verse of the law of נגעי בגדים it is always specially repeated again and again, בבגד או בשתי או בערב או בעור לכל אשר יעשה העור למלאכה. Just in this, in this extension of the conception בגד, which is the heading of these particular laws — והבגד כי יהיה בו נגע צרעת וגו׳, the extension to every form of the specific garment-material, — is the deep, important meaning of these laws of נגעי בגדים expressed. But צמר ופשתים are, everywhere in the Torah exclusively the specific materials for human clothing, and so it is with them, too, that the conception בגד begins already in the mere threads. But here the conception “clothing” is extended to עור also, but there it only begins with skins worked ready for use, (לכל אשר יעשה העור למלאכה. I.L.). פשתים, and in the vast majority of cases, צמר too, in their natural colour are white, the colour of purity, and so already by their original colour represent the “purity of character” in which Man should clothe himself — בכל עת יהיו בגדיך לבנים — (Prov. 9,8; see Sabbath 153,a) — and so the laws of נגעי בגדים fix only the natural white linen or woollen garments for giving warning of the unblemished state of Man’s social character which is demanded by God. Finally, in the case of נגעי אדם, the special reference to the social side of human life was to be demonstrated by limiting the expulsion of those affected to עיירות מוקפות חומה. But in בגדים, this reference is quite clear by itself through the בגד idea, and hence, its expulsion is prescribed out of all human habitations. (The choice of only certain things is symbolic laws — as here only cities which were walled at the time the land became the Land of Israel, even if they are no longer so, in שעטנז, only to mixtures of wool and linen etc. etc., — is always made in the Torah, to make it perfectly clear that the law is not referring to anything real or concrete, but that the idea of a social community, or of the interference with God’s great Law of למינו etc. etc., is purely symbolic to act as a reminder and deterrent of the actual thing. I.L.)

One law could appear to be in contradiction to the way the Torah itself shows us to take its laws of נגעים. It is this, that even a תינוק בן יום אחד, a child from the first day of its life, can be affected by a נגע with all its consequences (v. 2). The purpose of a moral warning and of improvement, which the Torah has in mind with its נגעים prescriptions, would, we should have thought, have restricted giving any meaning to a נגע, to an age of sufficient maturity, for its being able to be called to account. But children, in the age of their immature dependence are most intimately part of their parent’s personality; they are the tender shoots of humanity which should grow on the foundation and example of their parents’ lives to their calling of being likenesses of God. Just as a נגע on garment or house is a warning admonition to its owner, so, and ever so much more deeply piercing, is a נגע on the forehead of their innocent little child, the most impressive terrible warning to the parents to examine themselves and consider what picture of life their social behaviour will serve as an example to their child. The נגע-mark on their child and its declaration as טמא with its consequences constitute the most solemn warning to the parents: “for your child’s sake, better yourself, for the sake of your children become good”. For the social imperfections which will cling to your children, you are accountable — and most certainly a נגע on the brow of their innocent child is a much more effective warning from God than if the נגע had come on their own persons.

We have now only to consider what influence the declaration of טמא and its consequences is likely to have on the מנוגע. The very fact that he does not automatically become טמא by the bodily condition itself, unlike זב ,זבה ,נדה etc., where טומאה יוצאת עליהן מגופן, but that his טומאה only starts with the declaration of the כהן, and is entirely dependent on that, tells him that his טומאה does not emanate from his bodily condition but that it has its roots in his moral behaviour, in his relation to the Torah, the Sanctuary of which the priest represents — the priest, on whose declaration his נגע awaits as a cipher from God, which the priest is appointed to decipher. It is no נבלה and no זב and no מת and it is not the skin disease itself which presents a condition similar to these which produces the condition of טומאה and its consequences for him. But it is more than these. On account of his social misbehaviour the servant of God’s Sanctuary of the Torah has to declare him as נבלה and as מת — cf. נְבֵלָה and נְבָלָה and the sentence רשעים אפילו בחייהן קרואין מתים, he is, like מטמא במגע ובמשא :נבלה; more, he is מטמא משכב ומושב, like or at least, similarly to זב ,זבה (v. 6, see note on Ch. 15,4), he is, like מטמא בביאה ,מת, at which the fact that a מחיצת עשרה טפחים is sufficient to exclude it, stamps this טומאה with just the character of having social meaning; and — which occurs at no other טומאה, he is isolated and expelled from society, הסגר and שלוח מחנה — and only by effecting a change in himself before God, can he expect the sign that the doors of society and the Sanctuary are to be reopened to him.

If we now look at the נגעים-laws in their totality, we see the grandest institution of the most direct management of God, watching over and educating every single individual; and in the Jewish State of God, we see social sins and misdemeanours brought out into the light of publicity, punished and rectified, things like pride, lies, greed, calumny, etc., which otherwise escape all recognition by human tribunals, but for which in the Jewish state of God, God himself, appears as accuser and witness. So the ת״כ comments on Ch. 14,35: ובא אשר לו הבית והגיד לכהן לאמר, לאמר, יאמר לו הכהן דברי כיבושין: בני, אין הנגעים באים אלא על לה״ר וכו׳.

V. 2. זאת תהיה וגו׳. The word תהיה gives the character of מעכב, of sine qua non, indispensability to all the objects mentioned in the following ordinances as well as to the order in which they are to be brought. Accordingly, ארבעה מינין שבמצורע מעכבין זה את זה, the four objects prescribed in v. 4, are mutually necessary to each other, should any one of them be missing, the whole act is invalid and without meaning (Menachoth 27a). Equally so, הקדים שמן למתן דם וכו׳, מתן בהונות למתן שבע וכו׳, if the procedure described in v. 16 has been performed before that of v. 14, or that of v. 17 before that of v. 16, (ibid 5a). תורת המצורע, we have already repeatedly learnt that the term תורת is a generalising one (see Ch. 7,37). Here, too, the expression is generalising. The following institution applies to every מצורע without exception, בין גדול בין קטן, even to little children who have no consciousness at all of the proceedings, also the offering prescribed in v. 40 et seq., which is necessary to obtain the state of purity to be allowed contact with קדשים and the Sanctuary. Hence the significant canon: הכל צריכין דעת חוץ ממחוסרי כפרה, all offerings can only be brought with the understanding, and by the will, of the person who has to bring them, only the offerings which have to be brought by זב וזבה יולדת ומצורע, which are necessary to obtain the required state of purity for מקדש וקדשיו are valid even if brought without דעת בעלים, can even be brought for other people without their being previously informed: שהרי אדם מביא קרבן על בניו ובנותיו הקטנים, (Nedarim 35a). If we consider the fact that all other offerings do not effect anybody but the person who brings them — it is his sin which is to be atoned for, his acts, his life, which are to be brought near to God — whereas the effect of טומאה and טהרה does essentially go beyond the person who is טמא or טהור, any object he touches becomes טמא not only for him but for the whole Jewish community, altogether the idea of טומאה, which arises from his condition, has to be rectified not only for him but for everybody who is summoned to טהרה, we may be able to find the reason for this differentiation.

ביום טהרתו, this too, the act of the purification of a מצורע is also limited to day time, ביום, and is thereby raised of the sphere of merely physical meaning and transferred to that of the free-willed human activties (Megilla 20b). (ת״כ) ,שלא ישהה :ביום טהרתו והובא אל הכהן, as soon as the נגע has altered its appearance so that it could be declared טהור, the declaration is not to be postponed. The transition from ימי הסגר to טהרה depends on the completion of the weeks. But the cessation of the החלט-condition has no fixed time. At any time, as soon as the נגע has sufficiently changed, he can regain טהרה, his צרעת is תלויה בגופו, whereas :מצורע מוסגר אין צרעתו תלויה בגופו אלא בימים, (Megilla 8b).
V. 3. ויצא :ויצא הכהן וגו׳, only a כהן who may be inside the מחנה is qualified for טהרת מצורע, but (ת״כ) ,אין מצורע מטהר את מצורע.
והנה נרפא וגו׳, it need not have completely disappeared, as long as it has lost the טומאה-symptoms described in the previous chapter (ת״כ).

V. 4. לשם מיטהר בין איש בין אשה בין קטן וכו׳ :ולקח למטהר, the birds are to be destined quite generally for the purpose of this purification, but need not be specifically assigned to any special person. They are not to be used as offerings and do not represent any definite person, accordingly שינוי בעלים does not apply to them (ת״כ).

מצותן שיהו שוות במראה ובקומה ובדמים ולקיחתן כאחת :שתי צפרים, they should both look alike, be of the same size and value and taken at the same time (cf. Ch. 16,7). But all this is only למצוה and is not מעכב, (Negaim 14,5). In ת״כ, on Ch. 14,53: ושלח את הצפוד החיה אל מחוץ לעיר ר׳ יוסי הגלילי ,אל פני השדה explains: צפור שחיה חוץ לעיר, ואיזו זו, זו דרור, that this is a species of bird that has not really settled in cities, it is the bird known as דרור. In Sabbath 106b, this bird is given more detailed characteristics, it is a bird שאינה מקבלת מרות, that does not become tamed, דתנא דבי רבי ישמעאל, למה נקרא שמה צפור דרור, מפני שדרה בבית כבשדה, its name indicates that “it lives in a house as in the fields”, i.e. that it retains its wild freedom in the house as in the fields, it does not yield to capture and taming. Rashi takes it in Betza 24a, that its name is derived from דור, “to live”, but it seems more probable, as מל״מ on הל׳ טומאת צרעת 2,1 says, that it means “freedom”, from וקראתם דרור in Ch. 25,10. In Chulin 62a, the bird for טהרת מצורע is called the סנונית, which is usually taken to mean the swallow.

חיות טהורות. According to Chulin 139b, the term צפור itself is used solely for “pure” birds and the adjective טהורות here makes the demand that it must also be מותר אכילה, e.g. not צפורי עיר הנדחת; and חיות demands that שחיין ראשי איברים שלה, that its principle limbs are not mutilated.

עץ ארז: a piece of cedar wood one cubit long and “a quarter of the thickness of the foot of a bedstead”, כרביע כרע המטה, and with cedar leaves at the top, (ת״כ) ,ובראשה טרף. But in Negaim 14,6, the latter is not accepted. The ר״ש in Negaim has a different version of the ת״כ, but quotes this last law from תוספתא.

ושני תולעת: wool dyed with dye extracted from a worm, supposed to be carmine.. The expression לשון, (Negaim 14,1), seems to indicate that the wool was unspun. From Menachoth 42b, we learn that this שני תולעת as well as the תכלת for ציצית, had to be dyed specially for these purposes, לשמה, so that טעימה, if a piece of wool had been dipped into the dye to test the shade, it would be פסולה; more, even טעמה פסלה, if one dipped a piece of wool into the saucepan of dye to test the colour, the whole contents of the pot becomes unfit for שני תולעת.
ואזוב, it must be the plant which is known simply as אזוב, and not one which has an additional name, (e.g. the spreading hyssop. I.L.), (ת״כ) אזוב, ולא אזוב יון וכו׳ ולא כל אזוב שיש לו שם לווי.

V. 5. (ת״כ) ,הברורה שבשתים :את הצפור האחת, the better, the “most choice” of the two, or perhaps ברור, the most “certain decided” of the two, the one who has the characteristic signs of the species most definitely marked.

מה מים חיים שלא נעשתה בהן מלאכה אף בלי —: אל כלי חרש על מים חיים שלא נעשתה בו מלאכה, (Sota 15b), the vessel is to be as “fresh” as the water, must not have been used, פיילי של חרס חדשה, a new earthenware basin (ibid). שלעולם נובעים ולא פוסקים :מים חיים, which always flow and never fail or dry up, (ר״ש, Negaim 14,1).
After the bird has been killed, it is buried there and then, as it is אסור בהנאה, (Negaim ibid).

V. 6. (ת״כ) ,מלמד שהוא מפרישה לעצמה :את הצפור החיה יקח אותה וגו׳. Although, as remarked on v. 2: ארבעה מינין שבמצורע מעכבין זה את זה, and so must be regarded as forming one united unit, nevertheless the bird is left by itself and the other three items are tied together in one bunch: נטל עץ ארז ואזוב ושני תולעת וכרכן בשירי הלשון, (Negaim ibid), the end of the wool which hangs down is used to tie three items together; hence also the wording of the text: וטבל אותם ואת הצפוד החיה וגו׳, for the dipping he takes the three tied together and the bird all together in his hand (ibid). — בדם וגו׳ על המים החיים: the proportion of the water to the blood must be such that both are noticeable in the mixture. For that, one רביעית of water, was fixed, which quantity was estimated not to disappear even in the blood of the largest צפור דרור, and in which the blood of the smallest remains visible, אין לך גדולה שמדחת את המים, ואין לך קטנה שנדחית מפני המים.
V. 7. לאחר ידו, ויש אומרים על מצחו :והזה על המטהר וגו׳, these sprinklings were made on-to the back of the hand, or, according to other opinions, on the forehead, (Negaim ibid).

ושלח את הצפוד וגו׳. In v. 53 it says: ושלח את הצפוד החיה אל מחוץ לעיר אל פני השדה, and the Gemora in Kiddushin 57b, comments on that: ,שדה שלא יעמוד ביפו ויזרקנה לים, בגבת ויזרקנה למדבר, ושלא יעמוד חוץ לעיר ויזרקנה בתוך העיר, אלא כל שעומד בעיר ויזרקנה חוץ לחומה. The bird, accordingly, must be sent outside the city, and over worked fields, not over the sea and not over bare or uncultivated land. As the preceding acts (the sprinkling etc. I.L.), had to be done outside the city, the bird had first to be taken into the city to be sent out of it, (תוספות ibid). שלחה וחזרה, חוזר ומשלחה אפילו מאה פעמים, if the bird flies back into the city, he must send it away again and again (הל׳ טומאת צרעת ,רמב״ם 11, 1, according to תוספתא). Once it has been sent completely out of the city, it may be eaten. כשדה, מה שדה מותרת אף האי נמי מותרת, it belongs again to the free open fields and may be considered part of them, for, as רבא says: לא אמרה תורה שלח לתקלה, the Torah can not possibly mean to order us to send something which is אסור באכילה away into the open, without any sign, so that somebody could come to eat forbidden food without knowing it, (Kiddushin 67b).

V. 8. וכבס וגו׳ וגלח וגו׳ ורחץ וגו׳. In the days of חלוטו, also called ימי גמרו — out of which he is now to come — he was ,מטמא במגע ובמשא משכב ומושב ובביאה. In the stage of ימי ספירו, into which he is now transferred, he is still מטמא במגע, but is freed from all the other טומאות. So that at the end of ימי חלוטו, he has to have טבילה of himself and his clothes for these, (Negaim 14, 2: זכבס בגדיו וטבל טהור מלטמא בביאת, והרי הוא מטמא כשרץ).

וגלח את כל שערו ורחץ וגו׳. Before the טבילה, all hair that is visible on the whole of his body has to be shaved off by a razor, העביר תער על כל בשרו, ibid). מגלח כדלעת, with the exception of בית סתרים, hair which is not visible on the surface, such as שיער בתוך החוטם, (see note on v. 9; Sota 16a & b).
וטהר, from טומאת משא מושב וביאה, but is still מטמא במגע כשרץ.

נכנס לפנים מן החומה :ואחר יבוא אל המחנה, thereby his exclusion from מחנה ישראל is finished, he may come again into the social circle grouped around the Sanctuary of the Torah, but the Sanctuary itself as well as its קדשים remain closed to him. For that he required the passing of a seven-days of ימי ספירו, during which וישב מחוץ לאהלו שבעת ימים: in this stage יהא כמנודה והוא אסור בתשמיש המטה אהלו, אין אהלו אלא אשתו, שנאמר, שובו לכם בימי ספירו .(ת״כ) ,לאהליכם, sexual intercourse with his wife is forbidden, (it is permitted in all the previous stages). In the case of women, אשה מנוגעת, this prohibition is not imposed: מחוץ לאהלו ולא מחוץ לאחלה, (Kerithoth 8b).

Let us try to understand the meaning of this procedure as precribed in verses 2—8 for the return of the healed מצורע out of the isolation, of ימי הלוטו, back into the general public society. Re-entry into the social community is quite clearly the idea to which it all must refer. Because it is only the social community, the entry into מחנה ישראל, which is opened to him by all this procedure. From the מקדש and its קדשים he is still excluded during ספירו and for his re-entry into the מקדש, special further procedures have to be taken as prescribed in the following v. 9 et seq. So the procedure prescribed here in vv. 2—8, can only be meant to represent the ideas and thoughts which are to accompany his re-entry into social life with his fellow men. We have then to consider the various objects and acts as being in connection with this point of view.
First, let us note the analogies which these objects and acts have to other significant institutions of the Torah.

The two birds which, at least למצוה, should be שוין במראה בקומה ובדמים ולקיחתן כאחת (v. 4), remind one at once of the שני שעירים of י״כ (Ch. 16,5), for which also — and indeed in that case made into an absolute necessity — such similarity is demanded, and which also meet such a contrasting fate, the one by שחיטה and the other by שילוח; only there the שילוח has to be המדברה whereas here, on the contrary, מדבר is prohibited and שלוח על פני השדה is ordered.

The character of these birds, that they are not מקבלי מרות (v. 4), is analogous to the אשד לא עלה עליה עול of the פרה אדומה, Numb. 19,2, and to the אשר לא עבד בה אשר לא משכה בעול of עגלה ערופה (Deut. 21,3).

The דם על מים חיים בכלי חרש is analogous to עפר אל מים קדושים בכלי חרש of the סוטה (Numb. 5,17) and to אפר במים חיים אל כלי of the פרה אדומה (Numb. 19,17); and finally עץ ארז ושני תולעת ואזוב are quite the same objects as are used with the שרפת הפרה (ibid 6).

שדרה בבית כבשדה, שאינה מקבלת מרות: “which does not submit to any control”, “lives in the house with the same free wildness of the outdoor fields”, the character of the most completely unsocialable being as represented by the צפרי דרור at once springs to one’s mind as the opposite contrast to what is demanded for re-entrance into the social life of the community. It is the contrast of the animals of the “field” to the humans of the “city”.

The demand which is made as the condition for the re-entry into the social life of the community is ושחט את הצפור, is energetic subjection of the wild untrammelled animal life under the sharp control of the morally strong human will. But this breaking of the animal lack of control and restraint in Man is not just any killing of life”; the שחיטת הצפוד occurs אל כלי חרש על מים חיים. It is just only as דם שחוט (and we know the symbolism of שחיטה. I.L.), just only in the being controlled by the moral free fill of Man, that the animal side of Man, too, achieves taking part in the “immortal, ever-flowing Life”, which “in an earthly sheath” is allotted to Man. (This is what the “ashes” in the מים חיים of the מי חטאת expresses:— although אפר, still חיים, although transient, passing into ash, still immortal; and עפר, the humus of the soil in the מים קדושים of the סוטה:— although provided with the material means for all the attractions of organic life, still called to moral holiness, see notes on Numb. 5,17).

עץ ארז and אזוב, cedar tree and hyssop, the highest and lowest type of plant life, but equally representing the whole total vegetable-life (cf. I Kings 5,13), just as שני תולעת, wool dyed with worm-blood, “mammal and worm” the highest and lowest type of the animal world represents the whole range of animal life (perhaps that is why whenever it is in connection with עץ ארז and אזוב it says: שני תולעת, with שני parallel to ארז and תולעת to אזוב, whereas otherwise it always calls it תולעת שני). All three, bound together with the red thread to form one unit, present the general idea of all organic life which develops in the vegetable and animal life of the שדה, to be an inhabitant of which, the מנוגע because of his unsocial and misanthropic character, had been judged. To these three, the צפור החי, the living “free, wild bird”, is added; the uncontrolled being, simply following its instinct animal nature, living out in the open, belongs equally to vegetable-animal organic Nature. Between them and the “immortal ever-flowing Life” which is to be attained by exercising free-will in mastering instinctive animalism, as expressed by the דם צפור השחוטה על המים החיים, and which is to find its realisation in the social life of moral humanity, yawns a sevenfold wide gap. He, who up till now has been banished to the community of plant and animal life is admonished by the הזיות שבע פעמים, that he must climb up across this gap using all his energy seven times over before he can be declared purified for his re-entry into the community of Man. These sprinklings warning him of the height of the moral calling of Man are made, לאחר ידו, on the back of his hand, or according to other opinion, on his forehead. For hand and forehead are the two “most human” parts of the human body. They are the outword representation of “thought” and “action”, which are the two most characteristic traits which demonstrate a human being. The Halacha has decided that the sprinklings are to be done on the hand, for it is the incorrectness of his “actions” towards his fellowmen which has caused him to be banished from their company. But note that it is just לאחר ידו, the back of the opened hand which is always representative of action, deeds, whereas the inner surface of the hand, כף, the palm, would express “having”, “holding”, “possessing”.

ושלח את הצפוד החיה על פני השדה, or more precisely, in v. 53: אל מחוץ לעיר אל פני השדה, “the living bird he is to send out of the city, onto the field”. This preaches two sermons. The uncontrolled, untrammelled nature, simply following its instincts, as characterises the צפור דרור, stands in opposition to the foundation on which human society is built. But it is right and justified in the life of the wild, in the life of Nature in the fields and forests which surround the life of cities of Man. Hence, על פני השדה, and not into the “desert”, and not over the “sea”.

גלוח וטבילה. After the conditions for the new life have been brought home to him by שחיטת הצפוד and the הזיות, the next step is to break off completely with the past. This is symbolized by טבילת בגדיו וגופו. But there is one other act associated with it, גלוח, the meaning of which must be sought. This גלוח, this shaving of the hair from the whole of the body with a razor, תער, is bracketed as being of equal importance, with שחיטת צפור והזיות, it says in ת״כ on v. 1: שחיטת צפרים והזיות דם צפור ותגלחתו ביום ובכהן, all three must be done in daytime and by the כהן. The only analogy for this תגלחת של מצוה of the whole body is to be found in Numb. 8,7, in the prescribed: והעבירו תער על כל בשרם, for the Levites at their induction into office. If we look for the similarity in the two cases, we think we can find it in the fact that in both cases men are to be led out of the individuality of living their own lives by themselves into living for the community. In the case of the Levites it is giving up a hitherto perfectly justified private life to become public servants, and then giving themselves up to the service of the community is expressed by סמיכה and תנופה, (see notes there in Numb. VIII). Here it is the giving up of a hitherto unjustified, selfish, anti-social living for oneself to adopt the self-sacrifice of one’s duties to one’s fellowmen. In both cases, the giving up living for oneself is brought home to them by תגלחת, by העברת תער על כל בשרם. For, we believe we are not mistaken in taking hair to represent a protection of the skin, protecting it from, and minimising the impressions of the outer world, an isolating material (cf. above). To completely strip a body of all hair, would be to expose it naked to all the influences of the outer world, would be well suited to awaken thoughts of removing isolating selfishness. But whereas in the case of the Levite voluntarily giving up the fully justified private life he had been living up to the present, the act of תגלחת is performed by himself, with מצורע, the giving up of the unlawful selfish life with its lack of consideration for his fellowmen has to be brought to his mind by the representative of the Sanctuary of the Torah, by a כהן (cf. Isaiah 7,20, where the Assyrian might is called a razor in the employ of God, and the deprivation of all the protective elements of the Jewish National Body is described as the shaving off of all its hair).

וישב מחוץ לאהלו וגו׳. After the re-entry into the social community is again opened to him, he still remains for seven days shut out of מקדש וקדשיו as אב הטומאה כשרץ, and during these ימי ספירו, he is also limited with regards to his home life. He is now אסור בתשמיש המטה, which was not the case during the days of his הסגרו והלוטו. While he was expelled from society on account of his unlawful behaviour towards it, he was allowed to have ‘his tent” outside. But when he is again admitted to the community which has grouped itself around the Sanctuary of the Torah, but, on account of the social sins he had been committing hitherto, he is still barred from the Sanctuary itself, the Torah denies him the full enjoyment of his own home for as long as, not considered yet fully cured from his social misdemeanours, it keeps the doors of its Sanctuary closed to him. Does not this express the deeply significant Truth:— Only to those who fully recognise the rights of their fellow-men does the Torah recognise the full rights to their own homes? He who undermines the well-being of the home of his neighbour can not be allowed to settle quietly in his own home in the vicinity of the Sanctuary of the Torah. Only when the Sanctuary of the Torah can again open its gates to him, is the gate to his “own tent” in its vicinity open to him again: ישב מחוץ לאהלו יהא כמנודה והוא אסור בתשמיש (ת״כ) ,המטה.

V. 9. והיה ביום השביעי וגו׳. Just as the complete surrender of egoism which is demanded from him on his re-entry from the unsocial animal attitude to life to the social human one had to be brought to his mind by תגלחת (v. 8), so is the same demand made to him regarding his re-entry from the social human circle into the Jewish godly calling by a repeated תגלחת, the תגלחת שניה. It teaches him to appreciate the conception of the absolute ideal which the Mikdosh preaches, in its whole supreme height, far transcending that of simply social human duties, and the necessity for energetic work on self-improvement and increased self-respect.
את ראשו ואת זקנו: this is an example of an עשה being דוחה a לא תעשה, (Nazir 41a; see note on Ch. 19,27).

וטהר: After the טבילה he has the character of a טבול יום, he is מותר במעשר and אסור בתרומה. After הערב שמש he becomes מותר בתרומה, but, being מחוסר כפרה, is still אסור בקדשים until he has brought his offering on the following day.

V. 10. וביום השמיני — see article in Jeshurun 5th year, p. 13 et seq., (or Ges. Schriften vol. 3 p. 301 et seq. I.L.) — שיהיו שניהן :שני כבשים שוין, they should both be exactly similar, but this is only למצוה, it is not מעכב (Yoma 62b; see note on v. 13). The lesson, which, with שחיטת צפור והזית דם צפור ותגהלתו, accompanied his re-entry into human society only taught him to be conscious of the high moral dignity of a human being and what being a human being should entail, the fundamental condition for which is the stripping oneself of every selfish feeling of being concerned solely with one’s own self. Such feelings, such egoism, is the powerful spring which activates the whole life of all non-human organic life, but which is in complete contrast to that feeling of brotherly consideration which should form the principle of life of social Man. But this lesson only introduces his rebirth as a Man. His rebirth as a Jew — ביום השמיני — only becomes completed when to this general feeling of the common duty of all men, to be worthy to be called human beings, is added the positive duties of carrying out God’s Will for the conduct of human life as revealed in His Torah, and when he, as a Jew, has contracted afresh his bond with this Torah in its Sanctuary.
This renewal of his bond with the Torah and the assurance of an undisturbed life in future, which only so is to be found, is to be accomplished by the offering-ritual here prescribed.

As hardly anywhere else — (only in the case of נזיר טמא in Numb. 6,10 — 12, do we find anything similar, and even there it is only עופות which are brought as חטאת and עולה) — all the shades of dedication of one’s actions: עולה ,חטאת ,אשם, have to be expressed; and as in no other case at all, all three, even the אשם and חטאת, have to be accompanied by נסכים, (the שלשה עשרונים וגו׳ of v. 10; Menachoth 90b & 91a). For, as can be seen from the following verses, the שני כבשים are אשם and עולה respectively, and the כבשה אחת is a חטאת, and with each one of them a separate כפרה is to be achieved, (vv. 18, 19 & 20). The threefold dedication of his future actions is to be done from the standpoint of כבש, of the fate of one’s life being gained from the guidance, and “shepherding” of God. For, it is just foregetting that he is a כבש of God, imagining that he can forge his own fate by himself, that lies at the root of all the social sins which caused his expulsion from the congregation of God. That, too, is the reason why, as in no other instance, his אשם and his חטאת are also accompanied by נסכים. More than with anybody else, just with him, at his now complete re-entry into the Jewish Community, is the fact to be impressed that his future “flour, oil and wine”, his future existence, well-being and joy in life are solely dependent on his ordering his life on faithfulness to duty. And that is also why אשם is his first offering, and the one about which the whole ritual prescribed in vv. 14—18 is grouped, and also the one which the Halacha indicates as being the offering which definitely and finally settles his past. הביא צפרים ונתנגע אין מביא אלא קרבן אחד, if the נגע recurs before he has brought the אשם, then both conditions are considered as being one and the same מצורע and he has only to bring one offering for both, if it recurs after the אשם, it is considered as being two separate attacks, to be atoned for with separate offerings. In the same way it is the moment of the bringing of the אשם which is decisive as to his עשיר or עני-character: לאקבועי בעניות ובעשירות לא מיקבע עד שיביא אשמו (Kerithoth 9b). When we consider that it is just אשם, (see notes on Ch. 5,14 et seq.), that brings to our minds the desolation which threatens the life of the person who has sinned through selfish misuse of his powers and only considering his own interests, then we understand the prominent importance of the אשם in the group of קרבנות of the מצורע.

As something quite unique we find prescribed here, besides the oil in מנחה בלולה בשמן, a separate לוג of oil. This oil can not have the meaning of a sanctifying anointment, for after the prescribed sprinkling and placing on the various parts of the body of the person to be purified — vv.15—18, the remainder of the oil is eaten by the זכרי כהונה in the עזרה, like the שירי מנחה and its היתר אכילה is dependent on the preceding מתנות. According to פגול ,ר׳ מאיר would apply to it as to all other שירים (Zebachim 44a & 91a), but the Halacha is doubtful on this point. This לוג שמן של מצורע can, accordingly, only be taken to have a similar meaning to the שמן of מנחות. Nevertheless, although as we remarked in Ch. 2,1, the oil which is added to the flour of the מנחות, as לחם שמן, brings the idea of well-being, comfort, to that of mere existence, this separate לוג שמן של מצורע must be taken from the meaning of oil by itself with reference to the human body. Expressions as: כשמן בעצמתיו (Ps. 10,27), ובשרי כחש משמן (ibid 24), וחבל עול מפני שמן (Is. 10,27), ומשמן בשרו יזרה (Is. 17,4) and כל שמן כל איש חיל (Judges 3,29), show that it has the idea of health and plumpness. But if it was just a bodily disease which proclaimed God’s displeasure at the social behaviour of the מנוגע, the connection is at once clear between this idea of שמן and the thoughts and hopes of future health which are to be brought from his renewal of his bond with the Torah to the cured מצורע.

V. 11. לפני ה׳ ;והעמיד הכהן המטהר וגו׳: this is the entrance to the Mikdosh. In the second Temple this was the Nikanor Gate, שער ניקנוד, that on the eastern side led from the עזרת נשים. The עזרת ישראל is the beginning of the real “holy” Temple into which no טמאים מן התורה may enter. The door itself still belongs to the “outside”, so that the מצורע, who, as מחוסר כפרה, is still forbidden to enter the Mikdosh, could stand in the doorway (Sota 7a & 8a). There, in the east, facing the Holy of Holies, he stood with the three lambs for his offering, the bringing of which is to open the entrance for him.

V. 12. והקריב אותו לאשם. This והקריב means dedicating it to be an תנופה :והניף אותם וגו׳ .אשם, the ritual expressing dedication to God and to the community in general (תנופה and תרומה), otherwise is only performed with שלמים and מנחות, these being offerings referring to a happy and well-provided-for condition of life, and by the תנופה, the bringer places himself and his worldly possessions in the service of God and his fellow men. Appropriately it is to be performed here at the אשם מצורע. To the one who is returning from sin brought about by egoism it calls special attention to that side of the אשם-idea which is calculated to work just against selfishness. Immediately the offering is fixed to be an אשם, this warning name reminds the “person who is to be saved from threatened loneliness” to dedicate this offering which represents his own personality, to the service of God and his fellow men. Facing the Holy of Holies of the Torah, לפני ה׳ he does this by תנופה and תרומה, with the living animal and the לוג of oil representing health. Thereby, he places himself and the healthy existence he is now hoping for, in the service of God and the community by keeping God’s Torah.

V. 13. ושחט וגו׳: that אשם, like עולה and חטאת, is a קדש קדשים and, as such, that שחיטתו בצפון, has already been said above (Ch. 7,1 & 2), and there we have already been told that the מתנות of its blood are like those of an עולה, while the הקטרת אימורים ואכילת בשרו are like a חטאת. That, nevertheless, it repeats here that an אשם מצורע is to be given the treatment of partly that of an עולה and partly that of a חטאת, is explained in Zebachim 49a, in accordance with the canon: דבר שהיה בכלל ויצא לידון בדבר חדש אי אתה רשאי להחזירו לכללו עד שיחזירנו הכתוב לכללו בפירוש וכו׳, לפי שיצא אשם מצורע לידון בדבר החדש בבוהן יד ובוהן רגל ואזן ימנית יכול לא יהא טעון מתן דמים ואימורין לגבי מזבח, ת״ל כחטאת האשם הוא וכו׳, that anything that would normally belong to a class, but for which something “new” is prescribed, i.e. something which is quite in contrast to all the other objects in that class, (see תוספות thereon), is to be excluded from that class unless the Torah explicitly puts it back into that class. For, all other אשמות the Torah orders that all the blood has to be given onto the Altar, but here, for this אשם, it is prescribed that the מתנה is to be made on parts of the body of the bringer. So that, unless the Torah has repeated that it was similar to a חטאת, we could have assumed that neither the דם nor the אימורים were to be brought onto the Altar. If we consider that in v. 10, the demand is made that למצוה, the כבש אשם and the כבש עולה should be exactly similar even in external qualities, then the החטאת, the העולה and the כחטאת of our verse could even refer specially to the חטאת and עולה of the מצורע itself. Then, in the sense of the canon just quoted the idea could be:— By the מתנות of the blood being made on the person and not on the Altar, the importance of the person who is to be brought from desolation to health and life (which meaning is always innate in every אשם), is so much stressed, that this personal idea of this אשם might seem to exclude the ideas which are expressed by the מתנות being made on the מזבח. To counteract this idea, the making of not only אשם in general, but particularly this, אשם מצורע, completely comparable to חטאת and עולה, expresses the important fact that the care of one’s own person, one’s efforts for health and life, if looked at it the right way, belongs to those purposes of life which are dictated by the Altar. If looked on as a “duty” taught by the Sanctuary of the Torah, and carried out solely on that basis, it becomes a holy act dedicated to God, completely equal to any of the other activities of life which receive their direction and dedication in עולה and חטאת. The אשם of the מצורע, our verse insists, is as much קדש קדשים as its עולה and חטאת. The Gemora (Zebachim ibid), takes the fact that here, to teach צפון for אשם, the Torah compares it not only to עולה, the classical case for צפון (I,11), but also to חטאת, for which צפון is only derived from היקש (its being compared) to עולה, to teach us the rule that דבר הלמד בהיקש אינו חוזר ומלמד בהיקש, to show us that the היקש to חטאת would not have sufficed. This canon limiting the transference of comparison, as well as the one that דבר הלמד בהיקש אינו חוזר ומלמד בגזרה שוה, and others, belong to the rule applying to קדשים, viz. בכל התורה כולה למידין למד מלמד חוץ מן הקדשים שאין דנין למד מלמד (ibid 49b).

V. 14. ולקח הכהן. This is the קבלה, the blood being accepted by the Mikdosh. Here, there is a double קבלה. The one, the acceptance of the blood for the Altar in a כלי, in an integral part of the Sanctuary, by one כהן, who carries it to the Altar to perform the שתי מתנות שהן ארבע with it. Tho other, the acceptance of the blood for placing on the מיטהר, in the cupped palm of a second כהן who carries it to the מצורע to perform the מתנות on תנוך אזן etc. (Yoma 61b & Negaim 14, 8). According to the תוספתא (see ר״ש on Negaim ibid), the קבלה for the מזבח was done first. These קבלות and מתנות, differ, so it seems to us, from the similar ones prescribed for the איל מלואים (Ex. 29,20), in that there was only one קבלה and that in a כלי, and in that the מתנות from it on to the ear, hand and foot preceded the מתנות על המזבח. In these separated קבלות in our case here, and in the contrasted order of the מתנות, the following idea may be meant to be expressed:— The מצורע rising to a higher life, and in שחיטה giving his old life up entirely to new directions is taught to find the path in two separate ways of life, which, however, are completely reciprocal and complementary to each other. First, he has to give up his previous living for himself (שחיטה), and henceforth to belong to the Mikdosh (קבלת הדם בכלי מקדש), and to energetically strive upwards to the ideals represented by the summit of the Altar (זריקה למטה); and at the same time he must give himself up to live an ordinary human life in a priestly manner in his “mind”, his “deeds”, and his “efforts”, (אזן יד ורגל), as the כהן clad in the garments of the Sanctuary of the Torah indicated to him. It is one and the same beat of his pulse which raises him upwards to God, and to the goals which He points out, and with which he is to gain for himself a lofty true Life, as well as a life of health and physical strength as is represented by the לוג שמן (v. 15).

V. 15. ולקח וגו׳ ומק על כף הכהן וגו׳. He pours it into the left hand of another priest, but it is also כשר if he pours it into his own left hand (Negaim 14,10). It is repeatedly stressed that the oil is to be received in the left hand. In the case of קבלת הדם, the left hand is not mentioned at all, and according to רמב״ם, (מחוסרי כפרה, 4, 2; but see מ״מ thereon), קבלת הדם in the left hand would even be פסול. The blood to be placed on the אזן ובהונות of the מיטהר, obtains the meaning of a priest-like life of service just by the act of its being received in the hand of the priest. Here, the hand of the priest is exactly similar to that which the כלי שרת, the vessel, which is an integral part of the Mikdosh, is to the דם על המזבח. The hand of the priest has a meaning for the דם, and we can understand that the hand to be used must be the right one. But the oil only receives reference to the duties and mission of life which are indicated by God, by the הזיות towards the Holy of Holies, and only comes back to refer to the priest in the שירים. So, the hand of the priest has no special meaning for the oil, it is merely the vehicle for the הזיה.For that the left hand is the fitting means to be used. More, קבלת השמן בימין would be פסול and would confuse and distort the meaning. Only the sprinklings towards the קדש-קדשים have to be done with the right forefinger.
V. 16. על כל הזיה טבילה :וטבל וגו׳ והזה וגו׳, each of seven הזיות has to be done with a fresh wetting of the finger, (Negaim 14, 10). :לפני ה׳ כנגד בית קדש הקדשים (ibid).

V. 17. ומיתר וגו׳. The repetition of על בהן ידו וגו׳ here and in v. 28, although these places on the body have already been exactly indicated by the על דם האשם and על מקום דם האשם is taken in Menachoth 9b & 10a to tell us precisely that although צדדין are צדי צדדין ,כשר are not, that although the blood and the oil may be placed on the upper or side surfaces of the thumb and toe, they may not be placed on the under surfaces. The organs in question are meant to be regarded as being under the control of the extending muscles, i.e. in their active movement.

על דם האשם: The מתנות דם on תנוך אזן ובהונות must be done first, but it is not necessary that the blood should remain there when the oil ritual is performed, it says in v. 28: מלמד שהמקום גורם ,על מקום דם האשם, (ת״כ. See also Menachoth 10a). For all these מתנות of the blood and oil, the מצורע, standing in the Nikanor gateway outside the עזרה, had to stretch his head, hand and foot into the עזרה to the כהן, as the דם אשם would become פסול if it reached outside. On this point the question is raised in Zebachim 32b whether altogether ביאה במקצת, partially entering the Mikdosh, i.e. putting just single parts of the body inside, שמה ביאה or not.

V. 18. By these sevenfold הזיות of his oil to the קדש קדשים, by the מתנות on his ear thumb and toe which follow, by the pouring of all rest of the oil which had been taken out of the לוג for these הזיות and מתנות on to his head, and then finally by the remainder of the לוג being given over to be eaten by the priests (v. 13), by this whole procedure, the great sermon is preached for his future, to the one who is now restored to health from נגע illness, before he is again accepted into the sphere of the Mikdosh:— It tells him that his physical health is dependent on his spiritual and moral health; only if he dedicates beforehand every particle of the health and strength he is now hoping to be granted, with ever fresh, ever renewed energy (על כל הזיה טבילה), until it is absolutely consummated (שבע הזיות), to making a reality of the Torah which reposes untouchable and unalterable in the קדש קדשים, then, and then only, can he hope that this health and strength will be the lot of the physical-psychical dedicated Man, which he can enjoy henceforth, priest-like, i.e. in the service of the Torah, to a serious but happy life (מתחלקת לכהנים). The dedication is made first of the power of the mind to hear and drink in thoughts (the ear), and of the power of accomplishing deeds (the hand) and of the power of striving for possessions and attainments (the foot). Then, this dedicating every thought and every activity and every effort to the service of the Torah finally grips the very root and source of all thinking, all receptivity, all action and all striving — the head.

וכפר עריו לפני ה׳, — at the following חטאת it says: וכפר על המטהר מטמאתו, and the וכפר עליו הכהן וטהר :עולה, — by the אשם and the ritual of the לוג שמן associated with it the atonement of the social sins which had caused the mark of God’s displeasure to be shown to him, was accomplished. All the teachings which form the basis for a true social Jewish life before God, have been brought home to him, for him to take to heart and from resolutions for his future conduct with his fellowmen. With that his sinful past is wiped out and all he has to do now is, henceforth to conduct his social life in accordance with the dictates of God’s Torah.

V. 19 & 20. But to be socially just and true forms only one phase of the demands of a full Jewish Life. To keep oneself up to the whole high standard of all Gods laws of morality as taught by חטאת and unceasingly to carry out all the duties demanded by God, as symbolically expressed by עולה, is not only necessary for the making of a complete Jew, but is what forms the real root and trunk of a godly life out of which a true honest just social life is expected to blossom and be the fruit. A so-called Judaism consisting of Jewish ”goodness of heart” and justice alone, stripped off and torn away from the whole system of conscientiousness and devotion demanded by God, would never have celebrated — and never will celebrate — its world historic triumph. The אשם מצורע must get its hold and duration from חטאת and עולה. It must vow by the חטאת to completely rid itself of its lack of moral self-determination, טומאתו, and with the עולה to direct its moral free devotion to all the goodness indicated by God, וטהו, so that it becomes “pure” and remains “pure” and never again need the Finger of God touch him as a sign of His displeasure and as מנוגע have to banish him out of the circle of Jewish Life which develops around the Sanctuary of God’s Torah.

V. 21—31. ואם דל הוא וגו׳. For the poor man the אשם remains exactly the same. The duty of social justness is the same for rich and poor and the social position does not enter into the judgment of those sins against brotherhood and justness for which the אשם מצורע is designed to atone. It is only in the tenor of life as a whole which is different in the higher or lower “class” in which our fate has placed our lives, and it is in different phases of our moral strength which become tested and proved in the different external conditions of life. So that although the אשם ולוג שמן are the same for a rich מצורע or a poor one, the חטאת and the עולה representing the dedication and direction of their general lives, consists for the עני, just as in the קרבן עולה ויורד, of a חטאת עוף and an עולת עוף. See notes on Ch. 1,14 et seq. & V,7 et seq.

Vv.34 & 35. נגעי בתים .כי תבאו וגו׳, only apply to houses in א״י — (which is probably why they are treated in a quite separate paragraph) — and only after the Land had been completely divided up into individual holdings so that כל אהד מכיר את שלו, each house had its permanent inhabitant. It had to have become אחוזה (v. 34), and אשר לו הבית (v. 35): מי שמיוחד לו (Yoma 12a). Houses are only מיטמא בנגעים if they are אחוזתכם, Jewish possessions, but not בתי נכרים. Hence הלוקח בתים מן הנכרים יראו בתחלה (Negaim 12, 1), similarly to נגעי בגדים (see Ch. 13,47). בית השותפים is מיטמא בנגעים, it has definite owners. בית הכנסת is only מיטמא בנגעים if יש בה בית דירה לחזן הכנסת, if the “Inspector of the ביה״כ״ has a dwelling apartment in it. On the other hand no houses in Jerusalem are מיטמא בנגעים. Jerusalem was considered as being national property, לא נתחלקה לשבטים, so that אין משכירין בתים בירושלים לפי שאינן שלהן, so that those who pilgrimed up to Jerusalem had to be given lodgings free of charge; house owners were not allowed to charge rent because they themselves were not considered as full owners of their houses (Yoma 12a).

Häuser sind auch nur מיטמא בנגעים, wenn sie אחוזתכם, jüdisches Eigentum sind נגעי בגדים, (Negaim 12. 1), wie הלוקח בתים מן הנכרים יראו בתחלה nicht בתי נכרים (siehe Kap. 13, 47 und die Abhandlung Ende Kap. 13).

ובא אשר לו הבית. The Gemora, Yoma 2b, finds in these very words a hint of the kind of social misbehaviour which called for the proclamation by a נגע of God’s displeasure with the inhabitant of the house: אשר לו הבית, so it says there, מי שמייחד ביתו לו, he considers the purpose of his house to be exclusively for himself; שאינו רוצה להשאיל כליו, he does not want to lend any of his utensils; ואומר אין לו, and says he has not got the article requested; הקב״ה מפרסמו כשמפנה את ביתו, the lies of such a man, God exposes to the public by having his house cleared out into the street. — אפילו ת״ח ויודע שהוא נגע תאי לא יגזור ויאמר נגע נראה לי בבית, :כנגע נראה לי בבית אלא כנגע נראה לי בבית, (Negaim 12,5); this is taken to be a lesson in the good manners of modesty (רא״מ).

ולא לאורי, מכאן אמרו בית אפל אין פותחין בו חלונות לראות את :נראה לי (ת״כ) ,נגעו. The נגע must be visible by ordinary daylight. In a corner, where it can only be seen by the aid of artificial light or by making an opening in the wall, it is no נגע. Altogether, the rule applies in houses that נגעים בבית הסתרים, e.g. in a wall under the cover of panelling or wainscot, or under carpets, are not מטמא, similarly to the case of human beings, (תוספתא quoted in the ר״ש, Negaim 13,1).

V. 36. וצוה וגו׳ ופנו וגו׳. See end of Ch. 13,59: ולא יטמא כל אשר בבית, it is doubtful whether articles which otherwise are not מקבל טומאה e.g. חבילי עצים וחבילי קנים also become טמא in a בית המנוגע. (See ט״צ ,מל״מ 14,4).

לראות את הבית, not only את הנגע, for the build of the house itself has also to be examined. טומאת נגעים is not applicable to every house, the shape and the building have to be considered. The house must be foursided (not round or irregular), must rest directly on the earth, and must be built of stone, wood and earth (Negaim 12,1), (not of bricks and not of marble).

V. 37. וראה את הנגע והנה הנגע: by the repetition, double the size of an ordinary נגע, viz. two גריסים, are considered necessary for ,נגעי בתים שוקעות במראיהן :שקערורות—.(ת״כ), appearing deeper. We think the idea that it is only the appearance of depth due to the deeper colour, but any actual sinking in the level of the wall (see Ch. 13,2, 3, & 20), is not expressed by the word שקערורות. This idea is expressed at the end of the verse: ומראיהן שפל מן הקיר, which ת״כ explains: מראיהן שפל מן הקיר ולא ממשן. The word שקערורות would only mean deepening, pitting, coming from the root קער, from which we get קערה, a dish, a deepened plate.

V. 38. ויצא :ויצא וגו׳ ,והסגיר וגו׳, he is to leave the house before the טמא-declaration, but only as far as אל פתח הבית, just outside the threshold: (ת״כ) ,עומד בצד המשקוף ומסגיר. The Gemora in Chulin 10b, sees in this a practical example of the general principle: אוקי מלחא אחזקתיה, namely, that once any condition of an object has been ascertained, it can legally be presumed to continue in that condition until the contrary is ascertained. Accordingly here, the priest makes his declaration outside the house, from where probably he is unable to see the נגע in the presumption that is has not meanwhile changed its ascertained טומאה character.

וד[[illegible]]סגיר את הבית, it is not quite clear exactly what is to be understood by this הסגיר (as indeed by all cases which occur at a מצורע), whether it means actually locking up or only a declaration of isolation. See מל״מ on הל׳ ט״צ 14,5. See note above on Ch. 13,4.

V. 40. וחלצו :וצוה הכהן וחלצו, from this word being in the plural, the Halacha teaches that if it is a common wall to two houses, the neighbour has to share this מכאן אמרו אוי לרשע אוי לשכנו—,חליצה (Negaim 12b).— אל מקום טמא, the place becomes טמא as the stones are מטמאין במגע ובמשא ובביאה (Negaim 13,2). אתהן אל מהוץ לעיר: not like אדם, only out of מוקפות חומה, but out of any city (ת״כ, cf. בגדים above on Ch. 13,47).

V. 41. יקציע :ואת הבית יקציע וגו׳, from the root קצע, similarly the following הקצו from the root קצה, from which we get the ordinary קצה, the end; phonetically, related to both is גזע, a shoot cut from the trunk. The basic meaning is certain, viz. to divide, to separate, to cut off. Here, to scrape off. Perhaps the difference between קצע and קצה is that קצע is used exclusively to refer to the object from which something is taken off, ואת הבית יקציע, and similarly the related גזע; but קצה is used for both the object taken off and for the object from which it is taken off. From the same root would come מקצוע, the plane. Wessely takes מקצעת המשכן in Ex. 26,23, to mean a right-angled planing.—סביב: all around the ,נגע (ת״כ).

V. 42. ולקחו וגו׳ ועפר אחר יקה וטח וגו׳, the neighbour has to take part in the removal of the stone and replacing it with other stone, but the fresh plastering over is the responsibility of the owner of the בית המנוגע by himself, (ת״כ and Negaim 12,6).
V. 43. ואם ישוב: after again being shut up for seven days, similarly to ושב הכהן ביום השביעי of v. 39, הקצות—.(ת״כ): an irregular form. If the נפעל, it should be: הקצות; if the הקצות :הפעיל.

V. 44. ובא הכהן וראה והנה פשה וגו׳. As the same expression צרעת ממארת, is used here as in Ch. 13,51 & 52 referring to בגדים, the Halacha is established in ת״כ, that just as in the case of בגדים, if the נגע comes back without any increase of size, החוזר אע״פ שאינו פושה, the garment has to be burnt, (v. 57 ibid), so here, in the case of huoses, if the נגע reappears after חולץ וקוצה וטח, even if there is no פשיון, it entails the נתיצה of the house. Taking this into consideration, we have to take the פשה here as being synonymous with ופרח in v. 43, and as Wessely takes it, the re-appearance of the נגע on these new stones, for the old ones have been taken away, can in fact justly be considered as a פשיון. Nevertheless, see what is said below.—טמא הוא: although it was already טמא as מוסגר, its טומאה is now intensified as בית המוסגר מטמא מתוכו ,מוחלט מתוכו :מהולט ומאחוריו ,וזה וזה מטמאין בביאה (Negaim 13,4). According to our version in רש״י Yebamoth 103b, if one touched the wall of a בית מוסגר on the inside without going into the house, one would become טמא, but in a בית מוחלט even if one touched the wall on the outside. But this version of the difference is not the only one. See תוספות thereon and מל״מ on הל׳ ט״צ 16,3.

V. 45. ונתץ את הבית את אבניו וגו׳. Although the neighbour has to share in the חליצה, the נתיצה is restricted entirely to the בית המנוגע. Equally so, in a two-storied house, בית ועליה על גביו, only the story affected by the נגע has to be demolished, (Negaim 13,2 & 3).

V. 46 & 47. כל ימי הסגיר אתו, and of course, not necessary to say, also השכב וגו׳ והאכל וגו׳ —.בימי חלוטו: both these are only meant to be the expression for just staying in the house. הבא אל הבית is only a momentary entry, as soon as one pokes one’s head and the greater part of one’s body, ראשו ורבו, into a בית המנוגע one becomes טמא until nightfall, but one is not מטמא בגדים שעליו. But of course, בגדים by themselves (not worn as clothing) which are brought into a בית המנוגע become טמא immediately like a man or any other כלים, is is only when actually clothing a human being that they remain טהור if the entry is only momentary. But if the person remains in the house, then the בגדים שעליו become טמא too, as it says יכבס בגדיו. The minimum time for such “remaining in the house” is given here by והאוכל בבית. This period is fixed Negaim 13,9: שישהה כדי אכילת פרס פת חטין ולא פת שעורין מיסב ואוכלן בלפתן, i.e. the time it would take to sit down comfortably at table and eat half a loaf of wheaten bread (פרס: to break, divide), with jam or vegetables. The Gemora in Eruvin 72b, takes a whole loaf to represent the food for two meals, מזון שתי סעודות, accordingly פרס, the half, would be the normal measure of one סעודה, the אכילה of our text, which by being placed together with שכיבה designates more than a hasty snack, means having a meal. And again, by its association with שכיבה, the אכילה does not mean necessarily actually eating but only designates the time, the שיעור זמן is אכילה אחת. On the actual size of this אכילת פרס opinions differ in Eruvin 83a. According to ר׳ יוחנן בן ברוקה, it would be the volume of ג׳ ביצים, and this view is adopted by רמב״ם and רשב״א, but ר׳ שמעון takes it to be the quantity of ד׳ ביצים and this view is followed by רש״י and תוספות. This latter view is also in accordance with the general rule that טומאת אוכלין בכביצה. See on the Tur Ch. 612.
V. 48. ואם בא יבא וגו׳. See below.

Vv. 52 & 53. The ritual with the צפרים etc., for a בית המנוגע is exactly the same as for a מצורע, only that in the case of persons the הזיות are made on to the hand (on the external surface) and in houses to the outside surface of the upper lintel, על המשקוף שבבית מבחוץ, (Negaim 14,1). At the house the object of these proceedings is described as ,וכפר על הבית והטא את הבית, the “freeing from sin and atonement”, the doing away of the past, and the reopening of a new future is accomplished with the צפרים etc., whereas with persons this consummation is attached to קרבנות, to the וחטא את בית וגו׳ —.אשם חטאת ועולה, the דם צפור etc., expresses the lesson which is to be taken to heart, which henceforth is to allow the house to be free from sin; ושלח וגו׳ וכפר וגו׳, the sending of the ‘unsocial’ bird out of the region of the city into the freedom of the fields allows a “cover, a roof” to fall over the unsocial past of the house and gives it the possibility of a pure future again.

If we call to mind the laws given here from vv. 37-53, the wording of the text discusses only one course of נגעי בתים, namely when after the first הסגר the נגע has grown, פשיון לאחר הסגר ראשון (v. 39), and after ,חליצה קיצה וטיחה and הסגר שני (vv. 40-42), either the נגע reappears, חזר (v. 43), which entails נתיצה (v. 45), or it does not reappear, לא חזר (v. 48), in which case it is declared טהור and צפרים (v. 49 et seq.), have to be brought. But just this course of events described in our text, postulates a whole series of other eventualities. Instead of פשיון, the נגע can remain unaltered, עמד; instead of increasing in can decrease in intensity כהה, shade down to a מראה כשרה, or even disappear altogether, הלך לו, or what amounts to the same thing, shrink in size פחות מכשיעור, have become smaller than two גריסין. This would already give four modifications, הלך ,כהה ,עמד ,פשה, each of which could occur after הסגר ראשון or after הסגר שני, accordingly eight, to which must be added the two cases mentioned in the text, חזר or לא חזר after חליצה וטיחה, altogether ten modifications, the treatment of which is laid down in the Halacha as follows: עשרה בתים הן הכהה בראשון (1), והולך ,לו (2), קולפו והוא טהור, והכהה בשני (3), והולך לו (4), קולפו והוא טעון צפרים והפושה בראשון חולץ וקוצה וטח ונותן לו שבוע חזר (5), נותץ, לא חזר (6), טעון צפרים, עמד בראשון ופשה בשני חולץ וקוצה וטח ונותן לו שבוע חזר (7), נותץ, לא חזר (8), טעון צפרים, עמד בזה ובזה חולץ וקוצה וטח ונותן לו שבוע חזר (9), נותץ לא חזר (10), טעון צפרים, (ת״כ Negaim 13,1). We note:—at the first :הסגר כהה או הלך לאחר הסגר ראשון קולף וטהור, עמד מסגיר פשה חולץ ומסגיר at the second כהה או הלן לאחר הסגר ב׳ קולף וטהור וטעון צפרים, עמד או :הסגר פשה חולץ ומסגיר. So that the difference between the first and second הסגר lies in that, if the נגע gets weaker or disappears after the first הסגר, the place has only to be scraped away and thereby becomes טהור without צפרים, but after the second הסגר it would require the צפרים; and further in a case where the נגע remains unaltered, after the first הסגר it has to be מוסגר, without חליצה) חליצה only required if פשיון occurs), whereas after the second ,הסגר חליצה must be done whether עמד or נתיצה .פשה, pulling down the whole house is only necessary if the נגע reappears, חזר, after חליצה.

These Halachic Laws are indicated in the text from which they are derived. In v. 44, that which is demanded in connection with פרח is expressed by the term פשה, which in its real sense is only applicable to the time after הסגר where חליצה had not to have been done. That is taken to indicate also the case of פשה לאחר הסגר שני, i.e. when the priest comes at the end of the first week and finds it unaltered: שבא בסוף שבוע ראשון ומצאו עומד ובא בסוף שבוע שני ומצאו פשה, (for this ובא הכהן does refer to after a הסגר שני; see note on v. 43); and by a גזרה שוה on ושב הכהן (v. 39) and ובא הכהן (v. 44) — זו היא שיבה זו היא ביאה — learns that just as the first ושב הכהן וגו׳, treating of פשיון after the first הסגר entails חליצה etc., so does the ובא הכהן וגו׳ here, indicating פשיון after the second הסגר, demand a similar treatment (ת״כ). In the sense of this Halacha the meaning of the sentence: ובא הכהן וראה והנה פשה הנגע בבית, would have to be taken as being in parenthesis and put in brackets, thus:— (“and equally so, if only now when he comes for the second time, he finds that the נגע has spread in the house”), i.e. and the procedure prescribed in vv. 40—43 must be followed here too. This hermeneutic case, where a גזרה שוה is learnt not only from two expressions which are identical, such as שיבה ,שיבה, but also where they are similar as here, שיבה and ביאה, is taken in Yoma 2b, and many other places, from this example here to be an extension of the idea of a גזרה שוה (and deductions based on a גזרה שוה can, of course, only be made if the tradition for such deduction has come down from משה. I.L.). Again in v. 48, by the choice of expression לא פשה in place of לא פרח and by the repetition in ואם בא יבא, the modification עומד לאחר שתי ביאות, i.e. עומד בראשון ובשני, is indicated and the laws for this Halacha are also derived from analogy with נגעי בגדים.

That נגעי בתים, like נגעי אדם ובגדים, have nothing whatsoever to do with precautionary sanitary or health measures, but that they have exclusively the meaning of an admonishing and warning finger-mark of God’s displeasure over social misbehaviour, is evident — apart from all the characteristics which they share with them — also from the even more characteristic laws which apply specially to them. So above all the peculiarity that they only have any meaning attached to them when they occur in ארץ ישראל, and even there only when the Land had been divided up right to individual holdings, and only apply to such buildings which can definitely be described as private dwellings. This quite definitely shows that the נגע does not refer to the building as such, but to the personality of its inhabitant to whom it is evidently addressed. It is not the house which is affected but the “home”, the domesticity, the sphere which individualises a human life towards the general community, which a house represents. That, too, is why it is only a נגע if it appears on the walls, בקירות הבית, which are really the “isolating” element of a house, and on the actual material of the walls, the stone, wood and plaster, and only on a house of normal construction, a four walled structure and neither of brick nor marble. All this to make it perfectly clear that the whole thing is symbolic, to prevent any thought of there being any other purpose, and to insist on the point of regarding a house as the place of human home-making.

Amongst the social wrong-doings which in general provoke נגעים as the mark of God’s displeasure, our חכמים name one as being quite specially the one to which נגעי בתים are primarily directed. And that is selfishness which shuts itself up against being of service in neighbourly kindness. They stress אשר לו הבית to mean שמיחד ביתו לו, who keeps his home exclusively for himself, that מדת סדום which applies that principle of Sodom, which, misusing the sharp principle of the rights of property, says: שלי שלי שלך שלך, “what I have is mine, what you have is yours”.
