He forgets that to the exclusiveness of rights must be added the inclusiveness of love, to צדק must be added צדקה,if society is to become a Jewish society before God, and every house is to be allowed to have and keep the right of private living in it. So that in א״י, all נגעים on houses on the ground of God’s Torah, express His judgment on this cold naked loveless conception of justice and rights, and the proclamation of this judgment begins just at the moment when individual right to landed property receives its sanction by the parcelling out of the Land to individual owners under the aegis of that Torah. Then, in the sense of the חכמים, how apt are the introductory words: כי תבאו אל ארץ כנען אשר אני נותן לכם לאחוזה ונתתי נגע צרעת בבית ארץ אחוזתכם ובא אשר לו הבית והגיד לכהן לאמר כנגע נראה לי בבית! “From the moment when you take possession of the Land which I give you, will I send the touch of My Finger on houses of your possession, so that the one who owns the house for himself, must come to the priest and say: “it seems to me that God’s Finger is pointing to my house! ! !” —

The various modifications of the course taken by the נגע on a house—with the variations of remaining unchanged, getting smaller or disappearing, spreading, returning, or not returning, until the final pulling down of the house or declaring it alright again — are to be taken, in the same way as נגעים on people, as so many admonitions, warning, intensification, and time for consideration to the owner of the house. The prescribed קליפה which has to be done in even the weakest form: כהה והלך לסוף הסגר ראשון, is designed to keep the נגע-warning in permanent remembrance for the future. The sevenfold sprinkling of the blood of the slaughtered bird, together with “living” water and the live bird and the bundle of cedar-hyssop-carmine-dyed-wool, on to the upper lintel of the threshold of the house, as well as the sending of the unslaughtered bird into the free open country, before restoring the house to a justified private domain in the midst of the communal life, preach, in a similar way to that of the ritual before the re-admission of a person into the social community, the lesson which has to be taken to heart as the preliminary condition for an undisturbed life. Namely, that living purely for oneself, having all one’s actions dictated by selfish motives is a justified mode of life only for organic life in every stage and degree of development in the vegetable and animal world. Man, however, can only begin to have a justified social existence by readiness for self-sacrifice and service to others, by that, thereby, he gains eternal life; and only if his house, that home of his private life strives with unfailing energy to reach the ideal of unselfish devotion to duty, then and only then, can the walls carry a “roof”, then, and only then, the private life, shutting itself up in four walls can obtain and keep protection from Above, (cf. מזוזות ומשקוף at the פסח, on Ex. Ch. 12,7).

By טומאת מגע ומשא וביאה of the בית המנוגע, and even more by an אבן המנוגע having to be avoided as a מקום טמא outside all inhabited parts of the community, a נגע is made into a solemn permanent warning against similar unsocial faults for every member of the Jewish national community on the soil of God’s Torah.

That simply entering such a house only brings טומאה on the person himself, while staying in the house, שהה בכדי אכילת פרס, makes בגדים שעליו, the clothes he has on, (and anything he has in his pockets etc. I.L.), also טמא, gives entering the conception of merely of coming into contact, while staying in the house has the idea of actively taking part and joining with one’s whole personality, a similar idea to the difference between מגע נבלה and משא נבלה (see on Ch. 11,47), and in the sense of the idea of נגעים is the same comparison as עמידה בדרך חטאים to ישיבה במושב לצים (Ps. 1,1).

Vv. 54—57. זאת התורה וגו׳. The order in which the names of the various נגעים are placed here at the recapitulation of the נגעים-laws may be understood in this way: כל נגע צרעת and נתק form the two main classes which together comprise all forms of נגע צרעת .נגעים is a positive alteration in the outer surface of things either on the skin of a person, on clothing material, or on the wall of a house. But נתק is the one form of נגע which becomes מוסגר and מוחלט also in a completely negative character, loss of hair and continuous loss of hair, פשיון, as well as שער צהוב. See notes on Ch. 13,29. So that: זאת התורה לכל נגע צרעת ולנתק is the general statement and includes all forms of נגעים, positive and negative. ולצרעת הבגד ולבית ולשאת וגו׳: then reckons retrospectively the נגעים which appear on the various object which cause the variations in their appearance and treatment: cloth, house, person. It starts with בגד and then follows בית and אדם, — although, looking backwards, we should have expected the order to be ,בית בגד and אדם, — the reason probably being, because בגד has the simplest treatment — its state of טהרה is regained without צפרים etc., טהרת בית מנוגע demands the more complicated ritual of צפרים etc., and טהרת מצורע requires צפרים and קרבן. From this summarising זאת התורה וגו׳, the ת״כ further derives the law that all the נגעים-laws form one connected idea, so that only one who completely understands all of them is competent to judge any one particular case, and כהן שבקי בנגעים אבל לא בנתקים וכו׳ וכו׳ לא יראה את הנגעים עד שיהא בקי בהם ובשמותיהם.

V. 2. בני ישראל מטמאין בזיבה ואין עכו״ם מטמאין :דברו אל בני ישראל בזיבה, (Nidda 34a).— מן הדיבור ואילך :כי יהיה, even for בני ישראל, the טומאת זיבה only applies to such occurrences of זב which come after the Law had been given, simlarly to ,ולא מחמת דבר אחר :מבשרו — .(ת״כ) ,טומאת נגעים (ת״כ), or as it puts it in Kerithoth 8b, and elsewhere: ולא מחמת אונסו, the occurrence of זב only causes טומאה if it is brought about by some local organic disturbance of the part affected, but not if it is a secondary effect of other illnesses or other nervous causes, such as from over-eating or drinking, from physical exertion, from mental excitement, obscene pictures or pornographic literature etc. Hence, בשבעה דרכים בודקין את הזב עד שלא נזקק לזיבה במאכל ובמשתה ובמשא ובקפיצה בחולי ובמראה ובהרהור, seven other possible causes have to be eliminated before a man becomes “זב״, viz. overeating, overdrinking, carrying or lifting heavy weights, violent exercise (including riding), general illness, looking at sexually exciting sights, having similar thoughts, (Zabim 2,2). זובו טמא הוא: the exudation itself is מטמא במגע ובמשא, and more, not like חשוכי בגדים במגע ,נבלה, but even מגע is מטמא בגדים, (Kelim 1,3 & Nidda 55,b).

V. 3. טומאתו בזובו תלויה ואינה תלויה בימים :טומאתו בזובו, the טומאה is solely dependent on the occurrences, ראיות of the exudation, and a second or third recurrence even on the same day entails a higher degree of טומאה (see below and v. 14), which, in the case of a זבה (v. 25), only applies if the repetition occurs on consecutive days רר בשרו וגו׳ — .(ת״כ): the exudation may be flowing, i.e. plentiful, as ריר (Sam. I 31,14), or: החתים בשרו וגו׳, or only sufficient for the organ to close itself for the discharge to stay in the aperture, (הל׳ מחוסרי כפרה ,רמב״ם ,ת״כ, 2,9, but see the כ״מ on הל׳ אבות הטומאה 5,1). In בשרו את זובו the organ itself, his בשר, is clearly the subject, and also serves as the subject of החתים of which the following בשרו would be the object:— Verse 2 mentions the זב twice and then mentions זב זובו טמא הוא — ,טומאה —; in verse 3 it occurs three times and then mentioned בזובו את זובו, מזובו טמאתו היא — טומאה —, the Gemora in Megilla 8a, uses this as a peg on which to hang the Halacha that with two ראיות the טומאת זב is fully established as far as מגע ומשא, משכב ומושב, ז׳ נקיים, וביאת מים חיים, but only after three ראיות the duty of bringing the offering prescribed in v. 14 is imposed: מנה הכתוב שתים, וקרא טמא שלש, וקרא טמא הא כיצד, שתים לטומאה ושלש לקרבן. A single ראיה is considered a normal non-pathological exudation of semen, and comes under the class of טומאה described in v. 16.

V. 4. כל המשכב אשר ישכב עליו וגו׳ וכל הכלי אשר ישב עליו וגו׳. Not every object on which a זב has lain or sat attains the טומאה described here and in the following verses, but only such which are suitable for lying or sitting ראוי, and which are meant to be used for that purpose only מיוחד לכך, hence it does not say משכב אשד שכב and כלי אשר ישב עליו, but אשר ישכב אשר ישב עליו ,עליו, “which is meant” for that purpose. So that not כפה סאה וישב עליו וכו׳, not if he upturns a measuring-barrel or anything similar and sits on it, because such an object is meant for another use, and the formula: “עמוד ונעשה מלאכתנו״, “Get off, and let us get on with our work”. (ת״כ Sabbath 59a), can be applied to it. But משכב and מושב are only given as examples and include every article which is meant to serve as a support for the human body: standing, lying, sitting or swinging, and in any such position of the body whether: עומד ,יושב ,שוכב ,נתלה ,נשען, a זב would make any of these articles טמא, including, accordingly, שוכב על ,יושב על המשכב המושב, etc. The common idea, which the Halacha takes to include all these supports intended for these various positions of the body, is termed: מדרס (Zabim 2,4, רמב״ם commentary thereon.) But the article—(chair, bed, mattress, stand, hammock etc. I.L.) — must have the purpose of the body resting on or against it, עשויה להנאת מדרס, but not anything like a ladder, סולם, the rungs of which only serve לירד בו ולעלות, to support the body in motion (תוספות Menachoth 31a, ד״ה שידה). It is not necessary for the זב to have direct contact with the article, but, if the article is one to which טומאת מרס is applicable, it becomes טמא as soon as the body of the זב rests on it, even if there are a whole number of כלים in between, even if it was under a great heavy stone against the weight of which the pressure of the weight of the body of the זב would be completely negligible. This latter case is called תחת אבן מסמא, (הל׳ משכב ומושב ,רמב״ם 5,5; כ״מ thereon and תוספות Nidda 55b). According to ר״ש on כלים 1,3, under the heading of אבן מסמא would be understood any burden, even if it is carried indirectly by means of objects themselves not liable to טומאה, and simply laden, without movement, משא בלי היסט, in contrast to the משא of all other טומאות which is identical with היסט (see notes on Ch. 11,25). The term אבן מסמא is explained by ושומת על פום גובא (Daniel 6,18), where it is used for a large stone only to be moved with great difficulty.— כלי אבנים, כלי גללים, כלי אדמה, as well as כלים made of marine materials or bones of birds, are not liable to טומאת מדרס similarly to other טומאות (see notes on Ch. 11,32). But כלי חרס are also excluded from טומאת מדרס (Sabbath 84a).

V. 5. משכב ומושב :ואיש אשר וגו׳ become אב הטומאה and are מטמא אדם וכלים במגע ואדם במשא, and אדם במגע, to such an extent that בגדים שעליו also become טמא, i.e. any כלי, with the exception of a כלי חרס, with which he is in contact בשעת מגעו becomes ראשון, (cf. on נבלה, Ch. 11,25).

V. 6. וחישב על הכלי וגו׳. In exactly the same way as a כלי מדרס becomes טמא, not only by direct contact with the זב, but as soon as it comes under the weight of the body of the זב, so does a זב impart his טומאה to another person who is טהור not only by touch, but as soon as the weight of his body rests on him, whether עומד ,יושב ,שוכב ,נתלה or נשען, even through several intervening articles, even it there was an אבן מסמא between them, even (ת״כ) ,עשרה מושבות זה על זה ואפילו על גבי אבן מסמא.

V. 7. והנגע בבשר וגו׳, on the actual body but not on anything that is connected with him by way of ornament or even as clothing, provided that such articles are not טמא מדרס, that he is not sitting, lying or standing on them. They would only be ראשון and אדם וכלים are only מקבלי טומאה from זב .אב הטומאה is חמור than נבלה inasmuch as even מגעו, as already remarked on v. 4, is מטמא בגדים שעליו.

V. 8. רוקו :וכי ירק הזב וגו׳, which includes כיחו וניעו ומי האף שלו are אב הטומאה and מטמא במגע ובמשא, (Nidda 55b), equally with זובו etc. (v. 2). They come under the general classification of משקין של זב, of which, however, certain liquids, e.g. זיעה, perspiration, etc., are completely טהורים and others, e.g. דמעת עינו, tears, etc., are not אב הטומאה. The משקין של זב, which have טומאה חמורה, are also called מעינות של זב. The idea which they have in common is, that, like the saliva, they מתעגל ויוצא וחוזר ונבלע, they gather from the glands in the body and can unconsciously be retained and kept back, (Nidda 56a).

V. 9. מרכב :וכל המרכב וגו׳ is the equipment by means of which the body is able to ride. The saddle itself is, of course, מושב. So in Erubin 27a: האוכף טמא מושב, the saddle is טמא מושב, and התפוס טמא מרכב, but the bridle is טמא מרכב. In כלים 23,2, several parts of the riding equipment of camels and horses are named, which come under the heading of מרכב.

V. 10. בכל אשר יהיה תחתיו :וכל הנגע וגו׳ refers to the מרכב mentioned in the previous verse, by מגע, it is only מטמא אדם, but not בגדים שעליו, the clothes he is wearing, or כלים שנוגע בהם בחיבורין, anything which he is touching at the time. In this, מרכב is different to משכב ומושב. Of נגוע במרכב, it says here that it is only יטמא עד הערב, without כיבוס בגדים, but והנושא אותם וגו׳, “he who bears them” — and אותם comprises all the objects mentioned before: מושב ,זב ,מעינות ,מרכב and מה ביז מרכב .יכבס בגדיו וגו׳ — משכב למושב, מרכב חלק מגעו ממשאו, ומושב לא חלק מגעו ממשאו, (Kelim 23,3).

The Gemora in Nidda 32b, uses the words of our text: וכל הנוגע בכל אשר יהיה תחתיו יטמא, to apply also to the teaching of עליונו של זב, i.e. the treatment of objects which are above the זב who rests תחתיו under them without necessarily touching them. Such objects are there declared to be ראשון and so can only be מטמא eatables אוכלין ומשקין, but not persons or vessels. In this, עליונו של זב, differs from תחתונו, which is אב הטומאה. This lesser טומאה of עליונו של זב, is termed מדף (from קול עלה נדף), to designate its weaker character. It is difficult to reconcile these two opposite ways of taking the meaning of the word תחתיו (see תוספות there in Nidda), and כ״מ on הל׳ ממו״מ 6,3, finds in this the reason for רמב״ם, in opposition to ראב״ד who takes this טומאת מדף of עליונו של זב to be only דרבנן. The common expression: בועל נדה מטמא משכב תחתון כעליון, (see v. 24), would seem to show that it is דאורייתא.

V. 11. וכל אשר יגע בו הזב וגו׳. After we are told that anybody who has become טמא through a זב or even indirectly, by anything that itself has become טמא through a זב, must ורחץ במים וגו׳, that he can only become טהור by bathing the whole body, and for the זב himself, moreover, it says that: ורחץ בשרו במים חיים וטהר (v. 13), gushing “living” water is required, it is quite impossible to think that וידיו לא שטף במים here can mean that he could become טהור by a mere rinsing of his hands. שטיפת ידים במים only expresses the effect the bathing of the whole body — including of course the hands — has on the hands. By bathing the body, the character of טומאה is “washed away” from the hands too, which had affected them by the טומאה of the whole body. But the reason why, here, just the hands are singled out as being affected by טומאה and to be freed from it by this bathing, and why just by זב the טומאה of the hands, as being transmitted by the body, is expressed by the same term (שטף. I.L.), which is used immediately afterwards for vessels which have become טמא by means of a זב, can be found in the Halacha and the specific idea of the טומאת זב. For the Halacha teaches (Nidda 43,a): כל אשר יגע בו הזב וידיו לא שטף במים זהו הסיטו של זב, that here it is not talking of the mere touching by the זב, the effect of which has already been declared by והנוגע בבשר הזב וגו׳ (v. 7), but of הסיטו של זב, of the moving of another man by the זב. This is unique in the whole range of the laws of שלא מצינו לו טומאה בכל התורה כולה :טומאה, or, as it puts it in Sabbath 83b: שלא מצינו לו חבר בכל התורה כולה. For elsewhere, היסט always designates a טמא object being moved indirectly by the טהור. We have explained this היסט to be a secondary idea of משא, or rather to be identical with it. It is not the body, as in מגע, which comes into contact with the טומאה, but the power, the force of the body which is exercised on it, (see notes on Ch. 11,25), and that is why the טומאה is extended to the whole personality, to כלים בחיבורין. But never do we find that the היסט of a טהור by the power of the טומאה, a moving of the טהור by means of the טומאה also makes the former טמא. This is the case exclusively here with a זב, and with that of the equally-ranking נדה and זבה and יולדת. But if here it is speaking of the power, the activity which the זב exercises on people or things, it is at once understandable why here ידים, the specific organs of the power of moving are stressed. We shall find, when we try to get at the whole idea of this טומאת זב, that it is not just Man’s life of Man’s personality — (the sphere of his night-life. I.L.) — with which this activity, not his deeds, as in the case of מצורע, but the other phase of טומאה deals. It is accordingly highly significant that here at the זב, the טומאת ידים is designated as being secondary, as a טומאה which comes over to them from the טומאה of the rest of the body. This may well be to lay down the weighty Truth, that, when the other side of the physical human being has sunk to טומאת זב, then the side of human life represented by ידים, Man’s actions, does not remain free from טומאה, (see below).

But the Halacha (ibid) goes on: ואפקיה רחמנא בלשון נגיעה למימרא דהיסט ונגיעה כידיו מה התם מאבראי אף הכא מאבראי, i.e. the reason why our text uses this roundabout manner and described היסטו של זב not, as usually done by the term משא, but by נגיעה and ידיו, is to affirm the fact that there is a difference in the case of זב to ordinary היסט. Whereas, in other cases היסט by a טהור in contrast to מגע makes him טמא even בבית סתרים, e.g. הנושא נבלה בקומטו, the היסטו של זב, like his מגע, is restricted to movements made by means of his external body, such as ידיו.

V. 12. וכלי חרש אשר יגע בו הזב וגו׳. In Ch. 11,33, it has already been remarked that כלי חרש is only היסטו של זב ;מקבל טומאה מאוירו is the only case where a כלי חרש becomes טמא also from its outside, that is why it does not say here בתוכו, but בו; for, in connection with the preceding verse this נגיעה is also ישבר .(ת״כ) ,היסט, see Ch. 11,33. ישטף במים is, like the term יכבס בגדיו, equivalent to טבילה.

V. 13. וכי יטהר הזב. We have already remarked that the complete טומאה necessitating ספירת ז׳ נקיים and טבילת מים חיים comes already after two ראיות (on v. 3), and that the necessity for bringing a קרבן only arises after three ראיות. Thus, Megilla 8a: אין בין זב הרואה שתי ראיות לרואה שלש אלא קרבן. So that the ספירת ז׳ נקיים and the טבילה במים חיים prescribed here have to be done even after two שתהא ,לטהרתו :שבעת ימים לטהרתו —.ראיות טהרתו אחת, the seven days which he has to count must form one unbroken “clear” period of seven consecutive days. A single טומאה recurrence even on the seventh day, even after he had already been טובל, undoes all the previous counting, סותר למפרע, and he has to start a fresh counting of seven “clear” days. Similarly it says in v. 28 concerning the ספירת ז׳ נקיים of the ואחר תטהר :זבה, (Nidda 68b): אחר אחר לכולן שלא תהא טומאה מפסקת ביניהן. In one single case only is an occurrence of the טומאה on the seventh day after the טבילה not retrospective and that is the case of v. 12, the היסט כלי חרס, which can only occur by a זב. A כלי חרס שהיסט בין טבילה לראיה, remains טהור (Megilla 8a).— :היקש כיבוס בגדיו לרחיצת בשרו :וכבס בגדיו ורחץ בשרו במים טבילת כלים here is placed together with טבילת גופו, both must be done בנקיות, before the טבילה of either, every foreign body must be conscientiously removed; חציצה applies also to ת״כ) ,טבילת כלים see on v. 16).

זב :ורחץ בשרו במים חיים is the only טמא who requires מים חיים for טבילה. For all others, and even the כליו של זב, the מי מקוה suffices (ת״כ see on XI,36).— וטהר, the טבילה on the seventh day, as already remarked, is only absolutely effective for היסט כלי חרס only, otherwise it is conditioned on the day remaining “clear” until nightfall.

V. 14. לפני ה׳ אל פתח אהל מועד: at the Nikanor Gate, similarly to the מצורע in Ch. 14,11. The gate itself, שער ניקנור, the border line between עזרת נשים and עזרת ישראל, is reckoned as still belonging to מחנה לויה which begins at the הד הבית and reaches to the עזרת ישראל where the מחנה שכינה begins. See note on Numb. V.,1—4. Just as the מצורע has to be excluded even from the מחנה ישראל, the זב וזבה etc., were not allowed to enter מחנה לויה. It is not quite decided whether מן התורה a טבול יום דזב is similar to a זב in this respect. (See Nazir 44b, תוספות there and Zebachim 32b; see also the כ״מ on הל׳ ביאת מקדש 3,9, regarding מחוסר כפורים במחנה שכינה). If טבול יום דזב מן התורה אסור במחנה לויה then the זב here must have gone into the מקוה already on the seventh day before nightfall so that with העריב שמש he would have lost the character of a טבול יום.

V. 15. ועשה אותם הכהן אחד חטאת וגו׳. Such pairs of doves for an offering are called קינין, and each single dove of such a קן a פרידה. Here it says: יקח לו וגו׳ ונתנם אל הכהן ועשה אותם הכהן וגו׳, he gives the pair together, סתומין, to the priest, and only at the actual time of offering them does this latter designate one as a חטאת and the other an עולה. Above in Ch. 12,18, at the similar offering of a יולדת, it says: ולקחה שתי תודים וגו׳ אחד לעלה ואחד להטאת וכפר וגו׳, the bringer, beforehand, takes one for an עולה and the other for a חטאת, and the priest has to offer each one accordingly. Hence, the dictum in Nazir 26b: אין הקינין מתפרשות אלא או בלקיחת בעלים או בעשיית כהן, at two points only can the pair of doves be given their destination, either at the time of their being picked out by the bringers, or by the priest at the moment when they are actually being offered, but not at any time in between.

V. 16. ורחץ במּים את כל בשרו: every tiny part of the body must come into direct contact with the water, no extraneous matter may be present on the body. במים: in the water, in the מי מקוה, not in water, but in water as an element, מחוברין not מים שכל גופו עולה בהן :את כל בשרו .שאובין, the bath must contain a quantity of water, sufficient to cover the whole of the body, אמה על אמה ברום שלש אמות, this is three cubic cubits, which represents the size of a Mikvah containing forty סאה (Pesachim 109a & b), (see note on Ch. 11,36).— את הטפל לבשרו ווהו שער :את כל בשרו, by the addition of the particle את (which is always taken as extending the object, see note on Gen. 1,1), the conception, body, is designated as extending in its widest sense, so that the hair is included. The hair, too, must be completely immersed in the water with the body, and must have nothing חועץ on it, (Erubin 4,b).

V. 19. בבשרה: Here it does not say מבשרה as it does above in v. 2, here the limitation מחמת אונס does not apply, (see Nidda 36b).— כל חייבי טבילות טבילתן ביום נדה ויולדת טבילתן בלילה, :שבעת ימים תהיה בנדתה דתניא יכול תהא טובלת מבעוד יום, תלמוד לומר שבעת ימים תהיה בנדתה, תהא בנדתה כל שבעה, (Pesachim 90b), their טבילה can only be done after the complete passing of seven days, accordingly only in the night after the seven days.— יטמא עד הערב: he is ראשון not אב, similarly to נוגע בזב, but also similarly has to do כיבוס בגדים as even נוגע במשכבה (v. 21), (ת״כ) ,בגדיו.

V. 20—23. נדה and זבה are exactly the same as זב regarding טומאת ואם על המשכב הוא וגו׳ —.משכב ומושב ומרכב והיסט ומעינות: This verse 23 is very difficult. According to the accents it would be dealing with נוגע במשכבה או במושבה, and it would further be demanded that היא יושבת עליו בנגעו בו. But נוגע במשכבה ובמושבה for טומאה בכיבוס בגדים has already been declared in verses 20—22 — while here it does not say כיבוס בגדים — and besides it was evident there, that there was no necessity for the נדה to be sitting on the משכב or מושב at the time it was touched, as long as it was a כלי המיוחד לשכיבה או לישיבה, and had been used by someone in the condition of נדה. In any case, as what was necessary to be said about מגע במשכבה, had already been said, ואם על המשכב הוא can only want to discuss a fresh case here, where the משכב is not touched. Actually in אם על :ת״כ המשכב הוא is taken to refer to the case where the weight of the body of the טהור is above the underlying משכב or מושב. A similar case to that discussed in v. 6 with a זב. There the person who is weighing on the משכב, without touching it in any way, becomes טמא, however many layers may be intervening, even על אבן מסמא (see notes on v. 6). Here, by the “הוא״, the additional condition is indicated that the טהור must have the whole of his body, or at least the greater part of his body which is always considered as being the same as the whole, רובו ככולו, resting above the משכב or מושב, in the same way as a משכב or מושב itself only becomes טמא in such conditions by a זב etc. (ת״כ) ,עד שינשא רובו עליו. In Pesachim 3a, we learn, לעולם יספר אדם בלשון נקיה :תנא דבי רבי ישמעאל, “one should always use the “cleanest’ possible expressions”, שהרי בזב קראו מרכב ובאשה קראו מושב, as we find the Torah unreservedly uses the term מרכב when it speaks of a זב, but changes it to מושב when referring to a woman. Rashi (ibid) — in contrast to תוספות, who, following ת״כ, takes על הכלי to refer to the מרכב of a woman — teaches the same lesson from the whole sentence: על הכלי אשר היא יושבת עליו. If we note further מרכב differs from מושב characteristically in that, as we noted in v. 10, מגע of מרכב does not necessitate כבוס בגדים as משא would, חלוק מגעו ממשאו, then we think we are justified in taking the whole sentence: כלי אשר היא יושבת עליו בנגעו בו יטמא עד ערב, as another way of saying מרכב. For a כלי on which she sits, by which if he touches it, he only becomes טמא until the evening and does not require כבוס בגדים is actually only מרכב. The verse follows the preceding one in which כבוס בגדים is prescribed for מגע משכב ומושב. To that our verse 23 adds: “and so also if the weight of his body rests on a משכב or even a מרכב, although the מגע of the latter entails טומאה without כיבוס בגדים״. Even so the accent on בו is not explained.

V. 24. ותהי נדתה עליו, her condition of being “separated”, goes over to him, he becomes אב הטומאה as she is and is מטמא אדם וכלים. Moreover, he is not יעלה לרגלה, i.e. he does not take over the same condition regarding time that she is in, so that if she has already passed three נדה-days, he would not also have only four more days of טומאה, but יטמא שבעת ימים, he remains for full seven days in the state of וכל המשכב אשר ישכב עליו .טומאה יטמא, but his משכב only gets a טומאה קלה, it only becomes ראשון, is only מטמא אוכלין ומשקין, but not אדם וכלים as the משכב של זב does, (Nidda 33a). This טומאה קלה of the משכב בועל נדה is usually expressed as מטמא משכב תחתון כעליון, i.e. כעליונו של זב which is also only ראשון. See v. 10.

V. 25. ימים רבים .ואשה כי יזוב זוב דמה וגו׳: at least three consecutive days. סמוך לנדתה :בלא עת נדתה, after the passing of the seven נדה-days, accordingly, the first, second and third day after the seven נדה-days; או כי מופלג לנדתה :תזוב על נדתה, somewhat later, i.e. one day later, the second third and fourth day after the seven נדה-days, in both cases the procedure ordered in v. 28, has to be followed, viz. seven “clear” days have first to be counted, ז׳ נקיים and the קרבן (v. 29 et seq.), then to be brought before טהרה is regained. The condition, which thus arises, after the ימי נדה have passed is called זיבה to differentiate it from נדה. These ימי זיבה, accordingly, last, in the first case, till the tenth day after ימי נדה, and in the second, till the twelfth, and the Halacha teaches, (Nidda 73a), that whenever ראיות occur on three consecutive days in these eleven days, even on the ninth, tenth or eleventh day, ז׳ נקיים וקרבן are demanded, and ימי נדה can only start again after such ז׳ נקיים have passed. These eleven-days are accordingly termed the כל ימי זוב טומאתה וגו׳ —.י״א יום שבין נדה לנדה, but if an occurrence of זוב happens on two or only one of these eleven days, then כימי נדתה תהיה וגו׳, it entails טומאה like ordinary נדה with regards to טומאת משכב ומושב, and although she does not require ז׳ נקיים, she must have one יום נקי for the טומאה to cease. This condition is called: שומרת יום כנגד יום. The condition which starts with three-days occurrences is termed: זבה גדולה, with one or two days: זבה קטנה. So that ימי נדה differ from ימי זיבה in that a repetition of a ראיה during ימי נדה does not bring about any intensification of the טומאה. A single ראיה entails seven days טומאה and further ראיות do not require ז׳ נקיים and קרבן. During the following eleven days ראיות cause either זבה קטנה or זבה גדולה with the consequences described above. In accordance with the law given in Ch. 18,19, seven “clear” days, ז׳ נקיים, have to be counted for both זבה גדולה and קטנה (Nidda 66a).
V. 28. לעצמה :וספרה לה, (ת״כ & Kethuboth 72a). In Gittin 2b, תוספות refers to this as an example of the law that עד אחד נאמן באיסורין, (see ibid 17,b).

V. 31. נור :והורתם את בני ישדאל (from which is derived נזר, the crown which distinguishes or “separates” its wearer, and נזיר, the one who distinguished or “separates” himself from the mass of the people by adopting a priestly, self-sanctifying life, see on Numbers 6,2), has the fundamental meaning of keeping away from, “separating”, but not simply in space but also a “keeping away” which demands a moral self-control, hence also הנזר (Zach. 7,3), to fast. The הנזר demanded here, the keeping away from all טומאה, and especially מטומאתם, from the טומאה of bodily conditions brought on by themselves, טומאה היוצאה עליהן מגופו, does require the use of moral self-control, and has indeed, as the observation of the טומאה-laws in general has, the ultimate purpose of insisting on the fact that Man is master of his moral self and can exercise self-control. So that the use of this particular expression for the “keeping away” demanded here is surely of deep significance. This command to observe the טומאה-laws does directly place it under the self-controlling conscientiousness of the people in a similar way to which the duty of שמירה demands it for the whole Torah and orders not only the avoidance of טומאה which is already in existence, but also the avoidance of its proximity in place or in time when it is likely to occur (Moed Katan 5a, & Nidda 63b). But this command of keeping away from טומאה, is not made directly to the people themselves, it does not say: וינזרו בני ישראל מטומאתם, the mission is given to Moses and Aaron to teach and educate the people so as to bring them to such keeping away from טומאה. For the whole mission of Moses and Aaron, the knowledge of and keeping of the Torah, and the everlasting constant education to both is essentially, and in the very first place, dependent on the keeping clearly in the mind of the People the conception of טהרה and the consciousness of its existence. That is why the reason for this demand is also given as: ולא ימותו בטמאתם בטמאם את משכני אשר בתוכם. The observation of any one of the טומאה-laws places every single person in the Nation, from the highest to the lowest, in direct relation to the Sanctuary of the Torah, to משכן ה׳ by means of which God wants to announce His direct Presence in the Nation. Every such טומאה-law says to every single individual of the People that this Sanctuary of the Torah does not wish to have its place in “Moses and Aaron”, not in the sphere of the spiritual and priestly elite of the Nation, but בתוך בני ישראל ,בתוכם, and places the free elevation of oneself above every טומאה conception of moral force or lack of self-mastery, as the first demand to everybody towards moral nobility. Inasmuch as God set up the Home of His Torah, which He calls His Home, משכני — with all its demands which can only be carried out on the basis of טהרה, i.e. on moral freedom — in the midst of ordinary people this Torah cannot be based on the Utopia of a complete absence of sensuality, but as it immediately says in the following chapter v. 16: השכן אתם בתוך טומאתם, and as the significant explanation of our verse in ת״כ runs: בטמאם את משכני אשר בתוכם אע״פ שהם טמאים שכינה ביניהם. Hence, the whole phase of the human life of the senses, with all its manifold tempting inclinations to moral lack of freedom, was completely present in God’s Mind and it was just with an eye to this טומאה-phase of human nature, and “next” to it (שכן) that He places the Torah as a condition for His שכינה, so that this Torah, with the power of its enlightening and life-giving flame, should awake just that other, the bodily phase of Man, to free self-mastery over all his unfree senses, and lead him to elevate everything of himself, even the most sensual of his senses to the use of free, God-serving acts, and up to the goal of moral victory. But that was why the alternative was placed before this Nation: either it lets itself be educated by this Torah to a state of טהרה of self-control, which is in accordance with its demands, and so already gains even here below eternal life in the proximity of God, or it perishes in its טומאה, and by its טומאה, as persistence in its טומאה in contrast to “God’s living in its midst” destroys the idea of moral purity which must be coincident with it.

Not for naught is the כרת penalty for טומאת מקדש (Ch. 17,16), expressed here by the term of ordinary מיתה, for, for Israel, the whole progress of its quite ordinary earthly life is attached to its striving upwards to the pure accomplishment of the moral-mission set for it by the Sanctuary of the Torah.
V. 32. בעל ראיה א׳ :הזב, who, as remarked on v. 2, is on the same level as the case discussed in v. 16. Both have only טומאת ערב and are not מטמא משכב ומושב.

V. 33. טומאת זיבה :והזב את זובו, which is מטמא משכב ומושב like נדה, but is different for זכר and נקבה. For a זכר, if two מטמא מו״מ :ראיות ובעי ז׳ נקיים וטבילה במים חיים, but does not have to bring a קרבן; if three ראיות, has also to bring a קרבן. For a נקבה, if one or two days, מטמא מו״מ, but is only שומרת יום כנגד יום, and if three days requires ז׳ נקיים and קרבן.

The bodily conditions which result in the טומאות treated of in this chapter have this in common, that they all are related to the sexual side of human beings and to the calling of the human race. They are normal occurrence, e.g. verses 16, 18 & 19, or have an abnormal character as in verses 2 & 25. Only the abnormal conditions in their intensified state are מחוסרי כפרה.

On טומאת יולדת, Ch. 12,2 et seq., we have already indicated how just the highest factors of life which should really be accomplished in moral freedom, factors on which the whole spiritual and normal future of humanity rests, marriage, the home, the family with the moral character of which even the State stands or falls, rest on physiological, animal procedures, which, more or less belong to the physical unfree side of human beings. So that the raising of just these factors up into the realm of moral freedom, and the warning against the erroneous idea of there being altogether no moral freedom for Man, seems of paramount necessity. This necessity which is so apparent at the striking physiological nature of birth is equally so for all matters in general connected with sex. And the טומאות which are here described even for quite normal occurrences may all serve to awaken, and keep awake, the knowledge that, in spite of the physiological lack of freedom, which cannot be denied, moral freedom is a fact guaranteed by the Sanctuary of the Law of God, and that it is only its acknowledgement even with the most sensuous side of human nature that can open the portals of the Sanctuary of God, and allow contact with all holy things dedicated to God.

But the abnormal conditions may be ascribed to sexual errors, or to the necessity for a special warning against such, and have the character of warning and admonition similar to נגעים. Hence the necessity for כפרה and the חטאת ועולת עוף before readmittance to the Sanctuary. By the חטאת עוף, he vows that in spite of his recent experience of having passively to submit to physical illness, he will pull himself up, and actively and energetically use all his powers, and with every beat of his pulse strive upwards towards the ideal of the whole of life becoming holy and ideal which beckons to him from the summit of the Altar; and by the עולת עוף that he will adhere to such “progress in elevating the passive sensuous side of his human nature” in ever greater victorious assertion of that which the height of the Altar preaches, by keeping the laws of morality which the Law of God indicates.

Looking at it this way, the different stages of the abnormal occurrences of זב וזבה, the זיבה קטנה and ב׳ ראיות — זיבה גדולה or ג׳ ראיות — may correspond to the warning and educating stages of מצולע מוסגר and מוחלט.

But what is most characteristic of these טומאות is the ,טומאת מדרס משכב ומושב. They apply exclusively to these טומאות. Although מצורע is also מטמא משכב ומושב, its מו״מ is still only ראשון as mentioned on Ch. 14,8, whereas at זב וזבה נדה ויולדת, it is אב הטומאה and it is just this difference which shows the meaning of these laws. משכב ומושב, objects destined to bear the weight of people resting on them, represent, as nothing else does, the passive, purely material physical side of human life; just that very sphere of the bodily senses to which the conditions and occurrences of bodily human existence which זב וזבה etc. represent, belong. They repeat, so as to say, the זב etc., and so awaken the same thoughts of the lack of freedom of the senses as the זב etc., themselves do, and hence are אב הטומאה (see Ch. 11,45). And then, it is just again the same mental sphere of the טהור which, absorbing or impressed by the משכב or מושב of the טמא becomes טמא. (This may also offer a solution to the strking anomaly of מפץ remarked above in Ch.XI. For מפץ seems to be the special mattress designed for sleeping on. See Kethuboth 64b and B.M. 113b. So מפץ represents in the most predominant manner, Man in a sleeping, i.e. in a condition where he is not master of his mental and sensory capacities, and indeed to such a degree that on the one hand it is certainly suitable for אב הטומאה as משכב ומושב, but on the other hand, for similar reasons to אוכלין ומשקין וכלי חרס, once they have become טמא, they have no טהרה במקוה). But the side of human life in which the conception of מצורע enters, is the very opposite one. It is that of the general active social life, and only to a secondary degree does משכב and מושב apply as ראשון to demonstrate the Truth that both sides of human life, the right attitude to social life, and the personal individual attitude to moral life belong intimately together, and when the first is neglected, as a rule, the latter is also endangered. But to a much greater degree is social conscientiousness dependent on moral purity. Hence it is not in a secondary degree, but quite predominately that היסט occurs with זב etc., and also quite characteristic that היסטו של זב is expressed by טומאת ידים as already expressed on v. 11. And this may be also why with a זב and משכב and מושב which represent it, מגעו is not חלוק ממשאו as it is with נבלה (v. 7). The טומאה which arises from מגע של זב and its representatives which does not primarily apply to the force of active life but solely to the bodily forces, spreads nevertheless over the whole personality and הנוגע בזב במשכבו ובמושבו requires כבוס בגדים וכלים בחבורין which otherwise is only the case with משא. In the case of מרכב this representation of זב etc., seems to be present to a lesser extent which would be the reason for its weaker degree of טומאה in this respect. רכב certainly does not represent the purely passive side of human existence as שכב and ישב do, it represents more of an activity than they do. The actual idea of מרכב itself is, anyway, not quite clear (v. 9).

Finally, זב, the abnormal occurrence in the male in this class of טומאה is the one טומאה which necessitates ביאת מים חיים to achieve טהרה. Is it perhaps that just for such a man (one who has suffered from gonorrhoea. I.L.), for the future way of purity in his sexual life, the Truth must be impressed that חיים and טהרה must spring from one and the same fount, that חיים is only to be found בדרך טהרה, yea חיים and טהרה must be identical to him, and only as טהור does he live and remain truly חי?

If we consider how, in accordance with the way we have tried to understand וידיו לא שטף במים (v. 11), the hands, ידים, are there so significantly taken to represent the whole activity of Man, the purity of which depends on the morality of every sphere of his life, then we can well understand how our חכמים could attach just to this verse the constant admonition to moral purity throughout our daily lives, by their introduction of the institution of טהרת ידים as ר׳ אלעזר בן ערך puts it in ת״כ on this verse מיכן סמכו חכמים לטהרת ידים מן התורה. (See Chulin 106a, and also notes on Ch. 11,47).

V. 1. With the last verse of the previous chapter, the cycle of laws about טומאת גויות and טומאת קדושות which started in Chapter XI comes to an end. At the introduction to Ch. XI, we tried to show the deep connection between these laws and the incident recorded in Ch. X of the death of the priestly youths with their offering. The death of these members of the spiritual elite of the Nation at the moment of the sanctification of the Sanctuary of the Torah, by “the Presence of God taking up Its home on earth” shows the whole weight and seriousness of the demand which the entry of this Torah into the midst of the Nation made on the People; showed how free-willed self-controlling subordination under the laws of this Sanctuary was the indispensable condition for existing as a member of this People of the Law even for those members of it who were nearest to God. And therefore a careful selection in the choice of one’s food, which promotes such subordination and makes it easier, as well as a sanctifying regime interwoven into every phase of one’s life of activity and enjoyment, as is prescribed by the Laws of מאכלות אסורות and of טומאה וטהרה are the immediate result of the sanctification of the Sanctuary in the midst of the People; so that this People remain conscious in all that they do, and refrain from doing, of the Laws of this Sanctuary which can only be carried out in free-willed self-control; and so that they do not sink into such lack of the consciousness of the ability to control one’s senses, in complete contrast to the whole idea of the Sanctuary, that the salvation of the Sanctuary of the Torah for the future of Mankind could only accomplish its object over the grave of this People; even as the closing and final admonition of the giving of the Laws of טומאה and טהרה at the end of the previous chapter runs והורתם את בני ישראל מטמאתם ולא ימתו בטמאתם בטמאם את משכני אשר בתוכם, (Ch. 15,31).

All this is now concentrated in this chapter into a great institution, to the establishment of which, one day in the national Jewish calender is fixed. Its establishment is made in connection again with the event to which the whole giving of the טומאה-and-טהרה-laws had been attached.

בקרבתם לפני ה׳ וימתו, “in their entering close to nearness to the Presence of God”, lay the cause of their death. Misunderstanding the height of the Jewish Ideal and a complete overestimation of their own importance and not recognizing their own imperfection formed the personal side of their error, קריבה, which brought about their ruin (see notes on Ch. 10,1).

V. 2. אהרן אחיך. By this addition of the nature of the relationship (which otherwise seems quite superfluous I.L.), the prohibition which follows applies not only to the person himself but extends to his whole family, to כהן הדיוט as to a אל הקדש ,מבית לפרכת ,אל פני הכפרת —.(ת״כ) ,כהן גדול, clearly the Sanctuary is here differentiated into three separate degrees of holiness. קדש: the היכל representing the height of what can humanly be achieved (from יכול, to be able I.L.); מבית לפרכת: the דביר representing the Ideal (from דבר, the Word); and within, and part of that, :פני הפרכת בין הבדים, the front surface of the ארון facing the East, turned towards the Nation. The prohibition, אל יבא, applies to all three places. Entry into the (קדש) ,היכל, and similarly entry into the קדש הקדשים avoiding the east-facing side of the ארון, the פני הכפרת, if only דרך משופש is only prohibited בלאו and not במיתה. It is only entering the קדש הקדשים and facing the פני הכפרת which is במיתה (Menachoth 27b). Hence, too, the accent on לפרכת.— אל יבא בכל עת, these places may only be entered לצורך עבודה. As nothing which is simply נדבה is brought in them, entry into them is barred for purposes which are purely self-dictated. (It is not at all sure that this applies to השתחויה. See כ״מ on הל׳ ביאת המקדש 2,4. If we consider, that if entry to the היכל for השתחויה were to be permitted whenever anybody wished, this would then be also allowed מבית לפרכת, then everything speaks for the way the סמ״ג takes it, that השתחויה is no exception).

כי בענן אראה וגו׳. According to Ex. 40,35 & 36, the cloud does not appear to have been within the Sanctuary. It is repeatedly differentiated between the ענן which rested above the משכן and was then resting about it, and the כבוד ה׳ within it. Here, too, (Yoma 53a), the בענן is taken to refer to ענן הקטרת (v. 13). According to that it would say here: “For, through the cloud will I be seen above the כפרת״. When the High Priest has stepped behind the dividing curtain, he shall make a second separating curtain by the cloud of קטרת and thereby, before he looks up to the כפרת, bring home to himself the distance that exists between himself and the People he represents, and the ideal of Israel which the cherubim-cover represents. Only through that which the קטרת expresses as his vow may be dare look up to the שכינה which rests above the כפרת-cherubim. The כי, “because”, referring to אל יבא וגו׳, could be explained by the fact that קטרת, as has already been remarked in Exodus 30,9, was never allowed to be brought בנדבה. So that the condition: בענן אראה וגו׳ completely excludes entry at any other time, (see note on v. 13).

The קדש הקדשים with the evidence of the Torah in its ark of wood and gold under the cover of golden cherubim — the פרכת-curtain hanging, separating and protecting, in front of it — the היכל, with the golden Menorah, the wooden-golden-Table, the wooden-golden-Altar, all these places represent, as we have worked out in Ex., the Torah, and the Jewish National Life which develops from it, in its complete ideal perfection. In all of them the idea is alive of the one ultimate ideal goal to which everybody must eternally strive, a goal which is set from above. Entry into these places which is commanded, procedures in them which are ordered to be done, by this very fact that they are done in obedience to command, bear the character of submission to the formula of life and existence which these places preach, and of which they are symbolic. However far off from these ideals of perfection, the actual lives of those who enter, or perform the procedures, or of those whom they represent and on whose behalf they act, are, they are commanded to enter and do these acts for the purpose of refreshing and renewing the thought of these ideals for future life; and just by such commanded renewal of the ideal, to become conscious of how far from perfection their actual lives are. But entry into, and carrying out rituals in these places on their own initiative would be a presumptuous act implying their having already achieved this ideal and imagining that they were actually justified by their lives in so doing. And by such presumption the whole object of these ideals to have an influence on future life would be destroyed. But on the other hand, the עזרה, the חצר, of the Sanctuary with its מזבח העולה and the כיור bears through and through the symbolism and meaning of being an antechamber, “a preparatory place for the Sanctuary of the Ideal of Life”. Any and every entry into, or ritual performed, therein partakes of this meaning, and bears the character of working on oneself to elevate oneself to a condition which renders one fit to strive upwards to the height of the ideal of life which God has set.

V. 3. בזאת יבא אהרן. With the expression of his being conscious of the meaning of his office as a פר, as “a worker on God’s fields of the Jewish way of Life”, and as a פר בן בקר remaining eternally “young”, not allowing habit or arrogance to dull the devotion and enthusiasm of his original dedication to services, that is to say, being completely conscious of the nature of his appointment before God and His Torah — as it occurs only on one other occasion, in the Miluim days of the consecration of the priesthood (Ex. 29,1) or in the פר כהן המשיח (Levit. 4,3), when an error in theory or practice on his part has made a renewal of this consciousness necessary — בזאת, with the consciousness of his personal high calling, shall Aaron enter the Holy of Holies. But with the consciousness expressed as a חטאת, not as anything already achieved, not with any feeling of pride in having fulfilled his life’s mission, but with full realisation of the necessity for atonement, which the deep gulf between the mission and the accomplishment entails. And with איל לעולה, again as in the מילואים-days with the expression of his consciousness of the dignity of his position as “the leading ram of God’s flock”. But not with thoughts of the advantages associated with this position, as were expressed by the איל מלואים, but with thoughts of the responsibility for never-ceasing energetic striving upwards towards the height of godness and nobility which is expected from his influential position. בזאת, with the expression of this goal of life which is given to him, not with any subjective ideals of his own, יבא אהרן אל הקדש.

V. 4. כתנת בד קדש ילבש וגו׳. And not clothed in his בגדי זהב, not with the positive colours of the ideal place of the Heichal, not in the blue-red-gold colours of the High-priestly garments in which otherwise at offerings he represents the symbolic picture of the ideal Jew, consistently living the ideal spiritual and physical Jewish life, and in which he has already on this day offered the Tamid and part of the Mussaf offerings — but in בגדי לבן, he is to clothe himself in the negative colour of the preparatory forecourt, he is simply to wear only the colour of purity. כתנת בד קדש ילבש, his receptive, directive, striving and accomplishing self is he to clothe with the purity of will and deed which the Sanctuary of the Torah demands (see Ex. XXVIII, end); ומכנסי בד יהיו על בשרו, after the purely physical part of his self had already attained that purity which keeps sensuous desire within the prescribed limits (ibid & Yoma 23b); ובאבנט בד יחגר, and even this stage of the very first preparatory condition for purity, he does not claim — as even a כהן הדיוט does — to have already positively achieved, so that he now could brace himself — as they can — to progress to the positive stage of moral perfection, and could at least “gird” himself with the positive colours of the היכל-stage, but even his “girdle” still bears the character of preliminary negative purity. To reach even the stage which the girdle represents, he still has to exert all his energies. At the moment when he draws near and stands before the very highest ideal of the Torah in the Holy of Holies even the girdle of the High Priest becomes only a girding towards purity, אבנטו של כהן גדול ביום הכפורים לא זה הוא אבנטו של כהן הדיוט, (Yoma 12a). ובמצנפת בד יצנף: the head of the High Priest is always also crowned only with the colour of purity; he only ranks separated above all others as long as he raises himself up separated from everything low and ignoble, (see Ex. XXVIII end). בגדי קדש הם: they are not his own garments, they are the garments of the Sanctuary, clad in them he enters the service of the Sanctuary, and the character he symbolises through them is not just what he may consider right and befitting, but they bring home to his mind the demands which the Sanctuary makes on behalf of the Torah which reposes in it.

ורחץ במים את בשרו ולבשם. And before he may clothe his concrete self with even these modest and unassuming symbolic garments of the Sanctuary he must first symbolically by טבילה take his body right out of the sphere of any טומאה and let it go back to the beginning of elementary primitiveness (see Ex. 27,7) so that he realises without any delusions, how far off his actual reality is from satisfying even the very first demands of the Sanctuary.

Just as טבילה is prescribed here, at the transition from bringing the תמיד and מוספים-offerings in the בגדי זהב to the offering-rituals which were to be done in בגדי לבן by entering the Holy of Holies, in the same way in vv. 23 & 24, טבילה is required at the change back from בגדי לבן to בגדי זהב, as it says: ופשט את בגדי הבד וגו׳ ןרחץ ןגו׳ ויצא ועשה את עולתו וגו׳. But, as will be explained on v. 23, there were four such changes necessary on י״כ, and as כל המשנה מעבודה לעבודה טעון טבילה, the כ״ג would have to do that number of טבילות. But מדרבנן anybody who enters the עזרה on any day has first to undertake טבילה. The כה״ג on י״כ accordingly had to טובל himself five times. Now the Halacha teaches that just as ordinarily through out the year before starting any fresh עבודה, the קידוש ידים ורגלים מן הכיור prescribed in Ex. 30,20 had to be done, so here, too, apart from the טבילות, each time קידוש ידים ורגלים had to be undertaken, and indeed twice, one before each הפשטה, before taking off the בגדי זהב or בגדי לבן and then again, after טבילה and putting on the garments appropriate to the coming function, before proceeding to do the ritual. We have already indicated that the עבודה which the כה״ג had to perform in the בגדי לבן were to be done realising his own actual personal imperfection, while those done in בגדי זהב were to be in realisation of the idea of the ideal of moral perfection which is innate in the conception of the Jewish Nation. Now, as קידוש ידים ורגלים is commanded to be done before each הפשטה, this הפשטה itself, taking off the בגדי זהב as well as the בגדי לבן must have the nature of an עבודה. Raising oneself up, above one’s own imperfection to the height of the moral greatness which is innate in the national ideal, as well as coming down from such height to the thought of the actual level of one’s own imperfect moral worth, the one as much as the other forms a most important moment, full of meaning for the work on our individual and national life which the Sanctuary of the Torah wishes to impress on us by the ritual of this impressive day. It is only by acting on a combination of the teaching of both these moments that the spiritual and moral goal that is set for us can be reached. קידוש before taking off the בגדי זהב teaches, that grasping the idea of the national ideal only has value when it is used as a yardstick with which to measure how far from it the actuality really is. And קידוש before doffing the בגדי לבן teaches, that being depressed over actual short-comings is only pleasing to God, is only Divine Service, only serves God’s purposes, when it becomes the foundation on which one elevates oneself upwards towards the Ideal which God sets as humanly attainable. So five טבילות and ten קידושין ring the changes in the עבודה of the כה״ג for the great ritual of יום הכפורים. But the most significant seems to be the קידושא בתרא, the final קידוש, which he כי פשט בגדי קדש ולביש בגדי חול, performed at the end of the Day, before taking off the garments of the Sanctuary, to go out in the clothing of every-day life. Inasmuch as not only הפשטה for the change of בגדי קדש לקדש, but also the last הפשטה of בגהי קדש לחול demands no less קידוש ידים ורגלים מכלי שרת, the doffing of the garments of the Sanctuary to come back to everyday life in ordinary clothes is also impressed with the character of an עבודה. Thereby, the thought to be taken away by the final word of the whole great day is given, viz., that the whole life inside the Sanctuary and all the rituals which are performed in it have only meaning and value in the concrete life outside the Sanctuary which is to be based on the spirit which is gained within it, and that what is striven for in the בגדי קדש, must wait for its true meaning for what is accomplished in the בגדי חול.

V. 5. ומאת עדת בני ישראל. But he has to appear before God in the Sanctuary not only with the offerings expressing his own relation to God and to His Torah, but equally so, and at the same time, with the offerings expressing the same relationships of the People. For, in no wise is the Jewish priest an intermediary between God and the People. Priest and people stand in exactly the same direct proximity of relationship and mission to God and to His Torah; the Priest as פר with his service of working for God on the fields of the minds and heart of the people, cultivating them for God and His Torah; the People as שעיר only tractable to God’s leading, but obstinately resisting any attempt at strange guidance, standing firm in following God’s guidance and determinedly carrying out His Laws, and therefore equal to the Priest as איל, for that which the Priest is to be to the People, the People are to be to the rest of Mankind, the “leading ram” at the head of God’s flock of human beings, showing the way to accomplish all that is noble and good.

But the חטאת which the Nation has to hand over to him is to consist of two שעירים. This fact already — for otherwise no חטאת ever consists of more than one animal, it always represents either a private individual, or the whole community regarded as a single unit — must as once make us realise, that if here שני שעירי עזים לחטאת are ordered, the single חטאת-idea must wish to be represented in two different ways, in each of which the same national unit is to be represented by a שעיר. And actually we find in the succeeding verses that these two animals receive totally different and contrasting treatment which does bring out the one single חטאת-idea in its two contrasting aspects.

שני שעירי עזים, and again repeatedly in vv. 7 & 8: שני השעירים. Hence, although the different designation of these two animals expressed in vv. 7—10 form the most complete contrast to each other, nevertheless, according to the Halacha given in Yoma 62a & b, they have to be as nearly identical in all essential points as is possible. For it is, after all, one and the same personality which both are to symbolise: מצותן שיהיו שניהן שוין במראה ובקומה ובדמים ובלקיחתן כאחד, they are to be similar in appearance, height and size and value and also in that they are both to be selected for offerings at the same time. This similarity is a מצוה although it is not מעכב. We found this demand for similarity also at the שתי צפרי מצורע and at the שני כבשי מצורע (Ch. 14,4 & 10), and in all these places the Gemora Yoma 62b, finds it indicated by the term: שני שעירים ,שני כבשים ,שתי צפרים, (For it is assumed that any superfluous word in the Torah must be taken as a “note” referring to the oral law which had previously been given to Moses and taught to the Children of Israel for forty years before they were given the written Torah as reference. I.L.). The simple plural form: שעירים ,כבשים ,צפרים, would be sufficient without mentioning the number two, as: מיעוט רבים שנים. And in any case, even without applying this rule, it is abundantly clear from the context of the succeeding verses with all the details of the treatment of each one of the pair, that it is only a question of two animals. The explicit order “two”, always expresses a pair in external appearance, value and in time of being appointed.

V. 6. בכפרת דברים הכתוב מדבר :וכפר בעדו וגו׳ ,והקריב את פר וגו׳, (Yoma 36b). Here כפרה is not to be understood — as it is everywhere else at offerings — to refer to כפרת דמים, the כפרה to be achieved by the ritual of the blood, but to that part of the כפרה which is brought about by וידוי דברים, by the confession which is made at the סמיכה (see note on Ch. 1,4). Similarly the וידוי which is prescribed to be said at the שעיר המשתלח (v. 21), is called כפרה in v. 10. And, in any case, as is explained there in Yoma, here it can not be speaking of כפרת דמים as v. 11 shows that it is only after repeated כפרה that the שחיטה of the פר takes place. So that in both sentences it can only be speaking of כפרת דברים. For although the real כפרה is associated with הרצאת דמים, as it says in Ch. 16,11: כי הדם הוא בנפש יכפר, still the סמיכה with its associated וידוי does form an integral part of the וסמך ידו וגו[[illegible]]‘ ונרצה לו לכפר עליו[[illegible]] :כפרה, (Ch. 1,4; Yoma 5a). For the essential meaning of כפרה is, as has already been explained on Gen. 6,14, a “covering over”, a “burying” of the past. It is the highest act of the absolute, free-willed almighty power of God, Who alone can do away with the natural law of cause and effect, which, after all, He Himself has instituted, so that the consequences of the errors and sins of the past have no disturbing effect on the internal and external life of the future; so that after a morally bad past, the blossoming out of a pure and happy future is still possible. And He has promised this “burying” of the past for every honest firm resolve of future faithful surrendering of one’s whole being to the duty of keeping God’s commandments, which is the vow expressed by the מתנות דם. Every קרבן, and the ritual prescribed for it, represents the picture of the life which ought to have been lived in the past and which must be lived in the future, if God’s approval and satisfaction is to be expected. The solemn promise to realise this picture of one’s future life is the real condition for obtaining כפרה. Hence דם הוא בנפש יכפר. But it is essentially necessary to further the carrying-out of the vow, and indeed the sincerity of the vow demands, that the more a bad past is to be “buried” by the absolute omnipotence of God’s benevolence, the more necessary it is that it should not be buried from the mind of the person, but rather be and remain vivid in unadulterated clarity in his mind. That is the meaning of the Jewish וידוי, which is no “confession” to any other person, not even an avowal to God, but essentially, as the expression התודה signifies, an “admission to oneself”, which in one’s innermost self silences every extenuating, excusing defence. It is only when one has the courage to look at one’s wrongdoings in the same disapproving clarity with which God’s Eye sees them, only then will our resolutions for the future betterment not fail to be realised. A genuine חטאתי precludes the recurrence of the sin. Every true self-judgement includes self-knowledge, not only that we should have behaved otherwise, but that we could have behaved otherwise, and by such recognition of our moral freedom of will rejects any excuse for present or future failings.

ובעד ביתו. The Jewish High Priest is not thought of without a home, i.e. unmarried, without a wife. The man who is to represent in the Sanctuary of God’s laws the moral ideal of the Nation and whose life is to be a model for all the people, must show the picture of a human life in the completeness of its moral mission; marriage, the foundation of all moral development, the basis of all moral prosperity and happiness of a nation, may not be lacking. So essentially does the wife belong to that which the High Priest represents in the Sanctuary, that even if the High Priest had been married, but had lost his wife before he had done the עבודה on י״כ, he was not allowed to perform the עבודה as a widower (Yoma 13a). The High Priest on י״כ must be the husband of a wife, but only of one wife, בעדו ובעד ביתו ולא בעד שתי בתים, (ibid).

V. 7. ולקח את שני וגו׳. After he had first recognised and acknowledged himself and his home as requiring atonement, he is to go to the pair of שעירים with which the community declared itself as requiring atonement; והעמיד אתם: the two similar animals, the one as well as the other were given their position, turned towards God, לפני ה׳, in the עזרה, at the entrance in the East, on the north side of the Altar, as all offerings which were holiest of the holy.

V. 8. ונתן על שני השעירים גורלות: not that two lots were to be drawn for each of the two animals not that both lots were placed on both of them, but that both lots hovered over both animals; it had to be perfectly undecided beforehand which lot each animal would receive. Hence: מה תלמוד לומר גורלות, שיהיו שוין, the two lots had to be exactly similar: שלא יעשה אחד של זהב ואחד של כסף אחד גדול ואחד קטן, not one of silver and one of gold, not one large and the other small (Yoma 37a). But it is of no consequence at all out of what material the lots are made: גורלות של כל דבר (ibid). The two lots were placed in an urn (קלפי) into which the High Priest plunged both his hands and grasped one in each hand simultaneously (טרף). The one in the right hand was taken to be for the animal standing on the right and the one on the left hand for the other (Yoma 39a). For the reason given above the animal had to receive its fate solely by the drawing of lots, so that if one of the animals died after the drawing, one could not simply take another in its place but הגרלה מעכב, it must have a chance for either fate, and fresh lots had to be drawn for two other animals: מת אחד מהם אם עד שלא הגריל מת יקח זוג לשני, ואם משהגריל מת יביא זוג אחר ויגריל עליהם בתחלה, and the one on whom the lot of the dead animal fell was taken in its place to pair with the one that had remained alive. This is in accordance with the accepted principle that בעלי חיים אינן נדחין, that living animals that had been dedicated for offerings and then, for some reason or other had been temporarily rendered unfit to be brought are still to be brought when that reason had been removed. If the same rule applied to בעלי חיים as does to other sacrificial objects viz. נראה ונדחה אינו חוזר ונראה, that once their validity has been interrupted, they do not regain it even after the interruption has been removed, then with the death of one of the animals the other would lose its validity permanently, and a complete new pair would have to take the place of the first one (Yoma 62a & 64a). Finally, again for the same reason, we have the rule: אין הגורל קובע אלא בראוי לשם (Yoma 63b), at the moment of the הגרלה both animals must be fit for חטאת לה׳; even the lot לעזאזל, only affects the animal concerned if it was also fit for the lot לה׳, but not, for instance, if it was טרפה or לעזאזל ,לה׳ —.בעל מום: see v. 10.

V. 9. עלה :והקריב וגו׳ אשר עלה עליו הגורל לה׳ ועשהו חטאת is the coming up out of the urn, עליית גורל מתוך הקלפי. It is only the lot raised up from the urn, not the declaration of the Priest, that makes the animal into a חטאת. He has to treat that animal as a חטאת for which the lot לה׳ fell: הגורל עושהו חטאת ואין השם עושהו חטאת, (Yoma 3b & 40b).

V. 10. והשעיר וגו׳ לעזאזל יעמד חי וגו׳. While its companion with the decision לה׳ went to its death, suffered the sacrificial death, but with this sacrificial death was accepted by God’s Sanctuary to a new elevated existence, the one with the decision לעזאזל remains חי in undisturbed freshness of life, standing at the entrance to the Sanctuary. לכפר עליו: for — as v. 21 teaches — self-confession of all the sins and transgressions of the Nation to be made with סמיכה on his head, לשלח אותו, and so, to send it away, untouched, from the threshold of the Sanctuary — the entrance to which its companion had gained only at the price of sacrificial death — away, but far away, not just out of the surroundings of the Sanctuary, but right out of the zone of human habitation, המדברה, into the wilderness.

Quite clearly we have here the representation of two creatures originally completely identical, who, at the threshold of the Sanctuary, part, and proceed on two entirely contrasting paths. They are both similar: במראה בקומה בדמים ובלקיחתם כאחד, both are placed together in a similar way: לפני ה׳ פתח אהל מועד, the decision לה׳, as the decision לעזאזל, hovers over both of them in exactly the same way, both have exactly the same possibility of decision for one or the other, more, the one can only become what he does become because he could have become the other, אין הגורל קובע אלא בראוי לשם — and from there on they separate into such complete contrasts. The one, decided לה׳, suffers שחיטה-death by the sharp cut of the Sanctuary, but is then gathered up in holy vessels and gets admitted to the Holy-of Holies, into proximity of that most holy spot where the ideal of a Jewish Torah-Life perfects itself as the bearer of godliness on earth. The other, decided לעזאזל, remains untouched by the cut of the Sanctuary, does not suffer the שחיטה-death, remains untouched and unchanged, חי, full of lively self before God, at the entrance to the Sanctuary, but as such is not admitted farther into the Sanctuary, but is sent out of its precincts, out of the sphere of human habitation, out into the desert, and there turning its back to the Sanctuary, desolate in the desert, ends the uncultivated living for itself which it had preserved. And both are שני שעירי עזים לחטאת — חטאת (v. 5) — the one, as well as the other must be meant to bring to our consciousness the same חטאת-idea, only looked at from two contrasting points of view. We accordingly think that we are not wrong in taking it that, whereas in חטאת generally, only that picture of life is represented which the past should have realised and which the future is to realise, here, the reverse side comes also to be represented, viz. the picture of the life our past should never have shown, and which we are to vow that we shall give no place in our future. Each one of us is a “שעיר״. Each one of us has the power to resist, to be obstinate, the ability to oppose with firmness demands made on our will-power. It is on the way we use this power that the worthiness or worthlessness of our moral existence depends. We can use it in attachment to God, in resisting all internal and external temptation and considerations which would lure us away from God and His Holy Will, in being a שעיר לה׳. Or we can use it in obstinate refusal of all compliant obedience to God, and to the demands of His holy Laws of Morality, can turn the power of resistance which He has granted us against Him, and give ourselves up without a fight to the power of our senses and their allurements, to fight against which was just the purpose for which God gave us that power of resistance. This sinking into the power of sensuality in contrast to attachment to God, obeying His laws of morality is here called לעזאזל.

The simplest, most unforced way of taking the meaning of this word is עז אזל, the character of firmness, obstinacy, עז which אזל, which has no future, which disappears, which, in thinking itself עז just thereby digs its own grave. It is that giving way to one’s senses, raised to a principle, which God had denied any permanent future in the destiny of Man. A Boreitha in Yoma 67b, explains the word as עזז אל or עזאל, which comes to much the same idea. It is that עזוז which is conformable with the nature and purpose of the אלים, the non-human forces of Nature, to whom the Creator has granted only one possible direction from which לא יסבו בלכתן, from which they are not to turn, and therefore can not turn aside; they obey their Creator and Master when they follow the dictates of their nature with all the firmness and determination of their being. That is the lot and the mission of the primitive and organic world which has no free will of its own.

But Man has been given something different and higher, and it is only when he practices this other and higher calling that he is really a Man and proves himself worthy of being a human being. For high above these אלים, above the sphere of these creations of God, ruled by, and bound to His Laws of Nature, and who are strong and firm only in unchangeable obedience to these laws, stand ה׳ in the absolute freedom of His Will, the One Unique, Free, Almighty God. And He has sent down to earth a ray of His own unique free nature, of His free-willed power of directing forces, and breathed it into one creature in the midst of the countless unfree אלים and clothed it in an earthly case as a breath of His spirit, and has said to it, “Be thou Adam, a likeness of Me, be a God in miniature, in and over the little world which I have appointed for you with your mortal frame”. “Thou hast freedom of will of My Freedom, power of My Power to direct forces. Within thy frame, that part of thee which is of the earthly world, powerful forces and urges work in the same way as they do in the whole of the rest of the primitive and organic world from which it is derived. Left to themselves they drive with hot determination on the way which is innate to their nature, and find satisfaction in so doing. But thou art free willed, hast freedom of My Freedom, hast power to master forces of nature from My Power, hast the spirit to understand My Will from My Spirit, and thou art to use this power to master and guide with a strong hand these forces and urges of thy world, with free-willed energy to make them all, all of them, serve the Laws of My Will. Thus making thy forces and urges subservient to thy self, and thyself to Me. Thou rankest high, near unto Me, the one free being in the midst of a world of forces and powers which have no free-will of their own”.

But the conception “Freedom” at once, of course, implies the possibility of setting oneself against the Divine Will. So little is the ability to sin and the tempting allurement of the senses a result which only followed Man’s Fall or degeneration, that without such ability and such allurement he would not be Man. The whole height and dignity and worth of human beings lies just in the ability to sin, in the possibility which has been given to him to disobey the Will of God. In the sphere of the primitive and organic world — animal vegetable or mineral — there can be no sin, but just on that account no virtue, no morality. And if the urge of the human senses which are not in accordance with the Will of God were not endowed with attraction and allure, if Man only found satisfaction and enjoyment in the use of his forces in the God-pleasing way, if everything good was sweet and everything bad bitter, if he could not resist God, as he can resist the desires and urges of his senses, if he could not be a שעיר לעזאזל as well as a שעיר לה׳, then the Law of God would work in him too with irresistable force as it does in all the other non-free creatures of His creation through which they are kept on the one prescribed path in which alone they find their satisfaction, and any deviation from it repulses them, leaves them quite cold.

So are all of us, without distinction, placed at the entry to God’s Sanctuary to decide between ה׳ and עזאזל, between God, and the power of our senses. There, in the Holy of Holies, as the holiest of holies rests the Torah, the Law of His Will for us. Facing this, His Law, has the decision to be made. It can be made לה׳, for God, we can decide for God, gathering together all the powers of resistance we have been given, to resist everything which would tear us away from our vocation, to be near to God, to belong to God, to be like God, in free-willed carrying out His Will, keeping pure and doing good of our own free will. Then we will come in joyful readiness into the forecourt of the Sanctuary of His Law to give up, under the sharp cut of His Sanctification, the selfish life of our bodily senses, and thereby achieve acceptance into His Sanctuary, and achieve being near God, even with our quite earthly bodily material and sensual life in fulfilling His Holy Will on earth. Or the decision can be made לעזאזל, at the entrance to the Sanctuary, facing the demands His Laws make on us, we can turn the power of resistance which is given to us just against these demands of His Will. At the entrance to His Sanctuary we can refuse the sacrifice of our self-willed life of desires, refuse to give up the power of exercising our own will which is open to us, refuse the cut which the purifying and sanctifying divine Law would impose on our sensuality, and, at the entrance to His Sanctuary, facing His Law, we can uphold, unmastered, our selfish life of desires, but thereby we give ourselves over to עזאזל, to the uncontrolled might of sensuality, which has no place in the Sanctuary, no place in the sphere of the human or national life which should flourish in the surroundings of that Sanctuary under the rays of the Divine Torah, and only belongs out in the wild where this earthly world does not become elevated by the free-willed moral government of Man into the sphere of bodily freedom.

And the decision is not made for anyone of us beforehand. Not מראה, not קומה, not דמים, not more or less respected appearance, not more or less greatness, not more or less riches, also not the time at which we are called on to make this decision, has any compelling influence on the decision. Respected or otherwise, great or small, rich or poor, today or tomorrow, in any state of life, in every degree of power and possession, and at every time, can each of us be לה׳ or לעזאזל. And the decision לה׳ has only meaning and value because at the same moment it could have swayed to עזאזל; and the decision לעזאזל is only a disgrace to Man, because at the same moment he could have become and remained attached and faithful to God. The עזאזל-attraction itself should have led him to God, for without it he could never become the free-willed son and servant of God, and sensuality is not given to Man so that is should master him, but that he should master and guide it, ואליך תשוקתו ואתה תמשל בו, (Gen. 4,7. See notes thereon).

לעזאזל :לשלח אותו לעזאזל, is not the indirect object of לשלח. It does not mean to send it to עזאזל, as those people explain it who would like to make out of Azazel a demon of the wilderness to whom the he-goat is to be sent as an appeasing offering! In all the numerous places in which שלח occurs in the Piel-form in the overwhelming majority of cases it does not have the meaning of “sending to” but quite definitely the meaning of “sending away”, of “letting go”, dismissing. Only of evil things does it usually have also the meaning of “sending to”, as ושן בהמות אשלח בם (Deut. 32,25) et alia. And there, too, the basic meaning is, of letting the evil loose, which otherwise is being held back. There are only a few isolated instances as in Gen. 38,17, where אשלח does definitely mean “sending to”. We think, therefore, that we are not mistaken if we take the לשלח אתו here to have the same meaning as in the parallel case in Ch. 14,7: שלח את הצפר, viz. simply sending it away. The לעזאזל is then in apposition to אתו, sending it away, as pertaining to Azazel, in the wilderness.

V. 11. Above, in v. 6, it has already said: והקריב וגו׳ וכפר בעדו וגו׳, here he is told to come a second time to his bull, and acknowledge again the necessity for atonement for himself and for his “house”. Yoma 46b, teaches that in this second וידוי the conception of his house, ביתו, is extended to include the whole of the priestly tribe, and runs: אנא השם חטאתי וכו׳ לפניך אני וביתי ובני אהרן עם קדושיך.
