There, on p. 43b, this separation of the first confession on his own behalf before he makes the second one on behalf of his tribe is explained as being so that before he seeks atonement for others, he first attains it for himself by his personal confession: יבא זכאי ויכפר על החייב, ואל יבא חייב ויכפר על החייב. But there seems to be a threefold reason for the separation of these two וידויים by the intervening הגרלה (vv. 7 & 8). The הגרלה had of necessity to be done before the שחיטת הפר, because it and the succeeding הזיות דם הפר were directly connected with the שחיטת השעיר and הזיות דמו (v. 15). But his וידוי had to precede the הגרלה so that the High Priest, before he went to the חטאת of the People had first acknowledged that he himself required a חטאת. And the second וידוי did not follow this one, to give effect to the rule that תיכף לסמיכה שחיטה (see Ch. 1,4 & III,2).

ושחט את פר החטאת אשר לו. The first condition for the co-worker in the service of the work in God’s fields of the minds and hearts of the people, remaining in future free from חטא ועון, is the renewed giving up all living for self and the ready cheerful giving up the whole of one’s sensual and spiritual being to the cutting sharpness of God’s hallowing, the vow symbolically expressed by שחיטה.

V. 12. מעל המזבח מלפני ה׳, from the מזבח העולה in the עזרה. This and not the מזבח הזהב in the היכל is characterised by the addition of מלפני ה׳, which indicated that the coals of fire are to be taken from the side of the Altar which is turned towards God, i.e. the West side. The מזבח הזהב in the היכל is designated as כולו לפני ה׳ (Yoma 45b). גחלי אש: glowing coals (Pesachim 75b; תוספות Zebachim 64a).— ומלא חפניו קטרת וגו׳: A pan full of the incense prepared for the daily קטרת was brought to him — on the previous day it had been again rubbed smooth in a mortar, in accordance with the demand of the text: קטרת סמים דקה, from which he lifted out his two hands completely full. This חפינה is, like קמיצה, an independent עבודה ritual by itself, and מחשבה מהניא בה, i.e. a מחשבת פגול at it would render the קטרת unfit to be used (Yoma 48a). It is left undecided (ibid b), whether the same applies to the והביא וגו׳ —.חתיית גחלים: as he had to carry the pan with the glowing coal and the incense into the Holy of Holies at the same time, he poured the two handfulls into a spoon or ladle — as, at the נשיאים (Numb. 7,14): כף אחת מלאה קטרת, — and with the pan in his right hand and the ladle in his left, he entered the Holy of Holies (Yoma 47a).

V. 13. ונתן את הקטרת וגו׳: there, in the Holy of Holies he placed the pan of coals בין הבדים, on the ground between the two poles of the Ark, filled both his hands again full with the incense out of the :כף חופן וחוזר וחופן — (Yoma 49b) — and then poured the קטרת, heaped up, not scattered, (צוברה), on to the coals, so that the whole holy place slowly filled with the smoke of the incense (ibid): וכסה וגו׳ ולא ימות, as is prescribed in v. 2, for going into the very holiest place, אל פני הכפרת אשר על הארון. The smoke of the incense rose straight up like a palm tree between the בדים and then at the roof spread out laterally and down the walls and filled the whole room: היה מתמר ועולה כמקל עד שמגיע לשמי קורה כיון שמגיע לשמי קורה ממשמש ויורד בכותלים עד שנתמלא הבית עשן, (ibid 53a).

The כה״ג had already killed his פר by שחיטה, had given up his individual living for himself for his service as a פר in God’s Kingdom, had, himself, taken up his unselfish פר-being for the Sanctuary in a vessel of the Sanctuary, קבל במזרק (Yoma 43b); and now he is to take it, the symbol of his נפש, unselfishly given up and accepted for holiness, right into the Sanctuary of Holiness, and stand before God, in front of His Torah and the ישראל-ideal of perfecting itself by this Torah into “cherubim” of God’s שכינה on earth, there to impart to his נפש the unceasing working up to this goal with every beat of his pulse (הזיות). To do this on his own initiative this direct looking up to the very highest conceivable ideal, and to give himself up to it, would be overbearing self-confidence and arrogance were it not part of the lesson for which God’s Fire shone out day and night in the forecourt of His Sanctuary from the top of the Altar, calling all, everybody, the priests and people, to constant devotion and constant change and progress; were the thought in the mind of the High Priest other, than that he himself was but a tiny part of that great immortal national institution which God had established to endure throughout the centuries of time; a nation which God had established, which only through thousands of years was to grow up to that ideal goal for which He had instituted a symbol in the קטרת, which, without any reservation and without leaving anything behind, sublimates itself entirely in ריח ניחוח, in giving satisfaction and pleasure to God. This קטרת has its beginning in the fire-offerings of the מזבח החיצון, has daily to represent progress on the מזבח הזהב and finds its culminating height in the קטרת בין הבדים, the whole deep meaning of which became clear to the National Leader on this first national historical יום הכפורים by the summary of all the teachings which had led up to it, and which he puts into the words: וסלחת לעוננו ולחטאתנו, “Thou will ever, again and again, grant pardon to our lapses from Thy paths, and to our sins, and ever keep the future open for renewed efforts, ונחלתנו, until we become completely and entirely Thine”.

Therefore — before he appeared in the Holy of Holies with the דם of his נפש — he took fire out of the אש אוכלה which flamed for all on the מזבח החיצון, from the side turned towards the Holy of Holies, took his two joined hands-full from the קטרת which daily smoked up to God, as an expression of the People’s compliance to the Will of God, and only with these two did he enter the Holy place. There, בין הבדים, where the Ark of the Torah constantly streched out its arms, and in every contemporary Israel awaits its bearers, there he deposited the brazier. Thereby the אש אוכלה על המזבח becomes the אש דת בארון הברית, and, inasmuch as it is there, בין הבדים, where every living Jew is to take the בדי הארון on his shoulders to carry the Law of God in unfailing strength and faithfulness through all times and places, through all trails and dangers that he strews the קטרת, and there that the “palm” of smoke of the ענן הקטרת rises up, it is just the ideal Israel which, as bearer of the Divine Law, gives itself up entirely to ריח ניחוח לה׳, and perfects itself to be the Cherubim-intermediaries of God’s Presence on Earth. Only by the representation of the realisation of this highest ideal of the future perfection of the whole Nation, may the High Priest of any time — however far off it may be from this ideal future — איזהו כפרה ששוה לו ולביתו ולאחיו הכהנים ולכל קהל ישראל ,הוי אומר זה הקטרת (Yoma 44a) — tread the most holy spot, looking up to God: וכסה ענן הקטרת את הכפרת אשר על העדות ולא ימות.—

In a highly characteristic manner, the way of this bringing the קטרת in the קדש הקדשים on יום הכפורים became a point of cardinal difference between the צדוקים and the traditional teaching of the חכמים which they denied. The צדוקים teach that יתקן מבחוץ ויכניס, the כה״ג has to put the קטרת on the coals outside the קדש הקדשים and enter the Holy of Holies with the incense already smoking, whereas according to the tradition of the הכמים he had to carry the coals and the incense together inside, and only there, as already remarked, בין הבדים, pour the קטרת on to the coals (Yoma 53a). To uphold this erroneous doctrine was so clear to them that it is recorded that a Sadducee who became High Priest was absolutely over-joyed, שמח שמחה גדולה, at the opportunity of carrying it into actual practice (Yoma 19b), and subsequently every High Priest had to make a definite oath on ערב יום כפור, not to adopt the teaching of the צדוקים when he offered up the קטרת. Now, it is extremely interesting to note that, although it was the general principle of the Sadduces to follow the literal wording of the text and to reject the traditional תורה שבעל פה, in this instance it is just the tradition of the חכמים which follows the strict wording of the text, whereas the Sadducean teaching is very forced and difficult to fit in with the wording. Clearly and quite unambiguously the orders run in v. 12 & 13:— ולקח מלא המחתה וגו׳ ומלא חפניו קטרת וגו׳ והביא מבית לפרכת ונתן את הקטרת על האש לפני ה׳, and this wording is in accordance only with the way taught by the חכמים, that fire and קטרת are to be brought into the קדש קדשים and that only when inside, there the incense is to be poured onto the fire! Against this clear wording, the צדוקים refer to v. 2: ואל יבא וגו׳ כי בענן אראה, which they explain as if it were: ואל יבא וגו׳ כי אם בענן, he may only come in with the cloud of smoke, without being able, however, to give any new interpretation to the clear dictum of vv. 12 & 13. When we inquire into the motive which drove them to adopt this obvious disagreement with the wording of the Torah, we find a note in ת״כ that they gave the demand of “etiquette”, “good manners”, as the ostensible reason: אם לפני בשר ודם עושין כן קל וחומר לפני המקום, “if at human banquets the incense is always brought in already smoking, but not brought in and lit in the presence of the guests surely good manners demand that we should do no less for God Himself!” So already with these ancient Sadducees, empty conventional forms were the same hollow idols to which alone our modern Sadducees bow, and in whose name they try to introduce the most open breaches of the Law into the most holy moments of our divine services. If we look into it more closely the way the צדוקים adopted to offer the קטרת was just the one in which Nadab and Abihu (Ch. 10,1) brought their disastrous offering of קטרת. Of them it says:— ויקחו וגו׳ איש מחתתו ויתנו בהן אש וישימו עליה קטרת ויקריבו לפני ה׳. Clearly they, too, did not put the incense onto the fire לפני ה׳, but they brought it already smoking before God! According to ת״כ on שמיני and אחרי מות on v. 2, (see ראב״ד thereon), they took it into the קדש הקדשים (see also Yoma 53a). So that they went, exactly as the צדוקים demanded, with the smoking incense into the Holy of Holies before God! If this is so, then we should have here again what is so very characteristic, viz., that already the ancient צדוקים took their models from Nadab and Abihu, in exactly the same way as the Karaites, their epigones, paid homage, as authorities, to all those men who, with their opinions and teachings are rejected and condemned by the national ecclesiastical authorities. Altogether, in the תקון בחוץ והכנסה בפנים, the Sadducee may be expressing the whole principle of the Sadducean contrast and opposition to the traditional adherence to the Law of the Chachamim. The true High Priest of the Jewish Law of God is nothing else but a ministrant of the Will of God, completely subjugating his own ideas to the Divine Torah. To him the Altar-fire is the Torah-fire, the fire of the Law, and only that which is pleasing, giving satisfaction to God, is pleasing, gives satisfaction to him, only that which is ניחוח לה׳ is for him ריח ניחוח at all. He places the Altar-fire on the foundation of the Law of God, and for him, only such actions that are done under the testing Eye of God and His Law and which are done on the basis of that Law can be ריח ניחוח לה׳, can be pleasing and give satisfaction to God. All his activities for the Torah are all based for him on its laws. But the Sadduceean priest makes the Altar fire into his fire, as a receptacle for his handling, and outside the area of the Law he first lights the קטרת to his ריח ניחוח in a way that appeals to him, gives him satisfaction, and that which he imagins is right and good and considers proper, he carries into the Sanctuary of the Law, forces his own idea of what is suitable for God’s satisfaction, and that which has passed the test of his conception of ריח ניחוח, God, too, must be pleased with, as His ריח ניחוח!

Who knows whether it was not just because of this deep underlying difference, in which lies the whole nature of the Sadducean principle which would be so strikingly expressed in the Sadducean ritual of the הקטרה of the קטרת at the very highest and most sacred moment of the consecration of the Nation, whether it was not just because of this that the Sadducean leaders chose this ritual in such an arrant contradiction to the clear word of the text of the Torah?

The כף ומחתה remained בין הבדים until the special עבדת היום was finished, all of which was centered round the הקטרת הקטורת, which, for priests and people alike, atoning for the past, was to be the fresh impulse which was again to lead every contempory time into the path which prepares the way to that ideal future which finds its symbolic expression in קטרת as completely sublimating itself into that which gives God satisfaction, and which was expressed by Moses’s “ונחלתנו״.

V. 14. ולקח מדם הפר: meanwhile the blood had been given למי שהוא ממרס בו כדי שלא יקרוש, to a priest who kept stirring it to prevent it congealing (Yoma 43b). The High Priest now took it from him, and with the vessel of the Sanctuary which had received the blood of the פר he reentered the Holy of Holies, stood again in the same place, בין הבדים, where he had evaporated the נכנס למקום שנכנס ועמד במקום שעמד :קטרת (ibid 53b). והזה :והזה באצבעו על פני הכפרת וגו׳, see note on Ch. 4,6: על פני הכפרת, not on the cover, but כנגד עוביה של כפרת, towards the flat surface of the front of the כפרת, the cover which rested on the Ark and was one טפח high and covered by the זר. This was a sprinkling upwards, למעלה. And ולפני הכפרת, in front of the cover, this was a sprinkling למטה downwards. כשהוא מזה למעלה מצדד ידו למטה, וכשהוא מזה למטה מצדד ידו למעלה, at the upwards sprinklings he turned the back of his hand downward, and at the downward ones he turned it upwards (Yoma 55a רש״י). Upwards he only made one sprinkling, it says further on at the והזה אתו על הכפרת :דם השעיר. Downwards he made seven. All the הזיות were made כמצליף, according to בשורה זו תחת זו :רש״י, in one line every הזיה perpendicularly below and in a straight line with every other one (ibid 53b). Now it does not say: והזה על פני הכפרת ושבע פעמים לפני הכפרת, he sprinkles once למעלה and seven times למטה, but והזה באצבעו על פני הכפרת קדמה ולפני הכפרת יזה וגו׳, he sprinkles once on the surface of the cover, but in front seven times, by which obviously the שבע למטה are placed in special relationship to the אחת למעלה, a relationship which is expressed by the method in which the counting of the הזיות was done. Each one of the lower sprinklings is associated with the single upper one which is repeatedly mentioned at each of the seven lower ones: ר׳ יוחנן אמר אמר קרא ולפני הכפרת יזה שאין תלמוד לומר יזה ומה ת״ל יזה, לימד על הזאה ראשונה וכך היה מונה, אחת, אחת ואחת, אחת ,שצריכה מנין עם כל אחת ואחת (יומא נ״ה ע״א) ושתים, אחת ושלש, אחת וארבע, אחת וחמש, אחת ושש, אחת ושבע, “and thus did he count:— one, one and one, one and two, one and three, one and four, one and five, one and six, one and seven” (ibid 53b).

The Cherubim-cover had a dual reference. They were פרשי כנפים למעלה in their סוככים בכנפיהם על הכפרת, they spread their wings upwards to What was above, in covering the כפרת with them. Their direction was למעלה to the שכינה and the direction was also למטה, to the Torah of God which was to be realised on earth, the fulfilment of which was the condition for the Presence of God and godliness on earth from above. (See Ex. Ch. 25,19). אחת למעלה towards God, that is the first impulse which is given in the Holy of Holies to the דם הפר to the life-blood of the “worker in God’s fields”, the direction to ה׳ אלקי הצבאות יושב הכרובים. But soaring upwards to God, to which every beat of our heart should belong, is not to remain merely an inner exaltation. If the אחת למעלה is a true and genuine and Jewish one it must be followed by שבע למטה, its fruit must be the penetrating of the whole of our ordinary daily life with spirituality, and rendering it godly as, in the Divine Torah which reposes under Wings of Cherubim, is declared to be the Will of God. אחת למעלה is only worth anything through שבע למטה has only any value if all our earthly doings and existence (six) join themselves in eternal bond (seven) with this “one which is above”. And ever afresh has every progress, every step forward down on earth to attach itself to devotion to God above. Not: אחת ואחת שתים שלש etc., but: אחת ואחת, אחת ושתים, אחת ושלש etc., are the beats of our hearts to be counted in the whole moral life which, coming from God, is to be lived in continuous progress. And ever deeper and deeper: ,כמצליף זו תחת זו, has the Spirit of God to penetrate from the height into everything earthly, until the very lowest, deepest, most earthly phase of human life has entered into attachment to the spiritual and godly, and under the “One” above the “seven” below on earth has perfected itself in the bond with God.

This “one and seven” counting of the beats of his heart, this expression of the highest ideal of a Jewish life striving to attain nearness to God here on earth, has the “פר״, “the worker in God’s fields” to renew, first for his own, and for his nearest ones’ future way of life; and at the same time to take to heart as the goal of his work for the life of the Nation, the bringing of the spiritual into all material matters.

V. 15. ושחט את שעיר וגו׳. The people have no other goal than that of the priest. The priest no higher, the people no lower. The High Priest has to carry the דם השעיר into the Holy of Holies in front of the בדי הארון just as he did to the דם הפר. He has to give the blood of the People the same upward cast to the One above and from in the same downward direction to the sevenfold completion of the cultivation of godliness on earth. שעיר-like, will the Nation remain henceforth firm against all external and internal trials and temptations, will allow nothing to entice them away from the One Above nor from the fulfilling His Will on earth, as is symbolised by the אחת למעלה על הכפרת, and the שבע למטה לפני הכפרת of the דם השעיר for the firm and faithful endurance of the Nation in the Bond with God. In Yoma 55a, it is pointed out that אחת למעלה is definitely mentioned only at the שעיר where it says: והזה אתו על הכפרת, and the שבע למטה only expressly mentioned at the ולפני הכפרת וגו׳ שבע פעמים וגו׳ :פר, and that by ועשה את דמו כאשר עשה לדם הפר, both are applied to both. Thereby in a striking manner the complete equality of the vocation of the people and the priests, and that of the priests to the people is expressed. At the priest the אחת למעלה is what is taken for granted and the שבע למטה is expressly mentioned, and at the ritual of the people it is the reverse. Just as in the case of the Priest, so is it with every single son of the People, that with every beat of his heart, he is to soar upwards to the one Only God up Above, and just as the People do, so does the Priest belong to the earth, and his relation to God, too, is to show itself genuine in living a full earthly life which is penetrated through and through with godliness.

V. 16. וכפר על הקדש מטמאת בני ישראל וגו׳. We have already on Ex. XXVIII end and XXX,10, indicated the meaning of a כפרה atoning the Sanctuary. The perfect ideal of the Torah, which is expressed in the Sanctuary, and which, penetrating from there into the life of the People, is always to get nearer and nearer to being actually achieved, is in danger of becoming lost and something less than perfection aimed at if the contrast between the actual life of the people and the ideal is not recognised as being a contrast, and the Torah in the ideal purity of its demands is not brought home to the minds of the people. This saving of the ideal purity of the Sanctuary of the Torah from being lowered by the actuality of the sinful lives of the people is what is meant by כפרה על הקדש מטמאות בני ישראל וגו׳. But (Shebuoth 2a & b, 8a & b, & 12b), the כפרה which is to be achieved by the פר ושעיר של י״כ הפנימיים is referred primarily to sins or carelessness regarding טומאה, by which moral life is shaken in its very foundations, by a denial or weakening of the fundamental idea which underlies all Jewish life of duty to God, the idea — guaranteed by God — of human free will in all matters of morality: זדון טומאת מקדש וקדשיו and יש בו ידיעה בתחלה ואין בו ידיעה בסוף — ,שגגת טומאת מקדש וקדשיו, intentionally flouting the laws against entering the Sanctuary or contacting קדשים while in a state of טומאה, or, knowing his own state of טומאה and knowing that this is the Mikdosh or that these objects are קדשים he has transgressed the laws, but has no knowledge of having done so. In these cases, if finally he gets to know that he has transgressed, i.e.: יש בו ידיעה בתחלה וסוף והעלם בינתים, he would have had to bring a קרבן עולה ויורד (see Ch. 2,5 et seq.). So that laying a fresh foundation for a future morally pure life begins for priest and people with establishing afresh the very first fundamental fact, on which everything else depends, of Man’s ability for self-determination in all matters of morality, of his being master of himself and high above having to obey the instinctive demands of his senses.

טמאות בני ישראל .ומפשעיהם לכל חטאתם are the conditions of טומאה which, as bearing the stamp of “compulsion”, of the lack of free will, exclude a person from פשעיהם לכל חטאתם .מקדש וקדשיו, according to Shebuoth (ibid), includes two cases, pure פשע, i.e. זדון טומאת מקדש וקדשיו, and also the פשע which really lies behind every חטאת שגגה and which has had no כפרה as there was no ידיעה בסוף (for had there been ידיעה בסוף an עולה ויורד would have been demanded). A שגגה, provided there was ידיעה בתחלה, i.e. knowledge of the prohibition, always has a certain amount of guilt behind it, our forgetting or not noticing shows a certain indifference, a carelessness in our attitude towards our duty without which the wrong would never have been committed.

כשם שמזה לפני ולפנים כך מזה בהיכל מה לפני :וכן יעשה לאהל מועד וגו׳ ולפנים אחת למעלה ושבע למטה וכו׳, (Yoma 56b). The same ritual of הזיות which he had performed in the דביר, in the Holy of Holies with the דם הפר, and then with the דם השעיר he has now to repeat in the same way in the היכל which here is called אהל מועד in contrast to the קדש, the Holy of Holies. From ויצא וגו׳ in v. 18, it is evident that, for these הזיות in the היכל he stood in the western, inner, part of it in the space between the מזבח הזהב and the פרכת, hence his going to the מזבח הזהב is termed a יציאה, going farther out towards the east side where the entrance was. Actually these הזיות בהיכל were also done on the פרכת towards the ארון resting behind it: על הפרכת שכנגד הארון מבחוץ, first אחת למעלה ושבע למטה, with the דם פר, and then the same with the דם שעיר both similarly to the counting in the קדש with אחת, אחת ואחת etc. (Yoma 53b). As the purpose of these sprinklings on the פרכת is given as being לאהל מועד, we must look for their meaning in the relation of the פרכת to the אהל מועד, i.e. to the היכל.

If we call to mind the various prescribed הזיות-procedures with the blood of the פר and of the שעיר in their consecutive order:— בין הבדים לפני ולפנים, על הפרכת כנגד בין הבדים, על מזבח הזהב, after which (Yoma 59a), the שירי הדם was poured onto the יסוד of the מזבח החיצון we get a picture of the aim of the life-impulse of priest and people being to build up the life of the Nation starting from the inner innermost and from there working backwards out into the outermost reality of life. It is the same direction horizontally from within to without as vertically from למעלה to למטה. The Ideal, indicated by God, taken to heart afresh in the דביר — the Home of the “Word”, — is to obtain in the היכל — the Home of the “Power” — the “Means”, the spiritual and material gifts as the means to make it a reality, and ultimately for it to be a reality; and with this renewed lofty goal of all Jewish endeavours, finally the “base” of the purifying work from the bottom upwards and from the outside inwards — which is that which the מזבח החיצון is to do — receives fresh strength and nourishment. But the היכל in which the Word of the דביר gets the power and ability (היכל from יכול. I.L.), to direct and govern life may itself be divided into two parts, corresponding to the two ways in which the power of the “Word” manifests itself, a western part, the half nearest to the “Home of the Word”, containing the Menora and the Table, and the eastern part, nearest the entrance in which the Incense Altar had its place. The היכל shows the power of the Word of God in its granting spiritual and material gifts for the creation of the spiritual and material body of the nation; and it shows its power in granting and causing the free-willed devotion and free-willed surrender of all these gifts to the carrying out of all its commands, the manifestation of its power in its mastery of the whole spiritual and material nation it has constructed, In the westerly half of the היכל, the home of the Torah’s granting, the nation appears more receptive, passive, and it is only in the easterly half, the home of the free-willed tribute to be paid, does it appear active in the realisation of the Word of God. But also in the “granting” part, priest and people are given an important high order to activity, namely, to make as the object of their activity, their becoming co-worker with that cherubim-guard of the Torah with which God Himself had promised to build up the spiritual and material development of the Nation, as is symbolised by the פרכת אשר על העדות, (see Ex. 26,31 & 37; and XXVII,21).

This is the order of שמירת התורה, which is to be carried out theoretically in caring for the “teaching and learning” of the Torah, and practically in עשית סייג לתורה and which, as here it does to the מזבח הזהב must always precede the עשיה. The consciousness of the ideal of life’s work which is indicated by the Torah which is to be renewed in the דביר, can only become a reality, the achievement of which is to be symbolised in the מזבח הקטרת, if and when priest and people give themselves up with all their forces to the “Word” which reposes beneath the Cherubim-Wings; if and when they give and ensure it the first place in their spiritual and intellectual development, by constant study and nuturing their knowledge of it, and by constant keeping at a distance everything which would endanger their keeping of it, and thus taking upon their shoulders the Cherubim-service of the Word of God. It is the work for the spiritual and intellectual welfare of the nation and for its conscientiousness, for דעת ה׳ and יראת ה׳. So that when priest and people have gained afresh, as the foundation of their new future, the impulse for the highest ideal individual and national life by the Words which repose under the Cherubim-wings, to make this Ideal into practical reality, Priest and People, the one by his fertile efficacy and influence in working as God’s פר, the other by its שעיר-like firmness in resisting all estranging temptations, have to impress upon themselves the necessity of giving up their life’s blood to the human-cherubim work of guarding the Torah, as is symbolised by the הזיות on the פרוכת in front of the ארון. This, too, must be done by counting repeated energies, אחת למעלה and שבע למטה. For דעת ה׳ remains very incomplete, is only the beginning of “knowing Him”, if it stays at just recognising Him, and does not endeavour to obtain from Him the knowledge and recognition of the Torah, the true nature which everything earthly bears of His impression, everything, down to the very last and nearest-to-earth instance. And the יראת ה׳ which only allows the feelings in general to soar upwards to the One Above is meaningless if it does not consummate itself in making everything here below, on earth, down to the very lowest and nearest-to-earth instance holy to God. Only in אחת למעלה ושבע למטה על הפרכת כנגד :הזיות הארון, with the פר-blood of the priest and the שעיר-blood of the People do priest and people keep the שמירה which both have to keep in דעת ויראת ה׳ for the preservation of the Torah.

לאהל מועד השכן אתם בתוך טמאתם. Even more than the Ideal expressed in words in the דביר does the idea of the היכל suffer by the insufficiency of every contemporarary age which has yet to be freed from the bonds of טומאה of the senses. For it is just the היכל which presents the postulate that the דבר ה׳ does not remain merely an idea, but becomes a power, and exercises power in mastering subordination of everything spiritual and material under the dictate of His Will which gives freedom, and releases the bonds of טומאה. If the דביר suffers, surely the היכל does so too, from the טומאה-contrast of the actual conditions of life in the midst of which it nevertheless makes its home, and accordingly, like the קדש of the דביר, it requires כפרה from the טמאות בני ישראל.

V. 17. וכל אדם וגו׳. While the עבודה — the קטרת והזיות — is being performed in the דביר, nobody is to be in the היכל and similarly when, on י״כ, or otherwise during the year at the daily קטרת, or during the מתנות דמים of a פר כהן המשיח or a פר העלם דבר של צבור, and עבודה is done in the היכל, nobody is to be in the part of the עזרה which is next to the היכל, viz בין האולם ולמזבח (Yoma 44a & 8b): כשם שפורשין מבין האולם ולמזבח בשעת הקטרה (בהיכל) כך פורשין בשעת מתן פר כהן המשיח וכו׳; (the אולם itself is reckoned with the קדושת ההיכל, ibid b). As has already been indicated on v. 16, the idea of the דביר is to find its realisation in the היכל and the idea of the היכל its realisation in the עזרה, so that the עבודה בקדש הקדשים for its purpose must include the היכל and that of the היכל must include the עזרה, the reason for nobody being allowed in the adjoining outer hall while the ritual is being carried out in the inner one, may be just to stress this inclusion and to drive home the significant fact in general, namely, that anything gained in the Mikdosh must, if it is to have any value, go backwards out into everyday life and there bear its fruit: שתולים בבית ה׳ בחצרות אלקינו יפריחו, (Ps. 92,14). (“That which is planted in the House of God, blossoms and flowers in the courtyards—the streets—of our God”. I.L.).
וכפר בעדו וגו׳ ובעד כל קהל ישראל refers primarily to the הקטרת הקטורת, in which the whole national community, priests and people together, represents its combined self (Yoma 44a).

V. 18. ויצא וגו׳. Farther and farther outwards, back into real life, the path of the עבודה moves. At the הזיות על הכפרת he stood within the western part of the היכל, the part nearest to the דביר and had the מזבח הזהב which stood at the border of the eastern half, at his back. In this, these הזיות differed from those of the פר כהן המשיח and of the פר העלם דבר which also were not fundamentally אחת למעלה ושבע למטה. At these the כהן remained standing in the eastern half, and having the מזבח הזהב in front of him, made the הזיות over it (see Ch. 4,6). Here on י״כ he had come out of the דביר into the western, the פרכת-part of the היכל, and now ויצא, he goes out of this part too, right back into the eastern, the Altar part, so that he has the מזבח הזהב in front of him (Yoma 58b): וכפר עליו, it, the מזבח הקטרת, presents the postulate that, that which once a year came to be taken to heart afresh לפני ולפנים in view of the ארון העדות as the highest ideal of life, should be made into a reality, day by day, out in the whole of everyday life at each rising and sinking of the sun’s rays; that, for this the spiritual of the Menora and the material of the Table should unite in being penetrated through and through with this purpose, and קטרת should be ריח ניחוח לה׳. This completely giving oneself up to fulfilling the Divine Torah to God’s satisfaction, which the מזבח קטרת represents, is the whole object of the שמירה-פרכת, the undertaking of which has just been vowed afresh. If this object had up till now been only imperfectly attained, if the past stood, still held in the טומאה-lack-of-freedom, in contrast to the קטרת-perfection of life, then the כפרה-עשיה of the מזבח הקטרת must now follow the כפרה-שמירה of the פרכת, and by vowing to have a future completely in accordance with it, restore the קטרת demand for aiming at the perfect ideal which had been lowered by the imperfect past, restore it to its original beckoning purity.

ולקח מדם הפר ומדם השעיר. For the שמירה which had to be taken to heart afresh in front of the פרכת, priest and people, who alike have to undertake it, have a different and separate approach. The priest as פר the people as שעיר. But in the עשיה, in combining everything spiritual and material for the fulfilment of the Torah in קטרת completion to which the מזבח אשר לפני ה׳ invites us day by day, in life, Priest and People have to combine all their forces, the דם הפר and the שעיר have to mix in intimate union and with united forces have to strive unitedly to accomplish the mission of life in conformity with God’s Will. מערבין לקרנות, עירה דם הפר לדם השעיר, (Yoma 57b), “The blood of the bull and the blood of the he-goat were mixed and stirred together for the application to the horns of the golden-altar”. The Gemora in Menachoth 22a & b points out that: הדבר ידוע שדמו של פר מרובה מדמו של שעיר, although, obviously, the quantity of blood from a bull is much greater than that of a goat, nevertheless, in this mixture, the latter does not lose its character in the greater mass of the former, but retains its שעיר-character. (From this רבי יהודה deduces that altogether מין במינו as here דם in דם, is not בטיל, that a small quantity of a substance is not considered as absorbed by a greater quantity of the same substance. The רבנן, however, only deduce from this that עולין אין מבטלין זה את זה, that substances having symbolic characters as offerings, when mixed together, do not lose their own individual meanings.

ונתן על קרנות המזבח סביב. He goes round the Altar, הקפה ברגל (Yoma 59 & 58b), beginning at the N.E. and turning right until the S.E. corner, and puts some of the combined פר and שעיר blood on each horn: מתחיל מקרן מזרחית צפונית צפונית מערבית מערבית דרומית דרומית מזרחית מקום שהוא מתחיל בחטאת על מזבח החיצון משם היה גומר על מזבח הפנימי. The order of the קרנות was:— E.N., N.W., W.S., S.E.; the מתנות on the inner Altar finished where those of the חטאת on the outer altar began (the S.E. corner, see Ch. 1,5 & IV,25). The fundamental building up of the Jewish life on י״כ starts with the sanctification of the national efforts for material welfare to be made having regard to the Torah (E.N., מזרחית צפונית), then the using of the material well-being for the upkeep and realisation of the Torah (N.W. צפונית מערבית), the realisation of the Torah as the basis of the educational development of the mind and intelect (W.S., מערבית דרומית), and finally the penetration of this spiritual development into the life of the Nation (S.E., דרומית מזרחית). The Nation animated solely by the spirit of the Torah is the final goal of every phase of national life. To keep the Nation on the heights of such a life, morally free and holy, is what Priest and People have to undertake with their united forces, before God, at the Altar of the Perfect Life. To keep oneself on this height of a life always inspired by the spirit of the Torah and always to act in accordance with its teachings, in every phase of ordinary life, קרן דרומית מזרחית, that is the standpoint which has firmly to be kept in the course of the whole year for the purity of life to which one has ever again and again to strive. It is, accordingly, with this, with the קרן דרומית מזרחית, that the חטאת חיצונית starts, with the standpoint on which at the חטאת פנימית, the finger of the High Priest finally rests, as that which is to be taken out for life in general.

V. 19. על טהרו של מזבח :עליו .והזה עליו וגו׳, on it, itself, on the pure gold surface of the top of the Altar, and not on any remains of ashes or coal that might be on it. After the מתנה על הקרנות, the seven הזיות follow, downwards on the surface of the Altar, on that side where the מתנות finished, בצד דרומי (Yoma 59b). Here we have again the אחת למעלה ושבע למטה. The מתנה אחת על כל קרן has to prove its value in the שבע הזיות על טהרו של מזבח. To the firm keeping on the moral heights of Life, guarding oneself against any false step (the מתנות above. I.L.), must be joined the completely positive planting of everything godly down on earth — the earth which is to be elevated to God. To the טומאה-free purity on the heights must be joined the טומאה-free sanctification of life at the ordinary level, וטהרו וקדשו מטמאות בני ישראל.

V. 20. וכלה מכפר וגו׳. While the blood of the שעיר לה׳ which had died under the cut of the Sanctuary had thus been accepted by the Sanctuary, had reached the Holy-of-Holies, and from there had celebrated resurrection for a new full life dedicated to God, and thereby had helped to lay the foundation for a fresh new future, its contrasting comrade, the שעיר לעזאזל remains in undiminished and undisturbed fullness of life, חי לפני ה׳ (v. 10). Now, after the mission of life had been given by the Truths presented by the היכל ,דביר and מזבח being rendered again in their full undimmed clarity by the כפרות, as the postulate of what is to be done in the future, after this, the שעיר לעזאזל is to serve as a means of demonstration of the picture of the life of those who will not, of their own free will, make the sacrifice of their past at the threshold of the Sanctuary of God. Hence, וכלה מכפר וגו׳ is followed by והקריב את השעיר החי.

V. 21. סמך .וסמך וגו׳ על ראש השעיר החי, see on Ch. 1,4: על ראש השעיר החי, it is repeatedly called השעיר החי. For just in this חי lies the significance of the moment and of the procedures. All the עונות ופשעים וחטאים of the past have their roots entirely in the fact that we remained שעיר עומד חי לפני ה׳, that, instead of using the power of resistance which is given to us against the lure of our senses, we turn it against God and His Sanctuary. Placed at the threshold of the Sanctuary of His Torah to make the decision, we fight shy of giving up our selfish living for our own pleasure, and, repulsed by, and afraid of, the demands of God’s laws of morality, we hold ourselves stubbornly against Him as שעיר חי. Therefore והתודה עליו את כל עונות וגו׳, that is why he has to realise that it is on the head of a שעיר חי that he has to lay all the sins of the past. עון is the departure from the one right, “straight” path, (עוה the opposite of ישר), which is made consciously, but only through yielding to temptation, ,לתיאבון עונות אלו הזדונות, (Yoma 36b).— פשע is rebellion, פשעים אלו המרדים (ibid), doing wrong out of contempt of God’s Torah, להכעיס, which is done, not although, but because, it is forbidden. חטאה is wrong done through carelessly forgetting the laws of the Torah: לכל חטאתם אלו השגגות (ibid). Note it says: לכל חטאתם, not: וכל חטאתם, for עונות ופשעים are related to חטאות, they are their children. Indifference, carelessness towards the Torah, indifference, carelessness in what should be our attitude towards the Torah, out of which alone a שגגה could occur, is in itself the beginning of a פשע and leads to complete עונות and פשעים. Between indifference and contempt is only a small step, easily taken. The sweetness of sin, first tasted in careless forgetfulness, very soon allows the cup of sin not to be withheld from the lips even with the full consciousness of its being wrong, and then finally to hate the Torah as the disturber of the joy of life, as the enemy of our unrestricted שעיר-life, and to raise contempt of it to a principle of life. So that this לכל חטאתם refers to the חטאות as being the first cause, the original begetter of the more serious sins. The order of the וידוי of the High Priest also runs in the same way according to the חכמים (Yoma 36b) חטאו עוו פשעו וגו׳ (ibid 66a), as well as at his own הטאתי ועויתי ופשעתי :פר וכו׳, (ibid 36b), a rendering which occurs in Ps. 106,6; Kings I 8,47; Daniel 9,5; and is also the version generally accepted for our וידוי.

ונתן אתם וגו׳. Similar to Deut. 11,29: ונתתה את הברכה על הר גרזים ואת הקללה על הר עיבל, where the “נתון״ surely does not mean a concrete placing of blessing and curse, that the blessing should cling to Mount Gerizim and the curse to Mount Ebal, but certainly does not mean to say anything but that the blessing which is to be obtained by fulfilling the Torah and the curse which results from the non-observance of it is to be so publicly declared on them in the presence of the whole Nation, that these two mountains lying at the immediate entrance to the Holy Land are for all future times, to remind the People of the decision they have to make for the alternatives of the future fate which had already beforehand been proclaimed and put before them. Already by their appearance, these two hills, such contrasts to one another, brought to mind this alternative set in the land of God’s Torah, as we have already remarked on אלון מורה (Gen. 12,6). So here, too, surely, there is no idea in ונתן אתם על ראש השעיר, of any mysterious magic actual laying the sins on the head of the goat. It means nothing more than by the acknowledgment of sins on the head of the goat, this שעיר החי is to call to mind the wrong attitude to Life in which all חטאים עונות ופשעים have their root, and on which they rest.

ושלח, he sends it away (see v. 10). That which is represented by שעיר החי, the attitude of life which refuses the self-sacrifice of giving oneself up to God and His Torah, to which all the sins and errors of the past are attributed, obtains no admission to the Sanctuary, must be sent away from its threshold, away from its neighbourhood, away from the habitations of Jewish people. It, which ridicules the sacrifice of a life turned towards God, sees over the threshold of the Sanctuary of the Torah only slavish repressions in life, and death, and sees freedom and life beckoning far away from it. It has, just with this shrinking from sacrifice, chosen desolation and death. It does escape thereby the threshold of the sacrifice-demanding Law, but only to become banished from it and from human circles and to finish up in the desolate wilderness, המדברה — ושלח! And all unbeknown to it, this end in the wilderness stood behind it as the fate of its future already even when it was standing in unbowed שעיר-pride, הי at the entrance to the Sanctuary, yea it had already incurred it at the moment we made the decision, עתי, — מוכן, שיהא מזומן :ושלח ביד איש עתי לכך מאתמול, (Yoma 56b, Rashi there). The man who was to lead it to the Wilderness had to be appointed for that purpose already on the previous day.

V. 22. ונשא וגו׳. By the שעיר החי, on whose head the errors and sins of the past had been acknowledged being sent by the People, through their representative the High Priest, out of the neighbourhood of the Sanctuary and of the People, out into ארץ גזרה במדבר, the acknowledgment and the vow is made that the power of resistance if turned to defiance of God and His Torah with all the errors and sins which emanate therefrom, is עזאזל and shall be עזאזל; is “without any future” and shall be “without any future” (see v. 10), shall have no future in the lives of the people, who, on the contrary, see the model of their calling and the promise for their future in the ארץ גזרה —.שעיר לה׳, (Yoma 67b): אין גזרה אלא חתוכה, a piece of ground which is cut off, a place where the ground is suddenly cut away and falls steeply down to the depths where the desert begins. ושלח את השעיר במדבר: from there he has to push the goat over into the desert far below. This leading the goat out into the wilderness and pushing it down from the cliff is only מצוה, it is not מעכב, not essential for the כפרה, certainly nothing like being the כפרה itself. Only the הגרלה and the וידוי are מעכב, are essential. Only the decision לעזאזל and the recognition that it is on this misuse of moral will-power, turning what should be לה׳ to “self-will without a future”, that all the errors of the past rest, but which is to have no “future”, is עז-אזל, only these two moments are essential. יעמד חי לכפר עליו (v. 10) it only need live until the כפרה is completed by the וידוי דברים and it receives the fate to be sent to the wilderness as being עזאזל׳s. The actual carrying out of this שילוח and pushing it down the precipice belongs only to the completion, the rounding off of the thought which is to be presented, but is in no wise essential for the כפרה itself, (Yoma 40b). This Halachic fact very definitely contradicts every attempt of taking Azazel to be a demon of the wild and the sending and hurtling down of the goat an offering sent to appease him, or as a destruction of a substitute “scape-goat”, (cf. the article in the Gesammelte Schriften vol. V, entitled “The Two Lots”).

V. 23. ובא אהרן וגו׳. It is impossible that ופשט וגו׳ should be a subordinate clause to ובא אהרן וגו׳, to show the reason for his having to enter the Sanctuary again. For it is impossible that the היכל ,אהל מועד and קדש הקדשים were the place where change of clothes are to be made and in which clothes are to be kept. And now Aaron should be told to re-enter the Sanctuary simply and solely to undress there! To that would then be added that v. 24 in the same way would follow v. 23 and Aaron would be taking his טבילה in the Sanctuary itself, or anyway would have to go out from there to the place of the טבילה quite undressed. All of which is quite impossible to be the meaning of the text. The Halacha (Yoma 70b), accordingly teaches: ובא אהרן אל אהל מועד למה הוא בא להוציא את הכף ואת המחתה, that the reason for this going into the Sanctuary again was to bring out from the Holy of Holies the מחתה and the כף of the קטרת which were still lying at the foot of the כפרת between the בדים. This purpose which forms no עבודה and is not even a part of an עבודה, but merely what is self-understood to be necessary after the end of the עבודה is accordingly not expressly mentioned in the text. It is the last act which the כה״ג had to do on י״כ in the בגדי לבן. Then, after the completion of this act, ופשט, he had to take off the בגדי לבן which he had again put on before this last act אשר לבש כבר (Yoma 71a), והניחם שם, and deposit them there for ever in the עזרה-hall in which he had put them on, מלמד שמעונין גניזה :והניחם שם, they were never to be used again (Yoma 24a).

At the same time the Halacha teaches, there on 71a) that כל הפרשה כולה נאמרה על הסדר חוץ מפסוק זה, all the verses of this chapter are in the correct order in which the procedures described were to be done, except this verse. This is only put here to finish off all the procedures that had to be done in the בגדי לבן. For everything up to this point belonged to the עבודות פנים which had to be done בבגדי לבן. The וידוי ושלוח שעיר המשתלח, too, although they took place בעזרה ,בחוץ, belonged to it also. The שעיר המשתלח is the representation of the other side, the opposite of the שעיר הנעשה בפנים. Both belong to the most characteristic עבודות היום for which בגדי לבן are prescribed. All that follows belongs to the עבודות חוץ, which were done in בגדי זהב, and is therefore introduced by ויצא ועשה את עולתו וגו׳. Actually, the Halacha teaches us, the הוצאת הכף והמחתה was only done after the offering of אילו ואיל העם of the following verse, which had to be done in בגדי זהב. So that, according to tradition, the עבודת י״כ fell into five divisions, which, as already remarked on v. 4, were marked by changing from בגדי זהב and vice versa four times. For the עבודה which had to be done in the בגדי לבן, of which the last act was the הוצאת הכף, was interrupted by עולתו ועולת העם of v. 24, making thereby three divisions. These were preceded by the one in בגדי זהב, and one in בגדי זהב concluded the Service of the great day. The order in which the individual procedures took place within these divisions is not quite certain. רש״י and רמב״ם differ as to the place which the הוצאת הכף occupied in relation to the evening תמיד של בין ערבים. According to רש״י, this preceded the תמיד של ב״ע, but according to רמב״ם followed it, and after it only קטרת ונרות had to be done, (see ל״מ on הל׳ עבודת יום כפור, 2,2).

The ritual of the offerings ordered here in Levit., ת״כ, form only one part of the offerings which have to be brought on this day. They are the ones most characteristic of the day, which mark it as יום הכפורים, and they come from the special character of the day. They form the עבודת היום and so are the prominent central point, about which the other series of offerings are grouped; those other offerings which result from the general idea of the day, the תמידים and the general idea of the מועד with which the Day is associated with the cycle of the other מועדים, the מוספים. The ordering of these is contained in the chapter of offerings in Numbers, חומש הפקודים (Ch. 29,7—11). The עבודת היום on י״כ stands in a similar relation to these תמידים ומוספים as the עומר and the שתי הלחם on Pessach and Shebuoth (Levit. 23,9 et seq. & 15 et seq.) do to their תמידים and מוספים. There are two references which mark the connection between these two series of offerings and thereby determine their relative position in the order of the day. In Numb. 29,11 at the end of the מוספים for י״כ it refers to the עבודת היום which is given here in our chapter. It says: שעיר עזים אחד חטאת מלבד חטאת הכפרים ועולת התמיד וגו׳. This חטאת הכפרים is the שעיר הפנימי of our עבודת היום and from the “מלבד״ it is clear that this שעיר המוספים has to come after the שעיר הפנימי (Yoma 70b). The שעיר הנעשה בחוץ is, accordingly, directly connected with the שעיר הנעשה בפנים. Further the איל העם which, according to v. 24, had to be brought at the same time as the איל of the כה״ג prescribed in v. 3, after the completion of the עבודות פנימיות at the first going out to the עבודות חוץ is identical with the איל המוספים of Numb. 29,8. There was only one איל העם לעולה, which had to be brought. Accordingly, while in v. 3 it simply says ואיל לעולה, in v. 5 it expressly says: ואיל אחד לעולה (Yoma 7b). So that we get two animals, the שעיר and the איל taken out of the מוספים and both — the שעיר by מלבד וגו׳ and איל by ויצא ועשה וגו׳ — given their place immediately after the עבודת היום.

If we add to this the fact that, according to ר׳ עקיבא (Yoma 70b), by that which is said referring to the מוספים both regarding those of the רגלים as well of י״כ, viz. מלבד עולת הבקר אשר לעולת התמיד (Numb. 28,22), the מוספים — here with the exclusion of the איל and the שעיר — are normally to be in connection with the תמיד של שחר, then we have the essential order for the סדר of the עבודה של י״כ laid down. We have: (a) the תמיד של שחר and the פר and the שבעת הכבשים of the Musaf offerings; (b) the עבודת היום, i.e. the ritual prescribed here in verses 6—22; (c) the שעיר חטאת of the Musaf offering: אילו ואיל העם (v. 24), the אימורי חטאת (v. 25), and (according to רמב״ם, see above), the evening-תמיד; (d) הוצאת כף ומחתה (v. 23 see above); (e) קטרת ונרות. This is the order given explicitly by רמב״ם in הל׳ יום הכפורים 4. All these עבודות had to be done on י״כ by the High Priest himself: (a), (c) & (e) in בגדי זהב (b) & (d) in בגדי לבן. The meaning and significance of the תמידים, of the תרומת הדשן, which precedes it and of the קטרת נרות חביתים ונסכים, associated with it, we have already tried to explain in Ex. 29,38; Levit. 6,1—5 & 12—16. Here we shall go into the מוספים, the explanation of which will be given in Numb. 28,29 only in as far as to try to understand the connection of the שעיר and איל which belong to them (the מוסף-offerings) with the עבודת היום with which we are dealing here, and so to understand the whole grouping.

Just as the rising and sinking rays of light of every day invite our homage to the One sole Creator and Director of the whole existence of the world, and to unreserved surrender to His guidance in all the rising and falling phases of our lives, and such homage and surrender finds its expression in the Tamid offerings, in the same way the making remembrance of historical events which showed the special guidance of God for Israel and the mission He entrusted to them, into Remembrance Days, invites Israel to special homage to that same unique One, as the sole Creator, Director and Guide of Israel, and so to some renewed expression of Israel’s special relation to Him, even as their Tamid offerings express their homage to Him as the Creator and Director of the World in general. These are the days in which God’s special relation to Israel and Israel’s special relation to Him were historically experienced, and which God therefore fixed for all time to be מועדים as “meeting times” in which God expects His People in renewed intimacy of union. The fundamental מועד of all מועדים is the ראש חדש, the day of the New Moon, whose cosmic מועד-appearance was dedicaed immediately on Israel’s elevation to “The People of God” to be an ever recurring memorial of the establishment of the idea “מועד״ in Israel as we evolved on Ex. 12,2. The מועד-offerings in which the national מועד-idea are expressed, are compiled in Numb. XXVIII & XXIX, the offerings which are to be “added” to the Tamid as מוספים on each מועד. The fundamental formula for these offerings is the מוסף-offering of ראש חדש, viz.: פרים שנים ,איל אחד ,שבעת כבשים, all to be brought as עולה, and a שעיר לחטאת. This group of offerings recurs in all the מוספים with the only modification that on י״כ ,ר״ה and שמיני עצרת, instead of the two bulls only one is brought. This formula lies also behind the מוסף-offerings of סכות, as we shall have to show.

In the מוסף group of offerings Israel represents itself as being called on, as one united Nation (פר אחד) not only so, but also every single member of it (פרים שנים) to give active service in God’s work on earth (the קרבתנו מלכנו לעבודתך of our מוסף-Prayer), that thereby the Nation should march in prominent national eminence as איל leader, in front of the nations of God’s pasturage on earth; and by that, the closeness of their union to God, their one and only Shepherd, שבעת כבשים, stamped on their fate and history (the ושמך הגדול והקדוש עלינו קראת of our מוסף-Prayer).

פר ,איל ,שבעת כבשים yea פרים, such is the signature under which God has entered Israel in the book of human history in accordance with their mission and their destiny. פר, yea שבעת כבשים ,איל אחד ,פרים, that is the signature under which Israel, on each of its מועדים has again and again to represent the picture of its calling and of the mission of its existence and destiny; and in which to give expression in עולה of completely giving up the whole of its being for this mission and for such a God-borne destiny. But it can not think of this, the mission and destiny of its national life, without at the same time becoming conscious of the fact that the nature of this mission and destiny has received its everlasting unambiguous plain attestation from God, in His Torah; the Torah which forms the sole bond between it and its God, and to which it accordingly erected the Sanctuary of its God, and which forms the one criterion before God at all times of how it is fulfilling this, its mission. And if it can not think of this mission before God, without at the same time putting the testing question to itself whether it had not perhaps even unconsciously fallen into the bonds of טומאה from the pure heights of טהרה on which the Sanctuary of the Torah wishes always to see it, then it can not bring the happy עולות of its national mission on the Day of God’s מועד without, at the same time, renewing the חטאת-vow for the future; the vow henceforth to exercise, with שעיר-like tenacity, resistance to all internal and external lures which might drag it down from the pure Altar-height of its holy calling. Hence, although otherwise חטאת always has to be brought before עולה, in the מוסף-offerings it follows the עולות.

י״כ, too, the 10th of תשרי (v. 29) is מועד, is מועד in the very highest sense of the word. Although on ניסן 15th Israel experienced the nearness of God in the foundation of its existence as a Nation, and hence every recurring 15th of ניסן led Israel, in joyous consciousness of the continuance of God’s proximity to them, to meet God, the creator of its national existence; although on the Day of the Lawgiving, God sent His Word, as herald of His Presence, directly to each single soul in Israel, and gave him the mission of his national existence and the task of his personal life in the service of His God, and hence every recurrence of that great day led Israel, in joyous consciousness of being still in possession of that Word as the one pledge of its connection with God, led Israel up to meet God, to the Granter of its national importance, to the One Who gave meaning to its life; nevertheless already before the first tenth of תשרי Israel had lost both through their folly, thrown away by Israel’s greatest historical sin. Turning the Jewish mission into ridicule had prescribed the destruction of Jewish existence. But to all the great historical facts which the actual experiences of Jewish life had proved, the 10th of תשרי added the proof of the greatest of all great Truths, namely that God does not only once grant existence and impart the task demanded from such existence, but that He is always ready again and again to grant a new existence which has been forfeited by deriding its mission, and with the renewal of the old broken Law, for its future faithful fulfilment, to “cover over”, to “bury” the past and to introduce a completely new rejuvenated future. If פסח is the מועד for the revelation of the miracle of God’s almighty power by the creation of the Jewish Nation, for which שבועות brought the conditions for its continuance, יום הכפורים is the מועד for the revelation of that miracle of miracles, God’s almighty power in eradicating all consequences of the past, the re-creation of an existence which had already lapsed to extermination, the מועד of כפרה, the spiritual, moral, social rebirth through the almighty grace of God, the resurrection out of spiritual moral and social death. Hence: לא היו ימים טובים לישראל כט״ו באב וכיוה״כ (Baba Bathra 121a), hence יום הכפורים ranked with the most joyful מועד-days which Israel had, and that is why on יום הכפורים Israel joined itself to the morning offering of the Tamid as the re-established פר as being renewed afresh to the service of God, as the re-established שבעת כבשים, as the renewed flock of God, which had once lost the Shepherd of its life and had again found Him for ever.

But to the איל-idea, to the thought of Israel being the leading ram blessed by God, to the feeling of striding at the head of God’s human flock, leading them on the way they are to go, to that, on י״כ the consciousness of one’s own insufficiency, the inadequate way in which the mission of Israel has hitherto been accomplished, stands in the way. It is only the thought of the coming regained spiritual uprising before God as coming from God, which can draw the present with it also into contemplation of the everlasting ideal of the Israel of the Holy of Holies, to find from the unshakeable evidence of the כפרה actually experienced in the past כפרה-ground for the present; עולתו ועולת העם, the איל of the Priest and of the Nation of Priests can only come after the כפרה achieved by the עבודת היום, and this itself must first be completed by the חטאת חיצונית, the שעיר הנעשה בחת of which it says in: חומש הפקודים, מלבד חטאת הכפורים, which must first have been associated with the שעיר הנעשה בפנים. For the שעיר הנעשה בפנים is essentially כפרת הקדש and only indirectly כפרת העם (see Ex. Ch. XXVIII end) but the שעיר הנעשה בחוץ is truely and quite specially: כפרת העם מטומאת מקדש וקדשיו, in it Israel again bestrides the Altar-heights of טהרה on which it has consciously to keep, and from those “summit horns” it should never have thoughtlessly slipped.

Before the High Priest went to the עבודות חוץ which are introduced in the following verses, he read out the פרשת אחרי-מות and also ובעשור in חומש הפקודים, by which all that had been done, and all that was now to be done, was proclaimed as being the fulfilment of God’s orders, and thereby any semblance of their being the expression of his own ideas or feelings was refuted (see Yoma 68b רש״י).
V. 24. ורחץ וגו׳ ויצא וגו׳, see on v. 23.
V. 25. ואת חלב החטאת וגו׳, i.e. the אימורים of the פר ושעיר הפנימיים, see on Ch. 4,8—10.

V. 26. והמשלח את השעיר וגו׳ יכבס בגדיו. This is the איש עתי who brought the goat to the wilderness. He is מטמא בגדים וכלים שנוגע בהן בשעת שלוחו, (like one who is נושא נבלה while he is carrying it) from the moment that he goes out of the walls of Jerusalem (Yoma 67a). The animal itself is not מטמא (Zebachim 105a). The moment the goat is sent out of the מחנה, it appears with the utmost conciseness as the embodiment of that mistaken way of life which misuses the Divine gift of free decision by giving oneself up to be mastered by one’s senses, and which turns that which was given to us to devote to moral freedom, to devotion, into moral lack of freedom. It becomes the representation of the טומאה which is to have no place in מחנה ישראל. So it is the idea of lack of free will, of having to yield to the dictates of the senses, the idea of טומאה which the משלח receives as long as he is מתעסק בשלוחו. Hence his טבילה ,טומאה and הערב שמש before he may come into contact with קדש again.

V. 29. והיתה לכם וגו׳: that which follows. It is certainly not without reason that the way in which the laws of י״כ are set out differ conspiciously from that which is used for all the other festivals. To be analagous with these we should have expected to have been given the day and month right at the beginning as well as the character and meaning of the Day, something like this: בחדש השביעי בעשור לחדש יום הכפורים יהיה לכם ובא אהרן לכפר בקדש, בזאת יבא אהרן אל הקדש וכו׳. But then the essence of the יום הכפורים would lie in the כפרות which are to be achieved by the offerings in the Sanctuary. But in the way it is set out in the text all these rituals of offerings are only stated to be the condition for, and the result of ביאת אהרן אל הקדש, everything from vv. 3—28 is solely dependent on the: בזאת יבא אהרן אל הקדש of v. 3, and only now, with our verse 29 is it set into connection with י״כ. But this keeps the כפרה-character of י״כ separate and independent of the offerings.

In verses 29—31 it is declared as יום ענוי ואיסור מלאכה, both repeated as הקת עולם, and its purpose proclaimed in v. 30, as יום הכפורים. So that the sole condition for this כפרה is fulfilling the demand for ענוי and שביתה. But at the same time, the כפרת הקדש והעם is to be achieved in the Mikdosh by the High Priest through the offerings, verses 32 & 33, as is ordered in vv. 3—28. The יום הכפורים celebrated by the whole Nation by ענוי and שביתה also leads their symbolic representative, the כה״ג into the Holy of Holies in front of the בדי הארון. Just as on י״כ every individual Jew has to examine the whole of his life by the yardstick of the Divine Torah, and the result of such testing finds its expression in ענוי and שביתה, so has the Nation as one symbolic unit to step before the “evidence of this Torah”, and the result of this ביאת אהרן אל הקדש finds its expression in the procedures of the offerings in the בגדי לבן, as we have tried to show.
בחדש השביעי בעשור לחדש: See on Ch. 23,27.

תענו את נפשתיכם. From Isaiah 58,3 & 5, it can be seen that עינוי נפש is identical with צום, fasting; and again in v. 10 there: ,ונפש נענה תשביע ענוי נפש appears as the opposite of שובע. It means literally “to make the נפש poor”, to deny the נפש the means of its existence; it is, accordingly, the prohibition of eating and drinking. The Gemora says definitely in Yoma 74b: יכול ישב בחמה או בצינה כדי שיצטער וכו׳, that no positive tormenting pain-producing procedure is indicated here by ענוי, but solely an abstention from food in the same way as איסור מלאכה is an abstention from constructive work. Hence it is quite inapt and misleading to use the term “afflict” which coming from the Latin affligere has the innate idea of inflicting grievous pain. Apart from eating and drinking the conception of עינוי in its wider sense includes abstention from רחיצה, סיכה, נעילת הסנדל ובעילה. But it is not quite certain whether these extentions of the idea of עינוי are דאורייתא or וכל מלאכה לא תעשו —.דרבנן, the prohibition of מלאכה on י״כ is quite as comprehensive as on שבת and is not limited to מלאכת עבודה as it is on the other מועדים. Hence the sentence in Megilla 7b: אין בין שבת לי״כ אלא שזה זדונו בידי אדם וזה זדונו בכרת. They only differ in the punishment. On מלאכה ,י״כ is punishable only with כרת while on שבת it is האזרח והגר וגו׳ —.סקילה: see on following verse.

V. 30. כי ביום הזה יכפר עליכם. The subject of יכפר can only be the עשור לחדש, the 10th of תשרי, of the previous verse. It is the day itself which is to bring כפרה. The 10th of תשרי, which established the fact of כפרה, like all the great Truths of Judaism, by the convincing certainty of actual historical experience, is, as often as it recurs, to accomplish afresh the Almighty Miracle of Divine Grace. That is why, because the nature of the Day rests on national historic experience, in the previous verse: האזרח והגר וגו׳, are specially mentioned in order to include one who has become a Jew, not by descent but by his own free will, in the meaning and in the resulting duties of the Day.

כי ביום הזה וגו׳: the כפרה and טהרה to be achieved by י״כ is the reason for the איסור מלאכה and the עינוי which is ordained. י״כ is to bring us כפרה, literally is to “cover” us from the effects of a sinful past, and the direct working of this כפרה is לטהר אתכם, is טהרה, the regaining of moral freedom, of mastery of ourselves, which is dulled by every sin committed. Every sin has a double effect:— disaster in external life and lack of moral control in one’s inner life. Without the intervention of the Almighty miracle of God’s Grace, in a world built on the principle of Right and Justice, of cause and effect, every wrong committed would bring about the ruin of the sinner, and every first sin would progressively make the pure soul ever more and more sinful, ever more conversant with sin and more liable to continue sinning. The former is the resultant external punishment often only coming later, the latter is the immediate unhappy result on the internal life, שכר עברה עברה. Life about us and life within us moves in accordance with certain Laws, which, in themselves immutable, are only unalterable for those for whom an Almighty Free Will had instituted them, and for whom that Almighty Free Will allows them to be in force. But God has promised Man that He is ready at any moment to use His Almighty Will to introduce a completely new future for his external and internal life, completely independent of the seeds of that future which he may have sown in the past. Hence He has proclaimed Himself not only as אלקים, as the Ordainer of the Laws of Nature which govern the world, but also, as ה׳, as the One through Whom not only everything which was to be, came into existence, but as He, on Whose free Almighty Will every coming moment depends, and Who in His Love for the progressive education of mankind is ready at every moment to allow a new and fresh future to begin for every man. Hence the great כפרה saying:— מכל חטאתיכם לפני ה׳ תטהרו, “Whatever your past may have been, however and wherever you may have sinned, לפני ה׳, before ה׳ your God, the Owner and Dispenser of all Future, you can and you are to, rise to a new pure future”. Before Him and by Him you will be delivered and freed from the seeds of failure and ruin which you have laid by your sins in the lap of the future, and from the bonds of lack of freedom in moral matters in which you have become bound by your sins, and rise up before God, with a new spirit and a new heart, with new pure moral feelings which are again receptive for godliness, and joyously and enthusiastically swell towards everything pure and good. The איסור מלאכה and עינוי with which the day expects us to celebrate it, expresses this obtaining a new future before God with the double gifts of כפרה, the protection for external life and of טהרה, the rebirth to a pure inner nature. Just as on שבת, refraining from all productive work brings home to our minds the fact that the right we have to master the world about us does not come from ourselves, so does the איסור מלאכה on י״כ express our consciousness that we have forfeited the right which God has given Man to master the world about us for our own purposes, as the עינוי which goes with it expresses the avowal that we have forfeited the right which God has given all creatures to sustain their lives by food. Both together express the avowal by actual deed, that by our misused past we have lost the right to enjoy further existence and creative life; that, without the intervention of God’s Grace we should have to cease living. The one, איסור מלאכה, is the act correponding to the כפרה which we are to achieve. By sinning against the world around us and by misusing the power which has been given us to mould and adapt our civic lives (the ל״ח מלאכות and הוצאה, see Ex. 35,2), we have sundered the bond with which the Word of the Creator placed His earthly world at the feet of Mankind and forefeited the blessing necessary for success which the King of the world of humanity has promised for all honest efforts in the struggle for existence. Nature and Society fight against us and only the כפרה which is to be obtained before God, and from God, can give us again a position of power and blessing in Nature and Society. But the other, עינוי, is the corresponding act by which we avow the טהרה which is to be regained. By yielding and giving ourselves up to the enticement of the pleasures of life which God has given us to be used only to further God-serving purposes of the world, we have stripped our physical beings of its moral character, the character of טהרה, of being in full control of ourselves, we have sunk our moral freedom of will in the bonds of physical sensuality and thereby sunk to the level of animals and given up the basis of a continued existence worthy of human beings. לפני ה׳ תטהרו only before God, the pure fountain-head of all freedom of will and all pure moral force, can we be redeemed from the bonds of feeling that we can not resist these lures, can we achieve our resurrection, our rising up anew to purity.

אשריכם ישראל, accordingly, is the proclamation of ר׳ עקיבא on this point: אשריכם ישראל לפני מי אתם מיטהרין מי מטהר אתכם אביכם שבשמים שנאמר וזרקתי עליכם מים טהורים וטהרתם, ואומר מקוה ישראל ה׳, מה מקוה מטהר את הטמאים אף הקב״ה מטהר את ישראל, “Happiness is thine, O Israel, before Whom dost thou obtain thy purity! Who maketh thee pure? Thy Father in heaven! For it says: ‘I pour pure water over you and ye become pure!’ The fount of Israel’s purity is God, even as a Mikvah purifies the unclean, so doth God make Israel pure”, (Yoma 85b).
So איסור מלאכה and עינוי on י״כ are a continuous וידוי which loudly proclaim the חטאתי עויתי פשעתי with all their dire results, more deeply than the mere words do.

But the Halacha teaches (Yoma ibid) that only עבירות שבין אדם למקום יוה״כ מכפר, that it is only our own personal sins against God which do not adversely affect any of our fellowmen, which receive כפרה on יוה״כ and they refer this teaching to the words of our text: מכל חטאתיכם לפני ה׳ תטהרו. But: עבירות שבין אדם לחברו אין יוה״כ מכפר עד שירצה את חברו, where we have sinned against our fellowman, we can not look up to God for כפרה until we have satisfied and pacified our fellowman and endeavoured to obtain his pardon. And further: האומר אחטא ואשוב אחטא ואשוב אין מספיקין בידו לעשות תשובה, אחטא ויוה״כ מכפר אין יוה״כ מכפר, he who sins with the consoling thought: “I will repent and better myself later on”, will never achieve repentence and betterment; to him who sins relying on יוה״כ to receive כפרה, to such a one יוה״כ brings no כפרה (ibid).

V. 31. שבת שבתון היא לכם. The Sabbath of Creation, שבת בראשית, is always called: שבת לה׳ (Ex. 16,25 & XX,10; as well as Levit. 23,3; and Deut. 5,4). שבתות ה׳ (Levit. 23,38); for its שביתה is homage paid to the sovereign authority of God, it expresses the fact that the world belongs to God. Similarly the שבת הארץ (Levit. 25,2), in which the שביתה expresses that the land and state of Israel belongs to God. But of י״כ it says: שבת שבתון היא לכם, for its שביתה is the expression of our unlawfulness; so also in Ch. 23,32: שבת שבתון הוא לכם. Now it says: שבת שבתון היא לכם ועניתם את נפשתיכם. Were it a שבת לה׳ then שביתה ממלאכה would suffice, it is only a question of stopping the exercise of our own mastery in face of the acknowledgment of God’s Mastery. But it is שבת לכם, it is a question of expressing our own unworthiness by this שביתה, it extends not only to the loss of the justification for the position of power given to Man, but even to the loss of the justification for existing. Hence ועניתם את נפשתיכם! In this connection of ענוי with שביתה in which עינוי is taken to be only an extended idea of שביתה — not only “arresting” your work, but “arresting” your means of existing — is explained (Yoma 74a), that the additional word שבתון is taken to apply also to עינוי; so that, just as for איסור מלאכה by the conception of שבתון, the extension of the prohibition of work is extended to activities which do not really have the actual character of ,מלאכה (אין שבתון אלא שבות) (See Ex. 20,10), so, here, the additional word שבתון extends the conception of עינוי beyond refraining from אכילה ושתיה to include the other עינוים mentioned on v. 29 as being שבות of עינוי. The word שבת itself only means suspension of activity and so can equally well be applied to the act of eating etc., as to that of working. (See Rashi in Yoma ibid).

V. 32. וכפר הכהן וגו׳. By שביתה from מלאכה and eating etc., it is only our necessity for כפרה from God which is primarily made evident. But that our sins against God as individuals can only consist of sins against the Torah in which His Will is revealed to us, so that our opposition to God always manifests itself in opposition to His Torah, and every return to God can consist of nothing else but a return to His Torah: that — when this Torah with its demands has its symbolic representation in our midst in the Sanctuary of God — is to have its public national expression, through the national religious representative, the כה״ג, by the כפרה-ritual in the Sanctuary of the Torah which is complementary to the איסור מלאכה and עינוי acknowledgment made by each individual member of the Nation. Hence וכפר הכהן, the כה״ג has also to ratify in the Sanctuary the כפרה which the Nation has to celebrate by שביתה and עינוי. The כה״ג is described as the one אשר ימשח אתו and אשר ימלא את ידו. From Ex. 29,29 we know that the installation of the High Priests into office consisted of anointment, and investure with the משיחה and ריבוי בגדים, anointment was sanctifying him, separating him out from the midst of the Nation for holiness, and ריבוי בגדים was investing his person with the symbolic expression of the qualifications which the Ideal Jew should have to carry out to the full the ideals of the Torah. This investment with the ריבוי בגדים is the real מלא יד, the positive granting of authorisation to act as High Priest. It sufficed by itself if there was no שמן המשחה and after the end of the שמן המשחה. The subject of the verbs ימשח and ימלא is either, as is often the case, impersonal general “whom one has anointed”, or it is ה׳, God, (v. 30), to Whom the whole connection can very well refer back, and it would then be the Sanhedrin, who, in the name of God and the Torah had to perform the installation of the High Priest. Based on the fact that here, on the one hand it says: לכהן תחת אביו, and on the other: ואשר ימלא את ידו, the ת״כ sees here the great important principle laid down of conditional heredity of office which is in force in Jewish Law for every public officer who wields any power whatsoever, from the King downwards to the smallest petty official, any מינוי שיש בו שררה. The ת״כ says on our verse לכהן תחת אביו מלמד שהבן קודם לכל אדם. The words לכהן תחת אביו give the son the right to inherit the office of his deceased father. יכול אף על פי שאין ממלא מקומו של אביו, ת״ל ואשר ימלא את ידו, בזמן שהוא ממלא מקומו של אביו הוא קודם לכל אדם ואם אינו ממלא מקומו של אביו יבא אחר וישמש תחתיו, had there been nothing further added , this right of inheritance would be unconditional, the office of the father would be given over to the son even if the latter were not suitable for filling his father’s place. But as the application of this right of succession is made dependent on a special act of authorisation, אשר ימלא את ידו, it is clear that the right of a son to inherit his father’s position and office is not as absolute and unconditional as his right to inherit his land and property. It is dependent on the fitness and ability of the heir. The Nation or the community has to investigate this worthiness and ability. If the son has the necessary qualities למלא מקום אביו he is קודם לכל אדם, he is given the office and post of honour of his father, and the Nation or the community may not confer it on another. If he lacks this worthiness, then another has to be chosen in his stead. And it is the worthiness of character rather than knowledge or wisdom which gives the casting vote in such choice: חכמה .ממלא מקומו ביראת חטא, the depth of theoretical competency which the office demands; if still incomplete, can always still be acquired. But where יראת חטא is lacking, the claim is lost. (See Kethuboth 103b; רמב״ם Melachim 1,7). This principle of “conditional right of heredity” combines the advantages of the rights of heredity and those of election without the disadvantages which are peculiar to each of them (see responsa on א״ח of חתם סופר 12,13).

ולבש את בגדי הבד בגדי הקדש. The priest who has been found worthy to be invested as High Priest with the vestments symbolic of moral perfection in which he represents the Ideal Jew living the Ideal Life has to take off these garments on the day of י״כ. For on this day he and his people are demonstrating, by refraining from food and creative work, the contrast which their actual life and doings show to the lofty ideals which are promulgated in the Sanctuary. He is to clothe himself in the garments representing the state of still striving for moral purity, as designated in v. 4, and, so apparelled is first:—

V. 33. וכפר את מקדש וגו׳, by the מתנות בפנים, on the פרכת and on the מזבח הזהב to atone for the dimming of, and to restore the purity of, the ideals of the תורה and of ישראל as presented by the דביר and היכל which had been dimmed by the contrast which the actual life of ישראל showed to these ideals, and so directly by these rituals — see Ex. 28,43 — as well as indirectly by the שעיר המשתלח, to achieve atonement for both priests and people.

V. 34. והיתה זאת לכם. This זאת summarises together into one idea the עינוי and the איסור מלאכה which each single individual has to observe on י״כ and the עבודות in the Mikdosh. The whole is חקה, is nothing which comes from human ideas, is a demand prescribed by God, and only as such has it meaning and importance, and only as such is it to be celebrated by us on the one day of the year which God has fixed on which He has promised to answer our fulfilment of that demand by granting us כפרה.

ויעש כאשר צוה ה׳ את משה. The reason for this final verse is not quite clear. Perhaps it refers back to the introductory words of v. 1 & 2.
