The death of the sons of Aaron, to which the warning: ואל יבא בכל עת, is attached, held up a stern warning to Aaron and to every one of his successors in the office of High Priest, from the very beginning of the priestly activities in Israel, against the assumption of any presumptuous pride. Our verse may wish to tell us that it was in the full sense of that warning that Aaron carried out all his priestly services, in spirit as well as in deed solely in obedience to the commands which he received from God through Moses. That is how the ת״כ explains this verse:— מנין שאין אהרן לובש בגדים לגדולתו אלא כמקיים גזירת מלך ת״ל ויעש כאשר צוה ה׳ את משה; “Not for his own honour or elevation did Aaron wear the garments, but as fulfilling a command from a King”.

Vv. 1 & 2. In the previous chapter the underlying thought was the warning against that error, which, in failing to recognise the lofty ideal of moral perfection and at the same time to recognise the imperfection of what has actually been attained, overlooks the gap which still separates us from meriting proximity to God; which, like the case of the young priests, celebrates the elevated feelings of a moment of consecration, as a credential of already having attained perfection, and does not see that it is not moments of exaltation soaring above the ordinary, but just making the ordinary way of everyday life holy by assiduous attention to one’s duties towards God which leads to the Moriah height of an existence which is near to God. Hence that chapter ordains a searching estimation of the past way of life as the condition for entry accross the threshold of the Holy of Holies, ordains the discarding of any proud illusion of any greatness already attained before facing the Ideal of Life which shines forth from the Holy of Holies of the Torah, and only allows a modest approach to the sublime goal with the renewed determination of eternally striving to attain it.

Now, this chapter has the underlying thought of warning against the opposite error, that of dismissing the idea of the nobility of moral human worth, of turning one’s back to the moral ideal of humanity which is attested by God in the Sanctuary, as being mere illusory presumption; and which takes the basis of Man’s position in the world to be, not his relationship to God, and the purpose of his existence not the fulfilment of God’s Laws of morality, but his relationship to the animal world, the basis of his position in the world, and animal-like gratification of his senses the ideal of his vocation.

Both, ideal overrating our nature, as well as underrating it, deprive us of a true sense of what we should be and what we should do and makes us lose the attainment of our vocation. The one, the chapter warning against ideal overrating was primarily directed to Aaron. The other, this one, meant to protect the consciousness of moral human dignity and worth is directed to all classes of the Nation.

זה הדבר אשר צוה ה׳ . The deep importance of the following law is already announced by these introductory words. Only once again do we find a Divine command enjoined by a similar formula, at צנצנת המן in Ex. 16,16, where an eternal memorial to God’s special providence was to be made by keeping a flask of the Manna. Moses himself uses it for specially important institutions, at the תרומת המשכן (Ex. 35,4), at the מלואים (Levit. 8,5 & IX,6), at נדרים (Numb. 30,2), and נחלה (Numb. 36,6). But as a direct commanded form of communication it only occurs here and at the מן .

V. 3. In Chulin 16b & 17a, there is a difference of opinion between ר׳ ישמעאל and ר׳ עקיבא. According to the former during the whole period of the sojourn in the wilderness, בשר תאוה, i.e. killing שור כבש ועז solely for the purpose of eating the meat, was forbidden. Only that which had been consecrated as שלמים, and, as such, brought as an offering in the משכן could afterwards be eaten by the בעלים. It was only after the entry into the Land that הותר להם בשר תאוה, and the permitting order in Deut. 12,20 & 21 would refer to this. Then, as Rashi says there in Chulin, the prohibition of בשר תאוה in the wilderness would be contained here in verses 3—7. But according to ר״ע, the killing and eating of בהמת חולין was not prohibited in the wilderness: בשר תאוה לא איתסר כלל, and the law in Deut. 12,20 & 21, would only give the command for שחיטה which, before the entry in the Land was only required for קדשים whereas the character of נבלה was removed from חולין by simple נחירה (see notes there in Deut.). In accordance with that conception our verses here, as well as the laws which follow in v. 8 et seq. would only refer to רמב״ם .קדשים בחוץ in הל׳ שחיטה 4,17 adopts the view of ר״ע. But Rambam remarks here on our verse, that in the majority of depositions of our sages which have come down to us, the opinion of ר׳ ישמעאל stands pre-eminent, and it is really more in accordance with the wording of our text. If we compare the wording of verses 3 & 4 with that of 8 & 9, everything seems to indicate that the former is speaking of חולין and the latter of קדשים. In v. 3 the objects are: שור כשב ועז, while in v. 8 they are described as עולה או זבח. We should accordingly, here, have the prohibition of killing שור כשב ועז, i.e. the kinds of animals suitable for offerings, not as offerings, but for ordinary profane food, חולין. Every such animal is to be brought to the forecourt of the Sanctuary and there alone may it be killed, and must be offered as שלמים. By Deut. 12,20, where it says: כי ירחיב וגו׳ בכל אות נפשך תאכל בשר, this prohibition of בשר תאוה is then limited to the stay in the wilderness and ceases with the entry into the Land.

במחנה או וגו׳ מחוץ למחנה. In v. 5, this killing of animals is characterised as a killing על פני השדה and this would indicate the reason of the prohibition. It was therefore necessary to say that it is not only outside the camp, actually in the open fields, that killing not in the משכן is considered as זבח על פני השדה, but that even within the area of the camp, during the wandering in the wilderness, the ban applies. Similarly, in ת״כ, where our verse is referred to שחיטת קדשים בחוץ, taking the opinion of ר״ע every במה-offering is explained as an offering מלמד שכל הזובח בבמה כזובח :על פני השדה בשדה. So also in Zebachim 106b.
V. 4. דם יחשב וגו׳. Slaughtering an animal על פני השדה is to be taken as murder. See on v. 7.

V. 5. למען אשר יביאו וגו׳. This אשר יביאו is a contrast to the על פני השדה. For בוא is exactly a coming in from the open into an enclosed space. The יביאו is quite definite here, and by the repetition והביאום, where the accomplishment of the aim לה׳ וגו׳ is only then added, the law which is given here seems to be given in its two factors. It is the negative factor, the keeping away from the sphere of פני השדה with the pernicious erroneous train of thought which is attached to it: יביאו. And then the positive factor, in contrast thereto, the devotion to ה׳ and to His Sanctuary: .והביאום לה׳ וגו׳ אותם: וזבחו זבחי שלמים לה׳ אותם are the animals that they want to slaughter for the requirements of their ordinary food, they are the זבחיהם אשר הם זובחים וגו׳, they are, as long as they are wandering in the wilderness, to bring such animals out of the open into the פתח of the אהל מועד אל הכהן to ה׳, and slaughter them as שלמים. See on v. 7.

V. 7. ולא יזבחו עוד את זבחיהם לשעירים וגו׳. In the preceding chapter we already came across a שעיר as the representative of that sensuous animalism which in uncontrolled wildness lives out in the מדבר, but which is to have no place in that sphere of human lives which was being built up about the Sanctuary of God’s Law’s of Morality. In Isaiah 13,21: ושעירים ירקדו שם, as well as in XXXIV,14: השעיר על רעהו יקרא, we also find שעירים as the most characteristic animals of the wild. So there can be no greater contrast to the godly human ideal of the laws of morality, in paying homage to which Man gets near to God than שעירי השדה. A man who brings his offering, his representation of himself, to the שעירים על פני השדה instead of לה׳ אל פתח אהל מועד אל הכהן, to get near to God in the Sanctuary of His Torah, to the representative of His Torah whom He has appointed to be the condition for, and the means of attaining His Proximity, such a man makes animalism, living uncontrolled out in the open, as his ideal for Mankind; he denies the godly character of Man as being the specific mark of difference between Man and Beast, he makes the most materialistic part of ourselves and of all our days, in animal-like yielding to our senses, the one and single calling of Man; he tears up the very last fibres of the roots by which he was attached to the sphere of humans specifically belonging to God, ונכרת האיש ההוא מקרב עמו. He commits thereby a spiritual murder, דם יחשב לאיש ההוא דם שפך (v. 4). It was just respect for the completely different nature of Man which by his likeness to God, raises him high above the animals, having respect for the צלם אלקים in Man, that the Word of God (see Gen. 9,6), proclaimed as the reason for murder, in contrast to the permitted killing of animals, being stamped as the highest outrage against God’s commands. He who offers up an offering meant to be the symbolic expression of a human personality (or one phase of his personality as with מנחות), to the ideal of animal life commits a spiritual sacrilegious murder to the צלם אלקים nature of Man, דם יחשב לאיש ההוא דם שפך!

Not in the purely physical life of Nature which matures על פני השדה, to which Man is related only through his body, but in the dictates of the Divine Laws of Morals, which speaks to the free Spirit of God in Man, and for which he has been given free-willed mastery over his physical body, only in these dictates of God’s Laws have we to seek the Word for our calling. As soon, therefore, as this “Word” had obtained its permanent דביר, its exclusive abode — בשעת איסור במות — every offering which was not brought into the sphere of its Sanctuary was considered as turned away from the Laws of morality which were there attested by God, considered as a ת״כ) ,זבח בשדה and Zebachim 106b; see v. 3), and was forbidden under penalty of כרת (see on Deut 12,13).

But according to the tradition of ר׳ ישמעאל (see v. 3), not only an offering, but every killing of שור כבש ועז, even simply for food, בשר תאוה, as a זבח על פני השדה was forbidden as being a זבח לשעירים. We have repeatedly had occasion to remark how the fact of nourishing the human body by the flesh of animals was quite specially likely to have the tendency to disturb the consciousness of the higher dignity of the human being, and to drive home the fact that the nerves and muscles of animals were the same as those of human beings. Now when men were living in what was really the realm of animals: על פני השדה, במדבר, where שעירים ירקדו שם, where they were surrounded by, and impressed by, the free, unfettered life of the animals around them, it could easily happen, especially at the moment when they are killing animals to nourish their own life, that their senses become gripped by the urge to similar animal freedom from restraint, and they זונים אחרי השעירים lust after animal life, turn away from human morality and יזבחו זבחיהם לשעירים וגו׳, and in every slaughter of an animal for human consumption they celebrate their homage to the Animal Ideal. These considerations may explain to us why just in the wilderness, בשר תאוה was forbidden and could be compared to שחוטי חוץ of all times. According to that, every animal destined for ordinary food, in the wilderness would have had to be made into a שלמים, it would have had to be brought to the משכן ה׳ and as a קרבן לה׳ have had the purpose of attempting to get near to God, having regard to His Torah. Taken out of the realm of purely physical nature, its existence must be given the purpose of striving upwards to God, (וזרק הכהן את הדם וגו׳) and its desires to giving satisfaction to God, (והקטיר החלב לריח ניחוח לה׳), before it may be allowed to enter as food and nourishment in a human existence.

זאת :חקת עולם תהיה זאת להם לדרתם, the prohibition of לזבח זבחים which in the מדבר extended even to איסור בשר תאוה, and for all time resulted in איסור שחוטי חוץ and איסור במה. In Chron. II 11,15 we find במות and שעירים paired in the defection of Jeroboam: ויעמד לו כהנים לבמות ולשעירים ולעגלים אשר עשה, as in Sanhedrin 63b it is said: יודעין היו ישראל בע״א שאין בה ממש ולא עבדו ע״א אלא להתיר להם עריות בפרהסיא, “Israel knew perfectly well that there was nothing in idol worship, they only gave themselves up to it on account of the practice of open sexual immorality that went with it”.

Vv. 8 & 9. ומן הגר אשר יגור בתוכם. It is wrong to translate יגור in this connection, with “sojourn”. The גר צדק who here and in similar places is referred to by this term is one who has taken up permanent residence in the Jewish community. Clearly here the root גור has the meaning of “being a גר״ or “entering as a גר״ and in this sense we translate the phrase as “the stranger from foreign parts who has entered into your midst”. Moreover we believe as remarked on Gen. 13,9 that the original meaning of גור is “having no land”. So that גר would be the opposite of אזרח. He is replanted here from a different ground. Also he has no original right to the possession of ground, and through the effect of the יובל-laws can hardly ever get possession of real estate permanently, especially if ירושת הבעל is not דאורייתא.

אשר יעלה עולה או זבח ואל פתח וגו׳, here definitely the העלאת קדשים בחוץ, the bringing of offerings dedicated to God, outside the מקדש at the time of איסור במות is forbidden. And equally with העלאה, i.e. הקטרה, both שחיטה and זריקה are included in the prohibition Zebachim 106 et seq.). Further, it is clear that the חיוב כרת is only incurred for bringing such offerings which would be fit to be brought in the Mikdosh, which are ראוין לבא אל פתח אהל מועד, which are ראוים לפנים, excluding all פסולי מוקדשים (ibid 112 et seq.). שחיטה and העלאה differ, each has its own חומרא. The חומר בשחיטה is that שהשוחט להדיוט חייב while המעלה להדיוט פטור, if one is מקטיר an offering בחוץ, one is only חייב if it is done לה׳, whereas השוחט קדשים בחוץ is also חייב even if the שחיטה is done merely for ordinary food. The חומר בעלייה is that שנים שאחזו באבר והעלו חייבין, but שנים שאחזו בסכין ושחטו פטורים. Even if the act is done by two people together, העלאה, they are both guilty, but in the case of שחיטה one is only חייב if one does the act alone (ibid 108a), this is indicated by the repeated: האיש ההוא ,לאיש ההוא, at the שחיטה (v. 4) (ibid). The ההוא which we ordinarily find with כרת, the ונכרת האיש ההוא is taken to indicate that the penalty of כרת is only incurred when the act is done with full consciousness, and is free-willed: למעוטי שוגג אונס ומוטעה (ibid b). שחיטה and העלאה are to be taken as two independent prohibitions so that השוחט והמעלה בחוץ חייב על השחיטה וחייב על העליה, (ibid 106a). In 108a, there, we learn further that: אינו חייב עד שיעלה לראש המזבח, that העלאת קדשים בחוץ is only punishable if they are burnt on an altar erected for that purpose, but not if they are brought on a rock or stone.

If we consider all these laws:— that שחיטת והעלאת קדשים בחוץ are both forbidden, if they are done לה׳, but העלאה, only when they are לה׳, but not if they are done for ordinary food, further that the object must be ראוי לפנים and the הקרבה on a מזבח, then שחוטי חוץ is clearly not to be taken as being, like ע״ז, a defection from God, but as a defection from His Torah which reposes in the Mikdosh. As soon as this Torah had found its permanent home, בשעת איסור במות, bringing an offering dedicated to God elsewhere than in the Sanctuary of the Torah, expresses the conviction that relation to God can be established, “nearness” to God obtained, by other means than the Torah, without necessarily treading the path of God’s Laws, that one can turn one’s back on the Torah, and still turn one’s face to God. But thereby he has torn himself and his future out of Jewish ground as ונכרת האיש ההוא מעמיו actually declares for him and his descendants. For to one born in Judaism and to one who has entered Judaism as a גר, the way to God lies solely over the way of His Torah. The bond which joins Man to God, for the Jew, is no other than alliance with His Torah.

But העלאה and שחיטה are two separate ideas. שחיטה expresses a negative idea. It is the giving up of one’s own selfish life, of the animal life, living solely for satisfying the senses. העלאה is a positive idea, devoting one’s life to the purposes indicated by God. העלאת קדשים לה׳ בחוץ would be devotion to self-suggested purposes, taking purposes not taught by the Torah as being ordered by God. שחיטת קדשים לה׳ בחוץ, not בפתח אהל מועד, not with regard to the tasks of life ordained by the Torah, would be the heathen erroneous idea that self-destruction is pleasing to God. But שחיטת קדשים להדיוט בחוץ comes within the conception of זביחה לשעירים על פני השדה, within which the איסור בשר תאוה במדבר falls and understandably remains prohibited for all time. Hence, even according to the opinion that בשר תאוה was never forbidden, still שחיטת קדשים להדיוט בחוץ would be prohibited, as according to this opinion, it is just that which alone expresses the pernicious idea to which the prohibition: ולא יזבחו עוד וגו׳ of v. 7 refers. More, we have already referred to the sentence in ת״כ which teaches that every זובח בבמה, even if it is זובח לה׳, in to be considered as a זובח בשדה. And actually, if in our relations to God, we turn our back to the Torah, and in bringing our offerings to Him we place ourselves outside the sphere of the Torah, we not only renounce adherence to a life of duty dictated by God, but endanger the whole purity and truth of our consciousness of God. That which we call God, and to which we approach with our offering may be just nothing else but the God of Nature, Who is regarded by us an על פני השדה, as being the laws of Nature, but not the One completely Free, Personal God, of the Torah. And this is even more likely, the more this true consciousness of God would have kept us within the bounds of morality which He has revealed to us in His Torah, out of which we are stepping just by our שחוטי חוץ.

What, however, does still remain difficult is the ruling that שנים ששחטו בחוץ פטורים, especially as such a שחיטה is quite כשרה if done בפנים (Chulin 30a). According to remark of הגאון ר׳ עקיבא איגר זצ״ל on Zebachim 13,3: שנים ששחטו בחוץ would only be פטורים when זה יכול וזה יכול, and so would be analogous to other איסורים (see on Ch. 4,27), and then one would only have to consider why in a similar case in העלאה they would be חייב.

The introductory words: ואליהם תאמר in v. 8, are worth considering, as well as the insistence of the גר in this verse, whereas above in v. 3, he is taken to be naturally included in the conception: בית ישראל. If the first paragraph of this chapter, verses 3—7, in accordance with the opinion we have followed, speak primarily of שחיטת חולין בחוץ i.e. of the prohibition of בשר תאוה, and it is only in verses 8 & 9 that it comes to speak of קדשים בחוץ, then we can find a reason for both. The first paragraph forbids a שחיטה which could be taken as a זבח לשעירים על פני השדה, a wrong-doing the denial of which does not only begin with Judaism. Here it is self-understood that the prohibition affects גרים as much as the children of Israel. But the prohibition contained in verses 8 & 9 refers, as we have said, quite definitely to an offering, לה׳. The thought of God is essentially kept, but the relation to God’s Torah is not only not kept, but, by the הקרבת חוץ בשעת איסור במה, is actually denied. But the relation to Torah does only begin with Judaism, it is that which makes the Jews into Jews. Here the גרים would specially be mentioned, and the ואליהם תאמד would express the following thought:— “You have just warned the priests and all those that belong to the Nation against erroneous ideas of God Himself, but tell them that, to be a Jew, it is not sufficient to truly believe in “God”, but that the relation of a Jew to God, at once necessitates relation to תורה, and a denial of this latter is quite the same for a Jew, as the denial of God Himself, both entail, in quite equal severity, כרת, being uprooted from the national existence.

Vv. 10—12. We have already explained, on Gen. 9,4, the different expressions used here and in v. 14 for the relation of the blood to the soul, and the repudiation of any material aspect which they might be thought to have, and we would refer to that explanation.
Here, too, גר is brought into prominence; for the prohibition of eating blood also only starts with Judaism, although אבר מן החי is forbidden to non-Jews also.

We have already twice had the prohibition of the eating of blood combined with that of חלב in connection with the laws of offerings in Ch. 3,17 and in Ch. 7,26 & 27. Here the prohibition of blood in itself is repeated with quite special seriousness. Just as in Gen. 9,4 et seq. for the post-diluvian world, the אבר-מן-החי-prohibition is placed in connection with murder, and comes to vindicate the specific higher dignity of the human soul as contrasted to the animal soul, so here for the Jewish world (v. 4). שחוטי-חוץ was described as murdering the ideal of Man, committing murder of an idea, ranking Man as equal to, nay subordinating Man under, the animal ideal. Then, directly following that, comes the repetition of the prohibition of eating blood from the point of view of negating any indentification of the human soul with the animal soul. By means of blood, that medium which circulates throughout every part of the body, the soul regulates and directs the nerves and muscles which are only the organs of its activity. The ever present blood in the body is the ever present visible messenger in the body of the ever present invisible directing soul. Hence it is the visible representative of the soul, and hence is most suitable to be the symbolic expression in offerings of elevating and devoting the soul to God, as well as of its faithful remaining with God.

ואני נתתיו לכם על המזבח. On the Altar, for the symbolism of the offerings, God has given blood to us to express our souls by it, there the blood means בנפש יכפר, that we can only obtain atonement with our souls. As the priest throws the blood to the Altar, or with his finger quietly indicates its place at the heights of the Altar, so has our soul to raise our blood afresh up to God, or with renewed strength of concentration to keep it firmly on lofty Godliness whenever a past error is to be atoned for and a fresh future, near to God, started. בנפש יכפר can not mean: “it achieves atonement for the soul”. The prefix -ב with כפר never refers to the object but to the means of the atonement. So in Ch. 7,7: הכהן אשר יכפר בו לו יהיה, and in Numb. 5,8: איל הכפורים אשר יכפר בו עליו. In Zebachim מ״ו from לכם or from לכפר we learn: שאינו חייב בדם משום מעילה נותר וטומאה, (see Ch. 5,15).

But just the nature of blood and its close relation to the soul which makes animal blood suitable for symbolic expression of the human soul, forbids its being actually taken up in the realm of the body of the human soul. And this seems to be not only to combat the pernicious erroneous idea — which might seem to be favoured by this symbolism in offerings — that animal and human souls are identical, but at the same time to prevent some concrete danger to the mental state of the human character. The whole weighty warning in v. 10: ונתתי פני בנפש האכלת את הדם וגו׳, as well as the urgency of the admonition, repeated again and again in Deut. 12,23—25: רק חזק לבלתי אכל הדם etc.,לא תאכלנו etc. לא תאכלנו למען ייטב לך etc., goes to show that eating of the blood of animals is prone to bring about a real endangerment, or anyway such a depravement of human nature, that could be capable of robbing the aptness for the moral heights which God’s Torah has set for the vocation of a Jew.
אמרתי לבני ישראל כל נפש מכם לא תאכל דם: the way this is put implies the duty of all to see that this prohibition is kept by all, hence Yebamoth 114a: להזהיר הגדולים על הקטנים, (see on Ch. 11,42).

V. 13. In closest connection with this prohibition of eating blood, as v. 14 shows, we get here the further command of כיסוי הדם, i.e. the duty of covering with עפר, the blood of deer or birds which are permitted to be killed for food: חיה ועוף טהורים וכשרים. This duty only applies to game and birds and only to חולין, but not to מוקדשין — from which in any case חיה are excluded — and they must be טהורים וכשרים, but not נבלה or טרפה. This is implied by the condition אשר יאכל (Chulin 83b & 85a). There, too, we are taught that יצוד is not to be taken strictly but that the covering of blood has to be done בחיה ועוף מזומן וכשאינו מזומן, not only to those that have been caught but also to those bred at home.

וכסהו בעפר: According to Chulin 83b, not with עפר but in עפר. The עפר must be shaken under and on top of the blood. Actually if עפר had to be simply a covering the wording עפר would have sufficed. The name of the means of covering requires no preposition. We find ואכסך משי in Ezek. 16,10; and וערום יכסה בגד (ibid XVIII,7); כסו הרים צלה (Ps. LXXX.11).— עפר, (see on Gen. 32,25), is in its real meaning fertile earth. Chulin 85a explains that עפר here is not meant literally but is given as an example and designates anything in which plants can successfully be grown, or to which the appellation עפר is given:— :כלל אמר רשב״ג דבר שמגדל צמחין מכסין בו ושאינו מגדל צמחין אין מכסין בו. Nevertheless, ashes and gold dust are also declared (ibid 88,b), as suitable, as both occur under the name of עפר, we find עפר שרפת החטאת (Numb. 19,17), and עפרות זהב לו (Job. 28,6). The phrase: וכסהו בעפר, does not come under the heremeneutic rule: כלל ופרט, אין בכלל אלא מה שבפרט, by which the carrying out of וכסהו would be limited exclusively to עפר because here the כלל, i.e. וכסהו, requires the פרט to make us understand what is meant, that the כסוי does not mean just a covering over, with a lid or covering of any sort, but must be something that can be completely mixed up with that which is to be covered, a כלל הצריך לפרט (ibid 88b). The Halacha teaches further that the covering need only be done once, so that if it had been covered and then became uncovered it need not be covered again. On the other hand, if the wind had blown ashes or earth over it and then it had become uncovered again, the duty of covering it remains (ibid 87a). Finally, the whole of the blood need not be covered, it is sufficient if only a part of it is done (ibid 88a).

The point of view from which the underlying thought behind all these laws may be found may be given in the introductory words:— ואיש וגו׳ אשר ציד וגו׳. The animals concerned, חיה ועוף are thereby designated with reference to their being animals, by their original natures, in the free state away from the power of Man, animals of the open, “על פני השדה״. But, in the שחוטי-חוץ-laws, which preceded the associated blood-laws, we have been told to regard the sphere of just these “על פני השדה״-animals as being the one where the ideal of a free untrammelled animal life is most alluring to the sensuality of Man. It is understandable, that at the moment when animals of this sphere are taken to nourish human beings, the prohibition of blood and the separation of animal nature from Man’s nature which it presents, should be given a further special mark of emphasis. The deepest difference between these two natures is, as we recognised in Gen. 2,7, comparing that verse with I,24, that in animals, not only the body but the life itself, the נפש came from the earth, whereas in Man, only the body was עפר מן האדמה, but his life, his נפש חיה, his living soul, was a breath of God Himself, and so does not belong to עפר. At the moment when animal body is to become a part of the human body — both related in being עפר, — the blood, representing the nature, the נפש of this animal is rejected from the threshold of the human being and mixed in עפר to which, in contrast to the נפש אדם, it belongs. The דם the נפש בהמה can never reach or become an integral part of Man, but when freed from the body of the animal can only regain shape or form down in the realm of vegetable organism, it truly belongs to עפר מגדל צמחים. Hence the double definition:— anything which comes under the conception עפר, and anything which is מגדל צמחים, is qualified to be used for כסוי הדם.

That the fulfilment of this command is meant to be the representation of a thought, and not just simply an actual covering up of the blood is quite evident from all the more precise laws governing it; for instance, that the duty falls away in cases of נבלה וטרפה, that if it becomes uncovered one need not cover it again, that, according to the accepted Halacha of ר׳ יהודה, it is sufficient to cover just a part of the blood, that altogether it is not actually covering but a mixing in עפר which is prescribed, it requires עפר למטה ועפר למעלה.

V. 15. This group of laws finishes with a supplementary completion of the law of טומאה given in Ch. 11,24—40, which finds its place here as, according to the traditional teaching it only refers to נבלת עוף טהור, to the dead body of a “pure” bird, and we have just had a characteristic law given to us regarding the blood of just such an עוף אשר יאכל. In Ch. XI: טומאת נבלה was restricted to only the dead bodies of בהמה וחיה טהורה וטמאה and for these טומאת מגע ומשא was declared, but מגע only applying to the external parts of one’s body, but not to בית הסתרים. By this latter restriction, eating a piece of נבלה by contact in the act of swallowing, would not by itself make one טמא provided one had not touched it במגע or במשא (this latter even בבית הסתרים, see Nidda 42b). And this although there, in v. 40: והאוכל מנבלתה וגו׳, is specially mentioned as well as הנוגע and הנושא, as we have explained there. So that if here it talks about a טומאה for אכילת נבלה, it can only refer to an object for which, according to Ch. XI, there is no טומאת מגע ומשא, and that is just נבלת העוף. And here it can only be concerned with a נבלת עוף טהור as here the case is a combined one, viz. a נבלה which previously while still alive was טרפה. But the conception טרפה only applies to טהורים, that יש במינה טרפה. It probably chose this combined case to teach us at the same time that טרפה by itself is not מטמא. A bird which had become טרפה is only מטמא if afterwards it becomes נבלה by death, but if it dies by שחיטה, then שחיטתה מטהרת אותה מידי נבלה. The same applies to בחמה טרפה ששחטה (see Ch. 11,39 & 40, — כן נראה לפרש אליבא דר׳ יוסי שהלכה כמותו, (Zebachim 69b).

So that here we are told that eating the נבלה of a “pure” bird makes one טמא and that the clothes he is wearing at the time of eating, or כלים which he touches at the same time become ראשון just as he himself does, in exactly the same manner as by משא נבלה (see Ch. 11,35), or, as it is generally put:— נבלת עוף טהור מטמא בגדים בבית הבליעה, and only at the moment of אכילה, i.e. the moment it touches the throat, neither before nor after, when, as טומאה בלועה, it is considered as non-existent. Neither בתוך הפה nor בתוך המעיים, but only בבית הבליעה, although for all other טומאה, contact with the throat in swallowinng is not ת״כ) ,מטמא, Nidda 42b; See Ch. 22,8).

If the way we have taken it is correct, that the reason why טומאת נבלה is restricted to land-mammals is because the formation of their bodies is most similar to that of human beings, so that their dead bodies bring to mind the picture of dead human bodies, and that is why birds are excluded from טומאת נבלה, then the same reason which imposed: כסוי דם for the blood of birds as a special mark of the divorce of the idea of animal nature from human nature, may lie behind this specially characteristic טומאה בבית הבליעה of birds. The bodies of birds are only one degree further removed from the human organism than are those of mammals, and if on that account ordinarily touching a dead bird does not cause טומאה, still, just on that very account, at the moment of its being about to become a part of a human body, the טומאה and טהרה-Law does raise its voice as, from another point of view, the picture of the free life of a bird, as is shown by כסוי דם, and the attractive idea of complete unrestricted freedom makes a special warning necessary for the sensual side of Man’s nature. We believe further, that the reason why מגע בית הסתרים does not make one טמא, is to show that the animal’s similarity to Man which is the underlying reason for טומאת מגע, is only an external appearance, נבלת בהמה and also נבלת חיה must accordingly remain free from טומאת בית הבליעה, and it could only apply to נבלת עוף, to which all other טומאת מגע does not apply, and had to be applied only to נבלת עוף טהור, as the character of this species as being fit for human food gives countenance to placing them on par with human bodily nature. So it seems לענ״ד.

But this טומאת אכילה by touching the הבליעה, which is peculiar to נבלת עוף טהור, goes beyond that of ordinary מגע, and has all the consequences of טומאת משא, because, like that, it goes beyond mere external contact and affects Man to a deeper degree. It comprises Man’s food in relation to the moral factors of his nature, and hence has to guard Man from טומאה-thoughts in all phases of his moral being, in his personal appearance and in his activities, בגדיו וכליו.
ונשא עונו: if he enters the Mikdosh or eats קדשים while in a state of טומאת גוף, or if he brings כלים טמאים into the Mikdosh, the former is punishable with כרת and the latter with (ת״כ) ,מלקות.

V. 1. Not to elevate the free uncontrolled impulsive life of animals to the ideal of human life, and to allow animal nature no entry into human nature is what we have taken to be the contents of the laws which were given in the previous chapter on: כיסוי דם ,שחוטי חוץ and נבלת עוף טהור, and the prohibition of eating of the blood. But the most powerful factor of this animal life just following instinct, which free-willed morality mastering and using in the service of God forms the foundation of personal and national civilisation, is sexual life, the Divine regulation for which forms the contents of the laws contained in this chapter. Verses 1—4 are the introduction.

V. 2. דבר וגו׳ ואמדת וגו׳: “Say unto them” and “explain to them” the whole great meaning of the three words: “אני ה׳ אלקיכם״. Just as the words: אנכי ה׳ אלקיך stand at the head of the whole Lawgiving, so here again stands this axiom at the head of these laws of sexual living and stamp them beforehand with the whole seriousness of their importance. The keeping of these laws forms the very first presumption of Jewish life, just as with מילה, with the symbol of mastery over the carnal side of Man’s nature, the foundation stone of the Jew’s bond with God is laid. And, in conformity with the seriousness of this meaning it says: not אנכי, but אני, the Personality Which, if necessary, appears against your world and your “I”, ה׳, the One on Whom every next moment of your being and existence is dependent, Who alone can and will bring you to the goal of a happy future, He is אלקיכם, your Creator, Lawgiver and Judge; just as you received your personal and your national existence from Him, so have you to accept from Him, and from Him only, the law for the use and development of that existence.

V. 3. כמעשה וגו׳ לא תעשו ובחקתיהם לא תלכו. We have already remarked on Gen. 6,8 that by פעל and עשה social conduct is chiefly indicated whereas הלך is used for individual moral way of life. So we find the sum of all the duties of life summarised as הדרך ילכו בה, and: המעשה אשר יעשון, in Ex. 18,20. Here, too: מעשה ארץ מצרים, and: מעשה ארץ כנען, seem to designate the social behaviour which marked the relation of men to each other in Egypt and Canaan, but לכת בחקתיהם, the individual and private ways of life which they practice in their individual and family lives. The former are regulated by State-laws, the latter less by legislation but rather by rules which become sanctified by custom and convention. The former, the social condition of life of the country, show the attitude of a nation towards justice and civic life. The motives which prompt them and the principles behind them, whether pure or the reverse, true or false, are, as a rule, transparent, and can be recognised by the conditions of life which they effect and the purposes they are to accomplish. The traits of the private and family life, and also the personal national traits, i.e. those which are characteristic of a nation, are usually influenced by the more or less obscure ideas of the relation of the supernatural to individuals and nations. The gods are mostly considered as being of an inimical nature and as being a disturbing element in Man’s endeavours. To obtain grace from the gods, or at least to ensure their non-interference in projects and undertakings, becomes a consideration and purpose in the name of which conventions are regulated, and customs showing honour to the gods and supposedly gaining their favour become firmly embedded in the private and public life of nations. The former are the משפטים, the latter חוקות of the nations. In the Egyptian state the former had dug the grave of all consideration of the dignity of a human being as such and of human freedom, in Canaan the latter had sanctified moral excesses to the depths of bestial depravity. Just as השחתת דרך and חמס in the antediluvian world had led to ruin, as the Sodomite Union of Cities which lie buried in the bed of the Dead Sea had been both רעים and חטאים so everywhere משפטים and חוקים react mutually in dual effect; everywhere depravity of morals and social tyranny and oppression go hand in hand. It is only a morally pure family life that becomes the cradle of a free nation which stands for Right and the duties of brotherly love of fellow man, and only in a free nation based on justice and duty does the heavenly blossom of morally pure human existence thrive. In social slavery lies the death also of morally pure Man.

Accordingly, it is to the social and moral degeneration as it appeared in Egypt and Canaan that the introduction to the laws regulating sexual life and the building of families refers, and says, “Let not the pattern of Egypt and Canaan form the guiding influence for your social and moral life, not from Egypt and Canaan are you to fetch your משפטים and חוקים, but rather: את משפטי תעשו ואת חקתי תשמרו, etc.

חקות :ובחקתיהם לא תלכו, in contrast to משפטים are the laws and rules for what is to be allowed or forbidden, which are not to be formed by ourselves out of the nature of things and conditions, but which are given from some outer source. They are primarily the wider or narrower limits within which the yearnings of Man may be given satisfaction. Hence here in the very first place the חקות התועבות אשר נעשו לפניכם, the principles of sexual excesses mentioned in v. 30, which worshipping the animal life of instinct had led men into the most bestial unnatural practices. In animals instinct itself is also bound by the power of the Creator’s Law of למינהו. But in Man this most powerful of all his instinctive urges is given to be also mastered and controlled by his moral free will, and to be elevated to a holy, morally free act of service to God. This very freedom itself, the essential condition for his moral superiority to be proved even in this sensuous sphere, and just in that sphere, obviously assume the possibility of lust going astray in licentiousness. The temptations to go astray in these matters are given him so that he should overcome them, and, just in such mastery, exercise his moral free will (see on Gen. 7,7). But not to master the animal-like urge but to consider it given animal-like to be satisfied, as the חקות of the Canaanite point of view regarding Man and the World taught, must in the ordinary course of nature, debase Man, far lower than the animals, in the whole mire of moral degeneration.

But, in a wider sense, חקתיהם, includes all customs, usages and practices which are even remotely connected with that un-Jewish point of view of Man and the World, or even, for quite unknown reasons could be connected with it, and which would make one who pays attention to them and practices them, as acknowledging such un-Jewish views. Thus we find in :ת״כ יכול לא יבנו בנינות ולא יטעו נטיעות כמותם ת״ל ובחקותיהם לא תלכו לא אמרתי אלא בחוקים החקוקים להם ולאבותיהם ולאבות אבותיהם, i.e. it does not mean that we may not build or plant in the same style as the other nations, but only that we must refrain from such established practices which have come down to them from ancient times. In Aboda Zora 11a, and in Sanhedrin 52,b, that which is forbidden under חוקת הגוים is taken to be the general idea of דרכי האמורי and according to תוספות there, there are two categories of חוקת הגוים. (a) such practices and customs which are connected with non-Jewish polytheistic or immoral purposes and ideas; copying these is unconditionally forbidden even if their origin was pure and Jewish. Hence the declaration that, for instance, the organ was originally a Jewish instrument and was to be understood by “מנים״ would in no wise make its introduction into Jewish Divine-Service plausible, as no one disputes the fact that this instrument has received the specific character of an adjunct to the religious services of a non-Jewish religion, (b) Non-Jewish customs and practices for which there are no recognisable reasonable and permissable reasons. In a narrower sense דרכי האמורי is taken to mean that which is forbidden as coming under the conception of ניחוש (see on Ch. 19,26).

Vv. 4 & 5. את משפטי וגו׳. My Law, and My Law only shall regulate your social and moral life. Whereas everywhere else, as a rule, חוקים and חוקות are mentioned before משפטים and the other classes of the laws, here where the holiest and most important of the חוקים are given, משפטים, are mentioned first! This is surely to tell us that the social order itself can not exist without this moral order, and that the laws of justice and rights which God wants to have respected and practiced as the basis of His human society presupposes people who have been conceived, born, brought up, and living under the regime of His moral sexual and family laws. In ת״כ we find משפטים explained as matters written in the Torah שאלו לא נכתבו בדין היה לכתבן, the laws concerning which, even according to general ideas would be recognized as necessary and pertinent. But חקים, as being such as יצר הרע משיב עליהם ואומות העולם משיבין עליהם, our materialistic nature and the non-Jewish would remonstrate against. At rock bottom they are both, the one as much as the other, the expression of the very highest wisdom of right and justice. It is only because the nature of, the justification for, and the purpose of the משפטים are readily grasped by everybody, they deal with the conditions of ordinary social life, whereas the matters and circumstances dealt with by the חוקים are such as are based on the combined inner, spiritual and bodily nature of Man, and the resulting conditions of his sensual life in relation to his spiritual moral calling, these are not clearly apparent to the human mind, and are only apparent to God, their Maker; that is why the reasons of the משפטים are more easily understood and recognisable and the חוקים are wrongly taken by superficial judgment of Jewish and non-Jewish thinkers to be without meaning or purpose. So that what the ת״כ says is deeply significant when it points out that first in v. 4. עשיה is demanded for משפטים, and שמירה for חקים, but then in v. 5, combined שמירה and עשיה for both חקים and משפטים. For, as has already repeatedly been remarked, our teachers take the first obligation for the demanded שמירה of the Torah to be “learning”, giving one’s time and energy to studying and obtaining a clear and comprehensive understanding of the theory of the Torah. For laws which only exist in books but do not appeal to the understanding have had the very first condition for the likelihood of their being kept taken away. Now a superficial judgment would consider study of the chapters dealing with the social laws as being less necessary, perhaps entirely unnecessary, they are, after all, one thinks, merely מצות שכליות which with a little thought, one would have worked out for oneself, but insistence on the עשיה on their being kept, must be impressed quite specially, as the danger to the community in general of their non-observance seems to be evident. On the other hand, the same superficial judgment would declare that study of the חוקים, if, indeed, these are to be considered at all, to be quite indispensable. For they are, as one calls them: שמעיות-laws which have been given by revelation and which are solely thus made, but would never have been obtained by Man’s thought or consideration. These one would like to satisfy theoretically by study and not put too great an insistence on their being actually kept, as the advantages they confer and the ill effects of their being neglected is by no means superficially apparent. Hence, the Torah does first of all say: את משפטי תעשו, for, to some extent one can carry out the Torah-conception of social Right even before one has studied the laws which God has revealed to us concerning these rights. A general conception of Right, of what man owes to his fellow-man is planted in the conscience of every uncorrupted human being, and this general consciousness of Right is also the Voice of God. But the laws of social Right, on which alone the whole human social happiness can truly flourish and blossom, the Rights of Man, as God sees them, require study from the revealed Word of God, no less than the חוקים. Far below God’s pure conception of Right do all the man-made laws and regulations of human governments lie. These mostly originate in utilitarian reasons and are often toned down, with, at the best, wise modifications to protect the interests of the community as a whole. But משפטי ה׳, God’s dictum on Rights, אמת, are the truth of matters and conditions, they flow from the inner nature, from the actual conception and the true purpose of things; hence צדקו יחדיו, they do not change, giving advantage to one at the cost of the other, in every case they are fair to everyone, ensure harmoniously a suitable position to everyone and demand that everybody does his share, all in accordance with his rights as a human being and with his condition in life. God’s Right is nothing else but the practical application of Truth. That is why, not only חוקים, but also ומשפטים בל ידעום, the Psalmist sings, of the nations in general in contrast to the People of God’s Torah. And hence, although the Word of God does, in the first place, demand שמירה for His חוקים, deep penetrating study, ואת חקתי תשמרו, for without their being revealed by God’s Word, Man’s limited brain would not have formed the very first idea of them, it immediately adds: שמירה .ללכת בהם, the study itself, must be undertaken for the purpose of carrying them out: לא המדרש עיקר אלא המעשה, not the study but the practical observance is the principle, or, as it puts it in תשמרו ללכת בהם לא המשנה נגוד אלא המעשה נגוד :ת״כ, it is not study which is to be the purpose in your mind (בגוד from נגד, that which you have before you, that which is placed as the goal of a direction), but active carrying it out, The value of “learning”, of Torah study, is only so great: גדול תלמוד, because it מביא לידי מעשה, because it leads to practice. More, true study, the right and true knowledge, is only acquired by such as, from beforehand, study with the intention to practice: ,שכל טוב לכל עושיהם ללומדיהם לא נאמר אלא לעושיהם, the understanding of what is good is only reached by such who do not only study the Divine Torah, but who practice it. Hence the Word of God finally combines them all together, and demands both שמירה and עשיה for both חוקים and משפטים, because only when one is clear about both of them, and both find their realisation in one’s social and one’s private life, is the lofty goal of a perfect human life achievable.

The ת״כ gives further significant laws for the study of the Word of God, ללכת בהם: עשם עיקר, ואל תעשם טפלה ללכת בהם: שלא יהא משאך ומתנך אלא בהם, שלא תערב בהם דברים אחרים בעולם, שלא תאמר למדתי חכמת ישראל אלמד חכמת אומות העולם ,ת״ל ללכת בהם, אינך רשאי ליפטר מתוכן, i.e. “ללכת בהם״, in them is the whole purpose of your life to be, they are to form the whole principle of your life, the absolute, not just accepted with conditions as being secondary; your whole spiritual acceptance and activity is to occupy itself solely with them so that you never introduce and mix alien matters with them, that you do not say: “now I have studied Jewish wisdom, I will go and study the wisdom of other nations”, that is why it says ללכת בהם, “thou mayest not depart from their sphere”. If we understnd these sentences of the ת״כ aright, then the sentence which stands at their head: עשם עיקר ואל תעשם טפלה, forewarns one not to take the following sentences to mean that one is completely to ignore and remain in ignorance of all knowledge and science which has been gained and nurtured by non-Jewish sources or which have no direct bearing on the knowledge to be gained by the study of the Torah. Inasmuch as what is commanded is: עשם עיקר ואל תעשם טפלה, the permission to occupy oneself also with other spheres of knowledge is assumed. Only, the knowledge of the Torah and the understanding we derive from it is to be our principle concern and to be regarded as having been given to us as the absolute and firmly established Truth. Only as accessory knowledge and in as far as they serve to truly help the study of the Torah and are subordinated as the טפל to the עיקר, are they to be studied. But the Torah and all its teachings must always remain that which we have received from Above and must be the yardstick by which we measure all the results obtained by other spheres of learning. Only that which is in accordance with the Truths of the Torah can remain true for us. All that we accept intellectually as well as all our actions must always be considered from the point of view of the Torah and be within the lines of the doctrines it teaches, so that we only accept and adopt that which is in accordance with them, and do not adulterate the knowledge we draw out of the Torah with ideas which have developed from other and strange premises. We are not to consider Torah-knowledge as being the same as other knowledge, so that the Torah is for us only another branch of all other knowledge; that we have a Jewish knowledge, have Jewish Truths, but that there are also, with equal importance and having equal authority, non-Jewish knowledge and non-Jewish truths; and after we imagine we have exhaustively absorbed the Jewish thoughts we turn with the same mind to get hold of the non-Jewish ones, and so, placing in our minds and feelings one teaching next to the other, one Truth next to the other, and lacking complete conviction of either, surely go to spiritual and moral ruin in discordant teachings and opinions. But as surely as the Torah comes from God, and all other knowledge and wisdom which have been found by Man only consist of the results of Man’s limited insight into the actual nature of things, so sure is it to us, that for us there is only one teaching, knowledge and truth by which all else must be measured, and all others have only conditional acceptance and can only have value in conformance with it. So that when we study and occupy ourselves with other spheres of knowledge we still never leave the basis and aims of the Torah, to which alone all our intellectual work is dedicated and from which אינך רשאי ליפטר מתוכן.—

אשר יעשה אותם האדם וחי בהם. It does not say: אשר תעשו אותם ותחיו בהם, but: אשר יעשה אותם האדם וחי בהם, and does not say אדם, but: האדם, i.e. everybody who strives to realise to himself and by himself the high human moral and spiritual character which is expressed by this appellation (see on Gen. 1,26). Hence in ת״כ the significant sentences:— מנין אפילו נכרי ועושה את התורה הרי הוא ככ״ג, ת״ל אשר יעשה אותם האדם וחי בהם, וכן הוא אומר וזאת תורת הכהנים והלוים וישראל לא נאמר כאן אלא וזאת תורת האדם ה׳ אלקים (שמואל ב׳ א׳ י״ט): וכן הוא אומר פתחו שערים, ויבאו כהנים לויים וישראלים לא נאמר, אלא ויבא גוי צדיק שומר אמונים (ישעי׳ כ״ו ב׳): וכן הוא אומר, זה השער לד׳, כהנים לויים וישראלים לא נאמר, אלא צדיקים יבאו בו (תהלים קי״ח כ׳) וכן הוא אומר רננו כהנים לויים וישראלים לא נאמר כאן, אלא רננו צדיקים בד׳ (תהלים ל״ג א׳): וכן הוא אומר הטיבה ד׳, לכהנים ללויים ולישראלים לא נאמר כאן, אלא הטיבה ה׳ לטובים (תהלים קכ״ה, ד׳): הא אפילו גוי ועושה את התורה הרי הוא ככהן גדול, i.e. even a non-Jew who keeps God’s Laws is equal of the High Priest for it says: “… which a man shall fulfil them and live”. Similarly it also says: “This is the teaching for man”, and does not say for Priests, Levites and Israelites. Equally so: “Open ye the gates, that priests, Levites and Israelites may enter” is not said, but “Righteous ones may enter”. Further, it does not say: “This is the gateway to God, Priests, Levites and Israelites shall enter therein”, but: “that a just righteous People”. And again “exult ye Priests, Levites and Israelites” is not said, but “exult ye righteous one in God”. And finally it does not say: “Deal well O God with Priests, Levites and Israelites”, but: “with those that are good”. From all these quotations from the Holy Writ, it follows that even a non-Jew who fulfills the Law of God, is equal to the High Priest. Life, the Teaching, the Proximity to God, Happiness and Well-being is not opened solely for Israel with these Torah laws but for everyone, everyone who draws their outlook on life and men out of them, and bases the principles of his life on them, and who elevates himself to the heights of pure humanity by keeping their חוקים and משפטים. Anybody and everybody is thereby ensured the attainment of the highest degree of perfection and happiness possible for a human being to reach in nearness to God.

But this establishes the fact, that for a correct estimation of these חוקים and משפטים which regulate the whole of Jewish individual private as well as social public life they are nothing exceptional, nothing calculated for supermen or out of the ordinary. They are just meant, starting with the Jewish family of mankind to ensure that the stage of human life shall be regained which was the original purpose, and which still remains the purpose of a race of beings — humanity — created in the likeness of God, and to guide the whole of the human race up to such a level which is the meaning of God’s direction of the whole of world history. That is why the whole summary of all the happiness which is to blossom and mature from these חוקים and משפטים is crystalised in these two words: וחי בהם. Nothing more and nothing less is to be won from their observance than וחי, that the highest conception of having positively and truly lived!

Of the “life” to be gained by carrying out the מצות the רמב״ן speaks poignantly as follows:— “The life to be gained by anyone, by carrying out the מצות, is exactly in accordance with his attitude to them. He who keeps the מצות, not disinterestedly, but because he reckons to reap reward for it in this world will indeed receive long life, riches and honour, and of such a one it says in Prov. 3,6: “in its left hand are riches and honour”, i.e. it, the תורה, grants those who deal with it left handedly (that is exactly: not with the right attiude) riches and honour. Equally so, those that keep the מצות to get life in the next world, but serve God out of fear of what otherwise might happen, also achieve their purpose, remain free from the punishments which await the guilty, and their souls will rest happy in peace in the next world. Those who keep the מצות in their life down here in purely loving devotion as the תורה pictures in בחקתי, “the threshing-time will last till the time of the wine harvest etc. “they will have here below a happy earthly life and complete bliss awaits them in the hereafter”. But those who already here below give up all claim to everything material as if they were creatures without any earthly desires, so that all their wishes and all their thoughts centre solely on their Creator, as we have an example in Elijah, inasmuch as their souls are attached completely to God, they become bodily and spiritually immortal as is clear from the Scriptural account of Elijah and as is known from tradition. That is also why Scripture, to describe the reward for the מצות uses terms like: למען יאריכון ימיך, למען תחיה והארכת ימים, for those expressions include all the various degrees of the conception of living, in accordance with the deserts of each particular case

For the דין, the traditional law that: אין דבר עומד בפני פקוח נפש is also tacked on to our sentence: וחי בהם, that, where there is any question of saving life, transgression of the Law is not only permitted but commanded: וחי בהם ולא שימות בתם (Yoma 85,b), as has already been noted in connection with Sabbath on Ex. 31,17. For the וחי בהם does express the ennobling and the happiness of earthly life as being the immediate purpose of God’s Laws, so that it is quite understandable that, for the possibility of saving a life still rich in the possibilities of fulfilment of duty, a momentary lapse of the law must stand back. Nevertheless, this canon does not hold good regarding idolatory, sexual immorality or murder. Laws regarding: ע״ז, ג״ע וש״ד may in no case be broken even for the purpose of saving life (see Deut 6,5 & XXII,26). With reference to these, the high points of our duty towards God, towards our own purity, and towards our fellow men, it is said, in every case: יהרג ואל יעבר (Sanhedrin 74a). In addition there is the case where, out of enmity to God’s Torah we are given the alternative of publicly transgressing the Torah or forfeiting our life. There the duty of קידוש השם and the prohibition of חילול השם demands that we cheerfully sacrifice our life rather than yield to the attempt to force us to transgress even the smallest of the commandments (see on Ch. 22,32).

V. 6. שאר (see on Gen. 19,1). לא תקרבו: Although the whole chapter is taken from the standpoint of the man, the prohibition is directed equally to both sexes, and both are punishable in exactly the same degree לגלות עדוה — .(ת״כ): any sexual act which is forbidden by the Creator as not being a moral sanctified God-serving act is simply naked beastiality. Hence the general term for all forbidden sexual acts is גלוי עריות (cf. remarks in Gen. on Ch. 11,25; III,7 & 21). Immediately when God led the first woman to the first man for their union to be a matter for the exercise of their own moral free will, in contrast to the blind physical urge of animal life, and He erected the pillars of the whole development of the human race, in His proclamation of the purpose of Woman to be עזר כנגדו and in His first proclamation for moral human marriage:— על כן יעזב וגו׳ (see notes thereon), He indicated that it was not within the narrow circle of blood relationship that the human male is to seek his mate if the morrally high purpose of human marriage is to be reached. This is His למינהו-Law for the human race, which in the sphere of plant and animal sexes is carried out immutably by the almighty power of His Word at their creation, but which His one creature with moral free will, His Adam, His Man, is to accept from His Mouth to carry it out with his moral free will. The antediluvian world went to its ruin morally and socially, from the time when, at their choice of mates, men did not obey God’s Will but only listened to their own caprice, and with: ויקחו להם נשים מכל אשר בחרו (Gen. 6,2), the dying out of the spirit of God, and the grave of the human race was started.

To obtain a “priestly nation and a holy people” in the midst of, and for the salvation of, Mankind which had gone astray, the Father of Mankind drew the borders for the choice of mates still narrower for this people, and then, for the priests of this priestly nation we find them drawn yet narrower still in Ch. XXIX. To obtain nobler and higher species of plants and animals, human gardeners and breeders do not leave the planting of the seeds for the production of the desired objects just to chance, and do not allow any and every kind of seed to mix, or to be planted in any and every condition or time.— To obtain the noblest blossom out of material matter, to obtain earthly creatures in the likeness of God, to obtain Man, can it be superfluous to listen to, and to obey the directions of the Father and Teacher of human generation?

The reasons for His Laws on the choice of mates surely lies deep in the very source of human nature, unfathomable to Man himself, and are certainly only clear and apparent to the One Who can see the result already when it is just beginning to form, and Who has woven, and weaves, that most mysterious combination, the union of heavenly spirit and earthly body. Not of these motives, but of the possible physiological results of transgressing these laws, we have dared on Gen. 2,25 to make some speculative suggestions. Here, at the laws governing Jewish permitted choice of mates, where the idea of relationship prohibiting sexual union goes still farther, where it even extends in part even beyond the idea of blood relationship, and makes degrees of forbidden relationship start even before marriage, even when only קידושין have taken place, so that, from the moment when a man and woman are bethrothed to each other by קידושין, their relations on either side are אסור to one another, here quite apart from physiological effects, surely it is moral social factors of marriage and family which must enter into consideration. May we, in this direction too, dare to make a few conjectural suggestions.

Amongst the factors that raise into the sphere of holy and sanctifying Mitzvahs what otherwise would belong, as ערוה, to crude animal life, surely must be reckoned as not the least, the fact that the bodily union of the sexes at once lays the foundation for the purest, most intimate, strongest spiritual union of the minds and hearts of two beings. It lays the foundation for that blossoming which our marriage-blessing celebrates as: אהבה, אהוה, שלום ורעות, and which forms that sublime conjugal love, which the Song of Conjugal Love and Love of God praises as “stronger than death and which all the stormy floods of fate can not quench”. In short, the ודבק באשתו loses all ערוה-sensuality and becomes invested with the highest moral dedication, if it does really effect that wonder of wonders, that והיו בשר אחד on which all true family happiness and national happiness builds itself up.

Hence the less there is in existence before marriage any bond of attachment of family love, the more that the strongest form of attachment starts with marriage, the more does the sexual side of marriage become a basic factor in the whole moral sphere of happy married life full of love in every phase. It starts and is brought about by it and elevates it to the realm of pure morality.

But where there is already the affection of parents, brothers and sisters, and relatives, in the ordinary course of nature, attaching hearts and feelings to one another — and the purer and more truly the family life of the priestlike People of God exercises its moral influence, the stronger and farther reaching will the pull of this family love be — marriage will only have to bring some weak addition to this love. Love will have been there before, and marriage will add almost nothing more than the sexual element, which by itself alone without bringing about the miracle of the loving union of two beings, sinks down to naked ערוה.

And again, parental, brother and sister love, family love, altogether the mission and influence of parents, brothers and sisters, children and relatives, form, by themselves, apart from conjugal love and the conjugal mission, such important independent factors on the pure and mutual working and effect of the family life which God’s Torah aims at producing, that it can not approve or tolerate the misplacing of any one of these factors. A mother can not become a wife without ceasing to be a mother, a sister can not be a wife without ceasing to be a sister, an aunt can not become a wife without giving up being an aunt etc. etc. But mothers, sisters, aunts, etc. are to remain as such. But a sexual union with them which does not allow them to become wives would become nothing more than mere ערוה and God’s Torah says: אחותך היא לא תגלה ערותה! ,אמך היא לא תגלה ערותה!. We are indeed far from believing that with these suggestions we have even touched the real motive of these laws, let alone to have found it. But we believe that we may indicate, how, even with our limited insight, and in that moral social sphere that is accessible to that insight, we can see certain recognizable results of deep importance attached to the fulfilment or non-fulfilment of these laws.

All the marriages which are forbidden in this chapter are forbidden to the degree that אין קדושין תופסין בם, that a marriage between them is altogether impossible. Any קידושין which may have taken place are null and void, and have no legal standing at all. So that they come quite specially under the conception ערוה. The sexual intercourse is just nothing but ערוה. Only in the case of אשה נדה (v. 19), are קידושין תופסין, for in that case קריבה is only forbidden during a transitory period (Yebamoth 49a & b; Kiddushin 67 & 68).
לא תקרבו לגלות ערוה: every approach which might lead to גלוי עריות is to be avoided.
V. 8. ערות אביך היא: Through your father she is ערוה to you. Similarly in v. 14: ערות אחי אביך.
V. 9. מולדת בית או מולדת חוץ: as ומולדתך אשר הולדת, (Gen. 48,6). It is a noun means “one who is begotten, one who is born” or rather “birth”, like מודעתנו בועז :מודעת (Ruth 3,2), our acquaintance.
בין שאומרין לו לאביך קיים בין שאומרין לו לאביך הוצא: מולדת בית וגו׳ (Yebamoth 23a), either if the mother belongs to the house of the father, or if she does not do so, i.e. married or unmarried.
V. 10. עדותך הנה: they are ערוה to you through you yourself. By that which you are to them, they cannot be sexually to you otherwise than ערוה.

V. 17. זמם :זמה היא, see Gen. 11,6. The word in the form זמָה occurs some twenty time in תנ״ך, but only in one instance is it used in a good sense (Job 17,12). In all the other cases it refers to something immoral, and predominantly to sexual immorality. Now as זמם indicates having one’s mind on something, זמה would have the same idea as sensuality where the idea of “senses” is limited to the lower senses, and means addiction to the excitement of the lower senses.

V. 18. צרר :לצרר designates the closest joining, a tight holding together, and binding (— and that is why in an inimical sense it means compressing, confining, oppressing—), as in: צרור כספו (Gen. 42,35); צרור מים בעביו (Job. 26,8); נפש אדוני צרורה בצרור החיים (Sam. I 25,29). Hence it also designates the most intimate joint union of two women in the material bonds of one man, and each wife is called, in her relation to the other, צרה. Now here it says: you are not to marry two sisters at the same time so that they are bound together in one and the same conjugal tie. So that if you have married one of them, during her lifetime, the other may not become your wife. Any sexual intercourse with her is, accordingly, nothing else but ערוה. Only after the death of the first is marriage with the second permitted. אחות אשה is the sole case in which the איסור ceases לאחר מיתה. All others: אשת אחיך ,אשת אחי האב ,אשת האב, (except in the case of יבום, Deut. 25,5), אשה ובתה, remain, after the death of the father, the uncle, the brother, etc. unaltered and prohibited. It is only אחות אשה where the איסור is limited in time בחייה. In that case, too, גירושין, divorce, makes no alteration to the prohibition.

As here the relation to each other of two wives of the same husband is expressed by the strongest term of belonging together, צרור, the Gemora uses that for the Halacha that, if, in the case of יבום (see Deut. 25,5) the deceased brother had left two wives, one of whom is forbidden to the living brother, the יבם, as ערוה — she was, e.g. אחות אשתו or בתו etc. — then the מצות יבום of the dead brother’s house does not apply at all. If he can not marry one of the wives on account of ערוה then he is not to marry the other, she remains, like her צרה, forbidden to him as אשת אחיו and both of them (provided there is no other brother), are free to marry anybody else without יבום or חליצה. If she, the צרת ערוה becomes the wife of another brother through יבום and this one also dies childless, and leaves another wife also, then the same condition applies again in relation to the first one who is still living, to whom she was once already אסורה as צרח ערוה. As he could not marry her as אשת אח הראשון, so is this present co-wife אסורה to him and again the מצות יבום וחליצה does not apply etc. Hence the dictum in Yebamoth 2a: חמש עשרה נשים פוטרות צרותיהן וצרות צרותיהן מן החליצה ומן היבום עד סוף העולם. When we consider the fact that if the childless deceased brother had left several wives, יבום may only be carried out with one of them, and nevertheless, according to the Halacha laid down in accordance with the expression לצרור, if one of them is an ערוה to the remaining brother, יבום may not be carried out with any one of them, then in this expression and in this Halacha, we see the most intimate relationship and unity of these co-wives affirmed. במקום מצות יבום, where the conception of a house as a “home” is so very much in the foreground, if there are two of more wives, the house, “the home”, is represented not by one of them, but by them all together as one united unit, so that where one of them stands in the way of the מצות יבום being able to be kept, then for the whole home this מצוה altogether falls away and not only is she פטורה מיבום, but she also פוטרת צרותיה etc.

V. 19. Just as with שאר בשר permanently, so here temporarily, during the duration of the condition and its ensuing טומאה results, any sexual approach is pure ערוה. Apart from deep physiological reasons, which surely prevail here too, no law more than this, raises sexual intercourse out of the sphere of lower sensuality into the realm of morally pure, sanctified humanity. טומאתה: as long as the condition and its טומאה-results exclude from entrance to the מקדש or contact with its קדשיו, for so long is קריבה a קריבה לגלות ערוה. Only after שבעת ימים וטבילה (Ch. 15,19), resp. שבעת ימים נקיים וטבילה (ibid v. 28), only then, ואחר תטהר, does a woman become fit again for both, at the same time.

V. 20. לזרע, by the addition of this word — cf. the immediately following: להיות לך לאלקים ולזרעך אחריך ;ומזרעך וגו׳ (Gen. 17,7); כי ביצחק יקרא לך זרע (Gen. 21,12); ומה האחד מבקש זרע אלקים (Malachi 2,15); and in many similar places — may be indicated the high purpose, furthering the moral upbuilding of Mankind, which is placed in the sexual side of marriage which sanctifies it through and through, and which forms the essential fundamental condition for the inviolable sanctity of marriage. תת שכבתו אל אשת עמיתו is the worst and gravest breaking through the moral fundamentals of Mankind, that is why the immediate result thereof is called: לטמאה בה, by that sin the whole being of a human being is demoralized.

V. 21. ומזרעך לא תתן. From Sanhedrin 64a, it is clear that מולך לאו ע״ז היא, that מולך does not come under the general conception of ע״ז. Further that two factors, נתינה and העברה, are essential to it. נתינה is the מסירה למולך, the handing over of the child to the priests of Moloch. העברה is the passing of the child through fire, and according to the way the רמב״ם takes it, the father receives the child back from the hands of the priests, and he the father, passes it through fire. Just how the procedure of this “passing through” is, is not quite clear. In any case it is no burning, and so is quite different from what is usually taken to be the “ritual of Moloch”. The Halacha further stresses the word “מזרעך״ and takes it to mean: ולא כל זרעך, and so one is only חייב, if one gives a part of one’s children to Moloch and passes them through fire, but not if one were to do this to all one’s children. Were he to do so, העביר כל זרעו, he would be פטור. Further the prohibition is not limited to father and child, but grand-father and grandchild, any descendant is meant here; it does not say: מבניך ומבנותיך, but: מזרעך (ibid).

If we consider all these laws and note at the same time that — as never elsewhere concerning מסירה והעברה למולך — ע״ז is designated as a חילול השם, it says: ולא תחלל את שם אלקיך אני ה׳, that, in Ch. 20,3, it is declared as: טמא את מקדשי וחלל את שם קדשי, that, there, the Nation as such, the עם הארץ, the State, is specially made responsible for the punishment of this abuse; that — as is the case in no other crime or criminal — it is assumed that the nation could close an eye to the commission of this crime, ואם העלם יעלימו etc., and then the whole weight of God’s punishment is proclaimed right down to the destruction of the man himself, his family and all those who are inclined towards him and his serving of Moloch, ושמתי אני את פני באיש ההוא ובמשפחתו והכרתי אתו ואת כל הזונים אחריו לזנות אחרי המולך מקרב עמם, of necessity we come to the conclusion that here we have to deal with not just merely a defection from God to idolatry, but with such a criminal aberration which brings idolatrous ideas into the very sphere of worshipping God, and thereby it does just מחלל ה׳ and is מטמא מקדשו. One who is עובד עבודה זרה leaves God and His Sanctuary and turns to others. The עורד למולך thinks that, with this procedure he still remains within the sphere of God and His Sanctuary, and just thereby becomes provocative and corruptive to the pure conception of God and His Sanctuary in the nation.

If we ask for the meaning of the word מֹלֶך, the form tells us that it does not convey the idea of a person as מֶלֶך, but is an abstract conception, like קֹדֶשׁ; holiness, גֹדֶל, greatness, so it does not designate the king, the ruler, but reigning, ruling, governing. We think we find in it the conception of a highest power which governs the world, we think we find in it the heathen idea of irrevocable fate, luck, which “rules” the world, on which even the gods have no power to change, to whose decisions they themselves cannot but submit. This would then offer an explanation to the otherwise striking fact of מקצת זרעו and כל זרעו. Fate is something that disturbes the ordinary happy smooth course of life, is a power that is inimical to, jealous of it. By giving up a part of it of one’s free will one propriates this power and renders it favourably inclined towards leaving the remainder undisturbed. So one gives over one part of one’s children to this “ruling fate, by passing it between the flames and abandoning it to the blind haphazard “chance” of destruction or protection, so as to be able to keep the rest safe to oneself.

How much this Moloch illusion of the way the powers of chance or luck can insinuate itself even within the sphere of supposed consciousness of, and honouring of, God and His Power, is evidenced by instances of such belief amongst ourselves even in these days. But such belief either removes the one sole world-directing power from God freely governing the world in Love and Righteousness, or reduces Him Himself to the heathen conception of the passionate, jealous, blind power of the gods. But the one as much as the other is against the pure Jewish conception of God, and the pure Jewish conviction that it not by destructive acts, but solely by living on a high moral level, and by acting in free-willed obedience to God, that we can ensure His Favour towards us and our children; and we can understand the sentence: ומזרעך לא תתן להעביר למלך ולא תחלל את שם אלקיך אני ה׳, (see further notes on Ch. 20,1—6).

The position which this ומזרעך לא תתן וגו׳, is given amongst the list of sexual laws is certainly not less significant. The list of sins which immediately precede it deals with sexual sins, in which children; זרע, human seed, can come into existence and, as we thought we could believe, the last of that list, in the word לזרע indicated that high moral purpose of human sexual life. On that follows then the Moloch-prohibition with the underlying thought:— Just as your children are not to be the product of blind physical urge, just as they are to be begotten morally, so, in their life you are not to let them belong to a blind physical force casting their fate for them. Just as they have been acquired under the protection and guidance of God’s Torah, so are they to belong, in all the purposes of their lives, and in all the good fortune of their lives, to this protection and direction of God, which aims at the moral development of the happiness of Man. ״אני ה׳״ says God, regarding your children. It is to Me, the God of Compassion and Benevolence, Who consummates the future of Mankind in moral fulfilment of Life, to Me do your children belong, educate them, each one of them, to Me, leave each one of them to Me, train each one of them in My ways, and leave it to Me to lead each one of them in its own way, happily to the goal of life — לא תתן מזרעך להעביר למלך ולא תחלל את שם אלהיך אני ה׳!

V. 23. תבל היא. In the same way as the noun תבלית, (ואפילו על תבליתם, Is. 10,25), is formed from בלה, so, we think, is תבל a noun form of the root בלה. But בלה means the gradual accomplishment of the non-existence of the hitherto existing. Hence used in reference to mechanical or physical processes, the wearing away of substance through use or age. Hence, then, used in moral or spiritual sense, תבלית and תבל:— the ultimate non-existence of the whole morality of the being brought about by progresive debauchery. So, too, in Ezek. 23,43 in a description of the תועבות of the Kingdoms of Israel and Judah, beginning in v. 37 with כי נאפו, we find: ואומר לבלה נאפים, i.e. then said I: it is to such complete degeneration that adulterous excesses lead! Hence here we have translated תבל by “complete brutalisation”.

V. 24—28. נטמאו הגוים וגו׳ ותטמא הארץ וגו׳. So also in Ch. 19,29: אל תחלל את בתך להזנותה ולא תזנה הארץ. Similarly with reference to murder, Numb. 35,33: ולא תחניפו את הארץ וגו׳ כי הדם הוא יהניף הארץ ,ולא תטמא את הארץ אשר אתם יושבים בה וגו׳. And in Deut. 24,4, referring to מחזיר גרושתו משנשאית, we find: ולא תחטיא את הארץ אשר ה׳ אלקיך נותן לך נחלה. In all these places it speaks of a corrupting influence which sins of murder and immorality exercise on the land and on the relationship of the land to its inhabitants, which in the case of sexual excesses can mount to the height that, as the expression runs, the land “spews out” its inhabitants. The טומאה of its inhabitants makes the land also טמא, their זנות makes it also to a זונה, in the חטא and עון of the inhabitants the land too is drawn in, it becomes חנפה, a “pretender”, does not carry out that which its purpose promised. This too, is what is taught by the earth being called אדמה as being, by its relationship to Man, the basis of human development. Just as in the days of creation, the first drop of rain waited for the arrival of the first man, so altogether there, the first pages of the history of man and the world show us the blessing of the world’s blossoming being dependant on the morality of Man.
