The world in as far as it is אדמה was cursed as a result of the sin of אדם; the אדמה which had drank of the brother’s blood from the hand of the brother’s murderer denies him the further use of its strength; and the debauchery, the השחתת דרך of the generation of man dragged everything living down into this השחתת דרך and to destruction with that degenerate generation of man. And God’s judgment of the Nations of the world is proclaimed through the mouth of Isaiah (Ch. 24,4 & 5), in these words:— “The earth mourneth and fadeth away, because the human world languisheth and fadeth away, because, above all, the higher ranks of society do languish. The earth hath become a “pretender” (חנפה) under the inhabitants thereof because that which is still theoretically taught (תורת) is transgressed in practice, because they have transposed the Law of Morality into its reverse (חק הפרו) and broken the covenant of eternity”. But just for the same reason does “Heaven rejoice and the earth be glad, doth the sea rejoice and the fulness thereof, are the fields joyful and the contents thereof, doth every tree of the forest rejoice before the Presence of God, when He cometh, when He cometh to judge the earth, when He bringeth to the human world the basis of Right and to the peoples Faithfulness unto Him”: Ps 96,11—13, and elsewhere in so many places in the Prophets and Psalms.

But God had made this position which the earth as a whole takes, in relation to the behaviour of mankind in general, much closer and much more intimate in the inter-relationship of that land and that nation which He chose to be His instruments for the moral rebirth of humanity in the development of nations. Just as the nation is “the People of God” so is the land “the land of God”; He calls it ארצי and נחלתי (Jer. 2,6 and in many other places). In the future, the whole of humanity and the whole of the earth is going to be exclusively His, is going to carry out exclusively His Will, and for this purpose of educating the generations of Man up to God, the foundation stone was laid with the establishment of this People and this Land.

From the time that Abraham was chosen, and the land was chosen for him, the land does not tamely endure any degeneration of its inhabitants, the flourishing of the land is attached to the moral flourishing of the people it engenders whom it feeds with its products, and enriches with its treasures. All that stirs in the womb of the earth of this land, all that its soil produces, that moves about its fields and meadows, that absorbs dew and rain under its heaven, that the rays of its sun animates and matures, all belong to God’s Laws for Man; it is for the fulfilment of God’s Will by morally pure Man that every seed pushes its way through, every blossom blooms, every fruit ripens, that the sun’s rays shine and that the dew waters. It is as bearer of a free-willed morally perfect national life, in such morally free human perfection that the whole physical life of this Land is to find its own perfection; and the purpose of its existence is killed when the human society living on it undermines the purpose of its existence by social and moral degeneration. Hence on this soil, no socially and morally degenerate population has any future. For it is the forces of God’s Land, forces and means which are holy to God, forces produced by God’s soil, transposed to human nerves and muscles which achieve sacrilege to the Laws of God, and which are wasted and misused in every act of transgression and excess. In their טומאה it itself becomes טמא, their sin becomes its sin. As long as sins and excesses remain confined to individuals, but God’s Law of Morality finds supporters and avenging defenders in the main body of the nation, the sinful degenerate members become purged out of the midst of the nation by God’s or Man’s courts of justice, and the nation, acknowledging the Law of God, can continue to find the land the source of blessing for its development. But if sins and excesses become general, if just by this general practice of wrong-doing it becomes looked on as excusable, even as being the national custom, approved and right, then the opposition to God’s Laws of Morality into which the community has fallen becomes at the same time opposition to the Divine Law of Morality of the Holy Land, and, even as the body vomits forth anything which is irreconcilable to it, so does the Land then eject its inhabitants.
ושמרתם אתם וגו׳, is, in connection with the ולא תקיא וגו׳ of v. 28, the admonition, primarily to the community to watch over the carrying out of this Law.

V. 29. כי כל אשר יעשה וגו׳, at the same time places every single individual regarding the purity of his sexual morality under the judging Eye of God. Some of the sexual sins prohibited here are חייבי מיתות בית דין (see Ch. XX). But here they are all threatened with the punishment of God, by כרת. This comes in where such sins escape human justice and it affects הנפשות העושות in all cases both the sexes to an equal degree (ת״כ). As, referring to כרת, here all the עריות are classed together, הוקשו זה לזה, anything specially mentioned in any one case applies to all of them, by virtue of this placing them all together (היקש). So, for example, regarding the nullity of קידושין in one case of ערות (Kiddushin 67b): הוקשו כל העריות כולם לאחות אשה מה אחות אשה לא תפסי בה קידושין אף כל עריות כולם לא תפסי בם קידושין.

V. 30. משמרתי .ושמרתם את משמרתי לבלתי עשות וגו׳ is God’s guard over the Law which He has transferred to us. The Law, the Torah, is a treasure which is entrusted to us, and each one of us is its שומר, its appointed guardian, and we have, in the very first place, to guard it against ourselves, have to guard it against injury from our own intentional or unintentional transgressions. Now it does not say: ושמרתם את משמרתי ולא תעשו וגו׳, but: ושמרתם את משמרתי לבלתי עשות וגו׳. Clearly this means: Guard the care of the Torah which has been transferred to you from Me, so that you do not come to transgress the Torah. But that means nothing else but: “Do not only forbear from transgressing, but also forbear from everything that could lead you to a transgression of the Law”. Or, as it puts it in Jebamoth 21a, & Moed Katon 5a: עשו משמרת למשמרתי, the guard of the Torah is itself to be an object of your guard, i.e. keep afar from everything which could lead to an infringement of your duty of guarding the Law. But that drives home to our hearts conscientiously to avoid not only that which is forbidden by the Torah, but also everything which, by similarity or other connection with that which is forbidden, could easily lead us to it. This is the idea of Jewish conscientiousness which is understood under the names of גדר and סייג, “making a fence round the Law”, and is expressed by the formula: הרחק מן הכיעור ומן הדומה לו, or as it puts it in Sabbath 13a: לך לך אמרי נזירא סחור סחור לכרמא לא תקרב, “to whom, like the Nazir, wine is forbidden, we say, make a detour and avoid going near a vineyard”. When, then, the deep insight into human nature and into the practical carrying out of the mitzvahs caused our sages to make general rules, גזרות of such protective, preventive nature, they were only making such laws which every far-seeing, conscientious Jew who has the carrying out of God’s Torah at heart would really have had to make for himself as a general habit for controlling his actions, (cf. Ex. 23,13 & Levit. 19,2). Especially in reference to the עריות-laws given here, laws of this protective nature have been laid down, known as שניות. These are such degrees of relationship which, on account of their similarity to, and easily to be confused with, those relations who are prohibited by the Torah, are forbidden מדרבנן (see Yebamoth 21).

מחקות התועבות, sexual excesses amongst the Canaanite population had not only ceased to be considered as תועבות, but by general custom and the practices of the religious cults had received general sanction and had even become חלפו חוק :חוקות, as Isaiah describes the age of a similar general degeneration (Ch. 24,5), “they have changed the Law over to the very contrary”, i.e. they have raised immorality into a law.

V. 1. קדושים :אחרי-מות ,מצורע תזריע ,שמיני, צו ,ויקרא! To achieve the purpose of the moral ideals of the Word of God, reposing under the wings of cherubim, which were symbolically represented by the משכן and by the קרבנות of the chapters of ויקרא and צו, and to bring them to practical reality in actual life, people have to be conceived and ripened, born, fed, and brought up under the regime of the laws of טומאה וטהרה of מאכלות אסורות and עריות as laid down in the chapters from שמיני to אחרי-מות, before it can be said to them: קדושים תהיו כי קדוש אני ה׳ אלקיכם, “Be ye holy, for I, your God, am holy!” In direct connection with the preceding chapter on עריות there follows here in short aphorisms, the outlines of a holy Jewish life. They are the fundamental principles for everyday Jewish life blossoming under the משפטים, God’s behests for social life, which had been referred to right at the introductory words of the עריות-laws in connection with the חוקות, and which will again and again be referred to (Ch. 18,4 5 & 26; XIX,37; & XX,22), obviously to say, that only in a people whose whole existence is rooted in the soil of these חוקות, can that justice, that unselfishness, that love of one’s fellowman, which God demands, and on which alone Man’s true happiness is founded, be expected to be realised. For not only does the concluding sentence of this משפטים-chapter — ושמרתם וגו׳, v. 37 — compared with v. 26 of the preceding chapter and v. 22 of the following one, show the close connection of these chapters, but this chapter actually appears to be an interpolation in the עריות-laws. For quite clearly chapter XX is the direct continuation of chapter XVIII. If, in addition, we consider the fact that the greater part of the laws contained in this Ch. XIX have already been given elsewhere, we certainly seem to be justified in taking the view that just as in the previous chapter the negative contrast to the חוקות התועבות of a Canaanite is depicted, so here it wants to show the positive contrast of a social life such as can only be built up on the foundation of a godly morally pure sexual life. That too, is why this chapter begins with כבוד אב ואם that corner-stone of all human social good behaviour, and puts אם, the Mother, first. For it is only where the man has attached himself to the right woman in a marriage which is sanctioned by God that the children find the right אם, “Mother”, — the very first “condition” (אם I.L.) for all spiritual moral humanity, — and only there, is begotten the Jewish relationship of children to their parents, the soul of that family life in which the children flourish and blossom up to God, and all the seeds of social virtues find effective care and attention from the cradle upwards, That is also why those demands of social behaviour which are introduced as new, characteristically in this משפטים-chapter are, as we shall see, primarily virtues of character which induce uprightness, sincerity conscientiousness, brotherliness and the spirit of forgiveness, those traits of character which are the protecting genii of a happy and neighbourly social life. No institution of the power of the state can really achieve them, and crimes against them are beyond the reach of any human court of justice, mastery of them is purely dependent on the character of the persons concerned. But if there is anything in which the observance or non-observance of the עריות-laws shows its importance it is the blissful or baneful influence which the one or the other respectively effects on the future of the human seed in the predisposition of its character.

V. 2. דבר אל כל עדת בני ישראל. Only at the giving of the very first Law which Israel received, the command for the Pessach offering, (Ex. 12,3), do we find the order couched in similar terms, to announce the Law to the whole community of the Children of Israel. Apart from these, this is not to be found at any other paragraph of the Torah. But indeed, just this admonition, קדושים תהיו, the admonition to the highest degree of moral human perfection, can, in such significant manner, well be addressed expressly to each and every individual of the nation. No position in life, no sex, no age, no degree of fortune, is excluded from this call to the very height of absolute morality, and to no one in particular is this call specially addressed, קדושים, “holy”, are we all to be.

קדושה, the very height of being absolutely ready for all that is good, presupposes the whole being in such a state of being penetrated by morality, that its opposite, the inclination to evil, finds no longer any place therein. The saying of the sages in ת״כ which explains the demand קדושים תהיו as פרושים תהיו stresses just this negative idea of the conception קדושה. At the same time it indicates the nature of the work that every one of us who would strive for the lofty goal of קדושה which is held out to him, must do on himself. קדושה is the product of the completest mastery by the god-like free-willed human being over all his forces and natural tendencies, with the allurements and inclinations associated with them, and placing them at the disposal of God’s Will. This mastery over one’s self, the highest possible art which human beings can practice does not consist of neglecting, curtailing, killing, or doing away with any of one’s powers or natural tendencies. No single one of the powers and natural tendencies which are given to Man is either good or bad in itself, from the most spiritual down to the most sensuous. They are all given to him for beneficial purposes to accomplish God’s Will on earth. The Divine Torah gives them a positive aim and a negative limit. In the service of this purpose indicated by God, and withtin these limits, set by God, everything is good and holy, Separated from these purposes and outside these limits, coarseness and evil begin. Virtuosity in this, the highest human art, is only attained, as in any other art, by practice, by constant exercise in using one’s moral free will in mastering existing tendencies. But these exercises are not to be practiced in the realm of the forbidden where a slip would result in wrong doing, but it is in the realm of the permitted that the resolution of one’s will is to test and strengthen itself. In exercising one’s power of restraint and self-control in things which are permitted but are related to the forbidden, is one to gain mastery of one’s inclinations, and so make all one’s powers and tendencies subservient to the pure fulfilment of the Will of God. That is the work that everybody is called on to do, each one according to his own individual peculiarities, work that is done quietly, silently, known to no one but himself, on his own inner self, the task which the sages call: פרישות, abstinence, and for which the Gemora in Yebamoth 20a, gives the formula: קדש עצמך במותר לך, “achieve the holiness of yourself in the realm of that which is permitted to you”, פרישות is not yet קדושה, but it is a preliminary stage towards it, as Rabbi Pinchus ben Yoir teaches in his “ladder of stages” leading to moral perfection (Aboda Zara 20b).

”כי״ קדוש אני ה׳ אלקיכם, the source of the possibility that you can be holy and the reason why you should be holy, lies in the fact that קדוש אני ה׳ אלקיכם, that I, Who am ה׳ אלקיכם, am קדוש. The קדושה, the holiness to which you are to strive with all the force of your moral free will is, in its true absolute purity, an attribute of Me Myself, and as ה׳ have I given you with My Breath, participation in this freedom, and continue giving you constantly strength and assistance for everything which is good. In קדוש אני ה׳ lies the source of your ability for קדושה. And קדוש אני ה׳ אלקיכם and the same Who gives you this ability for קדושה, He is the same Who is אלקיכם, Who is the One Who directs your fate and Who wishes to be the Guide of your deeds, Who makes it your duty to become קדוש and Who makes your fate dependent on your carrying out this duty. In קדוש אני אלקיכם lies the reason for your duty of קדושה. As it says in ת״כ:— קדושים תהיו וגו׳ לומר אם אתם מקדשים עצמיכם מעלה אני עליכם כאלו קדשתם אותי, i.e. inasmuch as I am your God, inasmuch as you call Me your God, and I call you My People, the holiness of My Name in the world is dependent on your manners, morals, and way of life. By your holiness you proclaim My Holiness to the world. אבא שאול אומר פמליא למלך ומה עליה להיות מֵחֻקָה למלך, the surrounding of a King have to be stamped with the manners of the King, i.e. you, Israel, your being near to God, makes it incumbent on you, not only to have nothing in you which is absolutely contrary to the holiness which is in Him, but to show in your characters the imprint of His Holiness, (מחקה as מחקה על הקיר, Ezek. 8,10).

The verses in this chapter are quite clearly divided into groups by the concluding words: אני ה׳ אלקיכם, in verses 2, 3, 4, 10, 25, 31, 34 & 36 of which the groups 11—25 & 26—31 are subdivided by certain sentences being made into separate paragraphs by the concluding words: אני ה׳.

Three fundamental sentences form the basic pillars of our rendering ourselves holy, they deal with: (a) parents and Sabbath, (v. 3); (b) the purity of our conception of God (v. 4); (c) the purity of, and the social results of, our relationship to God (vv. 5—10).

V. 3. איש אמו ואביו תיראו. “Fearing” mother and father and sanctifying Sabbath are the educators and guides of Jewish People to the sanctification of their lives, from cradle to the grave. יראת אם ואב is the first step towards קדושה. It is not fear, awe of the presence of mother and father, though we use that word in translation of יראה which can easily be taken as a feeling that is to fill us in the presence of parents; -יראה את is rather having a person constantly in one’s mind’s eye, and taking what their wish would be as the deciding factor in our lives. (ירא is the mental, the spiritual; קרא, “to call it to one’s mind”), its very first and most essential effect is obedience, in completely subordinating one’s own wishes to the will of those to whom יראה is directed. Already in Ex. 20,12, on: כבד את אביך ואת אמך, in the decalogue we have tried to indicate the significance of parents to which they have to thank their high position in God’s Torah. We understood them to be considered not only the medium of the physical existence of the child, but as the medium through which the mission and calling of Jewry, its history as well as the Torah is to be transmitted from God’s Hands to every coming generation. We told ourselves that it was not the measure of what parents do for their children, but the great and lofty mission which God has given parents concerning their children in whose name God’s Torah says: כבד את אביך ואת אמך. It is God, and His revelation of history and Law to which the tribute of honour and fear is to be paid in honouring and fearing parents. Here in this chapter of קדושה, it is that aspect of the child’s duty towards its parents that in the very first place is “obedience”, that is stressed. The over-ruling of the will of the parents over its own will, the cheerful yielding of its own will to that of the parents, is the first, earliest and most lasting school of practicing self-control, which leads young human beings out of the life of enforced obedience to one’s urges into mastery over one’s passions and impulses, into freeing the godly element in man, into that moral freedom, the achievement of which constitutes the character of קדוש. And significantly, ואת שבתותי תשמרו, is placed immediately in the same sentence together with כבוד או״א. This gives the one limitation which exists to the obedience which the child must accord to its parents. יכול, it says in אם אמר לו אביו ואמו :ת״כ לעבור על אחת מכל המצות האמורות בתורה ישמע להם ת״ל ואת שבתותי תשמרו כולכם חייבין בכבודי, “You might think that even if parents demand the transgression of any command of the Torah, you may, nay you must, obey them, that is why it at once says: “and keep my Sabbaths”; all of you, parents and children alike are in duty bound to honour Me”. For it is just as appointed heralds of God’s Will that God’s Torah has given the Will of Parents such lofty power. Quite naturally the will of the parents must retreat before the Will of God. Here שבת as the source and basis of the whole of the Jewish calling is given as an example for all the laws of God’s Torah, it, — שבת, — being the everlasting, most speaking sign of our allegiance to God in all our doings in the sphere of nature and our social life. It is only when a Jewish child sees his parents “Keeping Sabbath” that he learns from their example, that he learns to lay himself and his world in obedience at the feet of God, his obedience to his parents leads to obedience to God. כבוד אב ואם is the living “sabbath” for children, and Sabbath is the spiritual father and mother for everybody. Both educate Jewish people to God. Here it is not put in the singular, as in the decalogue, תשמור ,תירא, but: תשמורו ,תיראו. It is not only by the single individuals themselves that these two fundamental institutions of Jewish breeding are to receive homage, by כבוד אב ואם and שבת the whole Jewish national character receives its stamp. Through them, God becomes “Our God”, in them our allegiance to God is made manifest, and as long as these two pillars of the holiness of Jewish life stand erect, our whole relationship towards God stands on firm ground, and God can say of us: אני ה׳ אלקיכם. Experience throughout the ages has taught us too, that the breakdown of one of these pillars does not remain without the other one also breaking down.

V. 4. אל תפנו אל האלילים. Whereas לא — from לאה, to become tired, worn-out, powerless — indicates negative, negation generally, also negation of being; אל from אלל expresses only the negation of what one wishes or ought to do. So that אל can never be used in conjuction with the past or present tense. אל is, accordingly, the conception of refusing, denying, hence אללי, the exclamation for wishes which have been refused or denied. So we find in Job 10,15: אם רשעתי אללי לי, literally: “if I have trespassed against the Will of God, I can not reckon on my wishes being fulfilled, I can expect nothing but refusal”. אלילים are denying powers, the heathen conception of gods. They honour their gods primarily because they fear them as powers hostile to furthering the wishes of men. Left to himself Man always feels himself at the limit of his powers, feels himself with his longings and desires ever at war with higher powers, powers whose tolerance must be forced or flattered and cajoled out of them. This is a point of view and a necessity which, more than anything else, is begotten by the heathen gods and their cults, and which, even today, lead minds which have become estranged from the Jewish true conception of God, into the arms of heathen illusions and practices. To such ideas shall ye allow no entry into your thoughts of God. In the trend of your thoughts there shall be no beings vested with godly power who are inimical to Man. You shall not allow the idea of their existence to rise in your minds. Hence (Sabbath 149a): דיוקנא עצמה אף בחול אסור להסתכל בה משום שנאמר אל תפנו אל האלילים מאי גמרא אמר ר׳ חנן אל תפנו אל מדעתכם, i.e. it is prohibited to gaze consideringly at idols, for it says: “do not turn the thoughts of God out of your minds” (see ערוך under פן). That would take the אל תפנו as coming from the root פנה and used in the sense of אנכי פניתי הבית (Gen. 24,31), where פנה used referring to the acceptance of objects means “to be ready for that purpose”, (see Gen. on XXIV,31), from which we get in Rabbinic Hebrew the word פנוי: vacant, unencumbered, and leisure, and our text would mean: “Give no room (in your thoughts) to denying powers. But the idea: “clearing away” presupposes that the place had been previously occupied by something else, and, according to ר׳ חנן that something else referred to here is the thought of God. This should constantly and completely fill our mind and not even by a momentary contemplation of אלילים should it even temporarily be crowded out therefrom.

ואלהי מסכה וגו׳. One can not be quite sure how אלהי מסכה is to be taken. At first glance one would only think of the root נסך to pour out and take אלהי מסכה to be gods cast in metal. And, actually, we do find נסך used for casting the image of a god: הפסל נסך חרש (Is. 40,19). Nevertheless, as the form מסכה is quite definitely used also to mean covering, protection: והמסכה צרה כהתכנס (Is. 28,20); ולנסך מסכה ולא רוחי (ibid XXX,1); so also קשות הנסך (Numb. 4,7) — and also in מסכת the warp in weaving, the idea of pouring over and covering over occur together in נסך, see note on Levit. 22,47. — it does not seem far fetched to take אלהי מסכה as protecting gods. For then the connection between the two parts of this sentence would be perfectly clear and understandable. The erroneous idea of אלילים, of godly forces inimical to the success of human beings produced the other erroneous idea of the necessity for protective idols. But you: “Have no belief in the existence of אלילים, and make no אלהי מסכה for yourselves”. I am at the same time ה׳ and אלקיכם, I am He to Whom alone your trust and your fear should be directed, Who blesses you with His Love, and with His justice demands honesty in all your doings for His Blessings.

But still, phrases like: הבטחים בפסל האומרים למסכה אתם אלהינו (Is. 42,17), seem to speak rather for the material meaning, cast images. אלהי מסכה would then be gods made out of cast metal, and here would refer in general to gods made by man’s hand. אלילים would be the gods as they are imagined to be, and אלהי מסכה, the moulded representation of them. Then, if we are not mistaken, אלהי מסכה is the term chosen as a general description of manufactured gods, because just in that particular mode of construction the subjectivity — the viewing of things exclusively through the medium of one’s own mind — of all manufactured gods is most strikingly manifest. Cast idols are figures which at any desired moment can be remoulded to any shape or form. We have already shown this subjectivity of every gross or refined heathenism when dealing with the מעשה עגל in Ex. 32,1. Neither in shaped form nor in speculative thought has Man to create his gods or his God. God is given to Man, is something which is really the one absolutely objectively given thing, the one true “אני״. Man is not to imagine God out of himself but to conceive and mould himself out of God. For God is not only not an אליל, not only not a power inimical to the existence, work and thriving of Man, He is rather One in Whose everlasting existence our temporary existence has its roots, out of Whose Freewill and freewilled creative power, our freewill, our personalities, all our morally free wishes and accomplishments have their origin; and Who not only fitted us out with these highest possessions of Life and effort, but, as ה׳ gives us every present and coming minute of our life and efforts; Who, in the success of our striving and in the blossoming of our moral perfection, sees just the realisation of His Will and therefore as ה׳ is אלקינו; Who directs all our doings for this highest, most blissful goal of our lives, and also in that which He forbids and denies us, yea, often just in that, proves His highest and most caring Love: אני ה׳ אלקיכם.

V. 5—8. וכי תזבחו וגו׳. So that when we bring שלמים offerings in the feelings of our undisturbed happiness, no trace of that heathen erroneous idea may be present, as if it were necessary to placate the deity jealous of our undisturbed happy condition by giving something of it up to him out of our own free will. It is not to satisfy God’s requirements but our own, that the offering is to be brought. לרצונכם תזבחוהו, the purpose of our offering is to be an expression of our vow to make and keep good intentions (cf. Ch. 1,3).

ביום זבחכם יאכל וגו׳ וגו׳, and so little is death or destruction the meaning of the slaughter of the offering, that אכילה, the joyful eating of the offering in the Presence of God in one’s own homely family circle belongs essentially to the objects of the offerings. It is in this that the meaning of the זביחה really culminates and therefore the זביחה and the אכילה must be kept in close connection in time. Not only that which is actually left uneaten beyond the fixed time, נותר, has to be burnt, but even if only האכל יאכל וגו׳, if at the moment of זביחה there should be only a thought, only the intention of separating the אכילה from the זביחה in time — מחשבת חוץ לזמנו — the whole offering becomes פגול, and with נותר, any meat which has actually become separated from the זביחה by lapse of time, or with פגול, that which has become rejected only by intended separation of the זביחה from the אכילה, the gravest desecration of קדשים, punishable with כרת has been done. נותר, i.e. אכילה without זביחה, is the sanctioning of uncontrolled enjoyment of one’s senses, and פגול, i.e. זביחה without אכילה, is the idolatrous polytheistic אלילים-delusion. Both are blasphemous perversion of God’s קדשים into their very opposite meaning, and anyone doing so is אוכליו עונו ישא ;חילול קודש ה׳, (for a full detailed note on נותר ,פגול and פסול see Ch. 7,16 et seq., where our text here is explained in connection with the text there).

How significant is it that here, right at the beginning of the קדושה-chapter, the שלמים-offering with its נותר and פגול-laws, is placed as the third fundamental law! How clearly does that show that the holiness of Jewish life is characterised as being equally far from a “killing of everything carnal” as from an uncontrolled abandonment to the pleasures of the senses! Fearing one’s parents and keeping the Sabbath are the educators for holy living, a clear and pure true conception of God is the soul of such a life; שלמים, spiritualising and penetrating with morality even the enjoyments of our senses, so that even the ordinary table of our joyous and happy family life becomes an altar of God, and even in eating we look up to God, — that is the flower of making our lives holy, which, if it is genuine, must at once produce the social fruit, the duties of brotherly love towards our fellowmen. To שלמים are attached מתנות עניים. He who would enjoy his own and his family’s well-being in happiness before God, when he would get near to God with his own happiness, must be freed from every selfish narrowness of heart which only recognises himself and those near to him as belonging to him. The Jewish spirit of צדקה must be awake within him, that spirit that sees in every particle of happy blessing granted by God the duty to use the power it gives him to help and further and build up the happiness of all those who are not yet שלמים, who are still hungering for complete content and joy in life.

V. 9. ובקצרכם את קציר ארצכם לא תכלה וגו׳, the change in the person is significant. The Land at rock bottom is the land of the community, is, even after it has been divided, given to no one for purely exclusively selfish egoistic purposes. It is ארצכם even at the moment when each one takes home the produce of his own portion of the communal soil and it becomes quite specially שדך. Therefore, לא תכלה פאת, let no one completely gather in, as if it had grown for him alone, that which has grown on his particular portion. Let him leave one part of his field untouched, and preferably at the end of his field. This “duty-part” which is to be left standing, as well as the duty so to leave it, is called פאה. The duty extends to all produce of the soil which come under the conception of קציר, i.e. to all the produce of the ground or trees which constitute the real yearly harvest of the Land. The characteristic signs of such are that it must be: (a) אוכל, food, i.e. not dye-stuffs etc.; (b) נשמר, cultivated, i.e. not growing wild, not הפקר, (which would be excluded also by the term שדך as שדה, phonetically related to צדה is a piece of land by which a man “catches” the produce of the earth); (c) גדולו מן הארץ, that its growing is dependent entirely on earth, and not such thing as כמהים ופטריות, not fungi, mushrooms, which do not require earth but only moisture for their growth and thrive on damp wood etc.; (d) that לקיטתו כאחת, that they all ripen at about the same time and so are harvested all together and not like תאנים, figs and similar fruit, which are gathered gradually as they ripen; and finally (e) that they מכניסו לקיום, that they are gathered, not necessarily for immediate consumption but to be stored, excluding such things as fresh vegetables: כלל אמרו בפיאה כל שהוא אוכל ונשמר וגידולו מן הארץ ולקיטתו כאחת ומכניסו לקיום, (Peah 1,4; Sabbath 68a). All these conditions are characteristic of such produce which mark קציר ארצכם, which make one realise the real achievement obtained from the land. Indeed according to תוספות and the ר״ש ibid, the obligation מן התורה to give Peah would only be for דגן תירוש ויצהר for corn, vines and olive trees, and its extension to other products of the soil and other fruit trees would only be דרבנן. Moreover, Peah מדאורייתא belongs to the דברים שאין להם שיעור, to those things which מן התורה have no fixed amount given for them. For פאה there is no שיעור למטה and no שיעור למעלה given מן התורה, no minimum and no maximum limits. With the very smallest quantity that one leaves on each of one’s fields of each kind of produce, one has fulfilled the duty מן התורה and, if one wishes, one could cut just one ear of corn and leave all the rest as פאה, so that, as such, it would all go to the poor and would not be liable to the duties of תרומה ומעשרות (Peah 1,1; Nedarim 6b and וא״ש and תוספות thereon). But מדרבנן, a minimum, שיעור למטה has been fixed, viz. אין פוחתין לפאה מששים, one may not leave less than a sixtieth part of the produce of any field (Peah 1,2). This is the minimum, but one is expected to do more, according to the size of the field, according to the number of needy poor, and according to the abundance of the harvest—לפי רוב השדה ולפי רוב עניים ולפי רוב הענוה, (the latter as ענבה, or, “according to the size of his modest unselfish disposition”), Pea ibid, see ר״ש and רמב״ם.

לקט .ולקט קצירך לא תלקט: its relation to לכד, to catch capture, seize, makes us take the meaning of לקט to be the taking up of objects which otherwise, on account of their nature and position would escape us. Hence especially the gathering up of single objects lying about, the plucking of isolated plants or flowers etc. לקט קציר, accordingly, would be single ears which, at the moment of cutting, escape the scythe or the hand. One or two such ears are considered together as single ones and come under the heading of לקט, but three together do not (Peah 6,5). “Such isolated ears which escape thy cut, לא תלקט, shalt thou not gather up”.

V. 10. עולל .וכרמך לא תעולל, the פיעל of עול or עלל. As עולֵל :עויל and עולָל have the meaning of Man in childhood, in the process of developing, so does ונשאר בו עוללות :עוללה (Is. 17,6), mean fruit which has remained backwards in its development, which has not attained full development. In a vineyard the berries which have not reached the formation of clusters are so called. Now the פיעל form עולֵל similar to :סֵקֵל :דֵשֵׁן would mean: taing the עוללות away from the vine. At the grape harvest, only the grapes in bunches may be cut, but single berries which have not developed into forming bunches are to be left on the vine. This is an obligation which in vineyards is added to the duty of פאה. The characteristics of עוללות are given in Peah 7,4 as: כל שאין לה לא כתף ולא נטף. On well-formed grape-clusters small twigs go out from the central stem of the cluster in all directions, with grape-bearing ramifications which become fewer and fewer towards the bottom of the cluster, until finally the little twigs cease altogether and the grapes grow directly on the stem. If the grapes are so thickly clustered in the bunch that the upper ones rest on the lower ones, are, so-to-say, borne on their shoulders, then the twigs and ramifications are called כתף, and the grapes growing closely one after the other on the stem of the bunch on its lower edge are called נטף. Where both these signs are lacking the grapes which grow singly are called עוללות (see ר״ש on Peah ibid, and on הל׳ מתנות עניים, 4,17).
פרט .ופרט כרמך לא תלקט, related to פרד etc., are single grapes that fall off during the cutting of the bunches, it is exactly similar in a כרם to לקט in a cornfield.

לעני ולגר תעזוב אותם. We find repeatedly with these מתנות עניים, that the expression: תתן אותם is not used, but here, and in Ch. 23,22 it says: תעזוב אותם, and in Deut. 21,20 & 21: לגר ליתום ולאלמנה יהיה, and again there, in v. 19, with the further duty given there of שכחה. For with these מתנות עניים the טובת הנאה, the right of disposal, of giving it to any particular person of one’s choice, is not accorded to the owner. He has no right to distribute them amongst the poor. More, he has no right to give even any part of them to any particular poor man. Whereas, for other gifts, even for מעשר עני המתחלקת בתוך ביתו, the charity tithe which is distributed in the house, יש בו טובת הנאה for the owner (Chulin 131a). So that neither he nor any well-to-do person may take possession of any part of these field-gifts to the poor on behalf of any particular poor man, even if that poor man has appointed him as his שליח; although generally even without special appointments, anybody can act as representative of somebody else and take possession of his behalf of anything to which he is entitled, זכין לאדם שלא בפניו, here because he would be חב לאחרים, because through his intervention, other people with equal rights to it would be prejudiced, he may not do so. The rule applies that: תופס לבעל חוב במקום שחב לאחרים לא קנה, no seizure of a debt that is due made by somebody who has no claim himself, on behalf of a creditor, is valid if there are other creditors. But one poor man can gather up these field-gifts for another poor man, and as soon as he gathers them up they become the property of that other one on whose hehalf he has picked them up, just as somebody can legally pick up something lying ownerless in the street for somebody else and it then becomes that other person’s property: המגביה מציאה לחברו קנה חברו, both in accordance with the basic principle: מגו דזכי לנפשיה זכי נמי לחבריה, “any legal power of appropriation which a man can exercise on his own behalf he can legally do for anybody else”, (Baba Mezia 9b & 10b). From the repeated תעזוב אותם it also follows that even if the prohibition לא תכלה has been transgressed the rights of the poor have not been lost, but that: לא הפריש מן הקמה יפריש מן העמדים, לא הפריש מן העמרים יפריש מן הכרי. And if, according to the canon established by רבא (Temura 4b et seq.), that: כל מלתא דאמר רחמנא לא תעביד אי עביד לא מהני, that any action which is forbidden by the Torah, if done, can have no legally-recognised effect, this would be self-understood, then from these repeated expressions: תעזוב, we learn that this duty can not be circumvented by a temporary giving-up ownership of the whole field (הפקר), but that: המפקיר כרמו והשכים לבקר ובערו חייב בפרט וכו׳, and that even a permanent change in the formation of the material, שנוי שנוי שאינו חוזר לברייתא ,דלא הדר, which generally makes the claim to the material lost, שנוי קונה (see notes on Ch. 5,23), here does not remove the claim of the poor, and if פיאה had not been given even up to the stage of the dough being made, מפריש מן העיסה ונותן לו, (Baba Kama 94,a, תוספות there).

The keeping of these rights of the poor to the produce of the land is accordingly made here into a duty by a negative and a positive command. לא תכלה ,לא תלקט ,לא תעולל, prohibits one to lay one’s hand on the last corner of one’s fields, on that which drops from the cutter, or the vine-knife, or the grapes which have remained back from forming bunches: לעני ולגר תעזוב אותם, commands one to leave them to the poor and to the stranger, and moreover, this command is not only מעיקרא משמע, not only as an obligation coming simultaneously with the prohibition, not to be taken as: לא תלקט וכו׳ לא תכלה כי אם תעזוב, “thou shalt not cut off, not harvest etc., but leave the corner of your field etc., “but השתא משמע, after the prohibition has been transgressed, the positive command comes into force, to place back that which has been illegally taken at the disposal of those legally entitled to it (Yoma 36b). Such a prohibition, for whose transgression a positive command follows is called a לאו הניתק לעשה (form נתק, to tear away, נתוק וכרות, Ch. 22,24, and in connection with נתקו כפות :אל- ,ל- רגלי הכהנים אל החרבה. Josh. 4,18, departing from one standpoint and immediately going over to another): a prohibition which goes over from the character of a negative command to that of a positive one. It is also called: לא תעשה שיש בו קום עשה. An example of such a לאו הניתק לעשה is לא תותירו וגו׳ והנותר וגו׳ באש תשרפו (Ex. 12,10), or: לא תקח האם על הבנים שלח תשלח את האם (Deut. 22,7 et alia.). By this transference from a negative command to a positive one, the definite punishment for transgression is changed. By carrying out the positive command which follows the transgressing, the punishment which otherwise would have to be imposed for the later is abrogated. In Makkoth 15b et seq. there are two ways in which this is taken. According to the one, the result of the transgression only is connected with the positive command, the prohibition has been transgressed and is punishable, but the punishment can be avoided by carrying out the positive command; this way of taking it is expressed by the phrase: קיימו ולא קיימו, the punishment is dependent on the fulfilment or non-fulfilment of the obligation which then exists. The עשה is תקונו של לאו, is a making good of the transgression. According to the other way of taking it, the transgression itself is connected with the positive command, and is only really made, if, after transgressing the prohibition, the positive command is frustrated, if e.g. the object concerned is destroyed, only then does the transgression become punishable. This way of taking it is expressed by the phrase: ביטלו ולא ביטלו. The transgression is dependent on the frustration or non-frustration of the positive command. The first way of taking it is the one accepted for the Halacha.
This duty of לקט שכחה ופאה, is encumbent on every owner of a field, however poor he may be. He must leave these rights to his field to other poor people.

When we consider that פאה מן התורה has no שיעור למטה no minimum limit, that the obligation is discharged with even the tiniest quantity, it is evident that these laws are not made for the direct purpose of the actual maintenance of the poor. Even the poor man himself has to leave his לקט שכחה ופאה ועוללות from his field to other poor people! It is clear that, at once at the harvest, at the moment when a person takes home that which Nature and his own own hard-work has yielded to him, and puts the proud and far-reaching word “my own” in his mouth, these laws are to remind every member of the Nation, and to demand an act of recognition from him, of the fact that this “my own” includes for everybody the duty of caring for others who are needy; that field and vineyard have not yielded their produce for his exclusive use (פאה עוללות), and that his hand is not to work exclusively for himself (לקט ופרט), that in God’s holy State the care for the “poor and the stranger without property” is not a matter which is left to the greater or lesser soft-hearted feelings of sympathy, or to the greater or lesser feeling of expediency, that the despair of the poor and needy classes may constitute a threatening danger to the property of the well-to-do, in short, not to be left to sympathy nor to policy, but is raised to a God-given right to the poor, and to a God-ordained duty to the owners of property from God, Who proclaims His אני ה׳ אלקיכם over all of them, and thereby assures that each and every one of them is equally considered by Him, that each and every one of them is equally encompassed by His Love, and granted rights from Him, that they are all equally bound to give the same rights and the same love, and so to unite to form a community holy to God, and held together by respect for rights and for the duty of brotherly love.

These foundations for holy living (קדושים תהיו) start with the fundamental principles of the family and the individual with כבוד אב ואם and שבת, and the finishing stone is laid with the fundamental basis of social life, the Jewish conception of צדקה, of the rights to brotherly love and the duty of brotherly loving. It is significant that this social foundation is woven into one group with the laws pertaining to the service of God, those of שלמים and פגול — the service of man with the service of God. On the basis of a true Jewish life, social life and so-called religious life form no contrast to each other, they are not even co-existing separate parts of one higher whole, but belong together in essential organic unity as root and tree, as blossom and fruit. Jewish Truth teaches: אוהב את המקום אוהב את הבריות, the movement towards God includes the movement towards His human beings. In the same underlying feeling in which the pure שלמים-joy in the content of one’s life granted by God has its roots, the duty of loving one’s fellow-man and respecting his rights is also rooted.

Vv. 11 & 12. In connection with the social principles given in the preceding verses now follow several sentences out of the social catechism of the Nation which is to be holy to God. ,לא תשקרו ,לא תכחשו ,לא תגנבו לא תשבעו, are — in contrast to the succeeding לא תעשוק etc. — given in the personal plural, and just that gives us the character of their meaning. לא לא תשבע בשם ה׳ לשקר ,לא תשקר ,לא תכחש ,תגנב, would be addressed to the individual as in the Ten Commandments, and would speak of the sins of lying, of stealing, of swearing falsely, and abstaining from these surely does not have to wait to be told until this chapter of קדושה. One is still a long way from being a קדוש if one is simply not a thief or does not commit perjury. But, addressed in the plural to the national community, it can not be thinking of these gross sins, which were never, could never, have been practiced by the whole, or even by the greater majority of the nation. These sins, in every national community are only traits of individuals, and to suppress which, the state by itself would take steps. But here it refers to such, גנבה, such שקר, such שבועת שקר, such unlawfulness, such dishonesty, such cursory swearing which have become so interwoven into the ordinary daily business and social life of the people, that they can become the ruling national characteristic of a people, that, being universally used, lose the stigma of something to be avoided, and can even rise to be considered as a praiseworthy and enviable art — and yet, before God, remain equally reprehensible to actual theft, real lies, real perjury. It is from such that God’s Word here warns His People. In their business and social intercourse:

לא תגנבו, “unfair advantage gained by sharp-practice” is not to be your method of dealing, for that, in its wider sense is the idea of גניבה. גנב, is related to כנף, covered up, for secrecy and lawlessness are its essential characteristics. Hence wherever sharp-practice, unnoticed by the other jury extracts even a peruta, even a penny, and appropriates it, in God’s Eyes a theft has been committed and His לא תגנבו transgressed. Yea, our sages explain the term in ת״כ thus:— לא תגנבו על מנתלמקט לא תגנבו על מנת לשלם כפל ולא על מנת לשלם ד׳ וה׳ בן בג בג אומר לא תגנוב את שלך מאחר הגנב שלא תראה גונב, “not even as a practical joke to tease shall we allow ourselves to take something that does not belong to us, not even with the intention to repay double, or if making restitution four or five fold, should not even take back that which has been stolen from us by secretly stealing it from the thief, to avoid even the appearance of a גניבה, or as it says in the ח״מ, referring to stealing for a joke, or just to annoy for the time-being: הכל אסור כדי שלא ירגיל עצמו בכך, “a conscientious Jew does not practice being clever at stealing”.

And just as in business dealings, so does this Word of God, לא תגנבו, banish all deceit and slyness from social intercourse, all deceit intended by גניבת דעת, by “stealing” somebody’s opinion or feelings. A conscientious Jew achieves the good opinion and the sympathetic feelings of his fellowmen, but he does not “steal” them. Every action, every word, by which we make other people have a higher opinion of us than we really deserve, or gain more gratitude than we have really earned, is reprehensible as being גניבת דעת (Chulin 94).

כחש .ולא תכחשו ולא תשקרו איש בעמיתו is to deny a justified accusation. Related to כעש ,כעס, to be angered when perceiving a wrong, כַחֵשׁ, in the Piel means to give cause for such anger by lying, denying the truth. לא תכחשו also affects our sincerity equally in business as in social intercourse. Neither in one nor in the other may the consideration of our own interests be the deciding factor for our words. In business as in social intercourse everybody must be able to demand the truth from us, and even if it is to our disadvantage must be able to depend on our admission of the truth.

שקר, to lie, includes the whole great sphere of lying, in the widest sense. Lying, which in business and private life fights shy of the truth, of acknowledging things and circumstances to be what they really are, that fundamental basis of all well-being and all faithfulness to duty. Lying, which turns the word of a human being, that should be the pledge of the godlike worth of human beings, that should be the magic that makes all social working of happiness, turns it into the very opposite, into the means of unhappiness and crime. כחש is the robber of truth, שקר its thief, and as certain as the acknowledgement and knowledge of the Truth has an incomparably higher and farther-reaching importance than that which is attached to any material possession, so certain is it that the theft of truth is a much more pernicious crime than stealing of any actual object. Flatterers, who steal from their fellowmen the most important truth, the truth of knowing oneself, and hypocrites, who pass the whole of themselves as a false coin, belong to the most objectionable characters which are to be banished from Jewish social life by לא תשקרו. Further, just as אמת means not only logical but also practical truth, faithfulness, fidelity, so שקר too, designates also unfaithfulness, not keeping one’s given word, as in בנים לא ישקרו (Is. 63,8), and elsewhere, and לא תשקרו איש בעמיתו also includes the injunction, “do not deceive by empty promises, keep your word one to another”.

Finally: ולא תשבעו בשמי לשקר. “Do not misuse the calling on My Presence to judge between man and man, to confirm a lie”. All these prohibitions have already been implied in the אזהרות, the warnings as to the punishable results of the common sins of theft, denying and false swearing. But here given in the plural number, they are addressed to the whole nation in all its members, to include in the warning prohibition, that unfair dealing, that unreliability, that untruthfulness and untrustworthiness, and also that misuse of swearing which, extending far beyond individual cases of general sinful behaviour, can become so much habit and custom of the national community that by its universal usage, all consciousness of its being wrong and disgracing the holy character of Man disappears. That is why these sentences, which up to then had been addressed to the national community as an עם, as the internal society in all its members, now, looking on this community as a גוי, as a unit regarded externally, addresses the Jewish Nation, as one amongst the other nations, and says: וחללת את שם אלקיך. God has sent you into the midst of the nations as bearers of His Name; as His People are you to show the rest of the nations a pattern of a community built up by God on justice and truth and trustworthiness. If you stain yourself with unfair dealing, untruthfulness, unreliability, untrustworthiness and careless false swearing then you desecrate the name you bear, you kill the recognition of God, Whose herald and priest you should be.

רש״ל !אני ה׳ on ב״מ 61a. תוספ׳ בד״ה שתולה וכו׳, expresses the opinion that wherever a law concludes with אני ה׳ these words come to work against any attempt of deceptive misconstruction, and to produce that conscientiousness which the thought of God, as the Ever-present, All-seeing One, brings about. Thereby one particular phase of the inexhaustible abundance of Truths which are innate in this, the four-lettered Name of God, is brought to the fore. This would be that immediate reference to that conception of God, which we have dared to assume to be the fundamental notion that this Name brings to us. If this Name makes us think of God, as that One Who orders and arranges every coming minute of our lives in accordance with the requirements of our being educated up to holiness and true happiness, that He is the One Whom we have to thank for every coming moment, then every present moment of our lives must be in His mind for Him to decide what the coming one is to be — happy and joyful, or the reverse. Realising this, we pay attention to all our feelings, think all our thoughts, speak all our words, do all our actions before Him, conscious of His Presence and of His critical Eye, which is to render our whole existence becoming a holy one and effect that conscientiousness, honesty, fair dealing, and straightforwardness in the degree that He demands from those whom He would regard as belonging to Him and who call themselves His.

V. 13 & 14. After the foregoing paragraph has proclaimed the general principles of honesty and straightforwardness, in these two verses now follow some of the results in certain cases which illustrate the range of these general principles.

עשק .לא תעשק את רעך ולא תגזול, related to חשק ,חשך ,חשך ,חזק ,אזק, all of which have the meaning of holding fast and holding back, showing strength and force therein, עשק means withholding, a retention of that which is due to somebody else. But as it is always constructed with the person in the accusative, the idea is rather focused on the illegal disadvantage which accrues to the person than on the object retained. It is a chaining-up and keeping the person back from obtaining possession of, and the use of, his property. Every non-satisfying a justified demand made to us is accordingly עשק. In Baba Mezia 3a, even simply keeping somebody in suspense with regards to such a demand, not paying promptly when it is within your power to do so, saying: לד ושוב ומחר אתן ויש אתך (Prov. 2,28), is considered עושק; although on 110b, there, this is taken not to come under the prohibition of עושק but under the special prohibition of בל תשהא.

גזל .ולא תגזול, in its real sense is to rob, to forcibly take something away. But in Baba Mezia 61a, it is pointed out that the prohibition of “robbing” has been already implicitly given in other laws, and that there is no necessity for saying it again here — and, may we add, that the prohibition of common robbery would hardly find its place in this chapter of “making one’s life holy” — and there it teaches that under the לא תגזול here, is to be understood the כובש שכר שכיר, keeping back the wages of a daily worker. So that he who keeps back the wages of a worker, עובר עליו בשני לאוין, transgresses two prohibitions, the special one forbidding keeping back wages: לא תעשוק שכר עני ואביון (Deut. 24,14), and the general one: לא תגזול. Equally so it says in the Gemora (ibid 111a): זה הוא עושק זהו גזל לא תעשוק .ולמה חלקן הכתוב לעבור עליו בשני לאוין and לא תגזול are understandably identical. Both are a forcible taking away that which belongs by rights to someone else. The law separates them to make anybody transgressing the prohibition liable under two counts. So that לא תגזול here does not come to forbid common robbery — it could not then have possibly have found its place after לא תעשוק, if even עושק is already forbidden, no need then to say that גזל is — but ולא תגזול comes in immediate connection with לא תעשוק and then follows לא תלין in ascending gravity of the offence against earned wages: not only direct forcible taking away, but every simply keeping back anything that rightfully belongs to someone else is to be considered by a Jewish conscience as common robbery. But regarding the wages of a labourer it is considered so important that לא תלין comes into force, that not even over night until the next morning may payment be delayed of wages that were due at the end of the day.

Accordingly, we find it stated in Baba Mezia 111a, that anybody retaining the wages of a day-labourer transgresses five negative commands and one positive one: עובר משום בל תעשוק את רעך ומשום בל תגזול ומשום בל תעשוק שכיר עני ומשום בל תלין ומשום ביומו תתן שכרו ומשום לא תבוא עליו השמש (Deut. 24,14 & 15).

The prohibition of לא תלין makes it incumbent for wages to be paid within the period of the day in which, or with which, they become due. For the day worker whose time is up at nightfall, wages must be paid that night, i.e. before the next morning: שכיר יום גובה כל הלילה. A night worker whose wages are due in the morning must be paid on that day, i.e. before the next night: שכיר לילה גובה כל היום. A part time worker, paid by the hour, must be paid during the period in which the work was completed whether day or night: שכיר שעות גובה כל היום או כל הלילה. Our text here refers to a day-worker, that in Deut. 24,15 to a night worker. Under the heading פעולת שכיר is included wages due for piece-work or under contract, קבלנות, and also שכר בהמה וכלים, hire of objects or use of power. The prohibition is only actually transgressed when the payment is demanded, and it is within one’s power to pay it, it says: אתך לדעתך ,אתך שיש אתך ,אתך (ibid 112a).

Just as here the conception גזלה is extended to עשק and כובש שכר שכיר, so is even a momentary taking possession of another’s property, e.g. using it without the owner’s permission — שואל שלא מדעת הבעלים — considered גזלה (חשן משפט 359,5). Arbitrarily distraining on a debtor is there also called גזלה, as is also, using an object with the permission of its present owner when you know he has no real right to be in possession of it, (ibid 369,2). Our sages have extended the conception גזלה yet further for Jewish consciences. They warn us against מפריחי יונים, not to allow our pigeons to fly in such places where they might bring strange pigeons back with them to nest in their cote with them. Equally so, not to keep pigeons in such a place where they will fly over people’s fields and gather their food from them. Also the idea of אסמכתא, that no possessions of another may be acquired which that person only agreed to give hypothetically, when it can be assumed that he did not agree to its loss definitely but only did so because he depended absolutely (סומך) on the opposite happening to what actually did occur. Under this title would come certain forms of betting, gambling and speculation in business, and our sages say: אסמכתא לא קניא, (see Ch. M. 207,370). Further, although the legal concept, גזלה only applies to the minimum value of a Peruta (a פרוטה = the weight of half the size of a barleycorn of silver, Ch. M. 88,1), so that things on which nobody places any value such as a straw, a splinter of wood etc., can not be claimed as גזלה, nevertheless one should refrain from taking, for instance, a straw out of a made-up bundle, or cutting a splinter from a fence with which to pick one’s teeth, for, as our sages give as the reason for their prohibition, if every passer-by helped himself in a similar manner, there would ultimately be no bundle or fence left to the owner (Ch. M. 35,9).

V. 14. לא תקלל חרש וגו׳. The previous verses taught the lessons of being careful to refrain from injuring the possessions of others out of selfishness. Now we get two sentences warning us against doing any injury at all to others, in the widest application of the word injury.

Firstly: לא תקלל; not even by word — however impotent it may be — may the wish for the adversity of another — for that is what קללה, from קלל to lose weight, is — may be expressed. For a curse does express the ill-will that one feels towards another and that only lack of power prevents one from actually bringing about the downfall of one’s neighbour. This prohibition: לא תקלל, is quite a general one. The addition חרש does not limit it, it extends it. Even where the other does not hear it, so that the curse has not even the effect of hurting his feelings, the prohibition still applies (Shebuoth 36a, Rambam, הל׳ סנהדרין 26,1). It is equally prohibited to curse oneself: מקלל עצמו, (ibid).

ולפני עור לא תתן מכשול. This is a sentence of the most far reaching import. It warns us against carelessness in word or deed through which the material or spiritual well-being of our fellow men could in any way be endangered. By עור is understood not only the actual blind, but also those who are, in any way, spiritually or morally blind, dazzled by passion or ignorance. So that not only anybody who actually places a stone in the path of a blind man, but also he who deliberately gives wrong advice, עצה (ת״כ) ,שאינה הוגנת. — who gives the means, or prepares the way for wrong to be done, e.g.: מושיט כוס יין לנזיר, he hands a Nazir a glass of wine (Pessachim 22,b), sells a weapon to a suspected bandit (Aboda Zara 15b) sells a בגד שאבד בו כלאים, cloth or garment that has שעטנז that is unrecognizable in it, so that people could come to sin unknowingly (ibid 55b), or similar acts — who, in any way is מחזיק ידי עוברי עברה actively or passively assists or furthers people in doing wrong (Ramban, הלי רוצח, 12,14) — who excites anybody to anger — e.g. a father to his grown-up son — so that he forgets himself in passion (Moed Katon 17a & Kiddushin 32a) — all these and such like, transgress this prohibition. Thus the whole great sphere of the material and spiritual happiness of our neighbour is entrusted to our care. Our care and consideration must be exercised for the benefit of our neighbour to prevent him coming to any material or moral harm through our means.

ויראת מאלקיך אני ה׳. And in all these matters, we are not to feel ourselves under the judgment of our fellowmen, to be before a human tribunal, but to be placed under the Eye of God, the All-seeing One Whose constant presence teaches us the most conscientious watch over ourselves and self-criticism of all our behaviour: והרי הדבר מסור ללב שנאמר ויראת מאלקיך (ת״כ) ,אני ה׳.
Vv. 15 & 16. These two verses warn against misuse of our powers, and forgetting our duty where the happiness and honour of others lie in our hands.

First the community: לא תעשו עול במשפט, it is not to misuse the position which the institution of lawcourts gives it over individuals, by force or caprice. For that is עול. Just as און is the misuse of און, the misuse of power and fortune, so is אול the misuse of עול, set above, higher position (synonymous with עלה from which we get עול young, considered as still growing up). עול במשפט is misuse of the institution of Law. משפט is applied צדק, applied right and the consequent laws of rights. This is the highest purpose of society which has to give it the power of the whole community to enforce these laws being carried out. Any misuse of the framing of these laws or even only vexatious lengthy dragging out the laws is עול במשפט, (Rambam הל׳ סנהדרין 20b).

Then the warning for each individual judge: לא תשא פני דל ולא תהדר פני גדול, but: בצדק תשפט עמיתך. These three sentences demand the absolute equality of treatment of parties at law by the judge. In Deut. 1,17 this is put in general terms: לא תכירו פנים במשפט, literally, “ye shall not recognize faces in the law-court”, i.e. in forming your judgment and in giving the verdict the person concerned must completely disappear. You have only to recognise and judge the case before you. According to Jewish jurisprudence the fairest judgment is given when both parties are completely unknown to the judge; if he does know them, he is to forget who they are. Not even the previous record or the general reputation of one standing before the court, may have any influence. The most righteous man may be in the wrong in the present case, the worst moral character may be right in the case before the court. The Mechilta teaches this already on the verse: לא תטה משפט אביונך בריבו in Ex. 23,6: רשע וכשר עומדין לפניך בדין שלא תאמר הואיל ורשע הוא אטה עליו את הדין ת״ל לא תטה משפט אביונך בריבו הוא אביון במצות, there lack of good character is also understood under אביון. That which there is called: הכר פנים, is called here: נשא פנים. We have already remarked in Ex. 23,6, that נשא פנים in law cases means to admit the personalities of the parties into one’s mind and consideration, a consideration of the persons concerned and not solely of the case in hand.

Now here the warning is given not to allow any consideration of the social position of the parties to effect the verdict or their treatment in court. Not even with the very best intentions may considerations which outside the court might be extremely laudable, have any influence on the verdict. A rich man and a poor one are standing before the court, the poor man may even be a דל, one who has come down in life, and so is ashamed of his poverty (see on Ex. 2,32). Do not say: עני הוא זה הואיל ואני והעשיר הזה חײבים לפרנסו אזכנו ונמצא מתפרנס בנקיות לכך נאמר לא תשא פני דל, “I, as well as this rich man, are both bound to give this poor man help and assistance, so I will give the verdict in his favour, and so he will get what he needs without feeling the shame of accepting charity”, against that is said: “have no consideration for a poor man even if he feels ashamed of his poverty”, (ת״כ).

הדר .ולא תהדר פני גדול is the respectful affirmation of the honour due to the character or to the position of anybody, cf. והדרת פני זקן (v. 32). So that if a great חכם and a quite ordinary man come before the court, the judge may not show the great man the special courtesies (e.g. “be seated, sir” I.L.), which otherwise he would accord him, so that the other party should not feel himself intimidated already before the case starts. The judge must refrain from any greeting to one or the other until the verdict has been declared (Rambam, הל׳ סנהדרין 20,4). This is also what the ת״כ means when it says on our text: שלא תאמר עשיר הוא זה בן גדולים הוא ,זה לא אבײשנו ואראה בבושתו עד כמה שאני מבײשו לכך נאמר לא תהדר פני גדול, “do not say: this is a rich man, he comes from such a great family, I will not offend him, and see his offended feelings, for how long should I leave him in such a shamed state”, for this it says: לא תהדר פני גדול. Rambam, too, seems to take this text to have this meaning, and not as ק״א who takes it to refer to actual partiality in judgment.

בצדק תשפט עמיתך is the positive complement of the preceding. Thou shalt not תעשו עול במשפט etc., but rather צדק .בצדק תשפט וגו׳ (phonetically related to שדך ,שתק, see on Gen. 6,9), is the ideal of Right, the general carrying out of which would make all dealings with persons and things satisfy the higest demands of that which is due to them. Regulating matters in accordance with this conception of Right is שפט. This idea of Right to be obtained out of God’s Torah is to be always in the mind of the judge, and as it is the exact opposite of the עול, which is forbidden in the first verse, it, and it alone, without consideration of the position or other conditions of the parties, is to be realised in his decision. “With what is Right” is he to measure those that stand before him, and in accordance with that measure is he to arrange matters. In every party standing before him he is to see עמיתו, one having equal rights and privileges. All those to be judged stand זה לעמת זה, on exactly one line, every one of them without exception has equal claim to equal justice. Hence with this sentence the judge is warned (Shevuoth 30a), to give exactly the same courteous treatment to both parties: שלא יהא אחד יושב ואחד עומד אחד מדבר כל צרכו ואחד אומר לו קצר דבריך (Not to allow one to sit and the other to stand, one to speak at length, and say to the other “cut it short” I.L.).

For judgment outside the court of justice, for judging our fellows in ordinary life, out of this sentence imposing the duty on the judge to adhere sharply to the absolute facts in all strictness, the Gemora there learns the rule: הוי דן את חברך לכף זכות, always give the best possible interpretation to all matters concerning your neighbour and judge him to his advantage. This is only apparently in contradiction with the judical formula. For judgment in a court of justice and social judgment do not serve the same purpose. The former has to test the action solely as to whether it is in accordance with the dictates of justice or not, quite apart from any considerations of the individual circumstances or conditions and without regard to the motives. An action, although it may not be legal, can be entirely excusable and yet at the forum of justice must be judged as punishable. And an action judged by its motive can be stamped as highly vicious and yet legally be within the law and unpunishable. But Society has, on the other hand, above all, the personality, the character, in its eye, and every action is, to it, only a symptom by which to judge the integrity or the reverse of its members. Exactly the same justice which in court banishes personality entirely from the judgment, and judges the action entirely in absolute objectivity, that same justice demands in social life the most meticulous and anxious conscientiousness in considering every possible condition which could make the person and his character appear in a better light, and admonishes: Be not hasty in throwing mud at anybody’s character, always be inclined to find excusing circumstances for all actions! This is the same idea of justice which for social judgment says: אל תדין את חברך עד שתגיע למקומו, “Judge not thy neighbour until thou hast been in a similar position”, (Aboth 2,5). It differentiates between forensic and social judgment to such an extent that to the judge in civil cases it says: When the parties stand before you, consider them both in the wrong, but once they have accepted your decision and have left you, regard them both as good men”: כשיהיו בעלי הדין עומדים לפניך יהיו בעיניך כרשעים וכשנפטרים מלפניך יהיו בעיניך כזכאין כשקבלו עליהם את הדין, (ibid 1,8).

רכל .לא תלך רכיל בעמיך related phonetically and by meaning to רגל. Whereas הלך means moving away, either for the purpose of getting away from where you are or to get to some other place, רגל (from which we also get רגלי, a pedestrian), means step by step to find its aim at every step in getting to know the locality. דַגֵל את הארץ: to spy out a land, to get to know its characteristics step by step. Then דַגֵל ב־ (Sam. II. 19,27), to give information against somebody, to give a bad report about somebody.

Similarly רכֵל :רכל means primarily a pedlar who goes from house to house, brings wares to satisfy requirements to the house. So we find it in Song of Songs 3,6 & Nehemiah 13,20. Then in trade it means intermediary agents, who arrange the export and import of the products and requirements of one land to the other. So, in Ezekiel XXVII & XXVIII. From that רָכִיל then comes to mean the “news-pedlar” who goes from one person to the other, from house to house, and at the one finds out matters which he can then unpack as a welcome “bit of news” at the other. לא תלך רכיל בעמיך forbids in general, telling tales of matters which are unknown from one person to another, unless one is certain that the person about whom it is said would like to have the information spread. Thus in Prov. 11,13 & XX,19: הולך רכיל is explained by מגלה סוד and גולה סוד. This prohibition looks on the national community as עמים, as a number of more or less closed circles, homes and families, within which their affairs are carried on, and by the natural and mutual confidence in the inmates, these cicumstances are kept within the bounds of that particular circle and do not spread by themselves from עם to עם. Now anybody who carries matters which are confidential from one circle or one house to another is הולך רכיל בעמיו It is, accordingly, the prohibition of not having consideration for every person and his private affairs, and makes it our duty to keep the strictest conscientiousness in talking about them. Nobody can judge how far-reaching the effects may be of spreading news of the private affairs of others, and once one allows tittle-tattle to get into its stride, all the bounds of confidence become loosened, and רכילות forces everybody anxiously to keep all his private matters strictly to himself. This prohibition also applies to members of the bench, to exercise the utmost discretion in revealing particulars of the discussions and opinions expressed before arriving at a verdict. Even if one of them only remarks that he had voted in favour of the person concerned, but had been outvoted by his colleagues, who were in the majority, he is guilty of הולך רכיל מגלה סוד and transgresses the prohibition, (Sanhedrin 31a). A yet higher degree of רכילות is לשון הרע, slander, chattering about the character and actions of others, even if it is entirely true; and the teaching of our sages reckons לשון הרע amongst the greatest and most reprehensible of sins (see Arachin 15a et seq.).

לא תעמד על דם רעך. The הולך רכיל endangers the welfare of his neighbour maliciously or at least carelessly. But it is not enough simply not to be a הולך רכיל and refrain from yourself endangering your neighbour’s welfare, but לא תעמד etc. Whenever and wherever we see our neighbour’s welfare endangered we are not to remain indifferent and inactive but must go ourselves, or if the circumstances are beyond our own powers of help, call others, to the rescue (Sanhedrin 73a). For is he not רעך, he is to find his “pasturage”, the “furthering of his well-being” in you, you are to find your “pasturage” in him, in his progress to find the furthering of your own. Out of the duty here imposed to look after the well-being of your neighbour, the ת״כ derives the positive duty to come forward with any evidence you may have in his favour: אם אתה יודע לו עדות אין אתה רשאי לשתוק עליה. The ק״א adds to this, the explanation of the connection with the immediately preceding לא תלך רכיל, namely that this prohibition is to be disregarded, and the whole unvarnished truth must be given in such voluntary evidence even when the character and the actions of the other party are shown up in the worst light, or his private matters are publicly revealed thereby. Furthermore, there in ת״כ the teaching is given that just as is the case where one’s own life is threatened it is permissable to save it by killing your would-be murderer, so is it your duty to save the life of your neighbour by killing the murderer who is threatening it: ניתן להצילו בנפשו של רודף (see Sanhedrin 73a). — אני ה׳: See on v. 12.

V. 17. לא תשנא וגו׳. The laws contained in verses 11—16 speak of our behaviour towards our neighbour in general. They teach how we must not allow our speech and actions to be influenced in any way by our own interests, nor by indifference, and certainly not by malice; but rather, how, under the ever present Eye of God, we are to measure all that we say and do, and refrain from saying and doing, by the yardstick of truth, honesty, concientiousness and the brotherly love which God expects from us as being “His”. These principles of social life lived under the dictates of that which God considers social life should be, are now complemented by indicating what our relations are to be towards those of our fellowmen who, forgetting these principles, have misbehaved towards us, and who thereby might be considered to have forfeited their right to demand our consideration and love. Against that idea comes the holy and sanctifying Word of God: לא תשנא את אחיך בלבבך! The Torah assumes that, left to ourselves, the behaviour of our fellowmen towards us might have allowed the feeling and the conception of שנאה to arise in our heart. שנאה, the “thorn-and-thistle feeling” (סנה = שנא), which stretches distance-keeping and obstructing unfriendly arms against fellowmen whose existence one feels as a hinderance to one’s own progress, and whose ruin one wishes for, even to the extent of ending their existence. Such a feeling, which may be quite a natural one to a human heart not ennobled by the control of God’s Torah, we are not to allow to arise within us. However badly our fellowman may have behaved towards us, however much, by his forgetting his duty towards our welfare, he may be unworthy of the name רע, however much, by failing to recognise our rights, he may have forfeited the demand of עמית, of equality of rights, one name he can never lose, אחינו he remains. This he remains by the common thread of Divine descent, מאוחה, joined in brotherhood to us in God, and through God. We remain brothers, children of the same Paternal House. And for the sake of this common Father, Who still recognises him as His child, and Who still grants him a place next to us in His House — and in His Heart — שנאה must not arise within us. But the warning: לא תשנא וגו׳ in all its earnestness is all the more necessary, as human feelings, left to their own natural, unnobled trend, know even שנאת חנם an unjustified and unprovoked hatred, against which the Torah by its all embracing term: לא תשנא את אחיך בלבבך, has to elevate its followers all the more, as this “unreasonable hate” is so very prevalent amongst lower natures. To them the fact that a “brother-man”, in the struggle for existence”, in a perfectly justified manner is working for the same goal, and by his perseverance and abilities threatens to overtake him, or at any rate forces him to greater efforts, this alone suffices to see in his “brother-man”, a hinderance to his welfare, a condition justifying hate, and wishes for his downfall even to the extent of complete ruin. שנאת חנם was the sin which, according to Yoma 9b, brought about the destruction of the Temple, and there is no more effective thought to suppress such a destructive and pernicious feeling of שנאה, unworthy of any Jew, than that which lies in the word “אחיך״, which makes us look on every other human being working alongside us as a “brother” in our Father’s house. In our Divine Father’s House no enmity or jealousy is to be known!

הוכח תוכיח וגו׳ teaches, primarily, that not only is it permitted, but that it is a duty imposed on us, as soon as by word or deed we feel ourselves hurt by anybody, to tell them of it. But it also imposes the same duty at all times in general towards anybody whom we see straying from the path of equity and justice or from God’s commandments. הוכיח: in the vast majority of cases הוכיח means to bring somebody to the recognition of some unpleasant knowledge, either to convince him of some logical error, as in Job 9,33, or to convince him of having done some wrong, as in most other instances. This latter either by direct oral proof as in Is. 29,21, and elsewhere, or indirectly brought about by trouble and suffering, as in Prov. 3,13 and elsewhere.
