In this relation יכח may be related to יגע which in the הפעיל also means to cause suffering, and perhaps, like הלך and ילך, is also related to הגה, the expression of inducing thought. There is only one single instance where the knowledge imparted by הוכיח is not an unpleasant one, viz.: אותה הוכחת לעבדך ליצחק of Eliezer (Gen. 24,14). Eliezer may have wished to express thereby the complete certainty with which he would take the result of the test which he proposed for himself. For him it was to be the absolute declaration of the Will of God, against which any opposing scruples or considerations must not be entertained. In accordance with our way of taking it, the ואת כל ונוכחת of Ch. 20,16 ibid, would also be understandable. By this Abimelech stated that henceforth she could declare quite openly and definitely who and what she was, and this final behaviour towards her would do away with any opposing reflections. We find הכיח construed both with ל- and את. The former means to make somebody aware of something and the latter to make somebody aware of his own true self.

Now here it says: Do not keep hatred of your brother-man in your heart but reprove him, make him realise what he has done, and this lays upon us the high duty that when anybody has wronged us, or we feel hurt or offended by somebody, either to completely forget the whole matter and not to allow it to have the slightest influence on our attitude or feelings towards him, or if we feel we cannot do this, not to let black hatred smoulder in our heart, but, by frankly speaking out, place the matter openly before him, give him an opportunity of justifying his behaviour, or of making amends for it. Silently bearing ill-will characterises a low nature. The תנחומא on Gen. 37,4, points to Absalom in this way, of whom in Sam. II 13,22, it says: ולא דבר אבשלום עם אמנון למרע ועד טוב כי שנא אבשלום את אמנון.

But at the same time הוכח תוכיח imposes the duty on every member of the Jewish community generally not to remain silent when they see their Jewish companions committing big or small sins, but to do their best by exhortation, and indeed by repeated exhortation as is expressed by הוכח in the infinitive, to effect, where possible, correct understanding and betterment (B.M. 31a). There the Gemora takes our text to impose this duty also to a teacher towards his pupil, and according to Arachin 16b, the duty continues until, by recrimination, or even by corporal punishment the pupil responds to the reproof. In Sabbath 54b, it says, that, he, who could have kept the members of his houshold, his fellow citizens, or the whole world back from sinning, and refrained from doing so, is held responsible for their guilt, and even if his own life is exemplary and blameless he gets judged and punished first of all, if he has kept himself to himself and not done everything within his power to improve his fellow-men (ibid 55a). The practical application of this law which is based on the idea of ערבות, the complete solidarity of the Jewish People for the carrying out of God’s Laws, could change the moral aspect of the whole world. But the possibility of such a complete realisation would necessitate the existence of a nation which had already reached such an ideal stage of general broadmindedness, the absence of which has been bewailed centuries ago. A Society in which every member can call the conduct of every other member to account presupposes that every one is equally prepared to accept admonition on his own behaviour. It presupposes altogether such an objective impersonal appreciation of the laws that all consideration of persons and everything personal is delegated completely to the background. Already ר׳ טרפון complained (Arachin ibid): “I should be surprised to find anybody living in our times who is ready to accept a telling-off; if he is told: “take that splinter out of your tooth”, he replies: “You take the beam out of your own eye”; אם אמר לו טול קיסם מבין שניך אמר לו טול קורה מבין עיניך. But his contemporary ר׳ אלעזר בן עזרי׳ was of the opinion that there was also hardly anybody to be found in their time who understood the art of correctly and tactfully admonishing people. For does not the Torah, in giving the duty of תוכחה, call the person to be admonished עמיתך, and the use of that term already imposes the duty of avoiding the slightest trace of any assumption of superiority. It implies that the one to be admonished must be made to feel how completely we value him as עמיתנו, as our absolute equal, and how he has quite the same right to treat us in a similar way, and that the duty which alone impelled us to approach him, applies equally to his attitude towards us. But the Torah adds even more explicitly:—

ולא תשא עליו חטא, “but lade not thyself with sin thereby”, (cf. Numb. 18,32), i.e. be careful to exercise this duty of תוכחה in such a manner that you yourself do not commit a sin thereby. Thus we find it in Arachin ibid: הוכיחו ולא קבל מנין שיחזור ויוכיחנו ת״ל תוכיח מכל מקום יכול אפי׳ משתנים פניו ת״ל לא תשא עליו חטא. Even if the admonition remains fruitless at first, one must always repeat it, but as soon as one notices by his losing colour that the admonition has made an impression, one is not to go on with it. Anything further could be an unnecessary humiliation, and causing any unnecessary humiliation, especially in public, מלבין פני חברו ברבים, is a grave sin. See ק״א in ת״כ on this verse. Rambam (הל׳ דיעות 6,8), differentiates between דברים בין אדם לחברו and דברי שמים, and thinks that the example of the Prophets teaches that בדברי שמים if private admonition has no effect, public humiliating admonition is permitted, nay, a duty.

In Beitza 30a, we are taught that transgressions of such prohibitions which are not expressly mentioned in the Torah, and which are practiced habitually, and which are done without knowing that they are wrong, and one has the certain conviction that warning them of the wrong that they are doing would have no effect, and would only result in their committing the wrong knowingly which hitherto they have done in ignorance, in such cases the duty of הוכח תוכיח does not apply, as: מוטב שיהיו שוגגין ואל יהיו מזידין. We believe we do not err in our opinion that it only speaks of a useless intervention at the time when the wrong is actually being done, or at most of an individual admonition to the sinner, but that it by no means wishes to limit a general teaching of what is right and wrong, and that this is a definite duty at all times for every one who is called on to teach, and who is able to disseminate knowledge, the more that faithful adherence to the Law suffers from ignorance. The wording of the Gemora quoted: חזינא דעבדן הכי ולא אמרינן להו ולא מידי, as well as: הני נשי וכו׳ ואזלן ויתבן וכו׳ ולא אמרינן להו ולא מידי, clearly shows that it is speaking only of the time when the wrong is actually being committed, and indeed otherwise it would mean nothing less than these laws gradually becoming considered archaic if ignorance is not to be countered by teaching as soon as it becomes the cause of habitual general law-breaking. And anyway the ריטב״א in the name of רב גדול מאשכנזים שהעיד בשם רבותיו הצרפתים ובכללם ר״י והרב מרוטנבורק, affirms (and accordingly in the name of dependable authorities), that the practical application of this rule of מוטב שיהיו שוגגין וכו׳ is only meant to be made in times in which the laws are generally strictly observed, and transgressions of them are only individual cases, but in times when מקילין בכמה דברים, laws are being treated lightly in many directions, it is a bounden duty to stand up for their protection, and to take vigorous steps to protest against all transgressions of even the מצות דרבנן until they are no longer ignored either בשוגג or במזיד, (see שיטה מקובצת ביצה thereon).

V. 18. לא תקם ולא תטר וגו׳. See notes on Gen. 4,15 & XXVII,41. We would add that in מטרה, a target, derived from the same root נטר, the underlying idea of keeping one’s attention riveted on an object for a time so as to be able to hit it is quite in accordance with the concept here of hatred kept silently within one’s heart, i.e. bearing a grudge. In the previous verse the duty was taught that whenever anybody felt themselves hurt or injured by anybody, they were not to keep silent about the matter, but to inform the person concerned about their feelings and “have the matter out”. Now the highest and most difficult task is imposed on an offended person, even if the effort to convince the offender and patch the matter up has proved fruitless, no revenge may be taken, more, the very remembrance of the wrong suffered is to be purged from one’s mind and feelings, although the other has done nothing at all to make amends. This demand is supported by the injunction for the offended party to think of his opponent as בן עמו, the duty runs: לא תקם ולא תטר את בני עמך. Just as above, the thought אחיך, the thought of the irrefutable relationship, we are all sons of the One Father, is to prevent any real hatred arising in our hearts, so the fact בני עמך is to do away with any thought of revenge. For עמך is just עם ה׳, is that national community which God had in His Eye when He said: ולקחתי אתכם לי לעם, when He made Israel into “His” People. It was just in this mutual relationship that God being the Ruler of this nation is to be shown, their behaviour towards each other is to make the foundation of universal brotherhood, the recognition of God in the whole world. The God Who has the disposition of our land, our possessions, our rights and our justice, and Who demands by שביעית and יובל, by שמיטה and רבית acts of devotion and loyalty to Him to the benefit of our fellow-men. He has also reserved to Himself the disposition of our feelings, and by לא תקם ולא תטר demands the still greater sacrifice of our feelings by submitting them entirely to the dictates of His Will, and purging them from every feeling of revenge or of bearing any grudge against our offending fellow-men.

In Yoma 23a, even patting oneself on the back, mentioning the wrong you have suffered at the moment you are returning good for evil, is reckoned as transgressing the prohibition of לא תטר, “What is נקימה, what is נטירה?” “I won’t make you a loan because you refused to make me one”, that is נקימה. “I will lend you money, I am not like you who refused me when you could have obliged me”, that is נטירה! There the Gemora demands complete forgetfulness with respect to every and any material damage suffered even if the other party has done nothing at all to atone for it. And if it is a question of honour having been injured to an extent which one may not pass over, the utmost readiness to accept apology and to forgive is made an absolute duty: דמפײסו ליה ומפײס. “God lightly passes over transgressions for him who lightly passes over offences committed against him by his fellow-men”, כל המעביר על מדותיו מעבירין לו על כל פשעיו, and “They that put up with insults, and do not reciprocate them, hear abuse and make no reply, do all their deeds in love and are happy in suffering”, of such it is said in Judges 5,31: “Those that love Him are like unto the sun, which goeth radiantly forth in all its power from all darkening clouds”: הנעלבין ואינן עולבין שומעין חרפתן ואינן משיבין עליהן הכתוב אומר ואוהביו כצאת השמש בגבורתו.

ואהבת לרעך כמוך אני ה׳, is the summarising final maxim for the whole of our social behaviour, in feelings, word and deed. The most noble fundamental feeling towards God and Man is Love. It is הב(ה) with the individualising א, and means equally giving oneself up for others and bringing others most intimately near to oneself. Both together are: Love, the opposite of שנאה (see v. 17). Now here it does not say: ואהבת את רעך, as it does everywhere else (with the exception of verse 34, the parallel verse to ours). That would entail the loving of the person of our neighbour as we love ourselves which is practically impossible to carry out, and the demand is for such love to be given to all our fellow-men. Such complete sympathetic harmony of two natures in every direction is only seldom to be found. A David did find a Jonathan, and of their love it is said: ונפש יהונתן נקשרה בנפש דוד ויאהבהו יהונתן כנפשו, (Sam. I 18,1). But what it does say here is:— ואהבת לרעך כמוך, and לרעך is not the person himself, but everything that pertains to his person, all the conditions of his life, the weal and the woe which make up his position in the world. To this, his weal and his woe, we are to give our love as if it were our own, we are to rejoice in his good fortune, and grieve over his misfortune as if it were our own. We are to assist at everything that furthers his well-being and happiness as if we were working for ourselves, and must keep trouble away from him as assiduously as if it threatened ourselves. This is something which does lie within our possibilities, and is something which is required of us even towards somebody whose personality may be actually highly antipathetic to us. For the demand of this love is something which lies quite outside the sphere of the personality of our neighbour, is not based on any of his qualities. אני ה׳ is given as the motive for this demand. It is something that is expected from us towards all our fellow-men in the Name of God, Who has given all men the mutual calling of רעים. Everyone is to find and recognise in everybody else his מרעה, “the pasturage of his life”, the furthering of his own well-being, the conditions for his own happiness in life. Nobody may look on the progress of another as a hinderance to his own progress, or look on the downfall of another as the means for his own rising, and nobody may rejoice in his own progress if it is at the expense of his neighbour’s retardment. ואהבת לרעך כמוך, the spiritually and morally perfect man only loves his own well-being as serving the same purpose as that of his neighbour. His own self-love, too, is only a consciousness of duty. He sees in himself only a creation of God, entrusted to himself to attain that bodily, mental and moral perfection for which God has designed him and placed him in his earthly existence, and for which He had given him directions in His Torah. In exactly the same way, and from the same consciousness of duty he directs his love to the well-being of his neighbour, loves him as being equally a creation of God. He proclaims his love of God, by his love to His creatures: אוהב את המקום אוהב את הבריות.

In the mouths of our sages this sentence is repeatedly used, apart from the general principle of acting lovingly for others, as an injunction for exercising humane considerations even towards criminals sentenced to death (Sanhedrin 52a and elsewhere: ואהבת לרעך כמוך ברור לו מיתה יפה), and as a maxim for husbands to be careful in sexual matters, to avoid first impressions which might have the effect of lessening mutual affection (Kiddushin 41a & elsewhere).

The saying of Hillel is well known: דעלך סני לחברך לא תעביד, “Do not do unto thy neighbour that which thou wouldst hate to have done to thee”, with which he satisfied the request of a heathen, who had asked him to teach him the Torah in the shortest possible manner, “this is the quintessence of the whole Torah, everything else is only the explanation and elaboration of this principle, now go and learn it”: זו היא כל התורה כולה ואידך פירושה זיל גמור. And actually this saying is only the negative expression of that which our text: ואהבת וגו׳, expresses as a positive duty. “Do unto your neighbour nothing that you would hate to have done to you” imposes complete equality of all, as the guiding principle of all our deeds, makes everyone take to heart the weal and woe of everybody else, changes selfishness and self-love into consideration and love of one’s neighbour, and teaches us to respect and love every contemporary as being completely equal in birth and rank. The conception חברך extends the idea beyond the narrow confines of your fellow-men to the idea of fellow-creatures, so that in fact this sentence does contain the contents of the whole Torah, which indeed is nothing else, but the teaching of avoiding everything which is contrary and hateful “סני״ to the happiness and well-being of ourselves and to that of the fellow-creatures who enjoy existence down here in this world. Only, of course, it can not leave this “סני״ — this deciding what does really threaten the true well-being of ourselves and the world about us — to the decision of the subjective, unclear opinion and feelings of the limited insight of human beings, but gives us a criterion by which to judge, which is the revelation of the Wisdom and Insight of God Himself. This is just what Hillel called the פירושה, the commentary on the עלך סני which must be learnt from the Torah. So Rashi takes it there, Sabbath 31a: אידך שאר דברי תורה פירושה דהא מלתא הוא לדעת איזה חבר שנאוי זיל גמור ותדע. (“Only by learning the rest of the Torah can we find out what is truly hateful to us” I.L.).

Of course if one translates Hillel’s saying by “That which you do not want others to do to you refrain from doing to them”, and change this wisdom into the clever social precautionary measure, “People who live in glasshouses should not throw stones”, “If you do not want other people to do you harm, then you must not do them any harm, force begets force and wrong wrong, and he who would suffer no wrong must do no wrong”. If that is what you teach, then of course, not only have you taught nothing of the contents of our Divine Torah, but you have taught nothing “ethical” at all, you have only taught calculating cleverness, and raised selfishly looking after one’s own interests to the guiding principle of all human actions.

But how little is the: זו היא כל התורה כולה ואידך פירושה, in the mouth of Hillel to be taken as just a mere figure of speech, how, deeply underlying is it, it contains a deep truth concerning the very nature of the Divine Torah, that may be shown in a striking manner just in our text. Without starting a new paragraph, without a pause, as if continuing the same theme, quite in similar mutual connection as לפני עור and לא תעשו עול, as לא תלך רכיל and לא תשנא את אחיך, it goes on from ואהבת לרעך כמוך to בהמתך לא תרביע כלאים שדך לא תזרע כלאים ובגד כלאים שעטנז לא יעלה עליך. Indeed, as this group of laws, and the accompanying law of שפחה חרופה finish up the first part of making social ethics “holy”, the text seems quite specially to point to some underlying connection between these apparently so unconnected categories of laws. They must act mutually towards forming one another and be mutually complementary to each other. And, in fact, such a connection does strike one immediately in two ways. The teachings of honesty, sincerity, truthfulness, faithfulness, conscientiousness, caution, justice, consideration of, and the care for the well-being of others in word and deed, suppressing all tendencies to hatred, together with the teachings of the highest godliness in man and complete forgetting of all wrong suffered, and finally the quintessence of making social life holy in the teaching of the most general and equalising love of one’s fellowman, all these demands for the ordering of our social life are ordered under the Divine seal “ אני ה׳״, and thereby eliminating any selfish motive of practicing them as a wise measure for reciprocal benefits. They are registered as the sole consequence of a true consciousness of God Realise God, and hence honour everything that exists and breathes as belonging to Him, as being His. Realise God, and hence the ability in ourselves to be, and our calling to be, holy, i.e. to be “Man”, having complete freedom of Will in all moral and ethical matters, and striving to imitate God in truth, in justice and in love. These two fundamental thoughts of the call for sanctifying Jewish life, “the godliness of all creatures as coming from God”, and “the higher calling of Man as coming from God”, lead us immediately upwards, out of the narrow sphere of human considerations, and teach us just in them to respect, in a higher sphere, the seal of God, the אני ה׳ stamped and imprinted everywhere in the world on His Laws; and also to be conscious of the higher kind of position in His World we have received from Him — as this is brought out in the immediately following group of laws.

V. 19. את חקתי תשמרו. We have already remarked on the foregoing verse how the transition without any break to this group of laws, points to an intimate connection which the following laws of having respect to differentiation of species in the whole organic world must have with the preceding laws of having respect for beings in the human world, yea, with the whole chapter of the sanctification of social life, to the first section of which they form the conclusion. In לא תקם ולא תטר ואהבת לרעך כמוך the humane sanctification of the human character reaches its very height. The feelings of revenge and of bearing grudge for insults or wrongs suffered are interwoven inalienably deep in the physical nature of animals. They are part of the urge for self-preservation, of that powerful self-love which governs so forcibly the animal world, with which the Creator has provided and armed each one of His creatures for its self-preservation. To rid oneself of every feeling of revenge, and of the very last spark of hatred after insult and wrong, to change love of self into love of one’s neighbour is the hardest demand made on our self-control. It takes the most energetic exercise of our moral will-power to subordinate all the feelings of our physical nature to the higher dictates of the Will of God. With its accomplishment Man bridges the gulf that divides the physical animal part of himself from his spiritual godly self, that differentiates Man from beast, and leads him to the holy height of being in the likeness of God, and near unto Him.

From the summit of these lofty demands, the Torah now makes us look into the sphere of the whole organic world lying deep beneath us, to show us that world too as a world of God’s Laws, to let every plant, every animal proclaim God with every fibre as the Lawgiver for its existence and continuance, so that we raise ourselves to the thought that if we have climbed up to the summit of making our lives holy, we have done nothing more than fulfilling the purpose for which God made us, viz., of our own free will — having been given by Him the ability and power not to do so — to obediently tread the path of His Will, a path which every plant, every animal has no option but to tread, and unconsciously, of physical necessity, to fulfil the purpose of its existence.

תקים שחקקתי לך כבר :את חקתי תשמרו, “Keep My Laws”, the laws of Nature which I established long before these laws which I am giving you now (Sanhedrin 60a; — see Gen. I). It is out of consideration of just those laws that the prohibitions: בהמתך לא תרביע כלאים etc. etc., are made.

Addressing the nation as a whole the verse begins: — את חקתי תשמרו. In other circles it is the nation which is the source of justice and which makes the laws. It, through its representatives, has the legislatory power. The Jewish nation is only the guardian of laws, the Law-giver, the Legislator is God. And it is especially these laws, חוקים שחקקתי בעולמי (Jerusalmi Kelayim 1,7), the laws on mixing species in the organic world which proclaim God as the Universal Lawgiver, and which have far-reaching application in agriculture, which were under the special care and supervision of the legal representatives of the Jewish Nation.

On the first of Adar in each year, when the seeds have sprouted and are visible above ground, משמיעין על הכלאים, the summons went forth from the courts to the owner of every field in the Jewish Land to clear his field from כלאים. And on the 15th of the month officers of the courts went out to see that the order had been carried out, יוצאין על הכלאים (Sanhedrin 1,1), so that the very sight of the fields arranged in accordance with the laws of כלאים proclaimed to everybody who sets foot on Israel’s soil: “here is the Land of the Torah, the Laws of God reign here”.

בהמתך לא תרביע כלאים. It is not impossible that רבע, related to רבה means the increase, the propagation of animals. Generally in Chaldean רבע is the equivalent of the Hebrew רבץ תחת משאו .רבץ is translated by Onkelos: כלא :כלאים .רביע תחת טועניה means to hold back, to restrain. Hence כלא, the prison. Transferred to organic creatures כלא designates creatures, who, in accordance with God’s law of למינהו (see on Gen. 1,11—13), “hold back” their powers of reproduction from every creature that is not of their species, do not mate with them. Now כלאים means two creatures who are so different to each other that Nature makes them “hold back” from each other. But as nevertheless the dual suffix ים- does not indicate just simply two, but always two belonging together, a pair — ידים ,רגלים etc., are not two feet, two hand, but a pair of feet or hands belonging together, etc. — we believe that כלאים also means going together, pairing. So that the word כלאים itself already contains the complete idea of an unnatural pairing. They are כְלָאִים closed to one another by Nature, and Man has made them into כלאים has brought them together in spite of their naturally not belonging together. By the introductory reference to חוקים שחקק במעשה בראשית whose שמירה is to be kept in these prohibitions, the prohibition of לא תרביע כלאים is extended to the whole of living creation whose organic development is kept within the limits of the Law of Species by the Word of the Creator: למינהו (Gen. 1,20—25), with which the caprice of Man is not to interfere. בהמה is only mentioned because that is the species of animal the breeding of which is a usual occupation of men, (Baba Kama 54b & 55a, תוספות ד״ה למינהו מיבשה).

שדך לא תזרע כלאים primarily forbids sowing two different kinds of seeds together. By the word שדך the prohibition of כלאי זרעים (in contrast to that of כלאי אילן), as all מצות התלויות בארץ, as a rule, all laws referring to the ground, is limited to ארץ ישראל. Only sowing different seeds indiscriminately together is forbidden. Any separation suffices which either gives each sort sufficient room below the ground to get its nourishment separately, שיעור יניקה, or some external division, above ground, which make the separation apparent to the eye, מראית עין such as ריש תור: seed A would be sown in an angle and the other seed B lengthwise in front of the angular point, A |, B ¼, or any similar differentation. By the introductory reference to the Law of את חקתי תשמרו .למינהו, the law is extended to trees also, and similarly to הרבעת בהמה, grafting different kinds of trees together, הרכבה, is forbidden. הרכבת כלאי אילן like כלאי בהמה is forbidden also בחוצה לארץ (Kiddushin 39a & B.K. 55a תוספות there ד״ה למינהו; & Sabbath 54b, Rashi תוספות ד״ה באמצע there).

The Halacha teaches that not only sowing and grafting of כלאים — and that includes any kind of propagating such growths, e.g. מנכש ומחפה, hoeing, covering over with earth, etc. — is forbidden, but even המקײם כלאים, simply having and keeping כלאים is included in the prohibition. In this respect כלאי זרעים ואילן differ from הרבעת כלאים ;כלאי בהמה is done without any action on the man’s part, it is an act which the animal does by itself, and בהמה הנרבעת is not אסורה לקײם; at the moment of הרבעה the כלאים-act is completed, while in the case of זרעים and אילן the כלאים-mixture always continues. The understanding of the citation which the Halacha gives for this Law is difficult, and the versions in which it is given differ. In ת״כ the citation runs as follows: — שדך לא תזרע אין לי אלא שלא יזרע שלא יקײם מנין ת״ל שדך לא כלאים לא אמרתי אלא משום כלאים. We have already remarked that the word כלאים itself contains the idea of unnatural pairing. Now if the prohibition had in mind only the creating of כלאים by sowing it would have run simply: לא תזרע כלאים, or to exclude לא תזרע כלאים בשדך :ח״ל. But as the text makes שדך the object of the כלאים-sowing, the chief thing that seems most important is that the field should not be allowed to have כלאים in it, לא אמרתי אלא משום כלאים, and זריעה is only secondary to it, the means by which it is brought about. The text gives the warning — שדך לא כלאים — not to endure, and certainly not to cause, our fields to mix כלאים. That this way of taking it must lie entirely in the actual construction of the verse is evident from ספרי כי תצא, where לא תזרע כרמך כלאים is also taken to refer to מקײם כלאים בכרם and in Jerusalmi Kelayim 8,2 it says similarly: כתיב לא תזרע כרמך כלאים אין לי אלא הזורע מקײם מנין ת״ל כרם ולא כלאים, The meaning of the ולא could, of course, be: your כרם, shall be a כרם, i.e. only have vines and be no כלאים but that too would come to the same way of taking it, that thereby not only the sowing of כלאים is prohibited but the whole condition of the field and vineyard is disallowed.

ובגד כלאים שעטנז לא יעלה עליך. Apart from the general rule enunciated by the תנא דבי ר׳ ישמעאל, that by the term בגד in the Torah, only woollen or linen materials are to be understood as tacitly implied (as is expressly specified above in the chapter on Negaim 13,47), where after it first mentions והבגד generally it qualifies it by adding: בבגד צמר או בבגד פשתים, on which the Gemora in Yebamoth 4b says: הואיל ונאמרו בתורה סתם בגדים ופרט לך הכתוב באחד מהן צמר פשתים אף כל צמר ופשתים, in Deut. 22,10 it definitely says לא תלבש שעטנז צמר ופשתים יחדיו, and the two sentences in the Torah complement each other further in that it is not only actual לבישה which is אסור, not only may you not clothe yourselves in garments in which there is שעטנז, but even העלאה, just placing it over any part of the body is forbidden by our verse. But by the other verse in Deut. it is not any and every העלאה which is forbidden but only דומיא דלבישה דאית ביה הנאה, as use which is similar to the purpose of clothing, warming the body, etc., but throwing שעטנז-clothes over the shoulder to carry them to some other place, or for a salesman, a מוכרי כסות to demonstrate clothes to a non-Jewish prospective buyer by putting them on his own person would be permitted (Yebamoth ibid.).

So that the Torah declares: צמר ופשתים, wool and linen, to be כלאים for use in our clothes, they mutually exclude each other. In our woollen garments there may be no thread of linen, in our linen ones no thread of wool. But such כלאים-clothes are only forbidden for לבישה or העלאה. To make them, to keep them, or to use them for other purposes is permitted Altogether the product of כלאים is אסור בהנאה only in the case of כלאי כרם (see on Deut. 22,9). Hence in Kilayim 8,1 we find: כלאי הכרם אסורין מלזרוע ומלקײם ואסורין בהנאה כלאי זרעים אסורין מלזרוע ומלקײם ומותרין באכילה וכל שכן בהנאה כלאי בגדים מותרין בכל דבר ואינן אסורין אלא מללבוש כלאי בהמה מותרין לגדל ולקײם ואינן אסורין אלא מלהרביע. In the Mishna Kelaim 9,8 it gives a double way of taking the word לא תלבש שעטנז דבר שהוא שוע טווי ונוז ר׳ שמעון בן אלעזר אומר נלוז —: שעטנז ומליז הוא את אביו שבשמים עליו. According to the ת״ק the word is an abbreviation made up out of שע (שוע, ט (טווי), נז (נוז). It would express the three processes which the raw material has to undergo to become finished thread:— combing: שוע, spinning טווי, weaving or some similar process נוז. According to ר״ת the whole prohibition only speaks of the completed formed threads and נוז would be שזירה: the twisting together of spun threads (Nidda 61,b). There is a difference of opinion in the Halacha between רמב״ם and the other פוסקים whether any one of these stages of preparation or whether all three together are required for .שעטנז דאורײתא ר׳ שמעון ב״א sees in the word שעטנז an expression of the spiritual meaning of the law of כלאים (see below).

If we consider the prohibitions classed together in this verse, viz.: כלאי זרעים ,כלאי אילן ,כלאי בהמה and כלאי בגדים all of which are introduced by the one general sentence: את חקתי תשמרו, we find that כלאי בהמה and כלאי אילן are actual interferences in the Law of Creation. Species of animals and plants which Nature has ordained “closed” to one another are forced unnaturally into union. But already in כלאי זרעים there is no such unnatural pairing of species. By simply planting the seeds next to each other there is no interference with the propagation and development of the original species. Actually, there is no objection to planting them next to each other as long as provision is made for the different kinds to be kept visibly separate when they come up above ground. It is quite evident that already in כלאי זרעים the prohibition goes further than forbidding any interference in God’s Laws of Nature regarding mating. It is rather to bring Man in his work of plant culture to the thought of the Creator’s rule of למינהו, and thereby to God Himself, the Lawgiver in Nature, Whose Lawgiving does not begin with the Jewish Nation, or even with Man, but Whose Law rules all formative force, and to Whom the smallest seedling and the tiniest fibre of all organic life yield obedience.

From that, then, continuing the same trend of thought, the Torah proceeds to כלאי בגדים. Here, even less than in כלאי זרעים can there by any idea of an actual interference with any of God’s laws of Nature. If nevertheless, for this law too, the great admonition applies את חקתי תשמרו, it can only be meant as a reminder to Man, at the moment he clads himself in human raiment to awake and keep vivid in his mind the Great Lawgiver of the World and His great law of למינהו — the Law that separates and keeps apart the countless numbers of His creations in all their manifold diversity, and assigns to each one of them a separate purpose and a separate form for such purpose. And Man, too, has been given the Law for his own mating, and is to be reminded of it especially at the time of his wearing human clothing. We have already repeatedly had occasion to remark on the deep moral importance and significance of clothes for human beings, how the Torah sees in clothes a characteristic differentiation between Man and Beast, and in them retains the admonition given through their origin (Gen. 3,21): Be ye Man, remain what ye were meant to be, and fall not into the teachings and examples of Beasts! An admonition, which, for the calling of Jewish men, receives a further special expression in the מצוה of ציצית (see the article on ציצית, reprinted from the Yeshurun 5 in the Gesammelte Schriften). We have also already remarked that the specific materials for clothes are only צמר and פשתים, so that where בגדים סתם are mentioned it means only garments made out of one of these two materials. So that just as when he works the fields, keeping the various kinds of seeds apart brings home to the thinking man the great law of למינהו, and thereby the thought of the “One Unique All-directing Lawgiver of the World”, and should admonish him to subordinate himself and all his doings likewise to the Laws of God, and warn him not to be the one creature in all God’s great universe that scorns His Laws, in the same way just keeping apart the specific materials in human clothing brings this reminder of the “Lawgiver of Species” to fulfil the moral calling of Man, the path to which is started by clothing. It is specially to remind Jewish people that in carrying out the laws of the Torah they are doing nothing more than all the non-human creatures of God do, they are merely ranging themselves harmoniously in place with all the creatures that obey God’s Laws. All around them everything attains existence, life, development, accomplishment and increase only by faithful devotion to the למינו-Law which God has set for their particular kind. To them, too, God has given their למינו-law the Law for Man’s calling in the midst of all living creatures, the Law of their Jewish calling in the midst of humanity, and only in carrying out the Torah can Jewish people discharge the task of the mission which God has appointed to them by their being born as Jews. Otherwise, to use the words of our sages: יתוש קדמך, “a gnat is greater than you”.

But a clear consideration of their relation to the human being makes the keeping apart of צמר and פשתים as materials of clothing be a yet more direct and positive expression of the pure high calling of Man, and thereby a still more precise recognition of clothes as human clothing. We have already explained on בשר בחלב (Ex. 23,19) that, just as in the organism of animals, so in that of Man, two elements are present the vegetative one of nutrition and reproduction, and the animal one of perception and movement, but Man differs from animal specifically in the respective relation of these two elements to each other. In animals the animal element: perception, feeling, and motion are used entirely in the service of the vegetative purposes, the urge for food and reproduction. In Man the vegetative is to be subordinate to the animal, and the animal to the human, to the understanding, distinguishing and self-deciding will of man, and by this to God and His holy Will. Man is a pyramid made to stand upright towards God; an animal, a self-contained sphere; in it, in the animal, the animal and vegetative elements are inimately interlaced with each other. Expressed symbolically — taking צמר as cloth-material to represent the animal and פשתים the vegetative element in the human being—in animals צמר ופשתים are יחדיו! But in Man, the animal element, mind and will power, is not to incline towards the vegetative one, is not to be closely connected with the urges of the stomach and of sexual life. In Man צמר and פשתים are to be separated, each one to be kept contained in its own separate realm. Not downwards towards vegetative sensuality, upwards towards the pinnacle of Mankind, to the understanding and godlike free-willed mind of Man, is the animal element in him to ennoble itself in accomplishing purposes which are holy to God. And so, the Spirit of God which is in Man is to elevate everything, including the animal and vegetable parts of his nature, up to the proximity of God, Whose שכינה lowers Itself down to Man in proportion to the degree which Man morally raises himself, with the whole of his being up to Him.

So that the man who attaches his animal senses and desires, not upwards to the godly, but downwards to vegetable sensuality, the man who, in the garments of his human appearance, joins צמר and פשתים together, in the degree to which he binds himself to sensuality does he tear himself away from the godly. And he also brings it about that godliness holds itself aloof from him, נלוז הוא, as רבי שמעון בן אלעזר explains the word שעטנז to mean, he is one who has “let go” of his true connection and מליז את אביו שבשמים עליו, “and also brings about that his Father in heaven Who rests Above him, lets go of him”. (נלוז and מליז as in Prov. 3,32: תועבת ה׳ נלוז and elsewhere, in Prov., also: אל יליזו מעיניך (ibid IV,21). רשב״א seems to take נז as an abreviation of נלוז and according to that שעטנז would be שעט נלוז, “one who clads himself in the character of a נלוז, of one who has abandoned God; שעט from עטה, to envelop oneself in something, עטה אור כשלמה (Ps. 104,21).

But in the way the תנא קמא takes it, which is also given in Nidda 61,b and Yebamoth 5,b, נז means firmly joined together by being woven or twisted together. To get at the meaning of נז as it is used, we find נזה as the root of הזה, to sprinkle, to splash. In the אשר יזה מדמה :קל (Levit. 6,20), and ויז מדמה אל הקיר (Kings II 9,33), to splash, intransitive. So that נז would mean splashed away, accordingly something forcibly separated from, isolated from the large mass to which it belongs. But that at once gives us the נלוז and מליז of רשב״א as the literal explanation of נז. In joining his higher part to his lower he “isolates” himself from God, and also brings it about that God “separates” Himself from him.

But in Gen. 1,4, in בדל and פתל we have already found roots in which the ideas of separating and joining form one combined conception, that by a joining, a separation is effected. So that it is not at all far fetched if in נז too, we see both joining and separating combined to one idea, in exactly a similar manner in which the idea פתיל, threads twisted together, has the underlying idea of separating in בתל בדל etc. Then the ת״ק would only be laying stress on the actual representation, and רשב״א, the spiritual representation, of the meaning of “separating”.

Accordingly נז would be the most pithy expression of a being isolating itself within itself in the same way that we found the conception of animal life in contrast to human life striving upwards towards the godly and subordinating itself to God. ש-עט-נז would then mean:— he who envelops himself in the animal-like quality of being entirely self-contained. It is accordingly a deriding of God’s Law of למינו for Man.

But the admonition to remember the “human” character, and the “human” purpose of the body is associated with העלאה and לבישה, with caring for and clothing the body, times when the body is the subject to which Man’s mind is directed, and both are associated with the historical origin of clothes and their meaning and importance with morals.

In the case of ציצית, as well as in that of the girdles of the priests, and the garments of the High Priest, the law of שעטנז does not apply. ציצית and בגדי כהונה are positive expressions of the sanctifying and subordination of the whole of the human being by and to the Torah. In this subordination to the Torah the difference between the vegetative and animal parts of Man’s nature is done away with. Encompassed by God’s Torah and dedicated to godly purposes, all phases of human life are holy to God. In the service of God’s Torah, ruled and guided by it, not only may the lower vegetative requirements of eating and sex be directed into the sphere of the higher animal activities of life, but they are to be so elevated. The תכלת thread of wool which bears the High-priestly colour of the Mikdosh, as ציצית is to be joined onto the linen garments and in the חשן ,אבנט and אפוד both צמר and פשתים are joined on a footing of equality, just as the Torah, in whose Sanctuary-service the priests stand, prescribes and values equally both חוקים and משפטים, laws governing diet and sexual life as well as those governing social life (see on Numb. 15,37 & Deut. 22,11 & 12).

V. 20. שפחה נחרפת לאיש. According to Kiddushin 6,a, נחרפת, or in the form usually used there in the Gemora: חרופה is synonymous with מקודשת. And actually there, and in Kerithuth 11a, as well as in Gittin 43a & b, the Halacha teaches that the problem our text deals with, concerns a שפחה חציה שפחה חציה בת חורין המאורסת לעבד עברי, a Canaanite slave, only partially freed, who had been betrothed to an עבד עברי by his master, who, in accordance with Ex. 21,4 can give him a Canaanite slave as wife. Had she not been given her freedom at all, the קידושין would be altogether invalid as אין קידושין תופסין בשפחה כנענית. Were she completely freed, משוחררת, the קידושין would be perfectly valid, she would be an ארוסה and any intercourse with her by an other than her affianced husband would be adultery punishable by מיתה. So that שפחה נחרפת לאיש designates a “betwixt and between” condition, she is still שפחה, not entirely free, and still נחרפת לאיש, still already sufficiently free, that by קידושין she has become attached to a man by a legal betrothal, which is binding as a marriage.

והפדה לא נפדתה וגו׳ explains the legal procedure out of which this middle condition has arisen, either her master has received only part of her redemption-money but has not yet received the whole of it; or: או חפשה לא נתן לה primarily this puts the case that the full amount for her redemption has been paid, but she has not yet received her certificate of freedom, the גט שחרור. This explanation would pass if — as actually is the opinion of ר׳ שמעון משום רבי עקיבא in Gittin 39a & b — שטר גומר בה ואין כסף גומר בה, that it is only the certificate, but not the redemption-money which completely effects her freedom, that כסף only releases her from having to work for the master, to save him ממון, but for her person to lose the status of a slave, to release her from the איסור of marriage, only the certificate can effect. But it is definitely finally decided that אין הלכה כר׳ שמעון and כסף is גומר as much as שטר, and if the full amount of money is paid, no certificate is necessary. So we think that the second case: או חפשה לא נתן לה must be understood to refer to where no money at all is to be paid, where the actual release from servitude occurs without כסף, but the personal release from the status of a slave, the release from איסור still requires a certificate of freedom: מעוכב גט שחרור, e.g. המפקיר עבדו (Gittin 38b), or יוצא בראשי איברים (Kiddushin 24b).

נחרפת: When we try to find the idiomatic use and underlying idea of the root חרף here used as an unusual synonym for קידושין we find it used as casting shame, reviling, in קל and פיעל in the word חרפה, abuse, insult, shame and as winter in the word חרֶף. On Gen. 8,22 we took the underlying meaning of חרף to be abandonment, to be abandoned, from which then חורף would be the time of the year when the earth is completely passive, and חרף would be exposing a person to shame, to deny somebody of all personality. One could then explain נחרפת here also as being given over to a man. But then this conception would mean a lowering condition, being delivered to the caprice of a man, but it designates rather a relationship which is only possible to be attained after personal independence is reached, and so the very opposite conception to חרפה must essentially be innate in it. From a careful and thorough investigation into the meaning of the phonetically related root חרב we come to the conclusion that the underlying idea of the root חרף must be, having become still, rigid, benumbed. So that נחרף ל- used as a legal term would mean one, who by union with one person has become “benumbed” towards all others, and this would aptly apply to the consequence of the betrothal act for a betrothed bride. It is similar to the term in civil law, צמיתות (Levit. 25,23), for freehold property acquired as perpetual unchanging possession, the word formed from צמת to become rigid. Here the term נחרפת is used in place of the usual מאורסת just because the incomplete freedom of the woman prevents the קידושין procedure from having the full character of אירוסין and its only effect is that any union with anybody else is אסורה.

בקרת תהיה. Tradition teaches (Kerithuth 11a) that, while in all other cases of עריות the punishment is exactly the same for both parties concerned, here, in the case of שפחה חרופה she is punished with מלקות while he has to bring an אשם as is prescribed in the following verse. This punishment of מלקות is here designated as בקרת. Already in בקר, morning, in contrast to ערב, the idea emerges of recognising the distinguishing character of separate objects. Hence לא יבקר בין טוב לרע in Levit. 27,33, to differentiate. Hence also בַקֵר, to treat something in accordance with its special requirements, to take care of, to tend, as in ומזבח הנחשת יהיה לי לבקר (Kings II 16,15). So also used specially for the care which the shepherd gives to the individual sheep of his flock: ודרשתי את צאני ובקרתים, כבקרת רעה עדרו וגו׳ וגו׳ (Ezekiel 34,11 et seq.), in contrast to the behaviour of the bad shepherd pictured in v. 4. Inasmuch as the punishment of מלקות is depicted here as בקרת, thereby making the object to be attained by this procedure to be “betterment”, it gives us the specific character of this punishment in the Jewish legal code of penalties. It gives just this one punishment a disciplinary character — all others are death penalties, so that by the term בקרת the מלקות punishment is precisely defined. All the directions given for the execution of this sentence, the choice of the instrument, of the persons who carry it out — they have to be חסירי כח ויתירי מדע, only men of little strength and great understanding! — the maximum number of stripes fixed for any case, and the most exacting medical examination of the physical condition of the prisoner, and all the other instructions given in Makkoth 22b et seq., all have very definitely the בקרת nature of punishment inflicted only for teaching and improving.

In Kerithuth 11a, two of these instructions are given special prominence: תהא בקראי, “she is read to”, i.e. while the punishment is being carried out, גדול הדײנין, the President of the Court reads to her verses from the national תוכחה (Deut. 28,58 & 59): אם לא תשמור לעשות את כל דברי התורה הזאת הכתובים בספר הזה ליראה את השם הנכבד והנורא הזה את ד׳ אלקיך והפלא ה׳ את מכתך וגו׳ וגו׳. The מכות proceeding from the human court of justice are only a warning reminder of the מכות גדולות ונאמנות of the real “blows” of God’s Justice which our transgressions bring on us and ours when our fear of God does not result in faithful adherence to His Divine Law. And further, it stresses there that בביקור תהי׳ the amount of punishment depends on an examination of the physical condition. All other punishments are given definitely, they are entirely judged as being sufficient for the crime, not the criminal. This fixing the amount of punishment for each individual in the case of מלקות shows the disciplinary nature of this punishment.

Vv. 21 & 22. והביא את אשמו. The man was the subject in the beginning of v. 20, and the sentence is only now continued in our verse 21; it reads: ואיש כי ישכב וגו׳ והביא את אשמו וגו׳. But in v. 20 the declaration concerning the woman בקרת תהיה וגו׳ is iterposed to make the imposition of an offering to be brought dependent on punishment having to be pronounced on the guilt of the woman: אם בקרת תהיה היא והביא וגו׳ ואם לא תהיה בקרת לא יביא הוא את אשמו (Kerithuth 11a). He is only חײב to bring an אשם if through him the woman committed the crime במזיד and thereby became liable to the punishment. But he has to bring the אשם also even when on his part the crime was done בשוגג, for it says in v. 22: ונסלח לו מחטאתו לעשות שוגג כמזיד :אשר חטא (ibid 9a).

This law of שפחה חרופה given in vv. 20—22 directly continues on the law of כלאים of v. 19. In looking at the development of all organic life in the animal and vegetable worlds governed by, and conditional on, God’s Law of למינו, Jewish men are warned and reminded by ובגד כלאים שעטנז לא יעלה עליך, that they too have been given a למינו-law by God, which they are to respect. They have been told that just as they must continually keep in mind the laws of “species” in the reproductive life of the animal and vegetable life which has been entrusted to their mastery, and not interfere with these laws by their caprice, in the same way they must keep continually in mind the laws governing their own reproductive powers, the laws of their own special “species” given to them by God for their higher calling as Men and Jews. They are not, by surrendering their “human-animal” nature to the calls of the “vegetable” element which is part of their being, to lower themselves to the status of an animal, and give up God and their own godly calling. In the very first place this demand has to be fulfilled in the control and exercise of that most powerful of all the “vegetable” urges, the sexual urge. In animals and plants, reproduction is kept within bounds physically, by itself; bounds which only allow themselves to be broken by the caprice of Man. Within these bounds of the same species however, freedom of mating is entirely given. In the case of Man, and still less in the Jew, the instinctive physical law does not by itself keep him within the limits which God’s laws of למינו have set for his sexual life, on the keeping of which his whole individual, family, and social calling is dependent. Just because his calling is not merely a purely physical one, for him the physical is meant to be only the under-structure of an ethical and social ideal, he is not to place his sexual life, on the purity of which all ethical and social ideals of humanity stand or fall, under the dictates of his mere physical nature, but to keep himself within the limits which God’s Laws for his sexual life have drawn from the standpoint of his ethical and social calling. We have learnt to know these laws in the פרשת עריות.

Amongst these עריות-limitations of the human למינו-laws, the one which is furthest away from the purely physical character of the למינו-limitations of all other living creations, and so shows most strikingly the higher מין-calling of the human race, is the: ואל אשת עמיתך לא תתן שכבתך לזרע by which an entirely free-willed act, and even — in the case of Jews — merely a symbolic expression of this free-willed act, makes the wife of a man a sexually unapproachable sanctuary to every other man. And it is this purely spiritual limitation — marriage — which is the foundation of all physical, spiritual and moral well-being and happiness of the great calling of Man and Nation.

Therefore, directly attached to the given laws of כלאי בגדים which are connected with those of כלאי בהמה אילנות וזרעים and, as it were, as the first result of Man’s למינו-law which כלאי בגדים represents, comes the law of שפחה חרופה to teach respect for the sanctity of marriage as the first demand of the recognition of what Man’s calling on earth is meant to be. If your sexual life is not to call your שעטנז-free human clothing a hypocritical lie, then your sexual life must be pure; above all, the married wife of your neighbour must be a sexually unapproachable sanctuary to you. That is the alpha in Man’s moral ABC. And how significant is the special case which the Torah takes to teach here, in this place and in this connection, this untouchable sanctity of human marriage; and how instructive is it according to all experience through-out the ages! It does not speak of the breaking up of a consumated marriage of people on one’s own standing — that sin has already been mentioned above in the עריות chapter — here he is not עמיתך, the girl is not yet completely אשתו, she can not yet become his wife, he is עבד עברי, she is still half שפחה, and you are a free man, you belong to the class which is that of אילי הארץ towards them (which accordingly makes you represent yourself as an איל in the אשם שפחה חרופה which you have to bring); towards them you belong to a higher class of society. Leave it to other nations to adopt the maxim that the laws of morality only apply to the “plebeians”, that the honoured garb of the upper classes is a license for sexual laxity, and above all that playing with the sexual purity and the sanctity of the marriage tie of the “lower” classes is permissable or at least excusable.

In Jewish circles, from the way of looking at life created by the Torah, the demand for a high standard of moral character rises with every rung up the social ladder, and the finer the apparel, the nobler the character of the man it covers is to be. That is why here, the girl only, gets punished if it was במזיד, if she was fully aware of the sinfulness of her behaviour, and she gets בקרת, the ordinary corrective punishment for active positive transgressions. But the man, whether it was בשוגג or במזיד, just as in the case of שבועת הפקדון where he has aggravated the crime against his neighbour’s property by חלול השם (Levit. 5,21, and see Kerithuth 9a) he has to present himself as an איל in an אשם at the entrance to the Sanctuary of the Torah, and to bring אשמו, as it significantly calls it, the expression of his “having well merited desolation and isolation” in an איל אשם. By his deliberate guilt (מזיד), or by his indifference and sin, (שוגג), he has brought a girl, who, as חציה שפחה חציה בת חורין, stood on the threshold of “freedom”, and who was חרופה לאיש, had already crossed the threshold of a moral bond of matrimony, has brought her to make a breach in that bond. And he, the “free man” should as “איל״, be the model, just in his higher social position be the one to lead, to show the path of sexual morality! He has laden himself with אשם, he has debased the moral character of the higher class of society to which he belongs, and into which the woman of his sin was on the point of entering, he has defiled that class in her eyes, and has deserved social “desolation”, being ostracised (אשם). He can only avoid this by atonement, by vowing henceforth to keep his איל-status also in the eyes of God and His Torah, to use the calling which his social position gives him in giving up all unholy selfish life (שחיטה), in devoting his life to, and in energetically striving upwards to, the heights of morality as directed by the Sanctuary of God’s Torah (קבלה and זריקה), in giving up all his sexual urges and sexual aims to be changed into directing them into purposes which are pleasing to God, and which further godliness on earth (הקטרה), and finally to sanctify his own personality to priest-like efforts and a priest-like life (אכילת כהנים), as behoves a son of the ממלכת כהנים; all which is expressed by his bringing the אשם (see on Ch. 5,14—26).

(We are not quite sure whether an עבד עברי שבא על שפחה חרופה would be חײב אשם as the צד שפחות שבה is not אסור to him. If he, too, has to bring an אשם, as seems probable, as nowhere do we find the contrary mentioned, then he would also be taken as being an איל towards the שפחה).

V. 23. וכי תבואו אל הארץ, not only לאחר כבוש, after you have taken possession, but as soon as you enter the Land (Orla 1,2), as soon as the manna ceased and Israel resumed dependence on the products of the earth for their food, the Law of ערלה applied. The כי תבואו אל הארץ is a definition of time, not of place. And, in fact, according to Kiddushin 37a, ערלה, although it is a מצוה התלויה בארץ, a Mitzva dealing with the produce of the land, is nevertheless: נוהגת בין בארץ בין בחוצה לארץ. It also applies to fruit trees planted by non-Jews and also to wild trees (Orla 1,3).

ונטעתם כל עץ מאכל: the prohibition of ערלה only applies to fruit-trees planted for the purpose of producing fruit for eating, but not, for instance הנוטע לסײג ולקורות, but not for such as are planted to serve as fences or boundaries or for timber, (ibid. 1).

וערלתם ערלתו וגו׳. We have already pointed out on Gen. 17,16 that the word ערל expresses the idea of “being checked, hindered in the use of something that is really given to the mastery of man”. But now ערל designates this idea with dual reference. It can refer to the person who is hindered in the use of something which really is subject to his dominion, so we find ערל שפתים ,ערל אזן ,ערל לב, and also the condition of complete disablement: הערל. And it can also refer to the object, adjectively ערל, or as a noun ערלה, regarding which somebody has been hindered or restricted in its normal use. So we find: לבכם הערל (Levit. 26,41); הנה ערלת אזנם (Jer. 6,10); and בשר ערלתו in פרשת מילה. Here, in our case, it occurs in both references, and that explains the otherwise completely anomalous construction יהיה לכם ערלים. For the fruit, and the condition of the tree, as long as it is not available for its normal use by its owner is called ערלה, and the man who is hindered in its use is called ערל, and his being hindered is expressed by the verb וערלתם .ערל, accordingly, means: “you are to be hindered in its use”; and ערלתו, “during a time when your use of it is being denied to you”, and this prohibition of use does not apply to the whole of the tree, but only פריו, only to its fruit; שלש שנים יהיה לכם ערלים: clearly ערלים is only an attribute of לכם, the fruit of the tree, — יהיה can refer to the one or the other, — the fruit or the tree is only ערלים to you, i.e. the fruit or the tree remains your property, no one else has any right to it, but you are ערלים towards it, you are hindered in your use of it, לא יאכל, its fruit may not be eaten.

לא יאכל. In the prohibition of אכילה the איסור הנאה is always taken to be included, unless the contrary, as e.g. at נבלה (Deut. 14,21), at טרפה (Ex. 22,30), and elsewhere, is indicated by the Torah (Pesachim 21b, ר׳ אבהו, in opposition to חזקיה who takes איסור הנאה to be indicated only when the form לא יאכל is used). Anyway, here, in our case, the איסור הנאה lies already in the conception ערלה, and by the repeated calling special attention to that conception: וערלתם ערלתו ,ערלים, the prohibition of its use is extended (ibid. 22b), even to צביעה and הדלקה, to using the fruit for dying or lighting purposes. The expression את פריו designates the fruit in its widest meaning, and includes את הטפל לפריו; pips and seeds, גרעינין, peel, קליפי ערלה, and shells which are necessary for the preservation of the fruit, שומר לפרי, are all included in the prohibition of use (Berachoth 36b).

V. 24. קדש הלולים, not absolutely קדש לה׳, but, like מעשר שני (Ch. 27,30 & 31), only in so far ממון גבוה (Kiddushin 34b), that in its use itself must be הלולים ה׳, “a reflection back to God”, a realisation of God, i.e. that its use must express the recognition that it is God, the Lawgiver of the Torah, Whose management we have to thank also for the fruit of the trees, and Whose Will should accordingly be carried out also in the enjoyment thereof. This innate destination of נטע רבעי, the fruit of the fourth year, to be הלולים לה׳ is accomplished practically by the obligation to take it up to God’s City of the Sanctuary of the Torah (similarly to מעשר שני, Deut. 14,27 & 31), and to eat it only in the environs of that Sanctuary. Alternatively it could be redeemed, with the addition of a fifth, חומש (actually a quarter of its value, Levit. 27,31), and instead of the fruit itself, whose “sacred nature” has then been transferred to the redemption-money, the money has to be taken up to Jerusalem and spent in buying food for a meal to be eaten in happiness within the purlieus of the Sanctuary of the Torah. Bringing the fruit or its redemption-money up to God’s city of the Sanctuary of the Torah expresses the recognition that the work of Nature and the success of Man’s work is no mere mechanical result of the laws of nature and Man’s application of them, but it is to the ruling and blessing of God, and Man’s free-willed submission to His Will, that thanks for success are due, and that He has made a home for the revelation of His Will in the National Sanctuary. As the Jewish National Song sings, (Ps. 133,3), that the most distant spur of the Lebanon range is still counted as belonging to the mountains of Zion, and the dew which moistens Mt. Hermon is still reckoned as falling on the hills of Zion, “because it is there (in Zion), that God orders blessing and life for ever”, so does every fruit that is brought from east and west, from south and north up to Zion express this same thought. And further, that this Sanctuary of the Law draws into its sphere of sanctifying holiness, not only one’s deeds and life of action but also one’s eating and enjoyment of life. That these are elevated to the height of a moral God-serving act is expressed by the duty to enjoy the eating of the fruit, or its equivalent bought by its redemption-money, happily in the enviroment of the Sanctuary of the Torah.

But that there is no actual innate holiness in the fruit itself, that it is only holy for serving a holy purpose, that this whole law of נטע רבעי is only a קדש הלולים, a means of expressing recognition of our acknowledging God,למען תלמד, — as it says in the מעשר שני — chapter: ליראה את ה׳ אלקיך כל הימים, “so that we learn to fear God, as our God, all the days, the days of enjoyment as much as the days of working”. This הלולים-character shows itself specially in the חילול, the fact that redemption is permitted, in certain cases even prescribed. The fruit itself can, if desired, be used at home or anywhere else as חולין, as long as their redemption value is brought up to Jerusalem in its place, and there consumed in happy enjoyment. This חילול is the most telling הילול, that the fruit comes from God, and is given to Man for serving God, in happiness and joy (see רשב״א בשם ראב״ד, on Berachoth 35a). But what this חילול expresses in deed is exactly the same that all our ברכות הנהנין express in words. Those ברכות which our sages have instituted for us to say before we eat anything, and which, according to ר׳ עקיבא (there, in Berachoth), were suggested just by this חילול = הלולים. Quite in the same way as these הלולים, our ברכות before food lay that which we are about to eat acknowledgingly at the feet of God as the נסתר ,בורא) — ,בורא: it is the שוכן בציון up to Whom the fruit has first to be brought) — and express by ברוך וכו׳, the resolution not to recede from the Presence of God by eating, but rather to enjoy the food in the Presence of God — (hence ברוך אתה), — and also in eating to serve God and further His holy purposes, as is expressed by the conception ברוך (May your wishes be fulfilled. I.L.). ר׳ אבהו in Jerusalmi (Berachoth 6a), does call the ברכה just פדיונו של עולם ומלואו.

The Law of ערלה and those of נטע רבעי are closely connected with the preceding Law of שפחה חרופה, and form one group with it and the כלאים-law that precedes it. Just as in the sexual life represented by שפחה חרופה, so in the life on enjoying food and drink which comes close to it, the moral specifically human character, which is stressed in the שעטנז-law, has to be respected and proved. The Jew waits three years before he enjoys the fruit for which he has planted the tree. And in refraining from using the fruit at God’s command, he strips himself of the rights of property before God, and so for three years he practices by this restraint the self control which is so necessary for keeping enjoyment within the limits of morality — נטיעה מקטע רגליהון דקצביא ודבועלי נדות (Beiza 25b) — by עדלה and נטע רבעי, he learns to bring even the enjoyment of his senses out of the chains of animal greed into the sphere of self-controlled, God-remembering and God-serving happiness, and so remains worthy of being a human being and near to God also in the enjoyment of his senses.

V. 26. With לא תאכלו על הדם, another fresh group starts. It does not say: לא תאכלו על דם, this would mean: do not eat with blood. לא תאכלו על הדם forbids eating with such blood that is connected with this eating. The Halacha (Sanhedrin 63a), takes this to forbid five separate procedures: (1) שלא לאכל מן הבהמה קודם שתצא נפשה, not to eat the meat of a completely correctly slaughtered animal as long as life is not visibly extict, as long as the animal is still quivering (quivering, reflex movements continue after actual death in a slaughtered animal. I.L.); (2) שלא לאכול בשר ועדײן דם במזרק, not to eat the meat of an offering while any of the blood still remains in the sprinkling-bowl; (3) שאין מבריז על הרוגי ב״ד, that the public meal (סעודת הבראה), which is given to mourners on return from the burial is not to be given in cases where the death sentence has been carried out by order of the court; (4) לסנהדרין שהרגו את הנפש שאין טועמין כלום כל אותו היום, that on the day when a death sentence is carried out, no member of the court which passed the sentence may eat anything at all, but must observe as a complete fast; (5) that these four words are also: אזהרה לבן סורר ומורה, the legal warning for the disolute gluttony of the “disobedient son” which is punishable by מלקות and מיתה (Deut. 21,20).

An example of the transgression of this prohibition: (1) is to be found in Sam. I 14,32 et seq., where the people worn out with hunger fell on to the animals in the captured booty: וישחטו ארצה ויאכל העם על הדם They slaughtered them there where they found them so as to eat at once, and so ate some of the meat, קודם שתצא נפשה, and Saul took measures to prevent such an occurrence by having numbers of animals slaughtered at a fixed place. If, as suggested in Zebachim 120a, the people dedicated these animals as שלמים, as קדשי במה, then they would also have transgressed the other prohibition; (2) which is understood by this law, and would have eaten, in their famished condition, of sacrificial meat: ועדין דם במזרק, as Rashi actually explains this verse. Regarding this second prohibition understood under לא תאכלו על הדם, we must remark that eating בשר קדשים before זריקה has been performed is in any case otherwise prohibited under penalty of מלקות by לא תוכל לאכול בשעריך וגו׳, (see Makoth 17a & b). The prohibition included here can accordingly only wish to stress the case where עדײן דם במזרק, whereas the other general prohibition applies even when e.g. נשפך הדם.

If we compare the first four procedures which here are to be understood by the prohibition of אכילה על הדם, they can all be taken to come under the idea of not “eating” under the impression of “animal” life. The muscles still quivering, quite simply represent and bring home to one’s mind “animal”-life. Blood present in the sacrificial bowl and not yet “sprinkled” on the Altar, equally represents animal life not yet having attained higher, moral, human life. One who has been condemned by a court of justice and suffered the death penalty has sunk down to animal life from moral human height. “Eating”, this function in itself belonging to the purely physical side of human beings, is already by itself inclined to stress the idea of the relationship of the nature of human beings to animals. It requires the thought of moral duty and of the higher moral calling of Man to raise it into the sphere of moral free-willed human acts. All the more then may it not be done under any impression which brings the contrary to mind, and so pushes into the background the idea of Man being master of himself and morally free-willed. Finally an eating and drinking which has sunk down to זולל וסובא, to “gluttony and swilling” as occurs in the case of the בן סורר ומורה, is itself a real “animal”-אכילה, and, accordingly, it can be understood that לא תאכלו על הדם can, at the same time, be a warning for the בן סורר ומורה. Quite in agreement with the above, the Gemora in Berachoth 10a, takes the warning: לא תאכלו קודם שתתפללו על דמכם, not to eat in the morning before one has said one’s prayers, to be also included. The body is not to be nourished before it has been dedicated in תפלה, for service to God (see רמב״ם ס׳ המצות שורש ט׳).

This לא תאכלו על הדם, is a classical example of a לאו שבכללות, i.e. a prohibition affecting several procedures which are quite different from each other, but which all come under the same underlying conception. The transgression of such a prohibition does not incur the penalty of מלקות because דלא מײחד לאויה כלאו דחסימה, because the Torah does not express the prohibition as specifically as it does in the prohibition: לא תחסם שור בדישו, to which the law of מלקות-punishment is immediately attached, and which serves as the example for it (Deut. 25,4; Sanhedrin 63a & Pesachim 41b — Regarding לאו שבכללות, and the various kinds of it see ,ספר המצות לרמב״ם שורש 9 and רמב״ן ibid.).

לא תנחשו. In Sanhedrin 65b & 66a, the נחוש here forbidden is explained as follows: — מנחש זה האומר פתו נפלה מפיו מקלו נפלה מידו בנו קורא לו מאחריו, עורב קורא לו, צבי הפסיקו בדרך, נחש מימינו ושועל משמאלו, אל תתחיל בי שחרית הוא, ראש חדש הוא, מוצאי שבת הוא, i.e. מנחש is, if for instance one says “it is unlucky today as a piece of bread fell out of my mouth, my stick fell out of my hand, my child called from behind me, a raven croaked as I passed, a deer crossed my path, there was a snake on my right and a fox on my left; or he says to the tax collector (Rashi ibid.): “It will bring me bad luck if you start just with me”, unlucky to pay out money early in the morning, or on the first of the month, or to start the week with paying out just after the termination of Sabbath, (it brings bad luck for the rest of the day, for the whole month, the whole week, Rashi ibid.). Further on there it says: — לא תנחשו וגו׳ כגון אלו המנחשים בחולדה בעופות בדגים וכדו׳, those who see omens in black cats, fish, birds, etc.

In Jeshurun 8, p. 536 we have pointed out the relationship of the word נחש to נחץ, and there we thought, that as נחץ means pushing one’s way successfully over intervening obstacles, נחש, in accordance with the general rule of the change from צ to ש in the root, would mean striving towards a goal without any consideration for the intermediate stages which may lie hinderingly in between, hence also used for the quick passing lightly over things, the slipping glide of the snake. So is every ניחוש, as in the examples given by the Halacha, a complete ignoring of the lacking intermediate stages between two completely unconnected conditions, where superstition supplies a connection between cause and effect which has absolutely no existence. Between the black cat, the raven etc., between the bit that falls from your mouth, the stick from your hand etc. etc., and the success or failure of an undertaking, the lucky or unlucky future of anybody, there is no causative connection thinkable. This can neither be the result of those occurences, nor can such occurences be taken to be the effects of some future happening starting now. Nevertheless to ascribe some influence on future happenings is just to change נחץ into נחש, is just to satisfy your urge to understand events by completely ignoring the non-existence of all the intermediate stages which would be necessary to bring about such a result.

ניחוש of this kind would simply be senseless laughable absurdity did it not at the same time involve a denial of God’s free-willed government of the world, and exercise a pernicious checking influence on Man’s free-willed activities, for which, regarding their purpose, their admissibility or their moral necessity, God has referred up solely to His Torah, as well as, regarding their practicability, to the sense of the true relationship of things which He has given us.

The delusion which is forbidden by לא תעוננו is of a similar nature. This is explained by ר׳ עקיבא in Sanhedrin 65b, as: זה המחשב עתים ושעות ואומר היום יפה לצאת למחר יפה ליקה, reckoning times and hours and predicting, “today is a good day for starting on a journey, tomorow will be a good day to make purchases, etc.”. The root of עונן would then be עון and its meaning:— time, which we meet in עונתה (Ex. 21,10), and which is common in Rabbinic Hebrew as עונה. Elsewhere we only find the root עון in מעונה .מעון, place of residence, dwelling, and if עון means that which is in Time, מעון would be the place, the point in place for that which exists in Time. But עון is also the root of עין, the spring, the source, the well. But a spring is nothing else than the particles of water coming into appearance one after the other from a contiguous mass of water in the depths. But that is precisely the conception of Time. Whereas Space encloses things contiguously together, Time is the conception of things coming “one after the other”. And עין, the eye also only conveys the impression of contiguous things one after the other to the perceiving inner mind, and it is only the perceiving mind which combines the single impressions it receives one by one, to a whole contiguous unit. The eye is “the source, the well” from which the mind draws its impressions of the physical world. If, then, עון is not Time in general, but parts of time, periods of time coming one after the other, עונן is an illusive differentiation of such times to have effect on conditions regarding which such differentiation completely lacks any reason or has any results. Only physically, and to achieve physical results by physical means, does one time differentiate from another time. But beyond that, as long as the physical conditions on which the success of our activities are also dependent are complied with, the success and the hopes for results of our efforts depend solely on the Yea or Nay of their complying with the laws of God’s Torah, and on the support and assistance of God, which can be hoped for accordingly. Like in all superstition, all ניחוש, in מעונן too, there lurks a denial of God’s free-willed direction of events, and a placing of Man’s morally free-willed activities under the influence of Man-created erroneous conceptions of strange outside powers.

In Deut. 18,10, מעונן ומנחש occur in connection with ,קוסם קסמים מכשף etc., etc., and there the pernicious aspect of these errors on our relationship towards God is stressed. Here, placed in the sentence with לא תאכלו על הדם, it is the danger which all three generate to the higher character of the moral nature of the human being which is the reason for their being placed together in one dictum of the Torah. Just as לא תאכלו על הדם takes Man, morally free-willed Man, in his activity which is nearest to the purely physical, אכילה, and teaches that this, even this, — and thereby the whole nature of Man — is to be separated from הדם, from the impression of a purely physical “unfree animal life; so לא תנחשו ולא תעוננו, in truth is fundamentally nothing but the further consequence of this separation. Only a man who is אוכל על הדם, who puts himself on a level with animals in feeding, and who, when he eats, only sees the animal in himself, he, similarly to המנחש והמעונן, may believe in what he does or does not do, with his fears and hopes for the future that he is subject to some physical-mechanical blind force that governs the world. But he who is not אוכל על הדם, who, even in eating, remains a human and morally self-willed and self-controlled servant of God, the consciousness of the moral ideals of his being, raises him high above the whole realm of a conception which buries the world under the government of dark physical mecanical powers of the night. He stands, with all that he does, or refrains from doing, before the clear dictates of the moral laws of God’s Torah, not under mechanical-physical powers, but under the loving, caring and just government of God. For him cats and snakes and raven-croaks and falling sticks have no dread meaning, he knows only one fear — sin, only one trust and reliance — keeping the מצות; the consciousness of this duty is his whole policy — הולך בתום ילך בטח — and sharply does he differentiate between the physical laws of nature given for the physical world, and the free untrammelled government of God, under which God has placed him.

Als Beispiel von מעונן führt ר׳ עקיבא (daselbst) noch auf: לימודי ערבי שביעיות חטין יפות עקורי קטניות מהיות רעות, das dem Erlassjahr vorangehende Jahr pflegt guten Weizen zu haben, Hülsenfrüchte pflegen "dann" vor Missraten geschützt (eigentlich entrückt) zu sein. (Nach Raschi: wenn sie עקורים, ausgerissen und nicht geschnitten worden Jedenfalls scheint diese Bauernregel sich auch auf ערבי שביעיות zu beziehen, sonst fiele sie ja nicht unter מחשב עתים). Wir wären damit auch vor der entgegengesetzten Verirrung gewarnt, rein gesetzlichen Verhältnissen keine ihnen fremdartige, in keinem Zusammenhange mit ihnen stehende physischen Einflüsse zuzuschreiben. Daß dem z. B. das שיפורא גרים (Nidda 38a) nicht widerspricht, ist von selbst klar. Noch viel weniger das וצויתי את ברכתי לכם בשנה הששית (Kap. 25, 21), wo Gottes freie Segenspende für das dem Jobel vorangehende sechste Jahr zugesagt ist, während jener מחשב עתים dem sechsten Jahre eine physisch magische Eigentümlichkeit unterlegt.

The Halacha further takes אחיזת עינים, occular illusions, sleight-of-hand pretending to be magic, to be forbidden as coming under the heading of לא תעוננו. This would then prohibit us to have any idea of magic being able to accomplish anything outside and beyond natural cause and effect even only in appearance.
