According to this application of it עון would be taken to be the root of עין and עונן would be deceiving the eye, similarly to that which we understood under the לטים and להטים of the Egyptian magicians.

V. 27. From the admonition to keep ourselves conscious of the higher moral dignity which being human entails which the Torah introduces into our eating and our general active life by: לא תאכלו על הדם לא תנחשו תעוננו, it progresses to those activities which we perform on our human bodies, there to awake and nuture the same feelings. For that is the spirit of making Jewish lives holy, what it tries to avoid most is thoughtlessness, it wants even the smallest acts to be done thoughtfully. It grasps any and every opportunity in our daily life to keep those ideas, those truths that should form the whole underlying foundation of what we are and what we should be, ever more and more awake in our minds; so that from them we learn to make the way we do all our actions and the purpose we aim at by our actions worthy of our calling, and productive for it. To that spirit a Man is only a Man when he thinks, and to the thinking man nothing is too small to be worth considering.

Also when our purpose concerns our outward appearance, and we treat our hair and beards to make a pleasing impression in our social contacts, it lifts up a teaching finger and says: לא תקיפו פאת ראשכם ולא תשחית פאת זקנך.

הקיף means: to move in a circle round about something, or to make a circle round about anything: והקיף את העיר פעם אחת (Josh. 6,3); ויקיפו על העיר (Kings II 6,14). It is synonymous with סבב, but there must be some slight difference in its meaning as we find: סבו ציון והקיפוה (Ps. 48,13). It seems that סבב is to go round generally, even at a distance whereas הקיף is closely to enclose. In rabbinic Hebrew the word is used for the close approximation of things by itself, leaving out the idea of encirclement. For there הקיף also means bringing two things closely together for comparison or other purpose, מקיפין בבני מעײן (Chulin 50a); אין מקיפין שתי חביות (Beitza 32b); וכי נחשדו חברים לתרום שלא מן המוקף Gittin 30b). The meaning of placing next to one another for comparison also occurs in the word קוף ape. The Halacha teaches (Makkoth 20b), פאת ראשו is סוף ראשו and הקפת פאת ראשו is זה המשוה צדעיו לאחורי אזנו ולפדחתו, making the hair at the temples level with the hair behind the ears. פאת הראש is accordingly where the hair of the head ends at the temples and which marks the division of the forehead and front of the head from the back of the head. Removal of this hair at the temples does away with this division and allows the forehead and the back of the head to run in one line. As thereby the whole head is encircled by a continuous line of hair — הקיף, too, in the תנ״ד, as we have remarked, only means going round, encircling, — it seems most likely that here, too, הקפת הראש could be explained as rounding off the head by removing the פאות. But then the prohibition should rather run:— לא תקיפו ראשכם, as the הקפה would refer to the head and not to the פאה. It is accordingly not impossible that לא תקיפו here is to be taken in the sense of having the meaning which is not uncommon in rabbinic Hebrew, of putting something next to something else. By removing the hair at the temples the forehead and the back of the head are united, and the משוה צדעיו וגו׳ would be the literal explanation of לא תקיפו פאת וגו׳: “You shall not make the hair of your heads level at the two side-ends”. There is no indication of limiting this prohibition to the use of any particular method. What is prohibited is the effect, the making level. According to תוספות (Shebuoth 2b), and the רא״ש any removal of the hair, with scissors or otherwise is equally forbidden. רמב״ם takes this prohibition, too, like the פאת זקן, to apply only to the use of a razor.

ולא תשחית פאת זקנך. For פאת זקן, the Mishna (Makkoth 20,a), describes שתים מכאן ושתים מכאן ואחת מלמטה, two on each side and one below, five “corners” accordingly on the beard of the cheeks and chin. The exact position of these places of these פאות זקן is not sure, so that conscientiousness ordains that one must refrain from השחתה of the beard on the whole of the cheeks and chin. Regarding the hair of the beard, the Halacha is quite definite: אינו חײב עד שיטלנו בתער, that only shaving with a razor is prohibited, but not with scissors. For לא תשחית פאת זקנך finds an explanation by its being repeated for the כהנים with the words: ופאת זקנם לא יגלחו (Ch. 21,5). So that the prohibition is limited by two conditions: גלוח and השחתה. Only גלוח שיש בו השחתה is אסור, shaving with the instrument usually used for that purpose (גלוח), and which removes the hair level with the skin (השחתה), these two conditions are only fulfilled by the razor: הוי אומר זה תעד (Makkoth 21a).

Let us try and get at the underlying thought which these two prohibitions want to express and bring home to us. לא תקיפו פאת ראשכם clearly forbids the removal of the externally visible division between the frontal part of the head and the rear part of it, coinciding with the cerebrum and the cerebellum respectively. This division is in a fissure which runs vertically between the forehead and the parietal bone, above the temples in front of the ears. The hair at the temples is accordingly a natural veiling which hides the view of the back of the head in the human countenance. But the relation of the frontal part of the skull containing the cerebrum to the back part with the cerebellum is that of the human element to the animal element in human beings; and so here again we meet the importance and weight which the teaching of the sanctifying of our lives lays on keeping vividly in our minds the existence of these two specifically different elements in Man’s nature, and of the higher dignity of the intellectual moral spiritual factor to which the animal factor has to subordinate itself and be kept in the background. It is in the former alone in which Man is to recognise his appearance as Man. The hair down the temples is an admonition for a Man to be a Man.
Hair at the temples is present in both sexes of the human being, and at all ages. The countenance of the human child is already graced with this emblem of its spiritual moral calling.

But it is in a similar relation to that of the front and back of the head that the upper jaw stands to the lower; the lower, with cheek and chin, to the maxilla and the rest of the upper part of the human face. Whereas the latter pertain primarily to the spiritual intellectual activities of the mind, and, at the animal activity of eating hold themselves more passive, the lower jaw, with teeth, tongue and masticatory muscles are the real active factors at this more animal function of eating and tasting. As they come to sexually mature age, the male sex, who are more inclined to sexual depravity than the female, have beards growing which cover the parts of the face which are active in satisfying the senses. Beards covering these parts leave only the purely spiritual intellectual human face exposed to view, and thereby bring the admonition quite specially to “man” to show his worth and his strength only in spiritual values, and to master all the urges of his senses, and to keep them modestly and decently in the background, an admonition which women, thanks to the innate modesty of their nature require much less. We presume that the פאות הזקן must be just those places, such as the joint between the lower jaw and the bone, the posterior corner of the chin etc., which show the action of eating and mastication most clearly. Accordingly, as nevertheless the “Law for sanctifying our lives” permits the shaving of the beard in general, it seems to take just the moment when a man is occupied with the hair on his face to give himself a pleasing appearance, to admonish him, by making him forego the use of a razor, (גלוח), to use these “פאות הזקן״ as a reminder not to destroy (השחתה) this hair which veils the “sensual part” of a man’s countenance, and to take to heart the lesson it preaches, not to trifle away his manly calling, and his worth as a human being by thinking too much of, and overrating the value of the material value of the senses.

But as the Father of the human race already at its formation showed the innate more modest nature of Woman by the fact that He could, in her case, dispense with the veil of hair on the cheeks, so, not only the law of לא תשחית פאת זקנך, but also the לא תקיפו פאת ראשכם, only applies to the masculine sex (Kiddushin 29a).

We have already remarked above that the wording of the text is in favour of the opinion that הקפת פאת הראש is אסור in every way whereas השחתת פאת הזקן is limited to תער. This assumption would also explain the peculiarity that לא תקיפו פאת ראשכם in the plural is addressed to the national community consisting of all its members, while לא תשחית פאת זקנך speaks to the individual. For if הקפת פאת הראש is cutting of the hair at the temples in any way, בין בתער בין במספרים, refraining from doing this gives a striking characteristic appearance to all men of the Jewish nation. They, as bearers of the common national calling, express, already in their external appearance, this calling as being the mission of intellectually moral subordination of, and decently veiling of, all that pertains to the senses. Observing the prohibition of השחתת פאת הזקן does not show itself so strikingly. Other people can not notice so easily whether it is done במספרים or בתער. So that לא שחית פאת זקנך remains more of a silent reminder for each personal individual himself to take to heart the lesson that he is to understand his physical manhood only in the light of his spiritual and moral calling, and to act only in a way that is worthy of that calling.

V. 28. שרט is any kind of wounding, even merely grazing or scratching, whether done by the hand alone or by means of an instrument. This wounding is only prohibited to be done on account of a death but not if done for any other loss. Five שריטות for one death, or one שרט for five deaths would count as a fivefold transgression of this prohibition (Makkoth 20b). This law can be indicated by the wording of the text. It does not say: ושרט בבשרכם לא תתנו לנפש, but: ושרט לנפש etc. Thereby, שרט is connected directly with נפש, so that the prohibition repeats itself with each נפש.

כתבת קעקע is an inscription so deeply impressed into the flesh that it remains permanently, — tattooing. According to Rashi (really ר׳ יהודה בן נתן, his pupil and son-in-law who wrote the commentary on the last pages of Tractate Makkoth, Makkoth 21a). כתבת is writing on the skin with some dye, and קעקע is puncturing the skin with a needle or lancet by which the dye penetrates under the skin and the inscription becomes permanent.

When we consider these two prohibitions more closely we notice that it does not say: ושרט לא תשרטו, but: ושרט לא תתנו בבשרכם, so that the Torah wants to forbid not as much the act of שריטה, but rather the existence of a שרט לנפש in our flesh which this act brings about. Therefore, we think, the prohibition is not, simply expressing the loss we have sustained by wounding ourselves, inflicting pain on ourselves. This forbidden שרט לנפש seems rather to have a similar meaning to the prescribed קריעה על מת. If the rent in our garment expresses our acknowledgment that the departure of the one who has died has made a “rent” in the closest surroundings, the intimate world, of those left behind, then a cut into our flesh would express the thought that with the death of a relation our own bodily self has suffered a breach, — and that is not to be. However dear and valuable, however important the existence of somebody else may be to us, our own importance and our own worth may never end with the end of his existence, may never even be allowed to lessen. Every person has his own importance and meaning for God in his existence here below. Every fibre of our bodily existence belongs to God, every spark of power with which He has endowed us, and every minute of our life, all is His. For as long as He directs our existence down here to last, we have to hold out to the end, and serve Him with all our might, and may not diminish our strength of our own free-will. Just the homegoing of one who is important to us must rather incite us to double energy to try to fill out the gap in the service of God’s work on earth which the death has caused.

But the connection which שרט לנפש has also with חדידה לע״ז (Makkoth 21a), does nevertheless make it possible that this prohibition comes also to oppose a pagan idea which, in spite of the fall of the so-called heathen nations, has not altogether vanished from people’s minds. The heathen conception regarded Death as a Power which, inimical to human life found pleasure in the death of human beings. By self-inflicted wounds and mutilations, even by the offering of human sacrifices, those that remained paid homage to this Power thirsting for human life, and believed that by this homage they could divert a similar fate from themselves and others. Jewish Truth teaches something different, and Jewish recognition of it has to believe otherwise. “ אני ה׳״: To it, Death and Life come from One Loving Hand, to it, both stand in the service of One Living and animating God. Death leads out of life to life, out of being here to being there; here as there, a realm of the One God of Life and Love. The life of those who go on living is equally His Will as the death of those that die. שרט לנפש, self-wounding on account of the dead, throwing your life, or even only a particle of your life, after that which had died away, is no homage, it is a wanton offence against the Hand which led your brother to death. For it is just this Hand that wills that you live, live for its service until It calls you also away; every fibre of your bodily existence is holy unto It: ושרט לנפש לא תתנו בבשרכם — אני ה׳!

וכתבת קעקע לא תתנו בכם, not בבשרכם, but בכם, an inscription tatooed on you, places the whole of yourself in the service of that which is designated by such inscription, and you are holy to God, belong exclusively to Him: אני ה׳. Indeed in Makkoth 21a, this prohibition is taken: אינו חײב עד שיכתוב שם של עכו״ם, but then all other inscriptions are taken as being implicitly included in the prohibition (see Rashi there), so that even the very opposite, שם ה׳, would come under the prohibition of tattooing. The human body has already the stamp of belonging to God, and of consecration, by its very form made in the likeness of God, ומבשרי אחזה אלוה (Job 19,26); tattooing לה׳, on it would designate as something which we have decided of our own free will which really is the natural calling for which God made Man, and which is so to be regarded by us. Our belonging to God, our being לה׳ is something which is given to us by our birth as human beings, it is the essential fact that must decide and guide all that we do, it is not to be something that only emerges from some act of our own.

If we connect up the six detatched sentences of this group, we find the four last ones a further extension of the two first ones, and all together they serve as a constant realisation of two fundamental facts, viz.: that Man has a moral dignity to uphold, and that his whole being and fate is submitted exclusively to God. לא תאכלו על הדם finds its further extension in demonstrating on the human body itself its higher moral calling in לא תקיפו פאת ראשכם and לא תשחית פאת זקנך; just as our placing our fate exclusively in the Hands of God, as expressed in לא תנחשו ולא תעוננו finds its natural consequence in the prohibited שרט לנפש and כתובת קעקע.

These two facts, taken together, our high moral calling, and the blossoming or the reverse of our fate in life depending on our living up to this calling or not, are thrown into bold relief in the admonition which immediately follows:— אל תחלל את בתך וגו׳ וגו׳.

V. 29. In the preceding group, the higher moral calling of the human being demonstrated in פאת ראש and פאת זקן on the body itself, was directed only to the male sex. The Torah presumes an inborn greater degree of chaste modesty and morality in Woman, so that there is no necessity for such special reminders. In general it is not from women but from the degeneration of the male sex that morality sinks. If the Law succeeds to save the morality of the men, the moral nature of the women will by itself keep it within the limits of decency and morality.

This fact already implied by the preceding laws, receives here in our v. 29, its most momentous significance. אל תחלל את בתך להזנותה, says God to the Jewish fathers, and, at the same time — as ת״כ points out on this sentence: יכול על מעשה יחידי ת״ל ומלאה הארץ זמה ולא על מעשה יחידי — it is addressed to the Jewish Nation, and the term אל תחלל assumes as a most significant fact the “holy” nature of Jewish daughters — unless led astray. The daughters of the Jewish Nation are “holy” in well-behaved modesty. If they degenerate into immorality, the sons of the Jewish nation, the fathers, the men, are to blame. In connection with the preceding verses, this is what it would express: — if only for the sake of your daughters, keep the sensuality of your bodies holy! The responsibility for the degeneration of the daughters rests as a heavy guilt on the way of life and the example of the fathers. So, in Ch. 21,9, we find the immorality of a daughter of a priest reflected back on the priestly father, את אביה היא מחללת; so, in Deut. 22,21, the punishment of the immoral daughter is carried out אל פתח בית אביה, at the gate of her Father’s house; so, Hosea says in Ch. 4,14: לא אפקוד על בנותיכם כי תזנינה ועל כלותיכם כי תנאפנה כי הם עם הזונות יפרדו ועם הקדשות יזבחו ועם לא יבין ילבט, “I will not punish your daughters when they commit whoredom, nor your daughters-in-law when they commit adultery; for they themselves go apart with the whores, and they sacrifice with the harlots; a people that doth not understand the consequences will have to bear the punishment”.

According to ת״כ and Sanhedrin 76,a, this prohibition refers to giving your daughter up to leading an immoral life: במוסר את בתו שלא לשם אישות. But nevertheless it also says definitely in ת״כ that the prohibition applies to any and every extra-marital sexual intercourse and pre-marital intercourse etc.: חילול שהוא לשם זנות ואיזה זה זה המוסר לחברו בתו פנויה שלא לשם אישות וכן המוסרת עצמה שלא לשם אישות, and ר׳ אליעזר points out there how the Torah uses the same word for extra-marital intercourse זמה as it uses for incest, and although the Torah does not impose the same penalty to be imposed by the human court, before the Divine Court it is punishable to the same degree. (There it says on ואיש אשר יקח, (Ch. 18,17); מנין שהוא ענוש לפני המקום כבא על אשה ואמה נאמר כאן זמה ונאמר להלן את אשה ואמה זימה היא מלמד שהוא ענוש לפני המקום כבא על אשה ואמה (פי׳ הק״א לענ״ד לא יתכן דהא נושאין על האנוסה ועל המפותה). For although, in Ch. 21,14, referring to the marriage prohibitions for the priests, the conception זונה is taken in its narrower sense, and restricted solely to cases where no legal marriage can take place: שנבעלה לאדם שהיא אסורה להנשא לו, so that there the Halacha is not in accordance with ’ר׳ אליעזרs opinion that the character of a זונה applies also to the ביאת פנוי על פנויה שלא לשם אישות (Yebamoth 61,b), still the conception of the term זנות does, in general, and here too, include every sexual intercourse outside marriage (see Mizrachi and Korban Aaron, thereon).— ולא תזנה הארץ: The earth, as an astronomical body, may have its own telluric and cosmic meaning and importance. The fruitful upper surface of the earth is “adamah”, is wedded to the human race. If men break their moral faithfulness, the earth breaks its faithfulness to men. If men play about with the noblest product of the world, human seed and human fruit, then the womb of the earth, too, refuses, becomes stunted, deterisrates seed and fruit, מזנים הם לפירות ר׳ יהודה אומר הרי הוא אומר ותחניפי ארץ בזנותיך וברעתך וימנעו רביבים ומלקוש לוא היה וגו׳, (ת״ב, Jer. 3,2 & 3).

ומלאה הארץ זמה, as this is not the result but the cause of the preceding: ולא תזנה הארץ, the ו of ומלאה must express the simultaneousness, the coming of these two moments at the same time. Similarly to הלא אזן מלין תבחן וחך אוכל יטעם לו (Job 12,11), “the ear tests the words as the gums taste the food”; or: כי אדם לעמל יולד ובני רשף יגביהו עוף (ibid V,7), “that Man is born to trouble as the sparks fly upwards”.

The בה״ג, however, reckons ולא תזנה הארץ as a separate prohibition. This would then still refer to general debauchery. The land, i.e., the general impression of its inhabitants is not to become immoral, and this would then be, as the רמב״ן explains it, a warning for all who practice immorality, whereas אל תחלל is a warning for fathers against bringing about an immoral life for their daughter. Then ומלאה הארץ זמה would be a still further result: finally the whole country would be full of incest.

V. 30. This group of laws began in v. 26 with לא תאכלו על הדם and לא תנחשו ולא תעוננו. Then לא תאכלו וגו׳ would receive an extension in לא תקיפו and לא תשחית; and לא תנחשו וגו׳ in ושרט לנפש וגו׳ וגו׳. The purely symbolic warning against lowering the dignity of the high moral status of Man above Beast as given by לא תאכלו על הדם receives its actual realisation with the אל תחלל וגו׳ of v. 29, with the banning of all זנות from Jewish circles; the absolute reverse of נחש and מעונן is now expressed by את שבתתי תשמרו, and in את מקדשי תיראו. For, taken in its general meaning, את שבתתי תשמרו offers the most complete contrast to, is the exact opposite of לא תעוננו; and ומקדשי תיראו of לא תנחשו. Not the difference in times for undertaking activities, as taught by the מעונן-illusion, but My שבתות, — the times that I have ordered your conscientious observance of abstaining from work — are what you have to take into consideration, for work undertaken on those times you can expect no blessing. For אני ה׳, in My Hand lies the blessing of your future. And equally so: Have no fear of infringing on those things that the ניחוש-illusion teaches as being lucky or unlucky, but מקדשי are you to fear, fear to sin against the regime taught by My Sanctuary; only by keeping to it will you find your “luck”, only infringing it brings misfortune and unhappiness; for אני ה׳, it is I Who have instituted this Sanctuary to sanctify yourselves and your doings, it is in My Hands that blessing or the reverse lies.

In Yebamoth 6,a & b, two things are taught from this juxtaposition of שמירת שבת and מה שמירה האמורה בשבת לא משבת אתה מתײרא —:מורא מקדש אלא ממי שהזהיר על השבת אף מורא האמורה במקדש לא ממקדש אתה מתײרא אלא ממי שהזהיר על המקדש; And further: אין לי אלא בזמן שהב״ה קײם בזמן שאין ב״ה קײם מנײן ת״ל את שבתותי תשמרו ומקדשי תיראו מה שמירה האמורה בשבת לעולם אף מורא האמורה במקדש לעולם. First, the important injunction not to make our honouring the Sanctuary an honouring of the building to a fetich-like worship of the wood and stone, but just as our keeping the Sabbath holy is not meant to be directed to the day itself, but to God, Who ordered the institution of the Sabbath, so in honouring the Temple we are not to let our thoughts be directed to it, but to God Who ordered us to keep the Temple holy.

And further, just as the Sabbath, by its very nature, is eternal, and so is not bound to any particular age or conditions, so, also, the place of the מקדש has not, by the destruction of the Temple lost any of the מורא which is due to it. The place which God chose to be the permanent home of His Sanctuary remains for ever holy to that purpose. Inasmuch as even today we are not allowed to erect an altar to God anywhere else, it is, today, and at all times, the invisible, but strong bond of union which joins all those who honour as the Law of their lives, the Torah, to be the Sanctuary of which God had dedicated that place. And just as it is thither that our dearest recollections of the past turn, so also are the most ardent hopes and wishes for our future — together with the hopes for the future of all mankind, for whom the salavation of the whole world through the Torah will come — attached to that place. And so, in the words of the Prophet, it remains “a throne of the Glory of God, higher than ever, this desolate place of our Sanctuary”, (Jer. 17,12): כסא כבוד מרום מראשון מקום מקדשנו. The visible Temple only held the nation together within the narrow limits of Judea. But the invisible idea, which the undying meaning of this place over the ruins of their Temple lights up in the minds and hearts of Judea’s scattered sons, is the invisible bond of union, which, across the wide continents of the world, holds these sons, powerfully and unshakeably together in a common mission, in the present, and for a common hope for the future.

And so the laws which kept טמאים out of the מקדש and its precincts (see on Numb. 5,2 et seq.), are still in force today. Even today, even if a person were טהור nobody may go on the הר הבית, the mount of the destroyed Temple, במקלו במנעלו בפונדתו ובאבק שעל רגליו, with his stick, his shoes, his girdle-pouch, or with dust on his feet, nor may he use the הר הבית as a “short cut”, just to pass through it: ולא יעשנו קפנדריא, just as all these were forbidden while the מקדש was still standing as coming under the heading of the מורא מקדש here enjoined (Yebamoth 6,b; Rambam, הל׳ בית הבחירה 7,7; & כ״מ on 6,14).

Vv. 31 & 32. From Sanhedrin 65,a & b, we learn that אובות and ידעונים are oracles connected with invoking the dead. According to תוספות there, and also the corresponding Jerusalmi, as well as according to רמב״ם (הל׳ ע״ז 6,2 & 11,14), what is to be understood here is the practising of such oracles, of which, in Ch. 20,6 it is said that they incur the punishment of כרת, and in v. 27, of סקילה, whereas הנשאל בהם consulting them is only באזהרה, is simply forbidden, (Deut. 18,11: לא ימצא בך וגו׳ וגו׳, ושואל אוב וגו׳) — (נשאל is the one whose affairs are enquired about from the אוב through the בעל אוב. He is the object of the consultation. תוספות י״ט on the Mishna leaves the explanation of the term undecided. We find a similar term used in connection with נשאל על נדר :נדרים, hence also the expression מיתשאיל עליה, and this also can have the meaning, to consult oneself. More probably, however the expression gives the precise idea of the whole procedure. The חכם has no power to absolve or to bind. He is not asked, but has only to ascertain by questioning, and to find out in the conditions themselves, the reason for release. So that the one who stands before the חכם with his vow is the נשאל, the interrogated one. Possibly in our case of שואל אוב, the Mishna uses the term נשאל in the same way, and indeed ironically. Actually the one who is seeking replies from the oracle is himself giving them. The “asker” is the “asked”. It is only by clever questioning that the soothsayer can give the illusion of obtaining pertinent replies from the oracle. Actually the soothsayer is told more about the circumstances etc., of the enquirer than the latter gets told from the soothsayer). — But according to Rashi Sanhedrin 65,a on the Mishna, אל תפנו is the admonition for the נשאל and לא ימצא for the one who sets up and manages the oracle.

אל תבקשו לטמאה בהם. Unless we are mistaken, the word טמא here is in the sense of its real original meaning, which, as we have so often indicated, is nothing else but the conception of “subjection”, lack of freewill, having no choice, which is at the roof of its phonetic relation to ,טמע דמה ,דמע, all of which have the meaning of losing one’s independence. The erroneous conception of these oracles “seek”, try — by vigorous bodily movements, dancing, gyrating, by narcotic fumes (in speaking about בעל אוב, Sanhedrin 65,a mentions הקשת זרועותיו and הקטרה לשד), or other means — to lose all their own powers of thought or feeling, so that, deprived of all their own senses, they fall under the power of the oracle-giving spirit, and serve as the completely passive medium for it. This would be the “mental” טומאה, which the בעל אוב “seeks”. But the נשאל “seeks”, “moral” טומאה. He does not wish to place the decision for what he is to do and for what he is not to do under the dictate of the Word of God, Whose laws for human behaviour are addressed to the clear wakeful mind, nor under the dictates of his own thinking brain which has grasped and understood God’s Will from this Word. But, with all his mental moral free will, with his God-like freedom of action, he places the decision for himself and his acts under the dictates of some supposed dark mysterious power, which itself belongs to the unfree “bound” realm of nature, so that he “seeks”, he asks, to become טמא.

But both, the mental and moral טומאה which is sought by אוב וידעוני and in consulting them, are the absolute opposite of that קדושה which forms the contents of this chapter, and which is nothing other than the freest placing, — with complete consciousness of what one is doing, and completely of one’s own freewill, — the whole of oneself and one’s actions ready for the dictates of God’s Will as revealed in His Torah.

That is why the previous verse had already contrasted the לא תעוננו and לא תנחשו of the verse introducing this group with its את שבתותי תשמרו ומקדשי תיראו; and now this group concludes with the אל תפנו אל האובות of this verse and the מפני שיבה תקום etc., of the following verse, in which both together reach the high point of the whole.

For מפני שיבה תקום etc. is again the complete positive opposite to שיבה .אל תפנו אל האובות (from שיב, related to שגב, to attain a lofty aim) designates ripe old age. Job 12,24: יחשב תהום לשיבה, where the foaming floods following the wake of the Leviathan are compared to שיבה proves that שיבה also designates the hoary head which shows old age. In the same way עטרת תפארת שיבה (Prov. 15,31), may be understood, and so in several other places. Kidushin 33,a teaches the Halacha that by the term שיבה, an old man is to be understood, and by זקן not old in years but in intellectual accomplishments, “old”, mature in wisdom: זקן זה שקנה חכמה (see on Gen. 24,1), a quality that was also a decisive factor in choosing the “elders”, the זקני העם, the שבעים זקנים. Here, where it is mentioned next to שיבה, by זקן only חכם is to be understood, even יניק וחכים, even a young man if he is mature in wisdom. Our text demands קימה and הידור, rising to one’s feet, and generally showing honour, for both. For שיבה an honourable old age (תוספות ibid 32,b), which, according to Prov. 15,31 is attained by a life spent in faithfulness to duty בדרך צדקה תמצא, as well as for זקנה for maturity of wisdom which has been obtained by the study of the Torah. Thus experience, i.e. natural common-sense, human knowledge, gained and matured by the repeated events of life and nature, and wisdom, i.e. a true estimation of life and nature regarding them as coming from God, as designed for a purpose by God, and having meaning for our mission in life are both to be honoured. To them, — experience and wisdom — to the clear circumspect human understanding which matures by experience, and the spirit of God which speaks out of the Torah, are we to pay due tribute, and when we meet their representatives, in “old men” and “wise men” we are to show our homage by rising and giving honour to them.
But this is the positive opposite to אוב וידעוני.
Paying attention to the Oracle of some imagined unfree Power of the Night, placing the exalted morally free human being under the ban of blind sophistry is טומאה, and leads to טומאה.

The clear bright human mind and the wisdom of God, which He has laid down in the תורה for its instruction, they, which God has appointed to be exclusively our guides; they are only to be found on the way of קדושה and lead to קרושה.

Hence: אל תפנו אל האבת ואל הידעונים אל תבקשו לטמאה בהם אני ה׳ אלקיכם. But rather: מפני שיבה תקום והדרת פני זקן ויראת מאלקיך אני ה׳; (cf. Is. 8,19 et seq.; & Introduction to Isaiah: Is. and his contemporary world in Ges. Schriften).

Kiddushin 33,a teaches that by קימה and הידור, showing honour to our scholars and elders by gifts of money or kind is not to be understood, and therefore also: אין בעלי אומניות רשאים לעמוד מפני תלמידי חכמים בשעה שעוסקין במלאכתם, workmen while engaged in their work have not to rise when sages pass. And our Jewish sages also teach (ibid) that although ויראת מאלקיך is addressed to the general public as an admonition not to neglect the duty of rising before a תלמיד חכם, it is at the same time a warning directed to the תלמידי חכמים, not to seek such signs of honour, to avoid it as much as possible and to refer to go a round-about way so as not to give people the trouble of rising: ר׳ שמעון בן אלעזר אומר מנײן לזקן שלא יטריח אבײ ;ת״ל זקן ויראת נקיטינן said: we have been taught דאי מקיף חײ, that a ת״ח who goes out of his way to avoid the honouring acknowledgments due to him, is rewarded by length of life.

V. 33 & 34. יגור ,גר (see on Ch. 17,8). בארצכם ,אתך: The change to the singular number אתך teaches that it refers, not to the individuals but to the nation as a whole. He is only to be considered as a גר when his joining the nation is official, when it has been done before a body representative of the nation, a ב״ד של שלשה (Kiddushin 46,b). בארצכם, when he is there as an immigrant in your land, where already every piece of land has its native owner, and through the law of the jubilee year (Levit. 25,23), he can not, as a rule, ever obtain permanent possession of landed property, and so remains for ever a גר בארצכם, a landless man in your land: לא תונו אותו (see on Ex. 22,20). There it says וגר לא תונה, whereby the state as such is warned against victimizing strangers, not giving them equal treatment and rights in law with that of the native-born inhabitants. Here לא תונו in the plural, make a demand to every member of the nation, in their general intercourse with strangers not to let them feel that they are newcomers, not even by a word that might hurt their feelings, אונאת דברים (Baba Kama 59,b). But rather treat them כאזרח מכם; either as one native born, i.e. as one of yourselves, or it might mean, as one born from one of you, i.e. as if of Jewish descent. In any case it expresses the complete equality of status and treatment, and not only in law and rights, but also in your feelings and your duty of brotherly love. The ואהבת לו כמוך said here for the גר is exactly the same height as the principle: ואהבת לרעך כמוך, for every other fellow-Jew (see on v. 18). כי גרים הײתם בארץ מצרים: You yourselves learnt to know to what harshness a country sinks when human rights are not recognised for aliens. All your trouble in Egypt arose because you were גרים there and treated as such. That led on to your עבדות and your ענוי, your slavery and wretchedness. So that the constitution in your land is to be rooted in the principle of the complete equality in the eyes of the law of all inhabitants, whether they are native born or otherwise, (see Ex. 22,20). But the sanctification of your life in mind and deed to which you are to strive, demands more than just equality at law, it demands the complete equality of the stranger and your native born brother in your attitude towards him, in your feelings and your well-wishing. More, it wants, just in the love that you bring towards the stranger who has come from outside to dwell in your midst, it to be recognised that in very truth אלקיכם :אני ה׳, that God, in truth is your God, and that for His sake you encompass all His children in truth with brotherly love. The consideration and love for strangers is the true test of your fear of God and your love of God.

Vv. 35 & 36. The kind of משפט of which it is speaking here is shown by the complement: במדה etc. It is the justice of those things on whose correctness the honesty of human intercourse depends. The Torah considers everybody who counts, measures, or weighs anything and on that declares its content, or who declares an object to be a measure of some definite size, to be, and to have the responsibility of, a שופט. He is an officer of justice, he pronounces judgment as to what is right and fair, his word is משפט, a declaration of what is right. But this places the responsibility for and guard of, the honesty and legality of things in general in the hands of the conscience of every single person. Every one is placed in charge of it, over it, עול, and any misuse of this power is עָוֶל just as great a wrong as a misuse of the legal power of a judge, (v. 15).

But the abuse of the confidence in the honesty of every person, of which it is speaking here, is not actually cheating somebody out of their rights by giving short weight etc. Using false weights or measures in buying and selling, or with correct weights and measures giving the wrong amount is גזל מעליא הוא, is simple robbery, pure גזלה וגנבה, that need not come at the conclusion of such a chapter of making our lives holy. The לאו דכתב רחמנא במשקלות, the prohibition regarding honesty in weight and measure which the Torah mentions here is לעבור עליו משעת עשײה, makes us responsible for making, or not doing away with, the possibility of our fellow-men being wronged, even before any wrong has been done. It forbids us even to have an imperfect weight or measure in our possession, it forbids us to be careless in measuring off or weighing our material even if there is no immediate idea of trading with it, if there is the slightest possibility of its being bought or sold, commands us, not only to exercise the utmost care in the manufacture of weights and measures, but to be most conscientious in keeping them in good condition and repair, to take meticulous precautionary measures against any change in weights, scales, and measures due to wear or to deposits, or in the case of measures of length, to the effect of changes of temperature, as all these, and other matters of the same nature relating to measuring materials, retail and wholesale trade, household purchases, etc., are taught most explicitly in Baba Bathra 88,a & b et. seq. (see Baba Metzia 61,b; תוספות B.B. 89,b ד״ה ובמשורה). משורה, see on Gen. 17,65 Epha and Hin are measures of capacity and one Hin is one-sixth of an Epha. The smaller measure of a הין is a לוג; 1 הין = 12 לוג.

The reference to יציאת מצרים, with which this command of honesty in measures concludes, shows what an important position in the sphere of the Lawgiving it occupies. It is on the basis of the Redemption from Egypt and all that which it made known to us of God’s managment בקרב הארץ, in the midst of the life of nations on earth, as well as all that which thereby established for all time our special relationship to God, and our duty towards Him, that God makes the demand: לא תעשו עול במשפט etc., מאזני צדק etc. Hence we find in ת״ב on our verse: אני ה׳ אלקיכם אשר הוצאתי אתכם מארץ מצרים על תנאי כך הוצאתי אתכם מארץ מצרים על תנאי שתקבלו עליכם מצות מדות שכל המודה במצות מדות מודה ביציאת מצרים וכל הכופר במצות מדות כופר ביציאת מצרים, “the obligation to fulfill the command of “measures” was a presupposed condition for, and an intended purpose of, the Redemption from Egypt, so that all who acknowledge their duty to keep this duty acknowledge יציאת מצרים as pertaining to themselves, and who denies the one denies also the other”. The “Law of Measures” is considered as being on a level with the עריות-laws (B.B. 88,b), more, with regards to the punishment incurred by transgressing them, as being even worse: ,קשה עונשן של מדות יותר מעונשן של עריות. So that just as in עריות we see the foundation of personal morality and family life, so in מדות is the foundation of social life. Inasmuch as the Torah does not forbid dishonesty in weights and measures only when actually exercised, which, as already remarked, comes under the heading of pure and simple robbery, but regards a weight and a measure in itself as משפט, its possession as being an act of “justice”, and in every Jewish measure, and in everything measured by a Jew wishes to see a Jewish act of justice, a symbol of Jewish respect for justice and right, it makes Right in itself, in its most absolute form something to be unviolably held as something sacred. It wants to make the feeling for right and the respect and consideration for right, honesty, to be a fundamental trait of the Jewish national character.

In B.M. 49,a, the הין צדק of our verse, which seems redundant as it is already implied by the example given of measures of capacity, the איפה of which it is only one part, is explained that by it the Torah wants to impress that: שיהא הן שלך צדק ולאו שלך צדק, i.e. that “your yea shall be yea, and your nay, nay! Thereby the principle is firmly established that, quite apart from the law courts, the word of a Jew must be a holy thing which can be utterly depended on: דברים יש בהם משום מחוסרי אמנה. And actually, every measure and everything that is measured is nothing else but the most simple, and therefore the far reaching embodiment of a word. It is on the truthfulness of your word that your pound is actually a pound, for people must be able to take your word for it. It is on the sanctity and reliability of your word that the whole fair and honest social intercourse rests, and the simplest and first representative of your word is a correct weight and a correct measure.

So our sages use their harshest terms against one who is משקר במדות, “who lies with weights and measures”, קרוי עוול, they say he is called: עוול שנאוי ומשוקץ וחרם ותועבה, criminal, hated and despised, banned and an abomination: גורם לחמשה דברים, מטמא את הארץ ומחלל את השם ומסלק את השכינה ומפיל ישראל בחרב ומגלה אותם מארצם; and causes five things: he robs the land of its moral purity, desecrates the Name of God, drives the Presence of God away from earthly conditions, causes Israel to fall under the sword of her enemies, and be driven out of their land (ת״כ). He shatters one of the pillars that held up the Jewish State.

So that the whole chapter of קדושים, of making Jewish life holy, concludes with two demands which contain the two fundamental principles which are to bear the Jewish State of God in contrast to the other States of Self-Interest, and which are to reach their complete actual realisation in this Jewish State:— (a) the principle of respect and consideration of one’s fellow-man, and love of one’s fellow-man, which is to find its most glowing proof in the laws giving complete equality of all rights of domicile and everything else to the alien and the native born in the eyes of the Law, and enjoining equal love and consideration for the stranger in Jewish social life (vv. 33 & 34); and (b) the principle of objective respect for right and truth which in the correctness of weights and measures in themselves is to express homage to our God (vv. 35 & 36).

It is only on the tree of the whole sanctification of Jewish life that these healthy fruit for social human happiness ripen. Only when the חוקים and משפטים, the משפטים and the חוקים, the whole of God’s Torah without exception gets full and complete שמירה and עשיה, studying it with one’s intellect and keeping it in practice, only there does God lay His Seal on private and public life, only there does the whole and the individual bear His Name: אני ה׳!
ושמרתם את כ ל חקתי ואת כ ל משפטי ועשיתם אותם אני ה׳! (ת״כ) לתן שמירה ועשיה לחוקים ושמירה ועשיה למשפטים אני ה׳ אני נאמן לשלם שכר,, (See on Ch. 18,4 & 5).

V. 1. We have already remarked, in introducing the previous chapter how this twentieth chapter is clearly the continuation of the eighteenth chapter, and completes the laws of עריות which are begun there. Ch. XVIII contained the laws prohibiting them. Ch. XX tells of capital punishment or the fate of כרת which transgressing them entails. In Ch. XVIII, the real עריות-laws concluded with the attached prohibition of Moloch in v. 21, Ch. XX introduces the laws for the punishments of עריות by giving the punishment for the sin of Moloch. Between the two is placed Ch. XIX, the chapter on making Jewish life holy. Before the death penalty and כרת punishment are pronounced for transgression of the עריות sins, and the nation through their representative, the Sanhedrin, are called on to carry out such a sentence, the weighty importance of these laws for the individual and national mission is first shown. It is driven home, how the whole well-being and holiness of the whole of the life of the individual and the nation depends on the fulfilment of these עריות-laws; that it is only to a nation whose sons and daughters have blossomed out of a family life regulated by the regime prescribed by these laws that the demand can be made: קדושים תהיו, and carrying them out with all their expected consequences, as these are pictured and described just in this chapter on the underlying principles of an internal and external private and communal life lived in holiness before God. In this connection it is shown how with every sin against the עריות-laws the moral future of the individual and the nation is affected in its innermost being, and so the whole seriousness of the law which by מיתת ב״ד or כרת denies the עריות-transgressor further existence in the nation, and makes it the duty of the nation itself to inflict the death penalty can be understood.

V. 2. ואל בני ישראל תאמר: this way of expression always implies a contrast to what has preceded, so in: ואל בני ישראל תדבר in Ex. 30,31; in Levit. 9,3; in Levit. 24,15; Numb. 27,8; in all these places what had preceded was addressed or referred to certain individuals or limited groups of individuals, and then with אל בני ישראל, “but to the children of Israel in general” the Word was, in contrast, directed to the whole community of Israel. Here it seems to be the reverse. Here, the preceding chapter to אל כל עדת בני ישראל, to the whole community in its widest conception, every individual of it is to receive the call and the duty “you are to make your lives holy”. In contrast, the בני ישראל here designates the community in a more limited conception, the community of all the male independent members of it, as we find elsewhere also our sages taking בני ישראל to be the sons of Israel and not בנות ישראל, not the women. Here, dealing with punishments and the death penalty, it is speaking of the existence and enforcement by punishment of the general upkeeping of the Law. To that, only the representatives of the national mission, the independent male members of the nation, are called upon. But here, where the serious duty is imposed of guarding the Law against crimes where the death penalty has to be inflicted, the curt peremptory expression: ואל בני ישראל תדבר, is not used as it is in the other places referred to, but it says: ואל בני ישראל תאמר, i.e. explain it to them, let them see the reasons for it, so that they may understand and appreciate the necessity and justice for the severity ordered in these cases.

אשר יתן מזרעו למלך. We have already explained the meaning of this sin on Ch. 18,21 as well as its relation to the עריות-prohibitions. It subscribes to the idea which believes that the family, and especially the children, are under a power which reigns over their fate (מלך), a blind power which is inimical to the happiness of human well-being to which some of the children can be given over to save the rest of them. This illusion, blasphemously recognising a Power of Fate other than God, and acknowledging it with the offering of our dearest, with the sacrifice of a child, kills at the same time the idea of our children belonging to God, and the holy moral meaning of children as זרע, as human seed meant to blossom out under God’s care and for God’s purpose. But this is a denial of our sexual life being something morally holy to God, denies it in its very fundamental truth, which is why its meriting the death penalty introduces the laws of the punishments for transgression of the עריות-laws. נתינה מזרעו למולך contains the underlying idea of both ע״ז and ג״ע.

עם הארץ וגו׳. See on Gen. 23,7. It is the nation — borne and sustained by the land — by whose commission, and as its representative, that the Law, with the nation’s actual assistance if, and where necessary, has to carry out the punishment (see ת״כ). There it says: אם אין בב״ד כח יפה עם הארץ מסײעין אותו. And further: עם הארץ שבגינו נבראתה הארץ, or according to עם שהם עתידים לירש את הארץ על ידי הדברים הללו :ר׳ גמליאל, i.e. that union of people (עם), which has the purpose for which the world was created; or, that People who, by carrying out these laws become worthy to occupy the Land. If we consider the manner and meaning of the סקילה-punishment pronounced here, the expression עם הארץ, which is used just here, and the explanation of it given in ת״ב appear in a most significant light. We have already remarked on Ex. 19,13, that the first and essential act of סקילה is not stoning at all, but דחיה, a precipitation from a height, and only in the case of this fall not being fatal, was the finishing stroke, the death-blow administered by stoning (throwing a heavy rock on to his heart), (Sanhedrin 45,a & b). It is, accordingly, death by the earth itself, on which Man lives, and as a part of it, the stone or rock completes the deed when necessary. According to the wider or narrower conception one adopts, it is the Earth or the soil of the Land which is the instrument. It is Man who is the victim, Man, with his God-like free will, the noblest product of the Earth: שבגינו נבראתה הארץ. The particular part of the Earth that carries out the sentence on its immoral inhabitant is the Land, the possession of which is attached to its inhabitants keeping the laws of morality: שהם עתידים לירש את הארץ על ידי הדברים הללו, and which, as repeatedly stated, rejects and expels immoral inhabitants. It is in this sense, realising this relation of the people and the nation to the world and to the Land, that the Torah here imposes the duty on the עם הארץ to see that the criminal, who has become unworthy of the world and the Land, finds his death by סקילה, viz. precipitation to the earth, or eventually, if necessary by a part taken from it. If we look at the crimes which are to be atoned for by סקילה, viz.: — הבא על האם ועל אשת אב ועל כלתו ועל נערה המאורסה ועל הזכור ועל הבהמה והמגדף ועובד ע״ז והנותן מזרעו למולך ובעל אוב וידעוני והמסית והמדיח והמכשף והמחלל את השבת ומקלל אביו או אמו ובן סורר ומורה, we recognise in them all the highest points of the עריות and the ע״ז sins, and crimes related to them, (as חלול שבת is related to ;ע״ז מקלל אב ואם and בן סורר ומורה are the corresponding sins in an upward direction to what עריות-sins are in a downward one, גלוי עריות is חילול זרע, while קללת אב ואם and בן סורר ומורה are חלול אב ואם), sins against which the world revolts and against which the soil which is holy to the Laws of God rises up and refuses to tolerate those that commit them.

The characteristic legal term for סקילה is דמיו בו ,דמיהם בם (Sanhedrin 23,a): his blood is reflected back to himself, he is isolated, rejected, “thrust back” from the surface of the earth which otherwise would bear him as she maternally bears all her creatures.

According to ר׳ אלעזר, at all נסקלין, according to the חכמים only at the two worst סקילה-sins, שכפרו בעיקר, viz. מגדף and עובד ע״ז, this idea of isolation received an even more significant expression by the procedure of תליה (hanging) following the death by סקילה. In accordance with the instructions given in Deut. 21,21 & 23, shortly before sunset the body of the person who had had suffered סקילה was hung on a post, and then at once taken down and buried. Just for a moment the body hangs between heaven and earth, has no resting-place between heaven and earth, is accordingly the most complete דמיו בו, the most complete being sent back to itself, the most complete isolation. This could also be the explanation of כי קללת אלקים תלוי (Deut. 22,23). We take this to mean: “one who is hanging is an expression of a curse of God”. For just as ארר, the synonym of קלל, is related to ערר and has the underlying idea of isolation (see on Gen. 3,14), so קלל is the reverse of כבד, and has the idea of being light, having no weight, and so having no point of support on a base, from which comes the phonetically related גלל, to roll. So that קלל means to express the wish, or the destiny, that something should become completely without weight, held up by nothing, find no support or hold in anything, and so to go completely to wrack and ruin. תלוי, swinging between heaven and earth, represents, accordingly, the most complete קללה, being rejected by heaven and earth, the penalty which the מגדף and the עובד ע״ז would incur by their crime, if the punishment of סקילה and תליה at the hands of the court did not act as atonement for them: מיתה וקבורה מכפרת (Sanhedrin 47,b). So the קללה of the מגדף who cursed his God, אשר קלל אלקיו is made to fall back on himself by תליה and Sanhedrin 45,b takes כי קללת אלקים תלוי to refer only to the punishment of the מגדף and the similar sin of עובד ע״ז, and the addition of אלקים to קללת to be taken as being both active and passive.

V. 3. If, as we worked out on Ch. 18,21, paying tribute to Moloch is not renouncing God for idolatry, but the erroneous idea that there is a force of fate, inimical to Man, which is to be feared and placated, a force which is side by side with God, or even within the conception of God, then we can understand the severe rigorousness of this pronouncement.

One who is עובד ע״ז turns his back on God and His Sanctuary, he goes to ruin, but the purity of God’s Sanctuary and the Truth of the Name of God, i.e. the conception of God which is to be held and acknowledged in the minds of men, remain unsoiled. But he who pays tribute to Moloch claims, with his belief in fatalism, to still remain on the basis of the Jewish Sanctuary and the Jewish conception of God, and that is why he is מטמא מקדש ה׳ and מחלל את שם קדשו. The מקדש ה׳ expresses placing the whole of oneself with one’s whole fate and all one’s actions under God alone and under His Torah, and makes one’s happiness and well-being exclusively and solely dependent on faithful carrying out of this Torah. But the Moloch illusion concedes the power of Moloch a place at the side of God and His Law, and makes its influence to be feared as something that is beyond the power of God Himself and His Laws to annul. So that he brings the most demoralising erroneous opinion into God’s Sanctuary-of-the-Torah, as well as mixing-up and rendering unclear the recognition and acknowledgment that it is God’s Almight, Wisdom, and Goodness alone, which has the sole control of everything. Yea, he is so penetrated with the necessity of fearing and paying tribute to this providence as being מלך, as being the real ruler of and dispenser of fate in the world, that openly and without shame, just מזרעו נתן למלך למען טמא את מקדשי וגו׳, practices this illusive act. Hence, then to him it is said: ואני אתן את פני באיש ההוא וגו׳; for him My Management of affairs, and My bringing up of his children is not sufficient to ensure the well-being of his children, he has given over some of his children to have to suffer the uncertainty of the power of Moloch so as to ensure the maintenance and well-being of the rest. The whole of Myself and the Eye of My Providence will I direct — if the arm of human justice can not mete out the appropriate punishment, as for example, if there are no עדים והתראה — against such a man, inasmuch as I will cause the very opposite of that which he had tried to obtain by means of Moloch, and will make him together with his children disappear from out of the midst of his people (according to Rashi’s explanation that every כרת entails הוא וזרעו נכרת).

V. 4 & 5. Just because מולך is not an idol an ע״ז the practice could find so many adherents amongst their relations and friends, that the representatives of the Nation, the Sanhedrin, might, out of fear of these adherents, forgo the imposition of the penalty for this crime. In the word זנה — related, as it is, to זנח and שנא — lies the double conception of unfaithfulness, forsaking the one and turning to the other.

V. 6. See on v. 31. The belief in the imaginary power of oracles is closely related to that of the power of Moloch, a power of ill-luck or providence apart from God. It is seeking pronouncement on the desirability of taking action, or abstaining from it, and of one’s fate, from other imaginary sources. Just as the follower of Moloch does not believe that purely and simply depending on God’s Management and on the dictates of His Will as contained in His Torah is sufficient to ensure the happiness of his children and the prosperity of his family, so do these seekers of oracles not find it sufficient for the general well-being for which they strive. Like the follower of Moloch, they, too, deny the exclusiveness of the government of God affecting everything, the פני ה׳, so that here it says, to,, ונתתי פני וגו׳. The change of gender from feminine to masculine is quite common with נפש. We find it in פרשת קרבנות, Ch. 1,1; IV,2; XXVII,8; V,1 and elsewhere.

V. 7. זו קדושת פרישות ע״ז :והתקדשתם ,(ת״כ). It is not speaking here of the קדושת כל מצות, of the general קדושה to be striven for in connection with the dictates of the Torah in general, of which the previous chapter קדושים תהיו dealt, but of the special קדושה which is to be sought and kept by keeping away from all forms of idolatrous practices, as has just been dealt with in connection with מולך and אוב וידעוני (ibid.). We have already indicated elsewhere how the conception קדוש in its highest degree, and so used as an attribute God, comprises not only absolute freedom of will, but also the absolute freedom of existence, and hence eternity. Thus we find Sanhedrin 92a on the verse in Isaiah 4,13, saying: והיה הנשאר בציון והנותר בירושלים קדוש יאמר לו וגו׳, מה קדוש לעולם קײם אף הם לעולם קײמין. Here, too, the idea קדוש may have its complete meaning in both connections. It had just previously been dealing with the sins of מולך and אוב וידעוני. On that comes the admonition keep yourselves clear of all heathenism, raised above all fear of the dark forces of human illusions and above putting your trust in any of them, keep yourselves ready for the absolute fulfilment of My Will, then with this freeing of your minds and your own will, you will also free your existence, with your complete subordination to Me you will become untouchable by any other power, for I, ה׳, on Whose nod every coming moment is dependent, am אלקיכם, as equally the Guiding Hand of your destiny as the Director for your deeds.

V. 8. ושמרתם וגו׳, introduces the following, God appoints you as the guardians of His Laws, and to carry out the punishments He has prescribed for their protection. That may be the explanation of the כי which follows.

V. 9. כי וגו׳, for God has imposed punishments upon the individuals, for the transgression of these laws which are to be carried out only by the community as a whole that is why He appointed the Community in the previous verse as guardians of His Law.

If we compare the prohibitions of the עריות in Ch. XVIII, with the laws for the punishments for their transgression which follow here, the order in which these latter are given shows quite clearly a different point of view to that which decided the order given in Ch. XVIII. There the underlying idea is שאר, blood relationship decided the order. It begins, accordingly, with ערות אב ואם, to which is attached ערות אשת אב, then אחותו, then בת בנו and then אחות אביו and אחות אמו, to which אשת אחי האב is attached as equally important. Only then follow the עריות which arise through relations by marriage, from the combination of blood relationship and connection by marriage such as: אחות אשתו ,אשה ובתה ,אשת אחיו ,כלתו. Then also the ערזה condition which occurs also in married life, i.e. נדה, and only then finally the ערוה relationship which arises without any blood relationship whatsoever, only from connection by marriage viz., אשת איש. The sins of the sexual abnormalities follow last of all.

Here at the laws of the penalties incurred, a different point of view clearly decides the order, partly in the very opposite order. In verses 10—16, all those עריות, which are חײב מיתת ב״ד, are first of all put together, and then in verses 17—21 the חײבי כריתות. According to ר׳ מאיר אליבא דר׳ עקיבא, who, in Sanhedrin 57b & 58a estabalishes the canon: כל ערוה שב״ד של ישראל ממיתין עליה בן נח מוזהר עליה אין ב״ד של ישראל ממיתין עליה אין בן נח מוזהר עליה (see כ״מ on הל׳ מלכים ,רמב״ם X,5, where a different way of taking it is adopted), the first group would, at the same time, be those which have to be obesrved in the sexual life of non-Jews also, whereas the חײבי כריתות would only arise from the קדושת ישראל. A pronouncement which would then give a quite special significance to the expression which is usually used in connection with the כריתות, viz.: מקרב עמם ,מעמיה.

But even within the first group, which contains the חײבי מיתת ב״ד, there seems to be another point of view which decides the order. Whereas, as remarked, in Ch. XVIII, the idea of שאר, blood relationship, is in the foreground, and therefore אשת איש, which is purely and simply אישות and no blood relationship at all, comes last and concludes the list of עריות, here, the idea אישות, the sanctity of marriage, the ערוה which arises from the marriage tie, is so much to the fore, that אשת איש, there the last, here (v. 10) is the first. Moreover, all the חײבי מיתת ב״ד which follow here, אשת אביו in v. 11, כלתו in v. 12, חמותו in v. 14, are all מחמת אישות, so that those עריות which are purely on account of שאר amongst the חײבי מיתת ב״ד as בת בנו ,בת בתו ,בתו ,אמו, are only included in their עונש by implication. The עונש for אמו is expressed in that mentioned for אשת אביו, the עונש for ,בתו בת בתו and בת בנו, all implied in that of אשה ואמה (Sanhedrin 54a and 75a & b).

So that already the way in which the laws for the punishment of עריות are given, stresses the institution of marriage. The institution of marriage is not merely one of convention. The relationships created by marriage are completely equal to those of blood relationship. A step-mother, אשת אב, is a mother, so much a mother that God’s Torah makes a real mother understood to be included in that term. A daughter-in-law is also a daughter, and indeed a daughter of a higher degree, כלתו, is בסקילה, and בתו is only בשרפה, by implication in v. 14. A mother-in-law is also a mother, in one instance considered even more seriously a mother, אם חמותו is ערוה while אם אמו is only שניה. A stepdaughter, בת אשתו, is a daughter, so much so that the Torah does not mention a real daughter, but takes her to be understood as included in that term. More, the Torah adds and interpolates the sins of unnatural sexual acts to these עריות מחמת אישות, these עריות-by-marriage, (verses 13 & 15), and so makes us take these sins against relations created by the institution of marriage as being equal to, and as serious as the most unnatural sins against nature.

So that these laws of the Torah place God’s seal on the institution of marriage and on the condition of relationships resulting therefrom, so that it should become for us something true and holy. It places, accordingly, at the head of these laws the sin that breaks the institution of marriage, sanctified by the Seal of God, the sin of adultery (v. 10).

Let us now at last come back to our verse 9. There we find the very reverse of כבוד אב ואם, which was given in Ch. 19,2, as the first underlying principle of making our lives holy; and there, too, we found that the means of furthering this great principle was dependent, again, on keeping sacred the laws of עריות which preceded it. The relation of children to parents and the institution of marriage, these two irreplaceable foundations of all human and social development, stand (v. 9 & 10), as pillars at the portals of the chapter of the dire penalties for sexual sins. As God makes it the duty of the arm of the Law of the Jewish Social Community to be the guardians of these laws, it brings it home to us thereby that sinners against parental influence or against marriage — sins which undermine the very roots of, and the first conditions for, all true human development — may not be allowed to continue to exist in our midst.
אביו ואמו קלל, even after their death (Sanhedrin 85b). The influence of parents is not supposed to end with their lives. — דמיו בו: see on v. 2.

V. 10. ינאף. The meaning of נאף is quite definite. It is the specific term for adultery and is used in no other sense. The etymology is obscure. It is not impossible that, like באר and באש ,בר and גהא ,בוש and גוה, and לאט and לוט, so also נאף is related to נוף .נוף meaning a horizontal movement of the hand away from the body, (hence in Chaldean, also a branch) in תנופה obtains the meaning of the movement of turning something away from where it is with you, towards someone else. But that is exactly a description of adultery. The wife belongs exclusively to her husband. In adultery she is turned away from her husband and turned towards another. That would be why the term is applied to no other sexual sin. — אשר ינאף את אשת רעהו. Wessely, in his commentary, explains this apparently superflous repetition, as coming to prevent the mistaken idea that the sin is any less of committed with the collusion of the husband, who would then still remain the רעהו, the friend of the adulterer. Adultery is a sin against marriage itself, against the sanctity of the institution of marriage, not only against the husband who possibly might condone it.

כל מיתה האמורה בתורה סתם אינה אלא חנק .חנק :מות יומת, (Sanhedrin 52b). It is taken to mean the simplest method of execution, the one most similar to natural death. It stops the life-giving act of breathing. Apart from אשת איש there are five crimes which incur this penalty of death by :חנק מכה אביו ואמו וגונב נפש מישראל וזקן ממרא ונביא שקר והמתנבא בשם ע״ז. Taking them together, this particular form of the death-penalty would express the idea that every coming breath of our life is only justified by our not injuring our parents, by in private life respecting the personal freedom as well as the marriage of our fellow-man, and in public life by not misusing any position we may hold as teacher of God’s Laws, or as transmitter of His Word, to teach disobedience to the highest authority of those laws, or by using such position in the service of apostasy and untruth.
V. 12. תבל עשו, exactly the same expression as used in Ch. 18,23 of unnatural perversions; see notes thereon and remarks already made on v. 9.

V. 14. אשר יקח את אשה ואת אמה, either the mother of a daughter he has married, or the daughter of a mother he has married, his mother-in-law or his stepdaughter, this is the most natural way of taking the אתהן which follows, the one or the other whichever one of the two with whom he had criminal association. In any case here by אתיא הנה הנה אתיא זמה :ג״ש זמה, all the עריות mentioned in verses 10 & 17 of Ch. XVIII, are included in the עונש, accordingly: בתו ובת בתו ובת בנו ובת אשתו ובת בתה ובת בנה חמותו ואם חמותו ואם חמיו (Sanhedrin 75a & b). — באש ישרפו is an internal burning of the entrails: מדליק וכו׳ ויורדת לתוך מעיו וחומרת את בני מעיו, (Sanhedrin 5b). This form of the death penalty is only fixed for the עריות mentioned here and for בת כהן שזינתה. Its legal characteristic is זמה (see Sanhedrin 75b). If זמה, as we believe it does, specially indicates sexual immorality, this form of שרפה would exactly hit and kill the very centre of sexuality, the בני מעים. That is probably why, in the case of שרפה, it does not say, as it does by the others: מות יומתו באש ישרפו, where the death sentence is first pronounced and then the mode of death, so that here שרפה would only be the mode of execution. But here, as well as in Ch. 21,9, it simply states שרפה without שרפה .מות יומת is the direct destruction of the organs of זמה and death is only the indirect result.

V. 15 & 16. ואת הבהמה, either because through it a man has come to ruin, שבאת לאדם תקלה על ידה, or so that no remembrance should remain that such bestial degenerate action had been performed on it: שלא תהא בהמה עוברת בשוק ויאמרו זו היא שנסקל פלוני על ידה (Sanhedrin 54a).

V. 17. At the head of the list of חײבי מיתת ב״ד in verses 9 & 10, stand מקלל אב ואם and אשת איש thereby giving the mutual relationship of parents and children to the institution of marriage. Out of these two relationship parents and children and marriage all the חײבי מיתת ב״ד are derived. They are limited to crimes against either upward or downward relations, or against marriage. The fundamental relationship for the חײבי כריתות is אחוה, that of sibling, and the resulting relations which arise from both the parents and relationship by marriage, i.e.: ,אשת אחיו ,אחות אמו ,אחות אביו ,אחותו אחות אשתו ,אשת אחי אביו, to which only נדה is added, which could be in a similar relationship in the חײבי כריתות to that of the unnatural practices of זכר and בהמה in the חײבי מיתת ב״ד. Regarding all these עריות both חײבי מיתת ב״ד and חײבי כריתות, the general remark has already been made above in Ch. 18,29: כי כל אשר יעשה מכל התועבות האלה ונכרתו הנפשות העושות מקרב עמם, “For anybody who does any of these abominations will be cut off from the midst of his people”. The חײבי מיתת ב״ד, too, are חײבי כרת, when the legal punishment can not, or does not, be carried out on them. Some of the חײבי כריתות, actually all of them, except אחות אשתו, are here again repeated, giving the penalty of כרת, to establish also, at the same time some important legal points which mostly apply to all עריות, in accordance with the canon: כל דבר שהיה בכלל ויצא מן הכלל ללמד, לא ללמד על עצמו יצא אלא ללמד על הכלל כולו יצא. Also: כרת ;לכך יצא כרת באחותו לחלק is made especially prominent in the אחותו case to tell us that in עריות, each case is considered separately, so that if in one act several עריות are combined, e.g. אשת איש and נדה, the guilt is reckoned separately for each, consequently if it was בשוגג as many חטאות would have to be brought as איסורים had been committed: שאם עשאן כולן בהעלם אחד חײב על כל אחת ואחת (Kerithoth 2b). — וראה וגו׳ והיא תראה וגו׳, they are both completely aware of the sinful character of the act: ,עד שיהיו שניהן מזידין (ת״כ). This condition, which applies generally in all cases of punishment, is probably mentioned just here where the conditions of life, living together, could more easily bring about the possibility of the sin being committed in error.

חסד הוא. As חסד everywhere else expresses the highest degree of goodness, its meaning in this place is difficult to understand. On Gen. 47,29, we have given the underlying conception of חסד as being personal devotion. As the character of one’s own behaviour, it is, accordingly, the highest selfless devotion to the well-being of another, acting לפנים משורת הדין, kindness and goodness that goes beyond the bare dictates of duty. But where it refers, not to the person himself, but to another, חַסֵד את, causing somebody else to be devoted, it becomes the complete opposite, the ruthless abandonment of the well-being of another: פן יחסדך שמע (Prov. 25,10), “one who hears you, might find you despicable to the highest degree and abandon you”. Hence the Chaldean word חסודא, outrage, disgrace. Perhaps suspicion is also related to it. Our supposition that it is also phonetically related to אשד, to let oneself go, might find confirmation in the word חסודה, blood-letting, יד לחסודה תקצץ (Sabbath 108b). If then חסד elsewhere has the meaning of an unrestrained going beyond the dictates of duty, giving oneself up to another where one is not duty bound to do so, here it can also very well mean giving oneself up to another where forbidden by duty, and it is in this sense that we have translated it.

לעיני בני עמם. Not only the punishment of כרת from Above, but even the disappearance out of the national future here below, which in other כרת-sins may not always be apparent. Here it will occur strikingly.

אחותו שהיא בת אביו ובת אמו :ערות אחותו גלה. The same penalty of כרת applies to sinning with a sister. Although this could certainly have been deduced from the law giving the penalty for a stepsister, בת אביו או בת אמו, it is mentioned expressly here so that we deduce from it the general canon that אין עונשין מן הדין, that in criminal law no penalty may be imposed if it is based on mere deduction and not expressly stated (Kerithoth 3a). — עונו ישא: his guilt weighs down on him until it brings about his destruction.

V. 18. וגלה את ערותה, in this relationship sexual intercourse is nothing but sheer animalism, as every גלוי ערוה is in all the other עריות. —  את מקורה הערה: see Yebamoth 54a. — והיא גלתה וגו׳: Here, also, by את מקורה הערה והיא גלתה וגו׳, it seems to say, just as above at אחותו, that the punishment of כרת is only incurred when the relationship and the wrongfulness of the action are realised by the perpetrators (see remarks there). Here נדה is placed immediately following אחותו, perhaps to tell us that there are periods in Jewish married life in which husband and wife may only live together as brother and sister. A condition, which, far from any lessening of the intimacy of marriage, has just the capability of making this intimacy still more intimacy and raising is constantly spiritually and morally.

V. 19. This is only a repetition of the prohibition already given in Ch. 18,12 & 13. By the repetition, the prohibition is extended to any sister of the parents, even to half-sisters on the maternal side, whereas at the prohibition there, and the following one here of אשת אחי אביו ,דודתו, only makes אשת אחי אביו מן האב, only the wife of the uncle on the paternal side into an ערוה, nevertheless the one on the maternal side is a דוד .שניה is an uncle only on the paternal side (Yebamoth 54b).

V. 20. ערות דודו, and similarly in the following verse: ערות אחיו, the woman who is an ערוה through the uncle, through his brother (see on Ch. 18,7). ערר :ערירים (related to ארר, see Gen. 13,14), from which ערער, the lonely one, is derived, designates isolation in place or time; in place to be isolated, out of touch with fellow-men, in time: to remain out of touch with the future through childlessness, or by early, untimely death of all one’s children. ערירי always designates this isolation in time, childlessness or the cessation of descendants. According to Rashi (Sabbath 25a), this condition of ערירי is connected with every כרת, not only himself disappears early from the midst of his contemporaries, but he is not allowed to continue living even in descendants, הוא וזרעו נכרת, and it is just in this point that כרת differs from מיתה בידי שמים, with which ערירי is not associated. But according to ריב״א (ibid תוספות), ערירי only applies to the עריות, where it is expressly mentioned. The difficulties which arise against Rashi’s way of taking it are solved by אמ״ו מו״ה יעקב עטלינגער ז״ל in ערוך לנר on Yebamoth 2a by taking it that ערירי is connected with all cases of כרת, but that the death of the descendants can take place after the death of the person who incurs כרת, whereas, where ערירי is specifically mentioned, he lives to see it occur. Here it says: ערירים ימותו and in v. 21: ערירים יהיו. This is explained in Yebamoth 55a: יש לו בנים קוברן, אין לו בנים הולך ערירי. If he has children at the time the sin is committed, they die before he does: ערירים ימותו, he dies childless; if he is without children, he remains without offspring, ערירים יהיו. Thus Rashi on the Pentateuch. But Yebamoth 55a takes it the other way round:— ערירים יהיו means they become childless, they lose the children they have; ערירים ימותו, they will die childless, even if they do get children afterwards they will lose them before their own death (see Rashi thereon — Moed Katan 28a; also speaks of a כרת דיומי see there).

V. 21. נדה היא, unless it is the case laid down in Deut. 25,5 of her being the widow of his childless brother, when the מצות יבום occurs. שהיא כנדה מה נדה יש לה איסור ויש לה היתר אף אשת אח יש לה איסור :נדה היא (ת״כ) ,ויש לה היתר.

Vv.22—24. When, in Ch. 18,2—5, & 24—30, the Torah gave the laws regulating sexual life, it introduced them and concluded them with a call for שמירה and עשיה of all God’s Laws (see on Ch. 18,4 & 5). In the same way, here, at the conclusion of the laws of the punishments which are to watch over the keeping of these laws, and which bring to a conclusion the whole cycle of laws on the regulation and sanctification of our individual moral life which began in Ch. XI, the Torah again calls for שמירה and עשיה of all God’s laws and social regulations. It reminds us, that, not only is the national prosperity and remaining in the land dependent on the keeping of these laws, but that altogether the whole purpose of Israel being chosen is conditional on that. The Land, as is explained in ת״כ פ׳ י״ב, is: ארץ ישראל אינה כשאר כל הארץ אינה מקײמה בעלי עוברי עבירה, the Land is not like other lands, it does not tolerate sinful inhabitants, it throws them out as one throws out food or material which is not assimilative. The degenerate Canaanite inhabitants did not posses it as their permanent possession, they were only its temporary guardians until your arrival, שהיו שומרי המקום עד שתבואו (ibid פ״ט), but you come לרשת אותה ,לשבת בה, to take possession of it as your property, to have your permanent dwelling there (ibid), ולא תלכו בחקת הגוי וגו׳, therefore beware of copying their dogmas,, manners or morals; every moment of your existence in the Land gives you this warning. For everything that I have forbidden you is just what made the inhabitants before you become so degenerate, ואקוץ בם, that I could not endure them. ואומר לכם אתם תירשו וגו׳: I appoint you for this land; by keeping the purity of your family life in the midst of a similarly degenerate nation, you have already shown the predisposition for living the moral lives which is the condition for permanent possession of it, אתם נאים יורשים אותה שאתם פותחים תחלה (ibid). אני ה׳ אלקיכם אשר הבדלתי וגו׳ there is, it is true, a tremendous gulf between the spiritual and moral height that I demand from you and the depth to which the nations you see around you have sunk, ראו כמה ביניכם ולאומות etc. (see ibid).

V. 25. והבדלתם וגו׳. But if you do not wish to degenerate like them, if you wish to let Me begin with you the building up again of the spiritual and moral heights of Mankind, in the midst of a humanity which had developed spiritually and intellectually in the wrong direction, and degenerated morally (see below on v. 26), then you must make the beginning with conscientiously keeping to the choice of nourishment, which I have prescribed as the very first preliminary for the way to spiritual, mental, and moral health, for the way to spiritual, mental, and moral clarity, purity, and holiness (Ch. XI). You only remain מובדלים מן האומות, if you are מבדילים between בין הבהמה הטהורה וגו׳ and if לא תשקצו את נפשתיכם וגו׳, if, right from the beginning, at the actual forming of the tissues of your body, the physical formation of the fibres of your brain, nerves and muscles, you keep to the choice which you are taught to observe. This protects you, ולא תשקצו את נפשותיכם בבהמה וגו׳ אשר הבדלתי לכם לטמא, so that your physical nature is not in opposition to your holy moral calling that no tendency is formed towards low, “unfree”, animal inclinations and forces which would lead you to become שקץ to Me and ואקוץ בכם as I spoke of the Canaanite nations ואקוץ בם.

This reference back to the dietary laws given in Ch.
