XI: אשר הבדלתי לכם לטמא, in this significant connection with the highest ideals of the Jewish calling, and so, at the conclusion of such a sequence of chapters of laws referring back to the very commencement, proves the extreme importance of these dietary laws. It proves their meaning to be independent of time or place for the highest spiritual and moral aim of the Jewish calling for all time. Incidentally it also shows the close connection between all the laws contained in the chapters from XI till XX, to which we had already referred on chapter XIX.

The changes, with which the order of the הבדלה we are to make, is expressed, first בין הטהורה לטמאה, and then בין הטמא לטהור, just as in Ch. 11,47: להבדיל בין הטמא ובין הטהור, and then: בין החיה הנאכלת ובין החיה אשר לא תאכל, can not be without significance. הבדיל בין ובין or בין ל-, always wants to prevent mixing the first with the second. The Law is always to remain so vividly in our minds that we take just as much care not to bring the טהור amongst the טמא as the טמא amongst the טהור. Thereby the canon is given: כשם שאסור להתיר האסור כך אסור לאסור את המותר.

V. 26. והײתם לי קדושים. The existence of God, and the Holiness of God, are identical. For קדושה, holiness, is nothing but the absolutely free-willed readiness for the fulfilment of the laws of morality given by God. We are only קדושים, if we belong to God with every fibre of our being; we only belong to God if we are קדושים with every impulse of our being.

כי קדוש אני ה׳. Once again we are referred to the Holiness of God as being the source of our ability to attain holiness, and as the reason for our duty to attain it. Moral freedom of will as well as the ability for holiness, God has breathed into us with the breath of life emanating from His Holy Being. This breath of God’s Holy nature is the cause of our ability to be holy, and the reason for our duty to be holy is again the Holiness of God, to Whom we belong, Who has given us the command to be holy; and Who only recognises us being His as long as we do not deny our belonging to Him, but show it by striving to attain holiness.

ואבדיל אתכם מן העמים להיות לי: only for this belonging to God, and for you to arrange the whole regime of your lives out of this belonging to God, did I raise you up out of the other nations. If you give this up you sink back into the mass of nations and become submerged in them. אם מובדלים אתם מן העמים הרי אתם לשמי ואם לאו הרי אתם של נבוכדנצר מלך (ת״כ) ,בבל וחבריו. Further on there, on our verse, we find the saying of  ר׳ אלעזר בן עזריה, so worth taking to heart; Keeping the dietary laws and the other laws which make our way of life different from that of the other people, should not be done out of some inborn aversion and dislike to the food or to whatever it is, but just out of our submission to God, and to the obedience we owe Him. The motive and purpose of our הבדלה מן העמים is to be: “להיות לי״, so that every breath which a Jew draws which is free from sin becomes a homage to God: ר׳ אלעזר בן עזריה אומר מנײן שלא יאמר אדם אי אפשי ללבוש שעטנז אי אפשי לאכול בשר חזיר אי אפשי לבא על הערוה אבל אפשי מה אעשה ואבי בשמים גזר עלי כך ת״ל ואבדיל אתכם מן העמים להיות לי נמצא ,פורש מן העברה ומקבל עליו עול מלכות שמים (ת״כ ibid).

Further on our verse, we find in the ילקוט, at the end of קדושים, the great saying of אלו אמר ואבדיל עמים מכם לא היתה :ר׳ ברכיה בשם ר׳ אבהו תקומה לאומות העולם אלא ואבדיל אתכם מן העמים כזה שבורר היפה מתוך הרע וחוזר ,ובורר אבל כשהוא בורר הרע מתוך היפה שוב אינו בורר (Yalkut end of קדושים). “were it to say”, I have separated out the nations from you, there would be no hope of a future for the nations, but as it says: “I have separated you out of the nations”, it is as one who first picks out the best from the lesser good, and then goes on and on picking out the good ones; but one who picks the bad out of the good, throws the bad away, and has nothing more to do with them”. So that in no wise does Jewish thought look on the choice of Israel as a rejection of the rest of humanity. It regards the choice of Israel only a beginning, only the restarting of the spiritual and moral rebuilding of Mankind, only the first step to that future where: ונלוו גוים רבים אל ד׳ ביום ההוא והיו לי לעם ושכנתי בתוכך, where many nations will attach themselves to God, and become His People, and Israel’s Sanctuary will not only be the central heart of Israel but the centre of Mankind who will have found their way to God.

V. 27. Three times in פרשת קדושים does the warning against the imagined wisdom of אוב and ידעוני oracles occur, in Ch. 19,31 as a prohibition, in Ch. 20,6 with the penalty of כרת-punishment, and now here, at the end of everything with the imposition of סקילה. The Divine Torah seems to fear nothing more for its integrity in us, and for its being kept by us, than the mixing up of the clear, reasonable dictates and promises of God’s Laws, disseminating power, wisdom, justice, and goodness, with the oracles of an illusory supposed science which crops up again and again in various guises and different forms; and which claims to be able to obtain from the dead, solutions of the problems of the living and of life; to interpret the fate and the future of Man, who is morally free-willed and near to God, and conscious of his immortality, from apparitions from the unfree world of death and decay.

So too, it became Isaiah’s task — Ch. 8,16 to IX,1 — to guard the עדות, and to protect it, and keep it in its purity from all admixtures with alien ideas, and to seal this by faithful handing down the living tradition in the hearts of the students — צור תעודה חתום תורה בלמדי. Thereupon he found it his duty to make the people recognise in him, his children and his pupils whom God has sat up as “אתות and מופתים״ in Israel, the contrast to “אובות and ידעונים״, who speak only “stutteringly and in riddles” המצפצפים והמהגים, and to whom — following the ways of the nations — the people enquire of the dead on behalf of the living — בעד החײם אל המתים. He testifies for the Torah and for the evidence of its promises, לתורה ולתעודה, that the אובות and ידעונים also clothe their words in the form of a word from God, אם לא יאמרו כדבר הזה, but that, born of the night, they bear no light of Truth in them, and that no dawn of fulfilment can be expected of them, אשר אין לו שחר. They do indeed beguile suffering mankind, but all too soon these become undeceived, וקלל במלכו ובאלהיו, and then thy seek a Higher One, ופנה למעלה — and find Him not. But the People of the true Word of God, העם, have always struggled through darkness to the light, and have always, even in the deepest shadow of death, treasured rays of the coming dawn, ההולכים בחשך ראו אור גדול יושבי בארץ צלמות אור נוגה עליהם.

V. 1. The whole cycle of laws from Ch. XI, till here treated with making Jews “holy” people. The ways were shown by which the susceptibility and ability for such holiness is obtained, and it was shown what living such holy lives really means, how it embraces the whole internal and external existence of individual personal and social life. Now follows a chapter on the special holiness of the lives of Jewish priests. It starts with the words: אמור אל הכהנים בני אהרן ואמרת אליהם וגו׳. As ואמרת וגו׳ starts a fresh sentence, a fresh speech, אמור אל הכהנים בני אהרן must also by itself be an independent speech having its own meaning. It is not comparable to the ordinary דבר אל בני ישראל ואמרת אליהם, where the דבר aims at giving the short curt idea, the general order of the law, and the ואמרת, the complete explanation of all the details, and giving the understanding of the spirit of the law, appealing to the mind and the heart.

דבר and אמר differ as “speaking” and “informing”. Speaking is the expression of thoughts in words without any consideration of its being accepted by the hearer. But informing is always “telling somebody”. One can “speak” to oneself but not “inform”. Quite the same with דבר and אמר. Whereas דבר is the concise expression of a thought, אמר is addressing the same to the mind and feeling of another person, the complete explanation and development of a thought. Hence in the speech of the Torah, דבר is always the concise pregnant expression of the Law as it is given to us in the תשב״כ, but אמר is the full explanation of it as has come to us in the תשב״פ. Hence אמורא, the interpreter, and hence אמוראים, the interpreters of the Law, the successors to the תנאים, whose task consisted of שנה really repeating, giving back, they handed on that which they themselves had received. Hence we speak of עשרת הדברות and עשרה מאמרות. The word of creation is an אמירה. It immediately realises itself in the object to which it is addressed. The word of the Torah is a דבור, in the first place it is just said, and then it awaits being accepted and carried out.

Now here both are אמר. Tho whole sentence moves in ויאמר :אמירה ה׳ וגו׳, then אמר וגו׳ and ואמרת וגו׳, Everything that follows here in short curt sentences, was said by God to Moses completely according to its meaning and content, and was to be brought to the intelligence, and to be taken to heart by those who were to be affected by these laws. So that אמור אל הכהנים בני אהרן must by itself be an independent thought and bring some message. And this can hardly be anything else but: Speak to the כהנים as בני אהרן, explain their כהונה to them as coming from their parentage, bring it home to them and let them be always conscious of the fact that their priesthood is not due to any special qualities of their own, but is only thanks to their birth. Jewish priesthood is a mission which is imposed at birth; for its accomplishment one has to be born and brought up so that this mission fills the whole life of the future man. So that just as they are to regard themselves as כהנים, only because they are בני אהרן, so are they to see in their children the future כהנים, and bring them up in the duties, and for the duties, of their tribe. It is this which is also indicated here by the term: הכהנים בני אהרן, not to be found elsewhere, everywhere else in the Torah it says: בני אהרן הכהנים. So, too, the ברײתא in Yebamoth 114a teaches: אמור ואמרת להזהיר גדולים על הקטנים, on which the רא״ש remarks in his ולכך שנה הלשון כאן שבכל מקום נאמר בני אהרן הכהנים : (הלכות טומאה) ,הלכות קטנות וכאן נאמר הכהנים בני אהרן להזהיר הכהנים על בניהם (see the version in מעדני י״ט).

The prohibition includes all כהנים of pure descent, even if they have become unfit for עבודה, so that בעלי מום are included. This lies in the extension of the idea כהנים by the addition of בני אהרן, but excludes חללים (see on v. 15), who, by their birth have lost the whole כהן-character (,ת״כ ק״א).

לנפש לא יטמא בעמיו. The subject being singular can only be אהרן as the representative of the priesthood. The first special duty of a priest is to keep away from טומאת מת, (לנפש לא יטמא, re the construction with ל see Ch. 11,26).

בעמיו. While it is a duty for all the other tribes of the nation to occupy themselves with attending to the dead, the tribe of Aaron alone has to stand back, and may not come into contact with a dead body and not touch any טומאות הפורשות מן המת, nor may they remain under the same roof with a באהל המת ,מת (see Numb. 19,14). But it is implied that the prohibition only applies בעמיו, when the body is בעמיו, amongst its own people. But a מת מצוה, an abandoned body which a כהן finds in a place where he can find nobody to call to attend to it, may not be left by the כהן, but must be attended to, and buried by him, (ת״כ and Nazir 43b), כל שאין לו קוברין, קורא ואחרים עונין אותו אין זה מת מצוה. Berachoth 19b teaches that even where a whole accumulation of מצות would be against the burial of a מת-מצוה, e.g. he was the כהן גדול and at the same time a נזיר and on his way to שחיטת פסחו and also to מילת בנו, he must nevertheless leave all these, and occupy himself with the burial of the dead body lying before him. Placing such great importance to the duty of fulfilling the last possible act of love to an unknown corpse is one of the most characteristic deep traits of Jewish teaching. It shows how the very highest goal of all the teachings of all the מצות is to train humans to be humane.

V. 2. אין שארו אלא אשתו :כי אם לשארו וגו׳, (ת״כ), under שארו here, only his wife is to be understood. On Gen. 19,1, we took it that the underlying idea of שאר — which has the meanings of:- the rest, nourishment, blood-relationship, and wife — is complement. Above in Ch. XVIII, where שאר only meant blood-relationship, this is indicated by calling it שאר בשרו in the general introductory sentence. That the שאר only means the wife, as being the spiritual and moral complement of a man’s human existence, is according to ק״א already indicated by the addition of הקרוב אליו. Blood relations are and remain tacitly always “near”. Only the wife becomes a near relation by the blood of marriage, and she ceases to be one if and when this ceases. Only in the case of a sister (v. 3), where the law is to be limited to אחותו בתולה and ceases even with אחותו ארוסה, is this limitation definitely expressed by הקרובה אליו אשר לא היתה לאיש. For the other blood-relations enumerated לאמו וגו׳, the near relationship remains in all circumstances. In Numb. 27,11, by the addition of הקרוב אליו ממשפחתו to שארו, the right of inheritance is limited to blood relations of the father’s side, as only משפחת האב gives the conception משפחה (Baba Bathra 109b). Equally so, אחיו and אחותו here only refer to siblings coming from the same father (ת״כ).

הקרוב אליו, who is actually married to him הנשואה, but not if only ארוסה, and not גרושה. Here, in this verse the mother לאמו, is again placed before the father. It is, in the first place, to the moral purity of his mother that he owes his priestly character. His being a priest is just inalienably inborn in him through his father. But for a woman to attain the dignity of becoming the mother of a priest, she must have passed the test of morality (see v. 7).

V. 3. הקרובה: even if she had been ארוסה, but had been נתגרשה אשר לא היתה לאיש .מן האירוסין: not even as an ארוסה (Yebamoth 60a). — לא רצה מטמאין אותו בעל כרחו ;מצוה :לה יטמא (Zebachim 100a); making himself טמא on the bodies of the relations mentioned here is not only allowed but is a positive duty.

V. 4. בעל: the husband, לא יטמא להחלו, is not to make himself טמא in connection with his desecration, i.e. in connection with a marriage through which he had desecrated himself, accordingly not לאשתו פסולה, a wife whom he had been forbidden by the Torah to marry (Yebamoth 22b), but this also only בעמיו, if there are other people to attend to burying her, not if she is a מת מצוה, i.e. שאין לו קוברים.

V. 5. לא יקרחה קרחה. All the three prohibitions of this verse have also been proclaimed as the general law of non-priests; גילוח פאת זקן and שריטה already above in Ch. 19,27 & 28, קרחה in Deut. 14,1: לא תשימו קרחה בין עיניכם למת. In Makkoth 20a & b and 21a the prohibitions of קרחה and גילוח פאה which have already been given in general terms, receive from our verse here, certain more precise explanations. Regarding שריטה even this is not the case. But for all three we could find cause for the repetition of these laws just specially for קרחה .כהנים is any tearing out of hair, or removal of the hair by any means whatsoever (e.g. by נשא, paste that removes hair permanently), so that the place remains permanently bald (see Rashi ibid), and even making quite a small bald patch is forbidden (ibid). From Deut. 14,1 it is evident that such spoiling the body is only forbidden למת, if done on account of a death, and the term לא תשימו וגו׳ already tells us that just as in the case of ושרט לנפש לא תתנו וגו׳ (see Ch. 19,8), it is not the act of pulling the hair out, but the effect produced which is what is forbidden. So that here too, it is not speaking of an expression of pain, a “tearing of hair”, — if the procedure is done by means of a paste, by נשא it is probably completely painless. — But here we have, like the case of שריטה, a permanent sign of the loss of the value of one’s own bodily existence by the loss of the departed one, or rather, as explained there, a sign of atonement brought as homage to the dread power of the gods who are hostile to human life. That קרחה is a “sign” expressing a thought is vouched for the addition in Deut. 14,1 of בין עיניכם, by which קרחה, like the תפילין של ראש, is given the position on the forehead as an אות, although in our verse the prohibition is expressed for the whole head.

But if קרחה, like שריטה, is brought as tribute to the god of Death who owerpowers everything, then we can understand why these prohibitions were to be repeated just for the כהנים, (although everything which is prohibited to the people is of course prohibited to the priests), and they could be closely connected with the increased טומאת-מת-prohibition for the priests.

Antique and modern heathenism like so very much to associate religion and religious matters with death and thoughts of death. For them it is where Man ends that the Kingdom of God begins. For them death and dying are the real manifestations of their godhead, who to them is a god of death and not of life. A god who kills and does not animate, and sends death and its fore-runners, illness and wretchedness, so that men should fear him, realise his power and their impotence. The places which they dedicate to temples are therefore round about graves, the foremost place of their priest is therefore at the dead and dying. There, where the light is fading from the eye, and hearts are broken, is the most fruitful field for their religious sowing.

Not so is the Jewish priest because not so is the Jewish teaching of God, the Jewish religion. The God, Whose Name assigns the Jewish priest to his office is a God of life. His sublimest manifestation is the elevating power of Life, freeing, animating, raising Man to free will and to eternal life, not the crushing power of death. Not how one is to die, but how one is to live, how, living, one has victoriously to conquer death, death in life, thraldom, enslaved by one’s physical urges, moral weakness, how one has to live every second of a morally free, thinking, desiring, working and accomplishing life, and also enjoying all the pleasures of life as a moment of service to God, that is the teaching to which God has dedicated His Sanctuary, and for the service of which He has consecrated the כהנים to care for the “basis of life and direction thereof” (כון = כהן) amongst the people.

When Death summons the people to come to busy themselves in acts of love with the empty body of a נפש which God has called home, the כהנים have to remain away, and by standing away to keep aloft the Standard of Life next to the corpse, and by the thoughts of what life really is, prevent the thoughts of death overpowering the truths that the real Man himself is morally free and not subject to forces which kill his power over his own moral free will. Only where ths duties of life call on the priest personally to fulfil the last possible acts of love to the empty shell of the נפש of his wife, child, parent, brother or sister, or where the forsaken state of a corpse makes him to a father and brother of the forsaken one, there his calling as a priest has to retire behind the calling of family and humanity, and his activity with the dead is not only permitted but is a duty. Otherwise priests have to keep away from dead bodies.

And hence it says regarding Jewish priests: לא יקרחו קרחה בראשם וגו׳, they are not to go about with a symbol of death on themselves. By their outward appearance it is the force of life and not the power of death that they have to preach. It is worth noting that יקרחה is written with a ה instead of יקרחו. Something similar only occurs once again, in Deut. 21,7 at the עגלה ערופה, where the authorities of the court of justice of a city in whose proximity a corpse has been found murdered by an unknown hand, have to declare: “our hands have not spilt this blood”. There, too, the שפכו is spelt with a לא שפכה :ה. If the way we have taken the repetition of the prohibition of קרחה for the priests is not incorrect, these two places have such a very definite similarity in one way, that therein may lie the reason for the similar anomaly of the spelling. The repetition of the statement of the prohibition of קרחה for the priests seems at first glance to be completely superfluous. It is certainly self-understood that the priests are not permitted to do something which the Torah has forbidden to be done in general for everybody. And yet, on deeper consideration, the prohibition was to be specially emphasized for the priests, otherwise it might be thought that the sign which preaches the almighty force of the power of Death would be something which does specially pertain to the role of a priest, that remembering death during life is something specially religious as a “memento mori” in the midst of the symposium of life. But this is similar to the demand for a solemn affirmation from the heads of the law-courts of a city: “We have not committed this murder”. וכי על דעתנו עלתה, explains the explanatory Halacha, שזקני ב״ד שופכי דמים היו, “Would it enter anybody’s head that the elders of a city, the judges of the court, are murderers”! Surely such an affirmation is superfluous. But such a protestation is nevertheless required. If the officials of a town have not behaved hospitably towards poor wanderers, towards a tramp who passes through their town, if they have allowed him to leave hungry and without protection: שלא פטרנוהו בלא מזון ולא הנחנוהו בלא לויה, and through that he has come to grief or been driven to crime, then they have the responsibility for his fate, are guilty of his death, and it is from this guilt that they have to clear themselves, (Sota 45b). So here we have a statement which, with regards to the persons who have to make it, seems at the first glance to be completely superfluous, but in reality is of the profoundest importance and necessity. Now in both cases, the suffix of the predicate which refers to the subject is written with a ה instead of a ו. This ה is a muting sound which is often used paragogically to modify the meaning. So that the כתיב at first gives rise to a doubt as to what the subject of the sentence can be, but the קרי teaches that, quite specially, in our case, the priests, and in the עגלה ערופה case, the hands of the elders, are meant.

Together with קרחה and שריטה, both of which have reference to acknowledging the overpowering force of the almighty power of Death, the priests are at the same time specially warned against גלוח פאת זקן. We have already explained above in Ch. 19,27, how this law admonishes Jewish men to keep their virile forces and virile acts under chaste control and to subordinate their passions to their power of human moral free will. A השחתה of these פאות denies the contrast between the moral and the sensual urges of human beings, removes the difference between being the bound slave of the physical senses and the godly moral freedom of Man, makes the whole of Man into a creature forced to obey the dictates of his senses, and makes him already during his lifetime the plaything of physical forces to which not only his empty body has to submit after the soul has left it, but which, admitted in life, rule over him as the dark forces of urges, passions and lusts.

Antique and modern heathenism not only deify the power of Death but also place these sensual forces amongst the gods. עבודה זרה and גלוי עריות have always gone hand in hand. So we can understand that the אסור גלוח פאת זקן is specially stressed together with קרחה and שריטה; and the placing of פאת זקן in the same verse with קרחה can well be because they both refer to the growth of hair.

V. 6. קדושים יהיו לאלקיהם, not only inside the Temple, but outside it too are they to be holy to the God Whom they have to teach to the people, and not desecrate His Name which they bear, and which they represent. By contact with a dead body, by שריטה and קרחה and השחתת פאות, they would proclaim the God Whom they teach to the people as a God of the human lack of freedom in life and in death, and He is just a God of moral freedom Who sets Man up triumphantly over sin and death to life and purity, and keeps him upright. Who, accordingly, bases the honour and homage to be paid to Him not on the death and weakness of men, but on their life and strength. His priests at a dead body or with שריטה ,קרחה and השחתת פאות the symbols of death and sin, would be a חלול שמו הגדול, a desecration of His Name, a truth-killing reversal to its absolute opposite of the conception of Him which He wishes us to have.

כי את אשי ה׳ וגו׳: For all that the people give over to the “Fire of the Torah” for guidance and purification, their aims, their efforts, the whole of their living organic selves, their property, their food, their well-being and all the joy of life — as represented by: ,איברים ,כליות ,חלב קומץ סולת ושמן and כל הלבונה — so that God may find pleasure and satisfaction in them, and their lives be worthy of His Presence, — all this הם מקריבים, they have to bring near to God, in the Sanctuary of His Torah: והיו קדש, that is why they themselves have to be a Sanctuary wherever they are, by their way of living are they to impress the teaching and aims of the Sanctuary; for it is only by the life lived outside the Temple that their symbolic procedures inside the Temple have any meaning. That is why the כהן is to be a “כהן״ outside the Temple too, his presence among the people is, everywhere in their ordinary daily lives, to bring to them the same “basis” (כון. I.L.), and the same “aims” (הכין. I.L.) on which the teachings of the Sanctuary wishes lives to be built up. And that is why, above all, the opposite of the truth of this basis and the sanctity of these aims must be avoided in the whole of the life of the priest.

V. 7. אשה זונה וגו׳. The precise concept of זונה in this connection to be considered here, is given in Yebamoth 61a as being, שנבעלת בעילת זנות. According to תוספות and רא״ש, by the term בעילת זנות is here to be understood any such association at which a marriage is not legally possible דלא תפסי בה קדושין, accordingly, only חײבי כריתות ומיתות ב״ד נכרי ועבד. But according to רש״י and רמב״ם it applies to כל שנבעלה לפסול לה, even if marriage is not legally permitted. For there are various degrees of prohibited marriages: (a) חײבי מיתות ב״ד, e.g. those mentioned in Ch. 20,10—12 & 14; (b) חײבי כריתות, v. 17 et seq.; (c) חײבי לאוין of which there are three inds:— (1) חײבי לאוין דשאר, those that arise through blood-relationship, e.g. אנוסת אביו לרבי ,חלוצתו יהודה, according to ר״ת also מחזיר גרושתו which, according to רש״י belongs to the following group; (2) חײבי לאוין דלאו דשאר e.g.: ,גר עמוני ומואבי ,יבמה לשוק ממזר; (3) חײבי לאוין דכהונה, which are not שוין בכל, do not apply generally but only to כהנים, e.g.: גרושה לכ״ה ,אלמנה לכה״ג; (d) חײבי עשה, e.g. גר מצרי ואדומי קודם ג׳ דורות (Yebamoth 49a). According to the accepted Halacha, the prohibitions of marriage in (a) & (b) are of such a nature that a marriage is completely impossible. An act of קידושין would be completely void, and have no legal consequences whatsoever. In the case of (c) & (d), חײבי לאוין ועשה, the marriage is a prohibited one and may not legally be continued — divorce must take place — but the act of קידושין does have the result — (with the exception of יבמה לשוק where קידושין are only תופסין מספק and צריכה גט מספק (Yebamoth 92b) — that the relationship must be dissolved by גט. According to תוספות and רא״ש, only a woman who has sinned against (a) & (b), would be forbidden to a כהן as coming under the ban of זונה; according to רש״י and רמב״ם also those coming under the heading of (c) & (d) with the exception of חײבי לאוין דכהונה transgression against which renders the woman a חללה (see below) but does not make her a זונה. But the difference, according to most opinions, is purely a formal one, as a נבעלת לחײבי לאוין is, also according to תוספות and פסולה לכהונה ,רא״ש, in accordance with the canon: ובת כהן כי תהיה לאיש זר (Ch. 22,12); כיון שנבעלת לפסול לה פסלה (see there). Also גיורת and משוחררת as not having been born under the regime of Jewish marriage laws are אסור to a כהן (Yebamoth 61a, תוספות).

וחללה. If a כהן sins with one of the איסורי כהונה, a כהן הדיוט with a גרושה or a זונה, or a כה״ג with an אלמנה, the woman becomes a חללה and likewise any daughter that is born from such a union becomes a חללה and a son a חלל. Also the son or daughter of a חלל are חלל or חללה (also the wife of a חלל is, according to most opinions, פסולה לכהונה; according to רמב״ם she even comes under the concept of זונה). But the children of a חללה born to a לוי or to a ישראל cease to be חללים, and a daughter born from such a marriage would be בת חלל זכר פסולה מן הכהונה לעולם, ישראל שנשא .כשרה לכהונה ,חללה בתו כשרה לכהונה, חלל שנשא בת ישראל בתו פסולה לכהונה (Kiddushin 77a. — See on v. 15).

לא יקחו לא יקחו, this repeated admonition makes the legality of the marriages of the priests a duty not only to the priests themselves but also the concern of everybody (see v. 8), but primarily also of the woman who is associated with the illegal act, זונה ,חללה and מלמד שהאשה מוזהרת — ,גרושה על ידי האיש, (Yebamoth 84b). If a כהן marries a גרושה etc., she is equally punishable as the man. Thereby the general rule of ר׳ יהודה אמר רב that השוה הכתוב אשה לאיש לכל עונשין שבתורה is extended to apply also the לאוין שאינן שוין בכל. Its only exception is the prohibition of טומאה to a priest, which only applies to בני אהרן and not to בנות אהרן as well as the prohibition of בל תשחית פאת זקנך and בל תקיף, which only apply to the male sex. כל מצות ל״ת בין שהזמן גרמא בין שלא הזמן גרמא אחד האנשים ואחד הנשים חײבין חוץ מבל תקיף ובל תשחית ובל תטמא למתים, (Kiddushin 29a). On the other hand, where the פסול, e.g. a חלל may marry an אשה כשרה, she, too, may enter such a marriage, לא הוזהרו כשרות להנשא לפסולין, (Yebamoth 85a).

כי קדוש הוא לאלקיו, just as these laws concerning the priests begin in v. 1 in the singular, referring to the tribe of Aaron, so here, too, they finish in the same way in the singular. The tribe is holy to the Teachings of God which it is to represent inside and outside the Sanctuary, that is why the marriages by which it reproduces itself, and the family life it lives before the eyes of the people must clearly bear the stamp of the principles of that Teaching. Taking together the two special characteristics which mark the priestly tribe, the prohibition of טומאת מת and the איסורי כהונה, the idea is preached thereby that this tribe — whose mission it is ”להכין״ לבבו אל אלקיו, to keep the “basis” (כרן. I.L.), and the thoughts (כון. I.L.), of our lives always directed to God, — by keeping afar from טומאת מת is to establish the thoughts of the One Unique, Free, Personal God, and the morally free personality of Man as the basis of our whole life; and by the marriage prohibitions גרושה ,חללה ,זונה, chaste morality, priest-like holiness, and intimate living for one another, as the fundamental conditions of our family life, and thereby preserve the aims of our lives by itself also outside the Temple.

But these marriage-laws which primarily actually apply only to the priestly tribe have had the effect of making the narrower considerations of יוחסין ,יחוס, of morally pure descent, a point in the choice of suitable partners in marriage in the whole of the Jewish nation; and national experience has stamped predominating character-faults, such as feuds in families, quarrel-someness, disposition to slander, impertinence, hardheartedness, or misanthropy, as being also symptoms of doubtful purity of descent (see Eben Haezer 2).

V. 8. וקדשתו, this is addressed to the Jewish public in general. Thereby Jewish priests, with the observation of their priestly duties, are placed under the control of the public. מנין שאם לא רצה דפנו (פירש״י: הכהו וקדשו בעל כרחו), ת״ל וקדשתו כי את לחם וגו׳, (Yebamoth 88b). The holiness of the priest is a matter which concerns the nation; for the manner in which the whole national life is arranged to be pleasing to God, is to be made worthy of the nearness of God, which is to be expressed on behalf of the nation in the Temple, is the mission of the priest. His life in the midst of the people must be arranged in harmony with the principles of this arrangement of the national life. If he neglects that, the people themselves must keep him to it. His own desecration is a desecration of the national mission.

קדוש יהיה לך, but you, the people have also to pay tribute to the holiness of the priestly calling, by your behaviour towards the priests: לכל דבר שבקדושה לפתוח ראשון ולברך ראשון וליטול מנה יפה ראשון, everywhere where opportunity arises, to distinguish the priestly office in its rank and sanctity, רא״ש) ,בכל דבר שיראה גדול ומקודש Nedarim 62a). At the opening of any gathering or meeting, at pronouncing the ברכה over the reading of the תורה or at grace after meals, the כהן is to be given the first word, and at banquets he is to be served first (רא״ש ibid). In Nedarim there, in Gittin 59b, and elsewhere, the duty of thus distinguishing the priest is referred to וקדשתו of our verse. But Rashi takes קדוש יהיה לך to refer to this duty, and in that case, the ברײתא — as is often the case — would be quoting only the beginning of the verse (see Misrachi). According to תוספות (Chulin 87a וחײבו), this duty is only אסמכתא. But according to the most generally accepted view it is דאורײתא (see מ״א on א״ח, 202, 2). Moreover the Mishna itself teaches: כהן קודם ללוי ולוי לישראל וישראל קודם לממזר etc., and adds: אימתי בזמן שכולם שוים אבל אם היה ממזר תלמיד חכם וכהן גדול עם הארץ ממזר ת״ח קודם לכה״ג ע״ה, (Horaioth 63a). But with regards to קה״ת the rule is nevertheless that כהן קורא ראשון without making any differences, (א״ח 135, 3 & 4).

כי קדוש אני ה׳ מקדשכם. The holiness of the Jewish priests is not only not of such a nature that it does not exclude the holiness of the rest of the nation, but, on the contrary, it is just the holiness of the whole nation which is its root and its aim. The holiness of the life which the priest as such has symbolically to represent is what the whole nation, including the priests, has to live concretely in actual life.

V. 9. ובת איש כהן. In Ch. 22,12, it says: ובת כהן כי תהיה לאיש זר; if the daughter of a priest marries a non-priest. It considers her, there, at the moment when she goes out of her father’s house, into the house of her husband. She is still a בת כהן, has, at that moment the priestly character, but she loses it with her entry into her husband’s house. But here, in our case, it does not say בת כהן but בת איש כהן, the father is a כהן but she is such no longer, she does not belong to her father’s house, she is married. Even if she is married to a non-כהן, even to one through whom she has forfeited the כהונה-character for ever (see in Ch. 22,12), nevertheless, regarding the demands of morality she remains the daughter of a priest, and if she commits adultery she received a more severe punishment than she would if she was the daughter of a בת ישראל אשת איש שזנתה .ישראל is בחנק, but she is בשרפה, (see on Ch. 20,14). Sanhedrin 50b also limits our case to זנות עם זיקת הבעל, to the adultery of a married daughter of a priest and then it says (51a): אין לי אלא שניסת לכהן ניסת ללוי ולישראל לחלל ולממזר ולנתין מנין ת״ל ובת איש כהן אע״פ שאינה כהנת.
כי תחל, is, in any case an anomalous form, as the נפעל of חלל it should be תֵחַל, as the תַחֵל :הפעיל. we have translated it as the reflexive form of the נפעל.

V. 10—12. והכהן הגדול וגו׳. In Numb. 35,25 & 28 הכהן הגדול by itself is used to designate the High Priest. If here it is more precisely described as והכהן הגדול מאחיו, this would primarily be with reference to that which just preceded it; his companions in the office of priest, the כהנים הדיוטים, in the obligations of טומאת מת and of the איסורי כהונה which apply to them also, have certain concessions. For their nearest relations, wife, parents, children and siblings, not only may they, but they are to put their כהונה in the background; they may not have any permanent mark of mourning (קרחה), on the hair of their heads, or make any cut in their flesh on account of a death any more than any other person, but, like every other person among the people, they may give expression to their grief at their loss by a temporary neglect of the growth of their hair, and by a rent in their clothes (פריעה ופרימה), and are to give way to their pain and grief to the extent of not performing any עבודה while in the state of an אונן — indeed the עבודה would be פסול were a כהן to perform it during אנינות. Finally, their איסורי כהונה are limited to זונה ,חללה and אלמנה .גרושה is allowed to them and בתולה not demanded. All this is in accordance with their position as כהן הדיוט which is a preliminary stage to positive קדושה in a similar relation as the חצר is to the משכן, the עזרה to the היכל. But הכהן הגדול מאחיו, the priest who ranges above them all, who is to represent the כהונה in its highest positive stage, who, therefore, as is taught in Yoma 18a even before the anointing oil has dedicated him to the High-priesthood is to be גדול מאחיו, is to excel in bodily and spiritual qualities and in his socially independent position, בכח בנוי בחכמה ובעושר, so much so, that if the fortune necessary to ensure his independent position is lacking, גדלהו משל אחיו, his companions, the priests at whose head he is to be placed, are to see to it that he is provided with this wealth to render him financially independent; אשר יוצק וגו׳, who then has received personal dedication by שמן המשחה at the hands of the highest representation of the Nation, the Sanhedrin, and the authority to wear the בגדי כהונה גדולה by which he represents the symbolic expression of the highest positive ideal of life which is to be lived by the whole nation of Israel: he ceases to be just an individual Jew, and has to look on and appreciate also his private individual reactions primarily from the standpoint of the national ideas which he represents. These are to by so predominant in his life, that, where he has to give positive expression to them, personal feelings and frames of mind which would be disturbing to these ideals have to be kept back. The ideal of the National knows no death, אין צבור מת; in this idea of the immortality of the community, the individual who belongs to it, and lives for it, takes part. With every fibre of a faithfully lived mortal life he remains immortally interwoven with the undying nature of his community, and with the effect of his noble individuality he lives on immortally also here below after the bodily casing in which he visibly lived in its midst has fallen to dust when he had left it. And the man who has lost his wife, and with her his “home” his parents, children, brother or sister, and with them, his family, finds a home and family again in the national community to which he belongs, a sphere for his working and living, which can not be lost. But above all, the name “God”, Whose Sanctuary he serves, and Which he proclaims by the statement he bears on his forehead, elevates to that bright height of thoughts and feelings, which transforms the whole of ones existence with all its vicissitudes to a constant cheerful path of life which does not lead from the cradle to the grave, not from existence to non-existence, but from life to life, from immortality to immortality.

The priest, accordingly, הגדול מאחיו, who is placed on the very height of priesthood, who represents the priestly nation, on whose “head” the nation has poured the national oil dedicating him to belonging to God, and invested him with the “garments” of all the perfections of virtues, making him the symbol of the ideal model to be copied, he may not allow this head even temporarily to bear the signs of neglect caused by grief and mourning, he may not show himself rent in his “garments” even at his bitterest loss (פריעה and פרימה are clearly parallel to משיחה and לבישה), he may not approach the body even at the death of his nearest and dearest (only towards a מת מצוה does his כהונה גדולה also retire); even as an אונן, smitten with the deepest pain and grief, may he not forsake the עבודה; for everywhere and at all times is he to represent “Life” and the “joy of life” which is to find its source in God, and which is to be fostered in the national Sanctuary which He had established.

Not that he is to be free from human feelings, that he must allow the loss of the dearest members of his family to pass over him without touching his heart, that he, — just the one, who, as we shall see, even more than all the other priests, is to shine forth as the example of what married and family life should be, — is to find his greatness in cold indifference, where every pure human heart finds pain and grief, and every pure human eye drops tears. He does become אונן and accordingly, although he performs the ritual of the offerings, he may not enjoy the eating of קדשים, he is מקריב אונן ואינו אוכל (Horaioth 12b; see on Ch. 10,18 & 19); and although he may not give expression to the cleft in his immediate surrounding by קריעה in a conspicuous place in his garments למעלה, at his neck above his breast, פורם למטה, he does make a rent below at the seam (ibid); and although he does not directly join the cortege at the funeral, אינו יוצא אחר המטה, he still follows it at a distance until the gate of the city is reached, so that he enters each street as the funeral-train leaves it הן נכסין והוא נגלה הן נגלין והוא נכסה ויוצא עמהן עד פתח שער העיר, (Sanhedrin 18a).

But, at the same time, with the pain in his heart, and in the presence of these thoughts of death, he has all the more strikingly to teach the power of the “Life” that flows forth from God, and, with all its bitterness, the “joyousness” of life which flows forth from God, which the Sanctuary preaches, the Sanctuary whose first servant he is.

יוצק: the future tense of the ומלא וגו׳ ;הפעל: the past tense. The משיחה is to take place, but it is conditional on the unbroken blossoming of the Jewish national condition. Together with the ארון the צלוחית של שמן המשחה was hidden by King Josiah for future purer times, and thenceforth the consecration of the high-priests was performed solely by the investment with the garments, מרובה בגדים, (Kerithuth 5b). Only regarding פר הבא על כל המצות (the פר העלם דבר of the כהן המשיח, Ch. 4,3), is there any difference between a כה״ג מרובה בגדים and a כהן המשיח. The former has not the same position to the תורה and his שגגות are considered as being exactly the same as those of any יחיד of the people, (Horaioth 11b).
את ראשו ואת בגדיו וגו׳. See on Ch. 10,6. Also cf. on Ch. 19,28.

ועל כל נפשת מת לא יבא, this ביאה is טומאת אהל see on Numb. 19,14). לא יטמא is טומאת מגע. The plural and the stat. constr. of נפשות is difficult. The feminine plural is occasionally used to express a single abstract noun which shows itself in a plurality of ways. Thus we find חכמות בנתה ביתה (Prov. 9,1); חכמות נשים בנתה ביתה (ibid XIV,1). This refers to wisdom which has to show itself in the most varied conditions of life. This is even more the case when, as here, the plural form is written נפש מת .חסר would be the actual dead person. But נפשת מת is the human personality which is brought to mind by every dead body. If we consider that here, in the first instance, it is referring to טומאת אהל and that this טומאה, as no other does, rests on the mental conception of the human personality which reigns over a certain place, and everything in that space is impressed by the power of that personality, then we see why just here this singular-plural form is used. In Sanhedrin 4a we learn the Halacha that, although שני חצאי זיתים משני מתים together represent the idea of מת, and as such are מטמא, nevertheless: רביעית דם שיצא משני מתים do not represent נפש המת and only שני חצאי רביעית דם ממת אחד are together מטמא, and this law is traced back to the singular-plural form here: נפשת כתיב (see תוספות there). According to Misrachi, the נפשת מת is as much as saying: על רביעית דם של מת, then נפש would be the material which represents the נפש, (דם), and the verse would tell us that not only the whole body, but that every part of it which represents the נפש, (i.e. כזית or רביעית. I.L.), is מטמא באהל.

לאביו ולאמו וגו׳. By על כל נפשות מת it is already said that, in contrast to a כהן הדיוט, the טומאה-prohibition applies even to the near relatives. לאביו etc., is only mentioned to stress that it is only to even such near relatives that it applies, but not to a לאביו הוא דאינו מטמא אבל מטמא הוא :מת מצוה למת מצוה, (Nazir 47b).

מן הקדש לא יצא ולא יחלל, if the news of the death reaches him בשעת עבודה, he has not to leave the עבדוה and therefore may not leave it, for he is not מחלל את מקדש אלקיו if he performs the עבודה while he is an אונן, on the contrary, his leaving it would be a חלול. But for a כהן הדיוט, the reverse is the case אחר שלא יצא חילל, and if he were to do an עבודה as an אונן, his עבודה would be פסול, (Zebachim 16a).

This antithesis of אונן to the service in the Temple, which is so great that even an offering sent by an אונן may not be brought on his behalf: אונן אינו משלח קרבנותיו is one of those points which mark, in the most striking manner, the fundamental difference between the Jewish Temple of God, and all other religious institutions (see on Ch. 3,1).

כי נזר שמן וגו׳: his high-priestly dedication to God is a נזר to him. It is a consecrating crown which separates him from all others and raises him above all others. Even in moments of deepest pain it protects him from being overpowered by it, and allows him, even in such moments, to find the courage of living and the happiness in living to fulfil his עבודה which brings him near to his God, which the two words אני ה׳ grants to everybody who knows how to understand them truly, in a high-priestly way.
V. 13. והוא וגו׳. According to Yebamoth 58a, it must be a virgin maiden in the early נערה-age; not even if she has reached the age of בוגרת (see on Ex. 21,7).

V. 14. אלמנה, not even if only אלמנה גרושה חללה זונה .מן האירוסין, in this order these four איסורים could be combined in one and the same person, so that if a כה״ג were to marry her he would transgress four prohibitions, and would be liable separately for each one of them: בזמן שהן כסדר חײב על כל אחת ואחת. For she could have been a widow, married again, and then become divorced, then married a כהן which would make her a חללה and finally misbehaved in a manner which make her a זונה (see v. 7). For, if occurring in that order, each succeeding איסור is an איסור מוסיף in relation to the preceding one, inasmuch as it extends it, making something אסור to it which hitherto had been מותר. As an אלמנה she was only אסורה to a כה״ג, by becoming a גרושה she is so also to a כהן הדיוט, then, as חללה she is אסורה also regarding the eating of תרומה, and finally, the conception זונה is considered as הואיל ושם זונה פוסל בישראל ,מוסיף, because is can effect איסור beyond the כהונה, e.g. in cases of adultery, prohibited even to a non-priest. In the reverse order, starting with זונה, none of the other איסורים would apply, as with this first one all the conditions for all the איסורים are extant, and אין איסור חל על איסור אלא באיסור כולל או מוסיף או איסור בבת אחת, (Kiddushin 77a & b. — See on Ch. 7,24). Perhaps it is because of this that the ו is lacking at זונה, so that it could also be read:— an חללה-גרושה-אלמנה, who then becomes a זונה. But so that the איסורים should not appear to be forbidden only when thus cumulative it then says: את אלה לא יקח, by which each איסור is shown to be prohibited by itself.

מעמיו :כי אם בתולה מעמיו, from any tribe that he wishes, not only from the tribe of the Aaronides or Levites. That the Jewish High Priest had to be married has been already noted on Ch. 16,6 (refer to it, there). By the extension of the איסורי כהונה in the case of the כה״ג to include אלמנה, and the requirement to marry a נערה בתולה, to the general ideas of chastity, priestliness, and harmony, which, by the איסורי זונה חללה וגרושה, are to mark the marriages of the priests as pillars of Jewish married life, comes the further idea of the highest and most complete unison in views, sentiments and tendencies, inasmuch as אלמנה excludes any previous adaptation to the mode of life and the points of view of another man. The duty of the High Priest to marry a נערה בתולה makes him choose his wife at an age where it can be asumed that no thoughts of any other man would have entered her mind.

V. 15. ולא יחלל זרעו בעמיו. Kiddushin 77a teaches the Halacha that by transgression of the איסורי כהונה both the wife and the children become חלל and חללה. If, for instance, a כה״ג were to בא על אלמנה or a כהן הדיוט על גרושה, the woman as well as the daughter from such a union would be חללה and a son חלל. The same result is effected by the marriage of such a חלל-born son. חלל שנשא בת ישראל, his daughter, and according to most opinions also his widow, are פסולין לכהונה, and sons and grandsons etc., of a חלל are all מקיש זרעו לו מה הוא בתו פסולה אף בנו בתו פסולה [[illegible]]חללים. On the other hand if a חללה marries a ישראל, the daughter would be כשרה ישראל שנשא חללה בתו כשרה לכהונה :לכהונה (ibid). These laws, we believe, simply result from the conception חלל. For חלל designates the loss of the character of a priest brought about by a transgression of the priestly marriage laws. Naturally then, such a loss can only occur when the priestly character was there beforehand. But where, even before such a transgression took effect, there was already no priestly character there, the חלל-character can also not come into being. The wife and children of a כהן participate in the priestly character. Wife and daughter, as long as they belong to a כהן-house may eat תרומה and חזה ושוק, and the sons and son’s sons of a כהן throughout all generations are כהנים. But if one who is entitled to the rights of the כהונה is a חלל by his illegal birth and marries a בת ישראל then his wife and daughter, and son, and son’s son, forfeit their rights to כהונה benefits to which otherwise they would be entitled, and are חלל and חללה. If a בת כהן or an אלמנת כהן marries a ישראל, although the marriage is perfectly legal in every respect, nothing of the כהונה-character is transmitted to the offspring. Hence also if a חללה or a בת חללה marries a ישראל nothing of the חלל-character becomes transmitted to the children. This is what is meant by the saying: בני ישראל מקוה טהרה לחללות, but בנות ישראל are not מקוה טהרה לחללים, (ibid).

We believe the idea of this law can lie in the expression: חלל ודעו בעמיו. For ורעו בעמיו is the different position in the nation which the כהונה-character gives to the descendants of a כהן. Quite in the same way as above, in verses 1 & 4 the word בעמיו designates the difference to the rest of his people which a כהן has to have towards a מת. While they exercise all the living duties to the dead body, he has to stand afar. But the כהונה-character is transmitted only through the male descendant, from son to son. The duty of לא יחלל is therefore one which affects posterity to all eternity. But the children which the daughter of a כהן bears to a ישראל are no longer זרעו בעמיו, but they belong, through the ישראל-nature of their father, to עמיו. Hence the effect of לא יחלל does not reach them. In short, just like the כהונה-character, the חלל-character is only transmitted through the male line, from son to son, and ceases already in a granddaughter, if the father is a ישראל. This may also be the sense of the explanation given in Kiddushin 77a to the sentence: ישראל שנשא חללה בתו כשרה לכהונה חלל שנשא בת ישראל בתו פסולה לכוהנה, מנהני מילי אמר ר׳ יוחנן משום ר׳ שמעון נאמר כאן לא יחלל זרעו בעמיו ונאמר להלן לא יטמא בעל בעמיו מה להלן זכרים ולא נקבות אף כאן זכרים ולא נקבות.

A חלל has completely the character of a זר, of a non-כהן, and his relation to the Temple and all holy things, both within and without the Temple: בין קדשי מזבח בין קדשי גבול, so that תרומה is included. He is just the same as any non-כהן among the people. But the כהן himself, who by his illegal marriage has made the offspring of his marriage a חלל from birth, does not himself become a חלל, he retains the status of a priest (Kiddushin 77a). As long as he has not made his intention to break the marriage quite irrevocable by an oath that cannot be revoked, ידירנה הנאה על דעת רבים, he may not perform any עבודה (Bechoroth 45b) — as indeed in any case, any כהן is only entitled to כהונה-rights as long as he belongs to his priestly calling in letter and spirit, כל כהן שאינו מודה בעבודה אין לו חלק בכהונה, (Menachoth 18b; see on Ch. 7,33). But as Jewish priesthood is no profession chosen at will, but a calling, and a mission for life, which is given by God at birth, the worthiness, and the ability to carry out this mission which is dependent on it, can indeed temporarily cease, but it can never be entirely irrevocably lost. The removal of any temporary unworthiness is itself always the very first duty of the calling to which a כהן has been appointed by God, and a כהן pure-born, מזרע אהרן, can never cease having the calling to be a כהן. (Only a כהן שעבד ע״ז remains פסול לעבודה, Menachoth 109a). In exactly the same way for the priesthood as for the human race, one who is born a Jew can never lose the calling to be a Jew. As, for him, Judaism is no religion of choice, but a life-calling to which he has been appointed from birth by God, this calling and this mission can never cease to exist for him, אע״פ שחטא ישראל הוא. In his mind, his feelings, and way of life, he can estrange himself from this mission, in complete unfaithfulness he can turn his back to it, in such estrangement he can lose the worthiness and the ability to perform the acts which are presupposed to be activated by the mind, feelings, and way of life of the faithful Jew, but return to Jewish Truth in mind, feelings, and way of life, never cease to be the very first task of the life-mission which God has given him, and which can never be lost.

V. 16 & 17. איש מזרעל. Apart from the following defects, to qualify for עבודה, a priest must be איש, must have reached the age of manhood. Although this law is expressed by קטן פסול לעבודה אפילו תם, the priests allowed none of their sons to perform any עבודה until they were twenty years of age (Chulin 24b). — אשר יהיה בו מום: the idea of a מום is an externally visible bodily defect, מומין שבגלוי. Here the מזמין are reckoned which are preclusive for men, in the following chapter XXII, those for animals for קדשים and in Deut. 15,21 specially those for בכור. These three are all complementary to each other, and the defects reckoned in each case are only taken to be examples (Bechoroth 43 & 37a & b). All the defects which render an animal unfit for an offering apply also to the ability for men to perform the ritual of offerings, כל הפוסל בבהמה פוסל באדם, but יתר עליהן באדם, for human beings, the bodily perfection demanded goes farther. In verses 21, a כהן who has become unfit for service on account of a מום, is designated — apart from his מום — as an איש מזרע אהרן הכהן, i.e. an איש who is איש ששוה בזרעו של אהרן, as one who is not different in any other way from the rest of the descendants of Aaron, e.g. by having an abnormal shaped head, a hump etc., More, the Halacha recognises other bodily defects which should keep a כהן back from performing עבודה on account of מראית עין unpleasant appearance, such as lack of eyelashes, toothless, etc. שנשרו שניו ,שנשרו ריסי עיניו: So that for מומי אדם there are three classes, which differ as follows: (a) actual מומין which affect בהמה and אדם, these are מחיל עבודה any עבודה performed by a כהן so affected would be פסולה; (b) שאינו שוה בזרעו של אהרן, afflicted with deformities, the עבודה performed is not פסולה, but the כהן is לאו הבא מכלל עשה עשה) ,עובד בעשה. I.L.) or according to Maimonides, בלאו; (c) משום מראית עין, these should not do any עבודה, but if they do so, it is כשרה and they have not transgressed an עשה or a לאו. (Bechoroth 43a & b). — אשר יהיה בו מום, it makes no difference whether the defect is congenital or has occured later.

לא יקרב להקריב וגו׳. In a striking manner the prohibition for בעלי מומים to function as כהנים in the Temple is repeated three times, verses 17, 18, 21 & 23 and each in a different manner:— ,לא יגש להקריב להם אלקיו לא יקרב: לא יגש להקריב אשי ה׳, אל הפרוכת לא יבא ואל המזבח לא יגש, לחם אלקיו לא יגש להקריב. In these four places, the terms vary from לא יקרב to לא יגש, and also from לחם אלקיו to אשי ה׳.

קרב which occurs referring to things as well as persons, and expresses equally being near, getting nearer, and approaching, designates the nearing movement from the point of view of the purpose, the attempt to get into contact with some other object. Hence קרוב absolute near, in contrast to רחוק, far. נגש, on the other hand, which in the קל is only used of persons, and expresses their activity in getting near to a goal, looks on this activity from the point of view of the place from which one moves towards another, so that even one step in that direction is called נגש. The different aspects of the offerings which are expressed by לחם and אשה respectively, we have already tried to explain on Ch. 3,2. We believed that we could take it that לחם designates such a perfect condition of the human objects represented in an offering that they achieve God’s satisfaction and can bring God’s Presence into human circles; but אשה designates human objects which still require the purifying and forming work of the Fire of God’s Torah, that which is represented by the כליות and חלב, the איברים, the שמן ,סולת and לבונה, Man’s strivings and aims, his activities, his goods, and all his joy of life.

לא יקרב להקריב, looks on the celebrant as being of the same degree of godliness as that to which he is to raise the human being who is represented in the offering as לחם אלקיו. The כהן הדיוט, clad in the garments of purity, and girded with the emblem of striving for perfection, or the כהן גדול clad in the garments representing having achieved perfection, do represent just this degree of godliness to which the person, with every phrase of his life, seeking expression in an offering is to become לחם אלקיו. It is evident then, that the appearance of the כהן המקריב must not be in anyway a contradiction of the character which makes the קרבן worthy of הקרבה. Those מומים which render the בהמה unfit for a קרבן, make the כהן also unfit for הקרבה and a קרבן brought near to God by a כהן בעל מום is just as פסול as if the קרבן itself had a מום. We have already indicated on Ch. 1,3, the intimate relationship between the כהן המקריב and the קרבן, and have worked out the meaning of the bodily lack of imperfection for both. They express equally the completeness of the surrendering which is demanded from us, and the completeness of the life which is thereby to be gained in nearness to God. It is not the afflicted and the infirm, not the blind and the lame, the disfigured and crippled, the broken and the sick, for whom the Jewish Altar is erected, so that weary, burdened humanity can drag itself up to it to find compassionate consolation or even miraculous healing. It is life in its completeness, in its freshness and strength, which there is to gain consecration to an active life of God-serving deeds, and thereby acquire the everlasting freshness of youth and unbroken forces of life. Life and strength, not death and weakness, live at the Altars of God. They demand the surrendering of the whole human being to make man flourish in every phase of human life,אם שמוע תשמע לקול ה׳ אלקיך והישר בעיניו תעשה והאזנת למצותיו ושמרת כל חקיו כל המחלה אשר שמתי במצרים לא אשים עליך כי אני ה׳ רופאך, “if thou wilt diligently hearken unto the voice of thy God, and do what is right in His Eyes, and give ear unto His commandments and observe all His statutes”, so runs the very first sentence on the meaning and the power of God’s Laws, if you give up the whole of your life to fulfilling the whole of God’s Laws, then these laws will be the most prophylactic medicine against all physical and social ills which oppress the rest of mankind, this Torah will protect you: כי אני ה׳ רופאך. And it is this promise, and the conditions attendant to it which priests and offerings have continuously to illustrate and give a clear idea of in the Sanctuary of this Torah. That is why it must be perfect, complete men — not בעלי מום — who have to perform the offerings in this Sanctuary of the Torah, who — according to רמב״ם, see on v. 23 — may appear at all in the consecrated halls of this Temple. איש אשר יהיה בי מום לא יקרב להקריב לחם אלקיו, at the height at which the whole of human life has become לחם אלקיו, there are no broken men: כי כל איש אשר בו מום לא יקרב, for “a broken man” can not represent Man in the proximity of God.

And just as a בעל מום can not represnt Man as he blossoms out in the nearness to God, so also: לא יגש להקריב את אשי ה׳, so also can he not illustrate, give a clear idea of, the point of view from which nearness to God is to be sought. It is not to be only, and not in the first instance, the calamities of life which bring a Jew to seek God at His altars; and it is not to be only a life that is already broken, nor only a part of life, which is to be given over to the purifying and formative powers of the Fire of the Torah to become את לחם אלקיו לא יגש להקריב :לחם אלקיו, that which is to be formed to a perfection of life worthy for the proximity of God, must beforehand be striven for, and approached, from the standpoint of the whole of life.

We remarked on Ch. 1,3 that the conception תמים at offerings goes a good deal further than the mere negation of a מום, that it demands the inner perfection of the animal as well, and an animal that is מחוסר אבר בפנים is unfit for an offering, whereas in men it is only שבגלוי that renders them פסול. This inner state of completion in an animal is, as a rule, only recognizable when it is cut up. On the other hand the demand for physical completeness and freshness of life in the external appearance goes further in the case of men than it does for animals. Deformities and imperfections which do not affect an animal’s qualification for an offering — such as those understood under אינו שוה בזרע של אהרן, and משום מראית עין — do hinder the priest’s qualification to serve at the Altar. It is in its harmonious, healthy and attractive aspect, not deformed or unpleasant, that Man is to picture life in the proximity of God.

V. 18. כי כל איש וגו׳: see on previous verse. אשר בו מום: as long as he has the defect, even if it is not permanent, a מום קבוע, but merely a passing blemish, חרום — .(ת״כ) ,מום עובר: According to Bechoroth 43b, חרום is primarily one whose nasal bone has sunk so that the upper part of the nose is flat, שחוטמו שקוע בין עיניו, but it is, as all the defects mentioned in the text are, only meant to be an example and includes any deformity of the nose.—שרוע from שרע to stretch, is, according to Bechoroth 40a שנשתרבב לו ירכו, one whose one hip is stretched higher than the other.

V. 20. גבן. In Ch. 14,9, the position of the eyebrows is called גבות עיניו, the eyebrows themselves are called in Chaldean גבן .גבינים is, according to Bechoroth 43b, primarily one שיש לו בגינין הרבה, which Rashi explains there as meaning having the two eyebrows growing together without any space between, or שגביניו שוכבין, the brows being bushy and hanging down over the eyes. (According to Rashi’s explanation on זהו מדרש, both must be understood to be meant by the term). But any other deformities of the eyebrows are equally included.— דק, according to Rashi on Bechoroth 44a, מחסורירתא, a film or membrane in the eye which lessens the power of sight.— תבלל is, according to 38a ibid., a mixing of the white into the eyeball, that לבן פוסק בסירא ונכנס בשחור, a streak of white cuts across the iris and penetrates into the “black”. The reverse would not be a גרב וילפת —.מום, are according to 41a ibid., both incurable scabs. רמב״ן remarks: עור או פסח are examples of organic incompleteness; הרום או שרוע of organic malformation; שבר רגל or שבר יד of organic wounds; גבן או דק או תבלול of merely disfiguring malformation, (דק, according to him, is only having raised spots, גרעינין, in the eye which do not affect the eyesight), and גרב או ילפת, of skin diseases.
V. 21. כל איש וגו׳, see on v. 17.

V. 22. לחם אלקיו, after it has already become לחם, i.e. after the הקרבה has been done. A בעל מום is only excluded from הקרבה, but not from אכילת קדשים. Although the אכילה also belongs to, and is part of, the כפרה (see Ex. 29,33), it is still only the complementary result.

V. 23. אך אל הפרכת לא יבא. There is a difference of opinion between רמב״ם and רמב״ן in ל״ת ס״ט) ס׳ המצות), as to whether a בעל מום is forbidden to enter מן המזבח ולפנים at all, even simply going in, a ביאה ריקנית, or whether he is only excluded from עבודה (see מל״מ at the end of הל׳ ביאת מקדש, Ch. 9). המב״ם (there Ch. 6,1), prohibits the בעל מום even from ביאה ריקנית. Now if it appears from what he himself says in Ch. 9,1 that a זר would not be חײב אביאה ריקנית, although, as מל״מ remarks thereon, it seems impossible that then a כהן בעל מום would stand lower than a זר, the reason for this could well be found in the way we have sought to take the פסול בעל מום. A כהן clad in the בגדי כהונה within the space, מן המזבח ולפנים, i.e. בין האולם ולמזבח, or in the היכל, the places which form the real מקדש-משכן— (or as seems probable from the wording of the text ואל המזבח לא יגש, the Altar-space would be included as being part of the whole real עבודה-space, see מל״מ there 6,1), would represent there just by his character of a כהן and his מקדש-garments, “Man in the proximity of God”, and it is Man in the fullness of all the freshness of life, not crippled or hampered, not a בעל מום, who is able to represent Man blossoming out in the proximity of God. Any כהן בעל מום in these places, just because, as a כהן his belonging to the מקדש is stamped on his very person, would be, literally, as it says here, a חילול מקדשי, a desecration of places holy to God, near to God. But a זר has no such innate relation to the מקדש, he is not symbolic of anything there, and even a זר בעל מום—a crippled non-כהן—would in no wise bring any lessening of the idea of the holiness of the Sanctuary. Wessely, in his commentary expresses a similar thought. It must be remembered that even a כהן who has no מום may only enter the היכל for the purpose of עבודה (see on Ch. 16,2). So that for a כהן בעל מום this would only be further prohibited by a special לאו and extended by אל המזבח לא יגש also to the space in front of the היכל (probably to the whole of the thirty-two cubits of the Altar-space).

But according to the way the רמב״ן takes it, the אך אל הפרכת, would only prohibit the בעל מום from עבודה, and the מקדשי could not then refer to the places, but must, in an unusual manner only designate קדשים. But nevertheless it is possible that, as presumably the קרבן itself is brought into the מקדש in a תמים state, and the מום-idea which is against the מקדש-idea is brought to the offering just by the משרת מקדש, the כהן, the חילול הקדשים is a חילול of the מקדש. In any case it is declared thereby that the עבודה which a בעל מום performs is מחוללת.

כי אני ה׳ מקדשם, the object of מקדשם can only be מקדשי. It is ה׳, the Eternal Giver of ever fresh rejuvenation of existence and life, Who in the whole of His Personality, Himself sanctifies these places for such existence and life. A מום-imperfection in the men who, belonging to these places, perform the services in these places, would be contrary to the idea of the life, to foster which is just that which makes these places into מקדשי ה׳, would be חילול מקדשי as אני ה׳ מקדשם.
V. 24. This keeping the Jewish Sanctuary of God free from the idea of being a moral infirmary for crippled broken lives is here made the concern of the whole nation.

V. 2. וינזרו. The basic meaning of נזר definitely has the idea of exclusion from some sphere, and it is used both ways, derogatorily, as having no right to something, unauthorized, incompetent, and elevating, as standing above. Used in the קל and the נפעל the derogatory sense is predominant. נזרו אחור, Is. 1,4; נזורו מעלי, Ezek. 14,4; וינזרו מעלי ibid. 6; also הנזר in Zacc. 7,3; as an expression for fasting, which is really excluding oneself from food as having no right to take it, or being unworthy of being fed. Clearly נזר is almost identical with זור as נדה and נהם ,דוה and ,הום נמל and נסג ,מול and נסך ,סוג and נפח ,סיך and פוח etc. etc. The command וינזרו מקדשי בני ישראל, accordingly, makes the demand to the כהנים that they are not to consider themselves simply unconditionally entitled to the קדשים which are handed over to them by the people. They are times when they have to consider themselves excluded from them, to stand as זרים towards them, and may neither deal with them for the עבודה nor eat them. This is when they are in a condition of טומאה, which regarding אכילת קדשים בטומאת הגוף will be discussed in the following paragraph. But וינזרו refers equally to שימוש בטומאה as to תוספות) ,אכילה בטומאה Zebachim 15b). The almost identical meaning of נזר and זור, according to which וינזרו is taken to be the command “to hold themselves as זרים towards קדשים״, at times, may perhaps give an explanation which would render it possible to do without the extremely difficult way in which a dogma in Zebachim 15,b, is usually taken.

For, on the Mishna: כל הזבחים שקבלו דמן וכו׳ פסל, the Gemora says: זר מנלן דתנא לוי דבר אל אהרן ואל בניו וינזרו מקדשי בני ישראל וגו׳ בני ישראל למעוטי מאי וגו׳ אלא הכי קאמר וינזרו מקדשי בני ישראל ולא יחללו לימד על זר שעבד שחילל, so that there, the sentence addressed to Aaron and his sons is taken to give at the same time the same warning and the same results to זרים, to non-פהנים. So that זר ששימש and כהן טמא ששימש are מחללי עבודה quite equally. Now this is explained as if the words: וינזרו מקדשי בני ישראל ולא יחללו were divided to make a fresh sentence begin with בני ישראל. The וינזרו מקדשי referring to the כתנים בטומאתן and בני ישראל ולא יחללו, the זרים are לא יחללו (see Rashi there). But if the way we have taken the וינזרו is not erroneous, then in the וינזרו ולא יחללו directed to the כהנים בטומאתן, the פסול זר is immediately given: “the כהנים in their condition of טומאה are to consider themselves as זרים towards קדשים so that they should not מחלל עבודה״. Then, of course, it is self-understood that a זר שעבד חילל. To confirm this more deeply the text adds the words בני ישראל directed to קדשי to show how the idea of זרות altogether predominates in the sentence. It should have said more shortly and precisely: דבר אל אהרן ואל בניו וינזרו מן הקדשים. The addition of ישראל could be taken either in contrast to בנות ישראל or non-ישראל, or מהנים. It can not be to exclude נשים or נכרים to make טומאה not applicable to their קדשים, as קרבן נשים most certainly may not be קרב טומאה, and even if, as we shall see a little later on, the קדשי נכרים are excluded from the חיוב כרת of אכילת קדשים בטומאה, here the וינזרו refers to the general idea of keeping away when in a state of טומאה, which in the first instance has the performing of the עבודה in mind, so the קדשי בני ישראל can not be meant to exclude קדשי נכרים, for קדשי נכרים too, may not be offered בטומאה. So that בני ישראל here can only be in contrast to כהנים and thereby it is said: The בני ישראל, as non-כהנים, hand over their קדשים to the כהנים, because as זרים they can not offer them up themselves; but to the כהנים it is said: “וינזרו״, at times they have to keep themselves as זרים away from the קדשים of the בני ישראל which are handed over to them, ולא יחללו, so that they are not לימד על זר שעבד חילל ,מחללים. The thought that they are בני ישראל stresses the gravity of the responsibility of the כהנים. They are handed over to them because the בעלים are זרים and are they then to handle them in a condition where they themselves are equal to זרים?

ולא יחללו וגו׳ אשר וגו׳. The construction is difficult. It seems that אשר הם וגו׳ can only refer to the קדשי ב״י and then the ולא יחללו would be interposed between the object and relative pronoun אשר referring to it, a construction which is certainly not usual. But more probably the construction may be a normal one, and the אשר וגו׳ refer to the immediately preceding שם קדשי. For the expression שם, especially when referring to God, frequently goes beyond the conception “name” in its narrower sense, without fundamentally losing the sphere of that conception. A name is nothing other than the phonetic recognition and acknowledgement of a person or thing by means of the medium of sound. The name “tree” for instance, used for an object, teaches us to recognise it, is a means for its recognition. The name “father”, “master” etc., attached to a person, is a means for recognizing or acknowledging the same. Now the use of the word שם goes beyond the sphere of a mere phonetic and quite frequently designates every other means of recognition and acknowledgement. In Isaiah 55,13, the whole of the recognization of the conditions of life to be brought about by the Word of God, once it has been fully accomplished, is called : :God’s Name”, i.e. a permanent means of recognizing and acknowledging God: והיה לה׳ לשם לאות עולם לא יכרת. Jeremiah 33,9 says the re-established Jerusalem will become “a joyful Name of God”: והיתה לי לשם ששון etc.

In Sam. II 6,2 the Ark of the Covenant is actually called אשר נקרא שם :שם. That this is a sentence by itself and is not completed by the: שם וגו׳ עליו, which follows, is proved by Chron. I 13,6, where this addition is lacking and the sentence inverted:— את ארון האלקים ה׳ יושב הכרובים אשר נקרא שם. It seems rather that the שם ה׳ וגו׳ עליו is the explanatory reason of אשר נקרא שם in Sam. II 6,2 The Ark of the Covenant becomes שם, is called “the means of acknowledging God”, because the name ה׳ צבאות יושב הכרובים is borne by the ארון, i.e. the acknowledgement of God as ה׳ צבאות יושב הכרובים, rests on the Ark, on that which it represents and contains, and therefore it itself is called שם. According to this, too, the great idea which Jeremiah expressed in Ch. 3,16 & 17 explains itself. He said that the time would come when to acknowledge God and His Will one would not have to mention the Ark of the Covenant, not bring it to one’s mind, or think of it, one would not need it at all. What previously the Ark of the Covenant had been, that, then, would Jerusalem be. כסא ה׳ will Jerusalem be called, and to Jerusalem, as to the Name of God, would the nations stream: ונלוו אליה אל הגוים לשם ה׳ לירושלים etc. Previously, for Jerusalem, and in Jerusalem, and besides Jerusalem, the Ark, the ארון ברית ה׳, was necessary to keep the ideal of the Godly ideal way of human life at least symbolically present to the reality which fell so far short of it, and then the Ark of the Covenant was called כסא ה׳ and שם ה׳. But then, at the time Jeremiah prophesies, that which the ארון taught only symbolically will be actually lived in Jerusalem, and Jerusalem itself will become a כסא ה׳ and a שם ה׳. To recognise the Ruling of God, and what His Will is, one will only have to look at the life actually being lived in Jerusalem, and from there the recognition of God will penetrate so illuminatingly into the nations of the world, that thither, as to שם ה׳ to the means of getting to know God, the nations will stream: ולא ילכו עוד אחרי שרירות לבם הרע. More, the expressions which recur so frequently: להיות שמו שם ,לשכן שמו שם ,המקום אשר יבחר ה׳ לשום שמו שם, also show that fundamentally שם ה׳ is not simply the name of God, presented in word and thought, but that it describes any and every arrangement that serves as a means for the recognition and acknowledgement of God. The מקדש ,ארון and קדשיו are specially to be understood by it, they find their home in the place chosen by God, so that in consideration of them the place is called:— המקום אשר יבחר ה׳ לשום שמו שם.

Accordingly, we think that we can not be entirely mistaken if we believe that every object which is dedicated to God, which is, and is to be, nothing but the expression of the acknowledgement and recognition of that which God should be to us, and we are to Him, and especially here, where the קדשי בני ישראל are to be brought to the minds of the כהנים, to whom they are entrusted with the full meaning of their importance, these קדשי בני ישראל can also be understood as שם קדשו. Every animal dedicated to be a קרבן and every part of it is a שם קדש, is the expression of something holy in relation to God, and דבר אל אהרן ואל בניו וינזרו מקדשי בני ישראל ולא יחללו את שם קדשי אשר הם מקדישים לי, would mean: “speak unto Aaron and to his sons that they too, in times of טומאה hold themselves estranged from the holy things of the Children of Israel, and do not desecrate the holy expression of the relation to Me to which these קדשים are dedicated”.

In Zebachim 45b the necessity, for protecting the קדושה of a קרבן from חילול by טומאה, which by אשר מקדישים לי is extended over the whole of the קדש-object, is taken to apply in its widest extent, so that even דברים שאין חײבים עליהם משום פגול חײבין עליהם משום טמא. For the חווב פגול, i.e. the חיוב כרת על אכילת פגול is restricted to those parts of an offering: שיש להם מתירין בין לאדם בין למזבח, i.e. whose permission to be offered on the altar, or to be eaten, is conditional on some preceding עבודה, which in relation to them, is called their “מתיר״. Thus, by the preceding מתנות דם the אימורים and איברים are allowed to the מזבח and the בשר חטאת ושלמים to the מהנים and the בעלים, equally so by the הקטרת קומץ, the שירי מנחות to the כהנים. So that שירי מנחות ,בשר ,איברים ,אימורים, are things שיש להן מתירין, and who eats them as פגול is חײב כרת. But דם and קומץ are themselves מתירין and eating them as פגול does not entail כרת. The reason for this lies in the essential conception of פגול, which has its roots in the separation of the אכילת אדם או מזבח from the שחיטה or respectively the קמיצה (see on Ch. 7,18). But the חיוב על אכילת קדשים בטומאה extends over the whole קרבן in all its parts, even, according to the חכמים, to the עצים לבונה וקטורת, only one thing — and that is really most significant — is excepted, and that is דם! As the Jewish confession runs:— נשמה שנתת בי טהורה היא, so is that which represents this נשמה, the נפש in a קרבן untouchable by ,טומאה פגול ,נותר and מעילה. It is the personal godliness in Man, which can be overclouded by his ways of life and actions, but in its real deep nature remains pure and unreachable and always there, (Zebachim 45b & 46a; Maim. הל׳ פסולי המוקדשים 18,7 & 1,36; but see כ״מ thereon, and צאן קדשים on Zebachim 45b).— In all these נותר too, is the same as טומאה, and in Zebachim 46a, is included in the general idea of חלול in the proclamation: ולא יחללו את שם קדשי. How each little piece of נותר does represent a חלול שם קדש is shown on Ch. 7,17 & 18. There, too, the teachings of נתור ,פגול and טמא are taken together.

V. 3. אשר יקרב וגו׳ ונכרתה וגו׳. This forbidden approach to the קדשים אשר יקדישו וגו׳ with the penalty of כרת is not coming into contact by touch, but, as is made clear in the following verse, only אכילה. If the way we have taken the meaning of וינזרו is correct, — and this verse and the following ones are more detailed explanations of that proclamation — then, in any case the קריבה here could not possibly be “touching”.
