For here it explains how a כהן בטומאתו is to consider himself a זר towards קדשים. And a זר is not precluded from touching קדשים but certainly from אכילה and שימוש. It further says in Zebachim, following up that which we have already quoted on v. 2: — חײבין על הטומאה אפילו על דבר שאין לו מתירין יכול מיד ת״ל יקרב אמד ר״א וכי יש נוגע שהוא חײב אלא מה ת״ל יקרב בהוכשר ליקרב הכתוב מדבר הא כיצד יש לו מתירין משיקרבו מתירין אין לו מתירין משיקדש בכלי, i.e. here the חיוב כרת of אכילה is expressed by קריבה to tell us that the חיוב כרת is only incurred for אכילת קדשים בטומאת גוף, when these have been placed ready for הקרבה. If they have מתירין as אימורים, בשר, ושירי מנחה, then only after the מתירין have been offered; if they have none, as מנחת כהנים and נסכים, then as soon as they have been accepted in כלי מקדש for הקרבה. This detailed exposition seems to refer the word יקרב — the subject of which in the text is undoubtably the פהן — to the קדשים. We have expressed the thought above on XXI,7 on לא יקרב להקריב that at the moment of the הקרבה of a קרבן the כהן represents the degree of nearness to God, enters the stage of nearness to God, to which, through him, the קרבן is to be brought. The expression קריבה applied to the כהן would accordingly presuppose that something is already there ready for הקרבה, and אשר יקרב אל הקדשים אשר יקדישו וגו׳ can, just simply, only be said of such קדשים which are already הוכשרו ליקרב. That אכילת קדשים too, belongs to הקרבה and complements the כפרה has already been repeatedly remarked (see Ex. XXIX, on vv. 15 & 33).

טומאת הגוף ,וטומאתו עליו, see on Ch. 7,19 & 20. The whole teaching of אכילת קדשים בטומאת הגוף and בטומאת בשר of which the former is בכרת and the latter בלאו is developed there and we would refer our readers to it. Here the teaching is specially stressed for the כהנים and on that we would add a few remarks. In this chapter קדשים repeatedly have reference to בני ישראל added to them: וקדושו בני ישראל ,אשר הם מקדישים לי ,קדשי בני ישראל, and, unless we are mistaken, this is to give the priests a solemn warning against that mental conceited attitude with which priests regard themselves as the real bearers of the Sanctuary, and look down condescendingly on lay folk as being of less spiritual value; and those consecrated objects which these “lay folk” for “the benefit of their souls” entrust to them, they treat with scant holy enthusiasm. Here the Jewish priests are told that the whole Sanctuary itself, and everything in it which is holy to God, — with the exception of private personal קרבנות כהנים — has only become “holy” by the consecrating act of the people, either in its national capacity or by individual members of it. Whether it is קרבנות צבור or קרבנות יחיד, it is always the thoughts of the “lay-folk” which the priests have to carry out. And if our understanding of the ולא יחללו את שם קדשי of v. 2 is no erroneous one, in the tiniest particle of the קדשים of the very lowest man of the people, the priest has a שם קדש, has a name of God, written by a Jewish hand, has an object in his hand, which by an act of Jewish thought and Jewish will has become an expression of relationship to God, and as such must be treated with the whole respectful solemnity which every Name of God expects and demands. According to this we can also understand — even if, as remarked on v. 2, the קדשי עכו״ם no less than those of Jews, may only be treated בטהרה and have to be guarded against טומאה, and so are not excluded from the וינזרו-warning given to the priests — nevertheless קדשי עכו״ם could be excluded by אשר יקדישו בני ישראל from חיוב כרת על אכילת קדשים בטומאה which is here imposed, which is the opinion of ר״ש (whose opinion המב״ם accepts הל׳ פסולי מוקדשים 18,24, but see צ״ק ,כ״מ and תוספות י״ט). (See תוספות Zebachim 15b ד״ה אלא למעוטי). As the קדושה of a שם קודש is dependent on the disposition and intention which the writer is presumed to have (see Gittin 45b), it is understandable that, even if dedicated to ה׳, the full קדושה of a קדש is only innate by Jewish sanctification of it.

But just as, according to this view, the חיוב for טומאה would not apply to קדשי עכו״ם, so also, as נותר is included in חילל (v. 2), and as פגול is always so closely related to נתור, the חיוב would also equally not apply to פגול and נותר. Also מעילה would not be applicable to קדשי עכו״ם, and so perhaps קדשי עכו״ם stand predominantly in the idea of דם, with which also נותר ,פגול ,טומאה and מעילה lose their effect. It does not seem far-fetched to take it, that, in the non-Jewish point of view, one can assume that the relation of Man to God is more predominantly in devoting one’s דם, the נפש one’s personal inner self, one’s spiritual life, to God, from a feeling of dependence on Him, rather, than in the אימורים and איברים which preferably express the dedication of one’s actions to subordination under the Law of God. This would also agree with the further law that השוחטן בחוץ פטור. We have already repeatedly remarked that in שחוטי חוץ and איסור במה it is not so much the relation to God, as the relation to God’s Law, that is dishonoured. However ד׳ יוסי teaches (ibid.) also for קדשי עכו״ם that רואה אני בכולן להחמיר שנאמר בהן לה׳, that in all the named instances, קדשי עכו״ם and קדשי ישראל are quite the same, and the Halacha for all of them is undecided on this point (see on v. 18).

ונכרתה הנפש ההיא מלפני does not occur elsewhere. It always says: מעמיה, or something similar. Here it could be in significant reference to the sin of אכילת קדשים בטומאת הגוף. “I was not present in his mind when he dealt with קדשים, he did not see Me, שם קדשי, My Name imprinted on the קדשי ישראל, so he will be banned from My Presence”, — thereby the deep חלול השם of a כהן אוכל קדשים בטומאתו is brought home to him.

V. 4. איש איש מזרע אהרן וגו׳ בקדשים לא יאכל וגו׳. This according to Yebamoth 74a & b refers primarily to the prohibition of אכילת תרומה בטומאת הגוף, as being just those קדשים which are דבר ששוה בזרעו של אהרן, which are the most general and permanent “holies” which are specifically given to the whole family of the descendants of Aaron. מעשר שני and קדשים קלים are accessible also to non-קדש קדשים ,כהנים only to the זכרי כהונה and חזה ושוק become permanently lost to her in every case when a בת כהן marries a non-כהן (see on v. 13), even if she becomes a childless widow.

V. 5. שרץ אשר יטמא לו, even if only a part of a שרץ, as long as it has the minimum size requisite for טומאה, viz. באדם אשר יטמא לו .שיעור כעדשה could perhaps exclude any ראשון who although he is טמא does not מטמא anybody who touches him according to the rule that: אין אדם וכלים מקבלים טומאה אלא מאב הטומאה. The לכל טומאתו is to include all those אב הטומאה conditions which have not been mentioned such as נדה זבה יולדת ובועל נדה.

V. 6. נפש אשר תגע בו, on one of the indicated אבות הטומאה. He remains וטמאה עד הערב — ,טמא — until a new day has commenced, ולא יאכל מן הקדשים כי אם רחץ וגו׳: with the טבילה a certain class of קדשים is allowed to him, viz. מעשר שני which is why the passage is introduced by the addition of the comprehensive word נפש to איזהו דבר ששוה בכל :זרע אהרן נפש הוי אומר זה מעשר, (Yebamoth 74b).

V. 7. טהר יומא :ובא השמש וטהר (Berachoth 2b), i.e. the “unclean” day has completely passed, and a pure day dawns for him. :ואחר יאכל וגו׳ תרומה (see Yebamoth ibid.). Hence also תרומה :כי לחמו הוא, is that holy gift to which the כהן is primarily directed for his food, and which is given him directly as such, whereas the other קדשים only come to him indirectly, משלחן גבוה קא זכי (cf. v. 13).

תרומה may be eaten by the כהן as soon as העריב שמש even in the case of such טומאות which, as זבה ,נדה ,יולדת ,מצורע, are still מחוסרי כפרה, but קדשים only after the offering has been brought. In cases of טומאות which are not מחוסרי כפרה, the היתר comes for קדשים also with העריב שמש (see on Ch. 7,20).

V. 8. נבלה וטרפה וגו׳, see on Ch. 17,15. נבלת עוף טהור שמטמא בבית הבליעה, this טומאה has specially to be stressed, as it alone does not come under the headings of those mentioned here. But it may not be overlooked, all the more in the case of כהנים because, as is explained in Menachoth 45a in connection with Ez. 44,31: ואישתרי מליקה לגבײהו, because חטאת עוף may be eaten by them although the method of slaughter which is prescribed for them, everywhere else would render the meat נבלה (see on Ch. 1,15 & V,8). Altogether in connection with the preceding and succeeding verses it has to be brought home to the כהן whose לחם is תרומה, whose ordinary everyday food is a קדש which may not be eaten in טומאה, that while a non-כהן has only to be careful that his food is not an איסור, for him, the כהן, the care שלא לטמאה בה, is added to it.

V. 9. ושמרו את משמרתי. That which is לחמו, which is given to him as נכסי כהן and as food for himself and his dependents in the widest sense, so that he may even use it for food for his animals, is nevertheless, by virtue of his own character and what is innate to him משמרתי, something entrusted to him by God, towards which he has not only rights, but obligations. The קדש, the תרומה, which is called לחמו של כהן, is the one, amongst all the מתנות כהונה, on which the material existence of the priestly tribe is founded. It is ראשית, the first duty which lies on every member of the nation, in the use of the yearly produce of the land of the Nation when it is stacked (מירוח) ready for their use, to give to the ministers of the spiritual land of the Nation, the Sanctuary of the Torah. According to the majority of opinions (against that of Rambam, הל׳ תרומות 2,1), this duty מדאורײתא only applies to the main products of the land: דגן תירוש ויצהר grain, wine and oil. But the right of the priestly tribe to this provision for their existence is only a collective one. The tribe as such, the שבט, has the right to it. No individual priest has the right to demand it, or directly to collect it. טובת הנאה לבעלים. The one who is in duty-bound to give תרומה may give it to any כהן he likes. And this תרומה is a two-fold one, תרומה and תרומת מעשר, a direct and an indirect one. The direct one, the one to be given by the people to the priests is, as far as the amount to be given, מן התורה, left completely free to the giver. By giving one single grain of corn from the whole stack he has performed his duty: חטה אחת פוטרת את הכרי. So that this direct provision, called: תרומה גדולה, can by its very nature, only have symbolic meaning. The grain which he has heaped up for his own use, is prohibited to the farmer as טבל until he has thought of the tribe of the Sanctuary of God, by giving them some of it. And as he is מרים this gift, symbolically “raises” it, and calls it: תרומה, “something raised”, he endows it with participation in the קדושה which emanates from the Sanctuary of the Torah, and acknowledges this Torah and its institutions as “something higher”, superior, as something to which he has to subordinate himself with all the aims he achieves with his material powers and possessions; and realises that only by such acknowledgement do his possessions and the use he makes of them get any real purpose, meaning, and justification, in the eyes of God. And as the priest receives this symbol of acknowledgement and of the duty of providing for him, from the hands of the people, as a means of existence for himself and all his dependents, and at the same time has to treat it as קדש, this תרומה גדולה tells Jewish priests that, on the one hand, in his profession of priest he stands in the service of the people, but on the other hand, just this service places the whole of his every-day existence in the service of the Sanctuary of the Torah, and that he and those that belong to him, even in the most ordinary moments of life, are stamped with the impress of priestly sanctity and should be filled with the spirit of holiness and purity. That is — if we understand it correctly — the meaning of the לחמו הוא of our text referring back to ושמרו את משמרתי of v. 7. Whereas a non-כהן may look on his חולין-bread as the achievement of his own industry, blessed by God, every little piece of תרומה-bread is entrusted to the כהן as a reminder of his duty, a warning of the whole of the profession with which God has entrusted him.

But the actual means of existence of the כהן and his family seems to be based on תרומת מעשר, on the fixed תרומת-delivery which comes to the כהן indirectly from the people. For, out of the מעשר, the tenth part of all grain, wine, and oil which the people have to give to the Levites, the לוי has to give a tenth of it to the מעשר מן המעשר ,כהן as תרומה. And even if, according to Gittin 30b, the ישראל is allowed to take this תרומת מעשר out of the מעשר he separates for the לוי, and give it to the כהן, still as a rule the כהן receives it from the hands of the Levi, and even when he gets it from the hands of the ישראל he still only gets it out of the portion of the Levi. But as the מעשר again is prohibited to the לוי as טבל until the מעשר מן המעשר has been separated out of it for the כהן, and as this portion is מרים symbolically “raised” and called תרומה exactly as the תרומה גדולה from the ישראל and so endowed with a part of the קדושה of the Sanctuary of the Torah which the כהן represents and is exactly, like אסורה לזרים ,תרומה גדולה and אסורה בטומאה, and חײבים עליה מיתה וחומש; all this makes the לוי conscious that it is the Sanctuary of the Torah represented by the כהן to which he and his profession as a Levite are subordinated, and only thereby is it that his maintenance and position in the nation receives its justification, purpose, and meaning before God.

And as the priest receives this means of existence, which he has to treat as קדש, only from the Levites, he is to be made conscious that he, as priest, with his profession of priest and his position as priest, at rock bottom, only stands on the base of the tribal spirit of the tribe of לוי. He has to behave as the elite of that tribe which from the beginning showed the powerful fire of the communal spirit, which alone responded, when the nation had fallen to degenerate ways, to Moses’s cry: מי לה׳ אלי, and thereby ennobled itself for all time, as the champions and saviours of the ideas of God in the nation. As כהנים they may never cease to be לוײם, in spite of being dependent for their livelihood they must remain the most independent unintimidatable and unbribable representatives of God’s Torah in the nation. When the necessity arises they must be against the people, and know that the nation does not give them the bread for their maintenance for them to be fawning yes-men, agreeing to, and conniving at, all their weaknesses and errors, but so that, if needs must, they find in them stalwart, relentless fighters for the ideas of God and His Torah even in opposition to them. Of them, the greatest man in the world, who was also the greatest Levite, proclaimed that “Father and Mother they do not see, brother and children they do not recognise, when it is a matter of protecting God’s Word, of keeping His Covenant”. The bread which the nation hands them through the Levites is קדש, is holy to the Sanctuary of the Torah, it places the one who receives it for his holy food, with all those who belong to him in the levitical service of the Santuary of the Torah — woe the priest who does not keep the holy bread of his existence holy, woe the priest to whom every particle of this holy bread does not call him to attention in his holy calling, woe the priest who desecrates it: ושמרו את משמרתי ולא ישאו עליו חטא ומתו בו כי יחללוהו, it touches his very life, does he desecrate it, it spells Death.

בעשרים וארבע מקומות, in twenty four places, it says in Gittin 86b: נקראו כהנים לוים, the priests are called Levites, and וזה אחד מהם, and one of them is this verse in Ez. 54,15 & 16: והכהנים הלוים בני צדוק אשר שמרו את משמרת מקדשי בתעות ישראל מעלי המה יקרבו אלי לשרתני ועמדו לפני להקריב לי חלב ודם נאם ה׳ אלהים המה יבאו אל מקדשי והמה יקרבו אל שלחני לשרתני ושמרו את משמרתי, “the priests, the Levites, the sons of Zadok who have kept the guard of My Sanctuary when the Children of Israel erred and strayed away from Me, they shall approach Me to serve Me, they shall stand before Me, to bring “fat and blood” near unto Me”, sayeth God, “they shall enter My Sanctuary, they shall approach My Table to minister unto Me, and to guard that which I entrust unto them”. The true כהנים are just the לוים par excellence.
עליו :ולא ישאו עליו חטא, i.e. on משמרתי, or rather, as משמרת is feminine, and also as the בו which follows must refer to a masculine subject, on לחם משמרתי.

ומתו בו כי יחללהו, this is מיתה בידי שמים. Although otherwise מיתה האמורה בתורה סתם חנק, and we find the death penalty to be inflicted by the human court expressed not only in the passive יומת, but also in the active mood, intransitively ומת, e.g. Deut. 17,12 XVIII,20, XXII,5 & XXIV,7 still in those cases the construction is different. In all these cases, the doing of the sin comes first and the ומת is the imperative apodosis: אך הנביא אשר יזיד וגו׳ ומת האיש ההוא etc. But, here the ומתו בו is still part of the preceding warning, it is assertive, not imperative, “they will die”, not “they are to die”. This is also indicated by the ומתו בו, by which their office, or the bread of their office, is designated as the cause of their death, if they desecrate it. If this ומתו meant to impose their death by human justice, it would simply have said ומתו. What is primarily said here is: האוכל תרומה טהורה בטומאת הגוף חײב מיתה בידי שמים, the reason given: כי יחללוהו, excludes eating תרומה טמאה from מיתה as it is already מחוללת (Sanhedrin 83a), פרט לזו שמחוללת ועומדת. But as we believed that eating תרומה as לחם משמרת ה׳ brings to the mind of the כהן the duties of his calling, and a חילול of the תרומה corresponds to the idea of a חילול of משמרת so we find in the Gemora there, that actual sins against his office which are designated as חילול by the Torah, such as טמא טבול-יום ששימש, are taken to be included in the penalty of מיתה בידי שמים of our ומתו בו כי יליף חילול חילול מתרומה : יחללוהו.

V. 10. זר is any non-קדש ;כהן here, in accordance with the whole of the preceding and succeeding verses, refers to תושב כהן .תרומה is a non-כהן who has become a permanent member of the house of a קנוי קנין ,כהן עולם, e.g. an עבד עברי שנרצע (Ex. 21,6). שכיר, a servant who is only hired by him by the year, קנוי קנין שנים, e.g. an עבד עברי יוצא בשש (ibid v. 2; Yebamoth 70a). Both these classes only belong to the כהן with their work, but not with themselves, לא קני ליה רביה, their master has not bought them. Although to become free, the עבד עברי also requires a bill of divorcement, a גט שחרור (תוספות ibid b), nevertheless he does not participate in the personality of the כהן to such a degree that he loses the character of being a זר.

V. 11. נפש קנין כספו, are all such creatures who have been acquired in such a manner that they become completely part and parcel of the personality of the כהן. These are on the one hand עבד כנעני and בהמה, real slaves and animals, and on the other, his wife, even from the moment of personal betrothal. אירוסין ,קידושין, although the real complete marriage, the groom taking his bride into his home (symbolised by חופה. I.L.), has not yet taken place (Yebamoth 66a). Nevertheless מדרבנן, the permission for a ישראלית to eat תרומה only starts when she has symbolically shared a home with him: אין האשה אוכלת בתרומה עד שתכנס לחופה. The reasons for this are given as either משום סמפון, conditions might arise which would render the קידושין invalid, or: שמא ימזגו לה כוס בבית אביה ותשקה לאחיה ולאחותה, as long as she has not been brought to her husband’s house and is still living with her parents, if she were allowed to have תרומה, it could easily happen that she might give a piece of the cake, or a sip of the wine, to her brother or sister (Ketuvoth 57a & b). It is further taught in Yebamoth 66a & 67a, that those who, as קנין כספו or יליד ביתו, acquire the right to eat תרומה are regarded as partaking the character of a priestly home to such a degree that they, as our text puts it: הם יאכלו לחמו, they eat this food as in their own right, so that not only יאכלו, but like the כהן himself, יאכילו, have the right to share it with any creature that belongs to them, and is part of their personality: קנין אוכל מאכיל. Hence the wife of a כהן who acquires slaves or animals in her own right, or a slave of a כהן who does so, may feed them with אשת כהן שקנתה עבדים ועבדיו שקנו עבדים יאכלו בתרומה :תרומה (ibid). Also the wife of a כהן or his slave is entitled מן התורה independently to receive תרומה for themselves (Yebamoth 99b).

V. 12. איש זר .ובת כהן וגו׳ is primarily any non-תרומת הקדשים .כהן is not ordinary תרומה, but מורם מן הקדשים, that which is lifted out of the קדשים. This is the חזה ושוק which is lifted out of קדשים קלים and given as food for the כהן and all the members of his household. Our verse tells us that as soon as a בת כהן has married a non-כהן she loses for ever the permission to eat of חזה ושוק, even in the case treated in the following verse, where, after the death of her husband, and having no children, she returns to her parents home and may again eat כשהיא חוזרת חוזרת לתרומה ואינה חוזרת. תרומה לחזה ושוק (Yebamoth 87a). But this whole law would be learnt out of the following verse. For from ושבה אל בית אביה the prohibition to eat תרומה whilst still married to a non-כהן is clearly evident, but the prohibition being a לאו הבא מכלל עשה would only have the power of an עשה, but then the final clause: וכל זר לא יאכל בו, would raise the prohibition for as long as she is reckoned as a זר, i.e. during this marriage, to the degree of a לאו. Even the limitation of the permission, to תרומה only, could also be learnt from this verse from the term מלחם אביה, either from the limiting מ (only part of her father’s food), or because חזה ושוק altogether fail to come under the term: לחם אביה, as these משלחן גבוה קא זכי, (see ibid 68a & b, and 87a). The Gemora accordingly teaches us (ibid 68a), to apply the איש זר of our sentence: ובת כהן כי תהיה לאיש זר וגו׳, to the illegality of the marriage, as a description of an איש שהוא זר לה, a man who should have remained a זר to her, who was פסול לה, and so give the sentence the additional meaning that כיון שנבעלה לפסול לה פסלה. That, just as the legal marriage with a non-כהן precludes a בת כהן from eating תרומה and קדשים for its duration, and from חזה ושוק for all time, so does any illegal sexual association with any man who would not be permitted to marry her, exclude her for all time from eating תרומה and קדשים, and precludes a לויה or a ישראלית altogether from the כהונה, i.e. from marrying a כהן, (see on XXI,7).

V. 13. See on v. 12 — וזרע אין לה, not only son or daughter, but also grandchildren etc. By the most distant offspring of her marriage to the non-כהן she still belongs to his family and is not שבה אל בית אביה כנעוריה (Yebamoth 70a). But in the same way that the offspring of the marriage of a בת כהן and a non-כהן exclude her from תרומה even after his death, as keeping her still attached to his home, so does the offspring of the marriage of a בת ישראל to a כהן, even after his death, constitute a bond which joins her to the home of the כהן and gives her permission to eat תרומה until either she marries again, but to a non-כהן, or there is no longer any offspring of the marriage living. For the duration of such a second marriage or during the lifetime of any offspring from it, the right to eat תרומה ceases. But if this marriage ends without any offspring, if there is still an offspring of her first marriage with the כהן living, she can return again to his home with the right to eat תרומה, and indeed without the restrictions of a returning בת כהן, but she can eat even כשהיא חוזרת .חזה ושוק לבית אביה חוזרת לתרומה ואינה חוזרת לחזה ושוק, בשביל בנה חוזרת אף לחזה ושוק, (Yebamoth 86b & 87a).

V. 14. ואיש כי יאכל קדש: this קדש is תרומה with which this whole chapter is primarily dealing. Unlawful eating קדשי מזבח or using קדשי בדק הבית comes under the heading of מעילה which was dealt with in Ch. 5,1[[illegible]] et seq. Here the Torah speaks of שאכל תרומה and tells us that if it was בשגגה, he has to pay קרן and חומש. Moreover: ונתן לכהן את הקדש, the קרן וחומש which he has to pay is again to be קדש, i.e. תרומה. Accordingly, he has to pay דבר הראוי להיות קדש, i.e. פירות של חולין which then become תרומה. In Pesachim 32a the question is discussed whether this payment which has to be made is לפי מדה or לפי דמים, whether the quantity of the תרומה which he had eaten בשגגה comes into consideration or the value. If, for instance, someone eats תרומת חמץ בפסח בשוגג which, as חמץ בפסח is אסור בהנאה and therefore completely valueless, if לפי מדה משלם, he would nevertheless have to pay קרן וחומש, but if לפי מדה משלם, he would have to pay nothing at all. This קרן וחומש payment is not to be taken so much as compensation to the כהן as atoning restoration (כפרה) of the conception of the holiness of the תרומה against which he had sinned by mistake. This is also the reason why אם רצה הכהן למחול אינו מוחל, the כהן has no authorisation to remit the payment if he wished to do so. Also it is only the קרן which has to be paid to the כהן whose property the תרומה had been, the חומש may be given to any כהן one prefers (Terumoth 6,1, 2, and Pesachim 29a ד״ה יש אומרים). He who eats תרומה במזיד has only simply to pay the קרן, its value, this compensation remains חולין and אם רצה הכהן למחול מוחל, if the כהן wishes to, he can remit the payment. But this duty of repayment is only incurred when, in the case of there being no התראה, no punishment of מלקות can be imposed, otherwise the offender would get מלקות and not have to pay anything, in accordance with the canon: דאינו לוקה ומשלם. This is the rule, that no crime gets punished from two aspects of it, the criminal offence and the civil one: ,משום רשעה אחת אתה מחײבו ואי אתה מהײבו משום שתי רשעיות see on Deut. 25,2, and: כל היכא דאיכא ממון ומלקות ואתרו ביה מילקא לקי ממונא לא משלם (Kethuboth 32a & b). In Baba Mezia 99b this imposition of חומש is only made where the תרומה is eaten, but damage to it, is free from חומש, as the text says: כי יאכל, which is taken פרט למזיק. More, according to תוספות ibid, מזיק תרומה is like all damage to קדשים is entirely free from compensation, as was explained on Ex. 21,36: נזקין להדיוט ואין נזקין להקדש. For notes on חומש, see on Ch. 6,16.

V. 15. ולא יחללו וגו׳ את אשר ירימו לה׳. In Sanhedrin 82a, the אשר ירימו לה׳ is explained as being in the future tense בעתידים לתרום הכתוב מדבר, the holy parts which have yet to be raised out of the fruits, i.e. produce from which תרומה and תרומת מעשר have not yet been taken out, in which condition it is called טבל, and here we are taught that אכילת טבל comes under the conception of חילול as much as the eating of תרומה itself by a זר or בטומאה and incurs the penalty of מיתה בידי שמים (see on v. 9). Even if תרומה has been taken, but the מעשרות have not yet been separated out, the whole is forbidden to be eaten, is still טבל. Whether then eating it, whether such טבל would be חײב מיתה is not quite sure (see רש״י and תוספות on Yebamoth 86a and against them רמב״ם מאכלות אסורות). This prohibition of eating is quite universal and applies to the כהן as much as to the ישראל (ספרי on Numb. 18,28). From his own fruit too, the כהן may not eat as טבל, but has to separate תרומות ומעשרות from them before eating from them although he himself may keep and eat that which he has separated out (see הלכות מעשר 1,4). טבל as well as תרומה לזר is, as תוספות repeatedly remarks (Sabbath 26a ד״ה אין מדליקין and elsewhere) only אסור באכילה but not אסור בהנאה, only any use which would destroy it, הנאה של כילוי such as להאכיל בהמתו would be אסור. But included in the prohibition of ,אכילה שתיה and סיכה are of course to be understood, (Nidda 32a). Nevertheless תשלומין, both the קרן and the חומש does not apply to טבל; only את אשר ירימו is לה׳, hence אין לך בהן אלא משעת תרומה ואילך (Chulin 130b).

V. 16. אותם .והשיאו אותם עון אשמה reflexive, themselves (Sifri on Numb. 6,13). אני ה׳ מקדשם: the קדשים. This concluding verse includes all the regulations given in this chapter regarding the eating of תרומה both for the כהנים and for the זרים, and gives the general result of breaking these regulations as the conception of אשמה.

We know the idea of אשם as the sins whereby the whole future of the happy blossoming out of life is threatened with desolation. We saw in Ch. 5,14—26 that this idea is specially prominent where one has enriched oneself by indifference to, or taking possession of, holy things, of things which have been dedicated to holy purposes. There, too, the thought is expressed that the blossoming out of one’s own sphere of existence can only be hoped for, and have a future, if everything which is made holy in the name of the Torah of God receives conscientious careful treatment and consideration.

That is exactly what is stated here as the concluding warning against any carelessness in using food for oneself and transgressing the limits which the institution of תרומה places on the capricious use of one’s own food.

If we realise the principles of this institution which are laid down for us in this chapter, both regarding those who are in duty bound to give תרומה and those who are entitled to receive it, all the basic fundamental foundation which is necessary for all progressive development to a material and spiritual achievement of a happy private everyday life seems to be given.

The produce which is stacked ready for the provision of his home is unapproachable for its use as food until the owner, by the תרומה symbol and the תרומה-מעשר gift, has demonstrated to himself the provision for his household as being subordinate to the holy ideas of the Torah, and has separated a contribution for the existence of representatives of the Sanctuary of the Torah. Thereby this Sanctuary of the Torah and its demand become the “superior”, that which rules over his private life. Every little piece of תרומה which he has to separate brings this thought afresh home to him, that it remains prohibited for him to eat it, as a זד, and any careless infringement of such homage and recognition must be restored by קרן וחומש.

This homage and recognition of the Sanctuary of the Torah forms the fundamental condition for the “blossoming of the happiness” of the home. והשיאו אותם עון אשמה באכלם את קדשיהם, all who refuse this homage and recognition by profane enjoyment of its holy things load themselves with אשמה, the prospect of desolation and unhappiness.

But for the priest himself and his household this institution of תרומה forms, even more, an ever-present admonition to everything on which the material and spiritual thriving and happy development of a priestly home depends. It immediately tells the priest, inasmuch as his own produce is טבל and אסור to him as long as he has not separated תרומות ומעשרות from it, that he has to represent the Sanctuary of the Torah in no less degree to himself than towards the people. And if, as we have already worked out on v. 9, תרומה is quite specifically לחם משמרתו food which is constantly to be a reminder to him of the duties of his office, all the members of his household whom he can call “his own”, by partaking of it, nay more, by being entitled to receive this priestly bread in their own right, are raised up into the sphere of a priestly position in life. They, too, are to realise, by the condition imposed for using it, the regime of טומאה and טהרה which must surround the whole of their lives and actions, and its whole effect on the spiritual and moral elevation of their lives, (as we have tried to sketch on Ch. XI). Altogether the institution of תרומה must tend to exercise a deep education and moralising influence on even the very lowest member of a priest’s household: והשיאו אתם עון אשמה באבלם את קדשיהם, and impress them with the idea of how heavily they are loading themselves with the prospect of אשמה, “desolation and unhappiness”, if they profane their holy things by enjoying them as טבל or in a state of טומאה.

The role of woman in this institution is characteristic. As, in accordance with the saying of the rabbis ביתו זו אשתו, “a man’s house is … his wife”, and children, בנים, form the building-bricks of the home and effect the real purpose of the home, we find that the wife, in this institution, always completely bears the character of the house, and after the death of the husband retains this character as long as there is some offspring of the marriage — even the most distant one — still alive, as Mother, Grandmother, Great-grandmother, Great-great-grandmother etc., her status in this respect is quite unaltered. In this manner a בת ישראל becomes a כהנת; a בת כהן, a ישראלית, and in her new position in life has to prove herself worthy, in the one case of the priestly calling, and in the other of the ישראל calling. And as, the higher the degree of any holiness is, the more sensitive it is to desecration, and the more receptive it is to being profaned, so the higher degree of holiness of the woman’s position in life for the mission of a priest’s home shows itself in the loss of qualification and right to תרומה and מהונה by any הויה לאיש זר, by any sexual lapse with anybody who is פסול לה. Only in one small matter does a fallen בת כהן retain her original character of a כהן as an admonition of her former priestly calling, in that — similarly to a בת כהן שנשאת לישראל — if she mistakenly eats תרומה she does not have to pay קרן and חומש as a זר does, but only has to pay the קרן (Terumoth 7,2).

But over this whole institution hovers the fact, the significant fact, that only אכילת תרומה בשוגג, that only profanely eating תרומה by mistake demands restitution of the profaned holy object by קרן וחומש, both of which become תרומה. But in the case of אכילת תרומה במזיד intentional profane eating, the holy object makes no demand for restitution as such, and the case is simply treated as an offence against the private property of the כהן. Moreover for מזיק תרומה, for unintentional “damaging” תרומה — as, in general for all נזקי הקדש, for damaging any Jewish holy object — according to the Torah, there is no claimant and no judge on earth, to demand or impose payment! God reserves His own punishing judgment for wrong done to His holy objects. He has appointed no human hand to administer punishment for it, not even to demand compensation on His behalf. This is the most striking stamp of their belonging to God on Jewish holy objects; they require no human representative! (See notes on Ex. 21,36; cf. also remarks made above on Ch. V, on the related מעילה-canon: הקדש בשוגג מתהלל במזיד אינו מתהלל).

V. 17. In the previous chapter, verses 16—24, the necessary “bodily perfection”, the absence of bodily faults of the priests as a condition for their being allowed to function in the Sanctuary, was discussed. Now here follows the corresponding demand for the same condition for the animals brought for sacrifices. This condition has already been remarked in the general term תמים in the first chapter on the offerings, and here we are given more precise details. We have discussed the meaning and the necessity of the paragraph which follows here, on Ch. 1,3, and would refer to that.

V. 18. איש איש. By this universal generalisation, נכרים are included, שנודרים נדרים ונדבות כישראל, that they, too, although heathens, can bring free-will offerings in the Jewish Sanctuary of God, as indeed is also implied in v. 25 by the instructions to the priests also not to accept animals with מומים, as offerings from them. The Jewish Altar being open for the reception of offering from all men is indeed already indicated in the very first words of the giving of the facts of offerings אדם כי יקריב וגו׳ in Ch. 1,2 (see notes there). This inclusion of the right of נכרים to bring free-will offerings is indicated here under the heading of עולה, to tell us at the same time that the offerings of non-Jews are limited to עולות, as is said in Menachoth (ibid), אשר יקריבו לה׳ לעולה אין לי אלא עולה בלבד, that the offerings which נכרים bring are only to be offered as עולות; so much so that even (ibid) שלמי נכרים עולות, that even if a נכרי brings a שלמים it is to be offered only as an עולה. The reason given is that נכרי לבו לשמים, that one can only assume in him that he has the sacrificial idea of giving himself up entirely to God, but not that he has the specifically Jewish idea that it is even, nay, that it is just in the happy, joyful, moral enjoyment of the earthly material human life, looking up to God with it, as is expressed by a שלמים-offering, wherein lies the true Divine Service. We have had repeated opportunities of referring to this characteristic difference between the Jewish and the heathen aspect of God and Life (see on Ch. 3,1).

לכל נדריהם ולכל נדבותם וגו׳ (see Ch. 7,16). Here the more precise details of the מומים-law are given for free-willed offerings, and apply all the more to duty-offerings. Even where there is no consciousness of previous lack of attention to duty in life, the representation of devoting the whole of one’s life to duty (תמים) is demanded. This alone makes one worthy to come near to God, as it is just the devotion of one’s life in its “entirety” which is adequate to the expression of this demand. It alone is the purest and most direct corollary of the “oneness” of God: the complete unity of life for the complete “oneness” of God, (see on Ch. 1,3).

V. 19. לרצונכם וגו׳ (see Ch. 1,3). תמות וזכרות :בבקר בכשבים ובעזים בבהמה ואין תמות וזכרות בעופות, the demand תמים and זכר is limited to קרבן בהמה only, at an offering of birds, the sex is immaterial, and also the פסול מום does not apply to עוף as it does to בהמה. Nevertheless מחוסר אבר, the loss of a whole limb, as יבשה גפה, נקטעה רגלה, נחטטה עינה, a withered wing, a broken-off leg, a lost eye — ברמב״ם איתא ניסמית עינו (a blind eye), ,והוא על פי הגירסא דת״כ אכן בש״ס קידושין כ״ד ב׳ איתא נחטטה עינה וכן מוכח מתוך הסוגיא עי׳ רש״י ותוספות שם דעינה סמויה לא פסלה ע״ש — does make a bird unfit for a קרבן, which is indicated by the selective particle ואם :מן מן העוף וגו׳ (Ch. 1,14, see there and on v.17).

V. 20. לא תקריבו (see on Ch. 1,3 יקריבנו). The פסול בעל מום is specially expressly forbidden in all stages of the הקרבה in verses 20, 22 & 24. These are the three progressive stages of the הקדיש, the שחיטה, the זריקה, and apart from these, again specially for the ואשה לא תתנו מהם :הקטרה, and indeed not only תתנום, but even מהם, even מקצתו, not even a tiny part of a מכאן אמרו המקדיש בעלי מומין לגבי מזבח עובר משום ה׳ שמות משום בל .בעל מום תקדישו בל תשחטו ומשום בל תזרקו ומשום בל תקטירו כולו ומשום בל תקטירו מקצתו (Temura 6b). In the הקטרה of the אימורים or the איברים the living organism and its relation to life which is represented thereby is more prominently stressed than in the עבודת הדם, the completeness with which it is given up to the Fire of the Torah is just what seems denied by בעל מום.

V. 21. That which was said in vv. 18—20 in connection with the עולה is here repeated again specially for שלמים. Not only for an עולה the special expression for dedicating one’s actions, which is brought from the consciousness of insufficient devotion, but also for שלמים, where this devotion only seeks one’s actions being raised to a higher level on the basis of the consciousness of one’s happy fate in life, is the “completeness” of devotion the absolutely necessary preliminary condition.

לפלא נדר. On Gen. XVII, we have already pointed out the connection of the meaning of פלא, a wonder, with the specific use of this root here and in Numb. 6,2 for the act of making a vow. פלא is an act of God which, completely beyond any connection with the existing order of things, comes as a pure act of the Will of His Almightiness. נדר, a vow, is an intention which is independent of the commands of duty which otherwise rule a person’s will, and comes as a pure act of his will; a freely made duty which he imposes on himself. On Gen. 8,18 we have also already indicated the relationship of the roots פלח ,פלה ,פלא, all of which express a sharp and definite separating. From Numb. 6,2: כי יפלא לנדור נדד וגו׳, it is definitely clear that פלא נדד does not refer to the act of fulfilling a vow, here the bringing of the promised offering, but describes the act of actually making the vow. So that the ל- here, לפלא, can not be the ל- of intention “to vow etc.”, but can only designate the relationship of the הקרבה, to a previously made נדר. There had been a פלא נדר or a נדבה, a vow to bring an offering: הרי עלי שלמים, or a dedication of an offering: הרי זו שלמים, and now the animal is brought to be offered as a result of such vow or dedication. כל מום לא יהיה בו תמים יהיה לרצון, commanding and forbidding, prohibits making or causing to be made (שלא יגרום) a מום on an animal dedicated for an offering (ת״כ, and Menachoth 56b). Any such making or causing is a denial of the “completeness” of the giving oneself up which is demanded by the Sanctuary of the Torah.
V. 22. עורת, according to Rashi, a noun, blindness (similar in form to ילפת ,יבלת). As an adjective it would have the form עויר (as אדיר from לא תקריב וגו׳ ,(אדרת, see on v. 20.

V. 23. שרוע וקלוט. Bechoroth 40a: שרוע (stretched), שנשתרבב לו יריכו, having one hip bigger than the other. קלוט (joined together), שרגליו קלוטות כשל חמוד וכשל סוס, having the hoof formed like that of an ass or a horse.

נדבה תעשה אותו ולנדר לא ירצה. As in v. 18, a בעל מום is precluded from being brought for any offering: לכל נדריהם ולכל נדבותם, whether to fulfil a נדר or a נדבה, it is quite impossible that נדבה תעשה אותו should mean that it is allowed to be brought as a נדבה. In any case, the expression: נדבה תעשה אותו would not be correct. Where עשה in connection with offering designates the carrying out of a sacrificial procedure it always has as its object the animal and the nature of the offering which decides the procedure which is to be performed with it. Thus we find: את השני יעשה עולה כמשפט, (Ch. 5,10); ועשה הכהן את החטאת (Ch. 14,19); ועשה וגו׳ את האחד חטאת ואת האחד עולה (ibid XXX,51); ועשיתם עולה (Numb. 29,2); וכי תעשה בן בקר עולה (ibid XV,8) etc. But נדבה is not a thing which is accomplished in the first instance by the offering procedure, or which characterises that procedure; it is the preceding cause of the offering, to which, of course, the offering relates. So that if here תעשה referred to the actual procedure of the offering it would have to have said: לנדבה תעשה אותו, as it says in v. 21: ואיש כי יקריב זבח וגו׳ לנדבה, or in Numb. 15,3: ועשיתם וגו׳ עולה וגו׳ לפלא נדר או בנדבה. So that נדבה תעשה can only designate that action by which an animal becomes נדבה, the dedicating action which expresses itself in the formula: הרי זו נדבה. Thus we find a similar expression in Ch. 16,8: ועשהו חטאת, deciding that the animal is to be a חטאת. But inasmuch as here it stands in contrast to the לא ירצה of the following sentence, which refers to the final and highest factor of the purpose of an offering, here, too, the contrasting תעשה must designate such a dedicating action which does not merely introduce some procedure which is to follow, but which constiutes in itself a final act, similarly to the לא ירצה which follows. Hence the Halacha explains (Temura 6b): נדבה תעשה אותו זה קדשי בדק הבית ולנדר לא ירצה זה קדשי מזבח. Thereby the Law is given that בעלי מומים can be dedicated to קדשי בדק הבית, i.e. as holy objects to be used for the upkeep of the Temple, but not to קדשי מזבח, to offerings to be brought onto the Altar. קדשי בדק הבית are only holy for their value, they are either used themselves where possible for the Temple, or they have to be redeemed and the redemption money goes to the Temple treasury. קדשי מזבח have קדושת הגוף, are holy in themselves, as long as they remain free from מומים, they can not be redeemed, but must themselves be brought as offerings on the Altar. This idea of the קדשי בדק הבית is expressed here by the term נדבה, just as the gifts dedicated to the building of the Sanctuary, the first קדשי בדק הבית were called נדבה (Ex. 35,29 & XXXVI,3). In contrast to these, the קדשי מזבח destined for offering, are forbidden by ולנדר לא ירצה. That here it is speaking of קדושת הגוף, of the dedication of the animal to be an offering, is clear from the expression לא ירצה. But unless we are mistaken, the whole conception of an offering is here expressed in a very significant manner, by נדר in contrast to נדבה, and thereby the idea of פסול מום is placed in the clearest light. For every offering is, in the real meaning a נדו. It does not so much fulfil a vow but rather expresses a promise. The one who brings an offering undertakes to give up his urges and aims, all the actions of his limbs, so to fulfil the Divine Torah that it shall give satisfaction to God, as the דם, the אימורים and the איברים of his offering do achieve symbolically:  אספו לי חסידי כרתי בריתי עלי זבח runs Ps. 50,5, the call with which God collects His חסידים about Him for judgment of Israel. חסיד is one who offers himself up to God, who renews his vow of union with God, with every offering he brings, and it is in this giving oneself up to God that everyone should make his offerings be a vow of his future intention. זבח לאלקים תודה ושלם לעליון נדריך, thus runs the demand which this chapter — the chapter criticising and blaming the misuse of offerings which bringing them in the wrong spirit entails — makes to everybody. תודה, an offering of grateful acknowledgment of God, is what an offering should be, and the fulfilment of the promises expressed by it, are to follow. Wherever, in the Psalms and Prophets the contemporary bringing of offerings is deprecated and blamed it is never offerings as such, but the mistaken idea of what offerings really are meant to be that is criticised. The idea that offerings in themselves and by themselves have any value, and which forgets that offerings are only worth anything when they are not regarded as a substitute or dispensation for faithful adherence to duty but must be a renewed introduction to a faithful life of duty; the זבח רשעים, our Psalmist goes on to say, of those who think they can get absolution from their wrong doings by bringing an offering to God, is תועבה. This is a criticism which is levelled with quite similar solemnity and quite equal weight at prayers, and at keeping the Festivals (see Isaiah I), when these serve as a substitute for righteous living rather than as a spur to further it. The Psalmist and the Prophet would in quite a similar way, with their wrathful words, break a lance with the Divine service of quite a number of our present day Synagogues. Hence we find in other places too נדרים in connection with offerings: ויזבחו זבח לה׳ וידרו נדרים (Jonah 1,16); ועבדו זבח ומנחה ונדרו נדר לה׳ ושלמו (Is. 19,21), and there the vows and the fulfilling of them are clearly not the cause but the effect of the offerings, they clearly refer to the resolutions made with the offerings.

Here, in our text on the validity or invalidity of בעל מום for holy objects, נדבה and נדר are contrasted. נדבה, a gift dedicated to holy use, where only the object itself, and that only for its value, becomes holy, can be made with an animal affected with a מום. True, the imperfection does lessen the value, but it is only to become holy for what it is worth, and that value it does completely represent. But in נדר, the resolution to do an action, to bring an offering, it is the person himself, and indeed the person in the completeness in every phase of his life and his efforts, to represent which the animal is to serve, there לא ירצה, to express such a complete promise, an imperfect, incomplete animal is unfit.

Now, according to Temura 6 & 7, to dedicate a perfect animal to בדק הבית is just as much forbidden as to dedicate בעלי מזמין למזבח, but nevertheless, if done is effective. The acts are effective in so far that the value of the בעל מום must be reserved for the Altar, it has to be redeemed, and the redemption money used for the purchase of an offering; but the מום-free animal dedicated to the בדק הבית must itself be offered on the Altar. It has to be redeemed and its value goes to the benefit of the בדק הבית fund, but whoever redeems it must use it as an offering: המתפיס תמימים לבדק הבית כשהן נפדין אינן נפדין אלא למזבח; for the canon rules: כל הראוי למזבח אינו יוצא מידי מזבח לעולם, “anything which is fit and suitable for the Altar can never be taken away from it (Temura 5, 6, 32 & 33).

The prohibition to dedicate תמימים to בדק הבית, as well as the law that anything which has the ability to be used for the representation of human actions may never be diverted from this purpose and used for the upkeep of the Temple, should, for all time, bring home to us the fact how incomparably high above the magnificant equipment of the Temple, the devotion of our life to a higher level, which is striven for in the Temple, stands, so much so that this real meaning and purpose of the Temple may not be lost sight of in the mere use to which one single object is made. According to Shevuoth 16a & Zebachim 62a, even if the whole building of the Temple were to fall to pieces, the place of the offerings and the halls of the Temple would retain their complete holiness and the power of accomplishing their purpose: אמר ר׳ יהושע שמעתי שמקריבין אע״פ שאין בית אוכלין קדשי קדשים אע״פ שאין קלעים קדשים קלים ומעשר שני אע״פ שאין חומה, and thus the most dilapidated synagogue may far trancend in holiness the most magnificent Temple, if in the one, in contrast to the other, devotes pray who are כורתי ברית עלי זבח, who, at each visit to the synagogue renew the bond of self-sacrificing devotion to God’s Torah.

In Temura 4b—6b the question is discussed whether כל מלתא דאמר רחמנא לא תעביד מהני or לא מהני, i.e. whether in the absence of any direction from the Torah, an action done in spite of its being prohibited by the Torah can have any actual legal validity. Amongst other instances quoted to decide the matter the two cases in our text מקדיש תמימים לבדק הבית and מקדיש בעלי מומין למזבח are referred to, where although the act of dedication is prohibited, nevertheless it does take effect, and has legal consequences. But, in general, the decision was adopted that the canon: כל דאמר רחמנא לא תעביד לא מהני, should rule, but with certain limitations. According to תוספות (ibid 6a), a difference has to be made whether the procedure is directly forbidden by the Torah or whether it is an אסור שהוא בדה, or prohibition which he has imposed on himself, e.g. נשבע שלא לגרש את אשתו ועבד וגרשה. according to סמ״ג and ש״ך (on ח״מ 208,1), the procedure would only have no legal effect when the nature of the act is in itself a forbidden one, but not if it is only relatively wrong. Thus a sale made on Sabbath would be binding, because the act of selling could be done בהיתר, on any other day. But: נשבע שלא למכור ומכר, would, according to this, be invalid. The general principle: אי עביד לא מהני, moreover, applies also to acts forbidden by the רבנן. (See Kethuboth 81b: כיון דאמור רבנן לא ליזבון אע״ג דזבין לא הוה זביניה זביני.)

V. 24. ומעוך וכתות wounds and mutilations of the sexual organs. ובארצכם: the prohibition of castration of any kind, on man or beast, being חובת הגוף, a duty pertaining to the person and having nothing to do with the Land is בין בארץ בין בח״ל is also in force outside Palestine. ארצכם here, accordingly, seems to designate the whole country and to be used only in contrast to the מקדש (as the whole chapter has been dealing with offerings) similar to גבולין and מדינה in the rabbinic mode of expression. We are told thereby, that this kind of wounding or mutilation is not only forbidden to be done to בהמות קדשים, not only to animals destined for offerings, or fit for offerings, altogether not only in connection with the מקדש but also is quite generally forbidden without any reference to the Mikdosh, for economic or other reasons. Thus we find in Chagiga 14b: שאלו את בן זומא מהו לסרוסי כלבא אמר להם בארצכם לא תעשו כל שבארצכם, (see תוספות ibid).

V. 25. ומיד בן נכר וגו׳. We have already remarked that at the offerings of the Noachides which they might bring to God, outside the מקדש only מחוסר אבר but not מומים need be taken into account (Aboda Zara 5b). Now here it is taught that in the Jewish Sanctuary of God, from a בן נח too, no בעלי מומים may be brought as offerings.

כי משחתם בהם מום בם. In Temura 28b and in other places, it is taught that in משחתם is understood the exclusion of רובע ונרבע מוקצה ונעבד from offerings (this had already been indicated in Ch. 1,2 by the selective proposition מן, it says there: מן הבהמה מן הבקר ומן הצאן), and at the same time by the juxtaposition of משחת and מום, the canon is taught that: כל שהמום פוסל בהן דבר ערוה וע״ז פוסלין בהן, that everywhere where a מום makes something unfit (as, for example, at a פרה אדומה too, see ע״ז 23b), there, too, unfitness arising out of sexual immorality or idolatry, רובע ונרבע מוקצה ונעבד applies; and also the converse (Bechoroth 57a). כל שאין המום פוסל בו, (e.g. מעשר, see Ch. 27,33); אין דבר ערוה וע״ז פוסל בו (see תוספות Chulin 23a ד״ה כי). Reference is made to the fact that everywhere in the Torah השחתה designates immorality and idolatry, כי השחית כל בשר את דרכו על הארץ (Gen. 6,12); and פן תשחיתון ועשיתם לכם פסל (Deut. 4,16). Then the connection of כי as cause seems difficult. In the whole chapter up to now it has only been a question of פסול מום, and the reason for this disqualification for offerings by the מום-fault is now given as משחת through the רובע ונרבע-fault. More, apparently, by the cantilation: משחתם בהם מום בם is one sentence, so that משחת and מום would be identical, or, in any case the one would presuppose the other! But if the way we have taken the conception of פסול מום to be is not quite erroneous, this difficulty would be solved simply by considering the fact that that which a מום would express symbolically in an offering, רובע ונרבע מוקצה ונעבד represent in actual fact. The תמים-character which is demanded in offerings represents nothing other than the completeness with which one must devote one’s life to God, the subordinating of every phase of one’s being to the Law of God, the Torah. It is, as we have already remarked above, the most direct result of our consciousness of the “Oneness” of God, (as expressed by שמע. I.L.), the unity of life from the Unity of God. In בעל מום “the non-complete offering”, a part of this life kept back from being given up to God and His Torah. But any and every phase of human life not subordinated to God and His Torah is immoral, which reaches its quintessence in דבר ערוה. The partial non-subordination is in itself a denial of the exclusive Unity of God, is an acknowledgement of there being other powers besides God, is עבודה זרה. And so in very truth מום בם, a מום on our offering is משחתם בם, the expression of a moral and spiritual degeneration in it, and then it follows logically that when and where מום, the mere symbolic expression of ערוה and ע״ז renders an animal unfit for an offering, then and there any actual concrete use of it for the sins of ערוה and ע״ז must preclude its use for offering.

V. 27. To the expressions which are used here to specify animals which are fit to be used for offerings viz.: שור או כשב או עז כי יולד, the Gemora attaches the Halacha, that, apart from the פסול מחוסר זמן of which the verse is primarily speaking, the nature of the species of the animal (that is why here it says כשב או עז, and does not combine them with the general term שה as it does in v. 28), must be purely impressed on it, both with regards to its breed and its appearance. Hence כלאים, mixed breeds, as well as freaks, e.g. a sheep that looks like a goat, are precluded from being brought as offerings. Further, כי יולד, it must have been born in a natural manner, excluding יוצא דופן. Then, of such an animal destined for an offering — of pure descent, normal formation and normal birth — it says והיה שבעת ימים תחת אמו, that before it may be used for an offering, seven days must pass. During this period its unfitness is called: מחוסר זמן, it lacks the necessary time, it is premature. The meaning of תחת אמו is doubtful, whether תחת means under, or in place of. The Halacha teaches: תחת אמו פרט ליתום (Bechoroth 57a), that it must have a mother, that an animal which is born “an orphan”, i.e. whose mother dies whilst giving it birth may not be used for an offering, if זו פירש למיתה וזה פירש לחיים, so that the animal had never lived one minute together with its mother. This living together, which in Ex. 22,29 is expressed by: עם אמו, would, accordingly be what is here called: תחת אמו, describing the position in which the young obtains warmth and nourishment from the mother. But in ת״ב (see Rashi, Bechoroth 57a), it also teaches that, from the change of עם to תחת, which also has the meaning of in the place of, “instead of”, the mother need not have lived seven days with the young that is born from her, but that it suffices if the animal lives seven days after the mother, so that it can represent taking the place of the mother in the world of living creatures. So that תחת אמו can designate the first stage of the normal continuance of the life of mammals, and this is not to be disturbed for a period of seven days by deciding that it is to become an offering, and the normal condition of the relation of the young animal to its parent must have existed at least for one minute, but a יתום, whose mother died before birth was completed, is פסול for an offering. We have already remarked on Ex. 22,29 that in cases where it is doubtful whether the offspring has the ability to live, the first seven days are considered the critical decisive period for animals — as the first thirty days are for humans — in which the normal care of the mother animal is most important for the young. ומיום השמיני והלאה ירצה: From the conclusion of this period of seven days, with the entry of the night of the eighth day, the מחוסר זמן ceases, and it can henceforth be dedicated for an offering. But it can only be brought as an offering on the eighth day: לילה לקדושה ויום להרצאה (Zebachim 12a).

V. 28. שה .ושור או שה וגו׳ comprises כבש and עז. The law forbids the killing of the mother animal and its young on the same day. If the mother animal has been slaughtered, the young may not be done on the same day, and vice versa. Only שחיטה, the act of killing which the Torah allows for human consumption is forbidden. Any other mode of killing נחירה or נתנבלה בשחיטה if the שחיטה was incorrectly performed, does not come under this prohibition. Whether the prohibition applies to the male parent animal and his young is doubtful. As this law stands in the midst of laws regulating offerings (vv. 27 & 29), and is connected with the preceding by the copulative ושור) ו), this prohibition applies also to מוקדשין animals for sacrifices, and a sacrificial animal whose mother or young has been slaughtered on that day is also called מחוסר זמן. But as the Law starts again with specially repeated objects שור או שה וגו׳, and does not just continue the preceding, שור הפסיק הענין, it applies quite generally, to חולין and מוקדשין alike (Chulin 78a et seq.).

The regulations given in this chapter regarding the negative qualifications which are conditional for the validity of an animal for sacrifices, the absence of any משחת or מום, everything which actually or symbolically represents any ערוה or ע״ז, are here finally complemented by positive demands which in no lesser degree are conditional for the nature of the offering. First of all the animal must bear the stamp of purity of species. Both in its descent and its form a שור is to be a שור, a כבש — a כבש, and an עז — an כלאים .עז and נדמה are unfit for offerings. We have already remarked on Ch. I, what a significant bearing this character of species has on the conception of an offering, so that the positive demand for the imprint of purity of species is easily to be understood. The other demands, normal birth excluding תחת אמו ;יוצא דופן, the necessity for at least one moment of having had the normal maternal relationship to its young, which excludes יתום and ensures that a period of at least seven days be granted, to such condition; מחוסר זמן, to which then אותו ואת בנו follows as a law applying also to מוקדשין; all these laws could be connected together with the one idea of the animal mother-relation to the animal young. We think that we may venture to make the supposition that it is in this phase of animal life that the beginning of an approach to human character shows itself. Egotism, love of oneself, looking after oneself, is the powerful spring that moves animal life. Sacrificing oneself for the existence of another creature and devoted care for its well being, as occurs in the birth and care for the young, and as shown in the mother love of animals, is the first elevation to that forgetfulness of self, which, in the general love of one’s fellow man forms the most divine trait in the nobility of human character. This humanlike spark is not to be allowed to be extinguished, but rather is it to be stressed by significant consideration in the animal-creature that, as an offering, is to represent the ideal of morality to which Man is to aspire.

This trace of humanity renders the animal being fit for such representation, and the fact that it has to be taken into consideration shows the Jewish conception of sacrifices in their having the sole purpose of the furthering of human morality, and sharply differentiates it from the pagan idea which sees in sacrifices a killing which gives satisfaction to their gods.

As this same consideration for the humane factors in animal life is demanded in the אותו ואת בנו law for חולין, for the provision of meat for ordinary human consumption, the stamp of altar-like purpose of morality is impressed on the every-day Jewish table. As it is only שחיטת אותו ואת בנו, but not נחירה any other mode of killing which is forbidden, it can not be actual kindness, consideration of an animal’s feelings etc., which lies at the root of this prohibition. But rather the reason must be that when, by slaughtering it, we are about to change a living animal into food for human nourishment we are to grant the animal child an extra day’s life for its mother’s sake, or the animal mother for its child’s sake, and thereby bring home to our minds the idea of humaneness at the moment we are deciding to assimilate an animal into our being (cf. Deut. 22,6).

V. 29 & 30. To all this the פגול and נזתר-law, which is here, at the conclusion of the whole of the laws concerning offerings, specially repeated for the נאכלין ליום אחד of the תודה, stands in a twofold close connection. Just as פסול ,יוצא דופן ,יתום ,מחוסר זמן, and אותו ואת בנו, show the character of offerings to be that of an institution for the moral spiritual ennoblement of human beings, in contrast to the pagan conception of their being a pacification of the gods by the shedding of blood, so is the פגול and נזתר-law the great seal of God on the Jewish institution of offerings, which safeguards it against such demoralising erroneous delusion of the pagan ideas. פגול, which is שחיטה separated from the idea of אכילה, represents the pagan conception that self destruction is a means of conciliation of the gods, and נתור which is אכילה separated from שחיטה represents animal enjoyment without moral restriction by submitting to the Divine laws of the Torah, (see on Ch. 7,17 & 18 & XIX,6—8). And just as אותו ואת בנו applied to חולין elevates ordinary meals to the spiritual idea of the Sanctuary, so does אכילת תודה bring the homely room and the homely meal into the atmosphere of the Temple. The פגול and נותר-law when referred to תודה, the expression of thanks for one’s life being saved and preserved, does emphasize quite specially the Jewish true teaching as opposed to the false heathen ideas. What God — the God of Jewish Teaching — wants in the way of thanks for the saving and continuance of happiness, is not throwing oneself in a self-destructive and immorally uncontrolled celebration in the enjoyment of earthly joys, but rather only in the happy — but kept within the limits of moral laws, and thereby raised into the sphere of God serving fulfilment of life — enjoyment of the life He has granted, saved and continued.

V. 31. The Lawgiving on the subject of priests and offerings concludes with the general demand for “the care and fulfilment of the Divine Commandments”. Thereby this שמירה and עשיה of the מצות is given as the purpose and aim of the whole institution of priests and offerings. Above all, the priest stands in the service of שמירת המצות. For that “guard” of the Divine Torah which manifests itself primarily in “learning and teaching” the Torah — שמירה זו משנה — and which forms the fundamental condition for the existence and continuance of the Torah in the minds and hearts of the Nation, is the most important characteristic ascribed to Jewish priests: כי שפתי כהן ישמרו דעת ותורה יבקשו מפיהו כי מלאך ה׳ צבאות הוא (Malachi 2,7). Did not the previous chapter teach us how even the private and homely life of the priests is consecrated to the service of this שמירה, the keeping the moral ideals of the Torah ever present in the midst of the people. And the offerings themselves, are they not entirely and completely in the service of the עשיה, in the service of the carrying out of the Torah, altogether nothing but the vow to actively dedicate our חלב ,דם and כליות and אברים together with our flour, oil and incense, accordingly, everything which we are, we strive for, and have, to fulfilling the Law of God, to allow Him to find satisfaction on earth. But that which the priests represent and teach and that which our offerings which they perform for us symbolically express as vows, is what we all, priests and people, are to “guard and fulfil” in the reality of our lives.

V. 32. ולא תחללו את שם קדשי. With the erection of His Sanctuary of the Torah in our midst לשכן שמו שם, God has made us, the whole of our national and individual lives, to be bearers of His Name, has declared us and all of ours to be His. He has deposited the proclamation of His Will in our midst telling us how we are to behave as being His People, and how we are to justify the name we bear. This Name of God, which we bear, is to be קדש, the absolute highest in our midst, and it is also to be the central soul which, by the might of its power, holds us and all ours together, keeps us, stirs us to activity, animates and elevates us by holding us to our duty in His service. With every refusal to sacrifice any impulse of our being, and any attraction which draws us, any fibre of ourselves, any tiny morsel of our possessions from the fulfilment of His Will we are מחלל את שם קדשו, make the Name that should be the highest, the holiest, the most absolute for us, on which the justification for all our existence and possessions depends, and as such should rule over us and all of ours with absolute power, we make that name חלל a “lifeless and powerless corpse” — We desecrate thereby the holiness of His Name, and inasmuch as our sin against God’s Laws comes to the knowledge of other people, we make, as far as lies in our power, our example into propaganda for the powerlessness of the Name of God, which rests on us, show that one can still call oneself a Jew, and be called a Jew, and still can abandon the obedience which this name involves, as being worth nothing against the first temptation which attracts our senses, or against the first chance of enjoyment, or of achieving some material benefit. We show that one can call oneself a Jew, and be called a Jew, and still not recognize God’s Will as the absolute, and one’s own will as conditionl, but can set up one’s own will as the absolute god before which the Will of God must vanish as being conditional to it and powerless before it. And the more anybody, by his knowledge of the Word of God, and by his position in the social world, is prominent as a “bearer of the Name of God”, the sharper and the more imperative is the demand made to him: לא תחללו את שם קדשי, and all the more in his case is the slightest, even only a seemingly, deviation from the truthfulness and honesty, from the morality and holy living from the justness, kindness and goodness which the Torah demands reckoned as a great חלול-השם-crime (Yoma 86,b). The ever-recurring canon: אדם חשוב שאני, that every enhanced degree of mental or spiritual superiority demands a higher degree of conscientiousness, shows in what sense the intelligentsia and men of special gifts of the Jewish people regarded their position in relation to the laws of morality, and how far away they were from that deplorable erroneous opinion which is ready to grant every upward step of intellectual greatness a greater dispensation from having to keep the laws of morality. But on the contrary, ונקדשתי בתוך בני ישראל, God, and His Holy Will are to be considered as the holy highest, as the underlying condition for all things in Jewish life. And that which every offering teaches, and which is vowed and undertaken at every offering:— to offer up on the altar of our God, every drop of our blood, every urge and aim of our wishes, all the active power of our limbs, all our food, our well-being, and the joys of our life for the carrying out of His Holy Will, that is to be the picture of the life of every single individual for our own perfection and for a teaching example to every one of our contemporaries. Such is the Jewish mission: בתוך בני ישראל, to be a real actuality in the Jewish People.

For this תוך בני ישראל forms a lively living whole to which all its parts belong and contribute. The cheerful sacrifice to duty of each one is to raise each other one to similar adhesion to duty, and the sins against duty of the one does not only dig the grave of his own mission, the faithfulness to duty of others who stumble at this example, lies buried in the same grave.

In Sanhedrin 44a & b this demanded sacrifice of even the most precious of our earthly values, even of life itself, for the glorification of the Name of God, by the strictest adherence to obedience of the Law is explained in connection with the וחי בהם of Ch. 18,5, that, in ordinary circumstances it is only ע״ז ג״ע וש״ד, only in the laws concerning idolatory, sexual immorality, and murder that one has to make their observance outweigh the value of life itself, of them it says that in all circumstances יהרג ואל יעבור, “one must let oneself be killed rather than transgress the Law”. But בתוך בני ישראל, if it is a case of בפרהסיא, openly, publicly, in the midst of a Jewish community (in the presence of ten adults, which is always taken as an עדה, as representing the Jewish community), if in such circumstances the transgression of the Torah is forced on us with the threat of death, or בשעת גזרת המלכות in times of the persecution of the Jews, where the fury of persecution of the nations has proclaimed a war of extinction against Judaism as well as Jewry, in these cases אפילו מצוה קלה, even the smallest law, ואפילו לשנויי ערקתא דמסאנא, even if it is only a question of deviation of an established custom in Jewry regarding a shoe-lace, may not be transgressed to save one’s life. In such cases it says repeatedly: יהרג ואל יעבור, the glorification of the Name of God, קידוש השם, by Jewish faithfulness to the Torah has to be confirmed even at the price of death.

And this מסירת הנפש, this giving up one’s life with all its efforts and aims to faithfully keeping the dictates of God’s Torah, which the offerings in God’s Sanctuary teach daily and hourly symbolically, and which the Word of God here demands from us as the sanctification of His Name which we bear, it is this which has become the historical strength of the Jewish People, it has found its most brilliant fulfilment in the glorious pages of the Jewish history of the Galut. All the החסידים והתמימים והישרים, all the קהלות הקודש שמסרו נפשם על קדושת השם, the הנאהבים והנעימים בחייהם ובמותם לא נפרדו, who, in their lives sought nothing but the love of God and His satisfaction, and in their death did not relinquish their endeavours, and found therein the strength of lions and the towering flight of eagles to fulfil the Will of their Master and the desire of their God, all these martyrs have brought the offering-conception to its loftiest ideal in reality, have sacrificed life and efforts, and all their powers of action, and all the means of existence, of well-being, and the joys of life, on the Altar of God’s Torah, have proclaimed the absolute power which God’s Torah exercises over a true Jewish heart, have shown how Jews understand the ולא תחללו את שם קדשי.

So this group of laws begins with the consideration to be given to that self-sacrificing devotion which manifests itself in the mother-love of the instinctive life of animals, and thus celebrates the beginning of humaneness on earth, and concludes with the fully conscious, completely free-willed martyrdom, in which this beginning reaches its highest summit.

But just as that which the Torah expressed in words by ונקדשתי בתוך בני ישראל and which is expressed symbolically at the rise and decline of every day, by the daily offering, and thus was brought again and again to the minds of the nation as the height of the national mission, so have the אנשי כנסת הגדולה, those true Fathers of the Nation, when they composed the order of the synagogue service in words to be parallel to the Temple service in offerings, arranged the maxim and the promise to carry out of the ונקדשתי וגו׳ as being the quintessence of the idea of the procedures of all offerings, to be also the high point of all national prayer gatherings. Hence, where at least ten adults gather for prayers, this idea finds ever-repeated, enthusiastic expression in קדיש and קדושה (Berachoth 21b).

V. 1. With the last group of laws of the preceding paragraph the Law giving which commenced with the building of the אהל מועד really reaches its conclusion. The laws of the festivals which follow in this section are only connected primarily with the laws of the Temple inasmuch as each one of these festivals brings with it the duty of a national offering being brought: והקרבתם אשה לה׳, as it says at each one of them. But the ordering of this Festival offering is not the real subject of this section. The duty to bring it is only quite generally indicated and all the details concerning it are only given in Numb. 28,29. Here it is the order in which the Festivals are to follow each other in the cycle of the year, סדרן, as the Sifri calls it on Deut. 16,1, and the detailed laws concerning the special laws pertaining to each Festival by means of which the particular meaning of that Festival is expressed, which form the contents of this chapter. בשלש מקומות, it says there in Sifri: ,מזכיר פרשת מועדות בתורת כהנים מפני סדרן בחומש הפקודים מפני קרבן, במשנה תורה מפני צבור. “In three places the Torah contains a section about the Festivals, in Leviticus concerning their order, in Numbers concerning the offerings, and in Deuteronomy to teach the duty of publicly expounding the lessons which each Festival is meant to impress on us. But the reason why the special Festival offerings, the מוספין only follow in Numb. and are not prescribed here, where we should have expected them to be placed, may very well lie in the fact that to appreciate the value of the national Festival offerings in their full meaning, the Nation had first to have learnt their own relation to their great mission which the events of their long wanderings in the wilderness — so full of tests and trials — brought home to them. And this, of course, is just what the contents of the book of Numbers records.

The three pilgrim-festivals, רגלים, have already been mentioned in Ex. 23,14 et seq., and XXXIV,18 et seq. Two of them, שבועות and סוכת, only here receive their more precise date, and their more detailed laws. ר״ה and י״כ whose meaning in any case, are connected with events which only occurred later, viz. עגל, and מיתת בני אהרן appear here for the first time in the cycle of Festivals of the year.

There is one conception which the Festivals which follow here have in common with the Temple and the offerings, the lawgiving for which, essentially closed with the preceding group of laws, and that is מועד (see ibid). That which the Temple is in space, is what the Festivals are in time. Both have our union with God as their aim. The one sets God’s Torah as the centre point of our lives, down in the actual centre of our world, and says to us:— This is where you find your direction to the way to your God. The other calls special attention to certain fixed times in the changing course of the year, which were marked by the revelation of God in special acts, and says to us: in these times God was at one time very near to you, at each anniversary God awaits you for renewed and refreshed union with Him. But in their nature these two institutions — Festivals and Temple — differ as space and time do. Just as Space is the conception of persistence, of infinity, so does God’s Sanctuary in space deal with the eternal Godly, i.e. the Torah and the eternal human, i.e. human nature, in their eternal mutual and conflicting relations to each other. And just as Time is the conception of the changing succession of things one after the other, so do God’s Sanctuaries in Time — the Festivals — deal with the manifestations of the Godly in the course of time, i.e. the revelation of God in nature and history, and the human element, in time, i.e. our human and national relations to nature and history.

The laws which formed the conclusion of the preceding chapter: מחוסר זמן ,אותו ואת בנו ,פגול ונותר, have, besides the inner understandable connection which has already been indicated, yet another common factor with our chapter, inasmuch as they concede important consideration to time within the sphere of God’s Sanctuary in space. Moreover it is also periods of one and seven days with which these considerations are concerned. The possibility of the exercise of mother-love of an animal to its young must be granted for a period of seven days, אותו ואת בנו forbids an offering procedure within one day, just as פגול and נותר demand offering procedures just within one day, and in these cases a whole day has the character of the procedure which occurred on it. It does not seem far-fetched to think that just the time factor of these offering-laws quite significantly leads over to the Sanctuaries of God in Time (the Festivals) which also are concerned with similar periods of one and seven days.

Nothing marks the independence of a man so much as his unfettered right to the disposition of his time. He who can dispose of his time as he wishes, that man is free. Who has the right to dispose of the time of somebody else, he is that person’s master. In Egypt we could call no minute our own, and the lack of this right to dispose of our time right to the end, still at the very moment of our delivery from Egypt, showed us still as subordinates, and made the Mazza to the symbol of our dependence. By the fact the God disposes of our time, and takes days and weeks out of the course of time of our years, and reserves their use according to His instructions, He proclaims Himself our Master, and this placing our time at His disposal becomes the most demonstrative symbol of our belonging to God, into which we passed out of belonging to other men, and which, for all time, made and makes us free.
