But that this, our relation to God, is not to be considered only as that of a servant to a master, but as that of a child to its father, is very significantly brought out in the following verse which introduces the lawgiving concerning the Sanctuaries of God in Time.

V. 2. מועדי ה׳ וגו׳. Clearly this verse is not to be taken as an introduction to a register of the Festivals. Otherwise it would have said: אלה מועדי ה׳ אשר תקראו אותם מקראי קדש, or shorter: אלה הם מועדי. But this verse is an independent sentence on its own, and מועדי ה׳ אשר תקראו אותם מקראי קדש is the subject and אלה הם מועדי is the predicate. Thereby an essential condition is given to which the character of a day being a מועד ה׳ is attached. “The מועדי ה׳, which you anounce, they are My מועדים״. A time indicated by God for a מועד only becomes a מועד ה׳ by the Nation proclaiming it as a מקרא קדש. Thereby the great principle is pronounced that we have already worked out on קידוש החדש (Ex. 12,2), according to which the days of the Jewish new-moons and festivals are not fixed astronomically, so that with the arrival of the astronomic moment in time, the day would automatically, without further ado, become sanctified into a new-moon day or festival. But for both, times dependent on the course of the moon and of the sun are only given as occasions for which, and in conjunction with which, Jewish National Days of New Moon and Festivals — i.e. מועדים, times for “Meetings” of Israel with its God — are to be fixed and sanctified. A principle, by which every semblance of a pagan nature-worshipping moon and sun worship or cult is removed from our summer and harvest festivals. Moreover, the times for the coming together of God and Israel are raised out of the slavish relationship of servant and master, into the loving relationship of Father and His Children, who, by the fixing of the times for meeting by both parties, only show the satisfying of a mutual loving longing for each other. Now here, first of all, the direction is given, that fixing the year of the festivals which fixes the commencement of each festival in the appropriate season, is dependent on the decision and proclamation of the representatives of the Nation.

For the מועדים have a double reference, a seasonal one and an historical one. With regards to the first they are connected with the season of the year as well as with the state of development of the products of the soil. The פסח and מצה Festival is referred to the חדש האביב (Deut. 16,1); the שבועות-Festival is the חג הקציר בכורי מעשיך (Ex. 23,16), is the יום הבכורים (Numb. 28,26); the סוכת-Festival is חג האסיף תקופת השנה (Ex. 34,22). Three demands arise from this to be considered for fixing our Festivals in relation to their seasonal character: (a) תקופה, the first day of the מצות-Festival, the 15th Nissan, must fall in the spring-season, the תקופת ניסן, and at least the last day of the סוכת-Festival must be already in the Autumn season, the תקופת תשרי; (b) אביב, for the מצות-Festival, the grain must have reached its appropriate first stage of ripening; (c) פירות האילן, for the שבועות-Festival the fruit-trees must be sufficiently advanced, so that the fruit is ripe enough to bring בכורים from them. But the beginning of Spring and Autumn, the ripening of grain and fruit, are matters which are connected with the year’s course of the sun and its influence. The months of the year of the Jewish calendar, however, are lunar months, and a lunar year of twelve months in nearly eleven days less than a solar year, so that without some regulating, any date of a year, e.g. Nissan 15th, would occur eleven days earlier each year. Thus, throughout the years פסח would sucsessively be in spring, summer, autumn and winter. Hence the canon: על שלשה דברים מעברין את השנה, out of three considerations is one extra month, the month אדר שני to be inserted: על האביב ועל פירות האילן ועל התקופות, (Sanhedrin 11,b), to keep the Festivals in accord with the seasons. The representatives of the Nation, accordingly, have to reckon astronomically the path of the sun and the resulting times of the commencement of Spring and Autumn in relation to the dates of the festivals in each year, and also to note the probable ripening of the produce of the soil and the trees, and according to that to insert, or refrain from inserting, an intercalary month in the year. As this gives room for play, and it can very well make no difference for the general concurrence of festival and season whether the extra month is put in this year or the next, other considerations could also come into question when the decision was to be made, e.g. ,מפני הדרכים מפני הגשרים ומפ׳ תנורי פסחים ומפ׳ גליות ישראל שנעקרו ממקומן ועדיין לא הגיעו, if the roads have become impassable, or bridges broken which would hinder the pilgrimage up to the Temple, if the פסח-ovens had become damaged by the rains etc. of the winter, shortness of time for the return of contemporaries who had already been exiled into the Diaspora, as well as those other secondary reasons as סעד לשנה if the animals for the various offerings were behind with their growth: מפני הגדיים טלאים וגוזלות שלא פרחו (ibid. 11a). All this lies in the task ordered here:— אשר תקראו אותם מקראי קדש. The great dictum applies both to עבור השנה and to קידוש החודש, that: אתם אפילו שוגגין אתם אפילו מזידין אתם אפילו מוטעין, that even if the National Representatives through error, or even intentionally, or misled by false information, should have made a dicision which is not really corresponding to the seasonal requirements, nevertheless God says: אין לי מועדות ;אלה הם מועדי אלא אלו (Rosh Hashana 25a ת״כ thereon — cf. Ex. 12,2 on החדש הזה לכם), “I do not recognize as My holy days any other than those proclaimed by Israel”. For the festivals of חדש האביב, of חג הקציר ביכורי מעשיך of חג האסיף are just as little Spring Festivals, Summer or Autumn Festivals, sun-worshipping Nature cults, as the New Moon Festival is far from being any pagan idea of a Moon cult. Just as the renewal of the moon each month is only to be an inducement to celebrate our renovation, so are the Jewish Spring, Summer and Autumn Festivals מקראי קדש, they really call us away just out of the realm of Nature, away from the fields, from forests and meadows, call us up, towards, into, the Temple of God’s Torah. They are really a loudly protesting Truth, opposing a heathen worship of Nature. They proclaim that it is not by grace of the spring, summer and autumn regulating power of the sun that the produce of our fields and orchards ripen and our barns become full, but that it is the free control of our God, judging the faithfulness or unfaithfulness of our duty towards His Will as declared in His Torah deposited in His Sanctuary, which grants or denies the blossoming in our Springs, the maturing in our Summers and the abundance in our Autumns. Only if we freely place our whole moral and social conditions under the rule of the Torah which He has given us, and let the power of its light and heat exercise its awakening, developing, and forming force to master us, even as the seeds and the fruit beds awake, develop, and form by the power of light and heat of the laws of Nature which He has established, it is only our own moral blossoming, our own moral developing and maturing for which God grants the blessing of the blossoming of our meadows, the ripening of our fruit, and the filling of our barns, as His Word has said again and again: אם בחקתי תלכו ואת מצותי תשמרו ועשיתם אתם ונתתי גשמיכם בעתם ונתנה הארץ יבולה ועץ השדה יתן פריו והשיג לכם דיש את בציר ובציר ישיג את זרע ואכלתם לחמכם לשבע וישבתם לבטח בארצכם! (Ch. 26,3—5, and elsewhere).

V. 3. ששת ימים וגו׳. The Sabbath law occurs repeatedly in the Torah and always with reference to a different phase of Jewish life, to which, indeed, Sabbath forms the fundamental institution. Thus we find the Sabbath of the Creation (Gen. 2,1), the Sabbath of the Wilderness in connection with the struggle for existence, for obtaining food (Ex. 16,22 et seq.), the Sabbath of the Decalogue, as evidence of the whole Jewish consciousness of God (Ex. 20,8), Sabbath in its effect on humane and social life (Ex. 23,12), the sanctity of Sabbath in its relation to the Temple, (XXXI,13 et seq.; and XXXV,2 et seq.); Sabbath in its relation to education (Levit. 19,3); and Sabbath in its relation to heathen necromancy (XIX,30). Now, here, Sabbath stands in its relation to the cycle of Festivals of the year. These Festivals have just been described as מועדי ה׳, as times destined for meetings with God, which, at God’s command and direction, the Nation itself was to fix as invitations for themselves:, אשר תקראו אותם מקראי קדש, and whose sanctity is essentially dependent on this free act of decision of the Nation. In contrast to them, at their head at once stands the Sabbath, as the unique one, fixed, and sanctified once for all by God, the appointment of which is not to be fixed by the Nation, whose holiness does not come from the Nation, is not first to be proclaimed by the Nation as a “invitation to holiness” or “to the Sanctuary” but which is, at its entry, itself מקרא קדש and so proclaims itself as the one given starting point and the culminating point of all holy days, it is their basis and should find its realisation in them. And in fact, it is Sabbath, that day symbolising God as Master of nature and history, that institution for the education of mankind, out of which, and for which, Israel came forth, and all those special days which Israel has to sanctify have no other purpose than to make the teaching of mankind to acknowledge God which is postulated by Sabbath a reality to Israel and in Israel. So too, the formula for the ending of the blessings on the Sabbath during the festivals runs: מקדש השבת וישראל והזמנים, and not: מקדש ישראל ושבת והזמנים, because as is explained in Beitza 17a, it is not ישראל who are מקדש השבת, Sabbath is not dependent on being proclaimed by Israel as a holy day, but שבת מקדשא וקיימא, and in Berachoth 49a, the whole is regarded as one uniform act of God: לפי גירסת הרי״ף) הא בהא תליא, see ר״ן there, ענין אחד הוא שקדושת ישראל תלויה בקדושת השבת וקדושת הזמנים וראשי חדשים תלויה בקדושת ישראל).

שבתון (see Ex. 16,23). מקרא קדש: As, already remarked, there is no proclamation to fix the Sabbath day, but it is one of its essential characteristics that its holiness is not dependent on any proclamation, מקרא קדש here, and in general, can not be the gerundial form of קרא to proclaim, and also אשר תקראו אתם מקראי קדש in v. 2 can not mean “which you shall proclaim as holy”. But מקרא in the expression: מקרא קדש is rather to be taken entirely in the sense in which it is used in Numb. 10,2. למקרא העדה: a summons to the Sanctuary, or rather a summons to “holiness”. For while מקדש refers almost exclusively only to a holy place, the Sanctuary, or the Temple, (only in Numb. 18,29: את מקדשו ממנו, does it exceptionally refer to a mass to be separated out as a holy part), קדש designates the idea of holiness in general, as in שם קדשי and elsewhere, and in general any holy object. Thus Israel too is called קדש ישראל לה׳ :קדש (Jer. 2,3); and Sabbath is also called ושמרתם את השבת כי קדש הוא לכם :קדש (Ex. 31,14). But if the holiness of human beings consists in nothing else but in being unswervingly ready to do their duty, then the holiness of objects, places, and times, only arises from their purpose to raise us above everything that opposes this readiness for duty, and to make and keep us alert to do that which is right. So that every קדש is really a ”מקרא״ קדש, it “calls us away, out and up”, out of stagnation, and out of being held by the influence of our senses in the neglect of our duties and in pursuit of wrongful aims, up to the height of completely unreserved devoted readiness for our duty. And each קדש works by means of the power of that particular fact which it represents, and which is its meaning and teaching. Now the מועדי ה׳, the Days of Remembrance, which by reason of the revelations of God, in nature and human history, invite us to a meeting with God, and just by this demand which they bring to us become a מקרא קדש, they await, to call us to this קדש, the proclamation of the Nation. But שבת is in itself a מקרא קדש, it is the original and very source of all dedication and sanctification of Man to Law and duty, it is the acknowledgement of God in nature and history, which acknowledgement is to be expressed by the שבתון of men, it is the unique basis on which the general idea of duty is built up. So that all the מועדים presuppose שבת, and it is the only day which is fixed by God, and without any decision by Man, as being ויברך אלקים את יום :קדש השביעי ויקדש אותו (Gen. 2,3) hence שבת שבתון מקרא קדש. Also at all other מועדים, their אסור מלאכה is only a result of their מקרא קדש character (see on Ex. 12,16). But on Sabbath, the אסור מלאכה lies in its nature, it is to be celebrated by שבתון because it is שבת, and it is that which it expresses as שבת שבתון, which makes it to מקרא קדש.

שבת הוא לה׳: not to satisfy the requirement of a day of rest, but a day acknowledging God, is Sabbath; its שביתה is an expression of this homage to God, it is given, fixed by God, sanctified by God, and it is just this fixed nature of its demands — free from all human choice — that makes submission to it into an act of homage-offering to God. And שבת היא לה׳ בכל מושבתיכם, and as such it comes to us everywhere, wherever we find ourselves, however far we may be scattered over the world. Regarding all other מועדים we are referred to the Nation, to their being fixed by the representatives of the Nation, accordingly, to the place which is the centre-point of our national life. But the holiness of the Sabbath is older than the Nation. It does not require the agency of the Nation. It is the man himself who is called on to pay homage to his Creator and the Creator of the World. Wherever he may be in God’s World, Sabbath comes to him and invites him, by laying down his mastery of the world, by sacrificing “his” world to acknowledge and pay homage to the real Master of the world — מושב דכתב רחמנא גבי שבת למה לי איצטריך ס״ד אמינא הואיל ובעניינא דמועדות כתיבא תיבעי קידוש כי מועדות קמ״ל (Kiddushin 37b; see תוספות 37a ד״ה והרי שבת).

V. 4. אשר תקראו אותם במועדם. Although the entry of the festival month is already regulated to fall in its appropriate season by the fixing of the year by the national representatives, עיבור שנה (see on v. 2), still the entry of the festival itself on the appointed date depends again on the fixing of the beginning of each month at the new moon by the same national representatives, קידוש החודש (see on Ex. 12,2). This proclamation of the beginning of the months on which the day of the commencement of the festivals depends, has to be done במועדם, in the appointed time of the appearance of the new moon, the sight of which has to be testified to by witnesses, and to make this possible in the appointed time, if needs must, these witnesses, have even to be מחלל שבת to arrive in time before the ב״ד who are awaiting them (Rosh Hashana 21b).

V. 5. בחדש הראשון. In the Spring month of the redemption, which was fixed to be the beginning of the Jewish national year (Ex. 12,2) on the fourteenth of that month; at every anniversary of the last day of slavery, בין הערבים, in the time which begins to lead over to the day of deliverance, which starts with the night of the 15th, the time which introduces the coming twilight of that night (see on Ex. 12,6) פסח לה׳, then comes again and again the remembrance of that halting testing time of God’s consideration of the Jewish homes, when Israel’s fate hung between life and death, between freedom and slavery; and always again and again, correspondingly, have the Jewish People to dedicate their homes, and every soul in every home, to God in the פסת-offering, just as in that first solemn hour of hope of the birth of the Jewish Nation, to receive ever afresh from His Hands the gift of life and freedom. (See on Ex. 12,3—11; XIV,27 & 48).

V. 6. ובחמשה עשר יום. And with each return of the 15th ניסן, the day of the deliverance, חג המצות לה׳, the redeemed people, enjoying their freedom, have again and again to gather themselves to a closed “circle” (חג. I.L.), about God, with unleavened bread, the remembrance-sign of slavery, the mark of our freedom having been won solely by God, and the acknowledging-sign of our eternally belonging to Him. And שבעת ימים מצות תאכלו, for seven days are we to keep away from eating any leavened bread, to let ourselves be permeated with the facts which the מצות represents, (see Ex. 12,8, 15, 18 & 39). That שבעת ימים מצות תאכלו only expresses a prohibitory command, if one wants to eat bread one may only eat it unleavened, has already been explained there in v. 15. חג המצות: three terms are used to designate the Festivals:— מועד .חג ,רגל ,מועד, referring to our “meeting” with God, רגל to our meeting with His Torah in its Sanctuary, חג to our meeting with the Nation in its circle gathering about God (see Ex. 5,1).

V. 7 & 8. See on Ex. 12,16: מלאכת עבודה, an objective work on matter in general which is done for the general service of the world, furthering and keeping the culture of the world (we were placed in the world לעבדה. I.L.), in contrast to מלאכת אוכל נפש, subjective work for the purpose of furthering personal human nourishment (see ibid). והקרבתם אשה לה׳, seeking nearness to God by giving oneself up to devotion to the Fire of His Torah is the common aim of all מועדים, which is to be gained by each מועד from the standpoint of the special meaning which is innate in that particular festival.

On Ex. 12,16 we have already referred to the words of our sages who explain the words: החדש הזה לכם, by דוגמא שלכם. Thereby they include the meaning of our whole lunar calendar in the thought that, in the phases of light and darkness of the moon we are to find the picture of our own internal and external radiation by the Light of God, and the Grace of God, which waxes and wanes according to the position we assume towards Him. Towards this Light we are ever again and again to strive, moon-like, out of the deepest darkness. We even find God, in the dispensation of His Grace and His Justice, called sun and shield: כי שמש ומגן ה׳ אלקים (Ps. 84,12). It is not the sun which is to be the light of our days nor the moon which is to be its reflection for us at night, but God will ultimately be the eternal Light which will never set. לא יהיה לך עוד השמש לאור יומם ולנגה הירח לא יאיר לך והיה ה׳ לד לאור עולם וגו׳ לא יבא עוד שמשך וירחד לא יאסף כי ה׳ יהיה לד לאור עולם ושלמו ימי אבלן, (Is. 9,19 & 20). And the beginning of this chapter visualises us, ultimately fully radiated with the Light of God, rising like a sun on the dark skies of the world, lighting the way to nations and Kings: קומי אורי וגו׳ כי הנה החשך יכסה ארץ וגו׳ ועליך יזרח ה׳ וכבודו עליך יראה והלכו גוים לאורך ומלכים לנגה זרחך, (ibid. 1—3).

If we continue in this trend of thought, the day of the full moon — the moon being fully illuminated by the light of the sun — would represent the condition of our being fully radiated with the Light and the Grace of God; the day of the new moon, just the beginning of our struggling upwards out of night and darkness to the Light and Grace; the first quarter, a stage of having already achieved the first rising step to the Light and Grace; and the last quarter an already declining or waning stage of falling away out of the nearness to the Light and Grace of God; and the lunar dates fixed for our festivals fit very well in with the character of these phases of the moon. The two festivals celebrating the creation and the preservation of the existence of our Nation, פסח and סכות, both complete gifts of acts of grace from God, fall on days of the full-moon. The gift of the Torah to us was not an unconditional gift, it is only one half of God’s act of Grace. God gave us the Torah, but for its blessings to accrue for us, requires the addition of our own work of recognition and fulfilment. The giving of the Law and its festival falls in the time of the first quarter of the moon. The day of תרועה, shaking us up out of having slipped far from God, into struggling up and back into Life and Grace, reaches us at a time when the moon is in darkness and the new-moon is seeking the light. And first, by our own work on ourselves in the days of returning to the light we must have passed through the first quarter. We must first, in definite efforts for progress, on the half-way path from the first quarter to full-moon, have grasped that Hand of God, which, atoning for the past, illuminating the darkness, is ever stretched out to us to help our efforts to be worthy of the full Light, before we then, on the day of the full moon can, happy in the rays of His Grace trustfully build up our “huts” on earth and rejoice in the abundance of His “gifts”. Finally, that Festival which would teach us, taking the Torah in our arms, cheerfully to endure and remain unchanged with God, even when the material signs of His Grace dwindle, the huts fall, and we have no longer His gifts in our hands, that Festival, שמיני עצרת, falls in the last quarter, in the phase of the declining moon. The two festivals which come from our history in the פורים :גלות and חנוכה, also fall in characteristically corresponding phases of the moon. פורים is the פסח of the גלות and, like it, falls on the fourteenth day of the lunar month. חנוכה is the שמיני עצרת of the גלות, preaching standing fast and holding out with God and His Torah, even when one’s material fate is inclining downwards, and this falls, like it, in the phase of the declining moon.

V. 10. לא נתחייבו בעומר קודם שנכנסו לארץ :כי תבואו (Menachoth 84,a). When you have attained, not only freedom, but also the national independence which the possession of one’s own land gives, וקצרתם את קצירה, and you cut the produce of the land, bring that which the land has produced into your own personal possession, then והבאתם וגו׳, then bring the first omer that you cut, i.e. the amount that corresponds to one day’s food (see Ex. 16,36), to the כהן, to your representative in God’s Sanctuary of the Torah. That which the soil has produced and the sun matured has not grown for you, but for the Torah of God’s Sanctuary, so that its demands may be fulfilled. And this עומר must be ראשית קצירכם, no other cutting may precede it. But nevertheless this קצירה and קצירכם only apply to those products of the soil which are regarded as the real harvest of the Land, those five kinds of grain which represent the real bread, the real food of the Nation, viz. חיטה ,שעורה ,כוסמת ,שבלת שועל and שיפון (wheat, barley oats, rye, and spelt). They are the same which in the מצוה of מצות and הלה represent the idea of bread (Menachoth 70a & b). And even with these five kinds, cutting before the עומר is only forbidden from such fields which can be considered as those from which the real harvest of such grain is hoped for, but not from בית השלחים שבעמקים, from fields which require artificial watering and which lie in deep valleys. The עומר was also not allowed to be brought from such fields. ממקום שאתה מביא אי אתה קוצר ממקום שאי אתה מביא אתה קוצר (Menachoth 71,a, see תוספות 68a).

V. 11. והניף וגו׳: Above in Ch. 2,14—16 it has already been ordained that this מנחת בכורים, this homage-paying gift of the first cutting is not brought in ears but, like every other מנחה, in the form of flour with oil and incense, and of that a קומץ of the flour and oil together with the whole of the incense is given over to the fire on the altar. The process is also indicated there by which the flour is obtained at once from the fresh grains of corn. From the expression אביב which is used there, the traditional law is taught, that this עומר is to be brought from barley which is the earliest grain, to ripen (see ibid). Here, only the law of the תנופה is added. We have explained on Ex. 29,24 the meaning of this procedure, consisting of an horizontal movement away from oneself and towards oneself in all four directions, מוליך ומביא and a vertical one upwards and downwards. Then follows the procedure of הגשה בקרן דרומית-מערבית, which is prescribed for all independent Menachoth of which a part, as here, or the whole, is burnt on the Altar. (See on Ch. 2,8). By the procedure of the תנופה, one’s material nourishment (flour) one’s well-being (oil) and one’s mental satisfaction with life (incense) which are all represented in the עומר are stripped of every idea of selfishness (תנופה) and of every purely material earthly character (הרמה), and placed in the service of one’s fellow men and of God. And then in הגשה this symbol of our whole earthly existence with all its prosperity and joy of life is laid in homage at the feet of the Torah and of the spirit which is begotten by it (west-south corner. I.L.), to acknowledge that it is only and solely through its ruling influence that this dedication of our earthly existence to the community and to God can find its realisation.

ממהרת השבת יניפנו הכהן. In opposition to the Sadducean way of taking this ממחרת השבת to mean the day after Sabbath, i.e. the first day of the week, so that the Festival of Shebuoth, which is fixed on the fiftieth day after bringing the עומר, must always fall on a Sunday (and this interpretation and fixing of Shebuoth is made into a cardinal point of their denial of tradition), the Halacha, (Menachoth 65a & b), teaches that by this ממחרת השבת nothing else is to be understood than the 16th ניסן, the day after the first day of פסח. There, too, the inappropriateness, nay the absurdity, of this Sadducean interpretation is shown — amongst other proofs — by the fact that the Torah could not possibly have meant to say that the עומר should be brought on the day after the Sabbath in the sense of the שבת בראשית, the ordinary weekly Sabbath, as there are more than fifty such days in the year and there would be no indication at all which of these Sabbath’s the Torah meant. Also it has quite rightly been remarked that the Sudducean interpretation must then also take the עד ממחרת השבת השביעית of v. 16 to refer likewise to the weekly Sabbath. But if the first day of the counting is “a day after Sabbath”, then the fiftieth day is not “a day after the Seventh”, but after the eighth Sabbath. Maimonides (הל׳ תמידין ומוספים 7,2) also refers to Joshua 5,2: ויאכלו מעבור הארץ ממחרת הפסח, where, quite in agreement with the traditional Halacha, the eating of the new produce of the Land is connected with the first day of פסח. Accordingly the first day of the Festival, the fifteenth ניסן, would be called שנת here by virtue of its שבתון character, which, by איסור מלאכת עבודה, differentiates it from the succeeding intermediate days of the Festival.

Nevertheless it does not occur anywhere else that the term שבת is meant to be understood as a יום-טוב, and morover there is no indication in the text of the Torah that it is just the first day, and not the last day, which is also שבתון, which is meant. Although against this, Wessely in his commentary points out that in that case the text would more suitably have said ממחרת החג.

Perhaps the whole difficulty may be solved by the following consideration. In the verse immediately preceding, the עומר is called: ראשית קצירכם. Thereby, before it is brought, or at any rate before it is cut, any cutting of the new produce of the land is forbidden, as well as also (v. 14), up to this day, eating or using this new produce in any form is prohibited. So that up to the day of the עומד, a pause in the agricultural activity is called, the grain stands ready on the stalks, but may not be cut or used. Such a stop in agriculture is simply called שבת. So, in Ch. 25,2 et seq. we find ושבתה הארץ שבת לה׳ etc. On the 15th ניסן it was still שבת הארץ, and the 16th, the day of the עומר, with which this “Sabbath” came to an end was in quite a literal sense, מחרת השבת.

V. 12 & 13. קצירה וספירה בלילה והבאה ביום :ביום הניפכם את העומר, (Menachoth 56a). The cutting, and the counting that begins with it, (v. 12), is done in the night, but the offering is only made in the daytime. It is to be the clear sphere of morally-free human life, not to the dark night province of physically-bound life in Nature, that the Omer — like the bringing of all other offerings — belongs. כבש תמים בן שנתו: Arising out of the עומר התנופה, which dedicated the Nation’s harvest to humanity in general and to the service of God, this lamb represents the Nation as a single living unit which gives up the whole of its life and efforts, with the everlasting freshness of youth, to the guidance of its Divine Shepherd, and strives ever upwards towards the height of the goal He sets for it; and in this striving up to the goal of national moral perfection it elevates its “flour and oil and its wine” with it, also into the realm of ennobled, spiritual, godly aims of the Nation. Thus it may be significant to the highest degree, in what way, here, where the national efforts for prosperity through possession of the soil are expressed before God, this expression receives its own special mark. For whereas elsewhere the Mincha of a כבש consists of one עשרון (see Numb. 15,4), here, for the Mincha כבש העומר two עשרונים are ordered. But the wine remains just the ordinary quantity of one רביעית, and the Halacha (Menachoth 89b) teaches us that the oil too which is mixed with the flour, also remains at the usual quantity of the רביעית (this is also indicated by the written form of the word נסכה, which makes the נסל of the Mincha, i.e. the oil, the same as the נסר of the כבש, i.e. the wine, נסכה דמנחה כנסכו דיין (see Rashi ibid.), and prescribes the one usual quantity for both). Now there is a characteristic difference in the objects used for a קרבן צבור, an offering made in the name of the Nation, whether the number brought is one or two. In the same way as the signal given to call the Nation together through its representatives, the נשיאים and ראשים, i.e. looking on the Nation as a unit, was given by one חצוצרת, but if the signal was given by two חצוצרות it meant the calling of the Nation together by every member of it, looking on the Nation not as one unit, but as a plurality of individuals, so in the same way in a קרבן צבור, the single number, one פר, one איל, one כבש is the symbol of the Nation as a single unit, whereas two פרים, two אילים, two כבשים, is the expression of each individual of the Nation, the Nation regarded as a plurality of individuals. If then, here, two עשרונים סלת are prescribed as the Mincha for the one כבש of the national offering, it proclaims that the Jewish Nation is not to know any national prosperity at which individuals starve. The Nation is only to think itself rich, when, by all working together, no single individual of all its members goes hungry, when each single member of its great numbers has “his עשרון״. On the other hand the “oil and wine” of the Nation is only ascribed to the Nation as a whole. “Riches and unworried joy of life are not ensured to every son of the Torah in his individual private life, לא יחדל אביון מקרב הארץ, and pain and grief belong, just as joy, to the testing tasks of a complete Jewish life. Only in the prosperity of the community as a whole is the individual to know himself rich, and in the immortal blosoming of his Nation is he to find his own part, too, of undisturbable happiness in life. To the two עשרונים of “flour” one רביעית “oil” and one רביעית “wine”.

V. 14. ולחם וקלי וכרמל. From Kerithuth 5a, it is evident that קלי is flour obtained from roasting the fresh grain (as above Ch. 2,14), but כרמל is the unaltered green grains of corn, לא נשתנה מברייתו. So that חדש, new produce, i.e. the five kinds of grain mentioned above on v. 10, are not allowed to be eaten in any form whatsoever: עד עצם היום הזה עד הביאכם את קרבן אלקיכם. According to סוכה 41a & b, this fixed two terms for the beginning of the permission to eat. בזמן שאין בהמ״ק קיים, when the Temple and the Altar are not in existence so that bringing the עזמן-offering is not possible: עד עצם היום הזה, then יום הנף, the day fixed for bringing it brings permission to eat the new fruits. בזמן שבהמ״ק קיים, but when Temple and Altar are there, the permission only starts: עד הביאכם את קרבן וגו׳, with the bringing of the עומר. Regarding the first period there is a difference of opinion as to whether עד ועד בכלל or ולא עד בכלל, whether “until” is inclusive or exclusive, whether the יום הנף כלו אסור, whether, when the Temple was not in existence, the day of the bringing the עומר still entirely belonged to the period of prohibition (עד ועד בכלל), or whether as soon as האיר פני מזרח at daybreak of the 16th the היתר applied (עד ולא עד בכלל). The עומד is מתיר בהשרשה, i.e. by the bringing of the עומר, all produce which had already taken root in the ground becomes allowed; but what has only been sown, but not yet taken root, as well as all that is sown after the עומר, remains prohibited until the עומר of the next year (Menachoth 71a). בכל מושבותיכם: according to Kiddushin 37a, by בכל מושבותיכם, i.e. בכל מקום שאתם יושבים, outside Israel, חוצה לארץ would also be included. But nevertheless, according to another opinion חדש being a מצוה התלויה בארץ is only prohibited in Israel, and מושבותיכם only gives the Law that the איסור חדש is only to start לאחר ירושה וישיבה, after the settlement in the Land has been completed (see ibid. and Menachoth 68,b); (ועיין שו״ת כנסת יחזקאל י״ד סי׳ מ״א דס״ל דאף דק״ל דחדש בח״ל דאורייתא ודחדש אסור אף בשל נכרים מ״מ ה״מ בא״י אבל בח״ל מותר בשל נכרים ע״ש).

V. 15. שתהא ספירה לכל :וספרתם לכם .וספרתם לכם ממחרת השבת וגו׳ אחד ואחד, not the Nation as a unit, through its representatives, as it is for the Yobel, where וספרת לך is addressed to these, to the ב״ד, but the Nation in all its members, each individual of the Nation has the duty to count (Menachoth 65b תוספות there). So that, ממחרת השבת, when you have not only celebrated the Festival of your having attained freedom, but you have also brought to your mind before God the fact of your independence gained by possession and enjoyment of one’s own land, so that you are conscious of both those possessions, freedom and prosperity which, in general, are the aims which all national desires and all national efforts are directed to attain, then you are to consider yourself not at the goal, but only at the beginning of your national destiny and only then begin to count for the acquisition of another goal. Thus this command to count is expressed in Deut. 16,9, in these terms:— מהחל חרמש בקמה תחל לספור שבעה שבועות, “When the sickle begins at the standing corn, begin thou to count etc.”. Where others leave off their counting, you begin your counting.

שבע שבתות תמימות תהיינה. The addition of the word תמימות to שבתות proves definitely that by שבת here a Sabbath day can not be meant. “Completely full Sabbaths” must of necessity refer to periods of time consisting of several days. Now we know from Nedarim 60a that in Hebrew phraseology שבת אחד, “one Sabbath” designates a Sabbath with the six weekdays belonging to it, no matter whether these days come before or after it. So that if, for example, somebody swears he will hold off from drinking wine for “one whole Sabbath”, קונם יין שאני טועם שבת אחד, if this vow was taken on a Sabbath, he may not drink wine until and including the following Friday, if it was made on a Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday etc., wine is אסור to him until the following Sunday, Monday, Tuesday etc. So that every Sabbath is taken as the beginning, end, or centre point of a fixed number of days which are attached to it or which are grouped about it, and שבת תמימה means a Sabbath with the six week days attached to it, מיום ליום as the Mishna there puts it. And actually the meaning of the Sabbath does extend to the weekdays before and after it. The days leading up to it, see their goal in it, and are to be lived in the idea that the work that is done in them is of such a nature that one need not be ashamed when Sabbath arrives to lay it in homage at the feet of the Lord and Master. The days that follow it are to bring into effect the fresh spirit that was won anew on it, and to be the proof that, and how, one has renewed the bond between oneself and the Lord and Director of one’s world, and dedicated one’s weekly activities to His service. Thus, in general, Sunday Monday and Tuesday are regarded as the result of the past Sabbath, and Wednesday, Thursday and Friday, as preliminary to the coming one (Pesachim 106a). We accordingly believe that here too שבע שבתות תמימות תהיינה mean nothing other than:— seven complete sabbath cycles are to have come, seven times is the Sabbath to exert its full educating and sanctifying influence on the working weekdays that precede and succeed it, accordingly, on a Sunday Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday, Thursday and Friday, whether these days come before or after the Sabbath. So that on whatever day of the week, the 16th ניסן, the יום הנף may fall, that day is the first of a seven-day period grouped around a Sabbath, and such a period must have occurred, and passed seven times, before the counting which is prescribed here, is completed. Hence this complete Sabbath period begins at the entry of the night of the 15th to the 16th ניסן and then, too, the counting is to begin (Menachoth 66a).

We can accordingly understand why it does not say: וספרתם לכם וגו׳ שבע שבתות תמימות, as it runs quite simply in the repetition of the command in Deut. 16,9: שבע שבועות תספר לד, but here gives the command first in general without an object and then: שבע וגו׳ תהיינה follows as an independent sentence. שבתות is not identical with שבוע .שבועות is any period of seven days, שבת is the seven day period borne by the Sabbath. As the object of וספרתם לכם, the seven day period would only be the time formed just by the counting. Separated from the command to count, as a separate sentence, and called “Sabbath” it is the result of the seven day period given by the Sabbath which the counting only serves to bring home to our minds.

So that it is commanded to “count” from the day celebrating our freedom and our self-supporting national prosperity. Thereby these achievements are first of all, in general, taught to be considered not as the end, the goal, but only as the beginning of our national efforts. Then it goes on to teach that before the goal up to which this “counting” leads is reached, Sabbath, with its ever freshly recurring acknowledgement of God as the Creator, Lord, and Ruler of the world which Man Masters, and of the world which masters Man, must have proved its educational and healing strength on us seven times. So that freedom and the basis of independence—possession of land — must seven times have received their purification and adjustment by Sabbath thoughts before we can be reckoned fit for the remembrance of that acquisition up to which the counting leads, and in which, accordingly the freedom ensured by possession of land is to regard as its true goal.

Now if this acquisition — as tradition teaches, and as we shall have to consider more fully below — is none other than the Law of God, the Torah, we can at once understand how this Torah sets being completely permeated with the homage to God, and the joyful entry into His service which Sabbath teaches, as the preparatory preliminary condition for its acquisition. For Sabbath is older than the Jewish nation. And in fact it was the reintroduction of the institution of Sabbath, — with its homage-paying act of שביתת מלאכה and quite specially with the release which this gives from the overpowering worry of providing food, — that preceded the giving of the Law, and which was the preparatory education of the freed People to become the People of God’s Law. If we consider what we remarked on Ex. 16,1 & 2, on the meaning of the Sabbath of the Manna, and which finds complete confirmation in the words with which Moses at the end of the wandering reflected on Israel’s having been fed with the Manna and its meaning for faithful obedience to the Law of God, in Deut. 8,1—3 et seq.: לדעת את אשר בלבבך התשמר מצותיו אם לא, then this sevenfold counting of Sabbath weeks from “עומר״ to “Torah” appears in a self-explanatory light.

V. 16. תספרו חמשים יום עד ממחרת וגו׳. The counting is twofold. Seven Sabbath weeks are to be counted, as it says in Deut. 16,9: שבעה שבועות תספר לך, and the days are also to be counted until the fiftieth day which marks the day after the seven Sabbath-weeks, מצוה למימני יומי ומצוה למימני שבועי (Chagiga 17b). This fiftieth day is the goal to be reached by the counting. This day itself is not counted. It is not impossible that the חמשים יום is in apposition to ממחרת השבת “until the day after the seventh Sabbath-week, the fiftieth day, are you to count”. חמשים יום similarly to ביום עשתי עשר יום ,ביום שנים עשר יום, in Numb. 7,2 & 28, where also the ordinal number is expressed by the cardinal number in the sense of:— the day on which eleven days, twelve days, have passed since the beginning of the counting. Or the תספרו here is not such an explicit counting as וספרתם לכם, but it means to imply thereby that, up till then, not only weeks but days are to be counted, as the text does not satisfy itself with designating the seven Sabbath-weeks which have passed, but sums up also the number of days which thereby have passed, together with the one which has now been reached.

So that, apart from the sevenfold effect which the Sabbath is thought of as having in the seven weeks, the period which is passed through and ultimately reached by the forty-nine and fifty days must have some meaning in itself. Now counting days, and actually the number seven in such counting, is not unknown to us elsewhere in the Torah. For instance in connection with זב and זבה (Ch. 15,13 & 28), and in general the passing of a period of seven days in the laws of טומאה and טהרה are given for striving to get out of a condition of טומאה, and as bringing it to a close, so as to enter the state of טהרה with the eighth day. A sevenfold counting of periods of seven days, a counting of forty nine days, so as then to enter a new condition on the fiftieth day would accordingly be the most complete doing away with the unfree טומאה restraint of being bound by one’s senses, and the fiftieth day would bring the most positive entry into the טהרה-realm of moral freedom. Just as the fiftieth year brought a fresh foundation of the Jewish State on the basis of the most general internal social freedom, so the fiftieth day of the עומר denotes the inner moral freedom to be necessary for the political external freedom and independence, and as being that acquisition which is the first condition for the country in which, to the freedom and independence granted by God, the Torah of God can then be received from the Hand of God. The former, political freedom, can be received passively by us as a gift from the Grace of God. But this moral freedom, only beckons to us as an acquisition to be acquired only by the sevenfold strenuous inner work on ourselves.

If we consider that in accordance with all this, the fiftieth day, i.e. the day after the seven times seven days, falls very closely in the same idea as the meaning of the eighth day of the מילה (see article thereon in the Gesammelte Schriften vol. III), and we combine the idea of counting the Sabbath weeks and the counting of the days together, then they appear simply as an emanation from just those two institutions Sabbath and Mila with which God wished to lay the foundation for Israel to be the People of His Law. Paying homage to God in nature and history, and the resulting subordination of Man and his position in the world to the service of God, as is taught by Sabbath, and struggling for moral purity by subordinating, of one’s own free will, the body to God’s law of morality as Mila demands, these were initial impulses which were laid as a foundation in the People long before they were constituted into the People of the Torah. And it is just these factors which the counting of the days and weeks from the עומד to the Day of the Receiving of the Torah is to bring home to our minds each year afresh as the preliminary fundamental conditions for our great mission in the world.

והקרבתם מנחה חדשה לה׳: this refers to the שתי לחם mentioned in v. 17. They are מנחה חדשה, they are the first מנחה that may be brought from the new produce of each year. Although secular use of the new produce was allowed from the time the עומר was brought, the prohibition for the Temple lasted till the bringing of the שתי לחם, and not only מנחות but also בכורים and נסכים were not allowed to be brought from the new produce until then: העומר היה מתיר במדינה ושתי הלחם במקדש (Menachoth 84b & 68b).

V. 17. ולא מחוצה לארץ :ממושבתיכם (Menachoth 83b), According to ר׳ עקיבא (Menachoth 46a): הלחם מעכב את הכבשים ואין הכבשים מעכבין את הלחם, it is the שתי הלחם which are the indispensable condition. All the offerings mentioned in the following verses, and also the שני כבשים prescribed in v. 19 and in v. 20 connected in תנופה with the שתי לחם, all are only additions to the שתי לחם, so that it would be possible for the loaves to be brought without the lambs, but not the lambs, without the loaves. It is the לחם which is the עיקר (ibid. 46b). Perhaps that is why the א in תביאו so abnormally has a דגש, to raise the הבאת שתי לחם to the foreground in contrast to all the other מנחות which are connected with other offerings, to show it as the centre-point about which all the offerings which follow are grouped.—שיהו שוות :שני עשרונים ;שיהו שוות :שתים, they are to be equal both in quality and in quantity (ת״כ), as in all cases where pairs occur in offerings the greatest possible similarity is demanded. — סלת תהיינה: in contrast to the עומר which was brought from barley. חמץ תאפינה in contrast to all other Menachoth which were not allowed to be חמץ and of which even the שירים were not allowed to be baked חמץ (with the single exception of the לחמי תודה, see Ch. 2,11 & VI,10). This bringing the שתי לחם of חמץ has already been referred to in Ch. 2,13, and there, on Ch. 2,11 & 12 and Ch. 7,13 we have explicitly explained the significance of the Azereth loaves being brought just of תמץ and would refer to there. בכורים לה׳: these two loaves were the first מנחה in each year which was allowed to be brought from the fresh produce to that year; with them, as already remarked above, the Altar was opened for the admission in general of the produce of that year, but they, themselves, according to an opinion in Menachoth 83b, which is accepted by רמב״ם as the Halacha, הל׳ תמירים ומוספים 8,2 (see מל״מ there), need not inevitably be of the new produce: שתי לחם הבאות מן הישן כשרות. This Halacha would strongly support our way of taking these loaves being חמץ and altogether raise the whole procedure out of the sphere of being merely a harvest festival.

The עומר was brought from barley flour. But barley does not really represent human food, it is מאכל בהמה (Sota 15a & 15b). It is, accordingly, in the עומר merely physical existence which appears to be granted by possession of the land. It is only on the fiftieth day, after the seven weeks counting of the days and weeks of the God-acknowledging struggle upwards to טהרה, only after the recurrence of the “Day of Remembrance of Lawgiving”, that the Jewish Nation approaches the Altar of its God with the real human food, bread made from wheat. And this bread is חמץ. It bears the stamp of social political freedom and independence, possessions which the Jewish People never originally had, the representation of which, שאור, equally with the representation of riches of the soil דבש, is never to be used as something to be given up to the Altar לריח ניחוח. They are rather something which is only to be obtained from the Hand of God, by Israel giving itself entirely up to God’s Torah. They are, accordingly, in the חמץ) ,שתי לחם), and ,ביכורים (דבש), only to be laid in homage in front of the Altar as acknowledgement of possessions promised and granted by the Torah (see, explicitly, above on Ch. 2,11 & 12).

And it is two loaves which represent the bread of the Jewish National existence and independence, they are quite similar to each other, but nevertheless: נילושות אחת אחת ונאפות אחת אחת, each has to be kneaded and baked quite separately by itself, and all oil and incense must be missing from them (Menachoth 59a). They thereby express, even more poignantly than the עומר, the fact that the Jewish Nation is only to reckon on the independence of its existence as a whole, on the ensured continuance of the existence of its individual members. But it quite definitely denies that prosperity and well-being is a necessary part of the life of every person.

V. 18. שבעת כבשים .והקרבתם על הלחם שבעת כבשים: seven sheep, really “a number seven of sheep”, a number seven presented in sheep, similarly as we find שבעת ימים, ’a number seven formed by days. We have already learnt to recognize the numbers one and two in public offerings as representing the Nation as a single joint unit or as a community of separate individuals. Apart from these, the only number which normally recurs in public offerings is the number seven. The מוספים prescribed in Numb. XXVIII and XXIX only consist of these three numbers, and even the decreasing numbers of the פרי החג, from thirteen to seven, have the underlying number seven as their base, as P.G., we shall have to show. In an article in the Jeshurun (5th year and reprinted in the Gesam. Schriften. I.L), we have already worked out how the idea of the Sabbath makes the number seven indicate the invisible abstract One connected with the visible concrete six, invisibly revealing itself in the visible, invisibly ruling and guiding the visible world. Accordingly, if כבש in offerings is the symbol for a person following a higher guidance, a Shepherd, for his fate and fortune, and in public offerings, for the Nation regarding its fate from following a Higher Guide, then the Nation presenting itself as שבעת כבשים represents itself as having its fate connected with God, the invisible One, its fate mastered and guided by Him, He being visible in its fate, its fate being nothing other than a revelation of God in the world of humanity. We have already repeatedly remarked that פר represents a person actively working in the service of God, and איל, one who has the strength and power to be a leader to his contemporaries. So that if the general formula for the festival offerings, as laid down by the ראש חדש offering, is:— פרים בני בקר שנים ואיל אחד כבשים בני שנה שבעה תמימים לעולה ושעיר עזים אחד חטאת, then the Nation “invited to a meeting with God” presents itself as such whose every member stands active in the service of God, which therefore in its strength, blessed by God, is, as a nation, the leading nation, inviting all the other nations to follow its example, whose whole history is naught but a God-revealing pointing Finger of God, and which therefore, with all these factors, and for all of them, gives itself up entirely to the service of following God, and with regards to where it has slipped in its eternal mission as shown in the Sanctuary of God’s Torah, it promises in future to stand firm, faithfully clinging to its duty, and so atone for the past. Only on ר״ה and י״כ, where quite specially the consciousness of past shortcomings calls the Nation to God, and equally so on the day of שמיני עצרת, when Israel even if deprived of “house and possessions” still holds fast to its God, happy with the Torah in its arms, only on these days does the Nation appear not in the plurality of its individual members, but only in its joint community as the Nation of the Law, not as פרים בני בקר שנים, but only as פר אחד, is there in the “elevating offering”, the expression of efficiency of service in God’s Kingdom on earth. For if is just from that, from the general mission of the nation, that, on ר״ה and י״כ each individual is to work himself up again to the pure stage of a worker in the service of God; and it is only just the thought, that, in spite of all the shortcomings of the individuals, the Jewish Nation as a whole, still has the unloseable eternal meaning of being the unique People of the Law of God, that even when “robbed of home and possessions” still keeps happy in their bond with God.

Now here we find the same group of offerings as the מועדים-offerings, but with some nuances of difference, There is one פר, similarly to י״כ ,ר״ה and ש״ע, there are seven כבשים as on all the Moadim, but there are two אילים which never occur elsewhere, and the כבשים come first; whereas at all the מוספים the order is:— פרים or פר, then איל and then כבשים, at the offerings accompanying the שתי לחם it is פר ,כבשים and אילים that are ordered. The group here accompanying the שתי לחם differs from the מוסף prescribed for the ביכורים-day in Numb. 28,26 in two respects: (a) in the number of the bullocks and the rams, there it is פרים שנים and איל אחד, here פר אחד and אילים שנים; and (b) in the order of precedence, סדרן: there the פרים come first, here the כבשים. So that the two groups are by no means identical. Those in Numb. חומש הפקודים come on the בכורים-day in consequence of its general character as a מועד as מוספים, those prescribed here come in consequence of its special character of a בכורים-day. The two groups stand in relation to one another in exactly the same way as the offerings prescribed in אחרי מות for י״כ do to the מוספים of that day ordered in Numb. 29,7. In conformity with the idea of the בכורים-day which characterises the שתי לחם, the שבעת כבשים come first here. For the independent life which is granted to each single individual by the Land of God, is a part of, and emanates from, the general fate of the nation which proves His guidance and His nearness and government. Every single individual has his “bread” as a consequence of his participation in the general subordination and acquiescence to the guidance of “Israel’s Shepherd”, and each single individual receives his “bread” so that he can do his part in working for the accomplishment of Israel’s mission to be צאן מרעיתו. A mission which can only be realised in faithfully following the paths laid down in His Torah. Then, by carrying out this mission, the Jewish Nation as a whole becomes פר אחד, the one animal working on God’s acres of mankind, and it is only on the basis of the accomplishment of the national mission of the realization of God’s Will on earth, to build up the Jewish welfare internally, and the welfare of mankind externally, that every member of the nation becomes of equal value in God’s Eyes, the Nation can present itself as שני אילים, every Jew becomes an איל, one who stands in the van, blessed with full strength as an example showing the way to his fellow men. Equality, which in participation of wealth and external fortune remains a utopia, becomes a reality, a complete reality, to be obtained at all times and by everybody on the basis of carrying out the dictates of the Torah and the moral value which that alone confers. In participation in worldly goods the two עשרונים of the עומר only received one common part of oil and wine and incense, and the two chometz loaves of the ביכורים-Day lack these entirely. But in the spiritual energy of the living personality, equal blessing, equal strength, and equal importance, beckons to every individual Jew for the mission of the whole Nation. However small or however great his portion may be of the “oil” and “wine” and “incense” which is promised to the community as a whole, he is to find his own independent existence (שתי לחם חמץ) and whether in rich or modest circumstances become an איל, a man showing the way on those paths and to those ends which God has indicated. And as such, even his smallest participation in those possessions which make life powerful and cheerful gains the richest importance, and so, like the שבעת כבשים and the פר of the community as a whole, each איל of the multitude of the community also does not lack its מנחה nor its ומנחתם ונסכיהם :נסך (as is prescribed in detail in Numb.) אשה ריח ניחח לה׳.

V. 19. ועשיתם שעיר. But the Nation never approaches its God, with the expression of its כבשים-אילים-פרים-ideal in the elevating offering, without at the same time in שעיר לחטאת giving expression to its consciousness of how far off from this ideal the past and present state of the nation still is, and how, only in the promise of future שעיר-like, unseduceable steadfastness, the Nation dares allow itself the expression of its ideal mission.

ושני כבשים בני שנה לזבח שלמים: to the participation in that ideal of the Nation, and the consciousness of past insufficiency keeping one out of it, and the eternal ideal of atonement ever offering new happy absolution, now finally come: שני כבשים בני שנה לזבח שלמים, to be attached to the שתי לחם חמץ. They are the only שלמי צבור, public peace offerings, which exist at all, and as שני כבשים, they must be taken to represent the nation in all its individual members. They come as an essential complement to the שתי לחם. The Nation accordingly expresses thereby that the independence of existence granted on the soil of the Land-of-the-Torah by the Torah, and for the Torah, is not only to ensure everybody its לחם חמץ, its “bread of independence”, but that just in that consciousness of its being granted by God, and for God, everybody is to enjoy a happy satisfied existence, knowing that he is living under the Eye of God, the Shepherd of his life, as is symbolised by the שלמים-offering. But being שלמי צבור, it does not emanate as שלמי-יחיד do, from the happy contented feeling of satisfied happy conditions of individual life, but is rather to bring to the consciousness of the comunity its destination to live a happy contented life, and so, like עולה and חטאת it stands in the קדש קדשים class of serious dedication of one’s actions, and accordingly its שחיטה is בצפון and אינן נאכלין אלא לזכרי כהונה like the חטאת (Zebachim 55a).

V. 20. והניף וגו׳ על לחם וגו׳ על שני הכבשים. In other cases where bread and the animal offerings, or parts of them, are waved and raised together, the bread lies on the parts of the animal. There the bread is an accessory to, and a complement of, the animal offering. The personality which is represented by the animal is the bearer of the bread. The consecration of the person is what really is required, and with it, and by it, his food and his means of procuring his food also become consecrated. But here it is the bread the שתי לחם which, as remarked above, has its own independent meaning. The loaves form the characteristic factor of the day, they are מעכב את הכבשים, not the reverse (v. 17). That is why it says first: והניף הכהן אותם על הלחם, as לחם עיקר. But on the other hand, the essential fact of the relation of the person to the food always remains. Hence: אם הוזקקו זה לזה, once they have been brought into connection in an offering procedure they are מעכבין זה את זה, then the loaves too may not be brought without the כבשים. More, if they have both been brought as prescribed, then, as always, the קדושה of the loaves is dependent on the קדושה of the כבשי עצרת מקדשין את הלחם בשחיטה :כבשים (47a). So that after it has first said אותם על לחם, where לחם is shown to be the עיקר, it then readjustingly adds על שני כבשים by which expression the כבשים are depicted as the bearers of the loaves. Accordingly in the actual practice neither the כבשים were laid on the loaves nor the loaves on them, but were held next to each other so that neither lost their own particular importance: מניח זה בצד זה ומניף (Menachoth 62a). This תנופה was done while the כבשים were still alive. The means of independent existence which comes from the national possession of the land is granted to every member of the nation so that each one can become a living member of God’s flock following the Shepherd, and only as such does each one get the bread necessary for an independent existence.

Referring to this תנופה, it says in Menachoth 62a: מוליך ומביא כדי לעצור רוחות רעות מעלה ומוריד כדי לעצור טללים רעים, that thereby injurious winds and damaging downfalls are kept away from the seeds and fruit. The blessing of the fields of the Land of Israel is not dependent solely on physical influences. The physical prosperity of the soil itself is dependent on the unselfish renunciation of its products, and devoting them to the purposes of a God-serving life as directed by His Torah. It is not outside, in the physical areas of heaven and earth, but in the halls of the Sanctuary of God’s Torah, where the source of the blessing of the Land of Israel lies.

קדש יהיו לה׳ לכהן. According to Menachoth 45b, this refers to the שתי לחם of which it has just been asserted that although they form the characteristic central point of the ביכורים-offering, they are nevertheless also to appear in the procedure of the offering as being dependent on the שני כבשים. Regarding these loaves we are now finally told that their whole consecration to God is transferred to giving them over to the קנאו השם :כהן ונתנו לכהן. No part of these חמץ-loaves are to come unto the altar (Ch. 2,12). But brought with the כבשים, they, the כבשים, are their מתיר, but they have to be eaten by the זכרי כהונה in the קדש, and teach that the bread of independent existence promised and granted to every individual by the soil of the Torah, and for the Torah, is to be enjoyed priest-like before God, so that even eating one’s material food becomes a holy service of God.

V. 21. וקראתם וגו׳. This verb lacks an object; for מקרא קדש יהיה לכם is a separate sentence. So that we are not told in the text what it is that is to be proclaimed. בעצם היום הזה evidently wishes to fix and connect the Festival instituted here with its מקרא קדש and איסור מלאכת עבודה firmly and permanently to the day of bringing the לחם ביכורים, the fiftieth day of counting the עומר. This presupposes reasons which might have caused us to wish to keep the festival on some other day. We can only obtain an explanation of this from tradition.

As is well known, in accordance with our definite tradition, in our prayers, we designate the ביכורים-day, called חג השבועות in Ex. 34,22 and Deut. 16,10 & 16, as זמן מתן תורתנו, as the time of our lawgiving. And in fact, a careful reading of Ch. XIX in Exodus shows that the day of the Revelation on Sinai was on the sixth or seventh day of the third month, accordingly on or about the fiftieth day of the day-and-month-counting which began on the sixteenth day of ניסן, as is explained in detail in Sabbath 86b et seq.

According to the tradition generally firmly held in the Nation, the Day of Lawgiving was on a Sabbath; the day of the exodus from Egypt, the 15th ניסן, was, according to the סדר עולם on a Friday, but according to the Talmud (Sabbath 87b) it was on a Thursday. According to that, taking the reckoning from the סדר עולם, the מתן תורה would actually have been on the fiftieth day from the 16th ניסן, but according to the Talmud, which is authoritative for us, it would only have taken place on the fifty-first, which the מ״א on א״ח Ch. 494 remarks as being striking (see חק יעקב thereon); so that the fiftieth day after the עומר would be, not the anniversary of the Day of the Lawgiving, but of the day before it. Now we have only to realise that, according to the Torah, the fixing of the beginning of the months is dependent on observation of the new moon, קידוש על פי הראיה, to see, that the fiftieth day after the עומר is by no means definitely attached to a particular day of the month of סיון (there being two new moons in between. I.L.). This is remarked on in Rosh Hashana עצרת פעמים חמשה פעמים ששה פעמים שבעה, that the Festival of שבועות starting on the fiftieth day after the עומר can fall on the fifth, the sixth or the seventh of סיון. Had the Torah intended the recurrence of the Lawgiving to be a Day of Remembrance of that event, it would have given us that historic date with the same precision that it gave us the 14th and 15th of ניסן to be Days of Remembrance of the Exodus from Egypt. But the idea of such a Festival of Remembrance may be so far from the intention of the Torah that it expressly wanted to ward off such an erroneous conception by saying: וקראתם בעצם היום הזה. For — so we believe — this wants to say:— not on the day of the month on which the event of the Lawgiving took place, which lies so near, but on the fiftieth day after the עומר which is fixed for the bringing of the ביכורים-bread, are you to celebrate the Festival, without any consideration of the day of the month. קרא is the special expression used in this chapter for the fixing of the festival which falls in a month by the act of the representatives of the nation sanctifying the new moon which, of course, fixed the date for that festival. But here, in this instance, it is not to be the fixing of the day of the new moon of סיון which is to determine the date of the festival in סיון, but it is to depend on the day when the new moon of ניסן was sanctified and the resulting date of the counting of the עומר.

But the fact that the day which is elevated to a Festival should be just not the day of the revelation on Sinai, but the final day of the counting which leads up to that, the greatest event in our history; that it should be, according to the generally accepted reckoning, the day before the Lawgiving, which did not occur on the fiftieth but on the fifty first, that fact should surely have a deep and important meaning for us.

It is not the fact of the revelation of the Torah, but our making ourselves worthy to receive it, that our מתן תורה Festival celebrates. It is the day before the Lawgiving, the last day of the הגבלה and פרישה, the day on which the nation finally presented itself as ready and worthy for the great mission to the world, to be the receivers and bearers of the Law of God, it is that day which the fiftieth day of the counting of the עומר represents. As we have remarked elsewhere, this Festival, differently to all the others, is not called after that which characteristically has to be done on it, but שבועות, after the counting of the weeks which preparatorily lead up to it. The Lawgiving, too, was in no wise concentrated on the day of Sinai. The Lawgiving and the receipt of the laws lasted during forty years, and the ten commandments received at Sinai have no greater divinity or holiness than any of the other six hundred and three commands and prohibitions which God gave through Moses. Quite clearly God Himself has explained the meaning and importance of the revelation on Sinai as being only an introduction to the laws which were to be transmitted through Moses. The Sinai-day was to be a proof by personal experience that God can speak to Man and had spoken to Moses, so that we would receive the whole Torah from the mouth of Moses with full confidence that it was the Word of God. הנה אנכי בא אליך בעב הענן בעבור ישמע העם בדברי עמך וגם בך יאמינו לעולם. So that as “the Ten Commandments” received no special place in the order of the daily public divine services, מפני תרעומת העם, so as to give no support to the non-Jewish idea that the “ten commandments” form the whole of God’s laws, or even that they had only a greater degree of godliness and holiness (see Berachoth 12,a), in the same way probably a similar consideration is the motive of the Torah in not raising just the day of the “Revelation of the Ten Commandments” to a national festival.

In this apparent intention of the Torah to keep the שבועות-day characterised as the final day of the counting which begins on פסח, the reason may also be sought which impelled the Nation and its sages to call this Festival עצרת. This name is never applied to this Festival in the Torah, but only to the final moed of סוכות and to the last day of פסה (see on v. 36 and Numb. 29,35, as well as Deut. 16,8).

חקת עולם בכל מושבותיכם לדרתיכם: Also when you have lost having “national” loaves, and, being far away from the Land of the Torah, can not celebrate the day as the “ביכורים-Day of חמץ-bread” it still remains עצם היום הזה, still it remains as the fiftieth day of the עומר, as the Day of Remembrance of making oneself worthy for receiving the Torah, in eternal value of a מועד.

V. 22. ובקצרכם וגו׳ (see on Ch. 19,9 & 10). These laws, and their being carried out, are the practical corollary to the promise in the עומר, and still more in the שתי לחם, which guaranteed that through the Torah, by means of the Nation, every one would receive the means of independent existence due to a human being. Without God’s Torah, it is only for those who possess land that an “independent existence worthy of human beings” ripens on the prosperous fields of the land, but the landless ones, the poor, and strangers in the land must wait on the sympathy or the perspicacity of the landed ones for a sufficiency for existence. To demand it from them is stamped as almost a crime by our “advanced” age, and their gifts of charity are humiliating to the receivers. Not so is it in the Nation whose members carry away the first cutting of their fields to the Sanctuary of the Torah of their God, and “wave” it; and then, on the commemoration-time of having received this Torah, bring, by the שתי לחם חמץ in the Sanctuary of this Torah, the acknowledgement and the vow that they can feel themselves as the People of the Torah only if the independent existence which is the due of every human being grows out of their own prosperity for every one of their fellows. In this nation the fields do not ripen, nor do the arms labour, solely for the owners of the land and the rich. The poor, the landless ones, and the strangers in the land have the right to be partners in the harvest to such an extent that this care for them is an imposed duty on the landowners, to which the poor have an absolute right. This is shown, as we worked out on Ch. 19,9 & 10, by the פאה and לקט rights of the poor, regarding which the owner of the field has not even טובת הנאה, the right to choose which poor man shall glean his field (see ים של שלמה, Chulin 8). Thus, to the conscientious owners who respect the Law, part of the field belongs to the poor and the stranger, and care for the poor becomes “צדקה״ a legal duty. The receiver of צדקה, no less than the giver, has his לחם חמץ and can remain erect in his human dignity; and the giver, in caring for his poorer compatriots sees nothing but the liquidation of a debt he owes to God, which he has incurred with every grain of corn which God has blessed on the fields of his possessions and allowed to mature from his labour. This conception of “צדקה״ is the greatest social triumph of the Torah in the People of God.

V. 23. Gratitude to God, as the source of freedom, country, and law, and of the prosperity of all the members of the nation which is to blossom from these factors, is what the Festival of the first month, and that of the third so closely connected with it, are to bring ever afresh to our minds. פסח with the שבועות ,עומר with the two חמץ-loaves are the Festivals of the Constitution of the Jewish Nation. Then the seventh month is the month for consideration and testing our relation to these factors of national and individual prosperity which God has given us, so that we work ourselves up to that height of purity and truth on which alone these factors of the promised blessing can result in a truly happy existence on earth.

V. 24. יהיה לכם שבתון וגו׳. Not like v. 8: בחדש וגו׳ ,פסח לה׳, or v. 27: אך בעשור וגו׳ ,יום הכפורים הוא, or v. 34: בתמשה עשר וגו׳ ,חג הסכות, does it here give first the general character of the day, saying: יום תרועה יהיה לכם, and then give the mode of the special procedure of the Festival. But here the day is at once characterised by the duties we have to fulfil on it, and this introduction to the seventh month is quite in accordance with the idea of the nature of its festivals which we have already indicated in the previous verse. No commemoration of gifts received from God, do we celebrate on this day but it is a day which invites us to work on our own selves. Its tasks are described as שבתון, cessation of our activities with material matter, of working for the establishment of our future, and instead of that to give our energies to זכרון תרועה. From Numb. 10,5, we know that תרועה directed to the people from Moses, was a signal blown to order “break camp”. From v. 9 there, we are told that, directed to God, from the people, it was a signal for help, to be a cry for God’s active intervention in times of invasion, danger or distress. It was a note coming from human beings calling for intervening activity to alter the existing circumstances. The instrument to be used is to be חצוצרת, a man-made silver bugle. Further from Levit. 25,9, we know תרועה as a signal for the return of all men and possessions, out of strange and estranging attachments, back to the freedom and purpose originally destined for them by God. It is a call for deep reaching change in the existing social relations of men and possessions, to re-establish them in their original conditions as had been ordained by God. There it is God, the only real Owner of Men and possessions in Whose Name the תרועה proclaims the breaking away. Hence, not with חצוצרת, an artificial man-made instrument but with שופר, made by God, that there the תרועה-signal is given. Tradition teaches (Rosh Hashana 34b), that here too, the תרועה prescribed for the first of the seventh month in the jubilee Year (Levit. 25,9), has to be blown on a שופר, altogether that the תרועות of the seventh month are all in intimate connection with one another, שיהיו כל תרועות של חדש שביעי זה כזה. But that at once gives us the meaning of our תרועה here. Both, the תרועה של יובל and that של ראש השנה are בשופר, accordingly are in the name of God. For that which the תרועה של יובל means for the social material relation of men and possessions, the תרועה של ר״ה means for the spiritual relation of men to God. With the תרועה של ר״ה God enters our sphere of life as the one real Master and Director above us and our possessions, and calls us away from, and out of, any estrangement, wherever, and however, and by which, by non-observance, or transgression of His Will as revealed to us in His Torah, we may have yielded to any other than to Him. The yearly תרועה on ר״ה calls us to spiritual יובל just as that of the fiftieth year does to social יובל. Just like that, it calls us to God, and thereby to moral freedom and to the repossession of those spiritual treasures which were originally our very own and which we have parted from. Thereby it is at the same time a signal spiritually to strike camp, to leave and give up our old ways of which we have become fond but which are not approved of by God, as well as a “spiritual war” against everything which is an enemy to our moral well-being, in which fight God’s assistance and support is certain: ונזכרתם לפני ה׳ אלקיכם ונושעתם מאיביכם. But when God calls us to return to Him, to the repossession of moral purity and spiritual treasures, to forsake and give up everything which He dislikes, to fight against everything which is inimical to our moral well being, all this involves a judging of, and a judgment on, the life we have hitherto been living. Even if this conception is nothing other than the meaning of the תרועה which the Torah clearly gives us, in very truth יום תרועה is completely identical with יום הדין. But here, as we have already remarked, it does not say יום תרועה but זכרון תרועה. Inasmuch as here זכרון is placed between שבתון and מקרא קדש, it is, like these, something that we have to do. זכרון is the retrospection on one’s past life, and such retrospection is what the תרועה is to beget. It is to call us to alter that which is displeasing to God, to return to God, and to the regaining of our moral freedom of will which that brings about. This זכרון תרועה which is ordained makes the day to a קדש which invites us all up to the heights of its lofty significance.

In Numb. 10,7, two notes are specifically differentiated. There it says: ובהקהיל את הקהל תתקעו ולא תריעו by which תקוע is differentiated from תקיעה .הריע is accordingly a different note to תרועה and they have different meanings for the purpose of giving signals. תקיעה is the signal for gathering about Moses, תרועה the signal to strike camp. It nevertheless, in verses 5 & 6 the order for the signal to strike camp does not run: ,תרועה ירעו והרעותם תרועה, but: ותקעתם תרועה ,תרועה יתקעו, the breaking up signal is described as a combination of תרועה and תקיעה, the תרועה is to be introduced by a והרעותם תרועה) ,תקיעה), and concluded by one (תרועה יתקעו). Thereby the assembling signal is differentiated from the breaking up signal by תתקעו ולא תריעו that the תקיעה is blown without a following תרועה (see Rosh Hashana 34a). The word תקע means to bring something energetically into something else: to ram home, to thrust into, to sink, to plunge into. Hence also the term used for the symbolic binding by a handshake as a sign of assurance and emphasis on the transaction to be made. By it, the one party thrusts his hand to remain (symbolically) permanently in the hand of the other. Here, at a wind instrument it designates the sustained unbroken note produced by a prolonged blowing of air into the instrument (פשוטה). It is the calling note, calling your attention and holding you. The word תרועה from רוע ,רעע, to break, designates the broken note interrupted by shorter or longer quavers (שברים or תרועה). It is the note for bustling, speeded activity, the signal for breaking up. The combined notes of תקיעה and תרועה as a signal for decampment and moving on worked as follows:— the תקיעה called the people to attention to Moses. If no תרועה were to follow, they had to hurry to him to receive his orders. But the תרועה following immediately, informed them at once that it was a signal for striking tents and breaking up camp. And then the final תקיעה after packing up, called them forward thither to where God had indicated their new resting place. Quite in this way, with every תרועה consisting of the threefold note introduced by, and concluding with, a תקיעה does tradition (ibid.) teach the procedure for blowing the prescribed תרועה on the שופר on ר״ה and יובל. It points out (ibid. 33b) that these תקיעות accompanying the תרועה are expressed in the chapter giving the laws of יובל (XXV,9) by the term העברה it says:— תעבירו שופר בכל ארצכם ,והעברת שופר תרועה. Now העביר קול is the special idiom for publishing a demand to a large body of people where the summoning call does not stay with the hearers, but עובר, passes on and spreads from one to the other. In terms of symbolic signals this does not correspond to the short broken note but to the long drawn out, continuing note, the תקיעה. Now transferring it to the first of the seventh month, the preparatory תקיעה would be the summons in general to listen to God, to receive from Him the orders for the day. Then the תרועה would then give this order to be a breaking off and away from all things that are disliked by God, a tearing ourselves away from every attachment that estranges us from God, and from consciousness of having the power of moral freedom of will, and leaving everything worthless behind, in short in giving up everything in our present mode of life which is displeasing to God. The תקיעה which then follows calls one to the new standpoint, to the new attitude to life, to faithfully giving oneself up to following the road set out by God, which alone is the path of freedom, and which is blessed by the favour of God.
