But just as the first תקיעה is a call to the Master, the תרועה, a call to decision, and the final תקיעה, a call to follow God, so have our sages translated the thoughts awakened by these tones of the שופר into words in זכרונות ,מלכיות and שופרות (see in detail in חורב, Ch. XXXII).

The law that טור א״ח) ,לא בתקיעה תליא מלתא אלא בשמיעה 589), that the essential point of the מצוה is not in blowing the שופר but in hearing it, bears out fully our way of taking the תרועה of the שופר as being a summons, a word of command directed to us. As nevertheless the תוקע must also have the intention: להוציא השומע ידי חובתו, to blow the תקיעה in the name of, and as the agent of, the hearer, and hence must himself be a בר חיובא and ח׳ ש׳ וק׳ (a deaf-mute, mentally deranged or under-aged person I.L.) are not qualified to blow, we think the idea of the law must be taken to be:— The duty lies on everybody להשמיע לעצמו קול שופר, to make himself hear, understand, what the שופר says to him, accordingly himself to be תוקע for the purpose of לשמוע קול שופר, or to arrange for somebody else to blow the תקיעה for this שמיעה-purpose for him. In Rosh Hashana 28b, it is taught that both the תוקע and the שומע must have כונה, the blower as well as the hearer must have intent, which would exclude מתעסק or, according to other opinions, would require the purpose and intention of fulfilling the כונה לצאת :מצוה. This would touch on the general question as to what extent מצות צריכות כונה. If, even according to the accepted Halacha, מצות צריכות כונה, (א״ח 60,4), this is limited to כונה לצאת, to having the intention of doing a מצוה, but having fulfilled one’s duty is not necessarily dependent on being permeated with the spirit and meaning of the מצוה at the time of doing it, this would lie in the deep importance and significance of our מצות which extends far beyond the limited moment of their being performed. The performance of a מצוה embodies it concretely in our thinking consciousness and it makes an impression on our subconscious mind which never forgets. At an appropriate time our memory can fasten on some past מצוה procedure and its meaning and implications come to our mind and become a salvation in the hour of trial, or a consolation in times of trouble, or a warning in the hour of jubilation over some great piece of good fortune. The מצה and מרור which one had eaten on פסח without special thought, the סוכה in which one had sat on סכות without special thought, could, at the right time, when change or circumstances had brought the bread of misery with all its bitterness, the bread of poverty with all its lack of the protection of a secure home, or the first prize in the big lottery the most ostentatious opulence, prove their power of bringing reflection, encouragement, fortification and sober-mindedness. The תלמיד of whom the ברייתא (Menachoth 44a) speaks had possibly no thought in his mind at the time he attached the tzizis to his garment, or when he wore it, of the meaning of it. But in the excited moment of sexual temptation their admonishing and warning meaning suddenly struck him, and they became the saviour of his morality.

Concerning the beginning of the year with the first or the seventh month from which it gets the name ראש השנה, see on Ex. 12,2 (at end). In the list of the cycle of our Festivals ראש השנה, the beginning of the year of our earthly life, is the Day of Examination which calls us to find out how we stand with all phases of our earthly existence to the eternal Jewish mission which the 1st of Nissan brought us. It is the balance sheet between what we actually “are” and what we spiritually “should be”.

V. 25. כל מלאכת עבודה לא תעשו, in the previous verse it says: יהיה לכם שבתון זכרון תרועה, whereby our productive activity was ordered to halt so that in its place we can come to reflection and to rearrange our activities wherever they have been displeasing to God. But this call of God with all its innate solemnity, inviting us to self examination is nevertheless to be no call for dejection, it is a מקרא קדש, a call inviting us into the holy and sanctifying proximity to God. The return to God, to which we are bidden is the most elevating, the most rapturous thought, so that אוכל נפש in a raised festival degree belongs with the מקרא קדש of ראש השנה (see on Ex. 12,16), and the שבתון of the previous verse is here restricted only to מלאכת עבודה (cf. Nehemiah 8,2 & 9—11).

V. 26. See on the י״כ-laws in notes on Ch. 16,29—34. Here the introductory: דבר אל בני ישראל וגו׳, which we find at the other moed-laws, is missing. This is no completely fresh paragraph. י״כ belongs essentially to ר״ה which preparatorily introduces it.

V. 27. אך בעשור וגו׳, only on the tenth of this seventh month etc. כפרה, — that highest act of grace of the miraculous almighty power of God, the undoing of what is done, the removal of the natural course of cause and effect, the doing away completely of all the pernicious mental and physical effects of a sinful past on the future life of the sinner — to this full extent can not be obtained at every time nor isolated by itself בחדש השביעי הזה, only for one to whom תשרי is not the first, nor the only month, which leads him to the Feet of God, only for the one who reckons it the seventh, who, in the first went out of Egypt with his Forefathers, and with them, in the third received the Law of his life from the Hands of God, only one for whom the whole year is a Jewish year, can expect in the seventh month of such a year the highest grace that can be granted by God to a mortal being, כפרה. But not to know פסח, not to know שבועות, to count the years of life in an un-Jewish way, not to count תשרי from ניסן, and in תשרי to expect כפרה from God, from an un-Jewish past for an un-Jewish future, is blasphemous mockery of God, and self deceiving falsehood. But also in this seventh month it is only on the tenth of the month that it is יום הכפורים. The 1st of the month must have been זכרון תשובה ;תרועה must first have brought an alteration to one’s life, and then nine days must have been dedicated to this alteration to life leading back to God, so that on the tenth of the seventh month the Jew comes before God as a different man and in a different position towards God, if this tenth is to be a אין יום הכפורים מכפר אלא על השבין :יום הכפורים (Shebuoth 13a). This tenth of תשרי was the day on which an insight into God’s ways of loving management was revealed to Moses, and he brought the “new Tablets with the old Law” over to the People as a pledge of a regained future as gift of God’s Love and Grace, a future which it had forfeited by the sin of the golden calf. So that the day bears the historic stamp of the fact that God’s Grace can be regained even from the deepest depth of sin by recognising one’s sin, repenting and returning, that His miraculous Almightiness can eradicate the whole past with all its consequences. This day is the historic proof of כפרה (see Ex. 30,16).

יום הכפורים, it is the day which has already been designated as such in Ch. 16,29—34. And it does not call it יום כפרה, but כפורים, it brings כפרה for all the various and manifold sins and errors of life, whereas the כפרה-place in the Sanctuary is open the whole year primarily only for the spiritual recovery from serious sins committed through carelessness (חטאת) and slackness in active carrying out the precepts of the Torah (עולה).

מקרא קדש יהיה לכם ועניתם את נפשותיכם (see on Ch. 16,29). Whereas other מועדים, by virtue of their מקרא קדש character, count a higher standard of good living as being part of their festive nature, this מועד which is no less a מקרא קדש, yea, to those Jews who celebrate it in its true innermost nature of bringing the highest gift of God’s Grace, it is the most blissful, most sublime, most joyfully elevating of all the לא היו ימים טובים —:מועדים לישראל כחמשה עשר באב וכיום הכפורים. Israel had no more joyful festival than the fifteenth of אב and the Day of כפורים, as the days of regained unobstructed union with the community and with God, (Taanith 26,b & 30b) — this מועד demands, to characterise the קדש to which it leads, ענוי נפש the renunciation of all sensuous enjoyment. The fact to which we have just referred is a proof of how far away Jewish thought is from that heathenish point of view which sees in the ענוי נפש by which יום כפור is to be celebrated an appeasement of a wrathful God by the physical mortification of sinners. It is accordingly not correct to call יום כפור, “Versohnungstag”, Day of Propitiation” as the object of propitiation is always the one who hitherto has been angry, but כפרה is always directed to the sinner and the sin. It is, as we have repeatedly remarked, protecting the sinner from the consequences of the sin, a stemming of the results which otherwise would ensue from the sin on the internal and external well-being of the sinner. ענוי נפש and איסור מלאכה (v. 28) are acknowledgements in deeds, a twenty four hours ודוי of the fate we so deservedly should get, did not God’s miraculous Grace grant כפרה to our past. Without כפרה, which can be hoped for only from God’s Grace having absolute power, by our guilt we have forfeited the right to “exist” (צנוי נפש) or “to be productive” (איסור מלאכה). As “creature” and as “man” we have trifled away all our future. In its whole depth, and to the whole of its extent, we have to recognize and acknowledge this fact. In והקרבתם אשה לה׳ as well as in the prescribed קרבנות מוסף (Numb. 29,8—11), with the recognition and acknowledgement of the whole of our eternal calling and the vow to adhere more faithfully to it in the future, and to get near again to our God, we are to form happy hopes for the granting of a further future for the fulfilment of such a vow (see on Ch. 16,23).

V. 28. וכל מלאכה וגו׳, see on Ch. 16,29. Here in verses 28—30, the כפרה to be obtained on י״כ — introduced by תשובה on ר״ה and celebrated by עינוי and איסור מלאכה — is repeatedly attached exclusively to the tenth day of תשרי, and is limited to it. כפרה as יום הכפורים is to bring — the spiritual rebirth, and the physical and social rebirth associated with it — is nothing that could possibly be achieved by Man by itself out of psychic, physical or cosmic force. It is the most free-willed act of God’s free Grace, an act of His Power of Creation repeatedly exercised for repentant Man returning to Him, the granting and attainment of which is chosen and fixed for the tenth of תשרי. Fixed for all time just on the day which once was proof to us of God’s Grace in annulling our past and granting us a future by the rebirth of the People who had become bereft of their future by the sin of the Golden Calf. And it is עצם היום הזה, it is this day, this day that can never be lost to us, which quite independent of any other considerations for fixing it — especially independent of Temple or offering — which brings this Act of Grace, כפרה, to repentant, returning men, fasting and festive, and acknowledging their necessity for כפרה. As surely as that first tenth of תשרי allowed Israel to find its God and His expiatory Grace again out of the deepest debasement without Temple or offering, so certain is it that Israel can be sure of its Day of Expiation with its gift of expiation at all times, even if Temple and offerings have vanished, and no offerings are necessary “to be sacrificed in place of oneself” as people say. All that took place in the Temple and on the Altar on י״כ — and which will again take place in the future — the whole עבודת היום was only a symbolic expression of that which has actually to be done in actual reality outside the Temple and in the real inner self of every Jew, and עצם היום הזה, the tenth of תשרי remains יום כפורים for Israel: יום כפורים הוא לכפר עליכם לפני ה׳ אלקיכם.

V. 29 & 30. For transgressing the laws of ענוי the Torah states כרת, for transgressing the law of איסור מלאכה it says אבדון; ruin and death by the forces of nature and human society. כרת and אבדון are the retributions due for every intentional offence against God’s law of eating or His law against productive work. כרת, annihilation of existence for every intentional offence against the prohibition of enjoyment of the senses, אבדון ruin, for every intentional offence against the prohibition of work. ענוי נפש on י״כ is the acknowledgement that by our misdeeds in the enjoyments of life we have forfeited the right to a continuance of our life, just as איסור מלאכה is the acknowledgement that by wicked actions we have lost the right to “act”, for that is the right given to Man to have active power to rule over nature and the raw products of nature; ענוי נפש is the acknowledgement that one deserves כרת, and איסור מלאכה, the acknowledgement that one deserves אבדון. He who does not fast on י״כ denies that with his “eating”, and the life he gains thereby, he is responsible to God, he wishes to continue prolonging his existence without God; ונכרתה מעמיה is the answer. He who does a מלאכה on י״כ denies that with his “working” life and the position of power in Nature and Society he gains thereby, he is responsible to God, he wishes to continue his position of power without God: והאבדתי את הנפש ההיא מקרב עמה, is the answer he gets.
V. 31. The validity and importance of י״כ being entirely independent of time and place already indicated in the previous verse is expressly stated here.

V. 32. See Ch. 16,31: בתשעה לחדש בערב מערב עד ערב תשבתו שבתכם, there, in Ch. XVI, we have already remarked how the conception שבת designates cessation from activities in general, and so can comprise both eating and working. By כל מלאכה לא תעשו said of שבת בראשית it is limited to cessation of work. But the שבת-idea of י״כ includes also cessation from eating etc. Hence: שבת שבתון היא לכם ועניתם את נפשותיכם, it is not, like שבת בראשית, a שבת לה׳, a Sabbath expressing recognition of God, but a cessation of our activities, expressing our unworthiness, and hence include ענוי נפש also.

It would be self-understood that, as Jewish days are reckoned from eve to eve, the duration of a Jewish שבת or מועד is from eve to eve, and naturally the איסור מלאכה and ענוי start with ערב and end with ערב. If then here the time for the ענוי is specially definitely encompassed: בתשעה לחדש בערב מערב עד ערב, it can only have the purpose of limiting the fasting to that period. The fasting may only begin on the ninth when it is night, but on the ninth itself you may not fast. This prohibition to fast on the ninth, on ערב י״כ may to a very high degree prove the moral Jewish character of our fasting on י״כ and allow us to understand the words of our sages:— כל האוכל ושותה בתשיעי מעלה עליו הכתוב כאלו התענה תשיעי ועשירי (Yoma 81b). If our י״ב were the heathenish idea of pacifying a wrathful god, and our fasting a heathenish self-torturing castigation to satisfy its thirst for vengeance, how much greater would the מצזה be, by a two days fast! The law which makes eating and drinking on ערב י״כ into just a מצוה, and which forbids fasting on that day, comes to oppose sharply this immoral and un-Jewish way of looking at י״כ. Our eating on ערב י״כ is a suitable expression for giving our fasting on י״כ the true meaning of a כפרה promised on י״כ and only on אך בעשור) י״כ). But nevertheless as the text expresses this limitation in a positive manner and does not directly say בעשור לחדש, the indication is, at the same time, given that the fasting should begin on the ninth, i.e. at a time which still belongs to the ninth, but of course only in the evening. By this the duty is imposed to start the fast before nightfall (ibid.) מתחיל ומתענה מבעוד יום מכאן שמוסיפין מחול על הקדש, and according to one opinion which is accepted by many authorities this תוספות מחול על הקדש is not only with ענוי, altogether not only with י״כ but with every שבת ומועד always כל מקום שנאמר שבות מוסיפין מחול על הקדש :דאורייתא (ibid. cf. the הג״ה on א״ח לבוש 608, who also holds the opinion that תרתי שמעינן מיניה see Ex. 20,8 at end of notes).

V. 34. בחמשה עשר יום לחדש השביעי הזה, of just this month, the first day of which was a Day of תרועה, a day of shatteringly shaking us up out of ways of life displeasing to God, and whose tenth day made us appear before God, “poor” in every justification for further living and working, the fifteenth of just this month brings to us, as the fruit of the כפרה obtained on the tenth, the Festival of the building of our homes on earth in full trust in God, and the “taking” of the produce of the earth to gain the joy of living and working in happiness before God. Our past had made us lose the right to “living and doing”, י״כ had eradicated this past, סכות sets us up afresh in living and doing on earth to achieve the highest earthly possession: Joy and happiness before God.

חג הסכות, see on v. 42, שבעת ימים לה׳. One day for the תרועה mood, one day for the כפרה-fasting, but seven days, a whole cycle of days, for the joyful building of our huts, and for enjoying our possessions before God. This is what is most characteristic of the Jewish Law of Truth which teaches the normal mood of one’s life to be, not the bowed down broken feeling, but the erect happy joy of life which runs equally throughout the year of a life faithfully devoted to duty.

כשם שחל שם שמים על החגיגה כך חל שם שמים על :חג הסוכות שבעת ימים לה׳ הסוכה, (Sucka 9,a). Just as the personal offering with which every Jew, on each of the three national festivals, ranks himself as a member of the national circle which gathers about God and His Sanctuary of the Torah (חגיגה ,חג, see Ex. 5,1), bears the name of God, is holy and dedicated to God, and hence is אסור for any other use, so does the Name of God rest on the סוכה with which each Jewish member of this national circle places “his dwelling place on earth under the protection and direction of God”. This dwelling place is not called simply סוכה, a succah, any succah, but הסוכה (see on v. 42), the Succah that is built according to God’s Teaching, the construction of which teaches all the conditions on which the building of happy homes on earth depends. The סוכה is accordingly, like the חגיגה, an object of instruction, holy to God, and עצי סוכה אסורין כל שבעה and hence all those parts of its construction which belong to the presentation of the lessons it is meant to teach (according to the general opinion the סכך and דפנות, according to ר״ת only as much as the שיעור הכשר סוכה, see תוספות Succah 9a and ב״י on טור א״ח 638), are דאורייתא אסורים בהנאה, during the seven days of the Festival. To that is added the conception of the רבנן of בזוי מצוה, that the respect due to a מצוה excludes any object destined for a מצוה from being used for any other purpose, wherefore, e.g. נוי סוכה, objects which serve merely to decorate the סוכה are also אסורים בהנאה and also מוקצה, that every object which בין השמשות, i.e. at the entrance of a שבת or י״ט, by reason of its nature or purpose is out of use remains אסור for the duration of the שבת or י״ט. Hence סוכה and נוי סוכה are still אסור on שמיני עצרת because, when it came in, בין השמשות, when it is doubtful whether it is day or night, on account of the doubt they are still הוקצו למצותן and מגו דאתקצאי בין שמשות אתקצאי לכולי יומא (see תוספות Sabbath 22,a & ר״ן on Beitza 30b). [The סייג idea (see on Ex. 23,13) of מוקצה seems to be an extension of the דאורייתא idea of דאורייתא .[מלאכה, the rendering usable of something unusable is מדרבנן .אסור the prohibition extends to bringing into use, or handling, טלטול, something that is placed out of use. It is classified and differentiated into:— מוקצה מחמת חסרון כיס, things which on account of their value are placed out of use for any purpose other than their real one; מחמת מיאוס things which are not there to be used, on account of their repulsiveness; מחמת גופו, on account of their unfinished condition; מחמת איסור, things which at the entry of שבת or י״ט could only be used by transgressing the law; מחמת מצוה things which are destined to be used for מצוה purposes; כלי מלאכתו לאיסור, a tool for work which is prohibited to be done on שבת or בסים לדבר אסור ;י״ט something on which a מוקצה object is resting (— see א״ח 308—310). Nevertheless, all things which, like סוכה, are only means for fulfilling a תשמישי מצוה ,מצוה, and only on that account become holy, do not receive their holiness merely by being designated for that purpose, הזמנה לאו מלתא היא, only when it is first used for the מצוה does the object receive holiness. Thus our synagogues, too, do not become consecrated and holy by being dedicated, however elaborate the programme of the dedication ceremony may be. It is only the first communal prayer, תפלת צבור, the first קדיש, the first ברכו, and even if it is only ten unknown wanderers who had chanced to meet there, the first prayer makes it into a House of Prayer, consecrates it and confers on it the holiness of such. Thus, in Jewish Teaching in the sphere of duties, it is only the fulfilment of it, the deed, that counts, and all consequent ostentation and show is without real meaning. It is a different matter with קדושת הגוף, objective sanctity, where the holiness of the relation of the object to the divine is innate in it, where it is the expression or the bearer of it, e.g. ,תפלין קרבן ,ספר תורה. There הזמנה is מלתא, there the objects become holy as soon as they are designated for their holy purpose, even before the תפילין have been put on, or the ספר תורה read or the קרבן offered, more, even קלף המעובד לשם תפלין אסור לכתוב עליו דברי חול, (see א״ח 42,3 & 638,1).

V. 36. אשה לה׳ refers to the מוסף-offering ביום השמיני etc. prescribed in Numb. 29,13 et seq. As in v. 34 there are only seven days fixed for חג הסכות, clearly this eighth day does not belong to the סכות-Festival, but is an independent מועד on its own, רגל בפני עצמו (Succah 48a). Only לענין תשלומין for the purpose of making up for neglected חגיגה offerings is שמיני also reckoned as belonging to סוכות (Yoma 3a see on v. 41). Also by its offering שמיני is marked as being separated from the preceding days of סכות (see on Numb. 29,35). Hence we are given in Succah 48a the mnemonical formula ”פייס בפני עצמו״, ”זמן בפני עצמו״, ”רגל בפני —:פזר קשב עצמו״, ”קרבן בפני עצמו״, ”שיר בפני עצמו״ ”ברכה בפני עצמו״, (see Rashi and תוספות there). The denomination to this special מועד-Day runs:— עצרת היא. In Chagiga 9a עצרת is explained as עצור בעשיית מלאכה. But to take it that in עצרת we can only see the simple idea of a festive day, refraining from מלאכה, to take it that עצרת is applied to this day because just thereby and by no special מצוה the day is characterised, hardly suffices. For the seventh day of the מצות-Festival is also called עצרת (Deut. 16,8), and there, apart from the איסור מלאכה, the איסור חמץ is also still relevant. If we examine the places where the root עצר is used in תנ״ך, we find, in the far predominating number of cases, that it has the meaning of retaining, keeping back persons, things, or forces to guard against their becoming withdrawn or lost. And even in the few cases where it designates the negation of an activity it is more a denial of the continuation of activity already begun than of intended activity, so that, applied to איסור מלאכה it would confirm more to the first day of the festival than to the last. עצר is evidently related to עשר ,אסר ,אזר ,אצר and עזר all of which mean holding together and concentrating. The current phrase עצור ועזוב is striking where עצור is that which is held tight, valuable, in contrast to עזוב that which is let go, abandoned, worthless. We accordingly think we are not wrong if we take עצרת to designate a day which is not fixed to bring new lessons and new truths for us to accept and assimilate, but which has the mission to keep us still before the Presence of God — with this the idea of עצירה ממלאכה would certainly also apply — to strengthen and solidify the impressions and knowledge we have already gained, so that they remain with us permanently, and do not become lost in the hurly-burly of life. This would be entirely in accordance with the designation of the last day of a festival. Take פסח: for six days we have lived permeating ourselves with all the facts and teachings which the יציאת-מצרים-thoughts pledge and grant us, the Children of Israel. The seventh day is עצרת, it is a gathering up of all the spiritual “treasures” that we have collected during the days of the Festival before the Presence of God, so that we can, at the end of this seventh day, step over into the course of our ordinary life which then begins, truly enriched by them. The purpose of עצרת is accomplished by our realising once again all that we have gained by the festival, and by the firm resolution not to allow ourselves to be robbed in the turmoil and struggle and work of our lives of what we have won.

Therein lies the dual conception of עצר: persistance, remaining with God, and holding fast to all the spiritual acquisitions obtained, both really at bottom coming to the same thing. Now if עצרת were on the seventh day of סכות, it would only have the meaning of summing up and holding fast to the teachings which have been given to us by the Festival of סכות. But as עצרת here comes בשמיני as an independent festival on its own, and makes the mission of perservering and continuing and holding on before God, into a separate מועד-idea, and with it brings to a close, not only the cycle of Festivals of the seventh month, but the whole cycle of the festivals of the whole year, שמיני עצרת would then come to tell us, once again to summarise and gather to ourselves all the thoughts and messages and resolutions which the מועדים of the whole year have brought to us, and to resolve to persevere and hold fast to them before God. To impress them so deeply in our hearts that they become an unassailable part of ourselves which can not become lost in the course of the ordinary run of our yearly life on which we are now entering. That, in all the vicissitudes which may be awaiting us, richly endowed by the מועדים, we may “persevere and remain’’ with God. In this same way the ספרי on Numb. 29,35, takes עצרת to be the task of “Persevering and Remaining” being with God: אין עצירה אלא כניסה עצרו הכתוב מלצאת. There this is brought in connection with the general law that every offering that is brought טעון לינה, i.e. that nobody may bring an offering in the Sanctuary and then immediately leave Jerusalem, as if the object of bringing an offering is achieved merely by offering it. But everybody who has brought an offering over the threshold of the מקדש must tarry in its immediate neighbourhood — the town of Jerusalem — at least until the next morning so that he first gathers together the impressions of holiness he has received to take back with him on his return to the circle of his own home (see on Deut. 16,7). But the עצירה which otherwise only demands לינה staying over the night, is here formed into a complete מועד-institution, to an עצרת, a special festival “Day of Remaining”.

V. 37. אלה וגו׳ להקריב וגו׳. All the מועדים, inviting the Nation to come to God on the grounds of the various moments in their national history and also on the life of Nature, have the one common purpose:— to nourish and foster, ever afresh, their devotion to keeping alive on earth the fire of God’s Torah; as is expressed for the Nation as a whole in the אשה לה׳) ,מוספים, the והקרבתם אשה לה׳ said of each מועד), and by every individual in the עולה ומנחה) ,עולות ראיה), and in the ,שלמי חגיגה ושמחה (זבח ונסכים), (see Ex. 23,15). Here the מנחה, the allegiance offering subordinating and dedicating the means and goods of life to the Will of God is placed next to the עולה — the offering approaching God with the promise of the dedication of one’s actions — to teach, according to Menachoth 44b that תבא מנחה ואחר כך נסכים, that this paying homage to God with the means one has of existence and comfort must follow the dedication of one’s self in עולה as well as in זבחים before, in נסכים the expression of one’s joy of life in God, may come on God’s Altar. And נסכים are added to זבח — the offering seeking to come near to God with the enthusiasm of unclouded happiness — to teach that אין נסכים מתקדשין אלא בשחיטת הזבח, that only in the moment of the unselfish giving up the “ego” in שחיטה can this “ego” attain the joy in life which is worthy of being expressed before God, (see רש״י there in Menachoth). נסכים presuppose שחיטה and מנחה having occurred, and עולה and זבח precede both, the dedication and consecration of the נפש and איברים in the עולה, and of the נפש and חלב וכליות in שלמים. In Jewish Teaching, the consecration of one’s own self with one’s actions and one’s will and desires always comes first, and only when one can assume that, has the acknowledgement that one’s possessions and one’s happiness come from God any true worth or meaning. דבר יום ביומו: Of these offerings, those that come from the special nature of the day, these are the מוספים, belong to that day and the whole day is fixed for them, every minute of the day has the meaning of the day innate in it, כל היום כשר למוספין. But just for that reason: אם עבר היום ולא הביאן אינו חייב באחריותן, once the day has passed there is no compensation to be made subsequently, (Temura 14a). עבר יומו בטל קרבנו :דבר יום ביומו. That which the single day is for the מוספין, the whole duration of the festival is for מי שלא חג ביום טוב הראשון של חג חוגג את כל הרגל ויום .שלמי חגיגה ועולת ראיה טוב האחרון של חג עבר הרגל ולא חג אינו חייב באחריותו, על זה נאמר מעוות לא יוכל לתקון וחסרון לא יוכל להמנות, (Chagiga 9a). All the days of the duration of the festival, and, as already remarked on v. 36, in this respect even שמיני עצרת, are to be considered as תשלומין לראשון. The gravamen of each festival lies in the first day, so that: כיון דלא חזי בראשון לא חזי בשני, he who may not bring a קרבן on the first day has not to bring one on the second day (ibid.). For שבועות also, the period for תשלומין, for קרבנות חגיגה וראיה, is like, that of פסח, seven days, תשלומין שלה כל שבעה, (ibid. 17a).

V. 38. מלבד שבתות ה׳. If a מועד falls on a Sabbath due tribute has to be paid to it in the מוספי שבת besides the מספי רגל, and the רגלים are also the times which invite the discharging of all other vows and promises of voluntary offerings which may have been made previously. Every מועד is also an admonition to every individual to think back and settle any obligation towards the Sanctuary which he had undertaken of his own free will, which may have arisen out of his private life. The first רגל that meets him demands such settlement, and if he fails to make it he transgresses the command, והבאתם שמה ובאת שמה, (Deut. 12,5 & 6). If he allows ג׳ רגלים to pass and he has failed to take the threefold warning, he has transgressed the prohibition: לא תאחר לשלמו (Deut. 23,21). ת״ר חייבי הדמים והעדכין החרמין וההקדשות חטאות ואשמות צדקות ומעשרות בכור ומעשר (ופסח?) לקט שכחה ופאה כיון שעברו עליהם שלשה רגלים עובר בבל תאחר, (Rosh Hashana 4b). But regarding the צדקות which are here mentioned with the others, however, we are taught (ibid. 6a) that, if there are poor people there to receive the צדקה then מיחייב עליה לאלתר, the לא תאחר לשלמו is immediately transgressed (see תוספות 4a). But here נדרים ,מתנות and נדבות are mentioned as having to be paid on מתנות .רגל would be those obligations which occur by themselves as בכור and נדרים ;מעשר בהמה those which are undertaken with the formula הרי עלי and נדבות with the formula הרי זו (see Ch. 7,16). Nevertheless, although every מועד by its very nature is an admonition to discharge all our obligations towards God and the Sanctuary of His Torah, still on י״ט itself only עולות ושלמים הבאים מחמת י״ט, only those offerings which come from the special character of the day may be brought, עולות ראיה ושלמי חגיגה ושלמי שמחה תמידים ומוספים, but נדרים ונדבות, which only come to discharge some special obligation which has been incurred, אין קרבין ביום טוב may only be brought on חול המועד (on שבועות on the six following תשלומין-days (Beiza 19a, — regarding שלמי נדר ונדבה see Chagiga 7b, תוספות ד״ה עולות and Beitza 27b תוספות ד״ה ועל החלק).

V. 39. In verses 37 & 38 the conclusion of the year’s cycle of festivals with the end of סכות and עצרת has already been summarised by אלה מועדי ה׳. Now, very peculiarily the Festival of סכות is brought into prominence for special review and discussion. And although in v. 34, this Festival has already been specifically bounded within “this” seventh month, לחדש השביעי הזה, this delimitation to just the fifteenth of the seventh month, and altogether to the seventh month is expressed again and again in verses 39 & 41.

If our way of taking the meaning of עצרת is no erroneous one, namely, that this day is an invitation to gather together, and hold fast to, all the spiritual achievements of the whole cycle of festivals of the year, then it is quite understandable why first of all the festivals are brought to our attention in their common purpose of renewing and strengthening our relation to God’s Torah. This common factor of all the festivals is clearly expressed by the uniformity of all the special festival offerings and sharply impressed by the exactly similar admonitions to our duties and responsibilities which are part and parcel of all of them.

If further we consider the Festival of סכות according to its historical basis and its eternal meaning we could really form the opinion that this Festival could well be celebrated at any time, in any month of the year, especially in ניסן. The historic fact that God let us dwell in huts in the wilderness lasted continuously for forty years, so that it was not connected specially with any day or any month. Yea, if it was to be referred to יציאת מצרים one could have expected the command to dwell in huts to apply to פסח. Indeed the ת״כ on v. 34 finds that the injunction לחדש השביעי הזה is not superfluous as it comes to tell us that it is only in the Festival in the seventh month, but not also that of the first month, that dwelling in סכות is demanded. But the lesson which realisation of the experienced fact of the life lived in huts under the protection of God is to teach throughout the generations of Jewish life, viz. that we are to build our homes trusting entirely to the protection of God, and to gain the joy of life with the earthly goods that God grants, is one which is bound to no particular time, and is one which is to find its place and have its effects in every moment of the whole course of our lives. So that the Torah could very well find itself called on to repeatedly remind us that it is only on the fifteenth of this seventh month that the Festival of סכות has to start.

Accordingly, after in verses 34—38 the Festival of סכות has already been introduced in connection with the rest of the festivals of the year, v. 39, takes up again that which had been said in verses 34 & 35, and completes the special meaning of the seventh month for סכות by the additional provision: באספכם את תבואת הארץ. By עבור שנה (see above v. 2), it is to be arranged that the seventh month falls in the harvest time. And just at the time when the nation sees itself in the greatest contrast to its condition in the wilderness is it to revive the memory of that life in the wilderness throughout its generations, so that the realisation of the conviction which a forty years experience in the wilderness had forged into a certainty for the whole nation who did experience it should be the foundation for life under quite opposite conditions.

During the time of harvesting all that the years work on the land had produced “to bring home”, which is the time which should chain everybody to his home and fields, leave your home and field, pilgrim up to the spiritual centre of your united nation and “תחגו את חג ה׳״ rank yourself in to the “circle forming itself about God” for seven days. This conception of “חגוג את חג ה׳״, of “forming a circle round about God” finds its special expression in the חגיגה-offering. This offering, in itself, is nothing other than a שלמים-offering, with which a Jew, feeling that he has received a happy satisfied life from God, strips himself of his ego, his existence, his strivings, דם ואימורים, all his living for himself and striving for himself, and gives them up to the Altar of his God, for the fulfilment of His Will, and thereby receives it all back, with himself and his household elevated to priestlike sanctity and into the holy proximity of his God. But as on the רגל every Jew at the same time comes to the Torah Sanctuary of the nation and gives up his דם ואימורים to the Altar and the Fire of the Torah, and after such sacrifice receives his offerings back to be enjoyed in his homely circle within the environments of the Sanctuary — משלחן גבוה קא זכו — every Jew thereby ranks himself — completely forgetting all his own personal selfishness and just by that in a higher, purified and dedicated consciousness of himself and his worth — as a member of the national circle which is gathering round about God and the Sanctuary of His Torah. Then, in the חגיגות which are brought one after the other on a רגל, this חג ה׳, this festive circle forming itself round about God is concretely demonstrated. So that חגיגה is also looked upon as a קרבן צבור (Pesachim 70b & Yoma 15a). משום דאתי בכינופיא, because it is brought in the assembled masses of the people. But at no רגל does this conception, this idea of giving up living separately to join oneself to the Nation assembled around God, appear more significant, more pregnant with meaning, than at the חג האסיף, at the חג when באספכם את תבואת הארץ, where this giving up living by oneself and joining in with the Nation formed by God, is to be practised just as the time which invites one most to stay at home and which really grants the basis for living at home by oneself. So that although the Festivals of פסח and שבועות are also called: חג השבועות ,חג המצות, it is only חג הסכות which we find called חג ה׳ in the Torah, and our sages call the Festival of סכות simply החג it is just the חג par excellence. Already in Kings I 8,2 & 65 it occurs under this designation.

And as just being חג האסיף, the seventh month was fixed for the חג ה׳, so is all the bliss and happiness that the Festival is to bring, the building of our “huts” full of trust and confidence, and taking our possessions in our hands full of joy before God, only to be attained on the fifteenth of the seventh month. Only as the blossom and fruit of the tree of life planted on ר״ה and י״כ with תשובה ,תרועה and כפרה are the joyful gifts of סכות to be plucked in the Presence of God (cf. v. 27).

בחמשה עשר יום תחגו את חג ה׳ שבעת ימים: the wording is peculiar, on the fifteenth you are to celebrate the Festival seven days! Similarly v. 41 runs: וחגתם אותו חג לה׳ שבעת ימים, where the אותו clearly refers to the יום הראשון of the preceding verse, and then it would say: you are to celebrate this first day seven days! The Gemora in Chagiga 9a, takes the teaching of the law of תשלומין (see v. 36) from that too. The gravamen of the duty of חגיגה lies, as already remarked above, in the first day. It is primarily on it, accordingly, that the חג character should be expressed by the bringing of the חגיגה. Seven days should then remain dedicated to the permeation of the חג-spirit which the first day brought, so that if the חגיגה had not been brought on the first day, this duty can be retrieved during these seven days, they are תשלומין, and in truth all תשלומין לראשון. Hence “the first day is celebrated for seven days” and even the eighth day is, in this respect, united to the first, and therefore the end of the verse repeats בחדש השביעי תחגו אותו, i.e. the חגיגה-idea of the first day stretches itself over the whole of the festive period of the seventh month. Then Pesachim 70a teaches further that although the חגיגה could be regarded as a קרבן צבור, it is nevertheless, not like the other festival מוסף-offerings דוחה שבת. The reason is given for this in Yoma 50a as being because, having the תשלומין-days it can not be considered as an offering שזמנו קבוע as being limited to one special day and נקוט האי כללא בידך כל שזמנו קבוע דוחה השבת ואת הטומאה אפילו ביחיד וכל שאין זמנו קבוע אינו דוחה לא את השבת ולא את הטומאה ואפילו בצבור The only thing that counts for דחיית שבת וטומאה is being fixed for the one particular day (see on Numb. 9,2 et seq.). And Pesachim (ibid.) finds the fact that חגיגה is not דוחה שבת also laid down in the words of the text: וחגתם אותו חג לה׳ שבעת ימים בשטה. For as the eighth day is added to the first regarding the duty of חגיגה it should say: וחגתם אותו שמנת ימים. But just because שבת always falls out of the days for bringing the חגיגה there can never be more than seven days for bringing it. Then our verse could be taken to have a similar meaning; on the fifteenth day you are to celebrate the חג ה׳ seven days, i.e. you are to bring the חגיגה on the first but when necessary it is to be brought on one of the other seven days in place of the first day. And equally so when in summing up, referring back to v. 36 it says: ביום הראשון שבתון וביום השמיני שבתון, so that clearly the Festival extends over eight days, and if nevertheless it says only תחגו שבעת ימים, the fact that a שבת falls out in every case is assumed.

V. 40. ולקחתם לכם ביום הראשון: the tenth of תשרי with its demand: ועניתם את נפשותיכם found us “עניים״, poor, found us the poorest, found us with the confession of having forfeited the right to the food necessary for our existence and for the continuance of our existence. The recognition and acknowledgement of this before God brought us כפרה, had “covered over” all that which out of our past had rendered us without a future, and had appointed us to a new existence, to a renewed continuance of our existence as a member of the immortal nation about God. To the consciousness of this renewed right to such an existence, the exact opposite of the כרת ואבדון מקרב עמו, seven days are dedicated. On the first of these seven days the same God Who on the preceding tenth of the month had called to us: ועניתם את נפשתיכם! says to us: “ולקחתם לכם״, “take to yourselves”. Thereby He tells us that He has again given us the right, yea the duty, to stretch forth our hands and grasp the good things of His earth, to obtain thereby, in contrast to the lot of עינוי, the most precious treasure of earthly existence, yea as far as our knowledge goes, of all existence, “happiness before the Presence of God”: ולקחתם לכם ושמחתם לפני ה׳ אלקיכם!

פרי עץ הדר. According to all the places where it occurs in תנ״ן, the word הדר is quite definitely a noun and not an adjective. In one single instance in Ps. 149,9: הדר הוא לכל חסידיו it seems to be adjectival but there too it is clearly a noun (see Hirsch’s commentary on Psalms. I.L.). הדר is, in every instance, an outward appearance, striking the eye, distinguishing the object, hence also ornament, finery, splendour. It is phonetically related to: חדר ,עדר ,אדר, which all designate confining, with the underlying idea of isolating from others. עץ הדר is accordingly a tree whose external appearance and special characteristics make it stand out above others, an exceptionally beautiful tree. Tradition has it that it is the אתרוג, a certain kind of citrus tree. רמב״ן in his commentary reminds us that רגיג is the Chaldean equivalent of חמד which is a synonym of הדר, so that אתרוג would designate an עץ נחמד or פרי נחמד which would come very near to the Hebrew description פרי עץ הדר. In Succah 35a the הדר of the אתרוג-tree is characterised by three special characteristics which make it stand out: ת״ר פרי עץ הדר עץ שטעם עצו ופריו שוה הוי אומר זה אתרוג, the הדר of the אתרוג-tree shows itself in “the tree and its fruit having the same taste”, i.e. that the ethereal material which gives the aroma to the fruit exists already in the wood and leaves of the tree, and give them the taste of the fruit. This speciality is expressed by the designation פרי עץ הדר. To the best of ouur knowledge it is not usual in any case, and least of all in a precept concerning a מצוה, to name a fruit in a devious way as the fruit of a certain tree instead of naming it directly, instead of saying an apple, a nut, to call it the fruit of an apple tree, of a nut tree, etc. If nevertheless this circuitous method is chosen here, the characteristic of the fruit which comes into consideration here must lie in the tree, the fruit must represent the tree, from the tree one must be able to recognise the fruit and from the fruit the tree, in short: טעם עצו ופריו must be שוה. Then thereby the tree is actually characterised as an עץ הדר. It is so permeated with the fine etherial substance that this is developed not only in the fruit but already flavours the wood and leaf. We think that, in parenthesis, we may remark that the עץ הדעת, that tree endowed with all the allures of Paradise is characterised in a similar way.

For in Gen. 3,6 it says: ותרא האשה כי טוב העץ למאכל וכי תאוה הוא לעינים ונחמד העץ להשכיל ותקח מפריו ותאכל. Here too the lure of the fruit is described as existing already in the tree, and very probably the ותרא האשה, “the woman perceived” כי טוב העץ למאכל, tells us that she nibbled at those parts of the tree which were not forbidden, the wood, the leaves etc. and that it was just their wonderful flavour which tempted her to taste the forbidden fruit: “If the wood already tastes so wonderfully, what must the fruit be like!”. This deduction, which seems so probable, and the סייג-warning which lies therein, viz. ourselves to forbid what is allowed when it can easily lead to what is not allowed, is of no little significance for the lesson of rightly using our moral freedom of will which was to be taught by this עץ הדעת טוב ורע (see on Gen. 3,6 et seq.).

A second speciality which forms the distinguishing הדר of the אתרוג-tree is that עד שבאין קטנים עדיין גדולים קיימין, that the tree is never without fruit The fruit remains on the tree for two or three years until it is completely ripe, so that the old fruit of the previous year is still on the tree when the new little ones of this year come. Mnemonically this characteristic is kept by association with the word הדר it is like a דיר a sheepfold which also contains old and young at the same time, or by דר the fruit is דר באילנו משנה לשנה, it remains on the tree from year to year, so that in truth it is to the eye and for the mind a עץ הדר it stands in the glory of its fruit at all times.

The third speciality of the אתרוג-tree, (which the Gemora there also mnemonically connects with the word הידור by the Greek: hudor) is that, although it is a tree, it can be kept fresh and flourishing, and grown, like a vegetable, by artificial watering only, שגדל על מים (see Kiddushin 3a) so that its הדר, the beauty of its growth is quite independent of the changes of drought or exceptionally dry seasons of the year.

L. Reichenbach, Professor of Botany and National Sciences in Dresden, in his Flora germanica excursoria, dealing with the development of the plant world and its various classes and families, comes to the conclusion, that — inopposition to Decandolle and Stephan Endlisher, who find the highest degree of vegetable organism in the family of leguminous plants and especially in the mimosas, — he can claim this for the family of Hesperides, especially for the group of Aurantiacex (citron and orange trees) “These trees”, he says on p. 840 of his Flora germanica, “seem to me really to be the pinnacle of the highest development of the whole vegetable kingdom” and he gives sixteen reasons to subtantiate his claim of which we quote six: (1) “no other plants contain such a quantity of delicious ethereal oils in cells specially made for them already in the seed-lobs and earliest shoots, in all branches, peticles, leaves, bosses, petals, stamens and even in the fruit itself”; (5) “the stems last longer than any other known kind of wood etc., etc.,”; (6) “the leaves are lasting and evergreen”; (7) “these trees blossom, one can almost say, throughout the whole year”; and (8) “fruit of various years can be seen on them year in year out”; and (11) “they can be grown with remarkable ease almost everywhere. It seems to us most interesting to find these remarks of a modern botanist of the highest standing almost literally agreeing with the sentences in the Gemora Succah about the family to which our אתרוג undoubtedly belongs. If the signs which our sages give for the הדר-character of the אתרוג are to be found on the whole of the family of citrus trees, it seems probable that these signs are most prominent and exist to a fuller degree just in the species of the אתרוג trees. Thus the כפות תמרים on סוכה remarks that the speciality טעם עצו ופריו שוה exists to a certain extent in lemon trees and orange trees, but not to the full extent which it does in אתרוג trees, as in the abundant juice of oranges and lemons there is a certain acidity which is not noticeable in the taste of the other parts of the tree so that they are not completely טעם עצו ופריו שוה.

תמר .כפת תמרים is the date palm. We have translated כפת תמדים as branches of palm trees. But this is not really accurate. Palms do not actually have branches and twigs, but only leaves which grow out directly from the stem. לולב, as we call our כפת תמרים, is neither branch nor twig but always only leaf or a part of the tree similar to a leaf, thus we find עלי גפנים ולולבי גפנים, leaves of the vine and tendrils or shoots of the vine. Our לולב is in reality only a leaf of a palm. It is a closed pinnated leaf (pinnated or feathered, because the spread of the leaves stand on either side of the central rib like the tufts of a feather). That which we call שדרה is the central rib of the leaf and what we call עלים, leaves, are only parts of the leaf, the spread of the leaf, the pinnated parts of the one large leaf. The top leaf to which the שדרה extends (which some people take to be that which is called תיומא) is only the extreme top edge of the whole leaf. Each of the pinnated parts of the לולב and also the top pointed leaf is folded closely together.

The explanation of the word כפת is not quite sure. The difficulty lies in the meaning of the root כפף. This definitely means to bend, to bow We think that just as כף means the hollow part of the hand formed by bending the hand together on both sides, so is each part of the leaf of the לולב folded inwards called כף (cf. אוכלין על של בין הכיפין, Pessachim 25b & Rashi thereon). It would then only be difficult that while כפף does mean bending together we do not find it used for such a close folding together as the leaves of the לולב form. But if our assumption is correct the term כפת to describe this particular palm leaf is most apt. It is a pinnated leaf consisting of many leaf-like parts and yet is one single unit, a leaf on its own. It appears as a plurality and is a single thing. This would completely agree with the way the ריטב״א takes the deduction the Gemora makes in Succah 32a. There it says:— ואימא תרתי כפי דתמרי כפת כתיב ואימא חדא (the Yalkut has the rendering חדא כפתא), לההוא כף קרי ליה; On which —:ריטב״א ואימא תרתי כפי דתמרי פי׳ שאינו יוצא אלא בשני לולבין ומהדרינן כפת כתיב ואימא חדא כלומר עלה אחת ההיא כף קרו ליה. By the way the plural is written without a כפת ,ו instead of כפות the supposition that it might mean that two לולבים were to be taken is countered, and the plural form shows that it is not one single leaf that is to be taken. A single leaf would be called כף. So that כפת means, one single unit which consists of many כפות that is why it is written חסר, and כפת תמרים is the completely pertinent expression for the pinnated and closely folded-up leaf of the date palm. If כף means the closed leaf one could perhaps translate חסר) כפת) the folded or closed leaf.

וענף עץ עבות, according to tradition עץ עבות is the myrtle, הדס, and according to Succah 32b the circumlocutory עץ עבות gives the description of a certain kind of myrtle. For עבות is a plaited cord. A plait consists of at least three threads or strings. Every link of the plait is made by the three parts of the plait starting at a common point, then separating in three different directions, and then by crossing over, meet again at a second point. The kind of myrtle mentioned here corresponds in the formation of its leaves to such a three-stranded chain: קלוע כמין קליע ודומה לשלשלת, “it is plaited like a plait and looks like a chain”. This is accomplished by the position of its leaves which קיימי תלתא תלתא טרפי בקינא, which have three leaves at every point of branching from the stem (lit. go out from one nest). A second sign is, that שענפיו חופין את עצו, that, by the position and upward direction of the leaves, the wood is covered. The leaves stand almost vertically and the points of foliation are so close to one another that one only sees leaves and the wood of the stem is hidden from sight. The term used: ענפיו חופין את עצו is difficult, one would have expected: עליו חופין את עצו and equally difficult is the reference to this command in the words of the text: ענף עץ עבות. We think it might be that other plants which do not have such foliation show to the eye of the observer more of the naked wood. But here where the wood of the twigs is quite covered by the leaves, the twigs appearing to be all leaves also cover the wood of the tree. The tree or bush appears as a tree of chain-like leaves, as a tree which bears not twigs but such leaves, and the text can add עבות, which is really the characteristic of the ענף, to the tree itself and say: ענף עץ עבות. Perhaps this is also the meaning of the explanation of Rashi which otherwise is difficult to understand: שכולו ענף שהעץ מחופה בעלין ע״י שהן עשויין כקליפה ושוכבין על אפיהן, “it is called this because the wood of the twigs being completely covered by the chain-like leaves the whole tree looks like a twig”, i.e. as itself bearing leaves, וצ״ע.

וערבי נחל, “willows of the brook”, and Succah 33b teaches that this term only designates the species of willow, namely the kind that usually grow at the side of streams, but that they need not actually be grown there.

So that it is of these four kinds of plants that the command is given: ולקחתם לכם וגו׳, that on the first day of סכות we are to “take” them, moreover ולקחתם that שתהא לקיחה ביד כל אחד ואחד, not merely by a representative of the Nation as a whole, but, as is usually the case when the command is worded in the plural, the Nation in the plurality of each individual member. Each one shall take them, and לכם which is added, משלכם להוציא את השאול ואת הגזול, completely your own, not borrowed and far less robbed or stolen which would already be rejectable as מצרה הבאה בעברה, as a duty accomplished by committing a crime. ולא בלילה :ביום, the command is limited to daytime, night is excluded. This places the מצות לולב in the long list of those commands which are restricted to daylight, to counter the erroneous idea that they refer to some Nature Festival or nature cult, the honouring of that power whose kingdom belongs more exclusively to the night than to the daytime in which the powers of Nature at least share their automatic mastery with that of the work of free-willed Man. But restricting the taking of these products of nature to clear daylight places them in the sphere of the work of free-willed Man, and it is there that its meaning must be sought (Succah 43a & 30a). In Menachoth 27a and Succah 34b we are taught that the four kinds of plants of the מצות-לולב are all essential: מעכבין זה את זה, so that if any one of them is missing the מצוה can not be fulfilled. But the four מינים still do not form one conception to such an extent that they necessarily need be all taken together, but, according to the opinion of the בה״ג the מצוה can be fulfilled if all four lie before one and are taken up one after the other (תוספות ibid.). Nevertheless everybody agrees that — in accordance with the concept: זה אלי ואנוהו התנאה לפניו במצות, that every מצוה must be done in the most appealing manner possible and the one which is most in accordance with its meaning — it is a מצוה to bind the myrtles and willow twigs into the לולב, and to take the לולב thus bound in the right hand and the אתרוג in the left hand at the same time (Succah 11b & 37b). The idea of completeness, תם, demands also that none of the four plants may be חסר, may not be mutilated, damaged (ibid. 29b, תוספות ד״ה בעינן). This demand that שתהא לקיחה תמה is taken from the expression: ולקחתם, in which is indicated incidentally ולקח תם just as the Gemora in Berachoth 15b learns from ולמדתם, that עבודה תמה :ועבדתם ;שיהא למודך תם, (Yoma 24a); and similarly in Sabbath 103b, וכתבתם: that your כתיבה must be תמה; and Menachoth 35b: וקשרתם, that your קשירה must be ,תמה (עי׳ לבוש ל״ג שהיה לו גירסה אחרת). Perhaps it is not so far fetched to say that a מצוה which has to be performed by all the members of a community at a similar time the לקיחה of which, the למוד of which has to be done by אתם, or the עבודה of which, the whole priesthood have to accomplish, (as the construction of the word אתם implies), where the fulfilment of the command requires certain objects as the means of its performance and these requirements are those of the whole community, it can be expected that the community make provision that these objects are there in sufficient quantity and of such suitable quality that each individual can fulfil the מצוה completely and perfectly; so that by the manner in which the individual carries out the מצוה it can be said of the community as a whole ולקח (א) תם! And inasmuch as the מצוה demands knowledge, understanding and actual practice, and this is a general requirement for the public, it can be expected of the community that due provision be made for the attainment of it, and by the correctness and precision with which the individuals carry out the מצוה it can be seen that the provision of the means to acquire such knowledge and practice is a national concern, so that to the community as a whole it can be said: ולמד (א) תם. Or, when the מצוה consists of several successive procedures, that when the whole is concluded it is to be complete and perfect in every way, and just in this completeness the whole is sharply defined and made clear, so that to the community it can be said ועבד (א) תם. Equally so, when in duties addressed to the individual, they do not separate the object from the person and procedure, not וכתבת אותם ,וקשרת אותם, but closely unite the object to the acting person in one mental picture: ,וכתבתם וקשרתם, then in such a fulfilment of the מצוה it can be expected that in the object achieved, the whole devotion of the person will be sharply defined, the object will prove this devotion of the person: קשירה תמה ,כתיבה תמה is expected. Finally the concept הדר is demanded for the quality of all the four מינים, they are all to be beautiful in their kind, and for this reason, e.g. לולב היבש פסול (ibid. 29b). For this application of the sign of הדר to all the four plants of the לולב-command see below.

We have already remarked that the palm leaf is bound together with the myrtle and willow twigs, but the אתרוג remains unbound. The form of the text also corresponds to this, ענף עץ עבות and ערבי נחל and both joined to כפת תמרים by the conjunctive ו but כפת תמרים is not joined to the preceding פרי עץ הדר, it does not say וכפת (Succah 34b), but: כפת. When we enquire about the meaning of these four kinds of plants on the Festival of סכות, modern thoughtlessness replies that they are just a harvest bouquet, a sign of the blessing that has been granted to our harvest, and so, for our climate and agricultural conditions should be replaced by other plants and fruit more suitable to the lands in which we live. But this superficiality overlooks one small fact. We know the products by which the land of Israel was to recognize the blessing of its harvest. These were, wheat and barley, vine and figs, pomegranates, olives and dates (Deut. 8,8). Amongst these, at most כפת תמרים could be reckoned, but אתרוגים myrtle and willows are not to be found. And anyway has there ever been anywhere a land which would see the blessing of its harvest in the granting of a crop of myrtles and willows?!

Pray let us for once allow the Torah itself to speak to us, and in the way it tells us that the מצוה is to be carried out, perhaps there, plants will speak for themselves. The Torah puts the אתרוג into our hands and then to it places the palm leaf, the myrtle and the willow twigs, and demands that with all these together, or also, as we have seen: לולב אינו צריך אגד with each separate one of these, we are to rejoice before the Presence of God. We are to rejoice, find joy, with the פרי עץ הדר, likewise with the כפת תמרים, with the ענף עץ עבות and ערבי נחל. Let us consider these four species in their belonging together and in their separate characteristics. Then we think that what we first notice is that which the אתרוג as פרי עץ הדר by itself represents is a combination of the characteristics which are divided amongst the three parts of the לולב group. The date palm gives fruit but the כפת תמרים, the part of it that we hold in our hand shows that it is no עץ הדר, that the עצו ופריו is not שוה, that the fruit has its beginning only in the fruit, and the tree itself — which as no other tree does, strives upwards with all its fibres to the fruit at the top (it is the only monocotyledonous fruit tree) — exhibits none of the fragrant material that it works up deep in its interior and leads upwards. So כפת תמרים represents פרי without הדר. The myrtle, ענף עץ עבות immediately represents to us הדר without פדי; indeed it is הדר in the highest degree, not only in the beauty of its leaf formation which shapes all its twigs into a leafy chain, but it is also עץ הדר, its ethereal fragrant material penetrates every part of it to such a degree that the Gemora in Succah 32b takes it to be also characterised as עץ שטעם עצו ופריו שוה, though ריטב״א thinks that this sentence must be amended because in the text it does not speak of פרי in connection with the myrtle. In any case the berries of the myrtle can not be called “fruit” in the ordinary sense of the word. ערבי נחל: the willow, is simply עץ without הדר and without פרי.

Here clearly עץ and הדר and פרי, and then פרי עץ הדר are definitely progressive stages in vegetable development. The willow is simple wood, the myrtle has developed fragrance as well, the date palm developes this fragrant material to the formation of fruit, and the אתרוג combines all three stages in the highest degree of perfection. The אתרוג in my left hand is a commentary on the לולב bunch in my right; and as the מצרה thus commands us to take in our hand the products of God’s creation in Nature in the diversity of their various degrees of development, it expresses the character of תם and הדר on all of them; each one in its own way perfect, each in its own way beautiful. The modest willow, the beautiful myrtle, the proud lofty palm and the sumptuous אתרוג fruit, each in its stage of development and for that stage תם והדר, in its stage, and for its stage, to an equal degree and created with equal love and with equal wisdom, and with equal care of creation, made “perfect” and “beautiful”, and to each of them Man is called on, with equal conscientiousness “ולקחתם״. But לכם, he may, he is to, take all that Nature offers into his possession, let it become part of his personality, use it all to build up his personality and his work, but also לכם in a way that has the approval of God, so that it is really “his” in God’s Eyes, so that, without necessity to blush, he can stand with it in the Presence of God, in the consciousness of an independent living granted by God. Accordingly not בא בעברה, not “his” through sinful acts, not גזול and not ושמחתם לפני ה׳ אלקיכם —.שאול! With all of them, and with each of them, rejoice, find joy in the Presence of God. Does not the מצוה represent, do not these מעוה-plants represent — though primarily they only represent the whole plant world matured in the course of the year — all the gifts that God’s management has procured for us? Whatever these gifts may be, and whatever position in life they have alloted to us, does not this מצות-לולב preach to us:— Whether “willow-like” without intrinsic beauty, without its own fruit, without resisting strength, we are only able to prove our worth as “baskets” (Bikurim 3,8), for carrying and keeping — whether “myrtle-like”, we shine forth in our own beauty, — whether, like the date-palm, quietly and without glory, with hard, straight, strong unyielding work we produce that which is most useful and helpful, — whether we sparkle like the “splendid fruit of the splendid tree”, any and every sphere of life can be תם and הדר, can in its own way achieve perfection and beauty and if only lived in all that is implied by ולקחתם לכם (see above) can give us that most precious posession in life, “joy, happiness in the Presence of God?”

At least this is the way in which our sages have taken this מצוה and its ארבעה מינים to have a general application. True enough, they see them concretely as representing the vegetable kingdom as a whole, and connect the fulfilment of this מצוה with the rain which we have to ask from God, for the new plant year, the granting of which just this מצוה is to make us worth of: ולקחתם לכם וגו׳, כדי לזכות אתסם להוריד לכם מטר. But at the same time they see in them the phenomenon of the various different ways in which the One God reveals Himself; also the different life-pictures which the lives of the patriarchs and the matriarchs, all equally important, exhibit; and also the different spiritual and moral gifts of the people who form the one nation of God. To our sages פרי עץ הדר signifies the revelation of God in all His Glory, כפת תמרים ;הוד והדר לבשת, the revelation of God in the just and righteous ones striving upwards, straight and strong like the palm tree, ענף עץ עבות ;צדיק כתמר יפרה, the revelation of God’s Ruling which shows itself wherever “myrtles flourish in the midst of whirlpools”: ערבי נהל ;והוא עומד בין ההדסים אשר במצולה, that revelation of God’s Ruling which shows itself in “striding through the bleak flowerless wilderness”, סלו לרוכב בערבות. Or, to them the lovely אתרוג is the picture of the life of Abraham and Sara, the solemn palm-branch that of Isaac and Rebcca, the myrtle, rich in leaves, that of Jacob and Leah rich in children, the quickly withering willow twig that of Rachel, who had to die so young, and Joseph. Or they make the four different kinds of plants show us the Jewish Nation and say: פרי עץ הדר אלו ישראל, just as the אתרוג-tree has אוכל וריח, the top of the tree bears fruit and the ethereal fragrance of its smell permeats the whole tree in all of its parts, so in the Jewish Nation are to be found men: שהם בעלי תורה ובעלי מעשים טובים, whose minds are matured in knowledge and wisdom and understanding of the Torah, and at the same time their מעשים טובים show how their whole active life is permeated with the spirit of their knowledge; but כפת תמרים also אלו ישראל, also, like the date palm, rich in fruit but poor in fragrance, men are to be found in the Nation who are indeed אוכל but not ריח, who have a store of wisdom and knowledge in their heads, but whose practical life does not show this wisdom in מעשים טובים, they are בעלי תורה ואין בהם מעשים; but again: ענף עץ עבות אלו ישראל, like the myrtle poor in fruit, but rich in fragrance, men are to be found in Israel who have ריח but not אוכל whose whole practical life is penetrated by the spirit of the תורה but whose minds have not attained the mental fruit of learning and knowledge: שיש בידיהם מעשים טובים ואין בהם תורה; but also: ערבי נחל אלו ישראל, like the willow, with neither fruit nor fragrance, there are men in Israel: שאינן לא בעלי תורה ולא בעלי מעשים, who have neither theoretical knowledge of תורה nor in their practical lives carry out its dictates. אמר הקב״ה לאבדן אי אפשר אלא יעשו כולן אגודה אחת והן מכפרייִ אלו על אלו, none may be lost on account of their failing, but God teaches the joining them together in one combined union so that the failings of the one are balanced by the perfection of the other (Yalkut). Similarly the Gemora in Menachoth 27a: ארבעה מינין שבלולב שנים מהן עושין פירות ושנים מהן אין עושין פירות העושין פירות יהיו זקוקין לשאין עושין פירות ושאין עושין פירות יהיו זקוקין לעושין פירות ואין אדם יוצא ידי חובתו בהן עד שיהיו כולן באגודה אחת כן ישראל בהרצאה עד שיהיו כולן באגודה אחת שנאמר: הבונה בשמים מעלתיו ואגודתו על ארץ יסדה (Amos 9,6), “Two of the לולב plants bear fruit, two are unfruitful, the fruit bearers are to bind themselves to the unfruitful ones, the unfruitful ones to the fruitful ones and the command is only fulfilled if they are all together in one combination, so Israel can only aspire to God’s good will when they all join in one union. Thus we find in Amos: “in heaven He buildeth His grades but on earth He hath founded His union”. Although the last two ways of taking it have the opinion which is not accepted, that לולב צריך אגד, all these quotations agree that they see in the מצות-לולב the expression of the revelation of the “oneness” of God in the multiformity of the world of life, and of men.

We would add that according to their geographical dispersion the four לולב-plants could also be representative of the plant world. The date palm belongs exclusively to the torrid zone, citrus plants to countries of lesser heat, myrtle is a plant of the temperate zone, and willows grow in colder climates.

ולקחתם לכם ביום הראשון וגו׳ ,ושמחתם שבעת ימים. Here we meet a similarly striking construction to that of v. 39, (see there), “You are to take on the first day and rejoice for seven days”. If the command is to take the לולב all the seven days it would say: ולקחתם לכם שבעת ימים וגו׳ ושמחתם לפני וגו׳. In the way the text is given it clearly indicates a double command regarding the לקיחה ושמחה of the מצות-לולב: on the one hand ביום הראשון, and on the other שבעת ימים. And in fact the Halacha is (Succah 41a), that מן התורה the מצות-לולב in the מקדש is for seven days but במדינה, i.e. outside the מקדש, in Jerusalem and everywhere else it is only commanded to take the לולב one day, and accordingly ת״כ explains our verse: ושמחתם לפני ה׳ אלקיכם כל שבעה ולא בגבולין כל שבעה. (According to the most general idea, the terms מדינה and גבולין here and elsewhere, comprise the whole Land including Jerusalem, in contrast to מקדש, the Temple. But רמב״ם in his commentary on the Mishna, as well as the Aruch on גבול take them to refer to the Land outside Jerusalem, and consider Jerusalem included in מקדש. (See תוספות י״ט on Shekalim 1,3). In the Jerusalmi too, on our Mishna Succah 3,2. Jerusalem here also seems to be reckoned to the מקדש. There it says: ולקחתם לכם מכל מקום ושמחתם לפני ה׳ אלקיכם שבעת ימים בירושלים. In רמב״ם 7,13, הל׳ סוכה ולולב also follows the general opinion that it is only in the מקדש that the מצות-לולב was commanded for seven days. Deut 12,7 & 18 designates Jerusalem by לפני ה׳ אלקיך and in XXVI,5 & 10 uses the same term for the Temple. So that the expression לפני ה׳ אלקיכם in our verse can be taken to mean one as much as the other.

Accordingly our verse is to be taken thus:— ולקחתם לכם ביום הראשון ושמחתם and moreover: לפני ה׳ אלקיכם שבעת ימים. Everywhere for one day, and in the National Sanctuary of the Torah (or alternatively, in the National environs thereof) for seven days, we are to rejoice before the Presence of God, with the symbolic expression of the gifts in our hands which He, as “our” God, has granted to us. Or rather: ולקחתם לכם ביום הראשון וגו׳, but: ושמחתם וגו׳ שבעת ימים. Everywhere we are to take the symbolic expression of the gifts which God has granted us, on one day, the first of the Festival; but we are to rejoice with it before the Presence of God, in His Sanctuary for seven days.

We have already above on v. 13 & 17 been shown that the Torah promises material independence to every individual, and that no national state of well being and prosperity is recognised when individuals suffer in proletarian wretchedness.

Every Jew, even the most isolated, כל אחד ואחד, wherever he may happen to be, has to take the לולב on the first day; to each one, to such a one too, God says: ולקחתם לכם, but only in the מקדש is he told: ושמחתם לפני ה׳ אלקיכם שבעת ימים.

The seven-day complete national rejoicing with the gifts of God in the Sanctuary of the Torah presupposes the לקיחת כל אחד ואחד בגבולין, on the first day. The nation as a whole can not rejoice before God, in the presence of His Torah, if the achieving of an honest independent sufficiency — not גזול and not שאול has not been made possible everywhere for everybody. It is only this ולקחתם לכם directed to כל אחד ואחד for the first day which introduces the ושמחתם לפני ה׳ אלקיכם שבעת ימים. But the real full joy of life, the undisturbed and undisturbable happiness in life, is not to be found in the well-being and prosperity of private individuals however prosperous and splendid it may be; only לפני ה׳ אלקיכם, in all joining together before God about the Sanctuary of His Torah; only in the individual giving up living for himself and his own private interests to join the national body in their common calling of making God’s Torah a real practised actuality, only if he wishes his own private life and efforts, in whatever social position he may move, to be nothing but one brick in the great building which God, the Master builder, has planned and ordered, then and then only, whether serving like the willow, brilliant like the myrtle, quietly happily productive like the palm, or crowned with fame and accomplishment like the אתרוג, does he attain full, lasting permanent joy before the Presence of God. For only there in that eternal undisturbed godly brotherhood, that real אגודתו על ארץ יסדה, does the insufficiency of any and every individual life and individual endeavours find its completion and permanent meaning — only אין צבור מת and only אין צבור עני; and it is in this existence of living, conscious of duty and faithful to duty, in and with and for the godly תורה-community wherein lies the secret of the heavenly bliss of the Jewish calling, already in this world. The King on his throne to the lowest beggar in the street, or better, to use the Jewish way of thought from the hewer of wood to the drawer of water, there is but one common task, the מורשה קהלת יעקב to which each one has to dedicate his powers and his wealth all having equal value and equal importance. From it each one can attain nobility, each one happiness. Happiness and grief, riches and poverty, rising and falling, life and death find in it — taken in the spirit of the תורה and accepted and used to carry out its teachings — their permanent value and meaning, and it is referring to this, to the participation of the individual in the national treasure of the תורה and the consequent immortality already in this world, that the wish of the alien prophet refers when he said: תמות נפשי מות ישרים ותהי אחריתי כמוהו, then also יקר בעיני ה׳ המותה לחסידיו.

With whatever worries and troubles the individual life of any Jew may be clouded, if only he is conscious, in his mind and in his doings, of his participation in the common national treasure of the תורה, and of the place he occupies in its Sanctuary, the Festival with its varied expressions of all the varied conditions of life, calls him before his God, in the Sanctuary of the Torah, and he feels that to him also is said: ושמחתם לפני ה׳ אלקיכם שבעת ימים!

And with whatever joy and happiness his own private life may be graced, it is only when he is conscious in his mind and in his doings of his participation in the common national treasure of the תורה, and of the places he occupies in the Sanctuary, and knows how to rank himself-along with the gathered “People of the Torah” before God in the Sanctuary, with the multiple expression of all the varied conditions and classes of life, only then does he, too, feel that to him also is said: ושמחתם לפני ה׳ אלקיכם שבעת ימים!

בראשונה היה לולב ניטל במקדש שבעה ובמדינה יום אחד משחרב בית המקדש התקין רבי יוחנן בן זכאי שיהא לולב ניטל במדינה שבעה זכר למקדש (Succah 41a). As long as the Temple was in existence, the לולב was, accordingly, taken in the מקדש for seven days and elsewhere only one day, after the destruction of the Temple, Rabbi Jochanan ben Zacchai instituted that, in remembrance of the Temple, it should be taken everywhere for seven days. But, as our sages always took care when they instituted regulations, מצות דרבנן, although the general rule applies: כל מה דתקון רבנן כעין דאורייתא תקון, that the particulars of their laws should be based on those which apply to the דאורייתא-laws, that nevertheless some indication of their origin should not be lacking in their laws. They did not wish in any way — although made in accordance with God’s behest (see on Deut. 17,10 & 11) — to hand out what were after all human ordinances and rules as being God’s commandments. They accordingly ordered that in this institution which they made that מצות לולב כל שבעה במדינה, i.e. from the second day onwards, the rules that no פסול may be allowed on the ארבעה מינין need be less stringently observed, and for example — probably with special intent — relaxed just those פסולים which are derived from the actual wording in the Torah: ולקחתם לכם, viz. חסר ושאול, and thereby said, as we think, in a striking manner that the ולקחתם לכם of the Torah was not said for these days במדינה (Succah 29b cf. תוספות there ד״ה בעינן).

In accordance with the duty which lies on the Nation as a whole and especially on those who act as representatives of the communities to guard the laws, our sages have further decreed that neither נטילת לולב nor תקיעת שופר should be done on the Sabbath. This decree was made out of fear that, to perform the נלצות-יום-טוב, a desecration of the Sabbath by transgression of the הועאה-prohibition might occur: גזרה שמא יעבירנו ד׳ אמות ברשות הרבים. Thereby they wished that very significant fact for the whole application of Jewish conscientiousness to be deduced, viz. that the avoidance of even the mere possibility of doing an עברה is of greater importance than the certainty of doing a מצוה. At the same time they ensured that the higher meaning and importance of Sabbath compared to that of the Festivals should receive its due consideration. God’s laws as we saw on v. 3, placing Sabbath at the head of the lawgiving of the festivals, gives it special import as the basis of the whole institution of festival days. The experience of our present days gives only too full justification for this solicitude of our sages for the keeping of the holiness of the Sabbath as against that of the Festivals. People speak of the holy days which, in contrast to the weekly occurring Sabbath, only come once a year as the “High Festivals” whereas, according to God’s Torah, all these “High Festivals” including יום כפור, do not attain the holiness of Sabbath (for full details on the לולב see the חורב and the Jeshurun).

V. 42. בסכת תשבו שבעת ימים. The מצוה of לולב, and that of שמחה which goes with it, the joy of living with God’s gifts in our hands, is, in accordance with the text of the previous verse, לפני ה׳ אלקיכם שבעת ימים, only encumbent on every individual for seven days, in the מקדש, and is only applicable ביום in the day time, the time of full activity of life. But the מצוה of סוכה with all the great Truths of Life which it preaches, and the blessings it brings has to be kept everywhere and during the whole period of seven days, of it, it says: בסכת תשבו שבעת ימים כל האזרח בישראל .ישבו בסכת
