בַסכת. The basic meaning of סכך is protection, and סוכה is a roofing erected for temporary protection. This lack of solidity, עראי, as the character of the סוכה as contrasted to the house is expressed in Gen. 33,17: ויכן לו בית ולמקנהו עשה סוכות. Equally so in Sam. II 11,11: הארון וישראל ויהודה יושבים בסוכות ואני אבוא אל ביתי וגו׳. It does not say בְּסכות but בַּסכות, not in סכות in general, but in the סכות, not any סכות, but the prescribed ones, the kind and construction of which is presumed to be known. Clearly the written text of the Torah presupposes that which has been taught by oral teaching, (In Sam. II 11,11 & Kings I 20,16 it also says: בַסכות and presumes army huts as being self-understood as dwellings for the army in camp in wartime). And tradition has given us quite definite particulars for the “huts” in which we are here commanded to dwell during the סכות-Festival. It differentiates between the סכך, the roofing, the actual covering, the protection, the real סוכה, as it says in Is. 4,6: וסוכה תהיה לצל יומם מחורב וגו׳, and the דפנות, the walls enclosing the space.

The סכך has to bear the character of עראי temporary, casual, non solid: סוכה דירת עראי בעינן, the height to the roof may not exceed twenty cubits: סוכה למעלה מעשרים אמה פסולה. It may only consist of דבר שגידולו מן הארץ ואינו מחובר ואינו מקבל טומאה, plant material severed from the ground, in a condition when it is not receptive to טומאה. Accordingly the roof may not be formed by a tree because it is מחובר, and not by fruit nor by wood or other material of vegetable which has been made into כלים as these are able to be מקבל טומאה (Succah 11a). It must be made into the covering roof in the first instance, conforming to the prescribed rules: תעשה ולא מן העשוי, a law which applies to every symbolic formation, e.g. ציצית etc. So that at a bower formed by a vine, ivy or creeper it would not suffice simply to cut off its connection with the ground, but each separate branch must be lifted up and then put down again, because at the time it was formed into a roof it was מחובר and as such unfit for a הדלה עליה את הגפן ואת הדלעת ואת הקיסים וקצצן צריך לנענע :סוכה (Succah ibid.). It must also be sufficiently thickly covered that חמתה is not מרובה מצלתה that the light that comes through is not greater than the shade afforded by the roofing, the total space covered on the roof must be greater than the open spaces (ibid. 2a). דפנות, the walls, may be as solid, permanent, קבע, as desired, may be of any material, and may be fixed in any way desired but must be of at least sufficient strength to withstand an ordinary wind: שיכולין לעמוד ברוח מצויה (ibid. 2a, 12a & 24b). They must be at least ten טפחים high, and enclose an area of ראשו ורובו ושלחנו, a space which at least can contain the greater part of a man’s body and a table for his meal (ibid. 3a). Moreover it need not have four complete walls but: שתים כהלכתן ושלישית אפי׳ טפח, it is sufficient if there are two adjoining walls at an angle and the third could be indicated even by a טפח (ibid. 6a).

The symbolic nature of the Succah can be seen, not only by the idea of תעשה ולא מן העשוי as remarked above, but also by the ideas which apply to the measurments which are fixed for the structure of the building, similar to those which apply to the הועאה-laws of שבת. Some of these we will mention. For example, a מחיצה which can represent a partition of rooms must be at least ten טפחים high. A מקום חשוב, a space to be considered as such, and not too small to be recognized, must have at least an extent of four טפחים. A space of less than three טפחים intervening is considered as לבוד joined up and non-existent. The frontal surface of a horizontal beam fixed high up is considered as being extended downwards, and so continuing the effect of being a division between two spaces: פי תקרה יורד וסותם. According to some opinions we also consider גוד אסיק מחיצות, that the conception of a division by a wall extends upwards above the wall itself. All these and similar laws prove that the erection of a Succah is not concerned with satisfying actual requirements, but is to symbolise certain ideas and thoughts (see Succah 4a & b; 17a & b; 18b and elsewhere).

These are the most important fundamental conditions of the סכות, to which the Torah refers when it speaks of בַּסכות תשבו וגו׳, “under these succoths are ye to dwell”, not just enter, tarry, spend a while, but תשבו, for seven days we are to “live” in succoth, כעין תדורו, similarly to the manner in which we live in firm permanent houses. כל שבעת ימים אדם עושה סוכתו קבע וביתו עראי, during all the seven days you are to make the סוכה your real permanent home and your house just for occasional temporary use (28b).

כל האזרח בישראל ישבו בסכת. Generally it is only homeless strangers who live in “temporary huts”, but here it is emphasized that just כל אזרח בישראל, everyone, even those who have full rights of domicile, the full native-born citizens are to dwell in “succahs’, and these dwellings should give the impression that it is not necessity, not lack of room or home that has driven them to flee to the protection of such a leafy roof. Hence the Succah may not be uncomfortable, only to be endured with discomfort, and מצטער פטור מן הסוכה (Succah 25b). Thus the ריטב״א בשם רמב״ן (Succah 28b): ויש לשאול למה נכתב האזרח כלל שמעתי בשם רבינו הגדול הרמב״ן ז״ל שבא לומר שלא יתחייב בסוכה אלא מי שהוא כאזרח רענן פרט להולכי דרכים ושומרי פירות ומצטער וכיוצא בהן וכן מאי דאמרינן בכל דוכתי תשבו כעין תדורו מהא נפקא לן דהא קרא גלי לן דמאי דכתיב תשבו אינה ישיבה כל דהוא אלא ישיבה כעין דירה כענין וישב יעקב בארץ מגורי אביו ואחרים בכתוב. Moreover, it is not only every אזרח, every actual native-born, but every one האזרח בישראל who has become “naturalised” in Israel, a גר too, who is bound to keep this סוכה-duty. But the Halacha expressly frees women from it, and accordingly makes סוכה no exception to the rule that: כל מצות עשה שהזמן גרמא נשים פטורות, that all commands which are dependent on a special time do not apply to women. In this respect סוכה is not similar to מצה בליל ראשון של פסח, which is an exception to this rule. See on Deut. 16,3 & Succah 28b.

V. 43. למען ידעו דרתיכם וגוי. Here we are given the purpose of this living in succahs. We are to “live” in these “huts” for seven days so that our “descendants” should know that בַּסכות in “such huts” God let us “live” when He brought us out of Egypt. So that our סכות must have signs which remind us of the way in which we lived during the forty years wandering in the wilderness on our way from Egypt to Israel, moreover on the way of living which God gave us there. For it does not say: למען ידעו דרתיכם כי בסכות ישבו וגו׳, but: כי בסכות הושבתי את בני ישראל. So that those סכות, or the homely stay enjoyed in them, or both, must have had the stamp of the special Godly providence of which the festival-succahs which are prescribed for us must have some corresponding reminder. Our סכות must be modelled on those to which they suggestively refer. The Gemora, Succah 7b, points out that in v. 42 which gives the command for our succahs, these succahs are written סכת, deficient, חסר, whereas in v. 43 which speaks of the סכות, to which our succahs are to serve as reminders, the word is written מלא completed, סכות. To this is attached the Halacha that the structure of our succahs need not be complete but, as remarked on v. 42, it suffices if they have: שתים כהלכתן ושלישית אפי׳ טפח. For they only need to suggestively refer back to those of our forefathers.

(This attention to the traditional way of writing a word full or deficient is called: אם למורה, whereas laying the stress on the vocal way in which it is read is called: אם למקרא. The use of the word אם in this connection is explained in the ערוך as the power of motherhood. To the traditional way of spelling in the text is ascribed the power to “bear” certain ideas, i.e. it is meant to indicate certain delicate nuances of ideas, while אם למקרא only gives this power to the way the text is read. Similar to the technical expression בנין אב).

It is this “living” in the “wilderness”, — no mere wandering through the wilderness, — the remembrance of which is to be renewed through all succeeding generations by the סכות-Festival, that Moses refers to at the time when it came to an end and the Israelites were to pass over to a normal condition of life in inhabited countries and cities (Deut. Ch. VIII). He enjoins them to keep it ever in mind, and to hold fast to the truth of the fact which the forty years personal experience was meant to impress upon them with absolute certainty. That fact is to be the eternal basis of our relation to God, and of the mission He has given us. That whole chapter is a commentary on the mitzva of סכות, and its contents, the sermon that the סוכה by the symbolism of its construction preaches to all the generations of Israel. At the head of that chapter the sentence stands:— כל המצוה אשר אנכי מצוך היום תשמרון לעשות למצז תחיון ורביתם ובאתם וירשתם את הארץ אשר נשבע ה׳ לאבתיכם, the fact, that it is only by the conscientious keeping the commandments of the Torah that our individual lives (תחיון), the flourishing of our families (ורביתם), and our national independence (ובאתם וירשתם את הארץ) is ensured. The firm conviction of this fact is the granite rock on which the Jew and Judaism stands. As long as we believe that in the duty of self-preservation we are thrown solely on ourselves, solely on our own powers and ability to wrest our existence from nature, and from a society equally engaged in the struggle for existence, as long as we do not consider this duty of self preservation itself as being, not apart from, but itself a Torah duty, not something to be achieved solely by our own clever manipulations whether they are in accordance with our Torah duties or not, we come very soon and very easily to believe that the care for wife and children — in itself a most justified duty — justifies the setting aside of all other duties and obligations. Therefore, when God wished to create in Israel a nation that was to have one and only one worry, namely to fulfil their duty, He led them first of all into the wilderness to cure them for ever by a great forty-year-long national experience from the “overwhelming weight” of the worry of the struggle for existence. “Remember the whole of the manner in which thy God led thee these forty years in the wilderness to let thee be poor, to test thee, so that thou mayest know what is in thine heart whether thou wouldest keep His commandments or no”. The test, even in complete poverty, in complete deprivation of all the help that nature and society can give, the test, if it has to be, not to despair with wife and child even in the solitude of a wilderness, to live in the solitude of a wilderness only to fulfil one’s duty in cheerful happy confidence in God, that is the test of Jewish faith in the Torah, that is the preliminary condition for a Jewish calling. “He made thee become poor, He let thee hunger, He fed thee with the manna which thou knewest not, neither did thy fathers know, so that He might make thee know that not by bread alone can man live, but by every decree that proceedeth out of the mouth of God man can live. Thy clothes did not wear out, neither did thy foot swell, these forty years” etc., (see Deut. Ch. VIII).

Accordingly it is to free us from putting too much weight and valuing too high and idolizing our skill and ingenuity in obtaining our “bread” that the experience of the wilderness was given to us. And it is of the wilderness filled with God’s loving providence and care, of “the happy satisfied living under the roof of the wilderness” that the סוכה is to tell and preach to our generations. So that whether הסכות to which our succahs are to refer were — as several opinions take them to be, (Succah 11b) — the ענני כבוד, the clouds which intimated God’s Presence, the clouds under whose protecting cover God sheltered His People in the wilderness, or whether they were סכות ממש, actual huts which the people built for themselves, in any case our succahs are to bring to mind the way our forefathers “lived” in the “wilderness” and all the truths and lessons it teaches. But the conception “wilderness” is the absence of all the assistance to the means of living which is normally afforded by nature and human art. Entering the wilderness a man steps out from the protection and assistance of Nature and the work of Man, and can only retain existence through God. But the products of the earth cut off from nature and lacking the stamp of Man’s power is exactly what the Law prescribed for the סכך which forms our succahs. It must be גידולי קרקע product of the earth, but it must be neither מחובר, joined to the earth, so that he who places himself under it would be committing himself to the protection of the powers of the earth, nor may it be מקבל טומאה, material such as פירות or כלים which bear the imprint of Man’s mastery. So that our succah-roofing has either the signs of the ענני כבוד, they, too, have their origin in the ground — אד יעלה מן הארץ, — and still has neither the character of the power of the earth nor that of Man; or it brings to mind סוכות ממש, it has the character of the wilderness, the abandonment of the normal assistance of Nature and Man, it may be neither גרן ויקב not from the threshing-floor nor wine-press, the normal means of “food and enjoyment”, but it is the פסולת גרן ויקב, that which people usually throw away as being empty of nourishment or enjoyment (ibid. and 12a). It is עראי, it does not show the normal condition but bears the stamp of a דירת עראי, of an exceptional condition of life. It is not the precarious life of a dweller in the wilderness, without, or poor in, the amenities for pleasure and art, that God’s leading wants us to find by wandering through life in the paths of His Laws. God wanted to bring us into “a good land, into a land of streams and brooks of water, where springs and depths spring out from valleys and hills, into a land of wheat and barley and vines and fig-trees and pomegranates, a land of olives and dates, a land where one eats bread without scarceness, where nothing is lacking, whose stones yield iron and out of whose hills one can dig copper.”

But so that there we do not “eat and be satiated, build goodly houses and dwell in them, and our herds and flocks multiply, and our silver and gold increase, and all our possessions increase, and then we become proud and forget God … and say in our hearts: My powers and strength of my activity have procured me all this wealth …” therefore, every year, just at the time of the harvest, we are to revert in our minds to the complete contrast of our lives in the wilderness, where no springs gush forth, and no green fields ripen, and no fruit trees blossom, and no harvests are taken home, where no houses make a show, and no business and trade increase our silver and gold, but where nevertheless we lived with wife and children under God’s protection and by His Word without worry of deficiency. By forsaking our fine houses, our דירת קבע, and living, living happily (for מצטער is פטור) under the modest temporary roof of our Succah, a roof destitude of the imprint of Man’s power, or of being nourished by Nature, we are to throw off our dependence on the protection given by Nature or the art of Man, and ever afresh repeat to ourselves and our children the old lesson that we learnt for all time for forty years in the wilderness: that the Jew, the true Jew, כל האזרח בישראל, every one whose mind and heart are substantially implanted in Israel, ישבו בסוכות, should at all times, and at every hour, be ready, if needs be, to renounce the protection and confidence which the powers of Nature and Man offer, and, if God so wills it, to move even into the “wilderness” without fear and trepidation, with cheerful trust in God, and to feel confident even there of God’s Protection and God’s provision, and to live even under the “wilderness-roof” as cheerfully and care-free as in the stately town house כי לא על הלחם לבדו יחיה האדם כי על כל מוצא פי ה׳ יחיה האדם for it is not by “bread” — the product of, and that which represents the combination of Nature and the art of Man — “not by bread alone that Man lives, but by anything that proclaims the Will of God, does Man live.” The normal city life with all that its combination of Nature and Man’s productive powers of active and passive protection offers, does not simply by itself bear, protect and nourish human life, but only as long as, and inasmuch as מוצא פי ה׳ as the Will of God, permits and wishes it (cf. chapter XVI of Exodus).

But the Succah, as every human habitation, consists of two elements, the סכך, the protective roofing, and the דפנות, the separating, delimiting enclosing walls. The protecting element has essentially the character of עראי, of being precarious, not firm, denying the powers of Nature and Man, and, in the fundamental nature of its material, the same for all. The separating delimiting element, the walls, must have a certain degree of solidity, and may have any degree of it desired, and in the kind of material used for them, completely free choice is allowed. If we realise that the סכך represents that which gives us protection, the walls that which ensures our social privacy, then this law would express the thought:— however greatly we may differ in our social conditions which separate man from man here below on earth, whether the space that one man calls his own and which contains his little world is enclosed in marble walls, another must content himself with four wooden ones, a third only succeeds in shutting himself in with two proper adjoining walls and only an indication of a third, and perhaps must even help himself with a slanting roof, a “דופן עקומה״ (see Succah 6b and 17a), in that which protects us from above we are all equal, the סכך is the same for all, the beggar and the millionaire both alike are to reject the combination of Man and Nature’s powers as the protective power of their lives. And in their living under the סכד of the סוכה they acknowledge God, and God alone, as their protection, which the one can not do without, and which suffices for the other. That is also why — according to the one opinion — (Succah 2a) the Succah may not be above twenty cubits in height, so that the צל סוכה does not disappear in the דפנות, and it could appear to be thought that under the protection of high walls of human greatness, the protection of God from above might be dispensed with עד עשרים אמה אדם יושב בצל סוכה, למעלה מעשרים אמה אין אדם יושב בצל סוכה אלא בצל דפנות or so that in the pride of the height of human building one should not lose sight of the protection of God עד עשרים אמה אדם יודע שהוא דר בסוכה למעלה מעשרים אמה אין אדם יודע שהוא דר בסוכה דלא שלטא בה עינא. But in any case the space covered over by the סכך must contain at least ראשו ורובו ושלחנו ourself and our table, that we do not separate ourselves from our tables, that we do not place ourselves under the protection of the סכך, but leave our table under the house-roof, that we consider person and table under the one protection, under God’s Protection alone, that we do not say: yes, our life is in God’s Hand, but the bread for our life is influenced by so many concurrent factors, by the course of the development of Nature, by chance, by human cleverness, with all of which we have to reckon, and against which we can not be satisfied with the simple “pious” belief in the Protection of God”. Not so, תשבו ;בסכות תשבו בעין תדורו, we are to take our whole normal way of living with us into the Succah, and to impress ourselves with the idea that when God led our forefathers out of Egypt, He taught them the cheerful, careful and adequate life in simple huts, lacking nothing under God’s sole protection and אני ה׳ אלקיכם He, and He alone, is also our God.

We have already remarked on V. 42 that women are not obliged to live in the Succah. Succoth is a מצות עשה שהזמן גרמא a command which only applies to a certain fixed time, and such, as a rule, do not apply to women. Thus women are free from the duty of תפילין, ציצית, חגיגה, ראיה, סוכה, לולב, שופר. Exceptions to the rule are: מצה, פסח, קידוש, הקהל, שמחה. The exceptions are nearly as many as the rule. When we consider that Sabbath and Pessach are the two greatest institutions of the Torah recurring from time to time, and that for both of them women are duty bound to observe not only the negative commands איסור מלאכה and איסור חמץ but also the positive זכור) ,קידוש) of Sabbath, and פסח and מצה of Pessach, and that, equally so, although free from ראיה and חגיגה they nevertheless have the duty of participating in the three great national festival gatherings by שלמי שמחה (see תוספות Kiddushin 34b) and also in the great national gathering of every seventh year, הקהל, their being freed from other מצות עשה שהזמן גרמא can most certainly not be on account of their being considered in any way of lesser worthiness or importance. But it seems to us to be rather much more likely that the Torah did not impose these מצות on women because it did not consider them necessary to be demanded from women. All מצות שהזמן גרמא are meant, by symbolic procedures, to bring certain facts, principles, ideas and resolutions, afresh to our minds from time to time to spur us on afresh and to fortify us to realise them to keep them. God’s Torah takes it for granted that our women have greater fervour and more faithful enthusiasm for their God-serving calling, and that this calling runs less danger in their case than in that of men from the temptations which occur in the course of business and professional life. Accordingly it does not find it necessary to give women these repeated spurring reminders to remain true to their calling, and warnings against weaknesses in their business lives. Thus, at the very origin of the Jewish People, God’s foresight did not find it necessary to ensure their bond with Him by giving women some permanent symbol in place of Mila for men. So, also, at the Lawgiving on Sinai, God reckoned first of all (Ex. 19,3) on the faith and devotion of the women. So also, the Jewish Nation has established the fact — and all our generations have inherited it — that in all the sins into which our nation has sunk, it has been בשכר נשים צדקניות, the faithfulness of our women to their convictions and sense of duty which has preserved and nurtured the seed of revival and return. Women are free from the duty of ראיה and חגיגה because the open public national gathering of the nation as the representatives of the Torah which the gathering about the Sanctuary of the Torah means, primarily belongs to the metier of the men.

V. 44. וידבר משה וגוי (cf. above XXI,24) Here also the keeping and carrying out the institution of the מועדי ה׳ is made the concern of the nation. And just as here, it was Moses, the very highest member of the national Body of Representatives of the Torah, who proclaimed the מועדי ה׳ to the nation, so at the realisation of this institution it remained the perogative of the contemporary highest member, the ראש בית דין at קידוש החדש to proclaim “מקודש״ and so sanctify and fix the day of the New Moon in the name of the Nation, and in consequence the day of the Moed. ראש בית דין אומר מקודש וכל העם עונין אחריו מקודש מקודש (Rosh Hashana 24a). According to Megilla 31a and 32a this וידבר etc., with which the Moed-chapter concludes, comes to inform us, not merely that Moses transmitted the Moed-laws which he had from God to the people — which, of course, applies to all the other laws at which it is not expressly mentioned, and is self understood — but rather that it tells us that Moses made it his duty to make an opportunity at the occurrence of each of these מועדי ה׳, by repeated reminders and teaching, to ensure their being observed with all holiness. Thereby he introduced the rule for all future time that on each Moed the chapter referring to it, should be read from the Torah in public, and the meaning and teaching of the particular day explained. וידבר משה את מועדי ה׳ אל בני ישראל, מצותן שיהיו קורין אותן כל אחד ואחד בזמנן. ת״ר משה תיקן להם לישראל שיהיו שואלין ודורשין בענינו של יום הלכות פסח בפסח, הלכות עצרת בעצרת הלכות חג בחג.

V. 1. The great institutions of the Festivals of the cycle of the year which was given in the preceding chapter all refer back to glorious acts of God, which reveal Him as the Founder and Maintainer of the material and spiritual nationality of Israel. God has fixed their recurring anniversaries as מועדים as times for renewing the “coming together of God and His People” on the grounds of the meaning of the various historical events as well as on their relation to the respective seasons of the year. But that the spiritual and material welfare of the nation was not the object of God’s attention only just at the time of these great events revealing God’s intervention in the history of man, when He founded with them Israel materially and spiritually as a nation; that not only at the recurrence of the anniversaries of these deeds .of God, is Israel to feel that their spiritual and material existence is under the direct guardianship of God, and so place themselves under God’s guardianship, but that Israel’s spiritual and material welfare has the Eye of God constantly on it, and that Israel is constantly to place its spiritual and material welfare under God, and only consider itself fit for continued existence under His guardianship and guidance, for that, the consciousness of this fact is to be expressed by Israel’s “light” לפני ה׳ תמיד and Israel’s “bread” לפני ה׳ תמיד. The instructions for the care of both of these, the laws for the מנורה and for לחם הפנים which follow here are partly repetitive and partly additional and complementary. That which is begun by all the individual members of the nation ממועד למועד, through the Festivals, finds its perpetual continuance in the symbolic expression of תמיד in the Sanctuary.

V. 2—4. These verses contain, in the main, the laws already given in Ex. 27,20 and 21 (see notes thereon). מחוץ פרכת העדת באהל מועד. There, where the Service of the Lights is first ordained it says באהל מועד מחוץ לפרכת אשר על העדת, the “Light” of Israel and the care for it is first indicated as having to have its home in the Sanctuary, but restricting its place מחוץ לפרכת אשר על העדת. This sets the purely objective given nature of the תורה as the unalterable preliminary condition for, and the necessary limits for, the mind directed towards the Torah and seeking enlightment from it. Here, where the constant care of the Menora, the “Light of the Spirit” before God, is given in connection with the memory of the historic revelations of God to be awakened ever afresh by the Moadim, naturally the Torah, by the indicated position of the Menora מחוץ לפרכת העדת is in the foreground as being something given by God, and unalterable, untouchable by Man. It must first of all be taken to heart לפני ה׳ תמיד, and only with this precaution does the care of the development of the human mind, even though directed towards the תורה and being enlightened by it, find its place in the אהל מועד. More, according to the way our sages take it (Sabbath 22b), it is only when it has first been פרכת אשר על העדת, when it has been the protecting cover separating off the evidence that the Torah is God’s Torah, that the פרכת does become a פרכת העדת on both sides, on the outside too. Just as, on the inside, the Torah reposing under the protection of the פרכת is “Evidence” of the revelation of God, so, on the other side, the spiritual illumination of the mind to be kindled by, and directed towards the “protected” Torah is no less “evidence” of the proximity of God, which proclaims itself at the cherishing and maintaining of this spiritual and mental light. This was expressed by the miracle of the נר מערבי which occurred daily down to the time of Simeon the Just. Although the same quantity of oil was placed in all the seven lamps, just sufficient to burn from the evening till the morning, the נר מערבי was always still burning when the priest came to light up the lamps the next evening. עדות היא לבאי עולם שהשכינה שורה בישראל, מאי עדות, א״ר זו נר מערבי שניתן בה שמן כמדת .חברותיה וממנה היה מדליק ובה היה מסיים

לפני ה׳ תמיד. Above (in Ex. 27,21 I.L.) תמיד is not mentioned, but here as we have remarked, it is just on תמיד that the stress is laid. על המנרה הטהורה לפני ה׳ תמיד is a complementary addition made here which according to the ת״כ contains the twofold command (a) על המנורה הטהרה שלא יסמכם בקסמים ובצרורות and (b) יעיד את נרות לפני ה׳ שלא יתקן מבחוץ ויכניסם i.e. the עריכה, the lamps must be inserted directly into the Menora without any intervening material, whether for ornamentation or otherwise, and the lamps may not be prepared or inserted outside the היכל and then, all in order and perhaps even already kindled, brought in. But the עריכה and the הדלקה must be done directly on the Menora and inside the Sanctuary itself. The lighting, and especially the preparation of the lamps, which latter is the real עבודה (see on Ex. 27,20) is the sole purpose of the Menora, and here the lesson is specially taught that Israel must place the education and illumination of its mind constantly under the supervision of God. And that, in its constant work on the development of its mind, provided it is done לפני ה׳, it can always expect the furthering and illuminating assistance of God. See ethics of the Fathers 3,6,7.

V. 5 and 6. ולקחת סלת (see Ex. XXVIII. on V. 23-31). There it has already been explained how the material, shape, preparation and presentation of the loaves to be presented on the Table in the Sanctuary, as representing Jewish National Prosperity, all show the character of brotherhood as being the necessary fundamental condition. Now it does not say simply ואפית שתים עשרה חלות סלת but ולקחת סלת ואפית אתה וגו׳. So that the quantity of material representing the Jewish National Prosperity is primarily one single whole, and אתה, that, is then divided into twelve, corresponding to the twelve tribes of Israel. (cf. Ex. XXIV. 4 and Kings I. 18,31). Prepared from the same material, hence qualitatively, and according to the instructions which immediately follow, also quantitatively, they are all completely equal to one another. שני עשרונים: just as the form כמין תיבה פרוצה (see Ex. XXVIII on V,29) shows that just as much, or very nearly just as much, of each of these “tribe-loaves” as is prepared for its own support is directed towards the support of its brother tribe, so does this quantity of material to be used for each loaf indicate the requirement of a double purpose — יהיה החלה האחת, not תהיה so that it is not החלה האחת but שני עשרונים which seems to be the subject of the sentence, and the two עשרונים to be thought of in the singular, as one. Not each loaf shall be of two tenths, but one quantity of two tenths shall each loaf be. יהיה החלה האחת ושמת אותם: each loaf was kneaded separately but they were baked in pairs נילושת אחת אחת ונאפת שתים שתים (Menachoth 94a). Each “tribe-loaf” is directed to have its own individual separate basic care and attention, but it receives consistence only when paired with others, mutually with each other and for each other.

על השלחן הטהור. There in Exodus we have shown how, if the bread expresses the national prosperity, שלחן the Table, represents that which yields this well-being, viz. the development of the material life of the state. We showed how the whole construction of the Table demonstrated all the conditions which are necessary if this life is to result in such national prosperity, namely asiduous industry developing freely, but kept within the limits of what is holy and pure as the basis, brotherliness as the underlying principle, and justice as the supporting pillar. But there is one character which is stressed above all others as the most fundamental of all fundamental conditions for the שלחן as well as for the מנורה, for the development of the material as well as for the spiritual life accordingly, as that which is to be the most characteristic trait of the “Jewish Light” and the “Jewish Table”, and that is טהרה moral purity. Without moral purity Jewish conception of Truth can receive no true development of the mind, and no true height of prosperity. Only המנורה הטהרה (V.4) and only השלחן הטהור (V.6.) have a place in the Sanctuary of God’s Torah. Only המנורה הטהרה only השלחן הטהר can bear “Israel’s Light and Bread” before God.

V. 7. ונתת על המערכת not, on, but next to each stack, as pertaining to it. לבונב זכה the expression of satisfaction with pure simple natural life (Ex. XXV, On. 5,23). והיתה ללחם לאזכרה אשה לה׳: the symbol of our satisfaction stood there ready to become incense for the fire of God’s Altar, accordingly to become the symbol of achieving the Divine Satisfaction. Prosperity can give us satisfaction only for as long as our satisfaction with it is matched by God’s satisfaction with us. God’s satisfaction with it is the condition for our own joy in our good fortune, and only this allowing our own satisfaction to be absorbed by God’s satisfaction can make our bread לאזכרה, can allow our bread to be נזכר לפני ה׳, can we expect our prosperity to have the special attention of God’s Providence (See Ch. II on V,2). Moreover the לחם הפנים is without oil, hence not the bread of riches, but primarily bread just of food. The satisfaction connected with this simple nourishment is specially expressed by לבונה (not קטרת I.L.), and it is only in the idea of its being connected with this that we have called it the bread of well-being. But it is the specifically Jewish bread that becomes “rich” by “contentment”, and its contentment has its roots in God’s satisfaction.

V. 8. ביום השבת וגו׳. On Sabbath, — on which every individual Jew, by שביתת מלאכה, by the cessation of his activities to gain his livelihood and fortune from nature and society, lays himself, his world, and his efforts for his food, at the feet of God, acknowledging Him as the Creator and Lord of the World, — on Sabbath, the Jewish Community, through its representative, the priest, lays its “bread” and its “incense” on the Table in the Sanctuary. It is to be a “constant expression” before God of the fact that while, as the Sabbath teaches, God, as the Creator and Master of the world, is the Lord and Father of all Men, Israel’s fate is a special object of His provident care. God has made this into a special and everlasting bond to Israel. This ברית עולם is the climax of the whole institution of the לחם הפנים and of its place as the conclusion of the giving of the laws of the Moedim. All that of which laying the foundation was begun with יציאת מצרים, with מתן תורה, with the כפרה after the sin of the Golden Calf, with the סוכה-miracles in the wilderness, and which is revived ever afresh in the minds of the nation on the מועדים-anniversaries, all these are nought but the fundamental factors of the everlasting covenant which God made with Israel for all time just by means of these great acts, and which was kept continuously by the care and guidance which God lavished on the fate of Israel תמיד. And that which expresses on their side the acknowledgement of this “covenant-care”, and on their side, constantly keeping their corresponding part of the covenant by constantly placing their whole fate under the guidance and care of God, is the לחם לפני ה׳ תמיד מאת בני ישראל. That is also why it is called להם הפנים, the bread that is specially looked at by God, the bread of His special providence and administration. Tradition tells us that just as the constantly watching care of Israel’s “Light” was visibly demonstrated by the נר מערבי miraculously extending the period of its burning and the light never going out, so at the לחם הפנים was there also a visible sign of God’s constant care of the material welfare of Israel by the bread remaining as fresh at the end of the week as it was when first stacked on the Table: נם גדול נעשה בלחם הפנים סילוקו בסידורו, (Menachoth 29a).

יערכנו. The subject of the sentence is אהרן of the third verse. Thereby the intimate connection between the עריכת הנר and the עריכת הלחם, the constant placing both the spiritual and material development of the life of the nation before the Presence of God, is expressed.

V. 9. חזיתה : As far as we can see, only סלת of v. 5 is the subject to this, which indeed, as we remarked there, right from the beginning is what is regarded as representing the uniform welfare of the nation. לחם הפנים has completely the nature of a מנחה. Just as there, קומץ and לבונה together as אזכרה form the מתיר and the rest form the שירים to be eaten by the כהנים (See Ch. 2,2 and 3), so here לבונה by itself is the מתיר and the twelve loaves the שירים. Every Sabbath the old loaves are removed and fresh ones arranged in their place. This was done in such a way that not for one moment was the Table left without bread, pithily expressing the conception of “תמיד״. Then, after לבונה of the two stacks, which has been lying in two bowls, had been given over to the fire on the Altar, the loaves were divided amongst the outgoing and incoming divisions of משמר) כהנים) who were appointed to weekly service in the Sanctuary (Menachoth 99b). ואכלהו במקום קדוש: for this אכילה, like all the אכילת שירים of the כהנים is a symbolic procedure which complements the teaching of the offering. It preaches the thought of how, once our לבונה as אשה לה׳ has become אזכרה, once all the satisfaction that we seek in life has been sublimated in giving satisfaction to the Will of God, then, even our eating, the enjoyment of our senses, satisfying our bodily desires, becomes elevated into the sphere of pure, priest-like, holy God-serving procedures, (see ibid. and Ex. 29,33).

V. 10. The building of the “Moed” in space, the Sanctuary, the giving of the laws of the offerings, and of the priests and of טומאה and טהרה of symbolic and actual physical sanctification which are attached to it, as well as finally the moadim in time which are closely related to the Moed in space, formed the chief contents of the laws which run from Chapter XXV of Exodus up to here. But just as the whole institution of the sanctification of the Temple was preceded by the laws of social life in משפטים because it was not the foundation of a God-worshipping, Temple community, but — ולקחתי אתכם לי לעם — to form a nation whose whole social life in all its phases strives to accomplish the realisation of God’s Will, which was the ultimate purpose of the choice of Israel, as well as of the institution of God’s Sanctuaries in space and time, so here, too, in the same way, this book of תורת כהנים concludes with supplementary additions to the principles already laid down in משפטים. The immediately preceding institutions of the מנורה and שלחן which are really the essential conclusion of תורת כהנים lead over to these additions in the most striking manner. For these two institutions preach loudly throughout all the generations and ages of the Nation that only מנורה טהורה and שלחן טהור are able to bear “Israel’s Light” and Israel’s “Bread” before the Presence of God; and the construction and service of the שלחן especially stress, as we have seen, that only the life of a state developing itself to give satisfaction to God, and which is based on the principles of Right and Brotherliness can guarantee national prosperity and national weal. A very apt and proper introduction to the supplementary social laws which follow here and in the whole following section! If we consider the laws which follow here on the sins against life, health, and property, which result from ברכת ה׳ from the sin of blasphemy, and the laws on רבית ,גאולת שדה אחוזה ובית ,אונאה ,יובל ,שמטה and עבדים which form the contents of the following chapter, we find that they have all one common factor, viz. bringing the rights of person and property under the influence of the thought of God in social life. Then we understand all the more their place here after the giving of the laws of the Temple and the festivals. For קרבת אלקים, bringing the nearness of God into earthly material life and existence is the purpose which is aimed at with all קרבנות all טהרה and קדושה all the מועדי ה׳, and it is just only through these laws that the thought “God”obtained its full life-giving purport in the Jewish conception of the Deity. The laws from V. 15 et seq. are introduced by the report of an event which gave cause for the pronouncement of these sentences.

ויצא וגו׳ בתוך בני ישראל. He went out of the bounds within which he belonged, into the midst of the Children of Israel where he did not belong (cf. Ex. 11,4 אני יוצא בתוך מצרים, where it means the coming out of a retirement into a sphere where hitherto He had not been seen). He was the son of a Jewish woman but not of a Jewish man. Although, according to the accepted Halacha, in cases where קידושין are not possible שאין לו עליו ולא על אחרים קידושין the child follows the mother and is Jewish, הולד כמותה and נכרי ועבד הבא על בת ישראל הולד כשר and the child here, accordingly, would be a Jew (Kiddushin 66b and 68b as well as Yebamoth 45a) there is still a doubt whether this rule applies to cases where the child was born before the mother had received the Torah on Sinai. For this reason, in ת״כ the בתוך בני ישראל is explained מלמד שנתגייר that he had become a proselyte to Judaism. (See רמב״ן thereon. Also, there, in ת״כ, it may follow the view that הולד כשר is only said in contrast to ממזר, he would be כשר only after the גרות. See רש״י and תוספות on Yebamoth 13a and Kiddusin 48b. But in any case the ת״כ there seems to contradict itself. It says שנתגייר, this assumes that at birth he must have followed his father’s status, and, according to the version of the ילקוט immediately before it says: אע״פ שלא היו ממזרים באותה שעה הוא היה ממזר, but the concept ממזר assumes that he had followed his mother’s status. Perhaps that accounts for our version: ראב״ד .וצ״ע ;כממזר in his commentary on ת״כ makes the מלמד שנתגייר refer to the father, who had become a גר after the birth of his son. That of course, would solve all the difficulties, including that which the רמב״ן discusses, and it would only remain to make out the reason for telling it to us). The ת״כ explains על עסקי המחנה :במחנה and finds therein the nature and cause of the quarrel. It was not concerning an unjustified claim to his claim to being a Jew, but regarding his claim to have a place in the national camp that the trouble arose. For this, the belonging to a particular tribe, it is the paternal descent which is the deciding factor: איש על דגלו לבית אבותם. So that whether he had become a Jew by birth, or as a proselyte, he could in no case be counted as a member of the tribe of Dan to which he made a claim. The objection of his opponent was therefore fully justified. — איש הישראלי: it does not say איש ישראלי a Jewish man, also not האיש הישראלי, in which case one would have had to take it to refer to the Jewish husband of the woman, but איש הישראלי, a man who was an Israelite and claimed the full rights of Jewish descent, in which he declared the other deficient. (When we remember that a מצרי, even as a proselyte becomes a full Jewish citizen only in the third generation: דור שלישי יבא להם בקהל ה׳ (Deut. 23,9), in any case, here, even as a גר his exclusion בתוך בני ישראל was not without grounds).

Here accordingly we have a combined case in which purity of morals exercises an influence on social “right of position”, two principles whose importance for Jewish social life were represented by the שלחן just afore mentioned.

V. 11. ויקב וגו׳ את השם. We have already on Gen. 30,28 tried to identify the idea of נקב to name, to appoint, with נקב to perforate, to pierce. We believed that נקב means the lifting an object out of the generality of its species by naming its special name. So that it is the most special individualization of an object by a name. This name can only be a proper noun, and indeed according to Sanhedrin 56a too, מברך את השם is only חייב מיתה על שם המיוחד, if at the blasphemy, God, is named by the שם הוי׳ or by the substituting אדנות which is called שם המיוחד or שם המפורש because it is an individualising, specializing nomen proprium. הבנויים באזהרה if He is named only by an attributive or generic name as רחום ,אלקים, it is only עובר בלאו וכרת as is clearly apparent from verses 15 and 16. Now we find both נקוב בשם and אשר נקבו בשמות :נקב שם (Numb. 4,16), and וקרא לך שם חדש אשר פי ה׳ יקבנו (Is. 62,2). The former means “to name somebody by their proper name”. The latter “to give somebody a proper name”. את השם the Name, without further specification, implies the Highest Name in human conception. So, still to-day “Hashem” is used in Jewish colloquial speech to designate “God”. — ושם אמו וגו׳, at that time she was the only woman in Israel who had thus sinned, that is why she achieved the sad distinction of being remembered in a page of God’s eternal writing. But it is only after her son had sinned that her name is mentioned. For it is just in this sin that the sad consequence of her immorality is warningly shown. Without this, such an outbreak of un-Jewish depravity would never have occurred in Israel. Only her immoral association with a non-Jew could have planted the seed of such a crime in Israel. The horror at the enormity of the son’s crime showed up the mother, Shelomith, as the actual originator of the deed. According to all the indications in V.15 of the cause of this crime, this son of an Egyptian did actually blaspheme the specific God of Israel because he found in His building up His nation and its national rights on the institutions of moral purity — irreconcilable with the corruption of his Egyptian origin — limitations imposed on his desire.

V. 12. לפרש להם וגו׳. It is doubtful whether the underlying meaning of פרש would be to spread out, unfold, related to פרשׂ, or to separate divide, related to פרם. The former would be indicated by צאנו נפרשות (Ezek. 34,12) “the scattered flock”, and then its meaning “to explain” would be the “separating out of complicated matters”, similar to the Latin explicis. The latter would be indicated by the meaning of פרש dung, “that which is separated away from”, and then the meaning “to explain” would lie in the same trend of thought. As we have often remarked, all making clear, making understandable, pronouncing, fixing, have the underlying idea of separating, particularising. Cf. נכר ,נקב ,חרץ ,גזר etc. Probably the meaning of פרס to spread out, is itself also only a derivative idea of separating, particularising. By spreading out articles which are confined together in a small space or which are in a tangled mass, the objects are brought out from being in contact with other objects or with parts of the same object. So that every spreading out is an untangling, a separating, and פרץ ,פרש ,פרז ,ברץ ,ברז are only nuances of one and the same idea.

V. 14. הוצא את המקלל. The place of execution had to be outside the מחנה ישראל, (Sanhedrin 42b חוץ לג׳ מחנות) outside the city. If the law court itself was outside the city, the place of execution had to be some distance away from it, דלא מתחזי ב״ד רוצחין so that it should not appear as if the court considered its highest attribute to be “the sword of justice”. Altogether (— as we very conclusively prove in our article in the Jeshurun, Jahrgang XII p. 143 et seq. —) the essential character of the criminal courts was to direct its efforts to finding reasons for freeing the accused rather than for pronouncing him guilty. The verdict of “guilty” was already before the court in the התראה of the accusing witnesses and the real task before the court was to test and examine this pronounced sentence, and find out if there was not some mitigating reasons for a “not guilty” verdict. Another reason, given there, for having the place of execution at a distance from the court is, כי היכי דתיהוי ליה הצלה so that some time must elapse between the pronouncement and the carrying out of the sentence (the sentence had to be carried out immediately after the verdict), in which time some fresh reason for reconsidering the verdict might arrive. For while the condemned man was being taken away, אחד עומד על פתח ב״ד וכו׳, a man stood at the door of the court with a flag in his hand, and a mounted messenger was posted just within sight; should one of the judges find some fresh reason in favour of the criminal, the one waved his flag and the other galloped off at full speed and held up the proceedings. More, ואפי׳ הוא אומר וכו׳, even if the condemned man himself, on the way to execution, declared he had something fresh for his defence, he was taken back אפילו ארבעה וחמשה פעמים even four or five times, ובלבד שיש ממש בדבריו, provided that, in the opinion of the two judges who accompanied him for this very eventuality, there was some foundation, however slight, for his assertion (ibid. 42b and 43a).

וסמכו: see on Ch. 1,4. כל השומעים: the witnesses who had heard the blasphemy, and the judges who had heard the crime reported by the witnesses (ת״כ thereon) see on Ch. 20,2. — ת״כ) עדים במעמד כל העדה :כל העדה, it is primarily the witnesses who have to carry out the sentence which has been provoked by them, and others only come into it subsidiarily (see Deut. 17,7). But the act has to be done in national publicity for only in the name of the nation is it to be carried out.
V. 15. בכנויים :כי יקלל אלקיו not בשם המפורש see on V.11. ונשא חטאו i.e. כרת (Pesachim. 93b).

V. 16. ונקב שם ה׳, if he used the Personal Name of God, “ה׳״. See on V.11. רגם ירגמו בו: see on Ch. 20,2, there we have already mentioned that death by סקילה was primarily דחיה, by suddenly precipitating the criminal from a height to the ground, and only in the case where instantaneous death did not result was he “stoned” with a rock. Perhaps this is the explanation of the different way in which רגם is construed in verse 14 with אותו and here — רגם ב. The former refers to precipitation of the criminal, here to actual stoning with a rock.

V. 17. The sin of ברכת ה׳ dealt with in the previous verses was prohibited already in Ex. 22,27, by אלקים לא תקלל. Even if the name there is חול and refers primarily to human judges, it implies also the warning against the same sin if committed against the real Judge, the real .אלקים גמר קודש מחול (Sanhedrin 66a). And all the verses that follow here connected with it, dealing with the rights of life and property are only complementary to laws already given in the chapter of Mishpatim in Exodus. Our verse 17 is the complement of V.12 of Ch. XXI in Exodus (see notes thereon).

V. 18. ומכה נפש בהמה ישלמנה. This complements the laws given in Ex. 21,33 et seq., XXIV,33 et seq., and XXIV,4 et seq., on damage done to other peoples’ property, done or caused to be done by one’s own property, נזקי ממון בממון, by giving the case of other people’s property being damaged directly by Man, נזקי ממון באדם. It lays down the law that here too, damages have to be paid, תשלומין, reparation, i.e. reparation for the damage done, but no more; so that the risk of the killed animal losing (or gaining I.L.) in value is the concern of the owner: הבעלים מטפלין בנבלה ופחת נבלה לניזק (B.K. 10b and 11a, see Ex. 21,34). — נפש תחת נפש: he has to pay him such a sum, which, together with any value remaining to the injured animal, amounts to the full original value of the animal, so that the damage done to the property is made good again. This tells us, at the same time, that killing or injuring an animal, in civil law is considered only as a crime or misdemeanour against the owner.

V. 19. and 20. These two verses are complementary to the laws regarding wounding one’s fellow men, given in Ex. 21,18 — 25. ואיש כי יתן וגו׳ first of all limits the following שבר תחת שבר duty to give compensation for all the results of wounding, viz. נזק צער רפוי שבת בשת (Ex. 21,24 and 35) only to injuries done by men but not by animals: איש בעמיתו ולא שור בעמיתו (Baba Kama 26a), at שור שנגח only נזק has to be paid. Then, כאשר עשה כן יעשה לו that in certain circumstances, corporal punishment מלקות is imposed for inflicting wounds on others, namely in cases where the injury is so transient that the compensation would not amount to the minimum of a penny, שאין בה שוה פרוטה. The crime then is simply הכאה, a blow, and the מלקות punishment can be expressed by כאשר עשה כן יעשה לו (see שיטה מקובצת on Kethuboth at the end on 35a). חובל בחברו, for every attack on the body of another comes under the heading of the prohibition (which is against striking in general) לא יוסיף פן יוסיף להכתו (Deut. 25,3, see notes thereon) and so is liable to the punishment of מלקות. But here, as well as in Ex. 21,18 et seq. the liability for compensation for injuries inflicted is expressed, and the rule in Jewish law is that punishments are never cumulative, so that two penalties, מלקות ותשלומין are never imposed for one and the same crime. This principle of justice is taught in Kethuboth 32b to be indicated in Deut. 25,2 by the expression כדי משום רשעה אחת אתה מחייבו ואי אתה מחייבו משום ב׳ רשעיות :רשעתו. Every crime may only be punished from one point of view, either as a sin against the law of God, by corporal punishment, מלקות, or מיתה, flagellation or death, or as a sin against brother-man by תשלומין, compensation, or fine, קנס, but never by both. Where — as in our case here — both are incurred, the general rule is לוקה ואינו משלם, he gets punished by מלקות, and no payment is imposed Only עדים זוממין and חובל חברו are exceptions to the rule. In these two cases, where ממון compensation or monetary fine, is possible, משלם ואינו לוקה, that alone is imposed (ibid.). So that in cases of חובל בחברו only when the הכאה is less than שוה פרוטה is מלקות imposed. But as soon as the amount of the injury inflicted makes monetary restitution possible then, not מלקות but שבר תחת שבר etc., comes into force cf. Ex. 21,24. There we proved, how, in actual fact as well as literally the text is completely in accordance with the Halacha, the traditional practice, how the text can only be speaking of full compensation for the injury inflicted. Here כויה תחת כויה וגו׳, by which the pain caused by the injury is indicated as being an item for compensation, is missing; on the other hand, here, instead of רגל, the complete and permanent loss of a limb, we find שבר by which can be understood also the temporary loss of the use of a limb, or the partial mutilation and injury of it, So that by עין ,שבר and שן our text indicates damage done to a limb in the various possible degrees of injurious consequences: — שבר, the partial or temporary loss of use; עין, the complete and irreparable damage of an organ: and between the two שן, the loss of an organ which itself is permanent but which possibly could be reproduced by another one (e.g. in the first dentition, or by lateral movement of the teeth. I.L.). And then it goes on to say כאשר יתן וגו׳, that for estimating the amount of the compensation to be paid, each case has to be considered on its own particular merits. כן ינתן בו, a similar expression to ונתן בפלילים he has to pay through the verdict of the judges (Ex. 21,22), like כי בו נתן ה׳ תשועה, “God, has given victory through him” (II Kings VI) so here, “it is to be given through him”.

V. 21. ומכה בהמה וגו׳. Just as for the killing, wounding or damaging of animals (the word נפש is not used there) in every case, monetary compensation, and money compensation only, is imposed, so, for the killing of human beings, or, as is the case at מכה אביו ואמו even merely wounding, the death penalty is incurred, that, and that only can be imposed. Even in cases where the circumstances in which the deed was done precludes the death penalty being inflicted, e.g. בשוגג as the accused has actually forfeited his life, there can never be any question of monetary compensation being imposed, חייבי מיתות שוגגין פטורין מתשלומין (Kethuboth 35a) see תוספות Baba Kama 35a ד״ה מכה אדם).

We have already in Ex. 21,23, fully explained this principle in law of תנא דבי חזקיה and its applications and consequences. We found that, by a sharp line drawn to the very extreme between the life of a human being and that of an animal, the unparalleled higher dignity of human life is upheld in the concept of justice. If we sum up the laws given here on the rights of life and property, they too, all seem to have their point in this maxim of law differentiating between animal and man. It hangs on the difference between נפש אדם and נפש אדם ,נפש בהמה is a person, נפש בהמה is a thing. The killing of a נפש אדם has to be treated solely as a crime against a person, whose dignity allows no compensation in money, and restitution of the offence against the sanctity of human life can only be made by the loss of the earthly life of the murderer. The killing of a נפש בהמה is only treated as a crime against the owner, and certain though it is that צער בעלי חיים דאורייתא (see on Ex. 25,5), and is always a sin against God, human justice takes no cognisance of the killing of an ownerless animal. Only the body and limbs of a man are equally considered as being part of his possessions, as belongings of the נפש אדם whose tools they are, so that doing damage to the body of a human being is at the same time a sin against the person and against his God. Hence, where damages are possible as compensation, so that the damage done is rectified, the sin against the person comes to the foreground and מלקות is suspended.

All these principles of law, and their underlying conceptions of law and justice are already contained in משפטים, the chapter of the fundamental regulations for social life, and there, too, the specifically higher dignity of the human being is clearly the underlying factor. But here they are brought into connection with the pronouncement of a law which stands at their head, so that they should be taken as being simply the natural outcome of the acknowledgement of this law. So that the fact which is expressed by this law appears as the basic conception which underlies, and is the indispensable condition for, all true application of the rights of Man.
This fundamental conception of all justice, this indispensable condition for all rights of Man is simply a conception of the Personality of God.

Remove the Personality of God from the world and you have banished “Justice” from the world. For justice is a demand that can only be really demanded by the free. He who denies moral freewill must keep his mouth closed on the subject of justice. He can — without delusive deception — only speak of the effects of force, of the working of physical, mechanical or organic forces; the whole conception of right and wrong does not exist for him. But if the world, and hence Man too, has no completely free-willed Creator Who has granted Man, the noblest of His earthly creations, participation in His moral freedom of will, if there is altogether no supernatural free-willed world-creating Power, and Man, too, is naught but the physical product of an unfree physical world bound by physical laws, from where then should moral freedom come to the physical product of a physical world. If there is no free God, if complete and absolute freedom of will does not exist in God, how can Man have obtained moral freedom of will, and how then can there be talk of Right and Wrong?

And just as the idea of Right and Wrong, and its necessary corollary of moral freedom is unthinkable without a completely free God, in the same way the fact of God being a “Personal God” is an indispensable conception for the idea of human personality. For “person” is naught but a being who, in all moral matters, can decide for himself. Personality is really only the incorporation of moral freedom of will in an individual. But if such individual personality is not present, and present to the very absolute degree in God, if there is altogether no Personal World Creator outside the world Who has endowed Man, His noblest earthly creation, with spirit of His Spirit, set him in His world and said to him “be free, have the power to make your own decisions”, if there is only this material world and Man is naught but a product of this material world, then Man, too, is only one of the other “things” of the world, is no longer a personality. The difference between things is then merely quantitative, but not qualitative, everything is the toy and result of blind forces bound by the irresistible laws of nature. Plants are merely more highly developed, more complicated amoebe, animals more complicated plants, and Man only a more complicated animal. But, of a specific difference of kind, of a specifically higher dignity of Man, human personality, there can be no question.

So that, just as the first word of Law (Gen. 9,5 & 6) the higher dignity of human life over that of animal life is based on the fact of Man being in the likeness of God, so here ברכת השם, the sin against the Personality of God, is placed at the head of the sin against a human personality. Hence it is only ברכת השם המפורש which entails the death penalty, for it is only just in this Name that the Personality of God is descriptively expressed.

V. 22. And just as all the rights and all the high value of human beings are rooted in the Personality of God, so does this form the basis for complete equality in law and justice: משפט אחד etc., one and the same law for all in the procedures of the administration of justice. There must be the same demands on the personalities of the witnesses, פסול קרובים etc., the same meticulous care in probing the truth of statements of witnesses דרישה וחקירה, whether in criminal or civil cases אחד דיני ממונות ואחד דיני נפשות (Sanhedrin 28a & 32a). And כגר כאזרח יהיה, the same and equal rights for all, for the native and the stranger: for אני ה׳, I am the God of all!

V. 23. ובני ישראל עשו וגו׳: not only the רגימה mentioned here, but everything that was prescribed for this means of execution also סמיכה (v. 14), דחיה ,תליה and ת״כ) ,לא תלין, see on Ch. 20,2). As we remarked on v. 16 by the construction וירגמו אותו אבן also דחיה can be understood, and as ובני ישראל starts a fresh sentence, the ויוציאו and וירגמו can refer to the דחיה and possible דגימה demanded, in the first instance through the instigation of the witnesses, and the ובני ישראל עשו to the subsidiary intervention of the nation, and also the תליה with which perhaps the witnesses have nothing to do.

V. 1. The last verses of the previous chapter placed “God’’, as the fundamental source of all justice, and the “Personality” of God, as the basis of all “rights” of men and their possessions, at the head of the Lawgiving on rights and justice. To that, this chapter is now attached, going to the narrower sphere of the land owners in Israel and there proclaiming God as the one real Lord and Owner of the Jewish land, Jewish men, and property, and from that it develops a conception of rights in general from these laws on land, men and property. יובל שביעית, and the institution of גאולה at the purchase of land, houses and human service, as well as the law of רבית are all only consequences of the one principle of rights which regards God as the only real claimant.

These laws are introduced by the words: וידבר ה׳ אל משה בהר סיני לאמר, to which ת״כ gives the explanation: מה ענין שמטה אצל הר סיני והלא כל המצות נאמרו מסיני אלא מה שמטה נאמרו כללותיה ודקדוקיה מסיני אף כולם נאמרו כללותיהם ודקדוקיהם מסיני, i.e. “why does the Torah tell us that just שמטה and its laws were given at Sinai, were not all the laws given on Sinai?; but it comes to teach us that just as the Torah tells us expressly that שמטה was given with all its rules and details, so all the laws of the Torah were revealed on Sinai with all their rules and details. We think that the express declaration that all the laws with all their details originated from the revelation on Sinai, and the proclamation being made here just at the שמטה-laws, may be due to the immediately preceding event of the מגדף. For just in this case it happened that a law given on Sinai, only in its general character, בכלל, regarding its general application, judgment, and verdict, but all the details, any and every כללות and דקדוקים were lacking to such an extent that only when the case actually happened did a special proclamation have to be obtained from God as to the procedure to be followed: וינחהו במשמר לפרש להם על פי ה׳. And what a law, and what application, especially when contrasted to that of the שמטה-law does this law have! What this law deals with is absolutely the worst sin imaginable, yea, the one sin which is entirely independent of time or space or circumstances. It is present everywhere and at every moment, so that it can be transgressed at any time, at once and always. So one could say to oneself: if this law was given so vaguely and incompletely at Sinai that it was only when the necessity for it actually arose, that it had to be explicitly given, how then should laws, such as, for example שמטה, for which at the time of the Lawgiving and for years afterwards the object for their application — the land of Israel — was lacking, and in the course of time would again be lacking for centuries, perhaps thousands of years, how then should such laws have been given already back at Sinai in all completeness: בכללותיהם ודקדוקיהם! To oppose this idea the Torah could well see itself urged, just at the שמטה and יובל-laws which follow those on ברכת ה׳ to make the definite assertion that, although for מגדף it was only when the occasion occurred that instructions for details of the Law had to be sought, nevertheless all other laws, even those like שמטה etc., which were limited to space and time, were given in all detailed completeness at Sinai to Moses. But the reason why the law concerning ברכת ה׳ was not given in its details with the rest of the Lawgiving on Sinai, — more, actually only implied by being included in the אלקים לא תקלל — may be — as Wessely remarks in his commentary — because the Torah did not wish beforehand even to suggest the possibility of such a crime, the gravest of all grave sins, occurring amongst the People of God. And, as a matter of fact, it was only committed by one in whose character Egyptian blood could make itself manifest.

V. 2. כי תבאו אל הארץ. From the repeated expressions כרמך ,שדך, in the following verses, the ת״כ teaches the fact that the שמטה-law had to start only when the Land had already been divided amongst families and homes, so that כל אחד ואחד מכיר חלקו, each one had his allotted property. Accordingly only after שבע שכבשו and שבע שחלקו, after the seven years which were occupied in conquering the land and a further seven years in the division of the land. With the fifteenth year they began the first שמטה cycle, and the twenty first year was the first שמטה year. — ושבתה הארץ שבת לה׳: that which שבת בראשית, the seventh day is, in relation to the earth, the seventh year is, in relation to the Land. The one is a day of acknowledgement of God as the Creator and Master of the world, the other a year of acknowledgement of God as the Owner and Master of the Land (cf. on Ch. 23,32).
V. 3. את תבואתה refers to הארץ of the preceding verse.
V. 4. שבת לה׳. The Torah repeatedly says that the Sabbath of the Land is a Sabbath לה׳ and not, as one might suppose, a fallow year ordered in the agricultural interests of the land.

שדך לא תזרע etc. Whereas on Sabbath, not only the basic activities of work themselves (the אבות), but also their derivatives (the תולדות), are understood by the prohibition of work, e.g. not only זריעה, sowing or planting, but also any furthering of growth, such as watering, pruning etc., is אסור, here, this prohibition of agricultural activities is, מן התורה limited to only those mentioned in the text, viz. קצירה ,זמירה ,זריעה and בצירה. For if the Torah wished these to be taken merely as examples, so that by זריעה all activities furthering growth would be forbidden and by קצירה all kinds of separating growth from its attachments, then זמירה would not have been mentioned together with זריעה nor בצירה with קצירה. For זמירה is the same agricultural activity for the vine as זריעה is for grain, and בצירה for the grape harvest what קצירה is for the fields (Moed Katan 3a). This difference between שביעית and שבת would be because of the difference in their respective meaning. The recognition and acknowledgement of God as the Creator and Master of the world is not expressed by only subordinating Man’s creative powers over the raw materials of the world under God. The thought of God, as the only actual Creator does away with the idea of Man having creative powers. Any and every exercise of Man’s power over matter does really come under the conception of “מלאכה״ which is prohibited on Sabbath. There is no real difference between אבות and תולדות. But שביעית, the recognition and acknowledgement of God as the Owner of the Land of Israel, needs no more than the placing of the ground under the rule of its Master. The thought of the real Owner of the land does away with the idea of its being at the disposal of the fief-holder to work the ground, and harvest its products for himself at his own sweet will. To express this, it is sufficient to cease all sowing of seed and pruning of trees, as well as to abstain from storing that which goes on growing by itself to ensure a sufficiency for the year (see v. 20). Thus the soil of the whole country is stamped as ownerless for a year, and is made into a national public acknowledgement that the Jewish people are not the owners of the Jewish Land. Thus Sanhedrin 39a: אמד הקב״ה לישראל זרעו שש והשמיטו שבע כדי שתדעו שהארץ שלי היא. By the רבנן, most of the other agricultural activities are also forbidden, and included in the idea of איסור שביעית, and perhaps the general principle of these שבותים (prohibitions made by the Rabbis. I.L.), for שביעית — just like those for שבת — is expressed by the addition of the word שבתון (v. 4 [[illegible]] See Ex. Ch. 15,23).

V. 5. ספח .את ספיח קצירך (related to שפח, the root of משפחה, which also has the idea of attachment to a common stem) designates a dependent attachment to something else. So we find: ספחני נא אל אחת הנהנות, (Sam. 3,36). ספיח is that which has grown, not through this year’s cultivation but as a result of previous work, so that it is connected with previous agricultural activity. So that what grows from the leavings or droppings of previous harvests, or grows wild is called לא תקצור — .ספיח: you may not harvest it, not cut it off, heap it up and store it. — נזירך is everything from which on account of its having a higher calling, a higher character, others stand at a distance. Hence the sign of such a high “standing-apartness”, נזר a crown, a diadem. נזיר אחיו, the crowned-one of his brothers (Gen. 49,26). Similarly also the נזיר (Numb. Ch. VI, see thereon). Here נזיר refers to the vine, which in the שביעית-year is to bear the character of belonging to God, and on account of this higher calling is to remain untouched by the hand of the vine growers, לא תבצור, you may not make the usual grape harvest and wine-pressing from the grapes which nevertheless have grown by themselves.

Verses 6 & 7 tell us: והיתה שבת הארץ לכם לאבלה, that of the Sabbath of the Land, i.e. that which the land nevertheless produces by itself, והיתה לכם, is to be for you, is there for your use, but with the limitation לאבלה only לאכילה which term includes שתיה and סיכה eating, drinking and external application (of oil etc. I.L.), and generally such use where, like אכילה the הנאתו וביעורו שוה, the use and the absorption are simultaneous, where the material is used up by the use, e.g. להדלקה, to use oil for lighting purposes, but not where הנאתן אחר בעורן, where the purpose is only achieved after the destruction of the material, e.g. עצים להסקה converting wood to charcoal for heating purposes (Baba Kama 102a). Altogether the use is restricted to the ordinary purpose of the material, that which is really grown for human consumption may not be used for animal food nor used for medicinal purposes (Sheveith 8,1 et seq.). The whole manner of use which is permitted bears the stamp of only limited rights of possession. פירות שביעית are given לאכלה, and not להפסד. That which is eatable that grows in the Sabbath year is to be eaten, not wasted nor destroyed (Pesachim 52b). Finally פירות שביעית are given only for אכילה but not for סחורה, no business may be transacted with them, and that includes any use of them for the purpose of gain (Sheveith 7,3 & 8,3 etc.). Money or produce which has been obtained in exchange for פירות שביעית is considered as having the nature of שביעית itself, and may only be used within the limits which apply to פירות שביעית themselves. שביעית is תופסת דמיה: the שבועית-character becomes transferred to the bartered object, “שביעית grips its exchange”. There are three איסורים which are thus תופסין דמיהן, viz. ע״ז ,קודש and שביעית. But the effect of this peculiarity differs in each case. קודש תופס דמיו ויצא לחולין, an object which has become holy by being dedicated can, by redemption, transfer its holy character to another object, and itself becomes חולין again, profane. חליפי ע״ז, anything exchanged for an ע״ז becomes equally אסור בהנאה as the ע״ז, but the ע״ז remains as אסור as it was before. According to several opinions, and actually adopted as Halacha by רמב״ם, (הל׳ ע״ז 8,1), even חליפי חליפין, the exchange of an exchanged object is also אסור בהנאה in the case of שביעית .ע״ז is midway between the two: אחרון אחרון נתפס בשביעית ופרי עצמו אסור, the אםור-character which rests on שביעית fruit is irremovable, like ע״ז can not be redeemed, the fruit itself always retains its character as שביעית. But an object for which it is exchanged only receives the קדושת שביעית to the same degree that redeemed קודש has, so that its קדושה can be transferred from object to object, the last one becoming קודש and each preceding one becoming מותר again (Avoda Zara 54b). All other איסורי הנאה such as חמץ בפסח ,כלאי כרם ,ערלה etc., are not תופסין דמיהן, and if one — against the law— were to sell or exchange them, the money or the exchanged object is not אסור, and the person who has illegally sold or exchanged them is only מדרבנן prohibited from making any use of the money or exchanged object (see Kiddushin 58a; Chulin 4b Rashi and תוספות thereon; ר״ן Nedarim 47a).

This making שביעית on the one hand equal to ע״ז and on the other to קודש, can give us deep understanding of its nature. Just as שבת בראשית stands parallel to ע״ז so that the avowal of Sabbath is taken to be the positive contrast to the denial of God contained in ע״ז, so is שביעית too, a similar positive contrast to שביעית .ע״ז is equally a positive expression of the acknowledgement of God, of God being Ruler of the soil of the Jewish Land, as ע״ז is the denial of the exclusive Rule of God. Everything that the Jewish soil produces in שביעית is an object that bears the idea of the Rule of God, and is holy to the expression and realisation of this thought, just as an ע״ז is an object which represents the opposite of this thought. Both, פירות שביעית and ע״ז are objects of avowal regarding the highest fundamental truth of Jewish conception; the one the acknowledgement, the other the denial, of God being Ruler. In this they differ sharply from all other objects mentioned in the Torah. Concerning ע״ז that object which represents an error, the denial of which calls for the output of the whole of our spiritual and mental energy, the Torah says in Deut. 7,26: ולא תביא תועבה אל ביתך והיית חרם כמהו, i.e. “that which, with spiritual and moral disgust, thou are to keep afar from the sphere of thy thoughts (תועבה. I.L.) shalt thou not admit into the sphere of thine existence (ביתך. I.L.), otherwise thou couldst become banned, even as it is” From which Kiddushin 58a deducts: כל שאתה מהייה הימנה הרי הוא כמהו, everything whose existence you obtain through ע״ז becomes the same as it. i.e. just as ע״ז may have no existence for you, and hence is אסור בהנאה, you may have no use from it, so is everything אסור בהנאה which you obtain by means of it, it is תופס דמים, and, as already remarked, even חליפי חליפין ע״ז are אסור. Even by repeated transmission nothing in your possession may lead your thoughts back to ע״ז. The whole idea of ע״ז is חרם, it is a conception which is to be avoided like a “net” in which you might become entangled. In contrast to that, everything which the earth bears in the Sabbath year, all פירות שביעית. are things which represent God’s rule over your property, or rather which bring to your mind that the land and its products which you call yours really belong to its real Owner, God. This ownership is proclaimed in the limited manner and time (ביעור, see below) in which you are allowed the use of these products which “your” land and “your property bear in the Sabbath year. Were you able to have unrestricted use of the value of these products by selling them, you would be making the idea which they represent into a vain illusion. Hence the Torah says for שביעית the same as it says for יובל viz. (v. 12): קודש תהיה לכם, its products are holy to the idea of belonging to God, and, like all such holy things, קדש, selling or bartering them, the sale transmits this holiness to the other object. So that everything that is exchanged for פירות שביעית receives their state of קדושה. But, like all קדושת דמים, things which are not intrinsically holy, but only for their value, these things are redeemable, and their holiness completely transferred. The קדושה which rests on the פירות שביעית themselves, however, is not mere “holiness for their value”, it is intrinsic, something innate in the objects due to their having been produced in the Sabbath year, they are not redeemable, they are not יוצא לחולין, of them the Torah says: בהויתה יהא ;קדש תהיה; they remain קדש even when, by sale or barter, their קדושה has been transmitted to the other object too (ibid.) This would also be the meaning of the dictum given as Halacha in Succah 41a, that, for a פרי ראשון the actual שביעית-product, transmission of its קדושה to something else is only possible דרך מקח, but not דרך חילול; but for פרי שני, objects which have obtained the status of שביעית by transference, further transference can be made also by חילול. The conception “חילול״ redemption, quite definitely implies that what is redeemed is יוצא לחולין.

לך ולעבדך וגו׳ ולבהמתך וגו׳. In the Sabbath year, the right of private ownership of land is in abeyance. Nothing is considered as growing for the special benefit of the owner of the field. Everything grows for common use, right down for that of animals. No field may be fenced off, men and animals must be given free entry, and no hinderance may be made to their picking or eating. That which the land bears in the Sabbath year is הפקר ownerless property, the owner of the field may only have use of it in participation with all others: לך ולעבדך וגו׳, and he himself may, like everybody else, only take home small quantities at a time for his immediate requirements, והשביעית, it says in Ex. 23,11: תשמטנה ונטשתה ואכלו אביני עמך ויתרם תאכל חית השדה, “in the seventh year thou art to let the land lie fallow, leave it to itself, so that the poor of thy people can eat of it, and that which remains over the animals of the wild are to eat”. (See thereon).
