The owner has not even the right to distribute that which his land produces to the poor of his choice: שלא תאמר מפני מה אמרה תורה לא שיאכלו אותה עניים הרי אני מכניסה ומחלקה לעניים ת״ל והשביעית תשמטנה ונטשתה (Mechilta on Ex. ibid.). לך וגו׳ ולבהמתך ולחיה אשר בארצך: only in common with the animals of the wild are these products to be the disposal of men and domestic animals in the houses; as soon as each kind of produce ceases to be available in the open for animals, the right to keep any of that kind in the houses ceases. אמר קרא ולבהמתך ולחיה אשר בארצך כל זמן שחיה אוכלת מן השדה האכיל לבהמה שבבית כלה לחי אשר בשדה כלה לבהמתך מן הבית, (Pesachim 52b). This particular moment at which פירות שביעית must disappear from the houses which, of course, varies with the different products is called בעוד, and this time of ביעור applies not only to the products themselves, but also to any money for which they have been sold and which accordingly has acquired ,יש להם שביעית ולדמיהן שביעית יש להם ביעור ולדמיהן ;קדושת שביעית ביעור (Sheveith 7,1). The opinions of the commentators differ as to the manner in which this ביעור — this clearing of the products of the Sabbath year, and anything which has acquired that status, out of the houses as soon as there is no more of that particular kind to be found in the open for the animals — is to be carried out. (See Pesachim 52b Rashi and ,תוספות ראב״ד ,ד״ה מתבערין and הל׳ שמטה ,רמב״ם 7; and רמב״ן on our verse).

If we picture to ourselves the carrying out of these שביעית laws, they present to our minds a most wonderful year-long act of homage performed by a whole nation, where every field and orchard, every garden and meadow, every fruit, every blade of grass, is made to proclaim that God, and God alone, is the Lord and Owner of the Land. Dutifully laying the whole territory at His Feet, the inhabitants have to consider themselves as mere גרים and תושבים, as tolerated tenants of the land, and stripped of all haughtiness and pride of possession, retire before God in complete equality and equal rights with the poorest inhabitant and the animals of the wild.

V. 8. וספרת לך in the singular — the Nation as a whole, and, acting as its representative, the Sanhedrin, the ת״כ) ,ב״ד גדול), in contrast to the וספרתם לכם — in the plural — of the counting of the עומר, which is to be done by every individual of the Nation. שבע שבתות שנים: seven year-sabbaths, not seven consecutive years, but שבע שנים שבע פעמים, seven such seven-yearly Sabbath periods as had been ordained in the preceding verses (ת״כ). והיו לך וגו׳ and this period consisting, on the one hand of seven separate past sabbath years, is, on the other hand to be considered as one continuous period of forty nine years. Quite similarly to the עומר counting, which also is to be considered in a double sense, viz. as a counting of seven weekly sabbaths and as a counting of forty nine days to the fiftieth day. (see on Ch. 23,15 & 16). The counting of the עומר is a counting for the individuals, that of the שמטה and יובל a counting for the Nation. The former seeks, by means of a seven times repeated sabbatical acknowledgement of God as the Creator and Lord of the world, to achieve a seven fold working oneself up to moral freedom, rendering oneself fit and worthy to receive the Torah (the שבע שבתות and תשעה וארבעים יום). The latter seeks, by means of a seven times repeated sabbath-year acknowledgement of God as the Lord and Owner of the national land, to achieve a seven fold working the Nation up to a sense of political internal freedom, rendering it fit and worthy for the civil יובל re-birth (שבע שבתות שנים and תשע וארבעים שנה, see vv. 9 & 10). So that the sense of our verse would be:— Thou shalt count unto thyself seven sabbath-years and these seven periods shall, at the same time, form one consecutive period of forty nine years.

V. 9. והעברת שופר תרועה (See on Ch. 23,24). Here again it is ,תקיעה ,תרועה ,תקיעה blown on the שופר. It too, is a call from God (שופר) which invites to תרועה and leads to תקיעה. But it is a שופר call from God which goes forth (והעברת) in His Name from the national representative, the highest court of justice, and then is continued by every one of the people (תעבירו) throughout the land. For it is a call from God throughout the land that calls everybody and everything to Him as their Lord and Owner (תקיעה), bids them undo the shakles of social lack of freedom and inequality (תרועה) into which everybody and everything had become entangled; and so to bring everybody and everything back into the pure and undisturbed social condition (the second תקיעה) which is really what God allots to it as its innate possession.

יום כיפור ;ביום הכפורים תעבירו שופר וגו׳ in each year, the day of moral rebirth, in יובל year becomes at the same time the day of social rebirth for the nation, and on it God’s call to freedom goes forth in the land. It is social כפרה that יובל year is to bring to Israel (see v. 10). At the call of the שופר on י״כ slaves actually go free. But at the entry of the year, on the first of תשרי, God’s holy year makes its effect felt: וקדשתם את שנת החמשים שנה וגו׳ is said in the next verse, the year brings freedom at its entry, although the gift of complete liberation is only granted by יום הכפורים. Just as for the moral rebirth, the first of ר״ה ,תשרי, paves the way for the כפרה which is beckoning from the tenth, so does the sanctifying effect of the יום-כפור-יובל start already at Rosh Hashana: מתקדשת והולכת מתחלתה, “From ראש השנה till יום-כפור״ it says in Rosh Hashana 8b: מד״ה עד יוה״כ לא היו עבדים נפטרים לבתיהן ולא משתעבדין לאדוניהם אלא אוכלים ושותים ושמחין ועטרותיהן בראשיהן כיון שהגיע יה״כ תקעו ב״ד בשופר נפטרו עבדים לבתיהן ושדות חוזרות לבעליהן, “from ראש השנה till יום-כפור the slaves are not yet allowed to go home, but have not to do any service for their masters, but sit, and eat and drink and be merry, and wear crowns on their heads. But as soon as יום-כפור came, the בית-דין had the שופר blown, the slaves were free to go to their own homes and the fields automatically were restored to their original owners”.

V. 10. דרור occures in Is. 61,1 referring to the return of captives, and in Ezekiel 46,17 to the return of landed property to the original owners. As both of these form the most characteristic effect of the יובל, as is evident from the immediately following: ושבתם איש אל אחוזתו ואיש אל משפחתו תשובו, the meaning of the word is sure, but its etymology is more difficult. Apart from this legal meaning in the laws of civil rights, the word occurs as מר דרור (Ex. 30,23), where it means “pure”, pure myrrh, and as the name of a species of birds דרור (Ps. 84,4), by which, as already remarked on Ch. 14,4, a bird is understood which דרה בבית כבשדה, which does not allow itself to be tamed, and makes its nest as freely in human habitation as in the fields or woods. In the legal technology of the Talmud the word דררא occurs: דררא דממונא (Baba Metzia 2,b), and, according to תוספות there it indicates such a situation where, even before any pleading from the parties, the nature of the matter itself presents a legal question which demands the decision of the court: שבלא טענותיהם יש ספק לב״ד וכו׳, שהספק נולד מעצמו. If we take all these meanings of the word together, the fundamental underlying idea of דרור would be “to follow a natural trend”. Hence מר דרור, a material which consists purely of homogeneous particles, and no strange elements are present in it to alter the natural combination of such particles to form the pure material. צפור דרור is the bird which only follows its natural trend, without altering it, or being affected by human proximity. דררא דממונא is a question of law, provoked quite by itself, objectively. ממונא, the legal question would arise by itself, even if none of the parties has posed it. According to this the דרור of our point of law here would be: allowing persons and property to revert to where they naturally tend to belong, persons to the natural nature of a family, property to the original natural order of the right to possess land. In Rosh Hashana 6b, דרור is taken to refer primarily to שילוח עבדים, to the freeing of slaves, and the question: מה לשון דרור, as to how the word דרור is applicable is answered: כמדייר בי דיירא ומוביל סחורה בכל המדינה, and, according to the Aruch, the word דרור here seems to be taken to be connected with דר, which in Talmudic Hebrew has the meaning “to bear”. The root דרא for bearing is quite common in the Talmud. This way of taking it would be based on the idea that the moment יובל is proclaimed every person again becomes the “bearer” of possessions, but, himself, ceases to be any longer a possession. It is the restitution of Man to the rights and the dignity of Man, a poignant description of the restoration of a slave to freedom. Nevertheless this idea is not entirely apt when used for the liberation of an עבד עברי, and it is to such that it is here referring, as a Jew, even as an עבד does not lose the right to have possessions of his own, and the dictum: מה שקנה עבד קנה רבו, only applies to an עבד כנעני, (see משנה למלך on הל׳ עבדים 3,2).

לכל יושביה. We learn from Arachin 32b that the יובל is only effective when בזמן שכל יושביה עליה ולא בזמן שגלו מקצתן, when the whole nation is living in the Land, but not when — as occurred after the expulsion of one third of it by Pul and Tiglath Pilezer (Chron. I 5,26) — a part of it is in exile. More, the tribes as a whole must be living in their old provinces as allotted to them by Josua: בזמן שיושביה כתקונן ולא בזמן שהן מעורבין.

יובל .יובל היא תהיה לכם in the הפעיל means “to bring” and indeed, a suitable bringing, to bring a person to where he is suited to be, or a thing to whom it really belongs: אובילם (Jer. 31,8), or יובל שי (Is 18,6). Hence יבול, the produce of the earth, that which the earth “brings home” to its owner as יובל ;תבואה and יבל canal, aqueduct, by which water is brought there where it is required. Then our יובל is “the bringer”, that which brings men and possessions home to the due place and order to which they really belong. And from that, the horn through which the Shepherd calls His flock home is also called: שופר היובלים (Josh. 6,4 et seq.), or קרן היובל (ibid. 8). Those יובל tones blown on a שופד around the city of Jerico — the first to be taken into possession in the Jewish Land, — were a call to the city, in the name of God, to surrender to, or if you like, to come back to, its rightful owners. The collapse of the walls was the response to this demand (see also Ex. 19,13). In all these places יובל does not designate so much the horn as the home-calling signal. If, as according to Rosh Hashana 26,a, the word יובל also means דכרא the ram, this, too, can be fitted in with the explanation of the underlying etymology of the word which we have given, the איל, the ram, is the leader of the flock, the one who “brings” them to their pasturage, perhaps quite specially, who goes in front, and the flock following him, “brings them home”.

Now it does not say: יובל היא לכם, or: יובל תהיה לכם, but: יובל היא תהיה לכם, and this way of putting it is repeated again twice, in verses 11 & 12. Clearly the year is proclaimed here as having the character of יובל in itself apart from the resulting duties which it imposes on us. The year is a year of restitution and regeneration, a “יובל״ year; therefore we, too, are to celebrate it as such. We dare to believe that this gives the יובל-year a meaning of restitution and regeneration which goes beyond the liberation of slaves and restitution of property which we have to undertake. Just as the כפרה (apart from the סליחה and מחילה which precede it. I.L.), of the yearly יום הכפורים is to bring the moral rebirth of the individual, with all its healing and restoring effect on the internal and external life of the individual, as a miraculous gift (כפרה. I.L.) from the Almighty Grace of God, and this gift of grace brings with it, and is conditional on, the corresponding duties of ענוי and איסור מלאכה, so is the יום הכפורים of the יובל-year at the same time to bring the social and political rebirth of the nation with all its healing and restoring effect on the internal and external relations of the nation, as a miraculous gift from the Almighty Grace of God. All the wrongs and the whole diversity of different classes with its resulting contrasts of opulence and wretchedness, of independence and dependence, which the unequal distribution of wealth have brought to the internal social life of the nation, all the precarious situations unto which the nation has fallen in its political relations to other states, all this, יובל is to wipe out and clear up. The nation is again to be established by the Grace of God, socially healthy, and politically free, even as it was on the first day its national life was started on the basis of God’s laws. It is to progress in this fresh internal and external freedom and independence granted afresh by God, from יובל to יובל, until it reaches the goal where its national life shines forth so brightly amongst the other peoples of the world, that it invites all the nations to throng to it, to learn from it the institutions of God, which alone guarantee justice and freedom and eternal peace on earth (Is. 2,1 et seq. also verses 18 & 19).

But this great national rebirth of the nation, to be obtained from God, must be met on the other side by the two great acts of restitution and regeneration which are in human hands: שמיטת קרקעות and שילוח עבדים, and both not as human-political measures, but proclaimed by תקיעת שופר in the Name of God, as the effect of the justice of His Rule and of His fundamental right of possession . יובל היא תהיה לכם: it is a יובל of God, but it must also be proclaimed by us as such, and its working carried out by us, שמיטת ,שילוח עבדים :שלשתן מעכבת בו קרקעות, and תקיעת שופר (Rosh Hashana 9b). This relation between that which Man has to do in exchange for which he can expect God to grant יובל is expressed by Jeremiah in Ch. 34,17, where he tells of the opposite condition which will result from our non-fulfilment of Man’s part of the לכן כה אמר ד׳ אתם לא שמעתם אלי לקרא דרור איש לאחיו ואיש :יובל לרעהו הנני קורא לכם דרור נאום ד׳ אל החרב אל הדבר ואל הרעב ונתתי אתכם לזעוה לכל ממלכות הארץ, the non-dismissal of the slaves begets the dismissal of the masters by God, i.e. they will be left to themselves, and will no longer find in God a Master Who looks after their interest and protects them from the enemy at their borders. From this it follows that if we do keep the laws of the יובל, we remain in the service of God Who grants us, as His servants, independence, blessing, and protection against the powers of men and nature, against חרב דבר ורעב. Thereby, that — as we believe can be deduced from this — the regenerating effect of יובל goes beyond the restitution of property and freeing of servants which we have to do, and forms national כפרה, a rebirth of the state, which God performs, the meaning of the counting of the seven שמטות as one period of forty nine years leading up to the fiftieth year appears in its true light, as we have already indicated on v. 8. And then, thereby, the connection would also be clear between the institution of יובל and the necessity for the whole nation to be in the land, and living in the origninal division of the tribes in their own special provinces. The Word of God repeatedly calls the settling of Israel in their appointed land a “planting”, and, on Gen. 35,11, we have already remarked what a deep essential relation the characteristic diversity and variety of the twelve tribes — as shown by their ancestor in his farewell blessing, ibid. Ch. XLIX — has to Israel’s mission to the world. Thereby, too, we understand why, guided and directed by God’s intention, the original “planting” of each tribe was made in a separate part of the land alloted to it; and how far from indifferent the presence of the whole nation in the land, and the tribes living in that part of the land which had been directed to it as being suited for the full pure development of its special characteristics, would be for the reaching that ultimate goal of perfection which is to be furthered by each יובל.

With the exile of even only some of the tribes, or if the tribes are intermingled in the land, the importance of the יובל ceases. But as long as the יובל was in force in the land its liberating effects were incumbent on the individual members of the nation who happened to be out of the Land: בזמן שנוהג דרור בארץ נוהג בחוצה לארץ, (Rosh Hashana ibid.).

ושבתם איש אל אחוזתו, see v. 14 et seq. & v. 23 et seq. — ואיש אל משפחתו תשובו, both מוכר עצמו (verses 39 & 40) as well as מכרוהו בית דין, if the יובל occurs before the sixth year, and equally so, the נרצע (Ex. 21,6 & Kiddushin 14b).

Vv. 11 & 12. יובל היא: cf. v. 10. It is a year fixed by God for the regeneration of the state, it is up to you to make yourselves worthy of it by a sevenfold universal national purification, and by the ,תקיעת שופר שמטת קרקעות and שילוח עבדים prescribed in the preceding verse. If, by performing these three מצות of יובל in the name of God, you have done your part of the restitution and regeneration of your country then יובל היא, then it is a year in which God will grant restitution and regeneration, and לא תזרעו וגו׳. Each one has to consider his field as being received afresh from God’s Hand, and to use this consciousness of the country’s internal and political independence belonging to God, and only to be achieved and kept by such consciousness, by celebrating the יובל as a further Sabbath year. Granted possession of land the blessed feeling of freedom and independence which that gives, afresh from God, each person has to proclaim this granting of the conditions of his life by consecrating the soil, its ability to produce and what it produces to God. Hence a Sabbath-year of acknowledgement to God enters with all the agricultural laws and the regulations regarding the produce of the soil of the שמטה-year (see on v. 5). Accordingly every fiftieth year there were two consecutive Sabbath-years, the forty ninth and the fiftieth. In Rosh Hashana 9a there is a difference of opinion between ר׳ יהודה and the רבנן. According to the former: שנת המשים עולה לכאן ולכאן, the fiftieth year, the יובל, is at the same time the first year of the coming שמטה-period. But the רבנן teach: שנת חמשים אתה מונה ואי אתה מונה שנת חמשים ואחת, the יובל year is only to be reckoned as the closing year of the past יובל period, but not, at the same time, as the first of the new period.

V. 13 תשובו איש אל אחזתו, not only that which has been sold, but also which has been given away as a gift, a מתנה. Only possession of land which has been obtained through inheritance, ירושה is permanent. According to ר׳ יוחנן, even an inheritance reverts in יובל. It is regarded as a mutual exchange which is the basic principle of sale, as each heir gives up his claim to the estate for the benefit of the others, in exchange for the part he receives: האחין שחלקו לקוחות הן ומחזירין זה לזה ביובל (Bechoroth 52b). According to the principle of ברירה, i.e. that a decision which occurs later is considered as having actually been made beforehand, and the deciding event, or the choice which is made, only makes it clear to us that which had really been already settled beforehand: הוברר הדבר למפרע, according to this principle every part of an inheritance which comes to each of the heirs, only shows which part of the estate was really his by right of inheritance, and not as the result of any agreement of exchange, and so must be considered as being his inheritance left directly to him from the deceased. Then האחין שחלקו would not be considered as לקוחות but as יורשין, and an inheritance which had been divided amongst the heirs would not be affected by the יובל (Beitza 37b). But according to תוספות (Bechoroth 52b) ר׳ יוחנן is alone in his opinion of considering the heirs as לקוחות, and even those who do not accept the principle of ברירה so that the division of the estate could really be considered on par with the basic principle of sale still maintain that regarding יובל the character of a ירושה is not lost, and so is unaffected by יובל.

V. 14. וכי תמכרו וגו׳. As the whole verse is in the plural: ,תמכרו תונו, the singular suffix ך similar to that in ערכך, (see Ch. XXVII), seems to be part of the noun עמית. From the root עמת, from which we get לעמת opposite, עמית means one who is placed opposite, a relative conception but the designation of the one to whom one is placed opposite is missing. עמיתך, “one who is placed opposite to you” describes in general one’s fellow-men from the point of view of equality of rights. Or the ך is, exactly as in ערכך (see there) in reference to the national whole, and עמיתך is one who is your equal according to national rights. As, further, sale and purchase are given in two separate complete sentences, תמכרו לעמיתך and קנה מיד עמיתך, moreover purchase is expressed aoristically, קנה and so extended quite generally, and the word מיד added which is missing in reference to sale, and this מיד can only literally apply to moveable objects מטלטליו which go concretely “from hand to hand”, דבר הנקנה מיד ליד (Baba Metzia 47b), in contrast to קרקעות, landed property, which is not really “in the hand” of its owner (which is why the possession of land is not expressed in Hebrew by אחז, but always in the passive האחז as a possession which “holds” its possessor, holds him fast to the soil, so that its sale is regarded more as a transference of rights than a transference of an object); according to all this, our וכי תמכרו ממכר would, in the first place, come in connection with the preceding: בשנת היובל הזאת וגו׳, where it is speaking of the return of landed property (which, by the way, in accordance with the idea of יובל given above, is designated not as the return of the property to its original possessor, but as the return of that possessor to his original property) and would come, in first instance, to pave the way for fair dealing in real estate by changing the whole conception of such sale as a result of the institution of אל תונו איש את אחיו :יובל, the general warning against unfair dealing. Then the קנה מיד עמיתך comes to apply at once this warning to the whole of business in general which predominantly consists of the purchase and sale of moveable goods.

Accordingly, the verse here first contains the warning against אונאה, i.e. against “sharp practice” in business, equally for the מוכר, the seller, and the קונה, the buyer. Further, it says in Baba Metzia (ibid.) that the Torah, by separating dealings in landed property from that in moveable goods in this prohibition of אונאה, indicates a difference in the application of אונאה in these two classes of business.

On Ex. 22,20, we have already remarked the phonetic relation of the root ינה with כנע ,כנה and the Talmudic Hebrew גנה, so that the general idea of אונאה is: — the misuse of some weakness in one’s fellow-man to his disadvantage. In commerce it designates using the ignorance of the other party to his disadvantage, and the law differentiates between taking such advantage in the actual object itself and in the value of the object. The first, the objective אונאה comprises every kind of cheating in the quality or quantity of the object of the sale or purchase, even inexactitude במדה במשקל ובמנין in measure, weight or number. The second kind comprises unfairness in price, and it is this which is generally understood in the narrower legal sense by the term אונאה. The prohibition of אונאה extends to any and every kind of taking unfair advantage, and forbids it even in the very smallest quantity in any way whatsoever (see טור ח״מ רכ״ז ה׳ סמ״ע there ס״ק נ״ה). But as far as the effect of אונאה on the validity of the transaction, and on the right to demand repayment of excessive prices paid, the law varies according to the nature of the transaction and of the amount and value of the materials concerned. The first kind, the אונאה, in the object of the transaction, results, in every case and in every kind of material, in the transaction being invalid (ביטול מקח) or at least the right to demand readjustment of the overcharge or underpayment: כל דבר שבמדה ושבמשקל ושבמנין אפילו פחות מכדי אונאה חוזר (Baba Metzia 56b, see רש״י and תוספות there and מ״מ on הל׳ מכירה 15,1).

The second kind, unfairness in price, whether it is the disadvantage of the buyer or seller is divided into three classes: (a) מחילה, abandonment of all claim; (b) קנה ומחזיר אונאה, the transaction is valid but the excess must be repaid or deficit made good; (c) בטול מקח, the transaction is invalid. שתות, if the overcharge or underpayment is not more, not less than one sixth, whether it was made on the price paid or on the asserted value of the goods, then קנה ומחזיר אונאה, the sale is valid but the loser has the right to claim repayment of the difference; פחות משתות, if the amount is less than one sixth of the correct price, no redress can be claimed, מחילה; if it is more than one sixth יתר על שתות, the whole transaction is invalid בטל מקח (Baba Metzia 49b). This law of אונאה that one sixth is the determining amount for the right to reclaim, and more than that renders the transaction invalid only applies to מטלטלין, to transportable goods, but regarding landed property, קרקעות, (and also שטרות ,עבדים and הקדשות), it says: אין אונאה לקרקעות, but according to תוספות (ibid.) 57a), even with קרקעות, if the overcharge or underpayment is half the correct amount, the sale is invalid, ביטול מקח applies. Here, where, as is apparent from the connection with verses 13 & 15 it is referring to making it clear how many years the lease has still to run to the יובל-year, so that it really is a matter of מנין, any misleading statement, in any case would come under the application of the law of אונאה also in the case of landed property.

The form by which מכירה and ןקני sale and purchase, altogether the acquisition and transference of property, can be legally accomplished is also different in the cases of מטלטלין and קרקעות. The legal term usually applied to קרקעות is נכסים שיש להם אחריות and that can give us an indication of their significance in commerce which would explain many of the laws which apply to them. The term tells us that they are a class of property to which is granted an אחריות, a “recovery”. In necessary conditions any of their contemporary owners may have to return them. In commerce they stand “behind” the person and grant him an inalienable guarantee. The latter is the consequence of the former. In contrast, transportable property is called נכסים שאין להם אחריות, moveable goods which can be lost, which give no guarantee. Now we learn from Kiddushin 26a that נכסים שיש להם אחריות נקנין בכסף ובשטר בחזקה שאין להם אחריות אינן נקנין אלא במשיכה, landed property can be acquired by money, by document, or by doing an act showing taking actual possession of the land, i.e. as soon as the owner has accepted money for the land from the buyer, or has given him a bill of sale, or, with the agreement of the owner, the buyer has performed some act showing right of possession — נעל וגדר ופרץ כל שהוא — such as closing in, fencing off, or opening up a recognizable part of the property, the transfer is accomplished (Baba Bathra 42a). But moveable goods can only be acquired by actually taking them physically into one’s own domain — משיכה — or by simply lifting them up off the ground — הגבהה — or where the object is too big and heavy, such as a boat, and, according to some opinions also with animals, by מסירה, i.e. as soon as the sale is made, the buyer, with the knowledge of, or at the request of, the seller, draws the object towards him — מסירה — or where this is not practical, at the request of the seller simply takes hold of it. (Kiddushin ibid. & 25b; Baba Bathra 76a).

But the law that מטלטלין נקנין במשיכה, according to the teaching of ר׳ יוחנן (Baba Metzia 47b), which is accepted as Halacha, is only an institution of the תקנת חכמים ,רבנים, the original law was that the acceptance of money was the only means of transference of goods: דבר תורה מעות קונות ומפני מה אמרו משיכה קונה גזירה שמא יאמר לו נשרפו חטיך בעלייה, “according to the תורה, a deal is completed for moveable goods as soon as the money changes hands, even if the buyer has not touched them and they are still lying in the domain of the seller”. But our sages found it advisable to make the law that the deal is not considered completed until the goods are actually handed over to the buyer, so that the responsibility for care against fire or loss in the interim between purchase and delivery lies entirely with the seller. But ריש לקיש hold the opposite opinion, and takes the term או קנה מיד עמיתך of our text to expressly indicate that משיכה is the means of transfer משיכה מפורשת מן התורה, it obviously means (in his opinion) דבר הנקנה מיד ליד, that the Torah itself says that objects are to be acquired by handing over from the hand of the seller to that of the buyer. But ר׳ יוחנן takes the מיד עמיתך to refer, not to the form of the transfer, but to the nature of the object itself, which must be something that can be had from the “hand” of the owner, can be “handed” by him, is moveable, and by the term, as already remarked, the אונאה law is imposed for מטלטלין with special severity. According to ר׳ יוחנן, the legal form of acquisition by משיכה and הגבהה is מן התורה only applicable to ownerless goods, הזוכה מן ההפקר, or, according to תוספות, to gifts, מתנה, cases where there is no כסף, no compensation to be paid. According to רמב״ן for gifts also, משיכה and הגבהה have no power of legal acquisition, and gifts of moveable goods can only be acquired by חליפין (see below), or in connection with landed property. קנין אגב (see Kiddushin ibid.). (שיטה מקובצת, on Baba Metzia ibid.).

If we go back to the very foundation of all right of possession we can find no other basis for the possession of property than God’s dictum וכבשה (Gen. 1,28) with which He, the original Owner of the World, the real קונה שמים וארץ, set Man on the earth with the order “master it”, i.e. to make it his own by exercising his power over it. So that what a man takes to himself out of the wild, i.e. from a virgin tract that has not yet been appropriated by any other, with the expressed or implied intention to make it his own, that, by the expressed consent of the Original Owner becomes “his”. It must be respected and treated as such, and without his consent can not be transferred into the possession of anybody else. So that for ownerless goods the exercise of force, כבישה just “taking them into possession”, משיכה or הגבהה constitutes a right, they become ones’ property. But even here simple force is not the source of the right; here, too, force is based on this same right, on the declaration of the Will of the Original Owner. So that the conception of “property depends on two factors, the personal factor of the will of the present owner and the owner-to-be, and the factual factor of taking the object into possession consistent with this conception. In the sphere of human commerce too, the transference of goods from hand to hand, would follow the same course, and after the declaration of the consent of the present and the would-be-owner, the transference would be accomplished by the latter taking the goods into his possession. And this is actually the teaching of ריש לקיש that מטלטלין נקנין במשיכה מן התורה. But ר׳ יוחנן teaches that this means of accomplishing the acquisition of property — according to the original law — only applies to the non-Jewish, Noachian world, but for the תורה ideal of life in the Jewish State, acquisition of goods can only be made by כסף (Bechoroth 13b). Unless we are mistaken, the underlying idea of this teaching is to make the sharpest possible distinction between the relation of Man to object in the realm of Nature, and to that in the realm of fair dealing which the relation of man to man imposes. There, where there are no owners and so no personal relations involved, and there alone, force, actual seizing an object is a source of right to it. But here, where goods have already passed into possession they become part and parcel of their possessor, and not even complementarily is actual “grabbing” to be even an additional title to ownership. Between man and man, rights, and rights alone, are to be the source of ownership. Once the right to an object has been acquired, it passes automatically, wherever it happens to be, into the legal possession of the new owner. The right of claim to the object is acquired by its value being accepted from the hands of the new owner, and completely simultaneously, the object passes into his possession: דבר תורה מעות קונות. But for the practical application of this theory in law, the presumption is assumed that the general respect for fair play will assure that while it still remains in the premises of the seller it will receive exactly the same care and protection as the latter’s own goods. Unfortunately the חכמים could not, in general business affairs, depend on such respect, and: גזרה שמא יאמר נשרפו חטיך בעליה, they found it advisable, in Jewish commercial law, to revert back to the Noachian standard and to decree that for מטלטלין only משיכה is קונה. Regarding the standpoint in law and the importance of the תקנות חכמים for which, especially in legal matters regarding property, the law grants wide application (Yebamoth 89b), see Deut. 17,10 & 11. But if, according to ר׳ יוחנן, the original power of the act of taking possession has lost any application as a form by means of which ownership is established in law, nevertheless — even from this point of view — it does retain its effective importance for establishing the permanence of actual possession. (In Law there is a difference between possession and ownership, and the right to possession is a third conception. If I take away your umbrella without leave, you continue to own it although I possess it. You have a right of action against me etc. I.L.). Thus, for instance, in certain circumstances, a temporary impossibility of possession mav, in Law, suspend the right of ownership, e.g. אבדה ששטפה נהר (Baba Metzia 22b), שאבודה ממנו ומכל אדם (see נמוקי יוסף thereon). Thus, in the case of an אבדה, the right of possession of the owner is dependent legally on his still having hopes of recovering it, and in the case of גזלה if יאוש and שנוי רשות have taken place, the right to recover the object itself is lost, and only the right to recover the personal loss (i.e. the value) is permanent. All these are laws, we think, which are based on the constitution of the conception of ownership on the dual factors of personal consent and the act of actually taking possession.

Landed property, נכסים שיש להם אחריות, is not, as we have already remarked, by its nature really “in the possession” of its owners. They do not “grip” it, but are gripped by it. It does not wander from hand to hand, its owners change on it. Its sale, accordingly is more a transference of rights than a transference of objects, and the acquisition of the claim to rights is coincident with the acquisition of the property. Hence in its case everybody agrees that כסף is the real means of קנין. Hence in its case שטר, the handing over of the bill of sale, which is naught but the expression of the transference of rights incorporated in writing, is at the same time considered as a transference of the object itself. For indeed קרקע אינה נגזלת, landed property can not be robbed and always: ברשותא דמרא קיימא, always remains in the sphere of the rights of its owner (Baba Kama 117b and elsewhere). So that in all cases of landed property not only can the acquisition be completed by legal proof of the right having been exercised on it (שטר ראיה), but documentary evidence of the transference of rights (שטר קנין) can by itself be a means of such completion, and with the handing over of such a שטר, at once, without the necessity of any further act, the property passes over to the ownership of the buyer.

But just because קרקע, unlike מטלטלין, can not actually be taken into Man’s power by משיכה and הגבהה, any act of taking it into one’s possession can in no wise and never have the meaning of concretely actually bringing it into one’s power, so that, like moveable goods, exercising one’s power over it could be reckoned as a source of rights to it. In the case of קרקע any such act (e.g. fencing in etc. I.L.), can only be taken to have symbolic meaning, and to be of value as public demonstration of the acquired title to rights. Hence, just as in the case of קרקע, even according to ריש כסף ,לקיש is a means of acquiring property, so is חזקה, also according to ר׳ יוחנן even מן התורה, according to the original law.

There is another symbolic form of acquiring goods (קנין), which applies both to מטלטלין and קרקע, it is that which is described in Ruth 4,7: וזאת לפנים בישראל על הגאולה ועל התמורה לקיים כל דבר שלף איש נעלו ונתן לרעהו התעודה .וזאת התעודה בישראל, a mode of “evidence, announcement” or “giving permanence”. על הגאולה: at “acquiring”, ועל התמורה: at “exchanging”, גאולה זו מכירה תמורה זו חליפין (Baba Metzia 47a), לקיים כל דבר, “to keep something established”. וזאת לפנים: “thus was it ever the way in Israel”, that the one party, according to the accepted Halacha there, the קונה, the buyer, gives his shoe, or any other useful article (כלי) to the other, the מקנה, and as soon as the one who is transferring the property takes the proferred כלי in his hand he is considered as having given over the property in exchange, the transference becomes “firm”, established, מקוים, and the property, wherever it may be, passes into the ownership of the other party. This כלי is a symbolic article of barter, and this mode of קנין is accordingly called קנין חליפין.

Now, although, in Jewish Law a sale is not considered concluded by word of mouth alone, and as long as one of the acts of קנין described above has not been performed, legally, according to the letter of the law, either party can retract from the agreement, nevertheless, even if the business had only been agreed by word of mouth, any going back on it is proclaimed as a most reprehensible breach of faith, as being: דברים יש בהם משום מחוסרי אמונה ואין רוח חכמים נוחה הימנו. And if, in addition to the verbal agreement, a deposit of money has been made, or the buyer has put a mark on the goods, although legally the deal is not concluded thereby, and strictly speaking, it could be called off, if complaint is made to the court, the דיינים there have to warn the one who has gone back on his word with the solemn admoition: מי שפרע מאנשי דור המבול ומאנשי דור הפלגה ומאנשי סדום ועמורה וממצרים שטבעו בים הוא יפרע ממי שאינו עומד בדבורו, “He Who brought punishment on the generation of the flood, on that of the Tower of Babel, on the people of Sodom and Gemorrah, on the Egyptians who were drowned in the sea, He will bring punishment on anybody who goes back on his word”. (Baba Metzia 48a & 49a). This being placed under God’s punishment is expressed by the term: מקבל מי שפרע.

We remark, in parenthesis, that in many instances Jewish Law, civil law, dealing with matters between man and man, differentiates sharply between that which satisfies the strict letter of the law and the moral obligations which its spirit demands. There are quite a number of things which the former can not disallow, but which are definitely reprehensible from the point of view of the higher moral obligations, אין רוח חכמים נוחה הימנו.

Vv. 15 & 16. The prohibition of אל תונו, of the preceding verse applied to the effect of יובל on the sale of landed property makes it incumbent on both buyer and seller to keep in mind the different meaning of the words “sale” and “purchase” when referred to landed property, so that with each year of a יובל-period the value of such property diminishes. For whereas sale and purchase of moveable goods mean a permanent and complete sale and purchase, both are only temporary when they apply to landed property. There, the transaction is only of temporary duration, and, altogether, it is only the use of the land and not the land itself, which is really transferred, קנין שדה לפירות (Gittin 48a). It even remains doubtful whether the buyer has the right to make any permanent alteration to the property, whether he may make caves or dig pits etc., חפירות בורות שיחין ומערות, (see מ״מ on הל׳ שמיטה ויובל, 11, 1). As the ownership of all purchased land reverts to the original owner in the יובל-year, the value of such land obviously depends on the number of years during which the purchaser has the use of it. All this has to be clear in the minds of the parties if each of them is to act fairly towards the other. As the fairness of the deal in this respect depends on the buyer knowing the longer or shorter period during which he will have the use of the property for which he is paying, the text explains the fairness which both parties have to observe in the address to the buyer: במספר שנים אחר היובל וגו׳, “according to the number of years that have passed since the last יובל shalt thou buy”, i.e. the buyer must be aware of how many years have already passed since the יובל, so that he knows for how many years of the forty-nine years “lease” he has no benefit:; and במספר שני תבואות ימכר לד, “according to the number of years of produce shall he sell to you”, i.e. the seller must be aware of how many years of bnenfit he is transferring to the buyer. Only if both of them know, if the buyer knows what he is not getting and the seller knows what he is giving up, is the transaction free from deceit, is there no אונאה. (It has already been remarked on the previous verse that אונאה במדה במשקל ובמנין, does also apply to קרקעות).

לפי רוב השנים וגו׳, only describes the effect that this consciousness of the number of the years of the יובל period that have passed and which are still to come has on the sale price of the field. כי מספר תבואת הוא מוכר לך, what lies at the base of all this is, that the effect of the יובל is that it is not the field itself that is sold but only the use of it, its produce. This raises the question as to whether קנין הפירות כקנין הגוף דמי, whether one who has acquired all the rights to use an object just as he pleases can be considered the owner of it, and e.g. whether, when he has to bring the first fruits as ביכורים from such a purchased field he can make the prescribed acknowledgement: הבאתי את ראשית פרי האדמה אשר נתת לי (Deut. 26,10), whether מביא וקורא or מביא ואינו קורא (Gittin 48a).

The law is further laid down by: במספר שני תבואות ימכר לך, (Arachin 29b), that although fields may be sold at any time, close to, or afar off the Youvel סמוך ליובל or מופלג מן היובל, nevertheless is must be sold for a plurality (שני תבואות) of years, i.e. for at least two years, so that before the lapse of two years it can not, and may not, — in accordance with v. 27 — be redeemed, and both buyer and seller transgress a command, are עובר בעשה, if they carry out such a transaction. Accordingly, if a field is sold one year before the יובל, it remains in the possession of the buyer for one year after the יובל, and only then does the יובל take effect and the field revert. A year of general failure of harvests, or a שמטה-year does not count. The buyer must have the land in his possession for two שני תבואות years of produce. Land which is not fertile, can not be used for agricultural purposes, טרשין, can be redeemed immediately (ibid 14b). A sale made in יובל year itself is invalid (ibid 29b).

These שתי שנים שבשדה אחוזה are reckoned from day to day, two full years, and are שני תבואות, not תבואות, are harvest years, not harvests, there may be three harvests in two years, if e.g. the sale took place in harvest time before it had been cut, פעמים שאדם אוכל שלש תבואות בשתי שנים. In the same way as these two years are reckoned, so is the one year for house-sales in walled cities, (v. 29), the years for sacrificial animals (XII,6) the six years for Jewish slaves, (Ex. 21,2) for personal valuation, (Levit. XXVII) for the ages of maturity, and other years which decide the legal qualifications for various matters for both sexes, to be reckoned, שנה האמורה בקדשים שנה האמורה בבתי ערי חומה שתי שנים שבשדי אחוזה ושש שנים שבעבד עברי וכן שבבן ושבבת כולן מעת לעת, more, the years of the sacrificial animals and of the houses in walled cities are actually reckoned from hour to hour, שעות פוסלות בקדשים and בבתי ערי חומה (Arachin 18b תוספות there and 31a), whereas for other matters, such as מעשר בהמה, for ערלה, for מעשר דגן וירקות, the year is reckoned from the last day of אלול of any year (Rosh Hashana 2a & 8a).

V. 17. ולא תונו וגו׳, extends the prohibition of אונאה which has just been given for business dealings to general social intercourse, not even by words to take advantage of one’s position to hurt or to mislead one’s fellow men. This prohibition of אונאת דברים embraces (Baba Metzia 58b et seq.) any and every kind of hurting the feeling of others by words, making reference to the shady past of somebody, or to that of his parents; זכור מעשי אבותיך ,זכור מעשיך הראשונים, like Job’s comforters, making aggravating reproaches in times of trouble: זכור נא מי הוא נקי אבד (“Remember, I pray thee, who ever perished, being innocent” I.L.); putting to shame in public: מלבין פני חברו ברבים; calling somebody by jeering names מכנה שם רע לחברו; but especially hurting somebody by words in such a way that only God can see the evil intent: דבר מסור ללב, on which it quite specially says: ויראת מאלקיך such as giving bad, or even only teasing advice: אם היו המרים מבקשים תבואה ממנו לא יאמר להם לכו אצל פלוני שהוא מוכר תבואה ויודע בו שלא מכר לעולם; more, even capriciously arousing false hopes in somebody, such as asking the price of an article which you have no intention of buying: לא יאמר לו בכמה חפץ זה והוא אינו רוצה ליקח. All these and similar hurting the feelings of others by words have this in common with the sin of אונאה in business affairs, that it is misusing or taking advantage of some weak spot in somebody else, there, his lack of knowledge of the wares, here the susceptibility of his feelings. And the Law condemns even much more severly, and considers even more punishable, this אונאת דברים than it does אונאת ממון, and remarks: זה בגופו וזה בממונו, the one effects body and soul, the other merely money, זה ניתן להישבון וזה לא ניתן להישבון, the one can be made good, repaid, but not the other. כל המלבין פני חברו ברבים כאילו שופך דמים “he who puts his fellowman to shame in public is as if he commits a murder”, and כל היורדין לגיהנם עולים חוץ ג׳ שיורדין ואינן עולין ואלו הן הבא על אשת איש והמלבין פני חברו ברבים והמכנה שם רע לחברו: every sinner has a chance to come back up out of Gehenna except three, one who has committed adultery with another man’s wife, one who has put his neighbour to shame in public, and one who has attached a jeering name to his neighbour.

ולא תונו וגו׳ ויראת וגו׳ כי וגו׳ אלקיכם, The admonition addresses all members of the nation together and says: they are not to hurt one another in any way, each one is to fear his God, is to know that God has His Eye and His Ear directed to each one of them, and also that He is equally the God of each of his brethren. Thereby is described what is to be the direct result of the institution of שמטה and יבל for the whole social life of the people in the Land. Inasmuch as these institutions interweave the thought “God” into all business transactions, and inasmuch as they bring the thought continually to mind that all are living together on the same soil of God, in the same Land of God, where He is the Master and Owner of all possessions, and that in the exercise of this ownership He demands the tribute of acknowledging Him in the whole of business life: these institutions immediately beget the twin thought of these thoughts, viz. that the whole of one’s life takes place under God’s Eye, that God is present not only in the Temple but in the midst of all intercourse between people, that He only bears and blesses this intercourse and each individual of it in His Land if the intercourse tends to the happiness of all, where none hurts the other, no one misuses the position he may have won, or the breath he draws, in the Land of God, to the loss or mortification of others, and interweaves into every phase of private and public life that fudamental truth of all truths, with all its consequences, that אני ה׳ אלקיכם.

Vv. 18 & 19. The previous verse expressed the immediate result of the institution of שמטה and יובל as the basis for business life being the nuturing of the thought of everything belonging to God, throughout the life of intercourse between man and man. In this verse the thought is given its practical application to the whole individual and national life of the people. The Word of God knows only one means of acknowledging God, and that is, faithfully carrying out His Will. And so, too, only at one price is His Land ours, and that is by faithfully carrying out His Torah. If we pay this tribute then we have done all we have to do to keep the land for us and us in the land. The recognition and fulfilment of this Torah is our rampart and our wall, our science and our art, our policy and economy. Everything for which nations strive in vain in a thousand others ways, political security abroad, general welfare and prosperity at home, we obtain simply and surely by keeping this Torah. Its Lawgiver, the Lord of our Land, is at the same time Director of the fate of nations and of the development of nature; just as our Land, so is the path of fate and nature “His”, and “He” has undertaken the defence and the prosperity of our Land if we take “care of and fulfill” His “Laws” and “social rules”. תשמרו, “take care of”, by constant learning and by protecting ourselves from erring; ועשיתם by carrying them out in the whole of our individual, family and national lives (See on Ch. 18,5. הקים are the moral limitations to our individual and family life, משפטים, the rules regulating our social and business lives. The former are the prerequisites for the latter, both together form the purpose for which God gave us “His” Land).

וישבתם על הארץ לבטח is the assurance of political security abroad, וישבתם לבטח עליה, the certainty of physical development of prosperity at home. בטח: our ישיבה itself, the way we live and dwell will give us this certainty, will have the effect that we require neither means of defence against enemies nor measures of security against failure of crops. Equally so ואכלתם לשבע, the way we eat, the precautions we take with our food, will bring about the blessing of plenty. Both, provided we allow our ישיבה and our אכילה to be regulated and ruled by the משפטים and עליה ,על הארץ .חקים: the Land will “bear” us in contrast to the תקיא הארץ את יושביה (Ch. 18,25).

V. 20—22. This special care of God for the Land of His Torah will show itself in the yearly success of your agricultural labour. Just as at the first establishment of the weekly Sabbath, the לחם משנה, the gift of a double portion of manna each sixth day, announced the sanctity of the seventh, and at the same time guaranteed that God’s providence would see to it that nobody would suffer by the cessation of all work on the Sabbath day, so will the double harvest in each sixth year announce beforehand the sanctity of the seventh, and guarantee that God’s providence would see to it that nobody suffered by the cessation of all work in the fields in the Sabbath-year. As our years begin with the harvest, which begins in ניסן but only finish in תשרי, each normal year provides a part of the yearly requirements of that year and the principle part of the requirements of the following year. But each sixth year will provide the partial requirement of the sixth, the whole requirements of the seventh and the principle requirements of the eighth year, as the principle harvest of the eighth goes to the benefit of the ninth year. So that the real worry should have been expressed for the eighth year, for the principle needs of the seventh year would be covered by the harvests of the sixth year. And for this reason רמב״ן in his commentary explains the words וכי תאמרו וגו׳ to be taken in the sense of their meaning: וכי תאמרו בשנה השביעית מה נאכל בשמינית. But the accentuation speaks against this way of taking it. Perhaps this מה נאכל expresses more the worry that in the seventh year one would not dare to eat anything for fear that there would be nothing to eat in the eighth year if no harvest was to be made and stored in the seventh. For in other years while one lived on the produce of the previous year the field work went on to make provision for the next one. But in the seventh year nothing was sown and what grew by itself was not allowed to be stored, but during the course of the year had to be cleared out and enjoyed (ביעור). Without some special provision by God, there would not only be nothing to eat in the eighth year, but the prospect of the lack of bread in the coming year would make people afraid to satisfy their hunger in the seventh year too. לִשְׁלשׁ הַשָׁנִים not לְשָׁלשׁ שׁנים, which would imply three harvests, but one harvest which would be plentiful enough to last for the three years which had to participate in the harvest of the sixth year. It would have to suffice for the necessary part of the sixth — as explained above — the whole of the requirements of the seventh, and the greater part of the eighth. Altogether this would amount to the full requirements of two years. In the יובל-year, when the land had to lie fallow for two consecutive years, the forty ninth and the fiftieth, the forty eighth year had to provide for four years with one threefold harvest.

Vv. 23 &24. צמת .לצמתת, the meaning of which as having a destructive life-killing effect is clear from many instances, occurs in Job 6,17 referring to the parched wanderer in the desert ultimately reaching water which should be flowing only to find it a frozen solid mass: בעת יזורבו נצמתו. This becoming stiff, i.e. not killing life but movement seems to be the real meaning of צמת. Thus in Rabbinic-Hebrew it designates contraction, becoming stiff, hard by “congealing”, cauterising, the stiffening of limbs, the drawing together of the edges of a wound etc. It is phonetically related to צמד which, indeed, also means a firm joining together. Also חלט, the root of הלוטין, the Chaldean translation of צמיתות is a synonymous designation of the stiffening, hardening effect of congealing, similar to צמת (see Chulin 111a חלטי ליה בחלא). So that צמתות is a very apt expression for an irrevocable permanent transition of property into the possession of somebody else. There it crystalises, loses all movement, becomes fixed, grows permanently together to the new owner. This is what it is not to do. God has granted nobody such a right of disposition of “His” Land which even in our hands remains “His”. The division which took place when we first obtained possession of the Land, was, by Gods command, made according to tribe and family, which was to continue by the right of heritage, equally ordained by God, and this division is not to suffer a permanent change which “fixes” it for all time. Every change of the possession of landed property, except by means of inheritance is to remain fluid. Sale or gift revert automatically at the יובל. More, even before the גאולה תתנו לארץ ,יובל, the right to redeem it back remains to the seller. After two years of the new possession (see v. 15 above) the seller, or one of his relatives, — in accordance with the method of discharging the obligations laid down in the succeeding verses — has the irrefutable right at any time, to buy the property back. So that not even up to the יובל is the conversion of a purchased field “fixed”. It always remained “fluid”, and at any moment, after two years, it can “flow back” to the original owner. This institution of גאולה, which is further developed in the following verses, is indeed the most important and farthest-reaching stipulation of the יובל laws (see below). In Baba Metzia 79a: והארץ לא תמכר לצמיתות, is taken to be the explanatory and restrictive motive of the יובל laws. The reversion powers of יובל shall have the effect that no field can be sold לצמיתות, for ever. Every field, whether it was implied or expressly stated that its sale was for permanence, nevertheless reverts in יובל. On the other hand: מכר שדהו לששים שנה אינה חוזרת ביובל, if a man sells his field for a fixed term of years, e.g. for sixty years, so that it is not לצמיתות, it does not revert in יובל, but only at the end of the term. Nevertheless this apparent means of getting round the law of the יובל (as for instance giving a “lease” of 999 or even 9999 years), is not to be taken as permission to do so. Such permission would be against the positive injunction given in v. 10: יובל היא תהיה לכם ושבתם איש אל אחוזתו. The limitation given by: והארץ לא תמכר לצמיתות (i.e. as long as it is not לצמיתות, for ever. I.L.), only gives the possibility of extending the sale over the יובל and not invalidating such sale in quite exceptional circumstances, in order to try and keep a property for the owner which otherwise would be entirely and permanently lost to him, קא כליא קרנא, as in the case instanced in Baba Metzia 79a. More, we are very inclined to believe that the whole saying of ר׳ קטינא was only meant to be an academic, merely logical, point of law, and not at all meant to be a legal permission for practical application. He did not say: מוכר אדם שדהו לס׳ שנה ואינה חוזרת ביובל, but: מנין למוכר וכו׳ שאינה חוזרת וכו׳, clearly a דיעבד-construction and not a לכתחלה-sentence. The discussion there too would probably have opposed it, if its application to the problem under discussion had not been altogether refuted as having no bearing on it, סוף סוף לכי מטו וכו׳. But in any case even in a sale which did extend beyond the יובל, the גאולה-right would still be in force, and at any time after two years the means of redemption would always be there.

V. 25. מוך :כי ימוך and מכך phonetically related to: ,מיי ,מגג ,מוג מקק, designate the condition of becoming soft and liquid, dissolution. Applied to pecuniary circumstances it describes a dwindling fortune; thereby social power and influence “melt away”. כי ימוך ומכר: Landed estate may never be sold as a speculation, or for considerations of utility, but only and solely from necessity, poverty. אין אדם רשאי למכור את שדהו ולהניח באפונדתו וליקח לו בהמה וליקח לו כלים וליקח לו בית אינו מוכר אלא א״כ העני, “a man is not allowed to sell his field to keep the money, or to buy animals, vessels or a house, but only if he has become impoverished (ת״כ). Rambam (הל׳ שמטה ויובל 11,3), specialises even farther: אינו רשאי אלא למזונות בלבד, it is only allowed for obtaining food. If nevertheless the sale has been made for any reasons whatsoever it is legally valid. — ולא כל אחוזתו :מאחוזתו, even when necessitous he should not sell the whole of his land, but only part of it (ובא גואלו הקרוב אליו .(ת״כ, the heir who is the nearest relative has the prior right, קרוב קרוב קודם (Kiddushin 21a). — וגאל את ממכר, according to the accepted Halacha (ibid.) this is only a right, רשות, but not an absolute duty, חובה.

V. 26. שיש לו ואינו רוצה ליקח :ואיש כי לא יהיה לו גואל (ibid.), he has relatives (every Jew must have. I.L.), but none who are willing to be a גואל to buy the field back for him. — יד עצמו שלא ילוה ויגאל :והשיגה ידו, the seller has only the right to buy it back, if he has acquired the necesary means, but not if he borrows the money for it. למצוי שלא ימכר ברחוק :ומצא ויגאל בקרוב ברע ויגאל ביפה, his circumstances must really have changed, but selling some of his other fields which are not so good, or which lie in a more inconvenient position, does not give him the right to redeem a field which he has sold.
כדי גאולה הוא גואל ואינו גואל לחצאין :כדי גאולתו, he has only the right to redeem what he has sold, when he can pay for it fully, but not if he can only pay for it at a time (Arachin 30b).

V. 27. וחשב וגו, the money paid at the sale is to be considered as the purchase price for the use of the field for the years until the יובל. So that the redemption amount is reckoned by deducting the proportionate amount for the years passed since the sale, והעודף, and the remainder is what has to be paid. לאיש אשר מכר לו: If the first buyer has sold it to another at a higher price, it is redeemed by paying back to the first buyer at the rate paid by him, but if it was resold at a lower price it can be redeemed by paying this second buyer at the lower rate. In a quite similar manner the option of redemption is made easy if the value of the field has risen or fallen. In the first case it can be redeemed at the sale price, in the second at its present price, ידו על העליונה, “he always has the upper hand”, i.e. he can always choose the more advantageous terms (Arachin 30a).

V. 29. בית מושב עיר חומה, it does not say: בית עיר חומה, nor בית בעיר חומה, but: בית מושב עיר חומה, a house that belongs to the “occupation of a walled city”. Arachin 36b takes this to specify. ,שהוקף ולבסוף ישב ולא שישב ולבסוף הוקף, i.e. that the city was first walled in, and then by building houses became a place of residence. But if the houses were there before there was a city wall, they have not got the legal status of בתי ערי חומה spoken of here. והיתה גאולתו וגו׳: the laws regarding the sale of בתי ערי חומה, are totally different from those regulating אחוזה. Whereas the former can only be redeemed after the buyer has enjoyed two years of the harvests, and בגירעון, with deduction for each year so enjoyed, and redemption can be made any time from then on until יובל, and, if not redeemed before, reverts at the בית בבתי ערי חומה ;יובל can be redeemed immediately and at any time during the first year, but only during the first year and without any deduction, גואל מיד וגואל כל י״ב חדש, but if it is not redeemed in that year it remains the permanent property of the buyer, and does not revert in יובל (ibid. 31a). But it can only be redeemed by the seller himself, or after his death by his heirs, but not, like שדה אחוזה, by relatives (ibid, and Kiddushin 21a). עד תם שנת ממכרו, the year is reckoned from the date of the sale, and not שנה של מנין עולם, not the year which ends in ימים תהיה .אלול גאולתו, it is counted from day to day, מיום ליום, even, as already remarked on v. 16, מעת לעת, from hour to hour (Arachin 31a).

V. 30. שנה תמימה; in a leap year, the extra month, חודש העיבור, reckons to the benefit of the seller. אשר לו חומה, the written form is לא (the כתיב) from which is taught (in Arachin 32a) אע״פ שאין לו עכשיו והיה לו קודם לכן, although now it has no walls (כתיב לא), but it is known by tradition that it was built as a walled city originally (קרי לו). For this purpose, the status of a city is taken from the character it bore at the time Joshua took it into possession. Those cities that were מוקפות חומה מימות יהושע בן נון, that were walled at that time, retained that status, but those that were then open cities at the time of the conquest, are still considered as such, even if they were walled-in later on, as are also all cities that were built later than that period (ibid.).

V. 31. חצרים .ובתי החצדים וגו׳ are villages and open cities, in contrast to closed-in walled cities. As the word חצר designates a surrounding space, an accessory space, it is doubtful whether villages, open cities, are called הצרים, because there, each house is surrounded by its field, its “yard”, from which it gets all the necessary requirements for living, or because these villages and open country hamlets are considered as חצרים of the large strong cities whose necessities they supply. The repeated juxtaposition of ערים וחצריהם in Joshua Ch. XIV speaks for the latter (cf. Gen. 25,16). על שדה הארץ יחשב גאולה תהיה לו וביובל יצא: These בתי החצרים have the double prerogative, על שדה הארץ יחשב, they are like שדה אחוזה and revert automatically in יובל, or can be redeemed before with deduction for the years the buyer has had them, יוצאין ביובל ובגדעון כסף, and גאולה תהיה לו, like בתי ערי חומה, they can be redeemed at once, even in the first year, and do not have to wait two years like שדה אחוזה (Arachin 33a). The singular לו and יצא seems to refer to the word שדה which the בתי החצרים are considered to be.

Vv. 32 & 33. וערי הלוים וגו׳ refers to the forty eight cities which were to be given to the Levites, of which six were ערי מקלט (Numb. Ch. XXXV). גאולת עולם וגו׳, their cities and the fields which belong to them can be redeemed for an unlimited period, and this right is attached not to the person but to the city. Even if such a house or field has passed out of Levite hands, by inheritance, ישראל שירש אבי אמו לוי, the right of redemption remains for all times; and the house of a Levite, if sold, can always be redeemed, not only from the possession of a non-Levite, but also ואשר יגאל מן הלוים even if the buyer himself was a Levite. ויצא וגו׳, and, if it is not redeemed, in any case it reverts in the יובל (Arachin 33b). כי בתי וגו׳. The cities of the Levites and the land as far as the domain of the city extended, was the only landed possession given to the tribe of Levi at the distribution of the Land. Hence these cities and that land, were, like the שדה אחוזה of the other tribes, to be kept for the Levites under all circumstance.

V. 34. ושדה מגרש עריהם. The cities which, in accordance with Numb. Ch. XXXV, were to be given to the Levites, extended, as ordained in v. 5 there, 2,000 cubits in every direction, of which the inner 1,000 cubits according to v. 4 were called מגרש העיר. This “common”, the immediate surround of the city was an open space reserved לבהמתם ולרכושם ולכל חיתם, for the animals, moveable possessions and for the other amenities of the lives of the citizens, e.g. כביסה public laundries (Nedarim 81a). The outer 1,000 cubits (according to Rambam הל׳ שמטה ויובל XIII,2, 2,000 cubits), were fields and vineyards (Sota 27b). So that the whole domain of a city consisted of מגרש ,עיר and שדה. Now here it says: ושדה מגרש עריהם לא ימכר. This can not wish to altogether prohibit the sale, even temporarily, for גאולת עולם וגו׳ (v. 32), obviously presupposes the sale of landed property of the Levites. Equally so it can not come to prohibit or invalidate the permanent sale of such property, as its reversion in יובל has already been pronounced in v. 33 for both בית and עיר, and as בית is mentioned separately עיר can only refer to the whole extent of the city. Hence in Arachin 33b it says that these words are meant to be taken as extending the prohibition in the widest sense: — not only is the property not to be estranged from its original owner but also not from its original status: מאי לא ימכר לא ישנה, the field may not be converted to a מגרש, to a free open space; the common, not, by being ploughed and sown, into a field (Baba Bathra 24b) or by being built on, into the city, and equally so, not the city into a field or open space: אין עושין שדה מגרש ולא מגרש שדה ולא מגרש עיר ולא עיר מגרש, (Arachin 33b), כי אחוזת עולם הוא להם, becouse it was given to them as their possession for all time, therefore at no particular contemporary time has anyone the right to make any alteration to it. No present moment has the sole disposition of it, all future times have equal claim to it, and in the same condition that it has been received from the past is to be handed on to the future.

But that which is here said for the Levites regarding their cities applies for the whole nation to the Land of Israel. To it, too, the Land was given as אחוזת עולם, for all future generations, and also בערי ישראל no contemporary generation may change שדה into מגרש, nor מגרש into ,שדה מגרש into עיר, or עיר into מגרש (ibid.) and according to מל״מ פ״א מהלכות שמטה ויובל, this applies not only to ערי חומה but to every city in Israel.

מגרש: just as ירש has both the meaning of driving out of possession and of taking into possession, so does גרש in מגרש seem to designate the space surrounding a town as being such that, though not built on, and not lived on, still belongs to the town, and from which the town has the right to expel any unauthorised person.

We have already indicated — on verses 9, 10, 18 & 19, — the deep meaning of the whole institution of יובל as a national יום-כפור, as the restorer and regenerator of the social and political life of the nation; and how the Torah itself has shown, in the prohibitions of אונאה in verses 15—17, how the thought of God being the Ruler of “Land and People” which יובל interweaves into the general business life, has the result of bringing conscientiousness and respect for the rights of others and the well-being of others into all deeds and words.

Let us indicate a few more of the most striking effects which the laws of יובל must have had on the internal economy of Jewish national life. That, by the periodical reversion of the sale of all landed property, the original division of the land to tribes and families — which was to be such an important factor for the whole material and spiritual development of Israel — remained intact, is obvious. The future law given in v. 34 that אין עושין שדה מגרש וכו׳, as well as the differentiation between בתי הצרים and בתי ערי חומה as well as the limitation of these latter to מוקפות חומה מימות יהושע בן נון stabilises this division still more in a direction which seems to us to be of no small importance in influencing the general trend of development of the national character and the national life. That is, the relation of town to country. For clearly these laws establish the greatest possible upkeep of an “urban population occupied with agriculture” as the predominant fuadmental characteristic type of the Nation. It places an obstacle to the growth of large cities at the expense of the surrounding country which otherwise is so very prevalent. Not even the open spaces of the city, or any part of it, may be used as building sites. If the population of a city grows too dense, new cities must be founded on sites which have not been used for agricultural purposes, such as, for example, Joshua (Ch. 17,15—18) recommends the sons of Joseph to found new cities in the clearings of the mountain forests. Further, by the law that the houses in the country towns. בתי חצרים, were protected, like the land itself, from permanent sale, and in יובל reverted to the original owners or their heirs, provision was made, that, on the whole, town and land remained in connection as family property; so that, as a rule, every field and every vineyard would have as its proprietor a householder in the neighbouring town. Hence it is town-bred intelligence and culture combined with the natural and uncomplicated outlook of life fostered by living in close contact with nature which is the effect which this great penetrating statute tends to produce as the predominating characteristic of the inhabitants of Israel. Only walled cities were detached from the land. In them house property could be transferred permanently to other owners. There a population could develop which was unconnected with agricultural work, and had to find their means of living by trade and industry. But as this character was limited to just such cities which had been walled-in and separated from the land already before its inhabitants had settled in it, הוקף ולבסוף ישב, but where it had originally been an open city, ישב ולבסוף הוקף, the fact that later it had been surrounded by walls does not make it entirely lose that character; and moreover as only if they had been already walled off from the land from the time of Joshua, בתי ערי חומה, were differentiated from שדה אחוזה: a city life cutting itself off, and being cut off, from agriculture was altogether rigidly limited to a fixed number of points in the land, which number could in no wise be increased. But a state whose inhabitants are primarily grouped and kept in medium-sized country towns is equally protected against the contrasted luxury and proletariat of great cities, and the peasantry and dullness of “clod-hoppers”.

No less striking is the effect which the automatic reversion in the יובל of all landed property to the original owners or their heirs, must have in the prevention of complete permanent poverty of some families by the side of overpowering accumulation of property in the hands of a few. Never can a clique of so called great landowners build itself up in the midst of a landless, and therefore dependent, pauperism when every fiftieth year the whole land reverts to its original division, and the richest goes back to the original acres of his heritage, and the poorest is given back the acres of his. But even temporary impoverishment is protected against misusage by the avarice of the wealthy, by the Torah’s great institution of גאולה. Never can impoverished owners of land fall a prey to those who would use the need of the poor to speculate in real estate, where after two years, the seller or his relative, has the right to buy it back by repaying only the amount paid for it, and even deducting the value of the years it was in the possession of the buyer. The cheaper the buyer of a property has bought it the less can he be sure of being able to keep it, the easier will it be for the seller to afford the sum necessary for its redemption, or for his relative to decide to redeem it. If a rich man really would like to have the field for as long as possible he would have to be careful not to bargain for the very lowest price, as it is only a high price which would render redemption difficult.

On the other hand the Law takes precautions against fields and houses being used as means for being converted into temporary cash. Inasmuch as in general it gives no approval or assistance to the sale of real estate, and only seems to consider such sale justified in cases of dire necessity (כי ימוך), one who is hard up will not decide quickly or carelessly to sell his heritage, which can only get back after two years, and only if his circumstances have really improved. And if he has sold it, it is only by increased diligence and doubled activity that he can soon regain possession of the property he has sold, as he can not redeem it with borrowed money nor by the sale of other property, nor can he redeem it gradually in parts, but only has the right of redemption with freshly earned income, and by rebuying the whole field. לא ימכור ברחוק ויגאל בקרוב ברעה ויגאל ביפה ולא ילוה ולא יגאל לחצאין.

It is characteristic, that the Law leaves the legal possibility of the reverse open, and recognises the validity of a sale made not out of necessity, in the same way as we saw, it affirms the legal possibility of a sale lasting beyond the יובל. The Torah is satisfied simply to indicate its disapproval, and to depend on the self-judging conscientiousness of the people, as well as the public opinion which is formed by it, to be strong enough to achieve the realisation of its institutions on the whole. But it leaves the possibility of exceptional behaviour for the great diversity of conditions which may arise in private family life, which behaviour will find its surest control in the critical judgement of public opinion.

We are not quite clear about meaning of the redemption by relatives. Primarily it seems to be exercised in the interest of the relative himself, or in the general interest of the family, that the property should not remain even temporarily out of the hands of the family. No direct benefit seems to accrue to the original seller from such a redemption. Nevertheless the relative is called his גואל, which implies that some relief, some benefit, some salvation from his condition of need is brought to him by the relative redeeming his property. Perhaps the generally accepted custom went beyond the mere legal demand, as indeed we see from Ruth, IV,5, that, combined with the right to redeem the field of a deceased relative, custom added the duty of caring for, and marrying the widow who was left alone.

V. 35. וכי ימוך .וכי ימוך אחיך ומטה ידו עמך, see v. 25. — ומטה ידו. The verb מוט to totter, to be about to fall, does not occur elsewhere applied to יד, but only to רגל or to the general condition. Were it to say here ומט עמך or ומטה רגלו עמך, it would designate the case to be where the condition is such that his existence is already threatened, and the assistance which is to be granted is to sustain his very existence. But ומטה ידו expresses his “hand” having become shaky, it is only his activity which is tottering. Not yet the means of existence, but the means for actively gaining his livelihood begin to fail, assistance would enable him to continue independently gaining his living. ידו עמך: up till now his “יד״, his power to work was עמך, “with you”, he was your equal in being able to carry on working: והחזקת בו, therein, “בו״ shalt thou keep him, strengthen him to keep “בו״. Hence the explanation of ת״כ on our verse: אל תניחהו שירד הא למה זה דומה למשוי על גבי החמור עודנו במקומו אחד תופש בו ומעמידו נפל לארץ חמשה אין מעמידין אותו, “Do not let him get right down! It is like the load on an animal’s back, as long as it is still up there, a single person need only give it a hand and it keeps up, but once it has fallen to the ground, five people are not sufficient to restore it”. ומניין אם החזקת אפי׳ ארבעה חמשה פעמים חזור והחזק ת״ל והחזקת בו יכול אפי׳ אתה מפסידו לתרבות רעה ת״ל עמך, “and even if you have already given assistance four or five times, you must help him again and again for it says “והחזקת בו״ (You are to make him strong and “firm”, and as long as he totters again you have not made him “firm”). “But not so that you reduce him to a condition of sloth and loss of self respect, for it says עמך, (and according to the sense of the sentence this עמך also refers back to והחזקת בו עמך :והחזקת, you are to support him to be an independent bread winner עמך, next to you. You have to assist him in such a manner that he does not sink below you in morale. גר ותושב וגו׳: as a גר צדק is already included in אחיך, the term גר ותושב is probably just a personal description similar to Gen. 23,4, where Abraham says: גר ותושב אנכי עמכם, “I come from a strange land but live here amongst you”. I am neither native born nor naturalised, but I live here among you. This is exactly the status of a גר תושב. He has not entirely adopted Jewish nationality, but by renouncing ע״ז and accepting the Noachism laws of the duties of mankind in general, he has acquired the right to live in Israel, (see Ex. 12,45). Similarly in v. 47. Accordingly, the duty to render assistance so that וחי עמך, he can make his living amongst you, extends also to the stranger who lives in your midst and who is not yet אחיך.

V. 36. אל תקח מאתו וגו׳. The preceding גר תושב וחי עמך is in parenthesis, and מאתו refers to אל תקח וגו׳ .אחיך is the continuation of והחזקת נשך :נשך ותרבית .בו phonetically related to נזק, damage, designates interest on loans from the point of view of the “damage” the loss incurred by the borrower, while תרבית looks on it from the point of view of the “increase”, the gain to the lender. Baba Metzia 60b develops the idea that in actual practice there is no case where one can occur without the other, and that, nevertheless, here, not only both are mentioned, but in the following verse they are expressed as two separate prohibitions, את כספך לא תתן לו בנשך ובמרבית לא תתן אכלך.
