It takes it that this is only to impress the gravity of taking interest on loans, by repeatedly prohibiting it: אי אתה מוצא לא נשך בלא תרבית ולא תרבית בלא נשך ולא חלקן הכתוב אלא לעבור עליו בשני לאוין.

We have already in Ex. 22,24, worked out fully and in detail the Jewish conception of the prohibition of taking interest on loans. There we showed that the Torah in no wise looks on interest on loans as anything which is morally wrong. Otherwise it would not forbid with equal solemnity the paying of interest as it does the taking of it, nor would it restrict the prohibition to Jews only. But it is rather a great act of acknowledgment, of recognising God as the Lord and Owner of our moveable property just as שמטת קרקע and יובל are, regarding His Mastery and Right of disposal of our landed property. It comes here also clearly as a continuation and further effect of the יובל. For land and soil are the source of all national wealth, and all moveable goods are, in the first instance, the result, the product of the blessing of the soil (cf. v. 38), and just as the gratuitous return of all purchased land in the יובל is to proclaim in Israel, God as the Lord and real owner of the Land of Israel, so is the gratuitous loaning of all our moveable goods to proclaim Him everywhere as the Lord and Real Owner of all our moveable fortune. Were we the real owners of our money, and if the loaning of it was completely an act of our own free will, then possibly the interest on loans which we take after a time might be considered neither as נשך towards our debtors nor תרבית on our part. Our debtors may have earned money with our money (— and it is just of such a loan for business purposes that our text speaks, see v. 35). The interest which he gives us is no “bite” (נשך. I.L.), no loss of any of his fortune, it is only a part of the fruit which our capital has begotten in his hands. And equally so is it no adventitious “increase” (תרבית) of our capital. For we were not bound to lend him our money. Had we kept it in our own hands it could also have been fruitful capital, we could also have earned with it, and the interest we receive is no real increase of our fortune, it is only compensation, perhaps only part-compensation, for an increase which we have lost. Against this way of looking on interest on loans from the non-Jewish standpoint is the fact that interest has to be paid in any case even when the debtor has not earned anything with the loan, even if it is notorious that he has lost with it; and also when it is well known that in the hands of the creditor it would have lain idle or that he would have sustained a loss with it. In every case capital and interest have to be paid, so that nothing remains in equity but to look on money as a useable object, and regard interest as the price paid for hiring it. (We have already pointed out on Ex. 22,24, the difference which nevertheless exists in equity between money paid for hire of articles and interest paid on loans of money).

But, now, looking at it from the Jewish point of view, our money is not absolutely our own property, it is only conditionally ours. God has the real right of disposal of it, and “He” has made it our duty to place some of “His” property that happens to be in our hands into the hand of our brother, not only to provide the necessities for his life, but also for the upkeep and continuation of his business. Against his duty to pay us back a similar sum in a certain time, the money, which up till then had been ours, at God’s behest, at the moment of transition becomes “his”. It is not with our money, it is with his own, that he does business. The profit made is the product of his activity with his own money and consequently exclusively his. If we demand any part of it, we are demanding a נשך, a “bite” at his fortune, and at the same time, in any case, תרבית, it is an increase, an addition to our fortune, not compensation for anything that we might have been able to earn with the money loaned, for we had no right to keep it back for our own use, as God, the real Owner of all property, had placed it at the disposal of somebody else. So that, even if the debtor had been able to make a profit out of the loan, the interest paid would still be נשך and תרבית. This is altogether the great effect of the Jewish conception of צדקה which undeniably belongs to the sphere of צדק of what is right and just. It is, from the receiver, a demand of love, compassion and benevolence, but from the giver’s relation to God, it is a debt which in simple justice must be paid (see on Gen. 15,6). Thus the thought of God as the Owner of our possessions, when introduced into the social relations of man to man, makes the otherwise justified interest on loans into נשך and תרבית, and interest-free loans become the greatest act of sacrifice with which we have to seal our homage to God. So that by the Torah stressing the prohibition of interest separately from both points of view, by the prohibition of נשך it demands the acknowledgment that our money in the hands of a borrower ceases to be ours, and by the prohibition of תרבית that our act of lending is a simple duty in the eye of the Tribunal of God, before which it is an act that we dare not evade, and for which we have no right whatsoever to accept compensation.

ויראת מאלקיך, accordingly, comes immediately to be added to the נשך and תרבית prohibition. יראה מאלקינו is the real reason for the prohibition of interest on loans, which, as far as human social ideas go, can find no justification. It is the recognition of God, as “your God”, as the arbiter of your fate and the guide for your actions, in which capacity He has forbidden you to take interest on loans with the purpose that: וחי אחיך עמך. We have already (in Ex. Ch. 20,24), indicated the deeply penetrating and far reaching effects which the forbidding of interest has on the welfare of the national economy of Israel. The effects of the institution of יובל (to which, in its wider sense the prohibition of interest also belongs) on the general business life of the people, finds in it its important complement. All these beneficial effects on the welfare of the people are summarised in the words: וחי אחיך עמך. It does not say, as it does above וחַי וגו׳, by which only the care for keeping our brother alive is made our duty, but וחֵי אחיך עמך. Now חֵי seems to be the stat. constr. of חיים as מֵי from מים. Thus we find it in the assuring exclamations חי נפשך ,חי פרעה etc. That חי here is a noun and the stat. constr. of חיים is evident from the juxtaposition: חייך וחי נפשך (Sam. II. 11,11). So that it says: “the life of your brother is with you”, i.e. the whole of the development of his life, the fulfilment of the mission of his life is closely bound up with you and yours. You are not there only for yourself, and you do not earn only for yourself. Although, in the first instance, you have to look after yourself in order to acquire the means which enable you to accomplish the mission in life which God has set for you, part of this mission in life is to acquire also the means which enable you to help the brother who is socially connected with you to achieve the mission of his life. What you earn you earn for yourself and for him. His life is bound up with you and with what you posses. This עִם makes you to an עַם. And inasmuch as it is not communist compulsion, not the force of taxation, not the fear of the spectre of red revolution, but the consciousness of duty dictated by the fear of God which binds this free-willed, and nevertheless — or perhaps therefore — so eternally strong bond of mutual help and assistance, this constitutes the realisation of that word of God when He chose us: ולקחתי אתכם לי לעם, for it is the pure consciousness of God which forms such a community of a nation.

The interest on a loan which is forbidden by the Torah as נשך and דבית דאורייתא — תרבית — by which capital and the stipulated interest has to be repaid to the lender under all circumstances is called רבית קצוצה. If such is paid, in accordance with the text אהדר ליה כי היכי דניחי ,וחי אחיך עמך, it can be reclaimed by order of court, יוצאה בדיינין (Baba Mezia 61b). Here too, the Jewish national conscientiousness, to which the guarding of the Mitzvas of the Torah is entrusted, has included within the orbit of the prohibition everything which is similar or near to such interest as רבית דרבנן. Such רבית דרבנן is called אבק רבית and is not יוצאה בדיינין (ibid). Different from רבית is the permitted relationship of a commercial company עיסקא an association of capital with labour, where profit and loss is borne by both, and the working side or partner receives payment or salary for what he does for the one who provides capital.

V. 37. את כספך לא תתן וגו׳. The transgression of the Law does not only begin with taking the interest, as might seem to be the case from v. 36, but as soon as a loan is given at any rate of interest, שימה, the sin is committed. Thus the prohibition of interest in Ex. 22,24 runs לא תשימון עליו גשך, and not only the lender himself but guarantors and witnesses also are included in the prohibition (Baba Mezia 62a). ובמרבית, above in v. 36, it calls it תרבית and that is the term that is generally used for taking interest: לקח תרבית. See Ezekiel Ch. XVIII and XXII,12. Also in Prov. 28,8. Perhaps fixing the interest, the “increase” which is only settled, only later to actually accrue, is called מרבית and only interest which is actually paid, and which has accrued is called תרבית. Thus תרבות אנשים חטאים (Numb. 32,14) refers to descendants who have already increased in numbers (a “brood” of sinful men. I.L.) while וכל מרבית ביתך ימותו אנשים (Sam. I. 2,33) refers to the increase of a family which will occur, which is still at its beginning.

We have already remarked that, according to Baba Mezia 60b, נשך and תרבית occur simultaneously, and every loan on interest, by the two aspects which are innate in it, is doubly forbidden. So that whether it is money or food or anything else that is lent on condition that more is returned than that which was lent, both נשך and תרבית are present. Thus it says in Deut. 23,20, expressly: ,נשך כסף נשך אוכל נשך כל דבר אשר ישך and in Baba Mezia 61a it is explained that our verse here is to be taken in the same way that similar passages are interpreted, viz, that, as both נשך and מרבית apply to both כספך and אכלך so that the Torah could make one sentence את כספך ואכלך לא תתן לו בנשך ובמרבית or if it wanted to make two separate prohibitions apply to each single act of interest (as explained above by the use of the two terms נשך and מרבית) is could say, את כספך לא תתן לו בנשך ובמרבית, ואכלך לא תתן לו בנשך ובמרבית, but the Torah separated them, and applies נשך to כסף and מרבית to אוכל, and places the words in such a way that they can be read forwards and backwards, then we are to do so, and read it with that interpretation, viz.קרי ביה הבי את כספך לא תתן לו בנשך ובמרבית, בנשך ובמרבית לא תתן אכלך. If we consider that money represents all objects to be used in business, i.e. productive objects, while אוכל food, represents things to be used up themselves, i.e. nonproductive objects, perhaps we can see the reason for stressing נשך at כסף and מרבית at אוכל. Interest received for money does not always appear as מרבית, an added increase of the lender’s fortune, for in his hands too, in the ordinary course of business, it would have increased his fortune. But נשך, a loss to the borrower’s fortune, it always remains. On the other hand in the case of אוכל, receiving back any greater quantity than the amount lent is always not only נשך but also תרבית. Left in the lender’s hands it would not have increased.

V. 38. אני וגו׳ לתת לכם את ארץ כנען להיות לכם לאלהים. By the redemption from Egypt I made you into possessors of the land, both had the purpose (and the attainment of this purpose was the condition for both) להיות לכם לאלהים, that you place the social life you will establish on this land, and by means of this land, entirely under My guidance, that you consider land and property merely as a loan from My Hands, that is only yours for as long as you use it to fulfil My Will and do not presume to have the right to anything that I forbid you. הלואה without נשך and מרבית, interest-free loans are the most expressive acts for the acknowledgment of the attitude which we adopt towards God, in regarding all our possessions as being in the nature of a loan from Him (see Baba Mezia 71a). That is why here, at the prohibition of lending on interest, the Torah reminds us of the gravity and the deep underlying meaning of the procedure, while above, (v. 36) at the prohibition of taking interest, it says: Fear thy God, and if you have taken interest, return it, וחי אחיך עמך אהדר ליה כי היכי דניחי, (Baba Mezia 61b).

V. 39. וכי ימוך אחיך עמך. This is still a continuation of the institution of the Youvel. After dealing with its redeeming effect on dealings of landed and moveable property, now, until the end of the chapter follows its effect on the rights of the person. Under the influence of the Youvel an institution is introduced which appears as the final salvation from poverty. Previously the Torah had directed the impoverished to the brotherly help of their compatriot brethren. Thereby no political communism, but a moral communism was established, that was justified, not indeed to demand, but certainly to expect that purely by the force of God-fearing feelings of duty, the capital of the well-to-do was ready without fee or interest, to come to the assistance and rescue of anyone threatened with impoverishment. Now it says וכי ימוך אחיך עמך, if nevertheless, in spite of being עמך, although you have stood brotherly at his side, he still had not been able to save himself from financial ruin, ונמכר לך, and has sold himself to you as an עבד, etc. Obviously ונמכר here is reflexive, as נועץ ,נשמר et. alia. But the reason that the hithpael form והתמכר is not actually used may have to do with the halacha which in any case states that such selling oneself is only allowed under the pressure of the very extremest degree of dire necessity, where no other possibilty offers itself to find the means of continuing existence. מניין שאין אדם רשאי למכור עצמו ולהניח באפונדתו וליקח לו בהמה וליקח לו כלים וליקח לו בית, אלא אם כן העני ת״ל וכי ימוך ונמכר הא אינו נמכר אלא אם כן .(ת״כ) .העני

לא תעבוד בו עבודת עבד, according to ת״כ and מכילתא, you may not demand from him any service which would mark him as an עבד, which, as a rule, is only performed by real slaves. Examples of such service are given as; washing the feet, taking the shoes off, carrying towels etc. behind the master to the bath, acting as a support, carrying in a sedan-chair etc., although one may have all these services performed by a free man against payment, or by son or pupil for love.

כשכיר, just as a day-labourer does not hire himself to work day and night, so may you not let him work day and night, but must allow him proper time for rest (מכילתא). And further, just as a day-labourer only engages himself to do his own particular work (a gardener to garden, a bricklayer to lay bricks etc. I.L.) and you have no right to demand other work from him, so also עבד עברי אי אתה רשאי לשנות מאומנתו (ibid.).

כתושב, just as an escaped slave who seeks refuge in the Jewish Land has the right of domicile, and all the privileges of a גר תושב, and of whom it says in Deut. 23,17: עמך ישב וגו׳ בטוב לו לא תוננו, you must allow him to live comfortably with you, and you may not offend him or hurt his feelings, so must you grant a comfortable, non-abaseing home to the עבד עברי who seeks refuge from his wretchedness in your service (ת״כ).

עמך במאכל במשתה בכסות נקיה וגו׳ :יהיה עמך. You must treat him as your equal, in food, clothes and living conditions (see Ex. 21,5). There we referred to the popular saying that resulted from this, viz, כל הקונה עבד עברי כקונה אדון לעצמו “who buys a Jewish slave for himself has bought himself a master”, and this, as תוספות on Kiddushin 20a points out, can be a literal fact, as, for instance, if the master has only one bed; he can not sleep on it himself, because it would be against the טוב לו עמך (here יהיה עמך) that neither he nor the slave should sleep in it, would be a Sodom-like dog-in-the-manger attitude of one who will not allow anybody else to enjoy something which is useless to himself, and according to the legal principle זה נהנה וזה לא חסר כופין על מדת סדום, the slave can claim, and the master be forced by law to allow, the right to sleep in the bed while the master lies on the floor!

עד שנת היובל. We have already remarked on Ex. 21,6 (at end of notes thereon) that מוכר עצמו, one who sells himself of his own free will, can contract for a longer term of service than six years, but, according to the ריטב״א, without any special contract the service is understood to be for six years. In any case the entry of Youvel sets him free. If the master dies before the expiration of the term of service, the service is transferred to the son, but not to any other heir (Kiddushin 17b),
יעבד עמך, you may not hire his service to others.
V. 41. ויצא מעמך הוא ובניו עמו. During the period of service the master has to provide for the wife and children (see on Ex. 21,3).

ושב אל משפחתו ואל אחוזת אבותיו ישוב. In Makkoth 12a ר׳ יהודה teaches לא היה חוזר לשררה שהיה בו, that he does not automatically return to any high office or dignities that he may previously have occupied. So that אחוזת אבותיו here can not have the figurative meaning — as חזקת אבותיו has — of “the right to the honours of his fathers,” but only the literal meaning of the landed possession of his fathers. Although here it is not dealing with the sale of his land but of his person, the Torah takes it for granted, — as already remarked on v. 39 — that it is only when he is in the direst need, with no possibility of raising the means for his existence in any other manner, that he may go to the extreme of selling himself. So that when he has come to taking this step, he, or his forbears before him, equally from necessity, (see on v. 25) must have sold their last field. But the Youvel brings every Jew back to the possession of landed property, and that makes an end to his condition of utter penury. So that when he ceases to belong to another family i.e. to the household of his master, to return to his own family אל משפחתו i.e. to his own home, Youvel brings him at the same time a piece of land, and thereby again the means of earning his own living. In these two sentences ושב וגו׳ and ואל אחזת וגו׳ the whole blessing of the Youvel institution is, accordingly, summarised.

This עבד עברי-institution is the last anchor of hope of salvation for a family sunk in destitution, who have struggled in vain against the opposing forces in the fight for independent existence. Nothing is left to the bread winner but his ability — and perhaps that of his family too — to work. With this ability, he, together with his family, temporarily pass over into the family-circle of somebody who is well off, who, in return for the use of his powers to work, takes over the responsibility to look after him and his family. The master however, remains bound to treat him as a man and a brother; and while he is thus protected against forlorn wretchedness, after his term of service is completed, he goes out with a capital for which he has worked to make a fresh attempt to earn his own independent living. Alternatively when Youvel comes, it frees him from his service and gives back to him together with his independence, the fields of his original inheritance by means of which, if God blesses his industry and perseverance, he and his family can gain an independent existence. Of course the establishment of such institution of “slavery” reckons on a standard of social life, built up on equity, humaneness and love, ruled through and through by the conception of “duty”, which can only be created by the State of God’s Torah. Hence this institution too is dependent on the integrity of the Jewish National State, and אין עבד עברי נוהג אלא בזמן שהיובל נוהג (Arachin 29a).

V. 42. כי עבדי הם. Belonging to God excludes belonging to anybody else, entering the service of God makes one free. לא ימכרו ממכרת עבד: The manner of the sale of an עבד עברי too, according to ת״כ may not be like a slave sale, not by public auction, or anything like that.

V. 43. בפרך. Examples of what is here forbidden by the term פרך are given in ת״כ as: שלא תאמר לו החם את הכוס הזה והוא אינו צריך הצין לי את הכוס והוא אינו צריך עדור תחת הגפן עד שאבוא, you are not to tell him to warm a cup which is not wanted at all, or say to him “cool this cup” and you do not require it, or “go on hoeing under this tree until I come”. The master may not make him work just to keep him working, doing work which is quite unnecessary, and not tell him to do even necessary work in such a way that it sounds as if the purpose is not to accomplish the work, but just to be working. To make a slave work so that he does work can only have the purpose of making him feel his servile position, to wear him out, and to harden and blunt his feelings, purposes which the Egyptians had in mind with their פרך (see Ex. 1,14).

V. 44—46. אשר יהיו לך, who remain yours, who do not come to you, like the עבד עברי to render temporary service, and who do not go free in the Youvel, such עבד ואמה can you etc. — אשר סביבתיכם beyond your land, the seven nations who had inhabited Palestine were not allowed to stay in the land, and were not allowed to enter it even as עבד. The customary expression עבד כנעני is, accordingly, strictly speaking, incorrect. (וצ״ע, as, with the renunciation of idolatry and קבלת ז׳ מצות they were allowed to remain — see רמב״ן on Deut. 20,10. — their entry as עבד who becomes a full בן ברית should all the more be allowed. וצ״ע). וגם מבני התושבים: A גר תושב could also, of his own free will, sell himself as an עבד to a .ישראל וממשפחתם וגו׳, also if they had married a Canaanite woman, the children had the nationality of the father and not of the mother באומות הלך אחר הזכר (Kiddushin 67b).

לעולם בהם תעבדו. The status of an עבד כנעני in the Jewish State has already been discussed on Ex. 12,44. The same motive — as worked out there — which underlay the continuance of slavery in the Jewish State, would also be the motive of לעולם בהם תעבדו, which is taken as a positive command (Gittin 38b). Nevertheless for the purpose of מצות and for the reasons of general morality, giving them their freedom was allowed. And the Halacha learns just from this לעולם בהם תעבדו that אין לך בהם אלא (ת״כ) עבודה בלבד, that your right over them extends purely and solely to work, but you have no right to mishandle them, to hurt their feelings, or put them to shame, לעבודה נתתיו ולא לבושה (Nidda 47a) and Jewish writings are full of features showing characteristic kindness, mildness and humaneness which marked the treatment of עבדים. See רמב״ם at the end of הל׳ עבדים).

לא תרדה בו בפרך. We indicated on v. 43 what the Halacha understood by עבודה בפרך which was not allowed to be exercised with an עבד עברי and which here is implied to be allowed with an עבד כנעני. It is making him work not for useful purposes but as a disciplinary measure to prevent him becoming used to idleness, or to keep him conscious of his duty to work. Hence also the Halacha here teaches בו אי אתה רודה בפרך, רודה אתה בבן חורין בפרך that, what it here allows towards an עבד כנעני and is only forbidden towards an עבד עברי is also allowed to be exercised towards a free fellow-Jew if you are in such a position over him, or if he has placed himself voluntarily in such a position where you are justified and even in duty bound to use work for disciplinary purposes. Solely of an עבד עברי as it said that only as his necessitous condition has driven him to a subservient position under you, you have no right whatsoever to use your authority for disciplinary uses.

V. 47 & 54. The Torah gives rules for yet one final case in which inexorable necessity may have forced one to sell himself to a גר תושב, or even to an עובד עבודה זרה, The Torah does not sanction such a step, it says ונמכר לך in v. 39. (ת״כ) כשיהיה נמכר אינו נמכר אלא לך, and indeed it is quite understandable that it does not approve or sanction it. If he goes, even temporarily, completely, even with his children if he has any (v. 41), into the sphere of the home of the non-Jewish master, it is almost impossible that he and his family do not become estranged from the duties of Judaism. But, if the step has been taken, the demands of justice must be satisfied, and only by full fair repayment to the non-Jew can he be redeemed, even if the sale had been made not to a גר תושב but to a משפהת גר, or even to עקר משפחת גר. When mentioned next to גר תשב a משפחת גר must undoubtedly mean a family which is not גר תושב i.e. who have not acquired the right of domicile by renouncing עבודה זרה, and so refers to an .עובד עבודה זרה עקר משפחת גר is taken, in Kiddushin 20a, to refer to עבודה זרה עצמה, to one who has sold himself to the service of the idol itself, e.g. as a temple slave to chop wood or draw water for the requirements of the temple of an idol. As עֵקֶר, to hamstring means a severance of Achilles’ tendon עֵקֶר would designate that, in which, or by which, something receives its hold and support, the basis on which something stands. It is accordingly quite a pithy expression to describe the idolatory by which a foreign family, remaining isolated in the midst of God’s country, recognises it “hold and support”. Accordingly, even if dire necessity had reduced one to this extremest estrangement, the condition may only be redeemed by fair and just means. וחשב עם קנהו (v. 50), if, and when he is to be redeemed by relations or by his own means, it has to be fairly and exactly estimated, in accordance with the rules the Torah lays down here, how much of the purchase price paid, after deducting the proportionate sum of the value of service already rendered, must be repaid to the purchaser. So that here, even towards an avowed idolator in the Jewish Land, and even when it is a matter of saving a Jew from a condition where the whole Jewishness of his life is endangered, the Torah makes it incumbent on us to keep to the strictest and most correct fair dealing, מנין לגזל עובד ע״ז שהוא אסור תלמוד לומר וחשב עם קונהו ידקדק עם קוגהו (Baba Kama 113a).

V. 55. כי לי בני ישראל וגו׳. Repeatedly here, at the conclusion of the laws concerning personal freedom, the fundamental fact out of which the unloseable unsaleable freedom of the Children of Israel flows is stated, viz, the fact that, based on the redemption from Egypt, we do belong to God, and that precludes our belonging to anything else. The fact that God is the Master raises His slaves above all other slavery and makes them unable to allow themselves to be bound in the bonds of any other master. שטרי קודם “My bill of sale has precedence, it came first, I have the priority”, ת״כ explains our verse. “Every fibre of your being, every fraction of your strength and powers belong to Me, you can not transfer it to the binding ownership of another.” This principle of keeping the Jew conscious of the inalienability of his personal freedom is nurtured by Jewish law so consistently that normally not even the daily contract of a daily worker is considered as irrevocably binding, and in normal circumstances can be refuted by him at any time of the day, פועל יכול לחזור בו אפי׳ בחצי היום.

V. 1. Looking back at all the blessing which the thought of God, that, in the previous chapter, is shown to be the effect of the Youvel, grants to the Jewish State as a whole, and to the individuals that comprise it, and, introductory to the following, here are placed two significant sentences: לא תעשו לכם אלילים etc., and את שבתותי תשמרו etc. The אלילים, as we have repeatedly remarked, are the heathen gods looked at from the point of view of their being hostile powers which are opposed to the happiness of human beings, “denying” (אל “do not” I.L.) their independent flourishing; פסל is a representation in relief. Such representations are forbidden, not only of heathen idols, but also as any material symbol of God or divinity. See Ex. 20,22 & 23. אתם ראיתם כי מן השמים דברתי עמכם לא תעשון אתי וגו׳. And Deut. 4,15 & 16 ושמרתם מאד לנפשתיכם כי לא ראיתם כל תמונה וגו׳ פן תשחיתון ועשיתם לכם פסל where obviously any material representation or picture to represent God Who was revealed to us on Sinai is forbidden. מצבה: we have already explained on Gen. 28,18 & XXXIII,20 the relation of מצבה to מזבח.

מצבה consisting of a single stone is a memorial stone of that which God has done for us here below, and is erected by God-worshipping hands to bring an offering on it from that point of view. Erected by polytheistic hands it is similarly a memorial stone of the imagined revelation of the might and power of a heathen deity. Before the giving of the Torah, when God was revealed to the אבות above all in nature and in guiding our lives, when bringing offerings to God was an act of homage and recognition of, and thanks for, this providence of God in nature and human destiny, then מצבה was permitted, yea desired. But after the revelation on Sinai, when God’s Will for the regulation of the whole of our life was given, then it was not what God had done for us, but what we have to do, the godliness that is wished to be revealed by our active lives, which is to form the foundation of our getting near to God, is to be the basis of our offerings, the מזבח of our קרבנות. From that time a מצבה-stone was incorrect and undutiful, אשר שנא ה׳ אלקיד (Deut. 16,22); and the מזבח alone, representing Man’s work in adding stone to stone and raising the earthly upwards to the godly, is henceforth the place for our offerings, seeking to get nearer to our God:

אבן משכית: meaning of משכית is not quite certain. Derived from שסת = שכת from which we get הסכת, to attend, to note, משכית would be attention, and אבן משכית a directing stone, a stone set in the earth to direct attention to that place. Similarly, as the singular of משכיות from the root שכה, it would mean the Chaldean word, to gaze, to look at, and אבן משכית a stone to attract notice. Onkelos translates it אבן סגידא, a stone of “bowing down” corresponding to the prescribed purpose להשתהות עליה and then perhaps שכת is phonetically related to סגד and would also mean exactly “bowing”. But there is no doubt about what the prohibition consists in. It forbids בארצכם in the whole land, outside the מקדש to set a stone in the ground and to prostrate yourself on it to God בהשתחויה i.e. בפשוט ידים ורגלים with your whole body outspread. Such throwing yourself down before God is only allowed on the stone-paved ground of the מקדש (Megilla 22b).

These three sentences: ,ופסל ומצבה לא תקימו לכם ,לא תעשו לכם אלילים ואבן משכית לא תתנו בארצכם וגו׳, are obviously the negative opposite of the two positive commands that immediately follow: את שבתתי תשמרו ומקדשי תיראו, not אלילים, not פסל ומצבה not אבן משכית but שבת and מקדש are the institutions towards which your careful attention is to be concentrated. In connection with the preceding this may be taken to say: — the whole preceding institution of Youvel shows God as the One Who is ever ready to regenerate and restore the combined life of family, society and state. Yea, the mitzvoth of this institution which we have to fulfil are — as we have already indicated on v. 9 et. seq. — only the price for which God promises us His Youvel, His social and political כפרה the constant healing and rebirth of our whole social and political life. The כל המחלה אשר שמתי במצרים לא אשים עליך כי אני ה׳ רפאך, which God proclaimed before all His Lawgiving (Ex. 15,26) as the result of paying the toll of obedience to His laws, found the key-stone of its realisation in His institutions of Youvel. All His laws — of which the Youvel is the culminating point — are our רפואה, our cure from all our personal and national ills, yea, they are more than this, they are to be the prophylactic regime which, if faithfully adhered to, will keep us individually, socially and politically healthy, and keep all the evils of individual, social and political illnesses far from us. Hence our health, our life, our happiness, our prosperity our independence, our strength, our freedom, and our joy in life is the aim and purpose of God’s rule and guidance. He is a God of the most positive affirmation of human happiness and well-being, this is already expressed in His Name ה׳. It is this which forms the most profound contrast to the heathen conception of אלילים, the denying gods, the gods who are envious of and inimical to Man’s happiness.

אני ה׳. As the underlying reason for your inalienable, always recoverable, freedom and independence it had just been given, ,לי בני ישראל עבדים אני .עבדי הם, I, in the whole of My personality, ה׳, the four-lettered Name, always ready to grant a fresh future, I am your God, guide your fate, guide your actions, therefore: “make no אלילים for yourselves”, for you, there are no denying gods; as עבדי, as “My servants” as long as you are in My service with every fibre of your being, with every spark of your life, you are the freest of the free, and there are no unfriendly enemy forces which can deny your well-being, whom you have to fear, or whose supposed favour you have to seek by supposed honours.

But also in your relation to Me, in seeking to get nearer to Me, to My proximity, on which all your happiness, blessing and protection is dependent, do not lose your way. Not by means of פסל and מצבה, not by any image by which you may think of My Presence, and through which you will only banish My Presence, will I really be always be near to you. Also, not by a mere grateful memorial to My Rule will you obtain My blessing and protecting rule and management. Not even at any spot of your own choice throughout the wide world may you mark, by cementing a stone there, as being specially consecrated, there to throw your whole self down in devotion. There is only one way by which you can everywhere realise Me and My management and obtain My blessing and protecting Proximity. And there is only one place which I have consecrated to be a means for you to feel My Presence, on whose ground, as being such a marked-out place, you may throw yourself down with your whole being in prayer and devotion to Me. Its existence in your midst is to make such demands on you to keep your lives in concord with it, that by living such holy lives, in every minute of your existence, wherever your earthly wanderings may lead you, you will be able to bring yourselves near to Me so that I can fulfil that which I have promised you: “I will dwell amongst you”.

It is My שבתות which will bring Me and My Rule home to you wherever you are, and the sanctifying place which will win your whole life over to My Presence מקדשי, the Sanctuary of My Torah. Hence את שבתתי תשמרו ומקדשי תיראו אני ה׳.

Not by means of פסל and מצבה, not by likeness and memorial stones have we to keep ourselves conscious of God and His Rule: שבתות ה׳, the sabbaths of God, שבת בראשית and the שבת ,שבתות הארץ and שמטה and יובל, which regulate the whole of our private and public lives with the thought “God”, and by great acts of sacrifice make the acknowledgment of God real in our lives, as well as the sabbaths of God in the wider sense, the מועדי ה׳ the times of gathering and reunion dedicated to the memory of His rule and management, these are our אות and ברית and מועד. From these, not from moulded dead stone, but from the symbols of acknowledgement, bond and memories woven out of the living tissue of our active life, not so much from them themselves as from the influence they have in forming the pattern of our daily lives, from these do we draw the inspiration which makes us find ourselves at one with our God.

And not אבן משכית בארצכם להשתהות עליה, and not by your throwing yourselves down before God wherever you please, — however filled with fervid devotion you may be — does God wish to receive your prayers. He has set His Law, His Torah, in the centre between Himself and us. Only in homage to His Torah does He recognise homage to Himself, and only inasmuch as we prostrate ourselves before His Torah do we prostrate ourselves before Him. Therefore for us it is only מקדשו, only the Sanctuary which He has dedicated to His Torah on Moria-Zion, that is the sole spot on earth which is designated as the place where one can pray to God with completely throwing one’s whole self before Him in true devotion. And inasmuch as everywhere else we may only throw ourselves down before God, on ground which is not specially marked out by stone for that purpose, the whole wide world becomes simply a great surround of that one central point which God has consecrated for the evidence, the Testimony of His Torah; the place which even in ruins remains consecrated ground — כסא כבוד מרום מראשון מקום מקדשנו — (the very fact that it is in ruins, that it had to be reduced to ruins, makes it even a higher, holier place than it ever was I.L.). Wherever we throw ourselves down before God, it is only in the thought of His Torah. And it is not השתחויה, not the outward sign of our giving ourselves completely up to the Sanctuary of the Torah, but ומקדשי תיראו — יראה — the serious thought that should always accompany us, and wherever we may be, always keep in our minds, the demands which radiate from that holy centre point to keep our lives holy, and to realise the lofty ideal of life which was laid down there, so that in our private and public life we can think of that ideal without having to blush — this יראת מקדש ה׳ which alone does actually make the Sanctuary of God’s Torah a centre point which always and everywhere draws us up upwards towards it and thus towards God — this it is which makes us conscious of the Eye of God being always on us, and brings about all the seeds of security and blessing and happiness which the commands of His Torah sow in the fields of our life, אני ה׳ says God. It is not on Me, but on yourselves that you have to work, to try and influence and alter. My Being is always ready and anxious to love and bless. It only lies with you, by making My Torah something real, to make yourselves worthy of this loving blessing.

מקדש ה׳ and שבתות ה׳, the Sanctuary of God’s Torah in space with all its results to render our moral life holy, and His holy days in time with their results on our spiritual and social life, are not these the summary of all the laws, the giving of which form the contents of this third book of the Torah from the first chapter right up to here.

V. 3. In the previous chapter in verses 9—12 it has already been indicated how keeping the laws of Youvel, and the resulting placing of the whole material and social matters of the nation under God, would effect a quite special ever-renewing, prosperity-furthering shaping of them on God’s part. And in verses 18 & 19 it has already been indicated how keeping the prescribed laws of morality and justice would have the result of the physical, social and political well-being of the nation prospering in a manner which would show the special care of the Providence of God.

Now this happiness and prosperity attached to the fulfilment of God’s Torah is pictured in bold strokes in fuller details in verses 3 & 13. Then, from verse 14 onwards equally so, the dire results which would ensue to the nation from not keeping the Torah.

הלד .אם בחקתי תלכו is the movement towards a goal. Hence preferably, the effort to satisfy the attainment of possessions and enjoyments whose purity or impurity depends on their particular morality or immorality. הקת ה׳ are the bounds set by God in accordance with our moral nature and our moral calling, within which these efforts to obtain satisfaction remain pure and even a duty, but beyond these limits become corruption and sins against ourselves (see on Gen. XLVII.22). So that אם בחקתי תלכו means: “If, in satisfying your physical requirements, you move strictly within the limits drawn by My Laws”. All the other laws are summarised here under the conception of הקת .מצות are what are necessary for our moral integrity, for the purity of our being. מצות give this being and its powers the commands to carry out the duties on the post which God has allotted to us. These duties are to be kept constantly present in our minds by “learning” and by “self imposed precautions”, — both are called שמירה — and by עשיה, by being faithfully performed.

By לכת בהקת ה׳ and שמירת ועשית מצותיו we have done all that is asked from us on our part to found our physical, social, and political well-being. Everything else we can leave to God. If, by wandering in the paths of His Laws we make ourselves into morally pure men, by studying and taking to heart His Commandments, into intellectually clear thinking and conscientious beings, and by fulfilling them, into a just and benevolent people, God undertakes to raise our land out of the political and physical dilemnas of the rest of the world. He sets heaven and earth into such harmonious concord with such men and their efforts that nothing is in opposition to them, and everything works together to further their progress, which is then nothing else but the realisation of God’s Will for the world and humanity. That which was disturbed by Man forsaking obedience to God, that which will ultimately be regained by the whole of humanity in the future re-entering obedience to God, is what should have found a beginning, is to find its beginning, in, and be brought about by, the entry of Israel into its own land, where such obedience can be realised and shown as an example to the rest of the world (see Gen. Ch. 3,19).

V. 4. ונתתי גשמיכם, your rains, יורה ומלקוש, the autumn rains after the sowing, and the spring rains before the cutting, on whose timely and blessed coming the whole prosperity of the year depends. These rains are not merely the result of physical causes, but in accordance with your deserts and requirements God guides these physical causes. He grants these rains as your rains and sends them at the right times. ונתנה הארץ יבולה: freed from the curse (Gen. 3,17) the earth yields its יבולה its undiminished unhindered natural might of the blessing of produce, and so do the trees of the orchards yield their fruit, פריו.
V. 5. ואכלתם וגו׳ וישבתם וגו׳ see on Ch. 25,19.

V. 6. ונתתי שלום בארץ: the social happiness of internal peace brought about by the satisfying feeling of all being well, and the harmonious unselfishly living for one another of the inhabitants, the joy of Man such as only blossoms on the basis of God’s Torah under the rays of His blessing. והשבתי חיה רעה cf. Is. XI.16—19. וחרב לא תעבר וגו׳, to the social peace is added the political, you will remain untouched by the horrors of war outside your land, however near your borders they may reach.

V. 7 & 8. ורדפתם וגו׳. If enemies of your happiness dare to attack you, their courage will forsake them when they meet you; for ורדפו וגו׳, the smallest minority of you will suffice to put to flight any overpowering forces, that is why ונפלו וגו׳, they lose all courage before you.

V. 9. And so, upheld by the most flourishing blessing of produce, undisturbed by party factions from within, and by enemies from without, I bestow on you that greatest of all riches, the blessing of children, ופניתי אליכם, I direct My benign Providence towards you, your bodily and spiritual well-being, והפריתי אתכם, will give you a wealth of children, והרביתי אתכם and make your children thrive and grow up spiritually and morally to be reproductions of you, so that you do live on in them (see on Gen. 1,28) and —

והקמתי את בריתי אתכם. From the danger which everywhere else develops from great growth of population, viz. degeneration and laxity of morals, חקתי, in whose path you tread, and מצותי which you learn and practise, will protect you. Your moral worth will not diminish with the increase of your population, it rises with each new addition to your numbers. With each one, you get a fresh member of the bond with God, however numerous you become, the covenant made with your forefathers remains with you.

V. 10. ואכלתם ישן וגו׳, And just as the purity of your morals has nothing to fear from the numbers of your population, so is the abundance of the produce of your land not affected by over-population. However rich you become in people, the fertility of your land will always be richer still. You will never be able to consume all the produce of your land. ואכלתם ישן ישן .נושן would be only the fruit of the previous year, in contrast to חדש, this year’s, the new. ישן נושן is the old which has become old, that which has been stored for several years. ואכלתם ישן נושן, all your produce will not only stand storage but will improve by it, כל המתישן יפה מחברו, and it will always grow in such abundance that שיהיו הגרנות .ישן מפני חדש תוציאו מלאות חדש והאוצרות מלאות ישן, that the granaries will be full of the new produce and the store-houses will still be full of the old, and you will have to clear out the latter to make room for the new (ת״כ). So that the ever-increasing number of the inhabitants will be matched by the fruitfulness of the land.

V. 11. ונתתי משכני וגו׳. Just as it says in Numb. 10,36, שובה ה׳ רבבות אלפי ישראל that the Presence of God on earth does not come to isolated individuals but to Israel growing to myriads of thousands, and is conditional to a numerous nation paying Him the tribute of free-willed obedience, so here, too, we find the ונתתי משכני בתוככם said only after והפריתי אתכם והרביתי אתכם. I will give משכנ, My Sanctuary, the expression of My Presence on earth, in the midst of your national community, and however large this may grow, לא תגעל נפשי אתכם. As long as My חוקות and מצות remain the paths of your endeavours, and the purport of your deeds, you and your national life will not be in opposition to My Will, or to that which משכני expresses as being laid down for your yardstick, and נפשי, My Being, My Will, will find nothing repellant in you.

V. 12. והתהלכתי בתוככם, and like I am to the life and fate of the nation, will I also be intimately near to the individual families and members of your nation, and will make the life and fate of every individual home, of every individual person of every home, a special object of My Care and Provision, and a revelation of My guiding Proximity. And thus will be realised that which from the beginning was proclaimed as the purpose of your calling (Ex. 6,7) that I will show Myself as the Guide of your fate and Director of your action, and under My Guidance you will form a united and happy community.

V. 13. מוט ,מטת עלכם to vacillate, waver. From that we get מוט the stretcher on which the load is kept suspended. מוטות עול are probably the two poles by which the load is attached to the yoke, the point where the power or strength is applied. With the redemption out of Egypt the Egyptian yoke was broken from off our necks, but the shafts of the yoke we took out with us, we still carried the equipment of slavery with us, and even if we were freed for ever from the Egyptian yoke of slavery, nevertheless another yoke could always take its place, and we still had the tendency to bear, instead of the Egyptian yoke, the yoke of moral, social and political slavery.

It was only through מתן תורה that the shafts of the yoke were also broken from off our necks, that He raised us up for evermore and made us independent and free, at least gave us the guidance to remain upright in everything and against everything. The whole effect of keeping the Torah in granting human dignity and sovereignity the forces of sensuality, of nature, of social and political powers is summarised in this קוממיות.

V. 14. שמע בקול ,שמע לקול — ,שמע אל — .ואם לא תשמעו לי definitely means: to obey, but, -שמע ל equally often means: to listen, to hear somebody, to listen to somebody. It occurs in that sense frequently in Job. 15,17 ; XXIX,21 ; XXXI,35 ; XXXII,10; etc. So, as disobedience is fully expressed in the ולא תעשו וגו׳ that follows, the ואם לא תשמעו לי here can designate just failing to listen to the Word of God, and can show the beginning of the actual practical disobedience to lie in neglecting “learning” the Torah, in failing to study to make oneself acquainted with the Torah. The results of this theoretical sin is then practical defection, כל שאינו לומד .ולא תעשו וגו׳ (ת״כ) אינו עושה (a kind of rake’s progress I.L.).

V. 15. ואם בחקתי תמאסו. The defection progresses. Once you have lost the theoretical knowledge and understanding of the Torah, and, for any reason whatsoever, put it behind your back in practical life, your conscience gives you no rest, until, to justify yourself to yourself, you have sophistically converted the defection into progress, and accustomed yourself to look down on faithful adherence to the Torah as something to be conquered. For the existence of the Torah and its power to form and rule life, even if the knowledge of it has been lost and it has ceased to be a factor of practical life, does still come to us from the life of its contemporary faithful adherents. And every such loyal adherent is felt as a reproach to the deserter, until he has succeeded in sophistically considering himself as the better man, and learnt to look down with disdain on the Torah and its followers. And it is especially the “school” of the חוקות those laws which put limitation on the life of our senses, which so easily appear to those who have fallen away from the Torah as narrowing the lives and stunting the happiness of their contemporaries who are loyal to the Torah. More than at any other of God’s Laws, the extremely sanctifying and moral effect of these laws are only apparent to those who keep them. They, too, are the laws most easily looked on contemptuously by those that pride themselves as having become “emancipated from the bonds of chains erroneously affixed”. Thus the fall from the Torah, begun with the lack of study and knowledge, progresses to contempt of the Torah. כל שאינו לומד ואינו עושה .(ת״כ) סוף שהוא מואס באחרים

ואת משפטי תגעל נפשכם. The defection goes on. Unable to rise to the understanding that it is pure deep-felt conviction and freewilled enthusiastic attachment to God and His Torah which produces the loyalty to the Torah of its adherents, the apostates look around for external causes to explain this riddle to them. They find these in the institutions of Jewish social life which are all based on the knowledge and practice of the Torah which have created a family and communal life — once a national life also — which makes the knowledge and practice of the laws of the Torah the most important concern of all classes of the Jewish community. It is, accordingly these Jewish social institutions, and above all, their bearers and promoters, the chachamim, which receive the full weight of their hatred. In them they see the “misfortune” of their race, and the disdain which they feel towards their brethren who remain faithful to the Torah becomes transferred to the spiritual bearers and guardians of the institutions of the Torah, the כל שאינו לומד ואינו עושה ומואס באחרים סוף שהוא שונא את .חכמים .(ת״כ) החכמים

לבלתי עשות את כל מצותי. The defection goes on further. Until then it had not gone beyond apostasy in one’s own life, and the feeling of disdain and hate towards the Torah, its followers, and cherishers. But the tendency to this direction does not remain at that, where opportunity offers it grows into persecuting intolerance. That which it does not honour shall nowhere be honoured, that which it does not practise shall not be practised by anybody else. It declares war on the Torah, and disturbs and hinders its being carried out wherever and whenever it can. Naturally it thinks it must succeed and persuades itself that its movement is an act of salvation to the benefit of humanity, and persuades itself that its fight against the continuance of observation of the dictates of the Torah is not a fight against God and His holy Will. But what they are fighting against must for them cease to be the work of God, the Revelation must be relegated to a myth, Moses and the Prophets to imposters, the transmitters of the laws from Sinai to deceived deceivers, and inasmuch as they make the prize for their victory לבלתי עשות את כל מצותי, the thwarting of the practical keeping of the laws of the Torah, make this the banner which they carry before their intolerant war of persecution; these laws must cease for them to be “מצותי״, to be מצות ה׳ God’s commands, as ת״כ designates this further step in the defection כל שאינו לומד ואינו עושה ומואס באחרים ושונא החכמים סוף אינו מניח לאחרים לעשות וכל שאינו לומד ואינו עושה ומואס באחרים ושונא החכמים ואינו מניח לאחרים לעשות (ת״כ) סוף שהוא כופר במצות שנאמרו מסיני.

But even at that the defection does not stop. There still remains one step further to be taken: להפרכם את בריתי, to tear asunder the last thread which still holds them in connection with the Covenant of God. This is, according to the explanation given in כפירה בעיקר :ת״כ, denial of the existence of God. On the downward path of apostasy one is inevitably brought to this last stage. As long as the thought of “God” still lingers in his breast, as long as, even with wavering doubt, the conception of the existence of God still finds room in his soul, for so long the inner self-accusing voice of conscience finds no rest from the conception of God being actually there, and in the possibility of His Revelation which, after all, is associated with it. Complete night must have descended within him, the last glimmering spark of a consciousness of God must be extinguished, the last thread leading back to His bond torn asunder, if his conscience is to be at rest; and to find this presumed rest, he must stamp these last sparks out with an audacious foot, tear these last threads asunder with an audacious hand: ת״כ) כל שיש לו כל המדות הללו סוף שהוא כופר בעיקר).

V. 16. אף אני אעשה זאת לכם. Just as you started by being indifferent to My Will so that you would not, right at the beginning, trouble yourselves with “learning” My Torah to keep My Will always in your minds, and finished up from that by making just the non-observance of My Will as the task of your lives: so I, too, will not let the fulfilment of your wishes, the success of your endeavours, be any longer the subject of My special Direction. I shall make the denial and frustration of them be what you will experience in your lives, by the events which I shall direct, will show you that the fulfilment of your will in your earthly existence is only given to you by the fulfilment of My Will. Only in proportion to the extent to which you make the realisation of My wishes the most serious preoccupation of your lives will you experience the realisation of your wishes, but with indifference, yea, with behaving in direct opposition to My wishes, your own prosperity, even your own existence, is undermined (see on V. 21—24).

בהלה .והפקדתי עליכם בהלה וגו׳ (from בהל related to בעל social domination), designates the physical and mental domination, the dismay and enervation which arises out of the feeling of helplessness against the effects of opposing forces, out of the loss of self-confidence. It is just the very contrary of קוממיות, the feeling of security, assurance, of being master over all material powers, a feeling that is necessary for our progress, and for achieving all our aims, a feeling that is only reached by the consciousness that one is breathing and adjusting one’s wishes in the service of God, and therefore under His protection and blessing. This feeling of self-confidence is the first thing that God causes to diminish when we start leaving off obedience to Him, and this slackening of assurance, and uncertainty in mind and feelings, begets torpidity and fever in the body. For it is the mind that governs the body, and psychical unrest has physical results. שחפת (from שחף related to סחב to drag along the ground) designates that condition of weakness in which a person drags himself along, has not the strength to lift his feet in hale active walking. Thus we find שחוף (in Sota 26b), the weak, powerless one. — קדחת (from קדח to glow) the heat of fever. מבלות עינים ומדיבת נפש originating from mental conditions, the physical conditions work back on the condition of the mind. The feeling of weakness and the fever of illness are physical conditions which make one without courage for the future and depressed for the present. מכלות עינים the eye, the mental outlook כלה languishes, i.e. looks listlessly without hope to the future, expects no improvement. דוב :מדיבת נפש as much as דאב, (similar construction to רום and ראם), is distress over present pain. Related to תאב, the expression for ardent wishing, דוב and דאב is the condition of “longing”, the condition of uneasiness where one longs for some change. Now it does not say: ואת השחפת וגו׳ but השחפת both שחפת and קדחת are only the external signs of the inner בהלה, so that if they are threatened with בהלה the threat includes at the same time שחפת and קדחת.

וזרעתם לריק זרעכם וגו׳. Through the low level to which, internally and externally, you have sunk, you no longer have the power to protect your property. As long as you stood there קוממיות, faithful to the Torah, your very name alone sufficed to keep guard at your frontiers. Three times each year, when fields and orchards glowed in full glory of the riches of the soil, and all your virile armed strength could be found at the centre point of your land at the feet of the Sanctuary of the Torah, still no raiding foot dared to cross your unguarded borders (Ex. 34,24). In בהלה, through your disobedience, this wholesome dread and awe of you is lost, and that which you have sown and which the still faithful earth matures gets carried away by the enemy neighbours of your land.

V. 17. ונתתי פני בכם. My Presence which otherwise was always directed towards you, I now turn against you. When you pursue your raiding neighbours it is you — in contrast to verses 7 & 8 — who get beaten. ורדו בכם שנאיכם, you fall under the subjection of your “haters”, under the subjection of the neighbouring nations who have envied your previous prosperity and happiness and who had become your enemies because your way of life was so diametrically opposite to theirs. In this political dependency, by your falling away from My Laws, your personal nature will have become so timid that ונסתם ואין רודף אתכם, you see danger and anti-semitism even where there is none. The ת״כ takes שנאיכם as opposed to אויביכם to refer to internal enemies מכם ובכם. The external political bad conditions beget internal division into parties. Internal enemies of the Jewish way of life arise, who see the cause of the political unfortunate state of affairs, not in the defection from the Torah but in those who are still faithful to its tenets; they promise emancipation from the political yoke of the nations by emancipation from the yoke of the Torah. These internal enemies act as a fifth column for the external ones, and this internal schism only increases still more the external wretchedness.

V. 18. ואם עד אלה. And if, arrived at such pitch, you still remain in such indifference to My Will that you still do not find it worth while even to take trouble to learn what My Will really is. You go on looking for the cause of your unhappy condition in external causes, and do not see that the whole cause of it lies in your neglect of My Laws (cf. Is. 9,9 & 12).

ויספתי וגו׳ שבע על חטאתיכם. We have already proved elsewhere that the number seven in תנ״ך designates the full, the complete, especially when referring to the size of something progressing in time to its full limit. And so here, and in the following sentences the שבע כהטאתיכם ,שבע על חטאתיכם means: My punishment will keep step with your defection. I will not become tired of punishing you. I will not give up punishing you, as being hopeless of attaining its purpose. Just as your defection does not stand still, but progresses from indifference to the limit of definite opposition, so does My punishment not remain still, but gets more and more intense until the whole of your political ruin is threatened. In ת״כ the “seven” is taken literally אתס עברתם לפני שבע עבירות בואו וקבלו עליכם שבע פורעניות. And actually the defection described above — in the reckoning which the ת״כ adopts, that לבלתי עשות את כל מצותי comprises two stages — does progress in seven stages, and the punishment threatened, also in seven intensifications. These would then probably be, verses 16, 18, 21, 23, 27, 33 and 36.

V. 19 & 20. את גאון עזכם, the pride of your power of resistance i.e. your national prosperity, which makes your land rich, that, out of which you draw the haughtiness for resistance to Mv Will. My Blessing grants it such wonderful abundance (verses 4 & 5); My Displeasure changes this to the opposite condition.

V. 21. קרי .ואם תלכו עמי קרי from קרה (see on Gen. 24,12) is all that occurs without our intention, and without our having reckoned on it. It is accordingly a purely relative conception. Something in itself can be intentional to the highest degree, and brought about with the greatest predetermination, yet to us it was quite beyond our reckoning or intent, and seems to us just “to have happened”, to us it is “chance”. Now הלך עם quite definitely means “going with somebody” i.e. going in agreement together with somebody, accordingly, when used, as here, of us with God, would indicate not behaving against His Will, but rather fulfilling that which is in accordance with His Will. In any case it designates, at least in comparison with the extreme stage of defection just described, a movement back to betterment. But it has the addition of קרי, your הלך עמי is only קרי. Your way of life being in agreement with My Will is only something fortuitous, casual, it happens to be in accordance, it is not your direct intention, your deliberate purpose, not what it should be, your very first determination, coming before any other consideration, to obey Me, only to do that which is in accordance with My Will. You are no longer in principle an opponent to My Will, but you are indifferent to it. Quite other considerations decide your line of conduct, and you leave it to chance whether it is in contradiction to Me or falls in with My Will; ולא תאבו לשמע לי, it is not your decision to take My Will into consideration in the very first place, and before each step that you take, to ask Me whether what you propose to do is also in accordance with My Will.

V. 22. והשלחתי בכם, cf. הנני משליח בך (Ex. 8,17). In contrast to V. 6, I withdraw the fear of Man which I have instilled into beast, and leave them to their natural tendency to attack you, ושכלה אתכם. See on Gen. 27,45. והמעיטה אתכם in contrast to V. 9.

V. 23 & 24. ואם באלה לא תוסרו לי, as already remarked on Gen. 2,19, יסר is for the moral nature of man what יצר is for material matter. It is the moral limiting his efforts, to keep them within the boundaries of what is good and right. The noun מוסר which generally also designates this morally constructive discipline, also occurs with the meaning of actual bonds and chains. הִוָסֵר ל- means to be moulded morally similarly to somebody i.e. to accept the direction of your will to correspond to his. All the troubles which occurred up to now were sent for the purpose of bringing home to them, how all the promised blessings of prosperity which go with obedience to the Will of God, power, peace, and riches only become lost to them the more they strive directly for these possessions and do not regard them as the result of keeping the Torah, the more they make the attaining of them the decisive factor for the efforts of their life, and where it seems to clash with it, allow consideration of the will of God to be relegated to the background. With the suffering depicted in the previous verse the last trait in the picture of the promised blessings disappears. With that, the tendency of their lives should have become redirected again towards God, and the fulfilment of His Will made their first single resolution.

But if this does not occur והלכתם עמי קרי, but your way with God still remains left to chance and convenience, then a treatment will commence which is repeatedly described here and in V. 28 & 41, as being on the part of God, too, as הולך עם- .הילך עמם בקרי used of God towards men, as in Ex. 33,16 and Deut. 20,4 & XXXI,6, always designates the protection and assistance of God accompanying man. If the suffering which has been sent to Israel will have had the effect that at least the extreme opposition in principle to the Torah has been broken, but Israel is still far away from allowing obedience to God and His Torah to be the first and only duty of life, but rather still placed in the foreground what they think is in the interest of their advantages and of their position in life, and leave their being in agreement with God to the realm of “chance”, and only keep God’s Laws as far as they “happen” not to interfere with their own supposed interests, then the further treatment which God will assign to them will assume exactly the same pattern.

As long as Israel gives itself up to God, doing its duty to God faithfully and leaves its fate trustfully in His Hands, for so long is its individual, social, and political existence, and the development of its prosperity and happiness, a special mark for God’s providence and direction. The flourishing of its existence, and the success of its endeavours, are independent of the ordinary laws of cause and effect which rule the physical and political world around it. “God turns His Face towards it” and “bears it aloft on eagles’ wings”. From its very beginning, Israel’s historical birth was not the result of the combination of the working of the usual causes which, in world history, have produced new nations, All external conditions were — and still are — against its birth and continued existence, and it lacks all the material foundations on which everywhere else nations depend. The “nation” Israel is simply an historical creative “Let there be” act of God. If Israel trifles away the mission for which God made it into a nation, then God has only to turn away His Face, His special particular providence and guidance, and by itself it falls to ruin in the midst of all the enemy elements which throughout the history of the world have worked against it. Not its downfall, its continued existence is the historical miracle of God. Its downfall would be merely the results of the given causes in the natural course of events. הסר משובתו, as it says in Is. 5,5, God has only to remove His special protection, והיה לבער and it falls to destruction by itself. But if it has not completely given up its “going with God”, if, as here the case is put, it has partly returned to the path laid down for it, it does “go with God” or goes again with Him, but it only does so בקרי, it leaves it to “chance”, this going with God is by no means the first and primary consideration for the choice of its path, it does not depend on it for the continuance of its existence and prosperity, but seeks existence and prosperity on quite other paths, and leaves it to chance how much or how little these ways “happen” to coincide with God’s ways, then God indeed does not let Israel be destroyed, then, in what it does still keep of God’s laws — though quite casually and quite unconscious of their true meaning — there lies a marvellous power of keeping it in existence for a better future, “God walks with them”, — but בקרי. He no longer bears them aloft on eagles’ wings over all the enemy forces working in the natural course of events against Israel’s existence and prosperity. Its existence and prosperity are no longer the mark of His special blessing and protecting miraculous powers. He rather leaves it over to the natural course of world history which in no wise furthers the existence and prosperity of a “nation of Jews”, a nation which should be directed solely by God’s Torah and by the moral feeling of duty, and lets them experience the whole weight of these enemy forces, inimical to their existence and prosperity. This giving Israel over to the natural course of events, in the development of which its existence and progress are never made with intention or premeditation, but on the contrary, are only granted as much space as the exigencies of the other nations “casually” leave room for, and everywhere and at all times, finds its interests furthered only as far as they “happen” to suit the interests of the other nations, this it is — unless we are greatly mistaken — what is pronounced by the proclamation: והלכתי אף אני עמכם בקרי. So it seems also to be understood in ת״כ where the explanation runs: אתם עשיתם את דיני עראי בעולם אף אני אעשה אתכם עראי בעולם, “you have made My Laws insignificant in the world, I will make you insignificant in the world”.

V. 25. והבאתי עליכם וגו׳. This חרב נוקמת וגו׳ is clearly an enemy force of a different sort to the one which is designated above in verses 16 & 17 as אויבים. It is characterised as being “a sword avenging the covenant, achieving the vengeance of the covenant”, and the covenant is not הברית the covenant with Israel, but ברית in general. If we understand this phrase correctly it refers to those world-conquering powers which arise from time to time in history, which, as we know from the Prophets, act, unknown to themselves, as an instrument in God’s Hands to purge the world of degenerated peoples, and to advance the history of the development of Man one step forward, until they too, having fallen into similar degeneration, suffer a similar fate. They are the Sword of God, to protect His covenant with mankind, which is threatened by the degeneration of the nations. For the great general principles of Justice, Morality and Humanity are regarded as a ברית (a ברית, an absolute promise to be fulfilled against any and all odds, which God gave Noah, the father of the new world, that ultimately the problems of life would be solved, and Man be happy I.L.) as the necessary conditions for the ברית which must form the foundations of the code for all human society. When the nations degenerate, then (Is. 24,5) the earth rises up against its inhabitants, because they have transgressed the Teaching of God, they have turned the Law of Morality into its very reverse, and have “broken the everlasting covenant” עברו תורות חלפו חוק הפרו ברית עולם; and the angels of peace weep over the wretchedness and desolation on earth because אנוש, degenerate Man, breaks “the covenant”, rejects the foundation of every social reconstruction and remains inaccessible to every reflection, הפר ברית מאס ערים לא חשב אנוש (ibid. XXXIII,8). Such an avenging sword for God’s covenant with Man was the Assyrian-Babylonian, the Persian, the Macedonian and the Roman world-conquering power. But such a sword is not נוקמת ברית, it does not avenge consciously and intentionally the treason practised against the covenant of God with Man, it is not wielded in the service of justice and morality, it is נוקמת נקם ברית, God has ordained the avengeance of the “covenant”, and it is only the blind instrument of its accomplishment. Its success results simply from the law of the power of the stronger over the weaker, of power over importance, of strategy over simplicity, of preparedness over carelessness. In the highway of all these world-wars lay Judea. Had Judea remained “the Land of God”, no sword would have dared to cross its boundaries, in the centre of all the world-shattering wars of conquest the land of Israel would have remained the land of peace. With the miraculous power of God’s protection forfeited, the little unwarlike Judea fell, in the most natural way, a prey to every wild conqueror. So that the first effect of the withdrawal of the special protection of God, its being left to the natural course of events, the introduction of קרי into the guidance of the fate of Israel which is promised henceforth is, accordingly: והבאתי עליכם חרב נוקמת נקם ברית, that God allows it to be invaded by the conquering sword of a world-power.
ונאספתם אל עריכם וגו׳, they flee into the fortified towns, there pestilential disease breaks out amongst the overcrowded masses of humanity, and to escape this they give themselves up to the enemy.

V. 26. בשברי וגו׳. The way is prepared for the plague by famine. — בתנור אחד, the ovens at that time were small portable ones, and usually sufficed only for the requirements of one household. But the scarcity of bread will be such, that ten families will have to be satisfied with the quantity that otherwise one family required. במשקל, bread will be so dear that one will jealously watch the other with exact scales that none should get one ounce more bread than the other.

V. 27 & 28. ואם בזאת וגו׳ בחמת קרי. As with ונתתם ביד אויב of V. 25, the ultimate result of the misfortunes of the war had already been announced, with which then, in V. 26, the associated calamities of war had been described, the pronouncement in V. 27 & 28, in the event of continued disobedience, of an increased state of famine resulting in the horrors depicted in V. 29 with the complete destruction of the land and its inhabitants, can only have in view a later final succumbing to the fury of conquering world powers. According to that, the ואם בזאת וגו׳ would mean: — If by such experiences of war, through which you fall into the hands of a world power wielding the avenging sword of God’s covenant with man, you have not been taught your complete helplessness without God’s Protection, have not been brought back to definite faithfulness to God’s Torah, then I will make you experience the same fate again but in the whole intensity of its utmost fury. This ruthless fury of happenings, the whole destructive fury of a savage conquerer towards a weak disarmed people, is called חמת קרי.

V. 29. ואכלתם בשר וגו׳. This is preceded by the והבאתי עליכם חרב וגו׳ ונאספתם וגו׳ ,בשברי לכם וגו׳ of the preceding events, and here only continues with the calamitous final catastrophe! ובשר בנותיכם וגו׳ seems to be a still higher degree of gruesomeness in the horror.

V. 30. & 31. The destruction by the concueror starts at the periphery and finishes at the centre, the place of the Sanctuary; first the erections and the emblems of gods to be found in the open, גלוליכם ,חמניכם ,במתיכם; then the cities, עריכם, and finally במתיכם .מקדשיכם are the altars erected to God, forbidden by the Torah, (Deut. 12,13), by which just subjective caprice, and indifference to the Torah of God, which is deposited in the one central sanctuary is begotten and nurtured. (See Ch. VIII & IX). It came from the use of such altars, erected at will, at any place, that even right next to them, although they were dedicated to our unique God, emblems dedicated to the worship of the sun, חמנים were to be found yea, even גלולים, the most despicable appellation of heathen gods were also to be found there. For גלל is animal excrement, that which the body rejects, throws out as being entirely unassimilateable. By the name גלולים, idols are designated as being of such a nature that is so completely the antithesis of pure human beings, that it should be repulsive to us being completely incompatible to us, and where it is nevertheless cherished and fostered, the deepest depravity is intimated.

פגריכם. The relationship to בגר ,בקר etc., shows that the basic meaning of פגר is to be free, to be unmastered, to be abandoned, given up, and designates a dead body looked at from that angle. A living body belongs to the living individuality which is inherent to it, it is mastered and guided by it. When this has left it, the body has lost its master and owner, is free from him, but thereby it is abandoned to the power of every other mastery, especially to the influence of the elements. From this non-mastery of the body the word פגר has the meaning of being inert, sluggish in carrying out an obligation; probably, as it occurs in this sense in I. Sam. 30,11 & 12, to lag behind because of tiredness, faintness. The soul has not the power to move its body to accomplish the demanded action. פגרי גילוליכם, a smashed idol is also the dead body, the carcase of a god. As long as it stands undamaged and honoured, it has the conception of a god to its worshippers, and thereby has a meaning which goes beyond the mere wood or stone. Once it is broken down, the destruction itself is a denial of the imagined godly power that was inherent to it, the idea flies away, and it lies there — even, although, on account of its past, ע״ז של ישראל אין לה ביטול עולמית Avoda Zara 53a. — a mere mass of empty material.

V. 31. מקדשיכם. The conception of the מקרש is sometimes expressed in the plural, referring to all its halls. So probably already above in Ch. 21,23. Also in Ps. 24,7, LI,51, and elsewhere. The Sanctuary there is regarded in the three stages represented by its three divisions, not so much as being the place of sanctity, as the place of sanctifying, looked at from the point of view of its purpose. Hence here in quite special apt poignancy: - the holy places which should have made you holy.
ולא אריח וגו׳: regardless of the fact that there you still brought in offerings, the symbolic expression of your devotion to carrying out My Will.

That at the time of desruction there could be, next to each other, such extremes of symbols of God and the gods: גלולים ,חמנים ,במות, and then also מקדש ה׳ and קרבנות, shows very exactly conditions which could only develop under a regime of indifference and superficiality which characterise the הלוך עם ה׳ קרי. There must be other considerations and purposes than considerations of God and His puposes that are the decisive factors for the standard of life, hence one is neither definitely עובד ע״ז nor definitely עבד ה׳. That is why self-appointed Bama service of God, yea, even heathen worship of gods, could flourish next to the Temple of the One Unique God, and this Temple and its offerings were cared for, and next to it also Bamath and idolatry. They wanted to be on the right side in any case, and imagined, as Elijah put it, that they could serve Baal as well as God, and at bottom were not enthusiastic about either, but had quite other interests in which possibly “by chance” one or the other might be interested, as the case might be. As a matter of fact, the destruction did not occur when the defection was at its height, not at the time of a Menasseh but only after the faithful regenerating works of a Hezekiah who had preceded him, and of Josiah who succeeded him, had strewn the seeds of betterment.

V. 32. והשמתי אני וגו׳. Everything up to now was the natural working of a conquest which God had refrained from curbing; what follows — the permanent desolation of the land that, whereas under the blessing of God it developed an extraordinary state of productive perfection, henceforth was to sink below the level of even ordinary productiveness — is as much a direct special touch of the Finger of God, as was the previous abundance. That, והשמתי אני, that, I will bring about. The land will remain desolate and your enemies, who will live there in your place, will not prosper.

V. 33. זרה .ואתכם אזרה is the real expression for letting the wind blow the chaff away in all directions, which is why the winnower, the tool that is used for it is called מזרה.
