It is an expression which most aptly describes the disposition of Israel amongst the nations. והריקתי וגו׳, and it is the sword of the enemy and the fear of it which will first drive you to all parts of the world. והיתה ארצכם וגו׳: you without the land, and the land without you, neither, when separated, will avoid desolation.

V. 34. והרצת את שבתתיה ,אז תרצה וגו׳. Similarly in 5,41, ואז ירצו את עונם and V,43, והם ירצו את עונם ,ותרץ את שבתתיה וגי. It is not easy to be quite sure of the meaning of the root רצה in these expressions, although the context is quite clear, and it undoubtedly means an atoning reparation for sins. It has first of all to be noted that רצה by no means simply has the meaning “to desire or wish”, i.e. to decide to do something. Only in one single instance does it occur with a verb as object — רצה ה׳ להצילני Ps. 40,14 — in all other instances it has a noun, or a pronoun, as object and is construed with ב- or את as לא בשוקי האיש ירצה (Ps. 147,10 & 11), or רוצה ה׳ את יראיו, i.e. to find the satisfying of His Will with something or to find something that does satisfy His Will. But it also expresses the reciprocal feeling, finding the satisfaction of our own will in giving satisfaction to the will of another. This meaning is frequently very clear in the noun. Whereas in לעשות רצונך א׳ חפצתי (Ps. 40,9), and elsewhere it designates that which is in accordance with God’s Will, the satisfaction which God finds with us, in נפתלי שבע רצון (Deut. 33,23) ורצון שכני סנה (ibid. 16) חיים ברצונו (Ps. 30,6) ויפק רצון מה׳ (Prov. 18,22) and frequently elsewhere, it designates the satisfaction of our wishes which God’s well-wishing grants to us. So that רצון means satisfaction, as well as the will to satisfy the wishes of another. In the verb this meaning appears specially as the designation of the regranting of well-wishing which had already been lost. So, in ותרצני (Gen. 33,6); יעתר אל אלוה וירצהו (Job. 33,26) רצית ה׳ ארצך (Ps. 85,2). This dual meaning of the idea seems to be similar in the root רעה (which indeed in Chaldean is equivalent to רצה). There again in a similar manner it has the meaning of both feeding the flock (granting pasturage) and the flock feeding (enjoying or receiving pasturage) (the word graze in English has also exactly the same meaning I.L.) See Gen. 4,2.

So that in the expression רצה עון the sin committed seems to be regarded as something that awaits satisfaction. Every sin once committed is not something done and finished with, it is a debt incurred “which can be satisfied and which awaits satisfaction”. For as long as the sinner lacks the right perception of things, the sin complains at God’s Court of Justice, does not let the matter rest but makes it into a debt that is always there and demands payment. As soon as the right perception dawns, this nature of the sin committed rejoices, as thereby the possibility of reparation is given, it begins to “find satisfaction of the sin-debt”. It is the stage of atonement, of which, when it is achieved, it says נרצה עונה (Isaiah 40,2).

Hier tritt nun diese Doppelseite der Befriedigung in der ganzen Schärfe des Ausdrucks hervor: תרצה הארץ את שבתותיה und והרצת את שבתותיה. Alle die Jahre bleibender Verödung werden als ebenso viele Bodenschabbate der Jobel- und Schebiit-Institution begriffen. Die von uns nicht gehaltenen Bodenschabbate stehen als eine Schuld da, die ihrer Befriedigung harrt. Diese Schuld wird abgetragen durch die Verödung des Landes während unseres Exils. Das Land freut sich seiner Schabbatöde während unseres Exils und gewährt damit den von uns vernachlässigten Bodenschabbaten Befriedigung. In der Tat, wie שמיטה und יובל die weithin unter die Völker leuchtenden, großen nationalen Bekenntnistaten der Gotteshuldigung im Staatenleben sein sollten: so ist die von Gott angekündigte, von Gott verhängte, von Gott vollzogene und alle die Jahrhunderte unseres Exils hindurch bis auf den heutigen Tag erhaltene Verödung des Bodens des heiligen Landes das große Ausrufungszeichen in dem Gottesbuch der Geschichte, daß Gottes die Erde sei und Er die Erfüllung Seines Gesetzes auf Erden erwartet. So auch wohl:ת׳׳כ אני אמרתי לכם שתהיו זורעים שש ומשמטים לי אחת בשביל שתדעו שהארץ שלי היא ואתם לא עשיתם כן אלא עמדו וגלו ממנה והיא תשמט מאליה כל שמיטים שהיא חייבת לי.

V. 36. & 37. מרך related to מרק, fluid, boiled to a pulp, hence מרך soft, timid, muddled; used of the heart: lack of courage, the opposite of חזק יב, similar to מגג and מסס of heart. בארצות איביהם on strange soil in the midst of hostile people who deny them the rights of domicile, and embitter their lives, they will not have bright courage for life, or the virile insistence on obtaining their human rights. Yea, ורדף אתם וגו׳ etc., they will live in constant fear of attack and mishandling, even where no danger of it is threatened. וכשלו וגו׳ and, living in such fear that makes each one think only of his own safety, there will be no solidarity amongst them, and without intending to do so, one gets ruined through the other. ולא תהיה לכם וגו׳: whereas while you were faithful to the Torah, God led you קוממיות, the consciousness of God, and of your sole allegiance to Him gave you self-confidence, and raised you above all and everything, now, you will not have the strength to stand upright before your enemies and make a stand for yourselves.

V. 38. ואבדתם וגו׳. As the next verse speaks of הנשארים בכם this ואבדתם בגוים can not announce complete destruction. It is either being lost in the masses, disappearing from notice, as שה אובד (Ps. 119,16), and האובדים בארץ אשור (Is. 27,13), or, as after all, ואכלה אתכם ארץ וגו׳ does designate a wasting destruction, here, too, probably an actual destruction of part of the nation is proclaimed.

V. 39 & 41. והנשארים בכם etc. והתודו etc. אף אני אלך etc. For these who still remain left after all these crushing events of the first period of exile, there are two alternatives for the future of the exile, depending on how they understand their mission in exile, and carry it out. Either, the whole weight of what they have had to live through has not yet brought them to the right frame of mind towards God, instead of bringing them to greater faithfulness to the Torah, the exile has the effect of loosening still further the bonds that should keep them to obedience to the laws of God; they see in the exile an excuse for not keeping the duties of the Torah, בארצות איביכם, living in conditions which are calculated to suit everything else rather than observance of the Torah, they say that the Torah was only meant to be kept in Palestine; strangers, in strange lands, faced with adverse hostile conditions, they persuade themselves that the duty of self-preservation at least excuses defection from God’s Torah, as Ezekiel in 20,32, characterises this error in the exile אשר אתם אומרים נהיה כגוים כמשפחות האדמה. This would be עונם, the new exile-sin, the conscious defection, excusing itself on the grounds of altered circumstances which בארצות איביכם is begotten on the foreign lands. Naturally then, that of course עונות אבתם אתם the sins of their fathers, which brought them into exile, still stay with them, and exile has not yet cured them of that indifference that “leaves walking in God’s paths”, just to “chance”. If this is so, then ימקו בעונם בארצות אויביכם מקק .ואף בעונות אבתם אתם ימקו, phonetically related to מכך ,מיי ,מגג means rotting, decaying (see Nidda 69b). With this עון, with this new and continued defection from God’s laws, the one principle of life disappears, that, even in exile could have revived them to a “live” nation, flourishing in a unique galut-blossoming of spiritual and active life developing from the Torah. Without this life-principle the galut becomes a grave for them, and ימקו בעונם, and instead of attaining “life”, as they had so erroneously imagined, by casting off all their peculiar characteristics, they perish, “decay”, through their sin.

והתודו. This will go on until they recognise the fact that their continued defection, their continued treating the laws of the Torah indifferently, as if merely of secondary importance, has not helped them to “life”, but to “decay”, spiritually, socially and morally. This will then ultimately bring them to self-knowledge and self-confession and they will admit that במעלם אשר מעלו בי, that in their Galut unfaithfulness and אף אשר הלכו עמי בקרי in the indifference with which they have just casually kept parts of God’s Torah, they עונם ועון אבותם, like their fathers before them, have only departed from the straight path which is shown them to lead to life and happiness, and will confess to themselves that their defection and indifference was “sinful”.

אף אני. Just as they had not completely broken with Me, but, although only as a secondary consideration, had remained in contact with My Torah (see on V.21), so I, too, in spite of their old and fresh sins, will not entirely give them up, I will keep with them, but likewise בקרי. I will leave them entirely to the influences of the historical happenings of the nations amongst whom they live. But בקרי, in all these happenings, which seem to them to be just unlucky “chance”, I shall be with them, shall not let them be entirely destroyed, yea, והבאתי אתם בארץ אויביהם. This can hardly mean: “I will bring them into the land of their enemies”. Apart from the fact that to come to a land is, as a rule, expressed by אל הארץ, and בא בארץ generally means an enemy incursion into a land — cf. Josh. 2,18, Judges 6,8, Kings II. 6,23, & XIII,20, (perhaps with the single exception of Sam. I. 9,5), — here, they are described as already being in the land of their enemy, whither already in V,33, their being scattered had been announced, and according to the whole context this והבאתי אתם seems to be the last phase in the one alternative of the future, the other beginning with the immediately following: או אז וגו׳. We think, therefore, that the והבאתי אתם is meant to be taken by itself, and בארץ אויביהם is not the place to which they are to be brought, but the place where והבאתי אתם will take place. Now בא by itself does not designate simply “to come”, but, as a rule, to come to a place where one belongs, “to come home”. So that בא is really the opposite of יצא, and הביא of הוציא. And הביא by itself is especially used for the ultimate return of the exiles to their original home. Thus, ממזרח אביא זרעך (Is. 43,5). הביאו בני מרחוק (ibid. 6); בעת ההיא אביא אתכם (Zep. 3,20). And so the והבאתי אתם here, too, would mean: I will bring them home, I will bring them to their old home again, בארץ אויביהם in the land of their enemies. בקרי, in all the world-historical events, which apparently are nothing further off than being for the purpose of the spiritual and political rehabilitation of these exiles, I am walking with them. All the painfully educative effects of the ordeals they have to endure in the land of their enemies, as well as the development of the events of the history of the world itself, will ultimately have the final result that these exiles mature to be fit for independence, and the trend of the events of the nations itself will bring them to their homeland. So the long exile “in the land of their enemies” over all their old and new mistakes is, in spite of everything, nothing but an והבאתי אותם, by a long circuitous route, under the invisible guidance of God, the achievement of leading them home to their old homeland, to their eternally unloseable old calling.

או אז: or the other possibility of the alternative for their future becomes realised. Instead of continuing on in the sins of their fathers, and increasing them by the addition of new exile sins, אז, after all the crushing blows of the first period of the exile, the hearts of הנשארים בכם of those that have outlived that time, become bowed down, bowed down before God, and cease to be ערל towards God, that the heart gives up its hitherto intractableness against God (see on Gen. 17,10), ואז, then, not having to wait till the end of time, but then ירצו את עונם, they will bear and carry out the whole fate of their further exile cheerfully as רצוי עונם, as the means of making good again and “satisfying” the debt of the sins of their past. Thereby the whole Galut receives a different aspect. Instead of being a grave of decay, it itself becomes the ground for a new carrying-out of their mission, the fertile soil for a Galut-life directed towards God, and kept in connection with God, the purpose and meaning of which is called ירצו עונם. The הלוו עם ה׳ בקרי, the indifference, which in happy circumstances in one’s own land works, in the first place, for independance of livelihood, and well-being and good living, and leaves carrying out the Will of God as a matter of casual secondary importance, is atoned for, when, thrown into the power of forces which are indifferent, cold, obstructing, or even in burning hatred actively opposing Jewish existence and the Jewish mode of life, nevertheless only thinking of carrying out the Jewish calling is made the first consideration of life, and everything else, existence, progress, and enjoyment of life is left, as secondary considerations, to the chance of God’s arranging matters. The careless attitude towards God’s Torah in our own land is atoned for by a careless attitude towards our own existence for the sake of faithfulness to the dictates of God’s Torah.

V. 42. וזכרתי את בריתי וגו׳: it does not say בריתי עם or את יעקב etc., but בריתי אברהם ,בריתי יצחק ,בריתי יעקב. So that clearly it is not the covenant with Jacob etc., but Jacob, Isaac and Abraham are in apposition to בריתי. There is an Abraham Covenant of God, an Isaac Covenant of God, and a Jacob Covenant of God. Similarly to הנני נותן לו את בריתי שלום in Numb. 25,1, where שלום is the covenant of God which He gives Pinchas. The ברית the absolute promise of God (see Gen. 6,18), that is called שלום, the peace on earth which, in spite of all opposing disturbances, God promises will form the final state of matters on earth, He has entrusted, not to fainthearted and mercenary compromising spirits, but to those who steadfastly honestly stand up, with self-forgetting courage, with the zeal of a Pinchas. In the same way, for the historical development of the Jews, God has established a ברית which is called Abraham, a ברית which is called Isaac, and one which is called Jacob. All three, Abraham Isaac and Jacob were near to God, the lives and fate of all three were directed by God, and had significance for the foundation of their nation, and yet each one of them had a different position in the world. Corresponding to the tradition that Abraham originated the morning prayer, Isaac Mincha, and Jacob the night prayer, the different position in the world of each of them was in accordance with these times of the day. Abraham’s lot fell in increasing brightness. Happy, and richly blessed in all and by all, he stood, although alone, against the whole world and called them to the altar of a One Unique God. Nevertheless none were jealous of him, none were his enemies; yea, highly honoured, he lived as נשיא אלקים in their midst. Isaac’s position was already clouded. Isolated by treading his path with God, he found only jealousy on account of the blessings He gave him amongst his contemporaries, and was thrown back on himself and his own home. Finally, on Jacob, the shades of night fell; his whole life was a chain of trials and tribulation, and only seldom and for a short time, did the external joy of life smile on him. And yet all three were the Fathers of our People, all three bearers of the Covenant of God, and Jacob’s hard position in the world no less a revelation of the nearness of God in Man’s fate in life than the bright picture of Abraham’s life. That is why here all three are separately mentioned as ברית, and thereby God’s Promise is proclaimed to the nation, whose ancestors and roots they form, that its fate, too, would be a varied one, as those of its fathers were, without thereby ceasing to be the mark of God’s special proximity and of God’s special guidance and attention. And that, like Abraham Isaac and Jacob, in the midst of the nations of the world, whether their fate be like that of an Abraham, bright, rich and honoured, or of an Isaac, rich but envied and disliked and rebuffed, or of a Jacob, full of trials and troubles, in all cases they have to bear themselves and behave as true and faithfull sons of the covenant.

In connection with what was said before, the three promises of the covenant are significantly placed in inverted order, the covenant “Jacob” first, and moreover by being written in full, מלא, as well as by the accent and the construction of the sentence, it is brought into prominence. It is given as the principle promise to be considered quite specially to which the covenant “Isaac” and the covenant “Abraham” are only attached by אף as extension and continuation.

With the beginning of the Galut the children of the Abrahamite covenant entered into the “Jacob” fate. But if — as is assumed in the second half of V,21, when introducing the other possibility of the future of the Galut — they take the Galut with its bitterness in its true right meaning as רצוי עונם, as an atoning nullification of the debt of their past, and in true faithfulness to duty, pay it off in such a way that they work themselves upwards towards the absolute opposite of their previous mistakes, the וזכרתי את בריתי יעקב, then will I fulfil My covenant-promise “Jacob”. I will be with them through all the long, long, Galut-night, and will form even their darkest Galut-night to an illuminating revelation of Divine Guidance, as they, the faithful, like bright stars of cheerful sacrificing devotion show up the spiritual and moral calling of human beings in living and dying. And then, when they have endured enough, and in world-historic martyrdom have entered their faithfulness to duty with their blood in the pages of history of misfortune, then ואף את בריתי יצחק, then they will not have lived and bled in the midst of the nations for nothing, by the example of their lives, the spirit of the nations becomes enlightened and their manners milder, with the dawning morn of the world, the darkest midnight of their Galut also passes, they begin to breathe freely again and to prosper in the lands where hitherto they had been so sadly persecuted. And just as in the Jacob period they had to endure the hate, now like Isaac it is the jealousy and rebuff of the nations that they are made to suffer. Now they have to go through the second school of the Galut for their whole attitude to life, truly no easy one. They learn, in growing prosperity under the regime of nations swaying between humaneness and envy, not to assimilate, but, Isaac-like to keep their own Jewish characters; to use the richer and freer forces they now possess only for increased faithfulness to the Torah, and, undisturbed by being isolated by the envy of the nations, to develop a more perfect, more versatile development of their particular task in Galut. Then, when they have successfully passed the second Galut-test, remaining faithful to the Torah in prosperity, then ואף את בריתי אברהם אזכור, then the Abraham sun will shine for them in Galut, then Abraham-like, they will build their alters to God and His Torah in the midst of the nations; Abraham-like, they will make the nations so realise the abundance of all that is true and good that the Teachings of God have entrusted to them for the salvation of mankind, that they will not be tolerated, not be honoured, although they are Jews, the People of the Abraham covenant, but because they are Jews, because they are the People of the Abraham-covenant, because, in spirit and deed they know and practice God’s Law for the salvation of mankind. And just as Jacob’s fight through the night with the Genius of Esau did not come to an end until Jacob had wrested from him his acknowledgement and succeeded in receiving his blessing, so the children of Jacob and Isaac, hated for so long, then tolerated and begrudged will finally, as the people of Abraham in the midst of the nations, receive the reverential, acknowledging greeting נשיא אלקים אתה בתוכנו! Then, ultimately, when in Galut they have learnt to overcome all the dangerous rocks of the enmity of the nations, of the favour of the nations, of the example of the nations, and of arrogance in good fortune, on which originally in their own land their faithfulness to the Torah foundered, then, only then והארץ אזכר, when they have become “Abraham”, will I, too, bring them to the land promised to Abraham, and give them back the land for a final permanent carrying out of their mission to be the People of God on the Land of His Torah. So that ברית יעקב and ברית יצחק and ברית אברהם form the three progressive stages of the tasks the performance of which in Galut achieves the atonement of their guilt and at the same time matures them for the future permanent return to the land of their independence.

V. 43. והארץ וגו׳. For the land, of which it has just been said, that when the people will have become mature for their final purpose, it, too, will regain its purpose to be the land for God’s people to keep the whole of God’s Torah, the land, until then will await its people in desolation. It will serve no other people as a suitable soil for their development. By lying idle it will make reparation for the Sabbaths that were not kept, and it will remain desolate for as long as the people, by their life in exile, have to make reparation for the guilt of their past.

יען וביען: all corresponding to, and in accordance with, i.e. the whole fate of the Galut completely corresponds to their sins. The guilt of their sins is atoned for by the exercise of just those virtues which are the exact opposite of the sins. The sins which weighed on them as a guilt to be atoned for were, that במשפטי מאסו, that they rejected God’s regulations for social life, that they depended on other maxims for the rules of their national civil lives; and also את חקתי געלה נפשם, that they felt their individual happiness restricted by the Laws of the Torah, and refused to comply with them as cramping their lives, especially the laws that affected their enjoyment of food and their other senses. Corresponding to the one, their national social life was shattered for centuries, and for centuries they had to live in foreign states as aliens without any civil rights, excluded from the blessing of security which the possession of rights confers they had to feel only oppression and harshness handed to them as their due right. Corresponding to the other, their individual happiness in life was stunted for centuries, and all participations in the pleasures and enjoyments of life remained curtailed to them. And just as the reproving punishment fits the crime, so does the corresponding virtue atone for it. They had placed social advance ment, and individual gain, and pleasure as the first consideration for their lives, and the Torah and its demands had to retire to the background if and when it interfered with these. The corresponding virtue had to atone. For centuries they had to live and move in personal and factual conditions under which almost any keeping of the Torah had to be paid for with the giving up of some pleasure, with the renunciation of some of one’s rights. In such circumstances the Torah must really appear — in the words of the Prophet — as חוקים לא טובים and as משפטים לא יחיו בהם yea, for centuries for faithfulness to the Torah they could only expect misery and wretchedness, prison and the stake. They had only to utter one single word declaring their renunciation of the Torah to save themselves and their children from all this misery and wretchedness, and to enable them to participate in all the pleasures of the world — but this word they may not utter, with God’s Torah in their arms they must cheerfully mount the scaffold, be tied to the stake; for the fulfilment of this Torah they must cheerfully build their huts, contract their marriages, bring up their children, live their lives, die their deaths, heedless of what sacrifices and privations, what persecutions, what wretchedness they are prescribing for their own and their childrens’ lot. Always and in every case they must place keeping God’s Torah as the first unconditional consideration, against which everything else, all thoughts of one’s position in life, of pleasures of life, must retreat to the background as of secondary importance, with this indifference to the pleasures of life they must make good their former indifference to faithfulness to the Torah, and thus, ביען, by the corresponding virtue achieve יען .רצוי עונם: the state of suffering corresponds to the sin, and with faithfulness to the Torah in the state of suffering the sin is fitly atoned for.

Above it says: ואם בחקותי תמאסו ואם את משפטי תגעל נפשכם, here במשפטי מאסו ואת חקתי געלה נפשם; Now מאס ב- is to find a defect on something, it is an objective judgment without any consideration of the relation of the object to us. געל, on the other hand, designates the repulsive objection we find in something — it is accordingly frequently construed with נפש as subject — it is a subjective judgment. Generally speaking, חקים the moral limitations to our senses, will jar against our subjective dislike, whereas one critises משפטים civil laws objectively, finds something faulty, unjust, unwise in them. Thus our verse here. And it is just because the verbs are changed over in the verse above, that, as ק״א already remarks, the way the ת״כ takes it seems justified. The defect there no longer refers to the חקים which he has long ago given up in his own life, so he has no more any objection to them personally, subjectively, but to those which come objectively to his notice, and his personal objection is to those Jewish regulations which he can not avoid coming into contact with in his social life.

V. 44. ואף גם זאת. In verses 38—43 two possibilities are indicated as alternatives for the future course of the Galut; the one, that the end of the exile will be brought about as the result of external events in the world, the other, that the exiles will achieve the גאולה by their own internal change of behaviour. These are the same two eventualities to which our sages point in Sanhedrin 98a, on Isaiah 60,22, זכו אחישנה, if they merit it, I will expedite it, לא זכו בעתה but otherwise I shall let circumstances force it at the proper time. In any case the first step into exile is at the same time the first step towards the redemption. Now here it says ואף גם זאת “but even this also”, or as it is usually understood “and nevertheless”, בהיותם בארץ איביהם, even if the time for the redemption is a long period, even if they remain on foreign soil a long time, לא מאסתים וגו׳, this does not mean that I have found them blameworthy and opposed to My Wishes to such a degree as to bring about their entire destruction, לכלתם, to cease My Covenant with them, but אני ה׳ אלקיהם, in all circumstances I remain their God.

V. 45. וזכרתי להם וגו׳. This ברית ראשונים is not the ברית אבות already mentioned above, but ת״כ explains it, and as is evident from the addition אשר הוצאתי וגו׳ refers to the ברית שבטים, the covenant renewed with their descendants, who indeed still required the purifying effects of the Egyptian Galut melting-pot and whom I nevertheless considered worthy of the great historic redemption before the eyes of the world, to prove to them that I was their Guide and Leader. אני ה׳ I am that same God still now, I will fulfil My Promise, be with them in Galut even as I was with their forefathers in Galut, and will redeem them even as I redeemed their forefathers, and remain their God, even as I did to their forefathers.

V. 46. אלה החקים וגו׳. This looks back on all the teachings and commands, regulating morals, ordering justice, ennobling hearts and thoughts which have been given from מתן תורה until now. Concerning them, i.e. of all the divine laws, it says: אשר נתן ה׳ בינו וגו׳ that God had given between Himself and the children of Israel. They are the one and only conditional and connecting agent between us and God. For us there is no other intervention, no other way to God than the way over his Torah, which is just what the: תוכחה אט בחקתי etc. teaches, that our nearness to God, our weal and our woe, are decided solely by our keeping or not keeping this Torah. They were all, not only the “Ten Commandments”, all the הקים משפטים ותודות, given by God at the same time on Mount Sinai, all of equal importance and equal worth. And what was given on Mount Sinai was not limited to that which was written down here, but included everything that was given to Moses in explanation of the meaning and spirit underlying the laws, and the details of the performance, to be transmitted to the children of Israel, and by them to their children by word of mouth. בהר סיני ביד משה מלמד שניתנה (ת״כ) התורה הלכותיה ודקדוקיה ופרושיה ע״י משה מסיני.

V. 1. The contents of this third book consisted of instructions as to how the Sanctuary of the Torah which had been erected, was to fulfil its purpose, by symbolic ritual of the offerings, and of teachings, for leading an individual and national holy life. Then finally, at the end of the previous chapter, retrospectively, the משפטים ,חקים and תורות the demands for our activities for such private and national sanctified lives, were declared as being the sole means of our connection and bond with God, and the sole means of our welfare and happiness.

Now follows as the concluding chapter, a chapter dealing with the possibility of free-willed gifts to the Sanctuary. It tells how the case is to be treated when somebody feels the necessity, or cherishes the wish to present an object or its value to the Sanctuary to express thereby his special interest in the Sanctuary, or his idea that the object in question has some special relation to the Sanctuary. All such endowments or gifts are expressed as כי יפליא נדר) הפלאת נדר), as something not demanded by the Torah, not originating from any of the demands of the Torah, but purely as an act directed by one’s own feelings and wishes. It is extremely significant that this chapter on gifts to the Temple is quite clearly, by its position in the book, only to be taken as an additional supplementary concluding chapter, and definitely does not belong to the חוקים משפטים ותורות which God has set as the condition בינו ובין בני ישראל, the fulfilment of which results in the whole abundance of blessing, and their non-fulfilment in the whole unspeakable misery depicted in the previous chapter. These laws concerning endowments and gifts to the Temple are strikingly separated from them, and that tells us the not insignificant fact: The Jewish תורת כהנים, the Jewish codex of the laws of the priests, declares Temple endowments and vows of gifts as being not such specially pious God-pleasing acts, and least of all does it ascribe to them the slightest value as atonement for leading a sinful life. Not in gaining riches or possessions, but in gaining souls and hearts, in gaining lives of individuals and the national life in the fulfilment of the חוקים משפטים and תורות does the Jewish priesthood of the Sanctuary see its task and mission. Its members point to “sanctification of morals and of the life of the senses” חוקים, to “justice, truth and right dealing in social life”, משפטים and “clarity of thought and ennoblement of the heart”, תורות, as the one “means of obtaining grace”, as the one and only way which — בינו ובין בני ישראל — joins men to God, and God to men.

V. 2. איש כי יפליא נדר. See on Ch. 22,21. בערכך נפשת. See Ch. 5,15. ערך according to its basic meaning, to place things which belong together next to each other (phonetically related to ארג to weave, joining together threads running parallel to one another) also means to place next to each other in judgment, אין ערוך אליך, there is nothing one can place next to Thee (Ps. 40,6); ומה דמות תערכו לו (Is. 40,18). Hence also, to realise the value or worth of something, to imagine what can be placed next to something as its equal. לא יערכנה פטדת כוש ,לא יערכנה זהב, not gold, not the most precious stones represent the worth of wisdom (Job. 28,17 & 19). ערך the realisation of the meaning, the expression of the value, לא ידע אנש ערכה (ibid. 13). ערך נפשות, is accordingly, the expression of the value, the estimation of the worth of persons. ערך נפשות לה׳ of persons for God, i.e. for the Sanctuary, the declaration of the worth, the meaning a person has for the Sanctuary. And ערכך נפשות, thy, the expression of thy, the nation’s, estimation of the value of its members. This ערך is to be differentiated from כסף ישיב ,כסף (Ex. XXI.32), וחצו את כספו (ibid. 35). כסף is the monetary value, and as long as slave-dealing exists, there can be a cash value for a person, one can estimate the cash value of a person by his ability to work, just as one values the utility value of any other object. Such a monetary value is called in Jewish legal terms דמים, and were someone to say דמי פלוני עלי or דמי עלי, the amount to be paid to the Sanctuary would have to be ascertained in each individual case. ערך does not mean such monetary value. ערך, and especially ערכך, is the expression of an ideal, imaginary value, the expression of the imaginary value a person has to God and His Sanctuary. This value is given as a fixed one, it has absolutely nothing to do with physical, spiritual, intellectual, moral or social qualities, and rises or falls purely according to sex and age. This universal equality is already expressed in the term ערכך נפשות, it is only the נפשות as such which are to be considered and every living person is a נפש (see Arachin 2a, et seq.).

V. 3—7. ועד בן ששים שנה. In 5,7 it says ואם מבן ששים שנה ומעלה. and from the ומעלה can be deduced that this period is reckoned as beginning only after the sixtieth year, but the sixtieth year itself belongs to the previous period. מבן עשרים שנה עד בן ששים שנה the שנת ששים כלמטה הימנה, from which it is taken that in this whole scale it is to be taken that עד ועד בכלל, and that in all the cases בן ששים ,בן עשרים etc., designates having reached the end of that year. Similarly בן חדש in V,6, means the completion of the first month just, as in Numb. 3,15 et seq. at the counting of the לוים and the בכורים it always says מבן חדש ומעלה, so that יום שלשים כלמטה הימנה the thirtieth day lies outside the ערך scale and אין ערך לפחות מבן חדש (Arachin 18a).

V. 8. ואם מך הוא מערכך. If the one who has made the vow is too poor to be able to pay the amount of the ערך-scale ועמידו לפני הכהן והעריך אתו וגו׳, then the person whose ערך he had vowed, has to be placed before the priest, והעריך אתו הכהן וגו׳, and the priest has to fix the amount of the ערך to be paid, according to the capabilities of the one who made the vow.

From this order of the Torah והעמידו וגו׳ ,והעריך the Gemora deduces, Arachin 4a, that the Torah presumes the possibility of standing the one to be valued before the priest, so that neither מת, one who is dead, nor גוסס, one who is dying, comes under the valuation, כל שישנו בהעמדה ישנו בהערכה etc. — In Arachin 23b, we are told that the ערך-vow is taken as a legal debt, and ממשכנין אותו, if necessary, the payment is exacted by distraint, but that nevertheless, in cases of poverty the consideration has always to be made that the necessities for food, clothing, furniture, and tools for work are left in natura, or enough money left for their acquisition. This procedure is called מסדרין (an arrangement) and according to Baba Mezia 114a, the same consideration has to be made in cases of legal seizure against proven debts, כדרך שמסדרין בערכין כך מסדרין בבעל חוב, this consideration is probably already implied by the term ואם מך הוא מערכך. Were it to say ,אם דל הוא ואין ידו משגת as in Ch. XIV.21, or ואם לא תגיע ידו or לא תשיג ידו as in Ch. 5,7, & 11, the case would be described as the absolute impossibility to pay, the non-existence of the means to pay, in which a reduction of the ערך is to be made. But מך designates only a beginning of becoming poor (see XXV,25), and מך מערכך means he is not rich enough for the fixed ערך amount to be in accordance with his means. The absolute amount to pay would be forthcoming, but then he would have to deprive himself of even the most necessary means for his existence. But that is just what he is not to do, and even in such a case a reduction is to be made by a כהן. In Baba Mezia 114a, too, the teaching of מסדרין בערכין ובבע״ח is attached to the term גמר :מך מיכה מיכה. In Arachin 24a, the procedure is attached to the sentence ואם מך הוא מערכך החייהו מערכך “do not let him forfeit his existence through the ערך״. Then ואם מך הוא מערכך would also be taken as, if “it”, i.e. his existence is threatened by the ערך.

So that the subject of this precept of the Torah is the case where somebody makes a vow to give to the Sanctuary a sum which represents the ערך of a נפש לה׳, the value which a certain person, himself or another, has to God. This sum is fixed here by a universal scale according to age and sex. The ages are divided into four periods, from the end of the first month to the end of the fifth year, from there to the end of the twentieth year, from there to the end of the sixtieth year, from there onwards until the end of life. The ערך for a male person in these various stages of life is, five, twenty, fifty and fifteen Shekels respectively; for a female it is three, ten, thirty, and ten, respectively. Surely these fixed amounts are not just arbitrary and without reason. As there is no consideration of any physical, spiritual, intellectual, moral or social qualifications, and it is only modified according to age and sex, in these amounts there must surely be some factor expressed which is universal to the same degree in all נפשות, in all persons. As, further, it is dealing here with ערכך נפשות לה׳ with the national valuation of persons for God and His Sanctuary, this factor which is common to all persons, and only modified by age and sex, should be looked for in the first place in the relation which declares the value the lives of the people have towards God and His holy things. Now unless we are mistaken, there can hardly be any factor which is common to all, and only modified by age and sex that can be found in the relation of נפשות to God and His Sanctuary other than the task and mission of life which is given to every נפש, and it only remains to elucidate the different numbers which are given here from the different conditions of this factor.

When we compare the numbers 5, 20, 50, 15 for a male soul, and 3, 10, 30, 10, for the female; if we consider that the full ערך for the mature male from twenty to sixty years is put at 50, and full ערך for the mature female at 30, and that these figures of 30 and 50 in each case are ten times the ערך of a female and male infant respectively, which start at 3 and 5; then we think we are not going wrong if we take the key to the whole scale to lie in the numbers 3, 5, 10. Three to be the formula for the life mission of a woman, five for that of a man, and ten the sign of completion, of perfection.

Now we venture to suggest that the home, the family, may well be represented by the number 3, husband, wife, child, but the community, as we have often found in the Torah, by the number 2, so that the family and the community together would be expressed by the number 5. If this is not far from the truth, then 3 is the sign of woman’s vocation, woman’s mission in life, the family, the home, 5 that of man, family life and communal responsibility; and with these two numbers, the signs of their respective missions in life the ערך of the infant until the time when they have reached the trainable age, the end of the fifth year. From the end of the fifth year to the end of the twentieth year are the years of training, of perfecting for their vocation, for the woman it is the single vocation of the home, its sign is 10; for the man it is the double one, home and community, its sign 20. The period from the end of the twentieth to sixtieth year, is the age of the full activity, of the completed training of the male and female vocations. Its sign for the full activity of the woman in her mission in life is the product of 10 x 3 = 30, for man it is 10 x 5 = 50. After the end of the sixtieth year until end of life is the age of זקנה the years of the harvest of life. The individual worker can look back with satisfaction at the completed edifice of his life and the communal worker at least at an honest contribution to the whole building of social life. Hence the sign for the single vocation of the woman is that of completion, 10, and for the dual vocation of man the number 10 for the private life, plus a half completion for the communal life 10 plus 5 = 15.

V. 9. In the preceding law, a symbolic expression of value, ערך, was fixed for the actual person having regard for its meaning and purpose to God and His Sanctuary. To that is now added a sentence telling us: - but for an animal that is appointed to be the symbolic expression of an offering of a person seeking to attain nearness to God, there is no redemption, but it must itself be used for the sacrificial procedure. More, even if just one limb of an animal is dedicated, means must be taken that the whole animal is used as an offering: הא כיצד תמבר לצרכי עולות ודמיה חולין חוץ מדמי אבר שבה (Temura lib). But if the dedicated limb is a vital organ, דבר שהנשמה תלויה בה, then the dedication is automatically extended to the whole animal (ibid). This judging whether the limb or part of the animal is of greater or lesser vital importance is called נידון בכבודו (Arachin 4b). We have already remarked above on Ch. 22,23, on the much greater importance of the dedication of one’s own activities as expressed by bringing an offering than that of the upkeep of the Temple, and found in this the reason for the prohibition to להקדיש תמימים לבדק הבית to dedicate fit animals to be sold for the upkeep of the Temple, as well as for the Law that, if, nevertheless, it has been done, i.e. dedicated, everything which is ראוי למזבח must be brought on to the ,מזבח אינו יוצא מידי מזבח לעולם (refer to there). So that our verse here, does not refer only to the case where the animal is expressly dedicated for a קרבן, but also if it by itself, or included with other articles, is dedicated לבדק הבית as long as it is בהמה אשר יקריבו ממנה קרבן לה׳ it יהיה קדש, it must be offered as a קרבן (Shekalim 24,7).

V. 10. לא יחליפנו. The basic meaning of חלף is changing to a completely opposite place, transitively וחלפה רקתו (Judges 5,27) pierced through; intransitively, וחלף ביהודה (Is. 7,8), וחלפת משם (Sam. 4,3) to transfer to a different place. In all cases it designates a transference to a different place or condition. From that, the knife of the slaughterer, which transfers the animal from life to death is called מחלפים (Ezra 1,9). Samson calls his hair, plaited שבע מחלפות (Judges 16,34 and 19) and it is doubtful whether his hair gets this special description because it was so long that it stood ready to be cut off, or whether plaits are generally called מחלפות because a plait consists of strands which constantly criss-cross from one side to the other. חלף עבדתם ,חלף (Numb. 18,21) “in the place of their service”. In the Piel and Hiphil חלף and החליף it means to make something go away in order to put something else in its place as ויחלף שמלתיו (Gen. 41,14) והחליפו שמלתיכם (ibid XXXV,2) and also that which takes the place of something else as וארזים נחליף (Is. 9,10), ועוד יחליף (Job. 14,7). But in all cases, by חלף and החליף the thing to be changed is the worse, to be changed by something better. Thus old or unsuitable clothes, weakened strength, etc. Also in והחליף את משכרתי (Gen. 31,7) in Laban’s opinion the wage to be changed was one which was bad, unprofitable to him.

Exactly the opposite is the meaning of המיר, throughout it designates the exchange of something good for something worse ההמיר גוי אלהים וגו׳ (Jer. 2,11) כבודם בקלון אמיר (Hosea 4,7) וימירו את כבודם (Ps. 106,20) חלק עמי ימיר (Micha 2,4).

Accordingly, we believe that here too, לא יחליפנו ולא ימיר אותו is to be taken in these different meanings, the first forbids the exchange of a bad קדש for a good חולין and the second a good קדש for a bad חולין, good and bad in the sense which we shall immediately explain. Just because by this prohibition the קדש is always the right one, against which the חולין now raised into the sphere of קדש is always considered as the wrong one, every change, even the bad קדש to the better חולין is actually really a change for the worse. Hence the general comprehensive term embracing both cases, is ואם המר ימיר, and the comprehensive term for such wrongful exchange is תמורה. As, moreover, both kinds of exchange are immediately given in detail: טוב ברע או רע בטוב, Temura 9a takes לא יחליפנו to prohibit also the exchange of somebody else’s קדש for a חולין of one’s own, לא יחליפנו בשל אחרים ולא ימיר בשל עצמו. This, of course, could only occur with the expressed permission of the other. טוב ברע או רע בטוב good, or bad from the standpoint of their qualifications to be an offering טוב would be תמימים and בעלי מומים :רע. In the same sense it says explicitly in Deut. 17,1 לא תזבח לה׳ אלקיך שור ושה אשר יהיה בו מום כל דבר רע. Regarding the טוב ברע and רע בטוב we find two different ways of taking it. In Temura 9a, according to our version and Rashi’s explanation, and, according to צאן קדשים, in לתוספות׳s opinion too, the first-mentioned in both these phrases is the חולין and the second the קדש whose קדושה one wishes to transfer to the חולין. That is to say: no חולין תמים in the place of a קדש בעל מום and no חולין בעל מום in the place of a קדש תמים. Then the first would be an example of לא יחליפנו and the second of לא ימיר אותו. But in Bechoroth 14b, it takes it in the reverse manner, the first mentioned is the קדש and the second the חולין.

ואם המר ימיר, the doubled expression to include the heir, לרבות היורש (Temura 2a). בהמה בבהמה excluding עופות and מנחות at which the result of תמורה here designated, viz., הוא ותמורתו יהיה קדש does not take place, העופות והמנחות אין עושין תמורה (Temura 13a). — In V. 33 the prohibition of תמורה and its effect if done, is repeated specially for מעשר בהמה and on that the teaching is given in Temura 13a and b that תמורה is only applicable for a קרבן יחיד but not for קרבנות השותפים והצבור, and not for קרבנות נכרים and only for קדשי מזבח but not for מעשר ;קדשי בדק הבית, as a דבר שיצא מן הכלל ללמד על הכלל כלו יצא, is, in all these cases an example which applies to the whole law.

The Torah, accordingly, gives us a תמורה-prohibition לא יחליפנו ולא ימיר אותו and a תמורה-law והיה הוא ותמורתו יהיה קדש וגו׳. The one forbids the exchange of an animal dedicated for the purpose of an offering for another one not dedicated, and it makes no difference whether either animal has a מום or not, provided of course, that in the case of the dedicated one the מום occured only after its dedication, שקדם הקדשן את מומן. For if anybody dedicates an animal that has a מום for an offering it has only קדושת דמים, its value only is dedicated for sacrificial purposes, but it has no קדושת הגוף, it itself did not have the dedication of an actual offering (Chulin 130a). The תמורה-law ordains that if anybody places a בהמת חולין in the place of a בהמת קדשים with the formula הרי זו תחת זו ,תמורת זו,חליפת זו the בהמת קדשים retains its קדושה quite undisturbed, and the בהמת חולין nevertheless receives exactly the same קדושה, and in accordance with that, if it is fit to be offered, has to be brought on to the altar as a קרבן of the same nature as the other one. So that תמורת עולה is an עולה the תמורת שלמים a שלמים, only תמורת חטאת ואשם are not brought as offerings (see on Ch. 4,24), and תמורת בכור ומעשר also do not come on to the altar, but remain watched until they get a מום when they are allowed to be eaten by their owners (Temura 17b and 21a). If the תמורה-animal has a מום it has to be redeemed, and the value used for an offering corresponding to what it otherwise would have been. It itself, however, in contrast to other קדשים whose מומן were קודם להקדשן remains אסורה בגיזה ועבודה it is prohibited to be used for any work, or to make use of its fleece, even after it has been redeemed (Temura 16b). This power of transferring its קדושה to a תמורה without any lessening of its own קדושה is confined, as already remarked, to, קרבנות בהמה ,קרבנות ישראל ,קרבנות יחיד and קרבנות מזבח. This power is also only innate in the original קדושה but not in the young born to an offering-animal, nor to the קדושה obtained by ;תמורה אין ולד עושה תמורה ,אין תמורה עושה תמורה (ibid 12a). It is not quite sure whether the prohibition of תמורה only extends to where the תמורה is effective, or if it applies even where the act is without effect, e.g. in the case of שותפין and צבור, whether in such cases, although their offerings confer no קדושה on their תמורה, nevertheless לוקין על תמורתן (see לחם משנה on הל׳ תמורה I,1). Finally, only the one to whom both animals belong has the power to effect תמורה (Temura 9a), and here it is not the מקדיש but the מתכפר who has the power. So that if somebody A dedicated an animal for the offering of B, not A but B, the מתכפר, the one for whose כפרה the animal is destined, can effect the תמורה, and the prohibition applies to him, whereas for anything else, such as regarding the redemption, the מקדיש A, is considered the המקדיש מוסיף חומש ומתכפר עושה תמורה :בעלים (Temura 2b and 10a).

Let us now try to ascertain the ideas which could be the underlying thoughts of all these laws. First of all we must bear in mind that these thoughts must be such, that, to a very high degree touch on the very nature and meaning of the holiness of offerings. For the transgression of the prohibition of Temura is of such a serious nature that according to one way of considering it (Temura 17a, see רש״י and תוספות thereon, and רמב״ם and ראב״ד הל׳ תמורה I,2), even בשוגג it incurs the penalty of מלקות an example which would be perfectly unique in the whole of Jewish Law!

But there is one point which we have not yet touched on, which is so very characteristic that it could well lead us to ascertaining the thought that lies at the base of the law of Temura. By the sentence לא יחליפנו ולא ימיר אותו טוב ברע או רע בטוב the Torah unequivocally forbids also the exchange of a קדש בעל מום for a חולין תמים, and even in that case, if it is nevertheless done the Temura is effective and the קדש remains קדש and the חולין becomes equally קדש and then immediately afterwards in V,11 and 12 the Torah actually prescribes redemption for a קדש בעל מום, which according to the Halacha need not be made by money or its equivalent, but can be done by giving an animal which is fit for an offering. So that if one places a חולין animal which is fit for an offering, besides a קדש animal that has become unfit for an offering, and declares הרי זו מחוללת על זו the unfit קדש animal transfers its קדושה to the other, and becomes חולין. From this it seems that quite the same change may be done, more, is ordered to be done, which the Torah has just prohibited with such seriousness. And actually the fact is that the whole difference lies in the contrasting wording of the formula by which the exchange is made. If the sacrificial animal is made the object of the procedure by saying הרי זו, let this קדש animal “מחוללת״ become secular על זו through this חולין animal, or just simply תחת זו (חולין) הרי זו (קדש), this is not תמורה but the formula for the legal procedure for redemption (פדיון) for the redemption act ordered by the Torah. The קדש בעל מום is יוצא לחולין and the קדושה of its having been dedicated for an offering is transferred to the animal which hitherto was חולין. But if on the other hand, the חולין-animal is made the object of the procedure by saying הרי זו “let this חולין-animal” תחת זו “be instead of this קדש-animal” or תמורת זו, or חליפת זו, this is not פדיון, but putting an ordinary animal in place of a dedicated one, an act of תמורה, and the dedicated animal remains קדש and the other receives an equal status of קדושה and becomes dedicated to a similar purpose (Temura 26b and 27a).

Verse 9 stated that an animal destined for sacrifice by an act of dedication can in no way be altered from that destination as long as it is fit for it. Should it become unfit for it by a מום, then, as it had received this destination by a completely free-willed act, an equally free-willed act can transfer this destination for which it has now become unfit to another animal which is fit. This transference can be made either directly, or indirectly by depositing its value in money for which the other animal is to be bought. By such a transference the destination and resulting קדושה passes over to the new animal, and the one which had orginally been dedicated reverts to its previous חולין- state, with the exception of the איסור of גיזה ועבודה, that the animal that has once been dedicated for an offering may not be shorn or used for work. This is the prescribed procedure for the פדיון קדשים שהוממו. That this redemption of the קדושה of a dedicated object is dependent on the dedication having been made by an act of human free-will is evident from the fact that such sacrificial animals whose dedication occurs from external sources, and is in no way dependent on the exercise of human will, e.g. בכור and מעשר even if they have become unfit for offering through a מום are not able to be redeemed, can have no פדיון.

The case is quite different, if somebody, not in the character of the מקדיש of one who has given the animal its consecrated destination, but as the מתכפר, the one who is to find his כפרה in the offering for which the animal is destined, and, accordingly, is to see in the animal, not the “animal” but the expression of his own personality with all his urges and forces, his purposes and activities to be directed towards God and His Torah, if such a person sets an ordinary animal, which is just nothing else but an animal, in the place of one which has been dedicated as his offering, and declares: זו “this animal” תחת זו shall take the place of his offering. In that moment the whole moral purpose and the whole symbolic meaning of the “offering” disappears. Nothing remains for him but an animal life that, heathen-like, is to be offered to his God, Whose wrath may be appeased by the death of an animal. At the act of פדיון the thoughts are directed on to the sacrificial animal, and the procedure is the transference of its holiness and spiritual meaning to another, as yet unconsecrated, animal. At such a procedure the consciousness of the spiritual meaning of the offering and its resulting holiness remain entirely undisturbed. But at the act of Temura the thoughts are directed towards the undedicated animal, and the consciousness of the symbolic meaning and holiness of a sacrificial animal is, at the moment, in the background; his words seem just to oppose it. He does not say he is sanctifying the undedicated animal by transfering the holiness of the other to it, but he just puts the undedicated in the place of the dedicated. This seems to be the reason for the prohibition of Temura. It is understandable that such an act is only punishable in cases of such offerings as קרבן בהמה which are to represent the whole personality of the מתכפר in every sphere of his moral life and desires, but does not affect to such a degree עופות and מנחות which only represent certain phases of the personality. Equally understandable is it that the whole conception of תמורה and its prohibition affects only קדשי מזבח and is not applicable to קדשי בדק הבית. Only the former are symbolic bearers of the idea of spiritual and moral sanctification, whereas the latter merely belong to the purposes of the Temple as objects of value. And for that purpose, in truth, one object of value is as good as any other of the same value; the substitution of one for another does not affect in the slightest the nature of the conception of holy things. So that in their case it is quite immaterial what formula of substitution is used, and הרי זו “this חולין-object” תחת זו “shall take the place of this קדש-object” is here also legal פדיון. See תוספות on Baba Mezia 55a ד״ה פרה.

But the Torah is not satisfied with the mere prohibition of the Temura-act. It does not simply decree the complete nullity of the pronounced exchange, by the animal which had been dedicated for an offering remaining unaltered in that condition, but, to make restitution to the spiritual nature of offerings which had been attacked by the sin of Temura, it makes this threatened holiness of the sacrificial animal appear in such power that, instead of its passing over into the chulin condition of the other animal as intended, it elevates the latter up to its own degree of holiness, and confers on it the same character and destination that it received at its own dedication.

Diese Restitutionswirkung kann naturgemäß nur dann eintreten, wenn der מתכפר dessen תמורה-Handlung dadurch in eine הקדש-Handlung umwandelt werden soll, die ganze Persönlichkeit, die in dem Opfertier, welcher die תמורה galt, zum Ausdruck kommt ganz vertritt, so daß nunmehr auch das Temuratier als sein Opfertier dastehen kann, also nur, wenn das erste Opfer ausschließlich das seine, somit ein קרבן יחיד ist, daß aber bei קרבנות שותפין und קרבנות צבור diese Wirkung nicht eintritt.

V. 11. and 12. Now follows a list of objects which, having been rendered holy by the dedicatory word of mouth of the owner, may be redeemed back into his possession by payment of money or in kind; may be, or in certain cases must be. The valuation, as in V. 8, is to be made by the כהן i.e. by a ב״ד של כהנים, a court of priests as the representatives of the Sanctuary. The first object in the list is: קדשי מזבח שהונלמו, a sacrificial animal that has become unfit through receiving a מום. This is what this verse deals with. For, as explained in ת״כ it can not be speaking here of בהמה טמאה in the usual sense of that term, for that is dealt with in V. 27. There too, it says simply בהמה טמאה by itself. But here, by the addition of אשר לא יקריבו ממנה וגו׳ it qualifies the טמאה of an animal as being solely that it has been rendered unfit for offering, and accordingly is to be taken simply as the contrast to the מום-free animal of V. 9. אשר יקריבו ממנה קרבן לה׳ the קדושה of which can in no way be redeemed. And in any case, as Wessely remarks in his commentary, not only בהמה טמאה is excluded from קרבן but צבי ויחמור וגו׳ are בהמות טהורות and still not allowed to be brought as קרבנות. It still remains to be explained why the Torah here designates the פסול מום by the term טומאה.

אשר לא יקריבו ממנה וגו׳ that has become permanently unfit for offering, that has received a מום קבוע (see Ch. 22,12 et seq.). Such an animal is to be redeemed by an act of פדיון (see on V. 10). Its קדושה is transferred to the redeeming object, which is used to reproduce the same kind of offering, but the animal itself becomes חולין and only remains אסור בגיזה ועבודה. If the animal had a מום before it was dedicated, שקדם מומו להקדשו, so that it had never received קדושת הגוף had never itself been dedicated for an offering, was only קדושת דמים i.e. was only destined to have its value used for sacrificial purposes, it must be redeemed in the same way, but then, like all קדושת דמים reverts completely, without any restrictions at all, to the חולין-condition.

והעמיד את הבהמה וגו׳. Amongst all the קדושת הגוף, all objects which are dedicated to be used themselves as offering, (as opposed to קדושת דמים which only belong to sacrificial purposes as far as their value goes), it is only בהמה which, if it becomes unfit by receiving a מום is able to be redeemed, but עופות, birds that are dedicated for offerings, and equally so מנחות ונסכים, which only become material for offering after being received in a כלי שרת, are קדשו בכלי, have no פדיון, and can not be redeemed even if they have lost their fitness for offering שלא נאמר פדיון אלא בבהמה (Menachoth 100a).

We have already remarked that the act of פדיון is the transference of the sactifying destination of an object from one object to another. This power of transferring holiness is always regarded as an attribute of a very high degree of holiness, אלימי למיתפס פדיונם. The sanctification resulting from its destination is so strong that it can completely grip the redeeming object. According to that idea we can again understand that it is only when the offering symbolises the whole personality of its bringer in every phase of his life and desires, as in the case of a קרבן בהמה that it has the ability to transfer the holiness of its conception, but that the idea of symbolising only part of a person’s life as is expressed by מנחות ,עופות and נסכים, such an intensity of קדושה is not ascribed to them, and that these, accordingly have no ability for פדיון: The same idea may touch the following law which results from the words:

והעמיד וגו׳ והעריך הכהן אתה וגו׳. For according to this the ability for פדיון is further made conditional that the animal is still fit for העמדה, that it is able to be “stood” before the priest, i.e. that it is still living. If the animal that has become unfit by a מום dies, it can no longer be redeemed but must be buried. If the animal died without שחיטה, then, in any case redemption can not be done as אין פודין את הקדשים כדי להאכילן לכלבים as then it could only be used as animal food, and redemption for such a purpose is not permitted (Pesachim 29a and b). But even if death occured by שחיטה there can be no פדיון as there can be no העמדה. The same principle applies also to קדשי בדק הבית (Temura 32a & b). אחד קדשי מזבח ואחד קדשי בדק הבית היו בכלל העמדה והערכה and the only exception is קדשי מזבח שקדם מום קבוע להקדשן, an animal which is already בעל מום קבוע, which has a permanent מום, and as such is dedicated for an offering, has פדיון even after it dies (ibid 33a, see משנה למלך on הל׳ אסורי מזבח I,10).

Now we believe that the whole idea of an offering, which gives a קרבן בהמה the ability to transfer its holiness, can only be represented undiminished by an animal during its life. Life, נפש, is the first and most essential factor in the conception of a personality, the existence and desires of whom are to be brought near to God by an offering. If life has departed from the animal, then the idea of the symbolism of an offering has lost one of the most essential signs which it is to express, and thereby has lost all power to transfer it to another animal.

More obscure is the application of this law to קדשי בדק הבית also. They are only declared holy for their value to be used for the upkeep of the building of the Sanctuary, and their condition and nature has really nothing to do with its symbolism or meaning or teaching. And actually as a matter of fact, objects of any kind, even dead animals, as long as they have some value, can be dedicated to בדק הבית, and then valued according to their worth, and redeemed for the בדק הבית fund, and yet if a living animal had been dedicated to the בדק הבית, and then died, it can no longer be redeemed, it is lost for the purpose it was dedicated for, and must be buried!

Perhaps there may be some truth in the following suggestion. Although in general, the nature of the objects which are given to provide the funds for the upkeep of the building of the Temple, and are redeemed for that purpose, come so little into consideration nevertheless the sign of “life” is so very intimately connected with the meaning of the Sanctuary yea, whenever the opportunity offers, the very thought of it may be joined to the “dead” wood and stones of the building and make them “alive” and pregnant with meaning — היכל ה׳ המה as the Prophet expresses this thought — we think that this might be so important for the whole purpose of the Temple building, that, when “living” creatures are given to further this purpose, even if only with their value, the Temple idea holds fast, even for this dedication of value, to the existing idea of “life” and if that is lost, allows the object itself to be lost for its purpose.

V. 13. ואם גאל יגאלנה. The value fixed by the valuation of the court applies to everybody else. But if the original owner himself buys it back, he has to pay an additional fifth to the pay office of the Sanctuary. This fifth which has to be added to the value at every redemption which the owner himself makes, is one quarter of the valuation. It is one fifth to be added to make the sum up to five fifths: חומש מלבר. See on Ch. 5,16 & 25.

V. 14 & 15. ואיש כי יקדיש את ביתו. According to ת״כ, the conception בית here means his home, not only בית דירה just the house. By the repetition of the word ביתו instead of just a pronoun in V,15, all that comprises his “home” is included, any of his possessions, מקדיש את נכסיו. The Halacha also teaches from the word ביתו — and not בית — the far reaching general law that אין אדם מקדיש דבר שאינו שלו and also דבר שאינו ברשותו that, what a man can make holy must be, like “his house”, his own property, and even if it is his property, must not be removed by external circumstances from his having access to it, it must be, like his house, שלו and ברשותו. Something which is stolen can not be made קודש either by the owner or by the thief זה לפי שאינו שלו וזה לפי שאינו ברשותו (Baba Kama 68b).

The so called “canonical law” in Judaism is far removed from ascribing to holy articles which have been made holy by human dedication any sacramental, unredeemable, mystic, magic power. The conception of הקדש, the Sanctuary, in law is no more than that of a person, its right to property extends in no way any further than that of any private lay person with legal rights, more, in many very essential laws of rights, it lags behind. The Jewish הקדש can only acquire that which an honest and legal owner dedicates to it. And not only an illegal but even an erroneous dedication is not recognised, הקדש בטעות אינו הקדש (Nazir 31b). And the whole of this chapter of הקדש-dedication, which shows a פדיון, a redemption, in all cases proves how far removed the Jewish conception of “making holy” is from the idea of any magical properties, or healing, or other powers being ascribed as being permanently associated with such holy things. Everywhere it impresses the clear conscious thought, that it is not the thing itself, but the idea behind it — which can be transferred from one object to another — in which holiness lies. Yea, every “making holy”, which is taken as being no more than a vow, — as long as the dedicated article has not yet been handed over to the Sanctuary — has the possibility of being cancelled, like any other vow, by שאלה (see Numb. 30,3), אי בעי מיתשיל עליה (Bechoroth 31a, and Pesachim 46b, תוספות ד״ה הואיל). Finally, regarding נזיקין, damages, הקדש, the Sanctuary, is deprived of the protection of the law which every private lay person רעהו enjoys (see Ex. 21,36). Also the law of אונאה and בטול מקח (see Ch. 25,14), is not applicable to הקדש, so that הקדש שוה מנה שחללו על שוה פרוטה מחולל; if an article of the Sanctuary worth £100, had been wrongfully redeemed for one penny the deal is valid (Temura 27b).

Only in one case — that of שעבוד pledges, temporary conditional rights over property — does הקדש, by the one who has still the absolute right of possesion over it, oppose any private rights (similarly to: (חמץ ושחרור הקדש מפקיעין מידי שעבוד (Gittin 40b, Rashi, תוספות ibid).

V. 15. המקדיש ולא המתפיס :ואם המקדיש וגו׳. Only the one who had dedicated the object and now himself wishes to redeem it, has to add the fifth, but not one who has transferred the קדושה to another object by redemption, and now wishes to redeem this second object; על הקדש ראשון מוסיף חומש על הקדש שני אינו מוסיף חומש (Temura 9b). Above Ch. 25,29, et seq. a difference was made between בתי ערי חומה and בתי חצרים regarding their returning to the vendor. In Arachin 33a, regarding הקדש it is taught that a בית ערי חומה if it is redeemed by another than the original owner, remains permanently in his possession after it has been in his hands for twelve months, similarly to an ordinary sale, a בית חצרים however, in such a case, again similarly to an ordinary sale, would revert in the Youvel to the original possessor. As long as the house is in the hands of the הקדש it can always be redeemed by the מקדיש.

V. 16. ואם משדה וגו׳. Now follow the laws concerning making a field “holy”. A difference is naturally made between שדה אחוזה, a field of inheritance, of which he holds the freehold, so that in certain cases, his dedication can involve his complete withdrawal of all his rights over it and giving the field entirely over for the purposes of the Sanctuary, and שדה מקנה, (V. 22,) a field which he has bought, and which accordingly is only leasehold, and his rights to the use of it only extend to the Youvel, so that he can only dispose of it until that time, when it reverts to the original vendor.

והיה ערכך לפי זרעו זרע חמר וגו׳. For a שדה אחוזה, here a general estimated value is fixed without consideration of the quality of the field. But in the case of שדה מקנה (V. 22), the price of the redemption is taxed, in accordance with Arachin 14a, according to its actual value בשדה מקנה נותן את שויו. Further, at the redemption of שדה אחוזה the original owner has to add the fifth, but not at that of a שדה מקנה (ibid). We think we can see the reason why the Torah sees it fit to fix a universal redemption price for a שדה אחוזה. As a שדה אחוזה, if it was not redeemed back by its owners, remained permanently the possession of the הקדש, as a business article it had the character of ordinary goods, and, like them, in every given case the actual intrinsic value of the article itself should be ascertained. Now as long as the Youvel was in force, in Jewish trade a field was an article that had no real price for itself as it could not be absolutely and completely bought and sold. The case, our case of מקדיש שדה אחוזה was the one unique case, standing quite by itself, where a field could be sold and the purchase ultimately become permanent. Hence for buying back, for the redemption of such a field which could eventually become a permanent purchase there could be no market price ascertained, so that the fixing of a universal fixed value was a necessity. The Torah ordains fifty shekels per the area required for sowing a chomer of barley, as the fixed price. On Ex. 22,16 we worked out that one could reckon 50 shekels as the business capital necessary for a man’s livelihood. If we now consider that a chomer is the equivalent of the talmudic כור which contains 30 סאה, and 30 איפה = 10 סאה which are equal to 100 tenths or 100 עומר which represent the basic requirements of a man for 100 days; take an average 20-fold produce, against which reckon a loss of 25% until it is reduced to edible flour, and take the proportion of the other requirement for sustenance as 3:1, a piece of land of an acreage for sowing a chomer would yield the livelihood of one man, so that its worth would be represented by 50 shekels. And moreover the Torah has taken the lowest kind of grain used for human consumption, viz. barley, for its computation. (To make this reckoning quite clear I have written it out in the following form: —
1 Chomer=1 כור estimated by Torah as value of 50 Shekels.
1 סאה = 30 כור .
30 איפה = 10 סאה .
10 איפה = 100 tenths of איפה .
1 tenth איפה = 1 day’s food=l עומר .
Hence 1 Chomer=100 עומר .
The average yield of seed=20 times the amt. sowed.
Hence 1 Chomer=2000 עומר of seed.
Loss in reducing to flour given as 25%.
Hence 1 Chomer= 2000-500 =1500 עומר .
Now proportion of food to other requirements is given as 3:1 so that total requirements of that for food would be 1:4, 1:4 of 1500 = 375 which gives us one year’s full sustenance. I.L.)

That no fixed tariff is required for שדה מקנה is quite clear. As, in any case, the field itself reverts to its original owner in Youvel, and the one who dedicates it really can only dispose of the expected produce until the Youvel as אין אדם מקדיש דבר שאינו שלו (Arachin 26b), and the price of that is regulated by the ordinary market prices (Ch. 25,15 & 16), the redemption fee can easily be exactly reckoned. The reason for the payment of the חומש for a שדה אחוזה and not for a שדה מקנה may be quite similar. At the former, as by all other הקדש, the object itself is dedicated, and when one takes it back again — as we believed on Ch. 5,16 & 25, — the additional payment of a fifth to its value is to counter the appearance that the Sanctuary to which we had dedicated the object was not sufficiently worthy to receive it, or that it was too valuable an object to give up to the Sanctuary. But with a שדה מקנה the object itself is not at all dedicated to the Sanctuary, only the temporary use of it. We would consider this way of taking it sounder if, in the case of מקדיש בית החצרים which also reverts to its original owners in Youvel, no חומש was to be paid, but that is not the case. But, nevertheless, as a בית החצרים all the time it is in the hands of the הקדש only reverts to the hands of the מקדיש even in Youvel by פדיון (Arachin 33a), such a הקדש can still be looked on as a dedication of the actual object itself.

V. 17—19. אם משנת היובל וג׳. The fact that the fixed sum of 50 shekels has to be divided into the 49 years of the Youvel period, and the amount of the redemption money varies according to the number of years left till the Youvel seems to contradict our view that this fixed universal sum is a general acceptance of the absolute value of the ground, but not to be varied according to the ascertained market value. But the laws regarding the מקדיש שדה אחוזה can be taken as being affected by two considerations. On the one hand, the principle that rules all other traffic in land, that no field is to be permanently estranged from the one whose heritage it is, and hence even a gift reverts in Youvel, a principle which indeed rests on the fact that כי לי הארץ, which is meant to preach, that God is the real Owner of the land. On the other hand, just giving a piece of land to God and for the purpose of His Sanctuary, could do away with the effect of this fact, as indeed actually the Torah recognizes the renunciation of even a heredity-field permanently for all time for holy purposes when done by the formula “חרם״, (V. 28), and here at מקדיש שדה אחוזה (V. 21), explicitly refers to it again. Both these factors are given consideration at מקדיש שדה אחוזה. It can (V. 21), become a renunciation to the Sanctuary, from whose hands it can go to its representatives the כהנים, for all time. For if it is not redeemed back from the hands of the הקדש (or according to רמב״ם, also from the hands of a buyer from the הקדש) by the entry of the Youvel by the מקדיש, then it goes over to the כהנים as a permanent possession, who, if they receive it from the hands of the הקדש and not from the hands of a buyer, pay the full fixed taxed value of 50 shekels to the בדק הבית fund. הגיע יובל ולא נגאלה הכהנים נכנסין לתוכה ונותנין דמיה (Arachin 25b — see כ״מ on רמב״ם הל׳ ערכין IV,19). For that, the fixing of an absolute tax value was necessary. On the other hand the Torah wishes to make the regaining of his hereditary fields as easy as possible for the מקדיש but at the same time, as long as it has not been redeemed by him, to make them useful to the הקדש בדק הבית. It allows therefore the temporary sale to anybody else until the Youvel against the deposit of a forty-ninth of 50 shekels for each year until the Youvel for each area of the field in which a חמר שעורים can be sown, but reserves the right of the מקדיש to buy it back at any time up to the Youvel, at the same rate plus one fifth. For these two purposes the fixed estimation of the value of the use of the field is placed at the 50 shekels. But, the Halacha teaches, the amount payable to the הקדש בדק הבית must at least amount to two years rental value, the text (V,18), assumes that there are שנים הנותרות. In the forty eighth year it can only be redeemed by the payment of the whole fixed estimation of the value of 50 shekels (Arachin 14a & b, see on מל״מ on ערכין IV,26).

V. 20. & 21. ואם לא יגאל וגו׳. If the field has not been redeemed from the הקדש by the מקדיש by the beginning of the Youvel, or if by then it had already been sold by the הקדש-administrator, the גזבר, to somebody else, in both cases it can no longer be redeemed by the מקדיש. It goes out of the hands of the הקדש or out of the hands of the buyer, or even, if the מקדיש himself had bought it from the buyer, out of his (the מקדיש׳s) hands, into the possession of the division of the priesthood (משמר) which happens to be on duty at the entry of the Youvel.

This is how the case would be according to our version in the Gemora: גאלה אחר וכו׳ ,וגאלה מידו יוצא לכהנים ביובל (Arachin 25a). But Rambam has the version אינו יוצא וכו׳, and according to that, our verse would have to be taken as saying: — If the מקדיש has not redeemed the field back by entry of the Youvel and it is still in the hands of the הקדש, or if the הקדש administration had sold it to somebody else, in whose possession it still is, then it can no longer, once Youvel has started, be redeemed back by the מקדיש (who had the power to do so up till then) but in both cases it goes over to the כהנים as a permanent possession. (See הל׳ ערכין ,רמב״ם IV,20).

לאיש אחר: only out of the hands of a buyer who is a stranger does it pass into the possession of the priesthood. But if a son of the מקדיש had redeemed it, then at the entry of the Youvel it passes back into the possession of the father. גאלה בנו יוצאה לאביו ביובל (Arachin 25a).

כשדה החרם. See in 5,28. — לכהן וגו׳ to the division of the priesthood who are functioning at the entry of Youvel. As the field was primarily dedicated to הקדש בדק הבית, if the הקדש has already reaped the benefit by having sold the field, then the priests get it without having to pay anything for it, but if it has remained unchanged in possession of the הקדש until the Youvel, then it passes into the possession of the כהנים only on the payment of the full fixed estimated value of 50 shekels per חומר-area (Arachin 25b). The Jewish priesthood has in no wise to identify itself with the Sanctuary of the Temple, so that priestly advantages and furthering Temple purposes are identical. Only symbolically do the priests stand as bearers and representatives of the idea of the Temple, and they have special definite prerogatives which, as the expression goes, have been assigned to them משלחן גבוה from God’s table. In every other respect their relation to the Sanctuary is exactly the same as every lay man.

V. 22—24. ואם את שדה מקנתו אשר וגו׳. Only if it is purely a שדה מקנה and can not at all become the שדה אחוזה of the שאינה ראויה להיות ,מקדיש שדה אחוזה do the following laws apply. But if he had dedicated it as שדה מקנה and before the Youvel it had become שדה אחוזתו e.g. לוקח שדה מאביו והקדיש ואח״ב מת אביו (he bought a field from his father and dedicated it to the Sanctuary as something he had acquired by buying it, and subsequently his father died.
