I.L.), then if he has not redeemed it before the Youvel, it passes over into the possession of the כהנים like שדה אחוזה (Arachin 26b). — וחשב וגו׳ את מכסת הערכך :את מכסת הערכך וגו׳, not the universal fixed valuation, but שויו, the value of the harvests to be expected for the greater or lesser number of years remaining until the Youvel (Arachin 14a), and the מקדיש too would have to pay only this amount without חומש (ibid. — see on V,16).

אין להקדש אלא מקומו ושעתו :ונתן וגו׳ ביום ההוא וגו׳, the estimation of the redemption money to be paid for anything dedicated to הקדש has to be made according to the value at that day and place, even if it would fetch a higher price at a later date or in another place. The Mishna (Arachin 24a), mentioned as an example מרגלית בכפר, a valuable pearl in a small village. Nevertheless the offer for the sale of land to be redeemed is extended to sixty days שום ההקדש ששים יום וגו׳ (ibid. 21b). Such a period for sales is not regarded as being in contradiction to ביום ההוא of our text.

V. 25. וכל ערכך וגו׳. Only by money or equivalent value can הקדשות be redeemed, but not by עבדים שטרות וקרקעות (Bechoroth 31a & b). Only mobile or moveable goods (excluding קרקרעות and עבדים which are always considered in legal matters to be in the same category), and things of intrinsic value (excluding cheques, documents etc.) are valid for the purpose of the exchange.

אשד יבכר לה׳ ,אך בכור וגו׳, that which belongs to God by reason of its birth, being the firstborn, לא יקדיש איש אתו. One may not dedicate it to be any other offering if it is a בכור i.e. as soon as it is born. It only becomes a בכור with יציאתו מרחם, with its birth it becomes קדוש as we have already remarked on Ex. 13,2 (to which refer). So that before it is actually born it can be given yet another קדושה (Temura 25a). But once it is born no other קדושה can be given to it. Only הקדש עילוי — i.e. one can dedicate that value of a הקדש which the sacrificial animal as such has for its owners e.g. in the case of a בכור the טובת הנאה the right to give it to a relative or to any special כהן of his choosing, — only that value is available to be made הקדש in the case of a בכור as it is in all other קדשים (Temura 32a, and Arachin 28b).

V. 27. בהמה טמאה is the exact opposite of בכור. A בכור is, at its birth, קדש מזבח, a בהמה טמאה on the other hand, whether a בכור or not, is not fit for an offering. A בהמה טמאה can be dedicated, like any other object, for בדק הבית, it then becomes קדושת דמים, is holy for its value, and is to be redeemed, if by the מקדיש for its estimated value plus a fifth, by anybody else, just by paying its value.

V. 28. אך בכור .אך כל חרם וגו׳ (V,26) was the first contrast to what had preceded it, it was an object that was automatically holy by itself. חרם here, is a second contrast. It is a category of קדש which has no חרם .פדיון, really a net (Habakuk 1,15 and Ezekiel 26,5), designates a condition of being in and away from all other relationships. Absolute exclusion and seclusion is annihilation. Thus in Deut. 7,2, החרם תחרם אתם and frequently elsewhere. But, as a rule, it is used where the purpose of such annihilation or destruction is to prevent its being brought into contact with others. Used, not in its absolute sense, but relatively, חרם is that which is placed out of use and employment. Thus the highest degree of איסור הנאה of ע״ז (Deut. 7,26), is designated by חרם.

Now every הקדש has two factors innate in it; a negative one, its exclusion from profane use, and a positive one, its serving for a holy purpose. At ordinary הקדש the positive, being given up for holy purposes, is in the foreground, and the negative, the exclusion from profane use, is only the result of the former. But in חרם the negative, the exclusion from profane use, is the primary object, and קדושה, the positive, only appears as the consequence of such exclusion. Now here it says: If somebody declares that any of his living or lifeless, moveable or landed, property is to be “חרם״, they or it thereby completely cease to be “his”, they may neither be sold to anybody else nor may they be redeemed back by their hitherto owner. He has given them back to God, and accordingly they have the character of קדש קדשים; they represent that fundamental conception on which the sanctity of all holy things rests, “belonging to God” (see on Ex. 29,37). Hence they are not, like קדשי בדק הבית, being placed positively as objects valuable for the purposes of the Sanctuary, a purpose which can be equally as well achieved by any other object of the same value, but their hitherto owner by his declaration of חרם has returned them to God, and renounced any further right of disposition of them. Under the universal direction of God, they had become his property, he returns them to the Giver; they were his, now they are God’s. But God, in His Torah (Numb. 18,14), has already placed everything which has been returned to Him in this manner as חרם at the complete disposal of the כהנים by His dictum כל חרם בישראל לך יהיה to which reference was made above in V,21, כשדה החרם לכהן תהיה אחוזתו. Hence the sentence in the Gemora: החרמים כל זמן שהם בבית בעלים הרי הן כהקדש לכל דבריהן שנא׳ כל חרם קדש קדשים הוא לה׳, נתן לכהנים הרי הן לכל דבריהן חולין שנא׳ כל חרם בישראל לך יהיה (Arachin 29a — see תוספות Bechoroth 32a ד״ה רבא אמר).

In all this we have followed the opinion which רמב״ם and סמ״ג take as the Halacha, viz. that סתם חרמים לכהנים and that only when a positive purpose of dedication e.g. חרם לבדק הבית is added to the simple negative declaration הרי זו חרם are חרמים dedicated to בדק הבית, belong to הקדש בדק בית, and have פדיון. In such cases חרם is simply a synonym for הקדש (Arachin 24a).

In our text it says: מכל אשר לו מאדם וגו׳ ומשדה וגו׳ and not ,אדם וגו׳ ושדה וגו׳, according to Arachin 28a, this teaches that the Torah assumes that a person only dedicates as חרם something of his possessions, but not all his possession, not even the whole of one kind of his possessions, not all his sheep, all his cows, etc., and there, a person is seriously blamed if, by dedication to the Sanctuary he deprives himself of all his worldly wealth, or even of all of one kind of his possessions. So that the teaching of the Jewish Temple is that it is no pious act, it declares it rather as a sin, if one gives up the whole of one’s fortune for the benefit of the Temple’s holy purposes. It declares אין אדם רשאי להחרים כל נכסיו that a man has no right to such renunciation, and thereby places the faithful dutiful use of the goods which God has given him in building up and expanding his life in accordance with the Torah, in the clear light of a God-pleasing service to God.

V. 29. כל חרם וגו׳. In Ex. 22,19 also the pronouncement of the death sentence is expressed by החרים and understood in the sense of withdrawal from the midst of earthly existence. Now here it says: Everyone who has had the sentence of being banned from the sphere of human existence pronounced on him, shall have this doom irrevocably resting on him. Unless the pronouncement of the judge can be shown to have rested on an error, and so regarded as not having been made, there can be no appeal against his fate. For it is not the judge, altogether it can be no sentence given for reasons of expediency, it is God’s Justice which pronounces the “death-cherem” on the criminal, in accordance with clearly defined legal limitations, and the judge is merely its instrument. Just as there can be only one truth, and with truth there can be no compromise and no substitution, so with justice there may be no compromise, no substitution.

This principle which, as worked out in Ketuboth 27b and 38b, by repeated pronouncements as ולא תקחו כופר לנפש רוצח (Numb. 35,31), לא תקחו כופר לנוס אל עיר מקלטו (ibid. 32), et alia, is proclaimed for all the special problems of justice, is here wound up in the most perfect manner possible by the generality of calling the death sentence כל חרם.

In connection with the preceding laws, our verse would want to say: Decisions, which, such הקדש, emanate from the free-will of human beings exercised on objects, can, if need be, find a way to be altered or compromised with, but the decision of a judge is naught but the decision of God expressed through the mouth of man, which allows of no alteration, substitution or compromise. If, as the preceding verse teaches, an object which has been given back by human free-will to be at the disposition of God, is also a חרם, it too, is immediately withdrawn from any further altered disposition by man, and can have no substitution by redemption’ Ketuboth ibid, and Arachin 6b derive from our verse the Halacha that היוצא ליהרג ואמר אחד ערכו עלי לא אמר כלום, that one who has been sentenced to death has lost all meaning for an ערך valuation, and any vow of ערך on him is quite invalid and has no effect. We think we can see in this Halacha just the consequence of the way we took the meaning of our verse to be. Because the death sentence given in accordance with God’s commands can not be bought off, and hence is irrevocable and unavoidable, anybody with such a sentence has ceased to have a justified existence for the Sanctuary of God on earth. He is therefore not a person to whom the ערך-conception, and hence an ערך vow can apply, not even, as מל״מ remarks on הל׳ ערכין I,13, even if he has escaped by flight from the sentence being carried out.

V. 30. וכל מעשר הארץ וגו׳ ,לה׳ הוא. cf. Numb. 1,4. ראש לבית אבותיו הוא. Next to the conception of חרם from which the owner entirely withdraws all right of disposition, is the category of מעשר שני where the owner retains limited right of disposal. For this verse speaks of מעשר שני, the second tithe which has to be separated out of grain, wine, and oil in every first, second, fourth and fifth year of the Shemita cycle, the detailed laws of which are given in Deut. 14,22 et seq. (to which refer). It, itself, or its equivalent if redeemed, has to be eaten in Jerusalem. In the third and sixth year מעשר עני takes its place, (ibid. XXVI,12). It is mentioned only because of its relationship to הקדש and particularly to מעשר שני .חרם like חרם בבית בעלים (see V,2) is God’s property ממון גבוה. But God has placed חרם at the disposal of the בחנים and in their hands it becomes completely חולין. But מעשר שני remains ממון גבוה; only God, its Owner, has granted its previous owner again a limited right of disposal over it, and prescribed a special way in which it may be used. Our verse says: Every tithe which is given to God from the seed of the land and from the fruit of the trees: (this refers to the second tithe which is to be enjoyed in happiness in the surroundings of the Sanctuary of God, for מעשר ראשון is given to the לוי and מעשר עני to the poor) — shall remain a holy thing belonging to God, ממון גבוה, even in the hands of the people who are to eat and enjoy it, they may not sell it, not simply give it away (cf. Kiddushin 54b with מעשר שני I. I. ר״ש ibid.) not pledge or pawn it, nor barter it or exchange it, and it can not be acquired, as other mobile goods can, by משיכה. (Kiddushin 54b, מ״ש I,1).

V. 31. ואם גאל יגאל וגו׳. In the real מעשר שני-chapter (Deut. 14,22 et seq.) we are told that if the transport of the מעשר שני from a distance to Jerusalem is too difficult, one is allowed to redeem it by money. The קדושה of the produce is then transferred to this money which then has to be spent on food in the City of the Temple and eaten in the idea of מעשר שני (see ibid.). Now here it says that when the owner himself redeems the מעשר שני he must add a חומש to its value, as with all הקדש.

V. 32. מעשר בהמה .וכל מעשר בקר וגו׳ is the same for livestock as מעשר שני is for land produce. One tenth of the increase of one’s herds and flocks has to be designated as a קרבן of which the דם and אימורים are brought on to the altar but the whole animal remains to be eaten by the בעלים without any part being given to the כהנים. If it gets a מום, or if it had a מום when declared a “tenth” (see v. 33), then it may simply be eaten by the owner, but like all פסולי מוקדשים is אסור בגיזה ועבודה. It is נוהג בחוצה לארץ, to be observed also outside Israel, but according to ר״ע even בזמן הבית was not brought as a קרבן from outside the Land, but in these cases, can only be eaten by the owners if and when it has received a מום (Bechoroth 53a). Only those born to the livestock of one owner in each year, or those purchased by him before they had reached the age fitting them for offering (seven days, see Ch. 22,27), form a group from which מעשר must be separated. The group must consist of at least ten. Those that are born in one year are not grouped together with those of a previous or later year. Also from לקוח, — animals brought after they are seven days old, — and ניתן לו במתנה, — received as presents — no מעשר is to be given. (Bechoroth 55b & 56a). The ten animals must belong to one owner, partners are פטורין ממעשר בהמה (ibid. 56b). From a heritage which falls to a number of children, if they are all living together in one household, מעשר must be separated. But if the children have divided the heritage, even if later on they all join together again, חלקו וחזרו ונשתתפו, they do not give מעשר בהמה (ibid. 56b). For the purpose of מעשר, cattle on one hand form a group as בקר, and sheep and goats together form a separate one as צאן. One can mix the sheep and goats and whichever animal comes as the tenth is the מעשר for the group, but בקד and צאן are not interchangable for מעשר purposes, (ibid. 52a). This duty of tithe is not as absolute as מעשר דגן, that the animals should be טבל before the tithe is separated out, and as such should be אסור בהנאה. Sale and use of the animals before the duty of מעשר has been performed is permitted, but nevertheless it is a מצוה not to shirk the duty of giving מעשר (ibid. 58a).

כל אשר יעבר תחת השבט העשירי יהיה קדש. The animals are made to pass through a narrow gate one by one under the crook of the owner, who counts from one to ten, and marks the tenth with a red stripe. It is also valid if they are counted at rest and the tenth taken as מעשר, but not, if without counting in due order, one out of ten, or ten out of a hundred are taken out. (ibid. 58b). Also if nine have passed through the gate and the tenth remains behind it it is automatically עשירי מאליו הוא קדוש ,קדוש (ibid. 59a). Also, if after a number have passed through, out of the pen and have been counted to make the tenth one holy, and then this tenth one dies inside the pen, those that have already passed through out of the pen and have been counted are free from the duty of having מעשר taken מנין הראוי פוטר (ibid.) it says יעבור וגו׳ and not שכבר עבר. Now it does not say: וכל מעשר בקר וצאן עשירי אשר יעבר וגו׳ but the construction is interrupted: כל מעשר וגו׳ ,כל אשר יעבר תחת השבט העשירי יהיה קדש. So that there are two subjects to the predicate יהיה קדש viz. וכל מעשר וגו׳ כל אשר יעבר וגו׳ יהיה קדש and also וכל מעשר וגו׳ ,העשירי יהיה קדש, and the Halacha teaches (ibid. 60b): (a) that the passing through under the staff as the tenth, itself objectively makes the animal in question קדש even if it has erroneously been counted as the ninth, as well as (b) the calling of it “number 10” also makes an animal קדש even if it is really the ninth or the eleventh. Both עברה and calling it עשירי are given the power to make it קדש so that קרא לתשיעי עשירי ולעשירי תשיעי ולאחד עשר עשירי שלשתן מקודשין. In Nazir 32a, the question is raised and not definitely settled, whether it is only if done by mistake, that when the ninth and eleventh have been called the tenth that all three are קדש, or whether the result is the same if it was done deliberately, whether we take it טעותו ולא כונתו or טעותו וכל שכן כונתו (see מל״מ on Bechoroth 8,1). But the degree of holiness which falls on the ninth, tenth and eleventh in this manner differs in each case. The ninth does not come on to the altar at all, but is נאכל במומו, is kept and watched and is eaten if and when it receives a מום; the tenth is מעשר, and the eleventh is קרב שלמים (Bechoroth 6a). But although through a mistaken calling of the numbers, or perhaps even through an intended one, the קדושה of the real tenth can spread to the ninth and eleventh, nevertheless a doubtful tenth is in no ways עשירי ודאי אמר ,קדוש רחמנא ולא עשירי ספק, so that, accordingly קפץ אחד מן המנויין לתוכן הרי אלו פטורין, if one of those already counted, and so, as mentioned above, by מנין הראוי has become פטור jumped bark among the still uncounted ones, then they all become free from מעשר because the doubt hangs over each animal that it might be the one that is מעשר-free, so that amongst the whole mass of uncounted there is not a single one of which it could be said with certainty that it is a “tenth”, and the legal majority rule which is otherwise generally applied, בטול ברוב and כל דפריש מרובא פריש docs not afford the required certainty (see Baba Mezia 6b; ש״מ ibid.).

V. 33. לא יבקר בין טוב לרע: in the same sense as in V,10 above. He is not to examine each animal to see if it has a מום or is a תם, and may not try to arrange which animal shall come tenth (Bechoroth 36,b). Just as the מעשר-lot can fall on a בעל מום so can it fall on the other related רובע ונרבע וכו׳ :פסולים but not on כלאים טרפה וכו׳ (Bechoroth 57a; see on Ch. XXII.25). ולא ימירנו ,ואם המר ימירנו וגו׳ see above on V,10. והיה הוא ותמורתו וגו׳ nevertheless a תמורת מעשר does not come as a קרבן on to the altar; in this respect, בכור מעשר ופסח are alike, the תמורה of all three do not come onto the altar (Zebachim 37b); תמורת מעשר has to be kept watched until it receives a מום and then is allowed to be eaten, יאכל במומו לבעלים (Temura 21a).

לא יגאל. Neither the מעשר itself nor its תמורה can be redeemed (see on V,10); and, according to Bechoroth 31b et seq. the לא יגאל is to be taken in the sense of the extension of the limitations of the rights of disposal, so that it, like חרמים, of which it says in V,28, לא ימכר לא יגאל, may also not be sold. Its purpose is solely to be an offering; its blood, its דם and its אימורים are to be brought on to the altar, and then it itself like מעשר שני is to be eaten in the surroundings of the Sanctuary, anywhere in Jerusalem. Let us now try to find out the thoughts that are expressed by all these laws. We have already remarked on Gen. 14,20, that מעשר does not at all mean a tenth part — for that the term is עשירית — but the tenth, the one that completes, rounds off makes a whole unit of ten. It is an active form, like משען ,מפתח,

There in Gen., we expressed the idea that, in the same way that in בכור and בכורים, the beginning, the first start of an increase to our possession is dedicated to God, in acknowledgement of and thanks for, His having granted it, so in מעשר the tenth, which, so to speak, rounds off a completed attainment of wealth, we still acknowledge that the last penny, which can so easily be taken as merely the natural result of the preceding ones, is as much the direct gift granted by God, as the first which laid the foundation for it. Now this thought, which dedicates to God, as the expression of our relation to Him, not a tenth of all our possessions, but each tenth, as a tenth, i.e. as the product of the whole preceding succession of possessions coming from Him, and thereby acknowledges in this achieved tenth the whole preceding gradual accumulation of possessions which achieved it, as well as itself, as the gift of Divine Providence, this idea is most prominently expressed by the tithe of livestock, in מעשר בהמה. Not any one out of ten, or ten out of a hundred, taken out or even chosen from the herd or flock constitutes מעשר בהמה. That would only be dedicating that fraction, that tenth to God. But left entirely to itself, so that any animal can be the tenth as much as any other, the herds and flocks are made to pass one by one under the counting staff of the master — or at least while they are resting quietly are counted — and as soon as nine have been counted, the next one is automatically holy, העשירי קדש מאליו, it is just the preceding nine that sanctify the tenth as being their achievement, their product. And that also is just why the מעשר-command has been fulfilled on those which have been counted for this purpose, even if, after they have been counted, the completion of the counting has become spoilt, מנין הראוי פוטר, for in their having been counted for the purpose of dedicating the tenth they have already given expression of their relation to God, as being possessions which achieve increase of possessions by and under God’s management. And that is also why the sanctification of the tenth is not absolutely confined to itself, it can be shared by the ninth and spread to the eleventh, קרא לתשיעי עשורו ולעשירי תשיעי ולאחד עשר עשירי שלשתן מקודשין. Refusing the קדושה which had been proclaimed over the ninth and eleventh would be in contradiction to the whole intended trend of thought to be expressed, it would limit the conception of being holy to God to the one animal to be sacrificed (cf. מזבח מקדש הראוי לו ,חומש ,תמורה and similar ideas). But the קדושה of the tenth can only spread to the eleventh if the tenth had not tacitly or definitely been called the tenth, but had been called the ninth, as one that had not yet completed the series, that נעקר עשירי ממנו. Otherwise the series is completed with the tenth, and the eleventh can only be the commencement of a fresh unit.

But when the sanctification of the tenth does spread to the preceding and succeeding animals, the offering-idea is applied to them in three progressive stages. The ninth simply obtains קדושה, but is not actually brought as an offering, the tenth is brought onto the Altar as מעשר (see below) and the eleventh becomes שלמים.

To represent this thought which proclaims the prosperity of your possessions as being due to the blessing of God also in its final consummation which results from that which you already had, the definite presence of “a tenth” is essentially required. Only then does ten stand symbolically as a completed series of possessions, for which the nine forming elements can be counted. But as long as the finishing tenth is doubtfully there, the whole cohesive connection of the group is lacking, and the elements fall apart as single objects, hence probably עשירי ודאי ולא ספק. Finally, as, in מעשר בהמה it is not “one tenth” of your livestock but each “tenth one” which is to be dedicated, a herd which has not yet been counted can not be considered as divided off. In a stack of grain, the “tenth” part awaiting being separated off is there as the tenth part, for the whole is only the sum of all the parts that are there, and bears the character of every part of it. Hence a stack of grain which is dutiable for tithe is טבל. But in a herd which has not been counted no animal yet bears the character of a “tenth”, the whole conception only begins with the orderly counting, that is why the idea of טבל does not apply to מעשר בהמה .מעשר בהמה is accordingly an expression of acknowledging that the progressive prosperity of our livestock is due to the providence, the divine government, of God. As an offering it is understandably related to מנחה, which likewise is laid before God acknowledgingly, as the Giver of our food, our well being, and our satisfaction in life. Just as there מנחה is the one קרבן נדבה which can only be brought by single individuals but not by שותפות, to emphasize השגחה פרטית, the care and provision which God’s Love gives to each one of us, so מעשר בהמה also is not brought by partners, שותפין פטורין ממעשר בהמה (see on Ch. 2,1).

And as מעשר בהמה is to express the blessing of the increased prosperity of each individual home as the direct care and provision of God, it is to be given only from animals new born from one’s old stock, or at least those that have been reared in one’s own home (i.e. brought within eight days from birth as מחוסר זמן) but not from those bought already reared, or from those received as presents; and also the blessing of each separate year and the increase in each year of the different kinds of animals are looked on as a special separate gift of God’s management, and accordingly one may not give מעשר from animals born in one year for those born in another year, nor from צאן for בקר or vice versa.

Finally, therefore all the animals that represent the prosperity of our livestock are placed together in their respective מעשר-pens, even if they are פסולין לגבוה by a מום or otherwise, as long as they are מותרין להדיוט and so can be reckoned among the blessings of the home. The only ones excluded are טריפה, and apart from these also כלאים (animals bred in contraversion to the laws of the Torah), יוצא דופן (animals born not in the natural way) and יתום (animals whose mother died). All three probably not suitable to be reckoned in with the representation of the blessing of one’s livestock.

The tenth animal on which the lot falls to be the symbol of acknowledging God as the Dispenser of the prosperity of the home, becomes thereby consecrated to be an offering. It becomes the symbol of the personality of the owner of the herd or flock who wishes to get near to God with this offering, which is to preach to him that all the happiness which the prosperity of his home makes him enjoy should have the result of bringing him nearer and nearer to God. As with the קרבן פסח, only the דם and אימורים of the מעשר בהמה come onto the Altar. After this procedure has brought home to him that his whole existence (דם) and all his desires and endeavours (אימורים) must be related to God and to His Torah — his existence taking its root in the soil of the Torah leading upwards to the godly heights, מתנה אחת כנגד היסוד (it is not quite certain whether by שפיכה or זריקה see Zebachim 56b and ל״מ on הל׳ מעשה קרבנות 5,9), his will to be entirely absorbed in fulfilling the Will of God, to keep godliness on earth alive, כליות וחלב לריח ניחוח אשה לה׳ — after this, like with the קרבן פסח, the whole of the animal comes to the בעלים and their household, without any participation of the priests, to be eaten in homely enjoyment in the surroundings of the Sanctuary of the Torah, in the City of God.

The book of the Jewish Teachings of the Priests, concludes with two holy things מעשר שני and מעשר בהמה in which the happy enjoyment of life, kept within moral limits, is itself elevated to an act which is near to God, in which every home becomes a Temple, every table an altar, every Jew, every Jewess, without priestly intervention, consecrated as priests, themselves eating the holy things from God’s table. Thereby the “teachings of the priests” proclaim, as the final goal of all the institutions of the Sanctuary and of the work of its priests, the penetration of the whole of the people and the whole national life with the spirit of holiness, and the character of priest-like living and endeavours, the source of which springs from the Torah of God, which alone makes the Sanctuary the place of God, and in the realisation of which alone the priest has to see the whole meaning of his priestly consecration.

It is a goal which Zacharia has proclaimed will be be realised to the full in the future when history will have achieved its purpose, ביום ההוא יהיה על מצלות הסוס קדש לה׳ והיה הסירות בבית ה׳ כמזרקים לפני המזבח והיה כל סיר בירושלים וביהודה קדש לה׳ צבאות ובאו כל הזבחים ולקחו מהם ובשלו בהם ולא יהיה כנעני עוד בבית ה׳ צבאות ביום ההוא: Even the ornaments on the horses will bear the inscription “holy to God”, the cooking pots of the meals of the priests in the House of God will be like holy vessels for throwing the blood onto the altar, every cooking vessel in Jerusalem and Judah will be a holy thing of God’s, the God of all the spheres of the world, and there will no longer be any “traders” in the House of God”. No longer will one build and run temples and temple-life as a “business”, to try and trade the few buildings and the few minutes given to holiness and holy matters, for holiness in one’s life and in whatever place one happens to be, but one will build temples and visit them to sanctify and dedicate one’s whole life with the holiness that they teach.

V. 34. אלה המצות וגו׳. These words are repeated here to conclude the book of “the Teachings of the Priests”, to include this chapter of dedicating and valuing things for the purposes of the Sanctuary too, within the compass of God’s Torah, after a similar — but not the same — declaration was made at the end of the previous chapter V,46, looking back on all the other laws of this book. Even if the contents of this chapter on נדרי הקדש, on vows to dedicate things to the Temple, as being left entirely to the free will of the people, and just on that account not part of the real object of the “bond between God and us”, as the Torah is designated at the end of the previous chapter, (see V,1), nevertheless they are no less commandments given to Moses on Mount Sinai for Israel. Vows of dedication are not demanded, but if made, they come under the laws of God no less than any of all our other activities in life.
Numbers: V. 1. After the erection of the Sanctuary of the Torah had been described at the end of the second book of the Pentateuch, the whole of the third book was devoted to the demands which that Sanctuary made to the whole life of Israel. It demanded symbolic expression by the sacrifices and actual concrete sanctification of the whole mode of living. Thereby the ideal was shown which was to be realised by the public and private life of every individual and by the national life of the State. The final chapter, in נדרי הקדש allowed for the possibility of any individual feeling the necessity to express his special personal relation to this Sanctuary by vowing to undertake symbolic consecration of his own person, or by consecrating some of his possessions to the use or benefit of the Sanctuary.

Now this fourth book comes back to stark reality and shows us the actual relationship between the actual nation and this ideal of their calling shown in the third book. Accordingly it begins by having the individual members of the nation counted, but as an עדה, as one body united by this calling. By such a census, it is brought home to the government that the united nation is no mere vague conception, but exists in this universal calling of its members, and to the individuals that each one of them is reckoned as a not unimportant member of that nation, and that the national mission reckons on the faithfulness to duty, and conscious devotion to the common calling of all, of each individual.

The third book ends with instructions for dedicatory counting of sheep in groups of flocks by their owners. The fourth book begins with orders to count the nation as “God’s flock” for their “Shepherd”, in their family and tribal groups, and here too each one passes singly under the crook of the Shepherd and knows that he gets counted as an independent member of His flock.

במדבר סיני. The wilderness as the place for this counting is a proof that this counting was not for political purposes or for the national economy, for which in the “wilderness” there could be no possible inducement. But the immediate addition of סיני and אהל מועד at once tells us that this counting was in service of the Torah which was given on Sinai and had found a home for its homage in the אהל מועד. After the Torah had been received on Sinai, and, on the 1st of Nissan had found a home for its ideals with the re-presented tablets given as a pledge of the nation being re-accepted in the covenant with God after the sin of the golden calf, on the 1st of Iyar all tribes, families and individual men of the nation were to be counted for this Torah, and to muster about this Torah as its guards.

V. 2. שאו את ראש. See notes on Ex. XXX.12 et seq. According to the instructions given there in V.12 and 16, every such census had to be made by a half-shekel being given by every one who was to be counted. The total sum so collected was then used for בדק הבית for the upkeep of the Sanctuary-building, על עבודת אהל מועד. Through this contribution, by which a Jew is only “counted” as belonging by his doing something for the Torah, every census is expressed as being in the service of the Torah. Also this form of counting makes this introductory chapter of the fourth book in direct connection with the chapter of ערבים ונדרי הקדש with which the third book ended.

עדה .כל עדת בני ישראל (like דֵעה ,לֵדה ,שֵׁנה etc.) from יעד (related to יחד to join together for a certain purpose) designates people joined together for a common calling, and held together by the solidarity of that calling: a congregation. בני ישראל is the whole Jewish nation, within which the independent bearers and guardians of the common mission, the fulfilling of the Torah, form the עדה. What is here called עדה was expressed above, in Ex. XXX.12 by לפקדיהם which reproduces the same idea. פקודי בני ישראל are those whom the Jewish common mission “thinks of”, “appoints”, “entrusts”, that is, every “man” in Israel. Accordingly it is not a question of a census of the population, not how many people there are in Israel, but to find out how many “men” in Israel the Torah can “reckon” on.

למשפחותם לבית אבתם. But the individual members do not form the national congregation directly and immediately. The all-comprising national congregation consists of two concentric circles. The congregation is formed by tribes and every tribe by families. So that the men are to be counted in their belonging to a family, and the families in belonging to a tribe, and the numbers contained in each tribe added together form the sum total of the עדת בני ישראל.

משפחה (from שפח related to ספח to be added, to join oneself (Is. XIV.1) and שפע which means a gathered mass holding together as שפעת יהוא (II. Kings, IX.17), שפעת גמלים (Is. LX.6) שפעת סוסיו (Ezek. XXVI.10)): שפח with prefixed מ, the factor that joins and keeps individuals in natural groups, the family. But the factor that forms the family is, descent from a common parent, and marriage that transfers the wife to the home of her husband. בית אבותם, from places like Ch. II. 2. 32, 34; XVII, 17. 18 and elsewhere it is quite definitely clear that by בית אב the tribe is meant to be understood. The individuals first group themselves into families, the families into tribes, and finally the tribes, in the higher union of all originating from one common house, into the “House of Israel”, בית ישראל. From their spreading out from the one common stem the tribes are called מטות really branches (Cf. Ezek. 19,11-14), and from the various families belonging to the common branch, the original family home, are called בתי אבות. So that the one בית ישראל consisted of twelve בתי אבות, and each בית אב of several משפחות which formed the first unit which joined the individuals into groups. The tribe of Levi separated out from the general nation to a special unit on its own shows the same grouping in nuce. For it לוי is what ישראל is for the rest of Israel, the sons of גרשון קהת ,לוי ומדרי form the בתי אבות (Ch. 3,24, 30, 35), their sons לבני ושמעי ,עמרם ויצהר חברון ועוזיאל ,מחלי ומושי, form the משפחות הלוי לבית אבותם (ibid 18-20). This fact, that the whole nation is looked at and called as one household בית ישראל as the children of one man as בני ישראל, and, on the other hand, within this union still remain and are considered as separate units, ,משפחות בתי אבות, forms the peculiarity of Jewish nationality. By considering the nation as “the House of Israel” and all its nationals as “children of Israel”, the conception of the Jewish “nation” is protected from taking itself to be without the necessity for real internal union, or to imagine that the appearance of a united representation of a model nation is a mere fiction. It must always and at all times make itself thought of in the essential real universal calling of its members, who by a common inner factor are one, and each one of them must feel himself to be, and to present himself as a concrete and important part of this unity. Even when the decendants of the one Jew Israel had grown to six hundred thousand men (at least two million souls I.L.) they were still all members of “one house”, sons of “one man”, stamped in spirit and heart with the same stamp, bearing one mission, one destiny as their heritage through the ages. And in the midst of this fundamental sameness and unity and under its influence, the greatest diversity of tribal and family specialities of traits and dispositions was diligently and carefully nurtured, so that — as we have repeatedly pointed out in Genesis — the one great task of humanity as shown by the Torah is to be demonstrated as a model for the whole human race, as being in no way dependent on any speciality, but applies to every diversity of character, tendency, profession or position in life. Every tribe in its speciality and every family in its own peculiarity have to work at the common task of the House of Israel and educate and bring their children up to it in their own speciality and peculiarity. That is why the hundreds of thousands of the House of Israel do not come to the nation as a disjointed mass but למשפחתם לבית אבותם according to their families, and these families in reference to the tribe to which they belong. The number of the men in each tribe is noted and the families in each tribe kept separately. And each family במספר שמות, every member of the family is counted by name, so that each one joins the whole, conscious of the importance of his personality to the nation, and indeed כל זכר לגלגלותם, each person has personally to hand in his half-shekel and report as so-and-so from this or that family, of this or that tribe, unless the attachment to family and tribe had been proclaimed already by grouping beforehand. In any case every one who came to be counted had his relation to his family and tribe brought to his mind and “as such” was he counted to the total. By למשפחתם לבית אבתם, the principle is at the same time implied that the tribal character, a ,יהודי ,לוי ,כהן שמעוני etc. and also the right of inheritance, goes from the father’s side and not from the mother (Baba Bathra 109 & 110b). גלגלת really skull, at the counting, stands for the actual presence of the individual in person. At the mass of people, the heads offer the best means of counting them. But at the Jewish counting, the heads themselves were not counted but בקע לגלגלת (Ex. XXXVIII.26) a half-shekel was paid for each head.

V. 3. צבא ,מבן עשרים שנה ומעלה כל יוצא צבא בישראל is by no means, not even primarily the army or military service. Ch. IV.3. כל בא לצבא לעשות מלאכה באהל מועד or ibid. 23, לצבא צבא לעבוד וגו׳ and elsewhere there referring to the service of the Levites in the Temple, as well as Ch. 8,24, 25 are sentences which prove that צבא is altogether to be understood as every united body under higher orders for public service or for such services to be rendered by such a body. And here too, one need not necessarily think of military service. יצא צבא ישראל would rather designate everyone who is in duty bound to step out of his simple private life into the public service of the community whenever it is demanded of him to do so. Accordingly, every one on whom the community can reckon to carry out its general concerns. And that is כל זכר every man מבן עשרים שנה ומעלה. Referring to the Levites whose whole lives stand in service of the public it does not say יוצא צבא but בא לצבא (Ch. IV) — לצבאתם see ibid. XII.51.
V. 4. ואתכם וגו׳. It seems that at the whole proceeding, the heads of all the tribes assisted and not just each one at the counting of his own tribe.
V. 5. The ל in לשמעון ,לראובן etc. would mean for Reuben etc.; the tribe was represented by its head.

V. 16. קרואי העדה, written קָרִיא .קריאי, noun form, like שָׂכִיר ,נדיב designated “being called” as the permanent character of the men; קָרוּא a verbal form would indicate that he was called for the occasion in question. The men, named here were those whom the community generally called on for their guidance in and for carrying out their concerns, they were קריאי העדה, so that they were those who had the confidence and recognition of the public for national affairs, and they were קרואי העדה, they were specially called on for this business of counting which was to be undertaken. They were also נשיאי מטות אבותם those who within their own tribes, by reason of their social position were the princes, had been placed at the head of the tribe as “raised bearers of public concerns” (see note on Gen. XXV.16 I.L.). Accordingly they were ראשי אלפי ישראל, those who, on account of their characters and their positions the whole nation recognised as its leaders.

V. 18. ויתילדו על משפחתם וגו׳. They reported by giving their names according to their birth belonging to families and tribes. ,מבן עשרים וגו׳ ואת כל העדה וגו׳. The עדה consisted of all the men over 20 years. See on V.2.
V. 19. ויפקדם במדבר סיני. By this repetition, before the beginning of the counting the idea and meaning of it is again brought to mind and stressed. See on V.1.
V. 20. ויהיו בני ראובן. The order of the tribes in which they came to be counted is exactly in accordance with their grouping in the camp, as is described in Ch. II, to which refer.

V. 22. תולדותם וגו׳. All these details which characterise this counting so peculiarly are factors which are to be brought home to the mind of each person who was thus counted. They are repeated expressly with each tribe. By this the complete equality and the completely equal valuation of all the tribes and their members in their meaning and importance for the nation is maintained. This is stressed quite specially already at the second tribe Simeon by the extra word פקדיו. After Reuben’s, his, Simeon’s counting too, was done exactly and literally as prescribed, and so, of course, all the following ones, at which moreover all the essential factors were specially repeated again.

V. 42. בני נפתלי, here it does not say as it does to all the preceding ones לבני נפתלי and this confirms that לבני גד ,לבני שמעון etc. does not mean “of” but “to the sons of Simeon” etc., and means, out of the assembled mass of the nation (V.18) there stepped to the tribe of Simeon etc., as belonging to him etc. So that after eleven tribes had been counted, the rest, those who had not been counted, remained over by themselves as forming the twelfth tribe and there was no necessity for them to step up to be recognised as such. Hence not לבני נפתלי but בני נפתלי. Such a missing ל- is a striking sign of the recording of a proceeding which had been directly personally witnessed.

V. 47. לא התפקדו, a form compiled from a combination of the התפעל and הָפעל. They were not allowed or were not induced to number themselves together with the rest of the nation. Not by their own suggestion because perhaps they imagined themselves something special did they keep back from the general census. They would have counted themselves with the others if left to themselves, but this was prevented by the Higher Command as the following verse immediately informs us.

V. 48. We have already remarked on V.2 how the common possession of a task to be done or a mission to be carried out is essentially innate in the concept עדה. It forms the reason and purpose of the unity of a congregation, the uniting element in the Jewish national community is none other than the Divine Torah. This uniting factor is to be provided with some concrete visible symbol to be with them on all their journeys whether they are wandering on or encamping. The concrete evidence of the revelation of this Torah consisted in the two Tablets of the Law, which later on were accompanied by a copy of the Torah itself in writing. Its abode was the Tabernacle, the Tent of Meeting, which represented symbolically the demands and the effect of making it a reality. It, the “abode of this evidence” was always to form the centre point about which the Children of Israel are to form groups in their families and tribes. But just as at the giving of this Torah to be the uniting soul of the Jewish people, the fact was to be made clear by הבדלה and התקדשות (fencing off and purifying preparations I.L.) — as we recognised on Ex. 19,10-13, 20-25 — that the Torah did not emanate from the people but came to them from Divine origin; and it was and is the lofty inviolable ideal which every individual in Israel, and Israel as a whole, is to use all power and energy to attain, but which we can never approach, however united we may be, to lay mastering hands on it; in the same way, after it had already entered in Israel’s midst — as the Psalmist sings ה׳ בם סיני בקדש “God is already in their midst and Sinai henceforth is in the Sanctuary” (Ps. LXVIII.18) — this Torah and its Sanctuary, “the abode of the Evidence” received a place apart from the people, became a cut-off, separated centre point, round about which at a distance — מנגד סביב as it significantly calls it in Ch. II. 2. — the Children of Israel are to encamp. By “this circle keeping at a distance” the Torah remained for ever something given from outside, something that ever draws us to it but is never absorbed into us, is always our master which directs and keeps us in the paths indicated by it. And the tribe that remained faithful to God and His Torah and defended its inviolability against the people and their own relatives at the first defection from the Torah, when the people, forgetting its “given” nature took steps on their own to make a divine Moses for themselves, the tribe of Levi remained as “guardians” around the Torah. As such they were separate from the people, they did not belong to the “congregation” but to the “abode of Evidence” which was to be upheld as the ruling soul of the congregation, so they, as was already said in the previous verse and is developed further in the next one, were not to be counted בתוך בני ישראל.

V. 49. אך את מטה לוי לא תפקד וגו׳ בתוך בני ישראל, it alone is not to be reckoned on for the general public service, ואת ראשם לא תשא וגו׳, and as a body they form a community apart from the natural community, they do not belong to the עדה but to the עדות.

V. 50. ואתה הפקד וגו׳. As they had to care for and act for the Torah in their life, the care and representation of the Sanctuary of the Torah is also to be in their hands. Their care for it is to consist in carrying it and its appurtenances on the wanderings, as well as in erecting it etc., the ישרתהו, in their position in encamping immediately round about it and keeping guard over it.

V. 51 מיתה בידי שמים: והזר הקרב יומת (death by God’s Hand) — In the previous verse it said ואתה הפקד את הלוים. Only as a result of direct appointment by Moses through God’s command were even the לוים to approach the Abode of the Evidence with the duties they were to discharge. Everybody who was not bound by duty to do so was considered to be unauthorised to do so, to be a זר, so much so that even a Levite was only authorised to perform the particular task allotted to him, and it was forbidden for a Levite to transfer himself from one function to another נקיטינן משורר ששיער בשל חבירו במיתה (Arachim 11b). More, just as the Levite had to abstain from the functions of the priests, so were the priests not empowered to do those of the Levites (ibid). So much so was the whole service of the Sanctuary to be stamped with the character of “being prescribed, ordained”, of inviolability, and it was just that that was to be constantly kept vivid in the minds of Israel by this keeping apart of the Sanctuary of the Torah and its ministers (See on Ch. III.10).

V. 52. וחנו בני ישראל וגו׳. As is more precisely ordered in the following chapter, the whole nation is to encamp and journey in four sections, each camp is to consist of three tribes, one of which is appointed as leader of that section. There was a camp of Judah, one of Reuben, one of Ephraim and one of Dan. Although in the following chapter, standards are only expressly mentioned at the leading tribe of each camp, דגל מחנה יהודה דגל מחנה ראובן etc., verse 2 ordains איש על דגלו באתת לבית אבתם, clearly that every tribe is to have its flag, and in our verses too מחנהו and דגלו are clearly not identical. But what it says here is: each one is to encamp at his camp, and in the camp, and each one by his flag, i.e. at his tribe. So it is also understood in במדבר רבה that each tribe had its own particular flag, the colour of which corresponded with the colour of the jewel on the breast pocket of the high priest which bore the names of the tribes. Perhaps in V.2 of the following chapter there is a difference between דגלו and אתת לבית אבתם. Perhaps דגל is the large standard of the camp of the leading tribe of that camp to which two other tribes were attached, and the אתת לבית אבתם are smaller field flags, signs for the position of each individual tribe. The איש על דגלו of our verse nevertheless in our opinion is only to be taken as referring to the tribal flags, לצבאתם would then be the still smaller group of each family within its tribe, and also in V.2 of the following chapter, the accentuation speaks only for the first way of taking it. דגל is presumably related to דקל the Chaldean word for the palm tree, which grows straight up and with its spreading top is visible far away and so could easily express a military standard. Thus pillars of smoke rising high up are also called “smoke-palms” (Joel 3,3; Song of Songs III.6) תמרות עשן.

V. 53. ולא יהיה קצף וגו׳ Cf. Ch. 17,11, XVIII,6. The rebellion of Korach was nothing but a denial of the Divine origin of the laws of the Torah, and the inviolability of the Torah which was always to be known and recognised by the unapproachableness of the Sanctuary for every unauthorised person.
V. 54. שריחקו עצמן מן המשכן ונתנו מקום ללוים לחנות סביב :ויעשו וגו׳ (במדבר רבה) למשכן they drew back from the Sanctuary and left space for the Levites to encamp round about the Sanctuary.

V. 1. The grouping of Israel in separate fixed camps and, separated from them, the camp of the Levites and the Sanctuary, which was ordered in general terms at the end of the preceding chapter is now gone into in detail in this chapter. The order up to now to count the nation according to tribes and families was given to Moses alone, this final grouping of the counted tribes in a circle at a distance from the Sanctuary in the centre was directed to Moses and Aaron, and just thereby this grouping of the camps about the Sanctuary of the Torah is indicated as being the important purpose of the whole census-taking. We have already remarked on Levit. 11,1 and XIII,1 that drawing Aaron in to receive the Word of God with Moses indicates that the quite special importance of the laws so given is to be the law which is represented by Moses, but especially also of attracting and gaining the masses to carry it out, which is set as the task of the life of the priests. And this law too, which directs each individual to his family and tribe, and the tribe to its group in the camp, and makes all the camps, whether resting or marching, rest and march מנגד סביב לאהל מועד, with the Sanctuary as their centre-point, by mentioning Aaron’s name in the introductory heading receives great importance for the education of Jewish people, Jewish families, Jewish tribes to the Torah. The prince, the head of the camp, when they came to rest planted his flag מנגד סביב “even if at a distance still facing and within the circle of the Sanctuary”, and on the journey had it raised and kept in that relative position, and so gathered and kept together his tribes, and similarly each tribe its families and each family its members, thereby proclaimed the משכן העדות (V.53 I.L.) to himself and right down to the smallest growing Jewish child, as being the אהל מועד (V.2 I.L.) the Abode of the Evidence as the place of the common mission which united and held them all together. Thereby the Torah — testified for by God — became, from the princes of the tribes and leaders of the camps down the smallest lisping child, the real ever-present life soul of the people in the whole height of the holiness necessary for its effectiveness — מנגד, — and in the nearness of its power of embracing everything and everybody — סביב. That is why, in this chapter of ordering the positions of the camps the Tent of the Torah which previously in V.50 and 53 was called משכן העדות is here called the אהל מועד. In itself it is the משכן העדות, the “Abode of the Evidence” (the place where the tablets of stone, visible evidence by the miraculous nature of the letters, of the Divine origin of the Torah I.L.), and for the people it is the אהל מועד, in all their wanderings always before their eyes, the centre point which unites them all in their common calling (יחד יעד: מועד).

V. 2. איש על דגלו באתת וגו׳. As already remarked on V.52 of the previous chapter, by the cantillation באתת belongs to דגלו (i.e. דגל which in the rest of the chapter refers to the large camp-standard, here is qualified by אתת, the smaller tribal flags I.L.). The flags of each בית אב, each tribe, had an אות, a distinguishing emblem representing the tribe. According to במדבר רבה, each flag was of the colour of the stone on the breast of the high-priest which corresponded to that tribe and also had a characteristic emblem on it (Reuben had flowers, דודאים, on a red flag, Judah, a lion on a sky-blue flag etc. I.L.) מנגד, at a distance of a מיל, i.e. 2000 cubits (ibid) corresponding to the תחום שבת, so that, as it says there, they could go to the אהל מועד on Sabbath.

V. 3. קדמה. The front of the general camp. The entrance to the אהל מועד also faced to the east. There in the east, Judah with his associated tribes had his camp and he was always the first to break camp and start the journey forward.

V. 4. וצבאו ופקדיהם. Throughout, here and in the following, those belonging to a tribe are designated by the two expressions צבאו and פקודיהם or, as in the three following tribes צבאו and פקדיו. Once, in their totality they are called צבא הנשיא, as being under the command of the leader, which is really what makes them into a צבא (See on Gen. II.1). But it is brought to their and his consciousness that they are פקודים, they had already, independently, before they came under his orders, been counted, and counted not for his command but for their tribe and for the nation as a whole. So that they belong to themselves and to the mission of their tribe and nation, and they are only placed under his command for the accomplishment of this mission; and his orders have only power for such accomplishment. The addition of ופקדיו ,ופקדיהם accordingly gives the necessary limitation to his power and assures all those who are under his command, inalienable independence. That is why in the overwhelming majority of cases the צבא is thought of in possessive relation to the פקדים with the latter as a plural unit consisting of a number of individuals as פקודיהם and one has to consider why in the cases of the tribes Isaachar, Zebulun and Reuben it remains as a single unit, וצבאו ופקודיו.

V. 14. רמב״ן points out the difference in the name of the father of the prince of the tribe of Gad, which above Ch. I.14 was given as Deuel and here as Reuel. He remarks that the differences in the names of the same man which occur not infrequently show that people often took the name of a man to have a meaning and not to be just an “appellation-sound” and hence his contemporaries used commonly to call a man by a name which was synonymous with his real one and so two names of a man both having similar meaning became usual and current. Thus the name זרח and צוחר were identical, both meaning shining, and so also דעואל and רעואל, his mind (דעת) or his thoughts (רעיון) were directed towards God. Moreover, cf. our remarks on Gen. XXXVI.1.

V. 17. אעפ״י שנסע אהל מועד הוא :ונסע אהל מועד: even when dismantled and in transit on the journeys, the Abode of the Evidence remained the holy gathering point of the national mission. The camps remained מחנה ישראל so that קדשים קלים (the offerings of “a meal of peace”) could be eaten in them, and even if the אהל מועד had already been taken to pieces, the place still enclosed by the hanging tapestry retained the קדושת עזרה so that קדשי קדשים could still be eaten there; also on the journeys מצורעים had to be banned out of the מחנות ישראל and זבים from the מחנה לויה. See Ch. V. 2 & 3 (Menachoth 95a. Zebachim 61b, 116b. 117a תוספות there) כאשר יחנו כן יסעו, on their journeys too the arrangement of the camps was the same:- the אהל מועד, surrounded by the Levites, in the centre, in the van at the prescribed distance the camp of Judah with the attached tribes, on the right the camp of Reuben, on the left that of Dan and bringing up the rear the camp of Ephraim. And also according to the view that on the journeys they marched in one straight line (see on Ch. X.25), the same order was kept, the various tribes keeping in the groups ordered here and following in the same succession, with the אהל מועד entrusted to the Levites in the centre of the line.

V. 34. ויעשו בני ישראל. If we picture to ourselves the grouping of the Jewish nation in the camps prescribed here, we have in the front to the east under the standard of Judah, the tribes of Judah, Isaachar and Zebulun; to the right, in the south under the standard of Reuben the tribes of Reuben, Simeon and Gad; to the left, in the north, under the standard of Dan the tribes of Dan, Asher and Naphtali; at the back opposite to Judah, under the standard of Ephraim the tribe of Ephraim, Menasseh and Benjamin. Each of the three tribes which form the leading camp is characterised in two directions, (material and spiritual I.L.). The father on his death-bed (Gen. 49,8-10) already visualised Judah as the prominent foremost tribe with both שבט and מחוקק, with the sceptre of rule and the engraving style of the Law. Isaacher was the tribe of both agriculture and of securing leisure for study (see vv. 14 & 15 ibid) Zebulun (v.13 ibid) was the commercial tribe and also — as we can deduce from the song of Deborah (Judges V.14) — מושכים בשבט סופר of cultivators of literature. So that in the leading camp of Judah all the essential factors were united on which the material and spiritual welfare of the nation depend — the sceptre and the law, agriculture and science, commerce and literature. These two factors, the spiritual and the material combined in the leading camp are separated right and left in the two subordinate camps behind it. The camp to its right consisted of Reuben, Simeon and Gad. Reuben, the firstborn, gifted with all the advantages of intelligence and a deep feeling for what is right and just, but with a softness and tenderness of character which denied him the firmness for leadership, and in conjunction with him, Simeon, the quick impulsive avenger of honour, and Gad, the arrow-like avenger of unjustified attack (see Gen. XLIX. 3, 4, 5-7, 19). So that on Judah’s right there was the courage and the disposition to ward off insult and attack, placed under the aegis of mildness. On his left was Dan, the tribe of adroit cleverness (ibid XVI.17); Asher, refinement of taste (ibid. 20, cf. חמרא וריחני פקחין Yoma 76b), and Naphtali (ibid. 21), eloquence. So that, under the aegis of Dan, there was a rich development in the direction of culture as on the right, under Reuben, development in the direction of strength and force. On the side opposite to the eastern camp, to the west, the tribes of Ephraim, Menasseh and Benjamin were encamped under the standard of Ephraim. The “meaning and importance of these three tribes for the nation are not as clearly characterised as with the others. Ephraim and Menasseh together really represent the tribe of Joseph. But what Jacob said on his death-bed regarding Joseph had more reference to Joseph personally than to his tribe. What was pronounced on Ephraim and Menasseh (ibid XLVIII.19) lies in the indication of development of greatness and might; especially of Ephraim it says that he will become very “great” and that his descendants will become מלא הגוים which we there took to mean “the complemental armour of the rest of the tribes”. So that in Ephraim’s camp we probably have to look for “bravery” which, for the national well-being should find its place as the leading tendency of the camp of Judah, Judah in the east, supplemented by Ephraim in the West. Thus Asaph’s song sees (Ps. 80,2 3) the well-being of Israel dependent on the successes of “Joseph” and implores ,רועה ישראל האזינה נוהג כצאן יוסף ישב הכרובים הופיעה לפני אפרים ובנימן ומנשה עוררה את גבורתך ולכה לישעתה לנו the Shepherd of Israel to give ear”. “O Shepherd of Israel, incline Thine ear, Thou that leadest Joseph like a flock, Thou, that art enthroned on the cherubim, shine forth; before Ephraim and Benjamin and Manasseh (just the tribes of the camp we are considering I.L.) awake Thy Allmight and come and save us”. When later on in our history, instead of complementing Judah, the house of Joseph opposed Judah and took the leadership away from him, planted its standard not “behind Judah” but at the head of the nation, the grave of the national well-being was dug, and the “House of Joseph” — estranged from the evidence (v.1 ibid I.L.) of the Torah and its “Abode”, — perished and dragged with it down to its ruin ten-twelfth of the nation which had attached itself to it.
In במדבר רבה too there is given an explanation of the four camps in accordance with their importance and meaning for the nation. (Refer to it).

V. 1. The sons of Israel had been counted as the עדה, the community. Now the Levites are to be counted as the guardians of the עדות. But first Moses and Aaron are thought of, those who were not among the counted but were the counters. At the same time names of the family of the one, Aaron, were established, for their descendants were not reckoned actually as Levites but formed a national group on their own, כהנים, the priests. It was to be established that only two sons, Eleazar and Ithamar were to carry on the priesthood after Aaron, so that for all time only those are eligible for the כהונה who descend from either Eleazar or Ithamar. It is significant that although it says תולדות of משה also, the sons of Moses are not named. For in all these chapters of numbers, only those are mentioned of the dead who formed the separate branches of the tribes and families, but of the living only those are named who had some official public position as נשיאים and כהנים. But our Moses allowed his sons to be quite absorbed in the masses without any special distinction, he did not have even a small position, a tiny title, a small badge for his own children.

ביום דבר וגו׳. As Nadab and Abihu were to be named to say that no priestly families descended from them, but they were already dead at the time of the counting, the ביום דבר here must refer to an earlier date. When God gave the Torah and appointed Aaron and his sons to the priesthood, Aaron had four sons, all four of whom were consecrated and appointed as priests.
V. 2. The notation is peculiar. It is as if the report pauses painfully over Nadab, then lingers on Abihu and then quickly adds Eleazar and Ithamar.

V. 4. וימת נדב וגו׳. See on Levit. X. 1, 2. — ובנים לא היו להם. Had sons been born to them after they had been consecrated, these would have received the character of priests by birth and the priesthood would have been inherited from them by families that descended from them. But as they left no sons when they died ויכהן אלעזר ואיתמר על פני אהרן אביהם. We remarked on Gen. XVI.12 that the expression על פני is not infrequently used in connection with unpleasant disagreeable experiences. Through his two elder sons dying childless Aaron was left with only Eleazar and Ithamar to carry on the priesthood.

V. 5. וידבר וגו׳. In the preceding verses the families who are appointed to the priesthood are established, and, at the same time the death of the two elder sons is remembered, who, immediately at the very first days of the completed consecration of the priests, at the first holiest function of the priestly service, met their death because they brought אש זרה “their own ideas” into the priestly service. And the whole of the service in the Sanctuary rests just on “service” and in “service”, has its root and symbolic meaning just in obedience. It is to represent “joyful obedience”, happy submission to the will of God, — putting aside our own ideas however lofty they may seem to us, — as the base and goal of the whole mission of our lives. How very much the accomplishment of this mission is dependent on the definite consciousness, ever to be kept awake in our minds, that this Will of God — the evidence of its revelation resting in its “Abode” — is something that came to us directly from God Himself — how this “given” nature of the Torah is always to be kept before our eyes by the position of its “evidence” in the centre of the nation and by keeping this centre-point at a distance from the habitations of the nation, and that the tribe of Levi was appointed as guardians for the nation of this God-given evidence, has already been exhaustively described in Ch. I.48. Now here this guard of the Sanctuary, itself, is regarded in its relation to the priest and to the nation, and in accordance with that the relative position of the Levites entrusted with this guard, to the other two national circles, the priests and the community, is detailed. First their position in relation to the priest.

V. 6. הקרב וגו׳. The “Evidence of the Torah” itself, or rather the demand which it makes has already received a living representative in the midst of the people, in the כהן, who, by the symbolic procedures of the offerings inside the Sanctuary, as well as by living his whole life outside it in accordance with the laws of the כהונה is to be מכין and מכונן the nation, prepare them and direct them to carry out these demands. The priestly task of educating the nation up to the meaning and ideals of the Sanctuary of the Torah belongs in the very first place to the “Levite Guard” about the Torah. For the inviolablity of the Sanctuary and its demands is the very first starting point of the position of the priest, the כהן is appointed to be the first watchman of the Torah over the nation — and over himself. So that primarily the guard which the Levites have to keep about the Sanctuary is given the character of assistant service to the mission which the priests have to carry out. Thereby the function of the Levites themselves is placed in the light of a higher closer relation to the godly educational purposes which the priests have to look after. הקרב, it says, “let them come near” to you and to Aaron, והעמדת אותו לפני אהרן הכהן cf. Esther IV.5, Daniel I.5, I Sam. XVI.16, 22, I Kings I.2 etc. where עמד לפני always designates the position of personal service. — ושרתו אותו we have already referred on Ex. XXXI. 10, to the relationship between שרת and שרד and remarked how שרת always indicates personal service, i.e. doing something for somebody which excuses him from doing something which otherwise he would have to do himself to satisfy his wishes, his duties, etc. The use of these two expressions here, והעמדת אותו לפניו וגו׳ and ושרתו אתו give the לויה the office of the Levite the character of co-working assistant to the כהונה.

V. 7. ושמרו את משמרתו, the guard which they have to keep they are to do as an office transferred to them from the priesthood but also as משמרת כל העדה. The priesthood itself is only the representative of the national community in the Sanctury. For the Torah is not given to the priests and Levites, it is given to the whole nation who are responsible for it. It was not priests and Levites who had to build a holy place for it and who did build it. ועשו לי מקדש ושכנתי בתוכם was said to the whole nation, who were to build for God a holy place for His Torah so that God should be present בתוכם amongst them. So that the priest and the Levite stand there in the name of the nation and the watch of the Levites about the Sanctuary is to be made as representative of the nation. The Torah and its Sanctuary is a holy treasure entrusted to the nation. שמירה “guarding” it against infringement by others — and by themselves — is the first duty of those to whom the guarding of such a treasure has been entrusted. So that in their own interests, to carry out their first responsibility the nation as a whole and individually makes the Levites keep guard about the Sanctuary of the Torah against themselves, as indeed this watch has to be kept not only against the nation but even against the priests. And והזר הקרב יומת that warns every unqualified person from officiating as a Levite, and keeps not only the people but the Levites mutually against each other, and the priest in relation to the functions of the Levites — as already remarked above — each to the limitations of his appointed place.

לעבד את עבודת המשכן. The Levites are commissioned by the priest (משמרתו) and by the national community לעבד את עבדת (משמדת כל העדה) המשכן to the service of the Sanctuary. They stand, in their service to the Sanctuary, as the representatives of Aaron and of the community.

V. 8. ושמרו את כלי אהל מועד, the מנורה ,שולחן ,ארון and the מזבחות are the כלי אהל מועד, they make the משכן to the central assembly point where the whole nation finds the common mission which unites them all. For in them are laid down the task that is incumbent on all of them (the ארון) and the resulting demands on the mode of living of every individual soul in Israel (the שלחן, מנורה, ומזבחות). The משכן entrusts them with these כלים, and they are at the same time a treasure entrusted to them by every individual Jew, they are משמרת בני ישראל, every Jewish soul has a right in them, and with that in mind are they to attend to the service of the Sanctuary.

V. 9. ונתתה. Now although the Levites have to perform their services in the name of the priests and in the name of the people they are in no wise generally under the orders of either priests or officials of the community by some innate power of authority. But rather ונתתה: God ordains that through Moses — a Divine command to be carried out through Moses — the obligations which lie on the community, and on the priests on behalf of the community, to guard and look after the Sanctuary are to be transferred to, and taken over by, the Levites. For this purpose Moses is to “give” them from out of the people, or as from the people to the priests. But beyond these specific purposes the priests have not the slightest power of command over the Levites. נתונים נתונים המה לו “given, given” are they to him. The position of the Levites towards the priests does not arise from any general superior position of the latter, and altogether goes no further than the purposes and terms of these arrangements are specified.

V. 10. ואת אהרן. After the priests had been relieved of their obligations towards the watch and care of the Sanctuary and its contents, the real obligations of the כהונה remained to them. The Sanctuary itself, established by the nation, was entrusted to the Levites. They had to guard it against non-authorised intruders, to care for it on the journeys, dismantle and re-erect it on each occasion. They had to see to it that the Sanctuary was “there” in all its prescribed details. But the Aaronides had the responsibility for the כהונה, for the performance in that Sanctuary of all those procedures in which the everlasting preparation of the people for, and directing them to, the demand to work themselves towards the ideal was expressed, and the effect of which go out from this Sanctuary of the Torah to have practical results on the national and private life of the people.

V. 11. The position of the Levites to the community and to the priests had just been characterised as an arrangement ordered by God. This arrangement and the special relationship of the Levites towards God which lies in it, is now here more fully explained.

V. 12. ואני, it is God who took the Levites out of the people to be in a special relation to Himself, to be specially belonging to Him, a condition which hitherto had been innate in the firstborn. The sanctification of the firstborn, as we worked out on Ex. XIII.2, appointed the firstborn son in every family to care for and represent godliness i.e. the fulfillment of God’s Will, within each family circle. It was accordingly on them that the responsibility rested for the common factor that joined the differing and different groups, the צבאות ה׳ to the one united people of God. When then this common factor was to be expressed symbolically and play an important part in the Sanctuary of the Torah and guards were to be appointed for it, the first born, already sanctified by God as the representatives of godliness amongst the people would naturally present themselves also for this post of guarding and servicing the Sanctuary. But on the fateful day of the sin of the golden calf the firstborn did not prove themselves as the champions and guardians of the Divine Torah. What one would have expected them to do was done by the Levites. The sons of Levi stood up “לה׳״ in their place. Already then Moses had exhorted them to keep this position of defender of the Torah amongst the people and to expect the blessing of God for it. (see on Ex. XXXII.29). So here we see them picked out from the midst of the children of Israel by God in place of the firstborn and given the vocation והיו לי to be “His”, to belong to the representation of His Sanctuary among the people. So that if, after what has already been said, they are to undertake the guard of the Sanctuary and the service of it as משמדת משכן העדות (Ch. I.23) as משמרת אהרן and as משמרת כל העדה (Ch. III.7) in the name of the Sanctuary, in the name of the priests and in the name of the whole community, they are in the very first place to do it in the name of God, בשם ה׳ as those that belong לה׳ Who has appointed them for His Sanctuary, and Who has transferred to them the obligations of that Sanctuary which without them would be incumbent on the general community, their natural representatives (the firstborn I.L.) and the priests.

V. 13. כי לי כל בכור. Cf. Ex. XIII.15 — לי יהיו. By the transference of the service of the Sanctuary from the firstborn to the Levites, the consecration of the firstborn is not removed. They remain, unaffected by the transference, holy, consecrated to God. By this transference they have only forfeited the position of representing the nation at the Sanctuary, but their meaning and importance within the family as expressing the family belonging to God, as well as the meaning of the consecration of the firstborn of בהמה טהורה and that of פטר חמור as symbolic of the family food and the family possessions belonging to God is unimpaired and continues. In Becharoth 5a this expression לי יהיו is taken as בהוייתן יהיו (they shall be as they were hitherto I.L.), and as a confirmation of the teaching of ר׳ יוחנן that the sanctification of the firstborn which started in Egypt continued uninterruptedly קדשו ולא פסקו and not as ריש לקיש takes it that it was only resumed with the entry into the Land of Israel (see on Ex. XIII.11) הקדשתי לי כל בכור בישראל. The consecration of the firstborn has no physical significance, it is purely symbolical and has only a moral national meaning of the highest import. בכור is accordingly only בישראל, has holiness only in a sphere of holiness that is exclusively Jewish, but as soon as there is any non-Jewish right of possession, whether on the mother-animal or on the young, the קדושת בכורה is not applicable. כל זמן שיד נכרי באמצע פטורה מן הבכורה (Bechoroth 2b).

V. 14. After the appointment of the Levites to the service of the Sanctuary had been given in general in the preceding verses 5-13, now follows counting them according to their fathers’ houses and their families and fixing the various objects of the Sanctuary to be the charge of each “house”, as well as fixing their position in the camp around the Sanctuary. במדבר סיני: here too, as in Ch. I.1, by this mention of the place, the counting is given its pure significance of having inner relation to the Torah without any semblance of political or economic reference.

V. 15. פקד etc. We have already remarked on Ch. I.2 that the tribe of Levi forms by itself a miniature copy of the whole of Israel in being grouped into branches. Just as the sons of Jacob formed בתי אבות, tribes, and their children family branches, so that the whole nation divided itself into tribes לוי ,שמעון ,ראובן etc. after the sons of Jacob, and these tribes again into families משפחת הפלאי ,משפחת החנכי etc. after the sons of these sons (see Ch. XXVI.5 et seq.), in a similar way the three sons of Levi גרשון קהת ומררי formed the בתי אבות the “tribes” of the Levites, and their sons לבני שמעי etc., the משפחות of the Levites.

מבן חדש ומעלה תפקדם. This counting the Levites from earliest infancy, after living for thirty days (the minimum period taken as showing that a baby is capable of growing up) can be taken to prove that the calling of Levites goes far beyond the service of the Sanctuary which is here declared to be their calling. This, the service and care of the Sanctuary during the encampments and wandering can only be the result of, and a concrete expression of their general calling. For the actual entry into that service they were counted again in Ch. IV and then only from thirty years upward. So that counting them from childhood must have some calling in view beyond this service and especially beyond just that calling which this actual service implies. It must be a calling for which perhaps they are fit for at an earlier age, but which, in any case, must demand the whole of the bringing up and education of youths from earliest childhood onwards. And in fact the tribe of Levi were not to be merely the guardians and watchers over the Abode of the Evidence of the Torah, presented in wood and gold, in purple and byssus, but were to be the defenders and protectors, teachers and advocates of the Torah itself and its observance. Thereby they were to promote the realisation in the life of the people of that which the concrete care of the Tabernacle of the Torah which had been handed over to them was to be the illustration of the common task of the whole nation. See the blessing of Moses to Levi in Deut. 33,9, 10, 11. This general calling of the Levi belongs to the Levite child from the first month, and he must be brought up for it from the beginning of his growth.

But there was besides, apart from the services to the Temple buildings, another service of the Levites in the Temple. And if their services to the Temple is described primarily as a משמרת המשכן, as a משמרת אהרן הכהן as a משמרת כל העדה as being performed in the name of the Sanctuary of the priests and of the whole community, and on V.12 we believed we could say that nevertheless in the very first place it was to be done in the name of God just this service of the Levites in the Temple was one which was to be performed purely and solely in the name of God. Of the service of the Levites in the Temple it says in Deut. XVIII.7 ושרת בשם ה׳ אלקיו, and the explanation given to this in the Gemorra (Arachim 11a) is איזהו שרת שבשם which service is performed in the name of God and with the name of God: הוי אומר זה השירה that is no other than song. Thereby the divinely inspired song with which the Levites had to accompany the קרבנות צבור, the national offerings in the Temple, is regarded in the whole depths of its nature and meaning.
