The divinely inspired psalms of a David, an Asaph, of the sons of Korah which were said by the mouths of the Levites at the offerings were in very truth בשם ה׳ ”שירות״. The singer speaks in the name of God. He says that which God Himself would say to us were He not to use the singers as His instruments and stir the singer’s heart with His Spirit and lay His Word on the singer’s tongue. רוח ה׳ דבר בי ומלתו על לשוני. “the Spirit of God spoke in me, and His Word was on my tongue” said Israel’s greatest champion of song, looking back retrospectively on his life’s work of songs (II Sam. XXIII.2). And it is through the name of God that the singer effects influence, for it is the name “God” (the four-lettered Name with all its meaning and implication I.L.) directed to all men and all human conditions (see Hirsch’s commentary on Psalms I.L.) — To this service of song in the Temple, young Levite boys were allowed to assist. אין הקטן נכנס לעזרה לעבודה אלא בשעה שהלוים אומרים בשיר (Arachim 13b).

V. 22.—26. משפחת הגרשני etc. The Levites fell into three groups, the Gersonides, the Kohathides and the Merarides. The Gersonides encamped to the west. They were placed in charge of the Cherubin-tapestry of the Tabernacle, the covering of goatshair, the ram and tachach skins of the roof, the curtains of the courtyard, and the curtains of the entrances of both the Tabernacle itself and of the courtyard; taken altogether accordingly, the whole of the tent (without the structure I.L.) — the Kohathides encamped to the south. They were placed in charge of the ark, the table, the candelabrum, the altar, the utensils necessary for them, and the dividing curtain. — The Merarides encamped to the north, and they were placed in charge of the boards, bars and bolts, pillars and the feet (the sockets into which the boards fitted I.L.) of the tabernacle as well the pillars and feet of the courtyard and the accessories for both; taken together, the wooden structure of the Temple.

If we consider the parts of the Temple, and the particular point of the compass to which their respective bearers and orderlies were directed, then first of all we must take it that the Temple can be divided into three parts viz: (a) the Abode i.e. the tapestry surround, (b) the appurtenances i.e. the objects which are the real purpose of the Abode, (c) the boards i.e. the firm frame work.

The getting near to God and achieving His Presence and special care by having the מזבח, מנורה, שולחן, ארון and the acts performed on them is represented by the Tabernacle which consisted of tapestry woven in the pattern of cherubim, to which the coverings of the roof as well as the curtains which enclosed the courtyard are added as supplementary parts (see Ex. Ch. XXV, XXVI, XXVII, especially on XXVI,36). The concept of an “Abode” — as we have indeed worked out elsewhere — is concentrated on the extremest side, the one opposite the entrance. One thinks of the dwellers being in the innermost appartment, the farthest away from the entrance, to which the outer roomes lead up to. The hindmost room is the real interior of the house. Hence the expression ירכתי הבית for these innermost rooms (Ps. CXXVIII.3, Amos VI.10). Now as the entrance to the משכן was in the east, the real משכן idea is concentrated in the west, and that is where the קדשי הקדשים was, and hence also שכינה במערב. That is why we see the bearers of the משכן also directed to encamp in the west.

To the right of the bearers of the משכן, in the south, the side of the light, inside the Temple the side representing spiritual life, the bearers of the מנורה ,שולחן ,ארון and the מזבחות have their place. For the objects which are given over to their charge are just those by which our spiritual lives are to be developed under the rays of the Light of the Divine Spirit to attain the richest blossoming. To these the פרכת essentially belongs, the cherubim-curtain which protectingly divides off the ארון from possible degeneration by שולחן and מנורה life, see on Ex. 26,31 (and the chapter referred to above, explaining the meaning of the inaccessibility to the ארון etc. I.L.).

To the left of the bearers of the משכן, the northern aspect, the side that requires Light, the side of midnight awaiting the light, opposite the camp of the מנורה ,שולחן ,ארון, and מזבחות, the bearers of the קרשים the gold-covered cedar boards together with their accessories, had their place. We believed we could recognise (see Exodus again) in these gold covered cedar boards the representation of the tribes of Israel in the Sanctuary, who were to devote their “wood and their gold” i.e. the ever progressive development of their lives and their strength and firmness in what was represented by the wood and the gold of which the ארון, the שולחן the מנורה and the מזבחות were formed, to accept and realise the sermon which these were meant to preach, and from them, under the protection and demands of the cherubim (the bearers of the Glory of God etc., as worked out there I.L.) to receive back ever fresh life and ever fresh strength and energy. The קרשים-bearers, accordingly have their appropriate position in the north, opposite to the מזבחות-מנורה-שולחן-ארון-bearers.

In front of the משכן, to the east, Moses and Aaron and his sons had their appointed place, as being nearest to the entrance of the Sancturay of the Torah, and as being called upon to be the representatives and transmitters of the Torah to the people.

V. 26. ואת מיתריו refers to the משכן, they are, like the court itself, an appendage to the משכן. The cords of the court are reckoned in V.37 as an appendage to the pillars of the court. The hangings of the court were fixed by them — עבדת המשכן :לכל עבדתו is everything that was required for its erection and taking down.
V. 31. והמסך is the פרכת המסך (Ex. XXXIX.34) the curtain that protectingly divides off the ארון.

V. 32. פקודה ,פקדת וגו׳ is a noun, from פקד in the sense of appointing to an office, the authorisation (as in V.20). Eleazar had to appoint and direct all the שמרי משמרת הקדש to their service, hence also to supervise them.

V. 36. ופקדת וגו׳. At the assignment of the objects of the charge to the last division of the Levites, the Merarites, this assignment is again specially called פקודה, probably because they were the last. It wants to obviate the idea that the objects entrusted to their care are merely those that are left over and of no special importance. That is why their duty is specially stressed as being a פקודה. It was no less than the others a special charge entrusted to them, and the objects of their care no less required being appointed to a special office.

V. 38. שומרים משמרת המקדש. The בני קהת (v.20) as the bearers of the real objects of the Sanctuary, and also all the others (v.32) were שומרי משמרת הקדש, for the single objects of the Sanctuary are also a קדש. But the whole Sanctuary is, as a rule, called מקדש ה׳ כוננו ידך .מקדש (Ex. 15,16), ועשו לי מקדש (Ex. 25,8), את מקדש ה׳ טמא (Numb. 19,20). The others are also called שומרי וגו׳, that was their office, the whole content of their being appointed to their calling, more, as they were counted מבן חדש (from a month old), all those that were counted here were not yet שומרים וגו׳ (actual guardians I.L.) but were שומרי משמרת הקדש, the משמרת הקדש was their calling and what they were to be. But for Moses and Aaron this care of the Sanctuary was only one of their activities. They were שומרים משמרת הקדש.

V. 39. נקוד על אהרן שבחמש הפקודים .אשר פקד משה ואהרן, the dots over אהרן are to remind us that שלא היה באותו המנין, that he himself was not included in this count of the Levites (Becharoth 4a). Aaron’s appointment to the priesthood was not, like that of the Levites, only made to take the place of the firstborn. His appointment, and that of his sons, to be כהנים was made at once with the command to make the Sanctuary, before the firstborn had forfeited their position by the event of the golden calf (see Ex. XXVIII.8). Had it not been for that occurrence one can take it that the firstborn would have attained the full position which was given to the Levites. But with the erection of the Sanctuary the service of the offerings was handed over to the Aaronides, in any case for קרבנות צבור and קרבנות חובה (offerings on behalf of the nation and obligatory offerings which had in duty bound to be brought I.L.) which, even בשעת היתר במות (the time when private voluntary offerings were allowed to be brought on altars not in the Sanctuary) had to be brought exclusively in the משכן (see Zebachim 117a). שנים ועשרים אלף, the total sum of all the Levites counted here was twenty-two thousand, three hundred. But these three hundred were, according to Bechoroth 5a, firstborn sons. They are not reckoned in the total mentioned here, as the number here has reference to the substitution of the firstborn by the Levites, the instructions for which follows immediately, and the firstborn of the Levites took no part in that, they only had “to supplant themselves as firstborn, by themselves as Levites”, to perform as Levites the duties they were called on hitherto to perform as firstborn, די לבכור שיפקיע קדושת עצמו (ibid).

V. 40. ויאמר ה׳ וגו׳. The installation of the Levites in the place of the firstborn is now to be definitely expressed by a concrete act, the counting of the firstborn against the counting of the Levites. This counting of the firstborn is only a complementing act of what God had already proclaimed as occurring. It was altogether only of passing importance, all future firstborn are automatically discharged from עבודת המשכן, and are only liable for the פדיון which had been fixed beforehand at the introduction of the קדושת בכור (see Ex. Ch. XIII, v.1 & 11 et seq.). Perhaps this is the reason why the order for this counting is introduced by ויאמר instead of the usual וידבר. It is only an additional explanation of an ordinance which had already been given.

ושא את מספר שמותם. Counting by individual names brought home to each one of them personally the consciousness of the forfeit he had to pay for not fulfilling the mission of the firstborn at the sin of the nation at the golden calf.

V. 41. לי אני ה׳: this is a choice which has been made for ever under the seal of the Name of God. מפשט הסוגיא דבכורות) ,ואת בהמת הלוים וגו׳ ד׳ א׳ ב׳ משמע דלא פטרו בהמת הלוים במדבר אלא פטרי חמורן של ישראל ולא בכור בהמה טהורה שלהן שהיא גופא דבר תמוה שיהא פדיון לקדושת הגוף שאינו בעל מום והלא אפי׳ בכור בעל מום אין לו פדיון וכן פירש״י, הכא בחומש וכן נלע״ד פשט לשונו שם בבכורות, והא דפריך רבא התם אם איתא אפי׳ מבהמה טהורה ניפטרי ופרש״י אם איתא דדרשינן ק״ו גבי בהמה מבכור בהמה טהורה ניפטרי לוים דהא בהמה טהורה דידהו הפקיעה בהמת ישראל. אי לאו דמסתפינא הייתי אומר דה״ק בהמה טהורה דידהו כלומר שה של בן לוי הפקיעה בכורה של בהמת ישראל כלומר פטר חמור של ישראל ואם הפקיע שה של בן לוי בכורה בבהמת ישראל אינו דין שיפקיע בכורה של עצמו שהיא בכור בהמה טהורה. אלא התוספות לא פירשו הכי וס״ל דבהמה טהורה של בן לוי הפקיעה (בכור בהמה טהורה של ישראל במדבר וצע״ג. We have worked out on Ex. XIII.13 that חמור as the beast of burden represents moveable goods, and פטר חמור expresses the idea that all lifeless family possessions belong to God, and redeeming it by a שה given to the כהן illustrates the thought that all lifeless possessions have value and meaning only in their convertibility into living human possibilities of furthering the general purposes of the Sanctuary. According to this, the fact that, at the same moment that the persons of the Levites, now entering the service of the Sanctuary, absolve the firstborn from that duty, their שה also effects the redemption of all the פטרי חמורים of the whole nation, appears as a clear admonition to them. It tells them that it is not only with the spiritual moral side of his personality but also with the means of his existence that a Levite is to know himself in the service of the Sanctuary and its purposes. For, with their entry into the service of the Sanctuary the Levites had to renounce all claim to any participation in the land which was the national means of existence, and were dependent for their existence on that which the nation would have to separate out of their productive possessions for the care and upkeep of His Torah as an expression of fealty to God. And this consciousness that they were in the service of the Sanctuary with the whole of their persons and possessions, with “life and property” was kept alive in the whole tribe of Levi for all future time by their firstborn and their פטרי חמורים no longer requiring redemption כהנים ולוים פטורים אם פטרו את של ישראל במדבר דין הוא שיפטרו את עצמן (Bechoroth 3b). (If the tribe of Levi could free the animals of the whole of Israel in the wilderness, how much more must they be able to free their own from having to be redeemed I.L.) And this law is so sweepingly effected for the whole tribe that even the daughters of a כהן or a לוי who marries a ישראל and has a firstborn son, and that son of course belongs to the tribe of his father and so is not a Levite, nevertheless her womb dispenses the necessity for redemption. And also the פטרי חמור of a כהנת or a לויה do not require redemption in accordance with the principle that כל שישנו בבכור אדם ישנו בבכור בהמה טמאה וכו׳ (ibid 4a).

V. 47.—48. ולקחת. This is the manner and the amount which in Ch. XVIII.16 is fixed in general for the redemption of the firstborn already ordained in Ex. XIII.13. The amount corresponds to the first ערך of a boy after the first month of his life. See Levi. XXVII.6. For each of the other firstborn (apart from the overplus I.L.) a Levite was “given” to the כהן (see V.9) For each of the overplus, the symbolic expression of the imaginary value of a young male child in its relation to the Sanctuary; its ערך, was given to the כהן.

V. 1. In the previous chapter the count was ordered to be made of all those who were destined for the calling of a Levite. This affected all the Levites from a month old and upward. Now follows the counting of all of the Levites who were called upon for active service during the years of wandering, for bearing the Sanctuary, and guarding and caring for it, with more detailed instructions for the particular service of each of the three Levite-houses. This service of lifting and carrying the parts and contents of the Sanctuary demanded an expenditure of strength and was limited to the age of thirty to fifty years. On Ch. II.17 it has already been remarked that even in transit the Sanctuary dismantled into its parts still retained its meaning.
V. 2. נשא וגו׳ מתוך וגו׳. The Kohathides come first for the holiest objects of the Tabernacle have been allocated to their charge in Ch. III.31.
V. 3. כל בא לצבא, see on Ch. I.3.

V. 5. ובא אהרן. The actual objects of the Sanctuary, the ,ארון מזבחות ,מנורה ,שולחן were not allowed to be touched by any but priests, not even Levites. They were accordingly handed over already covered with their travelling covers by the priests to the Levites. Considering the fact already referred to just above that the “Abode of the Evidence” even when dismantled and in transit still retained its holy and sanctifying meaning as the unifying gathering centre of the nation, this covering up and making ready for the further wandering was in itself a priestly act pregnant with meaning. The covers themselves corresponded to the character of that which they covered. The wandering on, not to be kept back by any hindrance was symbolised by the protective exterior covering of all the objects with an עור תחש, the pelt of an “animal of speed”. (Ex. XXVI.14). The מזבח הזהב ,שולחן ,מנורה ,ארון belonging to the קדש הקדשים and the קדש received a cover of תכלת, the colour of godlines and nearness to God (Ex. XXV.3 p.430). In the case of the ארון, which was first wrapped up in the protective and separating cherubim-tapestry which belonged to it, this sky-blue covering was right on the top, the outside visible covering, demonstrating the Ark of the Evidence as כליל תכלת, as in holiness near to God of the highest potency. On the “Table of God’s Care” — which was also covered with a תכלת-covering of holiness — rested the bread of God’s constant care and provision with the conditions for ensuring this care shown by its mode of formation and by its appurtenances for keeping its shape, keeping fresh and pure, straight and upright, devotion to God and brotherliness to fellow man (see Ex. Ch. XXV.23-30). This “bread” of Jewish national well-being was covered with a cloth of תולעת שני, and over the מזבח העולה one of ארגמן. We have explained in Ex. XXV.3 p.430, how, if red in general represents “life”, שני would express the subordinated animal side of life and ארגמן the higher, human side. By covering the showbread with שני but the offering-altar with ארגמן the relative stages of both are indicated. With all the means of existence and well-being granted by God’s “Presence”, (לחם הפנים לפני ה׳ I.L.) only שני, only the animal bodily life is given. ארגמן, the higher, the human stage of life is nothing that is given by God, it has to be won by Man himself, only by free-willed mastering, subordinating and devoting all the animal material side of life to fulfilling the Will of God, just as is represented by the offering-altar with the procedures performed on it, and to which it is dedicated and has its purpose.

ושמו בדיו can not mean here as it does with the other כלים to insert the carrying-poles, as, according to Ex. 25,15 they were never allowed to be taken out of the rings of the Ark, but it must only mean adjust the poles.

V. 7. לחם התמיד עליו יהיה. Although everything that had been מקודש בכלי, had been accepted for the Sactuary by a vessel of the Sanctuary, if taken out of the Sanctuary is considered estranged from it and is פסול יוצא (see on Ex. XXII.30), nevertheless the shewbread on the Table remains in its intimate connection with the Sanctuary even on the wandering and is not נפסל ביוצא (Menachoth 95a).

V. 15. את הקדש designates the ארון עדות as being preeminently the הקדש, the relation to which gives all the others their כלי הקדש .קדושה are the מזבחות ,מנורה ,שולחן whose relations to the ארון are of כלים which serve to accomplish the purpose set by some object.

V. 16. ופקדת וגו׳ ,פקדת וגו׳. According to the formation of this verse, the second half is an explanation of the first. Eleazar’s task is… etc. But this is the charge etc. i.e. — the oil for lighting, the incense of spices, the fealty-offering of the daily offering (this is the offering of flour, the מנחת סולת which had to accompany every תמיד, according to the version of the Yalkut in the Jerusalmic Talmud, Sabbath X.3, it is the חביתי כה״ג, see Levit. VI.13), and the oil for anointing were given into the charge of Eleazar, but thereby he was charged with the whole purpose and mission of the whole Sanctuary namely the קדש) ארון) and the שולחן, the מנורה and the כליו) מזבחות) (cf. V.15) שמן המשחה ,מנחת התמיד ,קטרת הסמים שמן המאור: Enlightenment, completely sublimating oneself in giving satisfaction to God, constant homage with every moment of one’s life, and holiness, these are the purposes which the Ark, the Table, the Candelabrum, and Altars are meant to teach us to strive for. It is not with the mere existence of the objects, the care of which was entrusted to the Kohathides, but only with the carrying out of the messages they preach that the משכן becomes alive and achieves its purpose, and the symbolic representation of this was given over to Eleazar. So that he was really entrusted with the פקדת כל המשכן etc. with what was the whole and final content and meaning of the whole of the Sanctuary and its holy objects.

V. 17. וידבר וגו׳. In the preceding verses the order had been given that the Kohathides were to be given the holy objects they were to carry only after they had their covers put on to avoid their touching those objects directly. Now here it is said that they may not even be present when the covering is done. They are not to “see” the holy objects when they are being covered. Unless we are mistaken, the effect of this prohibition would be that the holy objects remain to their bearers as symbolic objects, subjects for the mind, for thoughts, not so much as actual tangible objects, and so all the more fill their minds with thoughts of their meaning. And this keeping constantly in their minds the true meaning of the holy objects entrusted to them would be an essential factor of their duty to which gazing at their being wrapped up for transit could very well have a disturbing effect.
V. 18. See on Ch. III.15.

V. 20. בלע .כבלע וגו׳, to sink something entirely in another body. Hence to swallow. Hence also similarly to פלא being something which is inaccessible to one’s reasoning insight, בלע is used for something which is inaccessible to one’s actual sight. Thus in Is. III.12. ודרך ארחתיך בלעו.

V. 22. נשא וגו׳. The counting of the Kohathides came first. Although Gershon was the eldest, neverthless, here, where at the same time the handing over of the holy objects of the Sanctuary at the striking of camps was fixed, the Kohathides were considered first, as their task consisted of the holiest objects, the wrapping-up and delivery of which was also done first at the dismantling of the Sanctuary. That was why counting them was commanded with the expression מתוך בני לוי as it involved giving them prominence out of the other Levites. Then, when now the counting of the Gershonides and their instructions follow, it says with reference to that, גם הם to say that indeed by this apparent rejection, no real rejection was intended. Perhaps that is also why it says here לבית אבתם למשפחתם as it does for the whole tribe of Levi in Ch. III.15, whereas otherwise it runs למשפחתם לבית אבתם. It stresses that the Gershonides formed a “house”, a branch of the tribe no less than the others: מה שאמר :מ״ר הכתוב גם הם שלא תאמר שלכך מנה בני גרשון שניים שהם פחותים מבני קהת לאו אלא כתב גם הם שאף בני גרשון כיוצא בהם של בני קהת אלא שהקדימם הכתוב כאן בשביל כבוד התורה לפי שקהת הי׳ מטועני הארון ובו׳.

V. 26. ואת כל אשר וגו׳. Everything which had to do with the care and transport of the parts of the Sanctuary which was entrusted to them, they had to see to. מ״ר) כל מה שהי׳ נעשה לכל הכלים יהיו בני גרשון עושים).

V. 27. את כל משאם :ופקדתם עליהם במשמרת וגו׳. Everything which they receive to carry, they are not to accept as mere mechanical porters but a demand is made to their intelligence and their consciousness; it is an office which is to be carried out with conscious care of a warden. מ״ר) שיהיו מצווים עליהם שיהיו שומרים על כל מה שנושאים).
V. 28. ושמרתם, The first direction for their charge was given by Aaron and his sons (v.27) but after that they were under Ithamar (מ״ר).

V. 32. ובשמת תפקדו את כלי משמרת משאם. The objects entrusted to the Merarides were also of symbolic meaning (see on Ch. 2,17 et. seq..), things which had to be kept with consciousness of their meaning. They therefore were to be handed over “by name” (explicitly mentioning what they were I.L.).

V. 47. עבדת עבדה ועבדת משא. By עבודת עבודה, the Gemora in Arachin 11a understands the accompaniment of the Levites’ song to the offerings. איזהו עבודה שצריכה עבודה הוי אומר זו שירה. It is a service, an עבודה which only occurs as an accompaniment to another עבודה. Then the name of עבודה for the offering-procedure, which otherwise is missing from the תורה (see on Ex. II.25) would be found here, and the accompanying song is regarded as an assistance to that procedure, as furthering the purpose for which offerings are to be brought. The complete submission, and indeed not the passive submission of endurance, but the positive active submission to the Will of God, cheerfully entering His service by performing the deeds of God’s purposes on earth, that is the meaning of offerings in the concept of עבודה. Its beatitude finds its highest expression in the נסבים, by which we symbolise the cup of joy of our feelings overflowing down into the base of the altar of the Torah. The human brain can conceive no higher beatitude than the thought of a life lived faithfully in the service of God. And, inspired by this happy, happiness-bringing thought, the Temple-Songs flow out. It clothes in words the thoughts and feelings which the offering-procedure symbolises in acts. שירה accordingly is עבודת עבודה.
V. 49. ופקדיו. His counted ones, at God’s command, counted for God.

V. 1. In the previous chapters I—IV the people were counted as עדה, in their common union of the Torah, directed to separate camps at some distance round about the Sanctuary of the Torah, with it as their common centre point; and in the immediate surround of it, the Levites were posted as being chosen for service to it. This arrangement of the people — God’s Sanctuary of the Torah as centre-point, round about it, its guardian and representative, the camp of the Levites, and round about them in a larger circumference, the camp of the people — expressed unequivocally the nature and calling of this nation. The Torah is its soul, its hold and its bond, the Torah of God, Who did not want to establish a temple with it or a church-going congregation, but Who wanted to establish a nation with it, a community that was to build up its whole social life on God’s Torah and through its laws, on God, Who had set the fulfilling of His Torah as the condition for His Presence in the nation. The Levites, as guardians, bearers, representatives, promoters of the fulfilling of this Torah, are separated from the people and picked out from the people themselves, and “given” to the Sanctuary of this Torah for the nation to be always wedded through them to the spirit of this Torah.

Now laws follow here which express in concrete working, this organised division into sections and arrangement of the nation around the Sanctuary of the Torah. First שלוח מחנה (expulsion from the camp I.L.).

V. 2.—3. צו וגו׳. As the simple speech of God expressing His Will in the words דבר אל בני ישראל already involves a command, a מצוה for Israel, those commands which are introduced with the special צו את בני ישראל are stressed with special seriousness for their being carried out with the utmost conscientiousness. According to the expression of the sages in ספרי it is always a זירוז מיד ולדורות, a demand for zealous attention immediately and for all future time which is specially to be applied to such laws which involve material sacrifice חסרון כיס (see on Ex. XXVII.20) (sacrificing material wealth for spiritual ends).

צו את בני ישראל. The previous commands to organise the counting, division into sections and grouping of the nation were directed to Moses, Aaron and the princes of the people. The consequences of this grouping which follow here are directed to every individual of the people, and expect their being observed and carried out by everyone.

וישלחו מן המחנה. The טומאה of the צרוע (the so-called leper I.L.) is ordained in Levit. Ch. XIII, and already there in V.46 says כל ימי אשר הנגע בו יטמא טמא הוא בדד ישב מחוץ למחנה מושבו that during the whole of the time that the טומאה-condition is definite, the person affected must remain outside the camp. The טומאה of the זב is also discussed there in Ch. XV and includes all the various conditions of טומאה mentioned there and in Ch. XII.2 viz. זב וזבה נדה ויולדת ובעל קרי (see מל״מ on הל׳ ביאת המקדש III.3), and of this latter it also says in Deut. XXIII.11 ויצא אל מחוץ למחנה טמא לנפש .לא יבא אל תוך המחנה is one who has become טמא by having come into contact with a human corpse. This טומאה is discussed at length in Ch. XIX of this book. It is mentioned already in Levit. V.3 in connection with all the other “טומאות-by-touch” discussed fully here in Ch.XI, such as מגע שרץ ונבלה, and already there, the prohibition of all those who become a טמא by “touch” from entering the precincts of the Sanctuary and from touching sanctified objects is presumed, as indeed the general duty of keeping away from the Sanctuary when in any state of טומאה is expressed in Levit. XV.31 in the sentence: והזרתם את בני ישראל מטמאתם ולא ימותו בטמאתם בטמאם את משכני אשר בתוכם (refer to our notes there). This duty is now gone into more in detail here. The three categories of טומאה mentioned here, זב ,מצורע and טמא מת are not all the same in degree or extent of their effect. מצורע is stricter than זב inasmuch as it is מטמא בביאה (that it conveys טומאה by the mere entry into a house which has been declared “leprous” I.L.); זב is stricter in one aspect than טמא מת as it is מטמא משכב ומושב and even תחת אבן מסמא (see on Levit. 15,4) and the Halacha teaches (Sifri and Pessachim 68a) that regarding the enforced withdrawal from the camp ordered here they are also not alike. As already remarked on V.1 and as is evident from the arrangement of the camp ordered in the preceding chapters, the national circle falls into three spheres. There is the centre point, the sphere of the Sanctuary of God, the מחנה שכינה; the immediately surrounding camp of the Levites, the מחנה לויה, and then the camp of the people; the מחנה ישראל Corresponding to these, later on in the City of God the Temple there was the מחנה שכינה, extending from the עזרת ישראל inwards; the מחנה לויה from the הר הבית to the עזרת ישראל (which began at the Nickanor Gate): and the מחנה ישראל, the whole of the rest of the city up to the הר הבית. The מצורע, the gravest of the three categories of טמאה is משתלח חוץ לשלש מחנות banned from all three spheres, has to keep out of even מחנה ישראל; the second category, זב, וזבה, נדה, ויולדת ובעל קרי all טומאה היוצאת עליו מגופו, states brought about by bodily conditions are משתלח חוץ לשתי מחנות are banned from two spheres: the מחנה שכינה ומחנה לויה, but may remain in מחנה ישראל; the third category, טמא מת and so also מגע שרץ ונבלה, altogether all טומאות מגע are only banned from מחנה שכינה but may stay in the two other מחנות.

Now we think that the first sentence in the text: ושלח מן המחנה כל צרוע וכל זב וכל טמא לנפש refers specially to the מחנה שכינה in which none of the three categories, not even טמא מת may remain. The second מזכר עד נקבה תשלחו would refer specially to מחנה לויה out of which זב וזבה etc. have to be sent, those טומאות which differ in the sexes and hence the addition מזכר עד נקבה (see Nidda 28b, מזכר ועד נקבה תשלחו זכר ודאי נקבה ודאית וכו׳ וכו׳ אי הכי כי אטמי בשאר טומאות לא לישלחי אמר קרא מזכר הפורשת מן הזכר ע״ש ברש״י). Finally, the third sentence, אל מחוץ למחנה תשלחום would then speak specifically of מצורע who has to keep right out of the camp, even out of מחנה ישראל. And then it concludes referring to all three, ולא יטמאו את מחניהם, with מחנה in the plural. Each one of them by the prescribed exclusion from the special camp which is characterised for his special condition, shall not desecrate it, אשד אני שוכן בתוכם, I am present in all three of them, in מחנה ישראל and מחנה לויה as much as in מחנה שכינה and before My Presence the designated טמאים have to forsake the various camps.

Now if we compare the meanings of these three classes of טומאה they correspond most strikingly to the different spheres out of which they are to be banned. In Levit. Ch. XIII & XIV we found that the נגעי צרעת with all their associated laws resulted from the Finger of God pointing to sins of social defection. It is social purity which the separation of the מצורע is to bring about and so it is understandable that he has to withdrew also from the זב וזבה .מחנה ישראל stand on the basis of sexual purity which is to be kept (see Ch. XV ibid). But sexual purity, purity in sexual life, is the very first demand on all those who are to live spiritually high lives, near unto God. In the Jewish point of view high spirituality, great intellectuality is no licence for moral lapses. On the contrary, the higher the spiritual gifts and spiritual profession the more serious and the more comprehensive are the demands for moral purity. Our poets, our singers, our men of clear-sighted knowledge and of instructive and stirring speech are not to give their minds up to lofty matters and their bodies to lustful sensuality. We are told that where ערוה stays, God and the Divine departs, ולא יראה בך ערות דבר ושב מאחריך (Deut. XXIII.15) מלמד שהעריות מסלקות (ספרי) את השכינה. Jewish אורים were always paired with תומים, and יחוס, sexual purity, must have surrounded already the cradle in which the priests and the singers of the choir of our Sanctuary are born (see Arachim 11a). That is the spirit that has to create the atmosphere of the מחנה לויה and that is what is represented by שלוח זב וכו׳ ממחנה לויה. In Leviticus we have repeatedly had to touch on the contrast which טומאת מת makes to the teachings of the Jewish thoughts of God which belong to the Torah and its Sanctuary. To the heathen thought, death and a dead body are signs of homage to its god. They reveal the power to which proud Man has to submit, and this power, the irresistable power of the forces of nature is the heathen’s god. But Jewish Truth teaches אין במות זכרך בשאול מי יודה לך. Not Death and the grave is the signature of God, they are not the homage we give to God. The power which lays Man low in death does come from God as does the subjection to which god-like Man has to submit in life, but לא תעזוב נפשי לשאול “Thou doest not leave my soul, my true self, to the grave”, it is only the outward casing that He leaves to the grave, which itself being earthly finds its home there. But the Man himself, who even in life is near to God with the divine-freedom of his moral powers which God has given him, in death flies back to Him with his wings unchained. Not the dead man, the living one, freely mastering the earthly part of his being with his free-willed moral power in god-like disposition of his life, is a revelation of and homage to God. For this power of himself disposing the mode of his life, which is the real nucleus of his personality, is itself a spark of the Spirit of God, is itself a breath of the Almighty free nature of God, and in every moment of free-willed active performance of duty is a natural fruit of the divine nature of a human being. Not the dead body, חי חי הוא יודך does Jewish teaching jubilate, the living man is the revelation and homage of the אלקים חיים, and banns death, and dead bodies טמא מת and the related מגע שרץ ונבלה (see Levit. on XI,47 et seq.) altogether everything which makes people טמא by external touching, out of the sphere of the Sanctuary of God. משתלח חוץ למחנה שכינה.

V. 5. וידבר. Now three laws follow, viz. סוטה ,גזל הגר, and נזיר. They, as we shall see, are in intimate relationship to the three national spheres discussed above: שכינה ,לויה ,ישראל and to the זב ,צרוע and טמא מת who had to be sent out of them. That which שלוח מחנה out of the three camps taught symbolically is brought into the reality of actual life by the laws concerning סוטה ,גזל הגר and גזל הגר .נזיר is parallel to שלוח מצורע ממחנה ישראל and shows the Presence of God in the social intercourse of the people, סוטה parallel to שלוח זב ממחנה לויה and shows the Presence of God in sexual family life, נזיר is parallel to שלוח טמא מת ממחנה שכינה and shows the Presence of God in the individual life of human beings striving upward to moral freedom.
First פרשת גזל הגר:

V. 6. דבר אל בני וגו׳. The principle points of this law have already been given in Levit. V.20 et seq. It is the אשם גזלה. There the law is proclaimed, that if somebody has denied a debt, however it may have been incurred, and has denied it on oath whether in court or out of court, he has to pay קרן (the full amount) and חומש (plus a quarter of the amount) to the person entitled to demand the repayment of the debt, and moreover has to bring an אשם offering. We have already fully discussed this law there and would refer to there. Here this law is repeated primarily to complement it in two ways. Firstly that (v.7) חומש and אשם are to be imposed only following his own admission of his crime, but if his false oath has been established only by the conviction of witnesses then he has simply to pay the קרן (the capital sum) but, on the other hand the לא ינקה ה׳ (Ex. XX.7) rests on him in the full weight of its seriousness (see on Levit. V.8). Secondly, that if the one who is entitled to repayment has died without legal heirs the debtor who has sworn falsely has to pay the קרן and the חומש to the כהנים.

מכל חטאת האדם. Just as עון הקדשים (Ex. XXVIII.38), עון מקדש (Numb. XVIII.1) designates a sin against holy things and against the Sanctuary, so here too חטאת האדם could mean sin against other human beings; but more probably it is the ordinary genetive, “sins of men” and is referring to the quite similar case introduced in detail in Leviticus. From what follows it is evident, clearly enough, that here too it is dealing with the denial of an unpaid debt, accordingly with a sin against the right of possession of one’s fellow-man. למעל מעל בה׳ every such sin against one’s fellow-man is immediately an act of treachery towards God, Who is the guarantor and pledge in transactions between man and man. But this is raised to a higher degree when he has taken an oath, calling on God to witness the truth of his statement. If then he has misused this call to support an untrue dishonest statement, the oath makes the debt he owes to his fellow-man to something he owes to God, it raises it to a holy object by appealing to his “nearness to God” he invests himself in the garment of a priest, and treachery practised in such a manner towards his fellow-man becomes מעילה (see on Levit. V.15, 20 et seq.) There it used a similar expression. נפש כי תחטא ומעלה וגו׳ and there the sin is explained in detail as ובחש בעמיתו בפקדון etc. etc. מבל אשר ישבע עליו לשקר etc. — ואשמה הנפש ההיא, by such enrichment of his own possessions through a false oath he has laden himself with the guilt that brings desolation in its wake (see Levit. V.6 20 et seq.).

V. 7. איש או אשה: thereby the great far-reaching principle in law is given. השוה הכתוב אשה לאיש לכל עונשין שבתורה that the Torah holds men and women in equal responsibility for all transgressions against the law (Baba Kama 15a, Pesachim 43a & b).

והתודו. See on Levit. V.5. This is the first fresh factor which complements the presentation of this law already given in Leviticus. Not only the אשם, which, like every other offering of promise of betterment presupposes confession (see Levit. V.5), but the duty to pay an additional חומש only applies when the repayment is made as the result of the guilty party having confessed his guilt, but not if it is the result of a legal conviction brought about by the evidence of witnesses. In that case he is only condemned to repay the actual loan. It is his confession, whether quite spontaneous or after the declaration of witnesses, which necessitates חומש and אשם (Baba Kama 108a & b)

ממון המשתלם בראש מוסיף חומש ממון שאין :והשיב את אשמו בראשו וגו׳ משתלם בראש אין מוסיף חומש (Baba Kama 65b). Only in cases where the simple capital would have to be paid if convicted by the court does חומש have to be added if the restoration is the result of confession but if the nature of the case is such that the court would impose payment of double the amount כפל, as in cases of גנבה (theft) or טוען טענת גנב (falsely pleading theft) — see Ex. XXII.6 — then even after confession חומש is not to be paid but only כפל and אשם is incurred. More, כפל excludes חומש to such an extent, that the object of a claim which has already been adjudged to be paid in double can not have חומש imposed even if an oath has been made concerning it which has no reference at all to the כפל-question, e.g. טוען טענת גנב ונשבע וחזר וטען טענת אבד ונשבע ובאו עדים אקמייתא והודה אבתרייתא (he had pleaded that it had been stolen and taken an oath to that effect, then he put in another plea that he had lost it, and witnesses came and gave evidence that he had sworn falsely on the first plea, which entailed the imposition by the court of double payment, and then he confessed that his second oath was false, and on this confession he should add the חומש, he still does not have to pay this חומש I.L.) because, as it says there ממון המחייבתו כפל פטרתו מן החומש (ibid 108a).

ונתן לאשר אשם לו: according to ר׳ נתן (Gittin 37a) eventually even to one who is only indirectly involved in loss through his dishonesty נושה בחברו מנה וחברו בחברו גובין מזה ונותנין לזה, if his creditor, on the strength of a legally recoverable debt, borrowed an equal sum from a third party, the original debtor has to pay directly to this third party.

V. 8. גואל :ואם אין לאיש גואל is the nearest relation who is entitled to inherit (cf. Levit. XXV.25). The Torah omits to mention the selfevident case that when the one who is entitled to demand has died the debt must be paid to his heirs. This passing over in silence to the case of one who dies without any heirs is the more explicable in view of the explanation given by ר׳ נתן to the immediately preceding verse ונתן לאשר אשם לו. For, according to that, it has already been said there that the payment need not necessarily be made to the original person who was entitled to demand it but also to one who has a legal claim to his property, e.g. one of his creditors. His heirs would be included even more as being the natural claimants to his property, so that it goes straight on from the previous verse to the case ואם אין לאיש גואל, if the one who has right to claim dies without heirs. But according to Jewish law this can only arise at a גר (a proselyte I.L.) who dies leaving no children. With everybody else, in such a case, there is always a relation, however distant ascending or descending the family tree, who is entitled to inherit. But a גר enters a new existence at the moment of his conversion, is considered as newly born, גר שנתגייר כקטן שנולד דמי and so can only have heirs from children begotten by him after his conversion. If he dies without having had such children he has no legal heirs and any outstanding debts owing to him have no legal creditors. As ownerless property they would belong to the first person who takes them into his possession, in this case, the debtor. But if this debtor, as in our case here, has falsely sworn, during the life of the גר, that the latter’s claim is a false one, then the order is given here — and this is the second complementing factor to the laws already given in Levit. — that האשם המושב לה׳ לכהן, even if the creditor who has been defrauded out of his property by a false oath dies without leaving anybody entitled to claim his property, as soon as the false oath has been confessed, the property concerned becomes “holy property belonging to God”, and is handed over by God to the קנאו ה׳ ונתנו לכהן שבאותו משמר ,כהן (B.K. 109b). It has to be returned to God. When he swore he not only denied his fellow-man but also God, and by his confession gives Him His due. He has to pay both קרן and האשם זה קרן המושב זה חומש :חומש (ibid 110a), the offering is specially mentioned, מלבד איל וגוי. The קרן to be given back is itself called אשם and חומש is indicated by the המושב לה׳ which is just what marks the property as one which has become sanctifed to God by the oath taken in His Name. But by calling the property which has to be restored to God by the name אשם it is stamped with the character of an offering and must be done only in the daytime, can not be paid in instalments, each member of the division of priests on duty at the time must receive an equal part of it, and they can not come to any mutual arrangement of exchange at such distribution, all exactly as if it was an אשם-offering מה אשם אין חולקין אשם כנגד אשם אף גזל אין חולקין גזל הגר כנגד גזל הגר (ibid.).

מלבד איל הכפורים אשר יכפר בו עליו. The offering may not be brought until the money has been repaid, and both, the money and the offering belong together, and both go to the same division of priests who are functioning in the Temple (משמר see Levit. VI.19).

V. 9. וכל תרומה וגו׳. This and the following verse are attached to the preceding only as an opportune remark on the general disposition of the gifts which are directed to the priests. It says in the preceding verse: המושב לה׳ לכהן, that what is to be given back to God is to be given to the priest, and to that the remark is added וכל תרומה etc. תרומה is literally: that which is lifted up out of something to God and so designates in general everything which is dedicated to God. Hence, here, the unusual term הקרבה otherwise only used in connection with offerings is used: אשר יקריבו לכהן One brings it to the priest inasmuch as one really wants to “bring it near” to God. Now it says that all such תרומה which one brings to a priest as הקרבה is to become that priest’s own property, it has been transferred to him by God. It is just that which was just said regarding קנהו השם ונתנו לכהן :גזל הגר, or, as it generally says of the holy things which are given to the priests: כהנים משלחן גבוה קא זכו. Thus in ספרי too it deduces from this verse that בכורים regarding the disposition of which nothing is said in Deut. Ch. XXVI, that they are to be given to the priests.

V. 10. ואיש את קדשיו לו יהיו וגו׳. According to the grammatical formation these are two sentences. ואיש את קדשיו. But every man has his own holy things! i.e. every man has the right of disposition of his holy things, לו יהיו, although dedicated to God and from Him transferred to the priests, they are still to a certain extent his, inasmuch as איש אשר יתן לכהן לו יהיה, that only that belongs to the priest which somebody gives him. No priest has any direct claim to any of the holy things which are directed to be given to the priesthood in general. Every one who is in duty bound to give can give to any particular priest he pleases. No priest can demand it from him. This right of disposal of his holy things is called טובת הנאה. Thus the ספרי explains our verse: ואיש את קדשיו לו יהיו למה נאמר לפי שהוא אומר כל תרומת הקדשים אשר ירימו בני ישראל שומע אני יטלום בזרוע ת״ל ואיש את קדשיו לו יהיו מגיד שטובת הנאת קדשים לבעליהם.

If we consider the fresh factors which are given here in פרשת גזל הגר, viz. that self-confession is necessary for the imposition of חומש and ,אשם והתודו, and that if there is no person living who is entitled to receive the debt, that which has been denied with a false oath has to be repaid to God, then clearly both are factors by which the Presence of God in transactions between man and man, in other words the sanctity of the camp of the people, קדושת מחנה ישראל, is demonstrated in its practical application with practical results. The wording of an oath, placing all one’s worldly possessions under the judgement of God as evidence of the honesty of any special transaction in ordinary human intercourse already assumes the presence of God at every word spoken and every deed done in ordinary daily life, and uses and places God’s seeing and His Power as the power Whose office of Judge begins where the short-sightedness and lack of power of human justice ends. And now when self-confession shows this power of God showing itself present within Man’s own mind in that Voice of God which we call “conscience”, with which God “illuminates and investigates even the most secret innermost chambers of our minds” (Prov. 20,27), and when, by calling God into the matter, the wealth which he owes but has denied has become one of God’s holy things which then, like all holy things, has to be returned to Him with the additional “fifth” even if the person to whom it was due had died and left no legal heirs, then the whole law appears as the fullest proclamation and glorification of the sanctifying Presence of God in the ordinary social life of the People.

The antagonism between כפל and חומש, which, as remarked on V.7, ממון המחייבו כפל פוטרו מן החומש, can not make both of them be imposed on the same claim, is easily understandable according to this. For כפל, as worked out on Ex. 21,37, is the expression of acknowledgment of the universal presence of human justice and honesty in social life to which the owner had entrusted his property, and which the thief had misused and scorned: Whereas חומש is to represent the ever-present justice of God, and just in such cases where, as when an oath is imposed, human justice fails to reach. Which is also just why חומש necessitates previous self-confession, while קנס is not imposed in cases of confession. קנס is, accordingly, a specific attribute of the effectiveness of human justice. So that if a claim has already successfully provoked this reaction, as is apparent when קנס is imposed, it automatically excludes חומש.
פרשת גזל הגר is nothing but the actual practical consequence of that which שלוח מצורע מן מחנה ישראל is symbolic of, is the practical application in social life of the underlying principle of it.
V. 11. Thereupon follows פרשת סוטה, the teaching of the Presence of God in sexual family life, parallel to שלוח זב וזבה ממחנה לויה.

V. 12. שטה :איש איש כי תשטה אשתו, to deviate from a direction on the way, שטה מעליה (Prov. IV.15), thus here: to turn aside from the prescribed moral road. Thus also in Chaldean שטה: to deviate from the right mental way: insanity, Hence taking both together, the saying of our sages: אין אדם עובר עבירה אא״כ נכנס בו רוח שטות (Sota 3a) every moral lapse is at the same time a mental one, moral truth and logical truth coincide, and no man sins unless he has first lost the true conception of things. — ומעלה בו מעל, just as in the preceding פרשה the term למעל מעל בה׳ is used to show that the social relationship of man is at the same time something which is sacred to God, so here, too, the conjugal relationship of man to wife is marked by the term מעילה as something sacred to God. Hence in the following verse and further on, the woman having degraded herself to the extent of preventing the marriage to be allowed to continue is described by the term והיא נטמאה. Marriage is a קדש, the corresponding moral relationship in conjugal faithfulness is called טהרה (V.28), the opposite is called טומאה, and when the wife has become אסורה (forbidden I.L.) for the husband to carry on the marriage this is called נטמאה just as the טומאה condition in general means the exclusion from מקדש and קדשים (the Sanctuary and holy things I.L.). The behaviour of the wife described here in this verse does not yet imply actual adultery, but it does describe in any case already a blameworthy deviation from the real path of propriety of conduct and established usage of Jewish married women which had given the husband just cause to warn her (v.14).

V. 13. ושכב וגו׳. As this verse concludes with the clause והיא לא נתפשה, what had occurred had not happened by force, against her will, so that it could not be a case of אונס which would excuse her, this case must be one of her proven guilt, which immediately forbids the legal continuance of the marriage and not one of doubt to be placed under the Divine decision. The Halacha takes this clause והיא וגו׳ to express איסור so definitely that whenever it quotes it it at once adds the explanatory word ,אסורה והיא לא נתפשה אסורה. To the limiting pronoun והיא it attaches the law that, though in general תפישה, i.e. אונס (the woman being forced against her will I.L.) does not prevent the continuance of the marriage, with an אשת כהן (the wife of a priest) even in such a case the marriage may not continue והיא לא נתפשה אסורה הא נתפשה מותרת ויש לך אחרת שאף על פי שנתפשה אסורה ואיזו זו אשת כהן (Kethuvoth 51b et seq.). And in fact it assumes it to be a case of complete adultery, ושכב איש וגו׳, but that it is not proved. ונעלם וגו׳, what is proved, is only ונסתרה, that she had been found בסתר secreted with a man in such a manner that והיא נטמאה could have been possible, and moreover the man was one with whom her immodest behaviour described in v.12 had given her husband cause to warn her. This ונסתרה (her having been found in the manner mentioned above I.L.), as well as her having been warned against him (see next verse) must be proved — as every relevant fact in civil or criminal law דבר שבממון and דבר שבערוה must be — by two witnesses (Sota 2a, 31a & b). But then ועד אין בה, no complete testimony is required against her. Even if there are no two witnesses of her real adultery, but only one witness testifies to that, then it is only a question of לא נתפשה (that she had not been forced I.L.) but if she has not got this excuse of אונס then without anything further she is אסורה לבעלה (the marriage may not be continued I.L.) This decision of the law that a single witness in this case is sufficient is explained (ibid. 3a) רגלים לדבר, that the fact to which the one witness testifies has been already indicated as being probable by the preceding complete testimony of two witnesses of the קנוי and the מפני מה האמינה תורה עד אחד בסוטה שרגלים לדבר ,סתירה שהרי קינא לה ונסתרה ועד אחד מעידה שהיא טמאה (ibid). But this testimony of one witness although supported by רגלים לדבר only effects the marriage being broken up but in no wise has any effect in the criminal-law aspect of the matter.

V. 14. ועבר עליו רוח קנאה. We have already remarked in Ex. on Ch. XX.5 the relationship of קנא to קנה to acquire something for one’s own, and explained that קנא means to make one’s right to something valid, to demand something as rightfully belonging to you, hence -קנא ב: to lay claim to something in somebody else’s possession as really pertaining to you, to envy somebody about something. So that קנא את אשתו means to assert his demands on his wife, to demand her as belonging to him, to remind her of the rights to her person which he possesses as her husband, and to warn her against violating them. Thus Sota 3a אין קנוי אלא לשון התראה, and (ibid. 5b) כיצד מקנא לה אמר לה בפני שנים אל תסתרי עם פלוני (what does קנא imply here? that he says to his wife in the presence of two witnesses “do not be alone in a closed room with that man I.L.). So that רוח קנאה is the feeling that he fears that his conjugal rights have been, or may become infringed. It is the suspicion of unfaithfulness. Of this רוח קנאה it says ועבר עליו, it has come over him “from without”, it is not just an inner feeling, no mere morbid imagining. His suspicions were forced on him by the immodest or at least unseemly behaviour in v.12 וקנא את אשתו and he had warned his wife against forgetting her wifely duties. With this ועבר עליו a fresh eventuality is introduced. And this fresh case does not lie in the ועבר עליו וגו׳ ,וקנא וגו׳. For the Halacha teaches (Sota 3a) that already in the previous verse, the case where the decision is made on the evidence of a single witness, וקנא, i.e. warning in the presence of two witnesses, must have first taken place. For it is just this warning and the סתירה which followed in spite of it which together form the factors of probability, the רגלים לדבר which makes the evidence of the single witness having some effect. The factor which comes to be discussed now in this case is that there is no witness at all of טומאה (actual adultery) so that after the previous קנוי and סתירה it is completely doubtful whether נטמאה or לא נטמאה (adultery had or had not taken place). This doubt is just what is expressed here in this verse by placing the two possibilities in juxtaposition: the woman had aroused his suspicion by unseemly behaviour, he had warned her against סתירה, against being alone with the man behind closed doors, she had ignored the warning ונסתרה ונטמאה and had also committed adultery; or the woman had aroused his suspicions by her unseemly behaviour, he had warned her against סתירה she had ignored the warning ונסתרה, but nevertheless לא נטמאה, had not committed adultery. The two verses 13 and 14 mutually complement each other. The ונסתרה of v.13 assumes the warping, קנוי, mentioned in v.14, because only a warning testified to by two witnesses, followed by evidence, equally testified by two witnesses that the warning had been disregarded, constitute sufficient רגלים לדבר, sufficient circumstantial evidence for the testimony of the single witness to have any effect. And similarly the קנוי, the warning spoken of in v.14 has to be complemented by the סתירה, its being disregarded, of v.13, as a simple warning without evidence of its having been ignored does not justify such a doubt of continued טהרה on the part of the wife that the continuance of the marriage must be made dependent on a Divine decision.

The law in short is as follows: — If the warning having been given and also its having been disregarded is confirmed by two witnesses, קנוי וסתירה על פי ב׳ עדים, then a single witness testifying that adultery took place is sufficient to make her אסורה לבעלה (the marriage must be dissolved I.L.) If there is no witness of adultery, the evidence of the other witnesses causes the marriage to be kept in abeyance until, by the procedure described in the following verses, the unbroken innocence of the wife has been established by Divine decision.

Our verse accordingly tells us that as long as it is doubtful whether the סתירה resulted in נטמאה or not the wife is אסורה לבעלה. In Sota 28, a.b. the state of טומאה resulting even in a case of ספק, doubt, expressed here for concrete actual sexsual cases is transferred to cases of doubt in cases of symbolic טומאה and the far-reaching Halacha is laid down for ה׳ טומאה that דבר שיש בו דעת לישאל ברשות היחיד ספקו טמא, ברשות הרבים ספקו טהור, ושאין בו דעת לישאל בין ברשות היחיד בין ברשות הרבים ספקו טהור. We have already fully explained this Halacha derived from Sota on Leviti. 7,19-20, and here we would only remark that this equal treatment of the two kinds of טומאות, the moral sexual one and the symbolic can be taken as an important indication of the identical idea of them both. It stresses the thought that just as the conception of טומאה and טהרה for the demands of the moral purity of marriage presents the institution of marriage as a מקדש, a Sanctuary, in the same way by transferring the same methods of judging mental purity in the הל׳ טומאה allows us to look on these latter as the symbolic representation of our building up our moral purity on the basis of our free will in moral matters.

V. 15. והביא האיש. As remarked in the previous verses, as soon as there is a doubt whether טומאה, actual adultery, has followed proven קנוי and סתירה (warning and being shut in together) the wife is אסורה לבעלה (may not live conjugally with her husband) until the question of the continuance of the marriage has been decided by placing the doubt for the decision of God by the procedure which is now described. But this placing the decision in the Hands of God is entirely dependent on the complete willingness of both the husband and wife. The husband can prefer to have the marriage concluded, or the wife, without admitting any guilt, can prefer divorce to continuing the marriage after her innocence has been proved, or simply does not wish to undergo the test. Neither the husband nor the wife can be forced to have the test made (Sota 6a). Also if the husband dies in the meantime, so that the immediate object, the continuance of the marriage, is no longer there, the test is not made (Kethuvoth 81a). Moreover, the whole procedure prescribed here for a woman whose faithfulness is in doubt can only be carried out by the highest court, the ב״ד הגדול בירושלים (Sota 7b) so that the husband has to bring his wife to Jerusalem.

והביא אח קרבנה עליה. All offerings which a wife has to bring must be brought by the husband (Nedarim 35b) and this expresses the whole intimate unity which exists in marriage between the parties before God. Also as here the husband brings the offering for his wife he makes it clear that it is his desire for the marriage to continue if only God decides favourably. But this offering consists of עשירית האיפה קמה שערים, not סלת, not חטים but קמח unsieved, the coarsest sort of flour, and שערים, barley, the commonest kind of grain, usually used only for animals’ fodder, מאכל בהמה. It is a question here of simple existence, to be or not to be, and indeed, as it is the man who brings the Mincha of the wife, the existence or non-existence of the marriage. Really in every Mincha, a person lays the means of his nourishment, the means of the continuance of his existence, acknowledgingly at the feet of God. According to Sota 14, a שעורים, as מאכל בהמה also expresses doubt as to her moral worth as a human being, כשם שמעשיה מעשה בהמה כך קרבנה מאכל בהמה a character which she deserves in any case, for, even if her guilt had not reached the stage of actual טומאה, she had in any case left the pure path of decent womanhood (v.12, 14). לא יצק עליו שמן ולא יתן עליו לבנה, no sign of well-being and no sign of satisfaction is it to bear, כי מנחת קנאות הוא מנחת זכרון מזכרת עון, for the seriousness of the doubt which the Mincha serves to express and which it is to bring to a decision excludes שמן and לבנה. The two sides of the doubt out of which the Mincha is brought are here described by the two terms מנחת קנאות and קנאות .מנחת זכרון: the husband wishes to vindicate his wife, he wants her to remain his if she still is his, the fact that he leads her for a decision before God, itself shows that. Had he wished the marriage to cease he would not have required that, she is אסור to him, he is seeking היתר from God. On the other hand it is מנחת זכרון מזכרת עון. We have already worked out on Levit. II.2 that the concept אזכרה ,זכר forms an essential part of the meaning of a Mincha. In a Mincha, the existence of a person, and joined with שמן and לבנה his well-being and his satisfaction is understood as being an object of the Divine provision, and God’s remembering to send His blessing on these things prayed for. But here the מנחת זכרון becomes a מזכרת עון. He to Whom all things are known is to decide whether the marriage is to continue in accordance with His knowledge of the degree of the guilt of the wife, and if she is really guilty to the extreme He is to inflict punishment. This is the other side of the doubt. There it is no question of granting well-being and satisfaction, it is the grave fundamental question as to whether the very existence or not of the further married life is to continue which is to be laid for decision at the feet of God. Hence לא יצק עליו שמן ולא יתן עליו לבנה כי מנחת קנאות הוא (cf. Levit. V.11). הוא refers to the קמח according to רש״י.

V. 16. לפני ה׳ .והקריב אותה הכהן, in the eastern entrance of the Nickanor Gate through which all those that enter or leave the Temple pass: והוא הפתח שבו דרך כניסה ויציאה לכל באי עזרה (Sota 8a Rashi thereupon) — עמד לפני — ,והעמיד לפני: means to stand before somebody at their disposal, he (the priest) places her before God for His disposal, His decision cf. above III.6, XXVII.19, I Kings XVIII.1 XVIII.15 et alia.

V. 17. מים קדשים, water which is dedicated in the כיור (the basin in the entrance hall of the Temple which contained the water for the ritual washing of the hands and feet of the priests see Ex. XXX.18-21) אשר יהיה בקרקע המשכן, if no such earth is there, some earth must be brought into the היכל beforehand and spread over the floor (Sota 15b). קרקע: from רקע, as כרכוב from רקע ברגלך ,רקע .רכב (Ezek. VI.11) רקעו ברגל (ibid XXV.6) to tread firmly, to stamp, from which it obtained the meaning to press flat, to hammer out, and from that, to stretch. So that קרקע is really the earth trodden on by people, the ground, the floor. It is repeatedly used for the floor of the Temple, (I. Kings, VI). But also used quite generally קרקע הים (the bed of the sea) Amos IX.3. In the היכל of the Temple a priest raised a marble tile of the flooring which was specially designated for this purpose and took some of the earth from beneath it (Sota 15b) — ונתן אל המים not במים but כדי שיראה על המים :אל המים, it was not to be stirred into the water, as the אפר פרה had to be in the מים חיים in the case of the פרה אדומה, but was to remain visible on the water, so that if the earth had been put into the vessel first, it was not allowed to be used אל המים כדי שיראה על המים הקדים עפר למים פסול (Sota 15b, 16b).

There, at the מי חטאת, the fact was to be brought home by the sprinkling with the water, to a person who had become טמא by having come into contact with the dead body of a human being that: although אפר, although his body would ultimately revert to the dust of dissolution, his real self was מים חיים, an immortal drop from the source of eternal life (see Ch. XXIX.17). Here at סוטה the fact was to be brought home to one who had incurred the suspicion of moral טומאה, that although עפר, although the earthly body, by its nature and for its purposes, was — like its mother-earth — gifted with powers of motherhood and urges to accomplish that purpose, neverthless מים קדושים, nevertheless purity of moral holiness was the purpose of its true fudamental self, for which the bodily strenuousness belonging to its earthly nature was only to be an apparent external trait, but in reality to be held aloft and mastered by the true internal self. But this clear pure real self must never be made muddy by being mixed with the other trait (cf. Sota 17a) אמר רבא מפני מה אמרה תורה הבא עפר לסוטה, זכתה, יוצא ממנה בן כאברהם אבינו דכתיב בי׳ עפר ואפר, לא זכתה תחזור לעפרא.

Just as here the earthly sensuous side of woman’s nature is represented by עפר, so, in Ps. CXXXIX.15, the womb in which the coming human child is formed is called the depth of the earth, רקמתי בתחתיות הארץ.

But this earth belongs to the ground on which the people stand in God’s Sanctuary of the Torah. This Sanctuary in its demands does not assume any superhuman nature of people which would be above or contrasting to the actual state of ordinary human beings. It is rather the bodily sensual earthly side of the nature of human beings which forms the קרקע המשכן, it is what it presupposes and on it and from it builds up the whole mode of life which its holy demands entail. And the מים קדושים are taken from the כיור, out of which the priests fit themselves for every holy act (the ritual washing of the hands I.L.) and for every holy “step” they take (the ritual washing of the feet I.L.). And this “vessel for the sanctifying of the priests” was made out of the מראות הצובאות, out of the mirrors of the women who once used to throng to the entrance of the Sanctuary, just where their sister who had become so unlike them stands for the verdict of God. So it is just the modest decent moral behaviour which is expected from Jewish women which is the original source which, out from the Sanctuary, is to penetrate the whole of Jewish life with priest-like consecration.

V. 18. והעמיד הכהן את האשה לפני ה׳ It has already been said once in V. 16 והעמידה לפני ה׳, but she was led from place to place to draw out the procedure so as to give her time to confess (Sota 8,a) — ופרע את ראש. The hair of the head of a chaste wife is “kept back” by her head-gear from being seen hence the uncovering of her hair is called פרע, freeing. According to Sota 7a her dress is torn open and held in place above the breasts by a ribbon of bast and the uncovering of her hair completed by undoing the plaits and letting it hang loose. This uncovering of her hair gives a shock to the propriety of a Jewish wife, אזהרה, it says in Ketuvoth 72a, on this verse, אזהרה לבנות ישראל שלא יצאו בפרוע ראש. “The daughters of Israel are forbidden to appear in public with the hair of their head exposed”. The uncovered hair of a Jewish married woman belongs to the conception of ערוה in the literal meaning of the word, and here it is just used to give the woman the character of being deficient in Jewish modesty. Keeping the hair of the head covered is the external sign of married propriety. The woman who by her behaviour has forsaken the path of this propriety no longer deserves this diadem of צניעות, that fundamental characteristic of Jewish Womanhood. By removing her head-covering the priest expresses the whole reproach which rests on her. One has to remember that although it is still questionable if she had actually committed adultery — and that is what is to be decided now — in any case the woman had — by סטיה מדרכי הצניעות — by her behaviour given cause for קנוי (V.20) and then by proven סתירה had disregarded the solemn warning given to her, so that in any case she had deserved the reproach of at least immodest frivolity.

ונתן על כפיה את מנחת הזכרון מנחת קנאות היא. Here the one aspect of the meaning of this Mincha is in the foreground; מנחת זכרון, that the possible guilt of the woman is placed before the consideration of God. For just by this Divine deliberation and the possible resulting fate does the drinking of the water become so portentous. See on V.25. But the other aspect, the vindication of the woman to continue as the wife of her husband, for which this Mincha is brought for her, is not forgotten, מנחת קנאות הוא.

וביד הכהן יהיו. The Mincha in the hand of the woman and the water in the hand of the priest belong together. By the Mincha the water becomes מי המרים המאררים. The Mincha is מזכרת עון, without it the water has no meaning at all, כמה דלא קרבה מנחתה לא בדקה לה מיא (Sota 14a, 20b) — מי ,מי המרים is stat. constr. to המרים, the water of bitterness, the bitter water itself would be מרים .המים המרים are the bitternesses, the bitter facts which the מי סוטה hold up to the woman. We have seen how the מים קדשים בכלי חרש and the עפר מקרקע המשכן make the definite demand for keeping holy purity of morals in spite of the earthly nature of bodily sensuality, more, with the most complete assumption and on the base of it. If this truth, this fact is a “bitter” one for the woman, i.e. if her behaviour hitherto has actively opposed this demand then drinking the water representing this bitterness brings a curse on to her. מאררים is an active form: curse-bringing. They are מאררים if what they represent is מר. Both the lesson it preaches and the curse it brings if this teaching is bitter was also expressed materially by something which tasted bitter being added (Sota 20a) צריך שיתן מר לתוך המים מ״ט דאמר קרא מי המרים שמרים כבר (See Rashi thereon). That seems to us to mean to show that it is not its fateful effect that makes it “bitter” but what it preaches and its meaning. Its fateful effect is only the result of the bitterness of its “contents” its preaching and lesson. And similarly the curse-bringing effect of the water is only effected by the material concrete dissolution of the written actual words of the curse.

V. 19. אם לא שכב וגו׳ ואם לא שטית וגו׳ .והשביע אתה וגו׳ this explanatory repetition ואם לא שטית may be meant to avert a not unimportant misunderstanding. Were it only to say אם לא שכב etc. this could be taken to mean that the Torah considered it reprehensible only if unfaithfulness went to the extreme in marriage, but otherwise, frivolity, departing from the path of decent modesty was not blamable unless it went to complete unfaithfulness. That is why certainly the fateful possible effect of the water of bitterness is attached to אם לא שכב וגו׳, not to the actual act of adultery, but at the same time, what obviously led up to it, the ואם לא שטית וגו׳ is stressed by the Torah as a departure from that path of chaste modesty which the Sanctuary of this Torah has prescribed for the marriages of its people. She is in any case a סוטה even if she did not go to the extreme limit, to טומאה. Similarly both actions are stressed in the positive supposition in V.20: תחת אישך — ואת כי שטית תחת אישך וכי נטמאת ויתן וגו׳ seems to describe the relationship which a right-thinking wife thinks of herself towards her husband, the consideration of which should have protected her from slipping. Cf. Ps. XCI.4 תחת כנפיו תחסה, Ruth III.9 ופרשת כנפך על אמתך, Is. IV.1 רק יקרא שמך עלינו. A wife is under the protection of her husband and owes him a duty. She is bound to respect his exclusive conjugal rights. She bears his name. She belongs to him. She has rejected the position and its attendant duties which she assumed with her marriage, she has become a הנקי — .סוטה, if we consider the ascending scale of ,נכה ,נגח ,נגע נקה, the last would have the meaning of a hefty movement fending off something from oneself, and הנקי would mean remain untouched by the power of this water.

V. 20—21. בשבעת האלה .ואת כי וגו׳ והשביע וגו׳. Here, in the affirmative case, the priest makes the woman accept the curse יתן ה׳ וגו׳ Her condition will be such that in future if anyone would wish to express an אלה and a שבועה he would use the term: “may God let a similar fate befall the person concerned”. Note that in all the preceding and succeeding procedure it repeatedly designates the כהן who is to be the one who undertakes the proceedings. For it is no process of the law court but an appeal to the Sanctuary of the Torah, whose herald and representative the priest is, and whose founder and guarantee for its demands God wishes to demonstrate Himself. That is also why it is ה׳ the God of love — the Name designating the dispenser of loving life and blessing — from Whom the fateful action is expected. Not the punishing destruction of the sinner, but the chaste morality which is to be ensured and furthered, upon which all the happiness and all the blessings of the people depend is the ultimate purpose of this solemn and stern procedure.

V. 22. אמן .ואמרה האשה אמן אמן, see Gen. XV.6. If one responds to any oath by saying אמן, one gives oneself up entirely to the terms of that oath, it makes it exactly the same as if one had made the oath oneself. The idea of שבועה in an oath (see Gen. XXI.23 et alia) the submission of our whole being under the power of God’s judging Might is given undisturbable firmness by being responded to with אמן which makes our whole future dependent on it כל העונה אמן אחר השבועה כאילו מוציא שבועה מפיו (Shevuoth 29b) יש בו קבלה יש בו שבועה ויש בו האמנת דברים (ibid 36a). So that by saying אמן the woman accepts all what the priest has said, the simple oath without the אלה of V.19 as well as the one with the אלה of V.21; and as תוספות in Kiddushin 27b takes it, both the oath that she had not sinned with the man on whom the suspicion rests as well as that as long as she had been תחת אישה married to her husband she had not been unfaithful to him. But as she doubles the אמן her oath goes farther and stretches even to the time in which she had not yet been completely תחת אישה in which she had been ארוסה or שומרת יבם (see Deut. XXV.V). (In that time, although unfaithfulness would prevent the consummation of the marriage, doubtful cases like ours here, could not invoke the Sota process) על מה היא אומרת אמן אמן, אמן על האלה אמן על השבועה אמן אם מאיש זה אמן אם מאיש אחר אמן שלא סטיתי ארוסה ונשואה שהמרת יבם וכנוסה. (Sota 18b).

Wir haben hiermit den Fall, daß ein zur Leistung kommender Eid auch auf Gegenstände erweitert wird, die ihn ursprünglich nicht veranlasst hatten, ja sogar auf solche, die einen Eid gar nicht selbständig hätten hervorrufen können. Der Ehemann hatte die Frau nur in Beziehung auf einen bestimmten Mann in Verdacht. Da sie sich von diesem Verdacht durch einen Eid zu reinigen hat, so wird in den Eid auch jeder andere Ehebruch eingeschlossen, hinsichtlich dessen kein bestimmter Verdacht vorliegt, ja, er wird sogar auf Zeiten ausgedehnt, deren etwaige Vorgänge selbständig gar keinen Reinigungseid hätten veranlassen können. Diese Eideserweiterung heißt גלגול שבועה und kommt beim gerichtlichen Eid überall da zur Anwendung, wo der Beklagte außer dem den Eid provozierenden Prozessobjekte noch in anderer Beziehung zu dem Kläger gestanden, in welcher er sich nach dessen Meinung oder Vermutung, eventuell auch nach Vermutung des Gerichtes, einer Unredlichkeit oder Veruntreuung schuldig gemacht habe oder haben könne, selbst wenn sich hierauf die ursprüngliche Klage gar nicht erstreckt hätte, ja selbst wenn dies Objekte träfe, die, wie z. B. קרקעות (siehe Schmot 22, 8) überall nicht eidesfähig sind. Daher der Satz: נכסים שאין להם אחריות זוקקין את הנכסים שיש להם אחרית לישבע עליהן, obgleich אין נשבעין על הקרקעות (Kiduschin 26a u. 27b).

The principle in the law of גלגול שבועה (making the oath extend beyond the matter in question I.L.) laid down here would result from the deep inner nature of the oath. Every oath imposed by the court is an appeal from the shortsightedness of human insight to the All-Knowingness of God, to Whose judging insight the one who swears submits himself and all his possessions if any part of these latter is, as is claimed, illegally in his possession. The admissibility of this appeal must be established by an actual objective doubt in law as to the right of possession of some property. But the appeal is made to the Court of God and once that is done it is transferred from the object to the person and the person in question has to vindicate his whole honest dealing with all human beings, i.e. to answer for his honesty and loyal dealing in all connections he has ever had with the claimant.

V. 23. וכתב וגו׳. In V.30 the whole procedure of Sota is called תורה, Law, and from that it is taught in Sota 17b that the whole process, including this writing, bears the character of the most exacting application of the law, דיני נפשות, accordingly, right through from beginning to the end, בין גמר בין תחלה must be done in broad daylight. It is not the dark powers of night whose affairs are being looked after, it is a human being in the highest morally free affairs of his human associations whose interests are to be maintained here by the intervention of the Divine powers of the Divine Torah. That is why all the laws pertaining to the writing of a ספר תורה apply also to the writing of מגלת סוטה.

בספר on a page of parchment. את האלות האלה: he writes אם לא שכב איש אותך etc. v.19, ואת כי שטית etc. v.20, יתן ה׳ אתך v.21 ובאו מים etc. ולנפל ירך v.22. But he writes neither the words והשביע הכהן etc. of v.19, nor ואמרה האשה אמן אמן of v.22. He may only write the adjuration after the woman has accepted it by saying “Amen”, and he must write it לשמה, having in mind the particular woman who is standing here for the procedure. The writing, accordingly, is naught but the fixation in writing of the שבועה and אלה which rest on the woman and which she has already accepted verbally. ומחה אל וגו׳, this is not a blotting out by the water but a dissolving into the water. The letters of the writing dissolve and are completely mixed with the water, and thereby the bitter truths which are taught by the components already there, the מים קדושים and the עפר, are complemented in a most serious manner by the fateful possible results taken over by the written אלות. By this dissolving the writing of the אלות into the water, the מי המרים become מאררים.

V. 24. והשקה וגו׳. The expression “drinking from the cup of fate” (used both for good fortune, salvation and for the reverse I.L.) occurs so frequently in the scriptures, and even “שתה״ alone, simply the word “drinking”, is used with the meaning of receiving one’s destiny from the Hand of God, as in Obad. 1,16, כי כאשר שתיתם על הר קדשי ישתו כל הגוים תמיד, that it is in no way far-fetched to take the drinking here to be merely translating into a concrete symbolic action the metaphor of accepting her fate in accordance with her guilt or innocence. Like Ps. 75,8, 9, the cup of fate in God’s Hands is “mixed”, so here the ingredients of her fateful drink are mixed out of the representation of what she shall be, of what she was meant to be, and of the consequences of her living up to that or failing to do so. — ובאו בה וגו׳. The curse-bringing water comes into her firstly למרים, its portentous effect does not start yet, that depends on the following. First it comes into her למדים, as the most bitter truths to prove itself on her past.
