V. 25. והניף .ולקח וגו׳ ,והניף וגו׳ :והקרוב וגו׳, the movements of the תנופה and מוליך ומביא מעלה ומוריד ,תרומה (see on Ex. XXIX.24). Heaven and Earth and the people of the four quarters of the world are invited as witnesses of the procedure. Heaven and earth and all humanity are involved in the vindication of the morality of a wife; in the Presence of God the Mincha of the vindication of marriage honour is directed to them and after that והקריב etc. to the altar of the sanctification of the Torah, ברוח מערבית דרומית, in הגשה (see on Levit. II.8) placed on the side dedicated to the concept of spiritual life to be developed from the Torah. So that the decision asked from God is not from the point of view of the private life of this one marriage, but is made in the name of heaven and earth, in the name of the Jewish spiritual life to be achieved out of the Torah, all of which are concerned in the same way in keeping aloft the standard of wifely morality. And it is the woman and the priest — the woman in the interests of her asserted innocence, the priest in the interests of the sanctity of marriage demanded by the Sanctuary of the Torah — who conjointly (as in Levit. VII.30 Sota 19a) perform the introductory act of the begged-for decision of God.
V. 26. וקמץ וגו׳. This begging for the decision is done by הקטרת קומץ which above was called מזכרת עון (see V.15) and here אזכרה.

ואחר ישקה את האשה. This drinking the Sota-water is already prescribed above in V.24, before offering the Mincha, and in fact in Sota 19, the predominant Halacha is משקה ואחר כך מקריב, (that drinking preceded the offering). If nevertheless here, after the הקרבה it is repeated that she is to be given the water to drink, תוספות there explains that it comes to tell us that it appears in the Jerusalmi, although of course the prescribed order is the reverse, אם הקריב ואחר כך השקה כשרה a case which could also occur, according to Babli 19a, if it should happen that the dissolution of writing had not completely occurred, שרישומו ניכר, that traces of the lettering was still visible on the parchment, the solution and the drinking would have to be done a second time.

We have already remarked on V.18 how the drinking and the Mincha belong together. There is no power in the water by itself to have any effect, only by calling on God to give a decision made by the offering of the Mincha does the water become momentous, כמה דלא קרבה מנחתה לא בדיק לה מיא. This is completely and clearly shown when she drinks the water first and the effect is only visible after her Mincha has been brought. By drinking the water, the woman in a striking symbolic action has taken on herself and accepted the adjuration. Thereby her whole bodily self has placed itself under the power of the solemn truths and their consequences which are to prove themselves on her past, and then her מנחת קנאות מזכרת עון calls for God to decide in accordance with her guilt or her innocence whether the drink is to be one bringing blessing or ruin. Although drunk before, the idea of the drink is only completed after bringing the Mincha. By the doubling of the verse of the drinking, putting it both before and after bringing the Mincha, the intimate connection between the two procedures is shown.

V. 27. והשקה. This repeating once again that she is to be given the water to drink, is, according to Sota 19b to say that once the inscription with the name of God has been obliterated in the water she must be made to drink it unless she admits being guilty. Until then, without necessarily admitting guilt, still asserting her innocence, she only drinks completely of her own free will and is, in no way, compelled to do so. If she declares herself unwilling to drink at any point up to this, the procedure is simply stopped. Her guilt remains doubtful and the marriage has to be dissolved (see V.13). But if the writing has been obliterated she is given the alternative of confessing her guilt or in the consciousness of her innocence to drink the Sota-drink (Sota 20a).

ובאו בה המים המאררים למרים, “the water expressing the curse enter her body as bitterness”, or “and prove themselves as bitter”. The truths, the preachings they express as מים קדושים and עפר מקרקע משכן are in truth, bitter for her, and prove themselves by carrying out the terms of the curse which has been dissolved into them if she has been נטמאה וגו׳, only if she has lost her purity and so stands in contradiction to the holiness of morals postulated by that teaching. If the water in accordance with its contents is not “bitter” to her, they have no bitter results, on the contrary they bring blessing to the sexual future of the woman, as is immediately proclaimed in the following verse.

V. 28. ונקתה, see on V.19, then she is completely untouched by the curse which she had conditionally taken on herself by drinking the water. Her innocence “strikes the curse completely back”. ונזרעה זרע: her purity corresponding to the מים קדשים proves itself in a happy increase of her עפר force and her עפר-מקרקע-המשכן mission in life in blessing of her “fruitful womb”. If she had been childless hitherto, she now received the blessing of children, were her child-births up till now difficult they become easy etc. (Sota 26a).

V. 29. אשר תשטה וגו׳ ונטמאה, this is the case described in V.13, if, after the giving of the warning and the subsequent ignoring it had been duly confirmed by evidence of two witnesses, evidence of adultery having been given by one witness only, the marriage must be dissolved without further ado.

V. 30. או איש וגו׳, or if the absence of any witness at all regarding her actual guilt causes the whole procedure instroduced in V.14 ועשה לה הכהן את כל התורה הזאת, the whole process described here is called תורה and is thereby placed on par with the most important laws of the Torah the carrying out of which belongs to the duties of the highest supreme court of law. So that the whole procedure must be done under the direct authority of the ב״ד הגדול (Sota 7b V.15 and V.23).

V. 31. ונקה האיש מעון וגו׳. Only if, at the time when the husband wants to place the decision as to the guilt or innocence of his wife before God, he knows himself to be free from the same sexual misbehaviour, yea, from every sexual misbehaviour, can he expect the decision of God regarding his wife. But if he has sinned against the laws of sexual purity, if after קנוי וסתירה when his wife had become אסורה to him, he had nevertheless continued to have sexual intercourse with her, or if otherwise he had ever, from the time he had been responsible for keeping the Mitzvas, transgressed in any way against the laws of sexual purity, more, even if he had kept indulgently quiet over sexual excesses of his family he can not hand the Sota-drink to his wife ת״ר ונקה האיש מעון בזמן שהאיש מנוקה מעון המים בודקין את אשתו אין האיש מנוקה מעון אין המים בודקין את אשתו ואומר (הושע ד׳) לא אפקוד על בנותיכם כי תזנינה ועל כלותיכם כי תנאפנה כי הם עם הזונות יפרדו ועם הקדשות יזבחו ועם לא יבין ילבט מאי ואומר וכי תימא עון דידה אין דבניה ובנותיה לא ת״ש לא אפקוד וגו׳ וכי תימא עון דאשת איש אין דפנויה לא תא שמע כי הם עם הזונות יפרדו וגו׳ מאי ועם לא יבין ילבט אמר ר׳ אלעזר אמר להם נביא לישראל אם אתם מקפידים על עצמיכם מים בודקין נשתיכם ואם לאו אין המים בודקין נשותיכם (Sota 47b Jebamoth 58a. תוספות ד״ה ונקה). God’s laws of morality grant men in no ways greater license for sexual irregularities than they do for women.

The Halacha teaches further that just as the wife who is under suspicion of having been unfaithful to her husband is אסורה to her husband as long as she has not been declared pure by the Sota-drink, in the same way, the man who is suspected of being her partner in adultery may never marry her even after she has been divorced כשם שאסורה לבעל כך אסורה לבועל. She is repeatedly called “נטמאה״ (V.14, 27, 29) that she has forfeited her “purity” for the sanctuary of marriage and for the sanctuary in general to say that she has lost her טהרה for בועל ,בעל and תרומה if she is the wife or daughter of a כהן (see Levit. XXI.7, XXII.12) that she is אסורה for all three (Sota 28a).

And finally the Halacha teaches כשם שהמים בודקין אותה כך המים בודקין אותו, her drinking the Sota-water has the same effect on the man with whom she committed the sin as it has on her. In V.22 when it gives the fateful wording of the adjuration it does not say לצבות בטנך ולנפל ירכך but לצבות בטן ולנפל ירך, for the guilty בועל receives the same fate. (Sota 27b, 28a).

But not every marriage can make an appeal to God to decide if the marriage may continue after its purity has come into doubt by קנוי and סתירה. There are marriages which once they have reached that stage must be dissolved at once. The Halacha derives from the text of our chapter the law that it is only in the cases of fully consumated marriages — אשה תחת אישה — that an appeal by Sota decision for their continuation after the permission to do so has been rendered by קנוי and סתירה is allowed, but not if this doubt has arisen already in the period of ארוסה or שומרת יבם (Sota 23b). It indicates further that the Law assumes that both parties of the marriage have complete use of all their physical faculties, and teaches that if the husband or the wife suffers from some bodily incapacity e.g. is blind, lame, dumb, with קנוי and סתירה the marriage has immediately to be ended (ibid. 27a & b). Also if the husband has no children and no children can be expected from the wife, the same rule holds good. Also if the behaviour of the wife which led to קנוי and סתירה has gone beyond causing just the suspicion of the husband but is a public scandal, is “the talk of the women at their spinning-wheels”, the same applies. In V.28 it says וטהורה היא on which the Gemora says (ibid. 6a) ולא שישאו ויתנו בה מוזרות בלבנה, the Sota test is given for the case where, apart from the suspicion of the husband, she stands as a pure woman. But if her behaviour has already made the marriage into the talk of the town, its continuation would be a moral scandal מכוער הדבר ותצא (see Rashi ibid 31a).

Taking all these matters together we see that it is no question of an inquisition into the private conditions of the married life, but matters which are open to everybody, partly matters which are purely external or physical, which, if the wife, by קנוי and סתירה has given cause for grave suspicion of unfaithfulness, call for immediate dissolution of the marriage without any Sota process. That, if, as in the cases of ארוסה and שומרת יבם the personal marriage bond only has been made, but the woman has not yet gone to live with the man, and equally so in the case of אילונית and עקרה, one of the most essential purposes of marriage can not be fulfilled, that the mere stage of קנוי and סתירה suffice, in the first case, for the marriage not to be proceeded with and in the others to be dissolved, seems to us to be quite natural. For, in any case an actual act of unfaithfulness with an ארוסה is punishable more severely than with a נשואה. But also the motive for consideration of the physical integrity of both parties seems not too far to seek. For any bodily disablement brings with it the requirment of greater help from the one partner and lack of independence on the part of the other. This, with nobler natures begets an increased intimacy of conjugal attachment but with lower ones is taken advantage of. If in such conditions the wife has behaved in such a way to give occasion for קנוי, grave official warning in presence of two witnesses, and then it has been proved that she disregarded the warning by סתירה, this would indicate such a high degree of fickleness that the continuation of the marriage would be infeasible.

If we consider this whole law, of which רמב״ן in his commentary pertinently remarks that it is the one institution in law of the whole of the laws of the Torah which would regularly ask for the direct intervention of God by a miracle, it is one in which God is shown as the author and founder of the whole institution of human marriages, and as the witness and watcher of each individual Jewish conjugal union. It shows the Presence of God in every Jewish married life, the faithfulness to each other of wife and husband as the quite special object of God’s attention, sexual morality as the root of spiritual and moral human happiness, so that for it alone a direct appeal may be made to the All-seeing Presence of God. So that this whole institution of Sota is nothing but a realisation in the actual concrete life of the people of the great fundamental Truth which is symbolically taught and kept before the eyes of the people by the banishment of the זב זבה וכד׳ from שילוח זב וזבה ;מחנה לויה from the מחנה לויה places sexual purity as the first indispensable condition for all spiritual working one’s way up to God, and השקאת סוטה shows just this sexual purity of married life as the most pressing object of the immediate administration of God. So that פרשת סוטה stands in a similar relation to שילוח זב וזבה ממחנה לויה as פרשת גזל הגר does to שילוח מצורע ממחנה ישראל.
V. 1. Now follows the third פרשה, the פרשת נזיר parallel to שילוח טמא מת from the מחנה שכינה.

V. 2. כי יפלא. See on Levit. XXII.21. נזיר. The basic meaning of נזר is quite definitely: to keep aloof, to keep separate, and הנזר (Levit. XXII.2, Zac. VII.3) means undoubtedly, to abstain or refrain from something. It would therefore seem very natural to take נזיר — having regard to the abstaining from wine ordered in V.3 — to mean “the abstenious one”. But already the fact that he is not only forbidden wine or grapes, but even wine-vinegar, and even the skins and pips of grapes, refraining from eating which would not demand the sacrifice entailed by great abstemiousness, makes us imagine that the conception of נזיר must go beyond mere abstinence. The fact, further, that although touching a dead body, even doing so unintentionally (V.9) does cancel the time already spent in fulfilling his vow of Nazaritehood, drinking wine does not do so, shows us that “abstaining from wine” just as not touching a dead body and not cutting his hair do belong to the obligations which a Nazarite undertakes, they, by themselves, do not by any means constitute the concept of a Nazarite, or even form the predominant signs of one, so that one would have to take “Nazir” to mean primarily “an abstemious one.” A careful consideration of verses 4, 5, 6 and then summing up in V.8 makes us realise that all the three restrictions together do not constitute the concept “נזרו״, the conception of Nazaritism, but that they are to be just the external manifestations by which, and in which Nazaritism declares itself, but that the idea itself is given in V.8. קדוש הוא לאלקיו and the three restrictions: הטומאה ,והתגלחת ,והיוצא מן הגפן (Nazir 34a) appear only as a result of this קדושה. And in fact we also see Amos II.11, classing נזירים and נביאים (Nazarites and prophets) together, and stressing the existence of both of them in Israel as a fact of special Divine preference. If we compare the expression נזירים used in Levit. XXV.5, 11, for the vines which have to be left to themselves in the seventh and Jubilee years then נזיר in any case does not mean he who keeps himself away from others but from whom others have to keep away, from whom others are separated. So that just as נזר means the royal diadem which marks the person whose head it surrounds as being set apart and inaccessible, so here נזר designates a regime of living and striving that raises the person who vows of his own free will to undertake it, out of and above the midst of the people amongst whom he lives and sets him the task to be completely קדוש לאלקים, to belong with the whole of his being and will exclusively to his God. He wishes to draw a נזר a circle round about himself in which only God is to be present. This isolating himself with and for God is termed הזיר לה׳ and one who does so isolate himself: a נזיר. But this is no hermit-like isolation, no shutting oneself up in the wilderness, it is an isolation of one’s mind and spirit with God in the midst of the most active ordinary life.

V. 3. יין״ :מיין ושכר יזיר and שכר is he to place in the distance-keeping circle about him”. Like the priests entering to function in the Sanctuary, like the teachers of the Law before they expound it (Levit. 10,9-11) have to avoid intoxicating drinks, so does the Nazarite — and to a much further extension — during the whole period of his Nazaritism have to keep away from wine and everything that originates from the vine. Priests and teachers have to refrain at the time of their exercising their functions from everything that is really intoxicating, even from drinking the small quantity of a רביעית. True, the prohibition for the Nazarite is limited to wine only, but it is extended to everything that even remotely comes from the vine, everything which even if it is not in the slightest degree intoxicating still reminds one of wine. For as long as the Nazarite is a Nazarite his mind is to be directed to the Sanctuary and to the Torah, for as long as he is a Nazarite he is to be steadfastly a priest and a teacher, and keeping away from the vine and everything derived from it is to be a constant warning and admonition to him to keep the undisturbed clarity of mind and the unexcited tranquility of disposition which Nazaritism demands for his thoughts and feelings.

מיין ושכר. Whereas above in Levit. X.9 according to the way רמב״ם takes it שכר is partly an explanatory addition to יין and means כדרך שכרותו (only prohibited in an intoxicating manner) and partly to extend the prohibition to all intoxicating drinks שאר משכרין (see Kerithoth 13b) (שו״ת רשב״א 363), here, by the additions which follow, חומץ ,ענבים ,חרצנים שכר ,זוג, too is to be understood only as a “partial notion”, a special example, a פרט of the comprehensive idea, the מכל אשר יעשה מגפן היין :כלל, so that יין is wine, in its weak early stage of grape juice, מגתו, during the first forty days of its formation, and שכר, wine already having reached the stage of being intoxicating. Onkelos too takes that to be its meaning: מחמד חדת ועתיק “from wine new or old”. The whole form of the verse is פרט וכלל ופרט viz. מיין ושכר יזיר :פרט then מכל אשר יעשה מגפן היין :כלל and מחרצנים ועד זג :וחזר ופרט, and the rule is פרט וכלל ופרט then אי אתה דן אלא כעין הפרט (this formation of the sentences has the full import of כלל ופרט וכלל see Levit. XI.10) only at פרט וכלל ופרט the פרט raised to a כלל is to be taken more limitedly אי איכא פרטא דדמי משני צדדים מרבינן בחד צד לא מרבינן Nazir 36b). מה הפרט מפורש פרי ופסולת פרי (e.g. חומץ Rashi) אף כל פרי ופסולת פרי (See Nazir 34b).

שרה .וכל משרת ענבים in Chaldean to dissolve, loosen, (hence to allow, like התר) occurs only here and with the latter meaning, to soak. Nazir 37a gives us two ways of taking משרת ענבים, either שרה ענבים במים ויש בהן טעם יין that if one soaks grapes in water until the water has the taste of wine, and then this is taken as an example of the general law that טעם כעיקר that if a material that is an איסור is even only recognisable by its taste it is still אסור; or ששתה פתו ביין ואכל כזית מפת ומיין, that if he ate the minimum quantity of a כזית of bread and wine together so that the היתר, the permitted food the bread makes up the שיעור of the איסור the prohibited one, the היתר מצטרף לאיסור, a law that would then only be applied to איסורי נזיר (see Levit. 6,11 and Numb. 31,23).
V. 4. מחרצנים עד זג. According to ר׳ יוסי (Nazir 34b) חרצנים are the pips and זג the skins.

V. 5. כל ימי נדר נזרו. At the prohibition of drinking wine and of touching a dead body it says כל ימי הזירו ,כל ימי נזרו, both order keeping away from objects and so belong to the concrete realisation of נזר, keeping oneself within the limited sphere of the נזר. But the prohibition of cutting the hair is not to be understood as such a limitation. It is not itself a concrete נזר but it expresses the נדר נזר, it characterises the person who undertakes a vow of Nazaritism — תער, from ערה to be uncovered, (like תבל from בלה) an instrument that uncovers the skin, makes it naked. In Nazir 39a and b the Halacha is given that removing the hair by any other means is included in the prohibition, even if not done with a תער, a razor, the real instrument for shaving. Because of this extension the text does not use the usual term, shaving גלח, but uses the circumlocution לא יעבר על ראשו thereby extending the limiting term תער, in contrast to והעבירו תער (Ch. VIII.7) where the generalising והעבירו is limited by the following תעד. The prohibition here does not lie in the תער but in the effect, in removing the hair of the head. That is why this forbidden action is also specially stressed by the contrast, allowing it to grow, the intentional effect of not cutting it, קדוש יהיה גדל פרע וגו׳, thereby making cutting his hair forbidden to the Nazarite by a לא תעשה (a prohibition) and an עשה (a positive command). He transgresses both by the removal of even a single hair (ibid 39a) — קדוש יהיה, his head, cf. V.11. וקדש את ראשו, his head shall be holy, he shall let his head have the stamp of holiness, גדל פרע שער ראשו inasmuch as he allows the hair of his head to grow wild. According to Nazir 5a the hair attains this character of a wild growth of hair in at least thirty days, hence סתם נזירות ל׳ יום, unless a longer period has expressly been vowed, the ordinary minimum for the duration of Nazarism is thirty days. For, as the text says here, the growth of his hair is the expression of his נדר נזרו, of his vow of Nazirism. We have already remarked on Levit. XIV.8, how hair can be considered as insulating the skin and reducing receptiveness to outer influences, so that giving up inconsiderate conduct and selfishly living for oneself, and devoting oneself to the social life of the community could well be expressed symbolically by the תגלחת מצורע (the shaving of the hair on the return of the cured “leper” I.L.) and the תגלחת לוים (performing the same operation at the induction ceremony of the Levites I.L.). The reverse, allowing the hair to grow unrestricted would then express withdrawing oneself to isolation, sinking oneself more into oneself as being the task set for the Nazarite during the period of his Nazaritism. What he wants to do is, without retiring from actual contact with the social life around him, to work on himself, spiritually and mentally for the time of his vow of Nazaritism (see on V.3) to be more by himself with God, His Sanctuary, and His teachings. It is to this vow that the insulating growth of his hair admonishes him. His head accordingly bears the sign of his holy resolution, becomes holy, becomes קדוש as everything does which has the purpose of bringing home to us the ideal of our spiritual and moral perfection, becomes a קדש and is called קדוש (See on Ex. 29,37, Levit. 23,3).

כל ימי הזירו לה׳ וגו׳. Here it does not say simply, as in V.4 and 5: כל ימי נזרו or כל ימי נדר נזרו, but כל ימי הזירו לה׳, for this prohibition of טומאה comes from the relation of Nazaritism to “God”, and it is just this relation which is to be kept undisturbed. — נפש .על נפש מת וגו׳ is, as a rule, feminine. So that מת is probably not an adjective qualifying נפש, but either genitive to נפש, like נפשות מת in Levit. 21,11, or is apposition to it, a נפש which now lies there as a מת. It would then clearly be במת בנפש (Ch. 19,13) (that which dies of a life I.L.). The נפש חיה (the living life) of human beings is never מתה. But the נפש, the individual, the personality of a person (see Gen. I.20) which up till then we had only known in its bodily appearance, when we come into contact with a dead body, involuntarily makes us think of its death too. It is not really a נפש which lies before us, it is מת, but the מת does represent the נפש, the person, to us, and it is just that we should not objectively refer the מיתה to the נפש that is one of the purposes of טומאת מת (see on Levit. XI.47) and (Numb. Ch. XIX). Everywhere in the Torah the expressions used and the way the words are put are most carefully chosen when referring to this subject. Here, where it is not a question of touching, but of ביאה, of being in the same room, the text allows itself to refer primarily to the נפש, and then rectifies it by מת. But at נגיעה it never says נגע בנפש המת but נגע במת בנפש or still more clearly הנגע במת לכל נפש (who touches that which dies of every personality I.L.) (Ch. 19,11). For the נפש in the sense in which it is thought of here, and is to be thought of, is altogether not accessible to touch. In this way may lie the explanation of a peculiar interpretation of Onkelos. He constantly translates טמא לנפש by דמסאב לטמי נפשא דאנשא. So that he avoids saying דמסאב לנפשא and inserts the word טמי instead, which Rashi says (on Ch. 5,2) is a Chaldean expression for עצמות אדם, human bones. Just as Onkelos, when referring to the conception of God, expresses every anthropomorphic term by a circumlocution, so when referring to the soul he does not want to give the slightest possibility for it to be taken that the נפש could be מטמא a person. Accordingly wherever the טומאה effect could be referred directly to the נפש by the term טמא נפש he inserts word טמי the “frame” the bones, the empty body of a person. But actually it is avoided in the text itself by being construed with -ל. It never says טמא בנפש but לנפש, the טומאה comes from the application to the נפש to which one has come by touching the body. As altogether the mental symbolic טומאה (which arises from contact I.L.) is constantly differentiated from the actual real טומאה brought about by מאכלות אסורות and עריות (eating prohibited food and indulging in prohibited sexual acts) by the different construing of -טמא ל and -טמא ב which we have already indicated in Levit. 11,24.

In V.3 we concluded from the analogy to Levit. X.9-11 that the vow of Nazaritism gives the Nazarite a priestly relation to the Torah. By the prohibition given him here and in the following verse: על נפש מת לא יבא, analogous to the כהן הגדול in Levit. 21,11: ועל כל נפשת מת לא יבא לאביו ולאמו לא יטמא he is raised even to that of a high priest. For as long as he withdraws himself into the Nazarite circle isolating himself for God and with God he may not come near a dead body. We have already repeatedly had to bring to mind how a dead body reminds one of the lack of freedom of his physical nature, and at the same time brings the thought of powerful compulsion of the forces of nature to which the heathen idea raises its highest altars, but how the Jewish Sanctuary of the Torah and the thoughts that prevail in it teach the very opposite, and the thought of a completely free God insists on the complete free-will of human beings in all matters of morality and the consequent complete absence of compulsion to having to submit to the power of physical urges. That was why death and everything referring to death was banned from that Sanctuary, and that was why its servitors, and even to a higher degree, its first representative servitor though living in the midst of the people, the high-priests, were not allowed to come into contact with a dead body. The inscription קדש לה׳ on the forehead of the high-priest was the loudest protest against that heathen thought. It proclaimed definitely that it was not the power of Death that lays low even free-willed Man, but it was to God, לה׳, the completely free-willed living God Who eternally dispenses eternal life, Who gives Man personality from His Personality, freedom from His Freedom, life from His Life, to Whom the power of Death itself is but one of His messengers, a messenger who delivers to complete freedom, it is He to whom the Sanctuary is dedicated (Cf. Ex. XXVIII.28). Now that which keeping טומאת מת out of מחנה שכינה is meant to be for the national Sanctuary and for educating the nation to the ideal of moral perfection, is exactly the same for the individual limited sphere of Nazaritism within which the Nazarite wishes to live, keeping away from טומאת מת.

The general social life out of which the Nazarite temporarily withdraws himself to live more in himself and his relationship to God, is lived by the intimate union of the moral freedom and the physical lack of freedom. For just these two factors intimately combined, intimately united, make a human being. So that partially withdrawing oneself from the usual lively social life can equally mean devoting oneself more fully to what one feels necessary to satisfy one’s physical needs as to giving more devotion than usual to one’s free-willed moral life. So that the God to whom the Nazarite in his retirement dedicates his life could easily become the compelling force of nature which finds its triumph in the sensual grave of morality and its trophies in the waste over graves and tombstones. That this is not the case, but that the God to whom the Nazarite dedicates his isolating Nazarite life, is the free personal God Who has gifted and called Man to use the free-will which He has given him to live a life of free-willed self-control, that it is ה׳ to Whom and to Whose Torah the life of the Nazarite turns, that his temporary withdrawal into himself is only to prepare and arm himself for a fuller, more active life of duty, to make him “live” in the highest possible meaning of the word and not to make him “dead” and useless in the world, that his מחנה is to be a מחנה שכינה of אלקים חיים, that, that admonition and reminder banns Death and dead bodies from his proximity.

Der soziale Menschenverkehr, aus welchem der Nasir zeitweilig sich zurückgezogen, um mehr sich selbst und seinen Beziehungen zu Gott zu leben, verwirklicht sich durch die innige Vermählung des Sittlichfreien mit dem Physischnotwendigen. Denn eben beide Momente, innig verbunden, Physisches mit Sittlichem innig vermählt, ist der Mensch. Das teilweise Hinaustreten aus dem lebendigen Menschenverkehr kann daher ebenso leicht eine größere Hingebung an das Physischnotwendige, wie eine größere Hingebung an das Sittlichfreie bedeuten, und der Gott, dem der Nasir in seiner Zurückgezogenheit sein Sinnen und Trachten weiht, kann sehr leicht die zur Allmacht potenzierte Naturgewalt werden, die ihre Triumphe in dem sinnlichen Grabe der Sittlichkeit feiert und ihre Trophäen in der Öde über Gräbern und Leichensteinen findet. Dass dieses nicht also, daß vielmehr der Gott, dem der Nasir seinen ihn isolierenden Nasirkreis weiht, der freipersönliche, den Menschen zur sittlichfreien Persönlichkeit befähigende und berufende Gott, daß es ד׳ sei, dem und dessen Worte des Lebens der Nasir sein Sinnen und Streben zuwenden, daß er in seiner Selbstumschränkung nur in noch erhöhtem Maße sich für ein sittlichfreies Pflichttatenleben vor Gottes Angesicht rüsten soll und rüsten will, daß seine Zurückgezogenheit dem "Leben" in seiner höchsten Potenz und nicht dem Ersterben und der Erstorbenheit geweiht ist, daß sein מחנה ein מחנה שכינה des אלקי חיים sein soll, das, diese Mahnung, und Erinnerung, bannt hohepriesterlich Tod und Leiche aus seiner Nähe.

V. 7. כי נזר אלקיו על ראשו. The growth of the hair of his head proclaiming his withdrawal into himself expresses that he has consecrated himself to “his God”, and his keeping away from טומאת מת is to express What he considers as his God, that אלקים חיים, the God of Life הוא אלקיו, He is his God. In the same way the ציץ of the high-priest is called נזר הקדש (Ex. XXIX.6, and elsewhere, cf. Levit. XXI.12). By the general prohibition על נפש מת לא יבא (v.6) the prohibition of touching any dead body, even that of his nearest relatives, is already pronounced. If nevertheless the text in V.7 expressly stresses לאביו etc., this, according to Nazir 48a and b. indicates that although family considerations, even of father and mother etc., may not permit the Nazarite to טומאה, there is a duty to human beings in general, the burial of a corpse which otherwise has nobody to attend to it, a מת מצוה, regarding which the טומאה prohibition of a Nazarite must stand aside, and even if the קדושה was a cumulative one, a high-priest who was also a Nazarite, and even if he was engaged in the most important mitzvoth, שהיה הולך לשחוט את פסחו ולמול את בנו even though לאביו ולאמו לאחיו ולאחותו לא יטמא, אבל מטמא הוא למת מצוה.
V. 8. כל ימי נזרו וגו׳ sums up the whole meaning of Nazaritism, and especially its connection with the law of טומאה which it is to serve to demonstrate (see V.2).

V. 9. בפתע פתאום. In Kerithot 9a פתע is explained as meaning שוגג — unintentional — as in אם בפתע בלא איבה הדפו (Ch. XXXV.22), and פתאום both as אונס — being forced — as in ויאמר ה׳ פתאום אל משה (Ch. 12,4) and also as מזיד as in ערום ראה רעה ונסתר ופתייס עברו ונענשו (Prov. XXII.3) where, as Rashi points out the ונענשו obviously assumes that the procedure of the פתיים could only have been done במזיד (quite intentionally) and therefore the Halacha teaches that the consequences described here in V.9-12 apply also במזיד. So that the Nazarite would be one of those few cases where מביאין על הזדון כשוגג, where an offering has to be brought even where the transgression was done במזיד with full consciousness and intention. Clearly this Halacha looks on the underlying conception of both פתע and פתאום as being derived from פתה, the root of פתה .פתי related to פתח, designates that open-heartedness of inner feelings against which the external consequences can offer no defence. It designates both the lack of experience and insight of judgment as well as lack of caution and circumspection in matters of practical and moral behaviour. פתי יאמין לכל דבר the פתי believes everything (Prov. 14,15), and פתיים עברו ונענשו they transgress the laws of morality even with complete consciousness because they do not consider the consequences. Then פתע is the condition of thoughtlessness which is surprised at results and events which could very well have been foreseen if thought had been given to what was to be expected in accordance with the laws of probability or possibility. So that in moral matters it corresponds completely to the concept שוגג (see Levit. 4,2). פתאום, on the other hand, designates something happening which was quite beyond any expectation regarding which human judgment was altogether פתי and people פתאים, could not have been prepared for by any expectation. It is the sudden surprising event which in moral matters would correspond to the concept אונם. Hence in Is. (XXIX.5, and XXX.13) the combination לפתע פתאום and פתאום לפתע to characterise the collapse of tyranny and wrong, which God brings about. The event in itself is a פתאום, something which lies completely beyond ordinary reckoning, it reveals the Finger of God, and it is all the more weighty as it comes לפתע, so unexpectedly, because the tyrants never even gave a thought to the normal consequences of their tyranny and wrong-doing. Now in the moral sphere the Halacha looks on absolute מזיד also as פתאום, as something which really lies beyond all expectation. For, that a man with full consciousness of its nature and its consequences — for that is the legal conception of מזיד as is shown by התראה — should trangress the Torah does really lie beyond all normal expectation — פתע is subjective, it designates the relation of the consciousness of a person to happenings which occur to him and to actions which he does. But פתאום is objective and designates the nature of an event or an action in itself. So that it can designate equally אונס, the character of a happening that was unexpected neither by the person to whom it occurred nor to occur at all as well as מזיד, the character of a wrongful deed which certainly had been done by the one who did it with complete consciousness, but just because of that, in itself was completely beyond all expectation. Accordingly the Halacha teaches that the term used here, בפתע פתאום includes all three possibilities, מזיד ,שוגג ,אונם. In whatever manner he came into contact with a dead body, whether by being under the same roof (אהל, see Ch. XIX.14) or by touching it, it annuls the period in which he had been observing Nazaritism hitherto, he has to shave his head, תגלחת, bring on offering, קרבן, and start again, as at the beginning of his vow. The Halacha makes one case of אונס an exception to this rule. It is the one where he has touched or been under the same roof as, or stood over a dead body (himself formed the אהל) during the period of His Nazaritism, and this is brought to his knowledge only after he has completed it and brought his offering, as, at the time of the occurrence its presence was unknown to anybody in the world. This case is called טומאת התהום “a טומאה of the depth”, (buried and hidden). Coming to his knowledge after the completion of his Nazarism a טומאת התהום does not act retrospectively to annul his having fulfilled his vow (Nazir 63a). This law of טומאת התהום only applies to נזיר ועושה פסח, to one who has completed his period of Nazaritism, or has brought his פסח offering, and only to טומאת מת but not to other טמאות which could invalidate עושה פסח.

וטמא ראש נזרו. The טומאה-idea conjured up in one’s mind by a dead body is so much in contrast to that which is proclaimed by the growth of hair (V.6) that if this טומאה-idea was not refuted by its completely breaking the Nazaritism which had already been observed would transform the sanctifying consecration of the Nazarite to its opposite. Hence וגלח ראשו ביום טהרתו, after by הזיה בשלישי ובשביעי (Ch. XIX.12) he again enters the state of טהרה (mental purity, I.L.) he has to proclaim, by completely shaving off his “nazarite” hair, the complete cancellation of his previous Nazarite state brought about by the ביום השביעי יגלחנו .טומאה, this he can do on the seventh day, he need not wait for טבילה and הערב שמש to be completely טהור, for this shaving belongs to the expression of doing away with the injury done to his Nazaritism by the טומאה and not to the entry of the status of regained טהרה which the following offerings which can only be brought after הערב שמש on the eighth day, bring. It is different to the second shaving of the מצורע (Levit. XIV.9) which belongs to the reinstallation of טהרה and so can only be done after הערב שמש on the day when the offerings are to be brought.

V. 10.—11. וביום השמיני וגו׳. A טמא מת is not considered, like זב וזבה etc. as belonging to the מחוסרי כפרה whose טהרה for מקדש and קדשים is attached to their bringing the prescribed offerings, but as soon as he has had טבילה ,הזיה שלישי ושביעי and העריב שמש he is טהור for מקדש and קדשים. A Nazarite, too, whose Nazaritism has been interrupted by טומאת מת is טהור for מקדש וקדשים with הערוב שמש of the seventh day, and although he has not brought his offerings is not classed as מחוסרי כפרה in its real sense. Nevertheless regarding the beginning of his fresh period of Nazarism he is considered as a מחוסר כפרה, so that if after העריב שמש and before he has brought his offerings (see below) he had become טמא מת again, the whole is considered as one prolonged טומאה אריכתא and on the second eighth day he has only to bring one קרבן (Nazir 18a & b, and Kerithot 8b). The Nazarite who had become טמא has to bring two doves after his having shaved his head, of which the priest has to offer one as a חטאת (expiation from sin I.L.) and the other as an עולה (an elevation offering I.L.). We already know these birds as the positive expression of טהרה at the transition of the יולדת זב וזבה from the condition of טומאה (Levit. 12,8, XV.14 & 29). They are the symbolic expression of soaring upward to moral freedom and moral perfection which can always be done in spite of the physical lack of freedom to which the physical sides of human beings are subject (חטאת העוף), as well as the energetic perseverance we have to exercise to keep at every spiritual height we have attained, in spite of the depressing compulsion of the physical side of human life (עולת עוף see Levit. on Ch. I.17). So with this positive expression of טהרה the Nazarite starts his fresh period of Nazaritism, וכפר עליו מאשר חטא על הנפש, and thereby, paralysing the טומאה-idea, he declines to have anything to do with everything that he has sinned against the pure Nazarite concept of moral freewill by his contact with a dead body (— חטא, he had sinned against Nazaritism על הנפש by having been next to a dead body of which he had been told על נפש מת לא יבא. For טמא מת is called just הנפש .טמא לנפש the מת מת עליו וגו׳ that of V.9 —). וקדש את ראשו ביום ההוא and thereby he sanctifies his head afresh to Nazaritism on that day, on the eighth, not the seventh which still belonged to laying the טומאה aside. Inasmuch as here the entry of the new Nazaritism is, on the one hand attached to the bringing of the offering and on the other already to the day itself, the Halacha teaches that his new pure Nazaritism does not start only when he has brought all the offerings, the עולה ,חטאת and אשם (V.13) but already as soon as he has brought his חטאת עוף (Nazir 18b).

V. 12. והזיר לה׳ את ימי נזרו וגו׳. He has now to fulfil afresh the days of Nazaritism he had vowed to God, והביא כבש בן שנתו לאשם but has still to bring an אשם for the past. This אשם is clearly and definitely separated from the חטאת and עולה of the previous verse which he has to bring at the same time. In no way does it belong to the offering of birds which introduce the fresh new Nazaritism. That new Nazaritism starts quite independently of this אשם. Before ordering it to be brought it already says וקדש את ראשו ביום ההוא והזיר לה׳ את ימי נזרו, and only then והביא כבש וגו׳ לאשם (Nazir 18b). By its meaning it must rather be in connection with the past, for only following after it does it say of that past והימים הראשנים יפלו, that it is completely shelved. In Levit. we have learned to know אשם as אשם שפחה חרופה ,אשם מעילה ,אשם גזילות ,אשם תלוי ,אשם מצורע, we recognised the common fault for which an אשם had to be brought, egoistic lack of consideration towards people and things which, if unatoned for, would ultimately bring desolation to the person who had selfishly gone the wrong way. All these אשמות, except אשם מצורע consist of an איל for it is sins in the sphere of persons selfishly putting their own interests and power to the fore that are to be atoned for and whose future progress is to be sanctified by being dedicated to duty (see on Levit. V.26 and XIX.21). Only אשם מצורע is a כבש, for it is not egoistic trying to push ahead in social life, but selfish contrast to the laws of society is the character of the unsocial behaviour which the מצורע has been guilty of, and which had brought about the “desolation” which was necessary for his betterment. At his reentry into the social communal life he has to be taught to rank himself as כבש, as a “simple member of God’s flock”, as a simple social member of the whole community “grazing” under the guidance of their Shepherd, and giving up all selfishness and with selfless devotion to the purposes indicated by God, dedicate his “efforts and his goal” to be pleasing to God, and his “achievements and enjoyments” to be priest-like. The נזיר טמא too, we see here appearing like the מצורע, with an אשם, and indeed with a כבש as an אשם as final result of his נזירות טומאה now ended and it is not far-fetched to take the meaning of this אשם in almost the same sense as that of the מצורע re-entering the general society of the community. Of course in the נזור טמא there has been no actual sin or misbehaviour against the social life of the community. But the vow of the Nazarite would appear in itself as an unsociable arrogance, placing himself apart in the midst of the community, were it not that the purpose of spiritually and morally ennobling himself removes the reprehensible semblance. But if this purpose is so frustrated by טומאה that the vow which he has kept up till now is regarded as not having been carried out והימים הראשונים יפלו, then what he had been doing up till now remains as unsocial, purposeless and unjustified making himself superior to and apart from the rest of the community which awaits its atonement in the כבש אשם.

והימים הראשונים יפלו כי טמא נזרו. Only טומאה interrupts the carrying out of the vow of Nazaritism to the extent of making the days already lived as a Nazarite void and necessitating a fresh start, סותרת הכל. But if he sins against the two other prohibitions of Nazaritism, in no case does it do away with the days already lived as a Nazarite. Drinking wine does not discontinue it at all. Cutting off the greater part of his hair, תגלחת רוב ראשו only demands a further continuance of at least thirty days .נזירות (תוספות Nazir 39a ד״ה סתם נזירות) (i.e. if he had vowed to keep 100 days, and he cut the greater part of his hair on the 30th day, as there is still a 30 days growth — the minimum period for the growth to be striking — before the final shaving, it would not prolong the period of his vow I.L.). According to רמב״ם, however, in any case it would prolong the period of his vow by an extra thirty days.

V. 13. וזאת תורת הנזיר. But this is the normal teaching for the Nazarite, i.e. this is what is the normal procedure at the conclusion of the period vowed by the Nazarite. — יביא אתו: himself, a similar expression to: והשיאו אותם עון אשמה in Levit. XXII.10 (פסרי). He has really to bring “himself”, i.e. to place himself before the Sanctuary, himself, with all that he has gained in spiritual and moral strength for his life by the Nazaritism he has kept. Thus he has to place himself at the entry of the Sanctuary of the Torah and

V. 14. והקריב וגו׳ in an offering seeking to get near to God, to express what henceforth the import of his life is to be. In youthful freshness (בן שנה) and in flawless completion of the whole of his self and will (תמים) will he rank himself as a simple member in the great flock of social community guided by their Shepherd (כבש and כבשה) to an energetic life of activity, manfully working his way upward towards God (עולה), keeping in mind his need consciously to keep to the spiritual height he has achieved (חטאת). But the culminating point of the offerings which he has to bring lies in the איל לשלמים. This forms the very opposite to his conception of Nazaritism, which led him to withdraw from the general mass of society, and in such retirement, and in refraining from the more joyful enjoyments of life, to strive to get nearer to his God, in working on his inner self to try to get more spiritual and moral ennoblement of himself. But these efforts directed more to his own inner self were only to be an exceptional educational condition. If his Nazaritism was the true and right one, it should have been only a temporary withdrawal from the social life of the community so that when it is over he can give himself up, with fuller and stronger force, purified and elevated, to carry out the tasks of life indicated by God. And, as he has made himself known by his withdrawal and renunciation he is now to distinguish himself in noble flawless strength (איל תמים) as a model example of how, in the midst of the efforts and aspirations and enjoyments of social communal life, upheld by the עולה and חטאת dedications to a full active and morally pure life, one attains the blissful harmony of a happy life lived in the Presence of God — as is expressed by the typical Jewish offering (שלמים).

In the group of offerings prescribed here, the עולה precedes the חטאת, above in V.11 the order is the reverse. In general חטאת always comes first. Purity from sin is always the preliminiary stage of sanctifying one’s actions. First סור מרע and then עשה טוב. But we find the order changed in the prescriptions of the Torah, as it is in these two verses here. So also in Levit. V.7, והביא וגו׳ אחד לחטאת ואחד לעולה, and then in XII.8 אחד לעולה ואחד לחטאת. Also previously in V.6. כבש וגו׳ לעולה ובן יונה וגו׳ לחטאת and then in XIV.22, אחד חטאת והאחד עולה. Where the חטאת refers back to a חטא actually committed the stress is on the חטאת and that then is to be brought first. Thus at קרבן עולה ויורד and מצורע and also at נזיר טמא V.11. But where no actual sin has been committed and the חטאת is only the expression of the undertaking of future firmness in the avoidance of sinning, there the stress is in עולה to which is then attached the precautionary חטאת which is then brought after it. Thus at יולדת and here. According to this it would be characteristic that at the מלואים of Aaron prescribed in Deut. IX.2, the חטאת came first whereas at the מלואים of the Levites in Numb. VIII.8 the עולה took precedence. This confirms the way the sages take the עגל בן בקר לחטאת of Aaron in Levit. IX.2 to refer to the sin of the golden calf. But this was just the event at which the Levites proved their spotless faithfulness and devotion which indeed formed the reason for their being chosen later on. In contrast to that of Aaron, their חטאת מלואים referred only to the future and hence came after the עולה. Then herein could be found an explanation for two things that are striking at the מלואים of the Levites. There, in V.8 the עולה is not explicitly mentioned and the פר, although a חטאת חצונית was not given for Aaron and his sons to be eaten. The former probably forbearingly only to hint at the contrast to Aaron, and the latter because, like at the פרים הנשרפים, for just this חטאת there was no priest there (see on Levit. VIII.8).

V. 15. וסל מצות. As is evident from V.17, this basket of unleavened bread is in connection with the איל שלמים. Apart from the acknowledging dedication to God of one’s possessions of food, of comfort, of joy by the מנחה ונסכים which always accompany the devotion of one’s person and life vowed by עולה and שלמים — and which here too were not to be missing, as it says at the end of the verse ומנחתם ונסכיהם — here, by the סל המצות, yet another expression of his relation to the possessions of his life is given to the איל-vow of the Nazarite to live a model influential שלמים-life of happiness granted by God, and dedicated to God. (cf. the מלואים of the priests, Ex. XXIX.2). For, in contrast to the anomaly of Nazaritism, when he returns to full communal life the whole normal life with all the godly relationships to holiness with which it is impregnated is to be brought to the mind of the Nazarite. Amongst these relationships which are awaiting a correct estimation the relationship to the material possessions which form the external measure of our happiness in life is by no means the least to be considered. The סל המצות represents these completely. In the “basket of mazzo-bread everything that we possess of the material means for happiness finds its representation. Everything should be and remain “mazzo” in our hands, should bear for us the stamp of our lack of self-dependence and our dependence on God, and it is significant that the contents of this basket are limited to בלולות בשמן and מרבכת .רקוקי מצות משוחים בשמן is missing, the rich, artistic oil-bread of the תודה and of the מלואים of the priests. That high standard of artistic good living as is represented by מרבכת in addition to the חלה-bread soaked in the oil of good living in opulence, and the thin mazzoth just painted over with oil of limited means does not belong to the normal goal of the efforts of God-serving people to which the attention of the Nazarite is now to be directed. The feeling of שלמים and the happiness of שלמים does not necessitate the rich artistic bread of life. Sufficient food and a greater or lesser degree of comfort and prosperity are included in the שלמים-mood of normal life and these are what are represented in the Nazir-basket, (Menachoth 19a).

ומנחתם ונסכיהם, the usual מנחות ונסכים belonging to עולה and שלמים had to be specially mentioned here, as one might have thought that the special סל המצות would have displaced them, מפני שהיה בכלל ויצא לידון בלחם (ספרי) החזירו הכתוב לכללן in accordance with the hermeneutic rule: כל דבר שהיה בכלל ויצא לידון בדבר החדש אי אתה יכול להחזירו לכללו עד שיחזרנו הכתוב לכללו בפרוש.

V. 17. מלמד שהסל בא חובה לאיל ושחיטת ;ואת האיל וגוי על סל המצות איל מקדשן, the basket of mazzos is an essential appendage to the ram, and the mazzos in the basket receive their קדושה, their sanctification, at the moment the ram is slaughtered, and their קדושה is conditional on the slaughter of the ram being correctly performed (Menachoth 46b). In the ram, the person whom it represents has to think of himself in connection with his material means of existence and comfort, and to include them in the giving up selfishly living for himself and devoting himself selflessly to God which is symbolised by the שחיטה. The קדושה, the sanctity of our daily bread is dependent on our עולה, on our giving ourselves up entirely, in every phase of our life, to strive upwards, to keep the fires of godliness burning on earth — ועשה וגו׳ את מנחתו ואת נסכו. The סלת בלולה בשמן of the מנחת נסכים is given over entirely to the Altar-fire, and the whole of the wine is poured down from the top of the Altar into the foundations of the Altar. These two acts express the vow that the whole of our existence, and all our comforts in life are to further godliness on earth to give satisfaction to God, and all the joys of our life shall serve to give joy to our Creator, in the building up of His children on earth (the Altar, as always, being considered Man’s efforts to raise the earth upwards towards heaven I.L.). The giving up of all our earthly existence and our joys in life to God incidentally forms the priestly dedication and the priestly nature of our enjoying our daily bread, as comes to be expressed symbolically by the treatment of the סל המצות in verses 19 and 20.

V. 18. וגלח הנזיר וגו׳. The shaving of the hair ordered here and then placing it on the fire which is cooking the שלמים meal forms the most striking expression of the meaning of the Nazaritism just ended, and of its value only being relative to the happy life to be lived henceforth before God. His life as a Nazarite was only to have been a preparatory provisional training. If letting the hair grow was the sign of a sanctifying separation and withdrawal into oneself (v.5), the complete shaving is the expression of thenceforth ceasing this separation and thenceforth completely entering again the whole social life of the community. This completely entering into the whole social life of the community is not merely something permissible, it is just Mitzva, duty. And so much does a happy life enjoyed in the שלמים sense transcend in value and importance a life merely lived in guarding the power of one’s senses by renunciation and absteniousness in Nazaritism, so much has the latter only value if it leads to the former, that, for the holy שלמים offering, the hitherto untouched hair of the Nazarite’s head is given over to the razor and is then placed in the fire under the pot in which the meal-of-peace-offering is being cooked in a holy place. Thereby Nazaritism subordinates itself to the שלמים spirit and the שלמים life as means to the end. — פתח אהל מועד: not actually in the entrance to the Sanctuary but at its opened doors, at a time when the doors of the Sanctuary are open for bringing his שלמים offering, which may only be offered with the doors of the Sanctuary open (Levit. 3,2, Nazir 45a).

V. 19. הזרוע ,הזרוע .ולקח הכהן וגו׳ are the two upper joints of the right foreleg corresponding to the two upper joints of the right hindleg which form the שוק הימין which, together with the חזה, the breast, are normally given to the priest from every שלמים offering (Chulin 134b). The חזה ושוק are given to the priest raw, here at the ram of the Nazarite the זרוע is added, but that is given בשלה, it is only cut off and given to the priest after the cooking is completed. According to one opinion in Chulin 98b, בשלה means complete אין בשלה אלא שלימה (probably from שלה to be complete, unabridged, undisturbed, as אויבה שלו in Lament. 1,5, שלה accordingly, unabridged. בשלה in a complete condition), but the general way of taking it is בשלה the fem. of בשל, cooked, from ובשל מבושל במים ,בשל, in Ex. 12,9 but even according to the other opinion, the זרוע of the ram of the Nazarite was only to be given cooked. The difference between חזה ושוק and זרוע בשלה could well be taken to be:- חזה ושוק are retained for the priest from the sacrificial animal meant to be eaten by the בעלים. The בעלים only receive it back for their own enjoyment after they have dedicated their thinking and feelings (חזה) and their active efforts (שוק) to the Divine Torah represented by the priests. But זרוע בשלה comes to the כהן from the animal which is already prepared in its entirety for the בעלים to enjoy for themselves. It is a participation of the priest in the שלמים meal of the בעלים. It belongs, as it were, to their enjoyment, they would not really be happy if they did not care for the כהן with their זרוע, But זרוע is everywhere the organ of power and hence is the symbolic expression of it. The זרוע is the מושל over that which the שוק had striven for. So that זרוע belongs completely to the sphere of thought of the איל representing having striven for and possessing riches and influential leading position. If then the Nazarite, before enjoying his איל שלמים meal has to give the priest his זרוע, he is taught thereby, both that exercising his power of influencing and setting the lead with all that God grants him, has simply and only the one purpose of keeping up the Torah of God represented by the priest, that our זרוע should be the זרוע התורה, as well as that we can only enjoy that which God grants us in the שלמים spirit before God if we are conscious that our זרוע includes the זרוע of the Torah, that our success must include the success of the Torah of God represented by the כהן.

Inasmuch as here the זרוע which may only be eaten by the כהנים is cooked together with the rest of the meat to be eaten by the בעלים accordingly איסור (for זרים) together with היתר, this is taken in Chulin 98, a & b, as the classical example of בטול איסור בששים.

ונתן וגו׳ אחר התגלחו את נזרו וגו׳. Only after he has laid aside his elapsed isolation by תגלחת does the priest give him the זרוע בשלה and חלה מצה אחת and רקיק מצה אחד, and together with the חזה ושוק, makes him do the symbolic actions of תנופה and תרומה before God in the east of the forecourt opposite the Holy of Holies. Not in isolation, only in complete participation in the whole social life of the community does the Sanctuary recognise justification for one’s own individual feelings and strivings (חזה ושוק) and the exercise of one’s own power (זרוע); justification for using one’s own means of existence and well-being even in the service of God (חלת מצה ורקיק מצה). Only in complete union with the social community do all these matters of our own lives and endeavours receive their meaning of being really dedicated to, and their importance for, heaven and earth (מעלה ומוריד) and for God’s communities on earth (מוליך ומביא); only in complete union with the social community do they become a holy thing, a Sanctuary directed to the Torah, קדש הוא לכהן. And only then: ואחר ישתה הנזיר יין, does the Nazarite re-enter a full normal joyous life.

Nevertheless it is taught in Nazir 46a, that carrying out this procedure is מצוה (a duty I.L.) but not מעכב (a sine qua non I.L.) but if it had been interrupted or suspended, already after offering the first offering the Nazarite could drink wine, and was not restricted in matters of טומאת מת.

V. 21. ואת תורת וגו׳ מלבד וגו׳ כן יעשה על תורת נזרו. This is what is prescribed to the Nazarite for the conclusion of the period of his vow. But thereby he is perfectly at liberty, apart from, and in addition to, these prescribed offerings, to give expression to any of his special thoughts, feelings, aspirations and vows by עולות ושלמי נדר ונדבה.

If we consider the whole of this institution of Nazaritism we see that the way is open, and it is permitted for any individual among the people to satisfy his urge for spiritual and moral ennoblement, to raise himself temporarily to a priestly, yea a highpriestly position in which his efforts to get nearer God show themselves essentially in his keeping afar from טומאת מת. So that it clearly corresponds to the שילוח טמא מת out of the מחנה שכינה.
Accordingly the three סוטה ,גזל הגר :פרשיות and נזיר looked at in conjunction with the preceding פרשת שלוח מחנה give us the parallel thoughts:
שלוח מצורע out of מחנה ישראל finds its concrete realisation in פרשת גזל דגר the institution which proclaims the Presence of God in the social life of the nation.
שלוח זב וזבה out of מחנה לויה finds its concrete realisation in פרשת סוטה, the institution which proclaims the Presence of God in the chaste sexual life of the family.

שלוח טמא מת out of מחנה שכינה finds its concrete realisation in פרשת נזיר, the institution which proclaims the Presence of God for every individual striving upwards to God in spiritual and moral sanctification.
All three impress on society, family, and individual the stamp of being holy to God.

V. 23. דבר אל אהרן וגו׳. It is not the authority to bless the children of Israel which is here conferred to the Aaronides, but a duty which is given them to perform. The blessing of the priests does not flow from their well-wishing, their benevolence but it is part and parcel of their service to the Sanctuary. This service is defined in Deut. 10,8 as לעמד לפני ה׳ לשרתו ולברך בשמו (“to stand and perform the service (the offerings) in the Sanctuary and to pronounce the blessing in His Name” I.L.). And again ibid. XXI,5: כי בם בחר ה׳ אלקיך לשרתו ולברך בשם ה׳. So that ברכת כהנים belongs to שרת and is closely associated with it. The priest stands in service before God and pronounces the blessing in His Name and at His bidding. Hence only בעבודה at the conclusion of bringing all the offerings, did the priest have to pronounce the blessing — just as it says of Aaron in Levit. 9,22, וישא אהרן את ידו אל העם ויברכם וירד מעשת החטאת והעולה והשלמים. And also בגבולין, when the people came together for prayers outside the Sanctuary, and still today in our prayer-gatherings, ברכת כהנים, the blessing by the priests, must always be attached to עבודה (the prayer beginning with רצה I.L.) and כל כהן שאינו עולה בעבודה שוב אינו עולה, any כהן who does not start moving towards the raised platform (דוכן) on which the priests are to pronounce the blessing, while the reader was still reciting the prayer for the רצה) עבודה) may not take part in pronouncing the blessing that time (Sota 38b). As accordingly ברכת כהנים belongs to שרת and is a part of the עבודה, the priestly blessing has entirely the character of all עבודה-procedures, its meaning lies in its objective prescribed contents, and the ministering priest who pronounces it is nothing but the appointed instrument through which, in the Sanctuary the act, here the word, receives its significant expression. The stamp which the death of the first noblest youthful priests placed on all עבודה, namely, that only the “prescribed” act is true עבודה, true “service”, but that every idea chosen of one’s own free-will, אשר לא צוה, which God has not prescribed is זרה, the opposite of a God-serving procedure, that stamp applies also, in full measure, to כה תברכו את בני ישראל .ברכת כהנים runs the command כה, “thus”, in the prescribed words, in the prescribed manner “have ye to bless the children of Israel”. And the traditional Halacha is taught in Sota 38a ,בלשון הזה :כה בלשת הקדש, in the same words in the original language; בעמידה, standing, expressing service; בנשיאת כפים with raised hands, raised upwards towards God (see V.27), not with horizontally outstretched hands as if they themselves were bestowing the blessing: פנים כנגד פנים, face to face with the congregation; בקול רם in a loud voice. The priestly blessing has no magic force lying in the priests or in the formulae. The appropriation by those to be blessed is an essential part of the blessing, yea, it is that which really makes it into one (see V.27). The prescriptions בלשון הקדש ,בעמידה בקול רם ,פנים כנגד פנים and not בלחש quietly, all lie simply in the word “כה״. Just as I transmit the command to you in the name of God, so have you to fulfil it in the name of God (לבוש א״ח 128). Finally אמור להם: You have to tell them, referred to the priests in Sota 38a; just as you, Moses, are to give the order to Aaron and his sons to pronounce the blessing, so always in every single case only when the demand is made is the blessing to take place, otherwise the priests have not the duty nor the authorisation to pronounce the blessing. The demand has to be made to them in a loud voice by the representative of the requirements of the congregation (,הזן הכנסת חזן in the sense in which it is used in the Talmud, the superintendent or beadle of the synagogue המתעסק בצרכי בית הכנסת or שמש הכנסת, not to be confused with שליח צבור, the שץ, the reader who represents the Congregation in prayer, תוספות Berachoth 34a. If nowadays this demand is made by the reader, he still does this only by delegation as חזן: in the name of the congregation), and indeed after the first word has been pronounced in response to this demand, every succeeding word of the blessing (according to our custom even the first word too) is dictated to the priests, and they have only to repeat the blessing which is dictated to them by the representative of the congregation which is to be blessed, and according to Maimonides הל׳ תפלה XIV.13 this belongs to the carrying out of the command in the Torah אמור להם. According to this, our priests in pronouncing the blessing are a completely passive instrument. Only in reply to the summons of the congregation and only in the blessing dictated to them by the representative of the congregation do they pronounce it. So that in truth it is the congregation which has the blessing precribed by God pronounced over itself through their mouths.

The summons “כהן״ is not made to a single priest, ,לשנים קורא כהן ולאחד אינו קורא כהן (Sota 38c). Possibly calling on one man to pronounce the blessing might easily invest that single personality with the appearance of an overweening semblance of lustre, and perhaps that is the reason why the call “כהן״ was to be omitted. The passivity demanded by the אמור להם would, in any case, be impressed on the individual priest too by יברכך being dictated to him (see מ״א on א״ח 128, 13). (According to some opinions the command of ברכת כהנים is not given at all מן התורה to a single כהן).
Onkelos too takes the אמור להם to refer to the priests: כד יימרון להון (see above).

V. 24. יברכך וגו׳. As this יברכך is complemented by וישמרך, the blessing pronounced here would primarily refer to such possessions which, once they have been granted, still require שמירה, protection, that they remain “kept” for us, that having them tends to our true happiness. Thus the ספרי also takes it (Deut. 28,3) בברכה המפורשת ברוך אתה בעיר וברוך אתה בשדה ברוך טנאך ומשארתך וגו׳ יברכך ה׳ בנכסים וישמרך בנכסים, וישמרך בגוף, וישמרך מיצר הרע, וישמרך שלא ישלטו אחרים עליך, וישמרך מן המזיקים.. Accordingly the prosperity of all bodily and material possessions, and protection from all spiritual and material injuries form the contents of this first sentence of blessing.

V. 25. יאר וגו׳. Cf. בעמוד אש להאיר להם (Ex. 13,21), להאיר להם את הדרך (Neh. 6,12) האירו ברקים תבל (Ps. 77,19) יא[[illegible]]רו ברקיו תבל (ibid. XCVII,4) where האיר means to illuminate something, to make it light so that it can be seen. Thus in Ps. 76,5 נאור אתה referring to God when He has become apparent, visible by the Almighty deeds of His Rule. The events of the world cast their rays back onto their Causer, and show Him in the greatness and almighty power of His Management. פני ה׳ are “what God looks towards”, the purpose He achieves by His Management, and which He wishes to see accomplished by the free-willed acts of human beings called on to serve Him. Thus it says in Ps. 139,15. צדק ומשפט מכון כסאך חסד ואמת יקדמו פניך “Righteousness and justice are that on which the Throne of God rests, love and truth are that to which His Countenance is directed”.

חנן we have already recognised on Gen. 6,7 from its relation to ענן and הנן as being the granting of somebody’s wishes which they deserve. As the complementary sentence to the preceding, יאר וגו׳ is the granting of the knowledge and understanding of the required spiritual gifts for our satisfying the demands which our being placed in the light of פני ה׳ demands. יאר ה׳ פניו אליך would accordingly mean:- May God reveal to you the purposes of His Management and His goal to be achieved through you — the former through the words of His prophets, the latter through the words of His Torah, — ויחנך and may He equip you with the spiritual intellectual abilities to understand the revelations contained in תורה and נבואה to gather from them insight in His Management in history and of your own mission and tasks in life. Thus also in יאר זה מאור תורה, שנא׳ כי נר מצוה :ספרי וו.ורה אור, ויחנך יחנך בתלמוד תורה, ויחונך בדעת בבינה ובהשכל ובמוסר ובחכמה. Thus also in מ׳ רבות with incidental reference to the use of חנינה in prayers for the granting of mental gifts, ויחנך, הרי הם מבורכים ושמורים ושכינה ביניהם ומנין אף חנונים בדעת ובבינה תלמוד לומר ויחונך כמה דתימא דמצלינן אתה חונן לאדם דעת לאנוש בינה.

It is on the granting of this intellectual blessing that Ps. LXVII looks, and recognises in Israel’s enlightened outlook on the ways of God on earth (דרך ה׳ includes both, the ways of God’s Management and Rule, and the ways of duty which God has indicated we are to tread) the means for the general enlightenment of the whole of mankind: אלקים יחננו ויברכנו יאר פניו אתנו סלה לדעת בארץ דרכך בכל גוים ישועתך יודוך עמים אלקים יודוך עמים כלם ישמחו וירננו לאמים כי תשפוט עמים מישור ולאומים בארץ תנחם סלה וגו׳ וגו׳.
The whole psalm is a commentary on our verse.

V. 26. ישא וגו׳. The expression -נשא פנים אל does not occur elsewhere referring to God. In מ׳ רבות the explanation is given יהפך פניו כלפי אצלך, as it says in Levit. 26,9 ופניתי אליכם so that it would be a way of saying יפנה ה׳ אליך. And actually there too אליכם introduces a zenith of the Divine promises of blessing (see notes there). So Onkelos takes it also: יסב ה׳ אפיה לותך. There, an abundance of blessings had already been promised, fertility, peace and victory, on which then follows ופניתי אליכם which can only indicate nothing other than a still more intimate personal relation of God and His Management to the personal factors of individual and communal life which then reaches its very summit in והתהלכתי בתוככם ונתתי משכני בתוככם. Here, too, material and spiritual blessing, and indeed, by the generality of the expression in which the blessings are worded, to the most comprehensive degree, has already been pronounced. To that then ישא ה׳ is now attached, and that expresses the highest final result of blessing which is to crown the fulfillment of the preceding ,יאר יברכך. It is the most intimate, most personal nearness of God. It is attained when all the material and spiritual possessions and gifts which are granted by God are directed and used, in the sense of the enlightened knowledge of the Will of God, entirely solely for the realisation and furthering of the godly purposes revealed by God. The nearness of God is not to be desired for receiving in it and through it material and intellectual blessings. But all material and spiritual blessing is only desirable for using it in the ways indicated by God to become worthy of the nearness of God. קרבת אלקים nearness of God is טוב in itself, is the absolute good (Ps. 73,28).

The פנים in ישא וגו׳, taken as in יאר וגו׳ would express this most intimate relationship of God even more closely, thus:- if, by the intellectual gifts granted to you, you bring the purposes of God to being clearly and truly understood, and by the material means granted to you, to being truly accomplished, then God will let you see all the purposes of His Management in nature and history. Then through you an existence and a development of such a God-serving circle on earth will have been made into a reality, which will be a result in which all the purposes of God’s Rule on earth meet; ישא ה׳ פניו אליך may God direct His attention to making you a goal of His Management of the world — וישם לך שלום, and whereas it seems as if you, by directing your endeavours to God, and solely to God, and He, by apparently directing His Management solely to you, isolate yourself quite alone with Him, in fact, it is just you to whom God שם שלום, ensures the highest degree of harmonious living. If you are only a true servitor of God with all your physical and spiritual powers, so that God can see in you the goal of all His ultimate aims being made a reality, then all those that are sensitive and thoughtful around you will feel that you complement their existence, and every breath that a true God-serving man draws strikes a harmonious chord with every phase of the universe.

V. 27. ושמו את שמי וגו׳. The priests do not bless Israel, their words have no power of conferring blessing, their mission is only לשום שמי על בני ישראל, the blessing itself I look after, ואני אברכם. To “lay” the name of God impressively on Israel, to make Israel the bearers of God’s Name, to impress the name “God” on every phase of Israel, to proclaim that Israel looks to God, and to God alone for all protection, all revelation, all gifts, all elevation and all peace, and expects it from Him in such a manner that this blessing and protection, this revelation and granting of gifts, this elevation and peace will all in itself constitute a “Name of God”, will itself be a revelation of God’s acts, as He Himself has said (Ex. 20,23) לא תעשון אתי וגו׳ בכל המקום אשר וגו׳, that not in images, but in the blessing which He sends to us, there would His Presence be evident, thus He wished His Name to be proclaimed. For this proclamation of God’s Name over Israel, for that, the priest is to be the instrument, to be the instrument for a nation that is to be blessed; then God will bless them.

The ברכת כהנים in the מקדש differed from that outside the מלדש in that: בכדינה אומר אותה ג׳ ברכות ובמקדש ברכה אחת במקדש אומר את השם ככתבו ובמדינה בכינויו במדינה כהנים נושאים את ידיהם כנגד כתפותיהן ובמקדש על גבי ראשיהן (Sota 37b). Outside the Sanctuary the ברכת כהנים was said in three separate verses, as it is done today in our synagogue, in the Sanctuary the three verses were said together as one verse. In the Sanctuary the Name of God was spoken as it is actually written, outside the Sanctuary only in its attributive form (אדני). Outside the Sanctuary the priests raised their hands only to the height of their shoulders, within it, above their heads.

The reason given there on 40b, for the three verses being said in the Sanctuary together as one verse is:- לפי שאין עונין אמן במקדש, because ברכות in the Sanctuary were never responded to by “Amen”. In its place the congregation said: ברוך שם כבוד מלכותו לעולם ועד (Blessed be the name of the glory of His Kingdom to the appointed hidden future I.L.), and indeed, as seems in accordance with the wording in Thaanit 16b, at the end of every ברכה in lieu of “Amen” (not, as תוספות suggests as “possible”, immediately when the name of God was pronounced). It says there, referring to the והן עונין אחריו ב׳ש׳כ׳מ׳ל׳ו׳ :מקדש in exactly the same wording as it says referring to בגבולין (anywhere outside the והן עונין אחריו אמן :(מקדש. The fact that those assembled in the Sanctuary do not say “Amen” to the ברכות said by the reader, but associate themselves to the ברכה by ב׳ש׳כ׳מ׳ל׳ו׳, is repeatedly referred to in Nehemiah 9,5. where the assembly is admonished קומו ברכו את ה׳ אלקיכם מן העולם עד העולם and directed to God, correspondingly admonished with: ויברכו שם כבודך ומרומם על כל ברכה ותהלה. The commentator ר׳ אליהו ingeniously explains this at the end of the Jerusalmi Talmud Berachot: מנין שלא היו עונין אמן במקדש ת״ל קומו ברכו וגו׳: משמע כלם היו מן המברכים ולא היו בהן שאינו מברך אלא עונה אמן ש״מ שהמברך אומר בא״י וכו׳ והעונים בשכמל״ו וה״ל שפיר כולן מברכין. Outside the Sanctuary the reader says the ברכה primarily on behalf of the assembled congregation, that they should appropriate it to themselves and make it as if they had said it. That is the purpose of having it said out loud by the reader, and this appropriation is accomplished by “Amen” (see above V.22). But what is spoken in the Sanctuary is spoken for the whole nation, is of national import, exactly as the Sanctuary itself, and the offerings at which the ברכות are said, have only a completely national character. Whatever was said in the Sanctuary was altogether nothing but expressing in words that which was in the Sanctuary or acts which were performed there, for the minds, the consciousness of the entire nation. Therefore no “Amen” was to be pronounced in the Sanctuary. Every “Amen” would have given that which was said for the most general application the appearance of being limited to a negligable fraction of the nation. But those who are present are rather to join themselves to the idea that what is being said is on behalf of the whole nation, and what has been said loses nothing of the character of being meant for universal application.

ברכת כהנים too, in the מקדש is not said, as in בגבולין, for the limited circle of the fraction of the nation who are attending that particular service, so ברכת כהנים also should not there be given the appearance of that limited application by “Amen”. And for the same reason, because, in the ,מקדש ברכת כהנים also, and especially ברכת כהנים, is meant to reach far beyond the confines of the building, because in ברכת כהנים the Mikdosh-thought is expressed for the whole nation, yea, in its ultimate meaning, for all humanity, and the underlying thought is then in reality one single all-comprising שלום one. That is why there ברכת כהנים is said as one single ברכה. For, at the very first glance one can see how the three sentences are nothing but expressing in words what מקדש וכליו, the Sanctuary itself and its contents, represent. יאר ,יברכך and ישא correspond to the ideas of the מנורה ,שולחן and יברכך .ארון places, like the שולחן, the material wellbeing, יאר, like the מנורה, the mental enlightenment of the nation under the dispensation and care of God, and ישא, like the ארון and כפרת completely expresses the Presence of God everywhere where everything material and spiritual — מנורה-יאר ,שולחן-יברכך — is combined to realise and accept the revealed Will of God — ארון. Just as the cardinal-point of the Sanctuary lay in the ארון to which the שולחן and מנורה were subordinate as preparations, so is ישא the gravamen of the ברכת כהנים in the Sanctuary, to which יברכך and יאר are attached as antecedent clauses, and in the Sanctuary ברכת כהנים says: May God give thee blessing and protection, light and endowments and then let His Presence be near unto thee and grant thee everlasting peace. Of course, outside the Sanctuary, where it is a matter of these blessings being made into a reality (not as inside the Sanctuary, where the ideal is always presented I.L.), of striving up to this goal of the blessings by the individual circles and ranks of the nation, there every sector of this blessing must be separately brought to the minds of the people.
