The congregation striving for the blessing must first associate themselves by saying “Amen” with the idea of looking only to God for material blessings and care, and then to agree by saying “Amen” that the only way to allay the longing for peace and to be sure of getting it is by securing the Presence of God. ברכת מזנים בגבולין and ברכת מהנים במקדש in this are related to each other similarly to the תפלין של יד and the תפילין של ראש (where the paragraphs are divided in the one and joined in the other I.L.) see on Deut. 6,8).

If this way of taking it be not erroneous, the question raised by תוספות in Sota 40b. ד״ה כל כך, could be answered:- because always in the Sanctuary אמן was not said and therefore what was pronounced there was not limited to those present, the ברכת כהנים there was only one ברכה so that if those present were to make a response, it could only be at the conclusion of the third sentence. According to רמב״ם at the end they said ברוך ה׳ אלקי ישראל מן העולם עד העולם, according to others ברוך ש׳כ׳מ׳ל׳ו׳ and thus associated themselves with the ברכה-promise (Hirsch explains elsewhere that our blessing God is an undertaking on our part to use that to which the blessing refers to give Him satisfaction, as having free-will, it is within our powers to further or thwart His Will I.L.) regarding the awaited blessing from Him. This need not exclude the possibility envisaged by הוספות that, similarly to the service on the Day of Atonement, here, too, at each mention of the Name of God, those present said ב׳ש׳כ׳מ׳ל׳ו׳.

Corresponding to this would be the fact that in the Sanctuary at ברכת כהנים the four-lettered Name of God was said as it is written, while elsewhere it was pronounced only in the attribute of אדנות. There the whole act is a pronouncement of the ideal, the whole concept of the מקדש is expressed by it. Here, it is something to be taken up, to be apprehended, and the Name of God also is given in the form under which we are to think of Him. Finally בגבולין the כהנים raise their hands only to the height of their shoulders, in the מקדש they stretch them up above their heads. In the Sanctuary the idea had to be countered that the Presence of God was only to be found there in the Temple. That was why the hands of the priests pointed to God high up in the heights, towards God in the universe, Whose “throne is the heaven and Whose footstool is the earth”. But outside the Temple the thought is to be animated that here too is God’s Presence, that מלא כל הארץ כבודו, that שכינה למעלה מראשינו, that God’s Presence is here just above our head wherever we are, infinitely near to us, and just where Man’s kingdom ends that of God begins (Kidushin 31a) so just up to their shoulders rise the hands of the priests directed to God.
Finally let us consider פרשת ברכת כהנים in connection with the preceding פרשיות, then
יברכך is the ברכה to be realised in the מחנה ישראל.
יאר is the ברכה to be realised primarily in ,מחנה לויה
ישא is the ברכה to be realised in the מחנה שכינה: thereby these three מחנות of the Jewish People form the uniform fundamental idea of placing these different laws togther: —
שילוח מחנה
גזל הגר סוטה נזיר
ברכת כהנים.

V. 1. At the beginning of this fourth book we have already remarked how the whole contents of the third book were attached to the erection of the Sanctuary with which the second book concluded, inasmuch as they taught the laws of holy living which the Sanctuary and the “Evidence for the Torah” to which it was erected set as the task of our lives. Now this fourth book has for its contents the relationship and the behaviour of the nation towards this Sanctuary of the Torah. The first six chapters had shown the whole nation in its members, families and tribes called upon individually by counting each member, to serve the purposes of the Sanctuary. Then, in their original allotted closer or more distant positions — כהנים ,לוים ,ישראל — with the Sanctuary as their common centre point, had represented the effect of this holy centre point on its national tricircular surrounding (symbolically in שלוח מחנות and concretely in סוטה ,גזל הגר and נזיר). And finally the promise that by the erection of the Sanctuary with its contents the proof of God’s Presence would be shown by the national blossoming prosperity was to be declared daily by the priestly blessing ברכת כהנים.

Now this seventh chapter goes back a little to the day already mentioned in Ex. 40,17, as the day of the definite erection of the Sanctuary, the 1st of Nisan of the 2nd year, and which had been referred to again in Levit. 9,1. The beginning of this book had only passed over it by a month to complete and perfect, by counting, grouping and positioning, the orders and regulations for the various groups which were brought about by the erection of the Sanctuary. Now this chapter goes back to that day of the erection of the Sanctuary to inform us how, even before the edict of these regulations was given, how at once on the very day the Sanctuary was erected the princes of the tribes of the nation understood their position towards the Sanctuary and in what way they showed that understanding and their feelings.

ויהי ביום כלות משה להקים וגוי. See on Ex. 40,17, -8. — וימשח אתו see on Ex. 30,23-29 — וימשחם ויקדש אתם, this repetition is explained in ספרי thus: וימשח אתו ויקדש אותו ואת כל כליו שומע אני ראשון ראשון שנמשח היה קדוש ת״ל וימשחם ויקדש אותם מגיד שלא קדש אחד מהם עד שנמשחו כולם. The משיחת וקדושת of אותו ואת כל כליו was only completed when וימשחם ויקדש אותם i.e. the sanctification of any part of the Sanctuary was only accomplished by the sanctification of the whole. The sanctification of the whole Sanctuary formed one idea which as a whole confirmed sanctity on the meaning of every separate part. Each part by itself, lacking combination to the rest, is not fit to be the symbolic bearer of the sanctity which it is its function to represent. The sanctity of each part is dependent on the complemented attachment to it of all the other parts. And equally so the whole can not do without even its least important part. Nothing is superfluous for the whole, nothing is without meaning. All together it is a concrete representation of the sentence: ועשו לי מקדש ושכנתי בתוכם. But just as a sentence can not miss one word, one syllable, one letter, but on the other hand, no letter no syllable, no word by itself conveys any meaning, so is the Sanctuary the symbolism of a whole sentence in which the whole can not do without any part and no part without the whole.

אתו ואת כל כליו ואת המזבח ואת כל כליו, here the Sanctuary as a whole is designated in its two principle parts: משכן וכל כליו represents the task the mission, חצר) מזבח וכל כליו), the way to accomplish it.

V. 2. ויקריבו וגוי. The object of ויקריבו is קרבנם in the next verse what it really wants to say is: ויקריבו ויביאו את קרבנם וגוי. The sentence is interrupted to give a more detailed description of the subject of the sentence, the נשיאי ישראל. They were the נשיאי ישראל, Israel’s “bearers who had been raised”, the men by their position stood at the height of the national mission and from that position were to elevate the nation, to equal height. They were the ראשי בית אבותם, the heads of the paternal homes: בית אב are the families united by descent from one ancestor to tribal union. These prominent men, conspicuous as the נשיאי ישראל were those who, by their personality and social character had been accorded confidence, and exerted influence within the united families of the tribe, and were called upon to represent the interests of their tribe in all national matters which affected the tribe. On the strength of this dual character, as נשיאי ישראל and ראשי בית אבותם they were the most fitting to be נשיאי המטות. The tribe, called בית אב after its internal formation is called nationally מטה as a “branch” of the great national tree, which as such, growing out of the common root and the common trunk has to guide and retain the common national spirit over the speciality of the tribe’s peculiar characteristics, and make the common mission of the nation a reality within the special characteristics of the tribe. As נשיאי ישראל of the nation and as ראשי בית אבתם, belonging to the speciality of their tribes, they were called upon as ראשי המטות to represent the common national interests within their special tribe, hence they were also הם העומדים על הפקודים they, who, a month later had to assist taking the census of the individuals for the whole nation after families and tribes. (See on Ch. 1, 2-4).

V. 3. ויביאו את קרבנם. We have already remarked on Levit. 1, 2, that everything by which one seeks to get near to God is called קרבן. These wagons too, were a gift that showed by the purpose for which they were given, the disposition of the giver to be striving upwards to God. ,עגלת צב צב occurs again in Is. LXVI.20, as a means of transport. Phonetically related to סבב it could indicate a surround on all sides of the wagon by which people or articles placed in the wagon are protected. Here for the transport of the uncovered parts of the Tabernacle such a covering was indispensable. Onkelos takes it also as מהפין (covered wagon). These wagons they brought as נשיאי ישראל, as the heads of the nation as a whole. They proved thereby that the nation considered the sanctuary of the Torah as a national treasure which the nation had to carry with it on all their wanderings as the soul which gives life to the body. That they presented these wagons for the sacred objects in their capacity of נשיאי ישראל and not as ואשי בית אבותם or נשיאי המטות showed itself by two tribes joining together for each wagon and its team of oxen. So that none of them made the presentation for his own tribe alone. ויקריבו אותם לפני המשכן: מלמד שהביאום ומסרום לציבור, they made the wagons public property. (מדרש רבות).

V. 9. כי עבודת הקדש עליהם, in contrast to עבדת אהל מועד of V.5 They had the service of the קדש in its real narrower sense. The objects which they had in their charge were the real objects for which the אהל מועד had been ercted. They are the real sacred objects through which all the other holy objects received their holiness. They are the קדש of the ,קדשים קדש הקדשים as they are called in Ch. 4,4. They are that קדש in which the whole of the task we have to accomplish in life is expressed, for which, accordingly, we have to expend the real force of our being, hence בכתף ישאו.

V. 10. ויקריבו הנשיאים, thereupon they, not as נשיאי ישראל as the princes of the nation but as נשיאי המטות and ראשי בית אבתם, brought the חנכת המזבח. On Gen. 14,14, we have already explained the concept חנך as the induction of an object in its office. We remarked there how there is a negative and positive idea innate in this conception. It is a negative limitation and just by that grants a more intensive positive activity. The negative sanctification — separating the altar away from any other use or purpose — had already been expressed by משיחה, the anointing, and at the same time the positive was just indicated by the aromatic ingredients of the oil (see on Ex. 30,25). The princes wanted to initiate the altar in the positive use of its purpose at once after its משיחה. For the illuminating אש-דת fire burning as אש אוכלה on the altar is a summons to everyone to give himself up, with everything that comprises his “self” to the power of God’s Torah, to be “food” (לחם I.L.) to keep godliness on earth, and to make everything material and earthly something which gives “satisfaction” (ניחח I.L.) to God. This silent summons, starting the moment the altar had received משיחה, anointment, made the princes of the tribes of Israel feel the urge to answer it immediately. And thereby at the same time to announce how they understood and took to heart what the activity of the Sanctuary in the centre of the nation starting with the משיחה of the altar was to effect on the whole nation. Accordingly ויקריבו הנשאים את קרבנם לפני המזבח and they brought it all together at the same time, proving thereby the equality and the unanimity of feelings towards the Sanctuary of the Torah of all the tribes they represented.

V. 11. ויאמר ה׳ וגו׳. But God gave orders for the princes that each tribe represented by its prince was to have a separate day allotted to it for bringing its offering. For each tribe represented a special kind of social activity, and its being purified and being penetrated with the spirit of the Torah and using its activities in making the demands of the Torah a reality, formed a completely essential specialised contribution for accomplishing the common mission of the nation.

V. 12. ויהי המקריב וגו׳. The order in which they brought their offering was the same as that prescribed in Ch. II for the wandering and encamping position and grouping of the tribes. Refer to it there.

V. 13. קערה .וקרבנו וגו׳ is a vessel, a כלי שרת in which a מנחה offering received its sanctification by being accepted by the Sanctuary, and in which by הגשה in the S. W. it was presented to the side of the altar representing the Torah (the W. I.L.), and the spirit illuminating the Torah (the S. I.L.). מזרק is really a bowl for the זריקה, the throwing of the blood on to the altar. According to ספרי both these vessels, though different in weight were of the same cubic capacity, it was only that the מורק was much thinner, גלדו דק, and so weighed less, but they both contained an identical quantity, a similarity which is indicated by the redundant word שניהם (Cf. Levit. 16,5). Inasmuch as the prince as ראש בית אבתיו and נשיא מטהו brought both filled with flour and oil for a מדחה-offering he expressed thereby the thought that all that his tribe acquires, in their own special way, for food and well-being shall be acknowledgingly dedicated to the spirit of God’s Torah (expressed by the Mincha in the קערה I.L.). And that his tribe would never consider the acquisition and mere possession of the means of social well-being in itself a factor of greatness, but that all material riches would only have meaning and importance when their dead capital was made “living”, when their “flour well mixed with oil” was transformed into “blood”, into נפשות, into lives that would live up to the heights which God had indicated they were meant to climb, that in the future דם of the מזרקות the סולת and שמן itself would gain a life striving upwards to God (expressed by the same quantity of Mincha material placed in a מזרק I.L.).

V. 14. כף .כף וגו׳ is a vessel for the presentation and offering of the incense which accompanied the לחם הפנים (Ex. 25,29) as well as for the offering of קטרח daily and on י״כ (Yoma 47a Thamid 5,4). Normally it is really לבונה that goes with מנחת סלת (see on Levit. 2,1). Here it is offered independently by itself and burnt on the מזבח העולה (not on the golden altar where incense is otherwise offered I.L.) and not לבונה but the highest form of incense קטרת. As we have already remarked on Ex. 30,34 et seq., קטרת is the highest expression of the most ideal devotion, of the most complete giving oneself up to God, it is the ריח ניחוח itself up to which all the other procedures performed on the altar in the עזרה only prepare the way. It was therefore only to be offered on the מזבח הזהב inside the היכל and could never be brought בנדבה of one’s own free will. It represents the highest ideal which is placed before us. But it must appear only as such, as the high goal placed by the Sanctuary before us. To offer it as נדבה of one’s own free will would be the most presumptuous assumption that one had attained the ideal. Here its being brought בנדבה and on the מזבח החיצון was accordingly only הוראת שעה and an exceptional explicit permission given on account of the important meaning of the moment and the momentary purpose. As חנכת המזבח as dedication of the altar it shows the ריח נחוח in its purest perfection up to which the מזבח החיצון henceforth is to teach the way. Offered by the tribal prince as prince of the tribe it expresses the vow that this highest goal of Jewish perfection shall shine before his tribe as the ideal to which for all future time they will always strive to reach with all the possessions and gifts which are granted to them. All the wishes of his tribe shall be at one with the wishes of God. All that it finds satisfaction in, its ריח נחוח shall be what God finds satisfaction in, a ריח ניחוח לה׳.

Taken together מורק ,קערה and כף express in general the three fundamental procedures, הקטרה ,זריקה ,קבלה acceptance, giving oneself up to, sublimation (being accepted by the Sanctuary, throwing the blood unto the altar, burning in the fire on the top of the altar I.L.) which would be performed at and on the altar and so form the basis of the חנוכת המזבח. The acceptance begins within the Sanctuary with one’s material possessions: קערה; the giving oneself up to higher spiritual endeavours, is done with the living being of the person: מזרק; and the most complete sublimation in God with כף, is accomplished above all with the divine flaming godliness in Man. [Possibly these or similar considerations may have assisted in the choice of the weights chosen for these vessels קערה: 130 shekels, מזרק: 70; כף: 10. Taking 10 as the unit we get the figures 13, 7, 1, obviously an arithmetical progression: 13 — 7 = 7 — 1. Now we know the number 6 as the sign of the material, created matter. Man consists of the two material phases, the vegetative and the animal joined with the one spiritual godly unit. Expressed in figures Man is 6 plus 6 plus 1 = 13. For the קערה the consecrating vessel, of the external possessions of food and enjoyments the full number 13 is chosen. סלת and שמל in itself already represent one of the material sides, the vegetative, and their purpose is, to be changed to the animal combined with the divine in Man. Their sign is therefore 6 and 7 = 13. The נפש which in the blood of the מזרק is to receive its devotion to higher things is expressed by the number 7. In it the one material side, the vegetative has already been absorbed by the animal side combined with the godly to be human. It is 13 — 6 = 7. The sign of the מזרק is accordingly: 7. The complete sublimation in God of the קטרת is the divine element itself which is joined to the animal side of Man. It is the godliness in Man after taking away the animal element, it is 7 — 6 = 1. The sign of the כף is accordingly: 1.]

V. 15.—16. After the dedication of the property of the tribes in מנחה, the חנכה progresses in עולה and חטאת to a dedication of all their activities on the basis of a חטאת seriousness in life keeping up their moral standard. His tribe, שעיר-like, shall at all times, keep untemptable firmness on the heights of all moral standards, and in the service of God keep an unweakened strength for work (פר בן בקר), amongst its brother-tribes keep a progressive leading position (איל) and in following God keep ever active in energetically striving upwards to Him, never presuming too far, never imagining it had outgrown the necessity for guidance (כבש בן שנתו לעולה). (See on Ch. 6,14). Also that they could bring this חטאת נדבה was in הוראת שעה, belongs to the חנכה moment. See on Levit. 4,24.

V. 17. ולזבח השלמים וגו׳. But the dedication of the altar reaches its crowning point in the זבח שלמים, in the offering in which — having dedicated their possessions and activities — the tribe comes to God in happiness at its own existence, and wishes, in the happy enjoyment of itself to attain nearness to the Presence of God. In it is mentioned an animal which never again appears in offerings designated as such — עתודים. According to רד״ק they are the bigger older he-goats compared to שעיר the usual characteristic animal for offerings out of goats. So it is not far-fetched to see in עתודים those animals amongst the goats in whom the עז and שעיר character appears in an enhanced degree, they are the עתידים, always “prepared, the big strong he-goats of the herd, always ready for the fray. Hence Isaiah 14,9 uses עתודי ארץ to designate all the other great martial powers that pass across the stage of history, like Babylon. So that the tribe rejoices before God in its existence and purposes as בקר, as a co-worker with God in His great work in the world, as איל, as being in the van in the sphere of its national contemporaries, as עתוד, in defending the vindication of rights against the rest of the world, and finally as כבש, as faithful devotion to the guidance of the “Shepherd of Israel”. The numbers are characteristic. A number occurs here which otherwise never occurs as being ordered for offerings, viz. five. If we consider ten is the radix, the basic number of an עדה of a company of people forming a closed unit, then five as a half would represent a company not closed in to form a unit, but requiring another half for its completion. We understand then why, in שלמים, in expressing its joy in its existence and purpose before God, the tribe does not wish to express itself as a closed unit, but as half such a one, requiring union with a brother-tribe. In עולה the expression of what it should be, it can appear as פר אחד etc. For each tribe should form a separate “one” in the total of the People of God through its own characteristic speciality. But in שלמים, the expression of joy in what it is, the tribe does not think of itself as a closed separate unit and not one and not ten is the sign-number of its offering. As בקר, in its activity, in working in the service of God, the tribe avows itself as בקר שנים as a “Plurality”, it thinks of the contribution of God’s Work on earth that is made by the activity in every hut of the tribe, in every breast of every single individual of the masses who only reckons himself as one of the “thousands and ten thousands of Israel”. And in his joy at his איל influence at home and his עתודים strength abroad, and his כבש consciousness of God’s Guidance he thinks of himself only as a part of the whole, feels himself only complete in brotherly union and expresses this joy as אילים חמשה ,עתודים חמשה ,כבשים בני שנה חמשה.

V. 18.—19. ביום השני הקריב וגו׳ הקרב וגו׳, The offering on the second day is again introduced by הקריב to give it and all the following ones — which then are reported in the shorter informative style: ביום השלישי ביום הרביצי נשיא וגו׳ ,נשיא וגו׳ etc. — quite the same importance and independent declaration of behalf of their tribe as the first, although they are all just a repetition of the first. The Sifri recognises in it a mark of distinction for the tribe of Issachar which distinguished itself as יודעי בינה לעתים לדעת מה יעשה ישראל (1. Chron. 12,32) and whose prince Nethanel was just the one who had instigated and planned the whole חנכת המזבח.

V. 84. זאת חנכת וגו׳ etc. This recapitulation and summing up expresses the complete equality and the harmonious agreement of the princes of Israel in the position of each one of the tribes they represented towards the common Sanctuary and its holy objects, as they demonstrated in this חנכת המזבח.

V. 89. ובבא משה וגי׳. Cf. Ex. 25,22, and the remarks thereon. The preceding חנכת המזבח effected by the נשיאי ישראל, and the fact which that demonstrated, viz, that the tribes of Israel, in unanimous harmonious union, recognised the Sanctuary of the Torah as their Sanctuary and in it the guide and the furthering of the well-being of the whole of their national being is followed correspondingly by the information that when Moses went in to the Sanctuary לדבר אתו because God wished to say something to him, וישמע וגו׳ מעל הכפרת אשר על ארן העדות מבין שני הכרובים he received the Voice speaking to him from the cover, the כפרת which rested on the Ark of the Evidence, from between the two כרובים. For, as we remarked there, God did not allow His Word to come to Moses because of some special personal relationship of Moses to God, but only as a result of the Divine bond of proximity with Israel which is expressed by just the ארון and כפרת (see Ex. 25,10 — 22 I.L.), as a result of the Presence of God in the midst of a people keeping His Torah.

V. 1. In this section the history of the development of the people who had been redeemed out of Egypt to be a People of God is taken up again. It was broken off with the 34th Chapter of Exodus, the chapter of the renewal of the Covenant after the atoned-for sin of the golden calf so as to proclaim the ideal that was to be proclaimed by the erection of the Sanctuary of the Torah and by the associated laws which then form the contents of the whole of the third book and of the beginning of the fourth up to here. The ideal for which Israel should become the People of God, the ideal towards which it was to be educated through the long course of centuries, yea through the thousands of years which reach to our present day and extend beyond it. We have already noted in the second book how just this fact, that for centuries and centuries after the Lawgiving, there was, and is, such a contrast between Israel as it was at the time of the Lawgiving and the Torah itself, with all its assumptions and demands, would be a striking proof of the Divine origin of the Torah, and of its being something unique in the history of mankind. All other laws have had their origin in the requirements of the time and the assumptions which the contemporary conditions justified. This system of Law alone establishes itself as the absolute zenith, the highest goal to be attained by a mode of life, and awaits the generation which will finally have become matured for its ideals to be made into a reality.

We are led over to the continuation of this history of development by a repetition of the instructions to the priests for the administration of the Menora-light, the induction of the Levites to their position of service to the Sanctuary of the Torah, the revival of the national consciousness of the whole nation of being the People of God by celebrating ever afresh the foundation of Israel’s mission in the Pesach-offering, and finally the first breaking camp and moving on from the Mount of the Lawgiving, which, in the ordinary course of events, should have led them directly into the Promised Land which was destined, and is destined for all time, to be the home for making the Torah into a reality. Then, in Chap. X with verses 35 and 36, the story makes a “break”, and takes us down into the midst of the camp to teach us henceforth to know how greatly the people needed to be educated up to the high goal set before them.

V. 2. בהעלתד. See on Ex. 27,20. — אל מול פני המנורה, the מנורה in the real sense is the centre shaft bearing the centre light. Three arms project from this centre shaft on both sides which also bear one light each. Now Aaron is commanded here to turn the side lamps on either side towards the centre one on the middle shaft, so that all seven lamps unite their light in this one direction. This is only a more precise description of the והאיר על עבר פניה said in Ex. 25,37. In Ex. in the explanation of the whole symbolism of the Menora we dwelt on the two views as to the position in which the Menora stood in the Sanctuary. According to the one, it was placed from north to south and the centre light turned towards the Holy of Holies in the west, the three lights on the right turned from the north to the south, those on the left, from south to north. According to the other opinion it was placed from east to west; its centre light burned straight upwards on the centre shaft, the three lights on the eastern side were directed to the west, those on the west to the east. In the first position what would be symbolised would be, that the spirit to be nurtured in the Sanctuary is the idea of seeking God in His Torah and of the covenant relationship between Him and Israel depending on their keeping the Torah. The spirit which the southern lights turned to the north would symbolise, would be, the spiritual side of life directed to impregnating all the material elements of life, and the northern lights turned to the south:- all the material elements of life used for higher, spiritual, ends and the centre light to which both sides are directed: — with both, the spiritual impregnating the material, and the material devoted to the spiritual, striving for nothing else then to making the Torah, reposing in the Holy of Holies in the west, into a reality of life and so realising the proximity of God which was promised as a result of so doing. In the other position the Light to be nurtured in the Sanctuary proclaims itself (burning straight upwards I.L.) as the spirit striving upwards to God, the western lights directed to the east symbolise the Torah reposing in the Holy of Holies, as well as the knowledge of the promise of the proximity of God which can be obtained by the terms of the covenant made concerning it, radiating over to Israel expectantly awaiting being elevated and sanctified by it; and with the eastern lights directed to the west:- that all the intentions and desires of that awaiting Israel turn towards the Torah of God and the promise connected with it; and with both:- the spirit of the Torah brought into the reality of the life of Israel and Israel’s spirited turning towards it — seeking for and finding nothing else than the one object of living upward towards God. In whichever position the Menora stood, its seven lights, seeking and finding, turned towards each other and all united in the centre light, represent nothing other than the most intimate conjunction of the practical גבורה ,בינה and יראת ה׳ with the theoretical עצה ,חכמה and דעת to a complete development of spirit based on יראת ה׳ and so enlivened by יראת ה׳ that ונחה עליו רוח ה׳ that the Spirit of God takes its rest on the spirit of Man developed to such a degree (see Ex. Ch. XXV on the Menora).

The princes of Israel’s tribes had — as reported in the preceding chapter — approached the Sanctuary with the best and most precious of their belongings, with their silver and gold, their flour and oil and fragrant spices, with the best of their herds and flocks. On behalf of themselves and on behalf of their tribes they had made it all into a representation of devoting all their possessions and all their lives and wishes to God and His Sanctuary of the Torah, and of their happiness in such devotion. And as thereby they proclaimed their own and their tribes unanimous posit on towards the Sanctuary, at the same time they accomplished the חנוכת המזבח and inducted the altar in the efficacy of its purpose. The tribe of Levi and its prince Aaron were missing from this declaration by the tribes of Israel and their princes. For they really had no part in the national possession of flour and oil, of silver and gold and fragrant spices, no riches of herds and flocks, their position was altogether not towards the Sanctuary but at the Sanctuary, and the Sanctuary itself was their earthly allotment in life.

So that while the princes of Israel brought their Chanuka-offerings to the altar, and thereby gave expression to the relationship of the nation to the Sanctuary, Aaron, and then his tribe in V.5. et seq., were told what their position was towards the Sanctuary in the nation. להעלות את הנרות so that אל מול פני מנורה יאירו שבעת הנרות. To tend the “lights” in such a way that all the manifold directions of mental and spiritual activities are united in striving towards God by making his Torah a reality, that is the mission of the priests, and the meaning and efficiency of the Levites in the nation for the Sanctuary. That which was expressed by the princes of the nation in those days of exaltation and elation at the dedication is what the priests have to attend to daily and to see to it that the spirit becomes a normal daily one, and that the whole nation, faithful to its mission, unceasingly matures towards its spiritual and moral perfection. This mission of the priests Aaron accordingly had to express silently but expressively by turning the lights on each side towards the centre light in the Sanctuary, and it adds at once,

V. 3. that when Aaron did this, and, by correspondingly arranging the direction of the lights on the Menora expressed that the priest was to see to it that all the spiritual efforts of the nation were to be directed to God and His Torah, this was no presumptuous priestly arrogance but only fulfilling that which God had commanded Moses.

V. 4. וזה מעשה וגו׳. If the reason for the repetition of the instructions for Aaron’s tending the Menora were only to lie in its relation to the preceding Chanuka-offerings of the princes and in his relation to them, it would hardly justify the reference here to the work of the construction of the Menora and the way in which it was carried out. The whole construction of the Menora is given in full detail in Exodus. But we believe we are not in error in assuming that this fresh reference to the meaning and mission of Aaron and the tribe of Levi at the beginning of this section is at the same time also to be a preparation for the recounting of the continuance of the history of Israel’s development for its great mission which begins in this section of this fourth book. If this history shows how far Israel’s beginning was alogether from that devotion to, and giving oneself up to God and His Torah which forms the ideal of its mission, there was nevertheless a whole tribe in it which had already proved its faithful enthusiasm for God and His Torah and on that account had been chosen as the servitors, representatives and maintainers of that ideal amongst the people. In the past they had שמרו אמרתו and in the future they are to יורו משפטיו ליעקב ותורתו לישראל (Deut. 30,8-10); so we have only, above all, to look at the Menora and keep its construction and meaning vivid in our minds: מקשה זהב עד ירכה עד פרחה מקשה היא! A tree, completely golden, from its root-stock to its blossoms, beaten out by repeated hammer- blows from one piece of solid gold, is the Menora, the bearer of the flood of light in the Sanctuary shining up to God and His Torah! Through and through pure gold in unchangeable purity requiring no refining, is the spirit whose representation and care is the purpose of the Sanctuary. But its bearer is a tree, a tree which develops from a deepest root-stock up to highest blossom. In individuals, and so also in a nation, the development to the highest spiritual blossoms required……time. It takes years in the individual, centuries in a nation. The tree is formed from one single piece of gold. In the mass out of which it is formed the material is already there for all of it, material for the root-stock, material for the blossom. מקשה heavy hammer blows from the Master of Israel and the world formed the raw material into the root-stock and have still in the future to form the final blossoms at the top of the tree of light, מקשה זהב עד ירכה עד פרחה מקשה היא. What Moses had formed for the Sanctuary was the representation of Israel which God had shown him as the tree of the whole future of Israel, המאמין לא יחיש — :כמראה אשר הראה ה׳ את משה כן עשה את המנורה (Is. XXVIII.16).

V. 5. Refer to the notes on V.2, and V.4 on the meaning of this consecration of the Levites in connection with the preceding Chanuka-offerings of the princes and the succeeding continuation of the history of the development of Israel. On the day on which the erection of the Sanctuary was completed, the 1st of Nissan, the eighth day of the מלואים (the induction of the priests I.L.) on which the consecration of the priests was concluded and the Chanuka-offerings of the princes began, this consecration of the Levites too was prescribed. The procedure of the פרה אדומה (Ch. XIX) was accomplished on the second of Nissan and the prescribed consecration of the Levites was carried out on the third (ספרי נשא VII,1; Gittin 60a). — וטהרת אותם. The טומאת מת was not banished from the מחנה לויה and had the service of the Levites consisted only in being on guard outside the Sanctuary and in carrying its parts after it had been taken down, they would hardly have required the טהרה from טומאת מת which here clearly was aimed at by הזית מי חטאת. The sacred objects could only be approached after they had been wrapped up, and even if the idea of the Sanctuary still retained its influence on מחנה לויה and מחנה ישראל even after complete striking of the camp, as remarked on Ch. 2,17, the שכינה was nevertheless in abeyance (see תוספות) Zebachim 61a). And their guard duty they also probably held only outside the קלעי החצר, accordingly in מחנה לויה. In the Temple too this duty seems only to have been carried out outside the עזרת ישראל accordingly only in מחנה לויה (see Middoth 1,1, but see מל״מ on הל׳ בית הבחירה VIII,4). But, as we already remarked on Ch. 4,47, an essential part of the service they rendered to and in the Sanctuary was שיר the song with which they had to accompany the national offerings, the קרבנות צבור, and this part of their duty did call them daily right into the Sanctuary around the altar, where no טמא מת may step.

הזה עליהם מי חטאת וגו׳, see Ch. 19,19. This sprinkling with the מי חטאת could not be done before the third day of the טומאה and then had to be repeated on the seventh, הזאת שלישי ושביעי; and as we have already remarked on Gen. 1,11, even if the הזיה had taken place at a later day, that day is always reckoned as a third day so that the second sprinkling had to be done four days later as a “seventh”. Now here the טהרה to be attained is definitely shown by the הזה עליהם וגו׳ as a טהרה from מת, so that the והעבירו וגו׳ וכבסו וגו׳ which follows appears as only a completion of the טהרה belonging to the הזיה, as indeed is shown by the והטהרו by which the טהרה to be attained appears as the result of the preceding procedures. And actually טבילה does belong to הזיה and has to be done on the seventh day after the second הזיה has been performed, and this טבילה is expressed here, as in Levit. 11,25, 28 and elsewhere, by the term כבוס בגדים. This includes the טבילה of the body and of the clothes (see Levit. 11,25). But here nevertheless an act is prescribed which otherwise does not occur at טמא מת. viz., והעבירו תער וגו׳ which, by its position, quite definitely belongs to טהרה, and indeed, by the cantillation is to be added before the ordinary טבילה which has to be done on the seventh day (instead of the second sprinkling I.L.). Quite in agreement with this the ספרי also teaches תחת נשא ,הזאה שנייה גלחו Ch. 7,1 (although in the later edition with the הגהות הגרא״וו ז״ל these four words are put in brackets as an interpolation). In רבות it is given more explicitly: ותחת הזאה שנייה שהיו צריכים הלוים לחזור מפני שהיו כלם טמאי מתים במה שהרגו בעובדי העגל צוה המקום לגלחם במקום הזיה של יום שביעי (“And instead of the second sprinkling which the Levites should normally have had to have done, as they were all unfit owing to their having been in contact with dead bodies when they slew the worshippers of the golden calf, God ordered them to shave themselves entirely, instead of the sprinkling of the seventh day” I.L.). In Gen. Ch. 1,11, we have expressed the view that the first sprinkling on the third day represents, and is meant to elevate the “vegetative” side of life, the life of eating and reproduction, out of the realm of moral force; (I should like to abstain from doing this or that but I cannot help myself it is my nature. I.L); but the second, on the seventh day, to effect the elevation of the main action into the realm of moral freedom (all our acts to be performed in the consciousness of our power to do right I.L.). That העברת תער על כל בשר (completely shaving all over I.L.) is meant to impress the mind with giving up all isolating selfishness, we believe we have repeatedly recognised. If then this complete shaving of the whole of their body at the time of their induction to their office brought home to the minds of the Levites in the most impressive manner the complete cessation of any hitherto living for themselves, and a complete giving up their whole lives to the service of the community, it is easily understood how such a stripping of “the man of action” from all belonging to himself, such placing his person in the service of national purposes demonstrated the entry of the man of action into the realm of moral freedom in the most positive manner, so that the גלוח of the Levites here could well take the place of the second sprinkling, the הזיה שניה.

V. 8. פר בן בקר ,ולקחו וגו׳: the Levites come as a body to represent themselves, in the consciousness of their future work in the profession as a פר, as a worker in the service of God, and vow in a חטאת to keep themselves always on the height of that calling, and in עולה with its attendant מנחה to always strive with all their energy to strive upwards with their actions to the lofty goal of their profession, and only from the point of view of these efforts to be worthy of all the food and possessions they get from God. But in several ways the ordering of this induction of the Levites is peculiar. The purpose of the first פר is not mentioned, and only from V.12 do we know that it was to be an עולה. Whereas in Aaron’s מלואים (Levit. 2,9) the חטאת is ordered first, here it comes after. Further, whereas in every other חטאת whose blood is placed only on the מזבח החיצון (the outer altar) the meat comes to be eaten by the priests, here, according to Horioth 5b, it is not eaten but has to be burnt. We have already discussed these peculiarities on Ch. 6,14, and found the reason for them in the historical event which led to the Levites being chosen. Here we will only add the change of the second person plural ולקחו to the singular תקח in this verse can thereby be explained. It says even more clearly that this חטאת was not “theirs”, was not brought on account of anything in their past, but proceeded from a consideration of the future which now is brought to them by Moses, hence not ולקחו, but תקח.

V. 10. וסמכו וגו׳. Refer to Ch. 1,4 in Levit. By this סמיכה the nation expresses that all the following procedure with the Levites is done in their name, and it is their will that the Levites shall become their representatives towards the Sanctuary.

V. 11. תנופה .והניף אהרן וגו׳ (waving I.L.) occurs three times in this act of the dedication of the Levites, V.11, V.13 and V.15. The meaning of the תנופה act is known as the expression of “dedication”, presenting an object to the person or thing towards which it is waved. Now the dedication of the Levites is accomplished in a threefold presentation, as is explained in V.16—19. Israel dedicates them to God, God presents them to Aaron and his sons, Aaron and his sons dedicate them to the service of the Sanctuary. So that it is in the name of God, in the name of the nation and in the name of Aaron that the Levites take up their position and have to carry out their mission, and these three relationships of their future profession were brought to their minds by the three ת[[illegible]]ופות. Here we first have the Levites being dedicated to God by the nation: והניף וגו׳ לפני ה׳ מאת בני ישראל והיו לעבד את עבודת ה׳.

V. 12. והלוים יסמכו וגו׳. Their חטאת and their עולה bullocks express how they vow to fulfil this “service of God”, to which they henceforth belong in “persevering enduring faithfulness” and in “energetic efforts to strive upwards”, and thereby they enter a completely fresh future undimmed by any weakness of any past whatsoever (לכפר על הלוים).

V. 13. והעמדת וגו׳. The עבודת ה׳ which the Levites had entered with their dedication to God extends beyond their mere relationship to Aaron and their service at and in the Sanctuary. It includes their being the representatives of the Torah, for the “keeping of the covenant”, in the people, for which they had ennobled themselves by their godly action against the defection from God at the golden calf. But within this belonging to God in general they now also get the special devotion to the purposes which the priests have to look after. Hence והעמדת וגו׳ לפני אהרן וגו׳ והנפת אותם תנופה לה׳. This תנופה expresses their dedication to Aaron. But this dedication remains a תנופה לה׳, only for sacred purposes, not for private ones are they subordinated to the priests:

V. 14. והבדלת וגו׳. In this manner are you to separate the Levites out of the nation; and express their belonging to God. ואחרי כן, only after that, after, as prescribed in V.13, they have been placed under Aaron and his sons, יבאו וגו׳ they come to the service of the Sanctuary, and just for this service must טהרה have first preceded their תנופה.

V. 16. כי נתונים. The concept “נתונים״, “given” presupposes a right, or at least a claim, which the giver has to the object of the gift, and which he now renounces in favour of the receiver. If we look for such a relationship hitherto between the Levites and the nation that in giving it up for the benefit of their new profession the term מתנה מתוך בני ישראל could in any way be applied to the Levites, it might be found in the following idea. Every nation does indeed have a claim on each of its nationals to use his powers productively, i.e. to contribute to increase the means of existence and well-being of the state, מתעסק בישובו של עולם as our sages term it, only at that price has the community, on the other hand, the duty of guaranteeing every individual participation in the general welfare. Here, by the nation placing the whole of one of its tribes at the disposal of God and His service, it dispenses it from having to work for its own existence and for that of others, more, it is rather undertaking thereby the duty of providing for their material existence. From this point of view the dedication of the Levites can truly be looked on as a מתנה (a gift I.L.) from the nation to God and His Sanctuary. And probably just because of this implied duty which grows out of the תנופת הלוים by the nation is this מתנה idea so strongly stressed by the repeated נתונים נתונים. The nation shall know what it is undertaking with this תנופה. Without such an undertaking would the תנופה on the part of the nation indeed have no sense.
אדם ובהמה :כל ,בכר כל as in V.17. Cf. Ch. 3,45.

V. 19. נתונים לאהרן וגו׳. Aaron and his descendants have no original claim on the Levites, they are “given” to them by God for a specified purpose לעבד וגו׳: the service at and in the Sanctuary which, in the first place, is the duty of the nation to discharge, and which originally should have been done by their first-born sons, is henceforth to be undertaken by the Levites. ולכפר על בני ישראל: If we understand this term rightly, this withdrawing of the first-born and substituting the Levites could be a continuous כפרה for Israel’s defection at the golden calf. It is a continuous reminder of that first great sin in which the great distance between the actual state of the people and their great mission, and the necessity for their being educated up to it, showed itself, and which they acknowledged and acknoweldge by their willing appointment of the Levites in the place of their first-born sons. ולא יהיה בבני ישראל וגו׳, at the same time this withdrawing the children of Israel from the Sanctuary is nothing but a continuation of that הגבלה (fencing off I.L.), with which at once on the day they received the Law just this distance, which still existed, between the nation and the height of their mission which was revealed to them in that Law, was brought to their consciousness; and the fact was shown for all time that the Torah was a “given” one that came to the people not out of the people. Hence it remains untouchable for all time, and it can never appear Israel’s task or authority to form for itself out of its own subjective idea any form of “honouring God”, a fact, the misunderstanding of which formed at rock bottom the root of the sin of the golden calf. Refer to what we noted in Exodus on the הגבלה and on the event of the עגל.

V. 21. ויתחטאו הלוים refers to the הזיה cf. Ch. 19,12; ויכבסו בגדיהם to the טבילה, see V.7. — ויכפר עליהם אהרן by bringing their חטאת and their עולה, V.12 — לטהרם by these offerings their טהרה received its positive completion, without them they would have been מחוסרי כפרה and would not yet have been allowed to enter the Sanctuary.

V. 24. זאת וגו׳. Above, Ch. 4,2, the age for the entrance into service for the Kehathides was fixed at after the thirtieth year, and if here in general for the Levites it was fixed for after the twenty-fifth year, this is explained (in Chulin 24a) חמש ועשרים ללמוד ושלשים לעבודה that after their twenty-fifth year they enter the service to learn it but only after their thirtieth year they were allowed actually to perform service on their own. It is doubtful what the difference is between שרת and עבודה in V.26. According to the text in מלמד שחוזר לנעילת שערים ולעבודת בני גרשון ,ספרי it seems that עבודה refers to the harder physical work of the Kehathides who had actually to carry on the journeys, and to that of the Merarides who had to load up the heavy timber of the Sanctuary, in contrast to the Gershonides whose service consisted in participating with all the others in the guard and choir duties as well as loading up the tapestries etc., and these services had to be rendered even after passing the fiftieth year. But nevertheless the views of the various commentators differ on this point. See Misrachi hereon. Moreover this limitation to certain years only applied as long as the Sanctuary had to be erected, taken down and transported, as in the wilderness and Gilgal, but in Shilo (where the Sanctuary remained for 369 years I.L.) and in the Temple finally in Jerusalem age made no difference and the only thing that could disqualify a Levite from service was his voice, בשילה ובית עולמים אין נפסלין אלא בקול (Chulin 24a).

V. 1. במדבר סיני. While still in view of the place of the Law giving, before they first broke camp to move on to the land which belonged to the fulfilling of this Law, the whole of the Jewish nation were first to bring the offering which was always to renew afresh the consciousness of the first fundamental basis of the national mission — the Pessach-offering. In view of Sinai and on the basis of the redemption from Egypt every household in Israel and every person of every household is to be made conscious of those two pillars on which their calling rests and to manifest that consciousness in the פסח-offering. But there would have been several reasons present then for a special reminder to fulfil the Pessach commands. Apart from the fact that the Mechilta on Ex. 12,25, says that the yearly bringing the Pessach offering was commanded to be done only after they had taken possession of the Promised Land — the reason for which can well be understood from our remarks on that verse — but, apart from that, as that opinion is not universally accepted (see תוספת, Kidushin 37b ד״ה הואיל) rules came into force at this first repetition of the Pessach offering which are prescribed for פסח דורות, (the yearly Pessach-offering) which are partly different from, partly extension of, those prescribed for the first one in Egypt, the מקחו בעשור, הזאת באגודת אזוב, על המשקוף ועל שתי המזוזות אכילת בחפזון all did not apply to פסח דורות, but on the other hand, הקטר חלבים, שפיכת דם ליסוד מזבח came into force, and whereas in פסח מצרים the prohibition of חמץ only lasted one day, with פסח לדורות it extended to seven days (see Pessachim 96a & b, and Ex. 12,4). So that before the first anniversary of the fourteenth of Nissan there was reason enough for a fresh reminder of the duties to be necessary, and the complete instruction for the forthcoming laws for פסח דורות could well be indicated by the ככל חקותיו וככל משפטיו וגו׳ of V.3. There is yet one other matter that we would draw attention to. According to סדר עולם (Sabbath 87b) the first of Nissan of this second year fell on the first day of the week. But then the 14th, the day on which the Pessach had to be brought, would be a Sabbath, and the pronouncement had to be made that פסח דוחה שבת, that the duty of bringing the Pessach offering over-rides the prohibition of מלאכה on Sabbath. A ruling which, in fact, is first given here in the במועדו (at its appointed time I.L.) of V.2. — בחדש הראשון we have already pointed out on Ch. 7,1, how there the text goes back again, after the beginning of the book had already reported events of the second month, and we believed we could see the reason for that order of recounting events. This peculiarity, that the text does not always report events in their chronological order but sometimes puts things together for inner reasons is just here, in the ספרי and in Pessachim 6b, designated by the canon: אין מוקדם ומאוחר בתורה. In accordance with this canon, the text, in cases where it is revelant to the matter in hand, frequently refers to laws in an earlier chapter although the law itself is only given in a later chapter, and takes it that one is conversant with that particular law. Thus, for example, הזיה במי חטאת in V.7, of the preceding chapter, about which we are told details only in Ch. XIX. For the Torah was only given to Israel in writing at the end of the forty years after it had been taught to the people verbally and completely explained to them in every detail so that every paragraph that was set down could assume the full knowledge of the whole of the Torah.

V. 2. ויעשו בני ישראל. It says here regarding the פסח במועדו, using the same term as it does in Ch. 28,2, regarding the תמיד-offering (the daily offering) from which term — in its appointed time — the Halacha is taught (Pessachim 77a): במועד ואפי׳ בשבת, במועדו ואפי׳ בטומאה that, as soon as the appointed time has arrived, the offering is to be brought, even if it falls on a Sabbath, and even if it can only be brought בטומאה e.g. if all the priests, or all the כלי שרת or, in the case of פסח, if the whole nation or the majority of it, were טמאים. And (ibid.) it is further applied to all קרבנות צבור to which this term can be applied as: אלה תעשו לה׳ במועדיכם (Ch. 29,39), and וידבר משה אח מועדי ה׳ אל בני ישראל where they are considered together under the concept “במועדו״, the text קבעו מועד אחד לכולן. In Pessachim 66 and 67 the fact that תמיד is to be brought even on שבת and פסח even בטומאה is proved directly by the text, as for תמיד on שבת it says עולת שבת בשבתו על עולת התמיד (Numb. 28,10) and for פסח בטומאה it says here that only for איש איש (V.10) only for any individual who happens to be טמאים לנפש is פסח שני to be brought in Iyar but the community as a whole in such a case is to bring the פסח in its proper time in Nissan. איש נדחה לפסח שני ואין צבור נדחין לפסח שני אלא עבדי בטומאה ,בטומאה And then the two laws are made to apply to both cases by גזירה שוה of במועדו במועדו used for תמיד and פסח. The two disquisitions (66 et seq. and 77a) could be mutually complementary and only by the גזירה שוה does the term במועדו receive its circumlocutary application. Without it, and its application the law of טומאה from פסח to תמיד, the idea expressed in במועדו that it has to be brought in all circumstances would have been extended to all טומאות, even to טומאת זב וכו׳. But by the ג״ש bringing it into line with פסח, the rule is limited to טומאת מת only. If it was deduced solely from the ג״ש, the rule would apply only to תמיד and פסח, but as the ג״ש only establishes more precisely what the concept of the term במעדו which we learn from the משמעות (the implications of the texts given in 77a, as above I.L.), the law applies also to all קרבנות צבור to which the concept of מועד is given in the text. Such a combination of the two disquisitions seems also to be behind what תוספות says in Menachoth 72b, ד״ה שנאמר. And in fact it is the concept which lies in במועדו, the duty of bringing an offering at a fixed time and confined to that time, שזמנו קבוע which is the decisive factor for דחית שבת וטומאה. Although the constanly repeated expression טומאה הותרה בצבור, טומאה דחויה בצבור (see below), the idea צבור seems to be what is stressed, and similarly in the disquisitions quoted above it always speaks of קרבנות צבור nevertheless it is pointed out in Temura 14a and Yoma 50a, that the פר יום הכפורים of the High Priest and his daily הביתי כה״ג (Levit 6,13) are קרבן יחיד, and still are דוחין שבת וטומאה while פר העלם דבר של צבור (Levit. 4,13), and שעירי ע״ז (Numb. 15,24), although they are קרבנות צבור are not דוחה שבת וטומאה. Finally the one decisive factor is established to be נקוט האי כללא כל שזמנו קבוע דוחה את השבת ואת :זמנו קבוע הטומאה אפי׳ ביחיד וכל שאין זמנו קבוע אינו דוחה לא את השבת ולא את הטומאה אפי׳ בצבור (Yoma 50a). Considered more closely the concepts זמנו קבוע and צבור may cover each other, inasmuch that although not all קרבנות צבור are also זמנם קבוע still all קרבנות שזמנם קבוע do fall under the concept קרבנות צבור in its wider sense, for offerings which the High Priest has to make in his official capacity, as חביתין and the פר ביה״כ on the Day of Atonement can understandably be differentiated from those he brings from purely personal conditions e.g. as מחוסר כפרה after טומאה. Such would be purely קרבנות יחיד. But פר ,וחביתי כה״ג mark him as כהן גדול, as the ideal representative of the nation in the Sanctuary, and is not bound to his personality as an individual and if rendered unfit by an accident is immediately replaced by the nation by somebody else. So that although Yoma 50a, will not accept the view that the פר יה״כ is a קרבן צבור in the narrower sense, we still think from the reason we have given the rule may be summarised as: כל קרבנות צבור שזמנם קבוע דוחין את השבת ואת הטומאה.

If we try to get at the reason for this rule, it may well be that the concept “במועדו״ as it gets expressed in קרבן שזמנו קבוע or more fully in קרבן צבור שזמנו קבוע would have innate factors which demonstrate in such a positive manner the Truths which the שבת and טומאה institutions are to foster that שבת and טומאה can well stand back in face of that demonstration. For מועד is a time designated by God for our special union with Him, a summons which we meet with a קרבן לה׳. All these times are based on some special act of God’s Management through which each of these times received its own special character, the meaning of which was to serve for our moral elevation. Every such time is accordingly a revelation of God as the Free-willed, Personal Almight, Who not only created the world, but after its creation too, mastered and managed it on completely free-willed government. Thus, the acts of revelation of God’s Power out of Israel’s early history to which all the מועדי ה׳ (including ראש חדש), see Ex. 12,2) are attached. So that all these times are proofs which lie within the actual historical experience of our own past of the fundamental facts of God having created the world, and ruling it afterwards. Sabbath is the first and most general memorial of this fact but one which goes beyond our actual experience. All מועדי ה׳ are only renewed evidences for the שבת, and it is understandable how the קרבן with which we draw near to God in such a moment of remembrance of acts which revealed Him to us, may lay claim, for its accomplishment, to מלאכות which otherwise are prohibited on the Sabbath. This accomplishment is no breaking down of the Sabbath but a raising up of it. And if the תמיד too, the daily morning and evening offering is linked together with these מועדי ה׳, these moments of acts revealing God, which call us to Him; if, as it does here, the תמיד with its במועדו steps to the side of the במועדו of the פסח in complete equality of importance and meaning — (both are the only instances in which the word is written מלא, in which accordingly the decisive conception of יעד is stressed with definite clearness) — then just thereby every day becomes in its relation to us a special act of God. The ordinary every-day “common place” joins the “unique event” in a hymn of the world, proclaiming God; and the rays of each rising sun and the falling of the shades of each night become a מועד, a moment of our experiencing the Presence of God, a moment which incites us to a קרבן לה׳, to an offering which seeks to get nigh unto Him in the moments when He reveals Himself to us. Such a תמיד-moment is accordingly nothing but a revelation of God in the present as the Sabbath proved Him in the מעשה בראשית, so that bringing the תמיד is no breaking down, but a building-up of the Sabbath.

And entirely in a similar manner is דחית הטומאה. For טומאת מת in contrast to the Sanctuary is a denial of a free-willed personal God, as it is of the morally free-willed nature of Man. But both these Truths are positively asserted by each במועדו of a קרבן שזמנו קבוע, which is accordingly an expression of the negation of the טומאה idea. For a special moment in Time only becomes a מועד, a זמן קבוע by some extraordinary act accomplished by the free-will of God, (showing Him free and not bound by the laws of Nature or anything else I.L.). In it God does demonstrate the complete freedom of His Will which forms the indispensable preliminary condition for any moral freewill of Man. And inasmuch as in remembrance of just such a moment He invites us to elevate ourselves up to Him (by an עולה I.L.), He sets His own personal freedom of will as the basis of ours, and guarantees us the moral freedom which finds its highest symbolic expression in the קרבן לה׳. The freedom of the acts of God which lies at the reason of every זמן קבוע invites us to freedom in our own acts and to that we give adequate expression in our קרבן.

But the concept צבור added to it has a quite special significance here. For, it seems to our mind that a קרבן שזמנו קבוע in the sense of the law, is a duty that can only fall on a צבור. Only the community can celebrate by a קרבן, any certain moment at every anniversary of that time. For only the community is there at every recurrence of that time but not the individual. The individual dies, is mortal but אין צבור מת the community as a whole, the nation, is immortal. But that at once makes the nation as it is represented in קרבנות שזמנם קבוע, itself the most positive evidence of spiritually godlike, morally free Mankind being raised above טומאת מת which cannot affect it. For it is not the material bodies of its members which are destined to disappear in death, it is the godly spirit, their morally freewill, that unites the members to be a צבור, and through which the individual member who becomes absorbed in and by the community also goes on living in the community beyond his bodily death, remains present with all that he has brought into the community with his godly spirit, with which he still remains alive down here on earth in the eternal continuance and progress of his work. Hence טומאה דחויה or טומאה הותרה בצבור, and hence the limitation of this דחיה to טומאת מת. (Hence also would the concept צבור next to זמנו קבוע keep its essential meaning, and שלמי חגיגה and עולות ראיה not be דוחה שבת וטומאה which although they are limited to the רגל and אם עבר רגל אין להם תקנה still, as יש להם תשלומין כל שבעה it is not brought so much בכנופיא, not so much by all the nation together at one time, as פסח is, so that the concept צבור does not appear so salient and significant, and thereby the questions raised by תוספות in Pessachim 76b could be answered. Cf. לחם משנה on Chagiga 1, 8, where these questions are answered in a somewhat different manner). But the thought engendered by טומאת מת is one which is so contrary to the whole meaning and purpose of the מקדש that the general way of taking it that טומאה is דחויה בצבור and not, as the more individual opinion has it that it is הותרה בצבור, remains effective so that the permitted repudiation of the טומאה-concept by the concepts of צבור and זמנו קבוע still requires the co-operation of the ציץ (the inscribed golden plate on the forehead of the High Priest, I.L.), בעיא ציץ לרצות (Pessachim 77a). For the meaning of the ציץ being qualified to abrogate טומאה see Ex. XXVIII, on verse 38.

V. 3. תעשו אתו ,בארבעה עשר וגו׳. This is a rare, perhaps unique case, where, after a command has been given in the third person as a duty for the nation, ויעשו בני ישראל it then, in the next verse, changes to the second person, including Moses. In ספרי the במועדו of the first verse is taken to refer to דחית שבת but the במועדו of this verse to דחית טומאה. Now we have already worked out above the deep importance which the concept צבור, the concept of the national community, could have for the canon that במועדו ואפי׳ בטומאה. The inclusion of even a Moses, and especially a Moses, in the general national community could be a better proof than hardly anything else would be, for what we stressed above, viz., the immortal character of the national community. Who is present, living in the nation, and through the nation, for all time, more than Moses! Who, himself participates in earthly immortality through the immortality of the Community, more than Moses! Who, although physically dead is more unreachable by Death than he! — בארבעה עשר וגו׳ בחדש הזה בין הערבים. See Ex. 12,6 and XXIX,38.

ככל חקתיו וככל משפטיו, for the פסח שני in V.12, it says only ככל הקת הפסח יעשו אתו, the idea משפטיו is missing there. Now we know from Pessachim 95a, that the difference between פסח שני and פסח ראשון was, that at פסח שני only the מצות שבגופו (the commandments concerning the animal itself I.L.) as, אל תאכלו ממנו נא וגו׳ כי אם צלי אש, עצם לא תשברו בו לא ישאירו ממנו עד בקר, as well as מצות שעל גופו (commandments in connection with the animal I.L.) as על מצות ומרורים יאכלהו had to be observed but not the מצות שלא על גופו (the commandments which do not refer to matters which are actually in contact with the animal itself I.L.) such as תשביתו שאור ,לא תשחט על חמץ ,לא יראה לך, but rather [[illegible]]סח שני חמץ ומצה עמו בבית (— it is not quite sure whether איסור הוצאה מחבורה applied to פסח שני, Rambam in הל׳ קרבן פסח X,14 denies it —). According to that, it is clear that מצות שבגופו as well as those שעל גופו, i.e., all those laws that relate to the offering itself and to the eating thereof, and, of course the סדר עבודותיו (the way it has to be offered I.L.) are classed under חקתיו. But משפטיו the מצות שלא על גופו comprise those laws which are ordered for conditions which lie beyond the actual offering itself as a result of it, such as the prohibition of חמץ starting with the שחיטת פסח. At חקתיו the פסח is the object, at משפטיו it is the effecting cause. Here at פסח ראשון the פסח laws are in force to their fullest extent, and we have already remarked on V.1, how there was special occasion at this first פסח דורות for the reminder ככל חקתיו וככל משפטיו תעשו אותו.

V. 6. ולא יכלו לעשות הפסח. Even if the law had been given by במועדו in V.2 and V.3, that the פסח was not to be omitted in any circumstances, even in טומאה there could still exist a doubt which had yet to be resolved. We have seen that in addition to the concept שזמנו קבוע the idea of קרבן צבור also held sway. Even if קרבן יחיד שזמנו קבוע like פר יה״ב and חביתי כה״ג are still brought even בטומאה, the High Priest at such offerings does not stand simply as an individual but is considered as the representative of the whole nation, and moreover, if those offerings were not דוחה טומאה, in cases of טומאה, they would not be brought at all at the appointed time. But the פסח is the one קרבן צבור in which the צבור appears, not in its union as a unit but as the actual numbers of its members and it could still well require elucidation as to which position any single individual takes relative to the whole number that bring this offering. It could well be perfectly clear that if the whole nation, or a majority which is considered the same, were to be hindered by טומאה from bringing the offering and so the community-offering, the קרבן צבור, would have to be omitted to be brought במועדו, then טומאה would have to recede before במועדו. But if such a hindrance only affected some individuals could there not be some definite alternative for them. It could be that, in such a case, as after all, the objective purpose of the offering had been sufficiently carried out by the community במועדו, at its appointed time and only the subjective obligations of some individuals were not fulfilled, these latter would have to remain unfulfilled. Or, is the subjective obligation of each individual so much integrated in the general obligation of the whole community to bring the offering במועדו, that his במועדו too suppresses the טומאה, and he — although he is טמא — brings his offering with all his co-members of the community. Actually the decision was made against both these suppositions and in such cases a פסח שני was ordained for individuals. From the additional words ביום ההוא in the report of the incident, it is deduced in Pessachim 90b, that they would have been fit to bring the offering on the following day: טמאי מת מצוה היו שחל שביעי שלהן בערב פסח שנאמר ולא יכלו לעשות הפסח ביום ההוא ביום ההוא הוא דאינן יכולין לעשות אבל למחר יכולין לעשות they had already reached the seventh day of their טומאה on which by הזיה and טבילה and הערב שמש i.e., on the new day that commenced with sunset of that day, they would have been completely טהור. So that they could have eaten the פסח that evening but were unfit to have brought it at the proper time in the afternoon because at the time of the שחיטה they had not yet had טבילה. This is the principle that אין שוחטין וזורקין על טמא שרץ, that one may not slaughter an animal, nor may a priest perform the blood-procedure on the altar for a person who is unfit, although by טבילה and הערב שמש he can be quite טהור that same evening. (According to this supposition the men in question had already brought their פסח and then afterwards had had הזיה and טבילה and the doubt only arose when the time for bringing another פסח had passed. (See ראב״ד on הל׳ קרבן פסח VI,2, רמב״ם takes it in a different way. See מל״מ there).

V. 7. ויאמרו האנשים ההמה אליו אנחנ. וגו׳. In their question can be seen how completely these men understood the real meaning of the approaching time which here came into consideration. That is probably why it is stressed that האנשים ההמה that these men themselves, although just ordinary men of the people put this question quite by themselves. What they put for consideration was:- אנחנו טמאים לנפש אדם, had it been a case of any other טומאה they would not have asked. They knew, they had been taught that only טומאת מת had to stand back before ,קרבן פסח למה נגרע וגו׳ קרבן ה׳ במועדו: it was a קרבן שזמנו קבוע, and בתוך בני ישראל: it was a קרבן צבור to which they, as members of the community, surely belonged. Two factors which, as we recognised on V.6, could speak for their admissibility.

V. 8. עמדו ואשמעה וגו׳. This is a concrete voucher for the fact that all the laws of the Torah were given to Moses not just in their general principles, כללים, but that he received all the more detailed particulars of them פרטים by direct revelation from God. Here there was a particular case to be decided, for which decision he awaited a special decree from God.

V. 10. איש איש וגו׳. The Halacha teaches (Pessachim 93b) that the institution of פסח שני is given not only for טומאה and distance, but for being prevented in any other way. Yea, even במזיד, if a man wilfully and wickedly failed to bring the offering in Nissan, the duty still lies on him to keep פסח שני. This extension to any other טומאה, or any other hindrance is taught by the tradition that דרך רחוקה is given merely as an example. It says טמא לנפש i.e. טומאת מת (instead of simply טמא I.L.) to teach that פסח שני applies only to individuals who constitute a minority but not to the whole community; איש איש restricts it to individuals, but if the majority of the community is טמא they bring the offering בטומאה in Nissan, but this only applies to טומאת מת but even if the whole community were to be affected by other טומאות they would not be allowed to bring the offering בטומאה. In such a case they would not bring the פסח at all, neither ראשון nor שני. (Pessachim 67a). (איש נדחה לפסח שני ואין צבור נדחין לפסח שני אלא עבדי בטומאה וכי עבדי בטומאה בטמא מת אבל בשאר טומאות בדרך רחוקה .(לא עבדי. The ה of רחוקה has a dot above it, to teach that it need not be really so far away, it just depends on whether they can reach the Sanctuary in time to make the offering. If at the beginning of that time, i.e. midday of the 14th Nissan, anybody is at a distance from where he cannot reach the עזרה before the closing time for the offering so that he cannot be there בין הערבים, he is רחוקה and can בדרך רחוקה not bring פסח ראשון. Neither may anyone else do the שחיטה etc., on his behalf even if he could be home in time for the eating. Just as אין שוחטין וזורקין על טמא שרץ so also היה בדרך רחוקה ושחטו וזרקו עליו לא הורצה (ibid. 92b). Such a distance is reckoned at fifteen מיל, the distance of Modein from Jerusalem. (According to דרך רחוקה ,רמב״ם is such a distance that, at sunrise on the 14th Nissan he could not be there at the beginning of the time for bringing the offering. Rashi and תוספות and the wording of the Jerushalmi are opposed to this view).

V. 11—12. We have already remarked on v.3, that all the שבגופו and שעל גופו are to be understood under the term חקת הפסח and have to be observed at the פסח שני, but שלא על גופו as ,יא יראה לך ,השבתת שאור לא תשחט על חמץ which come under משפטי פסח do not apply to פסח שני, but חמץ ומצה עמו בבית.

V. 13. והאיש אשר הוא טהור. In Pessachim 93a, there are three opinions as to the relation of the second Pessach to the first. According to רבי, the second is רגל בפני עצמו, each is an independent festival on its own, so that even שגג בראשון והזיר בשני חייב כרת (if he inadvertently missed bringing on the first and intentionally omitted to bring on the second Passover, he would incur the full punishment, I.L.). According to רבי נתן the שני is תשלומי הראשון, hence שגג בראשון והזיר בשני פטור. (The second is just an extra extension of the first so that if he did not incur the full punishment on the first, even if he intentionally missed the second, he would not incur the full punishment I.L.). According to רבי חנניה בן עקביה the שני is תקנתא of the ראשון hence he would only be חייב if he missed both במזיד and even הזיד בראשון ושגג בשני פטור. (The second is a chance to make good the omission of the first, hence only if he omitted on both occasions intentionally would he incur the full punishment, but even if his omission on the first was quite intentional if he inadvertently missed the second he would not incur the full punishment I.L.). Rambam adopts the first opinion that each is an independent institution so that a גר שנתגייר בין שני פסחים וכן קטן שהגדיל בין שני פסחים חייב לעשות פסח שני, even a person on whom the duty to bring the offering was not at all encumbent on the first would still have to bring the offering on the second (e.g. a proselyte who became converted, or a child who attained maturity, between the two Passovers. I.L.). According to this opinion our verse would declare כרת separately for both institutions, the first sentence for פסח ראשון, and the second for פסח שני. The האיש ההוא would then refer to the same man, one who, for whatever the reason may have been, missed the first פסח and then (intentionally I.L.) neglected to bring the offering on the 14th Iyar as prescribed for such cases. חטאו ישא is כרת as ונשא חטא in Levit. 24,15, at מברך ה׳. See Numb. 15,30.

It says: והאיש אשר הוא טהור ובדרך לא היה. Perhaps the change of tense may be explained by, as seems to be the case from Passachim 9a, the concept דרך רחוקה being taken to be absolute, so that a fixed radius of fifteen miles around the city of the Temple forms the radius within which the duty of bringing the Pessach-offering applies, and anyone who is outside this radius, although by means of riding or transport he could reach the Temple in time, nevertheless does not incur כרת for neglecting to bring the פסח. In this אונם דרך רחוקה differs from אונם טומאה. A man who is טמא, and could have been טהור on the fourteenth and neglects to have taken טבילה and thereby fails to bring the פסח is חייב כרת (Pessachim 69b). Now it seems to us that it is by no means impossible that a person who, by דרך רחוקה at the beginning of the time for bringing the offering and thereby was free from the duty of having to bring it, would still be free from כרת if he had used transport and had come to Jerusalem in time and had not brought the offering. If this is so then the change of tense in our verse in quite precise. He who during the time for bringing the offering is טהור or even could have been טהור and at the beginning of the time for bringing it was not בדרך etc.

But although according to the accepted way of taking it פסח שני is רגל בפני עצמו nevertheless it is subsidiary to the real and has its character impressed on it only through the real. It is, as already remarked only for individuals who, by it, attach themselves subsequently to the national offering which the nation brought at the proper time, and which they had missed. איש נדחה ואין צבור נדחה לפסח שני, and פסח שני can only be celebrated by individuals if פסח ראשון had been brought by the צבור in טהרה. But if, for any reason other than טומאה the nation had been prevented from bringing the offering in Nissan, or had had to bring it בטומאה, then פסח שני is not allowed to be brought by יחידים, individuals, אין תשלומין לפסח הבא בטומאה (Pessachim 80a).

V. 14. וכי יגור וגו׳. See on Ex. 12,48. This equality of the -ג even with regards to the Pessach-offering (which, after all, had no reference to his forefathers I.L.) which is repeated here, can be taken as the general basis for his complete equality of rights in every way in the eyes of the Torah. For by his thus celebrating the Passover lamb, the whole Jewish past becomes his too, and, as we worked out the reason there, any difference in his treatment, socially or legally, which might be incited by reference to where he came from, is completely eliminated. But this equality was specially to be stressed here at פסח שני as it could happen that a גר could even have to celebrate the פסח quite by himself. Whereas at פסח ראשון it could appear that he was only not to be excluded from the general community, here at פסח שני, as remarked on V.11 & 12, even a proselyte who had become converted in the time between the two Pass-over, would have to celebrate the second Passover, although at the first, the national duty did not apply to him at all. כמקת הפסח וכמשפטו וגו׳ expresses the duty of the Pessach offering applying to him in general, particularly to פסח ראשון (see on V.3). His equal obligation to פסח שני is given by חקה אחת.

V. 15. וביום הקים וגו׳. This וביום just carries on from the preceding without any transition record (it does not even start a fresh paragraph in the Torah, there is just a small space but no fresh line I.L.) so that it evidently implies an intimate connection with it. And actually what follows is nothing but an example in actual active life of what was expressed symbolically in the Pessach-offering to bring afresh to the mind of Israel its mission and its undertaking to fulfil it. To place itself ready as צאן to its רועה, as God’s flock to the guidance of its Shepherd, (as we recognised in Ex. Ch. 12,3-6) was the fundamental thought which Israel in the first Pessach-offering, entered under the leadership of God, and by which it made itself worthy for it, and it is the same thought which with every annual recurring Pessach is to come as a fresh vow to every member of Israel. What all the families of Israel express coming near to God with their Paschal-lambs is nothing other than: על פי ה׳ יחנו ועל פי ה׳ יסעו that they encamp only at the Word of God, and journey on only at it.
