Another says it was משה מת יהושע מכניס ישראל לארץ (Moses will die and Joshua will bring Israel into the Land I.L.) and finally a third opinion declares על עסקי גוג ומגוג היו מתנבאין, they prophesied about the last war of Gog and Magog, which, according to Ezekiel and Zacharia, will form the final development of the history of the ages. Gog of whom Ezekiel says in XXXVIII,17: האתה הוא אשר דברתי בימים קדמנים ביד עבדי נביאי ישראל הנבאים בימים ההם שנים להביא אותך עליהם “Art thou he of whom I have spoken already in the days of yore, through my servants the prophets of Israel, who in those days prophesied that in years to come I would bring thee against them?” These men, who at the same time prophesied about years to come, would then refer to Eldad and Madad. Elsewhere we have developed the thought that Gog and Magog represent the גוג-principle, the “roof-principle”, the principle of a dictator at the summit, the concentration of all leadership in one supreme “head” in its most absolute consistency, and therefore, after the defeat of גוג, the city of the opposing principle of democracy will be called המונה, the “City of the Masses” (Ezek. 39,16). If there is any truth in this thought it would be of no small significance that the prophecy of Eldad and Madad is taken to refer to that distant final victory of the principle of democracy over that of Gog and Magog, or to the nearer event of the death of Moses and the leadership of Joshua. Then it would be just the mouths of the most modest men, who, out of modesty kept back from a recognised most influential official post and preferred to remain במחנה, amongst the people, which were deemed worthy of proclaiming the most ideal democratic future, where the centre-point of the social well-being of the world will be focussed not in the “אהל״ but in the “מחנה״, not in “גוג מגוג״ but in the “המון״. Or they proclaimed a fact, that, as the death of Moses and the completion of the national destiny through Joshua made clear, no man, not even a Moses may consider himself, or be considered by his contemporaries, as indispensable. Moses dies — and the destiny of the nation still gets fulfilled.

V. 31. ויגז שלוים מן הים. It seems that the quails were doing a huge migratory flight over the sea, a sharp wind blew under them cutting them off from the sea (גוז) blew them upwards off their course and threw them down round about the camp.

V. 32. ויקם וגו׳. Both greed and mistrust in the assurance that Moses had brought them are shown in this rush to gather the quails. They had been assured that they would be able to enjoy meat for a whole month. Hence perhaps the ואף ה׳ חרה of the following verse.
V. 35. ויהיו בחצרות, probably leads over to the following event, as it gives the place where it happened.

V. 1—2. ותדבר מרים. These verses present difficulties in understanding them, which however can be solved. They tell us that Miriam and Aaron spoke scandal about Moses regarding האשה הכשית אשר לקח which on the face of it would simply mean: “concerning the Ethiopian woman whom he had married”, כי, “for”, it adds, the fact in itself is really true אשה כשית לקח he had married an Ethiopian woman”. So far the meaning would be clear, and then it would not be so surprising that Miriam and Aaron dwelt on the matter as the fact that Moses should indeed have married an Ethiopian woman. And if this Ethiopian or Abyssinian woman refers to the Midianite Zippora, then, apart from the fact that כוש is by no means identical with Midian, what possible wrong was there in that marriage and further, that fact had long been known, and surely need not be stated as a piece of news, כי אשה etc. But the words of Miriam and Aaron which are immediately told us in the next verse do not at all agree that the marriage with the אשה כשית — whoever she may have been — in itself was the subject of their condemnatory talk. For clearly the words: הרק אך במשה דבר ה׳ place the fact כי אשה כשית לקח in close connection with Moses’s prophecy, and indeed undoubtedly put it that Moses אשה כשית לקח because דבר ה׳ בו, but, they say, they find no justification for לקיחת אשה כשית in this דבר ה׳ במשה. For he, Moses, was not the only one to whom God had spoken, and all the others, including themselves, although they too had been found worthy to be granted the spirit of prophecy, did not on that account feel themselves called on לקחת אשה כשית! Now it is absolutely unthinkable that Moses, or anybody else in the world, because he had been found worthy to be endowed by God with the spirit of prophecy should “therefore” have married an Ethiopian. If then, as the whole context does not allow it to be taken otherwise, the fact that כי אשה כשית לקח was brought about by Moses’s prophetic calling, the words must express something other than that he had married an Ethiopian. When we look through the whole of the Torah for some relation between marital conditions and prophecy the only case we find is in Ex. 19,15 where the people who are to be deemed worthy of receiving the Word of God directly from Him, as a preparation for that were to abstain completely from sexual intercourse with their wives. And indeed this preliminary stipulation must be one that is so essentially demanded by the occasion that it is tacitly comprehended in the general instructions וקדשתם וגו׳ והיו נכונים וגו׳ (V.10 & 11 ibid.). As a matter of fact tradition (in the ספרי) also explains that the condemnatory remarks of Miriam and Aaron were solely referring to Moses abstaining from sexual intercourse with his wife, פירש מז האשה a fact which only became known to them on the occasion of the prophecy of the appointed elders. The complaint was entirely in the interests of the wife, for they found it wrong and thought it was nothing about which Moses had been commanded, as they themselves and the Patriarchs before them had been considered worthy to receive the Word of God without thereby having to suffer interruption in their conjugal lives. They overlooked the difference between the stage Moses had reached and their own, and did not know that, when at the conclusion of the Revelation on Sinai the people were told שובו לכם לאהליכם (Deut. V.27) to return to family life and conjugal intimacy, Moses was commanded to remain separated and given the duty with the words ואתה פה עמד עמדי ואדברה אליך וגו׳. That this is the meaning of our verse here is beyond all doubt. This explanation would also be supported by the consideration of the fact that the term על אודות in every case where it occurs in the Torah in a similar connection it always designates a suffering condition on behalf of whose interests it is used. Thus, Gen. 21,11 וירע וגו׳, על אודות בנו; ibid. 25: והכיח וגו׳, על אודות באר; Ex. 18,8 אשר עשה ה׳ לפרעה וגו׳ על אודות ישראל. So here too the אשה כשית herself is not the subject of the complaint, but the one in whose interests it was made. It only remains to discuss the meaning of האשה הכשית אשר לקח, in the connection of the undoubted meaning of our verse. We would venture to believe it not impossible that לקוח אשה כשית is just nothing else but a circumlocutary expression for “living apart sexually”. The term כושי is found several tin es having a typical meaning. In היהפוך כושי עורו (Jer. 13,23) it designates black people in general. In הלא כבני כושיים אתם לי (Amos 9,7) it designates the lowest and farthest-off race of men “And if ye were children of the Hottentots, would ye not be equally Mine”. In Ps. 7,1 שגיון לדוד אשר שר לה׳ על דברי כוש בן ימיני it designates the whole depth of the contrast which the conduct of Saul displayed to that which would be expected of a בן ימיני of the son of Jewish stock. It was as much a moral degeneration as a Hottentot (or whatever is the lowest ethnological human being I.L.) born from Jewish stock would be a physiological one. Could not then marriage with a כושית be considered as something so objectionable and irreconcilable that a marriage in which the partners live sexually apart could be called “to have married a blackamoor”. We can in any case only offer this as a suggestion, but we believe that we have adopted something that is not impossible, and if we have hit on the right idea we would have found the natural interpretation of our verse.

הרק אך וגו׳. This doubling of the limiting particle expresses the complete exclusiveness, “only and solely”, in which they imagined Moses must have considered his position, that he believed that he had to adopt such an attitude towards his wife. “Has then God really spoken only and solely to Moses?” Were not Abraham, Isaac and Jacob also considered worthy of receiving the Word of God? and they did not have to give up living conjugally with their wives. הלא גם בנו דבר. Were we not ourselves deemed worthy also, and we have not had to give up our sexual lives in our marriages! וישמע ה׳. They only spoke to each other, but God heard.

V. 3. ענה .והאיש משה ענו, used referring to the mental state: to say something which is caused by something said or done by somebody else, to reply “in accordance” with it, or to start saying something in accordance with such a cause; used referring to the social state: the designation of complete dependence of one’s existence on the will of others; and ענו and ענוה become the designation of the character of complete self-lessness, where the thought of one’s own worth, one’s own greatness, has no place, and towards God, simply and completely to be absorbed by His Will. It is the negative preliminary condition for the positive character of חסידות, the most complete self-sacrifice for the practical fulfillment of the Will of God. The two qualities together form the summit of greatness of character and deed, so that in Avoda Zara 20b one can only waver between awarding the palm to חסידות or to ענוה. Here attention may have been drawn to this greatness of the character of Moses for two reasons. Just this particular phase of their brother’s character, which must surely have been known to them, should have prevented them from making a false judgment on his behaviour which, according to them, was only due to an exaggerated idea of his own importance. And no man was farther off from such overweening pride than just Moses! And then certainly it was not in Moses’s nature to have justified himself by explaining that his position towards God was so much higher than theirs, and so God Himself had to do it for him. And finally perhaps the words והאיש משה give an indication as to how they came to such a judgment on Moses. His unlimited ענוה was the cause of it. Through it they had no idea of his special, yea unique, relationship to God. He only let himself be considered as their equal, never spoke about the specific height of his prophecy, perhaps in his perfect ענוה was not conscious himself of how special it was, and imagined that all the others to whom the spirit of prophecy was granted stood on the same stage as he did.

V. 4. פתאם (see on Ch. 6,9). As God’s speech in V.6 is the reply to what V.2 tells us they said, and, moreover, the “he” and “him” in it obviously refer to what they said, this summoning them out to the Tent must have followed immediately on their remarks.

V. 6. אם יהיה נביאכם: were he, Moses, your prophet, i.e., the prophet that you seem to think him to be. Or: were he one of your prophets, similar to you, in your class. — במראָה different from מראֶה (V.8). מראֶה is direct sight, עץ נחמד למראה (Gen. 2,9) אשה יפת מראה (Gen. 12,11). מראָה is what is seen indirectly, hence a mirror (Ex. 38,8). In two ways prophecy can be not direct, objectively and subjectively. Objectively: the Divine, which is manifested to the prophet, he does not see directly, but reflected, as in a mirror. He has to draw his conclusions as to the One Who has manifested Himself to him from the vision in which He revealed Himself to him. Subjectively: It is not in his ordinary state of wakefulness in which his receptive faculties are under his conscious control, but בחלום אדבר בו in a dream-like condition, in which he is capable of receiving the Word of God to reflect on it and take it to heart afterwards when he awakes, that the spirit of prophecy comes over him. The Divine comes down to him indirectly and raises him out of his usual condition when He wishes His Word to reach him. Both reasons why at other times his life can run its ordinary normal course and no restrictions need be imposed.

V. 7. לא כן עבדי משה, “not so My Servant, not so Moses. Not so My “Servant”, he is more than prophet, he stands permanently in My service, and is “Moses”, is this in the whole uniformity, the undividedness of his personality which raises him humanly above all other human beings, בכל ביתי נאמן הוא. If we have any inkling of what would be expressed by this it would be:- everything is open, unlocked and uncovered for him. Altogether everything in God’s household in this world which is able to be comprehended by mortal flesh and blood stands open for him. To a servant who is not entrusted with the whole of the house certain things are inaccessible. He may have no idea perhaps that certain things are there at all. Certain things he knows are there, perhaps also where they are, but he has never seen them himself, or only covered up. He is full of the idea what treasures the house contains, can even describe what his inkling is and can even bring other people to share his ideas; and in certain elevated moments his master shows him some of the things that otherwise have to remain hidden from him so that he can tell his brethren outside of the glories of his master within the house. But all this is different with one who is בכל ביתו נאמן, trusted to free entry everywhere in the house. He wanders freely always in the Light of the House. He has the full, unabreviated uncovered knowledge.

V. 8. פה אל פה .פה אל פה אדבר בו designates, in contrast to the objective (במראָה) and subjective (בחלום) indirectiveness indicated in V.6, the objective and subjective directness of the revelation. The פה speaks to him, and speaks to him when he is in a condition himself to be a פה, able to speak, accordingly not במראָה and not ובמראה .בחלום, that of which he is to be made conscious is brought to his vision clearly and directly, ולא בחידות, he had not to come to his conclusions out of an indirect vision, out of some symbol. חידה, root is אחודה נא לכם חידה) חוד Judges 14,12 “I will now set you a riddle”; חוד חידה ומשל משל Ezek. 17,2 “set a riddle and speak a parable”), phonetically related to אוד and אות, the concept of mechanical and mental indirect means (see Gen. I on את V.l) ותמונת ה׳ יביט not ה׳ במראה אליו אתודע (see on Gen. 1,11).

ומדוע לא יראתם וגו׳, “how did you dare to place yourselves parallel to עבדי, to Moses, to draw conclusions from yourselves to עבדי, to My servant Moses. Did you imagine that you were able to judge what becomes My Servant, what is suitable and right for Moses?

V. 10. והענן וגו׳ והנה מרים מצורעת כשלג ויפן אהרן אל מרים והנה מצורעת. As soon as the cloud went out of the Tent, והנה, it was seen that Miriam was snow-white with leprosy. When Aaron went to her and examined the leprosy more closely והנה, he recognised that the leprosy was of that kind of נגע which is called צרעת in the Torah, which marks the person affected by it as being “touched” by the displeasure of God (see Levit. XIII).

V. 11. אל נא תשת עלינו חטאת. The meaning of this request is not quite clear. As he admits that they have sinned, it is difficult to see what he is asking for in אל נא. If they have sinned, the sin is there and does rest on them. Perhaps the appeal lies in the expression אל נא תשת ,שות, similar to אם כפר יושת עליו (Ex. 21,30), and the meaning is: do not make the sin weigh down on us, do not place that which we have sinned as something that has to be paid for. Possibly also it has to be taken in conjunction with the preceding ויפן אהרן וגו׳ והנה מצורעת as: do not let us be stamped with sin (by the marking נגע) by what we have thoughtless y done (נואלנו, see on Ex. 2,21).

V. 12. מצורע חשוב כמת ,אל נא תהי כמת (one who is affected by this kind of leprosy is considered as a dead body, see Levit. 13,46). ספרי) מה מת מטמא באהל אף מצורע מטמא בביאה). By the נגע they bear the sign of exclusion from all society, and, as the Sifri remarks, there was no כוזן there who could perform the prescribed procedure to restore them to טהרה, as the only priests were Aaron and his sons and קרובים פסולים לראות נגעים (relations are not entitled to examine the נגע and decide whether seclusion is necessary and if so, when it may cease etc.). So that her state of טומאה and the consequent seclusion could also not have been incurred at all, as that is entirely dependent on the declaration of the priest, (see Levit. 13,3) had it not been declared by God Himself (V.14) Who also alone could have set the term for seven days and given permission for it to end after the seven days, as there was no כהן המטהר. In the words of the הקבייה הסגירה ,והקב״ה טימאה ,והקב״ה טיהרה ;ספרי (see Zebachim 102a).

אשר בצאתו מרחם אמו. The pronoun in בצאתו refers to מת, in אמו and בשרו back to אדוני (Moses) and the person addressed is put in the third person as a mark of submissive respect, as in יעבר נא אדני ,אדני ידֵעַ (Gen. 33,14). In such addresses the change from second to third person is quite frequent (cf. II. Sam. 14,11). The same in ויאכל חצי בשרו (instead of בשרך I.L.). Similarly to אחינו בשרנו הוא (Gen. 37,27). To make the meaning clear we have translated אמו and בשרו in the second person. Aaron appeals to Moses’s brotherly feelings “she is your own sister”. “Were she to remain in the same “dead” condition, half of yourself would cease to exist”.
V. 14. ואביה ירק וגו׳. (See Levit. XIII p. 358, in the explanation of בפניה .(נגעים, before her, like יתיצב איש בפניך (Deut. 7,24).

V. 16. חצרות .ויחנו במדבר פארן as רמב״ן remarks, was also in the wilderness of Paran. They had entered it already in Kibroth-hataava, as is evident from Ch. 10,12. ויחנו וגו׳ can accordingly only mean, “and they encamped further on in the Wilderness of Paran.”

If we look back on the events which are specially predominant in this section בהעלתך, they show us preferably the general idea of the manifold degrees of possessing spiritual gifts in various positions towards the Divine. We have Moses and the nation in general (Ch. 10,35 and 36), Moses and the elders Eldad and Medad (XI,24 et seq.), Moses and Aaron and Miriam and the other prophets (XII,4 et seq.). Should not, perhaps, this matter contained in this section also be in deep underlying connection with the “Tree of Life” of Jewish spiritual development, the מנורה which stands at the beginning of the section?

V. 1—2. שלח לך. Cf. עשה לך שתי חצצרת (Ch. 10,2), קזז לך בשמים (Ex. 30,23) and other places where the addition of the word לך in no way diminishes the commanding meaning of the demand. Here, too, the שלח לך appears in the sense of a simple command. Hence, indeed in the following verse the mission is described as being sent על פי ה׳. From the retrospective reminders (Deut. 1,19 et seq.) we know that they had now traversed the wilderness of Paran, which is there described as “the great and terrible desert”, המדבר הגדול והנורא, and had reached Kadesh-barnea, at the border of the land to be conquered. The Amorite mountain range lay before them, after ascending them, the conquest of the land would begin. Then the proposal was made by the people to Moses that, first of all he should send some of them ויחפרו את הארץ, as they put it, “to reconnoiter the land for them”, literally “to raise the knowledge of it out of the darkness of the unknown into the clear daylight of the known” (ibid. 22 et seq.) with the expressed purpose of finding out the best way to enter the land and take the city. In this proposal itself there was nothing improper. Moses himself says there: וייטב בעיני הדבר “and the matter seemed good to me.” For, after all, with their entry into the Promised Land, the special extraordinary direct guidance of God was to be more in the background, and the further life of the nation to have recourse to tie more normal activities of the people themselves; even during the wanderings in the wilderness Moses could ask for the assistance which the knowledge of the various localities which his father-in-law would give him, although those wanderings were undertaken under the immediate direction of God. According to Sforno, the Divine order שלח לך of our verse only modifies the request of the people inasmuch as that נשלחה אנשים לפנינו “let us send men”, they asked for permission to send men of their choice, whereupon God commanded that Moses was to choose and brief men from each of the tribes, and indeed those of the highest qualifications, for that mission. Also the nature of the orders to be given to them was to receive certain modifications. In the proposal of the people they were to go “ויחפרו וגו׳ וגו׳״, let them spy out the land for us. Now חפר את הארץ seems predominantly to be such for finding out the weak spots of a land for the purpose of conquering it. Thus in Joshua II. 2 & 3. Thus also in Job 39,29: משם חפר אכל, speaking of the eagle searching out her prey. Perhaps חפר used intransitively also indicates the feeling of shame at disclosed faults, and probably the whole underlying conception of the meaning of the word is excavating, to bring out into the light that which really should remain hidden. In contrast, the term used in God’s command is ויתרו וגו׳. But תור (related to טור, a row, תפר joining in a row, sewing etc.) designates not only searching in general, a purely objective searching of things in general by joining together all the known peculiarities of a thing to get an idea of what it really is, as in Eccl. 1,13, 11,3 & VII,25, but where it occurs with a subjective purpose, it seems to mean searching out the good points suitable for some intended purpose. Thus in Ch. 10,33 לתור להם מנוחה and in Deut. 1,13 לתור לכם מקום לחנתכם. So also quite specially of the choice of the Promised Land as the best and most suited for Israel’s calling in Ezek. 20,6: ארץ אשר תרתם להם זבת הלב ודבש צבי היא לכל ארצות. By the order: ויתרו את ארץ וגו׳ the mission received a somewhat different and extended task. It was no longer just to spy out the most suitable way to conquer the land. That purpose was to be in the background, and the task set was to learn to know the land itself as a base for national development, and the significant indication was given to consider it from two points of view, as ארץ כנען אשר אני נתן לבני ישראל it is at the present ארץ כנען, the land of a most degenerate nation, and it is the land that is given by God to the children of Israel for them to develop in it a national life according to His revealed Will, the Torah.

כל נשיא בהם. According to the notation (כל has a separating accent marked on it I.L.) נשיא is more adverbial to the verb implied by כל. Not every prince, but every one is to be a “prince of men” amongst the people. These were not the tribal princes, the נשיאי מטות אבותם, who are called ראשי אלפי ישראל, ראש לבית אבתיו in Ch. 1,4 & 16, the official heads of a state division, but each one was נשיא בהם, they were בהם, not at the head but amongst them; but in their characters and abilities they ranged above the masses, were נשיא בהם. Although they were not the official leaders, they were, as it says in the following verse ראשי בני ישראל, popular heads, men of leading influence among the people.

V. 3. כלם אנשים, they were all “men”, individually efficient and distinguished. Cf. מי שמך לאיש (Ex. 2,14). Thus the Midianites called Gideon איש ישראל (Judges 7,14). Thus David to Abner הלא איש אתה ומי כמוך בישראל (I. Sam. 26,15).

V. 16. ויקרא משה להושע בן נון יהושע. With this change of name he gave him and his companions, for every time they addressed him it would bring it to their minds too, a guiding hint which they were not to lose sight of in their carrying out their mission. It was to remind him and them that הוֹשֵׁע that He Who in the past had always helped us was also the One Who יהושע, Who would see to our salvation in the future, yea, that יְהוֹשֻׁעַ that God was our whole riches, our whole power, all that we strive for, and beside Him everything else loses its meaning or importance. For יהושע is not only a change of the past הושע into the future, it would then have had to be יהושיע. It is rather turning the conception of ישע, the root of הושע to שוע with the name of God prefixed. Whereas ישע (related to ישה the root of יש and חושיה) means full measure of existence, שוע (phonetically related to שפע ,שבע) designates full measure of possessing, hence שוע: rich, opulent. Perhaps שַׁוֵעַ is a cry for help against robbery, and תשועה preferably help to gain victory in a war of defence of country, and ישועה help for existence in general. That this change of name was in close connection with the mission which Joshua and his companions were to accomplish is evident from the context of where it is told to us. Had it merely personal reference we should have been informed of it above in V.8. But here it is given after mentioning the general mission אשר שלח וגו׳, and before giving the detailed instructions for that mission. So that this change of name forms the seal of, and the foundation-laying introduction to this mission. It tells Joshua and his colleagues that their mission is not to convince themselves of the certainty of victory and confidence in thriving in it, their שוע and their תשועה is to be God, and does not rise or fall with the favourable or unfavourable light in which the land may appear to you in these respects. Accordingly, with this change of name Moses accompanied his messengers in spirit, and gave them a compass by which to judge in which sense to take their mission.

V. 17. לתור את ארץ כנען. They are to find out the land as ארץ כנען, in its present condition as the ground of the Canaanite inhabitants. — עלו זה, literally: go up this here. For your mission it is immaterial from where you enter the land. בנגב: they were encamped to the south-east of Palestine. — ועליתם את ההר, the Amorite mountains to which they had reached (Deut. 1,20).

V. 18. וראיתם את הארץ מה היא; this would be the question on the topographical nature of the land in general, whether mountainous or flat, well watered or not, etc. ואת העם היושב עליה is the question on the ethnological nature of the physical, spiritual and moral qualities of the inhabitants. החזק הוא הרפה etc., stresses special points in connection with the more general aspects. The way the question החזק הוא הרפה is put seems significant. In contrast to all the following questions the alternative way of posing the question is avoided.

If we consider the import of this question, it would be the one among the others which, at the first glance could appear decisive for undertaking the conquest of the land. Are the inhabitants strong, it will be difficult, perhaps impossible, are they weak, these doubts do not arise. And it is just this way of looking at the question which is to be avoided. Israel is not to be interested whether the inhabitants are weak or strong. The conquest is no question of yes or no, so that this question is put, not one or the other but only side by side as only an accidental difference but not in terms of actual contrast. Thereby the whole mission would be given quite a different character to what was originally intended by its proposers. Not for the purpose of the conquest, but for a permanent important teaching for all future time is the knowledge of the land in its present conditions to be obtained. The tradition of the disadvantages which the land and people show at present will be handed down in future in comparison with the flourishing happy conditions under the protection and blessing of God; what it has to show now in abundance and riches will give some idea of the height of happiness and blessing it will blossom up into under a development directed by God; but, above all what it shows in strength and might and greatness in its Canaanite present could transmit to all succeeding generations of the Jewish future, the lesson of how all power and greatness, however gigantic it may be, cannot protect a nation from ruin if it neglects to render homage with everything, and in everything in the first place to God’s laws of morality. Thus Amos (II,9) brings the warning to his contemporaries who were heedless by giving themselves up to degeneration: ואנכי השמדתי את האמרי מפניהם אשר כגובה ארזים גבהו וחסן הוא כאלונים ואשמיד פריו ממעל ושרשיו מתחת. “And I destroyed the Amorite before them, whose height was like the height of cedars, and strong was he like the oak trees, yet I destroyed his fruit from above and his roots from beneath”.

V. 19. ומה הארץ אשר הוא ישב בה is the question regarding the significance of the land as the basis for human beings. Above it said ואת העם הישב עליה, it looked on the inhabitants apart from the soil, how had they developed on it. Here the question runs: אשר הוא ישב בה it considers them in the land, how have they formed themselves under the influences brought upon them by the peculiarities of the land which surrounds them, it asks after the value of the land as the planting ground of a national development, הטובה היא אם רעה, whether, in this respect it is “good or bad”, whether it would further or hinder the spiritual and moral cultural life of a nation. We think of the experience remarked by our sages: אוירא דא״י מחכים “the very air of Israel makes people wise” (Baba Bathra 158b) — מחנים .ומה הערים וגו׳ and מבצרים seem to designate the same contrast as עיר חומה and חצרים אשר אין להם חומה (Levit. 25,29 & 31), מחנים open cities, מבצרים walled, closed cities, only that the difference here is considered primarily in its strategic importance. To the enemy, open cities are of the nature of a מחנה the defence lies solely in the bravery of its people. The walled city, on the other hand, is מבצר, a place difficult to take (cf. Gen. 11,6). In Midrash Rabba living in open cities is taken as a sign of bravery, and in fortified ones, a sign of weakness, “how can you tell what the people’s nature is? if they live in open cities they must be brave and strong, depending on their strength; if in fortified ones they are weak and cowardly.” Moreover, as open cities, according to Levit. 25,31, are considered as pertaining to fields, על שדה הארץ יחשב, they give an important indication of the nature of the occupation of their inhabitants, as we tried to work out in Levit. 25,24.

V. 20. ומה הארץ is finally the question regarding the nature of the soil of the land as the source of food and the national well-being. As the question השמנה היא אם רזה already comprises information as to the fertility or otherwise of the soil, the question היש בה עץ can hardly refer to fruit trees. That would also probably not have been expressed simply by עץ. But we think the question referred to whether there were also forests besides fruitful districts. Forested regions are in themselves places of industry, as they deny the other sources of productive nourishment by agriculture and sheep and cattle breeding. והתחזקתם, have the courage openly to take away samples of the fruit although it makes the purpose of your mission clear. והימים ימי בכורי ענבים, not yet the time of the general or grape harvest when taking some of the fruit could be given another interpretation.

V. 21. ממדבר ציו. From the description of the borders of the land in Ch. XXXIV it is evident that the wilderness of Zin formed the southeastern boundary. There, in V.3 it says ממדבר צין על ידי אדום. And from V.7-9 there it is equally clear that חמת was part of the north-western border. The northern border there is described as a line from the Mediterranean Sea on the west, over חצר עינן, זפרן, צדד, חמת, הר ההר, the latter the extreme north-eastern point. So that חמת belongs to the north-west. Accordingly they traversed the whole land diagonally from south-east to north-west.

V. 22. ויעלו וגו׳ ויבא וגו׳. The singular ויבא is striking. According to Sota 34b it refers to Caleb, who went there to pray on the grave of the forefathers for strength to stand up against the intentions of his colleagues. Confirmation could be found in Deut. 1,36 where it says referring to him ולו אתן את הארץ אשר דרך בה “and to him will I give the land upon which he hath trodden”, and in fact Caleb did get Hebron. Judges 1,20: ויתנו לכלב את חברון כאשר דבר משה “and they gave Hebron to Caleb, even as Moses had said”! But in V.28 the messengers on their return said: ואינו שם. According to that not only Caleb went to Hebron, the home of the Anakites. It was quite specially his colleagues who reported as recorded there and even more explicitly in V.33, of the Anakites and of the impression which the sight of them made on them. Yea, in Deut. 1,28, it was specially the reports of these gigantic sons of Anok which brought the faint-heartedness of the people into complete lack of courage. And in any case there is nothing at all in the context of our verse to make Caleb, or any other individual, the subject of ויבא, and also, in accordance with the cantillation, ויבא is so closely connected with ויעלו, that both seem to be predicates of one and the same subject. We would therefore actually believe that ויבא refers as much as ויעלו to the whole company. But ויבא is put in the singular to indicate that up to Hebron they came “as one man” in complete unison in feelings and unanimity of mind and purpose. “They went up from the south and came in unison until Hebron”. But there they saw the descendants of the race of giants, and the impression these made on them, and probably, as we shall see, the strangeness and the huge dimension of the buildings and the whole appearance of a city built to accomodate its inhabitants brought about the beginning of the wavering alteration in their courage and resolutions. It is not impossible to connect this way of taking it with that quoted from Sota. Until Hebron the predominating influence of Caleb kept them all in the same mood of courage, determination and faith. In Hebron, (due to the above mentioned facts I.L.) Caleb felt the beginning of difference between himself and the others, and this caused him to go alone to the grave of the forefathers to pray for resisting strength and courage. And just because there Caleb’s faithfulness in contrast to the defection of his comrades was decisive, later on at the division of the Land, he received Hebron, and it was just Caleb who conquered the Anakites, the mere sight of whom shattered the courage of his associates. (Joshua 15,14).

ילידי הענק. In V.33 the בני ענק are declared to be הנפילים and מן הנפילים, themselves נפילים (see on Gen. 6,4) or descending from them. A gigantic race of giants, the remains of the original race, or descending from them. Now we know from Joshua 11,21 that “Anakites” lived in several cities and districts in the land and this race of gigantic growth must have formed such a considerable part of the inhabitants that Moses could say of the inhabitants in general עם גדול ורם בני ענקים אשר אתה ידעת ואתה שמעת מי יתיצב לפני בני ענק “a people great and tall, the children of the Anakim whom thou knowest, and of whom thou hast heard saying: Who can stand up before the children of Anak”. (Deut. 9,2). One can also understand from that the description of the cities as ערים גדלת ובצרת בשמים “Cities great and fortified up to heaven” as naturally the houses and cities would have to correspond to the huge dimensions of their occupiers. So that if here these three giants are named as being one of the sights of Hebron, and also called ילידי הענק, and are also specially stressed by the spies in V.28: וגם ילידי הענק ראינו שם these three must have been giants even amongst giants; this must also lie in the expression ילידי הענק which must not be identical with the general term בני הענק .בני הענק are, like the term בני ישראל, the descendants of Anak. Whole generations could lie between them and the old race of giants. Their gigantic stature could still show their descent and nevertheless have sunk to be considerably less than that of their forbears. But ילידי הענק, like the term ילידי בית (Gen. 17,12 & Levit. 22,11) were those who were born to the first Anaks, remainders of the second generation, who, accordingly by their gigantic height overtopping the others, and their extreme age reaching back into the dim past made an overwhelming impression. Thus in Joshua also (XI,21) the three living in Hebron, ששי ,אחימן and תלמי, are called ילידי הענק, the others simply הענקים, and this term is added in XV,14 just specially to distinguish them from the others, after they had already been called בני הענק. And there in XV,13, their father ארבע is mentioned, ארבע אבי הענק from where Hebron had its original name קרית ארבע, and in XIV, 15 there, this man ארבע is called האדם הגדול בענקים the biggest giant amongst the giants. Accordingly his immediate descendants were still living in Hebron.

צען מצרים .וחברון שבע וגו׳ must have been known as a very ancient city, and now here it says that Hebron was even older. It is not impossible that שבע שנים נבנתה does not mean that it was built seven years before Zo’an but that it took seven years to build it, “was seven years in building”, like ויבנהו שבע שנים (I Kings 6,38) and indeed long before Zo’an, which also was well known as a very ancient city. The name קרית ארבע (the city of Arba I.L.) which was its earlier name, indicates that it was built by Arba, the huge ancestor of the race of giants, and קריה designates a strongly fortified city. Cf. לא היתה קריה אשר שגבה ממנו Deut. 2,36. Accordingly Hebron presented the view of an overpoweringly strong citadel out of ancient times built up with great perseverance, by giant hands and so increased the overwhelming impression which the giant inhabitants made on the newcomers.
V. 23. אשכל. See Gen. 27,45. מוט, see Levit. 26,13.

V. 26. וילכו ויבאו וגו׳. At their return they had already decided beforehand not to go first to Moses and Aaron, but to give the result of their investigations immediately to the people. And just thereby they showed the malevolence of their behaviour. Had their intentions been good, whatever conclusions they might have arrived at, they would first have made their report to Moses and Aaron and sought advice and instructions. But that was just what they did not want. They thought that the only means for their own and the people’s salvation lay in opposition to Moses and Aaron. Their report took the form at once of an accusation against Moses and Aaron in the presence of all the people and a call to these latter to save themselves from the ruin with which they were threatened by Moses and Aaron’s intentions. ויראום את פרי הארץ: their whole report is an explanation of what they believed to be their incontestable argument. From the extraordinary size of their fruit they can form some idea of the overpowering size of the type of men and the whole corresponding strength of everything else in the whole country.

V. 28. אפס, literally, nothing: but all this is nothing, loses all value for us, for the people are too strong for us. בצרות גדלת מאד, not חצרות גדלת, enormously strongly fortified, built by giants to resist giants, so that for ordinary people they are completely impregnable. וגם ילידי הענק, see above, on V.22.

V. 29. עמלק וגו׳. The whole land is sketched. The south is rendered inaccessible by the Amalakites; the inhabitants of the centre, the Hittites etc. are protected by the Lebanon range of mountains running from nor:h to south (יושב בהר I.L.); the sea and the Jordan form the bulwarks on the west and east. They had already experienced the power of the sword of Amalek. The Amalakites were not actual inhabitants of the land. But they were in their close neighbourhood and they could well fear a sudden attack if they attempted an invasion on the south.

V. 30. ויהס, the Hiphil of הסה, phonetically related to חשה, to be silent. הסה always expresses a suppressed sound. Thus in Habakuk 2,20; Zach. 2,17 and elsewhere. Caleb tried to quieten the people against Moses. Immediately on the report of the spies the vexation of the people wi:h Moses broke out. We can understand why here, where it was a matter of supporting Moses, it was not Joshua but Caleb who stepped forth. Through the close association of Joshua and Moses, his reassurance would carry little weight with the people.

V. 32. ויציאו וגו׳ (דבת, see on Ex. 37,2). In this defamation of the land their sin reached its height. Not ויביאו as in the case of the brothers of Joseph, but — ויציאו, they produced, fabricated bad news of the land (רמב״ן). By that they completely frightened the people, scared them away from attempting the conquest. Even if they were to succeed, to have to live there would be a misfortune. It is a land that wears down, exhausts its inhabitants. It is a land that is not designed for people of ordinary size. It demands the constitution of giants. Ordinary people soon become moribund there. That is why the inhabitants have developed into such extraordinary size. Small and weak people do not survive there (רמב״ן).

V. 33. את הנפילים ,ושם ראינו, those ancient giants אשר מעולם אנשי השם (Gen. 6,4) of whose enormous size and strength the sagas of the past were full, those we actually saw with our own eyes. These were the giant brothers living in Hebron, the ילידי הענק (V.22 & 28); בני ענק מן נפילים are the other Anakites living in the land, who were also descended from the נפילים (see above on V.22).

Moreover, the fact that there were still remnants of the antediluvian Nephilim living in Palestine could be in accordance with the opinion, given in Zebachim 113a, that לא ירד מבול לא״י that the land of Palestine was spared from the flood. Then the land could have kept some of the original strength of the earth which under a Canaanite people showed itself only in production of bodily greatness. But it could also have made it suitable to be the soil for the People of God,who, by fulfilling the Torah of God, strive to achieve the ideal of spiritual and moral greatness, and who were thereby to begin a Paradise-like rejuvenation of the world. (See on Gen. 3,19 at end of notes). Let us not forget that the Gemorra teaches that bodily strength and health form one of the preliminary conditions for the highest spiritual development, and, if we are not entirely deceived, that, which, where the mind lies fallow, begets gigantic bodies; in races which are inclined preferably to mental and spiritual directions can become used up by such activities without the great bodily growth having the benefit of it.

V. 1. ותעוא כל העדה את קולם ויתנו את קולם ותשא וגו׳. They first broke out in a great cry at the bad news and then let their voices go in wailing and complaining. בלילה ההוא, according to Taanith 29a, that was the night of the ninth of Ab, the day on which also in the future, the saddest and most tragic catastrophies of the nation’s downfall occurred. This could explain the ההוא by which that night could be marked to be noted for the future.
V. 2. וילנו וגו׳. The grumbling was universal, and all the men who had the right to represent the “congregation” came directly to Moses and Aaron with accusations.

V. 5. ויפל וגו׳. By the נתנה ראש of the previous verse the people renounced their allegiance, thereby on their side their mission had come to an end. They threw themselves down before קהל עדת וגו׳ .כל קהל וגו׳ is the council entrusted with the leadership of the people, the elders (see Ex. 12,6). By throwing themselves down before them they gave their leadership back to the people, and expressed thereby that with this renouncement by the people of obedience to them, their power was at an end, and humanly they could do nothing further.

V. 6. ויהושע וגו׳. Here, in קריעה, in the feelings of grief for Moses at the complete shattering of his mission and at the fateful sin of the people, it is Joshua who stands prominent. קרעו בגדיהם, as soon as they saw the direction the matter was taking, they, in contrast to their colleagues, rent their garments.
V. 7. טובה הארץ מאד מאד, not only is it not a land which אוכלת את יושביה but it is טובה מאד מאד very very good.

V. 8. אם חפץ וגו׳, and our taking possession of it only depends on our remaining worthy of God’s satisfaction with us. ארץ אשר היא וגו׳ expresses the whole degree of their disgust at the slanderous report of the land. They have seen the land and it is indeed in truth as it has always been pictured and promised to them. זבת חלב ודבש.

V. 9. ואתם “and ye” — all that can be thought of of spiritual greatness, of moral nobility, of Divine destination, of the “bond-nearness” to God, in the thought of Israel’s past and its future destination lies summed up in this “and ye”. Let them be the most mighty giants with castles and fortresses of solid granite you should have no fear of them. Before the consciousness of your strong spiritual and moral power in God and with God, they should dissolve into their nothingness. You should be ashamed to be afraid of them! — כי לחמנו הם expresses the complete lack of resistance and importance of these people, — spiritually and morally degenerate and demoralized, and only imposing in their material physique — against the godly, spiritual and moral principles which are to combat them in Israel. סר צלם וגו׳: they only continue to exist for as long as they remain in safety, hidden in the shade of being left alone. But with us, God and His Truth and His Justice intervening for the salvation of mankind comes to them. And in the light of that Truth and Justice, the protecting shade vanishes and their depravity appears in the full clear light, and in that depravity they are condemned and destroyed, — fear them not!

V. 10. נראה באהל מועד. In the moment when the downfall of the whole nation was threatened because they had become unworthy of their mission and destination, the Glory of God could only find a place for Itself within (not on I.L.) the Sanctuary of the Torah. The Torah deposited there, and the future that was promised for it there, would remain even if the whole of any contemporary generation become lost for it.

V. 11. נאץ ,ינאצני (phonetically related to נחץ, urgently pressing away) means to hasten away from something as it is completely unworthy to be considered. It is the highest degree of scorn which does not consider the object worth consideration. It exactly describes the feelings of the people on receiving the report of the spies. In the judgment they had formed over their future, “God” had momentarily completely ceased to be a factor to be considered.
V. 12. ואורשנו. “I will drive them completely out of existence here below.

V. 13. ויאמר משה וגו׳. Moses quite understands God’s thoughts, and only mentions the effect which, to his mind, would result on the work of God to which he, as well as the nation, belong as the implements for it to be accomplished. God’s work for the future of mankind will not become lost by the destruction of the whole of the contemporary generation. Let another four hundred years pass and there can be another Abrahamic nation coming from Moses which can offer itself to carry on the Abrahamitic promise. But in the meantime the destruction of the people will work just against the enlightment of the nations of the world which was one of the principle purposes for which Israel had been chosen. The eyes of both the cultured nations of that time, the Egyptians and Phonecians, were already directed on these people as the “People of God”, and they follow with anxious tension its national history. They have received some idea from it of a future All-Mighty God with free power over everything to direct the world for the salvation of Mankind and Justice, Who, just with the introduction of this people into the midst of the nations proclaimed war against the gods. The Egyptians — for they themselves have seen and felt Thy Power with which Thou didst raise this people out of their midst up to Thee and took them on the long journey to the land that Thou had promised them. The Phonecians — for they also have heard of the Might of God revealing leading and protecting these people who are threatening them — כי העלית וגו׳ until מקרבו, as well as שמעו until לילה, is in parenthesis. Then והמתה takes up the thread of the thought again, and as there has been a longish interruption, comes back to the אכנו בדבר. The way these sentences run is:- If You do this, the Egyptians will say to the Phonecians — both of them have already become aware of You and are anxiously watching for Your further guidance of this people — so that if You now suddenly make an end of the whole nation, they will say to these nations who have heard of You: מבלתי יכלת etc. Such a denouncement would thereby just go against Your purpose with Israel, t would only strengthen the nations in their denying Your supreme overpowering Might. And indeed, the initiative for taking such a regrettable view of the event would come from Egypt who had already been forced to recognise Your Power in such a painful manner.

V. 14. ואמרו וגו׳. (See notes above on V.13) — עין בעין: “the human eye sees Thy Eye”, human beings see that You see, are conscious of Your Seeing Presence of earth. — ובעמד ענן אתה הלך לפניהם, You go in front of them and show them the way to the land which You have promised them.

V. 15. והמתה וגו׳. (See on V.13). והמתָה, if now You, Who have so publicly proclaimed Your intention to lead this people into the Land, instead of doing so, כאיש אחד, make the whole nation die suddenly in an abnormal manner. Clearly this כאיש אחד contains the idea that if the fathers who have become unworthy for the Land were to die off gradually in a natural way, and their children come into the Land in their stead, the recognition of God among the nations would not suffer. It is only the sudden general death which had been announced, by which the promise of God could only be expected to be realised after centuries had passed, which would give occasion for that misconception.
V. 16. יכלת, a noun, like יבשת המים (Gen. 8,7), קטרת etc.

V. 17. ועתה and “now” — if, accordingly, perhaps other considerations may prevail against carrying out what, on the other hand, is the richly deserved destruction, Thou hast granted me an insight into the ways of Thy Ruling of the world; into the whole infinite greatness and manifold variety of Thy “Goodness”, and see, — is not this exactly a case for the exercise of Thy Power in its true greatness. יגדל נא, the sign of the future tense is stressed by a large י. All the miraculous and mighty Power which Thou hast shown up till now in Egypt and in the wilderness does not reach up to the greatness in which Thy כח would appear, Thy world creating, world bearing, world conquering “strength” to accomplish Thy purpose, — all this is כח —, if, in face of such a fall, such defection, Thou art — as Thou hast proclaimed Thy Way of ruling to be — ארך אפים רב חסד נשא עון ופשע “of long-enduring patience and full of love, lifting away iniquity and revolt”. And even if נקה לא ינקה Thou does not grant remission from obligation, yet פוקד עון אבות על בנים rememberest the iniquity of fathers על שלשים ועל רבעים unto the third and fourth generation. The heathen thought regards the strength and greatness of its gods in their power of destruction. Not destructive might, but כח “strength” is the thought we have of the greatness of the true God. “Strength” which knows how creatively to change opposition into the happiest agreement with His plans; “strength” which has the power to hold on to the almost disappearing sparks of harmonious agreement in the strongest opposition, and, in the course of time, to fan them up to open the way for conversion; “strength”, in the slow progressive development of His methods of educating mankind, to allow centuries to shrink into seconds; “strength” which has infinite “patience” for it has the whole of eternity before it.

ועתה יגדל נא כח אדני כאשר דברת לאמר, the sudden destruction of the whole nation would indeed be a demonstration of Thy Might, but Thy “Strength” would show itself in all its greatness if Thou wouldst let it live, and in spite of them, and with them, and through them, and in them achieve Thy purpose which they so scornfully reject. And here he calls God “אדני״ My Master, by that Name which those who are called upon to be the tools in the service of God designate their relation to Him. For he is appealing to just those methods of God’s ruling, the כח, “strength” by which He educates men and nations, which God revealed to him when he prayed to Him, after the great first national sin, to give him an insight into His ways, to accompany him and help him in his task of carrying out his mission (refer to Ex. 33,12 et seq.).

V. 18. ה׳ ארך אפים וגו׳, and he brings into prominence those measures of God’s ruling which had been revealed to him to which he would specially appeal in this case. ארך אפים is the most prominent and comes first: having long-enduring patience for obtaining satisfaction for a justified demand. Instead of the immediate destruction which they had deserved, the people would, by the exercise of this measure, be given time, long time, to think over, to better themselves, to rise out of their fall, to regain what they had lost by their folly. And רב חסד that rich abundance of love, which is not parsimonious with love, which always keeps a reserve of love, which gives and gives again and is prepared to give it again at the thousandth time after it has been spurned nine hundred and ninety-nine times. נשא עון ופשע: the lifting up (נשא I.L.) of iniquity and rebellion, of departure from the straight path done consciously but caused by passion or desire (עון I.L.) or even of direct rebellion against the laws of God (פשע I.L.) so that the weight of the sin should not weigh one down. Finally that depth of the greatness of God’s loving rule that considers every present time in conjunction with its future. It considers men in conjunction wi:h their children, the contemporary generation in its future generations. Arid while He, for the sake of purifying men, generations or times, to save them from moral ruin, נקה לא ינקה, does not let the smallest sin go unavenged, still spreads the chance for repentance over generations, arid before He passes sentence on the grandfather looks on the greatgrandson who perhaps may recover his senses and climb back to the moral heights from which the greatgrandfather had sunk down — ונקה לא ינקה פקד עון אבות על בנים על שלשים ועל רבעים. (See Ex. 34,6 et seq. and XX,5).

בנים here is used in the sense of descendants generally, and first the idea of God’s “method of ruling” is given by אבות על בנים and then its limit is added by על שלשים ועל רבעים. For שלשים are greatgrandchildren, and if בנים meant just direct children, בני בנים grandchildren, which are specifically mentioned in Ex. 34,7, would be missing here, and also in Ch. 20,5.

V. 19. כגדל חסדך .סלח נא, similarly the Psalm of Providence, CXLV, glorifies the “greatness” of God especially in describing His Love. — וכאשר נשאת לעם הזה וגו׳ the whole history hitherto, from Egypt till now, has been nothing but a manifestation of Thy forgiving love exercising toleration of their going astray and sinning, and not allowing them to go to their deserved destruction under the weight of their sinning. Both ideas — forgiveness and “lifting up the burden of the sin” lie in the concept נושא עון. The one who is נושא עון both takes the sin on himself, assists the sinner to bear it, and finds other ways for repentance and healing than complete ruination. It repeatedly says לעם הזה ,העם הזה, their present behaviour is no contradiction to their previous behaviour, it is only the summit of defection to which it has also up to now constantly been swinging.

V. 20. ויאמר ה׳ סלחתי כדברד. “And God said, I have forgiven, in accordance with what you have said”. God had already beforehand decided to forgive for the very reasons that Moses had adduced. He had only declared to Moses in V.12 what should really happen to the people, were it not for these considerations, and at the same time also to give Moses an opportunity to exercise his perfect selflessness. Not the slightest trace of bitterness did he feel towards the people whose revolt was primarily directed against him, and nothing tempting did he find in the glorious prospect of becoming a second Abraham, to be the ancestor of the promised People of God. Only to such an ענוה, to such a completely selfless character is it granted to elevate itself to a perception of the ways of God’s management, to have a human insight which meets that of God. Only for such a person is it possible to have the objective view of matters completely undisturbed by subjectivity which such a perception presupposes (cf. the preliminary condition of עשיר to נבואה), (Ex. on VI,14). In Ps. 99,6, the nearness of God to Moses, Aaron and Samuel is described by the favourable response which God gave to their invocations: קראים אל ה׳ והוא יענם. But in this קראים the א is mute, and it is read קורים as if it came from the root קרה. We believe that in this mode of the word being written in one way and pronounced in another, the secret is revealed why just they, more than other mortals could reckon on a favourable response to their prayers. With them, in what they asked from God they “met” Him. They asked for nothing that was not suitable. With their entreaties they placed themselves on the stand-point of the thoughts of God’s methods of ruling the world, so that their considerations met God’s thoughts halfway. It is exactly what is expressed by the סלחתי .סלחתי כדברך: we have already in Gen. 24,21 indicated the relationship of סלח to שלח and צלח. Here we have סלח in this, its real proper meaning. By their sin the whole progress of the nation was hindered. God’s kindness and His Wisdom in His ruling gave it access again to the possibility of such a progress.

V. 21. ואולם חי אני וגו׳. These could be just the factors which we tried to indicate on V.17 and 18 as the motive for the measure of God’s rule, ארך אפים to be applied in this case. As sure as חי אני, I am Eternal and could postpone the achievement of My goal from any present time to any future time, and as sure as ימלא כבוד ה׳ את כל הארץ, My Glory will fill the whole of the world, Israel’s mission lies in bringing the Light to the whole of mankind, so sure do these two factors speak against destroying the nation, but equally sure is that,

V. 22—23. כי כל האנשים וגו׳, the pardoning can be no absolute one. That all the men to whom all the God-revealing experiences up till now have not sufficed to win their hearts and minds to limitless confidence in God have thereby shown their unworthiness and unfitness for possessing the Land. הראים את כבדי, they have seen the whole “weight” of My Greatness, they have “seen” כבדי, for them God did not remain merely a thought, a belief, a presentiment, they had actual physical, material experience of Him; they had experience of Him as the mightiest force, as the Almighty force in the midst of all concrete earthly mighty forces; אתתי אשר עשיתי וגו׳, they have seen His “signs”, have experienced His deeds in Egypt and in the wilderness, in the midst of a powerful nation of the most highly developed human culture, and in the midst of a waste where all the help of human culture was lacking. They have seen how all the pomp and power in the one case crumbled to nothing in disobedient opposition to the Will of God, and how the other was changed for those who obeyed Him, simply by faithfully giving themselves up to His Will, into a homely place for human existence and living. They have seen all this, ten times already, in the various camps have they put God to the test, doubting in the reality of God’s intervention in earthly matters, and have tried out and found the actual sincerity, the dependability, the actuality, the sufficiency of His promised succour, ולא שמעו בקולי, and still have not learnt to obey God. אם יראו, firm and irrevocable is it, as an oath (see Gen. 21,23), that they shall not come to see the Promised Land.

אם יראו — הראים. It seems to us as if these two terms are in close relation to each other and that that is why instead of the usual אם יבואו אל הארץ here that coming to the Land is expressed by ראיה. The Land that זבת חלב ודבש, that, as the Land of the People of the Torah, is to develop to unimagined fullness of blossom and blessing, can only attain that destiny if to the people under whose sway it is to develop to that height, God, and God’s rule, and God’s Presence is at least as real, does actually intervene in earthly matters as much as the land itself, if the people “see” God as much as they “see” the Land. For everything which they had experienced in Egypt and in the wilderness had no other purpose than to bring them to this seeing God; to plant deep and unchangeable in their hearts and minds that fear of God and that trust in God which thereafter made them fear nothing else in the whole world, and trust in nothing else in the whole world than God. But the very opposite of this “seeing God” in the Land is ניאוץ ה׳, that frame of mind which, as we explained on V.11, considers God as “nothing” in matters of material welfare, and hurries away from “Him” in considering prosperity. Hence אם יראו את הארץ אשר .נשבעתי לאבתם וכל מנאצי לא יראוה

וכל מנאצי לא יראוה. Ps. 106,24-27 looks back on this phase in the development of our history with the description:- וימאסו בארץ חמדה לא האמינו לדברו וירגנו באהליהם לא שמעו בקול ה׳ וישא ידו להם להפיל אותם במדבר ולהפיל זרעם בגוים ולזרותם בארצות. “Yea, they despised the pleasant land, they believed not His word; they grumbled in their tents and hearkened not unto the voice of God. Then He lifted up His Hand against them to let them fall in the wilderness, and to let their descendants fall among the nations and to scatter them in the lands”; according to that, the future loss of the Land and the dispersion amongst the nations was proclaimed at the same moment in which the fate of the generation that went out of Egypt was declared. Well could that future being driven out of the land be announced in this וכל מנאצי לא יראוה (see רמב״ן thereon). If, in the future, the children fall back into the same state of blindness which allowed their fathers to throw away their opportunity to enter the Land of God’s Torah, it will not allow them either to remain in possession of the Land. And indeed we could well say:- the ארך אפים method of God’s Rule which allowed the fate of complete destruction to pass over the immature generation, and led the sons begotten and to be begotten by it into the Land, included the whole sequence of the following centuries in that plan of education which was introduced here by it, and have looked for the complete realisation of His purpose even beyond our own present time. For the generation begotten by the generation of the wilderness, to whom the prospect of entering the Promised Land was held out, was still by no means at the complete mature height of their calling. The whole of their twofold occupation of the Land as well as their twofold exile from the land until this very day is nought but the ארך אפים, the patiently guided way of education to our spiritual and moral destination; and the pure, complete, permanent, faithful devoted realisation of the Torah even today still belongs to the future. With וכל מנאצי לא יראוה the whole sequence of our history was given.

V. 24. ועבדי כלב. His faithful fearless standing up for following God’s behests made him worthy of the highest designation of a human being working for God, עקב .עבד ה׳, (see Gen. 22,18). היתה רוח אחרת עמו probably means:- a different spirit supported him, a different way of looking at things and a different will saved him from the sin of his comrades. מלא ,וימלא אחרי occurs frequently with the meaning of fulfilling a word, a promise, a wish. Thus, למלא דבר ה׳ (I. Kings 22,6), ימלא ה׳ כל משאלותיך (Ps. 20,6). So that it can also mean: he fulfilled the duty expected from him, inasmuch as אחרי, he followed Me, he remained faithful to Me, not like his comrades סר מאחרי ה׳. Or אחרי can be understood as just the object of וימלא: he fulfilled following after Me, i.e. he fully carried out the loyalty due to Me. וזרעו יורשנה cf. את אשר יורישך כמוש (“that which Chemouth (your god) bequeaths to you” Judges 11,24). Caleb is the subject and זרעו the object of יורשנה. He will bequeath it to his children, whereas with the others, their children will be the first possessors of the Land.

V. 25. והעמלקי וגו׳ בעמק: on the other side of the mountain ridge before which they were encamped. So that they could not proceed without fighting, and for this fight God’s support was lacking (Rashi). So that, in accordance with the fate that had been declared for them, that they were not to enter the Land, they were immediately to turn away from the Land and turn back into the wilderness of the Red Sea.

V. 26. וידבר ה׳ וגו׳. Verses 11-25 contained only the information in general of the future which now lay before the people. Here the more precise details were given. They were given to Moses and Aaron for they were together appointed as leaders of the people (Ex. 6,26), whose further fate was now to suffer such a disastrous change. Together they were given the task to make the people understand this change from the right point of view and take its lesson to heart.

V. 27. עד מתי לעדה וגו׳. In Megilla 23b this is taken to refer to the spies who returned and were “מלינים עלי״ provoked the revolt against God. The general rule that ten men joined together for a common purpose constitute the concept of a congregation is referred to the use of the term עדה here. — מלינים, see on Ex. 16,2.
V. 28. אמר אליהם, to both, to the complaining people (V.2) and to those who invited them to it. נאם ה׳: see Gen. 5,30 at end of notes thereon. — כאשר דברתם (V.2 לו מתנו).

V. 29. פגריכם: those primarily addressed are the speakers of the people (V.2) who formulated and brought the accusations. וכל פקדיכם are all the rest, the men, from 20 years upwards who are duty bound to public service, on whom the community reckons and who were counted for the community (see Ch. 1). On this virile core of the nation, the machinations of the returned spies should have been wrecked, and above all, the intelligent section of the people who acted as spokesmen for the masses should have exerted their influence to bring that about. Instead of which, just these influential men brought the universal dissatisfaction to a formulated complaint and open revolt. (V.2-4). It is understandable that all the men מבן עשרים ומעלה, from twenty years upwards, were treated as guilty.
V. 32. פגריכם אתם, the אתם stresses once again the contrast between the fate that awaits you to that of your children.

V. 33. ובניכם יהיו רעים, inasmuch as the fate that is to befall the children is designated by the term רעה, being shepherded, tended, it expresses that at the same time this wandering is to bring them maintenance and thriving. ישאו את זנותיכם, here we have a living commentary on פוקד עון אבות על בנים. In the unavoidable consequence according to the natural course of things, the children will be affected by the fate which these parents had earned, but at the same time, this suffering of the children with the parents bring the children unending well-being and salvation. For just this forty-year wandering was the university for the Jewish nation for becoming penetrated with the spirit of the Torah and an immutable trust in God, which was to — and is to — reach its true full maturity only after centuries. — זנותיכם: for the children to be implicated in the suffering, the sin in its relation to God is regarded as an apostasy, as it was just the altered attitude towards God which brought about the fate under which the children had to suffer. For the parents themselves, the real delinguets, the sin (V.34) is regarded objectively as עון, a divergence from the straight path. But in both cases the plural form is used: עונתיכם ,זנותיכם, your defections, your divergencies. The fate which is now falling is the fruit of the whole series of sins and divergencies of which they had been guilty.

V. 34. תרתם ,במספר הימים וגו׳: “ye investigated”; the nation, by its messengers in whose sin they, too, joined. יום לשנה וגו׳: by fitting this time of the duration of the punishment in proportion to the sin, the sin is kept in the minds of the penitents during the whole course of the duration of the punishment. This method, by which, simply by using some external similarity of numbers, something is brought to, and kept in, the mind, is frequently used by our sages in their institutions. Thus ,ג׳ קרואים ז׳ קרואים כנגד וכו׳, י״ח ברכות כנגד וכו׳, and the question when certain numbers are fixed is always raised: הני כנגד מי, and, like here, there is always some inner reference explaining the fixing of any particular number in the institutions of our sages. — תנואתי. The noun תנואה only occurs here and once elsewhere in Job 33,10, הניא .הן תנואות עלי ימצא, a hiphil form, means to refuse, to deny. נוא, the Kal, accordingly, to suffer refusal, denial, to be prevented from carrying out an intention by being refused, denied (see Gen. 12,13 at end of notes). So that the quotation from Job would mean: “See he tries to find refusals from me”, i.e. he wants to find things that I have refused him, have not rendered to him. תנואתי here would then be: the refusals I have endured from you. I wished to lead you to the way to your happiness, you refused to accept My Will, you will learn to know the unhappiness into which people fall when they refuse to go on the way that God indicates.

V. 35. העדה הרעה וגו׳ are all the adult men הנועדים עלי who united in the revolt against Me. במדבר הזה יתמו, their destiny does not extend beyond this wilderness, they shall not come out of this wilderness alive.
V. 36. וילינו וגו׳ להוציא וגו׳, they brought the whole congregation of Israel to revolt against God by calumniating the Land.
V. 43. כי על כן (see Gen. 18,5). For I only say this so that you should not venture to go up, because you turned back from following God.
V. 44. ויעפלו (see Gen. 4,2). They insisted, remained obstinate.

V. 45. בהר ההוא in that mountainous region. Above in V.25 it says that they lived בעמק, not בהר on the mountain but in the highlands, in a valley on the other side of the height up which they wanted to go. ויכתום, similarly in Deut. 1,44. ויכתו אתכם seems to be a hiphil form of כתת to smash, or rather the kal of נכת, like ואֶכת אותו טחון (I smashed it into smithereens) but then the normal form should be ויְכתוב; perhaps the Pathach is used to correspond to וַיַכום and is also kept in Deut. 1,44 where וַיַכתו is said alone, and in this form ויכום and ויכתום go together “they smote them to smithereens.”

V. 1. The laws contained in this chapter are in close connection with the fateful events reported in the two previous chapters. And indeed to such a degree that they seem to be given just with regard to them, as will appear from a closer consideration of their contents. The first law is the פרשת נסכים, the law of the מנחה (the flour offering) and the נסך (the wine) which were to be added to every עולה (elevating-offering) and שלמים (a meal-of-peace offering).

V. 2. נסכים .דבר וגו׳ כי תבאו וגו׳ have already been ordained to be brought as a constant accompaniment to the Tamid-offering (Ex. 29,40 & 41), as well as then in Ch. 28,29 again for the מוספין. According to Kiddushin 37a & b (see Rashi thereon and ד״ה לא קרבו ,תוספות) our chapter speaks primarily of קרבנות יחיד, and there we are given two opinions on the way our verse is to be taken. According to ר׳ ישמעאל in the wilderness only קרבנות צבור were accompanied by נסכים (the Tamid and Mussaf offerings — see Menachoth 45, 6 שכל האמור בחומש הפקודים קרב במדבר). The duty imposed here, to accompany every קרבן יחיד too, i.e. also offerings that can be brought בנדר ונדבה, viz. עולה and שלמים, with נסכים only began בארץ, and indeed only after ירושה וישיבה, after the complete conquest of, and settling down in the Land, a condition which is expressed here by כי תבואו אל ארץ .מושבותיכם which attaches the law given here to entry and settlement. In the fourteen years of conquest and division of the land, שבע שכבשו ושבע שחלקו (seven for the complete conquest and seven for dividing it up) during which the משכן had only a provisional home in Gilgal and במות were permitted (see Deut. 12,8 & 9) no נסכים were yet brought with קרבנות יחיד. This duty only commenced משעת איסור במות when the משכן received a permanent home in Shilo. But according to ר׳ עקיבא the duty to bring נסכים also for קרבנחת יחיד applied immediately it was given here like the already existing duty for קרבו נסכים ,קרבנות צבור במדבר; and the כי תבאו אל ארץ מושבתיכם was rather to ,להטעינה נסכים בבמה קטנה, to make it encumbent to bring נסכים during the fourteen years after entry into the Land when the Sanctuary was provisionally in Gilgal, and במות יחיד were permitted to be used everywhere בכל מושבתיכם, wherever there was a settlement of the people. (במת יחיד is called במה קטנה in contrast to the מזבח in the משכן which, during the period of היתר במות was also called the במת צבור — as the national altar, and also במה גדולה. (Zebachim, 111a).
V. 3. ועשיתם אשה לה׳ וגו׳ belongs to the introductory sentence כי וגו׳ of the previous verse.

זבח ,עולה או זבח includes שלמים and תודה; although the latter is accompanied by לחמי תודה it still requires the extra מנחה ונסך ordered here. פלא נדר ;לפלא נדר occurs at the moment the vow is made הרי עלי; the bringing of the offering is only fulfilling it. So that the ל- in לפלא can only mean “for”. But at a הרי זו ,נדבה is the first act, the הקדש, the dedication of the animal itself to be an offering, is already a procedure of the offering and comes under the conception of the term הקרבה (see Levit. on Ch. 1,3). Hence the ב in בנדבה, at the dedication or through the dedication the עשית אשה begins. By פלא נדר או נדבה the law which follows here is limited to such categories of offerings which can be brought בנדר ונדבה, and these indeed even if they are brought as חובה as is immediately indicated by the addition of או במעדיכם for this must refer to חובות הבאות מחמת הרגל, offerings which one is bound to bring on festivals, עולות ראייה ושלמי חגיגה. So that what are excluded are:- הבכור והמעשר והפסח והחטאת והאשם, catagories which are only possible to be brought as duty-offerings. The only exception would be חטאתו של מצורע ואשמו, (see Levit. 14,10). מן הבקר או מן הצאן excludes עולת עוף (Menachoth 90b and 91a).

V. 4. והקריב המקריב וגו׳ מנחה וגו׳. Although the offering itself is entirely a free-will one, its accompaniment by the מנחה ordained here is compulsory. The מנחה is an essential complement to the offering. Like the עולה or the אימורים of the שלמים, it is burnt in its entirety on the altar.

V. 5. נסך .ויין לנסך in the meaning of pouring never means pouring away but always has the intention of getting the liquid to some certain place. Hence also to cast liquid metal into a mould, and to pour oil of consecration on the head wherefrom we get נסכים, the anointed ones, Kings. The wine of the נסכים was poured into a bowl on the south-west corner on the top of the altar from where it flowed through a shallow cavity into the depth of the foundations of the altar (שיתין) (Succoth 48b and 49b. — see ל״מ on הל׳ מ״ק 2, 1). ויין לנסך As יין is not simply added as a further object of the predicate והקריב of the preceding verse, but by תעשה forms a separate command, this יין is not to be taken as being just one concept together with the סלת and שמן but is to express an independent thought on its own. Thus the Halacha runs in Menachoth 44b הסלת והשמן אין מעכבין את היין ולא היין מעכבן that, in the absence of the wine or the Mincha, the one could be brought without the other. על העולה או לזבח, the thought which is expressed by the wine is co-ordinate with the עולה but, belongs to the זבח.

V. 6. או לאיל. In its first year a sheep is called כבש, after the first month of the second year and onwards איל, during the first month of the second year, פלגס. According to Chulin 23a, the disjunctive conjunction או tells us here that as soon as it is no longer a כבש, even if it has not yet reached the age of becoming an איל and is really a פלגס, it still demands the נכסים of an או לרבות את הפלגס .איל. (In precise terms, the מנחה which has to accompany an עולה or a שלמים is called מנחת נסכים, and by נסכים the wine is understood, but not infrequently both together are designated simply as נסכים; — see תוספות י״ט Shekalim V.1).

V. 7. תקריב ריח ניחח לה׳. Just as above in V.5 the לכבש האחד refers to all the preceeding sentences so here, too, the תקריב refers back to everything that is brought for the איל. And inasmuch as here the נסך יין is put in conjunction with ריח ניחח, a term which otherwise is confined to that which goes on to the altar-fire, thereby the very essential meaning of נסך for the offerings is indicated as their ריח ניחח presupposes נסכים.

V. 8. איל .וכי תעשה וגו׳ and כבש together form the קרבנות מן הצאן which is why איל in V.6 is simply added on, או לאיל תעשה etc., to the עולה and זבח of the כבש. Both express the עולה and שלמים thoughts from the point of view of צאן, of the flock looking up to the Shepherd for guidance and destiny. But בן בקר brings these thoughts to mind from the point of view of a co-worker in God’s work on earth, which is why the נסכים injunctions for בן בקר are again separately introduced. — לפלא נדר או שלמים. This term, the expression נדר or שלמים is very difficult to understand, שלמים is by no means the opposite number to נדר, it itself is either נדר or נדבה and in any case is already included in זבח which comprises שלמים and תודה. What is contrasted to נדר is נדבה as indeed they are paired in exactly the same law in V.3. Perhaps the reason for this strange term might be found in the meaning of בן בקר in offerings. As שלמים is here placed in contradistinction to נדר it is clear that here by נדר only עולה can be thought of, and שלמים would remain for נדבה. It might “perhaps” thereby want to say that, as a rule, from the standpoint of בקר one would not be expected to make שלמי נדר, but rather שלמי נדבה, so that here נדבה could be expressed by שלמים. Consider the frame of mind which would promote the bringing of a שלמים-offering from the point of view of בקר, i.e. from the feeling of joy at the completely undisturbed satisfaction with one’s active life of being a co-worker in God’s fields, helping Him in His work in this world. One can imagine the flowing feeling of being satisfied with the perfect state of one’s working life arising at the complete success of some particular good work that one has undertaken to accomplish, which would urge one to express one’s thankful feelings by there and then dedicating an animal to be a שלמים-offering as the bearer of that glorious moment, i.e. making a נדבה. But נדר, making a vow to bring a בן בקר as a שלמים at some future moment would anticipate the probability of the continuance of perfectly complete satisfaction with one’s work, a feeling of complacent self-satisfaction which the Divine Torah could well see itself inclined to suppress rather than to encourage.
V. 9. והקריב וגו׳, for והקריב המקריב, referring back to V.4 (see note thereon).
V. 10. אשה ריח ניחח לה׳ (see on V.7) (and on Gen. 8,21 I.L.).

V. 11. מיעוטו מעכב את רובו :ככה ,ככה יעשה וגו׳.
