The quantities prescribed here must be adhered to strictly, the slightest deviation whether in deficiency or excess would invalidate the whole (Menachoth 27a, and 11a). לשור האחד, with a שור there is no differentiation for the accompanying נסכים between עגל and פר, its meaning lies in the character of the species. או לשה וגו׳, apart from איל, with animals from the flock, sheep and goats there is no difference in age or sex.

V. 12. כמספר וגו׳. Each animal has to be given the prescribed accompaniment even if the offering consists of more than one of quite similar animals, e.g. two עולות פר בנדר or both בנדבה, or two שלמי כבש בנדר or בנדבה, one מנחה ונסך would not suffice for the two (Menachoth 91a). For the נסכים have not got the subjective character of a personal duty which would be accomplished by one offering but they belong objectively to every עולה or שלמים and none of these are complete as long as its מנחה and נסך are not brought with it or after it. For if the offering had not been accompanied by its מנחה and נסך on the day it was brought, the neglect has to be remedied at some subsequent time (Zebachim 44a). And this defect-remedying offering is so urgently necessary that such נסכים which had not been brought directly with the offering — נסכים הבאים בפני עצמן — were allowed to be brought even at night, מנחתם ,מנחתם ונסכיהם בלילה ונסכיהם למחר (Temura 14a & b).

V. 13. כל האזרח יעשה ככה את אלה להקריב וגו׳. According to Menachoth 104a this announces the permission for an אזרח to bring these נסכים, ordered here as an accompaniment to עולות and שלמים, also as independent offerings and even to bring oil or wine by itself. But even then the prescribed measures given here must be adhered to. Of wine only 3, 4 or 6 logs (i.e. ¼, 1/3 or ½ hin) but not 1, 2 or 5 logs. But of oil 1 log is also permissable as that is the quantity prescribed for מנחת נדבה (Levit. 2,1 et seq.) Menachoth 104a and 107a. But according to רבי (ibid.) oil, too, may only be brought in one of the measures fixed for נסכים, the minimum being 3 logs. This difference of opinion is based on the hermenutic question as to whether דון מינה ומינה or דון מינה ואוקי באתרא, i.e. whether something which derives its general law from another law given in the Torah has to take all its detailed laws also from it דון מינה ומינה, or whether in its detailed laws it goes according to its own special character, דון מינה ואוקי באתרא. The whole law that שמן can be brought by itself just like the wine of the נסכים, finds its legal indication from מנחת נדבה. According to the canon דון מינה ומינה it would have to adjust its quantity also to follow מנחת נדבה. The other canon ואוקי באתרא however would direct the law of its quantity to be similar to נסכים to which it belongs according to character. But this permission to bring נסכים as a separate offering by itself is restricted to אזרח to those belonging to the Jewish nation, אזרח מביא נסכים ואין הנכרי מביא נסכים. Although non-Jews could also bring free-willed offerings on the altar of the Jewish Sanctuary נכרים נודרים נדרים ונדבות כישראל (See Levit. 1,2) they are excluded from bringing נסכים. But although they cannot bring independent נסכים offerings, their offerings nevertheless objectively have to have נסכים brought with them, and these are provided by the Jewish community (Temura 3a). According to one opinion (See Rashi ibid., and ל״מ on מ״ק III,5), they themselves can bring the נסכים belonging to their offerings, and האזרח here only excludes them from bringing them as independent offerings.

V. 14. וכי יגור וגו׳. Whereas, by the אזרח of the preceding verse, the non-Jew is, according to everybody, precluded from bringing independent נסכים, the גר, the גר צדק (see Ex. 12,48) is expressly made equal to the native-born Jew with regards to the duty and the authority of bringing וכי יגור אתכם וגו׳ .נסכים, if now, או אשר בתוככם or at any future time a גר comes to enter your midst (Kerithoth 9a).

V. 15. הקהל. Perhaps in the same sense as מעיני הקהל in Levit. 4,13, and is addressed to the governing body entrusted with the whole guidance of the nation. But according to Kiddushim 73a, it appears to be taken, like קהל ה׳ in Deut. 23,3, as the Jewish people in general. חקה אחת וגו׳: one duty, one law, the same rights (cf. Gen. 47,22). ככם כגר יהיה לפני ה׳, just as here in offerings, so altogether there is complete equality before God, i.e. in all relations of man to God and God to man; and finally in general:
V. 16. תורה אחת ומשפט וגו׳: complete equality in all matters of the Law: בא הכתוב והשוה הגר לאזרח בכל מצות שבתורה (Sifri).

Kerithoth 8b teaches from this expression regarding the offerings, כאשר תעשו כן יעשה (V.15) the Halacha is also derived that for the complete entry of a גר into Judaism, in addition to מילה וטבילה (circumcision and ritual immersion) an offering has to be brought, הרצאת דמים. Just as Israel’s entry into the Bond of the Torah was also expressed by offerings (Ex. 24,5), so, as long as the Temple was standing, every gentile convert to Judaism, after מילה וטבילה had to bring an עולה, either from בהמה or שני בני יונה או שני תורים ,עוף, and until he had done so was precluded from partaking of holy food, מעוכב לאכול בקדשים. But when the Temple is not in existence entry into the Bond of the Torah is not hindered by the impossibility to bring an offering. The Torah itself here, in V.15, anticipates the entry of proselytes at all times או אשר בתוככם לדרתיכם (ibid. 9a).

Accordingly, by this institution of נסכים it is ordained that henceforth no עולת בהמה or שלמים may be brought without its being accompanied by an allegiance-offering of flour and a libation of wine, and moreover separately for each animal offered ,with it or at least following it. Henceforth the Jewish נפש of an individual or of the community as a whole is never to approach God with the expression of dedicating its actions to Him on account of its feelings of its duty (עולה) or from feelings of its happy and harmonious life (שלמים) without bringing to the same altar and the same fire which had received the devotion of the personality, its life and its forces, also the expression of the dedication of its possessions which give it its existence, its well-being and its happiness. That which had already been prescribed for the daily national offering (the תמיד) shall henceforth become a bounden duty to be brought for every עולה or זבח offered by any private individual, — or at least a conditional duty inasmuch as the duty to bring נסכים with a נדר or נדבה only arises as the consequence of the perfectly free-willed vow to bring an עולה or זבח. So that נסכים are not like other מנחת נדבה, or like the offering they accompany, the expression of thoughts and resolutions by which one feels the urge to seek to get nearer to God, they are rather to be understood as an admonition with which the Sanctuary of the Torah demands that every offering which it receives shall be accompanied. With that the completely objective character which is impressed on the נסכים-duty would then agree; it is attached not to the person but to the offering itself. Thus even where, as in the case of a non-Jew, the personality of the bringer does away with the duty, perhaps even the qualification for the נסכים, they still have to be provided by the צבור, by the national Sanctuary (see V.4, 12 and 13). If we consider further what fundamental national meaning the Torah ascribes to this נסכים-duty, and what national qualification it demands for it, so that on the one hand it finds it necessary to specify it solely for the אזרח to the exclusion of the נכרי, and on the other hand not merely expressly to include and qualify the גר for it but raises this duty and qualification of the גר for נסכים to a criterion of his equal rights and equal position within Judaism and Jewry, and thereby to attach the proclamation of this equality before God and the Law in the most ceremonious manner, then it appears to us that the נסכים-idea must touch on the most important fundamental pillars of Jewish nationality and the Jewish calling. Indeed it must be rooted in a factor which is lacking in a גר as such, and without the Torah expressly ordering it would have made us consider him as excluded from the duty of נסכים and as being unqualified to perform it.

But the demand of the Sanctuary for a Mincha and a libation of wine to be added to every עולה and שלמים clearly expresses that this Sanctuary demands that all its adherents shall recognise the fact that for them it is not only the נפש, the thinking, feeling, striving, active life of a person which they are to remember belongs to God and His Torah, but that also all “תירוש ,דגן and יצהר״ (שמן ,יין ,סלת) all the elements which are necessary for his existence, his well-being and his joy in life are no less belonging to God and His holy Torah, come from Him, are dependent on nothing else but Him, and can only be gained by us by fulfilling His Will by “keeping godliness alive on earth”. To our keeping the אש דת, the fire of the Torah burning on the Altar, supplying it with fuel (לחם I.L.), to that alone do we owe our own food, our own existence, as is inserted in the lesson our daily שמע preaches to us: והיה אם שמע תשמעו וגו׳ ונתתי וגו׳ נסכים .ואספת וגו׳ are accordingly the expression of that direct connection between God and the Jewish fate which forms the basis of the Abrahamitic covenant which is fulfilled in Israel, and which equally forms the basis of the Jewish calling for the Torah of God. The expression of just that connection between God and the shaping of the fate of Israel, the non-recognition of which had caused the fateful sin of the Jewish nation, its men and its messengers, in contrast to whom only Caleb realised the truth, and so manfully and truly proclaimed it in his אם חפץ בנו ה׳ (Ch. 14,8). By the truths which נסכים teach, obedience to God is the one sun for our fields, the one sword for our victories so that the ultimate connection between פרשת נסכים and the מרגלים is given by itself, to which also the introductory words in V.2, כי תבאו וגו׳, point, by which the נסכים-duty for private offerings was, according to one opinion, altogether only to start after the conquest of the land, and according to the other had such significant meaning just for that conquest, that even during the time of conquering and before the conquest was completed it had to be performed even on במת יחיד (see V.2). It seems to us also clear why the special inclusion in, and qualification for the duty of נסכים was necessary for גרים, and how the general equality and equal qualifications of proselytes could be attached to this inclusion. A גר lacked descent from forefathers to whose descendants such a direct care of God in their fate had been promised, and also he had no participation in the land which was to be the realisation of that promise. His very name designated the “landless person” (see Gen. 23,4). Just as at the Pesach-offering (Ex. 12,48 & 49, refer to it) so here at נסכים this equality of the גר had specially to be taught, and as here the same direct care of God was assured to the ככם כגר יהיה לפני ה׳ — גר — which, without giving him any direct claim to the land, elsewhere (Deut. 10,18 et seq.) guarantees him humane and civic existence in it, the equality given him in the נסכים institution both implicitly and explicitly assures him of complete equality before the law. Often as the גר and his treatment is mentioned in the Torah, still it is here in פרשת נסכים which is the principle place for asserting his complete legal equality of rights, a fact which quite specially characterises the meaning of this institution of נסכים.

But the addition of נסכים consists of two parts viz. מנחה of סלת סלת עשרון בלול ברבעית ההין שמן (fine flour thoroughly stirred into a quarter of a hin of oil, a hin = 12 logs I.L.), and the real נסכים of יין לנסך רביעית ההין (a quarter of a hin of wine for a libation I.L.). The Mincha accordingly is a מנחת סלת similar to the מנחת נדבה (Levit. 2,1; refer to it). But it differs from that offering in the quantity of the oil. An ordinary Mincha of flour has only one log of oil, the מנחת נסכים gets three times as much. The ordinary Mincha requires הגשה (depositing at the S.W. corner of the Altar I.L.) and קמיצה (taking out an exact handful of the dough I.L.); only this handful is burnt on the altar, the remainder is given to be eaten by the priests (Levit. 7,9 and 10); מנחת נסכים has neither הגשה nor קמיצה and is given in its entirety to the Altar-fire. We believe we can explain these peculiarities of the מנחת נסכים from the nature of what it is meant to represent. In the ordinary free-willed Mincha, the bringer expresses an allegiance to God, and a dedication to God with reference to the possessions of food and well-being which have been granted to him. He is accordingly taught by the Sanctuary to place his possessions, as being granted by God, acknowledgingly at His Altar (הגשה), fully to satisfy all His demands on his possessions (קמיצה) and also only to enjoy the rest of them in a priestly manner (אכילת כהנים). But מנחת נסכים is a general objective expression of what the Jewish people get from God, what He gives directly and specially to the Jewish people as keepers of His Torah, and therefore the possessions given for their existence and comfort belong entirely and absolutely to the fulfilling of His Torah and must be used entirely as fuel to keep the fires of godliness burning on earth. Hence there is no קמיצה ,הגשה, or אכילת כהנים but it is completely and entirely אשה ריח ניחח לה׳. Hence also the rich fullness of oil which only occurs elsewhere in מנחת חבתים. (See on Levit. 6,14 and 15), threefold the amount of an ordinary free-willed Mincha. For here it is not the expression of an individual state of being well-to-do; it is expressing the fact that well-being altogether even in the richest measure of national wealth is exclusively a gift from God; and regarding this, מנחת נסכים and the חביתי כה״ג — which are also 3 logs and entirely given over to the fire on the altar — are considered from a national point of view. The quantity of the סלת (the flour) does not change. It represents simply “existence” and so cannot be increased or decreased, and the quantity עשירית האיפה is fixed with reference to the Manna.

מנחת נדבה has also a קומץ לבונה (a handful of incense) as expressing the feeling of ease and comfort, of satisfaction with the amount of food and degree of comfort granted. This is lacking in the מנחת נסכים, but it is replaced by the still higher expression of the highest degree of satisfaction, the blessed state of joy at the whole tenor of life given by God, expressed by the special offering-procedure, exclusive to the נסכים institution that of the libation of wine which accompanies this Mincha.

That יין “wine” is used in the Scriptures as representing the highest enjoyment, giving pleasure to mind and feelings is clear. “Wine maketh glad the heart of man” (Ps. 104,15). “Wine is enjoyed with song” (Is. 24,9). “Wine rejoiceth life” (Ecel. 10,19). “Give strong wine to the unhappy ones, wine unto those that be of heavy hearts”. (Prov. 31,6). “Their hearts shall rejoice as though with wine” is the expression of the highest joy. (Zach. 10,7). “Thy love is better than wine” (Song of Songs 1,2), is the expression of the highest happiness of love. “Wine and milk” are metaphors for the happiness and sustenance which the Torah gives (Is. 55,1).

Equally well-known and frequent is wine used to represent the portion of happiness which God grants to individuals and nations, and hence “cup” is used as an expression for divine decrees, fate. “For in the Hand of God there is a cup, and the wine is strong and fully mixed and He dispenseth therefrom, but the dregs thereof all the wicked of the earth shall wring them out and drink them (Ps. 75,9). Thus there is a cup of wrath, a mighty goblet of stupor (Is. 51,18), but also a cup of happiness and salvation (Ps. 116,13) and a cup of consolation (Jer. 16,7). The Babylonian might, the power that altered the fate of many nations is “a golden cup in the Hand of God” (ibid. LI,7). Under the guidance of God the cup of the pious ones is always overflowing (Ps. 23,5), yea, God is the sum-total of their portion in life and their “cup” (ibid. XVI,5).

If we take all this together and add to it that in Ch. 28,7, the נסכים-procedure is expressed as בקדש הסך נסך שכר לה׳, so that the wine of the נסכים is regarded in its strong spiritual power, then we surely do not go wrong if we see in the נסכים-wine the expression brought into the Sanctuary of our highest earthly blissfulness. This wine, the expression of our supreme happiness is received in a vessel of the Sanctuary, a כלי שרת, holy, belonging to God, and, not poured out, but “poured in” (V.5) to the depth of the foundations of the altar. This pouring down expresses the thought that our highest earthly bliss in itself is not the summit of our endeavours, but, just as it comes from God, and from Him alone, so does it again only form the basis of our building our lives upwards towards God, yea in truth, real and permanent happiness only becomes ours if and when and because it does belong to the deep foundation of His Altar.

But then at once it becomes clear that נסכים can only be the accompaniment of עולת בהמה and שלמים. Sin and the consciousness of guilt which are expressed in חטאת and אשם are not compatible with the happy bliss that finds its expression in נסך. The מנחת חוטא (Levit. 5,11) lacks even oil and incense, and the depressed suffering condition out of which all קרבנות עוף result is equally unsuitable for מנחה ונסך. The halachic fact that the שירי הלוים, the songs of the Levite choir singing of God in the history of Israel accompanied just the libation part of the נסכים (Arachin 11a) would then be entirely consonant with our way of taking the meaning of נסכים. These שירים expressed in words that which the בקדש הסך נסך שכר לה׳ expressed in such meaningful symbolic procedure. Even without this we have already indicated the lingual and understandable connection between שכר and שיר on Gen. 9,21.

But if the addition of נסכים to עולה is the avowal of the fact that lies at the base of Jewish life and obligations, viz. that all well-being, all that determines Jewish happiness in life is dependent completely and directly on God, and only on God, is to be gained by cheerful obedience and only by cheerful obedience, then this avowal rises in importance and meaning the higher the social or official position which an individual or the community occupies. That which is a truth to be taken to heart by an individual who is just one member of God’s flock, a כבש is doubly to be taken to heart when his conviction and faith does not only affect his own adherence to duty but when the eyes of his contemporaries rest on him, and because of his social position he has to take the lead as איל in setting the example in obedience to the dictates of God. But the avowal of this fundamental truth of Jewish life gains three times in importance if he is called to be representative of, and co-worker with God’s work on earth, to be a פר in his circle. Did not the מרגלים catastrophe which preceded, and, as we believe was the incentive for the פרשת נסכים arise so fatefully from a deviation from the נסכים-Truth by just such a section of the people, by men who were charged with the commission of leading the community in the work of God, by פרים, who misused their פר calling and turned it to the very reverse. The spokesmen of the community, the אלים allowed themselves to be enticed by them into open rebellion and dragged the whole nation, the כבשים down with them in their apostasy. We believe we can very well understand why henceforth the avowal of the נסכים-Truth was emphasized doubly and trebly for the אלים and פרים of the community by the constant formula for the offering: שלשה עשרנים לפר שני עשרנים לאיל ועשרון לכבש. For the fundamental truth of Jewish acknowledgment will only then become the common possession of the whole of the nation to be the mastering and forming power in their lives if their leaders set the example before them in word and deed in double and treble power. An insight into the meaning of the proportion of the oil and wine to the flour remains difficult. While the flour rises in the proportion of 1, 2, 3 for ,כבש איל and פר respectively and we should have expected the oil and wine simlarly to rise from 1/4 to 1/2 and 3/4 they rise only from 1/4 to 1/3 and 1/2 so that the Mincha of a lamb appears richer in oil than that of a ram or bullock. It has 1/4 of a hin to an עשרון while the ram and bullock only get 1/6 of a hin for each עשרון. Perhaps just by this, the oil and the wine in the מנחת נסכים are shown to be not just accessories to the flour, as a modification of the concept “food”, richer, richest food, but as altogether independent conceptions of well-being in general, the symbolism of their measure remaining not parallel to the measure of the flour. For although in מנחת נסכים the סלת ושמן אין מעכבין זה את זה (see תוספות Menachoth 44b) oil can be brought as בנדבה by itself (see V.13). But if the 1/4 hin of oil and wine is to rise independently then the usual rising scale for fractions viz. 1/4, 1/3, 1/2 would come into play.

But the reason that wine, and according to רבי oil also, may only be brought even בנדבה in the measures fixed for נסכים (V.13) could lie in the objective character which is always to remain applied to this offering. Even in נדבת יחיד the form of the avowal in which the national Sanctuary expresses this fundamental Jewish fact is to be adhered to.

V. 17. וידבר וגו׳. This פרשת חלה which now follows is intimately connected with the preceding פרשת נסכים. If פרשת נסכים makes us take to heart the fact that the food, well-being and happiness of the national prosperity is a direct gift from the ruling of God in general, פרשת חלה teaches us to consider the existence of every home, yea, of every individual person as a special object which God keeps in mind in His Ruling. Not only the rain and sunshine which brings the produce in the fields to ripeness for the nation are messengers directly from God to His land, but also the participation which every home, yea, every individual person has in this general prosperity is again a special act of God within this general ruling for the nation and demands its recognition and taking to heart in חלה.

V. 18. בבאכם אל הארץ. Above on V.2 we have mentioned the various ways in which the expression used there כי תבאו אל ארץ מושבותיכם is taken. In consequence of that difference, here too, there are two conflicting opinions. ר׳ ישמעאל who takes the כי תבאו וגו׳ and the similar כי יביאך, everywhere as after ירושה וישיבה (after conquest and settlement) teaches that here, the unusual term בבאכם indicates that the מצות חלה was to become a duty immediately on entry into the land even during those fourteen years of conquest and settlement. שינה הכתוב ביאה זו מכל ביאות שבתורה ללמדך שכיון שנכנסו לארץ מיד נתחייבו בחלה (Sifri and Kethuboth 25a רבנן דבי רב). But according to the teaching of רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע, in בבאכם lies rather (or more correctly “still more” — see תוספות Nidda 47a, the בבאכם is only the continuation of the ברייתא in Sifri out of which the fact which the רבנן דבי רב allege of the fourteen years of conquest etc. comes; so the סמ״ג in the Sifri also quotes) the demand ביאת כולכם, and the duty of הלה would depend on the nation as a whole being in the land, בביאת כולכם אמרתי ולא בביאת מקצתכם. A future legal result of this difference is, that, according to רבנן דבי רב the duty of חלה בזמן הזה דאורייתא, according חלה בזמן הזה דרבנן :ר׳ הונא בריה דרב יהושע. This בזמן הזה includes all the time after the resettlement under Ezra. For a ברייתא out of סדר עולם quoted in Yebamoth 82b, and in Nidda 46b, teaches from the sentence אשר ירשו אבותיך וירשתה in Deut. 30,5, ירושה ראשונה ושניה יש להן ושלישית אין להם i.e. according to the most general way of taking it (see Rashi and Tosephoth there in Yebamoth) the taking possession of the land under Joshua and the resulting sanctification of the land as being the ground of the Torah for such laws that were attached to this sanctification of the land as שביעית ,מעשרות ,תרומות etc., became lost at the Babylonish exile and had to be re-established by the taking possession under Ezra. But this second taking the land into possession conferred sanctification of it for duties attached to it for all future time and did not become lost by the second exile, so that it does not require a third sanctification for any subsequent repossession. So that the conquest of the Romans and the resulting dispersion did not bring about any alteration in the קדושת הארץ, and those מצות התלויות בארץ which during the period בית שני were דאוריירא in the Holy Land are still duty bound to be kept מדאורייתא to-day. But, according to רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע, nevertheless, for חלה, apart from קדושת הארץ the condition was given by בבאכם that the presence of the whole nation in the land was required, so that even if in the period of בית שני and at the present day, the duty of תרומה ומעשר were דאוריתא, for חלה it would still be דרבנן as this condition was not fulfilled under Ezra, as only a part of the nation returned then, וכי אסקינהו עזרא לאו כולהו סלוק. But according to רבנן דבי רב, just by בבאכם an incomplete possession of the land suffices for חלה, so that even if, by the complete national repossession under Ezra the duty for תרומה and מעשר remained only דרבנן — (כן נלעייד צריכין למימד לסברת רבנן דבי רב דהא אי אפשר לאמר דס״ל דטעמא דמ״ד דרבנן משום דבטלה קדושת הארץ דאי בטלה לתרומה בטלה לחלה, ועוד מאי ראיה מביאין מהא דחלה היה נוהג בז׳ שכבשו וז׳ שחלקו ואם כן י״ל דיש לימוד לתרומות ומעשרות שיהו דרבנן אפי׳ לא דרשינן בבואכם ביאת כולכם גבי חלה ונראה דס״ל דרבנן דבי רב דמ״ד תרומה בזה״ז דרבנן היינו דאין חיובה אלא אחר ירושה וישיבה וירושת עזרא וישיבתו לא מקרי ירושה וישיבה או משום שלא כבשו כל הארץ דשבקו הרבה כרכים או משום שהיו משועבדים למלכי פרם א׳ ע׳ פי כן חלה דאוריי׳ דהא נתחייבו בחלה קודם ירושה וישיבה. ואפשר דלדינא מודה לזה רב הוגא אלא דקאמר אפי׳ למ״ד דזה מקרי ירושה וישיבה ותרומה דאורי׳ מ״מ חלה עוד תנאי אחר לה והיא ביאת כולכם ואפשר שזה עיקר טעם הרמב״ם וצע״ע) — for חלה it would still be רמב״ם .דאוריתא adopts the teaching of רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע that חלה בזמן הזה is only דרבנן, and takes it that, as חלה has also the character of תרומה, the condition for the necessity of ביאת כולכם also applies to תרומה ומעשרות, so that חלה ,תרומה ומעשרות were even in the time of the second Temple in א״י only דרבנן (see כ״מ on הל׳ תרומות I,26). But this extension of the condition of ביאת כולכם to apply also to תרומות ומעשרות, is by no means admitted by everybody, but rather this opinion that קדושת הארץ בזמן בית שני למעשרות ולכל מצות התלויות בארץ ה׳תה מדרבנן is considered by תוספות (there in Yebamoth) as completely unacceptable. So we must take this condition primarily as being characteristic for חלה.

The legal fact, that the effect of ירושה שניה was not ended by the second exile could be ascribed to the fact that, during the whole period of the second Temple, the state was not granted national independence which could be considered to have come to an end by the subsequent exile. The whole of the second Temple appears only to have been a gathering of the people about their Sanctuary of the Torah to equip them in preparation for the centuries of dispersion that lay before them. Ezra’s repossession of the land and sanctifying it as the soil of the Torah was just a taking into possession and sanctification in the exile and for the exile which indeed had not come to a complete end with his return. The catastrophe under Titus was accordingly only a bitter and deeper aggravation of the fate that was still continuing under Ezra, but in no way formed such a complete contrast to Ezra that the sanctification which he had made should be paralysed. The effect of Ezra’s occupation of the land is still working to day, ירושה ראשונה ושניה יש להן שלישית אין להן

V. 19. והיה באכלכם מלחם הארץ. The following duty of חלה, by the selective preposition מ- is restricted to everything that falls in the narrow sense under the conception of לחם. That is the five kinds of grain ,חיטים שעורים ,כוסמים ,שבולת שועל ,ושיפון, wheat, barley, oats, rye, and spelt. These are the same kind of grain which, as being able to be leaven, constitute the conception of לחם עוני (unleavened bread) for Pessach (Challa 1,2, see ר״ש there). Further, the duty of חלה only applies if they are made into bread-dough (not cake-dough I.L.) complying with the concept מלחם הארץ. In the preceding verse it does not say: בבאכם אל הארץ אשר אני נותן לכם but אשר אני מביא אתכם שמה. Thereby, it seems to us, could be indicated already that the laws that follow are not so much bound to the land itself, as to our presence in the land as indeed then by בבאכם even the presence of the whole nation in the land is required. And in fact the Halacha teaches (Challa 2,1) that the duty of Challa is imposed on dough made in the land from flour made from grain from outside the land, but dough made outside the land from grain grown inside the land. פירות חוצה לארץ שנכנסו לארץ חייבים בחלה יצאו מכאן לשם ר״א מחייב ור״ע פוטר are free from the duty of Challa as the Halacha is according to ר׳ עקיבה. This Halacha that the deciding factor is not the origin of the grain but the place where the bread is made is also referred to on verse 18: הארץ אשר אני מביא אתכם שמה שמה אתם חייבים בין בפירות חוצה לארץ בין בפירות הארץ; (see ר״ש ibid.). According to that מלחם הארץ is not to be understood as referring to what is grown in the land but to bread made in the land, as is explained in the Jerusalmi Challa 2,1 according to ר״ע. Indirectly all bread made in a land, as a rule, is something granted by the land, as the land provides the means to obtain it, so can in a broader sense be termed לחם הארץ, and this all the more if — as here is assumed — the whole nation is living in the land. (This Halacha based on אשר אני מביא אתכם שמה that the produce grown out of the land has the duty imposed in the land, but produce grown in the land is not liable outside the land is only found expressed for Challa. But by the רמב״ם it is applied equally to תרומות ומעשרות, so that for these duties too it is not the place of origin but the place where the preparation for food is completed, the מירוח ,גמר מלאכה which is the deciding factor. Regarding פירות ח״ל שנכנסו לארץ his opinion regarding תרומות ומעשרות is not clear — See הל׳ תרומות I,22 כ״מ. This opinion of the רמב״ם we could not find in סמ״ג, he only brings it referring to חלה).

V. 20. ראשית עריסתכם. One can doubt whether עריסה means the container in which the dough is prepared, the trough, or the dough itself. Onkelos translates it as אצוותא equally with ובמשארותיך in Ex. 7,28, which next to ובתנוריך clearly means kneading-trough. That meaning would be supported by the meaning of ערש, a press-bed (or box bed) which also is a container for storing bedding, sheets etc. On the other hand, in Rabbinic Hebrew the root ערס is used for kneading: הכא במאי עסקינן בשערסן (Berachoth 37b), and similarly in Jerusalmi, Challa 1,1 and III,1, and elsewhere. The meaning of ערס as mixing the flour with water appears most clearly in Sifri:- מראשית עריסתכם למה נאמר לפי שהוא אומר והיה באכלכם מלחם הארץ שומע אני אף הקמחים במשמע ת״ל מראשית עריסתכם, משיתערס מכאן אמרו אוכלין עראי מן העיסה עד שתתגלגל בחטים וטימטמה בשעורים. In Kilayim 4,7 אם ערסן מלמעלה, the word ערס there means an arbour-like binding together of vines over a partition and describes a lattice work made out of reeds to which vines are tied (ibid. VI,1). If we consider the relation of all these and similar places to ארס, the act of the first binding in marriage, the fundamental meaning of the root ערס could well be a mutual binding together, so that ערש is really a criss-cross bed frame where the side pieces are held mutually bound to each other by strong webbing. Finally mixing flour and water to make a dough, and indeed, just as ארס, betrothed, is not the completed binding in marriage, but only the first act towards it, so ערס is not the completed act of dough-making, but the preliminary mixing of the flour with water which in the above quotation, the Mishna calls גלגול for wheaten flour and טמטום for the less easily mixed barley flour as the stage of the mixture where the duty of taking Challa starts. עריסה is then, either the mixing of flour with water to make a dough, or according to ת״א, the vessel for that purpose. The dough finished by לישה, kneading, is called בצק.

עריסתכם: the Halacha takes this to indicate the minimum quantity which entails the duty of Challa. This is the minimum of one mix for one day’s requirement of one person, taking it from the manna in the wilderness this is one עומר which is one tenth of an איפה. 1 איפה = 3 סאה, 1 סאה = 6 קב, 1 קב = 4 לוג, so that one tenth of an איפה = 7 and 1/5 לוג and as 1 ביצים 6 = לוג the size necessitating the taking of Challa is 43 and 1/5 eggs. As it does not say העריסת but עריסתכם, only “our” dough has to have Challa taken from it, but not the dough of non-Jews, nor that of הקדש, (Menachoth 67a).

כתרומת הגרן; Just as the barn presents the sight of the blessing that God has granted to the fields so does the עריסה represent His blessing on the home; and just as the owner may not enjoy the products laid up in his barn before he has acknowledged his recognition that it is only God Whom he has to thank for the blessing of his fields, by making the symbolic gift of תרומה גדולה to the כהן (see on Levit. Ch. 22,9), so are the same thoughts to strike him with renewed force at the moment when he prepares the daily bread for himself and his family and recognises the care and providence which God dispenses on every home and on each individual soul in every home. The ears of corn ripen in the fields under the rays of the sun which is a blessing which everybody enjoys in common. The participation in this general blessing to obtain bread for the daily requirements of any individual is a gift, the result of the special attention of the Divine Providence. Hence just as a portion of grain has to be “raised” out of the corn stack, so is a piece of dough lifted up to God by the thought of what one owes to Him and to the Sanctuary of His Torah, and given to the representative of that Sanctuary — the כהן. It becomes קדש like תרומה with all similar responsibilities, שחייבין עליה מיתה וחומש ואסורה לזרים, it becomes the property of the כהן exactly like תרומה (Challa 1,9 — refer again to Levit. XXII). Further, neither have any minimum limit, מן התורה one has fulfilled one’s duty with the tiniest piece of dough (see on next verse), just as חטה אחת פוטרת את הכרי, with one grain from the whole heap, with תרומה. But on the other hand, there is a maximum limit for both. Both are called ראשית, and for something to be called ראשית there must be a recognizable amount left. Hence the dictum in Chulin 136b: האמר כל גרני תרומה וכל עיסתי חלה לא אמר כלום — “if someone declares his whole barn shall be Teruma or the whole of his dough Challa, his declaration is invalid, and has no effect.” Hereby the most important fact is expressed for the relation of the nation and every individual of it to the Sanctuary of the Torah. No one may consider the relation of the priest to the Sanctuary of the Torah to be a substitute for his own, that with the maintenance of the priest, his own existence is negligible and immaterial for the Sanctuary of the Torah. But rather it is the maintenance of his own existence for the Sanctuary of God’s Torah which is the reason and purpose of his duty to maintain the priest of which the giving of Challah is to remind him. By giving Challah he is to remember and take to heart the dedication of his own existence and his own household to God and His Torah; his gift of Challah only becomes Challah if he reserves something at the same time to symbolise his own existence, ששיריה נכרין.

V. 21. מראשית ערסתיכם. In the previous verse the י, the sign of the plural is missing. It only represents the conception עריסה in general. But here it wants to refer to every kind of dough (see next paragraph) and so puts the full plural, but still by the limiting prefixed מ indicates the restriction to the five kinds of grain mentioned above in V.19.

מראשית ערסתיכם. In the previous verse תרומת עריסה is placed on a level with תרומת גרן, here it is repeated by itself to teach its independence of תרומת גרן. For even those kinds of dough to which תרומת גרן is not applicable because for example, it was הפקר or שכחה ,לקט or פאה, it still has to have Challah taken from it. More, the Torah adds לדרתיכם, the challah-duty goes on uninterruptedly, even in the שביעית years, when the תרומות ומעשרות-duties are not in force for produce grown in that year, but dough made out of them have to have Challah taken from it (ספרי). Thereby just that phase of God’s care and provision to which Challah pays tribute is marked as being a special idea, different from that which is expressed by its colleague the תרומת הדשן. For at a general good harvest an individual and his house can starve; yea, he can even participate in such a general blessed harvest and yet the bread of his house may not be blessed. And equally at times of the most widespread drought and scarcity and high prices, an individual can remain protected from want. It is just taking Challah from the “manna-measure” of the שיעור חלה which acknowledges the continuation of that “manna-providence” which not only cares for worlds and countries, but in countries provides for the cities, and in cities for the houses, and in the houses for every soul that looks up to it and trustingly awaits its love. Challah is the expression of the most individual השגחה פרטית, and so forms an essential complement to the preceding institution of מנחה ונסך which is dedicated to God’s Providence in general. Then it seems to us that it is a precept of infinitely far-reaching significance that Challah, just the appreciation of God’s care and provision for the individual in his own special position, should be attached to ביאת כולכם, to the presence of the whole nation on the soil of the land of God’s special attention. If, similarly to that great institution which God’s Love for Israel ordained, the יובל (see Levit. 25,10) — the regenerating power of the Youvel is attached to the presence of the whole nation in the land — Challah, expressing the personal special care of God for each individual, is also conditional to the presence of all Israel in the land, under the protective Wings of God’s Grace, this clause is a reminder to every individual in Israel, at the moment when he is justified, nay, ordered to think of himself as being under the special personal attention of God’s Care, that nevertheless his own well-being, and that of every individual is dependent on the well-being of all. No man is to feel himself happy and provided for, sitting “under his vine and under his fig tree” as long as there is still one of his brethren still “outside”, an alien in another country.

We have already remarked on the previous verse that מן התורה the smallest quantity is sufficient for the fulfillment of the duty of Challah. But it is a מצוה דרבנן to comply with the inference of the word “תתנו״ to give such a quantity that it can be called a נתינה a “gift”, and they fixed the amount at 1/24th of the quantity. of the dough in domestic baking, and 1/48th, for bakers’ baking.

The Challah which we take now, away from א״י is only a reminder of the real duty. As חלה טמאה it has to be burnt. The smallest quantity sufficies for that, but it is customary to take at least the size of an olive.

V. 22. וכי תשגו וגו׳. The nature of the sin of the מרגלים (the spies) was to cast doubts whether God’s special exclusive care for Israel was sufficient to ensure our earthly existence. And then with נתנה ראש ונשובה מצרימה (let us appoint a leader and let us return to Egypt) its character formed itself into complete rebellion and complete defection from God. The institutions of נסכים and חלה proceeded from the nature of the מרגלים-sin. The fact of the actual occurrence of this defection begat the following פרשת שעירי ע״ז which envisages nothing less than the possibility of a repetition of such an erroneous national apostasy, or of personal conscious and intentional defection from God; and for the return of the nation out of such a national error ordains that a special offering of an עולה, accompanied by prescribed נסכים should be brought in addition to the חטאת, yea, should precede it.

וכי תשגו. Already on Levit. 4,13 we have shown how that root שגה designates especially theoretical errors, differentiating from שגג, errors in practice. From this meaning of the word שגה, the following ולא תעשו can not specify the error itself, but can only refer to the practical result of the theoretical error. But just as little can it refer to the immediate practical result brought about by the theoretical error, which here is to be atoned for. For לא תעשו expresses not doing something which you are commanded to do, and it is clear from V.24, והיה אם וגו׳ נעשתה לשגגה, as well as from V.30, והנפש אשר תעשה ביד רמה, that here it is talking about a positive transgression, doing something which you are commanded not to do. Further, את כל אשר צוה ה׳ וגו׳ וגו׳ ,ולא תעשו את כל המצות וגו׳, speaks of not fulfilling the whole Torah, while נעשתה לשגגה of V.24 as well as the expressions תחטא בשגגה שגגתם ,שגגה היא (in verses 25, 27, 28) speak, in accordance with every analogy elsewhere, of the transgression of only one sin. Accordingly the ולא תעשו וגו׳ can only want to indicate the character of this one aberration and transgression, in its importance and further consequences, as a defection from fulfilling the whole of the Torah: “if you should ever fall into such an aberration by which you would express the further non-compliance with the whole of the Torah etc.” In V.31, the conscious and intentional transgression of what is here done in error is also designated as דבר ה׳ בזה ואת מצותו הפר, as a derision of the Word of God and a complete doing away with His commandments. So the Halacha teaches that our verse is speaking of an error in the sphere of idolatry, ע״ז, and that this is indicated just by the אמר קרא וכי תשגו :ולא תעשו וגו׳ ולא תעשו את כל המצות האלה איזו היא מצוה שהיא שקולה ככל המצות הוי אומר זו ע״ז, by the addition of ולא תעשו וגו׳, the one error of which it is speaking here is designated as being the transgression of such a command, the weight of which is equal to that of the whole contents of the Torah, i.e. by the fulfilling or non-fulfilling of which, the whole Torah stands or falls, and that is no other than the command about idolatry, in which, in fact the fundamental principle of the whole law-giving is rooted. In ספרי זוטא this Halacha is thus explained on our text:- יכול שהוא מדבר בכל המצות אמרת אם מעיני העדה נעשתה בשגגה באחת מכל המצות דיבר ולא דיבר בכל המצות, אי אפשר לאמר בכל המצות שכבר נאמר באחת ואי אפשר לאמר באהת שכבר נאמר בכל המצות הא מה מצוה שכל מצות תלוין בה זו ע״ז. And according to ס׳ באר שבע on Horioth it is just this way of taking the text which lies at the base of the explanation given there.

According to this, then, perhaps the ולא תעשו וגו׳ could be what the error presumed by וכי תשגו really was. But, as a theoretical error (שגה) it would not be the actual non-fulfilling of the whole Torah, but express the opinion that the Torah need no longer be kept. Then והיה אם מעיני העדה וגו׳ would put forth the case where this erroneous teaching from the authorities resulted in actual wrong doing. It would say: “if you ever fall into the error of thinking that you have no longer to keep all these commandments which God spoke unto Moses, all that which God commanded you through Moses, from the day that God gave commandments and henceforth for your generations, if then, coming from the “eyes of the community” it came to an actual sin committed, then etc.” But this one actual sin in which the theoretical abrogation of the whole Torah is expressed is none other than an act of idolatry. And indeed even the possibility that an act of idolatry could be taught by the עיני העדה by the board of education which forms the “eyes”, the deciding “intelligence” of the nation as being permitted is hardly thinkable unless the whole Torah, or at least the whole necessity for the continuance of the duty to fulfil its ordinances, had found its grave in their minds. God as the one exclusive Leader of our fate and Guide for our actions is the very fundamental basis of the whole lawgiving as had been promulgated at Sinai (refer to Ex. 20,2 & 3). One step away from this basis is defection from the whole Torah, and conscious intentional defection on principle from the Torah is identical with giving up this basis. And indeed, as רמב״ן remarks in his commentary, times are not unknown in Israel’s history, when the whole nation or whole communities were overpowered by an erroneous opinion of the antiquated nature of the Torah, or an almost complete forgetting of the Torah, through mistaken understanding of the prevailing conditions, through the sacreligious policy of kings and leaders, or through the heavy tribulations of their fate: It was the “elders of Israel” who approached the prophet Ezekiel with the request that he find out from God new instructions for the new age. For they had the feeling that it was questionable whether the old duty of keeping the Torah was still binding. They thought that it was possible that by the abandonment of the Nation, God has expressed the dismissal of its people from His service, and thereby emancipation from the duties of the Torah. That was why the Word of God was sent to them, to the “elders of the people” (Ezek. 20,1 et seq.), the thought that is arising in your minds will never come to pass, that you imagine now we can become like the other nations, “like the families of the land, to serve wood and stone.” “As sure as I live” says God, “with a strong hand and an outstretched arm, and with outpoured fury, do I remain your King” (ibid. 32, 33; Sifri end of שלח לך). Under the influence of Jeroboam and his successor ten-twelfth of the Jewish nation were withdrawn from all knowledge and practice of the Torah; and under the heavy pressure of the Babylonian exile the greater part of the lower ranks of the people remained so far from knowledge of the Torah that those that returned with Ezra had to be taught to understand it quite afresh; and in our times is there not in large circles a generation growing up who have been brought up and kept in the thoughts of those elders of Ezekiel of the abrogation of the Torah and in designedly ignorance of the Torah?

But as here it is speaking of the theoretical defection from the whole Torah, expressed by an act of idolatry, the text is not satisfied simply to say: ולא תעשו את כל המצות האלה but specifies the Torah in accordance with the mode and time of its revelation אשר דבר ה׳ אל משה, את כל אשר צוה ה׳ אליכם ביד משה מן היום אשר צוה ה׳ והלאה לדרתיכם. With this specification, the defection from God and His Torah is clearly described in its comprehensive totality. If one takes the אשר דבר ה׳ אל משה as a subordinate sentence to את כל המצות האלה it would refer to all the laws (האלה I.L.) written down in the Torah, תורה שבכתב ביד משה, and then את כל אשר צוה ה׳ אלקיכם would then refer also to the tradition which was verbally given to you through Moses, the מן היום וגו׳ .תורה שבע״פ, as it does not say אשר צוה ה׳ אליכם but אשר צוה ה׳ in general, this refers, without doubt, back to the time in which God first revealed His Will to mankind in general, the general Noachian Laws given to Adam and Eve as well as those given to the אבות. And, in fact, the ע״ז prohibition is not only the foundation of the Jewish sphere of duty but of all human beings. Equally so, by לדרתיכם the thought is extended beyond the Mosaic period and includes every Word of God that He sent thereafter through the mouths of the Prophets (ספרי). Thereby our relation to God and His commandments is described as an undivided one which knows no choosing or dividing, and allows no room for the erroneous idea that, if one wishes, one can give up the specific Jewish ideas and remain on the Noachian standpoint of the purely human, or that one could give up the Mosaic and make for oneself a so-called “Prophetic” one. For us there is no alternative. Either a complete Jew with the whole Torah or to turn our back completely to God. Not for nothing has God here described defection from Him ,as being identical with defection from His Torah, or rather defection from his Torah as being identical with defection from Him; not for nought does He use the circumlocutory language of describing defection from Himself by practicing idolatry as just defection from His Torah; for He recognises no connection for us with Him other than faithful adherence to His Torah, (see on verses 30 and 31).

In ספרי the אשר דבר ה׳ אל משה is explained as not being a subordinate sentence referring to את כל המצות האלה, but אשר דבר ה׳ אל משה together with the following את כל אשר צוה וגו׳, מן היום אשר צוה וגו׳, form the complete contents of כל המצות האלה. For, when used contrastingly to אשר צוה ה׳ אליכם ביד משה, the words אשר דבר ה׳ אל משה designate those words of God that did not come to us first through Moses, but (אליכם I.L.), but that came to us at the same moment that God spoke them to Moses. These were the first two of the ten commandments which מפי הגבורה שמענום, in which God speaks in the first person and which came directly to the consciousness of all the people — אנכי וכו׳ אשר הוצאתיך לא יהיה לך וגו׳ על פני — whereas in the others He speaks of Himself in the third person, accordingly expresses His words in the way they are to be transmitted by Moses to the people, like all the other laws which follow — the Torah. Through these first two speeches of God we received the certainty that ידבר אלקים את האדם וחי, by the following the certainty that God used Moses as His instrument to transmit His Laws to us. Although דבר ה׳ אל כל קהלכם את כר הדברים האלה, although we were present and aware of all the Ten Commandments on Sinai, it was the first two in the overwhelming might of their direct speech coming to them, that so overpowered the people and made them feel that they were unequal to bear it that they begged that the whole rest of the Lawgiving might be made through the agency of Moses (Deut. 5,19-24; see באר שבע on Horioth 8a). According to that אשר דבר ה׳ אל משה designated only אנכי and לא יהיה לך which were received directly from God by the people, and אח כל וגו׳ ביד משה the rest of the Ten Commandments and the whole Lawgiving transmitted by Moses (ביד משה I.L.) verbally and in writing, as well as by מן היום וגו׳, all the Words of God given before and after that to Adam and Eve and Noah, the Patriarchs and the Prophets. But אנכי and לא יהיה לך are the two fundamental sentences which, by the exclusive allegiance to God as the Director of our fate and Guide for our actions, demand the complete break with heathenism in every shape or form, and to which all the rest of the laws and all that was said by the Prophets are really only a commentary. Then perhaps these two sentences are specially stressed here because here it is just speaking of a complete defection from the Torah proved by an act of idolatry, and perhaps it is in that sense that תנא דבי רבי (Horioth ibid.) says:- אמר קרא אשר דבר ה׳ אל משה וכתיב אשר צוה ה׳ אליכם ביד משה איזו מצוה שהיא בדיבורו של הקב״ה וצוה ע״י משה הוי אומר זו ע״ז דתנא דבי רבי ישמעאל אנכי ולא יהיה לך מפי הגבורה שמענום. Then the צוה ע״י would not be understood only as the special explanation of the prohibition of ע״ז, but of all the מצות, which in a wider sense can be understood as the consequence of the ע״ז prohibition which is promulgated by אנכי and לא יהיה לד. Then תנא דבי רבי would express the same idea as רבא or רבי יהושע בן לוי expresses, viz. that ע״ז is the מצוה that is ככל המצות.

V. 24. עיני העדה :והיה אם מעיני העדה וגו׳, the eyes, the “intelligence” of the nation, is the ב״ד הגדול, (the Sanhedrin I.L.). If this highest ecclesiastical authority (through a שגיה (an error in theory I.L.) V.22) has declared the performance of an act of ע״ז, idolatry, as permitted, and thereby נעשתה לשגגה, this theoretical error has resulted in actual sinful practice, as it says in V.26 לכל העם בשגגה i.e., the whole nation, or at least a majority representing the whole nation — be it רוב הקהל במיעוט שבטים or רוב השבטים במיעוט הקהל (see Levit. on IV,13) — sinned בשגג, thinking the act of עייז which they did was permitted as decided by the Sanhedrin: This is precisely an example of the case described in Levit. 4,13-21, of all erroneous decisions of the Sanhedrin regarding any sin which is liable to the punishment of כרת, and for which in these cases the פר העלם דבר של ציבור is ordained. But here, in the case of ע״ז, the offering prescribed is different. There, each tribe of the nation brings a פר so that there are twelve oxen as חטאת, and the זקני העדה, the Sanhedrin, express their special relation to this offering by סמיכה, (ibid. V,15). Here each tribe of the nation brings one פר for an עולה and one שעיר for a חטאת, so that twelve oxen are offered as עולה and twelve he-goats as חטאת, and, as at all other קרבנות ציבור, no סמיכה takes place (Horioth 4b and Menachoth 90a).

Thereby the national atonement for שגגת ע״ז differs not only from the corresponding national atonement for all other שגגות but also altogether from all other שגגות. At every other שגגה the כפרה striven for is expressed by חטאת, but here by an עולה and a חטאת, and indeed, significantly enough, the עולה is in the foreground. Whereas in general the חטאת is brought first, before the עולה, here the עולה has the precedence, and the חטאת stands back as secondary, which is also indicated by the abbreviated spelling, חטת כתיב, חסר א׳ (Zebachim 90b).

The error to be atoned for in the case of פר העלם דבר של ציבור also consists of a שגיה (an error in theory I.L.) and a שגגה (error in practice I.L.) of a הוראת ב״ד and a מעשה ציבור. But the שגיה goes no farther than the שגגה and goes with it in the כפרה. But here the שגיה is the theory, the idea of defection from the whole of the Torah as is designated quite clearly in the preceding verses 22 and 23, and the שגגה, the ע״ז act, is only one specific consequence of it. Here the two factors of the sin come to be atoned for in separate offerings, the שגיה by עולה, the שגגה by חטאת, and indeed the general bond of duty to God and His Torah must first be re-attached before one can speak at all of atonement for the one single act. But purely mental errors, הרהורי הלב, find their atonement in עולה. They come from insufficient exercise of mental energy in devotion to knowledge of the Truth, the lack of which was responsible for the arising and establishment of the error being possible. Significantly enough, just on the verse we quoted above on V.22, (viz. Ezekiel 20,32 I.L.) the Jerusalmi Yoma 8,7 teaches on the words העולה על רוחכם (which arose in your minds I.L.) that where Truth does not עולה על הרוח the error is עולה (see Ex. on XXVII,8 p.497). Moreover it is עולה and not חטאת which is the expression of our normal relation to God (see Levit. Commentary on IV,24 where Hirsch says inter alia “it is not a permanent consciousness of חטאת, not a permanent feeling of being a sinner that is the mood in which Jewish hearts are to beat, and in which Jewish minds are to find their enthusiastic soaring upwards to God… עולה ,עולה, עולה. Upwards, upwards, upwards! Up to the radiant proximity of God, and ever higher and higher in constant energetic progress! That is the call that comes unceasingly to His sons and daughters out of the Sanctuary of God” etc. etc. I.L.). So that when the bond between the nation and its God has been torn asunder through their mental erroneous idea, and after the nation’s recovering its senses is again to be established, this renewed bond can not be expressed other than by עולה. And then the נסכים-institution comes again significantly beside the עולה as is here quite specially stressed: ועשו כל העדה פר בן בקר אחד לעולה לריח ניהח לה׳ ומנחתו ונסכו כמשפט. If, as repeatedly indicated, the fundamental axioms of Jewish Truth, אנכי and לא יהיה לך are merged in the thought of God being the sole Guide of our fate and Leader of our acts, then this thought would be fully expressed by פר לעולה and מנחתו ונסכו כמשפט. The עולה acknowledges God as the Guide of our deeds, and מנחה ונסך as the Guide of our fate; and if the whole nation places itself again, after such a great defection, as פר etc., before God, it vows thereby henceforth to keep itself faithful in His “service”, and by giving up the whole of itself and all its efforts to the heights of the altar and the Fire of His Torah (אשדת) to strive to carry out the whole of His Will on earth, and to show allegiance to Him, and Him alone with every phase of its existence and its happiness on earth. Only then can it add the חטאת-vow as a שעיר, not again thoughtlessly to sink down from the height on which God has placed us, and with שעיר firmness to resist all attempts to entice us away from our Guide and Leader. It is significant that here at the offering for the ע״ז error, the Sanhedrin as such retire completely and are merged with the nation. In the פר העלם דבר של ציבור the offering is really that of the Sanhedrin. Every tribe gives it its פר and thereby the warning to be more circumspective and more judicious in discharging the duties of its office, and by סמיכה the Sanhedrin adopt the offering as its חטאת. But with שגית ע״ז the Sanhedrin has dismissed itself; the atonement-offering is not פר חטאת but שעיר חטאת and accordingly remains, without סמיכה, purely atonement for the nation, within which the Sanhedrin also finds itself again at one with God and its office.

ועשו כל העדה פר וגו׳: the פר and שעיר, according to the Halacha (Horioth 4,b) is one ox and one he-goat from each tribe. These שעירי ע״ז belong to the חטאות הפנימיות and are treated in exactly a similar manner. They get הזיה in the היכל towards the נתינה על קרנות ;כנגד בין הבדים ,פרכת מזבח הזהב; שפיכת שיריים אל יסוד מזבח העולה, and after this עבודת הדם the אימורים are burnt on the מזבח and the whole of the rest of the body burnt חוץ למחנה (the meaning of this whole procedure fully explained on Levit. 4,4-21 I.L.).
V. 25. והם הביאו את קרבנם אשה לה׳: the עולה and the ;נסכים וחטאתם לפני ה׳: the שעיר הנעשה בפנים as חטאת פנימית.

V. 26. Perhaps the fact that here, speaking of כפרה for שגגת ע״ז, the גר הגר בתוכם is specially stressed as being deemed worthy for סליחה may be because one might think that for one who has come over from heathenism the defection to ע״ז might be taken more seriously as being a relapse.

V. 27. ואם נפש אחת וגו׳. The ע״ז sin committed by the nation had been preceded by a lapse in the way of thinking which led to an erroneous teaching by the supreme ecclesiastical authorities, hence, as we have tried to show, the עולה with מנחה and נסך, hence the חטאת as פנימית. Not the Sanhedrin as פר but the nation as שעיר had to admonish itself and vow by the הזיות and מתנות in the היכל henceforth to satisfy, with virile firmness, the demand which the waiting בדי הארון outstretched towards them make for them to be the bearers of the Torah, giving it the required care by studying and keeping its laws (הזיות על הפרכת כנגד בדי ארון); and to expect the blossoming of the national spiritual and material well-being only on the heights of the ideals indicated by God (מתנות על קרנות מזבח הזהב). After the momentary break in the nation’s relationship to God by its sin, the task which in the normal course of the national life is to be accomplished by the office of כהן המשיח and the Sanhedrin as delegates of the nation, falls back, when the relationship to God is to be re-established, in its original responsibility on the nation itself. The tribes of the nation by their twelve שעירים place themselves in the היכל as guardians and bearers of the tasks represented by the פרכת and the ואם נפש אחת תחטא ,מזבח הקטרת בשגגה, but when it is not a case of the national “intelligence” causing a national sin to be committed, but of an individual having committed an ע״ז sin in careless ignorance coming to get atonement for it — and that is always if there was no הוראת ב״ד הגדול or שגגת רוב הציבור — then שגגת ע״ז is to be atoned for, like any other שגגת יחיד in איסורי כרת, by an ordinary חטאת חיצונית (Levit. 4,27 et seq.). The only difference is that there the choice is left open between שעירת עזים and כבשה (both female animals I.L.), but here the offering is fixed (נידון בקבוע the Sifri calls it) as an עז בת שנתה. Towards an ע״ז aberration every individual in the nation is expected to have שעיר-like independence and firmness, and not to fall in careless thoughtlessness, and to remain protected against such far-reaching errors. Even against an erroneous decision of the highest authorities, יחיד שעשה בהוראת ב״ד חייב (Horioth 2b), an individual who follows it is not freed from responsibility before God. This is a principle which perhaps was necessary to be taken seriously to heart by no age as much as our own, in which people are so prone to barricade their consciences behind erroneous declarations made by individual rabbis or by a congress of rabbis. Possibly some indication of this may be found in our text in the “dagesh-less” spelling of בחטאה בשגגה. Even when “the person” (הנפש I.L.) does not appear entirely responsible by himself, inasmuch as he acted under the cloak of an erroneous teaching of an authority, even then the necessity for כפרה remains. But as, in the case of שגגת ע״ז של ציבור the Sanhedrin as such is not represented in the national offering which is accordingly not a פר but a שעיר, so that, when it concerns an ע״ז aberration all office and all personal value disappears, neither the כהן משיח — the High Priest — nor the נשיא — the King — has any special representation, as they have if they have to bring any other חטאת (Levit. 4,3 & 22). Should they have to bring a חטאת יחיד של ע״ז they are completely on the level of the lowest individual of the people, and they appear as שעירה, not שעיר, before God. ובע״ז ,היחיד והנשיא והמשיח מביאין שעירה (Horioth 9a).

V. 29. האזרח וגו׳ (see on V.26) תורה אחת יהיה לכם לעשה בשגגה. By this generalization given here of the law, the case discussed here for the ע״ז sin is made into an example for the חטאת-duty of שגגות in general. The sin of ע״ז which here necessitates a חטאת offering to be brought if committed שוגג is one which if done במזיד would — as the following verse says — entail the punishment of כרת; further, it is a sin which is committed by an action, as is specified by the word תעשה i.e., a sin of commission not by omission. Hence the canon: הוקשה כל התורה כולה לע״ז מה ע״ז דבר שחייבין על זדונו כרת ועל שגגתו חטאת אף כל דבר שחייבין על זדונו כרת ועל שגגתו חטאת, and further מה ע״ז שב ואל תעשה אף כל שב ואל תעשה (Sabbath 69a, תוספות thereon, and Kerithoth 3a). Hence all transgressions which are not punished by כרת are excluded from bringing a חטאת offering, and hence also פסח and מילה, although punishable with כרת, still do not bring a חטאת, because transgressions against them are sins of omission and not of commission. Also מגדף, blasphemy, is excluded, for the transgression, although punishable by כרת and an act of commission of a prohibition, is still not like ע״ז done by an actual deed, a מעשה but only in words. (Kerithoth 2a; see on Levit. 4,2).

V. 30. ביד רמה .והנפש אשר וכו׳ designates independence recognising no master; הרים יד ב- is rebellion (refer to com. on Ex. 14,8). Here, in contrast to the שגגה discussed just beforehand it is simply מזיד, conscious transgression of the law (Sabbath 68b, and 69a). But עבודה זרה במזיד, an act of worshipping an idol with full consciousness and intention, by its very meaning is itself מרד rebellion against God, and becomes .יד רמה מגדף; what גדף means referring to God is evident from Kings II. 19,6 & 22 with reference to XVIII,32-36, where the messengers of the Assyrian King compared God to the powerless futility of all the gods of heathenism, and this denial of God is there termed גידוף. In Ezekiel too, offering sacrifices to the gods by Israel in the land God had given — or rather lent — them, is called גדף את ה׳. Now here it says:- But if anybody should, with full consciousness and intention do an act of ע״ז, even if it is only of the nature of one about which a ב״ד הגדול could possibly make a mistake (and the context indicates this) he has thereby already committed גידוף, has expressed God-denying blasphemy. Here גידוף is obviously the more comprehensive, more reprehensible sin, and here even one single act of ע״ז if done במזיד is pronounced equal to גידוף .גידוף is ברכת ה׳ (cursing the Name of God or blasphemy I.L.) and every act of it is declared complete גידוף. To protect the holy thought of God from any trace of the breath of blasphemous words, Kerithoth 7b ingeniously illustrates the relation of ע״ז to ברכת ה׳ by the metaphor of a concrete object, wittily using the similar sounds of גדף (blasphemy I.L.) and גרף (clearing out, scraping away I.L.) ע״ז, it says there, is כאדם האומר לחברו גירפת הקערה ולא חיסרת, “you have completely scraped all the contents from the dish but you have not scraped any of the dish itself away. But ברכת ה׳ to כאדם האומר לחברו גירפת הקערה וחיסרת, “You have scraped the vessel clean and have injured the vessel itself too”, or in the version of the Sifri: גירפת את כל הקערה כולה ולא שיירת ממנה כלום: “you have scraped the vessel itself right away too.” ע״ז does turn to another the recognition and devotion of service which is due to God alone, does take away from God that which He alone is entitled to, but possibly thinks it does not necessarily take away any of the recognition of God itself, could leave that untouched. But ברכת ה׳ turns directly against God with complete blasphemious denial. If here, according to the accepted teaching of the Sages, by מברך את ה׳ :מגדף is to be understood, and what it says here is that עובד ע״ז במזיד is identical with מברך את ה׳, that does say that the sin of עובד ע״ז that one who does just one act of עבודה to any one idol goes far beyond what the intention of his act appears to be on the surface, inasmuch as with every עבודה זרה a complete denial of God is effected. He may have wanted only to גורף את הקערה but he has גיררה ולא שייר ממנה כלום. This comes from the concept of קנא, the idea of the absolute exclusiveness of monotheism, the belief in the existence of only One God. Further, inasmuch as here ע״ז is proclaimed identical with ברכת ה׳, and here כרת is declared for ע״ז it is taken that by את ה׳ הוא מגדף it is implied that blasphemy is likewise punished by לא בא הכתוב אלא ליתן כרת ;כרת במברך את ה׳ (Kerithoth 7b). That blasphemy is punishable by סקילה is already mentioned in Levit. 24,13 et seq. and here כרת is imposed for it if it ocurrs without עדים and התראה. But although blasphemy is a כרת-crime nevertheless if done בשוגג a חטאת-offering is not brought for it, because there is no action done אין בו מעשה (see ל״מ I,2 רמב״ם הל׳ שגגות thereon), just as עובד ע״ז בשוגג itself is only to bring a חטאת if some action is done.

V. 31. כי דבר ה׳ בזה וגו׳. This passage of the Torah of שגגת וזדון ע״ז was introduced (V.22 and 23) by the assumption of a defection from the Torah, which only in V.24 comes to be concretely referred to the ע״ז-sin. Thereby the ע״ז-sin is already — even before it is discussed — marked in its real seriousness as a defection from the whole Torah, and how just it, and not, as one could have imagined, scorning God in the actual factor in which the ע״ז-sin reaches its zenith. This is expressed just in those two introductory sentences which rivet our attention on the whole of God’s revelation of our duties in all its comprehensive parts and stages. This is so much in the foreground that the ע״ז-error and sin is expressed in the round-about manner as defection from the Torah. In accordance with this, the ע״ז passage concludes with, and gives the reason for declaring כרת for the עובד ע״ז and מגדף, as כי דבר ה׳ בזה ומצותו הפר הכרת תכרת וגו׳ (not ה׳ but דבר ה׳ I.L.). The punishment of כרת is given even to the one who serves idols or blasphemes God, but not so much because he serves idols and blasphemes God as because by doing so he has scorned a word of God (דבר ה׳ בזה I.L.) and treated a command of God as non-existent (מצזתו הפר I.L.); because he has acted against the Word of God, אנכי, ולא יהיה לך, and the commandment of God אלקים לא תקלל. Thereby it is not the metaphysical objective recognition or denial of God of His Existence, but our subjective moral acknowledging Him or not, that matters; the acknowledgment or not of His relation to us, in which He came to us by giving His Law, in short the acknowledgment of God as our God to Whom we owe allegiance, as indeed His אנכי ה׳ אלקיך not אנכי ה׳ אלקים promulgated as the fundamental principle for us, and that describes everything by which our relation to God altogether stands or falls (see Ex. Ch. 19,4 et seq.).

In all this then, the sentence מין אוכל נבלות להכעיס or מומר (Avoda Zara 26b) whosoever, not out of yielding to temptation (תיאבון) but out of basic scorn of the laws of the Torah, trangresses only one of its laws, is considered as having joined the ranks of those who revoke the whole of the Torah and renounce God, this sentence finds its full justification. Here זדון ע״ז is banned in its full gravity as an act done ביד רמה, in scorn of a Word of God, and non-observance of one of His Commandments, ע״ז ;כי דבר ה׳ בזה ואת מצותו הפר is only specialised in that here, in accordance with the nature of the sin, an ordinary לתאבון) מזיד I.L.) is, in this case, raised to the level of להכעיס, to a מרד exercised ביד רמה (see י״ד ,ב״י end of ס׳ רמ״ח). But every transgression against the Torah done להכעיס is equally a יד רמה, a “hand raised” against God and His Torah, and places the doer in the same category.

Hence also then the traditional sentence in Sanhedrin 99a כי דבר ה׳ בזה זה האומר אין תורה מן השמים ואפילו אומר כל התורה כולה מן השמים חוץ מפסוק זה שלא אמרו הקב״ה אלא משה מפי עצמו זהו כי דבר ה׳ בזה ואפילו אמר כל התורה כולה מן השמים חוץ מדקדוק זה מק״ו זה מגז״ש זו זהו כי דבר ה׳ בזה i.e. he who denies the revelation of the Torah by God, and even if he admits the whole Torah does come from God with the exception of one verse, which he ascribes to Moses and not to God, and even if he denies the nuance expressed by one certain law, the hermenutic validity of a קל וחומר (the inference from minor to major, or the reverse I.L.), denies a גזירה שוה (a deduction from a similarity of phrases I.L.), he falls under the conception which is expressed by כי דבר ה׳ בזה. Not for nothing does the concept of the revelation by God on His Law in all its parts, comprehensively including תושב״כ, the written Torah, תשב״פ, the traditional full explanation of it transmitted verbally, אדם ,נח ,אבות, the pre-Moses laws, נביאים, post-Moses period of the Prophets, stand at the head of this passage. Of one who denies one single מצוה of these מצוות the Torah says: כי דבר ה׳ בזה .ואת מצות הפר

הפר .הפר occurs mostly in connection with מחשבה ,עצה ,ברית and נדר and means the upsetting, breaking, frustration, and defeat of that which should occur. So הפר מצוה is not making a command non-effective in general but for oneself treating it as if it did not exist for oneself, to deny it having any authority over oneself, to treat it with scorn.

עונה בה. His enmity against the command of God is futile. God’s Torah continues in its holy inviolability but his sin falls back on himself. By his scorn of the Law he has destroyed his future, הכרת תכרת הנפש ההוא עונה בה. — Hence also probably why עונה is רפה (see Levit. 20,5).

V. 32. The preceding law had treated the sin of ע״ז as defection from God and His Torah, and in the offering referring to it the stress is on the allegiance to God as Director of our actions and Dispenser of our fate and fortune as is expressed by עולה and מנחה ונסך. It concluded with discussing the case where the ע״ז-sin was committed במזיד but without עדים והתראה and so escapes human justice, but remains under that of God, which imposes כרת for ע״ז and ברכת ה׳.

Now there is another Mitzva in which God has made doing something, or rather, refraining from doing something into an act of recognition of our allegiance to God as well as His being the Master of all our fate and deeds, so that observing this Mitzva denotes allegiance to and non-observance of it deniance of God being Master over our fate and deeds. So that scorning this Mitzva is, similarly to ע״ז and מגדף, punished by כרת and סקילה, and this Mitzva is: שבת. Inasmuch as Sabbath, at God’s command, orders a stoppage to our creative work, with this one שביתה (ceasing work I.L.) we lay our deeds and at the same time our human world at the Feet of God. Our refraining from creative work is just this double homage to God just as every doing such work on Sabbath is a double denial of God’s Mastery. So there is an intimate connection between the concrete instance of a חילול שבת, a desecration of the Sabbath, which follows, and the precedings laws and proceedings. And indeed we see the same בני ישראל, the same עדה, the same people whom, at the beginning of the chapter, we saw in full rebellion against God and His Guidance returned to their right senses — and although במדבר, although for their present generation consigned to hopeless wandering in the wilderness, — we see them again conscious of their duty and standing up with all earnestness against any of its members for the due allegiance to God and His Torah. The introductory words: ויהיו בני ישראל במדבר, as well as the whole way in which this event is reported compared with that of the מקלל in Levit. 24,10 et seq. indicates that here special stress is laid on the initiative of the people which was exercised. It does not say: ויצא איש ויקושש עצים ביום השבת ויביאו אותו אל משה וגו׳ but ויהיו בני ישראל במדבר וימצאו וגו׳ ויקריבו המוצאים אתו וגו׳ whereby the report directs our attention more to the activity of the children of Israel and their intervention to uphold the Torah than to the sinner.

מקושש עצים (see Ex. 5,7). There we left it undecided whether קשש was related to גזז ,קצץ, to cut, to cut short, or to גשש to grope about, to pick up something solid. So also in Sabbath 96,b it is left in doubt which actual מלאכה the מקשש was guilty of committing, whether תולש or מעמר or מעביר ד׳ אמות ברה״ר whether it was cutting wood, gathering or carrying (see Ex. on Ch. 35,1 & 2). If it was the latter, the introductory remark of ויהיו בני ישראל במדבר could have a very significant meaning in relation to the whole event. For from Sabbath 6b it is evident that מדבר, the wilderness in itself, is not reckoned as רשות הרבים, as a public domain, and it was only בזמן שישראל שרויין במדבר that only owing to Israel’s presence there and during that time that the wilderness had the character of a רה״ר. So that by the remark ויהיו בני ישראל במדבר, the action of the מקשש — assuming it to have been העברת ד׳ אמות ברשות הרבים — could first have established the fact that it was against the law and thereby at the same time to forestall the error of making the event a precedent for fixing the character of a wilderness at other times, when Israel is not במדבר. To this we would add a further remark. If, according to the accepted Halacha, Sabbath is the one institution the desecration of which is raised to the level of ע״ז only if committed in public, פרהסיא, and מומר לחלל שבת בפרהסיא, similarly to מומר לע״ז is considered מומר לכל התורה כולה (Chulin 5a), then just here, where the similarity of חילול שבת and ע״ז is stressed by its juxtaposition with the preceding passage, the remark that בני ישראל were at the place and that the sin was committed in their presence, המצאים אתו מקשש עצים (see V.33) would be of the most essential importance. When we consider that the concept פרסום ,פרהסיא, “in public” is not confined to the actual presence of ten people, עשרה ישראל, but applies if the sinner knows that his act will become publicly known, יודע שיתפרסם (Avoda Zara 74b: שו״ת מהרי״ק 160), then every desecration of the Sabbath which would come to be punished by the human court of justice would come under the heading of being done in public and so be equal to ע״ז. The עדים והתראה, the two witnesses of the deed who have also to warn the sinner of the gravity of what he is about to do, and of the penalty entailed, make him aware that he will be committing his sin in the publicity of the whole nation whose court of justice he treats with his attitude of אף על פי כן, “I don’t care”. So that the stress which our text here lays on the presence of the בני ישראל at the sin of the מקשש can well be the reason for the fact, which has legal repercussions, that it is only בפרהסיא that חילול שבת is equal to ע״ז

V. 33. ויקריבו אתו המצאים וגו׳. By this repeated naming of the subject “המצאים אתו מקשש עצים״ the Gemorah in Sanhedrin 41a takes it that we are told that not only did they find him having done the action, but found that he went on doing it, i.e. that he did it completely conscious of its illegal character and of the consequences of it, a condition that could only arise by the continuation of the act after due warning, שהתרו :התראה בו ועדין הוא מקשש (cf. Levit. 20,2 p.570).

V. 34. ויניחו אתו במשמר. This is detention in custody on remand, which is also assumed in Ex. 21,19 פרש .כי לא פרש מה יעשה לו see on Levit. 24,12. There, at the מקלל it says:- לפרש להם על פי ה׳, nothing at all had yet been said about the nature of punishment to which the crime made the criminal liable. But here: כי לא פרש מה יעשה לו, that it was a capital crime punishable by death was in no doubt, מחלליה מות יומת (Ex. 31,14) had already been proclaimed, the only doubt was מה יעשה לו, which form of death was to be administered. יודע היה משה רבינו שהמקושש במיתה שנאמר מחלליה מות יומת אלא לא היה יודע באיזו מיתה נהרג (Sanhedrin 78b). Nevertheless the התראה was legally sufficient, for all that is required is שהתרו בו כתם that he is told that what he does is a capital crime (Ibid. 80b). But in the opinion of ר׳ יהודה any התראה is incomplete if the actual form of the death to which he is liable is not specified to the criminal, then the killing of the מקושש was a special case, an הוראת שעה dictated directly by God, and can not be used as an example for general practice. Perhaps this opinion of ר׳ יהודה may be the explanation of the sentence in the Sifri on our verse: מות יומת האיש לדורות רגום אותו באבנים לשעה, it would mean we can learn from this case that מקושש is to be put to death, provided of course that all the legal requirements are complied with and the full warning given, but this particular case was carried out only in accordance with the special directions from God. In the case of מקלל where the התראה could not have been on the death penalty at all, it was in any case an הוראת שעה (ibid. 78b).
