ויוצא פרח וגו׳. Whereas פרח (related to פרה, see Gen. I, on V.11, p.16) quite definitely means flower and blossom and hence as a verb פרח predominantly means to blossom, everything indicates that in ציץ we can only see the expression for shoots which push their way out. So that one is scarcely justified in taking ציץ here to indicate a further stage of the blossom. But almond trees have the peculiarity to a much higher degree than apple trees or other fruit trees (see Sabbath 88a) of putting forth blossoms before leaves in Spring. It hardly shows any leaf formation before it stands in all the glory of blossom. Hence we take ויצץ ציץ to refer to the putting forth of leaves. But the sprouting of the staff to the branch of just an almond tree would be, to the highest degree the most suitable to conform to the thoughts to be symbolised here. Is not the germinating power to produce leaf, blossom and fruit similar in all the trees in an orchard, does not the same earth bear them all, the same moisture water them, the same air waft over them, the same rays of sunlight warm them? And yet does not the almond tree stand out distinguished among all its comrades in the early days of Spring. And in what is it distinguished? In שקידה from which it gets its name, in eager zeal, in keenness, in happy vigorous devotion and energy for that which it has to accomplish. While its brother-trees are still making up their minds it has already acted, and right from the beginning puts the goal, the production of fruit, the fruit-blossom, in the foreground, the object for which it exists, and for which it then produces its leaves, the lungs to supply the necessary saps for the ultimate goal, the fruit. But is not this the most complete pithy picture of the Levite spirit which had ennobled the tribe of Levi to be the representative of the Divine Torah and its Sanctuary, when it alone amongst its fellow-tribes flocked to Moses in response to the call מי לה׳ אלי (To me, those who are for God. Ex. 32,26 I.L.), and which is to be inherited in its purest perfection by the elite of that tribe, Aaron and his descendants, (cf. Ex. XXV, on the Menora p.469 et seq.). There we took ציץ to be the pollen stamens or the pistils. But we are doubtful if that is exactly what is meant, as these are already formed when the blossom opens and do not belong to a later stage. But at the same time the consolatory thought could be expressed that, just as the almond tree only blossoms and matures its fruit earlier than the others, only leads the way in development, which the others then follow, so the Levites and Aaronides are not superior to the rest of the Israelites but are only always to be in the van, leading spiritual and general development of life which all the other brother-tribes are called on to follow and attain the same spiritual level.

V. 25. ויאמר וגו׳. Just as the לוחת העדות testified to the fact of the Divine origin of the Torah, so did the מטה אהרן testify to the fact of the Divine origin of the choice of the Aaronides to be the priests of the Sanctuary of that Torah. This co-ordinating the מטה אהרן to the לוחת העדות in the Sanctuary, the separating the Aaronides out of the Levites, and the Levites out of the nation who are thereby kept at a distance from the Sanctuary of the Torah may be taken as a continuation of the הגבלה (fencing the people off from the Mount at the Lawgiving on Sinai, I.L. See Ex. 19,10-13) by which, immediately at the giving of the Torah — the evidence for which was perpetuated by the לוחות — it was brought home to the minds of the people that the Torah came to the people, did not emanate from them. We have already worked out there the deep importance of that fact. The whole indivisibility, inviolability and eternity of the Torah rests on it. But the same הגבלה is carried on for all time by the grouping of the Aaronides and Levites about the Sanctuary of the Torah and the keeping the people afar from it, and thereby the firm establishment for all time of the same fact of the superhuman origin and the independence on place or time of the Torah. For the more the Jewish people, without any difference of class, profession or occupation, are called upon unreservedly to study, acknowledge and keep this Torah; the more in course of time the Torah accomplishes its purpose on the people, and permeates all their minds, hearts, feelings, ways of looking at life and the achievements of life; the more thereby in course of time, the spirit of the people begotten by the Torah comes near to the spirit of the Torah; finally, the more the gap closes between the ideals of this Torah and their being realised in the lives of the people, the more, in the course of time, the assertion of Korach כל העדה כולם קדושים ובתוכם ה׳ loses its arrogant presumptiousness, — the more grounds there are for the fear that the human mind might turn against the source of its enlightenment, and, denying its Divine origin and substituting a human brain as its begetter, cease to be pupil, adherent and servitor of the Torah and make bold to be its critical master. To that, for all time, comes the warning to the people by the continuance of the הגבלה of the עדות and its Sanctuary by the לוים and כהנים. It brings home to them with all seriousness, how even the highest intellectuals of the Jewish people, to whom the Torah is still to form the constant object of their inner lives and the central focus to which their brains must trust, must realise how it must remain untouched and unapproachable in its God-given objectivity; how even the כהנים, the priests dare not approach its עדות, the Sanctuary in their individual personalities but only in the vestments symbolic of their service and only after קידוש ידים ורגלים (the symbolic washing of hands and feet I.L.). It repeats throughout the centuries the warning from Sinai: רד העד בעם פן יהרסו אל ה׳ לראות ונפל ממנו רב וגם הכהנים הנגשים אל ה׳ יתקדשו פן יפרץ בהם ה׳!

V. 27—28. ויאמרו וגו׳. By all these experiences and the final evidence of Aaron’s staff the people at last fully appreciated the sanctity of the Evidence which lay in the allowing Aaronides and Levites exclusively to approach the Sanctuary itself (their presence being limited to the חצר the courtyard, I.L.). So now death threatened even from some unintentional unavoidable approach to it. They saw themselves, if not yet actually dead, still near unavoidable death בגויעה in the transition stage of death. And in their anxiety they pertinently express the danger-bringing sharp thin line at which altogether every Jew is placed in his relation to the Divine Sanctuary of the Torah. Every one is קרב and yet may not be too קרב; Everyone is called to its proximity, to its approach — and still may not come too near. God’s Torah, the Evidence for which reposes in the Sanctuary is exactly “fire” as remarked by our Sages in ספרי on Deut. 33,2, קרוב לאדם נכוה רחוק ממנה צונן “who comes too near gets burnt, who keeps afar remains cold”. One has to come near to it but in doing so must always have respect to keep at the required distance and not lay hands on it.

But as a matter of fact regarding the קריבה אל משבן ה׳, regarding the approach to the actual Sanctuary there is no such wide gulf between priest and non-priest as the people in their anxiety imagined. Any capricious entry into the היכל, not for the purpose of עבודה as prescribed, is forbidden to every priest, and into the קודש הקדשים, for him too, is under the threat of death of מיתה בידי שמים (see Levit. on XVI,2); but for the purposes of the Sanctuary, for repairs to the building, or other requirements לבנות לתקן ולהוציא את הטומאה, in necessary cases, entry into the היכל is permitted to non-cohanim (Eruvim 105a see מל״מ end of הל׳ ביאת המקדש). It is only regarding עבודה, against performing any of the service, where there is a difference between priest and non-priest, and where the latter if transgressing במזיד, intentionally, comes under the penalty of מיתה בידי שמים, and even then, only in certain limited cases (see next chapter 3-7).

V. 1. ויאמר וגו׳. This is no new law (not וידבר I.L.). It was only the explanation of the conditions already existing in accordance with God’s commands which was reassuringly to be given to the people to set their minds at ease. It was not the people who need fear the threat of the consequences of a forgetful or careless attitude to the Sanctuary, but Aaron and his tribe, all those who are called on for service to the Sanctuary and its holy objects, only they bear responsibility for any carelessness or forgetfulness in their duty. It is in this way too that the Sifri takes it: ויאמר ה׳ אל אהרן אתה ובניך ובית אביך אתך תשאו את עון הקדש, ר׳ ישמעאל אומר למי הדבר מסור לאהרן אותו הזהיר (גי׳ הגר״א), ר׳ יאשי׳ אומר מנין אתה אומר שאם זרק את הדם כראוי ואינו יודע לשם מי זרקו הקטיר את החלב כראוי ואינו יודע לשם מי הקטירו שהטעים נושאים עון על כך ת״ל אתה וביתך ובית אביך אתך תשאו את עון המקדש. ר׳ יונתן אומר שאם זכה בבשר קודם זריקת דמים, בחזה ושוק קודם הקטר חלבים שהכהנים נושאים עון על כך ת״ל ואתה ובניך תשאו את עון כהונתכם. וכן מצינו שלא נחתם גזר דינו של יעלי גם בטרם יקטירון את החלב ויאמר (I. Sam. 2) אלא על שנהגו בזיון בקדשים וכה״א אליו האיש קטר יקטירון כיום החלב ותה׳ חטאת הנערים גדולה מאוה וכן מצינו שלא נחתם גזר דינם של אנשי ירושלים אלא על שנהגו מנהג בזיון בקדשים שנאמר (Ezek. XXII) קדשי בזית. Clearly the Sifri does not regard the תשאו את עון המקדש and the תשאו עון כהונתכם as referring to the responsibility of Aaron and his fellow ministers of the service for not allowing the people into the Sanctuary itself, for, as already remarked, and as is clear from the following there is no real wrong, and certainly no capital sin, if the people do enter the halls of the Sanctuary, (with the exception of the Holy of Holies which even the high-priest may not enter except on י״כ). But they refer to the responsibility of Aaron and the priests for sins which they themselves could come to commit carelessly (such as not keeping in mind the person on whose behalf he was functioning, or not keeping strictly to the order prescribed for the procedures of the offerings etc. I.L.) in their service in the Sanctuary. So that it is not on the people — who in any case are not called on for such service — but just on those who are called on to perform it, that such a grave responsibility lies. Not the people, but למי הדבר מסור to whom the service of the Sanctuary is assigned, אותו הזהיר, they have to keep the stern admonishment constantly and keenly in mind. So that in the exclusion of the people from service in the Sanctuary, which certainly was sharply demonstrated for all time by the outcome of Korach’s rebellion, there lay more protection than threat for the people.

The examples which the Sifri gives to explain what constitutes an עון המקדש and an עון כהנתכם show the מקדש to be regarded not as a “Sanctuary Building” in the world, containing certain objects, but as an “Institution for the dissemination of Holiness”, the purpose of which is attained principally by the procedures of the offerings which express and preach to us its demands for the way our lives are to be lived. Now it takes as its example as a sin against this Institution, the case where the functioning priest does not keep in mind all the particular details of this particular offering, e.g. although he performed the זריקת דמים and the הקטרת חלב (the Service of the Blood and the offering of the “fat pieces” on to the fire on the altar I.L.) perfectly correctly, and realised what the acts were meant to symbolise, he did not keep in mind the particular individual on whose behalf the offering is being made, and whose life and desires and endeavours are to be symbolised by this זריקה and הקטרה as being brought near to being devoted to God. Now although not only כל הזבחים שנזבחו שלא לשמן כשרים אלא שלא עלו לבעלים לשם חובה (Zebachim 2a), “If an offering brought by somebody to fulfil his vow to bring an elevating-offering had been slaughtered for a peace-offering, the remaining procedures may be done, and the offering is כשר, only the owner has to bring another elevating-offering in fulfilment of his vow”, (see also Levit. 1,9 at end of commentary thereon), but even in the case where the priest “forgets” to think לשם מי זרקו, for which particular person he is performing the “blood-service”, the owner would not have to bring another one, it is עלה לשם חובה (ibid, b) as סתמא עלו נמי לבעלים לשם חובה (not being slaughtered for any particular person or offering does not interfere with the general lesson and sermon preached by the “service of the blood” applying to the owner as well I.L.). Further, even a positive alteration by mistaking the nature of the animal (e.g. the priest thought a sheep was a ram I.L.) does not interfere with the validity of the offering, עקירה בטעות לא הויא עקירה (Menachoth 49a); and finally regarding הקטרה, which is also given here as an example of our שינוי בעלים ,עון מקדש is altogether without any effect (תוספות Zebachim 2a) (Yea, according to מל״מ הל׳ פסולי מוקדשים 15, 1, even at the זריקה the complete validity of the offering would only be marred by שינוי בעלים in the case where שחט או קבל או הלך קרבן ראובן על מנת לזרוק דמו לשם שמעון but זרק דם קרבן ראובן לשם שמעון would not matter). Accordingly the Sifri chooses for an example of עון מקדש a case of thoughtlessness out of which no disturbance in the normal procedure of the Sanctuary arises, and which nevertheless falls back on the person of the priest as a grave sin, who, in any case, has sinned against the canon לשם ששה דברים הזבח נזבח ובו׳ (see on Levit. 1,9) and even comes near to that thoughtlessness, מתעסק בקדשים (just performing the physical actions of all the procedure of an offering without any thought of the symbolic spirit it expresses I.L.) which, in any case, would annul the whole meaning and validity of the offering. (Zebachim 47b).

So that עון המקדש is a sin against the Institution for Disseminating Holiness, towards which עון הכהונה is a misuse of the priesthood for one’s own selfish ends. Such a misuse is a sin against the priesthood, which it degrades thereby. As an example, a case is again chosen which, on the face of it, appears very slight but which involves one of the worst sins. Not only if a priest were to presume to take to himself something to which he is not entitled, but even if he only takes to himself something which is to come to him a little before it is due to do so, the בשר before the זריקת הדם (the meat before the Service of the Blood had been performed I.L.) the חזה ושוק before the הקטר חלבים (the breast and thigh before the fat-pieces had been placed on the fire on the altar I.L.) he would commit a grave sin. The whole meaning of the Sanctuary and his service therein must have escaped his attention, he must have quite forgotten that, as the saying goes, משולחן גבוה קא זכי (what he gets from the offerings for himself is something from “God’s Table”, I.L.), he must be considering himself as quite in the foreground, and looking on the whole Sanctuary as being there just for his emoluments.

In that forgetfulness and in this greedy coarseness the whole character of the Sanctuary becomes lost, it is מנהג בזיון בקדשים, attaching little value to the holy things entrusted to the priest in their behaviour and handling of them. It was on this fault that the house of Eli foundered, and is referred to with great seriousness. And when the people lost valuing the Temple at its true worth and for its true function, and it became no longer an institution for the dissemination of holiness which only a holy national life is justified in having, but had sunk down to a place for coming to an arrangement with God, that by meticulously keeping up all the prescribed procedures in it one could thereby purchase a licence for unbridling all restraints in life, then to it also God applied the term: קדשי בזית (Ezek. 22,8), and the Temple went to ruins and the people to exile.

It only remains to explain the meaning of בית אביך in the first sentence of our verse. If, as it seems from the Sifri the עון המקדש refers to sins of the priests against the holiness of the procedures which were performed in the Sanctuary it is difficult to whom this בית אביך refers. Apparently, as is clear from the second sentence, אתה ובניך describes the whole tribe of priests and בית אביך can only be a description of the בית לוי the whole tribe of Levi, of which the בית אהרן only form a special branch. And as a matter of fact there is an extract from a Midrash quoted in the Yalkut on our verse which does take the בית אביך to mean the Levites and makes them participate in the responsibility for the lapses of the priests in the Sanctuary: אתה ובניך, הכהנים, ובית אביך, אלו הלוים, מלמד שהלוים מוזהרים על ידי הנהנים, a relationship which is quite in keeping with the position of the priests to the Levites (See Levit. on Ch. 22,9 p.620). But this can not be the way the Sifri takes our verse to mean, for there, on V.23 והם ישאו עונם it expressly says that the Levites have no responsibility for the services which the priests have to render in the Sanctuary. We believe, accordingly, that עון המקדש embraces both the service in the Sanctuary as well as that of the Sanctuary i.e., of the whole dissemination of holiness emanating from the Sanctuary, and the care of the Sanctuary itself, and makes the Levites responsible for thoughtless or unworthy carrying out their service, in the same way as the Sifri pictures the possibility of the priests doing theirs in the examples it gives.

V. 2. וגם וגו׳ refers back to the last sentence in the previous verse. Although the real priesthood devolves on you and your sons, nevertheless, the Levites הקרב אתך, let them come near with you. This הקרב אתך is certainly to be differentiated from the וילוו עליך וישרתוך .וילוו עליך gives them a position next to and, subservient to you. But הקרב אתך allows them to come near to God with Aaron parallel to him and assigns them to a function side by side with the priests. This, as ר׳ עקיבא explains in the Sifri, להזהיר את הלוים בשיר על דוכנם, is the singing of Divinely inspired songs with which the Levites complemented the procedures of the national offerings in the Temple standing at the side of the priests, (see above on Ch. 3,15). This is the specific office of the Levites in the Sanctuary. וילוו עליך וישרתוך בעבודתך, thus, the version in Tamid 26b. Whereas הקרב אתך confers on them an independant office, viz., שיר, the וילוו עליך וישרתוך allows them to attach themselves in a co-ordinate and subordinate capacity, and participate בעבודתך in the service which really belongs to the priests. This priestly service in which the Levites also have to take part is, according to Tamid 26b, the guard in the עזרה (the ante-chamber of the Sanctuary I.L.) which here is entrusted to the priests by אתה ובניך אתך לפני אהל העדות. In that service the Levites also participated (ibid.): הכהנים שומרים מלמעלה ולוים מלמטה. The Sifri has the version הכהנים מבפנים והלוים מבחוץ. Apart from this the Levites by themselves kept guard at twenty one posts round about the Temple (ibid. 27a; see מל״מ, ה׳ בית הבחירה VIII,4). For the meaning of this Levite guard see on Ch. 1,51. Further, they rendered help by acting as גזבר (administrators, treasurers etc.) and אמרכל (senior inspectors etc.) (Sifri). And besides this even at the service of the offerings there were acts such as ניתוח ,הפשט ,שחיטה (the slaughter, flaying and cutting up of the animals for the offerings) which need not be done by the priests themselves, and so when the pressure was great (e.g. erevpessach etc. I.L.) could be done by the Levites and possibly could also be considered as וישרתוך.

In laying down the precise position of the Levites here, the relation of the tribe of Levi to Aaron is described in three ways, as ,מטה לוי ,אחיך אחיך .שבט אביך represents the equality of birth, out of which a position near to God similar to that of the priest could arise. This would refer to the הקרב אתך, to the singing of appropriate psalms and hymns at the service of the offerings, which our Sages take to be meant by ושרת בשם ה׳ מטה, from נטה, the horizontal direction, looks on the tribe as a “branch” of the basic stem, accordingly as being on a line with the other tribes, and so, being excluded from the actual priestly service, would only be allowed to be allocated to assist at subsidiary offices, the שבט .וילוו עליך וישרתוך is the tribe as independent stem, “stave”, hence, as the word itself is an expression of strength and power, as a rule is the designation of the “tribes of Israel” in their independent strength and value, שבטי ישראל not מטות ישראל etc. So that שבט אביך is the tribe in which your father lives on in his speciality, your father who subscribes such an important quota to the Jewish national body, the tribe that by its unreserved devotion to the cause of God showed itself as the “born guard of the Sanctuary”. As שבט אביך the Levites received their position and mission towards the people, which was represented by the guard of their camp round the Sanctuary in the wilderness, which belongs to the משמרת אהל מועד of the next verse. This was carried on in the time of the Temple, in the twenty one posts round about the Temple and its halls, (the so-called “outer watch” I.L.). The inner watch, לפני אהל העדות, at three posts inside the halls before the real Sanctuary, was undertaken by the priests, who were to look on themselves therein only as the flower of the Levites, and by this watch were to manifest their Levite character. In these three posts the Levites only took an auxillary part as mentioned above.

V. 3. ושמרו וגו׳ (cf. Ch. 3,6-8). משמרתך is your service, in which at your request they are to be at your side as helpers. משמרת כל האהל is all their independent service in erecting maintaining and guarding the Tabernacle which is entrusted to them. אך אל כלי הקדש וגו׳: It is not approaching, touching or handling the holy objects which is forbidden to them here, but approaching the Altar for (to perform the offering-procedures I.L.) which they are prohibited to do (See ל״ת ,ספר המצות ,רמב״ם 32, and מל״מ at the end of ה׳ ביאת המקדש. Also ל״ת ,סמ״ג 297). ולא ימותו גם הם גם אתם, אתם בשלהם והם בשלכם במיתה (Arachin 11b) just as the service of the offerings is given over to the priests, so is the accompanying service of song given over to the Levites, and just as the Levites may not undertake the service of the priest, so may no priest undertake any of the services of the Levite, and both would incur the death-penalty, מיתה בידי שמים. More, even הם בשלהם, amongst the Levites even the capricious change from משורר to משוער, from the choir to the guard or vice versa is forbidden באזהרה or even במיתה (ibid.; see on Ch. 1,51).

V. 4. ונלוו עליך וגו׳ (cf. Ch. 3,7 & 8). לעבודה :וזר לא יקרב אליכם (Sifri). No unauthorised person may come to perform any עבודה to which you have been appointed. This is the warning, the non-observance of which is considered in V.7 as incurring מיתה בידי שמים (Sifri, see also Zebachim 16a).

V. 5. משמרת הקדש ,ושמרתם וגו׳ is the guarding and care of the Sanctuary which represents the Jewish task of life; משמרת מזבח is the guarding and care of the Altar, the purpose of which is to represent the deeds of devotion to that task. The former is the task of the Levites in conjunction with the priests, the latter the special task of the priests. In Sifri, in this ושמרתם is seen the demand for the highest representative body in Israel, the Sanhedrin, to supervise the priests and see to it that they do carry out their service. הרי זו אזהרה לב״ד של ישראל להזהיר את הכהנים שתהא העבודה כתיקונה שכשעבודה נעשית כתיקונה הם כלים את הפורענות מלבא לעולם. A supposition which seems all the more admissable as, according to Rashi’s way of taking the Sifri, this and the following פרשה were not said directly to Aaron, but to Moses for Aaron.

Part of this שמירה certainly consisted in keeping all זרים away from performing the עבודה. The carrying out of all the עבודה in the Sanctuary and at the Sanctuary is so stamped with the imprint of submitting oneself to obedience of the Law, even for the priest and Levites who are permitted to serve, any and every subjective idea of their own is so rigidly excluded, all clearly expressing the fact that the whole Sanctuary and its service down to the smallest detail is something dictated by God and not by human beings, that by faithfully carrying out the service in that way, the erroneous idea which had threatened the downfall of the people would automatically be prevented from arising again, ולא יהיה עוד קצף על בני ישראל.

V. 6—7. ואני וגו׳. Finally, once again the exclusive permission for the Levites and Aaronides to perform service at and in the Sanctuary is proclaimed as proceeding purely from God Himself. This does away with every idea of arrogance and presumption and all danger of conceited pride on the part of those who are permitted, and vindicates the stamp of absolute godliness on the service, the servers and on the Law to which the whole of the Sanctuary is dedicated and to which the whole service refers. ואני, it is from Me that the whole choice emanated. הנה לקחתי וגו׳, the Levites themselves were completely passive at the whole of this choice and only carry out a decree which God made for them. לכם וגו׳, and the priests to whom they are subordinated have no original right over them, or anything arising out of their own authority. מתנה וגו׳, they get them as a gift, and moreover, only for quite fixed limited purposes: לה׳, only in the service of God, not in their own service may they use them. לה׳ הם מסורים ואין מסורים לכהנים (Sifri).

כל דבר המזבח .ואתה ובניך וגו׳ is everything that has to be done on the מבית לפרכת ;מזבח החיצון are all the עבודות פנים in the קדש הקדשים on י״כ, and ולמבית לפרכת includes everything to be done on the מזבח הזהב in the היכל and on פרכת כנגד בין הבדים (Yoma 24, 36). ועבדתם, accordingly, all the עבודות which are to be done either in the עזרה, the היכל or in the קדש הקדשים, you have to do. And by וזר לא יקרב אליכם (V.4) every non-priest has already been prohibited to perform anything that comes under the heading of עבודה by אזהרה the Halacha teaches that here, where by והזר הקרב יומת, any non-priest who takes upon himself to perform a priestly function is punished by מיתה בידי שמים, an עבודה is only considered as such in the stage of its being completed (cf. Ex. 28,357), עבודה תמה ולא עבודה שיש אחריה עבודה so that the חיוב מיתה for a זר is only incurred if he had performed an עבודה which completes the act. e.g. זריקה which completes the עבודת הדם, or הקטרת קומץ by which the עבודת אש of the מנחה is completed, and so also הקטרת אברים ואימורים but not if he only performed an introductory עבודה such as קבלה והולכה with the blood, or קמיצה at the מנחה (Yoma, 24a).

Further, the specifically priestly עבודה is characterised as עבודת מתנה as עבודה as a gift, of giving oneself, of devotion. All the acts performed in the Sanctuary reach their height in the concept: מתנה, in the concept of giving oneself up, of devotion. Whereas the מקדש with the שולחן ,ארון and מנורה, Ark, Table and Lamp, represent all that we receive from God through the Torah and for the Torah, the whole עבודה in the Sanctuary has the purpose of teaching us to give ourselves and to give all the gifts that we receive from God up to Him and His Torah. זריקה and נתינה and הזיה of the דם הנפש on the Altar, the פרכת and the הקטרה — כפרח of the חלב and כליות, the אברים, the קומץ and the מנחה on the fire of the Altar, and the קטרת on the מזבח הזהב; and on י״כ in the ניסוך המים — קדש הקדשים on חג and ניסוך היין daily, all these acts in which the עבודה in the Sanctuary reaches its high points, are all מתנות are “gifts”, giving ourselves up, in which the sum of the tasks and mission of our lives are represented. The whole כהונה, the whole purpose of the priesthood is to teach themselves and the people the “direction” of their lives indicated by God, and is nought but עבודת מתנה, a service to effect “giving oneself up” to God. That is why the badge עבודת מתנה ולא עבודת סילוק, i.e. “an act of giving and not an act of taking away” (as e.g. תרומת הדשן) is added to the badge עבודה תמה to mark the specific priestly עבודה. The performance of which by a זר entails death must be both an עבודה תמה and an עבודת מתנה (Yoma 24a). Hence the sentence in Sanhedrin 82b: היוצק והבולל והפותת והמולח והמניף המגיש והמסדר את השולחן המטיב את הנרות והקומץ והמקבל דמים בחוץ פטור ואין חייבין עליהן לא משום זרות ולא משום טומאה ולא משום מחוסר בגדים ולא משום ריחוץ ידים ורגלים.

But now follows the deeply significant saying: עבודת מתנה אתן את כהונתכם: “God will give us our giving ourselves”, i.e. — if we understand it rightly —: מתנה, a gift, certainly designates a free act of our personal will. Therefore עבודת מתנה, the giving up of ourselves and our possessions to God is to be an act flowing from the deepest well of our moral freedom of will. Still, on the other hand, this עבודה, this giving up to God, in its motives, in the way it is to be done, in every way is so far from all arbitrary action, is so very much formulated, is to be so very much nothing but free-willed obedience, is so much regulated by the laws of God’s Torah, that not only the things we “gift”, the things we call our own in reality belong to God, and we are only returning what we received from Him, (מידך נתנו לך, I. Chron. 29,14), but the very fact that we do give is itself a demand from God, so that in truth our עבודת מתנה, the free-willed devotion of ourselves and all we have to God, as accomplished by our priests on our behalf, is a נתינה from God. It brings about that God’s Will becomes accomplished by our free-willed obedience.

It is on this free-willed obedience to the Will of God that Judaism stands. It rejects the mere internal “pious” devout impulse that seeks to express itself and find satisfaction in its own idea of pleasing God, and calls the ritual “Divine Service”. Judaism believes “God hath told thee, O man, what ‘good’ is, and what He requireth of thee” (Micha 6,8), its Divine Service is serving God, obedience, is faithfully carrying out God’s expressed Will. The most holy object in its holy of holies is God’s Law, His Torah; the acts of symbolic devotion to this Torah are themselves regulated and fixed by this Torah; those who perform these acts are appointed by God as ministrants of this Torah, as is also its Sanctuary, and in the name of God and His Torah, they accept and administer the symbols of our free-willed devotion to the demands fixed by that Torah. By the exclusive appointment of the Aaronides for the עבודת מתנה in the Sanctuary of His Torah, this Torah itself and its Sanctuary receive the last stamp of its Divine origin as well as all the life we are to lead being shown to be devoted to fulfilling the Divine Will.

Korach’s כל העדה כולם קדושים ובתוכם ה׳, by which he proclaimed the uprising against the choice of the priests, was, at its base, a denial of the divinity of Moses’s mission and of the laws transmitted by him. In its place he wanted to substitute the subjectivity of every individual, who would only have to follow the holy inner impulses of his heart and its inspirations to attain nearness to God and His satisfaction.
To this subjectivity undermining the whole of Judaism the Word of God concludes here with :עבודת מתנה אתן את כהנתכם והזר הקרב יומת מיתה בידי שמים (Sanhedrin 84a).

V. 8. וידבר וגו׳. The foregoing announced the privileged position of the priests and Levites towards the Sanctuary and the responsibility which that entailed. To that now here is added a summary of their rights in the nation, on which the stamp of Divine arrangement is no less imprinted, but also, at the same time, the duties which are attached to these rights.

ואני הנה נתתי וגו׳. In Sabbat 25a, and 26a, and also in Bechoroth 34a, תרומתי is understood to refer to the “heave-gift” which is specially called תרומה to be given from the produce which is ready to be used for human food, מן התורה only from דגן תירוש ויצהר, grain, wine and oil, the three principal products for human food. This is the most generally accepted opinion (see תוספות, Bechoroth 54a). רמב״ם הל׳ תרומות 2,1, seems to take תרומות ומעשרות of all produce as דאוריתא with the exception of ירקות which do not come under the conception of תבואת זרעך the real harvest (see מל״מ thereon; ש״ע י״ד 331, 13, adopts the view of the רמב״ם). On Levit. 22,19 we have already worked out the meaning of the “heave-gift”, and showed how, on the one side, to the people, to whom before “heaving” the תרומה may not use the rest of their produce, it brings home to them that their whole material existence is dependent on their observance of the laws of the Torah, but on the other side, to the priest, whose whole existence is directed to this gift from the people, dedicated to him by God and His Torah; it brings the reminder and admonition with every piece of bread he eats that the Torah and the Sanctuary, in whose service he stands, is not a monopoly of the priests but is the Sanctuary of the nation. That he is only appointed by God as minister of the Torah and its Sanctuary, as the representative of the people; that he has to thank that Torah and its Sanctuary for the whole means of his existence; that he is only worthy of his bread if the whole existence of himself and his household, which is fed by this bread of the Sanctuary, is used to furthering and blossoming in the nation of the seeds which he has to plant in the Sanctuary. That is why he has to respect his Teruma-bread as תרומתי as something belonging to God which has been entrusted to him למשמרת to guard with due respect to its character and purpose. Although לך, although the property of the priest, נכסי כהנים, it still remains קדש, holy, and as declared in Levit. (ibid.), has to be protected from טומאה and may only be eaten בטהרה, and in its use, too, there are restrictions. He has to protect it from טומאה, and indeed, as the Halacha in Bechoroth 34a, explains, בשתי תרומות הכתוב מדבר אחת תרומה טהורה ואחת :תרומותי תרומה תלויה ואמר רחמנא עביד ליה שימור, even תלויה, where the טהרה character has become “wavering”, שנולד בה ספק טומאה even where there is a doubt that it might be unfit, it must still be guarded not to become טומאת ודאי, certainly unfit. As here it is talking about Teruma in both conditions, in טהרה and טומאה, and it says לך that both are placed at the disposition of the priest, the Gemora teaches in Sabbat, 25a that תרומה טמאה, which, like all קדש שנטמא, has to be burnt, is permitted to be made use of, as implied by לך. Hence שמן תרומה טמאה, usually called שמן שרפה, may be used for lighting or cooking as it is being burnt, בשעת ביעורה תהנה. This use, הנאה של כילוי, “a use by destroying it”, as it is called is not permitted in the case of תרומה טהורה (which must be eaten and not burnt I.L.). As already remarked, the priest is altogether restricted in the use he may have of his Teruma. He may use it for סחורה, trade (Shevieit 7,3), אסור לאבדן, he may not use it even for food by cooking or preparing it in such a way that only part of it will be eaten and the rest thrown away (Terumoth 11,1), may only use it in its original form, אין משנין אותן מברייתן (ibid.) (may not make it unrecognisable I.L.), not make dates into honey, apples into cider, etc. etc. טהרה (the conviction of the certainty of moral free-will I.L.) and obedience are the two thoughts that are constantly brought home to the minds of the priests and their families with תרומה, the food they live on; they feed themselves on “bread which is holy to God” for which they have to make themselves worthy by “moral purity and faithfulness to duty” in their whole lives.

לכל קדשי בני ישראל: the same responsibility and care which is made their duty to have with Teruma, they are to have for all קדשי בני ישראל, which לך נתתים למשחה, are given by God to the priests for a continuous משיחה “anointment” i.e. given to be a continuous reminder of the separating out and keeping apart from everything low and not holy, which indeed is the meaning of anointing (see Ex. 29,7). And only in anticipation of this “consecration” are they given to the priests as חק עולם, as an everlasting due.

V. 9. זה יהיה לך וגו׳. The summary of the מתנות כהונה, the gifts to be given to the priests, starts with the final one, the parts of the offering they receive. First מקדש קדשים from offering dedicating future actions (see (Ex. XXIX). מן האש, after the אש אוכלה, the consuming fire, the אש דת (representing the Fire of the Torah I.L.) has become לחם אשה (food, the means for keeping the fires of godliness burning in the world I.L.), to which the אכילת כהנים is attached merely as the complementing and completing consequence (see Ex. 29,33). כל קרבנם, everything that they bring near to God in order therewith to attain nearness to God. In Zebachim 44b, the comprehensive terms לכל מנחתם ,כל קרבנם etc., are explained as being meant to include the priest’s rights in such categories of offerings which otherwise have not been mentioned and which cannot be deduced by analogy; כל קרבנם including לוג שמן של מצורע (Levit. 14,12 & 18) which comes under the heading of קרבן by the term והקריב being applied to it there, and we would not have deduced it, as it does not come לכל מנחתם ;מן האש including מנחת העומר (Levit. 23,10) and מנחת הקנאות (Numb. 5,15), although their purpose is not actually כפרה and would not be taken to be included under ואכלו אותם אשר כופר בהם (Ex. 29,33, refer to it); ולכל חטאתם, including חטאת העוף, although killed by מליקה which in general effects נבלה (see Levit. 5,8); לכל אשמם, including אשם נזיר (Numb. 6,12). although this too does not come from any real necessity for כפרה, but only brings the broken period of Nazaritism to a close and starts a fresh one; ולכל אשמם אשר ישיבו לי: the אשם גזלות ,אשם תלוי ,אשם מעילה, and in a broad sense all the other אשמות in all of which, as we worked out in each case, there lies at base, a sinning in the realm of misuse of possessions, hence אשר ישיבו לי, — in Zebachim ibid, it includes specially גזל הגר, the קרן of which is just called אשם and where אשר ישיבו לי would apply in its full significance.

V. 10. בקדש הקדשים וגו׳. Not actually in the Holy of holies, but in the place appointed for the consumption of the most holy things, the עזרה, as has been already ordained for מנחה and חטאת and אשם in Levit. 6,9, 19 and VII,6. Here קדש could mean not the Sanctuary but holiness, as in אדמת קדש ,שבת קדש and בקדש קדשים here means in the holy manner of the holy things, part of which would be, as declared in the quotations referred to above, their having to be eaten in the עזרה. The eating of the offerings in these cases is itself a continuation and conclusion of the כפרה started by the עבודות at and on the Altar (see on Ex. 29,33). That is why this eating has to be done only by the זכרי כהונה. It is further taught from here in Zebachim, 97b that זבחי שלמי ציבור (Levit. 23,19) as belonging to קדש הקדשים may also be eaten only by זכרי כהונה.

V. 11. וזה לך וגו׳, here follow the קדשים קלים, such as שלמים and תודה, offerings referring more to our fate, which, after the חלב and כליות have been offered, come to be eaten in the family circle by the owners themselves. Of these the priests only get the חזה and שוק and at the תודה, one loaf of each of the four kinds of the לחמי תודה which accompany the תודה (see Levit. 7,14 & XXXI,32). With all these parts taken up from the meal-offerings for the Altar and for the priests, with the אימורים and חזה ושוק from the שלמים, and at the תודה also the four loaves, the procedure of תרומה ותנופה has to be performed. The אימורים are then placed on the Altar-fire. But the תרומה ותנופה is the characteristic procedure for חזה ושוק and לחמי תודה and they are called תרומה and תנופה after it (ibid. VII,14 and XXXII,34).

The construction of וזה לך תרומת וגו׳ נתתים וגו׳ is difficult to understand. Actually the object to which זה refers is missing. We believe that the thought תרומות is to be repeated, supplemented from תרומת מתנם, “This” is to come to you as תרומת מתנם, as a share which, inasmuch as it had been “raised up” to God received the idea of מתן, a gift given by Him to the priests as differentiated from the אימורים which have also been raised up to Him but in order to be given over to the fire of the Altar. These, זה, are the תרומות of all the תנופות, namely, the four לחם of the חזה ושוק ,לחמי תודה and זרוע בשלה of the איל נזיר. (Numb. 6,19 & 20). Although with all of them תנופה is done equally as תרומה they are nevertheless understood here under the name of תרומה because that is the usual expression used for the priest’s share. These מתנות כהונה from the meal-offerings may be eaten by the priests in the same manner as the owners may eat the meal-offerings themselves, viz., in the family circle anywhere within Jerusalem נאכלין בכל העיר לכהנים לנשיהם לבניהם ולעבדיהם (Zebachim 55a).

V. 12. כל חלב וגו׳. Now the קדשי גבול follow, the holy things that, unlike the קדשי קדשים which could only be eaten in the עזרה, or קדשים קלים which had to be eaten in the city surrounding the Sanctuary, Jerusalem, could be eaten anywhere in the whole of the land. First: תרומה (see Levit. 22,9 et seq.). חלב יצהר see Gen. 45,18 where חלב הארץ is used for the most valuable, the best. Here too, as has to be remarked on V.30, it is a duty to “lift out” the best as מן התורה .תרומה there is no שיעור, no fixed quantity for תרומה. The duty would be fulfilled by a single grain for the whole heap of grain. But it corresponds to the idea which this duty is meant to represent that this one grain should come from the very best of the heap (Terumoth 2,4). Hence the expression here: חלב יצהר. As is clear from V.27, כדגן מן הגרן וכמלאה מן היקב the real duty of תרומה only comes into force at גמר מלאכה at the final work for storing the produce. It is therefore not called גפן and זית but יצהר and תירוש, and דגן is the name which is applied only to grain when it is already stacked up in heaps (Pessachim 35b). The word דגן seems to be related phonetically with תכן which means a quantitative summing up, and equally so with תקן the general expression for getting things ready. If the produce of the olive trees and the vines are to be used for consumption as olives and grapes they are nevertheless liable to the duty of תרומה when they brought home as fruit (Baba Mezia 88b). Now it does not say here כל חלב יצהר תירוש ודגן but כל חלב יצהר וכל חלב תירוש from which the Halacha is taught in Bechoroth 53b, that אין תורמין ממין על שאינו מינו ואם תרם אין תרומתו תרומה אמרה תורה תן חלב לזה וחלב לזה, that one can not take תרומה collectively from different kinds of produce but must give it separately from each kind. Each kind of produce is to be considered as a separate grant from God which demands the expression of devotion to God’s Torah by itself, the realisation of which is indeed the purpose which is aimed at by every grant which God gives. ואם תרם ממין על שאינו מינו אין תרומתו תרומה according to רבא in accordance with the general canon: כל מילתא דאמר רחמנא לא תעביד אי עביד לא מהני, that every action performed against the law automatically remains without effect. According to the opposing opinion of אביי, (who does not agree with the canon quoted, I.L.) it is because ראשיתם implies ראשית לזה וראשית לזה (Temura 5a); see Levit. on XXII,23, (p.634 in my translation I.L,).

ראשיתם, similarly in Deut. 18,4, ראשית דגנך וגו׳, it is the first charge on the produce at the end of the work of the harvest (Terumoth 3,7). At the same time the word ראשית implies that מן התורה there is no minimum quantity but there is a maximum. The Torah demands nothing more than ראשית, a “first” of the heap of grain, whatever the quantity might be, hence חטה אחת פוטרת את הכרי “one single grain discharges the duty on the whole heap”. But on the other hand it is to be a ראשית of the whole, בעינן ראשית ששיריה נכרין, an appreciable amount must be left, so that if anybody were to declare his whole heap of grain to be תרומה it would mean nothing and the stack would not be תרומה (Chulin, 137b, & 136b). The same law applies also to חלה (see Ch. 25,20).

V. 13. בכורי כל. (See Ex. 23,19, and Deut. 26,2). כל אשר בארצם. In contrast to תרומה the ביכורים duty becomes due as soon as the produce becomes ripe, במחובר before it is cut. (Sifri). Hence indeed the term מלאתך in Ex. 22,28. The difference in the expressions used for תרומה and אשר יתנו לה׳ — בכורים at the one and אשר יביאו לה׳ at the other — is also significant. The produce which is liable to the duty of giving תרומה is already completely in Man’s possession, belongs entirely to him. From that which he has taken to himself, before he enjoys it he gives the first part to God. The produce which is liable to the duty of giving בכורים is still standing in the field attached to the ground, but instead of bringing it home to himself he brings the first part home to the Sanctuary to acknowledge that what ripens in Jewish fields is, in the first place תבואת הקדש (see Ex. 23,19). — בכורים .כל טהור בביתך יאכלנו have quite the same character as תרומה, and both, as well as חלה are permitted to be eaten by the whole household of a כהן. This consists of wife, the daughter of a nonpriest who is betrothed (מאורסת) to a priest, sons, daughters and non-Jewish slaves, male or female, who as קנין כספו, bought with his money, personally belong to him. Equally, so, also the חזה ושוק of קדשים קלים (V.11), with the one exception, that the daughter of a priest who had married a non-priest, and then after becoming a childless widow or divorcee, returns to her father’s home may eat תרומה but not חזה ושוק (see Levit. 22,10 & 14).
V. 14. כל חרם וגו׳. (See Levit. 27,21 & 28).

V. 15. כל פטר רחם וגו׳. (See Ex. 13,2 & 12-15. As clearly פטר רחם לכל בשר includes all the three categories אדם ובהמה טהורה וטמאה as is evident from the detailed explanation באדם ובבהמה the אשר יקריבו לה׳ cannot mean “which are dedicated as an offering to God,” but can only mean which are dedicated in general to God. The בכורות of all three categories are placed in a near relationship to God. It is exactly the same concept as is expressed in והעברת כל פטר רחם לה׳ (ibid.). — אך תפדה וגו׳, here בכור אדם, as far as the duty of redemption goes, is placed in the same category as בכור בהמה טמאה so that כל שישנו בבכור אדם ישנו בבכור בהמה טמאה וכל שאינו בבכור אדם אינו בבכור בהמה טמאה and consequently כהנים ולוים פטורים, priests and Levites are free from having to redeem their own firstborn as well as פטר חמור (Bechoroth 4a, and see on Ch. 3,41 et seq.). — אך פדה תפדה וגו׳ ואת הבהמה הטמאה תפדה, the redemption of human first born sons is an absolute duty, that of פטר המור only an optional one, עריפה can be done in its stead, although indeed only secondarily, as an alternative. (See Ex. 13,15), this perhaps explains the change in the wording. In Kidushim 29a it is further taught from the stressed importance given to the redemption of firstborn sons by פדה תפדה (the infinitive added to the indicative I.L.) that this duty must be fulfilled in any case, and if the father has not done it, the son himself must do it as soon as he reaches independent responsible age. But inasmuch as here the duty of redeeming himself is expressed in one thought together with the duty of redeeming a son, the Halacha takes it that the sentence teaches that the duty of redeeming sons only lies on the one who could have had the duty of redeeming himself, i.e. the father but is not encumbent on the mother: כל שמצווה לפדות את עצמו מצווה לפדות את אחרים וכל שאינו מצווה לפדות את עצמו אינו מצווה לפדות את אחרים.

In a striking manner, here and in the following verse, the action of the redemption is referred to the priest. תפדה is addressed to Aaron, the representative of the priesthood, although there is no doubt that the redemption of the firstborn is something that the father, not the priest, does, and is to be accomplished only by him. Indeed it says so expressly in Ex. 13,13 & 15, וכל בכור בני אפדה ,וכל בכר אדם בבניך תפדה. But in Bechoroth 51a, the rule is laid down that — as is the case in no other המפריש פדיון בנו ואבד חייב באחריותו — פדיון הקדש, if the father has redeemed his son but the redemption money has become lost before it had been handed over to a priest, the redemption is considered not to have taken place. So that the redemption is perfected only at the moment the priest takes over the money, so that this taking over the money on the part of the priest is an essential co-operative act of redemption procedure. The priest accordingly is to be considered as co-operating in the פדיון-act, and this could explain the personal תפדה referring to the priest. The sense of the verse would be:- יהיה לך, the firstborn really belongs to the Sanctuary represented by the priest, and should really have a priestly, or at least a Levite, position relative to the Sanctuary (See Ch. 3,12) אך, by taking over the redemption money, the priest, in the name of the Sanctuary frees him from this position in or at the Sanctuary, in order that he may influence the realisation in actual concrete family life of what he would have had to represent symbolically by service at the Sanctuary. (Cf. שו״ת ריב״ש 131).

But this peculiarity does not apply to פדיון בהמה טמאה. Like every other הקדש, and e.g. also at מעשר שני the redemption is accomplished even before the means of redemption have come into the possession of the priest, or respectively been brought to Jerusalem (Bechoroth 12b), so that regarding this the pronoun in the second person תפדה remains difficult. In Sifri, on the introduction to this law in V.8 it says that it was not addressed directly to Aaron but to Moses for Aaron. It seems to us that it is quite possible that the word תפדה led to this assumption. If the law was said to Moses, then this תפדה refers to the nation, and only פדה תפדה of the firstborn son which by אך is directly attached to the preceding יהיה לך would undoubtedly refer to Aaron.

V. 16. ופדויו וגו׳ refers to the redemption of בכור אדם, the redemption of which is specially stressed in the preceding verse, and to which פדיון בכור בהמה טמאה is only added secondarily and has already been discussed in detail in Ex. 13,13. The פדיון פטר חמור may be done immediately. (Bechoroth 12b). מבן חדש תפדה, after the thirtieth day like the בכורי מדבר (above Ch. III) where it says explicitly מבן חדש ומעלה. The duty of redemption only applies when the child has reached the thirty-first day; should it die on the thirtieth day, that day is reckoned as belonging to the previous days (Bechoroth 59a). Once it has passed the thirtieth day its ability to live is considered established. כל ששהה שלשים יום באדם אינו נפל (Sabbath 135b). But even if its ability to live is otherwise established, קים לן שכלו חדשיו, nevertheless the redemption is not to be made earlier (Bechoroth 49a תוספות). The פדיון is indeed not meant to be considered as some protecting act against physical collapse but to remain kept in the pure moral spiritual sphere of its meaning. — בערכך חמשת שקלים וגו׳. This is the ערך of a בן חדש (see Levit. 27,6). — שקלים (see Ex. 30,16, at the end of commentary thereon, (pp.582 in my translation, I.L.) and also Bechoroth 49b et seq.). A shekel, according to the נ״ש XII,31 is 1 1/95 loths of fine silver, so that the five shekels of our verse would be 5 1/3 loths of fine silver. But the form of the sentence ופדויו וגו׳ תפדה וגו׳ כסף is that of כלל ובלל ופרט which reckons the same as כלל ופרט וכלל hence אי אתה דן אלא כעין הפרט ,מה הפרט מפורש דבר המיטלטל וגופו ממון so also כל דבר המיטלטל וגופו ממון. Accordingly כסף is to be taken as an example for anything which can be moved and has intrinsic value and would exclude landed property and עבדים (which legally are placed in the same category) and also documents and paper money which have no intrinsic value, and פדיון הבן can be made with anything that is mobile and has the instrinsic value of five shekels. (Bechoroth 51a).

V. 17. עד שיהא הוא :בכור עז ,בכור כשב ,בכור שור .אך בכור שור וגו׳ שור ובכורו שור, it only receives the character of בכור if in its appearance it does not deny the characteristic character of the mother animal, but רחל שילדה מין עז ועז שילדה מין רחל פטורה מן הבכורה ואם יש בו מקצת סימנין חייב (Bechoroth 16b). In Ex. 13,2 we have shown that the consecration of the firstborn is to be taken as a consecration of the womb and by it of all further births (refer to it there). We think we can take the law given here as a result of that idea, as it makes the representation of the mother animal by the firstborn as a condition for its consecration.

לא תפדה וגו׳: their קדושה cannot be redeemed in any way. Even as בעל מום they cannot be redeemed as other פסולי מוקדשים can, as is laid down in Levit. 27,11 & 12, because they are not מוקדשים, did not receive their קדושה by human free will, but קדש הם, they are קדש automatically by birth, and that קדושה remains in all circumstances (Temura 6b — see Levit. 27,26). They do not transfer it completely even by תמורה, and תמורת בכור, like תמורת מעשר is not brought as an offering on the altar. (Zebachim 37b and see on Levit. 27,33). In בכור בהמה טהורה the לי הוא of קדש לי כל בכור וגו׳ (Ex. 13,2) is most purely incorporated which is why there in verses 12 and 15 it is placed first before the other two. (look up).

את דמם תזרוק וגו׳. As the Torah says סביב (which tells us that the blood has to be thrown on all sides of the altar, two throwings on diagonally opposite corners I.L.) at the עולה (Levit. 1,5) and repeats it for the חטאת (ibid. VIII,15, it also has to be placed on all sides I.L.) and again for the אשם (ibid. VII,2), the סביב cannot be taken as being of an exemplary nature for שני כתובין and certainly שלשה כתובין הבאין כאחד אין מלמדין, so that as it does not say סביב here, only one מתנה is to be understood with the proviso that it is כנגד היסוד (i.e. not on the south-east corner of the altar I.L.) Bechoroth 57a. In this, בכור is similar to פסח and מעשר בהמה which also have מתנה אחת כנגד היסוד (see Deut. 12,27). All three meet in having the common meaning of taking to heart and consecrating the blessings of the home as coming from God and being hallowed to God. Hence with them the אכילת בעלים the eating of the offering in the family circle stands in the foreground. From the פסח and the מעשר only the blood and the kidneys and the fat come on the altar-fire — the expression of dedicating the life and will and the desires and aims of life to God — but the whole of the remainder of the offering, after such renunciation of all selfish aims of life, comes to be enjoyed by the bringer with his family in the neighbourhood of the Sanctuary, thereby drawing such enjoyment itself into the sphere of God-serving procedures and realisation of the task of the מקדש. Quite similarly בכור בהמה טהורה which, on being handed over to the priest, becomes his property, ממון כהן, to which he stands thenceforth as בעלים. In it he is to understand the meaning and importance of his own existence and that of his family from his position towards the nation and towards the Sanctuary. As “כהן״ he is to give his own life and that of his family, with their desires and worldly aims, up to the Altar of God, and from that, and with that, to raise the enjoyments of his home (ובשרם וגו׳ of the following verse) into the service of the Sanctuary of God.

That is why, as in בכור מעשר ופסח it is less one’s actions, but more the dedication of one’s means of existence that is to the fore, they have only מתנה אחת and not the שתי מתנות שהן ארבע which are meant to express the complete striving up to all the spiritual, intellectual and material aims of life indicated by God. At בכור, one זריקה כנגד היסוד suffices to express in general the striving upwards to God and His purposes as being the necessary preliminary condition for sanctifying his own enjoyments of life; or at מעשר and פסח only by שפיכה in the יסוד, by placing his life on the base of the altar and pouring out the blood thereon, representing making the roots of his whole existence lie in the base of the Sanctuary of God. Yea, according to the text of רמב״ם הל׳ מ״ק V.17, even at בכור there was only שפיכה, which, being in contradiction to the words of our verse here seems hardly to be probable (see לחם משנה thereon). ר׳ יוסי הגלילי on the other hand deduces from our text that זריקה applied also to פסח and מעשר (Pessachim 64a).

V. 18. ובשרם יהיה לך, both תם after זריקת הדם and הקטרת החלב and בעל מום which is unfit for an offering but still has to be given to the priest as his property and for him to eat, only remain prohibited for him to use for its fleece or for work (see Deut. 15,19 et seq.; Zebachim 37a) — כחזה התנופה וכשוק הימין לך יהיה, like חזה ושוק of שלמים it may be eaten for two days and the intervening night (See Levit. 7,16) and, as above V.11, by all the members of a priest’s household. (Bechoroth 32a).

V. 19. כל תרומת וגו׳ finally summarises it all again: everything which is “raised and hallowed”, i.e. which is directed to the Sanctuary of the Torah as being dedicated to God, by which it participates in the holy character of the Sanctuary, has God given to the priests and their family as an everlasting due for their being appointed as guardians and representatives of the people’s relationship to God and His Sanctuary. This appointment, which is to be kept constantly in the minds of the people in the various phases of their national and domestic lives by the מתנות כהונה is in itself of the nature of a ברית, something given by God as absolute, unconditional and irrevocable. ברית and מלח, something “given” and “immutable”, it itself illustrates the Torah and its Sanctuary, but at the same time, as it says in the Sifri, like salt it is to penetrate into all the relationships and conditions of national and family life, giving them the lasting taste of the spirit of the Torah and keep it unspoilt and fresh and healthy for God and His Sanctuary — כרת הכתוב עם אהרן בדבר הבריא ולא עוד אלא שמבריא את אחרים (Sifri, see on Levit. 2,13). The Jewish priest has to look on himself as the “eternal salt” in the people, under God’s supervision and protection.

The מתנות כהונה expressed here first בכלל, in general terms in V.8. then בפרט, in detail in V.9-18, and then again in general terms, בכלל in our Verse 19, according in the primary form of the whole of the rest of the lawgiving, fall into three groups:- (a) those that may only be eaten within the Sanctuary, in the עזרה, V.9-10; (b) those that may only be eaten within Jerusalem, V.11, to which ביכורים in V.13 also belong, but as they otherwise come into the class of תרומה are mentioned in connection with it, and further בכור בהמה טהורה in V.17-18, which are nevertheless mentioned in connection with the two other בכורות; (c) those that may be eaten and used anywhere within the Jewish domain in V. 12-16. In the same grouping the תוספתא reckons up twenty-four עשר במקדש, וארבע :מתנות כהונה בירושלים ועשר בגבולין. עשר במקדש: חטאת, וחטאת העוף, אשם ודאי, ואשם תלוי, וזבחי שלמי ציבור, ולוג שמן של מצורע, ושתי הלחם, ולחם הפנים, ושירי מנחות, ומנחת העומר. וארבע בירושלים: הבכורה, והבכורים, ומורם מן התודה ומאיל נזיר, (ובכללם חזה ושוק של שאר שלמים) ועורות קדשים. ועשר בגבולין: תרומה ותרומת מעשר וחלה וראשית הגז ומתנות (הזרוע והלחיים והקבה, דברים י״ח ג, ד) ופדיון הבן ופדיון פטר חמור ושדה אחוזה (ויקרא כייז כייא) ושדה חרמים וגזל הגר. In the second group, the four in Jerusalem, the skins of the offerings are included, although their use is not restricted to Jerusalem, because, as the רשב״א explains, their being given to the priests depends on the flesh being eaten by priests who could participate in the division of the flesh and such priests were, of course, in Jerusalem. אין נתנים אלא לכהנים הראוים לחלוק בבשר והכהנים האוכלים בבשר עומדים בירושלים משום הכי קרי להו מתנות ירושלים.

The תוספתא says as introduction עשרים וארבע מתנות כהונה הן וכולן ניתנו לאהרן ולבניו בכלל ובפרט וברית מלח כל המקיימן כאלו קיים בכלל ופרט וברית מלח וכל העובר עליהן כאלו עובר על בכלל ופרט וברית מלח, “Four and twenty מתנות כהונה are given to Aaron and his sons in the כלל ופרט (in general and in detail I.L.) primary form of the whole Torah and as a ברית מלה as a covenant of absoluteness and “immutability”. He who carries this command out, he achieves thereby the fulfilling of everything “in general and in detail” and as something given him as an absolute everlasting covenant, and one who refuses it, goes away from it is as if he had already set himself apart from everything, given as an absolute eternal bond בכלל ופרט, in principle and in detail.

And in truth it only requires a superficial glance over these groups of the מתנות כהונה to appreciate how through them the activities of the priests come into contact with all the manifold phases of the life of the people. And equally so how with each one of these “gifts”, the admonition comes to the priest and his household of the mission to lead a life that is a model in every respect, so that by its example his contemporaries should rise to the moral heights of the Torah; how he is to consecrate himself by giving up his whole life to making that Torah realised בכלל ובפרט as a ברית מלח עולם in all circumstances, whatever the condition of the times might be.

V. 20. ויאמר ה׳ וגו׳. This is added explanatorily almost as if it was a self-understood result of all the preceding. Hence ויאמר, and not as a fresh command: נחלה .וידבר is the possession which flows down from ancestors to descendants and from them to their descendants, and נהלה is such a possession which the children come to inherit from their parents. Such a נחלה in the first instance is a land which has been promised already to the forefathers and on the strength of that promise is considered as their property. חלק is the participation of the individual in the progressive national prosperity brought about primarily by the cultivation of the land and other favourable junctures of affairs. The priestly tribe is denied direct participation in both of these. Neither taking possession and leaving it as a legacy nor increasing the national prosperity by agricultural work on the land and its produce is their mission: אני חלקך ונחלתך וגו׳, but rather the relations to God of all these national foundations of the lives of the people is to be their office and task in the nation; the progressive blossoming of these relations in understanding and realisation is to be their חלק, their participation in the achievements of the nation in all times; and looking after and handing down these spiritual achievements of the parents to the children is to be their נחלה, their spiritual heritage, and both at the same time to be the basis of their material living and prosperity. In the second half of the verse חלק comes significantly first because in that second sentence the spiritual harvest of the work of every contemporary generation of priests is proclaimed: אני חלקך.

In the Sifri, חלק is taken to refer to non-participation in the spoils of war. We believe that this is only to be taken as an example of all the general achievements of the nation apart from taking possession of the land.

V. 21. את כל מעשר .ולבני לוי וגו׳, but still only the tithe from the produce of the soil, and indeed, as already remarked on V.8, in the most generally accepted opinion, only from grain, wine and oil, as also verses 27 and 30 assume. The Levite, although he gets no direct share in the land, does get a fixed considerable share of the most important produce of the land as נחלה. A distinct difference is made between this מעשר of the Levites and the preceding מתנות of the priests. The מעשר is taken to be חלף עבדתם, as שכר (V.30) as a wage for their service at the Sanctuary. The nation owes it to them for taking over and doing the service which otherwise it would have to do. But the מתנות of the priests are no wages for the עבודת כהנים. As God appointed representatives and ministers in His Sanctuary of the Torah, God has transferred to them holy things which had been dedicated to Him and to His Sanctuary. Their eating the מתנות שבמקדש was even itself quite an essential part of the הכהנים אוכלים ובעלים מתכפרים :עבודה. Most of the מתנות כהונה have the character of קדש, of most of them can it be said: .כהנים משולחן גבוה קא זכו תרומה, the most general gift to the priest can so little be considered a wage, has so much through and through the nature of a symbol that, as we have so frequently remarked, חטה אחת פוטרת את הכרי, a single grain suffices for the whole stack. So that אני חלקך ונחלתך and ולבני לוי נתתי כל מעשר בישראל לנחלה וגו׳ are in clear contrast to each other. Thus also in Sifri: כל מצות כהונה קנאו השם ונתנו לכהונה וזו חלף עבודתם. Hence the כהנים are to be considered not so much as שלוחי דידן (our representatives I.L.) as שלוחי דרחמנא (God’s representatives I.L.) Kiddushin 23b, and our way of taking it (חורב Ch. 118) that the service in the Sanctuary was not given over to the priests through the nation’s disgracing itself at the golden calf, may find a confirmation by the difference expressed here between their position and that of the Levites.

V. 22. ולא יקרבו וגו׳, by their undertaking to do the service of the Sanctuary in place of the rest of the nation, the Levites protect the children of Israel against committing the error of doing such עבודות which are prohibited to the זר on pain of death (בידי שמים, V.7).

V. 23. ועבד הלוי וגו׳. Although the Levite gets a wage for his service, he can not evade the service by renouncing the wage. He still has to render the service even if he gets no מעשר. And this is quite possible as no Levite has any direct claim to any tithe, the disposal of which is entirely in the hands of the one who has to give it, טובת הנאה לבעלים (he can give it to any Levite he chooses, Ch. V.10). The Levite must do his service even in years like שמטה and יובל where all produce is הפקר (ownerless) and there is altogether no מעשר at all to be given. His duty to render service is an unconditional one although his claim to מעשר is by no means so. — והם ישאו עונם, and added to it, their service is one full of serious responsibility (V.3). ובתוך בני ישראל לא ינחלו נחלה: and although the מעשר is only given to them as compensation for the service they have to render the community, nevertheless they have to renounce any right of participation in the heritage of a part of the land. So that the position of the Levites was by no means a materially preferential one, which is why the tribe of Levi is repeatedly recommended to the kind benevolence of the nation (Deut. 12,12 and XVIII,19), yea, in just this respect he seems to be classed together with גר יתום ואלמנה (the stranger, orphan and widow, ibid. XXVI,11-13).

V. 24. כי את מעשר וגו׳. The מעשר which everybody has to separate before he is allowed to have any use of his own produce, for the upkeep of the tribe dedicated to the service of the Sanctuary of the Torah, caring for keeping the spirit of the Torah alive before looking after his own material existence, is also designated here as תרומה לה׳, the more so as in it is contained the תרומת מעשר which the Levite again has to separate as real תרומה for the priest, קראו המקום תרומה עד שיוציא ממנו תרומת מעשר (Sifri). This indirect referring the תרומת מעשר back to the first owner, the ישראל has, as we shall see at once, certain halachic results. In Menachot 31a the two opinions are discussed, whether יש קנין לנכרי בא״י להפקיע מיד מעשר or אין קנין i.e. whether by transferring a field to a non-Jew in the land of Israel, tithe has to be taken from the produce or not. The most generally accepted opinion, including the רמב״ם is that אין קנין וכו׳, that the produce of the land of Israel remains liable to tithes even if the field is in the possession of a non-Jew; and if Menachot 67a deduces from מעשר דגנך, (the tithe of thy grain, Deut. 12,17) that דגן נכרי the grain of a non-Jew is excluded from the duty of giving tithes, that would only apply if the produce remained in the possession of the non-Jew right up to the final work on the corn, then מירוח נכרי פוטר, but if it passed into Jewish possession before the final process, and was winnowed ברשות ישראל, because אין קניו וכו׳ it is טבל, i.e. תרומה ומעשר has to be taken, but the ישראל keeps the מעשר for himself, and need only give the תרומת מעשר, which is אסור לזרים, to the priest if this latter pays for it. מעשרן והן שלו is a special condition which does not apply to תרומה גדולה which does apply to grain which is winnowed ברשות ישראל and in any case has to be separated and given to the priest. Here we follow the opinion of תוספות) ר״ת ibid.) with which רמב״ם agrees (see further on V.27).

There is another decision in connection with this development which we shall have to consider in detail when we come to the real מעשר chapter, Deut. 14,22 et seq. That is that — according to ר״ת and רמב״ם — the whole duty of מעשר only applies if the final process of the grain מירוח, winnowing, is done for one’s own home consumption, but if it is for the market and sold to others, neither the buyer nor the seller need give tithes, לוקח פטור (see Baba Mezia 88a תוספות there and Bechoroth 11b. ריב״ם and ראב״ד have a different opinion, see Menachoth 31a, and כ״מ on הלי מעשר ,רמב״ם III,1). We shall בע״ה discuss all these decisions in connection with others in Deut. We only mention them here because they may help to elucidate a problem which has been raised regarding the proportion of the tithe to the relatively small number of the Levites in the nation. It has been suggested that a tenth of the produce of the whole nation would make the tribe of Levi unduly richer than the rest of the nation. For according to the census reported in Ch. 3,39, the number of the Levites was twenty thousand against six hundred thousand of the rest of Israel, i.e. only 1/30th. Added to this they were counted from one month old whereas the rest were only those over twenty years old! But — apart from the fact that one only has to compare the inequality in the numbers of the other tribes to see that there is no means of reckoning the probabilities of the size of any tribe or family in the next decades or centuries, — one must bear in mind that, as we remarked above, according to the generally accepted opinion, only grain, wine and oil were subjected to being tithed, accordingly only a part of the national produce, and even from these, only that which was finally prepared for the family consumption, but not what was marketed or bought was tithed. In no case could the tithe have given the tribe of Levi more than a bare sufficiency, but rather, as already mentioned, the Torah sees cause repeatedly to recommend the subsistence of the Levites to the benevolence of the nation.

בנחלתכם, in the nature of a נחלה, as being your נחלה, similar to above בקדש הקדשים in V.10. The Gemora in Rosh Hashana 12b refers the fact that this מעשר ראשון was continuous without interruption year after year in the six tithe-years to the term מעשר ראשון אין לו הפסק :נחלה, whereas מעשר שני was replaced by מעשר עני in every third year (see Deut. 14,22).

והרמתם ממנו תרומת ה׳ מעשר מן המעשר. In V.29 it says: מכל מתנותיכם תרימו את כל תרומת ה׳ and from that Beitza 13b teaches that if the Levite receives his tithe from grain from which תרומה ought to have been taken but has not been taken (Ex. 22,28), the duty devolves on him to take את כל תרומת ה׳, to give the priest not only תרומת מעשר but also תרומה גדולה from his tithe. This case is designated as הקדימו בכרי, the Levite was given (illegally I.L.) first, at a stage where תרומה was due to have been given. But if הקדימו בשבלין he had received his tithe before the final process of grain-preparation, i.e. at a stage when תרומה was not yet due to be separated, then, in accordance with the text of our V.26 he has only to give the priest תרומת מעשר but not תרומת מעשר מן המעשר אמרתי לך ולא :תרומה גדולה תרומה גדולה ותרומת מעשר מן המעשר (see תוספות שבת 117b, ד״ה אידגן).

V. 27. ונחשב לכם וגו׳: cf. נכריות נחשבנו לו (Gen. 31,15), your תרומת מעשר is considered as coming from you with the same idea as תרומה גדולה is taken up from the barns and wine-presses. (Rashi, Gittin 31a and everywhere else where the verse is quoted). דגן מן הגרן is תרומה גדולה and תרומת מעשר is placed on the same level as it. Now as it does not say והיתה לכם תרומתכם but ונחשב, which implies that מחשבה, thought is the essential purpose of both תרומות, on which the Halacha is based that all תרומות can be ניטלת במחשבה, receive their character simply by thought. Without a word and without a touch, simply by setting a quantity aside in your mind to be תרומה or תרומת מעשר, it is as good as if you had actually separated it out and the rest of the mass is no longer נותן :טבל עיניו בצד זה ואוכל בצד אחר. In this respect תרומה and תרומת מעשר differ essentially from מעשר and are similar only to קדשים which become hallowed as vowed to God by the mere thought of dedicating them to that purpose (Menachoth 54b and 55a, רש״י ותוספות there, Shebuoth 26a תוספות ד״ה משם).

Further, we have already on V.24 deduced from כי את מעשר בני ישראל אשר ירימו לה׳ תרומה that what the Levite has to give the priest, the תרומת מעשר, refers indirectly back to the duty of the ישראל to give tithe from his produce. And in fact as soon as the owner separates out the tithe, it, containing תרומת מעשר, becomes at once טבל, and from this latter being put on par with תרומה גדולה it is taught that יש לו רשות לבעל הבית לתרום תרומת מעשר, that it is open to the ישראל to give תרומת מעשר at once just as he gives תרומה גדולה to the priest (see on next verse).

But although תרומת מעשר is completely the same as תרומה גדולה regarding אסורה לזרים וחייבים עליה מיתה וחומש it differs from it in some respects. תרומה גדולה ניטלת באומד; while גדולה has no fixed amount מן התורה, and may be separated just approximately, and further אין תורמין אלא מן המוקף, the whole mass and the part you separate from it as תרומה must lie together adjacent to each other, תרומת מעשר must be an exact tenth but may be separated שלא מן המוקף, from any heap not necessarily adjacent. (Beiza 13b; Terumoth 4,6; Bekurim 2,5 — see Gittin 30b תוספות ד״ה וכי).

From the term תרומתכם addressed to the Levite, by which the תרומה which he is forbidden to eat is still called “his”, it is taught in Pessachim 23a that תרומה is מותר בהנאה for a זר. (may be made use of by a non-priest. I.L.).

V. 28. כן תרימו גם אתם. In Kiddushin 41b, the idea of the ability to have representatives for oneself, שליחות is developed, that שלוחו של אדם כמותו. This is a concept that has been established as a general rule by Ex. 12,4 & 6 (refer to p.338 in English translation I.L.) and Deut. 24,1 & 2 (refer towards end of commentary 1-4 I.L.). Here it is more precisely defined: מה אתם בני ברית אף שלוחכם בני ברית, that a person can only really be represented as himself by one who is of the same religion, hence אין שליחות לנכרי, there can be no legal mutual representation between ישראל and נכרי (see ש״ך ח״מ רמ״ג ס״ק ה׳). The גם is taken as an extension of the concept אתם. The תרומה can be raised also by whatever is “you”, i.e. by a person who fully represents you and your intentions for this act. When we consider that, according to what we have said on V.24 and V.27, the תרומת מעשר is referred back to the ישראל, yea he is qualified himself to raise it for the priest, the Levite, at bottom should really consider himself only as a שליח, a representative. — It is the nation which, through the Levite, gives the מעשר מן המעשר to the priest — so that the teaching of שליחות which our sages have taught from here would have deep significance. גם אתם says: just as the ישראל makes you his שליח to the priest, so can you, too, in a similar manner appoint someone else to do this act on your behalf.

לאהרן הכהן. As the priests who are entitled to receive תרומה are designated here as אהרן הכהן, according to Sanhedrin 90b only such priests who by their spiritual and moral character are not dissimilar to Aaron are designated as being worthy of מכאן אמרו שאין נותנין תרומה לכהן .תרומה עם הארץ, לאהרן כאהרן מה אהרן חבר אף בניו חברים. So it also says in Chron. II. 31,4; ויאמר לעם ליושבי ירושלים לתת מנת לכהנים ולוים למען יחזקו בתורת ה׳, כל המחזיק בתורת ה׳ יש לו מנת ושאינו מחזיק בתורת ה׳ אין לו מנת i.e. only the priest who theoretically and practically holds fast to the Torah has a claim to the מתנות כהונה.
V. 29. מכל מתנותיכם וגו׳ (see on V.25) מכל חלבו: it is a duty to give the תרומה from the best of the grain, אין תורמין מן הרעה על היפה (Temura 5a).

את מקדשו ממנו, from this expression our Rabbis have fixed the law that (תרומה עולה באחד ומאה (מדרבנן, that a mixture of תרומה in a similar kind of מין במינו ,חולין becomes בטל, one in a hundred. For תרומת מעשר is one out of a hundred and this one out of a hundred here is called מקדשו, that by which the other ninety-nine when it was mixed with it had the character of קדש and were אסורים לזרים. But if there were one hundred against it the one תרומה would be absorbed. A mixture of תרומה in which it is not absorbed is called דמוע (see on Levit. 7,19) and its effect מדמע (Orla 2,1).

V. 30. ונחשב ללוים, it belongs to the Levites, and מעשר ראשון has no further קדושה, just like תבואת גרן after תרומה ומעשר has been separated off (see on Levit. 22,15) (Sifri). תבואת גרן וגו׳ is that which remains to the גרן and יקב differentiated from דגן מן הגרן of V.27, which designates the תרומה taken therefrom. Hence:

V. 31. אף בקבר :ואכלתם אותו בכל מקום וגו׳ (Sifri), whereas תרומה may only be eaten בטהרה: also דלא בעי חומה that, unlike מעשר שני it need not be eaten in Jerusalem (Yebamoth 86b) — אתם וביתכם, the tithe is given to your wives as much as to you, and they are entitled to separate the תרומת מעשר from it, as you are, or to authorise it to be taken, לימד על נשואה בת ישראל שנותנת רשות לתרום (Yebamoth 86a).

V. 32. ולא תשאו וגו׳ בהרימכם את חלבו ממנו. It has already been repeated in verses 24 and 30 that one is bound לתרום מן היפה, which is חלבו. Here one is warned that תורם הרעה על היפה, separating it out of the bad part (i.e. not the best) is designated as נשיאת עון, as lading oneself with sin. From this in Temura 5a is deduced that if one were to do so, his action would nevertheless be valid, for אם אין קדש נשיאת חטא למה, if what he had done was invalid and the whole heap remained טבל as before so that he would have to take תרומה מן היפה before he could eat any of it so that his transgression would have been rectified.

ואת קדשי בני ישראל לא תחללו וגו׳. As the distribution of the תרומות and the מעשרות was entirely dependent on the goodwill of those that were in duty bound to give them, and no priests and no Levite had any direct claim on any of it, the temptation was very near for them to try and curry favour with people who had to dispense priest-gifts and tithes, and thereby degrade the holiness of their office and the holiness of the gifts attached to it. The Gemora in Bechoroth 26b takes our sentence here to warn them against that: ת״ר הכהנים והלוים והעניים המסייעים בבית הרועים ובבית הגרנות ובבית המטבחיים אין נותנין להם תרומה ומעשר בשכרן, אם עושין כן חיללו ועליהם הכתוב אומר (מלאכי ב׳) שחתם ברית הלוי ואומר ואת קדשי בני ישראל לא תחללו ולא תמותו.
Regarding the institution of תרומות ומעשרות see on Levit. 22,9, and summarising, on Deut. 14,22 et seq.

V. 1. (See on Levit. 11,1 & XIII,1). This mode of address to Moses and Aaron shows the high importance of its contents for the theoretical understanding of the Law, and of the practical bringing the individuals of the people to it.
