V. 2. זאת חקת התורה. This expression only occurs once again, in Ch. 31,2, as the introduction to the הכשר וטבילת כלי מדין. Those institutions and what follows here, the institution of the פרה אדומה, “the red cow”, have this in common, that their purpose is the re-instatement of food-vessels for טהרת גויות as that of פרה אדומה is the re-instatement of persons for טהרת קדושות. Both are highly important fundamental laws of the whole Torah, and the laws concerning them have to be carried out in a manner which is absolutely essential. Without means of restoring the כשרות of our vessels and the טהרה of our persons from the unavoidable טומאת מת the Torah would not be achievable. So both are חוקות התורה: arrangements which are necessary conditions on which the Torah rests. And if then, as we shall see, and which indeed the first glance establishes, פרה אדומה is the most outspoken proclamation of טהרה — that fundamental thought of personal moral freedom of will, which in fact is conditional for the keeping of the whole Torah — all the more can one understand the dictatorial introductory words: זאת חקת התורה “this is a fundamental law of the Torah”! In Menachoth XlXa, it teaches further from the term חוקה that every single detail of the prescriptions that follow here for the institution of the פרה אדומה is essential for the validity of the whole: מתרומת הלשכה :ויקחו אליך — .כל מקום שנאמר חוקה אינו אלא לעכב, out of the yearly national fund for offerings made by the annual contributions of the מחצית השקל (see Ex. 30,16, p.581 in English translation; Shekalim IV). — בת שלש :פרה, from the beginning of the third year and onward (Para 1,1), after it had reached the age of ability to bear, פחותה מבת ג׳ שנים מי קא ילדה (Avoda Zara 24b). — פרה אדומה תמימה, the demand for being without a מום is immediately added by אשר אין בה מום so that תמימה must be taken to qualify the demand for its being completely red תמימה באדמימות (Sifri). Even two black or white hairs would render it unfit for its intended purpose (Para. 2,4). אשר אין בה מום, although the פרה אדומה only has the character of קדשי בדק הבית and not of an offering קדשי מזבח, still all מומין or other failings such as רובע ונרבע ,מוקצה ,נעבד ,אתנן ומחיר and also יוצא דופן וטריפה which render animals unfit for offerings do so also for פרה אדומה for it is also called חטאת (V.9) and accordingly, although קדשי בדק הבית, has the character of חטאת (Avoda Zara 23b and Para 2,2 & 3). — אשר לא עלה עליה עול, nothing may have been placed on it which could come under the concept “yoke”, it does not say: אשר לא עלה עול עליה, in which case it would exempt עול and that only, but it says אשר לא עלה עליה עול, nothing has come on to the animal which could come under the conception of a yoke, so that not only עול but work of any kind makes it unfit to be used; and thereby Sota 46a, takes the law here to be similar to that of the עגלה ערופה (Deut. 21,3), אשר לא עבד בה אשר לא משכה בעול (refer to it there), but nevertheless here for פרה the law is given in detail as: עול פוסל בין בשעת עבודה בין שלא בשעת עבודה שאר עבודות אין פוסלות אלא בשעת עבודה i.e. putting an actual yoke, the sign of service, on the cow renders it unfit, even if it is put on not for the purpose of immediately using the animal for work, but engaging the animal’s power to work by other means than by putting an actual yoke on it would only render it unfit if it is done for the requirement of work to be done. Accordingly putting a yoke on the animal’s neck renders it unfit even if it is only put on without any intention of using the animal now, but putting any other object on, only if the animal is to be used for work at the time.

V. 3. ונתתם וגו׳ ,ונתתם אתה אל אלעזר הכהן, probably the aforementioned בני ישראל and אתה אל אלעזר הכהן .משה: In Yoma 42b, one opinion takes this to refer לדורות, that for all time it must be the כהן גדול while another takes the opposite view that it may be a כהן הדיוט who undertakes the procedure of the רמב״ם .פרה adopts the latter view (הל׳ פרה I,11). Nevertheless as a rule it was the כה״ג who performed the act (see Para. 3,8). The priest had to appear as such in the priestly garments and מחוסר בגדים renders the פסול פרה as it does at all offerings (Ex. 28,43). Indeed it had to be done in בגדי לבן like the עבודה of the High Priest on י״כ. (Para. 4,1; see מל״מ on הל׳ פרד I,11). Equally so the מעשה פרה requires קידוש ידים ורגלים (the ritual washing of hands and feet I.L.) כעין עבודה although it was done בחוץ, outside the Sanctuary and without כלי שרת (Zebachim 20b). Similarly to the service on י״כ, the priest who was entrusted with the service of the פרה had to prepare himself for it by seven days seclusion, שבעת ימים קודם שריפת הפרה היו מפרישין כהן השורף את הפרה מביתו ללשכה שעל פני הבירה צפונה מזרחה, a chamber in the north-east of the Temple building was allocated to him for this purpose, in the north-east to remind him of the double nature of the procedure he was to undertake. The פרה is חטאת (V.9) hence בצפון the side to which all קדשי קדשים were directed, but it was to take place outside the Sanctuary, yea, outside the city but had to be in view of the entrance of the Sanctuary which was on the east side, hence במזרח, the “door side”, which indicates the way out of the Sanctuary, and towards which, as the entrance to the Sanctuary, the הזיות, the sprinklings prescribed in V.4 had to be directed (Yoma 2a, see on Levit. 8,34).

חוץ לשלש מחנות :והוציא אותה אל מחוץ למחנה, not just outside the מחנה שכינה — the Temple itself, — and the מחנה לויה — the mount on which the Temple stood, the הר הבית — but also out of the מחנה ישראל — the character which the city of the Temple, Jerusalem, bore up to its walls (see on Ch. 5,2 & 3 — cf. Levit. 4,12). It was led to הר המשחה, Mt. Olives which lies to the east outside the city (Para. 3,6). והוציא אותה לבדה, it had to be taken out entirely by itself, no other animal was to be with it (Yoma 43a), and so also ולא אותה וחברתה ,ושחט אותה no second פרה אדומה was allowed to be slaughtered with it on the same occasion, even if an ordinary animal בהמת חולין were to be slaughtered next to it, its שחיטה would render the פרה unfit (Para. 3,7 and Chulin 32a).

ושחט אתה לפניו, the שחיטה also may not be done by a non-priest. שחיטת פרה בזר פסולה and the לפניו comes primarily to say that he must keep his whole mind concentrated on the פרה and the procedures to be done with it, שלא יסיח דעתו ממנה (Yoma 42a). This is the only שחיטה (according to רב) that may only be done by a priest. At all the קרבנות (with the one exception of the פר of the High Priest on י״כ according to שמואל I.L.) the שחיטה does not come under the category of an עבודה which may only be done by a priest, שחיטה לאו עבודה :שחיטה כשרה בזר (see on Levit. 1,5); even the שחיטת פר כה״ג בי״כ (according to רב). But although פרה only belongs to קדשי בדק הבית, its שחיטה, as well as the whole procedure until it is reduced to ashes, is confined to the priest. In this respect it is (there in Yoma) compared to מראות נגעים (see Levit. 13,2). Also מעשיה ביום, all the procedure has to be done only during day-time (Par. V.4). But according to one version in Sifri the burning may be done also at night, similarly to the שריפת אימורי חטאת בלילה. But against that is the development which the Gemora in Yoma 42b, makes from the sprinkling, the הזאת מימיה at which the Torah says expressly that it must be done in the day-time: ביום השלישי וגו׳, that all the processes, the killing, receiving the blood, sprinkling the blood, the burning, throwing in the cedar wood and the hyssop and the dyed red wool, all had to be done only in the day-time, and only the subsequent gathering up of the ashes, filling a vessel with water and placing and mixing the ashes therein could be done also at night.

In Para. 4,4, it says: כל העוסקין מתחלה ועד סוף ובו׳ ופוסלין אותה במלאכה and המלאכה פוסלת בה עד שתעשה אפר, that from beginning to end, i.e. until it is reduced to ashes none of all those who are ocupied with the פרה may do any other מלאכה at all at the same time that they are doing any of the acts, and were they to do so it would invalidate the פרה. In the Sifri this halacha is taught from the words of our text as follows:- ושחט אותה, בא הכתוב ולימד על הפרה שתהא מלאכה פוסלת בשחיטתה, ושרף את הפרה וגו׳ בא הכתוב ולימד על הפרה שתהא מלאכה פוסלת בשריפתה וכו׳, אלא בא הכתוב ולימד על הפרה שתהא מלאכה פוסלת בה משעת שחיטתה עד שתעשה אפר. Now we have already quoted the teaching from Yoma 42a that the sentences ושחט אותה לפניו ,ושרף את הפרה לעיניו meant שלא יסיח דעתו ממנה, that the mind of the functioning priest had to be concentrated on the פרה and was not to be distracted by anything else, and this פסול through היסח הדעת extended even to אסיפת אפרה and קידוש) מילוי מים לקידוש is the placing and mixing of the ashes in the water I.L.) (Ibid.), and finds this demand in למשמרת למי נדה (V.9) by which שמירה, the giving of undivided attention to the פרה is demanded until the מי נדה is established, i.e. the ashes mixed into the water, the only exception being the act of השלכת עץ ארז ואזוב ושני תולעת because this act refers to objects other than the פרה itself (and the mind has to be directed to their meaning I.L.). It is not definitely clear whether this פסול היסח הדעת and פסול מלאכה are identical or whether they are two different concepts. As it seems impossible to conceive doing another מלאכה without interrupting your concentration, the two would seem to be one and the same and doing the מלאכה to be only a proof of היסח הדעת. The same thing which the Gemora in Yoma designates as היסח הדעת with the water is called מלאכה in the Mishna in Para. 4,4, and in Sifri deduced from למשמרת in our text. On the other hand it is striking that the Sifri does not mention היסח הדעת בפרה as the Gemora in Yoma does, and further the Gemora takes היסח הדעת to be פוסל even at אסיפה and according to תוספתא פ״ג, which רמב״ם follows, מלאכה is not פסול at אסיפה, and everywhere else, as far as we can find, the השלכת עץ ארז וכו׳ which the Gemora in Yoma makes an exception from פסול היסח הדעת is nowhere given as an exception to פסול מלאכה. Quite strikingly this exception is not mentioned at all by רמב״ם in הל׳ פרה, and its omission as well as that of פסול היסח הדעת at אסיפה according to Yoma, is not remarked on by any commentator, וצ״ע (cf. ראב״ד and כ״מ on הל׳ פרה VII,3, concerning היסח הדעת and מלאכה).
According to Gittin 53b, מלאכה without היסח הדעת seems to be possible, and according to תוספות there, היסח הדעת ,ד״ה הא דאסח without מלאכה would also make וצע״ע .פסול in ש״מ ,מאירי on ב״ק 56a.

V. 4. מצותה מצות יד ולא מצות כלי :ולקח וגו׳ מדמה באצבעו, not in a vessel but in his hand is he to receive the blood and then sprinkle some of it with the forefinger of his right hand towards the entrance of the Sanctuary (Sifri). The remainder of the blood, which according to V.5, had to be burnt with the rest of the cow, he caught in a vessel (הל׳ פרה III,2, על כל הזיה טבילה :והזה וגו׳ מדמה שבע פעמים .(ראב״ד, at each sprinkling he had to dip his finger afresh in the blood, and before each dipping to cleanse his finger from the remains of the blood of the previous sprinkling (Para. 3,9 and Zebachim 93b; cf. IV,6).

הזה ולא כיון כנגד הפתח פסולה ,כנגד פתח ההיכל .אל נכח פני אהל מועד. “if he sprinkled and did not aim at the entrance of the Sanctuary, it rendered the procedure invalid.” (Para. 4,2). In Zebachim 113,a, the halacha is taught, that, just like the הזיות, so had the preceding procedure of שחיטה and the succeeding שריפה to be done facing the entrance to the Sanctuary, and פרה ששחטה או שרפה שלא כנגד הפתח, or, as it calls it in the Mishna חוץ מגתה is גת ,פסולה is the excavated cavity prepared for the burning of the פרה, which was made on the Mount of Olives facing the front of the Temple.

V. 5. ושרף את הפרה לעיניו (see on V.3) שרמז חוץ מגתה או שרפה בשתי גתות או ששרף שתים בגת אחת פסולה (para. IV,2) — את עורה ואת בשרה וגו׳. It must be burnt entirely with every part of it, it is immaterial whether one first flays it and cuts it up and burns the skin and all the parts together or burns it as it is without flaying: הפשיטה ונתחה כשרה (Para. 4,3).

V. 6. ולקח הכהן וגו׳ and equally so וכבס בגדיו הכהן (V.7). The repeated designation of the one who is functioning as כהן teaches that although every priest is fit for this, still it must be בכהונתו only when it is recognizable that he is such, i.e. בבגדי כהונה in his priestly vestments. (Yoma, 43a).

עץ ארז ואזוב וגו׳, the אזוב must be at least a hand-breadth long (Nidda 26a). ששינתו תולעת ולא ששינתו דבר אחר :ושני תולעת (Sifri) it must be wool which has been dyed with תלעת and not by any other dye (תולעת is the dye obtained by extraction from a certain worm I.L.). The explanation of the Sifri might throw some light on the term שני .שני from שנה means change of colour and indeed of such a nature that the new colour remains permanent, as fast as the original colour. So that שני designates what we call a “fast dye”. שלשה מינים שבפרה מעכבין זה את זה; each one of these three things (the cedar wood, the hyssop and the scarlet wool I.L.) is absolutely indispensable (Menachoth 27a). כרכן בשיירי הלשון he must tie them together with the ends of the שני תולעת-wool (Para. 3,11), but it is not decided whether the purpose is to make them into one joined object, באגודה אחת, or to give them a certain weight to enable all of them to be thrown so that they fall into the fire of the burning cow, כדי שיהא בהן כובד ויפלו לתוך שריפת הפרה (Yoma 41b). In any case according to the תוספתא it would not render the procedure invalid if they were thrown into the fire one after the other (הל׳ פרה המב״ם III,2), but it seems likely that this תוספתא adopts the latter opinion of the Gemora.
אל תוך שריפת הפרה, while it is already שריפה and still פרה, accordingly, after the greater part of the cow had been caught by the fire, before it had been reduced to ashes, משיצת האור ברובה (Sifri).

V. 7. וכבס בגדיו וגו׳, “the priest who threw”, the כהן המשליך of the previous verse, although he did not come directly into contact with the cow, and it uses a similar phrase in V.8. והשרף אתה יכבס וגו׳ for the one who performs the principle act of the לימד על העוסקים בפרה ;פרה מתחלה ועד סוף שיהו טעונים תכבוסת ורחיצת הגוף והערב שמש, to teach the rule that everybody who takes part in any of the acts of this procedure of the “red cow”, from the beginning to the end, including accordingly the שוחט and the מזה (the one who performed the slaughtering and the sprinkling) are טמאים and require טבילה ,כבוס בגדים and הערב שמש (Sifri and Para. 4,4). But the עוסקים בפרה are only טמא if the procedure is correctly performed; as soon as anything is done against the prescribed laws and the cow has become פסולה, having anything to do with it no longer entails .טומאה אירע בה פסול בשחיטתה אינה מטמאה בגדים אירע בה בהזיתה כל שעוסק בה לפני פסולה מטמא בגדים לאחר פסולה אינו מטמא בגדים (ibid.). But it is only being occupied with the פרה, doing one of the prescribed actions, slaughtering, sprinkling, burning and gathering up the ashes (V.10) that makes the doer טמא, but touching it does not do so. פרה עצמה אינה מטמאה (Para. 8,3 cf. פרים הנשרפים in Levit. on IV,12, p.108-109).

But he who is עוסק בפרה becomes as completely טמא as the נושא נבלה, i.e. בחיבורין; as long as he is occupied with the פרה he is not only מטמא בגדים שעליו but altogether all כלים which he touches, everything except אדם וכלי חרס, and these כלים which he touches during that time become ראשון לטומאה, the same as he is (see Levit. 11,25, p.281 and 310 et seq.; — but see רמב״ם׳s commentary on Zabim V.10 and תוספות י״ט thereon).

וכבס בגדיו (see on Levit. 11,25). — וכבס בגדיו הכהן וגו׳, the peculiar order of these words would come to tell us that he requires this טהרה only just because he is a כהן and consequently the following ואחר יבא אל המחנה would also refer only to his own מחנה of the כהנים to the מחנה שכינה which begins in the Sanctuary at the עזרת כהנים (see on Ch. 5,2 & 3). There is occasion to tell us this as he was sent (V.3) חוץ לשלש מחנות, outside the מחנה ישראל also, so one might have thought that, like a מצורע he would have to stay outside the city until he was טהור. Hence וכבס בגדיו הכהן, he requires this טהרה only as a כהן, to eat תרומה and to go into the Sanctuary. Hence also the transposition of ואחר יבוא אל המחנה next to וכבס בגדיו הכהן although it should come after וטמא עד הערב. It wants to designate the מחנה just as the מחנה הכהונה, and the וטמא הכהן עד הערב is merely added as a self-understood reference to everything which belongs to the כהונה, i.e. as a “כהן״ the state of טומאה only ceases after sunset, טבילה before that time only brings טהרה for eating מעשר שני but for eating real priestly food תרומה and קדשים and for entry into the Sanctuary, sunset is always required. For מחוסרי כפרה cases, eating קדשים and entry into the Sanctuary is further prohibited until the prescribed offerings have been brought.
V. 8. והשרף וגו׳ (see V.7).

V. 9. איש להכשיר את הזר טהור להכשיר את האשה והניח ;ואסף איש וגו׳ מי שיש בו דעת להניח יצאו חרש שוטה וקטן. For the gathering of the ashes no priest is necessary, any adult, sane person is qualified to do that. It may also be done at night, and doing something else at the same time would not render it invalid, אין מלאכה פוסלת בה (Para. 4,4).

והניח מחוץ למחנה, this “outside the camp” also refers only to the מחנה שכינה, the Sanctuary. None of the ash was brought into the עזרה. It was divided into three parts. One part was deposited on the Mount of the Temple, within the wall of the inner ring, another on the Mount of Olives, and the third divided amongst the 24 orders of the priesthood (who took turns to come on duty in the Sanctuary). The first was kept לעדת בני ישראל למשמרת as a permanent reminder, the other two parts were used as and when required for the purification process. (Para. 3,11; — see רמביים and תוספות י״ט thereon).

במקום טהור. The place in which the ashes are stored must be absolutely טהור and even if in an earthenware vessel with an hermetically closed lid (V.15), would be rendered unfit by being under the same roof as a dead body (Para. 11,1).

נדה .למשמרת למי נדה (see on Levit. 12,2). Just as there נדה designates a condition which makes a temporary separation necessary and reaches its conclusion by a period of seven days and טבילה, so here the condition brought about by טומאת מת which brings about a separation from all קדש and likewise reaches its conclusion by a period of seven days and טבילה is also called נדה. But here the טבילה has to be preceded by the sprinkling with the ashes mixed with מים חיים as prescribed in the following verses. This מים חיים mixed with אפר פרה is called מי נדה. What is really meant by the שמירה here called משמרת is an undivided concentration of thought given to something, so that the Sifri teaches from the expression למשמרת למי נדה that in the same way as at פרה עד שתעשה אפר, the processes before the cow is reduced to ash, so also at this stage of its mixture in the water, מלאכה, diverting one’s attention by doing anything else at the same time, פוסלת, makes the water unfit to be used. As already remarked, at the gathering up of the ashes, מלאכה does not render them unfit, but when they are to become מי נדה then during the whole process until the מי נדה has been made, i.e. until the ashes have been strewn on the drawn water, accordingly at the drawing, carrying and pouring the water into the vessel, sprinkling the ashes on to it in the vessel, the mind may not be diverted from it by doing anything else at the same time, the given command is: משמרת until it has become מי נדה. Once it has become מי נדה, even at the מלאכה ,הזיה is not המלאכה פוסלת עד שיטילו את האפר :פוסלת (Par. 4,4).

חטאת היא. It has the character of חטאת hence מעילה ,מועלין בה is applicable to it, as to all קדשים, more, according to תוספות in Menachoth 57b, in this respect it has the character of קדושת הגוף so that even מועל אחר מועל is possible at it (see Levit. 5,15, p.154). But מעילה is only applicable while it is still פרה but not after it has become ash בה מועלין באפרה אין מועלין. Further like חטאת if it has been slaughtered שלא לשמה or קבל והיזה שלא לשמה it would be פסולה, hence also, according to one version in the Sifri אין נשרפת בלילה. According to another נשרפת בלילה like the אימורי חטאת (see on V.3). Nevertheless אינה נפסלת בלינה and נשחטה היום והוזה דמה כהלכתה ונשרפה למחר כשירה (רמב״ם, הל׳ פרה IV,13).

V. 10. וכבס האוסף וגו׳ (see V.7). Only the one who gathers up the ashes, but anybody who is occupied with dividing and distributing them or comes into contact with them in any other way is פרה ,המב״ם) טהור V.4).

The פרה אדומה institution falls into two parts:- the preparation of אפר הפרה and its application for טהרת טמא מת. Its preparation is concluded with our verse וכבס וגו׳, its application begins in the next verse. Both parts, here in V.10 and equally so in V.21 conclude with the saying: והיתה לבני ישראל וגו׳ והיתה להם לחקת עולם, a saying which we only find elsewhere at the institution of י״כ (Levit. 16,29) and at the institution of the חצוצרות (Numb. 10,8) to be performed by the כהנים. Accordingly, as in these places the principle of כפרה and the principle of basing all authority and all hopes of salvation on the Torah is proclaimed by the saying והיתה לכם לחקת עולם to be an eternal fundamental norm for Israel, the concept of the פרה אדומה institution must likewise concern a similar fundamental principle of Jewish life, which, just by this repeated saying והיתה וגו׳ must prove its application for all time. And at the same time this concept must be of such a nature that it gives occasion for the specific remark of its universal application also for גרים (see the comprehensive explanation of the whole institution at end of V.21, I.L.).

V. 11. הנגע במת, clearly here מת is differentiated from נפש אדם. The dead body is in relationship to the נפש אדם, comes from it, belongs to it, but itself is not the נפש (see V.13). להביא את בן שמנה :לכל נפש (Sifri), even of such a human creature that has not had the possibility of living on.

V. 12. הוא יתחטא בו ביום וגו׳. From V.19 it is clear that the sprinkling is to be done on the third and seventh day, and then, after the sprinkling has been done on the seventh day, the טהרה, the reinstatement is completed by טבילה, (immersion in a Mikva) and הערב שמש (sunset). So that, of necessity the וביום השביעי must refer back to the ביום השלישי and יטהר taken to follow on as the result of the purpose: “he has to expiate himself from sin on the third and seventh day then he can become pure” (by טבילה), or alternatively “then to become pure” (by טבילה). For this התחטא by sprinkling is a characteristic speciality for טומאת מת. For all other טומאות, even for those that last seven days as זב וזבה נדה ויולדת, (with the exception of מצורע whose טבילה has likewise to be preceded by another act of הזאה (Levit. 14,7 & 8) טבילה alone after the lapse of the prescribed period suffices, but here הזית שלישי ושביעי must have preceded for the טבילה to be effective. The two preceding הזאות are the condition for taking the ordinary act of טהרה, the טבילה, which here is accordingly expressed simply by יטהר and לא יטהר. These sprinklings with אפר פרה bring about the effectiveness of the טבילה which follows them, but in themselves effect no alteration in the טומאה-condition. So the הזיה cannot be taken as an act of טהרה but very much as one which is calculated to bring the person striving for טהרה to a special frame of mind. It accordingly has a special name, one which harmonises with the character of the פרה. It is חטאת and the effect which it is to achieve is called התחטא and the act itself: חטא (V.19). Similarly the sprinkling act to be done to a בית המנוגע is also called in Deut. 14,51 & 52 חטא. According to ר״ת (Yebamoth 46b תוספות ד״ה דאין טבילה) had to be done before each sprinkling on the third and seventh day, but this was only to be considered as pertaining to the הזאה and not as having any effect on the טומאה.

From רש״י (Kiddushim 62a) and תוספות (Yoma 8b) it is clear that if the sprinkling had been omitted on the third day and done on a later day then this later day is taken to have the meaning of the third day (explanation and reason given later on I.L.) and four days exactly must always be reckoned between the first and second sprinkling as it would between the normal third and seventh day. רמב״ם הל׳ פרה XI,2 has a different way of taking it.

V. 13. כל הנגע וגו׳. With extreme precision the expression and construction of the wording of the conception of טומאת מת is chosen here. It does not say כל הנגע בנפש אשר מת then the נפש itself or the נפש of a dead person would be considered lying there. נפש האדם and נפש האדם אשר ימות would also be something quite different to נפש אדם and נפש אדם נפש אדם .אשר מת is the soul of an individual person, and נפש אדם אשר מת is the soul of a person who has died. But נפש האדם is the soul of Man, the soul of mankind in general, and האדם אשר ימות is not a man who has died, but mankind which is mortal, that dies, is liable to death, so that נפש האדם אשר ימות, is the soul of human beings, the soul of mortal Man. Every מת, every dead human body does represent the mortality of human beings, and the danger is very near to lead to thinking of this physical lack of freedom which death demonstrates as extending also to the psychical nature of Man in its connection with the physical during life. — נפש האדם אשר ימות is the living human being who cannot escape the fate of death which hangs over him, a force to which he has to submit, a fact which every dead human body brings home to him. Every dead human body makes him, the living man, realise that he is subject to death, hence coming into contact with death, נוגע במת is therefore under the impression of נפש האדם אשר ימות, and indeed, נפש האדם וגו׳, not just of this dead person, but of האדם, of the fate to which all mankind must submit. בנפש האדם וגו׳ accordingly introduces the reason for הנגע במת, he needs חטוי not because he is נוגע במת but because through נגיעה במת he comes to the idea of נפש האדם אשר ימות, it is therefore either in apposition to במת, or, as we have translated it the ב of מת is the medium, the causative מ “through a מת״.

So that, as is clear from V.16, it is not necessary for a whole dead body to bring about the state of טומאה, but any part of it which would bring to mind the idea of a dead person, everything, as is explained in Nidda 55a, שנברא עמו ואין גזעו מחליף, which is born with a person, and if lost does not completely reproduce itself, is מטמא. Not teeth, hair or nails which do reproduce themselves, but the flesh of muscles, which even though it does grow again always leaves a visible scar, נעשה מקומו צלקת. Blood, being something that does completely reproduce itself if lost, does not induce a state of טומאה unless it comes directly from a dead body and does then represent the immediate bearer of the life the נפש. Hence the halacha teaches on our text הנגע במת בנפש וגו׳ that רביעית דם הבאה מן המת מטמא (Chulin 72a, see on Levit. 21,11).

את משכן ה׳ טמא, even if he had undergone טבילה, as long as he had not had the הזיות prescribed here, and without having had them had entered the Sanctuary. In V.20 it says similarly: כי את מקדש ה׳ טמא. If משכן expresses the meaning of the Sanctuary as the place of the Presence of God, and מקדש as the place of the sanctifying elevation of everything earthly up to God, (see on Levit. 25,8), then these two sentences would declare the concept טומאה as being equally in contrast to the thought of God represented by the word משכן as to the sanctifying of all earthly existence which מקדש expresses. That כרת is incurred not for neglecting to have the הזאה but for entering the Sanctuary without having had it is, according to Sifri, evident already from the preceding verse. There it says ואם לא יתחטא לא יטהר but not ולא יתחטא ונכרתה וגו׳. So that את מקדש ה׳ טמא is to be taken as belonging to the first part of the verse i.e. “everybody who, after touching a dead body, and not having חטוי, enters the Sanctuary and thereby has been מטמא it, ונכרתה וגו׳. But probably את משכן etc., is simply the concluding sentence and ביאת מקדש without הזאה is already contained in ולא יתחטא. For in the preceding verse it is already said that without הזאת שלישי ושביעי he is not טהור, he cannot become so by the טבילה (expressly prescribed in V.19) on the seventh day. To that now V.13 states the case that a person not having had הזיה behaves as being טהור, i.e. without הזיה although he has had טבילה has entered the Sanctuary or contacted קדשים. His supposed condition of טהרה only shows itself, can only show itself in such a way. So that in fact in the ולא יתחטא already the whole consequence of entering the Sanctuary or eating קדשים is already said and את מקדש וגו׳ can therefore be the concluding clause.

טמא יהיה עוד טומאתו בו, having no הזאה has the same effect as having no טבילה. The law of a person who is טמא, keeping away from the Sanctuary and קדשים has already been declared above Ch. 5,2 & 3, as well as in Levit. 22,2 et seq., XV,31 and V.3 and here only the rule is given that all cases of טמאי מת who require הזאה, without having that הזאה, even after טבילה remain in the state of טומאה.

V. 14. טומאת מגע במת .זאת התורה וגו׳ has been discussed already in the previous verses. This is the method of becoming טמא common to all זאת התורה .טומאות. Now follows the law that is given specially for תורה חדשה .טומאת מת, as Sifri calls it, to which only מצורע, which is also מטמא בביאה, is analogous (see Levit. 13,46). It, טוממא אהל, according to a teaching (in Yebamoth 61a) applies only to מת ישראל but the halacha is not quite decided on this point, but טומאת מגע ומשא applies without difference to any human body. Perhaps הנגע במת לכל נפש אדם of V. 11 already indicates this. In explaining the או בקבר in V.18 as זה קבר שלפני הדבור, by which קבר שלפני הדבור is included in תוספות ,טומאת מגע there is of the opinion that טומאת אהל does not apply to קבר שלפני הדבור i.e. to those that were buried before the Lawgiving; it says כי ימות באהל, if anybody dies from now onwards, and מו״ר המנוח מהור״ר יעקב עטלינגער ז״ל in ערוך לנר on Yebamoth 61a is of the opinion that this is the opinion of רמב״ם also. Rashi takes קבר שלפני הדבור (Nazir ibid.) in a different way (cf. Levit. 13,2, I.L.).

כל הבא אל האהל, as soon as it enters, even הבא מקצתו (Sifri), even if only one limb or member of the body has entered into the tent in which there is a dead body, the whole person becomes טמא. Nazir 43a: דאהל המת תוספות) ,כמליא טומאה דמי ומיד שהושיט ידו בפנים כאלו נגע במת ibid.) (the whole room is as if it was solidly full of the depressing influence of death so that as soon as one stretches one’s hand into it, it is as if one had touched the dead body I.L.). With this explanation the question of the מל״מ on הל׳ טומאת צרעת 16b, could be answered. It is not because ביאה במקצת שמה ביאה but because it is as good as actually touching the מת. — כל אשר באהל, not only everything which is under the same roof but everything which lies buried in the ground below it, the concept “house” extends right down to the depths beneath it, ספרי) לעשות קרקעו של בית עד תהום כמוהו אהלות XV,5).

דרך פתחו הוא טמא ואין מטמא בכל צדדיו כשהוא פתוח .כל הבא אל האהל, as long as the home has a door for entry and exit it is only the actual interior space of the house that makes entry טמא but touching the walls from the outside would not do so. But if the doorway is completely walled in, בית סתום and פרץ את פצימיו, then it has the character of a closed grave and is מטמא כל סביביו (Sifri, Baba Bathra 12a; see V.16).

The concept אהל is represented by any roofing of at least one cubic טפח and extends to all rooms which are connected by an opening of at least a square טפח with the room the roof of which is over the מת. (Oholoth 13,1. et seq.).
Further, just as an אהל טפח spreads the טומאה to all objects beneath it, so also does it act as a protection against such spreading if it intervenes. It is both מביא and חוצץ (Oholoth 8).

V. 15. וכל כלי פתוח וגו׳. By כל אשר באהל of the previous verse it has already been said that everything which is affected by טומאה, so that vessels are also included, which are under the same roof as a dead body become טמא. If then here it speaks of a vessel becoming טמא through not having a tightly fitted covering it must be speaking of such a vessel which cannot be affected by טומאה touching it on the outside but only by entering into its inside, it is מיטמא מאוירו but not מגבו. We know of such vessels from Levit. 11,33 as being כלי חרש, earthenware vessels. Such vessels if they have צמיד פתיל covers remain טהור even in an אהל המת and protect their contents from becoming טמא הוא — .טומאה, it does not say here שבעת ימים as in the preceding and succeeding verses, because it is speaking of a כלי חרש which אין לו טהרה מטומאתו hence טמא הוא is absolutely and permanently טמא.

צמיד פתיל. Both roots צמד and פתל designate joining. We find צמד in צמד בקר, a harnessed team of bullocks; צמידים על ידיה, bracelets, ויצמד ישראל לבעל פעור in Ch. 25,3 designating the close attachment to the evil-doings of Peor. פתל in פתיל, a twist made by joining several threads twisted together. There is also וקצץ פתילים (Ex. 39,3) for the single strong and stiffening single metal wire. We have had occasion repeatedly to remark that its relationship to בדל and בתל rather indicates that the idea of separating from others by joining together is more prominent therein. Now a cover can close a vessel so hermetically that its contents are thereby kept quite apart from everything outside it without its being actually joined to the vessel, then it would be פתיל although not צמיד. If one would then cement the points of contact between cover and vessel with some soft material which hardens when set, צמיד would be added to פתיל, the closing cover would be actually joined to the vessel. Thus in Kelim 10,2 במה מקיפין, בסיד ובגפסיס ,בזפת וכוי ובכל דבר המתמרח, (it must be sealed with something like putty which can be smeared thoroughly into the joint I.L.). אין מקיפין ולא בבעץ ולא בעופרת מפני שהוא פתיל ואינו צמיד (but not with tin-foil or soft lead because although they close completely they do not make a joint. (I.L.). So that אשר אין צמיד פתיל עליו means, on which there is no closing joint. It is self-understood that this cover is also of earthenware or of any material that is not receptive of טומאה. Further, just as כלי חרס מציל באהל המת an earthenware vessel with a hermetically sealed lid saves its contents from becoming טמא because it does not become טמא by being touched on its outside, so certainly vessels which on account of the material out of which they are made or because of their size are not liable themselves to become גללים ,כלי אבנים) טמא etc. and כלי עץ הגדולים הבאים במדה שאין מיטלטלין מלא וריקן etc. see Levit. 11,47, p.307, 312, et seq.), similarly, if provided with a צמיד פתיל, save their contents from טומאה (Kelim X,I).

V. 16. טומאת מגע .וכל אשר יגע וגו׳ had already been discussed and finished in verses 11-13, V.14 introduced the special טומאת אהל teaching regarding מת, V.15 continued it, so according to the grouping of the verses this V.16 should also belong to that theme. And as a matter of fact Nazir 53b, does explain על פני השדה by המאהיל על פני מת, and similarly Chulin 72a: לרבות גולל ודופק. For the two previous verses deal with persons being under the same roof as a dead body, the usual way in which טומאת אהל is understood. This verse speaks of the second kind of טומאת אהל, that something is מאהיל על המת, that something is itself “roofing” a dead body, i.e. perpendicularly over it, which then corresponds to a third kind of טומאת אהל that the מת מאהיל עליו, something is perpendicularly under a dead body. All these three kinds of אהל have exactly the same effect in the טומאה they induce. (Oholoth 3,1). But that this טומאת אהל, the מאהיל על המת is called נגיעה here could be an important confirmation of a teaching of רבא. In Chulin 125b, a טומאת אהל is included in the concept of מגע, so that there must be an אהל נגיעה, a kind of טומאת אהל related in the wider conception of מגע and an גרידא, the ordinary kind of טומאת אהל. And רבא explains that אהל נגיעה refers to everything that is מאהיל על המת, just the kind of אהל of our verse where forming a roof over a dead body is considered as coming into direct contact with it. But אהל גרידא would be בהמשכה which, as רש״י explains is דבר אחר מאהיל עליו ועל הטומאה, that the same roof is over the מת and a pure object and extends the טומאה to the hitherto pure object, just the kind of “אהל״ of which verses 14 and 15 speak. The practical difference whether one considers a טומאת אהל as מגע or not would lie in צירוף, according to the canon זה הכלל כל שהוא משם אחד טמא משני שמות טהור (Oholoth ibid.). This differentation which רבא makes seems, according to the whole context there, to be the halacha. (See תוספות Chulin 126a, ד״ה מאן, the רשב״א there, the רא״ש on Oholoth 3,1, and it is striking that רמב״ם הל׳ טומאת המת IV,14 does not adopt this differentation of רבא and ר״ש, in his commentary on Oholoth 3,1, does not mention it, וצ״ע)

בחלל חרב, it does not say simply בחלל as in V.18, but בחלל חרב. The Torah suggests the presence of both the body and the instrument that caused its death, only by the presence of the חרב does one know that a body lying על פני השדה is a חלל חרב. But as the Torah does mention both here it wishes to say, according to the halacha (Nazir 53b) that חרב הרי הוא כחלל, it has the same effect whether he touches the one or the other, or in accordance with the preceding explanation he were to stand over (מאהיל) the one or the other. But, according to the halacha, it is not because it was the death-causing weapon, but simply because it must have come into contact with the dead body that it receives the same degree of טומאה as the body itself. And indeed not only חרב but any כלי מתכות, any metal implement has the same legal speciality that in touching a מת or a טמא מת it receives the טומאה-character of what it has touched, if a מת it becomes אבי אבות, if a טמא מת it becomes אב like it. But this only applies to human beings כלי באדם not from one implement to the other, not כלי בכלי. Every אבי אבות and אב הטומאה is טמא שבעה, every ראשון only טומאת ערב (see verses 11 & 22); אדם וכלים are as already remarked in Levit. 11,47, p.314, only מקבל טומאה מאב הטומאה: Our sentence accordingly speaks only of כלי מתכות. This is the way ר״ת takes it. But according to the way רבי יצחק מסימפונט takes it, which is also the opinion of הל׳ טומאת מת) רמב״ם V), all כלים — except of course כלי חרש which can never get even אב הטומאה and certainly not אבי אבות — receive the peculiar characteristic given by חרב הרי הוא כחלל and these verses speak of all תוספות) כלים Nazir 54b, ר״ש ,ד״ה ת״ש on 1,2 אהלות; see Levit. ibid.).

או במת או בעצם אדם, not only a complete body is מטמא באהל, but even הגלגלת ,השדרה .כזית מן המת etc. (Oholoth 2,1) and to be מטמא במגע ובמשא even a smaller portion, even עצם כשעורה etc. (ibid. 3) although not באהל.

או בקבר. In Nazir 53b it says זה קבר סתום, as here it is speaking of מאהיל על הקבר it must speak of a completely closed-in grave, and, moreover, as תוספות remarks there שיש בו פותח טפח, there must be at least a free space of one cubic טפח between the body and the covering earth. It is only by this free space that the earth surrounding the body gets its real character of a “grave” and if it is סתום, closed in on all sides, as is here presumed to be the case, it is as קבר itself מטמא כל צדדין, and anybody being מאהיל over it by stepping even שלא כנגד המת becomes טמא. But if the earth is direct upon the body and there is no free space of a טפח then it is not considered a קבר but only the מת itself is מטמא. It is then a טומאה רצוצה, a confined טומאה, which בוקעת ועולה בוקעת ויורדת, has effect upwards and downwards perpendicularly to an unlimited height and depth (unless it becomes checked somewhere by an אהל טפח). Then only the one who steps over the grave directly over the spot that covers the body becomes טמא, and indeed not through the grave as such but through the מת which, as טומאה רצוצה is בוקעת ועולה. So alco according to רמב״ם הל׳ טומאת מת VII,4 ראב״ד takes it differently.

A field in which ploughing discloses a hidden grave from which splinters of bone could be “scattered” about in the area is called a בית הפרס from פרש) פרס) to scatter, (see Oholoth 17,1 et seq. hereon).

V. 17. ולקחו ,ולקחו לטמא וגו׳, every sane adult is qualified for this, as at אסיפת האפר in V.9 (Yoma 43a). ולקחו ונתן, the change in number teaches that the two actions need not be done by the same person (ibid.) עפר .מעפר וגו׳ is really dust of the earth, but is also used in Kings II, XXIII,4 et seq., for dust produces by burning i.e. ash. Equally so in Deut. 9,21, compared with Ex. 32,20. Here the term would be chosen with significant intent, (see below) — ונתן עליו מים חיים אל כלי designates a combined act: מים חיים אל כלי ordains that the water is first to be placed in the vessel. When the water comes into the vessel there is nothing else there yet; ונתן עליו, but the ashes are then to be put into the water in such a way that they do not remain swimming on the surface of the water, but by stirring them about they mix with the water and the water comes over the ash. כתיב עליו אלמא אפר ברישא וכתיב מים חיים אל כלי אלמא מים ברישא הא כיצד וכו׳ אל כלי דוקא עליו לערבן (Sota, 16b). The act of putting the ash in the water and mixing is called קידוש, the water thus mixed is called מי חטאת; the water only becomes מי חטאת from the moment the ash is placed into the water, אין מי חטאת נעשין מי חטאת אלא עם מתן אפר (Temura XIIa).

The water for the מי חטאת must be filled in a vessel but anything that can be called a vessel, has the character of one, can be used for it. בכל כלים מקדשים אפי׳ בכלי גללים וכר אין ממלאין ואין מקדשין ואין מזין מי חטאת אלא בכלי (Para. 5,5). The water must be taken into the vessel directly from a spring (ibid.VI,5). By the term מים חיים all waters emanating from springs and which hardly ever dry up are understood, they must not have undergone any chemical change (מוכים) not contain salt and not hot springs, not מלוחים and not פושרים (ibid. VIII,9). At a distance from the source, flowing water is valid as long as there is no interruption to the flow (ibid. VIII,11). — See above on למי נדה (V.9) that, from the moment the water is drawn until the קידוש i.e. until the ashes are mixed in it, מלאכה פוסלת. After the קידוש and even at the time of the הזיה, the sprinkling, מלאכה and היסח הדעת do not matter. — In Bechoroth 29a it is taught that just as הנוטל שכרו להעיד דיניו ועדותיו בטלין, who accepts a fee for giving judgment or evidence renders his verdict and his testimony invalid, so also הנוטל שכרו להזות ולקדש מימיו מי מערה, אפרו אפר מקלה, the acts of קידוש and הזיה are only valid if they are done without being paid for, but for הבאה ומלוי for bringing the ashes and filling the vessel with the water, payment may be taken. According to Rashi there and in Kiddushin 58b at הבאה and מלוי the work entailed is not really an integral part of the duty of the קידוש and הזיה which are entirely part of the Mitzva, or as Rashi puts it in Kiddushin are שכר לימוד מצוה for which no payment may be taken in accordance with the canon: ראה למדתי אתכם וגו׳ מה אני בחנם אף אתם בחנם (Bechoroth 29a). But it seems that there must still be some reason why הזיה and קידוש are rendered invalid if payment is taken for doing them, whereas כתיבת ספ״ת ,שחיטה ,טבילת כלי paid מזוזה בבית ,הטלת ציצית בבגד etc. do not lose their validity because the work has been paid for (see תוספות Ketuboth 105a ד״ה גוזרי). (a note in the margin of the original manuscript of the author זצ״ל. runs:- אפשר לע״ד לחלק בין קידוש והזיה לשאר מצות, כל שאר מצות יש ביד המחויב לעשות המצוה ואינו מוטל על אחרים לעשות המצוד, בעדו לכתוב לו סת״ם, לשחוט לו בהמה וכיוצא, אכן קידוש והזיה אי אפשר לטמא לעשות והזה הטהור על הטמא קאמר רחמנא ומצוה היא על חברו לעשות ודומה ללימוד תורה עדות ודין שאי אפשר בלי אחר ודוק. — And in the notes and additions added to the first edition of Deut. referring to this, it says:- the reason for the difference between the mixing and sprinkling here, giving evidence, acting as judge, and teaching Torah and other mitzvas could perhaps be that, at the mixing and sprinkling the mitzva is essentially for somebody else to do for you, you cannot possibly do it yourself, the Torah says that it must be done for the unfit person by a fit one — ולקחו לטמא וגו׳ והזה הטהור על הטמא. — Similarly giving evidence and judging are functions which have to be done for you by others, and learning the oral law is also something that originally and essentially depended on oral tradition and teaching which you must get from somebody else. In all these cases the Torah imposes them on the unselfish actions of others. Doing them come definitely as a מצוה, a command of the Torah for which no payment may be taken. Other mitzvahs, as שחיטה ,כתיבת סת״ם etc. he can do by himself or get others to help him. As these doing it for somebody else is not the essential nature of the מצוה and accordingly may be paid for. “Perhaps” קידוש והזיה belong quite specially to the concept of “Teachings” regarding which the מה אני בחנם וכו׳ was primarily spoken, and perhaps the introductory זאת התורה (V.9) points to that. וצ״ע בצ״ק לבכורות ד״ט א׳ דמשמע דס״ל דהזיה וקידוש רמיא רחמנא על האי כהן דשייך בעבודה, מ״ה אסור ליקח אפי׳ אגר דמוכה עכ״ל וצ״ע מאי קאמר ועי׳ בריטב״א קידושין נ״ח ב׳ דס״ל דהא דדיניו בטלין. קנסא דרבנן הוא וס״ל נמי דשכר טבחים ובודקים שהוא מותר דהנהו פועלים נינהו ולא שכר הוראה הוא .אלא שכר פעולה ועדיף משכר הבאה ומלוי וצ״ע
ולקח וגו׳ ונתן, the אפר must be strewn on to the water by conscious, intentional human action (Para. 6,1 and רמב״ם there).
In הל׳ פרה אדומה X.2 & 4 there is a difference of opinion between רמב״ם and ראב״ד as to how the פסלו מלאכה and היסח הדעת is to be taken see כ״מ thereon (see below and on V.3).

V. 18. ולקחו וגו׳ איש טהור וגו׳. Every sane male, even minors, are qualified to do the הזיה, whereas the קידוש must be done by people who are over age, but women are also qualified for it. (Yoma, 43a).

כל אזוב שיש לו שם לווי פסול אזוב זה כשר :אזוב, it must be the ordinary common hyssop which people call just hyssop, would simply say “אזוב זה, this is hyssop”, but any special kind given another name (such as Greek hyssop I.L.) would be unfit. (Para. 11,7). It is a mitzva to take three separate twigs of hyssop and bind them together, as at פסח מצרים (Ex. 12,22). But two are sufficient and if, in the course of using, only one remains, the הזיה can be continued with that (Sukka, 13a). Regarding the length of the twigs, at first they must be at least one טפח (see תוספות י״ט XI,9) but it may wear down to a minimum and still be used גרדומיו בל שהוא (Sukka 13a). — והזה, the sprinkling must be done בכתה, with the mind concentrated on the act, according to רמב״ם, with the intention of טהרה to which the words of the following verse והזה הטהור על הטמא seem to point (Para. 12,3), according to ראב״ד as long as the mind is concentrated on the act, on the sprinkling, it would suffice without the idea of effecting הל׳ פרה) טהרה X,8). In this הזיה differs from טבילה, the latter is effective even without intention: גל שנתלש ובו מ׳ סאה ונפל על האדם ועל הכלים טהורין (Chulin 31a). The sprinklings with the מי חטאת do not require to be dipped afresh in the water before each sprinkling (as the הזיות does, Levit. 4,6) but as long as the twigs hold some water they can be used. And the one who has to be sprinkled only requires a minimum of water on any part of the body to become אגבא דגברא אין צריכה שיעור ;טהור (Yoma 14a, and Kiddushin 25a).

To have the full understanding of the sprinkling on the part of the person to whom it is being done, at the moment of its being done is not necessarily demanded, מזין על האדם מדעתו ושלא מדעתו (Para. 12a).

על האהל, the אהל itself becomes טמא although it is מחובר and as such is otherwise not מקבל טומאה. But this only applies to such materials which had the אהל character of roofing material at the Mishkon viz, wool, skins, goats-hair and, of vegetable origin, linen. Hence the sentence: כל היוצא מן העץ אינו מטמא טומאת אהלים אלא פשתן (Sab. 27b). All other materials are only מקבל טומאה when they are not מחובר. But this difference only exists relating to the roof itself becoming טמא. Regarding making everything under it טמא all materials are the same whether מחובר or תוספות) תלוש there and ראב״ד ,רמב״ם and הל׳ טומאת מת ,מל״מ, V.12).

V. 19. והזה הטהור על הטמא. In V.18 it already says ולקח וגו׳ איש טהור וגו׳ so that the demand for the absolute טהרות of the person functioning is made. Nevertheless it is repeated here to give details of the טהרה required in that person. He need only be טהור in contrast to the טמא, need only not be טמא, need only to have taken one step out of טומאה. So that the halacha is taught from this, that, not only for הזיה but altogether for the whole process of the פרה, a טבול יום is qualified to act, who, by טבילה has achieved the first degree of טהרה and, in Levit. 14,8, is called :טהור ורחץ במים וטהר (Yoma 43b). This traditional law that טבול יום כשר בפרה was vehemently disputed by the Saducees, who would not accept traditional laws. To prove and keep up the authenticity and authority of Traditional Law at such a public act as פרה אדומה at which every individual took such an essential part regarding his own טהרה, before the beginning of functioning the priest was publicly on the Mount of Olives, made to render himself טמא by touching a טומאה and then made to have טבילה, so that ostentatiously and with the fullest publicity every פרה אדומה process was carried out by a טבול יום. מטמאין היו הכהן השורף את הפרה ומטבילין אותו להוציא מלבן של צדוקין שהיו אומרים במעורבי שמש היתה נעשית. But on the other hand, the whole procedure had to be given the character of טהרה to the highest degree, and the most elaborate precautions were taken for that purpose (see ibid. and Para. 3).

V. 21. והיתה להם להקת עולם. This is a law that still affects us today. As we are all טמאי מת and, having no אפר פרה, have no means of attaining טהרה, anyone going on to the actual site of the Temple would incur the punishment of כרת. The site of the Temple did not lose its sanctity by the destruction of the Temple: קדושה ראשונה קדשה לשעתה וקדשה לעתיד הל׳ בית הבחירה המב״ם) לבא VI,14; but see ראב״ד there).

המזה מי הנדה וגו׳. With והיתה להם להקת עולם the second part of the פרה chapter comes to an end in a similar manner to והיתה להקת עולם in V.10 which concluded the first part, the act of burning. So that the following ומזה וגו׳ does not refer to the one who sprinkles the water on to a person to make him טהור. It also does not say וכבס המזה על הטמא את בגדיו in a similar way to V.19 and analogous to V.10 but ומזה מי נדה quite generally without reference to any person or object, just like the following והנגע במי הנדה which quite without doubt does not refer to the act of הזיה. But ומזה מי הנדה clearly speaks of somebody who moves or touches the מי הנדה not for the purpose of טהרה, and thereby expresses the contrast that מזה על הטמא remains טהור but הזה מי הנדה for any purpose other than for טהרה becomes טמא. But an act of bringing into motion is משא identical with היסט (see Levit. 11,25). The Gemora (Yoma 14a) accordingly teaches the halacha that by this מזה what is to be understood is נושא but that it uses the term מזה to tell us that נושא מי חטאת is only טמא if the quantity is sufficient to be used for sprinkling דבעינן שיעור הזיה, and one who carries that quantity טעון כבוס בגדים. But one who simply touches במי נדה is not מטמא בגדים but does become טמא even if the quantity of the water is less than the שיעור הזיה. Hence the sentences in Kelim 1,1 & 2: אבות הטומאה השרץ וכו׳ ומי חטאת שאין בהם כדי הזיה הרי אלו מטמאין אדם וכלים במגע וכלי חרס באויר ואינם מטמאין במשא. למעלה מהם נבלה ומי חטאת שיש בהם כדי הזיה שהם מטמאין את האדם במשא לטמא בגדים במגע וחשוכי בגדים במגע.

V. 22. וכל אשר יגע בו הטמא יטמא וגו׳. In the first half of the verse it says יטמא without any limiting addition, in the second half יטמא עד הערב. So the Gemora in Avoda Zara 34b, says the first half speaks of טומאת שבעה and moreover בחיבורין, i.e. someone who touched the טמא person at the time that the latter was still touching the מת. But the second half speaks of שלא בחיבורין, i.e. the one who touched the טמא מת did so after the latter had ceased to be in contact with the מת, and he would then only be טומאת ערב. The מת itself is אב אבות הטומאה, the one who is in contact with it becomes אב הטומאה and makes people who touch him שלא בחיבורין to ראשון which state only lasts to the evening. If, according to the way חלל חרב is taken to mean (V.16) that all כלים which come into contact with מת or טמא מת receive the same degree as that which they touch, then we can understand why in this second half והנפש, people are specially stressed, for כלים which touch a טמא מת even שלא בחיבורין would become אב הטומאה, the same degree as the טמא מת has, and would become טמא טומאת שבעה. Rambam in הל׳ טומאת מת V.2, takes this טומאה בחיבורין to be only דרבנן (see כ״מ and מל״מ there).

If we consider all these laws and instructions regarding the פרה אדומה and טומאת מת and try to understand the meaning and the thoughts they are meant to have and to impart we must first of all be clear about the concept under which the Torah itself tells us we are to think of this whole פרה אדומה institution, viz. the concept “חטאת״ by which the Torah characterises it, and which forms the underlying idea for its detailed laws.

חטאת, expiation, doing away with the sin and purging the sinner from his sin is a concept which belongs entirely to the sphere of morals. If then the Torah calls its פרה אדומה institution — the חוקת התורה which forms the fundamental institution of the whole lesson of טומאת-מת, which itself is the fundamental idea at the base of the whole idea of טומאה altogether — if it calls it חטאת it at once directs us most definitely to the sphere of morals as being that line of thought within which we have to look for the meaning of the whole of the laws of טומאה and טהרה in general and of the פרה אדומה in particular. At the same time that would give an unmistakeable confirmation to the way we have taken all the טומאה and טהרה laws we have hitherto come across in the Torah. We were of the opinion that “freedom of will in moral matters” was the first and irreplaceable condition for the whole living our lives on a higher plane, which the Torah makes it a duty for us to try to do. We took it that the conviction of this very first fundamental truth would be endangered by all that the fact that Man must submit to death, and to the superficial limitations which the forces of nature exert on everything including human beings which a dead human body lying before one’s eyes, demonstrate so drastically. If the whole human being has succumbed to death, if altogether it is the “human being” that lies there in the dead body overpowered by physical forces, if accordingly Man, the whole Man, stands, in his life, like all other organic beings in nature, under the spell of an irresistable overpowering force, then altogether nowhere is there place for the moral “thou shalt” next to the physical “thou must”. Moral freedom of will would be an illusion, and the whole Divine Law of morality with its demand for the most free-willed devotion of all one’s existence and purposes to its illuminating, purifying, warming and enlivening happiness-bringing fire of its Sanctuary (the אש דת I.L.) is an ununderstandable proposition. (Cf. Levit. 5,13, p.147).

Against this, the laws of טומאה and טהרה come, as given in Levit. and place the fact, guaranteed by God, of freedom in moral matters in opposition to the demoralising illusion of physical lack of freedom. Throughout life, whenever the energy which the consciousness of moral freedom gives, threatens to be disturbed by reminders of physical lack of freedom, these laws of טהרה endeavour to awaken the reminder that in matters of morality there is no lack of freedom, as we learnt to understand when we went into the various טומאה and moments in the sections of the Torah dealing with them.

Now here, the same Lawgiving on טומאה and טהרה — in the greatest publicity for the national community, through its priestly representative in view of its Sanctuary of the Torah — proclaims by means of an important function the great thought “חטאת״. Thereby it lays down, as the basis for the whole life of the people, the fundamental Truth that human beings “can be free from sin, can become so and remain so.”

That is the meaning of this חטאת this act of expiation performed outside the Sanctuary. It is different from the expiation-offering inside the Sanctuary, the expiation of a certain person from a certain sin by the symbolic act of promising faithful adherence to duty for the future. It is rather the proclamation of the public conviction of the possibility of freedom from sin, the ability of mastering all physical temptations and allurements, proclaiming the fact of the moral power of the human will in general.

But it proclaims this freedom of Man not forgetting where he has no freedom, it shows his freedom in moral matters in connection with his lack of freedom in physical ones. It does not teach to close one’s eyes to the lack of freedom to which the physical nature of Man belongs. It shows Man with the whole contrast of his being, his mortality next to his immortality, with his freedom and his subjection, with his physical nature and his moral nature. And as it places him in the totality of his dual nature before the mission-giving Sanctuary of the One absolutely Free-willed God, it raises him with the whole of his being, with his physical evanescence and his spiritual permanence up into the free eternal sphere of that Unique Free One and says to him: Be not deceived by corpse and death, become free, become immortal not in spite of, but together with all that is physical unfree and mortal on you, remain immortal master of your mortal body, protect yourself and prove the truth of טהרה in the midst of טומאה!
From this point of view, obtained from the concept חטאת the whole meaning of the פרה אדומה institution could be as follows: -

The פרה אדומה תמימה אשר אין בה מום אשר לא עלה עליה עול is the animal, full of life (completely red, אדומה תמימה) bodily completely faultless (אין בו מום), and mature (בת ג׳ שנים); having the purpose as פרה of being a serving help to human work, but which has never used its strength in the service of Man (פסול עבודה), yea, has never borne the sign of service (פסול עול see V.2), this animal, representing the physical-animal nature of Man not mastered and controlled, was taken by the national community (מתרומת הלשכה — בני ישראל), and handed over to the כהן, a servitor of the Sanctuary of the Torah, so that he, in the name of the Torah of that Sanctuary, could teach what position and meaning the uncontrolled physical nature of Man is to have in the sphere of the life of a human society which wishes to allow its life to be lived under the influence of that Torah. It is the כהן — the מכין and מכונן the one who is to “prepare and give direction” to the life of the people — to whom, as such, the פרה אדומה is delivered by the people, and who, accordingly, must present himself בבגדי כהונה in the uniform of such an office and indeed בבגדי לבן in the “white” garments like the High Priest in the service on י״כ. For it is just טהרה, the “purity” demanded by the Torah in the service of which he stands which he is about to demonstrate. והוציא אותה: that is the first lesson which he has to preach by symbolic action: חוץ לשלש מחנות, outside the מחנה שכינה, outside the מחנה לויה, yea, outside the מחנה ישראל has he to lead it out. The פרה אדומה תמימה אשר אין בה מום אשר לא עלה עליה עול, for uncontrolled physical animal nature — not only when it is withered and broken — just in the fulness of vitality and completeness and meant to give service to mankind but which has been left without control there is no place within the Jewish national life of the people. Outside, out of the whole sphere of the life of the people has the priestly servitor of the Sanctuary to lead the פרה וגו׳ אשר לא עלה עליה עול, and has to prepare a place for it (גת) high up the mountain at a distance from but opposite the entrance of the Sanctuary of the Torah.

And והוציא אותה, by itself has it to be led out, no other animal may accompany it, which would only have concrete meaning and would interfere with the purely symbolic meaning of the פרה. Neither may two פרות אדומות be taken out together. Two would give rise to the idea of plurality and it is just animal human nature completely by itself which is to be demonstrated.

ושחט אותה, that is the second lesson which has to be proclaimed by the priest in significant action. In the name of the Sanctuary of the Torah, as whose servitor he stands and to the entrance of which he looks — כנגד פתח ההיכל, see on V.4 — has he to perform the act of שחיטה on the פרה אדומה תמימה אשר אין בה מום אשר לא עלה עליה עול on the “animal” that hitherto had remained without a “yoke” in the “fulness of its vitality and completeness”. He expresses thereby, by that sharp decisive act, that complete mastery by human free will is the one condition under which animality, otherwise to be banned from human circles can, and should, gain admission and have hallowed relationship to the Sanctuary of God. This is the one act of שחיטה which must be done by a כהן and in that it differs essentially from all שחיטות at the offerings in the Sanctuary. At those the שחיטה is not really an עבודה. It is nothing positive which the Sanctuary has to teach and the one who is seeking to get near to God to learn and accept. It is the negative preparatory condition of self-renunciation, giving up living apart and for oneself alone. It is something that the one who is seeking proximity to God must first do to himself before his life (נפש) can be accepted (קבלת הדם I.L.) for devotion to the Sanctuary of God’s Torah. Hence that שחיטה is כשר בזר, may be done by anybody. But here the שחיטה is the real momentous act which symbolises the whole quintessence of what is to be impressed. It is the free human mastery over the physical animal side of his nature, the very opposite of the פרה אשר לא עלה עליה עול, which is to be proclaimed thereby. It was for this that the animal had been given over to the כהן so that just this point should be taught. This שחיטה can only be כשרה בכהן.

ולקח מדמה באצבעו, not in a כלי שרת, not in any vessel at all, in his hand does he receive the blood. For it is not the Sanctuary which is to accept the human personality, the human-נפש, it is the human being himself who is to take the animal-נפש in the power of his free will. In the Sanctuary it is the whole human being who, in his offering, gives himself up to His Sanctuary before the Presence of God. In the פרה אדומה it is the animal in Man which the Man takes in hand before the Sanctuary of God.

והזה אל נכח פני אהל מועד מדמה שבע פעמים, and with ever renewed energy, — על כל הזיה טבילה, he has to dip his finger into the blood afresh at each sprinkling, cf. Levit. 4,6 — seven times, until “completion”, until he has gained the “nearness to bond with God”, has he to impart its direction to the ideal of God’s Torah. שחיטה and הזיה form the most complete expression of moral freedom, mastering physical sensuousness and directing it to the part path of the Divine Law of Morals.

את ערה ואת בשרה וגו׳ ישרף ,ושרף את הפרה: only that which had been directed towards the Divine ideal of morals by human energy, that alone does not become dust, the free-willed power of Man makes that alone escape with him on the path to the ideal conception of morals into the eternal proximity to the bond of God. Everything else falls to the disintegrating elements and becomes dust of ashes even as it came from dust of the earth. But this reverting to dust of the unfree material, no less than the step to God and eternity of the free spiritual, is also solely related to God, is something which lies within the scope of His Purposes for the world and mankind. Both the mortal and the immortal belong to Him, come from Him — just as שחיטה and הזיה, so was גתה, the place for its reversion to ash, also כנגד פתח ההיכל, in view of, and in the direction of the gate of the Sanctuary of the Torah. One and the same God has mixed these two contrasting elements in the nature of Man for one and the same moral goal viz. that just in the struggle against the pressure of physical power to force, the godly power of free will in moral matters in Man’s nature should prevail, and the earthly part of his nature not drag him away from the gates of moral freedom and eternity — שרפה חוץ לגתה פסולה. — Gaining proximity to God on earth, building up an earthly Sanctuary to God by free-willed making His Torah a reality has the combination of both parts of Man’s nature as its goal; the laws of God’s Torah always presuppose the mortal body joined to the immortal part of Man’s being.

ולקח עץ ארז ואזוב ושני תולעת והשליך אל תוך שריפת הפרה: “Cedar”, the highest and strongest, “hyssop”, the lowest and weakest of plant life — “wool dyed with the blood of a worm”, worm and sheep, worm and mammal, the lowest and highest class of animal life — does not this represent the whole of organic life? And when the כהן throws this representation of the whole physical organic world into the fire of the פרה at the moment when the representative of the physical organic part of the nature of human beings is about to become ashes he expresses thereby that the disintegrating elements by which, according to the decree of God, the physical-animal human body reverts to the dust, is nothing more than, or different to, the fate that befalls the whole of the rest of the physical-organic world, and that part of a human being which does ultimately decompose is only that which came from the ordinary organic chemical world to be temporarily joined to his immortal being.

If we look back for a minute, we see the פרה אדומה before the שחיטה, we see it representing the uncontrolled lower, animal element in Man which is against what he was meant to be. With שחיטה, and הזיה and then שריפה a contrast appears in Man viz. his moral element directed towards God, and thereby his נפש escaping the fate of reverting to ash as shown by the דם (= נפש I.L.) of the שחיטה and הזיה, as opposed to the whole of the rest of his bodily element as shown by שריפת עורה בשרה דמה ופרשה. Hence this שריפת הפרה באש is in a totally different relationship to the preceding שחיטה והזיה than the שריפת איברים והאיסורים of the offerings on the fire on the altar is to their preceding שחיטה והזיה. Their burning is a continuation, the result and completion of the שחיטה and מתנות דם. After the נפש, the personality — as represented by the דם — has striven upwards towards the heights of the altar, or alternatively held fast to those heights, then all the efforts and desires of the bodily lower elements (as represented by the אימורים or the איברים) mastered by this נפש (as represented by the שחיטה, I.L.) also achieve what they are meant to be viz. fuel, food (לחם I.L.) for keeping the fires of godliness alive on earth to the satisfaction of God (אשה ריח ניחח לה׳ I.L.). In their case the שחיטה and the שריפה may not be separated, may not be dissociated from one another, it is only the positive idea expressed by the burning that the negative idea of the שחיטה achieves its purpose, and the positive idea of the הקטרה finds its inalienable basis. Both must be done on the same day, and anything left over from the איברים ואימורים which had not been given over to fire on the altar on the same Sanctuary-day, i.e. by the break of the next day becomes פסול בלינה (see Levit. on VII,18, p.210).

But in the פרה the שחיטה and שריפה have a totally different meaning in their relation to one another. Just as the fire, to which the פרה בגתה, the animal on its appointed place on earth is given over, is not אש דת על המזבח, the fire of the Torah on the altar, but the fire of the elements under whose mastery everything organic ultimately reverts to ash and dust, so also the שריפה of the animal is no continuation, not the purpose or completion of the שחיטה and הזיה כנגד פתח ההיכל but has quite a different purpose of its own which runs parallel to the other. It is the future of becoming ash of the body parallel to the future of sanctuary-holiness of the soul. So that the burning may take place on an earlier day and פרה is not פסולה בלינה.

אסיפה. With the burning of the cow the function of the כהן is completed. In the name of the Sanctuary of the Torah (in his priestly garments I.L.) and in full view of it he has demonstrated the double elements in the nature of human beings. By שחיטה and הזיה the human animal element that which can be mastered by the free-willed human energy and wrested upwards with themselves towards God and to the immortal divine free realm of His Torah; and by שריפת הפרה, the bodily animal element that forms their temporary transient substratum and which goes the way of all earthly things to death and ashes. Now it is up to the people of the community, for whom the whole procedure has been done, to keep, in these ashes of the burnt animal, the thought of this fundamental teaching of the two natures which are joined in human beings, the heavenly and the earthly, the godly and the animal, the immortal and the mortal, so that it is always there to be used; the erroneous טומאה-illusion of Man’s lack of freedom of will to be countered by the recognition of this fundamental teaching. ואסף איש טהור, the “gathering” of these ashes was accordingly done by an ordinary man of the public. Himself “pure” he had to deposit this “means of teaching purity” (טהרה-consciousness of the complete freedom of will in moral matters I.L.) in an absolutely pure place. This insistence of “purity” for the gathering and depositing of the ashes is of important significance. For although in itself it represents being subject to death, touching these ashes does not make a person טומאה and they demand the most absolute purity for the place where they are kept. This is a point we shall have to come back to. For it is not in the “death of the mortals” but in identifying the immortal with the mortal in which the pernicious טומאה-error hides, in not differentiating between the immortal and the mortal material which decays, in allowing the dead body to demonstrate the “you must” conception of the whole of Man, and out of the uncontrovertible evidence lying before him gives an affirmative reply to the question asked in surprise: אך הבל כל אדם נצב סלה, “is then the whole of Man completely nothing, however upright he may stand!” (Ps. 39,6). But all that lies there in these ashes does represent “that which dies” in a human being, for the other part, the godly immortal part has already been separated in הזיה כנגד פתח ההיכל, and therefore ואסף איש טהור את אפר הפרה והניח במקום טהור. But nevertheless it must be מחוץ למחנה, outside the מחנה שכינה, the Sanctuary. For it is only when it is joined to the godly element that the animal bodily element in Man has its appointed place in the Sanctuary of God. Separated from it, it belongs to the physical world, which has its sphere outside that of the Sanctuary of God which is dedicated to “Man” as he is meant to be.

But this “ash” is destined to be joined again to “living water”, and then, in that combination to bring home the thought of the “never dying immortal spiritual” being just temporarily combined with the “physical material” which does decay, to all those who have had this thought of the real Man never dying disturbed by having come into contact with a human corpse or part of one; and in this depressed mental state of not being so completely assured that Man is really a free agent, are shut out of the threshold of the Sanctuary and from its holy things. It is to be kept למשמרת למי נדה for the עדת בני ישראל, for the community of Israel, who must stand firmly on the basis of their god-like ability to exercise free will in moral matters, and not in itself, but only through this purpose does it become מי נדה, and as such, to banish the erroneous idea of moral unfreedom, of Man’s not being able to master and control his physical urges, the whole institution of פרה receives the character of חטאת (see above).

מלוי וקידוש: “directly and without any intermediate stage” מים חיים “living” spring water is drawn from the source or from the uninterrupted flowing stream in to a “vessel”, and some of the “ash” is strewn therein. Significantly enough, the “ash” is there (V.17) called עפר (dust, which in Torah-Hebrew is not so much what we call dust, as the upper loose layer of earth or humus as Hirsch explains on Ex. 8,12, I.L.). The ashes to which the organic body crumbles is nothing else but the material from which it originated: עפר אתה ואל עפר תשוב (Gen. 3,19), and it is just as such that it is presented here. What is Man? An immortal being, drawn from the source of eternal life, enclosed in an earthly container. This immortal part, מים חיים is the original primary part, the essential prior condition: מים חיים אל כלי — and to it “earth-dust” עפר is brought, and in such a way that these two elements, confined in an earthly container, are not next to each other or one above the other, but מעורב, the “living” and the earthly components mixed together, and in such a manner that the “living”, the מים חיים is not overcome or absorbed into the “earthly part”, but overpowers it and can be seen through it, contained in it, — עליו מים חיים — it is not something earthly containing life, but life containing something earthly, — עפר שריפת החטאת עליו מים חיים אל כלי, that is what a human being is.

And when the mixture has served its time, the ash-dust sinks to the bottom and the מים חיים appears in its original clarity, וישב העפר אל הארץ כשהיה והרוח תשוב אל האלקים אשר נתנה, “Then shall the dust return to the earth as it was, but the spirit shall return unto God Who gave it”. (Eccl. 12,7) cf. Jeshurun I on פרשת פרה, translated in Grunfeld’s “Judaism Eternal” p.51 et seq. I.L.).

At the moment in which the ash is strewn into the מים חיים, this latter becomes מי חטאת, a medium for teaching the doctrine of the ability not to sin, and this act of the mixing is called “sanctification”, קידוש.

Just as מי סוטה (see above Ch. V.17 I.L.) expresses the fact: although thou art עפר, although thou art provided with organic earthly urges, nevertheless מים קדושים thou art able and hast the power for every moral sanctification of life”, so does מי חטאת express the fact: although thou art אפר, although thou art “earthly ashes” nevertheless thou art מים חיים, life drawn from the source of immortality.

הזיה בשלישי ושביעי. But just as in the מי חטאת, both elements are present, the organic material and the immortal spiritual in — even if temporarily — intimate combination and just in such combination symbolise Man, so is the הזיה, which is to raise him out of the depressing incertitude back to this clear conception of humanity, directed to both these elements of Man’s nature. The consciousness of moral freedom and thereby the ability to subordinate oneself with the whole of one’s being to the laws of God has to form the basis as much for the sphere of one’s physical existence as for the realm of the higher spiritual life. The life of one’s senses, eating, drinking and sex, which belongs to the organic bodily part of Man, no less than the life of thoughts, striving and accomplishing in which the spiritual godly element of Man asserts itself, both require free-willed giving themselves up to the direction of God’s teachings and God’s Laws. So that before one who is טמא מת can rise up again through טבילה to טהרה, after he has lived through his טומאה-period, the fundamental teaching of the freedom of Man’s will has to be brought home to the organic bodily side of Man’s nature as well as to the spiritual godly part by הזיה. This הזיה takes place on the third day and is repeated on the seventh. We have already pointed out, on Gen. 1,11-13 (p.20 in my translation I.L.) how the third day of creation, when the physical organic world came to life stamped with the impression of God’s law of למינו, bears the signature of physical organic life subordinating itself to the laws of God, just as the seventh day stands as the day of Man, with his god-like powers of mastering the matter of the world, placing his use of those powers under the Mastery of God. Hence הזיה on the third day for Man as a physical organic being, and on the seventh, as a spiritual god-like being. The seventh day, the consecration of the spirit, the mind, to the recognition of God, and by human work being subordinated to God, and the third day the consecration of the body, keeping it within the moral limits of the Law of God. The consecration of the spirit, the mind cannot be achieved without the consecration of the body, so much so, that on whatever day the first הזאה may have taken place, even if done later, that day is always reckoned as being the third day, and four days must pass for the second הזאה to be done on the “seventh”. But that the הזיה with the מי חטאת does look back to the Creation, and consequently the days on which it is to be done get their character from it, is not such a far-fetched idea, is borne out by this עפר .עליו מים חיים אל כלי being — as we believe to have understood it — a representation of Man as he was created.

So that the first הזיה on the third day is a preparation of the physical bodily nature of Man, and the second on the seventh day, of his spiritual godly nature for the true “purity” of the human being, before by ultimate טבילה he can rise in his entirety and with all his appurtenances (הזיה וטבילה על אדם וכלים) back to complete “purity”.

It remains for us to consider certain details of the general laws which affect the פרה-institution, and in themselves, and partly in their relation to each other, profoundly characterise it. The third chapter of תוספתא פרה sums them up as follows:- כל מעשיה ביום חוץ מאסיפת האפר והמילוי והקידוש כל מעשיה בכהנים חוץ מאסיפת האפר והמילוי והקידוש והזיה וכל .מעשיה מלאכה פוסלת חוץ מאסיפה והזיה

ביום. Apart from gathering up the ashes, drawing the water into a vessel and putting the ashes into it, all the procedures of the פרה must take place in the day time. We have repeatedly noted that all actions which belong to the sphere of conscious, wakeful, free-willed human life, in contrast to pertaining to the realm of the powers of the unfree physical world, have to be done in the day-time. We can accordingly understand this demand being made for all the principle acts of the פרה-institution, which are so pregnant with teachings. But מלוי ,אסיפה and קידוש preach nothing in themselves, and are only acts necessary for the making of the מי חטאת, so that the time in which they are done is quite immaterial. If, as is the case according to one version in the ספרי (see on V.3), the שריפה also may be done during the night, that too would be very characteristic for the way we have taken the meaning of that act to be. For we believed that we saw in this change of the whole of the פרה — with the exception of its blood sprinkled towards the Sanctuary — into ashes only a representation of the way all matter belonging to physical nature reverts ultimately to its elements.
