A procedure which would be all the more significantly impressed with the meaning of its referring to the physical elementary world just by its not being restricted to the day-time.

כהן. As already remarked on V.9, proclamation to be made in the name of the Sanctuary of the Torah of the fundamental axioms of moral freedom, of both parts of the human being unitedly belonging to the one conception of God and His Sanctuary, and of its being only the physical material part that reverts to its elements in death, is concluded with the הזיה ,שחיטה and שריפה. So that all the further procedures:- ,קידוש ,מלוי ,אסיפה הזיה can be done by a layman.

מלאכה. The meaning of the פסול מלאכה is not so clearly apparent and the difficulty of understanding it is increased by the fact, as remarked on V.17, that opinions differ over certain modifications of the application of this law; and especially as it is not decided whether פסול מלאכה and היסרו הדעת are identical or two separate concepts. Accepting the latter idea, we should have the law that all the procedures of the פרה-institution — excepting אסיפה and הזיה (but see on V.3) — demand that one’s thoughts must be intensively and exclusively concentrated on what is to be done, a momentary diversion, היסח הדעת, would render the whole act invalid. And equally so, during the carrying out of all the procedures — excepting אסיפה and הזיה — no other מלאכה may be done at the same time by the one who is performing it. This essential intentional concentration of the mind while doing the various acts of the פרה-institution is expressed in the text by ושהם אותה לפניו — לפניו, — by ושרף את — לעיניו הפרה לעיניו, — and by למשמרת למי נדה — שמירה —. So that the activity of the mind is expressed as being threefold, the intention, the purpose desired to accomplish, what it is thinking about, לפניו; paying attention to the object concerned, לעיניו; keeping up the concentration, שמירה. When we consider that שחיטה and הזיה represent the god-like free element in Man that exercises self-control and devotes itself to the purpose of God; שריפה, on the other hand, represents the way of dissolution to which only the unfree material element is subject; and מלוי וקדוש finally, the normal combination of these two contrasting elements to a human being with the one purpose of sanctification, then we can understand the differentation of dividing these modes of using the intelligence between these different functions. The morally free שחיטה והזיה activity demands פנים, directing of the whole energy of the mind to a purpose to be accomplished. The dissolution of the material, the שריפה, only objective observation, עינים. The normal מלוי וקידוש, the two contrasting elements being joined in a pure human being, that a human being does consist of these two contrasting elements, is just that which is to be grasped and held firmly and retained carefully in the mind, hence שמירה. But when we consider that here דעת, the activity of the intelligence is not only something which should be exercised, נלצוה, but is מעכב essential, and היסח הדעת, that even only a momentary cessation of its being concentrated on the procedure renders the whole act invalid, then “דעת״, “intelligent understanding” must be taken to be a component part of what is to be effected by the proceedings. From this point of view, taking פסול מלאכה to be a different concept from היסח הדעת would be all the more understandable. For doing another מלאכה at the same time would give — as we thought — the appearance of the act of the פרה-institution being something casual, and what is wanted to be expressed is that it is not היסח הדעת and not מלאכה אחרת, not “done without thought”, not “just casually” which is the השגחה of Him — to Whose Breath of Eternal Life breathed into human beings the מים חיים refers us — under which the thoughts and intentions of mankind flourish. The act of the הזיה itself does not become invalid by מלאכה אחרת. It must be directed with full intention on the object requiring טהרה but the object itself and the one who performs the act may, at the moment of its being done, be doing something else at the same time. As the act can be performed by any sane man and מלאכה אחרת does not render it invalid, the מים חיים ועפר could represent to him as well as to the one requiring טהרה nothing special, but just the ordinary normal condition of life which every sane man would bring to the notice of everybody else to whom the specific difference which yawns between an empty dead body and a living human one with the soul still inhabiting it is to be brought. It remains to ascertain the reason why women are excluded from doing the הזיה while the text itself allows even a child to do, whereas women may do the קידוש which children may not. (see below).

טומאה. But the peculiar laws of טומאה which occur at the various phases of the פרה-institution must be of the deepest significance. We find that כל העוסקים בפרה מתחלה עד סוף מטמאין בגדים, all those that take active part in the פרה from beginning to the end, i.e. at the ,שריפה ,הזיה ,שחיטה אסיפת האפר ,השלכת עץ ארז become טמא to the degree that they make all כלים which they touch during such activity טמא, quite similarly to נושא נבלה (Levit. 11,25), but touching the פרה or the ashes does not make the person who does so טמא. (Verses 7, 8, & 10).

On the other hand כל עוסקים במלוי וקידוש והזיה, all those that take an active part in the drawing of the water and mixing in the ashes for the purpose of the sprinkling and also the one who does the sprinkling itself do not become טמא thereby, while touching the מי חטאת not for the purpose of sprinkling does make טמא, and if אין בה כדי הזיה only במגע but if יש בה כדי הזיה even במשא לטמא בגדים.

Taking active part in the execution of the פרה-institution as well as touching the מי חטאת only inflicts טומאה when they are כשרים, but as soon as the פרה or the מי חטאת become פסולים, occupying oneself with it, or respectively touching it does not make them טמא.
Touching the water or the ashes before they are mixed does not make טמא, only when they have become מקודשים by being mixed does touching them not for the purpose of sprinkling inflict טומאה.

This last law, that מזה מי חטאת טהור, the one who sprinkles the water mixture remains טהור but נוגע ונושא מי חטאת touching or moving it not for the purpose of sprinkling makes טמא could offer the key to the whole problem. The whole process, as indeed it expresses in its end product, the מים חיים ועפר of the מי חטאת brings to mind the two contrasting factors combined in human beings, that which goes on living for ever and that which is subject to death. The consciousness of these contrasting factors is of importance to re-establish the consciousness of the ability for the exercise of moral freedom of will where the confidence of this has been disturbed by contact with the dead body of a human being. There the one factor of human life, the fact that one is not free, that no amount of willpower can prevent death, is clearly demonstrated, and it is curative medicine in the מי חטאת with its מים חיים containing the עפר, to bring to mind the other factor, the never-dying free element in contrast as a no less certain fact. But that which is medicine for the sick troubled mind is the very opposite, poison, for the untroubled healthy mind. The untroubled normal existence is not lived thinking of this contrast. In normal untroubled life this contrast is altogether in abeyance, should be so, the thought of death is not to lurk constantly next to the thought of life, the thought of life to pulsate constantly next to the thought of death, feelings of death, thoughts of corpses are altogether not to be present — the normal, pure, undisturbed beat of the pulse is entirely that of life. The spirit of God in Man raises the material body, which it quickens and masters, up with it and makes it participate in the eternity which lies in every pure moment of the life of human beings. Not consisting of two parts, undivided does the pure human being feel itself, and the consciousness of the contrasting elements in his being is itself a disturbance of what is, and should be, his normal temperament. מי חטאת is medicine, not bread. As surely therefore as bringing to mind the מים חיים in which the עפר is temporarily mixed in the מי חטאת helps to bring back from death a mind which has been infected by the thoughts which contact with a human corpse have given it, and accordingly handling the מי חטאת for such a purpose is a medium for טהרה and leaves the bringer טהור, so surely does any other touching or handling the מי חטאת by a normal person, uninfected by thoughts of dead bodies, bring to his mind the thought of his dual nature, of the עפר in the מים חיים in the מי חטאת, of the fact that willy-nilly he will have to die, and makes him טמא. In any case the sprinkling with the מים חיים ועפר of the מי חטאת does not effect immediate טהרה, the טמא is still as טמא as he was before. The הזיה-thought which brings the contrasting elements in a human being in the right relation to one another is only a preparation for טהרה, it preaches to human beings:- although thou art עפר and wilt become אפר, still it is מים חיים which is the real, most lasting element of thy being which can never be lost. But טהור, “pure” does he become only when he then immerses himself entirely, with the “whole” of his being, in the element of purity, and with the setting of the sun with the passing of the day, puts all thoughts of dead bodies behind him, and he enters a new fresh pure day, free from all ideas of contrasts within himself.

Ganz denselben Gedanken spricht die טומאה-Bestimmung für alle die an dem Vollzuge des פרה-Aktes Beteiligten aus. Dieser Akt mit seiner שחיטה והזיה einerseits und שריפה ואסיפה andererseits spricht ja eben in größter Augenfälligkeit diesen Gegensatz des ewig-freien und vergänglich-gebundenen Elementes im Menschenwesen aus. Es spricht ihn aus ohne vorliegende Veranlassung als allgemeinstes Bedürfnis, und führt eben damit alle die עוסקים בפרה מתחלה ועד סוף erst ganz eigentlich in den Gedanken dieser Gegensätzlichkeit ein, unterbricht damit ihr einheitliches Reinheitsbewusstsein, macht sie טמא. Nicht das Gegensätzliche des פרה אדומה-Gedankens ist das Normale, in welchem das Heiligtum und seine Heiligtümer die Lösung ihrer Aufgabe erwarten. Todesbetrachtungen wohnen nicht auf ihrer Schwelle. Bevor die an dem פרה אדומהAkte sich Beteiligenden dem Heiligtume und den Heiligtümern sich wieder nahen, haben sie die durch den Akt, den sie mit vollziehen, geweckten gegensätzlichen Gedanken hinter sich zu lassen und müssen erst in טבילה und הערב שמש die Einheitlichkeit des reinen Lebensgedankens wieder gewonnen haben.

The fact that פרה and מי חטאת are no longer מטמא once they have become פסולים requires no explanation. If they become פסול they obviously have no longer any symbolic meaning and revert to their concrete character, and as ordinary water and ash have no reason at all to be מטמא.

Equally so it is self-understandable that the אפר by itself and, even more so, the מים חיים by itself are טהורים. The process of decay, of reverting to its elements, of all organic matter is in itself a completely true pure thought, to which no breath of the erroneous conception of טומאה clings.

Finally, the law which applies to the whole פרה-institution: טבול יום כשר בפרה. The degree of טהרה which the law demands for all those who take part in the acts of the פרה as well as of the sprinkling is only of the lowest degree achieved by the טבילה before the טהרה is completed by הערב שמש. This Halacha, which was strenuously opposed by the Sadducees who refused to accept the traditional explanations of the Torah, was upheld with the greatest publicity whenever the occasion arose, in order to demonstrate the falsity of the Sadducean teachings. The functioning priest, before the beginning of the act went to the Mount of Olives, and in full view of the public was made טמא for the day, so that he would first have to undertake טבילה and could only start his function with the פרה as טבול יום. But then, so that through this publicly bringing the functioning priest into a condition of טומאה removable by טבילה the whole פרה act should not essentially suffer in its character of a טהרה institution, and might even be misrepresented into the very opposite — כי היכי דלא ליזלזלו בה — the most elaborate precautions involving great sacrifices were instituted with the greatest publicity to ensure the prevention of the most far-fetched shadow of doubt of any possibility of the priest in question becoming טמא למת, and to vindicate the character of absolute טהרה of the whole process. Imagine the elaborateness of these precautions. Closed-in courtyards were built for this purpose on vaulted rocks to do away with any טומאה רצוצה (see above) coming up from the depths. In these, women who were near the end of their pregnancy waited, and boys who were born there were brought up until their seventh or eighth year so that these boys who could never have been touched by טומאה could perform the sprinklings on the person for whom the functioning priest had prepared himself. Imagine how elaborate these טהרה arrangements are, and then tell ourselves that they are only made after having kept the priest who is appointed to perform the פרה with the most scrupulous care in a state of טהרה for seven days, and then at the moment when he is to act, brought into contact with טומאה so that he should require טבילה and after the טבילה perform the פרה-act only as טבול יום — and all these elaborate and expensive arrangements only להוציא מלבן של צדוקים to oppose the Sadducean assertion that only במעורבי שמש, only priests who were completely טהורים were qualified to perform the פרה-act; then it seems to us that there must be some deep significance innate in the sentence טבול יום כשר בפרה for such imposing national arrangements to be worth while for its public proclamation.

If we really look at this sentence, we see that the axiom on which it is based must be that the concept טהור must form the complete contrast to טמא not only with completed טהרה but already in its very first stage. According to Sadducean claims by והזה הטהור על הטמא only the completely טהור is to be understood. But the tradition of our sages teaches that already in טבול יום the טהור is placed in full contrast to the טמא. According to the Sadducean claim, between טבול יום and טמא there is only a quantitative degree of difference between טבול יום and טמא and the specific difference in kind between them only begins with הערב שמש. According to the tradition of our sages, the complete specific difference in kind of טהור to טמא is given by טבול יום and between טבול יום and הערב שמש there is only a quantitative difference of degree. Transposing this to the sphere of the thoughts of the fundamental teachings to be proclaimed by the פרה-institution it would follow, according to Sadducean pride, that the sentence would read: that only mental and moral perfection is free and immortal, everything on a lower stage still belongs to the transient perishable realm of physical force and lack of free will. But the teaching of the sages says: Even on the lowest stage, in every human being the divine freedom of will exists that divides him sharply from all physical transitoriness and makes him participate in moral freedom and eternal life. Only difference in degree exists between him and the very height of spiritual and moral perfection. According to the erroneous Sadducean teaching immortality and eternity is an ideal which could only be attained through spiritual and moral perfection, so that — perhaps — it is unattainable by human beings. According to the wisdom of our sages, immortality and eternity is a gift innate in the being of a human being which God gives to every one at his entrance into this world, a gift whch enables him to wander in the land of forced, bound evanescence on the path of freedom which leads to homecoming to eternity in the higher perfection. — Is the thought very far that the Sadducean opposition with its במעורבי שמש היתה נעשית is in deep connection with their opposition to the עולם הבא teaching of those same sages?

We are very much inclined to believe that the admissibility of boys, yea of a child for הזיה (to which we have already mentioned) see Para. 12,10, is connected with this admissability of a טבול יום. It is the same wisdom which sees the טהור already in the טבול יום, the “pure” already in the beginning of purity, which also allows one to see the future “man” in the child, and qualifies even a קטן טבול יום to demonstrate the deep yawning difference of life from death, of a human being from a dead body. The same idea which is laid down in the admissability of the טבול יום also teaches the admissability of the קטן, just as by והזה הטהור על הטמא the concept טהור for פרה is extended to טבול יום, so Yoma 43a, teaches ולקח אזוב וטבל במים איש טהור איש ולא אשה טהור להכשיר את הקטן.

That אשה כשרה לקידוש ופסולה להזיה could perhaps be in connection with the fact that קידוש כשר בלילה while הזיה is limited to day time so that it is a כתנות עשה which can only be done in a limited period שהזמן גרמא. Inasmuch as the law restricts הזיה to day time it ranks it in the sphere of those procedures which are to be understood as proclaiming those Truths on which the whole of Jewish life rests, the representation of which and the duty of transmitting them from generation to generation is the mission of the male sex in Israel (זכר I.L.); the Jewish boy as the future man responsible for the representation of Jewish Truths cannot be introduced early enough into the circle of those who recognise this particularly fundamental Truth of all fundamental Truths. As far as we know, הזיה במי חטאת is the absolutely only case for which קטנים are allowed to perform a מצוה and נשים precluded.

V. 1. ויבאו וגו׳, the addition of כל העדה can hardly want to tell us that all the people came into the Wilderness of Zin and none stayed behind. Apart from the fact that there was no point in specially mentioning כל העדה, the whole congregation, even if it did wish to say so, it would simply say ויבאו עדת בני ישראל as it does in Ex. 16,1, and even then designating the nation as an עדה would have its special motive (see there). But here this idea is quite specially stressed as כל העדה. After it had mentioned the בני ישראל they are then characterised as כל העדה. The בני ישראל who entered the Wilderness of Zin were כל העדה, “the whole congregation”. They were now united in the same common destiny — for that is the concept of the term עדה —; the fate to which some had been destined in Ch. 14,29-35 had already been fulfilled. All those that entered the Wilderness of Zin were the עדה who now were to enter the new future. עדה השלמה as the מ״ד explains the same term on V.22 (see there) שנכנסה לארץ .לפי שמתו יוצאי מצרים ואלו מן שכתוב בהן חיים כולכם היום
בחדש הראשן, at a time when the land of an inhabited country displays all the promise of coming fruit by the beauty of blossom.

וישב העם בקדש not ויחן, they encamped, as the stay in the temporary resting places on their wanderings was always designated, but וישב, the term for settling down, as in Ch. 21,2 5 & 31. Kadesh is called in V.16, עיר קצה גבולך, a city at the border of the Edomite territory, and even if they were probably not in the actual city of Kadesh they were already in the province which bore its name. The people accordingly believed themselves to be already at the end of their wanderings in the wilderness, and in Kadesh, after their forty years of wandering, to have come at last to habitable and inhabited places. וישב העם בקדש, in such feelings they settled down there. They believed they had reached their goal.

ותמת שם מרים ותקבר שם. There Miriam died, and there she was buried. She had completed her mission on earth. Her grave in Kadesh could tell future generations that she did not leave this world until the new young generation stood ready to enter the Promised Land. And if it was the women that took least part in the repeated despairing defections from God during the wanderings so rich in such sad experiences, if it was mostly the women that kept up cheerful and patient devotion to God, so that the women were not included in the fateful decree of having to die in the wilderness — according to מ״ר on Numb. 27,1 — and so, as mothers and grandmothers, could bring over into the new generation personal recollections of the past in Egypt and the glorious personal experiences of the Exodus and the subsequent living under the direct protection and guidance of God, and impregnate their grandchildren and great-grandchildren with the spirit of these God-revealing experiences, then no small part of their being endowed with the true Jewish spirit must be ascribed to their brilliant leader and prophetess Miriam and her shining example ever before them (see on Ex. 15,20). But probably it is not for nothing that this chapter, which records so curtly and simply the deaths of Miriam and Aaron, is preceded by the great פרה אדומה chapter of the Jewish teaching of immortality. That chapter is itself an introduction to these deaths and says: That which was Miriam in Miriam, Aaron in Aaron, that did not die. Just as their work here below lives on immortally in all the succeeding generations of the nation, so their own real selves did not die, but went back out of earthly transience into eternity to God, the source of all life. And if the words of our sages (Moed Katon 28a) teach: למה נסמכה מיתת מרים לפרשת פרה אדומה לומר לך מה פרה אדומה מכפרת אף מיתתן של צדיקים מכפרת the proximity of these two chapters to each other teaches that in the death of the righteous there is innate a power for producing atonement similar to the חטאת effect of the פרה אדומה, this can well be meant in the sense that just as the פרה אדומה institution teaches immortality and the moral freedom of will of the godlike nature of Man, so does the death of the righteous directly teach both. For truly he must be spiritually blind to whom the death of a צדיק, a truly righteous man, does not preach the most vehement sermon on immortality, who can see in that which lies dead and motionless before him bearing traces of decay, the same person who so recently was occupied with spiritual strength and all the force of free moral powers of thought and will, who can see in the corpse of a צדיק anything other than the empty cloak, cast into the corner, of a man who has departed from here.

V. 2. ולא היה מים לעדה. We have already remarked on Ex. XVII5, that the well which was opened from the rock at Choreb did not only satisfy the requirements of the moment but accompanied them on all their subsequent wanderings in the wilderness, and in fact we do not hear any complaints again about the water supply all the time in the wilderness. But now, according to Taanith 9a, immediately after Miriam’s death, the well dried up, and the עדה, the people who for the first time felt themselves “the congregation of the future” found themselves deprived of the very first necessity for their continued existence, were without water. ולא היה מים לעדה! By reason of this sequence ותמת שם מרים ולא היה מים לעדה, the benefit they enjoyed hitherto of having the Choreb-Well accompanying them is (ibid.) ascribed to the merit of Miriam, באר בזכות מרים. What Miriam’s quiet unobtrusive work for the moral future of the people, and how much her death was a national loss is announced immediately by the drying up of the Choreb-well after her death.

V. 3. וירב העם, just העם, of whom it had just said וישב העם בקדש, that they greeted Kadesh as their first return to an inhabitable country, felt their hopes dashed to the ground by the sudden lack of water which they had not experienced in all their wanderings in the wilderness and felt that they had been betrayed by Moses and Aaron. Hence וירב העם עם משה. —  ולו גוענו וגו׳. By the term גויעה, the easiest most peaceful death (see Gen. 6,17), they designated the death of all those who died in the wilderness to whom the decree of God had denied entry into the Land. They had all died לפני ה׳, God’s care had not forsaken them right to their last breath. Their deaths went the way of the natural mortality of human beings without being brought about by any dreadful calamity — but we are to perish by thirst!

V. 4. ולמה הבאתם this cannot be God’s Will, this is what you have brought about, by this you are acting treacherously towards קהל ה׳. God wishes to keep us, His intention is for us to remain alive and enter the Promised Land but you have brought this whole קהל, this whole human company belonging to God, whom God wished to have the happiest future, into this desert so that they and their beasts may die the most terrible death. The term בעיר is chosen meaningly, it represents animals under the mastery of their natural urges (see Ex. 12,4), here the urgent imperative need to drink. The reproach runs: Even for the sake of our animals you should have refrained from doing this, should have had pity for the poor blameless creatures!

V. 5. ולמה העליתנו וגו׳. The decree that we were to wander in the wilderness is finished. We should already be entering the promised blooming land which in this time of Spring must be glorious with all the beauty of blossom and bud — what a contrast to this place to which you have brought us, where there is not even a drop of water for us to drink! This is not the Will of God, this is your doing.

V. 6. ויבא וגו׳ מפני וגו׳. Cf. Gen. 7,9: ויבא נח וגו׳ אל התבה מפני מי המבול; Is. 2,19 & 21 במערות וגו׳ מפני וגו׳ לבא בנקרת הצורים וגו׳ מפני פחד ה׳ וגו׳. They made no answer, they fled for refuge to the Tent of Appointed Meeting as always when there was a question whether their mission was really given and directed by God.

V. 8. קח את המטה וגו׳. Since the victory over Amalek (Ex. 17,9) we do not find the staff in Moses’ hands again. It had been deposited, as we see from V.9, “before God”, i.e. in the Sanctuary next to the ארון העדות. The staff of God in the hands of Moses designates him as being sent by God. A movement with that staff, a waving, a blow with it before an announced event takes place proclaims that event to be the result of a momentary direct intervening act of God. They had reproached Moses and Aaron with betraying their mission from God. It was not in accordance with God’s Will or Direction that they had led them to this waterless place, that had occurred through the malevolence of Moses and Aaron, God cannot wish them to die of thirst. “Take the staff” says God to Moses, “show them that you are still My messenger, have not ceased for one moment to be My servitor, והקהל את העדה, and on the strength of the staff in your proclaiming your mission as coming from Me, gather this “congregation of the future” together ודברתם אל הסלע לעיניהם, but do not use the staff, לעיניהם, in presence of the whole nation you are to demand the rock merely with words — no use of the staff — to yield up מימיו, its waters, the water which is already there. A blow with the staff, as in Ex. 17,6, would give the impression that the water came as the result of a fresh intervention of God in response to their uproar, and that was just what it was not to be. They are to be made to see that it was not Moses and Aaron but God Who had led them to this place, and His cloud which had directed them hither, that it was not just their stormy agitation that necessitated and caused the intervention of God, but rather that the required water was already provided by God at the place to which He had directed them, and that it merely required a word from Moses and Aaron to the rock which would suffice for it to produce the water which God had placed ready for them, ונתן מימיו; accordingly והוצאת וגו׳ והשקית וגו׳ without any fresh miracle, simply with a word from you, you are to provide them with a sufficiency for their undeniably present requirements.”

This manner of obtaining the water from the rock would have convinced the people of the deep wrong they had done in accusing Moses and Aaron of leading them to this waterless place against the will of God; whereas the water gushing forth only as the result of a blow with the staff could still leave room for the assumption that their having been led into the Wilderness of Zin was originally a wilful arbitrary act on the part of Moses and Aaron, and only subsequently their justified revolt and their pressing need brought about the merciful miracle of God. It would have taught the people that under the guidance of God one can dismiss all worries from one’s mind, and even without the miracle-causing staff of Moses can be confident at all times of the right help coming at the right time. It would, — as I once heard the explanation given by the late lamented Bernays נ״ע — just at the border of the Promised Land and the new future awaiting them when the visible constant miracles of God’s guidance during their wanderings were henceforth to be replaced by the invisible but no less miraculous נסים נסתרים of God’s no less closer guidance, have brought this home to the people. It would have taught them that that which hitherto the staff of Moses had been, henceforth the word of Moses is to be for all future time. And if — according to the profound way our sages take it — the wandering in the wilderness started with the Mara miracle, which was to equip them with the experience that דבר מן התורה, a word of the Torah is sufficient to sweeten the bitterest water (see Ex. 15,25), then the wandering in the wilderness was to have been concluded, and the new future started, with the experience that the word of Moses suffices to bring the fresh draught of life out of the hard rock.
V. 9. ויקח משה את המטה מלפני ה׳ וגו׳ (see V.8).

V. 10—11. יקהלו וגו׳ ויאמר וגו׳ וירם וגו׳. May we dare to try and follow the track of his mind, and imagine what the emotions must have been to have been able to make a Moses — that most faithful servant of God, of whom God Himself testified בכל ביתי נאמן הוא — deviate, in one moment of his life, from exactly carrying out a mission given him by God? Our conjecture is:- At God’s command, Moses took the staff again in his hand out of the Sanctuary where it had reposed for nearly forty years, and with this badge of his mission coming from God, he assembled the nation. But when, after nearly forty years, he saw himself directed to the people with the staff of God again in his hand, the staff which nearly forty years ago he had required for the people as testimony and credential of his mission (see Ex. 4,1-15 & 17), it hurt him grievously to think that in all these forty years, and with all that he had done in those forty years, he had still not won the confidence and trust of his people, and in the bitterness of these feelings he forgot his orders, and spoke, instead of quietly addressing the rock, words of deep reproach to the people, and in passionate agitation struck the rock — whereupon water in abundance gushed forth and satisfied the thirst of the people and their animals.

But the reproach was worded: שמעו נא המורים וגו׳. We have already on Gen. 26,35 recognised the fundamental meaning of the root מרה to be: “to go in the opposite direction” (hence also מרה a razor which must go at the right angle against the hair). We have an English word for behaviour which is derived from an exactly similar conception viz., “untowards”. Now, although מרה chiefly refers to actions and designates both positive and negative acts of disobedience, it does also occur as a term for general behaviour and a condition of completely opposing wishes and expectations. Thus, of a condition of wretchedness where everything wished for is denied, it says עני ישראל מרה מאוד (Kings II. 14,26) (“For God saw the affliction of Israel was extremely bitter I.L.). Thus Job describes his complaints as גם יום מרי שיחי ,מרי (XXIII,2), he could not formulate his complaints in accordance with the wishes of his friends for ידי כבדה על אנחותי the trouble that had overtaken him was too heavy to be expressed by his groans; and Is. 50,5, ה׳ אלקים פתח לי אזן ואנכי לא מריתי, “God hath opened mine ear and I have shown myself not unapproachable.” This being inaccessible for teachings he calls מרה. Here, too, המרים would not mean specially disobedient, for in what they did there was no act of direct disobedience. But it would refer rather to their intractability and to their general behaviour not being in accordance with what one was justified in expecting of them, but especially in their irresponsiveness to all the teachings which, after all, must have been impressed upon them by the wonderful imposing experiences they had had. In this sense then could the various meanings be taken which the מ״ר gives, the שימין הרבה to the term המרים, according to which the reproach המרים means ,סרבנים, שוטים, מורי חצים מלמדים את מלמדיהם, disobedience, lack of understanding, conceit, quarrelsomeness, wishing to teach their teachers. It cannot wish to express disobedience in the narrow sense of the word, but — general resistant obstinacy. — המן הסלע הזה נוציא לכם מים. We think this question is to be taken: could we bring water for you out of this rock? i.e. you have reproached us as if we had brought you “into this wilderness, this evil place where there is not even water”. All right then, but if then at our word, as we have been commanded, this rock, before which you stand, gives you the required water, will you then cease to be מרים, would you then at last be open to the conviction that altogether it was not we but God Who had led you here? By these words, Moses had not yet departed in any way from the orders he had received. What he said was quite a suitable preparation for that which was to occur לעיניהם before their eyes and for their instruction. It was only the passionate manner, the excitement in which they were spoken, and which then led him to impulsive vehement raising the rod in his hand and smiting the rock in which the wrong consisted.

V. 12. יען לא האמנתם בי להקדישני. If we have not gone completely wrong in the way we have taken the episode up to now, if Moses’s excitement sprang from the bitter feeling that the whole of his devoted work for the people had been in vain, that the attitude of the people towards him was still that of המרים, no confidence, no response to efforts to alter their minds to being more fully convinced; if such an excitement could be regarded as a stressing of his own personality not quite in keeping with the frame of mind of a Moses, and which should in all cases recede into the background in consideration of his mission coming from God, and — surely the hardest of all trials — should never have lost patience as long as God remained patient; if one cannot take away from it a momentary doubt existing in Moses’s mind of the ultimate success of God’s mission of the people being finally won over to accomplish their mission and purpose on earth; should not all this together be able to be taken as a momentary sinking of the אמונה which holds fast and firmly on to God and His purposes however much appearances seem to be antagonistic, and which proves itself most of all in trying to find the fault in the messenger himself for a mission of God which goes — or seems to be going — awry. And should not then the opposite demand; the demand never for a moment to lose consciousness of God being the decisive One Whom nothing can hinder in absolutely achieving His purpose, and from this consciousness being never misled by whatever happens, the demand for a messenger of God to be like His holy angels with covered eyes (not looking at what is before them I.L.) with covered feet (not caring where they are going I.L.) only active in flying to accomplish their mission, should not this demand be able to be regarded as the highest form of קידוש השם? And from that point of view does not האמנתם בי להקדישני hit the very essence of the lapse, the impatient passion of Moses, in its real innermost nature?

But who could dare to fill in the unspoken reason for the connection which joins the יען to the לכן, or to express exactly the similar lapse which in God’s eyes made Aaron appear equally guilty and deserving of the same verdict. But the impressive fact remains that, on account of such a small, easily to be understood, momentary weakness in their אמונה, the leaders had to suffer the same fate that was meted to the generation of the wilderness for their continuous lack of אמונה. The grave of the great leader at the very border of the Promised Land to which he had at last brought his people, next to the graves of those who died in the wilderness, now bears everlasting witness to the impartial justice of the Divine rule, in the scales of which the slightest errors of the great saintly men, so close to God in their service, weigh equally to the worst sins of ordinary mortals. It shows itself in the whole קדושה of its absolute greatness in giving up even a Moses and an Aaron for the further accomplishing of its work, its goal is dependent on nothing but itself and even a Moses or an Aaron are not indispensable for it. In later years, when one of Israel’s national hymns wishes to sing of God’s קדושה, to describe graphically His unapproachable eminence and sublimity; how His Throne above the Cherubin who protect His Law would have to shatter the world in the ways it had hitherto gone; what greatness, what fecundity, what holiness is innate in acknowledging His Name; how His Might loveth Right, and wishes to beget equity — justice and love — in us; how the thought קדוש הוא “He is holy” demands the complete devotion of the whole of ourselves to His Torah: then it directs us to Moses and Aaron, makes us consider how Moses and Aaron were the most eminent amongst His servitors, Samuel amongst those that call upon His Name, who prayed for others and were sure of being answered, to whom God spoke in the cloudy pillar, who were the watchers over His testimonies and receivers of His ordinances, to whom God listened and to whose entreaties for others God showed Himself a forgiving God……… and yet for their own lapses He had no forgiveness: רוממו ה׳ אלקינו והשתחוו להר קדשו כי קדוש ה׳ אלקינו (Ps. XCIX.).

V. 13. בם .ויקדש בם probably refers to Moses and Aaron who are named in the previous verse, and this sanctification is to be understood in the sense of קידוש השם, as worked out on V.12. The death of Moses and Aaron in the wilderness places the final and most lasting seal on the “godliness” of their mission, of its being entirely “God-sent”. It demonstrates to us, through them, the most inviolable holiness and untouchable exactness of the Will of God which He has revealed to us for the life in the world He wishes us to lead. רוממו ה׳ אלקינו והשתחוו להר קדשו כי קדוש ה׳ אלקינו sounds through the world as a warning cry from their graves through all time and space to all the generations of their people.

But deeply significant is the juxtaposition of בני ישראל and בם in this verse. The children of Israel had contended with God……… and Moses and Aaron were sentenced to death. It is just this contrast which proclaims the קדושת ה׳ in the whole of its greatness (see on V.12).
The המה differentiates between these מריבה of this fortieth year and those of the first year (Ex. Ch. XVII).

V. 14. וישלח. Undaunted, not disconcerted by the fate that hung over him, which denied him personally the prospect of reaching the long-pursued goal, Moses carried on, energetically to fulfil his mission for as long as God would let him live with his people. — אחיך ישראל, he reminded him of their common descent; according to מ״ר, at the same time of the different fortunes which had befallen the twin branches of the Abrahamitic stem.

V. 15. ולאבותינו. It was not just this recent generation coming out of Egypt of whom you could possibly think that they had somehow deserved the treatment they received but it had begun already with our forefathers whose honest characters would be known to you by tradition. It was accordingly an outrageous wrong brutally decreed against our whole people as such, to be handed on from the one generation to the next.

V. 17. ולא נשתה מי באר: We will not touch any private property. דרך המלך: a road laid down by the “crown” i.e. the state, a road belonging to the public, no private property, perhaps not even the property of the local commune, strictly the open high road.

V. 19. ויאמרו וגו׳ במסלה נעלה. The meaning הסתולל (Ex. 9,17) to exalt oneself, סלסל (Prov. 4,8) to raise up, סוללה (Jer. 6,6) cast up wood to make an attack on a city, also סלם (Gen. 28,12) a ladder, all leave no doubt that the fundamental meaning of סלל is raising up. מסלה would accordingly be a road leading upwards. And we find other examples of מסלה being construed, as it is here, with the concept of עלה. Thus, for example, מסלה העולה בית אל (Judges 21,19). The road going eastward from the Philistine coast mounts upward (Sam. I. 6,9) hence ,אם דרך גבולו יעלה וגו׳, and this road is (V.12 there) called מסלה. In Chron. I. 26,16) we find במסלה העולה משמר. Also מסלת שדה כובס (Is. 7,3, XXXVI,2) seems to be a road climbing uphill. In Kings II. 18,17, it says, speaking of it:- ויעלו ויבאו ירושלים, ויעלו ויבאו ויעמדו בתעלת ברכה העליונה במסלת שדה כובס. The road from Jerusalem to שדה כובס is accordingly described as עליה. According to all this, we believe that here too the מסלה which they asked at their second petition, to be allowed to use, was a mountain road. The land of Edom, Seir, is quite definitely a mountainous region, the whole land is therefore also called הר שעיר. There were two routes through Edom to Palestine. The more convenient one, leading through valleys was the דרך המלך, the highroad, to the right and left of which were fields and vineyards and by which wells had been dug. The use of this route was the first request which Moses sent; hence the self-imposed condition attached, לא נעבר בשדה וכרם ולא נשתה מי באר דרך המלך נלך לא נטה ימין ושמאל (“we will not pass through fields or vineyards or drink the water from the wells, we will stick to the highroad and not turn aside to the right or to the left” I.L.). When this was refused to him, the people asked to be allowed to use the more difficult route over the mountains. במסלה נעלה, and if they or their animals should drink from the mountain waters, which flowed freely up there, but strictly speaking, could still be called מימיך, Edom’s property, they offered to pay compensation even for that, so that Edom would not have to give them anything at all except the permission to just pass through their land.
V. 21. ויט ישראל מעליו. From Deut. 2,4 et seq., we know that they were forbidden to use any aggressive force against Edom.

V. 22. כל העדה (See on V.1). This remark made here before the death of Aaron might be made to stress the fact that, although Aaron died in the wilderness, his death there was not in consequence of the fate decreed on the general body of the generation who died in the wilderness. When the region of Hor was entered that decree had already been fulfilled and the cause of Aaron’s death was solely what happened at Kadesh with the מי מריבה.
הר ההר: according to הר על גבי הר כתפוח קטן על גבי תפוח גדול ,מ״ר, a mount on top of a mount, a small mountain summit rising on the top of another mountain.
V. 23. על גבול ארץ אדום, described again in Ch. 33,38 similarly as בקצה ארץ אדום. There was another Mt. Hor at the north-west border of Palestine, hence the necessity for the precise location.
V. 24. יאסף אהרן וגו׳. (See Gen. on XXV,8).

V. 26. והפשט וגו׳ והלבשתם וגו׳. Thereby Eleazar was inducted to be High Priest in place of Aaron (See Ex. 29,29), and Aaron had the satisfaction before he died, of seeing himself living on in the person of his son.

V. 29. ויראו וגו׳, (“and they saw” I.L.). Just as after the death of Miriam the loss to the nation became manifest by the well drying up, so, according to the teaching of our sages (Taanith 9a) Aaron’s death was “seen” by a similar external manifestation. With Aaron’s death, the cloud which had accompanied them throughout their wanderings in the wilderness to protect and to guide them, left them. נסתלקו ענני כבוד, a state of lack of protection which at once encouraged the nearby Canaanitish King to attack them (Ch. 21,1). (This could lie simply in the word ויראו of the text, and the אל תקרא ויראו אלא וייראו of ר׳ אבהו be only explanation). There it says ג׳ פרנסים טובים עמדו לישראל אלו הם משה אהרן ומרים, וג׳ מתנות נתנו על ידם ואלו הן באר וענן ומן, באר בזכות מרים עמוד ענן בזכות אהרן מן בזכות משה וכוי. To their three leaders, Moses, Aaron and Miriam the nation had to thank for three benefits which provided for their existence in the wilderness, the well, the cloud and the manna. The well was due to the merit of Miriam, the cloud to Aaron and the manna to Moses. To these three leaders of the nation Micha (VI,4) directs the consideration of his contemporaries, that they could never complain that God had imposed upon them, that it had not been made clear to them beforehand in what the security of their future lay, that they could possibly be justified in placing the condition for and the protection of their national existence in anything other than purely moral and spiritual strength. “O My People what have I done unto thee, and wherein have I worn thee out in vain?; testify against Me” says God through the mouth of Micha, “did I not send before thee a Moses, an Aaron, a Miriam immediately when I brought thee up out of the land of Egypt and redeemed thee out of the house of slavery?” These three personalities, the only work for which they were qualified being the instructing and educating influence on mind and heart, were from the very beginning, the most striking proof of what the task was for you to accomplish which I made the condition for your future. A task which there in V.8 is described as עשות משפט ואהבת חסד והצנע לכת עם אלקיך, acting justly, loving doing kindnesses, and walking in quiet modesty with your God. But it springs to our mind at once how these three factors of our moral mission in life are just the qualities which respectively characterised our three leaders and their work in the nation. משפט, the norm of right, of living one’s whole life justly in accordance with the Laws of God’s Will formed the characteristic aim of the mission of Moses. חסד, and indeed אהבת חסד loving loving, inclining the whole formation of one’s character to loving doing kindnesses, to relinquishment of one’s rights, to unselfishness, to happy self-sacrificing acts of love characterised the activities of Aaron. So too is Aaron’s activity in conjunction with that of Moses described in Sanhedrin 6b:- משה היה אומר יקוב הדין את ההר אבל אהרן אוהב שלום ורודף שלום ומשים שלום בין אדם לחברו. Moses had to represent the principle of the law boring through a mountain, but Aaron the self-sacrificing feeling for peace, which loves peace and pursues peace and makes peace between man and his fellow. הצנע לכת עם אלקים, the unpretentious, morally pure, modest walking through life with God, צניעות, the fundamental character of Jewish womanhood, that surely found its most successful fostering under Miriam’s influence. Are not perhaps those מתנות טובות given for the material well-being of the life of the Jewish people parallel to these spiritual moral מתנות to which these three פרנסים טובים gave their special attention to foster for the spiritual welfare of the Jewish people? Can we not say that צניעות is the quiet hidden “well” out of whose depth all holiness of life springs, חסד, is the granting, cooling and protecting “cloud” which must be joined to the clear penetrating rays of pure justice to mature the seeds of welfare and happiness on the fields of mankind, but משפט, justice, right, the very bread from heaven, the “manna” which is necessary to keep alive the existence and endurance, the health and strength of all human and national life? And hence: באר through the זכות of Miriam, the cultivator of ענני כבוד ;צניעות through the זכות of Aaron, the cultivator of חסד; but מן through the זכות of Moses the transmitter and cultivator of the משפט teachings of God? —

ויבכו את אהרן שלשים יום כל בית ישראל. Our sages remark that after the death of Moses it says ויבכו בני ישראל את משה (Deut. 33,8) but here of Aaron כל בית ישראל. Just on account of that gentleness and the peace-loving and nurturing activities of Aaron his loss was more keenly felt and more generally mourned in every household in Israel than even that of Moses the man of — uncomfortable to some people — strict godly truth and justice.

But this fact should still not be overlooked:- Only a few days earlier this same people who now so deeply grieved in every home for the loss of this man, had overwhelmed him with the deepest unjustified reproaches and accusations (V.2). This deep mourning for Aaron following so soon after can make us realise how those uprisings which disturbed and darkened the lives of Aaron and Moses were, after all, only passing excitements brought about by momentary moods of despair, but the normal feelings and mood of the people knew how to value and knew what was owing to their great leaders.

V. 1. וישמע הכנעני (see on previous verse) — הכנעני the first of the nations really belonging to Palestine and as such they considered themselves threatened by the intended settlement of Israel in the land of Canaan, and so they threw themselves against them at the border. ערד, according to Onkelos the name of the province, according to Rosh Hashana 3a, the name of the king, identical with סיחון, and either סיחון was his proper name and he was celled ערד “the wild ass” because of his wildness שדומה לערוד במדבר, or ערד was his proper name, and he was called סיחון “the young ass” because of his recklessness, סיח) שדומה לסייח במדבר, a young ass Baba Bathra 78b). — האתרים from תור with a prefixed א like אגמון ,אגם from אזנך) אזן ,גמא) from אכן ,זון from אכר ,כון from כור, etc. etc.

V. 2—3. ויתן את הכנעני ,אם נתן תתן וגו׳ etc. רמב״ן remarks that the Trans-jordan country is never called ארץ כנען, and this king Arad whose people are called כנעני is said in Ch. 33,40, to live in the south בארץ כנען. So it must be assumed that he lived in the south of the West-jordan country, and from there launched an attack against Israel, the vow then would not refer to the contemporary present but to the future taking possession of the land. That would also be why the end is missing at ויתן וגו׳, as the complete conquest of the nation was only made later. Israel vowed that if God would grant them victory over these present attackers, then when later they took possession of the land they would leave their cities uninhabited and give all the spoil to the Temple, as a memorial of their first victory over a Canaanitish people, similarly to Jerico. They then accordingly also named the place of the victory they did obtain, חרמה. And we do find amongst the kings whom Joshua conquered in the West-jordanian lands a מלך ערד (Jos. 12,14) and according to Judges 1,1 ערד lay within Israeli territory at the desert of Judah. רמב״ן also refers ויכו את הכנעני יושב צפת ויחרימו אותה ויקרא את שם העיר הרמה (V.17 ibid.) to the final fulfillment of the vow. But one must nevertheless note that in Jos. 12,14 a מלך הרמה is mentioned next to מלך ערד which would still have to be explained.

V. 4. דרך ים סוף, this was a move backwards and a long way round. In Deut. 11,1 it says of it ונסב את הר שעיר ימים רבים (we went round Mt. Seir for many days). ותקצר נפש העם בדרך, cf. Ex. 6,9, מקצר רוח. As remarked there קצר רוח, and so here קצר נפש, is probably the reverse of ארך אפים, and would designate impatience. רוח and נפש cannot stand the waiting for the desired end to be reached. Here, especially the נפש, the spirit of life urging forwards could not bear patiently the long long road to the longed-for goal. There was no real concrete cause for dissatisfaction, they had all their requirements.

V. 5. וידבר העם באלקים. Their discontent turned also directly against God, they did not doubt the authenticity of Moses’s mission, but they were dissatisfied with God’s guidance. למה העליתנו וגו׳: God and Moses, למות במדבר: in this way we shall never reach our goal and shall end our lives in the wilderness in quite abnormal uniform manner. כי אין לחם ואין מים cannot wish to say they lacked these necessities of life for they immediately admit they did have לחם but they missed food and drink in the ordinary human way, The effortless, though miraculous, provision of both had become humdrum to them, the monotonous special provision by God’s Grace repeated daily for forty years had become something quite ordinary, and this dissatisfaction even turned them against, and unfair to the great nutritive value of, the manna food which God gave them, they called it לחם הקלקל, accordingly to the לחם קל :פסיקתא, a light easily digestible food, so digestible that, according to מדרש שוחר טוב it was נימוח באיברים, completely absorbed in the body, so assimilated that there was no residue and entirely used up in reproducing the tissues of the body, שנבלע ברמ״ח איברים (Yoma 75b). Their dissatisfaction twisted this excellent quality into its reverse, it was not substantial enough for them.

V. 6. שלח .וישלח ה׳ בעם in the Kal means to send to put something in motion towards a goal. But שַׁלֵחַ in Piel predominantly has the meaning of letting something go, to leave it to its natural way, not to hold it back. Thus וישלח את היונה ,וישלח את העורב (Gen. 8,7 & 8) ושלח לכם את אחיכם (ibid. XLIII,14) ושלח את בערה (Ex. 22,4) ויה׳ בשלח פרעה (Ex. 13,17) and elsewhere very frequently. Here too, not God sent serpents, but, let them go, did not keep them back. Hence not נחשים שרפים but הנחשים השרפים, they had always been there in the wilderness, but hitherto they had been kept back by God’s careful protecting Power. Now God withdraws this restraining power, and the serpents of the wilderness follow their natural traits to which the people succumbed. Thus in Deut. 3,15 Moses describes the wilderness through which they had wandered unscathed through God’s miraculous protective power as המוליכך במדבר הגדול והנורא נחש שרף ועקרב וצמאון וגו׳ (“Who led you through the great and terrible wilderness of poisonous snakes, scorpions and drought”). So that נחשים שרפים are as much a natural appendage of the wilderness as thirst. נשך ,וינשכו phonetically related to נזק to injure, נשק to burn נשק armour (see Gen. 41,40).

V. 8. והיה כל הנשוך וגו׳ ,ויאמר ה׳ וגו׳. The serpents’ bite had the sole purpose of letting the people see the dangers which dog a person’s steps when he goes through the wilderness, and that it was only the miraculous power of God which had hitherto kept them far from them, so far indeed that they did not even have an idea of their existence. One, who had been bitten had only to fix the image of a serpent firmly in his mind so that he realises that even when God’s gracious power will again keep the serpents at a distance he will remember that the danger is still in existence, dangers that daily and hourly the special care of God lets us escape quite unconsciously. So that every breath we take in our life is made into a fresh gift from God’s might and goodness. Nothing is so thoroughly calculated to conciliate us in the everyday disappointments in life which so easily sting us to impatience — every big prize in the lottery which God has failed to let us win — and to mix them with the exalted feeling of God having saved us, and the joy of being granted a new life, than the conviction of the abyss on the narrow edge of which the whole path of our life treads which the loving Hand of God veils from what would be our giddy sight, nothing so much but to see, to realise the נחשים השרפים which lurk invisibly on our path, and which only the Almighty Power of God knows how to impose the ban of impotence to injure us on them. Hence the punishment of these כפויי טובה, these “ingrates”, as our sages call them, by God removing the protection and the evil which hitherto had made the poisonous tooth of the serpent hidden and innocuous in the wilderness; hence the remedy, that one who had been bitten impressess on his mind to remember permanently the picture of the serpent — והיה כל הנשוך וראה אותו וחי!

V. 9. לשון נופל על לשון ;נחש הנחשת, a play on words (Rashi). Jerusalmi ר״ה III,9, עשה לך שרף לא פירש אמר משה עיקרה לא נחש הוא לפיכך ויעש משה נדוש הנחשת, the material was not told Moses out of which he was to make the שרף, but just on that account Moses concluded that it was self-understood that it was to be of copper, as שרף (poison I.L.) designates the kind of נחש and so implies the material too. By the serpent being made of נחשת the material itself by its name assists in impressing the idea of נחש which is the purpose of the figure as explained on the previous verse. מכאן היה ר״מ דורש שמות, this stimulated Rabbi Meir altogether to attach meanings to names.

If the way we have taken it is not erroneous, the נחשת material of the נחש would perhaps represent still closer the purpose of the whole arrangement. Henceforth this נחש נחשת was only to be the means of giving “some idea” of the real נחשים which lurk everywhere on the way in the wilderness.

V. 11. עי .בעיי העברים, like אי from איה means an out-of-the-way, isolated place, and hence איה (where?) the question concerning a place unknown to the questioner, so does עי from עיה mean an out-of-the-way, uninhabited place, a desert.

V. 12. נחל ,בנחל זרד is both the stream that flows down from the heights and the lowland or valley which forms the water-course for it. The fundamental concept is the natural movement from above to below, related to נהל. Hence the specific expression for the legal right of inheritance (see on Ch. 27,7 et seq.). The opposite term to it is נעל to close, shut in, stemming the natural forward movement.

V. 13. מעבר הארנון אשר וגו׳, the אשר refers to עבר. They had gone round the Moabite territory and now encamped on the north side of the Arnon, on the far side which forms the stretch of desert land which projects from the Amorite territory. So that they now first set their feet on the soil which was to be their own, as is related in V.21 et seq.
V. 14—15. על כן, therefore, because the Arnon is the dividing boundary between Moab and the Amorites, — its course is thus described in the ספר מלחמות ה׳.

ספר מלחמות ה׳, similarly to the ספר הישר (Jos. 10,13; and Sam. II. 1,18) proves that in Moses’s time, literary activities was not lacking amongst the people, these would be the מושלים of V.27, those who wrote and sang ballads and epic poems narrating the great deeds which they had experienced, for the benefit of their contemporaries and for later times. But at the same time these references to other books prove that the holy book of God, the תורה itself, does not consist of such compositions. But the incorporation of quotations from this ספר מלחמות ה׳ in the Torah may well be meant to recommend the records contained in that book as being worth-while giving attention to by the nation. את והב בסופה וגו׳: for us later generations the data of this citation has been lost. סופה and והב seem to designate geographical places to which the memory of great experiences is attached, as also Berachoth 54a, gives us the tradition that מעברות נחלי ארנון, the crossing across the streams of Arnon was comparable to that of the sea and of the Jordan and if one comes there one should say the: ברכה ברוך שעשה נסים לאבותינו במקום הזה (Blessed be He Who performed miracles for our forefathers at this place. I.L.) הנחלים ארנון describes the Arnon consisting of several streams, hence also in V.15 אשד .אשד הנחלים phonetically related to חסד ,חשד (see on Levit. 20,17).

According to Rashi and Onkelos והב is a noun formed from יבה to give, like ועד ,ולד from ילד and יעד, and סופה refers to ים סוף and the translation would then be “that which was granted at the Reeds was also at the streams of the Arnon”, i.e. the miracle of the Red Sea was repeated at the streams of Arnon.

ער .ואשד הנחלים אשר לשבת ער is a Moabite city (V.28), אשד הנחלים is the Arnon which is formed by several streams flowing together, after it has been formed it makes a bend and in the land enclosed by this bend lies the city of Or. It bends away from its straight course לשבת ער for Or to be established in its bend. We do find ישב used for cities themselves: לא תשב לנצח is said of Babylon (Is. 13,20), פרזות תשב ירושלים (Zac. 2,8). נטה לשבת עד, “it deviates for Or to be established”; ונשען לגבול מואב, from there onwards it flows along the boundary of Moab.

V. 16. ומשם בארה. Either the Arnon flows from there to the well, or from there one comes to Well. היא הבאר. The place was called באר, “Well” either because there they received again the well which had been given to them forty years before (Ex. 1,7) and which disappeared at the death of Miriam, or, more probably because the well which they had had, lost, and received again, and which had accompanied them up to here, finally stopped here. באר would then be the name of the summit of which V.20 speaks.

V. 17. אז ישיר, then, when the well was to be given to them again. עלי באר the people called it up, to rise from the depths. ענו לה, it is a well that one can raise from its depths by a “calling” song. Just as it arose in the first instance from no physical efforts so will it respond to a re-awakening call.

V. 18—20. באר חפרוה, for it is a well that was not dug by mechanical tools by mechanics. Princes and nobles — Moses, וזקני העם, and the elders of the people — (see Ex. 1,7) brought it into existence by the spiritual stylus of their sceptre of law. It was given to them from Horeb, the mountain of the Law (see ibid.). וממדבר מתנה, and now it was presented to them a second time from the wilderness and became a stream flowing down (נחלה I.L.) from God, and accompanied them up the heights, and down the valleys into the fields of the valley of Moab and finally up to the summit of a height, and now from there looks down on the vista of the wilderness through which it had wandered. There, ראש הפסגה, it came to rest. Henceforth they would no longer require the miraculous well. They were in an inhabited land which they conquered and took into possession, as is immediately recorded.

V. 24. מארנון עד יבק, from Arnon right up to Jabbok in the north and the territory of בני עמון in the west. כי עז גבול בני עמון. As it is at once explained, Israel was only permitted to conquer Cheshbon which originally belonged to Moab against whom all warfare was interdicted (Deut. 2,8), because it was already under the sway of Sichon and in his possession. The territory of the children of Ammon stood in the same relationship. As long and as far as it belonged to Ammon it was untouchable by Israel. Sichon had wished to conquer also the territory lying eastward to him, and had that actually occurred, this would then also have passed over to the possession of Israel, but עז גבול בני עמון, there Ammon was able to resist Sichon, Sichon was unable to conquer it and so it remained also untouchable by Israel (see below on V.30).
V. 26. כי חשבון עיר סיחון. See on V.24. הראשון, who was king of Cheshbon before him.

V. 27. על כן יאמרו המושלים see on V.14. המושלים, see Gen. 2,7, p.104. He who looks at the events of time, not as a chronicler, as a mere recorder of them, but from the higher point of view from which single happenings are expressed in the connection they have with the universal laws of God demonstrated by world-history, that historian is the veriest באו חשבון .משל, “Go to, all ye who need to learn the teaching of the transience of dynasties and of the fluctuation of power built up on the illusion of the might of pagan gods. See how the hitherto proud Moabite luxurious city of Cheshbon has been built up and changed and fortified to a city of Sichon, yea, to one of his citadels (V.28) from where he accomplishes the capture of a great part of the rest of the Moabite territory!”

V. 28. כי אש יצאה וגו׳, for the fire of war to which the whole territory from Jabbok to Arnon which belonged to Moab fell as booty to Sichon, belched forth just from the Moabite city of Cheshbon transformed to a citadel of Sichon. בעלי במות ארנון either refers to Moab as the hitherto lords of the heights of Arnon, or to אש and להבה of the henceforth ruler.
V. 29. אוי לך וגו׳, in this defeat the impotence and helplessness of Moab and its national god showed itself. The subject of נתן is כמוש.

V. 30. ונירם, and now we came and overthrew them. ונירם the future Kal of ירה with the converting ו. The suffix normally should be ונירֵם. But the future does occasionally have the suffix of the past tense, e.g. ילבשָׁם הכהן (Ex. 29,30). There we thought that the reason for the apparent anomaly might be for the purpose of stressing the future (now the present) having been an important consideration to something in the past. If then here the form of the suffix of the past tense is given to the future tense and gives it a concept of the past, it could change it to a pluperfect, a past perfect, and say not “now we overthrew them”, but — “it was we who had overthrown them”, i.e. at bottom it was not Sichon but we who had brought about Moab’s downfall. Sichon was only a tool for us, he overthrew Moab so that we could take his — Moab’s — land into our possession. Yea it could even be that the suffix ם refers to Sichon and ירה to be taken in its actual meaning of shooting arrows. “We shot Sichon at Moab”, Sichon was our arrow.

In this sense we could then also take ונשים to be the ordinary Hiphil of נשה with the suffix, like ישיא מות עלימו (Ps. 55,16). “God made Death into a demanding creditor over them”. So here “and we made him into a demanding creditor”. Sichon collected a debt on our behalf. Otherwise it can also be the Hiphil of שמם to lay waste, and the form similar to אם לא יַשִׁים עליהם נויהם (Jeremiah 49,20), and mean “we laid waste”.

This fact, that Sichon’s conquests benefitted Israel who otherwise would not have been allowed to touch the territories had they remained in the possession of their previous owners is expressed in Chulin 60b, by the words: עמון ומואב טיהרו בסיחון, Ammon and Moab’s territories became accessible to Israel through Sichon. Ammon is named there together with Moab, although it said above:- כי עז גבול בני עמון, for in fact in the territory which Israel took from Sichon there was included a part which had originally belonged to Ammon and which Sichon had conquered, as is apparent from Joshua 13,25 & 27, and Judges 11,13. From the latter it follows that, in the territory from Arnon to Jabbok which fell to Israel some parts which previously belonged to Ammon must have been included, and accordingly the עז גבול בני עמון can only refer to that part of the Ammonite lands which still remained in their own hands because Sichon had been unable to conquer it. (see Rashi on Chulin ibid.).
V. 32. וישלח משה. According to Josh. 13,25 this seems to have been just the territory previously belonging to Ammon.
V. 33. ויפנו ויעלו דרך הבשן: they turned northwards.
V. 1. ירדן ירחו .לירדן ירחו is the Jordan flowing past or opposite Jerico. Onkelos also takes it so:- לירדנא דיריחא.
V. 2. וירא בלק בן צפור (see on V.4). לאמורי, the conquered nations of Og and Sichon, Og’s realm also belonged to the Amorites (see Deut. 5,8).

V. 3. ויגר מואב. In the previous verse Balak is designated just personally and not as the king of Moab, so that here Moab cannot be just Balak himself the king but ויגר מואב is a continuation of what Balak saw, he saw that the Moabites were in a state of terror. He had seen the downfall of Sichon and Og and also perceived the effect these events were having on Moab. The effect was ויגר מואב and ויגר .ויקץ מואב, they were seized with such fear that all feeling of security was lost (see Gen. 37,1) as if their very ground was cut off from under their feet, as the מ״ר pithily puts it, they saw themselves already as ויגר) גרים) in their own land, the land no longer belonged to them, was already in Israel’s hands. And this fear was caused מפני העם כי רב הוא because Israel as a nation had shown itself so overpoweringly mighty. רב by no means only numerous, it is also an expression for might. קרית מלך רב, the city of the great King (Ps. 48,3); וישלח להם מושיע ורב והצילם (Is. 19,20 et alia.), and indeed they had reason enough for their fear. Had not Sichon who had overthrown them, himself been overthrown by Israel! ויקץ מואב מפני בני ישראל (see on Ex. 1,12), and they got the idea that there must be some factor working in this people, “these Israelites” against which everything else that normally meant power and might and greatness lost all meaning. קוץ, vomit, the highest degree of dislike, they became sick of everything, all that they had became distasteful, despicable, yea repulsive מפני בני ישראל, at the thought of the children of Israel.

V. 4. ויאמר מואב אל זקני מדין, and that this feeling had already driven them to take action. Moab, the Moabites, the people, going behind their king, had sent to the elders of Midian, again not to their kings, of whom they had five (Numb. 31,8), and had informed them of their fears. As Sichon and Og, the most powerful kings of the time, had proved themselves utterly powerless against Israel, the power of kings as defenders of the independence of their people had received a severe shock to the confidence with which their people could rely on them. So that from nation to nation, leaving out the kings the intelligence had gone forth with the invitation for common consultation and action. But the message ran:- לחך .עתה ילחכו means to lick, to lick up; to lick up water or dust with the tongue: ילחכו עפר כנחש “they shall lick the dust like a serpent” (Micha 7,17) or metaphorically of fire המים אשר בתעלה לחכה, (Kings I. 18,38). Now, as a matter of fact the ox first grasps with its tongue, the grass which it tears off and swallows. So that one can literally say “the ox licks up the grass”, and לחך here is an apt expression. But the sense of the message was:- as naturally and effortless as the ox takes the grass for its food just with its tongue, so naturally and easily will we all become the booty of this קהל. They intentionally do not call Israel an עם or a גוי, they do not appear to them yet as a constituted nation, for they have no country, the normal indispensable factor for a national body. But nevertheless they did appear to them as a קהל, a congregation united and held together by some factor which was unknown to them. את כל סביבתנו, not only us, against whom they are at the moment encamped so that we are primarily threatened, but all our neighbouring territories are in the same plight. Why they sent just to Midian, who were after all farther away from them, and not Edom their immediate neighbours seems questionable. Perhaps because Midian lay nearer to Egypt and particularly to the wilderness where Israel had lived for so many years, they could suppose Midian might know more about these mysterious people and be more likely to give advice in the matter. According to מ״ר it was because they knew of Moses’s past in Midian and so hoped they might get some particulars about him from them.

ובלק בן צפור מלך למואב בעת ההיא. The king of Moab is called מלך מואב but never מלך למואב. So that מלך למואב designates the royal position that somebody has, or should have, in Moab, and בלק בן צפור מלך למואב means:- Balak had the calling and the position of a king for Moab, and in connection with the beginning of the verse would have the nuance, ובלק וגו׳, “and yet Balak the son of Zippor was king for Moab at that time!” It was to him in the first instance that the Moabite people should have turned with their fears, it was for time such as this that, above all, the king was there as king. But inasmuch as the people in their anxiety completely ignored him as king, and in such a time (בעת ההיא) was no more than Balak the son of Zippor, as he is called in V.2 and did not see himself as מלך מואב; in this he recognised the whole danger of the position, and this was the reason for the whole of his following proceedings. Israel’s mere presence and the marvellous victories they had already achieved had worked such magic on his people that they had lost all confidence in the ordinary power of their nation and its military might, and expected nothing from their kings military prowess against Israel. This magic, or the idea of it in the minds of his people — no matter whether he himself believed in magic powers, or, as it seems from V.7 was initiated into the mysteries and secret tricks of the art — must be countered and broken by some higher or equal secret power before he could dare to, or even probably be given the opportunity of, leading his people out to war against Israel.

V. 5. וישלח מלאכים, so he sent messengers to the original homeland of the feared “wonder-working” people, to Aram in the Euphrates district, where the cradle of the ancestor of these people had stood, in the “Land of the Morn” (Ch. 23,7) whither offsprings from that ancestor’s home had been sent to settle (look up Gen. 25,6), and where, accordingly, heathen soothsaying and belief in magic were tempered and mixed with purer monotheistic thoughts which had been retained so that even a Job and his friends (Job 1,3) could have had their homeland there, and to where he himself belonged by descent, to Balaam, to invite that national seer and prophet to come to him.

הנה עם וגו׳ הנה כסה וגו׳. The repetition of הנה shows that with עם יצא ממצרים a separate independent thought is given for his consideration. The fact that עם יצא ממצרים, that a mass of people politically and socially completely submerged in the power and nationality of Egypt could go out of Egypt as a socially united people to freedom and independence, marks this people as something unique. And it is to the cause which could have effected this remarkable unheard-of event which your mind must concentrate on if you are willing to help my purpose to be achieved. הנה כסה את עין הארץ (Cf. Ex. 10,5). As the following והוא יושב ממלי necessarily describes a limited space and hence a not unlimited number the כסה את עין הארץ cannot be a hyperbole describing his numbers. But it would refer to the greatness of power he has already proved and thereby to realise what can be expected from him in the future. He has already covered the sight of the land, i.e. as far as one’s sight reaches in one’s mind he has already overpowered all the lands lying near to us. Wherever our sight may roam we no longer see the old cities but him: יושב ,והוא יושב ממלי is no threatening attitude. What he wanted to say could well be: it is doubtful whether he will attack me, but his proximity makes me anxious, it goes against me, and now, if I can succeed in doing so, is the best opportunity, in the general interest, of going out against him.

V. 6. ארה לי וגו׳ .ועתה לכה נא, destroy the germ of the inner life of these people (see Gen. 12,3 p.228), get at them internally, כי עצום הוא ממני for to conquer them by purely physical forces alone, that I feel is somehow beyond my strength. נַכֵה could be the infinitive of the Piel, like נֻכוֹ ,נֻכָתָה (Ex. 9,31) from the Pial. But then, to be regular, it would have to be נכה .נַכֵה is rather the future of the Hiphil, and it would then probably mean: perhaps then I shall be able to bring it about, that we, I and my people (Rashi) or we, you and I נכה בו. To strike an enemy in battle, to conquer, is always construed with the accusative, ,נכה אותו נכה ב- probably means only to strike a blow, to disconcert him ואגרשנו מן הארץ, not that we shall be able to destroy them but only to drive them away to the other regions. Even with the aid of Balaam, Balak does not dare to speak of a complete anihilation.

V. 7. זקני מואב וזקני מדין. Balak chose for his messengers, not royal nobles of the highest rank, standing apart from the people, but, in accordance with his purpose, such men who were near to the people and in whom the people had confidence, whom they honoured as their זקנים, as their advisers. For he must have wanted the greatest publicity possible to attend the whole procedure. זקני מדין with whom the people had already been in consultation (V.4) attached themselves to the mission.

וקסמים בידם. We have already remarked in Gen. 2,6, p.212, on the probable connection between קסם and גזם by which קסם would mean an operation which goes beyond what is natural or possible. In the word itself there would then lie the implication of sham. It is just גוזמה. In by far the greater number of cases in which קסם occurs its purpose is not so much to effect some result, as to predict the future, especially to decide whether to undertake something one intends to do or to leave it. Thus in Ezek. 21,26 etc. So that the קסמים here would also not be meant to be means for effecting the curse. In that case Balaam would have used them, not in Aram but in Moab. But it would probably have been assumed that they would be necessary to decide for or against Balaam’s undertaking. It is only striking that the messengers should have taken these magic oracles with them. For they were going to a קוסם (Josh. 13,22) and could indeed presume that he would have all the necessary apparatus for his work. Possibly it was part of the superstition that the oracle-worker had to have something in his possession of the person in whose interest the oracle was to give the required decision. (Fortune-tellers and crystal-gazers of to-day still ask for something on these lines I.L.).

V. 8. ויאמר וגו׳ כאשר ידבר ה׳ אלי. We saw, in Abraham’s time that, in the midst of a polytheistic world, there was still a Malchi Zedek, the priest of the highest god, who was the One and only God of the Abrahamites, how Job and his friends appeared as pure honourers of this One, so we see Balaam also considering himself and calling himself solely in service of this One. Altogether the monotheistic truth as opposed to the polytheistic error is not the special, and certainly not the whole, characteristic of Judaism. That is rather the monotheistic truth with the full realisation of what it entails for human living, the identifying One God with one mode of life, by His revealed Law. But Balaam’s monotheistic spiritual height appears morally muddled, far off from even that of Malchi Zedek, far off from a Job and his friends. His high spiritual gifts bringing him near to God were subordinated to his egoism and placed themselves at the service of earthly potentates and mighty ones and their lowest desires. “Wouldst thou see the difference between the prophets of Israel and the men of prophetic spirit of the nations”, runs a saying of our sages, “compare a Balaam with an Isaiah, a Jeremiah, an Ezekiel and their fellow prophets. Israel’s prophets acting as God’s watchmen warned the people against sin, Balaam advised moral seduction to tempt people to corruption (Ch. XXV). The prophetic spirit of Israel’s prophets was filled with pity and commiseration with both Israel and the nations, Isaiah’s inside vibrated like the strings of a harp over Moab’s woes (XVI,11), Ezekiel wailed lamentations over the fall of Tyrus (XXVII), while Balaam — wanted to ruin a whole innocent nation with his curse”. One could really say that this whole chapter of Balaam has the purpose of showing the reason for God ceasing to shower His Holy Spirit (רוח הקדש, Divine inspiration I.L.) on men of other nations.
