Balaam was one of those who received it, and see how he misused his spiritual gift (Tanchuma). — וישבו שרי מואב. The Midianites seem to have gone away. As Balaam had nothing to expect from Midian, perhaps they were not treated with the same consideration as the זקני מואב in whom he recognised the real envoys of Balak and whom he accordingly treated as שרי מואב.

V. 9. ויבא אלקים אל- — .ויבא אלקים אל בלעם only occurs elsewhere, at Abimelech (Gen. 20,3) and at Laban (XXXI,24), in both places as an unexpected message from God and to restrain a person from some intended action. Here, too, it is by no means necessary to assume that Balaam expected or even asked for this communication from God. What he said in the previous verse כאשר ידבר ה׳ אלי seems to be entirely just a phrase in the mouth of Balaam. At least the messengers from Balak and especially Balak himself took the מאן ה׳ וגו׳ in Balaam’s mouth as having no other meaning than: “I will not go with you, my ambition and my interests are not yet satisfied”. These elders surely belonged to the class of those that know and beguile rather than to those who are ignorant and beguiled, they knew what an appellation to the will of the gods meant in the mouth of those who practice their art of divination in the interest of rulers, and that the מאן ה׳ — God refused — in the mouth of Balaam was merely equivalent to מאן בלעם — Balaam refuses. But what seems to us to be quite decisive of this is the interrogative address by God מי האנשים האלה עמך. If Balaam had actually really wished to appeal for a decision from a higher authority and had asked God for that, the introductory question מי האנשים וגו׳ could certainly not have arisen. It announces itself as being an intervention of God completely unexpected by Balaam. What he had been playing at all his life and being pretending to his contemporaries to have happened now suddenly, unexpectedly, and, as it seems, undesireably, became an actual happening.

V. 11. קבה לי. The root קוב or קבב in the meaning of cursing, invoking curses only occurs in this episode in the mouth of Balaam and Balak, and moreover in an abnormal form. Derived from קבב, normally it would be קֻבָה or קָבָה as רָנוּ ליעקב (Jer. 21,7). From קוב it would be קובה. For קבה there is no analogy at all. In 23,8 where אקוב is used having the same meaning, the root is probably נקב which we find used in a similar way in Levit. 24,11 and 16. As נקב means to make a hole, קבב would probably mean to hollow out, and קב, a hollow measure of capacity (Kings II. 6,25 and common in the Talmud). So that if נקב is used for beshrewing a person with words, קבב would mean, to wish a person to become quite hollow, without any internal support or content, to make him into a מץ, an empty husk (Ps. 1,4); and מה אקב לא קבה אל would mean literally: how can I make even the smallest hole if God has not already completely hollowed it out. In קבב ,מ״ר is taken to be a higher degree of ארר.

V. 12. לא תאר וגו׳: Do not go with them for you will not accomplish the purpose of your journey. You will not curse this People, however much you might want to do so, I will prevent it; for it is blessed, that which makes these people into a People is just that for which I have pledged My word to further with the whole of My rule. Even by the nations of the world this People is to be thought of as being destined not to be cursed but to have the blessing of God. Now had Balaam been a prophet of the Truth he would faithfully have transmitted this declaration of God to the envoys of Balak and the purpose of God’s intervention would have been achieved without the whole following episode. Balak, and Moab, instead of fearing the attacking and conquering might of this People, would have been induced to know the moral factor which was innate in it to which God had promised His Blessing, and to befriend them to their own advantage. But

V. 13. ויקם בלעם וגו׳, Balaam suppressed the second part, the really essential part of God’s warning. He just speaks in general terms of a refusal, מאן ה׳, which forthwith allows it to be understood that he himself would be pleased to curse the people, only מאן ה׳ לתתי להלוך עמכם, the God Whose prophet I am, does not find it befitting for me to go with you. After all, they were only, as remarked above, זקני מואב not שרי מואב, only plebians, not really princes.
V. 14. מאן בלעם, See V.8.

V. 15. ויסף עוד בלק. Balak knew his man and did not let himself be put off from his purpose by the first refusal. ויסף עוד בלק forms a sentence on its own, hence the semi-colon after the word בלק, and hence the use of the word שלח שרים .עוד, this time he sent real princes, and a larger number and of high rank.

V. 16—17. מנע .ויבאו וגו׳ refusing, is the opposite of מנה and מנח, meting out, conceding. אל נא תמנע, only do not refuse me and וכל אשר תאמר אלי אעשה I will do everything that you say to me, both what to do to get my purpose achieved and to satisfy all your own desires. ולכה נא, by the manner in which these sentences are formed, two requests seem to be expressed here. Firstly, come, come in any case. In the tottering position in which he felt towards his people Balaam’s refusal to come would not be exactly calculated to raise his prestige in the opinion his people were forming as to the value of kingship. And secondly, to carry out his wish for the effective laying a curse on Israel. Balak could not imagine any reason why a Balaam should not concede this request which was so completely within the sphere of his profession.

V. 18. ויען וגו׳ אל עבדי בלק. The זקני מואב, in contrast to the זקני מדין, he treated as שרים, princes (V.8) and continued treating them as such (verses 13 & 14), thereby he did not demean himself in the slightest. But the real שרים, princes of high and highest rank, he treated as עבדים, servants, that showed the whole nature of the man, courteously affable to inferiors, proud towards superiors. אם יתן לי בלק מלא ביתו וגו׳. Therein, too, he showed his character. Much as he sought honour, solid gold and silver meant more to him than honours. In his message, Balak had not referred in any way to a fee in gold, had only spoken of confering the highest honours and further of fulfilling all his wishes. But Balaam at once translates the honours into gold, or states that even if he were to receive the very highest fee, he would still, etc. etc. Accordingly gold is to him the highest, above everything. So, in words of our sages, describing the character of Balaam (Ethics of the Fathers, V) נפש רחבה, avarice is placed parallel to רוח גבוהה, pride.

V. 20. ויבא וגו׳. We have already remarked on verses 16 & 17 that Balak’s request had two points, (a) that Balaam comes at his invitation and (b) that he curses Israel. For the first part he was given permission, regarding the second part, which constituted the real intended purpose of Balak, it had in V.12, already at the first mission been peremptorily denied to him: לא תאור את העם כי ברוך הוא, and here it was only further indicated to him that if he did go, he would rather have to be the herald of the Word of God, which, in accordance with the revelation which had already been vouchsafed to him כי ברוך הוא could be nothing other than blessing. He was accordingly completely prepared beforehand that if he did go, his going would only bring about the very opposite of what Balak’s intention was. Nevertheless

V. 21. ויקם וגו׳, nevertheless Balaam rose up in the morning, and went — keeping silence — with the princes of Moab. Without giving them any explanation at all, more, implicitly agreeing to both parts of their mission, he went with them. As the sequel shows in Ch. 23,3 & 15, and XXIV,1, Balaam himself, even after all that had happened in the meantime, and so, certainly at this time at the start of his journey, was of the opinion that in spite of everything, he would still succeed in pronouncing the curse. So little was he yet imbued with the fact that later on he was forced to proclaim לא איש אל ויכזב ובן אדם ויתנחם (Ch. XXIII), so little was he disturbed by the purity of the conception of God, the consciousness of ה׳, Whom he so submissively proudly called ה׳ אלקי, so much was even the conception which he had of the four-lettered Name of God half submerged in the heathen conception of the gods, that he thought that even this One God could be brought to change His mind, and be brought to accomodate his own lower desires by נחשים, magic charms, or in a moment which would withdraw His influence be able to escape Him.

V. 22. ויחר וגו׳ כי הולך הוא, not כי הלך that he went with Balak’s messengers. For, to go with them He had given him permission. But he did not just go with them, הולך הוא, he was “a goer” with them, one striving to reach his own end. In spite of the definite warning he had received from God, his mind was still obscured by the obsession that he would be able to achieve the purpose so desired by Balak and himself. So, while the angel, unseen by him, stood in the path to obstruct him, he trotted on proudly on “his” she-ass, with two of “his” attendants with him. The royal mission which had been sent to fetch him had surely brought a suitable riding-horse for him, and there were surely sufficient people to attend him. But it suited his pride to be apart and ride on his own animal — the sumptuous saddling of which he had, cavalier-like, attended to personally in the morning (V.21) — and to allow himself to be served only by “his own” attendants, and by “two” of them. All this obscurity of mind towards God, and pride towards men had first to be broken on the journey so that he would present himself to Balak as the tractable organ of the Word of God.

He wants to amend God’s plan for the world and is blinder than his own animal, he wants to vanquish God’s resistance and must accomodate himself to the wish of his own animal, he wants to ruin an entire nation by his word and has to confess the impotance of his wrath against an animal, he wants to be arrogant towards lords and princes and becomes a laughing-stock before his own attendants.

שטן .לשטן לו is used here in its real meaning, “to hinder”, to stand in the way. It seems to be related to the term in Rabbinic Hebrew ,סדן סדנא, block which occurs in Pesachim 28a, as the ball or heavy block attached to the legs of prisoners to hinder their walking.
V. 23. שלף ,וחרבו שלופה. See Ex. 23,8.

V. 24. במשעול הכרמים. The meaning of the root שעל is not quite sure. Comparing our verse here with אם ישפק עפר שמרון לשעלים לכל העם (if the dust of Samaria shall suffice for paths for all the people that follow me Kings I. 20,10 I.L.) and מי מדד בשעלו מים (Is. 40,12), שעל seems to be a foot or step as a measure, and משעול would be a narrow path along which one can only proceed step by step. But that would make the meaning בשעלי שעורים (Ezek. 13,19) still obscure. Perhaps a fox is called שועל as the one who creeps stealthily through the paths between the vineyards to which just foxes are so destructive. גדר to fence in, to form a boundary around is related to כתר, a circlet which shuts off from all others, a crown (Cf. זר from זור).
V. 26. עבר ,ויוסף וגו׳ עבור really to pass by somebody, hence to pass in front of him in the direction which he will be following.

V. 27. ויחר אף וגו׳. Had Balaam not been so completely obsessed by his presumptious conviction that he would be able to achieve his own purpose on this journey, these thrice-repeated checks must have seemed to him extremely ominous and have rendered him dumbfounded, especially as he was a man who was generally addicted to נחשים, signs and omens. — במקל. Up till now he had hit the ass only with the reins, to guide it in the right direction, but now he used his stick in his anger, to punish it.

V. 28. ויפתח וגו׳. At the moment when Man’s superior intelligent speech, obscured and benighted by passion and base greed, showed itself unworthy of this intellectual talent, God granted animal intelligence under the pressure of unjustified hurt to the feelings of an animal the gift of human speech. Just by that did God prepare the man of eloquent speech, however unworthy he may have shown himself for it, and to whatever misuse he may hitherto have employed it, for the moment when he — reluctantly — would have to lend his mouth to be the herald of the proclamation of Truths of God. He who can vouchsafe speech to an animal can also use the mouth of a Balaam to proclaim His Word. — רגלים (see Ex. on XXIII,14).
V. 29. כי התעללת בי. (see Ex. 10,2).

V. 30. הלא אנכי וגו׳. In מ״ר, the remark is made that this verse shows us that we are not to picture Balaam as an old man. His ass must have been older than he was. This more youthful age is more in accordance with the impetuous spirit which his behaviour discloses. — ההסכן וגו׳. We have already remarked on Gen. 19,4 that הסכן means to have one’s attention on something permanently. The same idea lies in the conception of “nursing” an idea, “nursing” an infant or an ill person, and also constantly doing some particular act, or constantly having the same thought etc., hence it also means “habit”.

V. 32. כי ירט הדרך לנגדי does not occur again. ועל ידי רשעים ירטני (Job 16,11) would come, according to the form, from ירט .רטה could be a stronger form of ירד and mean the steepness, precipitousness, of a way. לנגדי in the sense of אין חכמה ואין תבונה ואין עצה לנגד ה׳ (Prov. 21,30). Not just because you went — for you had permisison for that — but because you undertook the journey with the intention of doing something against My will, and you so completely unconcerned, contemplate surely to achieve your purpose just as in a steep precipitous path one is quite certain to arrive at the bottom.

V. 33. אולי נטתה מפני. We know of no instance in which אולי has the meaning of “unless”, “had not”. It always has quite definitely the meaning of “perhaps”. But there could be a difference between נטה לפני and נטה מפני .נטה מפני clearly means a turning aside out of fear. Thus ויסב דוד מפניו פעמים (Sam. I. 18,11). But נטה לפני can also mean simply to turn aside, to go out of the way, to show honour. The angel says: Why did you strike your animal? It was my fault that it turned aside out of the road three times. It did this out of respect for me, ותט לפני. Perhaps it did so out of fear of me אולי נטתה מפני, for I would have killed you, but of course I would have left it alive; גם אותכה הרגתי, this גם probably refers to Balaam’s utterance: לו יש חרב בידי כי עתה הרגתיך. You said that if you had had a sword in your hand you would have killed the ass for its behaviour, but it was you who would have been killed. Hence also the prominently stressed form: אותכה, you.

V. 34. חטאת, it was unwittingly that I sinned. ועתה אם רע וגו׳, now at last he came to the submissive, unassuming way of thinking which was befitting for him to have towards God from the beginning, and which was necessary for the mission he was now to accomplish.
V. 36. אשר בקצה הגבול, he went to meet him as far as he could possibly go. He received him at the very first place that lay in his territory.

V. 37. הלא שלח שלחתי, could not have been meant to refer to the repeated sending, for he reproached him that he did not respond at once to his first mission. It can accordingly only refer to the impressiveness and seemliness of that first mission.

V. 39. חצות .קרית חצות does occur, although seldom, with the meaning of highway, roads. Thus, probably, in Job V.10: ושלח מים על פני חוצות and in Kings I. 20,34 וחוצות תשים לך בדמשק. So that קרית חצות could designate a city which forms a central point out of which highways radiate in all directions. But a much more definite meaning of חוצות is its use for the business or main streets of a town, and it is in this sense that the מ״ר takes it here, a city of many streets, שעשה שווקים של מקח וממכר ועשה לו אטלית להראות לו אוכלוסין לומר ראה מה אלו באין להרוג בני אדם ותינוקות שלא חטאו להן, to show him streets, markets, busy traffic of commerce and full of people, Moab in the whole of its national prosperity, so that he should realise the importance of the mass of innocent inhabitants for whose continued existence he was concerned.

V. 40. ויזבח וגו׳ וישלח וגו׳ not ויעש משתה, he did not invite him to a banquet made in his honour, also the Piel form וישלח does not express exactly sending the food in a way that shows honour. Balak does not seem to have been too favourably impressed by what Balaam said.
V. 1. שבעה מזבחות. By the number seven the altars were erected to the invisible One God, the seven oxen and the seven rams dedicated to Him. (cf. Gen. 21,28).

V. 3. על עלתך. As indicated on V.1 the seven offerings formed a single conception (עלתך is singular I.L.). אולי יקרה ה׳ וגו׳. See on Levit. 1,1. Literally it would mean: Perhaps God will let Himself be brought towards me by the power which lies in our offering. The monotheistic conception of ה׳ was not foreign to Balak and Balaam, as already remarked on Ch. 22,5. But the thought was muddled by heathen ideas, and they believed they could impose a spell-like influence on God by their offerings. מה יראני והגדתי לך, he expected a מראה אלקים a phophetic vision and will describe to Balak in words that which he will see.

V. 4. ויקר וגו׳. God allowed Balaam’s expectation to be realised. He gave in to Balaam. And Balaam says: I have prepared the altars for Thee, the invisible One God (שבעה) and solicited a revelation about “earthly-doing and earthly fate” (פר ואיל).

V. 5. וישם ה׳ וגו׳. God did not grant a vision to which he would then have to give an explanation and meaning in words of what he took the vision to mean, but put in his mouth the actual words he was to say.
V. 7. משל .וישא משלו see above Ch. 21,27 and Gen. 4,7 (p.104).

מן ארם וגו׳. By this Balaam himself declared that he has an inkling that there is something, a special peculiarity innate in these people to which one would have to go back if one wished to form a judgment on this people and its future. Above all he declares that the fate of this people is dependent on that God of Whom the sages of Aram still kept some knowledge, and Who was not unknown to Balak from there, which was his real homeland. ארה לי יעקב וגו׳, according to its actual material appearance it is: Jacob, the most powerless amongst all the nations; according to what is godly in it and its spiritual importance it is: Israel, proclaiming the dominance of God on earth. By Balaam’s word, Balak wants the hopes of a future for Jacob to be struck at the root, it shall be ארור, cut off from the source of blessings; and as Israel זעמה ישראל. Whereas the other expressions for anger, כעס ,קצף ,אנף intransitively express the mood of the one who is angry and hence are construed with a preposition זעם ,על- ,ב- is active and has the object of it in the accusative. העם אשר זעם ה׳ (Mal. I,IV), יזעמוהו לאומים (Prov. 24,24) et alia. Hence also in the passive זעום ה׳ (ibid. XXII,14) the one that is affected by God’s Wrath. By the words of Balaam, the goodwill the favour of God, on which the flourishing condition of Israel is dependent, is to be changed into the reverse, His Wrath. Onkelos translates it תריך, the Chaldean for גרש to drive away, that God will drive them away from Him. זֹעֲמָה the seldom-used פּוֹעֵל form, like למשופטי (Job. 9,15).
V. 8. מה אקוב וגו׳. See Ch. 22,11. קבה with the sign of the feminine and the sound of the masculine. It must first have lost its virility by God’s curse before my word can affect it in any way.

V. 9. כי מראש צרים וגו׳. “From a high point of view I saw it near, from a lower one it was still far off”. Just as distances draw together in a panoramic view from a height, so is it with time. To a comprehensive survey of world-history over centuries, taken from above, events seem close together, which, to one looking more on the basis of the present, lie far apart from one another. שור is the view in the distance which sees that which remains hidden to others (see Gen. 49,22 p.673). Balaam says: I see this people in a future time — which, if not in the immediate future, yet in the whole development of time, not so very distant future — in which it will have reached the ideal of its purpose. (cf. Ch. 24,17).

הן עם לבדד ישכן וגו׳. It will live in an insulated land without much intercourse with other nations living its “internal” national mission as “עם״ as a national social body, and will not seek its greatness as “גוי״ among גוים, not as a powerful imposing national body among the other individual nations.

V. 10. מי מנה עפר יעקב וגו׳. You, Balak count the numerical size of this people. (Ch. 22,5 I.L.), the number of its fighters, by that reckoning it seems too big for you, and you believe that if one could reduce it in that direction you would be able to conquer it, you believe that altogether one could get at it vitally if one could succeed in bringing a curse on its material bodily thriving: מי מנה עפר יעקב וגו׳, who then counts what is earthly in Jacob, ומספר את רבע ישראל, and counts the physically born numbers of Israel (— רבע in the same sense as in Levit. 19,19 & XX,16 —). The prestige of other nations may rest on the number of the “bodies” of its population, their increase may form a threat to be feared by other nations, their decrease give rise to hopes. Not so is it with Jacob-Israel. Whether they are small in numbers as “Jacob” or growing numerous as “Israel”, it is not that which is עפר and which increases or diminishes itself just by animal-like breeding in which its importance, its happiness or unhappiness consists. Not even death have they to fear, bodily death cannot reach their true selves תמת נפשי וגו׳. I would like to die as they do, to know that my end would be like theirs, their dying is more blissful than our living, because they are ישרים, because they correspond to the calling for which on the whole men are “men” and strive for this purpose in “a straight line” without turning aside.

Summarising this first “parable” of Balaam, he had thereby to point out to Balak the complete specific difference of Israel to all the other nations, and to tell him that the future of this nation was completely independent of the physical-material causes which could be assumed to be the conditions for the growth and development of other nations. Hence they would also be unreachable by all damaging influences to which the welfare of other nations could be made to succumb. But as his words made the judging of the well-being of this nation altogether depended on the principles out of which it made its prosperity, this speech is a true משל, one that goes beyond the concrete single case, a saying which brings a fact, a moral, applicable generally out of the actual example quoted.

V. 13—14. Balak had first taken him to the במות הבעל, now he led him to the שדה צופים and when here too his purpose became changed into its very contrary he tried to obtain it down from ראש הפעור (V.28). If we compare the names of these three places to each other and to the speeches which Balak had to hear from them as the answer to his desire, then it is evident that with each of these places, and with the change from one to the other Balak must have wanted to present Balaam with a special point of view from which he was to try to arrive at laying the curse on the people, and therefore after the failure of each attempt he always tried to change the point of view.
פעור ,צופים ,בעל, these would well be the three mightiest powers which, in the opinion of a Balak, would decide the weal or woe of nations.

בעל. Baal appears as the most popular god of the Canaanites the highest power of Nature under whose influence all physical prosperity and the flourishing of material well-being stood. According to Avoda Zara Jerushalmi 3,6, רב חמא בר גוריון בשם רב וכו׳ the sign by which he was represented was identical with the phallus, the symbol of generative power in nature (also the name and conception פעל ,בעל, ‘phal’ could be identical). The first condition for a national future was, according to Balak’s way of thinking, the favour of “Baal”, the favour of the force of nature which decides over material growth and decay, and by leading Balaam to the Heights of Baal he posed the question: In what relation does this nation stand regarding the material factor of its life in the favour of the god who has power to direct it, can it not be impeded in its prosperity in that direction? After Balaam had answered this question in the negative because an “עפר and רביעה״ greatness granted under Baal’s influence did not count at all in the basic conditions for Jewish national existence, Balak led him to שדה צופים to the “Field of Seers and Watchmen” and there took him up to the top of the hillock. The second condition seemed to him to be intelligence, the nation to be possessed of mental spiritual gifts, to have clever gifted men, seers who could seek the advice of the gods, look into the future, see events before they happen and empowered with mastering powers of clairvoyance and astrology. And taking him to the Field of the Seers he posed the question to Balaam: How does this nation stand towards having the gifts which can decide the fate of nations, the spiritual gifts of insight, foresight, knowledge of the future, powers of magic that can force fate? Do these, the צופים side offer any flaw which could admit a weakening of its future? And again he builds seven altars, and in פר and איל offerings directs the question to the One Invisible Divinity up above Who judges the “acts” and decides the “fate” of mortals.

V. 15. אקרה כה ,התיצב כה .ויאמר וגו׳. Cf. ויפן כה וכה (Ex. 2,12) where כה also occurs with the meaning “here” or “there”. אקרה, relinquishing all self-direction I will give myself up to the “Divine Call”, to the Divine ordinance.
V. 17. ושרי מואב, not וכל שרי מואב as in V.6. After the first abortive attempt several of them had gone away already.

V. 18. וישא משלו וגו׳. Balak had bidden him to find out some weak spot on the צופים side of the people. Thereupon Balaam issues the command: Stand up Balak! You have asked about how this nation stands in the matter of getting near to the gods. You must stand up to listen to what I have to inform you of that. Both Balak and his father Zippor would have been inducted in the Aramean צופים knowledge. In the demand קום בלק ושמע האזינה עדי בנו צפור, right from the beginning, the whole distance in which the spiritual stage of Israel which is here to be proclaimed rises superior to the Aramean seers, is expressed. “You must have respect, O Balak, and will get to hear that of which your father, whose worthy son and pupil you are, had no idea”. האזינה עדי, it is well worth to incline your ear quite attentively. בנו צפור, probably: Zippor is pleased to call you his son.

V. 19. לא איש וגו׳. Immediately on your first request God told me regarding this people כי ברוך הוא that it was blessed. God does not speak in the ambiguous words of the oracles. If God says that something is blessed then it is blessed, and there is no phase of it which is accessible to the reverse. And if God has once said לא תאור את העם (“thou shalt not curse the people) He does not afterwards change His mind and give permission for the opposite. ויתנחם (see Gen. on VI,6, to change one’s mind I.L.). ההוא אמר וגו׳. As soon as He has said ברוך הוא He has already promised the people blessing and what He has promised shall He not keep? דבר is a continuation of the query: And if He has only said something, even if it is not a promise to anybody, if it is just a statement, should He not maintain it? Such a statement was His לא תאור with which He forbade my curse, or denied it.

V. 20. לקחתי ,הנה וגו׳, I have received the mission, have been qualified for it. Thus indeed teachings from the point of view of the pupils who receive them are called הנה .לֶקַח “And see, now too blessing is given to me as my mission, וברך and He has already blessed the people in general and in particular with the commission which has been given to me. My mouth only expresses what He has already done. I can do nothing to alter that”.

V. 21. לא הביט וגו׳ gives the reason why God has blessed this people. עון is the misuse of אוֹן, power and wealth (see Gen. p.531). Before God blesses a nation He first finds out whether it will misuse the און which is to be granted to it. Before God promised און to Jacob to raise it thereby to Israel He found out whether he would misuse this אוֹן to לא הביט און ביעקב .אָוֶן, God did not foresee in Jacob any misuse of the greatness with which he was to be invested, that is why He saw no misfortune in Israel, i.e. no necessity, no cause for עמל, for trouble, for lowering the pitch of their high spirits by worries, by hard struggling and often toiling in vain against obstacles in the way of thriving, for that is what עמל is (see Gen. on Ch. 41,51). He saw no misfortune in Israel (that He could allow to be announced through my mouth).

ה׳ .ה׳ אלקיו עמו, the Invisible One, Whom we also know from our native home as the source of all existence and as the Ruler over heaven and earth, He is אלקיו, is the special owner, guide and leader of this nation in their fate and deeds, He, this God is with them as their God, assists them and leads them through their wanderings through the ages — תרועה .ותרועת מלך בו is a stirring up sound, also the shattered mood of deeply agitated timidity which that sound arouses in the human breast. Thus וירא פניו בתרועה (Job. 33,26); ואזבחה באהלו זבחי תרועה (Ps. 27,6). Referring to God, it designates the completely submissive feeling of homage brought about by the overpowering thought of His Greatness. Now here it means: God is with it (the nation I.L.) and in it there is nothing but homage paid to a king, i.e. it acknowledges Him as its King, and the whole internal realm of the nation is filled with this homage. The ו could also be a causitive conjunction: God is with it because His homage as a King is in it.

V. 22. אל מוציאם וגו׳. In Egypt they were still a disjuncted down-kept “mass”, and as such a mass of being without any power to help themselves did God lead them out of Egypt and united them into a nation. The God Who thus effected their freedom without their doing anything at all on their own part is also God Who, again without any assistance on their part, will lead them further to the whole height of power and independence, it is that which invests this people with such a fearsome “reem-like” swing up to power. It is not necessary for it to seek this power, has not to exert any physical or spiritual leverage to obtain that. It is handed to them all ready and prepared from God. God wants them mighty and great and all He demands from them is תרועת מלך, the homage due to a King which shows itself in keeping afar from all און, from all misuse of that which they receive from God.

תועפות from יעף identical with עיף and עוף (on Gen. 1,21, Hirsch compares עיף and עוף to יגע and יגע, tired, worn-out and striving, working and takes “flying” to be the continuous effort at progress as can be seen by the merest observation of the unceasing movement of the wings, whereas “walking, going” progresses step by step I.L.) designates a continuous constant striving upwards to the heights. Hence the metaphor in Ps. 95,4 תועפות הרים the mountains striving upwards in contrast to מחקרי ארץ, the depths of the earth.

V. 23. כי לא נחש וגו׳. For the צופים-wisdom that you enquire about in this people, and according to the extent of its existence there, you imagine you can measure the success or failure of its future position of power, that wisdom which with “omens and oracles” knocks at the doors of darkness, and by the supposedly overwhelming powers of “magic” thinks it can sway the ways of fate to its favour and desires — for these arts, to which people turn when helpless and at their wits end, Israel has no need. Not to “omens and oracles” does Jacob hearken in his need, not to “magic arts” does Israel thank its greatness. כעת, at this moment when we are talking together and become aware of our utter helplessness before God to start anything against this People of God, it is being revealed to them what God is effecting with us, so that it may be understood by them as Jacob, and as Israel never be forgotten.
Instead of the beggarly assistance we get from the נחש and קסם of our dark צופים-wisdom, Jacob-Israel receives the bright clear Word of God without having to seek for it.
נחש, see Gen. on Ch. 43,5. — קסם; ibid. Ch. 11,6, p.212. — כעת as in Judges 13,23 וכעת לא השמיענו כזאת.

V. 24. הן עם וגו׳, Jacob-Israel does not require our צופים-science. Neither does it require any נחשים, it is sure of its future. It requires no קסמים, it becomes master of its fate by other means. Not as a גוי of the גוים, not as a national force externally has it to fight against other national forces to obtain its position and to hold it securely, הן עם, by fulfilling its social mission internally, by quietly living its own social life (עם = עם together, one with the other I.L.) it becomes dauntless as a leopard and strong as a lion to the external world, and by its internal virues it conquers the world. — לא ישכב עד יאכל טרף וגו׳ carries on the conception of the lion’s power which Jacob-Israel attains by way of peaceful moral social energies. The subject of ישכב is ארי.

V. 28. From במות הבעל and שדה צופים, from the standpoint of the physical material, and from the standpoint of the godly spiritual, Israel had been shown to be untouchable by Balak. But a nation can be blessed with all physical and spiritual gifts and yet be irrevocably hastening to its ruin. Providence can shower on it all the treasures which heaven has to give, with all physical and spiritual riches, and the nation can be nurturing a worm that eats away from its inside which turns all the blessings into the reverse, and finally makes it not only unworthy but incapable of receiving and keeping blessings, and the name of the cancer is immorality, shameless giving oneself up to dissolute debauchery.

So that after במות הבעל and שדה צופים had made Balak look in vain for a weak spot in the hated nation, he said: לכה נא וגו׳ (cf. V.13 לך נא וגו׳), “I would still like to make one further attempt, so do come and let yourself be brought to another point of view, there can still be another from where perhaps God Himself would allow a curse to be cast against the people.” And he took him to the point where he could look down over the “waste of deified Shamelessness”, for that is “Peor”, a cult which turns the most animal side of human functions towards the gods, and says to Man: Why do you dream of decency and modesty and a higher calling, your own alimentary system shows that you are no better and designed to no higher calling than an animal. Hereby Balak posed the question: How does the nation stand with regards to decency and modesty and to sexual purity of morals in which finally the strength and flourishing of all nations have their root.

Not without reason is the saying of the sages in בלק היה בעל :מ״ר קסמים ובעל נחש יותר מבלעם שהיה נמשך אחריו כסומא למה הדבר דומה לאחד שיש בידו סכין ואינו מכיר את הפרקים וחבירו מכיר את הפרקים ואין בידו סכין כך היו שניהם דומין. Balak was even more deeply initiated in the arts of magic and omens than Balaam who let himself be led about like a blind man. They are like two men who wish to perform an operation. One of them has the instruments but has no knowledge of anatomy, the other has the knowledge but has no instruments. Thus Balaam let Balak show him the place where to make the incision of his words.

V. 1. וירא. Only now did the cloud completely disappear from Balaam’s mind, he no longer believed that by his magic he could exercise influence to reverse the decision of God. What his mouth had declared in V.9 and V.20 of the previous chapter had now become fixed as truth in his heart. He therefore simply looked out into the desert from the point of view that Balak had directed him to adopt, and waited to see whether God would use him further as His organ.

V. 2. וישא וגו׳. But when he raised his eyes and saw Israel “לשבטיו״ encamped according to their tribes arranged according to families and homes, at this sight he already saw the answer to Balak’s question there before him, and “the Spirit of God” came upon him. He was not, as he had been in the two first cases, against his own will a reluctant organ of the Word of God placed in his mouth; that which he speaks henceforth is said in the pure spirit of prophecy.

V. 3—4. וישא וגו׳. This רוח אלקים seems to have been something new to Balaam, something he had never experienced before. This would explain why he — as is the case in none of the prophets of Israel — is so full of himself, and at first cannot get over describing his new condition and his elevated spiritual personality to get to what he really has to say. בנו בעור see on Ch. 23,18. The Gemora in Sanhedrin 105a, takes it in the opposite way: אביו בנו הוא לו בנביאות, Balaam, whose father Beor was only like a son compared to him, as a prophet he went far ahead of his father.

שתם .שתם only occurs again in the Mishna (Avoda Zara 109a) as the opposite of סתם, closed: כדי שישתום ויסתום ויגוב where it means the opening of a bung. שתם העין, he feels that only now his eyes are opened. מחזה שדי: that which He, — Who, standing above the laws of Nature by which He governs the world, sets the limit and measure to all things, (שדי, I.L.) — allows to be seen by mortals of this His government of the world (see Gen. on XVII,1, p.291). — נפל, who had been overpowered by the רוח אלקים which had come over him, but who is nevertheless גלוי עינים thereat, his mind is clear and alert.

V. 5—6. מה טובו. How do you see the people מראש פעור was what Balak asked; how do they stand regarding decency, regarding sexual morality? The camp “לשבטיו״ which he saw before him, the אהלי יעקב, the משכנות ישראל that he vizualised, with each child knowing his father, and houses and families and tribes grouped according to the paternal derivation — משפחת האב קרויה משפחה — that is the yardstick by which sexual morality could be judged.

מה טובו, how “good”, not how “beautiful”. How good, how greatly do your “homes” correspond to the moral ideal and the true well being of a nation. They can be the temporary tents of wandering “Jacob” or the stately mansions of “Israel” משכנות, cf. משכנותם לדור ודור Ps. 48,12; וישב עמי בנוה שלום ובמשכנות מבטחים, (Is. 32,18). Israel’s family homes are נחלים and גנות. They are blessing-bringing brooks and even blessed “gardens”. Every home and every family branch, like a brook, makes material, spiritual and moral welfare flow down to each succeeding generation, and itself is a material, spiritual and moral blessed human-garden in any of its own contemporary periods. Each one in its own speciality is a brooklet running its own particular course, but all these courses lead their achievements down to one common stream. They are at the same time אהלים and ארזים, combine the delicate ethereal essence of aloes with the firm strength of cedars, the beneficent noble and ennobling spirituality with strength and endurance. — אהלים as מר אהלים וקנמון, “myrrh”, aloes and cinnamon” (Prov. 7,17) or מר ואהלות עם כל ראשי בשמים “myrrh and aloes with all the chief spices”. (Song of Songs 4,14). This ethereal quality of the אהלים, representing the spiritual gifts of the generations of Israel is, he says, a direct dispensation of God dependent on its being “planted” in accordance with the Will of God, hence אהלים נטע ה׳, as is the water, the source of life and strength on which the human cedars grow.

V. 7. יזל מים מדליו, the water flows out of God’s buckets, and every human germ which is sown at these streams of the godly life-giving source is His seed. The whole secret which gives the tents and habitations of Jacob-Israel the character of “being good”, and makes the whole life which develops in them to such a “blessing-spreading and blessed” human plant lies just in the sanctification of their sexual family life, which consecrated and made invunerable against any trace of Peor-like coarseness, respects the power of human seed as belonging to God and most sacred to him. It makes every human sprout sown and planted only in accordance with God’s directions at the source of His teachings and laws, for His Glory and for the realisation of His Will on earth; all this is expressed to an onlooker by the very sight of the tents and habitations of Jacob-Israel encamped according to homes, families and tribes about their common Sanctuary of God and His Torah — the sight of ישראל שכן לשבטיו. And just in this morality of its most private sexual and family life lies Israel’s external power of victory and invincibility. Because יזל מים מדליו, because God’s directions for life are the vessels out of which the stream emanates at the banks of which the Jewish human-garden blossoms, because זרעו, every human sprout is a product of passion subordinated to the Law of God, Israel’s King rises higher than Agag, its realm soars upward, for it is the victory of the Divine Law of Morality, the elevation of the Kingdom of God on Earth which is the victor in every victory of Israel, and gains its sovereignity on earth with every extension of its realm.

V. 8. אל מוציאו וגו׳. Above in 23,22 מוציאם. (here in the singular, the nation as a whole, there in the plural, the individuals of the nation I.L.). For it was just this chaste morality of character, this being free from גילוי עריות and all Peor-immorality which was already in Egypt the general inherited nobility of its sons and daughters. It was this unanimity of moral character which already then formed a strong bond of fellowship when externally every other condition for a national union was lacking. The God Who brought them out of Egypt because of this fundamental moral character which they possess is the One Who further grants them this sudden mighty growth of power because through them His Law of Morality obtains a place again amongst mankind. They conquer nations, or rather God makes nations go down before them, because those nations are צריו, because they are enemies of His laws of morality and make the world opposed to Him. For it is repeatedly pointed out in the עריות chapter (Levit. Ch. XVIII) that the inhabitants of Canaan come under the heavenly decree of doom, just on account of their moral depravity!

ועצמתיהם יגרם. We have remarked on Gen. 19,14 that גרם does not designate the hard bony substance as עצם does, but the joints. גרם in the Piel would accordingly mean the disjointing, severing the joint, or taking away the joining power of the joint. עצמתיהם יגרם would accordingly mean: All their strength avails them nothing against Israel, before Israel they lose all the power of their joints “it will come about that all their bones will no longer serve them as גרמים, as means of further movement.”

וחציו ימחץ, and as the arrows of God will Israel wound them, i.e. Israel is a weapon in God’s Hand against His enemies, against the enemies of the reign of His Law of Morality on earth, and it is only as the arrows of God that Israel has the power to vanquish nations.
V. 9. כרע שכב, and when it has conquered the nations and has taken up its peaceful position in their midst, then it rests, commanding such respect that no one dares attack it.

מברכיך ברוך וגו׳. He looks down again at Israel and pronounces the great saying מברכיך וגו׳, the greatest one, that once God proclaimed when He first chose Abraham (Gen. 12,3), and Isaac repeated when he blessed Jacob (ibid. XXVII,29). Here, as in the last quotation mentioned, מברכיך and אורריך are in the plural but the predicates ברוך and ארור are in the singular. So it seems that it is to be taken thus:- all those that bless thee, i.e. that respect thy principle and further it, they have the blessing, i.e. they are those that can expect blessing and prosperity from God, they are those who altogether have a future under God’s government of the world. But those that curse thee, i.e. who are opposed to the principle which is to be brought into the consciousness of mankind through thee and wish to see its ruin through thy ruin, ארור, they are just those who bear the curse in themselves, whom God has destined to ruin, that have no future on God’s earth.

V. 10. ספק .ויספק את ידיו and שפק occurs as here in the meaning of striking one’s hands together as an expression of surprise and dismay. Also as striking one’s thigh as an expression of grief (Jer. 21,19) ספקתי על יהך. But it also has the meaning of sufficing, satisfying: אם ישפק עפר שמרון (Kings I. 20,10) etc., and is also, especially in the Mishna and Talmud the ordinary expression for doubt. The clapping the hands together seems to be the basic meaning. Stretching the hand out with the palm turned upwards expressed the requirement for “receiving” and is accordingly the expression for desiring a material gift and also for an intellectual one, information respecting something, an answer. Striking the open hand on to such an asking open hand says: “so this is what I asked for, this is to be what I expected”! is accordingly an expression of surprise or even disgust. From that ספק or שפק could mean to lay something in the palm of an outstretched hand, i.e. to satisfy a wish, to supply a demand. To stretch the open palm downwards instead of stretching it out and to strike it against one’s own hip or thigh would express hopelessness: “We can hope for nothing further, we shall get nothing more.” Finally ספק striking one hand into the other would also express complete equality of two conditions so that they mutually balance each other, and admit no way out in any direction and so come to the meaning of “doubt”.

V. 14. לכה איעצך. In Ch. 31,16 speaking of the Midianites, it says: הן הנה היו לבני ישראל בדבר בלעם למסר מעל בה׳ על דבר פעור that they (the Midianite women and girls) gave themselves up to the sons of Israel, at Balaam’s instructions, in order to bring them to commit treason against God by the cult of Peor, an occurrence which is described here immediately after Balaam’s departure (Ch. XXV). So one is certainly justified in referring that event to the איעצך with which Balaam gave him the advice to entice Israel’s youth to their downfall. For Balaam had just declared in his last prophetic speech, that it was just in the Peor aspect in which Balak made the last attempt to find a weak spot in Israel, just in this that the people’s strength lay, yea, that it was this sexual purity which formed the fundamental condition for their close relation to God. What lay nearer then that he should say to him: Your people will have to suffer from these people, but that is a matter for the future. At the moment you have nothing to fear from them, but on the contrary, in accordance with the revelation which has just been made to us, I can give you an advice as to how you can try to do this hated nation of yours very considerable harm. We have just heard אלהיהם של אלו שונא זימה הוא, as it puts it in Sanhedrin 106a, “the God of these people is an enemy of all unchastity”, He is the very antithesis of Peor. If you succeed in enticing them to sensual depravity you will lead them to their ruin, and you can make the attempt through the daughters of your people (see the following chapter).

V. 15—16. וישא וגו׳. (see on verses 3 & 4). He still speaks of himself here as יודע דעת עליון because, as Ramban explains in his commentary, he reveals here events of the most distant future, which at the present are mere thoughts of the very highest minds.

V. 17. אראנו וגו׳. I see it as clearly as if it were before my eyes, although it is not happening now, but rather I am gazing into the far future at events which are not yet near. By this he calmed Balak’s fears that Israel’s growing strength were, or could be, an immediate danger to him and his people. This follows immediately on his last saying in V.14: אשר יעשה העם הזה לעמך באחרית הימים.

דרך כוכב וגו׳. Stars go along their appointed courses. הככבים ממסלתם (Judges V.20). Stars are signposts in the sky by which people find the right way for their journeys on earth. ומצדיקי הרבים כככבים (Dan. 12,3). Such a star showing mankind the way it should go will enter on its God-directed course out of Jacob, hitherto little respected on account of its weakness. וקם שבט מישראל, and this “star” will at the same time become a “sceptre” (the symbol of authority I.L.), it will be invested with governing influence. מישראל, out of the people “proclaiming and spreading the Glory of God” it will rise at the same time as “sceptre”. Just by its rising as שבט does יעקב become ישראל. Balaam, in his mind is present at the time when this event is happening, hence דרך, “it has stepped forth”, not ידרוך “it will step forth”.

ומחץ פאתי וגו׳ וקרקר וגו׳. The meaning of פאתי is doubtful. (It is usually translated corners I.L.). By the form of the word it cannot be the stat. constr. plural of פאה, a corner. For then one would have to think of a dual form פאתים of which our פאתי would be the stat. constr. But the meaning of such a dual form (a pair of corners I.L.) remains obscure. We believe it could be synonymous with פות, like ראם from רום which also, in וראמה (Zac. 14,5) and in ראמות (Job. 28,18) changes the quiescent ו into an א so that it could be taken, like הפותות לדלתות (Kings I. 7,50) to be hinges to represent doors. Then פאתי would be in the same train of thought as the following וקרקר וגו׳. For קרקר appears to be a doubling of the Piel form of קיר, wall, and means to “dewall”, to pull down, do away with a wall. Thus מקרקר קיר (Is. 22,2). בני שת are the descendants of Seth. This description comprises the whole post-diluvian world as the descendants of Noah, the last of the offsprings of Seth. The sense would be:- this guiding star and sceptre coming forth from Jacob-Israel will smite Moab’s gates and do away with the walls of all nations, i.e. before the might and influence of its teachings, directing the world to the one path to security and happiness, Moab will no longer have any hinges to isolating gates: its pride in standing alone will cease, and all mankind will become “without walls”: material strongholds will no longer afford any protection and will no longer be valued as giving security.

V. 18. ירשה .והיה אדום ירשה: something which passes over into the possession of another. As Edom is mentioned here as well as Seir and the same thing is prophesied for both, Edom would refer to the Edomite power and Seir to its original homeland. The former extends much further than the latter. The Edomite power, until then the greatest national power which has no master over it, will become ירשה, will receive a master, will pass into other possessors, and thereby Seir, the homeland of its origin, changes its owner because both are אויביו, the arch-enemies of Jacob-Israel. And whereas Seir-Edom thus loses its independence Israel grows strong and becomes the most influential power. עשה חיל means equally getting, gathering strength and forces as in הנתן לך כח לעשות חיל (Deut. 8,19), and using such forces as in ימין ה׳ עשה חיל (Ps. 18,15). חיל see Ex. 18,21.

V. 19. וירד מיעקב. But as it is just out of the powerless “Jacob” that the sceptre-bearing star comes before whose spiritual loftiness all material power and even the Edomite sceptre bows down, the last one-sided worship of “culture” perishes והאביד שריד מעיר. For inasmuch as עיר stands here quite by itself, self-existing, it can well designate the material culture of cities, with the one-sided, self-contained and self-sufficing development of which the history of Man’s worship of Man and his self-sufficiency began (Gen. 4,17 and XI,4). It is this that is to come to an end with the ultimate acknowledgment of the guiding sceptre of the star which will come out of Jacob. Thus in Is. 32,14 & 19, we also find עיר used as the representative of one-sided worship of culture, and the hymn of that future God-seeing age, runs עיר עז לנו ישועה ישית חומות וחל (Isaiah 26,1), “We have an invincible city, for it appoints God’s salvation in place of walls and bulwarks”.

V. 20. ראשית גוים, the first in rank, for in time Moab was older. It was also the first of the nations which, entirely unprovoked, started war with Israel, ואחריתו and its end will be עדי אבד, it goes on its way so long until it becomes אבד, completely lost, even the recollection of it will disappear from the minds of mankind.

V. 21—22. הקיני וגו׳. We are informed in Judges 4,11 that a branch, separated from its aboriginal race Cain, נפרד מקין, had settled amongst Israel and was accordingly called קיני. This was the branch to which Moses’s father-in-law belonged, under whose example this attachment to Israel took place (see above on Ch. 10,29). Balaam warned them not to leave this attachment and settlement in Israel. Let him keep fast to this settlement, and never alter it. Let him build his nest in this rock which he has once chosen and never return again to his aboriginal race. For Cain will be destroyed by Asshur and led away in captivity. So that if he returns to Cain the same fate will overtake him and whither then will he be led in captivity? He will escape this fate if he remains in Israel. It seems, as already remarked on Chap. 10,29, that he will not even be subjected to the Assyrian might, and be left in freedom and independence when Israel is overcome by that force. In Israel accordingly in very truth he kept his מושב as איתן.
תשבך. Here Asshur is written in the feminine. Probably in view of the pronouncement which is immediately to be made of the fate which also awaits Asshur.

V. 23. אוי מי יחיה משמו אל. In face of Israel being established by God, nobody who opposes the principle which just thereby is to achieve mastery will be able to keep their independence. With the entry of Israel, guided by God, into the world history, the future of all those who oppose this purpose of God, is cut off.

V. 24. וצים וגו׳. From Is. 33,21, וצי אדיר לא יעברנו (neither shall gallant ship pass thereby I.L.) and Ezek. 30,9, יצאו מלאכים מלפני בצים (messengers shall go forth from me in ships I.L.) it is evident from the context that צי, plural צים means “ship”. On the other hand ציה is the wilderness, and ציים the inhabitants of the wilderness. Analogies, as בי from בעה ,בהה (see Gen. 1,2), הי from ההה in מי ,אהה from פי ,מהה ,מה, plural פים (Sam. I. 13,21) from קי ,פהה ,פה (in קיקלון Habakuk 2,16) from קאה, make one think of a common root for both צי, ship and ציה wilderness, possibly being צאה related to שהה ,שאה ,צעה. The fundamental conception would then be, a long or short movement towards a goal. שהה in Chaldean, to tarry a long time without coming to the goal, to dawdle; to think a long time about something without getting at the knowledge you want; צעה to move, to go along with emphasis, with special attention, to stride along; צי, a ship that has to make long journeys overcoming difficulties, a large vessel. ציה, a region where one has to wander for a long time and overcome difficulties before arriving at one’s goal, a wilderness.

כתים .מיד כתים (Gen. 10,4) were descendants of Yavan. Tradition takes them to be the ancient Italian inhabitants of Greek ancestry, hence איטליא של יון, Greater Greece, and takes the כתים to be the Romans. יד כתים would then be the Italian coast on the Mediterranean. עבר, according to Onkelos, the lands on the further side of the Euphrates. Possibly עבר means all the Joktanites mentioned in Gen. 10,26—30 as descendants of Eber. יד כתים like יד הירדן (Ch. 13,29) and יד אשדוד (Josh. 15,45) מיד כתים could also mean from the power of the וגם הוא .כתים refers to יד כתים and יד would then be thought of in the masculine as it is in Ezek. 2,9 והנה יד וגו׳ והנה בו וגו׳.

V. 1. The sword of no stranger, the curse of no stranger had the power to damage Israel. Only it itself could bring misfortune, by seceding from God and His Torah. וישב וגו׳. As the מ״ר remarks, after the victorious fight against Sichon and Og, rich with their booty, Israel settled down to a comfortable enjoyable rest. בַשׁטים not בְשׁטים. The district was called הַשׁטים (Micha 6,5). It was a wooded shady region which offered a very welcome relaxation after the long wandering in the burning sun of the desert. — ויחל העם. The מ״ר remarks כל מקום שנאמר העם לשון גנאי הוא וכל מקום שנאמר ישראל לשון שבח הוא, wherever the term העם is used it is derogatory whereas ישראל is an honourable appellation. Thus ויהי העם כמתאוננים (XI,1) וידבר העם באלקים ובמשה (XXI,5), ויבכו העם בלילה ההוא (XIV,1) עד אנה ינאצוני העם (XIV,11) etc. — לזנות אל וגו׳: they began to break away from the moral faithfulness to duty to which they kept themselves hitherto and to give themselves up to the daughters of Moab. In this אל is already indicated that the initiative came in the first instance from the בנות מואב (see Ch. 25,18 & XXXI,16 and above on XXIV,14).

V. 2. ותקראנה וגו׳. Those by whom they had been led astray invited them to their sacrificial feasts and finally brought them to prostrate themselves before their Peor gods in whose cult sensual depravity ceased to be sinful but became a homage-showing giving oneself up to the power of the gods.

V. 3. ויצמד וגו׳. There were several בעלים, deified powers. There was a בעל צפון a midnight god of the desert (Ex. 14,1). In contrast, there was a בעל מעון (XXXII,38) a god of habitations, and a בעל ברית (Judges 8,33) a god of the union of nations. There was also a בעל זבוב (Kings II. 1,2) a god of flies, probably a god of decay, cf. זבובי מות (Eccl. 10,1) to whom one prayed in illnesses to intervene between life and death, and there was also a בעל פעור, a god of shamelessness, to whom one paid homage by giving brazen, unabashed prominence to the most animal aspect of human life. Hence Hosea says in IX,10 באו בעל פעור וינזרו לבשת “they came to Baal Peor and dedicated themselves to shame”. צמד. See Ch. 19,15. The cult of Peor is an illustration of that kind of Darwinism that revels in the conception of Man sinking to the level of beast and, stripping itself of its divine nobility learns to consider itself just a “higher” class of animal. ויחר אף וגו׳. But thereby the very first condition on which Israel’s future before God rested was destroyed. Thereby God’s wrath against Israel was again kindled and He “touched” (נגע I.L.) those who had become unworthy to live with מגפה (sudden death I.L.) cf. Ch. 17,11 & 12.

V. 4. ויאמר וגו׳. The procedure of the Torah Criminal Court rests purely and entirely on a charge being brought against a person. The Jewish Court itself had no authority to intervene on its own initiative if there is no accuser. But no public prosecutor is appointed to be such an accuser, but the whole nation is appointed to be the State’s legal prosecutor in Jewish jurisdiction. Every two men out of the public have the duty of presenting a criminal, at the moment of the crime about to be committed, with the law and the legal punishment attached to that particular crime. If in spite of this the crime is committed, they have to bring the criminal whom they have warned to the Court and, in the name of the law, demand the punishment to be inflicted. So that if, on any particular occasion, no witnesses bring the criminal to court, this latter has no legal authority to exercise its rights of judgment. But just because here, at such a widespread infectious open defection from the law, no men from the public intervened and warned the criminals, and after the perpetration of the crime, dragged the criminals before the judge, and thereby tried to stay the spread of the crimes, just that made each inactive witness into an accessory of the crime, and so drew the whole nation into responsibility for what was happening. Therefore it says: ויחר אף ה׳ בישראל, and therefore God gave Moses the authority and thereby the duty for an exceptional intervention — הוראת שעה — by the court. קח את כל ראשי העם, these are the שופטי ישראל mentioned in the next verse. This קח וגו׳ corresponds completely to the ויקח משה ואהרן את האנשים וגו׳ of Ch. 1,17 where distinguished men were taken by Moses and Aaron to act as co-working assistants in carrying out any official procedure that was demanded of them. So here, Moses, as the highest authority of the Law and the personification of the Sanhedrin — משה במקום שבעים וחד קאי — (Sanhedrin 16b) took all the ראשי העם, the שרי אלפים etc., who had been appointed as judges (Deut. 1,15 & 16) to his assistance and carried out the סקילה penalty prescribed by law for עובד ע״ז on all those who had worshipped פעור, the punishment to which, for מגדף ועובד ע״ז, momentary תליה (hanging I.L.) after death was attached (Sanhedrin 46b; see on Levit. 20,2).

והוקע אותם לה׳. That in such a moment when a large part of the people had fallen into idolatry, God should simply say אותם to Moses without further specification is deeply significant. It was just those concerning whom Moses’s mind was full, could only have been filled, the guilty ones who were pushing his people down such an abyss.

In Leviticus (ibid.) we have already understood the meaning of תליה על העץ attached to the סקילה penalty in cases of מגדף and עובד ע״ז as being a suggestive stressing of the sense in which this particular form of punishment is to be taken. If, we thought, already סקילה in itself, actually a killing by the earth, designates those crimes (there are sixteen of them, six acts of grossest sexual immorality and the other ten associated with idolatry or denial of God I.L.) for which it is prescribed as being such against which the very earth itself revolts, and refuses to allow the criminal to continue living on it, then this depravity of the criminal in the very worst cases of depravity is further demonstrated by תליה for one minute, to say thereby that heaven and earth reject the מגדף and עובד ע״ז and grant them no place on which to rest. It is just this conception which the term הוקע expresses most poignantly. For יקע appears to be a stronger form of יגע. But יגע means to be without rest, so that הוקע, the momentary hanging of the dead body of the criminal on a gallows, is the most striking expression for the state of absolute lack of any resting-place in heaven or earth into which his crime would have brought the criminal had not the punishment inflicted on him accomplished atonement for him. (See Sanhedrin 47b).

לה׳ .והוקע אותם לה׳ נגד השמש, to satisfy thereby the demand of God, Who only bases a future for Israel on purity of the principle of morality and the thought of God. By removing the criminals from the ranks of the living population and the visible proclamation of the depth of depravity of the sin committed, the idea of the holiness of the principle involved is established again and “ה׳״ can allow His relationships to Israel to be resumed. נגד השמש, the whole procedure of criminal cases according to Jewish Torah-Law, תחלת הדין, the beginning of the case, גמר דין, the verdict and also the carrying out of the sentence has to be ביום in day time; it is a part of the clear, upright, free, social-human life of the day. It does not belong to the dark, gloomy, sunless spirit of revenge. It is a procedure of duty to be carried out by the nation conscious of itself and its mission, bringing atonement to itself and the Law, and to the criminal himself. Hence לה׳ and וישׂב .נגד השמש instead of the usual יָשׁוב definitely expresses a return to a previous condition which one had reluctantly left. Thus ילך וישב לביתו (Deut. 20,5 et seq.) וישב למקומו (Sam. I. 5,11) וישב אל מקומו (ibid. XXIX,4) וישב העפר על הארץ (Eccl. 12,7) et alia.

V. 5. אל שופטי ישראל ,ויאמר וגו׳ (see V.4). אנשיו, just as later on in addition to the highest court of seventy-one which sat in a hall of the Temple in Jerusalem, every large city had its criminal court of twenty-three members, in the same way during the wandering in the wilderness the people were divided into groups under the jurisdiction of appointed judges over each group (see Ex. 18,21), or, according to Sanhedrin 35a חלק להם בתי דינין, here an ad hoc division of the people was made under a corresponding number of courts. אנשיו וגו׳ would then refer here to the people under each of such judges. So that each court is to judge and sentence those of the people placed under its jurisdiction who had committed the crime of worshipping Peor. איש would be not the individual judge but the presiding judge, אב בית דין, after consultation and agreement with his colleagues on the bench.

V.6. והנה: before this order had been carried out, and while the judges of the nation were still gathered around Moses. איש מבני ישראל: from V. 14 we learn that it was one of the tribal princes. Nevertheless here he is designated simply as “a man of the children of Israel”, so that what follows is to be taken purely from the standpoint of “a Jewish man”. Sure though it is that his sin must appear worse through his rank as prince, as one who should set the example as a pattern of noble moral purity, and sure though it is that Phinchas’s act must appear greater the higher the man stood above him in rank on whom he became the avenger of the Torah — which is also indeed doubtless why verses 14 & 15 informes us of the rank of the man and the woman — nevertheless it is certain that the sinfulness of the sin which here was committed and avenged did not consist just in his being a prince. It was the “Jewish man” the “איש מבני ישראל״ who, with the “Midianite woman” the “מדינית״, derided God and His Torah and Israel and thereby in flagrante delicto was subject to the קנאין, those who are zealous adherents to God and His Law and .ישראל הבועל את הארמית קנאין פוגעין בו.

ויקרב, he brought her there, up to them just to deride them. The עדת בני ישראל, as also מתוך העדה of V.7 is probably the gathering of the judges called by Moses (see Sanhedrin 82a). — והמה בוכים, the sight was so overwhelmingly painful that they had no strength or thought for virile action.
V. 7. מתוך העדה, he was probably one of the judges assembled about Moses. רמח related to רמה to shoot an arrow, נושקי רומי קשת (Ps. 18,9), רמח, a javelin.

V. 8. קבה from קבב (to hollow out, see XXII,11 from which we get קבה, a small tent, according to Menachoth 31b narrower above than below. קבתה from the related root קוב from which we get קבה the stomach, the abdominal cavity. — תעצר המגפה and there was no further necessity to carry out the exceptional intervention of the law ordered in V.4, רמב״ן refers to Deut. 4,3, כ׳ כל איש אשר הלך אחרי בעל פעור השמידו ה׳ אלקיך מקרבך according to which all those who fell to the cult of Peor met their death by the Hand of God.

V. 9. ארבעה ועשרים אלף. At the Golden Calf only three thousand fell, and although there, too, in addition, guilty ones also died by sudden death, the number that fell here still seems to have considerably greater. Thus a cult of idol-worship of depraved immorality gains infinitely more ground than mere metaphysical idol-aberration.

V. 11. פינחס, the “י״ has to be written זעירא, small. It is not impossible that his name was originally פנחס but that the י was added after his energetic stepping forward to make it sound as נחס ;פי נחס being the same as נחץ, to urge on, to say thereby “my mouth, the mouth of God urged me to it”. קנא .בקנאו את קנאתי, see Gen. 26,14 and Ex. 20,5. It is significant that בקנאו the Piel-form is written without a Dagesh in the Nun, accordingly in the Kal-form. Whereas קנא in the Piel designates acting in demanding the rights of somebody which one takes charge of, קנא in the Kal expresses more the feeling that one has for somebody else’s affairs which one takes to heart as if they were one’s own. So that this way of writing the Piel in the Kal-form here would say that Pinchas’s act was not merely an external forward rush but the result of his deep inner feeling which made a betrayal of God’s affairs felt as treachery against one’s own self.

בקנאו וגו׳ בתוכם ולא כליתי וגו׳. He asserted My Rights and made them respected amongst the people, and thereby saved the whole nation from the destruction into which they would irrevocably have fallen had I been forced to assert My Rights Myself. If a challenge to God finds no champion amongst a circle of human beings and the consciousness of the Rights which God has on them has disappeared from this circle, then they have lost God, and thereby their own future existence. And this must be the case especially in the Jewish circle of human beings, Israel, whose whole human historical existence rests on the word “לי״ with which God called Israel “His”, and thereby dedicated every member of it to be “His” in every phase of its existence, and for all eternity makes this Right of Possession valid. Israel is either “God’s” or it ceases to exist.
One such single man, a Phinchas, and one such single manly deed becomes the saviour of the whole nation.

V. 12. לכן אמר וגו׳, not אמר לו or אליו, but in general, make it known generally and let everybody take it to heart: הנני נתן לו את בריתי שלום! As in Levit. 26,42 it talks of a ברית יעקב, a ברית יצחק, a ברית אברהם, and thereby every condition conceived under the concept “אברהם ,יצחק ,יעקב״ is designated as a ברית, as an absolute decision of God sustained by His Promise, so here it says a ברית שלום, and thereby the concept “שלום״, the state of the most complete harmony of all the conditions of the world with each other and with God is declared to be a “ברית״. An absolute decision sustained by God’s Promise, the ultimate realisation of which is guaranteed to have the absolute attention of God’s rule, and is therefore absolutely guaranteed ultimately for the world. God places the responsibility for the realisation of this highest harmony of Peace just on that way of thinking, that disposition and way of acting which a world hiding its thoughtless inactive forgetfulness of its duty under the cloak of “love of peace” — likes to designate and condemn as “disturber of peace”. “Peace” is something highly precious, for which everything, all one’s own rights and possessions may be sacrificed, but never the rights of others and never what God has declared to be right and good. True Peace of men with each other rests on the peace of all of them with God. He who dares to wage war with people who are against Divine Goodness and Truth is, in the midst of his fight and by it, fighting for the ברית שלום on earth. He who, for the sake of so-called peace, quietly leaves the field to people who are really at variance with God, his love of peace is at one with the enemies of the ברית שלום on earth. It was not the inactive standing apart of the masses, not even the tears of those who stood inactive at the entrance of the Sanctuary weeping at the treason, it was the honest brave act of Phinchas which saved the nation and restored his peace with God and His Law and thereby brought back the basis for real true peace on earth. Thus God calls His ברית which He has entrusted to the general Levite spirit: “Life and Peace” (Malachi 2,5) בריתי היתה אתו החיים והשלום ואתנם לו מורא וייראני ומפני שמי נחת הוא “My ברית was with him: of Life and Peace. I gave him that, for fear that he had was solely fear of Me and bowed himself only before My Name”.

But the “ו״ in שלום is a ויו קטיעא, according to the most general way of taking it a broken Vov. For the Phinechas-covenant is just the “rejoined” peace. Where “Phinchas” zeal is required is just where real peace is broken. And the “Phinchas” fight is just for the re-establishment of true peace, he wants to make שלום again שלם. To this the Gemora (Kidushin 86b) attaches the sentence that בעל מום שעבד עבודתו פסולה, that the מום of an officiating כהן makes the עבודה invalid. It says here of Phinchas entering the priesthood:- הנני נתן לו את בריתי שלום כשהוא שלם ולא כשהוא חסר הא שלום כתיב א״ר נחמן ויו דשלום קטיעה היא “he who wishes to restore the peace broken with God, — and that is what every עבודה is symbolic of — must himself be שלם״.

V. 13. והיתה לו וגו׳. When Phinchas was begotten Eleazar was still a זר. Hence till now Phinchas did not bear the character of a priest. But just like the tribe of Levi by their coming to the fore at the Golden Calf attained the rank of “Levites”, which made them worthy of their then being expressly chosen, so did Phinchas by his rescuing deed truly a “directing sign-post”, truly act as כהן showing the way, and achieved the atoning devotion which the עבודה of the priests in the Sanctuary symbolically performed. That was why he was raised to the priesthood after such an act, and the everlasting covenant of priesthood given to him and his descendants here was substantiated by the fact that all the highpriests came from his descendants (see Chron. I,V, 39-41), and the highpriests of the second Temple were also, according to the ספרי, from his descendants (see תוספות, Yoma, 9a). Moreover Phinchas himself was granted a very long life. Even at the time of the murderous attack of the men of Gabeah (Judges 20,28) we find פינחס בן אלעזר בן אהרן as High Priest at the Ark of the Covenant of God. Yea, according to one opinion Phinchas was identical with Elijah in whose standing up for God in Israel against Baal, the spirit of Phinchas ruled; and it is he who will in the future come again to pave the way for the realisation of the ברית שלום, ultimate peace on earth, by healing the breach of the ages when the future will break away from the past, and by bringing the old Horeb spirit of submission to Law by all mankind the riddle of the ages will be solved, and universal peace and brotherhood of Man be established. Does not the very last word of prophecy run:- זכרו תורת משה עבדי אשר צויתי אותו בחרב על כל ישראל חקים ומשפטים הנה אנכי שלח לכם את אליהו הנביא לפני בא יום ה׳ הגדול והנורא והשיב לב אבות על בנים ולב בנים על אבותם פן אבוא והכיתי את הארץ חרם.

V. 14. ושם איש ישראל. see on V.8. The high rank of the man against whom Phinchas rose, raises still higher the significance of his acts. Undeterred by any consideration for the possible serious consequences to his own interests, he had only thought for the affairs of God — אשר הוכה את המדינית only את המדינית, together with the woman, in delecto flagranti was the act of Phinchas a laudable one. Had he done it afterwards it would have been a murder, incurring capital punishment (see Sanhedrin 82a) — בית אב here is synonymous with משפחה, a tribal family from which the whole tribe branches (see Ch. 26,12).

V. 15. ושם האשה וגו׳. Phinchas was also not deterred by any consideration of the possible enmity which his act might bring about against the nation. Nothing at all mattered when it was a question of saving the soul of his nation for faithfulness to God and His Law. — ראש אמות בית אב, here בית אב designates one of the tribes into which the Midian nation was divided. He was the head of one of these tribes, but at the same time ראש אמות, the influential head of the united national tribes.

V. 17. צרור וגו׳, literally means to press together, to oppress, to limit someone’s strength. The Midianites deserve צרור, that you break their might, and והכיתם אותם and you will receive the order to wage war against them and smite them. (see Ch. XXXI).

V. 18. כי צררים וגו׳, for they still threaten you as enemies with ruin. So Haman was called צורר היהודים (Esther 8,1). They still continue to employ the seductive arts which they have already exercised with only too great success against you. In this they differ from the Moabites who after they had once succeeded in bringing trouble and corruption and death to you ceased from further attempts. But the Midianites persisted in this hostile threat to your morality and your adherence to your duty to God’s Law, and in their case this hostility which they have already proved to have towards you is further nurtured by the special feeling of revenge, as their princess did not die in the general death of the plague but was killed by the hand of a Jew and they felt they had to take up the vendetta for their “sister”. The character of her father as ראש אמות gave Cosbi the national status of a sister to all of them.

V. 1. ויהי אחרי המגפה. The chapter finishes in the middle of a verse after the first sentence, and begins a new chapter with the concluding sentence in order to make it clear that with the death of those that fell in the Peor sin, a fresh pure chapter in the life of the people could start again. With the dying-off of those depraved by the sexual rites of Peor-worship, Israel could again shine forth in the hereditary nobility of sexual purity, as the Moabite prophet saw them before the Peor seduction, and for which every census taken of this people offered the most striking proof. Hence, after the מגפה a fresh counting was to be made. That every individual could still be counted למשפחתו לבית אביו as was done forty years previously after the exodus from Egypt was the proof that there was no doubt as to the paternity of any child in Israel, was the proof that the Peor debauchery was only an isolated exception, but that the words of the seer יזל מים מדליו וזרעו על מים רבים was in accordance with the actual facts of the life of the people (see מדרש אספה in the Yalkut on the verse).

V. 3—4. וידבר וגו׳ אתם. Not ויפקד אתם but וידבר אותם, here too, as was ordered at the first census Ch. I & II, למשפחתם לבית אבתם במספר שמת כל זכר לגלגלתם each individual was counted by name as belonging to his home and his family. Not to know the total number, the “counting” was the essential purpose. Each one being named according to his descent, his belonging to his family and tribe for his national public calling as יוצא צבא ישראל, was what was essential, and what was to give each individual the conscious feeling of his own importance for his house, his family, his tribe and his participation in carrying out the general task and mission of the nation. That which there is said in detail by למשפחתם וגו׳ במספר שמת וגו׳ is here piquantly summed up in the one phrase וידבר אותם “they spoke to each individual separately.” But the occasion which called for this counting made it of special importance to designate each individual specifically by name, as just such “announcing” each one according to his descent proved the sexual purity of the families. This probably is also the reason why just at this counting the naming of the families of each tribe is stressed.

But it is certain that this “calling out” the six hundred thousand names was not done by just two men, and that here too, as at the first census, Moses and Eleazar were assisted by the נשיאים. So that the וידבר does not mean so much that they actually “spoke” as that they “caused to be spoken”. Moses and Eleazar were only the organisers who gave the orders, and this explains the: לאמד at the end of the verse. “They arranged it to be said”. The punctuation, with an Ethnach (a semi-colon I.L.) on מואב separating it essentially from על ירדן וגו׳ is remarkable. It really makes two sentences of it and implies the repetition of וידבר משה to :על ירדן ירחו וידבר וגו׳ אותם בערבות מואב and וידבר וגו׳ אותם על ירדן ירחו. That gives the counting a dual purpose: בערבות מואב referring to the event which took place there, as we have already worked out, and על ירדן ירחו with reference to the taking possession of Palestine which they were now about to do (see V.53).

V. 5. משפחת החנכי. Each tribe divided itself into several family branches, the ancestor who gave the family its name being in most cases the eldest son of the tribal ancestor, only that in some cases, as so often happens with first names, the name becomes slightly changed.
