In some cases, as Judah, Ephraim and Benjamin, the grandchildren, in Menassah even the great-grandchildren formed separately named family branches. That, as רמב״ן remarks, the number of family branches did not depend on the greater or lesser number of the members of the tribe as evident, as e.g. compare Dan and Benjamin. Out of forty-five thousand members of Benjamin there were seven separate branches, whereas in Dan there was only one family branch and the tribe numbered sixty-four thousand.

V. 9. הוא דתן ואבירם. According to Baba Bathra 117b, all those that took part in the rebellion of Korach were considered as non-existent at the division of the land whereas the other יוצאי מצרים even if they had died before the entry into the land had to be considered as the real people taking possession of the land amongst whom the land was to be divided. Those between whom the land really had to be divided, the actual active takers of the land, were only to be taken as their heirs (see on Ch. LIII). עדת קרח לא היה להן חלק בארץ הבנים נטלו בזכות אבי אביהן ובזכות אבי אמותיהן. According to רמב״ן this is the reason for mentioning the death of Dathan and Abiram here. — אשר הצו וגו׳, the uprising against Moses and Aaron was in reality an uprising against God, hence ותפתח וגו׳.

V. 10. נס .ויהיו לנס is an emblem raised on high to direct those who are to follow a certain direction to a certain goal. The downfall of Dathan and Abiram was such a conspicuous act of God to be a direction for the teaching of the way of life to be followed or avoided to those who require such direction. In the Hebrew of a later period the term נסים is very much used for all prominent Acts of God which have occurred to teach us lessons.
V. 11. ובני קרח לא מתו (see Ch. 17,3).

V. 14. אלה משפחות השמעני. Above at the first counting, Ch. 1,22 when the moral honour of the tribe of Simeon had not yet been besmirched we find the concept פקודים used, twice, פקדיהם פקדיו to tell us at once at the second tribe that it, as all the following tribes, was not counted en masse, but quite individually, as the tribe of Reuben had been (refer to it there). Here, at the second counting after one of their princes had behaved in such an extremely dishonourable manner, and according to Sanhedrin 92a, the tribe itself had a prominent part in sharing the guilt, the honourable term לפקדיהם or ופקדיהם is missing and the whole report is made as curt as possible. The number of the tribe of Simeon is strikingly the smallest of all the tribes and has fallen by fully thirty-seven thousand from the number counted forty-years previously! It is not far fetched to assume that the greater part of the twenty-four thousand who died in the plague may have come from the tribe of Simeon.

V. 34. ופקדיהם. Whereas at most of the others it simply says אלה משפחת וגו׳ לפקדיהם, here at Menasseh and the following Benjamin it makes two sentences of it אלה משפחת וגו׳ ופקדיהם and thereby gives the result of the count special consideration. When we note that the total number of the nation had decreased by some thousands, that this census had been preceded by the death of all the יוצאי מצרים over twenty years of age, as well as by the repeated death toll of קברות התאוה, by Korach’s uprising, by נחשים השרפים, by Peor, then in an increase in the numbers of a tribe would lie a most honourable certificate of its having remained true and faithful to the fulfilment of its duty. This reflection is particularly applicable to the two tribes Menasseh and Benjamin. At the first counting they were definitely the smallest of the tribes and Menasseh had now to show the largest increase, over twenty thousand and Benjamin over ten thousand. Benjamin was only surpassed by Issachar with nineteen thousand and by Asher with his thirteen thousand. We consider it not unlikely that this is the reason for the different construction of the verses in the cases of Menasseh and Benjamin. At Naphtali (V.50) it also says ופקדיהם although the increase was only one thousand, probably because it is the conclusion of the counting, just as at Reuben the beginning of the count (V.7) is reported by a separate verse ויהיו פקדיהם.

V. 42. אלה משפחת דן למשפחתם, similarly in V.50 אלה משפחת נפתלי למשפחתם. We have already seen above, e.g. at Menasseh, that the conception משפחה is taken in a wider and narrower sense. The משפחת המכירי includes the משפחת הגלעדי as a sub-division and this again has six משפחות under it. For the word משפחה, from שפח related to ספח ,שפע etc., really means “group” and so can designate either larger or smaller grouping. Of Dan only a single family group השוחמי is recorded. This itself consisted already of several משפחות which again branched into further families, and the same applies to the משפחת נפתלי.

V. 53. לאלה וגו׳. Those who were counted here על ירדן ירחו in full view of the Promised Land, were those to whom the land would come to be divided, all the male באי הארץ over the age of twenty, and indeed במספר שמות “according to the number of names”. If we understand this term correctly, it tells us that every one who was named at this counting was to receive a plot of land as his own property. But at this counting the names of the tribes, the names of the families, and the names of every male member of each family who was over twenty years of age was mentioned: למשפחתם לבית אבתם כל זכר לגלגלתם (Ch. I & II,4). Accordingly the land was to be divided so that each tribe, and in each tribe every family every male individual over twenty years of age received his own defined piece of land. Thus immediately at the division of the land under Joshuah, the noun למשפחתם (Josh. XV) was prominently employed. And שמיטין and יובל are dependent on the land not only being in the possession of Israel as a nation, and perhaps being distributed amongst the tribes, but on the division being made to families, heads of families, and right down to the individuals. מנין אתה אומר כיבשו ולא חלקו, חלקו למשפחות ולא חלקו לבתי אבות ואין כל אחד ואחד מכיר את חלקו יכול יהו חייבים בשמטה ת״ל שדך שיהא כל אחד (ת״כ בהר) ואחד מכיר שדהו כרמך שיהא כל אחד ואחד מכיר את כרמו. This seems to be a realisation of what we have repeatedly remarked as being the fundamental character of the Jewish nation, that the greatest diversity of tribal family and individual characteristics within an equally great spiritual and moral uniformity belong to the calling of the People of the Torah. (See Gen. 25,11 and XLVIII,3). Each tribe, each branch of it, each home had its own special characteristics which it is to keep and develop and which is to have its place on the common universal ground of the Torah, as indeed the most dearly-beloved and intimate description of Israel’s being installed in God’s Land is נטיעה “being planted”.

V. 54. לרב וגו׳ איש וגו׳. As an individual has no פקודים belonging to him, but is himself a unit belonging to the איש ,פקודים here cannot mean an individual but can only mean the tribe and family looked on as a unit to which the twenty year old men are numbered as its members. So that the size of the territory allotted to a tribe and to any משפחה of it is to be measured by its size and that is to be reckoned not by the numbers at the time of the division of the land but by the numbers counted at this census. Accordingly as the ultimate result of the distribution every twenty year old man of the באי הארץ was to receive a piece of land and to receive it as a member of his family branch, itself a member of its particular tribe, so that through the position of their homestead the families and the tribes were held together.

V. 55. אך בגורל יחלק וגו׳. But the result of the division described in the preceding verses is not to be made by mutual compromise or by the decision of the national authorities, but בגרל and על פי גרל (V.56) but obtained and settled by lots with the assistance of a declaration of the אורים ותומים (Baba Bathra 122a).

לשמות מטות אבתם ינחלו. According to ר׳ יונתן (117a ibid.) these words contain an important modification of the principle on which the division was to be made as laid down in V.53; שמות מטות אבתם: For the באי הארץ who actually took possession of the land are considered as being only the present generation of their fathers named in the first counting as יוצאי מצרים. They, these fathers, named in that census should really have achieved the actual possession of the land; it was to them that the promise was given: ונתתי אתה לכם מורשה. If then they, these fathers, as a result of their rejection of the land (Numb. 14,31), lost the actual taking possession of the land, and their children received the land in their stead, and so, according to V.53 all the male descendants of the יוצאי מצרים who had reached twenty years were to have the right to participate in having possession of the land, they are, according to this V.55, לשמות מטות אבתם ינחלו, only to exercise this right for the names of their fathers, in the names of their fathers. They only came into possession of the land as their delegates, only as their heirs, just as they, too, the fathers, were only promised it as a heritage from their forefathers, as מורשה, as it says ונתתי לכם מורשה אני ה׳, ירושה היא לכם מאבותיכם וליוצאי מצרים קאמר להו (Baba Bathra 117b). According to that, the division of the land was to be based on a combination of both principles, on the באי בארץ to those מספר שמות who were counted in ערבות מואב, and on the יוצאי מצרים of the first counting referred to as שמות מטות אבתם. If, for example, amongst those counted of the יוצאי מצרים there were two brothers A and B of whom A had one son and B nine sons who now come as באי הארץ to have possession of the land, then if the land were to be divided amongst the יוצאי מצרים and these sons now to be considered to have rights solely as their heirs — as in fact is the opinion of ר׳ יאשיה ibid., 117a — the nine sons of B together would only receive the same size of territory as the one son of A. If the principle of the באי הארץ count were to be the sole principle adopted, then the nine sons of B would get nine portions and the one son of A only one portion. According to the combined principles the sons of A and B would get, the one one and the others nine, together ten portions, but they do not receive purely in their own rights but at the same time as delegate heirs of A and B. They take the ten portions together לשמות מטות אבתם as מורשה! a heritage from their fathers A and B, so the one son of A takes half i.e. five portions and the nine sons of B get the other half i.e. five portions between them. This mode of division is called חזרה, “going back”, as, in the property acquired now, one goes back and considers it having been acquired by the father or grandfather, hence the saying משונה נחלה זו מכל נחלות שבעולם שכל נחלות שבעולם חיין יורשיו מתים וכאן מתים יורשין חיין (ibid.) “this case is an apparent paradox, that the dead, the father, the grandfather receives a heritage from the living”.

When we consider this mode of the division of the land more closely, the land is presented as being treated as every father of the יוצאי מצרים being adjudicated to as many portions of the land as grandsons of his over the age of twenty entered the land, and that this legacy of theirs is only inherited by such of their sons who were over twenty years of age when as יוצאי מצרים they left Egypt and then could bequeath it to such of their sons who were באי הארץ over twenty years of age.
Two facts were thereby to be immortalised in the Doomsday Book of the Jewish National Land.

That which God promises is so certain that it is to be considered as being fulfilled even before it is carried out. Not only those redeemed even those still languishing in slavery under the hard Egyptian yoke are considered as already possessors of the God-promised soil with legal rights for their descendants. Therefore the Land of Israel was legally considered as מוחזק, as being already the actual property of the ancestors, not as ראוי as their merely having a claim to its possession, so that at its division, the right of בכור (the legal right of the firstborn in the distribution of legacies I.L.) could be effective (Ch. 27,6 and Deut. 21,17).

The greatest and richest acquisitions of parents are sons and grandsons who prove true and faithful. They are the witnesses of the merit of the parents and atonement for their weaknesses. Just as Jacob called his sons — according to the way we took the meaning of Gen. 48,22 to be — the conquests he had won from the Emorites and the trophies of his life, so here the number of good honest children go in thought to the credit of the account of fathers and grandfathers. That such a great number, that over six hundred thousand vigorous men, after all the trials of Egyptian slavery breaking all spirit and feelings were after all ready to follow the lead of God and be worthy of redemption, that an almost equal number again over six hundred thousand vigorous men should, after all the sins and errors and exhausting and galling disasters of the wandering in the wilderness stand ready and worthy for the land of the Divine Torah, to whom a Moses could say ואתם הדבקים בה׳ אלקיכם חיים כולכם היום, that was due to the spirit which the ancestors, in the midst of the presence of the Egyptian slavery succeeded in planting in their children. And every little plot of ground which the grand-children received in the Holy Land they lay in spirit, acknowledgingly at the feet of the grandparents as being their conquests. אמשל לך משל is a saying of our sages (Baba Bathra 117a) לשני אחים כהנים שהיו בעיר אחת לאחד יש לו בן אחד ואחד יש לו שני בנים והלכו לגורן זה שיש לו בן אחד נוטל חלק אחד וזה שיש לו שני בנים שני חלקים ומחזירין אצל אביהן וחוזרין וחולקין בשוה. “See it is like two brothers who are priests, of whom one had a single son and the other two who went to a barn to receive the gifts to be given to priests. The one who was sent there by one son received one portion, the other, two, but they took all that they had received to their father’s home to which they still belonged and to whose merit it was due that the gifts were given to the three grandsons, and divided the whole amount equally between the two fathers”. (In the Yalkut the version in the above ברייתא reads אצל אבי אביהן. But in the wording of our ברייתא the two brothers are the subject of the predicate מחזירין so that אביהן is already the grandfather. This seems to have escaped the notice of several commentators).

And the fact that these sons who were found worthy to take possession of the land still received it only לשמות מטות אבתם only as bearing the names and being the heirs of their fathers, is, after all, a proof that these fathers who by their erring lost permission to enter the land, still had understood in the thirty-eight years of their wandering to instil and nurture the right spirit in the breast of their following generation so that it, again as over six hundred thousand vigorous men stood ready and worthy to follow God’s Guidance into the Holy Land. It is, after all, a proof that they understood how to atone for their sin by their children, and, as our sages remark the דור המדבר was still a דור דעה (the generation that had to die in the wilderness was nevertheless an understanding one I.L.) במדבר רבה (Ch. 19). As the Gemora remarks in Sanhedrin 110b the word of the Prophet Jeremiah (II,2) looks back with love on that generation of the wilderness: הלוך וקראת באזני ירושלים לאמר זכרתי לך חסד נעוריך אהבת כלולותיך לכתך אחרי במדבר בארץ לא זרועה. “God says: Go and proclaim in the ears of Jerusalem, saying: Thus saith God, I remember unto thee the tenderness of thy youth, the love of thine espousals when thou wentest after Me in the Wilderness, into the land that was not sown”. And our sages remark hereon: ומה אחרים באים בזכותם הם עצמן לא כ״ש. “If others came into the land on their merit, what must they themselves have really deserved”! So that, on the whole, in spite of the repeated relapses the first and last picture of the wandering in the wilderness presents itself as a worthy one.

V. 56. על פי הגורל, according to Baba Bathra, 112a: באורים ותומים, differing from the בגורל of V.55 which means simply “by lot”: נחלתו: as ארץ is feminine as a rule, the נחלתו probably refers to איש in V.54. — בין רב למעט, according to one view there in Baba Bathra, with exact adjustment and equalisation regarding values. It could be on this that Sforno bases his theory that the twelve provinces of the tribes differed in size according to the numbers of the members of the tribe, but in value were all equal. The smaller provinces were more valuable by reason of produce or position.

In our presentation of the mode of division and distribution of the land, we have principally followed Rashi and Rashbam. There are however various other ways in which it has been taken (see תוספות Baba Bathra 117a and Mizrachi thereon).

V.64. ובאלה לא היה איש. Just as at the Golden Calf so, according to ב״ר, the women took no part in the “sin of the spies” (accepting the report and advice of the מרגלים I.L.) and hence were not included in the consequences which ensued therefrom. It says there אותו הדור היו הנשים גודרות מה שאנשים פורצים, “in the generation of the wilderness the women held up that which the men pulled down”. Moreover this ובאלה does not refer to the immediately preceding verses of the tribe of Levi, for the Levites were also not implicated in the מרגלים fate; it refers to the פקודי בני ישראל, the census of the children of Israel which was the principal object of this second counting which was important for the distribution of the land, but in which the Levites had no part.

V. 1. למשפחת מנשה בן יוסף. We have already remarked on V.5 above, how the tribe of Menasseh was the one at which the separation into separate family branches was most prominent. Whereas, for example, in the tribe of Reuben, only the immediate sons formed separate family branches, here, in Menasseh, who, after all was himself only a branch of the general tribe of Joseph, we find Machir, Gilead, Hepher and his brothers, i.e. son, grandson, greatgrandson, all forming separate family branches. With this special tendency of the tribe towards forming their own, independent separate family branches the wail למה יגרע שם אבינו מתוך משפחתו, “Why should the name of our father be done away with from among his family” in the mouth of the daughters (V.4) has an ethical meaning above the mere material interest in vested property. Father, grandfather, greatgrandfather had all formed separate branches of the family and in the forthcoming distribution of the land according to families, their names would be perpetuated in the name of the property allotted to them. And now in the case of Zelophehad shall such a starting of a family name come to an end already in the second generation, and the extraordinary opportunity for its perpetuation which the distribution of the land in the names of the family be lost and his name cease to be remembered! ואלה שמות בנתיו, in Ch. 36,11, they are named in a different order to designate, as is remarked in Sifri, their completely equal worthiness, שכולן שקולות זו כזו.

V. 3. אבינו מת במדבר etc. If our sages remark that these daughters were חכמות ודורשות conversant with the law and of penetrating intelligence, they could have drawn that conclusion from the whole text of their speech. They said everything that was pertinent to the matter and not a word too much. אבינו מת במדבר our father was one of the יוצאי מצרים over whom God had decreed the fate of dying in the wilderness, but who nevertheless, in accordance with the law for the division of the land just proclaimed לשמות אבותם ינחלו, should come into consideration at the distribution. והוא לא היה בתוך העדה etc. Had he belonged to the rebels with Korach we could not have made any claim for his name. Neither the descendants of the מרגלים, the spies, nor of those who joined Korach’s rebellion could claim any right of participation by reason of their names. These were the only ones who were excluded from the rule מרגלים .לשמות אבותם ינחלו ומתלוננים שבעדת קרח לא היה להם חלק בארץ (Baba Bathra 117b and 118b). כי בחטאו מת if he — as every mortal — did not depart this life without having sinned, his sins were personal individual transgressions, he had never any part in any national sin. ובנים לא היו לו and he had never had any sons. Had he had any sons their descendants could stand in the way of our claim. But he never had any and we are his sole descendants.

V. 4. למה יגרע וגו׳. The משפחת החפרי will divide up the whole property which will be allotted to them under the title of the sons of Hepher, they being the head of this family, and if one of these sons had died but had left a son that son would receive his portion as bearer of his father’s name. Why then should the name of our father, just because he left no son but only daughters, not be counted with in the family, and entirely disappear? תנה לנו וגו׳. Let us be counted with in the place of our father in the ranks of his brothers and give us the portion of the possession which he, were he alive, would have had the right to receive amongst his brothers, as Hepher’s sons.
V. 5. נון רבתי .את משפטן the “נ״ has to be written extra large: see on V.6.

V. 6. ויאמר הי אל משה לאמר. Inasmuch as the following laws are introduced by ויאמר and not by וידבר it appears to be not the heading of the new set of laws but explanation of a canon which has already been given. And in fact, by the two laws given above regulating the method of distributing the land, לאלה תחלק הארץ, to the men who had been counted, and לשמות מטות אבותם ינחלו the fundamental norm is given that legacy of land is inherited by the male descendants, as is also implicitly contained in the verse in Levit. 25,46 והתנחלתם אתם לבניכם אחריכם לרשת אחזה. This canon must also have been known already to the daughters of Zelophehad as is expressed quite clearly in their reasoning כי אין לו בן. If there had been a son living or, as is apparent from their saying ובנים לא היו לו, any male descendants at all, they would have had no cause to make a claim. It is therefore also not impossible that the suffix ן in משפטן is so prominently stressed just to say that Moses was already completely well versed in the law of inheritance in general but had to ask for the decision in this specific case. Yea, especially if the principle of חזרה which we expounded on V.55 was the deciding method to be employed in the division of the land, then the law in ordinary cases that in the absence of sons or male descendants the daughters have the right to inherit could well have been fully known to Moses, and the only doubt he had was whether it was applicable to the division of the land, and if so, to what extent it was to be applied. Hence the question for him was really only משפטן, only for their special case. For the question that was troubling him could have been whether as in the case of an ordinary inheritance to give five daughters when there are no male descendants the complete rights of five sons, so here too the five daughters of Zelophehad should be considered as five באי הארץ and receive five portions of land which then, in accordance with the principle of חזרה, would be reckoned together with all the portions of the other descendants of Hepher who were באי הארץ and be divided up between all of them together; or whether — as really the division of the heritage was worded, (see Baba Bathra 118b, רשב״ם ד״ה ותרי דידהו) — the daughters of Zelophehad were not to receive portions as independent באי הארץ but only participate in the distribution as heirs of their father’s one portion which he would have received amongst the other male באי הארץ of the descendants of Hepher, which then, going back by חזרה to Hepher would have to be joined to the portions allotted to Zelophehad’s brothers or respectively their heirs, and split up into equal parts to all of them.

V. 7. כן .כן בנות וגו׳, cf. Gen. 42,11, כנים נחנו, there it is correctness of character, here correctness of speech, a presentation of a fact. That which the daughters of Zelophehad have said is quite as it ought to be, their speech corresponds to the truth and right. דוברות: whereas דַבֵר in the Piel refers more to the audible presentation of thoughts, speaking דבר in the Kal refers chiefly to the contents of the thoughts which the words present, דובר שלום ,דובר מישרים ,דובר צדק etc. דַבֵר is to speak, אמֹר to say, דָבוֹר to specify. — נחלה ,אחזת נחלה, a possession that “flows down” like a stream from those that went before to those that come after. אחזה is like ישועה ,גאולה an active abstract conception, the grip that property exercises, that chains the possessor and gives him a permanent place in the world. (see Gen. 47,27). בתוך אחי אביהם, they take the place of their (uncles) departed brother. If the mode of distribution were simply to the יוצאי מצרים to whom Zelophehad belonged equally with his brothers, then they would receive the portion which was due to Zelophehad as such, they were his heirs. But if the method adopted was that of the חזרה canon according to which the land was first divided among the באי הארץ and then went back from them to the יוצאי מצרים and then divided into equal parts between themselves and their heirs as being a legacy from their forefathers, then had Zelophehad left five sons instead of five daughters, these five sons would first have received five portions which they would then pile together with all that their cousins, the sons of their father’s brothers had received and symbolically return the whole mass as חזרה to the grandfather Hepher and as his heirs divide it equally between them all as Hepher’s sons and their heirs. So that if these daughters of Zelophehad were to have the full rights of sons also in this חזרה method of distribution the decision should have run בתוך בני דודיהם (among their cousins) and not בתוך אחי אביהם (among their uncles) as it does. But as nevertheless the decision does say בתוך אחי אביהם it tells us that they do not receive the five portions similarly to what their cousins would, not בתוך בני דודיהם but they are only to receive the portion which would have been given to their father amongst their uncles as one of the יוצאי מצרים to whom the whole estate of all the cousins reverts by חזרה to חפר, as we have already indicated this on V.5. It is significant that the suffixes used here referring to the daughters are written in the masculine, אביהם ,להם. That says: You are to give them masculine rights of inheritance as if they were sons.

נחלת אביהן .והעברת נחלת אביהן להן, according to the יוצאי מצרים method, the portion their father would have received as a יוצא מצרים. According to the חזרה method, the portion he would have received after dividing the legacy between himself and his brothers. A legacy given over to an heiress is always called העברה a “passing over”. For if she marries a man from one of the other tribes, after her death, this inherited property will pass into the possession of that tribe and be lost to the tribe to which it originally belonged. For her sons belong to the paternal tribe, or — if ירושת הבעל דאורייתא (see V.11) — equally so if her husband inherits the property.
V. 8. ואל בני ישראל וגו׳. The fundamental principle to be applied in this case is to have permanent general application.

ובן אין לו. In Baba Bathra 115a, the Halacha is taught that the אין in this and the following verses is to be taken quite exhaustively. The right to inherit passes from son to daughter only if there is no son in existence in the widest sense, if there is no idea of his existence, if his existence is not represented by any offspring at all. But if there is a son of the son living, a daughter or grandchild of either sex, the right of inheritance passes through that line, and not to or through the sister. Similarly in V.9 the inheritance goes to the brother of the deceased, or in V.10 to his uncle, only when, in the first case there are no descendants from a daughter, or in the second from a brother. Every right of inheritance is hereditary and only passes over to another line if there is no direct descendant in existence however remote, כל הקודם בנחלה יוצאי יריכו קודמין. So indeed in the case before us Zelophehad was represented by his daughters when it was a question of dividing the legacy of Hepher between his descendants and those of his brothers. The Halacha stresses this emphatic meaning of ”אין״ לו by ”עיין״ עליו, i.e. before you say עיין עליו ,אין לו first seek. The son could still be considered to be in existence by some living descendant, then the condition which the Torah makes: ובן אין לו would not be fulfilled (see on Deut. 25,5).

והעברתם וגו׳ (see on V.7). The sense of the law is clear: the daughter has a right of inheritance only if there is no son or descendant of one. Compared to the right of inheritance of a son, that of a daughter is called by the Torah העברה, passing over, leading away. If a son is there the hereditary property remains in the tribe. If it falls to a daughter the risk of “leading away” to another tribe is incurred, hence it is only to occur במקום שאין בן. And even if the son had died before the father but had left a daughter, this granddaughter, as the heir of her father takes precedence for the legacy to the daughter, her aunt. Equally so, the daughter of a son has equal rights with the other sons (her uncles). Baba Bathra 115b, and 116a.

V. 9—11. :ואם אין לו בת וגו ואם אין לו אחים וגו׳ ואם אין אחים לאביו וגו׳ ונתתם נחלתו לשארו הקרב אליו ממשפחתו. The cases discussed in verses 9-11 are only examples for which finally the fundamental principle is given, according to which these and all other cases which are not gone into here are to be judged. This fundamental principle is based on three conceptions: שארו, blood relationship, — הקרב the closeness of such relationships so that הקרוב קרוב קודם the nearer relation has precedence over the more distant and finally ממשפחתו, the relationship must lie within the concept משפחה, the relation must belong to the משפחה of the deceased. But this concept משפחה is formed only by descent from a father not through a mother. אחים, brothers, for example, in the law of inheritance are only such as are begotten by a common father not those born of one mother. Sons of the same mother but of different fathers belong to the different משפחה of the fathers, but sons of one father from different mothers all belong to the same משפחת אב קרויה משפחה משפחת אם אינה קרויה משפחה דכתיב .משפחה למשפחותם לבית אבותם (Baba Bathra 109b). The nearest relations for inheritance of a deceased person are children, and in the first place, sons. The son also represents the father in יעוד (Ex. 21,9) and in שדה אחוזה (Levit. 25,25 and Baba Bathra 108b). If there is no son and no descendant of a son, then, according to V.8 the daughter or her descendants is the heiress.

Next to the children comes שאר הקרוב אליו ממשפחתו, the father. As near as the son is to his deceased father in the descending line is the father to his deceased son in the ascending line. If there are no children or their descendants of the deceased, the legacy goes to the father as the nearest relation upwards or then to his descendants the brothers or possibly (if there are none) the sisters of the deceased. If there is no father and no descendants of his alive, the legacy goes again to the nearest שאר הקרוב אליו ממשפחתו, to the father of the father, the paternal grandfather, of the deceased and then his descendants, the brothers or possibly the sisters of the father and then their descendants, and so on.

The legacy always goes in a direct line, and can only come to a member of a parallel line as a descendant of an heir who inherited by right of a direct ascending line, to siblings only as descendants of the father; to uncles and aunts as descendants of the grandfather. So that as long as the father is alive the brothers cannot inherit neither can the uncles, as long as the grandfather lives etc. סדר נחלות כך הוא, איש כי ימות ובן אין לו והעברתם נחלתו לבתו, בן קודם לבת, כל יוצאי ירכו של בן קודמין לבת, בת קודמת לאחין, יוצאי ירכה של בת קודמין לאחין, אחין קודמין לאחי האב, יוצאי ירכן של אחין קודמים לאחי האב, זה הכלל כל הקודם בנחלה יוצאי ירכו קודמין והאב קודם לכל יוצאי ירכו (Baba Bathra 115a). By the general direction ונתתם נחלתו לשארו הקרב אליו it is made clear that the verses 9 and 10 ונתתם וגו׳ לאחיו and ונתתם וגו׳ לאחי אביו speak only if in V.9 the father and in V.10 the grandfather are no longer alive. For the אחי אביו is only related to him through his father, so the latter is more קרוב to him than an אחי אביו and so the inheritance goes first to אביו and any of his direct descendants of either sex before it can come to an אחי אביו. It is not impossible that the norm for the general procedure given in verses 8 & 9 is directly attached to the special case presented here for decision where חפר was already dead and the question was only whether the heritage was to fall in the distribution of the land to the daughters of Zelophehad or to his brothers. Referring then to this it says that in such a case in general איש כי ימות ובן אין לו, the נחלה is to be given to the daughters and not to the brothers, although with the brothers the property would remain in the tribe whereas with the daughters there was the possibility of its passing right out of the possession of the tribe; and only where there was no daughter or descendant of a daughter ונתתם נחלתו לאחיו.

This norm of inheritance by which the heritage first seeks the descending line for the nearest living descendant and in the absence of any such goes back to the ascending line or any descendant from it, until in this order it finds a living שאר הקרוב אליו ממשפחתו of the deceased is called משמוש (from משש) “grouping”.

Just as the heritage of a father, so does that of a mother, go to the children or their descendants with preferential rights of sons to daughters, and in absence of children or their descendants, goes over to the nearest male forefather or his descendants, but with the limitation, that a maternal heritage only goes down in a direct line, but not, in the case where the woman who left the legacy died without children, to any step-children from the father’s side, but to her משפחה, i.e. to her nearest male ancestor or his descendants. This principle is called: אין הבן יורש את אמו בקבר להנחיל לאחין מן האב i.e. אין הבן בקבר יורש וכו׳ (Baba Bathra 114a). But nevertheless, although a legacy left by a mother goes to her children and descendants, mothers do not inherit legacies left by their children, that goes, as already remarked, if there are no descendants, back, up the line, to male ancestors or their descendants; a principle which by the deciding concept ממשפחתו is already given by our verse as משפחה (ibid. 115a).

Finally, Baba Bathra teaches that the concept לשארו of our text is to be understood to include also, and indeed in the very first place, the relationship of a man to his wife created by marriage (see on Levit. 21,2). Thereby a mutual right of inheritance would be established between husband and wife that, passing over all other relations, the nearest heir to the property of a deceased man would be his wife, and of a wife, the husband, were it not that this right of inheritance of a wife to the property left by her husband was denied by other indications in the Torah. For, as תוספות remarks (ibid.) it would have to be denied already by the fact that then, at every marriage the husband would be given a הסבה, the possibility of a deflexion of property belonging to his tribe to another tribe through his wife whereas the Torah only expresses such a fear in the marriage of women possessing land in their own right to men of other tribes. But regarding the right of inheritance of a husband to property left by his wife this principle remains in force, with, however, the double limitation expressed in the one sentence: אין הבעל יורש את אשתו בקבר (Baba Bathra 114b). This means both (a) that a husband has no rights of inheritance to property which would come to his wife only after her death, property which at the moment of her death was only ראוי for her but not yet actually מוחזק. This goes to her descendants or back to her male ancestors and their descendants. And it also means (b) the husband has only rights of inheritance to property of his wife if he outlives her אין הבעל בקבר יורש את אשתו. Whereas other rights of inheritance, by the principle of משמוש are represented as passing to descendants even if received after death “in the grave” i.e. would have been received by ancestors were they living, this principle is not applied to the right of a husband to the heritage of his wife. As a widow is entitled to marry another husband, the right to any property she leaves at her death which the first husband would have inherited had he outlived her ceases at his death and passes over to her second husband if he outlives her, or in absence of such, to her descendants or back to or through her male ancestors and their descendants. (See תוספות Baba Bathra 114b ד״ה מה אשה and רמב״ן thereon).
Moreover, whether ירושת הבעל דאוריתא or is only תקנת חכמים is not quite decided. According to one way of taking it this right of inheritance of a husband is only דרבנן (see Ketuboth 83b & 84a).
See further on Jewish Rights of Inheritance on Deut. 21,15 et seq.

V. 12. ויאמר וגו׳. This was not yet the command to go up the mountain. That came later (Deut. 32,48) וידבר וגו׳. Here it is only an explanatory addition to the preceding and gives the reason for the following. With the preceding the instructions for the arrangements for the division of the land were concluded, to which the explanation fits that Moses himself will not enter the land. With the sight of the land his active work on earth is to come to its end. Leading the people to the Land of the Torah and completing the preparation of the people for having possession of it formed the extent of his mission. The actual realisation of it was not to be through him. He is to die within sight of, but not in, the land to which he had led the people. Nothing new was told to Moses thereby. He knew of this decree of God since the event which occurred in Kadesh. But now it was to be brought home to Moses that he had now reached the end of his earthly pilgrimage, so that now he should do, on his own initiative all that he would like to do before his departure. That, above all, the appointment of his successor should come as a wish from his own faithful heart, and be still accomplished by him himself. — הר העברים, the Mount of Transition, the mount at which, by crossing the Jordan from one side to the other, the Promised Land is entered.

V. 13. וראיתה. By the addition of the “ה״ at the end of the word it is indicated that this seeing is not said as a command to be carried out immediately (I have translated it “and when thou wilt have seen it” I.L.) but is left to be done at the time of his own choice.

V. 14. כאשר וגו׳. We hardly think that there is another instance of כאשר occurring with the meaning of “because”; in any case its having the meaning of “as” is predominant, and here is all the more to be adopted as it is used just before, in the previous verse, with this meaning. But still the meaning of this comparison is difficult to understand. Possibly thereby Moses’s fate is only declared to be just the same as that of Aaron. As you both were guilty of the same sin for which Aaron has already died now you also must die from the same cause. Perhaps nevertheless it is a comparison of the two facts, the sin and the punishment in view of the long-desired Land. Their sin was the frustration of the Divine Intention. It becomes atoned for by the frustration of a long wished-for goal.

מריתם פי במדבר צין במריבת העדה להקדישני וגו׳ (see on Ch. 20,1-13) להקדישני וגו׳ is the explanation of the פי. God’s command had the intention of להקדישני וגו׳ and what they did worked against this intention. הם מריבת קדש מדבר צין, to differentiate it from the מי מריבה at Rephedim (Ex. 17,1-7) to which these מי מריבה in קדש מדבר צין, offered a complete contrast. In Rephidim, at the beginning of the wandering in the Wilderness, the water gushing out of the rock at the blow of the staff of God was to bring the guarantee for their being taken care of during the whole period of their stay in the desert. It was to reassure them that they could expect the direct intervention of God’s miraculous powers in all times of need, and every pressing requirement would be met. Here in קדש מדבר צין at the end of their wanderings, at the edge of the desert and at the beginning of inherited and habitable lands, here, just by the “non-striking of the rock”, by the effect of the Word of God next to the unused Staff of God, they were to be given the guarantee that in the coming normal conditions of life there would no longer be any necessity for the visible direct intervention of God’s miracles; that they would no longer require the use of Moses’s Staff of God, but that Moses’s Word of God would suffice to obtain God’s granting the way to life and welfare and security in the midst of, and by way of, His natural ordering of matters. A fact which would have expressed itself in this contrast between the two procedures of obtaining water from the rock was driven home by the death of Moses, just as that of Aaron, being connected thereto. With reaching the border of the Land the mission of Moses and Aaron was accomplished. That which God had made them responsible for, teaching the people the way of thinking and showing them the way of living, they had done and that suffices for all time. There is no necessity for further יציאת מצרים miracles and מתן תורה-revelations. Moses and Aaron could be taken home to their people on the other side. For their people here below, that which they had accomplished and taught at God’s command, remained behind them. Henceforth, with both their deaths it says לא בשמים היא, henceforth ושמרתם ועשיתם “guarding and carrying out” the Torah is the task of the people to be certain of God’s help and blessing. Just as it was not Moses’s staff but Moses’s words which was to have given them the life-giving water out of the rock at the border of the Promised Land, so, after this announcement had been frustrated by Moses and Aaron’s error, their death at the border of the Land preached the lesson even more eloquently. Is not this possibly the true explanation of the difficulty discussed above of the meaning of the “כאשר״ in our verse, comparing the death of Moses to that of Aaron?

Thus one of the last prophets at the border of the end of prophecy says: “Your fathers, where are they? and the prophets do they live for ever? But My Words and My Laws which I commissioned My servants the prophets, in truth did they not suffice your fathers” (Zach. 1,5 & 6).

V. 15. וידבר וגו׳ לאמר. This form of introduction to his speech shows the following to be not so much a request as a measure the necessity for which presented itself to Moses immediately following the pronouncement of his impending death. As it was not a matter which concerned his own welfare but solely that of his people he dared to couch his speech in this form: מ״ר) כל מי שמבקש צרכי צבור כאלו בא בזרוע hereon).

V. 16. מגיד הכתוב שכל הרוחות אין יוצאות אלא :אלקי הרוחות לכל בשר מלפניו, ר׳ אליעזר בנו של ר׳ יוסי הגלילי אומר סימן זה יהיה בידך שכל זמן שאדם נתון בחיים נפשו פקודה ביד קונו שנא׳ אשר בידו נפש כל חי מת נתונה באוצר שנא׳ והיתה א׳ הרוחות לכל בשר .נפש אדוני צרורה בצרור החיים. “It is God from Whom every spirit enters its fitting earthly case, it is God Who brings the רוחות to all בשר״; “for it is from Me”, so it says in Is. 57,16 “that the spirit is enclosed in its case, and I have made the souls”, כי רוח מלפני יעטוף ונשמות אני עשיתי (Rab. Eliezer adds thereon: “Hold fast to this idea: as long as a person is granted life, his soul is kept in the Hand of his Creator and Owner, for it says “in Whose Hand is the soul of every living person”: when he dies, however, his soul is stored up in the treasury of eternal life”. According to that God is אלקי הרוחות לכל בשר in a double sense: it is He through Whom the spirit comes into every body, and it is He through Whom the spirit remains in every body. He sends the spirit into the earthly body, and He keeps it there, and protects it, and strengthens it, and feeds it with gifts and progress, so that every soul in an earthly body is, for the duration of that life, personally nearer to God in a much higher degree that when, after its pilgrimage on earth, it is stored away in the “bond of life” with all the other souls which have been gathered and kept for a new future. A fact which seems to Rab. Eliezer of such importance for us to keep in mind throughout our path through this life that he admonishes us to hold it fast always in our hands as a directing sign: סימן זה יהיה בידך! Hence, God, Who, as אלקי הרוחות לכל בשר knows and watches over every soul sent by Him into every earthly body, He knows where to find the right man to be the successor of Moses, let Him appoint him. For even if there is no longer a necessity for Moses and Aaron to remain (see on V.14) it still requires a man to carry out the Divine mission which is now to be realised.

V. 17. יצא ובא לפני- .אשר יצא לפניהם וגו׳ by no means designates only the leading of armies in war. When Solomon begged for a לב שמע לשפט את עמך להבין בין טוב לרע “an understanding heart to judge Thy people, to discern between good and bad” without which he would be unfit to carry out his duties; he described this state of unfitness by ואנכי נער קטן לא אדע צאת ובא (Kings I. 3,7 & 9). יצא ובא is accordingly the term for the general activity of one set at the head of a nation. Yea, in Josh. 14,11, Caleb distinctly differentiates between going to war and לצאת ולבא, he says: ככחי אז ככחי עתה למלחמה ולצאת ולבא “My strength now is just as much as it was then, both for going to war and general getting about”, by לצאת ולבא he refers to his ability, apart from military powers, for public activity of every kind. יצא is altogether going out into publicity in contrast to בא, retiring to private spheres. A man is required אשר יצא לפניהם ואשר יבא לפניהם, who is in the forefront going about as an example for public and private life, and generally by his influence bringing the people to faithfully fulfil all public and private duties. That at the אשר יצא לפניהם וגו׳ leadership in war is not specially thought of is also vouched for by ולא תהי׳ וגו׳ כצאן אשר אין להם רעה, as the activity of a shepherd is devoted to the thriving and welfare of the flock.

V. 18. רוח .איש אשר רוח בו as the wind is something invisible only recognizable by its effects, an active and moving force, in human beings the discerning and willing powers (see Ex. on XXV,39, p.456, 457 et seq.). This spiritual and moral agent is present in every human being. If nevertheless it is said here of Joshuah that he is suitable to be the successor of Moses because he is a man who has רוח in him, רוח can only be meant to be used with an emphatic meaning, as we also call somebody “a man of spirit” one who possesses this quality to an eminent degree. Thus Hosea in 9,7 is called איש הרוח. In Joshua “spirit” was unweakened by material disturbing tendencies. In Deut. 34,9 it says ויהושע בן נון מלא רוח חכמה כי סמך משה את ידיו עליו, after his appointment to be Moses’s successor Joshuah’s natural gift of רוח became yet further enriched and became רוח חכמה with which he was entirely filled.
וסמכת את ידך עליו, see on Levit. 1,4.

V. 19. והעמדת אתו וגו׳. Cf. Ch. 3,6. To place somebody before somebody else means to place him at his disposal, in his service. By placing Joshua before Eliezar and he is placed in the service of the Sanctuary of the Torah (of which the High Priest is the chief representative I.L.) and of the national community. Thus Rabban Gamliel spoke to two of his pupils, who out of modesty, hesitated to accept a high public position to which he offered to raise them:- כמדומין אתם ששררה אני נותן לכם עבדות אני נותן לכם “You imagine it is honour, to be over others, that I offer you, it is service that I give you” (Horioth 10a). צוה .וצויתה אתו לעיניהם is a specific term used for giving the duties to be undertaken by somebody who is being appointed to an office. Thus: וצוך לנגיד על ישראל (Sam. I. 25,30), צויתי שופטים על עמי ישראל (Sam. II. 7,11) לצות אותי נגיד (ibid. VI,21), ויצום אל בני ישראל (Ex. 6,13). So also in Deut. 3,28 וצויתה .וצו את יהושע וחזקהו ואמצהו, you are to charge him with the duties of his office in the presence of the people so that he stands there commissioned by you, and what he does in future will bear your authority.

V. 20. הוד .ונתתה מהודך עליו, phonetically related to אוד, the idea of means, of the effective power of accomplishing something, and to עוד, the idea of lasting existence, הוד is the outward appearance of fullness of existence and power. It is intensively that which הדר means extensively. שמע ,למען ישמעו occurs by itself without a preposition as “obeying”. Thus והנה לא שמעת עד כה (Ex. 7,16), אם תאבו ושמעתם (Is. 1,19), etc. Perhaps it is used here in this way by itself and not למען ישמעו אליו because the obedience to be rendered to Joshua is to be at bottom only an obedience to the Will of God which Joshua learnt through Moses.

V. 21. ולפני אלעזר הכהן יעמד. But he is not set up as an autocrat, but at all occasions of the general national interests, where it is not a question of what is right or wrong in accordance with the revealed Torah, but of the advisability or inexpediency of some national plan, he is to ask and obey the Urim that rest on the breast of the national representative of the Sanctuary of the Torah, the ולפני וגו׳ יעמוד .כהן גדול (see on V.19) ושאל לו. Eleazar asks for the decision of the Urim before God. (see Ex. on Ch. 28,43, p.536-7 et seq.). שאל ב- the usual expression for asking God to give a decision about an undertaking. Thus in Judges 20,18 et seq.; Sam. I. 23; Sam. I. 22,10; XXIII,2; XXVIII,6; XXX,8, etc. ושאל לו בה׳ ,וישאלו באלקים. Hence also עמי בעצו ישאל (Hosea 4,12). As the desired declaration was not made directly by God nor by the Urim directly to the one who sought the decision, this ב seems to indicate the idea of mediation, through an agency. The answer is asked for not by God, but through His instrumentality. The question is made to God for Him to answer through the Urim and Eleazar. — על פיו, according to Eleazar’s declaration. But it is not Eleazar, who gives the answer. He is only the passive organ. וכל העדה, after כל בני ישראל have already been named, כל העדה here can only mean the ב״ד הגדול, the Sanhedrin as in Ch. 25,6 & 7, and Levit. 4,13.

V. 22—23. ויעש וגו׳ ויסמך וגו׳. Perhaps the appointment of Joshua as his successor, given in reply to Moses’s request brought about by his impending death, was only meant to be carried out in general and he was not commanded to do so at once. The reply was only given to Moses that, before his death he was to appoint Joshua in the presence of the people the actual procedure only took place just shortly before his death as recorded in Deut. 31,7. Then the ויעש וגו׳ ויסמך וגו׳ of our verse would only be the concluding information that later on Moses faithfully fulfilled the order. But nevertheless it is still possible that this induction was to be made and was done immediately; and then the ויקרא משה ליהושע וגו׳ in Deut. 31,7 as well as ויצו את יהושע וגו׳ (ibid. 23) would only be repeated admonition and consolidation for the fulfilling of the duties already undertaken — ויסמך את ידיו עליו. The command in V.18 only says וסמכת את ידך עליו but with all his heart and with “both hands”, ידיו, does Moses carry out the behest, and as the words in Sifri run, made Joshua ככלי מלא וגדוש, “to a vessel, full and heaped up” i.e. to a bearer of his spirit and views in the most abundant measure.

V. 1. In the previous chapter, at Moses’s instigation, provision was made that, after his impending death, the People of God should not remain without a leader who would shine in front of them as a model for private and public life, and who would, by his influence, guide and keep the individual and communal life of the people in the paths indicated by God.

But that the people and their leaders should never come to lose this, their calling, that Israel should always keep in mind their never-ending mission, their relations to God from His special guiding of their fate, and their obligations, and take these ever afresh to heart, for that the procedures of the national offerings which follow here, are to be effective. The קרבנות צבור, the public offerings, the תמידים ומוספים are to preach all this, and stimulate the corresponding feelings and vows in the minds of the people, in the eloquent language of the offerings so full of meaning.

Hence they complement the provision made by the appointment of Joshua for the continuation of God’s work on the people which Moses had begun, and follow on to it. One can say:- At his departure Moses is to hand over to Joshua and the קרבנות צבור the work of God which up till then had been entrusted to his care.

This chapter of קרבנות צבור forms in the true sense the end of the real Lawgiving (see on Ch. 30,2). It only comes here in the fourth book, “the Book of the Wanderings in the Wilderness”, and moreover, at the end of it (and not, as we should have expected, in Leviticus, where it would seem to belong I.L.) because, as already remarked on Levit. 23,1, it took these forty years of experiences in the wilderness for us to get to know ourselves, and to make us feel the necessity to be constantly reminded of our relationship to God and of the feelings and vows which that relationship expects of us.

V. 2. צו את בני ישראל וגו׳, the first קרבן צבור, public offering, the basis and bearer of all offerings altogether (see Levit. 6,5) is the תמיד, the constant daily elevating-offering brought every morning and evening. The directions for it were given (Ex. 29,38 et seq.), immediately after the sanctifying dedication of the altar, to show the altar at once in its living activity, the real purpose of its erection and dedication, and we would refer our readers to the explanations given there. Here the uninterrupted carrying out of this institution is made a special national obligation, and at the same time the time for bringing this Tamid-offering as a daily “Moed” (see on Ch. 9,2) is ranked in the number of the rest of the Moadim, yea is placed in front of them all. — צו את בני ישראל (see on Ch. V.2). Looking back on the preceding ויצוהו which placed Joshuah in the service of the public, this צו וגו׳ demands that the nation as a whole is placed in the service of God, and unremittingly by the Tamid-offering constantly reminds itself of this status of being in service. This is the sense in which the Sifri says hereon. עד שאתה מפקדני על בני פקוד בני עלי שלא ינהגו בי מנהג בזיון ושלא ימירו את כבודי באלהי נכר.

את קרבני וגו׳. Here, the Tamid, this basic offering is designated by all the essential points of the relations which offerings in general express. קרבני: the getting near to God; לחמי; by placing all earthly efforts ready to be used for the Presence of God on earth; לאשי: by means of submitting them to the purifying and life-giving fire of God’s Torah (see Levit. 1,2 & 9, and III,11); ריח נחחי, and all this, only as a hint, an indication of giving satisfaction to God by your way of living. Hence in Sifri: קרבני זה הדם, the נפש raising itself up to come near to God; לחמי אלו אימורים the submission of all efforts and all purposes; לאשי אלו קמצים ולבונה: of all food, well-being and joys of life — (although neither קומץ nor לבונה were brought at the Tamid, but the מנחת נסכים was placed on the fire in its entirety, the Sifri nevertheless mentions just such “gifts to the fire” which did not actually occur at the Tamid, just because the Tamid forms the foundation of all other offerings and the קומץ and לבונה of all מנחות are attached to the basic idea of מנחת תמיד) — thus the whole of Man and Nation’s material participation in the goods of this world becomes changed in the eternal fire of God’s Torah to keep alive the Kingdom of God on earth; גירסת הגר״א) ריח נחחי אלו נסכים), so that finally the sum of our highest supreme joy has its roots in the soil of the godly Sanctuary of the Torah, in the consciousness of God’s satisfaction with us and ours.

So that את קרבני לחמי לאשי ריח נחחי, this most precise and concise expression of the whole of our Jewish national position and calling תשמרו להקריב לי במועדו is here made to national מצוה and שמירה, an obligation to be fulfilled with due care in the time “fixed by God for our coming together with Him to bring us near unto Him”. And how did the genius of the Jewish people understand how to carry out this obligation. Drawn from the yearly half-shekel gifts of the ever-fresh (it had to be of the current year I.L.) devotion of every member of the nation, the תרומת הלשכה, the national offerings, but the daily Tamid offerings in particular, were provided for (Menachoth 65a). Four days before they were used — similarly to the Pesach-offering (Ex. 12,3) the continuation of which the Tamid-offering fundamentally formed — six flawless lambs were kept ready in the לשכת הטלאים (Arachim 13a and b). And by no means did one consider the daily national offering brought by the priests in the Temple as an opus operatum, as if that were all there was to it, as if, like the pagan conception of an offering, it was brought “to pay ones dues to the Godhead”. As here in the Torah’s directions for the Tamid, by the use of singular תעשה in V.4, the nation is considered in its totality as a unit and hence the Tamid can only be brought by the representatives of the nation as a whole, but nevertheless in V.2, by the plural תשמרו the duty of constant care over this national offering is imposed on the nation in all its members, Jewish minds have taken it that the Tamid offered in the Temple is only then a true constant national offering if all the living participants show daily, morning and evening, that their minds and feelings are directed to it. וכי האיך קרבנו של אדם קרב והוא אינו עומד על גביו! How can an offering be brought on behalf of somebody if that person is not present personally or at least in spirit? Does not the Torah say: תשמרו להקריב לי במועדו! So already under direction of the earliest prophets the nation divided itself into twenty-four משמרות corresponding to the twenty-four divisions of the priests (Deut. 18,8) who changed duty in the Temple service weekly. Each משמר of the people had people who lived in Jerusalem who attended at the offerings of the Tamidim each day as their representatives. At the same time the other members of the משמר gathered together in their cities morning and evening and by “קריאת התורה and תענית״ attended the Tamidim in spirit, and thereby took to heart the elevating lesson of progress and purification of mind which all the offerings preached. This standing-by at the Tamid offering, personally or in spirit, was called מעמד (Taanith 26a) and through these מעמדות in Jerusalem and in the cities of the land, the consciousness of and participation in, the daily national offering in the Temple was kept keenly alive in the whole nation. Thereby the twofold conviction is nurtured, firstly that for every Jew it is in the Sanctuary of the Torah, the centre point of the nation, that the spiritual hold of his life, his thinking and doing, lies, that his connections with God can only be guaranteed by means of the Torah which rests under the wings of the Cherubim in their own common Sanctuary; and secondly, that just on that account the national vow, freshly renewed daily on the altar of that national Sanctuary, to strive upwards to God in faithful fulfillment of His Torah reckons on every son of the nation and wishes to see its students and fulfillers in the very fartherst and last man of the people. And if even to-day, after all these thousands of years, faithful to the legacy of the later great leaders of our Galuth, the whole nation scattered all over the world has become one “Moamad”, and in north and south, east and west, the time of the former Tamid-offering in Jerusalem still now awakes in every true Jewish breast the call to turn towards the site of the Temple, and to repeat ever afresh the national Tamid-vows translated into words in שחרית and מנחה, and thus to find ourselves united with God and all our brethren on earth in a national vow of loyalty to God’s Torah, this, at bottom is nothing other than a manifestation in spirit of the את קרבני לחמי לאשי ריח נחחי תשמרו להקרב לי במועדו which in future will again be brought in reality on the altar rebuilt in the Temple in Jerusalem, and out of the united shekels of the nation the Tamid-offering will again express in the symbolic procedure of the sacrifices, the eternal Jewish national vows.

From all this one can very well understand the opposition which the Sadducees raised against just the Tamid-offering being provided for out of the public funds. The spirit which the daily national offering nurtured amongst the people and directed every individual of the people with dedication and recognition of the whole of his life to the centre in Jerusalem and the representatives of the nation there to whom the Evidence of the Torah and its teachings were entrusted (Deut. 17,10) and who had to attend the daily renewed vow of faithfulness to this Torah in the national Tamid-offering in the name of the nation, this spirit is a condemnation of Sadduceeism of all times. Sadduceeism acknowledges as the sole director of the Law keeping close to God only that which they claim “lies to the hand of every individual in the corner of his house” (Kiddushin 66a), the literal words of the bible which every one can interpret to suit himself, and take what happens to appeal to him to be the Will of God. He shudders at, rejects with horror, the spirit of the Tamid-offering which wishes to make the individual find his God and what is pleasing to Him only in being together with, and attached to, the whole national community and those who are entrusted with and guarantee for the living Word of God. That was why it was one of the first demands of the Sadducees that it should be acknowledged that the daily Tamid was not a public national duty-bound offering, but a free-will offering left entirely to the subjective urge of every individual. In superficial narrow-mindedness they urge the singular of את הכבש אחד תעשה בבקר ואת הכבש השני תעשה בין הערבים and quite overlook that the plural of the preceding תשמרו להקריב לי as well as אשר תקריבו לה׳ places the duty on the public which just in the offering wants to represent itself as one united body. This attempt of the Sadducees was of such trenchant importance, affecting a whole principle, that the days when the leaders succeeded in convincing the nation of the flimsiness of the argument, the days of “the Vindication of the Tamid”, איתוקם תמידא were incorporated in the list of national days of remembrance to be celebrated by the prohibition to fast on any of them or to hold funeral orations on some of them; it even heads the list in the national chronicle: אילין יומיא דלא להתענאה בהון ומקצתהון דלא למספד בהון מריש ירחא דניסן עד תמניא ביה איתוקם תמידא וכו׳ שהיו הצדוקים אומרים יחיד מתנדב ומביא תמיד מאי דרוש את הכבש האחד תעשה בבקר ואת הכבש השני תעשה בין הערבים מאי אהדרו את קרבני לחמי לאישי תשמרו שיהו כולן באין מתרומת הלשכה (Menachoth 65a).

במועדו. (see on Ch. 9,2). A Truth of no small importance lies in this inclusion of the “daily” occurrences of mom and even in the sphere of the “special” once-occurring events in the history of the world proving the existence of God and inviting us to Him, the miracles of ,יציאת מצרים מתן תורה and in the wandering in the wilderness. Just as the revelation of God in Egypt, at the Reed Sea, at Sinai, the manna etc., in the wilderness, were appointed at every anniversary of their happening as a “Moed”, a time appointed to refresh our minds with thoughts of God and to come towards Him, so did He appoint every daily appearance of morn and even, occurring regularly without any special overcoming of His laws of nature, to be just such a “Moed”. It makes every rising and falling ray of light to a daily no less intense witness and messenger which shows us God’s Presence in the world and calls every one of us towards Him. Just as they, the wondrous deeds of God suspending the natural order of things in Egypt were premonitory signs proclaiming God, so is just the constancy of the cycle of change in the laws of nature a still louder announcer of this God. Yea, the deeds of God interfering with the laws of nature had quite specially the purpose of showing Him as the Maker of these very laws, the Regulator of these rules so that by the constancy, the regularity of these rules we do not lose the thought of Him as being the Master, Regulator and Organizer of the Laws of Nature that govern the world. That He it is Who חק נתן ולא יעבר, Who gave the Law which does not waver as long as He wishes it to continue, that just as הוא אמר ויהי, “He spoke and it came into existence”, so also הוא צוה ויעמד “when He commands it endures”, so that ייראו מה׳ כל הארץ ממנו יגורו כל יושבי תבל, so that “men know Him as the Lord of the whole world” and learn to fear Him and to know that only such beginnings of men and nations have a future before them as fit themselves harmoniously with His Law and His Will.

Just as here the Moed of the daily creation of light comes at the head of all the historical Moadim, so also in these Moadim the historical is always also joined to the seasonal times of Nature, so that the Jewish mind sees God in Nature and history with the same glance and we wander through life on earth filled with the thought of God with every breath we draw.

V. 3. ואמרת להם. By this repetition the preceding צו וגו׳ ואמרת וגו׳ is made into a separate pronouncement, and just thereby, as remarked above, the duty of the community to the Tamid-offering is marked out with a special indication by the Torah. זה האשה וגו׳, compared with Ex. 29,38, there the tendency is to designate the Tamid-offering as the realisation of the purpose of the Altar whereas here it is reviewed in its importance for keeping the nations consciousness of God awake. As such its character as אשה and עולה is stressed. Giving oneself up to the אש דת, the fire of the Torah (which the fire on the altar represents as worked out in Ex. I.L.) to the illuminating, purifying and life-giving power of the Torah, and just thereby making continuous forward and upward progress to God and to the heights of the calling indicated by Him, אשה and עולה, they are the two fundamental thoughts which are to be aroused and constantly kept vivid in every Jewish breast by the Tamid. And by זה האשה the two lambs, the morning and evening offering are at once considered as one offering, one surrendering to the fire in order to get near to God. It is altogether one and the same thought of life that is to fill our minds day and night, just as it is one and the same God from Whom day and night come and to Whom both phases of our earthly life, the bright day and the dark night belong. Both together form our “one day” of life, to the ups and downs of which the two lambs, the שני כבשים are meant to correspond, as is expressed by שנים ליום (see Ex. ibid.). Corresponding to the tendency of this repeated order for the Tamid-offering is also the תמימים stressed, the demand for the “completeness” of our surrender.

V. 4. את הכבש אחד. It says אחד instead of האחד, so it is not, “the one lamb” but “the lamb, and indeed אחד, only one”. That would oppose the Sadduceean way of taking it, and it would say explicitly that for the whole united nation only one lamb is to be brought for the Tamid, which therefore makes it definitely a קרבן צבור and could not be brought by every private individual as a נדבה, (a free-will offering I.L.) ואת הכבש השני is not the direction for the evening Tamid which only follows in V.8, but only the explanation of the preceding את הכבש אחד וגו׳:- They are not both to be brought, only one — for the other is to be offered only in the evening — the necessity for this explanatory addition would stress yet further the concept of the Tamid-offering being one. The צבור itself could be represented by two animals and still the offering need not lose the character of a קרבן צבור, as is the case immediately following of the Sabbath Mussaf-offering. But then it would express the Nation in the plurality of all its members and not as a closed unit. But the Tamid is to present Israel in the ideal of its totality (see on verses 9 & 10).

V. 5. ועשירית האיפה וגו׳. In Ex. 29,40 it only says עשרון סלת and the explicit description למנחה is also lacking, both quite in accordance with the tendency of the repetition of the Tamid regulations here (as explained above I.L.). For the minds of the people the מנחה idea belongs as an essential complement to the עלה thought, in addition to the surrender of the whole of personality, the thought of all the possessions and material wealth on which the national existence and prosperity depends, belonging to God must be acknowledged. But it says עשירית האיפה in place of the constant עשרן used at all the following offerings, this is with a view to the והעמר עשירית האיפה הוא of Ex. 16,36 to bring home to the minds of the people with every Mincha-tenth offered on their behalf that national experience of God’s providing the basic necessities of life.

V. 6. עולת תמיד וגו׳. In Ex. Ch. 27,1-8, p.495-496, considering the fact that the Altar in Ezekiel is called הראל “Mount of God” and the verse in Ps. 68,18 ה׳ בם סיני בקדש (“God is amongst them, Sinai is in the Sanctuary” I.L.) we expressed the supposition that here too the Altar is called הר סיני and that the Altar with the Altar-fire in the Sanctuary represents Sinai with the אש אוכלה, the consuming fire on its summit. This would agree most intimately with the tendency —to which we have referred — of this repeated teaching of the Tamid. Thereby the Tamid-offering would become a constant continuation, daily to be refreshed, of the promise, the vow נעשה ונשמע with which the Nation met the revelation of the Torah on Sinai and first entered in the bond of the Torah. For the עולה is in fact nothing else but the vow, the resolution for constant progress in “doing and understanding”. This constant giving oneself up ever afresh to the אש אוכלה בהר סיני is expressed only by the עולה and מנחה on the אש על המזבח but not by the נסיך היין which is poured down to the base of the Altar. Hence here the עולת תמיד only puts the עולה ומנחה together to mark it as עולת תמיד העשויה בהר סיני and then only in the next verse goes on ונסכו etc.

V. 7. ונסכו וגו׳. But this giving up all existence, all desires and possessions to the fire of God’s Torah is not to be something which has to be done with reluctance. Israel is to find its highest intoxication of joy in this, its calling, its happiness has its roots in the earth of the Sanctuary of the Torah on which the Mount of God rises with its demands, and it finds its happiest enthusiasm in the fact that it can pour out the expression of its highest delight, symbolically in the Sanctuary before God. (see on Ch. 15,5 et seq.). שכר is strong wine in its capacity for affecting the brain and mind (both disturbing its clarity of thinking as in Levit. 10,9, 10 & 11, and here, and generally, in raising one’s spirits to a high degree of joy; wine is certainly used in תנ״ך to express joy in life, I.L.). Externally שכר and קדש are in contrast to one another. That is why it says בקדש first here. The place which is to receive Israel’s offerings is at the same time to be the soil in which its deepest joys have their roots and grow. It can carry its שכר into God’s Sanctuary, and it is only שכר to it because it can pour it בקדש לפני ה׳.

V. 8. ואת הכבש השני (see on Ex. 29,38 & 41). וכנסכו refers to בקר: the נסך & מנחה of the evening is exactly the same as the מנחה and נסך of the morning (see the implication of this and on the whole Tamid-offering, on Ex. 29,38-42).

V. 9. וביום השבת וגו׳. The elevating-offering on Sabbath, brought in addition to the daily Tamid to express the special character of the day, differs from the Tamid only inasmuch as the Tamid consists of one lamb, the מוסף, the additional offering of שבת, consists of two. So that the differing characteristics lie solely in the different meanings of the numbers one and two of the animals. Now we have already learnt to know the essential difference between representing the nation in an offering by one or two animals respectively (Levit. 23,13 and XVII,19 et alia). The number one represents the nation collectively as a unit, in its unity while two represents it in its plurality, looks at it, not as one body but in all its individual members. And that at once forms the specific difference between the עולת תמיד and the עולת שבת. In the כבש אחד of the תמיד the nation as such approaches the Leader and Guide of the national fate, and at every rising and falling of the light of day (whether to prosperity or the reverse, see Ex. ibid. I.L.) renews the nation’s vow to faithfulness, obedience and giving itself up to fulfil the aim pointed out to it by its “Shepherd”, Lord and Master.

In the שני כבשים of the עולת שבת all the individuals of the Jewish nation, each Jewish person is represented as approaching their Creator and Lord. And as, by the שבתון of the שבת, by the cessation of all work, they lay themselves and their world acknowledgingly at His Feet. So, by the עולה of the שבת they keep alive in their minds the consciousness that the רועה ישראל, the “Shepherd of the Jewish Nation” as a whole is also the “Shepherd of the life of every Jewish person”, Who כרועה עדרו ירעה בזרעו יקבץ טלאים ובחיקו ישא עלות ינהל (“as a Shepherd doth He feed His flock, He gathereth up the lambs in His arms, and carrieth them in His bosom, and gently leadeth those that are with young” I.L.). Is. 40,11; and renew the vow always to pay obedience, faithfulness and devotion to Him as the Shepherd of all His creatures, for which He has called them into existence and given them a portion of His world and mastering powers over His World, solely and only for that purpose.

So that after Israel has approached its God, as one national body as כבש אחד with its one עשרון and its one רביעית יין, on שבת Israel comes again, representing itself as a national plurality, all its individual members, with their two כבשים and their two עשרונים and their two רביעית יין, to bring, within the consciousness of belonging to the nation, the vivid consciousness of the same cared-for relationship of each individual belonging to God called to life by the שבת feeling of having been created by God.

Now because the עולת שבת is nothing but just a varied תמיד, its nuance consisting only in the two כבשים in place of the one, the regulations for it are attached to the orders for the Tamid offering as continuing it and without further introduction such as וביום השבת תקריבו עולה לה׳ שני כבשים וגו׳ but simply by וביום השבת שני כבשים וגו׳ stressing that what is characteristic is just the contrast of the two lambs to the one of the Tamid-offering.

ונסכו, it is doubtful to what the suffix ו refers. If, as in most cases, to the כבשים it would have to be ונסכיהם. Being in the singular it must refer either to סלת or to יום השבת or to שבת generally which in V.10 appears also in the masculine. So that:- either to the סלת of the נסך which belongs to every מנחת נסכים, to express the joy of life also as added to the expression of the possession of food and well-being; or to stress especially for שבת what has already been expressed in the Tamid, the joy in life which wishes to fill every individual life by the Sabbath which says to every individual: וקראת לשבת עונג (Is. 58,13) (“and thou shalt call the Sabbath a delight I.L.) just to raise the refraining from doing anything on Sabbath to increase the means of obtaining food and wealth from the appearance of being a tribute which has reluctantly to be paid, into a source of the highest happiness.

V. 10. עלת שבת בשבתו. In this construction, and so also in עלת חדש בחדשו (V.14) the words שבת and חדש clearly refer to the general institution of Sabbath and New-Moon, and שבתו and חדשו to the days when they actually come to realisation. עלת שבת is the elevating-offering corresponding to the meaning and purpose of the institution of Sabbath, שבתו is every seventh day on which this Sabbath-institution is realised. Perhaps that is why שבת is written here in סמיכות without נסמך just to express the generality of the concept of this first שבת. It is the “Sabbath” concept which lies at the base of every Sabbath. The Gemora (Sabbath 24b) learns from עולת שבת בשבתו :ולא עולת חול בשבת “only that which is required for the Sabbath institution itself may be brought on Sabbath, but not, for instance, חלבים ואיברים which have been left over from before Sabbath.” — על עולת התמיד ונסכה, the Tamid-offering with its מנחה and נסך is also to be brought on Sabbath (see on Ch. 9,2). Yea, the Sabbath-offering is only an addition to the Tamid-offering, על עולת התמיד ונסכה מגיד התמידין קודמין (ספרי) למוספין, שאין מקרבים מוספים אלא בינתים (Zebachim 89a). For the Tamid-offering altogether, as the perpetual expression of the unceasing duty of the nation to strive upwards and make progress towards the ideal heights of its calling, has to start and conclude daily the service of offerings in the Sanctuary, and all other offerings — including the Sabbath elevating-offering — have to be brought in between them solely as manifestations of this general task of striving upwards and making progress as we worked out already on Levit. Ch. 6,5.

The institution of the Sabbath too, although its origin and also the idea of its meaning existed before the nation was chosen, so much so that one could almost say that the re-introduction of the Sabbath and its meaning to a world that had forgotten God was really the cause for, and the ultimate purpose of, Israel’s being chosen, is nevertheless dependent for its re-establishment on the nation giving itself up to its mission, and only forms an integral part of that mission. So that the general rule על עלת התמיד ונסכה applies to עולת שבת בשבתו as well. Perhaps it is because of this, to a certain extent putting the essential priority and original independence of Sabbath in the background that here it is, on the other hand rendered conspicuous by referring to it in the masculine עלת שבת בשבתו and not בשבתה whereas otherwise it is feminine.

The Mussaph-offering of Sabbath consists solely of עולה, and no חטאת is prescribed to accompany it as is the case with all the other מוספים. If we call to mind what we worked out in Levit. (on Ch. 4,24, p.124 in the English version I.L.) over the idea of חטאת and its relation to עולה, the absence of חטאת at the Sabbath Mussaph-offering is easily understood. From all the laws which characterise these two classes of offerings we came to the conclusion that the חטאת-consciousness, the depressing feeling of sinfulness and lack of moral eminence was not to be the normal state or mood in Jewish life.
