So that, if on the Moadim — those special days of meeting, fixed by the mutual arrangement of God and the nation — the nation comes to meet its God with the most complete expression in offerings of its ideal mission in life, just this contemplation of the ideals of perfection necessitates at the same time a חטאת to bring to mind the disparity between reality and the height of these lofty ideals. But the Sabbath Mussaph-offering which only brings complementarily the acknowledgment of God from the consciousness of His being the Creator of His creatures to the national thoughts of acknowledging Him of the Tamid-offering, and from the two together is to form feelings of the deepest devotion to God and resolves ever to strive higher and higher, feelings and thoughts that are to fill our lives with every breath we draw, to that, as to the Tamid itself, the חטאת must remain afar.

V. 11. ראש חדש .ובראשי חדשיכם וגו׳ forms the foundation of the whole Jewish conception of God, the world, and human beings. With it God began the foundation of His nation and thereby set up the fact of חדוש, the concept of a fresh new creation of the world and the salvation of mankind out of the free-willed act of God in opposition to the heathen erroneous illusion of קדמות, fixing the world irretrievably in the grave of guilt and wretchedness. חדש is set up as the pillar of the future salvation of Israel and mankind as we have worked out in full in Ex. 12,2 (p.127 et seq. in English edition). The “renewal”, rejuvenation of ourselves, arising afresh to pure efforts and bright life, redemption from all moral, social and physical evil, the renewed directing of oneself upwards towards the Hand of God to strive towards the ideals of morality and salvation to which It eternally beckons, raising ourselves afresh to the sanctifying and healing Light of the proximity of our God out of the misery of darkness away from Him into which we may have sunk, such is the call which we are to receive at the sight of every new moon. The new moon which God’s words החדש הזה לכם ראש חדשים (“this renewal of the moon shall be a beginning of renewals unto you”) made into a model, a sign ensuring “salvation” just as He made the rainbow into a sign ensuring the continuance of the existence of mankind (see on Ex. 12,2). Therefore, as often as the new moon invites us to make our חדשים, our fresh phases of time in our lives, we approach our God in the Sanctuary of His Torah with the expression in offering of the complete ideal of the calling He has given us for life and deed, by עולה to vow to continually strive to attain the height of that calling and in חטאת to renew the vow to purer future care to firmly guard against any sinking or slipping down from such height as we may attain. That this ideal of Israel’s calling which was the purpose of the redemption from Egypt and the revelation on Sinai, and is the aim of all of God’s further guidance throughout the ages, is fully expressed by the offering of פרים בני בקר שנים ואיל אחד כבשים בני שנה שבעה תמימים we have already considered at length on Levit. 23,18, (and would refer our readers thereto I.L.). What God promised at the moment of the announcement of His redemption as the aim of that redemption with the pronouncement ולקחתי אתכם לי לעם והייתי לכם לאלקים (Ex. 6,7; refer to it) finds its complete expression in the group of Moed-offerings.

Israel shall be a nation, every member of which shall work in the service of God in the everlasting freshness of youth (symbolised by פרים בני בקר שנים) which thereby will appear as one united nation amongst God’s human flock leading the way as a model to all other nations of mankind in God-blessed strength (symbolised by איל אחד), and its whole history, its whole fate is nothing but the revelation of the Finger of God intervening in world history throughout the ages through which they pass in undying freshness of youth as the flock of God’s guidance (symbolised by the שבעת כבשים בני שנה); — see on Levit. 23,18.

This mission, this calling of Israel, to be taken to heart afresh at every ראש חדש, as the ever fresh goal to which it is to strive, it, and it alone, to be taken to heart, is the aim of all the Moadim inviting Israel to its God, for it was it freed out of Egypt, for it it received the Torah, for it the Protection of God was above it throughout its educational path in its wilderness, to it the call of Teruah awakens it on Rosh Hashonna, it unlocks the gates of atonement for it on יום הכפורים. That is why it is the one and same group of offerings with which Israel appears before its God on all these Moadim, with the only modification that, in accordance with the specific character of the particular days, the two פרים are changed to one פר on י״כ ,ר״ה and שמיני עצרת. For even the group of offerings on the Festival of Succoth — as we shall soon have to show, — is founded on the ר״ח group of offerings. Thus the ראש חדש-offering forms the basic type of all Moadim-offerings, just as the קביעות, the sanctifying fixing the date, the קרא מקרא קדש of all the Moadim, is really dependent on קידוש החדש, on the sanctifying fixing of the ראש חדש, and the Moed comes to be kept as having been included and reckoned on in that function.

V. 12. ושלשה וגו׳. But, as prescribed in Ch. XV, the nation as a whole as well as every individual as an individual has always to add to the elevating-offering dedicating the personal life of deeds, a fealty gift acknowledging that all possessions for food, comfort and enjoyment of life belong to and come from God. This acknowledgment is made by the Mincha-offering of סלת and שמן and the יין נסכים representing the national riches of דגן תירוש ויצהר. The higher the importance of the position in God’s household of the person to whom the offering refers — whether it is that of a faithful lamb, כבש, following the guidance of the Shepherd, or that of a pattern-setting leading ram, איל in God’s flocks, or that of an efficient worker, פר in God’s fields of humanity — the higher the importance of the position, the more important is the recognition and consciousness of all that a person has belongs to, and comes from God. Hence, the ever increasing amounts of the Mincha and Nesochim at the איל ,כבש and פר, the theory of which we worked out at their being prescribed in Ch. XV, and which here is to come into practice at the Moadim-offerings.

V. 13. עלה ריח ניחוח וגו׳. The Mincha of ones’ possessions is an essential completion of the פרים ,איל ,וכבשים and was given over to the אש על המזבח which awaits the devotion of the nation, just as they were. So, together with these, it forms one עולה, a vow to strive upwards to the heights indicated by God; ריח ניחוח, an expression of hinting at giving God satisfaction with one’s active life; אשה לה׳, getting near to God by devotion, giving oneself up, to the purifying life-giving and forming powers of His Torah.

V. 14. ונסכיהם, and this devotion, this “giving oneself up” is the source of Israel’s purest joy, and this joy increases with every higher degree of importance which he feels he is allowed to have in God’s household on earth.

זאת עולת חדש בחדשו (see on V.10). Every actual day of the new moon demands that one occupies oneself with the general idea of חדש, of refreshed renewal. Hence עבר יומו בטל קרבנו (Sifri), hence a Moed-offering being omitted on its proper day cannot be made good by being brought on a subsequent day. It is just the day itself with the thoughts that it arouses in our minds on it, and by it which we have omitted to drive home by symbolic action. That cannot be retrieved. The offerings are no regal paraphernalia of God so that as long as He receives them it is no matter if it is a day or two behind time. The Moed-offering is something brought for our benefit to raise our thoughts up in the direction which corresponds to the Moed-day. If this has not been done on that day it cannot be recovered on some other day, for each day brings its own demands which we have to satisfy with all our energy and devotion. Hence it says regarding the Tamid, the Sabbath offering and all the other public offerings: קרבנות צבור שזמנן קבוע עבר זמנו בטל קרבנו (Temura 14a). But not only that which corresponds to any day to be expressed on that day by national representation in the Sanctuary but all such Moed-offerings — and the Tamid belongs to that category in the very first place (see on V.2) — must be brought from the ever fresh participation of every member of the nation from the shekels which were collected each year for the חדשי השנה, the months of the year starting every Nissan (Rosh Hashana 7, 2) חדש והביא קרבן מתרומה חדשה. In this respect each year formed a separate cycle of offerings on its own, as has already been worked out on Ex. 30,16, (p.581 in English version).

V. 15. ושעיר עזים וגו׳. A שעיר החטאת belongs essentially to the group of offerings of all the Moadim. It represents the thought of the inadequateness of the reality, aroused by the ideal perfection of life expressed by the עולה-group. To ראש חדש with its whole meaning of renewed struggling up out of all abasement and back-sliding, the שעיר החטאת stands in special and closer relation. So that whereas in all the following orders for the Moed-offerings the שעיר חטאת אחד is simply attached to the group of עולה and מנחה ונסכים, here this group is shut off by זאת עלת חדש וגו׳ and then שעיר עזים אחד לחטאת by the addition of לה׳, similarly to עולה לה׳ of V.11, is given special importance of its own. As ה׳ the God of educative Love for Mankind, has indicated the changing phases of the moon to be a model for us, and with each regularly recurring new moon has instituted a דאש חדש for us, to be a day of fresh beginning of spiritual and moral renewal of ourselves, to struggle upwards out of every darkening or dimming of intellectual light into which we may have sunk, He has laid down the great fundamental Truth for us to take to heart, viz., that the חוטא too, that the sinner too, is still לה׳, an object of God’s Love, yea, that חטאת, the ability to sin, and feeling the requirement of atonement, and the expiation, the elevation again out of sin, all of which lies in the conception חטאת is לה׳, the highest gift of grace with which God has ennobled His noblest creation, Man. Man’s greatest superiority, the real height of his nature, that he can keep himself on the height of what is morally good by the exertion of his completely free will, that he can avoid evil and practice goodness without any compulsion, unavoidably presupposes that he could also sin, that sensuality has an enticing attraction for him which he has the power to withstand by the free decision of his will. It is in the exercise, the repeated exercise of such will that his nature works itself up ever more and more to the stage of moral purity near to God which he was meant to occupy. If Man could not sin, if sin had no attraction for him, he would not be a man, he would be an animal or an angel “who turn not aside in their goings”, but a “human being”, a creature that serves God out of its own free-willed energy, he would not be. His rising again out of sin, as חטאת teaches and effects, is accordingly the atonement for his ability to sin which forms his innermost self and is inseparable from it. The free-willed virtue to which he raises himself in the חטאת is a divine flower which blossoms purely out of the soil of his חטא-ability. Spoken in the language of the ראש חדש institution: the glory of the moon growing again to light reveals the Wisdom of its Creator Who has allotted the moon the power of temporary darkness. Should not this perhaps be the meaning of the saying of our sages on our verse, מה נשתנה שעיר של ר״ח שנאמר בו לה׳ אמר הקב״ה שעיר זה יהא כפרה על שמיעטתי את הירח (Shevuoth 9a). Sins which human beings do are after all, in truth the only bad things in God’s world. The thoughtless question, why has God provided Man with the ability to sin is given a pertinent reply by every man who rises again by his own free will out of sin to moral purity, an elevated stage which he could never have reached had he not been able to sin. Every victory over sin is, accordingly in truth an atonement for the ability to sin with which the Creator has made human beings to human beings; and every ראש חדש is to be taken as such a requisition for us to make such an “atonement for the work of the Creator”.

The ideal of our moral calling is symbolically expressed. The removal effected by the חטאת of every group of Moed-offerings, of the contrast which every actual contemporary time shows to the ideals of our calling which the עולה-group represents is accordingly adequately expressed by כפרה על טומאת מקדש וקדשיו. Hence the teaching in Shevuoth 2a and 9a, שעירי רגלים ושעירי ראשי חדשים מכפרין על טומאת מקדש וקדשיו, and indeed על שאין בה ידיעה לא בתחלה ולא בסוף, such טומאת מקדש וקדשיו are atoned for thereby, which had occurred completely unconsciously and had never come to one’s knowledge afterwards. (קרבן עולה ויורד for טומאת מקדש וקדשיו assumes ידיעה בתחלה ובסוף; see Levit. 5,2, and further p.146 in English edition). This טומאת מקדש וקדשיו which has no ידיעה בתחלה ולא בסוף comprises that state of lack of clarity of our moral freedom into which we so easily fall through the unavoidable contact with the unfree physical side of our life, and so unconsciously would tend to become more and more estranged from that pure responsiveness to light and understanding and clarity of thought which is the condition in which we are to keep our godly nature, did not just the מועדי ה׳ come to us from time to time and call us out of all the stuffy realm of “must”, the dark idea of moral slavery, up and into the free bright light of clear understanding which the proximity of our God gives us. — This freeing us from a state of טומאה into which we have come without being at all conscious of it, and which disturbs our קודש relationships can also be found in the addition of לה׳ to חטאת:- שעיר עזים אחד לחטאת לה׳ חטא שאין מכיר בו אלא ה׳ (Shevuoth 9a). Unless the way we have taken it is entirely mistaken, this sentence, at bottom would say the same as the above quoted saying: שעיר זה יהא כפרה על שמעטתי את הירח, for החדש הזה לכם is just the possibility of the temporary eclipsing of the Divine godly element in Man caused by the Creator having combined the pure Breath of God with the physical element of the senses.

V. 16—19. ובחדש הראשון וגו׳. And when the anniversary of the first month of Jewish National birth comes round, and then on the fourteenth of it, the eve of the Redemption, every Jewish home, with all the persons belonging to it, recalls the fateful hour of redemption when God made the decision between physical and national life and death, and by the Pessach-offering celebration again and again ever afresh places itself, and the constitutional building up of the nation, back on the basis of its fundamental laws (see Ex. 12,3-14 and 27). And when, then on the fifteenth, the nation links itself together to a חג, to a festive circle around God and His Sanctuary, and with the Mazzoth, unleavened bread in their hands for seven days acknowledges how it is God and God alone Whom it has to thank for the freedom and independence it enjoys, and for that it entered the upraising and free-making service of God out of the depressing and downcasting spirit of service of Pharaoh (Ex. 12,14 & 15), hence, at once on the first day of their being called out of all servitude on earth and up to God and His Sanctuary, and no hand being moved in creative work of earthly service (Ex. 12,16) והקרבתם they approach God, again as they did on ראש חדש, with the symbolic expression of all the relationship to God which the mission they received from all this in פרים שנים איל אחד ושבעה כבשים. Only here the ordinary expression of תמימים, as used normally, is specially stressed by being made into a special sentence תמימים יהיו לכם instead of merely an adjective. This is in order to specially stress, corresponding to the ideas of פסח and מצות, the “completeness” of our giving the “whole” of ourselves and “every” phase of our lives, (תמים) to the service of God which was founded with and by תמימים .יציאת מצרים יהיו לכם, only in the condition of completeness with nothing at all missing can they serve to express the mission that became yours with יציאת מצרים. (see Levit. 22,19 et seq.).

V. 20—21. ומנחתם. As the general prescription is given in Ch. XV, that with every עולה the corresponding מנחה and נסכים have to be added, bringing them with the Moed-offerings is self-understood. After they had nevertheless been mentioned in full detail at the ראש חדש-offering, at the rest of the Moed-offerings they are only mentioned in an abbreviated form as מנחתם, as the Mincha which naturally belongs to them, and the נסכים, as being then self-understood is not even mentioned here at the Moed-offering of the Pessach Festival, and otherwise only generally indicated by ונסכיהם without any details of the prescribed quantities. The different measures prescribed for the Mincha-offerings had to be mentioned, because, as Ramban mentions in his commentary, the quantity varies in some cases, as at the עומר (Levit. 23,13) where two tenths are prescribed for one כבש (refer to it there) while the quantities for the נסכים are constant in every case and so need no special mention. But a special consideration is required for the sudden change from the plural (in V.21) in which before and afterwards the address is couched to the singular תעשה at the Mincha of the כבשים, and altogether for this תעשה which here brings the מנחה of the כבשים into special prominence as a special command, whereas everywhere else the עשרון עשרון לכבש is simply attached to the עשרונים of the פרים and איל. This nice distinction of expression could also be explained as being due to the meaning of the יציאת מצרים Festival-offering. For the “seven” “כבשים״ are the expression in offerings of the “God revealing history” of the nation, a thought which comes in the most eminent sense afresh to one’s mind in connection with the remembrance of the יציאת מצרים of the nation, and indeed, of the nation as a nation rather than of the individuals comprising the nation. More than all the other benevolent deeds in our history that we experienced from God the redemption from Egypt looks on Israel in its totality as one unit. It was the love, the strong arm of a Father that saved His child out of death and dungeon up into the air of life and freedom. Hence עשרון עשרון תעשה לכבש לשבעת הכבשים on Pessach, and this uniformness of the עשרון measure for the כבשים of the Moed-Offerings had to be brought up as a special ordinance for the Moed-offering of Pessach because just at the Omer on Pessach the anomaly of two עשרונים for the כבש occurs.

V. 22. לכפר עליכם. On ראש חדש the nation which is represented in the group of offerings is only present in spirit, symbolically. Hence there the inadequacy of the nation in its concrete actuality is not so prominently apparent. It is nevertheless realised at least by God. So that there it says ושעיר עזים אחד לחטאת לה׳ (see above). But at the Pessach-offering the whole nation is actually present in person. There the thought of this inadequacy (— the difference between what they actually are and the ideals which they are represented to be in the offerings — I.L.), and the necessity for atonement which arises therefrom, springs immediately to every mind, hence here: ושעיר חטאת אחד לכפר עליכם.

V. 23. מלבד עלת הבקר. In V.24 it says, as it does at all the other Moed-offerings: עולת התמיד יעשה ונסכו. If then here it says specially מלבד עלת הבקר אשר לעולת התמיד תעשו את אלה it cannot just want to order the Mussaf-offering to be brought only after the Tamid as that instruction is given by the usual formula in V.24. But rather it must want to bring to our minds the contrast of these two offerings to one another in connection with the special meaning of the day which is the cause for the two of them to be brought. This would be the immediate purpose of commenting on the Tamid-offering here in terms referring to its national meaning עלת הבקר as it does in no other case in the whole chapter of Moed-offerings. There is perhaps no greater contrast than that between the day-break occurring as a result of the natural order of things, which brings about the Tamid offering, and the facts of the suppression of the natural order of things which brought about the יציאת מצרים the remembrance of which the Mazzo-festival celebrates in its Moed-offering, and yet these two facts are referred, one after the other, to the same One and Only God. It is the same God, to look up to Whom the rays of the morn invites us, and to Whom the remembrance of יציאת מצרים calls us, for it is the same God Who, in the laws of Nature which He made and keeps going and regulates, daily awakes the dawn, gives the morning to us and us to the morning, and Who once in Egypt, just by suppressing these laws revealed Himself as Lord and Master of these laws, and with that revelation appointed Himself as God to us and us as His People. Hence the significant מלבד עולת הבקר אשר לעולת התמיד תעשו את אלה apart from the elevating-offering of the “morn” which is fixed for a daily elevating offering “are ye to bring these”. Moreover ye are to bring these in connection with the daily offering which preceds it, as is expressed by על and מלבד (see verse 10).

As here the עולת הבקר, because, as it says, it is an עולת התמיד, a daily offering, precedes the less frequently occurring מוספים, the general order of precedence is taught (Zebachim 89a; see also Horioth 12a and Rashi) that כל התדיר מחברו קודם את חברו, that which occurs more frequently has precedence over the less frequently occurring, the ordinary over the uncommon, a rule which indeed must be taken to heart, as the general tendency is to value the seldom occurring religious service above the ordinary or even daily procedure or service.

V. 24. כאלה תעשו ליום וגו׳. Seven days on which the nation celebrates the Festival of its Foundation, shall ye approach God with the same expression each day of what you are meant to be (— not like on the Succoth Festival when a different group of offerings are to be brought each day — Sifri). For, on the festival of its foundation it is above all necessary to completely permeate the nation with the ideas of what it was founded for, as expressed by the normal formula for the Moed-offerings. Taking this to heart is to effect, just on Pessach — as it does not say so completely on any other Moed — לחם: making all the phases of the national life prepared and ready for the Presence of God in its midst, אשה ריח ניחוח לה׳: by submitting them all to the power of the Fire of the Torah (אשדת I.L.) as an expression of giving satisfaction to God in the active services of life. — ונסכו, “its” refers probably, as it does in the rest of the cases, to the Tamid. Otherwise, as the נסכים have not yet been thought of, it could also be referred to לחם.

V. 25. וביום השביעי וגו׳. And just as the first did, so does the seventh day again call you away from all the worldly creative service, up to God and His Sanctuary, so that all the thoughts and fresh intentions won under the influence of the seven days’ festival may be gathered together and held fast, and His Sanctuary left once again with one’s mind and heart refreshed and enriched with the true treasures of life. (see Ex. 12,16).

V. 26. וביום הבכורים. And then, when the festival of your having attained freedom and independence lies behind you, and you finally reach the day which inaugurates the season in which you are privileged to bring the “first fruits” of your year and lay them before God’s Altar in the Sanctuary of His Torah as acknowledgment of God’s having kept His Promise to bless the soil of your land as a result of your entering into the Covenant of His Torah: בהקריבכם מנחה חדשה לה׳; and you inaugurate this season of general bringing the God-acknowledging Mincha of the new fruits, with “two leavened loaves of wheat bread” which you bring before God’s Altar to express the “worthy human independence” which is granted to “every single member of the People of His Law” as a result of their realisation of His Torah; and indeed בשבעתיכם, on the completion of your weeks, after you have counted, not שבעות חקות קציר (Jer. 5,24) not the weeks of the ripening of the harvests, but your weeks, your maturing, your becoming spiritually and morally ripe for the reception and carriers of the Divine Torah, from the receipt of freedom and independence (see Levit. 23,15-22); and then again you are called away from the work of serving the world and invited to the service of God, to His Sanctuary —.

V. 27—31. Then again you approach God with the symbolic expression of what all this has brought forth, the symbolic ideal of every individual life working in the service of God; the nation as a whole, striding in front of the nations as an illuminating model; your history and fate being an ennobling lesson revealing God; your existence, your well-being, your happiness dedicated to an acknowledgment of God, a calling which constantly, out of the inadequacy of every contemporary time, opens the gates to a fresh, new, purer, more faithful future, again with two פרים, one איל, seven כבשים, with your סלת, your שמן, your יין נסכים and a שעיר לכפר. And here it says שבועתיכם on the festival of our having made ourselves worthy for God’s Torah, not as on Pessach (V.19) just referring with the sacrificial animals to ourselves have become free through God, but at the end of the period, with the retrospective summing up of all what the offerings represent for our lives, how the פרים איל וכבשים, the תמימים יהיו לכם :סלת שמן ויין, can only represent the relationships of our lives and our joys in life if they are absolutely complete. For תמימות, comprising everything, leaving nothing, no phase of our lives out, in our devotion, our surrender to God, the recognition that everything that we have comes from Him, the ואהבת את ה׳ א׳ בכל לבבך ובכל נפשך ובכל מאודך, to make the completeness the unity of our lives correspond to the Unity of God, as the meaning of תמימים in the offerings represents, (see Levit. 1,3) that is just the quintessence, the whole content of the Torah, which as תורת ה׳ is תמימה משיבת נפש.

V. 1. ובחדש השביעי. And when you then come to the seventh month, which — like the seventh day of the week invites us thoughtfully to lay our world and the powers we have to master this world, at the feet of its and our Creator and Lord, and thereby obtain the right, earnest but happy mood for our lives — invites us to thought, to self-examining retrospection as to what use we have made of the effect which freedom, and the Torah, and the blessings of property and riches, and the great institutions of Sabbath, New Moon and the Festivals have had on us — that which throughout the year is celebrated in the Sanctuary by the offerings so full of meanings and teachings of attaining, and returning to, nearness to God, and the atoning fresh start and the happy cheerful service before God which it then wishes to see realised in concrete active life by every individual — now, at once באחד לחדש, on the first day of this month, a New Moon Day in the deepest sense, again calls us out of our working service of the world into the service of God and invites us to the Sanctuary, but does not wish to find us just finding this feeling of getting near to God and of returning to Him only in the Sanctuary, but with the rousing-up tones of the Shofar bringing the feeling of the nearness to, and the return to, God, in every heart and in every Jewish home.

V. 2. ועשיתם וגו׳ — not והקרבתם — you do not yet approach near to God, you do not yet dare to approach Him with the symbolic expression of the ideal of your calling and especially not with the שני פרים representing every individual of the nation living up to the national mission. All you can do is ועשיתם to perform objectively the ideal of your mission which the Sanctuary of the Torah holds before you. And indeed only פר אחד, representing primarily the nation only in its totality as the active efficient worker in the service of God, from which, under the call of the Shofar, every individual of it is to find his way back to the service of God. And that is also why

V. 4. ועשרון אחד: (note the stress on the אחד in contrast to the ordinary term ועשרון עשרון used for Pessach, Shevuoth, Succoth and New Moon I.L.): the “one” tenth measure with which the Nation as a unit accompanies each of its sevenfold approach in its Moed-offering as כבש, as a lamb following God’s Guidance, and thereby expresses that, just as its history, its continuance as a nation does, so does the continuance of its material provision reveal the Finger of God, this “one” tenth is specially stressed in this prescription for the ר״ה-offering. For the material provision of every individual of this national unit the decision has still to be made in accordance with their response to the Terua and Kippur days. It is only the Succoth Festival which then again allows each individual to build up his hut again on the re-presented earth and gives him again the gifts of the earth into his hand for happy God-conscious existence and living.

V. 5. ושעיר וגו׳ לכפר עליכם, and however inadequate even the nation as a whole may be at any contemporary time to the expression of the ideal state of its mission, the Sanctuary of God atoningly guarantees its continued existence, and opens the gate for a rejuvenated future within which every individual member of it can and should achieve atonement for the past and his own rebirth for the future.

V. 6. מלבד עלת החדש. This serious character of the Terrua-day comes to its own in the ראש השנה Moed-offering, supported by the preceding ראש חדש offering, itself preceded by the Tamid-offering (see the rule כל התדיר מחברו וכו׳ Ch. 28,23) and all three do not lack the corresponding נסכים. For the day has a threefold source of thoughts leading up to God: the rays of daybreak each dawn proclaiming God, the New Moon inviting rejuvenation, the Terua note calling to commune with and return to God. All three find the symbolic representation of their surrendering devotion, their fealty, and their joy in their מנחה ,עולה and נסכים, and ראש חדש and ראש השנה their special expression of atonement in the חטאת (see ר״ה 8b, תוספות ד״ה שהחדש). But as they all three lead up to the same One God, so do all three unite to the same one sanctification of life for which the offerings together form an expression of giving satisfaction to God by giving oneself up to the fire-like power (purifying, warming, lightening I.L.) of His Torah: לריח ניחח אשה לה׳.

V. 7—11. ובעשור וגו׳. And when then, after these days full of thoughts of communing with and returning to God, the tenth of this great month arrives, the great day which celebrates the greatest miraculous power of God entirely wiping out a whole past, granting a rebirth to a completely new future as occurred when after the fall to the worship of the golden calf He guaranteed Israel כפרה, that miracle which comes after סליחה, after forgiveness, and wipes the past sin out so completely that the sin does not have the natural effect of making it easier to sin a second time, but the sinner is as if new-born and had not committed the sin. And God dedicated that day guaranteeing כפרה for all time to be a מועד ה׳, a day of finding oneself again, of meeting one’s God. And — while within the Sanctuary of the Torah, the renewed attachment to the re-presented Tablets of the Law reposing under the wings of the Cherubim next to the broken ones is being celebrated, and proceding outwards from there the atoning rebuilding of the whole Jewish life is being represented in a unique עבודה-procedure (Levit. Ch. XVI) — the nation, called to God, awaited the rebirth He promised them, without which they had completely forfeited all right to further existence or accomplishments, a fact they had to bring home to their minds by ענוי and שביתה מכל מלאכה, by ceasing to extend their existence by eating any food, and ceasing to do any work for their future, on that day, you, doing likewise:

והקרבתם, are to come near to your God, in happy confidence in the future He promises you again, with the representation of the ideals of your calling, with the vow of the elevating-offering to be His פר, His faithful worker in the fields of His human harvest, as an איל to be an example and lead the way in front of His herd of nations, as כבשים בני שנה שבעה, to follow His lead in the ever cheerful freshness of youth; and in all these respects to be תמימים to give yourself up completely without the slightest lack of any phase of your life; and to use all the goods and all the food and all the enjoyments which you recognise all come from God, for the requirements of such work, such a mode of life and such a carrying out of your fate; and henceforth to keep yourself with שעיר-like firmness and obstinacy on the height of your calling.
מלבד וגו׳. This group of Moed-offerings of יום הכפורים is joined to the procedures of the preceding עבודות היום and Tamid-offering, as the connection is worked out on Levit. 16,23.

V. 12. ובחמשה עשר. And then when finally with the fifteenth of the Seventh month the blossoming of the whole Jewish life planted on the fifteenth of the first month comes to be celebrated, and after the thoughtful self-examination and repentence of the Terua-day, and the rebirth of the Kippur day brought about with cessation of eating and working, the remembrance of the cloud-protected, mana-fed passage through the wilderness builds itself up to a Moed of joyful building of Succoth and enjoyment of one’s possessions before God, and you are called out of the creative work of serving the world into the Sanctuary of God, and filled with the spirit of happiness in God, you join “the circle around Him and His Sanctuary” (חג I.L.) as His People and the People of His Torah, and live for seven days in this feeling of elevation together with the Jewish National entity; then

V. 13. והקרבתם etc. The Moed-offering of this most joyful festival of all the Jewish festivals consists of an elevating-offering of thirteen פרים, two אילים and fourteen כבשים. The number of אילים and כבשים during the seven days of the festival remains the same each day, but the number of פרים diminishes by one each day, so that on the seventh day the group of offerings consists of seven פרים, two אילים and fourteen כבשים. The two אילים and fourteen כבשים announce, at the very first glance, this Moed-offering to be a double one, and make us take the thirteen פרים of the first day as being also of two groups, one of seven (as usual I.L.) and one of six. On the High Festival of its national consciousness of God, Israel approaches its God with a double elevating-offering, with one group of offerings of seven bullocks, one ram and seven lambs and another group of six bullocks, one ram and seven lambs. So that two sets of nations regarded in their totality are represented who are equal in the relationship of their historical path through the world to the one “Shepherd” of mankind (i.e. as sheep, כבש) and in the importance of their being leaders of the world in their being blessed with certain gifts (rams, איל), but as bullocks, as to their work (פרים) they differ essentially. The one, are not only seven, in alliance with God, as כבשים in the path of their history through the world (the number having in the Torah always the meaning of the attachment of the created to the Creator, lay to holy, visible to invisible, earthly to heavenly etc., as in Sabbath, Shemita, oaths etc. etc. I.L.), not only is their whole historical existence on earth a revelation of the One invisible guiding God, but also as פרים they are seven, in what they do and work they are attached to God, their acts and deeds are also a revelation of God, under Whose laws they place themselves of their own free will, and all that they do and refrain from doing show His Will. The others, although indeed they are near to God, their fate, their history their weal or woe is a revelation of God, but what they do and refrain from doing is not, passively they belong to God, but actively they do not, they are indeed seven כבשים, but as פרים they are only “six”; their life of action, of deeds is only “earthly” belongs entirely to themselves, follows only their earthly trends, their urges and inclinations, their opinions and caprices, but is not formed under the dictates of the Will of their Creator and Lord, does not bear the signature “seven”; their history comes from above, what they do and refrain from doing does not; they are שבעת כבשים but only six פרים.

Clearly here the contrast of Israel to the rest of the nations is designated. A contrast which does not consist so much in the recognition or non-recognition of God as the Director of human history as in the recognition or otherwise of Him as the Director of human acts. The group איל אחד ,פרים שבעה and שבעת כבשים is Israel; the group איל אחד ,פרים ששה and שבעת כבשים is the rest of mankind. And inasmuch as Israel, on the Festival of Succoth, the festival of happy building up homes on earth “under the protection and blessing of God,” that final aim of all mankind’s wanderings, approaches with thirteen bullocks, two rams and fourteen lambs, it comes to God not just for itself alone but with the symbolic expression of the whole of mankind of “Israel and the nations” but earmarking the “contrast between God-serving acts and non-God-serving acts which at the present divide mankind into two camps.

But this contrast is looked on as dwindling ever more and more. Under the influence of Israel’s mission and the effect of the silent example of their lives in the midst of the nations this contrast becomes smaller and smaller. It starts with six to seven, on the second day it is already five to seven, then four to seven etc., until on the seventh day, at the goal of the development of mankind and of Israel’s mission for it, the contrast will entirely have disappeared; and in acknowledging God, and in the active life of deeds, Israel together with the whole of mankind, will conjointly stand before God as seven bullocks, two rams and fourteen lambs. But regarding the historical guidance and participation in solving the mission of mankind in general, the position of Israel in the midst of the nations does not cease to be a special one. Israel and the nations, the nations and Israel remain, in accordance with their historical development and their different kinds of capacities and efficiency for the purpose of Mankind; remain two separate great factors in leading the world for the purpose of humanity, both equally near and equally precious to God in His Direction of world-history. They remain seven and seven כבשים, one and one איל, but in homage to God, the One and Only One, in fulfilling the laws given respectively to each of these great factors for carrying out their respective missions, the Sinaitic for Israel, the Noachim for mankind in general, in acknowledging God as the One and only God by carrying out His Will on earth, Israel and the rest of the world will become one. And the active life of all men on earth will bear the same God-revealing stamp of moral faithfulness to duty as the active life of Israel does, as פרים they will together form just “one seven” והיה ה׳ למלך על כל הארץ ביום ההוא יהי׳ ה׳ אחד ושמו אחד.

The words of our sages too in Succa 55b: הני שבעים פרים כנגד מי כנגד שבעים אומות, see in these Succoth Musaf-offerings a symbolic expression for the nations of the world. And if there it takes it as a plea for the atonement of mankind in general, unless our way of taking it is erroneous, that would come to the same thing. The plea would be just that, in the course of time, the contrast might diminish, accordingly, for the gradual return of mankind in their active lives to God. For the sake of this future and for this future may God forgive them and let them continue!

But if we find here in the group of Moed-offerings of Succoth the characteristic features of all the teachings concerning the world-historic purpose of all the developments of the nations of the world and Israel’s contemporary and future relations towards them which our prophets have taught, it seems to be just the festival of Succoth which we find connected with this future goal of the nations in the mouths of the Prophets. In Zacharia 14,16 all the efforts of the nations using their powers to fight against connections with God and His Laws end with their acknowledging God as King and coming to Jerusalem to celebrate the Festival of Succoth each year. More, we dare to express the thought: in Ezekiel 38,39 the leading head of the last fight against God and His rules and management on earth is called גוג. It does not seem far-fetched to recognise in this name the idea of building a roof, from גגג, and thereby at once see the contrast to סוכה, the unstable weak covering of foliage. Indeed the content of the whole history of the world could be understood in this contrast. One erroneous illusion leads mankind astray. Just as they are given the power to use their own strength to fix the boundaries of their own sphere and make it safe and sure against their earthly contemporaries by דפנות, by strongly built artificial walls, so do they imagine they have to use their power to make themselves safe and sure against that which comes from above, against God and the influences of His Power of directing matters. They think they can betake themselves under the protection of their own might, can take their fate in their own hands, and can crown the building up of human greatness by gabled roofs rendering them independent of God. It is the battle of the גג (roof I.L.) against סוכה, the fight of the “roof-illusion” of human greatness which never allows Man to come to repose, against the “Succah-truth” of cheerful confidence and quietness which putting one’s trust in God’s protection grants. World-history started with the building of a tower towering up to heaven by the self-worship of human power — and ends with the happy harmonious human life on earth building booths acknowledging God.

Judaism leaves other disciplines to teach that by renunciation of this world one wins the next world. It reserves for itself the teaching that by a life of God-acknowledging duty one can attain beatitude in this world and Paradise, life in the next world can begin here in this one. And this teaching preached by the Succoth Festival for Israel throughout the ages makes itself the universal prospect for the future of all nations by its group of Moed-offerings. From the summit of its national joy the People of God look to the future happiness of all mankind. According to the Jerusalmi Succa V.1 it was also just the summit of joy of this Festival of Succoth embracing the hopes of Israel and the whole of mankind, on whose heights the “Well of Happiness and Salvation” sprang out of which the young disciples of prophecy drew the spirit, which enabled them to prophesy. (see on V.19).

(Cf. the article on the universal meaning of the Festival of Succoth and the associated conception of סוכתו של לויתן in Jeshurun VIII, p.14 (subsequently reprinted in Gesammelte Schriften Vol. 5. I.L.).

תמימם יהיו. Everywhere else the תמימם is given merely as an attribute of the animal, פרים וגו׳ תמימם, or where the תמים character is to be specially stressed it says תמימם יהיו לכם, that their completeness is only to be an expression of ourselves. Here the לכם is missing, probably just on account of the universal character of these groups of offerings. They are not merely לכם, not just expressions of our own national personality, for they represent Israel and all the nations.

V. 19. ונסכיהם. In Succa 44a and Yoma 26b the tradition is taught as הלכה למשה מסיני that on the seven days of Succoth, at the same time (Succa 48b) as the libation of wine of the morning Tamid, a libation of water was poured, and in Taanith 2b this ניסוך המים is found to be indicated in the terms נסכיה ,נסכיהם and כמשפטם of the second, sixth and seventh days (and using the last letters of these words, gives מים as a mnemonic aid). If we consider the ונסכיהם of our verse here, and look for subject of the plural suffix הם we find that it cannot possibly refer to the פרים אילים וכבשים as in V.31 of the previous chapter and II of this one. For here their נסכים have been already expressly mentioned in V.18, ומנחתם ונסכיהם. We look in vain for any other subject for our ונסכיהם than the immediately preceding עולת התמיד and מנחתה. This obviously ascribes a נסך to the עולה and one to the מנחה. The נסך of the עולה we know quite well. It is the libation of wine with which the personality represented in the עולה pours “every drop of his joy in life” into the foundations of the Altar of God’s Torah, signifying it as coming from Him and dedicating it to Him. But now, that which wine is to the עולה-personality, to the person himself, water is to that which is represented in the Mincha, the possessions of the means of nourishment and well-being that are granted to him, i.e. the flour and the oil; every drop of rain on which the growth of the produce of the soil is dependent. We have already elsewhere found the parallel of the happy blossoming of the internal joy of the human heart with that of the blossoming of plants as expressed in the Jewish ideas in words in the parallels of שמח and שוש to צמח and יין .צוף is משמח לבב אנוש and מים is מצמח צמחים and if the נסך of the עולה is wine, the נסך ascribed here to the מנחה is, without further ado, water. On the festival of the happy trustful building of our homes and the joy in the blessing of our possessions before God, ניסוך המים is joined to ניסוך היין to express the idea that not only “every drop of our wine”, every emotion of the joys of our life, but that also “every drop of our water” everything on which our very existence depends comes from God, belongs to God, remains dedicated to a life lived in His Torah, and has its real base and foundation in the foundations of the altar of His Sanctuary of the Torah.

The indication (ונסכיהם I.L.) for the performance of this ניסוך המים, peculiar to the Festival of Succoth, is primarily given on the second day which is the first day of the gradual disappearance of the contrasting relationship of the nations towards the Divine Laws and so opens the prospect of the future complete return of Mankind to God. It is only in view of such an ultimate purification of humanity to the heights they are meant to occupy that God makes every drop of rain fall. Just as the first gift of rainfall waited for the creation of Man: כי לא המטיר ה׳ אלקים על הארץ ואדם אין וגו׳ (Gen. 2,5, refer to it), so, in the period during which mankind remains on the erring path onto which it has strayed, every raindrop keeping life going and developing falls only with a view to such a humanity of the future. And because after all every day of every contemporary time does mean, however small it may be, still a gradual progress towards that future, and the world-historic path of mankind does move, like the פרי החג, in a gradual lessening of the contrast, towards its high godly calling, accordingly, in definite moral progress. At the begining of this dwindling contrast the ניסוך המים belongs more to the מנחה than to the עולה to which at bottom the מנחה itself is only an accompaniment. The drops of rain are granted more by זכות of the corn that is to be kept growing for mankind of the future, than of the men of the time, who as “אדם״ (see Gen. 1,26, I.L.) are not there, ואדם אין. It is the נסך of the מנחה next to the נסך of the עולה, they are just עלת התמיד ומנחתה ונסכיהם. But the more the contrast between what mankind is and what it should be dwindles, the true worth of Man as such comes more to the fore and then one can say that it is the merit of the people themselves that the raindrops fall on their fields. On the sixth day, the eve of the goal, the two נסכים are no longer נסכיהם, separate in their relationships, but are both נסכיה (V.31) both נסכים of the עולה, of the Tamid, of men struggling upwards to God. Finally on the seventh day both נסכים, the נסך of human flourishing and the נסך of the earth flourishing attain their united original prescription משפטם (V.33). All the נסכים together form just one נסך (ונסכהם חסר), the concept of the ניסוך המים too is at one with the idea of the Moed-group of offerings, for all contrast has disappeared and mankind in general stands at one with Israel before God in working for His purposes on earth as פרים שבעה אילים שנים כבשים בני שנה ארבעה עשר תמימם.

The seven days of Succoth which by God’s proclamation ושמחתם לפני ה׳ אלקיכם שבעת ימים invited the people to “seven days of rejoicing before the Presence of God” (Levit. 23,40) was celebrated by the nation, assembled to “חג״, to a festive circle about God and the Sanctuary of His Torah, in the עזרות, the halls in front and at the sides of the Temple, in the highest mood of jollity. But the centre-point of this was formed by drawing the water for this ניסוך המים, on account of which it was called שמחת בית השואבה. But that this very highest enthusiasm of holy joy should be attached just to this libation of water is indeed characteristic to no small degree. It is not the thought of some special occasion for joy coming from God, it is only when the thought of every daily drop of water keeping our existence down here alive being a messenger from God raises us up to happy enthusiasm about the nearness of God and fills us with bliss, only that makes every breath we draw supreme happiness before God.

V. 35. ביום השמיני not וביום as at all the preceding days, for the eighth day stands by itself as a separate festival, רגל בפני עצמו (Succa 47a — see on Levit. 23,36). On this eighth day which invites us out of the exuberant public rejoicings of the Succoth Festival, and from its inspiring contemplation of the ultimate future happiness of all men, to quiet gathering together before God before returning to the imperfect, often raw reality of the present, so that we can go back to the work of God-serving lives enrichened and elevated by the whole cycle of festivals, and in the mood we have gained by association with all our national contemporaries before God not to be estranged by any trials that may be awaiting us, on this eighth day we renew, as a parting greeting in God’s Sanctuary, the consciousness of our individual belonging to God in our fate and in the work of our lives for his Torah, as united workers on the fields of the future of His humanity as the united guide, showing the way at the head of His herd of nations, as the People of God revealing His Guidance in our lives and history, as איל אחד ,פר אחד and שבעת כבשים, with eternally unweakened freshness of youth and completeness, בני שנה תמימם, as realising that all we possess for our good, our comfort and our joys in life only come from that which the Altar of the Torah represents, and dedicate them all to that which it does represent, מנחתם ונסכיהם וגו׳, and vow to remain steadfastly and unenticeably on the heights of our calling, ושעיר חטאת אחד.

If we consider once again the normal group of offerings on the Moadim which express the ideal which the Jewish Nation is meant to attain, we find they correspond in a surprising manner to the ways in which the foreign seer saw Israel in the height of its historical position in the world, as described in the immediately preceding chapters 23-25.

The question was put from the Heights of Baal concerning the position of this nation as regards to its material fate. What would be the attitude of those high powers of Nature who hold the decision for the material prosperity of nations in their hands towards this nation? And the answer he received was that this unique nation was not subject to the ordinary powers of nature. A different power revealed itself in their history. In its historical path it is seven כבשים, in bond with the Invisible One.

And from the “Field of Seers” this nation was seen in its spiritual greatness and the God-acknowledging faithfulness to duty of its social life, as the People of God amongst the nations. As such it led the way at the head of God’s herd on earth as an איל.

And from the summit of Peor he looked down and saw the spirit of God sown in every tent of Jacob, saw every home borne by and nurturing the spirit of God blossoming up to a family life as a garden of God, in the realisation of which every father of a family appears as a working servitor in God’s household, so that the whole nation appears as פרים, as פרים שנים.

This whole ideal of blessings and happiness has only one enemy to fear — as indeed the insight of that same seer discovered and put to such fatal use — and that is:- defection from the pure moral height of the calling. That is why, in spite of what was seen on במות הבעל, on שדה צופים and on ראש הפעור the שטים catastrophe followed, hence Israel had always to associate with its שבעת כבשים, its איל אחד and its פרים שנים the שעיר חטאת אחד and at every thought of its ideal greatness to warn itself of the danger which it has always to fear at the most ideal height of its calling.

V. 39. אלה תעשו וגו׳. The offerings prescribed in this and the previous chapter are those offerings with which the nation as a whole approach God in the Festivals inviting them to God. But not only the individual offerings, the עולות ראיה and שלמי חגיגה which each person had to bring on a Moed (see Ex. 23,15) but also the offerings which proceeded from free-willed vows and dedications (Levit. 1,2 et seq.) or from events which occurred in private life, such as יולדת etc., could also be brought during the festivals, the עולות ראיה ושלמי חגיגה even on יום טוב itself, נדרים ונדבות etc., on חול המועד (Temura 14b, Beiza 19a & b). The sanctification and getting near to God by dedications of private life is in no way a cutting down of the spirit of national feeling, the intensified feeling of being a member of the national brotherhood which the festivals are to engender (hence the term חג I.L.). But the fresh impetus which the Moed is to give to the national relationship to God and the Sanctuary of His Torah is rather to benefit private life and its relationships to God. Yea the Festivals are quite specially to prove their “stirring-up” power by awakening the consciences of everybody to fulfil neglected obligations, so that an obligation which remains unfulfilled after three Moadim comes under the בל תאחר reproach of duty-forgetting neglect (Levit. 23,37 & 38).

V. 1. ויאמר משה. The rules for the festival offerings form the last chapter of the actual Law-giving. What follows now is only פרשת נדרים, the chapter on vows, sanctioning, regulating and limiting such acts which not God but we ourselves, of our own free will, have set ourselves to do or abstain from doing. It is a chapter the underlying principle of which forms the basis for those by-laws and customs, תקנות and מנהגים which have arisen from the agreements and arrangements of the social life of the community which regulate and ensure the realisation of the Divine Torah according to the special requirements of local conditions. We believe therefore that we can recognise in this ויאמר משה אל בני ישראל ככל אשר צוה ה׳ את משה a final sentence referring back to the whole of the Law-giving. Unless we are mistaken there is no other occasion when we are told that Moses transmitted any special law he had received to the people which is couched in such terms as these: ויאמר וגו׳ ככל וגו׳. The ויאמר is characteristic which as a rule designates the explanation of something which has already been given, but especially the expression ככל by which the information given goes beyond the mere announcement of the law, and also the כ the “as” which would include the way and manner in which the announcement is to be taken and understood. An expression (the “כ״ I.L.) which otherwise is used only in reporting on the carrying-out of a law, ויעשו בני ישראל ככל אשר צוה ה׳ את משה כן עשו (Ch. 1,54, and frequently elsewhere) where it wants to say that they not only just fulfilled the commands in general, but also all the finer details, as it wished to be fulfilled. So that literally the sentence says: Moses explained to the children of Israel the “how” of all that which God had commanded Moses. It says this at the end of the whole of the Lawgiving up till here, that the people had not only been informed of the short curt sentences in which the Law lies written here in front of us but that Moses explained to them every law with its whole meaning and modality. Only once again as far as we can remember, does this term ככל occur at communicating a Law (Deut. 1,4) ויהי וגו׳ דבר משה אל בני ישראל ככל אשר צוה ה׳ אתו אליהם, and there too it clearly refers to the whole Law-giving which Moses, before his death, not only in short sentences (דבר) repeated but with the whole “כ״. It had already been given to the people בדבור and באמירה, in short curt sentences and also fully explained in detail; both were then “repeated”.

V. 2. וידבר משה וגו׳. But this was a fresh pronouncement. It starts the sphere of what we have called free-willed legislation. It is accordingly given as an appendage to the real legislation, the carrying out of which forms the basis for the reason sanctioning this free-willed legislation. It opens the possibility for individuals as well as communities and the nation as a whole to establish permanent rules for ensuring the faithful keeping of the dictates of the Torah. So it is not without reason that this chapter is directed quite specially to the נשיאים who are significantly designated as ראשי המטות. We have already explained, on Ch. I, how מטה looks on the tribe as “a branch” of the great nation as a whole, within which the one common national mission is to be brought to fruition through its own special characteristics. It was the task of the ראשי המטות to guide and then to keep the manners and customs which arose from the special tendencies of each of the “branches”, as well as their laws, activities and efforts, in the direction demanded by the common national mission. And what is most indispensable as a means to achieve such activity, to a general national development, altogether for communal life is the inviolability of the spoken word or promise, the לא יחל דברו which is what the following laws deal with. At the same time — as is given in the following verses on היתר נדרים — a healthy palliative to such vows and resolutions is entrusted to the ראשי המטות, as well as to family counselors and spiritual advisers amongst the people, and it is also with an eye to this that the laws concerning vows are primarily directed to the ראשי המטות.

זה הדבר אשר צוה ה׳. This formula to introduce an edict is primarily found, not to commands which are always applicable but usually to such which apply just to special occasions of the moment, as at the Manna (Ex. 16,16 & 32), תרומת המשכן (ibid. XXXV,4), מלואים (Levit. 8,5 & IX,6). Also, the law that an heiress is not to marry out of her tribe (Ch. 36,6-8) is taken on account of this to apply solely to that generation (Baba Bathra 120b). Only פרשת שחוטי חוץ (Levit. 17,2) although expressly ordered for all time, חקת עולם וגו׳ (V.7) is also introduced by זה הדבר. If we consider that a command to be fulfilled at once demands the immediate application of the whole force of our energy and exercise of will power, the same form of introduction for an unlimited time in which an order is to be obeyed may only wish to mark the significance and importance of it. Our law here about vows, although applying to all time, as is explained (in Baba Bathra there) by the application of a גזרה שוה to שחוטי חוץ, is also made important by this mode of introduction. By this making it parallel to שחוטי חוץ, the general address to ראשי המטות is extended to אהרן ובניו וכל ישראל as at שחוטי חוץ and the procedure of mitigating, making vows void is given to any three men out of the people who are capable of forming a just opinion, even if otherwise they do not belong to the class of those who possess legal knowledge, מומחה; as then רמב״ם, when he says that for נדרים altogether a יחיד מומחה suffices. מומחה is not to be taken in the strictness of a סמוך as it is for the procedures of other laws, and does not mean רב מובהק. A peculiarity which the ר״ן on Nedarim 87b simply deducts from the conception ראשי המטות which does not involve judicial qualification to an eminent degree, אלקים as decisions in other laws do. All these laws agree with the way we have taken the נדרים chapter to be a chapter on free-willed legislation and the rights of customs, separated from the real legislation and having a subsidary position. But this placing the נדרים chapter parallel to the שחוטי חוץ chapter which results (ibid.) in making the power of annulling the validity of vows apply also to the latter to יש שאלה בהקדש ,נדרי הקדש may rest on a deep inner reason. For the words of our sages הנודר כאלו בנה במה, והמקיימו כאלו מקריב עליו קרבן does express such an inner relation. Both, במה and נדר aspire to the sanction of acting purely subjectively at one’s own discretion, apart from and beside what the Torah ordains. The generality, the universal application which such a general sanction expresses for שחוטי חוץ and נדרים is absolutely reprehensible. In the נדרים-laws such subjectivity receives only a limited and conditional sphere of activity. (See Nedarim 22a, and ר״ן thereon).

V. 3. נדר .איש כי ידור נדר לה׳ וגו׳ (see Gen. 28,20). Up to now, apart from the special vow to Nazaritism, we only know נדר as נדרי הקדש, as dedicating or vowing an object to קדשי מזבח ,קרבן or for the Temple, קדשי בדק הבית, either with the formula נדבה ,הרי זו or ,הרי עלי נדר (Levit. 22,21), and in both cases the object affected, if by נדבה immediately, if by נדר at the moment it is fulfilled, becomes prohibited to be used for any profane use. Now the case is given here that a person ידר נדר לה׳ לאסר אסר על נפשו, that somebody makes a vow whereby an object does not become prohibited from use generally, but solely על נפשו, by himself, to himself it is as if affected by a נדר הקדש. Hence, we believe, the saying in Nedarim 14a: איש כי ידור נדר לה׳ עד שידור בדבר הנדור, the vow discussed here is only valid if made regarding an object which could legally be made prohibited for his use by himself e.g. could be vowed to קדשי מזבח or for בדק הבית. But not בדבר האסור, if e.g. he had said: it shall be prohibited to me as דם or נבלה, as the prohibition of דם or נבלה is not one which is effected by a vow. This limiting the object to one which must be of a הקדש-like character is called התפסה. So that the actual נדר is only a factual vow inasmuch as it is to give an object the serious nature of או השבע שבועה .אוסר חפצא על נפשיה :הקדש, or if he made the vow in terms of an oath. The nature of an oath is always a personal one, it binds his will with respect to an object or to some action. So we have here two categories: נדר לאסר אסר על נפש and שבועה לאסור אסור על נפשו. If someone says: Wine shall be to him as if it was a קרבן, then he has forbidden the use of wine to himself by a נדר. If he says he swears he will have no use of wine, then he has forbidden the use of wine to himself by a שבועה. This hypothetical difference between נדר and נדבה has several important results, a נדר can only refer to a concrete object, a דבר שיש בו ממש but not to an abstract idea a דבר שאין בו ממש, accordingly not to an action, whether this action is expressed as a noun or a verb. Accordingly not “sleep or sleeping”, to walk or walking shall be to me as prohibitive as a קרבן. On the other hand, by a factual vow one can indirectly make the fulfilling be as a קרבן to him. For the duty rests on the person and not on the matter. But a שבועה, by which the decision of the will of a person to do something or not to do so is affected can apply to something which is abstract a דבר שאין בו ממש, e.g. שבועה שלא אישן היום (I swear I will not sleep to-day). But a שבועה to abstain from a duty, e.g. שלא אשב בסוכה (that I will not sit in a succa) is invalid, for the will is already bound regarding the duty, relating to a Mitzva a person is not free. Hence the saying in Nedarim 13b: חומר בשבועות מבנדרים, ובנדרים מבשבועות, חומר בנדרים שהנדרים חלין על המצות כברשות מה שאין כן בשבועות וחומר בשבועות שהשבועות חלות על דבר שיש בו ממש ושאין בו ממש מה שאין כן בנדרים, But מדרבנן a נדר does apply also to תוספות) דבר שאין בו ממש ibid.). Further, in popular language כנויים, other terms, are used for נדרים and שבועות e.g. קונם for קרבן etc., which in effect have the full power of נדרים and כל כנויי נדרים כנדרים וכו׳ :שבועות, and also the full formula for vows need not necessarily be used, even if only the sense of a vow is indicated, יד so that what is said has only the “handle” of a vow, it is still fully binding: ידות נדרים כנדרים (Nedarim 2b). Altogether the addition of an התפסה is not essential, simply saying דבר זה אסור עלי has the full force of a ר״ן) נדר on Nedarim 2a). Finally it is only when referring to indifferent things that the express נדר or שבועה expression has to be pronounced. For a Mitzva purpose simply declaring one’s intention is binding (Nedarim 8a ר״ן and רא״ש ibid.). After all the very first נדר recorded עשר אעשרנו לך (Gen. 28,20) was not a correct נדר expression by נדר בלשון שבועה (see also 206,5). Even if such a vowing intention is not expressed in words at all but is shown by repeated practice it is binding (ibid. 214,1).

אסר .לאסר אסר the word for actual tying-up and chaining is here transferred to the binding down of the will by the word of a vow or oath. יחל ,לא יחל דברו is the Hiphil of חלל as in Ezek. 39,7, ולא אַחֵל את שם קדשי עוד. There must be a difference between the Piel חַלַל and the Hiphil חַלֵל .הֵחַל means acting against the holiness of an object the object itself remains in its holy state but one treats it as if it were profane, thus חלל ברית ,חלל את השם ,חלל שבת etc. But הַחֵל, hiphil, means to cause something to remain in a חולין, profane condition, but to allow it to come to holiness. Thus in the quotation from Ezekiel: ולא אחל את שם קדשי עוד it does not say: I will no longer desecrate My holy Name, but: I will no longer leave it in the desecration into which it has come through Israel’s sins. Accordingly לא יחלל דברו would mean: he shall not break his word, shall not act against the holiness of his word. But לא יחל דברו means: he shall not allow his word to be without result, not allow it to be חולין. It binds him. This expression itself points to the possibility that his word, although he has spoken it, could be without result. And then the Gemora lays stress on the concept of the pronoun form and teaches הוא אינו מיחל אבל אחרים מחלין לו (Berachot 32a), he has no power to make his word have no result but others can do that for him, so that in the words themselves they see the idea of what the halacha teaches of the mitigating power given to the חכם concerning נדרים, that חכם עוקר נדר מעיקרו. An investigation brings to light the fact that the vow which had been uttered was invalid already beforehand. The result leaves the utterance in its חולין lack of power. But as long as he has not placed his spoken word under such an investigation or if such an investigation does not lead to such a result, לא יחל דברו he may not allow his word to be חולין, to have no power but rather ככל היוצא מפיו יעשה.

This redress for vows, to which the ראשי המטות of V.3 — to whose administration of it, as remarked above, it is assigned — glances at, is indicated in the text by just the slightest nuance, so that — as רמב״ן remarks in his commentary — the written word of the Torah which is available to everybody should not seem to support any misconceived and misused carelessness in regarding the holiness of the spoken word or vow. It belongs to those institutions which are completely, or nearly completely reserved for tradition, which, as the Gemora in Chagiga 10a, puts it, are פורחין באויר without any literal support in the text of the Torah, or at any rate are כהררים התלוין בשערה, in comparison to the extent of their sphere and importance have only a hairbreadth indication in the written text are “like mountains hanging by a hair”, שהן מקרא מועט והלכות מרובות, whereas other institutions in the Torah are accorded long and detailed precise wording for their laws, and nevertheless הן הן גופי תורה these as much as those are equally essential parts of the Torah. The redress for נדרים, here entrusted to the ראשי המטות, consists in their finding that the one who made the vow, now regrets having done so, and if he had given the matter proper consideration he certainly would not have made it at all (חרטה מעיקרא); or that circumstances have arisen which in normal conditions could have been foreseen, and which would have restrained him from making the vow had he forseen them (פתח) (but אין פותחין בנולד not for circumstances which have arisen subsequently to his having made the vow and normally could not have been foreseen). He has then to submit his vow to the investigation of one who is competent to examine it, and if in accordance with such a one’s finding, the vow had been made from its inception through hasty thoughtlessness, he annuls it by declaring מותר לך, it is not, has really never been, binding on you. There are, nevertheless, a number of legal conditions under which a vow can be annulled, which have to be gone into very thoroughly and an annulment of a vow obtained by keeping back or being silent about any relevant factor would be totally ineffective and useless self-deception. For no power of “binding” or “unloosening” is placed in the hands of a Jewish חכם, only the ability and the duty of using investigating discernment.

V. 4. ואשה וגו׳. A resolution which a man has vowed to keep is from the beginning binding on him. Only to his national contemporaries and their representatives can he lay his vow — and, as it is worked out on Deut. 23,22 et seq., he should lay his vow — for discerning and circumspective decision. For a man is the independent maker of his position in life. And if, by some binding vow, not suitable for annulment, he has taken on himself to make some abnormal conditions in the ordinary course of his life, then it is up to him to see that this special arrangement in the conditions of his life be decisively kept. Not so for a woman. The moral greatness of the woman’s calling in life itself demands entering and adopting herself to a position in life created by another. The woman herself does not provide the house. She enters the home provided by the man and rules in it as the happiness-bringing administrator of all that is to be found there, in the sanctity of manners, and morals and feelings directed towards God. Still more than the man has the woman to guard against making restrictions, abnormal arrangements in the course of her life, they could permanently stand in the way of the fulfilment of her calling, and from this point of view one can understand the careful thoughtful prescriptions with which the Word of God has guarded the vowing woman against the consequences of her own words, and confers on the father a right of restricting veto on the vows of a youthful daughter still under his care, to the father and fiancé conjointly on those of a betrothed daughter, and to the husband on those of his wife.

בנעריה. The fact could rest on deep psychological reasons that in this one law amongst all the laws of the Torah, the age of maturity for making binding vowing resolutions starts earlier than that for all other declarations being considered legal. In every other relation the responsibility, the accountability for one’s actions starts, with boys after the thirteenth year, and for girls — to whom the Torah ascribes an earlier ripening of the intelligence — after the twelfth year, both moreover at having attained puberty. But the binding force of vows starts at one year earlier, at the thirteenth year for boys and at the twelfth year for girls, provided that they know that it is to God that vows are made יודעין לשם מי נדרו (Nidda 45b). This עונת נדרים, starting the period of maturity for making vows one year earlier than that for other legal matters, provided the general intelligence has also matured sufficiently, is expressed by the formula מופלא סמוך לאיש, and is considered so seriously as being דאוריתא, that according to one opinion, true not accepted as halacha, for a מופלא סמוך לאיש, even מלקות would be incurred if he broke his vows (ibid. 46a). If we consider how, in the years in which boys mature to youth, girls to maidenhood, quietly and known only to God, resolutions are often vowed which are decisive for the whole course of life, and the rich contents of the life of a noble man or noble woman are often only the ripened fruit of such resolutions vowed to God by the boy or girl, then the loving seriousness with which God receives these proferred resolutions can indeed be understood.

Now the Torah states: בבית אביה בנעריה and again at the end of this chapter (V.17) בנעריה בית אביה, that during the period of her נעורים age, i.e. until six months after she has attained puberty, when she goes over from the character of a נערה to that of a בוגרת (see Ex. 21,7) she is under the care of her father regarding her vows (Kethuvoth 46b & 47a).

V. 5—6. ואם הניא וגו׳ ושמע וגו׳. On the day on which the father learns of the betrothal (the legal betrothal is very much more binding in Jewish Law than what we call “the engagement”, it is called אירוסין, and nowadays forms the first part of our marriage ceremony I.L.) of a daughter who is still legally under his care he can still exercise הפרה, declare a vow she has made to be annulled. But if he allows that day to pass without saying anything, any later declaration has no effect, and moreover, the day is reckoned as being passed at sundown (Nedarim 76b). — הניא (from נוא, the root of נא, see Ex. 12,9), is the specific term for הפרה for the effect of the intervention of the father and the husband. It is an interruption, a stopping of the continuation of the vow — מוגז גייז — differentiated from the התרה of the חכם which does away with the whole existence of the vow from the beginning, is עוקר נדד מעיקרו (Nazir 21b and 22a).

כל נדריה וגו׳. As we shall see from verses 14 & 17, the power of veto given to a husband is limited to such vows that are either detrimental to the health, the physical well-being of his wife נדרי ענוי נפש or curtailing the mutual relations of married life דברים שבינו לבינה. According to almost all general views the paternal veto is similarly limited, as the Sifri also expressly teaches. Only רמב״ם (הל׳ נדרים 12, 1) confers on the father the right of unlimited veto on the vows of his young daughter, and the מגדל עוז in a recorded communication to the חכמי לוניל has endeavoured to justify this view of the Rambam, especially against the objections raised in the ספרי. His reasons for justification are based, apart from the unlimited application implied by the wording in the text of our verse, principally on the fact that the נדרי עינוי נפש but especially the דברים שבינו לבינה which, after all are totally different in the relations of a daughter to her father than those between a husband and wife, are not specially discussed at all in the Talmud with reference to the father. But if we can take the opinion we ventured to give on V.4 to be correct, viz. that even the power of veto conferred on a father is only out of consideration for her future calling of wife, then perhaps the difficulties raised against the general way would automatically solve themselves. The דברים שבינו לבינה against which the father can intervene would then perhaps be in fact only such which, looking ahead, could presumably interfere with a harmonious and intimate married-life, and the דברים שבינו לבינה which the father has power to veto would in fact be identical with those of the husband. Not quite irrelevant to this way of taking it may be that at the retrospective concluding sentence (V. 17) the בין איש לאישתו comes first and then בין אב לבתו follows almost only as a consequence of it. Finally it is this sentence בין איש לאשתו בין אב לבתו on which in the limitation of the veto of the father to the same extent of that of the husband is based: מקיש את האב לבעל מה הבעל אינו מפר אלא נדרים שבינו לבינה ונדרים שיש בהם עינוי נפש אף האב אינו מפר אלא נדרים שבינו לבינה ונדרים שיש בהן עינוי נפש.

V. 7. ואם היה תהיה לאיש וגו׳. It is only in V.11 that it comes to speak of נשואה, the case of the wife after her marriage, ואם בית אישה נדרה, if she had already gone to live with her husband. So that our ואם היה תהיה לאיש can only refer to the state of a נערה המאורסה of a girl still living in the house of her father and as נערה still of an age still under his protective care regarding vows but already legally bound to her future husband. In such a case the law declares that only the father and the bethrothed fiancé conjointly have the right to veto her vows: אביה ובעלה מפירין נדריה. Moreover, as soon as she is engaged, the ארוס has the right of veto even on such vows which she had made before the betrothal, the נדריה עליה, if the father had not heard of them and intervened before, but now, even for such vows he can only veto in conjunction with the fiancé. But a husband has no right of intervention on vows his wife made before the betrothal: אין הבעל מפר בקודמין (Nedarim 66b & 67a). — ואם היה תהיה, even at repeated betrothals, if the first ארוס died. If at the time of his death she was still at the age of a נערה she goes back again to the sole preventative care of her father regarding her vows, מת הארוס נתרוקנה רשות לאב (ibid. 70a). If she becomes betrothed again while still a נערה, her father can again only exercise the veto conjointly with the second ארוס (ibid. 17a). But if the father dies during the time of the אירוסין-conditions the ארוס then has no power of veto by himself: (ibid. 70b) מת האב לא נתרוקנה רשות לבעל.

V. 8. ושמע אישה. According to the accepted halacha (ibid. 73a) both the father and the husband can proclaim a veto in general terms on the vows of the daughter and fiancée respectively, and accordingly דרך ת״ח עד שלא היתה בתו יוצאת מאצלו אומר לה כל נדרים שנדרת בתוך ביתי הרי הן מופרין וכן הבעל עד שלא תכנס לרשותו אומר לה כל נדרים שנדרת עד שלא תכנסי לרשותי הרי הן מופרין שמשתכנס לרשותו אינו יכול להפר (ibid. 72b). — וקמו וגו׳ and then the father alone can do nothing.
V. 9. ואם ביום וגו׳, but the validity of the vow is broken if a similar utterance is made by the fiancé and added to that of the father.

V. 10. Verse 7 the case was already discussed where as indicated by the repeated הויה — she had repeatedly become an ארוסה, that the first אירוסין had been dissolved by death or גירושין and then, according to Nedarim 70b, מקיש קודמי הויה שניה לקודמי הויה ראשונה, the filial relationship before the second betrothal is made quite similar to what it was before the first; מה קודמי הויה ראשונה אב מפר לחודיה אף קודמי הויה שניה אב מפר לחודיה, even after broken אירוסין the right of intervention is restored to the father exactly as it was originally before the betrothal; היה תהיה the two states of betrothals and the transition to them are similar to each other.
