So that we have already been told that an אלמנה or גרושה from האירוסין if she is still of the נערה age is again under the protective care of her father regarding vows she may make, so that our verse can only be speaking אלמנה וגרושה מן הנשואין. Once she has entered the house of her husband as נשואה, she has — in a legal sense — left her father’s house for ever; and even if the marriage is dissolved by death or divorce, even if still in the years of a נערה she does not return to the old position, relative to her father, with regard to vows. Any vow she makes in the condition of אלמנה or גרושה that יקום עליה, neither father in the present nor husband in any future marriage has any power of annulling by declaration, for as we have already remarked on V.7, אין הבעל מפר בקודמין, the husband has no authority over vows made before the marriage. Only as it says in V.11, אם בית אישה נדרה, the husband has only power to annul vows made after the marriage.
V. 11. אם בית אישה נדרה, see above on V.10.

V. 13. וה׳ יסלח לה, even if she had broken her vow without knowing that her husband had pronounced the הפרה and made it null and void, for the validity of the vow is objectively removed by the הפרה of the husband either for all time or at any rate for the duration of the marriage (see on next verse).

V. 14. כל נדר. The authority of the husband to intervene is restricted here to נדרי עינוי נפש to such vows which would entail neglect of care for one’s health or curtailment of one’s joy in life, embitter one’s existence, or stunt one’s feelings. To which must be added the halacha derived from בין איש לאשתו of דברים שבינו לבינה vows which affect the conjugal relations of husband and wife. The former are rendered invalid for all time by the הפרה of the husband, these latter only for the period of the marriage with this husband (Nedarim 79b).

V. 15. ואם החרש יחריש לה, even בשותק על מנת למיקט (Nedarim 79a), even if he keeps silent, not to agree with the vow, but only to keep his wife in suspense for a time and then to annul it, once the sun has set and the day on which he heard of the vow has passed he has no authority to act. Keeping silent with the intention of agreement establishes the vow immediately and even on the same day cannot be revoked קיים בלבו קיים (ibid.).
V. 16. ואם הפר, if after his silent or definite agreement he still in any way brings her to break her vow, he has to bear the blame.

V. 17. בין איש לאשתו (see on verses 14 and 6). בנעוריה בית אביה, for as long as she belongs to her father’s house as נערה, accordingly until she has gone over to the house of a husband through נשואין.
See further about נדרים on Deut. 23,22.

If we consider that this retrospective final sentence אלה החוקים וגו׳ only stresses the regulations given in this chapter of the relationships between daughter and wife to father and husband, but the law given in V. 3 of the sanctity of vows and promises generally remains without mention, it seems that these regulations are what this chapter really wishes to deal with, and the general declaration of the gravity and binding force of the spoken word is only mentioned here as introduction and indeed as a contrast. A man has no power whatsoever to annul his own vows, for that he has to go to his national contemporaries, but towards his young daughter and his wife he has restricted authority to intervene. Looked at from this point of view this chapter on נדרים could be connected with, as complementing and perhaps even giving the reason for, the laws given in Ch. XXVII over the rights of inheritance of women. The calling of woman is, to be absorbed into the home of a man as the most important factor of the component parts of that home. But it is not her calling to found a home independently. From that springs both the dependence of her עינוי נפש and דברים שבינו לבינה vows on the agreement of her husband as we have indicated on verses 4-6, as well as the possibility of finding in that the reason for the law that normally the hereditary property passes to the son and not to the daughter.

V. 1. Already above in Ch. 25,16 it had been declared that breaking the Midianite might was a necessity for ensuring the moral and spiritual integrity of the Jewish People as the Midianites were continuing to try their arts of seduction on Israel. Now here the order is given to carry out the war to be waged against the Midianites.

V. 2. נקם נקמת וגו׳. Moses, who had had to bring the people over to the Torah of God built up on chastity and faithfulness is to see, before his death, the battle against the Midianites so necessary for making these two fundamental pillars of his mission secure, for protecting his people against ג״ע (Licentiousness) and ע״ז (Idolatry): נקם וגו׳. We have already on Gen. 4,15 pointed out the relationship of נקם to קום. (Cf. ;זול נזל ;הום נהם דוח נדח ;אוץ נאץ ;פוץ נפץ ;סוג נסג ;זור נזר et alia.). It is the re-erection of rights which have been trodden under foot, or a person who has been thrown to the ground. The נוקם identifies himself with the object to be raised up. That probably explains the reflexive form נקם, and also the mode of construing with נקם נקמת בני ישראל מאת המדינים ,מ. The purpose is not revenge, throwing down of an enemy, that would be construed with ב. The purpose is the re-erection of Israel from the Midianites, its spiritual and moral freeing out of the power of their arts.

V. 3. אל העם ,וידבר וגו׳ אל העם לאמר, not to the leaders, this act of vindication of its spiritual and moral integrity is to come from the people themselves. By this war being against Midian and not against Moab whose purpose was to destroy the material strength of Israel rather than their spiritual and moral strength, the spiritual and moral motive of this war must have been brought to the minds of the people with double significance. Not who brings about Israel’s material ruin, but he who achieves its spiritual and moral death is the real enemy. — חלץ ,החלצו, to bring something out of its present connections, e.g. stones out of a wall (Levit. 14,43), after loosening the straps to draw a shoe off the foot to which it had been firmly attached. (Deut. 25,9). Hence so frequently used for freeing somebody from a danger, from a fix into which he had landed, הֶחָלוץ in the army, an advanced column sent ahead detached from the main body of troops (Josh. 6,7 et seq.). Hence חלוצי צבא, those sent out from the midst of the people for military service. The duty of serving in the army lies on everybody. They send a part of the whole population out of their midst to fulfil this duty on behalf of this general duty. Hence the peculiar construction החלצו מאתכם. The subject of the verb החלצו is the general public, by מאתכם this is restricted to a chosen number. החלצו by itself postulates the demand to all to detach themselves from the restraining bonds of the home and to join the army (see Yebamoth 102b שלופי מביתא לקרבא. (מאתכם limits this duty to those chosen from them, but, by the preceding מאתכם these are to be regarded as the representatives of the whole nation. — לתת נקמת ה׳ במדין, that which in V.2 was regarded as נקמת בני ישראל is here brought to the minds of the people as נקמת ה׳. Every disturbance to their spiritual and moral integrity tears them away from God. He, accordingly sends them out to accomplish His retaliation against Midian. By their policy of seduction Midian had practiced the worst international crime and thereby in the eyes of God had lost the right to live as a nation amongst nations.

V. 4. אלף למטה וגו׳. This term, repeated again in Verses 5 & 6, expresses again the thought already remarked on V.3 that those that go out to fight are to accomplish a task as delegates of the whole nation, every tribe is to be represented by an equal number of men chosen from their midst.

V. 5. מסר .וימסרו only occurs in תנ״ך here and in V.16. In Rabbinic Hebrew it is the quite ordinary expression for handing over, delivering. Here the term corresponds to the whole conditions indicated. Each tribe delivered a thousand men to Moses, chosen as its representatives to carry out the common task of the whole nation.

V. 6. וישלח אתם וגו׳ ואת פינחס וגו׳. At none of the earlier battles, not in the war against Sichon, against Og, against the Emorites is the presence of a priest with ארון and חצוצרות so expressly mentioned as it is here. Those were wars undertaken for defence or conquest, material reasons. But at the base of this war there were motives of the highest spiritual and moral interests. For that, above all, the priest with the Evidence of the Torah and the חצוצרות calling up for the support of God were befitting. — זה ארון ולוחות שבו :וכלי הקדש (Sota 43a). For was it not a question of ensuring the unattacked existence of the לוחות and the ארון, the Torah and its bearers and protectors in Israel, in the midst of the nations of the world. חצצרות התרועה (see Ch. 10,8 & 9). ספרי) אין ידו אלא רשותו ,בידו).

V. 8. על חלליהם, the kings were not in the front of the battle. — את בלעם. It seems that after he had seen the success of his advice, he came again to Moab and Midian from his homeland and he was the life and soul of the continued seductive arts of the Midianites. According to Sanhedrin 106a, he had come to ask for recompense for his so successful advice.

V. 10. את כל עריהם במושבתם. In Habak. 3,7 we read: ירגזון יריעות ארץ מדין from which can be concluded that the Midianites dwelt in tents like nomads. The same seems to be deduced from Judges 6,5, where they are described — albeit in conjunction with other nations, as invading the land of Israel with their tents, herds and camels. Cf. also ibid. VII,12; VIII,21 & 24 where they are characterised as Ishmaelites by which probably nomads are to be understood. If, nevertheless, here it speaks of their cities and castles, they must, although predominantly living a nomadic life, still have had settlements in cities which would explain the addition of במושבתם to עריהם, the cities were places where, although generally leading nomadic lives they still had fixed settlements to which at times they retired. ואת כל טירתם (see Gen. 25,16), there we see that the Ishmaelites also had fixed settlements and castles.

V. 11—12. ויקחו וגו׳, here the whole booty is called collectively שלל and מלקח, in the following verse שבי is differentiated from מלקח. In Gen. 19,8 we have already pointed out the relationship of שלל to סלל ,זלל and צלל. The common basic conception is: to take something away from somewhere. So that the root שלל does not necessarily have the idea of using force, and in Ruth 2,16 it designates the intentional dropping ears of corn from the stacks to which they belong to increase the “spoil” of the gleaners. The ears are taken away from the possession of the owner of the field, but with his permission. In general שלל designates everything taken in war as booty, i.e. taken away from the hitherto lawful possessors including livestock as זה שלל דוד (Sam. I. 30,28). Used next to ,מלקח שלל designates lifeless booty but מלקח living, as such that only remain with the new owner if held fast by him, kept in his “grip”, here animals and people. But שבי specially designates human beings taken captive in war. שבה, related to ספח (משפחה ,שפחה) שפח ,שבע ,שבע ,צבא ,צבה, designates increasing the sphere of one’s personal power by absorbing the personality of another in it. — מלקוח used next to שבי, as in V.12 refers to the animals, and שבי to the people.
V. 14. פקודי החיל are those entrusted with leading the army, who have to conduct their behaviour and are responsible for it.

V. 16. הן הנה, like הן נזבח (Ex. 8,22). היו לבני ישראל, perhaps with the same meaning as כי תהיה לאיש זר (Levit. 22,12) and הייתי הלילה לאיש (Ruth 1,12); They gave themselves up to the sons of Israel to make them unfaithful to God for the sake of Peor, i.e. to make them fall to the god of lechery.

V. 17—18. As the purpose of this act was the prevention of heathen immoral elements becoming implanted in Israel, we must take it that the national degeneration had its roots essentially in the male sex, but that the female sex, if removed from impure influences and impressions at an early age remained fully able to absorb and adopt all the ideas of pure morality. Similarly in Deut. 23,4, regarding the adoption of Ammonites and Moabites into the Jewish nation, a difference is made between the sexes; whereas males are completely excluded, it is permitted to admit the feminine sex בקהל ה׳ even at more mature ages.

V. 19. ואתם וגו׳ (See Ch. 5,2 & 3, and XIX,11 et seq.). אתם ושביכם. As נכריות (non-Jews I.L.) the captives could not be .מקבל טומאה טומאה only begins with the relation of people to מקדש וקדשיו (the Sanctuary and its holy things I.L.). שביכם, the captives, accordingly, would only be receptive to טומאה after they had become converts to Judaism, שנתגיירו, an act that could have occurred immediately with many of them. Further as כלי מתכות — according to one opinion even all vessels except כלי חרס — become אבי אבות if they come into contact with a corpse and make people who touch them אב הטומאה and so require הזיה, the captives then, after having become גרים, by touching such a כלי would require הזיה.

V. 20. וכל בגד וגו׳ (See Levit. 11,32). תתחטאו: as כל בגד וגו׳ is the object of the sentence the reflexive of תתחטאו can only be understood as terminative in a similar way to והתנחלתם אותם (Levit. 25,46): “every garment etc., have ye to expiate from sin for yourselves.”

V. 21. ויאמר וגו׳ הבאים למלחמה. As it does not say מן המלחמה but למלחמה, one is justified in assuming that the following regulations were given not only at the return from the war but at the departure for the war.
זאת חקת התורה. See on Ch. 19,2.

V. 22. אך את הזהב. We have already remarked on Levit. 11,32, that the word כלי from V.20 is implied to be added here, and thereby the close attachment of this verse here to what is said there is given. Every garment etc., every vessel made from wood or leather you have to expiate from sin only by הזיה, but metal vessels require הכשר apart from that (כל דבר אשר וגו׳) as well as אך במי וגו׳) טבילה) as is prescribed in the following verse.

V. 23. כל דבר וגו׳, everything that has entered the material by fire, you have to extract by fire, and all that has not entered by fire you have to get rid of by water. תעבירו, in the sense of העביר חטאתך (Sam. II. 12,13) העבר חרפתי (Ps. 119,39) ויעבר הקדשים מן הארץ (Kings I. 15,12). This lays down the law that metal utensils used for food into which prohibited matter has penetrated must be freed from such matter before being permitted to be used. Vessels into which the prohibited matter has penetrated by heat directly, i.e. without the medium of a liquid, have to be heated up to a glowing red heat in the fire (ליבון) to draw such matter out; if it had not penetrated directly by the fire it becomes extracted by boiling water (הגעלה). This principle that matter can be extracted by use of the same medium by which it had penetrated is expressed by the canon: כבולעו כך פולטו (as it swallows so does it exude I.L.). See Avoda Zara 55b, et seq. Accordingly forbidden matter that has penetrated into a vessel: גיעולי נכרים, — the “issur matter” that exudes from non-Jewish vessels (געל, to cast forth from oneself, Job 21,10 and Levit. 26,11) — the fact that issur-matter remains issur even if it has penetrated into the material of a vessel, although in any case even for the taste, they have become weakened down sufficiently to become distasteful אי אפשר לקדרה בת יומא דלא פגמה פורתא (Avoda Zara 67b, תוספות there) presupposes the fact that has also been established already elsewhere (see Ch. V.3) that טעם כעיקר that prohibited matter that cannot be detected by any of the other senses but only by taste remains prohibited.

אך במי נדה יתחטא, by the whole construction of this sentence this cannot mean the הזיה of טומאת מת. For were it to do so it would surely come after כל אשר לא וגו׳ as all vessels even those that do not come in connection with fire at all, e.g. wooden vessels still require הזיה as already stated in V.20. Clearly אך במי נדה וגו׳ orders something which only applies to metal food-vessels. כל דבר etc. V.23 summarises the metals enumerated in V.22, two things are pronounced about them:- if it is assumed that they had been used directly on the fire, then the issur-material which has been absorbed into them must be extracted from them also by fire; and further, they, these metal cooking and eating utensils, are to be במי נדה יתחטא before being used. וכל אשר לא יבא באש, non-metallic utensils, which do not come on the fire need only be freed by water from issur-material that has been absorbed by them, and apart from that do not require the חטוי במי נדה prescribed for metal utensils. The Halacha teaches (Avoda Zara 75b) that by this חטוי, a special טבילה and indeed in a מקוה ארבעים סאה (see Levit. 11,36), and במים שהנדה טובלת בהן, whereas for טבילת כלים מטומאתן even a רביעית would suffice (see תוספות ibid.). מי נדה would then be here the general designation of the מקוה for people who have “to keep themselves away” on account of טומאה. Thus in Zach. 13,1, מקור לחטאת ולנדה, where the הזיה for טומאת מת is designated as חטאת and the general טבילה as נדה. By a טבילה similar to that prescribed for people being ordered here for metal utensils, the expression יתחטא which otherwise is so striking would be explained, making the utensil “to be expiated from sin” not the object but the subject, looking at the טבילת כלי as if it were טבילת אדם, it is the personality of Jewish people that is to be regarded in this טבילת כלי מדין hence יתחטא and hence the ארבעים סאה (see also Levit. 11,36).

This טבילה ordered for metal vessels when they pass from non-Jewish possession into Jewish, even if they are free from all טומאה and every איסור can only pertain to the קדושה, the conception of the moral sanctification of the whole of life, into the realm of which the Jew is to elevate his material enjoyment of food. But the limitation to metal utensils could be meant to give this טבילה yet a special meaning. A metal utensil is the most speaking sign of Man’s intelligent mastery over the earth and its materials. Not only the shape but the use of the material itself proclaims that. But eating food is just that activity which primarily belongs completely to the animal, physical, sphere of man’s nature, and a metal utensil used for eating purposes represents in itself the spiritual, the mental side of Man employed in the service of the sphere of his senses. But under the regime of the Divine Torah the whole life of the senses also is to be elevated out of the unfree physical realm and directed to the sphere of the moral inner free-willed God-serving activities. According to this, it seems to us, one can well understand why the Torah orders the consecrating expiation act of טבילה essentially for the admission of metal food-utensils and also why this טבילה is called התחטא “expiating oneself from sin”, for just through it the consciousness of our inner free will, which is the ability to abstain from sin, is revived and strengthened. So also the ירושלמי Avoda Zara V.15: לפי שיצאו מטומאת הנכרי ונכנסו לקדושת ישראי. Glass vessels are also made by being fashioned by fire and the material can be fused and melted and so is similar to metal, hence glass and glazed utensils used for food require טבילה מדרבנן (Avoda Zara ibid.).

V. 26. מלקוח השבי, only the living spoil was divided. Lifeless booty was kept by the taker of it. The reason may be, because the animals and the human beings could only be kept by everybody working together to look after them and so were regarded as universal spoil, whereas to guard lifeless objects the individual owner by himself would be sufficient. שא את ראש (see Ex. 30,12).

V. 27. תפשי מלחמה (cf. תופש כנור Gen. 4,21), תופשי התורה (Jer. 2,8); all those who have taken in hand the settling of this war. It comprises all those who were in the army, no difference to be made between officers and men.
V. 28. מכס. See Ex. XII5.

V. 29. תקחו. In verse 28 it does not say אחד אחז etc., as in V.30. As תרומת ה׳ the “heave-offering” is indeed not to be taken haphazardly, just as it comes, but to be chosen, and possibly this choosing is indicated by this absolute לאלעזר הכהן .— תקחו this was to be done, as רמב״ן remarks, as an exception in this case, a battle for the holy moral purpose of revindication. Otherwise the כהנים received no part of any booty captured.
V. 30. אחז, taken out, without choosing (see on V.29).

V. 32. יתר הבז (cf. V.53). אנשי הצבא בזזו איש לו. Lifeless valuables, which every man who had taken them kept for himself, are called בז. The מלקוח which came to be divided here was over and above this בז.

V. 49. ולא נפקד. We have already (in Gen. 21,1) stressed the relationship of the root פקד with בגד, and בית and remarked that פקד means mentally investing an object with the qualities, conditions and relationships that are due to it. So then as פקד as a rule means to think of the attributes which really belong to some existing object but which it still has not yet obtained, it is often used also for thinking of existing conditions and relationships which should be applied but have no object to which to apply them, i.e. which is missing.

V. 50. ונקרב את קרבן ה׳. It does not say ונקרב קרבן לה׳ (we will offer an offering to God I.L.) but את קרבן ה׳ (the offering of God I.L.) i.e. the offering which automatically results as a duty and necessity out of such an experience, to express being forced to the consciousness that it can only be the proximity of God. i.e. our relationship to God and His Torah that we have to thank for such an event. Thoughtfully they choose for that all the womens’ jewellery, perhaps with a double idea:- thereby to remove every remembrance of the Midianite women out of their midst, as well as to prove their future faithful adherence to morality to vindicate their having participated in the miraculous protective grace of God. This קרבן is taken in a similar way in the Gemora Sabbath 64a & b.
כומז: see Ex. 35,22.
V. 51. כל כלי מעשה, they brought these articles, not out of consideration of the value of the material, but with reference to the meaning of the use to which they were used. (see V.50).
V. 54. זכרון לבני ישראל לפני ה׳. (See on V.50).

V. 1. ומקנה רב. According to the accentuation the עצום מאד seems to refer to the בני גד so that their possession of flocks and herds was much greater than that of the Reubenites. In any case Ramban already remarks that the tribe of Reuben is only mentioned first here in the introduction as being the eldest, but in the whole talk in the assembly which follows, the sons of Gad are placed first. Also in Deut. 33,20 & 21, they are described as the real instigators of the idea and at the same time their bravery is mentioned with which the carrying out this idea of settling by themselves within special boundaries outside those of the general nation appealed to them.

V. 5. ויאמרו. This repeated restarting their speech implies a pause, and shows that they themselves were not without suspicion as to how their proposition would be received. They required a pause to pull themselves together to continue bringing their request forward.

V. 7. נוא .ולמה תניאון designates the interruption of a movement (it is between נוע and נוח—see Gen. V.30). Here it is used with its real meaning. They, and Israel, are engaged in the act of moving into the land. Then, all of a sudden they make a break in carrying on with this intention and bring the people too to giving it up. This double reproach is expressed by the קרי and the כתיב.

V. 11—12. מלאו אחרי ה׳ ,לא מלאו אחרי (see Ch. 14,24). The missing dagesh requires explanation. Perhaps in V.11 it designates the high degree of devotion to duty which they left unfulfilled. Not only not in פיעל, but even in קל could one say of them that מלאו אחרי. In contrast to that it then says of Joshua and Caleb also that מלאו אחרי. To be worthy to enter the land demands no higher degree of loyalty to duty.

V. 14. קמתם תחת אבותיכם. With your present request you step into the shoes of your fathers and continue their forgetfulness of duty. You show yourselves as תרבות אנשים חטאים, the breed of sinful men. (see Gen. 1,28).

V. 16. גדרת צאן נבנה למקננו וגו׳. Our sages in מ״ר say that the order in which they couch this suggestion shows us the trend of their thoughts and the overwhelming love of possessions which altogether lay at the root of their whole wish. Their herd were nearer to their hearts than their children, hence first גדרת צאן למקננו and then ערים לטפנו, otherwise they would indeed have thought twice, if only for their children’s sake, before endangering their spiritual connection with the nation and its Sanctuary by withdrawal on account of the attractive pasturage nature of the district. In Moses’s reply (V.24) he places the care for the children in the foreground and they took due notice of that. In their concluding words accordingly in V.26 they put the women and children before their animal stock. And, as the words of our sages go on to say, this placing too much value on material possessions did not do them any good in the long run. Just as they grasped at possession prematurely so they were the first to lose their possessions and homeland. They were the first to be exiled through Pul and Tiglath Pilezer (Chron. I. 5,26).
V. 17. אוץ ,עוץ ,חוש ,חשים, to push towards something, to hurry.

V. 22. והײתם נקײם מה׳ ומישראל (cf. Gen. 24,41). והײת נקי מאלתי אז תנקה מאלתי. You will be freed from the oath that you swore, you will be bound no longer and will have carried out all that you undertook to do. In the same way here: God and Israel will have no further demands on you.

V. 23. חטאתכם אשר תמצא, the consequences of sin fall on the sinner. Apart from the fact that they will not get the Transjordan territory if they fail to carry out the condition (V.30) they will also be guilty of the sin of breaking their words.

V. 24. לצנאכם not לצאנכם, similar to צנֶה in Ps. 8,8. Perhaps the word is drawn out to be able to linger over it, to stress thereby: “your sheep, on which you place such exaggerated value”. In any case the change of צאן to צנא and צנה would have the same sense of intensifying the conception of the word. צאן is related to שאן and designates something to be guarded, an animal to be penned (see Ex. 21,37); צנא and צנה related to צנע and צנח designates the still more intensive hiding away. (See on V.16).

This contract based on conditions made with the Gadites and Reubenites is the classic example in the Jewish theory of legal rights for the binding form of any act depending on conditions made. The demands to be proved are:- (a) תנאי כפול, both cases have to be expressly stated, as here it says: אם יעברו וגו׳ and also ואם לא יעברו וגו׳, and not be left to the simple self-understood alternative, מכלל הן אתה שומע לאו and the reverse; (b) תנאי קודם למעשה, the condition must precede the premise in the statement: אם יעברו ונתתם ואם לא יעברו ונאחזו, and not the reverse order תתנו אם יעברו. (According to רמב״ם Echious 6,4 this demand does not apply to the formula of the wording but to the act of carrying it out, that the condition is not made after the act has been done); (c) הן קודם ללאו that the positive case is placed before the negative one, first אם יעברו and then אם לא יעברו (d) תנאי בדבר אחד ומעשה בדבר אחר, the condition must not contain anything that if it is fulfilled does away with the clause to which it is attached e.g. אם תחזירי לי את הנײר הרי זה גיטיך; (e) אפשר לקיומיה על ידי שליח, the clause to which the condition refers must be able, if necessary, to be carried out by a representative, as here the division of the land was eventually done by Joshua, but not as, for instance the act of חליצה which can only be done personally (Kiddushin 61a, Gittin 75a & b and Kethuboth 74a). כל תנאי, it says in Kiddushin ibid. שאינו כתנאי בני גד ובני ראובן אינו תנאי “every form in which conditions are drawn up which do not conform to these demands makes the conditions unenforceable but the agreement remains binding, התנאי בטל והמעשה קײם. Whether this rule is applicable in all cases, and especially in which legal titles of possession and legal cases it is applicable is a matter of considerable controversy. In any case, there are cases where the conditions under which certain actions may be undertaken do not need formal expression if the intention for which it is to be done is declared and such intention implies it being done under certain conditions, גילוי מילתא, indeed cases where the conditions are so self-evidently clear and decisive, that it does not even require a declaration of the intention for which the action is to be done, דאפי׳ גילוי מלתא לא בעי (see תוספות קידושין 49b, ד״ה דברים שבלב).

V. 32. ואתנו אחזת נחלתנו. This probably means to say: Our taking possession of our inheritance on this side goes over the Jordan with us, i.e. we cannot really attain possession on this side, but with what we accomplish on the other side do we bring to realisation the taking possession of the land we desire on this side.

V. 33. ויתן להם משה וגו׳. The reason for and the causes which led to this participation of half the tribe of Menasseh in the Transjordan settlement is not given. Ramban assumes that when it came to apportion the country, the extent of the land proved too large for the two tribes and this brought about the addition of half the tribe of Menasseh. הארץ לעריה בגבלת, he directed them to the land and divided it amongst the tribes according to the cities in bordered-off districts. It was already decided which cities were to belong to the domain of Reuben, which to Gad, and which to the half tribe of Menasseh. ערי הארץ סביב, all cities were marked off as to where their province extended, even those which the present inhabitants could not use for residential purposes.
V. 34—36. ויבנו וגו׳ את דיבון וגו׳ ערי מבצר וגו׳. They built cities out into fortresses for their wives and children and into pens and sheds for their livestock.

V. 38. מוסבת שם. Nebo and Baal Meon — both names of gods — received altered names, ויקראו בשמות וגו׳, otherwise they kept the old names even for the cities they built out into fortresses. But according to Ramban, מוסבת שם means that the cities had received other names under the regime of Sichon; ויקראו וגו׳ but the Reubenites gave them back the old names they had originally when they belonged to Moab.

V. 41. חות יאיר. The etymology of חוה meaning village is not sure. It is believed to come from חײ with the י changed to ו, like הוה from היה, and then it would have the meaning, like חית פלשתים, a circle of people (cf. Gen. 18,10). Perhaps after all חוה is phonetically related to חפה ,חבא, to hide, cover up, and then חוה would designate the village as the protecting place, the houses of which are principally meant only for the protective accommodation of people, but not to be the places for their real activities, in contrast to the word for city, עיר, which organically encloses human society like a skin, עור, and is the home of its intellectual development and culture עור (awake I.L.) see Gen. Ch. 4,17. The other name for village כפר from כפר protective cover is clearly formed from the same trend of thought.

V. 42. לה ,ויקרא לה without mappick. On which מדרש רבות (on Ruth 2,14) remarks מלמד שלא עמד לה אותו השם that the suffix of the personal pronoun being written without a sound-making mappick is to indicate that the town and the district did not retain the name, so that Novack’s intention to immortalise himself thereby was not achieved. Does this perhaps express a slight reprehension of such procedure to found a memorial in bricks and stone to immortalise oneself, an earthly immortalisation which the true Jew should seek and find solely through the great deeds of spiritual and moral faithfulness to duty and through the whole content of a noble life?

V. 1—2. There could be various reasons for this summary of the moves and halts of the wandering through the wilderness. A whole list of events and experiences could have been connected with these journeys and resting-places in the wilderness the remembrance of which would have value for the families and relations and descendants of those to whom they occurred, but which found no place in these books of the general national population, but the verbal tradition of them would be incited for their remembrance by this summary. Further what footprints in the sands of time could these places still have for the immediate and distant future, and how much could the sons and grandchildren be invited thereby to trace and visit these places of the revelation of God’s miraculous guidance and care, and out of the history of the fathers, on the very spot of the revelation of it, bring to their own minds the speaking fact of the Presence of God on earth. Already the very sight of these barren and waterless deserts which are so great that even a caravan has carefully to reckon the days to provide itself with food and water, in which at least a million people lived for forty years, how much — as the רמב״ם remarks on Moreh — must this very sight alone prove the whole Godliness of the foundation of Jewish history. Rashi tells us of the remark of ר׳ משה הדרשן that of the forty-two moves recorded, fourteen fall between Rameses and Rithma before sending the spies, eight from Mount Hor to the wastes of Moab after the death of Aaron in the fortieth year, so that in the thirty-eight years of their fate of having to wander in the wilderness there were only twenty moves. So that the gentle love of God by no means made the verdict He pronounced be a continuous restless wandering about, as the average period for each resting place was nearly two years.

ויכתב משה את מוצאיהם למסעיהם על פי ה׳ אלה מסעיהם למוצאיהם, the change in this wording and conception of their journey is certainly not without significance. According to the way God takes it, they were מוצאיהם למסעיהם, to them they were מסעיהם למוצאיהם. Journey and halt were always made at God’s command (Ch. 9,17 et seq.). When God made them break camp, the purpose was always to reach a fresh goal for which God’s educational ruling considered the new halting place the most suitable. Each מסע (setting out again I.L.) was a progress, was the purpose of the מוצא (the breaking up of the camp), so that in reality all their “breaking ups” were מוצאיהם למסעיהם. But to the people it was the reverse. Wherever they stayed they were dissatisfied. When it came to breaking up the camp, that was what they wanted, that was their purpose. At the moment it did not matter where they were going to next, they were going on only to get away from where they had been stopping, for them למוצאיהם were מסעיהם. (We have already pointed out elsewhere how their natural impatience at having to stop and stay for some time is expressed in the Torah in Ch. 9,19 et seq. I.L.).

V. 3—4. ממחרת הפסח, not in the night. In the night the redemption was brought about by the death of the firstborn (Ex. 12,29). But the exodus took place in broad daylight. ביד רמה לעיני כל מצרים (Berachoth 9a). — ומצרים מקברים. This contrast belongs essentially to the thought which the redemption from Egypt is to be kept for all time as a fundamental idea for us. The rays of the morning sun showed the hordes of the slaves raised to freedom and the master race downcast and bewailing the loss of their most precious and dearest treasured firstborn, showed the one and same Hand of God punishing and delivering at the same time. Both together, the fear of deserved judgment and the confidence of deserved help filling the human breast is to be for ever the fundamental trait of Jewish consciousness of God, as that came to be expressed even more strongly at the banks of the Reed Sea: וירא ישראל וגו׳ ויראו העם את ה׳ ויאמינו בה׳ וגו׳. That is why this moment of the exodus is also mentioned in its full characteristics here in the list of journeys and halts of the Jewish wanderings, as indeed it also forms the foundation-forming cardinal point in the קדש of the תפלין out of which every Jewish man daily has to achieve afresh the sanctification of his “thinking, willing and doing.”

באלהיהם עשה ה׳ שפטים, just as the whole event proved the futility, the nullity of the supposed gods as opposed to the reality and dependability of the One Unique One, so did they and their emblems lie, dead and in ruins next to that which the Egyptians had lost in the death of their dearest ones.

V. 7. וישב וגו׳. This transference to the singular person whereas everything before and afterwards is related in the plural, requires explanation. Possibly it wants to show the unanimous confidence in God with which “it”, the whole nation as one man, undertook this move backward which certainly must have been most striking.
V. 9. ובאילם שתים עשרה וגו׳, such a place in which to encamp they did not find again in their whole journey through the wilderness.

V. 14. ולא היה שם מים וגו׳. From there the real terror of the waterless desert started and the never failing well of water which flowed down to them from Horeb accompanied them from here henceforth through the wilderness.
V. 40. וישמע וגו׳. This was the first enemy encounter with one of the nations of the land to be conquered.
V. 49. מבית הישימות עד אבל השטים, according to Yoma 75a, a stretch of 3 פרסאות = 12 מיל, hence the measure of 12 מיל for the תחום, according to the opinion that תחומין are דאוריתא (see on Ex. 16,29).

V. 51. דבר וגו׳. Already in Ex. 34,12 et seq., after the re-establishment of the bond with God which had been broken by the sin of the Golden Calf, in view of the unfortunately only too successful leading astray by the foreign elements present among the people, the warning had been given not to tolerate the polytheistic inhabitants of the land nor their polytheistic monuments to exist in their midst at their future settling in the land (refer to it there). Here, at the border within sight of the land, and before the exact borders of it are given, the land which is to be dedicated to the realisation of the Torah, this warning is repeated as the first fundamental condition. Yea, when it says in Josh. 4,10: הכהנים נשאי הארון עמדים בתוך הירדן עד תם כל הדבר אשר צוה ה׳ את יהושע לדבר אל העם ככל אשר צוה משה את יהושע “that the priests with the Ark of the Covenant stood still in the middle of the Jordan until Joshuah had finished telling the people all that God, through Moses, had commanded him to say to the people”, the Gemora in Sota, 34a, takes it to refer to the warning which here is attached to the crossing of the Jordan. In the Jordan, at the critical moment between being drowned in the floods of the Jordan and the happy safe passage through it into the land, the warning was repeated, on the attention to which the whole stability, the whole continuance of the possession of the land depended.

V. 52. ירש .והורשתם — phonetically related to גרש, to drive away, from which we get further תירוש, the juice pressed out of the fruit — in the Kal has the meaning of taking possession in the place of somebody else and can refer either to the previous possessor whose property it was, to inherit a property or to the property which is inherited: thus in Gen. 15,3 & 8, במה אדע כי אירשנה ,בן ביתי יורש אותי. In the Hiphil it designates such a change of possession forcibly brought about and can refer either to the possessor or to the possession: here והורשתם את יושבי הארץ and in V.53 והורשתם את הארץ, to drive the inhabitants out of the land, and to bring the land out of the possession of the previous possessors of it.

משכיתם, this plural shows quite definitely that the root must be סכה and not סכת as we mentioned as a possibility on Levit. 26,1. Here it does not say אבני משכיתם but משכיתם and this indeed includes all material representations which are designed to excite thoughts of gratitude; we have accordingly translated it “symbols” as being the word which corresponds most nearly to the concept. So also משכיות לבב (Ps. 73,7). The phonetically related roots שגע ,שגח ,שגה ,שכה all designate an intensive trend of thought to something (see Gen. 8,1).

ואת כל צלמי מסכתם (see Levit. 19,4). משכיות are most likely the public means of spreading the polytheistic views on general life; צלמי מסכתם, the plastic representations of their gods; במות the altars for offerings to the gods of the Nature cult.

V. 53. והורשתם את הארץ (see on V.52). You must first make the land fit to be your ירושה by the removal of all traces of polytheism, only then can you settle down in it. As long as polytheistic inhabitants and polytheistic memorials are there your ישיבה is no ישיבה (see Ex. 32,12 et seq.) כי לכם נתתי וגו׳, not by means of your own prowess and might do you have the land, it is God’s Will and God’s Might for which you have to thank your possession of the land. And also at the division of the land (v.54) it is not just your own arrangements, but God’s direction and God’s decision you have to follow. Hence you cannot dispense with the first preliminary condition under which God hands the land over to you.

V. 54. והתנחלתם וגו׳ (see on Ch. 26,52-56). בגורל, in a manner indicated by the אורים ותומים (see ibid.). But inasmuch as the division of the land is to be made by a lot confirmed by God, just thereby the task is given to first render the land fit and prepared for those who are now to take it into possession by the removal of its inhabitants and their polytheistic memorials.

V. 55. שוך .לשכים בעיניכם and שכך clearly related to סכך and סוג, means a defense by thorns, a hedge of thorns. Thus הנני שך את דרכך בסירים (Hosea 2,8), הסר משוכתו והיה לבער (Is. 5,8), משוכת חדק (Prov. 15,19). The meaning is accordingly to be taken:- the polytheistic inhabitants whom you leave in your land will become like a fence round about their polytheistic obnoxious practices, so that these escape your attention and insight into their nature and your condemning judgment. By your tolerance towards the polytheistic inhabitants amongst you, you become tolerant to polytheism (cf. Ex. 34,15 and 16). But by such authorised concession to the toleration of polytheism in the land of God, you forfeit the integrity of your own attachment to God, and with it, the justification for, and the protection of, your existence in the land. And once you have forfeited the protection of God, those whom you tolerantly allowed in your land become your oppressors and enemies in your own land. The whole book of Judges is nothing but the history of the result of disregarding this warning.

V. 56. והיה וגו׳. Finally you will become so unworthy of the land of God that He will drive you out of the land as His intention had been to let the nations be driven out by you. דַמֵה ,דמיתי: both to recognise and express the similarity of something which is in existence to something else, and also, as here, to form an idea of something which is still to come into existence, to intend.

V. 2. ארץ כנען לגבלתיה. An exact definition of the borders of the land is also of importance for the מצות התלויות בארץ as תרומות מעשרות ושביעית, as originally they only come into force within these borders. Only after the complete conquest of the land as its extent is here definitely described could other conquered territory participate in the קדושת הארץ and the duties incumbent thereby. Which is why the provinces conquered by David, ארם צובה and דמשק (Sam. II. 8,5 & 6), under the collective name of סוריא are recognised as having קדושת הארץ only מדרבנן. The conquest of the real land of the Torah had not yet been completed, even Jerusalem itself was not completely in Jewish hands. So that the conquest of Syria was not considered at all as a national undertaking and by the designation of כבוש יחיד was excluded from the legal קדושה-character. It is not even decided how far the Transjordan land of the two and a half tribes was included in the real קדושת הארץ. (Avoda Zara 21a, תוספות there, and Gittin 8b — תוספות Chagiga 3b, ד״ה עמון ומואב —. See further on Deut. 30,5).
V. 3. פאת נגב, the most southern point of the east.

V. 4. ונסב וגו׳ ועבר וגו׳ ויצא וגו׳. The translation of this geographical fixation of the borders of the Holy Land must waive claim to exactness, as the descriptive expressions in the Hebrew cannot be decided with topographical exactitude, because fixing the places which form the starting-points of these border-lines rests on suppositions which are by no means sure.

V. 6. הים הגדול וגבול: according to Gittin 8a, the Mediterranian Sea and an archipelago, הנסין שבים, which was included within the borders of Palestine. From the mountains of Ammon, the הר ההר of V.7, the north-western point of the border, a line is to be drawn cutting through the ים הגדול from north to south until נחל מצרים the extreme south-western point (V.5). All that lies to the east of this line belongs to ארץ ישראל, all beyond it to the west, to חוצה לארץ.

V. 7. תתאו לכם, the form תְּתָאוּ would be the Piel of a root תאה. תאה designates the direction from one point to another. It is related to תעה to be in constant movement from one point to another, to stray about. Possibly also to דאה, the to and fro hovering of the eagle before it shoots down to a certain point. הר ההר, not to be confused with the mountain of a similar name in the south-east on which Aaron died. Whereas this one lay in the exteme north-west of the land.

V. 10. והתאויתם לכם, from אוה. Like התאוה, as e.g. in ולא תתאוה בית רעך (Deut. V.21), means striving to extend the amount of one’s possessions, to draw an object within the sphere of one’s property, so here it is quite pertinently used for drawing a line to publish how far our property, here the land, extends, and that all within it is ours. If perhaps at this point, in accordance with the lie of the land, the border made a curve outward, the term would be significant to a yet higher degree (cf. קוה and קו).

V. 17. אשר ינחלו לכם. Under the supervision and guidance of Eleazar and Joshuah as the representatives of the nation, the prince of every tribe is “to take into possession” on behalf of his tribe, the portion of land allocated to it, and make the sub-division amongst the families and men of his tribe who are entitled thereto. As these princes are appointed here as such, to be representatives of the respective tribe, families and individuals they have full authority to act for all claims of heritage, and their decisions are legally and finally binding (Rashi). In the Gemora, Kidushin 42a, it bases the law on this:- that the courts are to appoint guardians for orphans to see to their rights of inheritance etc.; and such decisions of duly appointed guardians are binding and legally incontestable after the orphans grow up and come of age. מנין ליתומים שבאו לחלק בנכסי אביהם שבית דין מעמידין להם אפוטרופוס לחוב ולזכות תלמוד לומר נשיא אחד נשיא אחד ממטה תקחו.

V. 19—28. ואלה שמות האנשים. The order in which here the tribes and their representative are mentioned concerning the division of the land corresponds in a remarkable manner exactly to the position in the land, reckoning from south to north which the tribes received for settlement in the land next to each other. Judah, Simeon and Benjamin had the south; Dan, Menasseh, and between them Ephraim occupied the centre; Issachar, Zebulun, Asher and Naphtali, the north. If, later on, the allocation of the respective territories of the tribes was made by lot and received Divine confirmation through the אורים ותומים (see Ch. 26,55), still its predestined decision and the order of the arrangements is already given in these verses. — All the tribes are called — מטה בני here at the arrangements for the division of the land למטה בני דן ,למטה בני שמעון etc., only of Judah and Benjamin it says למטה בנימן ,למטה יהודה. Perhaps the following idea might be the underlying reason:- מטה בני looks on the tribe as the higher unit to which the individual בני- subordinate themselves. But Judah and Benjamin, on whose territory the National Sanctuary was to be erected, are, just on that account, to be regarded not merely as the higher unit of those that belong to the tribe, but only to be thought of as themselves belonging to the national community, as “branch” of the national whole, hence, not מטה בני בנימן ,מטה בני יהודה but מטה בנימן ,מטה יהודה. Perhaps another peculiarity might also be explained similarly. The representative of all the other tribes are presented by their honourable title נשיא, only not at the tribes of Judah, Benjamin and Simeon. When we consider that the territory of Judah and Benjamin is to be thought of as the nearest periphery of the Sanctuary of God which is to be erected on its soil, and that the realm of Simeon really only formed an enclave of Judah, it might appear to be suggested that, at the thought of the sovereignty of God and His Torah which that Sanctuary represents, no other is to be thought of in the commanding demeanour of “Prince”.

V. 2. ומגרש לערים. (See Levit. 25,24). סביבבתיהם. As עיר is feminine, סביבתיהם can only refer to לוים. The environs, the “green belt” is added to the towns, so that the Levites are to have not only cities, but also the surrounds as their property.

V. 3. ומגרשיהם .והיו וגו׳, of the Levites. ולכל חיתם, according to Nedarim 81a, for all purposes necessary for caring for health, e.g. for wash-houses, etc. Thus it says in Is. 57,10: חית ידך “the power of your hand to provide the means of living”. According to the Gemora, in Makkoth XII,a no graves were allowed to be made in any of the Levite domains: לכל חיתם לחײם נתנו ולא לקבורה (except for a רוצח שוגג who died there).

V. 4. מקיר העיר וחוצה אלף אמה, the thousand cubits did not begin at the actual wall of the city, but only וחוצה, from the outskirts of the town which belong to it תן חוצה ואחר כך מדוד (Eruvin 57). This is the “seventy cubits and a bit” שבעים אמה ושירײם beyond the city which is always reckoned as added to it עיבורו של עיר, so that the two thousand cubits of the תחום שבת also only start from these seventy cubits outside the city (ibid.). These “seventy cubits and a bit” is the length of the diagonal of a rectangle of five thousand square cubits which corresponds to the area of the hundred cubit length by fifty cubits breadth of the surround (חצר) of the Sanctuary (the משכן).

V. 5. ומדתם וגו׳. In V.4 the מגרש of the city was only given one thousand cubits. Beyond this מגרש, a further thousand was added which had to be kept “green” for fields and vineyards (see on Levit. 25,34). Altogether then two thousand cubits were measured in every direction and this whole space outside the city was broadly referred to as מגרש.

V. 6. ואת הערים וגו׳ את שש ערי המקלט וגו׳. This double accusative construction probably wants to say that the six cities designated in the first instance as ערי מקלט (V.13) were at the same time to be handed over to the Levites. But primarily they are to remain ערי מקלט so that the accidental manslaughterer who takes refuge there has to pay no rates or taxes to the Levites for his stay (Makkoth 13a). According to Rabbi (ibid.) they even have to provide rent-free housing for such manslaughterers. ועליהם תתנו וגו׳. Apart from these six ערי מקלט a further forty two cities were given to the Levites. By this term עליהם these forty-two cities are appointed in a secondary degree to have also ערי מקלט qualities. But they are primarily to be Levite-cities. From that two differences arise between them and the six real מקלט-cities. Firstly if an unintentional murderer takes up his residence in one of these Levite-cities, he has to pay rates and taxes etc., and further these cities only afford him protection if he remains there for the express purpose of protective asylum, whereas the six real מקלט-cities grant protection automatically if he just happens to be in one of them, more, even if he did not know at all that it was a city of refuge. (Makkoth 13a and 10a).

V. 10. כי אתם עוברים וגו׳. The land of the Divine Torah is there for the people who live in it. Its most valuable product, the purpose and goal of the whole of God’s Blessing directed to it, is every human life nourished by it, through its means able to dedicate itself to making God’s Torah into a realisation. The land is only given on the condition of every human life being respected as being unassailably sacred to the Torah. One drop of innocent blood shed and no notice taken of it drops a stitch in the bond which connects the land with the nation and both with God. (see verses 33 and 34). This holding human life to be so sacred is to be made evident immediately on taking possession of the land in the division of it by instituting the arrangement which the Torah had already referred to in the fundamental laws of Torah social life (Ex. 21,13).

V. 11. והקריתם לכם וגו׳. You shall arrange cities for yourself in such a manner that, without having to be looked for, they offer themselves, by themselves to those that are fleeing. (see on Gen. 24,12).

This והקריתם לכם is more precisely defined in Deut. 19,3, by תכין לך הדרך ושלשת את גבול ארצך וגו׳ the roads leading to these cities are always to be kept in good condition without any obstacles, according to Makkoth 10a, provided with signposts and situated at equal distances from each other. The three Transjordan cities not only lay quite parallel to those on this side — Hebron in Judah, Betzer in the wilderness; Schechem in the mountains of Ephraim, Ramoth in Gilead; Kadesh in the mountains of Naphtali, Golan in Bashan (Deut. 4,43)—but from the southern border till Hebron was exactly the same distance as from Hebron to Schechem and from Hebron to Schechem the same as from Schechem to Kadesh, and from Schechem to Kadesh exactly the same distance as from Kadesh to the northern border. So that from both borders to the first city was exactly as far as from that city to the next.

So that three equal distances are given, the distance from the borders and the distance from the first city to the second, and from the second to the third. Or to put it differently, the whole country was divided into four equal parts by fixing three equidistant points in the land. The text calls this act of dividing into equal parts שִׁלֵשׁ. In the language of our חז״ל, dividing a given quantity of any kind into several equal parts is termed שלש, e.g. משלשין בממון ואין משלשין במכות (Makkoth 5a — but nevertheless see Rashi there on p.3, a).

ערי מקלט. In the תנ״ך the word קלט only occurs as מקלט in this connection and in שרוע וקלוט where it means club-footed, where the hoof is undivided, grown together. In the language of our חז״ל the word קלט occurs for a foreign material being received and absorbed to form a permanent junction e.g. with dyes and in connection with a twig for grafting (Sab. 17b & Sheviith 2,6), although it also occurs for a temporary reception: קלוטה כמי שהונחה דמיא (Sab. 4a). Phonetically it seems related to גלד from which we get גלד, the skin (Job 16,15) the organic casing enclosing the body, hence in Rabbinic Hebrew גלדאי, a tanner. The contracting, rigid-making frost is also called גליד. From all this, קלט in מקלט seems to mean a permanent reception. Perhaps the phonetically related ילד designates being set in the world as the permanent surrounding in which the new-born baby is henceforth to be received, and consigning the unintentional murderer to a מקלט-city is similarly a second confining birth; the מקלט-city is henceforth the whole world to the one who is relegated to it.

Hence also, in the following verse: :לכם ,והיו לכם הערים למקלט לכל צרכיכם (Makkoth 13a). The city which receives him, shall in fact be the small world of the one who is banished to it. He is to find all his requirements provided for there: ינוס אל אחת הערים האלה וחי it says in Deut. 19,5 עביר ליה מידי דתהוי ליה חיותא, see to it that he finds a “life” there. The place itself should be of medium size, according to מל״מ הל׳ רוצח VIII,8, not enclosed by a wall, provided with water and food markets. At settling the ordinary inhabitants of the town one has to see to it that all the national classes, כהנים לוים וישראלים are settled there, yea, even for the special spiritual and intellectual requirements of the particular individual means have to be provided so that the teacher of a student of science who has been sent there, must follow him there to enable him to complete his studies, and in the reverse case the pupils must follow the teacher (ibid. 10a). So that in fact a מקלט-city must form a complete world on a small scale.

מכה נפש בשגגה. The conception שגגה for unpremeditated, unintentional manslaughter has already been precisely established. To fall under the protection and obligation of having to take refuge in an עיר מקלט the fatal event must be as far removed from מזיד as from אונס, from gross carelessness as from completely unforseeable accident. Only such a killing demands flight to an עיר מקלט where the occurrence, although as a rule not to be expected, still the possibility of happening should have crossed the mind and careful precautions might have prevented the accident, some element of slight carelessness must have been present. מכלל דהוי :בשגגה ליה ידיעה (Baba Kama 26b). The repeated expression בשגגה excludes the case where the presence of the object which is dangerous to life was unknown to the perpetrator of the deed, e.g. היתה אבן מונחת לו בחיקו ולא הכיר בה ועמד ונפלה.

V. 12. מגאל (see Ex. 6,6). Here, גואל is the one who takes up the cudgels for the man who has been killed, and sees to it that avengement for the deed done is brought home to the prepetrator of it. But this גואל is so little to be taken as the so-called “avenger of the blood”, a kind of vendetta, that the court appoints a גואל if there is no relation available, (Sanhederin 45b). אם אין לו גואל ב״ד מעמידין לו גואל (according to Rashi there ד״ה גואל הדם this was done even in cases of הורג בשוגג, but Rambam in סה״מ in connection with מ״ע סי׳ י״ג opposes this opinion and explains the sentence quoted from the Gemora to refer only to הורג במזיד).

ולא ימות הרצח. By the fact that in every case where somebody kills a person he can take refuge in one of these cities, precaution is taken to prevent any person being killed before he has been brought to court and the court decided whether it is a case for capital punishment, or for being banished to a מקלט-city for protection against the גואל הדם, or for being declared completely innocent and set completely free. So the Mishna teaches in Makkoth 9a, on verse 24 and 25:- בתחלה אחד שוגג ואחד מזיד מקדימין לערי מקלט וב״ד שולחין ומביאין אותו משם מי שנתחײב מיתה בב׳׳ד הרגוהו ושלא נתחײב מיתה פטרוהו מי שנתחײב גלות מחזירין אותו למקומו שנא׳ והשיבו אותו העדה אל עיר מקלטו. In Makkoth 12a, it is taught from our verse that the formal course is to be followed in every case, even where the guilt is perfectly certain, as e.g. if the murder had been committed deliberately in the presence of the court itself the criminal had to be sent, in the first instance, to a מקלט-city from where a different court had to have him brought before it, and the case gone into. The court in whose presence the murder had been committed were not allowed to judge him, מנין לסנהדרין שראו אחד שהרג את הנפש שאין ממיתין אותו עד שיעמוד בב״ד אחר ת״ל עד עמדו לפני העדה למשפט עד שיעמוד בב״ד אחר, the legal procedure must be undertaken by other judges who were not present when the act took place. Those who were present could only function as witnesses and not as judges, because, as it taught in Rosh Hashono 26 with reference to our verses 24 & 25 (refer to it there) at capital cases, בדיני נפשות no עד הרואה נעשה דײן, “no one who was witness of the deed can act as judge in the case, because it is the business of the court, in Jewish jurisprudence, to find every possible means of declaring the accused innocent (and leaving it to the judgment of God to inflict punishment if guilty I.L.), and כיון דחזיוהו דקטל נפשא לא מצי חזו ליה זכותא, the impression of actually seeing the murder committed does not allow us to assume that he will be able to have sufficient impartiality to win him over to any slight mitigating circumstances which would justify a verdict of “not guilty”.
העדה is the court as representative of the community entrusted by God with carrying out His justice.

V. 13. והערים וגו׳ שש ערי מקלט תהײנה. The three Transjordan cities which Moses had already appointed to be cities of refuge also did not come into force until the other three in the land had been also appointed. The institution of מקלט must come into force simultaneously in the whole Jewish domain. (Makkoth 9b). תהײנה לכם (see V.11).
V. 14. ערי מקלט תהײנה, at them the מקלט purpose is in the foreground, whereas at the other Levite cities their מקלט character is only secondary (see V.6).

V. 16. ואם בכלי ברזל etc. From verses 16-21 first follow laws on the ways and means by which an intentional murderer qualifies for legal reprisal. Apart from the proof of the subjective nature of the act as testified by עדים והתראה, witnesses present at the time who gave due warning to the criminal of the illegality of his projected crime and of the full nature of the legal penalty incurred by it, (Ch. 15,33), other objective conditions come into consideration as to the nature of the means used which caused the death and the circumstances under which the fatal deed was accomplished. It had to be ascertained whether the resulting death occurred in such circumstances that, according to human estimation, it could not be judged as other than the direct effect of the act of the accused. The size, material, nature and state of the weapon, the amount of force exercised, the place which was threatened by the dangerous accident which then actually occured, the physical condition of the victim etc., all have to be taken into consideration by the court, and all these considerations are indicated in the text. The various materials are mentioned עץ ,אבן ,ברזל; at אבן and עץ the word יד is added: כלי עץ יד ,אבן יד i.e. the ability to be manipulated, a stone that can be manipulated, a wooden instrument that can be manipulated, and this implies both the weight and size being sufficient as well as considering the amount of force which must have been necessary to use in setting the article in motion. At ברזל this addion is missing because, according to Sanhedrin 76b with an iron or steel weapon, however small it may be, a fatal wound can be inflicted. (see תוספות there); That is also why the words אשר ימות בו are added at weapons of stone or wood; the means and the blow must be of such a nature that they could have caused death, that the resulting death can be referred back to them, and finally it says everywhere הכהו וימות, in expert opinion death was caused as a direct result of the blow; then the accused is a רוצח, a “murderer”, and מות יומת הרוצח, his death is to be brought about by human hands.

V. 19. גואל הדם וגו׳ בפגעו בו וגו׳. Two things seem to be said by this sentence. If the court had found the murderer guilty in accordance with the three preceding sentences, then in the first place it is up to the גואל הדם to carry out the sentence, yea, as already remarked on V.12, if no relative is there as the גואל the court has to appoint a גואל הדם to carry out the sentence. But further בפגעו בו, if the court neglects to carry out the sentence, or if the criminal escapes, the גואל הדם is authorised, wherever he meets him, even inside an עיר מקלט to carry out the death sentence.

V. 20—21. ואם בשנאה וגו׳. In the cases discussed in verses 16-18, where the deed was done by an instrument, the details which qualify the act to be treated as murder rather than manslaughter are more easily ascertained with preciseness. That is why they are given first. To that now the verses: אם בשנאה etc., או באיבה etc., are attached to tell us that also at all other ways of killing the same factors of the amount of force employed, the means used and the result obtained have to be investigated to decide whether the death occured as the direct effect of the deed (see Sanhedrin 76a et seq.). ואם וגו׳ יהדפנו או השליך עליו. It makes no difference whether the person was pushed or thrown at the fatal medium or that was thrown at him.
צדה .בצדיה (see Ex. 21,13).

V. 22. ואם בפתע (see Ch. 6,9). פרט לקרן זוית (Makkoth 16b). At the moment of the occurrence the victim of the fatal accident must have been going in such a direction that the perpetrator was overtaken and surprised by the encounter בפתע, through thoughtlessness. But if, e.g. he was going from west to east with his face turned towards the east, and was passing by a side street corner or an inward bend of the road at the moment in which the victim was proceeding with his face turned to the north, so that though he could see the perpetrator, the latter could not see him, then the perpetrator of the act is an אנוס, it was a pure accident without any element of carelessness or thoughtlessness, and he is free from having to be banished to a מקלט-city (see ריטב״א thereon).

V. 23. שיפול דרך נפילה :ויפל עליו, it has only to be treated as a case of carelessness involving banishment to a מקלט-city if the lethal object was directed downwards from him but not if it was directed by him upwards and flew downwards against his will. Equally so, if he, coming down a ladder fell on somebody standing below, but not if he fell while going up and killed somebody standing below on whom he fell. זה הכלל כל שבדרך ירידתו גולה ושלא בדרך ירידתו אינו גולה (Makkoth 7b).

V. 24—25. ושפטו העדה וגו׳ והצילו העדה וגו׳. We have remarked already on V.12 how the tendency to give a non-guilty verdict forms an essential quality of a Jewish criminal court. This can be seen already in its constitution. The highest court, the סנהדרי גדולה consisted of seventy-one members, the smaller criminal courts which had to be appointed in every larger city, of twenty-three members, and this number is referred back, in Sanhedrin 2a, to our verse here: והצילו העדה ,ושפטו העדה, within a criminal court there must be an עדה שופטת ועדה מצלת at every criminal case, i.e. there must be a possibility of “guilty” as well as “not guilty” being represented by an עדה, a board of ten men. That gives the minimum number of twenty, and so that a majority verdict can be returned, which in criminal cases, if the verdict is guilty must consist of at least two votes (see Ex. 23,2), hence the board must consist of at least twenty-three members. This tendency towards “non-guilty” is also stamped on the whole procedure of Jewish criminal jurisprudence. A court which returns a unanimous verdict of guilty — where no member can find any possible plea for mitigation — שראו כולן לחובה — has to let the accused go free (Sanhedrin 17a). A member of the court, who, during the process of a criminal trial, has expressed his opinion that the accused must be considered guilty, can, while the case is still being discussed, change to the other side, but cannot change from non-guilty to guilty after he has given his opinion. But of course at the actual voting for the verdict at the conclusion of the case, the גמר דין, he must vote in accordance with his final opinion (ibid. 32a — refer also to Ex. 23,7).
על המשפטים האלה, on the basis of these regulations decide whether the accused has to submit to capital punishment, to be banished to a מקלט-city, or to go completely free.

V. 25. והשיבו וגו׳ והצילו וגו׳. If he has been judged to be banished to a מקלט-city, then the court has to care for his safe return to it, and provide protective accompaniment for the journey thither. (Makkoth 10b). וישב בה עד מות וגו׳. Similarly also in V.28 עד מות הכהן הגדול and ואחרי מות הכהן הגדול ישוב by which the concept “כהן גדול״ is extended, regarding the releasing effect of his death, to every one who had been appointed to office by having been anointed, or when that was lacking, by only being invested with the high-priestly garments (Ex. 29,29 and Levit. 16,32), or one who had been appointed to act during the illness of a כהן גדול and then had to retire when the כ״ג had recovered (עבר ממשיחותו), in this relation they are all quite equal: אחד משוח בשמן המשחה ואחד המרובה בבגדים ואחד שעבר ממשיחותו (Makkoth 11a) (see ריטב״א thereon who indicates how it could be possible for all the three kinds of כה״ג to be there at the same time). The question whether במיתת כולן הוא חוזר או במיתת אחד מהן, whether if there are more than one כהן גדול there all equally recognised for this purpose, the death of one of them would allow the return from a מקלט-city, or whether only the death of all of them would be effective, is not quite decided there (ibid. b).

(The relationship of a כהן המשיח to one who was only מרובה בגדים in other respects, as well as that of כהן משמש to כהן שעבר is given in Horioth 11b as follows:- (Levit. 4,3) אין בין כהן המשוח בשמן המשחה למרובה בבגדים אלא פר הבא על כל המצות ועשירית האיפה (Levit. 16,3) ואין בין כהן המשמש לכהן שעבר אלא פר יום הכפורים זה וזה שוים בעבודת יום הכפורים ומצווים על הבתולה (Levit. 21,14) (ibid. 7) ואסורים על האלמנה (ibid. VI,13) ומחזירין הרוצח (ibid. X,11) ואינם מטמאין בקרוביהם ולא פורעים ולא פורמים).

But only the death of such a כה״ג has the effect of permitting a return who was in office at the time the verdict was given, גמר דין. It says אשר משח אתו בשמן הקדש “whom he, the accused, had participated in his anointment, i.e. if we understand it correctly, who had been anointed when he, the accused, still belonged to the national body in whose name every high priest is appointed, before he had been banished out of the national body by the judgment pronounced against him, שנמשח בימיו (Makkoth 11b). If he dies before the verdict is pronounced, and the judgment is declared before the appointment of a new one, he may not return home at the death of this second כה״ג. If the verdict is pronounced at a time when there is no כה״ג functioning, or if somebody kills a כה״ג, or if a כה״ג kills somebody by an accident (which entails banishment to a מקלט-city I.L.), there is no return at all from the banishment. (According to תוספות, Sanhedrin 18b, ד״ה אינו יוצא these last two cases, ההורג כה״ג או כה״ג שהרג this only applies if no other כה״ג has been appointed before sentence had been passed, so that in this respect there would be no difference between a כה״ג and anybody else. (Rambam says the same in הל׳ רוצח VII,10) — אשר נס שמה וישב בה. During the period of his banishment he may not leave his מקלט-city in any circumstances whatsoever or for any purpose however urgent, not even for the purpose of a Mitzva, not even in the highest interests of the community or the state, אינו יוצא לא לעדות מצוה ולא לעדות ממון ולא לעדות נפשות ואפילו ישראל צריכין לו. Also after his death he has to be buried there. More, even if he died at home, after sentence had been passed, his body was taken to the מקלט-city, the grave belongs to the “habitation” to which he had been directed to occupy, and only after the death of the כה״ג could his bones be brought home and reinterred in the grave of his home city, שם תהא דירתו שם תהא מיתתו שם תהא קבורתו (Makkoth 11b).

V. 26—27. ואם יצא וגו׳ ורצח וגו׳. In Makkoth 11b it says: כשם שהעיר קולטת כך תחומה קולט, that not only the city itself, but the whole neighbourhood of the city also afforded protection; that is also probably why it does not say: אם יצא וגו׳ את עיר מקלטו, ומצא אתו וגו׳ מחוץ לעיר מקלטו but את גבול עיר מקלטו. On the other hand in V.28 it says כי בעיר מקלטו ישב and not בגבול עיר מקלטו for his right of domicile is limited to the city itself and does not extend to its purlieus. (ibid. 12a).

ואם יצא יצא, only if he went beyond the confines of the town במזיד (intentionally I.L.) has the גואל הדם the right to kill him, אין לו דם, and also if anybody else were to do so it would not be punishable, רשות ביד גואל הדם וכל אדם אין חײבין עליו (Makkoth 11b, according to the general version). But if he went out בשוגג (unintentionally (I.L.) killing him would be punishable murder (ibid 12a). His going out בשוגג only necessitates his returning back into the city, שלא יהא סופו (צאתו מחוץ ;במזיד נהרג בשוגג גולה לתחום) חמור מתחלתו (הרציחה). (Ibid.).

V. 28. כי בעיר מקלטו ישב. Makkoth 12b teaches from this repeated limitation to living in the city which has once received him into its protection (מקלטו I.L.) that in the event of a second similar accident happening to him in his מקלט-city, he need not flee to another מקלט-city, but he is relegated to another quarter in the same city, משכונה לשכונה, and henceforth he is limited to that particular quarter of the city. בעיר מקלטו ישב עיר שקלטתו כבר (ibid.).

לארץ אחזתו הוא שב ואינו שב למה שהחזיקו אבותיו ,אל ארץ אחזתו i.e. לא היה חוזר לשררה שהיה בה, he does go back to his old homestead but not to the social position or honourable civic post he may have occupied before his banishment, even if such position had not been conferred on him for his own personal achievements but were family positions handed down. (Makkoth 13a, see Ex. 29,30 and Deut. 17,20; cf. Levit. 25,41). ריטב״א there on Makkoth remarks that this loss of positions and honours previously held is peculiar to the returned manslayer. All other lawbreakers, once they have paid the penalty imposed for their misdeeds and presumably bettered themselves, are not only qualified to resume their former honours and offices as well as to follow their fathers in office and honours, but are eligible to be elected to all new ones for which they may be qualified.

V. 29. סנהדרין נוהגת בארץ ובחוצה לארץ ,בכל מושבותיכם (Makkoth 7a). As long as the criminal courts are functioning in the land of Israel — and this is dependent on the highest court, the Sanhedrin, being in existence in the “stone hall”, the לשכת הגזית in the Temple (see Deut. 17,10), ועשית על פי הדבר אשר יגידו לך מן המקום ההוא אשר יבחר ה׳ מלמד שהמקום גורם (Avoda Zara 8b, תוספות) — for so long criminal courts are to function in the Jewish settlements outside Israel. The judges at such courts act as delegates of the Sanhedrin by virtue of authorisation conferred on them in the land, סמיכה.

V. 30. כל מכה נפש וגו׳ seems, as well as the following verses, to be rules for the court. It was given the duty, in verses 12, 24 and 25, of judging, if need be, of condemning and appointing the גואל הדם as being, in the first place, responsible for the carrying out of the sentence. Here it is now supplemented by stating that it is not on the mere declaration of the גואל הדם but לפי עדים, only after the deposition of two witnesses has been investigated and accepted that authorisation may be given to the גואל הדם to kill the murderer as a רוצח. The subject of ירצח is the גואל הדם of whom it has been speaking all the time hitherto, both as the one who is responsible for the death sentence on the murderer being carried out, as well as being authorised to kill the manslayer if he goes outside the boundaries of his מקלט-city (see the Sifri).

ועד אחד לא יענה בנפש למות. The demand for at least two witnesses for a capital sentence to be given, as well as altogether for a testimony to be considered legally as evidence of an act is given at length in Deut. 17,6 and XIX,15: על פי שנים עדים או שלשה עדים יומת המת לא יומת על פי עד אחד. לא יקום עד אחד באיש לכל עון ולכל חטאת בכל חטא אשר יחטא על פי שני עדים או על פי שלשה עדים יקום דבר. Hence Sanhedrin 34a, takes the לא יענה of our verse not to refer to the evidence of the witnesses but to the whole of the procedure and discussion which precedes the verdict, quite in the sense of לא יענה על רב וגו׳ in Ex. 23,2 (refer to it).

For there it says. אמר אחד מן העדים יש לי ללמד עליו זכות מנין שאין שומעין לו ת״ל עד אחד לא יענה מנין לאחד מן התלמידים שאמר יש לי ללמד עליו חובה מנין שאין שומעין לו ת״ל אחד לא יענה בנפש למות. There the rule is given: Beyond giving their testimony the witnesses are not to add one word in favour or against the accused which might influence the proceedings in either direction. The court may not accept from them any opinions even to the benefit of the accused. On the other hand students of law — and there were sixty-nine of them who attended every case in the court, who sat in three rows of twenty-three each, silently to listen and study the procedure, and out of their ranks, if occasion arose, the court supplemented its members (Sanhedrin 37a) — students of law, תלמידים, if one of these thought he had something to say which would act to the disadvantage of the accused, he was not listened to, but if he thought he had a point of law which would go to the advantage of the accused he was encouraged to give his opinion. In such a case he was admitted to the bench of the judges (the Sanhedrin) who were discussing the case. If his opinion was found to be correct he was raised permanently to the rank of judge. If it was found that his point could not be admitted, he still remained for that day on the bench amongst the judges (ibid. 40a and 42a). There, in Sanhedrin 34a (the quotation above) both these rules, the complete exclusion of witnesses from giving any opinion at all at the proceedings of a case, as well as the admission of a student to vent his opinion in favour of the accused, are put in connection with the actual words of our text. But the interpretation of the words of our text as the source of both these rules is extremely difficult. We believe that the real motive for excluding witnesses from giving any opinion on the case בין לזכות בין לחובה could be found in the reason which ריש לקיש gives, viz. משום דמיחזי כנוגע בעדותן, which would apply even more for a declaration לחובה. Any taking part in the proceedings by the witnesses could raise a suspicion of their complete impartiality, of the complete objectivity of their testimony. Even if they raised a word in favour of bringing in a verdict of non-guilty it might have the appearance of their being afraid of an הזמה (see Deut. 19,19) which would only be dangerous for them if the verdict was “guilty”. But — so it seems to us — to a still higher degree would a word on their part speaking in favour of a verdict of guilty cast suspicion on their whole testimony and place it under the appearance of being not so much purely objective presentation of the facts as of being motived by getting the accused duly punished. The reason brought forward by ריש לקיש for excluding witnesses from לזכות could accordingly in truth be the motive for their altogether non-participation in proceedings in general, and the attaching this excluding of witnesses from the discussions to our text be only a mnemotechnic אסמכתא, and our verse be taken not to be actually speaking of עדים but of תלמידים and their exclusion from being allowed to express an opinion לחובה.

In fact, as, in criminal cases, testimony can only be accepted from at least two witnesses, one single witness in criminal law is altogether no witness at all and he is not of the slightest more importance than any other individual. Only as a specialist — as the testimony of any other authority on the subject in question — is his declaration of any influence. Now here it says: Only the words of witnesses, which, in accordance with the laws of criminal jurisprudence, are two witnesses, and indeed only as giving testimony as evidence of the fact of having witnessed the deed, can be allowed to have any influence on passing sentence on an accused, yea, must form the sole basis for the judgment.
