Quite in accordance with this position, in Numb. 13,30, we also see only Caleb mentioned as entering the lists on Moses’s behalf, and, if there XIV, 6, Joshuah and Caleb tried to keep the excited masses back from rebelling against God, and to change their cowardice to devoted confidence, and as a result of the manly way in which they stood up were nearly stoned by the people, still in V. 24 only Caleb is thought of, who, by his faithfulness made himself worthy of obtaining possession of the Land, although finally, in V. 30, both are mentioned as being the sole male survivors of that generation. Here, in our chapter too, Joshuah’s proven faithfulness to the mission is not mentioned and his being allowed to enter the land is only referred to his position as Moses’s personal attendant and his appointment to become his successor.
גם בי התאנף: later, at the end of the forty years, at Kadesh (Numb. XXI).
בגללכם: through you (see Gen. Ch. 12,13).

העמד לפניך: Standing is the position ready for action, standing before somebody, ready for his commands, directions or messages. Thus Elijah and Elishah express their position in service of God as עמד לפני ה׳ (Kings I, XVII,1 and II, V,16). Thus also the position of the Levites in service of the public: עמד לפני העדה לשרתם (Numb. 16,9 et seq.).

V. 39. וטפכם, in any case טף is the earliest childhood, from טפף, the tottering, toddling walk (see Gen. 37,2). But is not so certain which age is meant to be designated by בניכם. One would take it to be boyhood if all those under twenty were not included amongst those who remained to enter the Land. Accordingly דעת טוב ורע would refer to mature moral judgment with which the full responsibility before God begins. Even Solomon still prayed for לב וגו׳ להבין בין טוב לרע (Kings I. 3,9). According to Kiddushin 30,a, the real successful influence of the paternal guidance is effective only in the years between sixteen and twenty, or eighteen and twenty-four! And according to a saying of our sages (מ״ר קרח) full responsibility for one’s actions before God is only reached with the twentieth year of life. That the full responsibility for this national sin only fell on those who as “men” were counted in the census of the nation, i.e. after the twentieth year has already been noted on Numb. 14,29.

V. 41. ותהינו. The root of הן is הנן hence הנך ,הנני etc. But the root of תהינו is הין or הון. But הון means fortune and moreover a rich fortune, and הין accordingly the biggest fluid measure. In Prov. 30,15 & 16 הון occurs as “enough”, or perhaps “more than enough” ארבע לא אמרו הון, אש לא אמרה הון. We believe accordingly that we can take ותהינו to mean:- Each one of you girded on his weapons and “took that to be sufficient” or “more than sufficient” for going up the mount. So that you went from criminal cowardice to criminal conceit. That which you doubted you would be able to accomplish with God, you then believed you could do without Him. You imagined your swords were more than sufficient to conquer the Land.
V. 44. ויכתו (siehe zu Bamidbar 14, 45).

V. 45. ולא שמע ה׳ בקולכם: He did not accede to your desire, as שמע בקול always, and also from God to man, is fulfilling what is asked for or desired. Thus in Numb. 21,4; Joshuah 10,14; Judges 13,9 etc. ולא האזין אליכם, did not listen to you at all, had no consideration for your weeping, to moderate the fate He feared for you. On Numb. 21,1-3 we surmised as רמב״ן does, that the realm of King Arad lay in Palestine and not in Transjordania. But nevertheless this was not the case, in accordance with the opinion that takes Arad to be identical with Sichon so that Arad’s territory would be in Transjordania then it would not be impossible that the Chorma mentioned there would be the same as the Chorma of our text here. Then after forty years they would have won the first victory over a Canaanite nation at the very same place where, forty years earlier they had suffered a degrading defeat, forsaken by God. It would then not be impossible that the ולא שמע ה׳ בקלכם of our verse would refer to the later וישמע ה׳ בקל ישראל (ibid 3) in the sense: “that time God did not listen to you as He did at the same place later.”

V. 46. כימים אשר ישבתם, a long time, as long as you had had to tarry at any one place. And it was at Kadesh, at the border of the wilderness from where they only had a short way to go into the Land, that they had to tarry at the same place at which they now found themselves again after forty, or more correctly thirty-eight years. This “staying quietly” at the very end of the wilderness was the bitterest and most impressive atonement for the sin which rested on them. According to סדר עולם (Ch.VIII) they had to pass no less than nineteen years there. And then, as is reported in the following verse, when they did break camp, they did not have to proceed forwards to enter the Land, but to turn back into the wilderness again, back in the way that led towards the Reed Sea.

V. 1. ונפן וגו׳. See on previous verse. ימים רבים, another nineteen years according to סדר עולם (ibid), י״ט שנה היו חוזרין מטורפין (for nineteen years they had to wander round on this backward journey away from the Land I.L.).
V. 3. צפונה, in the direction to the Land.

V. 4. וייראו מכם, they will not attack you, ונשמרתם מאד, but be very careful not to allow yourselves to take any liberties with them. Or rather, they fear that they may have to suffer a great deal at your hands; they imagine that you must be starved after your long wandering in the desert where you were deprived of everything, and now when for the the first time again come into inhabited regions you will greedily jump on everything. Contain yourselves, and show them just the opposite of what they fear.

V. 5. גרה .אל תתגרו בם, phonetically related to קרה קרא, to turn somebody or something into a different direction, or to turn yourself to a different direction (see Gen. 19,8), hence also ירה shooting arrows. גרה מדון (Prov. 15,18) to set feelings against each other, to stir up strife: התגרה ב to excite or upset oneself against somebody, to bring yourself into feelings of enmity against anybody. כי ירושה וגו׳. It says in general of all the nations: בהנחל עליון גוים (Deut. 32,8), that it is not without the Guidance of God that the various nations have found their place of settlement in the world. But of the descendants of Esau and Lot the races which came from the family of Abraham—it says quite specially: ירושה לעשו נתתי and similarly also of Moab and Ammon (Ch. 2,9 & 16). The remembrance of this, just at the time when Israel is to receive its Land from the Hands of God could be of far-reaching importance. It brings home to the Jewish nation that God’s Providence rules also beyond Jewish circles and looks after the history of other nations too; that Israel is to enter and take its place amongst the nations with God-fearing respect for the possessions of the other nations, and not look on itself as a conquering nation before whom henceforth no nation in the world could feel secure in undisturbed possession of its land; but that its acts of war and the renown won thereby was to be limited to taking possession of the one land which God has designed for them and promised to them from the very beginning of their historical existence. Thus also in Nazir 61a, it proves from this ירושה לעשו נתתי that the rights of inheritance, one of the most important factors of all social development, has God’s sanction also in the sphere of Noachim humanity.

V. 6. אכל תשברו, not more than the immediate requirements of the moment (see Gen. 41,56). וגם מים even water, which by its nature belongs more to free nature than to man’s intervention. (תכרו, see Gen. 49,5).

V. 7. כי וגו׳ בכל מעשה ידך, even in those things which you did not receive directly from God, like Manna and water, such as clothing etc. (cf. Ch. 8,4 שמלתך לא בלתה מעליך). ידע לכתך וגו׳. He paid attention to your wanderings in the wilderness and directed His protective care thereto. The descendants of Esau shall get an idea of God and His unlimited powers by their contact with this people who had been provided with everything by God during the whole of their forty years wandering through the wilderness and their consequent behaviour so contrary to all that had been expected and feared from them. Hence the admonition ונשמרתם מאד in V. 4.

V. 8. ונעבר וגו׳. Mosche hob aus dieser Berührung mit Esaus Söhnen nur das hervor, was für die zu weckende rechte Einsicht und Gesinnung bei der bevorstehenden Landesbesitznahme von Wichtigkeit war. Daher überging er die unbrüderliche Weigerung Edoms, den Durchzug zu gestatten (Bamidbar 20, 21).
V. 9. ואל תתגר בם מלחמה, and do not work yourself up to fight against them. כי לא אתן: see on V.5.

V. 10. האמים etc. Verses 10-12 are clearly not part of Moses’s speech at the time, which is continued in V.13. These are rather explanatory remarks which Moses inserted when he wrote his speech down. They were intended to raise the courage of the people for their impending fight against the gigantic inhabitants of the Land, by reminding the people that under God’s direction, equally gigantic nations had to give way before the sons of Lot and Esau, and these are now in undisturbed possession of their lands.

V. 11 Places like Ps. 88,11; Is. 26,14; Prov. 2,17 et alia allow no doubt as to the meaning of רפאים being the concept of dying, having passed away from living, and indeed it seems easy to deduce this meaning from its relation to רפה, weak, to be or become without strength. (For the meaning “to heal” see Gen. 48,1.) If now, on the other hand רפאים with equal certainty means the race of giants, and in a more general comprehensive term are called ענקים as here the Eimim and Moabites are reckoned as belonging to the רפאים, we think we are not completely in error if we think that רפאים, used as here, designates the giants as “the dying-out race”, as a race of the ancient world, which no longer exists at the present time, and which, at Moses’ time had only a few descendants surviving in the land of Canaan. Sam. II,XXI,16 and XVIII,22 speak of the dying race of the giants as הרפה, and that this is no noun but an adjective is proved by the distinguishing adjective אמים .”ה״ (see Ex. 15,16) the “feared ones”. Just as the ענקים, the remaining few giants are given that name from the impression their necks stretched up so high makes, so are the אמים so called from the impression they make on beholders.
V. 12. כאשר עשה וגו׳, as Israel had already done to the lands of Sichon and Og which God had given into their possession.
V. 13. עתה קומו is the continuation of V.9.

V. 14. אנשי המלחמה, those, who at the time when the spies were sent out were of military age, and accordingly should have proceeded to action in taking the Land into possession, which was what was then what was already intended to be done. But they, forgetting God’s promised support, were too timid to attempt the task.

V. 15 וגם יד ה׳. Most of them came to the end of their lives, died a natural death. Others had their end hastened by special visitations of God, המם ,להמם, really to disarrange, to throw into confusion, probably here designates the stunning effect of the suddeness of the fate that overtook them. Thus Haman had the intention להמם ולאבדם (Esther 9,24).

V. 16 & 17. ויהי וגו׳ וידבר וגו׳. the Gemora in Baba Bathra 121b, finds an indication in these verses of the fact that during the whole of the thirty-eight years the Word of God did not come to Moses in the same direct immediate manner in which it had done before God showed His prolonged displeasure with Israel after the sin of the spies. From that, at the beginning of the Mechilta and the Sifra, the remark is made that it was not out of consideration of the personalities of the prophets, but only בזכות ישראל, for the sake of the nation as a whole that God allowed His Word to come even to Moses; and therefore as long as the nation lay under the consequences of God’s dissatisfaction the mode and manner in which God’s speeches reached Moses was somewhat clouded. רשב״ם on Baba Bathra there, as well as Rashi on our verse, find this indicated by the fact that in Moses’s speeches hitherto God’s Word is always designated as ויאמר :אמירה ה׳ אלי (Ch. 1,42 and II,2 & 9) and only now, after תמו כל אנשי וגו׳ he says וידבר ה׳ אלי. The ק״א aptly remarks on ת״כ (ibid) that אמירה altogether only designates the “communication” itself, but gives no indication of the manner in which it was made, can possibly only refer to the contents, the thoughts but not necessarily the actual words, and can also designate an indirect communication. But דבור specially designates the articulated words of the mouth, the spoken word, so that the medium of the communication expressed by וידבר ה׳ אלי would be the Word of God spoken directly from God to Moses: ודבר ה׳ אל משה פנים אל פנים כאשר ידבר איש אל רעהו. That the way in which the Word of God comes to human beings varies is evident from Numb. 12,6-8.
V. 19. See on V.5.

V. 20. ארץ רפאים וגו׳. See on verses 10-12. Verses 20-23 are also explanatory remarks inserted by Moses when he wrote down the report of his speech to the people. Only in V.24 is the speech itself continued. זמזמים from זמם, the description of a mental activity which is mostly taken in a bad sense, to think of something bad. Hence זמזמים, tricky people, who use their immense strength in the service of their bad intentions (see on Gen. 11,6).
V. 25. ורגזו: see Gen. 12,5, וחלו see Ex. 15,14.
V. 27. בדרך בדרך, only on the highroad which is open to everybody. The same as what is called דרך המלך, the King’s highway, in Numb. 21,22.
V. 29 כאשר עשו לי וגו׳ refers only to the sale of food and drink, as the sons of Esau in fact did not allow them to pass through their territory.

V. 30. כי הקשה ה׳ אלהיך (see on Ex. 14,3 & 4). Here too, Sichon could have found cause for resistance, and courage to fight, from Israel’s behaviour towards Ammon and Moab, especially by their going round the Edomite territory through which would have been their shortest route to the Land. הקשה: to resistance, ואמץ את לבבו: to attack.

V. 31. ראה: his resistance is already the beginning of his downfall. החל רש לרשת את ארצו: begin your taking the possession of the Land by taking possession of his land. Begin your taking possession with the land of Sichon.

V. 34. מתים, root מתה from which we get מתי (see Gen. 5,4-28, on עיר מתים .(מתושלח, that which is transient in a city, the living mortal people in it. רמב״ן remarks that the inhabitants were Amorites (see V.24), and as such, came under the Divine ordinance: רק מערי העמים האלה וגו׳ לא תחיה כל נשמה (Ch. 20,16 & 17 refer to it). But that fate was only conditional to their refusal to come to terms of peace by giving up polytheism and undertaking to dutifully keep the general laws of humanity, the ז׳ מצות בני נח, (the seven Noachian Laws I.L.). Which was then also the reason why here too, the Amorite king Sichon had first been offered peace (V.26 et seq.).
V. 35. בזז seems to mean division of that which had become without masters, שלל, spoliation of property (see also Numb. 31,11 & 32).

V. 36. קריה from קרה (see Gen. 19,8 & XLII,4): a city laid out in accordance with a fixed plan, self-contained, all the parts of which are so closely united to each other that entry from outside is rendered difficult. שגבה (see Gen. on XXV.8, on שיבה, which it is suggested may not unlikely be related to שגב, to be strong, to reach a height which surpasses others. What שגבה is in Space שיב would be in time I.L.). שקף would also be related, hence משקוף the upper lintel, and השקיף to look down from a height.
V. 37. וכל אשר צוה וגו׳: See on Levit. 4,2.
V. 1. ונפן. Turning away from the Ammonite territorry. ויצא וגו׳, As he came out and attacked them, no envoys of peace were sent to him (רמב״ן).

V. 5. בצרות. See Gen. 11,6. פרז ,הפרזי related to ברז to penetrate to bore into, from which ברזל and in Rabbinic Hebrew ברזא, the bung, are derived, פרס to break, פרץ to break in, to break through, hence also to spread afar, to extend without limits and פרש to spread out. Now פרזי means the open country, either because it is easily penetrated or because the houses there are spread far apart, and in that it is the opposite to קריה where the houses are connected closely to one another.

V. 9. צידונים וגו׳ is again an explanatory interpolation, inserted by Moses in his written report. שניר is translated by Onkelos as טור תלגא the snow mountain, and Rashi points out the similarity between the word שניר and the German word “schnee”, snow.

V. 11. כי רק וגו׳. The population under Og’s rule who were conquered were Amorites and not Reforim. Only he was left over of the race of the רפאים who had fallen to the conquering sword of the Ammonites, and he subdued the whole region of Bashan and made it into his kingdom. Moses remarks that his bed is still kept in the Ammonite capital, Rabba, in remembrance of the race of giants who previously lived there. (רמב״ן).
V. 12. ירשנו ,ואת הארץ הזאת, we have already taken it completely into possession and completed our possession of it by dividing it up.

V. 14. חות יאיר (see Numb. 32,41). There a conquest is reported to have been made by Nobach (V.42) who similarly gave Kenath which he conquered, his name, Nobach, a name which nevertheless was not retained, as indicated there. Probably it is to that the עד היום הזה here refers. Jair’s nomenclature was respected by his contemporaries and so remained permanently.

V. 23. חנן .ואתחנן (see Gen. on VI,8). חנן, granting, conceding, חן to be worthy of concession, חַנֵן, only in Prov. 26,25, to seek concession. התחנן, to seek concession for himself, or to seek to make himself worthy of concession. The construing with אל points to the latter. It is a reflexive action on one’s own inner self in connection with God to make it worthy of His being kindly disposed to grant. Thus, also in Berachoth 30,b, the concept התחנן it taken for the task for one who is about to say his prayers, to gather himself together internally beforehand כדי שתתחונן דצתו עליו, so as to get his mind in the right mood. בעת ההיא, see on Numb. 27,12.

V. 24. אדני: “Thou Who hath found me worthy to be in Thy service, Who hath allowed me to be the instrument for the accomplishment of Thy Will on earth”. It is the name which, above all, occurs again and again in the mouths of the prophets to designate their relation to God. יקוק the שם הויה which is pronounced as אלקים is God’s Love showing itself as “Justice”. אדני (“my Master” I.L.) expresses the complete readiness for obedience, to do everything that God wishes, יקוק the complete conviction that also in judging and denying, God is still only solely the God of Love. By addressing Him by both names Moses declares beforehand how without discontent he will not complain if God’s decision finds it right to deny him his last and warmest wish. Hence perhaps the לאמר of the previous verse. He feels it necessary to put his heart-felt wish into words and submit it to God’s consideration.

אתה החלות, everything which Thou hast let me experience up to now is but the beginning of getting an insight in Thy greatness and unlimited power. גדלך: see on Numb. 14,17. God’s Greatness is the creative forming power educating mankind to His purposes. (ספרי פנחס) גדלך זו מדת טובך.

ידך החזקה, the power that overthrows all opposing forces. .אשר וגו׳ אשר belongs to אשר מי אל וגו׳ אשר יעשה כמעשך וכגבורתך :כמעשיך. We cannot take such a sentence of comparison to be really a question, it can only positively deny that there is any power on heaven or earth that could exercise His creative and unlimited forming powers. כמעשיך corresponds to ,גדלך כגבורתך to יד החזקה.

V. 25. אעברה נא. The meaning and importance of the Land transcends far above all the Greatness and Almighty Power of which Thou hast already given me some insight. For in it lies the purpose of all the ordinances of which Thou hast made me aware hitherto. Through the Land Thou intendest Thy גדלך וידך החזקה to be the educative means to bring about winning over the whole of mankind to establish Thy Kingdom on earth. Seeing this land would open for me a further insight in the greatness and might of Thy future rule of the world. את הארץ הטובה, as it must correspond so completely to its great destiny for the world. ההר הטוב וגו׳ is in opposition to הארץ הטובה Moses, seeing the Land in his mind’s eye summarises the importance of the Land topographically in the description ההר הטוב הזה ההר הטוב .והלבנון is the Mount of the Temple, הר ה׳, the הר בית ה׳ (Ezekiel 2,2 & 3), which, as the place of the Sanctuary of the Divine Torah is first to achieve the illumination and sanctification of the Jewish people and then in the future of the whole of mankind; והלבנון, and to which the whole of the rest of the land joins itself from south to north rising in Lebanon-terraces. The hill of Moriah, the Mount of Zion, the last height of Lebanon in the south is looked on as the root of the Lebanon range, one comes down to it from the summit of Lebanon in the north. It is therefore called ירכתי צפון “the line of direction of the north”, ירכתי לבנון “the line of direction of Lebanon (Ps. 48,3 and Kings II, XIX,23; see Ex. 26,22; Ps. 128,3 and Jer. 22,6: ראש הלבנון, the principal—in importance—or the beginning of Lebanon). In their pertinent instructive manner accordingly the sages in the Midrash take the snowy whiteness from which the range gets it name לבנון to have reference also to the moral meaning of “white” as the colour refining and purifying, and say, referring to Isaiah’s saying יהיו חטאיכם כשנים כשלג ילבינו (“Though your sins be as scarlet they will become white as snow” I.L.) that והלבנון זו בית המקדש, that, looking at it this way the whole Lebanon range has its name from the “place of purification” that was founded on its last southern elevation of the earth.

V. 26. התעבר ,ויתעבר וגו׳ really to pass out of oneself, to pass over the border of one’s own inner self, to take a stand against somebody with the whole of one’s personality, i.e. to speak quite decidedly against somebody: “then God turned angrily against me”. למענכם. By far predominantly, yea we believe exclusively, למען does not designate the reason, the cause but the purpose. On Numb. 20,12 we have ventured to point out the deep significance which the deaths of Moses and Aaron in the wilderness in the Transjordan territory, next to the graves of the generation which had to die out, had for the whole accreditation of his mission in the midst of his people for all time, and this למענכם here may very well refer to that national purpose. רב לך: “thou hast done thy part. What thou hadst to do on earth thou hast sufficiently accomplished, the limit of insight into the greatness and might of My Rule granted unto thee thou hast attained”.

V. 28. צוה .וצו וגו׳ is a specific term used for giving the duties to be undertaken by somebody who is being appointed to an office. וצו, charge him with the duties of his office (see on Numb. 27,19). וחזקהו, make him firm that he allows nothing to turn him aside from the path of his duty, ואמצהו; and make him strong to overcome all difficulties and obstructions.

V. 29. ונשב וגו׳. Clearly this petition of Moses and this order which he received are indentical with the report given in Numb. 27,12 et seq. But we learn from here that the petition which was refused preceded the ויאמר וגו׳ of V.12 there. But if here Moses specially mentions the place where he ventured to make this request to be granted the concession to cross over into the Land with the people, that could indicate the special reason which in the depth of his heart prompted this wish. It was, he reminds us, just opposite Beth-peor, the place which witnessed that last sin, and showed the moral weakness of his people who so easily yielded to enticement. Deep in Moses’s heart may the worry have lain how his people would stand the test when they came into still closer contact with the degenerate inhabitants of the land, and how much they required—and would have to do without—his support and his admonishing and warning words.

V. 1. ועתה ישראל, this “ועתה״ is the call to the people to draw the moral for the new future they were now stepping up to, out of all that Moses had stressed to them out of their past history. Out of all the experiences they had had, one fact emerges, viz, that “obedience to the Will of God” is the one sole and indispensable condition for the security and happiness of their future. Moses is departing from them but the laws which he brought over to them from God and taught them, they contain everything which they require for the happy building up of their future. So that to speak to the heart of the people on keeping these laws, on how to keep them, and the seriousness of keeping them, was the last desire of Moses before his death.

—שמע אל is constant listening to a Teaching not to satisfy ourselves with having known it once, but always to keep it clear and present in our mind, above all, the time when it is to be given practical application שמע אל החקים וגו׳ demands that no step be taken without first considering the Torah and what principles may be involved in it.

אל החקים ואל המשפטים. It cannot be pointed out too often, how, in all Moses’s admonishments חקים are placed in the foreground. First חקים, then משפטים. Just חקים, just those laws which fence in, restrict our personal physical sensual life, with which God has measured out the limits of our personal, physical, sensual living and willing, its “no more and no less”, they form the very first foundation for fulfilling our human and national mission on earth. They, the חקים, above all the עריות and מאכלות אסורות laws, first beget individuals, people of such nature and feelings inclined towards spiritual matters and morality from whom a national life can be built up based on the equity of the משפטים (see on Levit. 18,3-5).

אשר אנכי מלמד אתכם. Repeatedly Moses designates the agency by which he transmitted the Torah of God to the people as למוד, not as כתיבה. So that it was not the written but the spoken word, verbal teaching, תורה שבעל פה, which was the medium by which the Divine Torah was implanted in the people. And Moses did not use the term הוריתי אתכם ,מורה אתכם ,הורה, but למד. Whereas הורה, the Hiphil of הרה (see on Gen. 26,5), to lay a mental seed in someone, means, chiefly, furthering spiritual mental knowledge, למד, which also means to accustom (habituate) a person to a thing, to practise, (and in מלמד הבקר, Jud. 3,31, is used for the ox-goad used to keep the animal at ploughing, as well as למודין in Mishnah Kelim V. 9 for ropes or hoops to hold things together in their right place) goes far beyond the mere making something understandable and designates such teaching which has the practical application of the subject in view and gives the most comprehensive instruction and guidance for that. Moses’s teaching of the Torah was accordingly literally תלמוד and “Talmud” is Mosaic Law.

למען תחיו ובאתם וירשתם: free-willed obedience to the laws of God makes us “live”. Only by devoting all our activities, our whole existence and all our willing, to the guidance of the laws of God, and allowing them to form all our thinking and feelings speaking and doings does our “existing” (היה) deserve the name of “living” (חיה), truly living, the most complete realisation of what lies at the base of our existing, what our existing brings to light, the realisation of our seeking “the thought, the conception of God” (הגה). Then, and then only, when we come to the end and look back on our life can we say חיינו (we have lived! I.L.), the thoughts of God which should have been realised through us, we have realised! And just as free-willed obedience to the Torah is the one condition for our individual lives to make our existing into truly living, so is it also the sole condition for our national life to be constituted on our own land. שמע וגו׳ למען תחיו ובאתם וגו׳.
In a narrower sense תחיו is the result of אל החקים, and ובאתם etc. of שמע אל משפטים.

V. 2. לא תספו וגו׳. Every command which God gives us, we are to carry out in its integrity. We are to allow no possibility thereby of any arbitrary alteration, no subjective addition or curtailment which might appeal to us, e.g. no more or less than the prescribed four paragraphs in the Tephillin, four kinds of plants in the Lulav, four double threads in the Tzitzis (Sanhedrin 88,b), no more or less than the three prescribed sentences in the blessing pronounced by the priests, than the one, two or four prescribed placings of the blood of the offerings on the altar (Rosh Hashona 28,b). All these and similar commands are a Word of God, what God says to us. Any arbitrary addition or curtailment would be tampering with the Word of God, bringing what human opinion deems right into the Truth of eternal Thoughts of God, dragging Divine Instructions down to the level of human superficialities.

לשמר מצות ה׳ וגו׳, this conscientious keeping to “not more and not less” at fulfilling God’s commands is just to have the result of making these commands realised in their full complete integrity, unabridged and pure. But in this addition of the purpose, given in this verse we believe we can at once find a reminder that what is done out of conscientious care for the most possible exact carrying out of the command, and not out of unabashed attempts at reform, does not come under this prohibition of לא תספו, but it rather the result of the שמירה of the מצות which is here and so often enjoined to us. Thus, when doubt, ספק, begat the יום טוב שני של גליות. or as a result of a difference in tradition, the one prescribed תרועה is presented in two ways as שברים and תרועה (see פ״מ an א״ח XXXIV,2, ט״ז). Equally a repeated carrying out of a מצוה, e.g. תקיעות מיושב and תקיעות מעומד does not fall under this prohibition (תוספות ר״ה 28,b; see also חידושי רשב״א on ר״ה 16,a).

According to רמב״ם (הל׳ ממרים II,9), this prohibition brought the warning at the same time to the ecclesiastical authorities not to allow those ordinances, תקנות and גזרות, which they have to make in accordance with their duty ושמרתם את משמרתי to protect the keeping of the laws (see Levit. 18,30), to appear as an integral part of the Torah itself, not as דאוריתא, which would be הוספה, as “addition to the Divine Torah”, but to keep their דרבנן character distinctly and clearly as סייגים as prophylactic measures. This warning, our sages have observed with meticulous conscientiousness, and in all their traditions and explanations have kept very definitely the distinction between דאוריתא and דרבנן. This prohibition occurs again in Ch. 13,1 and indeed in the following version: את כל הדבר אשר אנכי מצוה אתכם אותו תשמרו לעשות לא תסף עליו ולא תגרע ממנו. It is not impossible that each of these places refers specially to one of the two kinds of “adding and subtracting”. Our verse here speaks in the plural:— לא תספו על הדבר וגו׳ ולא תגרעו ממנו, it imposes the duty on the ecclesiastical authorities not to add any new law as coming from God to the written or oral traditional laws of the Torah, nor to abrogate the Divine nature of any law which traditionally did come from God. The further verse in Ch. XIII which expresses the prohibition in the singular number לא תסף עליו ולא תגרע ממנו could, on the other hand, be directed to every single individual imposing the duty to fulfil every command in the Torah without making any addition to it or curtailment from it. This would find support from the wording of the text: את כל הדבר וגו׳ אתו תשמרו לעשות לא תסף עליו ולא תגרע ממנו. This “אתו״ could show that it is not so much the whole of the Lawgiving which is the object of this prohibition but it stresses that it is each separate command which is to remain protected to be fulfilled in untouched integrity.

V. 3. עיניכם הראות. This was an event experienced in what was then quite recent times. The Peor-sin occurred after the victory over Sichon and Og. So that it was quite fresh in the memory of the generation now preparing to enter the Land. But the immediate transition from לא תספו and תגרעו to the warning reference to the annihilation of the עובדי ע״ז (idol worshippers) seems highly didactic. It proclaims the fact that every denial of the inviolable Divinity of the Torah even regarding one single commandment, setting Man’s opinion as being equal to the statutes of God is equivalent to a general defection to polytheism. Thus Saul allowed his own nice interpretation, his own opinion and discretion to influence his carrying out a mission which had been entrusted to him by God. Instead of strictly fulfilling the command which lay clear and definite before him, he allowed himself to do both more and less than he had been commanded to do, “Less”, inasmuch as he omitted to execute the judgment of God with which he had been commissioned on Agag and a part of the spoil. “More”, inasmuch as he kept back the best part of the spoil for offerings to God, and thought that thereby he was able to do something even better than destroying it as God had commanded him to do. So that Saul had quite definitely transgressed the warning לא תוסיף ולא תגרע. Thereon the Word of God was sent to Saul through Samuel:— החפץ לה׳ בעלות וזבחים כשמע בקול ה׳ הנה שמע מזבח טוב להקשיב מחלב אילים כי חטאת קסם מרי ואון ותרפים הפצר. “Hath God delight in elevating-offerings and offerings of meals-of-peace as much as in obeying the voice of God? See, to obey is better than sacrifice, to pay attention more than the fat of rams; for disobedience is the sin of witchcraft, and pressing your own arbitrary powers forward the cult of idolatry and oracles.” מרי, disobedience, which leaves God’s commands unfulfilled because they—actually, or in your opinion—do not fit in with some other factor, is it at bottom no other sin than allowing sorcery to decide whether to do an act commanded or approved by God? And הפצר, that arrogance which thinks it can better God’s commands by carrying out one’s own ideas of what should be done, is that at bottom anything other than that polytheistic defection which does not place everything, one’s whole fate and one’s whole life under the One Only God, but places at His side some glorification of oneself—(that is און from און) and allows that to sway one’s fate, and oracles to decide one’s deeds. (cf. on Numb. 15,31).
בבעל פעור is probably description of the place, as Ch. 3,29: בית פעור and בעל צפון (Numb. 33,7).

אשר הלך אחרי בעל פעור, it is possible that this expression includes not only those who actually performed the rites of the Peor-cult, but also those who participated in any way in that great sin and showed themselves inclined to it. Then the warning against defection from any of the Divine commands would be only the greater.

V. 4. דבק ,ואתם הדבקים is the closest attachment to somone else, ודבק באשתו (Gen. 2,24), so that one is not conscious of the slightest feeling of aversion. עיניכם הראות it says in the previous verse, you yourselves had the experience. There is not one amongst you who does not know that he did not allow himself to be guilty of the slightest deviation to Peor, and on that account remained saved in the midst of the pestilence which carried off the guilty ones. Thereby every one of you has in himself the strongest proof of the value of obedience to God and the strongest admonition to immutable faithfulness. Every member of the nation had had this experience. Hence the plural ואתם וגו׳ ,עיניכם וגו׳. But the punishing destruction struck the guilty ones with consideration of the nation having unitedly to keep their godly mission, hence the singular מקרבך. The calling of Israel to be the People of God does not tolerate any apprentice of Peor in its midst.

V. 5. ראה, a further fact that you are to hold firmly as something that you have experienced for yourselves is that למדתי וגו׳ לעשות כן וגו׳ אשר אתם באים ,וגו׳ see, I have taught you laws and social regulations in accordance with God’s commands to me so that you can keep them in the land into which you are now moving. Thereby the fact is established for your calling and for the meaning of these laws, a fact which differentiates them and you from all else, viz:—you are the only nation in the world that had laws before it had a country. And these laws are the only ones which present themselves not as the means for a national existence and for establishing national independence and welfare out of a national land, but as the purpose of it. Every other nation became a nation through its land and then made laws for that land. But you became a nation through the Law (the Torah) and received a land for that Law. All other laws have arisen from the characteristic peculiarities of the inhabitants engendered by the land and from the requirements of its changing development. Your lawgiver—the man from whose hands you received your Law—had never even seen your land, never put a foot into it, he was only the transmitter of the Law, and his grave in the wilderness is God’s seal on the Law, as well as the hall-mark of its everlastingness and unchangeableness. The Law (the Torah) is absolute and independent, you and the Land are conditional. The Torah does not have to go in accordance with your changing fate and that of the Land, but in accordance with your changing faithfulness your fate and that of your land changes. With the Torah in your arms you stood as a nation at the border of the land on which you were to set your foot, there to bring the Torah to be completely fulfilled; with the Torah in your arms—in days to come when you will temporarily have lost the Land—will you stand again and again as a nation that has no other calling than to live to fulfil this Torah and to wait for the moment in which entry into the Land is again open to it, the Land that was given to it for this Torah to be fully and completely realised. You are the People of the Torah and Israel is the Land of the Torah, but you are not the People of Israel and Israel is not the Land of the Jews.

כאשר צוני ה׳ אלקי. With this “teaching” I was only fulfilling the duty imposed by God, in Whose service I breathe, Whom I call אלקי, through Whom I am what I am, and Who has the disposition of all that I am and can do. From that comes the great Jewish principle for all men who follow Moses as teachers of the Torah: מה אני בחנם אף אתם בחנם (Bechoroth 29,a) that teachers of the Torah may only do so as a duty for doing which no compensation of any kind may be taken. This applies to all that was learnt from Moses, the whole of the written and oral Torah which God revealed to him, and indeed to all such teaching whether it be mere theoretical knowledge or direct practical teaching. Hence also the sentence: הנוטל שכרו לדון דיניו בטלין להעיד עדותיו בטלין להזות ולקדש מימיו מי מערה אפרו אפר מקלה, “he who takes payment for judging a case or for giving witness, his verdict or his testimony is invalid; he who takes payment for sprinkling the “expiation-from-sin water” or for pouring in the ashes, the water is considered just as ordinary water taken from caves and the ashes as taken from the kitchen hearth” (ibid). And further it goes on to say there ומניין שאם לא מצא בחנם שילמד בשכר ת״ל אמת קנה ומניין שלא יאמר כשם שלמדתי בשכר כך אלמדנה בשכר ת״ל אמת קנה ואל תמכור “if you find nobody who will teach you Torah without payment, then buy your instruction with gold, for it says in Prov. XXIII “buy the Truth”. But do not then say: “as I had to pay for my learning, so will I take payment for teaching it”, for it says: “Buy the truth but do not sell it”. This duty of gratuitously teaching the Torah and gratuitously performing its commandments which is demanded does not preclude taking payment for other tasks associated therewith such as שכר שימור the office of the necessary looking after the pupils, or שכר בטילה דמוכח, payment for loss of other occupation which is clearly caused thereby, or for payment for the livelihood of those who give up other means and devote all their time to teaching the Torah or to the fulfilment of its practice. (see Nedarim 37, תוספות Bechoroth 29,a).

V. 6. ושמרתם ועשיתם, the first condition for keeping the duty of “guarding” the Torah is:—“learning”, as everywhere ושמרתם זו משנה (see on Levit. 18,4 & 5). As your whole existence and the whole of your calling, and your whole future is rooted in this Torah, you have nothing else to do but to study it and to keep it. כי היא, for it, the two together, the שמירה and עשיה, the study and the practice of the Torah, is your חכמה and your בינה in the eyes of the nations. חכמה, taking in the teachings of the Truth; ובינה at their application, using the intellectual art of the right deductions and conclusions (see on Ex. p. 470). Whatever arts and sciences may form the characteristic inheritance of the culture of other nations, yours, the Jewish science and art is the science and art of building up the whole of personal and national life on the fundamental basis of the consciousness of God and the duties to one’s fellowmen, is the science and art of the knowledge and practice of the Laws of God, the science and art of the Truth and harmony of Life.

לעיני העמים, this, your science and art of living will form your distinctive feature in the eyes of the world. That which the old seer prophesied יפת אלקים ליפת וישכן באהלי שם, “the arts of beauty appealing to the senses one must seek at other nations, but the art of building huts, cities, states in which God shows His bliss-bringing Presence will only be found at the sons of Shem “that will be verified by you. And if you will live, all of you, knowing and practicing the Divine Torah before the eyes of the world, your whole existence will be a propaganda for the establishment of the Kingdom of God on earth.

אשר ישמעון את כל החקים האלה. Not for naught is the whole complex of Jewish laws in the conception of the other nations called חקים. Taking them all together they are just the unchangeable given “measure” for all the conditions of our lives. Other nations seek incessantly for some measure of state wisdom which would fit conditions of life which are constantly, unceasingly changing. And because their legislatory efforts only spring from the short-sighted narrow thoughts of the human brain, only seeing the superficial nature of things, their rules are in a constant state of flux, and what to-day is proclaimed as the right and wise means for ensuring happiness and well being is buried tomorrow as pernicious folly. Only the Jewish nation has an everlasting measure for the duties of the whole of its internal and external private and public life, to which it can submit, with full confidence its personal and national life for all times, knowing that just by this submission to God’s Torah, it makes itself lord and master of its own fate. As its Torah, so is its history something given beforehand. This, a whole nation in all its generations devoting itself to the knowledge and practice of a Law gives the Jewish nation an imposing spiritual greatness in the eyes of the world. They get to know of all these rules which are responsible for the formation of the Jewish individual and national life, and acknowledge that this great nation is a national union filled with wisdom and insight. It is doubtful to what the limiting idea of the רק refers. Perhaps:— however peculiar the Jewish people seem, one has no choice but to recognise them as a גוי גדול and an עם חכם ונבון. Or, this גוי גדול has its greatness only therein and thereby that it is an עם חכם ונבון.

V. 7. and 8. כי מי גוי גדול אשר וגו׳ ומי גוי גדול אשר וגו׳. If this was meant to be the question, which nation can compare itself to Israel, it would hardly say מי גוי גדול but מי גוי אשר, or better אי זה גוי אשר. We believe we can see in מי גוי גדול a question, and in אשר לו וגו׳, the answer. It says just before, that the nations will call Israel a great nation. The reason for it follows here. The greatness of a nation is found in two factors:— in its internal prosperity, and in the wisdom of its foreign policy. In Israel both spring to the eyes of the world. For, it says, which is a great nation? The one who has its gods near to it, i.e. whose Deity grants it progress and prosperity protection and victory; just as, in truth, God, the One Unique One, to Whom we pay homage and obey, has looked after us in all circumstances in which we required Him. And further: which is a great nation? One that has just laws and social regulations; just as in truth, the teaching contains, that Moses placed before us from God for our acceptence. Just the fact that Israel accepted this Torah for everlasting faithful fulfilment constitutes its spiritual and moral greatness. Nevertheless the word אלקים is קדש and refers to God Himself, for as in truth it is only God who is near to Man, all the illusion of gods and their worshipped powers are far away from Man and his requirements, so in reality the sense of אלקים here does refer to God, and what it says is really: Which nation is great? One to whom God is near, as God, our God is near to us.

But indeed it is not without reason that the prosperity of the Jewish people, and the nearness of God which it shows, is named first. For it is it, above all, which draws the attention of the nations to it and gives them some inkling if the deep importance of the Jewish Torah-life, which, just in these successes in external matters is proof to them of God’s nearness.

V. 9. רק השמר וגו׳. In verses 3 and 5, עיניכם הרואות and ראה למדתי refer to two facts which were personally experienced:—to the judgement of God which was meted out to each individual regarding his faithfulness or unfaithfulness to the Law, and to the absolutely deciding power which this Law has on our future. But everything rests on the fundamental fact of God’s revelation of this Law which the whole nation itself witnessed, and the direct guarantee of the Divinity of the Torah and the supernatural Personality of God. It is therefore, in the very first place, this historical thoroughly fundamental fact, the revelation of the Lawgiving on Sinai, proven by the evidence of our own senses, which must always be kept vivid in our minds and in our hearts, and be handed down to our children, generation by generation to be taken to heart with equal certainty. Based on actual experience, an experience made simultaneously by a whole nation, is the unparallel unique foundation for the historical fact of the revelation on Sinai; and the universal tradition by a whole nation from parents to children is the equally unparalleled unique preservation of the fact for the fundamental thought in the consciousness of all succeeding generations.

Here there are three separate warning admonitions, השמר לך פן .תשכח וגו׳, שמר נפשך מאד פן תשכח וגו׳, השמר לך ושמר נפשך מאד פן יסורו וגו׳ שכח is not really forgetting because of failing memory but (phonetically related to שגע ,שגה ,שגח see on Gen. 8,1) primarily, forgetting through taking so many other things in your mind. The real meaning of שמר is keeping away everything that is detrimental to a thing. So that השמר is keeping oneself away from all influences which would act against any definite purpose. Hence it is generally construed with the addition: לכם ,לך, literally guard yourself, i.e. keep yourself afar from anything that could endanger your own calling of being faithful to your duty. The other nations study Nature and their history without these two facts being firmly and convincingly establishel by actual experience, the existence of a supernatural One personal God, and the Law of Morality proclaimed by Him. “At every of thy considerations of Nature and at all thy study and estimation of the meaning of thy history art thou to keep in mind the underlying basis of both being in the facts which were proved to thee by thine own experience”. They are the most actual facts of all the facts of Nature and History. Keep thine own independence in the midst of a world whose outlook on the world and its opinions have grown from a deficient basis. Through the false deductions and opinions they have built up from their incomplete defective basis you run the danger of forgetting just the actual experience of those facts on whose basis alone the truths of existence and life are won. Therefore take care that you do not forget the facts which your own eyes witnessed.

But above all שמר נפשך מאד וגו׳. That un-Jewish consideration of the course of Nature and History has only too easily a dangerous advocate who speaks for it in your own inner breast. With the disappearance of God out of Nature, the way of nature enters the life of Man, his passions and natural urges tend to become worshipped as ruling powers, and with the denial of God’s Law governing history the throne of self-seeking, violent sovereignity of Man is set up. Both flatter only too easily your נפש, your inner sensual and mental being and desires, promise to free your senses from having to submit to the demands for sanctity, and your life in history from those of justice and brotherly love which the Law on Sinai brought you from your God. Therefore just as you must guard against un-Jewish influences from outside, so, above all, guard your own inner self against the flattering suggestions of sensuality and selfishness, that it does not become placed beyond the reach of the facts that vouch for God and His Torah, take care above all, that your inner self does not allow itself to forget the facts which your own eyes saw!

ופן יסורו מלבבך כל ימי חייך, and, as you are to keep them constantly in mind, so let them,—and this is the end the whole matter has in view—, not just at certain times of life, on certain sacred days or hours, but כל ימי חייך, as long as you live, at every breath you take let them govern your heart, that centre from which emanate all the thoughts and desires that lead to action, and not for one minute allow them to be absent.

והודעתם לבניך ולבני בניך, and that which you have come to know, and which through your own practical experience has become the unshakable granitic basis of all your thoughts and actions, you shall make that become the “knowledge”, not the “belief” of your children and grandchildren. You shall hand it down to them with all the full conviction and certainty that your personal experience has given you, that what you have lived through becomes the basis of the thoughts and knowledge of all your descendants. After all, the authenticity of even written historical records rests at rock botom on the uncontested tradition of all fathers to all sons. Hence the saying in Kiddushin 30,a, “he who teaches his son Torah, Scripture considers him as if he had taught not only him, but his son, and that son’s son until the end of all generations,” for it says והודעתם לבניך and thereby at once לבני בניך. Or, according to the opinion accepted there in the Gemora, that here the command is given not only to teach Torah to one’s children but also to grandchildren, the other saying כל המלמד את בן בנו תורה מעלה עליו הכתוב כאלו קיבלה מהר סיני שנאמר והודעתם לבניך. There can be some doubt who is the subject of the verb “קיבלה״, the grandfather who hands it down, or the grandson who receives it. The מהרש״א in ח״א on Berachoth 21, wavers between the two.

If it refers to the grandson, it clearly says what we worked out above:—that what was received by the first generation is to be kept as closely and handed down so faithfully that this tradition completely takes the place of what had been personally experienced, and makes the very last grandson in dutybound to keep the Torah faithfully as if he had indeed received it himself at Sinai.

If it refers to the father and grandfather it would be a demand that they hand it down with such clarity and perfect conviction as if they themselves had received the Torah at Sinai. Perhaps there is also the idea behind it that when someone teaches Torah to his children, and then becomes conscious with what faithfulness and conscientiousness he had to transmit to his children what he received from his own father, he only then properly realises the authenticity with which the Torah lives right back to Sinai. He says to himself that the conscientiousness and faithfulness with which he is now passing the tradition down to his son, his father exercised towards him, and his grandfather to his father and so back to the first ones who stood at Sinai. The chain of tradition leads every link that passes it down, by its own faithfulness to the tradition, directly back to Sinai, and, handing it down it first feels that it itself did receive it at Sinai.

It remains somewhat striking that the Gemora should attach this consideration to teaching a grandson and not take it already to teaching a son. (Actually the Yalkut hereon has the version הלומד את בנו תורה. He also has the version כאילו קיבלה, so that quite clearly the receiving son is the subject. In Berachoth 21,b, it also only says בנו). If one refers our כאילו קיבלה to the children who receive the tradition, then attaching the consideration to the grandson could have the further underlying thought:—If the grandson hears the same teaching from the mouth of his grandfather which his father has already taught him, then the tradition of the Torah is presented to him in its most living truthfulness. He sees that his father has only taught him what he himself had received from his father, and so the conclusion lies to hand that altogether the fathers back to Moses have only handed down what they had received from their fathers, and the mouth of his father and grandfather becomes for him as the mouth of Moses.

(The warning given in the verse against forgetting the fact of the revelation on Sinai is extended in Menachoth 29,b, to apply in general to the knowledge of the Torah. It says there:—He who forgets one word of what he has been taught of the Torah transgresses a Divine prohibition: כל המשכח דבר אחד מתלמודו עובר בלאו שנאמר השמר לך ושמור נפשך מאד פן תשכח את הדברים, for כל מקום שנאמר השמר פן ואל אינו אלא לא תעשה, for the terms פן ,השמר and אל are everywhere equivalent to a direct prohibition. But, it adds, יכול אפילו מחמת אונס, ת״ל ופן יסורו מלבבך במסירם מלבו הכתוב מדבר not if the forgetting occurs through unavoidable weakness of memory, for in the ופן יסורו מלבבך it assumes that he was guilty of causing the forgetfulness. This latter probably lies in the השמר וגו׳ ,ושמור וגו׳ פן וגו׳. Out of indifference to the Torah, one gives oneself up to so many other thoughts that they drive the knowledge of the Torah which one has learnt out of one’s mind).

V. 10. יום אשר וגו׳ is the object of the whole preceding verse: the day on which you stood before your God, on which God, your God personally came to meet you and you stood before Him “at His disposition”. עמד לפני always means that (see Numb. 3,6).

אשר ילמדון וגו׳ does not refer to the preceding דברי, for they were predominantly laws which were to be realised by deeds, so that it would probably then have run אשר ילמדון לעשות. But אשר ילמדון ליראה is rather the reason for the ואשמעם וגו׳ ,הקהל וגו׳, the whole nation is to receive the Words of God directly from Him so that they learn to fear Him as long as they live on earth, and teach their children to do likewise. This purpose of the direct revelation of God at His Lawgiving is expressed in similar terms in Ex. 20,17, כי וגו׳ בא האלקים ובעבור תהיה יראתו על פניכם לבלתי תחטאו.

But this fear of God, the Jewish fear of God, is no product of unclear vague feelings and moods or frame of mind; the fear of God has to be “taught and learnt”. Repeatedly the Word of God speaks of למוד היראה, here ילמדון ליראה אתי. Equally so in Ch. 14,23 תלמד ליראה את ה׳ אלקיך and in Ch. 17,19 למען ילמד ליראה, and in Ch. 31,13 ילמדו ליראה. The fear of God is acquired by learning and practicing; the fear of God is a mental, a spiritual knowledge and a moral ability, as indeed both together comprise the full conception of למד. The first lesson in this Jewish mental and moral art was given to us by God Himself. All what follows is a description of this lesson. Without showing Himself to us, He let us hear His Words, we heard but did not see Him. So that we became aware of Him in His Invisibility by His Word, and it was words of His Torah to us by which we entered into the everlasting alliance with Him. This constant awareness of God the Invisible One, in His Words, in the words which reveal His Will, this constant hearing God is the meaning of fearing God, is the meaning of ירא ,יראה את ה׳ related to קרא, to call God to be present in our mind, our soul. Hence His Word, the word of His Law, His Torah became His “name”, i.e. that whereby He became present to us, by which we have to think of Him, Whom we have never seen but indeed heard and there where the Word of His Torah abides, there does “His Name rest”. ואכלת לפני ה׳ אלקיך במקום אשר יבחר לשכן שמו שם וגו׳ למען תלמד ליראה את ה׳ אלקיך כל הימים (Ch. 14,23; refer to it there).

כל הימים אשר הם חיים על האדמה “as long as they are on the earth”, surrounded by the whole material earthly visibility of things are they to see the Invisible One above all this visibility. The One of Whom they had become aware in the midst of this visible material world so that He remains present to them and, in the midst of it, they walk in His Presence and listen to His Voice from Horeb.

V. 11. ותקרבון וגו׳. It is not easy to fix the exact meaning of ערפל. It occurs most frequently, as here, in association with ענן. In Job. 38,9, the Might of God is pictured as holding back the sea with doors and bolts, making cloud its cloak and ערפל its swaddling-binder. As there “cloud” is called its “cloak”, and ערפל its “swathing-band”— בשומי ענן לבושו וערפל חתלתו—(see Ezekiel 16,4 and XXX,21), ערפל seems to be the “bandage” pressing the waters still more closely and tightly together. In ענן the particles of water are still spread as vapour. In ערפל they are already thickened. In many places ערפל has the character of darkness, being impervious to light הבעד ערפל ישפט (Job. 22,13). החשך יכסה ארץ וערפל לאמים (Is. 60,2) וקויתם לאור ושמה לצלמות ושית לערפל (Jer. 13,6). So that ערפל seems to mean the dark low-hanging raincloud in which the water vapour has nearly condensed to drops. Possibly that would explain the derivation of ערפל from ערף, which in ערף, nape, back of the neck, has the meaning of a loosely connected division—(the violent יערף מזבחתם in Hosea 10,2, is probably transcribed from the killing from the back of the neck in Ex. 13,13 and Deut. 21,4)—and can very well describe this state of formation of drops, with which the term יערף כמטר לקחי (Deut. 32,2) and particularly אף שמיו יערפו טל (ibid. XXXIII,9) would agree.

What it says here would be that all round about was enclosed in deep darkness and only the place from which God wishes His Word to be directed to Israel was lit up by fire. Thereby all attention was riveted to that spot, and what was heard by the ear was immediately referred back to the One from Whom the Words emanated. (cf. on Ex. 20,15).

V. 12. וידבר וגו׳. You became aware not only that God spoke but that He spoke אליכם, to you, that His Words were directed to you out of the fire, and moreover it was not some mental awareness, דברים but actual קול דברים אתם שטעים, you heard the sound of the words with your ears, but that was the extent to which your perception was limited, no suggestion no outline of any form did you see (see on Ex. 20,4).

V. 13. ויגד וגו׳. We believe that עשה is never used referring to a ברית. So that אשר probably does not refer to בריתו but is the object of לעשות:- that, which He makes you in duty bound to do, and is the explanatory sentence referring to, and in apposition with בריתו. The Torah, which He makes incumbent on us, is His ברית, is the absolute condition for His connection with us, and this bond, namely, that which He makes it our duty to fulfil, He presents to us in ten sentences. These עשרת הדברים are not everything which He commands us, but they are הגדת בריתו a proclamation, a notification of the covenant, they give an idea of what He demands as His covenant with us, they contain the fundamental principles of the whole Law of the Covenant. ויכתבם וגו׳, and as His spoken word was the means by which He made every one of us aware of Himself and His Presence and His direct relationship to each one of us, so did He give into our hands the everlasting evidence of the revelation of these words by perpetuating them in stone, cut therein in His own writing.
V. 14. ואתי צוה וגו׳, the complete carrying out of these principles, the הקים and משפטים in which they are to be brought into realisation, that, He sent to you through me.

לעשתכם אתם בארץ, similar to לעשות כן בקרב הארץ above in V.5. In תקון סופרים of רש״ד a remark of the א״ת is recorded which points out the significance of the cantillation by which לעשות כן and לעשתכם אתם are first made to be the conclusion of the thought of the sentence and then בקרב הארץ and בארץ allowed to appear just as a special addition afterwards. Then what is said would be:- the duty of carrying out the Torah is an absolute one, given for all times and all places. Primarily, of course, and for its complete happiness-giving realisation the Land is fixed for us as our own national country to carry out our mission in the world as the People of God’s Law.

V. 15. השמר לנפש .ונשמרתם מאד לנפשתיכם does not occur anywhere else at all (with the one exception in quite a similar connection in Joshua 23,11; see below), it always says השמר לך ,לכם. If, as we explained above on V.9, השמרו לכם makes the demand to keep oneself (accusative) away from every estranging influence, and thereby for oneself (dative) i.e. to keep one’s real calling to be faithful to the Torah, then ונשמרתם לנפשתיכם would demand “keep, guard your souls for yourselves”, i.e. do not let yourselves be withdrawn by anything from the guiding and deciding influence of your true spiritual self (your נפש I.L.). When we consider that, according to all that follows, here it is a matter of not allowing ourselves to be robbed of the clarity of our conception and the certainty of our conviction of the supernatural, invisible yet absolutely real and personal existence of God, by any intrusion of any idea of substantiality, then referring this consciousness of ours to the forum of our souls, and the command to keep a strong guard over ourselves not to allow anything to estrange us from this forum, appears as highly significant. Besides God, there is only one other being of whose individual reality and personal existence, although invisible and unable to be realised by any of our physical senses, each one of us bears within himself the direct certainty of conviction, and that is our soul, our נפש. It is that, therefore, which reflecting back on oneself makes one comprehend the real existence of something which is invisible and intangible, and by the certainty of the conviction of one’s own self comprehend the conviction of the existence of God. As sure as we are of the existence of our own self so are we of the existence of God. Therefore “it is our soul that we lift up to God, therefore does our soul long for, thirsteth, languisheth for God”, אליך ה׳ נפשי אשא ,כלתה ,צמאה ,נפשי לאלקים (Ps. 84,3 and XLII,3 et seq). Therefore “doth our soul seek God in the night”, נפשי איויתיך בלילה (Is. 26,9), therefore “doth our soul cling to following God”. דבקה נפשי אחריך (Ps. LXIII). Therefore do our souls bless God. (Ps. 103,1, 2 and 22; CIV, 1 and 36) (a “blessing” of God by man means giving up his completely free powers of action to do solely that which will please and give satisfaction to God as explained on Ex. 18,11, and Gen. 14,19. I.L.). Thus our sages in Berachoth 10,a, ask: הני חמשה ברכי נפשי כנגד מי אמרן דוד, with reference to what relationship did David make this five times repeated exhortation to his soul to express its vow of dedication to God? And they give the answer: לא אמרן אלא כנגד הקב״ה וכנגד נשמה, with reference to the similarity between God and the soul. Just as God fills the whole world, so does the soul fill the body; as God sees but is not seen, so is the soul; as God nourishes the whole world so does the soul nourish the whole body; as God is pure, so is the soul pure; as God thrones hidden in the universe and cannot be found, so is the soul hidden and not to be found within the body. Thus the soul in its fivefold similarity to God may truly “bless” God, Who is so similar to it in five ways מה הקב״ה מלא כל העולם אף הנשמה מלאה את כל הגוף מה הקב״ה רואה ואינו נראה אף הנשמה רואה ואינו נראית מה הקב״ה זן (גרסת הילקוט דן) את כל העולם כלו אף הנשמה זנה (גרסת הילקוט דנה) את כל הגוף מה הקב״ה טהור אף הנשמה טהורה מה הקב״ה יושב בחדרי חדרים אף נשמה ישבת בחדרי חדרים יבא מי שיש בו חמשה דברים הללו וישבח למי שיש בו חמשה דברים הללו (see ח״א מהרש״א).

In מדרש תהלים (see ילקוט on Ps. CIII) this parallel is carried still further:- the soul bears the body as God bears the world; the soul outlives the body, as God outlives His world; the soul is one and alone in the body as God is One and Alone in His world; the soul neither eats nor drinks, so does God; the soul is the highest in the body as God is the Highest in His world; the place of the soul cannot be found in the body, so too the place of the Glory of God הנפש סובלת הגוף והקב״ה סובל את עולמו, הנפש יחידה בגוף והקב״ה יחיד בעולמו, הנפש מבלה את הגוף והקב״ה מבלה את עולמו, הנפש אינה אוכלת ושותה והקב״ה אינו אוכל ושותה, הנפש למעלה בגוף והקב״ה למעלה בעולמו, הנפש אינו ידוע מקומו והקב״ה ברוך כבוד ה׳ ממקומו.

ונשמרתם מאד לנפשתיכם accordingly in this connection means: Guard yourselves, keep, above all, the influence the knowledge of your soul exercises, for it comprehends that what cannot be grasped by your senses has a more real existence than what can be grasped by your senses so that God may remain for you, just in His insubstantiality the most real actual existing Being.

Similarly in Josh. 23,11 ונשמרתם מאד לנפשתיכם לאהבה את ה׳ אלקיכם, the true Jewish soul wanders naturally by itself to its God and its complete loving devotion to God is the highest bliss. Take care that you retain this influence of your souls upon yourselves, and above all guard yourselves against anything that would tear you away from this pure trait of your souls כי אם תשובו זדבקתם ביתר הגוים וגו׳.

V. 16. פן תשחיתון is the continuation of the thought started with ונשמרתם, and כי לא ראיתם וגו׳ is in parenthesis. Let yourselves be guided by your souls—for your souls, not your senses, saw God on Horeb, your senses only heard—so that you do not fall into the corrupting idea of making for yourself some material representation of God. As remarked on Gen. 6,11, שחת really designates a pit, the sinking down, falling away from the direction which leads to spiritual and moral well-being and happiness. It does not designate just single sins, just instances of departing from the right path where the possibility remains of finding the way back again as one has remained still on the same level, but a sinking in general principle, taking up a totally different and lower standpoint out of which no way leads out to goodness and truth. It is defection from spiritual and moral truth. Hence, as our sages remark, it is the specific term used for falling into polytheistic or immoral corruption, ע״ז and ג״ע, which as a rule go hand in hand and each one tends to beget the other.

ועשיתם לכם וגו׳. In connection with the preceding כי לא ראיתם וגו׳ the warning here is not defection to another god, but against our setting up some material form to represent the God Who revealed Himself to us on Sinai. Any such representation would drag God down into the sphere of all other material existences of which one can form an idea of some likeness and would be a denial of the conception of God as the One immaterial, supernatural, free-willed Unique Being. Hence, first of all the most general prohibition of any moulded representation. פסל (related to פצל to remove the skin, to peel, from which we get בצל, a bulb of skins, the onion) is a plastic likeness hewn or carved (also probably cast,—Is. 40,18). תמונה is, as already remarked, applied already to the general outline which would show the form of the species it was meant to represent but the individual itself need not be recognizable. סמל, a word which seldom occurs seems by its relationship to שמלה to designate the general conception of “form”, the “dress” of the body. פסל תמונת כל סמל would accordingly forbid without exception any plastic representation of any form whatsoever even if it is not a likeness of anything in existence but entirely a composition of the imagination.—תבנית. As בנה only occurs referring to the formation of an architectural building or of an organic living formation (Gen. 2,22) תבנית also designates only the model of a building or of an organic living creature and its parts. תבנית ,תבנית יד משכן וכליו (Ezek. 8,3). So here, for the representation of human or animal creatures. But as the term תבנית—really the picture of the structure—is used for the representation, it says thereby that this representation is not intended for beauty in itself, for aesthetic purposes, but is meant to represent the object in the meaning of the parts depicted. תבנית זכר או נקבה is the representation of a human figure.

V. 19 ופן תשא. Verses 16-18 forbad representing God by any likeness whatsoever. Now here follows the prohibition of the cult of star-worship, the deification of the heavenly bodies whose real and imagined influence on earthly matters probably was the most prominent source of idolatry. The view of the whole of the heaven, which as שמים the “double-there”, encircles the earth on all sides, and in it the sun (its very name in Hebrew שמש designates it as subservient, as the first “servitor”; “verger” in the dome of God’s world) and the moon and the stars, the whole great world of the heavens which in spite of the tremendous variety of size, brilliancy, distances and courses still presents itself to the thinking man as a צבה as an ordered mass under the direction and will of One Master—that view could easily carry you away to thoughtlessly ascribe to them powers of their own, and to imagine that they could use the powers they possess to influence your fate and fortune on their own initiative, and so והשתחוית להם consider yourself as powerless before their will ועבדתם and that you have to win their supposed good-will by some form of devised form of service.—אשר חלק ה׳ אלקיך וגו׳. It does not say אשר הלק להם ה׳ את כל העמים וגו׳ which would say that God had given them ruling power over the nations, but what it does say is just the contrary. True, they are allotted to the nations of the world. The nations are directed to use, by intelligent application, the physical powers of the sun, moon and heavenly bodies for the furtherance of their individual and national lives. But it is God, your God Who has given them as His servants, to the nations for this happy furtherance of their lives. So that it is His Goodwill alone that they have to seek by using these powers in a moral dutiful manner to justify the position they are given in the world. But the nations have forgotten this point, and thereby have sunk from their destined morally free position of mastering the world to the subservient unfreedom of a worship and service to physical Nature. In the pure position of the world, the forces of Nature are allotted to Man, in the erroneous one, Man is allotted to the forces of Nature.

V. 20. ואתכם לקח ה׳ וגו׳. And just now, to begin the building up of a new pure humanity, has God taken you out of this whole false link to Nature when He took you out of the “iron crucible”, out of Egypt “purified and united” for such a purpose. With your historic national arising out of historic national death, in contrast to all the predictions of the ordinary run of things, with your similar national wanderings under the direct guidance of God proclaiming Him and Him alone, as His עם נחלה, as the heritage which first comes back to Him out of the general nature-worshipping estrangement from Him, you are to be the world-historic meteor in the heavens of the nations that gradually leads the nations back to the consciousness that it is God—ה׳ אלקיך Who reveals Himself in your fate and life—Who has “allotted” to mankind all the forces of nature before whose might they acknowledgingly kneel. So that they, like you, render homage to Him and Him alone, and are to see at their feet, for their own use, those powers which they had raised to the eminence of gods, before whom, before the time they had attained the freedom-giving giving homage to the One God, they sunk tremblingly in unfree degradation.

To rightly appreciate the expression: אשר חלק ה׳ וגו׳ (V.19) it is not unimportant to refer to the linguistic fact that the sum of all that we possess of the world on which our state in the world depends is called בהמה שמן חלקו .חֵלֶק (Habak 1,16), חלקם בחיים (Ps. 17,14), ומה חלק אלוה ממעל (Job. 31,2). But quite specially does the Jew consider “God” as his one real possession of the world, as the one possession which he really “has” in life. חלקי ה׳ אמרה נפשי (Lament 3,24), ה׳ מנת חלקי וכוסי (Ps. 16,5 etc.). Or speaking in a roundabout way, using several words instead of one:-מי לי בשמים ועמך לא חפצתי בארץ כלה שארי ולבבי צור לבבי וחלקי אלקים לעולם (Ps. 123,25 and 26). Hence in the great chapter of Jeremiah extolling the highest degree of reality of the existence and being of God in contrast to the non-existence and the imaginary being of the gods of heathenism, it says: לא כאלה חלק יעקב כי יוצר הכל הוא וגו׳ (Ch. 10,15). In a similar way, Israel too, in its completely belonging to God and giving itself up to God for His purposes of the moral redemption of mankind is called God’s כי חלק ה׳ עמו :חלק (Deut. 32,9), ונחל ה׳ את יהודה חלקו (Zak. 2,16).—כיום הזה, as it now stands there today in reality.

V. 21 and 22. וה׳ התאנף בי etc. I must leave you, you are going over by yourselves to the new future where you will have to prove yourselves as the עם נחלת ה׳ (the People of God’s inheritance I.L.), therefore השמרו לכם etc.

דבריכם as -על דבר שרי ,על דבר (“because of the matter of Sarai” Gen. 12,17) etc. “because of you”, of your affairs. And this plural, דבריכם, could well be explained by the fact that the bitter feeling out of which Moses’ lapse arose (see on Numb. 20,10, 11 et seq. I.L.) which was so heavily punished, was not due solely to that last event at which it came to be expressed, but was the culmination of all the bitter experiences he had to endure from his people during the long years of his leadership of them. הארץ הטובה, see Ch. 3,25.

V. 23. שכח ברית .השמרו לכם does not mean so much a forgetting as a disregarding of the covenant (Cf. Prov. 2,17).—אשר צוך ה׳ אלקיך, with reference to which God made encumbent on you (cf. Ch. 2,37 and Levit. 4,2). The warning השמרו is in the plural, is accordingly directed to the whole nation in the plurality of all its individual members, but אשר צוך speaks to the nation in its unity as a nation. So that אשר צוך can well also express the thought: “which thy God hath commanded thee to watch over”. The nation as a whole shall see to it that the bond with God does not become broken by any of its members through any kind of idolatry.

V. 24. אש אכלה ,כי ה׳ אלקיך, next to Him, everything else simply has no existence. אל קנא: He is קונה שמים וארץ, He stands above all and everything as the Owner and imposes the rights of His supremacy on everybody and everything. His Being is exclusively unique. Nothing can be placed next to Him. In no ways can He be ranked in the sphere of anything else that exists by an image or otherwise without denying Him entirely. Only in His supernatural unrepresentable unique personal existence as a fact, accessible only to the thinking brain does He remain to us the ever-present, all-bearing, all preceding, Being, the sole condition for all existence, to Whom every breath we take soars up and every movement of our lives serves (cf. on Ex. 20,5).

V. 25. כי תוליד. Not immediately at their entrance into the land does Moses fear the danger of aberration, but he sees it coming the longer they are in the land, sees it coming only when the second and third generation will have been born in the land, ונושנתם בארץ, and they will have become “old” in the land. ישן is not, like זקן the opposite of “young”, but the opposite of “new”, “fresh”, as indeed already lies in the conceptions of “dark”, and “sleep” which are also designated by ישן (see on Gen. 2,21 and XXIV,1). Only when the nation will have had two or three generations behind it born in the land will its inhabitants consider themselves as ‘“natives”, originated from the land; the time when they had no home, no land belonging to them will have passed from their minds and they will entirely have forgotten their origin and Whom they have to thank for the land and for their being permitted to remain in it. Not for naught has God with His למען תזכר את יום צאתך מארץ מצרים כל ימי חייך interwoven the fact of the redemption from Egypt daily into our minds to be ever freshly remembered; not for naught founded His festivals and His great institutions of Shemita and Youvel for the ever-recuring acts of the united national remembrance of that origin of the land and of its belonging to God; not for naught was the כבש בן שנה, the “young of the flock appointed by God to be the eternal symbolic represenation of His People in their relation to Him. In our individual and national relation to God we have no greater enemy than the change of our fresh “youthful” enthusiasm of the consciousness of belonging to God to the worn out blase condition of “having grown old in the Land of Promise”. When that which as “promised” was the longed-for goal of our hopes and wishes has become “ours” and we “grow old in the possession of it.”

והשחתם. As the thought fades of the supernatural One which the history of your origin reveals as the only real bearer of your existence and of that of the whole universe, the material world of the senses with its imagined reality of your being the overlord of yourself pushes itself to the fore, and you throw yourself into the arms of heathen depravity which considers all individual and national existence only as the product of the physical forces of the world which form countries into cradles of nations, and from these powers the nation and the individual have to wrest their fate.

Then it is no longer God who blesses you in and through His Land according to how you regulate your doings and your abstaining from doing in accordance with His Will which He has revealed to you, but it is the land itself with all its visible effective material forces to which you look for the granting or denying of your prosperity. ועשיתם פסל תמונת כל. And you represent these forces to yourself by making images of them, and finally arrive at the stage where ועשיתם הרע בעיני ה׳ אלקיך להכעיסו you see in God not the Dispenser, but the Obstructionist of the joys of life with His laws always demanding the refraining control of your sensuality, and imagine that by making it a principle to disobey His laws you are achieving the salvation of a happy course of life.

V. 26. העידתי: just the heaven and the earth, the whole visible universe to which your worshipped powers of the world belong do I appoint as witnesses against you.
