And equally so הטרוד טרדא המצוה פטור מן המצוה, not only actually doing the Mitzva itself, but a disturbed state of mind and pre-occupation brought about by the preparations necessary for doing a Mitzva gives dispensation from doing another Mitzva which, like ק״ש requires quiet concentration of thought, whereas טרדא דרשות, excitement and disturbed conditions of mind brought about by other causes, even by unfortunate occurrences, demand the exercise of self-control to regain composure of mind to fulfil the Mitzva. The duty of fulfilling the Mitzva of ק״ש depends on בשבתך בביתך פרט לעוסק במצוה being occupied with our ordinary occupations but not if we are engaged in fulfilling a Mitzva, and בלכתך בדרך פרט לטרוד טרדא דמצוה, when our thoughts are full of accomplishing some ordinary purpose, but not if they are nervously labouring about the accomplishment of a Mitzva (see רשב״א ibid).

בשכבך ובקומך, at the time of your lying-down and your rising up. So that the time for saying night-שמע is all night, from the time the stars come out צאת הכוכבים until daybreak עלות השחר; and for the morning-שמע, from daylight משיראה את חבירו רחוק ד׳ אמות ויכירנו (when he can see somebody at a distance of four cubits—roughly eight feet—and recognise him) until the end of the first half of the forenoon i.e. three twelfths of the day (Berachoth 2,a, 8,b and 9a). The renewal of our taking to heart the “Oneness” of God and what that entails for the whole of our life is thereby commanded for the time of our night’s rest and for the time of our arising for the day’s activity. The former to concede our complete confidence in the One Director of our fate, the latter to equip ourselves with cheerful obedience to the One Guide of our deeds.

The school of Shammai taught that בשכבך ובקומך meant literally in a recumbent or in an upright position and demanded saying in the evening lying down and in the morning standing up. But that of Hillel deduced from ובלכתך בדרך the teaching that כל אדם קורא כדרכו saying שמע in any respectable position in which one happens to be. Now, according to Berachoth 11,a, although the Halacha decided according to the Hillel teaching that any position is fitting for the saying of שמע, if someone—following the Shammai teaching—were deliberately to stand up from a sitting position to say the morning Shema, or in the evening sit down from a standing one, not only would he be seriously blameworthy, but, as ר׳ יוסף puts it: עשה כדברי ב״ש לא עשה ולא כלום, he would not have fulfilled the שמע-duty at all (עיין פרי מגדים א״ח ס״נ ב׳ הניח בצ״ע דלא (כתבו הפוסקים שצריך לחזור ולקרות. The reason for this might perhaps be that Hillel’s teaching כל אדם קורא כדרכו, is not to be taken simply as a facility, a קולא, but as an essential characteristic of ק״ש which just by the fact that כל אדם קורא כדרכו is shown to be the thought that should fill our minds in every situation and every position in life, whereas the denial of the canon כל אדם קורא כדרכו by adopting a definite position in which to say it in the morning and another at night would give ק״ש the appearance of containing a thought which one would have to get out of one’s ordinary course to take it to heart. (According to this the difficulty raised by תוספות (ibid) ד״ה תני רב יחזקאל would also be solved). Only the first sentence, the real קבלת עול מלכות שמים is not to be said walking along on account of concentration of כונה demanded for it. Apart from that the teaching of the school of Hillel concerning ק״ש runs:- עומדין וקורין יושבין וקורין ומטין וקורין הולכין בדרך וקורין עושין במלאכתן וקורין (ibid). (One may say ק״ש—except the first verse as above—standing, sitting or leaning, walking along or continuing one’s work I.L.).

V. 8. וקשרתם וגו׳. The acknowledgement of the “oneness” of God, the giving up of the whole of our lives and wishes to this One God with all our heart and all our soul and all our fortune which we are daily to bring to mind as being the whole of our life’s task and the theme of our own education and of our educating our children, this we are to bind on our hands as a symbol of “binding duty”, and bind on our forehead as a symbol of “directing our eyes and thoughts”.

As here, so also in Ch. 11,18 it says וקשרתם אותם לאות על ידכם והיו לטטפת בין עיניכם just as it has already said in Ex. 13,9, והיה לך לאות על ידך ולזכרון בין עיניך וגו׳ כי ביד חזקה וגו׳ and in V. 16 there: והיה לאות על ידכה ולטוטפת בין עיניך כי בחזק יד וגו׳ and corresponding to these the Halacha teaches that four paragraphs viz: קדש (Ex. 13,1-10), והיה כי יביאך (ibid 11-16), שמע (Deut. 6,4-6), והיה אם שמע (ibid XI,13-21) are to be bound on the upper part of the forearm as a symbol of dedication and on the forehead as a symbol of remembrance. Corresponding to the singular form אות used referring to the hand-symbol and the plural טוטפות for the head-symbol, which, on the other hand has the singular used again לזכרון, the Halacha teaches (Menachoth 34,b) that for the תפלין של יד the four paragraphs, written on one strip of parchment are to be boxed in a single case, a בית, but for the תפלין של ראש the four paragraphs are to be written on separate pieces of parchment and placed in a case divided into four compartments. By the prescriptions given הלכה למשה מסיני, the בית, the case belongs essentially to the תפלין-symbol, and, as already remarked single for the hand and four-celled for the head; חריצן ניכר, its being divided into four compartments in the head-tephillin must be visible exteriorly; תיתורא, the cases rest on a base which ends in a loop, מעברתא, for the leather straps to be pulled through. In the sides of the cases of the head-tephillin a ש is formed by pressing the hard skin firmly which in the קדש-side is a four-headed one. מרובעות: the cases have to be square. שחורות: the outside surface of the leather straps must be black. קשר: the two ends of the head-straps are knotted together in a ד-shaped knot, and on the hand-straps there is י-shaped knot. (Menachoth 35a, and b).

The hand-tephillin are laid on the inner side of the biceps muscle on the left arm, וקשרתם וכתבתם מה כתיבה בימין אף קשירה בימין he has to perform the binding of his arm with the tephillin-symbol by the same hand with which he writes down the words (Menachoth 37,a). For in truth the binding of the tephillin on the arm a “writing” of the Words of God on the arm just as fixing the mezzuza on the door is called “writing” it there; וכתבתם על מזוזות וגו׳. The hand on which the tephillin is to be bound is also called the weaker one ידכה יד כהה (see on Ex. 13,16). Just as the head-tephillin have to be laid not ‘“between the eyes”, but בגובה שבראש (see below), high above on the forehead—the seat of the organ from where the eyes are controlled and the impressions of the thoughts they gather received—so also the hand-tephillin find their place, not “on the hand” but above, on the muscle of the upper arm that controls the whole organ בגובה שביד—where also, in conformance with the text ולא :והיה לך לאות לאחרים לאות, usually you are aware of it but not, like the head-tephillin, it is apparent to others also, and also finally in conformance with that other text: ושמתם את דברי אלה על לבבכם וקשרתם, Ch. 11,18) שתהא שימה כנגד הלב, that they are placed opposite the heart. The place for the head-tephillin is on the anterior part of the head perpendicularly above the centre-point between the eyes, where the hair starts to grow,—and the lower edge of the base, the תיתורא should not come lower that this part—and up to but not beyond the anterior fontanelle, the unossified membranous space on the skull which persists for a time after birth, מקום שמוחו של תינוק רופס. Just as בין עיניך in the sentence לא תשימו קרחה בין עיניכם למת (Ch. 14,1.) (“Ye shall not cut yourselves nor make a bald patch between your eyes for the dead”) obviously does not mean literally between your eyes, but designates a place in the hair on the anterior part of the head. כשהוא מניח מניח של יד ואח״כ מניח של ראש וכשהוא חולץ חולץ של ראש ואח״כ חולץ של יד, first one puts on the hand-tephillin and then the head-tephillin, but in taking them off, the head-tephillin come first. It says וקשרתם לאות על ידך and then והיו לטוטפת בין עיניך; and it says כל זמן שבין עיניך יהיו שנים ;והיו לטוטפת, only as long as one has both tephillin on shall the head-tephillin be בין עיניך, but the head-tephillin are not to be worn unless the hand-tephillin are in place too. (Menachoth 36,a). But if one is prevented from laying the hand-tephillin, one must nevertheless put the head-tephillin on by itself, for the two are separate mitzvas in themselves, they are not actually dependent on each other as one mitzva. תפלה של ראש אינה מעכבת של יד ושל יד אינה מעכבת של ראש.

That the whole command of tephillin is of symbolic character, and that a realisation of its meaning is expected, is said unequivocally by the concept of the words אות and זכרון by which it is designated; as well as by the prescription that for the whole of the making of the tephillin, for the parchment, for the ink, the cases, the hairs with which they are tied, the threads with which they are sewn, as well as the straps etc. may all only be made from material of a בהמה טהורה; and that brings them into the category of those objects which God has ordered to be presented for our spiritual mental “consumption” for which the rule applies לא הוכשרו למלאכת שמים אלא עור בהמה טהורה בלבד a canon which is attached just to the proclamation which the Torah makes at the command to lay tephillin: למען תהיה תורת ה׳ בפיך (Ex. 13,9—refer to it—and Sabbat 28,b) to which the Gemora says: מן המותר בפיך. In Menachith 6,b tephillin are considered to be on a level in importance for the consciousness of our thoughts with, yea even superior to, the ציץ, that “show-tablet” on the forehead of the High Priest, so that the dictum והיה על מצחו תמיד, שלא תסיח דעתו ממנו: “that we are to keep our mind constantly on it” applies to tephillin also. According to תוספות (Menachoth 34,b) the very name טוטפת indicates that just as בבל clearly comes from the root בלל, so would טטף come from טוף with the first radical letter doubled. But טוף in Chaldean means “to regard” to consider, and the name by which טוטפת are called תפלין, from פלל “to judge”, would designate the purpose of the tephillin to be: to accord ourselves correct self-judgement.

The importance and meaning of tephillin has already been very fully considered and explained in our article entitled: “Grundlinien einer judischen Symbolik” in the Jeshurun V. (since reprinted in the Gesammelte Schriften Vol. 3 I.L.) and we would refer you to that. Here we would only make the following remarks:

The four paragraphs קדש ,והיה כי יביאך, and שמע ,והיה אם שמע, form two groups of thoughts which mutually complement each other (according to R. Akiba—Menachoth 33,b—טוטפת is the foreign name for a housing of two pairs טט בכתפי שתים פת באפריקי שתים—cf. יגדום במשנה בכורות מ״ג ב׳ לפי גירסת הערוך ופירושו). The one group קדש ,והיה כי יביאך are to be on the right, the other שמע ,והיה אם שמע on the left (Menachoth 34,b), and the grouping remains the same both according to ר׳ תם, who has the two הויות next to each other in this order קדש ,והיה כי יביאך ,והיה אם שמע ,שמע, and according to the usual רש״י order קדש ,והיה כי יביאך ,שמע ,והיה אם שמע.

קדש and והיה כי יביאך represent the fact of יציאת מצרים with its consequence of our belonging exclusively to God as the Guide of Fate, according to both the phases of His governing which showed at the time of the redemption from Egypt, saving, in קדש, directing in שמע .והיה כי יביאך and והיה אם שמע represent the fact of מתן תורה with its consequences for the task of our lives; שמע, acknowledging God by private and national life being dedicated through and through to the knowledge of and fulfilment of His commands; והיה אם שמע, the dependence of our weal and woe on the fulfilment or non-fulfilment of this task of our lives. Clearly קדש stands in a similar relation to שמע as והיה כי יביאך does to והיה אם שמע. The belonging to God founded in קדש receives in שמע the explanation of its practical proof in our lives, and the directing government of God proclaimed in והיה כי יביאך receives in והיה אם שמע its importance for our future lives: the God Who did not tolerate Pharoah’s disobedience will also not overlook any defection on our part. But with יציאת מצרים and מתן תורה the foundation for the whole mission of our lives is laid.

To this mission which has grown to us out of יציאת מצרים and מתן תורה each one of us is to make a ”home“, a בית, a place for it to be realised and carried out, and moreover מרובע (see article referred to above) “by freewilled human activity” (as symbolised by being square, angles are not found in nature, only curves, angles denote human intentional work I.L.). And this “house”, the בית we are to create for the תורה is to have תיתורא, is to have its “base”, its basis on earth. Not in contrast to earthly matters, on the earth and with everything earthly it expects to be realised. And this base has its מעברתא, it wants essentially to be borne by us, by human beings. It is nothing external, separated from our own personality from ourselves; it wishes to become true as part of ourselves, to make our own personal selves into a priestly consecrated Sanctuary of God. Like the Ark of the Covenant stretching its בדים out towards the people, towards the nation, so do the tephillin, the Ark of the Covenant in miniature, stretch their מעברתא out to every individual and say to him “bind yourself to me and bear me eternally through your life”.

The “house” of the hand-tephillin is a single one. In a single room it harbours the four paragraphs of laying the foundation of and the carrying out of our mission in life written on a single roll of parchment. The “house” of the head-tephillin is a “four-roomed” one, containing each one of the four paragraphs in a separate compartment by itself. That which forms itself to one single motive as the “motor force of all our activities” is to be appreciated for the “consideration and retention” of our thoughts in its separate factors, one after the other and one next to the other.

Just as we are greeted by the name שדי—that name of God as being the all-sufficing One Who fixes the measure and limit and goal of everything—on the mezuza of our actual concrete houses, so do the side-walls of the symbolic houses of the head-tephillin show the letter “ש״, the indicating sign (אשר), and point to God, to Whom the title of “Unlimited Completeness” is to be ascribed, and make us think of Him, not as some vague inactive being of a metaphysical speculation, but as a, as the real Super-personality with the full unlimited powers of action and government.

And if an extra “י״ is added to one of these “ש״ and the “ש״ formed into a four-headed שין then thereby “י״ the basic sign of all existence (היה) is joined to the “ש״ that sign of fulness of strength and power and action, and both together, the most intensive existing and the most extensive power join to יש the “actuality” of existing and to שי, the expression of homage to the absolute Highest. In tephillin we go to meet Him the Highest, not as others do in fear but with the שי expression of fealty and homage and feel ourselves existing through His existence, and strong through His strength כל סביביו יובילו שי למורא (Ps. 76,12).

The tephillin teachings which lay the foundations for the whole of our existence we attach to our head and our hand, and thereby bring our “thinking minds” and our “accomplishing strength” into the bond of their duties. We place them on the anterior part of the head, the seat of our thinking and fix the קשר, the knot joining the יציאת מצרים and תורה groups from left and right, on the seat of “remembering” at the back of the head. From there they stream down on the right to the seat of our earthly sensuous organs, (the navel I.L.) and on the left to the seat of our higher moral wishings (the heart I.L.), accordingly to designate the whole of our physical-spiritual self to be included in the dedicating bond with our “thinking” head.

But that which—grasped by, and kept in, our minds—is to impress on our whole existence the stamp of being dedicated to God is the binding of all the work, all the accomplishing deeds of our lives to the service of the Divine teachings and the Divine Will as is expressed by the hand-tephillin on the forearm.

The tephillin teachings on the head are the Jewish truths and teachings which Jewish people openly profess, and representing them and carrying them through the world forms their world historic mission. Of these theoretical truths and teachings it says in Ch. 28,10 וראו כל עמי הארץ כי שם ה׳ נקרא עליך ויראו ממך “all the nations of the world will see that the name “God” is called on you” ר׳ אליעזר הגדול אומר אלו תפלין שבראש (Menachoth 35,b).

But as the motive power inducing our deeds and actions they are only known to our own consciousness. The Jew does not talk and brag about his principles. He lets his deeds speak, but the “principle”, the warm living source from which they spring, is his quiet sanctuary which he silently hides. The hand-tephillin he wears on a covered place, of it it says: והיה לך לאות על ידך לך לאות ולא לאחרים לאות, it shall be a sign for you on your hand, a sign for you but not for others (Menachoth 37,b).

But the hand-tephillin have to be put on first and then the head-tephillin, and the hand-tephillin have to be taken off last. כל זמן שבין עיניך יהיו שנים, as long as it is possible to have hand-tephillin we may never have tephillin on our head without having tephillin on our hand. And the first exalted feeling on receiving our mission expressed itself in the vow נעשה ונשמע, as Jewish wisdom says:- כל שיראת חטאו קודמת לחכמתו חכמתו מתקימת וכל שחכמתו קודמת ליראת חטאו אין חכמתו מתקימת, כל שמעשיו מרובין מחכמתו חכמתו מתקימת וכל שחכמתו מרובה ממעשיו אין חכמתו מתקימת “only where the fear of God is first and comes before erudition, and life is richer in deeds than in scholarship, there alone has learning the right stability”, so is all this expressed by keeping this tephillin-law, which makes him first place his actions in the service of the Will of God, and from this resolution and for carrying it out, then tread the path of learning and know-knowledge.

But as the knot of remembering is fixed on the head-tephillin in the form of a “ד״, and a “י״ is to be found on the hand-tephillin, and the two together with the “ש״ of the head-tephillin complete the name שדי, then the head and hand tephillin together—the dedication of mind and action—place the Jew in every phase of his life in the service of the One Who said to the Father of the Jewish race as being the Father of the whole of mankind, to “Abraham” (Gen. 17,1, see notes thereon): אני אל שדי התהלך לפני והיה תמים, and thereby set “conducting yourself before the Presence of the All-sufficient and All-sufficing One Who fixes the limits and measures for all “as the mission of the sons of Abraham”.
(For the further explanation of tephillin see the Gesammelte Schriften as above and the חורב Ch. 38) (—the latter about to be produced in English by Dayan Dr. I. Grunfeld I.L.).

V. 9. וכתבתם על מזוזות. Finally that which is to be the foundation of all your thinking and doing, to which you are to give over the whole of your being, and to accomplish which, you are to stake your life, to attain the knowledge of which you are to exert yourself for yourself and to hand down to your children, with which you are to occupy yourself early and late, and which is to accompany you wherever you go, and which accordingly is to make its mark on all your thoughts and doings: that is to form the inscription on the door-posts of your houses and on your gates, and thus dedicate the homes of your private and public lives to be places where all this is accomplished.

That the mezuza-command was reserved for this compendium given to those about to enter the Land is naturally explained by the fact that they would only have houses and gates when they obtained possession of the land. Their tents during the wandering in the wilderness, as דירת עראי would hardly have been חייב במזוזה (Yoma, 10 a and b). But the inscriptions of the mezuza are limited to two of the four paragraphs of the tephillin viz. פרשת שמע and והיה אם שמע, for our houses and cities are just the places where the task of תורה, as שמע teaches, is to be fulfilled, and in which, as והיה אם שמע teaches, the prosperity or the reverse consequent on the national observing or not-observing the dictates of its Torah, becomes realised.

וכתבתם. We have already remarked on Levit. 23,40 (p. 697 in my translation I.L.) how the close connection of a given mitzva with the community as a whole, marked by the pronominal form ולמדתם ,ולקחתם—תם etc. or, as here, the person whose duty it is to the object of the duty, by וכתבתם וקשרתם—תם—indicates that it is expected that the duty in question will be performed in such a perfect manner that all the abilities of the community or the complete devotion of the individual is expressed on the object of the duty. So that accordingly the performance of the mitzva is to be תמה a perfect one done completely, קשירה תמה למוד תם לקיחה תמה, here also, (Sabbat 103,b) שתהא כתיבה תם, כתיבה תמה :וכתבתם. In addition to the general rule applying to all Mitzvas: זה אלי ואנוהו התנאה לפניו במצות, to do them in the nicest possible way, making them attractive and showing the honour which the people feel in being priviledged to perform them: ,עשה לפניו סוכה נאה ולולב נאה ושופר נאה וציצית נאה ספר תורה נאה וכתוב בו לשמו בדיו נאה בקולמוס נאה בלבלר אומן וכורכו בשיראין נאין (Sabbat 133, b; see Menachoth 32b, תוספות ד״ה הא), for ספרי תורה תפלין and (סת״ם) מזוזות the further demand is made: תם that the writing must be of a specially perfect nature. Not only may no actual letter be missing but none of the essential strokes be lacking on a letter, no .קוצה של יוד שתי פרשיות שבמזוזה ארבע פרשיות שבתפלין מעכבות זו את זו ואפילו כתב א׳ מעכבן. Each letter must appear clearly in its traditional form, clearly differentiated from any other letter which is similar to it שלא יכתוב ביתין כפין כפין ביתין וכו׳ דלתין רישין רישין דלתין וכו׳ etc., and every letter stand isolated מוקף גויל (Menachoth 29,a and Sabbat 103,b), and the letters ש״ע״ט״נ״ז ג״ץ provided with תגין “crowns”, traditionally formed by three זיינין. Every letter must also be made solely by “writing” not by some scratching away the surrounding material, not וכתב ולא וחקק ,חק תוכות (Gittin 20,a), and attention must also be given to the traditional spaces to be left at fixed places at ends of paragraph, just a space סתומה or the whole of the rest of the line left blank פתוחה (Sabbat 103,b). Also there are quite definite rules regarding the number of columns דפין, the length of the lines: שיטות, the margins to be left at top and bottom: גליון, the space to be left between the columns, the lines, the words and the letters (Menachoth 30,a) as well as regarding ruling the lines שרטוט (ibid 32,b) etc. etc. For tephillin and mezuzoth there is the further demand that they must be written כסדרן, only in the order in which they appear in the תורה, no letter written before its preceding one, and also no paragraph which occurs later in the Torah may be written earlier which is why in tephillin and mezuzoth anything omitted or a wrong letter cannot be rectified once the writing has been continued and this further writing cannot be scraped away because it contains a name of God that may not be erased (see on Ch. 12,4). (Mechilta בא at the end:- כותבן כסדרן ואם לא כתבן כסדרן הרי אלו יגנזו). This demand is taken to be implied by והיו הדברים האלה that כהוייתן יהו, that just as קריאה למפרע is forbidden so כתיבה למפרע is also not allowed. (See O. Ch. 32, 23). Also no letter of the Torah may be written by heart, but must be copied from one in the front of the writer אסור לכתוב אות אחת שלא מן הכתב, only tephillin and mezuzoth may be written by heart as it can be assumed that the text of these familiar paragraphs are completely clear in one’s mind (Megilla 18b), but nevertheless the writer must pronounce each word to himself before writing it down (O. Ch. 32). They may only be written by the right hand וקשרתם וכתבתם מה כתיבה בימין אף קשירה בימין (Menachoth 37a). תפלין ס״ת and מזוזות are only כשר if they are written לשמה i.e. if they are written consciously and with the quite definite intention of their purpose in mind, and apart from this every Name of God must be specially written לשם קדושת השם, an intention which the writer must expressly announce before he begins to write the word (Gittin 54,b). The juxtaposition of וקשרתם וכתבתם also teaches that only a Jewish person who is in duty bound to lay tephillin and who acknowledges this duty is adequate for the writing of tephillin and so also for for writing מזוזות and כל שישנו בקשירה ישנו בכתיבה וכו׳ ;ס״ת (Gittin 45,b).

The materials to be used are also fixed by tradition. That all three (ס״ת״ם) may only be written on parchment made from the skin of a בהמה טהורה has already been remarked above. The skin of an animal before it is worked is called עור, made into parchment דוכסוסטוס ,קלף and גויל. According to the most general way of taking it קלף is the upper half of a split skin, דוכסוסטוס the lower half and גויל the undivided skin, and the rule is:- קלף במקום בשר דוכסוסטוס במקום שער, (Menachoth 32a and Sabbat 79 b), if you write on קלף you should write on the lower internal surface the part internally towards the flesh, if on דוכסוסטוס on the upper external side, the part towards the hair, on גויל on the hairy side. The parchment we usually use is of the nature of קלף as the under דוכסוסטוס half is scraped away in the preparation. So that the writing is done on the inner softer side במקום בשר. The writing must be done only with black ink: דיו (Sabbat 103,b). The preparation of the parchment must also be done לשמה (specially for the purpose I.L.), עבוד לשמה (Gittin 54 b).

The reason for the correctness and meticulous attention to keeping the traditional and nationally sanctioned forms of the letters by the conception of כתיבה תמה is clear in itself. We would only remark that in Menachoth 29b, important truths appear to be laid down in the traditional form of the letters, as also our prophets have handed down to their people, in the final letters (letters which have double forms I.L.) מנצפך the historical highpoints of Jewish fate, as already remarked on Gen. 12,1. (at the end of the notes thereon I.L.). And if the Gemora there records the tradition that certain letters of the Torah have to be ornamented with crowns (כתרים) and arms (three זיונין I.L.) then the letter of God’s Torah is armed from the beginning to fight, and is the one true fighter on earth that will finally be crowned with victory. But we would like to make a suggestion about the fact that these “crowned letters of the Torah” are just the letters שעטנז גץ. One could take it that שעטנ״ז refers to שעטנז and ג״ץ the initials of גמילות חסדים and צדקה. Then with these two crowned words the two poles of the Torah, and thereby the whole Torah would be crowned with victory. Now שעטנז is considered representative of those הקים the reason for which does not immediately strike the ordinary human mind, regarding which laws the ספרא says: יצר הרע ואומות העולם משיבין עליהם, “the urge of one’s inclinations and non-Jewish people think they are justified in remonstrating against them”. But גמילות חסדים and צדקה belong quite eminently to that category of laws שאלו לא נכתבו בדין היו לכתבן that even if the Torah had not imposed them, one’s own sense would have made them obligatory (see Levit. 18,4 and 5). But the “armed-crowned” letters teach us that both categories of laws, the one as much as the other have first to fight to gain general application, but victory is certain for them.

Equally clear is the demand made by the כתיבה תמה canon for the exact attention to be paid to the פתוחה and סתומה arrangement of the paragraphs. For the open פתוחה form expresses a completely separated paragraph, while the closed-in סתומה form more a mere break in a continuous whole.

Significant is the law that all must be done עיבוד וכתיבה לשם .לשמה סתו״מ and האזכרות לשם קדושת השם. It is not the mere contents in itself but grasping and understanding and acknowledging these contents as the Word of God and as the Divine national law that confers the high קדושה, the holiness that towers above all the other holy things, on the ספרי תורה, which are meant to be read aloud in public. Hence their whole production must from its very beginning be made with this idea; hence especially every Name of God must be written as the realisation of God as the One and Only One Who had been revealed to Israel. So much so, that a ס״ת שכתבה מין, where the conviction prevails that the wrong construction has been placed on the Name of God, so that the whole would be written לשם ע״ז (to the name of a false conception of God I.L.) would have to be burnt ישרף. (Gittin 45b). And altogether a ס״ת is only כשר if it has been written by a Jew who is fully bound to keep all its precepts, who completely recognises his duty to do so, and is qualified to represent the Jewish national community (ibid;—ש״ך on י״ד 281). And therefore also it may not be written by heart, but from another copy lying in front of the writer, accordingly in the full consciousness that it is only to be a replica of a copy itself made from a copy reaching back to the original. And although this demand is modified for תפלין and מזוזות because it is assumed that their text is so well-known and fluent in everybody’s mouth; nevertheless the writer of them must say each word aloud to himself before writing it down; and there is even an extra demand made just for these fractions taken out of the Torah so that they be chracterised as being just extractions from the whole of the Torah. Not only do all the prescriptions given for the making of the public ספרי תורה apply to these writing which belong entirely to private individual spheres, but for them the law of כסדרן is added. For by this law the writing of these extracts is so bound to the original text of the Torah that every paragraph and every letter in every paragraph must be written only the order in which it occurs in the original.

וכתבתם כתיבה תמה והדר על המזוזות ,וכתבתם על מזוזות וגו׳, first—presumably not feasible to be done directly on wooden or stone doorposts—a “perfect” writing of these verses on another material, and then fixing them on the posts. Accordingly, similarly to all writing which the Torah commands to be written not just temporarily, but have to be done throughout the ages (excluding the writing directly on stone which was ordered to be done just once, in Ch. XXVII, I.L.) כתיבה הנוהגת לדורות, the פרשת וכתב וגו׳ בספר :סוטה (Numb. 5,23); the copy for the king: וכתב לו וגו׳ ספר (Deut. 17,18), a writing on parchment with ink, as in Jer. 36,18, ואני כותב על הספר בדיו (Menachoth 34,a תוספות ד״ה נאמר כאן כתיבה). And it is to be the two פרשיות, the פרשת שמע (here, verses 4-9) and פרשת והיה אם שמע (Ch. 11,13-21) of which it also says וכתבתם על מזוזות ביתך ובשעריך in V. 20.

על מזוזות ביתך ובשעריך. The root זוז only occurs elsewhere as a movement, and indeed probably as a small movement. וזיז שדי עמדי (Ps. 50,11). “I know every movement of the fields”; והתענגתם מזיז כבודה (Is. 66,11) “ye will feel blissful at the slightest beginning of the movement of its glory”. In Rabbinic Hebrew זיזין are projections on buildings (e.g. אין מוציאין בה זיזין וגזוזטראות Baba Kama 82,b). The concept “to spring forward” is transferred to space, “to jut out”. Now the halacha is taught in Menachoth 33b, that posts פצימין, which חיזוק לתקרה הוא דעביד, which are meant only to support and strengthen the roof, do not come under the concept of מזוזה of our text. From that it follows that מזוזות are projections from either side of the walls for closing in a space already enclosed on three sides, but this closing has not been completed—or not entirely completed, according to רמב״ם הל׳ מזוזה the presence of doors are essential, and entrances without doors would not have to have mezuzas—but rather by openings and doors allow unconditional or conditional entrance.

ביתך. According to the halacha, only a space of at least four square cubits, enclosed by walls, roofed, and meant for permanent habitation is to be understood by the concept בית of our text, but that warehouses, storage-rooms, stalls etc. are included (Yoma, 11a,). Equally so by שעריך, the gates and doors of yards, cities etc. are included (ibid). The duty of having a mezuza is also conditional on the opening having two side-posts or projections from the walls, and a horizontal lintel above (Menachoth 33a).

Now it does not say מזוזת ביתך ושעריך but על מזוזת ביתך ובשעריך. We believe that מזוזת הבית form the שער הבית and על מזוזת ביתך is identical with בשער ביתך. Consequently it says בשעריך and not על מזוזת שערך because in שער itself the concept מזוזה is already given. שתי מזוזת and a משקוף form a שער. And just by this combination the concept מזוזת ביתך obtains its clear meaning. The מזוזת are not to be considered as bearers of the roof but as side-posts forming a שער (see above). Hence also in Menachoth 32,b it is taught on the expression בשעריך that מצוה להניחה בתוך חללו של פתח, the mezuza is to be placed on the side-post within the opening of the entrance. It is that place where the post fulfils its purpose as שער. On the other hand מזוזת ביתך looks at the doorposts as representing the house, as leading to the house, to the home, accordingly דרך ביאתך from the point of view of going in, not going out, at which it is not the actual living room, but the “hall” or outermost room which is the goal in mind. And as at entering as a rule the right foot is in advance דכי עקר אינש כרעיה דימינא עקר ברישא, the mezuza is to be placed on the post which is on the right-hand side on entering (ibid 34,a), and within the space of the opening in the טפח of the surface of the door-post nearest to the exterior and at a height that first catches the eye of anyone entering (ibid). If a door is between two living rooms both of which have separate doors opening on the hall which leads to the street (so that one cannot say which way is coming in or going out through that door I.L.) then the היכר ציר the hinge decides. The room in which the hinge is, on which the door turns, is considered as the one by which one enters, and the mezuza has to be fixed on the right side looking towards that room (ibid 33,a).

All these laws express quite definitely that, that on which the mezuza with its contents is meant to have an effect, is, in the very first place, the minds and feelings of people who live and work in houses. וקשרתם וכתבתם, just as he who lays tephillin places all his thinking, desiring and doing under the dictates of the Will of God which these tephillin contain, so does he who fixes the mezuza on the living rooms of his house place that house, i.e. the whole active life of those that live in the house, under those same dictates. So that it is seen by him and everybody who enters his house immediately they cross the threshold as a warning and reminder, for that purpose he fixes it on his house and not on his person as if it were an amulet. Only in as far as the contents of the mezuza achieve an effect on the minds and feelings of the household so that it does regulate their lives in consonance with those contents, can they expect protection and support in all the vicissitudes of domestic life from God, the Supreme “All-sufficing One” with which Name custom has adorned the outside of the mezuza.

So much is it not the actual rooms, but the moral concept of a “home” which the rooms represent, to which the mezuza-dedication refers, that it is only such rooms which are architecturally suitable to represent “a home” to which the obligation of having a mezuza applies, and rooms which are deficiently or incompletely built, שאין לו אלא פצים אחד ,פיתחי שימאי בית שאין לו תקרה, etc, do not require a mezuza (Menachoth 33, b and 34 a and Yoma 11 b—see above). Yea, so much is it not the house itself, but the people who look on it as the sphere of their lives, to which the mezuza-dedication refers, that most probably originally it was only a house which imposed the obligation to have mezuza which was the property of the one who lived in it, when his personality was expressed in it as its owner, and a rented house would מן התורה be free from the duty of mezuza, just as a garment in itself does not have to have ציצית but only as your garment, so ביתך like כסותך not בית and כסות. And only מדרבנן would the duty be imposed in both cases after thirty days. תוספות on Menachoth 44,a is still rather dubious on this point, but on Avouda Zara 21,a ד״ה הא אמר he is quite definite that שוכר בית מדאורייתא פטור מן המזוזה. So also ,רא״ש תרי ביתך כתיבי חרא אצטריך למעוטי שוכר ושואל .סי׳ ט״ו ,מזוזה ,הלכות קטנות. (see דברי חמודות ibid).

כל שיש לו, it says in Menachoth 43,b, כל שיש לו תפלין בראשו ותפלין בזרועו וציצית בבגדו ומזוזה בפתחו הכל בחיזוק שלא יחטא שנאמר והחוט המשולש לא במהרה ינתק, ואומר חונה מלאך ד׳ סביב ליראיו ויחלצם. “He who has tephillin on head and arm, tzitzis on garment and mezuza on his door, of him it can well be assumed that in all ways he will not sin, for it says: “the threefold cord is not easily torn”, and further: “an angel of God surrounds those that fear Him and he saves him (from sin I.L.); (סביב ליראיו: Rashi explains: העושים מצות ויחלצם מחטא).

V. 10-13. The end of the preceding paragraph gave the command for mezuzoth on our houses and gates, the symbolic dedication and submission of our domestic and public life to God and His Will. The following one teaches remembering God, faithful devotion to Him in thought, deed and word, and the warning against following the example of the other nations, as the immediate effect to be expected from these inscriptions on our houses and gates.

והיה כי יביאך וגו׳ אשר נשבע וגו׳. You cannot ascribe the acquisition of the Land to your own merit at all. It has been destined for you long ago, before you were historically in existence as a nation. You received it as the result of the assurance given to your first forefathers.—ערים וגו׳ ובתים וגו׳ וברות וגו׳ כרמים וזתים וגו׳, and also all the riches and all that human culture had produced on and in the land is not the result of your own labour and doing; everything so arranged that it should not really be necessary to have the mezuza admonition on your “houses and gates” not to become too exuberant and arrogant in the full enjoyment of all these good things, and always remember Him to Whom you have to thank for all this, and subordinate everything that gives you all this happiness to the fulfilment of His Will,—and still ואכלת ושבעת, you do run the danger, in sitting back in this full enjoyment, of forgetting Him Who brought you out of the destitute hopeless condition of slavery to this opulent independence, השמד לך וגו׳.

V. 11. ברת חצובים: Chron I. 22,2, חוצבים לחצוב אבני גזית, Kings II, XII,13, ולחוצבי האבן and repeatedly at the building of the Temple אבני מחצב as well as הביטו אל צור חוצבתם (Is. 51,1) and also later on here in Ch. 8,9, ומהרריה תחצב נחשת leave no doubt as to the meaning of חצב being “hewn out of the rock”. So that ברת חצבים are cisterns hewn in rocks.
V. 12. השמר לך, see on Ch. 4,9.

V. 13. תירא is the complete subordination under God in the sense of תעבד submission in deed, תשבע subjecting one’s whole existence to God as guarantee for the truth of one’s spoken word (see on Ex. 20,7). It is clear that an oath is only a guarantee for the truth of the words of such a person who in his heart really renders homage to God and who proves that homage by living a faithful dutiful life (אתו תעבד). When such a person places his whole earthly future under the punishing might of God— the recognition of Whom his whole life is a proof—then his oath (which pledges this stake I.L.) carries a convincing certainty which is entirely lacking if his whole practical life gives no evidence of his inner fear of God (תירא). In this latter case the oath itself borders very closely on playing about with the sanctity of God’s Name. From this point of view we can well understand that the מדרש תנחומא (see רמב״ן on the verse) takes the similar verse in Ch. X. 20, which complements it by ובו תדבק to mean:- אם יש לך כל המדות אלו אתה רשאי להשבע ואם לאו אי אתה רשאי להשבע that only a person whose character conforms to what is designated by את ה׳ א׳ תירא וגו׳ is altogether entitled to take an oath.

Rambam (ס׳ המצות מע״ז) and רמב״ן (ibid) differ in the way they take the dictum ובשמו תשבע. According to the former שבועת אמת is a מצוה, it is a direct command to confirm the truth by an oath on serious occasions. For such subjecting our whole existence under God as a guarantee of our truthfulness is, after all, an expression of our acknowledgment of His sublime, ever-present, all knowing, all-just, all-mighty government. But according to רמב״ן it is only רשות, permission, not “thou shalt” but “thou mayest”, on a serious occasion take a שבועת אמת but then you may only swear by God and not by anything else, to which the immediately following לא תלכון אחרי וגו׳ would refer, and then be a לאו הבא מכלל עשה.

V. 14 and 15. לא תלכון וגו׳. Do not let your path in life be guided by that which other nations honour as their divinity, let every one of your steps and those of every individual member of your nation—for לא תלכון is in the plural in the midst of sentences all in the singular—only seek the proximity of God by faithfully following His Will. כי וגו׳ בקרבך, for God to Whom you owe all your good fortune is in the midst of all your national life, and demands as His right that you tread in His paths with all that He has granted you, and that you fulfil His Will. For that it is not sufficient for the official public life to be dedicated to Him, but that the private home-life of every individual remains exclusively dedicated to Him, that not only the mezuzas on your gates but also the mezuzas on your houses mean something real and are no empty symbols, otherwise all your good fortune will go to ruin.

V. 16. לא תנסו וגו׳ (see on Gen. 22,1 and Ex. 17,7). In the preceding verses the whole of the Jewish private and public life is based on the consciousness that ה׳ א׳ בקרבך, that God, the Ruler of our fate and the Guide for all our actions is present amongst us with His Almighty powers of direction (אל I.L.) and that our great and small demands are not left to the infallible laws of blind physical nature, but stand under His completely untrammelled direction of the developments of nature and history. At the entry of our historical path as a nation through the world, the conviction of this Presence of God in the midst of human conditions on earth could still require proving acts, and then, if not right, it was at least excusable that you could still ask for some convincing proof of His Presence, and could say היש ה׳ בקרבנו אם אין, “is God indeed in our midst or not?” All the נסים, all the “proving-acts” with which God introduced you into history, from Egypt to Canaan had no other purpose than to proclaim His almighty, free-willed ruling Presence in your midst. These נסים now come to an end. They have sufficed to raise the conviction of God and His Presence on earth to a certainty beyond all possibility of doubt for all time. You are to hold fast to this certainty and not still ask for further miracles to convince you, but in the apparently ordinary run of things know that “God is in your midst“, and live and die in that certainty.

V. 17. שמר תשמרון. In this certainty that God is present amongst you, that every breath you draw is under His Eye, and everything that you are to get, you receive solely from His Hands, you are to have no other desire than to fulfil his Torah faithfully: The מצות, the tasks to fulfil which He has placed each one of you at his “post”, and which we usually take collectively to comprise תורה, עבודה וגמילות חסדים; the עדות and הקים with which He established the basis for your spiritual development, and gave the moral limits for the life of your senses. That which חקים are for the life of our senses, עדות are for our mental recognition. The former guard the moral purity for our senses, the latter, the truth for our mental recognition. Both contain that which is irrevocably given to us, the fundamental pillars of morality and truth. We are to “guard” them with anxious conscientiousness, watch carefully over them that none of them become lost to us, or dulled. By שמירת העדות all further נסים become superfluous, as they keep the נסים of the foundation of our history eternally fresh in the minds of all succeeding generations as being the facts on which our knowledge of God is based (see רמב״ן on this verse). This שמירה of the מצות עדות and הקים is the task of every single member of the nation (תשמרון). They were given to the nation as a whole (צוך) out of whose hands every individual receives them as the guaranteed Law of God.

V. 18 and 19. ועשית וגו׳. By doing that which is “straight” in the Eyes of God, that which really corresponds to your own nature and that of your fellow-men, and do that which is “good”, that which corresponds only to His plans for the world, you ensure God’s satisfaction with you, and thereby the permanent and undisturbed possession of the land and its riches described above. The טוב, the good that you accomplish makes you worthy of the Land, your יושר gives you the spiritual height before which the material importance of your enemies disappears. Inasmuch as here “that which in God’s judgment is what is right and good” is set as the guiding norm for our conduct, our sages take this as a demand to extend the principles of our social behaviour, and not to abide just strictly to the letter of the law regarding the demands of right and duty, but to let ourselves be guided by what we recognise as the general spirit of the idea of the Torah’s law regarding “right and good”. This principle, primarily comprises the concept of “equity”, and orders us not to make use of a right which we could legally enforce, where the advantage we forego is small and out of proportion to the advantage which the other party would gain by our relinquishment. In some cases this can even be legally enforced by the court. An example would be the דינא דבר מצרא, law of the right of preemption, that when a person sells a field, the adjoining neighbour of this field has the first option to buy it. (B.M. 108,a). So also the law שומא הדר לעולם, that where a field has been assigned by the court to the creditor for an unpaid debt, the debtor can reclaim the field at any time if his means subsequently improve and enable him to pay. (ibid 16,b.) According to רש״י and פשרה ,רמב״ן would also come under this concept, the order for contending parties to compromise and come to an adjusted agreement, whereas the duty for the court to try first to bring about an amicable settlement between the parties in every dispute is referred to the verse of the Prophet: אמת ומשפט ושלום שפטו בשעריכם (Zac. 8,16) as there משפט שלום an activity of the court to bring about peace is what is recommended. Perhaps the canon ועשית הישר והטוב וגו׳ is to be taken in the sense that we are to temper the ישר with the טוב. You are only to use that which in itself is ישר with consideration for the higher-standing ישר .טוב is that which legally appertains to one, free from .עולה טוב is every positive purpose furthering of which is in accordance with the Will of God. Accordingly the canon says:- Even to that which you are legally entitled you should relinquish for the sake of a positive higher good purpose. The one who would like to buy the field in דינא דבר מצרא, the creditor in שומא who would like to keep what is now his own field, give up their undisputed rights out of consideration for the “good” of others. In cases of compromise a party sacrifices some of his legal rights for the sake of peace. In the first cases it is brotherly love, in the latter it is peace which is the טוב which modifies the ישר. In Ch. 12,18 it is reversed כי תעשה הטוב והישר בעיני ה׳ א׳, there it is the ישר which modifies practising the טוב; even that which is in itself good you are only to do בדרך הישר, never let the end justify the means, not attempt to do good by using “crooked” not straight, or illegal means. (see more in detail there).

V. 20. כי ישאלך וגו׳. The previous paragraph (verses 16-19) reminded us not to demand continuous miracles from God to fortify ever afresh our conviction of the Presence of God in our midst, but to be certain for ever of His Presence by reason of the נסים with which the history of the establishment of our nation was filled, and that we could expect the manifestation of it only by our dutiful devotion to that which in God’s Eyes was right and good. Closely attached to this trend of thought comes the concluding paragraph of the chapter which now follows. It enjoins us to hand down the consciousness of these God-proving נסים of our early history as the basis of the whole bringing up of our youth for God’s Torah, and just by the constant repetition of this heritage of our historical experiences make such נסים, suspending the ordinary laws of nature, superfluous for all the succeeding times.

מחר, when the present time will have passed and other times will take its place in which what is happening now, will belong to the historic past (cf. מחיר the exchange value). מה העדת וגו׳. The answer which follows this question does not give the contents of the Torah (which seems to be what was demanded I.L.) but gives the information regarding the origin of our history as a nation, together with the God-proving נסים and the revelations of the Torah which we experienced thereat, as the reason for our obligations to the Torah. So that either מה העדת וגו׳ is in fact the question as to the contents of the Torah, and then the answer teaches that all teaching of the contents of the Torah must be preceded by explaining the tradition of the reason for our obligations to observe them resting on the historical facts of our own experiences so that according to the principle יראתו קודמת לחכמתו (Ovoth, 3, 9,) and the old Jewish military oath נעשה ונשמע, learning the Torah must from beforehand be guided by the purpose of fulfilling it; or מה העדת וגו׳ is not the enquiry as to the contents of the Torah but as to the reasons for the obligations of the Torah, like, מה חרי האף הגדול הזה in Ch. 29,23 the question for the reason for the great wrath coming over the land. It would then be that the later generations came to know the peculiarities of the symbolic procedures, the laws of morality and social life that differentiate the Jews from other people and they ask for information of the reason for this peculiar regulation of Jewish life.

V. 21. ואמרת לבנך וגו׳. The answer touches on all phases of our obligations to the Torah:- Our belonging to God Who brought us out of complete dependence (עבדים) to independence; our knowledge and consciousness of God which we obtained by the facts we experienced (ויתן); the present age which has only God and the covenant made to the forefathers to thank (ואותנו); the Divine origin of the Torah, in the faithful fulfilment of which alone God expects us to pay Him homage, and in which alone the permanence of our well-being and our truly living is rooted (ויצונו); the consciousness of duty which can only be satisfied by complete and unaltered fulfilment of the Torah on our part (וצדקה).

עבדים היינו לפרעה במצרים, we were not slaves of private individuals but the property of the State, so that, as far as human conditions went, there was no prospect of obtaining freedom, and this was in Egypt the most powerful and cultured state of the time. ביד חזקה ,ויוציאנו, not as a result of events brought about by Him in the ordinary course of happenings, but in direct revelation of His Almighty Power, wresting us away from human violence.

V. 22. אותת ,ויתן ה׳ אותת, deeds showing Him as Creator, Lord and Master of the world and its organisation; מופתים, events making Him known as Judge and Educator of men, for the purpose of convincing men and altering their will (from פתה=יפת); בפרעה ובכל ביתו, the teaching and convincing miracles did not occur only and not so much on and for the people but they affected the highest leading class of the people also, they were felt by the king, his entourage also who had to decide whether to let the Jews go or not, and at the same time demonstrated that no human augustness was a protection against God’s punishing justice. (cf. Gen. 45,2 and L.4), ובכל ביתו, we were the onlookers and not the sufferers, and it was our own personal experience on which the knowledge of God to be drawn from such events rested.
V. 23. למען הביא אתנו (cf, Zephan. 3,20). בעת ההיא אביא אתכם.

V. 24. ויצונו וגו׳. Significantly, here all the commands are grouped together in the concept הקים. In contrast to the excesses of the spiritual, moral and social arbitrary proceedings, the result of which we had got to know in Egypt, here, all the חקים ,עדות and משפטים are classed together as חקים as given by God as the immoveable spheres drawn by God within which the whole of our spiritual, sexual and social lives are to unfold. The obligation rooted in the history of our origin makes them all into חקים, and ensures them eternal inviolable fulfilment. We have to fulfil them all solely ליראה את ה׳ א׳, to prove to God that He is our God by paying homage to Him and demonstrating our “fear of God”, but at the same time we lay the foundation for our enduring happiness and our continued existence in true life. The purpose of our fulfilling them is יראת ה׳, its result: טוב לנו and טוב לנו .חיים is the harmonious agreement of all our external connections with our happiness, חיותנו, the development of our whole existence in agreement with what our lives were meant to be כהיום הזה, everything that we possess to-day of טוב and חיים we owe to our obedience to the Torah.

V. 25. וצדקה, see on Gen. 15,6. And it is our righteous duty, we can only discharge the mission of our life if we keep the Torah as מצוה, all, without exception as the “command of God”, as “direction to the post of our lives”, carefully, unstinted and unaltered, completely according to its contents and in the prescribed manner, as He has commanded us. כל המצוה—כאשר צונו. We have no right either to abrogate anything nor to reform anything.

V. 1. כי יביאך וגו׳. The final paragraph of the preceding chapter gave us the mission to hand down to our children as the life-task of every contemporary and future generation, the duty of faithfully carrying out the dictates of the Torah on the basis of the historical experiences of our past. But this heritage of the Torah, attracting and bringing up our children for our eternal life’s task is frustrated beforehand if they are born under non-Jewish influence, if they are conceived in non-Jewish wombs, rocked on the knees of non-Jewish fathers, if non-Jewish father’s or mother’s teachings and example form their minds and characters if our married life and family life is penetrated with non-Jewish elements. This endangering our mission at the root of our whole future is what the following verses come to counter.

נשל .ונשל is the specific term used for fruit being dropped from trees too early before they are ripe. כי ישל זיתך (Ch. 28,40). The land which up till now had borne the inhabitants denies them the use of its soil any longer, as God has judged them to have become unworthy of it. When you move in they will already be cast down by the land and you are only the gusty wind which has to clear the ground from what has fallen as waste on it, to make room for the planting of a more worthy pure growth. This thought lies in ונשל-מפניך. “Planting” Israel in the land of the Canaanite population is a frequent conception in scripture. (Cf. Ex. 15,17; Ps. 80,9 and 10 etc.).

V. 3 and 4. ולא תתחתן בם. In Yebamoth 76,a the Halacha is taught that hereby, regarding the Canaanite population, even in circumstances which allow marriage חתון with other nations, i.e. after they have been converted to Judaism by גרות, with them marriage is barred. חתון, marriage, with non-Jews can altogether not take place unless and until they have been converted. בהיותן נכרים לית להו חתנות, between Jews and non-Jews, Jewish Law recognises no state of marriage אין קדושין תופסין (Kiddushin 68,b), so the prohibition given here of marrying one of the Canaanite people ולא תתחתן בם can only refer to a marriage after they have become Jews, as only נתגיירו אית להו חתנות, only then can there be any question of חתון at all. For the Canaanite population accordingly גרות forms no qualification for חתון, and for them all the prohibitions בגיותן remain in force: בתך לא תתן לבנו ובתו לא תקח לבנך, not only shall you not give your daughter to a son of a non-Jew where you know beforehand that you are estranging your child and grandchildren from Judaism, but even their daughter you shall not take for your son, in which case you might think that the power of your influence and that of your family life would induce Jewish spirit and Jewish ways in the Canaanitish girl; you shall not think that you can expect a Jewish grandchild to be born and brought up for you out of a non-Jewish womb; for not only would no children be born to Judaism from a non-Jewish mother, but his father-in-law would bring your own son, begotten by you and his Jewish mother, away from being faithful to Judaism and over to his non-Jewish ideas, כי יסיר את בנך מאחרי, and the one and the other, your daughter married to a non-Jew, or your son married to a non-Jewess, ועבדו אלהים אחרים, will fall to the non-Jewish ways of the heathen gods. Then the way our text is taken implies also the legal canon that ולדה כמותה, that where the father or the mother entirely lack the qualification to contract a Jewish marriage, אין קדושין תופסין, then the child, going according to the principle of observing the actual origin, takes the character of the mother, either Jewish or non-Jewish, בנך הבא מישראלית קרוי בנך ואין בנך הבא מן הנכרית קרוי בנך אלא בנה a canon which in the Mishna (ibid 66,a) is expressed thus:- ,וכל מי שאין לה לא עליו ולא על אחרים קדושין הולד כמותה ואיזה זה ולד שפחה ונכרית. That is why the text speaks only of the danger of the defection of your son married to a non-Jewess, but not if your grandson, your descendants generally, כי יסיר את בנך not את זרעך, as the children begotten by him with a non-Jewish wife no longer belong to Judaism from their birth. In this we have followed the way ר״ת takes it, Rashi takes it in another way according to which כי יסיר refers to the first eventuality את בתך לא תתן לבנו (look it up).

How deeply sexual erring with non-Jewish women undermines the whole future of Judaism is warningly described in the Peor-defection, its cause and effect (Numb. 25,1-13). Malachi 2,11 and 12 pronounces כרת for just such sins בגדה יהודה ותועבה נעשתה בישראל ובירושלים כי חלל יהודה קדש ה׳ אשר אהב ובעל בת אל נכר יכרת ד׳ לאיש אשר יעשנה ער ועונה מאהלי יעקב ומגיש מנחה לד׳ צבאות (“Judah hath dealt treacherously, and an abomination is committed in Israel and in Jerusalem for he hath profaned the holiness of God which he loved, and hath married the daughter of a strange god. God will cut off the man that doeth this, be he master or scholar or priest that offereth an offering of allegiance unto the God of hosts, and Ezra (Ch. IX, and X) saw the spiritual ruin of his people before his eyes, because לא נבדלו העם מעמי הארצות כי נשאו מבנתיהם להם ולבניהם (“The people of Israel and the priests and the Levites have not kept apart from the people of the lands………for they have taken of their daughters in marriage for themselves and for their sons etc. etc.”) and the higher classes of Jewish society led the way in this sin ויד השרים והסגנים היתה במעל הזה ראשונה, so that the future of Israel could only be saved by casting out all these women and the children born from them, to regain a pure national Jewish body: להוציא כל נשים והנולד מהם וכתורה יעשה וגו׳.

The gravity of this sin, which had already been amply stressed by the Prophets for every Jewish conscience, gave occasion at the time of the Maccabees for it to be added to the crimes which were recognised by the human judicial courts: ב״ד של חשמונאים גזרו ישראל הבא על הכותית חייב משום נ׳ש׳ג׳ז׳ (“The Beth Din of the Hasmoneans decreed that one who had sexual relations with a non-Jewess was guilty of transgressing against ,נדה שפחה ,גויה ,זונה, I.L.”) (Avoda Zara 36,b, see חידושי ר״ן on Sanhedrin 82,a —Cf. Sanhedrin 82,b: והוא בועל את וכו׳—see שאילת יעבץ ס׳ קס״ו. Notes on 2nd Edition).

וחרה וגו׳ בכם והשמידך וגו׳. If these sins are committed by the Jewish majority, then, the sinners will be punished individually but the consequences affect the whole nation by the fall of the existence of the Jewish State.

V. 5. כי אם כה וגו׳. See on Ex. 34,13. Your children, to whom you are to bequeath your relations to God and your obligations to His Torah on the basis of your personal historical experiences (Ch. 6,20-25) and whom you can only beget for this mission in Jewish marriages (V. 3 and 4), to them you must hand over a land free from all memories of heathenism, from heathen altars, monuments, groves, images and pictures. (See also on verses 25 and 26.).

V. 6. כי עם קדוש אתה, for you are a “holy” people. The zenith of the mission of other nations is themselves, keeping their national existence is the highest purpose of the united nation. But the mission of your national union lies exterior to itself, it does not belong to itself, it belongs to God, it has to place itself, with all its relationships, with every phase of its individual, family and public life “prepared and ready” for certain purposes and tasks which are indicated by God its Lord and Master. Hence it has to keep out of all its connections everything which would work against these purposes. “A holy nation art thou, belonging to One God, thy God”.

בך בחר וגו׳, is explanation of the preceding כי עם קדוש etc. The whole purpose of your having been chosen was no other than to establish a national social life which would mould itself under the exclusive influence of God, i.e. which would conform with the dictates of His Torah. You are to present a nation that in none of its connections belongs to another power, and develops itself on no other basis than this exclusively belonging to God. For that is what it means to היות לו לעם סגלה (See Ex. 19,5).—מכל העמים, either, out of all the nations and referring to בחר, or, more than all the nations, by that which God has done to you He has a greater, more exclusive right over you than over all the other nations.

V. 7 and 8. לא מרבכם, not on account of your numerical size did God choose just you for His purpose, for just this imposing exterior greatness was lacking in you; כי מאהבת וגו׳ but the reason for your being chosen lay in your nature and in His relationship to your forefathers. He found your nature worthy of His Love, He found the mental moral qualities in your nature that are necessary for Man to get near to God. “He found Himself”, to speak in human terms, “attracted to you”, and at the same time He had to redeem the oath which He had sworn to your fathers—equally because of their spiritual moral worthiness.

V. 9. וידעת וגו׳. From the experience of your redemption you know that God, Who showed Himself in your history as your God, is altogether the God Whom all peoples—under whatever name they may call Him— recognise, or have some inkling of, as “God”. And you know further that He is the one divine power to which Man can trust etc. האלהים is the general conception of God, האל הנאמן etc. is the specifically Jewish conception of God. Sublimeness and Might are the attributes of God in the general conception of men. Dependable, Loving and Just, in benevolent alliance with human beings is the Jewish special conception of Him. Heaven and earth bow before His Might, but that He is near to Man, in union with him as friend to friend, that Israel has experienced in its history (Cf. Ps. 112,3-9).

נאמן, a passive concept, one in whom confidence can be placed. שומר הברית, as you can see for yourseves, that even after centuries He keeps the ברית which He made with your forefathers, and still rewards their merit on you.

V. 10. ומשלם וגו׳, seems to be fresh information over the ways of God’s government which would not have been obtained from the experiences the people had already had, unless perhaps one could take it that they could have seen what happens to the שונאי ה׳ from Pharoah’s fate and downfall. ומשלם וגו׳, He also rewards the good that these people do, and indeed אל פניו, each one “to his face”, either: he himself enjoys the rewards for his good deeds, not like the אוהבי ה׳ to whom God is נוצר חסד לאלפים, who receive the reward in this world for the good they have done, in happiness which they found thereby for their children and descendants (see Ex. 34,7): “in the direction of his face”, i.e. in accordance with his own point of view and desires. His selfish mind only puts value on what he himself can enjoy (Eruvim 22,a). להאבידו, parallel to the לאלף דור of the אוהבי ה׳ could also mean, the destruction of his line of descendants as expressed by כרת and specially ערירי. Goodness has immortality even in this world by its living on in the descendants, who, in the inherited moral tendency towards goodness, also inherit the rewards for the father’s virtues. The descendants of the bad people die out after the third or fourth generation if they continue on the evil path of life (Ex. 20,5). The reward for the good which bad people do, they receive in the material blessings in their own lives to let them (and their bad influence if it persists) disappear in the generations of the future.—Thus ילמדנו on עקב:- יד ליד לא ינקה רע אמר הקב״ה לישראל לא תעשו את התורה על מנת לקבל שכרה מיד כל מי שעושה כך נקרא רע ואינו מתנקה שלא הניח לבניו כלום שאלו בקש אברהם שכרן של מצות מיד היאך היה משה אומר זכור לאברהם וגו׳ אבל אם עושה רשע מצוה מיד ליד אני נותן לו שכרו שנאמר ומשלם לשונאיו בעה״ז ואין בידו לע״ה מהו לא יאחר לשונאו אינו נותן שכר לשונאו ממה שיש לאחריו אלא ממה שלפניו וכו׳.

This indication of the ways of God’s government of the world would give a solution to the old riddle of the world’s management. צדיק ורע לו רשע וטוב לו and allow one to recognise the constant development of the world towards a higher degree of goodness, inasmuch as the incurably bad dies out and the future moves on slowly more and more towards the good until finally ועמך כולם צדיקים וגו׳ (Is. 60,21). Then it would be in agreement with this that the Gemora, in Avoda Zara 4,b, remarks on ושמרת וגו׳ אשר אנכי מצוך היום לעשותם, stressing היום לעשותם ולא היום ליטול שכרך -:לעשותם “To-day to do them, but not to-day to receive the reward thereof”, or as this teaching runs in Kiddushin 39,b:- שכר מצוה בהאי עלמא ליכא “this world is a world of doing Mitzvas, not a world of reward of Mitzvas.”

V. 12. והיה עקב. Whereas in the preceding it was explained that in individual lives the reward for the good deeds of the really good people does not mature in their own lifetimes on earth, here the rich material blessings which will accrue to the nation from a national life kept true to the Torah are described as being the result of such a life, but not as a goal to be aimed at. Accordingly all the commands of the Torah, the ,עדות הקים ,מצות and משפטים are here classed together under the one concept משפטים. At rock bottom they are all nothing but “legal maxims” with which the most varied conditions and relationships of the spiritual and material life of the individual and state have to be carried out, so that they are in accordance with the yardstick צדק, the Divine ideal for all conditions of the world. As such, as the duty we owe to what is right, for which no thanks and no reward can be claimed, are they to be carried out. But they all correspond so deeply to the nature and purpose of things and men, and they are all so much in harmony with each other, that, by their being faithfully carried out by the nation, a condition of the richest blessings of a national existence on earth emerges.

This result which was not what was striven for, but which comes automatically by itself is called עקב, literally “heel”. It is that which follows obedience, not what went before, not what obedience had in eye. Hence our sages attach to this verse the most searching teaching as to the frame of mind in which the Torah expects us to fulfil its dictates: אורח חיים פן תפלס שלא תהא נושא ונותן במצותיה של תורה אי זו שכרה מרובה ועושה אותה למה נעו מעגלותיה ולא תדע מטולטלין הן שבילי התורה, that we are not to weigh the separate Mitzvas in our minds to consider which Mitzva would probably expect a larger reward so that we pay particular attention to that one. The paths of the Torah form an ever widening circle in which they overlap each other and lose themselves one in the other. We cannot forsee the results of fulfilling any Mitzva. They interlock one to the other, and far-reaching results arise from what is apparently the smallest, and seems to us the least important Mitzva. That is why all Mitzvas without distinction should be performed with equal conscientious faithfulness, all be of equal importance to us, all only be done in the feeling of its being our duty without giving a thought to what we might consider deserving of a greater or lesser reward.—Further, the linguistic fact that the word עקב indicates something not consciously striven for, something that remains unconsidered, behind, gives the teachings of our sages the opportunity to transpose it from referring to the effect of the Torah into the contents of the Torah, and to make it give the admonition: והיה עקב תשמעון וגו׳, to give our attention just to that which, according to the changing circumstances of the times, seems to be trivial and petty and tends to be left behind, as they put it מצות שאדם דש בעקבו mitzvas which one steps over as having little meaning. Making such capricious differentation in the Torah between what is supposed to be more important or less so, especially making such difference between the so-called מצות שבין אדם לחברו and שבין אדם למקום (mitzvas between man and man and those between man and God. I.L.) has from old always been most disastrous for us. The final collapse of our first State is ascribed primarily to disregarding the מצות שבין אדם למקום, that of our second State to the disregarding of מצות שבין אדם לחברו. A salutary future will only blossom for us if we take the Torah as a whole, and keep it in its entirety and completeness without making any distinctions. Only as תורת ה׳ תמימה is it משיבת נפש.

תשמעון את is not obeying, but hearing, taking it into the mind. The three stages are mentioned which belong to fulfilling the Torah: ,שמיעה עשייה ,שמירה, hearing it, studying and conscientiously guarding it, and fulfilling it, the Torah passing into the mind, the understanding, the deeds.

V. 13. ואהבך וגו׳, the first result of faithfully keeping the Torah is ואהבך, that God recognises in you a faithful servitor whose will becomes merged into His and He loves you accordingly as only a master loves a truly faithful servant; then וברכך: as, through you, that, and only that is furthered which is in agreement with His Will, and in your prospering His concerns on earth prosper, accordingly He gives you prosperity; והרבך: and sees in your increase, in your blossoming out in ever growing generations in which your spirit, your feelings and the faithful acts of your life repeat themeselves, only an extension of His Kingdom on earth. In this richness of ever-increasing number of pure, spiritual and moral souls lies the greatest blossoming of God’s state which is being founded by the keeping of the Torah, and parallel to it goes the ever-increasing blossoming of the riches of the soil, as depicted in the continuation of the verse. וברך פרי בטנך וגו׳ is only the carrying out of והרבך and the blossoming of the land which is necessitated thereby to satisfy the requirements of the increased population.—עשתרות, a word of doubtful meaning. In Chulin 84,b, it is taken to have the meaning of riches, from the root עשר.

V. 14. ברוך וגו׳, the tail-end of the sentence, לא יהיה בך וגו׳ proves that by this, the blessing that is to distinguish the nation that lives under the regime of the Torah above all the other nations, is to be understood as the blessing of having children. The Word of God knows nothing more precious than a human soul, and to it the number of the increase in souls is the measure of true national happiness (cf. the remarks made on Numb. 38,9 et seq.).

V. 15. מדוי. Whereas הלי designates the physiological effect of a condition of illness, as a disturbing element to development (see Gen. 46,1.) דוי is more a designation of the feelings caused by illness, the suffering. Hence frequently associated with לב. The phonetic relationship between דוה and טוה (spinning) makes one think of some similar connection between the meanings of חבל pain and cord. Should pathological pain be regarded as a separating and pressing together of heterogenous elements in the body which normally fit themselves in harmoniously to the whole organism, but now are spinning themselves together and twisting together inside the organism, and so דוי and חבל would only be different phases of one and the same procedure?

V. 16. ואכלת כל העמים. Cf. Levit. 26,28; Jer. 10,25; XXX, 16; L.17 etc. where the term אכל occurs with the meaning of destruction of a people, especially by war and the sword. For אכל is also used just as the predicate of חרב, as in Deut. 32,42 and elsewhere. And anyway the concept war, לחם is closely connected with that of food, and אכל in this connection would be not so much a war of objective destruction as the destruction of the nation for the purpose of self-preservation.

לא תחוס עינך עליהם. The repeated admonitions not to have any mercy on the Canaanite population shows how much such a merciless procedure goes against the grain to the Jewish people and is against what they are meant to be, which is, and is to remain the predilection to protect all living creatures. They are to regard this merciless procedure against the Canaanite population as an exception, expressly commanded by God, to be done at His bidding because of the special circumstances.

כי מוקש הוא לך cannot refer to ולא תעבד וגו׳. For defection to idolatry is in itself the highest depravity, the most to be feared. ולא תעבד appears as being in parenthesis, and כי מוקש וגו׳ refers to לא תחוס וגו׳, have no mercy on them so that you do not come to serve their gods, for it, the mercy you would show to them, would become a snare for yourselves, the mercy you exercise would bring you to defection. (cf. Ex. 23,33 and XXXIV,12). The positive expression הוא לך, not יהיה לך could designate this mercy as being that factor on which Israel’s happiness would surely be ship-wrecked—as indeed actually happened.

V. 19. המסות וגו׳, God has given you proofs (מסות) of all phases of His power of ruling, means of recognising His Presence and Allmight (אתות), Divine visitations for teaching and bettering (מופתים), of how He does not allow that which He calls His Own to be wrest away from Him (יד חזקה), and how His Might extends over all human power (זרוע נטויה). כן יעשה, in quite the same way as at your exodus from Egypt will God prove Himself at your entry into Canaan.
V. 21. לא תערץ (see Ch. 1,29).

V. 25. פסילי וגו׳ is the positive antithesis of the very first fundamental truth of all the truths on which the enlightenment and civilization of mankind rest. So that a worshipped idol has no right to be allowed to exist in a Jewish land. It must be destroyed as soon as it comes into the possession of a Jew. But only if it had hitherto been פסילי אלהיהם, a worshipped image of a god, (תוספתא ע״ז פ״ו) את שנוהג בו משום אלוה; but if an idolatrous non-Jew had beforehand already, by some act of mutilation or by abandoning it to be destroyed, done away with its character of something to be worshipped, that also does away with the איסור. In Avouda Zara 52,a, it takes the words of this verse and teaches פסלו לאלוה לא תחמוד, פסלו מאלוה ולקחת לך, “a blow from the chisel, לאלוה, forming the god prohibits you from possessing it, a blow from the chisel abrogating it מאלוה, from being a god (done by the idolator) allows you to possess it”. Hence the sentence in the Mishna (ibid,b); עכו״ם מבטל ע״א שלו ושל חברו וישראל אין מבטל ע״א של עכו״ם. The ע״ז of a Jew אין לה בטילה עולמית (ibid 53,a). On the words פסילי אלהיהם it is further taught (ibid. 52,a,) that ע״ז של נכרי אסורה מיד, an image made to be worshipped as a god in possession of an idolator is at once אסור as soon as it has become פסיל אלוה even before it has been worshipped, ושל ישראל אין אסורה עד שתיעבד (see Ch. 27,15). But only such polytheistic objects which have been worshipped have to be destroyed which שיש בהם תפיסת ידי אדם which can be considered as mobile work of man’s hands, and also not animals שאין בהן תפיסת ידי אדם, which are still purely the products of nature. Trees, שלא נטען מתחלה לע״ז, which had not been planted for ע״ז purposes, by being planted in the earth lose the character of mobile תפיסת ידי אדם and by being worshipped afterwards, and only such growths which then come from them are אסור. Of such of which it says above v. 5, ואשריהם תגדעון it says: איזה אילן שגידועו אסור ועקירו שרי הוי אומר אילן שנטעו ולבסוף עבד. But a tree which has been originally planted for ע״ז purposes is אסור, and that would be the אשרה of which in Ch. 12,3 it says ואשריהם תשרפון באש (Avouda Zara 48,a). On the other hand a house, in this respect retains the תפיסת ידי אדם character even after it has been built, המשתחוה לבית שלו אסור and for that the rule applies: תלוש ולבסוף חברו כתלוש דמי (ibid. 47b, and Chulin 16,a;—cf. Levit. 11,37.).

Although it says here: פסילי וגו׳ תשרפון וגו׳ and elsewhere the canon applies כל הנשרפין אפרן מותר וכל הנקברין אפרן אסור that the ashes of those איסורי הנאה which have to be burnt, as כלאי כרם ,ערלה etc., after the mitzva of burning has been carried out, are מותר, but where burning is not prescribed but the אסור has to be brought out of the sphere where they could be used, by קבורה, then the ashes too remain אסור, nevertheless the ashes of ע״ז are אסור in accordance with ולא ידבק בידך מאומה מן החרם in Ch. 13,18 (Temura 33 et seq; refer to it.).

לא תחמד כסף וזהב עליהם, so that not only ע״ז itself but also the things that go with it, or are on it are אסור בהנאה. In this connection there are three different categories:- נוי, that which serves as ornamentation or glorification of the משמשי ע״ז ;ע״ז, things which are used in the cultus; תקרובת what is brought to it as offering, if either the object itself or the manner in which it is brought is כעין פנים, either the קרבנות or the עבודות are similar to those in the Sanctuary of God, (Avouda Zara 50 & 51). ביטול is effective with נוי ותשמישי ע״ז as well as with the ע״ז itself, an act of ביטול done by a נכרי to an ע״ז automatically effects ביטול for its משמשים and נוי objects (ב״י on טור י״ד 139; Avouda Zara 50a and 52,b).

פן תוקש בו. We have already remarked on Levit. 19,6 how we must give no room in our thoughts for the whole conception of the existence of the heathen gods. Hence everything which has merely some relation to the heathen cult of the gods must be kept away from the sphere of our possessions and thoughts.
