V. 17. כי ד׳ וגו׳. These are the thoughts of יראה (of the fear of God I.L.). For God, Who has come so intimately into your fate and your active life as אלקיכם, He is אלקי וגו׳, all the forces of Nature are submissive to His Power, all the rulers of men to His Rule. He is האל, it is He from Whom all power and all movement emanates; הגדול, Whose greatness towers incomparably above all conception of greatness. He is “Greatness” absolute; הגבור, all might is His and He uses His Might to rule His world; and He is הנורא, He is not indifferent to how His human beings live on earth, what they think and do and refrain from doing, people have to take His Will into consideration with all their thinking and willing and doing, and, above all, to fear Him as soon as they dare to set their will and their actions in opposition to His Will and to the purposes of His Government of the world; אשר לא ישא פנים ולא יקח שחד, Who only values the true human value of men and finds no substitute for true human worth either in social position or in descent, nor in intellectual superiority and talents, Who, in His demands for His laws of morality pays no regards to social position and does not allow Himself to be bribed by intellectual genius.

V. 18. עושה משפט וגו׳, Who shows His respect for all persons just by taking the part of the forsaken and humbled orphans and widows, and in the loving provision which He makes for the stranger who comes to Him and to you from out of the heathen world, who, giving up all his previous social and national connection, without any past, without any זכות אבות, solely with the impulse towards pure human worth which has awakened within him, flees to God, confident that God will not fail to recognise his longing to come to God and to true human beings, and will not refuse to accept him in the bond of His proximity. God loves this true human feeling in people who flee to Him and grants it a home “means of living and civic position” as is expressed by לחם and שמלה. Jacob similarly condenses everything that can be hoped for towards material well-being in the words “bread” and “clothes”. (Gen. 28,20).

V. 19. ואהבתם וגו׳, practise the similar attitude which God shows, in the reception which the stranger entering your midst from outside receives at your hands, that you place the highest value simply on what a man is worth as a man. The complete equality before the law, more, the love that the stranger is to find in the Jewish nation characterises most strikingly the land and the people as the Land of God, and the People of God, that there the pure character of a man acknowledging God gives him that which, in other circles, riches and origin acquire for him.

V. 20. את ה׳ אלקיך וגו׳, the notation of the cantillation quite definitely joins את ה׳ א׳ תירא אותו תעבד to be one thought. This verse is the concluding verse of the יראה-thought introduced in V.17. Keep your God—Who has just been described in the greatness of His Might, and only valuing what a man really is in himself—constantly in mind, so that the consciousness that it is only with your own moral personality that you can satisfy Him makes you give yourself entirely up to His service. ובו תדבק, this expending all your powers in fulfilling His Will becomes the means of attachment between you and the אל גדול גבור ונורא “serving Him thou getteth near unto Him”; and ובשמו תשבע, inasmuch as your whole life bears witness that His Name is esteemed by you as the absolute highest conception possible, your “placing yourself under His Name” (see on Ch. 6,13) is the highest guarantee for your word.

V. 21. הוא תהלתך וגו׳ develops the thought of the התהלל .אהבה, literally: to “radiate oneself outward”, i.e. to make one’s inner self recognised by bringing one’s moral strength to the fore. הוא תהלתך, He and your relations to Him are that wherein your whole self finds recognition and realisation; והוא אלקיך, and His relations to you as the Director of your fate and Guide of your actions reveal Him, make Him recognised as your God. This reciprocality is the root of the most intimate אהבה love. אשר עשה אתך וגו׳ are just the revelations of God in the history of the foundation of Israel.
גדלת, the great deeds for the salvation of Israel. נוראות the dread deeds for the punishment of Egypt.

V. 22. בשבעים וגו׳ ועתה שמך וגו׳ (see on Ch. 1,10). This growth of the family into a nation occurring under God’s miraculous power makes that nation regard itself as the sign of God’s special care and by its very existence already feel in duty bound to God in love.

V. 1. ואהבת follows the preceding verse as the consequence:- so love etc.”. ושמרת משמרתו. God has given His Torah to Israel as a treasure entrusted to be guarded. והקתיו. This ו׳ means jointly with what follows; “as well as”, “as much as” and indicates the complete parity of the different parts of the Torah, the laws of morality, the social regulations and the positive commands all equally important parts of the treasure entrusted to them. With all the great deeds which God performed to save, to keep, to bring happiness, teach and form Israel, all He wanted was to make a depositary and a worker for His Torah in the sphere of the nations. In fulfilling this calling Israel has to prove its loving devotion to God.

V. 2 היום is probably in contrast to the כל הימים of the previous verse. The mission of guarding, keeping the Torah applies to all generations of all time. But that contemporary generation which was the first to approach that task had quite special reason to give all their strength and powers for the accomplishment of that mission. That which succeeding generations would only get to know by tradition was what they themselves had seen and experienced. כי לא את בניכם is clearly elliptical, as much as to say: “to whom I am speaking”.—את מוסר ה׳ אלקיכם refers to the whole guidance from Egypt through the wilderness, everything by which God exerted instructive and educating influence on Israel. (see on Ch. 8,5).
את גדלו: His Greatness, which everywhere proved to be adequate where all normal expectations were lacking; את ידו החזקה וגו׳, which He showed towards the Egyptians in freeing Israel.

V. 3. מעשיו וגו׳ are what are otherwise called מופתים (miracles I.L.), divine dealings directly affecting persons and their possessions for the purpose of changing convictions and ways of thinking. ואותותיו ומעשיו are the ten plagues.

V. 4. הציף וגו׳ על פניהם. In Ex. 14,27 it says ומצרים נסים לקראתו, accordingly the waters rushed forwards against them (as they fled in terror, נסים I.L.) and threw them down backwards. Hence צוף .על פניהם probably related to צפה which in Piel means to make a covering, a superficial layer, thus צוף to swim or float on the surface of the water, צפו מים על ראשי (Lament 3,21), ויצף הברזל, “he brought the iron to the surface of the water”, Kings II, VI,6). ויאבדם ה׳ עד היום הזה most likely means:- the Egyptians’ might has never recovered.

V. 5. ואשר עשה לכם. Verses 3-6 reckon up several facts which characterise the meaning given them in V.2, and ואשר עשה לכם וגו׳ would accordingly comprise all the joyful and the reverse of joyful events which they experienced under God’s guidance in the Wilderness.

V. 6. בתיהם mentioned as well as אהליהם would most likely refer to the members of the family, the household. (cf. Numb. 16,27 & 32). כל היקום אשר ברגליהם most probably refers to what is there described as כל האדם אשר לקרח. These would be the other members of the households. ויקום (see on Gen. 7,4) in V. 23 ibid. יקום comprises everything living. Possibly here too animals are included, for it says in Numb. 16,32 ואת כל הרכוש. In Sanhedrin 110a, under יקום, all the property of Korach is understood.—אשר ברגליהם, in this expression used here and elsewhere to describe a following the word רגל is most likely meant to be understood as “step”, as לרגל המלאכה in Gen. 33,14.
V. 7. את כל מעשה. The establishment of Israel as the People of the Torah of God is one great act of God, of which the events mentioned formed just single factors.

V. 8 & 9. ושמרתם וגו׳. The task of Israel which was represented in Ch. 10,12 et seq. and Ch. 11,1 in separate demands is here summarised in one single concept of the Mitzva:- it is the fulfilment of the whole duty for which Israel had received its special position amongst the nations and now is to enter into possession of the land which was designed for that purpose. למען תחזקו: in this שמירת המצוה lies the source of its strength and its power of overcoming all difficulties, as well as being the condition for the continuance of its future on the soil of that land.—זבת חלב ודבש. see Ex. 3,8.

V. 10 & 11. The constant change between the plural and the singular which occurs here and altogether in Moses’s exhortations could be intended to bring to the minds of the people that in spite of their settling down throughout the land and the decentralisation of the masses (plurality) of the people, they still remain united and belong together as a single unit (singular). והשקית ברגלך וגו׳: Egypt’s fertility is independent of the rain. It is watered by the Nile irrigation canals cut right through the country, made and worked by human efforts. Thus in Zacc. 14,18, Egypt alone is depicted as not suffering when there is no rain. Somewhat doubtful is the meaning of ברגלך, it might mean step by step, or refer to pedalling the wheels set in the canals to force the water along (there are still 100,000 water wheels and water lifts in use to-day in Egypt I.L.). According to the Gemora, Sabbat 85a, it would be the former. והארץ וגו׳. But Palestine is a land dependent for its supply of water on the mountain springs fed by the rainfall. Moreover it was built out not only in the valleys or plains but also on the mountains and hilly districts where means for artificial waterings are impossible So that its fertility is entirely dependent on the rainfall.

V. 12. ואת שעיר החטאת דרש וגו׳ :דרש .ארץ וגו׳ (Levit. 10,16); ואין דרש ואין מבקש (Ezek. 34,6) to look around for something, to bother about something, to look after something, ולך יקרא דרושה (Is. 62,12) in contrast to נעזבה. The prosperity of this land is not left over to just the consequences of an order to Nature once given, but is rather an object of the attention of the superintending and educating Divine arrangements for you whom He has destined to be the means for His purpose of achieving the spirituality of mankind. תמיד עיני ה׳ אלקיך בה, and unceasingly are the eyes of these watching and educating arrangements of God for you directed on the land to make the development of its agriculture correspond—hampering or furthering it—to the requirements of your education. (see Rosh Hashona 17,b). מרשית השנה ועד אהרית שנה, significantly the course of the year is written with the א missing, making it suggestive of the concept רש, poverty. The beginning of each agricultural year in this land starts quite without any “foresighted assumption,” quite poor, without any inheritance left from the previous year. No physical effects, either hampering or furthering, of the previous year, affect the new one. The character of the year, of every fresh year, is solely dependent on your moral behaviour. And—the Gemora remarks—the more deeply we are conscious at the beginning of each new year of the absolutely deciding factor of our moral behaviour, the richer in hopes does that year start: כל שנה שרשה בתחלתה מתעשרת בסופה שנאמר מראשית השנה, מרשית כתיב. The ספרי on this verse says: ארץ אשר ה׳ אלקיך דורש רבי אומר וכי אותה בלבד הוא דורש והלא כל הארצות הוא דורש שנאמר להמטיר על ארץ לא איש וגר׳ ומה ת״ל ארץ אשר ה׳ אלהיך דורש אותה כביכול אין דורש אלא אותה ובשכר דרישה שהוא דורשה דורש כל הארצות, i.e. if Palestine, the land of the Divine Torah is here designated as the object of God’s concern, that by no means is to say that the other lands are excluded from His care, for it definitely says otherwise in other places of the scriptures. But God’s solicitude for the world of mankind is concentrated in His care for this land. Inasmuch as the land of the Jews bears in its bosom the historical memorial of God’s revelation of His Torah and with that the moral happy future of mankind which ultimately through the Laws of Morality for mankind which emanates from Zion will make the Kingdom of God on earth a reality, one can really say that Zion’s blossoming is a condition for the blossoming of all mankind. Every drop of rain on earth that falls for the sake of Zion falls for the sake of the whole future of mankind which is guaranteed by Zion, however little any contemporary time may appear yet worthy of the drop of rain.

V. 13. והיה וגו׳. This carries on the preceding in which was said that the blossoming and prospering of the land is dependent on our behaviour towards “God our God”. And indeed, as is taught in Sifri on that verse, מראשית השנה עד אחרית שנה, not only the produce on the fields is subject to this constant watch on our moral behaviour, but also what is already harvested, stored up or even taken for our immediate eating is granted blessing or blight according to our behaviour, as it says in XXVIII,8 יצו ה׳ ברוך טנאך ומשארתך ;את הברכה באסמיך ובכל משלח ידך (ibid) ואכלת ושבעת (XI,15) והסירתי מחלה מקרבך (Ex. XXII), הם ברשותי ליתן בהם ברכה כשם שאני נותן להם בשדה ברכה.

To that then it goes on to say that as a result והיה etc. —אם שמע תשמע. The very first preliminary condition for all happiness is the continuous, ever-progressive “listening to the commandments of God”, which, according to the Sifri, before everything shows itself in “learning”, studying the Torah, and there it is pointed out how ignorance or insufficient knowledge of the Divine Torah has at all times been the fundamental root of all evil.

אל מצותי (to My commandments I.L.) and similarly in verses 14 and 15 ונתתי (and I will give I.L.). This admonition concerning the whole of our future is put in the first person as being spoken directly by God. It is exactly what God הדרש אותנו תמיד and אשר עיניו בנו מרשית השנה עד אחרית השנה says to us every minute. It is the sum total of His דרישה and השגחה. It is as if the word לאמר stood at the end of the preceding verses. —היום, every day is to bring us God’s commands afresh, they should never grow stale to us and our enthusiasm for them should remain in eternal freshness, שלא יהו בעיניך פדיוטגמא ישנה etc. (they shall not appear to you like antiquated ordinances, Sifri I.L.). (See on Ch. 6,6).

לאהבה וגו׳ is not the object of the preceding מצוה (it does not mean “that I command you to love God etc. I.L.) but of שמע תשמעו: the seriously giving up your mind and your will to the Torah is to beget אהבה, complete loving devotion to God. Such “love of God” and the nearness to Him which is achieved thereby is the highest goal of all endeavours. It will also beget עבודה, active furthering God’s purposes on earth. And both this אהבה and this עבודה require to be accomplished בכל לבב ובכל נפש with the surrender (אהבה), if needs be, with the sacrifice of all one’s “innermost thoughts and feelings”, just as the active carrying out God’s Will (עבודה) must be accomplished on ourselves, on the whole of our לב ונפש (see on Ch. 6,5).

We have already pointed out that —לעבדו ב comprises two things:- the service done on an object i.e. carrying out the will of somebody else on something, caring for it and arranging it according to his will, and the service rendered with something, using it as the means for accomplishing the purpose the other person desires. The realisation of the first part of the לעבדו בכל לבבכם, the Divine Service on our hearts is taught by our sages in Taanith 2, a, to be accomplished primarily by איזו עבודה -:תפלה שהיא בלב הוי אומר זו תפלה, and Sifri on our verse points out the identification of the idea of תפלה as עבודה שבלב with עבודת מזבח in places such as תכון תפלתי קטורת לפניך משאת כפי מנחת ערב (Ps. 141,2). (“May my prayer be set before Thee as the offering of incense, the raising of my hands as the evening allegiance-offering”) or ודניאל וגו׳ על לביתיה וכוין פתיחין ליה בעליתיה נגד ירושלים וזמנין תלתא ביומא הוא בריר על ברכוהי ומצלי ומודי קדם אלהא כל קבל דהוה עביד מקדמת דנא ואומר ובמיקרביה וגו׳ ענא מלכא ואמר לדניאל עבד אלהא חייא די אנת פלח ליה בתדירא היכיל לשיזבותך מן אריותא, וכי יש פולחן בבבל הא מה ת״ל ולעבדו זו תפלה כשם שעבודת מזבח קרויה עבודה כך תפלה קרויה עבודה. (Daniel 6,11 & et seq.) (“And Daniel when he knew that the decree was signed, went into his house, and his windows being open in his chamber toward Jerusalem, he kneeled upon his knees three times a day and prayed and gave thanks before God just as he did aforetime……and when he (the King) came near to the den etc. he said to Daniel:- O, Daniel, servant of the Living God, is thy God Whom thou servest continually able to deliver thee from the lions?” Now was there any Divine Service in Babylon, so what does it mean by “service”, he meant: “to whom thou prayeth continually”; just as the offerings on the altar are called service so is prayer called service I.L.).

Thus the conception of תפלה is given as being “work on oneself”, as being a penetration of one’s whole being with enlightening thoughts and ennobling feelings even as the word התפלל itself literally teaches (see Gen. 11,7 I.L); and the purpose of תפלה is given as being the elevation of the thinking, feeling, and desiring inner being of Man to a state of being worthy of getting near to God and of His benevolence. What the offerings were to accomplish by their symbolic procedure, viz. giving up all obstinacy and self-will, one’s whole being accepting the directing force of the Sanctuary of the Torah (שחיטה I.L.), one’s whole being striving upwards to the heights pointed to by the Torah (עולה I.L.), and keeping at that lofty level (חטאת I.L.), giving up all one’s spiritual and material gifts and possessions to the purifying and stimulating fire of the Torah (אשה I.L.), to be fuel for keeping godliness alive on earth and rendering everything earthly into something which gives satisfaction to God (ריח ניחת לה׳ I.L.), all this is exactly what the words of תפלה are to accomplish on our inner being. So that although just תפלה in general is דאוריתא, the three daily prayers, yea, according to the opinion of most authorities, altogether the duty to pray daily, are only דרבנן, still, we see from the above quotation from Daniel, how very old this saying prayers three times daily really is. Moreover we have already explained in great detail (see Gesammelte Schriften Vol. 4. I.L.) how the contents of our שמנה עשרה are exactly parallel to the procedures of the תמידין (the daily offerings) in consideration of which it was composed—כנגד תמידין תקנום—. Here מאודכם is missing, probably because it is already implied in ולעבדו which demands giving all one’s energies and using all one’s means to accomplish God’s purposes, and בכל לבבכם ובכל נפשכם only expresses the energetic, cheerful, unrestrained manner in which the “service” should be carried out.

V. 14. (ספרי) אני לא על ידי מלאך ולא ע״י שליח :ונתתי. The rainfall is each time an act of the direct Providence of God and not solely the result of the working of an elementary law of nature which God made originally once for all. The primary cause remains God’s providential care. It is, according to Taanith 3a, one of “the three keys which God has retained for His Own use, the key for rain, the key for the mother’s womb, and the key for the resurrection of the dead”, these He has not handed over to His angels, the mechanical laws of nature.

Our sages were well acquainted with the secondary causes of the changes of weather, the meteorological weather forecast, and the Gemora in Taanith has devoted its first pages to observations on that subject which are well worth perusing.

בעתו, “its proper time”, according to Sifri and Taanith 23a, even with consideration for the disturbing effect of rainfall on business and agricultural activities, preferably then during the nights and מלילי שבת ללילי שבת, on Sabbaths.

יורה ,יורה ומלקוש is the early rain which normally starts in מרחשון and מלקוש the latter rain, in ניסן. The fertility in Palestine is dependent on the regular start of these periods of rain, especially the first rain, so that the lack of rain in Marcheshvan was regarded as a great national calamity and brought about the imposition of three fasts of increasing severity. These fasts on account of drought are regarded as national fasts, have the laws of תענית צבור (Taanith 6a, & 15a). The etymology of יורה and מלקוש is doubtful. According to Sifri יורה would be derived from ירה pouring straight down penetrating the soil like an arrow, or as having the meaning of רוה “to refresh with a cooling drink”, similarly to the formation of טוב and יטב, the מרוה, the one who quenches the thirst. Also on account of the regularity of its start, the indicator, the teacher, מורה, as indeed it calls it in Joel 2,23 (גשם מורה I.L.). It announces the rainy season and thereby becomes the regulator of people’s activities.

מלקוש from לקש. In Chaldean לקש is used to designate everything late in time. Thus והון לקישיא ללבן (Onkelos on Gen. 30,42) and תרגום יונתן (on Ex. 9,32) ארום לקישין הינין. In Amos VII, לקש seems to be a second growth of grass and field produce, an after-crop of hay after the first had been cut down before it was mature (this cutting down of the stalks of the produce before it is ripe as food for the cattle is called קוצר לשחת).
V. 15. ונתתי. I make the herbage grow in the fields with consideration of the fact that they are your fields, that your animals are to find pasture there so that you get food in abundance.

V. 16. השמרו וגו׳. As then the prosperity of your land is so entirely conditional on your moral behaviour — and indeed, as the change in number in the preceding verses significantly show not only on the obedient submission to the Torah by the nation as a whole, but on that of all its members, אם שמע תשמעו (plural I.L.); all of you have to do their part, in whatever position they may be, in working together for carrying out the common task on which the national prosperity depends, the blessing comes as מטר ארצכם (plural I.L.); and this carrying out itself stipulates that, in doing so, you never lose sight of all being united together; it is as one national unit, and for the national union, that each one of you is to gather in his part of the national prosperity, ואספת דגנך וגו׳ (sing. I.L) if the prosperity of your land is solely dependent on your moral behaviour, then השמרו לכם “take care of yourselves”, be on your guard to remain solely under the influence of your own knowledge and your own experiences (see on Ch. 4,9), beware of every influence that would estrange yourselves from what you were meant to be, פן יפתה לבבכם, literally that your “heart does not remain open” (see Gen. 9,27) gives no place for inner or outer seduction.

וסרתם ועבדתם. The slightest deviation leads to עבודה זרה and, in principle, is already עבודה זרה. Thus the אמר להם הזהרו שלא יטעה —:ספרי אתכם יצר הרע ותפרשו מן התורה שכיון שאדם פורש מן התורה הולך ומדבק לע״ז.
ועבדתם אלהים אחרים, by submitting our active life to the influence of heathen erroneous conceptions, והשתחויתם להם, by placing our fate under the supposed power of their might.

V. 18. שום על לב .ושמתם means to make something an object of your consideration and care, really somehting that you “take to heart”, have it in your mind and have feelings for it (Is. 57,1 & 11 et alia). Accordingly “bear these My Words in your hearts and souls” i.e. let them be the objects of your thoughts and sentiments, of your desires and actions. וקשרתם and also express this symbolically by the תפלין-mitzva on your arm and forehead (see on Ch. 6,8). Taken in conjunction with the preceding verse this, as well as the following duty in V. 19 of teaching one’s children the Torah, expresses, according to the Sifri, the command that even if ואבדתם וגו׳, even when you are driven out of the real land of the Torah, even in Galuth, the duty of תפלין and תלמוד תורה and so also all מצות הגוף שאין תלויות בארץ all mitzvas which do not refer to the land and its produce, remain in full force also בחוצה לארץ, outside Palestine. This rule is also laid down in Kiddushin 36,b:— כל מצוה שהיא תלויה בארץ אינה נוהגת אלא בארץ ושאינה תלויה בארץ נוהגת בין בארץ בין בחוצה לארץ, כלאי אילן (see Levit. 19,19) and ערלה (see ibid, 23 and on חדש, Levit. 23,14) are exceptions to this rule. תרומות ומעשרות applied מדרבנן also to the countries neighbouring on Palestine, but חלה is obligatroy מדרבנן everywhere, and equally so כלאי כרם is אסור everywhere (see Levit. 19,19 and Numb. 15,18.).

When we compare these verses here 18-20 with the parallel verses Ch. 6,6-9, the tendency here to stress the duty of keeping all personal obligations to the Torah, חובת הגוף in all circumstances springs immediately to our eyes. There it is a matter of teaching the “oneness”, the undividedness of human life from the consciousness of the “Oneness” of God. That is why there the resulting devotion (אהבה I.L) of our whole being in every phase of it, בכל לבבך ובכל נפשך ובכל מאדך is taught to be our mission. And this mission is to be the tendency of all our thoughts and feelings (V. 6.), to be what the teaching and education of our children is to consist of, as well as of all our private and public life (V. 7), and then (verses 8 & 9) commanded to be kept constantly in mind by the symbols of תפילין and מזוזה. But here the תפלין-symbol is completely separated from that of the מזוזה because it means the fitting in the whole of the thinking, desiring and acting personality to the bond of the Torah, accordingly nothing else but the symbolic expression of the duty given by ושמתם את דברי אלה על לבבכם ועל נפשכם with which it is here placed together, and the thought given by the two together is made the lesson taught to the children and to be what all your private and public, reposing and active lives are to consist of. Clearly to say:- But also when you have to leave the Land and no longer have your own country which is in your power to make serviceable to God’s Torah, still take that Torah of God out with you, your hearts and your souls are still to remain bound to the Words of God, and make yourselves and others constantly reminded of this obligation to the Torah by the תפלין-sign on your arms and heads, remain bearers of the Words of God, remain the People of the Laws of God, and bring up your children to that idea, and make your whole life, within and without your houses, devoted to that idea. וכתבתם, (v. 20), as we shall note, belongs to the verse which comes after it.

V. 19. לימוד .ולמדתם וגוי is a more comprehensive term than שנון which on Ch. 6,7 we took to be teaching the Torah in short concise sentences. That is why, so we believe, the Gemora (Kidushin 29,b) attaches its saying בניכם ולא בנותיכם—whereby the duty of teaching Torah would be restricted to sons and exclude daughters—to ולמדתם אותם את בניכם and not to ושננתם לבניך. As a matter of fact women are only not to be directed to the scientific study of the Law, the acquirement of which and the duty of handing it down belong essentially to the calling of every Jewish man. But the understanding of the Jewish Scripture and the knowledge of the Torah that are essential for ויראו את ה׳ אלקיהם ושמרו לעשות את כל דברי התורה הזאת that belong to a true fear of God that leads to a conscientious fulfilling the duties of a Jewish life belong to the education of the intellect and feelings of our daughters as much as of our sons. That is already indicated in the Torah by the command of הקהל (Ch. 21,12). And if it does say, in Chagiga 3a, with reference to that sentence of the הקהל-command הקהל את העם האנשים והנשים והטף וגו׳ למען ישמעו ולמען ילמדו ויראו את ה׳ וגו׳ that אנשים באים ללמוד נשים באות לשמוע, still it has already said just there that למען ישמעו does not mean just hearing, but a proper competent understanding, to be taken as “learning” (see רש״י and תוספות there and תוספות on Sota 21b, ד״ה בן עזאי) to such an extent that the למען ילמדו said of the men, according to ר׳ אשי comprises ילַמדו.

The Mishna in Nedarim 35b, also speaks of a course of תנ״ך for girls אבל מלמד הוא את בניו ואת בנותיו מקרא and, as far as we can see, the assumption of the תי״ט that the version of the Mishna is incorrect, is against the explanation of the Gemora 37b, ולמ״ד שכר פיסוק טעמים מ״ט לא אמר שכר שימור קסבר בנות מי קא בעיין שימור ע״ש. And even if, according to ר״ן (there), בנותיו is not said explicitly in the Mishna but they are only tacitly understood, still the סתם גמרא clearly recognises a לימוד מקרא לבנות indeed the whole treatment of the subject there takes it for granted that לימוד in itself is מצרה and as such would be allowed even from the מודר as ע״ש ועי׳ מה שכתב ב״י לטור .מצות לאו ליהנות נתנו א״ח סוף סי׳ מ״ז ע״ש.

Also it has been the practice from times immemorial—in proof of which there is a whole literature in Yiddish written predominantly for women—to give women a knowledge of biblical and liturgical writings and a general knowledge and understanding of the Torah and the rabbinic teachings (see also טורי זהב on י״ד 246, 6).

לדבר בם, teach them the Torah so thoroughly and make its whole spiritual and mental treasures so impressive and penetrating that it becomes the fundamental subject of their thoughts and speech, and the basis of their outlook on life and the judgement (see on Ch. 6,7 and Ex. 13,9).

בשבתך וגו׳. Concerning the change in number see on V. 10. Here it is all the more important, as in the dispersion, where there is no external bond of union it is their minds, their thoughts which hold them together. Of that time it says then, that just this submission to the one Torah which rules the heart and soul ,the hand and mind of each one of them, and impresses the one stamp on the feelings tendencies, actions and point of view on each one of them, which by teaching and education is implanted in each young generation, that through all this, the widely scattered individuals would still stand there as one joint unit, and everywhere and always in their domestic and public life, in repose and action would remain marked as a unity belonging together.

ובשכבך ובקומך. This repetition here seems to us to strongly support the opinion we offered on Ch. 6,6 that if ק״ש דאוריתא, besides that, it is also a duty דאוריתא to occupy oneself with דברי תורה morning and evening (refer to it).

V. 20. וכתבתם וגוי, we believe that this verse belongs to the following one and has the meaning:- but write these words on the door posts of your houses and your gates, i.e. yea keep the whole of your domestic and public life dedicated to the Torah and allow nothing ungodly to enter therein so that the consequences threatened in V. 17 do not occur, but rather ירבו ימיכם וגו׳. For in the dispersion one cannot really speak of one’s own gates (of the city I.L.) can hardly rightly speak of one’s own houses; in any case ביתך ובשעריך designates the condition in the Land more than out of it (of which the preceding verses speak I.L.), which is also probably why the ספרי only stresses תפלין and תלמוד תורה for the בנין אב for all מצות הגוף which are incumbent also in ח״ל, but not מזוזה although that too is one which is not תלויה בארץ. If one wishes to refer וכתבתם וגו׳ also to the preceding, then למען ירבו would refer to the return to the Land which is to be achieved by שמירת התורה in the exile.

V. 21. למען ירבו וגו׳. If one considers that, by the addition of וימי בניכם, the generation present before Moses was addressed, or every person in it, at any rate a passing generation, one cannot refer the words כימי שמים על הארץ to ירבו and give them the attribute of unlimited duration. One could indeed say למען ירבו ימיכם כימי וגו׳ and take those addressed to be the everlasting nation as a whole, and equally so, ירבו ימי בניכם and take that to be the descendants of that generation reaching down the ages. But not ימיכם וימי בניכם which, as remarked above, by putting them together, makes ימיכם refer to a passing generation. One is therefore led to assume that כימי השמים is not the manner of the duration referring to ירבו, but the manner of the mode of existence referring to למען״ -:ימיכם וימי וגו׳, so that ימיכם וגו׳ על האדמה וגו׳ should be like ימי השמים על הארץ, and moreover ירבו endure for long to be so.” Just as the days of the earth are really the days of the heavens, inasmuch as the whole development of the earth is dependent on the effects of that which come from the skies, in the same way the days of the blossoming of your land are really “your days”, are dependent on your moral “blossoming”—which is indeed what this whole paragraph of והיה brings to your mind—your relation to your land is that of the sky to the earth, and if you comply with God’s Torah, this blessing-forming influence on your land will endure, and “your days” will be apparent in the “days of your land” for long periods, even as the “sky-days” materialize on the earth (see on Ch. 33,28). This way of taking it would also be the underlying meaning of what the ספרי says:- כימי השמים על הארץ שיהי׳ פניהם של צדיקים כיום וכן הוא אומר ואוהביו כצאת השמש בגבורתו (refer to it) and could also be what was meant to be made clear in Menachoth 31b, for the instruction given for the writing of the Mezuza: על הארץ בשיטה אחרונה איכא דאמרי בסוף שיטה כגבוה שמים על הארץ ואיכא דאמרי בתחלת שיטה כי היכי דמרחק׳ שמים מארץ where the position above or the distance of the sky away from the earth is given as a comparison for the position in which the words על הארץ are to be placed, and refer to our position above the earth participating in fixing the material condition of our land as long as we keep ourselves aloft in the heights of our spiritual and moral calling.

V. 22. et seq. כי וגו׳ is what the consequence of all the preceding will be for the immediate future which is imminent. For the conception שמירה applied to the Torah see on Ex. 25,17, and Levit. 18,5. There it is explained that what is understood thereby is, in the first place, getting correct knowledge of the Torah, “learning” by which alone the treasure transmitted to us from God and its demands remain in our minds, and inasmuch as this שמירה is repeatedly demanded of us, שמר תשמרון, the Sifri attaches on to our verse the admonition to repeat again and again what we have learnt שכשם שאדם צריך להזהר בסלעו שלא יאבד כך יהא אדם צריך להזהר בתלמודו שלא יאבד, the Torah warns, that just as one has to be careful not to lose any penny one has earned so one has to guard against losing any knowledge one has acquired. Knowledge is likened to gold and to glass (Job 28,17); it is difficult to obtain, like gold and easy to drop and lose like glass, קשים לקנותם כזהב ונוחים לאבדם ככלי זכוכית. And there in Job some rules for the study of Torah very well worth-while noting, are given.

ללכת בכל דרכיו, “to walk in His ways”, according to the Sifri, to try and copy His Ways of dealing with the world, to be like Him in pity and love and patience, benevolence and dependable, gentle and forgiving and make ourselves worthy of bearing His Name.

ולדבקה בו, according to the Sifri, to keep close to Him also in our association with other people, to seek association with such people who, by word and example, will strengthen us in our “walking in His ways”.

V. 24. כל המקום. After completely taking possession of the Land mentioned in V. 23, all the places lying outside Palestine which Israel conquer לכם יהיה, shall bear the full character of the Jewish Land קדושת הארץ and be subject to all the laws given for ארם צובה .ארץ ישראל and ארם נהרים, together known by the common name of סוריא were conquered by David before the real Promised Land had come completely into Jewish possession—even Jerusalem was still in the hand of the Jebusites—and סוריא accordingly did not receive קדושת א״י, is therefore accordingly not considered as a completely constitutional national conquest and is called כיבוש יחיד (see Sifri and Gittin 8,a).
והלבנון: see on Ch. 3,25.
הים האחרון is the Mediterranean Sea, which when one stands in Palestine facing the east is behind one’s back.
יהיה גבולכם, that is the territory which is really promised to you (see Numb. XXXIV).

V. 26. ראה etc. This is the conclusion of the introductory retrospection and passes over to the compendium of laws for the generation that was to take possession of the Land. ראה, see, it is not on faith and belief in the teachings which you have to accept from others, but out of everything which you yourselves have experienced up to now and what has been recalled to your minds by the retrospective view that you have just been given, you must have formed your own conviction that God has placed the making of your future fate most blessed or most accursed entirely in your own hands by His Torah which He has sent you through Moses.

ברך) .ברכה related to פרך to break through, פרק to unload, to load up somebody else, hence מפרקת ,פדק, joint, ברק lightning, as being an unloading of electricity from the clouds, ברך the knee-joint, the essential lever for moving forward, ברכה the water supply), ברכה the condition of unhindered progressive development, progressive prosperity, and קללה, which is not merely the opposite condition of lack of progress, of remaining isolated without prospering further—which would be ארר—but the contrasting condition of becoming empty devoid of self-substance, becoming shallow, worthless (from קל ,קלל light, completely without weight). The alternative between these two conditions is “placed before us” with God’s Torah, it depends on us to create the one or the other for ourselves.

V. 27. את הברכה אשר וגו׳, very significantly it does not say here, as it does in the following verse at the curse, אם תשמעו but אשר תשמעו. The actual fulfilment of God’s commands is already in itself a real part of the blessing, which not only follows the obedience but starts to be realised by and with the carrying out of the mitzva. The mental and moral act which is accomplished every time we faithfully obey the Torah is itself a blessed progress, a step forward of our whole being, and with every mitzva-act we bless ourselves.

היום is always said also with consideration of all contemporary moments in which the Words of God are read, בכל יום יהיו בעיניך כחדשים, every day they are to be considered by you as fresh as if they were just spoken “to-day”.

V. 28. והקללה אם וגו׳, but קללה, the positive loss of all one’s own value, the retrogression to absolute zero of one’s position in life only comes as the result of the disobedience. וסרתם וגו׳ ללכת אחרי וגו׳, every step away from the Torah is a step towards עבודה זרה. In the Sifri it says: מכאן אמרו כל המודה בע״ז ככופר בכל התורה כולה וכל הכופר בע״ז כמודה בכל התורה כולה, “from these words it follows that every acknowledgment of idolatry is to be considered equal to a denial of the whole Torah, and every denial of idolatry equal to an acknowledgment of the whole Torah”. We do not consider it superfluous to remark how, after all, these sentences wish to say the exact contrary of that supposed maxim that “belief in One God” is sufficient to qualify a person as a complete Jew even if otherwise he turns his back to the fulfilling of the dictates of the Torah. For here it is the acknowledgment of the whole of the Torah—which indeed means that one is in duty bound to fulfil all God’s commands—which is made inseparable from acknowledgment of the Unity of God or denying it. The Jewish “belief in God” is not the mere belief in the existence of God but in His rule over us, which, of course, is inseparable from our submission to His control. And the Jewish “belief in the Oneness of God” (our oft-repeated sentence of שמע I.L.) is קבלת עול מלכות שמים, is identical with submitting the whole of our fate and the whole of our actions under the rule of the One God, so that כפירת ע״ז denial of a plurality of gods, is identical with הודאה לכל התורה כולה, with acknowledging the whole of the Torah. Denial of the Jewish belief in there being only One God, recognising another besides, or beside Him is literally עבודה זרה “submission to another one”, a withdrawal of our existence and mode of life from the exclusive dictates of the Only One, so that הודאה בע״ז is identical with כפירה בכל התורה כולה. And as a matter of fact the source from which those sentences were deduced, מכאן אמרו leaves no room for the slightest doubt on the matter. Their source, our verse here: וסרתם מן הדרך וגו׳ ללכת אהרי א׳ א׳ does express the identification of one who is הודאה בע״ז with כפירת התורה inasmuch as it recognises every deviation from the way of the Torah as stepping on the road of ע״ז (see on Numb. 15,31 for the reasoning behind the sentence: מומר להכעיס אפילו לדבר אהד הרי הוא כעע״ז.

אשר לא ידעתם expresses the thoughts of how completely irrational ע״ז should be to them. God the Only One had given evidence of Himself and His relation to your fate and your behaviour in a thousand different ways which you had experienced. What manifestation have you had of any known rule or dictates from any other Power of nature or the world?

V. 29. ונתתה. The second person singular is stressed. When they come into the Land the whole nation as such, as the representative of God, is publicly to place the alternative of blessing or curse which God had put before them, i.e. to proclaim it for each one to decide, and thereby to proclaim that the realisation of the Torah by all of them was that on which the national welfare and the granting of their common national requests depended. As Ch. XXIX further specifies the whole nation, one half on Mount Gerisim and the other half on Mt. Ebal, had to place themselves about the priests and Levites who were congregated in the valley between the two hills and have the blessings and the curses recited by the Levites, and make that pronouncement as being said by themselves by their responding “Amen” to each blessing and each curse. Accordingly the people stood on Gerisim and Ebal and presented the alternative of blessing or curse to themselves and to all contemporary and future members of the nation. To pronounce the blessings the Levites turned towards Gerisim, for the curses towards Ebal. Blessings and curse, as we shall see, were represented materially by the contrasting aspect of these two mountains. The nation stood on both mountains, and standing on Girisim it signified the blessing, on Ebal, the curse, that is what is meant by ונתת את הברכה על הר גריזים ואת הקללה על הר עיבל.

Gerisim and Ebal are two peaks of the Ephraim range of mountains which still show a striking contrast in their appearance. Gerisim to the south of the valley of Schechem presents a smiling green slope rising in fruit-covered terraces to its summit, Ebal on the north side, steep, bare and bleak, some 2,900 ft. high, slightly higher than Gerisim. The two mounts lying next to each other form accordingly a most speaking instructive picture of blessing and curse. They both rise on one and the same soil, both are watered by one and the same fall of rain and dew, the same air breathes over both of them, the same pollen wafts over both of them and yet Ebal remains in barren bleakness while Gerisim is clad to its summit in embellishment of vegetation. In the same way, blessing and curse are not conditional on external circumstances but on our own inner receptivity for the one or the other, on our behaviour towards that which is to bring blessing.

Crossing the Jordan and treading the soil of the Land of the Torah, the sight of these two mounts preaches to us the eternal sermon:- that we are placed between the alternative of blessing or curse, and by our own moral behaviour we have to decide for ourselves for a Gerisim or Ebal future.

Abraham also came first to this place in the Holy Land and built there his first altar to God Who appeared to him again there, and, as we already remarked on Gen. 12,6 & 7 (refer to it) it is not unlikely that just on account of this “teaching” nature of the place it bears the name מורה.

V. 30. הלא המה indicates that these mounts were not unknown. Their characteristic contrasting difference, as well as the fact mentioned above that they were the first place which Abraham marked the revelation of God to him, by building an altar, and the name which the district bore on account of its significance could well account for their being known to the people. אחרי דרך מבוא השמש in a westerly direction, further on to the west, where in fact we have to look for אלוני מורה which, according to Gen. 12,6 lay in the district of Schechem. Rashi remarks that אחרי is separated from דרך by the accentuation and so must be taken by itself מופלג and be understood as “beyond”, further on, not directly at the Jordan. מבוא השמש quite definitely means sunset—ממזרח שמש עד מבואו.

In Sifri and also in Sota 33,b, there is a difference of opinion between ר׳ יהודה and ר׳ אלעזר regarding the position of the place described here. ר׳ יהודה understands it to be at a distance from the Jordan in the neighbourhood of Schechem, where indeed Gerisim and Ebal do in fact lie. But according to ר׳ אלעזר the place here for the proclamation of the blessings and curses was directly at the Jordan where one had to build up two mounds of earth artificially to represent Gerisim and Ebal (see תוספות there according to the Jerusalemi). Now the saying of ר׳ יהודה runs: הלא המה בעבר הירדן מעבר הירדן ואילך ואחרי דרך מבוא השמש מקום שהשמש זורחת, just as that of הלא המה -:ר׳ אלעזר בעבר הירדן, סמוך לירדן אחרי דרך מבוא השמש מקום שהחמה שוקעת According to ר׳ יהודה the west is indicated as turned away from the east, to ר׳ אלעזר, the east, as turned away from the west. It only remains difficult to understand how ר׳ יהודה can interpret מבוא השמש as מקום שהשמש זורחת, as Rashi takes its meaning to be, while מבוא השמש is everywhere given in contrast to מזרח השמש. We venture therefore to believe that ר׳ יהודה takes his מקום זריחת השמש not from מבוא השמש but from דרך מבוא השמש, the road that goes to the west. This road leading to the west naturally begins in the east, מקום זריחת השמש and אחרי דרך מבוא השמש after one has gone through this road lying in the east in a westerly direction one comes to the mounts Gerisim and Ebal. But according to ר׳ אלעזר one stops אחרי behind the דרך מבוא השמש, one does not go along this westerly road, remains “behind” the מקום שהשמש שוקעת, back in the east next to the Jordan. Both take מבוא השמש to be the west, and the difference lies in the way they take אחרי, “back from the west road”. According to ר׳ יהודה this road was left in the east, i.e. one went through it to the west, according to ר׳ אלעזר it was left in the west, i.e. one did not pass along it. This would solve the difficulties to which the מהרש״א already refers and would also justify Rashi’s commentary on the Pentateuch and would only make him not agree with what he says on the Gemora, but that could easily be explained by Rashi’s not keeping to his explanation there, because he took it as hardly thinkable that ר׳ יהודה would take מבוא השמש to refer to sunrise.

V. 31 & 32. כי “for”, this proclamation of the happiness or unhappiness of your future being dependent on your fulfilling or not fulfilling God’s Torah is to be one of your very first acts at your taking possession of the land; for you only receive the land to fulfil this Torah, its being fulfilled is the sole purpose of your taking possession of it.

But whereas in the last part of the preceding introductory speech this realisation of the Torah is repeatedly described in the ideal aspect of its highest fulfilment לאהבה את ה׳ א׳ ללכת בכל דרכיו ולדבקה בו (“to love our God, to walk in all His ways and to keep close to Him”), here the first indispensable conditions הקים ומשפטים, the laws of morality and social equity are stressed, the fulfilment or non-fulfilment of which decides in the very first place the blessing or otherwise of the land. Altogether in the following is told how the Torah is to be taken to heart in general in the wider sense of תקים and משפטים, as God’s laws which set the sphere and the limit for all our internal and external activities. Accordingly: חק to draw the circle within which the activity is a duty, and beyond which it is a sin; and at the same time as משפטים, as the laws of equity, by keeping of which all the human world around us and all the tasks set for us become just and fair; and how by their non-observance we sin against all these laws. As חקים, through them we do justice to God and ourselves, as משפטים to God and our world, and by both of them our claim for lasting happiness and well-being stands and falls.
V. 1. אלה החקים. Here the real compendium of the laws for taking the land into possession begins. אלה החקים etc. see at end of previous chapter.

V. 2. אבד גו׳. The first task is to clear the land from all traces of polytheism. The land is to be the Land of the One God and His Torah, it may bear no reminder of any contrary way of looking at the world and life. אבד תאבדון every trace must be eradicated: מכאן לעוקד ע״ז שצריך לשרש אחריה (Avoda Zara 45,b).

המקמות. We have already remarked on Ch. 7,25 and VII,5, that everything, כל שאין בו תפיסת ידי אדם, “that has not been handled by man” that is מחובר, joined to the ground, which does not belong to the nature of things fashioned by man, does not become אסור (prohibited to be used I.L.) by polytheistic misuse. Such things do not really become absorbed into human possessions by human ownership, until they are detached from the soil and pass actually into human hands they reach beyond and above any belonging to Man and therefore cannot receive the איסור character through Man. This rule is closely connected with that other one: אין אדם אוסר דבר שאינו שלו that no man can impart the character of איסור on any object which does not belong to him. Mountains, springs, trees which were not planted for idolatry purposes were therefore not אסור even if they were worshipped or used for idolatrous rites, although of course any participation in the rites of such a cult would be punishable העכו״ם העובדים .ע״ז את ההרים ואת הגבעות הן מותרין ועובדיהן בסייף (Avouda Zara 46,a). But if a human being had made any alterations to them then they too would be אע״פ שאמרו המשתחוה לקרקע עולם לא אסרה חפר בה בורות שיהין ומערות .אסור אסרה. (ibid 54,b), similarly to this it is said referring to דבר שאינו שלו (Chulin 40,a). אע״פ שאמרו המשתחוה לבהמת חברו לא אסרה, עשה בה מעשה אסרה (still see הל׳ ע״ז ,רמב״ם 8,1 and ראב״ד thereon).

On this verse it is taught in Avouda Zara 45,a: אבד תאבדון את כל המקומות אשר עבדו וגו׳ אלהיהם על ההרים ולא ההרים אלהיהם אלהיהס על הגבעות ולא גבעות אלהיהם: Here we are commanded to destroy the gods which they worship on the mountains and hills but are not commanded to destroy the mountains or hills if these should be worshipped as gods, and needless then to say if, as our text says, they are only places where idol worship is practised. If nevertheless it does say in our text: אבד תאבדון את כל המקומות אשר עבדו שם הגוים וגו׳ את אלהיהם על ההרים וגו׳ that the “places” are to be destroyed where the nations worshipped their gods on the mountains, this is understood (ibid 51,b) to כלים שנשתמשו בהן לע״ז to offering-utensils and implements which are used for the cults of idol-worship and mark the places on the mountains and hillocks where the rites are performed. Even if such utensils and appurtenances of idolatry had been built in or pent up into the mountain itself, they still retained the mobile תלוש-character and came under the איסור-prohibition and the אבוד-command, for regarding ע״ז, we apply תלוש ולבסוף חברו כתלוש דמי (Chulin 16,a). And equally so, as ריםב״א on ע״ז (ibid), remarks, the altars and mounds which are set up for offerings to gods would also have to be destroyed, just as the Halacha quoted above says .חפר בה וגו׳ אסרה אבד תאבדון את כל המקומות וגו׳ accordingly does not apply to the hill itself but only to such places on it which are marked on it by the appurtenances of the cults or which have been built up to serve as altars. Cf. on Ch. 7,25

לענין כלים שנשתמשו למחובר יש סתירה בין תוספו׳ חולין מ׳ א׳ ד״ה הא דאמר להר ובין תוספות ע״ז נ״ב א׳ ד״ה תנהו ענין לכלים. לתוספות דע״ז פי׳ לכלים שנשתמשו בהן לע״א הכתוב מדבר כלומר שנשתמשו להרים אלהיהם דהיינו מחובר ואם כן כלים שנשתמשו למחובר אסורים ולתוספות דחולין אדרבא מוכח משם דכלים שנשתמשו למחובר מותרים ובכלים שנשתמשו בהן לע״א הכתוב מדבר רצונו לומר שנשתמשו לאלהיהם על ההרים .ולא להרים אלהיהם ופירוש זה נראה יותר מסוגית הגמרא ע״ש ודו״ק

על ההרים וגו׳. High mountains are the physical “mothers” of life on earth. They absorb and gather the atmospheric precipitations and lead them down to the lowlands which they are to fructify. They also attract the electrical discharges from the clouds. Possibly the root הרר is related to הרה as שסם to דמם ,שסה to קצץ ,דמה to קצה etc. and mountains received their name from their receptivity for life to be transmitted to the earth. The heights sink down into hills for man to be able to cultivate them, and with hills the real soil for human beings to use has its beginning.

עץ רענן, an analogy for רען could be found in the rabbinic term רהן which refers to an object handed over which eventually is to remain permanently where it is deposited: עץ רענן .הרהינו אצלו would then be a tree of which it can be assumed will keep its colourful adornment, an evergreen tree. Heathen cults of the gods had places where the forces of nature showed itself in special power, such places were specially favoured for the worship of the gods of nature.

V. 3. ונתצתם וגו׳. You are to eradicate the traces of heathenism in the land, of its worship מזבחותם, its traditions מצבותם, and its superstitions ואשריהם תשרפון באש .אשריהם when the tree had originally been planted for ע׳ז, and if, above, it says ואשריהם תגדעון in Ch. 7,5 according to which the trunk may be left standing, that speaks of a tree which was planted בהיתר and afterwards became sacred to ע״ז, an אילן שנטעו ולבסוף עבדו at which only that which grew afterwards becomes אסור (see ibid).

לכנות לה שם ,ואבדתם את שמם מן המקום ההוא, by changing the name if the place is called by the name of the deity whose rites were celebrated there, and indeed by giving it a derogatory name לגנאי (Avouda Zara 46,a).

V. 4. לא תעשון כז וגו׳. Just as you must eradicate the very last trace of the heathen gods, so per contra, not the slightest of anything that bears the name of God or is consecrated to Him may be destroyed. Thus in the first place would come the אזהרה למוחק את השם, the prohibition of erasing the Name of God or even a single letter of it (Makkus 22,a). Seven such names come under this category of שמות שאינן נמחקים viz. שם ,שם ההויה צבאות ,שדי ,אלקים ,אלוה ,אל ,אדנות, and also the suffixes attached to them as ך ,כם from אלקיך ,אלקיכם etc. A prefix as ל from לה׳ or ב from בה׳ etc. may be erased. Attributes to God as הגדול ,הגבור ,הנורא etc. do not come under this prohibition (Shevouth 35,a). The slightest damage to the building of the Temple or the Altar, נותץ אבן אחד מן ההיכל ומן המזבח ומן העזרות or destroying any of the wood for the offerings שורף עצי קדשים would also transgress this prohibition (Sifri on this verse), such destroying places and objects consecrated to God would be what the prohibition meant to include in the prohibition by the context in which it is given.

V. 5. כי אם וגו׳, not only are you not to destroy anything that bears the name of your God, but the place which God will choose as bearer of His Name shall be held by all to be the highest centre-point of your lives which invites you all to national union round about God and His Torah. But the order is at once added that the choice of a place dedicated to bear the name of our God is not to be made by our own subjective ideas—as were the places of the gods which we were to eradicate completely from our land—but was made dependent on the express choice of God Himself. We have not to dedicate a place for God, but He has to indicate to us the place which He fixes for His Sanctuary and to be our rallying point round about Him and His Sanctuary.

מכל שבטיכם, from all and for all. Hence at the future acquisition of the place chosen by God to be the national Sanctuary for all Israel, all the tribes had to act in conjunction with each other. When Jerusalem was shown to be that place by the word of the Prophet of God and by the cessation of the plague there, David bought it from its previous owners (the Jebusites I.L.) for six hundred shekels. He paid fifty on behalf of himself and his tribe of Judah and raised an equal amount from each of the other tribes (cf. Sam. II, XXIV,24 and Chron. I, XXI,25 and Sifri thereon,—see Zebachim 116,b.).

לשכנו תדרשו. You are to enquire from a manifestation of His Presence, דרוש על פי נביא (find out what the Prophet of God has to say, Sifri), wait for an announcement from God, and then ובאת שמה, assemble thither in national unity. לשכנו (see Gen. at end of notes on IX,27 and Ex. on XXV,8).

V. 6. והבאתם שמה. Not only ובאת שמה, not only the procession of you yourselves and your personal relationship to God and the Sanctuary of His Torah is to proceed thither, but with every “coming”, a “bringing” is to be combined. You are to bring with you the expression of the dedication of your actions and of the harmony of your family life: עולותיכם וזבחיכם, of the prosperity of your animal stock and agricultural products: מעשר בהמה ומעשר שני ,מעשרותיכם: the expression of the whole of your landed possessions belonging to God and dedicated to the purposes of His Torah, בכורים :תרומת ידכם, as well as what you have vowed to bring because of some special necessity to express your devotion: נדריכם ונדבותיכם, and, as the fundamental and final expression of all these homage-paying dedications, that of your live-stock belonging to God and dedicated to His purposes, in offering their first-born: בכורות בקרכם וצאנכם—by which indeed Israel is always to keep in mind the experience of its national birth-right, how the most advanced and mightiest state with all its culture collapses if it is in obstinate opposition to the Will of God, and only faithful obedience to duty can maintain it, ויהי כי הקשה פרעה לשלחנו וגו׳ על כן (Ex. 13,15). With all these are you to trek up to the one national home of the Sanctuary of the Torah which bears God’s Name to proclaim that you yourself with all the actions of your life and all your fortune and fate belong to God and are dedicated to Him and His Torah.

בשני מעשרות הכ׳ מדבר אחד מעשר דגן ואחד מעשר בהמה :מעשרותיכם: See Ch. 14,22 et seq. and Levit. 27,32. תרומת ידכם here, v.11, and תרומת ידך in v.17 cannot mean ordinary תרומה which is never referred to by this name, as all תרומה has to be given to a כהן and moreover may be eaten by him anywhere whereas v.17 explicitly forbids תרומת ידך to be eaten outside Jerusalem. Hence תרומת ידכם is understood to be בכורים כענין שנאמר ולקח הכהן הטנא מידך והניחו לפני מזבח ה׳ א׳; (Ch. 26,4 Sifri). After all, בכורים, as the avowal which has to be made over them teaches, are the attestation that Israel has to thank God alone for its “hand”, that is, its freedom and its independent possessions, and holds them dedicated to God alone for the fulfilment of His Torah. (look it up there). בכורים are therefore, in the true sense of the word תרומת יד “the elevation of the hand to God” i.e. to express that the “hand” belongs to no other than God, and should be dedicated to none other than God. Bringing the בכורים basket in the hand and laying it down through the priest before God expresses both.

The Sifri takes חטאות and אשמות to be included in בכורות בקרבם וצאנכם. If we consider how the על כן אני זובח quoted above, the בכורות include the most faithful obedience to God, the idea of such an extension to חטאות and אשמות being implicitly understood does not seem far-fetched.

We have already remarked that by pairing ובאת שמה והבאתם שמה the עשה (positive command I.L.) of fulfilling at the first רגל any vow made, is given, although the negative command, the prohibition of delaying it לא תאחר לשלמו (Ch. 23,21) is only transgressed after three רגלים have passed (Levit. 23,38 and see further on Ch. 23,21). Rabbi Akiva teaches further (on Bechoroth 53a) that by combining the two מעשר בהמה מעשר דגן ,מעשרות in one conception and placing them together with בכורות regarding the duty of bringing them to Jerusalem and offering them there, that although מעשר בהמה and בכורות as חובת הגוף (see on Ch. 11,18), not being connected with the ground, and being also applicable בחוצה לארץ, still, as nevertheless they are placed together with מעשר דגן regarding the Land, that as although they are קדוש even outside לארץ they are still not brought on the altar, but are נאכלים במומן לבעלים.

V. 7. ואכלתם שם וגו׳ ושמחתם וגו׳. This feasting and this living and joy of life in the Presence of God in the vicinity of His Sanctuary of the Torah in which the Jewish “worship of God” reaches its highest point is one of the most characteristic features of Judaism. It differs, equally sharply from ancient heathenism, whose gods, born of fear, are enemies of cheerfulness and undisturbed happiness of human beings, as from that modern erroneous idea which teaches that one can only seek to get near to God with the “spirit”, the serious solemn aspect of life, but relegates the life of the senses to the unconsecrated lower side of life.—משלח ידכם with the whole of that over which your hand has power, i.e. with all that is at your disposal, that you can use and dispose of as you wish, on which you may be שולח יד, lay your hands on. Thus אדום ומואב משלוח ידם (Is. 11,14) (“Edom and Moab will then be at their disposal” I.L.). אשר ברכך ה׳ וגו׳, the real core of your joy lies in the fact that you may consider all that you possess as God’s blessing, accordingly, as proof of His satisfaction. This feeling of having God’s approval is the purest joy of our lives; and no egoistic personal way of thinking can attain this feeling, only in joining in with the community is it to be found, in the consciousness that the weal of each individual is only to be sought in participation in the general well-being of the whole community, hence ושמחתם (plural I.L.) etc., אשר ברכך (sing. I.L.).

V. 8. לא תעשון וגו׳: As is clear from Levit. Ch. XVII, in the wilderness too every offering was forbidden to be brought anywhere outside the שחוטי חוץ ,אהל מועד; more, as was explained there, according to the generally accepted opinion of ר׳ ישמעאל, during the whole of the wandering in the wilderness, once the Sanctuary had been erected, בשר תאוה the killing of animals which could be brought as offerings just for ordinary eating was altogether prohibited, but every such animal had to be brought on the altar as שלמים in the אהל מועד, to which the text in verses 20 and 21 of our chapter here refers. So that regarding the Sanctuary and procedures to be performed outside it, the generation of the wandering in the wilderness was far more restricted than at any later period. Hence איש כל הישר בעיניו cannot possibly refer to the freedom enjoyed by the people Moses was addressing at the time, when איש כל הישר בעיניו was allowed less than ever. Accordingly those words are taken in the Gemora to be understood as a definition of the authority given as beginning with the entry into the Land.

If we consider the fact that the real command to bring all offerings to the one place chosen by God, and none to be brought outside it, is only given in verses 10-14, then we shall understand verses 6 and 7 more as being just as characterising and giving the purpose of that chosen place, the announcement of which we are commanded to wait for and enquire after in v. 5. In contrast to the way we are to behave towards heathenism, the last traces of whose holy places and emblems we are to eradicate from the memory of our people (verses 2 and 3), we are told (verses 4-7) that not only may we not damage it as long as it exists, but even before it is there, we are to expect and wait for a holy place for our feasting and enjoyment before the Presence of God; which place to bear His Name must be chosen and fixed by God Himself; and so this place of the Name of God, even in the mere expectation, the דרוש לשכנו of v. 5, is to exert an effective influence on our behaviour.

Now to this דרוש לשכנו verse 8 then attaches itself, and says:- during this time of דרישה לשכנו, and until God by revelation of His Presence will again have fixed a centrepoint for the nation when it has settled in the Land, as the Tabernacle was in their midst during the time of their wanderings, during that time לא תעשון ככל אשר אנחנו עושים פה היום, “You may not do as we do here now”. You may not bring in the places which you temporarily may have chosen for yourselves to be offering-places, all the offerings which we do here in the Tabernacle which wandered with us everywhere in our wanderings and proclaimed the Presence of God and His Torah in the centre of our camp. But in those places you may only bring איש כל הישר בעיניו. Just as the place is one of your own choosing so there you may only bring offerings of your own choice, of your own free-will, נדרים ונדבות, but not obligatory-offerings as חטאות אמר להו משה לישראל כי עליתו לארץ ישרות תקריבו חובות לא תקריבו ;ואשמות (Zebachim 114a; also see Sifri on our verse). But this limitation only applies to איש, individuals, but צבור, the community brings at all times, in the משכן, wherever it happened to be, all קרבנוח צבור all the communal offerings just as it did in אהל מועד שבמדבר (Zebachim 18,a). But during those intermediary periods, individuals were only allowed to bring נדרים ונדבות even in the משכן (also called במת צבור or במה גדולה) (ibid).

V. 9. עד עתה, at the time of this provisional state when the nation is already settled but the משכן has not yet become permanently stable. The term עתה could all the more be used as indeed actually at the time Moses was speaking neither מנוחה nor נחלה was there yet. מנוחה, the political rest, as occurred after the greater part of the Land had been taken into possession under Joshuah; for then the משכן received in Shilo its first permanent resting place (where it remained till the destruction of Shilo by the Philistines in Eli’s time I.L.), after it had been in Gilgal during the fourteen years of conquering and dividing the Land, שבע שכבשו ושבע שחלקו (Jos. 18,1); ויקהלו כל עדת בני ישראל אל שלה וישכינו שם את אהל נחלה .מועד והארץ נכבשה לפניהם, after the last possession of the Land with Jerusalem was obtained under David. Shilo was a transitory מנוחה which was already indicated from the beginning by its external construction. ולא היה שם תקרה אלא בית אבנים בלבד מלמטן והיריעות מלמעלן, it was only a solid building at the base, above it was still only covered by the curtains of the Taberncale (Zebachim 112,b), which is why it is called both “house” ותביאהו בית ה׳ שילה (Sam. I, I,24) and “tent” ויטש משכן שילה אהל שכן באדם (Ps. 78,60), וימאס באהל יוסף (ibid 67). Jerusalem was נחלה, the everlasting heritage. Even at the time of its fall God still calls it “His heritage”; עזבתי את ביתי נטשתי את נחלתי וגו׳ היתה לי נחלתי כאריה ביער וגו׳ העיט צבוע נחלתי לי וגו׳ (Jer. 12,7-9 and Zebachim 119,a).

After crossing the Jordan, during the period of conquest and division of the Land the אהל מועד, the במת צבור, the במה גדולה was in Gilgal. במות throughout the Land were allowed to be used for private individual offerings of עולות and שלמים. This היתר במות lasted fourteen years. After that the Sanctuary was three hundred and ninety six years in Shilo, and נאסרו הבמות, the במות were forbidden to be used until the death of Eli and the fall of Shilo. Then for fifty seven years במות were again permitted while the אהל מועד was in Nob and Gibeon until finally the temple was built in Jerusalem under Solomon whereby the prohibition to use במות came into force for ever. (Zebachim 118a, and 119a).

We have tried to work out, in Ex. on Ch. 27,8 and in Levit. on Ch. 17,3-9, the conception “במה״ in contrast to מזבח and the sin that lay in offering on במות at the time when it was prohibited to do so, בשעת איסור במות. We found that only at the place of the national Sanctuary of God, erected to His Torah, is the assurance given that the one who brings his offering places his consciousness of God on the basis of the revelation of God at Sinai being guaranteed for by the whole nation, as well as the conviction that nearness to God (which is what an offering קרבן means I.L.) can only be sought by devotion to all the traditional laws handed down from God to the nation. For both of these the במת יחיד lacks any expression of definite acceptance. The God to Whom he dedicates his offering can be the One Unique and Only God of Judaism, but He can be at the same time coincident with שערים על פני השדה, the physical life of Nature, the deepest erroneous conception of heathenism. But, above all, the Bama lacks all relation to the Torah, and an offering brought to God בחוץ at the time of איסור במה becomes just a defection from the Torah which God has set for all time as the one medium between us and Himself. How deeply the Bama-sin—after the איסור במות—undermines the faithful attachment to duty of the members of the nation and opens wide the gate to the most pernicious subjectivity (the condition of viewing things exclusively through the medium of one’s own mind and opinion I.L.) is clear from the state of deterioration in the time of the kings at which nothing is so repeatedly stressed as the fact and complaint that the “Bamath were not taken away, the people still sacrificed the burnt incense on the Bamath” (Kings I. 22,44; II, XII,4; XIV,4; XV,4, 35).

After all this one has not got to go far to see the reason for the absolute prohibition of the Bamath, as well as for the restriction even in times of היתר במות to such offerings as עולות ושלמים which have the character of free-will offerings and the exclusion of חטאות ואשמות which have special relation to the dictates of the Torah to which the private Bama has no reference. But one still has to consider, firstly, why, as soon as, and as long as, the divine Sanctuary of the Torah had no permanent place, Bamath were allowed at all, and secondly, during those periods why, in the divine Sanctuary of the Torah itself, on the public Bama, the Altar, while the national community could bring obligatory offerings, especially שקבוע להן זמן, but individuals were in no wise allowed to bring their obligatory offerings, their חטאות and אשמות.

The משכן, erected by the nation in the wilderness at God’s behest retained, wherever it happened to be, the character of the national Sanctuary, in which, at the times fixed by God, the nation was to express in the deeply significant prescribed procedures of the prescribed offerings again and again the demands on the fulfilment of which the proximity of God in the nation, the realisation of ועשו לי מקדש ושכנתי בתוכם, depended.

But so that this Sanctuary shall fulfil its purpose of sanctifying the whole life of the people, so that it, and with it the Torah which forms its essential content, becomes the centre point elevated above the nation and its individuals, drawing everything and everybody up to it, uniting everything and everybody in equal obligation to dutifulness, and affecting everything and everybody with equal responsibility, nothing at all, and least of all, no fraction of the nation, may step in between God with His Torah and each individual with his duty. The man with the consciousness of his guilt and of his necessity to seek the atoning nearness of God (קרבן I.L.) may not go to any place of a Sanctuary not indicated by God Himself but appointed by some incidental choice, not to Gilgal, Nob or Gibeon, also not to Shilo or Jerusalem as such, as cities of Ephraim or Judah, but must pilgrim up to the place God has appointed to be the “bearer of His Name”, to be the Sanctuary of His Torah, of which place He has said פה אשב כי אויתיה, from which He wishes the sanctifying force of His Sanctuary of the Torah to go forth.

Accordingly as long as the משכן only has the bama-character of a במת צבור, individuals have not to bring their חטאות ואשמות thither. More, according to one opinion, even the צבור may not bring חטאות for specific sins perpertrated against the Torah, חטאות שאין קבוע להן זמן as פר העלם דבר של צבור and שעירי ע״ז: for it is only in קרבנות שקבוע להן זמן with which the nation expresses its everlasting mission and task that the nation stands there for the Torah, purely as its representative and depository (as we have repeatedly explained at the festival offerings, the חטאות are admonitions to stay at the moral heights reached and not to slip down from them, rather than sin-offerings for specific sins committed I.L.). But for actual sins committed, the community or nation stands in exactly the same relationship to the Torah as the individual and requires to keep its eminence and loftiness as a nation intact over the nation. Quite in the same trend of thought could the permission to use a private Bama בשעת היתר במות be understandable. Just because the משכן also only bore the character of a Bama, and God had not yet appointed the place where His “Name”—which fundamentally is equivalent to His “Torah” (see Chron. I, XIII,6)—was to be found, and individuals also could go there only to God and not specifically with his relationships to the Torah, God—so as to speak—can be found anywhere and everywhere and the private Bama is allowed to be used for נדרים ונדבות. This very permission itself keeps the consciousness alive in the minds of the whole nation that the contemporary place of the Sanctuary is still not the one chosen by God, that not yet have they come אל המנוחה ואל הנחלה, that לשכנו תדרשו ובאת שמה, that it is still the task for all ranks of the nation “to enquire for the place of God” and to wait for the “manifestation of the Presence of God”, by which God will just indicate the place as “His place”, as this “seeking” and this “announcement” is proclaimed in David’s upward-rising song (Ps. CXXXII). The place which was finally chosen by God to remain as נחלת ה׳ for all time as the place for the Sanctuary of His Torah turned out to be just the one which, with its historical significance reaching back far beyond every contemporary time of the nation, back to its origin, yea, in the traditions preserved in it, back to the early beginnings of the human race. Accordingly, treading on its site teaches every generation to consider itself as the heirs and bearers of the national calling, yea, of the mission of the whole of humanity, and to look on the Jewish mission as being merely a return to the original state of Man being in the proximity of God, and as the restorer of that condition to the world in general. The actual spot of the Mount of Moriah, where according to tradition Noah and Adam also built their Altar expresses by its human historic memories that מציון תצא תורה and ביתי בית תפלה יקרא לכל העמים.

V. 10 & 11. ועברתם וגו׳ וישבתם וגו׳ וישבתם בטח וגו׳ והיה וגו׳. The choosing of a place for God’s Sanctuary of His Torah to be the permanent eternal point of union for the nation is appointed as the final crowning act of the complete possession of the Land. Like the choice of a king (Ch. 17,15), the choice of the fixed place for the Temple is also only to follow the complete conquest and security of the Land, and indeed, according to Sanhedrin 20,b, the building of the Temple is to come last. Both, King and God’s Presence in the Temple, are not of importance so much for external affairs, for the protection and maintenance of the country against external enemies, as for the internal realisation of the national mission within the Land as promulgated by the Torah. This was also taken by David as being the time that had arrived to erect a permanent building for the Sanctuary of God. ויהי כי ישב המלך בביתו וה׳ הניח לו מסביב מכל איביו ויאמר המלך אל נתן הנביא וגו׳ (Sam. II, VII,1) (“And it came to pass when the king was settled in his house and God had given him rest from all his enemies all round that the king said to Nathan the prophet etc.” I.L.). And there in God’s speech through Nathan, the building of that permanent place for the Temple is brought into close connection with the meaning of the permanent establishment of the dynasty of David for Israel, yea, as is evident from David’s effusion, for the ultimate future of mankind—וזאת תורת האדם (V. 19)—a connection which could throw a still clearer light on the לשכנו תדרשו of our text. The permanent Place of God is not chosen until the man is found who could be deemed worthy that he and his descendants could become the national head for the realisation of the national mission which emanates from the Sanctuary of the Torah. The building of a solid Temple designates at the same time the tribe in whose domain it stood as being such in whose midst the permanent line of regal leadership of the nation lies. Therefore, as it says there in verses 6 and 7 “did I wander among the tribes of Israel in a tent and in a Tabernacle” and demanded from no contemporary tribe elected to leadership, the building of a solid Temple until He “found” (Ps. 89,21) David who showed himself worthy of this permanent leadership. The Tent (no solid roof or walls I.L.) at Shilo and the היתר במות were just so many signs that the nation had still to wait for the right leader and the real permanent everlasting place for the Sanctuary of God.

את כל אשר אנכי מצוה אתכם, both obligatory as well as free will offerings—וכל מבחר נדריכם, does not mean the choice i.e. the best of what you have vowed but what you have chosen, picked out to dedicate to God from your possessions. This implication is given hereby that, to fufil a vow to give something for a holy purpose, one should pick out the very best possible (see Kerithoth 27a.).

V. 12. ושמחתם וגו׳. Accordingly taking your complete household with you with all your dependants, out of the decentralisation to the centre point. It is just having the happy family life in the Presence of God in the surroundings of His Torah.

והלוי אשר בשעריכם. It seems to be taken for granted that the Levites, although provided by the Torah with cities in which to reside, would still live scattered amongst the other inhabitants. They would pilgrim up with the families and should participate in the meals of the family-offerings.

V. 13. השמר לו. This is the actual prohibition, the אזהרה, of שחיטה והעלאה בחוץ, to which the punishment of כרת had already been ascribed in Levit. 17,8 and 9 (refer to there). This is in accordance with the rule: — כל מקום שנאמר השמר פן ואל אינו אלא לא תעשה (Zebachim 106,a).

V. 14. כי אם במקום וגו׳ שם תעלה וגו׳ ושם תעשה וגו׳. Here, according to Zebachim 107,b, the prescribed procedure for the offerings are taken in two separate categories: העלאה, comprising הקטרת אברים ואימורים; and עשיה, the שחיטה וזריקת הדם and שחט וזרק והעלה בחוץ חייב שתים. Seeking to get near to God with giving up and devoting our spiritual inner self our נפש or seeking to get near to God with all our will and actions is pinned strictly down to the one Sanctuary dedicated to the divine Torah. Only the Torah elevates our soul to God, and only the Torah gives our will and what we accomplish consecration and importance.
