And the prohibition for all time laid down in verses 13 and 14 here not to do any sacrificial act outside the place on Mount Moria dedicated for all time to God’s Torah, by its negative binding force makes even the ruined bleak spot of our past and future Sanctuary into the invisible spiritual high centre-point from where the divine Torah embraces every true son of the People of God with untearable bonds to spiritual unity. And in its ruins it has proved its mastery on the dispersed nation of its power of winning hearts and minds even more gloriously than in the brightest days of its past existence, כסא כבוד מדום מראשון מקום מקדשנו (“A throne of glory, higher than the first, the very place of our Sanctuary remains” Jer. 17,12).

V. 15. רק בכל אות נפשך וגו׳. We have already remarked on Levit. 17,3, that according to the teaching of ר׳ ישמעאל—which is predominantly accepted—during the period of the wandering in the wilderness where the whole nation lived constantly in the immediate neighbourhood of the Sanctuary, בשר תאוה i.e. eating meat of animals that were able to be brought as offerings, but had not been, was prohibited. That was only allowed to be done with the settling down in the Land. This permission to slaughter such animals, i.e. מבקרך וצאנך for ordinary food without having to bring them first to the Temple as offerings, which was to start with the people settling in the Land right up to its borders far away from the Temple is given expressly in verses 20 and 21, the text of which clearly states the new law in connection with the altered condition of the position where the people were living. But here it is speaking of the slaughter of animals that had been fit for offerings, and as such had been dedicated to be offered, but in the meantime had been rendered unfit through a מום קבוע (Levit. 22,12 et seq.), פסולי מוקדשים, the slaughtering of which for ordinary food—after they had been redeemed (Levit. 27,11 & 12)—was permitted even during the איסור בשר תאוה in the wilderness, just as צבי ואיל (venison I.L.) was allowed כי אסר רחמנא בהמה דחזיא להקרבה אבל דלא חזיא להקרבה לא אסר רחמנא (Chulin, 17,a). And it is of such animals that here the law is given which differentiates them on the one hand from קדשים and on the other from חולין (see Sifri hereon). The traits by which they still retain some of their original קדשים character even after redemption are all contained in the sentence in Chulin 130,a:- כל שקדם הקדשן את מומן או מום עובר קודם להקדשן ולאחר מכאן נולד להם מום קבוע ונפדו פטורין מן הבכורה ומן המתנות ואינן יוצאין לחולין להגזז ולהעבד וולדן וחלבן אסור לאחר פדיונם ואם מתו יקברו.

All these points are indicated in our text תזבח ולא גיזה בשר ולא חלב ואכלת ולא לכלבים מכאן שאין פודין את קדשים להאכיל לכלבים, only slaughtering and eating the meat yourself is allowed but regarding the use of the fleece or working the animal, the prohibition given for קדשים in Ch. 15,19 remains in force (לא תעבד בבכור שורך ולא תגוז בכור צאנך). The rule that לאו הבא מכלל עשה עשה gives these limitations on the full חולין character of these animals the full force of a direct prohibition, although תזבח etc. from which they are derived is couched in positive wording, so that פסולי המוקדשים as far as גיזה ועבודה is concerned retain their קדשים character even after being redeemed, אהדריה קרא לאיסוריה (see תוספות Chulin 98,b. ד״ה רבא and Avouda Zara 67,a, ד״ה יוחנן). In the same way, only eating the meat is allowed but its milk or its young if it was carrying before it was redeemed, remain prohibited. And also, as it says ואכלת, it may only be eaten by human beings, but even if it has become unfit for human consumption, no animal may be fed with it. Finally by its being classed with צבי ואיל it is taught that just like חיה, the duty of בכור and מתנות כהונה (the gift of זרוע לחיים וקיבה Ch. 18,3) does not apply, the same is the case for פסולי מוקדשים שנפדו (Bechoroth 15,a,).

This law which gives permission for the meat of animals which have been dedicated for offerings and then redeemed to be eaten exclusively by human beings, could come, not only from the idea of the dignity of their having been originally dedicated as offerings—which indeed had been withdrawn and transferred to another object by redemption—but also could have in mind the dignity and value of human food as such, which, when primarily shifted to the purpose of offerings allows both offerings and human eating to be recognised in their true light. “What can no longer become אכילת מזבח shall at least become אכילת אדם״. This canon which could summarise the תזבח ולא גיזה ועבודה ואכלת ולא לכלביד, can bring the “Altar” into the sphere of human purposes equally with bringing the “table” into the proximity of the conception of an altar. The purpose of both of them is to further and maintain Man for his spiritual moral calling of a human being, and our ordinary חולין eating, kept within the limits of the Torah and serving the moral purposes of the Torah, becomes itself something holy. For the בשר on the מזבח, the איברים which are given over to the אש דת there to be ריח ניחוח לה׳ are only symbolic of the same איברים which we keep alive by eating our ordinary food just for the service of giving God satisfaction with us on earth. This moral sanctification of our ordinary eating lies so near the idea of this law that the Torah found it necessary to remark that nevertheless the symbolic laws of טומאה and טהרה are not prescribed for our ordinary tables; הטמא והטהור יאכלנו like צבי ואיל which are altogether not able to be brought as offerings. Yea, this closely associating אכילת אדם with אכילת מזבח may also explain why the Torah found it necessary to repeat the איסור אכילת הדם (v. 16) specially for פסולי המוקדשים, wherein then, quite oonsistantly, according to רבא (Bechoroth 15,a) the איסור חלב would also be implied. For both are אכילת מזבח and it is in consideration of that fact that they are forbidden (Levit. 3,16 & 17).

That פסולי המוקדשים שנפדו do not come under the duty of בכור and מתנות could be, at rock bottom, from the same reason which frees not only קדשי מזבח but also קדשי בדק הבית from that duty: מדחה מן הבכורה ומן המתנות (Bechoroth 14,a) for which, according to תוספות there, the reason lies in the command that בכורה and מתנות are to be given only from the sphere of human possessions. In Ch. 18,3 referring to מתנות it says מאת העם, and in Numb. 3,13, גבי בכור it says בישראל. Now פסולי מוקדשים also, even after they have been redeemed do not really belong to the sphere of the possessions of the individual person for he is restricted in their uses. We also thought in Ex. 33,34 that for the same reason we could understand the exclusion of שור פסולי המוקדשים even from the law of פסולי .בור המוקדשים, which the Torah excludes from the right of the owner to גיזה ועבודה, thereby represent their not being entirely and completely within the sphere of human possessions, just as צבי ואיל, wild animals חיה by their natural character do not completely subordinate themselves to the service of Man. פסולי מוקדשים in this respect have the character of חיה and therefore their exclusion from the duty of בכורה and מתנות is laid down by making them equal to צבי ואיל (see Ch. 15,21 & 22).

The Gemora teaches in Makkoth 22,a המרביע שור פסולי המוקדשים לוקה שנים (ממ״ל הל׳ מעילה א׳ ט׳ נראה דלא גרם שנים ע״ש) המנהיג בשור פסולי המוקדשים לוקה שהרי גוף אחד הוא ועשאו הכתוב כשני גופים. So that פסולי המוקדשים שנפדו are considered as כלאים which are אסורים בהרבעה (Levit. 19,19) and בהנהגה (Deut. 22,10), and indeed as Rashi explains the reason עשאן הכתוב כשני גופים, because the חולין and קדשים characters are combined in them they are considered as being two different species the breeding or working together with which is forbidden by the כלאים laws the כשני גופים refers to the text comparing פסולי המוקדשים to צבי ואיל, two different animals to which Bechoroth 33,a. also takes this Gemora to refer. If, as we thought we understood the כלאים laws listed there in Levit. not to be so much an actual unnatural disturbance in God’s laws of nature, the great law of למינו as to wish to direct us to God in all our activities in and with the organic world, Whose Law of species we see still actively working in all the natural things of the organic world and Who has prescribed for us too the Law which should govern the “way and manner” of our living, then we find in this כלאים ופסולי המוקדשים law the identification of the Torah laws with the laws of nature. According to מל״ם on הל׳ כלאים IX,11, according to the way that Rashi takes it, the joining of actual ordinary animals with קדשים-animals would be prohibited from a כ״ש deduction (the inference from minor to major I.L.) from פסולי מוקדשים.

V. 16. רק הדם לא תאכלו, see on V. 15. על הארץ תשפכנו כמים although פסולי המוקדשים regarding בכורה ומתנות have the character of חיה through the comparison with צבי ואיל their blood still does not have the obligation of כיסוי (being covered) as actual חיות do (Chulin 84,a; see on Deut. 17,13). At the same time the phrase על הארץ תשפכנו כמים teaches that blood not destined for the Altar, דם שנשפך על הארץ has the character of water, and like water is מכשיר זרעים (Chulin, 33,a).

V. 17. לא תוכל לאכול וגו׳. The obligation to bring all offerings, dedicated and vowed objects which are closely connected with the Sanctuary to the one place chosen by God has already been given in V. 11. Here now verses 17 & 18 limit the eating of the part of all such objects which come to be eaten by the priests or the owners, to within the prescribed areas in or round about the Sanctuary. V. 17 is the prohibition to eating them without such areas, V. 18 the positive command to eat them within them. Thereby the actual eating, in itself a physical enjoyment, is drawn into the sphere of the God-seeking, God-serving procedures of the Sanctuary. All the places lying outside the close and closest proximity to the Sanctuary are comprised in the term שעריך. As שער itself is the typical expression for the civic life of the people which is concentrated within the “gate”, so שעריך are still more specially the civilian places which remain “yours” in contrast to the חצרות ה׳, the localities of God, to the places, which bear “the Name of God”. The boundaries of these places vary according to the character of the sacred objects, ביכורים ,מעשר שני (here understood under תרומת ידך, see V. 6), קדשים קלים as נדבותיך) ,תודה ושלמים ,בכור) may not be eaten חוץ לחומה, outside the walls of Jerusalem, קדשי קדשים as בקרך וצאנך) חטאת ואשם) not outside the עזרה.

The Gemora in Makkoth 18,a, points out that if our sentence here לא תוכל לאכל בשעריך מעשר דגנך וגו׳ simply wanted to prohibit eating “holy” food outside Jerusalem, the text would simply and shortly have added לא תאכלם בשעריך to verse 11. But as the prohibition of אכילה בשעריך is given in a quite separate sentence, and repeats again, and specialises again the different objects affected, the meaning of בשעדיך is extended beyond the narrow concept of actually חוץ לחומה. Each of the specially mentioned objects brings a reference to laws already given elsewhere regarding the permission for its being eaten, to extend the conditions of the prohibition לא תוכל לאכל. Thus of תרומת ידך) ביכורים), the prohibition to eat it before הנחה, before its having been deposited before the Altar (Deut. 26,4 & 10); ונדבותיך) תודה ושלמים) the prohibition to eat them before זריקה, before the blood had been thrown on to the Altar (ibid XII,27); בכורות, the prohibition of their being eaten by a non-cohen even after זריקה (Numb. 18,18); בקרך וצאנך) חטאת ואשם) the prohibition of eating them outside the חוץ לקלעים ,עזרה (Levit. 6,19); נדריך) עולה) the prohibition of eating any part of it at all, even בפנים, as the whole had to be given over to the Altar Fire (Levit. 1,8 & 9); and, according to הל׳ מעילה ,רמב״ם I,3 this לאו is just the אזהרה for מעילה altogether (see מל״ם).

And the Gemora in Baba Mezia 56,a, sees in the prohibition לא תוכל לאכל בשעריך וגו׳, which indeed primarily expresses the prohibition to eat מעשר שני outside Jerusalem, at the same time the prohibition to eat it if the permitted redemption, חילול (Deut. 14,25) had not been done in the prescribed manner. Further, in Makkoth 16,b, the prohibition לא תוכל לאכל בשעריך מעשר דגנך ותירשך ויצהרך is generalised to apply to the eating of food which is liable for תרומה and מעשר but is still טבל i.e. has not yet had the תרומה and מעשר separated out from it, and even if it was only the מעשר עני which takes the place of מעשר שני every third year (Deut. 14,28) and which has no קדושה at all which had not been separated out, it still has the prohibition of טבל.

Finally Yebamoth 73,b, sees in לא תוכל לאכל בשעריך at the same time the prohibition to eat בכורים or מעשר שני if they have become טמא, whereas the prohibition to eat מעשר שני if the person himself is in a condition of טמא is already given in Levit. 22,6 (refer to it). For אכילה בשעריך by reference to בשעריך תאכלנו הטמא והטהור יחדיו said of פסולי מוקדשים in Ch. 15,22, is considered to be such an eating where טמא וטהור אוכלין על שולחן אחד בקערה אחת ואין חוששין, where all consideration of טומאה and טהרה is lacking, the טמא and the טהור eat together at the same table and out of the same dish and inevitably the food becomes טמא by the touch of the one. Such an אכילה בשעריך is here forbidden for מעשר שני and the בכורים which are mentioned together with it.

Putting all this together, בשעדיך as the contrast to מקום אשר יבחר ה׳ is the concept of “the realm of ordinary eating”, and לא תוכל לאכל בשעריך prohibits the ordinary unconditional eating of anything which, on account of its relation to the Sanctuary, actually, or by reason of time, place or kind, accordingly, either altogether, or for this person, or not yet, or not there, or not in that manner, is not to be eaten. בשעריך is eating outside the limits set in relation to the Sanctuary, of place, time, person or condition. Of place:- ;מעשר שני, ביכורים, קדשים קלים חוץ לחומה ;קדשי קדשים חוץ לקלעים; of time:- קדשים קלים לפני זריקה ,ביכורים קודם הנחה, מעשר שני לפני חילול, טבל קורם הפרשת תרומה; of person:- עולה completely barred, בכור לזר; of condition:- מעשר וביכורים שנטמאו.

From this, the unusual expression לא תוכל לאכל instead of simply לא תאכל בשעריך could be understood. Excepting the one case of עולה, all the holy objects spoken about here are such that one is authorised to eat but the authority to eat them is subject to certain limitations, and it is against the non-observance of these limitations that the warning is given here. The יכולת is indeed there, they are qualified to be eaten, but לא תוכל לאכל בשעריך, not without restrictions are you empowered to eat them, when and where and how you please, etc. or not in the unrestricted sphere of your own abilities are you authorised to eat etc.

V. 18. כי אם וגו׳ refers to דגנך ותירשך ויצהרך which was mentioned first in the preceding verse. מעשר שני accordingly is the principle object to which the others are added as being subject to the same and similar restrictions in eating. Hence the frequent היקש, comparison of ביכורים and other sacred objects to מעשר שני. (Pessachim 24, a, & 36,b, and Yebamoth 73b, et seq.).

V. 19. השמר לך וגו׳, see on V. 12. At the impending decentralisation of the nation settling in the land, the Levites living scattered amongst the people is of the greatest importance. They are the living nerves and arteries coming out from the centrepoint the Sanctuary by means of which the members are kept in spiritual connection with the brain and heart of the nation. They are the representatives of the Sanctuary of the Torah in the midst of the people. Amongst a nation actively engaged in agriculture, cattle breeding and the industries associated with them, such unproductive members of the community as the Levites could easily fall into disrepute, be looked on as a burden to the community, and remain unrespected and undervalued in their vital importance for the spiritual moral and national well-being of the nation. Hence the repeated admonition not to neglect the Levi כל ימיך על אדמתך, the duration of your remaining on your own soil is essentially dependent on the esteem and respect you give the Levi, and the influence you allow him to have on your spiritual and moral development.

V. 20. כי ירחיב וגו׳. We have already remarked in Levit. 17,3, that, according to the, most generally accepted as Halacha, teaching of ר׳ ישמעאל during the time of the wandering in the wilderness when the whole nation lived in the close surrounding of the Sanctuary, בשר תאוה, i.e. eating ordinary meat of animals that were able to be brought as offerings but had not been brought, was not allowed, but such animals were to be brought as שלמים and the meat could only be eaten as parts of the offering of the owner. In accordance with that way of taking it our verse speaks of the permission of בשר תאוה and v. 21 gives the reason for the permission as the distance from the Sanctuary which the settling in the Land brought to the homes of the people (see Sifri and Chulin 16,b). But in a peculiar manner here the permission for the eating of ordinary meat—and indeed the completely unconditional permission: בכל אות נפשך תאכל בשר—is introduced, we could say, with a three-fold stipulation: כי תאוה וגו׳ כי ירחיב וגו׳ ואמרת וגו׳ on which Chulin 84,a, teaches: למדה תורה דרך ארץ שלא יאכל אדם בשר אלא לתיאבון, that the Torah assumes that meat is not a regular article of diet but is eaten to satisfy a special longing for it, and from there it follows that it is only with the increasing weakness of constitutions that the daily consumption of meat became habitual and necessary. And in fact our verse takes it that even at הרחבת גבול when the restricting conditions are removed still eating meat is dependent on כי תאוה נפשך וגו׳, and אוה and אות נפש could well be different from התאוה. Whereas החאוה predominantly expresses an unjustified lusting desire, אוה, as a rule designates a perfectly permissable longing, and תאוה נפשך and אות נפשך can very well designate a longing caused by something which is really necessary and which just announces that requirement, and the reason for the permission to eat meat being given at such full length be just in consideration of that so disastrous unjustified lusting after meat at קברות התאוה.

V. 21. כי ירחק וגו׳ וזבחת וגו׳ כאשר צויתיך. Up till now all slaughtering of cattle or sheep was done only in the חצר אהל מועד, accordingly under the supervision of the priests. But in the Land, with the permission of בשר תאוה, the attention to the details of the prescribed method of slaughter is left to the conscientiousness of each individual. So that the admonition to fulfil those schechita laws belongs very rightly to this compendium of laws of the משנה תורה. This commandment on the ways and means of זביחה which is referred to here is not to be found in the written Torah, but forms a part of the traditional Torah, the תורה שבעל פה to which here we find direct reference (אשר צויתיך “as I have commanded thee” I.L.). Thus Chulin 28,a: וזבחת כאשר צויתיך מלמד שנצטוה משה על הושט ועל הקנה ועל דוב אחד בעוף ועל רוב שנים בבהמה. The verbally handed down laws of schechita are that the animal must be slaughtered by a clean crosscut performed by a mitzva-bound Jew through the trachea (קנה) and the oesophagus (וושט), by means of a detached cutting instrument (תלוש, not מחובר) without interrupting the cut (שהיה) or pressing rather than cutting (דרסה) or covering over (חלדה) or in a slanting direction (הגרמה) or tearing one of the tubes loose before cutting (עיקור), hence also not with a knife which has not a perfect edge (שיש בו פגימה). This traditional law applies to בהמה היה ועוף except that in the case of birds, if only one of the tubes had been cut it would suffice. Every animal that dies or has been killed without this prescribed שהיסה having been meticulously performed is נבלה and eating it is not only prohibited under the עשה-command here but also under the לאו (Ch. 14,21) לא תאכלו כל נבלה.

The root זבח is phonetically related to ספח which means the attachment to a person or to a personal relationship. ספחני נא אל אחת הכהנות (Sam. I. 2,36), ונספחו על בית יעקב (Is. 14,1) מהסתפח בנחלת ה׳ (Sam. I. 26,19). These places leave no room for doubt as to the meaning of ספח. It is almost identical with שפח from which the concept משפחה comes (cf. also שבע, צבה, צבא all of which mean an enlargement of the personality by attachment to, and taking up, others, also שבה the forcible taking persons away with you). From that, it might not be going far to take זבח to designate an act by which man brings the animal body which hitherto had belonged to the animal being, into connection with himself, his human personality, attaches it to himself, makes it relative to himself, prepares the body of muscles and nerves, which hitherto had been subservient to the animal being, to be ready to be changed into human muscles, human nerves. This act is accomplished by a man, using human activity (not מחובר I.L.), in a manner which proclaims human character, severing the connection with the world of nature in which the animal being up to then had lived, performing the absorbing and rejecting functions, which constitute חיים (see Gen. on I.20). Breathing and feeding are these functions which give every living creature (נפש חיה) its physical life. Windpipe and gullet are the organs of these functions. A clear cut across these organs brings the continuation of these life functions to an end and brings the animal body under the dominion of the one who ordered the cessation of the continuation of the animal life. But only a clean cut proclaims human mechanical power, not crushing (דרסה) or tearing (עיקור) which animal power can also effect. The cut must also be performed openly and freely (without חלדה) and without hesitation (שהיה) as corresponds to an act of masterly taking possession; and it is to be made there where the organs are purely in service of bringing air and food to the whole body and not allowed to slide to the side, where they already appear to flow into their special organs and seem to belong on the one side to the throat and gullet and on the other to the lungs and stomach (הגרמה).

If א כל(ה) אכילה means the completed change, the transformation of the food material into the parts of the individual which require building up or replacing, so is שפח ,ספח ,זבח :זביחה, the preliminary preparatory adoption of the body of the animal for human purposes. And as the זביחה is a free-willed act of human activity so is the animal material assimilated in the human body to remain subservient to the free-willed self-determination of the “human being” in Man, whereas in the animal it had to follow with body and mind solely the laws of physical necessity.

Hence שחיטת חולין (the ordinary slaughtering for our ordinary food I.L.) has the same meaning as the שחיטה has at קדשים (for offerings I.L.) only that the former need not have כונה (Chulin 31,a) (one need not necessarily have this underlying meaning when performing it I.L.). For שחיטת חולין accomplishes the actual subordination of the concrete animal, whereas for offerings the live animal before the שחיטה symbolises the uncontrolled animal-nature of Man, and giving this up for entry into the higher life of the Sanctuary is what the שחיטה of such an animal symbolically expresses (see Levit. on I,5).

According to that it can also be understood why the personality of the one who slaughters is a decisive factor and שחיטת נכרי נבלה. For the animal creature is to be taken up and used for a human life which is to correspond to the mission of the Jewish laws of morality and equally so it can be understood why it is only the higher animals, בהמה חיה ועוף need to be killed by זביחה. Only for those whose bodies and life-activity approach in external similarity to that of the bodily life of human beings is the warning necessary that when the tissue of their nerves and muscles is converted into human nerves and human muscles by this conversion they leave the realm where they are bound by physical necessity and enter the realm where all bodily material matter is subjugated to a free-willed moral mastery.

The external bodily appearance of the lower animals דגים וחגבים (fish and permitted edible locusts I.L.) is so far from that of human beings that for eating them, as well as for vegetable food, such a warning could well be quite unnecessary.

Finally it can similarly be understood that for a בהמה טמאה a שחיטה would be entirely without any meaning and the animal would remain נבלה. A בהמה טמאה organically is in such contrast to the personality envisaged by the Jewish Torah that it is absolutely excluded from being absorbed in any way in the bodies of such personalities. The natural character of the species accordingly excludes “זביחה״. But a בהמה טהורה is susceptible to זביחה and even if some condition of טריפה prevents its being allowed to be eaten, the שחיטה still effects טהרה מידי נבלה (see Levit. 11,39). For the meaning of the root שחט see Gen. 6,11.

To this sentence כי ירחק ממך וגו׳ וזבחת וגו׳ the Gemora, in Kiddushin 57a, attaches the teaching:- ברחוק מקום אתה זובח ואי אתה זובח במקום קרוב פרט לחולין שלא ישחטו בעזרה that the permission given here to slaughter for ordinary food only applies—as the actual wording literally says—outside the Sanctuary, but within the halls of the Sanctuary it is forbidden. More, according to Baba Bathra 81,b, bringing חולין objects into the halls of the Sanctuary הכנסת חולין לעזרה was altogether not allowed. It is not quite decided whether and how far these sentences are דאוריתא especially how far the latter sentence applies, whether all חולין objects, or only such as were similar to those used for offerings, whether bringing them in anyhow, or only in a way similar to the bringing offerings in, was to be understood (see ל״מ and מל״מ on הל׳ שחיטה II, 1-3). But to whatever extent this law may reach the purpose of it would be to ensure the objects and procedures in the Sanctuary their symbolic character which clearly would be weakened or made doubtful in the way their meaning would be taken by the presence of the same or similar objects or procedure of secular nature. A secular slaughtering, a secular joint of meat etc. which have a purely concrete meaning puts the symbolic meaning of all the שחיטה, all the אברים etc. in the Sanctuary into doubt. And from this point of view the apparent exceptions to the prohibition of הכנסת חולין לעזרה would also be easily understood as these are only allowed if they are necessary and indispensable for carrying out the procedures of the Sanctuary themselves and therefore cannot possibly prejudice the way of looking at everything in the Sanctuary having purely symbolic meaning. In these cases the very fact of their being merely articles required makes the difference in their character and that of the appurtenances of the Sanctuary perfectly clear (see מל״מ ibid).

אשר נתן ה׳ לך. This addition could wish to guarantee not only the permission but the approval, yea the purpose of such sensual eating kept within the bounds set by the Torah, going beyond the mere actual requirements of nourishment. The eating of בשר תאוה is one of the purposes for which God has given you your herds and your flocks.

V. 22. אך כאשר יאכל וגו׳. Although now henceforth even animals which are fit for offerings may be slaughtered at any distance away from the Sanctuary and as such are subject to exactly the same זביחה as קדשים, they still have exactly the same secular character as had hitherto been borne by the animals unfit for offerings, צבי ואיל, and at eating them the restrictions of טומאה and טהרה do not apply (Rashi, see Misrachi). Still it is only regarding these טומאה and טהרה laws that they are like צבי והאיל. Regarding eating the חלב, they, as well as קדשים-animals which have become חולין again through פסול or redemption, remain prohibited (see Levit. 7,25). It is to this limitation of the comparison to צבי ואיל that, according to an opinion in Bechoroth 15,a, the adverbial conjunction refers. It is well worth noting that, according to the way our sages take it, this adverbial conjunction is not so much a limitation of what has preceded it as of what is contained in the verse it introduces. Thus:- אך את שבתתי תשמרו יכול לכל (אפילו לפקוח נפש) ת״ל אך חלק (יומא פ״ה ע״א), אך אל הפרוכת לא יבא יכול לא יהו כחנים בעלי מומין נכנסין וגר׳ לעשות ריקועי פחים ת״ל אך חלק (עירובין ק״ה ע״א), פדה תפדה יבול אפילו נטרף בתוך ל׳ ת״ל אך חלק (בבא קמא י״א ע״ב), והיית אך שמח לרבות לילי י״ט אחרון או אינו אלא י״ט ראשון ת״ל אך חלק (סוכה מ״ח ע״א), אך ביום הראשון תשביתו יכול מצפרא ת״ל אך חלק (פסחים ה׳ ע״א), תאמר ליה״כ שמכפר על מזיד כשוגג יכול יכפר על שבים ועל שאינן שבים ת״ל אך בעשור וגו׳ חלק (שבועות י״ב ע״א), יכול אף כל הקדשים כן ת״ל אך בכור וגו׳ חלק (תמורה כ״ה ע״א). This meaning of the word still requires considerable examination. For in some of these verses and elsewhere too, a sentence is introduced with אך without a verse preceding it that is to be limited by it, as:- אך את שבתתי (Ex. 31,13), אך בעשור (Levit. 28,27) and so also Ps. 53,1 אך טוב לישראל, hence perhaps even when taken as an adverbial conjunction, אך always gives an exception to the subject of the sentence it introduces, which otherwise is to be the rule expressed in that sentence. It would have the meaning:- there is an exception (פיקוח נפש) still, אך, the rule is את שבתתי תשמרו; there is an exception (שאינן שבים) still, אך, for all other conditions, בעשור וגו׳ יום כיפורים. So here too, there is an exception (חלב) still, אך in everything else, כאשר יאכל הצבי גו׳. Accordingly by אך, a limitation, a מיעוט of the sentence introduced by it, is assumed וצע״ע.

V. 23. רק חזק. This quite specially serious admonition to the prohibition of eating blood shows the great value of the Torah sets on its being observed ,and the depth of the peril to which the spiritual nature of human beings towards the moral task which the Torah expects Jewish people to accomplish ,is exposed by the consumption of blood. In the Sifri is recognised therefrom, the passionate strength of the habit to which the pagan world clung just to drink animal blood, a propensity which, in Jewish circles, was entirely overcome by the laws given on Sinai. The prohibition to consume blood has already been given in three places, in Levit. 3,17; VII,26; XVII,12-14 (look up) and also already referred to above in V. 16 in connection with פסולי המוקדשים. Here, where with the settlement in the Land the permission for its eating of ordinary meat, בשר תאוה started and the observation of the laws of the Torah connected with it was left to the responsibility of the conscientiousness of each individual, the warning against the consumption of blood and against falling back into the superstitions and the passions associated with it was to be inserted with repeated seriousness in the compendium of the vade-mecum for the decentralisation in the Land.

כי הדם הוא הנפש. See on Gen. 9,4, and Numb. 17,11, regarding the significant changes in the way the words are placed in the sentences to avoid any erroneous identification of the blood and the soul. To the Torah, the blood is the material which at every beat of the pulse circulates through the whole body, is the medium by means of which the soul exercises its ever-present mastery of the body. So that it is eminently the foremost bearer of the soul, and the Torah forbids animal blood, as the bearer of the animal soul, animal life, any entry into the realm—the holy morally free-willed realm—of the human soul, human life. After the true pure relation of the blood to the soul has been made clear and ensured in all the above-mentioned places in the Torah it now can say for the last repeated warning against the consumption of blood, just כי הדם הוא הנפש the blood is the material representative of the soul, (the mind, the life I.L.), with the consumption of animal blood, the tendencies to the animal soul, and the influences of the animal soul which still adhere to it, enter with it into the human body!

ולא תאכל הנפש עם הבשר, and just as you are not to consume the blood, in which the soul has its foremost representative, so also you are not to eat the meat at the time when the soul is still in connection with it, in which the joint you are taking for consumption is still under the mastery of the soul. This is the prohibition of אבר מן החי of a joint taken from the living body of an animal. A prohibition which had already been proclaimed for the whole Noachian world in Gen. 9,3, but is repeated here to make it still encumbent on the Noachian world, even after the Sinaitic Lawgiving which applies only to the Jews, in accordance with the canon: כל מצוה שנאמרה לבני נח ונשנית בסיני לזה ולזה נאמרה לבני נח ולא נשנית בסיני לישראל באמרה ולא לבני נח (Sanhedrin 59,a).—In Ex. 22,32, by ובשר בשדה טרפה לא תאכלו eating בשר ניז החי “meat” taken from a living animal is forbidden to be eaten (look it up), while here it speaks אבר מן החי of a “limb” (Chulin 103,b—cf. Levit. 11,32 for the difference between אבר מן החי and בשר מן החי in relation to טומאה).

V. 24. & 25. לא תאכלנו וגו׳, לא תאכלנו וגו׳. The Gemora differentiates between three kinds of blood: דם התמצית ,דם הנפש and דם הנפש .האברים, the blood to which the soul, the animal-life, primarily clings, with the pouring out of which the נפש, the life, the soul escapes, שהנשמה ,שהנשמה יוצאת בו תלויה בו, it is recognisable by its gushing, its spurting out. דם תמצית, the blood that just flows out. דם האברים, capilliary blood, blood not contained in arteries or veins which is only forbidden if it is פירש, has flowed out. The punishment of כרת (Levit. 7,27) is only imposed on the consumption of דם הנפש, the prohibition of which is repeated in V. 23. Verse 24 refers to דם התמצית, v. 25 to דם האברים (Rashi, מה שתמה המזרחי על רש״י שפירש כאן למען ייטב לד אזהרה לדם האיברים ובכריתות ד׳ ב׳ ד׳׳ה חמשה לאוין מוקי ליה אזהרה לבשר בחלב כדאיתא חולין קט״ו ב׳, נראה לענ׳׳ד דלא קשה מידי דרש״י לטעמיה שהלך בפירושו לחומש בשיטת ר׳ ישמעאל דמוקי קרא דכי ירחיב וגו׳ להיתר בשר תאוה והא דרשה דחולין אי אפשר אלא אליבא דר׳׳ע דמיירי קרא בפסולי מוקדשין ע״ש ועי׳ רש״י .חולין כ״ח א׳ ד״ה מה פסולי
על הארץ תשפכנו כמים, in contrast to the heathen erroneous ideas you are to ascribe no special value at all to it, and do no procedures arising out of those heathen superstitions with it.

למען ייטב לד וגו׳. Your happiness and moral well-being and that of your children are involved in your abstaining from consuming blood. It keeps your children אחריך, following your footsteps and prevents them from degeneration. It keeps your nature ישר in the straight tendency towards the calling which God has allotted to you. And inasmuch as then your nature remains uninfluenced by animal inclinations and disinclinations which are unworthy of human beings, it remains thereby inclined towards the demands of unselfishness in greater and smaller matters. Gladly and willingly will you practise the acts of kindness, giving in, not standing strictly on your rights, the goodness that is in keeping with the nobility of your true being, behaviour that will satisfy the expectations which God has of you, just there where there is no legal necessity for you to act as you do (see on Ch. 6,18).

V. 26. רק קדשיך וגו׳. But those animals which have been removed from the material calling of providing actual food and have received the destiny to serve symbolically to express your relation to the Sanctuary of the Torah, and indeed both קדשיך and נדריך, offerings which you have to bring and those which are vowed out of your own free will, אשר יהיו לך—this addition which apparently expresses some adventitious increase, according to Nazer 25,a, and Temura 17,b, includes וולדות ותמורות קדשים (the young which are born to an animal after it has been dedicated, and animals exchanged for dedicated ones I.L.) which, (with the exception of חטאת and אשם; see Levit. on Ch. 2,24) have the same character as the mother animal or the original one, and have to be used for the same symbolic purpose,—accordingly, all animals which are in connection with your Sanctuary and are dedicated to its symbolism, תשא ובאת וגו׳, those cannot achieve what they were dedicated for at the places where you live, but must be “taken and brought” to the place which God will choose to be the “Home of His Torah”. Only there is the complete conception of what your calling to be “holy” consists in, guaranteed, only there do you with your devotion to His Torah get really into the proximity (the purpose of your קרבן I.L.) of your God.

V. 27. ועשית עלתיך הבשר הדם. See Levit. on Ch. 1,9; ודם זבחיך ישפך See Levit. I. 5 (towards end of notes, p. 28 in English translation I.L.). Significantly enough, here שפיכת שירים ליסוד (pouring what is left of the blood down to the base of the Altar after the main “service of the blood”—the prescribed sprinklings—has been performed I.L.) is placed in connection with the duty of having to bring the קדשים-animals away from the place where you live up to the Sanctuary and there obtain the consecration of our “spiritual and active life”. שפיכת שירים ליסוד is the knowledge which accompanies us home:- Bodily we go away to our homes ,our spirit remains there.

But as here the whole “service of the blood” for offerings is quite generally referred to by the term שפיכה the Halacha is thereon taught in Zebachim 37,a. that הניתנין בזריקה שנתנן בשפיכה יצא that if offerings for which זריקה is prescribed had had only שפיכה done, the “service of the blood” could be considered as having been performed thereby. The real fundamental demand is, that the נפש should regard itself as being in the יסוד המזבח, on the basis of building up life on the basis of rising upwards to God as taught by the Torah. What is expressed by the זריקה is the energy required and obtained for this striving upwards and is only a result of realising this fundamental idea. That is why all the מתנת זריקה, the שתים שהם ארבע of the עולה and the שלמים must have the יסוד beneath them (see Levit. 1,3). וצע׳ע ,ע״ש כ״מ ול״מ רמב״ם פ״מ פ״ב ב׳ ג׳.

V. 28. שמר ושמעת את וגו׳ (cf. Chron I. 28,8, and II, XIX,7, שמרו ועשו, שמרו ודרשו) so here also שמר ושמעת, listen carefully. כי תעשה הטוב והישר, above at the prohibition of eating blood it only says כי תעשה הישר. By abstaining from the consumption of blood, your nature remains on the right tendency towards your moral goal, but by devoting your whole self to the tasks taught in the Sanctuary of the Torah, these goals become realised, receive their positive purport all of which is here summarised by the concept הטוב; that which contributes to the good, the happiness which is God’s object for us to achieve. This reflection, that just here, at bringing the קדשים up into the Sanctuary of the Torah, the purpose is given as הטוב, could make the explanation which ר׳ עקיבא gives in the Sifri understandable: הטוב בעיני השמים והישר בעיני האדם, and it is not impossible that ר׳ עקיבא takes הישר also as modifying הטוב i.e. that also that which is טוב בעיני השמים (which is the right thing to do I.L.) should be והישר בעיני האדם, done in such a way that it also finds approval in the eyes of people. Similar to the saying of איזו היא דרך ישרה שיבור לו האדם כל שהיא תפארת לעשיה -:רבי ותפארת מן האדם, “the way we do things must in the first place be laudable in itself but then must also take into consideration the judgment of people”.

V. 29. Clearing the land they were to take into possession from all traces of the heathen evils; and in contrast the exclusive devotion of all the new inhabitants to the uniting centre of the place of the Sanctuary of God’s Torah; as well as keeping the material and spiritual tendencies of all members of the nation towards the goals and tasks set by that Torah by observing the laws of שחיטה, and of the prohibition of consuming blood, these were the matters which formed the contents of this chapter hitherto. Now, before the compendium of laws for the decentralised members of the nation goes over to complete the further dietary laws which belong to it, it gives first four warnings against mental and social influences which could lead the members of the Jewish nation astray from the direction towards their God and His Torah. The influence of the recollection of the heathen way of life of the previous inhabitants; the influence of spiritual conceit, the influence of members of one’s own family; and the influence of one’s fellow citizens.

V. 30. נקש .פן תנקש וגו׳ could be phonetically related to נגש, approach, a strong movement towards a person. Hence נַקֵשׁ, to bring something forcibly to yourself, ינקש נשה לכל אשר לו (“Let the extortioner seize all that he hath” Ps. 109,11, I.L.) וינקשו מבקשי נפשי (“they that seek my life lay snares to catch me” Ps. 38,13, I.L.). Hence הִנָקֵשׁ to be drawn towards somebody. So the Sifri also takes it: שמא תמשך אחריהם. Possibly in this root, just as in נגש there is some innate reflection to a real or imagined legal argument. You could imagine yourselves as owing something to the land and to the previous inhabitants driven out and dispossessed on your account. You could be caught by the erroneous idea that it was up to you to carry on their mode of life in their land. In any case the Sifri takes פן תנקש אחריהם as an independent prohibition, separate from what follows, and prohibiting in general following their specific manners and customs, similar to ובחקתיהם לא תלכו (Levit. 18,3).

ופן תדרש וגו׳ איכה עבדו וגו׳. This prohibition comprises worshipping heathen gods in the special way that is generally recognised as the official mode used by their followers. The Law differentiates between עבודת פנים, the prescribed ways of homage and service to be shown to our One God and His Sanctuary, as המזבח והמקטר והמנסך ומשתחוה, if anyone does any of these acts to any heathen god, it is punishable even if such act is not the customary way of worshipping that particular god, אפי׳ שלא כדרכו. All other means of showing honour to such gods are only punishable if it is כדרכו i.e. if that is the way this particular god is worshipped, if it corresponds to איכה יעבדו וגו׳ of our verse. (Sanhedrin 60,b, see Ex. 22,19).

V. 31. לא תעשון כן וגו׳. Not only to their gods may you not imitate their ways of worship, but even to your own God, the One Unique God, to do so in imagined adoration is accounted a sin. For the meaning of their worship is in direct opposition to that which pleases your God. For your God is a God of Life and Love while dread gods of death are the gods of their illusions. The gods of their illusion gloat over the death of their victims, elevation and rejuvenation is what your God delights in.

V. 1. את כל הדבר וגו׳. According to the Massoretic division into paragraphs this verse is the final one of the preceding portion, and says: Therefore do not try to discover new ways of honouring God, and do not seek giving satisfaction to your God by any other means than those which He has prescribed for you. Only by faithfully, conscientiously carrying out the commands He has given you do you render the homage He expects from you. The Mitzvas which He has commanded you, and precisely as He has commanded you, are the expression of His Will for you, and they tell you what He expects from you, and what you have to do to arrange your life on earth in accordance with His satisfaction. As they are not your own ideas of what is right and befitting but the dictates of your God, you have not got to try and improve them in any way, not to add to them or subtract from them. By doing more or less they would no longer be the dictates of your God (see on Ch. 4,2 — עיין רמב״ם הל׳ ציצית פ״א ט״ז פלוגתא דרמב״ם וראב״ד).

V. 2-6. כי יקום וגו׳. In Sanhedrin 90,a, there is a difference of opinion whether these verses speak of an attempt to seduce to idolatry, or in general to transgress other laws of the Torah. The Halacha is not quite certain (see ל״מ on רמב״ם הל׳ יסודי התורה IX,1.). The wording of v. 5. speaks definitely for the latter view. In that verse the observance of all the mitzvas and the most faithful and strictest obedience in every direction is clearly made to ensure it against the seductive efforts of false prophets. It is quite definite (there in רמב״ם) that עוקר הגוף דע״ז, the attempt to do away with the whole prohibition of idolatry, or or only the temporary קיום מקצת וביטול מקצת as well עוקר הגוף דשאר מצות, the attempt to abrogate completely any single mitzva in the Torah, incurs the death-penalty. The difference of opinion of ר׳ חסדה and אביי on the one hand, and ר׳ המנונא and רבא on the other is only that, according to the former, עוקר הגוף דשאר מצות is not spoken about here at all, but comes under the laws regarding the authority of prophets in XVIII, 15-22 where the attempt at abrogation is made liable to the death penalty of חנק, while according to the latter it is included in the law given here where, in accordance with the teaching of the חכמים which is valid as Halachah, the punishment, equally with that presribed for עוקר הגוף דע״ז, the punishment would be the worse one of סקילה.

In any case not only defection to idolatry, but also the abrogation of even one single command or prohibition is made safe against even the authority of a prophet, whether this prophet by an אות ומופת, legitimises his authority as being sent by God with this message or, as ר׳ עקיבא (ibid) explains the case of our text: חס ושלום שהקב״ה מעמיד חמה לעוברי רצונו אלא כגון חנניה בן עזור (ירמיה ל״ח) שתחלתו נביא אמת ולבסוף נביא שקר, one who had previously legitimised himself and had proved himself a true prophet of God and become known as such, but now turns and misuses his acknowledged position, in service of evil and lies. By their direct personal experience of the Revelation of God’s Laws on Sinai, the mission of Moses and the Torah brought over to the nation by Moses, stands far above over all subsequent prophecy. Only within that which is in conformity with God’s Torah, and for its being maintained, has the word of a prophet, legitimised by אות ומופת, authority. Any word, even of the most eminent man, which is against the Torah, is untenable and proves him himself to be a liar (see רמב״ם הל׳ יסודי תורה ibid, and Ch. 18,15 et seq.). Only, קיום מקצת וביטול מקצת דשאר מצות, only temporary momentary action against a command of the Torah in the interest of the Torah itself, הוראת שעה is—with the exception of the ע״ז laws—legally possible—if done or permitted by a prophet who has already proved himself a נביא אמת, such as Elijah on Mount Carmel when he transgressed the שחוטי חוץ law (Ch. 12,13) and brought an offering on Mount Carmel to convince the people of the futility of the priests of Baal (Sanhedrin 89,b and 90,a;—see on XVIII,15). נביא או חולם חלום: cf. Numb. 12,6.

V. 3. ובא וגו׳ אשר דבר ונו׳. The sign that he had announced occurred for him to say to you, i.e. to support his invitation. Or according to Rabbi Akiba:- If a prophet arises who has already previously given you signs and proofs and the signs and proofs have materialised, but now he says to you “Let us go etc.”
אשר לא ידעתם, of whom you have had no experiences, of whose existence you have not been convinced, but rather of their non-existence you have been convinced.
V. 4. כי מנסה וגו׳. God, Who by His revelation has become your God, the exclusive Guide of your destiny and Leader of your actions,

Him are you faithfully to follow and not allow yourself to be led astray by any prophet from that faithful following from the conscientious obeying His commands from the seriousness of holding fast to Him. We have already remarked that the wording of this verse shows that it is not speaking only of being led into idolatry but equally so of being led into any disloyalty towards the Torah. (Cf. Numb. 15,22-31 where intentionally and on principle transgressing one single item of the whole of the contents of God’s Torah is placed on par with defection to idolatry).
V. 6. יומת ,והנביא וגו׳, יומת וגו׳, להדיחך וגו׳: according to the חכמים in Sanhedrin 89,b, similarly to the מסית ומדיח of the following verse (v.11) by סקילה.

סור .כי דבר סרה designates both departure from the right path of duty as well as departure from existence as in והבמות לא סרו (But the Bamas were not removed I.L.; Kings, I. 15,14). ושבט מצרים יסור (the sceptre of Egypt shall pass away entirely I.L. Zac. 10,11), and departure from the normal, as in מה זה רוחך סרה (Why is your mood so strange that you eat nothing I.L. Kings I. 21,5). סרה as a noun, accordingly expresses moral defection, ceasing from following the right path in life, תוסיפו סרה (Is. 1,5). as well as ceasing an activity מכה בלתי סרה (Is. 14,6, I.L.). As the subject of an utterance it designates something completely away from actuality, without any foundation. Thus in Ch. 16,16 of the false witness כי יקום עד חמם באיש לענות בו סרה by which Makkoth 5,a, takes the complete unjustification of the witness’s pronouncement to be expressed, the non-existence of the witness at the place of the alleged occurrence, שתסרה גופה של עדות. Yea the form תסרה seems to refer to the root סרה to be foul, a meaning which would also not be very far removed from the root .סור סר סבאם (Hosea 4,18) “Their drink has gone sour”, has become foul. But דבר סרה על ה׳ or אל ה׳ as here, occurs twice again quite specially referring to misusing prophesy for pronouncing untruths in the name of God; כי סרה דברת אל ה׳, and כי סרה דבר על ה׳ (Jer. 28,16 and XXIX,32). From both these places it is evident that by this term סרה defection from God is not meant, and דבר סרה על ה׳ could not mean to invite defection from God. Apart from the fact that grammatically the construction with על and אל would not be suitable, there Hananiah and Shemaiah by no means invited defection from God. What they did was to proclaim in the Name of God something as a message from God, which they had no right to do as they had not been charged with it at all from God. In both cases they were refuted with the words אני לא שלחתיו, לא שלחך ה׳. Their position towards God was exactly that of an עד זומם. They testified to something as coming from God for which they had no authority as no Word of God had been received by them in this case.

להדיחך מן הדרך וגו׳, by the term מן הדרך, in Sanhedrin 90,a, the indication is found, that regarding ע״ז, even אפילו מקצת הדרך an invitation to the smallest, just temporary transgression is guilty of death.

V. 7. כי יסיתך וגו׳. The Torah lays stress on the most intimate relationships, the ties of blood, of marriage and of friendship—shows just thereby what value and what justification it recognises on their influence on the feelings and trend of thoughts—and wants to protect loyalty to the Torah against any attack by these most justifiable and most powerful bonds. The Gemora in Kiddushin 80,b, points out how that בן אמך is stressed to show that the Torah assumes a usual intimate familiar meeting together of the sons at their Mother. For here it speaks of such confidential intimacy: בסתר.

אשר לא ידעת can hardly mean not knowing them in general, for in the following verse it expressly includes הקרובים אליך by which a knowledge of them is assumed. But rather we believe that here, as well as above in v. 3; in Ch. 11,28 and 13 as well as in Jer. 7,9, these words are to stress the contrast of the difference of all the gods of heathenism. The reality of God, the One Unique One, has been brought home to your absolute conviction by the evidence of facts which you yourselves have directly experienced, your knowledge of God has the highest degree of certainty, whereas there is not a single fact which has been given to the mind, mentally or materially, from which the human brain can form its “knowledge” of the actual existence of all those whom otherwise human vain illusions worship as being divine.
V. 9. לא תאבה לו ולא תשמע אליו: Let it have no effect in word or deed; ולא תחוס עינך עליו (see on Gen. 45,20), let not the value which the person has in your eyes influence you to spare him or her.
V. 11. המוציאך וגו׳, all that you need know to acknowledge God for ever unchangeably as your God, is given to you by the exodus from Egypt.

V. 12. וכל ישראל וגוי. The sin and its punishment is to be brought to the notice of the whole nation. כותבין ושולחיו בכל המקומות איש פלוני נתחייב מיתה בב״ד (notices have to be written and sent to every place in the country: so-and-so tried to entice somebody away from God and suffered judical capital-punishment, I.L.). For four crimes, and for four crimes only is the publication of the sentence to be broadcast in this manner as a warning for the whole population. ועדים (XIII,12) ארבעה צריכין הכרזה, המסית, זוממים (XIX,20) ובן סורר ומורה (XXI,21) וזקן ממרה (XVII,13). In the case of זקן ממרה according to ר״ע the carrying out of the sentence was even postponed till the רגל so that the publicity should be as great as possible (Sanhedrin 89,a);—see ל״מ on הל׳ ממרים III,8. So that the principle of deterrent is by no means the purpose of Jewish judical punishment. Only at these four does the Torah wish to achieve that effect by publication.

V. 13-19. The two previous laws were to oppose the influence of prophecy, relationship or friendship if their power was misused to try to entice to defection from God. Now, the misuse of the influence of the leaders of society to entice a whole community to such defection is added. The problem is taken of the case—according to the תוספתא it is purely a theoretical case which never did and never will happen—when the attempt is successful and the majority of the members of a civic community are led astray to idolatry. Such a case calls on the whole Jewish State to save its integrity of belonging to God, by destroying the offending city, which is one of its members, and is not only sinning against God but is disloyal and performing an act of treason against the first fundamental principle of the nation, as indeed from the very first the attempt is designated יצאו מקרבך, it is departing from the national community and setting up as an enemy to the Jewish national state. For such a traitor to the common community of cities the Torah places the “sword” (v. 16) in the hand of the State “the weapon of defence of nations against their enemies”, and pronounces the bann even against the property of those executed, as well as the permanent destruction of the city; so that not even a trace of such property, desecrated and tainted by such treachery should pass into being the property of anybody else, and the ground desecrated by such treachery should never again become the place for the development of human beings. In this it differs from the fate meted out to single individuals who commit the sin of idolatry. They, such individuals suffer the severer punishment of סקילה but it stops at the person of the criminal, his property passes to his heirs. In the case of the community (or at least the majority of its members I.L.) having fallen to idolatry, it or they are punished by the easier mode, execution by the sword, but all their property also is destroyed זה חומד ביחידים מבמרובים שהיחידים בסקילה לפיכך ממונם פלט והמרובים בסייף לפיכך ממונם אבד (Sanhedrin 111,b). Regarding the personal punishment it seems likely that being led to commit the sin in common with, and by the example of, a large number of persons would account for the slight modification of the severity of the sentence.

אשר וגו׳ נתן לך לשבת שם (all in the singular I.L.) it is the “nation” to which every city, village or settlement belongs, which lives in every place of residence, the common character of which and the common mission of which is to be stamped on, and striven for, in every individual residence. Only by faithfully proving this common character and this common task has every tiniest place a justified existence in the midst of the great whole.

V. 14. יצאו וגו׳, see remark on v. 13. אנשים ולא נשים ולא :אנשים קטנים, אין אנשים פחות משנים, the defection is only judged as a crime of communal nature if the enticement thereto was made by the solicitation of people who in general are justified in having influence in civic circles, at least two men who are inhabitants of that community, יושבי עירם ולא יושבי עיר אחרת, otherwise the crime is looked on only as being committed by so and so many individuals (San. III,b).—בנים שפרקו עול שמים ,בני בליעל מעל צואריהם (ibid) i.e. בלי על, who recognise nobody being above them, who have thrown off the sovereignity of God. From the form of the word one would take it as בלי יעל having no future, not worthy of any rising, development, thriving. As בליעל, with few exceptions, is connected with preceding stat. constr. it is in any case a noun, so that it would mean the unrestrained one, the insolent one, or the one without any future, the good-for-nothing one; or insolence worthlessness.

נדח :וידיחו a stronger form of נדה, removal, retirement, withdrawal, and indeed preferably, personal withdrawal, the complete withdrawal, and הדיח, the successful enticement to defection. סדת, on the other hand, the root of יסיתך (v.7), related to צוד ,סוד ,זוד is the attempt at seduction, the cunning ensnarement, to win somebody over for some purpose. לאמר: their tempting talk must be adduced by witnesses. שצריכין עדים והתראה (ibid).

V. 15. ודרשת וחקרת וגו׳. The sentence ודרשת וחקרת ושאלת היטב giving the duty which lies on the court regarding the charge runs similarly in Ch. 17,4 at the charge of idolatry to a single individual: ודרשת היטב, and equally so at עדים זוממים at Ch. 19,18 ודרשו השופטים היטב, and thereby the דרישה וחקירה, the investigation, the cross-examination of the witnesses on whose declaration, according to the Jewish criminal procedure, the charge solely rests, is given as the first indispensable task of the court. The Halacha (Sanhedrin 40,a) differentiates thereby beween חקירות and חקירות .בדיקות consist of such questions, the answering of which is so essential, that if even only one of the witnesses declares “I do not know”, עדותן בטילה, the whole testimony, and with it the whole charge which rests on it, is invalid. בדיקות consist of such questions the answering of which is not indispensable: אפילו שנים אומרים אין אנו יודעין עדותן קיימת (even if both witnesses say: “we do not know” the evidence still stands and is valid I.L.); and their evidence would only render the charge invalid if their replies did not completely agree with each other: אחד חקירה ואחד בדיקה בזמן שמכחישין זה את זה עדותן בטילה (ibid). The seven questions to pin the exact place and time of the alleged occurrence belong, according to all the opinions to the חקירות viz. באיוה מקום, באיזה שנה, באיזה חדש, בכמה בחדש, באיזה יום, באיזה שעה, באיזו שבוע, in which year of the Shemita, in which year, in which month, on which day of the month, on which day of the week, at what hour, at what place.

(incidentally we would remark that under the regime of the Torah, the market-price of all real estate depended on reckoning the number of years since the last Youvel and those to come before the next, and also the nature of the tithe to be paid whether מעשר שני or מעשר עני depended on the year of the Schmita period, so that a knowledge of these times could be assumed to be universally known; see Levit. 25,15 and Deut. 14,28). On the precise determination of the time and place of the occurrence, the acceptance of the testimony of the witnesses having been present when it happened, is dependent in the very first place. Witnesses testifying that the accusing witnesses were elsewhere at that time not only render their evidence invalid but impose on them the same punishment and penalties that they were trying to obtain for the accused by their lying accusation (see Ch. 19,19 ibid). Every evidence can only be brought when it runs this danger of being refuted by a possible chance of a charge of alibi against the witnesses. It must be an עדות שאתה יכול להזימה. So that if any factor of determing the place and time is lacking, this possibility is also lacking, and with that, the validity of the whole evidence. These שבע חקירות, seven questions, although they only refer to establishing the time and place of the occurrence, nevertheless belong, for the reason stated, to those to which a definite answer is indispensable, and to which a reply of איני יודע (I do not know I.L.) would nullify the whole evidence. Questions which refer to unessential details, which could—and should—refer to matters which in themselves are quite immaterial but serve to test the agreement and veracity of the witnesses by cross-examination are called מסיעין את העדים ממקום—בדיקות (פ׳ הרמב״ם מעין לענין) למקום ibid 32,b. To these questions the answer איני יודע would not matter, but if contradictory to that given by the other witness, הכחשה, would render the whole evidence invalid. It seems that Rambam reckons the questions: מכירים אתם אותו התריתם בו העובד ע״ז את מי עבד ובמה עבד which follow in the Mishna (ibid 40,a) immediately after the seven חקירות, as being of the same nature and importance as them. For they, too, affect so much the actual foundation for the charge that it is difficult to think the charge could be substantiated if the reply given to one of these were איני יודע (cf. ל״ם on הל׳ עדות I,4). Nevertheless, according to ,ראב״ע רש״י and others, the inability to answer these questions, by which the possibility or otherwise of הזמה is not affected, would not alter the validity of the evidence, and they are reckoned as being among the בדיקות.

Taking the view of Rambam there would be three categories, two sets of חקירות, definite answers to which are essential, and less essential cross-examinations, בדיקות at which only contradictory answers from the witnesses would upset the evidence. This would be quite consonant with the wording of our verse:

It says ודרשת וחקרת ושאלת היטב. Now דרש is essentially seeking for something, ואת שעיר החטאת דרש דרש (Levit. 10,16) דרשה צמר ופשתים (Prov. 31,13), ודרשתי את צאני מידם (Ez. 34,10) etc. Referring to an occurrence and a resulting charge, it would be primarily finding out the validity of the charge and of the occurrence behind it, clearly finding the “solidity” of the charge and of the event alleged thereby, finding out the nature of the charge and establishing the facts on which it is based, just those questions which the Rambam reckons to the חקירות; the questions of which the דרישה of our text would consist. But חקר is essentially to search for what is hidden, finding out the foundation on which something rests. This is nothing other than finding out that the witnesses were actually present and saw the occurrence which alone justifies them in bringing the charge, just the seven חקירות, the questions probing the exact time and place, which accordingly is what the חקירה of our text demands. But apart from these there are questions of various kinds which in themselves are less essential—could indeed touch on matters entirely immaterial—but agreement or disagreement on the part of the witnesses would substantiate or shatter the evidence, בדיקות which our text brings under the term שאלה the general conception of interrogating. The היטב would refer to all three.

אמת :והנה אמת נבון הדבר, the truth of the objective establishment of the actual act; נכון, the foundation of the charge being in order and not shattered by הזמה, the former the truth of the crime having been committed, the latter, the truth of the witnesses who brought the charge.

V. 18. נתן רחמים ל— .ונתן לך רחמים וגו׳ does not occur with the meaning in which we would understand “showing mercy to someone” so that it should mean here:- “God will show you mercy”, and “giving” mercy (—נתן ל I.L.) would be the same as “showing” mercy (ירחם I.L.). In the sentences יתן לכם רחמים לפני האיש (Gen. 43,14) and ואתן לכם רחמים וגו׳ (Jer. 42,12) in each case it means: God will bring it about that a third party—Joseph or the King of Babylon—will show mercy to you, not that God will be merciful to you. Also in לא שמת להם רחמים (Is. 47,6) the might of the Chaldean power is reproached that it did not bring it about, make it a law that captives should be humanely treated. Here too, in a similar sense it would mean:- after you have cleared away the last trace of the crime and the criminals, God will again allow you to be merciful; whereas in your treatment of the עיר הנדחת, the voice of רחמים may not be heard; kindness, pity, which is to be your fundamental character, is not to alter in the slightest your treatment of the people of an עיר הנדחת; once the national justice has performed its harsh and distasteful duty, God allows you to resume your natural inherited tendency to kindness and mercy, so that you may remain worthy of His Kindness and Mercy. Thus our sages take it, in Sabbat 151,b, ונתן לך רחמים ורחמך והרבך כל המרחם על הבריות מרחמין עליו מן השמים וכל שאינו מרחם על הבריות אין מרחמין עליו מן השמים. and Yebamoth 79,a: שלשה סימנים יש באומה זו הרחמנים והביישנים וגומלי חסדים דכתיב ונתן לך רחמים ורחמך וגו׳, and Beza 32,b, ונתן לך רחמים ורחמך כל המרחם על הבריות בידוע שהוא מזרעו של אברהם אבינו.

V. 1. The previous chapter dealt with the misuse that prominent spiritual or social personalities, or people who are dear to us by relationship or friendship might make of their influence on our faithfulness to God. Spirituality, social position, relationship, friendship are not to exist for us as soon as they make themselves instruments for defection from God. In close connection with that, laws come here at the beginning of a new chapter which are given essentially in Leviticus (Ch. 19,27, 28, and XXI,5) but are repeated here because of their enhanced importance for the impending decentralisation of the people. In Leviticus we already have remarked how the prohibition of שריטה וקרחה למת (incisions on one’s body and making baldness on one’s head as a sign of grief over death I.L.) ensured the keeping of ones’ self-estimation, the consciousness of one’s own worth arising from being directly belonging to God, even in comparison and in connection with our dearest and most honoured personalities. No personality may chain us so closely to it, allow us to be so absorbed into it, that when it departs from us we may throw our own personality after it, as having no longer any value, as would be what the permanent sign of cut or baldness on our body is meant to express. Now in the previous chapter the danger was described which even our highest relationship to God could be exposed to by unrestricted devotion to persons who infuse us with love and respect. A danger which would arise all the more easily in the isolation in which the people were now about to enter, small settlements and circles far away from the centre, and people of imposing spirituality or in prominent positions would have much stronger influence. So that the Torah repeats with increased significance the prohibition against קרחה and שריטה which wishes to keep up our own self-valuation even against our nearest and dearest, and brings the great idea home to all classes throughout the people בנים אתם לה׳ אלקיכם, in the very first instance your nearest relation is your Father in heaven you are all His children. The tie that attaches you to your God is closer to, and comes before all other ties (see on Levit. 19,28).

In Makoth 21,a, (and similarly in Yebamoth 13b) it is true that the למת of our verse is taken to refer to לא תתגודדו, but there, having regard to Kings I, XVIII,28, it is also described as a גדידה לע״ז as a general heathen cult performed to their gods the meaning of which we have already gone into on Levit. 19,28 in connection with גדירה למת.

V. 2. כי עם קדוש אתה וגו׳, not גוי קדוש in your external political unity as a solid body, but as being a nation united in the uniformity of the internal formation of all its multitudinous social circles, each branch of this national community equally holy equally belonging to God, equally directly in contact with God. It is just this united community of people belonging exclusively to God, and the building up of a whole national social life on this basis which is the mission for which God chose you.—סגלה, see Ex. 19,5.

In Yebamoth 13,b and 14,a. the prohibition לא תתגודדו, make no incisions on your body, is referred also to the national body, and the lesson taught לא תעשו אגודות אגודות, to keep unity in the nation on the grounds of keeping the Torah, and not to allow differences in the teachings and decisions of the laws to lead to dividing into different communities, not to allow them to lead to “splits” in the nation. A separated mass, a detached troop of an army is also called גדוד, so that לא תתגודדו can very well have the meaning at the same time of “do not separate yourselves, do not divide into parties, separate groups”.

After all, if our way of taking the פ״א roots is correct, the root אגד itself would be nothing else but א גד to separate into a special unit. The verb to gather into clusters, to appear in separate groups only occurs in the Kal of גוד or יגוד עקב ,גדוד יגודנו -:גדוד (Gen. 49,19) and יגדו על נפש צדיק (Ps. 94,21). It is because of that ,it seems to us, that the Gemora in Yebamoth 13,b, remarks א״כ לימא קרא לא תגודו which we think must be read תגודו or לא תגדו. Simply to forbid the formation of parties לא תגודו would have sufficed.

According to this the Torah wishes at the same time to give us the admonishment not to allow a split to arise within a united communal body through differences of opinion in interpretations and deductions made from the Torah; that one part should form a group to follow the representative of one opinion and another part form one around the representative of the other opinion כגון ב״ד בעיר אחת פלג מורין כדברי ב״ש ופלג מורין כדברי ב״ה and thereby the אגודה אחת of a united community are split into אגודות אגודות. But that rather all such kinds of differences of opinion should be brought to an agreed decision made on the basis of the rules for decisions in such cases by the Torah itself, and uniformity of practice kept up as far as it is regulated by the Law.

And actually for over twelve hundred years, until in the first centuries of the period of the second Temple, there was complete agreement in the practice of the Laws. Just one single difference was not agreed upon and that was only concerning the extent to which a preventative law of the rabbis—משתמש בבעלי חיים—should be carried for the performance of the Mitzva of סמיכה on Yomtov (see Chagiga 16,a and b). Even Hillel and Shamai only differed in three matters, of which only one concerned the measure required by the Torah (the quantity of dough from which one has to take “Challah” I.L.), the other two were again only about preventative laws of the Rabbis (see Sabbat 15,a). It was only later in the time of their disciples, when the political turmoil upset clarity and composure, and the leisure of the pupils of Torah-study was no longer there, and with the catastrophe of the fall of the State overtaking them, oppression and persecution and dispersion broke the connection between disciples and masters of “learning”, as well as the connection between scattered communities and the centre, only then undecided doubts and questions, and different opinions regarding traditions and the interpretations of traditions naturally brought about differences in the way the law was observed in different places. These differences were only contravened by the activity of Rabbi Jehuda Hanassi in collecting, sifting and deciding the differences in traditions and opinions which were available and halachacly fixing the result in the Mishna, and thus some uniformity was restored. And then 250 years later Rabina and Rabbi Ashi completed the work by editing the Gemora to attempt uniformity in the even worse conditions which had arisen in the meantime through the greater separation of communities and individuals. For such times when there is a lack of any highest national authority which could decide and settle all differences which unavoidably arise from the differences in the exercising of the Law in the different places—or as Rambam in הל׳ ממרים I,5, adds, even when an authority did exist, in the interim between sending for, receiving and bringing the decision back—for such times above all was לא תתגדדו ,לא תעשו אגודות אגודות pronounced and desired:- That within a united communal body, ב״ד בעיר אחת—according to Rambam’s way of taking it in הל׳ ע״ז XII,4 even in two separate communities in one city ב, בעיר אחת (but see כ״מ and ל״מ thereon)—every difference of opinion regarding the administration of the Law should be discussed and decided in accordance with the existing regulations for such doubts and questions, and thus a greater failing in the observance of the Law is to be prevented.

When we consider how the preceding laws are concerned with the harm that could ensure from the overpowering influence that certain persons could exercise over their immediate circles; consider that, as we believe, the prohibition of גדידה ושריטה לנפש is to counter the unjustified over-valuation of other lives; if we finally consider that the אגודות אגודות, against the formation of which the other way of taking לא תתגודדו warns us, come into existence mainly from forming parties to follow the lead of the one or the other of two differing personalities, then we think we can understand the deep inner connection in which the two resulting prohibitions from לא תתגודדו stand to one another.

V. 3. לא תאכל וגו׳. The preceding laws all gravitate towards the one predominant final thought of the inexpressible dignity and worth of every single individual personality and its direct personal godly position and mission in life, only out of which the united circles of a national community holy to God can emerge.

In connection with this thought, and arising from it, now follows a continuation from Ch. 12,20 of the interrupted dietary laws, which, on account of the permission to eat בשר תאוה which was to commence with the decentralisation, are to be given a place in the popular compendium of the laws. In detail they have already been given in Ch. XI of Leviticus in connection with the laws regarding the sanctification and preservation of moral, spiritual and sensual purity. In accordance with the popular purpose of this compendium, here it would not be sufficient to give the theoretical indications for the kind of animals which are permitted for food, but in verses 4 and 5 the actual names of the ten permitted animals are given, the knowledge of the characteristic signs by which they would be recognised being more of merely theoretical interest (see Rambam הל׳ מאכלות אסורות I,8). Altogether only the larger species of animals are mentioned, out of which in general animals are taken for food, at which the opportunity is taken to mention amongst the birds some, as ראה and איה (v. 13) for which two different names were in common use. But the smaller creeping creatures, which in any case are not usually eaten at all, as food they are disgusting, are included in the general declaration לא תאכל כל תועבה (This would explain the sentence in Jerusalmi Sabbat 9,1: כתיב תועבה בשרצים לא תאכל כל תועבה. For שרצים are just not mentioned here at all. But just because of that it is taken that they are primarily to be undersood by the general canon לא תאכל כל תועבה).

לא תאכל כל תועבה, the extent of this sentence is not quite certain. As the quotation just given from the Jerusalmi proves, it refers in general to the forbidden food, the repeated mention of which is introduced by this sentence. That also explains quite naturally the position of this sentence at the beginning of the chapter on forbidden food. The forbidden animal food is thereby described as תועבה as such, the eating of which is opposed to our moral nature and destiny, and therefore would be inclined to “disgust” us. It would be an analogous expression of שקץ in the corresponding Chapter XI of Leviticus, and this conception would fit completely with the predominating thought of the preceding sentences of the direct proximity of the relationship of every single member of the Jewish nation to their Father in heaven. And this chapter concludes with exactly the same motive כי עם קדוש אתה לה׳ אלקיך (v. 21.) as that of the final thought (in v. 2) of the preceding group of laws.

But neither in the Sifri nor in the Babli is there any mention of this verse referring to the dietary laws which follow here. The teaching of ר״מ in ע״ז 66,a: מנין לכל איסורין שבתורה שמצטרפין זה עם זה שנאמר לא תאכל כל תועבה כל שתיעבתי לך היא בבל תאכל is not accepted as Halacha (see Rambam, הל׳ מאכלות אסורות IV, 16). Only ר׳ אשי (Chulin 44,b) finds in it the prohibition of eating בשר בהלב of which the wording of the text only prohibits the cooking:

מניין לבשר בחלב שאסור באכילה שנאמר לא תאכל כל תועבה כל שתיעבתי לך הרי הוא בבל תאכל, i. e. “everything of which the preparation is forbidden to be done, is also forbidden to be eaten”. But according to the general way of taking it, the prohibition to eat בשר בחלב is given by the thrice repeated prohibition to cook it (Chulin 111,b), and if (in 115,a ibid) every other application of the sentence כל שתיעבתי לך וגו׳ is rejected, then the canon כל שתיעבתי לד וגו׳ would have no application at all. Rashi’s explanation in his commentary on the Torah:- כגון צרם אזן בכור וגו׳ is not in accordance with the accepted Halacha (Bechoroth 34a & b), as the מל״מ on הל׳ בכורות IV, 1 already remarks as following from that the איסור אכילה would be only קנס דרבנן. Rambam does certainly take up another way of taking it in the Sifri, viz: בפסולי המוקדשין הכתוב מדבר in his הל׳ פסולי המוקדשים XVIII,3, and refers the איסור and מלקות for the eating of all קדשים שנפסלו back to it, but, as far as we can see it this אוסוד, according to Makkus 18,b, rests on the verse: לא יאכל כי קדש הוא כל שבקדש פסול בא הכתוב ליתן לא תעשה על אכילתן a sentence which, quite remarkably, Rambam himself in ’הל 10 assigns to פגול and נותר but which, from its general term כל שבקדש פסול seems to refer to all פסולי מוקדשים (see תוספות Makkoth 18,b). וצ״ע.

After all this, we believe that everybody agrees with what we have quoted from the Jerushalmi that our verse refers to all the מאכלות אסורות in the succeeding verses, and the various other prohibitions which we have quoted as being referred to it by various authorities were learnt from the generalising word כל תועבה—,כל—. But at the same time, the fact that in the שמיני) ספרא) a prohibition, a לאו for eating בהמות טמאות is sought, as גלוי מלתא by a ק״ו and not taken as a direct prohibition from our verse, could perhaps be explained, that then לא תאכל כל תועבה as a לאו שבכללות would not incur the penalty of מלקות, but against this תוספות in ע״ז 66,a, would be וכל זה צע״ע ,ד״ה כל שתיעבתי.

V. 4. זאת הבהמה וגו׳ איל וגו׳. We have already noted on Levit. 11,2, that the fact that at the dietary laws בהמה בכלל חיה and חיה בכלל בהמה, both names of the animals divested of their narrow meanings give us an indication of the characteristics which animals must have to be allowed to be used for food. Their constitution must be that of חיה, their ability to live must be unmitigated (not טריפה I.L.) and their nature must be that of בהמה, characterised by their animalism tending to accomodate itself submittingly to the humane qualities in human beings. According to that it is completely appropriate that just here, where the dietary laws are given from the point of view of the godly dignity and value which his calling gives to each individual, the “בהמה״ stands at the head—שור שה כשבים ושה עזים.
