It does not say כבש ועז but שה כשבים ושה עזים thereby to lay down the law that, regarding the permission for food, the nature of the descent, and moreover that of the mother-animal is the deciding factor and even if the young has not the signs of a “pure” animal it would still be allowed in accordance with the rule: היוצא מן הטמא טמא מן הטהור טהור (Bechoroth 5,b and 7,a, אליבא דר׳ אליעזר; — cf. on Levit. 11,4).

V. 5. איל וגו׳. As remarked above the complete list of the permitted mammals is given in these verses 4 and 5. There are no more than these ten kinds of animals (Chulin 80,a) of which the three in v. 4, belong to the class of בהמה whose חלב is forbidden, and those named in v. 5, to the class of חיה whose חלב is permitted but their blood has to be covered (see Levit. 7,25 and XVII,13). But regarding the seo tradition is not certain whether it should be considered as בהמה or חיה (Chulin, ibid.).
V. 6-8. See on Levit. 11,3-8. השסועה is, according to Chulin 60,b, an animal with a double backbone, and in Nidda, 24a, it is discussed whether such an animal is just a freak or does really exist.
V. 9 & 10. See on Levit. 11,9-12.

V. 11. כל צפור טהורה וגו׳. In Chulin 63,b, it is taught that, regarding the permission to eat birds, one has to rely on the tradition of the various places where any particular kind of birds are found as to whether they have always been eaten there or not. עוף טהור נאכל במסורה (see on Levit. 11,13-19). It seems to us that it is not impossible that, taken in comparison with v. 4 and 5, the directive for this practice may be found here. The law as to which mammals were fit to be used for food could be made sufficiently clear by naming them, the number of kinds is quite small. But the kinds of “fit” birds is so numerous that it was shorter for the Torah to enumerate the twenty-four kinds of “unfit” birds. (Chulin 63,b). So the Torah gives the indication for the popular practice to keep to the established custom (see on Levit. 11,13-19). From the word כל in כל צפור וגו׳ it is taught in Kiddushin 57,a, that the living bird which is set free at the procedure of טהרת מצורע may be eaten (see Levit. 14,7).

V. 13. והראה וגו׳. According to Chulin 63,b, דאה (Levit. 11,14) and ראה here are different ways by which the same kind of birds is named, and equally as דיה and איה and indeed according to one opinion there דאה ראה דיה ואיה are all of them only four different names for one and the same kind of birds. (see remark on V. 3).
V. 20. כל עוף טהור וגו׳. We dare to put forward the assumption that hereunder the permitted kinds of grass-hoppers could be understood under this heading (cf. Chulin 139,b).

V. 21. לא תאכלו כל נבלה. Every animal that requires שחיטה i.e. בהמה וחיה טהורה ועוף טהור which did not die by the prescribed שחיטה is נבלה (Chulin 32,a). שחיטה makes no difference to other animals, a בהמה טמאה שנשחטה is none the less נבלה and has the טומאת נבלה in מגע and משא (Levit. 11,8 & 26 et seq). But regarding אכילה the איסור נבלה does not apply as the animal is already איסור for eating, being an “unfit” animal in any case, and we have the rule that אין איסור חל על איסור unless it is an איסור מוסיף an איסור כולל or איסור בבת אחת (see Levit. 7,24); Rambam הל׳ מאכלות אסורות IV,2).

From the fact that the Torah finds it necessary expressly to allow the sale or gift of נבלה to a non-Jew, the Gemora in Pessachim 21,b, כל מקום שנאמר לא יאכל לא תאכל לא תאכלו אחד איסור אכילה ואחד איסור הנאה במשמע עד שיפרוט לד הכתוב כדרך שפרט לד בנבלה teaches that wherever there is a prohibition “to eat”, the prohibition “to make any use” is included, unless the Torah expressly gives the permission, as it does here at נבלה. We also find such permission to make use of it other than by eating, at טרפה (Ex. 22,30), at חלב (Levit. 7,24), and, as the Gemora there in Pessachim works out, also for יין לנזיר, תרומה, אבר מן החי, דם, חדש and שרצים.

In Avouda Zara 67,b, it is further taught from our verse that the prohibition לא תאכלו כל נבלה evidently assumes that it is still eatable and so deduces that הראויה לגר קרויה נבלה שאין ראויה לגר אינה קרויה נבלה, that regarding the prohibition to eat נבלה, and similarly for other forbidden food, the איסור only applies as long as it is eatable, which then results in the law (ibid) that in mixtures נותן טעם לפגם מותר, that if the prohibited matter in the mixture gives it a bad taste it would not render the mixture אסור. But the application of this law is subject to more definite rules (see ibid).

אכל would be, according to the way we take these roots (כל (ה destruction (כלה) of matter for the purpose of restoring one’s own self א. Uneatable, or material which can still be tasted in a mixture but is unpalatable, makes the mixture distasteful just by this state of being uneatable or unpalatable could be so rejected by the “self” to be restored, that it loses the presumed purpose of restoring one’s self and can no longer be considered as אכל.

Regarding טומאה a נבלה only loses the נבלה-character when it becomes no longer eatable by an animal נפסל מאכילת כלב (when even a dog would not touch it I.L.), but סרוח מעיקרא but if it had never been eatable from the beginning then it does not become טומאה at all even if this state of uneatableness was only as far as human beings go (Bechoroth 23,a & b).

לא תאכלו כל נבלה וגו׳ כי עם קדוש וגו׳ לא תבשל וגו׳. On Ch. 12,21 we expressed the opinion that the act of שחיטה was one of appropriation by Jews of bodily matter which hitherto had belonged to animal life, was an incorporation, a raising up, of an animal body into the sphere of Jewish human personality. (שפח ,זבח ,צבה ,צבא ,שבע. Very probably שחט is also only a strengthened, more powerful form of שחד which means to win somebody over to oneself). Its very opposite is נבלה, an animal which had died without schechita, whose body was not only already gripped by the world of reverting to elements as טרפה, but had already belonged to the world of complete lack of freedom: נול = נבל (decay ruin), נפל.

We have already worked out on Ex. 23,19 how the prohibition of בשר בחלב at the preparation of food not only represents an admonition in general to remember the human calling the Lawgiver has given us (our למינו I.L.) but also that calling being in such contrast to the animal character, that in us the animal phases of our nature—observation and will, thought and motion, are not to serve and belong to the vegetative phases of nutrition and reproduction (as they are in animal life I.L.), but with these subservient to the morally free-willed nature of spiritual Man, are to be elevated into the loftier sphere of true humanity and godliness (I would refer my readers to the lengthy notes in pp. 407-412 on the “milk-and-meat” prohibition in Ex. I.L.).

This regulation makes us to עם קדש וגו׳, and so the prohibitions of נבלה and בשר בחלב in deep inner connection would mean to express the following idea:- You are not to absorb as food for your own personality the unfree nature of the animal-world, which falls back to the world of the elements; for, as a member of a nation “holy to God” you have a calling which does not allow you to yield the animal phase of your nature down to the level of the lures of the vegetative functions of life, but is to elevate these up into the sphere of God-serving Man. Not only must you refrain from eating כל נבלה but even in the animal food which you are allowed to eat, and in its preparation, you are to keep in mind the moral and holy calling of the being that you wish to nourish, and the demands which this calling entails.

V. 22. עשר וגו׳. The preceding dietary laws repeated the duty, when choosing the material for our animal food, to take into account the moral and spiritual holiness of the human beings who are to be nourished by it; only to eat such food in conditions and ways of preparation by which our spiritual moral integrity is not endangered, but rather, even in the preparation of animal food to keep in mind the specific vocation of the spiritual element in Man to rule over and control the animal one in his nature. To that, the מעשר שני law which now follows is in the closest connection. By it just the sensuous material enjoyment of food is raised to a holy, God-serving act of duty to be performed in sight of the Sanctuary of the Torah. “Eating before the Presence of God,—ואכלת לפני ה׳ אלקיך—becomes a means of “teaching and educating” to the fear of God which is to accompany us throughout our lives—למען תלמד ליראה את ה׳ אלקיך כל הימים—. This is entirely in keeping with the fundamental character of Jewish honouring God and the Jewish ideal of Man. Neither know anything of nearness to God and human loftiness of the spirit only, which relegates the material earthly to moral worthlessness or even degradation. Judaism grasps the whole of Man for the sphere of his enoblement and places holiness in the life of his senses as the very first indispensable preliminary condition for the elevation of Man towards God, as indeed the institution of Mila expresses as the foundation.

מעשר שני has been commented on in Levit. 22,6 where it is understood to come under the conception of קדשים, of holy things that may not be eaten בטומאה (refer to it there). Also in Levit. 27,30 & 31, where it is characterised as ממון גבוה, as קדש לה׳, as being property given to God, belonging to Him, which is given back to the original owner by God with only limited rights of disposal, and as such has the חרם mentioned there attached to it. Now the real proclamation of its institution follows here. It could well have been kept back till here to be placed in the popular compendium for the decentralisation, as only now does it have any importance and will come to be realised, whereas hitherto all eating took place in the vicinity of the Sanctuary as the whole מחנה ישראל had the same symbolic meaning as ירושלים. This law is complemented by the law of וידוי מעשר (Ch. 26,12 et seq.) where the איסור אכילתו בטומאה ובאנינות for מעשר שני is mentioned (v.4).

עשר, numbers in the Piel elsewhere designate a multiplication of the number, שלש to triplicate (Gen. 15,9; Kings I, XVIII,34 and Eccles. 4,12); רבע to raise to the square, to place one measure on four sides (Kings I, VII,31 and Ezek. 40,46). But it is not impossible that here the Piel has the meaning of separating, putting aside, (like סקל ,דשן) and really means to take a tenth away, tithe.

עשר תעשר. In Numb. 18,21 et seq. it already speaks of a tenth which is to be given to the Levites from the “barns and wine-presses” of the people, as a wage for the Levites’ services at the Sanctuary. The use of this tithe, after separating out a tenth as Teruma for the priests stood entirely at the disposal of the Levites just as ordinary produce of the land and could be eaten by them as ordinary חולין wherever they pleased. Now here it says עשר תעשר, apart from that first tenth to be given to the Levites another tenth is to be separated out (see Sifri hereon) אין לי אלא מעשר שני שבו דבר הכתוב מנין לרבות שאר מעשרות ת״ל עשר תעשר. See רמב״ן on ספר את כל תבואת זרעך—.המצות שורש י״ב, we have already remarked in the chapter on מעשר in Numbers that, apart from the opinion of רמב״ם, the most general view is that the duty of תרומה ומעשרות applies מן התורה only to corn, wine and oil, as indeed in Numb. 18,12 and Deut. 12,17, in our following v. 23 and also in Ch. 18,4, they alone are expressly mentioned as those things to which this duty applies. The term כל תבואת זרעך would not be against this view. For תבואה is by no means a concept which embraces all the products of the soil. Even the opinion which extends the duty of תרומות ומעשרות beyond דגן תירוש ויצהר does not find this extension indicated by the term תבואה, not even by the all-including word כל (see on Jerushalmi מעשרות I,1, תוספות Bechoroth 54a, et seq.). Yea, even according to that opinion, in any case ירקות all vegetables are not included, and the Mishna (מעשרות I, 3, 6 et seq.) reckons special kinds of grain as being designated by תבואה. So that it is by no means far-fetched to understand by תבואת זרעך primarily those products of the land which comprise the real riches of the land, the harvest of which is what the farmers look forward to; that which they hope to bring in as תבואה (from בוא to come home) as the yield of the soil, what his sowing has brought out of the field (זרע היוצא השדה). It is just the תבואת גרן ותבואת יקב as it is called in Levit. 18,30. We also understand special cereals under the term “produce” or “fruits” (cf. ר״ה 12,b רש״י and רמב״ן .(ד״ה התבואת ,תוספות in his commentary explains כל תבואת זרעך as giving the admonition to tithe the whole output of all the products of the soil which are liable for such deduction and not to satisfy oneself with fulfilling this duty on some part of it.

In Baba Mezia 88,b, it is taught עשר תעשר ואכלת ולא מוכר תבואת זרעך ולא לוקח that the law of מעשר clearly refers to such produce that he who grew it did so for the purpose of his own use but not of such which he intended for sale; furthermore it refers to such which belong to him as being the producer, but not to such which he might buy. From this it follows that both buyer and seller מן התורה can avoid the duty of tithes. The deciding factor in this is in whose hands the produce was at the time it reached the stage at which the duty of giving the tithe arises. This is only at גמר מלאכה the moment the field work is finished. This moment is called גרנן למעשרות as differentiated from עונת המעשרות by which the degree of ripeness, the maturity of the produce on which the liability for tithing depends. This גרן למעשרות differs with different produce. For grain it is the moment it is laid in “level heaps”, נתמרח בכרי (the finishing process of storing up I.L.). This law is laid down already in the words מעשר דגנך וגו׳. For grain is only called דגן when it is “finished”, in evened heaps (Berochoth 47a). The phonetic relationship to תקן תכן would agree with indicating the underlying concept of דגן to be “being in order”, accordingly “being finished”. According to this only produce made ready for one’s own use is liable for the duty of taking tithes, and this duty remains obligatory even if subsequently it passes into other hands by sale. Equally the duty would fall on a buyer if he buys the produce before מירוה and he, the buyer, finishes it off to be ready for his own use. But produce bought made ready and finished for sale remains tithe-free permanently. A law which equally affects תרומות. (See הל׳ מעשר ,רמב״ם II, 1, 2, מל״ם on תרומות I, 11). ר״ת, Baba Mezia 88,a, ריטב״א and רשב״א are all in agreement with this way of taking the פטור לוקח. The ריב״ם and ראב״ד take it differently. But מדרבנן the obligation to tithe applies also to produce bought when made completely ready for sale, and they also forbid eating an אכילת קבע, more than just a casual taste, even if the produce is still in an unripe condition. A further limitation in the imposition of these duties lies in the manner in which the produce is brought home viz: אין הטבל מתחייב במעשר עד שיראה פני הבית, tithe is only obligatory מן התורה if the produce is brought in openly through the front door, but not if it is taken home דרך גגות וקרפיפות as we should say, “through the back door” (Baba Mezia 88,a;—see on Ch. 26,13).
היצא השדה. Cf. וצא השדה (Gen. 27,3), נצא השדה (Sam. I. 20,11) etc. accordingly here “that which comes out on the field each year from your sowing”.

שנה שנה. The produce of each year has to be tithed separately by itself. אין תורמין ומעשרין לא מן החדש על הישן ולא מן הישן על החדש, “one may not separate tithes or teruma neither from this year’s produce from previous years, nor from previous years from that of this year”. (Rosh Hashona 12,b). For grain the year is reckoned from the first of Tishri, for fruit from the fifteenth of Shevat, and the produce is reckoned to belong to the year within which it has reached the stage of לעונת המעשרות, one third towards complete maturity שהביאו שליש (see תוספות there ד״ה תבואה). For fruit this beginning of ripening is called חנטה. So that grain which has reached this stage before Rosh Hashona, and fruit before the fifteenth of Shevat belong to the previous year even if they only really ripen during this year.

As is prescribed in verses 28 and 29, every third year the tithe to be given differs from the two preceding years. מעשר ראשון, the tithe to be given to the Levite has to be given every year (except of course in the seventh year, the Schemita, when all produce is common property I.L.), מעשר ראשון הקישו הכתוב לנחלה מה נחלה אין לה הפסק אף מעשר ראשון אין לו הפסק (ibid—see on Numb. 18,24). But regarding the second tithe, there is a difference. In the first and second, the fourth and fifth year of each Schemita period, in addition to מעשר ראשון, the second tithe מעשר שני, prescribed here to be eaten by yourself in Jerusalem, had to be separated out. In every third and sixth year, מעשר עני took the place of this, the second tithe was distributed to the poor who could eat it wherever they pleased. For this too the עונת המעשרות applies, and whether that occurred before or after ר״ה, or before or after ט״ו בשבט decides whether the produce belongs to מעשר שני or מעשר עני.

The purposes which are to be served by מעשר ראשון מעשר שני מעשר עני correspond entirely to the purposes to which our material means altogether could be, and should be, directed. They are the care of the spirit, one’s spiritual life—the tithe to be given to the Levite—; the care of the body, one’s material life—the tithe to be eaten by oneself in Jerusalem—; the care of the well-being of one’s fellow-man—the tithe to be given to the poor. But if we consider the facts that מן התורה only דגן תירוש ויצהר are tithable and those only if they are made ready for your own personal use נתמרח לאכילה but not if prepared for sale, and that they altogether only become liable if they are brought openly and publicly into your house or yard, כשראו פני הבית, then we think that we can say:- in no wise is the care for these three purposes of our endeavours in life to be considered as accomplished by giving these three tithes which are conditional to such definite formal limitations. The adequate attention to these purposes is a responsibility which rests on the whole of our means (see on Ch. 15,8). They and their requirements remain, quite apart from just the specified amount from certain specified parts of our possessions which the Torah prescribes (and which we could easily legally avoid paying I.L.). These three tithes are just to bring to our minds our duty to assign, dedicate and direct the whole of our fortune to these three purposes prescribed by God, as is expressed in the words of our מעשר שני chapter here:- למען תלמד ליראה מעשר מן התורה .את ה׳ א׳ כל הימים is an act of acknowledging the dedication of our “working for our livlihood”. The finished fruits of the foremost rank of our work, now placed ready for our own use may not be surrendered for our consumption and enjoyment before a providing tribute is paid to the landless Levite tribe, who represent the care and nurture of the Torah, and to the teaching of the sanctification of our lives of enjoyment of our senses before the Presence of God, or in the the third year to the care of the lives of our needy brethren.

And God’s Law has handed over the procedure of this so significant and important duty of tithes entirely to the cheerful Jewish readiness to do mitzvas. The owner can legally evade paying them. If he wishes to bring his harvest home through quiet byways, דרך גגות וקרפיפות the duty to do this mitzva does not affect him. He can eat up all that he brings home without giving a thought to the Levi or the poor, and without a thought of having to enjoy it before the Presence of God in the vicinity of the national Sanctuary of the Torah. But if he wishes, in joy of God’s blessing of his labours, to bring his harvest happily through the opened gates of his yard and his home, then this mitzva is obligatory, and God reckoned on that, that Jewish landowners would not taste the blessing of harvest if they evade the duty of doing this mitzva by roundabout means. That is why a later generation could sadly look back at the “good old times when the produce used to be brought home through the wide-opened gates just to make the tithes encumbent on it, whereas nowadays, alas we all bring it home through the back door to avoid having to perform that mitzva”. בא וראה שלא כדורות הראשנים דורות האחרונים דורות הראשונים היו מכניסין פירותיהן דרך טרקסמון כדי לחייבן במעשר דורות אחרונים מכניסין פירותיהן דרך גגות דרך חצרות דרך קרפיפות כדי לפטרן מן המעשר (ברכות ל״ה ב׳). And in Baba Mezia 88,a, the early decline of the fruit trade in Israel referred back to the fact that the dealers took advantage of the opportunity given to them by the Torah to evade the duty of giving tithes by arranging their business on the basis of buyer and seller. מפני מה חרבו חניות של בית הינו שלש שנים קודם ירושלים מפני שהעמידו דבריהם על דברי תורה שהיו אומרים עשר תעשר ואכלת ולא מוכר תבואת זרעך ולא לוקח.

But as all produce must be tithed separately for the year and within the year, thereby the special השגחה פרטית (the individual care of God’s Providence I.L.) is brought to mind which makes the work of each separate year and of each different kind of produce the object of His Loving Care.

V. 23. לפני ה׳ וגו׳. See on previous verse. — ובכרת בקרך וגו׳. From what follows it is clear that בכורות cannot be the real object of this law. In v.24 it is prescribed that in the event of the foods mentioned in v.3 not being able to be taken up to the place of the Sanctuary in its natural state it may be redeemed by money and that money taken there and spent on eatables there. But in no case can a בכור בהמה טהורה be redeemed as is expressly said in Numb. 18,17. As תם, its אימורים have to be brought on the Altar and the meat eaten by the priests within the city of the Sanctuary; as בעל מום it is still the property of the priests, but, without any redeeming, may be eaten by anybody elsewhere. In no case are the laws which follow here applicable to it. So that here too only דגנך תירושך ויצהרך can be the real actual objects of which the verse is speaking, and בכורות בקרך וצאנך can only be brought in as being in an explanatory relationship to ,מעשר וגו׳ בכור בהמה טהורה belongs to that very first institution with which God pronounced His “לי״ on the people He had redeemed, and out of this “לי״ the holiness of every individual and all the property of this nation resulted. This sanctification was expressed by בכור בהמה טהורה, by which the food, the nourishing of all Jewish families is considered as being in service of the Sanctuary of the Torah, making the giving up of one’s life to nurturing godliness on earth (as expressed by הקטרת אימורים) the goal of all one’s endeavours and desires (expressed by חלב וכליות), and family meals enjoyed priest-like before God’s Presence (symbolically expressed by the priests and their families נשיהם ובניהם ועבדיהם eating it in the City of God). The whole institution is kept up by constant reference back to the hour of the birth of the Jewish nation, which, by the fall of the might of the Pharoahs and the destruction of the flower of the Egyptian families being eternally kept in mind, is to be a constant warning to Israel of the seriousness of obedience to God being the condition for all the “blossoming” of their families. That which בכור בהמה טהורה teaches symbolically as the ideal is to be carried out concretely in actuality by every individual by מעשר שני. Out of that which he has got ready of the foremost products of God’s land for himself and his family he extracts a tenth as ממון גבוה as the property of God, as קדש, as sanctified to the Sanctuary, not to give it to priest or Levite, but to become himself in spirit, priest and Levite, to take it up to God’s city of the Sanctuary of the Torah to eat it himself. There to enjoy it in priestly purity and priestly feelings of life—שלא בטומאה ושלא באנינות (see Ch. 26,14)—before the Presence of God, as being seen by his God in the neighbourhood of His God, and so to learn that true joy has its roots only in the true fear of God which makes every phase of life, even eating, even all that is the most sensuous lived in the Presence of God, and which knows how to elevate even the pleasures of indulgence to a holy and sanctifying godly act. למען תלמד ליראה את ה׳ א׳ כל הימים.

This connection between בכורות and מעשר שני in our verse is also taken in Temura 21,a & b, in a similar way to establish equality between them—היקש—from which is deduced that just as for בכור the importance of Jerusalem lay in the existence of the Temple, and the radius within which it was permitted to eat it was the walls of the city, these same restrictions בפני בית and לפנים מן החומה apply equally to מעשר שני. And also just as מעשר דגן had to be brought to Jerusalem only if grown within the Land so were בכורות from חוצה לארץ precluded from being brought as offerings in the Temple ממקום שאתה מעלה מעשר דגן אתה מעלה בכור וגו׳, and equally so, a בכור does not lose its fitness to be brought in its second year as מעשר דגן also does not become unfit to be brought if left from one year to the next, is not נפסל משנה לחברתה.

V. 24. וכי ירבה וגו׳. These repeated restricting conditions under which redeeming by money is permitted, כי ירחק, כי לא תוכל וגו׳, וכי ירבה, seem to indicate that preference is given to bringing the tithes up in their natural state, and that changing them to money itself might be only a sign of God’s blessing showing itself in the rich abundance of the harvest, and perhaps also in the wide borders of the land, both of which are adduced as reasons for making the change. Nevertheless according to the halacha changing the produce into money is allowed in every case where it may not be eaten in its natural state, i.e. anywhere outside Jerusalem, or within Jerusalem if it has become טמא and so may not be eaten there. According to Makkoth 19,b that is why our text uses the term לא תוכל שאתו ,שאת, because this term occurs also with the meaning of “serving up” food (Gen. 43,33), so that here it could mean either “you cannot carry it up” as well as “you cannot serve it up for eating” because it is מן התורה .טמא, even if מעשר שני has been inside Jerusalem it may be taken outside the walls and redeemed, but מדרבנן if it is טהור then קלטוהו מחיצות לפדיון once it has been in the city it may not be taken out and redeemed (ibid, 20,a).

V. 25. ונתת בכסף: then place it in money, transfer its character and its purpose to money. This is the case which was foreseen in Levit. 27,31, for which the order was given that if the owner himself redeems it he has to add a חומש.

וצרת הכסף בידך (cf. Kings II, V,23). But here this expression “you press the money tightly in your hand” is inserted in this sentence with essential reference to a particular detail concerning this law. For צור and צרר mean to press together, to compress something into the smallest possible space. Now here it is speaking of the case where the tithe of the produce is too much and too voluminous to take it up to Jerusalem in its natural form. Towards that the term וצרת is expressly used in order to say: by the exchange to money its size is to be reduced to such a small circumference that you can carry it up in your hand. That at once gives the order that it may only be exchanged into money, and moreover in current coin that, at any moment, can be transferred back to similar produce, so that the original object remains present in one’s mind and one can say one has the exchanged object in one’s hand. In “money” the most voluminous object can be concentrated into the smallest space. Hence ”וצרת״ הכסף בידך, and the halacha teaches:

- אין מחללין מע״ש על אסימון ולא על מטבע שאינו יוצא ולא על המעות שאינן ברשותו “one may not redeem מעשר שני by blank coins (according to תוספות Baba Mezia 44,a, even if they are not properly stamped) nor by coins which are not current and not by money which is not available to him at the moment” (Masser Sheni 1,2). If in Baba Mezia 47,b, ר׳ ישמעאל explains וצרת הכסף בידך as meaning לרבות כל דבר שנצרר ביד to include everything that can be compressed into the hand which would include unstamped (or imperfectly stamped) coins but ר׳ עקיבא says לרבות כל דבר שיש עליו צורה, any coin which is stamped, this would not be merely mnemonically from the similar sound of צרת and צורה but would be deduced from such stamped coins being a more complete conception of נצרר ביד as in fact only with a stamped coin can the redeemed object be considered epitomised in the hand (as it can be exchanged back immediately without weighing or valuation as would be the case with unstamped coins I.L.). The Jerusalmi similarly refers the demand that the money be current to the wording רמב״ם) שיש לו צורה ויוצא על גב צורתו :וצרת וגו׳ and ר״ש refer to v.26 where the wording ונתת הכסף וגו׳ by which the currency of the coins is obviously assumed. We can find this דרשה neither in the Sifri nor in either of the Talmuds). As long as the produce has not been brought to Jerusalem, enjoying it without its having been redeemed is forbidden by virtue of לאו הבא מכלל עשה. So that the produce itself or the money into which it has been transformed must be taken up to Jerusalem and no use may be made of it. But this prohibition (to make use of it other than in the prescribed manner I.L.) only attains the degree of making the transgressor liable to מלקות when it is within the walls surrounding the city: מע״ש מאימתי חייבין עליו משראה פני החומה then קלטוה מחיצות then they are accepted by the national ground of the Sanctuary of the Torah to be eaten within sight of the Temple. Then it says regarding it: לא תוכל לאכול בשעריך מעשר דגנך וגו׳ כי אם לפני ה׳ אלקיך תאכלנו, Ch. 12,17 & 18 (Makkoth 19b, and 20a), and eating it outside the area of the city without redeeming it would be a positive denial of the fundamental truth of the fact which אכילה לפני ה׳ (eating before the Presence of God I.L.) is to bring home to us, the inclusion of the life of our sensual pleasures in the sanctification which is to emanate from the Sanctuary of the Torah.

V. 26. ונתת הכסף בכל וגו׳. By spending the money on food, the מעשר שני character which rests on the money is transferred to the objects bought by it which then may only be eaten in the City of God and not בטומאה ואנינות, but the money becomes חולין, loses the character of a holy object. בכל אשר תאוה וגו׳ בבקר וגו׳ ובכל אשר תשאלך נפשך is a classical example of the rule of interpretation כלל ופרט וכלל (two general propositions separated by an enumeration of particulars, include only such things as are similar to those specified I.L.), the various ways of taking which, as רבוי מעוט ורבוי or כללא בתרא דוקא or כללא קמא דוקא we have already worked out on Levit. 11,9. The “particulars”, the “פרט״ which are mentioned here, בקר צאן יין ושכר have three essential characteristics according to Eruvin 27,b גידולי קרקע פרי מפרי וולד וולדות הארץ. All the objects brought as “פרט״ have these characteristics in common: they are all organic produce (פרי מפרי), obtain their nourishment from the ground (גידולי קרקע) and originally were created from the earth (וולד וולדות הארץ). Taken as רבוי מיעוט ורבוי, the רבוי would give the most extensive conception, would include everything that had only the one characteristic of being פרי מפרי, an organic product, all animals and plants. Then דגיס, fish, would also be included, and the only inorganic materials as מים ומלח, water and salt would be excluded. As כללא בתרא דוקא the objects to be included must have at least two of the פרט characteristics. דגים, fish would be excluded and only עופות, birds included as being organic products and obtaining their nourishment from the earth פרי מפרי וגדולי קרקע although, according to Chulin 27,b, in their original creation they do not belong to the creatures that were created purely from the earth תוציא הארץ but are in the middle between those and the creatures that were created from the water ישרצו המים and מן הרקק נבראו (birds were created from the alluvial mud I.L.) and so would lack the third sign וולד וולדות הארץ. As כללא קמא דוקא birds would also be excluded as they have not all three of the characteristics which are common to the פרט (see Eruvin 27,b).

ושמחת אתה וביתך. In Yebomoth 62,b, it is pointed out how the Torah considers happiness only to be found in married life, that unmarried men could not be really happy כל יהודי שאין לו אשה שרוי בלא שמחה דכתיב ושמחת אתה וביתך.

V. 27. והלוי וגו׳: refer to Ch. 12,12 & 19. We have already remarked that the entirely conditional and limited manner which the Torah prescribes for the duty of tithes could make us recognise that the puposes to which the tithes are to be used—including the provision for the Levites by מעשר ראשון—are in no wise completely fulfilled by these tithes, which are rather to be considered merely as an admonition to the duty of fulfilling of them,—an admonition coming particularly aptly at the moment we are about to use our produce already indicated in the words עשר תעשר which indicates מעשר שני as a second, repeated tithe, and here also the והלוי אשר בשעריך לא תעזבנו would refer to something more than מעשר ראשון. Thus the Sifri on our verse: בכל מקום שאתה מוצא הלוי הזה תן לו מחלקו אין לו חלקו תן לו מעשר עני — (כן הוא גירסת הילקוט, בספרי איתא מעשר שני, ונראה דלפי דקי״ל (קידושין נ״ד ב׳) כר״מ דממון גבוה הוא ולא מצי יהיב ליה במתנה גירסת הילקוט עיקר) אין לו מעשר עני תן לו שלמים אין לו שלמים פרנסהו מן הצדקה.

The בכל מקום שאתה מוצא הלוי הזה of the Sifri seems to be an explanation of אשר בשעריך, and to support the way we take it (Ch. 12,12) that, regardless of the special cities which were given over to them, the Levites lived scattered about in the land amongst the people.

V. 28. מקצה שלש שנים, every third year of the Schemita cycle, i.e. in the third and sixth year of that period, the whole of the second tenth about which the previous verses have been speaking, instead of being destined for one’s own enjoyment in Jerusalem is given away (תוציא) and left there at home for the poor, which is referred to again in Ch. 26,12. There, speaking of this third year, it says כי תכלה לעשר וגו׳, with this third year a tithe-cycle comes to an end. The first two years of the cycle, i.e. in the first and second, in the fourth and fifth מעשר ראשון and מעשר שני are to be given, in each third year, i.e. in the third and sixth מעשר עני takes the place of מעשר שני, and, as is there prescribed, at the end of every such three years cycle, every tithe which has been payable during those three years must have been used for the purpose designed for it. None of it may any longer be found in the possession of the tithable owner. (ibid. 13). Now, as v.22 says, all produce belongs to the year in which it reaches the עונת מעשר maturity, the end of the cycle of the third year for some produce reaches until about Chanuca time (see on Ch. 26,11) i.e. right up to then, some produce which is liable for מעשר is only harvested then; because of this the “tithe-confession”, ודוי מעשר, was only made on ערב י״ט אחרון של פסח of the fourth year (see ibid. 13).
והנחת בשעריך, according to the Sifri, if one had not been able to distribute it oneself, it had to be deposited in an official civic storehouse for the poor.
V. 29. ובא הלוי, either as being presumably without means and entitled to מעשר עני, or at the same time it includes the מעשר ראשון which has to be separated out for the Levites each year.

To the repeated reason given for the duty of giving tithe to the Levite כי אין לו חלק ונחלה עמל, the Halacha attaches the law, that הפקר, all ownerless produce, hence also לקט שכחה ופיאה is not subject to tithe, only ממה שיש לד ואין לו חייב אתה ליתן לו יצאה הפקר שידך וידו שוין on that to which you have the right to take but he has no right is the duty of tithe applicable, but not to that which grows wild or is ownerless and is available to him as much as to you (Jerusalmi מעשרות I,1).

V. 1. The previous chapter closed with the law of מעשר עני. Inasmuch as thereby in every third year this tithe for the poor took the place of what otherwise was to be eaten in happy enjoyment before God in the City of God, it set the care for the well-being of your poor neighbour as the consequence of your own enjoyment before God; and Jewish feelings were trained to the tendency of feeling that they could not enjoy their happiness before God without doing whatever lay in their power to make their poorer brethren participate in their happiness. שׇׂמחתי ושִׂמחתי “I have been happy and given happiness” runs the concluding sentence of the “confession of tithe-giving” at the end of every three years’ cycle (Ch. 26,14). But inasmuch as untithed produce, even if it is only מעשר שני that has not been separated out from it, is טבל, and as such may not be used for yourself, it is brought to the mind of those working for their own living, that with their work and the produce of it they do not stand merely in the service of their own existence, but that God places them and the results of their work also in the service of the existence of their neighbour and the happiness of their neighbour. That He is the One Who has the disposition of the fruits of their labour for the existence of the needy neighbour, and expects the care for the well-being of the neighbour from every member of the propertied class.

That by מעשר עני the duty of caring for the poor and needy which is incumbent on everybody, is by no means discharged, that it, like the other מתנות עניים, is only to bring home to the propertied class, the deep seriousness of their responsibilities—as we have repeatedly had occasion to remark—is perfectly clear by the laws of שמיטת כספים and צדקה which follow here, in which the duties towards our poorer brethren is designated as being of a much wider nature.

The reason that these laws were kept back primarily for this compendium for those entering the land is quite evidently—apart from the fact that, according to the Sifri, the laws of שמיטת כספים did not apply at all in the wilderness—that during the years of the wandering, of which it is said לא חסרת דבר, there would hardly have been any opportunity of fulfilling these duties at all.

מקץ שבע שנים. Already in Ex. 23,10 & 11, and in detail in Levit. 25,2-7, the character of a Sabbath Year is conferred on every seventh year, as being a part of the great Youvel institution; a year of acknowledging God as being the real Lord and Owner of the Land. For its duration all Man’s mastery of the soil comes to a halt, no field or orchard is worked, no harvest brought home, but all that the soil produces by itself becomes the common property of all men and animals. Now here one final result still emanates from God’s rights of possession of the soil which is the means of our existence. At the moment that the Sabbath Year ends it makes us look on God and acknowledge Him as being the Lord over and having the disposal of our fortune altogether and obliges, in the Name of the God Whose Rule every blade of grass has proclaimed for a full year, every creditor to forego every justified claim for any debt which is due to be paid and has not hitherto been settled. The fact that שביעית משמטת כסופה that this releasing of claims for debts by the Sabbath Year being effected just at its last moment (Arachin 28b) and that, according to the general opinion, the שמיטת כספים and שמיטת קרקע are connected with Youvel, so that at the present day, after the cessation of the Youvel, שביעית, regarding both of them is only מדרבנן (see Moed Katon 2,b, תוספות Kiddushin 38b, Gittin 36a, כסף משנה on הל׳ שמיטה ויובל IV,25), makes, so we believe, שמיטת כספים be considered as the consequence of שמיטת קרקע.

V. 2. וזה דבר השמטה שמוט וגו׳. In Gittin 36,a, רבי teaches: וזה דבר השמטה שמוט בשתי שמיטות הכתוב מדבר אחת שמיטת קרקע ואחת שמיטת כספים בזמן שאתה משמט קרקע אתה משמט כספים בזמן שאי אתה משמט קרקע אי אתה משמט כספים, and says thereby just the same law quoted on the previous verse according to which the שמיטה freeing the debt from the hand of the debtor is dependent on its freeing the land from the hand of its present holder, whether as Rashi refers the שמיטת קרקע to the stoppage of agriculture, or as ר״ת takes it, to the return of landed property in Youvel (see תוספות there). In any case in this sentence of the teaching of רבי the שמיטה in זה דבר השמיטה of our verse is taken to refer to שמיטת קרקע and not to כסף, so that it might not be at all far-fetched to take our two verses to mean:- With the end of every seventh year you are to make one further renunciation, and that is to “let your hand go” not to demand the repayment of any loan you have made which you would legally be justified in making. It is difficult to find a suitable word for שמט, literally to escape from your hand, to apply to releasing a debt as it does to refraining from agricultural work—the land escaping from being mastered by Man, and returning landed property that you have bought—the land escaping from “strange” ownership.
כל בעל, like בעל הבית (Ex. 32,7), בעל דברים (ibid. XXIV,14), בעל משפטי (Is. 50,5), אל תמנע טוב מבעליו (Prov. 3,27 etc.).

משה ידו, like משא כל יד (Neh. 10,32). We have already worked out on Ex. 22,24, from the underlying meaning of the root נשה that the term means an unsatisfied claim. At the time of contracting the debt the creditor has not yet become a נושה, that, he only becomes at the moment he can demand the repayment. So that משה ידו אשר ישה ברעהו would be demands for all debts of which the repayment had become due before the end of the seventh year. Accordingly מלוה, primarily, demands for repayment of loans, the time for which had not been fixed expressly beyond this date and also demands arising out of business contracts as soon as they obtain the character of a debt for a loan זקפן עליו במלוה i.e. as soon as the persons have been notified that they are now due to be paid (e.g. הקפת חנות shopkeepers’ accounts, which the seller likes to run up to a larger amount, only אם עשאה מלוה, if he has added them up to the total owing and notified the customer, or according to others credit accounts as soon as they have reached the agreed pay day, Schevouth 10,1; Makkoth 3b; (see ח״ם 67,14 and ב״ח there).

לא יגש וגו׳. When the end of the Sabbath Year has passed and a debt which was due had not been paid, the creditor may no longer demand it, for קרא שמיטה לה׳, at the end of that year he has to testify to the fact that the real Lord and Owner of all possessions is God, Who has declared the remission of all demands for debts which have become due up till then.

But this remission, literally, this “allowing to escape out of your hand” is entirely only one-sided. The creditor, the בעל, who by virtue of his legal claim on his neighbour had become a person in power, holding him in his hand, renounces for ever his right to assert that power. But the debtor remains for ever morally in his debt and duty-bound to repay him, and if the debtor offers voluntarily to discharge the debt the creditor certainly has to declare משמט אני and place the Shemita privilege at his disposal. But if nevertheless the debtor persists in the repayment, the creditor may accept it. Yea, it is by no means the tendency of the Torah to release people who can pay from their moral duty of discharging their moral obligations, and from such people the creditor can expect (this is the ותלי ליה in Gittin 37,b:- see רא״ש thereon) that they will make no use of the releasing Schemita favour. המחזיר חוב בשביעית יאמר לו משמט אני אמר לו אעפ״י כן יקבל ממנו שנאמר וזה דבר השמטה וגו׳ (שביעית י״ח). The Shemita declaration to be made by the creditor is what the Torah demands (דבר the words I.L.) but the relation of the debtor to the debt remains unaltered by it. In this שביעית is different from רבית which equally forbids the debtor to pay interest and the creditor to accept it. But the debtor who voluntarily pays a debt which was remitted by Shemita is only acting in the true sense of the Torah, המחזיר חוב בשביעית רוח חכמים נוחה ממנו (ibid.6).

It is with the title רעהו and אחיו that Shemita expresses its prohibition:- לא יגש את רעהו ואת אחיו. The Sabbath Year which brings the thought of God being connected with and entering into, the conditions of social life in the most actual practical manner, at its departure wishes to see us united again as רעים and אחים (true friends and brothers I.L.). Accordingly it places the flourishing of the well-being of one’s neighbour near to the heart of every man, and demands the breaking of the chains of debt which otherwise everywhere bind down permanently the free development of the powers of gaining their livelihood of those around whose necks they are hung. With the passing of the Shemita period all debts which have been contracted are reduced to moral obligations only, the settlement of which is left to the time and convenience which the debtor himself settles. Instead of the depression with which his debt loads him, he feels himself elevated by the confidence which the Torah places in him and he will make the repayment of what was a legal obligation and is now left entirely to his own free will, a matter of honour. The title רע (friend, worked out elsewhere as meaning being mutually the “shepherd”, the one who looks after the well-being and “pasturage” of the other I.L.) tells both the creditor and the debtor what is expected of them, and it is God the Father of them all, Who wishes to see them, in the exercise of such sentiments, as His children, as brothers in His household. (See Levit. on XIX,17 (p.522) and 18 (p.527).

V. 3. ולא של אחיד בידך :אשר יהיה לד את אחיך, the Shemita release only applies to the demand for payment of such loans the whole payment of which is in the hands of the debtor, but not if the creditor has security in his hands for it, המלוה על המשכון אין שמיטה משמטת (Baba Metzia 48b).

שמיטת כספים is only a complementary part of the great institution of Youvel, the great importance of which we have already worked out on Levit. 25,8 et seq. (see on v.10 p. 739). Just as the releasing powers of the Youvel extended to the members of the nation who were living outside the Land, so, as long as the laws of the Youvel were still in existence, did the law of שמיטת כספים which was dependent on it extend מן התורה to those living outside the Land (Kiddushin 38,b), and this extension of the Shemita effect is referred to the repeated כי קרא שמיטה לה׳. After שמיטת כספים is first connected to and made dependent on שמיטת קרקע by וזה דבר השמיטה שמוט וגו׳, by כי קרא שמיטה לה׳ the Shemita institution is repeated as being a personal independent duty, and thereby שמיטת כספים being conditional on שמיטת קרקע is to be taken only referring to time but not to place. וזה דבר השמיטה שמוט בשתי שמיטות הכתוב מדבר אחת שמיטת קרקע ואחת שמיטת כספים בזמן שאתה משמט קרקע אתה משמט כספים בזמן שאין אתה משמט קרקע אי אתה משמט כספים, ואימא במקום שאתה משמט קרקע אתה משמט כספים ובמקום שאין אתה משמט קרקע אין אתה משמט כספים ת״ל כי קרא שמטה לה׳ מכל מקום (see on v.2).

V. 4 & 5. אפס כי וגו׳. In the preceding verse the case is taken where one had borrowed from another but could not meet his obligations when the time for repayment became due so that recourse would have to have been made to the court to have the repayment enforced, a condition of debt, the continuance of which was what the Shemita institution was to prevent. This verse refers to the assumption that there would be such cases and remarks:- אביון .אפס כי לא יהיה בך אביון from אבה to submit to the will of somebody else, exactly describes the state of social dependence into which the impecunious debtor has fallen with regards to his creditor. The creditor has his future in his hands, at any moment he can exert his rights, the debtor loses all independence towards him must “fit in with his wishes” in all matters to keep in his good books and retain his favour. It is just this unhappy relationship which in other circles has undermined so much social happiness and political welfare. In that אביון is differentiated from עני .עני from ענה, designates poverty the dependence of existence אביון the dependence of will which results from it. The impecunious workman can earn his daily bread by his work but his virile independence remains completely untouched thereby. And even in the recepients of alms this independence is maintained in a much higher degree and only really disappears with liabilities which cannot be met. But poverty leading to such dependence and submission, it now says here, should really not occur in the Jewish State blossoming under God’s guidance and God’s blessing. After all איש תחת גפנו ותחת תאנתו “every man under his own vine and under his own fig-tree” (Micha 4,4) is an ideal which beckons mankind in general only in the distant future, but which under God’s guidance should have first become realised in the Jewish Torah-state. But the attainment of this ideal in Israel is just dependent on the complete fulfilment of the Torah and especially just on these Shemita and Youvel laws and the laws of Zedaka which result from them, which God has set as the condition for His constant Youvel-regeneration of the Jewish national body of the State. (See on Levit. 25,10 & 11). It is just the bringing about of this ideal that כל המצוה הזאת אשר אנכי מצוך היום has in view.

V. 6. כי ה׳ אלקיך וגו׳. When, by the fulfilment of God’s Torah you will have made yourself recipients of His Blessing, then, just by this national condition of prosperity which finds its realisation, not in a brilliant powerful state with a stunted standard of life of the inhabitants, but in the well-to-do prosperity of every individual citizen, then you will shine forth high above the other nations. With your national riches and surplus you will help the requirements and deficiencies of other nations, thereby they will lie under an obligation to you and be dependent on you, but you will remain the free and independent nation. A condition of national welfare and independence which, had it attained permanent realisation, would more than anything else have brought the nations already long ago to have expressed the wish: ויורנו מדרכיו ונלכה באורחותיו (Is. 2,3).

עבט, a strong form of עבד, designates the obligation to repay a loan, and also that which stands security for that duty, a pledge. From that, in Talmudic legal language is the term שעבוד. Related to it is עבת, a cord, similar to חבל and חבול, to pawn, and it could be the underlying conception of עבד, bound to somebody higher, to be unfree.

V. 7. כי יהיה בך אביון can only be said with any decisiveness to a community. One cannot say to an individual as such, “if there is a poor man amongst you”. לא תאמץ לבבך, and also the following sayings, according to the whole choice of the words used, are directed primarily to the individual. So that here the Torah has the community and the individual simultaneously in mind. The duty of caring and providing for the poor accordingly rests both on the community and equally on every single member of it. But that is characteristic of an essential principle of this law. There are few, perhaps not one single other, tasks which require the continuous activity of the community and the individual at the same time, as, in accordance with this law, the duty of caring for the poor demands. That which—as we shall see—this law demands cannot be accomplished by either the community or the individual alone. Both must join forces, both work hand in hand if the goal set by the Torah is to be reached. The notice affixed to houses “no beggars need apply, the owners subscribe generously to the public funds” has not engendered the Jewish spirit which this law has nourished. (see next verse).

מאחד אחיך. The sense of the law is:- as soon as there is even a single person in your city or your country who is in need of help, then there is a poor man amongst you, within the radius of your duty from whom you may not turn away; and the halacha teaches from the order of our text—ארצך ,שעריך ,אחיך—that relations have precedence to others, the poor of your city to strangers, and from abroad, the poor of the Jewish Land to those of other countries. (Sifri, ש״ך ,251,3 י״ד thereon, כנה״ג thereon).

לא תאמץ את לבבך, literally: you shall not be strong against your heart. This assumes that Jewish hearts left to their natural bent are inclined to benevolence, and this inclination can only be overcome by cold, calculating, selfish considerations. Equally so Jewish hands open by themselves to the poor and can only be closed by similar regards, hence ולא תקפץ את ידך.

In this chapter the poor are repeatedly designated אחיך. In every poor man, immaterially whether you know him or not there stands a brother, a child of your Father in heaven before you, and brings you a recommendation from your and his Father.

V. 8. כי פתח תפתח. All the commandments of benevolence are here proclaimed in this amplifying form פתח ,נתון תתן, העבט תעביטנו תפתח, and indeed, according to Baba Mezia 31,a & b, the unlimited number of times one has, if necessary, to repeat one’s charitable actions אפילו מאה פעמים—even a hundred times—lies already in the indefinite tense of the infinitive נתון ,העבט ,פתוח, while the addition of the definite tense extends the duty also in other directions e.g.: פתח תפתח: אין לי אלא לעניי עירך לעניי עיר אחרת מנין ת״ל פתח תפתח מכל מקום נתן תתן אין לי אלא מתנה מרובה מתנה מועטת מנין ת״ל נתן תתן מכל מקום. So that by the duty being expressed in the form נתון תתן ,פתח תפתח it is not only extended to each repeated opportunity אפי׳ מאה פעמים which would already lie in the infinitive form of the proclamation, but also to needy cases abroad, and not only confined to rich people who can give big amounts but also to less rich people from whom the fulfilment of this duty is equally expected, even if they can only give the very smallest amount. In the sphere of this duty the smallest weighs equally with the greatest, if the means do not reach to more. (If here עניי עיר אחרת is learnt from the פתח תפתח :רבוי whereas according to the Sifri, this is already expressed by עניי עירך in בשעריך as well as those בארצך, it could be in the sense of the טור (י״ד 257; see ב״ח there) that it requires a double extension for עניי עיר אחרת, to include those living in their home cities and those of them who may be temporarily in our town). According to the Sifri, the רבוי also extends the manner in which the duty has to be performed, making it necessary to adjust one’s assistance in accordance with the requirements of each particular case: פתח תפתח נתן תתן למה נאמר כולם מגיד הכתוב הראוי ליתן לו פת נותנים לו פת הראוי ליתן לו עיסה נותנים לו .עיסה הראוי ליתן לו מעה נותנים לו מעה הראוי להאכיל בתוך פיו מאכילים אותו בתוך פיו

והעבט תעביטנו, or, according to circumstances support him with a loan. And (Sabbat 43a) helping with a loan is considered a still higher form of benevolence than the giving of charity, because the borrower is helped to carry on his means of gaining his livelihood by it and at receiving it feels much less humiliated. גדול המלוה יותר מן העושה צדקה, and there it adds: ומטיל לכיס יותר מכולן, but the highest form of all, is for the rich man to keep the business going by investing a sum of money in it and so having a share in it, for then he is supporting the poorer man and treating him as an absolute equal and this form of exercising benevolence does not hurt the feelings of the receipient in any way. Altogether preventing anybody from falling into straightened circumstances is the very highest mission of benevolence as is made into a duty in Levit. 25,35 (refer to it). At the same time תעבט תעביטנו makes the suggestion that if the one who requires help is reluctant to accept it as a gift one should give it in the form of a loan. אין לו ואינו רוצה להתפרנס תן לו דרך הלואה. (Baba Mezia 31,b).

די מחסרו in these two words—sufficient for his need—the greatness of the Jewish duty of benevolence reaches its summit. The want of the poor man is to be made completely good by us אי אתה מצווה להעשירו, you are not called on to make him rich (Sifri) but what he “lacks” is to be supplied, and moreover אשר יחסר לו, with consideration of his particular position, and what possibly may be indispensable to him on account of habits formed in his previous better circumstances אפילו סוס לרכוב עליו ועבד לרוץ לפניו (Kethuvoth 67,b; refer to it there).

The admonition נתון תתן ,פתוח תפתח, and די מחסורו and on the other hand the warning לא תאמץ את לבבך ולא תקפץ את ידך מאחיך האביון has produced the whole wonder of Jewish benevolence which to this very day makes the scattered sons of the House of Jacob constituted into one great benevolent society for the relief of distress, to which every wretchedness in any Jewish hut, and every heavy heart, can turn. The duty to satisfy the requirements of the poor in every direction די מחסורו, has, on the one hand brought about the necessity to make the care of the poor a matter to be taken in hand by every Jewish community for the purpose of which it is authorised to levy a forced tax on the means of its members ממשכנין על הצדקה, (Baba Bathra 8,b), but on the other hand makes this duty by no means accomplished by this, but opens up an untiring noblest benevolent sphere of private charitable deeds and voluntary relief societies. The task which the duty of Jewish Zedaka imposes is so serious and so great that only the combination of these three factors, the community, the societies and private individuals working together can come near to accomplishing it. For כל הנופל אינו נופל לידי גבאי תחלה it says already in Nedarim 65b, “everybody who becomes needy is not at once to have to apply publicly to the administrator of public funds, the friends and relations have first to see what they can do, and only where that does not suffice does the community make the deficiency up. For the need of those who have become impoverished and are ashamed to apply for public alms and the requirements which arise everywhere for special cases remain the finest objects of delicate private benevolence. But equally so these purposes which can only be served efficiently by the care of the community, such as e.g. schools and care for the instruction of the children of the poor. This has always, from time immemorial been considered so much a communal task that it had become a habit erroneously—quite erroneously—to give the title תלמוד תורה, amongst the obligations which lay on Jewish communities—only to the provision for the instruction of the children of the poor.

But there are two factors which the Jewish sense of benevolence has specially to thank for the manner and the idea in which it carries out its charitable activities. Jewish thought is taught to look on the task of benevolence as צדקה, as duty in the most eminent sense (see Gen. on XV,6). He who does not help the poor to the utmost of his power commits a sin, and is guilty before God. והיה בך חטא it says of him in the next verse. But thereby charity is deprived of its protective armour of impulse, sometimes greater, sometimes lesser, of being dependent of feelings of sympathy and pity, and of personal appeal, and is relegated to the sphere of the strictest command of duty; and at the same time the feeling of degradation is removed from the recipient. The Jewish poor receive no “alms” (allemosyne = gifts of pity). And the deep insight of our “sages”—taking their cue from the מעשר עני law—has fixed the amount of this Zedaka duty to one tenth which is first to be separated out of every fresh capital amount obtained and subsequently from the income it brings each year. By this, every Jew has to consider himself the administrator of a small or large fund lying in his hands, dedicated to God to be used for benevolent and holy purposes, so that he must feel pleased when he finds opportunities to dispose of this fund, which no longer belongs to him, for the good purposes for which it has been entrusted to him.

V. 9. פן יהיה דבר עם לבבך .השמר וגו׳. see on Ch. 8,5. בליעל, see on Ch. 13,14, ולא תתן לו as a loan. One can see what weight the Torah lays on the duty of giving loans, and that the העבט וגו׳ of v.8 does not only refer only to a nominal loan which you really mean as a gift, but in the first place wishes to refer to actual loans (see there and Ex. 22,24). Referring to the similar expression בליעל used here and in Ch. 13,14 for making propaganda for idolatry. The Gemora in Kethuvoth 68a, teaches that כל המעלים עיניו מן הצדקה כאילו עובד עבודה זרה כתיב הכא השמר לך פן יהיה דבר עם לבבך בליעל וגו׳ וכתיב התם יצאו אנשים בני בליעל וגו׳ מה להלן ע״ז אף כאן ע״ז. It is God, in Whose Name every demand for help comes to us, and to deny paying sufficient attention to any such demand is equivalent to denying God and making money your idol.

V. 10. בינך לבינו :לו ;אפי׳ מאה פעמים :נתון תתן, “however often he comes again, and just between the two of you, that nobody sees it, and nobody gets to know of it” (Sifri). ולא ירע לבבך בתתך לו and give it with a cheerful mien, for the way and manner in which it is given can raise or lower the value of the gift infinitely. כל הנותן פרוטה לעני “he who gives a coin to a poor man” it says in Baba Bathra 9,b מתברך בשש ברכות והמפייסו בדברים מתברך באחד עשר ברכות הנותן פרוטה לעני מתברך בו׳ ברכות דכתיב הלא פרוס לרעב לחמך וגו׳ כי תראה ערום וכסיתו וגו׳ אז יבקע כשחר אורך וגו׳ אז תקרא וד׳ יענה וגו׳ והמפייסו בדברים מתברך באחד עשר ברכות שנאמר ותפק לרעב נפשך ונפש נענה תשביע וזרח בחשך אורך וגו׳ ונחך ד׳ תמיד וגו׳ וגו׳: “is blessed with six blessings for it says (Is. 58,7), “if thou breaketh thy bread with the hungry, bringeth the unhappy poor into thine house, seeth the naked and clothe him and hide not thyself from thine own flesh and blood, then will thy light break forth like the morn and thine own health quickly blossom etc. etc.” But he who speaks kindly to him is blessed with eleven blessings for it goes on to say there in Isaiah “but if thou draweth out thine own soul to the hungry, understand to soothe and satisfy the afflicted soul, then thy light will shine out in the darkness etc. God will always lead thee etc. etc. (the six blessings are given in the next two verses, 8 & 9, the eleven in verses 10-12 I.L.).

V. 11. כי לא יחדל אביון וגו׳. It does not say מקרבך (from your midst I.L.) or מקרב ארצך (from the midst of your land I.L.) but מקרב הארץ from the world. It lies quite in the course of the natural development of things that—left to itself—the greatest difference in fortunes, want and surplus, poverty and riches should exist next to one another. The inequality of mental gifts would already produce such inequalities as a natural consequence, and two sons starting from home with exactly equal means, and one having to provide for a single child, the other for a large family would soon present a very considerable difference in their means, and if the latter meets illness and other misfortunes, the second generation could already be in dire need in contrast to the rich opulence of the other branch of the family. But this condition of need which naturally arises elsewhere in the world ,you are not to allow to occur בארצך in your land, in “your” land, in the land of God’s Torah and in the carrying out of the special guidance which is attached to it, there the Torah effects the ironing out of these naturally occuring contrasts, there every poor brother is to find in his richer relations his “brother”, there every poor and needy person belongs to “thee”, the community, and as sure as אין צבור מת ואין צבור עני, a nation, “a community” never dies and never becomes impoverished, so sure is it that under the regime of a dutiful Torah-nation, a Torah community penury and need would only temporarily affect any individual, and with God’s assistance, be changed to a happy existence on earth commensurate with the dignity of a human being. In Sifri the מקרב הארץ is also taken in the same way: כי לא יחדל אביון מקרב הארץ ולהלן הוא אומר כי לא יהיה בד אביון כיצד יתקיימו שני כתובים הללו בזמן שאתם עושים רצונו של מקום אביונים באהרים ובזמן שאין אתם עושים רצונו של מקום אביונים בכם (cf. verses 4 & 5).

But as help and support for necessitous poverty is ensured under the regime of Jewish Torah law, Zedaka does not shame the recipient who requires it. Yea in the spirit of this law, one who is unable to work, or is out of employment, or, out of misplaced pride, goes short himself, or makes his family go short in the necessities of life rather than to resort to the Zedaka to which he is entitled is taking a grave responsibility on himself.—כל מי שצריך ליטול ואינו נוטל הרי זה שופך דמים—(Jerusalmi at end of Pea). But just this law lays very great value on retaining self-independence, on restricting oneself to the bare necessities of life, on taking on what in the eyes of the thoughtless world is looked down on as the very lowest work to avoid having recourse to charity. Nowhere in the world is honest work to gain an independent living held in such high esteem and honour as was the case in ancient Jewish circles. Our greatest spiritual heroes, whose light still illuminates us, and to whom their age and all ages looked up to, and still look up to full of respect and honour, a Hillel, a Rabbi Jehoshua, a R. Chanina and R. Auchio, a R. Huna all lived in the most straightened circumstances and earned their living as woodchopper, cobbler, porter, drawer of water, and by their example taught the maxim עשה שבתך הול ואל תצטרך לבריות, “live no better on Sabbath than on the rest of the week and be independent” (Pesachim 113,a); פשוט נבילתא בשוק ושקיל אגרא ולא תימא כהנא אנא וגברא רבה אנא וסניא בי מלתא, “skin carcasses in the open market and get paid and do not say “I am a priest, am a learned man, such work is beneath me”. (ibid; see רשב״ם on Baba Bathra 110,a). At the end of Pea, the Mishna says: He does not really require Zedaka and still takes it, will not be allowed to leave this world without having to resort to charity out of dire necessity. But he who really could be entitled to take charity but manages to live without doing so will not leave this world in his old age without having supported others out of his own fortune כל מי שאינו צריך ליטול ונוטל אינו נפטר מן העולם עד שיצטרך לבריות וכל מי שצריך ליטול ואינו נוטל אינו מת מן הזקנה עד שיפרנס אחרים משלו ועליו הכתוב אומר ברוך הגבר אשר יבטח בה׳ והיה ה׳ מבטחו.

V. 12. כי ימכר וגו׳. The laws concerning the provision to be made to those needing help conclude with the two cases with which the whole of the laws of social life, and especially of personal rights, was introduced in Ex. 21,2. These were, the case of the sale by the court of a thief, to wipe out the debt of restitution which he has incurred by his theft, and the sale of a daughter who is not yet of age, to ensure her getting enough food, and for her later on being permanently settled in one way or another. We have discussed both these cases at length in Exodus, and have shown how in these cases the Jewish concept of human rights shows itself characteristically in the treatment of people who have fallen into the very lowest degree of social status by crime or misfortune. The laws given there are essentially complemented here in the spirit of the preceding general laws of Zedaka by the duty of הענקה (v.14). This constitutes the duty, at the return to freedom of one who had been forcibly deprived of it, when the legal period of his servitude has passed, not to allow him to leave the service empty-handed, but to fit him out with the means of gaining an honest and “blessed” livelihood. Especially as it refers to the thief who has been condemned by the court to loss of freedom to pay back the value of what he has stolen, this duty completes the glorious picture of general considerate solicitude for human beings which the Divine Law extends even to criminals (see Ex. on Ch. 21,2 et seq.). The criminal who is without means and on that account has been sold to work off his debt of repayment of his theft in the temporary deprivation of his freedom is not to be returned to independence with empty hands. The duty of brotherly love makes it incumbent on his previous master to fit him out with a small provision of goods to enable him to earn an honest living. So that under the regime of the Jewish duty of Zedaka any Jewish social community can indeed quietly say with all assurance: “in our midst no man can find himself driven to crime out of dire necessity.” By the untiring working together of the public and private duties of benevolence the way to keeping and recovering an honest living is opened to everybody, and only the Jewish spirit of Zedaka can protect society from cases of utter destitution and criminals going to wrack and ruin.

כי ימכר לך וגו׳, a thief who is unable to pay back what he has stolen, sold by the court, or an under-aged daughter by her utterly destitute father (see Ex. 21,2 & 7). A woman cannot be sold on account of theft, and the רציעה act is also not applicable to her (v. 17). עבריה is only inserted here to declare her going out in the seventh year and to make the duty of הענקה apply to her also.
ועבדך וגו׳ see on Ex. 21,2; חפשי see ibid.

V. 14. לו .העניק. him, but not מוכר עצמו (Levit. 25,39; Kiddushin 15,a). העניק וגו׳ מצאנך וגו׳ אשר ברכך וגו׳ is כלל ופרט וכלל and gives the common idea of all natural possessions, animal and vegetable which are able to be productive, כל שישנן בכלל ברכה but money or similar possessions would be excluded (Kiddushin 17,a) and there the minimum value is set at thirty shekels, corresponding to the normal compensation to be paid for a slave killed by an animal (Ex. 21,32).
V. 15. וזכרת וגו׳: “I too,” the Sifri remarks on these words, “did not let you go out empty-handed when you went out from slavery to freedom, I fitted you out with רכוש גדול״.

V. 16 & 17. See on Ex. 21,5 & 6. ואף לאמתך. The sentences והיה כי יאמר and ולקחת etc. are only subsidary further remarks bearing on the הענקה-law which is really what this paragraph is dealing with. The whole procedure of the רציעה and its consequences have been already discussed in Exodus. Here they are interposed merely to show the gentleness and kindness which the slave has received from his master. Freedom beckons him and would be given to him accompanied by a suitable equipment and yet he prefers to remain with his master without his freedom! So that והיה כי יאמר וגו׳ until והיה לד עבד עולם is rather in brackets, and ואף לאמתך וגו׳ continues the command of הענקה.

V. 18. לא יקשה וגו׳ cannot refer to the actual fact of letting him go free. For that is simply his right, he had only been bought for six years service and to have kept him any longer would be pure forcible violence. But rather it must refer to the immediately preceding תעשה כן, the הענקה-law demanded at the setting free. This demand of equipping the slave when sending him out into the world is not to appear to the master as being something rather hard to ask of him. שכר ,כי משנה וגו׳ שכיר is not what the workman has done, but the wage of a day-labourer, and משנה שכר שכיר like משנה כסף twice the amount of money (Gen. 43,15) would be double the wages of a day-labourer. עבדך which is the predicate of the subject משנה שכר can then only have the meaning, he worked for, he earned by service, similarly to Ezek. 29,20; פעלתו אשר עבד בה נתתי לו, where פעלה, like פעלת שכיר means the wage worked for and עבד means earned by work. Perhaps also the word משנה is to be separated from שכר and the meaning would be: he has earned double the wages of a day-labourer. In Levit. 25,40, regarding the treatment of a Jewish slave it says: כשכיר כתושב יהיה עמך, the master can only demand from him an ordinary day’s work, accordingly the price he paid for him only entitled him to the work of the hours of a day-labourer, spread over the working days of six years. Nevertheless, as he lives with him as a member of his household he will have had considerably greater use of him. He will also have served him after hours, after nightfall. We have also already in Exodus pointed out, as the Sifra does, the great moral influence of the whole relationship prescribed by which the master has to treat the slave as a brother, but the slave nevertheless is to behave as a slave. Hence it says here: If, at his departure, you still have to provide him with an outfit of wares, and you might consider this a somewhat exaggerated demand, consider how much more service he has given you during those seven years, than what you actually paid for when you bought him. In Kiddushin 15,a this משנה שכר שכיר is taken to refer to the special authorisation given to the master in Ex. 21,4.

V. 19. כל הבכור. This whole portion of the Torah dealing with צדקה ,שמטת כספים ,מעשר עני ,מעשר שני and הענקה, concludes with renewed bringing the בכור institution into prominence which forms the basis for all these positive Divine dispositions of our property. All these duties are not the outcome of ordinary natural rights. All rest on the basic fact that God, when He raised Israel into freedom and independence proclaimed His “לי״ over all persons and property of His future nation, placed Himself as the One real Owner of all property in Israel, and thereby reserved to Himself the right of disposition of all persons and property. And the carrier and eternal proclaimer of this basic fact is just the בכור institution, to which reference was already made (Ch. 14,23) in the introduction to this portion. This law of בכור בהמה טהורה has its place in this compendium, as similarly to מעשר שני it can really only be carried out at the place of the central Sanctuary, only in the enviroments of which it may be eaten. By this also the consciousness is kept awake at this fundamental institution of the dedication of all our food, of the fact that dedication to God is equivalent, must be equivalent to dedication to His Torah which rests in the National Sanctuary, and that every individual is to dispose of his property only from the national point of view and the national calling.
Moreover this pronouncement of the law of the first-born of animals assumes the knowledge of the laws already given in the previous books and brings several essential complementary additions to them.

כל הבכור וגו׳ הזכר. By this הזכר, according to Bechoroth 19,a, the whole conception of the first-born given in Ex. 13,2 is limited to males and the relation of הזכר to כל הבכור is that of פרט to כלל. But בכור זכר could be first-born even if a female birth had preceded it. Against this, it is explained there, the addition of פטר רחם makes the concept first-born male not just the sex but altogether the first-born of the mother, the form would be כלל הצריך לפרט, that the פרט is not a quantitative limitation of the rule (restricting it to first-born males I.L.) but is a more detailed explanation of the כלל (the first-born must be a male I.L.). Equally so the פרט, the זכר פטר רחם could include the case if a ולד יוצא דופן had preceded it, so that the one now born would be בכור לרחמים but not בכור לולדות, this possibility is ruled out by the preceding בכור which fixes the concept to an absolute first-born and not a first-born in only one certain direction a בכור לכל מילי, so that the law is, it must be a בכור לרחמים ולולדות. This form would be פרט הצריך לכלל as the פרט is not extended by the preceding כלל but is itself precisely limited by it.

למעוטי שותפות נכרי :בבקרך ובצאנך excluding part ownership of a non-Jew, (Chulin 135,b). So also Numb. 3,13: הקדשתי לי כל בכור בישראל בישראל ולא באחרים (Bechoroth 2,a). All the family possessions being dedicated and belonging to God which is founded by קדושת בכור rests so deeply on the Jewish national history and calling that it can only apply when both the mother animal and the young are exclusively Jewish possessions.

תקדיש לה׳ אלקיך, although בכור קדוש מרחם, the sanctification of the first-born comes automatically with its birth still נולד לו בכור בתוך ביתו מצוה להקדישו if anybody has a first-born animal born within the sphere of his property it is a Mitzva for him to proclaim its קדושה in words, a law which surely is rooted in the far-reaching deep significance of this קדושה for the whole sphere of the possessions of the owner.

לא תעבד וגו׳ ולא תגז וגו׳. This prohibition of shearing or working which applies here at the first-born and extends to all קדשי מזבח (Bechoroth 25,a) does not emanate from the general law of מעילה (Levit. 5,15 and Deut. 12,17). This is evident already from the fact that מעילה applies also to קדשי בדק הבית whereas shearing and working is only prohibited מן התורה at קדשי מזבח (Bechoroth ibid), and on the other hand the prohibition of shearing and working is still in force at פסולי קדשי מזבח even after they have been redeemed (see above on XII,15).

V. 20. לפני ה׳ אלקיך וגו׳. In Numb. 18,18 the בכור בהמה טהורה is directed to be given to the priest as מתנת כהונה to be eaten like the breast and shank of the שלמים (refer to it). Here the further law is given that it is a Mitzva to bring every firstling in the first year of its birth to its destination of being sacrificed and eaten in the City of God. The law pronounced by שנה בשנה similarly to the tithe (Ch. 14,22) makes one take to heart the consideration of the blessing of the soil and of one’s livestock each year by itself as being the sign of God’s considered decision year by year, as it says in Ch. 11,12: ארץ אשר וגו׳ תמיד וגו׳ מראשית השנה ועד אחרית שנה (see notes thereon).
אתה וביתך like the חזה ושוק to be eaten by הכהנים ונשיהם ובניהם ועבדיהם (Zebachim).

V. 21-23. וכי יהיה בו מום וגו׳ בשעריך תאכלנו וגו׳. The rendering unfit for an offering which a מום effects on an animal has been discussed already on Levit. 22,23 et seq. and we have already explained there, as well as on XXI,17, the deep contradiction which bringing an animal with a bodily defect as a קרבן would be to the way of life which is to be represented and taught by every offering “seeking nearness to God”. But this unfitness to be brought as an offering through having a מום had to be mentioned again here because its effect on בכור is different from that on other קדשים. Other קדשים if they have become unfit to be brought as offerings through מום require to be redeemed before they may be eaten (Levit. 27,11) but firstlings, as already remarked on Numb. 18,17, have no means of being redeemed in any circumstances. Just as its קדושה did not arise out of any free-willed act of dedication, but came automatically with its birth, so is it not removable or transferable by any means. But rather its מתנת כהנה character is retained even with a מום. It still remains the property of a priest, and as soon as it gets a מום קבוע it may be eaten by him, and through him, by anybody else. But just because he may eat it without its being redeemed it had to be specially mentioned that it was like פסולי המוקדשים after they have been redeemed and no consideration for טהרה need be observed, but that the prohibition of blood is in force. (see on Ch. 12,15 & 16).

Which defects make it unfit for offering has already been discussed in detail in Levit. 22,20, et seq. Here it is given in the form of כלל וכי יהיה בו מום, פסח או עור, כל מום רע :ופרט וכלל, by which the last ,כלל כל מום רע has the force of an extending רבוי and extends the concept of a defect rendering unfit for offering to כל מומין שבגלוי ואינן חוזרין all visible defects which are permanent (Bechoroth 37,a).

V. 1. A chapter on the festivals follows, we have already discussed in Ch. 1,3 its being given a place here in the משנה תורה compendium.
