All those festival times as י״כ ,ר״ה ,שבת, and שמיני עצרת which could be kept completely during the years in the wilderness are not mentioned here. In this compendium for those coming into the Land only those are repeated which, like שבועות and סוכת really only come into their full significance in the Land, or, regarding which, as for פסח the duty of keeping it in the City of God as the national centre was specially to be stressed, as this duty is also declared for שבועות and סוכת. All three are רגלים (pilgrim festivals I.L.) their meaning as such also only beginning with the decentralisation in the Land, as indeed they are grouped together in this respect in v.16. Then, at the same time several essential complementary laws to those given in the previous books had been reserved for this compendium. Thus at once at the first sentence of the Pesach laws.

שמור את חדש האביב וגו׳. Already in the introductory words of the festival chapter in Levit. 23,2, the law is laid down that although the festivals are bound to definite dates in the months, the fixing of the times of the festivals require regulating by the national board of representatives, the Sanhedrin, and are dependent on their yearly seasonal decisions. We have already (ibid) explained how this necessity arises from the requirement made by the Torah that the dates fixed for the festivals must fall in specified seasons of the year. Now the seasons depend on the course of the solar year, so that, if left to itself, as the festival year of twelve lunar months is shorter by about eleven days than the solar year, the times of the festivals would fall eleven days earlier each year, and so slowly revolve right round the calendar and occur in turn at all the seasons of the year. This made it necessary for an extra month to be periodically inserted in the lunar year to keep the dates of our festivals in harmony with the specified seasons of the year, so that the Pesach festival falls in the beginning of the Spring תקופה (quarter I.L.) and the autumn תקופה while it is still Sukkoth (תקופה is the beginning of a quarter of the solar year of slightly more than 91 7/12 days, we have the Tishri quarter, and those of Tebet, Nisan and Tamuz) and Shevuoth with the bringing of ביכורים fall with the first ripening of fruit.
This regulating is now ordered here with details.

שמור את חדש האביב ועשית פסח. The idea חדש האביב already combines two factors of which one belongs to the cycle of the moon the other to the solar year. חדש, the real months depend solely on the moon, אביב, the ripening of the stalks, a sign of the beginning of Spring depends on the course of the sun. חדש, the month in which we are to bring the Pesach offering is always to be חדש אביב, the beginning of Spring is always to be in it, the תקופת ניסן, more precisely in the first half of it which still bears the חדש character as it belongs to the increasing “rejuvenating itself” light in contrast to the second half of the already decreasing light. But the first half of the month reaches to the fourteenth, just the day of bringing the Pesach offering. And only if on the fourteenth day or earlier the תקופת ניסן the Spring quarter has begun is the month חדש האביב and Pesach can be celebrated in it. But if the whole of the fourteenth still belongs to the winter quarter, the תקופת טבת and the Spring quarter starts only on the fifteenth or later, then the חדש האביב character has to be reserved for Nisan by the process of intercalation. If the תקופת ניסן falls on the fifteenth it is sufficient to put off the beginning of Nisan by one day through making the preceding month of Adar מלא (see Ex. 12,2, p. 125). But if it falls on the sixteenth or later then, to satisfy the demand that the Pesach month has the character of חדש האביב, it is necessary to insert a whole extra month, the אדר שני. Hence the sentence: כד חזית דמשכא תקופת טבת עד שיתסר בניסן עבדה לההיא שתא ולא תחוש לה דב׳ שמור את חדש האביב, שמור אביב של תקופה שיהא בחדש ניסן (ר״ה כ״א ע״א). Rashi there. (But according to תוספות there the fifteenth day still belongs to the “חדש״ to the “renewing” light and it would be sufficient if תקופת ניסן started on the fifteenth. The wording of our text שמור את חדש האביב ועשית פסח speaks for Rashi’s way of taking it, that already the עשיית הפסח is to fall in the Spring quarter. According to תוספות one would have to take it that the whole month is called חדש האביב if the Spring quarter starts not later than the fifteenth, and the command would run: take care that the month in which the Pesach is brought is חדש האביב).

This care for the Spring-character of Nisan is carrying out the task set by שמור את חדש האביב ועשית פסח and this insertion of the extra month into the lunar year is called עיבור שנה. We have already explained this in its connection with other laws, on Levit. 23,2 and would refer to that. The exercising of this care and the decisions constantly to be made based on astronomical calculations and observations of other conditions which have to be considered in this matter are among the functions of the highest national court of representatives. In our times we go according to Hillel the Younger, the last representative of the national court, who fixed the calendar for the times of the Galuth, and in each cycle of nineteen years there are seven such leap years of thirteen months, always the third, sixth, eighth, eleventh, fourteenth, seventeenth and nineteenth.

In Exodus on XII,2 and Levit. 23,2 & 4 we have worked out and shown how the institutions of קידוש החדש and עיבור השנה and the simultaneous historical and seasonal considerations for fixing our festivals oppose any and every idea of an ancient or modern cult of Nature; how rather they call us out of an idolatrous appeal to Nature to render homage to God, Whose Presence every creature, every seasonal change, every blade of grass in Nature proclaims, Whose Law is almighty in every development of existence in the life of Nature, but which is still more intimately near to the morally-free life of human beings which has been revealed to us by His direction shown in the development of our history and in the guidance of our life of actions by His Torah. The identification of the One God in both Nature and history, that is the basis of our being conscious of God and of ourselves, to the promulgation of which the שמור את חדש האביב ועשית פסח לה׳ אלקיד arranges our whole calendar. The festival of our historical revival must at the same time be the festival of the revival of nature. The God Whose breath of Spring awakes nature out of the stark death-like rigidity of Winter is the same God Who called us to life and freedom from death and enchainment, and the God Who once with His בדמיך חיי (Ezek. 16,6) broke open the Egyptian grave of our political existence is the same God Whose free-making, life-giving rule is still proclaimed by every shoot bursting through the soil, every bud breaking into bloom, every creature shaking itself up to fresh life out of the bleak stark winter in the fresh joy of Spring. The day, on the anniversary of which we are to celebrate ever afresh by the Pesach-offering the historic moment when physical and political death hovered over our heads, and after carefully considering the tests (פסח: literally He haltingly passed over I.L.) God made both pass away and rewarded the vows of ever faithful, virile, cheerful devotion, expressed by our offering, with life and freedom: that day, the fourteenth of Nisan must always stand in the awakening of Nature in the beginning of Spring, and held to that time by intercalation. We understand then, why אין מעברין אלא אדר (Sanhedrin 12,a) why this regulating is to be effected by the insertion of just another Adar and not by any other month. Only by inserting the extra month immediately before the commencement of Nisan does the purpose of the insertion—that the Pesach month must coincide with the Spring month—strike the eye. On the other hand, the revelation of God in our history is in the foreground with such preponderant significance that once the month of Nisan has entered, yea, even if the 30th Adar has arrived which could have been the first of Nisan, then insertion is no longer permissable. אין מעברין ניסן בניסן, more אין מעברין את השנה ביום שלשים של אדר הואיל וראוי לקובעו ניסן (ibid, b).

But the deep significance of this עיבור שנה institution is only really apparent when they settle in the land, and on that account its special arrangements could have been left for this compendium of the Torah. Only in surroundings of meadows and fields does the life of Nature in the awakening of Spring crowd men’s thoughts with its mighty urges and its imposing universal effect, and fills men’s hearts with the idea of the realisation of their hopes being dependent on the high power of Nature. Only in surroundings of meadows and fields does the People of God run the danger of sinking to the worship of these forces of Nature, and to find a place in their hearts for “Baal” next to that of the God of their history and doings. There the Torah steps in and demands the beginning of Spring for the day of Pesach-offering, demands the celebration of the remembrance of our Spring in full view of the Spring of Nature, and calls away from the tender young green of the meadows and the blossoming fields up and away to the place where the Divine Torah rests, the fount of our regeneration, the source of our moral and political blossoming, and wherein at the same time the real condition for the blossoming of our meadows and fields lies. And in full view of the glories of Nature, God’s pledge to us, we renew afresh our homage to Him, Who, in one night of Spring led us out of physical and political death to life and freedom, and Who with that one world-historic deed inscribed Himself in the book of the experiences of men and Nature,—above all for our remembrance and reflection—as the One Who with the one and same Hand controls both Nature and History, and how it is He Who made and upholds the laws which govern the path of the sun and the earth, makes time revolve, and seeds and all creations start and complete their development, and He is the One Who also wrote the Law for us, according to which we are to develop our natures and all the seeds of truth and goodness which are planted in us when we are born—“take care of the month of Spring and bring the offering of your revival”—that is the פסח (see Ex. 12,12 and 27).

לילה. “at night” you were passive at becoming free, like the child that is born to light and life from the dark womb of the mother so wert thou born to freedom. And the night of your birth, your political birth as a nation was a “night of Spring”. In a Spring night you do not see the sun, but in every rustling leaf, in every nodding calyx, in every balmy blossom you see and recognise its work, and up in the heaven, the moon illuminates for you its reflected light. To such a moon-like course in the firmament of the history of the world were you sent out by the Invisible One on that night to illuminate the world by His Light, to show the nations their world as being His world; all His, all coming into existence, all blossoming, all living His, the work of the Invisible One, Who one cannot see with one’s eyes but Whom the human mind knows and the human breast feels just as the Spring night lets one know and feel the sun although the eye sees it not.
פסח .שיהו כל עשיותיו לשם פסח :ועשית פסח together with חטאת form the one class of offerings which שלא לשמן is completely פסול.

V. 2. וזבחת פסח לה׳ אלקיך צאן ובקר. We know from Ex. 12,5, that the Pesach-offering is to be brought from lambs or kids, accordingly only from צאן. Hence the Sifri says: צאן ובקר והלא אין פסח בא אלא מן הכבשים ומן העזי׳ א״כ למה נאמר צאן ובקר צאן לפסח ובקר לחגיג׳. For in the Mishna (Pesachim 69,b) it is taught that if the Pessach offering by itself is not sufficient for a meal for the whole company on whose behalf it is brought, a חגיגה offering is also to be brought on the fourteenth of Nisan which has to be eaten first so that the Pessach offering is eaten when one is no longer hungry חגיגה הבאה עם הפסח נאכלת תחלה כדי שיהא הפסח נאכל על השבע (Pessachim 70,a). Rambam in הל׳ קרבן פסח X,12 teaches this sentence of the Mishna on the basis of the text of the Sifri quoted above, accordingly this explanation of the Sifri would remain Halacha although in Pesachim 70,b, the deduction which בן דורתאי draws from it remains rejected. This deduction could also actually not be attached to the text itself but to the setting of the text in which the בקר) חגיגה) is just called פסח like צאן on which בן דורתאי, in contradiction to the חכמים, makes the deduction that this offering which comes with the Pessach is to be afforded exactly the same treatment as the Pessach and so would also be דוחה שבת (Numb. 9,2). This deduction made from the setting of the text is rejected and is rather understood to be an indication of another Halachic sentence that מותר פסח שלמים (see below), but the law of חגיגה itself in this verse would remain undisputed, which is why then Rambam brings it and also the law of מותר פסח Ch. 4,6 et seq. We think that we can take it also in the sense of the Rambam that, although חגיגת י״ד דאורייתא, as it is not חובה but only מצוה when במועט (the company is large and the lamb or kid small I.L.), and only so that the Pessach should not be eaten when one is still hungry—a purpose which, we believe, could if necessary be also achieved by eating other food first—we believe that because of all these circumstances, the חגיגת י״ד, although דאורייתא, still is not דוחה שבת or טומאה, as the Halacha of the Mishna states (ibid 67,b) אימתי מביא חגיגה עמו בזמן שהוא בהול בטהרה ובמועט ובזמן שהוא בא בשבת במרובה ובטומאה אין מביאין עמו חגיגה. Hence רב אשי also explains: ש״מ חגיגת י״ד לאו חובה, but does not say לאו דאורייתא and hereby the difficulty which the זרע אברהם raises on the Sifri against the way the Rambam takes it could be easily solved. And if, in Chagiga 8,a, רב אשי does in fact deduce אלמא קסבר חגיגת י״ד לאו דאורייתא, Rambam could have taken this not in its real sense, for there it is just the question whether it is חובה or לאו חובה that is decisive, and so also in his commentary on the Mishna: להודיעך כי חגיגת י״ד אינו חובה. Perhaps there the Rambam also had the version חגיגת י״ד לאו חובה as in Pessachim. We have therefore allowed the concept “preparing a meal” which is essentially innate in זבח to appear predominantly in our translation of וזבחת פסח. The Pessach is to be brought as a “meal”, and where it does not suffice for that purpose בקר חגיגה is accordingly to be joined to זבח) צאן פסח itself, as we have already remarked elsewhere, is phonetically related to שבע).

The law that פסח נאכל על השובע which חגיגת י״ד serves, and out of which our custom to conclude the meal on the Seder-evening with a כזית מצה in memory of the Pessach has arisen as well as the further law אין מפטירין אחר הפסח אפיקומן that after the Pessach (and for us nowadays after the last piece of matzo) we are not to eat anything else can well be meant to bring to our minds that the institution of Pessach and Mazzo is to “satiate” us, that they contain everything which we require for the foundation of our existence and our duties on earth and we do not require to bring anything else to them to satisfy that need (see רשב״ם on Pessachim 119,b).

As already remarked above, on the form of our verse, the wording of which extends the concept פסח to צאן ובקר, accordingly to offerings, which, unlike Pessach, can also be brought from cattle, it is taught in the passage quoted from Pessachim as well as in Zebachim 9,a, that וזבחת פסח וגו׳ והלא אין פסח בא אלא מן הכבשים ומן העזים אלא מכאן למותר פסח שיהא לדבר הבא מן הצאן ומן הבקר ומאי ניהו שלמים. This is the halacha which we have already mentioned on Levit. 3,6 that מותר הפסח קרב שלמים, that an animal that had been destined for a קרבן פסח but could not be brought at the time the offering has to be made, either because it could not be found or for any other reason such as its being found to be more than one year old is to be brought as a שלמים with the full שלמים character. There we pointed out that שלמים, the offering of being conscious that one’s family happiness is before God, is the specific Jewish offering, the foundation of which is laid just by the Pessach-offering, accordingly that actually all the שלמים of the whole year can be considered as continuation of the Pessach-offering. חגיגה itself is nothing other than a שלמים induced by the חג idea, and just by this halacha the form of our verse וזבחת צאן ובקר appears in a clear light. Both when there is a necessity for it, the פסח is to be extended by a שלמים and also when the offering could not be brought as פסח it is subsequently to be brought as פסח שלא בזמנו קרב שלמים .שלמים. Both come from the deep meaning of the פסח as being the first building up of Jewish homes before God. (see Ex. 12,2, et seq). Hence also the sentence in the first Mishna of Zebachim: כל הזבחים שנזבחו שלא לשמן כשרים אלא שלא עלו לבעלים לשם חובה חוץ מן הפסח והחטאת הפסח בזמנו והחטאת בכל שלא בזמנו .זמן, beyond the time for offering the פסח—the fourteenth of Nisan בין הערבים—the animal is a שלמים, so that it then belongs to the class of offerings which are שלא לשמן כשרים although לא עלו לבעלים לשם חובה. At the historically given moment, when by showing absolute complete submission to God (the slaves must have known how seriously they were risking their lives I.L.) we first won the building up of our Jewish families, as was expressed by the first פסח, and which is to be expressed by every anniversary of the “fourteenth of Nisan turning towards evening”, just the חובה nature, the “duty” character of the offering belongs so essentially to it that if it cannot be עולה לחובה it loses the character of an offering altogether, just like a חטאת at any time.

But the extra significance which a law which makes the expression of the ordinary family happiness of the whole year (every שלמים offering I.L.) looked on and taken to heart from the standpoint of that פסח moment, has just for the time of settling down in the Land which was about to begin, is quite clear in itself.
במקום אשד יבחר. (see on v. 5).

V. 3. לא תאכל עליו וגו׳. The law of Chometz and Mazzo has been declared already in Ex. XII & XIII and there we explained it. That the chometz law comes into effect already on the fourteenth of Nisan at the time the Pessach-offering is to be brought has already been declared by אך ביום הראשון תשביתו וגו׳ in Ch. 12,15 and לא תזבח על חמץ וגו׳ in Ch. 23,18. Now here the definite prohibition of having any use of chometz, the איסור אכילה והנאה, (ibid XV,19 & 20) is declared to start at the beginning of that time, and the prohibition of chometz placed in close connection with the command of mazzo לא תאכל עליו חמץ שבעת ימים תאכל עליו מצות. Thus the halacha is laid down that the positive command to eat mazzo is dependent on the negative command of chometz in material, in person and in time. In material: דברים הבאים לידי חימוץ אדם יוצא בהן ידי חובתו במצה (ibid 35,a); the mazzo the eating of which is an absolute duty on the first evening of Passover and is to be a positive expression of the historical fact of our lack of independence at the time of the redemption as well as of our everlasting permanent lack of independance towards God, this mazzo must be made from material which was able to become chometz, leavened, symbolically to represent acknowledgment of these facts. What should be mazzo must have been able to become chometz. Not lack of the ability for independance was the cause of our slavery in Egypt, or is the cause of our servitude to God at all times. Forcible suppression was our עבדות פרעה, free-willed submission is our מצה .עבודת ה׳ itself is, literally, suppressed leavening (see on Ex. 2,13).—In person נשים חייבות באכילת מצה דבר תורה שנאמר לא תאכל עליו חמץ שבעת ימים תאכל עליו מצות כל שישנו בבל תאכל חמץ ישנו באכילת מצה והני נשי הואיל וישנן בבל תאכל חמץ ישנן בקום אכול מצה (Pessachim 43,b). Although as a rule positive mitzvas which are limited to a special time do not apply to women (see on Levit. 23,43, p. 711) nevertheless the duty of eating mazzo on the first night of Pessach does apply to them, for this positive command to eat mazzo applies to all to whom the negative command not to eat chometz applies. All those who were redeemed out of complete lack of independence to complete independence by God alone, and who have to acknowledge that fact by abstaining from eating chometz, at every anniversary of that hour of redemption, which at the same time was the hour of our birth to our national calling, because of the redemption to that calling, have to acknowledge it in joy by eating “the bread of our lack of independence towards God”. To this foundation-laying acknowledgement—just as also to the positive celebrations of ,פסח הקהל ,שמחה—women are in duty bound to do, although for several other מצות עשה שהזמן גרמא the Torah imposes no obligation on them (see Levit. p. 711. In time: לקבעו חובה בזמן הזה (ibid 28b). Although the command to eat mazzo is first declared as the food to accompany the Pessach צלי אש ומצות על מרורים יאכלוהו (Ex. 12,8), still the mazzo-command is an independent one and not dependent on פסח, so that even in times when the Pessach cannot be brought, the obligation to eat mazzo on the first evening of Passover remains in force, whether it be on account of personal prevention from bringing the Pessach such as טמא ושהיה בדרך רחוקה—for which the קבעו חובה, the making the duty quite independent of the Pessach is already laid down in בראשון בארבעה עשר יום לחדש בערב תאכלו מצות—or on account of the general temporary cessation of bringing offerings, as at the present time—for which period of Galuth the obligation to eat mazzo is placed together with the prohibition of eating chometz which is unlimited by time. (Pessachim 28,b). After all, the world-historic calling and destiny which we entered in the hour of our national birth was not altered by the Galuth, so that in Galuth also, where the Pessach-offering lies before us only in woeful remembrance, we still have to dedicate ourselves to our eternal mission by eating the mazzo showing our joyful submission under God’s Will and Guidance. And well could, as altogether the repeated obligation to eat mazzo and especially laying down the halacha for mazzo in the Galuth at this point of the compendium for settling in the land be of serious admonishing and warning significance (but see also Pessachim 120, a, and Kiddushin 37,b).

שבעת ימים, the direct duty to eat mazzo is only עליו, in connection with the moment of Pessach, in the night of the fourteenth to the fifteenth, indirectly the duty lasts seven days, inasmuch as no different bread, bread that is leavened, is allowed to be eaten (see Ex. 12,15 & 18).
לחם עני: bread of “dependence”, for this is the real concept of עני, and so is the most striking characterisation of the meaning of mazzo (Ex. 12,8).

כי בחפזון וגו׳. On the whole of your exodus from Egypt the stamp of “forced haste” was impressed. The Hand of God lay heavy on the Egyptians, they who earlier would not grant you three days freedom from work, yea, no breathing space of a moment’s respite from work, they now drive you to freedom, and, even as during the whole period of your slave labour, allowed you not even time to bake proper bread. Thus even in the moment of redemption you were still slaves, had not wrested freedom yourselves for yourselves, had received it from God through the hands of your oppressors, your oppressors were בחפזון, in haste, you were בחפזון, in haste, your oppressors were driven by God, you were driven by your oppressors—כי—ותחזק מצרים על העם למהר לשלחם מן הארץ כי אמרו כלנו מתים גרשו ממצרים ולא יכלו להתמהמה וגם צדה לא עשו להם (Ex. 12,33 & 39). Everybody was driven, God alone had a free hand on that unique day in the history of mankind, and all this was למען תזכר את יום צאתך מארץ מצרים כל ימי חייך, because that day is to be the starting-point for all your future thinking and doing, that with that day you did not become your own master, but went out of the violence of man into being the possession of God, and were to go out of servitude of man into servitude of God. (If it says in the Sifri on our verse יכול חפזון לישראל ולמצרים ת״ל ולכל בני ישראל לא יחרץ כלב לשונו אמור מעתה לא היה חפזון כי אם למצרים, this, in view of what the Torah reports in Ex. 12,33 & 39 can only mean that the real חפזון was only that of the Egyptians terrified with the threat to their lives, but that Israel in spite of the חפזון in which they undoubtedly were, nevertheless were not disquieted by it. More, in the parallel place in Mechilta on Ch. 12,11, it says that the actual wording of the text proves from לא יחרץ וגוי the חפזון דישראל, that although they were בחפזון still no dog barked at them, and deduces that both Israel and the Egyptians were in a state of חפזון).

In the למען תזכר וגו׳ the duty of remembering the exodus from Egypt daily is laid down, and in Berachoth 12,b, by the extension כל ימי חייך, the law is taught that night is included in this duty and מזכירין יציאת מצרים בלילות, we have to mention the exodus to bring it to our minds every night as well as every day. That this required to be specially declared although in v.1 it says: הוציאך ה׳ א׳ ממצרים לילה, and although the exodus only took place by day (Numb. 33,3,) still the actual redemption was accomplished by night (Berachoth 9,a), this command does primarily refer to daytime, could well be worth noting for the meaning and significance of this command. Both factors of our life, our historical life, our fate in the world, and our personal active life receive their foundation on יציאת מצרים. Our fate, our historical life is based on trust in God, our active life on our consciousness of the duty of obeying God. The former has to prove itself above all in the dark periods of life, in thoughts, the latter primarily in the days, when we are actively employed. Superficial thought would believe trust in God in the dark periods of life as being the deduction to be made in the very first place from the redemption from Egypt and take the command of זכירת יציאת מצרים as being primarily for the night time. But Jewish thought knows that it is much easier to trust to God in circumstances of dark misfortune than to remain faithful to our duties in the bright daylight of our active daily work. So that the consciousness of our Jewish duty which is ever to be renewed by the remembrance of the exodus is infinitely more important, and זכירת יציאת מצרים ביום, remembering it in daytime undoubtedly stands in the foreground. Hence Rab Eleazar had no doubt on this point and he only sought to find some indication in the text of the Torah for this command to apply also for the night time, and found it in the extending clause כל ימי חייך. Another opinion (ibid) finds an indication in this extension that זכירת יציאת מצרים will not have lost its importance even when in the future God will reveal His direct guidance of Jewish destiny, and His direct intervention in the history of the world, by His redemption of the Jewish nation scattered amongst all countries and all nations, in a manner far surpassing in extent and publicity the redemption from Egypt. And even if it does say of that future final messianic period of redemption: הנה ימים באים נאם ה׳ ולא יאמרו עוד חי ה׳ אשר העלה את בני ישראל מארץ מצרים כי אם הי ה׳ אשר העלה ואשר הביא את זרע בית ישראל מארץ צפונה ומכל הארצות אשר הדחתים שמה (Jer. 23,7 & 8), it still does not say שתעקר יציאת מצרים ממקומה that then י״מ will lose all its importance for Jewish remembrance, but שתהא שיעבוד מלכיות עיקר וי״מ טפל לו that then the contemporary gathering together and redemption from being subordinate to the other nations, which they will live to experience, will be the principle basis for the fulfilment of their duties in the future but the redemption from Egypt will still retain a place in the minds of the Jews. For ימות משיח itself is only the completion of that to which the י״מ, the exodus from Egypt laid the foundation for only then Israel will have achieved the mission it undertook with יציאת מצרים.

The reason for this duty of remembering (and actually mentioning I.L.), the redemption from Egypt daily only receiving its place here in this compendium for those about to enter and settle in the Land is fairly self-evident. For until then they could well be considered as being still in the midst of the redemption from Egypt. Only with the settling down in the Land could the remembrance of the historical origin of the nation and the consequences therefrom for our life of duty and obedience become fainter and fainter, and only for that time and all succeeding times does the command: תזכור יום צאתך מארץ מצרים כל ימי חייך—“thou shalt remember the day when thou camest forth from the land of Egypt every day of thy life”—receive its full significance and meaning.

V. 4. ולא יראה לך שאר, see Ex. 12,15 & 19; XIII,7. לך, that belongs to you. The prohibition of בל יראה banishes from the sphere of our possessions during the whole of the Festival of Remembrance of the Redemption from Egypt, not only חמץ, anything actually leavened, but also שאר, the means of becoming leavened; accordingly every trace of independence, yea, even only the ability and temperament which leads to it. The redemption found us not only without possessions but robbed even of the right to have possessions. It was from the Hand of God that we again obtained possessions. We must always remain conscious of that fact, and the acknowledgement of that fact we have always to show afresh by banishing all חמץ and all שאור from the whole of our domain. Now here it says, in connection with the two preceding verses: while all members of the nation gather together in their central city about the Sanctuary of God, there to bring the Pessach-offering, and in connection with it, by not eating חמץ and by eating mazzo, to occupy themselves with the remembrance of the redemption and the resulting feelings of the lack of dependence on themselves and the joy of depending on God, the whole land also, the whole national domain down to the very last Jewish hut, shall bear the stamp of this Festival of Remembrance and the expression of this feeling, and ולא יראה לך שאור בכל גבילד שבעת ימים! (“and no שאור shall be seen within all thy borders for seven days I.L.).

ולא ילין מן הבשר וגו׳: and just as the Pessach-offering, brought in the Sanctuary makes its effect felt as far away as Jews live, and, with the moment of its being brought, makes the very last Jewish hut, by removing every trace of חמץ and שאור, harmonize with the spirit and feelings of complete unselfishness regarding possessions which the offering is to express, so also has the Chagiga-offering attached to the Pessach-offering (v.2.) not to separate the happy enjoyment of life in the same spirit (as expressed by the אכילה, the eating) from the surrender and devotion of one’s personality (as expressed by the שחיטת הזבח, the slaughtering of the offering). The Pessach-offering, at which the אכילה, eating it oneself is symbolically so very much the predominant significant idea—שלא בא מתחלתו אלא לאכילה (see on Ex. 12,7 & 8)—is the basis for that great institution of נותר and פגול which governs the whole course of all the offerings of the Sanctuary. It declares that only the closest connection between the שחיטה (the slaughtering I.L.) and the אכילה (the eating I.L.) makes the offering an act of moral elevation of Man towards God. By separation of one from the other the offering falls into the heathen conception of self-abnegation in itself giving satisfaction to the gods, and the eating into the heathen raising gratification of the senses into a ritual of religious worship (see Levit. 7,16-18).

Here it is taught that for חגיגת ארבעה עשר —that is the בשר אשר תזבח בערב (see on v.2)—that although the period during which it may be eaten is longer than that for the Pessach-offering, which may only be eaten during the night following its שחיטה, so that it already becomes נותר on the following morning, the eating of the בשר חגיגה is still restricted to the fifteenth of Nissan, the יום הראשון, but what is left over to the morning of the sixteenth becomes נותר. That makes the שלמים-law which applies to all חגיגות viz. that they may be eaten during two days and the intervening night, apply to this ארבעה עשר. (In Pessachim 71,b, חגיגה although they are שלמי ציבור, regarding this extension of the time for their eating, are included in the law primarily given for שלמי נדבה in Levit. 7,16; נדר או נדבה וגו׳).

V. 5. לא תוכל וגו׳. Although bringing all offerings outside the place which God had chosen for His Sanctuary has already been forbidden in Ch. 12,5 et seq. there was still good grounds for the express repetition of this prohibition just for the Pessach-offering. For the Pessach-offering is quite specially an offering to build up the home and the family—שה לבית אבות שה לבית—“a lamb for the family, a lamb for the home” (I.L.) —so much so that the first one was sacrificed in every house and the doorposts and thresholds of the homes took the place of the Altar. So that, more than for any other offering, there was cause to definitely declare again that also after the impending decentralisation in the Land no one may bring the Pessach-offering in his own home but must be offered in the central Sanctuary of the City of God. This interposes the clause into the act of the constitution of the Jewish nation—and that is what the Pessach-offering is, (see Ex. 12,3-6) that everyone must first place himself and his household within the common circle of the nation united on the basis of the Sanctuary of the Torah, and only from there can his own home be happily conscious of standing before God. This is so important just at the Pessach-offering that even in the time בשעת היתר הבמות, it was only allowed to be brought at the central national Sanctuary, בבמה גדולה (Megilla 9,b, and Zebachim 114,b).
V. 6. כי אם אל המקום וגו׳ must be taken as a separate sentence referring back to v. 5. If it were to be taken referring to the end of the verse it would have to have been כי אם במקום.

בערב. In Ex. 12,6 the time is given as בין הערבים (the time between past mid-day and evenfall I.L.) (refer to notes there). Here it is designated more precisely by בערב, according to Pessachim 59,a, to say thereby that all the offering procedures of the fourteenth of Nisan which have to be done towards the declining day, נרות ,קטורת ,תמיד have to precede the Pessach-offering so that it forms the conclusion of the fourteenth in the Sanctuary. For the fourteenth of Nisan still belonged to the period of slavery, and the confidence in God shown by their risking their lives in bringing the Pessach-offering making them worthy of the deliverance which the night following was to bring them, was the purpose of that offering. All the procedures in the Temple belonging to the fourteenth must accordingly be completed before the Pessach-offering, the time for which was just בערב בין הערבים, in the time of the decline of the day towards the oncoming night. יאוחר דבר שנאמר בו בערב ובין הערבים לדבר שלא נאמר בו אלא בין הערבים בלבד. (ibid).

מועד צאתך ממצרים ,כבוא השמש ,בערב, are, according to Berachoth 9,a, three successive times on the eve of the fourteenth to the fifteenth. בערב:- the decline of the fourteenth, בוא השמש: the beginning of the fifteenth when the sun has completely set: מועד צאתך ממצרים:- daybreak, the beginning of the time of the actual exodus. בערב בין הערבים is the time of preparation for the redemption by completely giving up and devoting all one’s self-existence to the guidance of God by the שחיטת הפסח. (symbolised by the slaughtering of the lamb I.L.). בוא השמש, the night, starting with the completion of the sunset, the time when we were redeemed from death and slavery, that brought us into enjoying our freedom, when God gave us back to ourselves, Whose Act we realised symbolically by eating the offering ourselves. מועד צאתך ממצרים, the time of the actual effect of that redemption, the actual going out into freedom with which the work of redemption was brought to completion, and which, as the eating of the Pessach-offering says symbolically made each one of us present himself in the free and independent personality it conferred on him. Hence the sentence בערב אתה זובח כבוא השמש אתה אוכל ועד מתי אתה אוכל והולך עד מועד צאתך ממצרים, or, according to ראב״ע who limited the period of eating the Pessach-offering to midnight, the hour when the Hand of God really brought about the salvation, ומועד צאתך ממצרים אתה שורף, that at the moment of daybreak of the day of the actual exodus all that was left of the Pessach meal became נותר and had to be burnt, preaching thereby to the children of Israel at the moment of their first actual step into freedom that for them there was to be no אכילה separated from זביחה, no freedom without selfless giving oneself up to God, and every אכילה which they might henceforth seek to obtain not on the basis of זביחה would be futile.

V. 7. ובשלת ואכלת וגו׳, not when you have only understood only to pray and to sacrifice at places consecrated to God, but only when you have learnt “to cook and to eat” at places consecrated to God, only when the spirit of the Sanctuary has so penetrated the whole of your being that your “working and eating”, that even your bodily life of your senses, lived in the consciousness that it too is related to God, is elevated into the sphere of a moral holy, God-serving life of mitzvas; only when ובשלת ואכלת במקום אשר יבחר ה׳ אלקיד בו (“and you cook and eat in the place which God has chosen”) only then can you והלכת לאהליך, only then have you gained the right spirit of the meaning of the “Home of God” which is to accompany you home for your ordinary homely life.

ובשלת ואכלת, we think that the general term בשל, to cook, which includes both צלי and בשול (roasting and boiling) is used here because here it is considering not only the Pessach-offering, but also the חגיגת ארבעה עשר which is really what is new in the chapter on Pessach and of which verses 2 and 4 spoke. For, as pointed out in v.4, this Chagiga was eaten also on the fifteenth, the יום הראשון of verse 4, so that the בוקר of our text would be the morning of the sixteenth of Nisan on which the return journey would be possible. Agreeing with this way of taking it would also be the proof that is brought in Nedarim 49a, that under the term בשול the idea of צלי is also included, not from our text, which after all is closest to hand, but from Chron. II, XXXV,13, ויבשלו הפסח באש במשפט.

ופנית בבקר והלכת לאהליך: on this the halacha attaches the general rule: כל פינות שאתה פונה מן הבקר ואילף, that altogether if you come into the Sanctuary with anything that you have consecrated, not necessarily an offering, but even if it is only wood for the altar, עופות ומנחות יין ולבונה ועצים, you may not go back home, out of the area of the “City of God”, immediately you have made your presentation, but every such entry טעונים ליגה, demands that one stays in the surroundings of the Sanctuary over night, and only returns home the next day. (Sifri). Thus the Torah never, and in no circumstances, wishes the purpose of any pious gift or offering brought to its Sanctuary to be terminated by the mere objective bringing of it, but insists on its being completed by the impressions its Sanctuary is to make on us in its influence on our thinking and feelings, on our desires and actions. It accordingly demands at every offering in the Sanctuary the bringer must tarry in its surroundings, that we first collect our thoughts in its vicinity, and allow the impressions we have gathered to mature in the still night, so that then, with our clear morning thoughts spiritually enriched, we can carry that treasure, as the true blessing of the Sanctuary, back to our homely hearths.

According to one opinion in תוספות, Rosh Hashana 5, a, the ופנית בבקר expresses the return at all רגלים only after the conclusion of the whole festival and not already after the first day; (refer to it there) לא מצאתי מצות לינה ברמב״ם. כעת ראיתי אשר כבר הגאון מעין חכמה תמה על זה שלא מצא מצות לינה ברמב״ם רק בפ״ד דהל׳ ביכורים וצ״ע.

V. 8. ששת ימים וגו׳. In the previous verse it says ופנית בבקר וגו׳, and according to the general way of taking it, as we explained there, this refers to the return home on the sixteenth of Nisan. Now it goes on to say that from this day for another six days mazzoth are to be eaten, respectively, no chometz may be eaten, and on the seventh day of the festival (this is the sixth day of these six days) there is to be an עצרת-day which—like the first—permits of no work being done. This way of taking it corresponds to the ברייתא of the Sifri quoted in Menachoth 66,a, ששה מן החדש שבעה מן הישן (this is the rendering of the Mechilta בא) that when it speaks here of six mazzo-days while above in v.3, it says שבעת ימים וגו׳, here the six days refer to the six days in which the mazzo may already be made from the fresh produce (see Levit. 23,14). From that it is perfectly clear that this ברייתא counts the six days of our verse from the sixteenth to the twenty-second inclusive. The day of the sixteenth, just the day of the return home is also the day on which the Omer was brought with which eating the new produce was permitted, the day to which the following שבעה שבועות etc. also is attached. But if we consider how the whole institution of the Omer and the associated prohibition to eat of the new produce, always brings to mind afresh that not only the personal freedom, celebrated by the Pessach-offering, but also the independence which the Land gives is a direct gift from the Hand of God, so that no landowner may lay a sickle to his crops before, on the sixteenth of Nisan, homage is paid with the Omer-offering of the first cutting; if we consider this, then we understand the import of the ברייתא. It is the Day of the Omer on which the return to the homely circle is permitted. And if they may eat the acknowledging mazzo on Passover eve and the mazzo-bread on the first day of the festival only from the produce of the previous year, and only the Omer-homage of the sixteenth, the day of their homecoming, allows them to have the new produce, just this permission, and every piece of Mazzo that they may now eat during these six days, repeats for them in their homes the admonition:- that also with homestead and farm, to which they now return, they have to consider themselves and behave as merely tenants, and now in homestead and farm and with homestead and farm are to make that come true which, in the name of the whole nation, was vowed anew to God in the עומר התנופה.
This admonishment belonged above all in this compendium for the future of the decentralisation.

The way another ברייתא in Pessachim 120,a, takes it is more difficult. According to it the ששת ימים of our verse are the first six days, and although the seventh day is already (v.3) considered together with the preceding days, שבעת ימים תאכל עליו מצות, here the eating of mazzo is only proclaimed for the six days and for the seventh only the עצרת-command is given, omitting all reference to it, to tell us that altogether for the whole seven days, with the exception of the first night, eating mazzoth was to be regarded as permissable but not obligatory as a mitzva: מה שביעי רשות אף ששת ימים רשות. We believe that according to this ברייתא the sense of our verse to be as follows:- after the positive duty of Pessach evening the following six days have only the negative command of eating mazzo, that only mazzo-bread excluding chometz is allowed (see Ex. 12,15), only on the seventh day is there again a positive command: עצרת לה׳ אלקיך. The Torah could not mention eating mazzo also together with עצרת for the seventh day because the relative duties of these two commands are to be completely different. The one, עצרת is to be an absolute positive command while the other תאכל מצות is only to be relative, only denying אכילת חמץ. Then thereby the שבעת ימים תאכל עליו מצות is altogether given only the relative, chometz-denying character of רשות, (permission I.L.). This is in accordance with the hermeneutical law ,דבר שהיה בכלל ויצא מן הכלל ללמד לא ללמד על עצמו יצא אלא ללמד על הכלל כולו יצא here the eating of the seventh day was included in the שבעת ימים תאכל עליו מצות ,כלל and now it was specially left out of the כלל, it was יצא מן הכלל not to put it in the same class as the positive mitzva of עצרת but to give it the רשות-character, thereby this למוד is not only given for the seventh day but is also given for the eating of mazzoth of all the other days, לא ללמד על עצמו יצא וכו׳.

עצרת לה׳ אלקיך, see on Levit. 23,36 and Numb. 29,35. The seventh day brings us the task of now gathering together all the thoughts, feelings, and resolutions which the יציאת מצרים days should have awakened afresh in us, a summing up before God which we are to take out with us into our daily active life as a “permanent” possession. In Numb. 29,35 is says עצרת תהי׳ לכם and here עצרת לה׳ אלקיך from which Beiza 15,b, learns חלקהו חציו לה׳ וחציו לכם that this inner concentration before God is to be directed both לה׳, purely spiritually to God, as well as לכם to our earthly material human existence, or as it says in Sifri on our verse: וביום השביעי עצרת לה׳ אלהיך יכול יהא אדם עצור כל היום כלו בבית המדרש ת״ל עצרת תהיה לכם הא כיצד תן חלק לבית המדרש ותן חלק לאכילה ולשתיה. This is quite in accordance with the true Jewish aspect of the mission of life which is to elevate the whole human being, body as well as soul, into the sphere of moral and mental endeavours to get near to God.
לא תעשה מלאכה. see Ex. 12,16. The עצרת-character of the day excludes עשיית מלאכה.

V. 9. שבעה שבעות. We have already fully discussed the meaning of this counting the weeks and the Festival of Weeks to which it leads and to which it gives its name, on Levit 23,10-21. Here in the compendium of laws for the decentralisation in the Land, only that is stressed of this Festival which the individual members of the nation have to do for it. Each one has to fit himself into the national circle (חג) in the “City of God” with his own individual offerings,—עולות ,שלמי חגיגה ,שלמי שמחה ראיה, and there, not only enjoy life himself with his household but make the poorer people also, the Levite, the stranger, the orphan, and the widow get to know the blessings and happiness that flow from the Torah of God in the City of God which makes every one who is enjoying the material blessings before God in view of the Sanctuary of His Torah into the dispenser of such happy blessings to those who are in need of them. The procedure of the שתי הלחם, introducing the period of bringing the first-fruits, which characterises this Festival of Weeks is a national one, a קרבן ציבור, and how very much just the care of and provision for the existence and happiness of their poorer brethren being the duty of every private individual of the nation is expressed as the consequence and effect of just this קרבן צבור we have worked out on v.22 there.

שבעה שבעות תספר לך מהחל וגו׳ תחל לספר שבעה שבעות: The Torah clearly makes us think of this counting of weeks twice, in two separate relations. It is a counting of weeks for ourselves תספר לך, and a counting of weeks from the first swing of the sickle מהחל וגו׳. The exodus from Egypt made us free personally and that freedom was completed in the national independence by granting us possession of the Land. From the combination of both these factors we have to count the weeks which are to prepare us and make us worthy to receive the beginning of the Lawgiving (see Levit. ibid). Personal freedom means nothing without Law. Without law it just throws everything down in unholy capricious confusion. True freedom only exists in Law. Israel above all only received personal freedom for it to submit to the service of the Law, the Torah; its one destiny is to become the “People of the Law, the Torah.” It requires the whole virile work of a man on himself for that, to break also the chains and the yoke of greed and passion, of the defiance of peevish wilfulness and self-will, which make men slaves of sensuality and derision of the Law. It is easy to receive personal freedom as a gracious gift from the Hands of God. But to make ourselves really free internally, as free as is required for carrying out the Torah which is our calling, that demands a sevenfold repeated gripping of our inner efforts to make progress שבעה שבועות תספר לך!

And equally so, material prosperity without that mental clarity and moral ennoblement which places the material possessions of comfortable circumstances to be used only in the service of that which is lofty, true and good, material prosperity without teachings and law, and above all, Israel’s Land of God without Israel’s Torah, Israel who has to thank its possession of the Land only to the covenant made with its forefather which is nothing other than the ברית התורה, the covenant of the Torah, the covenant for the Torah to which the Land and all the prosperity guaranteed with it is only to be subordinate as the means for the end, Israel having the Land without having been given the Torah and keeping it is the surest and most positive means for Israel’s ruin—Israel is lost, has to strike itself out of God’s book of the history of nations, if it, like the masses of the nations, would see in its national soil and the prosperity to be derived therefrom the highest purpose of the nation against which all spiritual and moral interests lose all intrinsic value in themselves and have only to be considered in as far as they serve to further purely national interests. Israel would deny its real mission amongst the nations if it did not begin to count, there where the other nations cease to count. And it does require a sevenfold work on itself to work itself up permanently to the lofty height of this contrast to the point of view which the nations of the world take, to the conviction that right and morality are the only things in the world which have true value in themselves, where one does not recognise right and morality as having value only where they serve to obtain and ensure material prosperity, but material prosperity only has meaning and importance as far as it serves to obtain and ensure right and morality, to obtain and ensure humanity and humaneness in the truest most complete sense of the words, therefore מהחל חרמש בקמה תחל לספר שבעה שבעות!

To summarise: when you have not only attained freedom, but also the possession of land, which materially ensures the retaining of freedom, you are not to consider that you have reached the goal of your destiny, but know that you are then only at the beginning of your appointment, and begin the sevenfold working on yourself to qualify yourself to take God’s Torah ever afresh from God’s Hands to utilize freedom and possessions in its service and realisation, and only thereby make freedom and possessions attain their true real value.

שבעה שבעות תספר לך and above in Levit. 23,16 תספרו חמשים יום, hence the mitzva is to count the days and to count the weeks (Chagiga 16,b), see on Levit. ibid. Here it says מהחל חרמש and there in Levit. v.15, מיום הביאכם, hence the cutting and the bringing of the Omer must be done on the same day, and as שבתות תמימות (ibid) have to be counted but our days begin from the night before, the cutting and the counting must be done in the night before the day on which the “bringing” is performed in the Sanctuary קצירה וספירה בלילה והבאה ביום (Menachoth 66,a). חרמש: see Gen. on XXV,6.

שבעות here and in verses 10 and 16 is written מלא, most likely to stress the תמימות of this counting of the weeks, and thereby this counting itself, after which the festival to which it leads, receives its name, is made to appear in its full meaning and significance. Nothing may be missing in this period of preparation, it makes demands on the whole of our time and the whole of our strength of will, the whole of ourselves. It is the most exacting and important work that the Torah expects from us (see Levit. ibid).

V. 10. ועשית חג שבעות. In Ex. 23,16 the Festival is called חג הקציר בכורי מעשיך here חג שבועות to teach that even if in the duress of unfortunate times there is no longer any reaping of the produce of our own land the Festival still remains in its שבעות importance יכול אם יש לך קציר אתה עושה י״ט ואם לאו אין אתה עושה י״ט ת״ל ועשית בין שיש (ספרי) לד קציר ובין שאין לד קציר אתה עושה י״ט.

מסת נדבת ידך. We have already explained on ולא יראו פני ריקם (Ex. 23,15) that the festival-offerings which each private individual has to bring, the שלמי חגיגה ,שלמי שמחה ,עולות ראיה correspond to the three features which characterise our festivals. They are רגלים, (pilgrim-festivals I.L.) which call every man in Israel up to the City of God, there to present himself before the Presence of God in the Sanctuary of the Torah: the symbolic expression of this renewed giving oneself up to God to fulfil His Will is עולת ראיה. They are חגים, they call every man in Israel up to fit himself, as a member of the nation, into the national circle united around their common Sanctuary of the Torah, and only by virtue of belonging to this national body to be conscious of his secure and untroubled position on earth. This happy unworried feeling of security having its roots in the consciousness of belonging to the “People of God” finds its symbolic expression in the שלמי חגיגה. And they are מועדים, times fixed by God for meeting with His people, in which God wants to come to us just as we want to raise ourselves up to Him. And out of this consciousness of the Presence of God, the fount of the purest joy springs up in the heart of every human being, and every circle of human beings who are trying to get near unto God—a festive joy which finds its symbolic expression in the שלמי שמחה. These offerings which conform with and answer the purpose of לא יראו פני ריקם are summarised here in the concept מסת מסה .נדבת ידך from מסס (from which we get מס the tax imposed), designates paying a debt to a superior who allows his possessions over which he really has the right of disposal to be “fluid” in the hands of another who has the permission to deal with them as he pleases, so that נדבה is a free-willed gift prompted by free-willed inner feelings. The purely free-willed nature of such a gift is further stressed by the following כאשר יברכך ה׳ אלקיך which leaves the size of the gift corresponding to the benefits received entirely to the discretion of the giver. So that in carrying out this mitzva of festival-offerings the idea both of חובה (duty) and נדבה (free-will) comes into play, and indeed as this duty is here called ,מסה מס, a tribute, a tax, the Gemora in Chagiga 8,a, says that the חובה part must be paid for out of the strictly secular fortune of the bringer but what is spent for these offerings which goes beyond חובה, as נדבה, could also be bought from money already dedicated, which is at the bringer’s disposal, such as מעשר שני. The general rule for the provision of offerings which are in duty bound to be brought, that כל דבר שבחובה אינו בא אלא מן החולין (see Chagiga 7,b and 8,a) rests on this expression מסת יד.

ושמחת לפני ה׳ אלקיך. In Deut. 27,7, it says וזבחת שלמים ואכלת שם ושמחת לפני ה׳ אלקיך and the Sifri takes our שמחת לפני ה׳ also to express the joy of having a meal of peace offering with one’s family “before God”. Similarly in Pessachim 109,a, This is also the source of the general שלמי שמחה which are to be brought on all the festivals, and as here the demand is only made ושמחת so that it is only made directly to the joy of the meal at eating the offering and does not refer to bringing the offering, the bringing of the שלמי שמחה in itself is not חובה and can, if need be, be brought through מעשר בהמה and נדרים ונדבות whereas עולות ראיה ושלמי חגיגה being חובה are only to be brought from חולין.

והלוי וגו׳, the Levite is designated as בשעריך, he lives scattered in the midst of the other tribes each one of which was to receive a separate province, to which we have already referred above on Ch. 12,12. The cities of the Levites were not meant to be a concentration of the Levites. These cities themselves were scattered throughout the land, and the intention must have been for the Levites to live also outside their cities amongst the rest of the population. Of the stranger, orphan and widow it says בקרבך (who are among you I.L..), they miss being attached to families, and this is to be made good by their being adopted in your midst. What we said above of the Levite applies here also to the stranger, orphan and widow. They must have been taken with the families pilgriming up to the City of God to the celebrations of the festivals there. Their participation in the family festive celebrations belongs essentially to those festive celebrations, and the following וזכרת probably refers quite specially to this.

V. 12. וזכרת (see on previous verse). In this injunction of the Torah for seeing to it that those who otherwise are generally forsaken do participate in the joys of life, the character which the People of God, redeemed from slavery are meant to have expresses itself in its highest light.

V. 13. חג הסכת וגו׳ (see detailed explanations on the Festival of Sukkoth on Levit. 23,34 to 43). We have already introductorily remarked how probably this festival would only have been first celebrated with their entry into the Land and that was why its repeated directions had to be given again in the compendium for that entry. In their wanderings living in “huts”, the remembrance of which this festival is to celebrate, was the actual concrete state of their existence.

תעשה ולא מן העשוי :חג הסכת תעשה לך see on Levit. 23,42. באספך מגרנך ומיקבך. You are to make the Festival of Sukkoth when you gather up from your barn and your wine press. Not from that which as מחובר (still joined to the ground I.L.), still belongs to nature, nor from what you have brought into your house as the blessing of the harvest and to ensure your future, but rather from that which you have left as worthless on the floors of barns and wine-press, מפסלת גרנך ויקבך, that does not bear, as the other does, the stamp of human mastery and so is liable to טומאה, out of that are you to construct the roof of your “festival hut” reminding you of God’s protection (Sukka, 12,a, see Levit. ibid, on v.43).

V. 14. ושמחת בחגך וגו׳. Although all the pilgrim-festivals are called חג, after the circle which the nation gathered together form about God and His Sanctuary of the Torah, still Sukkoth as already remarked in Levit. on XXIII,39, is quite specially characterised as חג. Just at the time of the harvest which gives most incentive to staying independently at home, Sukkoth is to awake most keenly the consciousness and the feeling of the nation belonging together through the uniting force of the Torah, and is to be most strikingly expressed. But equally so is also שמחה, the joy of each individual family life lived before God, and the joyful feeling of His happiness-giving nearness, which, although equally a “mitzva-attachment” of all the festivals, is quite specially the aim to be attained at Sukkoth. In the Festival chapter of Leviticus (Ch. XXIII, I.L.) “joy” is mentioned only in connection with Sukkoth, and here also the demand for שמחה is made twice for Sukkoth (verses 14 and 15) whereas at the Festival of Weeks it is made only once (V. 11) and at the Festival of Mazzoth it is not mentioned explicitly at all, and only by analogy with our text here ושמחת בחגך that every חג is exhorted to שמחה, is it also applied to חג המצות (see סמ״ג, הל׳ קרבן חגיגה). Actually, as a matter of fact the real period of שמחה extends from the beginning of the Festival of Weeks till the conclusion of Sukkoth (see on Ch. 26,11). This close connection between שמחה and חגיגה given from our verse here is of the greatest significance, it expresses the thought that true individual joy should only be found on the basis of the feeling of the national unity, of being at one with the nation, just as the national whole is only to consider its true well-being in the happiness of the lives of each private individual (cf. Levit. on XXIII,40 p. 702).

As already remarked on v.13, at the time when the Temple was still there, this festive joy found its expression in the family feast at which the meat of the שלמים offering was eaten (in a state of טהרה in Jerusalem I.L.). But as here, unlike there, it does not say ושמחת לפני ה׳ אלקיך but quite generally ושמחת בחגך this injunction goes beyond the place and time of the Temple and expresses the duty for all time and everywhere to prepare pure joys and festive meals for oneself and one’s family for the festivals (Pessachim 109,a). And then the concluding words here אשר בשעריך the duty would be given that also at the time of the Temple, those of the household and dependants in one’s care who were not able to go up with the rest to Jerusalem, were not to be neglected but arrangements must be made at home for them too to enjoy the festivals.

In Moed Katan 14,b, and Chagiga 8,b, both ושמחת and ביתך are stressed separately, “you shall be joyful on your festival”, and “with your festival you are to be joyful”, and from that it teaches: you shall be joyful on your festival, hence אבל אינו נוהג אבילותו ברגל, a mourner does not keep the laws of mourning on festivals (does not “sit שבעה״, wear his rent garment etc. I.L.); אבילות דמעיקרא, existing mourning is put an end to by the entry of the festival, and אבילות דהשתא, mourning occurring on the festival through the death of a near relative only starts after the festival (see חורב Ch. 43 par. 317 and cf. on Levit. 21,12). And again “it is with your festival that you shall be joyful”, hence אין נושאין נשים במועד, no marriages may take place on the festivals. Both these laws emanate from the concept חג the predominant feeling of the unity of the nation which is to be the ruling feeling on the festivals. By that feeling the pain of individual mourning for what one has lost is tempered and arrested, just as it does not tally with any private individual festival. אבילות and שמחת חתונה are both equally impairments to the consciousness of חג.

V. 15. שבעת ימים תחוג וגו׳. See Levit. on XXIII,39. Here in accordance with the purpose of this compendium of the Festivals for the impending decentralisation, only the reference to the central place to be appointed by God is stressed, as was also the case at the two preceding festivals.

כי יברכך וגו׳ והיית אך שמח. This motive being adduced, taken in conjunction with the preceding, could, we believe, be taken in the following sense:- Make the huts of your festival from the leavings of your barns and wine-presses, feeling secure in belonging to your nation, rejoice in such temporary huts with all your family, yea, in harvest time forsake your fields and orchards, barns and wine-presses and assemble in national unity, in the city chosen by God, about His Sanctuary of the Torah, for the source of your wealth and blessing and happiness lies not in your fields and meadows, not in your barns and presses, it is God, your God Who grants blessing from the City of His Torah and through the same if you flock faithfully in its vicinity and in this attachment to God and His Torah, and not to your town and country, to your barn and wine-press והיית אך שמח are you to become and remain happy and joyful.

והיית שמח is a much higher degree than ושמחת. This latter designates some temporary action, a temporary manifestation of your state of joy. והיית שמח makes happiness a trait of character, the permanent nature of your whole existence. And אך שמח makes this joyful nature persist even in conditions which would tend to disturb it or at least to intermingle a different mood with it: you remain אך, “nevertheless” joyful “only” joyful. As sure as שמחה is the loftiest blossom and fruit which is to mature on the Jewish tree of life planted by God’s Torah, so sure is it that it is not a joy which is limited to festive times and festive gatherings but which accompanies one beyond the times of festivals out into ordinary daily life, beyond exuberant merry gatherings out into the quiet humdrum home life, and is permanently to be an accompaniment throughout the whole of life with all its vicissitudes. That is a happiness that is not to be found בשעריך not in גרנך ויקבר. One can certainly institute harvest festivals and joyful holidays on the terrain of barns and wine-presses, but והיית שמח “to become and remain joyful” is only to be learnt at God and His Torah. Accordingly to gain permanent happiness that cannot be lost, with the material well-being granted by “barn and wine-press”, forsake your barn and wine press and wander up to the place chosen by God, there, in assembled united company round about God and His Torah, to achieve the spirit which qualifies you for such true real joy of living which accompanies you through your life. You learn not only ושמחת “to rejoice”, but to be אך שמח happy, “nevertheless”, (In the word היה itself lies the conception of constant existence, הוא אמר ויהי (Ps. 33,19) שקדתי ואהיה, “I was on the watch and remained so” (Ps. 102,8.). Thus also in ב״ר, 4, יתחזק :יהי רקיע כל מי שנאמר בו היה מתחלתו ועד סופו הוא צדיק ,הרקיע (ibid, 30) et alia.).

These thoughts could then also make the explanation which the גמרא gives on our sentence, more easily understood. In פסחים ע״א and סוכה מ״ח it says והיית אך שמח לרבות לילי י״ט האחרון לשמחה אתה אומר לילי י״ט האחרון או אינו אלא לילי י״ט הראשון תלמוד לומר אך חלק מה ראית לרבות לילי י״ט האחרון ולהוציא לילי י״ט ראשון מרבה אני לילי י״ט האחרון שיש שמחה לפניו ומוציא אני לילי י״ט ראשון שאין שמחה לפניו. So that the Gemora teaches from it that by the expression והיית אך שמח the duty of שמחה celebrated primarily by eating the שלמי שמחה is extended also to the night between the seventh day of Sukkoth and the eighth day which is the Day of the Festival of Azereth. But, by the limiting word אך the first night of Sukkoth would be excluded from that duty. It gives the reason for this exclusion in the fact that whereas in the night before Azereth there had been שמחה, there had been none before the first night.

If we look once again at the whole text referring to Sukkoth here we find that, as we have already repeatedly remarked and believed to have understood as being characteristic for this compendium of the festivals, there is no reference at all to שמיני עצרת. It only speaks of the seven days of Sukkoth. But when we consider that, as we have already found on Levit. 23,36, the idea of the word עצרת itself gives the meaning to the eighth day of a “Festival of Remaining and Concentration”, gathering up all the spiritual “treasures”, the thoughts and feelings collected during the days of the Festival, so that we can step over into the course of ordinary life truly enriched by them. Already by the offering prescribed for it this עצרת is characterised as a day of quiet solemn gathering before God after the days of noisy public rejoicing, considering this, the והיית אך שמח as we have just taken its meaning to be, expresses just these עצרת thoughts as it enjoins us not only to rejoice on the Festival of Sukkoth but to remain cheerful, to remain so in spite of everything that may be in store for us in the course of the coming year introduced by such pure truly festive days of Sukkoth. So that the sense of והיית אך שמח is literally nothing but לרבות י״ט אחרון לשמחה. But if, according to Rashi in Pessachim 71,a, (תוספות there and Rashi himself in Sukka 48,a, do not agree with this) this transition of the duty of שמחה only applies to the night of עצרת and does not extend to the day thereof, this perhaps would be taken as a special stressing the general law of לילה (see on v. 7), for the special duty of the שמחה of a festival. But according to the most general way of taking it this duty of שמחה extends all the more to the day of עצרת and the Gemora only speaks of לילי י״ט אחרון in contrast to לילי י״ט הראשון to which in fact the duty of שמחה does not apply. But if the reason for this difference between the first and last evenings of the festival is that the latter has שמחה preceding it which the former has not (see above I.L.) then this could make the שמחה of the evenings of our festivals altogether considered as only a result and continuation of the שמחה obtained at the preceding festival day, and this idea would be of essential significance for the whole conception we are to have of the meaning of our שמחה.

The joy which finds its complete expression in the eating of שלמי שמחה. is essentially the happy elevated feeling of private and family life lived before God. But this individual feeling of שמחה is never to be the starting-point of our festival frame of mind. But it itself is only to grow on the basis of belonging to the nation and the Torah nurtured by the Festival which preeminently takes place in the daytime, and is to be expressed by שלמי חגיגה and עולות ראיה (see on v. 9) which belong to the daytime. They form the basis for the שלמי שמחה, and it seems to us to be immediately clear that the law of שמחה can only start with the first day of the festival and the first night remain excluded. For those who have come up to Jerusalem for the festival only find themselves all joined together with their festival-offerings in the Sanctuary of the Torah before the Presence of God on the first day, whereas the entry of the Festival in the evening is only celebrated in the family gatherings. In the Jerushalmi Sukka 4,5, the reason for this contrast in the שמחה between the first and last nights of the festivals is given just by ושמחת בחגך משאתה מתחייב בחגיגה אתה מתחייב בשמחה, that the mitzva of שמחה does not start on the first night because the duty of חגיגה must have started, and this only begins on the following day (cf. on v. 14).

V. 16. שלוש פעמים וגו׳ וגו׳, cf. Ex. 23,17, and XXXIV,23; refer to there. Here at the end of this final chapter of the Festivals, summarising them all together the way of writing שלוש in full makes one’s thoughts dwell on this number three and gives all three of the festivals completely equal consideration. Whereas at the earlier instructions for this festival-pilgrimage it says in general terms אל פני האדון ה׳ or, more precisely את פני האדון ה׳ אלקי ישראל, here, in accordance with this compendium of the Law for the impending decentralisation, the declaration runs: כל זכורך .יראה כל זכורך את פני ד׳ אלתיך במקום אשר יבחר are all the individual members of the nation, אלקיך is the One God common to all of them, במקום אשר יבחר, the one single place which He has chosen for the one common Sanctuary of the one common Torah. So that the sentence says: three times in the year all the individual members of the nation are to appear out of all isolation personally before the Presence of the One God of the nation in the circle around the one common Sanctuary and thereby become conscious of each one being in connection with all the others, with God, and with His Torah.

בחג המצות impresses once again the character of the nation being united, the nation forming one circle, on each of the three Festivals. The “bread of dependance is to be in the hands of everyone at the Festival of Freedom and Independence, “counting the weeks” in the mouth of everyone at the Festival of Preparation for the Torah, and everyone is “to live in huts” at the Festivals of the harvest, the respective national festivals of the Jewish national appreciation of the three national treasures, freedom, the Torah, and material prosperity being ensured from the central point of the common Sanctuary.

The equal appreciation to which all three of the festivals can lay claim to as expressed here, according to Chagiga 17,a, indicates that the one-day domain of the Festival of Weeks also extends to a period of seven days, beyond its actual duration regarding תשלומין. So that if the עולות ראיה and שלמי חגיגה had been neglected to be brought on the day of the Festival, or if that day happened to fall on a שבת and so they could not be brought, they were to be brought within these seven days (see Levit. on Ch. 23,37 and 39).

ולא יראה את פני ה׳ ריקם. See on Ex. 23,15 and XXXIV,20. We have already remarked on Levit. 23,39 that each Moed at the same time brings an admonition to settle all the obligations we have undertaken towards God and His Sanctuary. For people living outside Jerusalem, the first רגל that occurs makes it their duty to fulfil any נדר הקדש (any vow that is to be discharged in the Sanctuary I.L.). In accordance with our שלוש פעמים וגו׳ ולא יראה וגו׳ the actual prohibition לא תאחר לשלמו (Deut. 23,21, see notes thereon) is only transgressed when three רגלים have passed without the vow having been fulfilled (Rosh Hashona 4,b, רש״י ד״ה ש״מ).

V. 17 איש כמתנת ידו. Not by what a man has, but by what he gives for God-pleasing purposes is he weighed before God in His Sanctuary, “according to the gifts of his hand”. And not according to its actual size has his gift value, its relation to “what he has received from God” determines its worth. In the Jerushalmi Mishna Chagiga I. 5 it teaches on our text עני וידו רחבה קורא אני עליו איש כמתנת ידו עשיר וידו מעוטה קורא אני עליו כברכת ד׳ אלהיך אשר נתן לך i.e. of a poor man with a generous hand I apply the words of our text “each man according to what his hand can give”, to a rich man with a stingy hand I say “give according to the blessings God has given you”!

V. 18. The laws up to here are grouped about the common thoughts of the centralising powers of attraction which the place chosen by God for the Sanctuary of His Torah is meant to exercise on the sons of His People spread out over the whole country. The following laws are now dedicated to institutions by means of which representatives of this Torah are appointed from this central point throughout the whole land, and thereby the effectiveness of this Sanctuary of the Torah is to be assured in every city of the people. שופטים ושוטרים: see on Ex. 5,6. As remarked there שוטרים are executive officers who supervise the carrying out of a verdict or a decree and, if need be, effect it. There it was those who, in accordance with the orders of the נוגשים were to drive the people on at their work.

תתן לך, the one who is addressed is the whole nation who already had their representation in the Sanhedrin of seventy-one representatives (Numb. 11,16); and these were to appoint “themselves” i.e. as their delegates, שופטים ושוטרים in every city in the land, בכל שעריך, but which, even after the division of the land still remained שעריך, belonging directly to the nation as a whole, אשר ה׳ אלקיך נותן לך לשבטיך and intermediately were subject to the tribal unit. This resulted in the appointment of a supreme court at the head of the nation, consisting of seventy-one members, the בית דין הגדול, the סנהדרין גדולה של שבעים ואחד, and coming from them, courts of justice with judges and executive officers at the head of each tribe and in every city. Hence Snhedrin 16,b מניין שמעמידין שופטים לישראל תלמוד לומר שופטים תתן, שוטרין לישראל מניין תלמוד לומר שוטרים תתן שופטים לכל שבט ושבט מניין ת״ל שופטים לשבטיך שוטרים לכל שבט ושבט מניין ת״ל שוטרין לשבטיך שופטים לכל עיר ועיר מניין ת״ל שופטים לשעריך שוטרין לכל עיר ועיר מניין ת״ל שוטרים לשעריך.

What is called שבט here, would be the same which in Makkoth 7,a, probably after the time of the second Temple when the division according to the tribes was altered, is called פלך, district, (cf. ל״מ on הל׳ סנהדרין I.1.). The relation of the tribal or district court to the city courts is not quite clear. According to רמב״ן the relation was one of competence and the ב״ד של כל שבט stood in relation to the tribe as the Sanhedrin did to the whole nation. Actually there was the supreme court, the Sanhedrin of seventy-one in the לשכת הזגית of the ante-chamber of the Temple, a smaller Sanhedrin of twenty-three members who sat at the entrance of the עזרה, another at the foot of the Temple mount the הר הבית, a similar one in each large city and a court of three, ב״ד של שלשה in every small town (Sanhedrin 2,b).

בעל כרחם .ושפטו את העם (Sifri), as delegates of the representatives of the whole nation they had authority to summon an accused to their courts at criminal cases at the instigation of witnesses, at civil cases for any claim; and, if necessary, to force such attendance. זה מינוי :משפט צדק הדיינין (Sifri) and similarly further on:- שלא תאמר :לא תטה משפט איש פלוני נאה איש פלוני קרובי and more in detail on Ch. I. 17: לא תכירו פנים במשפט זה הממונה להושיב דיינים שמא תאמר איש פלוני נאה אושיבנו דיין איש פלוני גבור אושיבנו דיין איש פלוני הלווני אושיבנו דיין איש פלוני יודע בכל לשון אושיבנו דיין נמצית מזכה את החייב ומחייב את הזכאי לא מפני שהוא רשע אלא מפני שאין יודע מעלה עליו כאלו הכיר פנים בדין. According to this way of taking it the sentences would not be speaking so much of the duties of the judges, out rather of the duty of the national authorities who are entrusted with the appointment of the judges to appoint such men as judges through whom justice, pure unadulterated justice would be achieved; and at making such appointments, next to the honesty and uprightness of character to be guided solely by knowledge of the law and insight into the law. For these traits no other qualifications, personal, social, or of scholarly attainments may be substituted. The position of our text here offers quite specially a justification of this way of taking its meaning, as here it is a question of making it a duty for the nation to appoint judges for the first time all through the whole land. According to that the ושפטו וגו׳ would refer directly to the appointment ordered at the beginning of the verse and give the purpose of it. The representatives of the whole united nation are to appoint judges and executive officers throughout the land and in making these appointments be guided solely by the purpose, that justice and true justice only becomes achieved through these appointments. The following warning, equally addressed to the national representatives, לא תטה משפט etc. makes them, the Sanhedrin who appoint these judges, responsible for any twisting of the Law, partiality shown, or bribery accepted at any court in the land, if they have not taken the care demanded in the appointment of the local judges. לא תטה משפט etc. accordingly means: you are not to twist the law etc. through the judges whom you appoint.

V. 19. לא תטה משפט. The Sifri gives the explanation as:- לא תטה ממון .משפט בממון ולא תכיר פנים בדין is what the dispute is about, דין is deciding the verdict. The Law can be “deviated” through two methods. The judge can have formed a perfectly true judgment in his mind, but against his conviction he awards the object in dispute, ממון to the person who is not entitled to have it, so that it is “deviation” of the verdict, מטה משפט בממון. Or he forms his judgment, דין, not on purely objective actual grounds, but allows considerations of the personalities of the parties to influence his judgment, he is מכיר פנים בדין (see Ch. 1,16 & 17).
ולא תקח שוחד. See on Ex. 23,8.

V. 20. צדק צדק תרדף. As the highest unique goal, to be striven for purely for itself, to which all other considerations have to be subordinated, the concept צדק, “Right, Justice,” forming all private and public matters in accordance with God’s Torah is to be kept in the mind of the whole nation.
