To pursue this goal unceasingly with all devotion is Israel’s one task, למען תחיה וירשת etc. with that it has done everything to secure its physical (תהיה) and political (וירשת) existence. Inasmuch as here the political security of the land to be achieved by acknowledging and caring for Right and Justice, is called וירשת ,ירושה, even after possession of the Land has been completed,—and the text is obviously speaking of such a time—, the significant truth is thereby laid down that the possession of the land comes into question every minute, and it has to be taken into possession afresh every minute by the Jewish State as a whole paying acknowledging tribute to “Right and Justice”, and making this realised in the land. In Sanhedrin 32,b, the repetition of צדק צדק in our verse is further explained that every judical activity even if it is not to make a decision but only to arrange a compromise must be guided entirely by impartiality: צדק צדק תרדף אהד לדין ואחד לפשרה. Even in פשרה, to compromise, to arrange an amicable agreement between the contending parties, which, according to Sanhedrin 6, a, מצוה לבצוע, to attempt which is a mitzva in every civil quarrel which is brought to court, the judge may not favour one party more than the other.

V. 21. לא תטע לך וגו׳. We have already explained on Ex. 34,13, that אשרה was a tree which was supposed to be under the special protection of a god or goddess whose presence and influence could be obtained by tending and making it thrive (אשר) and showing it honour. This is entirely in keeping with the nature of the heathen gods whose godheads were, above all, forces of nature, whose rule manifested itself in the development and the phenomena of the physical world. But to that the Jewish conception of God is in complete contrast. Not only the physical world, but in a much higher, more intimate and direct manner is the spiritual-moral world of humanity the sphere of the rule of its God, and only by submitting the whole of his spiritual being, his desires and his actions under the authoritative orders of his God has the Jewish man to obtain also his participation in the thriving of the physical world. He has not to plant an אשרה, no tree whatsoever, כל עץ next to the altar of his God which he erects for “himself”. He has to erect his altars for “himself”, for the submission and dedication and elevation of himself towards God, and with this submission, dedication and elevation of his morally free human nature to God he has also submitted his material physical world to the blessing-giving and protective rule of God. No “tree” has he to plant next to his “altar”. With the moral “altar-dedication” and devotion of his human nature to God he has everything, without it, nothing. This is the pure result of the preceding צדק צדק תרדף למען תחיה and this sequence makes our sages say in Sanhedrin 7,b: כל המעמיד דיין שאינו הגון על הצבור כאלו נוטע אשרה בישראל שנאמר שופטים ושוטרים תתן לך וסמיך ליה לא תטע לך אשרה and gives the saying more than just superficial reference. The national authorities who appoint a judge who is not really a person who should be entrusted with such an office express thereby an indifference to the national high standard of moral life being the condition on which national prosperity depends which is similar to the idea expressed by planting an אשרה which also tries to obtain material physical prosperity by means other than a conscientiously lived life of duty.

A “tree” next to the Jewish Altar is such a clouding of the Jewish conception of God and life that an extension of its symbolic meaning by our sages banned מדרבנן any wooden structure from the architectural surround of the Altar (Tamid 28,b; see רמב״ם הל׳ ע״ז VI,10).

V. 22. ולא תקים לך מצבה אשר שנא וגו׳. We have already worked out on Gen. 28,18, and XXXIII,20, the relation of מצבה to מזבח, and have remarked how the מצבה, a stone taken from God’s creation, represents a memorial to that which God has done for us in Nature and History, whereas מזבח, a structure built up out of several stones by human hands is meant to represent the devotion of human activity to God. A difference in which we believed we could see why מצבה which had been אהובה לאבות (beloved by God when made by the forefathers I.L.) was expressed here as being שנואה לבנים (hated by Him if erected by their descendants I.L.). Before מתן תורה it was, above all, the Rule of God in nature and history which had to be recognised in its exclusiveness in the minds of men, and no complete individual and national life existed yet, which, by its submission to God’s Torah was to be a manifestation of homage to God. So that there was still place for the מצבה next to the מזבח. With מתן תורה, the מצבה concept is not only included in, and absorbed by the מזבח, but מצבה becomes actually sinful. Merely worshipping God in His Greatness and Allmight is not only a form of homage which is not pleasing to God, but, as our text expresses it, henceforth God “hates” any worship of His Greatness and Allmight which does not seek to express the moral submission of the whole of the human being to His Law, His Torah. It is our obedience which is to be the expression of our recognition of and homage to God. He measures our recognition of His Greatness and Allmight by the amount of our devotion to His Will; and He rejects every homage to Him in nature and history which places heaven and earth under His Mastery, but denies this mastery over one’s own self, one’s own heart, one’s mind and desires and actions. Not acknowledgment of God, but recognition of His Will is the Jewish mission and the way to Jewish happiness, not מצבה but מזבח is the symbol of the Jewish mission in life. מצבה-devoutness is deadening of the Jewish spirit. לא תקים לך מצבה אשר שנא ה׳ אלקיד (see on Gen. 33,20). Accordingly לא תקים לך מצבה is naught but a further consequence of the preceding צדק צדק תרדף למען וגו׳ וירשת. Only by unreservedly ruling our private and national lives in accordance with the dictates of God’s Will can we obtain the blessing-giving and sustaining ruling of God in our social and political fate, the consciousness of which is endangered by the מצבה conception and thoughts on the great deeds of God, and צדק צדק תרדף למען תחיה וירשת denies in the most speaking manner אשרה and מצבה.

V. 1. לא תזבח וגו׳ is the complementing final verse of the preceding. It has been said that devotion to the duties of our life, as it comes to be symbolically expressed on the Altar of God, is the foundation of our physical and political wellbeing and happiness. Now it is added that this devotion comprises the whole of our being, and must completely conform in the way it is expressed with what is in agreement with God’s Will for us. Nothing may be missing (מום) on the sacrificial animal which is to express the surrender of our own being to God, and it must have none of the repulsive qualities (כל דבר רע) described in Leviticus, which would mar the pure expression of our surrendering ourselves to our duties. כל דבר רע and תועבה, according to the Sifri, comprise all the איסורי מזבח and פסולי המוקדשים, viz. חרץ לזמנו ,חולה זקן ומזוהם ;בעל גרב יבלת ותזזית ,בעל מום קבוע ועובר אתנן ומחיר כלאים וטריפה ויוצא דופן ,רובע ונרבע מוקצה ונעבד ,וחוץ למקומו (see Levit. 1,2, 3; VII, 18; XXII, 22-24; XXVII, 28, and Deut. 23,19). And indeed the “completeness” and “blamelessness” of our lives and desires as is described here as the actual concrete goal of all the activities of the state, and as the symbolic sacrificial expression of the task of our private and public lives, is given here to be understood both from the standpoint of its relations to our work (שור) and activities as well as those of our fate and fortune (שה). That the individuals and the nation be, and remain, the שור of our “Master”, and the שה״ of our “Shepherd” is what the representatives of the nation have to strive to effect by the delegates they appoint in all parts of the country from their centre point in the Sanctuary.

V. 2. כי ימצא וגו׳. In connection with the preceding, now follows the form for the procedure of the court in criminal cases by which the board of national representatives (the Sanhedrin I.L.) itself, or through their delegates, have to carry out their mission of maintaining the Law, the Torah, at all crimes that are committed. For that, the case of the worst crime, עבודה זרה, idolatry, is chosen. Even for that, the persecution has to follow exactly the precisely prescribed procedure ordered for crimes of lesser gravity. The prosecution of even this deepest crime has to rest, as the whole of Jewish judical administration in criminal cases, solely on the declaration of actual witnesses, to the exclusion of any circumstantial evidence (however convincing this might appear to be I.L.). Here, too, the intervention of the court can only begin following a charge made by eye-witnesses who have to produce legal evidence, excluding any inquisitional procedure resting on mere denunciation. Here too the declaration of the witnesses has to undergo a very searching investigation and testing, and here too the crime comes under the jurisdiction of the human court only if the criminal, at the moment of committing it, is proved to have been made aware of, and conscious of the unlawful nature of his act. All these conditions are indicated in the cases which follow.

מצא .כי ימצא בקרבך is the term habitually used for noting something based on the evidence of witnesses (cf. Numb. 15,32, 33 and Ex. 22,3). Although מצא does also designate finding something through searching for it, still as a rule it means an unintentional finding, and this corresponds entirely to the completely objective conditions in which the witnesses came across the deed which their charge states to have occurred.

בקרבך באתר שעריך. It is the nation to whom these words are addressed. In whatever place in its domain the crime has been committed, it has been committed “in the nation”, and it is incumbent on the nation as a whole, in its members as witnesses, and its representatives, or the delegates of its representatives, as courts of justice, to uphold the Law against criminality.

אשר יעשה את הרע בעיני ה׳ א׳ לעבר בריתו probably does not refer just to the case of the ע״ז sin which is chosen as the example in the following, but is a general characterisation of all crimes which come to the knowledge of the court. Transgressing any prohibition, doing something which God has declared to be רע בעיניו is an infringement of His ברית. Without exception, every one of God’s Laws is held by repeated כריתות ברית (the establishment of a covenant I.L.), (see Ex. 24,8 and Deut. 28,69 and XIX,8 as well as Sota 37,b), and thereby established inviolably for ever as absolute, as a ברית (see Gen. 6,18). A crime can only reach judical recognition if that which is רע בעיני ה׳ had been committed with the consciousness that thereby one was עובר בריתו (breaking His covenant I.L.), accordingly, if the criminal at the moment of committing the crime had in mind the declaration of the Torah that it was forbidden and the judical punishment that it entailed. A condition that could only be proved by התראה having been made, i.e. by the witnesses having warned the criminal of it at the moment he was about to commit it, and by the latter’s express קבלת התראה, by his having declared that nevertheless and in spite of the consequences he would still do it. Hence the questions having to be put to the witnesses: התריתם בו קבל עליו התראה התיר עצמו למיתה המית תוך כדי דבור וגו׳ (did you warn him, did he realise your warning and say he was prepared to give his life for the crime? etc. I.L.), (Sanhedrin 40,b; see on Levit. 20,17 and Numb. 15,33; see also v. 6).

V. 3. וילד ויעבד. Cf. Ch. 13,6 and 14. This “and he went and served”, this “going to do something”, his having to “go” to do it expresses the whole antithesis to which such a crime should stand to the nature of a Jew, and at the same time the audacity which must have been attached to carrying out such a crime with full consciousness of its antithetical nature.
ויעבד וישתחו, see on Ex. 20,5.

אשר לא צויתי. This sentence is difficult if one refers the אשר to the עבודה and עבודה והשתחויה לאלהים אחרים ולכל צבא השמים .השתחויה is not only something which it is not commanded to do, but is something forbidden to do, and indeed the most prohibited of all prohibitions. So one must then refer the phrase to the עבודה and השתחויה directed to שמש וירח וכל צבא השמים and take it perhaps to be somewhat in the sense that הל׳) רמב״ם ע״ז I. and II) takes the origin of idolatry, in the time of Enoch, to have been that, without denying the One God, yea, in supposed honouring of Him, honour was paid to the heavenly bodies as being His servitors, which would then only have been a sin because God had not commanded this worship of His servitors as such. But we still believe to doubt whether עבודה והשתחויה directed to the צבא השמים as being servants of God, although certainly אסור would be חייב מיתה (a capital crime I.L.) כל זמן שלא קבלו עליו באלוה, as long as one did not take them to be divinities in themselves but only creations and servitors of the One God. (see כ״מ on הל׳ ע״ז III,6). But we prefer to think that אשר לא צויתי would refer to the immediately preceding כל צבא שמים which of course would include the sun and moon, so that this incomplete defection into ע״ז would be excluded. For there are really two categories mentioned here:- אלהים אחרים, gods of heathen erroneous ideas who have no real existence at all so that עבודה and השתחויה to them tacitly implies their divinity, recognises them as gods, and שמש וירח וכל צבא השמים bodies invested with real power and influence, honouring of which only bears the full character of ע״ז if they are taken to be independent godly forces able to dispense favour or the reverse at their own caprice. According to that the verse would read: “and serve and prostrate themselves to other gods, and to the sun and moon and to all the heavenly bodies whom I have not commanded” i.e. as being not under My command. Cf. המימך צוית בקר (Job. 38,12) (“hast thou ever commanded morn to come! I.L.), and especially ידי נטו שמים וכל צבאם צויתי (Is. 45,12) (“My Hands stretched out the heavens and all their hosts are at My command I.L.).

In Megilla 9,b. our verse is added to the alterations which the seventy Jewish sages allowed themselves to make in the translation of the Pentateuch they were ordered to make for Ptolmy II, to avoid misunderstandings. They allowed themselves to add the word לעובדם and to translate it as if it stood: אשר לא צויתי לעובדם “whose service I have not commanded, “and Rashi explains the reason for this alteration to be to prevent it being taken as meaning אשר לא צויתי שיהיו, “whose existence I had not commanded” from which it could be deduced that they were really gods. If we compare this with the other alterations enumerated there, we find that most of them do not correspond with the real sense of the text, but give a divergence from it, as the true sense might give occasion for misunderstandings. Thus: ,ותצחק שרה בקרוביה ,ויכל ביום הששי וישבת ביום השביעי ,אעשה אדם בצלם ובדמות .אשר חלק אתם להאיר לכל העמים ,וישלח את זאטוטי בני ישראל ,כי באפם הרגו שור לא חמר אחד ,על נושא בני אדם ,זכר ונקבה בראו ,אלהים ברא בראשית Even obliterates the real sense of the text.

Unless we are mistaken this confirms the way we took this sentence. אשר לא צויתי לעובדם is by no means the real sense of it. That is rather אשר לא צויתי שיהיו only that is not meant positively as it could be misunderstood to mean but hypothetically: the צבא השמים are worshipped with the idea that I had not created them to obey My orders and run in the course I set them, אשר לא צויתי “they are not under My orders”.
V. 4. והגד לך is the declaration of the witnesses, ושמעת, the judical hearing of the case, ודרשת היטב is the prescribed investigation of the witnesses by דרישות חקירות ובדיקות. (see on XIII,15).

V. 5. והוצאת וגו׳. See on Levit. 24,14. The place of execution is to be outside the city but, as we believe, in such proximity to the city that the place appears as “before the gates of the city” as belonging to the township. That is how we think the expression הוצאה אל שעריך is to be understood. The Halacha also runs in similar terms: העובד ע״ז סוקלין אותו על שער שעבד בו. Thereby it is to be made clear that the fellow citizens of the criminal reject his crime with horror, so that by it he has shut himself out of their confraternity. Hence further the sentence in the Gemora that if the majority of the inhabitants of the city were non-Jews, the sentence is to be carried out על פתח בית דין just outside the court of justice (Kethuvoth 45,b)—שעריך, similarly to v. 2, the gate of the city in which the sin was committed שער שעבד בו not the city where the court which tried him was, not שער שנידון בו (ibid).

את האיש או את האשה. By this repetition, the procedure here is limited to cases where the sin has been committed by individuals only. Only then is the smaller court of twenty-three members competent to deal with it, and the verdict has to be סקילה, whereas if the whole community of a town has fallen to idolatry, an עיר הנדחת, it can only be judged by the supreme court of seventy one members and the death penalty is to be carried out by the sword. אין עושין ערי הנדחת אלא על פי ב״ד של שבעים ואחד אמר קרא והוצאת את האיש ההוא או את האשה ההיא איש ואשה אתה מוציא לשעריך ואי אתה מוציא כל העיר כולה לשעריך (Sanhedrin 16,b; see on Ch. 13,13 et seq. — וצ״ע דהא האי אל שעריך הוא). שער שעבד בו ולא שער שנידון בו כדלעיל.
וסקלתם באבנים: see on Levit. 20,2.

V. 6. על פי שנים עדים וגו׳. In Sanhedrin 37,b, it is first pointed out from our text that altogether a judical procedure is only possible on the evidence of eye-witnesses, and that אומד, circumstantial evidence, even if it establishes practically a certainty—as in the case quoted there as an example—in no case suffices for the intervention of human justice.

It says further: על פי שנים עדים או שלשה עדים יומת המת, now it is clear that after the Torah has declared that the evidence of two witnesses is sufficient to establish the case, the addition of a third or any other number of witnesses is neither necessary nor can affect the case, the Gemora in Makkoth 5. takes the addition of the words “or three witnesses” to establish on the one hand, that the credibility of a declaration made by witnesses does not increase through the number of witnesses, but that two witnesses have the same power of authenticity as three or a hundred, and two witnesses can appear against a hundred. On the other hand, that although two witnesses are quite sufficient, still a larger number united to give the same evidence form an undivisable unit just as two do, so that with three or any larger number the הזמה penalty (see on Ch. 19,19) could only be imposed on each one of them if they are all convicted of the הזמה crime; but also that the third and further witnesses, although their evidence is completely superfluous and unnecessary, are nevertheless liable to be convicted of הזמה with all the consequences thereof; and finally, if amongst three or a hundred witnesses united to give evidence, only one is found to be ineligible on account of relationship to the accused or on any other count, the whole evidence (treated as one unit as above I.L.) is inadmissable just as it would be if it consisted of only two witnesses. על פי שני עדים או שלשה עדים יומת המת אם מתקיימת העדות בשנים למה פרט הכתוב בשלשה אלא להקיש שנים לשלשה מה שלשה מזימין את השנים אף השנים יזימו את השלשה ומנין אפילו מאה ת״ל עדים ר׳ שמעון אומר מה שנים אינן נהרגין עד שיהיו שניהם זוממים אף שלשה אינן נהרגין עד שיהיו שלשתן זוממין ומנין אפילו מאה ת״ל עדים ר״ע אומר לא בא הכתוב השלישי להקל אלא להחמיר עליו ולעשות דינו כיוצא באלו וכר׳ ומה שנים נמצא אחד מהן קרוב או פסול עדותן בטלה אף שלשה נמצא אחד מהן קרוב או פסול עדותן בטלה מנין אפילו מאה תלמוד לומר עדים (מכות ה׳ ב׳).

(The argument of this ת״ל עדים אפילו מאה seems to be: were it to say על פי שנים או שלשה עדים “on the declaration of two or three witnesses” one would take the number three to be definite, and make all the laws given for two witnesses to be the same if there were three, but one would not be justified in applying it to a larger number; but as it interposes the word עדים viz. על פי שנים עדים או שלשה עדים it allows the שלשה עדים just like the שנים עדים to be taken as just the beginning of an unlimited number of עדים).

Opinions differ on the questions as to what factors are necessary for the evidence of a number of witnesses to be considered together as one united piece of evidence with all the consequences enumerated above, whether they all have to have seen the act or acts at the same time (the ראיה), or whether they must all have come together to report at the same time (הגדה), whether either one of these would suffice or both are necessary. In cases where the attention of witnesses are not for the purpose of making an accusation before a court of justice, but to establish the legality of an act, such as marriage or divorce (see on Ch. 24,1) for which the presence of two reliable witnesses is necessary, there, in any case it is ordered that two unimpeachable witnesses be appointed to the exclusion of all others, so that the possible presence of relations of other ineligible witnesses of the act should not be able to bring the legality of the procedure into question (see תוספות ibid, and ח״מ Ch. 36).

יומת המת, on this, that the criminal, even before the execution, even before the verdict, as it is speaking of receiving the declarations of the witnesses, is already called מת, the Gemora in Sanhedrin 41,a, bases the halacha already quoted on v. 2, that he must not only have been warned, at the moment of the deed, of the prohibition, but also of the death-penalty attached to it and that he committed the act definitely under the presumption of such eventual consequence, התיר עצמו למיתה (in contemporary colloquial terms “I’ll do it if I hang for it” I.L.), So that he already has the verdict of death on him when he appears before the court, and the task of the court is rather to try and find some possible grounds for remitting the death penalty, ושפטו העדה והצילו העדה (see Numb. 35,24 and 25). Bechoroth 18,b, also takes these words used here as a basis for the saying: רשעים בחייהם קרויין מתים, that, whereas the righteous even in death are still called living on, the wicked even in their life can be called “dead”, a sinful existence does not correspond to the concept “living”.

לא יומת על פי עד אחד. After it has already been declared by על פי שנים וגו׳ that one single witness is ineligible to testify, the further declaration לא יומת על פי עד אחד is taken in Makkoth 6,b, to exclude separate single testimony, עדות מיוחדת. It is not sufficient that the crime was witnessed by two reliable men, but at the moment of their witnessing the act, they must each know of the presence of the other, each must know that he is not alone the sole witness of the act, they must see each other or both be seen by a third person who warns the criminal, a person who both of them see or (according to Rambam: and) who sees both of them, so that they can be joined together to give what has to be regarded as one corporate testimony. Otherwise their evidence remains עדות מיוחדת and they cannot appear in court as witnesses שנים רואים אותו אחד מחלון זה ואחד מחלון זה ואין רואין זה את זה אין מצטרפות .אם היו רואין את המתרה או (גי׳ הרמב״ם והמתרה) המתרה רואה אותן מצטרפין such עדות מיוחדת is only inadmissable in criminal cases, but not in civil cases, בדיני ממונות (ibid).

From the expression על פי שנים עדים (from the mouth of two witnesses I.L.) the Gemora deduces (ibid) that the court must obtain the declaration directly from the mouth of the witness, accordingly the judges must understand the language of the witness and they are not allowed to use an interpreter. שלא תהא סנהדרין שומעת מפי התורגמן. They need not necessarily be able to speak the language and may use an interpreter to convey what they have to say, to the witness.
See further on the institution of witnesses on Ch. 19,15.

V. 8. כי יפלא וגו׳. Verses 8-13 appoint the supreme court sitting at the central point of the nation at the Sanctuary of the Torah, to be the highest ultimate authority on whose shoulders rests the responsibility for the authentic tradition and interpretation of the Torah, as well as making all arrangements for its being kept correctly. It has the power to make final decisions which the people in general as well as the officials appointed to teach them the Law have to accept and put into practice without contradiction.—כי יפלא. In Levit. 22,21, we have recognised פלא, a miracle, to designate such an event which occurs without any connection with the existing order of things, and completely independent of it, as a pure act of the Will of God’s almighty power. To be by itself without connections is the basic meaning of the word פלא. So that used here for the teachers of the Law, and those whose function it is to make decisions in accordance with the law, it designates such a case for which the functionary can find no connection and analogy with other fixed norms and facts of the Law out of which he could deduce any decision he could make with certainty for this particular case. The case is a פלא to him. At the same time it is taken for granted (according to Sanhedrin 87,a) that it is dealing here with one who in general is fully qualified to make decisions, is well versed in the Law and not of one who is altogether not called on to make decisions on points of the Law. Such a one would not be liable to the consequence of a זקן ממרא expressed in v. 12 an authority who acts in contradiction to the supreme tribunal, כי יפלא ממך דבר במופלא שבב״ד הכתוב מדבר, למעוטי תלמיד (תוספות ibid). To a תלמיד שלא הגיע להוראה everything is פלא.

בין נגע ,בין דין זכאי לדין חייב :בין דין לדין ,בין דם טמא לדם טהור :בין דם לדם (רש״י) בין נגע טמא לנגע טהור ,לנגע. Thereby three principle categories are designated in which doubts as to decisions could arise: ,(בין דין לדין), דיני ממנות ונפשות ,(בין דם לדם) איסור והיתר .(בין נגע לנגע טומאה וטהרה. One is in doubt whether to declare the blood טמא or ,(לבעל) טהור the accused as חייב or זכאי, the plague as נגע טמא or נגע טהור.

דברי ריבות בשעריך comprises all other cases regarding which a doubt might arise, on which the delegate judges appointed בשעריך in the cities and the tribes (see v. 18) could not come to agreement and so remained open as disputed questions, דברי ריבות, amongst the local authorities of the Law.

מב״ד :וקמת (ibid), every lawcourt is thought of as “sitting” while functioning. In every place there was a permanent sitting of the Beth Din daily till midday where everybody who had a case to bring or a question of the law to be decided could obtain a hearing from a bench duly qualified. But if a court itself required instruction for some unsolved case of doubt it had to suspend its sitting and go up to the place where the decision would be made for it. (Rashi ibid).
מלמד שבית המקדש גבוה מא״י :ועלית (ibid) the Sanctuary of the Torah, in one of the halls of which the supreme court of justice held its sittings, lay higher than all the dwelling-places of Israel.

מלמד שהמקום גורם :אל המקום אשר יבחר ד׳ אלהיך בו (ibid), the place itself is of essential importance for the Law laid down here. Just as God had chosen one single place where the evidence of His revelation of His Law was to be deposited, where the demands and consequences of keeping that Law was to be addressed by symbolic representation to the nation, and where alone they were to come to express their devotion to this Law in symbolic procedures, in the same way He designated this same place to be the one and only place where the supreme authorities of the Law for the concrete recognition and realisation of this, His Law, were to hold their sittings. So that the central place of the symbolic theoretical and the concrete actual position of the Law, the Torah, should be one and the same. One can say that what the בגדי כהונה (the priestly vestments I.L.) were for the priests, the לשכת הגזית (the chamber in the Temple where the supreme court sat I.L.) was for the Sanhedrin. Only on the ground of the Sanctuary of the Torah, in the hall arranged at the side of the Altar for it, is the Sanhedrin, that Board of Supervision of the Torah, composed by the spiritual elite of the nation, invested with its full powers. Accordingly, only as long as it had its seat there, it, as well as its delegated courts of justice in all the cities of the country were authorised to decide between life and death in cases of capital crimes, דיני נפשות, and equally so only when the decisions of the Sanhedrin were given out from this place, was acting against them by any accredited functionary, a capital crime. (Sanhedrin 14,b; Avouda Zara 8,b, רש״י and תוספות ibid; cf. Levit. 4,3, p. 97 et seq).

V. 9. ובאת אל הכהנים הלויים ואל השופט. The intimate connection between the Sanhedrin and the Sanctuary of the Torah discussed on the previous verse is also expressed here in this placing together of priest and court of justice (see Sanhedrin 52,b). It is one and the same purpose and goal, one and the same true aspect of life which both serve (cf. Ex. 20,22). The authentic text of the Torah, תורה שבכתב rested, under the care of the priests, next to the evidence of its Divine origin (see Ch. 31,25, 26 and XVII,18) just as the Sanhedrin were the first possessors of the traditional explanation of the Torah תורה שבעל פה, and even if—as is perfectly clear from Levit. 4,3—there was no innate authority on the Torah vested in the priests, not even in the High-priest who regarding the teachings of the Torah was placed on exactly the same level as the lowest in the land,—was not the first Sanhedrin, the “College of Seventy” which Moses appointed to be at his side, chosen without distinction from all the twelve tribes (Numb. 11,16)—still, as remarked there, and can be deduced as taken for granted here, provided they were fit for it, it was a mitzva to appoint priests also to the Sanhedrin. Here and in v. 18 the כהנים are called by their tribal name הכהנים הלויים probably to stress that it is not so much their special character as priests, as their tribal character as Levites, who had proved themselves as undaunted practical representatives of the Torah, a spirit, the constant existence of which is certainly highly desirable to have in the supreme “College of the Torah”. Ezekiel in Ch. 44,15 calls the כהנים בני צדוק who had proved themselves steadfast guardians of the Sanctuary of the Torah amid all the defections of the nation away from God “Levites” והכהנים הלויים בני צדוק אשר שמרו משמרת מקדשי בתעות בני ישראל מעלי and the Gemora in Yebamoth 86, b, and elsewhere takes this as the classic example to prove that כהנים are also called לויים (cf. Levit. on IV,3). בעשרים וארבע מקומות נקראו כהנים לוים וזה אחד מהם וגו׳

ואל השופט, the President of the supreme court. In later centuries still only the presidents of the court, the נשיא or the אב בית דין were named in a similar manner and the whole of their courts were understood to be included.

ואל השופט אשר יהיה בימים ההם. By this addition “who shall be in those days” the Gemora in Rosh Hashona 25,a teaches the principle that at all times one has to obey and follow the contemporary ecclesiastical authorities who are qualified by their conscientiousness and their knowledge to be teachers of the Law, even if they do not attain the greatness of mind and spirit of the authorities of the past וכי תעלה על דעתך it says there on our verse, וכי תעלה על דעתך שאדם הולך אצל הדיין שלא היה בימיו הא אין לך לילך אלא אצל שופט שבימיך. In the Sifri the sentence runs thus: וכי תעלה על דעתך שאדם הולך אצל שופט שלא נמצא בימיו אלא מה תלמוד לומר אל השופט .אשר יהיה בימים ההם אלא שופט שהוא כשר ומוחזק לך באותן הימים
ודרשת, similarly to Gen. 25,22, דבר המשפט .ותלך לדרש את ה׳ is just the decision on the matter about which one was doubtful, כי יפלא ממך דבר למשפט (v. 8).

V. 10. הגיד ,אשר יגידו .ועשית וגו׳ from נגד is the real term for every saying which brings something before the mind of somebody else. It “puts it down objectively” before him. Hence, a report of something that has happened or has been said. Hence equally so, for revelation: ויגד לכם את בריתו (Ch. 4,13); מגיד דבריו ליעקב (Ps. 147,19) and for tradition שאל אביך ויגדד (Ch. 32,7). Hence also in V. 9 the general term for the decisions which emanate from the highest tribunal of the Law, whether such decisions are based on tradition, deduction or instructions. For the whole nation and its officials they are הגדה, objective sayings given out, which for theory and practice are henceforth to be used as basic facts for the Law. This duty of following with unswerving loyalty decisions made by the highest authority in response to enquiries is expressed in this verse (10) and moreover the decisions are characterised in two ways according to the source from which they are derived viz. הגדה in the narrow sense and .הוראה הגדה in the narrower sense is tradition. Your doubt, your question arose because a fact of the law belonging to the oral tradition הלכה למשה מסיני had escaped your notice. The ב״ד הגדול supplements the tradition for you יגידו לך מן המקום ההוא. Or their decision is an הוראה, a decision either arrived at by means of the hermenutical rules sanctioned by the Lawgiver for the interpretation of and research into His Torah, or a decree, an institution designed for the practical maintenance of the Torah, both in contrast to הגדה, to pure tradition, mental operations reproducing or producing, accordingly אשר יורוך ,הוראה. For the one as for the other the duty is promulgated, ועשית וגו׳ ,ושמרת לעשות with special stress for ושמרת לעשות :הוראה, the more so as with הוראה as human brains have worked with the God-given Torah to produce it.

V. 11. ועשית וגו׳. That which V. 10 made into a duty to be kept for the decision given in any individual case brought to the highest tribunal is here (V. 11) declared to be a bounden duty in general for the whole practice of the Law. Moreover in all the three ways of the teaching activities of the Sanhedrin already indicated above:- the protecting and furthering rules which they make for the practice of the Torah, the real אשר יורוך תורות דרבנן, the general duty of keeping them which is repeatedly given in the command of שמירה (see Ex. 23,30); the results of research and interpretation of the Torah based on the traditional hermeneutical י״ג מדות שהתורה נדרשת בהן the המשפט אשר יאמרו לך; and finally the further handing down the traditions they have received, הדבר אשר יגידו לך for all three the Torah demands the most unswerving obedience, active and abstaining, תעשה ולא תסור, and thereby already beforehand grants its full sanction to all future decisions of the ב״ד הגדול and making them imposed as an obligation on the whole nation. So that at the base of all מצות דרבנן there lies an obligation דאוריתא and acting against a law of the rabbis is no less than transgressing a Divine command and prohibition, which is indeed why before performing a command of the rabbis we can also say with full authority אשר קדשנו במצותיו וצונו (Who hath made us holy by giving us mitzvas, and He hath commanded us to … e.g. wash our hands I.L.) Sabbat 23a. Nevertheless the sages themselves have sharply marked their man-made laws and differentiated them from the actual God-made laws of the Torah, so that anyone who knows the laws can know which are which, inasmuch as they themselves order them in certain conditions to be treated less strictly thus ,אין גוזרין גורה לגזרה ,בשל סופרים הלך אחר המיקל ,ספק דאורייתא לחומרא ספק דרבנן לקולא ,המנינהו דרבנן בדרבנן ,לא אתי דרבנן ומפיק דאוריתא etc. (e.g. if you are doubtful whether you have performed a Mitzva or not, if it is a mitzva of the rabbis, you get the benefit of the doubt; if of the Torah the mitzva gets it, etc. etc. I.L.) see מגלת אסתר on שורש ראשון ,ספר המצות. And even if they were authorised by the Torah to issue their commands for the protection of the Torah with the full dictatorial powers of imposing them by law, as a rule they did not do this, but only then gave these instructions the full force of being definite laws after they had been accepted and received the sanction of the greater part of the nation: פשט איסורו ברוב ישראל גזרו וקבלו. (Avouda Zara 36,a and b).

V. 12. והאיש speaks of the teacher of the Torah who had to place the decision for the case which remained in dispute between him and his colleagues before the Sanhedrin in the לשכת הגזית. If he does not adopt the decision and decides in a practical case brought to him in accordance with the view hitherto taken by him and in opposition to the decision of the ב״ד הגדול, he forfeits his life thereby. חזר לעירו שנה ולמד כדרך שהיה למד פטור ואם הורה לעשות חייב שנאמר והאיש אשר יעשה בזדון אינו חייב עד שיורה לעשות (סנהדרין פ״ו ע״ב).

לשרת ,אל הכהן העמד לשרת שם וגו׳ (see on Ex. 28,35). It has already been remarked on V. 9 that the singular number looks on the whole court as being represented by its President. It was also remarked there that it was desirable though not imperative to have כהנים amongst the members of the Sanhedrin. Now here two possibilities are presumed, either the President is a כהן who would also be one העומד לשרת שם וגו׳ or a non-priest who then would only be in opposition to the זקן ממרא (the nonconforming rabbi I.L.) in his capacity as President of the bench. In the first case the personality of the Presiding Judge, who has to inform him of the decision of the bench, would bring home to him more strikingly the intimate connection between the procedures of the court and the service in the Sanctuary of the Torah, which, in the second case is only achieved by the place in which the decision is made. The concept שרת, in which the service of the priest in the Sanctuary is regarded, designates the procedures of that service as being expressive of the form which all conditions of the private and public life of the nation should adopt to be in accordance with giving satisfaction to God, and it is in service of accomplishing the actual concrete realisation of this form, that the proceedings of the court take place. Jewish Law with all its norms for the private and social lives of the nation, is not in service of man-made ideas of justice and expediency. It is the realisation of God’s Will on earth as is laid down in the written principles of the Torah, to which the Sanctuary was built, and which is expressed in further detail in the sayings of the oral tradition, in the service of which the Law and its proceedings stand. And it is the same lawgiving Will of God which sanctions the declarations of the decisions of all the supreme courts gathered together in His Sanctuary as being solely authoritative for the practical realisation of His Torah. Carrying out these decisions corresponds to the Will of God and His Satisfaction with the practical arrangements of our conduct on earth, and every practical action against any such decision—even if the decision in itself were erroneous—would be acting against God’s expressed Will. This by no means places the highest tribunal above the possibility of error, or considers it in itself infallible. But it is the Will of God, our Lawgiver, that His Law is to be carried out according to its—the Sanhedrin’s—mandates. That is expressed definitely by ועשית על פי הדבר אשר יגידו לך מן המקום ההוא. The Sifri explains definitely on the previous verse לא תסור וגו׳ ימין ושמאל אפילו מראים בעיניך על שמאל שהוא ימין ועל ימין שהוא שמאל שמע להם.

V. 13. וכל העם ישמעו וגו׳. See on Ch. 13,12. At מסית it says ולא יספו לעשות עוד כדבר הרע הזה. Similarly at עדים זוממין (Ch. 19,20) ולא יספו לעשות עוד כדבר הרע הזה. But here at זקן ממרא and at בן סורר ומורה (Chapter 21,21) it does not say ולא יוסיפו לעשות וגו׳, but וכל ישראל ישמעו ויראו ולא יזידון עוד ,וכל העם ישמעו ויראו. For, as the ר״ן explains on Sanhedrin 89,a at these two cases, by giving the greatest possible publicity to the verdict and the execution, the intention is not to prevent a repetition of the same crime עשות דבר הרע הזה. After all there are only very seldom and very few opportunities amongst the people to commit these crimes actually. The real בן סורר ומורה crime is limited to the first three months after attaining puberty (see Ch. 21,18) (and other extremely improbable if not impossible conditions, see ibid I.L.), to commit the זקן ממרא crime, one must be just a זקן ,ראוי להוראה (a learned rabbi, qualified to give decisions I.L.). So the motive for giving the greatest publicity is not the prevention of the same crimes in these two cases, but by these frightening intimidating examples, to drive home in general the seriousness of educating our children, and childrens’ obedience to parents, and obedience to the traditional verbally-handed-down Torah and its teachers and exponents וכן ענין זקן ממרא הוא כדי שידעו כל העם כח הקבלה מתורתנו הקדושה וכל החולק עלית אפילו המופלא שבב״ד כיון שהרבים חולקים עליו יש לו לחזור בדבריו ולהורות כדבריהם כדי שלא ירבה מחלוקות בישראל והיינו דלא כתיב גבי זקן ולא יוסיפו לעשות כדבר הזה שאין החשש מפני זקנים אחרים שימרו אלא כתיב ולא יזידון עוד ד״ל שלא יבא שום אדם לחלוק על הקבלה האמיתית (ר״ן ibid).

Although the duty of unswerving obedience to the orders and prohibitions of the ב״ד הגדול is quite general, nevertheless the penalty of death only applies to a definite practical contradiction of their decisions; and the Gemora (Sanhedrin 87 and 88) is not quite decided on the question whether it is only acting contrary to their decision regarding a prohibition שזדונן כרת ושגגתן חטאת or at least something that could lead to such a כרת transgression which would entail the punishment of a זקן ממרא, or whether it is only necessary for it to be עד דאיכא תורה ויורוך concerning a prohibition שעיקרו מדברי תורה ופירושו מדברי סופרים, the principle of which is written in the Torah but its detailed laws have only been received through the oral tradition. Further, as the crime must be a sin of actual transgression, commission, and not of omission—it says אשר יעשה בזדון—this must be, as a rule, only the transgression of a prohibition, and the problem of a possitive command, a מצות עשה being omitted to be done by some actual commission being done is solved by the fact that that could only happen by an illegal addition, and then it would be a transgression of the prohibition לא תוסיף (see on Ch. 4,2), inasmuch as the capricious addition to the number of the prescribed parts of a mitzva forfeits the validity of the mitzva itself, ,דבר שעיקרו מדברי תורה ופירושו מדברי סופרים ויש בו להוסיף ואם הוסיף גורע as this is proved there by the mitzva of Tephillin, where, if a fifth בית were to be added to the four בתים prescribed by tradition the mitzva of laying Tephillin with it would be entirely invalid (also see רמב״ם and ראב״ד on ה׳ ממרים, 4 and ר״ן on Sanhedrin ibid.).

V. 14. כי תבא וגו׳. The tendency of the preceding law was to ensure the integrity of the fulfilment of the Torah against any failure of a Torah-authority to recognise his duty. To that is now added the further insurance of the Torah against the failure to recognise his duty on the part of a man invested with the full powers of royalty. Already in Levit. 4,22 et seq. the offering prescribed for the atonement of the sins of the נשיא presupposes the normal existence of a king in Israel, and out of the comparison of this offering with that prescribed for the sin-offerings of the High-priest and of the supreme court of justice we could see the position of the Jewish Kings being in accord with the laws laid down here (refer to it there). “When thou art come to the land which God thy God giveth thee and have taken it into possession and dwell therein”, these introductory words to the chapter on kings, say right from the beginning that the appointment of the Jewish king is not for conquering the land and not for safeguarding its possession, altogether not for developing forces to be used externally. It is God Who gives the land to Israel, God under Whose support and help it conquered the land, and under Whose protection it lives safely in it, as this support and assistance is assured again and again in the Torah and which was stressed by Moses again and again in his exhortations preparatory for the conquest of the land. For that, Israel required no king, for that Israel had only to be “Israel”, had only to prove itself the faithful dutiful People of God’s Torah, had only to win the moral victory over itself to be certain of victory over any external enemy force against it. Sifri expresses this with a pithy word of explanation on our verse: בזכותך :אשר ה׳ אלקיך נותן לך: God gives you the land, to win that, you require no king, only you, your real selves. And indeed the Gemora (Kiddushin 37,b) points out that the appointment of a king is only commanded to be made, after the complete conquest and settlement in the land, לאחר ירושה וישיבה, and there definitely refutes any idea of warlike prowess being the purpose of having a Jewish king (see ibid).

If then it does nevertheless say: ואמרת אשימה עלי מלך ככל הגוים אשר סביבתי, that, after complete conquest of the land and quiet possession of it, the requirement for a royal head of the nation would make itself felt, and the satisfying of this requirement would not only be allowed, but, according to the Gemora (Sanhedrin 20,a,) actually commanded to be done, accordingly that the command to appoint a king, the שום תשים עליך מלך, only waited for the notification of this requirement from the people. So that coming thus from the people having this feeling and desire the institution of a king becomes rightly estimated and is not regarded as a dictatorial institution to which the people have to forfeit their independence. Thus the requirement can have no other purpose than that of ensuring the one factor on which the continuance of God’s protection and blessing depends, viz; to make the nation of Israel “Israel”, to the faithful dutiful People of God’s Torah. The addition ככל הגוים אשר סביבתי would then, without any doubt have the following meaning:- Just as all the other nations only achieve the highest national well-being—which for them consists in developing the greatest possible power and strength against the outside world—by subordination under one unifying Head of State at whose disposal all the national forces are placed for this purpose, in the same way you will feel the requirement to have a Head of State to unite all your national forces for the well-being of your State—which well-being consists only in the most possible complete realisation internally of God’s Torah. A Head of State who will shine forth as an example as the first faithful dutiful Jew in the moral nobility of this faithfulness to duty; who will be filled with the spirit of your calling as Jews and win all minds and hearts over to this spirit; who will oppose with all the might of his word, his example, and the prestige and power of his position everything which is in opposition of this spirit, and at whose disposal you are to place all your forces for this champion fighting in the front rank for the internal protection of your national calling. How very much this should be the real calling of the Jewish king, how very much it should work against the danger of estrangement from the one united national calling which the decentralisation threatened is shown by the reports of the Jewish defection recorded in the historical parts of the bible, especially in those of the most striking of such incidents as פסל מיכה (the graven idol of Micha I.L. and פלגש בגבעה (the horrible incident of the Levite’s concubine in Gibeah and its terrible consequences I.L.) where the Scripture reports: בימים ההם אין מלך בישראל איש הישר בעיניו יעשה (Judges 17,6; XVIII,1; XIX,1 and XXI,28). (“In those days there was no king in Israel, each man doing that which seemed right in his own eyes”, I.L.).

In complete contrast to this original calling of the Jewish king was the motive out of which, and the purpose for which the first election of a king occurred under Samuel (Sam. I, VIII. The reproach in Samuel’s speech to the people כי נחש מלך בני עמון בא עליכם ותאמרו לי לא כי מלך ימלך עלינו וד׳ אלקיכם מלככם (“and when ye saw that Nachach the king of the Ammonites came against you, ye said unto me: Nay, but a king shall reign over us, but God, your God is your King”, ibid XII,12) leaves no doubt about it, that protection against external enemies, completely ignoring the protection of the land resting in God’s Hands and to be expected only from Him, was the motive and purpose of that election of a king. They wanted a king, not only similar in form, but also in the sense of all the other nations, as is quite clear also from the demand of the people (ibid VIII,20) ויאמרו לא כי אם מלך יהיה עלינו והיינו גם אנחנו ככל הגוים ושפטנו מלכנו ויצא לפנינו ונלחם את מלחמתנו (“and they said: Nay, but we will have a king over us, so that we also may be like all the nations, that our king may judge us and go out before us and fight our battles” I.L.) where the “he may judge us” explained by the following “and” lead us and fight etc.” quite definitely is not meant in the sense of internal procedures of justice, but represent our rights in external politics, in which sense also the men who stood up for the defence of the independence of the Jewish land and people (e.g. Jephtha etc. I.L.) are called “judges” שפט את .שופטים predominantly has the meaning of helping somebody to get their rights, thus שפטו דל ויתום (Ps. 132,3), שפטני ה׳ כצדקי (ibid VII,9), יתום לא ישפטו (Is. 1,23) כי שפטו ה׳ מכל אויביו (Sam. II, XVIII,18 & 31) and frequently elsewhere. The שימה לנו מלך לשפטנו ככל הגוים in the mouth of the זקני ישראל (Sam. I. 8,5) is accordingly probably also to be understood also in this sense, or perhaps the elders of the nation did in fact have in mind the management of internal arrangements of justice, but the people definitely wanted a king only for military protection against external enemies, as the Gemora in Sanhedrin 20,b, takes it:- זקנים שבדור כהוגן שאלו שנאמר תנה לנו מלך לשפטנו אבל עמי הארץ שבהן קילקלו שנאמר וחיינו גם אנחנו ככל הגוים ושפטנו מלכנו ויצא לפנינו.

For the permanently established dynasty described in our chapter here, indeed, the time had not at all yet arrived. The condition definitely fixed ירושה וישיבה was only very incompletely fulfilled. Not for the successfully accomplished work of conquest, not crowned with the military wreath of laurel was the first Jewish king to mount the throne of an hereditary dynasty. The nation itself, destined thereto, was to accomplish the work of conquest under God and under God only, in faithful obedience to Him, and divide the land when the conquest was complete under His guiding arrangements. From that the future Jewish king was not to be able to make any demands for acknowledging recognition, no homage to be paid to his might and military prowess. Only when the whole land had been conquered and divided up, and every one would thenceforth see himself on his own acres giving himself up to peaceful carrying out the lofty mission of a Jewish life, then, similarly to the symbolic unifying point in the מקדש, a concrete bearer of this national unity was to be established in a king. Both factors ירושה וישיבה were to come first, and only one blow was the king, appointed for the work of peace of the Jewish nation, to strike, the last before the building of the מקדש, the battle against Amalek (Sanhedrin 20,b) after which the ideal Jewish king was to let his sword rest for ever in its sheath.
This ideal was not realised. It still belongs, as does the whole of God’s Law to the future.

The Sifri significantly explains our text אשר ה׳ אלקיך נותן לך בזכותך בשכר שתירש תשב :וירשתה וישבתה בה. You obtain the land from God solely through moral deserts, and you procure permanent secured settlement in the land only through complete fulfilment of the commands given you for the conquest. Neither occured. The conquest remained uncompleted, and all too soon the tribes allowed themselves to be led away by the allurements of the settlement, a large number of the inhabitants lived next to them in the land with their polytheistic views and morals and customs, and quickly the people let themselves be led astray to fall into these enticing indulgences. So that the moment of the election of a king under Samuel was in truth still premature. The work of bringing the people back to obedience to God, begun by Samuel should first have been completed, and thereby have obtained the support of God for the conquest of the whole of the land which was still to be accomplished. Instead of which the people imagined they could dispense with both, and their moral betterment, as well as the support of God could, like all the surrounding nations, be substituted by an hereditary military sovereign, and therein lay the sin. That, we think, would then also be the sense of the words of R. Yehuda in the Sifri:- והלא מצוה מן התורה לשאול להם מלך שנאמר שום תשים עליך מלך אשר יבחר ד׳ אלהיך בו ולמה נענשו בימי שמואל לפי שהקדימו על ידם The fault lay in making the election before the proper time. They demanded a king in a time when what was demanded was first the secure establishing the possession of the land and accordingly were demanding it “too early” in their imagined material interest

על ידם (על ידם, like על ידי עצמו ע״י בנו ובתו הגדולים etc. (B.M. 93,a); השוקל ע״י כהן וכו׳ ע״י עני וכו׳ (Shekalim 1,6 & 7) et alia. The בכל הגוים אשר סביבותי which the commentators on Sifri read upwards as belonging up to על ידם clearly belongs below and introduces a fresh explanatory sentence. It is also missing in the תוספתא on Sanhedrin (Ch. VI) where this saying of R. Yehuda is brought, and in the edition of the Sifri with the הגהות הגר״א, the punctuation is also in accordance with the way we have taken it.

If now, Sam. I, VIII,11 et seq. describes the משפט המלך, the rights of kings as being an absolute power over the persons and possessions of the people, and although quite clearly this description was given with the intention of frightening the people off from the election of such a king, which is made perfectly clear from the wording of the report of the failure of this description: וימאנו העם וגו׳ ויאמרו לא כי וגו׳ והיינו וגו׳ (ibid 19 & 20) (“Nevertheless the people refused to listen to the voice of Samuel, and they said: Nay but we will have a king over us. etc.” I.L.), nevertheless according to the opinion which is accepted as Halacha (Sanhedrin 20,b) all the absolute powers described there are taken to be the actual plentitude of power which accrue to an elected king כל האמור בפרשת מלך מלך מותר בו; and all that is said in Samuel’s warning speech thenceforth become the legal prerogatives of Jewish kings. That such an election of a king was not in the original sense of the Torah, that the demand was only given into, for the purpose of educating the nation, so that they, who saw their salvation therein, might learn by bitter experience the futility of such expectations, is expressed in bitter solemnity by the Prophet Hosea in 13,9-11:- שחתך ישראל כי בי בעזרך׳ אהי מלכך אפוא ויושעך בכל עריך ושפטיך אשר אמרת תנה לי מלך ושרים, אתן לך מלך באפי ואקח בעברתי “O Israel, thou hast destroyed thyself but in Me was thine help. Where then is thy king now, where, that he may help thee in all thy cities! And thy judges of whom thou saidst: Give me a king and princes! I gave thee a king in My Displeasure and took him away in My Wrath”.

Among the kings elected through this act of the people, there was one who, besides his military proficiency in protecting the people and the land, at the same time was so filled with the spiritual ideal of a Jewish king “after the heart of God”, that, like no other before or after him, so sang the whole rich store of human and national relations to God in such inspired and inspiring words of feelings and thoughts, that with his psalms he has become the real creator and bearer of the spiritual thoughts of the Jewish people. Still to-day, and far beyond Jewish circles, directly or indirectly, every soul that seeks the knowledge of God and help from God, is elevated up to God by the uplift of his words. This king, David the son of Jesse, in whom the dual phases of Jewish royalty, the sword and the lyre, the bearer of the spiritual capacity of the nation internally, besides the victorious defence of it externally, appeared to such an eminent degree that one of the national singers (איתן האזרחי I.L.) inspired by his spirit, in plain words called him a מציאה, a “find” which God found for the service of His work (Ps. 139,21); מצאתי דוד עבדי, This king, God dedicated to be the royal root of a line of descendants reaching until the ultimate future, which, together with the complete realisation of God’s Torah will bring the realisation of a pure Torah-king in Israel. And the man of this Jewish future, the future one who will bring about this realisation, upon whom the spirit of God will rest, the spirit of wisdom and perception, the spirit of counsel and strength, the spirit of understanding and fear of God, whose word will form itself into a world-directing sceptre before the spirit of which all lawlessness will die away, who will bring Right and Truth to reign to such a degree that the “wolf” will lie peacefully down beside the “lamb”, and the “tiger” next to the “kid”, that on the earth striving upward to the Mount of the Sanctuary of God, no evil, no immorality will any longer be practiced because the whole world will be filled with the understanding of God, even as the water covereth the bed of the ocean—this noblest realisation of a Jewish Torah-king will still be a sprout from the stem of Jesse which had apparently been cut down long ago, and a long awaited twig from his root so long hidden by night (Is. XI).

But, as the martial phase of his kingship witheld David from being considered worthy to build the Sanctuary of His Torah to God (Chron. I. 22,8) and this was left for his son to whom he had bequeathed the peace he had victoriously fought for, this phase of “kingship” after the manner of the other nations” grew rampantly in his son even over into the peace, and שלמה the Prince of Peace (as his name indicated I.L.) the intellectually great son of David who, with his wisdom, enlightened his people and attracted people from afar to wonder at, did not set his ideal in the spiritual and moral elevation and perfecting of his people, but in the imitation of the arts of peace of the “kings of the manner of other nations” whose daughters he wooed, and with whom he competed in splendour and luxury, and inasmuch as he broke the three laws laid down here for the conduct of Jewish kings and sought to possess “many chargers, many wives and many treasures” he himself laid the foundation for the ruin of the Sanctuary he had built to the Torah of God. “On the day” says an old tradition, that Solomon led the daughter of Pharaoh home, Gabriel, the “messenger of the Power of God” came down and planted a staff in the sea, on which a sandbank settled, on which the great city of Rome was built”. (Sanhedrin 21,b, according to the version of the ילקוט).

V. 15. שום תשום וגו׳. This is a positive command, not merely permission. (see v. 14). על פי נביא :אשר יבחר ה׳ אלקיך בו (Sifri), the man whom God will designate through a prophet as being the man of His choice, him shalt thou set as king above you, shalt invest him with the rights of a king and subordinate yourselves under him as your king. If nevertheless it says further מקרב אחיך וגו׳ ,לא תוכל לתת עליך וגו׳ and thereby makes conditions which the nation has to keep in electing a king, this clearly declares the possibility that a king could be elected, not directly by God’s appointing him through a prophet but by the free choice of the nation or by its representatives not guided by a prophet. When we consider that according to Jewish principles (see on Ch. 18,18) the man whom God chooses to be a prophet to be the organ of His Word to the nation must have first shown himself to be worthy of prophecy as a “man” by a high degree of mental and moral perfection, but that in addition, according to Sanhedrin 11,a, not only the personality of the person himself but also the contemporary age must also be considered worthy of being fitting to receive such a prophetic mission דורו זכאי לכך, then we can very well understand the necessity for both alternatives to be foreseen in the Torah. Normally שום תשים עליך מלך אשר יבחר ה׳ אלקיך בו, but when the intervention of a prophet is lacking then: מקרב אחיך גו׳.
אמו מישראל :מקרב אחיך, he must be born a Jew (Yebamoth 45,b, see תוספות there. According to תוספות Sota 41,b the father must also have been a Jew).

V. 16. רק לא ירבה לו וגו׳. The רק limits the capacity of שום תשים whereby the nation is commanded to grant the king considerable powers over them, שתהא אימתו עליך. To that then comes רק and imposes on the king the duty of himself limiting these powers, and primarily with regards to just those factors which, according to the experience of all ages have been the rocks on which the virtue of rulers has come to grief and the happiness of their people shattered. These are:- the passion for military glory and renown, women and possessions.

לא ירבה לו סוסים. The horse was the real war-animal, so that in the reports of battles we find cavalry—horses and riders—mentioned in the foreground. To be ready for war, in the first place a large number of horses were necessary (cf. Deut. 20,1; Pharaoh’s army, Ex. XIV; Joshua 11,4; Judges 5,22; Kings I. 22,4; Kings II, VII,6; Jer. 51,27; Ezek. 39,20 and frequently elsewhere. Hence also Prov. 21,31, Ps 39,17 and CXLVII,10 etc. etc.) Keeping a large number of horses and an unlimited increase of them is accordingly synonymous with keeping a large military force.

ולא ישיב העם מצרימה וגו׳ וה׳ אמר לכם וגו׳. If this simply meant to forbid a return to Egypt it would probably just have said וה׳ אמר לכם לא לשוב בדרך הזה עוד ;תשובו clearly lays stress on the manner or way of the return. It says in XXVIII,68 also: והשיבך וגו׳ בדרך אשר אמרתי לך, and we can at once say that in that place דרך cannot possibly mean the actual way by which they went from Egypt to Palestine, as it speaks of a return to Egypt by ship. Further, לא תוסיפון לשוב וגו׳ (“you shall not again go back etc.” I.L.) does not say simply “you shall not go back” but presupposes that they had previously gone to Egypt repeatedly, and does not refer to their present exodus out of Egypt, but to these earlier journeys to Egypt: לא תוסיפון לשוב וגו׳, “you repeatedly went to Egypt, that you are not to do any more”. For in fact Egypt had been a land of refuge from Palestine from the earliest times of Jewish history. Abraham went to Egypt because there was famine in Palestine (Gen. 12,10). For the same reason Isaac was about to go there and was only restrained by direct instructions from God (ibid XXVI,2). Israel’s whole settlement in Egypt was only brought about by the famine in Palestine which made the sons of Jacob go repeatedly to Egypt to buy food. So that the natural fertility of the Egyptian soil gave Egypt an ascendant superiority over other countries and that made other countries, especiallly Palestine appear dependent on them.

Accordingly לא תוסיפון לשוב בדרך הזה עוד would say:- you shall not go from Palestine to Egypt as in the past to obtain from there any national necessities which your own land does not supply. You are not to make yourselves dependent on Egypt. A Jewish king who makes it his pride to keep a large standing army commits a double sin. Firstly directly: his calling lies in quite a different direction. And then indirectly: he makes himself and his people dependent on Egypt. It is only from there that he can obtain horses for his mounted troops. If Egypt refuses to export horses for him, he is beaten. He must always keep on friendly terms and keep up a lively traffic with Egypt and with the import of horses, and with the import of horses the Egyptian outlook on state management and the general Egyptian outlook on life also filter into the land. In the description of the unspeakable horrors and wretchedness which await the Nation if it becomes unfaithful to its mission in the land of that mission, Ch. 28,68, at the end of the whole terrible picture, accordingly as the final stage and depth of forsakenness and misery describes: והשיבך ה׳ מצרים באניות בדרך אשר אמרתי לך לא תוסיף לראתה והתמכרתם שם לאיביך לעבדים ולשפחות ואין קונה, that as a last resource to keep themselves alive God will make them go back to Egypt in ships in the way He had said they would never again have to see it, there to offer to sell themselves as male and female slaves whom nobody would buy! Whereas they were to have lived in satisfied independence in their own land and should never have had to seek to satisfy any national requirement in Egypt, their land would cease to bear them, and they would find themselves in such wretched circumstances that the condition of slavery out of which God had freed them would appear as a desirable end, and after centuries they would offer themselves as slaves to their old masters and would be disdained by them!

With the way we have taken this prohibition viz: that primarily only going to Egypt which would show or effect a dependence and subordination of Palestine on and to Egypt would be forbidden, the ירושלמי quoted by הגהות מימוניות on הל׳ מלכים v. 7 would be in complete agreement. According to it, ordinary business traffic with Egypt לסחורה ולפרגמטיא, and also for purposes of conquest, would not be prohibited, but only a return to peaceful settlement there, לישיבה is prohibited, and moreover according to ר׳ אליעזר ממיץ only just out of Palestine but not from elsewhere. As long as the Jewish State existed in Palestine, an emigration from there to Egypt would be just the most positive repetition of the earlier immigrations there which is forbidden here. That is why the settlement of Jews in Alexandria at the time of the second Temple was a clear transgression of this prohibition (Sukka 51,b). With the downfall of the Jewish State a return of Jewish exiles to Egypt would not be prohibited, as in fact, for centuries many Jewish communities have settled in Egypt.

וה׳ אמר לכם (“and God had said to you” I.L.) the prohibition had already been transmitted to the people by Moses, and its being fixed in the written script was only reserved for the opportunity offered by these laws for the king. The כי אשר ראיתם את מצרים היום לא תספו לראתם עוד עד עולם of Ex. 14,13 appears by the way it is taken and by the context to be a promise and not a prohibition.

V. 17. ולא ירבה וגו׳. It does not say ולא יסורו, or ולא תסירנה לבבו (so that they will not turn his heart away I.L.) but ולא יסור לבבו (so that he does not turn his heart away I.L.). Even without any direct corrupting influence, his heart will become estranged from the spiritually high seriousness of the life of duty of a king.

וכסף וזהב לא ירבה לו מאוד, whereas at סוסים and נשים it simply says לא ירבה לו (he shall not have many horses or wives I.L.) at כסף וזהב (gold and silver) is says מאוד (he shall not have a great deal I.L.). For in fact a king does require more means than an ordinary person both for carrying out his duties in the nation and also to ensure the independence of his position. Even for the High Priest already, the order is given גדלהו משל אחיו (Levit. p. 598); if he is not a man of means, his colleagues, the priests at whose head he is to be placed have to see to it that he is provided with wealth to render him financially independent. The activities of a king to further the spiritual and material well-being of his people very much requires him to have considerable means at his disposal. Accordingly it does not say לא ירבה לו but לא ירבה לו מאוד, he shall not gather gold and silver more than is necessary, shall guard himself against passion for riches. Of all the possible passions of a ruler “avarice” is the most pernicious, and at the same time one that can never be satisfied. אוהב כסף לא ישבע כסף. Hence at the two preceding prohibitions, their bad consequences ולא יסור ,ולא ישיב is given as the reason, but the gathering of riches is simply absolutely forbidden. It is just evil in itself.

V. 18. והיה כשבתו וגו׳. At once, as soon as he has ascended the throne, his first act is to be וכתב לו וגו׳, that with his own hand he writes a copy of the Torah. With this act he acknowledges that, in the very first place the Torah is given for him, that he is not above the Law, but rather that it is to be the unalterable rule of conduct for his life, the realisation of which in the nation is to be the sum of his mission as king, and that in conscientious faithfulness to the Torah and in ready self-sacrificing devotion to the tasks dictated by the Torah he will stand as an example before the people as the “first and foremost son of the Torah”.

את משנה התורה הזאת: a double copy of the Torah, like ומשנה כסף (Gen. 43,15) משנה שכר שכיר (Deut. 15,18). According to Sanhedrin 21,b, one copy to be deposited on his book-shelves to be at the same time a permanent witness for and against him, and the other to accompany him constantly wherever he goes.

מלפני הכהנים הלוים (see on V.9). Copied from the scroll which was kept in the Temple in the care of the priests and the Sanhedrin, the ספר עזרה. Thus Sanhedrin Jerusalmi 2,4: ומגיהין אותו מספר עזרה ע״פ ב״ד של ע״א (see Ch. 31,9).

V. 19. את כל דברי התורה הזאת is not merely the laws contained in the Torah, they are summarised in the following ואת החוקים האלה, but is rather the whole historical and instructive contents out of which the Jewish king has to bring to his mind in ever increasing clarity and understanding the historical position and destiny of the nation as well as the conditions and relationship of the individual lives of the nation relative to it, so that he can be active in bringing about their ever increasingly realisation. ואת החקים האלה. Significantly enough all the dictates of the Torah are presented to the king as חקים, as given inviolable norms within which even the king’s authority and arbitrary actions find their limitations, just as in the following verse his position towards all classes of his people, whom he is to regard not as subjects but as Brethren, is given to him to take to heart as מצוה as “being appointed to his post” by a Higher Being, Whose first servitor he is to be.
הוא ובניו בקרב ישראל. See Levit. 15,32.

V. 1. In the preceding chapters the position of the authorities of the law and the king in the nation is discussed. To that now the Torah adds the position of the priests in the nation. That they, like the whole tribe of Levi, are to have no portion in possessions that accrue to the nation as such, no participation in the land and spoils of war, has already repeatedly been said, equally so that ה׳ הוא נחלתו, that their whole life is to be directed to their activities for God and the Sanctuary of His Torah. In the same way the מתנות כהונה have already been discussed in Levit. Ch. XXII, and Numb. XVIII, the gifts to the priests which they are to receive as representatives and ministers of this Sanctuary of the Torah. But all these, as בשר חטאת ואשם ,ביכורים ,תרומה ,חלה ,בכור ,חרם ,חזה ושוק are gifts which present themselves as dedicated directly to God and His Sanctuary but which are indirectly transferred to them by God as the servitors of His Sanctuary, they are קדשים, holy objects of higher and lower degrees, which are looked at in the wider sense of כהנים משולחן גבוה קזכו, that they are given to be eaten by the priests “from the table of the One Above”.

But with the entry into the Land a decentralising distance of the people’s homes from the Sanctuary took place which had a prominent result in היתר בשר תאוה the permission to eat ordinary meat which did not come from offerings (Ch. 12,20 et seq.). This prospective change had also important results for the priests. During the time of the wanderings in the wilderness they formed the narrow circle round about the Sanctuary and that was where they stayed, but now they were to follow the people in the decentralising distance from the Sanctuary where they settled, and thereby only then really enter on the second phase of their priestly activity viz. to represent the Torah and its teachings in the midst of the lives of the people. The Torah presupposes that only a part of the priests would be on duty to function in the Sanctuary at the centre, but the other would live scattered in the land amongst the people and only from time to time would come up for service in the Sanctuary (see verses 6-8). This activity on their part in the midst of the lives of the people was really an outcome from their Levite calling, they were the elite of the Levites (cf. Levit. p. 620-1) so that altogether when this aspect of their calling is discussed they are called הכהנים הלוים or at special reference to these circumstances (verses 6-8) just הלוי.

Out of this position of theirs in the midst of the lives of the people, they are now granted a portion directly from the “table of the people” as משפט הכהנים as a right of priests: viz זרוע לחײם וקיבה, gifts which are generally understood under the legal term “מתנות״, and which are not to be considered as coming through the agency of the Sanctuary, but as a gift coming direct “from the people to the priest”. The animal from which these parts come to the priest is חולין (not holy I.L.) is בשר תאוה (ordinary meat I.L.) is just that meat which only started with the decentralisation of the people, and these מתנות are accordingly the gifts to the priests which are characteristic of the decentralisation and of the position of the priests living in the midst of the people among their homes at a distance away from the Sanctuary. To this life of the people the priests are to be כהנים in the most concrete literal meaning of the word. By their teaching and the influence of their example they are to point the “direction” (כון) to the Torah and secure its aims and ways being kept. To themselves and to them, the people express this calling of their priests in their midst admonishingly by just these parts of their animal food, inasmuch as they thereby symbolically hand over their acts (זרוע = the arm I.L.), their words (לחײם = the jaw-bone and tongue I.L.) and its enjoyment of good and material pleasures (קיבה = the stomach I.L.) to the priest, and at the same time provide for the priest’s table.

And just as with these gifts from their own table the people have to provide for the priest’s table, so with ראשית הגז with the gift of the first shearing of the fleece, the admonishment is given to the people that it is up to them to see that their priests get the wherewithal to dress respectably so that their outward appearance should not be prejudicial or detrimental in any way to the influence they are to exert among the people.
From all this it is perfectly clear why the laws regarding the מתנות and ראשית הגז were only laid down in writing in this compendium for the entry into the land. Their importance only began then.

Moreover these מתנות כהונה like all the prescribed gifts to the priests are solely a general duty to be given to the priesthood in general. No individual priest has any right to claim any of them for himself. The person who is in duty bound to make the gift can give it to any particular priest he likes, he has only to be guided by the worthiness of the recipient shown by his general way of life. טובת הנאה לבעלים (Numb. 5,10). מנת הכהנים והלוים למען יחזקו בתורת ה׳ (Chron. II, XXXI,4) (“he commanded… to give the portions to the priests and Levites so that they might give themselves up to be the support of God’s Torah” I.L.) המחזיק בתורת ה׳ יש לו מנת וכל שאינו מחזיק בתורת ה׳ אין לו מנת. כל כהן שאינו מודה בעבודה אין לו חלק בכהונה (Chulin 130,b there תוספות, Chulin 132,a, see Levit. 7,33).

כל שבט לוי is more in parenthesis: as the whole Levitical tribe; for the laws which this verse introduces apply to the priests only. — חלק in the spoils of war, בזה (Sifri). ונחלה in the land which is to be divided between the tribes. אשי ה׳, these are the parts of the offerings which are given to the priests: קדשי הגבול :ונחלתו .קדשי המקדש, the things which are really directed to God and thereby become holy things, קדשים, although given outside the Sanctuary like חלה ,תרומה etc. (Sifri).

V. 3. וזה יהיה משפט וגו׳, we have already remarked that this is only the right of the priesthood as a whole but no individual priest has any legal claim to it, אין להוציאן בדײנין. These gifts are ממון שאין לו תובעין, property to which there are no legal claimants (Chulin ibid.). — הכהנים including a כהנת, a daughter of a priest married to a non-priest still retains her right to have these gifts (ibid 131,b; cf. כהנת ולויה at בכור, Numb. p. 39). מאת העם .מאת העם מאת זובחי זבח: whether Levites are also to be understood to be included is doubtful (ibid, 131,a). הדין עם הטבח :מאת זובחי זבח the moral duty is on the שוחט, on the one who actually slaughters the offering, to see that these parts are separated from the offering and given to a priest (ibid 132,b). פרט לטרפה :זבח, the animal must be found fit for a זבח, a meal. The duty to make these gifts does not apply to an animal that is found to be טרפה.

אם שור אם שה, excluding a חיה. הזרוע, the two upper joints of the forelegs, corresponding to the human arms, hence the term זרוע: arms instead of feet.—לחי ,הלחײם from לחה, related to לאה ,להה in Aramic לעה, to work strenuously, to tire oneself (cf. יגע) the mandible by means of which one chews and speaks, the two sides of the lower jaw together with the tongue.—הקבה (from קוב related to יקב (like טוב and יטב) the wine press: the fourth stomach of ruminants the rennet, in which the food reduced to a thin pap completes its digestion.
V. 4. ראשית דגנך וגו׳, the תרומה, also בכורים and חלה which are all called ראשית.

מן התורה :וראשית גז צאנך it, like תרומה has no שיעור and the duty can be fulfilled with a minimum quantity (ibid 137b). So that ראשית הגז seems to be, like תרומה גדולה, just a symbol given from the “harvest of clothing-material” (wool) as an acknowledgment that even if the priesthood is not productive of material goods for the people’s lives, the people are nevertheless under an obligation to it for its faithful activity and influence, and at the same time an admonition for due regard to be had for making provision for the external civil appearance of the priests in the ordinary life of the people.

V. 5. כי בו בחר וגו׳ refers to the whole special position of the priesthood and the prerogatives granted to it therefrom.—לעמד לשרת, similarly in V. 7: העמדים שם לפני ה׳ only standing, in the position of awaiting the orders of a superior and carrying them out, does he bear the character of having been chosen for service, לעמידה בחרתיו ולא לישיבה, no עבודה may he do in a sitting position, in the position of being gathered together about himself. Any procedure of the offerings performed while sitting down would be פסול, invalid, as if it had been done by a non-priest (Zebachim 23,b). Only in a standing position is the idea expressed that all that he is doing is בשם ה׳, done by command of God.
