כל הימים. His election extends beyond the existence of the Temple, and the priestly function which he still has to do after the destruction of the Temple, נשיאת כפים (pronouncing the blessing at public services I.L.) may also only be done standing (Sota 38,a; see Ch. 10,8).
V. 6. וכי יבא הלוי, this refers to a priest who lives amongst the people at a distance from the Temple (see on V.1.).

כל ישראל :מכל ישראל never means the whole Jewish land, and here, all the more it cannot have that meaning as the place wherever it may be outside the city of the Temple has already been designated, as always, as כל ישראל .אחד שעריך, accordingly here, as always, means “all Israel” the whole nation. A priest living in some city in the land comes forward out of the whole nation to perform the priestly functions in the Temple. That means, he came with the whole nation to Jerusalem and now he wishes to practice in their presence the functions of the office to which he has been appointed out of their midst. This would be at the time of the three pilgrim-festivals, ג׳ רגלים. The Gemora in Sukka 55,b, attaches to the words of our sentence: מאחד שעריך לא אמרתי אלא בשעה שכל ישראל נכנסין בשער אחד. We take this to mean that here also, as is so frequent, words are referred to words that follow, that the words כל שער have an eye on the words מכל ישראל that follow, inasmuch as by the presence of כל ישראל any idea of particularism is removed. On רגלים all the nation כל ישראל has only one שער (one city, Rashi ibid I.L.) and every שער belongs to כל ישראל, and all, from whatever שער they come, come as כל ישראל, as forming the united nation.

V. 7 & 8. ושרת וגו׳. In this, as in the following verse a priest coming up to Jerusalem from the country is given equal rights in the service in the Temple (שרת) and in the resulting parts of the offerings that accrue to him (אכילה) with the priests who are on duty there at the time, העומדים שם לפני ה׳, “with the exception of that which will have been arranged between the heads of the families” לבד ממכריו על האבות. For the Torah presupposes that in the course of time when the number of priests will have increased, all of them will not be able to function at the service in the Temple at the same time: So that by mutual agreement between the various families of the priests that a rota be established by which certain numbers go on duty for service in the Temple for a fixed period at the end of which others take their place. The arrangement of such a rota is called ממכר (barter I.L.) because, of the whole body of those entitled to participate in the service, a section surrenders its rights on the understanding that the other will do likewise for them when it comes to their turn, and so on until all will have come to function in the Temple. This is accordingly an arrangement which rests on reciprocal exchange מכר. The Sifri puts it concisely: לבד ממכריו על האבות מה מכרו האבות זה לזה אני בשבתי ואתה בשבתך. And it was assumed that this splitting up into groups (משמר) would be made according to families, whose belonging together rested on common ancestry אבות. Just as the systematic division of the nation, and within the nation, the tribe of Levi had to be made according to בתי אבות (cf. Numb. p.3) in the same way the tribe of the Aaronites would have to split up into family groups.

And in fact Moses already arranged eight such משמרות, four from Eleazar and four from Ithamar which then, in the course of time, were brought up to twenty four under Samuel and David (Taanith 27,a). Each משמר served for one week, and the change of the משמרות took place on Sabbath after the conclusion of the עבודת שחרית. Both משמרות, the incoming and outgoing, participated equally in the weekly distribution of the shewbread which took place each Sabbath (Levit. 24,8; Sukkah 56,a). The departing group greeted their incoming brethren with the blessing “May He Whose Name rests on this house cause love and brotherliness, peace and friendship to rest between you” מי ששכן את שמו בבית הזה הוא ישכין ביניכם אהבה ואחוה ושלום ורעות.

Now verses 6 and 7 here say:- If a priest on a רגל comes up to the City of the Temple with all Israel, or at any other time of the year that he pleases, then he can function in the Temple regardless of the section of his brethren who are authorised to perform the services that week, but, in the first case, on a רגל only at the festival-offerings which have to be brought by reason of that festival, and in the second case only at his own personal offerings either free-will or duty-bound ones. And with the right to perform the offering goes the right to have the parts of it that are to be eaten by the priests (see on Levit. 16,19), so that if nevertheless it says in v. 8 specially חלק כחלק יאכלו this can only refer to the distribution of such holy things that come to be eaten with which no further עבודה is to be done, and that is the shewbread, at the distribution of which on the festival Sabbath also every priest who is present participated, although no further עבודה took place with it. בג׳ פרקים בשנה היו כל המשמרות שוות באמורי הרגלים ובחלוק לחם הפנים—(מה שאמור ברגלים)— (Sukka 55,b). But regarding all other offerings the rota arrangement ממכריו על האבות held sway and even on רגל only the משמר of the week had the right to function and to the .אכילה משמר שזמנו קבוע הוא מקריב תמידין נדרים ונדבות ושאר קרבנות ציבור מקריב את הכל (שם) מנין לכהן שבא ומקריב קרבנותיו בכל עת ובכל שעה שירצה ת״ל ובא בכל אות נפשו ושרת (בבא קמא ק״ט ע״ב).

V. 9. כי אתה וגו׳. Judges, kings, priests, these were the officials standing in the service of the nation whose position and mission were reviewed in the preceding chapters and whose powers were definitely circumscribed within the prescribed limits. With these three the State-machinery which the Torah requires for its realisation is really completed. Now there still follows the position of the prophet to this whole organisation. This begins with a negative statement, with prohibition of functionaries whom the heathen nations considered indispensable, but for whom Jewish circles were to have neither room nor necessity, and whom the Jewish State may not tolerate, these are the functionaries of alleged divination.

The introductory words are a reminder that ה׳ אלקיך, that it is God as the sole Lord of our fate and Guide of our actions Who gives us the land, that basis of all our national progressive well-being, and that He grants it לך, as the Sifri repeatedly explains, בזכותך, exclusively by merit of the moral worth that you have, or are expected to develop. Then thereby everything that need be said for what follows, is said viz:- All that is necessary for acquiring and keeping any and every happiness you have in yourselves, it lies in your own hands.

לעשות אי אתה למד אבל אתה למד להבין ולהורות :לא תלמד לעשות. For the purpose of copying them it is prohibited to study the heathen abominations, but to obtain a theoretical knowledge of them to be able to understand and properly value the nullity of their pretentions and the moral dangers that lie at their base is not only permitted, but, in certain circumstances—e.g. for the members of the Sanhedrin for the purpose of their being able to give a correct judgment and verdict in cases which come before them—even essential (Sanhedrin 68,a Sabbat 75,a; Rashi there, and Menachoth 65,a. תוס׳ ד״ה בעלי כשפים).
כתועבת הגוים, everything which is called תועבה is not only repulsive to the mind but is something morally abominable.

V. 10 & 11. להזהיר ב״ד על כך :לא ימצא בך (Sifri). It is the special duty of the state and its representatives (the Sanhedrin and the courts of justice I.L.) not to tolerate these forbidden practices of heathen magic and divination, most of which have already been forbidden in Levit. 18,21; XIX,26; XX, 2-7, 27. Concerning מעביר בנו ובתו באש, מעונן, מנחש שואל אוב וידעוני see the places in Levit; on מכשף see Ex. 22,17.

קסם קסמים. In Ezekiel 21,26 it describes the King of Babylon being undecided whether to proceed against the Ammonites in their capital Raba, or against Judah in their capital Jerusalem and making the decision dependent on omens. Then it goes on to say: כי עמד מלך בבל על אם הדרך בראש שני דרכים לקסם קסם קלקל בחצים שאל בתרפים ראה בכבד He halted his army at the point at which the road divided into the two directions לקסם קסם (to seek omens I.L.). He arranged for the omens to be sought in three ways, by shooting arrows in the air, by enquiring of the teraphim and by killing a cock and examining the liver. According to that קסם seems to be the general idea of divination which was practised in various ways. Hence then the result is simply designated by קסם. It says, whichever way he looked for a decision בימינו הקסם ירושלים, Jerusalem was always to the right of the קסם and the campaign was accordingly decided to go against Jerusalem. In Joshua 13,22 Bileam is also called הקוסם. We have therefore translated it as “soothsayer”. We have already remarked on its phonetic relation to יזם and גזם according to which it would designate the claim to a superhuman amount of knowledge and ability. Just as כשוף is כזב so is :קסם גוזמא.

חבר חבר. Psalm 58,5 and 6 speaks of a furious serpent and a deaf adder who refused to obey the חובר חברים מחוכם the snake-charmer’s voice. In Isaiah 47,9 and 12 it is stressed at the fall of Babylon that all its Chaldean science which it had so assiduously cultivated had not sufficed, that in particular חבריך ורב כשפיך ,רב כשפיך עצמת חבריך (“the abundance of thy sorceries, the great strength of thy enchantments” I.L.) could not bring about salvation from the fall, his חוברים who even were bold enough to wish to be הוברי שמים and whose absurd pretentions are expressed—as we believe—by the change (in v.13) of the ח to the weaker ה. From both these places it seems to us to be perfectly clear that the pretentions of the חובר חבר boast not so much to some higher knowledge but to higher abilities, to make the will of a snake subject to his will, by secret methods to master the powers which threaten the continuance of a state, to be able to exercise a magic ban on whatever he likes, that is what the חובר חבר professes and pretends to be able to do. The Gemora in Sanhedrin 65a, also takes חובר חבר in a similar way. One can also consider the חבר in the Kal is used with the meaning of joining oneself with somebody—כל אלה חברו (Gen. 14,4) and if חבר means to force somebody or something to be in connection with something it should have the form of the Piel חבר. Perhaps then חבר designates that which in the terms of hypnotists is called putting oneself “en rapport” with someone. The magician puts himself in such close connection with another living creature that his will takes the place of the will of the other one and he guides the mind and muscles of the latter as he wishes. He knows how to put himself in connection with the other, hence חובר חבר.

ודרש אל המתים. The form — דרש אל as it occurs here and also in Is. 8,18 and XIX,3 could designate a procedure in which the question is not directly put to the one from whom the answer is expected which would be termed: דרש את-. The דורש אל מתים professes to put a question to some person or thing which reaches a certain person who has died who answers it through the medium (a person, a slate etc. I.L.). The whole process of spiritualism as practised to-day is nothing but such דרישה אל המתים.

V. 12. כי תועבת וגו׳ ובגלל התועבת וגו׳. What moral errors lie in these heathen practices and what moral depravity ensues from them we have already explained on the verses in Levit. and Ex. referred to above. As soon as a man gives himself up to, and believes his fate and his active life with his hopes and fears and decisions to be placed in the realm of dark, unfree, mysterious powers begotten by illusion, for which the moral worth or worthlessness of what he does has no effect, he immediately throws the scales which weigh his moral worth out of His Hands Whose conclusions alone should be decisive to him for what he does, for his fears and his hopes, and he makes himself subject to a lack of freedom of will which becomes the grave of all morality. The whole moral degeneration of the Canaanite nations came from these things, which supported and were the mainstay of immorality.

V. 13. תמים תהי׳ וגו׳. We have already worked out in Levit. p. 12 et seq. and p. 606 et seq. at the demand for the symbolic תמים-character for offerings and those who carry out the procedures of the offerings, the demand for the completeness of our devotion, the devoting of every phase, without exception, of our being to God as the most direct result of our consciousness of the “Oneness” of God, as being the realisation of the עם סגולה mission, the mission of a nation belonging exclusively, in every phase, to God. We are not to cut the slightest particle of any phase of our life away from God, we are to be with God with our complete life, with every fibre of it. Thereby the whole of the heathen attitude to life pictured in the preceding verses is banned from the Jewish sphere. God, the sole Director of our fate and Guide for our deeds, it is He alone Who decides our future, and Whose satisfaction is the sole criterion by which we are to decide what to do and what to refrain from doing. Not blind chance, the Moloch “luck”, rules over our lives or the lives of our children, not the dead, not the magicians wand, not a black cat etc. etc. know what is before us, not morbid or extatic frenzy etc. have to declare the oracle for what we are to do or refrain from doing, or the weight of a grain of dust on the scales to decide for or against what our future is to be. Only from God would we have to ask “to have our fortune told” if indeed a תמים would require to know what his future was to be, and only from God would we have to enquire for a declaration of what we should do or refrain from doing, if God had not long ago told us what to do and what not to do in His Torah. And in fact the תמים is so completely engrossed in God that he lives entirely in the thought of doing his duty all the time and leaves the result with his whole future to God. By fulfilling his duty, his doing and not doing, has for him already reached its highest goal, he has paid His God the tribute of duty faithfully fulfilled, for everything beyond that he is—as the phonetic relation of דמם and טמם teaches—quiet and impervious.

The positive demand תמים תהי׳ וגו׳ accordingly goes farther than the negative command of the previous verses prohibiting heathen immoral practices, and expects every kind of the supposed means of looking into the future to be left alone. (See תוספות Sabbat 156,b, ד״ה כלדאי).
Zum dem Ausdrucke תמים וגו׳ עם וגו׳, vergl. והיה לבבכם שלם עם ה׳ אלקינו וגו׳ (Kön. I. 8, 61).

V. 14. כי הגוים האלה וגו׳. They lack the inner testing of their behaviour, and the confidence in God. They have lost the inner stability and fixed principles. For them the result is everything, the result for the satisfaction of their passions or their greed and ambition, results which are dependent on a thousand external chances against which they are powerless, which they feel lie beyond the sphere of their control, chances which have no connection with, or feelings for, the desires which agitate human breasts, lucky or unlucky chances which stare at people as unsolved riddles, but of which they nevertheless would like to have some indication beforehand out of their closed mystery as to whether they will be favourable or not to their wishes and desires—men without their spirits looking to God and without feelings paying tribute to duty have always fallen to heathen immoral practices of fortune-telling, clairvoyance etc. in coarser or more refined forms (cf. our article on Isaiah and his world reprinted in Gesam. Schriften Vol. II). These nations listen to astrologers and fortune-tellers for their private and public affairs.

“But thou, not such hath God, thy God given thee”! Inasmuch as He has come to you in the most intimate relationship as the exclusive Director of your fate and Guide for your actions, and has transmitted to you His Law for the conduct of your individual and national life in written and oral teachings, He has thereby given into your hands all what you require for the happy solution of the problems of your life’s task. He establishes your future, and the conditions for a happy or unhappy formation of that future He has given to you with the Torah which you have in your hands and the explanatory understanding of which you are to obtain from the living national tradition. To learn, teach and practice this Torah is the summary of your life’s task. For the knowledge understanding and fulfilling of this task no supernatural, superhuman insight, no peering into the transcendental world veiled to mankind is required. It is handed over to the healthy, clear, clearly perceiving, reasoning human intelligence, and at all its demands it presupposes just this and only this. Regarding it it says: לא בשמים היא (“not in the heavens is it” I.L. Ch. 30,12 refer to there) and not even a prophet, as such, has to say one word for the perception of, or to pass judgment on the Torah (cf. Baba Mezia, 59,b). For you, therefore, with what your God has given you, there is no need of any further disclosure from above, not concerning what the future will bring nor for what you are to do or not to do. You not only require no מעוננים and קוסמים like the other nations but you do not require any purer and truer substitute for them. If then in the following verse

V. 15. נביא מקרבך וגו׳, the sending of prophets is promised and discussed, we believe that the motive for this sending and its purpose is not for them to take the place in Israel of the מעוננים and קוסמים of the other nations, a purpose which indeed the תמים תהיה עם ה׳ אלקיך denies any need in Israel (cf. Rashi on v. 14). Our lives, all what we have to do and not to do, are regulated and satisfied by the Torah and its teachings and judgments. Not to enquire from him as to the advisability and feasibility of our plans, not to satisfy our desires by some knowledge denied to ordinary persons, not to find out through him what we would like to know, but to tell us what is God’s Will that we ought to know, for that, God sends us His prophets, the prophet is not our instrument, he is an instrument of God. Not אותו תשאלון but אליו תשמעון he is not there for you to consult, but for you to listen to, to obey, is what our text says. God requires him for the fulfilment of His purpose. So now let us hear what our Moses says:

נביא מקרבך מאחיך כמני, the men whom God will send to you as His prophets will be men out of your midst, they will live ordinary lives amongst you, no mysterious secret obscurity will hover about them, you will know their origin they will have been born and grown up amongst you, they will have proved their characters amongst you, you will know their parents, their brothers and sisters, they will be מקרבך מאחיך, in no wise will they come to you with superhuman pretentions, they will be human beings and claim to be nothing but human beings, כמני, just as I am, the first whom God has sent to you (cf. Ex. 6,14). And again כמני, in the same position and for the same purpose as I am sent. They are to be nothing other then messengers of the Words of God to you.

And יקים לך, not יקים ,ישלח לך He will establish him as a prophet to you, not just suddenly send him, will equip him with such means that he is מקוײם and מוחזק that he will be able to prove himself authorised as a messenger of God (See v. 22).

אפילו אומר לך עבור על אחת מכל מצות שבתורה כגון אליהו בהר הכרמל הכל לפי שעה שמע לו (Yebamoth 90,b and Sanhedrin 89,b). If he is already proven and established as a God-sent prophet, מוחזק, then you have to obey him even if he—like Elijah on Mt. Carmel, in the interests of some special demand on a special occasion to fortify the general public obedience to the Torah, למגדר מלתא,—demands an exceptional transgression of one of the commands of the Torah. To put the priests of Baal to shame and to convince the people wavering between making sacrifices to Baal or to God, Elijah ordered the prohibited sacrifice on a Bama to be made, and transgressed the prohibition of שחוטי חוץ והעלאה בחוץ (Ch. 12,13 and Levit. Ch. XVII).

That a prophet who would proclaim the permanent abrogations, in the name of God, of even one single Mitzva of the Torah, could not only not expect to be obeyed but would incur the penalty of death has already been declared above in Ch. 13,4 and 6.

V. 16. ככל וגו׳ בחרב ביום הקהל. At Horeb in full broad daytime, in full wakeful consciousness your whole nation stood before God and there you experienced in yourselves what it means for “the Word of God to come to human beings”. There you experienced that it is nothing which a man in an exalted state of getting beyond himself or in a frame of mind with his senses all in a confused state of bewilderment or frenzy could produce out of himself. God spoke to you, His Word came to you, face to face He spoke unto you (Ch. 5,4) and this was not an experience which a single individual had, the whole nation was gathered together and all heard the first sentences of the revelation of His Torah which He made to you. There it was shown to you as a fact of the most certain personal conviction, experienced by yourselves that “God speaks to human beings and they remain alive” (see above Ch. V); and only because you feared that you would not be able to stand a continuation of this direct speech of God, did the conviction, gained by the evidence of your own senses, suffice for you, and you begged to be given the further Speech of God only indirectly through me (ibid 22-24). Here you are only reminded of what was given in detail there so as

V. 17 and 18. to add to it, that also after Moses’ death, God would give further communications to the successors of Moses who were to be the transmitters of His Word to Israel. They would also be מקרב אחיהם כמוך and would likewise receive the Words of God that they were to speak.

19. and 20. והיה האיש וגו׳ אך הנביא וגו׳. Verse 19 speaks of the case of non-observance of the Word of God given to the prophet: אשר לא ישמע אל דברי. According to Sanhedrin 89,a, this includes three cases: הכובש את נבואתו, that the prophet does not proclaim the Word of God which he has received; המוותר על דברי נביא, that somebody pays no attention to what the prophet proclaims, treats it as superfluous; ונביא שעבר על דברי עצמו or that a prophet himself acts contrary to what he proclaims; שלשתן מיתתן בידי שמים, all three are warned by God of the punishment of death that He will mete out to them אנכי אדרש מעמו. Verse 20 speaks of the sin of the false prophet, אשר יזיד לדבר דבר בשמי, who presumes to proclaim a message from God which he has not received at all; or even את אשר לא צויתיו לדבר which he was not charged to deliver; or finally אשר ידבר בשם אלהים אחרים, that he even proclaims the truth in the name of some heathen god, all three: המתנבא מה שלא שמע ומה שלא נאמר לו והמתנבא בשם עכו״ם are to be penalised by capital punishment at human courts, ומת הנביא ההוא, and כל מיתה האמורה בתורה סתם אינה אלא חנק (ibid. see Levit. on XX,10; see further above Ch. 13,2 et seq.).

V. 21 and 22. וכי תאמר בלבבך וגו׳, אשר ידבר וגו׳. In v. 20 the נביא שקר, the false prophet who speaks in God’s Name that which God had not commanded him to say, is condemned to judical capital punishment. That of course immediately raises the question by what is it to be judged that his proclamation is a false one. One criterion of the contents of the words of a prophet has already been given in Ch. 13,3 and 6. A proclamation which exhorts us to a defection from God, or from His Torah even if it declares only one single commandment as abrogated, proves thereby that the proclamation is false, and condemns the one who makes it, however well attested he may otherwise be as a prophet, to judical death. (refer to there).

But here it is speaking about authenticating a prophet as such in general, when his proclamation is not contradictory to the Torah, by what can his prophecy be recognised as not coming from God. On that the answer runs:-

ולא יהיה הדבר ולא יבא — אשר ידבר הנביא בשם ה׳ וגו׳. The occurrence of a miracle in the sphere of nature which has been previously prophesied is designated by its concept of היה. Thus of the miracles which Moses had to perform before Pharaoh. והיה לכנם ,והיה דם ויהיו דם ,יהי לתנין ויהי לתנין הברד לא יהיה עוד, לא היה ברד. ויהי ברד. היה השחין, למחר יהיה האות הזה היה כנים, ויהי חשך. Regarding the occurrence of events in the sphere of human conditions, as a rule they are expressed by the concept of בוא. Thus לא נפל דבר מכל הדבר הטוב אשר דבר ה׳ אל בית ישראל הכל בא. (Joshua 21,43) and elsewhere very frequently. We believe accordingly that by ולא יהיה הדבר ולא יבא both facts are designated by which the facts of the mission of a prophet can be authenticated. Either by the occurrence of a miracle in nature which the prophet had predicted: יהיה, or by the occurrence of a predicted event in history יבא. And in fact to substantiate the actual truth of a prophet being commissioned by God, by the Creator and Master of Nature and the Director of history there is no other means than either the occurrence of a miracle which he had predicted or the announcement of a future event which then happens. If a prophet, in the name of God declares a miracle will happen ולא יהיה and it does not occur, or some future happening which likewise ולא יבא does not come to pass, הוא הדבר אשר לא דבר ה׳, that is a word which God had not spoken, בזדון דברו הנביא, it is a word which the prophet has uttered in capricious misuse of God’s name; and had he hitherto stood in the very highest confidence of the people, with the conviction of one single such false word he has pronounced sentence on himself for ever, לא תגור ממנו: in whatever high respect and estimation his personality may have deservedly stood hitherto, you may have no scruples in giving him the lie publicly and to hand him over to the punishment he has incurred. Incidently, it seems to us, that this לא תגור ממנו is also a proof that the appointment of a person to be a prophet must be preceded by his having already attained a high degree of spiritual and moral greatness. For this לא תגור ממנו takes it for granted that, apart from the would-be assumed prophetic mission, he must have been a person who had earned a highly respected reputation.

But, as is explained in Sanhedrin 89,b, it is only at the first time that he comes to the people as a prophet with a message from God that he has to legitimize his position by a miracle, or by prophesying the advent of an occurrence which then does occur, but he has by no means to continue to legitimize any further declarations he makes in the name of God, but once he has established his position, is מוחזק, then for all time it says of him:-
אליו תשמעון (v.15; refer to notes thereon).

Altogether, performing miracles and so-called soothsaying does not belong to the real calling of Jewish prophets, and by no means form the purpose of their mission. To be a נביא, an instrument of God—נבא related to יביע אומר ,נבע (Ps. XIX), אביעה חידות (LXXVIII,2 etc.)—to act as an intermediary to give His people the insight in themselves, and in His Ways with them and with the nations of the world, to give them an understanding of their contemporary time and their expectations in the future, by all this to fortify them in goodness and to warn them against badness and to give them strength and courage and enduring faithfulness to God and the Torah throughout all the vicissitudes of the ages, that was—as their words still lie open before us—what their real calling was. Through them Israel was to be the “People of History” who go through the history of the world with open eyes seeing the Hand of God in all human history. The miracles that they performed—and how little, almost nothing, do we know of all the men, from Isaiah to Malachi, who bore the illuminating spirit of prophecy throughout the centuries—were all not done to serve their own immediate object but were all done in the service of this, their high national calling, and moreover, of men like Nathan and Gad whose words of prophecy did stand more in service of their immediate contemporary times and on that account are not recorded for all future generations (Megilla 14,a) (i.e. there are no books of the sayings of Gad or Nathan as there are of twelve of the so-called “minor” prophets I.L.) of them we are given no report of their having performed miracles. And if these do appear in greater number and predominantly in the conditions of private lives of individuals, in the record of the lives of an Elijah and Elisha, we think the remark is not quite erroneous, that these occurred exclusively in the kingdom of Israel where, under the influence of the upper classes, the life of the people was greatly overcast by the heathen evil practices of the priests and prophets of Baal. And their purpose was to work against this by showing the real Presence and Almight of the One True God even in the unimportant lives of individuals of all classes, and to awake, nurture and fortify the purer consciousness of God, and the pure recognition of God in the hearts of the sons and daughters of the people; as well as to oppose the lying pretentions of the expounders of the sacred mysteries to the Israeli court which had degenerated into Baalism, with destructive proofs of true authentic miracles. In the kingdom of Judah at least we hardly find any records of such miracles.

V. 1. On Numb. 35,9 et seq. and Deut. 4,41 we have already worked out the deep significance of the cities of refuge. We tried to show how their having to be established immediately at the divisioning of the land was to be the most public proclamation of the great fundamental principle of Man’s likeness to God and the high dignity and value of human blood for which there can be no compensation, as being, next to the “Oneness” of God, the second indispensable basis of the whole confederation of the Jewish State. That is why here also, after the establishment of all the instruments of state: Judge, king, priest, prophet, there follows, as the very first object of their activity, a supplementary chapter on the prescriptions for ensuring the safety of human life in the Jewish State. This supplement consists particularly in the explanation of the nature of a fatal blow which would necessitate the giver of it having to be banished to a city of refuge. (v. 5.), and in ordering the provision of three further such cities for the time when the extent of the domain of the state would be increased. (Verses 8 and 9).

כי יכרית וגו׳. (Cf. 12,29). On account of their moral depravity they have incurred destruction. וירשתם וישבת וגו׳. The actual working of the “refuge” institution (apart from the appointment of the cities for that purpose, which had to be done immediately on taking possession of the land I.L.) only came into effect לאחר ירושה וישיבה, (after they had settled in the land I.L.) see on Numb. 35,10. ובבתיהם. The addition of this word which only occurs here at the introduction to this institution which brings home to the State the dignity and worth of every single individual of its members without exception seems to be extremely significant, and indeed in two ways. It is not what goes on in the country and cities, but what goes on in the homes which decides the moral worth and thereby the weal or woe of a state. So that it is not in the land or the cities where the nation lives, you must seek it in the houses. And further: living in houses the previous inhabitants of which lived a life of immorality is not by any means a furtherance for morality, and with double poignancy must these the principles of the law of morals be stressed so that by the power of its spirit the influence of even thinking about the previous bad example disappears.

V. 2 and 3. שלש וגו׳ תכין לך וגו׳. See on Numb. 25,11 — אשר ינחילך וגו׳. In the previous verses it always calls it ירושה. Elswhere we have already discussed the difference between ירש and ירש .נחל looks on the heritage from the point of view of the heir, נחל from the standpoint of the one who leaves the heritage. Here by this change of terms it may mean to say: although you actually take the place of the previous inhabitants of the land, the cities and the houses, still the land with all its contents is to be bequeathed to those that come after you as completely other and different from what it was when you obtained possession of it in succession to the other nations. You are not to look on yourselves as יורש (the inheritors I.L.) of the nations, but bequeath the land spiritually and morally changed to your children as נחלת ה׳.
והיה לנוס שמה כל רוצח. See on Numb. 35,12.

V. 4. וזה דבר הרוצח, only here and above in Ch. 15,2 at השמטת כספים is the introduction of a judical regulation called דבר. The Halacha (Sheveith 10,8) teaches that thereby it is made a duty for any one who had been banished to a city of refuge to remind himself and others of his רוצח-character in certain circumstances e.g. if the officials of the city of refuge should at some time wish to show him some mark of honour, he may not accept such an honour or appointment to an office of honour silently without referring to it רוצח שגלה לעיר מקלט ורצו אנשי העיר לכבדו יאמר להם רוצח אני אמרו לו אעפ״כ יקבל מהם. For, that he should keep in mind the fatal result of his carelessness is part of the purpose of his banishment.

בבלי דעת: no thought of killing at all may have been in his mind, פרט למתכוין להרוג את הבהמה והרג את האדם, but if, for example, he intended to kill an animal and killed a man who was standing nearby, that would be criminal carelessness, קרוב למזיד, which would not be atoned for by mere banishment to living in a city of refuge (Makkoth 7,b) see תוספות B.K. 26,b, ד״ה פרט; refer to Numb. 35,12).

והוא לא שונא לו. Even a case where the circumstances are such that it would ordinarily have been judged as pure carelessness, שוגג, which is to be atoned for by banishment to a city of refuge, loses that character and is ranked as קרוב למזיד if the victim is known to be hated by the man-slaughterer. And this would be considered to be the case even if he had only refused to speak to him מתמול שלשום for the previous three days (Makkoth 9,b, ספרי; see Numb. ibid).

V. 5. יער :רשות לניזק ולמזיק ליכנס שם .ואשר יבא את רעהו ביער (Makkoth 7,b) “in a forest”: only then is it considered a case requiring atonement and to be atoned for in this manner, a שגגה, if the accident occured in a place where both of them had the right to be. But if, for instance, a man was in his own yard where the other had no right to enter without knocking at the door and receiving permission, so that the מזיק could have no idea that anybody else was there, the accident cannot be ascribed to carelessness, is קרוב לאונס, and does not require atonement by having to be banished to a city of refuge. זרק את האבן לחצרו והרג אם יש רשות לניזק ליכנס שם גולה ואם לאו אינו גולה שנאמר ואשר יבא את רעהו ביער מה יער מכות ח׳ א׳) רשות לניזק ולמזיק ליכנס שם אף כל וכו׳; but still see (תוס׳ ב״ק ל״ב ב׳ ומשמע דה״ה איפכא כשיש רשות לניוק ואין רשות למזיק ג״כ פטור מפני שהוא קרוב למויד ולא דמי ליער וצ״ע דלא הובא דין זה ומתוי״ט לא משמע דפטור ע״ש.

ונדחה ידו בגרזן. Cf. לנדח עליו גרזן Ch. 20,19. From there it is evident that the ordinary action of swinging an axe to fell a tree is called נדח גרזן. If on the other hand here the axe is put in the active voice, or rather the arm in the passive ונדחה ידו his arm is swung by the axe this could be meant to indicate that the action was not what was intended, or at least was not intended to be such a vigorous swing, “the axe swung the arm” further back than was intended and so the head flew off from the handle and the accident happened, which is the way the following ונשל וגו׳ is taken.

ונשל הברזל מן העץ. In Makkoth 7,b, there is a difference of opinion between רבי and חכמים. According to רבי the עץ refers to the tree which is being felled, עץ המתבקע, the same as the preceding לכרת העץ which would be why it does not say מעצו but מן העץ and the case would then be: the iron (the axe) chips a chunk of wood off the tree which falls on a man and kills him. (According to רמב״ם הל׳ רוצח VI,15, the way רבי takes it is: by the impact of the iron with the tree it slips off the tree. With that, the ונישל in the passive would agree better with the way רבי takes it). But according to the view held by the חכמים which is accepted as Halacha such a case would not entail banishment to a city of refuge, it being כח כחו, only an indirect result of his action (the chunk of wood, the medium by which the man was killed was not set in motion directly by his act), but the עץ of the text refers to the handle of the axe, and the case is נשמט הברזל מקתו והרג, by the force of his energetic swing the iron head of the axe flew off from the handle and struck the other person fatally. All the other places in which נשל occurs indicate that it does not designate a part being separated from the whole, as a chunk splintered off from the tree, but the separation of one body from another to which it had been attached, thus of a shoe from the foot (Ex. 3,5), the fruit from the tree (Deut. 28,40), the inhabitants from their land (Deut. 7,1) et alia. So that here it would designate the iron from its handle. Also נשל is predominantly active and not intransitive, as according to the way רמב״ם takes the opinion of רבי it would have to be. Even כי ישל זיתך (Ch. 28,40) can very well be transitive, “your olive trees will cast off their fruit”. That the term ונדחה ידו בגרזן would also be in favour of the explanation of the חכמים we have already remarked.

פרט לממציא את עצמו ,ומצא את רעהו. The penalty of banishment is only incurred if, at the moment when the careless action was done, the victim of it was in the spot threatened by the danger, the dangerous missile “found” the one who was struck by it, but not if the latter only afterwards presented himself to it, e.g. אם משיצאה האבן מידו הוציא הלה את ראשו פטור, if the one who was hit put his head into the line of danger after the stone had already been thrown. (Makkoth 8,a).

V. 8-10. ואם ירחיב וגו׳. Of the ten nations, the possession of whose lands was promised to Abraham (Gen. 15,19-21) they only received first of all the lands of seven of them. The complete heritage remained reserved for them (see on Ch. 1,7) for the future. If in the future they become deemed worthy of this increased possession of territory they are to begin the foundation of the Jewish social life to be developed there, likewise with the institution of cities of refuge. The holiness of human life, outweighing all possible earthly possession, remains for all time the basis of all Jewish human social conditions. The spilt blood of a single innocent person דם נקי, lays a heavy burden of blood-guiltiness on the whole state, והיה עליך דמים (see further Numb. 35,9-34).

V. 11 and 12. וכי יהיה וגו׳. In verse 4 it was said that if anybody kills a person through carelessness, the presumption of its being unintentional can only be maintained provided the killer was not known to hate the victim. But if this latter is really notoriously the case, the possibility or probability of some intentional carelessness is assumed which does not allow the atonement of the cities of refuge to be given to him.

But such notorious relation of enmity is by no means sufficient evidence for judical punishment. Even כי יהיה איש שונא לרעהו, even if the enmity had been most longstanding and well known to everybody and the fatal blow a direct hit and everything pointing to intentional murder all such circumstantial evidence would not suffice for a judical verdict of murder to be brought. The intention וארב לו and the fact וקם עליו that the execution of it was done to murder him must be proved and at the same time it must be proved that the blow itself was a fatal one and that death occurred as the direct effect of it (see on Numb. 35,16,17 and 18).

We have already remarked on Ex. 21,22 that the Gemora is not quite decided on the question whether נתכוין להרוג את זה והרג את זה is חײב or פטור, whether, to establish a case for capital guilt it is necessary for the murder to have been directed at a person whose murder would qualify for such capital punishment, and in addition had actually been committed on that particular person, or whether it is sufficient for the murderous intent and act to be established, even if the actual blow fell on a different person and killed him. This question depends on the way the case described there in Ex. 5,23 is taken, the wording of which ואם אסון יהיה ונתת נפש תחת נפש taken in conjunction with the preceding verse, would favour the opinion that, if, in the case presented in V. 22 the one wanted to kill the man but the blow had caught the woman, he would still incur capital punishment, whereas the other opinion takes these words in a different sense.

Now the way we take our case here depends on how this question is decided. If, as ר׳ שמעון teaches נתכוין להרוג את זה והרג את זה פטור then we have to take the text strictly וארב לו וקם עליו i.e. עד שיתכוין לו, he must have intended to kill a certain person and that must be the person whom he had killed. But if the halacha is according to the חכמים and in accordance with the wording of Ex. 21,23 נתכוין להרוג את זה והרג את זה חײב then our וארב לו וקם עליו would not exclude the case where the blow caught somebody other than the one it was directed at, but only demands that the intention and its accomplishment was done definitely for the purpose of the murder of a person, the killing of whom entails capital punishment. But if a person זורק אבן לגו, discharged a murderous missile with full consciousness and full intent into the midst of a mass of people amongst whom there was even a single individual the killing of whom would not entail the death-penalty—e.g. there was one amongst them who was already absolutely fatally injured, טריפה (Sanhedrin 78,a)—he could not be convicted of murder, as the discharge did not bear the character of being absolutely of necessity entailing murder with the death penalty, as it could conceivably have hit that person who was already irrevocably doomed.

The legal fact laid down here in this case where we do not follow the general rule that אזלינן בתר רובא (Ex. 23,2)—we go by the majority—by which a single one would be considered as absorbed into the majority and not reckoned, but here is considered as having as much chance as anybody else, מחצה על מחצה, a 50: 50 chance, gives rise to a far-reaching modification of the rule of רוב. Namely, that a minority of a special kind amongst a majority of a different kind, e.g. an איסור amongst a majority of היתר, only then loses its identity and need not be considered if it is unrecognisably mixed in the mass, but not if it can be picked out from it, and—according to תוספות in Chulin 98,a, ד״ה ספיקו, Zebachim 73,b, ד״ה אלא—there where it is can be recognised in its speciality, ,האיסור ניכר במקומו ידוע האיסור בדוכתיה. Such a condition is called קבוע, remaining fixed, as differentiated from תערובות, completely mixed up, and hence the law:- כל קבוע כמחצה על מחצה דמי, and e.g. תשע חנויות מוכרות בשר שחוטה ואחת מוכרת בשר נבלה ולקח מאחת מהן ואינו ידוע מאיזו מהן לקח ספיקו אסור, there are ten butcher shops of which nine sell kosher meat and one sells treifa meat, and someone had bought meat from one of them but does not know out of which one she bought it, so that the meat in her hand is doubtful and must be treated as אסור, prohibited, although the majority of the shops sold only kosher meat (Chulin, ibid).

The closer details of the conception קבוע and its application in actual practice are subject to further laws concerning it and partly to different opinions (see the commentators on Kethuvouth 15,a, Chulin 95,a, and Yoreh Dea, 110,3).

In connection with this קבוע דאורײתא and its practical application, מדרבנן certain things which, even though they are not recognisable, and could not be picked out of a mixture, are still, on account of their individual importance not considered as absorbed and negligible when mixed into a mass of other material. Things like דבר שבמנין, which are exclusively sold and counted piecemeal, את שדרכו לימנות, or at least mostly so counted, כל בעלי חײם ;שדרכו לימנות, living animals; or generally דבר חשוב, things of value which are specially considered, hence also חתיכה הראויה להתכבד a single piece of meat which by reason of its size and goodness would be kept for guests, all such things are not בטל ברוב, and even if one of them which was אסור became mixed in a large number of similar things which are היתר are considered as קבוע דרבנן, do not become absorbed in the majority, and the whole mass is considered as if consisting of half איסור and half היתר, and anything taken from the mixture is considered as ספק, as being possibly that very piece and must be treated as אסור.

There is another category which, for other reasons, is not בטל ברוב, this is דבר שיש לו מתירין, something which is only temporarily אסור, which after a time becomes automatically מותר, or a thing which is an איסור by a vow which could be revoked (Numb. 30,3), אי בעי מיתשיל עליה (see Yoreh Dea, 102,109, and 110).

Now here it says: וכי יהיה איש שנא לרעהו וארב לו, but if anybody has committed a murder and there is definite proof of the criminality of the intention, the act, and its result, then these cities of refuge afford absolutely no protection, but if he had fled to one of these cities—and as already remarked, (Numb. 35,12) it is presumed that in every case, intentional murder or accidental manslaughter, the perpetrator would flee to such a city to avoid the risk of his life being attacked without any trial having been held—זקני עירו וגו׳, the court competent to deal with the case send and have him fetched from there, so that the full measure of justice is meted out to him: ביד גואל הדם (see on Numb. ibid.).

V. 13. לא תחוס וגו׳. By committing a qualifying murder the life of the murderer is forfeited, and the same sanctity of every single drop of human blood exceeding beyond the value of any other earthly possession which lies at the base of the whole institution of refuge cities and characterises the nature of the Jewish State, demands the capital punishment of the intentional murderer as much as these cities have the purpose of protecting the life of every citizen against carelessness, and the life of the unintentional manslayer against revenge. Consideration for a murderer would not be consideration for human blood but indifference towards the shedding of innocent human blood.

ובערת דם הנקי מישראל, it is doubtful how this is to be understood, whether it is the debt which would be owing to the blood if the murderer would be spared, or the crime of the shedding of the blood which is to be purged out of the Jewish State. וטוב לך, regarding human life as sacred is the fundamental condition for human happiness (cf. Numb. 35,33 and 34).

V. 14. לא תסיג וגו׳, as the word השיג to which it is related means to reach, to attain, הסיג גבול would only mean incorporating your neighbour’s territory into your own by shifting the boundary line further away. From Sifri on our verse, it is evident that this prohibition of shifting the boundary of your neighbour, whether by force or secretly, which would already be forbidden under the conception of robbery or theft, if it is done in א״י (the land of Israel I.L.) is here given a further special prohibition. In Eretz Yisroel it is doubly forbidden בא״י עובר בשני לאוין, בח״ל אינו עובר אלא משום לאו א׳. Only the addition of אשר גבלו ראשנים remains difficult. If here it is simply robbing or stealing ground which is forbidden what difference does it make if the boundary dates from centuries or from yesterday. The sentence אשר גבלו ראשנים בנחלתך אשר תנחל בארץ אשר ה׳ אלקיך נתן לך לרשתה seems in any case to refer to the original division of the land which took place when the land was first taken into possession. If we consider that this original division of the land was made not merely to the tribes, into provinces, but at once to the installation of each individual into his own possession; and the national taking the land into possession was not considered as completed and the Youvel institution did not come into effect until כל אחד ואחד מכיר את כרמו (every single individual knew his own vineyard I.L.) see Levit. 25,2 et seq; and if we consider further that every change in the possession of land by sale or gift, yea, according to one opinion even by every division of an inheritance, reverts to its original state at the entry of the Youvel year, then the assumption would indeed be justified that on the whole, the regulations of the Torah would bring it about that the original arrangement of fixing the borders of real estate should remain permanent even to the extent of single fields. So that seeking to gain an advantage by shifting the border line of an adjoining field in the land of Israel, apart from the crime of גזילה or גניבה against the neighbour, would, at the same time, be a sin against the original division of the land under the direction of God. A division which by its permanent character ever bears the Divine sanction, and by which the whole possession of land is impressed with the stamp of hereditary estate or entailed property held in fief from the overlordship of God, the One unique true groundlandlord, a fact, the recognition of which underlies the whole institutions of Schemita and Youvel. Hence the repeated stressing of the concept בנחלתך :נחלה אשר תנחל וגו׳. You are never to lose sight of the fact that you possess the land as a whole, as well as any single part of it that you have, only as נחלה, as entailed property which you obtained from your ancestors with rights but also with duties attached to it. You have not to consider yourself as יורש who has dispossessed the previous owner of his property and could seek his absolute power of possession in himself and by his own authority. If you are a יורש and so dispossess the actual present possessor it is not by reason of your own plentitude of power which you yourself had, but it is ה׳ אלקיך Who נתן לך לרשתה. “giveth it to you to take it into possession”

In the Sifri also on our verse it goes on to say מנין לעוקר תחומים של שבטים שעובר בלא תעשה ת״ל לא תסיג. But it is doubtful whether this passage refers to our verse לא תסיג גבול רעך וגו׳ or to לא תסג גבול עולם אשר עשו אבותיך (Prov. 22,28). According to Rambam commenting thereon, and also according to Yalkut the Sifri does actually seem to have our verse in mind.

If the way we have taken it be not erroneous, the position of this law in connection with the preceding and, as we shall see, with what comes after would be understandable. Life and property are the two principle valuables which are to be placed under the protection of the Laws of God administered by the State, and their inviolable sanctity in the Land of God’s Torah proclaimed immediately that land is taken into possession, with, we would say, topographic and thereby permanent duration. The cities of refuge distributed to be available throughout the land proclaimed the sanctity of human life, the borders of the holdings being fixed for ever proclaimed the sanctity of property. But these two, life and property form the two great spheres of laws, the דיני נפשות and דיני ממונות which in the first place are the activities of the lawcourts (the Bethdins) which is really the object with which our whole portion of שפטים is dealing, and are moreover the categories to which the following laws regarding witnesses primarily refer.

V. 15. לא יקום וגו׳. In the two preceding sections of the Torah, ערי מקלט and הסגת גבול, life and property were fundamentally stressed as the two chief valuables of earthly existence the inviolability of which are placed under the guarantee of the state legal authorities, and which can only be assailed by a verdict of these authorities. The inviolability of life—in a wider sense including the whole of the body—and of property can only suffer forfeiture as a result of a sentence for the punishment of a crime given by a criminal court, as well as loss of property by proof given in the civil courts of dishonest possession, or to pay proven claims. From that the two great spheres of Jewish administration דיני נפשות and דיני ממונות emerge, the former from which the sentence to suffer capital or corporal punishment is pronounced, from the latter to suffer the imposition of having to pay something in the nature of a fine, or to pay a debt that was proved to have been owing. The object to which both are directed is the responsible nature of a person towards the legality of his actions and the honesty of his assets. The process of the proof on which any and every such sentence must be based rests on the declaration of witnesses, and this is the subject of the following verses.

There is another sphere in which the declaration of witnesses can be effective, and that is the sphere of איסור והיתר, on the question of certain foods etc. being permitted or prohibited, for which a declaration of the nature of their constitution and state can be decisive. The following laws do not deal primarily with this matter which will only have to be touched on incidentally.
Now here it says:-

לא יקום עד אחד באיש לכל עון ולכל חטאת. The testimony of one single witness באיש to make a person responsible לכל עון ולכל חטאת for having acted wrongfully, intentionally, עון, or unintentionally, חטאת, shall have no standing at all לא יקום, i.e. shall be invalid. And indeed בכל חטא אשר יחטא referring to any wrongdoing he could have committed, accordingly also to refuse payments, the refusal of which if the demand is justified would be sinful. Thereby then the law is given that nobody, neither with reference to capital or corporal punishment מיתה ומלקות nor to fines קנס, nor to payments in cash or kind, as a result of גזלות וחבלות הודאות והלואות etc. altogether in דיני נפשות ודיני ממונות in the widest sense can receive a sentence on the testimony of one single witness, and also the duty of having to bring a sin-offering, a חטאת for having unintentionally committed a major sin, is not to rest on the evidence of one single witness (see the Sifri, ומה דאיתא נמי שם להעלות לכהונה ולהוריד מן הכהונה הא להעלות לכהונה נראה דתלי בפלוגתא בין הר״ן והרמב״ם דלהר״ן סגי בעד א׳ להאכילו תרומה דאורײתא וע״כ צ״ל דלהעלות לכהונה בספרי אינו אלא אסמכתא עי׳ ר״ן כתובות כ״ג ע״ב).

In Levit. 4,23 and 28 (refer to it) the duty to bring a חטאת, as a result of transgressing certain prohibitions unintentionally, is attached to the presumption that הודע אליו חטאתו (his sin has become known to him I.L.). Inasmuch as the required knowledge of his having transgressed is expressed by הודע אליו, two things are told thereby. Firstly, that he need not necessarily have come to this knowledge by himself in which case it would have said: או ידע. And, on the other hand, that it would not be sufficient that only others were convinced that he had committed the sin, otherwise the Torah would have said הודע אליו .או הודע establishes the case that others have convinced him that he did do it, or at least, he does not contradict them. Hence the dictum in Yebamoth 89,b:- או הודע אליו חטאתו ולא שיודיעוהו אחרים, יכול אעפ״י שאינו מכחישו ת״ל או הודע אליו מ״מ, from which is deduced that also עד אחד אומר אכלת חלב והוא שותק, that the uncontradicted evidence of a single witness also makes it incumbent on a person to bring a חטאת. There is only a difference of opinion as to how such a silence with which this evidence of a single witness is to be taken. Does the mere admission of the possibility of the occurence suffice to incur the duty of bringing an offering, and the case would be the same, if he said איני יודע, “I do not know if I did it”, or does the silence imply the admission of the probability of the matter and would give רגלים לדבר, but איני יודע against a single witness would be equivalent to הכחשה (denial I.L.), or finally is שתיקה כהודאה do we have to take his silence as complete admission? According to תוספות on Kiddushin 56,b, ד״ה אמר לו, the difference which is made here between one witness and two witnesses shows that even regarding the bringing of a איני יודע ,חטאת only brings that duty in the case of עד אחד through the admission of at least the probability, (ibid, 66,b, ד״ה רבא אמר), but in the case of two witnesses, even saying איני יודע, or at least the possibility implied by שתיקה would necessitate the bringing of a חטאת. As a matter of fact, the declaration of two witnesses by itself even without any admission would completely establish the required או הודע אליו as everywhere the evidence of two witnesses effects the same certainty as noticing something oneself, so it can take the place of having noticed it oneself. (See ש״מ on ב״מ 3b, מה אם ירצה, ,בשם הרמב״ן והרשב״א).

Whether the assertion of two witnesses against the positive denial of a person can make it incumbent on him to bring a חטאת depends on the way one takes the motive of the חכמים to be in giving a negative decision for such a case as שנים אומרים אכלת חלב והוא אומר לא אכלתי (Kerithoth 11,b). According to one opinion (ibid. 12,a) their reason was that משום דאדם נאמן על עצמו יותר ממאה איש, because the purely personal need for atonement which a קרבן, an offering is to satisfy, the highest degree of credibility must evidently be granted to each person himself more than to a hundred other people. According to this reasoning, in no case could witnesses make a חטאת incumbent on anybody who contradicts the charge of a transgression which would make him liable to bring one. In cases where he does thus flatly contradict, two witnesses would be no better than one, and—as far as we can see—then our verse here, which clearly only makes the evidence of one witness invalid for חטאת while that of two witnesses could be effective, could only be explained as referring to cases of שתיקה or איני יודע as already remarked according to תוספות.

According to another way of taking it (ibid), what the חכמים say: שנים אומרים נטמאת והוא אומר לא נטמאתי פטור, שנים אומרים אכלת חלב והוא אומר לא אכלתי פטור is only meant to do away with the evidence of two witnesses if it is contradicted when the denial is not necessarily absolute i.e. when the evidence in itself can be true but still the duty to bring a חטאת need not necessarily result from it. If, for instance, the rebuttal לא אכלתי permits the meaning מתרץ דיבוריה: “I did not eat the חלב in a way that would entail a חטאת״, I knew quite well what I was eating, I did not eat שוגג but מזיד; or equally so in saying לא נטמאתי it can refer to a טומאה of previous condition, he says: No, I did not become duty-bound to bring a חטאת by entering the Sanctuary or by coming into contact with קדשים״, I had already had טבילה and הערב שמש and had got rid of the טומאה. But where the denial is just a positive absolute one, as it would be in the case of a טומאה having just been incurred when there would be no possibility of טבילה and הערב שמש, there, (according to this way of taking what they said I.L.), the חכמים also admit the full effect of the evidence of two witnesses against the denial of the one accused, as it is everywhere else so too here for the duty of bringing a חטאת, and they would in such a case agree with the deduction of אם הביאוהו שנים לידי מיתה תמורה לא יביאוהו לידי קרבן הקל :רבי מאיר (if the evidence of two people can condemn a man to death, surely it is sufficient to make it incumbent on him to bring a prescribed offering I.L.). According to this way of taking it, which Rambam also adopts (הל׳ שגגות 11,8) our text would have the simple explanation of speaking for חטאת as well as for עון of the case of absolute denial of that to which the evidence refers. Whereas לכל עון ולכל חטאת the evidence of two witnesses is valid even against the denial of the accused, the evidence of a single witness against such denial is null and void עד אחד בהכחשה ולא כלום.

This fact, which it seems to us cannot be evaded, that, according to our text, with regards to חטאת also, there is a difference between a single witness and two witnesses might, as far as we can see, have not been fully considered in all its ramifications by the commentators in their deliberations thereon. Thus Rambam, for instance, who in הל׳ שגגות III,1 and 2 makes no difference between one witness and two in cases of שתיקה would surely acquiesce in the necessity for making such difference in cases of הכחשה in accordance with the reasoning of מגו and would make the adoption of אדם נאמן על עצמו impossible for him, by which, it seems to us, what he says there in XI,8, is sufficiently explained (cf. כ״מ and ל״מ ibid).

We have only laid stress on the cardinal points of these deliberations as far as they seemed necessary for the elucidation of our text, but see in detail Kerithoth 11,b, et seq; Baba Mezia 3,b; Yebamoth 87,b; תוספות and the commentaries thereon.

It is on this legal fact that, in certain circumstances, even a single witness, when there is no הכחשה is given sufficient authority for the imposition of the חטאת-duty, that the further question already touched on as to the credibility given to an עד אחד באיסורין, the declaration of a single person referring not directly to responsible actions but primarily to the nature and condition of things. We shall note a few general principles of this too. In general עד אחד נאמן באיסורין where לא אתחזק איסורא, the declaration of one person regarding the character and composition of a thing where there is a doubt about it, is sufficient to permit it provided there is no reason for presuming it to be prohibited e.g. a piece of fat which one does not know whether it is שומן or חלב. Even where there is a presumption that it is forbidden, אתחזק איסורא a single person can be trusted if בידו לתקנו, if it lies within his power, and he has authority to use it, to bring about the היתר condition, e.g. an animal by שחיטה, or a טבל product by separating תרומה. Equally so any single person is qualified to declare that something of his own, or in his care, that, although the presumption is that it is alright, something has occurred to alter its condition e.g. טהרות that they have become טמא, wine that it has become נסך. But at goods which have been entrusted to his care, only if he declares this at the first opportunity. Similarily to what we have said above concerning the חטאת-duty, the same law holds good for a single witness in איסור matters, that such evidence accepted in silence by the owner is valid if circumstances make the truth of the declaration probable, there are רגלים לדבר, or according to another opinion, even if there is only the possibility of it, איני יודע. (Yebamoth 88,a; Kiddushin 56,b; Gittin 54,b; רא״ש ibid). For the practical application of all these laws more detailed particulars must be obtained, see Yore Dea, 127, ש״ך).

We add one further law which has important consequences. If on the testimony of one single person regarding the nature and condition of an object, the prohibition of its use has once been established and officially recognised, then anybody who acts against this officially recognised condition of that object, can, on the evidence of two witnesses be brought before the court and made responsible for his actions, although, at bottom, the prohibition of the object rests only on the testimony of a single witness; (see Rambam הל׳ סנהדרין XVI,6).

Other legal facts also in the sphere of איסור והיתר (see Rashi, Chulin 10,b; תוספות Gittin 2,b) which fix laws concerning the admissibility of the testimony of single witnesses can be implied in the wording of our text. It does not say that absolutely לא יקום עד אחד (no testimony of a single witness is admissable I.L.) but באיש, not against a person responsible for his actions. But it can well be accepted regarding establishing the actual objective condition and nature of things, and also the conditional limitation of this admissability to cases in which איתחזק איסורא is not present could lie no less in the sense of our text. The testimony against a generally held presumption (חזקה I.L.) or a justified presumption in a special case, is also a testimony באיש, against the general personality of people, if not against their responsibility for their actions, still against their intelligent knowledge of the world about them, and to challenge either our behaviour and actions or our knowledge requires the evidence of two people. On the other hand our knowledge of objects which are in other people’s possession is limited, or which are in possession of people who are able to alter the conditions which we presume these objects to be in, and everybody is נאמן על שלו and concerning every object שבידו לתקנו.

From the limiting addition of לכל עון ולכל חטאת to the inadmissibility of a single witness, the Gemora in Schevouth 40a, derives the law לכל עון ולכל חטאת אינו קם אבל קם הוא לשבועה כל מקום ששנים מחײבין אותו ממון עד אחד מחײבו שבועה, that also in cases of civil law, although a single witness has not the power to bring about a verdict on the accused regarding the legality of his ownership of some possession, his evidence still has the power to make the court impose an oath on the accused—except in cases of fines קנס—so that in all cases where the evidence of two witnesses would have entailed a judgment causing a payment to be made by the accused the evidence of a single witness causes an oath to be taken by the accused that he does not owe the money claimed from him. And indeed according to the view of the רי״ף which is accepted as Halacha, even where the claim rests solely on the declaration of the single witness, as the plaintiff himself lacks the positive knowledge of the claim: כגון שאמר לו עד אחד אמר לי שנטלת משלי מנה והלה כופר והביא את העד (the plaintiff says “a friend told me that you had this sum of money from me”, the defendant denies having had it, and the plaintiff brings the friend as witness I.L.) and cannot put in a plea, טענת ברי, “I am certain”, but only טענת שמא, “it may be so”. (רא״ש Shevuoth 1,5, and Ch.M. 75,23).

We have here the remarkable case that in contrast to the ordinary rule, the testimony of a single witness has some value in the sphere of civil law which it would not have in the sphere of איסור והיתר. Whereas באיסורין the testimony of a single witness if it is contradicted is completely invalid עד אחד בהכחשה ולא כלום in דיני ממונות it forces the defendant to take an oath. This is probably because of the gravity with which everybody must regard his responsibility for the lawfulness of all that he has in his possession, as well as of the meaning of the “judical oath”, שבועת הדײנים by which alone a person can protect his possessions against incompletely substantiated claims brought to the courts, by placing himself and all he possesses for God’s punishing intervention if his protestations are false (which, as has so often been explained, is the exact nature of an oath taken in God’s Name I.L.). A conception which immediately makes us understand why such an oath is not imposed for cases of קנס. For קנס fines, in cash or kind, only become payable as a result of a verdict of the court, and a claim for the payment of them makes no imputation of unlawfulness of the possessions of the defendant. We have already considered this oath against the claim of a single witness in connection with מודה במקצת and שבועת שומרין in Ex. 22,8 p. 353 et seq. (refer to it there).
על פי שנים וגו׳. See on Ch. 17,6. What there is declared for cases in the criminal courts דיני נפשות is here made universal and repeated also for דיני ממונות, those in the civil court.

In Gittin 71,a, the law is taught from the phrase על פי שנים עדים that מפיהם ולא מפי כתבם that witnesses can only give their evidence by word of mouth but not in writing and hence a dumb man cannot give evidence. How far this law extends, opinions differ. According to Rashi and Rambam evidence delivered in writing is altogether invalid. But according to ר״ת only of such, as dumb people or of dead people, who could not eventually give their evidence verbally. But normal people, as long as they are still alive, could, if necessary send their testimony in writing. The law is different with regards to שטר documents referring to debts, sales or gifts. Although these are given in the form of declaration of witnesses who sign such documents, the documents are accepted in court with the full weight of verbal declarations. עדים החתומים על השטר נעשו כמי שנחקרה עדותן בב״ד (witnesses who have signed a document are considered as having been cross-examined in court, Gittin 3,b, I.L.). For such documents are no independent declarations of the witnesses but are made at the request of the parties concerned, and so are recognised by them beforehand as proofs for and against them. They are essentially not so much כתבם written evidence given by the witnessing signatories, but a written proof of the transaction between the parties on whose behalf and at whose request they were drawn up (see Gittin 71a; Kethuvoth 20,a, תוספות there, and Yebamoth 31,b). According to Rambam (הל׳ עדות III,4) the admissibility of written documents by the courts was only an innovation made by the sages in the interests of business-life, an opinion against which Rambam on ספר המצות, שורש ב׳ very definitely speaks (see ש״ך on ח״מ XXVIII,12).

In Kethuvoth 20,a, a further law is concluded from the rule מפיהם ולא מפי כתבם viz. that a witness in court may only declare what is clear in his mind at the time if his being cross-examined, מפיהם but not that for which he has to refer to notes he has with him, ולא מפי כתבם, so that it requires notes to bring back to his mind exactly what happened (see ibid).
יקום דבר, (the “legal matter is to be established” I.L.). Cf. בעל דברים Ex. 24,14. refer to there.

V. 16. כי יקום וגו׳. As in the previous verse the evidence of a single witness making a charge against a person is deprived of any validity, the following case can only deal with the testimony resting on the declaration of two witnesses, as altogether, according to Sota, 2, a, the term עד if not specified as in V. 15 by the addition of אחד is always to be understood as the evidence of a pair of witnesses. ממשמע שנאמר לא יקום עד אחד באיש איני יודע שהוא אחד מה תלמוד לומר אחד זה בנה אב כל מקום שנאמר עד הרי כאן שנים עד שיפרוט לך הכתוב אחד But עד, as Rashi explains there לשון עדות it is not so much witness as evidence, legal validity can only rest on the declaration of two witnesses. The form of the singular with which the pair of witnesses appear in the text of the Torah, just justifies the demand for complete unity between the two witnesses in every direction, so that the grave responsibility for sinful depositions given by witnesses which is described here can only be brought into realisation if both witnesses have committed the crime: איו העדים זוממין נהרגין עד שיזומו שניהם (Makkoth 5,b and Rashi there).
עד חמס is a witness who misuses the power with which he is invested to give evidence by using it in an outrageous brutal manner against his neighbour.

סרה .לענות בו סרה, something which lacks the very first assumption of truth, which is through and through beyond actuality, is “foul”, from סור (turned away from I.L.) or סוה (rotten I.L.) see on Ch. 13,6. The very first assumption of the declaration of a witness to an act is that he was present at the place and at the time of the declared witnessing of the occurrence. Without being present at the place and at the time of the event which is to be proved having happened nobody can be witness of its having happened. If, in spite of that somebody does give evidence, his testimony is סרה, has absolutely no place in the world (is turned away from everything which exists I.L.) it lacks the very first presumption of an evidence, תסרה גופה של עדות, the fact itself may be perfectly true or untrue in itself, as it says in V. 18. עד שקר העד, he is a lying witness, שקר ענה, not what he says, but his saying it is a lie, he can say nothing about it because he was not there. Hence אין העדים נעשין זוממין עד שיזומו את עצמן the false witnessing of which it speaks here does not refer to the fact to which the witness is testifying but to the person who is testifying whose presence at the scene of the happening is disputed. מנה״מ אמר ר׳ אדא דאמר קרא והנה עד שקר העד שקר ענה עד שתשקר גופה של עדות דבי ר׳ ישמעאל תנא לענות בו סרה עד שתסרה גופה של עדות (מכות ה׳ ע״א).

V. 17. ועמדו שנו האנשים וגו׳. That witnesses should be shown up in court as עדי חמס could, according to the principle given in V.16, only be possible by two other witnesses declaring against them. The case of v. 16 כי יקום עד חמס וגו׳ must accordingly tacitly take it that two witnesses have accused the testimony as being סרה. Hence the שני האנשים, the two witnesses taken for granted in the previous verse. Their testimony is periphrased אשר להם הריב לפני ה׳, the men who have the הריב, who make the contention, the witnesses who arise to confront the other accusing witnesses with the contradiction:- עמנו הײתם i.e. at the time you assert you witnessed the happening you were with us in quite a different place, so that you could not possibly have seen it, and are, accordingly, in no way authorised to give evidence on it. It is clear that such an opposition to the evidence does not touch on the truth or untruth of the actual charge they brought, it only disputes their having had any right to bring it inasmuch as “we testify to your absence from “the place you assert having witnessed the occurrence”.

לפני ה׳: the precise place where they make their protest is given in the following לפני הכהנים וגו׳. So the לפני ה׳ appears rather to belong to אשר להם הריב and would then throw a light in a very significant manner on the function of witnesses which is here in question.

Jewish jurisdiction knows only one legal means of proof: the declaration of eye-witnesses. By the words על פי שנים עדים יקום דבר the Torah has placed the responsibility for the whole happiness, reputation, life and fortune of single individuals and groups of people into the hands of any two men who are impartial (i.e. unrelated and have no personal interest in the matter I.L.) and of unstained character. It is clear that the safeguard for such procedure at law and the guarantee for the life of the people ruled by it lies in the presumption that the conscientiousness of every individual can be assumed until and unless the contrary is proved. But this guarantee itself can only be guaranteed by the fact, and the all-pervading consciousness of לפני ה׳, of the Presence of God, that the whole of human intercourse and social life, as well as the administration of the institutions and laws which God has given for its formation and regulation are being duly carried on under God’s judging and ruling Presence, לפני ה׳. This fact and the tacitly understood reference to it is nowhere more significantly apparent than at every evidence given by a witness. If at anything, it is there that it is rooted with the full force of the consciousness that it is done לפני ה׳. In the end there is always the possibility of human eyes and human judgment being at fault. After all, every evidence, however purely objective its contents may be, does include a subjective assertion, a testimony regarding the witness himself, namely that he himself was present and witnessed the happening. This is an assertion concerning himself, and in every other case in Jewish law courts—except in matters of property or pecuniary concessions— such have no legal effect at all, neither for or against the one who makes it, and yet every עדות, that basis of the whole procedure of justice, rests on it. The Torah gives every witness the legal authority and the justified credibility to make the assertion regarding himself that he was present and did witness that which forms the contents of his evidence. But thereby the Torah places every witness לפני ה׳ Who alone can test the innermost hearts and feelings and thoughts and words on the scales of His justice and truth. Perhaps that is why Jewish Law does not make witnesses take an oath in the sense of our law courts to-day. The pronouncement of their evidence is itself a call to God under Whose Presence and Rule the witness places himself with his words.

Here, the coming forward of the witnesses is called ריב because they oppose the accusing witnesses by accusing those witnesses themselves. The two pair of witnesses form a fresh process on their own, with their declaration and counter-declarations are as plaintiffs and defendants in this fresh action. From that it is taken, that although here it is primarily speaking of witnesses against witnesses, עדים, the Gemora (Shevuoth 30,a) takes the ועמדו of our text and the laws which follow necessitating the close examination and questioning, to apply equally to all בעלי דינין, all parties who appear before the courts. For by אשר להם הריב these opposing pairs of witnesses are clearly designated as בעלי דינין, as two parties appearing before the court, and all what is said here regarding their treatment is considered to apply to all contending parties who come before the courts.

לפני וגו׳ אשר יהיו וגו׳, the witnesses with their declarations which they feel they are duty-bound to make “before God” are to come before the court “which is in their time” (see Ch. 17,9). Whatever higher or lower degree of spiritual greatness the judges may have if they are the most upright and best of their time, the witnesses stand before their court before God, and have to satisfy their demands before God.

הכהנים והשפטים. (See ibid.). This frequent combining priests with the bench of judges would bring home the fact that Jewish jurisdiction does not know two means of approach, a merciful gracious one, of which the priests might be considered the guardians, and a strictly just one which the judges would guard. Both, the priests of the Sanctuary and the judges of the law courts only serve the one and the same Truth of the Divine equity; and the grace of atonement which by means of the priest is achieved for sins is the same Divine justice as the atonement which the sentence of the judge wishes to achieve for the criminal. Both have the same object in view, both are to have the same effect which God allows His representatives on earth to bring about in accordance with their mode of action, and in no ways has He given the authority into the hands of His servitors to use the one way or the other as they might think fit.

V. 18. ודרשו השפטים, and then the judges find, after careful examination of the second pair of witnesses that it is clearly shown, והנה, that עד שקר העיד, that the first accusing pair of witnesses had come before the court with lying evidence, as their whole “declaration” (עדות I.L. see on previous verse) was a lie against their fellowman, as both of them, according to the evidence of the second witnesses, were with them at the time they asserted that the accused had committed a crime, or had entered into some binding agreements, at such a distance from the place that it would be quite impossible for them to have witnessed it—עמנו הײתם—and so were entirely unqualified to give such evidence:
