V. 19. ועשיתם לו וגו׳, then you, the nation as the fulfiller of God’s laws of justice, have to do to the lying pair of witnesses that which their secretly planned intention was to have done to their brother. We have already indicated on v. 17, that every assertion made by a witness implicitly includes, similarly to an oath, a call to God (that it is made לפני ה׳ I.L.) that he was present and witnessed the deed to which he testifies; how he thereby, just as by an oath, places himself, his person and his possessions under God’s punishing justice if the character of a witness in which he appears against a fellowman is a false one. Here God orders such an act of His punishing justice to be carried out by His deputising human courts of justice, by making them mete out to such false witnesses the same measure of suffering on person or possessions which they had wished to inflict on their neighbour. As a result of this law, no witness can come forth in a court of law with a charge involving the penalty of מלקות ,מיתה or ממון death, corporal punishment or monetary loss on somebody else without knowing that he is staking his own life, his own possessions against the possibility of its being proved that he is not fully authorised to make the charge. And every evidence involving possible capital, corporal or monetary penalties or disbursements in money or kind which, for any legal reasons— e.g. lack of being able to fix the time or place of the happening, so that the proof of an alibi would be impossible, or fatal bodily defects, טריפה, in the accused or the witness, which would make it impossible to carry out כאשר זמם—any evidence in cases of possible capital, corporal or monetary penalties or disbursements, which for any existing legal reasons is given not under the danger of such penalties ultimately recoiling on the person or possessions of the witness giving the evidence, is invalid and not accepted at all by the court. כל עדות שאי אתה יכול להזימה לא הויא עדות (Sanhedrin 78,a and Baba Kama 75,b). Such an alibi, i.e. a witness convicted of not having been present at the occurence is called עד זומם and the conviction הזמה.

But the Torah secures only life, body and possessions against an attack by false witnesses by this law of הזמה; of the penalty of life, body or possessions falling back on the false witness himself (see on V. 21). So that ועשיתם לו כאשר זמם only occurs at false testimony given in cases of מלקות ,מיתה or ממון, but where the evidence is directed against other legal disadvantages where on account of their personal nature and consequences the application of ועשיתם לו כאשר זמם is not possible e.g. מעידין אנו באיש פלוני שהוא בן גרושה או בן חלוצה, שהוא חײב לגלות (we testify that this man is the son of a divorced woman, or is a man who must be sent to a city of refuge I.L.) then the punishment of מלקות according to Deut. 25,1 & 2, is incurred. אין אומרים יעשה זה בן גרושה או בן חלוצה תחתיו או יגלה תחתיו אלא לוקה מ׳ (we do not say we make the witness the son of a divorced woman etc. but he is given the punishment of מלקות I.L.), and similarly in a case of מכירה בעבד for theft, and כופר, in a case falsely charged with his animal having killed a man (Makkoth 2a and b).

If the witnesses have to suffer מיתה or מלקות for their false testimony, they each pay the full penalty, but if it is a case of ממון, money, they divide the amount to be paid equally between them, משלשין בממון ואין משלשין במכות (Makkoth 5b).

Now in Makkoth 5b, the Halacha is taught: אין עדים זוממין נהרגין עד שיגמור הדין from which we learn two things: firstly that false witnesses only suffer the penalty that recoils on them if the sentence brought about by their charge has already been pronounced when they are made עדים זוממין, but not if they are convicted before their testimony has achieved its result in obtaining a verdict against the accused. It says in the following verse נפש בנפש etc. so that the נפש, the life of the accused must have been declared forfeited before their lives have to be forfeited in its stead. Their sin is completed only with the verdict. But then: that the verdict has only been pronounced but not carried out when they are convicted of הזמה. If, by reason of their evidence, the sentence had already been carried out when the עדי הזמה, the other witnesses appear against them, then they are discharged from the court without any punishment at all. The text of our verse runs: כאשר זמם לעשות לאחיו והרי אחיו קײם. “as he had planned to do to his brother” so that his brother must still be there, untouched, must have suffered nothing yet, you have only to do to him what he planned to do to his brother, not what he has done. Hence the saying לא הרגו נהרגין הרגו אין נהרגין (“if they killed they are not killed, if they did not kill they are killed! I.L.) and although the conclusion to be drawn from minor to major, קל והומר would make us infer that if bringing about merely the verdict brings punishment how much more then must causing the actual punishment to be inflicted do so, nevertheless, the rule we mentioned on Levit. 20,17 that אין עונשין מן הדין, that in criminal cases no punishment may be inflicted on the basis of mere inference, holds good here too.

This fact that even at false witnesses the infliction of the punishment ordered by the Torah is not allowed to go beyond the strict literal wording of the text, and the normal natural logical conclusion is not allowed to apply, and that here, at the crime of the false witnesses the אין עונשין מן הדין is stressed in such a striking manner that the false witnesses whose false testimony has already brought about the death of the accused, are sent away free from the threshold of the human court and left to the Justice of God, Who indeed has declared at the (related I.L.) crime of false oaths כי לא ינקה ה׳ (God will not let them go free I.L.), this fact can be the proof of the highest significance for the whole basis on which the whole institution of Jewish jurisprudence rests.

Loudly does this fact proclaim that the range and extent of a law given to the human court is not to be extended by human measurement, but that God stands above and beyond such a law and its application; that with the law and its application only a part of His administration of justice is handed over to the human court, and only as His delegates, and as far as the mandate reaches, has the court to administer justice, but that there where the power and authority of human courts end, the administration of the Justice of God Himself begins. Accordingly judge and witness stand לפני ה׳, as it says in our text, stand before God Who alone is the Founder and Source of conscience, of conscience which forms the rock basis on which the whole social state of justice really rests. But when conscience ceases to be God’s Voice—what then?

Rambam (הל׳ עדות, XX,2) takes this limitation: כאשר זמם לעשות ולא כאשר עשה to refer only to מיתה, cases of capital crimes, but not to cases of מלקות and ממון, for which view, however, proof is lacking. But that this limitation is not applied in cases of ממון and that at judgment involving payments הזמה could be effected even after execution of the verdict had been made, תוספות in B.K. 4,a, ד״ה ועדים would confirm, and indeed for two reasons, because in such cases the matter can be rectified by making repayments, אפשר בחזרה, and also because the rule of אין עונשין מן הדין might altogether not be applicable to ממון (cf. תוספות ibid, 2,a, ד״ה ולא זה).

In Sanhedrin 27,a, עד זומם is taken to be an anomaly, a חדוש, and from that, according to a view which actually is not accepted as Halacha, is deduced that, unlike a witness convicted of other sins, an עד זומם is not למפרע הוא נפסל, verdicts which have previously been based on his evidence are not retrospectively upset, but only מכאן ולהבא הוא נפסל, only from the time of his having been convicted of הזמה does he lose all future credibility as a witness, but all verdicts based on his evidence in previous cases stand. For as an anomaly, a חדוש its application is to be restricted as much as possible, אין לך בו אלא משעת חדושו ואילך.

The anomaly of course consists in מאי חזית דסמכת אהני סמוך אהני. For otherwise, in cases where two pairs of witnesses give contradictory evidence, שני כתי עדים המכחישין זה את זה, they mutually cancel each other out and the case to which the evidence refers remains in status quo, אוקי תרי להדי תרי ואוקי מלתא אחזקתה (only מדרבנן in such cases, any previously existing presumption in favour or against is annulled and the case treated as a purely doubtful without any bias one way or the other, Yebamoth, 31,a and b). To what extent both the pairs of witnesses who give contradictory evidence in a case can appear as completely creditable witnesses in any subsequent case is controversial (Baba Bathra 31,b). According to the one opinion, even for other cases all their credibility is upset, בהדי סהדי שקרא למה לי. But to the other view, accepted as Halacha, the presumption of their reliability for other cases remains unaffected. זו באה בפני עצמה ומעידה וזו באה בפני עצמה ומעידה. But in any case, in general, when two pairs of witnesses contradict each other, no credence is given to one pair more than to the other, but here at עדים זוממין the testimony of the first pair is completely upset and punishable by the testimony of the second pair that עמנו הײתם, accusing them of having been with them elsewhere at the time and place of the alleged crime or action, hence the question מאי חזית דסמכת אהני סמוך אהני (why should you believe the one pair more than the other? I.L.). And, as a matter of fact it seems to us that the reason given by the טור on Ch.M. 38 for—in contrast to הכחשה— the complete credence given to the עדים המזימים, and the complete disbelief and collapse of the עדים המזומים does not completely suffice to do away with the anomaly. There it points out that in cases of הכחשה the two pairs of witnesses contradict each other regarding some objective act itself אלו אומרין פלוני לוה מפלוני ואלו אומרין לא לוה e.g. one pair say A borrowed from B, and the other pair say he did not, in which case no greater credence is due to the one more than the other. But at הזמה the deposition of the second pair is not contradictory to the evidence of the first pair on which indeed it does not touch, but refers solely to the persons of the first witnesses of whom they assert that, at the place and time at which those witnesses testify that something occurred, they were with them far away from that place עמנו הײתם, so that they could not possibly have witnessed the happening. Against this personal charge their reply: “No, we were not with you, we were with the accused”, is as little to be believed as any other defendant would be in any other case where two witnesses testify that he committed some act and he replies “No, I did not”, as nobody can give a legally valid testimony on himself מפני זה האחרונים נאמנין כיון שמעידין על גופן של עדים והוי כאלו העידו עליהן שהרגו הנפש או שחללו שבת והן אין נאמנין על עצמן לומר לא עשינו כך וכך.

Unless we are mistaken one could object to this reasoning, as although it is true that in general nobody is נאמן על עצמו and nobody can testify concerning himself as to what he has done or has not done, still, regarding the fact of his having been present at an occurrence, the Torah has authorised everybody to appear in court as a witness to be believed regarding himself. Without such authority no testimony by witnesses in court would be possible at all. Every witness—as we have already remarked above—says, in the very first place, regarding himself: “I was there at the place and time and witnessed etc. etc.”. Also the testimony of the עדים המזימין rests on such a declaration regarding themselves: “we were at that time at a place distant from the occurrence reported and we saw that those witnesses who reported it were with us”. But if the Torah has authorised every pair of witnesses to testify to their own presence at an occurrence at a specified time, the question would always remain: why believe the one pair more than the other: מאי חזית דסמכת אהני סמוך אהני, and עד זומם would remain a חדוש, an anomaly. Which is why רמב״ם in הל׳ עדות XVIII,3, although it is accepted as Halacha that עד זומם למפרע נפסל still takes עד זומם to be a חדוש.

ומה שהבין שם פרק י׳׳ח ב׳ הלחם משנה דלהרמב׳׳ם כשאמרו העדים המזמין עמנו הייתם אתם והמלוה והלוה גם כן ולא היו הדברים מעולם דהוי הכחשה ולא הזמה ותמה עליו דכיון דאמרי עמנו הייתם למה לא יהיה הזמה עין שם לולי דמסתפינה הייתי אומר דלפי עניות דעתי עקר ההזמה הוא שאומרים דלא הוו העדים הראשונים ביום זה במקום אחר עם הלוה והמלוה או עם ההורג והנהרג ועל ידי זה אי אפשר להם כלל להיות עדים בדבר וסרה מפני זה גופה של עדות, וזה כונת עמנו הייתם כלומר עמנו ולא עם הלוה והמלוה וכו׳ אכן אם העידו העדים הראשונים פלוני לוה מפלוני ביום פלוני בבבל והמזימין אומרים ביום זה עמנו הייתם אתם והמלוה והלוה בירושלים ולא לוו זה לזה כלום, אין זה הזמה מאחר שמודו שהיו עם הלוה והמלוה והיו, יכולים לידע אם אתם היה שהלוה ביום זה פלוני לפלוני, מה אכפת לן אם ההלואה בבבל או בירושלים ולא הוי אלא הכחשה שמכחישין אותן שלא הלוה זה לזה כלום זה נראה לעניות דעתי ברור ואין מקום לתמיהות הלחם משנה ומהריב׳׳ל, ע׳׳ש.

V. 20. עדים זוממין .והנשארים are one of the four crimes of which the verdict and the execution of it have to be published to act as a warning and deterrent, ארבעה צריכין הכרזה המסית, ובן סורר ומורה, זקן ממרא ועדים זוממין, one who tries to entice to idol-worship, Ch. 13,7-12; the disobedient and gluttonous son, Ch. 21,18; the rabbi who will not conform to the majority decision of the Sanhedrin, Ch. 17,12,13; and our case here of false witnesses. At all these four consideration of the danger of the resulting spreading of such crimes may have influenced the severity of the punishment prescribed by the Torah, and therein also the reason for making them public. But just the fact that the Torah mentions the purpose of the punishment to be deterrent at these four cases and at these cases only, shows that otherwise, in general, deterrence is not the prime factor which lies behind the infliction of punishment by the courts. The Gemora in Sanhedrin 89,a, remarks that at all the other three instances, the warning is directed to the whole of the people וכל העם, וכל ישראל ישמעו ויראו but here it says only והנשארים ישמעו וגו׳, because not everybody is qualified to be a witness in court, דלא כל עלמא חזי לסהדותא, so that not everybody would have an opportunity to commit this particular crime, so that the warning need not apply to everybody (see on Ch. 17,13).

V. 21. ולא תחוס וגו׳ נפש בנפש וגו׳. In Ex. 21,23-25, and similarly in Levit. 24,20 where the legal consequences of actual injuries are discussed it says תחת ,עין תחת עין וגו׳, instead of, compensation, which, as we worked out there, is monetary indemnification which has to be paid. But here, where the injury was only attempted to be brought about, but had not actually been inflicted before the witnesses had been convicted of giving false evidence, there can be no question of indemnification for damage, loss, or penalties incurred, the consequences falling back on the witnesses is pure retributive justice; hence it does not say here תחת, but the more generalising term ב-. But inasmuch if the false witnesses have testified in a case of demanding damages involving money they do have to pay money, that too is pure retribution, as, if the charge of having caused the loss or injury of a limb were proved, the accused would not have to suffer the loss or injury of his own limb, but would have to pay indemnification, that is what falls back on the false witness who attempted to bring that about. But inasmuch as the Torah here goes on to explain the ועשיתם לו כאשר זמם by נפש בנפש עין בעין וגו׳, the indication would be given thereby that, as already explained above on V. 19, the ועשיתם לו וגו׳ only applies to evidence given by witnesses in charges involving מיתה or (נפש) מלקות or (עין וגו׳) ממון but not where other legal disadvantages would have accrued to the accused.

V. 1. With the last paragraph over the institution of witnesses, that basis of all the procedure of Jewish jurisdiction, the laws concerning the internal administration of the State is concluded. Now they are followed by regulations concerning the administration of the State towards foreign policy. First, verses 1-9 treat of the duties of military service, and the mobilisation at outbreak of war, how the nation had to arm for active service, then in verses 10-20 concerning behaviour in the war itself.

כי תצא למלחמה על אויבך. In Sota 44,b, a difference is made between מלחמת מצוה and מלחמת רשות, and by מלחמת מצוה only the wars expressly ordered by God for the conquest of the Land, or defensive wars if the country is attacked, are to be understood (רמב״ם מלכים ה׳ א׳, see ירושלמי ibid. and מראה פנים ibid). All other wars, even those undertaken not for defence against an actual attack by an enemy, but as a prevention of a threatened attack by weakening the enemy forces, למעוטי נכרים דלא ליתי עלײהו are considered as מלחמת דשות for which mobilisation may only be authorised by the decision of the supreme consultant body, the Sanhedrin of seventy-one members ומוציא (המלך) למלחמת רשות ע״פ ב״ד של ע״א, אין מוציאין למלחמת רשות אלא על פי ב״ד של ע״א (Sanhedrin 2,a and 20,b).

The laws following here (verses 5-8), according to Sota, 44,b, only apply to מלחמת רשות. This could perhaps be implied already by the introductory words: כי תצא למלחמה על אויבך. It is an attacking war, no war of defence against an invading force, “when thou goest out to battle against thine enemies”, you go out to them, in contrast to וכי תבאו מלחמה בארצכם על הצר הצרר אתכם (“When you go into battle in your land against the enemy”) of Numbers 10,9 (refer to notes thereon). And that they do not apply to the war of conquest of the Land is evident from the laws in verses 5-7 which refer to having already houses and fields.

וראית סוס ורכב עם רב ממך וגו׳, you are not to imagine that victory depends on the greatest possible number of combatants, and therefore you must furnish the largest possible contingent of fighting men, verses 5-7 discharge whole classes of able-bodied fit men from service in the army.

V. 2. והיה כקרבכם וגו׳. According to Sota 42,a & b, the following speeches were made at two different times. The demand contained in verses 5-8 for the return was made at crossing over the border of the Land, the encouragement to fearless courage (v. 3 and 4) at the beginning of the battle. פעמים מדבר עמם אחת בספר ואחת במלחמה בספר מה הוא אומר שמעו דברי מערכי מלחמה וחזרו במלחמה מה הוא אומר אל ירך לבבכם. According to that, the speech of verses 3 and 4 were delivered after the orders given in the speech of verses 5-8, and is only mentioned first as being the immediate continuation of the thought expressed in the preceding verse, לא תירא מהם. When the leaders of the Jewish State decide they have to go to war they must be conscious beforehand of the support of God in taking that serious step, and not make the main issue the size of their army; and, through the Priest, the representative of the Torah, are to awaken the same thought in the breast of every one of their soldiers, as being the one spirit that leads to victory. Rambam takes it in a different way (see הל׳ מלכים VII,2, ל״מ thereon).

ונגש הכהן. For this function a priest was specially appointed and consecrated by משיחה, being anointed for that purpose, he was termed the משוח מלחמה. According to Horioth, 12,b, this priest occupied quite the position of a High Priest in the national life. The five things which, according to Levit. 21,10-14 distinguished the High Priest among the people לא פורע ולא פורם ואין מטמא לקרובים ומוזהר על הבתולה ואסור באלמנה (look it up there) are also incumbent on him. Exactly what position he occupied in the מקדש, is, according to Yoma 73,a, not quite certain. Rambam accepts the view as Halacha that there he only functioned as an ordinary priest in the four priestly garments of an ordinary priest: משמש בארבעה בגדים ככהן הדיוט. On the other hand at the war he seems to have been invested with the eight high-priestly garments (Yoma ibid), בגדים שהכהן הגדול משמש בהן משוח מלחמה נשאל בהן (see Rashi ibid).

So that it is a servitor of the Jewish Sanctuary of the Torah, and indeed representing the national highest ideal of moral perfection (the eight garments I.L.) who has to accompany the nation to war and to pronounce the words of certain victory. Not military ability and knowledge of warfare, but the same Torah can be completely relied on with the same confidence for success in war as for prosperity in peace. It forms the basis for obtaining internal peace and harmony by victory in the fight over one’s own self and it ensures attaining the purpose of a justified war and gaining victory in battle. As the People of God’s Torah do the nation go to war, and it is a servitor of the Sanctuary of the Divine Torah, clad in the colours and garments of moral perfection, who, in the ordinary life of peace, also holds aloft the guiding light of the טומאה and איסורי כהונה duties, representing as a High Priest the moral ideals of general individual and family life, it is such a one who pronounces the declaration of the war. (והנה הרמב״ם השמיט הלכה זו דמשוח מלחמה אינו מטמא לקרובים ואינו פורע ואינו פורם ולא הביא לא בהלכות כלי מקדש ולא בהל׳ אבל ולא הביא אלא שהוא מוזהר על הבתולה ואסור באלמנה ככ״ג בהל׳ איסורי ביאה פ׳ י׳׳ז א׳. וכבר תמה על זה משנה למלך פ״ה מהל׳ כלי מקדש הל׳ ה׳ והניחו בצ״ע. והנה מנזיר מײז ב׳ משמע קצת דאין במשוח מלחמה מעלה דאינו מטמא לקרובים ככ״ג דאיבעיא להו התם משוח מלחמה וסגן הי מינײהו עדיף משוח מלחמה עדיף דחזי למלחמה או דלמא סגן עדיף דחזי לעבודה (ע״ש תוספות) ופשיט ת״ש דתניא אין בין משוח מלחמה לסגן אלא שאם היו מהלכין בדרך ומצאו מת מצוה יטמא משוח מלחמה ואל יטמא הסגן ע״כ ואם משוח מלחמה אין מטמא לקרובים ככה״ג תמוה׳ ההלכה שיטמא משוח שהוא בענין טומאת מת ככה״ג ואל יטמא הסגן שאינו אלא ככהן הדיוט לענין טומאה, ויותר תמוה הצעת האיבעיא דשבקא מעלת טומאה שהיא מאותו ענין דאײרי ביה ומביאה מעלת מלחמה, והכי הוי ליה למימר משוח מלחמה עדיף דאינו מטמא לקרובים או דלמא וגו׳ וגם היה לו להש״ס שם להורות דין כה״ג או לפחות דין משוח שעבר ומשוח מלחמה הי מינײהו עדיף לענין מת מצוה (ובמסכת שמחות ד׳ ל״ב איתא) מסוגיא זו היה נלע״ד קצת ראיה להרמב״ם מ״מ אין בכל זה כדאי לדחות ש״ס מפורש בהוריות י״ב ב׳ וביומא ע״ג א׳ בלי חולק וצ״ע ופלא הוא שגם נזיר מ׳׳ז ב׳ ד״ה ת״ש השמיטו תוסּפות הא דאין מטמא לקרובים מחמשה דברים ששוח משוח מלחמה לכה״ג (ע״ש וצ״ע.

V. 3. ודבר אל העם ואמר אלהם .ואמר אליהם. The כהן משוח מלחמה says exactly the words of the text בלשון הקדש (Sota 32,a and 42,a) so that it is not his assurances but the promises laid down by God in His Torah and given for all times. Just as the ברכת כהנים has to be spoken in לשון הקדש and exactly in the words of the text of the Torah. The משוח מלחמה made the speech and another כהן repeated it and explained it to the people, כהן מדבר וכהן משמיע (ibid 43,a). Hence probable ודבר אל העם and ואמר אליהם.

שמע ישראל, just as it is with these words that every Jew early and late daily brings home to his mind his allegiance to the One and Only God with all its consequences, so is it also the same thought and the same allegiance to the One and Only God before Whom in the moment of battle all other greatness and power loses all importance, and with the consciousness of serving His Will and confident of His support, in the weakest human breast, power and courage, calmness and strength grows (see Sota 42,a). There in the Gemora these four admonitions אל ירך לבבכם etc. are taken to refer primarily not to allow the war cries and alarums and clashing turmoil with which the enemy try to infuse terror and consternation to have any effect on them, but rather in their confidence in God to keep cool and collected against all blustering tumult.—אל תחפזו, whereas חפץ means a considered striving for some end, הפז always designates a senseless hurrying.

V. 5-7. ודברו השטרים. As already remarked on V. 2, these demands were made just before crossing the border out of the Land, and the משוח מלחמה made them also, and the officers explained them to the men, כהן מדבר ושוטר משמיע. Thereby the demand was characterised as coming from the deep innermost nature of the Torah, the Sanctuary of which the priest represented, but at the same time, it is one the carrying out of which must be done under the orders of the military officers. For, according to Jerusalmi Sota 8,9, every one who, for the reasons designated in verses 5-7 wishes to go home had to show proofs of the conditions in question. כולהן צריכין להביא ראײה לדבריהן.

Those who had a new house which they had not yet occupied, a vineyard the produce of which they had not yet enjoyed, had betrothed a wife but not yet taken her to their homes, had to march with the army to the border and from there go home again but from their homes had to render service behind the fighting line, bring up provisions, repair the roads etc. מספקים מים ומזון ומתקנין את הדרכים. But those who had occupied a new house, had brought a new vineyard to production or had brought a wife to their home, were, in accordance with Ch. 24,5 (refer to it) completely free from service for one year, they had not to turn out with the army at all, and had not to render any military service of any kind (Sota 43,a).

Clearly here the Torah brings, at the time of war, the peace-time tasks of life into prominence in their predominant importance; and inasmuch as the reason given for the return home is not given that if he should get killed in the war, the house might remain unlived in, the field unworked or the wife a widow, but פן ימות במלחמה ואיש אחר יחנכנו יחללנו יקחנה, it strikingly lays value on these peace-time tasks being accomplished by every individual personally and hence, for one who was just engaged in the course of carrying out any of these tasks in fresh fixed conditions has precedence over the call to army duty.

חנכו. The use of this term for the first use made of an ordinary house, gives the human activities, which houses serve, the higher consecration of a moral calling. — ,חלל, see on Levit. 19,24. By enjoying the fruit of the fourth year, or its value, in Jerusalem, the central city of the Sanctuary of the Torah, the vine-yard is thenceforth made over for חולין use, and this “profane-use” receives the stamp of a God-given, moral, concession, serving purposes which are holy to God. — ארש. See on Ex. 22,16. It is the procedure of the personal attachment of a woman to a man, קידושין, but she does not yet by that belong to the house of her husband (that is only after the procedure has been completed by נישואין, by his taking her to his house as symbolised by the חופה I.L.). This act of נישואין is what is referred to here by the term לקחה.

V. 8. ויספו וגו׳. The demand which follows here is made completely in the interests of the war itself, hence it is made solely by the officers, and explained to the men by them and the priest takes no part in it שוטר מדבר ושוטר משמיע (Sota 43,a). It is the demand that every man who lacks the physical courage and steadfastness which are required לעמוד בקשרי המלחמה ולראות חרב שלופה to stand firm and keep his place in the ranks at the shock of the charging enemy, and fearlessly to face the drawn swords (ibid) should go home, so that he does not infect others with his fears and panic. Another opinion (there), which is not accepted as Halacha, takes ירא ורך לבב to refer, not to lack of physical courage, but to a despondent faint-heartedness brought about by the consciousness of unatoned sins, המתײרא מן העבירות שבידו, and thinks that it was just to screen such as these from publicly disclosing their shame that the Torah allowed others (verses 5-7) to return for domestic reasons. As remarked, this opinion is not accepted as Halacha, nor would it be in agreement with the law quoted above from the Jerusalmi according to which all those who returned on domestic grounds had to produce proof of their assertions. But nevertheless מאירי adheres to this opinion of ר׳ יוסי as להלכה and limits it to עבירות של תורה שהן ידועות לכל.

V. 10-14. כי תקרב. The previous laws organise the army for open warfare. Now follow laws regulating sieges. It is made a duty always to offer first terms of peace, לשלום. If the town surrenders, no person and no property may suffer any injury whatsoever, they only were subjected to pay tribute and to be held in subjection. יהיו לך למס ועבדוך. According to the most general views expressed in ספרי and ירושלמי, and upheld also by הל׳ מלכים) רמב״ם VI,1) and רמב״ן, this applied in all cases, also to the inhabitants of the Land at the conquest. They too had to be offered peace and permission to stay in the Land in a tributary position, but only on the condition of giving up idolatry and returning to the universal human laws of morality and justice, the שבע מצות בני נח, the seven Noachian Laws. The complete annihilation out of the Land ordered in V. 16-17 was only if they refused to accept these terms of peace, and, keeping the polytheistic ways of life wished to assert themselves in the Land.

Thus it says in Jerusalmi (Schevuoth 6,1): שלש פרסטגיות שלח יהושע לארץ ישראל עד שלא יכנסו לארץ מי שהוא רוצה להפנות יפנה להשלים ישלים לעשות מלחמה יעשה גרגשי פינה והאמין לו הקב״ה והלך לו לאפריקי גבעונים השלימו שלשים ואחד מלך עשו מלחמה ונפלו: “Joshuah sent three heralds in front of him before he entered the Land, with the proclamation: Who wishes to leave the Land, let him go away; whoso will accept my peace-terms, let him make peace; whoso wishes to make war, let him make war! The Girgashi left the country and emigrated to Africa, the Gibeonites chose peace, the thirty-one kings chose war and fell. Hence it is recorded in Josh. 11,19: לא היתה עיר אשר השלימה אל בני ישראל בלתי החוי יושבי גבעון וגו׳, that, apart from the Gibeonites no city would accept peace terms with the children of Israel, which clearly indicates that such peace terms were offered to them. If then nevertheless the Gibeonites thought they had to take refuge by resorting to trickery, they must either—as the commentators explain—not have trusted the simple terms of peace that Joshuah offered, or have been trying to get a relationship that went beyond those terms, to make a treaty, a כריתות ברית as they themselves expressly said in their proposal כרתו לנו ברית, which however was definitely forbidden to Israel in Ex. 34,14.

It was further (verses 12-14) made a law that in the case of cities captured by force of arms, only the men capable of bearing arms were allowed to be killed, but women and children as well as all livestock and other property were not to suffer any injury or destruction.

V. 15. כן תעשה. This כן and the limitation which it introduces refers only to the care and forbearance ordered in V. 14, this is only to be exercised in cities conquered outside the Jewish Land. But the offering of peace as ordered to be made in Verses 10 and 11 was, as already remarked, commanded to be made also to the inhabitants of the Jewish Land. — הרחוקות ממך מאד, this מאד requires explaining. Perhaps it means to designate those living quite far away, but not those living near the borders of the Land.

V. 16. רק מערי העמים. In the previous verse where the cities are mentioned in connection with the foreign nations who are thought of only in their international relationship to Israel they are thought of as גוים, as externally closed bodies. But here where they are estimated according to their internal corrupt ways of life they are correspondingly called עמים.

V. 18. הא למדת שאם היו חוזרין בתשובה היו מקבלין : למען אשר לא ילמדו אתכם אותן; the annihilation was only ordered if, with their polytheistic depravity, they remained a pernicious enticing example to the people, but not if they were willing to return to the basic universal human laws of morality and justice (Sifri, and Sota 35,a, see above).

V. 19. לתפשה ולא לשבותה :לתפשה .כי תצור (Sifri), your purpose may only be to bring the city into subordination to your power, but never to make the inhabitants into slaves as war-captives, or, according to another version: לשביתה, to destroy it.

לא תשחית וגו׳, you may not cut down the trees round about the city just to destroy them, or rather you may not destroy them just to cut them down (scorched earth policy I.L.) so that your whole purpose is destruction. You may eat their fruit, yea, it is incumbent on you to keep them for food; ממנו תאכל is a positive command an זו מצות ל״ת :ואותו לא תכרות ;עשה (Sifri), by purposeless destroying a food-yielding tree both a positive command and a prohibition are trangressed.

כי האדם עץ השדה לבא מפניך במצור, for the tree of the field is the human being, the products of the soil are the condition for human existence, שחײו של אדם אינו אלא מן האילן (Sifri). (עץ השדה is the subject). אבן עזרא pertinently points out the similar idea in כי נפש הוא חובל (Ch. 24,6) where the millstone is called נפש (the life I.L.) because it is indispensable for the existence of the נפש. So the sense of our sentence, it seems to us, would then be:- thou shalt not fell the fruit-trees of the besieged city, for fruit-trees form the existence of human beings and are included in the siege, i.e. are part and parcel of what you are trying to obtain by the siege. And as little as destruction may be the object and intention of your siege, so little may you destroy the trees of the city.

V. 20. רק עץ אשר תדע, it does not say רק עץ אשר איננו עץ מאכל, that would only designate such trees which are altogether not fruit trees, but it says אשר תדע כי וגו׳ the judgment that it is no עץ מאכל depends on your special knowledge of that particular tree, it may belong to the kind of trees which do provide eatables, but it is still no עץ מאכל, cannot be reckoned amongst the trees which serve for providing food. It is so old that it no longer bears fruit or such small quantity that the fruit is negligible. Hence the law is given in Baba Kama 91,b, that דקלא דטעין קבא אסור למקצציה a date tree that yields a קב of dates yearly is forbidden to be cut down; and olive trees, the fruit of which is more valuable, if one of them yields even a quarter of a קב may not be felled כמה יהא בזית ולא יקצצו רובע (see כ״מ on הל׳ מלכים ,רמב״ם VII,9); and there it adds ואם היה מעולה בדמים מותר, if the value of the timber for building or other purposes exceeds that of the fruit it may be felled. Rambam explains לא אסרה תורה אלא דרך השחתה, the Torah only forbids a purely destructive felling, and further prescribes להקדים סרק למאכל (ibid) in every case where a non-fruit bearing tree would serve the purpose to give it preference even to a tree which only bears quite a small quantity of fruit.

But this prohibition of purposeless destruction of fruit trees around a besieged city is only to be taken as an example of general wastefulness. Under the concept בל תשחית the purposeless destruction of anything at all is taken to be forbidden, so that the לא תשחית of our text becomes the most comprehensive warning to human beings not to misuse the position which God has given them as masters of the world and its matter to capricious, passionate or merely thoughtless wasteful destruction of anything on earth. Only for wise use has God laid the world at our feet when He said to Man “subdue the world and have dominion over it” (Gen. 1,28 et seq.) see ל״ת רכם ,סמ״ג).

According to that, we believe that the sentences of our text here could have the following formation:- לא תשחית את עצה would be the general prohibition to destroy even a non fruit bearing tree לנדח עליו גרזן (“just to swing an axe against it” I.L.) where nothing but destruction is achieved or purposed.
כי ממנו תאכל ואתו לא תכרת would be the command to maintain and the prohibition to cut down fruit-trees.

רק עץ אשר תדע וגו׳ אתו תשחית וכרת ובנית allows felling old trees which produce hardly any fruit, and certainly non fruit-bearing trees for building or other purposes. But, according to Rambam (ibid) the extension of the prohibition לא תשחית generally to wastefully destroying anything is only דרבנן. (a later decision of the sages I.L.).

V. 1. This whole section, שופטים dealing with the judges and officials who are responsible for the administration of the Torah, now concludes with an institution which in a striking case calls those officials to clear themselves publicly from the suspicion of having been lax in the execution of their duties. We have already repeatedly seen how, under all property, goods or valuables, the safeguarding of which is under the protection of the state and the official representatives of the people, that of a human life is placed in the very first rank; on guarding the sanctity of human life the happiness and prosperity of the whole country is dependent. Now the procedure is given if it is established that a murdered body has been found lying in an open field in such a way which, as we shall see, appears to be just a derision of the officers of the law and so demands their justifying themselves. It says:-

ולא בשעה שמצויה :כי ימצא (Sifri). This institution assumes that the case occurs in times when, under the administration of the Torah-laws, murder was a rare occurrence, and the finding of such a body was a sensational “find” (מציאה I.L.). But in times, such as in the days of the decline and fall of the second Jewish State where the Torah and its laws had become so powerless that fatal stabbing was an everyday occurrence משרבו הרצחנין then בטלה עגלה ערופה, then this institution was no longer to be carried out (Sota, 47,a). Equally so it did not apply if the place where the body was found was one which was beyond the influence of the Jewish courts of justice, and so was the resort of bandits and murderers, כי ימצא פרט למצוי סמוך לספר או לעיר שרובה עכו״ם (places which were right at the border, (Sota, 45,b).

חלל באדמה נופל בשדה, each word has to be taken literally (Sota 44b). חלל לא חנוק ולא מפרפר, killed by direct stab but not by strangulation or any other means, and already dead when found, but not dying; באדמה ולא טמון בגל, lying openly on the earth, but not hidden in rubble; נופל ולא תלוי באילן, lying just as when fallen down, but not removed after death and hung on a tree or otherwise removed; בשדה ולא צף על פני מים, left lying on the field, but not thrown into the water after death and found floating there.

All the conditions excluded by באדמה נופל בשדה could be taken to show some endeavour to hide what had happened from the sight of passers-by, accordingly still some diffidence in the publicity of the deed, and not just showing complete disdain of the whole civil community and its legal representatives. In the same trend of thought could the reason for חלל ולא חנוק ולא מפרפר lie. The gaping wound immediately shows that it is a case of murder, the cause of death has not to be sought, it is quite clear, and if the victim is not quite dead when found, but only dying, the perpetrator of the deed must have wished to avoid discovery and fled, so again it would show a fear of publicity (and not be a case of sheer bravado and attitude of disdain of the authorities I.L.).

אשר ה׳ אלקיך נתן לך לרשתה, when God gives you this land so that you take the place of the previous inhabitants, it is under the assumption that through you His Law, His Torah would be maintained in the whole realm, and the officers of the law, (the members of the Beth Din I.L.) of each district are responsible to you, i.e. the representatives of the whole nation, for what goes on in their district. Jerusalem which, as the central city לא נתחלקה לשבטים, did not belong to any special tribe, but remained the possession of the nation as a whole, and was the residence of the highest representative court (the Sanhedrin I.L.) אין מביאה עגלה ערופה, if such a case occurred in its vicinity did not have to carry out this procedure. The highest authorities of the central city did not have to clear themselves of any suspicion of their having been slack in fulfilling their obligations (Sota 45,b).

הא נודע מי הכהו אפי׳ אחד בסוף העולם לא היו עורפין :לא נודע מי הכהו if anybody knew who had done the deed, however far away that witness might be at the moment, the procedure was not carried out (ibid. 47a). As soon as one knows that the perpetrator is known, the suspicion which in general could apply everywhere, falls away.

V. 2. ויצאו זקניך ושפטיך: the elders and judges of the nation, accordingly, members of the highest court of justice, מיוחדין שבשופטיך, three, or according to other opinions, five members of that body (ibid. 44b.), and indeed personally and not by deputy הן ולא שלוחיהן, although otherwise שלוחו של אדם כמותו, a procedure undertaken by a deputy is considered as having been done by the one who sent him (Ex. 12,3 p. 131, and XXI,37, p. 338), here, the prescribed measuring has to be done personally by a member of the supreme court. This personal attendance is expressed by ויצאו (and they shall go out I.L.). They, who otherwise are bound by their office to be always in attendance in the central city have “to go out” therefrom and betake themselves to the spot where the foul deed was done, the wording of the text excludes any deputising. But the reason for this function having to be undertaken by members of the Sanhedrin themselves and not by anybody whom they might authorise to act on their behalf lies in the nature of the occasion itself. For it is just their “delegates”, the officials of the subordinate courts, who function only as their deputies (see Ch. 17,18) on whom the occurrence has thrown the reproach of laxity in the carrying out of their duties from which they have publicly to clear themselves. The reproach thus falls indirectly back personally on the Sanhedrin itself, which accordingly has personally to introduce the act of expurgation.

אפילו נמצא בעליל לעיר היו מודדין שמצוה לעסוק במדידה .ומדדו וגו׳ (Sota 45, a). Even if the body lay quite near a city, which was then clearly the nearest of all cities in the district, the measuring still had to be done for the measuring itself was a mitzva. For this measuring by the members of the Sanhedrin themselves expresses both the superior authority of that supreme court, as well as the common equal responsibility of all the subordinate courts for all such occurrences, of which just the one is called on in this special case because it happens to be the nearest (see באר שבע on our verse).

ומדדו אל הערים. From the whole sequel it is clear that the Torah takes it for granted that there are זקנים, members of a Beth Din, in all the cities which come into consideration here, for it does not say in V. 6. וכל זקני העיר ההיא הקרובה but הקרובים אל החלל, so that it is not so much the city, as the municipal authorities which is being sought on whom, in accordance with the circumstances, suspicion of some laxity primarily falls, hence נמצא סמוך לעיר שאין בה בית דין מניחין אותה ומודדין לעיר שיש בה בית דין (שם מ״ה.) (if the body is found near to a city in which there is no Beth Din, one goes on measuring to the nearest city in which there is one I.L.). This would answer the question raised by תוספות in Baba Bathra 23,b. ד״ה בדליכא. Finding such a dead body casts a slur on all the municipal authorities in the whole district, hence the measuring to all county towns in the vicinity even if, as remarked above, it is quite evident which is the nearest. The words clearing themselves are spoken by only one of them which seems (see V. 3) to be the one most probably implicated in the matter. But this probability does not exclude the possibility of its being one of the others (cf. the commentator מראה הפנים on Jerusalmi Baba Bathra there).

אשר סביבת החלל, we believe that by this specification all distant places are excluded, and the measuring is limited to those cities which form the סביבת החלל the surrounding country, probably just the first ones that one meets in all directions from the body, but not those that lie behind those cities (see on following verse).

V. 3. והיה העיר הקרובה וגו׳. In Baba Bathra the rule is laid down:- רוב וקרוב הולכין אחר הרוב, that, in judging a fact according to the probabilities arising from the “majority” or the “proximity” conditions, we decide in favour of the “majority”, ואע״ג דרובא דאוריתא וקורבא דאוריתא אפילו הכי רובא עדיף, and although conclusions drawn from רוב (the majority I.L.) and those from קורבא are both legal from the Torah nevertheless when they are in opposition to each other, the decision is made for the רוב. This canon is applied e.g. in the case of a young dove unable yet to fly which is found between two dovecotes, ניפול שנמצא בין שני שובכין. If the number of doves in each cote is the same, the young dove is taken to belong to the nearer one, if the number is unequal it is taken to belong to the larger one. Although otherwise in disputes of “mine and thine” only positive proof not probabilities are decisive, אין הולכין בממון אחר הרוב, that is only when it is a question of changing the existing possessions of something from its present possessor to some other claimant of it, in such cases the rule is המוציא מחברו עליו הראיה (the onus of proof lies with the claimant I.L.) see Ex. 24,14. But here, where neither is in actual possession of the fledgling, and the doubt as to whom it belongs applies to both parties then either רובא or קורבא could decide. Applied to our case, nearness would also be decisive if no other city in the surroundings had a larger number of inhabitants, otherwise that city would be called on to function at the ענלה ערופה procedure, even if it was more distant from the place of the crime than the smaller city. According to this, the words קרובה and קרובים of our text must be taken to mean not only nearness in space, but nearness in the sense of greater likelihood (רלב״ג).

But we think that the wording of the previous verse אל הערים אשר סביבת החלל already excludes all cities which lie beyond the immediate surroundings of the place where the body lay, and only one of those cities has to undertake the procedure of the עגלה ערופה. These cities form the immediate surrounding of the place, and the supervision of their officials should ensure the safety of all the public ways of the district, so that their devotion to that duty is called into question by the occurrence. By this wording itself—as we believe—רובא דעלמא is excluded and the canon רוב וקרוב וכו׳ only applicable to that narrower circle (similarly to שכונה (the neighbour’s rights and privilege of preemption etc. I.L.) in a large city, רשב״א במשמרת הבית, end of דיני ײן נסך), and this wording would give considerable support to the codification of Rambam who does not mention the limitation ביושבת בין ההרים given in Baba Bathra 23b, in his הל׳ רוצח ט׳ ו׳. (Concerning its agreement with Baba Bathra 23b, see כ״מ ibid, and the commentator on the Jerusalmi quoted above. But especially concerning the extent of the concept of this canon see תורת חײם on Baba Bathra there).

ולקחו זקני העיר ההיא וגו׳, with the measuring the members of the Sanhedrin have concluded their participation in the procedure. What goes on after that is the concern of the officials of the town that was nearest to the occurrence, the Beth Din of twenty-three members which existed in most of the cities of the land. They take עגלת בקר (see Levit. 1,5. where the male calf is called עגל בן בקר), a female calf up to the end of its second year before it is mature enough to bear young (see ר״ש on פרה, I.). אשר לא עבד בה אשר לא משכה בעל (with which no work has been done, which has not yet been led by a yoke. At the פרה אדומה (the red cow I.L.) it says אשר לא עלה עליה עול, and there, even placing a yoke or a load to be carried already makes the animal unfit to be used for פרה אדומה purposes. But עגלה only becomes פסול if it has actually drawn by a yoke or carried a load or been used for any other work (Sota 46,a) עגלה also differs from פרה in that אין המום פוסל בה (ibid; see also Pessachim 26,b).

V. 4. איתן כמשמעו קשה ,אל נחל איתן, the meaning of איתן is hard (Sota 46,a) and there it refers to איתן מושבך ושים בסלע קנך (Numb. 24,21) (“Strong is thy dwelling place etc. I.L.) and שמעו הרים את ריב ה׳ והאיתנים מוסדי הארץ (Micha 6,2). (“Hear ye O Mountains, the controversy of God, and ye strong foundations of the world” I.L.) as proof of נחל איתן here meaning a hard strong valley and not as Rambam takes it, a strongly flowing brook, as otherwise the Gemora would have quoted אתה הובשת נהרות איתן (Ps. 74,16) as being more apt. Another opinion (there in the Gemora) takes איתן to mean old, ancient, as in Jer. V.15 גוי איתן הוא גוי מעולם הוא. For the etymology of the word see Gen. 49,24, p. 674.
אשר לא יעבד בו ולא יזרע, it is forbidden henceforth to cultivate the place. (Sota 46,b).

עורפין אותה בקופיץ מאחוריה ,וערפו שם, it is killed by a cut with a large strong knife or axe through its neck. שם תהא ,וערפו שם קבורתו (Kerithoth 6,a, Rashi), there it has to remain, be buried there, is אסור בהנאה (no use at all may be made of it I.L.) remains אסור even after the whole procedure with it is finished, an exception to the general rule that אין לך דבר אחר שנעשה מצותה ומועלין בה, that every object after it can no longer be used, has finished being used for the Mitzva it was designed to be used for, loses that designation and the resulting prohibition to use it for lay purposes (see Levit. on VI,3 p. 174 and Zebachim 86 and Yoma 20,a). And this anomaly could also give the עגלה ערופה—similarly to what we tried to explain at the תרומת הדשן—the meaning, by its permanent איסור הנאה, of its lesson extending beyond the moment of its actual procedure. (see on V. 8).

V. 5. ונגשו הכהנים וגו׳. In the presence of priests the officials of the city have to perform the washing of their hands prescribed in V. 6 and say the prescribed words of expurgation (V. 7) and then the priests say the prescribed prayer for atonement (V. 8). The priests assisting and functioning are presented in a complete list of their functions:- they are הכהנים, they who are to keep the nation in the “direction” of their spiritual moral calling; they are בני לוי, Levites, the elite of that tribe that ennobled itself in standing up for God in the nation (at the occurrence of the Golden Calf I.L.); they are they who were chosen by God לשרתו, to demonstrate in His Sanctuary of the Torah, by symbolic procedures, the rendering of all earthly conditions to His Satisfaction, and לברך בשם ה׳, there, in His Name, and with His Name to proclaim the blessings which are attached to the realisation of those tasks and resolutions which are expressed by those symbolic procedures; and finally they are those על פיהם יהיה כל ריב וכל נגע who, also outside the precincts of the Sanctuary, in the general national life of keeping the Torah, have to intervene and take part where justice has to be brought to bear between man and man, and who alone have to intervene where the “Finger of God” has to be diagnosed, where He has touched a person who is sinning socially with the mark of His Displeasure. All these considerations, the whole relationship of God to the nation, the whole recognition of the theoretical ideal and actual realisation of His Torah, with all the national and individual weal and woe which is attached thereto, all is made questionable by one single murder which the nation and its officials treat with indifference.

The life of every man, uninjured and undisturbed by his fellow-man, is one of the highest goals of the whole of God’s plans for Israel, and a murdered body thrown down on the soil of His Torah-land is the greatest mocking defiance of that Torah, is the greatest reproach for the representatives of it, and puts everything in question which the כהן represents. Hence the presence of the כהנים with the presentation of all their functions. The fact should not be overlooked that their assistance at the procedure only starts after the עריפה (the killing of the calf I.L.). By that the very slightest idea of the עריפה being of the nature of an offering is removed, and in this, too, it is entirely differentiated from the פרה אדומה where the entire procedure has to be done by a כהן.

V. 6. וכל זקני וגו׳ הקרובים וגו׳ (see verses 2 and 3). ירחצו את ידיהם (shall wash their hands I.L.) is clearly a symbolic act to express that their hands are clean from any direct or indirect blame for this occurrence, and from the lack of proceedings having been taken against the perpetrator of the crime.

V. 7. וענו ואמרו ידינו וגו׳. In the Mishna in Sota 45b, these words are explained thus: ידינו לא שפכה את הדם הזה ועינינו לא ראו וכי על דעתינו עלתה שזקני ב״ד שופכי דמים הם אלא שלא בא לידינו ופטרנוהו בלא מזון ולא ראינוהו והנחנוהו בלא לוײה and Rashi explains this sentence by לא נהרג על ידינו שפטרנוהו בלא מזונות והוצרך ללסטם את הבריות ועל כך נהרג (The Mishna in the Gemora runs:- “Our hands did not spill this blood, and our eyes did not see him”! Did it enter anybody’s mind then that the elders of the Beth Din were murderers, but what they mean to say is, that no man came to our hands and we allowed him to depart without food, and we did not allow him to go off without providing an escort”, and Rashi explains this by “he was not killed through us, that we sent him away without food and so forced him to turn highwayman, through which he was killed”. But it is evident from Rashi that in the Mishna itself it only said: אלא לא בא לידינו ופטרנוהו ולא ראינוהו והנחנוהו, the words בלא מזון and בלא לוײה are out of a ברײתא and the Gemora inserted them as explanation.

In the Jerusalmi the text of the Mishna is also quoted as saying only אלא שלא בא לידינו ופטרנוהו לא ראינוהו והנחנוהו and there the Gemora explains: רבנין דהכא פתרין קרײא בהורג ורבנן דתמן פתרין קרײא בנהרג רבנן דהכא פתרין קרײא בהורג שלא בא לידינו ופטרנוהו ולא ראינוהו והנחנוהו ועימעמנו על דינו ורבנן דתמן פתרין קרײא בנהרג לא בא לידינו ופטרנוהו בלא הלוײה והנחנוהו בלא פרנסה. The Palestinian rabbis explain the words of our text to refer to the slayer the Babylonian ones take it to refer to the slain one. According to the Palestinians it would mean they say:- “the murderer did not come into our hands and we allowed him to go free, we did not see him and close an eye to his guilt”. According to the Babylonians: “the murdered man did not come into our hands and was sent away without an escort, we did not see him and let him depart without food.”

At first sight one would agree with the Palestinian way of taking it, for in fact it is the murderer who is unknown, the victim could be quite well known, also quite well known where he came from, and still by measuring and considering the officials of that city are sought to which most probably the murderer belonged. Nevertheless, on further consideration, everything speaks more for the Babylonian way of taking it. Already the words of the text: ידינו לא שפכה (our hands did not spill etc. I.L.) seem to indicate that it refers to cleaning themselves from any blame in participation in bringing about the deed, rather than from any idea of their having been forgetful of their duty and showing leniency to the murderer after the deed had been done. If we consider further that, as we thought was shown when we discussed the conditions on V.1, the whole עגלה ערופה-institution only applies to cases where the victim has been left lying in the open as if in mocking defiance of the public officials, then there could really only be one case where such scorn could possibly be deserved, and that would be if the officials of the town had really sent a hungry travelling stranger away without giving him any food, and his hunger had driven him to try highway robbery in course of which the man attacked had killed him in self-defence; a case in which the slayer would be entirely guiltless, the slain one have at least some excuse, and the real blameworthy ones would be the officials of the city who had failed to exercise the Jewish communal duty towards the need of the slain man.

This same eventuality could also refer to the slayer (as the Palestinians would say I.L.) viz. that the neglect of their duty on the part of the town-officials had left him in such dire need that he had to resort to highway robbery and killed the victim of his attack. But the Babylonian Gemora could prefer to take the case primarily to refer to the slain man because then there would be the possibility of complete blamelessness in the actual deed, and also the Babylonian explanation seems more feasible as it puts the allowing to depart without food as the explanation of ידינו לא שפכה, accordingly as a possibility of actual participation in the causeation of the crime, and not, as the Jerushalmi does, as the explanation of עינינו לא ראו. So that according to the Babylonian Gemora the elders of the city have to make the impressive declaration: -No person is ever left by us in such straits that he must turn to crime to relieve his need!

For an explanation of the spelling שפכה instead of שפכו and the difference between the writing and the reading of the word see on Levit. 21,5, p. 591,592. Here perhaps writing ידנו לא שפכה in the form of the singular number might include the idea that they make this avowal not only for their own personal selves but for the community which they represent.

V. 8. כפר לעמך, as already remarked, it is the priests who utter this prayer for atonement. But as the priests do not function at the עריפה (the killing I.L.), but only assist the Elders at their clearing testimony and only after the elders have given that testimony do the priests make the prayer for כפרה, it is evident that it is not on the basis of the עריפה but on that of that testimony that atonement is hoped for and prayed for.

לעמך אשר פדית. Significantly at this prayer for כפרה, reference is made to the origin of the nation at the redemption from Egypt. ולקחתי אתכם לי לעם (and I will take you to be a people unto Me I.L. Ex. 6,7) was the avowed purpose for which they were to be redeemed. To build up a national life for God, to develop a civic life which in every phase is borne by God’s Will, penetrated through and through by the spirit of God, the whole positive and negative greatness of a national life formed under the rule of God in love and justice, that was what was meant by לי לעם, that is the “עמך״ to which the prayer for כפרה refers. The עם ה׳ when its representatives can say in its name, over such a murdered body: ידינו לא שפכה את הדם הזה, “even if a crime has been committed in our midst, the community as a whole is free from such crimes!”

Still deeper does a sentence in Horioth 6,a. take the meaning to be of this reference to the people redeemed from Egypt in the prayer on this occasion:- כפר לעמך ישראל אשר פדית ה׳, ראויה כפרה זו שתכפר על יוצאי מצרים, “this כפרה is fit to bring atonement retrospectively right back to יציאת מצרים the first generation redeemed from Egypt!” Whenever, at any time there is a Jewish generation that takes it gravely to heart, and is seriously perturbed if only one of its members has to take to crime through being in need, and its representatives can declare with a quiet mind, publicly before God, over the body of a murdered man the great statement: ידינו לא שפכה את הדם הזה “in our nation no man need turn to crime on account of being necessitous”, this triumph of the laws of rights and brotherly love taught by God in His Torah is such a great one that it ennobles retrospectively all the past generations out of the roots of which they have grown.

To that then the further thought attaches itself, the thought of the immortality of a national community, אין מיתה בצבור. In every national contemporary period, all the past generations which have already left this earth, are still present. Just like the fruit at the top of a lofty date-palm proves the good quality of the first seed-germ at its root, and in that fruit at the top the seed-germ at the root celebrates its victory, so is the nation such a tree having its roots in זכות אבות (the merit of the forefathers I.L.), and in the זכות of the latest grandchild the זכות of the earliest forefather celebrates its victory. Hence, as has been further worked out on Levit. 4,24, the concept חטאת שמתו בעליה cannot be used for קרבנות צבור.

ואל תתן דם נקי בקרב עמך ישראל. Cf. ואל תתן דם נקי (Jonah 1,14). “Place not an innocent charge of blood into the midst of Thy people Israel”, i.e. after the national community have declared themselves free from any even indirect participation in the crime, let not the consequences of the guilt of such a single isolated crime fall on the national community.

ונכפר להם הדם is not a continuation of the prayer, but is a promise made by the Torah, by carrying out this procedure of this institution the occurrence is atoned for. ונכפר is a composite form of the התפעל and the נפעל: the blood atones for the nation itself, and is atoned for through it, i.e. by the innocence which the procedure itself shows for the nation, and by the way and manner in which the nation have taken it up, and what they have thereby done and spoken in accordance with the prescribed law, atonement is achieved for them.

Inasmuch as כפרה is associated with the performance of the procedure, although עגלה ערופה in no ways bears the character of קדשים, it has nevertheless some phases of that nature, כפרה כתיב בה כקדשים. Hence it may not be טריפה, although, as mentioned above, a מום is no hindrance (Chulin 11,a; —this passage in Babli seems to have escaped the notice of the כ״מ on הל׳ רוצח X,2), it is already מחײם אסור בהנאה, indeed, from the moment it is brought down to the hard piece of ground, ירידתה לנחל איתן אוסרתה (Kiddushin 57a — that it remains אסור after it has been killed, see above on V. 4); the whole procedure must be done in the day time (Megila 21,b and 21,a); finally the עריפה of the heifer, quite similarly to the מליקה of חטאת ועולת עוף is effective לטהרה מידי נבלה (Zebachim 70,b).
It only remains now to try to find out what thought is expressed by the killing of the heifer in the נחל איתן.

When we consider that in the words prescribed for the testimony of the elders according to the way our Gemora (the Babli) takes their meaning to be, there is only a clearance from the more remote suspicion of an indirect participation in the cause of the crime but there is no denial of the nearer suspicion of some laxity on their part in not having taken proceedings against the criminal, then it would be natural to assume that just the act of killing the heifer was meant to show symbolically with what seriousness the Jewish community and its representatives regard murder and manslaughter. The heifer would then represent the slayer and the ערופה what they felt should have been done to him had they caught him. This explanation of the procedure would be alright if the wording of an Agada in the Gemora (Sota 46a) did not seem to take the heifer to represent not the slayer but his victim. For it says there: מפני מה אמרה תורה הביאו עגלה בנחל אמר הקב״ה יבא דבר שלא עשה פירות ויערף במקום שאין עושה פירות ויכפר על מי שלא הניחוהו לעשות פירות מאי פירות אילימא פריה ורביה אלא מעתה אזקן וסריס ה״נ דלא ערפינן אלא מצות i.e. “why does the Torah say: bring a calf that is not yet able to become a mother to a hard stony ground? God says: An animal that has not yet become fruitful is to be killed on a place that is not to become fruitful, and so atone for one who has been robbed of the possibility to become fruitful in doing dutiful deeds”.

But the Halachic discussion in Sanhedrin 52,b clearly sees in the killing of the heifer a symbol for the execution of a murderer: הוקשו כל שופכי דמים לעגלה ערופה מה להלן בסײף ומן הצואר אף כאן בסײף ומן הצואר אי מה להלן וכו׳ ע״ש (“all shedders of blood are compared to the עגלה ערופה, just as it is killed by the sword and at the neck so are these to be killed by the sword and at the neck etc.” I.L.). More closely considered then, the Agada in Sota could also have exactly the same view at base. If atonement is to be made for one who has been bereft of his future, such atonement lies not so much in realising what he has done to his fellowman, but in realising that at the same moment that he robbed his victim of his future, he robs himself of any claim to that of which he had bereft the other. He who bereaves a man of his earthly future, for him himself there is no earthly future any more, and even if he does not fall into the hands of human retributive justice, God’s administration brings about that which the arm of human justice had not been able to accomplish. Without a future he finds his end on soil that has no future.

According to this, in that Agada too, the heifer represents not the victim but the slayer who still lives, and demonstrates the consequences which have arisen for him from his act; every murderer at the moment of the murder becomes fruitless and useless עגלת בקר אשר לא עבד בה ולא משכה בעול (“a young cow that can bear no young with which no work has been done and which has not yet drawn in a yoke” I.L.) he bears no future and his work leads to nothing. The earth beneath him becomes a נחל איתן אשר לא יעבד בו ולא יזרע, and so he comes to his end. Similar to the words spoken to the first murderer: כי תעבד את האדמה לא תסף תת כחה לך נע ונד תהיה בארץ (“When thou tillest the ground, it will no longer yield unto thee its strength, unsettled and friendless shalt thou be on the earth” Gen. 1,12. I.L.).

V. 9. ואתה תבער. That which has been performed symbolically by עגלה ערופה has still to be done to the murderer by the human court if he and his deed ever come within its jurisdiction to be atoned for in the prescribed legal manner. For the procedure of the heifer in no wise exempts the court from that duty if at any later date the murderer is brought to court (Sota 47,a and b, תוספות Kethuboth 37,b).

V. 10. The section שופטים dealt chiefly with regulation of general affairs of the nation, the constitution of which was primarily demanded by the imminent civil settlement in the land. Now the section כי תצא brings a further number of groups of laws which primarily have the circumstances of family life and social intercourse in view, where the now imminent entry into the decentralisation and starting civic life naturally offer opportunities for excesses, and therefore make such regulations to be stressed in their special importance which are calculated to stimulate the spirit of keeping the Torah, of justice, brotherly love and the sanctity of morals in all the undertakings of the individuals who will then be left to themselves. Family-life, the behaviour of the sexes to each other, marriage-life, the relations of parents to children, as well as children to parents, all stand in the foreground. For after all, it is just the family-life which, on the one hand could be expected to suffer certain disadvantages from people living so close together, but on the other hand family-life only attains its full realisation at the moment when the living of the family is taken out of the hands of God’s immediate provision and transferred to the hands of the father of a family to provide for wife and children. At the head of these groups of laws there is a case which—similarly to the way that, at the head of the constitutional laws of social life (משפטים I.L.) the laws of human rights and marriage rights were taught by the treatment prescribed for criminals and the poorest of poor girls—by the treatment prescribed for a captive woman proclaims the sexual sanctity of every woman against the passion of men and secures her from careless misusuage. Similarly in Ch. XX.19 et seq. the general prohibition of לא תשחית, of every purposeless destruction and wanton waste, and in Ch. 23,10 et seq. the general command of exercising modesty and decency in words and deeds ולא יראה בך ערות דבר, ונשמרת מכל דבר רע are taught in the extreme case of the conditions of war, in which the lust of destroying and sexual licence tend to be given a free hand. That which even in all these extreme cases is made a matter of duty for Jewish consciences applies of course in a still higher degree for the conditions of normal life.
במלחמת הרשות הכתוב מדבר :כי תצא (Sifri) here it is not speaking of the wars undertaken for obtaining possession of the land of Palestine (see on Ch. XX.1).

כנגד אויביך :על אויביך (Sifri). This על does not mean an unprovoked attack on your enemies, such an act is not envisaged by the Torah. It designates a war against enemies who have shown themselves כנגד as the Sifri says, to have designs to conquer you.
וראית בשביה. According to most opinions it is speaking of a case where in the first heat of the conquest he had already yielded once to his passion. לא דברה תורה אלא כנגד יצ״ה (Kiddushin 21,b).

והבאתה אל תוך ביתך. Then his duty is, either to marry her after the proceedings prescribed in verses 12 and 13, by which she becomes a full Jewess and his legal wife with all the rights of every Jewish wife, or (v. 14) he has to set her entirely free. He may neither further misuse her in any way, nor keep her in his service, nor sell her or dispose of her to somebody else. According to another opinion he may not take advantage of her even in the first flush of capture, but must control his passion until after the treatment prescribed here, and then either marry her or set her free (see תוספות in Kiddushin 22,a).

According to Sifri and Yebamoth 48,a, the object of the proceedings prescribed here is to lessen her attraction, so that he sees her for a time in homely surroundings without ornaments or finery (it is well known that women expecting to be taken captive used to deck themselves out as attractively as possible I.L.) and has time to judge her character, and for her to give up idolatry and heathen practices (see below I.L.). For such a marriage, based solely on the dictates of passion, is by no means approved of, and the results thereof are warningly pointed out in the immediately attached cases in the following verse and then in v. 18, of discord in marriage life and unsuccessful bringing up of children which can be expected from all unions whose match-makers were not reason and suitability but solely passion.
ובכתה את אביה ואת אמה, according to Yebamoth 48,b this expression includes renunciation of the heathen customs of her parents’ home.

עמר :לא תתעמר בה is really a sheaf of corn, to bind the ears into a sheaf — התעמר בה to reap any advantage to oneself, to garner or harvest anything from her. Hence also as much as to say: לא תשתמש בה. You may not use her for any service at all (Sifri). Similar to והתעמר בו in Ch. 24,7.

V. 15. כי תהײן. The preceding יפת תואר-law gives, as an exceptional case for exceptional circumstances, the admission of purely sensual impressions as the guiding basis for choosing a wife. To that is now warningly attached the problem of relationships between husband and wife, parents and children marred by sympathies and antipathies, disagreements which by unequal inheritance are able to set at variance and estrange down through the generations branches of one family bearing the same name. In consideration of the endless variety of conditions and personalities, the Torah grants the father, as we shall see, wide scope of authority for the division of his legacy between his sons, but at the same time, by the limitations it does set, gives a hint to him to use that authority only with the wisest circumscription and greatest circumspection.

האחת אהובה והאחת שנואה. In Yebamoth 23,a, this אהובה and שנואה is understood to refer also to the marriage being approved or disapproved by the Torah, השנואה בנישואיה האהובה בנישואיה and in the כי תהײן לאיש the proof is seen that there can be cases of marriages which are forbidden, but nevertheless if made are legally binding and can only be dissolved by גט (divorce I.L.), e.g. חײבי לאוין (see Levit. on XXI,7). Moreover the greater or lesser degree of illegitimacy of birth has no influence on the rights of inheritance, even a ממזר מחײבי כריתות is a perfectly legitimate heir, with the exception of בן משפחה או נכרית (a son of a slave girl or a non-Jewish girl I.L.). But אהובה ושנואה is, we believe, meant quite generally loved or disliked and only by implication is meant to be understood also to refer to legal “dislike” by the Torah. Hence the Sifri teaches on והיה הבן הבכר לשנואה that the Torah says לשניאה (not שנואה I.L.) הכתוב מבשרך שבן הבכור לשנואה (the Torah tells us that if a man love one wife more than another the firstborn will be born by the lesser loved one I.L.) which clearly takes the שנואה to be taken as the one who is put in the background through undeserved dislike, similarly to Leah in comparison to Rachel. A שנואה בנישואיה whose marriage should really legally be dissolved would surely not be given the consolatory promise that she would bear the first son. Inasmuch as the Sifri bases this promise on the word לשנואה we can get the explanation of the difference between שנואה and שניאה and it gives the reason for this change in the form of the word. שנואה is a passive verbal form and states, taking it literally, that at the time of making the last will and testament the one wife was loved and the other hated. This affection and the reverse can have started just then in quite a later time of their association. But שניאה is an adjectival noun form, refers to a condition existing before the present moment, she was less loved from the beginning and just on that account was to be the mother of the firstborn to compensate for that.

In Baba Bathra 142,b, the Halacha is taught by the wording of the text וילדו לו that בן שנולד לאחר מיתת אביו אינו ממעט בחלק בכורה that the extra portion of the legacy which in the following verse is prescribed to be given to the firstborn son is only to be reckoned between sons who are born in the father’s lifetime, but a posthumous son is not taken into account in that division. If, for instance, there were three sons at the moment of the death of the father, one of whom was a firstborn, then that one gets an extra quarter of the estate, although after the death of the father another son is born who, had he been born in the father’s lifetime would have reduced the firstborn’s extra share to one fifth.

V. 16. והיה ביום הנחילו את בניו. This assumption is taken by the Gemora (Baba Bathra 120,a) to grant the father authority to divide his legacy amongst his legal heirs as he wishes, התורה נתנה רשות לאב להנחיל לכל מי שירצה. The כל מי שירצה nevertheless is limited to מי שראוי ליורשו to his legal heirs. Only among his legal heirs can he divide his legacy in unequal portions, or even make one of them his sole heir. But he cannot give anybody the right to inherit him who would not be legally entitled to do so. It says את בניו in the text. But the חלק בכורה is excluded from this authority given to the father. The father can in no wise curtail the heritage of the firstborn son.

את אשר יהיה לו. With very precise exactness the expression changes between here and in V. 17. The heritage which normally has to be divided amongst the sons is called את אשר יהיה לו. This term includes the whole fortune of the testator, “that which pertains to him”, “that to which he has a right”. That includes all that is actually in his possession at the time of his decease (מוחזק) as well as outstanding amounts that are owing to him which will increase the total of his fortune only after his death but are not in his possesion at the time of his death (ראוי). But the extra portion of the firstborn is only reckoned on בכל אשר ימצא לו that which is actually there at the time of death, but he gets no advantage over the other heirs in the division of anything outstanding to which they have the right to claim אין הבכור נוטל בראוי כבמוחזק (Bechoroth 52,a).

V. 17. כי וגו׳ יכיר. With this duty, the Torah recognises the right of a father and the credibility of a father to declare which of his sons is the firstborn: יכיר, יכירנו לאחרים נאמן אדם לומר זה בני בכור (Yebamoth 47,a). At the same time יכיר also excludes the case where the son was born only after the death of the father—it might be doubtful in the case of twins or of two wives of a man who dies before the children are born— such a son would not have the right of a firstborn as the father could not “declare” him: בכור שנולד לאחר מיתת אביו אינו נוטל פי שנים מאי טעמא יכיר אמר רחמנא והא ליתא (Baba Bathra 142b).

פי שנים, as much as two would get בכל אשר ימצא לו, see on v. 16. כי הוא ראשית אנו. See Gen. 49,3. It is the first child in which the father feels himself a father. If a human being is the highest of all earthly existences then there can be no higher acquisition than a child, that a man can feel in the noblest sense of the word feel justified to call “his son”. And if then the child, through which the man first experienced this lofty feeling is a child in whom the father is to feel that with it his own life will be continued also as a dutiful citizen, if ראשית אנו is a boy, then לו משפט הבכורה, then the child comes into the world with the unlosable right of the firstborn to the legal claim to the fortune of his father.

The בכור לנחלה (the firstborn for inheritance I.L.) is not identical with the בכור לכהן the sanctified firstborn treated of in Ex. XIII, and as requiring redemption in Numb. 3,40 et seq. For the latter פטר רחם is the decisive factor, for the former בכור לכהן .ראשית אנו is a son through whom a wife has first become a mother, בכור לנחלה one through whom a man has first become a father; and the condition of attaining motherhood is not dependent on the child living or having the ability to live, while that of fatherhood is only considered to have been attained if the child is living and has the ability to live. This difference lies in the concepts רחם and ראשית אנו. A father only sees אנו in a living child able to go on living and this proves itself in the feeling of loss if the child dies later on מי שלבו דווה עליו (Baba Bathra 111,b — see Gen. 35,18 for the double meaning of און). Both the characters of a firstborn can be combined in one baby, e.g. from a man who has never had children who marries a woman who has never given birth. But if the husband has had children before or the wife had previously given birth, then in the first case the child would only be בכור לכהן and in the second case only בכור לנחלה. Equally so הבא אחר נפלים (if the wife had had previous miscarriages I.L.) is only בכור לנחלה ואין בכור לכהן it is ראשית אנו but not פטר רחם (see Bechoroth 46,a).

לו משפט הבכורה. On this Baba Bathra 11,b, teaches the Halacha that the firstborn takes a double portion of the estate left by the father but not in that left by the mother. And moreover, as developed there, not only in the case of a one-sided firstborn such as from the case where an unmarried man marries a widow with children or a widower with children marries a virgin, but even in the case where the firstborn is the first of both father and mother, the inheritance right to a double portion only applies to the heritage left by the father but not to that left by the mother, for it says: לו משפט הבכורה: משפט הבכורה לאיש ולא משפט הבכורה לאשה.
