(cf. ויקח קרח, Numb. 16,1). והוציאו את בתולי הנערה, and again ואלה בתולי בתי means כשרי בתולי בתי, the vindication of the virginity of the accused by bringing opposing witnesses who oppose the charge of the accusing witnesses by הזמה (see Ch. 19,17 et seq.), by proving them to be false witnesses (Kethuboth 46,a; see כ״מ on הל׳ נערה III,12). — שמלה ,ופרשו את השמלה, everywhere is a garment in which something is wrapped up, hence also סמל the exterior form, שמלות the whole attire, the clothes, and לוטה בשמלה (Sam. I. 21,10), מי צרר מים בשמלה (Prov. 30,4). Shem and Japhet also took a שמלה to cover up their father (Gen. 9,23). Hence (Kethuboth ibid) מאי ופרשו את השמלה אמר רבי אבהו פרשו מה ששם לה, they explain the situation in which שמלה he had placed her i.e. they reveal his plot (or possibly literally “they spread out the wrapping in which he had enveloped her” I.L.) כדתניא ופרשו השמלה מלמד שבאין עדים של זה ובוררין את הדבר כשמלה חדשה. as it is explained in the ברײתא, the witnesses for the father oppose the witnesses for the husband and thus the matter is made clear like an uncreased new garment.

V. 18-19. ויסרו זה מלקות ,ולקחו וגו׳ ויסרו אתו וענשו אתו וגו׳ (Kethuvoth 46,a). This punishment is מלקות, just as above Ch. 21,18 at the בן סורר ומורה the punishment of מלקות is also expressed by יסר. Jewish judical punishment has only one corrective punishment, מלקות which we have already noted on Levit. 19,20 (refer to it). Here the מוציא שם רע is sentenced to both a money fine and corporal punishment. In all other cases the rule applies אינו לוקה ומשלם, both corporal punishment and a monetary fine are not imposed for the same crime. But in cases where both would be applicable, then לוקה ואינו משלם, only the punishment of מלקות is applied but no תשלומין has to be paid, or when damage to one’s neighbour has been done, in cases of גזלה ,גנבה ,חובל בחברו, injury, theft or robbery where the Torah expressly mentions payment of money, and also in such cases of false witnesses where the כאשר זמם etc. demands payment of money, then משלם ואינו לוקה then payment is exacted but no מלקות (Makkoth 4,a; Kethuvoth 32b).

This general regulation is taken from the words in the Torah where it gives the law of כדי רשעתו :מלקות (Ch. 25,2) which are taken to say: משום רשעה אחת אתה מחײבו ואי אתה מחײבו משום שתי רשעיות. In any punishable action there are two factors: the wrong done to one’s own self, the misuse of one’s physical and spiritual personality which is dedicated to duty; the wrong actually accomplished by that action, whether it be damaging the rights of one’s neighbour, or to the universal respect of right. Both are רשעיות, literally, wickednessess, lawlessness, the atonement for which and the restitution for which falls partly to the responsiblity of the human court. The subjective factor, the wrong done to oneself by the misuse of one’s powers is made good by enduring מלקות, the object of which is to achieve betterment (see on Ch. 25,2). The objective factor, the wrong done to somebody else, or to the general respect due to what is right is made good by תשלומין: restitution or קנס a monetary fine (see on Ex. 21,37). Now one could certainly think that at every crime which came before the court both these factors should come to be recognised by the sentence pronounced and penalties inflicted. But Jewish Law, the Torah, denies the human court the right to carry out the decision for the full atonement and in every case instructs it to intervene in only one of the two factors, either subjective correction: לוקה ואינו משלם מ״מ חײב כדי לצאת ידי שמים וכן מיתה וממון דקם ליה בדרבא מיניה וה״מ ממון אבל קנס פטור לגמרי ע׳ כתובות לג ב׳, ב״מ צא א׳), or objective restitution, משלם ואינו לוקה (see further on Ch. 25,2). Our case alone forms the one unique exception, מוציא שם רע לוקה ומשלם. In his case the flagrant wrong which he has done is to be brought home to him by judical recognition in every direction לוקה, for the subjective misuse of speech, transgressing the admonition לא תלך רכיל, although otherwise being a לאו שאין בו מעשה (see Ch. 25,2) it is not subject to מלקות, here by מלקות the whole disgraceful enormity of his crime is to be brought home to him; משלם, not תשלומין, the hundred shekels are not to compensate the young wife for the attempt to disgrace her by the shameful charge. It is the honour of the nation which feels itself injured in the disgraceful charge against one of its daughters and to whom the money has to be paid as a penalising fine. It does not say ושתו עליו מאה כסף לתת לאבי הנערה כי הוציא שם רע על בתו but וענשו אתו וגו׳. It is the nation which demands the money as penalty because he slandered one of its daughters, and the father receives the sum paid by the man from the hands of the nation “because he slandered a virgin of Israel”. Every father is a delegate of the nation to whom the most precious treasure of the nation is entrusted in the moral purity and innocence of its daughters; and when the father receives the money of the penalty paid by the calumniator of his daughter out of the hands of the representatives of the nation, it expresses the recognition that the proven chaste innocence of the daughter is the merit, in the first place, of the father, the merit of the home that had understood how to bring up and educate that pearl of the national wealth, the decency of Jewish Womanhood, in his daughter. Only if the father had already died did the daughter get the sum paid by her calumniator (Kethuvoth 44b). The sum to be paid by the מוציא שם רע is accordingly קנס, a fine, not restitution, and hence is a fixed amount, does not vary according to the individual, it does not say here: הכל לפי המבײש והמתבײש, it is a slander against the nation in one of its daughters, the slandering of a “daughter of the Jewish People” which has to be atoned for, hence אחד שהוציא שם רע על גדולה שבכהונה ועל קטנה שבישראל נותן מאה סלע (Arachin 15a) (“Whether the slander is against the daughter of the High Priest or of the lowest man in Israel, the fine is the same”).

נערה מלא דבר הכתוב ,לאבי הנערה, this is the only time that the word נערה is written in the Torah “full”, with the ה sign of the feminine. Only here, as indeed can be deduced from the sequel, if the sentence which is passed if the accused is really found guilty is the girl taken to have attained the age of sexual maturity, and קטנה, a girl in the years of immature childhood excluded. Everywhere else where נערה is written חסר without the feminine ה, a girl under age is also understood to be included. כל מקום שנאמר נער אפי׳ קטנה במשמע (Kethuvoth 44b).

ולו תהיה לאשה לא יוכל לשלחה כל ימיו. The original point of view of the Jewish Law could presume such a high estimation of the wife in marriage—as is apparent in the whole realm of the Jewish scriptures, and which we have already proved in an article “The Jewish Woman” in the Yeshurun Vol. X. which has been translated by Dayan Dr. Grunfeld in his “Judaism Eternal” taken from the Gesammelte Schriften—could take it for granted that the husband finds in his wife the pearl of his heart and the joy of his life to such an extent that it could safely and boldly entrust the decision to dissolve the marriage to the husband if that were not the case, if his wife were not that to him. The marriage which a Jewish husband could decide to dissolve—that, the Jewish Law could safely assume—was not worth being continued. And it was a sign not of progress but a step backwards in the development of Jewish culture when it became recognised as a necessity of the time and place to take away from the husband this one-sided authority (cf. on Ch. 24,1). Now the husband who, as in the problem of our text, behaved in such a disgraceful manner against his wife in order to bring about a forced dissolution of the marriage, from him the Torah takes away this authority for all time. As far as he is concerned the wife has to remain his wife for ever, he has no power ever to dissolve the wedding unless she wishes it.
This ולו תהיה לאשה לא יוכל לשלחה כל ימיו is also an example of a לאו שניתק לעשה (see on v.7).
V. 20. ואם אמת היה הדבר הזה וגו׳. The father had no witnesses to confront the others and prove them זוממין, or the opposing witnesses had themselves been proved עדים זוממין.

V. 21. והוציאו, out of the husband’s house to the entrance of the father’s house, as the Gemora (Kethuvoth 45a) says: כלומר ראו גידולים שגידלתם. The immorality of the young wife falls back as guilt on the bringing up she had received in her parents’ house, and is considered a disgrace for the whole nation. לא עצמה בלבד ניוולה אלא :כי עשתה נבלה בישראל כל בתולות ישראל ניוולה (ספרי).

לזנות בית אביה. The height of the gravity of the sin and depravity lies in the fact that the adultery occurred with full consciousness of its gravity—for עדים and התראה must have preceded it—by a girl not yet grown out of the protection of her parents, still belonging to “her father’s house”.

V. 22-27. כי ימצא. The following laws discuss the problem of conscious adultery, that sin against the fundamental institution of all human civilisation and society. It speaks of the sin having been committed after both factors of marriage have been carried out: נשואין after preceding קידושין (v. 22), and אירוסין (קידושין—verses 22—27) which indeed forms the spiritual moral basis of the whole marital relationship. We have already remarked above how the Torah punishes the sin against אירוסין (at נערה בתולה) with the worst form of punishment, סקילה, and just by that most significantly stresses the spiritual moral factor, uninfluenced by the physical one, as the fundamental factor of Jewish marriage.

בעדים :כי ימצא (Sifri), as already remarked on Ex. 22,3, the “finding” of a happening which leads to bringing the case to be considered by the court must be verified by the declaration of eye-witnesses, and in criminal cases must also have been given due warning, התראה must also have been given at the time the crime was about to be commited. (cf. Numb. 15,32 33) — ומתו וגו׳, as already remarked on Levit. 20,10, this punishment is carried out by חנק as כל מיתה האמורה בתורה סתם (see ibid). — גם שניהם, at all sexual crimes the punishment is the same for both the parties concerned, with the single exception of שפחה חרופה (see Levit. 19,20). — האיש וגו׳. If one of the parties lacks the qualification for punishment e.g. age, immaturity, having been forced, or mistake, ,קטן שוגג ,אונס ,קטנה, that does not exonerate the other party from receiving the punishment. Hence the repetition האיש וגו׳ והאשה (Sifri; Sanhedrin 66,b; Nidda, 44b, 45a).

את הנערה על דבר וגו׳: צ׳׳ע מאחר דקי׳׳ל דאין מיתה בלא התראה ואפי׳ חבר צריך התראה וצריך לקבל עליו התראה ולהתיר עצמו למיתה (עי׳ סנהדרין מ׳ ב׳ ,מא׳ א׳) ואם כן מה בכך שלא צעקה אפי׳ שתקה אפי׳ הרכינה ראשה אינה נהרגת כל שלא התירה עצמה למיתה ואמרה על מנת כן אני עושה (שם פא ב׳) ולולא דמסתפינא הייתי אומר ודאי כל שהעובר עבירה עושה מעשה די כשעושה המעשה המכוער תוך כדי דבור לקבלתו ההתראה והתירו עצמו למיתה. אכן כשהעובר עבירה אינו עושה מעשה אלא סובל אחרים עושים בו מעשה הרי הוא כקרקע עולם אף שקיבל התראה והתיר עצמו למיתה צריך הוכחה בשעת מעשה שסובל מעשה אחרים ברצון דאי לא כן איכא למימר אף שקבל עליו ההתראה והתיר עצמו למיתה לולא נאנס לא היה עובר. ואם כן מיירי הכא ששניהם קבלו ההתראה והתירו עצמן למיתה והוא עשה את המעשה תוך כדי דבור ואעפ׳׳י כן אי צעקה כשבא לעשות מעשהו עצמו למיתה והוא עשה את המעשה תוך כדי דבור ואף על פי כן אי צעקה כשבא לעשות מעשהו אינה נהרגת וכיון שלא צעקה במקום שהיה לה לצעק מוכח שברצונה נעשה המעשה אכן בפסוק כ׳׳ה אדרבא נתברר על ידי עדים שהחזיק בה כלומר שנאנסה לבא עליה אחר שקבלו שניהם התראה הא דלא צעקא אז אינו מוכיח שנתרצית קדם המעשה מפני שהיה במקום שצעקתה לא הועילה לה ואם כן חיזקתה שבאנס נעשה המעשה ואף שקבלה ההתראה אינה נהרגת כד נראה לע׳׳ד.
V. 24. התראה :כלומר ,על עסקי דבור :על דבר וגו׳ (Sanhedrin 41a).

אונס רחמנא פטריה :ולנערה לא תעשה דבר. The Torah makes no one responsible for any deed which was forced upon them. (B.K. 28,b). This concept of אונס comes also into the sphere of cases in civil law. Thus e.g. a condition of an agreement which was unfulfilled through superior force has not the same result as if it was simply left unfulfilled of one’s own free will. Nevertheless in such cases one has to differentiate between, say an אונסא דשכיח, or as it is called in Nedarim 27b, אונסא דמיגליא, a not infrequent prevention, the likelihood of its occurring might have been foreseen when the contract was made, and a completely unforeseen prevention—see ibid. and Kethuvoth 2,3).
אין לנערה חטא מות, not only אין מות לנערה but :אין לנערה חטא מות אונס is not treated as a חטא at all, has not even to bring a קרבן חטאת (Sifri).

כי כאשר וגו׳ ,כן הדבר הזה. As the reason for the preceding אין לנערה חטא מות, this sentence would say: Just as nobody is responsible for the crime of murder which someone commits on him (were he to agree to it, or even offer no resistence it would come under the heading of the sin of suicide) so, for the crime of adultery or for the similar crime of sexual immorality, no one is responsible if it has been forcibly committed with him. But by this comparison, sexual immorality is immediately placed on par with murder regarding its responsibility before God, and if it is self-understood that nobody may save his own life by murdering somebody else who is not threatening his life, as the other man’s life is worth at least as much as his; and he may not buy life with life according to the saying of our sages: מאי חזית דדמא דידך סומק טפי דלמא דמא דחברך סומק טפי “Who tells you that your blood is redder than his, perhaps the blood of your neighbour is redder than yours!” Thus it follows from this comparison of the crimes of lewdness and murder regarding responsibility that no one may save his life by committing the sin of sexual immorality, but that rather, for immorality as for murder, just as has already been said for idolatry (Ch. 6,5, אפי׳ נוטל את נפשך) the principle holds יהרג ואל יעבור, one may not save one’s life by committing one of these three sins. Hence also the rule: בכל מתרפאין חוץ מע״ז וגילוי עריות ושפיכות דמים, every means may be used for healing purposes except by transgressing the laws of idolatry, immorality and murder (Pessachim 25a; cf. Levit. 18,5).

But at the same time this putting the sin of נערה מאורסה on par with murder is instructive for laws of the latter. Of the former our text assumes that אין מושיע לה, that it was committed because “there was no one to save her”. That tells us that הא יש מושיע לה בכל דבר שיכול להושיע, were anybody there he is in duty bound to save her, if no other means were possible, even by killing the criminal, ניתן להצילה בנפשו. The same rule then applies to the sin of murder so that, if no other means are possible, anyone may save the threatened life of a person, by taking the life of the murderer. הרודף אחר חברו להורגו מצילין אותו בנפשו (Sanhedrin 73a).

This mutual learning the laws of נערה מאורסה from רוצח and רוצח from נערה מאורסה is expressed in the Gemora (ibid, and 74b) thus: רבי אומר כי כאשר יקום איש על רעהו ורצחו נפש כן הדבר הזה וכי מה למדנו מרוצח (that אונס is פטור for a נערה מאורסה is in any case expressly said, ולנערה לא תעשה דבר, so that this reference to a murderer can only be in general and be for the purpose of legal teachings of the law for murderers) מעתה הרי זה בא ללמד ונמצא למד (פרש״י אף למד) מקיש רוצח לנערה המאורסה מה נערה המאורסה ניתן להצילה בנפשו אף רוצח ניתן להצילו בנפשו ומקיש נערה המאורסה לרוצח מה רוצח יהרג ואל יעבר אף נערה המאורסה תהרג ואל תעבור (גי׳ הילקוט: וכי מה למדנו מרוצח מעתה אלא הרי זה וכו׳ וא״כ מעתה שײך למעלה וקשה להבין) (וצ״ע על אותה המדה כיון שבא על כל פנים ללמד מנא לן דבא אף ללמוד ועוד למה מקדים הקיש המלמד ללמד להיקש למד למלמד שהוא עיקר הפשט, ואפשר הוא הנותן כיון דהיקש מלמד ללמד הוא החידוש חשיב אתיא מדרשא חביבא ליה מקדים ליה וצ״ע (רש״י פסחים כ״ה פירש שהוא כמו והיה כעם ככהן שניהם שוין ע״ש, ועי׳ יומא פ״ב א׳ תוספות ד״ה מה רוצח).

V. 28 & 29. כי ימצא איש וגו׳ complements the case already discussed on Ex. 22,15 (refer to it there). The problem to be discussed here differs from that one, that there it speaks of מפתה and here of אונס, which would then also be why, similarly to מוציא שם רע, here he is given the additional ולו תהיה לאשה לא יוכל שלחה כל ימיו. At מוציא שם רע it says לא יוכל לשלחה here לא יוכל שלחה. There, up till now he had had the authority to divorce her, here that authority is taken away from him beforehand, as soon as she is his wife, perhaps that might be the reason for the slight difference.

V. 1. Whereas marriages forbidden on account of relationship have already been pronounced, חײבי מיתות בית דין וחײבי כריתות in Levit., those forbidden on account of physical deformities, birth and ancestry follow here (v. 2-9), whereby קהל ה׳, the sphere of the marriages of the priestly nation of God are to be kept free from unsuitable elements, just as within the same the marriages of the priests have their still closer limits. The former are the חײבי לאוין וחײבי עשין השוין בכל the marriages which are forbidden to every Jew by לא תעשה or עשה, the latter, the חײבי לאוין לכהונה. In front of them there are two forbidden marriages in V.1. which we would rather have expected to find in the עריות chapter in Levit. where in any case אשת אב, the first of the two prohibitions brought here, has already been given so that it would appear to be merely a repetition. So that the meaning and position of these two prohibitions require thorough consideration.

The Halacha is taught in Yebamoth 97a, that נושא אדם אנוסת אביו ומפו׳ אביו אנוסת בנו ומפותת בנו, that marriages which otherwise are forbidden are not affected by extra-marital relationships, that a man may marry a woman with whom his father or his son has had extra-marital relations, בנשואין איכא שאר באונסין ליכא שאר, “a legal union between man and woman establishes relationship with all its consequences, mere sexual intercourse does not. The previous chapter discusses cases of extra-marital affairs and concludes with one which lays down the law that in the case of אונס, of a man forcing a girl, he has to marry her and forfeits all right ever to divorce her. To that our verse could then come and referring to the verses in Levit. XVIII, and XX, which say ערות כלתך וגו׳ אשת בנך וגו׳ ערות אשת אביך וגו׳, stress the word אשת and repeat לא יקח איש את אשת אביו to say that the prohibition only applies to the legal wife of his father but not to אנוסת אביו ומפותת אביו etc. By this the spiritual moral character of Jewish marriage is strikingly proved. Only the spiritual mental union between man and woman, קדושין, forms the bond between man and woman with all the consequences of their relationship to each other, but not ביאה the mere sexual physical factor of their living together. קידושין without ביאה establishes שאר, but not ביאה without קידושין.

ולא יגלה כנף אביו, according to the accepted Halacha (ibid) this means כנף הראוי לאביו לא יגלה, a relation who is, in exceptional circumstance, permitted, nay commanded, for his father to marry, is forbidden to the son, even after the death of his father. This is the שומרת יבם של אביו, the childless widow of his father’s brother (ch. XXV,5). The father should have married her, or dissolved the bond between them by חליצה. But even if the father dies before he has done one or the other she remains prohibited for the son to marry, being his aunt. The position of this prohibition here may also be due to the case discussed at the end of the previous chapter. There it was commanded ולו תהיה לאשה thereby the duty to marry a certain person declared by the Torah. There is only one other case in which the Torah lays down a similar duty. That case is just יבום, and this marrying the childless widow of a deceased brother could be indicated by כנף, cf. ופרשת כנפך על אמתך in Ruth 9,9. But that the Torah could find it necessary expressly to limit the duty of the marriage of such a widow to the brother-in-law and reject its being taken up, if necessary, by his son, could be on account of the fact that, in certain other cases, the Torah does know of a similar procedure of the son taking the place which his father really should. Thus at יעוד (Ex. 21,9) and at שדה אחוזה (Levit 25,25).

V. 2 & 3. לא יבא ממזר וגו׳ ,לא יבא פצוע דכה וגו׳. A list of laws begins with these verses (2-10) by which קהל ה׳ the Jewish sphere of marriage is to be kept free from elements which would act against its calling, to become a קהל ה׳, a gathering called by God about Himself to further His purposes for the human race. These elements to be kept away are: firstly פצוע דכה and ממזר, they are in contradiction to the physical and the moral elements which constitute the very nature of marriage. Although in the preceding the principle holds that in the bond of marriage the spiritual element is to be in the foreground, that indeed the psychical factor without the physical, but never the physical without the spiritual, can form the establishment of a marriage, still verse 2, the prohibition of a פצוע דכה for marriage, at once declares that nevertheless the physical sexual is an essential factor which belongs to marriage. Just it, by marriage is to be elevated and ennobled into a morally free-willed life of duty, so much so, that for one to whom this is impossible entry into the sphere of marriage into קהל ה׳ is closed, just as then, the mutilation of the sexual organs in man or animal is prohibited by the Torah (see Levit. 22,24). פצוע דכה בידי שמים כשר (Yebamoth 75b) and such to be differentiated from סריס אדם is also called סריס חמה (ibid 79b).

ממזר, according to the accepted Halacha in Yebamoth 49a and Kiddushin 66b תוספות (ibid) is a child born from parents whom in themselves would be fit for a קידושין-marriage with others, but nevertheless such a marriage is legally impossible, אין קידושין תופסין, a canon which is laid down in Kiddushin (ibid) in the words:- כל מי שאין לה עליו קידושין אבל יש לה על אחרים קידושין הולד ממזר. These are the children of all עריות חײבי כריתות שאין קידושין תופסין בהן with the exception of Nidda, which although בכרת still קידושין תופסין בה (ibid 68a). On the other hand, where the father or mother are altogether unfit for מי שאין לה לא עליו ולא על אחרים ,קידושין קידושין, the child is not ממזר but follows the character of the mother, thus ולד שפחה ונכרית (ibid 66b) and so also נכרי ועבד הבא על בת ישראל הולד כשר אלא שפגום לכהונה, a daughter born from such a union should not marry a כהן (Yebamoth 45a).

ממזר accordingly represents, by his existence a sin against those laws by which God wishes marriage in His קהל to be elevated out of the sphere of simply physical association by that which קידושין expresses. So that a ממזר remains excluded from קהל ה׳, but may marry גרים in accordance with the canon קהל גרים לא איקרי קהל (Kiddushin 73a). But a ממזר is not affected by any other civic disadvantages, he is considered a legal son of his father in every direction בנו לכל דבר and also in the laws of inheritance he is in no way different to the other sons. (Yebamoth 22).

The etymology of the word ממזר is not certain. From the form it would come from a root מזר and that we can only find in Job. 37,9. מן החדר תבוא סופה וממזרים קרה and in XXXVIII,32: התציא מזרות בעתו ועיש על בניה תנחם. From this last quotation it seems to us clear that מזרות designates stars or constellations whose position in the sky announce certain sessions or periods. The first quotation is partly a description of the oncoming of winter. “From its hitherto (retirement) restraint the storm cometh and the מזרים bring on the cold. The breath of God brings frost and the wide surface of the waters solidify”. Here clearly again מזרים are constellations. Perhaps מזר is phonetically related to מסר to transmit, hand over. According to that מזרות and מזרים would designate means of transmission, and therby represent the phenomena regulated by them as parts of an order of Nature which is not innate in itself but merely transmits and furthers that which is transmitted to it by a Superior Power. Then, according to that מזר would be the term for everything physical, altogether having no freewill, and ממזר would be one who owes his existence solely to the physical order of things but not to the moral, to which his existence is contrastingly rather in opposition. He is a child of the מזרות in contrast to תורה. In Yebamoth 76b, the concept ממזר is explained as a composition of מום זר, as such an ailment which is “strange” to the Torah, a stranger who should have no home on the soil of the Torah, is accordingly not a personal designation but is a conception of a state which embraces both the masculine and feminine sexes.

לא יבא לו and similarly in V. 4. לא יבא להם, although everywhere else the rule is: כל מקום שיש קידושין ואין עבירה הולד הולך אחר הזכר, at every sexual union which is affected by קידושין and is not illegal the child takes the character of the father, still in the case of ממזר and the other פסולי קהל, even if the union is quite in order, the child takes the character of the lesser desirable order of the two parents, e.g. גר שנשא ממזרת הולד ממזר, the child follows לו, the פגום (Kiddushin 67a; Yebamoth 78a).

V. 4-7. לא יבא עמוני ומואבי. In Yebamoth 76b, the Halacha is given: עמוני ומואבי אסורים ואסירן אסור עולם אבל נקיבותיהם מותרות מיד the male generations of the men of Ammon and Moab, even after they have accepted Judaism, remain prohibited to enter the sphere of Jewish marriage throughout all their generations, but the women are permitted to do so immediately they have been converted to Judaism; the prohibition only affects the men of Ammon and Moab, but not the women. The reason for this Halacha refers to the reason given in the Torah for the prohibition: על דבר אשר לא קדמו אתכם בלחם ובמים, because they showed such inhumanity in not exercising the international humaneness in offering food and water to refresh the people, worn out and weary from their long wanderings in the wilderness who were marching past their territory, דרכו של איש לקדם ולא דרכה של אשה לקדם, but the public exercising of humaneness on such an international scale depends primarily on the men and not on the women. The women could not undertake it on their own so the reproach of hardhearted lack of humane feelings cannot be levelled against them. The change in the number used in the verbs should also not be overlooked. The charge of neglecting to offer refreshment is worded in the plural: לא קדמו וגו׳, that was a humane duty which fell on them all. The attempt to destroy Israel by a curse, however, was made by the head of the nation, the King of Moab, and so does not express the feelings of hatred of the individual members of the nation so much as that of the nation as a whole. This attempt at getting at Israel by a curse is accordingly recorded in the singular שכר עליך וגו׳.

It is the same general harshness, roughness and lack of humane feelings with which the later prophets also reproach Moab. In view of the catastrophe about to fall on Moab, Isaiah in XV, and XVI, refers to how all the neighbouring inhabitants, all the nations round about Moab cry out about Moab, כי הקיפה הזעקה את גבול מואב, how from far off one only heard tales of Moab’s arrogance and pride and blind fury נאותו וגאונו ועברתו, so that (ibid) he is advised, as the one possible means that perhaps would avert the doom about to fall on him, to turn to kindness, even in the zenith of his success and deal gently with unfortunate refugees. “Take advice” cries Isaiah to Moab, “Take thought, imagine the shades of night had already fallen in bright midday, hide the outcasts, betray no wanderer, let my refugees find a home with you; O Moab, be thou their protector from the spoiler; for extortion must cease, the extortioner brought to nought, spoiling cease, the oppressor disappear out of the land, and a throne established in mercy and kindness etc.”.

If, in accordance with the Halacha, the Moabite women had no part in the general lack of feelings of humaneness, in this special pride and arrogance of nationality it must be twice as highly esteemed when one remembers the type of men they lived with. And well could the flame of a universal love of humanity, bridging over all the differences of nations have burnt brightly in the breast of that noble humane woman of Moab, Ruth, the great mother of the family of David, and have had some part in the spirit which, in the tones of the harp of her descendant, sings of a future morn of a universal brotherhood of Man united around God, that descendant who has become the herald of that dawn:- מאי רות, אר״י שזכתה ויצא ממנה דוד שריוהו להקב״ה בשירות ותשבחות (ברכות ז׳ ע״ב).

V. 8 & 9. לא תתעב אדומי וגו׳. Although both these nations showed enmity towards you, you are still not to shun them entirely, you may allow them to enter into the sphere of marriage with you, but still only in the third generation. The grandson and the grandaughter of an Egyptian or Edomite who has become a Jew may marry Jews. Until then they may only marry amongst themselves or other proselytes (see V,3).
בנים אשר יולדו להם. See on V, 3.

Summarising the פסולי קהל given in verses 2-9 together, the Jewish Nation is to build itself up by keeping the physical and spiritual integrity of its sexual life (the איסור פצוע דכה וממזר) and guarding feelings of general humaneness and kindness, as well as fostering those of gratitude (the פסול עמוני ומואבי, היתר עמונית ומואבית מיד ומצרי ואדומי דור שלשי).

But since the Assyrian-Babylonian wars of conquest the original inhabitants of the lands of Ammon, Moab, Edom and Egypt have been driven out of their lands and have been mixed up amongst all the other peoples of the world, כבר עלה סנחריב מלך אשור ובלבל את כל האומות שנא׳ ואסיר גבולות עמים ועתידותיהם שוסתי ואוריד כאביר יושבים (Is. 10,13) so that the laws given here in verses 4-9 affecting the exclusion of certain nations have no longer to be recognised. Since that time, every non-Jew who becomes a גר, even if he comes from the present inhabitants of those countries is at once, for himself and his descendants מותר לבא בקהל allowed to intermarry with us. The principle applies that כל דפריש מרובא פריש (Berachoth 28a, תוספות Yebamoth 76b, ד״ה מנימין וכו׳).

V. 10. כי תצא מחנה וגו׳. The laws immediately preceding were purposed to ensure feelings of personal morality and of sympathy with mankind in general, as being the fundamental principles of the character which is to be formed of the Jewish Nation. Now follows in verses 10-15 and 16-17 two instances, קדוש מחנה and עבד שברח in which these two fundamental tendencies of the Jewish character are to be specially strongly marked.

כי תצא מחנה. Even when you have left your homes and the restricting influence of ordinary family and social life and find yourself in a military camp set out for war against an enemy (the Sifri stresses the words על אויביך, the Torah assumes you will only wage war against enemies כנגד אויביך, who have proved themselves to be such, from whose enmity you have suffered and whose further actions you must expect, against whose attack you have to protect your land and your families; (this axcludes any aggressive war of conquest) — so that even when you are in a military camp where the ordinary restrictions of morality and decency become so easily loosened, and the purpose of the war itself could tend to foster unrestrained coarseness and brutality, ונשמרת מכל דבר רע, you are not to loose your self-controlling inner inspection and keep yourself on guard against everything “bad”. This כל דבר רע, which in Sifri is referred to consideration of the ושב מאחריך in V,16 primarily to such excesses as שפיכת ,ע״ז ,ערוה קללת השם ,דמים which spurn the Presence of God, מסלקין השכינה and to לשון הרע, is taken in the Gemora (Avouda Zara 20b) in connection with the immediately following v. 11, quite specially to refer to all lasciviciousness which even in thought must be avoided, שלא יהרהר אדם ביום ויבא לידי טומאה בלילה. We are to keep away all indecent thoughts from our minds, and
V. 11 & 12. כי יהיה וגו׳ even in military camps observe the regulations given in Numb. 5,2-4, regarding sending out of the camp טומאות היוצאות עליו מגופו (refer to it there); even in military camps.
V. 13 & 14. ויד וגו׳, every trace of the unavoidable animality of the human body be kept out of sight and reminder.

אין יד אלא מקום שנאמר והנה מציב לו יד ואומר איש על ידו :יד (Sam. I, XV,12; Numb. 2,17): Sifri, יד designates a place, probably a specially appointed place to be kept for a purpose. Thus Ezek. 21,19 ויד ברא, to choose a place, or prepare a place, as ת״י translates it ואתרא אתקין “and prepare, make out a place”.
יתד, generally a nail, a woodden peg etc. here a sharp pointed instrument (a loy I.L.) for making holes in the earth. אזנך, as in Rabbinic Hebrew כלי זײן, with prefixed א (cf. לחם) : accoutrements.

V. 15. כי ה׳ אלקיך וגו׳. For your victory is dependent on the Presence of God in your midst, so that your victory means a victory of the Kingdom of God on earth. And this Presence of God in your camp does not depend on your external strength and bravery but in the first place on your internal bravery and strength over yourself, that you watch over yourself and “keep guard against everything bad”. That all naked animality of human beings, and everything that reminds one of it, is kept in the background, in your appearance, in your acts and speech, in your thoughts and feelings; for God does not lead in front of your camp, but “wanders in the midst of thy camp” in whatever sphere you are (see Sota 3,b). Therefore see to it that this sphere is a moral, holy one, let no “nakedness” in the widest sense of the word, ערות דבר, appear in the whole of your external and internal being, for only at that price is God your God, and wanders with you, and accompanies you and never turns back from doing so. מאחריך, you must go in front, and if the way on which you go is the right one, you can be assured that He will be with you.

מחניך, your “camps”, the word here is in the plural, probably to indicate that what is said here primarily for military camps is, of course, meant to apply to any “camp” to any sphere in which we may temporarily or permanently settle. All are to bear the stamp of pure moral way of living. All the places where we live, not just our synagogues and schools are not to lack consecration by thoughts of the mission of our life, the knowledge of which is to be drawn from the teachings of God’s Torah, thoughts which are to fill our minds at all times wherever we may be; driving out of them all that reminds us of the animal participation of our human bodies—צואה בהרחקה, במחיצה, בכסוי—keep all “nakedness” of the human body covered over—ערוה בבל יראה—so that without hindrance we can give up the direction of our minds to God and the teachings of His Torah והיה מחניך קדוש מקום חנותך תהא בקדושה וטעמא משום דישראל מהרהרין תמיד) בד״ת Rashi Sabbath 150a). For the undisturbed consciousness of our separate personal being and the morally free-willed loftiness of our spirit, temporarily wedded by the breath of God to our physically unfree body, that forms the very first indispensable basis for the mission of life to which God directs us. With it, all morality and every thought of a higher life of duty, stands or falls. So that just as the laws of טומאה and טהרה banish every erroneous conception of some animal-like lack of moral freedom from the symbolic sphere of the מקדש וקדשיו dedicated to the elevation and sanctification of our lives, so does this קדוש מחנה-law banish any actual appearance of animal-like corporeality out of the sphere of our thoughts and deeds directed towards God and our life of duty before Him; so that we remain conscious of the higher dignity of our spiritual selves, related to God and equipped by Him with God-like freedom of will, and give no place to materialistic erroneous ideas in which all morality and every life of duty become buried. Hence then the sentences in the Gemora בכל מקום מותר להרהר בדברי תורה חוץ מבית המרחץ ומבית הכסא — ת״ח אסור לו לעמוד במקום הטנופת לפי שאי אפשר לו לעמוד בלא הרהור תורה and all the laws concerning not being next to excretion or urine, and of covering nakedness, when reciting the Shema or saying prayers or even thinking of Torah matters which one may do everywhere except in bath-rooms and toilettes, and a real student of the Torah must avoid even standing in a place where there is dirt, as his mind is at all times full of his “learning”. Hence also the laws regarding decent behaviour בעשײת צרכיו and of washing the hands after having done so (Berachoth 22b et seq.). All are laws and Jewish habits of life which are meant to keep the fundamental truth of the dual nature of human beings ever present in Jewish minds. The deep importance and high value of these laws and customs are never to be more highly estimated than just in those times when Jews are called upon to carry on unswervingly their mission in life of demonstrating moral freedom of will in the midst of the most materialistic doing away with all the nobility of human morality which recurs from century to century.
Cf. Gen. 2,25; III,8 (ד״ה מתהלך I.L.); III,10.

On our sentences ונשמרת מכל דבר רע וגו׳ (verses 10 and 11) in which we are exhorted always to keep a strict watch on our inner selves and keep our thoughts clean and decent, Rabbi Pinchas ben Your, that man who was crowned even by his contemporaries with the palm of the highest nobility of morals, pronounced a most momentous saying:- ת״ר ונשמרת מכל דבר רע שלא יהרהר אדם ביום ויבא לידי טומאה בלילה מכאן אמר ר׳ פנחס בן יאיר תורה מביאה לידי זהירות זהירות מביאה לידי זריזות זריזות מביאה לידי נקיות נקיות מביאה לידי פרישות פרישות מביאה לידי טהרה טהרה מביאה לידי קדושה קדושה מביאה לידי ענוה ענוה מביאה לידי יראת חטא יראת חטא מביאה לידי חסידות חסידות מביאה לידי רוח הקודש רוח הקודש מביאה לידי תחײת המתים וחסידות גדולה מכולן שנאמר אז דברת בחזון לחסידך (תהלים פ״ט) ופליגא דרבי יהושע בן לוי דאמר ר׳ יהושע בן לוי ענוה גדולה מכולן שנאמר (ישעי׳ ס״א) רוח ד׳ אלקי׳ עלי יען משח ד׳ אותי לבשר ענוים חסידים לא נאמר אלא ענוים הא למדת שענוה גדולה מכולן “Learning Torah brings one to careful attention, careful attention to unimpaired moral vigour, vigour to external purity, external purity to abstemiousness, abstemiousness to inner purity, inner purity to holiness, holiness to humility, humility to fear of sin, fear of sin to self-sacrificing love, self-sacrificing love to Divine inspiration (the Holy Spirit), Divine inspiration (the Holy Spirit) to resurrection; and self-sacrificing love (חסידות) and humility (ענוה) fight for the first place. According to Ps. 89,20 where the חסיד is pictured as the man of self-sacrificing acts of love, חסידות would be the highest, according to Isaiah 61,1 where all future happiness is promised to the ענוים, people of selfless humility, ענוה would be the highest quality of Man. This ladder of the steps up to moral perfection, the first rung up which starts with the mental occupation of studying the Torah (“learning” as we call it I.L.) is worth the most intense consideration of the whole depth and instructive truth of its contents.

Here we would only once again remind ourselves that the abstemiousness, denying oneself even that which is really allowed, which is generally used to be associated with the nature of חסידות, but which in truth only corresponds to the concept פרישות, here only appears as a very preliminary step towards moral nobility, whereas the character of a Chassid, חסידות (self-sacrificing love I.L.) shines as the flower and fruit at the summit of moral maturity. As for the rest, most of the virtues which form the rungs of this ladder could be indicated in our text. We note זהירות from זריזות ;ונשמרת from נקיות ;ויד וגו׳ ,ויצאת וגו׳ ,ויתד וגו׳ from טהרה ;וכסית from ;כי יהיה וגו׳ קדושה from ענוה ויראת חטא ;והיה מחניך קדוש from רוח הקדש ;ולא יראה בך וגו׳ from כי ה׳ אלקיך מתהלך. If these characteristics do not appear here in the order of that progressive ladder we must remember that here it is not speaking of doing one after the other but what has to be done by all of them at the same time, and just thereby would proclaim the truth that on the way to moral perfection no preliminary step becomes superfluous when a higher one is reached, but that each one retains its value, yea, with the acquisition of the next step its own importance is only increased, and even at the highest stage it reaches its own most complete manifestation. For does it not say here that it is only ענוה that purest gem, the highest or second highest in the crown of qualities which leads to true יראת חטא.

V. 16. לא תסגיר וגו׳. In Gittin 45a, the case discussed in our text here is explained to be בעבד שברח מחוצה לארץ לארץ הכתוב מדבר that of a non-Jewish slave who had fled from a Jewish master living outside the land of Israel into the land of Israel. To such a one the Jewish officials have to give protection and care. They have—according to the way the Rambam takes it (Avadim V, III,10) which is also accepted by the י״ד)— in any case to give him his freedom, and place the alternative before the master, either to give the slave a certificate of freedom against an I.O.U. for his value, or in case of refusal the court has the power for expropriation, simply to dispossess the owner of all right of possession and set the slave free. Then, if the ex-slave wishes to become a גר צדק he attains the full rights of a Jewish citizen and is under the special care of the public protection of rights and good-will. In conformation with the regulation is the law that a person emigrating from the land of Israel is not authorised to take his slaves with him against their will, and that if a person were to sell a slave to be taken out of the land, that slave automatically becomes free המוכר עבדו לח״ל יצא בן חורין (Gittin 43b).

We have already had the opportunity in Gen. at end of notes on XIV,14, and Ex. 12,44 to elucidate the legal position of non-Jewish slaves in Jewish homes and in the Jewish State. They become members of the Jewish confederation and participate to a certain extent in the moral nobility of having to keep the mitzvas of the Torah. We understand the tremendous extent of the contrast between the conception of human values and human rights in a land under the regime of God’s Torah which is extended even to a non-Jewish slave and that which was accorded to the idea of slaves and slavery everywhere else in the world to which the עבד כנעני of a Jew would also be subjected to outside the land of Israel. We believe that just as we saw in the laws given in verses 11-15 the fostering of the moral factor of the Jewish character, so we can see in these verses 16,17 a fostering of the humane feelings of sympathy for all mankind, both of which, according to the preceding laws, were to form the predominant traits of the national Jewish character.

לא תוננו (see Ex. 22,20; Levit. 25,17). (בערכין כ״ט א׳ מײרי לרב ביבי קרא דבטוב לו לא תוננו בגר תושב לכאורה הײנו אליבא דת״ק דברײתא גטין מ״ה א׳ שנדחה מפני קושית ר׳ יאשי׳ אלא שיש לומר דלרב ביבי מײרי בעבד כנעני של נכרי שברח מח״ל לארץ שהוא נכרי גמור וכשניתן לו רשות לשבת בארץ הוא בתנאי שלא יעבוד עבודה זרה ואם כן הוא גר תושב דהא סתם עבד כנעני של ישראל כבר ישנו במצות כאשה וכשנעשה בן חורין הרי הוא גר צדק, ונראה דסברת רב ביבי היא כתרגום אונקלס עבד עממין, כלומר עבד כנעני של נכרים וזהו כוונת רש״י בפירושו לתורה כתרג׳ (כלומר עבד כנעני של נכדי) דבר אחר אפילו עבד כנעני של ישראל עכ״ל דלא כרא״מ דס״ל דפירוש ראשון של רש׳׳י הוא שראל שנמכר לנכרי והנה מימרא דר׳ שמעון בן אלעזר שם דאין מקבלין גר תושב אלא בזמן שהיובל נוהג היא אליבא דהלכתא מאין חולק וכן פסק הרמב״ם (הל׳ שמיטה י׳ ט׳ והל׳ ע״ז י׳ ו׳) והלכה זו בנדה על ג״ש דטוב טוב דרב ביבי ע״ש ואם כן צ״ל דקרא סתמא כתיב עבד אל אדוניו ומײרי בין בעבד כנעני של נכרי בין בעבד כנעני של ישראל כנלענ״ד).
Verses 18,19 are again in close connection with those moral factors, and 20,21 contain an adjustment of those universal relations to mankind in general.

V. 18. לא תהיה וגו׳. Just as קדוש is the complete surrender to what is morally lofty and good so is קדש the surrender to what is morally low and bad. An analogy can be found in the root כבד, which as כבוד designates the impression of the spiritual moral content, and as כבד the impression of the material content. Immorality is every sexual intercourse which has not had the dedication of קידושין, hence also the so-called marriages of people who are not eligible for שאין קידושין תופסין ,קידושין בהם, as then Onkelos translates the concept קדשה and קדש by concrete examples אתתא מבנת ישראל לגבר עבד and לא יסב גברא מבני ישראל אתתא אמתא. The wording of our text demands the same degree of chaste morality in its sons as it does in its daughters, and in their keeping such chaste morality recognises the justification for the name “children of Israel”. בנות ישראל and בני ישראל, “daughters of Israel”, “sons of Israel” such names should for all time exclude any trace of immorality. — thus Sanhedrin 82a, Malachi 2,11, כי חלל יהודה קודש ה׳, זו זונה וכן הוא אומר לא יהיה קדש ופרש״י וז״ל קדש מפקיר קדושתו והולך לרדוף זונות, קדשה מחללת קדושתה וכן חלל מחלל קדושתו.

V. 19. מחיר כלב .לא תביא וגו׳, if one had exchanged a dog for something that could be used as it is for an offering or for any use in the Temple, such an object is called מחיר כלב. It as well as a harlot’s wage are only prohibited to be used in the Sanctuary in their original condition, but if exchanged for something else, or the young of such an animal would be accepted שניהם ולא ולדותיהן ולא שינוײהן (Temura 30b). Sexual morality is one of the cardinal virtues, to nurture which the Jewish Sanctuary of God is dedicated. Nothing that, like אתנן זונה comes from an act that is directly in opposition to it, or, like מחיר כלב, which is reminiscent of a similar characteristic, is to have access to it. But regarding the latter, one be doubtful whether it is this characteristic which is the reason for its exclusion from the Temple. In the תנ״ך it is not this tendency for which dog or dogs are used as types. It is rather always a contempt for society manners or abjectness, villany for which כלב or כלבים are used figuratively. So that it is not impossible that here too it is the idea of this social factor which is the reason for the prohibition of מחיר כלב. Yea this seems the more likely reason, as the גם שניהם of our text implies a difference in the ideas represented by the wage of a harlot, and the exchange of a dog. Then, by the two prohibitions the representation of sexual and social depravity would be banned from the realm of the Sanctuary.

V. 20. לא תשיך וגו׳ is the prohibition to the לוה, the borrower, not to give interest for loans (Baba Mezia 61,a; 75,a). This lies in the Hiphil form. נשך in the Kal, literally, biting, means “to break a piece off” and designates taking interest. Hence in Hiphil: to pay interest. And indeed here by נשך כסף וגו׳ נשך כל דבר וגו׳ the concept of interest is extended to its full extent, so that it includes any advantage whatsoever that the lender gets from the borrower as a result of the loan, so that he may not even send the borrower, as such, on a message or to obtain information for him. דיש רבית דברים לא יאמר לו דע כי (נ״א אם) בא איש ממקום פלוני yea, it even goes so far as to include the debtor courteously forestalling the greeting of the creditor if ordinarily he would not do so: מנין לנושה בחבירו מנה ואינו רגיל להקדים לו שלום שאסור להקדים לו שלום ת״ל נשך כל דבר אשר ישך אפילו דבור אסור (B.M. 75a).

We have already fully elucidated the prohibition of interest on Ex. 22,24 and Levit. 25,36. We recognised the fact that charging interest at the usual normal rates can in no way be considered as anything wrong in itself, contraverting the idea of what is right and just. But that it rather belongs to the sphere of those great Jewish acts of acknowledgment which are incumbent on Jews to perform, such as יובל ,שמיטה ,שביעית ,שבת by which God is looked on and avowed as the real owner of all Jewish possessions. We tried to show the remarkable position which the prohibition of interest occupied and its momentous consequences for the whole business and social intercourse of the nation, for which the founding of Israel as “the People of God” was intended to prepare the way. We have also already remarked how just the two laws, that on the one hand not only the charging of interest, but with quite equal severity the paying of it was forbidden, and on the other hand both taking and paying interest is permitted to be done to non-Jews, definitely removed the רבית-prohibition from the idea of its being wrong in itself, and characterised it as a great act of acknowledgment of God, an acknowledgment which would be opposed equally by giving or taking interest.

According to that, we also understand why not only a repeated injunction against רבית, but quite specially its two characteristic laws were kept for this compendium for the settling in the Land. For just with that settling the real business and social traffic began, for which the duty to give loans without interest, but especially the prohibition of any and every kind of interest were of the most fundamental importance, and calculated to foster that spirit, under the influence of which alone the general social conditions would assume a form deserving of general happiness and God’s blessing.

V. 21. (ספרי) קבע לו הכתוב ברכה בשליחות ידו :בכל משלח ידך, “a blessing is promised on everything to which you lay your hand”. Physical causes are not sufficient to effect the blessing. A hand guided by the spirit of this law to God acknowledging feelings of brotherly affection in all its actions brings the blessing of heaven on all that it does and accomplishes.

V. 22. כי תדר וגו׳. This law concerning vows comes in close connection with the preceding. The prohibition of רבית (interest I.L.) rests on the recognition of the fact that everything that we call our own really belongs to God, as the real Owner and Master Who has the right to dispose of it as He wishes. To that the law of vows is added because through it God has a still more special right even to that which He has given us the permission to dispose of as we wish; and to that which is vowed fulfilment is made obligatory, although as a rule, abstaining from making any vows is more pleasing to God. The law concerning vows has already formed a special chapter by itself in Numb. XXX (refer to it). The complementing laws here:- לא תאחר לשלמו and וכי תחדל לנדר would all the more have been reserved for this compendium because, on account of the approaching distance from the Sanctuary at which they would be living, a great number of the נדרים ונדבות which could only be fulfilled in the Temple itself would be more precarious and more opportunity given for a sinful deferment in paying them. For the law given here speaks not so much of נדרי איסור (vowing to abstain from something I.L.) to which the Ch. XXX in Numbers is devoted, as primarily of נדרי הקדש, the fulfilment of which, in most cases—with the exception of נדרי צדקה which are in the same category but which, as a rule, can be paid anywhere and always—refer to the Temple. Thus in Rosh Hashona 5b:- ת״ר כי תדור נדר וגו׳ אלו הדמים והערכין והחרמים וההקדשות חטאות ואשמות עולות ושלמים צדקות ומעשרות ובכור לקט שכחה ופאה (refer to it).

That here it does speak primarily of vows which wait to be fulfilled by delivery of something of one’s possessions is already indicated by the words לא תאחר לשלמו which could only with difficulty be made to refer to other vows (see Nedarim 3b) and also, it seems to us, by כי דרש ידרשנו וגו׳ מעמך, which assumes that something promised to God is still wrongfully “עמנו״, in our possession.

לא תאחר לשלמו. We have already explained this prohibition on Levit. 23,38, and remarked that the first Festival, רגל, brings an admonition to fulfil any vow made before it, non-complying with it would be a transgression of the positive command ובאת שמה והבאת שמה (Deut. 12,5,6), but that the negative command, the prohibition לא תאחר is only transgressed with the passing of three such festivals. But for vows or promises to give charity the prohibition is transgressed immediately poor people are there and the opportunity is offered to fulfil the vow. (see ibid).

V. 23. וכי תחדל לנדר (see on Gen. 28,20). Making vows is not only in itself nothing meritorious, but actually belongs to the sphere of the sinful. כל הנודר אעפ״י שמקײמו נקרא חוטא (“everybody who vows, although he keeps his vow, is called a sinner”) is a principle of our sages. It would have been more right if the good deed had been done without its having been vowed to be done; for it says וכי תחדל לנדר לא יהיה בך חטא הא לא חדלת איכא חטא, only refraining from all vowing is no sin (Nedarim 77b). הנודר כאלו בנה במה. Making vows is similar to erecting a “Bama” at the time when such erections are forbidden (see Ch. 12,13), both are sins of a similar nature, both think they can do something “special” to please God, something beyond what He has commanded us to do (Nedarim 22a, ר״ן thereon). Regarding נדרי איסור the Jerusalmi says in Nedarim 11,1. לא דײך מה שאסרה תורה “are you not satisfied then with what the Torah has forbidden you?”, and regarding these נדרי אסור our Gemora in Nedarim 59a, says מצוה לאיתשולי עליהן, “it is a mitzva to have a searching investigation undertaken to see if there are not any legal means of abrogating the vow (see on Numb. 30,3). Only in times of tribulation, as was the case with Jacob (תוספות Chulin 2b) or having to fight against one’s inner urges, as was the case of the young student of שמעון הצדיק (Nedarim 9b) are נדרים approved of. Also a difference is made between הרי זו) נדבות, dedicating the thing itself I.L.) and הרי עלי) נדרים, promising to dedicate something I.L. — see Numb. 30,3), and the former, where there can be no fear of the vow being broken, is excluded from the general disapproval of vows. (Chulin 2b; Nedarim 10a).

V. 24. מוצא שפתיך תשמר. In Shevuoth 26b, with reference to כל נדיב לב (Ex. 35,5) it is taught that just for נדרי הקדש, of which our text here is primarily speaking, deciding in one’s mind, even without expressly making the vow in words, is completely binding, whereas for other vows, with the exception of vows to give charity, which comes under the category of נדרי הקדש, the rule holds that the decision to make a vow is only complete and binding when it is definitely expressed in words, גמר בלבו צריך להוציא בשפתיו (see on Ex. 35,5; Levit. 5,4). Nevertheless the rule holds also for הקדש that, if the vow has not only been decided in the mind but has also been expressed in words בעינן פיו ולבו שוין what he says must be exactly the same as what the intention decided in his mind was; (see Terumoth 3,8, ר״ש there).

כאשר נדרת לה׳ אלקיך נדבה. A נדר made with the formula הרי עלי e.g. הרי עלי עולה undertakes the duty of bringing such an offering to God. A נדבה, with the formula הרי זו, e.g. הרי זו עולה dedicates a specific object, e.g. this animal to be an offering to God. Now it is clear that at all נדרי הקדש, e.g. vowing to bring an offering, at some point between the vow and its fulfilment an act of dedicating a definite animal must take place. So that every נדר automatically includes a נדבה in it. Every הרי עלי עולה vows to dedicate an animal for an עולה and then to bring it as an offering. If then here our text stresses this intermediate act of נדר at a כאשר ,נדבה נדרת נדבה, the Gemora in Zebachim 2a, takes it that it wishes incidentally to indicate that there are cases in which the נדבה-act arising out of a נדר can really become a נדבה on its own, by which the נדר does not become fulfilled, e.g. in the cases where the קרבן by שינוי קדש or שינוי בעלים does remain כשר but לא עלה לבעלים לשם חובה (see Levit. at end of notes on I,9): מוצא שפתיך וגו׳ ועשית כאשר נדרת וגו׳ נדבה האי נדבה נדר הוא אלא אם כמה שנדרת עשית יהא נדר ואם לאו נדבה יהא (זבחים ב׳ א׳).

V. 25 & 26. The section closes with two sentences which, just like the preceding prohibition of interest, are rooted in the most unlimited rights of disposal of all our possessions which God retained when He founded our national society and laid the building up of a national social life based on the feelings of the duties of brotherly love and rights. Here He makes it a duty for Jewish landowners to allow the workers who are engaged on cutting and gathering the fruit in his orchards and vineyards to eat as much of the fruit as they please while working, and makes it a duty for such workers to keep strictly within the limits of this permission and to be careful not to misuse it.

כי תבא, for this term does not designate any irregular casual entry, but the ordinary justified entry of the workers, בפועל הכתוב מדבר (Baba Mezia 87b). (There it refers to the similar use of the term תבא in v. 15 of the next chapter, to designate the ordinary regular setting of the sun לא תבא עליו השמש to fix the time when the wage of a day-labourer becomes due and must be paid). The text also mentions that he is there with כלי and חרמש, with the necessary vessels for gathering the fruit and the sickle for cutting the corn.

Just as the workers are given the right here to eat of the fruit growing in the orchards or fields in which they are working, במחובר, so have they the right also—similarly to the שור בדישו (Ch. 25,4)—to the fruit after it has been cut and gathered, בתלוש, as long as they are still engaged in working with it. But this authorisation is very strictly restricted to the limitations given by the wording of the text. It applies solely to products of the soil דבר שגידולו מן הארץ and while they are growing, מחובר, the permission only starts when they are ripe, when Nature has finished her work and Man stands ready with “basket and sickle” to take to “himself” that which Nature has completed, and the permission with תלוש lasts as long as they have not reached the stage of being ready for human use as shown by the duty arising to give מעשר or בתלוש מן הקרקע עד :חלה שלא נגמרה מלאכתו (see Ch. 14,22). Taken together, accordingly, only then, and only so long as the workers are engaged in getting the fruit finished by Nature ready for the use of Man. Not earlier nor later, so that at the threshold of Man’s mastery of Nature, so apt to beget the selfish thought “Mine, mine own”, God strews the seeds of the thoughts of “duty” in both directions effecting brotherly love and justice, that which is right. (see Baba Mezia 87a, et seq.).

ואכלת ולא מוצץ ענבים ולא ענבים ודבר אחר וכו׳ שבעך ולא אכילה גסה he may only eat the raw fruit as it is, not press it out to drink the juice and throw the rest away, may only eat the fruit he picks by itself, not with bread and butter or anything else, by which one can eat much more of it, may only eat as much of it as suffices his appetite but not stuff himself immoderatly with it (ibid).

מלילות, from Beiza 12b, מוללין מלילות ומפרכין קטניות וכו׳ it is evident that מלל means shelling the grains out of the ears, hence מלילות are the shelled grains. Or the freshly picked ears are called מלילות out of which one picks the grains by hand.

V. 1. Now, in this chapter laws follow partly new ones, partly repeated and complemented, laws of the holiness of marriage, of the duty of the State to have consideration for the homely happiness of individuals and their ability to make a livelihood to be undisturbed, of the inviolability of personal freedom, of paying attention to God’s admonition to foster all the social virtues, the limitations of the right to take pledges, conscientious treatment of wage-earners, the protection of the rights of, and the duty of benevolent treatment of widows, orphans and strangers which are to be impressed as duties of the national social life. The fulfilment of these laws must be the quite special aim of every single circle of the now impending isolation of the people into groups, if happiness is to blossom in the Land, and Israel to prove itself as the People of God, redeemed out of the misery of Egyptian oppression of fellow human beings.

Verses 1-4 contain laws over the contracting and dissolving the bond of marriage. Clearly the prohibition contained in v.4. of מחזיר גרושתו לאחר שנשאת (remarrying one’s divorced wife after she had been married to someone else I.L.) is the real object of this pronouncement of the Torah, to which the ways and means of contracting and dissolving marriage precede as introductory clauses. Just for the sake of this prohibition, which prevents a shameful misuse of the Law itself to what is apparently quite legal lewdness, are these laws of contracting and dissolving marriage reserved for the compendium for those about to move into the Land. For there where the people are left more to themselves isolated from the centre, is such a misuse of the Law, undermining the morality of the whole land, mostly to be feared; to which indeed the concluding words ולא תחטיא וגו׳ refers.

כי יקח וגו׳. We have already noted on Ch. 22,13 that Jewish marriages are accomplished by two separate acts, by (אירוסין) קידושין and נשואין. The first founds the relationship of personal attachment, the second, the reception of the wife in the house of the husband with all its consequences. This first act, קידושין, is here designated by כי יקח. It is the personal adoption of the wife by the husband. As is implied by the word לקח itself and by the ג״ש (the inference drawn from a similarity of phrases I.L.) קיחה קיחה from שדה עפרון (Gen. 23,13) and is further explained in Kiddushin 2a, this adoption is made in the form of an act of appropriation. The groom gives the bride something of the minimum value of a peruta (a small coin I.L.) with the words הרי את מקודשת לי etc. and by the bride accepting this article in this sense before witnesses, she gives herself up to the man, is מקודשת to him, sanctified to him, and, like הקדש, is unapproachable to anybody else, דאסר לה אכולא עלמא כהקדש (Kiddushin 2b). This form of contracting a marriage is called קידושי כסף. From the ויצאה וגו׳ והיתה וגו׳ of verse 2 the Halacha teaches a second form:- קידושי שטר by the giving and accepting a document specially composed for this purpose and containing the קידושין formula. For the adoption of another husband, (V.2) והיתה לאיש אחר is placed in connection with the divorce from the house of the first one, ויצאה מביתו, and thereby just as a written form is the only legal way for the divorce, a written form is given validity also for the קידושין-adoption. מקיש הויה ליציאה מה יציאה בשטר אף הויה בשטר (Kiddushin 5a; 9b).

That with this act of אירוסין, although thereby the personal bond is made, and the woman becomes אסורה, prohibited for any other attachment, nevertheless the לקוחין the complete unity of the wife with the person of her husband is not yet completed, but is conditional on another act, that is clear from the text of the Torah. In Ch. 20,7 it says:- ומי האיש אשר ארש אשה ולא לקהה, so that after אירוסין another act is to take place. Also in the chapter on vows (Numb. 30,7,11), a difference is made between the ארוסה stage, ואם היה תהיה לאיש during which, regarding her vows, she is subject to the combined decision of her father and her husband, and ואם בית אישה נדרה where her vows are subject to the confirmation of her husband alone (refer to it there). So is it also clear from the מוציא שם רע-law (XXII,13-21) that as long as the מקודשת is still בבית אביה she has the character of an ארוסה, and only when she is given over to the husband את בתי נתתי לאיש to enter his household does she become נשואה, a completely married woman. And in fact the Halacha also teaches that the marriage only starts with קידושין but has to be completed by חופה (Kiddushin 5a, and b). But חופה is the wife being permanently introduced into the house of the husband, which is symbolically carried out by their entering together under a covering “roof” (a canopy טלית). Only with חופה is any sexual approach permitted, and the reciprocal legal relationship regarding rights to fortunes etc. and the laws concerning vows and טומאת מת at נהנים (Levit. 21,2) come into force, laws, amongst which those referring to legal rights to fortunes etc. only attained real meaning with the normal conditions of income, alimentation etc. which would begin with the entry into the Land.

והיה אם לא תמצא (see on Gen. 6,8). חן is quite specially the quality of a wife which makes her worthy of the devoted love of her husband. Thus Prov. 11,16:- אשת חן תתמך כבוד ועריצים יתמכו עשר, “as powerful men hold fast to riches, so does a wife worthy of the love of her husband hold fast to honour”. We already know the word דבר in the relations between men at law, as designating a declaration, claim or plaint in the law court (see Ch. 19,15). Now here it cannot mean—as the Jerushalmi at end of Gittin points out—legal grounds for divorce, as ב״ש takes it, an act of real adultery, a דבר ערוה which, in accordance with Numb. 5,13, would forbid the continuance of the marriage and make divorce an imperative duty. For in V.4. the remarriage with the first husband is only forbidden if she has married somebody else in the meantime. So that otherwise the continuation of the first marriage would be permitted by the Torah. Hence Gittin 90a, also remarks that if דבר ערוה was to be the only justification for divorce it would then not have been called ערות דבר but ערות .ערוה דבר clearly goes beyond just ערוה and grants the permission of divorce by any דבר, any behaviour of the wife which gives the husband grounds of complaint that it is impossible to continue the marriage. Behaviour of which ב״ה in contrast to the דבר ערוה of ב״ש gives as an example, אפילו הקדיחה תבשילו, even if the wife intentionally makes her husband’s food uneatable. But it does not say just דבר but ערות דבר, to indicate incidentally that even if a wife is divorced through ערוה, her marriage with another man is permitted. At the same time it follows from the term דבר that the grounds for divorce must be verified by two witnesses in accordance with the canon על פי שנים עדים וגו׳ יקום דבר (Ch. 19,15).

וכתב לה ספר כריתות ונתן בידה ושלחה מביתו, and again similarly in V.3. By these three sentences the form of the procedure by which a divorce is to be effected is detailed. כתב, just as at the marriage, קידושין, so here at the divorce, גירושין, the man is the active party. In Jewish Law both at marriage as well as at divorce, the officials only supervise and guide the order and regularity of the proceedings, the סידור קידושין וגטין, but in no wise “marry” or divorce the couple. But for divorce there is only the one way, וכתב, by writing the fixed formula of divorce, בכתיבה מתגרשת ואינה מתגרשת בכסף (Gittin 21b), and וכתב, the writing must be done by the man himself or by somebody he appoints to write for him, and וכתב ולא חקק, the letters must be written directly, but not engraved i.e. not indirectly by הק תוכות (by chiselling out the surroundings and making the letters come out in relief I.L.) ibid 20a; לשמה :וכתב לה, it must be written in the name of the husband with direct reference by name to the wife to be divorced, i.e. it must be written לשמו ולשמה (ibid 24a); ספר :ספר כריתות is not the material of the deed, but its contents ספירת דברים, what it tells, and this must be דבר הכורת בינו לבינה ,כריתות, it must expressly make the separation absolute, not conditional and not limited (ibid 21b); וכתב וגו׳ מי שאינו מחוסר אלא כתיבה ונתינה יצא זה שמחוסר כתיבה וקציצה ונתינה :ונתן וגו׳ the document must be able to be handed over without first having to be cut off from the sheet or roll. (ibid).

All these laws can be summarised in the one idea: the written word is to be used in place of the spoken one, instead of a speech made with full considered conscious intention, the thought of divorce must be expressed in writing with equal consciousness of its import and intention, with uninterrupted direction of the mind to that purpose; and moreover, with its being written down, just as the spoken word can be immediately used to transmit what it wishes to say, so must the written word be finished and equally ready to be handed over.

אין לי אלא ידה גגה חצרה וקרפיפה מנײן ת״ל ונתן מ״מ :ונתן בידה (ibid 77a), the notice of divorce thus made by him, or by his having had it made for him, has to be placed by the husband in the hand of the wife, or deposited in a place which is her own property, so that by such נתן “giving”, the document becomes a possession of the wife. יד here means רשות (possession I.L.) as in המצא תמצא בידו (Ex. 22,3, see note on p. 342). By depositing the deed of divorce in any place which is her domain (her garden, her roof etc. I.L.) the husband gives up any rights he may have in it, it becomes her exclusive גיטה וחצרה באין כאחד ,רשות (ibid 77b), so that the first concrete result of the divorce is achieved thereby.

ושלחה מביתו is not a third procedure, but designates the purpose and effect of the וכתב ונתן and the express sense in which the deed of divorce is to be handed over, which must be definitely made לשם גירושין. Thus it says in ונתן בידה ושלחה מביתו עד שיאמר לה הרי זה :ספרי גטך אמר לה כנסי שטר חוב זה אינו גט עד שיאמר לה הא גיטך (שם ע״ה א׳).

Hence also it does not say וגרשה מביתו as, for instance ואשה גרושה מאישה in Levit. 21,7, which would express an actual sending away from the home as some final act of divorce, but ושלחה. For שלח very seldom means to send away, to put away. Its real meaning is always a negative one, letting go, freeing, leaving to itself, releasing, not keeping back. Out of the numerous places where it is used in this sense we will just indicate a few characteristic ones. Thus שלח את בני וגו׳ (Ex. 4,23) and always for “letting the people go” out of Pharaoh’s servitude: ושלח לכם את אחיכם (Gen. 43,14), כי שלחו וילך (Sam. II, III,22); ושלחו בדרך טובה (Sam. I, XXIV,20); מי שלח פרא חפשי (Job. 39,8); לחפשי ישלחנו (Ex. 21,26). Even the marriage of daughters from their fathers’ house is also called ושלשים בנות שלח החוצה ,שלח (Judges 12,9). So there is no doubt that here too ושלחה מביתו does not mean her actually leaving the house, that is referred to in the next verse by ויצאה מביתו as the natural consequence of the divorce. ושלחה מביתו is simply the expression used here for the legal effect of the act of divorce: the freeing of the marriage bond which hitherto was in force, and the release of belonging to the husband. It is accordingly the specific contrast to the concept of כי יקח וגו׳ ,לקוחים which designates the contracting of the marriage bond by which a קנין is achieved from which the wife is released by the act of divorce. That is also why Onkelos translates שלח here by פטר which means “making free” “releasing”, and so also the whole legal concept of divorce כריתות by ,פטורין גט פטורין while he translates גרש in Levit. 21,7,14; XXII,13 by תרך.

ונתן בידה ושלחה מביתו is accordingly the demand that he gives her the deed of divorce in the sense of handing her over the release from belonging to his household and that she accepts it in that sense and with that meaning. Hence the Gemora (Yebamoth 113b) says that only such a woman is able to be divorced who יודעת לשמור גטה, who understands the mutual legal personal consequences of her accepting the deed, but not one who has become insane, שוטה, who משלחה וחוזרת who would still come back to the house of the husband after the release.

So that here, in verses 1,3,4, divorce is repeatedly given the meaning of a legal act of a purely personal nature, the cessation of a legal personal relationship. And by the repeated term of שליחות the Halacha is at the same time fixed that such a legal procedure can also be done by proxy, ע״י שליח, by a representative appointed by the husband שליח הולכה or by a representative appointed by the wife, שליח קבלה, and the general canon, referrred to elsewhere, שליחו של אדם כמותו applies to divorce also (see Ex. on Ch. 12,3 p. 131, as well as on Numb. 18,28).

The act of contracting the marriage bond as well as that of dissolving it may only be done in the presence of two qualified witnesses and the validity of the acts is dependent on their presence. It belongs to the nature of the קידושין by which, as remarked above on V.1. the wife becomes אסירא אכל עלמא כהקדש and equally so to the nature of גירושין, that thereby she becomes again מותרת לכל אדם. That general legal prohibition and permission can only be established by the testimony of two qualified witnesses in accordance with the canon על פי שנים עדים יקום דבר (Ch. 19,15), without them neither the איסור through קדושין nor the היתר through גירושין could come to practical materialisation. So that the presence of qualified witnesses at these two acts is essential for their validity whereas at other legal transactions and contracts their presence is only desirable to prevent any future denial by one of the parties, לא איברי סהדי אלא לשקרא (Kiddushin 65b — see פני יהושע thereon).

Whether the signature of the witnesses on the deed or their presence at the handing over of the deed is the more essential is a matter of dispute between ר׳ מאיר and ר׳ אלעזר. The accepted Halacha follows the opinion of the latter viz. that עדי מסירה כרתי, it is the presence of the witnesses, not their signature on the document which is essential. In practice both functions are demanded from the witnesses (Gittin 4a; 86a).

Elsewhere (in Jeshurun Vol.X) we have already worked out the beneficial influence which the possibility of legal divorce exercises for the tender intimate devotion of Jewish marriages, and for the purity and happiness of Jewish family life. In particular we pointed out what high value the Torah assumes Jewish women would be held in the nation, so that, with perfect confidence it could quietly leave the decision for divorce primarily to the heart of the husband; and how it was no sign of progress or advance in ideas, if, after more than two thousand years during which on the whole there was no misuse of that authority it was found necessary to prevent misuse of it by curtailment of the right. We allow ourselves to refer to that treatise on the Position of Jewish Women, and here content ourselves with just stressing the depth of the thought with which the Torah makes the law of כי יקח איש אשה חדשה (V. 5) follow immediately on the law of divorce. It is a law, which indeed like hardly any other, proclaims the high value, above anything else, which the Torah places on a wife and proves its appreciation of the duty of a husband to attend to the happiness of his wife in a manner which indeed no other nation on earth could—or can boast of. (Read Dayan Dr. Grunfeld’s translation (in Vol. 2 of “Judaism Eternal”) of Hirsch’s article The Jewish Woman I.L.).
But first verses 3 and 4 follow with a stipulation by which a possible misuse of the Law itself to an apparently legal immoral procedure is to be prevented.

V. 2. ויצאה וגו׳ והיתה וגו׳. See on V. 1. היה ל- ,והיתה לאיש אחר is the term for the personal attachment by קידושין. The following prohibition to remarriage with the first husband only applies if the divorcee had actually married someone else, but not if she had had immoral intercourse with others: איסור מחזיר גרושתו משנישאת but not משזנתה. And it applies even if she had only had קדושין from another man, although she was still only an ארוסה. Both these laws are given by the term והיתה לאיש אחר. The first is also clear already from the whole of V.3. in which clearly a union, אישות, is indicated which can only be dissolved by גט or death. (Sota 18b; Yebamoth 11b).

V. 3. ושלחה מביתו או כי ימות. By this juxtaposition of the husband’s death and divorce the Gemora teaches (Kiddushin 13b) that although forbidden relationships brought about by marriage, עריות, as step-mothers, daughters-in-law, wives of uncles, continue to be forbidden even after the marriages have been ended by the death of the respective father, son, or uncle, nevertheless the bond of marriage itself, the איסור אשת איש, is completely dissolved by the marriage being ended by the death of the husband, and nothing stands in the way of remarriages of widows (provided the death of the husband is legally established according to Jewish Law, and the הבחנה period (Yebamoth 42a) and, where indicated, also the periods of מעוברת חברו and מינקת חברו (ibid) passed.

V. 4. אחרי אשר הטמאה. It requires considerable consideration to decide to what this refers. We know from Numbers 5,13,14,19,20,28,29 that a sin against the sanctity of the marriage tie is expressed by the term טומאה, as well as that in Levit. 18,24 et seq. sexual sins generally are also called טומאה and there in V. 20 adultery is specially designated as ואל אשת עמיתך וגו׳ לטמאה בה ,טומאה. Now the marriage to a legally divorced woman is something completely lawful, so that in itself there can be nothing that would be called טומאה in it. Equally little is there anything wrong in the second divorce, or in the second marriage ending with the death of that husband, that לא יוכל וגו׳ אחרי אשר הוטמאה should be said. If then one can find nothing objectively wrong in the proceedings of the woman which would correspond to the epithet טומאה, this must refer only to a relative relationship, a reference to the first husband to whom she has once become a טומאה—in sexual matters having the same meaning as איסור—and to whom she can never become a מותרת again. Now there is only one single moment in which she became an איסור for her first husband and that was the moment she accepted קידושין from the second. As thereby she became אסירא אכל עלמא כהקדש any sexual intercourse with her husband again from that moment would be adultery, the prohibition ואל אשת עמיתך וגו׳ לטמאה בה applies to him; and this טומאה which has once come between them remains even after the cessation of the second marriage by divorce or the death of the second husband. The first husband may never marry her again after she has once become a טומאה to him, exactly as if she had become a סוטה (Numb. 5,13) during the first marriage.

This way of taking it is quite in keeping with the Halacha already remarked on V.2. that only קידושי שני (but not any act of whoredom I.L.) entails the prohibition of remarrying his wife after having divorced her אחרי) כתבתי זאת ראיתי שגם הרד״ק בס׳ השרשים ש׳ טמא הביא סברא זו בשם אביו ע״ש). Finally the unusual form: הטמאה would also agree with this, and at the same time would give the reason for the whole. For הטמאה is a composition of the Hopthal and the Hispoal (cf. התפקדו in Numb. 1,47) so that it says literally:- she had become induced to cause herself to become אסור to her husband. So that לא יוכל וגו׳ אחרי וגו׳ would say:- the first husband may never marry her again if, after having been divorced from him, she makes herself טמא for him, i.e. אסור for him, by קדושין with somebody else, an אסור which is necessary for the legal היתר of the second husband as איתתא לבי תרי לא חזיא (no wife may be shared by two husbands. I.L.). The Torah evidently sees, and wishes to forestall, the possibility of a reprehensible misuse of the seriousness of legal קידושין and גירושין to hide and gloss over an intended adultery, which by the connivance of all the parties could be accomplished under the cloak of complete legality. Any such sinful playing with the sanctity of marriage, and the seriousness of the Law is prevented by this law which assigns to the return of a divorced wife to her first husband after קדושין to, and גרושין from, a second husband, the full weight of an act of actual adultery; and with the קדושין of a second husband makes the wife remain for ever אסור to the first as if she were a real סוטה שנטמאה (Numb. 5,13).
