The sense of the Law is accordingly:- To prevent the misuse of קידושין ,גרושין and חזרה after גרושין for the perpetration of adultery under the guise of legality, the Torah has assigned to the second קדושין the force of making any intended חזרה as if it were actual adultery; and has strengthened the universal איסור אשת איש which starts with these קדושין into a permanent איסור סוטה for the first husband.

According to that we can then more easily understand the Gemora which, in Yebamoth 11b, teaches in our אחרי אשר הוטמאה a direct reference to סוטה שנסתרה ונבעלה for which the אסור has already been declared in Numb. 5,13, but for which the לאו is given here; and indeed to such a degree that the real עריות character given to the real סוטה by the word טומאה remains, but not so in the case of מחזיר גרושתו, as—in accordance with the way we have taken it—a remarried divorced woman is not called נטמאה in the proper sense of the word, and only for the case of any return to the first husband, and as a matter of fact only comes under the category of חײבי לאוין without the character of an ערוה, as in fact she has done nothing illegal. This difference between a סוטה, to whom the טומאה-character is really attached and a מחזיר גרושתו משניסת to whom this character is only figuratively applied has its effect on the law of יבום. A real סוטה is אסורה ליבם like an ערוה, and according to most opinions is פטורה מן החליצה (ופוטרת צרתה מן היבום והחליצה see Levit. on XVIII,18). But מחזיר גרושתו though אסורה ליבם must be חולצת and צרתה חולצת או מתײבמת (Yebamoth 11a, b).

היא תועבה ואין בניה תועבה :תועבה היא, the transgression of the prohibition to remarry her first husband after having been married to a second one entails no disadvantages to any children she may have afterwards, like all children of חײבי לאוין (see Ch. 23,3) they are כשרים לקהל.

תועבה היא לפני ה׳, in the eyes of Man nothing illegal has been done (she was divorced legally, married again legally, that marriage terminated legally, and her new remarriage performed in accordance with the law with kiddushin and chuppa I.L.), but in the Eyes of God the mere possibility to immoral intentions is a desecration of His Torah, His Teachings, and hence before Him it is a תועבה. And thou, the Jewish Nation, through its representatives the Beth Din (ספרי ,להזהיר ב״ד על כך) hast to see to it that, on the land that God has given us for His Torah to become something real, the moral height of the Torah does not become encroached upon, so that the Land does not gradually go to ruin under the moral sins of its inhabitants. (See on Levit. 18,24-28).

V. 5. כי יקח וגו׳. The preceding law set the fundamental condition for marriage in the intimate and harmonious merging of the wife into the life and household of her husband as this is to be founded by קדושין and נשואין, and where this condition is irrevocably shattered, has allowed, or if need be, ordered, divorce, and has only made it the duty of the courts to prevent any possible misuse of this permission for reprehensible purposes.

To that now comes this law, and proclaims the great duty of a husband: ושמח את אשתו אשר לקח, that he does not disappoint the wife, to whom he has attached himself with the little word “לי״, in the expectations under which she became his, that he would recognise as his highest task in the marriage, the duty to make the woman who has become “his” wife happy. And the Torah looks on this duty of a husband for the happiness of the marriage as being such a high one, and lays such importance to it, not only for its individual happiness but also for the national well-being that, for a whole year after marrying a wife, it frees him from all public services and duties, yea actually forbids him to undertake any of them so that he can give himself up entirely to his home life and to laying the foundation of his wife’s happiness.

חדשה only excludes remarrying a wife after he has divorced her, who is not חדשה לו, with whom he has already lived in marriage. But one who marries a widow or one who has been divorced from somebody else, is included in this law. (Sota 44a).

לא יצא בצבא, as differentiated from one who has only מארש אשה but has not yet taken her home; such a one has to join up, march with the army to the border but is then חוזר מערכי מלחמה sent back and is מספיק מים ומזון ומתקן את הדרכים (engaged on non-combatant military duties of the A.S.S. I.L.).

עבר על .ולא יעבר עליו לכל דבר is the usual term used for everything burdensome, onerous (including rates and taxes I.L.) and troublesome, to which one has to submit. Thus גם עליך תעבר כוס (Lament 4,21); ויעבד עלי מה (Job 13,13). Here: “he shall not have to submit to anything troublesome in any way”, and indeed as Rambam (Melachim 7,10,11) says, not only in military matters, but not be called on for any national or communal requirements, as indeed would correspond to the wording of the text לכל דבר and נקי יהיה לביתו. There it says אין מטריחין אותו לשום דבר בעולם and: כל השנה אין מספק מים ומזון ולא מתקן דרך ולא שומר בחומה ולא נותן לפסי העיר ולא יעבור עליו שום דבר בעולם שנאמר לא יצא בצבא ולא יעבור לכל דבר לעבור בשני לאוין לא לצרכי העיר ולא לצרכי הגדוד (ונראה שיצא זה להרמב״ם מן התוספתא סוטה פ״ז שמוספת פסי העיר על הדברים שפוטרת אותן המשנה וז״ל בתוספתא אין נותנין פסי העיר ואין מספקין מים ומזון למלחמה ואין מתקנין את הדרכים עכ״ל ובב״ב ח׳ א׳ איתא כל שנשתהא בעיר י״ב חדש נותן לפסי העיר ואם כן פסי העיר כולל כל צרכי העיר אפילו בשעת שלום ע״ש כנלענ״ד.

In Sota 44a, the נקי יהיה לביתו is taken to be extended beyond the אשה חדשה which the text mentions as the introductory case, and to apply to the fresh addition to the happiness of the house by a new house or a new vineyard and to all those who are exempted from military service and other services who are still in the first year of enjoying a newly built or bought house or vineyard. (Cf. Ch. 20,5,6).

Clearly at the root of these laws lies the point of view that a state, the concept of a state as a whole has only reality in the actual numbers of all its individual members, but apart from them, or next to them, one cannot consider the existence of a state as a concept in itself. So that the national welfare can only be sought in the well-being and happiness of all the single individuals, hence every flourishing and happy home is a contribution to the realisation of the goal set for the nation, hence has to be met by the nation with careful and encouraging and promoting consideration.

V. 6. לא יחבל וגו׳. The private individual too has to refrain from imposing the justified demands of his private rights if they would mean shattering the means of existence for his brother who is in debt to him. That altogether he may not press him for payment if he is convinced of his temporary inability to pay has already been said in Ex. 22,24 (refer to it), as well as in V. 25 there, if he had accepted something as a pledge for the repayment of a debt which has become due to be paid—which he is fully entitled legally to do—it is his duty to return it in exchange for something else, at the time the debtor needs it for his own use. Now a complementary law is added here, that all culinary vessels—כלי אוכל נפש, for which the millstones are only made into examples by the reason adduced כי נפש הוא חובל—may not be accepted even in this limited “exchange” manner. (See סמ״ע on ח״מ 97,b—and further on V. 10).
דחים. See on Gen. 8,21. רכב is the mill-stone “riding” on the lower one.

V. 7. כי ימצא. But it is not merely his material requirements as in the preceding, it is the whole personality, the freedom and human rights which in Jewish society is to stand untouchable by anybody else, so much so that if it is found—כי ימצא as always, meaning בעדים, charged by witnesses,—that somebody has treated somebody else “completely as if he were a thing, an object”, has forcibly taken him into his power (בידו, as it has already said in Ex. 21,16), has made him work for him, והתעמר בו, as is added here, and finally has sold him, such a robber, just as a murderer of physical life is to have his life ended בסײף by beheading, so does this murderer of spiritual life have to forefeit his life by חנק (see on Ex. 21,16).

V. 8. השמר וגו׳. The murderous attack of one man against another, described in the previous verse, are committed to the charge of the human law-court. But remember and by careful attention keep your mind fully awake to the fact that the whole social intercourse between man and man, even words and thoughts are under the watchful Eye and Judgment of a Higher Court, Who places His “Finger” admonishingly and warningly on the house, the garment, the body of anybody who, in his intercourse with his brethren forgets brotherly love and consideration (see Levit. pp. 355-367).

We recognised the whole laws of negaim as a great institution of admonishing and warning education for the correct social behaviour in feelings, words and deeds. And we understand quite well how, here, at the threshold of the land, on the soil of which now a social national life is to be developed, based on God, watched over by God, and guided by God, in the midst of to a great part, repeated reminders of the principles of the social duties, the conscientious attention to, and carrying out of, the laws of negaim is brought home to the people’s minds.

השמר, as always (see Ch. 4,9) is the term used as a prohibition, it is the warning to be careful not to transgress, here against paying no attention to, neglecting or even doing away with, the regulations of negaim, the latter, e.g. by mechanically removing the spot of the נגע צרעת from the house, garment or body (see on Levit. 13,46) by which carrying out the institution would be rendered impossible. הקוצץ את בהרתו אזהרתיה מהכא השמר בנגע צרעת וגו׳ (Makoth 22a).
ולעשות is the positive command to obey the regulations prescribed, צרעת עשה ולא תעשה הוא (Sabbat 132b).

ככל אשר יורו. At the carrying out of the institution of negaim, the intervention of a priest is indispensable. Not for the examination and judgment of the spot, but the result טמא or טהור must be proclaimed by a priest. (Levit. 13,2). And significantly the priests are here called by their tribal name לוים which warns them fearlessly to uphold the Law against whoever it may be of the people (see on Ch. 17,9). For the proclamation טמא has to designate the person affected (be it the King himself, as actually happened I.L.) as unworthy and unfit for the Sanctuary of the Torah and the company of its people (see Levit. p. 359).

זכור וגו׳. The warning to keep in mind what happened to Miriam the Prophetess who because of a conversation just between herself and Aaron, concerning their brother Moses, a conversation which was not free from defamatory talk and conceit, was marked by God’s Finger with a נגע in consequence of which she was shut out of the company of the whole nation for seven days—this warning proclaims loudly and clearly for all time the purely spiritual meaning of betterment from all social faults and misdemeanors, it also reminds of the gravity of the responsibility for every word which borders on לשון הרע which could not be overlooked even in a Miriam, which, according to the way it is taken, was not even said in a bad way with any bad intention; and finally it reminds us of the importance of carrying out the regulation of the negaim, seeing that for their sake the whole nation had to break its journey to the promised homeland for seven days, as the reference here adds, בדרך בצאתכם ממצרים.

V. 10. כי תשה וגו׳. Whereas verses 8 and 9 remind of the institution of negaim, by which the social life of all classes of the nation are proclaimed as being under the special testing and admonishing rule of God, the following verses 10-13,14 & 15,17 & 18,19-22 are repetitions of duties towards poorer people and dependants, duties, on the fulfilling of which God’s Eye is specially directed, on the fulfilment of which the hoped-for blessing of God on the land quite specially depends, and therefore at the entry into the Land, and the distinction of classes based on riches and posessions which only then would really begin, quite specially require impressing on the nation.

כי תשה. We have already remarked on Ex. 22,24 and Deut. 15,2 that the concept נשה does not begin when the debt is incurred, but at the time when the repayment becomes due. משאה is a debt which is already due to be repaid, the repayment can already be claimed in court. So that here it is not speaking of a משכון בשעת ההלואה, of a pledge to be given by the debtor at the time the loan is given, but שלא בשעת ההלואה of a pledge to be given when repayment is due to be made, and the article is not meant to be בתורת פרעון to get oneself paid by the debtor, but to ensure the demand against possible liquidation in שביצית (see Ch. 15,1,2) and so that if the debtor should die it should become the possession of the creditor to settle his loss. שלא תהא משמטתו ולא יעשה מטלטלין אצל בניו (Baba Mezia 115a).

The law which follows here only refers to demands for payment of debts and not only loans which are owing משאה, but also משאת מאומה, other demands which by the lapse of the time given for payment have become changed to the nature of loans owing זקפן עליו במלוה (Baba Mezia 115a; see on Ch. 15,2), but does not apply to entering a house to distrain for שכר דיוקנאות ,שכר פונדק ,שכר חמר ,שכר כתף, porterage fees, payment for hiring asses, for the hotel bill or artists’ fees etc., as long as the deferment has not been agreed to (ibid).

לא תבא וגו׳. The Halacha teaches that such fetching a pledge imposed to ensure the payment of a debt which has fallen due, may never be made by the creditor himself, but that he must engage the intervention of the court for it (such a personal coming of the creditor to a debtor who is temporarily unable to pay would already be forbidden by לא תהיה לו כנושה in Ex. 22,24. But according to תוספות (ibid) the complete exclusion of the creditor himself from distraining a pledge personally is only דרבנן). But also the agent of the court, the שליח ב״ד, may not enter the house of the debtor to take a pledge, it is to him that the words of our text לא תבא אל ביתו לעבט עבוטו really apply, but :בחוץ תעמד וגו etc. accordingly means, “thou, the creditor through thy representative from the court”.
עבט: See Ch. 15,6.

V. 11 &12. ואם איש עני וגו׳. Here it is speaking of a night-garment, the requirement for which commences with sunset hence השב וגו׳ כבא השמש, whereas in Ex. 22,25 it deals with day-garments which have always to be returned to be used until sunset עד בא השמש (see there; — B.M. 114b).

צדקה ;ולד תהיה צדקה: see Gen. 15,6. As the returning of the pledge for the use of the debtor for him to sleep in the pledged garment is here called צדקה, it is clear that, from a legal point of view the pledge is no longer, or at least not completely any longer the property of the debtor, and that, legally speaking it already to a certain extent belongs to the possessions of the creditor, and that in giving it back at night he performs an act of charitable benevolence with an object of his own.

Hence the sentence of ר׳ יצחק in Shebuoth 44a: מנין לבעל חוב שקונה משכון שנאמר ולך תהיה צדקה אם אינו קונה משכון צדקה מנין לו מכאן לבעל חוב שקונה משכון (“from where do we know that a creditor acquires possession of a pledge? Because the text says “it would be an act of pious duty before God”, if it does not belong to him where does the piety come in” I.L.). Concerning the practical application of this sentence of Rabbi Isaac, i.e. as to how far the right of a creditor extends over a pledge he has taken to ensure the payment of his demand, which, in any case, as remarked above, does protect him against שביעית and the death of the debtor, and so does establish the idea of its being his possession, opinions differ as to how far his responsibility goes for the article if it becomes lost, whether, as a שומר שכר he would be responsible for theft or loss, or as a שואל he would be also חײב באונסין (see Ex. 22,11,13), finally whether what Rab. Isaac says applies only במשכון שלא בשעת הלואתו of which our text, from which he deduces it, primarily speaks, or also to משכון בשעת הלואתו (see especially the ש״ך on ח״מ 72,2 and פני יהושע on Gittin 37a, and Kiddushin 8a).

We have already remarked that these laws here are not referring to pledges taken as security for repayments of loans at the time the loan is given, nor to pledges taken for payment of a debt but they refer to distraining a pledge to secure the repayment of a loan which has become due. Accordingly they regulate the behaviour of a creditor just at the time when the debtor remains most deeply concious all the time of his obligations and dependence.
What considerations have to be made at distraining for the actual payments owing, מסדרין לבעל חוב we have already given on Levit. 27,8.

V. 14 & 15. לא תעשק וגו׳. These duties of conscientiously paying wages punctually have already been declared in Levit. 19,13, in the chapter of sanctifying our lives, and there we have explained them fully. Their repetition here in the compendium for the settling down in the land is accompanied by the most impressive warning against sinning in this respect, especially towards the poor and needy. For its practical importance only really begins with the settling down, and the experience of ages teaches how just the unpunctuality of rich people in paying their obligations towards their workmen and craftsmen has undermined their developing and prospering.

לא תעשק. See Levit. there. In Levit. it says generally לא תעשק את רעך and enjoins punctual payment to be made to everybody, rich or poor. If here עני ואביון are specially stressed, according to the Sifri it wishes to say ממהר אני ליפרע על ידי עני ואביון יותר מכל אדם that unpunctuality in paying the wages of day-labourers and workmen who are poor and needy is a still more serious responsibility before God. — בשעריך even if he is only a גר תושב, is not a convert, but only has the right to live in your land (everybody has the right to domicile in the Torah Land of Israel, who renounces polytheism and accepts the seven fundamental moral laws I.L.). The preceding addition of the word בארצך, according to B.M. 111b, extends the duty of punctual payment of wages for כל שבארצך, everything in your land not only for persons but also to בהמה וכלים for wages earned by animals, machines etc. (See Levit. ibid).

נשא נפש אל :ואליו הוא נושא וגו׳ (literally “raising your soul towards” I.L.) means longing intensely for something. Thus in Jer. 44,14: אשר המה מנשאים את נפשם לשוב לשבת שם of the Land (to which they long from the bottom of their hearts to return to live there I.L.). משא נפשם “the object of their longing” (Ezek. 24,25). So here too: “he longs for the wage after doing the work”, or, “it is the wage he is yearning for with the work and at the work”. Or, according to the Sifri: אליו הוא נושא את נפשו, for it, the wage he even risks his life, undertakes dangerous work, climbs ladders etc. is equivalent to his life, כל הכובש שכר שכיר כאלו נוטל נפשו ממנו “who witholds the wages of a workman is taking his life from him” (B.M. 112a). והיה בך חטא, not only when he cries up to God about you, but והיה בך חטא מ״מ, in any case you have laden yourself with sin, but, ממהר אני ליפרע ע״י קורא יותר ממי שאינו קורא (Sifri), “My punishment will come more quickly if you have caused one to cry out up to Me”.

V. 16. לא יומתו וגו׳. According to the Gemora (Sanhedrin 27b) this proclaims the two principles, that neither the crimes nor the testimony of close relations, such as fathers and sons, may be used to their disadvantage, not merely that fathers should not suffer the death penalty for the crimes of their sons and vice versa. If now these sentences were meant solely to give rules for the administration of justice the position of these verses would be peculiar. Clearly V.17 with its לא תחבל וגו׳ continues the tendency of the preceding laws regarding the considerate treatment to be given to people who are in a socially depressed position; and the לא תטה משפט גר etc. (V. 17) must also be able to be taken as having the same tendency, as the motive referring to both of them וזכרת etc. (V. 18), as it does in Ch. 15,15 and XVI,12, and indeed here too again in V.22 gives the same explanatory motive for the harvesting laws towards גר יתום ואלמנה (the orphan, the widow, the stranger) is meant to make all these laws appeal to our hearts.

And the חידושי ר״ן on Sanhedrin (ibid) also explains that the wording of our text is not to be taken as meaning to prevent the improper action of a court actually carrying out the verdict for the penalty of the crime of a son on the father, or on the son for the father, a procedure which no court of law could even be thought of doing. But rather what it means is that politically and socially no member of a family should be made to suffer in any way even for capital crimes committed by a near or even nearest relative. עיקר קרא לא אתי לפוטרו מן העונש דהא פשיטא הוא אלא שהוא אזהרה על הדבר שלא יעלה על לב המושל לשפוך חמתו על הבנים בעון האב או על האב בעון בנים which is also why in Chron. II, XXV,4 reference is made to our verse here when it reports of Amaziah regarding the murderers of his father ואת בניהם לא המית (“But he put not their children to death, but did according to that which is written in the book of Moses etc.” I.L.). That, as the ר״ן explains further, no person who is in power should be bold enough to put himself in the place of the Divine Providence, which indeed has declared of Itself that פוקד עון אבות על בנים, that in It’s Rule, children כשאוחזין מעשה אבותיהם, if the pernicious tendency of their father is hereditary in them, have also to participate in making amends for the sins of their fathers, והײנו בדין שמים שיודעין בדין אחיזה מה היא ואם הוא אמת אם לא but that is the sole prerogative of the One Who alone knows how to judge heredity and whether in truth it is irretrievably working in the children. אבל דיני אדם הן אין בקיאין לידע אם אוחזין מעשה אבותיהם אם לאו but human judgment entirely lacks this knowledge, לפיכך מן הסתם מחזקינן להו כאלו אין אוחזין, so that human beings have always to assume that crime is not hereditary and must judge everybody by his actual deeds. והײנו דאמדינן בגמרא כשהוא אומר איש בחטאו יומתו בשאין אוחזין, שאחר שפירשו זה לדיני אדם הכי הוא שאין אוחזין שכך הוא בדינן בין שיהא אמת אם לאו, For all human judgment the sentence applies איש בחטאו יומתו, everybody only becomes a criminal through his own crimes, and the children of criminals are to be considered as אין אוחזין, not being tainted by crime, whether the human judgment is right in this or not. ע״ש.

In this sense then the לא יומתו אבות על בנים etc. would fit in very well with this whole group of laws concerning the treatment of socially depressed people. There are probably no more unhappy people, who feel themselves more hardly dealt with socially than the children and parents of murderers and criminals, and the primary tendency of this proclamation is to keep their own social and political blamelessness independently clear and unaffected in the Jewish national life.

But at the same time as it does not say: לא יומתו אבות בחטא בנים וגו׳ and that injunction is already given by the positive statement איש בחטאו יומתו, but it rather says quite generally לא יומתו אבות על בנים, that fathers are not to be brought to death by or through sons, nor sons through fathers, and altogether there is only one factor in Jewish law by which one person can be brought to capital punishment by another and that is by testimony, by this sentence, the Halacha quoted above is at the same time given that sons cannot give evidence in law against fathers; nor fathers appear as witnesses against sons. And there (ibid) the Halacha is further developed on out text that פסול קורבה, the rendering of the testimony of witnesses who are relatives invalid, is extended beyond father and son, that relations up to a certain degree of relationship cannot give evidence, not only against but even in favour of a person, and not only in criminal cases בדיני נפשות, but also in civil cases, בדיני ממונות, and not only in the case of a relative, but two relatives cannot both appear as witnesses for or against a third party. And, like the witnesses the judges may not be relatives of either of the parties nor to one another, and, according to the Jerusalmi (Sanhedrin 3,9) judges and witnesses should also not be related.

The degree of this relationship is reckoned from the descent from a common ancestor. Thus father and son, brother and brother is a relationship of the first degree, ראשון בראשון; first cousins between themselves form the second degree שני בשני; nephews and uncles, and grandson and grandfather are שני בראשון; great-grandsons and great-grandfathers, and also great-nephews and great uncles are שלישי בראשון, and so on. Now ,ראשון בראשון שני בשני שני בראשון are definitely פסול; concerning שלישי בראשון there are difference of opinion, further degrees are definitely כשרים. Regarding relationship marriages—“in-laws”—the general rule is that בעל כאשתו and אשה כבעל that if one could not give testimony in the case of a woman, on account of relationship, one would not be able to do so in the case of her husband, and who is unfit to give testimony in the case of a man could not do so in the case of his wife, and even תרי בעל כאשתו, for example, the husbands of two sisters are not valid as witnesses for or against each other. But the application of this sentence is subject to more detailed laws.

When we consider these regulations of this law, which makes relationship up to a certain degree between witnesses to each other, to the parties at law, probably also to the judges, and similarly also the members of the bench to each other, to the parties and probably also to the witnesses, a bar to functioning as witnesses or judges, and look for the reason for such a law, it has already been said in B.B. 159a, that the reason cannot lie in some lack of confidence in the credibility of the evidence given by relations, לאו משום דמשקר, for even a Moses and Aaron could not testify for or against a relation, and the reason could not possibly be because of any doubt of their truthfulness: לאו משום דמשקר דאי לא תימא הכי משה ואהרן לחותנם משום דלא מהימני הוא אלא גזירת המלך הוא שלא יעידו להם. But the reason must rather lie in the very nature of the Jewish institution of jurisdiction by judges and witnesses.

It is a procedure of the Law of God given over to the nation to be practised in its name, and the judges and witnesses to function as its representatives and delegates. All their power and meaning lies solely in this representation and delegation. And indeed in a quite eminent sense that of the witnesses. For in criminal cases they have to warn the perpetrator at the moment of the act in the name of the Law of God, and refer to the paragraphs in the Torah which give the punishment relating to it, and after the act has been committed, it is they who have to appear before the court as public prosecutors demanding the verdict which they have pronounced. So that witnesses form a necessary integral part of the nature of Jewish jurisdiction, and therefore in the Jerusalmi (ibid) that which in the Halacha is said of the bar of relatives primarily for witnesses is without further ado applied also to judges. ומנין שלא יהיו הדײנים קרובים זה לזה אמרה תורה הרוג על פי עדים הרוג על פי דײנים מה עדים אין קרובין זה לזה אף דײנין אין קרובין זה לזה. The common obligation of every Jewish man to the Torah and for the Torah forms the bond that joins two or more Jewish men to a group of witnesses, three, twenty-three, or seventy-one Jewish men into a judical tribunal, and is, at the same time, the basis on which witnesses stand towards the parties at law and to the judges, on which the judges stand towards the parties and the witnesses. That bond and this basis,—so we believe—undisturbed by the appearance of any other factor, is to be clearly obvious throughout the whole procedure at law. Only as members of the nation, as sons of the same common obligation to the Law, the Torah, in a word, solely as Jewish men are the witnesses to appear and conduct themselves to each other, to the parties, to the judges, and the judges towards each other, to the parties and to the witnesses. If any family relationship exists between any of these parties, then the whole of the more general bond would only be in the background behind that closer tie, and judges or witnesses would appear to be acting as relatives and not on the fundamental principle of the national unity, and the real basis of the duty and authorisation for their conduct would be obscured.

That would also be the thought that seems to be expressed in the deduction of the bar of relationship extending to the judges, which the Jerusalmi makes in Sanhedrin (ibid). For there the bar of relationship which is definitely fixed by the Halacha for witnesses and judges, is, as in the Babli, first found to be laid down and shown in our text. But then it goes on to say: עד כדון כר׳ עקיבא, this deduction from לא יומתו אבות וגו׳ is the teaching of Rabbi Akiva. But Rabbi Ishmael teaches that this law is derived from a different source: כר׳ ישמעאל מנײן תני רבי ישמעאל ושפטו העדה והצילו העדה שלא תהא העדה לא קרובי מכה ולא קרובי מוכה א״ר יוסי אם אתה אומר כן נמצאת אומר בית דין גואלי הדם מכאן וכו׳. In Numb. 25,24,25, the court is directed to be both judging guilty (ושפטו) and acquitting, delivering (והצילו), to act as עדה, as the representatives of the nation, between one accused of murder and the prosecuting relatives of the dead man. The concept that the nation as such, as עדה (a congregation of God and His Law I.L.) is to act between the parties, at once excludes its being a relative of either of them; and Rabbi Jose further makes this clearer by the reflection that a judge who was a relative of the dead man would appear to be himself a גואל הדם rather than a judge. The application of this principle also to the witnesses, and also to the mutual relationship of the witnesses and judges to one another is then further developed there.

V. 17. לא תטה וגו׳. We have already remarked on V. 16, how the position of this declaration, its connection with the immediately following לא תחבל, but quite specially with the motive given at the end על כן וגו׳ וזכרת וגו׳ which clearly refers to לא תטה משפט גר וגו׳, and compared with V. 23 and other similar places, all speak strongly for the assumption that the tendency of this לא תטה משפט is not meant to be limited solely to the legal sphere of the actual administration of justice. לא תשא שמע שוא (Ex. 23,1), בצדק תשפט עמיתך (Levit. 19,15) offer analogies for a similar way of taking it. Here, too, by משפט גר יתום, apart from the general rights to be preserved legally, the rights which are specially conceded to the stranger and the orphan in the social life of the nation—as indeed they at once follow in verses 19-22—are to be understood. (cf. משפט הכהנים, Ch. 18,3). If one were to understand the לא תטה משפט literally to be an injunction only not to twist the right in a case at law, then the contents of V.17 would say:- Do no flagrant injustice to an orphan stranger, and be considerately kind to the widow! One could also hardly take it to mean the prohibition of judically twisting the right, a prohibition which does not affect us only because we are Jews, of which it could be said: וזכרת כי עבד וגו׳ על כן אנכי מצוך לעשות את הדבר הזה. But the duty of considerate kindness towards socially depressed people could indeed very well be brought home to the hearts of the Jewish national society with reminding reference to their own feelings when they were slaves in Egypt. And so here too—apart from the special warning against wronging the rights of an orphaned stranger—the admonition could still quite specially be given not to curtail the orphaned stranger from the favours and gifts granted by Jewish Law. (See Ch. 27,19).

ולא תחבל בגד אלמנה. Even with the limitations given in Verses 10-13 for a משכון שלא בשעת הלואה (the distraining a pledge for payment when the payment is due to be paid I.L.) the pledge may not be taken from a widow, and according to סמ״ע and ט״ז on Ch.M. 96,14, a widow is only given as an example, but the prohibition applies to every single woman, even if she is still under her father’s protection. The ש״ך however refers the law only to a widow.

In B.M. 115a, the Mishna teaches the law which is also accepted as Halacha that, in accordance with the wording of our text, there is no difference between poor or rich widows, and from neither may pledges be taken: אלמנה בין שהיא עשירה בין שהיא עניה אין ממשכנין אותה שנא׳ לא תחבול בגד אלמנה But ר׳ שמעון teaches in the ברײתא that the Torah had only poor widows in mind, to whom the pledge had to be returned daily for their use (V.13), and by such daily visits of the creditor might easily come into evil repute amongst her neighbours.

This difference between the חכמים and ר׳ שמעון regarding the extent of the prohibition לא תחבול בגד אלמנה is a classic example of the principle of the fundamental difference of opinion between them as to whether דרשינן טעמא דקרא or לא דרשינן טעמא דקרא, whether or not the reason for a law is to be sought for its interpretation. ר׳ שמעון takes the reason for the law as being its foundation: because you are bound to return the pledge to her daily through which she might get a bad name amongst her neighbours the Torah says, “no pledges to be taken from widows”, so that this law, though expressed in general terms, is meant to apply only to poor widows. He is דריש טעמא דקרא. But the חכמים do not go into the reasons for the law, they are not דריש טעמא דקרא, and so, as the law is expressed in general terms, they hold it is to be applied generally to all widows. Quite mistakenly some people have taken the opinion of the חכמים that לא דרשינן טעמא דקרא to mean that it is wrong to try to find the reasons for the commands given in the Torah. But—apart from the fact that כ״מ on Rambam Isure Biah 12,1 says that the Halacha is in accordance with Rabbi Simeon, regarding which see ל״מ on Rambam Hilch. Malveh 3,1—תוספות already explains on Gittin 49b, ד״ה ר׳ שמעון and more fully on Sota 14a, ד״ה כדי ליגעה that the difference of opinion whether דרשינן טעמא דקרא or not in no way whatsoever refers to finding out the reasons for the commands in the Torah in general—for which indeed examples are at hand in abundance in the Talmud and Midrash—but only affects the question whether, in cases where the Law is given in quite general terms without any motive for it, one is justified in seeking the reason for it, the sense of which would limit its application to certain definite conditions. This is certainly denied by the חכמים. The actual words of תוס׳ in גטין 49b, are:- ור״ש היא דדריש טעמא דקרא. לא פליגי אלא היכא דאיכא נפקותא כגון גבי חובל בגד אלמנה וגבי לא ירבה לו נשים וה״ב משום האי טעמא שײמינן בדמזיק (כלומר משום דדריש ר׳ שמעון טעמא דמיטב שדהו כדי למנוע המזיקין מלהזיק). וכן סוטה י״ד א׳ ד״ה כדי ליגעה, ולא שײך למימר דדריש טעמא דקרא אלא היכא דנפקא לן מיניה מידי דמרבי מיניה (פי׳ רש״ל בחכמת שלמה וז״ל לאו דוקא אלא כלומר שמרבה לנו הטעם שום חידוש שזולתו לא הײנו יודעים ואפי׳ הוא למיעוט כדמסיק ודו״ק) וקרא סתמא כתיב וכולל הכל ואנו דורשין טעמו ואומרים זהו הטעם של פסוק הואיל וטעמו בשביל כך איכא דוקא כגון לא תחבול בגד אלמנה משמע בין ענײה ועשירה וקאמר ר״ש טעמא דקרא שאם אתה ממשכן אותה אתה משיא לה שם רע בשכינותיה מתוך שאתה משיב לה העבוט ונאמר ענײה דוקא אין ממשכנין אותה עב״ל. Accordingly it is only concerning limiting or extending or modifying a law that is not indicated in the text, but deduced from the apparent reason for the law, that the rule of the חכמים that לא דרשינן טעמא דקרא applies. But to try and find the reasons for the laws, as we have tried to do in our commentary, by which the actual carrying out of the law is in no ways to be altered, but on the contrary the given actual contents of the law would be carried out with the utmost possible understaning and completeness, and only endeavour to get at the thought which lies at the base of a law, such research is in no way touched by אי דרשינן טעמא דקרא, but rather, from times immemorial formed a part of the intellectual study of the sages in the Talmud and Midrash. We append a list of a few examples out of the different books dealing with the Torah.

Out of Exodus: מפני מה הקדים הכתוב לקיחתו של פסח: בא קודם לשחיטתו ד׳ ימים. פסחים קט״ו א׳: מרור זה על שום מה. קידושין ל׳ ב׳: השוה הכתוב כבוד אב ואם לכבוד המקום וכן בדין וכו. מדרש (ילקוט משפטים): וכי מה ראה ברזל ליפסל יותר מכל מתכות וכו׳ and so also מכילתא יתרו : המזבח נברא להאריך וכו׳. קידושין כ״ב ב׳ ורצע אדוניו וגו׳ מה נשתנה אוזן מכל איברים שבגוף וכו׳ מה נשתנה דלת ומזוזה מכל כלים שבבית אמר הקב״ה וכו׳. בבא קמא ב׳ א׳: לא הרי שור וכו׳ ולא זה וזה שיש בו רוח חיים וכו׳ ולא זה וזה שדרכן לילך ולהזיק וכו׳ וכן בהרבה לימודי ק״ו דרשינן טעמא דקרא. יומא פ״ה ב׳: במחתרת. מכילתא משפטים: חמשה בקר וגו׳ בא וראה כמה חביבה מלאכה וכו׳ חס המקום על כבודן של בריות וכו׳ בבא קמא ע״ט ב׳: מפני מה החמירה תורה בגנב יותר מגזלן. כתובות י״ח א׳: מפני מה אמרה תורה מודה מקצת הטענה ישבע

Out of Leviticus וקרן מזרחית דרומית לא היה לו יסוד מ״ט מזבחים נ״ג ב׳ -: מנחות ק״י א׳: נאמר בעולת בהמה אשה ריח ניחח וגו׳ לאמר לך אחד המרבה וגו׳. רבות ויקרא: והסיר את מוראתו העוף הזה פורח וטס בכל העולם ואוכל מכל צד ואוכל מן הגזילות ומן החמסים אמר הקב״ה הואיל והזפק הזה מלא גזילות וכו׳. שם: ונפש כי תקריב מנחה, ומה נשתנה מנחה שנאמר בה נפש אמר הקב״ה מי דרכו להביא וכו׳. תנא דבי אליהו: ואם מנחה על המחבת וכו׳ כיצד יש בו באדם דברי תורה יהא זהיר וכו׳ אמר לו הקב״ה בני שמא לא בללת מעשיך בשמן ואין שמן אלא תורה ומעשים טובים וכו׳. זבחים מ״א ב׳: מפני מה נאמר פרוכת הקדש בפר כהן משיח ולא נאמר בפר העלם דבר של ציבור משל למלך וכו׳. ספרא ויקרא: כאשר יורם משור זבח שלמים מה שלמים מביאין שלום לעולם אף זה מביא שלום לעולם. ומעלה מעל בה׳ מה ת״ל לפי וכו׳ אבל המפקיד אצל חברו אינו רוצה שתדע בו נשמה אלא שלישי שביניהם. ירושלמי סוטה פ״ח ה״ט: במקום אשר תשחט העולה תשחט החטאת שלא לפרסם את החטאים. סיפרא שמיני: ויאמר אל אהרן קח לך עגל מלמד שאמר משה לאהרן אהרן אחי אע״פ שנתרצה המקום לכפר על עונותיך וכו׳ וכו׳ יבא שעיר ויכפר על מעשה שעיר יבא עגל ויכפר על מעשה עגל. ושור ואיל לשלמים לפי שנידמית עבירה לשני מינים וכו׳ יבא שור ויכפר על מעשה שור וכו׳. נדה ל״א ב׳: מפני מה אמרה תורה יולדת מביאה קרבן וכו׳ ומפני מה זכר לשבעה ונקבה לי״ד וכו׳ ומפני מה אמרה תורה מילה בשמנה וכו׳, ומפני מה אמרה תורה נדה לשבעה וכו׳. ערכין ט״ז א׳: מה נשתנה מצורע שאמרה תורה בדד ישב מחוץ למחנה מושבו אמר הקב״ה הוא הבדיל בין איש לאשתו ובין איש לרעהו וכו׳. שם: מפני מה אמרה תורה מצורע יביא שתי צפרים לטהרו וכו׳. ילמדנו: מפני מה מצורע זה מטהר בגבוה שבגבוהים ובנמוך שבנמוכים בעץ ארז ואזוב וכו׳. פסיקתא: והובא אל הכהן והובה למה וכו׳, למה שוחט אחת ומשלח אחת. שבת כ״ב א׳: בשביל ד׳ דברים אמרה תורה להניח פאה וכו׳. ב״מ קי״א ב׳: וצריכא דאי אשמעינן אביון משום דלא כסיף למיתבעי׳ (וכיוצא רוב פעמים דעביד צריכותא דרשינן טעמא דקרא). סיפרא קדושים: והוצאת את האשה והבהמה וגו׳ בהמה מה חטאה אלא מפני שבאתה תקלה על ידה, וברבה: שלא תהא עוברת בשוק ויהו אומרים זו היא הבהמה וכו׳. ובפסיקתא אמור: אמור אל הכהנים משל למה״ד וכו׳ לפיכך וכו׳. רבה שם: והיה שבעת ימים, למה שבעת ימים כדי וכו׳ ד״א וכו׳. etc. etc.

Out of Numbers: והביא קרבנה עליה וגו׳ ולמה קמח שעורים: נשא תנחומא -  לפי שנהגה עמה מנהג בהמה וכו׳ לא יצוק עליה שמן למה וכו׳ שהשמן אור וקרוי יצהר וזו אהבה האפלה וכו׳ ולמה לא יתן עליה לבונה וכו׳ ולמה לוקח מים ועפר וכו׳. (עיין עוד סוטה י״ד א׳). נדרים י׳ א׳ מאשר חטא על הנפש וכי באיזה נפש חטא וכו׳. מנחות מ״ג ב׳ : מפני מה נשתנה תכלת מכל מיני צבעונים מפני שהתכלת דומה לים. פסיקתא חקת: ומפני מה נשתנה וכו׳ כל הקרבנות באים זכרים וכו׳. ראש השנה ט״ז א׳: מפני מה אמרה תורה הביאו עומר בפסח וכו׳ ומפני מה וכו׳ שתי הלחם בעצרת וכו׳ ומפני מה אמרה תורה נסכו מים בחג וכו׳ ואמרו לפני בר״ה מלכיות זכרונות ושופרות וכו׳ למה תוקעין בשופר של איל וכו׳. סיפרא מסעי: עד מות הכהן הגדול. רוצח מקצר ימיו של אדם וכה״ג מאריך ימיו של אדם אין בדין וכו׳ etc. etc.

Out of Deu. אם נאמר בכל לבבך ולא נאמר בכל מאדך וכו׳: סיפרא ואתחנן :שם חולין קל״ד ב׳: דורשי חמורות (מקראות הסתומים רש״י) היו אומרים הזרוע כנגד היד וכו׳ ולחיים כנגד תפלה וכו׳ קיבה כמשמעה וכו׳. סוטה מ״ד א׳: הירא וגו׳ שאם מתיירא מן העבירות שבידו לפיכך תלתה לו תורה וכו׳. שם מ״ו א׳: מפני מה אמרה תורה הביא עגלה בנחל אמר הקב״ה יבא דבר שלא עשה פירות ויערף במקום שאין עושה פירות ויכפר על מי שלא הניחוהו לעשות פירות. קידושין כ״א ב׳: יפת תואר לא דברה תורה אלא כנגד יצה״ר מוטב שיאכלו וכו׳ סיפרי כי תצא: וישבה בביתך בבית שנשתמש בו וכו׳ ורואה בנוולת סנהדרין ע״ב א׳: בן סורר ומורה נידון על שם סופו וכי מפני שאכל זה וכו׳ אלא הגיעה תורה לסוף דעתו שסוף מגמר וכו׳ אמרה תורה ימות זכאי ואל ימות חייב וכו etc. etc. See also תוספות יום טוב Sanhedrin 10,5).

V. 19. כי תקצר. The פאה ,מתנות ענײם and לקט and עוללות from the vine-yard have all been already ordered in Levit. 19,9,10 and XXIII,22, and there we have fully explained these harvest-gifts to the poor. That this duty of the harvest in its meaning of being conditional for happiness and blessing in the land, and as a continuous act of recognition for the redemption out of Egyptian slavery should be brought home to the minds of the people here at this juncture when the people were about to move into the land and independence, speaks for itself. At the same time a fresh harvest-gift which was not mentioned there is added here viz. שכחה and equally so, also for fruit trees.

כי תקצר קצירך בשדך. The thought of owning property is stressed here, thy harvest, thy field. You are standing now on your own soil, here Nature has worked for you, you have worked and cultivated it, yours is the blessed result which you are about to garner with your own strength or of that of those in your service. It is just this proud feeling of ownership against which—as we explained there—these מתנות ענײם come to admonish you, by the feeling of the duty of Zedaka that your food-producing fields are to flourish for those that have no land of their own. And if the פאה and עוללות duty is to admonish you that you may not consider the whole of your field or your vine-yard, not all that Nature has brought forth on your soil under the blessing of God, as having grown solely for you; the לקט and פרט duty that you may not greedily and jealously think that you must use the very last penny for yourself or that for which you have worked, that anything of that, which escapes you, you need not think lost, and therefore you have to have something standing in your fields and vineyards for the poor, and what escapes your cutting sickle and gathering hand must remain for the poor, then שכחה is now also added to them and teaches your mind too, that your thoughts directed to earning and getting and having may not avariciously and selfishly only think of yourself and what has once escaped your thought at your harvesting is also to be left to the poor. Moreover we have already pointed out there in Levit. that these gifts from the harvest are not meant so much to constitute your real care and provision for the poor as to be an admonition to your duty to care for them as, after all, פרט ,שכחה ,לקט (gleanings, forgotten sheaves, single grapes and those fallen off in the cutting I.L.) are quite dependent on chance, and the only one which is positive, and must of necessity be there, viz. פאה, can be discharged, according to the original law, מן התורה, with the smallest possible quantity אין לה שיעור למטה. Hence the law is quite precise as to what falls under the concept of עוללות ,פרט ,שכחה ,לקט. For they are just acts to admonish and remind us of our duty of fully providing for the poor and needy, and this is made clear by this definite precision. Taking them together, they express the thought: That which God makes grow in our fields and orchard is in the first place for ourselves, but in the second place, also for our necessitous brethren. So that what has once escaped our gathering or slipped from our mind at the harvest, is automatically, by God’s direction the property of the poor.

עומר ולא גדיש ,ושכחת עומר בשדה (Sifri), only a single sheaf but not a stack שיש בו סאתים, altogether only that is שכחה which as a rule one would only remember when one comes across it, but not anything that by reason of its size, its special shape, or special place, would recall it to our mind by itself שאתה שוכחו לעולם יצא שאתה זוכרו לאחר זמן (Pea. 6,5,6; VII, 1 ר״ש there. — לרבות את הקמה ,ושכחת וכו׳ בשדה (Sifri). Just as what is forgotten at the gathering-in, so is that which is overlooked at the cutting and left standing, also שכחה. It says: שלפניו אינו ,לא תשוב לקחתה שכחה שלאחריו שכחה מפני שהוא בבל תשוב. Only that for which he would have to go back is שכחה, but if he forgot to clear a patch in front of him it would not be שכחה (Pea, VI,3).
לגר וגו׳ יהיה. See Levit. 19,10.

V. 20. חבט .כי תחבם is knocking the fruit off with a stick, and thereon the Sifri says that in olden times one did not carefully gather the olives from the trees but was satisfied just to knock them down with sticks. הראשונים היו חובטין זיתיהם ונוהגים בו עין יפה. Perhaps this would be explained by the following:- in Chulin 131a, לא תפאר אחריך is taken to refer to two gifts, שכחה and לא תפאר ,פאה (Pial, like דשן): ממנו שלא תטול תפארתו, “one may not take off the “crown” i.e. the fruit that grows quite at the top of the tree, in other words, the duty of פאה for trees. :אחריך זו שכחה, not to take that which one has already left “behind”, what one has passed over. Now it is probable that if one does not use ladders, or climb up the tree, but stands below and knocks the fruit off, as a rule one does not reach quite to the top and the fruit there remains to be gathered subsequently. Thus that פאר would automatically be left. But as one has to leave it there intentionally, it is not in itself שכחה, and the לא תפאר would be an independent command for פאה: the top which is usually left to be gathered last, is to be left for the poor. But the law is thereby also implied that whatever else is אחריך, missed being gathered from the tree may not subsequently be picked, and thereby שכחה is declared for trees. The verse says: When you gather the fruit from your olive trees you may not finally pick off the פאר although you left it there with your full knowledge, not to speak of any other fruit, which you unintentionally forgot to gather. Similarly in the following verse לא תעולל אחריך. Also single grapes which, not having formed clusters, would normally be gathered after cutting down all the branches, but which you must not pick but leave to the poor (Levit. ibid.) do not come under the concept of שכחה as they are intentionally left. There too then there would be two prohibitions, עוללות and שכחה :אחריך.

V. 1 & 2. כי יהיה ריב. If verse 1 is taken as the introductory sentence to V. 2. and take the meaning to be:- If two men have a case before the court (V.1.) and the one is given a sentence for corporal punishment etc. etc. then a difficulty arises which it would be difficult to solve. Most cases of disputes between men that come before the court concern the question of mine and thine or compensation for injuries and damages. In neither case does the penalty of corporal punishment come in. Only in extremely rare cases in such processes could מלקות be inflicted e.g. if the estimated compensation for personal wounding was so tiny פחות משוה פרוטה (less than a farthing I.L.) that the court could not award compensation (Kethuvoth 32b) or, at the most, in a case of transgression of the law of taking pledges (Ch. XXIV) if, for some reason, it is impossible to be rectified by the return of the pledge (B.M. 115a; — see תוספות there and ל״מ on רמב״ם הל׳ מלוה ולוה XI,2). But it is hardly likely that the Torah would give the law for the infliction of corporal punishment referring just to such seldom-occurring exceptional cases.

But if we look into the position in which here the law concerning the penalty of מלקות occurs, and the close connection with which it is placed with the law of לא תחסום וגו׳ which immediately follows in the same section, then, — so it seems to us — the tendency of the teaching here is altogether not so much on the law of the מלקות punishment, as directed to the limitation of it. So that, just as in the preceding laws, kindness and consideration is demanded for socially depressed people, and in the immediately following one, considerate behaviour is demanded even for animals who serve us, so here towards a person who by sinful rebellion against the Torah has temporarily sunk to the level of an animal and has to be disciplined accordingly, the court is commanded to exercise careful consideration.

According to that—so we believe—verse 1 stands in a very marked contrast to verse 2. Verse 1 speaks, as indeed follows from the wording, of דיני ממונות, of disputes in money matters which the claimant and defendant bring to the court for a decision as to who is right. In such cases —as has repeatedly been declared to be their duty (Levit. 19,15; Deut. 1,17)—the court has to declare who is right without any considerations whatsoever, there והצדיקו את הצדיק if the one is settled by והרשיעו את הרשע of the other, there one cannot exercise forbearance or indulgence of the one without infringing the rights of the other, there the judge must declare what is right with the most extreme sharpness.

But where it is not a question of the legal claim of one person or another, where it concerns only the behaviour of a person charged with acting against the Torah and judgment has to be pronounced about a disciplinary punishment, as which we have already recognised the institution of מלקות on Levit. 19,20, there, the Torah certainly does draw limits, and establishes a completely individual treatment to be administered within those limits.

והיה אם בן הכות הרשע. This hypothetical wording assumes—as indeed the whole of the written Torah does—that the institution of the מלקות punishment had already been established and taught verbally, and now here, as already remarked, is only given, in connection with the preceding and succeeding laws, to stress the considerate limitation of the court of justice.

בן הכות like בן הכות .יהושע בן נון also like בן מות (Sam. I, XX,31). Expressing the liability to punishment by מלקות ,בן would be considering the punishment not as something cancelling but rather as such a factor, on the realisation of which either atoning or educative the whole moral continued existence of the criminal depends. Henceforth he is only a “son” of the punishment. And if this term only occurs in the Torah at the מלקות-punishment, that would only substantiate all the more what we remarked in Leviticus (ibid), that this is the only punishment which is of a disciplinary nature and which opens up to the one who receives it, a vista of further continuance of physical life with the past atoned for. (see on V. 3). Similarly this expression also occurs in connection with specialities of character: בן בליעל ,בן עולה ,בן חיל, and there too it designates the trait of character, good or bad, not as just occurring, as an accident, but as such a factor that governs the whole personality, of which a person is considered as appearing to be the product.

הפיל ,והפילו השפט is not just throwing down to the ground. ותפל מעל הגמל (Gen. 24,64) is translated by Onkelos ואתרכינת מעל גמלא, “she bowed herself down off the camel”, and here too, the Halacha teaches that he was bent forward over a pillar, כופת שתי ידיו על העמוד (Makkoth 22b; see רש״י there).

כדי רשעתו במספר, as many as he can bear at one time is what suffices for his guilt, and that number has to be fixed by the court in accordance with specialists’ advice. The מלקות-punishment is called in Levit. (ibid) בקרת and thereby designated as disciplinary punishment to be administered in accordance with a careful medical examination. This fixing the amount of punishment to be administered (up to the maximum prescribed in V. 3. I.L.) is called אומד.

V. 3. ארבעים יכנו לא יוסיף. The Halacha (Makkoth 22a) teaches that the maximum number of stripes is thirty-nine שנאמר במספר מנין שהוא סמוך לארבעים, or, according to Rashi’s version שהוא סוכם את הארבעים, the number that leads to forty. To establish this Halacha V.3. is usually taken as being the continuation of V.2, and the meaning to be: במספר, “in a fixed number, namely, within forty, may he strike”. Accordingly, not forty but thirty nine. ריטב״א on Makkoth (ibid) remarks that arithmetically the nine units of a decade are the real numerators, במספר, of it, as ten looks on the whole as one unity. So that מספר ארבעים would then be thirty-nine. But nevertheless the limitation to thirty-nine would still be a traditional Halacha (analogous to the תספרו חמשים יום Levit. 23,16 which the Torah itself in Deut. 16,9 reckons as a counting of only forty-nine days שבעה שבעות תספר לך). The reference to taking the two verses as continuous would be merely רמז.

But if we consider the words ארבעים יכנו לא יוסיף more closely, by the accentuation, they definitely do not form two sentences, but one sentence. Just as little as מצוא שפתיך תשמר ועשית (Ch. 23,24), כי תועבה היא לפני ה׳ (Ch. 24,4) כי תשה ברעך משאת מאומה (Ch. 24,10), לא תעשק שכר עני ואביון (V.14) etc. So that it is as much as saying לא יוסיף יכנו ארבעים. But הוסיף to go on doing something is by no means always construed only with the infinitive but also with the tempus finitum of the following verb. Thus כי לא יוסיף יבא בך ערל וטמא (Is. 52,1). כי לא אוסיף ארחם בית ישראל (Hosea 1,6), and the wording of our text, quite in accordance with the Halacha, would say,” he shall not go on to smite him forty”.

פן יוסיף להכתו על אלה מכה רבה, this is explained in Makkoth 23a: אין לי אלא מכה רבה מכה מועטת מנײן ת״ל לא יוסיף א״כ מה ת״ל מכה רבה לימד על הראשונות שהן מכה רבה, i.e. by the preceding לא יוסיף every stroke going beyond the number allotted to him is forbidden. Here the מכה רבה refers to אלה (this big beating I.L.) the number of strokes allotted to him is already considered a large number, so that any stroke given beyond that, together with them would most certainly be a מכה רבה. Or the מכה רבה refers solely to the ראשונות by themselves. However many or however few were allotted to him in accordance with his bodily constitution, the mere fact, as Rashi explains שניתן להכותו בעל כורחו, that it is permitted, nay, commanded to strike a man against his will makes every blow a מכה רבה, so that every despotic additional blow becomes a degradation, ונקלה אחיך וגו׳.
כשלקה הרי הוא כאחיך ;ונקלה אחיך לעיניך (ibid) once he has received the prescribed strokes, he is restored to your respect, he is again your equal, אחיך and no longer הרשע as he was called hitherto.

But the Halacha teaches at the same time from this that קלון, disgracing degradation of a culprit is never the intention of the Law of the Torah, so much so, that if a criminal, at the first stroke, yea, even if at the first raised arm, from nervous fear micturates or defecates, ,קלקול בין ברעי בין במים, further punishment has at once to be foregone. As we have already pointed out in Levit. (ibid) how the whole execution of this law bears the character more of an educative correction than a means of punishment.

We have already remarked on the close connection between the law of מלקות and the immediately following prohibition לא תחסום, and, from that, found the tendency of the מלקות-laws lay in the prescribed consideration even for people who, by direct rebellion against the Torah had temporarily lowered themselves to the level of animals. Also at the execution of the punishment consideration was given to this connection. The leather instrument had to be made out of straps—the length and breadth of which had to be of the exactly prescribed measure—of שור and חמור hide. From oxen with reference to לא תחסום שור וגו׳, from asses with reference to Isaiah I: ידע שור קונהו וחמור אבוס בעליו ישראל לא ידע וגו׳ and this is explained אמר הקב״ה יבא מי שמכיר אבוס בעליו ויפרע ממי שאינו מכיר אבוס בעליו that thereby the culprit is told how he, by his direct disobedience to the Law of God had disavowed a consciousness which even an animal does not lack. The animal obediently working in the service of man is conscious thereby of the master who feeds him; the human being who denies the obedience of service to the Divine Laws proves thereby that he has abandoned the consciousness, at least that the consciousness has no power to guide his actions, the consciousness of Who is his Master and to Whom he owes his existence and keep.

The law which places the prohibition of failing to have consideration for animals working obediently in human service in such close connection with the punishment for human beings who rebel against the obedient service they owe to God, has given, just by this prohibition לא תחסום the classical example for all those commands in the Torah, the wilful transgression of which is punishable by מלקות. They are all those that are דומיא דלאו דחסימה, which do not essentially differ from this prohibition.
לא תחסום is a לאו, a prohibition, and מלקות is only incurred by transgression of a prohibition but not for failing to perform a positive command.

לא תחסום is a complete prohibition in itself, and is not attached to any positive command to be performed if it is transgressed. But a prohibition which becomes transformed to a positive command when it has been transgressed is not subject to לאו הניתק לעשה אין לוקין עליו :מלקות (see on Ch. 22,7).

לא תחסום forbids a procedure that involves a direct action. A prohibition which is transgressed by word of mouth only, is not subject to :מלקות לאו שאין בו מעשה אין לוקין עליו. Exceptions are נשבע (Ex. 20,7); ממיר (Levit. 27,10); מקלל חבר בשם (Levit. 19,14); מוציא שם רע (Deut. 23,13); עדים זוממין (Deut. 19,16). — see below and Shevuoth 21a, תוספות there).

לא תחסום comprises just one definite prohibition. Prohibitions which are classed together and come under the heading of one pronounced prohibition are not subject to אין לוקין על לאו שבכללות :מלקות (see Levit. on XIX,26,p. 548).

לא תחסום is not made liable in the Torah to any other judical punishment. But a prohibition, the transgression of which is made liable to judical capital punishment for which the prohibition gives the warning is not to be punished by מלקות even if at the moment of transgression the perpetrator of the deed was warned of his liability to מלקות and not of capital punishment (so that the latter could not be inflicted I.L.): לאו שניתן לאזהרת מיתת ב״ד אין לוקין עליו.

Taking all together then, the rule holds that all prohibitions given in the Torah are punishable with מלקות except ,לאו שבכללות לאו שאין בו מעשה, לאו שניתן לאזהרת מיתת בית דין (מכות י״ג ב׳ סנהדרין ס״ג א׳, (פסחים מ״א ב׳.

The fact that neither neglecting to fulfil a command nor a transgression which involves no action is liable to מלקות is completely in keeping with the fundamental conception that by מלקות the transgression and rebelling physical part of human beings is to be taught by physical feelings its submission to the consciousness of its duty to obey the commands of God. At לאו שבכללות the special precision of the warning which was to be given would be lacking, particularly according to the acceptance of חדא מיהת לקי (Pessachim 41b), and at לאו שניתן לאזהרת מיתת ב״ד, just by the liability to judical capital punishment all reference to the diciplinary bettering idea of the מלקות punishment is taken away from the prohibition. (but nevertheless see תוספות Sabbath 154a).

To the words כדי רשעתו (V.2) the Halacha is attached that in Jewish Law punishments can never be prescribed cumulatively, a canon which we have already explained on Levit. 24,19, 20 (refer to it there).

On Ch. 19,19 we mentioned the Halacha which limits the application of ועשיתם לו כאשר זמם at false witnesses to cases where the lying charge refers to מיתה ,ממון or מלקות, but for other cases to which ועשיתם לו כאשר זמם cannot be literally applied, prescribes מלקות. Now it is worked out in Makkoth 2b, that this מלקות cannot be taken simply as the result of the transgression of the prohibition לא תענה ברעך עד שקר as this is a לאו שאין בו מעשה, and a hint of this Halacha, רמז לעדים זוממין שלוקין is taught from our text of the מלקות institution itself. For, taking V.1 כי יהיה ריב וגו׳ והצדיקו וגו׳ והרשיעו not, as we believed, in contrast to, but as an introduction to V.2, the question would then not be a general one, and the והצדיקו וגו׳ והרשיעו could not refer to the judges. For, as we remarked at the beginning, as a rule in cases referring to מלקות there are no two opposing parties involved, and the והצדיקו את הצדיק would, in any case be irrelevant. משום והצדיקו את הצדיק והרשיעו את הרשע והיה אם בן הכות הרשע (בתמיהא). So כי יהיה ריב בין אנשים analogous to ועמדו שני האנשים אשר להם הריב לפני ה׳ (Ch. 19,17) — can only refer to two parties of witnesses who oppose each other in court, of whom the last would present as innocent the one charged by the first witnesses, and make these witnesses themselves the guilty ones אלא עדים שהרשיעו את הצדיק ואתו עדים אחריני והצדיקו את הצדיק דמעיקרא ושוינהו להני רשעים והיה אם בן הכות הרשע etc. But this way of taking it is declared even there to be only a רמז, and everywhere else this place in the Torah is taken as the general teaching of the institution of מלקות.

The saying of the Torah פן יוסיף is at the same time the general prohibition of any unauthorised striking of anybody else. The one who even only raises his hand to strike is already called a רשע (Sanhedrin 85a; 58b).

V. 4. חסם .לא תחסום phonetically related to עוצם עיניו) עצם Is. 33,15). אסם means to close, to obstruct אשמרה לפי ומחסום (Ps. 39,2.) In accordance with the general term חסם any hindering an animal from eating the produce on which it is working, even by shouting at it חסמה בקול is forbidden (B.M. 90b). This חסימה בקול is considered as a שיש בו מעשה because by his shout a prohibited action is immediately achieved (see תוספות there; — cf. מ״מ and ל״מ on Rambam הל׳ שכירות XIII,2).

According to Rambam (there) the limitation מחובר בשעת גמר מלאכה ובתלוש עד שלא נגמרה מלאכתו as applied to the workmen (Ch. 24,25,26) does not seem to apply to the prohibition לא תחסום. For there in paragraph I. it says “an animal must be allowed to eat all the time it is working either on material that has not yet been cut or after it has been cut”, although according to B.M. 99a לאקושי חוסם לנחסם ונחסם לחוסם וכו׳ and (ibid) כרוך ותני מה דיש מיוחד דבר שלא נגמרה מלאכתו למעשר ולחלה וכו׳ the laws governing workmen and animals in this respect would seem to be the same. So also המרכסות בתבואה according to פירש״י ותוספות which case, it is true, Rambam takes in a different way. וצ״ע.

V. 5. כי ישבו אחים וגו׳. The subject of the preceding laws was the consideration, benevolence and kindness which the Torah commands to be shown to widows, orphans and strangers, and finally to criminals and animals. Now the group of laws dealing with these various duties of love concludes with a similar duty to be performed even towards a dead man and his remembrance amongst the living. The command to the brother-in-law to marry the widow, יבום and חליצה, which follows here is manifestly definitely of such a nature, a duty of love towards the deceased brother, and can in no ways be taken as having primarily in mind the care of the widow left behind. For the duty of יבום is solely dependent on the circumstances of the dead man and not on those of the widow he leaves. If there are any descendants begotten by him through another wife, however distant the relationship of these descendants may be, the יבום-duty does not apply, however alone the widow may be. On the other hand, if there is no such descendant existing, the duty to marry the widow applies, however many children she may have from an earlier marriage. In any case the ולא ימחה שמו בישראל (V.6), מאן יבמי להקים לאחיו שם בישראל (V.7), לא יבנה את בית אחיו (V.9) make it quite clear and leave no room for doubt that consideration for the deceased brother and his memory is the leading thought of these laws of the Torah.

The very first command פרו ורבו and for this purpose וכבשה (Gen. 1,28), the command to beget children and to bring them up and educate them, and for both these purposes to acquire property and possessions formed the first earthly calling of human beings. The accomplishment of this calling comprises the concept of a home, בית, the real “bricks” of which are בנים, children, (see Gen. on Ch. 15,2, p. 284). Now the case discussed in our text here is the following:- a man has tried to carry out this mission by founding a home and marrying a wife, by which he could have hoped to accomplish it, had it been granted to him together with her to beget children (פרו I.L.) who would live after them; and by their combined work of educating them, bring them up to be reproductions of their moral and spiritual selves (ורבו I.L.), and for that purpose administer together and spend the smaller or greater means which God had granted him. But he had not reached this aim. He would depart this life without leaving a descendant to whom the smaller or larger means he had acquired would accrue for him to carry on, sooner or later, life on the lines his father had started. In any case the man departs this life with the painful thought that immediately with his death there would be nobody to carry on his earthly duties in his memory. The wife whom he had called his own, would pass into quite other different circles, and what he had succeeded in obtaining of material possessions with which to go on building up his spiritual and moral existence on earth would be divided between his collateral relatives or their descendants—all this, had the Torah not created a spiritual moral substitute in the institution of יבום.

For if a nearest possible blood-relation survives him, one who has lived with him under the influence of the same atmosphere—as such would be only a brother, begotten by the same father, living at the same time as he did, not one born after him—then the demand is made on him to continue the marriage of his departed brother with the widow, with the idea of יבום i.e. in the sense of carrying on the building of the home which was left incompleted. And for this purpose he steps into the position of becoming the sole heir to all the material property of the dead man as soon as he takes over his widow. Over this marriage, which is to be considered solely as the continuation of the previous one—and consquently, according to the original law did not require fresh קידושין—as well as over the heritage which accompanies it, the name of the deceased remains hovering in spirit, so that there should be the possibility for his spiritual and moral influence, to be impressed on such a marriage and its results, a marriage made in his name with the idea of perpetuating his memory. An influence, which, after all, must be able to be so effective that the consciousness of it—וידע כי לא לו יהיה הזרע (Gen. 38,9).—in a bad brother in unworthy narrow hard-heartedness, could be considered by God as capital wickedness.

יחדו ,שהיתה להם ישיבה אחת בעולם .כי ישבו אחים יחדו, brothers living contemporaneously, excluding one born after the death of the deceased, פרט לאשת אחיו שלא היה בעולמו (Yebamoth 67b); further מיוחדים :יחדו בנחלה ,פרט לאחיו מן האם, only such brothers who are united in the rights of inheritance, excluding brothers from the mother’s side (see Numb. XXVII, on 9-11).

עײן עליו :ובן אין לו, search if there is no child existing from one of his descendants. The concept בן here is to be taken in its widest sense, any descendant, whether through male or female descent, even ממזר would be included, who, as we remarked on Ch. 23,3 is in no way curtailed in civil rights. Cf. ובן אין לו in the laws of inheritance (Numb. 27,8), only here the concept בן, by ולא ימחה שמו בישראל naturally includes a daughter and her descendants whereas in the laws of inheritance בן in contrast to the לבתו which follows there has to be taken strictly as a son and his descendants. Only בנו ובתו מן השפחה ומן הנכרית and their descendants would be excluded who are not מיוחסים אחריו (See on Ch. 7,4). Quite the same extension applies to אחים לענין יבום (Yebamoth 22b, תוספות there).

לא תהיה אשת המת החוצה, this forbidden marriage of a יבמה to anybody but the יבום is called יבמה לשוק. Hence יבמה לשוק is מחײבי לאוין. In Yebamoth 92b. it is even questioned whether by לא תהיה לאיש זר a יבמה לשוק is not given the character of חײבי כריתות, that ,לא תהיה בה הויה לזר אין קידושין תופסין בה.

יבמה יבא עליה. With ביאה עליה she becomes his wife. היבמה נקנית בביאה (Kiddushin 13b) the ביאה effects ליקוחין whereas in other cases לקוחין must precede (see Ch. 24,1), and originally קידושין did not take place with a יבמה, as the יבום marriage is the result of the קידושין of the deceased whose marriage it carries on. But although the יבום-marriage is to be made in that sense and also to be continued permanently in such a sense, it says ולקחה לו לאשה ויבמה, she nevertheless becomes the complete wife of the יבם in every respect with the ביאה עליה, it says ,יבמה יבא עליה ולקחה לו לאשה כיון שלקחה הרי היא כאשתו לכל דבר, the marriage could subsequently only be dissolved by גט but not by חליצה. (Yebamoth 39a). The widow of a man who has died childless, who thereby is placed into a relationship with his brother or brothers, and has to wait for the act of יבום, or as we shall see later, of חליצה, is called שומרת יבם, and the relation in which the קידושין of the deceased are still effective and can only be solved by יבום or הליצה is called זיקה a bond, so that she is also called זקוקה.

V. 6. והיה הבכור וגו׳ יקום על שם וגו׳. In Yebamoth 24a, the Halacha is taught that יקום על שם etc. does not direct the name of the deceased to be given to him, but that he receives the heritage left by the dead man and steps into his shoes, similarly to what it says of the brothers of Ephraim and Menasseh, על שם אחיהם יקראו בנחלתם, that they should be able to exercise their rights of heritage in the future Land only in the names of their brethren. And anyway it does not say here יקרא על שם but יקום על שם. But קום means to take up a right, as said in the passive of the field of Ephron: ויקם שדה וגו׳ (Gen. 23,17,20) so here actively of those who obtain the rights. קום על שם אחיו המת says literally “he is to appear on the ground of the name of his dead brother”, he has to assert the rights which his brother had, in a legal sense he is the “bearer” of his name. The Halacha teaches further that the subject of יקום is the same as that to which אחיו refers, so that it does not refer to some child that is expected from this marriage, of whom then it should have said אחי אביו, but comes to say that he, the יבם, by marrying the widow, takes over the rights to the property of the deceased. Finally the Halacha (there,b,) that the יבם is also the subject of והיה הבכור the one, in this succession to the rights of property of the deceased, and for them he is called בכור to give him in the matter of taking over the right only in the limited manner, לגריעותא, in which a firstborn gets the special first-born double portion, the מה בכור אינו נוטל בראוי .חלק בכורה כבמוחזק אף האי אינו נוטל בראוי כבמוחזק, just as the בכור can only assert his right of the firstborn on property which is actually there at the death of the father, but not on money or property which only comes in after the death, so the יבם also gets the property which was already in the possession of his brother at the time of his death, but has no right to possessions to which the brother had only legal claims and expectations, and of reversions. If, for instance, there are several brothers of the deceased and their father had died during the lifetime of the deceased brother so that he together with the brothers inherited the estate, then he, the יבם now receives in addition to his own share as son, by his marrying the widow, the share of his deceased brother. Exactly as if he were the בכור amongst the brothers. But if the father died only after the death of the brother whose widow the יבם marries, he only shares equally with his brothers the legacy which was only ראוי but not מוחזק at the time of the death of the brother (see on Ch. 21,17).

Both the special laws which characterise the right of the firstborn, as remarked there, viz. that בן שנולד לאחר מיתת אביו, a son born after the death of his father has not the right of a firstborn and that בכור אינו נוטל בראוי כבמוחזק apply in the same way to the יבום. A brother who was born after the death of a deceased brother, שלא היה בעולמו, does not become a יבם, and also a יבם has only rights to the fortune which is מוחזק but not to that which is only ראוי. Both institutions rest on similar lines, in the thought that the dying man sees in the בכור the foremost, in the יבם the most exclusive person to carry on the rights of property referring to pecuniary matters of his own personality. Quite corresponding to this idea the Halacha also teaches there (on a) that calling the בכור ,יבם implies that if there are several brothers, the Mitzva of יבום falls, in the first instance on the eldest of them מצוה בגדול ליבם לא רצה הולכין אצל אחיו הקטן.

והיה הבכור אשר תלד would accordingly mean:- and he becomes the the first child that she bears (to the deceased) i.e. not only in the child which is expected to be born by her through this marriage which has been made with that idea, but already at once with the marriage the deceased obtains someone to carry on his name in matters relating to the rights of his property; the brother-in-law whom she marries comes to the deceased in the rights of a first-born son, who as it says further יקום על שם אחיו המת; and by this giving the legacy together with the widow to the brother, the spiritual moral name of the deceased, as well as his good name referring to the legality of his pecuniary matters is kept, ולא ימחה שמו בישראל.

That this traditional way of taking it, handed down in the Gemora, which, as it says there אפיקתיה מפשטיה לגמרי, on the face of it, takes the meaning of this verse quite away from the apparent meaning of its literal wording, that this is the one real meaning of על שם אחיו המת, of ולא ימחה שמו מישראל as well as להקים שם בישראל in the following verse is quite definitely shown in a procedure, and the report of it, which is similar to יבום. In Ruth 4,5,10, the transferring of the property of Machlon, who died childless, with the marriage of his widow to the near relative Boas is declared to be a means להקים שם המת על נחלתו ולא יכרת שם המת מעם אחיו ומשער מקומו (“to raise up the name of the dead upon his inheritance, that the name of the dead man be not cut off from among his brethren and from the gate of his place” I.L.). And Rashi (there) also explains: להקים מתוך שאשתו יוצאה ובאה בנחלה ומכנסת ומוציאה אומרים ,שם המת על נחלתו זאת היתה אשת מחלון שמו נזכר עליה (as Machlon’s widow remains at the inheritance of her deceased husband, and is its mistress, and people say “that is the widow of Machlon”, his name is also not lost from what was his inheritance in Israel). And also the son who was then born to Ruth was not given the name of Machlon, as it certainly would have been done if the words which Boas quoted to express his intention להקים שם המת etc. meant “to keep up the name”. Yea, those that gave the child the name Obed and not Machlon said that with it Naomi had been given a son again because her daughter-in-law with whom she was still united in love had born it, and those who said” יולד בן לנעמי״ are called “the ones who gave the child its name”: ותקראנה לו שם! By that one can peer into the life of a people in which not externals like “names” in their literal sense, but spiritual and moral conditions and influences guided thoughts and actions. And it is on the basis of such a life of people activated by spiritual and moral points of view that our יבום law stands.

Was not the thought which sees in the spiritual and moral share in the birth and bringing up of a child a substitute for one’s own childlessness, that made a Sarah say right at laying the foundation of our people: אולי אבנה ממנה (Gen. 16,2). and a Rachel ותלד על ברכי ואבנה גם אנכי ממנה (ibid XXX,3).

Thus a dying childless man may look to one of his brothers together with the wife he leaves behind him and to his property and look to a married life and home as a continuation of his own married and home life, as a continuation of his own existence and endeavours on earth, and say to himself: לא ימחה שמי מישראל.
V. 7. ואם לא יחפץ וגו׳. But the command to perform the duty of יבום is not an absolute one. There can be:-

(a) existing degrees of relationship between a surviving brother and the widow, she could be his daughter, the sister of his wife, altogether one of the עריות חײבי כריתות between whom ולקחה לו לאשה would be legally impossible because אין קידושין תופסין בחײבי כריתות (see Levit. on XXI,7). To such a brother-in-law the widow is not bound in any way, does not come into the relation of זיקה and if he is the only one, the whole mitzva of יבום וחליצה does not apply at all; and not only the widow herself, who is in the ערוה-relationship to the surviving brother, but if the deceased had other wives, they too, as צרות ערוה are also, without further ado, immediately מותרות לשוק, as we already worked out on Levit. 18,18. For although אשת אח itself is an ערוה שיש בה כרת (ibid. V.16), the Torah has here expressly abrogated this אסור ערוה in the special case of an אח מן האב dying without having children, more, in such cases where there is no other ערוה relationship, commanded the marriage with the brother-in-law. But where there is another איסור כרת in the way of the ולקחה לו לאשה the two prohibitions remain in force, and neither יבום nor חליצה takes place.

(b) The whole institution can be set aside for physical reasons. At congenital incapability for fatherhood or motherhood, סריס חמה or אילונית (see Ch. 23,2; Levit. 22,24) on the part of the deceased, the brother, or the widow, the whole idea of the expectations which form the basis and purpose of the institution is lacking and neither יבום nor חליצה takes place.

(c) But the ולקחה לו לאשה can be possible and the marriage legally binding but the contraction, and in any case the continuation of the marriage inadmissable by law, there can be objections of לאוין and עשה, such as אלמנה לכה״ג, גרושה וחלוצה לכהן הדיוט, ממזר etc. at which although קידושין תופסין, (the marriage is binding i.e. see Levit. on XXI,7) nevertheless (as אלמנה מן הנישואין to a כה״ג which is prohibited to him by both a negative and positive command, viz. אלמנה לא יקח and בתולה יקח, and the positive command of יבום does not abrogate both a positive and negative command) in such cases even contracting the marriage, and in other cases of simple לאוין, the continuation of the marriage would be legally inadmissable, and divorce enforced.

(d) there are cases where both the contraction and continuation of the marriage would be completely possible legally, but other considerations, such as great difference of age, incurable diseases, unpleasant occupations or infirmities render the marriage impracticable and undesirable. In Yebamoth 4a, regarding such cases it refers to the immediately preceding law in V.4. where consideration is commanded for the feelings of even an animal and hence teaches: מנין ליבמה שנפלה לפני מוכה שחין שאין חוסמין אותה (כירש״י אין סותמין טענותיה לכופה להתײבם לו) שנאמר לא תחסום שור בדישו וסמיך לי׳ כי ישבו אחים יחדו וגו׳, and in Kethuvoth 77a, other bodily informities and unpleasant occupations are placed in the same category as מוכה שחין.
