For such and similar cases which fall under the categories of c. and d. in which for legal or desirable reasons the יבום-marriage is judged to be not permissable or suitable, the Torah has ordered the following מצות חליצה to take the place of מצות יבום, and has placed the judgment of whether it is permissible or suitable (V. 8.) to be considered and decided by the communal legal authorities, and in accordance with this authority placed in their hand our legal authorities have decided for us now that the Mitzva of חליצה is to be the rule.

For the Halacha (Yebamoth 101,b) has explained the ודברו אליו (“and they shall speak to him” I.L.) of V.8 to mean not only to persuade him to perform the mitzva of יבום desired by the widow but equally so to dissuade him from יבום and persuade him to perform the mitzva of הליצה, altogether to discuss the case and advise what is most suitable to be done according to the circumstances. Yea in that explanation the examples they give are just of the latter eventuality, to dissuade him from יבום:- ודברו אליו מלמד שמשיאין לו עצה ההוגנת לו שאם היה הוא ילד והיא זקנה הוא זקן והיא ילדה אומרים לו מה לך אצל ילדה מה לך אצל זקנה כלך אצל שכמותך ואל תכניס קטטה בביתך i.e. the elders advise him as to what is suitable in the case; if he is young and she old, he old and she young, they say to him:- what do you want with a young girl, what do you want with an old lady, look out for one of your own age and do not bring dissatisfaction and quarrels into your home! So that the halacha explains as examples of the intervention of the elders just the alternative opposite side of the introductory solution to the case presented by our text. But if we examine the wording of the text itself mere closely, verse 8 does speak of the opposite eventuality to that given in V. 7. For in normal construing the עמד אמר is not in opposition to the intention of ודברו אליו but the intended and expected result of it. They speak to him, and as a result of that he stands up and says: לא חפצתי לקחתה. So that it speaks, as the Sifri also expressly remarks, of the case where, regardless of the difference between their ages עמד ואמר שישאנו, he had come there with the proposal to marry her, and only as a result of their remonstrances: עמד ואמר לא חפצתי לקחתה, he declares that he does not wish to take her. If the ודברו אליו had been in the sense of their persuading him to יבום which however was fruitless, the text would surely have run somewhat like והיה אם לא ישמע אליהם ועמד ואמר. But as it is, in the Torah introducing the institution of חליצה, in its usual pithy way it goes over to the other eventuality and prefers to teach חליצה in the case where it agrees with the decision of the elders and is a result of their persuasion. Even if one were to take the וקראו לו ודברו אליו in strict connection with the preceding, one could nevertheless only take the ועמד ואמר as a result of their speaking to him and persuading him, and it would still speak of the case where the decision to חליצה and not to יבום had the approval of the elders.

But with that, at the same time the standpoint is at once given from which alone the act of חליצה must be taken. One believes that one has to see in it an expression of reproach and scorn which the widow declares against her despised and duty-neglecting brother-in-law. A way of taking it which the whole tenor of the law does not permit. חליצה is just as much mitzva as יבום, so much so that the Gemora (Yebamoth 39b) can discuss which of the two mitzvas is in the front rank, whether מצות יבום קודמת or מצות חליצה קודמת. Have we not pointed out above under (c) and (d) the numerous cases in which חליצה and not יבום is commanded, where חליצה and not יבום is what is legally permitted or approved. So that by performing חליצה in such cases the brother-in-law is no less fulfilling God’s command than he would, in different circumstances be doing by יבום. It is impossible that the Torah would wish him to be punished by contempt for his faithful obedience to his duty. Also at the whole act he is not the one who passively endures, he is as the term goes חולץ ליבמתו, he with complete willingness instigates the widow to remove his shoe, and to perform and say all that follows; it is his act, he makes the widow take his shoe off, spit on the ground and say: “thus should happen to him, or thus must be done to him who will not build up the home of his brother, his name must or should be called in Israel, “the house of the shoeless one”. He expresses thereby that it is no lack of love for his departed brother nor indifference to his broken home that causes him not to marry the widow of his brother. A brother who was not ready, provided the law and circumstances allowed it, to build up the home of his brother would deserve himself to become “shoeless” to lose all firm standing and means of going forward on earth, he would have earned contempt, and his house should itself be called “the house from which the shoes had been taken”, the house which had lost standing and progress. The act is accordingly an act of publicly clearing any suspicion of lack of fraternal love, and expresses the deepest feelings of love and readiness for brotherly actions in which the attachment of Jewish families has its roots.

הא חפץ מייבם כל העולה ליבום עולה לחליצה :ואם לא יחפוץ האיש לקחת וגו׳ חליצה .וכל שאינו עולה ליבום אינו עולה לחליצה (יבמות כ׳ א׳) can only be done where there is a legal possibility of יבום i.e. לקוחין i.e. where קדושין תופסין. But relationship which exclude any קדושין and accordingly also זיקת יבום also exclude any זיקת חליצה (see (a) above).

ועלתה יבמתו השערה. As here the subject יבמתו is (apparently unnecessarily I.L.) repeated, which makes the second sentence ועלתה יבמתו not only simply the continuation of the first as it would be if it only said ועלתה השערה, the Gemora (Yebamoth 20a) learns therefrom, that in cases where it cannot be strictly said of a יבמה that לא יחפץ האיש לקחת namely in cases where, although there is no legal impossibility for יבום, there is still no legal permissibility for it—as אלמנה מן הנשואין לכה״ג (see (c) above)—nevertheless חליצה has to be performed. Thereby the text itself already indicates that there are cases where not יבום but חליצה is what the elders approve of, an eventuality which, as remarked above, the ודברו אליו ועמד ואמר also assumes.

השערה, to the place which is already appointed for legal proceedings, hence צריכי דייני למיקבע דוכתא (ibid 111b). For this is a procedure to which deep moral interests of every Jewish community is attached, it is not to be done in any hole-and-corner manner. The family feelings and points of view on family life which are to be fostered by the act of חליצה must be of such deep national importance that the bench of elders which has to intervene at it must be representative of the nation in purer national descent than is necessary at any other act in civil law. Whereas in the procedures of civil law Jewish descent on the maternal side suffices, at חליצה every member of the Beth Din must also be of Jewish parentage on the father’s side גר דן את חברו גד ואם היתה אמו מישראל דן אפילו ישראל ולענין חליצה עד שיהא אביו ואמו מישראל (Yebamoth 102a). Twice the Jewish national sphere is stressed as being that within which the institutions of יבום and חריצה are to be effective, להקים לאחיו ,ונקרא שמו בישראל ;תרי ישראל כתיבי גירס׳ הרי״ף) שם בישראל).

V. 8. ולא זקני עירה .וקראו לו זקני עירו, the text assumes that, as a rule the negotiations will take place before the elders of his city, that, as a rule the widow who requires חליצה will have to go to the place of the יבם (Sanhedrin 31b).

ודברו אליו ועמד ואמר, see above on V.7 — לא חפצתי לקחתה, whether it is that through the representations of the elders he has come to see the inadmissibility, the unsuitability or the inadvisability of the יבום act, or whether the decision he had previously arrived at was confirmed by them.

V. 9. ונגשה .ונגשה יבמתו אליו, the Niphal. Whereas נגש in the Kal is also used to designate a bold approach as למלחמה (Judges 20,23; Jer. 46,3); גש פגע בו (Sam. II, I,15); מי בעל משפטי יגש אלי (Is. 50,5); ויגשו לשבר הדלת (Gen. 10,19) etc., in the Niphal it is predominently a modest, shy approach, משה נגש אל הערפל (Ex. 20,21) ונגש משה לבדו (ibid. XXIV, 2); והקרבתיו ונגש אלי (Jer. 30,21); ואחרי כן נגשו בני ישראל (Ex. 34,32) etc. So that in this ונגשה יבמתו אליו every appearance of an unfriendly opposing feeling is removed from the act from the beginning.

וחלצה : the term חלץ assumes that the shoe is tied tightly to the foot, thus וחלצו את האבנים (Levit. 14,40), hence also used figuratively for being freed from being “bound” by trouble צדיק מצרה נחלץ (Prov. 11,8).

נעלו (from נעל to close in, to shut in against entry from outside) is a covering to protect the foot from external injury, hence not a cloth slipper but a leather shoe, and moreover has to be of not too thin leather and it must reach sufficiently high to protect the greater part of the foot, שחופה את רוב רגלו. To correspond to the symbolic character of this shoe it must be made entirely from leather and sewn with leather strips. It is also נעלו, not only belonging to him at the time of the חליצה, but must also be נעלו הראוי לו, fitted to his foot. And, as follows from the idea of חליצה, provided with leather knobs and loops and similar laces so that it represents firm walkings and standing “a strong stand and progress” (Yebamoth 101,102).

מעל רגלו, in accordance with the symbolic meaning of the act, the shoe must be directly on the bare foot without any other covering intervening material. It says מעל רגלו, with taking away the shoe the foot must be bereft of any protective covering (ibid).

וירקה בפניו. The preceding לעיני הזקנים refers to the whole act, accordingly also to the דכתיב לעיני זקנים וירקה, צריכי דייני למיחזי :רקיקה רוקא כי נפיק מפומא דיבמה (ibid. 106 b). With this רקיקה על הארץ בפניו לעיני הזקנים, with this spitting on the ground in front of him before the eyes of the elders and following it with ככה יעשה etc. the יבם makes the widow say that besides taking the shoe from off his foot, besides the loss of his own protected “standing and progress”, he, who, out of indifference and lack of heart would not build up his brother’s broken home would have to be shown publicly the contempt in which he was held. (see above on V.7).

With the taking off of the shoe the יבמה becomes free from all זיקת יבום, is מותרת לשוק, may marry anybody else, but is then אסור to the brother-in-law and also if there are more brothers of her late husband, to them too, for it is in representation of all the brothers that one of them performs the חליצה. Once that is done, none of them may ever marry her, כיון שלא בנה שוב לא יבנה, as the halacha teaches the איסור from the term אשר לא יבנה (Yebamoth 10b) or, as it says in the Sifri: אשר לא בנה ולא עתיד לבנות.

We have already referred, in the explanation of the terms, יקום על שם אחיו המת, להקים לאחיו שם בישראל, ולא ימחה שמו מישראל to the report of the procedure, so similar to that of יבום, between Boas and Ruth. This, however, cannot be taken as a real act of יבום. Apart from the fact that Boas was no brother, but only one of the nearest relatives of the dead man, and the law restricts the duty of יבום strictly to brothers, and even only to brothers from the same father, Ruth only became a Jewess after the death of her husband so that the very first condition for יבום was lacking. But we can indeed well take it, that the point of view and feelings for family ties which the Torah had engendered through the institutions of יבום and חליצה had obtained such fostering and attention in the lives of the people, had engendered such a hold of the duties of love in family life out of which the spirit, and feelings and actions of a Boas, a Ruth, a Noami automatically blossomed. Was not the field for such feelings of attachment to one’s family in joy and sorrow already prepared by the institution of Geula (Levit. 25,25 49), an institiution which also comes into the story of Ruth and Boas.

V. 11. כי ינצו וגו׳. The three last chapters were devoted primarily to the fostering of the feelings and ways of behaving which should form the principles of the Jewish national character. The commands for consideration and benevolence towards sufferers of any kind, towards those who are sensitive to harshness on account of their lot and position in life are quite specially in the foreground in them. This whole catalogue of social laws closes with maxims expressed in few but weighty words by which the warning against self-forgetting coarseness and dishonesty of any kind which, on the other hand, can well be paired with kindness and charity is added to the foregoing and finally concludes with a reference to the complete opposite of the whole picture of the character, the fostering and ever progressing realisation of which is expected from the Jewish nation; with a reference to Amalek whose ultimate disappearance from the community of mankind, and making an end to the glorifying remembrance of his exploits form one of the final aims of the historical mission of Israel.
כי ינצו וגו׳. See on Ex. 21,22.

כי ינצו וגו׳ והחזיקה במבושיו. According to the Gemora, B.K. 86b, and 27a, here complementing the laws in Ex. 21,19-25 on compensation for bodily injurieis, the law of בשת, insulting action, is laid down, compensation for the shame which such action inflicts to be added to the claim for נזק צער רפוי שבת (for the actual damage done to a limb etc. for the pain inflicted, for the costs of the healing, for the loss of earnings I.L.). The החזיק מבושיו is taken as the example of an insulting action, and ושלחה ידה והחזיקה במבושיו is taken to teach that, differing from the other four titles under which compensation must be paid in which the rule holds that אדם מועד לעולם וגו׳ (the claim must be met whether the injuriy was inflicted wilfully or accidentally I.L.), the duty to pay compensation for בשת only implies if the action was done intentionally, במתכוין. The “thou shalt cut off her hand” is only a figurative expression for rendering the hand harmless and inoffensive for the future by the payment of the monetary fine which the court is to impose, quite similarly to the עין בעין שן בשן וגו׳ (Ch. 19,21) at עדים זוממין which, as we explained there, can only mean money; and it says here, just as it does there לא תחוס עיניך, probably because the insulting act was done in passion and with the intention of saving her husband, which is also why, as it is taught there on 28a, it is only liable to legal fines if she could, and hence should, have saved her husband by other means (she could have pulled her husband away by his arm or belt etc. I.L.) להציל על ידי דבר אחר. The case here, on which the liability to punishment for an insulting action is taught, contains, by the conditions in which it is described, the admonition to keep control over one’s feelings even in justified emotion, and never degenerate into coarseness. This admonition is directed in the first place to women, who, more than men must keep afar from all coarse passion and quick temper, and who, if they take any part to decide the quarrels of their menfolk should remain the guardians of good behaviour and decency.

But that this case with such a tendency should find its place just here could be attributed to the immediately preceding law of the יבום and חליצה institution. For that is the one occasion where the Torah instigates a woman to step into the publicity of a court, and there publicly assert her demand for a man to marry her, both matters which otherwise in themselves would seem repugnant to the modest retiring nature of Jewish women. Added to that, the חליצה-act, making somebody bare-footed, in other circumstances would be in itself an act of בושת, and only there is raised to express a moral ennobling thought by the sense in which it is performed, and the weighty meaning which the Torah makes it express.

The opportunity which this gives to attach to that the teaching of the punishableness of any real active deed putting somebody to shame, and especially of the feminine sex keeping self-control in all circumstances and keeping aloof from everything pert and vulgar, seems to us to be self evident.

In the Sifri, apart from the way worked out above, and adopted by the Mishna and Gemora, another way of taking our verse is given, according to which והחזיקה במבושיו is not an example for בושת but as an example of behaviour when there is danger to life, בדבר שיש בו סכנה, and the וקצותה את כפה taken literally as the means of saving the threatened life of the contestant. And on that and on what it says further לא תחוס עיניך the duty is taught of saving the life of anybody who is threatened with losing it by wounding the one who is threatening, or if no other means are possible, even by killing him. This way of taking our verse does not occur in the Talmud, and the teaching that it is permissable to save the life of anybody attacked by killing the attacker (if no other means are possible I.L.) is taught from Ch. 22,26,27 above. רודף אחר חברו להרגו ניתן להצילו בנפשו (refer to there, and Ex. on Ch. 21,23, p. 313). Rambam, surprisingly enough, has both versions, the one accepted by the Mishna and Gemora in הל׳ חובל, I,9; that of the Sifri in הל׳ רוצח I,7,8. But, it seems to us that Rambam himself indicates the reason for this striking fact. In הל׳ רוצח he works out at length the way of taking our verse as רודף like the Sifri without further comment. But in הל׳ חובל it says: ומנין שהוא חייב בבושת בפני עצמו שהרי נאמר ושלחה ידה והחזיקה במבושיו וקצותה את כפה בכלל זה כל המבייש. According to that our verse includes both רודף and בושת. Primarily רודף, but, by implication, as it chooses for an example just והחזיקה במבושיו which can effect בשת as well as סכנה, it includes בשת also; and וקצותה את כפה would command to make a hand which is violently laid against a person harmless in every way, literally, if danger to life is there, by monetary fine as far as בשת has been inflicted. Does not the לא תחוס עינך at עדים זוממין (Ch. 19,21) which is referred to for explanation, also refer not only to ממון but to both נפש and נפש בנפש .ממון is actual נפש and עין בעין etc. is ממון, and the introductory לא תחוס עינך refers to both. Yea, according to Sanhedrin 74a (see Ex. 21,23, p. 313) it could even be possible that both could be imposed at the same time. For assuming that cutting off her hand would suffice to save the threatened danger to life, this would be the case, for if יכול להציל באחד מאיבריו the רודף would not be ניתן להצילו בנפשו, so that תשלומין for בשת could also be imposed. (והיה צ״ע אם אין לפוטרה משום כדי רשעתו ודוק). (ומן התימה על הסמ״ג שהביא במל״ת קס״ד ובמ״ע ע״ז פירוש הספרי ותמה על רש״י שפירש הפסוק בחומש על תשלומי בושת כדברי ר׳ יהודה שהוא יחיד והלא אדרבה סברת ר״י הוא סתם משנה וגמרא כנ״ל ולא ידענו תשלומי בושת בנזקין בש״ס אלא אליבא סברא זו של ר׳ יהודה ואידך ספרי דמפרש הפסוק אהצלת נרדף מיד רודף לא הובא כלל בש״ס והוא דבר תמוה ארבינו הגדול בעל הסמ״ג וצ״ע).

V. 13 & 14. גדולה שהיא מכחשת את הקטנה :גדולה וקטנה, לא יהיה לך וגו׳ (Sifri) not that one may not have different sizes of weights and measures, pounds and half-pounds etc. but that one may not have different weights and measures supposed to be of the same size, a heavier and lighter pound weight, a larger and smaller pint measure etc. one for use when buying, the other when selling.

Just as the great chapter on sanctifying our lives, Ch. XIX in Levit., concludes with the teaching of honesty in weights and measures, so here, too, the list of social laws for those now about to settle in the Land ends up with a repetition of the injunction to honesty in weights and measures and a warning against any infringement of it. There in Leviticus we considered the whole connection of all the laws referring to it, pointed out the great importance and how deeply the Torah considered the Jewish character affected by this conscientiousness in business and social inter course, to such an extent that it declares that a Jew who is dishonest in weights, measures, counting etc. is rejected by the Presence of God, that the עונשן של מדות (the punishment for dishonesty I.L.) is completely equal to that for עריות (sexual immorality I.L.), yea is even greater, and it places conscientiousness in business matters as the fundamental principle of Jewish men in social matters, just as it places it in sexual matters as their fundamental principle in moral matters.
Here we would refer to what we worked out at length there and limit ourselves with noting those factors which were reserved to be brought here as complementary to what was declared there.

There (Ch. 19,35,36) by לא תעשו עול במשפט וגו׳, measuring, weighing, counting, reckoning etc. are characterised as acts of justice entrusted to every individual person, and the admonition not to betray this trust, as well as the positive duty to keep to correct weight, correct measure etc. is expressed in general terms. Here, referring to the civic life in the Land to which they are now going, the mere possession, the mere existence of inaccurate weights and measures in “bag or house” is forbidden, and thereby the prevention of any misuse, yea, the very appearance of any such possibility, is assured, as also by the addition of וצדק in V.15 the exclusion of anything that would be detrimental to anybody’s rights at measuring or weighing is made a duty, and the foundation given for all the practical most detailed laws which we already roughly outlined in Leviticus.

In Levit. 19,36 it says אבני צדק ,איפת צדק. If here too צדק was meant to designate the nature of the weight or measure itself as שלמה does, it should say איפת צדק ושלמה ,אבן צדק ושלמה as צדק as a noun used adjectively can normally only be added to a nounin stat. constr. But as it is, it is more abverbial: איפה שלמה יהיה לך and moreover צדק, used justly. Hence the Baba Bathra 88b, makes it a duty for the seller צדק משלך ותן לו, to measure and weigh fully and add a trifle more of his own so that the buyer in any case gets what is due to him.

למען יאריכו ימיך. The duration of your existence as a State on your own soil depends on the most conscientious honesty in business which your God demands from you and which is to form one of the fundamental traits in your national character, for

V. 16. כי תועבת ה׳ אלקיך כל עשה אלה, not only has he done wrong, he, a man whom God has deemed worthy to call Him “his” God, the Leader of his fate and the Guide of his deeds, a Jewish man becomes an abomination of “God, his God” if he calls himself a Jew and does not keep what is right and fair conscientiously and meticulously in his dealings with his fellowmen. The Jew with a false weight or measure may no longer call God “his God”. כי תועבת ה׳ אלקיך כל עשה אלה כל עשה עול

כל עשה אלה. In Baba Bathra 88b, these weighty words are spoken: קשה עונשן של מדות יותר מעונשן של עריות שזה נאמר בהן (ויקרא י״ח כ״ז) אל וזה נאמר בהן (דברים כ״ה ט״ז) אלה ומאי משמע דהאי אל קשה היא דכתיב (יחזקאל י״ז י״ג) ואת אילי הארץ לקח. The responsibility for sins against honest weights and measures is still greater than that for sexual immorality. The sexual sins are referred to by the shortened word אל (Levit. 18,27 כי את כל התועבות האל, but here the sins against weights and measures are designated by the full אלה, but in אל already lies the concept of something weighty, the mighty ones are called אילי הארץ, And in fact the dagesh in the ל of אלה points to a missing נח, accordingly to the root איל, power, strength and otherwise also in the root אלה itself (from which we get אלה the oak) lies the conception of powerful development. So that in איל we would have the idea of intensive and in אלה of extensive greatness and in אֵלֶה the combined intensive and extensive greatness could be expressed.

On the first verse of Gen. we have already remarked on the concept of the demonstrative adjective אלה, “these”, being the expression of the thought of a plurality of objects being combined and subordinated under the concept of a unity, and from that tried to understand the designation of God as אלה. The idea of the combination and subordination of a plurality under a single one does at the same time contain that of the development of the strength, power and relationship of that one over the many, more, at bottom, it essentially assumes it. In אלה, these, accordingly, the extensive greatness is in the foreground, the איל the intensive greatness is more something indicated, to be found by thought.

It is easily then to understand that there where the thought “these”! אלה, is expressed emphatically, especially where it stands by itself without any noun, כל עשה אלה that there the concept innate in the root makes one think of intensive and extensive greatness: things of such gravity and far-reaching effect.

Where then in such cases אלה occurs, shortened of the ה, as אל there only the thought of intensive gravity is stressed, whereas in such cases as it occurs written in full אלה the thought is raised to stressing the extensive, far-spreading effect. Both would correspond to the remarks made above comparing the sins against sexual morality and those against honesty in weights and measures. The former עונש עריות are predominantly of intensive gravity and hence also have כרת as a result. But their pernicious effect usually does not go beyond the persons of the sinners. But עונש מדות, dishonesty in weighing etc. affects a much wider circle and just therein, as is worked out further there, lies the outweighing gravity of its responsibility. עריות, although בכרת are אפשר בתשובה can be atoned for by true repentance and betterment. But atonement for sins against weights etc. is—like all other sins I.L.—dependent in the first place, on giving back what has been dishonestly obtained to those who have been wronged, but e.g. a dealer or shopkeeper who has bought and sold his goods with dishonest weights and measures has as a rule swindled so many and now unknown people that this very first act of restitution and righting the wrong he has done is impossible. Although one who is trying to atone for wrong done to people whom he does not know is advised (Baba Kama 94b) to use the money he ought to restore to them for צרכי צבור to make or maintain public requirements for general use such as wells, bridges etc. which could benefit these unknown people he has defrauded, still such disposing of the money is only an insufficient expedient which cannot fulfil the real restoration, the תשובה for dishonest weights and measures לאו מעליותא היא (See B.B. 88b, תוספות there).
כל עשה עול. See on Levit. 19,35.

V. 17. זכור וגו׳. Keeping afar from every עול, from the misuse of every position of power over others (עול) — even if only momentarily—to their disadvantage, from the misuse of the confidence which one person must place in the other if people living together is to be at all possible, being penetrated with the conviction that we can only call God our God as long as we anxiously avoid doing the slightest wrong to any of His human beings on earth, and the purest honesty in all our dealings with our fellow-men which results therefrom, those were the last strokes which the Torah drew of the picture of the people who were to be guided by it, and call themselves by its name. The people in whose national character the traits of sympathy, consideration, kindness and doing good to every living creature are to shine forth, as the last chapter of God’s Torah repeatedly admonishes; the people to whom “doing harm” should be an impossibility, who are to wander over the earth in the most complete ideal condition of “ישרון״ (Ch. 33,26), in their intercourse with other people are to show themselves as ישר, as the straightest, most honest, most upright nation amongst the nations; and שארית ישראל, those who last through all the ages and all the trials to the ultimate stage of the Jewish perfection are seen, in the words of the Prophet, to be those “who do no wrong, speak no deceit, and in whose mouths no word of fraud is to be found; they alone find their pasturage and repose on earth, they alone have not to tremble before anything or anybody,” שארית ישראל לא יעשו עולה ולא ידברו כזב ולא ימצא בפיהם לשון תרמית כי המה ירעו ורבצו ואין מחריד (צפניה ג׳ י״ג).

The very opposite to this picture of the national character of a people woven out of justice and the duties of love which only sees its power and its future in conscientous faithfulness to duty and through whose example the exclusive devotion to duty will ultimately in the future be participated in by the whole of mankind, is presented by a great nation, like Amalek, which only finds its strength in the might of its sword and its love of glory in treading down all unprepared weaker ones. They stepped out to oppose by the power of the sword the first entry into the history of mankind of the People representing the victory of the power of the Word (Ex. 17,8-16), and right at this first attempt at opposition, its ultimate disappearance from the memory of Man was proclaimed (see there in Ex.).

This most marked contrast was accordingly again pointed out to the people who were about to enter the Land of the Torah, there to faithfully carry out its dictates. The event itself—that first unprovoked attack by Amalek—with all the details of its contrast to what their mission in life was to be, was again brought to their minds, to be kept in perpetual recollection. And whereas there in Exodus, the fight against the national principle of Amalek until its complete disappearance was proclaimed as the whole meaning of the Rule and Management of God in the history of the world, here Israel is exhorted to consider itself, and prove itself a co-working tool for this War of God against Amalek’s leading mankind astray with the blinding glitter of military fame and glory in the palm awarded to victories of physical might. The last page of this war will not be closed until the sword of Amalek shatters against a mightier sword, when the Power of the Sword collapses before the Power of the Word, before a force which will blossom out in the world depending solely on faithful obedience to God’s Law of Morality.

בדרך בשעת טירופיכם, בצאתכם :את אשר עשה לך עמלק בדרך בצאתכם ממצרים ממצרים בשעת גאולתכם (Sifri), you, לך (in the singular), the nation as one unit, were on the journey, occupied with quite other thoughts and worries than thoughts of war. It was the wandering of a homeless multitude of people with women and children, whose position could be expected to arouse feelings of sympathy and pity and not hostility in every one who has human feelings. And over every single one of you (בצאתכם, in the plural) did not the evidence of the Presence of the One, Who had broken the chains of your slavery, and brought you out of the mighty power of Egypt into freedom, hover, a fact which should have served to protect and shield the most defenceless of you from any malicious attack.

מקרה :אשר קרך בדרך is that which happens to somebody beyond all reckoning or expectation (see Gen. 24,12). You were just proceeding on your way and had no cause to have any idea of a sudden assault. His attack was entirely unprovoked and was urged either by pure joy of massacre or possibly by some inkling of the danger which the principle of pure humaneness and obedience to duty which you were to introduce into history would begin to threaten his principle of the power of the sword.

זנב ,ויזנב בך, the tail (as used in Rabbinic Hebrew as סניף, appendage, an accessory, something depending on the principle body), here the tail-end, and the verb זנב, in the Piel (like סעף to lop off branches) to cut off or cut down the stragglers from the main troop. חשל :כל הנחשלים אחריך (related to חסל to eat away, to bring to an end, אזל, to disappear, עצל, lazy, פרזלא מהדק וחשל כלה, “iron breaks and subdues all things” (Dan. 2,40), חשל designates in any case a weak condition, similar to חלש, accordingly all those who could only weakly trail behind. ואתה עיף ויגע, you, yourself, the whole nation, the principle body, was faint and worn out. It was accordingly the weakest of the weak, who could not keep up even with a slow march whom he pounced upon. So that weakness did not move him to sympathy and forbearance, but to crude scornful mishandling.
ולא ירא אלקים, and he did not see God, Who takes the part of the weak against the fist of the strong, and had no fear of Him.

V. 19. והיה בהניח וגו׳. If God is your God, if you, in just the opposite of all these traits of Amalek, order all your doings in accordance with His Will, and thereby—not by your sword and your might—by His protection which you have won by your faithful adherence to duty, you rest, confident and happy, undisturbed by all your enemies round about, in the Land God has given you:

נתן לך לרשתה, the land which He is now giving you to take possession of is one which was already promised to your forefathers, it comes to you only as an inheritance so that you can leave it to your children after you. It is nothing that you have obtained possession of by your own plentitude of power. You have to thank the faithfulness of the duties in the covenant of God with your forefathers for it and only by similar faithfulness on your part will you be able to leave it for your children to inherit.
תמחה את זכר עמלק. See on Ex. 17,14.

לא תשכח. Forget this not, when you falter irresolutely and, Amalek-like, do not recognise God, and in big or small matters only seek opportunities to use your superiority in anything to the detriment of your fellowmen.

If ever you forget your calling as Israel and your mission as Israel in the world and feel envious of the laurel wreaths which a deluded world weaves to crown the memory of successful victorious wreckers of human happiness, and forgets the tear-soaked soil out of which the laurel grew for such wreaths.

Forget this not, when you yorself have to suffer under Amalek’s coarseness and power. Keep upright! Keep your humaneness and respect for that which is right even as your God has taught you. That is where the future lies, humaneness and justice will remain the victors over brutality and force, and you yourself are sent to proclaim that victory and that future by your fate and example and to be a co-worker in bringing it about.
לא תשכח. Forget it not, and so that you do not forget it, זכור, refresh from time to time your remembrance of Amalek and of that which is told you of its future.

V. 1. כי תבוא וגו׳. The whole Lawgiving concludes with two institutions, מקרא ביכורים (the procedure of the declaration at the bringing of the first-fruits I.L.) and וידוי מעשר (the declaration regarding tithes I.L.) which together pronounce the acknowledgment of the fundamental facts of Jewish national history and the fundamental rules for the Jewish national task. The yearly, respectively three-yearly regular repetition of these declarations is calculated to keep his national historical origin and the national laws and duties which arise therefrom alive and fresh in the mind of every Jewish man. Both declarations refer to two institutions, ביכורים and מעשר already given in the Torah. These institutions are meant to express by thoughtful acts, the appreciation of owning landed property and the material wealth derived therefrom according to its origin and purpose. The commands to make these declarations are therefore in the closest relationship to the land, taking possession of which was now imminent, so accordingly here, at the end of the Lawgiving—for the realisation of which the Land was to be attained—is their most suitable place.

V. 2. ולקחת וגו׳. The duty of bringing the first-fruits of the products of the Land up to the House of the Sanctuary of the Torah, has already repeatedly been given in the Torah (see Ex. 22,29; XXIII,19; XXXIV,26). The Festival of Weeks is called definitely חג הקציר בכורי מעשיך (ibid XXIII,19) and יום הבכורים (Numb. 28,26), with which the bringing מנחות from the new produce and bringing up of the new fruit is introduced (see on Levit. 2,11,12; XXIII,16,17 and Numb. 28,26). Equally so, above in Ch. 12,6,17, the duty of bringing the first fruits to the place chosen by God for the Sanctuary of His Torah, and the prohibition to eat them anywhere else in the Land is pronounced in connection with other holy things to be brought there. There בכורים are understood under the term תרומת ידך, a designation which will be explained in what follows.

Now here in the Torah more detailed laws of the בכורים institution follow which, simple though they are, carrying them out becomes a glorious joyful national movement which lasts throughout the summer months of each year from the Festival of Weeks until Sukkoth.

מראשית ולא כל ראשית :מראשית כל פרי האדמה (Menachoth 84b). It does not say ראשית כל פרי וגו׳ (the first ripe fruit of all the produce of the Land I.L.) because not all fruits of the soil are liable to be brought as בכורים, but the Halacha teaches with גז״ש reference to ארץ חטה ושערה וגפן etc. (Ch. 8,3) that here too, the Land in ארצך is only thought of in the seven kinds of fruit which characterise its richness which are named there. The Law accordingly could not run ראשית כל פרי but only מראשית כל פרי because the duty of בכורים applies only to a selection of the fruits of the land, to the seven which form the שבח ארץ ישראל, the riches of the soil of the Land. And just as מראשית limits it to “some” of the first fruits, so does מארצך (it could have said אשר תביא ארצך) limit the parts of the Land to those which are most suitable to produce the Lest kinds of these seven chosen fruits as being liable to the mitzva of bringing בכורים from their produce. Thus לא מתמרים שבהרים ולא מפירות שבעמקים, not dates from the mountainous districts nor other fruits from deep-lying ones. (ibid 84b,) כן נלענ״ד לפרש מימרא דר׳ אלעזר דלא בא לומד דיליף ר״י שאין חייב בביכורים מכל פירות ממראשית ראף הוא יש לו ג״ש דארץ ארץ אלא ה״ק כמו שהוצרך הכתוב לומר מראשית ולא כל ראשית כיון דלא מחייב אלא אז׳ המינים כדילפינן בג״ש כך אמר קרא מארצך ולא כל ארצך להוציא תמרים שבהרים וכו׳. כנלע״ד ובזה מסולקת קושית המפר׳ מאחר די״ל ג״ש לימוד מראשית ולא כל ראשית ל״ל עי׳ הרא״ם לרש״י וברכת הזבח מנחות פ״ד ב׳ ומן התימה על הגדולים הנ״ל דס״ל דבאמת דמראשית ולא כל ראשית דרשינן כמו בחלה דבעינן שיריה נכרים והלא בפירוש איתא פיאה א׳ א׳ דביכורים אין להם שיעור למעלה וביכורים ב׳ ד׳ עושה אדם כל שדהו ביכורים ע״ש בר״ש אלא ע״כ מראשית גבי ביכורים לא אתי כלל לתלמודא מאחר דילפינן מג״ש דלא חייב אלא בז׳ מינים ולא הוה אפשר לקרא לומר ראשית כל פרי כנ״ל. ואפשר הא דמדמי הגדולים הנ״ל דרשה דמראשית דביכורים לדרשה דחלה לא לגמרי מדמי להו אלא כמו דמראשית גבי חלה מלמד דאינו יכול לעשות כל עיסתו חלה כך מראשית גבי ביכורים מלמד שאינו .חייב לעשות כל פירות שנתבכרו יחדיו באילן ביכורים אלא סגי אפי׳ ענב א׳ אפי׳ תאנה

So it was only the seven kinds of fruit for which the Jewish Land was celebrated, and of these the choicest, the first fruits of which had to be brought as בכורים. For they were, as it says in the next verse, to represent the Jewish Land in the hands of the bringers, and “show” that they had come into possession of the Land promised to their forefathers. Understandably, only those fruits are suitable for this which are characteristic of the Land, and the best of their kind.

While still on the tree, even before they were completely ripe, one picked out the particular fruit one would take for כיצד מפרישין ,בכורים הביכורים יורד אדם בתוך שדהו ורואה תאנה שביכרה אשכול שביכר רימון שביכר קושרו בגמי ואומר הרי אלו ביכורים (“How were the first-fruits chosen, a man would go into his orchard, and if he saw a fig ripening, a bunch of grapes becoming ripe, he would tie a piece of ribbon or bast round it, and say “this will be בכורים I.L.) (Bikurim 3,1). For that is why the duty of Bikurim is called מלאה (see Ex. 22,28).

ולקחת והבאת עד שתהא לקיחה והבאה באחד ,ולקחת וגו׳ והלכת וגו׳ (בבא בתרא פ״א ב׳); (דכולל הש״ס כל ענין והלכת אל המקום וגו׳ ובאת אל הכהן וגו׳ בלשון הבאה דהא לא כתיב והבאת). Gathering the fruit from the ground or tree—according to ר״ת taking it out of the house—and bringing it up to the Sanctuary in Jerusalem, should be done by one and the same person, so that בצרן ושגרן ביד שליח, if the owner had plucked them and had them taken up to Jerusalem by somebody else מביא ואינו קורא, he has only to bring them into the Temple but may not make the declaration which is prescribed in the next verse. Similarly, if his שליח had plucked them but had died on the way and the owner himself or somebody else had completed the task, the law is the same. But if his שליח had both plucked the fruit and carried it up to Jerusalem for him, so that the לקיחה והבאה באחד then the owner himself can מביא וקורא, bring them in to the Temple and make the declaration. (רשב״ם there, but see תוספות there ועי׳ מהרש״א שם סוף ד״ה בצרן ושגרן). According to the חדושי הרמב״ן (ibid) הבאה does not mean bringing them all the way up from home but only הכנסתן לעזרה bringing them into the Temple, and this and the לקיחה, taking it out of the house is to be done by the owner himself. But it does not matter if it is carried by others changing about. In any case the לקיחה and the הבאה, taking it away from the field or tree—according to ר״ת from the house—and bringing it to the Temple must be in such close essential connection that they have to be done by one and the same person, and so this connection brought home to his mind, and the mitzva cannot be completely, but only partly carried out if the לקיחה והבאה are not done באחד.

We have already said on the sentence ראשית בכורי אדמתך תביא בית ה׳ אלקיך (Ex. XXIII) that by בכורים the thought is expressed that the first fruits of our fields and orchards do not ripen as תבואה for our house but for God’s house, for the house of the Sanctuary of His Torah, and thereby the knowledge and the acknowledgment is to be fostered that the blessing of our fields and the prospering of our work is only in the second place thanks to our assiduousness, and the favour of good physical conditions, but in the first place is due to God and our faithful adherence to His Torah-covenant. It is accordingly not only הבאה, the positive concept of bringing it up to this Sanctuary of the Torah but also לקיחה, the negative concept of taking it away from our own fields, or, according to ר״ת from our own houses, with the purpose of bringing it up to God’s House, the לקיחה לצורך הבאה which is an essential part of the בכורים-thought, which just by לקיחה והבאה באחד finds its full expression. But of course הבאה is the really essential part, and should they be lost on the way, others have to be brought in their place. חייב באחריותן עד שיביאן להר הבית שנאמר ראשית בכורי אדמתך תביא בית ה׳ אלקיך (Bikurim 1,9). In connection with this the following law

מלמד שטעונים כלי :ושמת בטנא (Sifri) could also come, according to which it is obligatory to place the first fruits which are to be taken up to the Temple in a basket. That makes it quite apparent that you are taking them away from your house to transport them elsewhere.

V. 3. וכי עלתה על דעתך שתלך אצל :ובאת אל הכהן אשר יהיה בימים ההם כהן שלא יהיה בימיך אלא כהן שהוא כשר וכה״א אל תאמר מה היה שהימים הראשונים היו טובים מאלה (Sifri) (“The priest that shall be in those days”! Well could it possibly enter your head to go to a priest who was not living in your days, but what it wants to say is, as long as the priest is a “kosher” one, do not say: how much better the priests were in the good old days”, (Sifri) I.L.) The Sifri teaches that the addition of the words אשר יהיה בימים ההם wishes to tell us that the fact that the priests of any contemporary time are not up to the standard of previous times should not deter us from going to them with our first fruits as commanded, provided that they are כשר, that they do represent only the demands of the Torah. It is not the individual personalities of the actual priests themselves that we have to look for in the Sanctuary of God’s Torah, but it is in their symbolic character as the representative and minister of that Sanctuary, the calling that God has given them from birth, to which they have not made themselves unworthy by undutifulness, that we seek them to take over to them, as the representatives of the Sanctuary of God’s Torah in our time, the first fruits of our fields and orchards. For, according to the immediately following declaration, by the בכורים, every generation, even the last one, is to come into connection with the very first original commencement of our nationality and the origin of our national calling and destiny. The less any contemporary time does conform with the highest ideal demands of this calling, and the more this disparity is evident also in the personalities of the כהנים of such a period, all the more important would be the handing of the בכורים over to them with the accompanying explaining and acknowledging words, so that the priest, no less then the bringer be admonished by the historical past on which every present rests, and out of which it has to draw its mission and vocation, and both learn to take the admonition fully to heart. Thus here this addition of אשר יהיה בימים ההם could have its meaningful justification even to a greater extent than when said referring to the judge in Ch. 17,9.

הגדתי היום וגו׳. Cf. והגדתי לו כי שפט אני (Sam. I, III,13); הגדת היום כי אין לד שרים (Sam. II, XIX,7) where הגיד means making clear not by words but by deeds, actions, that הגיד from נגד literally means showing. So here too, by bringing up the fruits from my fields I have shown, demonstrated. (See Bikurim 1,7, תוי״ט there).

לה׳ אלקיך, as much as to say “to God your God,” referring to the priest. Thus Saul to Samuel, אלקיך (Sam. I, XV,15; XXI,30) Hezekiah to Isaiah (Kings II, XIX,4). So also in Levit. 20,7, of the whole priestly tribe, כי קדוש הוא לאלקיו, it is God of Whom you teach, Whose Torah and Sanctuary you represent. By bringing the fruit of my land up to you, I have demonstrated thereby that I only possess my orchards and fields as the descendant of my forefathers whose God had promised in a covenant to give the land to their descendants, as is declared in the teachings of the Torah to which the Sanctuary which you represent is erected, and Who has now fulfilled that which He promised. My orchards and fields stand on the soil of “your” God, and only as a son of His covenant are they mine. To proclaim that have I brought these fruits.

V. 4. ולקח הכהן וגו׳ והגיחו וגו׳. As only in V.10 at the conclusion of the whole procedure it says again: והניחו לפני וגו׳, here with this ולקח הכהן וגו׳ והניחו וגו׳ it only expresses in general the purpose of bringing the fruit up, the detailed procedure then follows. They are handed over to the priest to lay them at the foot of the מזבח ה׳ אלקיך, the Altar dedicated to God, as “our” God in fulfilment of His Torah. The renewed consciousness of the intimate connection between any and every of our living present, with all its material wealth, with our national origin and the duties of the covenant which is rooted therein is to effect renewed devotion to the mission and task of our life which was given to us thereby.

The ולקח הכהן הטנא מידך, the basket of fruit being handed over by the hand of the bringer to the priest for the Altar is given its meaning by the ידיו תביאינה את אשי ה׳ (“his own hands shall bring etc.”) the handing over of the parts of the אימורים וחזה ושוק, the parts of the שלמים-offering to the priest in Levit. 7,30 (refer to it). As there, as here too, the handing over is made by the performance of a תנופה ותרומה by the combined action of the owner and priest; and by this מוליך ומביא מעלה ומוריד (a waving of the basket to and fro and up and down I.L.) the handing over itself is given the symbolic meaning of dedicating it to the whole of the rest of mankind and to God (see ibid on Verses 28-30). If we note that the הנחה referring here to the priest והניחו, at the end (V. 10. I.L.) is said of the bringer והנחתו, then the very wording of our text assumes an action to be performed by the two of them together, as is really the case at the תנופה (see Menachoth 61a. and b).

But just as the הגשה of the Mincha (Levit. 6,7) took place לפני (בדרום) אל פני המזבח ,(במערב) ה׳, accordingly at the south-west corner of the Altar, and thereby the possession of food and comfort represented by the Mincha are dedicated to be devoted to the spirit emanating from the Torah (see ibid, and on Ch. 2,8 there), so here too we find these two terms used for depositing the fruit at the foot of the Altar: והניחו לפני מזבח ה׳ and: והנחתו לפני ה׳, on which Jerusalmi teaches (Bikurim 3,6) that the south-west corner of the Altar was also the place prescribed for the הנחה of the Bikurim. The Bikurim were accordingly brought into the Temple to be laid down on the south-west corner of the Altar after the “waving” had been duly performed with them, thereby to place the Land as belonging to God with all its riches to be ruled by the spirit engendered by His Torah.

בכורים are the only ones, amongst all the gifts which have to be given from the produce of our own lands at which the תנופה ותרומה-procedure has to be performed. Neither at תרומה nor at מעשרות nor at חלה has it to take place. That explains why, as remarked above, only Bikurim are understood wherever the Torah mentions תרומת ידך. (see Rashi Pesachim 36b).

ולקח הכהן הטנא מידך accordingly designates the undertaking of the תנופה. The preceding declaration הגדתי היום וגו׳ was said according to Bikurim 3,6 עודהו הסל על כתפו while the basket was still on his shoulder. הגיע לארמי אובד אבי מוריד הסל מעל כתפו ואוחזו בשפתותיו וכהן מניח ידו תחתיו ומניפו וקורא מארמי אובד אבי עד שהוא גומר כל הפרשה ומניחו בצד המזבח והשתחוה ויצא. When he reaches ארמי אובד אבי he takes the basket down from his shoulder, holds it by its upper edge while the priest places his hand underneath it, and they make the “waving” movements with it (cf. on Levit. 7,30). Then he says from ארמי אובד אבי to the end, puts the basket down at the side of the Altar (on the south side of the south-west corner, see above), prostrates himself and goes out of the Temple.

וענית ואמרת וגו׳. With the basket of fruits in his hand already, by the waving, dedicated to endeavours for God and mankind in general, which he has brought, as he has already declared, to express his full consciousness of the fact that he has to thank his possession of the Land solely to the fulfilment of the promise made to his forefathers, now he looks back to that original beginning of the Jewish people, and stresses the fact that at the foundation of the Jewish People, the Will of God and His Almighty Power alone arranged it, and no other factor participated in any way.

אבד .ארמי אבד אבי in the Kal is always intransitive and means to go to ruin hence ﭏבֵד, one going to ruin, one to whom ruin is near. So that ארמי and אבד are together the predicate of אבי, and the separating accent on ארמי makes the thought rest first on it and then adds אבד to it as a second predicate: “an Aramite, near to ruin was my Father”.

The most complete contrast to the happy blessed independence in one’s own land, of which the fruit in the basket is brought as evidence is expressed by the word “Aramite” by which the bringer designates and pictures his ancestor.

The land of Canaan was not the birthplace of the ancestor, Abraham’s cradle stood in Aram. It was Aram which he called ארצי ומולדתי, his land and his birthplace. He, himself had no native rights in the land which, now, henceforth his descendants could enjoy as heirs naturally entitled to it. Their first ancestor was homeless in the present homeland of the descendants. He had to consider it an act of grace if a piece of ground was granted to him as a grave in which to bury his wife in what was now the native soil of his descendants. And when his first grandson, Jacob-Israel, whose name the nation now bore, tramped back as a refugee to the Aramite homeland, and there by hard serving work gained a living, again the Aramite homeland would not tolerate him. Threatened with ruin by his artful tricky father-in-law he, with wives and children sought Canaan’s soil, again as a refugee only there too to find no peace, and finally, escaping a famine, always still ארמי, always still homeless, and added to that, on account of the bitterest blows of fate, אובד, according to human judgment, without any hope of a future of independence, to go down to a country, strange in speech and customs, having a still stranger and contrasting outlook on life, to Egypt.

A national future on Canaan’s soil had been promised to their fathers, and as a family without a future, only able to claim native rights in Aram, they moved to Egypt, ארמי אובד אבי וירד מצרימה — אנוס על פי הדבור adds the Hagadda explanation thereto, the moving of the family of Jacob down to Egypt was, in human reckoning, nothing but a still greater move away from the future that had been promised them being realised. In spite of the temporary resplendence towards which they went, it was in truth a ירידה. Hence the necessity for the words of encouragement אל תירא מרדה מצרימה (Gen. 46,3). Hence, Joseph, in all his splendour, departed this life with the conviction that it would require a special פקידה, a special intervention of God’s Management, and with the full confidence that this would be vouchsafed, to lead them in the future out again to the Promised Land. (ibid L. 24). But they did go down, apparently ;אובד אנוס forced by the pressure of circumstance and על פי הדבור, and obeying the Divine direction.

ויגר שם, beforehand there was no intention להשתקע במצרים to settle there permanently, they sought asylum there as strangers, and that they got with all the bitter consequences which are attached to homeless foreigners without without any rights in a state like Egypt. במתי מעט, with seventy souls.

ויהי שם, and there, against all justified expectations, they became, by the spiritual and moral qualities which they kept, in contrast to the rest of the inhabitants, united לגוי, to a separate body of people, מצוינים שם (conspicious I.L.) and moreover to a large united body of men, by God’s blessing, strong and numerous.
V. 6. הרע ,וירעו אתנו to do hurt to somebody, mishandle him is construed with ל-, but also with את. Thus ולא הרעתי את אחד מהם (Numb. 16,15 מנעני מהרע אותך (Sam. I, XXV,34).
The explanation in the Hagadda which refers this to the הבה נתחכמה takes the וירעו in the sense of “they wanted to harm us” wanted to lessen and break our strength and greatness.
ויענונו ויתנו עלינו וגו׳ are the ענוי and עבדות which result from the גרות and together make up the three phases of the Egyptian Galuth (see on Ex. 6,6).
V. 7. לחצנו ;עבדות = עמלנו ;ענוי = ענינו .ונצעק וגו׳; really restrictions = גרות (see on Ex. 22,20).

V. 8. ביד חזקה .ויוציאנו וגו׳, a Hand that was stronger than that of our masters and burst our slavery asunder. בזרוע נטויה, Whose Mastery stretches over all lands, and makes all men into גרים so that they all have equal rights on His earth. ובמורא גדול, Whom all have to fear who misuse their power to the ענוי of their weaker human brethren. ובאותות ובמופתים. He reveals His נטויה ,יד חזקה and מורא גדול which He raises to make an end of this גרות ,עבדות and ענוי by מופתים and אותות by signs which teach and miracles which punish. (See Ex. 4,21; VII,15).

V. 9. אל המקים הזה .ויבאנו וגו׳, to this place which He chose for the Sanctuary of His Torah (cf. Ex. 15,17) and for the realisation of that Torah which rests here, ויתן לנו וגו׳, He gave us this blessed Land which wraps itself around the Sanctuary of the Torah as round its centre point, the possession of which at last gave us a homeland, which we had never had. ויבאנו אל המקום הזה, זה בית המקדש, ויבאנו אל המקום הזה ויתן לנו בשכר ביאתנו אל המקום הזה נתן לנו את הארץ הזאת (ספרי).

V. 10. ועתה וגו׳. And now, since we have only obtained the Land through You, and You have given us the Land for the Torah, to which this Sanctuary is erected, therefore have I brought here the first-fruits of the soil which You, God have given me.

And therefore והנחתו וגו׳ you are to set the basket of fruit down on that side of the Altar which is dedicated to the illuminating spirit that emanates from the Torah, before God, “your” God, and then you depart from His House with השתחויה, with the expression of your “complete devotion and surrender to God”. But not yet from its surroundings. For, like every other time you appear in the Temple, בכורים also demand your stay in the City of the Temple until the next morning. טעונין לינה (Bikurim 2,4; — see on Ch. 16,7).

As was declared in Numb. 18,13, the Bikurim are given to the כהן, and they have the character of קדשי מקדש inasmuch that the owner cannot give them to any כדן he likes, but they go to the משמר (see Levit. 6,19) the division of priests who are on duty that week (see Numb. V. 9). They may also only be eaten within the purlieus of the Temple i.e. inside Jerusalem. Like מעשר שני it is אסור לאונן (V.14), and subject to מעשר שני) בעור V.6).

V. 11. ושמחת וגו׳. Then, after the acknowledgment, brought about by reflecting on the past, that it was only thanks to God that the present consisted of independence and blessings, and after renewed devotion and surrender to God, brought about by that acknowlegment, you are to rejoice before God with all the good things that He has granted you. A rejoicing which is primarily celebrated with שלמים offerings like the joy of festivals, ושמחת בחגך (Ch. 16,14) which finds its expression in meals of the שלמים offerings, and it also says in V. 7 of the following chapter: וזבחת שלמים ושמחת לפני ה׳ אלקיך. And ושמחת בכל הטוב also demands that the material enjoyment of the good things granted to you shall also be expressed in joyful buoyant spirits, which according to Arachin 11a, is only done by שירה singing inspired rapturous songs and hymns. Hence בכורים טעונין קרבן ושיר. Just as the whole carrying out of the Bikurim-duty was stamped with the aspect of joy.

As a rule the Bikurim were not brought up by single individuals alone. All the people of the cities belonging to a מעמד-district (see on Numb. 28,2) asssembled in the county town, remained over night in the open places of the town without entering any of the houses (on account of טומאה). At daybreak the leader called out קומו ונעלה ציון אל בית ה׳ אלקינו. “Up, let us go up to Zion, to the House of our God!” The procession was led by a fife band and a steer for a שלמים, an offering of a meal of peace, its horns gilded and crowned with a wreath of olive leaves, until it reached the outskirts of Jerusalem. When they arrived there they sent into the town to announce their arrival, and in the interval adorned their baskets of Bikurim fruit. The President of the Temple, assistants, and administrators went out to meet and receive them, the number of these varied according to the size of the arriving parties. All the workmen and artisans in Jerusalem stopped work, even that which they were in duty-bound to attend to, to shout the greeting: “Brothers from such-and-such a city, peace be unto you!” The fifes continued to lead the procession until they reach the Mount of Temple. Arrived there, every one, even the king himself, took his basket on his shoulder and entered the ante-chamber of the Temple. There the Levites began to sing Ps. XXX. ארוממך ה׳ כי דליתני ולא שמחת אויבי לי (Bikurim 3,2-4).

The proper time for bringing of the Bikurim was also limited to זמן שמחה, to the happy summer time from the Festival of Shevuoth to the Festival of Sukkoth, the time when cutting and picking the fruit spreads joy in the hearts of man. Only in this joyful period מעצרת עד החג ,זמן שמחה מביא וקורא, at the bringing of the first-fruits was the retrospective avowal referring to the past allowed to be said (Pessachim 36b). The ואמרת and ושמחת of our text belong intimately together, as the Sifri teaches. It is for the time when the heart is full of joy over the blessed conditions of blessings in the present that the duty is given to reflect on the homeless, almost hopeless condition of our origin. בזמן קצירה ולקיטה שאדם לוקט תבואתו הצריכו מהחג ועד חנוכה .הכתוב קרייה דארמי אובד אבי (רש״י פסחים שם). It is true that after Sukkoth too, right up till Chanuka there is still fruit etc. to be gathered and brought home, so the law ולקחת מראשית כל פרי האדמה אשר תביא מארצך still applies but זמן שמחה and with it זמן קריאה also had passed hence מהחג ועד חנוכה מביא ואינו קורא (ibid. and Sifri).

מלמד שאדם מביא ביכורים מנכסי אשתו וקורא :אשר נתן לך וגו׳ ולביתך (Gittin 47b, and Sifri) “Thou and thy house”, as usual by “your house”, your wife is primarily understood, and from that it is taught that a man can bring the first fruits from his wife’s property, and in the avowal can say the words אשר נתת לי (“which Thou giveth me”) although by usage and later legal institution a husband has only the right of the use of his wife’s property and in other cases the rule holds good that קנין פירות לאו כקנין הגוף דמי, the right to the use or the income of a property is not to be treated as the right of possession of the object (see Levit. on Ch. 25,15,16).
אתה והלוי וגו׳. See on Ch. 12,12.

V. 12. כי תכלה וגו׳. In the real Masser-chapter, XLV,22-29 it has already been prescribed that, apart from the tithe to be given to the Levite each year, in the first and second, and fourth and fifth year of the Shemita period a second tithe מעשר שני to be eaten by oneself in the City of the Temple, had to be put aside, and in every third and sixth year, this second tenth was not to be used in that way but given, as מעשר עני to the poor and needy. We remarked there how these three tithes, מעשר ראשון, מעשר שני, מעשר עני, were designated to teach the principles of using our wealth for furthering the care of our spiritual life, our material life and our love for our fellow-men. By these laws of the tithes accordingly a three-yearly rota of tithes was ordered. Within such a rota which concludes with the third year, all the three kinds of tithes are to be paid, and with the end of the third year settled, so that by then all the tithes which had been set aside during that period should have been disposed of for their respective prescribed purposes. Now it does not call it שנת המעשרות but שנת המעשר the year in which a tithe occurs which does not appear in the other two, for the third one was not added to the other two, but took the place of the מעשר שני, only one addition was made each year to the מעשר ראשון (Rosh Hashona 12b; — see Ch. 14,22,28).

Of this conclusion of the three-yearly rota of tithes, it now says here כי תכלה לעשר etc, ונתת ללוי וגו׳ (see on Ch. 45,29). The sharp separating notation on ללוי would confirm the way it is taken that it does refer to the מעשר ראשון tithe which is given to the Levite as such (and not because, having no land himself he was necessitous I.L.). So that here the two tithes to be given in every third year are designated, מעשר ראשון ללוי and מעשר עני לגר וגו׳
ואכלו בשעריך. See on Ch. 12,17.

V. 13. ואמרת לפני וגו׳. As explained on Ch. 14,22,28, the years to which the fruit belong regarding the duty of giving tithes, is not reckoned from the time of their harvest, but according to the beginning of their attaining the stage of ripeness, the עונת המעשרות, so that for some fruit the third year extends into the fourth, and the sixth into the seventh, as we remarked on V,11, some fruit of the previous year remains in the fields and orchards up to חנוכה. As לפני ה׳ אלקיך gives the command to make the tithe-declaration, which follows, in the עזרה of the Temple (see ראב״ד on הל׳ מ״ש ,רמב״ם XI,3) the first opportunity to do so would be the first pilgrim-festival which comes after Chanukah, i.e. Pessach. And the Sifri on XIV,28 teaches that the מקצה שלש שנים said there for וידוי מעשר also refers to the first רגל following the end of the third year of the tithe-cycle, just as the מקץ שבע שנים does for the מצות הקהל (Ch. 31,10). So that this tithe-declaration had to be made במנחה ,בי״ט אחרון של פסח (Masser Sheni V.10).

בערתי הקדש מן הבית. This statement which is to be made after a preceding self-examination in which the one who makes it declares that he has dutifully fulfilled all the prescribed obligations on the products of his lands refers primarily to the three tithes; and of these מעשר שני is in the foreground, so much so, that if one considers what it says in verses 13 and 14, one has to say that in this declaration מעשר שני forms the centre-point to which the other two directly mentioned (מעשר ראשון ועני) and, as we shall see, all the other gifts from his produce which are only indicated, are attached.

For of the three kinds of tithes it is only מעשר שני to which the title קדש is given. It is included, in Levit. 22,6 amongst those קדשים which may not be eaten בטומאה and in Levit. 27,30 called, as ממון קדש לה׳ :גבוה (see there, and above Ch. 14,22). So that, although in the order in which they have to be separated out מעשר ראשון for the Levite comes first, and then מעשר שני for one’s own consumption in Jerusalem, in the avowal בערתי הקדש מן הבית it considers מעשר שני first and then the tithe for the Levite and the tithe for the poor only added “and also etc.” וגם נתתיו ללוי ולגר וגו׳. Yea, so much has this avowal מעשר שני principally in mind, that the special avowals in V.14 לא אכלתי באוני etc. which call the object simply (in the sing. I.L.) ממנו, can only refer to מעשר שני which is the only tithe which can only be eaten by the one who has to give it, in prescribed ways.

But by implication the avowal includes all the obligatory gifts etc. which apply to the produce of the soil. The concept קדש also includes נטע רבעי which in Levit. 19,24 is called קדש just like מעשר שני, and has also to be eaten only in Jerusalem (Masser Sheni V.10), and, according to the Jerusalmi (ibid) also בכורים which, as remarked on v. 10 have even the character of קדשי מקדש and may also only be eaten by the priests in Jerusalem in בטהרה and מן הבית .שלא באנינות also by implication includes חלה the duty which occurs at baking bread at home, and so quite specially has to be given “from the house”. The מעשר ראשון declared with the וגם נתתיו ללוי includes תרומה which also has to be given to a branch of the tribe of Levi, and the מעשר עני described as having fulfilled the obligation to the “stranger orphan and widow” includes לקט שכחה ופאה. (Masser Sheni ibid).

Referring to all these the declaration has to be made בערתי מן הבית “I have cleared them out of my house”, that he has nothing in his possession which has not been disposed of in the prescribed way. So that on the day before the day on which the declaration was to be made i.e. on ערב י״ט אחרון של פסח of the fourth and seventh year (see above) was the ביעור i.e. everything which had not yet been disposed of in the prescribed manner had then to be so disposed of, or if that were not possible, destroyed. תרומה ותרומת מעשר had to be given to the priest, מעשר ראשון to the Levite, מעשר עני to the poor; בכורים ,נטע רבעי ,מעשר שני, dutifully eaten in Jerusalem, or if they were not in the city, they may no longer be kept but must be destroyed (Masser Sheni V.6; see Yebamoth 73a, רש״י ותוספות there).
ככל מצותך אשר צויתני, that they had also been performed in the prescribed order, if, e.g. he had separated מעשר שני before מעשר ראשון he was not allowed to make the declaration (ibid).

לא הפרשתי ממין על שאינו מינו ולא מן התלוש על המחובר .לא עברתי ממצותיך ולא מן המחובר על התלוש ולא מן החדש על הישן ולא מן הישן על החדש that he had also given from each kind of fruit and of each year separately (see Ch. 14,22), and also not מן התלוש etc. not given what was already liable for what was not yet liable and vice versa, מן החיוב על הפטור ומן הפטור .על החיוב

לא שכחתי מלברכך עליו ולהזכיר שמך ומלכותך (ברכות מ׳ ב׳) :ולא שכחתי (ibid), I have also not forgotten to do what you have not expressly commanded but have taken for granted at the fulfilling of Your commandments, that we will perform them in the idea of Your having commanded them, and as being Your commandments, as we express in our ברכות מצות before each mitzva that we do.

V. 14. אוני .לא אכלתי באוני ממנו: see Gen. 35,18. We have already remarked that this and the following sentences refer only to מעשר שני (by implication also to נטע רבעי and בכורים which are related to it). The legal conception of אונן, i.e. the condition of one being immediately overcome with grief at the death of a near relation, we have already found in Levit. 10,13,14,19 as being a prevention of עבודה and אכילת קדשים for an ordinary priest, and of אכילת קדשים even for the High Priest (refer to it there). Now here the prohibition is given also for מעשר שני (implied also for בכורים and נטע רבעי) that it may not be eaten in the condition of אנינות. Whether such declaration as לא אכלתי באוני ממנו and the following ones, which are not given as direct prohibitions but are only commanded to be declared as not having been transgressed, are to be taken as direct prohibitions involving מלקות, or only as indirect ones as לאו הבא מכלל עשה is a matter of difference of opinion between Rambam and Ramban (see ס׳ המצות שרש ח׳ at end). For the following אכילת מעשר בטומאה (המעשר) בין בטומאת גוף בין בטומאת עצמו, direct prohibitions involving מלקות are proved in Yebamoth 73 (see Levit. 22,6; Deut. 12,17).

בין שאני טמא והוא טהור בין שאני טהור והוא :לא בערתי ממנו בטמא טמא (Yebamoth ibid), to eat מעשר שני in a condition of טומאה is prohibited whether the person or the object is טמא, has already, as remarked, been declared both, in Levit. and Deut. But it does not say לא אכלתי ממנו בטמא but לא בערתי ממנו בטמא and by that, any other use of מעשר שני שנטמא apart from eating is equally prohibited. For whereas with תרומה שנטמאת which like other קדשים טמאים, has to be burnt, one may have use of it for lighting or cooking or heating while it is being burnt (see on Numb. 18,8). such הנאה is prohibited in the case of מעשר שני שנטמא as the Gemora there in Yebamoth finds this contrast to תרומה expresssed by stressing the word ממנו in our text: ממנו אי אתה מבעיר אבל אתה מבעיר שמן של תרומה שנטמא.

As remarked on Ch. 12,24, מעשר שני שנטמא can still be redeemed even in Jerusalem, in which case the קדושה is then transferred to the money which must be spent on food which must be eaten בטהרה (ibid V. 26).

ולא נתתי ממנו למת, even in its condition of טומאה I have not used it for the dead, such as to anoint a dead body with מעשר שני oil. (Yebamoth 74a). Or according to Masser Sheni 5,12: לא לקחתי ממנו ארון ותכריכים ולא נתתיו לאוננים אחרים “I have not bought a coffin or shrouds with it, nor have I given it to other אוננים for them to eat”. According to רמב״ם in הל׳ מ׳ שני III,10, נתינה למת includes spending the money for anything “dead”, i.e. for anything that does not keep the body alive, anything other than אכילה שתיה וסיכה (eatables, drinks or oil for anointing I.L.) the things that מ״ש-money must be exchanged for.

הביאותיו לבית הבחירה :שמעתי בקול ה׳ אלקי: I have brought it up into the purlieus of the house that Thou hadst chosen. עשיתי ככל אשר ציויתני: שמחתי ושימחתי בו, “I have, even as Thou hast commanded me, rejoiced with it, and made others happy with it. (Masser Sheni 5,12). Both are commanded, above in Ch. 12,18 it says ואכלת שם לפני ה׳ ושמחת אתה וביתך והלוי אשר בשעריך וגו׳ and equally so in Ch. 15,26,27.
ואכלת שם לפני ד׳ ושמחת אתה וביתך ,והלוי אשר בשעריך וגו׳, und ebenso Kap. 15, 26 u. 27.

V. 15. עשינו מה שגזרת עלינו אף אתה עשה :השקיפה ממעון קדשך מה שהבטחתנו (Masser Sheni ibid 13). As we have done our duty, we can also hope that You will grant us the blessings that You have promised us. השקיפה: direct Your testing glance down on our doings and refraining from doing (see Gen. on XVIII,21). Hence the sentence in the בוא וראה ,ירושלמי כמה גדול כוחן של עושי מצות שכל השקפה שבתורה לרעה וזו לשון ברכה.

With this institution of וידוי מעשר the real actual law-giving comes to its conclusion. Only two further mitzvas follow, to be observed for the preservation of this now completed Torah in the minds of the people, the מצות הקהל (Ch. 31,10,11) and כתיבת התורה (V.19 ibid).

If we consider how these commands of מעשר (tithes I.L.) are the only ones out of the whole Divine Lawgiving, for the faithful carrying out of which such a formal retrospective declaration before God is prescribed, then the principles and feelings furthered by these laws and their performance must have a quite special importance for the goal aimed at by the whole Torah innate in them. (Mal. 3,10 would confirm this I.L.).

As we have repeatedly recognised, and thoroughly explained in the real tithe-chapter, (XIV,22 et seq.), giving the three prescribed tithes is to teach us to use our material possessions for the purposes which God has set before us; for fostering the spirit in which the Torah inspires us to live, i.e. for our spiritual welfare (מעשר ראשון); for caring for keeping our bodies in a state of purity and health i.e. for our material welfare (מעשר שני); and by a sacrificing sense of duty for furthering the well-being of our fellow-men (מעשר עני); all to be brought home to us by practical action. But by the realisation of these three aims the whole sum of our common tasks can well be summarised. And a national life given up to the realisation of these three aims could indeed — freed by them from all selfishness and from all moral degeneration — be such a healthy one and so near perfection as is humanly possible, that it could make the call up to God השקיפה, and ask for His Blessing on the material means for such endeavours to be granted.

These considerations could, so we believe, give us an insight to the motive which could have directed just the avowal of having fulfilled the duties of the tithe-laws to its place as the final stone to the whole edifice

But amongst these tithe-duties the מעשר שני, which is to be kept back for one’s own consumption, is placed, as we have seen, most strikingly definitely in the foreground—although in the order of performing these duties it only takes second place, and may not be separated before the מעשר ראשון if the avowal is to be allowed to be made at all—so much so that, not only the greater part of the avowal refers to this מעשר, and can only refer to it, but, according to the Halacha (Jerusalmi Bikurim 11,2), the whole avowal of having given tithes falls away if someone had given תרומה and the other מעשרות but had not been able to have מעשר שני — e.g. if he had only acquired fields and orchards in the third or sixth year of the Shimita cycle —. So we see here again how the sanctification of the material life of our senses is taken to be the foundation stone on which the whole Jewish life of duty rests. A fact which, as we have seen, can be followed right from the fundamental starting Mila-institution, circumcision, throughout the whole Lawgiving. It is true that in the performance of the tithe-duties מעשר ראשון has to be done first. For only through the spirit of the Torah which the tribe of Levi have to foster is the mission of elevating the material life of the senses (eating, drinking etc. I.L.) by sanctifying it (מעשר שני) and the welfare of one’s fellow-men cared for by the duties of love (מעשר עני) brought into real conscious activity. Without the illumination of the Torah the eating and drinking man remains just an animal, and the man of possessions an egoist. But in elevating human beings towards the Jewish ideals which the influence of the Torah effects, the מעשר שני concept of sanctifying the life of our senses stands definitely at the top. Only when a man in his enjoyments need not blush before God and His Sanctuary, only when a man in his enjoyments—equally far from moral lack of free-will and control (טומאה) as from grieving depression and undervaluing the joys of life (אנינות and נתינה למת)—tarries with his enjoyments, as being moral, holy, God-serving acts, in the purlieus of His Sanctuary of His Torah, with this sanctifying it to God, making all the contrast of His dual nature disappear from his sensuous life, and his morally sanctified body ennobled to be a bearer of the Divine spirit—only then does a Jewish person become enabled to draw the Truth from the pure spiritual well of the Torah, only then does his heart become wide enough to embrace the well-being of his fellow-men with happy selflessness as if it were his own. Does it not say in Ch. 14,23 referring to enjoying this מעשר שני in the City of the Temple:- ואכלת לפני ה׳ אלקיך במקום אשר יבחר לשכן שמו שם וגו׳ למען תלמד ליראה את ה׳ אלקיך כל הימים.

That is why the whole specific Lawgiving concludes with the מעשר שני avowal just as the whole of תורת כהנים, the great book of the priestly sanctification, Leviticus, closed with the institution of מעשר שני and the quite similar מעשר בהמה (see on XXVII,30-33 there).

V. 16. היום הזה. With to-day’s conclusion of the Lawgiving you really enter the duty of obeying this Torah. But, as so frequently in the Torah, the whole sum of the Lawgiviing is summarised in חקים and משפטים, in the laws of morality which fence in our private individual lives and in the regulations governing our living justly with one another, our social lives; as well as our task of שמירה and עשיה with reference to them, in our mental activity (learning I.L.) and conscientiousness (precautionary by-laws I.L.), and in our carrying them out in practice, but both בכל לבבך ובכל נפשך, with devoting the whole of our feeling and thinking and the whole of our living and striving selves.

V. 17. אמר .את ה׳ האמרת in the Hiphil only occurs here and in the following verse. In that form it can mean nothing else than to cause somebody else to say something. Now the whole contents of these two verses make את ה׳ האמרת וגו׳ being understood as “you have caused God to say”, and ה׳ האמירך וגו׳: “God has caused you to say”, for clearly V. 17 is what Israel says and V. 18 and 19 what God says. Now it is not unusual for the object about which one says something to be put in the accusative to the verb, אמר. Thus e.g. הוא הבאר אשר אמר in Numb. 21,16 (that is the well about which God said to Moses I.L.), אל המקום אשר אמר ה׳ אותו אתן לכם (ibid. X,29 “unto the place of which God had said etc. I.L.), אמרו צדיק כי טוב (Is. 3,10) “Say ye of the righteous etc.”. So that את ה׳ האמרת להיות לך לאלקים would mean: concerning God, of Him you have said that He is to be your God; and similarly ה׳ אמר אותך להיות לו לעם סגולה: God had said of you that you are to be a people belonging exclusively to Him. But האמרת and האמירך (in the Hiphil I.L.) means: You have brought it about, you have caused it to be said that He must be your God; and God has caused it to be said that you must be an עם סגולה to Him That is to say Israel’s solemn promise to God and God’s pledged Word to Israel has not remained, so to say, a private matter, it has become internationally known, a fact engraved in the mind of the world. Henceforth one designates God as “the God of the Jews”, and Israel as “the People of God”.

את ה׳ האמרת. Israel has vowed before all the world that להיות לך וגו׳, that it places its destiny and its deeds under the direction and guidance of God; וללכת בדרכיו that its efforts will only be to walk in the ways He indicates, ולשמר חקיו ומצותיו, to guard the laws, tasks and regulations which He has given it (see above) and obediently fulfil them.
