V. 18 & 19. וה׳ האמירך וגו׳: And God has spoken before all the world of Israel להיות לו וגו׳ that Israel belongs exclusively to Him, that no other might has power over Israel, ולשמר כל מצותיו like the cherub on the path of the Tree of Life, like the Cherubim over the Ark of the Covenant Israel is to be the Watchman, the guardian of God’s Laws of Morality on earth. ולתתך עליון על כל הגוים וגו׳. As soon as Israel proves itself a conscientious keeper of God’s Torah, He promises it a position in the history of the world which will raise it high above all the other nations which He has created, so that the fact of its national historical appearance will be לתהלה לשם ולתפארת to God on earth. Israel’s national historical appearance is to be תהלה, a revelation of God’s Ruling in the midst of the human world, really a “radiation” in historical appearances which leads back to God as its source, and proves His existence and ruling. And more than this, it is to be לשם, it is to be not a mere vague idea of there being One single Master of the ways of Nature and history, it is to be שם, by its wandering in the midst of the nations with the Book of His revelation of His teachings and laws in its hand as the one source of its spiritual, intellectual and active life and of its miraculous survival, it is to bring about a quite definite, clear, circumscribed conception of the Being and Will of this One God. And when, upheld by this God and by faithful adherence to His Laws, human beings and nations will have reached that ultimate security and happiness which God has guaranteed in His Torah, then Israel will be לתפארת, will become such a far-spread glorification of God and His Laws, outshining everything else that “nations will pilgrim to that Light”, and Israel will be “a crown of glory in the Hand of God and a royal diadem of its God” והיית עטרת תפארת ביד ה׳ וצניף מלוכה בכף אלקיך (Is. 62,3). ולהיותן עם קדוש וגו׳, and as God has declared before all the world that Israel, as the People of the Law of God are to be an instrument in His Hand for the enlightenment and civilisation of the nations, He has thereby האמירן brought to the knowledge of all men the calling of, and expectations from, Israel, that every member of it is to be one of an עם קדוש, a “holy” nation, only directed to what is morally good and satisfactory to God, so that if ever it should become unfaithful to its holy mission the smallest boy out of the other nations could remind it of its calling and obligations.

V. 1. שמר .ויצו משה וגו׳ infinitive “the guarding”. Now that the Lawgiving is quite concluded, the task is for you to “guard it”, i.e. to ensure that it is constantly studied and known and carried out, and moreover this is not to be the task just of the leaders and elders, the representatives of the nation, but of העם as well, of the whole people. Each one separately and all together are responsible for it. That is why Moses took the “elders of Israel” at his side and placed the whole nation under the obligation to keep the Torah. But he called the now completed Torah מצוה, one commandment, for all the laws together form the one mission for which Israel was appointed to its world-historic “post”.

V. 2. והיה ביום וגו׳. The erection of the stones, plastering them over, and writing the Torah on them is again commanded in verses 4-8 with the added details as to the place where they are to be erected and of the altar to be built and the offerings brought. So that verses 2,3 say: Not only when you have crossed the Jordan בעברכם, as in V.4, but, at once immediately, ביום אשר תעברו, at the time when you are about to cross over you are to busy yourselves with these stones plastered over, so that בעברכם when you will have crossed over (cf. בעברכם in V.12) you will write the whole Law on them. The erection of these stones, with which you are to occupy yourselves immediately when you wish to cross the Jordan, which you are to begin even before you have completed the crossing is to bring it about that you do actually cross the Jordan and enter the Promised Land. It is only the Torah that you have to thank for the Land, you receive the Land for the Torah, for its preservation and observation of its dictates. That is to be proclaimed immediately you cross over the river at its borders. Actually—as is reported in Josh. 4,2-8, and explained in Sota 32a, 35a—the stones were raised out of the Jordan itself, from the place where and while the priests stood with the Ark of the Covenant of the Torah, before which the waters of the Jordan retired (to make a dry passage for the People of the Torah I.L.),and then the stones were afterwards built up into an altar on Ebal and the words of the Torah written on them to a permanent memorial in Gilgal, the first resting place of Israel on the soil of their homeland; so that these stones could tell the very last grandson that נכרתו מימי הירדן מפני ארון ברית ה׳, that it was not before Israel, but before the Ark of the Torah that the torrents of the Jordan retreated, בעברו בירדן because it, the Torah, was moving to the place where its purpose could be realised. And already before they stepped into the Jordan, Joshua had appointed twelve men, one from each tribe, to raise and carry off these stones with them. If we look at the change from plural to singular, and from singular to plural in these verses 1-8, the thought could be expressed just in that, that the task of the שמירת התורה, to accomplish which the Promised Land was given, is not to be a matter for the single individuals of the nation, nor for the nation, as a whole as personified in its national representatives, but by the nation as a single unit made into such by the plurality of its members, so that the whole nation in the united working together of all its individuals were responsible for it. A thought which found a most suitable expression in choosing twelve men out of the people themselves from each tribe for the stones of the memorial to the Torah.
V. 4. בהר עיבל see on Ch. 11,29,30.

V. 5-7. ובנית שם וגו׳: on the bleak summit of Mt. Ebal, not on the blooming Mt. Gerisim the Torah-stones are to be built up into an altar. Fulfilling the Torah of God and the elevation of everything earthly to be striven for thereby is bound to no preliminary earthly conditions. The poorest earthly base is sufficient to lay the foundation there for the Torah of God and for your striving upwards to its ideal heights, is sufficient for you to find your peace and your happiness with these endeavours before the Presence of your God.
מזבח אבנים וגו׳: See Ex. on XX,24,25.
ושמחת לפני ה׳ אלקיך: Cf. Levit. P. 702.

V. 8. וכתבת וגו׳. In the rapturous feeling of what the future has in store for Israel if the Torah, by being made something real, itself becomes an altar striving upwards to God, and the rapturous feelings of how then, with the Torah taking the place of violence and force (ברזל), justice and the natural unstunted perfection of the spiritual and moral nobility innate in Man (אבנים שלמות), and thereby the spiritual and moral striving upwards to God (עולות) and the hale cheerful enjoyment of the things of this world (שלמים), and the undisturbable joy in the Presence of God, will enter into the sphere of Israel—in these feelings of rapture Israel is to write on these stones, brought up out of the bed of the Jordan by its tribes for the building of the first Altar of the Torah in the Land, “all the words of this Torah”. And with these stones and their origin it reminds itself that—as its national song (Ps. 114,7; Cf. Josh. 3,11,13) celebrates the memory of it—מלפני אדון חולי ארץ וגו׳ before the Lord, Whose Torah led the way through the torrents of the Jordan, all human force and greatness will retreat, and Israel, with all its “Jacob’s” weakness, as long as it follows the Ark of the Covenant of this Torah, will overcome all earthly obstacles.

באר היטב, compared with Habak. 2,2, כתוב חזון ובאר על הלחות למען ירוץ קורא בו (“write the vision down and make it clear on your tablets that he who runs may read it” I.L.), באר היטב here also could mean making the writing adequately clear and distinct. But Sota 32a, takes באר here in the sense of explaining, making it understood as in הואיל משה באר את התורה הזאת (Ch. 1,5), and teaches that a translation of this copy of the Torah was attached to it so that people of other nations might read it. Accordingly, far from the exclusiveness which is so falsely ascribed to us, Israel was from the very beginning to have to understand its mission for the spiritual and moral salvation of the whole of mankind whose future happiness was equally to be brought about by this entrance of the Divine Torah in their midst. More, there on 35a it is taught that even for the understanding of the people of Canaan, the proviso given in Ch. 20,18 for their being driven out למען אשר לא ילמדו אתכם לעשות ככל וגו׳ was repeated and explained in the copy of the Torah, so that they should know that the prospect of their being driven out was only if they persisted in their polytheistic ideas and ways of life, but if they would come back to obey the simple seven laws which apply to all human beings nothing stood in the way of their remaining in the land (see on Ch. 20,10 et seq. and 18).

V. 9. וידבר וגו׳. After the people themselves—not just their superiors—had been appointed the representatives and keepers of the Torah, made responsible for it, and had been given the order to give a permanent expression of this common responsibility by the erection of the “Stones of the Torah” on the first day of their entry into the Land, before the dispersion which would begin with their taking possession of the Land, Moses, gathering the priests, the teachers of the knowledge of the Law, around him, spoke to the whole of Israel as follows: -

הסכת .הסכת ושמע וגו׳ only occurs here. That אבן משכית (Levit. 26,1) might perhaps come from שכת ,סכת we suspected there, but see on Numb. 33,52. The phonetic relationship to שקט, perfect quiet, and שקד the intensive direction of one’s mind to a purpose, speak for its having the meaning of a strained intensive attention not to be diverted by anything else. Accordingly Moses demanded the most concentrated attention for what he had in mind to say to Israel and what he wanted the priests at his side to make everybody understand perfectly. And this speech which Moses was so anxious to be understood and taken to heart was the short sentence:-

היום הזה נהיית לעם. To-day you have become a people! The common duty to, and responsibility for the Torah which has just been declared for all of you without exception, the common care of the Torah to the guard of which you have all been posted, that makes you into a nation. To-day, before you get the impending possession of the Land, the common possession of the Torah, is what makes you into a nation. You can lose the Land, as indeed you may, but the Torah and your everlasting duty to it remains your everlasting unloseable bond which united you as a nation. This fundamental fact, deeply buried in Israel’s being, differentiates it sharply from that way all other nations have been formed, the secret of the national immortality of the Jews with all the consequences for Israel’s future which are attached to it, that is what—if we understand it rightly—which is the grave momentous importance of the sentence היום הזה נהיית לעם. The very first result of it is, of course: -

V. 10. ושמעת וגו׳ the still greater increased faithfulness and conscientiousness in fulfilling the dictates of this Torah. What treason to one’s country is to other nations, that is what treason to the Torah is to Israel. Significantly, here only מצות and חקים are mentioned, laws which, in the general opinion, do not affect the stability of the state or the welfare of the nation, as much as משפטים do, and moreover מצותיו is written with the plural form shortened, pointing to the unity and complete equal importance of all the mitzvas (cf. Ex. 33,13).

V. 11. ויצו משה. After Moses, drawing the elders round him, had first appointed the people to be the guardians of the Torah, then, drawing the priests around him, had called on the whole nation to regard and to take to heart this common obligation to the Torah as the one element which holds them together as a nation, he now commands the people to carry out from that standpoint the bestowing of the blessing and curse on Gerisim and Ebal which had already been ordered above in Ch. 11,29,30. Above it said ונתתה, the people themselves are to declare the alternative of blesssing or curse which God had placed before them for the fulfilling or not fulfilling of His Torah for themselves, those present and all those that at the time do, or in future will, belong to them, and thereby proclaim the Torah as the fundamental condition for the national welfare. This tendency of the proclamations is only intensified here after the people themselves have just been appointed the guardians of the Torah, and urged to take to heart that this “watch on the Torah” was the one and only soul of their national existence. The way in which the following proclamations are drafted shows still more specially how the whole of the nation, appointed as guardians of the Torah, before they separate and disperse to their individual homes, are to be individually reminded of their individual personal responsibility. Each one is to be reminded to take with him the thought of the ever-present Rule of God, dispensing blessing and curse for all cases which do not come to public knowledge, and therefore the communal authorities cannot exercise their duty of legal supervision over them.
V. 12 & 13. אלה יעמדו וגו׳ על הר גרזים וגו׳ ואלה וגו׳. See on Ch. 11,29,30.

לברך את העם not to receive the blessing, but to proclaim it over the nation. Equally so, יעמדו על הקללה is not passively standing to allow the קללה-proclamation to be declared over them, but designates rendering cooperative assistance at executing a task. Thus העומדים על הפקודים (Numb. 6,2) said of the princes who had to render asssistance to Moses and Aaron at taking the census of the people (ibid I,5). As remarked on V.11. the people themselves were to proclaim ברכה וקללה. It was therefore to be made clear by the arrangement and disposition, that the Levites (V.14) were not proclaiming blessing and curse as independent representatives of the Torah, but as agents and representatives of the people and in their name, accordingly the people declaring it over themselves. That is why the blessings and curses were not said from above, over the people gathered below, but the people had to be divided into two parts and the Levites stood in the middle between them. Thus what the Levites said came from the middle of the nation itself and by a universally pronounced “Amen”, from all sides, the assertion of the Levites became the assertion of the whole nation (see Gen. on XV,5, p. 273);.

When reckoning up the tribes, as in Ex. 1,2-4, the eight sons of Leah and Rachel are placed together (Joseph is missing there as he was already in Egypt) and then come the four sons of Bilha and Zilpa. Here the nation is to separate into two halves to have the Levites in the middle, so two of the eight have to be transferred to the other four. Now, to avoid any appearance of difference of rank in the two halves the tribes of the eldest and youngest of the sons of Leah, Reuben and Zebulun were to join those of Bilha and Zilpa. Hence the grouping:- Simon, Levi, Judah, Issachar, Joseph and Benjamin on the one side, and Reuben, Gad, Asher, Zebulun, Dan and Naphtali on the other. But also to avoid the slightest appearance of the קללה being said over the group of the בני השפחות, these were given their position just on Ebal so that the קללה pronouncements were made not to seem to be directed at them but to come from them. They were those that עומדים על הקללה and from the side of the בני אמהות the ברכות were directed at them. (But in reality of course, as explained above both blessing and curse were said as coming from the whole twelve tribes I.L.).

V. 14. וענו הלוים. The bulk of the Levites stood with the other tribes at Gerisim (V.12). In the middle between the two mounts only the זקני כהונה ולויה, the elders of the priesthood and Levites stood, or only כל הראוי לשרת, those called on for service in the Sanctuary between the ages of thirty and fifty (Sota 37a and Numb. IV; see Josh. 8,23). According to one opinion (ibid) the tribes as well as the Levites stood between the two mounts, and על הר גרזים only means “at”, בסמוך similarly to ונתת הפכו פניהם כלפי הר גריזים ופתחו בברכות .על המערכת לבונה זכה (ויקרא כ״ד ז׳) כלפי הר עיבל ופתחו בקללות, the Levites turned towards Mt. Gerisim and began the blessing, towards Mt. Ebal and began the curse (ibid). For the Halacha teaches that each of the following pronouncements of curse was preceded by the negative contrast as blessing. Thus: ברוך האיש אשר לא יעשה וגו׳ (“Blessed be the man that does not make” etc. I.L.) and then ארור האיש אשר יעשה וגו׳ (cursed be the man that maketh etc. I.L.) (ibid. 32a, 37b). And that agrees with the wording of V.12 and 13 and Ch. 11,29, and the report in Josh. (ibid.) which runs: כאשר צוה משה עבד ה׳ לברך העם ישראל בראשנה.

V. 15-25. ארור :ארור וגו׳, see Gen. 3,14. We have already remarked on V.11 that it is sins which as a rule escape the attention of the human courts, which are here placed under the Rule of God’s dispensation of blessing and curse. In verses 15 and 24 this is definitely expressed by בסתר (practised secretly I.L.). And if the other sins which are visited by בסתר are such which, as a rule, by their nature remain hidden secret sins, this express mention of בסתר at the beginning and end of the list stresses all the more the character of sinning in secrecy being the motive for these proclamations of ארור. Thereby, all those are particularly affected who under the cloak of apparent outer respectability practice in secret moral and social depravity.
Taking them altogether these curses would express the thought:-

ארור. All blessing is denied to him who outwardly plays the pious man devoted to God, but in secret denies the exclusive existence of One God and His Rule; who outwardly is respectful to his parents but inwardly considers himself vastly superior to them; who in the eyes of men preserves the reputation of an honest man, but where it is unobserved does not hesitate to injure the rights of his neighbour to his own advantage; who is full of enthusiasm for the welfare of his neighbours in the presence of clever and intelligent people, but pushes shortsighted and blind people into misfortune; who grovels before the powerful, but denies the weak and helpless their rights; pretends to be a highly respectable member of society, to wallow in sexual licentiousness in intimate privacy. (Verses 20-24); who does not dig a dagger into his neighbour, but under the cloak of conversation murders his happiness, his peace and his honour; who enjoys the highest confidence in his community but misuses it in secret corruption; finally also one, even if he lives correctly and dutifully for himself still looks with indifference on the abandonment of the duties of the Torah in his immediate and wider circles.

פסל ומסכה. If, according to a suggestion we made on Levit. 19,4, מסכה could be the representation of a protective god, or rather an idol to guard and protect (refer to it there), then פסל would be an idol made with the idea of its being a god, and by a פסל the monotheistic idea of there being only one God is denied, and by מסכה the extent of His Power being sufficient by itself is doubted.

קלה .מקלה related to גלה, to be deprived of external hold, to be deprived of the protection and support of one’s homeland; to כלה to cease to exist, to disappear from the sphere of existence, קלה means to rob something of its vigour and sap, to dehydrate, to wither, transferred to spiritual and moral conditions, to lose respect for somebody’s moral worth, to deny him the recognition of his moral value, hence קלון: disgrace (cf. כבד and קלל).
מסיג גבול רעהו, without his noticing it to shift the border of his property backwards or to lessen his rights in any way.
מטה משפט וגו׳. See on Ch. 24,17.

מכה רעהו בסתר, he strikes his neighbour without the latter knowing it, or finding out from where the blow came. This is the blow struck with slander, לשון הרע, which, out of the reach of the law courts, undermines the happiness, peace and honour of one’s neighbour. Scandal-mongering is a sin which, like no other, becomes so easily a habit, it becomes more and more a daily and hourly practice. That is why it does not say here מַכֶּה which as a verb would also designate the blow being given just once, but מַכֶּה (a smiter) which as a noun form designates one to whom scandal- mongering is habitual and has become part of his character. It does not designate the sin itself but the disgraceful creature who is a scandal-monger.

אשר לא יקים וגו׳, it does not say אשר לא יעשה whereby the neglecting of any single mitzva would entail the curse. But אשר לא יקים את דברי התורה הזאת לעשות אותם, who does not maintain the words of the Torah to be kept, i.e. who deprives one single word of God’s Torah of its validity and binding power, who persuades himself or lets himself be persuaded, that it no longer need be kept, has lost its meaning and importance (רמב״ן ibid.); and equally so, who, wherever he can, does not stand up with all his might, and is active in seeing that the mitzvas of the Torah are kept. למד ולימד שמר עשה והיתה ספוקו בידו להחזיק ולא החזיק הרי זה בכלל ארור and “even if a man had studied the Torah and taught it, had been careful not to transgress the prohibitions and to perform the commandments, but, although he could have been able to influence and strengthen others to do likewise, and had refrained from doing so, he too would come under this curse.” (תוספות Sota 37b according to the Jerusalmi.).

It could seem striking that in the list of these proclamations the sentences referring to social sins (verse 17-19) should be interrupted by the sexual sins (verses 20-23), and then continued again in V.24. We should have expected מכה רעהו and לוקח שוחד to have followed immediately after מטה משפט. But this inserting these secret sexual sins in between the social ones, could be just to show the complete equality of the gravity of both these kinds of sins. And it would work both ways. It would counter the erroneous idea that while משגה עור ,מטה משפט ,מסיג גבול (17,18,19. I.L.) could well be stigmatised as injurious to the public welfare, sexual sins, while at most they undermine the individual welfare, do not affect that of the public; or the other way, גלוי עריות would indeed weigh heavily on the Jewish conscience, but הסגת גבול and לשון הרע etc. do not seem so grave. In both directions this arrangement of mixing the two categories together would definitely counter such false ideas. And to still further stress this complete lack of any distinction, just between verses 19 and 20, where the social list is broken off and goes over to the sexual one, the פרשה סתומה stop (ס I.L.) which separates all the other sentences is lacking. (See כסף משנה on הל׳ ספר תורה ,רמב״ם VIII,4).

The text only contains the ארור sentences, which, as remarked, were always preceded by the ברוך declaration in the simple negation of the subject of the ארור sentence:- ברוך האיש אשר לא יעשה פסל וגו׳. All the sins which come under the curse, except the last one, are positive active transgressions of prohibitions, so that the sentences promising blessings refer to the mere abstaining from transgressing prohibitions e.g. “Blessed and prosperous will be he who does not give himself up even in secret to idolatrous ideas”; “even in his own secret heart does not nurse disrespectful thoughts of his father and mother”; does not allow himself to practice in secret sexual depraved acts etc. etc. What infinite comfort lies here! How much nearer is the blessing to us than the curse. The curse only comes if we positively and actually do something bad. But we have only to abstain from doing any of these curse-bringing acts to have already brought the blessing on us, without our doing anything at all. Only the last sentence of the list of the curses ארור אשר לא יקים וגו׳ speaks of being cursed for abstaining from doing something and thereby only promises the blessing if we actively do something ברוד אשר יקים את דברי התורה הזאת לעשות אותם. For this refers to recognising or not recognising, of maintaining or refraining from maintaining the Torah. In that case indifference is already sufficiently grave to entail coming under the curse, and blessing will only come if everyone does what he possibly can to ensure that the everlasting Torah receives everlasting recognition of its validity and is observed.

V. 1. והיה וגו׳. In the preceding chapter the people were appointed to be guardians of the Torah, and as such, immediately on their entry into the Land and before taking possession of it and apportioning it out they were ordered to write the Torah on stones erected as a memorial and altar, so that the Land be dedicated and proclaimed as the Land of the Torah. And also to put in the mind of every single individual, for his subsequent dispersal to his own home that his fulfilment or otherwise of his Torah-duties comes under the administration of God’s dispensing blessing or curse.

Now here Moses gives the people a picture of the future, how it will work out for the nation if the people as a whole do not keep the dictates of the Torah, what national prosperity or adversity it has to expect for faithfulness or unfaithfulness to the Torah. Such an encouraging and warning declaration of the future of the nation had already been given at the end of Leviticus (Ch. XXVI). If one carefully compares these two proclamations, one finds that whereas in the first one the national prosperity or the reverse is depicted more in the general condition itself of the nation, here, in this compendium for the impending dispersion of the nation all over the land, it is more the participation which each individual will have to enjoy or suffer in the general conditions which is described, so that his own personal interest in the national development is brought vividly to his mind. This is quite in keeping with the whole tendency of the משנה תורה (Deuteronomy I.L.) which we have so frequently pointed out. It would apply quite specially to the ערבות, the solidarity of all for all, which was expressed in the immediately preceding אשר לא יקים וגו׳ with the most serious gravity possible, making everyone responsible to use his utmost powers not only for his own, but in narrower or wider circles, for the general keeping of God’s Torah. The above-mentioned way of taking the תוכחה (the warning I.L.) which follows here by making every individual know and feel, how by every furthering of faithfulness to the Torah amongst his contemporaries he is only ensuring his own welfare, as well as by being indifferent to the defection from the Torah of his brethren he is only working at his having to share their ruin.

והיה אם שמוע וגו׳. Cf. Ch. 11,13. — את כל מצותיו, summarises the whole Torah and all its prescribed injunctions in the one concept of God-ordered duties. The results pictured here of fulfilling them rest on the fact that they are God’s directions for the tasks we have to do on earth. — ונתנך וגו׳ עליון, if your giving yourself entirely to fulfil His Will and His Will only becomes realised in your nation and through your nation, then He will raise you high above all the effects of the purely physical order of things, and thereby raises you high above all the nations of the world who strive for the conditions for their existence and prosperity in a fight against the forces of the world of Nature and human society which is opposed to them.

V. 2. ובאו עליך וגו׳ והשיגך כי תשמע. The blessings of thriving and prosperity come by themselves, they come to you without your having sought for them, they overtake you, you do not overtake them, they do not form the goal which your doings and abstaining from doing were aimed at. And just because that was not what you were aiming at, because all you wanted to do and accomplish was to fulfil the Will of your God on earth, had no other object in view than to do your duty towards God, the blessings of God pursue you to help and further your endeavours which are nothing but to accomplish the purposes of God on earth.

V. 3 & 4. ברוך וגו׳. As a result of your keeping the moral and social laws, your family life and your communal life blossoms, and as a result of your keeping the laws of agriculture and stock-farming, your fields blossom and your live stock thrives. Yea, in contrast to the usual way of economics in the world, the ברכה בשדה does not bring about the ברכה בעיר, prosperity in the town does not prevail because there is prosperity in the fields, but ברוך אתה בעיר comes first and then ברוך אתה בשדה. Because your family life and your social life is carried on in the principles of morality, justice and brotherly love, God’s blessing is deserved and won in the city, therefore God sends His blessing on your fields, makes the fruit of your body, of your soil, of your cattle, thrive, because your children are born for a moral, honest and righteous human life, and what gets increased for you out of physical Nature by being used in your hands for the purposes of a free-willed dutiful human life becomes elevated and ennobled.
שגר siehe Schmot 13, 12; עשתרות siehe Dewarim 7, 13.

V. 5. ברוך טנאך וגו׳. That is why your “basket” and your “kneading-trough” get blessed, that is why you find blessing when you stand with your “basket” in your orchards and fields to gather your fruit, and find it when you come to prepare the bread with which to feed yourself and your household. (טנאך and משארתך correspond to בכורים and חלה; — see Ch. 26,2, and Numb. 15,20; משארתך see Ex. 12,34). And that is why
V. 6. ברוך אתה בבאך וגו׳ you are blessed in your home life and in your public life.

V. 7. יתן ה׳ את אויבך וגו׳, and also for your external political relations you require no other national political administration than your faithful obedience to your duty towards God. God Who grants you the happiness of your homes and your cities, the prosperous state of your fields and livestock also makes you safe from any attack from outside. Yea: -

V. 8. יצו ה׳ וגו׳. This is no repetition of the blessing of the land already expressed in verses 4 and 5, otherwise its place would have been before v.6, but it is an intensification of the whole blessing described hitherto. The blessing of God does not only come over you and all that you do, as pictured hitherto ובאו עליך כל הברכות האלה but יצו ה׳ אתך את הברכה God will command the blessing to be always there with you, to accompany you always. Everything that you do, and because it is you that are doing it, will succeed and prosper. This is the summit of God’s most gracious placing a man with regards to his wishes and accomplishments, which marks his moral character deserving the proximity of God also in the eyes of other people. So it says of Joseph, in Gen. 39,3,5, וירא אדניו כי ה׳ אתו וכל אשר הוא עושה ה׳ מצליח בידו (“And his master saw that God was with him, and whatever he did God made succeed in his hand” I.L.). So it says of Laban that even he had an inkling that God helped Jacob: - נחשתי ויברכני ה׳ בגללך (ibid XXX,27). This is the stage of blessing and happiness that every member of Israel is to reach if Israel will prove faithful to God in its land.

אסמיך only occurs again in Prov. 3,10. It could be formed from a combination of שום and סמם (see Gen. 11,6) with prefixed א, like אצר is from צור with prefixed א. It designates that which somebody has laid aside for himself, has heaped up to be stored. In Aramaic and Rabbinic Hebrew סימא denotes a treasure. באסמיך וגו׳ (see on Ch. 11,12,13).

V. 9 & 10. יקימך וגו׳ בי תשמר וגו׳. You get this whole blessing because when you conscientiously fulfil God’s commandments, and strive for your personal and national aims in the way God directs, God wishes to establish you לו (I.L.) for Himself, i.e. for His purposes for mankind. You are to belong to Him as a “holy”nation. He wishes to mark you as a nation which keeps afar from everything low and vulgar, bringing to realisation only what is morally good and sound, as an example to all the nations of the world that they may see what it means to be “the People of God”, what it means if a whole nation, all of it, great and small, submits its whole existence and will, individually and nationally, to the Will of God. That they may see what a degree of blessing and happiness, what power and strength lies in such a “Tephilin-wearing” nation (as our sages pun on ויראו ממך in Menachoth 35b), and from your internal moral greatness and historic loftiness the glory of such a sublime life will radiate out to them, in face of which all the greatness of their power and glory will be recognised as petty and insignificant.

This effect which the whole nature and appearance of your nation is to have in influencing the rest of mankind to spirituality and morality is the purpose of your mission in the history of the world. That is why
V. 11. והותרך וגו׳, literally: God makes you appear in all that is good, compared to the other nations, as superior, ranking above, it is because of that

V. 12. יפתח וגו׳, that God makes even the weather conditions, which are necessary for the products of your soil to thrive, come with a punctual regularity which proves His direct intervention, and give you such abundance that when there is scarcity elsewhere you will have to help out from your superfluity, but the reverse situation will never occur with you, and so

V. 13 & 14. ונתנך וגו׳, God makes you into a leading head and not to a following tail. By the unexampled blessings which God showers on you as the result of your faithful devotion to duty you draw the eyes of the nations to you, so that they recognise your example to be worth following, and you will be the leading example, but in no ways will you feel inclined to imitate them והיית רק למעלה וגו׳, and in all human relationships, physical, spiritual and moral, in your individual, family and public life you will belong to the higher class of all human endeavours and have nothing in common with the low, the vulgar, the bad, the transient. All this: כי תשמע וגו׳ if you have the Torah which you have now received constantly before your eyes with שמירה and עשיה with intellectual knowledge and conscientious care in practising it. And לא תסור וגו׳, do not turn aside, neither to the right nor to the left, neither in doing nor in abstaining from doing, from any single one of the precepts, which I have now given not only to the nation as a whole, but אשר אנכי מצוה אתכם היום (in the plural I.L.) but to each individual person of you. The slightest deviation from God’s ways means an inclination towards those false gods whose supposed good graces and assistance every step away from God’s Ways imagines it can, and so has to, achieve. Every attempt to gain possessions, every enjoyment, every purpose that leads us away from obeying the Will of God is quite literally עבודה זרה, serving another power which we allow to become the god who directs our mind, our feelings and will. And just as the tiniest, almost imperceptible angle from a straight line never comes back into that straight line but becomes ever increasingly distant from it, so the slightest intentional deviation away from God’s ways leads to ever greater distance until complete defection. Hence ולא תסור מכל הדברים וגו׳ ימין ושמאל ללכת אחרי אלהים אחרים לעבדם.

V. 15. והיה אם לא וגו׳. Above, v. 1. in the introduction to the blessings which would come if the Torah was faithfully kept, all the commandments of the Torah were summarised in the one concept, מצות. For cheerful obedience, for the happy observance of our duty, all the commands,—the positive to be performed, the negative to be abstained from—are equal, they are the directions which we, on the post on which we have been posted for the service of our lives, have to observe as members of the great host of servants in God’s hosts of His realm of this world. The negative restricting ones no less than the positive active ones fill us with the same elevated feelings of the happy consciousness of faithfully carrying out the service to God of our lives. But here in the sad contrast of the eventuality of the Torah not being kept חקתיו are mentioned as well as מצותיו, for, to those who forget their duty, it is the הקים, that part of the laws which restrict the desires of our senses and national life, which to those who are turning aside from God are mostly in opposition to their feelings.
ובאו וגו׳ והשיגוך, they will sooner or later overtake you, you cannot escape them.
V. 16. ארור וגו׳. See on V.3.

V. 17 & 18. The blessing of God bringing happiness to those who are faithful to their duty shows itself first of all on the children and living creatures and then in this happy blooming condition of life in the blessing of the fruit of the soil. First ברוך פרי בטנך and then ברוך טנאך ומשארתך. But the adversity which follows defection does not at once affect the living creatures. It makes itself first felt as a warning on טנאך ומשארתך before it affects פרי בטנך.
V. 19. See on V.6.

V. 20. ישלח וגו׳. It has often been thought that one has to prove the literal realisation of the troubles proclaimed here in the following verses in the history of the sufferings of the downfall of the life of the two Jewish States. And as a matter of fact the history of the more than two thousand years of suffering on the whole of the Jewish people is also the most vivid commentary on these proclamations; and especially the literal realisation of the proclaimed fate of dispersion amongst the nations of the world of verses 64 and 67 makes—right up to the present day—even to the most unimaginative eye, every Jew a living testimonial and witness to the veracity and divinity of a writing which could make such a declaration as guaranteed for thousands of years of the future. But regarding the single phases which are prophesised in the picture of suffering unfolded here, we think there are two things we may consider.

Firstly, the description of the sufferings which follow here cannot possibly be meant to refer to the whole nation. That is already excluded by the oft repeated final fate עד כלתו אתך ,עד אברך ,עד השמדך (“until you are destroyed”, “until you are perished”, “until it makes an end of you” etc. I.L.). If the whole nation is sentenced and destroyed entirely by מארה etc. (in V. 20 I.L.) then that cannot happen to it by דבר (V.21, I.L.) and if by דבר it cannot be destroyed by שחפת etc. (in V.22 I.L.), and if it has already been made an end of by all these it cannot then in V.35 be visited by all the horrors of war etc. Rather, so it seems to us at least, these pronouncements are made only in the sense of that some will go to ruin through illness, others through pestilence, others through scarcity of crops, others again through wars etc. and this would be quite in accordance with the remark we made above on V.1. that the characteristic tendency of this תוכחה here is primarily directed to make the individuals feel how painfully the defection of the nation in general could affect them personally, how they would have to participate in the ruin of the State. Further we believe, it should not be overlooked that the proclamations of these verdicts on the nation are only hypothetical, dependent on the case of the complete defection and universal disobedience of the whole nation, a degree of deterioration which, thank God, has never been reached. Always, as we know from the Prophets, there has been a שארית, a minority left over who remained faithful. Yea, we have pointed out elsewhere, how this minority, although it was a minority, must still have been a very important minority, that the defection and deterioration spread primarily in the upper ranks of society, but that the people nurtured a very pure nucleus quietly in their midst, otherwise in times of the greatest deterioration, in the time of the Judges and Kings, men and women of such nobility of spirit and morals could not have arisen that God found them suitable for Him to use them as His instruments and messengers. But if the defection was never absolute in degree and extent then “destruction” was also never absolute, and God’s leniency could always save a “remnant” of them for the future final happiness and salvation which was no less definitely pronounced.

ישלח. Refer to Numb. 21,6. The curse of מהומה and מגערת (disquietude and self-reproach) comes by itself, it comes at once to everybody who leaves the path of rectitude and goodness, hence ישלח, God has only not to keep it back, gives you no help to get over it. את המארה את המהומה By the accentuation את המהומה is in apposition to את המארה, “the curse, restlessness”. By sinning, the inner serenity disappears, and מהומה, internal disquiet, and מגערת, a constant feeling of reproach, self-reproach takes its place, the consciousness of deserving the reproach of God. Thus ויגער בו אביו (Gen. 37,10; cf. Levit. 26,16). This inner feeling of restlessness and constant self-reproach disturbs the success of all that you do בכל משלח וגו׳.

V. 21. ידבק ה׳ וגו׳. It is not impossible that the state of inner restlessness and the worry of self-reproach itself has the effect of raising the attack of an epidemic (דבר I.L.) to a devasting degree, whereas serenity of mind and confidence in God in the mind gives resistance to the disease.

V. 22. שחפת; (related to שאב to draw, שאף to draw deep breaths), exhaustion, wasting away. חרחר from חרר to dry out by heat. ובחרב, taken in conjunction with the preceding words in the sentence, חרב here can scarcely have the meaning of sword. It could much more likely be in the meaning of חרב, dryness, desiccation. As in Ps. 32,4 נהפך לשדי בחרבני קיץ סלה (“My sap was changed into the drought of summer” I.L.). שדפון: cf. שדופות קדים in Gen. 41,6.
V. 23. תחתיך ,על ראשך. They are not general calamitous conditions, they affect just you.

V. 24. מטר ארצך אבק ועפר. Instead of the rain falling from heaven and just through the complete lack of it the wind will whirl dust and earth up in the air and it will then fall down on to the fields and meadows and spoil the crops and vegetation. Thus in Taanith 9b. it says: אבק ועפר מן השמים היכי משכחת ליה אלא כיון דמדלי להתם מן השמים קרי לה.

V. 25. לזעוה, from זעה synonymous with זיע to quiver, from which we get זועה in Is. 28,19 והיה רק זועה הבין שמועה. “To understand what is heard would be nought but terror”. The miseries of war which would be brought about by your enemies (e.g. V.32,57 I.L.) will be so unspeakable that the very thought of the possibility of such wretchedness would make your enemies shiver.
V. 26. והיתה וגו׳ ואין מחריד. None will be left to bury the dead and the land will be so desolate that the vultures will be undisturbed in their grisly meal.
V. 28. תמהון לבב, haziness, confusion, cloudiness of perception, of thoughts and ideas (see Gen. 43,33).

V. 29. והיית ממשש וגו׳, you will lose the clear perception of things and conditions and so you will bring about that what you undertake does not achieve the desired end, and others take advantage of your perplexity, especially the neighbouring nations to rob you of your rights (עשוק) and of your possessions (גזול).

V. 30-32. Verses 30-32 just give examples of what was indicated in V.29. In these and similar instances we believe we can see a confirmation of the opinion we have already expressed, viz. that in this תוכחה, it is not so much the fate of the general downfall of the state, as the extreme misery and wretchedness in the various stages which is to be brought vividly home to the minds of the individuals which they would have to suffer if the whole state collapses as a result of the defection of the overwhelming majority. שורך וגו׳ ,כרם וגו׳ ,בית וגו׳ ,אשה וגו׳ (a wife etc, a vineyard, a house, your ox etc. I.L.) etc. are all features which come to be realised in the fate of the individual rather than of the state.

V. 33. פרי אדמתך וגו׳, summarises the preceding again as the effect of the aggression which the neighbouring nations with whom in happier times you had no contact whatsoever now allow themselves, all as the result of your spiritual and material decay. They deny you all consideration of the commonest rights of nations (עשוק), and misuse their power, to crush your last remaining strength (רצוץ).

V. 35. יככה וגו׳. The isolated position of this verse just before the partial exile announced in the following verse, especially as מכת שחין is already mentioned above in V.27, could perhaps wish to say that the exiles referred to in the following verses would be led into exile afflicted with such a nasty skin disease by which their position amongst the foreign nations who hated them quite enough already, would be made still more unbearable.

V. 36. יולך וגו׳. As verses 38-43 still speak of troubles which clearly indicate their living still in their own land, the exile announced here could perhaps be only a partial one, by which only a part of the nation would have to wander off into banishment, similar to the expulsion of the ten tribes or the transportation of Jehoiachin and his court and seven thousand men to Babylon (Kings II,XXIV). But probably the way we take the following verses would be more appropriate and fit better. (see on verses 37-45).

ועבדת שם וגו׳, and again in V. 64. The context teaches that here it is not speaking of actual idolatry, but is rather a description of the general fate which would befall Israel in exile. The nations to whom Israel would be subject, and on whose feelings and opinions and outlook Israel’s future fate would depend, are themselves under the mastery of the heathen gods and form their whole way of life and behaviour under their influence. So that in truth Israel is subject to the pagan worship of the gods. It had rejected the service of the One God, now it learns to feel the errors and degeneration into which human minds and hearts sink which are not devoted to the acknowledgement of the One God, but form their thoughts and frame of mind, their feelings and behaviour under the sway of heathen imagined mighty powers. All the bitterness of the future centuries of exile is rooted in the fact that Israel’s fate became dependent on men before whose eyes the light of monotheistic Truth did not shine and did not bring them to humaneness by its penetrating education. That this is the sense of this sentence ועבדת שם is shown by its explanatory paraphrase in Jer. 16,13:- והטלתי אתכם מעל הארץ הזאת על הארץ אשר לא ידעתם אתם ואבותיכם ועבדתם שם את אלהים אחרים יומם ולילה אשר לא אתן לכם חנינה.

V. 37-45. והיית לשמה למשל ולשנינה וגו׳. With this verse, one purpose, in any case one good result is disclosed as being attached to the “desolation” which befalls Israel. שמה is the complete contrast to a condition flourishing in blessing (see on Gen. 42,21). This desolation, which is again presented with full details in the following verses 38-44, and the cause which brought it about (V. 45), becomes a world-historic fact, publicly making it known how and why Israel goes into exile, and thereby carries through the world the consciousness of God’s imposing duties on men and nations and passing judgment on them accordingly. Israel’s שמה, Israel’s downfall becomes למשל ולשנינה an admonishing and warning example and an impressive lesson for the nations. What has been done to Israel is only a משל, is only an example demonstrated on one nation, which all nations have to fear if they turn their backs to God’s Laws of universal morality. And inasmuch as Israel becomes scattered amongst all the nations and in spite of their dismemberment do not become absorbed into them, but, as it says in V.46, just by their fate, demonstrative of God, remain existing as a nation throughout the centuries, it becomes in truth a שנינה (see Ch. 6,7) a precise, sharply defined impressive lesson in God’s Hands for the education of the nations. And that which Israel faithful to God was to have been in joyful happiness, and what it will be in future in regained happiness and security, a lighthouse in the darkness of the world, guiding and gathering the nations to God and His Laws (Isaiah II; LX), that Israel is to become, suffering dire troubles in exile to prepare the world for its future complete salvation to happiness and security.
V. 38. חסל ,יחסלנו is a stronger form of אזל, the complete going away, disappearance, and an active form, completely consuming.

V. 39. אגר ,תאגר to collect to store up. אוגר בקיץ (Prov. 10,5), it is גור ,גר, taken away from the ground, with the prefixed individualising א, for one’s own purposes, for oneself. A writing in which one lays down collected thoughts about something is accordingly called אגרת, a letter. לא תשתה ולא תאגר. Ordinarily you not only have wine to drink but have enough to store up. Now you will have no wine to drink much less then to store any up. Or אגר refers to the gathering of the grapes. “You shall not have wine to drink, not even grapes to gather”.

V. 42. יירש, a stronger form of ירש; to take completely into possession. הצלצל, the swarm of locusts, so-called either because they are so numerous that they put the sun into shade or because of their deafening noise. Both factors are mentioned of such a swarm in Joel 2,2,5. צלל, see on Gen. 19,8.
V. 43. הגר. All this misfortune comes to you quite individually. On the very same ground that you go to ruin in complete devastation, the stranger next to you prospers.

V. 45. ובאו עליך. All these troubles come to you, and the stranger in your midst remains immune from them, and just that marks them as being God’s punishing judgment for your disobedience to His Torah.
V. 46. והיו בך. This punishing judgment bringing about the downfall of your State becomes a world-historic אות showing God’s Rule.

V. 47-48. אשר ישלחנו ה׳ בך ,תחת וגו׳, “whom God sent against you”, or rather, as שלח generally means in the Piel, “whom God allowed to come against you”, did not prevent them from subjugating you. Thus Israel’s downfall under the Assyrian-Babylonian might was a quite natural result of that world-conquering force against Israel’s unwarlike impotence which fell to the superior forces as soon as God withdrew His protection. הסר משוכתו והיה לבער (Is. 5,5).

V. 49. ישא וגו׳: If the way we described verses 36-48 to be taken be not erroneous, then those verses would be referring to the political downfall which Israel’s first existence as a state suffered under the Assyrian-Babylonian might. But with this verse (49) the announcement of the second catastrophe begins. The catastrophe which overtook the Jewish State, restored again after the Babylonian exile, and was brought about, not by a neighbouring nation but from the distant Roman Empire, and ended with Israel’s complete dispersion (V. 64). The realisation of the stress of war and the horrors of siege and the wretchedness of the dispersion described here in advance, can be followed almost step by step still to-day after nearly two thousand years in the records of the pages of history of the sufferings of the Jewish people beginning with the subjection of Judea under the Roman legions.
V. 50. גוי עז פנים, whose physiognomy expresses the stern harshness of his character (Roman I.L.).

V. 52. והצר לך וגו׳ והצר לך וגו׳. Two factors could have offered resistance to the progress of the enemy: - the fortifications of your cities, which seemed so strong in your eyes, and more than these, the protection of God, Who had directed you to land and the cities to be the place of your residence. Neither will help you. The former just because you trusted in them rather than to the support of God which you would receive for your faithfulness to your duty, and this latter just because you had become unworthy of it by failing to be faithful to your duty.

V. 57. כי תאכרם. There is a gruesome logical accuracy in which the same beings (grown up children and tiny babes I.L.) to whom she grudges to give a morsel of what she is eating—תדע עינה—are the same objects which she is driven to eat. Whom despair drives to the former will turn more easily to the latter.

V. 58. אם לא תשמר וגו׳. One thought should have kept the people back from disobedience to the Torah entrusted to them here, and that is this: - that with the giving and accepting of this Torah ה׳ had become אלקינו. That with the giving and accepting of this Torah, ה׳, He, the God of Love on Whose Will every coming moment of the existence of the world itself and every single being in it depends, undertook quite specially the guidance of our behaviour and the direction of our fate (Ex. 20,2), and as such expects unswerving obedience. This name “ה׳ אלקיך״ is “נכבד״ and “נורא״. Its possitive aspect is נכבד, is weighty, full of meaning, and to one who makes this meaning of the Name apply to himself, to him God lays the world at his feet; and equally so is He נורא to one who acts in opposition to the meaning of this Name. This Name ה׳ אלקינו was applied to us with מתן תורה and thereby we are appointed in the history of the world to be the bearers of that Name. כל דברי התורה הזאת הכתובים בספר הזה, every word of this Torah, given over to us with this written book, teaches us nothing else but how to be able to justify this שם הנכבד והנורא—which is undetachably attached to us—being applied to us. We are ever to keep vividly in our minds how נורא (fearsome I.L.) this שם הנכבד that we bear is at the same time, the steps of unspeakable woe which we can call down on ourselves and our children by degrading the name borne by us. So that we נשמר לעשות את כל דברי התורה הזאת הכתובים בספר הזה (“are to be careful to learn and observe all the words of this Torah which are written in this book” I.L.) if at the end it was still only ליראה את השם הנכבד והנורא הזה את ה׳ אלקיך (“to fear this honoured and fearsome Name of God Who is your God” I.L.). But if even this warning should be in vain, and you, taking no notice of it, by carelessness and disobedience are false to the name you bear, then

V. 59. והפלא וגו׳, then God will make the sufferings that you and your children will have to bear a פלא (see Ex. 15,11). They will not be ordinary sufferings which you will get, they will clearly reveal the השם הנכבד והנורא in the whole of its gravity to which you paid no attention. Every extraordinary suffering which comes to you will be a sign that God still keeps His Eye on you, a sign of the truth of the Torah and for the direction in which alone the road to salvation and happiness lies for you, and for the whole world it will be a sign for the One, Only One Whom they did not know, and of Man’s duty to Him of which they had no idea.

V. 63. והיה כאשר שש. It does not simply say כאשר שש להיטיב אתכם כן ישיש להאביד אתכם (just as He rejoiced to do you good so will He rejoice to let you go to ruin I.L.) but, כאשר שש עליכם כן ישיש עליכם וגו׳ “as He rejoiced for your sakes to do you good, so for your sakes will God rejoice to let you go to ruin”. That is to say that just as it was to have been for your good that He made you so extraordinary fortunate so will it be for your good that He lets you be so extraordinarily unfortunate. It is ה׳ the same God of Love, the same thoughtful wisdom, the same ruling of the world for your and mankind’s future that suspends such a fate of suffering over your heads. להאביד and להשמיד (to cause you to go to ruin and destruction I.L.) cannot mean a real complete destruction, as it then immediately goes on to say ונסחתם and והפיצך וגו׳ (“you will be torn away from your land and scattered I.L.) to explain the nature of the destruction being only comparative, a complete banishment from the land.
V. 64. ועבדת וגו׳. See on V.36.

V. 65. לא תרגיע. The phonetic relation to רקע to tread down (see on Gen. 1,6) gives the weaker form רגע the conception of letting oneself down, to stop or suspend a motion. Hence רגע, the thought of a tiny part of the restless continuous flow of time held fast, a minute (actually the very reverse of the conception expressed by our word moment). Hence רוגע הים to calm the ever-agitated sea. מרגוע, the mind or feelings becoming composed ובגוים ההם לא תרגיע “amongst those nations you will find no rest, really, your mind will not settle down, its activity will never be able to be quiet, and ולא יהיה וגו׳, and externally also you will find no spot on earth which offers your foot a secure footing to which it is entitled. You will never become absorbed into the nations to be considered as being entitled to completely equal rights.

ונתן ה׳ וגו׳. In V.3 of the following chapter, the effect which the experiences which God had given them was to have had on their minds and inner feelings but which had hitherto failed to have was expressed thus: ולא נתן ה׳ לכם לב לדעת וגו׳ עד היום הזה. Quite in the same way it says here ונתן ה׳ לך שם לב רגז וגו׳: God will make your fate among the nations such that it will give you a לב רגז etc.

רגז in the majority of cases does not designate to be angry but to tremble from fear (see on Gen. 12,5 and XLV, 24). Here too it does not mean being easily excited to anger, but an anxious, trembling state of mind.

כליון, from כלה “to long for something”. דאב designates, internal distress, woe. Cf. Levit. 26,16. לב רגז you will always fear some fresh misfortune. כליון עינים, you will never see your wishes fulfilled, ודאבון נפש, you will always have to mourn for a painful loss. The position which the nations amongst whom your God will send you, will place you, will be an adverse one, so that you will have everything to fear for the future, can have no pleasure in the present, and have only painful memories of the past. This position amongst the nations—of which the two following verses only give a more precise and tangible picture—is part of the final purpose of God in banishing you amongst the nation which comes to be given in Ch. 30,1 et. seq. It throws you always back on yourself and finally makes you seek security and salvation in your undeprivable calling and your equally undeprivable spiritual and moral possessions.

V. 66. תלאים from תלא, having the same meaning as תלה, swaying, hanging, thus also ועמי תלואים למשובתי (Hosea 11,7): “My people are wavering whether to return to Me” (hovering between Baal and God I.L.). Your life will always be unsettled, you will have no firm sure basis for your existence and maintenance, and מנגד, it will always be something not attained but to be attained, still afar off. You will always have to fear for your maintenance, yea, for your very life. Hence ופחדת וגו׳.

V. 67. בבקר תאמר וגו׳. Taken in conjunction with the explanatory מפחד וגו׳ וממראה וגו׳ the sense could be: When morn comes thou wilt be so anxious about what the day may bring for thee that thou wilt wish it were already evening and the day lived through. And when the evening has arrived thou wilt see such terrible things round about thee that thou wilt wish thou hadst the past still back with thee and wish it were still the morning. Or: You will be so filled with anxiety as to what will happen and so terrified about what has happened that at all times you will only long for the present to pass, and at the morning you will long for the evening and at the evening for the morning. According to other opinions the מי יתן always refers to the time just passed. The troubles will always get worse and worse so that you would always wish for the time that had just passed, bad though that was.

V. 68. והשיבך וגו׳ בדרך וגו׳ לא תוסיף וגו׳. See on Ch. 17,16. There we already pointed out that the word באניות (in ships I.L.) precludes the possibility of בדרך meaning the actual way as before they had neither gone to or from Egypt in ships. But, we believe בדרך to have the meaning of “the manner”, namely to seek assistance as had repeatedly occurred in the history of the nation’s wandering to Egypt. (cf. the expression בדרך מצרים in Is. 10,24,26). So that what it says here is:- God will make you sink so low and your position amongst the nations will become so unbearable that even your ancient condition of slavery in Egypt will seem preferable to you and some of you will flee thither in ships to offer yourselves as slaves again to your old enemies who will refuse to accept you. The באניות seems to indicate that this futile attempt will be made not from the land of Israel or Babylon, altogether not from Asia but from the great dispersion all over the rest of the world.

Mit diesem letzten, die tiefste Erniedrigung dokumentierenden Zuge schließt das Bild der sich an den nationalen Abfall von Gott und seinem Gesetze knüpfenden Leiden. Hier unterbricht Mosche seine Verkündigungsrede, um – bevor er sie Kap. 29, 21 bis 30, 10 fortsetzt und endet und in dem Nachwort (daselbst Verse 11-20) die daraus zu ziehenden Konsequenzen ans Herz redet – erst einige Tatsachen und Erläuterungen zu geben, durch welche die bisher ausgesprochenen Verkündigungen einer heil- oder leidvollen Zukunft in das rechte Licht gesetzt und als Basis eines erneut mit Gott und seinem Gesetze zu schließenden Bundes gewürdigt werden sollen.

V. 69. אלה, the pronouncements of blessings and the reverse, contained in the whole of this chapter, Moses had been commissioned by God to declare as a דברי ברית, as containing a renewal and continuance—made here בארץ מואב in full view of the Promised Land, and just before the imminent taking possession of it—of the covenant already made in Horeb at the place of the Lawgiving and after that had been given and accepted. Between them lay the whole time of the wandering in the wilderness and the beginning of the conquest of the land. By these two factors, the forty-year long wandering and the victories over Sichon and Og, the direct experience of God’s Ruling and His Presence in the affairs of men and nations, and especially in those of Israel, which had begun in the Redemption from Egypt, was completed. They had themselves personally experienced how God not only intervened with His mastery of the powers of nature and man, in great decisive moments in history for the salvation of the most helpless downtrodden ones, as in Egypt, but also how he could show His special providing care for maintenance in a miraculous manner in most forsaken conditions, and equally so, grant victory and defeat in quite normal relationships between nation and nation. These experiences were to be utilized before the entry into the Land to renew and fortify the covenant which had already been established for the Torah. And this was all the more called for as the covenant made at Horeb on the basis of the experiences of the Redemption from Egypt had proved insufficiently strong to keep the redeemed generation worthy to receive the Land. And now a fresh generation stood ready to take the Land into possession, a generation the greater part of whom only knew of that Redemption and conclusion of that covenant through the mouths of fathers who had already departed this world, and themselves had only experienced God in His leading them through the wilderness and His granting them the victories over Sichon and Og.

So that before Moses had to finish the declaration of the future which he had been commissioned to make by informing them (Ch. 29,21 until XXX,10) of what lay before them in the future as the result of Israel’s long periods of suffering, he made a break after describing the contingencies of blessing and the reverse, and
V. 1. ויקרא וגו׳ first called all Israel together to take to heart the following: -

אתם ראיתם. Amongst the generation which entered the Land there were still a great number of people who had themselves lived through the Redemption from Egypt. Apart from the whole tribe of Levi, and the women to whom the decree of dying in the wilderness did not apply, there were still amongst the rest of the male population all those between forty and sixty years of age who had themselves come out of Egypt. So that there were still large numbers of eye-witnesses present in the geneartion which stood before Moses and he was quite justified in saying: אתם ראיתם etc.

לפרעה ולכל עבדיו ולכל ארצו, also in the report of the punishments which were given to the Egyptians in Exodus the “servitors of Pharoah”, the court officials, in addition to the King and the people, are specially mentioned. For it is they who usually exert the greatest influence with their advice on the king and his decisions, and so have to bear the greatest responsibility after the king himself for the right or wrong which occurs in a state.

V. 2. המסות. Deeds of God which proved the Power and Might of God to you; אותות in which God showed His Ruling to you; מופתים divine dispensations which are felt on body and in possessions by which you are taught to know God, how He would lead men and nations who deny Him by disobedience to better recognition and submission (see Ex. on IV, 21).

V. 3. ולא נתן וגו׳. (see on Ch. 28,65). All these experiences which God prepared for you at your coming into existence as a nation should have sufficed to plant into your “hearts” for all time the knowledge of the truth about God, of His Power, of His Nature and His Rule, His Justice not looking on indifferently to the punishment-deserving crimes of men and nations. So that, on the basis of this knowledge your “eyes” would look on the world and its happenings quite differently, and your “ears” would open readily and willingly exclusively to the teachings of truth and duty, and thereby have qualified you to start the realisation of your calling of the People of God in the Land of God. But these experiences which they had had at the exodus from Egypt had proved insufficient. With all that God let you experience there He had still not yet given you, לב לדעת ועינים לראות ואזנים לשמע, you still had to have all that you lived to see from then till this very day עד היום הזה.

V. 4. & 5. ואולך אתכם, it still required to have the forty years of miraculous maintenance in the wilderness added למען תדעו כי אני ה׳ אלקיכם. As Moses is the speaker the אני cannot refer to the speaker but אני ה׳ is together the subject of אלקיכם (that אני ה׳ is your God I.L.). Right from the very first declaration to Moses answering all doubting questions, (Ex. 6,2) throughout the whole history of the redemption, the purpose of the knowledge which the revealing miracles of God were to achieve is given as וידעתם כי אני ה׳ ,בזאת תדע כי אני ה׳ ,וידעו מצרים כי אני ה׳, and אני ה׳ then remained as the signature with which God sealed His Laws. That He is the absolutely One and only One, bearing His Personality in Himself, Who can really and truly say אני אני הוא, the one actual and true “I am”, and that His absolutely untrammelled free Will controls every future minute of every existence in heaven and earth—as the momentous content of His four-lettered Name ה׳ indicates—that is the Truth, the knowledge of which is given by the intervention of His Might and His Will in Egypt, for Israel and for mankind. It is on this basis of אני ה׳ that God established the inviolability and the momentous serious results of His Torah. But it required the whole of the wandering through the wilderness with all its trials and proofs and rich experiences of God and His means of providing to firmly establish for ever in Israel that אני ה׳, that this Unique Being so high and yet so near, having the whole universe obedient to His Will, is אלקינו our God. Who, every minute watches over, and guides and examines and judges and demands and checks our nation as such and every individual in it, with all our national and individual fate, with all that we do and refrain from doing nationally and individually; to Whom we have to give ourselves up as belonging to Him, with all our existence and all our desires for all future time. “I led you forty years through the wilderness”, למען תדעו, that you should know that He Who proved to you in Egypt as אני ה׳ and Who sealed His Torah to you as אני ה׳, is אלקיכם, so that you start your future as a nation in the Land with this complete “knowledge of God”. — שלמתיכם, plural, נעלך, singular: that shoes are worn through, especially sandals, altogether the soles, is felt and noticed only by the wearer whereas clothes wearing out is something that strikes the eye of everybody. Compare לא תקיפו פאת ראשכם ולא תשחית את פאת זקניך (Levit. 19,27 at end).

V. 6. & 7. ותבאו וגו׳. And you have also already come out of the abnormal helpless life in the wilderness and have come over into the beginning of a normal national existence having and existing on a land of its own, and have experienced the help of this “God Who is yours” in the victories over the mighty kings Sichon and Og, and in gaining possession of their lands.

V. 8. ושמרתם וגו׳. Well then! take all these experiences together, which you had in Egypt and in the wilderness, and which must have firmly and unshakably established your “knowledge” of God, of His having the fate of men and nations in His Hand, and of His Almighty Power of making His promises come true, consider all this and then fully appreciate דברי הברית הזאת, this alternative of prosperous thriving condition or ruin entirely and solely dependent on your behaviour which I have announced as being established by God with the absolute certainty of a ברית (see Gen. 6,18). After all that you yourselves have experienced you know that no word of this ברית will remain unfulfilled — then

ושמרתם, then you will not let the words of this ברית slip your memory, and will use them for guidance in all that you do, so that תשכילו את כל אשר תעשון. There is, it seems to us, absolutely no occasion to take תשכיל wherever it occurs, to have the meaning “to prosper”. The natural meaning of the mind acting with understanding and discernment is applicable everywhere. השכיל דרך always means, to conduct oneself reasonably, sensibly. Here too, what it says is: if you lose sight of the words of this ברית you will not only be acting wrongfully but also unreasonably, unwisely. After all that you have experienced you must indeed know that your weal or woe depends on your conscientious regard of them.

V. 9 & 10. אתם נצבים, Moses made a break in the announcement of the future of the nation, — as we remarked on Ch. 28,69 — for the purpose of bringing about a correct appreciation of the announcement of the blessings and curses which he had made, and to prevent any mistaken way of taking their meaning to be, by reminding them of the facts they had experienced, and by giving them certain explanations. The facts which were to be referred to are contained in verses 1-8, then the explanations follow in verses 9-20. Verses 9-14 avert any taking the duties of the covenant to be limited to certain conditions or generations or times. But rather, Moses explains, the covenant and the oath make the duty to the Torah incumbent on all Israel for all future generations. Verses 15-20 avert the misunderstanding that the proclamation of the blessings and curses had only the national defection in mind, so that an individual could assume freedom for his own evasion of the Torah as long as the nation as such kept publicly faithful to God and His Torah. This pernicious error could all the more be likely to be made as in Ch. XXVII, in view of the impending dispersal of the people to settle individually in their homes in the country, it was just the feeling of permanently belonging all together, and the duty of the solidarity of all for the upkeeping of the Torah which was expressed and stressed, so much so that an individual, however pious himself, could never consider his task fulfilled, if he had not done his very utmost for the upkeep and observance of the Torah in the whole sphere of his community. Hence also Ch. XXVIII, by the ברכות and קללות, especially the latter, as we remarked there, the individual was brought to feel how bitterly he would have to participate in the general suffering if he were to look with indifference on the general defection and the general ruin threatened thereby. Then there was also the danger of the other erroneous conception of the other side of solidarity to be combatted, viz, that the individual could have done enough to ensure his own well-being if he had done his share of the work of keeping the communal duties of the Torah publicly kept in a seemly manner, but his own private life could be far away from being directed by the Torah. His participation in the general prosperity would be ensured, he could believe, even if his own individual life would not bear God’s investigating Eye. Verses 15-20 combatted this pernicious self-deception.

יצב .אתם נצבים (a strong form of ישב with the צ sound) does not designate like עמד just the standing position. It is standing firmly, energetically and purposefully. The תנחומא on our verse explains in a characteristic manner, the use of this term here instead of the usual עמד, which indeed is also used in V.14. In spite of all the unspeakable suffering depicted you are still נצבים, remaining upright and firm. They can all passover your head, you outlive them all. In Ch.XXXII,23, it says חצי אכלה בם (“Mine arrows will I expend on them” I.L.) הצי כלין והן אין כלין (I will use up all My arrows against them but they will not be used up I.L.) Yea, the very sufferings themselves are a means for your enduring because they ensure your betterment. הן מעמידות אתכם וכן הוא אומר למען ענתך לנסתך וגו׳ (Ch. 8,2). And also אתם נצבים: Ye are those that remain! I depart, Joshua too, to whom I hand you over, will also depart, and so also the leaders who will follow in generation after generation, they all depart, and the nature of the leaders changes—only you, the Nation is immortal, undying, remaining, in it the spirit to which God has entrusted the perpetuity of His work is inherited, and in service of that spirit every leader enters. The Nation is the מצבה, the eternal pillar of His Torah. דבר אחר מפני מה עשאן משה מצבה מפני שמשתמשין מדעת לדעת מדעת משה לדעת יהושע מדעת יהושע לדעת הזקנים. ואף יהושע עשאן מצבה שנאמר (יהושע כ״ד א׳) ויאסוף יהושע את כל שבטי ישראל שכמה ויקרא לזקני ישראל וגו׳ ויתיצבו לפני האלקים. ואף שמואל שמשתמשין מדעתו לדעת מלכים עשאן מצבה שנאמר (שמואל א׳ י״ב ז׳) ועתה .התיצבו ואשפטה אתכם לפני ד׳

ראשיכם שבטיכם, not ושבטיכם, not “and the tribes”, but the heads who really are the tribes, for above all it is not the heads but the tribes themselves on whom God reckons even after the heads have been appointed ראשיכם שבטיכם אעפ״י שמניתי לכם ראשים זקנים ושוטרים כלכם שוין לפני שנאמר (תנחומא) כל איש ישראל. Similarly טפכם נשיכם, not ונשיכם, your children who really are your wives. If God is to be able to reckon on your children He must be able to reckon on your wives; for the spiritual and moral future of your children rests on the faithful devotion of your wives to God.
מחטב עציך עד שאב מימיך. See Gen. on XIV,23. (on “from a thread to a shoelace I.L.).

טפכם נשיכם looks at the nation, like all the preceding אתם וגו׳, in all its members (hence the plural number I.L.) but the גר is attached to the nation as a whole, hence גרך (in the singular I.L.). Also חוטב עציך and שואב מימיך is taken in Yebamoth 79a, to refer to workers who belong to the national service, as in Josh. 9,21.

V. 11. לעברך ,בברית, you are all standing there in all your ranks, all together to enter unitedly the covenant with God. לעברך “to pass over”; if you want to enter the covenant with God you must leave the whole standpoint you have had hitherto, you must pass over everything else, must renounce everything else to enter quite exclusively into the relation to God. Hence not לבואך but לעברך. Having entered into the covenant with God you stand on quite a different mental point of view than before.
V. 12. למען הקים וגו׳ והוא יהיה וגו׳ are the two sides of the covenant. You are to be His People and He will be your God:

V. 13 & 14. ולא אתכם לבדכם וגו׳. Just as unlimited as the people are to whom the obligation to the covenant and the oath applies, so unlimited is the duration of the period to which the covenant of the Torah which is here made extends. It includes every single person belonging to Israel throughout the ages, and every erroneous idea of the obligation to the Torah being applicable only to some certain time, as well as the possibility of anybody being able to withdraw himself from that obligation is hereby quite definitely countered. “והעלה על רוחכם״, God makes Ezekiel reply to the elders of the nation who approach him with the suggestion that the altered conditions of the time surely necessitate some adjustment and alteration in the laws. והעלה על רוחכם היו לא תהיה אשר אתם אומרים נהיה כגוים כמשפחות הארצות לשרת עץ ואבן הי אני נאם ד׳ אלקים אם לא ביד חזקה ובחמה שפוכה אמלוך עליכם “the thought which arose in your minds that you say, now we can become like the other people and serve wood and stone, that thought will never become a reality. As sure as I live, says God, with a strong hand and with outstreched arm and with outpoured wrath do I remain your King” (Ezek. 20,32,33).

V. 15. כי אתם ידעתם וגו׳ introduces the reason why there was occasion for the preceding to have been said, expressly, that nobody then or in any future time could detach himself from the obligation of allegiance to God and His Torah. This reason follows in verses 17,18. The idols of the nations and the ways of life influenced by them are already not unknown to you. We lived in Egypt and we came more or less into contact with the nations living round about the wilderness, with Amon, Moab, Midyan, Edom, with the population of Arab, Cheshbon and Bashan, through whose territories, or at the borders of them we passed.

V. 16. שקוציהם ,ותראו וגו׳ and גלליהם, description of the heathen idols according to their detestableness to spiritually and morally pure human beings (see Levit. on Ch. 11,10, p. 276) and on XXIV,30 et seq.).

עץ ואבן כסף וזהב אשר עמהם. According to Avouda Zara 51b, the עמהם refers to the idols, similarly to לא תחמוד כסף וזהב עליהם (Ch. 7,25), and designates נוי, the costly ornamentation lavished on the idols, and according to the first way Rashi takes it there, עץ ואבן would also not refer to the material out of which the idols are made, as it usually does, but here refers also, like the silver and gold, to rich ornamentation which is added to glorify these idols. But according to the לשון אחר in Rashi there, it seems to us that עץ ואבן here too could describe the material out of which the idols are made, and כסף וזהב the ornamentation which is added to them. Then כסף וזהב אשר עמהם could be stressed to say: on the silver and gold dedicated to the wood and stone gods you have seen what high value the inhabitants place on their worthless and objectionable gods.

V. 17. פן יש בכם וגו׳; now, even to-day there could be an individual or a family or tribal circle amongst you whose mind already to-day turns away from God and inclines towards heathenism, or such a misleading thought might not yet have been definitely formed, but is to-day just a שרש, a root, just a beginning out of which only later on, perhaps only in the descendants, bitter fruit might grow. The meaning of ראש is doubtful. Whereas here, and also in Ch. 32,32, ענבי רוש and ופרח כראש משפט in Hosea 10,5, etc. it seems to designate a vegetable material, ראש פתנים אכזר in Ch. 32,33 points to some animal material. In any case it is something which has a highly injurious effect on the body.
