Ex. 33,19)—he proclaims. To Him, his and their Master, are they to ascribe Greatness, הבו גדל לאלקינו, in His Name does he expect co-operation in His Work.

The first three verses are the introduction to the שירה which begins with the following verse. In Berachoth 21b, the prescription of ברכת התורה לפניה of saying the Baracha before the reading of the Torah, is taught from this כי שם ה׳ אקרא הבו גדל לאלקינו. Just as here, before he began reading the Word of God of the שירה Moses declared its meaning as being a Word of God, as the proclamation of His Name, and thereby bound his hearers to listen to his words in that sense, and to manifest this by professing devotion to His Greatness, so, in truth is the whole Torah a “proclamation” of the Name of God, the revelation of God in this world, in the human race, in Israel, and in the way Israel has to form its life. And particularly who steps up to read or to have the Torah read out in the circle of his contemporaries is first to declare that it is תורתו, God’s Teaching that He has given us, and just as he himself in ברוך expresses the promise of allegiance to obedience to the Giver of this Torah, so does he summon the hearers to similar allegiance by ברכו את ה׳ המבורך with exactly the same meaning of הבו גדל לאלקינו. In the same way it is taught in Yoma 37a, from it that one has to reply to every utterance proclaiming the Name of God with the acknowledging words ברוך שם כבוד מלכותו לעולם ועד, or with the agreeing self-including word אמן (See Rashi there in Berachoth; cf. Deut. 8,10; Numb. on VI,27).

וכן איתא במכלתא פ׳ בא וז״ל: אין לי אלא אכילת מזון שטעון ברכה לפניו ולאחריו תורה מנין וכו׳ רבי חנינא וכוי אומר כי שם ד׳ אקרא זה המברך הבו גדל לאלהינו אלו העונין אחריו ומה הן עונין אחריו ברוך ד׳ המבורך לע״ו. והנה הרמב״ן בהשגותיו על הרמב״ם בס׳ המצות על מצות עשה לפי דעתו השיג עליו במצוה ט״ו על שלא חשב ברכת התורה לפניה שהיא דאוריתא על פי סוגיא הנ״ל ובעל מגלת אסתר לא מצא להליץ בעד הרמב״ם אם לא שחשב שמדרש הנ״ל בזה הפסוק הוא על דרך אסמכתא בלבד אמנם עליו להביא ראיה עכ״ל. ולענ״ד אפשר ראיה גדולה להרמב״ם דהא לכאורה הדבר ברור מתוך המכלתא ומתוך הסוגיא שמדרש הזה לא מיירי כי אם מקריאת התורה בצבור דהא רק בצבור יש עונין אחריו לדרוש בזה הבו גודל לאלהינו ורק בצבור יש ברכה לאחריה שרוצה ללמוד הש״ס מק״ו ע״ש והנה קריאת התורה בצבור גופה אינה אלא דרבנן—אם לא בפ׳ זכור והקהל—אחר זמן מצאתי אשר גם מעדני י״ט פ״ק דברכות סי׳ י״ג מוכיח דהסוגיא לא מיידי כי אם בצבור ומשום הכי הדרשא רק אסמכתא ע״ש.

V. 4. הצור וגו׳. With these words the real שירה begins. צור as the allegorical description of God occurs again repeatedly in this poem and appears as the characteristic conception of it. The first thought, one can say, the fundamental thought of the קריאת שם ה׳ (the proclamation of God’s Name I.L.) which begins here, is: צור (according to some opinions written here with a large צ). According to the way our sages take it in Sifri, two thoughts lie in the word התקיף :צור, the Strong One, and הצייר, the Former, the Creator. In fact, if the word צור, taken in the ordinary meaning of rock presents the natural picture of strength, firmness, unalterable and unconquerable and so expresses the strongest and most dependable mainstay and protection, then the meaning of the root צור used as a verb would already be two activities of the strength represented by the noun צור. As a verb צור mostly has the meaning of besieging, enclosing, strength shown in putting a strong barrier around, firmly fencing in. כי תצור אל עיר (Deut. 20,19), מצור, besieging and the implements for a siege (ibid. XIX,20), also in a protective sense ערי מצורות (Chron. II. 11,21) walled-in cities. But צור also means to form, to shape. ויצר אותו בחרט (Ex. 32,4; ,צורתו צורותו ,צורת הבית (Ezek. 43,11). For every forming, shaping is making the firm, permanent limitation of the material within the perimeter of the desired purpose. So that צור as a noun, apart from its meaning as a rock is used metaphorically as an expression of this dual conception of unalterable strength and the hardness which overcomes all other material. In Ps. 49,15, צור means the immortal part which is not subject to the decomposition which is innate in the human being וצורם לבלות שאול מזבול לו, “and their immortal being is ordained to outlast even the tomb that this should not be a resting place for it.” Ps. CXXXIX describes it as the hard sharpness of the sword אף תשיב צור חרבו. “Thou makest the hard sharpness of his sword rebound”. Applied to God צור is the allegorical expression for the unchangeable and the absolute power of overcoming everything. He is the absolute origin of all existence and of every manner of existence. What He has decided to exist finds in Him its eternal hold and support and every form that He intends it to take becomes realised with absolute certainty. Hence the sentence in Is. 26,4, בטחו בה׳ עדי עד כי ביה ה׳ צור עולמים. The two-lettered Name of God expresses, as we remarked on Ex. XV. 2, the Strength of God showing itself in the victorious overcoming of everything that is in opposition to Him. Were this the only way in which He rules the world, then everything on earth would immediately conform to the ideal of the Divine Will. Everything would then be the product of His irresistable Divine Power. But, with the granting of freedom of will to human beings He has relegated the fulfilment of His Purposes to be first accomplished in free-willed development in the future—but with no less certainty of their being accomplished as is expressed by the four-lettered Name. Hence, “trust in God (the four-lettered Name I.L.) until the end of Time; for in יה ה׳ (both Names I.L.) lies the eternal hold of both worlds”, the present world with all the imperfections and the future one when the ideal life as God means it to be, will be a reality. So that with reference to Israel, the designation of God as צור expresses the dual certainty. God desires that it shall exist, therefore it will never become lost. But God also desires that it shall exist in a certain way which He has revealed to it in His Torah. From those demands Israel can never withdraw itself. They are just as immutable as the existance and will of God Himself, and whatever changes of fate Israel may have to go through, they have all the purpose of bringing about the ultimate realisation of these purposes of God for Israel and through Israel. They are just the blows of the forming hammer of the irresistable forming Power of the Divine ruling of the world, כי ביה ה׳ צור עולמים (Cf. on Numb. 8,4). Hence the Name צור is the characteristic Name of God in this שירה, in it lies the key to these ways of God’s management of the world, this poem revealing them as they affect Israel.

תמים פעלו. The way our sages teach the concept צור to be taken, as given above, viz. also as a forming activity, is conformed by the addition of תמים פעלו by which just a special nature of His work is declared. פועל is not only the object, the product of a creative activity, the work, but also the creative activity itself, the working. Thus in Prov. 20,11; XXI,8; Job. 34,11 and Ruth 2,12. תמים, according to its basic meaning is essentially “finished”, “completed”, where nothing is lacking (see on Gen. 17,1). Here it is declared of the צור עולמים that, even if at any contemporaneous time, looked at as being still in the process of formation in relation to the finished goal to be reached, seems to be unfinished, incomplete and imperfect, nevertheless the formative work of God is a finished, highly perfect work in every stage of its creation. The workings of God are not like those of man, laboriously placing together incompleted and corrected and recorrected parts of the work to try to arrive at a satisfactory conclusion. At whatever moment one may seize hold of God’s ruling of the world, it is a completed work, perfectly in accordance with the requirements of the moment. Whereas Man’s doings progress through nothing but imperfections, slowly rectifying the mistakes made, God’s rule of the world advances in steps each one perfect and complete in itself.

כי כל דרכיו משפט, for all His ways, not only the last goal, are משפט: the exercise of justice, the realisation of that which in every moment is befitting to whatever is affected by His Ruling. דרכי ה׳ are essentially the ways, the manner, of His dealings with His creatures, especially with human beings (see Ex. 33,13). In Ps. 145,7 it says: צדיק ה׳ בכל דרכיו וחסיד בכל מעשיו. All God’s creatures are a product of the Divine Love, none, by themselves have any claim on what they are or for what they strive, for their whole existence is a free gift of the creative Love of God. And yet God treats them as if they did have some such claim on existence and wellbeing. The first gift of His creative love was just this claim (ויברך וגו׳ פרו ורבו ומלאו וגו׳ I.L.). —אל אמונה, He is a God in Whom one can have confidence, Who forsakes nobody, Who, just as צור, always remains the same in His immutability, and when He exercises justice not only does what is objectively just, but effects that which is the best for the particular individual who is punished by His justice. ואין עול, He never uses His Power on any creature merely for the sake of using it. However tiny even the sum of the whole world is to its Creator and Master, nevertheless His Might is never misused by Him against the tiniest creature.

אמונה see Gen. 15,6; עול, see Levit. 19,35. צדיק וישר הוא, this צור עולמים, in the absolute firmness of His Will, and the absolute firmness of His Being, is righteous and just in what He desires, and straightforward in His nature. Not only are His ends right ones, but the means, the ways to attain them are right and just. He exercises justice in the fair straightforward way, that is His Nature.
These general ways of the Rule of the “צור עולמים״ prove true also in His government of matters referring to Israel.

V. 5. שחת לו לא בניו מומם. The explanation of this verse offers considerable difficulty. These five words are usually divided into two or even three sentences, and שִׁחֵת taken more as a noun like והדִבֵּר אין בהם (Jer. V.13). Either: “Corruption is not His, His children, theirs is the fault”; or: “Corruption is it His? No! His children, theirs is the fault”. Against the first way of taking it would be the fact that, as far as we know, nowhere does the negation (לא I.L.) follow what is to be negated, it would have to say: שחת לא לו; and against the second would be the fact that while the cantillation as a rule does divide parts of a sentence, it does not divide sentences. Moreover, neither the cantillation nor the construction speaks for taking the words בניו מומם in the way both explanations do. Further, if we understand these versions correctly, שחת would then not be moral corruption but misfortune, the social and political deterioration which has overtaken them as a result of their faults. Then also מומם must be taken in that sense, as misfortunes. But מום is only a personal, usually indeed a bodily failing, which could very well be used in a moral sense, but hardly as a personal or national misfortune. Finally if we compare quite similar accentuations and constructions as: מרכבות פרעה וחילו ירה בים (Ex. 15,4); כי רחק ממני מנחם משיב נפשי (Lament 1,6) כאשר עוללת לי על כל פשעי (ibid 22), השיב אחור ימינו אויב (ibid. II,3); בדמי ימי אלכה בשערי שאול (Is. 38,10). Or also צוד צדוני כצפר איבי חנם, then we see cause to take שחת לו לא בניו מומם as being only one sentence, with מומם as the subject, and שחת לו as predicate and לא בניו adverbial phrase to the verb שחת .שחת, a verb from שחת in the sense of moral corruption like כי שחת עמך (Ex. 32,7). מומם: their characteristic failing which clings to them from old עם קשי ערף, which is transcribed in the following sentence as דור עקש ופתלתל. So the whole verse would read:- “Its old failing has corrupted it to be “no-children”, an obstinate and disobedient generation”. Passages like ומעקשים למישור (Is. 42,16) (“I will make crooked things straight I.L.) ואת כל הישרה יעקשו (Micha 3,9) (“they make all that is straight crooked I.L.) show us that עקש is the opposite of פתל .ישר we have already recognised as being a separation from others by a firm internal holding together (see on Gen. 30,8; Numb. 15,38, and XIX, 15). Transferred to traits of character עקש is the crookedness, dishonesty opposed to all that is straight, honest and fair, also the opposite of תם. Thus תם אני ויעקשני (Job. 9,20) (“If I say I am perfect, it shall also prove me perverse” I.L.), Cf. Ps. 18,27. פתלתול, disobedience that fights against any guidance of the law.

V. 6. הלה׳ וגו׳. The ה is written enlarged and as a word by itself. Accordingly as much as to say “Ask”. When we consider that, according to Ch. 31,19,20, the שירה is primarily intended to come to counteract the mistaken ideas in the minds of the people by bringing them a witness to the real truth, in such times when dire troubles have befallen them, brought about by their defection, but they, instead of blaming themselves accuse God of no longer showing His protective and rescuing Presence in their midst: then we have to take verses 4-6 together as follows: - To the people sighing under the sufferings which have befallen them, and complaining how their God had changed, the words of the שירה come with the attestation: - הצור, firm as a rock, unchangeable in His being and wishes, is your God, He is always the same, and His actions are always the same. Every moment of the fate He makes you suffer is perfect in itself founded on justice and equity, just as much as your former good fortune aiming only at the very best for mankind in general. It is not He that has changed, it is you that have changed. Your fortune has changed and no longer shows God’s miraculous rescuing power on you because you are no longer those, you have lost the character of those whose lives are the condition for the revelation of God’s Presence in your midst. שחת, your old fault of wrestling in disobedience against the absolute Will of your God has brought you to such a pitch of degeneration that you can no longer be recognised as His Children—as the People of God. Then ה, then there is only one question. Then, instead of accusing God, you should only put the question to yourselves, and this question should always hover in big letters before your eyes: לה׳ תגמלו זאת? Is this to be the whole fruit that matures out of all that God has done for you and to you? How can you imagine that God has done, and would go on doing such great unique deeds for you, for just you out of all the other nations, only at the end for you to sink into complete spiritual and moral degeneracy, no different from the rest of the nations of the world!

גמל. See on Gen. CH. 21,8.—נבל .עם נבל ולא חכם, see on Gen. 34,7, and Ex. 18,17. Taken in connection with the question הלה׳ תנמלו זאת the real meaning of נבל appears in full pithiness. Both refer in their original meaning to plant-life, נמל the complete ripeness of mature fruit, נבל, the withering, drying up of the plant, denying the production of fruit. All what God had done for and to Israel, the special guidance of their fate as well as the teachings and prescriptions of His Torah, was done for the one purpose, to strew the seeds of light and life in the minds and feelings of the people, that these seeds were to come up into fruit of knowledge and deeds in individual and national life. But the people is נבל, has become spiritually and morally withered, dried up. They have allowed the plantings of God, begun with so many institutions to become “withered”, before they could blossom, and there the nation stands—instead of developing a model national life,—as an עם נבל, as a spiritually and morally dried-up nation; and ולא חכם which in no wise is, as it imagines itself to be, and as it should be in the eyes of the world, an עם חכם ונבון (Ch. 4,6), “wise” clever, not, as חכם means (see Ex. p. 470) absorbing the Truths which had been given to it, out of which alone true knowledge, and right principles, and the right perspective for life result. Thus also in עם נבל לשעבר ולא חכם לעתיד לבוא :ספרי.

הלא הוא אביך קניך. If He calls you His own, and arranges all your existence and wishes, disposes of all your internal and external forces and means in His Torah, has He not a right to do so, and should not the imperturbable consciousness be ever in your mind that with all these demands and prohibitions He only wants what is best for you. Is it not your Father Who ordains all this for you, are you not historically as a nation quite specially begotten by Him! Your whole existence as a nation is exclusively His work. Without Him you would not be there. In the midst of nations forming themselves He alone laid the foundations from the very first most unlikely, most individual beginning and brought you up to be a nation. That which others are as human beings, you are at the same time as a nation: - God’s creation. So that He has an exclusive right to you, and this, your whole origin also guarantees that what He, your Father, demands from you, His own begotten child, is only for your own well-being.

הוא עשך ויכננך (Cf. כוננו חצם על יתר Ps. 11,2 and כחצים ביד גבור כן בני הנעורים, Ps. 127,3), if He wants to direct your whole life with His laws, to point out all the aims you are to strive for with all that you call your own, do not forget that הוא עשך ויכננך that the one who directs you to these aims is the one who had formed you before He appointed these aims for you, so that He had formed you just for these aims, so that they are quite specially and exclusively those that conform to your nature and correspond to your calling and destiny.

V. 7. זכור ימות עולם etc. The actual divisions of time, days, years, are called שנים ,ימים in the plural. The feminine plural שנות ,ימות designate, as a rule, times, periods in general. Now it says here: Remember the ancient times, and בינו, go into them, seek an insight into the connections between the successive generations, the generation of Adam, the generation of Enosh, that of the flood and that of the dispersion, follow the path of the development of the generations of Man, and then ,שאל אביך ויגדך, ask your father about your own history (which reaches back to its beginning in the דור הפלגה, the generation of the dispersion), ויגדך, he will make it vividly realistic to you (הגד from נגד I.L.), זקניך ויאמרו לך, your elders who are gifted with wisdom and insight, they will explain your history to you, will explain the connection between your origin and your mission to the world, with the sins and the phases of the education of the past generations.

V. 8. בהנחל עליון גוים וגו׳. When He, Who was still only honoured by the nations as “the highest” (see Gen. 14,19,20), when God let the nations take possession of the various countries in the world, בהפרידו בני אדם, and, by the diversity of these countries and the difference which the influence of this disparity brought about in the physique, mentality, speech, occupation, manners and character of the inhabitants, the original uniform generations of man—all, after all, the sons of the one Adam—became diversified into the different kinds of peoples, each one, as the product of its country, realising some special phase of the human character, (cf. Gen. 11,7; 8; 10; I.L.):

יצב גבלת עמים וגו׳, He prepared dominions for the children of Israel, still so few in number (מספר = countable, easily counted I.L.). He allowed a complex of territories to be taken into possession by various peoples who then went through the national process of mastering the land and being mastered by the land and the territories became גבלת עמים, the countries of those nationalities. But they were not to keep these lands which were destined already beforehand for a nation the very beginning of which still only existed in single members of one family. Thus Ps. CV. 11,12, לאמר לך אתן יצב וגו׳ למספר וגו׳ .את ארץ כנען חבל נחלתכם בהיותם מתי מספר כמעט וגרים בה,
Cf. ונצבת לקראתו (Ex. 7,15); ונצבת לי שם (ibid. XXXIV,2). אשר הצבת לבדגה (Gen. 21,29), הצב used for fixing territories: אתה הצבת כל גבולות ארץ (Ps. 74,17).

V. 9. כי חלק ה׳ עמו. God did not allow the children of Israel to grow into a nation in the land destined for them to live in and to develop and grow under the influence and conditions of that land. In contrast to all other nations, he let them become a nation without a land, and then to take possession of the land destined for them which had already been fully cultivated and built up by others—indeed as we had to remark on Levit. 25,34, p. 762 was to be kept to a certain extent stable in the conditions found of cultivation of the soil and town-building—because חלק ה׳ עמו, because this nation was to be and remain “the People of God”, as a nation, belonging to God, with its becoming a nation to be His due, His tenure. That which the soil of their land is to other nations, God is to Israel. If other nations have the roots of their whole national existence and being in their land, and out of it and in it—in conquering it, adapting themselves to it, altering it by cultivation and building, to be a home for their social life, and out of its climatic influence make the conditions for their physical, spiritual, moral and social development and culture,—and accordingly worship what they feel to be the powers which frame their national culture, and honour these powers as being what their national prosperity is dependent on: Israel is to bring its spiritual, moral and social culture, as formed by God, with it into the land, is not to subject itself and the life of its people to the land, but to subject the land to itself and the life of the people as fixed by God, and so, with its existence as a nation, its national life and the prosperity of its people proclaim God as the one real and true source and power of all national well-being, ולקחתי אתכם לי לעם (“and I take you to be a People unto Me”) was what God said at the benighted suffering cradle of the birth of Israel as a nation, and only then והבאתי אתכם אל הארץ (will I bring you unto the land etc. Ex. 6,7,8). At rock bottom other nations are חלק ארצם, Israel by its origin and destiny is חלק ה׳.

יעקב חבל נחלתו. That is why the root of this nation is not called Israel, but Jacob, a human family which as יעקב, landless and homeless, has to drain the whole cup of suffering which landless and homeless people,—and on that account, in the opinion of the nations, without rights anywhere,— have to swallow in the midst of nations proud of their landed possessions and sovereign power, who know nothing of the innate dignity of men as human beings with human rights. “Jacob”, “hanging on to the heel” in everything in which otherwise men seek their hold and their greatness; without land and without power, and therefore unskilled, untrained in the inventions, arts, sciences and dexterity which the minds of men acquire in the struggle with nature and fellow-man for building up individual and national life, and therein celebrate the greatness of Man, Jacob, יעקב חבל נחלתו, Jacob, on account of the poverty and lack of brilliance in his appearance, rejected by the symposium of the nations, nevertheless had the fate of becoming, so to say, God’s inheritance. All the other nations could make no use of God, and still less could they use His Torah. It was other gods whose favour they imagined made them great, and above all it was other aims and other motives in which they sought and made the regime of their lives. For a life built up on the dictates of God, of sanctifying morals, of truth, justice and love, which in every phase was to demonstrate God’s sole sovereignity on earth, for that, there was no place, where with the jubilating cry “we would make a name for ourselves” the building of the “Tower of Man’s historical fame and glory” was started. Only Jacob, who himself had nothing, who had been granted nothing from powers honoured as gods by the nations, who had received everything only from the Hands of God, only Jacob was the suitable instrument for God’s purposes for mankind on earth, only it as “Jacob” could receive the mission to become Israel: to proclaim in the midst of the world the Sovereignity of God and the allegiance to it by a dutiful faithful life.

חבל, a measuring rope, (used referring to a surveyor’s chain I.L.) and also the part measured out thereby. Expressions as חבלים נפלו לי בנעימים (Ps. 16,6) and still more משליך חבל בגורל (Micha 2,5) make one suppose that the measuring rope is also used in a division apportioned by lot, but it is not clear in which way.—נחלה is quite specially a possession that has come to somebody by being left by a previous owner. Forsaken and given up by all other powers that form nations, Israel fell to God’s “lot”.

V. 10. ימצאהו בארץ וגו׳. There where men had נחלות, God did not find His נחלה; with their own firm ground under their feet men had forgotten the Lord over their heads בארץ מדבר, in the treeless wilderness, where no verdant meadows and no towns stand out, where man is forsaken by all help from nature and fellow-man. —ובתהו: in the desolation, where, accosted by no appearance of the outer world man is thrown back to his inner self, is alone with his own inner self and his God. That inner self which to men and nations in their struggle for existence and good fortune is only of consequence in as far as it allows them to surround themselves with the external possessions of enjoyment and power, but which is still just that, and only that on which God wishes men to build up individual and national lives to permanent welfare and security.—

ילל ישימון; and where the opportunity is, to test the power of this inner self and its consciousness of God against all the terrors of the wild, there, בארץ מדבר ובתהו ילל ישימון God sought His חלק and His נחלה, from there to form עמו, His people.

יסובבנהו, He surrounded it with the protection which the forces of nature and Man denied it, יבוננהו, gave its awakened inner self understanding and insight of His Teachings, יצרנהו כאישון עינו watched over it as a man guards the apple of his eye. נצר means less protection against external wounds, than guarding against any spiritual deterioration and moral loss. Thus נוצר האדם (Job. 7,20), נוצר נפשך הוא ידע (Prov. 24,12) referring to men watching over their moral behaviour. נוצר תאנה (Prov. 27,18); נוצר פיו שומר נפשו (ibid. XIII,3) “He who watches over his mouth, protects himself from evil”; שומר נפשו נוצר דרכו (ibid. XVI,17), נצור לשונך מרע (Ps. 34,14). Referring to ברית ,עדות ,מצות, to keep the commandments of God always present in your mind, not to allow them to escape your memory. It is phonetically related to נזר, to keep back, to refrain from something. Here it appears, like נוצר האדם and נוצר תאנה in the sense of caring for and watching over the spiritual and moral development. Cf. אשקנה פן יפקד עליה לילה ויום אצרנה (Is. 27,3) (“I God will guard it, will water it every moment; lest anything happen to it, night and day will I guard it” I.L.) where the picture of such a watching care is drawn. The comparison כאישון עינו would refer then less to the manner of the looking after than to the value of the object “as a man is concerned about the health of his eyeball. אישון see Gen. 2,21.

V. 11. כנשר וגו׳. The picure is: Just as the eagle does not bear its young aloft sleeping or in a passive condition but rather first stirs the nest up and then spreads its wings not under but above its nestlings, so that, with keen courageous eyes they fly up to rest on the mother’s outspread wings awaiting them above, and with free, conscious, brave decision trust themselves to the upward flight into the heights—the eaglets must fly up out of the nest by themselves, set themselves on the wing—: so did God first awaken His people and get them used to have the courage to trust themselves with free-willed decision and full consciousness to His guidance. This conscious free-willed trust was the preliminary condition for the whole of the future further guidance and was to make them fit and suitable and worthy of it. Only a young eagle has the courage to leave the firm, warm secure nest and trust himself to the upward flight into the isolating heights where his parent hovers. And it does require courage, while everywhere men and nations only feel themselves secure in the comfortable life built up on human power and art, to sacrifice all the life of purely material human greatness and imagined security, and bring into it all that is spiritual and moral of the life men are meant to live; and it does require courage to deny this worshipping of nature and men, and to reach the lofty heights of mind and morals which Man can and should soar up to, turn from the geniuses of the world, and alone with one’s God give oneself over to the Almighty Wings of the One Unique God. And to obtain this courage, which can only be found in firm rock-like trust in the guidance of God, the whole wandering in the wilderness with all its experiences and teachings was given, to awaken, educate and train the People of God. For just as the uplifting power of the eagle alone bears the young with it up into the isolating heights so:

V. 12. ה׳ בדד ינחנו ואין עמו אל נכר, so does God also lead His People, בדד, separated from all others, up to the heights of its calling, and will not tolerate being connected with the powers which the other nations deify. בדד is not the same as לבדו, does not refer to God being alone but to the isolation, separating the nation from all other nations and what they consider their protecting powers. Cf. בדד ישב (Levit. 13,46); וישכון ישראל בטח בדד (Deut. 33,28) and other passages. The עמו could refer equally to God or the people.

V. 13. ירכיבהו על במותי ארץ. We have already remarked in Genesis, that במה does not mean the concept of heights in general, but of such a raised place which serves as a base or position for the elevation of what is upon it. So that במות ארץ is not synonymous with גבעות ארץ ,הרי ארץ (mounts, hills) but expresses the idea of such prominent eminencies of the land, to rise to which forms the aim which people strive for. Hence במות is used to designate all high position which have been striven for or attained: ועל במותי יעמידני or ידריכני (Ps. 18,34, Habak. 3,19); על במותימו תדרוך (Deut. 33,29). The stat. constr. plural form במתי points to a dual form of the plural, like ירכתי from ירכתים. The simple plural of במה is במות, also in the stat. constr. במות as in במות ארנון (Numb. XXI. 29), במות בעל (ibid. 41). In ירכתים the dual form designates two length which together make up the space at the back. במותי would accordingly be double heights, and in the way our במתי is written the sign of the simple plural is included. This dual form במתי only occurs as here in connection with mounting or occupying high places and moreover only in a metaphorical sense, והרכבתיך על במתי ארץ (Is. 58,14); ודורך על במתי ארץ (Amos 4,3, Micha 1,3); ודורך על במתי ים (Job. 9,8); אעלה על במתי עב (Is. 14,15): All these places have the thought of a position giving eminence, power, mastery. The dual form would accordingly express the double relationships of such a position. ים ,עב ,במתי ארץ referring to God; His eminent position over the world, sea and heaven giving Him in all cases the double mastery over the world of nature and the world of human beings. במתי ארץ referring to men; the double benefit to be obtained by a high position in the world, of material and of spiritual moral benefits. That here it cannot mean taking possession of a high-lying lofty territory could be deduced from comparing it with the quite similar verse in Is. 58,14, where the picture of the happiness and blessings to be won by a faithful dutiful Jewish life reach their zenith in the promise:- אז תתענג על ה׳ והרכבתיך על במתי ארץ (“Then wilt thou feel thyself full of bliss, and I will make thee mount the high places of the earth” etc. I.L.). It is worth noting that there, like here, that together with the dual form, the single form of the plural is also expressed by the way it is written. That may mean to say that on the one hand the material, and on the other the spiritual factors in the goal of human endeavours at rock bottom form something which is essentially one and the same, the one cannot be reached without the other. They are both to be struggled for as being equally worthy from the one standpoint of the feeling of duty, of Mitzva which is to be the basis of all human endeavour. Accordingly:-

After God had awakened His People in the wilderness and given them practice to trust themselves exclusively to the eagle wings of His guidance, ירכיבהו על במותי ארץ He made them mount the double heights of earthly aims, spiritual moral achievements together with all material well-being ויאכל תנובת שדה, everything that cultivated fields could yield they had for food and enjoyment. נוב ,תנובת (phonetically related to נוף, the horizontal movement of presenting, offering, hence נוף in rabbinic Hebrew, the branch) granting, tendering fruit. שדי, see Gen. on XVII,15.

וינקהו דבש מסלע, as well as ושמן מחלמיש צור, as it has already said ויאכל תנובות שדי cannot refer to the miraculous feeding in the wilderness. And anyway we only find there water being provided out of the rock. But it seems rather to wish to lay claim to the extraordinary fertility of the land being extraordinary, miraculous. Under the special blessing which God granted the land of His Torah for the People of the Torah, the fertility exceeded the ordinary natural nature of the soil, stony and gravelly sandy soil changed to orchard soil and bore dates and olives. See remarks on Gen. 26,1,2.

V. 14. חלב כרים .חמאת וגו׳ like חלב כליות חטה expression for the fattest and best. כרים, the etymology of כר is obscure. Perhaps כרים of sheep are what עתודים are of goats. עתודים. see Numb. 7,17. כליות חטה, the single grains of an ear of corn are compared in size to the lobes of the kidneys.
דם ענב .ודם ענב תשתה חמר is the new wine freshly obtained from the grapes, חמר is the strong wine already matured. חמר to ferment. יהמו יחמרו מימיו (Ps. 46,4). So also ויין חמר מלא מסך (Ps. 75,9).

V. 15. וישמן וגו׳. Here for the first time we meet the name Jeshurun. It designates Israel after the ideal of its moral calling, which in ישר, straight, never deviating in any way from the straight path, corresponds to this name. Cf. זבלון and זבל. Above it said that God wished Israel to ascend the summit of the dual heights of human aims, the highest material good fortune and the highest spiritual and moral perfection. For Israel is to show the world an illuminating example of how a life devoted entirely to spiritual moral duties by no means entails a renunciation of bright earthly happiness, on the contrary, how the highest degree of morality fits in very well with the highest amount of earthly happiness and all material wealth and earthly enjoyments can be turned into moral deeds and spiritual achievements. But when the destined Jeshurun-people get an abundance of all the good things on earth for the purpose of fulfilling this mission, when it has come out of the wilderness into the land of milk and honey, then it became fat and “kicked out”.

שמנת עבית כשית is an address in parenthesis made to the people present with Moses and to all future readers of the words of the שירה. It contains the quintessence of the whole of Jewish history. In suffering, the Jewish people have mostly proved themselves splendid. But it has seldom been able to stand good fortune. “As often as it has become fat, it has become corpulent and overgrown with fat”, literally: “covered”. כשית seems to be the Pual form, like כסו הרים צלה (Ps. 80,11) “Mountains are covered with its shade”, כסו פניו חרולים (Prov. 24,31) “its surface was covered with thorns”. True, the dagesh would then be missing in the ש but examples can be found for that, as יוקשים בני אדם (Eccl. 9,12); לב הותל הטהו (Is. 44,19). Or כשה is the intransitive form, to be covered as כסה is the active, to cover. The sense of the passage is:- the more strengthening, the fatter, the food which is given to the body is, the more should the surplus be used up in energy and work, the higher should the activity and achievements be. Then the person masters the abundance, and remains bodily and mentally healthy and fit, and by his greater achievements increases his moral worth. But if he neglects so to use it, then the surplus material stores itself up in his body, he becomes corpulent, obese, and instead of mastering the abundance, he, his real spiritual active self, becomes overcome by the fat, and sinks. That is the history of Israel. It did not use the abundance and surplus with which it was blessed to increased spiritual and moral achievements, not to the fuller carrying out of its mission. Its moral improvement did not keep pace with its material good fortune. It did not understand how to remain master of its riches and good fortune, did not know how to use them for purposes of mitzvas, it allowed itself to be overcome by riches and good fortune, and its better, spiritual moral self to be ruined by it.

נטש ,ויטש וגו׳ predominantly has the meaning of not bothering about something. When Israel became “fat”, it pushed everything which it itself was not, contemptuously away from it, did not bother any more about God, Who, after all had made it what it was; did not carry out the mission for which God had formed it, וינבל צור ישועתו, literally: considered the hold and creator of its well-being as “worn out”, used up. In the times of the Galuth and for such times He was good and useful, there, there was nothing else to hold on to, then it was good and useful to seek a hold up above. But in freedom and happiness, set firmly on its own feet, having faith in God, and having to keep loyal to Him, had become an old-fashioned, antiquidated point of view which one had to get over,—the “out-of-date belief” has done its part, the “out-of-date belief” can go—וינבל צור ישועתו.

V. 16. קנא .יקניאוהו בזרים in the Hiphil only occurs here, and in V. 21 and in a similar connection in Ezek. 8,3 and Ps. 78,58. קנא in the Piel, as already repeatedly remarked, means to assert a right which has been violated or feelings which have been hurt by words or deeds. In the Hiphil: to cause someone to feel that his rights have been violated. They turn the rights which God exclusively has over them to others who are completely strange to them, to whom they have nothing to thank for, who have done nothing for them, and can do nothing for them, to whom altogether their whole existence should never be in a relationship of allegiance or homage. And this defying and paying homage to other powers does not stop at mere theoretical errors, it has the most pernicious results, that בתועבת יכעיסהו, that their morality degenerates to the most abominable debauchery. For it had always been just this greater moral freedom from restriction which was not the result but quite specially the motive for the defection from God of the Jewish People, from God and His Laws so strict regarding morals, אמר רב יהודה אמר רב יודעין היו ישראל בע״ז שאין בה ממש ולא עבדו ע״ז אלא להתיר להם עריות בפרהסיא (“Rabbi Yehuda said in the name of Rav: Israel always knew quite well that there was really nothing solid in idolatry, but they only worshipped idols in order to have an excuse to join in the sexual orgies held publicly in honour of the gods” I.L.) Sanhedrin 63b.

V. 17. שדים .יזבחו לשדים וגו׳ only occurs in תנ״ך here, and, looking back at this same sin, in Ps. 106,37: ויזבחו את בניהם ואת בנותיהם לשדים. The root שד is שוד related to שוד .שדד only occurs once again but very significantly for the concept מקטב ישוד צהרים -:שד (Ps. 91,6). Whereas שדד means more a plundering by mechanical means, שוד refers to the baleful effect of some invisible force. שדים are invisible forces injurious to flourishing and prosperity, לא אלה, which even in the imagination of the erroneous conceptions of the nations are not invested with the power of gods; אלהים לא ידעום, for which also they had had no experiences which could cause them to deify them, חדשים מקרוב באו, born of ideas of the latest discovery and invention, לא שערום אבותיכם, of whom even your most ancient forefathers of the polytheistic pre-Abrahamitic times had no dread.—There is only one conviction, the conviction of the One God and His covenant with those that pay Him homage which keeps them upright and raises them above all other powers between heaven and earth and frees them from all fear and all degrading demoralising trembling before all real and imaginary forces which threaten their well-being and prosperity. Once he leaves the service of the One God, a man loses all hold and support, and free though he imagines himself, is beset with trembling before all the real things that might happen to him and all the superstitious fears born of erroneous ideas. Under the rays of Truth emanating from God he sees the whole world in the clear daylight of being illuminated by the Powers of wisdom and goodness in which everything is led, even over darkness and death, suffering and downfall to a higher state of existence and life, of strength and happiness, of immortality and eternity. A state in which Man, by his nearer relationship to God and his turning to a life dutifully devoted to following His directions, is able, even in his life here below, to wander, holding on to the Hand of his God, even through darkness and death in undisturbed calm felicity towards the Light.

But if Man closes his eyes to this Light and this Life, the world sinks from him into a night filled with real and imagined spectres and ghosts, in which his only guide is the Davy-lamp of his experiences, in which he has only to go through the fight with inimical demons for luck and existence, and every desire and enjoyment ends in disgust and disappointment, a life which he enters crying, to depart from it with wailing and renunciation, where Man is the unhappiest of all creatures because he is conscious of being unhappy, and because he bears in his heart an urgent demand for happiness and peace which—without a life devoted to duty—remains ever unsatisfied. From the blissful state of a godly world to the pessimism of a “demon”-haunted world has been the disconsolate road along which defection from God has always travelled, that is also the road which is pictured here of Israel’s defection: ויטש אלה עשהו וגו׳ יקנאהו בזרים וגו׳ יזבחו לשדים וגו׳.

ספרי) שלא עמדה שערת אבותיכם בפניהם :לא שערום) “before whom your forefathers’ hair did not stand on end”, before whom they had no dread. So also in Ezek. 27,35 ישערו עליך שער ;ומלכיהם שערו בשער (ibid XXXII,10). Similarly to תסמר שערת בשרי (Job. 4,15).

אבותיכם, nicht אבותיהם, vergl. Josua 24, 2. בעבר הנהר ישבו אבותיכם מעולם תרח אכי אברהם ואבי נחור ויעבדו אלהים אחרים. Sie fallen in eine noch tiefere Nacht der Verirrung zurück, als die eurer vorabrahamitischen Vorfahren gewesen und aus welcher ihr mit Abraham euch emporgehoben habet.

V. 18. צור ילדך וגו׳. This is again, like שמנת וגו׳ (V. 15). addressed to that generation then present, as well as to all the coming generations, a sentence containing the general experience of Israel’s history.

If תשי were derived from נשה (to forget I.L.) the ש would have a dagesh. As it is, it points to a root שיה, like יהי ,תחי. But שיה is the root of שי, an allegiance offering, לך יובילו מלכים שי (Ps. 68,30) (“Kings will yet bring Thee allegiance gifts” I.L.); יובל שי לה׳ צבאות (Is. 18,7), like גי from גיה. He had hardly brought you into the world before you bring your allegiance offering instead of to Him, to others. ותשכח אל מחוללך, have I not seen it, that you forgot God, even while He was in the process of begetting you, i.e. even before you had reached the goal of becoming an independent nation, e.g. in the wilderness, while you were on the way, and must have felt how He cared and provided for you! This צור ילדך תשי too, this fickleness, this readiness to disown the old Jewish relationship to God when one has hardly reached the better conditions prayed for, in order to pay tribute to some other power and obtain its favour, is no isolated fact in the history of Jewish development.

V. 19, 20. וירא ה׳ וגו׳. See Ch. 31,17, 18, 19. God saw this etc. and that is the reason why He said: אסתירה וגו׳, if you complain under the pressure of your sufferings that God’s help is no longer in your midst as it was heretofore, here you have the answer.

וינאץ, See Numb. 14,11. He felt Himself no longer bound by anything, could see nothing any more to be worthy of His remaining. (Cf. Jer. 33,23) ואת עמי ינאצון מהיות עוד גוי לפניהם, “and My People consider it no longer worth while in their opinion to continue to be a nation any more”.

ויאמר אסתירה וגו׳. They think they can do without Me, and My support, let them then experience where they will get without Me, אסתירה פני מהם, will no longer let My special care for them be apparent to them. כי דור תהפכות המה they are a generation full of changes, they change their feelings quickly, go quickly from one mood to its very opposite one. In trouble they seek Me and My Help and as soon as they have been helped, forget all about Me.

V. 21. הם קנאוני וגו׳. They have shown homage which by rights belongs only to Me to unreal things which are far off from even supposed godly powers, have acted against Me even with things whose nothingness—without aim or future—is quite obvious. I will let them be robbed of their rights by nations who even in their own circles have lost all respect for the rights on which the social existence of a nation depends. They oppress and rob each other amongst themselves, and logically, even more so the Jews.—בגוי נבל אכעיסם, will afflict them by nations who are in no ways better than they are, who are already effete and past their healthy national prime and delight in all kinds of excesses and horrible degeneration.
V. 22. כי אש קדחה באפי. For the destructive power which overtook them came as the result of My anger with them, it was that that gave it such deep and far-reaching destructive force.

V. 23. ספה .אספה וגו׳ to lay one next to the other, related to ספח (see Ch. 29,18). It is I from Whom the heaped-up troubles come, each one is an arrow from Me and אכלה בם, every kind of trouble will I send over them, but at the same time will give them the strength to live through them: ספרי) חצי כלו והם אינן כלים)!

V. 24, 25. מזי רעב וגו׳. Now the description of the various arrows of the heavenly decrees which Israel is doomed to endure, follows, through nature being against them (V. 24) and through the rage of enemies being directed against them (V. 25).—מזי from מזה (like מתי from מתה), related to מסה, to disintegrate, to grow thin, מצה to suck out, means the dwindling of the saps of the body through hunger.—רשף, the internal heat, thus of the passion of jealously: רשפיה רשפי אש (Song of Songs 8,6). Here, the heat of fever.—קטב, related to קטף, plucking ears of corn off (Ch. 23,26), a sudden death which unexpectedly snatches a person from life. זחל .זחלי עפר in rabbinic Hebrew, water flowing on the ground, מזחילה the gutter of a roof. Hence also, the trailing along the ground of snakes. Perhaps שעל, the sole of the foot is related to it; משעול כרמים, a narrow path only a foot wide, along which one can only pass step by step; ,שועל שחל, the fox slinking along the paths (see Numb. 22,24).

V. 26, 27. פאה .אמרתי אפאיתם the extreme end of a surface, the side or corner, related to פחה the root of פה, the mouth which in ולה ,פי חרב שני פיות (Judges 3,16) denotes the extreme edge, the sharpness of a sword.

אפאיהום is the Hifil of פאה with the suffix drawn apart, as much as אפאם, I relegate them to a corner. אגור from גור, (the root of מגורה a barn) to gather the cut grain in; or it comes from גור to be afraid, though this is generally construed with—לא תגור ממנו ,מ (Ch. 18,22).—For the connection between the various meanings of גור, see Gen. P. 240.

After they had endured all this suffering, to save them from further mishandling, I would have relegated them—something like the Ten Tribes—to some distant corner of the world, where, left entirely to themselves, they could mature towards serious reflection and ultimate return to Me, were I not afraid of still greater annoyance from enemies (or lest I gather in a harvest of annoyance from enemies).—כעס אויב like כעס בניו ובנותיו in V. 19.—פן ינברו צרימו, their enemies could misunderstand it, could “estrange” it from the truth, could take it to be something quite different from what it really is. Similarly in Job. 21,29 ואותתם לא תנכרו “do not misunderstand, misinterpret the truth of their signs”; וינכרו את המקום הזה (Jer. 19,4) they “estranged” this place, misunderstood its meaning”. So Israel must remain in the midst of a world which is inimical to them and their God, amongst people who are more sinful and degenerate than they are, and so certainly are exposed to their mishandling, if the very opposite of what was intended by the whole of Israel’s historic mission is to be avoided. Instead of being a world-historic finger pointing to God, to His Will and His Management of the World, Israel’s disappearance out of the memory of the world would be taken by the world only as a triumph of the pagan erroneous ideas over the Truths promulgated by Judaism. In the Judgement of God on the Jews they would see not the Judgement of God, but the triumph of their own human power. So Israel must endure and suffer for the teaching and education of the nations of the world—and remain.

V. 28. כי גוי אבד עצות המה, for the nations who are opposed to the Jews, all go in accordance with their own plans, in the darkness of their political wisdom to their own decline and fall and have not the insight to draw the right conclusions from the events and happenings of the world.

V.29. לו חכמו. Were they receptive to wisdom, they would direct their intelligence to God’s Judgment being exercised over Israel under their very eyes and through their agency, and from that deduce what their own fate would be.

V. 30. 31. איכה ,וגו׳. The complete lack of power and resistance against their enemies could have told them that it was not thanks to their own bravery or to any pre-eminence of the genius of their national powers of conquest that their victory was so extraordinarily easy, but was due to Israel being given up by God and handed over to their enemies. Abandoned by God Who hitherto had been their hold and strength and Whose support they had flung away by their folly. כי לא כצורנו צורם. For if Israel had not lost its Hold yea, if Israel’s Hold had not actually wished it to be subjugated by the nations, if He had not surrendered them for that purpose, if, in the battle between Israel and the nations it had really been a battle between the Rock of Israel and that of the nations, then it would not have been Israel, but the nations who would have been conquered. That their Rock to which they cling cannot be measured against the Rock of Israel, that the nations had already learnt from the whole of the past, about that they can be trusted to judge for themselves. פלילים, see on Gen. 48,11. One never finds פליל and the noun used as an expression to designate political power or force. It is always a judgement based on consideration and deduction.

V. 32. כי refers to the whole of the preceding verses, verses 29-31. For if they had taken Israel’s fate as the Judgement of God, if they had considered the judgement which this God of Israel had already meted out to other nations, instead of persecuting and mocking at Israel they would indeed have thought of their own end, what would happen to them when once God would call them for judgement. For the tree from which they pluck the joys of their life, the fields from which they harvest their food are offshoots from the plantings of Sodom and Gemorrah. (See Gen. 13,10), Sodom and Gemorrah which did not escape the Judgement of God. There is no thought of duty, only the same egoism and the same addictedness to sensuality which forms for them too, their guiding principle. Therefore nothing healthy grows on their tree, and the grapes of their enjoyments end up in bitterness.

V. 33. חמת וגו׳. Their pleasure degenerates into gloating over other people’s misfortunes, and cruelty. The whole is a picture of what is designated above as גוי נבל, as a nation degenerated morally and politically which God employs as a tool for His punishing judgment on Israel.—ראש, see Ch. 29,19.—אכזר. The meaning of אכזר is beyond all doubt. It occurs repeatedly meaning cruel, pitiless. The derivation is doubtful. Compared with אכזב (Jer. 15,18), the root would be כזר which does not occur anywhere else, and only could possibly perhaps be analogous to גזר to cut. One could almost be induced to take it as a composite אך זר, something which stands completely estranged, completely without love to others.

V. 34. כמס .הלא וגו׳ (related to קמץ, held gripped in the closed hand. Levit. 2,2) to hide. These punishments for the nations are the Judgments of God which await them, though unrecognised in the present, still are there hidden with God, sealed up above in His safe with the treasures which will bring about the future state of happiness and security on earth which is the purpose of His management of the world.

V. 35. איד .אידם .לי וגו׳ (a mist, see Gen. 2,6): the vapour which goes up from the earth to form clouds, which then discharge their moisture to the earth again. So does the fateful matter gather itself from the sins of men to the storm which breaks over their heads when their fate is decreed by heaven as mature, and איד, a mist, becomes the term for a misfortune which befalls people. הלא איד לעול (Job. 31,3). (Does not misfortune come to the wicked I.L.) גם אני באידכם אשחק (Prov. 1,26). וחש עתידות למו: the day of their יום אידם hastens towards them in all their future incidents. Every future incident is a step towards this end.

V. 36. דון .כי ידין ה׳ עמו means in general: to enforce the law in a given case, hence also quite specially: to take up the case of a person whose rights have been infringed (see on Gen. 30,6 and XLIX,16).—יתנחם, see on Gen. 6,6. The adverbial clause denoting cause, כי etc, belongs to the immediately preceding verses, and looks back at the description of the fate of sufferings which will befall Israel, which was broken off with V. 26. The nations are reminded to think of the day of judgment and retribution which will come to them too. Then, it says here, even if Israel on account of its sins, had to lose its national status and wander into exile and—for its own teaching and for that of the world—be scattered in their midst and delivered helpless to their caprice, it had still remained, however deeply it had fallen from its ideal calling ,as far as the nations were concerned, עמו ועבדיו, the People of God and subordinated to serve His Will and His Torah and His purposes. For it had never come to a complete break with God and His Torah and to completely deny Him and it. The כי לא תשכח מפי זרעו (Ch. 31,21) lying at the base of this שירה has proved as equally true as, and just in, the prophesied sufferings. So that even if, by the withdrawing of God’s protection, they were surrendered helpless to the excesses of the nations, that did not justify their having to endure all and every mishandling. This scattering of the powerless in the midst of the powerful was to have been at the same time a test for the latter to see how far humaneness and feelings for justice and the rights of man had gained prevalence in their hearts. For humaneness and justice does not manifest itself the treatment of powerful persons who, after all, have means of retaliation. But it is the amount of sympathy and respect for their rights which the weak find among the strong which is the measure of the moral worth of the strong. That is why ידין ה׳ עמו, God will “go to law” about the treatment which His People have found amongst the nations of the world, ועל עבדיו יתנחם and will show Hmiself in an altered frame of mind towards “His servitors”, כי יראה וגו׳, as soon as He sees that His People have given everything up, have nothing worth considering, no longer have anything at all out of which they could get any support or out of which a future could grow. With what is pictured in verses 23,24 and 25, the fate of sufferings to come over Israel will have reached its worst degree. With כי יראה כי אזלת יד etc. the declaration in V. 20 אראה מה אחריתם had been realised, and with dispersion having taken the place of אפאיהם (V. 26), a step had been made towards the beginning of rescuing and salvation. Cf. the sayings of our sages צדקה עשה הקב״ה עם ישראל שפזרן בין האומות (Pesachim 87b) and תנא דבי אליהו ששת אלפים שנה הוי עלמא שני אלפים תוהו שני אלפים תורה שני אלפים ימות המשיח ובעונותינו שרבו יצאו מהם מה שיצאו (Sanhedrin 98a). (In the chronological table compiled by Rashi of the שני אלפים תורה, the fact must be added that the drafting of the Mishna—that great act for the preservation of the Torah before the progressive dispersion of the Jewish nation into exile—took place about the year 3978 A.M., 150 years after the חורבן, accordingly fell into the last period of the שני אלפים תורה. About the year 3978 ,according to ר׳ שרירא גאון, in the life time of רב ,רבי went to Babylon and died there about the year 4003).

אזלת, a rare form for אזלה, similar to ונשכחת צור (Is. 23,15). עצור .אפם עצור ועזוב is that which a man takes trouble to keep, עזוב, that which is worthless to him, which he does not bother to keep. It describes the highest degree of powerlessness when that which one wants to keep is just as much lost, unable to be kept, as that which one oneself abandons.

V. 37, 38. ואמר וגו׳. When Israel, by the enmity of nature and human power has sunk so low that its complete loss of power of resistance and its helplessness is manifestly evident, God will at last have brought Israel to realise for ever the absolute futility of all the ways and means by which, turning away from God, the Creator and Protector of its happiness, it had sought to find good fortune and joy; to which it had sacrificed חלב זבחימו the best of its offerings of its wealth and יין נסיכם the libation of the wine of its joy. The subject of יאכלו and ישתו is אלהימו as the חלב and יין was not eaten or drunk by the bringer.

V. 39. ראו וגו׳. Now, after everything in which you placed your trust has proved useless and futile, and from nowhere does help or salvation beckon to you, now see that אני אני הוא, that I alone am I, I alone am the Absolute, dependent on nothing, eternally unaltering. I alone am the One Personality on Whom everything and everybody depends, and in opposition to Whom everything else is unsubstantial, from Whom accordingly everything was in the past and from Whom alone any future can be hoped for, Who now alone remains for you after everything else, when you had lost Him, has forsaken you. אני אמית ואחיה, in Me alone lives the eternal source of all existence and life, I kill and also bring back to life again מחצתי as it was I Who smote you ואני ארפא, so it is I alone Who heal you again, ואין מידי מציל you believed by paying homage to other protective powers that you should withdraw yourselves from My mastery and guidance, now you see that I would not allow you to lose yourselves away from Me, how, although by a long way round, over the paths of death and suffering, I led you back again to My exclusive mastery and guidance.

V. 40. כי אשא וגו׳. One certainly does find נשא יד repeatedly used, also referring to God, as an expression for an oath, in Ex. 6,8 and elsewhere. Also חי אני (not, as here חי אנכי) as the formula for such making an oath, e.g. Numb. 14,21,28. But one does not find נשא יד אל שמים used in that sense, and indeed it would seem quite unsuitable if used referring to God, just as, as will be evident further on, only חי אני also corresponds to an oath but חי אנכי לעולם appears as a completely independent sentence of a declaration. Finally if our phrase were of the nature of an oath, the following אם would be a negation, as always with oaths, such as: - חי אני אם אתם תכאו וגו׳ ואולם חי אני וגו׳ אם יראו וגו׳ (Numb. 14,23 and 30). So we believe it to be in the same sense as אשא אל גוים ידי וגו׳ (Is. 49,22) where it means admonishing to fulfil a demand. So here too:- “I enjoin the heavens to execute My will. חי אנכי וגו׳. We have already remarked on Gen. 7,4 and XXXII,3, the difference in the use of אני and אנכי, especially when spoken by God. Whereas אני means the personality who is speaking in contrast to the world in general and in its absolute independence from it—hence also in an oath אנכי—חי אני expresses the personality as being rather all-embracing, encompassing the whole world, in whom all can find support. Here, it says first, how, when Israel lies prostrated without help or hope, it will find out that after all, God alone remains the same, from Whom it had not escaped, but rather to Whom it will now return to obtain from Him, Who had cast them down and smote them, life and healing again. Then, says God, when Israel lies there quite lifeless, will I raise My Hand to the heavens and say: “I am the eternal living One”, I am the Almighty and eternal Life. I am the Almighty, let the heavens henceforth carry out My healing and rescuing Good-will towards My people just as they had been the executors of My Ill-will. Moreover I am the Eternal Life and eternally living not only in Myself and for Myself in contrast to everything mortal (I am not only אני I.L.) but חי אנכי לעולם, am life for everything mortal, let the dead partake of My eternal life, awaken the dead, awake Israel to fresh existence and fresh life.

V. 41, 42. אם שנתי וגו׳. When the nations have allowed it to come to the point that I sharpen My sword to execute justice, if they have not adopted a different course in time, if they decide to remain צרי ומשנאי, opposers and haters of My Rule and My Law of Morals, so that I have to exercise avenging retribution, were I to do to them as they have done to Israel and other defenceless people, then indeed My punishment would be bloody, savage and terrible. —מדם חלל ושביה (from the blood of the slain and captives I.L.) belongs to אשכיר חצי מדם (I would have to make My arrows drunk with blood I.L.), and מראש פרעות אויב to וחרבי תאכל בשר. They have not only slain חלל in the battle, but have massacred unarmed captives and have carried the cut-off heads triumphantly on their swords—therefore.

V. 43. הרנינו גוים עמו. Cf. ברכת אובד עלי תבוא ולב אלמנה ארנין in Job. 29,13 (“The blessing of him that was about to perish was given to me and I caused the widow’s heart to sing for joy” I.L.), therefore God proclaims, in scattering Israel among the nations: “Make the lot of My People a happy one, treat them not inhumanly and cruelly”. Three reasons are given for this warning. כי דם עבדיו יקם: Israel’s scattered sons are regarded as עבדיו as serving God, as such are they marked out in the midst of the nations, well, in this God there lives an Avenger of every drop of innocent blood of theirs that is shed; נקם ישב לצריו, every violation of the demands of human rights and humaneness God makes fall back on its perpetrators, who in denying these demands are denying His Rule, are opposing Him, are His צריו; and וכפר אדמתו עמו and His People are to bring atonement to His whole world of men, (to His אדמה; I.L. אדמה as Hirsch explains in Gen., is not the world looked on as a cosmic body, but, as the name already indicates, the stage for אדם Man I.L.) the treatment accorded to the Jews becomes the graduated scale by which the allegiance accorded on earth to God is measured, so that the commencement of the Kingdom of God on earth goes hand in hand with the ceasing of the nations of the world mishandling Jews.—Thus Isaiah concludes in Ch. 66,29: והביאו את כל אחיכם מכל הגוים מנחה לה׳ וגו׳ על הר קדשי ירושלים אמר ה׳ כאשר יביאו בני ישראל את המנחה בכלי טהור בית ה׳, “and they will bring all your brethren from all the nations as a gift of homage to God to the Mount of My Sanctuary Jerusalem, as the children of Israel bring the allegiance-offering in purified vessels to the House of God”.—

The warning given here to the nations, הרנינו גיום עמו, makes one think that it was anticipated—as has actually occurred—that this Book of God’s Teachings would become the common property of the nations of the world, through the hands of its scattered bearers. Thereby this warning would also come to their knowledge, as would altogether the understanding of the true conception of God and His Teachings, and the resulting principles of the equality and brotherhood of all men and the duties of respecting justice and the rights of Man, and an ever progressive carrying out of these principles brought into practice. An anticipation which at the same time would include the supposition that the Jewish people themselves, by the influence which the Book of Books which they brought out with themselves into the midst of the nations would exert on their own and the world’s enlightenment and civilization would pave the way for themselves to the gates of their own redemption.

גדולה שירה, it says in Sifri at the end of the explanation on the גדולה שירה שיש בה עכשיו ויש בה לשעבר ויש בה לעתיד לבא ויש בה לעולם הבא ,שירה how great is the שירה, in it you find the present, the past, the future and the future conformation of the world in the times to come.

As a “song” to accompany the Mussaf-offering on Sabbaths, the שידה was chanted in six parts, which were known by the catch-word הזיולך formed by the initial letters of each part:האזינו (V. 1) זכור (V. 7.) ירכיבהו (V. 13) וירא (V.19)—according to other opinions וישמו (V. 15) לולי (V. 27)—according to others לו (V. 29)—כי ידין (V. 36), (Rosh Hashona 31a) and there it is taught that these same divisions are to be observed when it is read on Sabbaths in our synagogues. (A direction which would be against the version of beginning the fourth part at V. 15, as that would then leave only two verses in part 3 which is against the rule). These divisions correspond to the natural grouping of the various lines of thought of the שירה. Verses 1-6 speak of God, the characteristics of His general and special relationships in His Management for the world and Israel. Verses 7-12 speak of Israel, its calling and the history of its coming into existence; Verses 13-18, its good fortune and its sins in such good fortune; Verses 19-26, its downfall as a result of these sins. Verses 36-43 redemption from that downfall and the prospect of the future for Israel and the world.

V. 44. ויבא וגו׳. As it has already said above (V. 30) וידבר משה וגו׳ את דברי השירה וגו׳ here it must wish to say further, that after Moses had first pronounced the שירה to the whole nation, he with Joshua assisting him, went to separate groups of the people, to make them understand the full meaning of what they had heard. So the Sifri takes it: באזני העם מלמד שהיה משקעם באזניהם “he ‘sunk’ it deeply into their ears”, made it really penetrate into their ears. הוא והושע בן נון not יהושע, at that moment in which, at the side of the departing leader, he first approached the people, entering the high position of his successor, he felt himself quite in the modesty of his youthful past when he was still Hoshea and not yet Joshua (Sifri).

V. 46. שים לב לדבר .שימו לבבכם וגו׳ designates an assiduous serious devoting the whole depth of one’s mind to grasp something. מלמד it says in the Sifri שצריך אדם שיהיו עיניו ולבו ואזניו מכוונים לדברי תורה וכן הוא אומר בן אדם ראה בעיניך ובאזניך שמע ושים לבך לכל אשר אני מראה אותך וגו׳ ושמת לבך למבוא הבית בכל מוצאי המקדש (יחזקאל כ״ד, ה׳) והרי דברים ק״ו ומה המקדש שנראה בעינים ונמדד ביד צריך אדם שיהיו עיניו ולבו ואזניו מכוונים דברי תורה שהם כהררים התלוים בשערה על אחת כמה וכמה. “In the expression שימו לבבכם לכל הדברים lies the teaching, that one must concentrate with all one’s eyes, heart and ears to grasping and understanding the words of the Torah. In similar terms Ezekiel was exhorted (in Ch. 44,5) when he was shown a sketch of the Temple of the future (“Son of Man, set thy heart, and see with thine eyes and listen with thine ears to all that I say unto thee concerning all the ordinances of the House of God and all its laws etc.” I.L.). Now if something that one can actually see, take exact measurements etc. still requires the concentrated attention of eye, mind and ear, how much more then for the words of the Torah whose weighty and meaningful sentences often hang on the most delicate and deepest understanding and the finest difference in an expression, like a mountain hanging on a single hair”. אשר אנכי מעיד בכם, which I testify and warn you. (see on Ch. 30,19).

V. 47. כי לא דבר רק הוא מלם. Just as the concept: to be full of something is expressed by מלא מ-, e.g. רוח מלא מאלה יבא לי, “a wind full of these” (Jer. 4,12), so, רק מ- seems to mean empty of, not to be filled with something, and כי לא דבר רק הוא מכם to mean: for it is not a word empty of you” without your being in it. Either: this testifying exhortation for you to understand and keep the Torah is not a speech which does not concern your whole existence and purposes, it contains your whole existence, (מכם, yourself I.L.). Or: In the whole Torah there is no word in which you, i.e. your whole existence and purposes is not included in it. No single word of the Torah is indifferent to you. In every one you can find important truths which have a bearing on your whole life. אין לך דבר ריקם בתורה שאם תדרשנו שאין בו מתן שכר בעולם הזה והקרן קיימת לו לעולם הבא (ספרי).
V. 48-52. See Numb. on XX, 12, 13; XXVII, 12-14.

V. 48. בעצם היום הזה. As already remarked on Gen. 17,23, עצם היום, according to the way our sages take it, always designates the “strength of the day” i.e. full daylight, and says that the procedure took place in broad daylight. The way to Moses’s death was quite in keeping with his whole life, belongs in the sphere of his whole free-willed life of duty. It was no passive submitting to physical necessity. It was a moral free-willed giving himself up to the Will of his God and His Ruling, as every act of fulfilling a Mitzva, a command of God. This was the more to be stressed the more painfully the moment his death deprived him of just what would have been the crowning act of the whole of his earthly activity. The more so as just then at the moment of crossing over to take possession of the Land and the real realisation of the Torah, the people might be in need of him. And the more so, as, according to Ch. 34,7 he was still in full possession of, and must have known that he had, the physical and mental strength to carry on his activities.

V. 49. אשר בארץ מואב אשר על פני ירחו. This double description of the place, expresses the two factors which characterised it. Moses was to die outside the Land, but in view of the Land which was the goal before his eyes during the whole of his leadership of the people.

V. 51. על אשר מעלתם בי וגו׳ על אשר לא קדשתם אותי. The event to which is referred is described in its double aspect, in its undutifulness towards God and its frustrating the purpose for which the order was given and both בתוך בני ישראל, not in your private life, but publicly in the exercise of the functions of your exalted position.
מעלתם בי, in that procedure you did not justify the trust I was entitled to place in the sanctity of your character and calling (see on Levit. V. 15). מי מריבת קדש מדבר צין See on Numb. 27,14.

V. 1. איש האלקים, the man of God, the man who stood in close relation to God, whom God had used as His servitor and messenger. In the Torah this characterisation of Moses only occurs here. If as we believe, this blessing of Moses was not said, as the rest of the Torah was, as the Word of God, but emanated primarily out of the depth of his own heart, then we can well understand, in that fact, this unique designation of Moses as איש האלקים at everything in the Torah hitherto Moses was the organ of God, and as such no such closer characterisation was necessary. But just because this blessing was not God’s declaration but Moses’, this description of the personality who spoke here tells us that nevertheless these words are to be accorded an incomparably higher value than if they contained merely the speech of an ordinary man. It was still משה איש האלקים who pronounced the blessing here, still the man whom God deemed worthy to be in such close relationship to Him, and even if this ברכה was perhaps not said בדרך נבואה (as a direct prophetic delivery I.L.) it was still in any case inspired by רוח הקודש (Divine inspiration I.L.). Cf. Ps. XC.

V. 2. מסיני בא .ויאמר וגו׳ not לסיני בא but מסיני.: from Sinai God entered Israel’s midst. (זרח ,הופיע ,בא .(מכילתא פ׳ יתרו or rather הופיע זרח ,בא are the progressive stages of one appearance of light. הופיע is the first stage out of darkness, a glimmer which heralds the coming light. יפע (related to יפח to exhale) corresponds to dawn, the break of day. זרח is the radiation, the divergence of rays of light (related to זרע, to sow or scatter seed), the red morning sky, the light is still far off but its rays penetrate already to us. With בא the light stands in its zenith. (קומי אודי כי בא אורך (Is. 60,1-3), the whole picture there says that when the Sun of God’s Light shines brightly over Israel, it is the dawn for the rest of the world). שעיר is Esau; פארן is Ishmael (Gen. 21,21). What it could want to say here would be:- the promise to Abraham could have been fulfilled on Ishmael and Esau, but when Paran developed from Ishmael and still more when Seir was later formed by Esau, their characteristics showed that the realisation of God’s promise would have to wait for a later generation until finally Israel by accepting the Torah offered an entry for the Glory of God on earth. The למו is also to be referred to הופיע. With the rejection of Ishmael, the day for Israel was heralded, with that of Esau, the day dawned for it, with מתן תורה on Sinai the Light of God entered its zenith for Israel. Similarly in הלך אצל בני עשו ואמר להם מקבלים אתם את התורה :ספרי etc. (refer to it).—ואתה מרבבות וגו׳. An examination into the various places where אתה occurs seems to show that this term is used not so much for coming to a place, but chiefly for coming to a person and especially to an expected, an awaited coming. רבבות קדש are the myriads of spirits, angels, standing in the service of God, to whose character the attribute of קדש—the unalterable readiness to do good acts in the service of God—belongs, whose nature has been denied the possibility of failing, who, as it says in Ezek. I.9, לא יסבו בלכתן, never turn aside from their path. For such beings also a Torah is not suitable which is designed to bring the regime of their lives to creatures who are a mixture of body and spirit, and are called on to obey God out of their own free-will, and are accordingly gifted with the ability to deviate from the straight path. Not שעיר, not פארן and also not רבבות קדש were suitable for this Torah.

אש דת .מימינו אשדת למו, these two words written as one word form one single idea. דת only occurs here as the designation of the idea of the Torah. It is also the cosmic conception of the Torah, what the Torah is in God’s universe. אש is the power which gives movement, alteration and life to all physical beings, the אש שחורה, as our sages call it in דברים רבה עקב, the dark invisible fire by which the eternal, God-given laws of nature work in all His creations. These laws which work unconsciously in everything created, independent of its will,—laws set and desired by the greatest mind and the highest will, by God, and working by the Almight of His Will—are to be kept by the one creature called on to exercise moral free-will, not in him, without his conscious willing, but are to come to him for free-willed acceptance in his mind and will—and that is the Torah. It is nothing but the Law of God spoken to Man which speaks out of every other creature. By keeping it Man only takes up consciously and of free-will the position which all other beings occupy unconsciously and without free-will. It is the “fire” become “law”. And מימינו, it is with His helping and supporting Right Hand of salvation with which He hands them the Torah (see Ex. XV.6).

דות die Wurzel von דת, kommt nur noch rabbinisch in der Bedeutung דות, einer nicht in der Erde gegrabenen, sondern oberirdisch gebauten Zisterne vor. Dieser Begriff einer oberirdisch, somit in der Ebene, im Bereich der Menschenhantierungen veranstalteten Sammlung des ihm vom Himmel gespendeten, für sein physisches Leben notwendigsten Elementes spricht sich, wie uns scheint, von selbst in zutreffendstem Maße zugleich als Bezeichnung der Sammlung der von Gott für die Fassung des Menschen gegebenen Weisungen für sein sittliches Leben aus. Übertragen finden wir dann später דת im Buche Esther auch als Bezeichnung einer von menschlicher Herrschaft erlassenen Weisung.

Lautverwandt ist דות mit דוד, der Bezeichnung einer zum väterlichen Beistand berufenen Verwandtschaft, dem Vaterbruder (siehe Wajikra 25, 49) und begegnen wir auch hier der parallelen Bedeutung דוד: Behälter. Vielleicht ist damit auch die Wurzel דדד in דד, die Mutterbrust, verwandt.

V. 3. חובב .אף חבב עמים (see Numb. X. 29) is the form of the present tense of חוב, to be bound to do something, to be owing, similar to נוצץ ,לוצץ from נוץ ,לוץ, and moveover in an active sense:- to oblige or bind a person to do something, to lead somebody to a duty. Or חובב is the infinitive form of the Piel, like כונן. “Also inasmuch as Thou wishest to lead the other nations to duty, Thou takest all Thy holy ones in Thy Hand”, i.e. all the holy ones of Israel are Your tools, your instruments thereto. Not only Israel itself, the whole of the rest of mankind get the benefit of those in Israel who sanctify their lives by faithfully fulfilling this Torah. Automatically they enlighten the whole world by being examples of the holy calling of Man. And even if it does say above that even שעיר and פארן those nations nearly related to Israel were not yet matured in civilization to accept the Torah, nevertheless the revelation of the Torah on Sinai took place in the interests of mankind in general. With Israel and through Israel the way is prepared for the future gathering of all men to recognise duty to God. והם, and they the other nations, תכו, the plural of תכה, a stronger form of דכה, to be crushed, to be bowed down, they will be brought to recognise their powerlessness לרגלך by Your steps, by the way Your Rule of the world (like לרגלי in Gen. 30,30), ישא, but it, Israel bears the words which reveal You. By the events which God brings about in the history of the world, by the “Ways of God” (רגלך I.L.), the nations are led to recognise their powerlessness. But first by the Word of God (מדברתיך I.L.) which Israel bears through the ages, do they learn to recognise the Superior Power which they divine in the ways of history, before which they have to bow down and to Whom they have to pay their homage. Only through the Torah, the bearer of which Israel became at Sinai, do the Teachings which history is meant to impart to the nations attain their purpose. מדברתיך like וישמע את הקול מדבר אליו, is expressing itself (Numb. 7,89).

V. 4. תורה צוה וגו׳. “The Teaching which Moses commanded us” so runs the national creed which is to be the heritage of Israel from generation to generation.
