It is this Torah which is מורשה, the real inherited estate, not the Land and what that offers, the Teaching is the national Jewish heritage, land and power are only the conditional consequences of this treasure. קהלת יעקב is vocative. יעקב and קהלה are significant in their being used here. יעקב is the name of Israel according to its material diminutiveness and added to that, קהלה, not קהל. Only there, this single instance, is the Jewish community called קהלה, everywhere else in its independence always referred to as קהלה .קהל ישראל is the weaker, more dependent concept of קהל, either the community in weak circumstances or each branch congregation of the great communal nation. Not to individuals, to the Jewish community as a whole has God entrusted His Torah as a heritage, for only the community lives for ever, and only the community has means for everything, אין צבור מת ואין צבור עני. And not only for times when Israel was flourishing, and not only to the Jewish community as a whole was the Torah handed over. As יעקב too it is to be carried on and kept, and the smallest branch community, every little “Kehilla” has to make itself responsible for inheriting and realising the Torah in its circle, however small that may be.

V. 5. ויהי בישרון מלך. The Torah, the Law became King in Jeshurun. It alone is the ruling ,directing and deciding power in Israel, the actual king stood under it and was only to be its first model subject. Through the reign of the Torah, Israel was to be Jeshurun, correspond to the ideal of its moral calling, hence בישרון. Although it refers to the Torah ויהי is written in the masculine gender of מלך, and in any case when היה is used in narrative form is usually takes its masculine form e.g. ויהי ברכת ה׳ (Gen. 39,5), כי יהיה נערה בתולה (Deut. 22,23) et. alia.

בהתאסף. In the assembly of the heads of the nation to the תורה the tribes of Israel find their union therein. The Torah forms the one real uniting bond of all the Jewish tribes. Inasmuch as the whole leadership of the nation attaches itself, and is subordinate to the Torah, the attachment of the people to the Torah becomes at the same time the uniting bond between them too, and in this participation of everybody in the highest national possession, everybody receives his completely equal position in the nation.

V. 6. יחי ראובן וגו׳. According to the sectional division this verse belongs to the preceding verses, in which they come to their conclusion. Reuben is—with the exception of Simeon who is not mentioned at all—the only tribe of whom no material or spiritual or moral speciality is mentioned, whereas all the other tribes are characterised by the nature of their territory, power, position or social or spiritual activity and efficiency. So that it seems that after Jacob’s last dispositions, Reuben had lost the leadership which otherwise would have accrued to him as the firstborn, his tribe did not distinguish itself by any material or spiritual speciality. But it had just been saying that there was one possession, and that indeed the very highest, the Torah, which was the one real and true treasure of the nation, and in that all had equal part and in which all the tribes were accorded equal valuation and appreciation. On that rested the fact that also a tribe not remarkable in any way for some material or spiritual speciality, a “Reuben” also would find in it, in faithful keeping and guarding it, a development of its life which was fully appreciated and valued, would not have to fall out of the nation, and that its מתיו, its worthless, ignoble members at all times would be “countable”, just few in number. מתיו. See Gen. on Ch. V.21. p. 123.

V. 7. וזאת ליהודה. The tribe to whom the high position, power, and leadership, which Reuben was denied, passed over was: Judah (see Gen. 49,8). Now it says here וזאת ליהודה: “the same goes for Judah”, the same thing wherein the tribe that had lost the leadership, and was without power or brilliance in the nation, still can find the basis for a development of life indeed to be highly valued, that same thing remains at bottom the one real true basis for the tribe invested with the high position and power of leadership. As Reuben, so also Judah has the Torah as the sole source of life and foundation and also for the carrying out of the special wishes of blessing which Moses adds for him, when he visualises him acting in his official capacity. The spirit of the Torah will bring it about that power in Israel is not used for covering oneself with glory but for the protection and support and defence of the brother-tribes. Judah goes there where his people need him, and only uses the might which is granted to him to fight for his people. That is why he looks up to God before he sets out and that is why God stands by him in his battles.

V. 8. תמיך ואוריך .וללוי. See Ex. 28,43, p. 536 et. seq. Everywhere else אורים are mentioned first, here very significantly תמים, the representation of the highest, moral perfection precedes אורים the highest degree of mental, intellectual perfection of clarity. For here it is the tribe which is designated, the tribe who are to be considerd worthy enough to bear them. There it is not the intellect but moral character which, in the first place, is demanded. The life lived by the tribe must be in no way in contradiction to the moral character which enabled it to be the bearers of the אורים and תמים. Is not the tribe immediately described, not after its intellectual, but after its moral characteristics:

תמיך ואוריך לאיש חסידך, as איש חסידך to whom Thou gavest Thy Urim and Tummim. This is altogether one of the deep differences of Judaism, that in its sphere the highest degree of intellectual gifts and mental callings does not grant a permit for looseness of morals, but rather on the contrary insists that respecting and keeping the moral laws must be on an equally high level. We have already repeatedly had occasion to point this out.
לאיש הסידך וגו׳, here the whole tribe is looked on as one individual, and the whole tribe is given the benefit of the characteristics which were shown by its most prominent members, אשר נסיתו וגו׳.

חסידך, who had proved himself Thy חסיד. For חסיד designates the highest degree of selflessness in practical active life to which—as we have already remarked on Ch. 23,15—the extra strict precautions taken to keep far away from everything bad and low, which is generally taken to be already חסידות, is only a preliminary stage. הסיד is a character that has to prove itself, before everything else, in an active life for the community. Thus David could pray: - שמרה נפשי כי חסיד אני “May God protect him for he had never looked after his own rights and own interests”, he lived for others in complete self-forgetfulness (Cf. Berachoth 4a). This character is claimed here for the whole tribe of Levi: אשר נסיתו וגו׳ תריבהו וגו׳, what seriousness of the moral demands was innate in the tribe whose heads were to be entrusted with the Urim and Tummim, the Divine declaration of the highest degree of insight and of morality, that had been demonstrated as a shining example for all time in the history of the first members of that tribe.

במסה can scarcely refer to the place Massah and to what took place there. Neither the tribe, nor Moses, and especially Aaron who, as the first bearer of the Urim and Tummim is thought of here, had any special trial to withstand there. But here במסה seems rather to be a noun form of the verb נסה to try, to test. So the Sifri takes it: הרבה נסיתו ונמצא שלם בכל נסיונות “You tested him repeatedly and he passed them all perfectly”. The sense of our verse would be:- You found him perfect in so many tests and still You contended (תריבהו I.L.) with him concerning the waters of contention, (Numb. 20,12), would not overlook this one slip, and on account of this one offence, the hopes of a forty-year-long tested activity were shattered. The deaths of Moses and Aaron as a result of מי מריבה is a solemn warning to all the future heads of the Levites.

V. 9. האמר וגו׳. At their rising against the sinners at the golden calf the Levites allowed themselves to show no consideration for relatives, however near these may have been, and faithfully carried out the command הרגו איש את אחיו ואיש את רעהו ואיש את קרובו. (Let every man slay his brother and every man his friend, and every man his relative I.L. Ex. 32,27) and further in V. 29, כי איש בבנו ובאחיו (refer to it there). But as it says in V. 26 that the whole tribe of Levi without exception, כל בני לוי rose to save the Law, the relatives mentioned here could only refer, as the Sifri remarks there, to relatives on the maternal side who did not belong to the tribe of Levi. The order of recognising, seeing, knowing ,לא ידע ,לא הכיר לא ראיתיו, seems worth noting. Perhaps the choice, and application of these terms is due to the fine distinction that with parents just the sight would have been sufficient for them to hold back the hand raised to save the whole nation, with brothers, the “recognition” of who they were, with children, the full feeling of their belonging to them as lies in the concept ידע. But in their zeal to stand up for God, (in their response to Moses’s cry מי לה׳ אלי I.L.) they forgot all human ties and carried out His command to execute justice and save the nation.

כי שמרו גו׳. We have already remarked on Ch. 32,2 that אמירה does not mean so much the proclamation of a law, but rather a promise; and also there in V.10 that נצר means more the careful watching over and caring for some inner development than the watching over and protecting against external danger. In any case כי שמרו אמרתך cannot reasonably mean “they have protected Thy commandement” in the sense that they themselves had not transgressed it. For in that respect they were not alone, that, they shared with the majority of the people. Only three thousand of the people let themselves be seduced to actual worship of the golden calf. שמרו אמרתך can rather only have the meaning of the act which they carried out against the guilty ones. By this act of vengeance the אמרת ה׳ was preserved, without it the whole nation was doomed to perish, and thereby God’s Promise to Abraham, at least for that generation, and for a long time would still have been frustrated (see Gen. 32,10 and 14).

ובריתך ינצרו. As at that time, by putting aside all personal considerations, they proved themselves the saviours of God’s stipulations, so they were thenceforth to be the internal promoters of and guardians of the Covenant of God.

V. 10. יורו וגו׳, This calling of promoters and guardians of God’s Covenant they have to fulfil by promoting knowledge of the Torah by being teachers of the Torah, and promoting the keeping of the Torah by their service in the Sanctuary of the Torah. The totality of the Torah is here epitomised as משפטים and תורה, that of the institution of the Sanctuary as קטורה and משפטים .כליל in the wider sense comprise all God’s orders for the conduct of our lives, (cf. Ch. 7,12), תורה the Teachings to direct and ennoble our minds and feelings. קטורת in the Sanctuary is the symbolic expression of the complete sublimation of our thoughts and feelings to give satisfaction to God (see Ex. 30,1, p. 571); כליל the offering that was completely given over to be consumed on the Altar is the symbolic expression of giving over the whole of our actions, איברי עולה to the אשלת to the Fire of God’s Torah (see Levit. 1,9, p. 37). Clearly קטורה corresponds to the תורה and כליל to the משפטים. In the actual real building up of the nation, משפטים comes before תורות as נעשה does to נשמע. The indispensable foundation for all moral perfection of the nation and for the individual is the submission of all the uses of our inner and external abilities and means, the submission of the whole of our inner and outer activities to the משפטי ה׳ under the dictates of God’s laws. Without giving the משפטי ה׳ the obedience due to them, we remain, whatever the conditions of our fortunes may be, יעקב, only by the oath of allegiance כל הדברים אשר דבר ה׳ נעשה (Ex. 24,3) did we become ישראל. But as ישראל, on the basis of the accepted life of duty, the intellectual understanding and the ennoblement of feelings, the תורות are to complete our moral and spiritual education. So that what the משפטים demand of us shall be done with the light of understanding and the warm enthusiasm of our feelings and our love. Hence יורו משפטיך ליעקב and ותורתך לישראל. But in the moral ideal of human national and individual life as portrayed symbolically in the Sanctuary קטורה comes before כליל. In the ideal, the realisation of which the Sanctuary serves, the inner self is won over to the truth of understanding and the nobility of feelings, and out of that the complete devotion of all one’s activities to a life of duty before God, flows naturally.

V. 11. חילו .ברך וגו׳, see Ex. 18,21. Bless his spiritual and moral gifts. The spiritual and moral strength and vigour and efficiency which his calling as teacher and guardian of the Torah in the people demands. ופועל ידיו תרצה and to that which his hands accomplish in the Sanctuary grant that which is aimed at by it. ונרצה לו לכפר עליו (Levit. I.4) and elsewhere.

מתנים .מחץ, the thighs are the part of the body, the girding around which mark a man as equipped for independent action. For at the command of the tribe entrusted with fostering the care of the Torah and the Sanctuary there are only spiritual means. But the teaching and representation of God’s Torah cannot fail to find active open opponents, קמיו, as well as the ideal fostered in the Sanctuary, if not open, still secret enemies משנאיו (cf. Numb. 10,35). Hence the prayer: May God break the power of the קמים these that arise against His Torah and its teachers and representatives, so that משנאיו the haters of His ideals of morality do not dare to become קמים. May the teachers and cultivators of the Torah have only, seriously and undeterred, to carry on their teaching and their service, and leave their protection and support to God.—The מן in מן יקומון means to keep back, to hold something back from something. Thus Jeremia says (XVII,16) לא אצתי מרועה אחריך “I have not held back from fulfilling the mission to be a shepherd to the people in Thy sense”.

In Pesachim 72b and Kiddushin 66b, out of this sentence ברך ה׳ חילו ופעל ידיו תרצה the Halacha is taught that in the case of the ministering priests if it is found out that a hitherto unknown legal blot exists in the ancestry of one of their members which renders him a חלל (see on Levit. 21,7) and ineligible for service, nevertheless the עבודות which he had hitherto performed in good faith do not lose their validity היה עומד ומקריב ונודע שהוא בן גרושה או בן חלוצה כל הקרבנות כולן שהקריב ע״ג המזבח ר׳ יהושע מכשיר מ״ט דר׳ יהושע דכתיב ברך ה׳ חילו ופועל ידיו תרצה אפילו חללין שבו תרצה. It is possible that, taking it in this sense חילו could be taken in its ordinary meaning of חיל, host: May God bless His host (His army of priests I.L.) and accept, graciously sanctioning that which his hands has accomplished. Thereby the whole tribe of the priests are taken as one closed unit and every single ministering member of it as one of its delegates, so that one in good faith reckoning himself as belonging to it, and as such not only entitled to perform עבודה, but in duty bound to do so, is covered by the general character of the corporation, so that all the procedures performed by him retain their validity, even if it should be subsequently discovered that some fault in his descent results in his being excluded from the unit. (cf. the working of the ציץ, Ex. 28,38).

V. 12. לבנימין. To Judah, the bearer of the national power, and Levi—responsible for nurturing the teaching of the Torah and the Sanctuary, Benjamin is attached. It is in his territory that the Sanctuary, or rather the holiest part of it, was placed. (see Levit. on I. 5 pp. 24,25). There we worked out the significance of the fact that the Altar, the Holy of Holiest and the Helchal were not to be found in the domain of the powerful royal tribe but in that of the youngest and weakest of the tribes (and that most significant fact that where the base of the Altar extended over into the province of Judah, the S.E. corner, the base was left unfinished I.L.). The Sifri also directs our attention to the early history of the father of this tribe. Benjamin was the only one of Jacob’s sons who was born in the Holy Land, the only one who was not stained with the blot of unbrotherly behaviour towards Joseph, the one who was the prop and comfort of his father in his old age. Accordingly, the one whose remembrance, entirely free from the slightest breath of any opposing thought, corresponded to the virtues which the site of the Sanctuary was dedicated to foster.

חפף .חפף וגו׳, the root of חֻפָּה and of חף a haven, means a protective and enclosing surrounding. חֻפָּה in Ps. 19,6 and Joel 2,16 is the specific name for the symbolically enclosing room into which bride and bridegroom enter to consummate their bond of marriage. Transposed to the union of God and Israel, which so frequently occurs as a metaphor in the holy scriptures חֻפָּה is a very striking expression for the place of the Sanctuary in which the daily repeated procedures so pregnant with meaning serve to express the ever to be renewed union of Israel with God. From this point of view the term חופף עליו here could be meant to be taken. Thus in Zebachim 118b, בג׳ מקומות שרתה שכינה על ישראל בשילה ונוב וגבעון ובית עולמים ובכולן לא שרתה אלא בחלקו של בנימין שנאמר חופף עליו כל היום כל חפיפות .לא יהו אלא בחלקו של בנימין

ובין כתפיו שכן, as is explained in Zebachim 54b, not on the summit of the mount בעין עיטם where the source of the Etam lies, but somewhat lower, on the slope, corresponding to the expression “between its shoulders”, the relative height of the shoulders to the top of the head.

V. 13-16. וליוסף וגו׳. Power, service of the Torah and the Sanctuary, and the site of the Sanctuary were the distinguishing specialities which marked the tribes of Judah, Levi and Benjamin respectively. The richest abundance of the blessing of the soil follows as marking out the tribe of Joseph. מגד: the root of מגד could perhaps be גדה, like ממר from ,מרה וממר ליולדתו (Prov. 17,25). But גדה, related to גדע, is the root of גדי, fruit detached from the body of its origin, the young of animals (see Ex. 23,19). So that מגד could mean altogether every production of “fruit”. מגד שמים is the dew, תבואות שמש are the harvests brought about by the sun, the fruit which has ripened through the sun, which are dependent on the course of the sun, accordingly the fruit of the vegetable kingdom; מגד גרש ירחים, on the other hand, are the fruits which are connected with a number of months, which are furthered by a number of successive months, these would be the fruit of the animal world. ירחים. See on Ex. 2,2.

גרש. The separation of the “fruit of the body” from the mother-animal with which the young was so intimately connected until its maturity, from which, as soon as the young no longer require the mother, they become completely estranged (compare שגר).

ארץ ומלאה ,גבעות עולם ,הררי קדם. The eye of the Seer first visualises Joseph’s territory encircled with blessings. The heavens from above and the earth from beneath give the very first preliminary conditions for all the development of fruit, i.e. moisture. Within this sphere closed in with blessings, he lets his eye roam above to below, and sees the sun, the moon, the mountains, the hills, the soil, all granting all that they have to give of blessing. The mountains, wooded to their very summits, the hillocks with their slopes full of ripening fruit, the plains with their cultivated fields. But all this material abundance does still not spell “blessing”. All this only becomes truly blessing and happiness-bringing if the inhabitants show themselves worthy of the satisfaction of Him Who took His place for Moses on the thorn-bush, Whose Presence does not require all this rich abundance, Who reveals Himself even in a thornbush if the right man is there—so that therefore this rich abundance is only granted to the sons of Joesph in the assumption that they will remember their forefather who showed himself modest and humane in the midst of glory and riches, who, even in his youth did not let himself be entrapped by the snares of sensuality, who was נזיר אחיו, the most abstemious of his brethren (see Gen. 49,26). תבואתה, with the sign of the optative doubled, really two ה, of which the one, as usual, is changed to ת. As much as to say: “O that it may come”, really “come home to”, that in this blessing, born of God’s satisfaction with them, in this blessing of his descendants Joseph may reap the reward for his moral greatness! As this wish is made dependent on continued moral perfection, the realisation of which lies entirely in the free-willed development of the tribe, the use of the subjunctive in this double form of the optative is understandable in Moses’s mouth. The later history of the tribe of Ephraim shows only too sufficienly how much of this wish—remained a wish. The materially blessed Ephraim dragged ten-twelfths of the nation down with it in its fall.

בכור שורו. In the preceding verses Joseph’s real calling is described as peaceful greatness, the general picture of which is agriculture, for which שור, the ox, not the lion, as for Judah in Gen. 49,9, is the suitable emblem. But בכור שורו, the firstborn of this tribe belonging to a peaceful calling, i.e. the first of this tribe to come into prominence in Israel’s further future history receives a military mission invested with eminence, he will have unicorn’s horns with which to overpower nations, these will primarily be formed under his leadership by the tens of thousands and thousands of the tribes of Joseph. This clearly refers to Joshua who belonged to the tribe of Ephraim (Numb. 13,8) and who received the mission to drive out the inhabitants of the Land. אפסי ארץ seems to designate the distance into which he would drive the nations.

V. 18-19. ולזבולון וגו׳. Jacob already saw (Gen. XL. 43 and 64) Zebulun dealing in sea-faring matters at havens and Issachar pursuing spiritual matters quitely at home on land (refer to it there). Here they are placed together in one verse, as indeed their territories were adjoining. But their sharing a common blessing rests on a brotherly working together as neighbours, and the spiritual moral influence which between the two of them was exerted on the foreign nations who came into contact with them in the international traffic of the sea. Zebulun gets about and abroad in the traffic which his maritime trade involves, and supports and furthers his stay-at-home brother-tribe with his studies, and they again on their part give them the benefit of their spiritual achievements and “learning”. Issachar has his part in the spirit of honesty and fairness which Zebulun develops in his business affairs, and Zebulun in the comfortable wealthy surroundings in which Issachar can pursue his studies (Gen. 49,14 and 15). But between them they bring about the first acquaintance which the outside world makes with the Jewish spirit, Jewish life and the source of both, the Sanctuary of the Jewish Laws. They are the cause of strangers who, by coming into contact with them, learn to know and respect the Jewish spirit and the Jewish way of life. There they are impressed by what the procedures there preach, how a life of duty to God must be dedicated to honesty (see Sifri). And indeed it is זבחי צדק, principally זבחים, yea שלמים (offerings which are brought neither to propriate an angry god for sins committed nor to obtain his special favour, which hitherto had been their sole idea of sacrifices I.L.) the happy dedication of a life of duty, that specifically Jewish accomplishment (see Levit. on III,1, p. 74, 75).

שפע ימים וגו׳ is the state of affairs which brings about their contact with other nations. שפע related to שבע etc. designates a fullness, riches. They get the benefit of the business which their living at the seaside brings, or they become a market into which the most varied goods from all the seas pour in for barter. ושפני טמוני חול and they also have on their waterside special wares which can only be found there, and which people come specially there to obtain. As examples of such goods the Gemora in Megilla 6a, mentions טרית ,חלזון and זכוכית לבנה, the special purple dye, a special kind of tunny, and white glass or crystal to the manufacture of which the sand on that shore was quite specially adapted.
שפן, also ספן related to צפן means covered up, hidden, טמן, hidden, hence מטמון, a secret treasure. שפוני טמוני חול, which lie buried in the secret treasures of the sand.

V. 20. ברוך מרחיב גד .ולגד וגו׳. Here Moses expresses the comforting feeling, that due to the permission to settle Gad in Transjordan territory, he was granted the favour of having his last resting-place in the purlieus of his people. Without this permission he would have had to have the hard fate of knowing that his grave would lie in the lonesome desert, or in the midst of the land of a foreign people. Hence ברול מרחיב גד, “Blessed be God, that He granted the wish of Gad to settle in these broad lands”. Now כלביא שכן, Gad has already settled down like a lion to rest having already טרף זרוע אף קדקוד “overpowered arm and crown of the head”, i.e. the opposition of the people and their directing generals or leaders. Gad has not first to fight to conquer his possession, he has already successfully overpowered and beaten the previous inhabitants of the land and now rests like a conquering lion in his possession. In his land—and therefore around Moses’s grave—no battles will rage.

V. 21. וירא וגו׳ כי וגו׳. This כי cannot mean to be giving the reason for Gad having chosen the Transjordan territory. That Moses would find his grave in that part was not known when Gad made his choice, and quite other reasons directed it. We take the וירא ראשית לו to say: He saw a start, with himself obtaining this possession a beginning of the establishment of the future Jewish Land. With this choice he did not set himself outside the national union. Gad’s province was not to be a foreign country, not “abroad”. It was to belong to the Holy Land, to the Land of God’s Torah. (שביעית IX,2 Numb. 34,2). His province formed the ראשית, the beginning of a Jewish Land. כי שם וגו׳ for there also the Lawgiver, Moses had his grave and thereby also his portion of it. This place of the grave of the “giver of the Torah” is consonant with the significance of the ground as the “Land of the Torah”. By reason of its gender ספון can refer only to מחוקק, and according to the annotation also, is not an adjective but in apposition to מחוקק. Moses was ספון, put beyond the sight of his people. He died but his grave remained unknown, see Ch. 34,6.

ויתא ראשי עם. These are words which, so to speak, could hover, as an epitaph which Moses himself writes over the region of his unknown grave, to perpetuate his memory: - “He came to be the Leader of the People, and, as being sent by God, had to transmit all the beneficence as well as all the serious decrees which God had decided for Israel. ראשי עם (cf. Chron. I. 12,18). צדקת ה׳, see Gen. Ch. 15,6 V. p. 274,5).

V. 22. זנק .ולדן וגו׳ does not occur again in תנייך. In the Mishna (Chulin 37a) it designates to spurt far away. There it is speaking of a strong outflow of blood. In Sifri, the word is explained more in detail as meaning a ray which darts forth from a point and then divides into two parts. Thus Dan who received his allotment of land in the south-west up to Jaffa, but from there they went up to Leshem far up in the north-east, conquered it, took possession of it and gave it the name of their tribal father, Dan. ויצא גבול בני דן מהם ויעלו בני דן וילחמו עם לשם וילכדו אותה וישבו בה ויקראו ללשם דן כשם דן אביהם (Josh. 19,41-47). (Already in Abraham’s time there was a place called Dan in the north-east (Gen. 14,14). It is quite possible that this influenced the Danites to win a possession in that district to which they could give their own name, so that in future centuries people should not make the mistake of thinking that they had previously lived there, but had forfeited their inheritance). The picture גור אריה יזנק מן הבשן could then show Dan as a lion with his claws spread out in two different directions, springing forth capturing with its one spring two provinces lying far apart. Bashan is just a mountainous district in the north-east in the neighbourhood of Leshem which Dan conquered. Dan at the same time took possession of provinces in the south-west and north-east.

V. 23. ולנפתלי אמר וגו׳, Naphtali—just in contrast to Dan and probably on that account placed together with him, without any division of paragraph—is שבע רצון, is completely and fully satisfied with the province allotted to him. Thus the Sifri מלמד שהיה נפתלי שמח בחלקו. And in fact he could well be so. His territory—neighbouring directly on the north-eastern possessions of Dan—was indeed מלא ברכת ה׳. It contained the ים כנרת, which by itself was a source of riches with its exceptional abundance of fish, and its surroundings noted for its great richness of the choicest fruits, the renowned פירות גינוסר.

ירשה ,ים ודרום ירשה, most likely the infinitive with the paragogic ה (like העמק שאלה Is. VII) and indeed in aoristic meaning. His province lay in the north-east, but on account of the excellency of the fruit which could only be found in such quantity there, he reaped the advantage of the advantages of the south and west which he constantly attracted to his domain. It is not impossible that this peaceful “conquest” is placed in direct contrast to the armed victories of Naphtali referred to just before.

V. 24. ולאשר וגו׳. It is doubtful how the מ in מבנים is to be taken, whether as comparative, “more blessed than sons”, i.e. than the others, or rather than some of the children of Israel, or like מבורכת וגו׳ ממגד וגו׳ “blessed by or with children”, or finally like תבורך מנשים יעל וגו׳ (which most likely must mean blessed by women) in Judges 5,24, “blessed by his brother-tribes”. As it does not actually say אחים but בנים the middle way of taking it seems more in accordance with the wording, and thereby would pronounce a blessing on the tribe of Asher in richness of children, be it in numbers or in capabilities. In a similar way רצוי אחיו wavers between meaning his brethren being well disposed towards his and his childrens’ character that they like to come into contact with them, or that his brethren like to come into business contact with them on account of the excellency of his soil. In any case טובל בשמן רגלו proves the enormous fertility of his ground.

V. 25. ברזל וגו׳. All the previous blessings are spoken of in the third person. The following blessings until the end clearly refer to matters affecting the general common community of Israel and so are addressed to it in the second person. As now this speech starts already in this verse 25, the blessings of the individual tribes could end with V. 24 and a quick transition to the general blessing start with this V. 25. We saw above in V. 6. how the transition from the general to the special individual tribes also occurred without a sectional stop. In the same way here, Moses’s speech of blessing goes back from the special to the general without interruption. By this form of the external arrangement, the part referring to the nation in general—verses 2-5 and 25-29—is stamped as the real blessing applying to everything and everybody, within which just a few individual tribes are ranked, who display these common blessings in some prominent specialities. These specialities, which from V. 13 onwards refer in the main to agricultural matters receive, as we believe, in this V. 25, some general complementing traits with which then the speech quickly turns again to the completion of the general blessing of the whole nation. So that after, with Judah, Levi and Benjamin, the prominent bearers of the national strength, the national teachings and the national Sanctuary had been thought of, the blessings of the other seven tribes express the national welfare borne by the specialities of the various provinces. To this blessed picture of the Jewish Land, V. 25 adds a few complementing words of the mineral riches and the healthy climate of the country, and then the speech, with V. 26, rises to its conclusion with a general blessing again embracing everything.

If we cast a glance at the map of the land of Israel, then the order in which the tribes are mentioned here, apart from the inner connection, will be seen to follow their geographical situation as the land is seen by Moses from his viewpoint on the summit of Mt. Nebo. He stood in the domain of Reuben. Looking across the Dead Sea, Judah and Benjamin first meet his eye, to whom, in accordance with the pre-eminence of his calling, Levi is attached in spirit. Immediately next to them Ephraim and the part of Menasseh occupy the real centre of the Land and immediately next to them again, to the north are the provinces of Issachar and Zebulan. Passing over Judah and progressing to Ephraim and Menasseh one comes to Gad on the east, with Dan directly opposite on this side on the west, being left out. Coming back to this and thereby to Dan’s conquest in the north, we come to Naphtali in the north-east and, bordering on him, Asher on the north-west. Asher forms the extreme north-west point of the Land. Beyond that Lebanon strikes the eye which, with its riches of minerals completes the blessings of the Land. This is expressed in Moses’s birds-eye view as מנעלך .ברזל ונחשת מנעלך from נעל to close, מנעול a lock to a door, here designates the Lebanon range of mountains as the “lock”, the natural defence of the northern border of the Land, which at the same time adds mineral riches to the vegetable riches of the soil already described.

כימיך דבאך. The root דבא does not occur again. The phonetic relation to דוה, to be sick, in ill health, and with דפה the root of דופי, a blemish, points to דבא having the conception of a condition of weakness. כימיך דבאך would accordingly say: “your loss of strength is only in accordance with your age” i.e. in your land, people do not grow old before their time. If this way of taking it be correct, then thereby the most beneficient nature of the climate would be designated which is favourable to the most normal development of people. But as this last trait in the picture of the blessings of the land is bracketed with the view at Lebanon, that range of mountains which high up in the north with its slopes extending southwards forms the skeleton formation of the country (see on Ch. 3,25), it is not farfetched to think that the climatic nature of the land is to a very considerable extent given by the Lebanon range, and the mention of the blessing of the climate comes in connection with the mental view of Lebanon which not only forms a bulwark on the border rich with minerals but also spreads a healthy climate throughout the land: ברזל ונחשת מנעלך וכימיך דבאך.

V. 26. כָּאל .אין וגו׳. This God, God, as He manifests Himself there is comparable to nothing else, nowhere is God so evident as in you when you are “Jeshurun”, when you live “undeviatingly” faithful to your duty. רבב שמים, not השמים, anything in the extramundane universe which could have any influence on your well-being He directs to your support i.e. when He helps you He directs all incorporeal powers to that end. שחקים ,ובגאותו שחקים compared to שמים belong already to the earthly realm, do they not form up from the earth, hence ובגאותו, in all His Loftiness, high above everything earthly though He is raised, nevertheless He also directs your earthly heavens to your benefit.

V. 27. מענה. See Levit. 19,26, p. 549. He, Who is the God of all eternity bears every flitting moment of every present time. And He is not only a God from the heights above, He is also that which מתחת from the depths below forms up here זרעת עולם the “eternal arms”, i.e. that which bears everything in this world from all the past into all the future, that is He. זרועות, not זרוע, earthly matters need a variety of arms to bear their existence. He, Who accordingly is the God of all times, all places and all things, has in the present directed the Land as being the place destined for your development, and decreed the withdrawal of the inhabitants from the land. השמד is destruction.

V. 28. וישכן וגו׳. Only through God, Who מענה וגו׳ ויגרש וגו׳ has Israel found its home on earth, בטח בדד, secure in isolation, under God’s protection detached from connection with the state of affairs of the other nations; עין יעקב: it is deeply significant that it does not say יעקב על עין ארץ דגן ותירוש, Jacob at the source of a richly blessed land, but יעקב אל ארץ וגו׳, literally “Jacob’s source to a land full of corn and wine”, i.e. it is not Jacob who flourishes through the land, but the land flourishes through Jacob. Jacob is the source from which the land becomes a land full of corn and wine. The flourishing of the land does not rest on physical causes. The moral behaviour expected from Jacob, his fulfilment of his moral calling is to be the source of the blessing of his land, hence אף שמיו יערפו טל. The enhancement implied by אף cannot possibly refer to טל, to dew, that the heaven sends him even plentiful dew. For dew is the most natural, almost never-failing precipitation of the atmosphere, טל לא מיעצר, even in years when no rain falls, as occurred after Elijah’s proclamation, the dew still fell (Taanis 3a, and b), so one cannot say “even dew is granted to him by the heavens”. But we think that the stress rather lies in the suffix שמיו, even the dew, this gift that comes so regularly in accordance with the laws of nature, is granted to him by his heavens, i.e. the skies grant it because they vault over Jacob’s land, because Jacob’s calling and moral behaviour deserve the blessing. Even in the dew the effect of Jacob is felt! In a similar way the passage in Judges V. 4, גם עביו נטפו מים, where the enhancement “also, even”, is difficult to explain, may have the same meaning. “When God at the Lawgiving on Sinai approached the earth, His proximity was felt in the whole territorial world, and even the otherwise quite natural drops of water from the clouds announced His Presence”. There, in any case, perhaps the very presence of rainclouds in the usually cloudless skies of the desert could mean that something unusual was about to happen.

V. 29. אשריך ישראל, see Gen. on XXX,13. In Israel the one principle is realised to which everlasting progress is certain, and that is the establishment of the social affairs of life to which God, the God of all future, guarantees a healthy happy life, He defends it against all dangers, and He it is Who gives it the “sword of its eminence”, i.e. He gives it the national eminence among the nations which in all others is borne by the “sword”.

ויכחשו אויביך לך. The time will come when the principle which you have held aloft will shine forth in the world so victoriously that all your opponents will give the lie to their past opposition and you will mount to the heights of all the human endeavours which they have all sought in vain to reach by other means.
V. 1-3. ויעל וגו׳. Concerning the naming of the provinces after the tribes already before the land had been partitioned, see on Numb. 34,19.
הים האחרון, see on Ch. 11,24—הכבר is the plain of the valley of the Jordan (See Gen. 13,10).

V. 5. וימת וגו׳ .על פי ה׳. It was God’s expressed decree that Moses was to die on this side of the Land. The deep significance of this for the whole mission of Moses we have already repeatedly gone into (see Numb. 20,12 and XXVII,14, as well as Deut. 3,26). Hence this definite mention at the moment of its actual occurrence. In Baba Bathra 15,a, there are different opinions. According to one it was Joshua who wrote the eight verses from here to the end, according to the other, these verses too, like the rest of the Torah, were written by the hand of Moses at God’s dictation, only until here Moses first repeated to himself what he received from God before writing it down but these eight verses he wrote silently with his tears. מכאן ואילך הקב״ה אומר ומשה כותב בדמע. Perhaps behind this sentence lies the thought:- What Moses had to write up to here was said for him also, for him to take to heart so he repeated every word of it to and for himself and then wrote it down for the people. But the contents of these eight verses goes beyond his stay down here, were not for him to take to heart, especially not the concluding posthumous fame. He wrote these last eight verses just quite objectively at God’s dictation for his people, and wrote them with tears. Also when they are read out in public, the special painful contents dealing with the death of Moses has to be stressed by יחיד קורא אותן (ibid) which means, according to the most general way of taking it, that they may not be divided up but must be read by one single person. Similarly, we believe according to the dictum in Megilla 31a, that אין מפסיקין בקללות אלא אחד קורא את כולן which we take to be for similar reasons.

V. 6. ויקבר אותו בגי. According to Sota 9b, the subject of the verb ויקבר is the preceding ה׳, of על פי ה׳, and there it points out on 14b, how at the beginning of the Torah and at its end God Himself sets the example of doing גמילות חסדים acts of love and kindness to the living and to the dead. In the beginning it is recorded in Gen. 3,21 how God “clothed the naked”, and here how he “buried the dead” דרש ר׳ שמלאי תורה תחלתה גמילות חסדים וסופה גמילות חסדים תהלתה דכתיב ויעש ה׳ אלקים לאדם ולאשתו But according to כתנות עור וילבישם וסופה גמילות חסדים דכתיב ויקבור אותו בגי ר׳ ישמעאל the אותו is reflexive, “he buried himself”, laid himself down in the grave, there to die, similar to יביא אותו אל פתח אהל מועד (Numb. 6,13) and והשיאו אותם עון אשמה (Levit. 22,16) (“and they bring upon themselves the sin etc.” I.L.)—קבורה ,ולא ידע איש את קבורתו, grave, as מצבה על קבורתה (Gen. 35,20), וקברתני בקבורתם (ibid XLVII,30). When one considers how often a cult of worship verging on idolatry has grown round the places of the graves of great men who have deserved great honour amongst mankind, one can understand the greatness of this last phase in the picture of the life of our Moses.
עד היום הזה. See on Gen. 32,33.

V. 7. ענבים לחים ,לחה .ומשה (Numb. VI.3) fresh grapes, hence לח or לחה, similar formation to רע and רעה: freshness. The root seems to be לחה related to להה ,לאה both of which mean a lessening of force (see Gen. 47,13), to which לחה, with the ח of contrast would express the opposite, the unlessened life, the freshness of forces. לחה with the feminine ה instead of ו refers to a freshness which is not usual in the age of weakness of a person.
V. 8. ויתמו ימי בכי אבל משה .ויבכו וגו׳, the days of the weeping in which the grief for Moses showed itself came to an end, but the grief itself went on.
V. 9. ויהושע וגו׳. See on Numb. 27,18.

V. 10-12. ולא קם נביא וגו׳ לעיני כל ישראל. These three final verses place a seal on the Law of God brought through Moses, and ensure it its eternal inviolability and unalterableness. Accordingly they stress only three factors out of Moses’s mission, and just those which hold out an iron shield against any complete or partial abrogation of God’s Torah by any later prophet, as well as against any bold or light-minded addition to it. The לא קם וגו׳ of verse 10 refers also to the לכל וגו׳ of verse 11 and 12. As well regarding the פנים אל פנים as the אותות ומופתים במצרים and the יד חזקה ומורא גדול which he had to do לעיני כל ישראל, Moses stands unique for all time.

The direct contact in which God made Himself and His Will manifest to Moses in raising him out of the rest of mankind for the mission he had to carry out—ידעו; see Gen. 18,19 and Ex. 33,12— was not attained by any later prophet, none of them can ever boast of that in Israel. פנים אל פנים, face to face Moses received every word of his mission—Ex. 33,11 and Numb. 12,8—and no word not received in a similar direct manner can ever shake in the tiniest degree that which was given so directly to Moses. And the אותות ומופתים revealing God and His Almighty Power with which Moses had to free Israel out of the power of Egypt for God and His Torah, and the יד החזקה and the מורא הגדול, the Strong Hand which allows none of Its possessions to wrest itself away, and the Greatness which has to be feared at any disobedience which Moses then had to bring לעיני כל ישראל to Israel for the Torah he had brought: all this stands for all time, warningly against every external power against Israel, and every internal pertness towards, or defection from, the Torah in Israel which would estrange Israel from its calling and thereby endanger the work of the mission of Moses.
ח ז ק
ברוך נתן ליעף כח ולאין אונים עצמה ירבה.
